translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb túń ditundi abin aluli Raseel pu ní an kaa kpáàa súŋkì u-cee, kun puee u nìn néeń-u tikpil.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jaakɔb bí Laaban yii: «M túń ditundi ki sāā m-yuntiŋu, an puee dū m-nimpuu ki tīī-mi ḿ cáá.»

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban kóoǹ niin yab kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní bi jíń tinimpucan jiŋaaliu.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Kunyeeuee ní Laaban yōoǹ u-biseebiki Leeya ki cáa kɔ́ǹ Jaakɔb cee ní u nì Jaakɔb kpáfì.

english_verse: Laban also gave Zilpah to Leah as her servant woman.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban dū u-yumbusapɔɔŋwu Siilpa ki tīī u-bisal Leeya ú nīn bí u-cee ki tūǹ ditundi ki tìì-u.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe, Jaakɔb kpēēyee Leeya dee, ní an ŋá-u bitii. Ní u bālifì u-wee Laaban yii: «Ba ŋá ní a ŋá-mi mimmee? An kaa sá Raseel pu ní m kāl̀ a-cee ki túń ditundi ki tīī-saaa? Ba pu ní a kíil̀-mi ki dū Leeya ki tīī-mi?»

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban kíí-u yii: «Timbi cee dooyee, an sá-ti dikoobil ní, uwaal kaa pēentí ukpil kí mɔ̄ǹ.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee púntí sii nì un bí nee nimpucanti kinyɔŋ nee, kin dāa bíńee, ḿ dū Raseel mun kí tīī-si, á tí kàl̄ abin aluli kí tɔ̄ ditundi kí tīī-mi.»

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb nì Raseel mun kpáfì. Jaakɔb nìn néeń Raseel ki jítiǹ Leeya, ní ki nìn gíti kāl̀ abin aluli ki túń ditundi ki tīī Laaban. Jaakɔb biyaamu bɔti

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín ká yii Jaakɔb kaa néeń Leeyayee, ní u pú-u mmaal, ní Raseel úǹ sá uŋmaŋŋmanti.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Leeya nìn dūu cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki, ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Rubeen. Di sá yii un nìn lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan ká m-falaau, kɔŋkɔnnee m-cal làá nīn kíǹ ki néeń-mi.»

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Ní u gíti cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki, ní ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín ká yii m-cal kaa néeń-mee ní u gíti pú-mi kibininjabiki kiba.» Ní u pú-kì diyindi yii Simeeyɔn, taapu di sá yii: <Ti-Dindaan gbìl̄.>

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Raseel nín ká yii waa bíi màal̀ Jaakɔb mbiyaamuee, ní u kíǹ ki ŋáań u-maan ipoompoon, ní ki bí Jaakɔb yii: «Yàntī ḿ màal̀, an yaa kaa sá míǹ m làá kpú.»

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb fōō u-pu diŋuul ní ki bí yii: «Man di sá Unimbɔti un kaa dū mmaal ki ŋá a-poon á nīn màal̀eeee?»

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Raseel bí Jaakɔb yii: «Kpèè, m-yumbusapɔɔŋwu Biila sɔ̀. Dū-u kí kpántí a-nimpuu ú màal̀ kí tīī-mi, ní u-puee ma mun ń ká kibiki.»

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Ní Biila cáá dipool ní ki màl̄ Jaakɔb kibininjabiki.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Ní Raseel bí yii: «Unimbɔti pílifiǹ-mi, ki pɔ̀n̄-mi ki tīī-mi kibininjabiki.» An pu ní u pú-kì diyindi yii Daani, taapu di sá yii: «U pɔ̀n̄-mi.»

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Ní Biila gíti cáá dipool ní ki màl̄ Jaakɔb kibininjabiki kililiitii.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Ní Raseel bí yii: «M mɔ̀n̄ nì m-maan Unimbɔti nimbiin ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-u.» Ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Neefitalii, taapu di sá yii <M-mool.>

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Leeya mun kpēē yii waa ti bíi màal̀ee, ní u dū u-yumbusapɔɔŋwu Siilpa ki tīī Jaakɔb ú dūú kpántí u-nimpuu.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Ní Leeya yumbusapɔɔŋwu Siilpa màl̄ Jaakɔb kibininjabiki.

english_verse: When they had another son,
translation_verse: Ní Leeya yumbusapɔɔŋwu Siilpa fātìi màl̄ Jaakɔb kibininjabiki kililiitii.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Ní Leeya bí yii: «Ba mɔŋŋu bulifi poon ní m bí nee! Bisapɔmbi làá dāá yíiń-mi yii mmɔn daan.» Ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Aseer, taapu di sá yii <Mmɔndaan.>

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi cēē tijimpinee, Rubeen cūtì dalba kusaau ní ki ká kufaapibiku kun bi yíì yii mandragɔɔree biliŋ ní ki kītìń ki cáań ki tīī u-na Leeya. Ní Raseel bí Leeya yii: «M gbāam̀-si, lēē mandragɔɔr biliŋ ŋin a-jipɔɔn cáań-see kí tīī-maa!»

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Ní Leeya kíí-u yii: «A fōō m-calee, an kaa yá ki kɔ́-si ní a gíti là kí fōō m-jipɔɔn mun mandragɔɔr biliŋ kí kūtàaa?» Ní Raseel bí yii: «An yaa sée, tí kpántí. Á lēē mandragɔɔr biliŋ ŋin a-jipɔɔn cáań-see kí tīī-mi, uninja ń dòon̄ a mun cee díǹ nyeeku!»

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Kujoou Jaakɔb nyánní kusaau ki kùnnée ní Leeya túŋkì-u nsanni ní ki bí-u yii: «Man cee ní a làá dòon̄ díǹ. Kí ŋmā kí ká-si á dòon̄ m-ceeyee, m-jipɔɔn mandragɔɔr biliŋ ní m dūu pàn̄ m-yɔnti.» Ní Jaakɔb lafun dōoǹ u-cee kunyeeu gbanti.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti fōō Leeya wimmeem ní u cáá dipool ki màl̄ Jaakɔb kibininjabiki kiŋmooŋmootii.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Ní Leeya bí yii: «Unimbɔti pàn̄-mi m nín dū m-yumbusapɔɔŋwu ki tīī m-cal u dūu kpántì u-nimpuuee pu.» Ní u pú-kì diyindi yii Isakaar, taapu di sá yii <M-paati.>

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Leeya bí yii: «Unimbɔti pú-mi dipɔl dimɔntiil. Min bí nee, m-cal làá tīī-mi m-nyooti, kun puee m màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu muluu dee.» Míǹ puee ní u pú kibikee diyindi yii Sabulɔn, taapu di sá yii <Tinyool.>

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Boonee ní u màl̄ kibinimpubiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Diina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Ní Raseel cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki bí yii: «Unimbɔti lēē m-pu icoo.»

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: Ní u pú-kì diyindi yii Jooseefi ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń gíti kūtì-mi kibininjabiki kiba!» Jaakɔb kpántì ugaaja

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Raseel nín màl̄ Jooseefi boonee ní Jaakɔb bí Laaban yii: «Pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ fàtīí nīn kùǹ m-tiŋkin.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Dū m-biyaamu nì m-nimpoobi bin pu m túń-si ditundee kí tīī-mi ḿ nīn cá, di sá yii sii a-ba nyí ditundi din bulifi m túń ki tīī-see.»

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bí-u yii: «Sii a-ba nyí m nín túń ditundi din ki tīī-see nì m nín ŋúb́ a-waŋkuti tì būtì miŋyee.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Di sá yii kí wàatī ḿ bàńee, tin a nìn cááyee kaa nìn náaǹ báà fiii. Ama kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun m-taal tāā a-dumpuee, a-wanti wíiǹ tikpil ní ti-Dindaan bīiǹ a-boon. Too, kɔŋkɔnnee ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní man làá gíti dūú tɔ̄ ditundi kí ká tin làá ŋmàntī ḿ kpèè m-dicaŋkuee?»

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban bí-u yii: «Ba ní m máaǹ kí tīī-si ní?» Ní Jaakɔb bí yii: «Taa pée tīī-mi tiba. Ama a yaa kíí kí ŋá min m làá màkà-si neeyee, m làá gíti kpàà a-waŋkuti.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Díǹ nee, m làá yìiǹ tipicaŋkpun nì tiŋɔcaŋkpun poon kí gàntī ipii in cáá atan atanee nì in bɔ̀ǹee, ní kí gàntī iŋoobu in mun cáá atan atanee, án di làá nīn sá man paati.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Fool boon a yaa láa dɔ́miń ki kpēē m-paati ní ki yaa láa ká iŋoobu kansikin in kaa cáá atanee nì ipii kansikin in kaa bɔ̀ǹee, mimmee m yùn̄ dee, maa cáá mbaamɔn.»

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban kíí-u yii: «An ŋān̄, a nín lī puee, án ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Yaadal yaadal ní Laaban lútì iŋɔjaa nì iŋɔsal in cáá atan atanee, an dàkà yii in kɔkɔ pée cáá mpimee, nì ipibɔn ki dūu tīī u-jipɔmbi.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: U nìn yāntì bi cáá-i ki búntì ndandati bi nì Jaakɔb kansikin sá kii iwiin ita saŋkindi nyɔkɔm, ní Jaakɔb gbíntìi bíi kpàá Laaban waŋkuti tin kíǹee.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bátì isufi in bi yíì peepiliiyee nì amandi nì plataanee pambiyaamu nsɔmu, ki cùkū cùkū-mu ki māntìi tú ki dāa kátì taapu, ní ki pɔ́kɔtì ajan ŋin u cùkūee, ní ndɔsɔmuee kíǹ ki cáá mpim mpim.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Ní u dū ndɔsɔmu mun u cùkūee ki ŋá tiwan tin poon tiwaŋkuti nyùee ki túĺ tiwaŋkuti nimbiin, ní tì yaa dòoń ki nyùee, tì jɔ́ḿ tɔb.

english_verse: in front of the branches, and their young were spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Ndɔsɔmu mun u cùkūee cee ní tiwaŋkutee jɔ́ḿ tɔb ní ki màal̀ mbiyaamu cáá atan atan.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nìn gāntì ipisalee ní ki yāntì i kpèé Laaban waŋkuti tin cáá atan atanee nì tin bɔ̀ǹee. Míǹ ní u ŋáaǹ ní ki ká tipicaŋkpun nì tiŋɔcaŋkpun, ní ki gāntì-tì ki yóoǹ u-ba kaa dū tíǹ ki kpáfì nì Laaban yati.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní tiwaŋkuti tin yáàyee yaa làá jɔ̄m̀ tɔbee, ní Jaakɔb ń yòon̄ní ndɔsɔmu mun u cùkūee kí ŋá tiwan tin poon tiwaŋkuti nyùee kí túĺ ti-nimbiin, ní tì jɔ́ḿ tɔb ndɔsɔmu mun u cùkūee cee.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Ama tiwaŋkuti tin sá ŋkaŋkalimuee yaa bāańee, waa yōontí ndɔsɔmuee ti-nimbiin tí jɔ̄m̀ tɔb. Ŋkaŋkalimu gbantee, Laaban yati dee, ní úǹ yati sá tin yáàyee. Jaakɔb sáǹ Laaban

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Jaakɔb ŋá ki kpántì ugaajakpaŋkpaan ki cáá tiwaŋkuti tikpil, ki cáá bitɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi nì bininjab nì igutaamu nì mmamu.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nìn gbìl̄ Laaban jipɔmbi bí ki lì yii: «Jaakɔb fōō timbi baa wanti kɔkɔ, an wanti pu ní u kpántì ugaaja nee.»

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nín kpēē Laaban nimbiinee, u dáań ki ká yii u nì u kansikin kaa ti mɔ̄ kii dooooyee an nín nìn bí puee.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Jaakɔb yii: «Nín̄ gítí a-naanjab tiŋkin a-dumpu, man làá nīn bí a-cee.»

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jaakɔb tú bi yíiń u-nimpoobi Raseel nì Leeya bí dāan̄ u-cee kusaaun laakin u-waŋkuti bée.

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Jaakɔb ceeyee ní u bí-bi yii: «M dáań ki ká ni-baa nimbiin yii man nì u kansikin kaa ti mɔ̄ kii dooooyee. Ama m-baa Nimbɔtiu bí m-cee.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Nimbi ni-ba nyí m nín dū m-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ ki túń ditundi ki tīī ni-baa puee.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: Ní an yaa bàà sá ú pà-mi puee ní ú cúú kpántí. U kpántì-mi míǹ ní áli ŋfunyɔm saalaa pu, ama Unimbɔti kaa kíí ú ŋá-mi digaŋgam.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: U yaa lī yii: <Tiwaŋkuti tin kɔkɔ cáá atanee di sá a-paatee>, tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ màal̀ tin cáá atanee ní. U yaa tí lī yii: <Tiwaŋkuti tin kɔkɔ cáá iluntoonee di sá a-paatee>, tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ tí màal̀ tin cáá iluntoonee ní.

english_verse: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun tiwaŋkuti bíi jɔ́ḿ tɔbee ní m ká kudamintiiu poon yii ijaa in bíi jɔ́ḿ isalee sá atan atan nì iluntoon iluntoon nì ŋmàtì ŋmati.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Kudamintiiuee poon ní Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu yíiń-mi yii: <Jaakɔb!> Ní m kíí yii: <M sèé.>

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Ní ŋu bí-mi yii: <Yáatí kí kpèè, iŋɔjaa in bí ki jɔ́ḿ isalee kɔkɔ sá atan atan nì iluntoon iluntoon nì ŋmàtì ŋmati ní. M ŋá míǹ kun puee m ká Laaban nín ŋá-si puee.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Man di sá Unimbɔti un nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-si Beeteel, laakin a nìn dū ditaŋkpal ki cóoǹ ki sītì di-pu ŋkpam ní ki pūtì ki pōoǹ-mee. Kɔŋkɔnnee yīkì kí nīn gítí a-tiŋkin, laakin bi màl̄-see.>»

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: U dū-ti ki gíiǹ binicambi ní, kun puee u nyáfì-ti ní ki fōō animbil ki jíń.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: An puee ti-baa gaajati tin Unimbɔti fōō u-ceeyee, timbi nì ti-biyaamu di yì. Min kɔkɔ Unimbɔti yaa bí yii á ŋée, ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jaakɔb yōoǹ u-biyaamu nì u-nimpoobi ki kāaǹ igutaamu pu kí yīkì.

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: U nìn yōoǹ ki kpáaǹ u-waŋkuti nì u-gaajati tin u nìn kāl̀ Padan-Aram ki kée kɔkɔ ki cáa nín gítí u-baa Isaaki cee Kanaan tiŋkin.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Laaban nìn búntì kí cā u-piii kuti. Ŋyunti gbanti ní Raseel yùn̄ u-baa waaŋi.

english_verse: long years to earn your two daughters and another
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bál̀ Laaban uaranja ki yíkì kaa kāaǹ-u.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: U nìn kpáaǹ u-wanti tin u cááyee kɔkɔ ki cūtìi dūtì Eefiraati mɔɔkpaandi ní ki dū u-ba ki túĺ Galaadi jool watil pú.

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb yíkìi sáǹ iwiin ita boon ní bi dāa nín tùkū Laaban.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Laaban yōoǹ u-nabiyaamu ní bi nín jì Jaakɔb boon. Bi cōom̀ iwiin iluli ní ki tin nín cúú-u Galaadi jool pu.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Ama kunyeeuee ní Unimbɔti nyántì u-ba ki dàkā Laaban uaranja kudamintiiu poon ní ki bí-u yii: «Á cúú a-ba kí taa lì Jaakɔb tiba nì tiba, kí taa ŋá-u tikpitil báà tiba.»

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Laaban dūu bàn̄ Jaakɔb ceeyee, Jaakɔb gāā u-tantiu Galaadi jool pu, ní Laaban nì u-nabiyaamu mun gāā bi-tantib Galaadi jool gbanti pu.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban bālifì Jaakɔb yii: «Ba ŋá ní a ŋá mimmee? Ba pu ní a kíil̀-mi ki kpáaǹ m-bisalib ki búntì kii kujaau ní a cūtì ki jáń ki cúuń-bee?

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní a kíil̀-mi ki sáǹ dibalin míǹ kaa kāaǹ-mi? M bàà kàantí-si nì ifaal ní kí yàntī bí gāā ilan kí bɔ̀ɔ̀ ŋgaŋgamu nì tibati.

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Aa yāntì m kpàl̄ m-bisalib nì m-naantiibi ki kāaǹ-bi. Min a ŋá nee sá digbaandi ní.

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: M bàà cáá nsan kí ŋá-ni tin kaa ŋān̄ee, ama fool kunyeeu ní a-baa Nimbɔtiu fu sòon̄ nì mi ki bí-mi yii: <Á cúú a-ba kí taa lì Jaakɔb tiba nì tiba, kí taa ŋá-u tikpitil báà tiba.>

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee a-landɔkɔŋu gítì a-baa cindi pu ní a yíkì ki kùǹ, kin ba pu ní a gíti yù man waaŋi?»

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb kíí Laaban yii: «M fāŋkì ní ki dākafì yii m yaa kāaǹ-si, an yaa yíì a làá fōō a-bisalib.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Ama un cee ní a yaa ká a-waaŋee, bí kpɔ̀-u. Ti-nabiyaamu kɔkɔ di bí nee. Dāan̄ m-cee kí kpèè a yaa ká a-wanti tiba á yòon̄.» Jaakɔb kaa nìn nyí yii Raseel di yùn̄ awaa.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban nín kóò Jaakɔb tantiun ki kpēē, ní ki kɔ́ Leeya yɔun ki kpēē, ní ki kɔ́ inimpuyumbu liitil cee ki kpēē kaa ká báà tiba. U nyáń Leeya ceeyee ní ki nín kóò Raseel tantiun.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Raseel nìn yōoǹ awaayee ki dūu bál̀ ugutaamu gakal taapu ní ki kāl̀ an pu, ní Laaban kɔ́ ki kpēē u-tantiu poon kɔkɔ ní kaa ká tiba.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Ní Raseel bí u-baa yii: «M nín ká-si kaa yíkèe, án taa wà-si, di sá yii m ká m-ba ní.» Ní Laaban kpēē kaa ká awaa.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Niinee Jaakɔb fōō Laaban pu diŋuul ní ki yíkìi nyáń u-pu, ní ki bí-u yii: «Tilati ní m yīntiǹ-si? Ikpiti ilai ní m ŋá-si ní a jìǹní m-boon nì dibaatandi míǹ?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: A nín kpēē m-wanti kɔkɔee, a ká a-wanti tiba bí poonaaa? A yaa ká, á nyāntiń-tì man nib nì si mun nib nimbiin bí sòoǹ kí tīī-ti.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Tiba di yaa cúú a-waŋkuluuku kubɔee, maa cāabìń-si diwaŋkpil, see ḿ nyàab̀ kí téeǹ kun an cúúyee yil. A-waŋkuti tin bi yù ŋwiimpuee nì tin bi yù kunyeeuee, a bàlifī-mi ní ḿ téeǹ-si.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Ŋwiimpuee, ŋwìiń ŋmóò-mi ní kí kpɔ̀, ní kunyeeuee, tiwool ń kɔ́ kí dóó-mi ní ŋgeem ń wāŋkì m-nimbiliŋin.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: An yaa kaa sá m-baa Isaaki nì m-naanja Abraam Nimbɔtiu, Unimbɔti un m-baa Isaaki jáaḿ ki fàŋkée pu, a bàà làá yàntī ḿ nīn fàtīi gítí nì iŋaŋkulim ní. Ama Unimbɔti ká m-falaau nì m-tundi din m túńee. An pu ní fool nyeekuee, u fu sòon̄ ki kpáafì-si.»

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban kíí Jaakɔb yii: «Binimpoobi nee sá man bisalib ní, ní bi-biyaamu sá man biyaamu. Ipii nee sá man piii ní, tin kɔkɔ a pée wāĺ nee sá man wanti ní. Díǹ pu nee, ba ní m làá ŋá kí tīī m-bisalib nì bi-biyaamu mun bi màl̄ee?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: An ŋmāntì man nì si tí sòoǹ kí bóob́ kí pòon̄ tɔb, án nīn sá kudaaŋŋu man nì si kansikin.»

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jaakɔb píí ditaŋkpal ki cóoǹ án nīn sá-bi kudaaŋŋu.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Ní ki bí u-nabiyaamu yii bí tòò ataŋkpee kí bíĺ dikpúkul. Bi tōō ki bíl̀ee ní bi-kɔkɔ kāl̀ di-pu ki jíń tijin.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban pú ditaŋkpakpukulee diyindi u-sooŋyi poon yii Yeegar-Saaduta, ní Jaakɔb mun yíiń-dì u-sooŋyi poon yii Galeedi.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Ní Laaban bí yii: «Ditaŋkpakpukul nee di sá dipoondi din dōoǹ man nì si kansikinee daaŋku.» An pu ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Galeedi, taapu di sá yii: <Kudaaŋŋu taŋkpakpukul>.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Bi gíti pú niin diyindi yii Miisipa, taapu di sá yii: <Unimbɔti ń nīn bí ki wāĺ-ti.> Di sá Laaban nìn bí yii: «Unimbɔti ń nīn bí ki wāĺ man nì si kansikin ti yaa kaa dāa gíti bí ki wāĺ tɔbee.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: A yaa láa cáá binimpoobi ki kútì ní ki ŋúb́ man bisalib ki sàantée, báà ubɔ yaa kaa dāa bí ki wāĺ tin a bí ki ŋáańeeyaaa, á nīn nyí yii Unimbɔti bí ki wāĺ tin bí ki jītí man nì sii kansikinee.»

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Ditaŋkpakpukul nee nì ditaŋkpal din cɔ́ nee di sá-ti kudaaŋŋu yii man kaa làá lákatí ditaŋkpakpukul nee pu kí póotí a-pu, si mun ń taa lákatí ditaŋkpakpukul nee nì ditaŋkpacooŋkaal nee pu kí póotí man pu kí ŋá tikpitil.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Abraam nì Naakɔɔr Nimbɔtiu un sá bi-baa Nimbɔtiuee ń dāá sòoǹ man nì sii kansikin bɔti.» Ní Jaakɔb pūtì Unimbɔti un u-baa Isaaki nìn jáaḿ ki fàŋkée.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Jaakɔb ŋá saraa ubɔ dijool pu niin ní ki yíiń u-nabiyaamu bi kpáfìi jíń tijin ní ki gbíntì dijool pu niin ki dōoǹ.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì an dáá bɔ̀ǹee ní Laaban yíkì ki kpàl̄ u-bisalib nì u-naantiibi ki kāaǹ-bi, ki mēē ki bīiǹ bi-pu ní ki fātìi nín kùǹ u-dumpu. Jaakɔb bɔ́ntì kí tūŋkì Eesayuu

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb mun nín nìkì u-saŋŋu. U cée ní Unimbɔti tuuŋyi cílìń u-pu nsanni.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: U ká-iee ní ki téeń yii: «Unimbɔti janjanaapaal sèé!» An pu ní u pú niin diyindi yii Maanayiim, taapu di sá yii: <Ajanjanaapaa ali>.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jaakɔb lēē binib ki tú u-maan Eesayuu cee Eedoom satin, Seeyiir tiŋki poon.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: U nìn kpáafì-bi ki bí yii: «Ni yaa bàn̄ee ní tùkù m-kpiliu Eesayuu yii: <Mama a-tɔntɔnliu Jaakɔb di túnní bí tùkù-si yii, doooo m nín búntì Laaban ceeyee, niin ní m kāl̀ ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: M cáá inaa nì mmamu nì ipii nì iŋoobu nì bitɔntɔnliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi. An pu ní m túnní bí dāá tùkù sii m-kpiliu yii á dàkà-mi a-ŋanti kí fōō-mi.>»

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Ní binib bin u túee fātìi gítìń u-cee ní ki tùkū-u yii: «Ti bàn̄ ki ká a-maan Eesayuu. U mun bí nsanni ki túŋkiń-si u nì binib alaataa anaa.»

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní tifaandi kɔ́ Jaakɔb ní u-pɔbil bíil̀. Ní u cúú u-nib nì u-piii nì u-ŋoobui nì u-naai nì u-gutaamui ki yākatì akiti ali.

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: M pátì kí fōō tiŋan tin a ŋá-mi nee nì tibulcin tin a dàkā man a-tɔntɔnliu nee, kun puee ŋkpandɔ baba ní m nìn ŋúb́ ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nee. Ama díǹ pu nee, m yākatì m-nib nì m-waŋkuti akiti ali ní nee.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee m gbāam̀-si, á fīī-mi m-maan Eesayuu ŋaan. M fàŋkí ú taa láa kpɔ̀ man nì m-nimpoobi nì m-biyaamu.

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: Di sá yii sii di líì-mi dimákal yii: <M làá bìin̄ a-boon kí yàntī a-naantiibi ń bùtī kii tiŋku gbandi bulee, bí taa ŋmā kí kàaǹ-bi.>»

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: Míǹ mbaantiim ní u tùkū u-tɔntɔnliu uliliiti nì utataati nì u-tɔntɔnliibi bin kɔkɔ u lēē tiwaŋkuti ki tīī bí lìntī u-nyɔkɔpuee, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ni yaa tú Eesayuu nsannee, min ní ni làá lèe dee.

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bí-u yii: «M gbāam̀-si, tùkù-mi a-yindi.» Ní u bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní a là kí béé m-yindi?» Niin niin ní u bīiǹ Jaakɔb boon.

english_verse: Jacob put servants in charge of each herd and told them, “Go ahead of me and keep a space between each herd.”
translation_verse: ki lēē igutaamu in cáá mbiyaamu ŋáaḿee nì i-biyaamu mmuŋku nì saalaa, ki lēē inasal imuŋku ili nì inajaa saalaa, ki lēē mmansalimu mmuŋku nì mmanjamu saalaa.

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: U nìn yākatì tiwaŋkutee akiti akiti ki dūu tīī u-tɔntɔnliibi ní ki bí-bi yii: «Lìntīmaan kí nīn cá kí nīn pá tɔb boon ki dátiǹ tɔb.»

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: Ní u kpáafì un līīyee yii: «M-maan Eesayuu yaa tú-si nsanni ní ki yaa bālifì-si yii: <A-kpiliu sá ŋma ní a cá la? Ŋma di yì tiwaŋkuti tin līī a-nyɔkɔpu nee?>,

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: á kíí-u yii: <An sá a-tɔntɔnliu Jaakɔb di yì. U túnní-mi ḿ cáań kí tīī u-kpiliu Eesayuu ní. Úǹ u-ba páń boon ki dòoń.>»

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Ní ní kūtì kí lì yii: <A-tɔntɔnliu Jaakɔb u-ba páń boon ki dòoń.>» Di sá u lī u-neen yii: «M làá dū tiwaŋkuti nee kí pɔ̄-u kí sɔ̀ŋkì u-pɔbil, boonee ní kí dāá nín ká-u. An yaa yíì u táá sɔ̄ m-saai kí fōō-mi.»

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbanti ní Jaakɔb yōoǹ u-nimpoobi liitil nì inimpuyumbu liitil ki kpáaǹ u-biyaamu saalaa nì kibee ki dūtì Yaabɔki buŋŋu laakin pú kaa nyóòyee.

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: U cáá u-yab kɔkɔ ki dūtì mbun ki kpáaǹ tin kɔkɔ u cááyee.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb cáá-bi ki dūtì míǹ ki dóò, ki kíǹ u-babee ní unaaciin ubɔ dɔ́miń kunyeeu ki cìb̄-u dimool ní bi mɔ̀n̄ áli ntaafaabɔmbɔm.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Unaaciinee kpēē yii waa làá ŋmā kí líí Jaakɔbee ní u fáá u-nantaŋkpal ní u-kpìiŋŋu yɔ̄tì, ama ní u nì Jaakɔb gbíntìi bíi mɔ̀.

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Ní unaaciinee bālifì-u yii: «Bi yíì-si yii ba ní?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «Bi yíì-mi yii Jaakɔb ní.»

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Ní unaaciinee bí-u yii: «Baa làá ti yíiń-si Jaakɔb, bi làá nīn kíǹ ki yíì-si yii Isirayeel ní. Di sá yii si nì Unimbɔti mɔ̀n̄ ní si nì binib mun mɔ̀n̄, ní a pɔ́ɔkiǹ bi-kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb pú niin diyindi yii Peeniyeel, taapu di sá yii: <Unimbɔti nimbiin>, di sá u lī yii: «M ká Unimbɔti yéè kpìrrr ama ní kaa kpíì.»

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì ŋwìiń nyáń ní Jaakɔb yíkì Peeniyeel. U-kpìiŋŋu puee, u nìn dúlifí ní.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: U nìn dá ntampaan ŋun pu u gāā u-tantibee Amɔɔr biyaamu cee. Amɔɔr gbanti di nìn sá Siikeem baa. U nìn dá ntampaan gbanti animbil jitɔmbi dilaataal ní.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: U nìn máń nsaraafan niin, ní ki pú ntampaan gbanti diyindi yii <Eel, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu>.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Dalbee, Jaakɔb bisal Diina un Leeya màl̄ee cūtì kí màntì kitiŋ kin poon bi nìn kóòyee sapɔmbi pu.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Ní Amɔɔr un sá Eefi tiŋki bɔtiuee jipɔɔn Siikeem ká-u ní ki cúú-u mpɔn ki dōoǹ nì u ki bíil̀-u.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: An ŋá mimmee ní u-naŋki kɔ́ Jaakɔb bisal Diina tikpil ki jíń mpaan u-pɔbilin. Di sá u nìn bíi sòoǹ nì usapɔɔnee kí gíiǹní u-landɔkɔŋu u-cee.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Ní Siikeem bí u-baa Amɔɔr yii: «Cùú mɔ̀nnì usapɔɔn nee kí tīī-mi, m là kí cáá-u.»

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb gbìl̄ yii Siikeem dōoǹ nì u-bisal Diina ki bíil̀-u, ama waa nìn lī tiba, di sá yii u-jipɔmbi nìn dáá bíń tisatin kunaakpaau ní u nìn cí yii bí bàń.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb jipɔmbi nín nyánní tisatin ki bāań ki gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní an wùn̄-bi tikpil ní bi fōō diŋuul tiŋan pu. Di sá yii Siikeem nín dōoǹ nì Jaakɔb bisalee, an sá disiibikpaandi ní Isirayeel yab cee, ki sá-bi dikoobikpaandi.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Ní Amɔɔr bí-bi yii: «Ni-bisal Diina kɔ́ m-jipɔɔn Siikeem tikpil, an puee m gbāam̀-ni, ní dū-u kí tīī-u ú cáá.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Tí kɔ́maan tɔbin, nimbi ń nīn tìì-ti ni-sapɔmbi ti cāab̀, ti mun ń nīn tìì-ni ti-yab ni cāab̀.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Ní gbíntí kí nīn kā ti-cee, ní ti-tiŋki ń kpántí ni-yaka ní nīn kóò, kí nīn tɔ́ ni-ba kí bàntì kí kpántí bitindambi.»

english_verse: Ask anything, no matter how expensive. I'll do anything, just let me marry Dinah.”
translation_verse: Gíímaan-mi kucootiiu nì tinimpucaŋwan pɔndi tikpil ḿ pà. M làá tīī-ni tin ni lèe kɔkɔ. Tin pée páb́ee di sá ní dū usapɔɔn kí tīī-mi ḿ cáá.»

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb jipɔmbi kíí Amɔɔr nì u-jipɔɔn Siikeem nì iciin poon, kun puee u nìn dōoǹ nì bi-niisal Diina ki bíil̀-u.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Bi kíí-bi yii: «An kaa ŋáań míǹ! Taa ŋūǹ kí dū ti-niisal kí tīī un kaa gíí dikpancandee ticati, an sá-ti icoo ní.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī tí gbìl̄ kí tīī nì nee, asee ní yàntī bin kɔkɔ sá bininjab ni-kansikinee ń gīfì akpancan kii timbi nín gíí puee.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Mimmee ti ŋūǹ kí tīī-ni ti-sapɔmbi ní cáá, ní ti mun ń cáá ni-yab, ní tí gbíntí ni-tiŋkin ní ti-kɔkɔ ń kpāfì kí ŋá kitimbaantii nib.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa yíì yii naa làá gīfèe, ti làá fōō ti-niisal ní kí yīkì.»

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Bi nín sòon̄ puee fáatì Amɔɔr nì u-jipɔɔn Siikeem.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Unaacimpɔɔnee nín nìn néeń Jaakɔb bisal tikpil puee yāntì u kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań tin bi bālifì yii ú ŋée malaa. U-baa dicaŋku poonee, úǹ ní bi nìn pée tɔ́ ki jítiǹ báà ŋma.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Ní Amɔɔr nì u-jipɔɔn Siikeem cūtìi kāl̀ bi-tiŋki punyɔkɔki caŋin ní ki tùkū bi-tiŋki nib yii:

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: «Binib nee cáá ti-pu nlandɔkɔmɔnti. Kitiŋ dɔ̄ ki wāā ki tīī-bi bí kàl̄ kí bàntì. Ti ŋūǹ kí cáá bi-bisalib, ní ti mun ŋūǹ kí dū ti-bisalib kí pɔ̄-bi ticati.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī bí kíí kí nīn kā ti-tiŋki pu ti-kɔkɔ ń kpántí kitimbaantii nibee, asee tí yàntī bin kɔkɔ sá bininjab ti-kansikinee ń gīfì akpancan kii bíǹ nín gíí puee.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Ti yaa gbìl̄ ki tīī nì bi bí nīn kóò ti-ceeyee, bi-waŋkuti kɔkɔ nì bi-gaajati kaa kpántì ti-yati deeee?»

english_verse: Every grown man followed this advice and got circumcised. Dinah's Brothers Take Revenge
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee fōō tibɔti tin Amɔɔr nì u-jipɔɔn Siikeem cáańee ki kíí, ní kitiŋ poon bininjab kɔkɔ gífì akpancan.

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Bi gífì míǹ iwiin ita dal ŋyunti ŋun bi dáá kā iween puee ní Jaakɔb jipɔmbi bili, Simeeyɔn nì Leefii bin sá Diina niijabee yōoǹ bi-tàataajimmu ki ŋá soooo ki kɔ́ kitiŋin ubɔ kaa béè ní ki kūū bininjab kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb jipɔmbee kɔ́ kitiŋin ki fúkúl̀ anikpilee wanti ní ki kóoǹ bi-wanti kɔkɔ, kun puee bi bíil̀ bi-niisal.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Bi nìn cúú bi-piii nì bi-ŋoobui nì bi-naai nì bi-mammu nì tin kɔkɔ nìn pée bí kitiŋ poon nì tisatinee.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kóoǹ bi-gaajati kɔkɔ pílpil ki kpáaǹ bi-nimpoobi nì bi-biyaamu nì tin kɔkɔ nìn pée bí bi-diiŋŋinee.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bí Simeeyɔn nì Leefii yii: «Ni kɔ́ǹ-mi tibɔtin! Ni náań kudɔ̀ŋu ki bíl̀ man nì kitiŋ nee nib kansikin ní nee, an dàkà yii Kanaan yab nì Peeriisi yab. Man nib kaa náaǹ. Bíǹ ŋūǹ kí kpāfì kí dāá jáǹ-mi ní kí kúntí m-dicaŋku kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí bi-baa yii: «Mimmee bi cáá nsan kí bíil̀ ti-niisal kii kilaakpaayeeee?»

english_verse: God told Jacob, “Return to Bethel, where I appeared to you when you were running from your brother Esau. Make your home there and build an altar for me.”
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Unimbɔti bí Jaakɔb yii: «Yīkì doo kí nīn jɔ́ḿ Beeteel kí cùú nīn kóò niin. Á mā nsaraafan laakin m nìn nyántì m-ba ki dàkā-si ŋyunti ŋun a nìn sáń a-maan Eesayuuyee.»

english_verse: Jacob said to his family and to everyone else who was traveling with him: Get rid of your foreign gods! Then make yourselves acceptable to worship God and put on clean clothes.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bí u-dicaŋku yab nì bin kɔkɔ bí u-ceeyee yii: «Nyāntímaan awaa ŋin bí ni-ceeyee, kí ŋá ni-ba circir kí kpántí ni-wampeeŋkaati.

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Tí yīkìmaan kí cù Beeteel. Ti yaa bàn̄ niinee, m làá mā nsaraafan kí tīī Unimbɔti un un fōō m-wimmeem ŋyunti ŋun m nìn bí dinimbinaamandi poon ní ki céeǹ-mi m-saŋkiŋŋi kɔkɔ poonee.»

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi nyántì awaa ŋin bí bi-ceeyee, ki túutì bi-falfatib ki tīī Jaakɔb ní u cáa gbìn̄ ki síb́ teereebinti subu bun yú ki pìlīǹ Siikeem tiŋkee taapu.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Bi yíkèe ní Unimbɔti yāntì dinyoondi kɔ́ ntimu mun kɔkɔ māntì ki tú-bee, ní báà ubɔ kaa mākaǹ kí jà bi-boon.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Bethel, also known as Luz.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb nì u-nipaaku dūu bàn̄ Luusi, an dàkà yii Beeteel, Kanaan tiŋkin.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Ní u máń nsaraafan ní ki pú niin diyindi yii Eel-Beeteel, taapu di sá yii: <Beeteel Nimbɔtiu>, kun puee niin ní Unimbɔti nìn nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-u ŋyunti ŋun u nìn sáń u-maan Eesayuuyee.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Niin ní Deeboora un nìn lōō Reebeekee kpíì ní bi síb́-u seeni subu bun yú ki pìlīǹ Beeteelee taapu. Ní Jaakɔb pú busubu gbanti diyindi yii <Nsiim subu.>

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kin m nìn tīī Abraam nì Isaakee, m làá dū-kì kí tīī sii nì a-naantiibi bin làá páanní boonee.»

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb dū ditaŋkpal ki cóoǹ laakin Unimbɔti sòon̄ nì uee, ní ki dū ndamam nì ŋkpam ki fá di-pu án nīn sá kudaaŋŋu.

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nì u-dicaŋku yíkì Beeteel. Bi cá ki tóob́ Eefiraata tiŋkee ní Raseel màl̄. U-maaliŋu gbanti nìn pɔ́ɔkì tikpil.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u bíi yáliŋkí imatiŋween ki làá màal̀ee ní umatimmaanli bí-u yii: «Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba, kibininjabiki ní a làá gíti màal̀.»

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u bíi dátí u-ba kí sìntēe ní u pú kibiki kin u màl̄ee diyindi yii Been-Oonii, taapu di sá yii: <M-falaau biki.> Ama ní ki-baa yíiń-kì yii Beenjameen, taapu di sá yii: <M-ŋaŋgiil pu biki.>

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Raseel kpíìyee ní bi síb́-u Eefiraata dandi kpaanceetiŋu. Kitiŋ gbanti ní bi gíti yíì yii Beetileem.

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb dū ditaŋkpal ki cóoǹ dikaakul pu án nīn sá Raseel kaakul daaŋku. Di bí ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yíkì niinee ní ki cūtìi gāā u-tantib Miigidaal-Eedeer tiŋki nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel nìn kóò kitiŋ gbantinee ní u-jipɔɔn Rubeen dōoǹ nì u-nimpuwaaki Biila, ní u-baa gbìl̄. Jaakɔb jipɔmbi nìn sá saalaa nì bili ní.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nìn bàn̄ u-baa Isaaki cee Mamiree, Kiiriyati-Ariba tiŋkin. Niin ní bi gíti yíì yii Eebrɔn. Abraam nì Isaaki nìn kāl̀ kitiŋ gbantin.

english_verse: Esau, also known as Edom, had many descendants.
translation_verse: Eesayuu un bi gíti yíì Eedoomee naantiibi yiŋŋi sèé.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Eesayuu cáá Kanaan tiŋkin ní binimpoobi. Ada un nìn sá Eelɔn, ueetija bisalee nì Ooliibama un nìn sá Ana bisal nì Siibeeyɔn ueefija naantiiuee.

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: U nìn gíti cáá Isimaayeel bisal Basmaati, Neebayɔti niisal.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: ní Ooliibama màl̄-u Yeewusi nì Yalaam nì Kɔɔra. Mbininjabiyaamu mun Eesayuu màl̄ Kanaan tiŋkinee dee.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Boonee Eesayuu yōoǹ u-nimpoobi nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-bisalib nì binib bin kɔkɔ pée bí u-dicaŋkunee, nì u-waŋkuti kɔkɔ nì tigaajati tin kɔkɔ u kāl̀ Kanaan tiŋkin ki kée ki yíkìi búntì kitiŋ kiba poon ki wāatì u-naal Jaakɔb.

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Di sá yii bi nìn cáá tigaajati tikpil, ní kitiŋ kin poon bi kóòyee kaa nìn gíti bà-bi, kun puee bi-waŋkuti nìn būtì tikpil.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní Eesayuu, un bi gíti yii Eedoomee, cūtìi kóòń Seeyiir jool pu. Eesayuu naantiibi

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Eesayuu maaliŋu poon bin sá adican kpilibee yiŋŋi di sá Teeman nì Oomaar nì Seefoo nì Keenaasi

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: nì Kɔɔra nì Gatam nì Amaleeki. Bi nìn kóò Eedoom tiŋkin ní. Eesayuu nì u-nimpuu Ada jipɔŋkpiliu Eeliifaasi jipɔmbi dee.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Basemath's son Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
translation_verse: Eesayuu jipɔɔn Reewuyeel maaliŋu poon bin sá adican kpilibee yiŋŋi di sá Naati nì Seera nì Sama nì Miisa. Bi nìn kóò Eedoom ní ki sá Eesayuu nì u-nimpuu Basmaati naantiibi.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Eesayuu nimpuu Ooliibama, Ana bisal jipɔmbi bin sá adican kpilibee yiŋŋi di sá Yeewusi nì Yalaam nì Kɔɔra.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Eedoom yab dicaŋŋi kpilib dee, ní bi-kɔkɔ sá Eesayuu naantiibi.

english_verse: Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Bin nìn péé péé ki kāl̀ Eedoom tiŋkinee di sá uoorja Seeyiir naantiibi. Bi-yiŋŋi di sá Lootan nì Soobaal nì Siibeeyɔn nì Ana

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lootan jipɔmbi di sá Oori nì Eemam ní u-niisal sá Tiimina.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Soobaal jipɔmbi di sá Alfan nì Manaati nì Eebaal nì Seefoo nì Oonam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Siibeeyɔn jipɔmbi di sá Aya nì Ana. Ana gbanti di sá un dāa nìn ká dinyimbɔbil diba kuteeun ŋyunti ŋun u nìn bíi kpàá u-baa Siibeeyɔn mammuee.

english_verse: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
translation_verse: Ana jipɔɔn di sá Diisɔn ní u-bisal sá Ooliibama.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Diisan jipɔmbi di sá Eemidan nì Eesban nì Yitiran nì Keeran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Eeseer jipɔmbi di sá Biiliyan nì Saafan nì Yaakan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Diisan jipɔmbi di sá Usi nì Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Oori yab bin nìn sá adican kpilibee di sá Lootan nì Soobaal nì Siibeeyɔn nì Ana

english_verse: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, and they lived in the land of Seir.
translation_verse: nì Diisɔn nì Eeseer nì Diisan. Bíǹ di nìn sá Oori yab dicaŋŋi kpilib Seeyiir tiŋkin ki dī nì bi-dicaŋŋi nín sá puee.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Eesayuu maaliŋu poon bɔtiibi nì bi-naakɔti nì bi-timmu nì bi-yiŋŋi di sá Tiimina nì Aliwa nì Jeeteeti

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: nì Ooliibama nì Eela nì Piinɔn

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: nì Keenaasi nì Teeman nì Miibsaar

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: nì Magidiyeel nì Iram. Eedoom tiŋki bɔtiibi nín sá puee dee, ubɔti kamaa nì u-tiŋki kin pu u kóò ki yèe. Eesayuu di sá Eedoom yab naanja.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nìn kóò Kanaan tiŋkin laakin u-baa nìn kāl̀ee ní.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Ní uninjee bí-u yii: «Bi yíkì doo, di sá yaadalee m nìn gbìl̄ bi bíi lì yii: <Tí yīkìmaan doo kí nīn cá Dootan.>» Ní Jooseefi nín jì bi-boon Dootan ní ki tin ká-bi niin.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Bi-baa Isirayeel nìn néeń Jooseefi ki jítiǹ u-jipɔmbi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ, kun puee u nìn màl̄-u u-tikpiti poon ní. U nìn ŋáĺ-u dibɔkutimɔntiil diba.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: U-mambi nín dáań ki ká yii bi-baa néeń-u ki jítiǹ bíǹ kɔkɔee ní bi kíǹ ki ná-u kaa ti sòoǹ nì u an mɔ̄.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Dalbee Jooseefi dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ ní ki dūu máafì u-mambi. Niin ní kináŋ mɔ̄tìi nín pɔ́ɔkì.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: U tùkū-bi yii: «Ní pīlifìmaan kudamintiiu kun m dámintèe!

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: M dámintì yii ti bí kusaau ki bōob̀ amɔpin, ní man yal yáatìi yúl̀, ní nimbi mɔpiŋŋi māntìi tú man mɔpindi ní ki lítì di-taapu.»

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u-mambi kíí-u yii: «Mimmee a dàkafī yii sii di làá nīn sá ti-bɔtiu deeyaaa, àá sii di làá nīn sá ti-kpiliu ní timbi ń nīn bí sii taapu ní?» U-damintiiku gbanti nì u nín sòon̄ puee yāntì bi-náŋki mɔ̄tìi wíiǹ u-pu.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Boonee ní u gíti dámintì ní ki tí dūu máafì u-mambi yii: «M tí dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ. M dámintì yii ŋwìiń nì uŋmal nì iŋmalbijaa saalaa nì ubɔ dòoń ki gbàantí m-nimbiin.»

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Ní u dūu lī u-baa nì u-mambi cee, ní u-baa bíi wòoǹ-u yii: «Ba damintiiku kúǹ dee! Mimmee man nì a-na nì a-mambi làá dāá gbàan̄ sii nimbiinaaa?»

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Ní u-mambi mɔ̄tìi díkí u-pu, ama u-baa úǹ dū an bɔtee ki ŋá u-taalin. Jooseefi mambi dū-u ki nyáfì

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Jooseefi mambi búntì Siikeem tiŋkin kí kpàà bi-baa piii.

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel bí Jooseefi yii: «Kéè a-mambi bíń Siikeem ki kpàá ipiiyaa! Dāan̄ ḿ tɔ̄-si bi-cee.» Ní u kíí u-baa yii: «Too, m sɔ̀.»

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Ní u-baa bí-u yii: «Á cù kí kpèè yii a-mambi pɔ̄ɔ̄ɔɔ, bi-waŋkuti mun bí mana, kí gítiń kí tùkù-mi.» Eebrɔn tantakalin ní bi nìn bí ní Jooseefi baa tú-u ní u yíkìi búntì Siikeem tiŋkin u-mambi cee.

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: U búntèe ní ki bàn̄ ki tú ki yìiǹ tisatin ní uninja ubɔ dāa ká-u ní ki bālifì-u yii: «A nyàab̀ ba?»

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Ní u kíí-u yii: «M nyàab̀ m-mambi ní. M gbāam̀-si, a yaa nyí laakin bi bí ki kpàá bi-waŋkutee, á dàkà-mi.»

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Bi nín ká-u u páaǹní ndan kaa láá bāań-bee, ní bi sòon̄ ki bɔ́ntì yii bí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Bi nìn tùkù ki nàatī tɔb yii: «Kpèè tidamintiil daanee di dòońee.

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Rubeen gbìl̄ míǹ ki là kí fīī-u bi-ŋaanee ní ki lī yii: «Tí taa lēē u-maŋfal.»

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: U nìn bí-bi yii: «Ní taa kpɔ̀maan-u, ní dū-u kí tɔ̄ dilɔkɔgindi din bí kuteeun nee poon kí taa ŋá-u tiba.» U lī míǹ ki là yii bi yaa dū-u ki tɔ́ dilɔkɔgindinee, boonee úǹ ń dāá ŋá soooo kí nyāntí-u kí cáá-u kí kpìnnì kí tin tīī u-baa.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jooseefi bāań bi-ceeyee ní bi pēetì-u u-bɔkutimɔntiil din u pēēyee.

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Bi ŋá mimmee ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ ki bíi jīǹ tijin. Bi dāa kpēēyee, Isimaayeel naakookun yab di páń tɔb pu ki nyánní Galaadi tiŋkinee. Bi-gutaamui nìn tú ikpafi nì talaalub ní bi nìn cáa cáǹ Eejipiti kí nyāfì.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Ní Juuda bí u-nabiyaamu yii: «Ti yaa bál̀ ki kūū ti-naalee, ba ní ti páatì poon?

english_verse: Let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not harm him. After all, he is our brother.” And the others agreed.
translation_verse: Tí dū-u kí nyāfiǹ Isimaayeel yab kí taa kpɔ̀-u, kun puee u sá ti-nabiki, ní ti sá fatikubaanti.» Ní u-nabiyaamu gbìl̄ ki tīī nì u.

english_verse: When the Midianite merchants came by, Joseph's brothers took him out of the well, and for
translation_verse: Madiyan nyampoobi jītée ní bi nyántìń Jooseefi dilɔkɔgindi poon ní ki dū-u ki nyáfiǹ Isimaayeel yab. Bi nìn nyáfì-u animbil jitɔmbi mmuŋku ní, ní bíǹ cáá-u ki búntì Eejipiti.

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Rubeen dāa cūtì kí nyāntí Jooseefi dilɔkɔgindinee, u bàn̄ee u kpá, ní an wùn̄-u tikpil ní u dáaĺ tiwan tin u pēēyee ki cátì.

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: Ní u nín fàtī u-naalib cee ní ki bí-bi yii: «Jooseefi gíti kpá dilɔkɔgindin! Kin man làá ŋá m-ba la?»

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi kūū uŋɔja ní ki dū Jooseefi bɔkutil ki tɔ́ fatikun.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū dibɔkutimɔntiilee ki nākaǹ bí cáá tīī bi-baa kí lì yii: «Kpèè kun ti píińee, kpèè tiŋan yii an sá a-jipɔɔn bɔkutilaaa, an kaa sá?»

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Bi-baa fōō ki kpēē ki béè dibɔkutilee ní ki fáá mbiil yii: «M-biki Jooseefi bɔkutil dee! Upeecuncuti ubɔ cúú m-biki ki ŋmɔ́, Jooseefi ní an lafun cúú ki tɔ̄ntì!»

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jaakɔb dáaĺ tiwan tin u pēēyee ki cátì ki dū kutuku ki gbìn̄ u-caŋ, ní ki dū iwiin kupaau ki súń u-biki kpool.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: U-jipɔmbi nì u-bisalib kɔkɔ nìn pɔ́ɔǹ kí ŋméeǹ-u, ama ní waa kíí bí ŋméeǹ-u, ní ki lì yii: «M làá nīn pée sūǹ m-jipɔɔn kpool míǹ ní kí dāá kpú kí bà-u ditaŋkpiilin.» Míǹ ní Jooseefi baa lafun súń u-pu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee Madiyan yab bíǹ dūu bàn̄ Eejipiti ní ki mun nìkī Jooseefi ki nyáfiǹ Pootifaar, ujanjakpil un cí Faaroo cindee.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Juuda yíkì u-nabiyaamu cee ki búntì Adulaam tiŋkin kijapaai kiba cee, bi yíì-u yii Yiira.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Niin ní Juuda ká ukanaanja Suuwa bisal ki cáá ní u nì u kpáfì.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: Unimpuee cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki, ní Juuda pú-kì diyindi yii Eer.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Ní u fātìi tí cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Seera. Juuda nìn bí Keesiib tiŋkin ní u-nimpuu màl̄ kibiki gbanti.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Juuda jipɔŋkpiliu Eer wíiǹee ní u cáá unimpu ki tīī-u. Bi yíì unimpuee yii Taamaar.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Juuda jipɔŋkpiliu Eer nìn sá unikpiti ti-Dindaan nimbiin, an puee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì u kpíì.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Ní Juuda bí Oonan yii: «Fōō a-maan nimpuu ukpiipu kii mara nín pée sá puee, kí màal̀ kí téeǹ u-yil u-dicaŋku ń taa kúntí.»

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Ama Oonan nín nyí yii u-maan nimpuu biyaamu mun u làá màal̀ee kaa dāa sá u-biyaamuee, ní ŋyunti ŋun u yaa bíi dɔ̀ nì unimpuee ní u nyāntí ki féeń kitiŋ kaa là kí màal̀ kí téeǹ u-maan yil.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: An bɔtee kaa nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ti-Dindaan, ní u yāntì u mun kpíì.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Ní Juuda bí u-coopu Taamaar yii: «Cù a-baabi cee kí nīn kā dikpiipool ki cí ŋyunti ŋun m-jipɔɔn Seera mun làá dāá wíiǹee.» Di sá u nìn lī u-neen yii: «Seera mun ń taa kpú kii u-mambee.» Ní Taamaar nín kùǹ u-baabi.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: An dāa bàn̄ ŋyunti ŋubɔee ní Juuda nimpuu Suuwa bisal kpíì. Juuda kāl̀ dikpool jítèe ní u nì u-bɔɔ Yiira uadulaanja búntì Tiimina tiŋkin, bin bíi cēē u-piii kutee cee.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū Taamaar yii: «A-cooja cá Tiimina kí cā u-piii kuti.»

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u pēetì dikpiipool wanti tin u pēēyee ní ki dū ŋŋaabu ki bīiǹ u-nimbiin ki kpáaǹ u-wunti, ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ Eeniyayiim tiŋki sampuyakatii, laakin bi dì ki cá Tiimina tiŋkinee. Di sá u dáań ki ká yii Seera wíiǹ ní baa dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ-u ki tīī-u.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Juuda ká Taamaar kā nsampuyakatee ní u dākafì yii an sá kinimpulaakpaai, kun puee u nìn bīī tiwan u-nimbiin.

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Ní Juuda kíí-u yii: «M làá lēeń m-ŋɔcaŋkpuŋku poon diŋɔbil diba kí tīiń-si.» Ní unimpuee bí-u yii: «See á tīī-mi tiba ḿ yóoń m-cee toolima. A yaa láa tīiń-mi diŋɔbilee, á fōō a-wanti.»

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Ní Juuda bālifì-u yii: «Ba ní a là ḿ tīī-si á yóoń a-cee toolima?» Ní unimpuee bí-u yii: «Tīī-mi a-jaliiki kin a cáa nyìitēe nì ki-ŋmiiŋu nì ŋkpandɔ ŋun a ŋúb́ee». Ní Juuda tīī-u an wanti gbanti kɔkɔ ní ki dōoǹ nì u ní dipool kɔ́.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee fātìi nín kùǹ u-dumpu ní ki lēē ŋŋaabu ŋun u nìn dūu bīiǹee ní ki gíiǹ dikpiipool wanti ki pēeǹ.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Ní Juuda dū diŋɔbil ki tú u-bɔɔ uadulaanja ú cáá tīī unimpuee kí fōoń u-wanti tin u dūu yóoǹ u-cee toolimee. U-bɔɔ bàn̄ee ní kaa ká unimpuee.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ní u bālifì binib bin bí niinee yii: «Kinimpulaakpaai kin kàal̀ Eeniyayiim tiŋkin doo, nsan caŋinee bí la?» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Kinimpulaakpaai kiba pée kpá doo.»

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Ní Juuda bɔɔ gítì ki tùkū-u yii: «Maa ká-u, ní niin yab mun bí-mi yii: <Kinimpulaakpaai kiba pée kpá doo.>»

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Ní Juuda bí u-bɔɔ yii: «Yàntī ú nīn cáa cá. Tí taa dī tiwan gbanti boon icoo ń dāá cúú-ti. Kéè man tīī-si diŋɔbil á cáá tīī-u ní a cūnnì kaa ká-ueeee!»

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Iŋmal ita boonee ní bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Juuda yii: «A-coopu Taamaar ŋá tilaakpaal ki cáá dipool.» Ní Juuda bí yii: «Bí nyāntí-u kí cáá-u kí wà ŋŋmi.»

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi nyántì-u ki cáǹ kí wà ŋŋmee ní u tú bí tùkù u-cooja yii: «Tiwan tin m ŋúb́ nee, uninja un tīī-mi dipoolee di yì tiwan gbanti. M gbāam̀-si, kpèè kijalii kin bi cáa nyìitī tiwanee nì ki-ŋmiiŋu nì ŋkpandɔ nee, a nyí un yì tiwan gbanteeee?»

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Juuda béè tiwanee ní ki bí yii: «U cáá ibaamɔn ki jítiǹ man. An bàà sá ḿ dū-u kí tīī m-jipɔɔn Seera, ní maa ŋá míǹ». Ní Juuda kaa ti pée gbēē-u.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u bíi màal̀ee ní jaasibee kansikin ubɔ nyántìń u-ŋal, ní umatimmaanli dū gulfaman ki kúĺ, ní ki bí yii: «Un bí nee di péé ki nyáń.»

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Ní kibikee fātìi gíiǹ ki-ŋal ki kɔ́ǹ, ní ki-nabiki nyánní, ní umatimmaanli bí yii: «A ŋá mpɔn ki tùl̄ ki nyánnáa!» Ní bi pú-kì diyindi yii Peereesi, taapu di sá yii: <U tùl̄ ki nyáń.>

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Boonee ní u-nabiki kin ŋal bi bàà dū gulfaman ki kúĺee mun nyánní. Ní bi pú-kì diyindi yii Seera, taapu di sá yii: <Un jìl̀ee.>

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Isimaayeel yab cáá Jooseefi ki cūnnì Eejipitee ní Faaroo janjakpiliu Pootifaar, ueejipitija dá-u bi-cee. Pootifaar gbanti di nìn sá bin cí Faaroo cindee kpiliu.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Jooseefi kpiliu nìn dáań ki ká yii ti-Dindaan yú u-boon, ki yàntī tin kɔkɔ u ŋáańee cá nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: An puee Jooseefi nìn ká diyimɔɔl u-kpiliu cee u dū-u ki kpántì úǹ u-ba tɔntɔnliu, ní ki dū-u ki ŋá ukpil ú nīn kpèé u-cindi poon tuuŋŋi nì tin kɔkɔ u cááyee.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: U ká mimmee ní ki dū tikɔkɔ nì tikɔkɔ ki ŋá Jooseefi ŋaan kaa ti pée kpèé báà tiba, asee tijin tin u làá jēe baba pu ní u dàkafī. Jooseefi nì u-kpiliu nimpuu bɔti Jooseefi nìn yáà unil ní ki nìn ŋān̄ unaacimpɔɔn an kaa cáá bí lì.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: An dāa bāań ŋyunti ŋubɔee ní u-kpiliu nimpuu dū u-nimbiliŋ ki mántì u-pu ní ki bí-u yii: «Dāan̄ kí dòon̄ nì mi.»

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Ní u yíì, ní ki bí u-kpiliu nimpuu yii: «Kpèè, man ní m-kpiliu dū dicindi tundi kɔkɔ ki ŋúbiǹ. U cáá m-pu dimákal, an puee waa ti kpèé tiba dicindi poon.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa jítiǹ-mi dicindi nee poon. U pú-mi nsan ḿ ŋá tikɔkɔ, asee sii baba ní maa máaǹ kí gbēē, kun puee a sá u-nimpuu. An puee maa ŋūǹ kí ŋá ikpitikpaan gbanti kí yìntīǹ Unimbɔti.»

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Baabadal unimpuee pée páb̀ Jooseefi ní yii ú dòon̄ nì u, ama ní úǹ kaa pílifíǹ-u.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Dalbee Jooseefi kɔ́ kudii poon ki bíi tūǹ ditundi báà ubɔ nì ubɔ kpá.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Niinee ní unimpuee cúú Jooseefi bɔkutil ní ki bí-u yii: «Dòon̄ nì mi!» Ní Jooseefi sáǹ ki nyáń mmɔŋki ki yāntì u-bɔkutil unimpuee ŋaan.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: ní u yíiń dicindin nib, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Dāá kpèèmaan! Bi cáań-ti ueebruja ú nīn cáá-ti ki gbíilíǹ ní! U dɔ́miń kí bàà dòon̄ nì man dee ní m fáá mbiil.

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: U nín gbìl̄ m fáá mbiilee ní u sáǹ ki nín nyēē ki fá u-bɔkutil.»

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Ní u dū Jooseefi bɔkutilee ki bíl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ u-ba u-cal ń bàń.

english_verse: Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me!
translation_verse: U-cal Pootifaar dāa bāańee ní u gíiǹ ki téeǹ míǹ mbaantiim yii: «Ueebruja uyumbu un a cáań-tee dɔ́miń kí dòon̄ nì mi.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun m fáá mbiilee ní u sáǹ ki fá u-bɔkutil m-cee.»

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Ní u yāntì bi cúú Jooseefi ki cáa tɔ́ sarka laakin ubɔti nìn pìintí bin yīntiǹ-uee. Jooseefi bí sarka Jooseefi kpántì usarkadaan.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan nìn yú Jooseefi boon sarkan, ki dàkā-u u-ŋanti ní ki yāntì u ká diyimɔɔl ujanjakpil un kpèé bisarkadambee cee.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Ujanjakpilee nìn dū bisarkadambi kɔkɔ ní ki ŋúbiǹ Jooseefi. Úǹ di nìn kpèé atuun ŋin kɔkɔ bi nìn tūǹee.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Ujanjakpilee kaa nìn gíti kpèé atuun ŋin u nìn dūu ŋúbiǹ Jooseefee, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn yú Jooseefi boon ní ki yàntī u-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ còom̄-u tiŋan.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: Ní u yāntì bi cáá-bi ki pīiǹ sarka ujanjakpil un kpèé u-sarkadambee cee, laakin bi nìn pīiǹ Jooseefee.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Ní ujanjakpilee lēē Jooseefi ú nīn bí bi-cee ki tútúǹ-bi atuun. Bi nìn yúntì sarka poon ŋwaam. Jooseefi lēē bisarkadambi bili damintiiti taapu

english_verse: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
translation_verse: Bi bí sarkan niin ní kunyeeu kubɔee, un pūul̀ Eejipiti bɔtiu kpɔnɔbee nì un bàtī ndaam ki tìì-uee liitil dámintì, báà ŋma nì u-damintiiku nì ku-taapu.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe Jooseefi dɔ́miń bi-cee ní ki ká yii an kaa mɔ̄ǹ-bi.

english_verse: and he asked, “Why are you so worried today?”
translation_verse: Ní u bālifì-bi yii: «Ba ŋá ní ni kā míǹ díǹ an kaa mɔ̄ǹ-ni ní?»

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Ti dámintì ní ubɔ kaa bí kí tùkù-ti taapu.» Ní Jooseefi bí-bi yii: «Unimbɔti di kaa tùkù tidamintiil taapuɔɔɔ? Míǹ puee māafìmaan-mi ni nín dámintì puee.»

english_verse: The king's personal servant told Joseph, “In my dream I saw a vine
translation_verse: Ní bin bàtī ndaam ki tìì ubɔtee kpiliu máafì Jooseefi u-damintiiku yii: «M dámintì yii busubu bun bi yíì fiinyee di yú m-nimbiin,

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: ki cáá apan ata. Ní busubuee púkuḿ ki lòon̄ abil ní abil mántì.
