english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Ní m ŋúb́ Faaroo sambinyɔkaaki m-ŋaan, ki kītì fiinyi biliŋee ki ŋmáaḿ ŋi-nyim ki ŋá Faaroo sambinyɔkaakin ní ki dūu tīī-u.»

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí-u yii: «A-damintiiku taapu sèé. Asupan atee, taapu sá iwiin ita.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: An kíǹ iwiin ita Faaroo làá nyāntí-si sarkan kí gíiǹ a-tundi kí ŋúbíǹ-si, ní á tīī-u tinyɔkaal kii a nín nìn pée kpààa tìì-u puee.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Ama m gbāam̀-si, bi yaa fātìi fōō-si ní a-pɔbil sɔ̄ŋkèe, a mun ń téetí kí ŋá-mi tiniti kí sòoǹ m-bɔti kí tùkù Faaroo kí nyāntí-mi sarka nee poon.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Di sá yii bi cúuń-mi mpɔn ní Eebru yab tiŋkin. Doo nee muee, maa ti ŋá tiba ní bi dū-mi ki tɔ́ sarka.»

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Bin pūul̀ ubɔti kpɔnɔbee kpiliu nín ká yii Jooseefi tùkū u-bɔɔ u-damintiiku taapu an ŋān̄ee, ní u mun bí Jooseefi yii: «Ma mun dámintì yii bikpɔnɔmɔntiibi tikabiti tita ŋɔ́kɔ́ tɔb pu ní m tú.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Ní kukabiku kun tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee poonee, bikpɔnɔmɔntiibi bin kɔkɔ ubɔti ŋmóòyee kā, ní inoon dòoń ki jīǹ an kpɔnɔbee m-yil pu.»

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí-u yii: «Kpèè, a-damintiiku taapu sèé. Tikabiti titee, taapu di sá iwiin ita.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: An kíǹ iwiin ita Faaroo làá nyāntí-si sarkan, kí lēē a-yil, kí cáá a-wunti kí lúntí ndɔ pu, ní inoon ń dāá jī a-nanti.»

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Iwiin ita dalee, an dūu ŋmāntiǹ Faaroo maaliwiiŋŋu jiŋaaliu, ní u yíiń u-tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ jiŋaal. U yāntì bi nyántì bin bàtī ndaam ki tìì-uee kpiliu nì bin pūul̀-u kpɔnɔbee kpiliu ki cáań u-tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_verse: He put the personal servant back in his old job
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo gíiǹ bin bàtī ndaam ki tìì-uee kpiliu tundi ki ŋúbiǹ-u, ní úǹ bātì ndaam ki tīī-u.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Ama ní u yāntì bi dū bin pūul̀-u kpɔnɔbee kpiliu ki lúntì ndɔ pu, kii Jooseefi nín nìn tùkū-bi bi-damintiiti taapu puee.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Abin ali boonee ní Faaroo dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ, yii u yú dimɔɔl din bi yíì Niilee caŋin.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: U yú mimmee ní ki ká inasal iluli, i bí màlmal ki ŋān̄, ki nyánní dimɔɔlee poon ki yú digbándi ki ŋmóò timool.

english_verse: Then seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river and
translation_verse: Boonee ní nnagɔŋgɔmu ŋkpiimu mululi mun nyánní dimɔɔl gbantin ki páaǹní in béeyee boon ki dɔ́miń ki yú ki kɔ́ĺ-i dimɔɔgbandi.

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: Ní nnagɔŋgɔmu ŋkpiimuee dū inasal in bí màlmal ki ŋān̄ee ki nátì. Niinee ní Faaroo cúu fīntì.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Faaroo fātìi gèen̄ ní ki gíti tí dámintì yii idifin iluli in nyìm̀ ki ŋān̄ee túuń dikakabaantiil pu.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: U kpēēyee ní ki ká ndifiŋkpiimu mululi mun ugbuŋkoon fáá mu fáaḿee nyáń ki kútì idifin in béeyee pu.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Ní ndifiŋkpiimu mun fáaḿee dū idifin in nyìm̀ ki ŋān̄ee ki nátì. Niinee ní Faaroo tí cúu fīntì ní ki ká yii an sá kudamintiiu.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ubɔti pɔbil bíil̀, ní u tú bi yíiń Eejipiti tiŋki poon bibɔɔbi nì biciŋfitiibi kɔkɔ. Bi bāańee ní ubɔti kàan̄ u nín dámintì puee ki tùkū-bi, ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa ŋúń ki lēē taapu ki tùkū-u.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bin bàtī ndaam ki tìì Faarooyee kpiliu bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa, diyìntil din m yīntèe, m làá bìitī di-pu díǹ.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Di sá dalbee, a nìn fōō timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi pu diŋuul ki cáá man nì bin pūul̀-si kpɔnɔbee kpiliu ki tɔ́ sarkan ujanjakpil un kpèé a-sarkadambee dumpu.

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: Man nì u nìn dámintì kunyabaantiiu poon ní báà ŋma nì u-damintiiku nì ku-taapu.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Ti nì ueebrunaacimpɔɔn ubɔ nìn bí sarkan niin, u sá ujanjakpil yumbuu. Úǹ ní ti nìn kàan̄ ti-damintiiti ki tùkū ní u lēē báà ŋma damintiiku taapu nín sá puee ki tùkū-u.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: U nín tùkū-ti ti-damintiiti taapu puee, míǹ ní an jítì. A fātìi gíiǹ ditundi din m nìn pée tūǹee ki ŋúbiǹ-mi, ní ki yāntì bi lúntì bin pūul̀ a-kpɔnɔbee kpiliu ndɔ pu.» Jooseefi lēē Faaroo damintiiti taapu

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Faaroo tú bi yíiń Jooseefi. Ní bi nyántì-u kusarkadiin malaa, ní u kōol̀ ki kpántì u-wampeeŋkaati ní ki nín cá ubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: U bàn̄ Faaroo ceeyee ní Faaroo bí-u yii: «M dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ ní báà ubɔ kaa ŋúń ki tùkū-mi ku-taapu. Ama m gbìl̄ yii bi yaa kàan̄ kudamintiiu ki tùkū-see, a ŋūǹ kí lēē ku-taapu.»

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi kíí Faaroo yii: «An kaa sá man di ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiba, Unimbɔti di làá tùkù-si a-damintiiku taapu ní án sɔ̀ŋkì a-pɔbil.»

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bí Jooseefi yii: «M dámintì yii m yú dimɔɔgbandi ní.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: M yúee ní ki ká inasal iluli, i bí màlmal ki ŋān̄, ki nyánní dimɔɔlin ki dɔ́miń ki yú digbándi ki ŋmóò timool.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Boonee ní nnagɔŋgɔmu ŋkpiimu mululi páaǹní. Doooo nee, maa láá pée ká nnakpiimu míǹ Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poon ki ká.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Ní a yaa ká-iee, aa lì yii i náĺ tiba gba. I nín pée bí pu ŋgɔŋgɔmu ŋkpiimu puee, míǹ ní i gbíntìi bí. Ní m cúu fīntì.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Boonee ní m gíti dámintì yii didikakabaantiil di lòon̄ idifin iluli ní i nyìm̀ ki ŋān̄.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Ní ndifiŋkpiimu mululi mun ugbuŋkoon fáá mu fáaḿee mun nyáń ki kútì idifin ipeekaayee pu.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: M yúee ní ndifiŋkpiimuee dū idifin in nyìm̀ ki ŋān̄ee ki nátì. M kàan̄ míǹ ki tùkū bibɔɔbi, ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa ŋúń ki béè taapu ki tùkū-mi!»

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí Faaroo yii: «Ti-baa, a-damintiitee liitil pée sá kudamintibaantiiu ní. Unimbɔti di là kí dàkà ubɔti tin u là kí ŋée.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Inasal iluli in ŋān̄ee, taapu di sá abin aluli, ní idifin in ŋān̄ee mun taapu sá abin aluli. Niin sá kudamintibaantiiu ní.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Nnagɔŋgɔmu ŋkpiimu mululi mun páaǹní ipeekaayee boonee, taapu di sá abin aluli mun. Ní ndifiŋkpiimu mululi mun ugbuŋkoon fáá mu fáaḿee taapu sá ŋkùm abin aluli.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Kii m nín bàà tùkū ubɔti puee, Unimbɔti di lēē min u là kí ŋée ki dàkā-u.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Tijin làá gbí Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poon abin aluli.

english_verse: when the king made him governor, and he went everywhere for the king.
translation_verse: Boonee ŋkùm làá nyā abin aluli. Binib dāa súntí gba yii tijin nìn gbí Eejipiti tiŋkin, kun puee ŋkùmee làá dāá nàan̄ Eejipiti tiŋki ní.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Ŋkùm gbanti nín dāa pɔ̄ɔ̄ puee dāa yàntī binib kaa dāa gíti nyí yii digbíl diba nìn kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Ti-baa, a nín dámintì kudamintibaantiiu mili kɔkɔ nee dàkà yii Unimbɔti làá lafun ŋá min u bɔ́ntì kí ŋée, án kaa làá ti yúntí.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: An puee, ti-baa Faaroo, á kpèè kí nyàab̀ unil un cáá dinyil nì iciinee kí dū-u kí kàan̄ tikpiti Eejipiti tiŋki pu.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Ti-baa, an ŋān̄ á kàan̄ bikpilib biba Eejipiti timmu poon, binib yaa kùn̄ tikpaajin digbíl biŋŋi alulee poonee, bí cúú yàkatī miŋmoo pu ní bikpilibee ń lēē diba pu kí dūú kpāafì cakalaabi poon.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Á yóoń mara yii Eejipiti tiŋki kamaa poonee, bí kóoǹ digbíl biŋŋi alulee jinti kɔkɔ kí kpāfì, kí dūú kpāafì ní tikɔkɔ ń nīn bí a-taapu.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: An jintee ń nīn yú míǹ, ŋkùm biŋŋi alulee yaa láa bāańee, bí dāá dūú fīī kitiŋ pu nib ŋkùm ń taa láa kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi.» Bi kāaǹ Jooseefi tikpiti

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin Jooseefi sòon̄ee mɔ́ɔkiǹ Faaroo nì u-naacimbi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bí-bi yii: «Ti ŋūǹ ki gíti ká unil ubɔ u cáá Unimbɔti Fam ki bí kii kijapaai neeee?»

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí Jooseefi yii: «Sii ní Unimbɔti dàkā tin bí nee kɔkɔ, ŋma di gíti bí ki cáá iciin ki nyí ki jítiǹ sii!

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Sii di kíǹ ki yì man samaau. A yaa lī puee, míǹ ní m-timbundi kɔkɔ nib làá pīlifiǹ-si kí ŋá. Man nín sá ubɔtee baba ní m jítiǹ-si.»

english_verse: You are now governor of all Egypt!”
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo gíti bí Jooseefi yii: «M dū Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ ki ŋá a-ŋaan.»

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: U lī mimmee ní ki fúutì u-bɔmbiki ki dūu fúuń Jooseefi ŋambiki ki pēeǹ-u dibɔkutimɔntiil ní ki léeǹ-u sindaariya léeŋkaati.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo yāntì Jooseefi kɔ́ u-tɔrɔkuliliitiu poon, ní binib līī ki tátí yii: «Ní gbàam̄maan!» Míǹ ní Faaroo nìn kāaǹ Jooseefi ú nīn kpèé Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bí Jooseefi yii: «Man di sá Faaroo, Eejipiti bɔtikpaaŋwu. Ama sii yaa kaa pú kinyɔkɔee, báà unil kpá kí ŋá tiba nì tiba Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poon.»

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo páaǹ Jooseefi diyindi yii Safnati-Paneeya, ní ki dū Pootifeera un sá utandaan Ooni tiŋkinee bisal Asinaati ki tīī-u u cáá. Boonee, Jooseefi yìin̄ ki māntì Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Digbíl biŋŋi alulee poonee, tijin nìn lòon̄ tikpil.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi kūliŋkì digbíl biŋŋi alulee poon tijin tin kɔkɔ bí Eejipitee nì ti-nyɔkɔm ki yóoǹ Eejipiti timmun. Kitiŋ kamaa poonee, u nìn kóoǹ tijin tin bi cáń tisatinee ki kpáafì.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Jooseefi nìn kūliŋkì tijin tikpil tikpil ki kpáafì an wīikí kii tiŋku gbandi bul nín dɔ̄ puee. Baa nìn gíti bíi ŋmàntī-tì gba, kun puee an kaa nìn bí ŋkaan.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī ŋkùm biŋŋi alulee ń bàńee, Pootifeera un nìn sá utandaan Ooni tiŋkinee bisal Asinaati nìn màl̄ Jooseefi mbininjabiyaamu muli.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi pú kikpilii diyindi yii Manasee, di sá u nìn lī yii: «Unimbɔti yāntì m súntì m-gìńdi nì m-baa cindi kɔkɔ pu.»

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Ní u pú kililiitii diyindi yii Eefiraayiim, di sá u nìn lī yii: «Unimbɔti pú-mi mmaal kitiŋ kin poon m jíń falaayee.»

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Abin aluli ŋin poon digbíl kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee yuntiŋu sāā.

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: Ŋkùm biŋŋi aluli ŋin bɔti Jooseefi nìn sòon̄ee kíĺ ki bíi dòoń. Ŋkùm nìn jéetì ntimu kɔkɔn, ama tijin nìn bí Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní Eejipiti yab jinti dāa dóò ŋkùm nyáń kitiŋ puee ní bi kíǹ ki sūǹ Faaroo cee ki nyàab̀ tijin. Ní Faaroo bí-bi yii: «Ní cùú ká Jooseefi, u yaa lī puee ní ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Ŋkùm nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poon. Jooseefi nìn pīitì cakalaabi kɔkɔ ní ki nyáfiǹ Eejipiti yab tijin, di sá ŋkùm nìn mɔ̄tìi bíi pɔ́ɔkí ki cá Eejipiti tiŋki poon.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Ntimu kɔkɔ nib nìn dòoń Eejipiti ní ki dāā tijin Jooseefi cee, kun puee ŋkùm nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jaakɔb gbìl̄ yii tijin bí Eejipitee, ní u bí u-jipɔmbi yii: «Ni kā ki kpèé tɔb míǹ an dāá kúntíǹ yii ba ní?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: M gbìl̄ yii tijin bí Eejipiti. Míǹ puee cùmaan kí dāń kí cáań tí jī kí ŋmátí, kí taa kpú ŋkùm.»

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jooseefi mambi saalaayee yíkìi búntì Eejipiti kí cùú dāń tijin.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Ama Jaakɔb kaa nìn yāntì Jooseefi naal Beenjameen táá u-mambi ki cūtì, di sá u nìn fàŋkí yii án taa ŋée tiba ń tin ŋá-u.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb jipɔmbi nì bijindaliibi biba mun dūu bàn̄ Eejipiti tiŋkin kí dā tijin, kun puee ŋkùm nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ Kanaan tiŋkin. Jooseefi sòon̄ nì u-mambi nì inimbinaakulim

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Jooseefi di nìn sá gɔmina Eejipiti tiŋki poon. Úǹ di nìn yàntī bi nyáfíǹ kitiŋ gbanti kɔkɔ nib tijin. Jooseefi mambi bāańee ní ki gbāaǹ u-nimbiin.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jooseefi téetì u nín nìn dámintì u-mambi pu kudamintiiu kuŋyee ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ni sá bicɔŋkiliibi ní. Ni dɔ́miń kí cɔ̄ŋkì ti-tiŋki kí dáań kí cúú ki-wɔfii laŋki ní.»

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Aayee, ukpil, timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi dɔ́miń kí dā tijin ní.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Timbi kɔkɔ sá unibaanti biyaamu ní, ki sá bibulcinnib. Timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi kaa sá bicɔŋkiliibi.»

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi fātìi bí-bi yii: «An kaa sá ibaamɔn, ni dɔ́miń kí kpèè ti-tiŋki kí béé ki-wɔfii laŋki ní.»

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Ní bi fātìi kíí-u yii: «Timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi sá binib saalaa nì bili ní, ubaatibaanti biyaamu, ní ki nyánní Kanaan tiŋkin. Ti-joolkaau bí ti-baa cee díǹ pu nee, ama ti-nabiki kiba wáŋkì.»

english_verse: Joseph replied: It's like I said. You're spies,
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí-bi yii: «M nín pée lī puee, míǹ dee. Ni lafun sá bicɔŋkiliibi ní.

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: M nín làá ŋá pu kí béé yii ni-bɔti nee sá ibaamɔn àá an kaa sée di sá, nì Faaroo yindi puee, ni yaa kaa cáań ni-naal ujoolkaayee doo, ni kpá kí nyā kitiŋ nee poon.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Ní lēē ni-kansikin ubɔ kí tɔ̄ ú cùú cáań ni-naal, ní nimbi bin kíǹee ń nīn bí sarkan. Min ní m làá lafun béé yii ni-bɔti nee sá ibaamɔnaaa, an kaa sée dee. An yaa kaa sá ibaamɔnee, nì Faaroo yindi puee, ni sá bicɔŋkiliibi ní.»

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi dū bi-kɔkɔ ki tɔ́ sarkan iwiin ita.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Ŋwintataati dalee ní u bí-bi yii: «Ní ŋámaan min m làá dàkà-ni nee kí ŋmátí, di sá yii Unimbɔti ní man fàŋkí.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Ni yaa lafun sá bibulcinnibee, ní yàntī ni-kansikin ubɔ ń gbíntí sarkan doo nee, bin kíǹee ń yòon̄ tijin kí cáá kpíiǹ ni-dicaŋŋi yab bí taa kpú ŋkùm.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Boonee ní cáań-mi ni-naal ujoolkaayee ní ḿ ŋmā kí béé yii ni-bɔti tin ni sòoǹ nee sá ibaamɔn, ní ní ŋmátí kí taa kpú.» Ní bi kíí ki ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíǹ ki sòoǹ nì tɔb yii: «Tiŋman, ikpiti in ti ŋá ti-nabikee pu ní ditafadaaldi din bí nee lítì ti-pu nee. Di sá ti nìn ká kunimbaau kun nìn bí u-pɔbil poon ŋyunti ŋun u nìn bí ki gbàam̄-ti yii tí pée sɔ̄ u-saayee, ama ní ti nìn yíì kaa pílifiǹ-u. Kɔŋkɔnnee an nimbaaku kubaantiiu di bāań ti mun nee.»

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Ní Rubeen bí-bi yii: «Maa nìn pée tùkū-ni yii ní taa ŋá kibiki gbanti tikpitil ní ni yíì kaa pílifiǹ-maaa? Too u-fatikuu kpuulool di lítì ti-pu díǹ nee.»

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Baa nìn nyí yii Jooseefi gbìl̀ tin bi sòoǹee, kun puee u yaa nìn sòoǹee, ubɔ di nìn nàatī-bi.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi yíkìi kākatì ki wāatì-bi ki cūtìi súń. Jaakɔb jipɔmbi gítì Kanaan tiŋkin Boonee ní u fātìń bi-cee ki gíti sòon̄ nì bi ní ki lēē bi-kansikin Simeeyɔn, ki bóob́-u ŋŋmii bi-kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí lēē tijin kí fúuń u-mambi kɔkɔ kutukubin an gbí, kí gíiǹ báà ŋma nimbiliŋ kí ŋá u-kutukuun, kí tīī-bi tijin tin bi làá nīn jīǹ nsannee. Ní bi ŋá míǹ ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Ní bi bóob́ bi-jinti ki túǹ bi-mammu ní ki yíkìi nín kùǹ.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ laaba kunyeeu mɔ́ bi làá dòon̄ee, bi-kansikin ubɔ gútì u-kutukuu kí lēē tijin kí tīī u-maŋkee, ki ká u-nimbiliŋ u-kutukuu nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Ní u bí u-nabiyaamu yii: «Kpèèmaan, bi gíiǹ man nimbiliŋ ki ŋá m-kutukuun!» Niinee ní bi-kɔkɔ pɔbiliŋ máĺ, bi-wunti bíi jìkì ní bi kíǹ ki lì tɔb yii: «Ba ní Unimbɔti ŋá-ti mimmee?»

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ bi-baa Jaakɔb cee Kanaan tiŋkinee ní ki máafì-u tin jítèe kɔkɔ.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Ní ti kíí-u yii: <Timbi sá bibulcinnib ní, taa sá bicɔŋkiliibi.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Ti nìn sá binib saalaa nì bili ní ki pēē baa. Ama ti-nabiki kiba wáŋkì, ní ti-naal un jóol̀ dibiil puee bí mmɔŋki ti-baa cee Kanaan tiŋkin.>

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Niinee ní kitiŋee kpiliu fātìi bí-ti yii: <Min ní ni làá ŋá ní ḿ béé yii ni sá bibulcinnibee di sá ní yàntī ni-nabiki kiba ń gbíntí m-cee doo, ní nimbi bin kíǹee ń yòon̄ tijin min nyɔkɔm làá bà ní tin kpíiǹ ni-dicaŋŋee kí nīn kùǹ.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Boonee ní cáań-mi ni-naal un jóol̀ dibiil puee, ní ḿ ŋmā kí béé yii naa sá bicɔŋkiliibi, ama ni sá bibulcinnib. Niinee ní ḿ dāá gíiǹ ni-nabiki kí tīī-ni, ní ní tɔ̄ ni-ba kitiŋ nee poon.>»

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Bi nín bíi kpáatí tijin bi-kutukub poonee, ní bi-kɔkɔ ká bi-nimbiliŋ kā nlɔbiyaamun bi-kutukub poon. Bi nì bi-baa nín ká bi-nimbiliŋ nlɔbiyaamunee ní tifaandi kɔ́-bi.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Ní bi-baa Jaakɔb bí-bi yii: «Ni làá yàntī ḿ nīn kā kí taa ti nín̄ cáá mbiyaamuɔɔ! Jooseefi kaa ti bí, Simeeyɔn kaa ti bí, ní ni là kí fōō Beenjameen mun m-cee! Tikɔkɔ fātìi lítì man pu ní nee!»

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Rubeen bí u-baa yii: «Dū-u kí ŋúbíǹ-mi, m làá gíiǹní-u kí tīī-si. M yaa kaa gíiǹní-u ki tīī-see, a ŋūǹ kí kpɔ̀ man bininjabiyaamu liitil.»

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb kíí yii: «M-biki kpá kí nóó-ni kí cù. U-maan kpíì an kíǹ úǹ baba ní. Ni yaa búntì ní tiba yaa tin ŋá-u nsannee, ni làá yàntī man nì m-yikpipinti nee, ḿ kpú nì kunimbaau.»

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Ŋkùm nìn mɔ̄tìi bíi pɔ́ɔkí Kanaan tiŋkin.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Bi nín jíń tijin tin bi dánní Eejipitee ki dóòyee, ní Jaakɔb bí u-jipɔmbi yii: «Ní gítímaan kí cùú dāń-ti tijin.»

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Ama a yaa yíì yii tí taa kpáaǹ-uee, ti mun kaa làá cù, kun puee uninjee baasii tùkū ki cántì-ti ní yii: <Ni yaa kaa cáań ni-naal, m gíti kpá kí fōō-ni.>»

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bí yii: «Nimbi di ŋá-mi míǹ. Ba pu ní ni bàà tùkū-u yii ni gíti cáá naal ubɔ ní?»

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Uninjee di páb́-ti ki bālifì ti nì ti-dicaŋku poon bɔti yii: <Ni-baa báaa? Ni gíti cáá naal ubɔɔɔ?> Tin u bālifèe ní ti kíí-u. Taa ŋūǹ kí béé yii u làá lì yii tí cáań ti-naalaa!»

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Ní Juuda bí-u yii: «M-baa, dū Beenjameen kí kpàan̄ man tí yīkì kí cùú cáań tijin tí jī kí ŋmátí. Tí taa nín̄ kā míǹ, timbi nì sii nì ti-biyaamu kɔkɔ ń dāá kpú ŋkùm.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Tin kɔkɔ yaa láa bāań u-puee, man fōō ki ŋá m-ba, á dāá bàlifì-mi. M yaa kaa gíiǹní-u ki ŋúbiǹ-see, ḿ nīn pée sá ukpiti a-cee kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Ti yaa kaa bàà bíil̀ ŋyuntee, naŋkɔnampu ti bàà gítìmaan mili mili ki cáań tijin.»

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Ní bi-baa kíí-bi yii: «Too, an nín sá yii míǹ ní tí pée ŋée, ni nín làá ŋá puee sɔ̀. Ní nyàab̀maan ti-tiŋki doo wammɔntiiti tiba kii talaalub nì ikpafi nì tisiil, nì asubil ŋin bi yíì piistaasi nì amandee kí cùnnì kí pɔ̄ uninja gbanti.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Ní ŋúb́ animbil mili pu kí fàtīí gíiǹ ŋin bi nìn dūu ŋá ni-kutukubinee kí tīī-bi. An yaa yíì, an nìn ŋá-bi inaatuu ní.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Ní yīkìmaan kí kpáaǹ ni-naal kí nīn gítí uninjee cee.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan ń yàntī uninjee ń tin sɔ̄ ni-saai kí yàntī Beenjameen nì Simeeyɔn ń nóó-ni kí fàtīń. An yaa kíǹ mamee, m làá nīn pée kā kii maa pée màl̄ ki kée ní.» Jooseefi sòon̄ nì u-mambi nliliitiim

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi bɔ́ntì tiwampɔkaal ní ki yōoǹ animbil mili pu, ki kpáaǹ Beenjameen ki nín cá Eejipiti ki tin bàn̄ ki kɔ́ ki yúl̀ Jooseefi nimbiin.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jooseefi ká Beenjameen nóoń-bee ní u bí u-tɔntɔŋkpiliu yii: «Cáá binib nee kí cùnnì m-dumpu kí kpɔ̀ kuwaŋkuluu kubɔ kí ŋá tijin, di sá yii man nì bi di làá jī ŋwiimpu nee.»

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Ní uninjee cáá-bi ki cūnnì Jooseefi dumpu kii Jooseefi nín bí yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ ki làá kɔ́ Jooseefi dumpuee ní tifaandi kɔ́-bi, ní bi bíi lì yii: «Ti nín nìn péé péé ki dɔ́miń bi gíiǹ animbil ŋin ki ŋá ti-kutukubinee, an pu ní bi cáań-ti doo kí sàaǹ-ti án bà-ti, kí fōō ti-mammu ní kí dū-ti kí ŋá iyumbu.»

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Bi làá kɔ́ee, ní ki sútì ki pìl̄ Jooseefi tɔntɔŋkpiliuee kipunyɔkɔpu ki sòon̄ nì u.

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lī yii: «Ti gbāam̀-si, ukpil! Ti nìn pée dɔ́miń doo ki dá tijin.

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: Ti nìn fàtīi kùǹ ki bàn̄ laaba kunyeeu mɔ́ ti làá dòon̄ ki gútì ti-kutukubee, báà ŋma nimbiliŋ nì ŋi-nyɔkɔm kā u-kutukuun. An puee ti fātìi gíiǹní animbil gbanti.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Ti gíti ŋúbiń animbil aba mun kí dā tijin. Di sá taa nyí un di yaa nìn dū ti-nimbiliŋ ki gíiǹ ki ŋá ti-kutukubinee.»

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔŋkpilee kíí-bi yii: «Yàntīmaan ni-pɔbiliŋ ń nīn sɔ̀m̀, ní taa fàŋkì tiba. An sá ni-Nimbɔtiu, ni-baa Nimbɔtiu di dū tigaajati ki ŋá ni-kutukubin. Ni-nimbiliŋee nìn kɔ́ m-ŋaan.» U sòon̄ nì bi míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki cūtìi nyántìń Simeeyɔn ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔŋkpilee cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ Jooseefi dumpu, ki tīī-bi nnyim bi fíntì bi-taaŋi, ní ki tīī bi-mammu timool.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Ní bi bɔ́ntì tiwampɔkaal tin bi cáań kí pɔ̄ Jooseefee ki yóoǹ kí wàatī ú nín bàń kuwiŋkuluu, kun puee bi nìn gbìl̄ yii niin ní bi làá jī tijin.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jooseefi bāań mmɔŋkee, ní bi yōoǹní bi-wampɔkaati ki cūtì u-cee ki gbāaǹ u-nimbiin ní ki dūu tīī-u.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi jáam̀-bi ki bālifì bi-gbampɔŋŋu pu, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ni-baa utikpil un bɔti ni nìn sòon̄ m-ceeyee pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋanaaa? U gbíntìi dáá bí dimaŋfalinaaa?»

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Iiin, a-tɔntɔnliu ti-baa pée pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní. U dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin.» Bi lī mimmee ní ki fātìi tí gbāaǹ u-nimbiin.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Jooseefi yáatì ki ká Beenjameen, u-naal u nì un pēē dinabiilee ní ki bí yii: «Ni-naal ujoolkaa un bɔti ni nìn sòon̄ nì mee sɔ̀ɔɔ?» Ní ki gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Unaacimpɔɔn, Unimbɔti ń bìin̄ a-boon.»

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Jooseefi nín ká u-naal mimmee, ní an kɔ́-u tikpil ní waa ti ŋūǹ kí cúú u-ba nnyinnyim ń taa nyā, ní u ŋá malaa ki kɔ́ u-diikun ki súń.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: U súń ki dóò ki fíntì u-nimbiin ki nyánnée, ní ki cúú u-ba ní ki bí yii bí yóoń-bi tijin.

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Ní bi gāntì Jooseefi sambil di-ba ní ki gāntì u-nabiyaamu bi-ba ní ki gāntì Eejipiti yab bin dɔ́miń kí jēe mun bi-ba. Di sá yii Eejipiti yab kaa nìn ŋūǹ bi nì Eebru yab ń kpāfìí jī disambibaantiilin. An nìn sá Eejipiti yab cee dikoobil ní.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Ní bi kāaǹ Jooseefi nabiyaamu u-nimbiin ki túĺ-u, bi kā ki dī tɔb ki nóó nì bi nín kpíǹ tɔb puee, ki kíĺ ujipɔŋkpil ki tin kátì un jóol̀ dibiil puee, ní bi kā ki kpèé tɔb, ní an ŋá-bi bitii.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi yāntì bi lēē tijin tin bi ŋá ki tɔ́kɔǹ u-nimbiinee ki yākatì-bi. Bi nín yākatì báà ŋma tijin miŋyee, u yāntì bi tīī Beenjameen míǹ miŋmoo pu ní. Ní bi nì Jooseefi jíń ki nyùn̄ ndaam ki bál̀ ní an nyāatì-bi.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Á dū m-sambinyɔkaaki kin sá animbil kútee kí kūtì bi-waakee nimbiliŋ ŋin u bàà cáań kí dā tijinee pu kí ŋá u-kutukuun.» Ní utɔntɔnlee ŋá kii Jooseefi nín tùkū-u puee.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaauee ní Jooseefi pú-bi nsan bí nīn kùǹ, bi nì bi-mammu.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Bi yíkì ki cōom̀ ki jítì kitiŋ pu kaa láá kɔ́ ndan ní Jooseefi bí u-tɔntɔŋkpiliuee yii: «Yīkìí jà binibee boon, a yaa tin ká-bee, á bàlifì-bi yii: <Ba pu ní ni dū ikpiti ki pàn̄ tiŋan?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Ba pu ní ni yùn̄ m-kpiliu sambinyɔkaaki kin poon u nyù ní ki cáa màkà ki béetí tin bí ki dòońee? Ni nín ŋá miŋyee kaa ŋān̄.>»

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Utɔntɔŋkpilee jìn̄ ki cúú-bee ní ki dū an bɔtee ki lī bi-cee.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Ukpil, ba pu ní a sòoǹ-ti mimmee? Timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi kaa pée ŋūǹ kí ŋá míǹ jaanjaan.

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Kpèè, animbil ŋin nìn kā ti-kutukubin ti kpáàa búntì Kanaan tiŋkinee, taa fātìi gíiǹní-si an nimbiliŋaaa? Kin mana ní ti gíti ŋūǹ kí yɔ̀ animbil àá sindaariya a-kpiliu dumpu?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Ukpil, ti-kansikin un kutukuun ní bi yaa ká kisambinyɔkaai gbantee, bí kpɔ̀ udaan, ní timbi bin kíǹee ń kpántí a-yumbui.»

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔŋkpilee kíí-bi yii: «Toooo! Ni nín lī puee m kíí míǹ. Ama un cee ní m yaa lafun ká kisambinyɔkaai gbantee, udaan baba di làá kpántí m-yumbuu ní nimbi bin kíǹee ń nyā tibɔtin.»

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Dicilpu niinee ní bi-kɔkɔ túutì bi-waŋguliŋ mmamu pu ki síiǹ kitiŋ ní báà ŋma cúú u-waŋgul ki gútì.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔŋkpilee kíĺ ujipɔŋkpil cee ki kpèé ki tin cáa sāā ujoolkaa cee, ní ki tin ká kisambinyɔkaayee Beenjameen kutukuun.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Niinee bi-pɔbiliŋ bíil̀, ní bi cúú tiwan tin bi pēēyee ki cátì, ní báà ŋma gíiǹ u-waŋgul ki túǹ u-maŋki ní bi-kɔkɔ fātìi nín gítí kitiŋin. Juuda gbāam̀ Beenjameen pu

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Juuda nì u-nabiyaamu fātìi bàn̄ Jooseefi dumpuee, u dáá bí, ní bi lítì u-nimbiin ki dɔ̄ kitiŋ.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí-bi yii: «Ba ní ni ŋée! Naa nyí yii unil kii man nee cáá dinimbil kí wāl̀ tin bíi jītéeee?»

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Ní Juuda kíí-u yii: «Ukpil, tilati ní ti gíti cáá kí lì a-cee ní? Ti làá gíti sòoǹ yii ba? Mana ní ti ŋūǹ kí dàkà ti-baamɔŋyi? Unimbɔti di nyántì ti-kpitii ki páaǹ. Kɔŋkɔnnee ti kpántì a-yumbui dee, timbi nì un cee bi ká kisambinyɔkaayee.»

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí yii: «M kpá kí ŋá míǹ! Un cee bi ká kisambinyɔkaayee baba di làá kpántí m-yumbuu, nimbi bin kíǹee ń nīn gítí ni-baa cee nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.»

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Niinee Juuda sútì ki pìl̄ Jooseefi ní ki bí-u yii: «M-dindaan, m gbāam̀-si á pɔ̄-mi diyimɔɔl ḿ sòoǹ nì si, á taa fōō m-pu diŋuul, di sá yii sii nì Faaroo ŋmà ní.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Ti nín nìn péé péé ki dɔ́mińee, a nìn bālifì-ti yii: <Ni-baa dáá báaa? Ni gíti cáá naal ubɔɔɔ?>

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Ní ti nìn kíí-si yii: <Ti-baa dáá bí ki púĺ. Ti gíti cáá naal ubɔ, úǹ di jóol̀ dibiil pu. Ti-baa màl̄-u u-tikpiti poon ní. U-maan kpíì, u kíǹ u-baba ní bi-na maaliŋun. An pu ní u-baa néeń-u tikpil.>

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Ní a bí timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi yii: <Cùú cáaḿmaan-u m-cee doo, m là kí ká-u.>

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: Ní ti kíí sii m-dindaan yii: <Kibikee kaa ŋūǹ kí yīkìí fá ki-baa, kì yaa yíkìi fá ki-baa, u làá kpú ní.>

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Ní a bí timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi yii: <Ni yaa kaa cáań ni-naal gbanti, m gíti kpá kí fōō-ni.>

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Ti nín fātìi gítì ti-baa a-tɔntɔnliu ceeyee ní ti tùkū-u a nín lī puee.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Boonee ní ti-baa bí yii: <Ní gítí kí cùú dāń-ti tijin.>

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Ní ti kíí-u yii: <Ti yaa làá cùee, see tí kpáaǹ ti-naal, taa ŋūǹ kí cù ti-ŋmaniŋma. Di sá gɔmina un bí niinee baasii kpáafì-ti ní yii: <Ni yaa kaa cáań ni-naal, m gíti kpá kí fōō-ni.>

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Ní ti-baa bí-ti yii: <Kéè ni nyí yii m-nimpuu Raseel màl̄-mi mbininjabiyaamu muli ja naa!

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Bi-kansikin ubɔ wáŋkì, ní m dākafì yii báà an ŋá pu, upeecuncuti ubɔ di cúú-u ki tɔ̄ntì, kun puee maa ti ká-u ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Ni nín là kí púntí un kíǹ nee mun kí cùnnì nee, tiba yaa tin ŋá-uee, nì kunimbaau ní m làá kpáaǹ m-yikpipinti nee kí kpú.>

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: «Kɔŋkɔnnee mana ní m làá fàtīí nīn gítí m-baa a-tɔntɔnliu cee, ní kibiki kin pu waa mɔ̄ nee ń taa nín̄ nóó-ti?

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Kí wàatēe, man a-tɔntɔnliu di dū m-ba ki yóoǹ kibikee yil pu m-baa cee ki yōoǹní-kì, ní ki bí m-baa yii: <M yaa kaa gíiǹní-kì ki ŋúbiǹ-see, ḿ nīn pée sá unikpiti a-cee kí nīn cá jaanjaan.>

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: An puee m gbāam̀-si, á yàntī man a-tɔntɔnliu ń fōō kibiki nee yil kí kpántí a-yumbuu ní kì nì ki-mambi ń nīn gítí mmɔŋki.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Di sá maa ŋūǹ kí gítí ti-baa cee kibiki nee kaa nóó-mi. Maa tin ŋūǹ kí kpèè inimɔɔn in poon m-baa làá nīn bée.»

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Niinee Jooseefi kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí cúú u-ba bin kɔkɔ nìn bí u-ceeyee nimbiin. Ní u téeń yii: «Nyāntímaan binib kɔkɔ m-cee doo.» An kíǹ u nì u-nabiyaamu ŋmaniŋmee ní u yāntì bi béè yii an sá úǹ Jooseefi.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Ní u bíi sūǹ mpɔn ní Eejipiti yab bin u nyántèe gbìl̄ ní an gbītì ki bàn̄ Faaroo cindi.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí u-nabiyaamu yii: «Man Jooseefi dee! M-baa gbíntìi dáá bí dimaŋfalinaaa?» Ama u-nabiyaamu wunti nìn kpíì u-nimbiin ní baa ŋúń ki kíí-u.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-bi yii: «Ní sútiń kí pìl̄-maa!» Ní bi sútì ki pìl̄-u. Ní u bí-bi yii: «An sá man Jooseefi, ni-nabiki kin ni nìn dūu nyáfì bi cáá-mi ki cūnnì Eejipitee.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, ni-pɔbiliŋ ń taa bīil̀, án taa wà-ni mun yii ni dū-mi ki nyáfì bi cáań-mi doo. An sá Unimbɔti di dū-mi ki péé ki līntìń ḿ dāá nīn bí doo kí ŋmā kí fīī-ni ní taa kpú.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋkùm nín nyáń kitiŋ pu nee, abin ali sèé. Abin aŋmoo ŋin mun dòoń nee, ubɔ kaa làá kpɔ̀ tikpaalaaa, kaa làá cā tijin mun.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti di túnní-mi ḿ lìntīń ni-nyɔkɔpu, án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa kúntí kitiŋ pu, ama ú dū u-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu kí fīī-ni ní ŋmátée.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee an kaa sá nimbi di yāntì ní m dɔ́miń doo, Unimbɔti di cáań-mi. Úǹ di kāaǹ-mi ḿ nīn sá kii Faaroo kpambal ki kpòotī-u, kí nīn sá u-dicaŋkun ukpil, ní kí nīn sá Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ gɔminau.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: An puee ní gítí m-baa cee malaa kí tùkù-u yii u-jipɔɔn Jooseefi nín tú bí tùkù-u puee sèé: <Unimbɔti dū-mi ki kāaǹ Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ kpiliu. Míǹ puee dāan̄ m-cee malaa, á taa tàan̄ní.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: A làá nīn kóò Gooseen tiŋgbaŋkin ní ki pìlīǹ-mi, sii nì a-biyaamu nì a-naantiibi nì a-piii nì a-naai nì tin kɔkɔ a pée cááyee.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: M làá nīn kpèé-si niin, sii nì a-dicaŋku nì a-waŋkuti kɔkɔ, án nín làá ŋá pu tiba nì tiba ń taa lóó-see, kun puee an gíti kíǹ abin aŋmoo ní ŋkùm ń jītí.>»

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi kútì ki lī yii: «Kéè nimbi ni-ba ká nì ni-nimbiliŋ, m-naal Beenjameen mun ká nì u-nimbiliŋ yii an baasii sá man di bíi sòoǹ nì naa!

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Ní māafì m-baa tinyool paaŋŋu ŋun poon m bí Eejipiti tiŋkin nee nì tin kɔkɔ ni kée, kí ŋá malaa kí cáań-u m-cee doo.»

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Ní u bìb̄ u-nabiyaamu mun kíǹee mun ki súń. Míǹ boonee ní u-nabiyaamu nín ŋúń ki sòon̄ nì u. Faaroo yíiń Jaakɔb ú dāan̄ Eejipiti

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Ní an gbītì ki bàn̄ Faaroo cindin yii Jooseefi nabiyaamu bāań, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ Faaroo nì u-naacimbi.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bí Jooseefi yii: «Tùkù a-nabiyaamu yii bí túń bi-mammu tijin kí nīn gítí Kanaan tiŋkin.

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: Bi yaa bàn̄ee, bí yòon̄ní bi-baa nì bi-dicaŋŋi kí cáań m-cee doo, ḿ lēē Eejipiti tiŋki dijandi din pée ŋān̄ee kí tīī-bi, ní bí nīn jīǹ tijimmɔntiil tin kitiŋ gbanti lòoǹee.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Yàntī a-nabiyaamu ń yòon̄ tɔrɔkub Eejipiti doo kí cùú yòon̄ní bi-nimpoobi nì bi-biyaamu nì bi-baa kí cáań doo.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Bí taa yāliŋkì tin bi làá yīkìí fáń lapuee pu, kun puee Eejipiti tiŋgbaŋki kin cáá tikɔkɔ nì tikɔkɔee poon ní bi làá nīn bí.»

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb jipɔmbi ŋá kii bi nín sáŋkì-bi puee. Ní Jooseefi tīī-bi tɔrɔkub kii Faaroo nín bí yii ú ŋá puee, ní ki tīī-bi tijin tin bi làá nīn jīǹ nsannee.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: U pú u-nabiyaamu kɔkɔ dibɔkutipɔndi diba diba, ní ki tīī Beenjameen úǹ animbil jitɔmbi alaataa ata nì abɔkutipɔɔn aŋmoo.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: U dū tiwammɔntiil tin bí Eejipitee tiba ki túǹ mmanjamu saalaa, ní mmansalimu saalaa mun tú tijin bí cáá tīī u-baa ú nīn jīǹ ki dòoń.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Ní u kpáafì u-nabiyaamu yii: «Ní taa tin já nsanni.» Ní ki pú-bi nsan bí nīn kùǹ.

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Niinee bi yíkì Eejipiti ki nín cá, ki tin bàn̄ Kanaan tiŋkin bi-baa Jaakɔb cee.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ee ní ki tùkū-u yii: «Jooseefi gbíntìi dáá bí dimaŋfalin, úǹ di sá gɔmina Eejipiti tiŋkin.» Ama an kaa nìn kɔ́ Jaakɔb pɔbilin, di sá yii waa nìn fōō tin bi lēe ki kíí.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Bi nín máafì Jaakɔb tibɔti tin kɔkɔ Jooseefi sòon̄ nì bee, nì u nín ká tɔrɔkub bin Jooseefi tīiń bí dāan̄ kí yòon̄-uee, ní u nín fīntì ŋgeem pu.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bí yii: «M-biki Jooseefi gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalinaa! An ŋmāntì, maa ti pée là tiba kí kūtì. M làá cùú ká-u ní kí nín kpú.»

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb yíkìi kāl̀ nsan pu ki kpáaǹ u-dicaŋku nì tin kɔkɔ u cááyee. U bàn̄ Beerseeba tiŋkinee ní ki ŋá saraabi ki tīī u-baa Isaaki Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbantee, ní Unimbɔti sòon̄ nì u kudamintiiun, ní ki yíiń-u yii: «Jaakɔb! Jaakɔb!» Ní u kíí yii: «M sèé.»

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti bí-u yii: «Man di sá Unimbɔti, a-baa Nimbɔtiu. A nín cá Eejipiti nee, á taa fàŋkì, kun puee niin ní m làá yàntī á kpántí ditimbuŋkpaandi baa.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Mama m-ba di làá céeǹ-si kí cùnnì Eejipiti ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-si. A-kúm dalee, a-jipɔɔn Jooseefi di làá cúú-si ní á sìntī.»

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Mbininjabiyaamu mun Leeya nìn màl̄ Jaakɔb Padan-Aram tiŋkinee dee. Bi-niisal Diina mun nìn kútì. Leeya biyaamu nninjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu nì u-naantiibi kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì binib mmuŋku nì saalaa nì bita ní.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Faaroo yaa láa yíiń-ni ki bālifì-ni yii ba tundi ní ni tūǹee,

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Siilpa un Laaban nìn dūu tīī u-bisal Leeya ú nīn sá ubiloolee bininjabiyaamu mun u nìn màl̄ Jaakɔbee dee. Siilpa biyaamu nì u-naantiibi kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì saalku nì ubɔ ní.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Biila un Laaban nìn dūu tīī u-bisal Raseel ú nīn sá ubiloolee bininjabiyaamu mun u nìn màl̄ Jaakɔbee dee. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì binib biluli ní.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb cindi poon nib bin nìn nóó-u ki cūtì Eejipitee kɔkɔ nìn sá binib imuŋku ita nì biluu ní, kaa kpáaǹ u-coopoobi.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nìn dū Juuda ki tú ú cùú tùkù Jooseefi yii ú dāan̄ kí ká-u Gooseen tiŋkin. Ŋyunti ŋun Jaakɔb nì u-yab nìn tóob́ kí kɔ́ Gooseen tiŋkinee,

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: ní Jooseefi yāntì bi kpàl̄ u-taamui in dátí tɔrɔkuee ní u búntì Gooseen kí tūŋkì u-baa Jaakɔb. U nín bàn̄ ki ká u-baayee ní u ŋàan̄ ki cìb̄-u ní u-yil pá u-baa sil pu ní u súń ki yúntì.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bí Jooseefi yii: «M ŋūǹ kí kpú kɔŋkɔnnee, kun puee m fātìi ká-si a gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin.»

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí u-nabiyaamu nì u-baa dicaŋku yab yii: «M làá cùú ká Faaroo kí tùkù-u yii: <M-nabiyaamu nì m-baa dicaŋkun yab bin nìn bí Kanaan tiŋkinee dɔ́miń m-cee.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Binib gbanti sá bin kpàá tiwaŋkutee ní. Bi cáań bi-piii nì bi-ŋoobui nì bi-naai nì tin kɔkɔ bi pée cááyee.>

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: ní dāá kíí-u yii: <Timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi pée sá biwaŋkpaaliibi ní doooo ti-biyatin ki dāa sāā díǹ, kii ti-baabi mun nín nìn pée sá puee.> Mimmee u làá yàntī ní kàl̄ Gooseen tiŋkin, kun puee uwaŋkpaal kamaa sá Eejipiti yab cee mbusu niliu ní.»

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bālifì Jooseefi nabiyaamu yii: «Ba tundi ní ni tūǹ ní?» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi pée sá biwaŋkpaaliibi ní, kii ti-baabi mun nín nìn pée sá puee.»

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Ní bi bí Faaroo yii: «Ti dá láá dɔ́miń kí kàl̄ kitiŋ nee pu ní, di sá yii ŋkùm pɔ̄ɔ̄ Kanaan tiŋki poon tikpil, ní timool mun kaa ti bí timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi waŋkuti ń ŋmɔ́. Míǹ puee ti mèé-si á pɔ̄-ti nsan tí kàl̄ Gooseen tiŋgbaŋkin.»

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bí Jooseefi yii: «A-baa nì a-nabiyaamu dɔ́miń a-cee.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ bí a-ŋaan ní. Kpèè dijandi din ŋān̄ee kí lēē kí tīī-bi bí nīn kóò. Bi ŋūǹ kí nīn kóò Gooseen tiŋgbaŋkin. A yaa ká bi-kansikin biba nyí diwaŋkpàal tundi tiŋanee, á lēē-bi bí nīn sá bin kpèé man waŋkutee kpilib.»

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi cáań u-baa Jaakɔb ki dàkā Faaroo ní Jaakɔb jáam̀-u ki mēē ki bīiǹ u-pu.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bālifì Jaakɔb yii: «A ŋá abin aŋa dee?»

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb gíti jáam̀ Faaroo ki mēē ki bīiǹ u-pu ní ki nyáń ki nín kùǹ.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Bi nyáńee ní Jooseefi ŋá kii Faaroo nín bí ú ŋá puee ki nyàab̄ Eejipiti tiŋkin dijandi din ŋān̄ ki bí Ramseesi tiŋkinee ki kāaǹ u-baa nì u-nabiyaamu.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Jooseefi nìn kpáfì animbil ŋin kɔkɔ Eejipiti nì Kanaan yab nìn cāabìń ki dāā tijinee ki cáa yóoǹ Faaroo dumpu.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Eejipiti nì Kanaan timmu yab dū bi-nimbiliŋ kɔkɔ ki dáal̀ tijinee, ní Eejipiti yab cūtì Jooseefi cee ki bí-u yii: «Tīī-ti tijin! Ba pu ní tí kpú ŋkùm a-nimbiin míǹ yii ti nín kaa ti cáá animbilee pu?»

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi kíí-bi yii: «Ni yaa kaa ti cáá animbilee, cáaḿmaan-mi ni-waŋkuti ḿ dūú kpántí-ni tijin.»

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Dibindi gbanti kúntì dipɔndi páaǹee ní bi tí dɔ́miń ki bí Jooseefi yii: «Ukpil, taa ŋūǹ kí dūú báĺ-si. Ti-nimbiliŋ dóò ní ti cáań ti-waŋkuti mun ki tīī-si. Tin pée kíǹ tí cáań-see di sá timbi ti-ba nì ti-kpaatanti.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní tí kpú a-nimbiin míǹ ti-timmu ń gbíntí fám? An puee dā timbi nì ti-timmu kí tīī-ti tijin tí jī kí ŋmátí, ní Faaroo ń nīn kíǹ ki yì timbi nì ti-timmu. Tīī-ti ijimbool ti-timmu ń taa nín̄ dɔ̄ fám, tí ŋmā kí ká tin ti làá nīn jīǹ kí taa kpú kí céetée.»

english_verse: and made everyone the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi yāntì Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ nib dūu kpántì iyumbu.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: See bitandambi baba timmu ní Jooseefi kaa nìn dá, kun puee Faaroo nìn yóoǹ mara yii bí taa gbēē bitandambi wanti, di sá yii Faaroo di nìn tìì-bi tijin. An pu ní bíǹ kaa nìn nyáfì bi-timmu.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi bí samaa kɔkɔ yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, m dá-ni ki kpáaǹ ni-timmu ki tīī Faaroo, an puee m làá tīī-ni iwambool ní bɔ̄l̀ ni-sati.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa cáńee, ní yàkatī miŋmoo pu ní kí lēē diba pu kí tīī Faaroo. Minaa min kíǹee, ní dūú kpíiǹ ni nì ni-biyaamu nì ni-dicaŋŋi yab kɔkɔ, ní kí kíń ibool kí dāá bɔ̄l̀.»

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Ukpil, a fīī-ti ní! A dàkā-ti tiniti, an puee ti kíí kí nīn sá Faaroo yumbui.»

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi dū an bɔtee ki kpántì mara Eejipiti tiŋkin. Mara gbanti bí ki dāa sāā díǹ. An di sá yii Eejipiti yab yaa cáń tijinee, see bí yàkatī miŋmoo pu ní kí lēē diba pu kí tīī Faaroo. Bitandambi baba timmu di kaa kpántì Faaroo wanti. Jaakɔb dàkā laakin bi máaǹ kí síb́-uee

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn kóò Eejipiti tiŋkin, Gooseen tiŋgbaŋkin míǹ ní ki dūu kpántì bitindambi niin, ní ki màl̄ ki būtì tikpil.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jaakɔb béè yii u tóob́ ŋkúmee ní u yíiń u-jipɔɔn Jooseefi ní ki bí-u yii: «M gbāam̀-si, á dàkà-mi a-neendi nì a-laŋŋaŋfitiiku kí dū a-ŋal kí tíkiń m-tapandi taapu kí pùtī kí pòon̄-mi yii m yaa kpíìyee, aa làá síb́-mi Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: M yaa kpíìyee, á yòon̄-mi Eejipiti tiŋkin doo kí cáá-mi kí síb́ m-baabi kaakul poon.» Ní Jooseefi kíí-u yii: «M làá ŋá a nín lī puee.»

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb fātìi bí-u yii: «Pùtī yii a làá ŋá míǹ», ní Jooseefi pūtì. Niinee ní Jaakɔb tīntì u-dooŋu pu ki jáam̀.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi tùkū Jooseefi yii: «A-baa būǹ.» Ní u yōoǹ u-jipɔmbi liitil, Manasee nì Eefiraayiim, ki búntì.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū Jaakɔb yii: «A-jipɔɔn Jooseefi dɔ́miń kí màntì a-pu.» Ní Jaakɔb pɔ́ɔǹ u-ba ki nyīī ki yíkìi kāl̀ u-dooŋu pu.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: U kāl̀ee ní ki bí Jooseefi yii: «Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nìn nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-mi Luusi, Kanaan tiŋkin ní ki bīiǹ m-boon.

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: U bí-mi yii: <M làá yàntī á màal̀ kí bùtī. Sii pu ní m làá dī kí náań anibul kupaau. M làá dū kitiŋ nee kí tīī a-naantiibi án nīn sá bi-tiŋki kí nīn cá jaanjaan.>

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: A-jipɔmbi bili bin a màl̄ Eejipiti tiŋkin ki wāatì ní man nín dɔ́miń a-ceeyee làá nīn sá man jipɔmbi ní. Eefiraayiim nì Manasee làá nīn sá man jipɔmbi kii Rubeen nì Simeeyɔn nín sá m-jipɔmbi puee ní.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ama mbiyaamu mun a làá dāá màal̀ bi-boonee, a-yɔmu dāa yá. Bi-mambi Eefiraayiim nì Manasee timmu poon ní bi mun dāa fòol̄ bi-fakal.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: M nìn nyánní Padan-Aram ki kùnní ki tóobiń Eefiraata, Kanaan tiŋkin ní a-na Raseel kpíì nsanni m-nimbiin ní m síb́-u nsan caŋin niin. Eefiraata tiŋki gbanti ní bi gíti yíì Beetileem.» -

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Ní Jaakɔb bí Jooseefi yii: «Maa pée dākafì yii m bí kí gíti ká-si ŋwindal. Ama ní Unimbɔti yāntì m tin ká ki kpáaǹ a-biyaamu gba.»

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.

translation_verse: Niinee Eejipiti yab mɔ̄tìi bíi sàantí Isirayeel yab tikpil kii iyumbuee.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab wunti túŋkì nì atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee tɔ̄tam, an dàkà yii bi nìn búù titan ki māā brikisib ki tūǹ asaatuun. Eejipiti yab nìn cáá atuun ŋin kɔkɔ pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki cáa nyìitī-bi mpɔn. Faaroo wɔ́b́ Isirayeel yab

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Eebru yab nìn cáá bimatimmaanliibi bili bi nìn yíì ubɔ yii Siifira nì ki yíì un kíǹee Puya. Eejipiti bɔtiu nìn bí bi-kansikin ubɔ yii:

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: «Ni yaa bíi màantí Eebru yab nimpoobi ubɔ ní ki yaa ká yii an sá kibininjabiki ní u bíi màal̀ee, ní fáá-kì kí kpɔ̀, ama an yaa sá kibinimpubikee, ní yàntī-kì.»

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Ama bimatimmaanliibee nìn fàŋkí Unimbɔti. An puee baa nìn pílifiǹ Eejipiti yab bɔtiu ní ki nìn yàntī bi màal̀ mbininjabiyaamu kaa kù-mu.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti yíiń bimatimmaanliibee ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni ŋá míǹ, ki yàntī Eebru nimpoobi màal̀ naa fátí ki kù mbininjabiyaamu ní?»

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Bimatimmaanliibee nìn kíí Faaroo yii: «Eebru nimpoobi kaa sá kii Eejipiti nimpoobee. Bíǹ màal̀ bi-biyaamu sɔkɔmii kí dóó kí wàatī ní umatimmaanli ń nín bà.»

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Kii bimatimmaanliibee nín nìn fāŋkì Unimbɔti puee, u nìn bīiǹ bi-boon bi-dicaŋŋi būtì.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Niinee Faaroo yóoǹ u-yab kɔkɔ mara yii: «Ni yaa ká Eebru nimpoobi ubɔ màl̄ kibininjabikee, ní fōō-kì kí cáá tɔ̄ Niil mɔɔlin. An yaa sá kibinimpubikee, ní taa kpɔ̀-kì.»

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Uninja ubɔ nìn sá Leefii naakookun ní ki fātìi cáá unimpu Leefii naakookun.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Unimpuee nìn cáá dipool ní ki màl̄ kibininjabiki. U nìn ká yii kibikee ŋān̄ tikpil ní u dū-kì ki bál̀ áli iŋmal ita.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun waa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí yàntī kí nīn gbíntìi kā dibalinee ní u nyàab̄ kikabiki kin bi dū papiirusi ki lùn̄ee, ki dū aŋɔ ki póoń, ki dū kibiki ki tākaǹ poon ní ki cáa nēeǹ dikal taapu dimɔɔgbandi.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Kibikee niisal nìn cūtìi yúní ndan fiii kí kpèè tin làá jītí ki-puee.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee Faaroo bisal cūtì dimɔɔlin kí fàl̀. Ŋyunti gbantee, binimpoobi bin céeǹ-uee bíi kpàkaǹ dimɔɔl, ní úǹ ká kikabikee nēē dikal taapu, ní u tú u-yumbusapɔɔŋwu ú cùú yòon̄ní.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: U cúu púkutèe kibininjabiki di kā poon ki sūǹee. An nìn kɔ́-u falaa ní u bí yii: «Eebru yab biki dee.»

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Ní kibikee niisal bālifì Faaroo bisal yii: «Ḿ cù Eebru nimpoobi cee kí nyàabìń-si umatimpɔɔn ú lòò-si kibiki gbantaaa?»

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bisal kíí-u yii: «Iiin.» Ní kisapɔmbikee cūtìi nyàabìń kibikee ki-ba na.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bisal bí unimpuee yii: «Yòon̄ kibiki nee kí lòò-kì kí tīī-mi, m làá dāá pà-si ditundi gbanti pu.» Ní unimpuee yōoǹ kibikee ki lōō.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Kibikee dāa wíiǹee ní unimpuee cáań-kì ki tīī Faaroo bisal. Úǹ nìn fōō-kì ki dūu ŋá u-ba biki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Mooyiisi. Di sá u bí yii: «Nnyimin ní m nyántìń-kì.» Mooyiisi sáǹ ki búntì Madiyan yab tiŋkin

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi wíiǹee, dalbee ní u cūtì kí màntì u-nabiyaamu Eebru yab pu. U bàn̄ee ki lafun ká atuun ŋin bi tūǹee nín pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki cáá agìń miŋyee. U nìn ká ueejipitija bíi gbáà u-nabiki ueebruja ubɔ.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: U nín fātìi kpēē ajan kɔkɔ pu kaa ká báà ubɔee, ní u fáá ki kūū ueejipitijee ní ki kūtì dibul ki dū-u ki síb́.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì u tí gítì bi-ceeyee ki ká Eebru yab ŋmaniŋma bili bíi jáà. Ní u bí un bɔti kaa ŋān̄ee yii: «Ba pu ní a gbáà a-juti míǹ?»

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Ní úǹ fātìi kíí-u yii: «Ŋma di kāaǹ-si á nīn sòoǹ ti-bɔti ní? Àá a là kí kpɔ̀ ma mun kii a nín fu kūū ueejipitija puee ní?»

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nín béè yii an bɔtee gbītì an kɔkɔee ní u fāŋkì. Faaroo gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní ki bíi nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀ Mooyiisi. Ní Mooyiisi sáǹ ki cūtìi kóòń Madiyan yab tiŋkin, ki kā ki kɔ́ĺ lɔkɔ ubɔ.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Madiyan tiŋki tandaaŋwu nìn cáá bisapɔmbi biluli. Bi nìn dɔ́miń kí lúń nnyim kí sìtī laakin tiwaŋkuti nyùee kí nyùntī bi-baa piii nì u-ŋoobui.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Ama ní bipikpaaliibi dɔ́miń ki jìn̄-bi. Ní Mooyiisi yíkì ki mɔ́tì bi-pu ní ki lúń nnyim ki tīī bi-waŋkuti nyùn̄.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Bi fātìi bàn̄ mmɔŋki bi-baa Reewuyeel ceeyee ní úǹ bālifì-bi yii: «Ba ŋá ní ni fātìń mmɔŋki díǹ malaa míǹ?»

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Ueejipitija ubɔ di fīī-ti bipikpaaliibi ŋaan ní ki lúń nnyim ki nyūntì ti-waŋkuti.»

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Ní bi-baa bālifì-bi yii: «Uninja gbanti bí la? Ba ŋá ní naa cáań-u? Cùú yíiḿmaan-u ú dāan̄ kí jī tijin.»

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi lēē yii u làá nīn kíǹ ki kóò uninja gbanti cee. Ní uninjee dū u-bisal Seefoora ki pú Mooyiisi cáá.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Unimpuee màl̄-u kibininjabiki, ní u pú-kì diyindi yii Geersɔm, an taapu di sá yii <Unicaan niin>, di sá u bí yii u sáǹ ki kpántì unicaan kinicantiŋ poon. Unimbɔti lēē Mooyiisi ú fīī Isirayeel yab

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: An yúntì boonee ní Eejipiti bɔtiu dāa kpíì. Isirayeel yab nìn bí ki fátí diniindi bi-yuŋku poon ki gbáà ibiil, ní bi-kuŋkuuntii bàn̄ áli Unimbɔti cee.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn gbìl̄ bi-yaliŋkii pu ní ki téetì u nín nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb puee.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn kpēē Isirayeel yab falaau ní ki súń bi-saai.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
