translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn bí ki kpàá u-coo Jeetroo, Madiyan tiŋki tandaaŋwu piii nì u-ŋoobui. Dalbee u yōoǹ tiwaŋkuti ki jítì kuteeu pu ki tin bàn̄ Ooreeb, Unimbɔti jool pu.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Niin ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nyántì ŋu-ba ki dàkā-u ŋŋmin kisugbooi poon. Mooyiisi ká aŋmilimbil nyēē kisugbooyee poon, ama ní kíǹ ki-ba kaa bíi wù.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí yii: «M làá sútí kí pìl̄ kí kpèè maamaaci bɔti tin di bíi jītí niin ní ŋŋmi gà kisugbooi poon lìblib ama ní kaa bíi wùee.»

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín ká yii u sútìń kí kpèèyee ní u yíiń-u kisugbooyee poon yii: «Mooyiisi! Mooyiisi!» Ní Mooyiisi kíí-u yii: «M sèé!»

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti bí-u yii: «Taa sútí kí pìl̄ kisugbooi nee. Tákatí a-naatakaŋ, kun puee laakin a yú nee sá circir paaŋŋu ní.

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Man di sá a-baa Nimbɔtiu, Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu.» Niinee Mooyiisi fātì u-nimbiin, kun puee u nìn fāŋkì kí kpèè Unimbɔti.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M ká m-nibul din bí Eejipitee falaau, ki gbìl̄ Eejipiti yab nín sàantí-bi bi gbáà ibiil iŋyee. Tiŋman m nyí falaa un bi bíi jīǹee.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: An puee m sīntìń kí fōō-bi Eejipiti yab ŋaan, kí nyāntí-bi kitiŋ nee poon kí cáá-bi kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin ŋān̄ ki sá kikpaaŋŋee poon. Kitiŋ gbanti poonee, nnaabiim nì tisiil di còol̀. Niin ní Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab kóò.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab biilii bāań-mi, ní man m-ba ká Eejipiti yab nín bí ki sàantí-bi puee.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee m làá tɔ̄-si Faaroo cee á cù Eejipiti kí nyāntí man nibul Isirayeel yab.» Unimbɔti nyántì u-yindi ki dàkā Mooyiisi

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Unimbɔti yii: «Man di sá ŋma ní kí cù Faaroo cee kí nyāntí Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin?»

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti bí yii: «M làá nīn bí a-cee. Kun làá nīn sá-si kudaaŋŋu á béé yii man di tú-see di sá a yaa láa nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkinee, dijool nee pu ní ni làá dāá jāam̀ man Unimbɔti.»

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Unimbɔti yii: «Too, m làá cù Isirayeel yab cee kí tùkù-bi yii: <Ni-naanjab Nimbɔtiu di túnní-mi ni-cee.> Bi làá bàlifì-mi yii: <Bi yíì-u yii ba? M làá kíí-bi yii ba?>»

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti gíti bí Mooyiisi yii: «TI-DINDAAN ni-naanjab Nimbɔtiu, Abraam Nimbɔtiu nì Isaaki Nimbɔtiu nì Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu di túnní-mi ni-cee. Man yindi dee kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. Diyindi gbanti ní iyunti kamaa nib làá nīn yíì-mi.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, cù kí kpāfì Isirayeel kpilib, kí tùkù-bi yii ni-Dindaan ni-naanjab Nimbɔtiu, Abraam Nimbɔtiu nì Isaaki Nimbɔtiu nì Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-si ní ki tùkū-si yii: <M ká Eejipiti yab nín bí ki sàantí-ni puee, kɔŋkɔnnee m làá fīī-ni.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: M làá nyāntí-ni kitiŋ kin poon bi bí ki sàantí-ni nee kí cáá-ni kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin poon Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab kóòyee. Kitiŋ gbanti poon ní nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀.>

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: «Isirayeel yab làá gbìl̄ kí tīiǹ-si. Niinee si nì bikpilib ń cùú ká Eejipiti yab bɔtiu ní kí tùkù-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan Eebru yab Nimbɔtiu, ti-Nimbɔtiu lēē u-ba ki dàkā-ti. Míǹ puee pɔ̄-ti nsan tí dū iwiin ita kí còom̀ kí cù kuteeun kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī-u.>

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Ama m nyí Eejipiti yab bɔtiu nín kaa làá kíí ní cùee, asee m yaa dàkā-u mpɔn.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: An puee m làá tàntī m-ŋal ki dū maamaacib nín bí tɔbin u-ba u-ba puee kí ŋá bi-kansikin niin, ní án fáá Eejipiti tiŋki. Míǹ boonee ní ú yàntī ní nyā kí nīn cá.

english_verse: After I punish the Egyptians, they will be so afraid of you that they will give you anything you want. You are my people, and I will let you take many things with you when you leave the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī gba ni-nibul ń ká diyimɔɔl Eejipiti yab cee, ní ni yaa làá dāá nyēe, ní taa láa nyā nì iŋaŋkulim.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Unimpu kamaa làá dāá bàlifì ueejipitinimpu u nì un kóò ki pìl̄ee nì un kóò u-dumpuee animbil kúti nì sindaariya wanti nì abɔkuti, kí dūú ŋá ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib wunti pu. Ni nín làá ŋá pu kí fūkul̀ Eejipiti yabee dee.»

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kíí ti-Dindaan yii: «Isirayeel yab kaa làá fōō ki kíí kaa làá pīlifiǹ-mi. Ama bi làá tùkù-mi yii: <Ti-Dindaan ubɔ kaa pée nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-si!>»

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Ba ní a ŋúb́ a-ŋaan ní?» Ní u bí yii: «An sá ŋkpandɔ.»

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Dū-ŋu kí lúkú kitiŋ.» Ní u dūu lúkú kitiŋ ní an kpántì ukoobu, ní Mooyiisi sáǹ ki wāatì-u.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Tàntī a-ŋal kí cúú u-juul.» U tāntì u-ŋal ki cúúyee ní an fātìi kpántì ŋkpandɔ u-ŋaan.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «A nín làá ŋá tin kí dàkà Isirayeel yab yii man bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu, Abraam Nimbɔtiu nì Isaaki Nimbɔtiu nì Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-see dee.»

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan gíti bí-u yii: «Dū a-ŋal kí páań a-bindi pu.» Ní u dūu páaǹ, ni ki fātìi cúu páatì, ní dinyaŋgbandi píń u-ŋal ní ŋu píil̀ káŋkaŋ.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Fàtīí gíiǹ a-ŋal kí páań a-bindi pu.» Ní u fātìi gíiǹ ki páaǹ, ní ki fātìi cúu páatì ní ŋu fātìi gítì kii ŋu nín nìn pée bí puee.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Bi yaa kaa fōō-si ki kíí kaa pílifiǹ-si maamaaci daanti tili nee puee, á jōō Niil mɔɔl nyim kí kpáatí kí fá kitiŋ, nnyim min a kpáatì ki fá kitiŋee làá kpántí fatiku.» Unimbɔti lēē Aarɔn ú nīn sá Mooyiisi taapu yɔu

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí ti-Dindaan yii: «Áù ti-Dindaan, man sá unil un kaa ŋūǹ isoonee ní. An kaa sá díǹ kaa sá fool bɔti, ní doooo a nín pée kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì man a-tɔntɔnliu nee, tiba kaa kpántì. An pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki tīī-mi ḿ ŋmā kí sòoǹ cábcab.»

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋma di náań kinyɔkɔ ki tīī unil? Ŋma di yàntī unil ń nīn sá umɔɔmiin àá utafakpaafu àá ujɔfu àá un wāĺee. Kaa sá man ni-Dindaanaaa?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, nín̄ cá, man làá nīn bí a-cee kí yábití a-nyɔkɔ kí dàkà-si tin a làá sòoǹee.»

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi fātìi bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan, m gbāam̀-si, tɔ̄ ubɔ!»

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan fōō Mooyiisi pu diŋuul ní ki bí-u yii: «A-nabiki Aarɔn uleefiija kaa báaa? M nyí u-pu yii u ŋūǹ ki sòoǹ cábcab. Úǹ gba di dòoń a-cee nee. U yaa bāań ki ká-see, án làá mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u tikpil.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: Aarɔn di làá nīn sòoǹ nì samaa sii yil pu. Úǹ di làá nīn sá a-nyɔkɔ ní sii ń nīn sá kii unimbɔtee ki tùkù tin u máaǹ kí sòoǹee.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Yòon̄ ŋkpandɔ nee kí ŋá a-ŋaan, ŋúǹ ní a làá nīn cáa ŋáań maamaaci daanti.» Mooyiisi fātìi nín gítí Eejipiti u-samaau cee

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Mooyiisi fātì mmɔŋkee ní ki tùkū u-coo Jeetroo yii: «M làá mèè-si nsan kí fàtī Eejipiti m-nabiyaamu Eebru yab cee kí kpèè yii bi dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalinaaa.» Ní Jeetroo kíí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá nì ŋgbansɔŋfi!»

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi Madiyan tiŋkin yii: «Nín̄ gítí Eejipiti, kun puee bin kɔkɔ nìn nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-see kpíì.»

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi yōoǹ u-nimpuu nì u-jipɔmbi ki kāaǹ mmamu pu ní bi búntì Eejipiti. U nìn ŋúb́ ŋkpandɔ ŋun Unimbɔti nìn bí yii ú yòon̄ee u-ŋaan.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn tùkū Mooyiisi yii: «A yaa gítì Eejipitee, atuŋkpaan ŋin kɔkɔ m tīī-si mpɔn á ŋée, á ŋá-ŋi Faaroo nimbiin. Ama man làá pɔ̄ɔkì u-pɔbil ú taa yàntī Isirayeel yab ń nyā.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Á tùkù Faaroo yii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Isirayeel yab sá kii m-jipɔŋkpiliuee ní.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: An puee m tùkū-si yii á yàntī m-jipɔɔn ú cù kí ŋá saraabi kí jāam̀-mi. A yaa yíì kaa yāntì u cūtèe, m làá kpɔ̀ a-jipɔŋkpiliu.>»

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Bi bí nsan pu ki cá ki bàn̄ laabee kunyeeu mɔ́. Bi gbíntì niin ki dōoǹ kunicandiin, ní ti-Dindaan dɔ́miń ki là kí kpɔ̀ Mooyiisi.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Ní Siipoora yōoǹ kitaŋkpajiki ki gíí u-jipɔɔn kunlam ní ki dūu gbēē Mooyiisi taal, ní ki bí yii: «M-cal sá-si nì fatiku cati ní.»

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì Mooyiisi kaa kūū-u. Di sá digiil pu ní Siipoora nìn lī yii: «M-cal sá-si nì fatiku cati ní.»

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Aarɔn yii: «Nín̄ cá kuteeun kí tūŋkì Mooyiisi.» Ní Aarɔn yíkìi búntì ní ki tin tú-u Unimbɔti jool taapu ní ki kpàl̄-u bi jáam̀.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi máafì-u ti-Dindaan nín dū tibɔti tin ki ŋúbiǹ-uee, nì maamaaci daanti tin u tīī-u ú nīn ŋáańee.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Ní bi-liitil nóó ki búntì ki cūtìi kpáfì Isirayeel yab kpilib kɔkɔ.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn máafì samaa kɔkɔ tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan tùkū Mooyiisee, ní Mooyiisi ŋá maamaaci daanti bi-nimbiin.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn fōō ki kíí. Bi nìn béè yii ti-Dindaan ká falaa un poon bi bée ní ki làá fīī-bi. Niinee ní bi-kɔkɔ gbāaǹ taapu ki bíi jáaḿ-u.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn cūtì Faaroo cee, ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu bí yii: <Yàntī m-nibul ń cù kuteeu pu kí jī jiŋaal kí tīī-mi tinyool.>»

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo kíí-bi yii: «Ŋma di sá ni-Dindaan ní ḿ pīlifì tin u sòoǹee kí yàntī Isirayeel yab ń nīn cá ní? Maa nyí-u kaa làá yàntī Isirayeel yab ń nyā.»

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn bí yii: «Eebru yab Nimbɔtiu lēē u-ba ki dàkā-ti. Míǹ puee pɔ̄-ti nsan tí còom̀ iwiin ita kuteeu pu kí cùú ŋá saraabi kí tīī ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu. An yaa kaa ŋá míǹ, u ŋūǹ kí yàntī bìlbil kúm ń dāá kpɔ̀-ti, àá tí kpú kujaaun».

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo nìkī ki lī yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee binibee būtì kitiŋ nee puee ní naa ti là bí tɔ̄ bi-tuuŋŋaa!» Faaroo gíti gbéeǹ Isirayeel yab atuun

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Yaadal wiiŋŋu ní Faaroo tīī Eejipiti kàliŋkpilib nì Isirayeel yab tɔntɔŋkpilib mara nee yii:

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: «Ní taa ti tīī Isirayeel yab timool bí ŋmàlim̀ titan kí mā brikisib kii ni nín kpààa ŋáań puee. Bí nīn kíǹ ki cá bi-ba ki nyàabìń timool.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Ama ní yàntī bí nīn māā brikisib bin nyɔkɔm bi pée kpààa māāyee, ní taa bàtī. Bi sá biwutijoodambi ní, an pu ní bi bí ki lì yii: <Ti là kí cùú ŋá saraabi kí tīī ti-Nimbɔtiu.>

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Bi yaa dū atuun ki lúuń-bee, baa ti kāntí mpaan kí dàkafì bi-nyimɔmbɔti pu.»

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Bikàliŋkpilibee nì bitɔntɔŋkpilibee nyáń Faaroo ceeyee ní ki cūtì ki bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Faaroo bí yii bí taa ti tīī-ni timool.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Nimbi ni-ba ń cù laakin ni làá kánní-tèe kí nyàabìń, ama taa làá bàtī brikisib bin ni kpààa māāyee nyɔkɔm pu.»

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Ní Eejipiti yab tɔntɔŋkpilibee kā bi-pu ki lì yii: «Ní pée mā bi nín nìn cāabìń-ni timool ni māā brikisib bin nyɔkɔmee deedee, ubɔ ń taa fɔ́tí!»

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Faaroo kàliŋkpilib nìn gbáà ki kpáaǹ Isirayeel yab tɔntɔŋkpilib bin bi lēē bí nīn kpèé bi-nabiyaamuee ki lì yii: «Ba pu ní naa ŋúń ki máń fool nì díǹ brikisib bàn̄ kii dooooyee ni nín kpààa māā puee?»

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab tɔntɔŋkpilib bin Eejipiti yab lēē bí nīn kpèé bi-nabiyaamuee dɔ́miń ki bíi yáliŋkí Faaroo cee ki lì yii: «Ti-baa, ba pu ní a bí ki sàantí timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi mimmee?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Baa ti tìì-ti timool, ama ní ki là yii tí nīn gbíntìi māā brikisib bin nyɔkɔm ti nìn kpààa māāyee, ní ki gbáà-ti. A-yab bíi ŋáań tin kaa kítèe!»

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo kíí-bi yii: «Biwutijoodambi, ni sá biwutijoodambi ní! An pu ní ni lì yii: <Ti làá cùú ŋá saraabi kí tīī ti-Dindaan.>

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, cùú nīn tūm̀maan ditundi. Baa làá ti tīī-ni timool, ama ni làá nīn gbíntìi māā brikisib bin nyɔkɔm ni nìn kpààa pée māāyee ní.»

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab tɔntɔŋkpilib bin bi nìn lēē bí nīn kpèé bi-nabiyaamuee ká yii laakin bi bí nee an pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, kun puee bi nìn bí-bi yii: «Ní taa bàtī brikisib bin ni kpààa māā ŋwiin kamaayee nyɔkɔm pu.»

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Bi nyáń Faaroo ceeyee ní ki cūtìi ká Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn, bíǹ yú ki cí-bi.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Bi nìn nyáń Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn pu ki bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan di wāĺ tin ni ŋá nee kí sòoǹ ni-bɔti! Ni yāntì Faaroo nì u-yab kaa ti là bi-nimbiliŋ ń wāl̀-ti. Ni ŋman dū kitàataajiki ní ki ŋá bi-ŋaan bí fōō kí kpɔ̀-ti.»

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi fātì ti-Dindaan pú ki bí-u yii: «M-Dindaan, ba pu ní a ŋá samaa nee tikpitil míǹ? Ba pu ní a nín túnní man dee?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Doooo m nín cūtì Faaroo cee ki sòon̄ a-yil puee, úǹ bí ki sàantí Isirayeel yab ní, ní sii kaa pée ŋá tiba kí fīī a-nibul.»

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee a làá ká m nín làá ŋá Faaroo puee. M-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu ŋun m làá dàkà-uee pu ní u làá yàntī m-nibul ń nyā. Mpɔŋkpaan gbanti di làá yàntī ú jà-ni kí nyāntí u-tiŋkin!» Unimbɔti pōoǹ Mooyiisi kí fīī Isirayeel yab

english_verse: My name is the Lord.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti gíti bí Mooyiisi yii: «Man di sá NI-DINDAAN.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: M nìn nyántì m-ba ki dàkā Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb yii man di sá UNIMBƆTI MPƆŊKƆDAAN. Ama maa nìn lēē ki dàkā-bi yii bi yíì-mi <NI-DINDAAN>.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: M nìn pōoǹ-bi dipoondi yii m làá dū Kanaan tiŋki kin bi nìn kóò ki sá binicambee kí tīī-bi.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: M gbìl̄ Eejipiti yab nín tīī Isirayeel yab atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄ bi bí ki tūǹ ki yáliŋkée pu, ní maa súntì dipoondi din m nìn pōoǹ-bee pu.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: An puee, tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: <Man di sá ni-Dindaan. M làá nyāntí-ni Eejipiti yab tuuŋŋi ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee poon ní kí fīī-ni kí nyāntí ni-yuŋkun. M làá dū m-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì m-tuŋkpaaŋŋi kí fīī-ni kí líí.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: M làá dū-ni ki ŋá m-nibul ní kí nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu ní ní béé yii man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di nyántì-ni Eejipiti yab tuuŋŋi ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee poon.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: M làá cáá-ni kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin poon m nìn pūtì yii m làá tīī Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔbee. Nimbi ní m làá dū kitiŋ gbanti kí tīī ní nīn kíǹ ki yì. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.>»

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi cáań an bɔtee ki lī Isirayeel yab cee, ama kuyuŋu gìŋ́ŋi ŋin poon bi bée kaa yāntì bi pílifiǹ-u.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan fātìi gíti sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: «Cù kí tùkù Faaroo, Eejipiti bɔtiu yii ú yàntī Isirayeel yab ń nyā u-tiŋkin.»

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kíí-u yii: «Isirayeel yab gba kaa pílifiǹ-mi, Faaroo di dāa nín pílifíǹ man un kaa ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ mmɔntiimin naaa?»

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn bi nín làá sòoǹ Isirayeel yab nì Faaroo, Eejipiti yab bɔtiu pu ní Isirayeel yab ń nyā Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn naanjab yiŋŋi

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab naakɔti kpilib yiŋŋi sèé. Jaakɔb jipɔŋkpiliu Rubeen jipɔmbi di sá Anɔki nì Palu nì Eetisirɔn nì Kaarmii. Rubeen naakookun yab naanjab yiŋŋi dee.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeeyɔn jipɔmbi di sá Jeemuyeel nì Jamiini nì Oodi nì Jaakin nì Sookaar nì Saayuul, ukanaannimpu jipɔɔn. Simeeyɔn naakookun yab naanjab yiŋŋi dee.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Meerarii jipɔmbi di sá Maalii nì Musii. Leefii dicaŋŋi yab nì bi-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ yiŋŋi dee.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Yitiseeyaar jipɔmbi yiŋŋi di sá Kooree nì Neefeegi nì Sikirii.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Usiyeel jipɔmbi yiŋŋi di sá Miisayeel nì Eeliisafan nì Sitirii.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aarɔn cáá Eelseeba, Amiinadaab bisal, Naasɔn niisal. U nìn màl̄-u Nadaab nì Abiyuu nì Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Aarɔn jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar cáá Putiyeel bisalib ubɔ, ní u màl̄-u Fineeyaasi. Leefii naakookun yab kpilib yiŋŋi dee.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn gbanti ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ní nyāntímaan Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin, bí nīn nóó tɔb akiti akiti kii bijanjaliibee.»

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn di nìn tí cūtìi sòon̄ nì Faaroo Eejipiti yab bɔtiu yii ú yàntī Isirayeel yab ń nyā u-tiŋkin. Unimbɔti fātìi būsì Mooyiisi u-poondi

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín nìn sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi Eejipiti tiŋkinee,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: u nìn bí-u yii: «Man di sá ni-Dindaan. Á tùkù Faaroo Eejipiti yab bɔtiu tin kɔkɔ m sòon̄ nì see.»

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kíí-u yii: «Man kaa ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ mmɔntiim, mana ní Faaroo làá ŋmā kí pīlifiǹ-mi?»

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Pīlifì, m làá dū-si kí kpántí kii Unimbɔtee ní Faaroo cee, ní a-maan Aarɔn ń nīn sá a-bɔnaatiliu.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Sii di làá tùkù Aarɔn tin kɔkɔ m sòon̄ nì see ní úǹ ń dūú nàatī Faaroo, án nín làá ŋá pu ú yàntī Isirayeel yab ń nyā u-tiŋkinee.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: Ama Faaroo kaa làá pīlifiǹ-ni. M làá dàkà Eejipiti yab m-pɔŋŋu, kí dáaĺ bi-tafal ŋkpitim pu, ní kí nyāntí m-nibul Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin bí nīn nóó tɔb akiti akiti kii bijanjaliibee.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M yaa láa dàkā-bi m-pɔŋŋu míǹ ki nyántì Isirayeel yab bi-kansikinee, niin ní bi dāa béetí yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: «Faaroo yaa bālifì-ni yii ní ŋá maamaaci ubɔee, á tùkù Aarɔn yii ú yòon̄ u-kpandɔŋu kí lúkú kitiŋ Faaroo nimbiin, ŋu làá kpántí ukoobu.»

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nín cá Faaroo cee, ní ki ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. Aarɔn dū u-kpandɔŋu ki lúkú kitiŋ Faaroo nì u-kpambaliŋ nimbiin, ní ŋu kpántì ukoobu.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo yíiń bibɔɔbi nì bikpaŋkpantiibi bin bí Eejipitee, ní bi mun dū bi-kpaŋkpantiiku ki ŋá míǹ mbaantiim.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Báà ŋma dū u-kpandɔŋu ki lúkú ní ŋu kpántì ukoobu. Ama ní Aarɔn kpandɔŋu dū bíǹ kpandɔi ki nátì.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Faaroo pɔbil gbíntìi pɔ̄ɔ̄ waa gbìl̄ ki tīiǹ Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn kii ti-Dindaan nín pée lī puee. Nnaabupeepeekaa: nnyim kpántì fatiku

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Faaroo pɔbil pɔ̄ɔ̄, waa là kí yàntī Isirayeel yab ń búntí.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Fool kutaafaauee, á fu kíntí Faaroo ŋyunti ŋun ní u cá dimɔɔgbandee. Ní cīití-u Niil mɔɔl caŋin. Á fu nín̄ ŋúb́ ŋkpandɔ ŋun a dūu kpántì ukoobuee a-ŋaan.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Á fu tùkū-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan Eebru yab Nimbɔtiu di túnní-mi ḿ dāá tùkù-si yii á yàntī u-nibul ń cù kuteeun kí jāam̀-u, ama ní ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, aa pílifiǹ-u.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: M làá dū m-kpandɔŋu nee kí fáá Niil nyim ní mí kpántí fatiku. Ti-Dindaan bí yii ḿ ŋá míǹ ní á béé yii úǹ di sá ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Ijɔm in kɔkɔ bí Niil mɔɔlinee làá kpú, ní nnyim ń bīil̀ ní Eejipiti yab kaa làá ti ŋmā kí nyɔ̀ nnyim gbanti.>»

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti bí Mooyiisi yii: «Tùkù Aarɔn yii ú yòon̄ u-kpandɔŋu kí tàntī Eejipiti yab nyiŋfii nì bi-buŋyi nì bi-nyimbɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ pu, án nín làá ŋá pu Eejipiti nyiŋfii kɔkɔ ń kpántí fatiku ki kpáaǹ bi-booŋŋi nì bi-lɔnti poonee.»

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. Aarɔn yōoǹ u-kpandɔŋu ki fáá nnyim min dɔ̄ Niil mɔɔlinee Faaroo nì u-kpambaliŋ nimbiin, ní ibun kɔkɔ nyim kpántì fatiku.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ní ijɔm in kɔkɔ bí dimɔɔlinee kpíì, ní dimɔɔl nyim núukì. Ní Eejipiti yab kaa ti ŋūǹ kí nyɔ̀-mì. Niinee Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ dūu kpántì fatiku.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ama Eejipiti yab kpaŋkpantiibi mun dū bi-kpaŋkpantiiku ki ŋá míǹ mbaantiim. Faaroo pɔbil pɔ́ɔkì waa pílifì Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn, kii ti-Dindaan nín pée lī puee.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Faaroo fātìi nín gítí u-dumpu kaa fātìi tɔ́ tin jítèe poon tiba.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Ní Eejipiti yab kíĺ ki bíi gbì anyimbɔbil Niil mɔɔl caŋin ki nyàab̀ nnyim kí nyɔ̀, kun puee baa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí nyɔ̀ dimɔɔl nyim.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Niil mɔɔl kpántì fatiku míǹ ki tin sāā iwiin iluli. Nnaabuliliiti: kpaabi

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Tùkù Aarɔn yii ú tàntī u-kpandɔŋu kí túĺ ikpin nì ibun nì anyimbɔbil ní kpaabi ń nyā kí gbí Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn tāntì u-kpandɔŋu ibun kɔkɔ pu, ní kpaabi nyáń ki gbí Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kíí-u yii: «Yóoń-mi ŋyunti ŋun a là ḿ dāá mèè kí tīī si nì a-kpambaliŋ nì a-nibulee, án nín làá ŋá pu ti-Dindaan ń kúntí kpaabi a-cee nì a-diiŋŋinee. Án làá pée kíń kpaabi bin kā Niil mɔɔlinee ŋmaniŋma ní.»

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Kpaabi làá fu wāŋkì kí wàatī sii nì a-diiŋŋi nì a-kpambaliŋ nì a-nibul, ní án fu kíń kpaabi bin bí Niil mɔɔlinee ŋmaniŋma.»

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nyáń Faaroo cee ní Mooyiisi mēē ti-Dindaan ú kúntí kpaabi bin u dūu dáaĺ Faaroo tafalee.

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Ní bi kóoǹ ki bíl̀ akpuku akpuku, ní kitiŋ fōō ki núukì.

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Tùkù Aarɔn ú dúkutí u-kpandɔŋu kí fáá kitiŋ dikpɔŋkpɔndi ń yīkì kí kpántí inaacib kí gbí Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Ní Eejipiti yab kpaŋkpantiibi mun nìn mākaǹ kí dū bi-kpaŋkpantiiku kí kpántí inaacib, ama ní kaa ŋúń. Inaacib nìn mɔ̄tìi dɔ́miń ki bīiǹ binib nì tiwaŋkuti pu.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Bikpaŋkpantiibi bí Faaroo yii: «An sá Unimbɔti pɔŋŋu di bíi tūǹ ditundi din bí nee.» Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Faaroo nìn pɔ́ɔkì u-pɔbil. Waa nìn pílifiǹ Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn pée tùkū-bi puee. Nnaabunanaati: ikpiŋki

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Fool kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, á fu péé ki kíntí Faaroo ŋyunti ŋun u yaa fu nyáń ki cá dimɔɔgbandee kí tùkù-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan bí yii á yàntī m-nibul ń búntí kí cùú jāam̀-mi.

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: A yaa kaa yāntì bi búntèe, m làá yàntī ikpiŋki ń fu nyā sii nì a-kpambaliŋ nì a-tiŋki nib pu nì a-diiŋŋin. Ikpiŋki gbanti làá kpátí kí gbí Eejipiti yab diiŋŋin kí kpáaǹ kitiŋ laakin bi yúee.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Ama yaadalee, m làá gàntī Gooseen tiŋki laakin m-nibul kóòyee. Baa làá ká ikpiŋki gbanti báà ubɔ niin, ní á béé yii man ni-Dindaan bí kitiŋ nee poon.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Niinee m làá dāá fīī m-yab ní digàntil ń dòon̄ man nibul nì sii yal kansikin. Fool ní kudaaŋŋu gbanti làá fu ŋá.>»

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan lafun ŋá kii u nín lī puee. U yāntì ikpiŋki dɔ́miń ki gbí Faaroo cindin nì u-kpambaliŋ diiŋŋin, ní Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ dūu kpántì ikpiŋki ŋma.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Faaroo yíiń Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn ní ki bí-bi yii: «Cùmaan kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī ni-Nimbɔtiu kitiŋ nee poon, ní taa nyā!»

english_verse: “The Lord's people in Goshen won't be bothered by flies, but your people in the rest of the country will be tormented by them. That's how you will know that the Lord is here in Egypt. This miracle will happen tomorrow.”
translation_verse: An puee ti làá nyā kí còom̀ iwiin ita kuteeu pu ní ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ń dàkà-ti saraabi bin an sá tí ŋá kí tīī-uee.»

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bí-bi yii: «M kíí kí yàntī ní cù kuteeu pu kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, ama ní taa nyā kí cù ndan. Ní mèèmaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kí tīī-mi.»

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn ŋá min Mooyiisi bālifèe, ki kúntì ikpiŋki Faaroo nì u-kpambaliŋ nì u-tiŋki nib cee, báà ukpiŋki kaa ti kíǹ.

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Ama min bí nee muee, Faaroo fātìi tí pɔ́ɔkì u-pɔbil kaa yāntì Isirayeel nibul búntì.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Cù Faaroo cee kí tùkù-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan Eebru yab Nimbɔtiu bí-si yii á yàntī u-nibul ń nyā kí cùú jāam̀-u.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: ti-Dindaan làá yàntī bìlbil kúm ń jēetí a-waŋkuti tin bí a-satinee pu. Bìlbil kúm min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee làá jēetí a-taamui nì a-gutaamui nì a-mammu nì a-naai nì a-piii nì a-ŋoobui pu.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī digàntil ń dòon̄ Isirayeel yab waŋkuti nì Eejipiti yab waŋkuti kansikin. Isirayeel yab waŋkuluku báà kubɔbɔ kaa làá kpú.»

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yóoǹ ŋyunti ki bí yii: «Fool ní m làá fu yàntī an bɔti ń jītí Eejipiti tiŋki pu.»

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní ti-Dindaan ŋá min u bí yii u làá ŋée. Eejipiti yab waŋkuti kɔkɔ kpíì, ama Isirayeel yab waŋkuluku báà kubɔbɔ kaa kpíì.

english_verse: When the king found out, he was still too stubborn to let the people go. Sores
translation_verse: Faaroo tú binib cūtìi kpēē ní ki ká yii Isirayeel yab waŋkuluku báà kubɔ kaa kpíì. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, u pɔ́ɔkì u-pɔbil kaa yāntì Isirayeel yab nyáń. Nnaabululuuti: anal

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii: «Jáfímaan dibubul poon ŋfantam aŋaŋkul ali kí nīn ŋúb́, ni yaa bàn̄ Faaroo ceeyee, Mooyiisi ń dūú yàaǹ kutaa pu Faaroo nimbiin.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Án làá kpántí kukpɔŋkpɔŋu ní kí bìin̄ Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ pu, ní án yàntī anal ń tɔ̄ binib nì tiwaŋkuti wunti pu kí kpántí ibuun Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔn.»

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn jáfì ŋfantam ki bàn̄ ki ká Faaroo, ní Mooyiisi dū ŋfantamee ki yāaǹ kutaa pu Faaroo nimbiin, ní an yāntì anal tɔ́ binib nì tiwaŋkuti wunti pu ki kpántì ibuun.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ibuun gbanti puee, Eejipiti yab kpaŋkpantiibi kaa ŋúń ki yúl̀ Mooyiisi nimbiin, kun puee ibuun nìn píń bi mun wunti pu kii an nín nìn píń Eejipiti yab kɔkɔ wunti pu puee ní.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan nìn pɔ́ɔkì Faaroo pɔbil ní waa pílifiǹ Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn pée tùkū Mooyiisi puee. Nnaabululuúti: ataanyiŋkumbil

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Fool kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, á fu cù Faaroo cee kí tùkù-u yii ti-Dindaan Eebru yab Nimbɔtiu bí-u yii: <Á yàntī m-nibul ń nyā kí cùú jāam̀-mi.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Di sá kɔŋkɔnnee, m làá dū nnaabu nín bí pu ŋu-ba ŋu-bee kɔkɔ kí tɔ̄ si nì a-kpambaliŋ nì a-tiŋki nib kɔkɔ pu, ní á béé yii ubɔ kaa bí kitiŋ nee pu kí dū u-ba kí ŋmàntīǹ man.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: M bàà dūmaan bìlbil kúm ki kúntì sii nì a-tiŋki nib dooooyee kí dàkà m-pɔŋŋu. Naŋkɔnampu nee, ni bàà kpíì ki céetì kitiŋ pu pílpil.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Ama m yāntì á nīn bí kí ŋmā kí dàkà-si m-pɔŋŋu ní m-yindi ń gbìtī ilaan kɔkɔ.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, aa pú m-nibul nsan bí nyā.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee yàntī bí kóoǹní a-waŋkuti nì tin kɔkɔ a cáá an bí tisatinee kí cáań mmɔŋki. Kun puee utaaja làá fu nì, ní ataanyiŋkumbikpaan ń fu lítí kí kpɔ̀ binib nì tiwaŋkuti tin bí tisatin kaa kūnní mmɔŋkee.>»

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Faaroo kpambaliŋ bin nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaanee nìn yāntì bi-tɔntɔnliibi kpáaǹ tiwaŋkuti ki kūnnì mmɔŋki.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Ama ní bin kaa nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaanee kaa nìn dū tibɔtee ki túń ditundi, ní ki yāntì bi-tɔntɔnliibi nì bi-waŋkuti bí tisatin.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Yòon̄ a-ŋal kí túĺ kutagbɔŋu utaaja ń nì ataanyiŋkumbikpaan ń lítí binib nì tiwaŋkuti nì tikpaajin tin kɔkɔ bí Eejipiti tiŋkinee pu.»

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Utaaja nìn̄ ataanyiŋkumbikpaan lítì nì itaaŋmɔŋmɔ tikpil. U nìn nìn̄ mpɔn mpɔn tikpil. Doooo Eejipiti tiŋki nín kíĺ ki bí ki dāa sāā an yuntiŋuee, an taajau juti kaa láá nìn̄ míǹ ki ká.

english_verse: People, animals, and crops were pounded by the hailstones, and bark was stripped from trees.
translation_verse: Ataanyiŋkumbikpaan nìn lítì Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ, ki kūū kūū binib nì tiwaŋkuti tin bí tisatinee. Ŋi nìn bíil̀ tikpaajin kɔkɔ ki kɔ́fì isufi in yú tisatinee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: See Gooseen tiŋki laakin Isirayeel yab kóòyee baba ní utaaja nì ataanyiŋkumbikpaanee kaa gbēē.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Niinee Faaroo yíiń Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn ní ki bí-bi yii: «Min bí nee, m béè yii m yīntì. Ni-Dindaan di sá deedeedaan ní man nì m-nibul fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Mèèmaan ni-Dindaan, utaaja nì ataanyiŋkumbikpaan nì itaatantati ń gbèen̄. M làá yàntī ní nyā, maa làá ti tàan̄-ni.»

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-u yii: «M yaa nyáń kitiŋ poonee, m làá yòon̄ m-ŋalii kí túĺ ti-Dindaan watil pú kí mèè-u, ataanyiŋkumbikpaan nì itaatantati kɔkɔ làá ŋmīĺ ní á béé yii ti-Dindaan di yì kitiŋ kɔkɔ.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Ama m nyí yii nì míǹ kɔkɔee, sii nì a-kpambaliŋ kaa làá tí fàŋkì ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti.»

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Utaajee nìn nìn̄ ki bíil̀ gulfa nì tijimpin tin bi yíì ɔɔjee, kun puee ɔɔji nìn bíi búù, ní gulfa bíi púkuḿ.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Ama tijimpin tin bi yíì bilee nì seegilee tíǹ kaa lòoǹ malaa, an pu ní utaajee kaa nìn bíil̀ tíǹ..

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi yíkì Faaroo cee ki nyáń kitiŋinee ní ki yōoǹ u-ŋalii ki túĺ ti-Dindaan watil pú ki mēē, ní utaaja nì ataanyiŋkumbikpaan nì itaatantati gbēeǹ.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Faaroo ká yii utaaja nì ataanyiŋkumbikpaan nì itaatantati gbēeǹee, ní u nìkī ikpiti diŋál ní u nì u-kpambaliŋ fātìi pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Faaroo pɔbil nìn pɔ́ɔkì ní u yíì kaa yāntì Isirayeel yab nyáń, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī Mooyiisi pu ki sòon̄ puee.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Cù Faaroo cee, di sá man di pɔ́ɔkì u nì u-kpambaliŋ pɔbiliŋ kí ŋmā kí nyāntí m-maamaacidaanti bi-kansikin bí ká.

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní si mun ń ká kí dāá māafì a-biyaamu nì a-naantiibi m nín dátì Eejipiti yab tafal puee nì m nín ŋá maamaacidaanti tin bi-tiŋkinee. Min làá yàntī ní béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaanee dee.»

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn cūtìi ká Faaroo ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan Eebru yab Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: <Kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá gbèen̄ a-pɔɔgbifiŋŋu kí sìntī a-ba taapu kí tīī-mi ní? Yàntī m-nibul ń nyā kí cùú jāam̀-mi.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: A yaa yíì kaa yāntì m-nibul nyáńee, fool m làá fu tɔ̄ń inaakitoon a-tiŋki kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: I làá dāan̄ kí kpátí kí bìin̄ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu bí taa ti wāl̀-kì. I làá dāá ŋmɔ́ ki céetí tin nìn kíǹ utaaja kaa bíil̀ee, nì isufi in bí tisatinee.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Inaakitoon làá dāan̄ kí gbí a-diiŋŋin nì a-kpambaliŋ kɔkɔ diiŋŋin nì Eejipiti yab kɔkɔ diiŋŋin. Doooo a-naanjab ki dāa dūu sāā a-baabi, bi nín kíĺ ki bí kitiŋ pu ki dāa dūu sāā díǹ nee, baa láá ká an bɔti juti ki ká.» Mooyiisi lī mimmee ní ki nyáń Faaroo cee ki búntì.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Faaroo kpambaliŋ bí-u yii: «Kijapaai nee làá nīn pée cāabìń-ti mbusu ní. An puee yàntī binib nee ń nyā kí cùú jāam̀ bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu. Aa ká yii an bíi nàantí ti-tiŋkaaa?»

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Ní bi fātìi yíiń Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn Faaroo cee, ní u bí-bi yii: «Nín̄ cámaan! Ní cùú jāam̀ ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. Ama, bilab nì bilab di cá ní?»

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kíí-u yii: «Ti nì ti-nipɔmbi nì ti-jaŋkpilib nì ti-nimpunaatiibi nì ti-jipɔmbi nì ti-bisalib nì ti-ŋoobui nì ti-piii nì ti-naai kɔkɔ di làá cù. Kun puee an sá ti-Dindaan jiŋaaliu ní ti làá cùú jī kí tīī-u tinyool.»

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bí-bi yii: «Baaa! M yaa yāntì ni nì ni-nimpoobi nì ni-biyaamu búntèe, ni-Dindaanee lafun bí ni-cee! Ni cáá ilandɔkɔkpiti páaa!

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: M yíì kpataaa! Bininjab baba ń cùú jāam̀ ni-Dindaan, kun puee kun ni mēē-mee dee.» U lī mimmee ní bi jìn̄-bi Faaroo cee ki nyántì.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Tàntī a-ŋal Eejipiti tiŋki pu inaakitoon ń dāan̄ kitiŋ pu kí ŋmɔ́ kí céetí kitiŋ pu mooti kɔkɔ, nì tin kɔkɔ kíǹ utaaja kaa bíil̀ee.»

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Mooyiisi tāntì u-ŋal Eejipiti tiŋki pu, ní ti-Dindaan yāntì kubuŋu kubɔ nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki jítì kitiŋee pu ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kɔkɔ. Kutaa wúntèe ní kubuŋuee cáań inaakitoon.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Ní i dɔ́miń ki gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu laaba kaa kíǹ. I nìn dɔ́miń ki wīikí tikpil tikpil, baa láá ká an naakitooŋyee wíiŋŋu míǹ dalba, kaa làá gíti ká míǹ mun dalba.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: I kpátìi bīiǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu bɔ̀mmm ní baa ti wāĺ-kì. Ní i ŋmɔ́ ki céetì kitiŋee pu mooti nì isufi in nìn kíǹ utaaja kaa bíil̀ee biliŋ. Kumɔsɔŋu kaa nìn kíǹ kitiŋ pu, míǹ ní kufaasɔŋ kaa nìn kíǹ busubu pu tisatin nì Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Niin niin ní Faaroo tú bi yíiń Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn ní ki bí-bi yii: «M yīntiǹ ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ki yīntiǹ ni mun.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Ní gíti dū m-kpitii kí pɔ̄-mi min bí nee mun, kí mèè ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ú tí kàkatī ŋkúm tafadaaldi nee kí wàatī-mi.»

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nyáń Faaroo ceeyee ní ki mēē ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kubɔ nyánní ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ki kpāā inaakitoon kɔkɔ ki cáa tɔ́ Tikati mɔɔl poon. Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poonee, baa nìn gíti kāntí unaakitoon báà ubambaanti.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan nìn pɔ́ɔkì Faaroo pɔbil, an yāntì waa nìn pú Isirayeel yab nsan bí nyā. Nnaabuwawaati: Dibɔmbɔndi

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Yòon̄ a-ŋal yilpu, dibɔmbɔndi ń dāá bìin̄ Eejipiti tiŋki pu, kí nīn gbìfì unil ń ŋmā kí gbēē-dì nì u-ŋal.»

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi yōoǹ u-ŋal yilpu, ní dibɔmbɔŋkpaandi diba dɔ́miń Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ pu áli iwiin ita.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Iwiin ita gbanti poonee, Eejipiti yab báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋúń ki wál̀ u-juti, kaa nìn ŋúń ki céefì u-taal ki nyáń. Ama ní laakin Isirayeel yab kóòyee wāĺ bɔ́mbɔŋ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo yíiń Mooyiisi ki bí-u yii: «Nín̄ cámaan! Cùú jāam̀maan ni-Dindaan. Ni ŋūǹ kí kpáaǹ ni-biyaamu. Ama ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui nì ni-naai íǹ làá gbíntí doo.»

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kíí-u yii: «Sii a-ba di làá tīī-ti tiwaŋkuti tin ti làá dūú ŋá mpèé saraau nì bisaraawɔkaabi kí tīī ti-Nimbɔtiueeee?

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Ama ní ti-Dindaan mɔ̄tìi pɔ́ɔkì Faaroo pɔbil ní waa là kí pɔ̄ Isirayeel yab nsan bí nyā.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bí Mooyiisi yii: «Nyā m-cee doo! Á taa ti dāan̄ m-cee dalba dalba! Daliŋkin ní a yaa ti dɔ́miń ki yúl̀ m-nimbiinee, a làá kpú ní!»

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kíí-u yii: «A nín lī puee, an ŋān̄! Maa làá ti dāan̄ kí yūĺ a-nimbiin!»

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «M làá tɔ̄ń nnaabujoolkaa Faaroo nì Eejipiti yab pu. Míǹ boonee ní ú dāá nín yàntī ní nyā. U làá dāá jà-ni ní nyā doo talku.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee á sòoǹ nì Isirayeel yab, bininjab nì binimpoobi, báà ŋma ń mèè u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔ sindaariya nì animbil kúti wanti.»

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ká diyimɔɔl Eejipiti yab cee. Míǹ ní Faaroo kpambaliŋ nì Eejipiti yab kɔkɔ nìn tɔ́ Mooyiisi u-ba tiŋan Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn bí Faaroo yii: «Pīlifì, ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <M làá jītí Eejipiti tiŋki poon kunyataasiiu búmbum.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: Eejipiti tiŋki biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kɔkɔ làá kpú, kí kíĺ sii Faaroo un kā dibeejal pu nee jipɔŋkpiliu kí tin cáá sāā uyumbunimpu un nà idee jipɔŋkpiliu, nì tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ bipeepeekaamu.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Ikuŋkuunti làá dāá nīn tùm̀ Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ poon ní dàii. Doooo nee, baa láá pée gbìl̄ míǹ ki ká jaanjaan, ki kpá kí gíti ká míǹ mun jaanjaan.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab kansikinee, baa làá gbìl̄ kibɔkɔ gbóol̀ unil àá kuwaŋkuluu gba. Niinee ni làá béé yii man ni-Dindaan ŋá digàntil Isirayeel yab nì Eejipiti yab kansikin.>

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Niin ní a-kpambaliŋ bin kā nee làá dāan̄ m-cee kí gbàan̄ m-nimbiin ní kí bí-mi yii: <Sii nì a-nibul, nín̄ cámaan.> Míǹ boonee ní ḿ búntí.» Nì diŋuul ní Mooyiisi nìn nyáń Faaroo cee.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan gíti bi Mooyiisi yii: «Faaroo yaa kaa bíi pílifíǹ-nee, an sá ḿ ŋmā kí bùtī m-maamaaci tuŋkpaaŋŋi u-tiŋki poon ní.»

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nìn ŋá maamaaci tuŋkpaaŋŋi kupaau Faaroo nimbiin, ama ní ti-Dindaan pɔ́ɔkì u-pɔbil, ní waa yāntì Isirayeel yab nyáń u-tiŋkin ki búntì.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn Eejipiti tiŋkin yii:

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: «Uŋmal un poon ni bí nee ń nīn sá-ni uŋmapeepeekaa iŋmal poon. U làá nīn sá-ni dibindi poon ŋmapeepeekaau ní.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Ní kpāfì Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ kí sòoǹ nì bi yii: <Uŋmal nee poon iwiin saalaayee, kudicaŋu àá kunaakoou kamaa ń lēē dipibil àá diŋɔbil diba.

english_verse: If any family is too small to eat the whole animal, they must share it with their next-door neighbors. Choose either a sheep or a goat, but it must be a one-year-old male that has nothing wrong with it. And it must be large enough for everyone to have some of the meat.
translation_verse: Kuwaŋkuluu kun bi làá kpɔ̀ee máaǹ kí nīn sá uja ki cáá dibindi diba, ku-laaba ń taa nīn wɔ̀b̄. Án ŋūǹ kí nīn sá diŋɔbil àá dipibil.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Ní kpāafì kuwaŋkuluu gbanti áli uŋmal poon ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal. An joopɔŋkuee, Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ ń kóoǹ kí kpāfì ní kudicaŋu kamaa ń kpɔ̀ ku-waŋkuluku.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Kudii kun kamaa poon ní ni kūū kuwaŋkuluu ki ŋmɔ́ee, ní dū fatiku kí ŋmìtī idɔ ili in pu punuu nákée nì ndɔ ŋun làl̄ punuu yilpuee.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Ní ŋɔ̄fì tinan gbanti, ní kunyeeuee, ní ŋmɔ́-tì nì kpɔnɔ un baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nì tifaal tin tūee.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Ní taa ŋmɔ́-tì tikaal, kí taa tɔ́kɔń-tì mun, ama ní ŋɔ̄fì-tì kí kpáaǹ diyil nì ayaka nì ina.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Ní taa ŋmɔ́-tì kí kíń fool. Tin yaa kíǹ kutaa wúntèe, ní dūú wà ŋŋmi.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Ni nín làá nīn bí min kí jī tijin gbantee sèé: ní gbìn̄ dambalab ni-cammu án cúú ni-wampeeŋkaati, kí táká ni-naatakaŋ, kí nīn ŋúb́ ni-kpandɔi ni-ŋaan, ní kí jī tijin gbanti malaa malaa. Dilákatil jiŋaaliu un ni làá jī kí tīī man ni-Dindaan tinyoolee dee.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: «Kunyeeu gbantee, m làá dāá jītí Eejipiti tiŋkin kí kpɔ̀ Eejipiti tiŋki biseebiyaamu kɔkɔ, kí kíĺ binib kí dāá sāā tiwaŋkuti. M làá dāá dáaĺ Eejipiti yab waaŋi kɔkɔ tafal. Man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama adiin ŋin nimbi kóòyee, fatiku di làá nīn sá-ni diwundi. M yaa láa ká fatikuee ní ḿ lákatí ni-pu, ní nimbi ń ŋmátí ŋkúm tafadaaldi din m dūu tɔ́ Eejipiti yab puee.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Ní ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee iwiin iluli. Kí kíĺ ŋwimpeepeekaa dalee, bí taa ti ká ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ ubɔ dumpu. Kí yòon̄ ŋwimpeepeekaa dal kí cáá sāā iwiin ilulee, un yaa ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔ un bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel nibul kansikin.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Ŋwimpeepeekaa dalee, ní kóoǹ kí kpāfì kí jāam̀-mi, ní ŋwinluluúti dal muee, ní tí kóoǹ kí kpāfì kí jāam̀-mi. Ní taa tɔ̄ ditundi diba ŋwiin gbanti, see tijin tin ni làá ŋá báà ŋma ń jēe baba.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: «Kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee jiŋaaliu sá ní nīn jīǹ ki téetí ŋwiin ŋun m nìn nyántì m-nibul Eejipiti tiŋkinee ní. Ní nīn jīǹ jiŋaal gbanti kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Án nīn sá-ni dibɔkpaal din kaa kpántée.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ uŋmapeekaa poon ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal kujoopɔŋ kí tin cáá sāā iwiin mmuŋku nì ŋubɔ dal kujoopɔŋuee, ní taa ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Bí taa ká ubɔ dumpu ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli. An yaa sá unicaan àá Isirayeel yab ubɔ di yaa ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔ un poon ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ ŋmàl̄ee, bí nyāntí udaan Isirayeel nibul kansikin.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Ní taa pée jī tijin tin poon bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee báà tiba. Báà laakin ní ni yaa pée bàn̄ ki kóòyee, ní taa ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin poon bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee.» Dilákatil jiŋaaliu jinti bɔ́ntitam

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi yíiń Isirayeel kpilib kɔkɔ ki kpáfì, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Kudicaŋu kamaa ń cùú nyàab̀ dipibil àá diŋɔbil kí kpɔ̀ kí jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Ní lēēmaan tifaapibiti tin bi yíì isɔpee bambiliŋ kí ŋá kibɔŋ kí dūu sēē kuwaŋkuluu kun ni kūū ki lēē fatiku ki ŋá disambil poonee. Ní dūú ŋmìtī idɔ ili in pu punuu cɔ́ee nì ndɔ ŋun làl̄ punuu yilpuee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ubɔ ń taa ti nyā kí cáá sāā kutaafaau.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá jītí kí dáaĺ Eejipiti yab tafal. Ama u yaa ká fatiku mpunyɔmu puee, u làá jītí ní kaa làá yàntī ŋkúm tafadaaldi ń kɔ́ ni-ciŋŋin.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa bàn̄ ki kɔ́ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan pōoǹ kí tīī-nee poonee, ní dāá nīn ŋáań akoobil gbanti.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Ni-biyaamu yaa láa bālifì-ni yii akoobil gbanti taapu sá yii bee,

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: ní dāá kíí-bi yii: <An sá saraa un ti ŋáań ki tìì ti-Dindaan Dilákatil jiŋaaliu yuntiŋuee ní. Ŋyunti ŋun ti-naanjab nìn bí Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ti-Dindaan nìn kūū Eejipiti yab. Ama u nìn lákatì timbi diiŋŋi pu kaa yúl̀, ní ki wúń ti-dicaŋŋi pu.>» Niinee ní Isirayeel yab tātìi gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi búntì ki cūtìi ŋá min ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii bí ŋée. Nnaabujoolkaa: Eejipiti yab biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kúm

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Kunyataasiiuee ní ti-Dindaan kūū Eejipiti tiŋkin mbiseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kɔkɔ, ki kíliń Faaroo un kā dibeejal puee jipɔŋkpiliu ki tin cáa sāā usarkadaan un kā u-sarkadiikunee jipɔŋkpiliu nì tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ bipeepeekaamu njamu.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Faaroo nì u-kpambaliŋ nì Eejipiti yab kɔkɔ yíkì kunyeeuee, dituweel fōō ki píĺ kitiŋ kɔkɔn dàii, kun puee dicindi diba nìn kpá unil kaa kpíì di-poon.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Kunyataasiiu gbantee ní Faaroo yíiń Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn ní ki bí-bi yii: «Yīkì kí nyāmaan m-tiŋkin, ni nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ! Cùú jāam̀maan ni-Dindaan kii ni nín bālifì puee!

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Yòon̄ kí kpáam̀maan ni-waŋkuti kɔkɔ kii ni nín bālifì puee kí nīn cámaan. Ní mèèmaan kí bìin̄ m-pu.»

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Eejipiti yab dākafì yii bi làá kpú kí dóó ní, an pu ní bi nìn jì Isirayeel yab bí nyā bi-tiŋkin malaa malaa.

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: An puee Isirayeel yab nìn yíkèe, bi nìn tú bukpɔnɔsaa bun kaa jɔ́m̀ee ní, ní ki dū kikabiki kin bi cáa nùkù bukpɔnɔsaayee ki póob́ abɔkutin ki dūu būkuǹ.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn ŋá kii Mooyiisi nín nìn tùkū-bi puee. Bi nìn mēē Eejipiti yab sindaariya nì animbil wanti nì tiwampeeŋkaal.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ká diyimɔɔl Eejipiti yab cee, di sá bi nìn kíí ki tīī Isirayeel yab tin bi mēēyee. Míǹ ní Isirayeel yab nìn dī ki fúkúl̀ Eejipiti yab!

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn yíkì Ramseesi tiŋkin ki búntì Sukooti tiŋkin. Bininjab nìn sá kii kutukub alaataa aluu nyɔkɔm ní ki còom̄ ataa pu. Baa nìn kàan̄ ki kpáaǹ mbiyaamu nì binimpoobi.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Biniyaŋyambi tikpil mun nìn nóó-bi ki búntì ní bi nìn cáá tipicaŋkpun nì tiŋɔcaŋkpun nì tinacaŋkpun tikpil.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū bukpɔnɔsaa bun bi nìn cáań Eejipiti tiŋkinee ki ŋá kalaabi bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee, di sá yii bi nín nìn jìn̄-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee puee, baa nìn ŋúń ki kāl̀ ki cíitì bukpɔnɔsaayee ń jɔ̄m̀. Baa nìn ŋúń ki bɔ́ntì tijin tin bi làá nīn jīǹ ki còom̄ nsanee.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn cíitì kunyeeu gbanti kɔkɔ ní ki nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin. An puee, kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaanee, Isirayeel yab máaǹ kí nīn kàal̀ kunyeeu gbanti kí taa gèeǹ, di sá yii ti-Dindaan di yì kunyeeu gbanti. Dilákatil jiŋaaliu marab

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii: «Kpèè, Dilákatil jiŋaaliu marab sèé: <Unicaan báà ubɔ kaa cáá nsan kí jī jiŋaal gbanti jinti.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: <Á gíí uyumbu un a dá nì animbilee dikpancandi kí wàatī ní ú nín jī jiŋaal gbanti jinti.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: <Unicaan un kɔ́-see nì upaadaan kaa cáá nsan kí jī jiŋaalee jinti.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: <Ní nīn kā adiinni ní kí ŋmɔ́ jiŋaalee nanti. Ubɔ ń taa kpáaǹ tinan kí nyā mmɔŋki. <Ní taa wīī kuwaŋkuluuee kpabil báà diba.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: <Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ ń jī jiŋaal gbanti.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: <Unicaan un kɔ́-nee yaa là kí jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu kí tīī ti-Dindaan tinyoolee, ú gíí u-dicaŋku yab bininjab kɔkɔ akpancan. Niinee udaan ŋūǹ kí jī jiŋaal gbanti kii Isirayeel yab ntindambiyaamuee. <Ama un kaa gíí dikpancandee ń taa jī jiŋaal gbanti.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: «<Marab gbantee ń nīn sá ki tīī Isirayeel yab, kí nīn sá ki tīī binicambi bin kóò ni-tiŋkinee.>»

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn mara yii bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti ní ti-Dindaan nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin bi nóó tɔb akiti akiti kii bijanjaliibee.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: «Á dū Isirayeel yab biseebiyaamu bininjab kɔkɔ kí sú-mi. Di sá yii unimpu kamaa biseebiki kininjabiki nì kuwaŋkuluu kamaa bipeepeekaaki kijaka sá ki tīī man ní.»

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yaa cáá-ni ki kɔ́ǹ Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab timmunee, ní dāá nīn ŋáań akoobil nee dibindi kamaa uŋmal nee poon ki tìì ti-Dindaan tinyool. Kitiŋ gbanti ní ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ ni-naanjab yii u làá dūú tīī-nee. Kitiŋ gbanti poon ní nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní dū iwiin iluli kí ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. Ŋwinluluúti dalee, ní jī jiŋaal kí tīī ti-Dindaan tinyool.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Iwiin iluli gbanti poonee, ní taa ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin poon bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. Ni-tiŋki kɔkɔ poonee, bí taa ká ni-cee kpɔnɔ un poon bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee àá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ ŋu-ba.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Jiŋaal gbanti poonee, ní dāá māafì ni-biyaamu yii: <Ti ŋáań míǹ ti-Dindaan nín nìn ŋá min ki tīī-ti ti nín nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin puee ní.»
