english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Jiŋaal gbanti ń dāá nīn sá-ni diteetil, kí dāá nīn sá-ni kudaaŋŋu ni-ŋalii nì ni-yigbeeŋi pu, ní kí nīn téetí-ni yii ni máaǹ kí nìn sòoǹ ti-Dindaan marau pu, kun puee an sá nì u-ŋampɔŋŋu ní u nyántì-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Dibintil kamaa jiŋaal nee wiiŋŋu yaa bāańee, ní ŋá min mara nee bí yii ní ŋée.

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá cáá-ni kí kɔ́ǹ Kanaan tiŋkin kii u nín nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ni nì ni-naanjab yii u làá dū-kì kí tīī-ni puee.

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní dāá dū ni-biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kí sú ti-Dindaan. Ni-waŋkuti bipeepeekaamu njamu mun sá ti-Dindaan wanti ní.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Ní dū upii àá uŋoobu kí kpántí kimaŋ bipeepeekaaki kijaka. Ni yaa kaa kpántèe, ní nyīī kí gíí ki-sil kí kpú. Ama ni-nibul poon biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamuee, ní pà mu-pu.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Boonee ni-biyaamu yaa láa bíi bàlifī-ni yii ba pu ní ni ŋáań mimmee, ní dāá kíí-bi yii: <Kun pu ti ŋáań mimmee di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn dū u-ŋampɔŋŋu ní ki nyántì-ti kuyuŋu poon Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Faaroo nìn yíì kpataaa yii u kpá kí líí-ti tí búntí. Niinee ti-Dindaan yāntì Eejipiti yab biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu nì bi-waŋkuti bipeepeekaamu njamu kpíì kɔkɔ. An pu ní ti cáá ti-waŋkuti bipeepeekaamu njamu ki ŋáań saraa ki tìì ti-Dindaan, ní ki pà ti-biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu pu.>

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Míǹ puee tin ti bíi ŋáań nee ń nīn sá-ni kudaaŋŋu ni-ŋalii nì ni-yigbeeŋi pu, kí nīn téetí-ni yii ti-Dindaan nìn dū u-ŋampɔŋŋu ní ki nyántì-ti Eejipiti tiŋkin. Unimbɔti līī u-nibul nyɔkɔpu

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Faaroo nín nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab nyáń u-tiŋkinee, Unimbɔti kaa nìn yāntì bi dī Fiiliistii yab tiŋki saŋŋu, niin mun di kaa bàà dátì. Unimbɔti nìn lī u-ban yii: «Binib nee yaa ká kujaau nsanni, bi-pɔbil làá yīkì ní bí bí yii bi làá fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin.»

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: An pu ní Unimbɔti nìn yāntì bi dūu dī kuteeu pú ki pɔ́tì ki tin nyáń Tikati mɔɔl pu. Isirayeel yab nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin ki nóó tɔb akiti akiti kii bijanjaliibee.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn kpáaǹ Jooseefi kpabiŋ, kun puee Jooseefi nìn bí u-nabiyaamu yii: «Unimbɔti làá jòoń-ni ní nyā kitiŋ nee poon. Ní pùtī yii ni làá dāá kpáaǹ m-kpabiŋ.»

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn yíkì Sukooti tiŋki ní ki cūtìi gāā bi-tantib Eetaam tiŋki, kuteeu kúntilaŋki.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: «Tùkù Isirayeel yab bí fàtīí gítí Pii-Ayirooti tiŋki caŋin, Miigidool nì dimɔɔl kansikin. Bí gāā bi-tantib kí kàl̄ niin kí nīn túĺ Baal-Seefɔn tiŋkin, dimɔɔl caŋin.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Faaroo làá sòoǹ ni-pu yii: <Naŋkɔnampu Isirayeel yab gáatì ki túĺ ti-tiŋki laaba pú ki tú ki yìiǹ ní kuteeu dū-bi ki náĺ.>

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: M làá lùkutì Faaroo ní ú jàń ni-boon. Di sá yii Faaroo nì u-janjaliibi di làá yàntī bí ká man nyooti. Niinee Eejipiti yab làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.» Ní Isirayeel yab ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn tùkū Faaroo yii Isirayeel yab yíkì. Niinee ní u nì u-kpambaliŋ landɔkɔŋu cúu kpántì bi-pu, ní bi bí yii: «Ba ní ti ŋá nan ní? Ba pu ní án nín bàà sá tí nīn ŋúb́ Isirayeel yab bí nīn sá ti-yumbuyee, ti yāntì bi nyáń ki búntì ní?»

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Faaroo kpàl̄ u-janjatɔrɔkub taamui, ki yōoǹ u-janjaliibi bi nín jì bi-boon.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn pɔ́ɔkì Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo pɔbil, ní u yíkìi bíi jì Isirayeel yab boon, ama ní bíǹ nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin nì dibatɔl nì ifaal.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Eejipiti yab janjaliibi nì Faaroo janjatɔrɔkub taamui nì bijanjaliibi bitanjakaliibi yíkìi kùl̄ ki páaǹ Isirayeel yab boon. Bi nìn cúú-bi dimɔɔl caŋin, Pii-Ayirooti watil pú ki túĺ Baal-Seefɔn tiŋki, laakin bi nìn gāā bi-tantib ki kāl̀ee.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab dāa béè yii Eejipiti yab bíi jìń bi-boonee, nì bi nín dāa ká yii Faaroo nì u-naacimbi tóobiń-bee, bi nìn fāŋkì tikpil ní ki nìn bíi kūuntí ki yíì ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí Mooyiisi yii: «Itaŋkpiifal kaa bí Eejipiti tiŋkinaaa? Ba pu ní a cáań-ti tí kpú kuteeun doo? Ba pu ní a yāntì ti yíkìń Eejipiti tiŋkin ní?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Ti nín nìn dáá bíń Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ti nìn tùkū ki cántì-si yii: <Yàntī-ti tí nīn sá Eejipiti yab yumbui. An sɔ́ tí nīn tūǹ atuun ki tìì Eejipiti yab ki jítiǹ tí kpú kuteeun.>»

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn kíí samaa yii: «Taa fàŋkìmaan! Nín̄ kāmaan soooo! Ni làá ká díǹ wiiŋŋu ti-Dindaan nín làá fīī-ni puee. Di sá yii Eejipiti yab bin ni wāĺ díǹ nee, ni pée gíti kpá kí ká-bi jaanjaan.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Nimbi dee, nín̄ kāmaan soooo, ti-Dindaan làá já kí tīī-ni.» Ti-Dindaan cátì nsan dimɔɔl kansikin

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Ba pu ní a kūuntí ki yíì-mi? Tùkù Isirayeel yab yii bí yīkì kí nīn còom̄ ki cá.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Sii yòon̄ a-kpandɔŋu kí dūú tàntī dimɔɔl pu kí cúú-dì kí búkutí mili nsan ń dòon̄ Isirayeel yab ń dùtī ŋkulimmi.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Man làá pɔ̄ɔkì Eejipiti yab pɔbiliŋ bí kɔ́ dimɔɔlin kí jà ni-boon. M làá dàkà Faaroo nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ nì u-janjatɔrɔkub, nì u-janjaliibi bitanjakaliibi m-nyooti.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ŋun nìn līī Isirayeel yab nyɔkɔpuee gítì bi-boon. Míǹ mbaantiim ní ditagbancancaal din nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpuee mun gítì bi-boon.

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: Di nìn cūtìi yúl̀ ki pītì Eejipiti yab kitil nì Isirayeel yab kitil kansikin. Eejipiti yab jandi púee, ditagbancancaalee nìn sá dibɔmbɔndi, ama ní Isirayeel yab jandi púee, di nìn ŋmíntí kunyeeu. An puee Eejipiti yab nì Isirayeel yab kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄ tɔb kunyeeu gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn tāntì u-ŋal dimɔɔl pu. Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì kubuŋu kubɔ nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki jítì mpɔn kunyamɔŋu ní ki téé dimɔɔl nyim. Dimɔɔl nìn cúu búkutì mili ní nsan dōoǹ ki kūń.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn cōom̀ ki jítì dimɔɔl kansikin ŋkulimmi, ní nnyim gāā aguŋkpaan bi-ŋaŋgiil pú nì bi-ŋaŋgan pú.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Ntaafaabɔmbɔmee ní ti-Dindaan un bí ditagbancancaal nì ŋŋmi poonee kpēē Eejipiti yab kitil pú, ní ki yāntì fìkil fikil kɔ́-bi.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: U nìn yāntì Eejipiti yab tɔrɔkub taaŋi kpàl̄ ki pɔ́ɔkì ní disaŋkindi ŋá-bi digìńdi. Ní bi bí yii: «Tí sām̀maan Isirayeel yab, kun puee bi-Dindaan kútì bi-pu bi bíi jáà nì ti!»

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Tàntī a-ŋal dimɔɔl pu nnyim ń fàtīí gítiń kí bìin̄ Eejipiti yab nì bi-janjatɔrɔkub nì bi-janjaliibi bitanjakaliibi pu.»

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn tāntì u-ŋal dimɔɔl pu. Kutaa tóob́ diwuntilee ní dimɔɔl fātìi gítì di nín nìn pée bí puee. Eejipiti yab bàà bí yii bí sāǹ ní ki dūu kɔ́ nnyimin, ní ti-Dindaan téé bi-kɔkɔ ki múĺ dimɔɔl kansikin.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Nnyim nìn fātìi gítìń ki bīiǹ Faaroo janjatɔrɔkub nì u-janjaliibi bitanjakaliibi kɔkɔ pu. Bin kɔkɔ nìn pée kɔ́ dimɔɔlin ki bíi jì Isirayeel yabee, ubambaanti kaa nìn ŋmátì.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab nìn cōom̀ ŋkulimmi dimɔɔl kansikin, ní nnyim gāā aguŋkpaan bi-ŋaŋgiil pú nì bi-ŋaŋgan pú.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan nìn dī ki nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti yab ŋaan ŋwiin gbanti. Isirayeel yab nìn wāĺ Eejipiti yab nín kpíì ki dɔ̄ dɔ̄ dimɔɔgbandee.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín nìn ká mpɔn ŋun ti-Dindaan nìn dàkā Eejipiti yabee ní bi fāŋkì-u, ní ki dū bi-mákal ki ŋá u nì u-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi nì Isirayeel yab gāā nlan nee ki pàkā ti-Dindaan yii: «M làá gāā nlan kí pàkà ti-Dindaan, kun puee u dàkā u nín sá ukpaan puee. U téé itaamu nì bitanjakaliibi ki tɔ́ dimɔɔlin.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di sá man pɔŋŋu, úǹ ní m làá nīn gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí. Úǹ di fīī-mi, úǹ di sá m-Nimbɔtiu, m làá nīn nyɔ́ŋkí-u. Úǹ di sá m-baa Nimbɔtiu, m làá yòon̄ u-yindi yilpu.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di sá ubaatandaan, u-yindi di sá ti-Dindaan.»

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: «U dū Faaroo janjatɔrɔkub nì u-janjaliibi ki tɔ́ dimɔɔlin. U-janjaliibi bimɔmmɔntiibi gbíntì Tikati mɔɔlin.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Nnyim bīiǹ bi-pu, bi sīntì nnyim taapu kii ditaŋkpalee.»

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan, a-ŋaŋgiil cáá mpɔŋkpaan, ŋúǹ di nàantí a-nannanliibi.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: A lafun sá ukpaaneeee! A lábitì a-nannanliibi ki cìb̄. A yaa gíí diŋuulee, a náań nì ŋŋmi ní, ní ki wù a-nannanliibi kii timoolee.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Kubuŋu kun nyēeń a-maŋfataabuŋyinee yāntì nnyim kóoǹ ki kpáfì. Nnyinjil yáatì ki yúl̀ kii digundee, nnyim min bí taapuee fōō ki pɔ́ɔkì dimɔɔl kansikin.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Binannanliibi nìn lī yii: <Ti làá jà bi-boon kí tin cúú-bi, kí yàkatī ti nín jáń ki fōō tin bi-ceeyee, ní kí nīn kíǹ ki cáá tikpil an lákatí. Ti làá fúutí ti-tàataajimmu ní kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi.>

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Ama ní sii ti-Dindaan púfì ní mmɔɔnyim bīiǹ bi-pu. An cáá-bi ki sīntì taapu nnyim poon poon kii tikúbɔnee.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: Óo ti-Dindaan, inimbɔti kansikinee, ŋma di bí kii sii? Ŋma di bí kii sii ki bí circir ki jìl̀ yéè? A sá un tūǹ atuŋkpaanee ki máaǹ inyɔŋki, a ŋáań maamaacib!

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: A tāntì a-ŋaŋgiil ní kitiŋ dū-bi ki náĺ.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: A dū a-neendi ki fōō a-nibul ki líì. A dū a-pɔŋŋu ki kpōotì-bi ki cáa cáǹ circir tiŋki kin a cúú ki síiǹ-bee.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Anibul gbìl̄ an bɔti ní tifaandi cúú-bi, ní Fiiliistii yab pɔbiliŋ bíil̀.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Dinyoondi nì tifaandi cúú-bi! Bi nín ká a-ŋampɔŋŋu ŋun a dūu jòoń-tee ní bi ŋmíl̀ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ kii ditaŋkpalee, áli a-nibul dāa jítì ki dóò, ti-Dindaan, dinibul din ní a dée.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: A cáǹ-bi a-jool din sá a-fakalee pu kí dū-bi kí kàan̄ niin. A bɔ́ntì mpaan kí nīn kóò niin, ti-Dindaan, Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun sii ti-Dindaan dū a-ŋalii ki máńee.

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Faaroo taamui nì u-janjatɔrɔkub nì u-tanjakaliibi nín kɔ́ dimɔɔlinee, ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì mmɔɔnyim bīiǹ bi-pu. Ama ní Isirayeel yab bíǹ dūtì dimɔɔl ŋkulimmi.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Niinee Aarɔn niisal Miiriyam un sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee yōoǹ kigaŋgaŋ, ní binimpoobi kɔkɔ mun dɔ́miń ki kútì u-pu nì bi-gaŋgammu ki bɔ̀ɔ́ ki ŋōō.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Binimpoobee yaa bíi gà ilanee ní Miiriyam ń kíí-bi yii: «Gāāmaan ilan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan, kun puee u dàkā u nín sá ukpaan puee. U téé itaamu nì bitanjakaliibi ki múĺ dimɔɔlin.» ISIRAYEEL YAB SAŊKINDI KUTEEUN (

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi yōoǹ Isirayeel yab bi yíkì Tikati mɔɔl ki túĺ Suur teeku watil. Bi cōom̀ iwiin ita kuteeun kaa ká nnyim kí nyɔ̀.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Bi nìn bàn̄ Maara ki ká nnyim, ama kaa ŋúń ki nyùn̄-mì, kun puee mi nìn tū. An pu ní bi kíǹ ki yíì niin yii Maara, taapu di sá yii <ntuntun>.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Ní samaa kɔkɔ kíĺ ki bíi wòoǹ Mooyiisi ki lì yii: «Ba ní ti làá nyɔ̀?»

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ní úǹ dàkā-u ndɔ ŋubɔ u dūu tɔ́ nnyimin ní mi mɔ́ɔkì. Niin ní ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Isirayeel yab marab nì akoobil, niin mun ní u nìn tí cɔ́ŋkì-bi.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: U nìn bí-bi yii: «Ni yaa pílifí man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín sòoǹ puee mmɔntiim, ki ŋáań tin bí deedee m-nimbiinee, ki yaa gbìl̄ m-marab ki ŋúb́ akoobil kɔkɔee, maa làá yàntī iween in m nìn dūu tɔ́ Eejipiti yab puee ń gbēē-ni. Di sá yii man di sá ni-Dindaan un cāantí-nee.»

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yíkì Eeliim tiŋkin ní ki bàn̄ Siini teeku kun bí Eeliim nì Siinaayi kansikinee. Isirayeel yab nín nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin uŋmaliliiti iwiin saalku dalee ní bi bàn̄ Siini teekun.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Kuteeun niinee ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ bíi wòoǹ Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan kaa yāntì ti kpíì ŋyunti ŋun ti nìn bí Eejipiti ki kā ki kɔ́ĺ anaŋkumboon ki jīǹ tijin ki díkèe. Ama ní ni yōoǹní samaa nee kɔkɔ ki cáań kuteeun ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀-bi!»

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «M làá tīī-ni tijin tin làá nīn nyēeń yilpu ki lítí kitiŋ kii utaa nín nì puee. Kutaa kamaayee binib làá nīn fà min làá ŋmàntī-bi ŋwiin ŋubɔ jītamee ní. M là kí cɔ̄ŋkì-ni kí kpèè yii ni làá nīn tɔ́ m-marabaaa, naa làá nīn tɔ́-bi.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Iwiin iluu dal, ni yaa láa fāā ki tɔ́kɔǹee, án làá bùtī mili pu kí jītíǹ ni nín kpààa fà pu ŋwiin kamaayee.»

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn bí Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yii: «Díǹ kujoou nee ní ni làá béé yii ti-Dindaan di nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Fool kutaafaauee, ni làá fu ká u-nyooti, kun puee ti-Dindaan gbìl̄ ni nín bíi gbùkum̄ puee. Ní taa dàkafì yii timbi ní ni wòoǹ. Timbi di sá bilab ní ni wòoǹ-ti?»

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Mooyiisi gíti bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan làá tīī-ni kujoou nee tinan ní ŋmɔ́, ní kutaafaauee ú fu tīī-ni tijin ní jī kí díkí, kun puee u gbìl̄ ni-gbukumii pu. Ní taa dàkafì yii timbi pu ní ni gbùkum̄. Timbi kaa pée sá tiba, an sá ti-Dindaan pu ní ni bíi gbùkum̄.»

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn yii: «Tùkù Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ bí sútiń kí dāan̄ ti-Dindaan nimbiin, kun puee u gbìl̄ bi-gbukumii pu.»

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Aarɔn fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki bíi sòoǹ nì bee, ní bi fātì bi-nimbiin ki túĺ kuteeu pú. Dicilpu kpalaayee ní ti-Dindaan nyooti cílìń bi-pu ditagbancancaal poon.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: «M gbìl̄ Isirayeel yab gbukumii pu. An puee tùkù-bi yii: <Kujoou nee, ni làá ŋmɔ́ tinan kí báĺ, ní fool kutaafaauee, ní fu jī tijin kí díkí ní kí béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.>»

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Kujoouee ní inoon iba, i bí kii njikpacimamuee dɔ́miń ki kpátìi gbí Isirayeel yab kaaŋu pu, ní kutaafaauee dimalindi bīiǹ bi-kaaŋu boon ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Dimalindee nín fóotèe ní mbilimu mbilimu mubɔ dōoǹ ki pīiǹ ki kpátìi gbí an kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kée kaa nyí kun an sée, ní ki bàlifī tɔb yii: «Ba wanti dee ní?» Ní Mooyiisi kíí-bi yii: «Tijin tin ti-Dindaan tīī-ni ní jēe dee.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín yóoǹ mara uŋyee sèé: <Ní fāā min unil kamaa ŋūǹ kí jēe. Báà ŋma ń fāā u-cindin niliu kamaa yil pu disambil diba kí sāā u-nib nyɔkɔm.>»

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn ŋá míǹ. Biba nìn fāā tikpil ki lákatì ní biba mun fāā fiii an kaa bàn̄.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi bí-bi yii: «Ubɔ ń taa kíń tijin kí kpāafì fool kutaafaau pu.»

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Ama biba kaa nìn pílifì Mooyiisi nín nìn lī puee, ní ki kíǹ tijin ki kpáafì kutaa wúntì. Ku wúntèe ní an sūū ki ŋá akoosibil. Niinee ní Mooyiisi fōō diŋuul bi-pu.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Kutaafaau sá kamaayee, báà ŋma nìn fà min làá ŋmàntī ú jēe ní. Ŋwìiń yaa nìn píĺee ní un kíǹee ń dùntī.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Iwiin iluu dalee ní bí fāā bi nín nìn kpààa pée fà puee mili pu, unil kamaa yil puee asambil ali. Ní Isirayeel yab kpilib dɔ́miń ki tùkū Mooyiisi an bɔti.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín yóoǹ mara uŋyee dee. Fool fu sá ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ní, ŋwiin ŋun sá ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋuee. Ní ŋàan̄ tin ni làá ŋàan̄ee, kí tɔ́kɔń tin ni làá tɔ́kɔńee. Tin yaa kíǹee, ní dūú kpāafì kí yóoń fool kutaafaau pu.»

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Ní bi bɔ́ntì tijin ki yóoǹ fool pu, kii Mooyiisi nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. Ku wúntèe an kaa sūūyaaa, akoosibil mun kaa kɔ́.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-bi yii: «Jīmaan tijin tin ni fu ŋá foolee díǹ, kun puee díǹ di sá ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ki tīī ti-Dindaan. Ni yaa nyáń mmɔŋki díǹ, naa làá ká báà tiba dɔ̄.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Ni làá nīn pée fà tijin míǹ ní iwiin iluu, see ŋwinluluúti ŋun sá ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaayee dal baba ní naa làá ká tiba ki fāā.»

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Isirayeel yab kansikin biba nìn nyáń ŋwinluluúti dal kí bàà tí cùú fāā ní kaa ká.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Ni làá nīn pée yíití m-marab nì m-dàkatam yéè kí tin cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Ní béé yii m tīī-ni ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ní dūú kàl̄ kí ŋùŋfì ní. An pu ní m tìì-ni iwiin iluu dal iwiin ili jinti, án nín làá ŋá pu winluli dalee, báà ŋma ń nīn kā u-dumpu kí taa nyā kí cù laabee.»

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab kíǹ ki kàal̀ ŋwinluluúti dal ki ŋùŋfī.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn pú tijin gbanti diyindi yii maana. U nìn bí mbilimu mbilimu ki pīiǹ, ní ki mɔ̄ kii tisiil kalaauee.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí yii: «Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé yii: <Ní lēē tijinee disambil diba kí kpāafì kí dāá nīn cáa dàkà ni-naantiibi bi mun ń ká ti-Dindaan nín nìn nyántìń-ni Eejipitee tijin tin u nìn cáa kpīintí-ni kuteeunee.>»

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn yii: «Fāā tijinee disambil diba kí ŋá diboolin ki cáá yóoń ti-Dindaan nimbiin, kí kpāafì-tì ni-naantiibi mun ń dāá yīkìí ká.»

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn bí Mooyiisi ń ŋá puee, Aarɔn nìn cáá tijinee nì dibool ki yóoǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi daaŋku nimbiin án ŋmā kí nīn bí ki téetí-bi.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yíkì Siini teekunee ní ki búntì, kii ti-Dindaan u-ba nín nìn bɔ́ntì bi-saŋkindi bí còom̀ puee. Bi bàn̄ Reefiidiimee ní ki kāl̀ niin, ama nnyim nìn kpá bí nyɔ̀.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi bíi nyàab̀ Mooyiisi kujaau ki lì-u yii: «Tīī-ti nnyim tí nyɔ̀!» Ní Mooyiisi bí-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni nyàab̀-mi kujaau? Ba pu ní ni cɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan?»

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Nnyinnyoo nìn gbìl̄ Isirayeel yab ní bi bíi wòoǹ Mooyiisi yii: «Ba pu ní a yōoǹní-ti Eejipiti tiŋkin ní? A là nnyinnyoo ń kpɔ̀ ti nì ti-biyaamu nì ti-waŋkuti níii?»

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ki lī yii: «M làá nín ŋá dinibul nee mana dee? An kíǹ fiii bí yāŋkì-mi ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀.»

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Lēē Isirayeel yab kpilib biba, kí yòon̄ a-kpandɔŋu ŋun a nìn dūu fáá dimɔɔlee kí lìntī samaa nyɔkɔpu ní nīn cá.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Man làá cùú yūĺ a-nyɔkɔpu Ooreeb jool pu ditaŋkpal pu. Á fáá ditaŋkpalee ní nnyim ń nyā samaa ń nyɔ̀.» Ní Mooyiisi ŋá min ti-Dindaan tùkū-uee Isirayeel yab kpilib nimbiin.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Ní bi pú niin diyindi yii Maasa nì Meeriiba, an taapu di sá <Icɔŋki> nì <Kujaau>. Di sá yii Isirayeel yab nìn nyàab̄ Mooyiisi kujaau ní ki cɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan mun ki lī yii: <Ti-Dindaan kalin bí ti-kansikinaaa, waa bí ní?> Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Amaleeki yab

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Amaleeki yab dɔ́miń Reefiidiim kí jáǹ Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Joosuwa yii: «Lútí bininjab kansikin biba si nì bi ń cùú jáǹ Amaleeki yab. Foolee man làá fu jɔ̄m̀ kí nīn yú kigbantaŋ pu kí nīn ŋúb́ Unimbɔti kpandɔŋu m-ŋaan.»

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Niinee Joosuwa búntì kí cùú jáǹ Amaleeki yab kii Mooyiisi nín bí yii ú ŋá puee. Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì Uur jɔ́m̀ kigbantaŋ yilpu.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní Mooyiisi yaa yōoǹ u-ŋal yilpuee, Isirayeel yab pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní, ama u-ŋal yaa sīntèe ní Amaleeki yab ń pɔ̄ɔkì.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi ŋalii dāa gīīyee ní Aarɔn nì Uur nyàab̄ ditaŋkpal ki bíl̀ ní u kāl̀. Aarɔn nì Uur nìn ŋúb́ u-ŋalii yilpu, ubɔ nìn bí dijandi diba ní un kíǹee bí dijandi din kíǹee. Míǹ ní Mooyiisi ŋalii nìn bí yilpu áli ŋwìiń dāa dūu jéetì.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nìn dū ntàataajimu ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Amaleeki yab.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Ŋmà tibɔti nee kugbɔŋu poon án nīn bí bí nīn téetí. Tùkù Joosuwa yii m làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Amaleeki yab, án nín làá ŋá pu báà ubɔ ń taa ti téetí bi-puee.»

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi máń nsaraafan niin ki pú-ŋu diyindi yii: <Ti-Dindaan di sá man jajil daaŋku>.

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: Ní ki lī yii: «An nín ŋá pu Amaleeki yab yíkìi jáń nì ti-Dindaan beejalee, ti-Dindaan mun làá nīn pée jáà nì bi ní baabadal.»

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Ní u tú bí tùkù Mooyiisi yii: <Man di sá a-coo Jeetroo. M cáań a-nimpuu nì a-jipɔmbi liitil tí dāá màntì a-pu.>

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi túŋkì u-coo ki gbāaǹ u-nimbiin ki jáam̀-u, ní ki yíkìi kpàl̄-u. Bi bālifì tɔb laafiyau pu, ní ki nín kóò Mooyiisi tantiun.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi máafì u-coo min ní ti-Dindaan ŋá Faaroo nì Eejipiti yab Isirayeel yab puee. U nìn máafì-u agìń ŋin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab nìn ká nsannee, nì ti-Dindaan nín nyántì-bi agìń gbanti poon miŋyee.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: M béè kɔŋkɔnnee yii ti-Dindaan di sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ inimbɔti kɔkɔ, kun puee u nyántì u-nibul Eejipiti yab ŋaan ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bí ki ŋáań-bi ntoomee.»

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Mooyiisi coo Jeetroo ŋá saraawɔkaa nì mpèé saraabi ki tīī Unimbɔti. Ní Aarɔn nì Isirayeel yab kpilib kɔkɔ dɔ́miń, ní bi nì Mooyiisi coo kpáfì ki jíń tijin Unimbɔti nimbiin. Mooyiisi kāaǹ bibɔsoonliibi

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: A bíi tìì a-ba digìńdi ní ki bíi tìì dinibul din bí a-cee nee mun digìńdi. Ditundi nee nyìm̀ ki jítiǹ a-pɔŋŋu ní aa ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄-dì a-baba!

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe Mooyiisi kāl̀ kí sòoǹ binib bɔti, ní samaa dɔ́miń ki yúl̀ kutaafaau áli kujoou Mooyiisi ń ŋmā kí sòoǹ bi-bɔti.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: U-coo nín ká tin kɔkɔ án sá ú ŋá kí tīī samaayee ní u bí Mooyiisi yii: «Ba ní a bíi ŋáań dinibul nee ní? Ba pu ní a kā a-baba ní dinibul nee yú ki māntìi tú-si, kí yòon̄ kutaafaau kí cáá sāā kujoou míǹ?»

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kíí u-coo yii: «Binib nee dòoń m-cee ḿ bàlifì Unimbɔti ń sòoǹ nì bi tin bée ní.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Bi yaa tí cáá tɔb tibɔti tibee, ní bí dāan̄ m-cee ní ḿ sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì bi-kansikin, ní kí dàkà-bi Unimbɔti koobiliŋ nì u-marab nín sá puee.»

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi coo bí-u yii: «Min a ŋáań nee kaa kítì.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee á pīlifì-mi, m làá tīī-si isaŋki ní Unimbɔti ń nīn bí a-cee. An sá yii sii ń fōō samaa yil kí yūĺ Unimbɔti nimbiin ní ki nīn cáǹ tibɔti ki nàatī Unimbɔti a-ba.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Á dàkà-bi akoobil nì marab, ní kí yàntī bí béé nsan ŋun bi máaǹ kí dēe nì tin bi máaǹ kí ŋée.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: Bíǹ di làá nīn sòoǹ dinibul bɔti ŋyunti kamaa. Tibɔti tin yaa jítiǹ-bee, bí cáań-tì a-cee, ní bíǹ ń nīn sòoǹ tibɔti tin kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Ŋá míǹ kí bàtī a-gìńdi pu ŋwaam bí tūtuǹ-si á túń.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: A yaa ŋá míǹ ní Unimbɔti yaa tīī-si marabee, a làá ŋmā kí ká mpɔn kí yūĺ ní samaa ń fàtīí kpì nì dipɔɔsɔŋkil.»

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Bikpilibee nìn kíǹ ki bí kutaa sá kamaa ki sòoǹ samaa bɔti. Tin yaa nìn jítiǹ-bee, ní bí cáań Mooyiisi cee, ama ní ki nìn sòoǹ bi-ba tibɔti tin kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄yee.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Mooyiisi kāaǹ u-coo Jeetroo, ní u fātìi nín gítí u-tiŋkin.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi dàb̄ dijool ki nín cá Unimbɔti cee. Ti-Dindaan nìn bíń dijoolee yilpu ki yíiń-u ní ki bí-u yii: «Á tùkù Jaakɔb naantiibi Isirayeel yab yii:

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: <Ni ká tin m ŋá Eejipiti tiŋkee, nì m nín yōoǹ-ni m-feeŋyi pu kii ukaalunee ki cáań-ni m-ceeyee.

english_verse: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee ni yaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ, ki ŋúb́ m-pooŋyee, inifunaan kɔkɔ kansikinee, nimbi di làá nīn sá man m-ba bindi pu nibul. Di sá yii man di yì kitiŋ kɔkɔ.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ama nimbee, ni làá nīn sá man beelin saraaŋaliibi, ní kí nīn sá ditimbundi din sá man yal ki tūǹ m-tundee.> Tibɔti tin a làá cáá nàatī Isirayeel yabee dee.»

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Mooyiisi bāańee ní ki yíiń Isirayeel yab kpilib ní ki dū tibɔti tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan tùkūń-uee ki bíl̀ bi-nimbiin.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Ní dinibul kɔkɔ kíí yii: «Tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan lēe, ti làá ŋá míǹ.» Ní Mooyiisi gíiǹ bi nín kíí puee ki tùkū ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kpèè, m làá dāan̄ a-cee kí nīn kāń ditagbancancaal din gbìfèe poon kí sòoǹ nì si ní dinibul ń nīn gbìl̀ m nín bíi sòoǹ nì see, án nín làá ŋá pu bí nīn cáá a-pu dimákal baabadalee.» Ní Mooyiisi cáá Isirayeel yab nín kíí puee ki tùkū ti-Dindaan. Unimbɔti nì Mooyiisi kpáfì Siinaayi jool pu

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Cù samaa cee kí tùkù-bi yii bí nīn bí circir díǹ nì fool, kí fíntí bi-wampeeŋkaati.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ naau di yaa gūū ki kūū u-juti yɔuee, bí dū unaa un gūū u-jutee kí nyāfì, ní bin yì inaayee liitil ń yàkatī animbil nì unaa un kpíìyee nanti.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Ama unaayee dindaan yaa nyí yii u-naau pée gùutī míǹ ní kaa kpēē-u tiŋanee, ú nyàab̀ unaa kí téeǹ unaa un kpíìyee yil pu kí yòon̄ dinakpil.» Tiwaŋkuti naayubu

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: «Unaayuu yaa bíi wìil̄ digundi kunyeeu kí kɔ́ kudiin kí yɔ̀ tiwan ní bi yaa fáá ki kūū-uee, un kūū-uee kaa ŋá nnikpaakoon.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa sēē u-kpaabun ŋŋmi ní an fōō ikuŋkum ki tin kɔ́ ubɔ saakun, ki wùn̄ bilee un bi cáńee, àá un baa láá cáńee àá un kaa láá lòon̄ee, un sēē ŋŋmee ń pà tin ŋŋmi wùn̄ee pu.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa tīī u-juti animbil àá tiwan tin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee yii ú dūú yóoń-u, ní unaayuu kɔ́ un fōō tiwanee dumpu ki yùn̄ tiwan gbantee, bi yaa cúú unaayuuyee, ú pà tiwan tin u yùn̄ee mili pu.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: Bi yaa kaa ká unaayuuyee, un fōō u-juti wanti ki yóoǹ u-ceeyee ń sútí kí pìl̄ Unimbɔti, kí pùtī yii waa gbēē u-juti wanti.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa dū u-maŋki àá u-naau àá u-piiiu àá u-ŋoobuu àá kuwaŋkuluu kubɔ ki kpāaǹ u-juti, ní kuwaŋkuluuee kpíì àá ku fōō tiweendi àá bi yùn̄-ku, ní báà ubɔ kaa ká kí lēē mmɔ́ɔnee,

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: u-juti ń pùtī Unimbɔti yii waa gbēē u-bɔɔ wanti ní u-bɔɔ ń gbìl̄ kí tīiǹ-u. Mimmee waa ti pà kuwaŋkuluu gbanti pu.

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: Ama u-cee ní bi yaa yùn̄ kuwaŋkuluu gbantee, ú nyàab̀ kuwaŋkuluu kí téeǹ uwandaan.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Upeecuncuti di yaa cúú kuwaŋkuluu gbantee, ú cáań ku-laakin kíǹee kí dàkà án nīn sá seera. Niinee waa ti pà kuwaŋkuluu kun an cúúyee pu.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa cūtìi pīnnì u-juti waŋkuluku ní ku ká tiweendi àá ku kpíì kuwaŋkuluu daan boonee, un pīnnì-kuee máaǹ kí pà uwandaan.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: An yaa sá uwandaan nimbiin ní míǹ jítèe, an kaa cáá ú pà tiba. Ama u yaa nìn fōō-ku ki ŋá gbaaree, ú pà gbaara nimbiliŋ.» Akoobil nì dinimbɔtinool marab biba mun

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: U-baa yaa yíì kpataaa yii waa làá dū u-bisal kí tīī-uee, ú pà kii bi nín pée pà bisapɔmbi bin kaa nyí bininjabee cootiiku puee.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa dōoǹ nì kuwaŋkuluuee, bí kpɔ̀ udaan.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
translation_verse: Un di yaa ŋá saraabi ki tīī awaa ní an kaa sá ti-Dindaanee, bí kpɔ̀ udaan.

english_verse: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
translation_verse: kí fōō diŋuul ni-pu, ní kí yàntī bí kpɔ̀-ni kujaaun. Niinee ni-nimpoobi làá kpántí bikpiipoobi ní ni-biyaamu ń kpántí ataŋkpiibil.

english_verse: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
translation_verse: «Man nibul kansikin ubɔ àá usoodaan ubɔ yaa dɔ́miń ni-cee ki pīnnì animbilee, ní taa páań-u animbipaaŋkaa.

english_verse: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
translation_verse: «A yaa fōō a-juti bɔkutikpaandi ki yóoǹ a-cee toolimee, á gíiǹ kí tīī-u kí wàatī ŋwìiń ń nín jēetí.

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: «Ni máaǹ kí cáań ni-kpaajinti ticɔfikaal nì ni-dapeepeekaam min ni ŋmáaḿee kí ŋá-mi saraa. «Ní dū ni-biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kí sú-mi.

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: «Míǹ mbaantiim ní ní tí dū ni-naai nì ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui biseemaliŋ kí sú-mi. Tiwaŋkuti gbanti yaa màl̄ee, ti-biyaamuee ń nīn bí mu-na cee kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli. Winnii dalee ní cáań-mu kí dūú ŋá saraa kí tīī-mi.

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: «Ni làá nīn sá binib bin bí circiree ní m-cee. An puee ní taa ŋmɔ́ upeel un upeecuncuti cúú ki tɔ̄ntèe nanti. Ní dū-tì kí tīī iboo.

english_verse: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
translation_verse: Ní taa fàŋkì kunipaau wíiŋŋu pu kí nóó ku-boon kí ŋá ikpiti. Ibɔsoon laŋki bi yaa yíiń-ni ní lēē seeree, ní taa kpèè kunipaau nín pá un boonee wíiŋŋu pu kí tɔ́kɔtí ibaamɔn saŋŋu pu.

english_verse: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
translation_verse: Ní taa pɔ̀ usoodaan digàndi yii u nín sá usoodaanee pu.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: «A-nannanliu naau àá u-maŋki yaa wáŋkì ní a kée, á péetiń kuwaŋkuluuee kí cáań kí tīī-u.

english_verse: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
translation_verse: A yaa ká a-nannanliu maŋki lítì ní diwaŋgul nyīkiǹ ki-puee, taa jītí. Tūtuǹ-u ú yòon̄-kì kí síiń ki-taaŋi pu.

english_verse: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
translation_verse: «Ní taa kpɔ̀ uwɔfi bɔti ibɔsoon poon.

english_verse: Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
translation_verse: Ní taa cèeǹ tinyimɔmbɔti poon. Ní taa kpɔ̀ maanyiiba nì deedeedaan, di sá yii maa càntī dibɔkpil daan kii waa ŋá tibee.

english_verse: Don't accept bribes. Judges are blinded and justice is twisted by bribes.
translation_verse: Ní taa yàntī ubɔ ń pɔ̄-ni tiba kí ŋéeb́ ni-nyɔkɔ, di sá yii tiwampɔkaal gbanti jɔ̀b̀ bin wāĺee nimbiliŋ ní ki kù deedeedambi bɔti.

english_verse: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
translation_verse: «Ní taa sàaǹ binicambi bin kɔ́-ni ki kóò ni-tiŋki puee. Nimbi ni-ba nyí unicaan gìńdi, di sá ni kāl̀ kunicaŋu Eejipiti tiŋkin ki ká.» Dibiŋŋuŋfikaal nì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa bɔti

english_verse: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
translation_verse: «Ní kpɔ̀ ni-kpaajinti ni-kpaatanti pu, kí bɔ̄l̀ kí cā áli abin aluu.

english_verse: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
translation_verse: Ama dibinluluútiilee, ní yàntī tikpaatan ń dòon̄ kí ŋùŋfì. Ni-yab bin sá biwɔfibee ń dāá ká tijin poon kí jī, ipeel ń dāá jī tin yaa kíǹee. Míǹ mbaantiim ní ní dāá ŋá ni-fiinyib nì ni-ɔliifi sufii.

english_verse: Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
translation_verse: «Ní dū iwiin iluu kí tɔ̄ ni-tuuŋŋi, ama ŋwinluluúti dalee, ní taa tɔ̄ báà ditundi diba. Niinee ni-naai nì ni-mammu ń ŋùŋfì, ní ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-tɔntɔnliibi mun ń ŋùŋfì bi-fam ń nàb̄.

english_verse: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: «Ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ m bí yii ní ŋée. Ní taa pée tòotī awaa aba. Diwaal diba yindi ń taa pée nyā ni-nyɔkɔn gba.» Jiŋaalib bin sá mara bí nīn jīǹee (Dūú ŋmàntī nì

english_verse: Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
translation_verse: «Ní taa dū kpɔnɔ un poon ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kēe kí kūtì kuwaŋkuluu kun ni kūū ki ŋá-mi saraayee fatikuu pu. Ní taa dū kuwaŋkuluu kun ni dūu ŋá-mi saraayee kpam kí yóoń áli kutaa ń wúntí.

english_verse: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
translation_verse: Ni-tiŋki poonee, naa làá dāá ká unimpu cáá dipool an nyáń àá unimpuŋmaŋŋmanti. M làá dāá tīī-ni mmaŋfafɔkɔn.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa bíi cēē ni-kpaajinti tin ni kùn̄ tipeepeekaalee, ní dāá jī kuceeu jiŋaaliu. Míǹ boon dibindi yaa láa kúntì ní ni yaa láa kóoǹ ni-kpaajinti kusaaun ki dóòyee, ní dāá jī tantib jiŋaaliu.

english_verse: Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
translation_verse: Dibindi kamaa poonee, ni-ninjab kɔkɔ ń dāá dāan̄ ŋfunyɔm mita man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
translation_verse: «Dibindi poonee ní jī jiŋaalib bita kí tīī-mi tinyool.

english_verse: Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
translation_verse: Ní dāá jī jiŋaal un bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin poon baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. Iwiin in m yóoǹ-ni Abiibi ŋmaliu poonee, ní dāá dū iwiin iluli kí ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee, kii m nín tīī-ni mara puee. Di sá yii uŋmal gbanti poon ní ni nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin. Ní taa dāan̄ m-nimbiin iŋaŋkulim.

english_verse: Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. A Promise and a Warning The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ní cáań ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu diikun ni-kpaatanti nín lòon̄ tiŋyee jincɔ̀fikaati. Ní taa dū uŋoobu biim kí ŋàan̄ u-biki nanti.» Ipoon nì tibɔkpaafikaal

english_verse: I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you.
translation_verse: «Kpèè, m làá tɔ̄ń m-tuuŋŋu ŋú lìntī ni-nyɔkɔpu kí nīn cí-ni kí cáá-ni kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin m bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ-nee.

english_verse: Carefully obey everything the angel says, because I am giving him complete authority, and he won't tolerate rebellion.
translation_verse: Ní kpèè tiŋan kí pīlifiǹ-ŋu, kí taa yìntīǹ-ŋu. Waa làá tàan̄-ni ni-pɔɔgbifiŋŋu pu. Di sá yii man yindi ní ŋu ŋúb́ ki tūǹ atuun.

english_verse: If you faithfully obey him, I will be a fierce enemy of your enemies.
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa tɔ́-ŋu mmɔntiimin, ki ŋáań tin kɔkɔ m bí yii ní ŋée, m làá nīn sá ni-nannanliibi nannanliu, ní kí nīn sá ni-pulincɔntiibi pulincɔnti.

english_verse: My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
translation_verse: «M-tuuŋŋu yaa láa līntì ni-nyɔkɔpu ki cáá-ni ki kɔ́ǹ Amɔɔr yab nì Eeti yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Kanaan yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab timmunee, m làá dāá kúntí-bi.

english_verse: Don't worship their gods or follow their customs. Instead, destroy their idols and shatter their stone images.
translation_verse: Ní taa láa pée gbàan̄ bi-waaŋi nimbiin kí jāam̀-ŋi. Ní taa láa fōō bi-bimbim, ama ní dāá gbá kí wīī bi-waaŋi nì bi-taŋkpeeŋi ŋin bi cóoǹ ki jáaḿee.

english_verse: Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu baba ní ní dāá nīn jáaḿ. Niinee ní ḿ dāá bìin̄ ni-boon kí tīī-ni tijin nì tinyɔkaal, ní kí wúń ni-pu iween ń taa cúú-ni.

english_verse: I will terrify those nations and make your enemies so confused that they will run from you.
translation_verse: «M làá dāá dū dinyoondi kí lìntī ni-nyɔkɔpu, ntimu mun poon ni làá dāá kɔ́ee nib kɔkɔ ń fàŋkì, ní ni-nannanliibi bin dòoń kí jáǹ-nee ń dāá lábití kí sāǹ-ni.

english_verse: I will make the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites panic as you approach.
translation_verse: M làá dāá dū abaakati kí tɔ̄ Eefi yab nì Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab pu.

english_verse: But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, maa làá dāá jà bi-kɔkɔ dibimbaantiil poon. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, kitiŋ làá dāá kpántí kupɔɔu ní kumooun peelii ń dāá bùtī kí jà-ni.

english_verse: Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
translation_verse: M làá nīn pée jì-bi fiii fiii ní kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ni làá dāá bùtī tikpil kí fōō kitiŋee.

english_verse: I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land.
translation_verse: M làá yóoń ni-tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ Tikati mɔɔl kí cáá sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu, kí fàtīí yòon̄ Siinaayi teeku kí cáá sāā Eefiraata. M làá dū ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ nib kí ŋá ni-ŋaan ní ní jà-bi ni-nimbiin.

english_verse: But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods.
translation_verse: Ni nì bi nì bi-waaŋi ń taa pée ŋá mpèé ŋubɔ.

english_verse: Don't let them stay in your land. They will trap you into sinning against me and worshiping their gods.
translation_verse: Bí taa nín̄ kóò ni-tiŋkin, án nín làá ŋá pu bí taa yàntī ní yìntīǹ-mi kí jāam̀ bi-waaŋee. Di sá yii ni yaa jáam̀-ŋee, án làá kpántí kutaliŋŋu kí sàl̄-ni.»

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bí Mooyiisi yii: «Jɔ̄mìń m-cee, sii nì Aarɔn nì Nadaab nì Abiyuu nì Isirayeel yab kpilib imuŋku ita nì saalaayee. Ni yaa dòoń ki dáá bíń ndanee, ní gbàan̄.

english_verse: but you are to come near. Don't let anyone else come up.”
translation_verse: Ama sii Mooyiisi baba ń sútiń kí pìl̄-mi. Bin kíǹee ń taa sútiń, ní samaa mun ń taa nóó-si kí jɔ̄mìń.»

english_verse: Moses gave the Lord's instructions to the people, and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded!”
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn cáá tibɔti nì marab bin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan dàkā-uee ki máafì samaa. Ní samaa kíí nì kinyɔɔbaantii yii: «Tibɔti tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan sòon̄ee, ti làá ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said. The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan tùkū-uee. Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, ní Mooyiisi máń nsaraafan dijoolee taapu. U nìn dū ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali, Isirayeel naakɔti nín sá puee, ní ki máń.

english_verse: He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord.
translation_verse: U nìn dū Isirayeel naacimpɔmbi biba ki tú bi cūtìi ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi. Bi nìn kūū inajaa mun ki ŋá mpèé saraabi.

english_verse: Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn dū tiwaŋkutee fatikuu dijandi ki ŋá disambilin, ní ki dū dijandi din kíǹee ki kpáatìi pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan pu.

english_verse: Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
translation_verse: Boonee ní u yōoǹ dipoondi taŋkpapilinti ki kàan̄ mpɔn ki tīī samaa. Ní samaa kɔkɔ bí yii: «Tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan lēe, ti làá gbìl̄ kí tīiǹ-u kí ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi dū fatiku ki yāaǹ samaa pu ki bí yii: «Kpèèmaan, fatiku nee di sá dipoondi din ti-Dindaan pūtì ki pōoǹ-ni ki tīī-ni marabee daaŋku.»

english_verse: and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
translation_verse: Bi nìn ká Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu. U-taaŋi taapuee, an nìn bí kii dikɔl din bi dū ataŋkpamɔnti ŋin bi yíì safiir ŋi wāĺ kílkil ki bɔ̀ǹ kii kutagbɔŋuee ki nákáǹee ní.

english_verse: Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank. Moses on Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan kaa nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab kpilibee kpíì. U nìn yāntì bi kpēē úǹ Unimbɔti, boonee ní bi jíń ki nyùn̄. Mooyiisi bí ti-Dindaan cee dijool pu

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Jɔ̄mìń m-cee dijool pu kí dāá yūĺ niin. M làá dū marab bin m ŋmàn̄ ataŋkpee pilinti puee kí tīī-si, á cáá dàkà Isirayeel yab.»

english_verse: Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi yíkì kutaafaau u nì Joosuwa un u dūu ŋàl̄ u-bee, ní bi nín jɔ́ḿ Unimbɔti jool pu.

english_verse: Moses had told the leaders, “Wait here until we come back. Aaron and Hur will be with you, and they can settle any arguments while we are away.”
translation_verse: U tùkū Isirayeel kpilib yii: «Ní cīití-ti doo, timbi ń cù kí gítiń. Aarɔn nì Uur làá nīn bí ni-cee. Ubɔ yaa cáá tibee, udaan ń ká-bi.»

english_verse: When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nín jɔ́ḿ, ní ditagbandi dɔ́miń ki bīiǹ dijool pu.

english_verse: and the bright glory of the Lord came down and stayed there. The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and on the seventh day the Lord told Moses to come into the cloud.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn bí Siinaayi jool pu ní ditagbandi nìn bīī di-pu míǹ ki tin cáa sāā iwiin iluu. Ŋwinluluúti dalee ní ti-Dindaan yíiń Mooyiisi ditagbandee poon.

english_verse: blue, purple, and red wool; fine linen; goat hair;
translation_verse: nì bigulifamambi nì gulfab bin bí gùŋgumee nì bigulifamambi cínciŋ nì iŋaapiin in bí fálfalee nì tiŋɔkuti,

english_verse: Tell everyone in Israel who wants to give gifts that they must bring them to you.
translation_verse: «Tùkù Isirayeel yab yii bí lēē bi-gaajati tin bi cááyee poon kí ŋá-mi saraa. Bin kɔkɔ làá tīī nì dipɔbil dibee cee ní ní fōō.

english_verse: Here is a list of what you are to collect: Gold, silver, and bronze;
translation_verse: Tin m là bí cáań kí ŋá saraayee di sá sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti,

english_verse: tanned ram skins; fine leather; acacia wood;
translation_verse: nì ipigban in bi mántèe, nì igban in dàfì tikpilee, nì akasiya dɔi,

english_verse: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices to mix with the incense and with the oil for dedicating the tent and ordaining the priests;
translation_verse: nì ŋkpam min bi làá nīn cáa ŋáań fitilabinee, nì talaalu kpam min bi làá nīn cáa sìtī binib pu kí dū-bi kí sú man ni-Dindaanee, nì talaalub bin bi làá nīn tùutēe,

english_verse: and onyx stones and other gems for the sacred vest and the breastpiece.
translation_verse: nì ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì ooniikisee nì ataŋkpanyaan aba mun bí dūú nákań eefoodi nì kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee.

english_verse: I also want them to build a special place where I can live among my people.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab ń gāā-mi circir kɔŋkooŋŋu, ní ḿ nīn kóò bi-kansikin.

english_verse: The lamp on the top and those at the end of each of its six branches must be made so as to shine toward the front of the lampstand.
translation_verse: Ní mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab biluli kí dūu tɔ́kɔń fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati pu, án nīn wāĺ nnimbiin pú.

english_verse: Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid.
translation_verse: Ní dū sindaariyamɔnti kí nyùntī poon nì boon, ní kí dū sindaariya kí kpākam̀ anyɔɔgbán.

english_verse: Make four gold rings and attach one of them to each of the four legs of the chest.
translation_verse: Ní dū sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ abɔmbil anaa kí báań dakaayee kpiŋŋi naatil dijandi diba abɔmbil ali, diba mun abɔmbil ali.

english_verse: Make two poles of acacia wood. Cover them with gold
translation_verse: Ní kpítí akasiya kpandɔi kí dū sindaariya kí nyùntī-i.

english_verse: and put them through the rings, so the chest can be carried by the poles.
translation_verse: Ní dū ikpandɔee kí bɔ̄ abɔmbil ŋin bá dakaayee kpiŋŋi an càatī bí ŋmā kí nīn yòontí ki bùkuntí.

english_verse: Don't ever remove the poles from the rings.
translation_verse: Ikpandɔee ń nīn pée fúuń abɔmbilee poon bí taa fúutí.

english_verse: Then hammer out two winged creatures of pure gold and fasten them to the lid at the ends of the chest.
translation_verse: Ní mɔ́ɔ́ Keerubim ubɔ kí tɔ́kɔń didakaabiil nyɔɔgbandi diba nín kúntí puee, ní kí mɔ́ɔ́ Keerubim ubɔ mun kí tɔ́kɔń didakaabiil nyɔɔgbandi din kíǹee nín kúntí puee. Keerubimbi bin tɔ́kɔ́ anyɔɔgbán kúntilaŋki puee nì dakaayee bìil ń kpāfì kí nīn sá tiwambaantiil.

english_verse: The creatures must face each other with their wings spread over the chest.
translation_verse: Bí kpátí bi-feeŋyi yilpu kí bìin̄ didakaabiil pu. Bí nīn tɔ́kɔ́ ki túĺ tɔb bi-nimbiiŋyi tīī didakaabiil pu.

english_verse: Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest.
translation_verse: Ni yaa dū dipoondi taŋkpapilinti tin pu m ŋmàn̄ dipoondi marab bin m làá tīī-see ki ŋá dakaayee poonee, ní dū dibìil kí púkuń.

english_verse: I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do. The Table for the Sacred Bread (Exodus
translation_verse: Keerubimbi bili bin tɔ́kɔ́ didakaabiil puee kansikin ní m làá lēē m-ba kí dàkà-si, ní kí tīī-si marab á dūú nàatī Isirayeel yab.» Kpɔnɔb bin bi ŋáań ti-Dindaan saraayee teebiliu

english_verse: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border
translation_verse: Ní kí kpítí kidɔpampaŋ, kí nīn wāā kii santimeetab binii kí kpākam̀ anyɔɔgbán, kí dū sindaariya kí nyùntīí tū.

english_verse: Make four gold rings and attach one to each of the legs
translation_verse: Ní mɔ́ɔ́ sindaariya bɔmbiliŋ anaa kí dūú bā kí nákáǹ teebilee kpiŋŋi naatil pu, ataa cee.

english_verse: near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Ní dū akasiya dɔŋu kí kpítí ikpandɔ, kí dū sindaariya kí nyùntī-i. Íǹ ní ni làá nīn cáa yòontí teebilee.

english_verse: The table is to be kept in the holy place, and the sacred loaves of bread must always be on it. All bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings are to be made of pure gold and set on this table. The Lampstand (Exodus
translation_verse: Teebil gbanti pu ní ni làá nīn cáá kpɔnɔb bin ni cáa ŋáań saraayee ki pāantí m-nimbiin baabadal. Fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati tin cáá ikpiin ilulee

english_verse: Make a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold
translation_verse: «Ní gbá sindaariyamɔnti kí dūú mɔ́ɔ́ fitila tɔ́kɔŋkaati. U-taapu nì u-kpinjaatiŋu nì u-kpiiŋyi nì u-gbiŋŋi nì u-pumpukum kɔkɔ ń nīn sá mmɔm.

english_verse: with three branches on each of its two sides.
translation_verse: Ikpiin iluu ń nyānní ŋkpinjaatee pu, dijandi kamaa ń nīn cáá ikpiin ita ita.

english_verse: The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold.
translation_verse: Agbin nì ikpiinee nì fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati jaŋŋi ŋin kíǹee ń nīn sá mmɔm. Bí gbá sindaariyamɔnti kí dūú mɔ́ɔ́ tikɔkɔ.

english_verse: The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold.
translation_verse: Ní dū sindaariyamɔnti kí mɔ́ɔ́ tibabiti nì nsambiyaamu mun poon bi ŋáań ŋfantamee.

english_verse: The lampstand and its equipment will require
translation_verse: Ní dū sindaariyamɔnti kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa kí mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_verse: Á kpèè tiŋan kí ŋá tin bí nee kɔkɔ tí nīn bí kii min m dàkā-si dijool nee puee.»

english_verse: For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
translation_verse: «Á dū gulfa un bí fálfal ki dàfèe, nì un máǹ gùŋgumee nì un máǹ cínciŋee nì un máǹ wèeeeyee kí lù ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋubɔ mun, usatalul ń nyāantì-ŋu bí dūú sàkan̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki pu.

english_verse: As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth
translation_verse: Diŋaajandi kamaa fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab saalku, ŋwaan ń nīn sá meetab bili. Ŋi-kɔkɔ fɔkɔŋŋu nì ŋi-waaŋŋu ń nīn ŋmà.

english_verse: The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
translation_verse: «Á dū gulfab bin dàfì ki máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee kí lù aŋaajan saalaa, kí lù keerubimbi kí nákań ŋi-pu.

english_verse: and sew them together into two panels with five sections each.
translation_verse: Á dá láá dū aŋaajan aŋmoo kí ŋáĺ kí kpāfì, ní boonee kí dū aŋmoo ŋin kíǹee mun kí ŋáĺ kí kpāfì.

english_verse: The panel of goat hair will be a meter longer than the tent itself, so fold
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ŋŋaabu meeta dijandi làá kíń ŋfɔkɔn pu kí nīn jòon̄ ajanliitil pu kí bìin̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent.
translation_verse: Á dū ajan aŋmoo kí ŋáĺ kí kpāfì ubaanti, ní kí dū aluu mun kí ŋáĺ kí kpāfì ubaanti. Á dū diŋaajandi diluluutiilee kí kpáb́ nnimbiin pú.

english_verse: Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Á dāá mántí tipigban kí dūú bìin̄ tanti un bīī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu puee, ní kí dū ŋgban ŋun dàfèe kí páań.

english_verse: Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid.
translation_verse: Á dū dibìil kí púkuń dipoondi dakaau pu <circir páaa laŋki>.

english_verse: Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: «Á dū akasiya dɔŋu kí kpáá idɔjaati kí cóoń án nīn ŋúb́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu.

english_verse: Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put
translation_verse: Á dū animbil kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ titílkaal imuŋku ili, ndɔjaati kamaa titílkaal tili.

english_verse: For the back wall along the west side use six frames
translation_verse: Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu boon pú jandi din bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, á dāá kpáá idɔjaati iluu kí cóoń.

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: Idɔjaati gbanti taapui làá nīn dátiǹ tɔb, ama ní kí tin dūú kpāfì yilpu dibɔmbibaantiilin. Míǹ ní idɔjaati liitilee làá nīn sá tiwambaantiil ní kí nīn sá titíkiŋkaal.

english_verse: Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
translation_verse: Mimmee idɔjaatee làá nīn sá inii dee, ní i-taapu tílkaati ń nīn sá saalku nì ubɔ, an dàkà yii ndɔjaati ŋubɔ titílkaal tili.

english_verse: Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold and attach gold rings to the frames to run the crossbars through.
translation_verse: Á dū sindaariya kí nyùntī idɔjaati in bi kpááyee nì ikalimee pu, ní kí dū sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu mun poon ní bi làá dū ikalimee kí bɔ̄ee.

english_verse: Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain. The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Á gāā circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kii m nín dàkā-si min dijool pu nee deedee.

english_verse: Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
translation_verse: Á kɔ́ǹ teebil kí yóoń poon ŋŋaasakaŋkaa nimbiin circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋgan pú, ní ŋgiil púee, fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati ń nīn yú ki túĺ teebil.

english_verse: Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_verse: Á kpítí akasiya dɔjaai iŋmoo, kí dū sindaariya kí nyùntī-i kí dūú cóoń, ní kí dū titábikaal tin bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́yee kí bā, ní kí dū tasa kúti kí nyùntī titílkaal tiŋmoo kí tíĺ idɔjaatee taapu.»

english_verse: Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Á dū ikpandɔee kí bɔ̄ abɔmbil ŋin bí nsaraafan jaŋŋi puee poon bí ŋmā kí nīn yòontí-ŋu.

english_verse: Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain. The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Á dū ndɔ kí kpáá nsaraafan gbanti, ŋu-poon ń nīn dɔ̄ fám tiba ń taa nín kā. Á kpáá-ŋu kii m nín dàkā-si dijool nee pu á kpáá puee. Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi ŋaabui

english_verse: Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning
translation_verse: «Á tùkù Isirayeel yab yii bí cáań-si ɔliifi kpam min ŋān̄ ki wāĺ kílkilee á nīn cáa sìtī fitilab poon, án nín làá ŋá pu fitilab ń nīn pée fòol̄ ŋyunti kamaayee.

english_verse: for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain
translation_verse: Á dū mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamu nì tibakaal tin bi dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee kí cúú satabee kí dūú sàkan̄ idɔjaa mmuŋku in bi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee pu. Idɔjaayee làá nīn cáá titílkaal mmuŋku tin bi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee.

english_verse: Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
translation_verse: Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu mɔŋkiŋu punyɔkɔ ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab saalaa. Á dū gulfa un dàfì kí máǹ gùŋgumee, nì un máǹ cínciŋee, nì un máǹ wèeeeyee kí nyāantì-i. Í nīn sàkā idɔjaa inaa in tɔ́kɔ́ titílkaal tinaa mun puee.

english_verse: Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard. The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place (Leviticus
translation_verse: Á dū tasa kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ tin kɔkɔ bi làá nīn cáa tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon tundee ki kpáaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kpakpaaŋi nì ŋu-cindi yaŋ.» Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu fitilab kpam

english_verse: in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_verse: Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń dāá dū fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati kí yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon ŋŋaapìtikaa ŋun lìkī baa wāĺ Dipoondi dakaauee nimbiin. Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń bɔ́ntí fitilab gbanti tiŋan án nín làá ŋá pu bí nīn pée fòol̄ ŋyunti kamaa m-nimbiin kí yòon̄ kujoou kí cáá sāā kutaafaauee. An sá mara ní m yóoǹ Isirayeel yab bí nīn ŋáań míǹ kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: Send for your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They are the ones I have chosen from Israel to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: «Á yàntī a-nabiki Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi, Nadaab nì Abiyuu nì Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar ń dāan̄ a-cee. Á gàntī-bi Isirayeel yab kansikin bí nīn tūǹ man saraaŋatundi.

english_verse: Aaron is to be dedicated as my high priest, and his clothes must be made only by persons who possess skills that I have given them.
translation_verse: Á sòoǹ nì bitɔntɔnliibi bin kɔkɔ m gbéeǹ iciin famee, kí yàntī bí ŋáĺ Aarɔn tiwampeeŋkaal. Ú dāá nīn pēē-tì ní á dū-u kí sú-mi ú nīn bí man saraaŋatundin.

english_verse: Here are the items that need to be made: a breastpiece, a priestly vest, a robe, an embroidered shirt, a turban, and a sash. These sacred clothes are to be made for your brother Aaron and his sons who will be my priests.
translation_verse: Tiwampeeŋkaal tin a làá yàntī bí ŋáĺ-uee di sá kilɔbiki kin làá nīn pá u-bindi puee nì eefoodi nì dibɔkutifɔkɔl nì poon bɔkutil nì ŋŋaabu ŋun u làá nīn cáa fìǹ u-yilee nì ŋŋaabu dambalau. Á yàntī bí ŋáĺ tiwan gbanti kí tīī Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi bí nīn tūǹ man saraaŋatundi.

english_verse: Use only gold and fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool, for making these clothes. The Vest for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: Bí dū gulfab bin cáá sindaariya nyimee nì bin máǹ gùŋgumee, nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe, kí lù tiwampeeŋkaal gbanti.» Eefoodi

english_verse: Put two onyx stones in gold settings, then attach one to each of the shoulder straps. On one of these stones engrave the names of Israel's first six sons in the order of their birth. And do the same with his remaining six sons on the other stone. In this way Aaron will always carry the names of the tribes of Israel when he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people.
translation_verse: Á dūú bā ŋŋaacalimu mun bi ŋáĺ ki tábíǹ eefoodee. Ataŋkpeeyee di làá nīn sá kii kudaaŋŋu ki téetí Jaakɔb jipɔmbi pu. Mimmee bi-yiŋŋi làá nīn náká Aarɔn gbigbipati liitil pu man ni-Dindaan nimbiin, ní ḿ nīn pée téetí bi-pu.

english_verse: Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold. The Breastpiece for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: ní kí dū sindaariyamɔnti kí mɔ́ɔ́ ikusaka ili mpalimu yam kí dūú cúú tisɔn tin poon ataŋkpeeyee fúuńee.» Kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee

english_verse: From the same costly material make a breastpiece for the high priest to use in finding out what I want my people to do.
translation_verse: «Á yàntī bitɔntɔnliibi ń dū gulfab bin cáá sindaariya nyimee, nì bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe kí lù kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee kí nákań eefoodi pu.

english_verse: with four rows of three precious stones: In the first row put a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald;
translation_verse: Á dū ataŋkpanyaan kí nákań ikuul inaa ki-pu kí nyāantì-kì. Ŋkuupeepeekaa ń nīn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì oodeemee, nì ŋin bi yíì piitidaayee nì ŋin bi yíì bareekeetee.

english_verse: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
translation_verse: Ŋkuuliliiti ń nīn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì noofeekee, nì ŋin bi yíì safiiree nì ŋin bi yíì yaaliimee.

english_verse: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
translation_verse: Ŋkuutataatee ń nīn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì leeseemee nì ŋin bi yíì seebooyee nì ŋin bi yíì alamaayee.

english_verse: and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount the stones in delicate gold settings
translation_verse: Á dū ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì taarsiisee nì ŋin bi yíì soowamee, nì ŋin bi yíì yaasipee kí nákań ŋkuunanaati pu. Á dū sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ tisɔn tin poon a làá dū ataŋkpanyaanee kí fúuńee.
