english_verse: Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps.
translation_verse: ní kí dū anyɔɔgbán ali ŋin kíǹee kí bā sindaariya sɔnti tili tin poon ní ataŋkpanyaan fúuń eefoodi ŋaacalimmu puee, ní an nīn bí kilɔbikee nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Then take a blue cord and tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. This will keep the breastpiece in place.
translation_verse: Á dū gulfaman gùŋgum ŋmiiŋu kí bɔ̄ kilɔbiki bɔmbiliŋ nì eefoodi bɔmbiliŋin kí kúĺ, ní kilɔbikee ń nīn pá eefoodi dambalau pu ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kaa cìŋkī.

english_verse: Under his vest Aaron must wear a robe of blue wool
translation_verse: «Boonee á dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee kí lù dibɔkutifɔkɔl din pu eefoodi làá nīn pée.

english_verse: with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out.
translation_verse: Á lēē di-kansikin kinyɔkɔ, u yaa làá pèen̄ee ú dū u-yil kí bɔ̄ niin. Á lù kinyɔkɔee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi ń nīn gbìfì ki dàfì kí taa ŋmā kí cátí.

english_verse: Along the hem of the robe weave pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a gold bell between each of them.
translation_verse: Á dū sindaariya waŋkilimmu nì greenaadi subiliŋ ŋin ni lùn̄ee kí lúntí dibɔkutil júti taapu kí nīn sākantí kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
translation_verse: Aarɔn yaa làá kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī-mee, ú nīn pēē dibɔkutil gbanti ní bí nīn gbìl̀ ŋwaŋkilimu siim pu, ní u yaa làá tí nyēē bí nīn gbìl̀ mu-pu. Mimmee waa làá kpú.

english_verse: On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.”
translation_verse: «Á dū sindaariyamɔnti kí nyùntī kí nántiǹ mpumpukum, ní kí ŋmà an pu kii bi nín ŋmà kijalii pu puee yii: <Bi dū-u ki sú ti-Dindaan>.

english_verse: Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord,
translation_verse: Á dū gulfa un máǹ gùŋgumee kí lù kiŋaacaliŋ kí dūú cúú kí nákań ŋŋaabu ŋun u cáa fìǹ u-yilee nyɔkɔpu pú.

english_verse: so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
translation_verse: Sindaariya pumpukumee làá nīn pée bí Aarɔn yigbeel pu, án nín làá ŋá pu ú fōō Isirayeel yab nín yīntiǹ circir wanti tin kɔkɔ bi cáań ki ŋá saraayee kpitii kí túńee. Sindaariya pumpukumee làá nīn pée bí u-yigbeel pu ní man ni-Dindaan ń nín fōō saraabi gbanti.

english_verse: Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them.
translation_verse: «Ní ŋáĺ tiwan gbanti tibaantiil, an dàkà yii dibɔkutifɔkɔl poon yal nì dambala nì ŋŋaabu ŋun bi cáa fìǹ diyilee kí tīī Aarɔn jipɔmbi, án nīn cáá kunyaaŋŋu kí dàkà usaraaŋal nyooti.

english_verse: Then dress Aaron and his sons in these clothes, pour olive oil on their heads, and ordain them as my priests.
translation_verse: «Á dū asaraaŋabɔkuti gbanti kí pèen̄ a-maan Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi. Á sìtī bi-yiliŋ ŋkpam kí dū-bi kí sú-mi bí nīn bí m-tundin. Mimmee a dū-bi ki sú-mi bi kpántì m-saraaŋaliibi dee.

english_verse: Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves.
translation_verse: Á dū ŋŋaapiin ŋun bí fálfalee kí ŋáĺ-bi ncukutigimu kí bìin̄ bi-cancaŋgbeel pu, kí yòon̄ bi-caŋ kí cáá sāā bi-tapaŋŋi.

english_verse: Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
translation_verse: Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi yaa làá kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun àá bi yaa làá sútí kí pìl̄ nsaraafan kí tɔ̄ circir laŋki ditundee, bí dū ncukutigimuee kí lòon̄. Mimmee baa làá ŋá ikpiti in làá cáań-bi ŋkúmee. Án nīn sá mara un kaa kpántée ki tīī Aarɔn nì u-naantiibi bin làá dāá páań u-boonee.»

english_verse: Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin kamaayee, á dū unaja kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau, ní kí ŋá saraa nsaraafan pu kí ŋá-ŋu circir. Boonee á dū ŋkpam kí sìtī ŋu-pu kí dū-ŋu kí sú-mi.

english_verse: Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: nì kpɔnɔ un kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee, nì kalaabi bin bi dū ŋkpam ki ŋmālim̀ ki búuń ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee, nì ŋkpɔnɔwaamu mun pu bi yɔ́kɔfì ŋkpam ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee. Bilee yim ní bí dūú ŋá an kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
translation_verse: Á dū kɔkɔ kí ŋá kukabiku kubɔn kí cáań circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, kí kpáaǹ dinajapɔmbil nì ipijaa ilee.

english_verse: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: «Á cáań Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu kí fàl̀-bi nnyim bí nyā kí nīn bí circir.

english_verse: Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash.
translation_verse: Á dū abɔkuti ŋin bi ŋáĺ ki dūu sú-mee kí pèen̄ Aarɔn, an dàkà yii poon bɔkutil nì dibɔkutifɔkɔl nì eefoodi nì kilɔbiki, ní kí dū eefoodi dambalau kí cúú.

english_verse: and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní á yòon̄ ŋkpam min bi cáa sìtī unil yilpu kí dū-u kí sú-mee kí sìtī u-yil pu.

english_verse: Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: «Á cáań dinajapɔmbilee dikpafindi tantiu nyɔkɔpu, ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań di-yil pu.

english_verse: Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent.
translation_verse: Á làntì dinajapɔmbilee man nimbiin niin circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar.
translation_verse: Á lēē fatiku kí dū a-ŋambiki kí sēē kí jòotì nsaraafan yiŋyi naatil pu. Boonee ní á kpáatí fatiku un kíǹee kí pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan taapu.

english_verse: But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
translation_verse: An di làá nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibi kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau. Ama á yòon̄ dinajapɔmbilee nanti nì di-gbaŋŋu nì di-binti kɔkɔ kí cáá wà ŋŋmi dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu.

english_verse: Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: «Boonee ní á cáań upijapeekaa ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań di-yil pu.

english_verse: Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Á làntì-dì, ní kí dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head.
translation_verse: Á càkà di-nanti anaŋkún anaŋkún, kí fíntí di-nai nì di-yakaŋ kí dūú páań anaŋkúnee nì diyil pu.

english_verse: Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Á dū upijamɔnee kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraawɔkaa un ni ŋá ki tīī-mee, saraa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī man ni-Dindaan pɔbilee.

english_verse: Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: «Boonee ní á cáań upìjaliliiti, ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań upìjee yil pu.

english_verse: Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Á làntì-u kí lēē fatiku kí jōō Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi tafalam ŋŋaŋgiil yaŋ pu, nì bi-ŋambijaliŋ ŋŋaŋgiil yaŋ pu nì bi-taŋambijaliŋ ŋŋaŋgiil yaŋ pu, ní kí dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Á dāá lēē fatiku un bí nsaraafan puee nì ŋkpam min bi cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú-mee, kí yàaǹ Aarɔn nì u-bɔkutiŋ pu, ní kí yàaǹ u-jipɔmbi nì bi-bɔkutiŋ pu. Mimmee a dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nì bi-wampeeŋkaati ki sú-mi dee.

english_verse: This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: Á dāá lēē upìjee kpam nì dijugbindi nì ŋkpam min bīī ina puee, nì mpɔɔlam nì aceebil nì ŋkpam min bīī ŋi-puee, nì diŋaŋgiitaal, kun puee an sá upìja un bi dūu ŋá saraa kí kàan̄ bisaraaŋaliibi bí nīn bí m-tundinee ní.

english_verse: and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Á dū tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ kí ŋúbiǹ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ní kí yàntī bí dúkutí yilpu kí fíiǹ fíiǹ man ni-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Boonee, á fàtīí fōō bi-ŋaan kí dūú kūtì saraawɔkaa un pá nsaraafan puee kí wà ŋŋmi. An saraau sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī man ni-Dindaan pɔbil ní.

english_verse: You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Á yòon̄ upìjaliliiti un a dūu ŋá Aarɔn yil pu saraa ki dū-u ki sú-mee bindi kí dúkutí kí fíiǹ fíiǹ man ni-Dindaan nimbiin. Dijandi gbantee, á yòon̄, a-yati dee.

english_verse: After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
translation_verse: U-jipɔmbi kansikin un làá fōō u-yil kí kpántí usaraaŋakpil kí kɔ́ dikpafindi tantiun kí lēē saraa <circir laŋkee> ń dāá pèen̄ asaraaŋabɔkuti gbanti iwiin iluli.

english_verse: then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń ŋmɔ́ tinan gbanti nì kpɔnɔb bin kā kukabikunee dikpafindi tantiu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it.
translation_verse: Bí ŋmɔ́ tin ní bi dūu ŋá saraa bí ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam kí dū-bi kí sú-mi bí kíĺ disaraaŋal tundee. Unifantanti ń taa jī saraabi jinti gbanti, di sá yii tì sá circir ní.

english_verse: Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you.
translation_verse: «Á ŋá Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi kí nóó nì m nín tīī-si mara puee deedee. Á dū iwiin iluli kí ŋá akoobil ŋin sá á ŋá-bi ní bí nín kpántí bisaraaŋakpilibee.

english_verse: Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy. Daily Sacrifices (Leviticus
translation_verse: Á dū iwiin iluli ní kí ŋá akoobil gbanti mun. Míǹ boonee nsaraafan kpántì circir páaa dee ní tin kamaa yaa pée gbēē-ŋuee kpántì circir wanti.» Ŋwiin kamaa saraawɔkaabi

english_verse: one in the morning and one in the evening.
translation_verse: Á dū diba kí ŋá saraa kutaafaau, ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá saraa kujoou.

english_verse: With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me.
translation_verse: Saraaliliitee, kujoou ní a làá ŋá úǹ kí tīī-mi. Tiwan tin kɔkɔ a kútì ki ŋá saraapeepeekaayee, tíǹ tibaantiil ní a làá tí dūú kūtì kí ŋá saraaliliiti mun. An di sá saraawɔkaa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī m-pɔbilee.

english_verse: Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: M làá dāá ŋá dikpafindi tantiu nì nsaraafan circir, ní kí ŋá Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi circir bí nīn bí m-saraaŋatundin.

english_verse: I will live among you as your God,
translation_verse: M làá dāá nīn kóò Isirayeel yab kansikin, ní kí nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá béé yii man bi-Dindaan di sá bi-Nimbɔtiu un di nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin kí nīn kóò bi-kansikinee. «Man di sá bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu.»

english_verse: Mix four liters of olive oil with the following costly spices: six kilograms of myrrh, three kilograms of cinnamon, three kilograms of cane, and six kilograms of cassia. Measure these according to the official standards. Then use this sacred mixture
translation_verse: Á dūú ŋmàlim̀ kí ŋá ŋkpam min sɔ́fèe kii utalaaluŋal nín ŋáań puee ní bí nīn cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú man Unimbɔti.

english_verse: Build an altar of acacia wood where you can burn incense.
translation_verse: «Boonee á dū akasiya dɔŋu kí kpáá nsaraafan ŋun pu bi làá nīn tùutī talaalubee.

english_verse: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it.
translation_verse: Á dāá dū sindaariyamɔnti kí nyùntī ŋu-yilpu nì ŋu-boon kí màntīí tū nì ŋu-yiŋyi, ní kí dū sindaariya kí kpākam̀-ŋu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Á mɔ́ɔ́ sindaariya bɔmbiliŋ ali kí bā bi nín kpákám̀ nsaraafan taapu puee ajan liitil pu, bí nīn cáá ikpandɔ ki bōotí ki yòontí-ŋu.

english_verse: These poles are also to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Á dū akasiya dɔŋu kí kpítí ikpandɔee ní kí dū sindaariya kí nyùntī-i.

english_verse: Put the altar in front of the inside curtain of the sacred tent. The chest with the place of mercy is kept behind that curtain, and I will talk with you there.
translation_verse: Á dū nsaraafan gbanti kí yóoń ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋun lìkī Dipoondi dakaau nì u-bìilee nimbiin, laakin man nì si làá nīn kpáfée.

english_verse: Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings.
translation_verse: Ní taa tūū talaalu ubɔ fám nsaraafan gbanti pu. Ní taa ŋá saraawɔkaa ŋu-puɔɔɔ, kí taa ŋá tijimpin saraau ŋu-puɔɔɔ, kí taa fá ndamam ŋu-pu.

english_verse: Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by smearing on its four corners the blood of an animal sacrificed for sin, and this practice must always be followed. The altar is sacred because it is dedicated to me. The Money for the Sacred Tent
translation_verse: Dibindi kamaayee, Aarɔn ń dū kuwaŋkuluu kun u dūu ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam wiŋkpaaŋŋu saraauee fatikuu kí fá nsaraafan yiŋyi pu kí ŋá-i circir. Kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaanee, ní nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ki ŋáań nsaraafan circir diba dibindi kamaa poon. Nsaraafan gbanti máaǹ kí nīn sá circir páaa wanti tin ni dūu sú man ni-Dindaanee ní.» Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu lampoou

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: Find out how many grown men there are in Israel and require each of them to pay me to keep him safe from danger while you are counting them.
translation_verse: «A yaa làá dāá kàaǹ Isirayeel yabee, báà ŋma ń dāá pà kunimbiŋmiiu kubɔ kí dā u-maŋfal, mimmee dikàandi kaa làá dāá cáań-ni mbusu ubɔ.

english_verse: , whether rich or poor, must pay me the same amount of money, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Nnyim gbanti ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi làá dāá nīn jòotī ki fíntí bi-ŋalii nì bi-taaŋi.

english_verse: This money is to be used for the upkeep of the sacred tent, and because of it, I will never forget my people. The Large Bronze Bowl (Exodus
translation_verse: A yaa láa fōō Isirayeel yab ŋaan animbil gbantee, á nīn cáa kpèé circir kɔŋkooŋŋu. Án di làá yàntī ḿ nīn téetí Isirayeel yab pu ki bìintí bi-pu.» Kusampeeu kun poon bi ŋáań nnyim ki fíntée

english_verse: If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_verse: Un di yaa ŋá talaalu gbanti kí nīn tíkì u-sɔnsɔfiŋuee, bí nyāntí udaan m-nibul kansikin.»

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Boonee ní ti-Dindaan gíti tí bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: By dedicating them in this way, you will make them so holy that anyone who even touches them will become holy.
translation_verse: Á dū tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ kí sú-mi ní tí kpántí circir páaa wanti, ní tin kamaa yaa pée gbēē-tèe ń kpántí circir wanti.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tí bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: for dedicating the tent and chest,
translation_verse: Á bàtī ŋkpam gbanti kí sìtī dikpafindi tantiu nì dipoondi dakaau pu.

english_verse: the table with its equipment, the lampstand with its equipment, the incense altar with all its utensils,
translation_verse: Á bàtī kí sìtī teebil nì u-wanti kɔkɔ, nì fitila tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ, nì nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalubee pu.

english_verse: When you ordain Aaron and his sons as my priests, sprinkle them with some of this oil,
translation_verse: Á dāá bàtī ŋkpam gbanti kí sìtī Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi yil pu kí dū-bi kí sú-mi bí nīn bí m-tundin.

english_verse: and say to the people of Israel: “This oil must always be used in the ordination service of a priest. It is holy because it is dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: «Á dāá tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: <Ŋkpam nee di sá min bi làá nīn cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú-mee. Man baba tundi ní ni làá nīn cáá-mì ki ŋáań kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: If you do, you will no longer belong to the Lord's people.” The Sweet-Smelling Incense
translation_verse: Un kamaa di yaa ŋá ŋkpam gbanti juti, ní ki dū-mì ki sītì unifantanti ubɔ puee, bí nyāntí-u m-nibul kansikin.>» Bi nín máaǹ kí bɔ́ntí talaalutuukaa puee

english_verse: Mix equal amounts of the costly spices stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, then add salt to make the mixture pure and holy.
translation_verse: Á dū ŋyaam kí ŋmàlim̀ kí ŋá talaalumɔnti kii utalaaluŋal nín ŋáań puee, án nīn bí circir.

english_verse: Pound some of it into powder and sprinkle it in front of the sacred chest, where I meet with you. Be sure to treat this incense as something very holy.
translation_verse: Á lēē dijandi diba kí ŋá talaalu un sá ŋyimee kí dūú yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, dipoondi dakaau nimbiin, laakin man nì si làá nīn kpáfée. Talaalu gbanti ń nīn sá ni-cee circir wanti.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: I have chosen Bezalel from the Judah tribe to make the sacred tent and its furnishings.
translation_verse: «Kpèè, m lēē Uurii jipɔɔn Beesaleel, Uur un sá Juuda naakookunee naantiiu.

english_verse: Not only have I filled him with my Spirit, but I have given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood.
translation_verse: Ú ŋmā kí kpítí ataŋkpanyaan bí nīn cáa nākantí tiwan pu, ní kí kpítí idɔ. U làá nīn sá unil un ŋūǹ ki ŋáań tikɔkɔ mmɔntiiminee ní.

english_verse: I have appointed Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to work with him, and I have also given skills to those who will help them make everything exactly as I have commanded you:
translation_verse: M dū Ayiisamaaki un sá Daani naakookunee jipɔɔn Ooliyaab ki ŋàl̄-u ú nīn tútúǹ-u. Míǹ mbaantiim ní m tīī bitɔntɔnliibi biba mun ŋŋmam bí ŋmā kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ m làá tùkù-ni ní ŋée, an dàkà yii:

english_verse: the sacred tent with its furnishings, the sacred chest with its place of mercy, the table with all that is on it, the lamp with its equipment, the incense altar, the altar for sacrifices with its equipment, the bronze bowl with its stand, the beautiful priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons, the oil for dedication and ordination services, and the sweet-smelling incense for the holy place. Laws for the Sabbath
translation_verse: nì ŋkpam min bi cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú Unimbɔtee, nì talaalutuukaa un bi tùutī circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee. Bitɔntɔnliibi ń ŋá kii m nín tīī-si mara yii bí ŋá puee ní deedee.» Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa bɔti

english_verse: Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had said: The Sabbath belongs to me. Now I command you and your descendants to always obey the laws of the Sabbath. By doing this, you will know that I have chosen you as my own.
translation_verse: ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Ní nīn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa tiŋan. Di sá yii ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa sá kudaaŋŋu kubɔ ní man nì ni kansikin kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Ŋu dàkà yii man ni-Dindaan di yāntì ni bí circir.

english_verse: Keep the Sabbath holy. You have six days to do your work, but the Sabbath is mine, and it must remain a day of rest. If you work on the Sabbath, you will no longer be part of my people, and you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ní dū iwiin iluu kí tɔ̄ atuun, winluli dalee, ní dūú ŋùŋfì. Ŋúǹ sá ŋwiin ŋun ni dūu sú man ni-Dindaanee ní. Un kamaa di yaa túń ditundi ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee, bí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
translation_verse: Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu ní man nì Isirayeel yab kansikin kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Di sá yii m dū iwiin iluu ní ki náań yilpu nì taapu, ní ŋwinluluútee, m kāl̀ ki ŋūŋfì.»

english_verse: When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi míǹ Siinaayi jool pu ki dóòyee, ní ki dū titaŋkpapilindi tili tin pu u dū u-ŋambiki ki ŋmàn̄ dipoondi marab ki nákáǹee ki tīī-u.

english_verse: Moses, I have seen how stubborn these people are,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti tùkū Mooyiisi yii: «M ká yii dinibul nee sá din gáatèe ní.

english_verse: The people got up early the next morning and killed some animals to be used for sacrifices and others to be eaten. Then everyone ate and drank so much that they began to carry on like wild people.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní samaa ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi. Boonee ní bi kāl̀ ki jíń ki nyùn̄. Bi dóòyee ní ki dūu gùl̄ agbiil pu.

english_verse: Moses said to them, “You obeyed the Lord and did what was right, and so you will serve as his priests for the people of Israel. It was hard for you to kill your own sons and brothers, but the Lord has blessed you and made you his priests today.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí Leefii yab yii: «Díǹ nee ni dū ni-ba ki sú ki túń ni-Dindaan tundi, kun puee naa yíì ki ŋúń ki kūū ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-nabiyaamu. An puee ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ ni-pu díǹ.» Mooyiisi gbāam̀ Unimbɔti Isirayeel yab pu

english_verse: After the people saw that Moses had been on the mountain for a long time, they went to Aaron and said, “Make us an image of a god who will lead and protect us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but nobody knows what has happened to him.”
translation_verse: Samaa nín ká yii Mooyiisi yúntìń dijool pu kaa bíi bàńee ní bi cūtìi kpáfì Aarɔn cee ní ki bí-u yii: «Kpèè doo, mɔ́ɔ́-ti unimbɔti ubɔ ú nīn līī ti-nyɔkɔpu, di sá taa nyí tin di yaa bāań Mooyiisi un di nyántìń-ti Eejipiti tiŋkinee.»

english_verse: Aaron told them, “Bring me the gold earrings that your wives and sons and daughters are wearing.”
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn bí-bi yii: «Lēēmaan ni-nimpoobi nì ni-bisalib nì ni-jipɔmbi sindaariyabɔmbiliŋ bi-tafaliŋ pu kí cáaḿmaan-mi.»

english_verse: then he melted them and made an idol in the shape of a young bull. All the people said to one another, “This is the god who brought us out of Egypt!”
translation_verse: Aarɔn fōō tiwan gbantee bi-ŋaanee ní ki dūntì ki dūu sītì tiwan tin bi ŋá ki nántiǹ dinabilee poon, ní an nyántì dinabil. Niinee ní samaa téeń yii: «Isirayeel yab, kpèèmaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee!»

english_verse: When Aaron saw what was happening, he built an altar in front of the idol and said, “Tomorrow we will celebrate in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Aarɔn ká mimmee ní ki máń nsaraafan dinabilee nimbiin ní ki bí yii: «Foolee ti làá fu jī ti-Dindaan jiŋaaliu.»

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Hurry back down! Those people you led out of Egypt are acting like fools.
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Sìntī malaa, di sá a-nibul din a nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee bíi ŋáań ikpitikpaan.

english_verse: They have already stopped obeying me and have made themselves an idol in the shape of a young bull. They have bowed down to it, offered sacrifices, and said that it is the god who brought them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Bi pūtì kpáàa dū nsan ŋun m dàkā-bee ki fá. Bi dūntì tikúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ dinabil, ki gbāaǹ di-nimbiin, ki ŋá-dì saraabi ki lī yii: <Isirayeel yab, kpèèmaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee!»

english_verse: and I'm angry enough to destroy them, so don't try to stop me. But I will make your descendants into a great nation.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, yàntī ḿ fōō bi-pu mbiim kí kúntí-bi. Boonee m làá dī sii pu kí náań ditimbuŋkpaandi.»

english_verse: Moses tried to get the Lord God to change his mind: Our Lord, you used your mighty power to bring these people out of Egypt. Now don't become angry and destroy them.
translation_verse: Ama ní Mooyiisi gbāam̀ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti ú jī kimɔtii ní ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ba pu ní a fōō dinibul din a nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkin nì a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì a-kpabilee pu mbiim míǹ?

english_verse: If you do, the Egyptians will say that you brought your people out here into the mountains just to get rid of them. Please don't be angry with your people. Don't destroy them!
translation_verse: A yaa ŋá mimmee Eejipiti yab làá lì yii: <Unimbɔti là kí cáá-bi kí tɔ̄ mbusu poonee pu ní u nyántì-bi ti-tiŋkin. U là kí cáá-bi kí cūnnì ntimu mun bí ajoon puee kí sàaǹ-bi kí kúntí-bi kitiŋ pu ní.> An puee m-Dindaan, sɔ̀ŋkì a-pɔbil, kí gíiǹ mbusu un a bàà làá dūú tɔ̄ a-nibul puee kí yà.

english_verse: Remember the solemn promise you made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You promised that someday they would have as many descendants as there are stars in the sky and that you would give them land.
translation_verse: Téetí Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb pu, a-tɔntɔnliibi bin a nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ-bi yii: <M làá bùtī ni-maaliŋun yab bí nīn wīikí kii iŋmalbijaa in bí kutagbɔŋu puee. M làá dū kitiŋ kin m pōoǹ-bee kí tīī-bi bí nīn kíǹ ki yì kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan.>»

english_verse: So even though the Lord had threatened to destroy the people, he changed his mind and let them live.
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan nín bàà bɔ́ntì kí dū mbusu un kí tɔ̄-bee ní u yāntì kaa ti ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: Moses went back down the mountain with the two flat stones on which God had written all of his laws with his own hand, using both sides of the stones.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti u-ba di nìn kpítì titaŋkpapilindi gbanti. Úǹ u-ba di nìn tí ŋmàn̄ ti-pu kii kigaai ní bi dūu cáká ki ŋmàn̄ee.

english_verse: When Joshua heard the noisy shouts of the people, he said to Moses, “A battle must be going on down in the camp.”
translation_verse: Joosuwa nín gbìl̄ samaa kuŋkuuntii puee ní u bí Mooyiisi yii: «Pīlifì, ijanjakuŋkuunti di tùm̀ ti-naapaal puee.»

english_verse: But Moses replied, “It doesn't sound like they are shouting because they have won or lost a battle. It sounds more like a wild party!”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-u yii: «Aayee, doo kaa sá dijajil kuŋkuuntii, kaa tí sá bin bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee yaliŋkii. Ilan pu ní man gbìl̀ nee.»

english_verse: As Moses got closer to the camp, he saw the idol, and he also saw the people dancing around. This made him so angry that he threw down the stones and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Bi tóob́ dinaapaalee ní Mooyiisi ká dinabil yú ní samaa bí ki ŋōō ní u fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. U nìn dū titaŋkpapilindi tin u ŋúb́ u-ŋaanee ki lúkú, ní ki gbáń ki wīī-tì dijool taapu niin.

english_verse: He melted the idol the people had made, and he ground it into powder. He scattered it in their water and made them drink it.
translation_verse: Ní u cūtìi yōoǹ dinabil din samaa mɔ́ɔ́yee ki tɔ́ ŋŋmin ní an wùn̄. U nìn nàn̄-dì dúsi dusi, ki dūu sītì nnyimin ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab nyùn̄.

english_verse: Moses asked Aaron, “What did these people do to harm you? Why did you make them sin in this terrible way?”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bālifì Aarɔn yii: «Ba ní dinibul nee ŋá-si ní a téé-dì ki tɔ́ ikpitikpaan in bí nee poon míǹ?»

english_verse: Aaron answered: Don't be angry with me. You know as well as I do that they are determined to do evil.
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn kíí Mooyiisi yii: «M-dindaan, taa fōō m-pu diŋuul. Sii a-ba nyí yii dinibul nee kaa pée pɔ̄ɔ̄ tin kaa ŋān̄ee diŋál.

english_verse: They even told me, “That man Moses led us out of Egypt, but now we don't know what has happened to him. Make us a god to lead us.”
translation_verse: Bi bí-mi yii: <Mɔ́ɔ́-ti unimbɔti ubɔ ú lìntī ti-nyɔkɔpu, di sá yii Mooyiisi uninja un di nyántìń-ti Eejipiti tiŋkinee, taa nyí tin di yaa bāań-uee.>

english_verse: Then I asked them to bring me their gold earrings. They took them off and gave them to me. I threw the gold into a fire, and out came this bull.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bālifì-bi yii: <Ŋma di cáá sindaariya?> Dicilpu niin ní bi túutì abɔmbil bi-tafaliŋ pu ki cáań ki tīī-mi, ní m dūu tɔ́ ŋŋmin ní dinabil nee nyánní.» Ditafadaaldi

english_verse: Moses knew that the people were out of control and that it was Aaron's fault. And now they had made fools of themselves in front of their enemies.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi ká yii fìkil fikil kɔ́ samaa ní Aarɔn yāntì bi ŋá bi nín là puee, ki dū bi-ba ki tīī binannanliibi ń bèel̀.

english_verse: So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and shouted, “Everyone who is on the Lord's side come over here!” Then the men of the Levi tribe gathered around Moses,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi cūtìi yúl̀ dinaapaal punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ní ki téeń yii: «Bin kɔkɔ bí ti-Dindaan jandee ń dāan̄ man cee!» Ní Leefii naakookun yab kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki yúl̀ u-cee ki māntìi tú-u.

english_verse: and he said to them, “The Lord God of Israel commands you to strap on your swords and go through the camp, killing your relatives, your friends, and your neighbors.”
translation_verse: Ní u bí-bi yii: «Kpèèmaan, ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé yii: <Báà ŋma ń dū u-tàataajiki kí gbìn̄, kí yìiǹ dinaapaal jaŋŋi kɔkɔ poon kí kpɔ̀ u-nabiki nì u-bɔɔ nì u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔ.>»

english_verse: The men of the Levi tribe followed his orders, and that day they killed about
translation_verse: Leefii yab nìn ŋá kii Mooyiisi nín nìn lī puee, di sá yaadal wiiŋŋuee, bi nìn kūū binib kutukub bita.

english_verse: The next day Moses told the people, “This is a terrible thing you have done. But I will go back to the Lord to see if I can do something to keep this sin from being held against you.”
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Mooyiisi bí samaa yii: «Ikpitikpaan ní ni baasii ŋá. Kɔŋkɔnnee m làá fàtīí jɔ̄m̀ dijool pu ti-Dindaan cee, an yaa yíì u làá fōō-mi kí dū ni-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ni.»

english_verse: Moses returned to the Lord and said, “The people have committed a terrible sin. They have made a gold idol to be their god.
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi fātìi nín gítí ti-Dindaan cee, ní ki bí-u yii: «Àaa ti-Dindaan, a-nibul ŋá ikpitikpaŋkpaan ní, bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ unimbɔti.

english_verse: But I beg you to forgive them. If you don't, please wipe my name out of your book.”
translation_verse: Ama m gbāam̀-si, dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi. An yaa kaa ŋá mimmee, á kpìtī man yindi dimaŋfal gbɔŋku kun a ŋmàn̄ee poon.»

english_verse: The Lord replied, “I will wipe out of my book the name of everyone who has sinned against me.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Un yīntiǹ-mee yindi ní m làá kpìtī m-gbɔŋku poon.

english_verse: Now take my people to the place I told you about, and my angel will lead you. But when the time comes, I will punish them for this sin.”
translation_verse: Too kɔŋkɔnnee, nín̄ cá kí yòon̄ dinibul kí cùnnì laakin m bí á cáá-bi kí cùnnèe. M làá yàntī m-tuuŋŋu ń nīn līī a-nyɔkɔpu. Ama dalba m làá dāá dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-kpitii gbanti pu.»

english_verse: So the Lord punished the people of Israel with a terrible disease for talking Aaron into making the gold idol.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan dáaĺ dinibul tafal Aarɔn nín nìn mɔ́ɔ́-bi dinabil diŋyee pu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: You led the people of Israel out of Egypt. Now get ready to lead them to the land I promised their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Yīkì doo, sii nì dinibul din a nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee, kí nīn cá kitiŋ kin m pūtì ki pōoǹ Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb yii m làá dūú tīī bi-maaliŋun yabee.

english_verse: It is a land rich with milk and honey, and I will send an angel to force out those people who live there—the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. But I will not go with my people. They are so rebellious that I would destroy them before they get there.
translation_verse: Ní cùú kɔ́ kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee. Ama man kaa làá nóó-ni kí cù, kun puee ni sá dinibul din pɔbil gbìfèe ní. Án làá yàntī ḿ kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni nsanni.»

english_verse: Even before the Lord said these harsh things, he had told Moses, “These people really are rebellious, and I would kill them at once, if I went with them. But tell them to take off their fancy jewelry, then I'll decide what to do with them.” So the people started mourning,
translation_verse: Di sá ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Ni sá dinibul din pɔbil gbìfèe ní. M yaa bí yii m làá nīn còom̄ ni-kansikin, án kaa làá gāā dikàakil ní ḿ kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni. Míǹ puee lēēmaan tiwannyaandi ni-wunti pu ḿ kpèè min ní m làá ŋá-nee.»

english_verse: and after leaving Mount Sinai, they stopped wearing fancy jewelry. The Lord Is with His People
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ Ooreeb jool caŋin niin ní Isirayeel yab kíĺ kaa ti dū tiwannyaandi ki ŋá bi-wunti pu. Dikpafindi tantiu

english_verse: Moses used to set up a tent far from camp. He called it the “meeting tent,” and whoever needed some message from the Lord would go there.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab yaa nìn bàn̄ laakin ki gāā dinaapaalee, Mooyiisi nìn yòontí tanti ní kí cùnnì kí cóoń dinaapaal boon ndandati. Bi nìn yíì-u yii <circir kɔŋkooŋŋu>. Un yaa nìn là kí bàlifì ti-Dindaan cee tibee nìn nyēē dinaapaalin ní kí cù circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.

english_verse: Each time Moses went out to this tent, everyone would stand at the entrance to their own tents and watch him enter.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti kamaa Mooyiisi yaa nìn yíkìi cá circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee, samaa nìn yíkí ní báà ŋma yú u-tantiu nyɔkɔpu, ní bi-nimbiliŋ cɔ́ u-pu áli ú tin kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.

english_verse: Then they would bow down because a thick cloud would come down in front of the tent, and the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, just like a friend. Afterwards, Moses would return to camp, but his young assistant Joshua would stay at the tent. The Lord Promises To Be with His People
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòoǹ nì Mooyiisi bi-nimbiiŋyi túĺ tɔb kii unil nì u-juti nín sòoǹ nì tɔb puee ní. Boonee ní Mooyiisi ń fàtīí nīn gítí dinaapaal pu, ní Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa un nìn bí ki tútúǹ-uee ń gbíntí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun. Ti-Dindaan nì Mooyiisi bíi sòoǹ

english_verse: Moses said to the Lord, “I know that you have told me to lead these people to the land you promised them. But you have not said who will go along to help me. You have said that you are my friend and that you are pleased with me.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi bí ti-Dindaan yii: «Kpèè, sii di bí-mi yii ḿ kpòotī dinibul nee, ama ní kaa yāntì m béè un ní a làá tɔ̄ń ú céeǹ-mee. Ama si mun di bí-mi yii: <M nyí-si tiŋan>, ní ki gíti lī yii: <A ká diyimɔɔl m-cee.>

english_verse: If this is true, let me know what your plans are, then I can obey and continue to please you. And don't forget that you have chosen this nation to be your own.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee m yaa lafun ká diyimɔɔl a-cee, á yàntī ḿ béé a-landɔkɔi nín sá puee. Mimmee m làá béé-si tiŋan ní kí páatí diyimɔɔl gbanti pu. Á nīn nyí yii ditimbundi nee sá a-nibul ní.»

english_verse: The Lord said, “I will go with you and give you peace.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti kíí Mooyiisi yii: «Mama m-ba di làá céeǹ-ni ní kí tīī-si diŋuŋfil.»

english_verse: Then Moses replied, “If you aren't going with us, please don't make us leave this place.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-u yii: «Sii a-ba yaa kaa bí ti-cee kí céeǹ-ti, á taa lì yii tí yīkì doo kí nīn cá.

english_verse: But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
translation_verse: Ba di làá dàkà yii man nì a-nibul ká diyimɔɔl a-cee? See a yaa céeǹ-ti baba di làá gàntì man nì a-nibul nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee nib kansikin.»

english_verse: So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kíí Mooyiisi yii: «M làá ŋá min a dáá bālifì-mi nee kí tīī-si, di sá a ká m-cee diyimɔɔl, ní man di baasii lēē-si.»

english_verse: Then Moses said, “I pray that you will let me see you in all of your glory.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí yii: «M gbàam̄-si, yàntī ḿ ká a-nyooti.»

english_verse: The Lord answered: All right. I am the Lord, and I show mercy and kindness to anyone I choose. I will let you see my glory and hear my holy name,
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti bí-u yii: «M làá yàntī m-ŋanti nín sá puee kɔkɔ ń jītí a-nimbiin á ká, ní kí yíiń man ni-Dindaan yindi a-nimbiin. M sūǹ un saai m là kí sɔ̄ee saai, ní ki ŋáań tiŋan un m là kí ŋá tiŋanee.

english_verse: but I won't let you see my face, because anyone who sees my face will die.
translation_verse: Ama aa ŋūǹ kí wāl̀-mi nì a-nimbiliŋ yéè kpìrrr, di sá unil kaa ŋūǹ kí wāl̀-mi ki gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin.»

english_verse: There is a rock not far from me. Stand beside it,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti bí yii: «Kpèè mpaan ŋubɔ bí doo ki pìl̄-mi. Tɔ́kɔń ditaŋkpakpaandi nee pu kí nīn yú.

english_verse: and before I pass by in all of my shining glory, I will put you in a large crack in the rock. I will cover your eyes with my hand until I have passed by.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun m-nyooti yaa láa bíi jītée, ḿ dāá dū-si kí báĺ ntaŋkpalɔkɔn ní kí dū m-ŋal kí bìin̄ a-nimbiin ní kí jītí.

english_verse: Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. You will not see my face.
translation_verse: Boonee ní ḿ dāá cúú m-ŋal kí bìitī ní á wāl̀ m-boon, an yaa kíǹ m-nimbiinee, ubɔ kpá kí ká-ŋu.»

english_verse: The Lord said: I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «M làá pùtī kí pòon̄ Isirayeel yab dipoondi. A-nibul kɔkɔ nimbiinee, m làá ŋá maamaacib bin juti kaa láá pée jítì kitiŋ pu laaba nì ditimbundi diba poonee. Dinibul din māntìi tú-si nee làá ká maamaacib bin man ni-Dindaan làá dī a-pu ki ŋée nín kaa cáá juti puee.

english_verse: Be ready tomorrow morning to come up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top.
translation_verse: Á bɔ́ntí kí cīití fool ntaafaabɔmbɔmee. Á fu jɔ̄m̀ Siinaayi jool yilpu kúnti kunti kí yūĺ niin kí cīití-mi.

english_verse: No one is to come with you or to be on the mountain at all. Don't even let the sheep and cattle graze at the foot of the mountain.”
translation_verse: Báà ubɔ ń taa fu nóó-si kí jɔ̄m̀. Bí taa ká uniseen dijool gbanti pu laaba. Báà uŋoobu àá upii àá unaa ń taa fu ŋmɔ́ timool di-caŋin!»

english_verse: So Moses cut two flat stones like the first ones, and early the next morning he carried them to the top of Mount Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kpítì titaŋkpapilindi tili kii tipeepeekaalee. Kutaa wúntì ntaafaabɔmbɔmee ní u nín jɔ́ḿ Siinaayi jool pu, ki ŋúb́ titaŋkpapilindi tilee kii ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: Then he passed in front of Moses and called out, “I am the Lord God. I am merciful and very patient with my people. I show great love, and I can be trusted.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan dɔ́miń ki jítì Mooyiisi nimbiin ki yíiń úǹ u-ba yindi yii: «Man di sá ni-Dindaan, Unimbɔti un sá ulaŋŋaŋfiti nì tiŋandaan kaa gífí diŋuul malaa, ki cáá dineendi tikpil tikpil ki bí deedeeyee.

english_verse: Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Dicilpu niin ní Mooyiisi gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaan,

english_verse: He prayed, “Lord, if you really are pleased with me, I pray that you will go with us. It is true that these people are sinful and rebellious, but forgive our sin and let us be your people.” A Promise and Its Demands (Exodus
translation_verse: ní ki bí yii: «M yaa lafun ká diyimɔɔl a-cee, ti-Dindaan, m gbāam̀-si, á nīn bí ti-kansikin ti-saŋkindi poon. Dinibul nee sá din gáatèe ní, ama á dū ti-yìntitam nì ti-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ti, ní kí fōō-ti kí ŋá a-nibul.» Unimbɔti fātìi pōoǹ Isirayeel yab dipoondi

english_verse: Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: «A-ninjab kɔkɔ ń dāá dāan̄ man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nimbiin dibindi kamaa poon mita.

english_verse: The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
translation_verse: «Kibiseebiki kininjabiki kamaayee, man di yì. Míǹ ní unaa àá upii àá uŋoobu yaa péé péé ki màl̄ kijakee, bí dū-kì kí ŋá-mi saraa.

english_verse: Your men will even marry their women and be influenced to worship their gods.
translation_verse: A yaa láa cáá bi-bisalib ki tīī a-jipɔmbee, bi-bisalib gbanti làá dāá nīn tòotī bi-waaŋi ní kí yàntī a-jipɔmbi mun ń nīn tòotī bi-waaŋi.

english_verse: Don't make metal images of gods.
translation_verse: «Á taa dū tikúti kí dùntī kí mɔ́ɔ́ diwaal.

english_verse: I will force out the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, but you must do what I command you today.
translation_verse: «Á ŋúb́ mara un m làá yóoń-si díǹ nee tiŋan. M làá jà Amɔɔr yab nì Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab a-nimbiin.

english_verse: Don't make treaties with any of those people. If you do, it will be like falling into a trap.
translation_verse: Á nīn nyíǹ a-ba kí taa ŋá mpèé nì kitiŋ kin poon a cá kí kɔ́ nee yab. A yaa ŋá míǹ, án làá nīn sá kutaliŋŋu ní ki tīī-si.

english_verse: Instead, you must destroy their altars and tear down the sacred poles they use in the worship of the goddess Asherah.
translation_verse: Ama ní gbá kí wīī bi-saraafaŋyi, kí kpìtī bi-kumpooŋi kí gàatì bi-windɔi kí lúkú.

english_verse: Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals.
translation_verse: Si nì kitiŋ kin a làá kɔ́ee yab ń taa pòon̄ tɔb kí ŋá mpèé. Bi yaa láa bíi tòotī bi-waaŋi ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì-ŋee, bi làá dāá yíiń-ni ní ní jī bi-saraabi jinti.

english_verse: Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.
translation_verse: «Á dāá jī jiŋaal un bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. Á ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee iwiin iluli kii m nín yóoǹ-ni mara puee, Abiibi ŋmaliu un poon bi yóoǹ kí nīn jīǹ-uee. Di sá uŋmal gbanti poon ní bi nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son. Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
translation_verse: Á dū kimaŋ biseemal kijaka kí kpántí dipibil àá diŋɔbil. A yaa kaa làá dūú kpántée, á nyīī kí gíí ki-sil. Ama a-jipɔmbi kansikin un sá kibiseebikee, á pà ki-pu. «Á taa dāan̄ m-nimbiin nì iŋaŋkulim.

english_verse: Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting.
translation_verse: «Á dū iwiin iluu kí tɔ̄ a-tuuŋŋi, ŋwinluluúti dalee, á kàl̄ kí ŋùŋfì. Báà an yaa sá tikpaal yuntiŋu àá tijin dical yuntiŋu, á kàl̄ ŋwiin gbanti kí ŋùŋfì.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: «Á dū bileepeepeekaa un a cáńee kí jī nnyɔmu jiŋaaliu, ní dibindi yaa bíi kúntée, á jī tantib jiŋaaliu.

english_verse: As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
translation_verse: Di sá m làá dāá jà atimbun kí pɔ̄-si mpaan ní kí wàan̄ a-tiŋki, ní ŋyunti ŋun a làá dāá dāan̄ man ni-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin dibindi kamaa poon mitee, ubɔ dāa kpá kí màkan̄ yii u làá jáǹ-si kí fōō a-tiŋki.

english_verse: When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
translation_verse: «A yaa làá dāá làntì kuwaŋkuluu kí ŋá-mi saraayee, á taa láa dū kpɔnɔb bin poon bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee kí kūtì saraayee pu. Á taa láa dū saraabi bin a ŋá Dilákatil jiŋaaliuee nanti kí yóoń kutaa ń wúntí.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
translation_verse: Á dāá cáań tijimpeekaal tin a-sati lòon̄ee circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin. Á taa dū uŋoobu biim kí ŋàan̄ u-biki nanti.»

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Á ŋmà tibɔti nee, kun puee tíǹ pu ní m tɔ́kɔǹ ki pūtì ki pōoǹ si nì Isirayeel yab dipoondi.»

english_verse: Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi kpákatìń Siinaayi jool pu, ki ŋúbiń titaŋkpapilindi tili tin pu bi ŋmàn̄ dipoondi marabee. Waa nìn nyí yii ŋyunti ŋun u bí ti-Dindaan ceeyee, u-nimbiin cúu kpántì ki kíǹ ki jìliŋkī.

english_verse: When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him.
translation_verse: Aarɔn nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kpēē Mooyiisee ki ká yii u-nimbiin cúu kpántì ki kíǹ ki jìliŋkī. Ní bi fāŋkì kí sútí kí pìl̄-u.

english_verse: Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi yíiń-bi. Niinee Aarɔn nì samaa kpilib dɔ́miń u-cee ní u bíi sòoǹ nì bi.

english_verse: Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ sútìń ki pìl̄-u ní u dū marab bin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan tīī-u Siinaayi jool puee ki tùkū-bi.

english_verse: The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi sòon̄ nì bi míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki dū ŋŋaabu ki bīiǹ u-nimbiin.

english_verse: Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Mooyiisi yaa nìn là kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan cee kí sòoǹ nì uee, ní ú cúú ŋŋaabu kí bìitī u-nimbiin kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun u yaa dóò ki làá nyānnée. U yaa nìn nyánnée ní ú dū marab bin u fōońee kí tùkù Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn kāntí yii Mooyiisi nimbiin nìn kíǹ ki jìliŋkī. Niinee ní ú gíiǹ ŋŋaabu kí bìin̄ ŋu-pu kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun u làá fàtīí kɔ́ kí sòoǹ nì ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death.
translation_verse: <A cáá iwiin iluu kí tɔ̄ ditundi, ama ŋwinluluúti dal sá ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ní, ŋwiin ŋun a dūu sú man ni-Dindaanee. Un kamaa yaa túń ditundi ŋwiin gbantee, bí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath. Offerings for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Laakin kamaa ni yaa kóòyee, ubɔ ń taa kpāā ŋŋmi ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal.>» Isirayeel yab cáań bi-saraabi

english_verse: The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made.
translation_verse: Binimpoobi bin nìn nyí diwanlulee nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin pīiǹee ki lùn̄ ki cáań.

english_verse: onyx stones or other gems for the sacred vest and breastpiece.
translation_verse: nì ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì soowamee nì ataŋkpanyaan aba mun bí dūú nákań eefoodi nì kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee.

english_verse: If you have any skills, you should use them to help make what I have commanded:
translation_verse: Bitɔntɔnliibi bin yáb̀ee kɔkɔ ń kpāfì kí tɔ̄ ditundi din ti-Dindaan bālifì yii ní tɔ̄ee.

english_verse: and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons. Gifts for the Lord
translation_verse: nì tiwampeeŋkaal tin bi làá nīn pèentí ki tūǹ atuun circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee nì usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn wampeeŋkaati nì u-jipɔmbi yati tin bi làá nīn pèentí ki tūǹ disaraatundee.>»

english_verse: Moses told the people of Israel that the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Mooyiisi bí Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yii: «Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan nín yóoǹ mara yii ní ŋá puee sèé:

english_verse: I will welcome an offering from anyone who wants to give something. You may bring gold, silver, or bronze;
translation_verse: <Ní lēēmaan ni-kansikin tigaajati tin ni cááyee poon kí ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa. Bin làá tīīyee ń tīī nì dipɔbil diba. Bí tīī sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti,

english_verse: blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair;
translation_verse: nì bigulifamambi nì gulfab bin bí gùŋgumee nì bigulifamambi cínciŋ nì bigulifapimbi bin bí fálfalee nì tiŋɔkuti,

english_verse: tanned ram skin or fine leather; acacia wood;
translation_verse: nì ipigban in bi mántèe nì igban in dàfì tikpilee nì akasiya dɔi,

english_verse: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or
translation_verse: nì ŋkpam min bi làá nīn cáa ŋáań fitilabinee nì talaalu kpam min bi làá nīn cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú ti-Dindaanee nì talaalub bin bi làá nīn tùutēe,

english_verse: the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it;
translation_verse: nì Dipoondi dakaau nì u-kpandɔi nì u-bìil nì ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋun pìtī circir laŋki nì circir páaa laŋki kansikinee,

english_verse: the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread;
translation_verse: nì teebil nì u-kpandɔi nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ditundi u-puee nì kpɔnɔb bin bi cāabìń ki pāantí ti-Dindaan nimbiinee,

english_verse: the lamp with its equipment and oil;
translation_verse: nì fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ nì fitilab nì bi-kpam,

english_verse: the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent;
translation_verse: nì talaalutuukaa saraafaŋŋu nì ŋu-kpandɔi nì ŋkpam min bi sìtī unil yil pu kí dū-u kí sú Unimbɔtee nì talaalutuukaa nì ŋŋaabu ŋun sàkā circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔkee,

english_verse: the altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand;
translation_verse: nì saraawɔkaa faŋŋu nì ŋu-làaŋ́ki kin sá tasa kútee nì ŋu-kpandɔi nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee nì kusampeeu nì tikúti tin pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee,

english_verse: the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance;
translation_verse: nì iŋaabu in bi làá dūú màntīí gíb́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindee nì i-dɔjaatii nì tikúti tin bi làá dūú tíĺ idɔjaa taapuee nì sata un bi làá dūú sàkan̄ dicindi punyɔkɔkee,

english_verse: the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard;
translation_verse: nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kpakpaaŋi nì ŋu-cindi kpakpaaŋi nì ŋu-ŋmiii,

english_verse: Moses finished speaking, and everyone left.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel yab nyáń Mooyiisi cee.

english_verse: Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes.
translation_verse: Bin nìn cáá tiniti ki làá tīī nì dipɔbil dibee nìn cáań ti-Dindaan bi-wanti bí dūú cóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu, kí tɔ̄ atuun ŋin kɔkɔ sá bí dūú tɔ̄ee ní kí dūú ŋáĺ circir wampeeŋkaati.

english_verse: Men and women came willingly and gave all kinds of gold jewelry such as pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní bininjab nì binimpoobi bin cáá tinitee yōoǹní akimbil nì falfatib nì mbɔmbiyaamu nì abɔmbil nì sindaariya wanti tin sá tiwannyɔkɔntikaalee ki dī akoobil nín sá puee ki dūu ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ nìn cáá bi-dumpui bigulifamambi gùŋgumee nì gulfab bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin pīiǹee nì tiŋɔkuti nì ipigban in bi mántèe nì igban in dàfèe, nìn cáań ki tīī.

english_verse: Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ nìn lēē animbil kúti nì tasa kúti ki yóoǹ kí dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan saraayee nìn cáań. Bin kɔkɔ nìn cáá akasiya dɔyee nìn cáań bí dūú tɔ̄ atuun.

english_verse: And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
translation_verse: Binimpoobi bin nyí diwanlulee nìn dū bi-pɔbiliŋ ki tīī ki dū tiŋɔkuti ki lùn̄ tiwan.

english_verse: The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest.
translation_verse: Samaa kpilib nìn cáań ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì soowamee nì ataŋkpanyaan aba mun bí dūú nákań eefoodi lɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee,

english_verse: They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests.
translation_verse: nì talaalub bin sɔ́fèe nì fitilab kpam nì min bi làá nīn cáa sìtī unil yil pu kí dū-u kí sú Unimbɔtee nì talaalutuukaa.

english_verse: Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts. Bezalel and Oholiab (Exodus
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, bininjab nì binimpoobi nìn dàkā tiniti ki cáań tin kɔkɔ máaǹ bí dūú tɔ̄ atuunee ki ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan nì dipɔbil diba. Bitɔntɔnliibi bin túń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tundee

english_verse: Moses said to the people of Israel: The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan lēē Uurii jipɔɔn Beesaleel, Uur un sá Juuda naakookunee naantiiu.

english_verse: Not only has the Lord filled him with his Spirit, but he has given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood.
translation_verse: U ŋūǹ kí kpítí ataŋkpee kí nákań, kí dū ndɔ kí kpítí kí dūú tɔ̄ atuun ŋí nīn bí a-ba a-ba.

english_verse: The Lord is urging him and Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to teach others.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan pú-u ŋŋmam ú dàkà bi nín nāantí tiwan kí dūú tɔ̄ atuun puee kii u nín tí pú Ayiisamaaki un sá Daani naakookunee jipɔɔn Ooliyaab puee.

english_verse: and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi dū tiwan tin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab nìn cáań ki ŋá saraa bí dūú tɔ̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋee ki tīī-bi. Kutaafaau kamaayee, binib nìn gbíntìi cāabìń tiwan nì dipɔbil diba.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.”
translation_verse: ki cūtìi ká Mooyiisi ki bí-u yii: <Binib bíi cāabìń tiwan an wīikí tikpil ki jítiǹ min ti-Dindaan bālifì bí dūú tɔ̄ ditundee pu kpataaa.>

english_verse: But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done. The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Di sá yii tiwan tin bi nìn cáań bí dūú tɔ̄ atuun kɔkɔ nín sá puee nìn wīikí tikpil. An nìn wīikí ki lákatì. Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu bɔ́ntitam

english_verse: and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū aŋaajan aŋmoo ki ŋáĺ ki kpáfì, ní ki dū aŋmoo ŋin kíǹee mun ki ŋáĺ ki kpáfì.

english_verse: These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ajan aŋmoo ki ŋáĺ ki kpáfì ubaanti, ní ki dū aluu mun ki ŋáĺ ki kpáfì ubaanti.

english_verse: Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Boonee ní bi mántì tipigban ki dūu bīiǹ tanti un bīī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu puee, ní ki dū ŋgban ŋun dàfèe ki páaǹ.

english_verse: Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
translation_verse: Mimmee idɔjaatee nìn sá inii dee, ní i-taapu tílkaati nìn sá animbil kúti ní ki nìn sá saalku nì ubɔ, an dàkà yii ndɔjaati ŋubɔ, titílkaal tili.

english_verse: Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpáá idɔjaati iluu ki cóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu boon pú jandi din bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee.

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: Idɔjaati gbanti taapui nìn dátiǹ tɔb, ama ní ki tin dūu kpáfì yilpu dibɔɔbaantiil dibɔmbipeepeekaalin. Míǹ ní idɔjaatiliitilee nìn sá tiwambaantiil ní ki nìn sá titíkiŋkaal.

english_verse: Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall.
translation_verse: Ŋkalim ŋun nìn bí kansikinee nìn jítì idɔjaati in bi kpááyee kansikin nì kansikin ní, kí yòon̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kílilaŋki kí tin cáá kátí.

english_verse: The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through. The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki nyūntì idɔjaati in bi kpááyee nì ikalimee pu, ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu mun poon ní bi dū ikalimee ki bɔ́ee.

english_verse: For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū gulfab bin bí fálfal ki dàfèe, nì bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee ki lùn̄ ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋubɔ mun, usatalul nyáantì-ŋu ní bi dūu sākaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bi máǹ wèeee nì bi máǹ cínciŋee nì gulfab bin bí fálfal ki dàfèe ki lùn̄ ŋŋaasakaŋkaa, ki lùn̄ keerubimbi ki nákáǹ ŋŋaabuee pu.

english_verse: They also made four acacia wood posts and covered them with gold. Then gold rings were fastened to the posts, which were set on silver stands.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū-ŋu ki sākaǹ akasiya dɔjaai inaa in bi dū sindaariya ki nyūntì sindaariya babikaati túuńee. Bi nìn dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ titílkaal tinaa ki dūu tíĺ taapu.

english_verse: They made five posts, covered them completely with gold, and set each of them on a gold-covered bronze stand. Finally, they attached hooks for the curtain.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpítì akasiya dɔjaatii iŋmoo, ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-i ki dūu cóoǹ, ní ki dū titábikaal tin bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́yee ki bá, ní ki dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ titílkaal tiŋmoo ki tíĺ idɔjaatee taapu. Idɔjaati gbanti pu ní bi nìn dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaayee ki sākaǹ.

english_verse: He covered it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the top.
translation_verse: U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì poon nì boon, ní ki dū sindaariya ki kpákám̀ anyɔɔgbán.

english_verse: He made four gold rings and attached one of them to each of the four legs of the chest.
translation_verse: U nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ abɔmbil anaa ki báaǹ dakaayee kpiŋŋi naatil, dijandi diba abɔmbil ali, diba mun abɔmbil ali.

english_verse: Then he made two poles of acacia wood, covered them with gold,
translation_verse: U nìn kpítì akasiya dɔŋu kpandɔi ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-i.

english_verse: The entire lid of the chest, which was made of pure gold, was the place of mercy.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u dū sindaariyamɔnti ki mɔ́ɔ́ dakaayee bìil. Di-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meeta ubɔ nì santimeetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo ní di-waaŋŋu nìn sá santimeetab biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa.

english_verse: On each of the two ends of the chest he made a winged creature of hammered gold. They faced each other, and their wings covered the place of mercy. The Table for the Sacred Bread (Exodus
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpátì bi-feeŋyi yilpu ki bīiǹ didakaabiil pu. Bi nìn tɔ́kɔ́ ki túĺ tɔb ní bi-nimbiiŋyi tīī didakaabiil pu. Kpɔnɔb bin bi dūu ŋá ti-Dindaan saraayee teebiliu kpáatam

english_verse: He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border
translation_verse: Ní ki kpítì kidɔpampaŋ, kì wāā kii santimeetab binii ki kpákám̀ anyɔɔgbán, ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: He made four gold rings and attached one to each of the legs
translation_verse: U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ sindaariya bɔmbiliŋ anaa ki dūu báaǹ ki nákáǹ teebilee kpiŋŋi naatil pu, ataa cee.

english_verse: near the edging. The poles for carrying the table were placed through these rings
translation_verse: Abɔmbilee nìn náká teebilee kpaanceetii, ní bi dū ikpandɔ ki bɔ́ abɔmbilee poon bí ŋmā kí nīn yòontí teebilee.

english_verse: Everything that was to be set on the table was made of pure gold—the bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings. The Lampstand (Exodus
translation_verse: U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ palantab nì kɔɔpub nì asambil nì itúun bí nīn cáa ŋáań ndaam ki féeń ti-Dindaan. U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ an wanti gbanti kɔkɔ. Fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati mɔ́ɔtam

english_verse: Bezalel made a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered gold,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u dū sindaariyamɔnti ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitila tɔ́kɔŋkaati. Ti-taapu nì ti-kpinjaatiŋu nì ti-kpiiŋyi nì ti-gbiŋŋi nì ti-pumpukum kɔkɔ nìn sá tiwambaantiil mmɔm ní.

english_verse: with three branches on each of its two sides.
translation_verse: Ikpiin iluu nìn nyánní ŋkpiinjaatee pu. Dijandi kamaa nìn cáá ikpiin ita ita.

english_verse: There was also a blossom where each pair of branches came out from the stem.
translation_verse: Ikpiin iluu in nìn túkú fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati kpinjaatiŋu puee taapu nìn cáá agbin.

english_verse: The lamp and its equipment, including the tongs and trays, were made of about
translation_verse: U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ. Talaalutuukaa saraafaŋŋu mɔ́ɔtam

english_verse: He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it.
translation_verse: U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì ŋu-yilpu nì ŋu-boon ki māntìi tú nì ŋu-yiŋyi, ní ki dū sindaariya ki kpákám̀-ŋu ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: Then below the edging on opposite sides he attached two gold rings through which he put the poles for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ abɔmbil ali ki bá bi nín kpákám̀ nsaraafan taapu puee ajan liitil pu, bí nīn cáá ŋi-kpandɔi ki bōotí ki yòontí-ŋu.

english_verse: These poles were also made of acacia wood and covered with gold. The Oil for Dedication and the Incense (Exodus
translation_verse: U nìn dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpítì ikpandɔee ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-i.

english_verse: Bezalel mixed the sacred oil for dedication and the pure spices for the sweet-smelling incense.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá ŋkpam min sɔ́fèe kii utalaaluŋal nín ŋáań puee bí nīn cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú Unimbɔti nì talaalutuukaa umɔnti.

english_verse: Bezalel made a large bowl and a stand out of bronze from the mirrors of the women who helped at the entrance to the sacred tent. The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: U nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusampeeu nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee. Bi nìn dū binimpoobi bin nìn tūǹ ditundi circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee gitiŋi ní ki túń an tuuŋŋi. Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi bɔ́ntitam

english_verse: Then he attached a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners to put the poles through.
translation_verse: U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ abɔmbil anaa ki dūu bá tasa kúti làaŋ́kee kpiŋŋi naatil pu kí ŋmā kí dū ikpandɔ kí bɔ̄ poon.

english_verse: put them through the rings for carrying the altar, which was shaped like an open box. The Large Bronze Bowl (Exodus
translation_verse: Ní ki dū ikpandɔee ki bɔ́ abɔmbil ŋin bí nsaraafan jaŋŋi puee poon bí ŋmā kí nīn yòontí-ŋu. Bi nìn dū idɔ ki kpáá nsaraafan ní ŋu-poon dɔ̄ fám tiba kpá poon.

english_verse: And it was used to make the stands for the entrance to the tent, the altar and its grating, the equipment for the altar,
translation_verse: Bitɔntɔnliibi nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki dɔjaatii taapu tílkaati nì tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu nì ŋu-tasa kúti làaŋ́ki, nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee,

english_verse: For the entrance to the courtyard, Bezalel made a curtain nine meters long, which he hung on four bronze posts that were set on bronze stands. This curtain was
translation_verse: I nìn sàkā tasa kúti dɔjaatii inaa in tɔ́kɔ́ tasa kúti tílkaati tinaa mun puee ní. Tibakaal nìn sá animbil kúti ní bi dū animbil kúti ki nyūntì idɔjaatee yilpu nì mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamuee.

english_verse: for the west. Then he hung a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. He placed three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hung a curtain
translation_verse: U nìn dū mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamu nì tibakaal tin bi dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee ki cúú satabee ki dūu sākaǹ tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ an bí kii idɔjaatee mmuŋku. Idɔjaatee nìn cáá titílkaal mmuŋku tin bi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee.

english_verse: Bezalel had worked closely with Oholiab, who was an expert at designing and engraving, and at embroidering blue, purple, and red wool. The two of them completed the work that the Lord had commanded to be done. Moses put Aaron's son Ithamar in charge of the Levites who kept record of the metals used for the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ayiisamaaki un sá Daani naakookunee jipɔɔn Ooliyaab di nìn tútuǹ-u. U nìn sá ukpiŋkpiiti ní ki nìn ŋūǹ ki lèekī tiwan naŋku tiba pu, ki nìn ŋūǹ kí dū gulfa un máǹ gùŋgumee nì un máǹ cínciŋee nì un máǹ wèeeeyee nì gulfapiin kí dūú lù sata àá kí dūú gbá tiwan pu.

english_verse: Two thousand four hundred and twenty-five kilograms of bronze were given.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín nìn cáań tasa kúti tiŋyee kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì kiiloobi kutukub bili nì dilaataal nì mmuŋku nì binaa.

english_verse: the stands for the posts that surrounded the courtyard, including those at the entrance to the courtyard, and the pegs for the tent and the courtyard.
translation_verse: nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi dɔjaatii taapu tílkaati kɔkɔ, nì di-punyɔkɔki dɔjaatii taapu tílkaati nì ŋu-kpakpaaŋi nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì dicindi naabakaku kpakpaaŋi.

english_verse: Beautiful priestly clothes were made of blue, purple, and red wool for Aaron to wear when he performed his duties in the holy place. This was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee ki ŋáĺ circir wampeeŋkaati bí nīn cáa tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ditundi. Bi nìn ŋáĺ Aarɔn circir wampeeŋkaati kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.

english_verse: The entire priestly vest was made of fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool. Thin sheets of gold were hammered out and cut into threads that were skillfully woven into the vest.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gbáń ki kpátì sindaariya ní ki gífì ncalimu ncalimu, ní biwanluliibi cáa ŋmàlintí nì gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgum nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì gulfab bin pīiǹ ki dàfèe ki lùn̄.

english_verse: Onyx stones were placed in gold settings, and each one was engraved with the name of one of Israel's sons.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì soowamee ali ki fúuń sindaariya sɔntin, ki dū kigaai ki ŋmàn̄ Jaakɔb jipɔmbi yiŋŋi ataŋkpeeyee pu, kii bi nín cákà kijalii pu puee.

english_verse: Then these were attached to the shoulder straps of the vest, so the Lord would never forget his people. Everything was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Breastpiece (Exodus
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ataŋkpeeyee ki bá ŋŋaacalimu mun bi ŋáĺ ki tábiǹ eefoodee. Ŋíǹ di nìn sá kii kudaaŋŋu ki téetí Jaakɔb jipɔmbi pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee. Kilɔbiki ŋáltam

english_verse: The words “Dedicated to the Lord” were engraved on a narrow strip of pure gold,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi dū sindaariyamɔnti ki mɔ́ɔ́ ki nántiǹ mpumpukum ní ki dū kigaai ki ŋmàn̄ ti-pu yii: <Bi dū-u ki sú ti-Dindaan.>

english_verse: a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond were in the second row;
translation_verse: Ŋkuuliliiti nìn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì noofeekee, nì ŋin bi yíì safiiree nì ŋin bi yíì yaaliimee.

english_verse: a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst were in the third row;
translation_verse: Ŋkuutataatee nìn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì leeseemee nì ŋin bi yíì seebooyee nì ŋin bi yíì alamaayee.

english_verse: and a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper were in the fourth row. They were mounted in a delicate gold setting,
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì taarsiisee nì ŋin bi yíì soowamee, nì ŋin bi yíì yaasipee ki nákáǹ ŋkuunanaati pu. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ tin poon bi làá dū ataŋkpanyaanee kí fúuńee.

english_verse: Two gold rings were attached to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fastened with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū anyɔɔgbán ali ŋin kíǹee ki bá sindaariya wanti tili tin poon ní ataŋkpanyaan fúuń eefoodi ŋaacalimmu pu, ní an bí kilɔbiki nyɔkɔpuee.

english_verse: To keep the breastpiece in place, a blue cord was used to tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Clothes for the Priests (Exodus
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee ŋmiiŋu ki bɔ́ kilɔbiki bɔmbiliŋin nì eefoodi bɔmbiliŋin ki kúĺ, ní kilɔbikee pá eefoodi dambalau pu ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kaa cìŋkī, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee Usaraaŋakpil wampeeŋkaati tiba mun ŋáltam

english_verse: which was fastened to Aaron's turban. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Work Is Completed (Exodus
translation_verse: Ní bi dū gulfa un máǹ gùŋgumee ki lùn̄ kiŋaacaliŋ ki cúú sindaariya pumpukumee ki nákáǹ ŋŋaabu ŋun bi cáa fìǹ diyilee yilpu pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee. Bi dóò circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ

english_verse: When Moses saw that the people had done everything exactly as the Lord had commanded, he gave them his blessing.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nín ká yii bi túń atuun gbanti kɔkɔ kii ti-Dindaan nín bí bí ŋá pueeyee, ní u mēē ki bīiǹ bi-pu.

english_verse: with an opening in the center for the head. The material around the collar was bound so as to keep it from wearing out.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lēē di-kansikin kinyɔkɔ, bi yaa làá pèen̄ee bí dū diyil kí bɔ̄ niin. Bi nìn lùn̄ kinyɔkɔee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi gbìfì ki dàfì kí taa ŋmā kí cátí.

english_verse: Along the hem of the robe were woven pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a bell of pure gold between each of them. This robe was to be worn by Aaron when he performed his duties.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū sindaariya waŋkilimmu nì greenaadi subiliŋ ŋin bi lùn̄ee ki lúntì disaraaŋabɔkutil júti taapu ki sákaǹ sákaǹ ki māntìi tú, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.

english_verse: Everything that Aaron and his sons wore was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, including their robes and turbans, their fancy caps and underwear, and even their sashes that were embroidered with needlework.
translation_verse: Ní bi dū gulfapiin un dàfèe nì un máǹ gùŋgumee nì un máǹ wèeeeyee nì un máǹ cínciŋee ki ŋáĺ dambala ki gbáń-u, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.

english_verse: the sacred chest with its carrying poles and the place of mercy;
translation_verse: - nì Dipoondi taŋkpapilinti dakaau nì u-kpandɔi nì u-bìil,

english_verse: So the people of Israel finished making everything the Lord had told Moses to make.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Isirayeel yab nìn túń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋi ki dóò. Ti-Dindaan nín nìn dàkā Mooyiisi yii bí ŋá puee, míǹ deedee ní bi nìn ŋá.

english_verse: Then they brought it all to Moses: the sacred tent and its equipment, including the hooks, the framework and crossbars, and its posts and stands;
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn yōoǹní tin kɔkɔ bi làá dūú cóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋuee ki cáań Mooyiisi cee: - tanti nì u-wanti kɔkɔ an dàkà yii, titábikaal nì tifukuŋkaal nì ikalim nì idɔjaati nì titílkaal,

english_verse: the covering of tanned ram skins and fine leather; the inside curtain;
translation_verse: - nì tipigban tin bi mántèe nì igban in bi cáa bìintée nì ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋun pìtī circir laŋki nì circir páaa laŋki kansikinee,

english_verse: the table with all that goes on it, including the sacred bread;
translation_verse: - nì teebil nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ditundi u-puee nì kpɔnɔb bin bi cāabìń ki pāantí ti-Dindaan nimbiinee,

english_verse: the lampstand of pure gold, together with its equipment and oil;
translation_verse: - nì sindaariyamɔnti fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ nì fitilab nì bi-kpam,

english_verse: the gold-covered incense altar; the ordination oil and the sweet-smelling incense; the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
translation_verse: - nì sindaariya saraafaŋŋu nì ŋkpam min bi sìtī unil yil pu kí dū-u kí sú Unimbɔtee nì talaalutuukaa, - nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu,

english_verse: the bronze altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand;
translation_verse: - nì tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu nì ŋu-làaŋ́ki kin sá tasa kútee nì ŋu-kpandɔi nì ŋu-wanti, - nì kusampeeu nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee,

english_verse: the curtain with its posts and cords, and its pegs and stands that go around the courtyard; everything needed for the sacred tent;
translation_verse: - nì iŋaabu in bi làá dūú màntīí gíb́ dikpafindi tantiu cindee nì i-dɔjaatii nì i-tílkaati nì dicindi punyɔkɔki ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu, nì ŋu-ŋmiii nì ŋu-kpakpaaŋi, - nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi làá nīn cáa tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon tuuŋŋee,

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: Set up my tent on the first day of the year
translation_verse: «Uŋmapeepeekaa wimpeekaaŋu dalee, á dū tanti un poon dipoondi taŋkpapilinti kēe kí cóoń.

english_verse: and put the chest with the Ten Commandments behind the inside curtain.
translation_verse: Á dū dakaa un poon Dipoondi marab kēe kí yóoń ŋŋaapìtikaa boon án nīn lìkī bí taa nín̄ wāĺ.

english_verse: Bring in the table and set on it those things that are made for it. Also bring in the lampstand and attach the lamps to it.
translation_verse: Á cáań teebil un pu bi làá nīn pāantí kpɔnɔb m-nimbiinee kpɔnɔb ń nīn pá. Á cáań fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati ní kí tūū fitilab.

english_verse: Then place the gold altar of incense in front of the sacred chest and hang a curtain at the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Á dū sindaariya saraafaŋŋu ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalubee kí yóoń dakaa un poon Dipoondi marab kēe nyɔkɔpu, ní kí dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa kí sàkan̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki pu.

english_verse: Set the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the entrance to my tent.
translation_verse: Á dū saraawɔkaa faŋŋu kí yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Put the large bronze bowl between the tent and the altar and fill the bowl with water.
translation_verse: Á dū kusampeeu kí yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì nsaraafan kansikin, ní kí lúń nnyim kí gbéeǹ.

english_verse: Surround the tent and the altar with the wall of curtains and hang the curtain that was made for the entrance.
translation_verse: Á dū iŋaabu in bi dū gulfab ki lùn̄ee kí màntīí gíb́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi, ní kí dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa kí sàkan̄ kipunyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Do the same thing with the altar for offering sacrifices and its equipment
translation_verse: Á dū ŋkpamee kí sìtī nsaraafan nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee, mimmee a dū-ŋu ki sú-mi dee, ní ŋú kpántí circir.

english_verse: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent and tell them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: Á cáań Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi kí yóoń dikpafindi tantiu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní kí yàntī bí fàl̀ kí kpántí circir.

english_verse: Dress Aaron in the priestly clothes, then use the sacred olive oil to ordain him and dedicate him to me as my priest.
translation_verse: Boonee á dū circir wampeeŋkaati kí pèen̄ Aarɔn, ní kí dū ŋkpam kí sìtī u-yil pu kí dū-u kí sú-mi ú nīn tūǹ man tundi.

english_verse: Put the priestly robes on Aaron's sons
translation_verse: Á yàntī u-jipɔmbi ń sútiń kí pìl̄-si, ní á dū poon bɔkutifɔkɔŋ kí pèen̄-bi.

english_verse: And on the first day of the first month of the second year, the sacred tent was set up.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín nyáń kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee, an tú dibindi uŋmapeepeekaa wimpeekaaŋu dal ní bi cóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu.

english_verse: then the two layers of coverings were hung over them.
translation_verse: U nìn kpátì tanti ŋaabui ki bīiǹ, ní ki dū iŋaabiiŋkaa ki páaǹ, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.
