english_verse: The stones with the Ten Commandments written on them were stored in the sacred chest, the place of mercy was put on top of it, and the carrying poles were attached.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn dū titaŋkpapilindi tin pu bi ŋmàn̄ marab saalaayee ki tākaǹ dakaayee poon, ní ki dū dakaa kpandɔi ki bɔ́ dakaayee bɔmbiliŋin, ní ki dū u-bìil ki púkuǹ.

english_verse: The chest was brought into the tent and set behind the curtain in the most holy place. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: U nìn cáá dakaayee ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ní ki dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ki pītì bí taa nín̄ wāĺ dakaayee, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.

english_verse: The table for the sacred bread was put along the north wall of the holy place,
translation_verse: U nìn cáá teebil un pu bi pāantí kpɔnɔb ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ŋgan pú, ŋŋaapìtikaa nyɔkɔpu pú.

english_verse: The lampstand was put along the south wall,
translation_verse: U nìn cáá fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ŋgiil pú teebil nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: then the lamps were attached to it there in the presence of the Lord.
translation_verse: U nìn tūū fitilab ti-Dindaan nimbiin, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.

english_verse: The gold incense altar was set up in front of the curtain,
translation_verse: U nìn cáá sindaariya saraafaŋŋu ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ŋŋaapìtikaa nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: and sweet-smelling incense was burned on it. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: U nìn tūū talaalub ŋu-pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.

english_verse: The curtain was hung at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: U nìn dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ki sākaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Then the altar for offering sacrifices was put in front of the tent, and animal sacrifices and gifts of grain were offered there.
translation_verse: U nìn dū nsaraafan ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu, ní ki ŋá saraawɔkaa nì tijin saraau ŋu-pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.

english_verse: The large bronze bowl was placed between the altar and the entrance to the tent. It was filled with water,
translation_verse: U nìn dū kusampeeu ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì nsaraafan kansikin, ní ki lúń nnyim ki gbéeǹ bí nīn jòotī ki fíntí.

english_verse: then Moses and Aaron, together with Aaron's sons, washed their hands and feet.
translation_verse: Nnyim gbanti ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nìn jòotī ki fíntí bi-ŋalii nì bi-taaŋi.

english_verse: In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti kamaa bi yaa làá kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun kí sútí kí pìl̄ nsaraafanee, see bí fíntí míǹ, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.

english_verse: Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ditagbandi dɔ́miń ki bīiǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu, ní Unimbɔti nyooti kɔ́ ki gbí ŋu-poon.

english_verse: And so, Moses could not enter the tent.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, di sá yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí ŋu-poon.

english_verse: Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow;
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, ditagbandee yaa nìn yíkìi dāntì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu yilpuee, ní Isirayeel yab ń yīkì dinaapaal din pu bi nìn bée kí nìkī bi-saŋkindi.

english_verse: then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again.
translation_verse: Ama ditagbandee yaa kaa nìn yíkìi dāntèe, bi nìn kā míǹ ní ki cí daliŋkin di làá yīkì kí dàntēe.

english_verse: No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tagbandee nìn bīī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu ŋwiimpu, ama ní kunyeeuee an sá ŋŋmi ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ wāĺ. An nìn pée bí míǹ ní bi cōom̀ bi-saŋkindi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
translation_verse: Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań kuwaŋkuluuee yil pu ní ti-Dindaan ń nín fōō u-saraau ní kí dū u-kpitii kí pɔ̄-u.

english_verse: After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ú làntì unaayee circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi ń dū unaayee fatikuu kí yàaǹ kí màntīí tū nsaraafan ŋun bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki caŋinee.

english_verse: Skin the bull and cut it up,
translation_verse: Ú lēē unaayee gbaŋŋu, kí càkà u-nanti.

english_verse: while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn jipɔmbi ń kpāā ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu ní kí dū idɔ kí páań.

english_verse: Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Un cáań kuwaŋkuluuee ń dū nnyim kí fíntí ina nì ayaka ní usaraaŋal ubɔ ń dū tinanee kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraawɔkaa, saraa un ní bi dù tinan kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi, u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.

english_verse: If you sacrifice a ram or a goat, it must not have anything wrong with it.
translation_verse: «An yaa sá upii àá uŋoobu ní udaan cáań kí ŋá saraawɔkaayee, kuwaŋkuluuee laaba ń taa nīn wɔ̀b̄.

english_verse: Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ú làntì-ku circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ti-Dindaan nimbiin, nsaraafan caŋin, ŋgan pú. Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi ń dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Un cáań kuwaŋkuluuee ń dū nnyim kí fíntí ina nì ayaka ní usaraaŋal ubɔ ń dū tinanee kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraawɔkaa, saraa un ní bi dù tinan kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi, u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.

english_verse: If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon.
translation_verse: «An yaa tí sá unoon ní udaan cáań kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, an nīn sá kinanjilii àá dibeenanjil.

english_verse: A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar,
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ubɔ ń fōō unoonee kí cáá cùnnì nsaraafan caŋin, kí tùkutī diyil kí dūú wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu, ní kí dū u-fatikuu kí còol̀ nsaraafan kpiŋŋi pu.

english_verse: remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar.
translation_verse: Ú lēē kunyannyanciliu nì tin kā ku-poonee kí fá nsaraafan caŋin ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, laakin bi bīil̀ ŋkpam min bi wùn̄ee fantamee.

english_verse: Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Ní ú cúú unoonee kí dáaĺ kí cátí mili ifeen kansikin án taa nàbitī, ní kí dūú páań idɔ in bi dūu páaǹ ŋŋmi pu nsaraafan puee án wà. An di sá saraawɔkaa, saraa un bi dù tinan kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.»

english_verse: When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour,
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa là kí cáań tijimpin saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, án nīn sá ŋyim. Ú bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī, kí dū talaalutuukaa kí páań,

english_verse: and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: ní kí cáań kí tīī Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi. Usaraaŋal un làá ŋá saraa gbantee ń yáfí ŋyim diŋaŋkul din sá kudaaŋŋu ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii úǹ di yì saraa gbantee kí dū ŋkpam kí búuń ní kí dū talaalutuukaa un bi cáańee kɔkɔ kí kūtì kí dūú wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.

english_verse: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
translation_verse: Saraayee jandi din kíǹee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di yì. Dijandi gbanti sá circir páaa wanti ní, kun puee an sá saraa un bi lēē ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki tīī ti-Dindaanee ní.

english_verse: If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
translation_verse: «An yaa sá tijin tin bi púĺ dibubulinee ní ubɔ yaa cáań kí ŋá saraayee, án nīn sá kpɔnɔ un bi dū ŋyim ki búuń ŋkpamin ki púĺ an kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee.

english_verse: If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast.
translation_verse: An yaa sá tijin tin bi pūul̀ titaŋkpapilindi puee saraauee, ú dū ŋkpam kí búuń ŋyim kí taa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ.

english_verse: Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil.
translation_verse: Ú càkà càkà-u ní kí bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī an pu. Tijimpin saraau dee.

english_verse: If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
translation_verse: An yaa tí sá tijin tin bi tòó kikpasaŋ poonee saraauee, ú dū ŋkpam kí búuń ŋyim kí ŋá tijin gbanti.

english_verse: You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Ú cáań saraa un u bɔ́ntì kí tīī ti-Dindaanee kí ŋúbiǹ usaraaŋal ní úǹ ń fōō kí cáá síiń nsaraafan caŋin.

english_verse: Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Saraa gbanti poonee, usaraaŋal ń lēē dijandi din sá kudaaŋŋu ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii úǹ di yì saraa gbantee kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraa un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.

english_verse: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
translation_verse: Dijandi din kíǹee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di yì. Dijandi gbanti sá circir páaa wanti ní, kun puee an sá saraa un bi lēē ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki tīī ti-Dindaanee ní.

english_verse: Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: «Tijimpin saraau un kamaa ni làá ŋá kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ ń taa nín̄ bí poon. Ubɔ kaa tí máaǹ kí dū ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ àá tisiil kí ŋá saraa kí wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Ama u ŋūǹ kí cáań kí ŋá tijincɔ̀fikaal saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Ú taa pée dū-tì kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu kii saraa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.

english_verse: Salt is offered when you make an agreement with me, so sprinkle salt on these sacrifices.
translation_verse: «Tijimpin saraau kamaa poon máaǹ kí nīn cáá ŋyaam. Ú taa pée yàntī ŋyaam min sá ni-Nimbɔtiu poondi daaŋkuee ń lóó u-saraabi poon.

english_verse: Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest.
translation_verse: «Tijincɔ̀fikaal ní ubɔ yaa cáań kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, ú púĺ ifin kí yìlifì abil ní kí cáań kí ŋá saraa.

english_verse: You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: Ú bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī an pu ní kí dū talaalutuukaa kí páań. Tijimpin saraau dee.

english_verse: A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń dū saraayee, an dàkà yii abil ŋin bi yīlifèe dijandi nì ŋkpamee nì talaalutuukaayee kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi. An di sá tijimpin saraau un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee.»

english_verse: When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa lēē u-nacaŋkpuŋkun unaa kí ŋá mpèé saraauee, ú nīn sá uja àá usal un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee. Ú cáań-u circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań kuwaŋkuluuee yil pu, kí làntì-ku circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi ń dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee, ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebil dicilpu.

english_verse: Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi ń dūú kūtì saraawɔkaa un pá idɔ in bi dūu páaǹ ŋŋmi pu nsaraafan puee. An di sá mpèé saraau un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.

english_verse: Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: «An yaa sá upii àá uŋoobu ní ubɔ cáań kí ŋá saraa kí dàkà u nì ti-Dindaan kansikin pèéŋuee, án nīn sá uja àá usal un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee.

english_verse: If you offer a sheep, you must present it to me at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: An yaa sá dipibil ní udaan cáań kí dūú ŋá saraayee, ú cáań-dì ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań dipibilee yil pu ní kí làntì-dì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi ń dū di-fatikuu kí yàaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee, ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebilee dicilpu.

english_verse: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
translation_verse: Niinee ní usaraaŋal ń cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá tijin saraau un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me
translation_verse: «An yaa sá uŋoobu ní udaan cáań kí dùú ŋá saraayee, ú cáań-u ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań uŋoobuee yil pu ní kí làntì-u circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi ń dū u-fatikuu kí yàaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebilee dicilpu.

english_verse: One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me. All fat belongs to me.
translation_verse: Niinee ní usaraaŋal ń dūú wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá tijin saraau un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee. «Tin kamaa pée sá ŋkpamee, ti-Dindaan di yì.

english_verse: So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
translation_verse: Án nīn sá dibɔkpaal din làá nīn bí ki cá jaanjaanee ki tīī ni nì ni-biyaamu yii báà laakin kamaa ní ni yaa bàn̄ ki kóòyee, ní nīn nyí yii naa máaǹ kí ŋmɔ́ kuwaŋkuluu fatikuu nì ku-kpam.»

english_verse: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
translation_verse: ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin niinee ní ú dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē fatikuee kí dūú yàaǹ ŋŋaabu ŋun bi dūu pītì ki yākatì circir páaa nì circir laŋkee pu ŋfunyɔm miluli.

english_verse: This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań uŋɔjee yil pu ní kí làntì-u laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkuti ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau dee.

english_verse: Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē uŋɔsalee fatikuu kí dūú ŋmìtī saraawɔkaa faŋŋu yiŋyi pu. Ú dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu taapu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do. When the High Priest Sins The Lord said:
translation_verse: «Tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Ubɔ yaa kaa nyí ní ki yīntì ki ŋá tin ti-Dindaan marab nee kansikin ubɔ bí yii bí taa ŋée,

english_verse: When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: «an yaa sá usaraaŋakpil di ŋá ikpiti ní u-kpitii gbanti yāntì samaa kɔkɔ kɔ́ ikpitinee, u máaǹ kí cáań dinabil din laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa ní kí nín ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.

english_verse: The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there.
translation_verse: Ú cáań dinabilee circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ti-Dindaan nimbiin, kí dū u-ŋal kí páań dinabilee yil pu ní kí làntì-dì ti-Dindaan nimbiin niin.

english_verse: He will take a bowl of the blood inside the tent,
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil ń dū dinabilee fatikuu kí kɔ́ǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon,

english_verse: Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil ń bàtī fatikuee kí ŋmìtī nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalub ŋu bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ti-Dindaan nimbiinee yiŋyi pu. Ú dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu ŋun bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee taapu.

english_verse: The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap. When the Whole Nation Sins The Lord said:
translation_verse: an dàkà yii dinabilee nanti tin pée kíǹee kɔkɔee, ú cáá nyāntí dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu mpaan ŋun pu bi féeń ŋkpam min bi wùn̄ee fantamee ní kí dūú wà ŋŋmi idɔ pu. Difantancundee pu ní bí dūú wà ŋŋmi.» b. Samaa kɔkɔ saraau

english_verse: When the nation of Israel disobeys me without meaning to, the whole nation is still guilty.
translation_verse: «An yaa sá Isirayeel nikitil kɔkɔ di yaa kaa nyí ní ki yīntì ki ŋá tin ti-Dindaan marab nee kansikin ubɔ bí yii bí taa ŋée, bi fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Boonee bi yaa láa béè ikpiti in bi ŋée, samaa kɔkɔ ń cáań dinabil kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau. Bí cáań-dì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu,

english_verse: where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
translation_verse: ní bitindaŋkpilib ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań dinabilee yil pu ní bi-kansikin ubɔ ń làntì-dì ti-Dindaan nimbiin niin.

english_verse: The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil ń yòon̄ dinabilee fatikuu kí cáá kɔ́ǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon.

english_verse: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
translation_verse: Ú dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē fatiku kí dūú yàaǹ ŋŋaabu ŋun bi dūu pītì ki yākatì circir páaa nì circir laŋkee pu ŋfunyɔm miluli.

english_verse: Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Ú bàtī fatikuee kí ŋmìtī nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalub ŋu bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ti-Dindaan nimbiinee yiŋyi pu. Ú dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu ŋun bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee taapu.

english_verse: After this, the priest will remove the fat from the bull and send it up in smoke on the altar. Finally, he will burn its remains outside the camp, just as he did with the other bull. By this sacrifice the sin of the whole nation will be forgiven. When a Tribal Leader Sins The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ú yòon̄ dinabilee nanti tin kíǹee kɔkɔ kí cáá nyāntí dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu ní kí dū-tì kí wà ŋŋmi kii u nín wùn̄ dinabipeepeekaalee puee. Samaa kɔkɔ kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau dee.» c. Dibɔtibil saraau

english_verse: As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: U yaa láa béè ikpiti in u ŋée, ú cáań uŋɔja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraa.

english_verse: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē uŋɔjee fatikuu kí dūú ŋmìtī saraawɔkaa faŋŋu yiŋyi pu. Ú dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu taapu.

english_verse: Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven. When Ordinary People Sin The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ní ú wà ŋkpam kɔkɔ nsaraafan pu kii bi nín ŋáań mpèé saraau kpam puee. Ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá dibɔtibilee pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní dí ká di-kpitii pɔ̄tam. d. Unifantanti saraau

english_verse: When any of you ordinary people disobey me without meaning to, you are still guilty.
translation_verse: «An yaa sá unifantanti ubɔ di kaa nyí ní ki yīntì ki ŋá tin ti-Dindaan marab nee kansikin ubɔ bí yii bí taa ŋée, udaan fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: U yaa láa béè ikpiti in u ŋée, ú cáań uŋɔsal un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraa u-kpitii gbanti pu.

english_verse: Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
translation_verse: Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań uŋɔsal un u cáań kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee yil pu ní kí làntì-u laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkutee.

english_verse: After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
translation_verse: Ú lēē ŋkpam kɔkɔ kii bi nín lèekī mpèé saraau kpam puee kí cáá wà nsaraafan pu, ní u-sɔnsɔfiŋu ń sɔ̀ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbil. Míǹ ní usaraaŋal máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí fíntí udaan kpitii ní ú nín ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.

english_verse: If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: «An yaa sá upii ní udaan cáań kí ŋá u-kpitii pɔ̄tam saraauee, ú nīn sá upisal un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee.

english_verse: Lead the lamb to the altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
translation_verse: Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań upisalee yil pu ní kí làntì-u laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkutee.

english_verse: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē upisalee fatikuu ní kí dūú ŋmìtī saraawɔkaa faŋŋu yiŋyi pu ní kí dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu taapu.

english_verse: After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Ú lēē upisalee kpam kɔkɔ kii bi nín lèekī mpèé saraau pibil kpam puee, ní usaraaŋal ń cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu nì saraabi bin kɔkɔ sá bí dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee. Usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní ú ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.»

english_verse: You are guilty if you find out that you have accidentally touched anything unclean that comes from a human body.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa tí gbēē unil jɔkɔnti, àá tin kamaa pée kɔ̄ntí unil tijɔkɔndee kaa kpáàa béèyee, bi yaa láa pée tùkū-u ní u béèyee, udaan fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: You are guilty the moment you realize that you have made a hasty promise to do something good or bad.
translation_verse: «Àá ubɔ yaa bíi sòoǹ ní u-nyɔkɔ ŋmátì-u ní u pūtì kí ŋá tikpitil àá tiŋan ní boonee ki dāa béèyee, udaan fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa ŋá ikpiti nee kansikin ibee, udaan máaǹ kí bìitī u-kpitii gbanti pu.

english_verse: Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, u máaǹ kí cáań upisal àá uŋɔsal kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaan kí ŋāŋkì u-bɔkpil. Ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋá ní ú ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tamee.» f. Biwɔfib saraau

english_verse: Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head,
translation_verse: Ú cáań kí tīī usaraaŋal ní úǹ ń lēē unoon un sá bí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee, ní kí míkí kí gíí u-sil kí nákáǹ u-kpaŋkpantaapu, ama ní diyil ń taa tùkutī.

english_verse: splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń dū fatiku kí còol̀ nsaraafan kpiŋŋi pu ní kí dū un kíǹee kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan taapu. Ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau dee.

english_verse: If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it.
translation_verse: «U yaa kaa tí cáá nnanjilimu muli àá abeenanjil alee, u ŋūǹ kí cáań ŋyim kiiloobi bita kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau. Ama ú taa dū ŋkpam nì talaalutuukaa kí kūtì, kun puee an sá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní.

english_verse: Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ú cáań kí tīī usaraaŋal ní úǹ ń yáfí diŋaŋkul din sá kudaaŋŋu ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii úǹ di yì saraa gbantee, ní kí dūú wà nsaraafan pu kí kpáaǹ saraabi bin bi dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee. Ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau dee.

english_verse: By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices. Sacrifices To Make Things Right (Leviticus
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní ú ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam. «Usaraaŋal ń ŋá saraa nee kii bi nín ŋáań tijimpin saraau puee.» g. Dibɔkpil saraau

english_verse: The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to: If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa kaa nyí ní ki dū saraabi bin sá ki tīī ti-Dindaanee ki ŋá min kaa kítèe ní ki kɔ́ diyìntilinee, udaan máaǹ kí cáań upìja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee. Ú lēē upìja gbanti u-picaŋkpuŋkun, u-daaku ń nīn nóó nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nimbiliŋ ŋmàntitam kí cáań kí ŋá saraa kí ŋāŋkì u nín yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan puee.

english_verse: The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar.
translation_verse: Baa pée máaǹ kí dū ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kí ŋá tijin gbanti. Saraabi bin bi cáa wù ŋŋmi ki tìì-mee, dijandi din m dūu tīī-bee dee. Saraa gbantee sá circir páaa wanti ní, a lì kii ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì dibɔkpil saraau nín bí circir puee.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses what the people must do when they commit other sins against the Lord: You have sinned if you rob or cheat someone, if you keep back money or valuables left in your care, or if you find something and claim not to have it.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń dū iŋaapiin in bí fálfalee bɔkutikpaandi kí pèen̄, kí dū iŋaapiin in bí fálfalee cukutigiŋki mun kí lòon̄ ní kí wúkutí saraawɔkaa un bi wùn̄ nsaraafan puee kpam fantam kí bíĺ nsaraafan caŋin.

english_verse: and told him what sacrifices the priests must offer on the morning and evening of the day they are ordained: It is the same as the regular morning and evening sacrifices—half a kilogram of flour
translation_verse: Un di yaa pée gbēē saraa gbanti nantee, udaan nì u-kpuulool dee. Fatiku yaa yāaǹ dibɔkutil din puee, bí fíntí laakin fatiku yāaǹee circir paaŋŋu pu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord: You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning.
translation_verse: Bi nín yáfì ŋyim ki ŋá saraa min kíǹee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ŋūǹ kí dūú ŋá tijin kí jī, ama bí taa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ tijinee poon. Bí jī-tì mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindin.

english_verse: The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out. Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord The Lord said:
translation_verse: «Daliŋkin bi yaa dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ki sú ti-Dindaanee, saraa un bi máaǹ kí cáańee di sá ŋyim kiiloobi bita. Kutaafaauee bí dū dijandi kí ŋá saraa ní kujoouee bí púntí dijandi din kíǹee kí ŋá saraa.

english_verse: When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar,
translation_verse: Bí dū ŋkpam kí búuń ŋyim kí dūú tɔ̄ kalaa kitaŋkpapiliŋ pu. Míǹ boonee bí càkà kí cáań kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaan ní u-sɔnsɔfiŋu ń sɔ̀ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbil.

english_verse: where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: An nīn sá dibɔkpaal din làá nīn dɔ̄ ki cá jaanjaanee yii Aarɔn maaliŋunee, un yil pu bi làá sìtī ŋkpam ú kpántí usaraaŋakpilee ń ŋá saraa gbanti kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Bí dū saraa gbanti kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change. When Priests Are Ordained
translation_verse: «Sòoǹ nì Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi kí tùkù-bi bi nín máaǹ kí nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau puee. Bi yaa cáań kuwaŋkuluu kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee, bí làntì-ku laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkuti ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, kun puee an sá circir páaa wanti ní.

english_verse: mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Bi yaa tɔ́kɔǹ saraa gbanti nanti dikumbool din poonee, bí gbá kí wīī-dì. Ama an yaa sá tasa kumbool poon ní bi yaa tɔ́kɔǹ tinan gbantee, bí fíntí-dì tiŋan ní kí dū nnyim kí cántí-dì.

english_verse: Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten! Sacrifices for Sin (Leviticus
translation_verse: Ama bi yaa ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní ki dū u-fatikuu ki kɔ́ǹ dikpafindi tantiun ki ŋá dikoobil din bi máaǹ kí ŋá kí ká ikpiti pɔ̄tamee, bí taa ŋmɔ́ saraa gbanti nanti, bí cáá wà ŋŋmi.»

english_verse: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me.
translation_verse: Niinee ní usaraaŋal ń cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraa un ŋáŋkí dibɔkpilee, saraa un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Bí lēē kpɔnɔbee kɔkɔ pu ubɔ ubɔ kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Kpɔnɔb gbantee, usaraaŋal un dū ijaam saraau waŋkuluku fatikuu ki yāaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi puee di yì.

english_verse: Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me.
translation_verse: Tinan yaa gbēē tiwan tin kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee, bí taa ŋmɔ́-tì, bí dū-tì kí wà ŋŋmi. «Unil un kamaa pée bí circiree ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ saraa nanti.

english_verse: The sacrifice to make things right is very sacred.
translation_verse: «Dibɔkpil saraau bí circir páaa ní. Bi nín máaǹ kí nīn ŋáań-u puee sèé.

english_verse: The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkulukuee, niin ní bi máaǹ kí làntì dibɔkpil saraau waŋkuluku mun, ní bí dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: Offer all of the animal's fat, including the fat on its tail and on its insides,
translation_verse: Tin bi làá lēē kí wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee di sá dijugbindi nì ŋkpam min bīī ina puee,

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee, ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebil dicilpu.

english_verse: This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi kansikinee, bin pée sá bininjabee ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ tinan gbanti, ama bí ŋmɔ́-tì mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu, kun puee tì sá circir páaa nanti ní.

english_verse: The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
translation_verse: Dibɔkpil saraau nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau sá ubaanti ní, bi-ŋátam marau mun sá ubaanti ní. Usaraaŋal un di ŋá saraayee di yì kuwaŋkuluu kun bi dūu ŋá saraayee nanti. ee. Usaraaŋal jandi

english_verse: In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal,
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa cáań kuwaŋkuluu ki ŋá saraawɔkaayee, usaraaŋal un ŋá an saraauee di yì kuwaŋkuluuee gbaŋŋu.

english_verse: All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family. Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing The Lord said:
translation_verse: Tijin saraabi bin kɔkɔ kíǹ bi dū ŋkpam ki búuń àá baa búuń ŋkpamee, Aarɔn jipɔmbi kɔkɔ di yì, bí yàkatī án nīn ŋmà.» f. Mpèé saraau

english_verse: Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing:
translation_verse: «Mpèé saraau un bi ŋáań ki tìì ti-Dindaanee ŋátam marau sɔ̀.

english_verse: If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa làá ŋá mpèé saraau kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaanee, ú dū kpɔnɔb bin bi dū ŋkpam ki búuń ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee, nì ŋkpɔnɔwaamu mun pu bi yɔ́kɔfì ŋkpam ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee, nì kalaabi bin bi dū ŋkpam ki ŋmālim̀ ki búuńee kí kūtì ijaam saraau waŋkuluku pu.

english_verse: When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day.
translation_verse: Bí ŋmɔ́ mpèé saraau un bi ŋá ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaanee nanti ŋwiin ŋun bi ŋá saraa gbantee, tí taa wúntí kutaa.

english_verse: It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day,
translation_verse: «Ama an yaa sá ipoon saraau àá nlammɔntiim saraau nantee, bi ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́-tì ŋwiin ŋun bi ŋá saraa gbantee nì ŋwinliliiti dal.

english_verse: but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa ŋmɔ́ mpèé saraau nanti winta dalee, ti-Dindaan kaa làá fōō un cáań saraa gbantee saraau. Udaan ŋman ŋá saraa gbanti fám dee, di sá yii tinan gbantee bíil̀. Un ŋmɔ́ tinan gbantee fōō dibɔkpil ní ki làá túń u-yìntitam tafadaaldi.

english_verse: But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Míǹ mbaantiim un di yaa gbēē tin bí tijɔkɔndinee, an dàkà yii tin kɔ̄ntí unil tijɔkɔndee àá kuwaŋkuluu kun kòóyee àá tin fù ti-pool pu bi kòóyee, ní ki yaa ŋmɔ́ mpèé saraau nantee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel nibul kansikin.» g. Samaa marau

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: to say to the people: Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
translation_verse: ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Ní taa ŋmɔ́ unaa àá upii àá uŋoobu kpam.

english_verse: If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it.
translation_verse: Ni ŋūǹ kí dū tiwaŋkuti tin kpíìyee àá tin ní an cúúyee kpam kí ŋá tiba, ama ní taa ŋmɔ́-mì.

english_verse: If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa ŋmɔ́ kuwaŋkuluu kpam min bàà sá bí dūú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel nibul kansikin.

english_verse: And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal,
translation_verse: Báà laakin kamaa ní ni yaa bàn̄ ki kóòyee, ní taa ŋmɔ́ kinɔmbiki àá kuwaŋkuluu kubɔ fatikuu.

english_verse: or you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Un yaa ŋmɔ́ fatikuee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel nibul kansikin.»

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests.
translation_verse: Niinee usaraaŋal ń fōō ŋkpamee kí cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. Ama dibindee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di yì.

english_verse: The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal.
translation_verse: Aarɔn jipɔmbi kansikin un cūnnì mpèé saraau waŋkuluku fatikuu nì ku-kpam nsaraafan puee di yì diŋaŋgiitaal gbanti.

english_verse: I have decided that the people of Israel must always give the choice ribs and the upper joint of the right hind leg to Aaron's descendants
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab saraabi bin bi ŋáań an sá mpèé saraabee poonee, m lēē dibindi din bi fīintí fīintí m-nimbiinee nì diŋaŋgiitaal ki tīī usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi. Tin Isirayeel yab máaǹ kí nīn tìì bisaraaŋaliibi kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaanee dee.»

english_verse: These are the ceremonies for sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessing or his forgiveness, as well as the ceremonies for those sacrifices that demand a payment and for the sacrifices that are offered when priests are ordained.
translation_verse: Bi nín máaǹ kí nīn ŋáań saraawɔkaa nì tijimpin saraau nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì dibɔkpil saraau nì bi yaa làá kàan̄ bisaraaŋaliibee saraau nì mpèé saraau puee dee.

english_verse: While Moses and the people of Israel were in the desert at Mount Sinai, the Lord commanded them to start offering these sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di nìn dū marab gbanti ki tīī Mooyiisi Siinaayi jool pu, kuteeun, ŋwiin ŋun u nìn bālifì Isirayeel yab yii bí cáań-u bi-saraabee.

english_verse: Moses lifted up the choice ribs of the ram to show that they were dedicated to the Lord. This was the part that the Lord had said Moses could have.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn yōoǹ upìjee bindi, ki dúkutì yilpu ní ki fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Dijandi gbanti ní bi nìn dūu tīī Mooyiisi kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn síiǹ-u mara puee.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: Send for Aaron and his sons, as well as their priestly clothes, the oil for ordination, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and a basket of bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: «Yíiń Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi, kí cáań asaraaŋabɔkuti nì ŋkpam nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam nabil nì ipijaa ili nì kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee an nīn kā kukabikun.

english_verse: Then bring the whole community of Israel together at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee á yíiń samaa kɔkɔ ń kpāfì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.»

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord, and when everyone had come together,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi ŋá ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ú ŋá puee ní samaa kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: he said, “We are here to follow the Lord's instructions.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí samaa yii: «Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan nín bí yii tí ŋá puee sɔ̀.»

english_verse: After Moses told Aaron and his sons to step forward, he told them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi cáań Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nyɔkɔpu ki yāntì bi fùl̄ nnyim kí nyā kí nīn bí circir.

english_verse: He put the priestly shirt and robe on Aaron and wrapped the sash around his waist. Then he put the sacred vest on Aaron and fastened it with the finely woven belt.
translation_verse: U nìn dū poon bɔkutil ki pēeǹ Aarɔn ní ki dū ŋŋaabu dambalau ki gbìn̄-u, ní ki dū dibɔkutifɔkɔl mun ki pēeǹ-u, ní ki dū eefoodi ki léeǹ-u, ní ki dū dambala un kā eefoodi puee ki cúú u-caŋ.

english_verse: Next, he put on Aaron the sacred breastpiece that was used in finding out what the Lord wanted his people to do.
translation_verse: U nìn dū kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee ki páaǹ-u ní ki dū Uriim nì Tumiim ki ŋá kilɔbikee poon.

english_verse: He placed the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban was the narrow strip of thin gold as a sign of his dedication to the Lord.
translation_verse: U nìn dū ŋŋaabu ki fìn̄ u-yil ní ki dū sindaariya un bi nyūntì ki nántiǹ mpumpukumee ki nákáǹ nyɔkɔpu kí dàkà yii bi dū-u ki sú disaraaŋal tundi, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Mooyiisi yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: Moses then dedicated the sacred tent and everything in it to the Lord by sprinkling them with some of the oil for ordination.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi yōoǹ ŋkpam ní ki bātì ki yāaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu nì tin kɔkɔ bí ŋu-poonee ní ki dū tiwanee kɔkɔ ki sú ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: He sprinkled the bronze altar seven times, and he sprinkled its equipment, as well as the large bronze bowl and its base.
translation_verse: U nìn dū ŋkpamee ki yāaǹ nsaraafan pu ŋfunyɔm miluli ní ki bātì ki sītì nsaraafan pu nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee nì kusampeeu nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee ki dū an wantee kɔkɔ ki sú ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: He also poured some of the oil on Aaron's head to dedicate him to the Lord.
translation_verse: U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki bātì ŋkpamee ki sītì Aarɔn yil pu ki dū-u ki sú ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Next, Moses dressed Aaron's sons in their shirts, then tied sashes around them and put special caps on them, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Mooyiisi yāntì Aarɔn jipɔmbi mun sútì ki pìl̄-u ní u dū bi-bɔkutiŋ ki pēeǹ-bi ní ki dū dambalab ki gbìn̄-bi ní ki dū iŋaabu ki fìn̄ bi-yiliŋ kii ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: Moses led out the bull that was to be sacrificed for sin, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
translation_verse: U dóòyee ní ki dātìń dinabil din bi làá dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee ki cáań, ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi dū bi-ŋalii ki páaǹ di-yil pu.

english_verse: After it was killed, Moses dipped a finger in the blood and smeared some of it on each of the four corners of the bronze altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the altar. This purified the altar and made it a fit place for offering the sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi lāntì-dì ní ki dū u-ŋambiki ki sēē fatiku ki dūu jōō nsaraafan yiŋyi pu ki māntìi tú ki ŋá-ŋu circir. U nìn dū fatiku un kíǹee ki kpáatìi pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafanee taapu. Míǹ ní u ŋá ní ki dū nsaraafan ki sú Unimbɔti, bí nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ŋu-pu.

english_verse: Moses then took the fat on the bull's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and sent them up in smoke on the altar fire.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi yōoǹ ŋkpam min kɔkɔ bīī ina puee nì mpɔɔlam nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min bīī ŋi-puee ki cáa wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu.

english_verse: Finally, he took the skin and the flesh of the bull, together with the food still in its stomach, and burned them outside the camp, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ama bi yōoǹ dinabilee gbaŋŋu nì di-nanti nì di-bintee kɔkɔ ki cáa wùn̄ ŋŋmi dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu kii ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì Mooyiisi yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: Moses led out the ram for the sacrifice to please the Lord. After Aaron and his sons had laid their hands on its head,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi tí dātì upìja un bi làá dūú ŋá saraawɔkaayee ki cáań ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi dū bi-ŋalii ki páaǹ u-yil pu.

english_verse: Moses killed the ram and splattered its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi lāntì-u ní ki dū fatiku ki yāaǹ nsaraafan kɔkɔ pu ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: Moses had the animal cut up, and he washed its insides and hind legs. Then he laid the head, the fat, and the rest of the ram on the altar and sent them up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. All this was done just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: U dū nnyim ki fíntì ina nì ayaka ní ki dū upìjee nanti tin kíǹee kɔkɔ ki kútì ki dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu ki ŋá saraawɔkaa, ní saraayee sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbil kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn kpáafì-u yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: Moses led out the ram for the ceremony of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u dātì upìjaliliiti ki cáań bí dūú ŋá saraa, bisaraaŋaliibi ń kíĺ bi-saraaŋatundi, ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi dū bi-ŋalii ki páaǹ upìjee yil pu.

english_verse: and it was killed. Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi lāntì-u ní ki dū fatiku ki jōō Aarɔn tafalam ŋgiil yal pu nì u-ŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu nì u-taŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu.

english_verse: Moses did the same thing for Aaron's sons, before splattering the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Mooyiisi yāntì Aarɔn jipɔmbi sútì ki pìl̄-u ní u dū fatiku ki jōō bi-tafalam ŋgiil yaŋ pu nì bi-ŋambijaliŋ ŋgiil yaŋ pu nì bi-taŋambijaliŋ ŋgiil yaŋ pu ní ki dū fatiku un kíǹee ki kpáatìi pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi lēē ŋkpam nì dijugbindi nì ŋkpam min bīī ina puee nì mpɔɔlam nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min bīī ŋi-puee nì diŋaŋgiitaal.

english_verse: Moses placed the bread on top of the meat and gave it all to Aaron and his sons, who lifted it up to show that it was dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi dūu ŋúbiǹ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ní bi dúkutì yilpu ki fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: After this, Moses placed it on the fires of the altar and sent it up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. This was part of the ordination ceremony.
translation_verse: Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní Mooyiisi fātìi fōō bi-ŋaan ki dūu páaǹ saraawɔkaa un pá nsaraafan puee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Míǹ ní bi nìn ŋá saraabi ní bisaraaŋaliibi kíĺ bi-tundi, ní saraayee sɔnsɔfiŋu nìn sɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbil.

english_verse: Finally, Moses sprinkled the priestly clothes of Aaron and his sons with some of the oil for ordination and with some of the blood from the altar. So Aaron and his sons, together with their priestly clothes, were dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi yōoǹ ŋkpam nì fatiku un nìn bí nsaraafan puee ki dūu yāaǹ Aarɔn nì u-wampeeŋkaati pu nì u-jipɔmbi mun nì bi-wampeeŋkaati pu. Míǹ ní u ŋá ki dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nì bi-wampeeŋkaati kɔkɔ ki sú ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Moses said to Aaron and his sons: The Lord told me that you must boil this meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it there with the bread.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi yii: «Tɔ́kɔḿmaan tinan dikpafindi tantiu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. Ni yaa tɔ́kɔǹ-tèe, ní ŋmɔ́-tì niin nì kpɔnɔb bin kā kikabikin bi cáań ki ŋá saraayee kii m nín nìn tīī-si mara ki lī yii: <Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di làá ŋmɔ́-tèe.>

english_verse: and stay near the entrance to the sacred tent until the ordination ceremony ends seven days from now.
translation_verse: Naa máaǹ kí yīkì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli dal. Naa máaǹ kí nyā áli iwiin iluli in bi síiǹ kí dūú ŋá saraabi ní kíĺ disaraaŋal tundee ń kúntí.

english_verse: We have obeyed the Lord in everything that has been done today, so that your sins may be forgiven.
translation_verse: Kii ti nín ŋá pu díǹ nee, ti-Dindaan u-ba di síiǹ mara yii tí ŋá míǹ ní ní ká ni-kpitii pɔ̄tam.

english_verse: The Lord has told me that you must stay near the entrance to the tent for seven days and nights, or else you will die.
translation_verse: Ni máaǹ kí nīn bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli. Mimmee ni ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ ti-Dindaan tundi kí taa kpú. Ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì-mi yii ḿ ŋá puee dee.»

english_verse: Aaron and his sons obeyed everything that the Lord had told Moses they must do.
translation_verse: Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ŋá tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan dī Mooyiisi pu ki síiǹ-bi yii bí ŋée deedee.

english_verse: Eight days later Moses called together Aaron, his sons, and Israel's leaders.
translation_verse: Ŋwinniniiti dalee ní Mooyiisi yíiń Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nì Isirayeel yab kpilib.

english_verse: Then he said to Aaron: Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
translation_verse: U nìn bí Aarɔn yii: «Nyàab̀ dinabil kí dūú ŋá a-kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau nì upìja kí dūú ŋá a-saraawɔkaau. Tiwaŋkutee liitil laaba ń taa nīn wɔ̀b̄ ní á cáań-tì ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee á tùkù Isirayeel yab bí cáań uŋɔja kí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì dinabil din cáá dibindi dibee nì dipibil din cáá dibindi dibee ŋi-laaba ń taa nīn wɔ̀b̄ bí dūú ŋá saraawɔkaa.

english_verse: Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
translation_verse: Bí cáań unaja nì upìja kí ŋá mpèé saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaan, ní kí dū ŋyim min bi dū ŋkpam ki búuńee kí ŋá tijimpin saraau. Kun puee díǹ nee, ti-Dindaan làá nyāntí u-ba kí dàkà-ni.»

english_verse: After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord,
translation_verse: Ní bi cáań tin kɔkɔ Mooyiisi bālifèe circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu, ní samaa kɔkɔ sútìń ki kíǹ ki sí ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Moses said: The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi lī yii: «M làá dàkà-ni tin ti-Dindaan kpáafì-ni ní ŋée. Ni yaa lafun ŋá míǹ, u làá lēē u-nyooti kí dàkà-ni.»

english_verse: Aaron, step up to the altar and offer the sacrifice to please the Lord, then offer the sacrifices for the forgiveness of your sins and for the sins of the people, just as the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn yii: «Sútí kí pìl̄ nsaraafan kí ŋá a-kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau nì a-saraawɔkaau, kí pítí a-kpitii nì samaa kpitii. Míǹ boonee á ŋá saraabi bin ní samaa cáańee kí pítí bi-kpitii, kii ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ mara puee.»

english_verse: Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins.
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn sútì ki pìl̄ nsaraafan ní ki lāntì úǹ u-ba kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau nabil.

english_verse: His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot.
translation_verse: Ní u-jipɔmbi cáań-u fatiku ní u dū u-ŋambiki ki sēē fatikuee ki dūu jōō nsaraafan kpiŋŋi pu ní ki kpáatì un kíǹee ki pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan taapu.

english_verse: But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: U dū ŋkpam nì aceebil nì mpɔɔlamee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn kpáafì Mooyiisi puee.

english_verse: Then Aaron burned the skin and the flesh outside the camp.
translation_verse: Ama ní ki yōoǹ tinan nì ŋgbanee ki nyántì dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi.

english_verse: After Aaron had killed the ram that was sacrificed to please the Lord, Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against all four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Aarɔn lāntì upìja un bi cáań kí ŋá saraawɔkaayee, ní u-jipɔmbi cáań-u fatiku ní u dūu yāaǹ nsaraafan pu ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: They brought him each piece of the animal, including the head, and he burned them all on the altar.
translation_verse: Bi càkā upìjee nanti ní ki dū diyil ki kútì ki tīī-u ní u dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu.

english_verse: He washed the insides and the hind legs and also sent them up in smoke.
translation_verse: U fíntì ina nì ayaka ki dūu páaǹ saraawɔkaa un pá nsaraafan puee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Aarɔn cáań samaa kɔkɔ saraabi: u yōoǹ samaa kɔkɔ kpitii pɔ̄tam ŋɔjau ki lāntì ki ŋá saraa kii u nín bàà ŋá dinabil puee.

english_verse: And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way.
translation_verse: Bi cáań saraawɔkaa waŋkutee nyɔkɔpu ki ŋá saraa kii bi nín síiǹ mara bí nīn ŋáań-u puee.

english_verse: He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
translation_verse: Bi yōoǹ tijimpin saraau ki yáfì diŋaŋkul ki dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu, ki kpáaǹ saraawɔkaa un bi ŋáań kutaafaau kamaayee.

english_verse: Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Boonee ní u lāntì unaja nì upìja un samaa kɔkɔ cáań kí ŋá mpèé saraauee, ní u-jipɔmbi cáań-u fatiku ní u dūu yāaǹ nsaraafan pu ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver
translation_verse: Bi gíti tí cáań-u unajee nì upìjee kpam, an dàkà yii ajugbin nì ŋkpam min pá ina puee nì aceebil nì mpɔɔlam,

english_verse: Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
translation_verse: Aarɔn yōoǹ tiwaŋkuti biŋŋi nì diŋaŋgiitaal yilpu ní ki fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin kii Mooyiisi nín nìn pée síiǹ-u mara puee.

english_verse: Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Aarɔn ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì saraawɔkaa nì mpèé saraau ki dóòyee ní u yōoǹ u-ŋalii ki túĺ samaa ki mēē ki bīiǹ bi-pu ní ki kpákatì nsaraafan pu.

english_verse: He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nín kóò dikpafindi tantiun. Bi dāa fātìi nyánnée ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ samaa kɔkɔ pu. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan nyántì u-nyooti ki dàkā samaa kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní ŋŋmi ŋubɔ nyánní ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki dɔ́miń ki wùn̄ saraawɔkaa nì ŋkpam min pá nsaraafan puee. Samaa kɔkɔ nín ká mimmee ní bi fáá iwiliili nì dipɔɔpindi, ní ki tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil.

english_verse: Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to.
translation_verse: Aarɔn jipɔmbi Nadaab nì Abiyuu yōoǹ bi-sambiyaamu mun poon bi tùutī talaaluee ki pātì ŋŋmi ki dū talaalu ki páká. Bi nìn cáań ŋŋmi ŋun an kaa pú nsan bí cáań ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, kun puee an kaa nìn nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ-bi puee.

english_verse: Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì ŋŋmi ŋubɔ dɔ́miń ki wùn̄-bi ní bi kpíì dibɔbil pu niin ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said: “I demand respect from my priests, and I will be praised by everyone!” Aaron was speechless.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn yii: «An ní ti-Dindaan nìn kpáafì-ni ki lī yii: <Bin sútiń ki pìl̀-mee ní m là bí dàkà m nín bí circir puee, ní ki là bí dàkà m-nyooti samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin.>» Ní Aarɔn wunti kpíì.

english_verse: Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.”
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi yíiń Aarɔn baawaai Usiyeel jipɔmbi Miisayeel nì Eeliisafan ki bí-bi yii: «Dāam̄maan kí yòon̄ ni-nabiyaamu circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu kí cáá nyāntí dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu.»

english_verse: So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
translation_verse: Ní bi dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ bi nì bi-bɔkutiŋ ki nyántì dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu kii Mooyiisi nín bí yii bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar yii: «Ní taa yàntī ni-yikpiti ń nīn bí fìkil fikil kí taa cátí ni-bɔkutiŋ mun kí dàkà yii ni bí kunimbaaun. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni làá kpú ní kí yàntī ti-Dindaan ń gíí samaa kɔkɔ pu diŋuul. Ní yàntī ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ń kàl̄ bin ti-Dindaan dū ŋŋmi ki kūūyee kpool.

english_verse: But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die. Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
translation_verse: Nimbee, ní taa nyā Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu, án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa kpúee, di sá yii bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì ni-yiliŋ pu ki dū-ni ki sú ti-Dindaan ní.» Ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ŋá ki nóó nì Mooyiisi nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. Idafi in pɔ̄ɔ̄yee marab

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Aarɔn yii:

english_verse: When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change.
translation_verse: «Sii nì a-jipɔmbi, ni yaa kóò circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poonee, ní taa nyɔ̀ ndamam àá ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee miba, án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa kpúee. Án nīn sá dibɔkpaal ki tīī ni nì ni-biyaamu kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean.
translation_verse: Mimmee ni làá ŋmā kí gàntī tin bí circiree nì tin kaa bée, nì tin bi kòóyee nì tin baa kòóyee.

english_verse: You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
translation_verse: Ni làá gíti ŋmā kí dàkà Isirayeel yab abɔkpaa ŋin ti-Dindaan dī Mooyiisi pu ki tīī-bee.» Saraabi nanti marab

english_verse: Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn nì Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar, u-jipɔmbi bili bin kíǹee yii: «Bi nín lēē tijimpin saraau poon dijandi ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki tīī ti-Dindaanee, dijandi din kíǹee, ní dūú ŋá tijin kí jī nsaraafan caŋin ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ ń nīn kpá poon, di sá yii an sá circir páaa jinti ní.

english_verse: The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place.
translation_verse: Mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu ní ní jī tijin gbanti, di sá yii saraabi bin bi cāabìń ki tìì ti-Dindaanee, dijandi din sá ki tīī sii nì a-jipɔmbee dee. Ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ-mi puee dee.

english_verse: But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Bi yaa lēē ditaal nì dibindi din bi làá fíiǹ fíiǹee, bí lēē ŋkpam min bi làá cáá wà ŋŋmee, ní kí yòon̄ yilpu kí fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Míǹ boonee sii nì a-jipɔmbi di yì, di sá yii dijandi din sá ki tīī-ni kí nīn cá jaanjaanee dee, kii ti-Dindaan nín tīī mara puee.»

english_verse: When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said,
translation_verse: Boonee Mooyiisi dāa béè yii uŋɔja un bi dūu ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee, bi dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Niinee ní Mooyiisi gíí Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar, Aarɔn jipɔmbi bin kíǹee pu diŋuul, ní ki bālifì-bi yii:

english_verse: “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt.
translation_verse: «Ba pu ní naa ŋmɔ́ ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nanti mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu ní, kun puee tinan gbanti bí circir páaa ní? Ti-Dindaan di dū-tì ki tīī-ni yii ní fōō samaa kɔkɔ kpitii kí túń kí ŋmā kí fíntí bi-kpitii ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
translation_verse: Baa dū uŋoobu gbanti fatikuu ki kɔ́ǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon, an puee an bàà sá ní ŋmɔ́ u-nanti ní, kii m nín síiǹ-ni mara puee.»

english_verse: Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn kíí Mooyiisi yii: «Díǹ di sá ŋwimpeepeekaa ŋun bi ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì saraawɔkaayee, ní sii a-ba nyí tin jítì m-puee. Mimmee an kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii ḿ bàà ŋmɔ́ ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nanti díǹ wiiŋŋuaaa?»

english_verse: Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi gbìl̄ an nyɔɔbuŋŋee ní ki tīī-u imɔ̀ń.

english_verse: any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud.
translation_verse: Ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ tiwaŋkuti tin tafuŋfukuti látì ní tì kpìkitī ki fàtīi ŋmóòyee.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: You may eat
translation_verse: bí tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Tiwaŋkuti tin kɔkɔ còom̄ kitiŋ puee poonee, tin ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ee sɔ̀.

english_verse: The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
translation_verse: Ama kunaakibuluu kun kíǹ ki cáá ifeen nì iyakal inaayee, ni kòó.» Tin kɔ̄ntí unil tijɔkɔndee

english_verse: Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Un mun yaa túǹ ti-waŋkpilee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. Udaan ń fíntí tiwan tin u pēēyee, di sá yii ni kòó tiwaŋkuti gbanti.

english_verse: Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean.
translation_verse: nì kijipatii nì jilkantoolii nì kaŋkampu nì ulɔ nì kunaatoou.

english_verse: Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Béémaan yii ni kòó tiwaŋkuti gbanti. Ubɔ yaa gbēē ti-waŋkpilee, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou.

english_verse: If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Tì yaa kpíì ní ki lítì tiba puee, an yaa sá ndɔ sambikaaa, tiwampeeŋkaalaaa, ŋgbanaaa, ditɔkɔlaaa, tin kamaa ní bi pée cáa tūǹ ditundee, tiwan gbanti kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Bí dū nnyim ki fíntí-tì ní tí sīĺ kí cáá sāā kujoou ní kí nyā tijɔkɔndin.

english_verse: If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean.
translation_verse: Tiwaŋkuti gbanti kubɔ yaa kpíì ki jéetì ditansambilin àá diboolinee, tin kā poonee kɔkɔ kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, bi máaǹ kí gbá kí wīī ditansambil àá dibool gbanti.

english_verse: If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed.
translation_verse: Tiwan tin kamaa ní tiwaŋkutee yaa kpíì ki gbēēyee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. An yaa sá dibubul àá ŋfan puee, see bí gbá kí wīī-ŋu, di sá yii ŋu mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi dee.

english_verse: A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, kuwaŋkuluu yaa jéetì nnyimbul àá dinyimbɔbil din poon ní nnyim dɔ̀ee ki kpíìyee, nnyim gbanti kaa kóò tijɔkɔndi. Ama un di yaa gbēē kuwaŋkuluu gbanti wuntee di kóò tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean.
translation_verse: Diwaŋkpil gbanti dijandi diba yaa lítì ŋwambool puee, ŋwambool gbanti kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
translation_verse: Ama bi yaa wōoǹ ŋwambool ní diwaŋkpilee yaa gbēēyee, ŋwambool gbanti kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening.
translation_verse: «Tiwaŋkuti tin ni jīǹee kubɔ yaa kpíì ní ubɔ gbēē-kuee, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou.

english_verse: If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Un di yaa ŋmɔ́ tinan gbantee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. Un mun di yaa yōoǹ diwaŋkpilee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou.

english_verse: Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground.
translation_verse: Ni kòó tin fù ti-pooŋi puee nì tin còom̄ ataa anaa àá ataa kupaau puee. Ní taa pée ŋmɔ́-tì.

english_verse: If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are.
translation_verse: Ní taa dū tiwaŋkuti gbanti tiba kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi. Taa pée yàntīmaan tí kɔ́ǹ-ni tijɔkɔndi án nín làá ŋá pu ní ti-puee, ní kpántí bijɔkɔndambee.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures.
translation_verse: Di sá yii man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. Nín̄ bímaan circir, kun puee man bí circir ní. Taa yàntīmaan tiwan tin fòotī ki kpátìi gbí kitiŋ pu nee kansikin kubɔ ń kɔ́ǹ-ni tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
translation_verse: Man di sá ni-Dindaan un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin kí nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiuee. Míǹ puee nín̄ bímaan circir, kun puee man m-ba bí circir ní.»

english_verse: I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
translation_verse: Marab gbanti di nìn yàntī bi gàntī tiwaŋkuti tin bi kòóyee nì tin baa kòóyee, nì tiwaŋkuti tin bi máaǹ kí jēe nì tin baa máaǹ kí jēe.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period.
translation_verse: «Tùkù Isirayeel yab yii unimpu yaa cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabikee, mara poonee, u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli dal kii u nín yaa ká u-ba, u bí tijɔkɔndin puee.

english_verse: Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day,
translation_verse: Ŋwinniniiti dalee, bí gíí kibikee dikpancandi.

english_verse: Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another
translation_verse: «An yaa sá kibinimpubiki ní u màl̄ee, mara poonee, u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā nnyɔmu muli kii u nín yaa ká u-ba, u bí tijɔkɔndin puee. Míǹ boonee ní ú gíti kàl̄ iwiin imuŋku ita nì iluu kí nyā fatiku un nyáń-uee jɔkɔntin.

english_verse: When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: «An yaa sá kibininjabiki àá kibinimpubiki ní u màl̄ ní ki kāl̀ iwiin in mara bālifèe ki tin sāāyee, ú cùú ká usaraaŋal circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. Ú cáań dibindi diba pibil kí ŋá saraawɔkaa nì dinanjil àá dibeenanjil kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau.

english_verse: After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl.
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋal ń fōō tiwaŋkutee kí cáá ŋá saraa ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí fíntí unimpuee kpitii ú nyā fatiku un nyáń-uee jɔkɔntin.» Mara un bi nìn síiǹ unimpu yaa màl̄ kibininjabiki àá kibinimpubikee dee.

english_verse: If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: «Unimpu ŋaan yaa kaa nyìm̀ ú dā dipibilee, u ŋūǹ kí cáań ananjil ali àá abeenanjil ali ní kí dū diba kí ŋá saraawɔkaa ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau, ní usaraaŋal ń dūú ŋá saraa kí fíntí u-kpitii ní ú nyā fatiku un nyáń-uee jɔkɔntin.»

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii:

english_verse: If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ wunti pu laaba yaa díkí àá tikalindi nyáń u-wunti pu laaba àá u-wunti pu laaba líkitì ki jìl̀ ní ki dāa dūu ŋá mbuun kii dinyaŋgbandee, bí cáá udaan kí dàkà usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn àá u-jipɔmbi kansikin ubɔ.

english_verse: If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń kpèè mbuun ŋun bí udaan wunti puee. Tikuti tin bí mbuunee poonee yaa pīiǹ ní mbuun yaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poonee, mimmee an sá dinyaŋgbandi buuŋŋu. Usaraaŋal nín kpēē-u ki ká mimmee ní ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
translation_verse: Ama u-wunti pu laakin líkitèe yaa pīiǹ ní kaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon, ní tikuti mun kaa píil̀ee, usaraaŋal ń dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii ú nīn bí niin u-baba iwiin iluli.

english_verse: If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days.
translation_verse: Ŋwinluluúti dalee ní usaraaŋal ń tí kpèè-u. U yaa ká yii mbuunee kaa kpántì, kaa wāaǹ muee ní ú fàtīí tí dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii ú nīn bí niin u-baba iwiin iluli.

english_verse: Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
translation_verse: Ŋwinluluúti dalee ní usaraaŋal ń gíti tí pìitī-u nliliitiim kí kpèè-u. Mbuun yaa píil̀ fàaa kaa wāaǹee, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii unilee kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, an pée sá tikalindi ní. Udaan ń fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati kí ŋāŋkì.

english_verse: However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest.
translation_verse: Ama usaraaŋal nín ká yii waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee ní boonee tikalindee yaa lālim̀ee, ú fàtīí gítí kí dū u-ba kí dàkà usaraaŋal ú kpèè-u.

english_verse: If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal yaa dáań ki ká yii tikalindi lālim̀ ki gbí tiwun kɔkɔ puee ní ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, an sá dinyaŋgbandi.

english_verse: Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest.
translation_verse: «Dinyaŋgbandi weeŋyi iba yaa tɔ́ ubɔee, bí cáań-u usaraaŋal cee.

english_verse: If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white,
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń kpèè-u. An yaa sá disiŋkpeepindi di bí udaan wunti pu ní disiŋkpeelee poon tikuti bí ki pīiǹ ní mbuun nútìńee,

english_verse: But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.”
translation_verse: usaraaŋal ń mɔ̀tīí kpèè tiŋan. U yaa ká yii an píń u-wunti kɔkɔ puee, ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Di sá an píń u-wunti kɔkɔ pu ki pīiǹ, waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal yaa pée ká udaan wunti léetèe, ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. U-wunti nín léetèe dàkà yii an sá dinyaŋgbandi weeŋŋu.

english_verse: However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń gíti kpèè-u. U mun yaa ká yii u-wunti laakin léetèe píil̀ee, ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii ŋweenee kaa sá tijɔkɔndi weeŋŋu, ní un pu ŋu kēe mun kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest.
translation_verse: ama ní laakin dinalee nìn tɔ́ee, ndulim miba nyáń àá niin léetì ki pīiǹ fàaayee, udaan ń cáá u-ba kí dàkà usaraaŋal.

english_verse: If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń kpèè-u. Laakin ŋá ndulim àá an léetèe yaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon ní tikuti tin bí ŋu-poonee pīiǹee, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Dinyaŋgbandi buuŋŋu di nyáń dinalee buŋweekun.

english_verse: But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
translation_verse: Ama usaraaŋal yaa dáań ki ká yii tikuti tin bí mbuunee poon kaa pīiǹ ní mbuunee kaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon, ní kaa léetèe, ú dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii u-baba iwiin iluli.

english_verse: If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boon mbuunee yaa nyātèe, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi: dinyaŋgbandi buuŋŋu dee.

english_verse: But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
translation_verse: Ama mbuunee yaa kaa kpántì kaa wāaǹ muee, mimmee an sá dinalee buŋweeku. Usaraaŋal ń lì báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white,
translation_verse: «Ŋŋmi yaa nìn wùn̄ ubɔ ní an ŋá ndulim kubuŋweeu poon ki pīiǹ fàaa àá ki máǹ wèeeeyee,

english_verse: a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.”
translation_verse: usaraaŋal ń kpèè-u. Tikuti tin bí ndulim poonee yaa pīiǹ ní mbuun yaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poonee, an sá dinyaŋgbandi di nyáń kubuŋweeuee poon. Usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.
