translation_verse: «A-nabiki yaa kpántì usoodaan kaa ti ŋūǹ kí kpèè u-bee, á tūtuǹ-u, kí tīī-u ú jī kí ŋmátí. An yaa sá unicaaneeee, unikɔkaayeeee, á ŋá míǹ kí tīī-u.

english_verse: Don't take advantage of them by charging any kind of interest or selling them food for profit. Instead, honor me by letting them stay where they now live.
translation_verse: Á taa pìnnì a-nabiki animbil kí yàntī ú dāá téeǹ-si kí páań, kí taa tí pìnnì-u tijin ú dāá téeǹ-si kí páań.

english_verse: Remember—I am the Lord your God! I rescued you from Egypt and gave you the land of Canaan, so that I would be your God.
translation_verse: Man di sá ni-Dindaan, ni-Nimbɔtiu un di nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dū Kanaan tiŋki ki tīī-ni, án nín làá ŋá pu ḿ nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiuee.» Bi ŋūǹ kí fàtīí dā un dū u-ba ki nyáfèe

english_verse: Suppose some of your people become so poor that they have to sell themselves and become your slaves.
translation_verse: «A-nabiki yaa kpántì usoodaan ní ki dū u-ba ki nyáfiǹ-see, á taa tīī-u ditundi din sá uyumbu tundee.

english_verse: Then you must treat them as servants, rather than as slaves. And in the Year of Celebration they are to be set free,
translation_verse: Nín̄ ŋúb́-u kii bi nín ŋúb̀ upaadaan àá unikɔkaa puee. Ú nīn bí a-cee ki tūǹ ditundi kí cáá sāā dibatɔl bindi.

english_verse: so they and their children may return home to their families and property.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, u tɔ́ u-ba ki kpáaǹ u-biyaamu kí fàtīí gítí u-dicaŋkun, u-baabi timmun.

english_verse: I brought them out of Egypt to be my servants, not to be sold as slaves.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Isirayeel yab bin m nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee sá man tɔntɔnliibi ní. Baa ti máaǹ kí dū-bi kí nyāfì kii bi nín nyáfí iyumbu puee.

english_verse: So obey me, and don't be cruel to the poor.
translation_verse: Ní fàŋkìmaan man ni-Nimbɔtiu kí taa wɔ́b́-bi.

english_verse: or from the foreigners who live in your own country, and make them your property.
translation_verse: Ni tí ŋūǹ kí dā binicambi bin kóò ni-kansikinee nì bi-dicaŋŋi poon mbiyaamu mun bi màl̄ ni-tiŋkinee bí kpántí ni-yumbui ní nīn yì.

english_verse: You can own them, and even leave them to your children when you die, but do not make slaves of your own people or be cruel to them.
translation_verse: Ni-kpátam boonee, bí kpántí ni-biyaamu fakal bí nīn yì. Bimbee, ni ŋūǹ kí yàntī bí nīn sá iyumbu kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ama ni-kansikin ubɔ ń taa wɔ́b́ u-nabiki kin sá Isirayeel yab kansikinee ubɔ.

english_verse: Even if some of you Israelites become so much in debt that you must sell yourselves to foreigners in your country,
translation_verse: «Unicaan àá binikɔkaabi bin kóò ni-puee ubɔ yaa kpántì ugaaja ní disool cúú ni-nabiki kiba ní udaan dū u-ba ki nyáfiǹ ugaajee àá u-dicaŋkun yab ubɔee,

english_verse: you still have the right to be set free by a relative, such as a brother
translation_verse: an pú nsan bí fàtīí dā-u kí líí. U-nabiki kiba ń fàtīí dā-u kí líí.

english_verse: The longer the time until then, the more you will have to pay.
translation_verse: Abin ŋin kíǹ dibatɔl bindi ń nín bàńee yaa kaa ti náaǹee, ú cɔ́tí kí kpèè abin gbanti nimbiliŋ kí téeǹ-u.

english_verse: And even while you are the slaves of foreigners in your own country, your people must make sure that you are not mistreated.
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun ní u dáá bí u-kpiliu ceeyee, u ŋman sá kii upaadaanee ní, kí nīn fòol̄ dibindi kamaa u-paati. Ní taa yàntī u-kpiliu ń nīn wɔ́b̀-u ni kā ki kpèé.

english_verse: If you cannot gain your freedom in any of these ways, both you and your children will still be set free in the Year of Celebration.
translation_verse: U-nabiki yaa kaa ŋúń ki dá-u ki líì ní úǹ u-ba kaa ŋúń ki dá u-ba ki líì ní dibatɔl bindi yaa dūu bāańee, u nì u-dicaŋku kɔkɔ fōō bi-ba.» Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu

english_verse: People of Israel, I am the Lord your God, and I brought you out of Egypt to be my own servants.
translation_verse: «Tiŋman, Isirayeel yab sá man tɔntɔnliibi ní. Bi lafun sá man tɔntɔnliibi, di sá yii man di nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin. Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Respect the Sabbath and honor the place where I am worshiped, because I am the Lord.
translation_verse: «Nín̄ ŋúb́maan ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun m tīī-nee kí nīn tɔ́ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tiŋan. Man di sá ni-Dindaan.» Unimbɔti biindi

english_verse: and I will send rain to make your crops grow and your trees produce fruit.
translation_verse: m làá yàntī utaa ń nì ŋyunti ŋun an máaǹee, kitiŋ ń lòoǹ tikpaajin mmɔntiimin ní isufi mun ń lòoǹ abil tiŋan.

english_verse: I will bless your country with peace, and you will rest without fear. I will wipe out the dangerous animals and protect you from enemy attacks.
translation_verse: M làá dāá yàntī ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí ni-tiŋkin. Ni yaa láa dɔ̄ ki gèeǹee, naa dāa fàŋkí tiba. M làá dāá jà ipeecuncuti kɔkɔ ni-tiŋkin. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti dòoń kí jáǹ-ni.

english_verse: You will chase and destroy your enemies,
translation_verse: Ni làá dāá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ ni-nannanliibi kí dāá jà-bi.

english_verse: I will treat you with such kindness that your nation will grow strong, and I will also keep my promises to you.
translation_verse: M làá dāá ŋá-ni tiŋan ní kí yàntī ní bùtī kí wíiǹ tikpil. M làá dāá nīn ŋúb́ m-poondi din m pōoǹ-nee.

english_verse: I will live among you and never again look on you with disgust.
translation_verse: M làá dāá nīn kóò ni-kansikin. M kpá kí fàtī m-boon kí tīī-ni.

english_verse: I will walk with you—I will be your God, and you will be my people.
translation_verse: M làá dāá nīn còom̄ ni-kansikin. M làá nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu, ní nimbi ń nīn sá m-nibul.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and I rescued you from Egypt, so that you would never again be slaves. I have set you free; now walk with your heads held high. Punishment for Disobeying the Lord The Lord said:
translation_verse: Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin, ní taa ti nín̄ sá Eejipiti yab yumbuyee. Man di léetì ni-neen kpancikil, ní ki yāntì ni kíǹ ki còom̄ ni-yil gáań.» Unimbɔti tafadaaldi

english_verse: I will punish you terribly, and you will be ruined. You will be struck with incurable diseases and with fever that leads to blindness and depression. Your enemies will eat the crops you plant,
translation_verse: m nín làá dāá ŋá ni-puee sèé: «M làá dāá kɔ́ǹ-ni dinyoondin, kí yàntī didúntil weeŋyi nì nnaanyeem ń cúú-ni ní kí yàntī iween gbanti ń ŋmɔ́ kí bīil̀ ni-nimbiliŋ kí bàtī ni-wiiŋyi pu. Ni làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí bɔ̄l̀ ni-sati fám, kun puee ni-nannanliibi di dāa yì ni-kpaajinti gbanti kí jī.

english_verse: and I will turn from you and let you be destroyed by your attackers. You will even run at the very rumor of attack.
translation_verse: M làá dāá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-ni, ní ni-nannanliibi ń pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-ni. Bin bin ná-nee di làá dāá jī ni-pu dibeel kí nīn kpòotī-ni. Ubɔ kaa dāa bíi jì-ni ní ní kíĺ ki bíi sáń.

english_verse: Then, if you still refuse to obey me, I will punish you seven times for each of your sins,
translation_verse: «Míǹ gbanti kɔkɔ boonee, ni yaa kaa gbíntìi tɔ́-mee, ní ḿ dāá kūtì ni-kpitii tafadaaldi din poon ni bée miluli pu.

english_verse: until your pride is completely crushed. I will hold back the rain, so the sky above you will be like iron, and the ground beneath your feet will be like copper.
translation_verse: M làá dāá nàan̄ kun tìì-ni mpɔn ni yòontí ni-ba yilpuee, kí dāá yàntī kutaa kun dàn̄ ni-pu nee ń pɔ̄ɔkì kii tikútee. M làá dāá yàntī utaa ń taa ti nì ni-timmu pu ní mú pɔ̄ɔkì kaŋkaŋ kii tikúbɔnee.

english_verse: All of your hard work will be for nothing—and there will be no harvest of grain or fruit.
translation_verse: Ní ní kpɔ̀ kí kpɔ̀ kí gīī púb, ama ni-timmu kaa làá lòoǹ tikpaajin ní isufi mun kaa làá lòoǹ abil.

english_verse: If you keep rebelling against me, I'll punish you seven times worse, just as your sins deserve!
translation_verse: «Ni yaa gbíntìi bíi jáà nì mi kaa là kí nīn tɔ́-mee, m làá dāá mɔ̀tīí kūtì ni-kpitii tafadaaldi miluli pu.

english_verse: I'll send wild animals to attack you, and they will gobble up your children and livestock. So few of you will be left that your roads will be deserted.
translation_verse: M làá dāá dū ipeecuncuti kí tɔ̄ ni-pu í kpɔ̀ ni-biyaamu, kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí ni-waŋkuti kɔkɔ, ní kí kpɔ̀ kí bàtī ni-pu ní kíń fiii. Áli gba ni-saŋyi kaa dāa gíti kāntí bin làá nīn còom̄ i-puee.

english_verse: I'll remain your enemy and punish you even worse.
translation_verse: ma mun làá dāá jáǹ-ni, ní kí mɔ̀tīí kūtì ni-kpitii tafadaaldi miluli pu.

english_verse: War will break out because you broke our agreement, and if you escape to your walled cities, I'll punish you with horrible diseases, and you will be captured by your enemies.
translation_verse: M làá dāá cáań kujaau ni-tiŋki pu kí tɔ̀ ipɔntoon ni nín dū m-poondi ki fée pu. Báà ni yaa láa sáǹ ki bál̀ ni-timmu poonaaa, m làá dāá yàntī bìlbil kúm ń jēetí ni-pu, ní ḿ dū-ni kí líiǹ ni-nannanliibi.

english_verse: You will have such a shortage of bread, that ten women will be able to bake their bread in the same oven. Each of you will get only a few crumbs, and you will go hungry.
translation_verse: M làá dāá yàntī tijin ń lóó-ni. Binimpoobi saalaa dāa ŋūǹ kí púĺ ni-kpɔnɔb dibububaantiil poon ní bí dāá cáań-ni kpɔnɔb fiiiyee ní ŋmɔ́ kaa làá díkí.

english_verse: I'll really get furious and punish you terribly for your sins!
translation_verse: ma mun làá dāá jáǹ-ni nì m-ŋuul poon. Man m-ba di làá dāá dáaĺ ni-tafal ni-kpitii pu ŋfunyɔm miluli.

english_verse: In fact, you will be so desperate for food that you will eat your own children.
translation_verse: Ni làá dāá ŋmɔ́ ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib nanti.

english_verse: I'll destroy your shrines and tear down your incense altars, leaving your dead bodies piled on top of your idols. And you will be disgusting to me.
translation_verse: M làá dāá gbá kí kpēelikì ni-waadiiŋŋi ŋin bí ŋgbantamu puee, nì ni-saraafaŋyi in pu ni tùutī talaalubee, kí kpɔ̀-ni kí páań awaa ŋin m kpéelikì ki bíl̀ee pu, ní kí dū-ni kí fá.

english_verse: I'll wipe out your towns and your places of worship and will no longer be pleased with the smell of your sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ni-timmu làá dāá kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma ní. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti gbōontí ni-saraafaŋyi laŋki, ní ḿ dāá fàtī m-boon kí tīī ni-saraabi.

english_verse: Your land will become so desolate that even your enemies who settle there will be shocked when they see it.
translation_verse: Man m-ba di làá dāá nàan̄ ni-tiŋki ní án dāá ŋá ni-nannanliibi bin làá dāá fōō-kì kí nīn kíǹ ki kóòyee bitii.

english_verse: After I destroy your towns and ruin your land with war, I'll scatter you among the nations.
translation_verse: M làá dāá cáań kujaau kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní ní yàl̄ kí kɔ́ ntincamun. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti kóò ni-tiŋkin ní ni-timmu ń dāá kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma.

english_verse: While you are prisoners in foreign lands, your own land will enjoy years of rest and refreshment, as it should have done each seventh year when you lived there.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔ poonee ní ni-tiŋki ń dāá dòon̄ kí ŋùŋfì kí téeǹ ni nín nìn dū iwiŋŋuŋfikaa in ki túń ki-pu ditundi ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn kóò niinee.

english_verse: In the land of your enemies, you will tremble at the rustle of a leaf, as though it were a sword. And you will become so weak that you will stumble and fall over each other, even when no one is chasing you.
translation_verse: Bi dāa sáń ki gbéetí ki lítí tɔb pu kii bi ŋúb́ ntàataajimu ní ki jì-bee, ama báà ubɔ kaa pá bi-boon ki jì-bi. Baa dāa ŋūǹ kí sīĺ bi-nannanliibi nimbiin kí jáǹ-bi.

english_verse: Many of you will die in foreign lands,
translation_verse: Ntincamun ní ni làá dāá kpú kí céetí, ní bí dāá síb́-ni ni-nannanliibi timmu gbanti poon.

english_verse: and others of you will waste away in sorrow as the result of your sins and the sins of your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ni-kansikin bin yaa láa kíǹ kaa kpíì ki bíń ni-nannanliibi timmunee làá dāá kpúń niin ní. Bi làá dāá kpú bíǹ bi-ba nì bi-baabi kpitii pu ní.» Unimbɔti làá dāá téetí u-poondi pu

english_verse: Then suppose you realize that I turned against you and brought you to the land of your enemies because both you and your ancestors had stubbornly sinned against me. If you humbly confess what you have done and start living right,
translation_verse: ní ma mun jáń nì bi ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì bi-nannanliibi tiŋkin. Ŋyunti gbantee, bi-pɔbiliŋ ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee yaa láa sīntì ŋi-ba taapu ki fōō bi-yìntitam tafadaaldee,

english_verse: I'll keep the promise I made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will bless your land
translation_verse: ní ḿ dāá téetí dipoondi din m nìn pōoǹ Jaakɔb nì Isaaki nì Abraamee pu. M làá dāá téetí m nín nìn pōoǹ kí ŋá tin kí tīī bi-tiŋkee pu.

english_verse: and let it rest during the time that you are in a foreign country, paying for your rebellion against me and my laws.
translation_verse: Ama bi làá dāá yīkì bi-tiŋki pu, ní kíǹ ń dòon̄ ki-ba pu kí ŋùŋfì. Ŋyunti gbantee, bíǹ bíi fòol̄ bi-kpitii paati nì bi nín dū m-koobiliŋ nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ki fá puee tafadaaldi dee.

english_verse: No matter what you have done, I am still the Lord your God, and I will never completely reject you or become absolutely disgusted with you there in the land of your enemies.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ŋyunti ŋun bi dāa bí bi-nannanliibi tiŋkinee, maa làá dāá dū-bi kí fá kɔkɔ, kaa làá dāá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-bi. Maa làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi, kaa làá dāá kpìtī m-poondi. Di sá yii man di sá bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: While nations watched, I rescued your ancestors from Egypt so that I would be their God. Yes, I am your Lord, and I will never forget our agreement.
translation_verse: M làá dāá téetí dipoondi din m nìn pōoǹ bi-baabi bin m nìn nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkin, kí nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu atimbun kɔkɔ ń kée pu, kí fīī-bi. Man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_verse: Moses was on Mount Sinai when the Lord gave him these laws and teachings for the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Abɔkpaa nì akoobil nì marab bin ti-Dindaan nìn yóoǹ án nīn bí u nì Isirayeel yab kansikinee dee. Siinaayi jool pu ní ti-Dindaan nìn dū-bi ki tīī Mooyiisi ú dūú nàatī Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If you ever want to free someone who has been promised to me,
translation_verse: ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Ubɔ yaa pōoǹ kí dū unil kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, udaan ŋūǹ kí dū animbil kí téeǹ unilee yil pu.

english_verse: you may do so by paying the following amounts, weighed according to the official standards:
translation_verse: «An yaa sá unil un cáá abin imuŋku ita nì ipaayee, uninja yil pu sá jitɔmbi saalku, ní unimpu yil pu sá jitɔmbi saalaa.

english_verse: Ten percent of everything you harvest is holy and belongs to me, whether it grows in your fields or on your fruit trees.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan di yì tisaalaatiil tin bi lēē kitiŋ nín lòon̄ tikpaajin tiŋyee nì isufi nín lòon̄ asubil ŋiŋyee poon, an sá úǹ ti-Dindaan wanti ní.

english_verse: If you try to substitute any other animal, no matter how good, for the one you promised, they will both become holy and must be sacrificed.
translation_verse: Nsan kpá bí kpántí-ku. Bí taa dū kun ŋān̄ee kí kpántí kun kaa ŋān̄ee, àá kun kaa ŋān̄ee kí kpántí kun ŋān̄ee. Ubɔ yaa dū kuwaŋkuluu kubɔ ki kpántì kun u dūu pōoǹee, ti-liitil kpántì ti-Dindaan wanti dee.

english_verse: But if you decide to buy it back, you must pay an additional
translation_verse: Udaan yaa tí là kí fàtīí dā u-diikuee, ú pà kudiiyee nimbiŋmiiku nín sá puee, ní kí kūtì bi yaa yākatì kunimbiŋmiiuee miŋmoo puee diba pu.

english_verse: If you have promised to give someone to me and can't afford to pay the full amount for that person's release, you will be taken to a priest, and he will decide how much you can afford.
translation_verse: «Ama un pōoǹ ipoonee yaa kaa cáá ŋŋmam kí pà kunimbiŋmiiu kun bi síiǹee, bí cáań-u usaraaŋal cee ní úǹ ń kpèè ŋŋmam min u cááyee ní kí nóó míǹ kí gíí-u kunimbiŋmiiu.

english_verse: If you promise to sacrifice an animal to me, it becomes holy, and there is no way you can set it free.
translation_verse: «An yaa sá kuwaŋkuluu kun ŋān̄ bí dūú ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee ní udaan yaa pōoǹee, kúǹ kpántì ti-Dindaan wanti dee.

english_verse: Donkeys are unfit for sacrifice, so if you promise me a donkey, you must bring it to the priest,
translation_verse: «An yaa sá kuwaŋkuluu kun kaa ŋān̄ bí dūú ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee ní udaan yaa pōoǹee, ú cáań-kù kí tīī usaraaŋal.

english_verse: But if you want to buy it back, you must pay an additional
translation_verse: Un cáań kuwaŋkuluuee yaa là kí fàtīí dā-kuee, ú pà kunimbiŋmiiu nín sá puee, ní kí kūtì bi yaa yākatì kunimbiŋmiiuee miŋmoo puee diba pu.

english_verse: If you promise a house to me, a priest will set the price, whatever the condition of the house.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa dū u-diiku ki sú ti-Dindaanee, usaraaŋal ń kpèè laakin ku ŋān̄ee nì laakin kuaa ŋān̄ee kí tīī-u kunyampoou.

english_verse: If you promise part of your family's land to me, its value must be determined by the amount of seed needed to plant the land, and the rate will be ten pieces of silver for every
translation_verse: «Ubɔ yaa lēē u-kpaatanti poon bukpaa bubɔ ki sú ti-Dindaanee, kunyampoou ń nīn nóó nì bukpaayee nín ŋūǹ kí lòoǹ puee. Bu yaa lòon̄ ɔɔji biliŋ kiiloobi alaataa atee, udaan ń pà jitɔmbi imuŋku ili nì saalaa.

english_verse: If this promise is made in the Year of Celebration, the land will be valued at the full price.
translation_verse: An yaa sá dibatɔl bindi poon ní u dū u-kpaabu gbanti ki súee, an nimbiŋmiiku ní bi làá nīn ŋúb́.

english_verse: But any time after that, the price will be figured according to the number of years before the next Year of Celebration.
translation_verse: Ama dibatɔl bindi boon ní udaan yaa dū u-kpaabuee ki súee, usaraaŋal ń cɔ́tí kí kpèè abin ŋin kíǹ dibatɔl bindi dipɔndi ń bàńee, ní kí bàtī ku-nyampooku pu kí nóó nì abin gbanti.

english_verse: When the Year of Celebration comes, the land becomes holy because it belongs to me, and it will be given to the priests.
translation_verse: Dibatɔl bindi yaa bāańee, bukpaayee kpántì ti-Dindaan wanti dee, kii bi nín yaa dū bukpaa ki sú ti-Dindaan puee. Bisaraaŋaliibi di kíǹ ki yì-bu.

english_verse: its value will be decided by a priest, according to the number of years before the next Year of Celebration, and the money you pay will be mine.
translation_verse: usaraaŋal ń gíí kunimbiŋmiiu kí nóó nì abin ŋin kíǹ dibatɔl bindi ń bàńee, udaan ń pà ŋwiin gbanti. An nimbiliŋee, bí dūú sú ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: However, on the next Year of Celebration, the land will go back to the family of its original owner.
translation_verse: Ama dibatɔl bindi yaa bāańee, un cee ní u nìn dá bukpaayee ń fàtīí fōō-bu, an dàkà yii un baabi kpaatanti poon ní bukpaayee dɔ̄ee.

english_verse: Every price will be set by the official standards. Various Offerings The Lord said:
translation_verse: «Ni yaa làá gíí kunimbiŋmiiu kun kamaayee, kú nóó nì bi nín ŋmàntī animbil circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon puee, an dàkà yii graambi saalaa.» Saraabi bin kíǹee bɔti

english_verse: All first-born animals of your flocks and herds are already mine, and so you cannot promise any of them to me.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ kaa cáá nsan kí dū u-waŋkuluku biseemal kí sú ti-Dindaan, kun puee ti-Dindaan di yì unaa àá uŋoobu àá upii biseemal.

english_verse: Anything that you completely dedicate to me must be completely destroyed. It cannot be bought back or sold. Every person, animal, and piece of property that you dedicate completely is only for me.
translation_verse: «Tin kamaa ní bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee, baa ti ŋūǹ kí nyāfì-tì, àá kí fàtīí dā-tì. An yaa sá unileeee, kuwaŋkuluueeee, tikpaataneeee, tin kamaa ní bi pée dūu sú ti-Dindaanee kpántì u-wanti dee.

english_verse: In fact, any humans who have been promised to me in this way must be put to death.
translation_verse: Báà an yaa sá unil gba, baa ŋūǹ kí fàtīí dā-u kí líí, see bí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: If you want to buy back this part of your harvest, you may do so by paying what it is worth plus an additional
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa tí là kí dā u-saalaatiiti jandi dibaaa, ú pà kunimbiŋmiiu kun usaraaŋal gííyee kí kūtì bi yaa yākatì kunimbiŋmiiuee miŋmoo puee diba pu.

english_verse: When you count your flocks and herds, one out of ten of every newborn animal is holy and belongs to me,
translation_verse: An yaa sá inaa àá ipii àá iŋoobuee, bí dáań tiwaŋkuti saalaa kamaa poonee kubɔ kí dūú sú ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: no matter how good or bad it is. If you substitute one animal for another, both of them become holy, and neither can be bought back.
translation_verse: Baa máaǹ kí kpèè yii kuwaŋkuluuee ŋān̄aaa, kuaa ŋān̄, kaa tí máaǹ kí nyàab̀ kubɔ kí kpántí-ku. Ubɔ yaa nyàab̄ kuwaŋkuluu kubɔ ki kpántì kun an sāāyee, ti-liitil kpántì ti-Dindaan wanti dee, baa ti ŋūǹ kí fàtīí dā ti-liitilee kansikin báà kubɔ.»

english_verse: Moses was on Mount Sinai when the Lord gave him these laws for the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Marab bin ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Mooyiisi, Siinaayi jool pu ú dūú nàatī Isirayeel yabee dee.

english_verse: The people of Israel had left Egypt and were living in the Sinai Desert. Then on the first day of the second month of the second year, when Moses was in the sacred tent the Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon Siinaayi teekun. An nìn sá Isirayeel yab nín nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkinee binliliitiil uŋmaliliiti wimpeekaaŋu dal. Ti-Dindaan nìn bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: I want you and Aaron to find out how many people are in each of Israel's clans and families. And make a list of all the men
translation_verse: kí yòon̄ bininjab bin cáá abin mmuŋku kí nīn cáa cá, ki bàn̄ kí cù kujaau Isirayeel yab kansikinee. Sii nì Aarɔn, ní kàaǹ-bi kí nóó nì bi-janjakitiŋi nín bí pu a-ba a-bee.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron, together with these twelve tribal leaders,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn dū bininjab bin bi nìn lēē gbantee ki ŋàl̄ bi-ba.

english_verse: called together the people that same day. They were counted according to their clans and families. Then Moses and the others listed the names of the men twenty years and older,
translation_verse: Bi nìn yíiń samaa kɔkɔ ki kpáfì uŋmaliliiti wimpeekaaŋu dal, ní ki ŋmàn̄ Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ cáá abin mmuŋku kí nīn cáa cée yiŋŋi, ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal nì adican puee.

english_verse: The people of Israel did everything the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara Isirayeel yab ń ŋá puee, míǹ ní bi nìn ŋá deedee.

english_verse: But the Levites will camp around the sacred tent to make sure that no one goes near it and makes me furious with the Israelites.
translation_verse: See Leefii naakookun yab baba di làá gāā bi-tantib kí kɔ́ĺ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu, ní kí nīn tūǹ bi-tundi nín sá puee. Mimmee maa làá dāá fōō Isirayeel yab pu diŋuul.»

english_verse: But those from the Levi tribe were not included
translation_verse: Baa nìn kàan̄ Leefii naakookun yab ki kútì Isirayeel naakɔti tin kíǹee yab pu.

english_verse: because the Lord had said to Moses:
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: When you count the Israelites, do not include those from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: «A yaa làá kàaǹ Isirayeel yabee, á yàntī Leefii naakookun yab kí taa kàaǹ-bi.

english_verse: Instead, give them the job of caring for the sacred tent, its furnishings, and the objects used for worship. They will camp around the tent, and whenever you move, they will take it down, carry it to the new camp, and set it up again. Anyone else who tries to go near it must be put to death.
translation_verse: Ni yaa làá yīkì dinaapaal din puee, bíǹ di làá cóotí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu. Ni yaa tí bàn̄ laakin ki làá kàl̄ee, bíǹ di làá dū circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kí cóoń. Unifantanti ubɔ di yaa sútìi pìl̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu gbantee, bí kpɔ̀ udaan.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites will camp in their own groups and under their own banners.
translation_verse: Ni yaa bàn̄ laakin ki làá kàl̄ee, Isirayeel yab báà ŋma ń gāā u-tantiu u-janjakitil paaŋŋu pu, kí nīn kɔ́ĺ di-falaŋkau.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii:

english_verse: how the Israelites should arrange their camp: Each tribe must set up camp under its own banner and under the flags of its ancestral families. These camps will be arranged around the sacred tent, but not close to it.
translation_verse: «Isirayeel yab báà ŋma máaǹ kí gāā u-tantiu kí kɔ́ĺ u-janjakitil falaŋkau nì u-dicaŋku falaŋkau. Bí gāā tantib kí màntīí tū circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kí nīn dátiǹ-ŋu fiii.

english_verse: Judah and the tribes that march with it must set up camp on the east side of the sacred tent, under their own banner. The
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub biluu kpá kutukub imuŋku inaa nì alaataa aluu.

english_verse: On one side of Judah will be the tribe of Issachar, with Nethanel son of Zuar as the leader of its
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub biluu kpá imuŋku ita nì binib alaataa anaa.

english_verse: On the other side will be the tribe of Zebulun, with Eliab son of Helon as the leader of its
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub bita kpá kutukub imuŋku ita nì binib alaataa anaa.

english_verse: Reuben and the tribes that march with it must set up camp on the south side of the sacred tent, under their own banner. The
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub imuŋku ili nì biluu nì binib alaataa aŋmoo.

english_verse: On one side of Reuben will be the tribe of Simeon, with Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai as the leader of its
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub ubɔ kpá kutukub imuŋku ita nì binib alaataa ata.

english_verse: On the other side will be the tribe of Gad, with Eliasaph son of Deuel as the leader of its
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub imuŋku ili nì biŋmoo nì alaataa aluu nì imuŋku ili nì binib saalaa.

english_verse: On one side of Ephraim will be the tribe of Manasseh, with Gamaliel son of Pedahzur as the leader of its
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì saalaa nì bili nì binib alaataa ali.

english_verse: So all the Israelites in the camp were counted according to their ancestral families. The troops were arranged by divisions and totaled
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin bi nìn kàan̄ ki nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋee dee. Bin kɔkɔ bi nìn kàan̄ ki dū-bi ki kpáfì ajanjakitee nìn nyáń binib kutukub alaataa aluu nì kutukub bita nì alaataa aŋmoo nì imuŋku ili nì binib saalaa.

english_verse: On the other side will be the tribe of Benjamin, with Abidan son of Gideoni as the leader of its
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub biŋmoo kpá kutukub imuŋku ili nì binib alaataa anaa.

english_verse: Dan and the tribes that march with it must set up camp on the north side of the sacred tent, under their own banner. The
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub imuŋku ita nì bili nì binib alaataa aluli.

english_verse: On one side of Dan will be the tribe of Asher, with Pagiel son of Ochran as the leader of its
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub imuŋku ili nì ubɔ nì binib alaataa aŋmoo.

english_verse: On the other side will be the tribe of Naphtali with Ahira son of Enan as the leader of its
translation_verse: U-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm sá binib kutukub biluli kpá kutukub imuŋku ita nì alaataa anaa.

english_verse: The only Israelites not included were the Levites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Baa nìn kàan̄ Leefii naakookun yab ki kútì Isirayeel naakɔti tin kíǹee yab pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.

english_verse: Israel did everything the Lord had told Moses. They arranged their camp according to clans and families, with each tribe under its own banner. And that was the order by which they marched into battle.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee, míǹ ní Isirayeel yab nìn ŋá deedee. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn gà bi-tantib ki kɔ́l̀ bi-falaŋkab, ní ki nìn yíkí ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal nì adican puee.

english_verse: But the Lord killed Nadab and Abihu in the Sinai Desert when they used fire that was unacceptable in their offering to the Lord. And because Nadab and Abihu had no sons, only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests with their father Aaron. The Duties of the Levites
translation_verse: Nadaab nì Abiyuu nìn kpíì Siinaayi teekun, ti-Dindaan nimbiin, di sá bi nìn mɔ́fìń ŋŋmi laaba ki kɔ́ǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun. Nadaab nì Abiyuu kaa nìn màl̄ mbiyaamu. Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar di nìn kíǹ ki bí bi-baa Aarɔn nimbiin ki tútúǹ-u disaraaŋal tundi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: who have been appointed to be priests. Anyone else who tries to perform the duties of a priest must be put to death.
translation_verse: Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi baba ní á kàan̄ bí nīn tūǹ disaraaŋal tundi. Un kaa sá usaraaŋalee yaa sútìi pìl̄ ki túń ditundi gbantee, bí kpɔ̀-u.»

english_verse: Moses, I have chosen these Levites from all Israel, and they will belong to me in a special way. When I killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in every Israelite family and the first-born males of their flocks and herds would be mine. But now I accept these Levites in place of the first-born sons of the Israelites. The Levites Are Counted
translation_verse: Kibiseebiki kininjabiki kamaayee, man di yì, di sá daliŋkin m nìn kūū Eejipiti tiŋkin biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kɔkɔee, m nìn dū Isirayeel biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu nì bi-waŋkuti biseemal njamu kɔkɔ ki sú m-ba. Man di sá ni-Dindaan.» Bi kàan̄ Leefii naakookun yab mpeekaam

english_verse: In the Sinai Desert the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi Siinaayi teekun ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: “Now I want you to count the men and boys in the Levi tribe by families and by clans. Include every one at least a month old.”
translation_verse: «Á kàaǹ Leefii naakookun yab kí nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋi nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee. Á kàaǹ kí yòon̄ mbininjabiyaamu mun cáá uŋmal ubɔ kí nīn cée.»

english_verse: So Moses obeyed and counted them.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi kàan̄-bi kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: Levi's three sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, had become the heads of their own clans.
translation_verse: Leefii jipɔmbi di sá Geersɔn nì Keeyaati nì Meerarii.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Geersɔn jipɔmbi ki nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋi yiŋŋi di sá Liibinii nì Simeeyii.

english_verse: Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Keeyaati jipɔmbi ki nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋi yiŋŋi di sá Amiiraam nì Yiisaar nì Eebrɔn nì Usiyeel.

english_verse: And Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the sons and grandsons of Levi, and they had become the leaders of the Levite clans.
translation_verse: Meerarii jipɔmbi ki nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋi yiŋŋi di sá Maalii nì Musii. Leefii naakookun yab dicaŋŋi nín nìn sá puee dee.

english_verse: The two Gershon clans were the Libnites and Shimeites,
translation_verse: Geersɔn yab dicaŋŋi yākatì mili pu, Liibinii yab nì Simeeyii yab.

english_verse: Their duties at the tent included taking care of the tent itself, along with its outer covering, the curtain for the entrance,
translation_verse: Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poonee, ditundi din Geersɔn yab nìn tūǹee di sá bi nìn kpèé tanti poon nì boon nì tibiiŋkaal nì ŋŋaabu ŋun sàkā circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpuee,

english_verse: the curtains hanging inside the courtyard around the tent, as well as the curtain and ropes for the entrance to the courtyard and its altar. The Gershonites were responsible for setting these things up and taking them down.
translation_verse: nì tanti satau nì dicindi punyɔkɔki ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu ŋun māntìi tú ŋkɔŋkoon nì nsaraafanee nì tanti ŋmiii. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The four Kohath clans were the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and the Uzzielites,
translation_verse: Keeyaati yab dicaŋŋi yākatì minaa pu ní, Amiiraam yab nì Yiisaar yab nì Usiyeel yab nì Eebrɔn yab. Keeyaati maaliŋu nín sá puee dee.

english_verse: Their duties at the tent included taking care of the sacred chest, the table for the sacred bread, the lampstand, the altars, the objects used for worship, and the curtain in front of the most holy place. The Kohathites were responsible for setting these things up and taking them down.
translation_verse: Keeyaati yab tundi din bi nìn tīī-bee di nìn sá bí nīn kpèé Dipoondi dakaau nì teebil nì fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì isaraafan nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa ŋáań saraabi tuuŋŋee nì poon ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Eleazar son of Aaron was the head of the Levite leaders, and he made sure that the work at the sacred tent was done.
translation_verse: Leefii yab kpikpaaŋwu di nìn sá Aarɔn usaraaŋakpil jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar. Úǹ di nìn kpèé bin tūǹ ditundi circir laŋkee.

english_verse: The two Merari clans were the Mahlites and the Mushites,
translation_verse: Meerarii yab dicaŋŋi nìn yākatì mili pu ní, Maalii yab nì Musii yab. Meerarii maaliŋu nín nìn sá puee dee.

english_verse: The Merarites, under the leadership of Zuriel son of Abihail, were to camp on the north side of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Meerarii yab kpiliu di nìn sá Abiyayiil jipɔɔn Tuuriyeel. Bi nìn gà bi-tantib circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋgan pú ní.

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and his sons were to camp in front of the sacred tent, on the east side, and to make sure that the Israelites worshiped in the proper way. Anyone else who tried to do the work of Moses and Aaron was to be put to death.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di nìn gà bi-tantib dikpafindi tantiu nyɔkɔpu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú. Bíǹ di nìn tūǹ circir laŋki poon tuuŋŋi Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yil pu. Ubɔ fám yaa nìn sútìi pìl̄-bi ní kaa sá usaraaŋalee, bi nìn kù-u ní.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord and counted the Levites by their clans. The total number of Levites at least one month old was
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín nìn yāntì Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn kàan̄ Leefii yab naakookun bininjab kí yòon̄ bin cáá uŋmal ubɔ kí nīn cáa cée, bininjab kɔkɔ wíiŋŋu nìn nyáń kutukub mmuŋku nì bili ní. Leefii yab fōō mbiseebiyaamu yil

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Make a list and count the first-born sons at least one month old in each of the Israelite families.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Á kàaǹ Isirayeel yab biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kí kíĺ mun cáá uŋmal ubɔ kí nīn pée cáa cée, kí ŋmà mu-yiŋŋi.

english_verse: They belong to me, but I will accept the Levites as substitutes for them, and I will accept the Levites' livestock as substitutes for the Israelites' first-born livestock.”
translation_verse: Boonee á gàntī Leefii yab bí fōō Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu yil kí nīn kíǹ kí sá man yab. Míǹ mbaantiim á tí gàntī Leefii yab waŋkuti tí kpántí man yati Isirayeel yab waŋkuti biseebiyaamu njamu yil pu. Man di sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord and counted the first-born sons;
translation_verse: Mooyiisi kàan̄ Isirayeel yab biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: Then the Lord said,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: “The Levites will belong to me and will take the place of the first-born sons; their livestock will take the place of the Israelites' first-born livestock.
translation_verse: «Á dū Leefii yab kí kpántí Isirayeel yab biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu paaŋŋu, bíǹ ń kpántí man yab. Á tí dū Leefii yab waŋkuti kí kpántí Isirayeel yab waŋkuti biseebiyaamu njamu yil pu. Man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: For each one, you are to collect five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Á yàntī bí pà unil kamaa yil puee, jitɔmbi biŋmoo kí nóó nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nimbiliŋ ŋmàntitam.

english_verse: Moses collected the silver from the extra
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi fōō Isirayeel yab cee bi-biseebiyaamu mun páaǹ Leefii yab puee nimbiliŋ.

english_verse: Then he gave it to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ní u dū animbilee ki tīī Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi, kii ti-Dindaan nín tīī-u mara ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii:

english_verse: The Kohathites will be responsible for carrying the sacred objects used in worship at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Atuun ŋin Keeyaati jipɔmbi làá nīn tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee di sá bí nīn kpèé tin kɔkɔ pée sá circir páaayee.

english_verse: When the Israelites are ready to move their camp, Aaron and his sons will enter the tent and take down the curtain that separates the sacred chest from the rest of the tent. They will cover the chest with this curtain,
translation_verse: Ni yaa làá yīkì ni-naapaal puee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń sàkatī ŋŋaabu ŋun pītì poon diiŋŋee kí gíiǹ-ŋu kí bìin̄ dipoondi taŋkpapilinti dakaau pu.

english_verse: and then with a piece of fine leather, and cover it all with a solid blue cloth. After this they will put the carrying poles in place.
translation_verse: Bí dū ŋgban ŋun dàfèe kí bìin̄, ní kí dū sata un máǹ gàaayee kí páań an pu. Míǹ boonee ní bí dū tikúti kpandɔi kí bɔ̄ Dipoondi dakaau kpiŋŋi bɔmbiliŋ poon.

english_verse: Next, Aaron and his sons will use another blue cloth to cover the table for the sacred bread. On the cloth they will place the dishes, the bowls for incense, the cups, the jugs for wine, as well as the bread itself.
translation_verse: Bí dū ŋŋaaman gùuu kí bìin̄ teebil un pu bi cāabìń kpɔnɔb ki pāantí Unimbɔti nimbiinee, kí dū palantab nì bikɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi nì asambil nì bikɔŋkɔŋkpaambi bin bi cáa féeń Unimbɔti ndaamee kí páań, ní kí dū kpɔnɔb bin bi pāantí ŋwiin kamaa ti-Dindaan nimbiinee kí páań.

english_verse: With another blue cloth they will cover the lampstand, along with the lamps, the lamp snuffers, the fire pans, and the jars of oil for the lamps.
translation_verse: Bí dū ŋŋaaman gàaa kí bìin̄ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-fitilab nì ti-babikaati nì nsambiyaamu mun poon ŋfantam kàal̀ee nì kpalbab bin poon ŋkpam kàal̀ee pu.

english_verse: All of this will then be covered with a piece of fine leather and placed on a carrying frame.
translation_verse: Bí dū an wantee kɔkɔ kí bóob́ kí tàkan̄ ŋgban ŋun dàfèe poon ní kí dūú páań nlún pu.

english_verse: The gold incense altar is to be covered with a blue cloth, and then with a piece of fine leather, before its carrying poles are put in place.
translation_verse: Bí dū ŋŋaaman gùuu kí bìin̄ sindaariya saraafaŋŋu pu, ní kí dū ŋgban ŋun dàfèe kí páań an pu, ní kí dū tikúti kpandɔi kí bɔ̄ ŋu-kpìmbiliŋin.

english_verse: Next, Aaron and his sons will take blue cloth and wrap all the objects used in worship at the sacred tent. These will need to be covered with a piece of fine leather, then placed on a carrying frame.
translation_verse: Bí dū tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ saraabi tuuŋŋi circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee kí póob́ ŋŋaaman ŋun máǹ gùuuyee poon, ní kí dū ŋgban ŋun dàfèe kí bìin̄, ní kí dūú páań nlún pu.

english_verse: They are to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and cover it with a purple cloth.
translation_verse: Bí fāā ŋfantam min bí nsaraafan puee ní kí dū ŋŋaaman kí bìin̄ ŋu-pu.

english_verse: On that cloth will be placed the utensils used at the altar, including the fire pans, the meat forks, the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls. All of this will then be covered with a piece of fine leather, before the carrying poles are put in place.
translation_verse: Bí dū tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ nsaraafan pu tundee kí páań an pu, an dàkà yii kisambiki kin poon ŋkpam min bi wùn̄ee fantam kàal̀ee, nì kijiii kin cáá anyinee, nì kun bi cáa mɔ́fí ŋŋmee, nì disambil din poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki yàantée. Bí dū ŋgban ŋun dàfèe kí páań an pu, ní ki dū tikúti kpandɔi kí bɔ̄ nsaraafan kpìmbiliŋin.

english_verse: When the camp is ready to be moved, the Kohathites will be responsible for carrying the sacred objects and the furnishings of the sacred tent. But Aaron and his sons must have already covered those things so the Kohathites won't touch them and die.
translation_verse: Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi yaa bɔ́ntì tin kɔkɔ sá circiree, ki bīiǹ ti-pu ki dóò bi làá yīkì dinaapaal puee, ní Keeyaati jipɔmbi ń dāá nín yòon̄-tì. Bí taa pée gbēē circir wanti gbanti. Bi yaa gbēē-tì bi làá kpú. Keeyaati jipɔmbi tundi di sá bí nīn tūntí circir wanti tin kɔkɔ bí dikpafindi tantiunee.

english_verse: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest will be in charge of the oil for the lamps, the sweet-smelling incense, the grain for the sacrifices, and the olive oil used for dedications and ordinations. Eleazar is responsible for seeing that the sacred tent, its furnishings, and the sacred objects are taken care of.
translation_verse: Aarɔn jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar tundi di sá ú nīn kpèé ŋkpam min bi cáa ŋáań fitilabinee, nì talaalub bin bi tùutēe, nì tijimpin saraabi bin bi ŋáań kutaa kamaayee, nì ŋkpam min bi sìtī unil yil pu kí dū-u ki sú Unimbɔtee. Úǹ di làá nīn kpèé circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì tin kɔkɔ bí ŋu-poonee, an dàkà yii circir laŋki nì tin bi cáa tūǹ u-poon ditundee.»

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: for carrying the curtains of the sacred tent, its two outer coverings, the curtain for the entrance to the tent,
translation_verse: bí nīn tūntí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋaabui nì ŋu-poon diiku ŋaabui nì igban in dàfì bi cáa bìintí an puee nì ŋŋaabu ŋun lìkī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔkee,

english_verse: the curtains hanging around the courtyard of the tent, and the curtain and ropes for the entrance to the courtyard. The Gershonites are to do whatever needs to be done to take care of these things,
translation_verse: nì dicindi punyɔkɔki ŋaabui nì a yaa làá kɔ́ dicindi ŋŋaabu ŋun sàkā kipunyɔkɔ kí màntīí tū tanti nì nsaraafanee, nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋmiii, nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ niin ditundee. Bíǹ di yì an tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ kí nīn tūǹ.

english_verse: These are the duties of the Gershonites at the sacred tent, and Ithamar son of Aaron will make sure they do their work. The Duties of the Merarite Clans
translation_verse: Atuun ŋin bi dūu ŋúbiǹ Geersɔn jipɔmbi bí nīn tūǹ dikpafindi tantiu poonee dee. Usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn jipɔɔn Itamaar di làá nīn kpèé-bi ní bi tūǹ atuun gbanti. c. Meerarii yab tundi

english_verse: The Merarites will be responsible for carrying the frames of the tent and its other pieces, including the bars, the posts, and the stands,
translation_verse: Atuun ŋin Meerarii jipɔmbi làá nīn tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee di sá bí nīn tūntí tanti punyɔmmu dɔi nì ikalim nì idɔjaati nì i-taapu tílkaati,

english_verse: as well as the posts that support the courtyard, together with their stands, tent pegs, and ropes. The Merarites are to be told exactly what objects they are to carry,
translation_verse: nì idɔjaati in bi cōontí kí màntīí tū dicindee nì i-taapu tílkaati nì akpakpaa nì iŋmii nì tin kɔkɔ pée sá ditundi gbanti wantee. Ní dāá ŋmà báà ŋma nín máaǹ kí túń kuwaŋu kuŋyee kí tīī-u.

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelite leaders obeyed the Lord and counted the Levi tribe by families and clans, to find out how many men there were between the ages of
translation_verse: Kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn bí Mooyiisi ń ŋá puee, u nìn tīī báà ŋma tundi din sá ú tɔ̄ee, ní ki nìn dàkā biwantunliibi tin sá bí túńee. Bi nìn kàan̄-bi kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Put out of the camp everyone who has leprosy or a bodily discharge or who has touched a dead body. Now that I live among my people, their camp must be kept clean.”
translation_verse: Udaan yaa sá uninjeeee, unimpueeee, ní nyāntí-u ŋkpaanceeti, án nín làá ŋá pu ú taa kɔ́ǹ Isirayeel yab naapaal din poon m kóòyee tijɔkɔndee.»

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you commit a crime against someone, you have sinned against me.
translation_verse: ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Uninja kii unimpu ubɔ di yaa ŋá u-juti ikpiti, báà in ní an yaa pée sée, man ni-Dindaan ní u yīntiǹ, udaan fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: You must confess your guilt and pay the victim in full for whatever damage has been done, plus a fine of
translation_verse: Udaan ń bìitī ikpiti in u ŋée pu, kí téeǹ tiwan daan tin u mūul̀ee, ní kí gíti nyàab̀ tiwan gbanti yaa yākatì miŋmoo puee diba pu kí kūtì kí tīī tiwan daan.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: If the victim has no relative who can accept this money, it belongs to me and will be paid to the priest. In addition to that payment, you must take a ram for the priest to sacrifice so your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Un bi mūul̀ee yaa kpíì kaa cáá kinabiki kin cáá nsan kí fōō u-wantee, bí dū tiwanee kí tīī ti-Dindaan, an dàkà yii usaraaŋal. Dibɔkpil daan ń gíti nyàab̀ upìja bí dūú ŋá dibɔkpil saraau kí fíntí u-kpitii.

english_verse: When you make a donation to the sacred tent, that money belongs only to the priest, and each priest will keep what is given to him. A Suspicious Husband
translation_verse: Tin kamaa unil yaa dūu sú ti-Dindaanee, ú cáań kí tīī usaraaŋal. Tin kamaa unil yaa dūu tīī usaraaŋalee, usaraaŋal di yì.» Unimpu un nyáń u-cal boonee bɔti

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Suppose a man becomes jealous and suspects that his wife has been unfaithful, but he has no proof.
translation_verse: ama ní u-cal dàkafī yii u nyáń u-boon ní ki díkí u-pu. An ŋūǹ kí nīn tí sá yii u-cal landɔkɔŋu di sá yii u nyáń u-boon ní an mun kaa sá míǹ.

english_verse: He must take his wife to the priest, together with one kilogram of ground barley as an offering to find out if she is guilty. No olive oil or incense is to be put on that offering.
translation_verse: An yaa bí mimmee, uninjee ń yòon̄ u-nimpuu kí cùnnì usaraaŋal cee, nì ɔɔji yim kiiloobi bita kí ŋá saraa. Ú taa dū ŋkpam kí sìtī ŋyimee pu kí taa ŋá talaalutuukaa, kun puee an sá ipoompoon saraau, saraa un di nyāntí ikpiti mpaampiin puee ní.

english_verse: The priest will lead the woman to my altar and make her stand there.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń yòon̄ unimpuee kí cùnnì circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ú yūĺ ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: He will then pour sacred water into a clay jar and stir in some dust from the floor of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń jōō circir nyim kisampeei ní kí jáfí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon tam kí dūú ŋá nnyimee poon.

english_verse: The priest will write these curses on special paper and wash them off into the bitter water,
translation_verse: «Ní usaraaŋal ń ŋmà mbusu bɔti tin u sòon̄ ki pūtèe kugbɔŋu pu ní kí dūú bɔ̄ nnyim min tūee poon án fíntí tiŋmaŋmabitee.

english_verse: so that when the woman drinks this water, the curses will enter her body.
translation_verse: Ú dū nnyimee kí tīī unimpuee ú nyɔ̀ án kɔ́ u-poon kí tūŋkì.

english_verse: He will take the barley offering from her and lift it up in dedication to me, the Lord. Then he will place it on my altar
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń fōō ipoompoon saraauee unimpuee ŋaan, kí fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ní kí cáań nsaraafan pu.

english_verse: But if she is innocent, her body will not be harmed, and she will still be able to have children.
translation_verse: Ama unimpuee yaa kaa nyáń u-cal boon ní ki sá un kaa ŋá tijɔkɔndee, tiba kaa làá ŋá-u, u làá nīn gbíntìi màal̀ u-biyaamu ní.

english_verse: This is the ceremony that must take place at my altar when a husband suspects that his wife has been unfaithful. The priest must tell the woman to stand in my presence and carefully follow these instructions.
translation_verse: An yaa tí sá yii uninja di dākafì yii an bí kii u-nimpuu nyáń u-boonee, uninjee ń cáá u-nimpuu u-saraaŋal cee ti-Dindaan nimbiin ú ŋá kii mara nee nín pée sá puee deedee.

english_verse: If the husband is wrong, he will not be punished; but if his wife is guilty, she will be punished.
translation_verse: Niinee baa pée cáá tiba kí ŋá uninja, ama an yaa cúú unimpuee, u làá túń u-kpitii.»

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: If any of you want to dedicate yourself to me by vowing to become a Nazirite,
translation_verse: ń tùkù Isirayeel yab kí síiń-bi mara nee yii: «Uninja àá unimpu ubɔ di yaa làá gàntī u-ba kí pòon̄ kí dū u-ba kí sú man ni-Dindaanee,

english_verse: you must no longer drink any wine or beer or use any kind of vinegar. Don't drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins—
translation_verse: udaan ń taa nyɔ̀ ndamam nì idafi in kɔkɔ pée pɔ̄ɔ̄yee, kí taa nyɔ̀ ndaam min nyàm̀ bi lēē-mi ndamam poonee, nì ndaam min poon bi tɔ́ dinyaalee, nì fiinyi subiliŋ ŋin bi ŋmáaḿee nyim. Ú taa ŋmɔ́ fiinyi subiliŋ asoon àá akulim.

english_verse: The hair of a Nazirite is sacred to me, and as long as you are a Nazirite, you must never cut your hair.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun kɔkɔ u dū u-ba ki sú-mee, ú taa yàntī bɔlfi ń gbēē u-yil. Ú nīn bí circir kí yàntī u-yikpiti ń nīn múkú, kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun u yóoǹee yaa láa bàn̄ee.

english_verse: During the time that you are a Nazirite, you must never go close to a dead body,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun kɔkɔ u dū u-ba ki sú man ni-Dindaanee, waa máaǹ kí gbēē utaŋkpiil.

english_verse: not even that of your father, mother, brother, or sister. That would make you unclean. Your hair is the sign that you are dedicated to me, so remain holy.
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti ŋun kɔkɔ u pōoǹ ki dū u-ba ki sú-mee, man ni-Dindaan di kíǹ ki yì-u.

english_verse: If someone suddenly dies near you, your hair is no longer sacred, and you must shave it seven days later during the ceremony to make you clean.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa lítì u-caŋin ki kpíì dicilpu dicilpuee, u nín dū u-ba ki sú-mi puee bíil̀ dee. Ú kòol̀ u-yil ŋwiin ŋun ní u làá nyā tijɔkɔndin kí fàtīí kpántí circiree, an dàkà yii winluli dal.

english_verse: Then on the next day, bring two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Winnii dalee, ú cáań ananjil ali àá abeenanjil ali kí tīī usaraaŋal circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. You will then be forgiven for being too near a dead body, and your hair will again become sacred.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń dū diba kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau, ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa. Boonee ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá akoobil nín sá puee kí fíntí-u kí nyāntí utaŋkpiil un gbēē-uee jɔkɔntin. Yaadal ní ú fàtīí kíĺ kí pòon̄ kí dū u-ba kí sú mpɔm.

english_verse: But the dead body made you unacceptable, so you must make another vow to become a Nazirite and be dedicated once more. Finally, a year-old ram must be offered as the sacrifice to make things right.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ú ŋá ní kí fàtīí kíĺ kí pòon̄ kí dū u-ba kí sú ti-Dindaan mpɔm. Ú dū dibindi diba pibil kí ŋá saraa un ŋáŋkí dibɔkpilee. Ŋyunti ŋun u ŋá ní ki dāa nín gbēē dinikpilee ŋá fám dee, kun puee u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin.

english_verse: When you have completed your promised time of being a Nazirite, go to the sacred tent
translation_verse: «Un dū u-ba ki sú-mee yuntiŋu yaa sāāyee, u nín máaǹ kí ŋá puee marau sèé. U-yuntiŋu yaa sāāyee, bí yàntī ú dāan̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: and offer three animals that have nothing wrong with them: a year-old ram as a sacrifice to please me, a year-old female lamb as a sacrifice for sin, and a full-grown ram as a sacrifice to ask my blessing.
translation_verse: Ú nīn ŋúbiń saraa wanti nee kí cáań man ni-Dindaan. Ú dū dipibil din cáá dibindi diba di-laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa, kí dū upisal un cáá dibindi diba u-laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau, ní kí dū upìja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá mpèé saraau.

english_verse: Wine offerings and grain sacrifices must also be brought with these animals. Finally, you are to bring a basket of bread made with your finest flour and olive oil, but without yeast. Also bring some thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Ú cáań kpɔnɔb bin poon baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee kikabiki poon, nì ŋkpɔnɔwaamu mun bi dū ŋkpam ki ŋmālim̀ ki búuń ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee nì kalaabi bin pu bi yɔ́kɔfì ŋkpam ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee, ní kí cáań tijimpin saraau nì ndaam.

english_verse: The priest will take these gifts to my altar and offer them, so that I will be pleased and will forgive you.
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋal ń fōō tiwanee kí cáań ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì saraawɔkaa.

english_verse: Then he will sacrifice the ram and offer the wine, grain, and bread.
translation_verse: Ú dū upìja nì kpɔnɔ un kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ ki kā kikabikinee kí ŋá mpèé saraau. Boonee ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá tijimpin saraau nì ndaam saraau.

english_verse: After that, you will stand at the entrance to the sacred tent, shave your head, and put the hair in the fire where the priest has offered the sacrifice to ask my blessing.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ní un pōoǹ ki dū u-ba ki sú-mee ń kòol̀ u-yikpiti circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní kí dū tiyikpitee kí tɔ̄ mpèé saraau un pá nsaraafan pu ki wùee poon.

english_verse: Once the meat from the ram's shoulder has been boiled, the priest will take it, along with one loaf of bread and one wafer brushed with oil, and give them to you.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u kōol̀ u-yil ki dóòyee, ní usaraaŋal ń lēē upìja nanti tin bi tɔ́kɔǹee kuboou, nì kpɔnɔb bin kā kikabikin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee ubɔ, nì kalaabi bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee ubɔ, kí dūú tàkan̄ un dū u-ba ki sú-mee ŋaan.

english_verse: You will hand them back to the priest, who will lift them up in dedication to me. Then he can eat the meat from the ram's shoulder, its choice ribs, and its hind leg, because this is his share of the sacrifice. After this, you will no longer be a Nazirite, and you will be free to drink wine.
translation_verse: Niinee ní usaraaŋal u-ba ń yòon̄ saraa wantee kí fíiǹ fíiǹ ní kí dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa. An saraabee sá circir ní, usaraaŋal di yì upiiyee taal din bi dūu ŋá saraayee nì u-bindi din bi lēē ki yóoǹee. Bi yaa ŋá mimmee, udaan ŋūǹ kí kíĺ kí nīn kíǹ ki nyù ndamam.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: “When Aaron and his sons bless the people of Israel, they must say:
translation_verse: ń tùkù Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi yii: «Ni yaa làá bìin̄ Isirayeel yab puee, ní lì yii:

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will bless and protect you,
translation_verse: <Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ a-boon kí wúń a-pu!

english_verse: and that he will show you mercy and kindness.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ń bútí a-pu nnimbiin, u-ŋanti ń nīn bí a-pu!

english_verse: May the Lord be good to you and give you peace.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ń pɔ̄-si nnimbiimmɔnti kí tīī-si ŋgbansɔŋfi!>

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If Aaron and his sons ask me to bless the Israelites, I will give them my blessing.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní bisaraaŋaliibi yaa yíiń m-yindi míǹ kí bìin̄ Isirayeel yab puee, man m-ba di làá bìin̄ bi-pu.»

english_verse: When Moses had finished setting up the sacred tent, he dedicated it to the Lord, together with its furnishings, the altar, and its equipment.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nín nìn cóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ki dóòyee, u nìn bātì ŋkpam ki sītì ŋu nì ŋu-wanti kɔkɔ pu ki ŋá-tì circir, ní ki bātìi sītì nsaraafan nì tiwan tin bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee ki ŋá-tì circir.

english_verse: Then the twelve tribal leaders of Israel, the same men who had been in charge of counting the people, came to the tent
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel naakɔti kpilib cáań bi-wampɔkaati ki tīī-u. Bíǹ di sá tinaakɔti kpilib bin nìn tútuǹ bi kàan̄ binibee.

english_verse: with gifts for the Lord. They brought six strong carts and twelve oxen—one ox from each leader and a cart from every two.
translation_verse: Tiwampɔkaal tin bi nìn cáań ti-Dindaan nimbiinee di sá tɔrɔkub bin pu bi kpáá ki bīiǹee biluu nì inaa saalaa nì ili. Bikpilib bili nìn kpáfì ki tīī tɔrɔku ubɔ ní ukpil kamaa tīī unaa unaa. Ní bi cáań tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: “Accept these gifts, so the Levites can use them here at the sacred tent for carrying the sacred things.”
translation_verse: «Fōō tiwampɔkaal tin bi cáańee bí nīn cáa tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋi. Á yàkatī-tì kí tīī Leefii yab kí táá nì báà ŋma tundi nín sá puee.»

english_verse: Then Moses took the carts and oxen and gave them to the Levites,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi fōō tɔrɔkub nì inaayee ki dūu yākatì ki tīī Leefii yab.

english_verse: who were under the leadership of Ithamar son of Aaron. Moses gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites for their work, and four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites for their work.
translation_verse: ki dū tɔrɔkub binaa nì inaa inii ki tīī Meerarii jipɔmbi bin tundi usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn jipɔɔn Itamaar nìn kpèéyee. U nìn tīī bi mun ki nóó nì bi-tundi nín sá puee.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any to the Kohathites, because they were in charge of the sacred objects that had to be carried on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Ama waa nìn tīī Keeyaati jipɔmbi tiba, kun puee bíǹ nìn kpèé circir wanti ní, ní an sá bí nīn bùkuntí-tì bi-gbigbipati pu. Tiwampɔkaal tin bi dūu pɔ̄ntì nsaraafanee

english_verse: On the day the altar was dedicated, the twelve leaders brought offerings for its dedication.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun bi làá sìtī nsaraafan pu ŋkpam kí ŋá-ŋu circiree, tinaakɔti kpilib nìn cáań tiwampɔkaal nsaraafanee nimbiin bí dūú pɔ̀ntī-ŋu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Each day one leader is to give his offering for the dedication.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí Mooyiisi yii: «Yàntī bikpilibee, báà ŋma ń nīn cáá ŋwiin ŋubɔ ŋubɔ kí cáań bi-wampɔkaati tin bi làá dūú pɔ̀ntī nsaraafanee.»

english_verse: kilograms, according to the official standards;
translation_verse: nì uŋɔja ubɔ bí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau,

english_verse: rams a year old as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing.
translation_verse: Ŋwiŋwawaati dalee, un nìn cáań u-wampɔkaatee di sá Giideewoonii jipɔɔn Abidan, Beenjameen naakookun yab kpiliu.

english_verse: Whenever Moses needed to talk with the Lord, he went into the sacred tent, where he heard the Lord's voice coming from between the two winged creatures above the lid of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní Mooyiisi kɔ́ dikpafindi tantiun kí sòoǹ nì ti-Dindaanee, u nìn gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan neen pu. Nneenee nìn nyánní keerubimbi bin tɔ́kɔ́ Dipoondi dakaau bìil puee watil pú ki bíi sòoǹ nì u.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: “Tell Aaron to put the seven lamps on the lampstand so they shine toward the front.”
translation_verse: ń tùkù Aarɔn yii: «A yaa làá yóoń fitilab circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee, á yàntī bi-walifiŋu ń nīn ŋmíntí fitilab bilulee tɔ́kɔŋkaati nimbiin pú.»

english_verse: The lampstand was made of hammered gold from its base to the decorative flowers on top, exactly like the pattern the Lord had described to Moses. Instructions for Ordaining the Levites
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati, kí yòon̄ taapu ki cáá sāā ikpiin. Bi nìn mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn dàkā Mooyiisi yii ú mɔ́ɔ́-bi puee ní. Bi dū Leefii yab ki sú Unimbɔti

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: The Levites must be acceptable to me before they begin working at the sacred tent. So separate them from the rest of the Israelites
translation_verse: «Á gàntī Leefii yab Isirayeel yab kansikin kí bɔ́ntí-bi bí nīn bí circir.

english_verse: They are to bring a bull and its proper grain sacrifice of flour mixed with olive oil. And they must bring a second bull as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Boonee ní bí cáań unaja nì ŋyim min bi búuń ŋkpaminee, ní sii a-ba ń yòon̄ unajaliliiti un sá bí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee.

english_verse: Then you, Moses, will call together all the people of Israel and send the Levites to my sacred tent,
translation_verse: Á yàntī Leefii yab ń sútiń kí yūĺ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu, ní kí yíiń Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ kí kpāfì.

english_verse: where the people will place their hands on them.
translation_verse: Á yàntī Leefii yab ń sútiń kí yūĺ m-nimbiin ní Isirayeel yab ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań bi-pu.

english_verse: Aaron will present the Levites to me as a gift from the people, so that the Levites will do my work.
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn ń dū-bi kí sú-mi kii saraa ní Isirayeel yab ŋá ki tīī-mee, ní bí nīn kíǹ ki sá bin bi gāntì bí nīn tūǹ man tundee.

english_verse: After this, the Levites are to place their hands on the heads of the bulls. Sacrifice one of the bulls for the forgiveness of sin, and the other to make sure that I am pleased. Then the Levites will be acceptable to me.
translation_verse: Leefii yab ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań inajaayee yiliŋ pu ní á dū unaja ubɔ kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau kí tīī-mi, ní kí dū un kíǹee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa. Míǹ boonee ní Aarɔn ń ŋá dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée Leefii yab pu ní bí ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam.

english_verse: They will stand at my altar in front of Aaron and his sons, who will dedicate the Levites to me.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní á yàntī Leefii yab ń yūĺ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nimbiin, ní á dū-bi kí sú-mi.

english_verse: This ceremony will show that the Levites are different from the other Israelites and belong to me in a special way.
translation_verse: Mimmee a gāntì Leefii yab Isirayeel yab kansikin dee, bí nīn kíǹ ki sá man yab.

english_verse: After they have been made acceptable and have been dedicated, they will be allowed to work at my sacred tent.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee ní Leefii yab ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ dikpafindi tantiu poon kí nín tūǹ bi-tuuŋŋi. «Míǹ ní an sá á dī kí ŋá Leefii yab circir ní kí dū-bi kí sú-mi.

english_verse: They are mine and will take the place of the first-born Israelite sons.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Isirayeel yab kansikinee, bíǹ ní bi dūu sú-mi kɔkɔ. Ní ḿ fōō-bi Isirayeel yab biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kɔkɔ yil pu.

english_verse: When I killed the oldest sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in each Israelite family would be mine, as well as every first-born male from their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Isirayeel yab biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu kɔkɔ ki kpáaǹ bi-waŋkuti biseebiyaamu njamu kɔkɔee, man di yì. Kí yòon̄ daliŋkin m kūū Eejipiti tiŋkin mbiseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamuee ní m dū Isirayeel yab biseebiyaamu ki sú m-ba.

english_verse: But now I have chosen these Levites as substitutes for the first-born sons,
translation_verse: M yōoǹ Leefii yab ní ki dūu kpántì Isirayeel yab biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu.

english_verse: and I have given them as gifts to Aaron and his sons to serve at the sacred tent. I will hold them responsible for what happens to anyone who gets too close to the sacred tent. The Levites Are Dedicated to the Lord
translation_verse: M lēē-bi Isirayeel yab kansikin ki dū-bi ki tīī Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi. Bi làá nīn bí dikpafindi tantiu poon ki tūǹ ditundi ki tìì Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee, ní kí nīn ŋáań Isirayeel yab pu akoobil nín sá puee bí ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam. Mimmee Isirayeel yab kaa ti sútí kí pìl̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ní kaa nín kpíì.»

english_verse: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelites made sure that the Levites did everything the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn ŋá Leefii yab pu kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara ú ŋá puee deedee.

english_verse: The Levites sprinkled themselves with the water of forgiveness and washed their clothes. Then Aaron brought them to the altar and offered sacrifices to forgive their sins and make them acceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Leefii yab nìn ŋá tin kɔkɔ pée sá bí ŋá kí kpántí circiree, ki fíntì bi-wampeeŋkaati. Boonee ní Aarɔn dū-bi ki sú ti-Dindaan, ní ki ŋá akoobil nín sá puee bí kpántí circir.

english_verse: After this, the Levites worked at the sacred tent as assistants to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Míǹ boon ní Leefii yab kíĺ bi-tuuŋŋi dikpafindi tantiun. Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di nìn kpòotī-bi atuun gbanti poon. Ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara yii bí ŋá Leefii yab puee, míǹ deedee ní bi nìn ŋá.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: They may help the other Levites in their duties, but they must no longer be responsible for any work themselves. Remember this when you assign their duties.”
translation_verse: Bi dāa ŋūǹ kí tūtuǹ bi-nabiyaamu circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon atuun, ama baa dāa sá bin bi tìì atuun aba bí tɔ̄ee. Án nín sá á bɔ́ntí atuun min kí tīī Leefii yabee dee.»

english_verse: During the first month of Israel's second year in the Sinai Desert, the Lord had told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi Siinaayi teekun. An nìn sá bi nín nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkinee binliliitiil uŋmapeepeekaa poon ní. Ti-Dindaan nìn bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.”
translation_verse: Ní jī-u uŋmapeepeekaa nee poon ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal kujoopɔŋ. Ní jī-u kí nóó nì u-marab nì u-koobiliŋ nín sá puee.»

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
translation_verse: Bi nìn jíń jiŋaal gbanti uŋmapeepeekaa ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal, kujoopɔŋ Siinaayi teekun. Isirayeel yab nìn pée nóó min ti-Dindaan tùkū Mooyiisi yii bí ŋée ní deedee.

english_verse: Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Bininjab biba nìn bí niin kaa nìn bí circir kí jī jiŋaal gbanti yaadal, di sá bi nìn gbēē dinikpil. Bi nìn cūtìi ká Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn ŋwiin gbanti.

english_verse: “Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí Mooyiisi yii: «Ti gbēē dinikpil ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Ba pu ní timbi kaa cáá nsan kí cáań ti-saraabi ŋyunti ŋun an máaǹee kii Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee nín bíi cāabìń puee?»

english_verse: Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-bi yii: «Cīitímaan ḿ kpèè ti-Dindaan nín làá tīī mara un ni-bɔti nee puee.»

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover.
translation_verse: ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Ni-kansikin ubɔ àá ni-naantiibi bin bí ki dòońee biba yaa gbēē dinikpil ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi àá bi bínní nsandandatee, bi ŋūǹ kí jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu nee kí tīī man ni-Dindaan tinyool.

english_verse: But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs,
translation_verse: Bidambi ń dāá jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu gbanti uŋmaliliiti poon ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal kujoopɔŋ. Bí dāá ŋmɔ́ saraa pibilee nì kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nì tifaal tin tūee.

english_verse: and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
translation_verse: Bí taa láa kíń tiba nì tiba kí wúntí kutaa, kí taa wīī dipibilee kpabiŋ. Bí dāá nóó akoobil ŋin m yóoǹ bí nīn dì ki jīǹ jiŋaal gbantee deedee.

english_verse: But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
translation_verse: Ama ubɔ yaa kaa gbēē dinikpil ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi ní kaa cūtì nsandandati, ama ní ki ŋá mpɔɔgbifin kaa jíń jiŋaal nee u-wiiŋŋu dalee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel yab kansikin u nín ŋá pu ní kaa cáań u-saraau ŋwiin ŋun bi yóoǹee kí tīī-mee. Udaan kpitii làá fàtīí gítí u-pu, kun puee waa cáań-mi saraa ŋwiin ŋun an sá ú cáańee.

english_verse: Anyone, including foreigners who live among you, can celebrate Passover, if they follow all the regulations. The Cloud over the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Binicambi bin kɔ́-ni ki kíǹ ki bí ni-tiŋkinee yaa là kí jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu kí tīī-mi tinyoolee, bí nóó marab bin m yóoǹ bí nīn dì ki jīǹ jiŋaal gbantee. Mara sá ubaanti ní ki tīī bitindambi nì binicambi.» Ditagbandi bīiǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu

english_verse: As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní an nìn kíǹ ki bí baabadal. Ditagbandee nìn bīī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu, ní kunyeeuee di sá ŋwalifi.

english_verse: whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ama dì yaa nìn kāl̀ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu iwiin ili àá uŋmal àá ki yúntì tikpilee, Isirayeel yab kaa nìn yíkí bi-naapaal pu, asee ditagbandi ń péé kí yīkì.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tùkū Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp.
translation_verse: «Á dū animbil kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ akantán ali kí nīn cáa búǹ ki yíì Isirayeel samaau ki kpáfí. An yaa tí ŋmāntì bí yīkì dinaapaal puee, á búń bí yīkì.

english_verse: If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Bi yaa búń akantán liitil dicilpuee, an sá Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ní ń kpāfì a-cee circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
translation_verse: Dikantámbaantiil ní bi yaa búńee, mimmee an sá Isirayeel yab naakɔti kpilib ŋmaniŋma di làá kpāfì a-cee.

english_verse: But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Ama bi yaa làá búń dikpafil kantándee, ikuŋkuunti ń taa nín̄ bí.

english_verse: The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
translation_verse: «Aarɔn naantiibi bisaraaŋaliibi baba di cáá nsan kí búń dikantándi. Án nīn sá mara un ní ni nì ni-naantiibi làá nīn ŋúb́ kí nīn cá jaanjaanee.

english_verse: Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you.
translation_verse: «Ni yaa làá yīkì ni-tiŋkin kí cùú jáǹ ni-nannanliibi bin táká-nee, ní búń akantán nì ijanjakuŋkuunti. An di làá yàntī ḿ téetí ni-pu, ní man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ń dāá fīī-ni ni-nannanliibi gbanti ŋaan.

english_verse: On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin, dibinliliitiil ŋmaliliitiu poon, iwiin mmuŋku dalee ní ditagbandi din nìn dàn̄ tanti un poon Dipoondi dakaau bée yíkì.

english_verse: So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn yíkì Siinaayi teekun ki nìkī bi-saŋkindi. Ní ditagbandee cūtìi yúl̀ Paaran teekun.

english_verse: This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
translation_verse: Mpeepeekaam dee Isirayeel yab ń nìn yīkì dinaapaal pu ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan marau un Mooyiisi nìn dūu tīī-bee.

english_verse: Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe,
translation_verse: Juuda naakooku janjakitil nì bi-falaŋkau di nìn péé ki yíkì ki līntì nsan. Bi-janjakpiliu di nìn sá Amiinadaab jipɔɔn Naakɔn.

english_verse: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe,
translation_verse: Suwaar jipɔɔn Neetaneeyeel di nìn sá Isakaar naakookun yab janjakpiliu.

english_verse: and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
translation_verse: Eelɔn jipɔɔn Eeliyaab di nìn sá Sabulɔn naakookun yab janjakpiliu.

english_verse: The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
translation_verse: Bi nìn cúú circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ki cóotì ní Geersɔn nì Meerarii naantiibi yab yōoǹ ki túǹ.

english_verse: Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe,
translation_verse: Rubeen naakookun yab janjakitil nì bi-falaŋkau di nìn páaǹ bi-boon. Bíǹ janjakpiliu di nìn sá Seedeeyuur jipɔɔn Eelsuur

english_verse: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe,
translation_verse: Suriisadaayi jipɔɔn Seelumiyeel di nìn sá Simeeyɔn naakookun yab janjakpiliu.

english_verse: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Deewuyeel jipɔɔn Eeliyasaafi di nìn sá Gaadi naakookun yab janjakpiliu.

english_verse: Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
translation_verse: Keeyaati naakookun yab Leefii yab bin tūntí circir wantee di nìn páaǹ bíǹ boon. Leefii yab bin kíǹee nìn līntì ki cūtìi bíi cōontí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu bi-yab ń nín bàń.

english_verse: Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, Eefiraayiim naakookun yab janjakitil nì bi-falaŋkau di nìn páaǹ. Bi-janjakpiliu di nìn sá Amiiyuudi jipɔɔn Eeliisama.

english_verse: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe,
translation_verse: Peedasuur jipɔɔn Gamaliyeel di nìn sá Manasee naakookun yab janjakpiliu.

english_verse: and Abidan son of Gideoni was the leader of the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Giideewoonii jipɔɔn Abidan di nìn sá Beenjameen naakookun yab janjakpiliu.

english_verse: Dan and the tribes that camped alongside it were to protect the Israelites against an attack from behind, and so they marched last, carrying their banner. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was the leader of the tribe of Dan,
translation_verse: Daani naakookun yab janjakitil nì bi-falaŋkau di nìn lúŋkì. Bíǹ di nìn sá bin pá akiti kɔkɔ boon ki cí-bee. Bi-janjakpiliu di nìn sá Amiisadaayi jipɔɔn Ayeeseer.

english_verse: Pagiel son of Ochran was the leader of the Asher tribe,
translation_verse: Ookiran jipɔɔn Pagiyeel di nìn sá Aseer naakookun yab janjakpiliu.

english_verse: and Ahira son of Enan was the leader of the Naphtali tribe.
translation_verse: Eeyinan jipɔɔn Ayiira di nìn sá Neefitalii naakookun yab janjakpiliu.

english_verse: This was the order in which the Israelites marched each time they moved their camp.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nì bi-janjakitiŋi nín nìn máaǹ kí dī tɔb pu kí yīkèe, míǹ ní bi nìn dī ki yíkì. Mooyiisi bíi nyàab̀ un làá dàkà-bi nsanee

english_verse: Hobab the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, was there. And Moses said to him, “We're leaving for the place the Lord has promised us. He has said that all will go well for us. So come along, and we will make sure that all goes well for you.”
translation_verse: Mooyiisi bí u-coo Reewuyeel un sá Madiyan yab tiŋkinee jipɔɔn Oobaab yii: «Ti làá yīkì kí nīn cá kitiŋ kin poon ti-Dindaan pōoǹ yii u làá tīī-tee dee. Dāan̄ ti nì si ń cù, sii mun ń dāá ká tiŋan tin ti-Dindaan làá ŋá-tee poon tiba.»

english_verse: “No, I won't go,” Hobab answered. “I'm returning home to be with my own people.”
translation_verse: Ní Oobaab kíí-u yii: «Aayee, maa làá cù. M làá gítí m-tiŋkin, m-dicaŋku poon.»

english_verse: “Please go with us!” Moses said. “You can be our guide because you know the places to camp in the desert.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-u yii: «M gbāam̀-si, taa dū-ti kí fá. Di sá yii sii nyí kuteeun jaaŋŋi ki ŋūǹ kí dàkà-ti laakin ti máaǹ kí nīn kàal̀ee. Nín̄ bí ti-cee ki dàkà-ti nsan.

english_verse: Besides that, if you go, we will give you a share of the good things the Lord gives us.”
translation_verse: A yaa céeǹ-tee, ti-Dindaan yaa làá tin ŋá-ti tiŋan tiŋyee, a mun dāa cáá tiba poon.»

english_verse: The people of Israel began their journey from Mount Sinai. They traveled three days, and the Levites who carried the sacred chest led the way, so the Lord could show them where to camp.
translation_verse: Ní bi yíkì ti-Dindaan jool taapu ki cōom̀ iwiin ita. Iwiin ita gbantee, ti-Dindaan dakaau nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpu ki nyàab̀ mpaan ŋun ŋān̄ee bí kàl̄.

english_verse: And the cloud always stayed with them.
translation_verse: Bi yaa yíkì dinaapaal pu ŋwiimpuee, ti-Dindaan tagbandi dàn̄ bi-pu ní bi còom̄.

english_verse: Each day as the Israelites began their journey, Moses would pray, “Our Lord, defeat your enemies and make them run!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi yaa làá yòon̄ ti-Dindaan dakaauee ní Mooyiisi ń téeń yii: «Ti-Dindaan, lìntī nyɔkɔpu a-pulincɔntiibi ń yàl̄, a-nannanliibi ń wāŋkì a-nimbiin!»

english_verse: And when they stopped to set up camp, he would pray, “Our Lord, stay close to Israel's thousands and thousands of people.”
translation_verse: Ní bi yaa làá tí dū u-dakaauee kí yóońee, ní ú tí téeń yii: «Ti-Dindaan, fàtīí gítiń kí nīn kóò Isirayeel yab dicaŋŋi cutimaanyi kansikin!»

english_verse: One day the Israelites started complaining about their troubles. The Lord heard them and became so angry that he destroyed the outer edges of their camp with fire.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Isirayeel yab tí bíi tíminsí ki sūǹ ki kɔ́kɔĺ ti-Dindaan. Ti-Dindaan gbìl̄ee ní ki fōō diŋuul, ní ki yāntì u-ŋmiŋu dɔ́miń ki wùn̄ bi-naapaal kpaanceetii.

english_verse: When the people begged Moses to help, he prayed, and the fire went out.
translation_verse: Ní samaa kɔkɔ gbáń ibiil ki yíiń Mooyiisi ní Mooyiisi gbāam̀ ti-Dindaan ní ŋŋmee kpíì.

english_verse: They named the place “Burning,” because in his anger the Lord had set their camp on fire. The People Grumble about Being Hungry
translation_verse: Bi nìn pú niin diyindi yii Tabeera, taapu di sá yii <ŋŋmi wùn̄>, di sá yii niin ní ti-Dindaan nìn wùn̄ bi-naapaal kpaanceetii. Isirayeel yab bíi bàlifī tinan pu

english_verse: One day some foreigners among the Israelites became greedy for food, and even the Israelites themselves began moaning, “We don't have any meat!
translation_verse: Nneel nìn cúú biniyaŋyambi bin nìn ŋmālim̀ Isirayeel yab kansikinee, ní Isirayeel yab bi-ba mun nìn kíĺ ki bíi sūǹ ki lì yii: «La ní ti làá nín ká tinan kí ŋmɔ́ dee?

english_verse: In Egypt we could eat all the fish we wanted, and there were cucumbers, melons, all kinds of onions, and garlic.
translation_verse: Áà! Ti yaa téetì ti nín nìn bí Eejipiti ki ŋmóò ijɔm faalaa pu nì aputaajul nì akambil nì gaabub nì ayoob puee!
