english_verse: But we're starving out here, and the only food we have is this manna.”
translation_verse: Doo nee tiba nì tiba kpá, ní ti bí ki dúntí, kun puee taa ti pée kāntí tiba kí jī ki kútì maana pu.»

english_verse: The manna was like small whitish seeds
translation_verse: Maana nìn bí mbilimu mbilimu, ki pīiǹ fàaa ní ki dàfì.

english_verse: He prayed: I am your servant, Lord, so why are you doing this to me? What have I done to deserve this? You've made me responsible for all these people,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí ti-Dindaan yii: «Ba pu ní a yòontí m-pɔbil míǹ? Ba pu ní a yíì kaa súń m-saai? Ba pu ní a dū samaa nee gìńdi ki nyīkiǹ m-pu yii ḿ kpòotī-bi ní?

english_verse: but they're not my children. You told me to nurse them along and to carry them to the land you promised their ancestors.
translation_verse: Man di kaa cáá dinibul nee pool ki màl̄-bi, nì míǹ kɔkɔee, a bí yii ḿ fōō-bi kí ŋmàb̄ kii ubilool nín ŋmàb̀ kibipɔŋ puee, kí cáá-bi kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin poon a nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ yii a làá tīī bi-naanjabee.

english_verse: They keep whining for meat, but where can I get meat for them?
translation_verse: La ní m làá ká tinan kí tīī samaa nee kɔkɔ? Di sá bi yú ki kɔ́ĺ-mi ki sūǹ ki bàlifī yii ḿ tīī-bi tinan.

english_verse: This job is too much for me. How can I take care of all these people by myself?
translation_verse: Maa ŋūǹ kí túń samaa nee kɔkɔ gìńdi m-baba, dì nyìm̀ ki jítiǹ-mi.

english_verse: If this is the way you're going to treat me, just kill me now and end my miserable life! Seventy Leaders Are Chosen To Help Moses
translation_verse: A yaa là kí dàkā-mi yii a ŋá-mi tiŋanee, á kpɔ̀-mi sɔ́ǹ min ní a bíi ŋáań-mi nee. M yaa kpíìyee, maa làá ti ká m-falaau nee.»

english_verse: While I am talking with you there, I will give them some of your authority, so they can share responsibility for my people. You will no longer have to care for them by yourself.
translation_verse: Man làá kpákatiń mpaan gbanti pu kí sòoǹ nì si, ní kí lēē a-pu ŋfam min m tīī-see fiii kí dūú ŋá bi-pu, án nín làá ŋá pu bí ŋmā kí tūtuǹ-si á túń dinibul nee gìŋ́ŋi án taa nín̄ gíti sá sii baba tundee.

english_verse: As for the Israelites, I have heard them complaining about not having meat and about being better off in Egypt. So tell them to make themselves acceptable to me, because tomorrow they will have meat.
translation_verse: Á tùkù dinibul nee yii: <Ŋámaan ni-ba circir kí cīití fool. Ni làá fu ŋmɔ́ tinan kun puee ti-Dindaan gbìl̄ ni-siim. Di sá u nyí nneel nín cúú-ni áli ni tin lī yii ni nín nìn bí Eejipiti tiŋkinee, an nìn ŋān̄ nì nee. An puee u làá fu tīī-ni tinan fool.

english_verse: . They turned against me and wanted to go back to Egypt. Now they will eat meat until they get sick of it.
translation_verse: Ama ni làá ŋmɔ́ tinan áli uŋmamɔn. Ni làá ŋmɔ́ míǹ an núutí-ni áli kí dāá nyānní ni-maŋfaliŋin. Kun puee ni kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ ti-Dindaan un bí ni-kansikinee, ki súń u-nimbiin ki bí yii ba pu ní bi nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin.>»

english_verse: Even if we butchered all our sheep and cattle, or caught every fish in the sea, we wouldn't have enough to feed them.”
translation_verse: Báà ti yaa kūū ti-piii nì ti-ŋoobui nì ti-naai kɔkɔ, an kaa làá bà-bi. Báà tí cùú kà dimɔɔlin jɔmii kɔkɔ, an kaa làá bà-bi!»

english_verse: Eldad and Medad were two leaders who had not gone to the tent. But when the Spirit took control of them, they began shouting like prophets right there in camp.
translation_verse: Binib bin bi nìn lēēyee kansikin bili, Eeldaadi nì Meedaadi nìn gbíntì dinaapaal pu kaa cūtì tanti cee. Ní Ŋfam dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ bi-ni ní bi kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ kii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibee dinaapaal pu niin.

english_verse: A boy ran to Moses and told him about Eldad and Medad.
translation_verse: Ní unaacimpɔɔn ubɔ sáǹ ki cūtìi tùkū Mooyiisi yii: «Eeldaadi nì Meedaadi bí dinaapaal pu ki nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti!»

english_verse: Joshua was there helping Moses, as he had done since he was young. And he said to Moses, “Sir, you must stop them!”
translation_verse: Ní Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa un nìn pée bí ki tútúǹ Mooyiisi doooo u-biyatinee téeń yii: «M-kpiliu Mooyiisi, pìin̄-bi nsanaa!»

english_verse: But Moses replied, “Are you concerned what this might do to me? I wish the Lord would give his Spirit to all his people so everyone could be a prophet.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-u yii: «A bíi ŋáań m-pu ipoompoon níii? Ti-Dindaan yaa bàà kíikí kí dū u-Fam kí ŋá Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ pu, bi-kɔkɔ ń bàà kpántí u-bɔnaatiliibi, an bàà ŋān̄!»

english_verse: Some time later the Lord sent a strong wind that blew quails in from the sea until Israel's camp was completely surrounded with birds, piled up about a meter high for many kilometers in every direction.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì kubuŋu kubɔ nyánní tiŋku watil pú ki kpáaǹní inoon iba, i bí kii njikpacimamuee ki cáań ki bīiǹ dinaapaal pu bɔ̀mmm. Inoonee nín nìn dɔ̄ ki māntìi tú dinaapaal pu ki tin gbēeǹ laakiŋyee nìn sá ŋwiin ŋubɔ saŋkindi ní. Ní mu nín nìn kpúkú kitiŋ puee sá meeta ubɔ nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: The people picked up quails for two days—each person filled at least ten large baskets. Then they spread them out to dry.
translation_verse: Bi nìn fāā inoonee yaadal wiiŋŋu nì kunyeeu áli kutaa dūu wúntì. Un kaa nìn fāā tikpilee di sá un nìn ká kiiloobi kutukub bili nì dijandee. Ní bi ŋáŋkì ki díntì ki māntìi tú dinaapaal.

english_verse: But before the meat could be eaten, the Lord became angry and sent a deadly disease through the camp.
translation_verse: Tinan nìn dáá kā bi-nyɔmmun baa láá ŋmɔ́ ki náĺ ní ti-Dindaan ŋuul yíkì bi-pu ní u dáaĺ bi-tafal ŋkpitim pu.

english_verse: After they had buried the people who had been so greedy for meat, they called the place “Graves for the Greedy.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn pú niin diyindi yii Kiibirooti-Taafa, an taapu di sá yii: <Nneel kaakuliŋ>, di sá niin ní bi nìn síb́ binib bin nìn gbí nneel tikpilee.

english_verse: and told Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to come to the entrance of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Kpalaayee ní ti-Dindaan yíiń Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì Miiriyam ki bí-bi yii: «Ni-taatil ń dāan̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu.» Ní bi nyáń ki búntì.

english_verse: There the Lord appeared in a cloud and told Aaron and Miriam to come closer.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sīntìń ditagbancancaal poon ki yúl̀ tanti punyɔkɔpu. Ní ki yíiń Aarɔn nì Miiriyam, ní bi-liitil nyáń ki síl̀.

english_verse: Then after commanding them to listen carefully, he said: “I, the Lord, speak to prophets in visions and dreams.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-bi yii: «Ní pīlifì tin m cáá kí tùkù-ni nee tiŋan. Ni-kansikin m-bɔnaatiliu yaa bée, an sá nì dileedakal nì tidamintiil poon ní man ni-Dindaan lèekī m-ba ki dàkà-u, ní ki sòoǹ nì u.

english_verse: But my servant Moses is the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Ama m-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi úǹ cee kaa sá míǹ. Úǹ kpèé m-nibul mmɔntiim ní ki bí deedee.

english_verse: He sees me face to face, and everything I say to him is perfectly clear. You have no right to criticize my servant Moses.”
translation_verse: M yú u-nimbiin ní ki sòoǹ nì u, ní ki cántí-u tikɔkɔ ní u wāĺ man ni-Dindaan naŋku. Ba pu ní naa fāŋkì m-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi ní ki kpákáǹ-u míǹ?»

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Aaron and Miriam. And after the Lord left
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan fōō bi-pu diŋuul, ní ki fātìi nín jɔ́ḿ.

english_verse: and the cloud disappeared from over the sacred tent, Miriam's skin turned white with leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her,
translation_verse: Ditagbandee tin lì yii dì yíkí tanti puee, Miiriyam wunti pu dinyaŋgbampindi píń ki pīiǹ kii ntaayimee. Aarɔn fātìi kpēēyee dinyaŋgbandi píń Miiriyam pu.

english_verse: he said to Moses, “Sir, please don't punish us for doing such a foolish thing.
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn bí Mooyiisi yii: «M-kpiliu, m gbàam̄-si, taa pà-ti ti-kpitii in ti-gbaandi yāntì ti ŋá-see paati.

english_verse: Don't let Miriam's flesh rot away like a child born dead!”
translation_verse: Taa yàntī Miiriyam ń kpántí kii kibiki kin kpíì ki-na poon ki-wunti dijandi sūū ki wāatì bi nín màl̄-kèe.»

english_verse: Moses prayed, “Lord God, please heal her.”
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi mēē ti-Dindaan nì dinimbinaamandi yii: «Unimbɔti, m gbàam̄-si, cáaǹ Miiriyam!»

english_verse: But the Lord replied, “Miriam would be disgraced for seven days if her father had punished her by spitting in her face. So make her stay outside the camp for seven days, before coming back.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «U-baa di yaa bàà tíil̀ ki làb̄ u-nimbiin nee, icoo kaa bàà cútí-u áli iwiin ilulaaa? Míǹ puee an sá ní nyāntí-u dinaapaalin ú nīn bí ŋkpaanceeti áli iwiin iluli, ní boonee ú fàtīí gítiń samaa kansikin.»

english_verse: The people of Israel did not move their camp until Miriam returned seven days later.
translation_verse: Niinee bi nyántì Miiriyam dinaapaal poon iwiin iluli. Samaa kaa nìn yíkì dinaapaal pu, see u nín dāa fātìi gítìńee.

english_verse: Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp in the Paran Desert.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní samaa yíkì Aseerooti ní ki cūtìi ŋātì dinaapaal Paaran teekun ki kāl̀.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: In fact, we saw the Nephilim who are the ancestors of the Anakim. They were so big that we felt as small as grasshoppers.”
translation_verse: Ti ká Anaaki naantiibi tijawɔkɔl niin, ní ti yaa kpēē ti-bee, timbi sá kii inaakitoonee ní bi-cee. Míǹ ní bi mun wāĺ-ti yii ti sá.»

english_verse: “Choose a leader from each tribe and send them into Canaan to explore the land I am giving you.”
translation_verse: «Tɔ̄ binib bí cùú cɔ̄ŋkì Kanaan tiŋki kin m làá dūú tīī Isirayeel yabee. Lēē kunaakoou kamaa poon ukpil ubɔ kí tɔ̄.»

english_verse: So Moses sent twelve tribal leaders from Israel's camp in the Paran Desert
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn lēē-bi ki tú, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn lī puee doooo Paaran teekun. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn sá Isirayeel yab kpilib ní.

english_verse: Before Moses sent them into Canaan, he said: After you go through the Southern Desert of Canaan, continue north into the hill country
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Mooyiisi làá nìn tɔ̄-bi bí nīn cée ní u bí-bi yii: «Ní dī doo ki jɔ̄m̀ Neegeeb, an dàkà yii ŋgiil pú, ní kí tin dàb̄ ajoon kí nyā Kanaan.

english_verse: and find out what those regions are like. Be sure to remember how many people live there, how strong they are,
translation_verse: Ní cɔ̄ŋkì kí kpèè yii kitiŋ gbanti bí mana, kí kpèè yii ki-nib pɔ̄ɔ̄yaaa, baa pɔ̄ɔ̄, kí kpèè yii ki-nib wīikáaa, baa wīikí.

english_verse: and if they live in open towns or walled cities. See if the land is good for growing crops and find out what kinds of trees grow there. It's time for grapes to ripen, so try to bring back some of the fruit that grows there.
translation_verse: Ní kpèè yii kitiŋ gbanti cáá ntiŋkpamaaa, kaa cáá, kí kpèè yii isufi nyēē tiŋanaaa, iaa nyēē. Kámaan dipɔbil kí nīn cá, ni yaa gítińee ní lēeń niin subiliŋ kí cáań.» An nìn sá ŋyunti ŋun ní fiinyi lòoǹ abipeepeekaayee ní.

english_verse: The twelve men left to explore Canaan from the Zin Desert in the south all the way to the town of Rehob near Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Ní bi búntì ki cūtìi cɔ́ŋkì Kanaan tiŋki ki kíĺ Siini teekun áli ki tin bàn̄ Leeyoob-Amati caŋin.

english_verse: As they went through the Southern Desert, they came to the town of Hebron, which was seven years older than the Egyptian town of Zoan. In Hebron, they saw the three Anakim clans of Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dī ki jɔ́m̀ Neegeeb pú, ki tin bàn̄ Eebrɔn, laakin Anaaki nibul nì Ayiiman yab nì Seesayi yab nì Talimayi yab nìn kóòyee. - Bi nìn máń Eebrɔn tiŋki abin aluli boon ní bi dāa nín náań Soowan tiŋki Eejipiti tiŋkin. -

english_verse: When they got to Bunch Valley, they cut off a branch with such a huge bunch of grapes, that it took two men to carry it on a pole. That's why the place was called Bunch Valley. Along with the grapes, they also took back pomegranates and figs. The Men Report Back to the People
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín nìn gāań fiinyi biliŋ disakalee pu ní bi pú niin diyindi yii Eeskool, taapu di sá yii: <Disakal tantakal>. Bin Mooyiisi túee gítìń ki cáań tin bi kée

english_verse: the twelve men returned to Kadesh in the Paran Desert and told Moses, Aaron, and the people what they had seen. They showed them the fruit
translation_verse: Bi bāańee ní ki cūtìi ká Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ Kaadeesi, Paaran teekun, ní ki máafì-bi tin kɔkɔ bi kée, ní ki dū kitiŋee poon subiliŋ ki dàkā-bi.

english_verse: and said: Look at this fruit! The land we explored is rich with milk and honey.
translation_verse: Tin bi nìn dɔ́miń ki máafì Mooyiisee sèé: «Ti nín bàn̄ kitiŋ kin poon a tú-tee, tiŋman nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ ní. Kpèè abil ŋin kì lòoǹee.

english_verse: But the people who live there are strong, and their cities are large and walled. We even saw the three Anakim clans.
translation_verse: Ama binib bin kóò kitiŋ gbantinee cáá mpɔn tikpil, ní bi máń aguŋkpaan ki māntìi tú bi-timmu. Ti ká gba kujawɔkɔu Anaaki naantiibi niin.

english_verse: Besides that, the Amalekites live in the Southern Desert; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites are in the hill country; and the Canaanites live along the Mediterranean Sea and the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Amaleeki yab kóò Neegeeb, ní Eeti yab nì Jeebusi yab nì Amɔɔr yab kóò dijool pu, ní Kanaan yab kóò dimɔɔl caŋin nì Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi.»

english_verse: Caleb calmed down the crowd and said, “Let's go and take the land. I know we can do it!”
translation_verse: Ní Kaaleeb céefì samaa un bíi kpākantí Mooyiisee ń ŋmīĺ, ní u bí-bi yii: «Tí cùmaan, ti làá já kí fōō kitiŋ gbanti, kun puee ti làá ŋmā kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ ki-nib!»

english_verse: But the other men replied, “Those people are much too strong for us.”
translation_verse: Ama bin nì Kaaleeb nìn cūtì ki cɔ́ŋkì kitiŋee bí yii: «Taa ŋūǹ kí cùú já nì binib nee, bi pɔ̄ɔǹ-ti sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ ní.»

english_verse: Then they started spreading rumors and saying, “We won't be able to grow anything in that soil. And the people are like giants.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ ki bíiĺ kitiŋ kin bi cūtìi cɔ́ŋkèe Isirayeel yab nimbiin. Bi nìn lī yii: «Kitiŋ kin ti cūtìi cōom̀ ki cɔ́ŋkèe nátí ki-nib bin kóò ki-puee, ní binib bin ti ká niinee sá tinikpaandi.

english_verse: and complained to Moses and Aaron, “We wish we had died in Egypt or somewhere out here in the desert!
translation_verse: Samaayee kɔkɔ nìn bí ki wòoǹ Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn ní ki lì-bi yii: «Ti yaa bàà nìn kpíìń Eejipiti tiŋkin àá ti yaa tí kpíì kuteeun doo, an bàà sɔ́!

english_verse: Is the Lord leading us into Canaan, just to have us killed and our women and children captured? We'd be better off in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan cáǹ-ti kitiŋ nee poon bí tin kpɔ̀-ti ní? Bi làá tin kpɔ̀-ti ní kí cúú ti-nimpoobi nì ti-biyaamu kuyuŋu. Ti yaa fātìi nín gítí Eejipiti, an kaa sɔ́ɔɔ?»

english_verse: Then they said to one another, “Let's choose our own leader and go back.”
translation_verse: Ní bi bí ki lì tɔb yii: «Tí kàam̄maan ukpil ubɔ kí nīn gítí Eejipiti!»

english_verse: Moses and Aaron bowed down to pray in front of the crowd.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil Isirayeel yab samaau kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_verse: and said: We saw the land ourselves, and it's very good.
translation_verse: ní ki bí Isirayeel yab samaau kɔkɔ yii: «Kitiŋ kin ti cūtìi yìin̄ ki kpēēyee sá kitimmɔmmɔntii ní!

english_verse: If we obey the Lord, he will surely give us that land rich with milk and honey.
translation_verse: An sá kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee ní. Ti-Dindaan yaa yú ti-boon, u làá kɔ́ǹ-ti ki-poon kí dū-kì kí tīī-ti.

english_verse: So don't rebel. We have no reason to be afraid of the people who live there. The Lord is on our side, and they won't stand a chance against us!
translation_verse: Tin páb́ee di sá ní taa jáǹ ti-Dindaan, kí taa fàŋkì kitiŋ gbanti nib. Ti làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ. Di sá bi-waaŋi ŋin cí-bee dū-bi ki fá, ama ní timbi Dindaan bí ti-cee. An puee taa fàŋkìmaan-bi.»

english_verse: The crowd threatened to stone Moses and Aaron to death. But just then, the Lord appeared in a cloud at the sacred tent. Moses Prays for the People
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun samaa kɔkɔ bíi màkafī kí yāŋkì-bi ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀ee ní ti-Dindaan nyooti dɔ́miń circir kɔŋkooŋŋun Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin. Mooyiisi gbāam̀ samaa pu

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I have done great things for these people, and they still reject me by refusing to believe in my power.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní dinibul nee làá gbèen̄ kí taa ti kpèè-mi fám ní? Kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní bi làá yíí kí taa nín̄ cáá m-pu dimákal, nì min kɔkɔ m ŋá maamaacikpaambi bin bí nee bi-kansikinee?

english_verse: So they will no longer be my people. I will destroy them, but I will make you the ancestor of a nation even stronger than theirs.”
translation_verse: M làá yàntī bìlbil kúm ń dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí bi-kɔkɔ, ní bí lóó bi-fakal ní m dī sii pu kí náań ditimbuŋkpaandi din cáá mpɔn ki jítiǹ-bee.»

english_verse: Show us your great power, Lord. You promised
translation_verse: Míǹ puee m gbàam̄-si, m-Dindaan, nyāntí a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu kí dàkà, kii sii a-ba nín lī puee yii:

english_verse: that you love to show mercy and kindness. And you said that you are very patient, but that you will punish everyone guilty of doing wrong—not only them but their children and grandchildren as well.
translation_verse: <M sá ni-Dindaan un kaa gífí diŋuul malaayee, ní m-ŋanti wīikí tikpil. M pūǹ ikpiti kɔkɔ nì i-bulifi. Ama maa tàantí unikpiti kaa dáaĺ u-tafal. M dátí unikpiti tafal kí tin kpáaǹ u-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ ata àá anaa.>

english_verse: You are merciful, and you treat people better than they deserve. So please forgive these people, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, kii a-ŋanti nín wīikí puee, dū a-nibul nee kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, kii doooo a nín nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin bi pée ŋáań-si ikpiti a cáa pūǹ-bi puee.»

english_verse: But as surely as I live and my power has no limit,
translation_verse: Ama tiŋman, m nín bí dimaŋfalin ní m-nyooti gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu nee,

english_verse: I swear that not one of these Israelites will enter the land I promised to give their ancestors. These people have seen my power in Egypt and in the desert, but they will never see Canaan. They have disobeyed and tested me too many times.
translation_verse: bi-kansikin ubɔ kpá kí kɔ́ kitiŋ kin m pōoǹ bi-baabi yii m làá tīī-bee. Bin kɔkɔ pée kpēē-mi fámee kpá kí kɔ́ ki-poon.

english_verse: But my servant Caleb isn't like the others. So because he has faith in me, I will allow him to cross into Canaan, and his descendants will settle there.
translation_verse: Ama kii ŋfam min kpòotī m-tɔntɔnliu Kaaleebee nín nyáń mi-ba u nóó-mi deedee puee, m làá yàntī ú kɔ́ kitiŋ kin u cūtìi kpēēyee poon, ní u-naantiibi ń dāá jī-kì.

english_verse: Now listen, Moses! The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valleys of Canaan. And tomorrow, you'll need to turn around and head back into the desert toward the Red Sea. The Israelites Are Punished for Complaining
translation_verse: Amaleeki yab nì Kanaan yab di dá láá kóò kitiŋ gbantin. Foolee ní fu fàtī ni-boon kí dūú dī kuteeun, Tikati mɔɔl watil.» Ti-Dindaan dáaĺ u-nibul tafal

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii:

english_verse: to give this message to the people of Israel: You sinful people have complained against me too many times! Now I swear by my own life that I will give you exactly what you wanted.
translation_verse: Ní tùkù-bi yii: <Man ni-Dindaan bí dimaŋfalin. M pūtì ki lī yii, ni nín pée sòon̄-mi puee, míǹ ní m làá téeǹ-ni.

english_verse: You will die right here in the desert, and your dead bodies will cover the ground. You have insulted me, and none of you men who are over
translation_verse: Kuteeun doo ní ni làá gbíntí kí kpú. Nimbi bin kɔkɔ bi nìn kàan̄ ni cáá abin mmuŋku kí nīn cée làá kpú ní, kun puee ni kɔ́kɔl̀-mi.

english_verse: will enter the land that I solemnly promised to give you as your own—only Caleb and Joshua will go in.
translation_verse: M pūtì yii naa làá kɔ́ kitiŋ kin m nìn pōoǹ yii m làá kàan̄-nee poon. See Yeefunee jipɔɔn Kaaleeb nì Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa baba di làá kɔ́.

english_verse: You were worried that your own children would be captured. But I, the Lord, will let them enter the land you have rejected.
translation_verse: Ni-biyaamu mun pu ni lī yii bi làá kpɔ̀-ni kí yòon̄ee, múǹ ní m làá yàntī mú kɔ́ kí béé kitiŋ kin nimbi kpēē ki sīŋkiǹee.

english_verse: You will die here in the desert!
translation_verse: Nimbee, ni làá gbíntí kuteeun doo ní kí kpú.

english_verse: So they got up early the next morning and got ready to head toward the hill country of Canaan. They said, “We were wrong to complain about the Lord. Let's go into the land that he promised us.”
translation_verse: Ku wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní bi yíkì ki cūtìi jɔ́m̀ ajoon pu tiŋki, ní ki bí yii: «Ti lafun ŋá ikpiti, ama kɔŋkɔnnee ti làá cù kí jáǹ binib gbanti kii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee.»

english_verse: Ten of the men sent to explore the land had brought back bad news and had made the people complain against the Lord.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn tú binib bi cūtìi kpēē Kanaan tiŋki. Bi nìn gítìńee ní ki sòon̄ ki bíil̀-kì ki yāntì samaa bíi wòoǹ Mooyiisi.

english_verse: but he let Joshua and Caleb live. The Israelites Fail To Enter Canaan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa nì Yeefunee jipɔɔn Kaaleeb baba di nìn kíǹ bin bi nìn tú bi cūtìi kpēē kitiŋee kansikin kaa kpíì. Samaa tí yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan

english_verse: But Moses replied, “You're disobeying the Lord! Your plan won't work,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni bíi yìntī ti-Dindaan marau míǹ? Ni yaa cūtì naa làá ŋmā.

english_verse: The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down from the hill country, defeated the Israelites, and chased them as far as the town of Hormah.
translation_verse: Ní Amaleeki yab nì Kanaan yab kpákatìń ajoon tiŋki pu, ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Isirayeel yab sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ, ní ki jìn̄ bin kíǹee ki tin bàn̄ Ɔrima tiŋki.

english_verse: The people of Israel were very sad after Moses gave them the Lord's message.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi cáań tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì uee ki tùkū Isirayeel yab, ní kunimbaakpaaŋŋu kɔ́-bi.

english_verse: so don't even try it. The Lord refuses to help you, because you turned your backs on him. The Amalekites and the Canaanites are your enemies, and they will attack and defeat you.”
translation_verse: Di sá Amaleeki yab nì Kanaan yab bí ni-nyɔkɔpu. Ni yaa cūtì bi làá kpɔ̀-ni. Ni nín fātì ni-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaanee, waa ti bí ni-cee.»

english_verse: But the Israelites ignored Moses and marched toward the hill country, even though the sacred chest and Moses did not go with them.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee bi ŋá ŋyipɔn ki nín jɔ́ḿ ajoon pu tiŋkin, ama ti-Dindaan dakaau nì Mooyiisi nìn gbíntì dinaapaal pu kaa cūtì.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: Bulls or rams or goats are the animals that you may burn on the altar as sacrifices to please me. You may also offer sacrifices voluntarily or because you made a promise, or because they are part of your regular religious ceremonies. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: ní dāá ŋá-mi saraabi. Ní dāá ŋá-mi saraawɔkaa àá mpèé saraabi kí pà ipoon àá an nīn sá nlammɔntiim saraau, àá ni-jiŋaalib yuntiŋuee. Ní dāá dū unaa àá upii àá uŋoobu kí ŋá an saraabi, ní u-sɔnsɔfiŋu ń sɔ̀ŋkì m-pɔbil.

english_verse: If you sacrifice a young ram or goat, you must also offer a kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil as a grain sacrifice. A liter of wine must also be poured on the altar.
translation_verse: Bi yaa làá dū dipibil kí ŋá saraawɔkaa àá mpèé saraauee, bí dū ndamam liitiri ubɔ nì dijandi kí kūtì kí ŋá saraa.

english_verse: If a bull is offered as a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing,
translation_verse: An yaa tí sá unaja ní bi làá dūú ŋá saraawɔkaa àá mpèé saraau kí pà ipoon àá án nīn sá nlammɔntiim saraau kí tīī-mee,

english_verse: you must offer three kilograms of flour mixed with two liters of olive oil.
translation_verse: bí dū ŋyim kiiloobi biwa, kí dū ŋkpam liitirib bita kí búuń ní kí dūú kūtì kuwaŋkuluu pu kí ŋá saraa.

english_verse: Two liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: Ní dū ndamam liitirib bita kí kūtì, ní u-sɔnsɔfiŋu ń sɔ̀ŋkì m-pɔbil.

english_verse: If you are a native Israelite, you must obey these rules each time you offer a bull, a ram, or a goat as a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ máaǹ kí nóó mara un m síiǹ nee kí ŋá saraabi bin nyiim sɔ́fèe kí tīī-mi.

english_verse: This law will never change. I am the Lord, and I consider all people the same, whether they are Israelites or foreigners living among you.
translation_verse: Marabaanti nì dibɔkpaal dibaantiil ní án làá nīn sá ki tīī nimbi bin sá bitindambee nì binicambi bin kɔ́ ni-puee kɔkɔ.» Bikpɔnɔpeepeekaabi saraau

english_verse: When you eat food in the land that I am giving you, remember to set aside some of it as an offering to me.
translation_verse: ní ki kíǹ ki jīǹ kitiŋ gbanti jintee, ní dāá lēē tijinee poon kí ŋá saraa kí tīī-mi.

english_verse: From the first batch of bread dough that you make after each new grain harvest, make a loaf of bread and offer it to me, just as you offer grain.
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa nùkū kpɔnɔ saabuee, ní dāá lēē dipál din ni péé péé ki nùkūee poon ki ŋá ŋkalaawaamu. Ní dāá lēē kii bi nín yaa gbáń tijimpin ki cāatì bi nín lèekī kí ŋá saraa kí tīī-mi puee.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses to tell the people what must be done if they ever disobey his laws:
translation_verse: an dàkà yii tin kɔkɔ man ni-Dindaan dī Mooyiisi pu ki ŋmàn̄ ki kpáafì ni nì ni-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ ní nīn ŋúb́ kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun ní u ŋmàn̄-tèe kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaanee.

english_verse: If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: An yaa sá yii udaan yīntì míǹ ní samaa kaa béèyee, samaayee di làá dū unaja kí ŋá saraawɔkaa, ní u-sɔnsɔfiŋu ń sɔ̀ŋkì m-pɔbil. Ú ŋá tijin nì ndaam saraau mun kii dikoobil nín sá puee, ní kí dū uŋɔja kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau.

english_verse: the sin of everyone—both Israelites and foreigners among you—will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ nì binicambi bin kóò bi-kansikinee làá ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam, kun puee bi-kɔkɔ di ŋá ikpiti gbanti.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Unibaanti di yaa kaa nyí ní ki ŋá ikpitee, ú dū uŋɔsal un cáá dibindi dibee kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau.

english_verse: The priest will then ask me to forgive you, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ń ŋá un kaa nyí ki yīntèe pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée man nimbiin, ní udaan ń ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.

english_verse: The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
translation_verse: An yaa sá Isirayeel yabaaa, binicambi bin kóò bi-kansikineeyaaa, mara nee làá nīn pée sá ubaanti ní ki tīī bin kɔkɔ kaa nyí ní ki yīntèe.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong on purpose, whether Israelite or foreigner, you have sinned against me by disobeying my laws. You will no longer belong to my people. A Man Put to Death for Gathering Firewood on the Sabbath
translation_verse: Udaan nín kpēē man ni-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi fám ki yīntì m-marabee puee, bí nyāntí-u. Udaan làá túń u-kpitii gìńdi. Un yīntì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa marauee tafadaaldi

english_verse: Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín nìn dáá bí kuteeun puee, bi nìn ká uninja ubɔ bí ki píikí idɔ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal.

english_verse: He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community.
translation_verse: Bin nìn ká-u u bíi píikí idɔee cúú-u ki cáań Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì samaa kɔkɔ cee.

english_verse: But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dá láá dū-u ki kāaǹ ki cí-u tiŋan, kun puee baa nìn dá láá nyí un yīntì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa marauee nín máaǹ ditafadaaldi diŋyee.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí Mooyiisi yii: «An niliuee máaǹ ŋkúm ní. Bí nyāntí-u dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu samaa kɔkɔ ń yāŋkì-u ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀.»

english_verse: So he was killed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Tassels on the People's Clothes
translation_verse: Samaa kɔkɔ nìn nyántì-u dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu ki yáŋkì-u ataŋkpee ki kūū, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Mooyiisi yii bí ŋá puee. Abɔkuti gbeeŋgbeeŋyi bɔti

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Sew tassels onto the bottom edge of your clothes and tie a blue string to each tassel.
translation_verse: ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Kí yòon̄ nimbi nì ni-naantiibi bin bí ki dòońee, ni yaa làá ŋáĺ abɔkutee, ní dāá ŋá igbeeŋgbeen tibɔkutijúti pu kí dū gulfaman kí kúĺ.

english_verse: These will remind you that you must obey my laws and teachings. And when you do, you will be dedicated to me and won't follow your own sinful desires.
translation_verse: Án làá yàntī ní téetí m-marab kɔkɔ pu kí nīn tɔ́-bi, ní kí nīn sá man ni-Nimbɔtiu yab.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God who led you out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin kí nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiuee. Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.»

english_verse: Korah son of Izhar was a Levite from the Kohathite clan. One day he called together Dathan, Abiram, and On from the Reuben tribe, and the four of them decided to rebel against Moses. So they asked
translation_verse: Bi nìn bóob́ kí jáǹ Mooyiisi, ní bi ká Isirayeel yab kansikin bin sá abɔtibil nì binikpaambi bin samaa nìn lēē bi kpáfí ki sòoǹ tibɔtee binib alaataa ali nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa ki kútì bi-ba pu.

english_verse: and Aaron and said, “Why do you think you're so much better than everyone else? We're part of the Lord's holy people, and he's with all of us. What makes you think you're the only ones in charge?”
translation_verse: Ní bi dɔ́miń ki kpáfì ki māntìi tú Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ni nín ŋáań puee gíti lákatì tikpil! Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ bí circir ní ti-Dindaan bí ti-kɔkɔ kansikin. Ba pu ní nimbi dàkafī yii ni jítiǹ ti-Dindaan nibul kɔkɔ ní?»

english_verse: When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nín gbìl̄ bi bíi wòoǹ-u mimmee ní u tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil,

english_verse: Then he said to Korah and his followers: Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
translation_verse: ní ki bí Kooree nì u-yabee yii: «Fool kutaafaauee, ti-Dindaan làá fu yàntī tí béé un sá u-yɔuee, un u dūu sú u-ba ú nīn sútí ki pìl̀-uee. U làá fu yàntī un u lēēyee ń sútí kí pìl̄-u.

english_verse: Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
translation_verse: Ní fu mɔ́fí ŋŋmi kí ŋá poon, kí dū talaalutuukaa kí páań ŋŋmi pu kí yóoń ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Niin ní ti làá fu béé un ti-Dindaan lēē ú nīn sá u-yɔuee. Nimbi Leefii yabee, m gīiǹ ni-bɔti!»

english_verse: You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want?
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lēē-ni ni-nabiyaamu kansikin ní nīn sútí ki pìl̀-u, kí nīn tūǹ atuun ni-nabiyaamu yil pu circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, an kaa yá kí kɔ́-naaa?

english_verse: The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest.
translation_verse: U yāntì sii Kooree nì a-nabiyaamu Leefii yab sútí ki pìl̀-u ní ni gíti bí ki nyàab̀ disaraaŋal tundaa!

english_verse: You and your followers have rebelled against the Lord, not against Aaron.
translation_verse: An pu ní sii nì a-naacimbi bóob́ kí jáǹ ti-Dindaanaa! Di sá yii, ŋma di sá Aarɔn ní ni kpākantí-u?»

english_verse: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come!
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi tú bí yíiń Eeliyaab jipɔmbi Daatan nì Abiiram, ní bíǹ kíí yii: «Taa làá dāan̄!

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: A yōoǹní-ti kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee ki cáań-ti kí kpɔ̀ kuteeun doo, míǹ kaa yá ki kɔ́-si, ní a gíti là kí dàkà mpɔn kí nīn sá ti-bɔtiuaa!

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní u fōō diŋuul tikpil ní ki bí ti-Dindaan yii: «Á taa fōō bi-saraau. Man kaa fōō bi-kansikin ubɔ maŋki kpaŋkpan. Maa tí ŋá bi-kansikin báà ubɔ ikpiti.» Kooree nì u-naacimbi tafadaaldi

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Kooree yii: «Sii nì a-naacimbi ń fu dāan̄ kí yūĺ ti-Dindaan nimbiin, Aarɔn mun làá fu nín̄ bí.

english_verse: Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Sii nì a-naacimbi binib alaataa ali nì imuŋku ili nì saalaayee, báà ŋma ń fu nín̄ ŋúb́ u-sambiki kin poon u ŋáań talaalutuukaayee nì talaalu kí cáań ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Sii nì Aarɔn mun ń nīn ŋúb́ ni-yɔmu.»

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ní Kooree nì u-naacimbi lafun ŋúbiń bi-sambiyaamu mun poon bi ŋáań talaalutuukaayee, ki ŋá ŋŋmi poon, ní ki dū talaalutuukaa ki sītì poon, ní ki cūtìi yúl̀ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu, bi nì Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Ní Kooree kpáfì Isirayeel samaau bi yú ki túĺ Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu. Ní ti-Dindaan lēē u-nyooti ki dàkā samaa kɔkɔ.

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii:

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: «Ní kàkatī ni-ba kí wàatī binib nee, di sá m làá kúntí-bi dibɔbil pu doo!»

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ní ki bíi kūuntí yii: «Óo Unimbɔti, sii un tìì tiwannáaŋkaal kɔkɔ dimaŋfalee, unibaanti kpitii puee, a làá fōō samaa nee kɔkɔ pu diŋuulaaa?»

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: «Á tùkù samaa un kóò ki pìl̄ Kooree nì Daatan nì Abiiramee yii bí kàkatī kí wàatī-bi.»

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi yíkì, ní Isirayeel yab kpilib páaǹ u-boon ní bi nín cá Daatan nì Abiiram cee.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Ní u bí samaa yii: «Ní kàkatīmaan kí wàatī binikpitib nee tantib, kí taa gbēē bi-wanti báà tiba, án nín làá ŋá pu bi-kpitii puee, ní taa kpúee.»

english_verse: So everyone moved away from those tents, except Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and their families.
translation_verse: Ní bin kóò ki pìl̄ Kooree nì Daatan nì Abiiramee yíkìi wāatì-bi. Ní Daatan nì Abiiram nyáń ki yú bi-tantib nyɔkɔpu, bi nì bi-nimpoobi nì bi-biyaamu nì bi-naantiibi.

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí yii: «Tin làá ŋá nee di làá yàntī ní béé yii ti-Dindaan di túnní-mi ḿ nīn tūǹ atuun ŋin bí nee kɔkɔ. An kaa sá man m-ba pɔŋŋu pu.

english_verse: If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me.
translation_verse: Binib nee yaa kpíì kii báà ŋma wiiŋŋu nín bà ú kpú puee, mimmee ti-Dindaan di kaa túnní-mi.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan yaa ŋá maamaaci tundi, kitiŋ dū bi nì tin bi cááyee kɔkɔ ki náĺ, bi yaa sīntì ditaŋkpiilin nì bi-nimbiliŋee, míǹ di làá dàkà-ni yii bi bēel̀ ti-Dindaan.»

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Mooyiisi tin pée lì yii u sòoǹ ki ŋmīlifée, laakin bi yúee, kitiŋ cúu látì bi-taaŋi taapu,

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Bi pée wāĺ ní ki sīntì ditaŋkpiilin bi nì bi-wanti kɔkɔ, kitiŋ bīiǹ bi-pu ní baa ti ká-bi Isirayeel yab kansikin.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin nìn yú ki pìl̄-bee nín gbìl̄ bi bí ki gbáà ibiilee ní bi sáǹ ki lì yii: «Tí sām̀maan kitiŋ ń taa kpáaǹ ti mun kí náĺ!»

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: Call together the twelve tribes of Israel and tell the leader of each tribe to write his name on the walking stick he carries as a symbol of his authority. Make sure Aaron's name is written on the one from the Levi tribe, then collect all the sticks.
translation_verse: Nì min kɔkɔ bin yì nsambiyaamuee ŋá ikpiti ní ki kpíìyee, bi nìn cáań-mu man cee ní m ŋá-mu circir. Bí dùntī-mu kí gbá kí kpátí kí wàan̄ bí nīn cáa bìintí nsaraafan pu. Mu làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu ki tīī Isirayeel yab ní.»

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar yōoǹ tasa kúti sambiyaamu mun binib bin ŋŋmi wùn̄ee nìn ŋúb́ee ki dūntì ki gbáń ki kpátì ki wāaǹ ki dūu bīiǹ nsaraafan pu.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Tibiiŋkaal gbanti làá nīn téetí Isirayeel yab yii unil un kamaa di yaa kaa sá Aarɔn dicaŋkunee kaa cáá nsan kí tūū talaalu ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Un kamaa yaa mākaǹee, tin nìn jítì Kooree nì u-naacimbi puee di làá jītí udaan pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī Mooyiisi pu ki lī puee. Samaa tí bíi kpākantí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ tí bíi wòoǹ Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii: «Nimbi di yāntì ti-Dindaan nibul kpíì».

english_verse: The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn sútìi pìl̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu,

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: U yúl̀ bin kpíìyee nì bin dáá wāĺee kansikin, ní ditafadaaldi gbēeǹ.

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Á dū a-nabiyaamu Leefii yab bin sá a-baa naakookun yabee kí ŋàl̄ a-ba bí nīn bí a-taapu ki tútúǹ-si atuun, ní si nì a-jipɔmbi ń nīn kpèé circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon tuuŋŋi.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Bi làá nín bí a-taapu ní ki kpèé circir kɔŋkooŋŋu. Ama bí taa gbēē circir wanti nì nsaraafan pu wanti tiba, án nín làá ŋá pu si nì bi ń taa kpúee.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Bi làá nīn bí a-cee ní kí nīn tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ. Un kaa sá Leefii naakookunee ń taa cèeǹ ni-kansikin.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Sii nì a-jipɔmbi di làá nīn tūǹ circir laŋki nì nsaraafan pu tuuŋŋi, mimmee m-ŋuul kaa làá yīkì Isirayeel yab pu.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Man di lēē a-nabiyaamu Leefii yab Isirayeel yab kansikin bí nīn sá man yab. Ní m dū-bi ki tīī-ni bí nín tūǹ dikpafindi tantiu poon tuuŋŋi.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ama sii Aarɔn nì a-jipɔmbee, nimbi làá nīn tūǹ disaraaŋal tundi nsaraafan pu nì circir páaa laŋki ŋŋaapìtikaa boon. Disaraaŋal tundi gbantee, man di pú-ni-dì. Un kaa sá Leefii naakookunee yaa sútìi pìl̄-dèe, udaan làá kpú ní.» Tin sá usaraaŋakpil yatee

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Tinanee sii di yì, kii a nín tí yì dibindi nì diŋaŋgiitaal din bi dūu ŋá-mi mpèé saraauee puee.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Saraabi bin sá circir bi cáań-mi ki dū dijandi ki wùn̄ ŋŋmee, tin kíǹ baa wùn̄ ki sá nimbi yatee sèé. Tijin saraabi nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabi nì dibɔkpil saraabi. Tiwan gbanti kɔkɔee sá circir ní. Ní yòon̄, sii nì a-jipɔmbi yati dee.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Ní jī saraabi gbanti jinti laakin bí circiree. Uninja kamaa ŋūǹ kí jī-tì, tiwan gbanti ń nīn sá circir a-cee.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: Ní dū ti nee mun kí kūtì. Tiwampɔkaal tin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab cāabìń-mee, sii di yì. M dūu tīī sii nì a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. An sá mara ní m yóoǹ. A-dicaŋku poon bin kɔkɔ bí circiree ŋūǹ kí jī an jinti.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: M dū tijincɔ̀fikaal tin bi làá cáań-mee, ŋkpam nì ndamam nì bilee ki tīī-si.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kpaajinti ticɔfikaal tin bi làá cáań-mee, a-dicaŋku poon un kamaa bí circiree ŋūǹ kí jī an jinti.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: Tin kamaa ní Isirayeel yab cáań ki sú-mee, sii di yì.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Mbiseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu mun bi cāabìń ki ŋáań-mi saraayee, an yaa sá binibeeee, tiwaŋkuteeee, sii di yì. Ama á yàntī bí pà mbininjabiyaamu yil pu, kí pà tiwaŋkuti tin kaa ŋān̄ bí dūú ŋá saraayee mun yil pu.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Bí pà kibininjabiki kin cáá uŋmal ubɔee yil pu jitɔmbi biŋmoo, kí nóó nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nimbiliŋ ŋmàntitam, nnyiŋfi ń nīn sá graambi saalaa.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Ama bí taa pà unaa nì upii nì uŋoobu biseemaliŋ pu. Tíǹ sá ki tīī man ní, bí làntì-tì ní kí dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan pu, ní kí dū ti-kpam kí wà ŋŋmi, ní nsɔnsɔfi ń sɔ̀ŋkì m-pɔbil.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Circir wanti tin kɔkɔ pu ní Isirayeel yab làá lēē kí ŋá-mi saraayee, m dūu tīī sii nì a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib ní. An sá mpèé ŋun m dū ŋyaam ki ŋá ki tīī sii nì a-maaliŋuee ní, yii sii nì a-biyaamu nì a-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ di làá nīn pée yì an wanti kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Mara gbanti kpá kí kpìtī man a-Dindaan nimbiin.»

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Aarɔn yii: «Maa làá tīī-si ditinjandi, kii m nín làá tīī Isirayeel yab atinjan puee. Man di sá sii jandi nì a-gaajati Isirayeel yab kansikin.» Leefii yab jandi din sá bí tīī-bee

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: «An yaa kíǹ Leefii yabee, difakal din m làá tīī-bee di sá Isirayeel yab nín tìì tisaalaatiil tin kɔkɔee. Án nīn sá bi-paati bi nín bí ki tūǹ ditundi din circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee pu.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Leefii yab baba di làá nīn bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki tūǹ atuun. Bíǹ di dāa yì bi-yìntitam tafadaaldi. An sá mara ní m yóoǹ kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Leefii yab kaa cáá kí fōō Isirayeel yab kansikin ditinjandi.

english_verse: they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me. What the Levites Must Give
translation_verse: Ama m làá dū tisaalaatiil tin Isirayeel yab lèekī ki cāabìń-mee ní kí tīī-bi difakal. An pu ní m bí yii baa làá nīn cáá ditinjandi kii Isirayeel yab naakɔti tin kíǹee nín làá nīn cáá puee.»

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: ń tùkù Leefii yab yii: «Isirayeel yab yaa láa lēeń bi-saalaatiiti ki tīī-nee, ni mun ń dāá fàtīí lēē poon tisaalaatiil kí ŋá man saraa.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Ni yaa lēē míǹ ki tīīyee, ni mun ŋá kii ni-jutiibi nín lèekī bi-kpaajinti nì bi-damam tisaalaatiil pu ki tììyee dee.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Tiwampɔkaal tin kɔkɔ bi làá cáań kí tīī-nee, ní lēē tin ŋān̄ee poon kí cáań kí ŋá man saraa.»

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Á gíti tùkù-bi yii: «Ni yaa lēē tin kɔkɔ sá timɔntiilee ki tīīyee, mimmee ni mun Leefii yab ŋá kii bin béeyee nín lèekī bi-kpaajinti nì bi-damam pu ki tììyee dee.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Báà laakiŋyee, ni nì ni-dicaŋŋi ŋūǹ ki jī an jikaati, kun puee an sá atuun ŋin ni tūǹ dikpafindi tantiunee paati ní.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ni yaa lēē dijammɔntiil ki tīī man ní ki yaa yōoǹ tin kíǹee, naa ŋá ikpiti, kaa kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ Isirayeel yab circir saraau, an puee án kaa làá cáań-ni ŋkúm.»

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: ki yóoǹ-bi mara yii: «Á tùkù Isirayeel yab yii bí cáań-si unasaman gàaa un ŋān̄ u-laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ ní baa kpàl̄-u u túń ditundi ki kée.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Bi yaa cáań-uee, á dūú tīī usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar ní úǹ ń cáá-u kí nyāntí dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu, ní bí làntì-u u-nimbiin niin.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar ń lēē fatiku kí dū u-ŋambiki ki sēē fatikuee kí yàaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki pú ŋfunyɔm miluli.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Boonee ní bí dū unaayee kí wà ŋŋmi u-nimbilin, an dàkà yii u-gbaŋŋu nì u-nanti nì u-fatikuu nì u-poon nanti.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋakpil ń dū busubu bun bi yíì seediree dɔŋu nì kifaapibiki kin bi yíì isɔpee bambil nì gulfaman kí dūú tɔ̄ ŋŋmi ŋun bíi wù unaayee poon.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní usaraaŋakpil ń fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati ní kí fàl̀ kí wàatī ní kí nín gítiń dinaapaal pu, ama ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Un di yaa dū unaayee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmee mun ń fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Uninja un bí circiree ń yáfí unaayee fantam kí cáá yóoń laakin bí circiree dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu laaba. Isirayeel yab ń dāá dū ŋfantamee kí kpāafì kí dāá dūú ŋá nnyim min bi cáa lèekī binib nì tiwan pu tijɔkɔndee. An sá kii ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee ní.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Un di yaa fāā unaayee fantamee, udaan mun ń fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. An sá dibɔkpaal din làá nīn bí kí nīn cá jaanjaanee ní ki tīī Isirayeel yab nì binicambi bin kóò bi-kansikinee. Unil nín máaǹ kí ŋá min kí nyā tijɔkɔndinee

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: «Un yaa gbēē dinikpilee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin kí tin sāā iwiin iluli.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Bí dū nnyim min lèekī tijɔkɔndee kí yɔ̄kɔfì u-pu winta dal nì winluli dal ní ú nín nyā tijɔkɔndin. Ama bi yaa kaa dū nnyimee ki yɔ́kɔfì u-pu winta dal u kpá kí nyā tijɔkɔndin winluli dal.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Un di yaa gbēē dinikpil ní baa dū nnyimee ki yɔ́kɔfì udaan puee kɔ́ǹ ti-Dindaan tantiu tijɔkɔndi. Bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel yab kansikin, kun puee bi nín kaa dū nnyim min lèekī tijɔkɔndee ki yɔ́kɔfì u-puee, u-jɔkɔnti pée gbíntìi bí u-pu ní.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: «Mara ubɔ mun gíti sá yii ubɔ yaa kpíì tanti poonee, bin kɔkɔ kɔ́ utaŋkpiilee cee tanti poonee nì bin pée bí utaŋkpiilee ceeyee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin áli iwiin iluli.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Ubɔ di yaa bí kusaau ní ki gbēē dinikpil din ubɔ kūūyee àá un wiiŋŋu di bàn̄ ní u kpíìyee, àá u gbēē anikpab àá dikaakulee, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin kí tin cáá sāā iwiin iluli.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Ní uninja un bí circiree ń lēē kifaapibiki kin bi yíì isɔpee kí nīn sèetī nnyimee poon ki cáa yàantí tanti nì asambil nì binib bin kɔkɔ bí niinee pu, nì un gbēē anikpab àá unil un bi kūūyee, àá un bàn̄ u-wiiŋŋu ki kpíìyee, àá un gbēē dikaakulee pu.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Un bí circiree di yɔ́kɔfí un kɔ́ tijɔkɔndinee pu nnyim winta dal nì winluli dal. Boonee ní ú fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, ní kí dū nnyimee kí fàl̀, kujoou dāa jóotée u nyáń tijɔkɔndin.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: «Unil un di kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ní baa yɔ́kɔfì u-pu nnyim an lēē u-jɔkɔntee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel yab kansikin. Di sá yii u kɔ́ǹ ti-Dindaan kɔŋkooŋŋu tijɔkɔndi. Bi nín kaa dū nnyim min lèekī tijɔkɔndee ki yɔ́kɔfì u-puee, u-jɔkɔnti pée gbíntìi bí u-pu ní.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: «Án nīn sá dibɔkpaal ki tīī-bi kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. Un di yaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ní bi yɔ́kɔfì u-pu nnyim u nyáń tijɔkɔndinee ń fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, ní un yaa gbēē nnyim gbantee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí tin cáá sāā kujoou.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Kun ní un bí tijɔkɔndinee yaa gbēēyee, kudɔŋu mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin, ní unil un gbēē un bí tijɔkɔndinee mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin kí tin cáá sāā kujoou.»

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn bàn̄ Siini teekun dibindi ŋmapeepeekaau poon ní ki kāl̀ Kadeesi. Niin ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn niisal Miiriyam kpíì, ní bi síb́-u.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Bi bí niinee ní nnyiŋkum nyáń Isirayeel yab pu, ní bi kpáfì ki múkuǹ Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn pu.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ní bi kíĺ ki bíi nyàab̀ Mooyiisi tibɔti ki lì yii: «Ti yaa bàà nìn kpíì ŋyunti ŋun ti-Dindaan nìn dáaĺ ti-nabiyaamu tafal bi kpíìyee, an bàà sɔ́!

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Ba pu ní ni yōoǹní timbi ti-Dindaan samaau ki cáań kuteeu pu doo ti nì ti-waŋkuti ń kpú ní?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Ba pu ní ni yōoǹní-ti Eejipiti tiŋkin ki cáań-ti ki tɔ́ falaa nee poon? Baa ŋūǹ kí bɔ̄l̀ doo tiba, kaa ŋūǹ kí cóoń isufi in bi yíì fiinyi nì fiigi nì Greenaadee, ní nnyim kpáàa kpá tí nyɔ̀.»

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nyáń samaa kansikin ki búntì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu. Bi bàn̄ee ní ki tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil, ní ti-Dindaan nyooti kpákatìń bi-cee.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: «Yòon̄ ŋkpandɔ si nì a-maan Aarɔn, kí kpāfì Isirayeel yab, kí sòoǹ nì ditaŋkpal nee bi-nimbiin dí tīī-ni nnyim. Ditaŋkpal nee ni ní a làá nyāntí nnyim Isirayeel yab nì bi-waŋkuti ń nyɔ̀.»

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi yōoǹ ŋkpandɔ ti-Dindaan nimbiin kii u nín lī yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yíiń samaa kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ditaŋkpalee cee, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ní pīlifì, nimbi pɔɔgaatibee. Ti ŋūǹ kí nyāntí nnyim ditaŋkpal nee poon kí tīī-naaa?»

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi lī míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki dúkutì ŋkpandɔ ki fáá ditaŋkpalee mili. Dicilpuee ní nnyim púnní, ní Isirayeel yab nyùn̄ ní bi-waŋkuti mun nyùn̄.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii: «Kii ni nín kaa máká m-pu kaa dàkā m nín bí circir puee Isirayeel yab nimbiinee, maa làá yàntī ní cáá samaa nee kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin m làá tīī-bee poon.»

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Di sá ní bi pú niin diyindi yii Meeriiba nyim, an taapu sá yii <Kujaau> nyim. Di sá niin ní Isirayeel yab nìn nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan tibɔti, ní u dàkā-bi u nín bí circir puee. Eedoom bɔtiu kaa pú Isirayeel yab nsan bí jītí

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Bi bí Kadeesi tiŋkin niinee, ní Mooyiisi tú binib Eedoom bɔtiu cee bí tùkù-u yii: «Pīlifì tin a-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab làá sòoǹee! A nyí falaa un ti jíńee bɔti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: Ti-naanjab nìn yíkìi cūtì Eejipiti tiŋkin ki kāl̀ niin ki yúntì tikpil. Ní Eejipiti yab sāaǹ ti nì ti-naanjab.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Ti kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ú jòoń-ti ní u gbìl̄ ti-kuŋkuuntii pu, ní ki túnní u-tuuŋŋu dɔ́miń ki nyántì-ti Eejipiti tiŋkin. Di sá kɔŋkɔnnee ti dūu bāań Kadeesi, a-tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, á pɔ̄-ti nsan tí jītí a-tiŋki poon. Taa làá jītí ubɔ kpaabun, kaa làá kɔ́ ubɔ fiinyi sufii saakun, kaa làá nyɔ̀ ni-lɔkɔb nyim. Ti làá nīn pée nóó mbɔtisanjaa, ní kaa làá pàatī ŋgiil, kaa làá pàatī ŋgan áli kí tin jītí a-tiŋki pu.»

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Ní Eedoom bɔtiu kíí-u yii: «Maa làá kíí ní jītí m-tiŋkin. Ni yaa mākaǹ m làá yàntī m-yab ń kíntí-ni kí jáǹ-ni.»

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab gbíntìi cɔ́ tin bi bàà pée sòon̄ee pu yii: «Ti làá nīn pée nóó mbɔtisanjaa ní. Ti yaa nyùn̄ a-nyim àá ti-waŋkuti di yaa tí nyùn̄ a-nyim, ti làá pà. Tin baba ti pée mèé-see di sá á yàntī tí jītí a-tiŋkin.»

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Ní Eedoom bɔtiu kíí yii: «M bí yii ni kpá kí jītí m-tiŋkin!» Ní Eedoom yab nyáń nì dijanjakitikpaandi din pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki túŋkì Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Eedoom yab kaa yāntì Isirayeel yab jítì bi-tiŋki poon, ní bíǹ dūu dī laaba pú ki búntì. Aarɔn kúm

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yíkì Kadeesee ní ki búntì Ɔɔr jool pu.

english_verse: on the Edomite border, the Lord said,
translation_verse: Ɔɔr jool pu, Eedoom tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii:

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: «Aarɔn làá kpú kɔŋkɔnnee kí cù kí ŋàl̄ u-naanjab. Waa làá kɔ́ kitiŋ kin m làá tīī Isirayeel yabee poon, kun puee ni yīntì m-marau Meeriiba nyim laŋki.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: An puee sii Mooyiisi, á yòon̄ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar kí jɔ̄ntiǹ Ɔɔr jool yilpu.

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Á pèetī Aarɔn saraaŋabɔkutiŋ kí dūú pèen̄ u-jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar, kun puee Aarɔn làá kpú niin ní kí cù kí ŋàl̄ u-naanjab.»

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín bí ú ŋá puee. Bíǹ binib bitee yíkì ki nín jɔ́ḿ Ɔɔr jool yilpu Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ nimbilin.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ee ní Mooyiisi pēetì Aarɔn saraaŋabɔkutiŋ ki dūu pēeǹ u-jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar. Dijool yilpu niin ní Aarɔn kpíì. Ní Mooyiisi nì Eeleeyasaar fātìi nín kpákatiń.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ nín béè yii Aarɔn kpíìyee ní bi súń u-kpool iwiin mmuŋku nì saalaa.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab yíkì Ɔɔr jool puee ní ki dūu dī Tikati mɔɔl watil kí gɔ́ntí Eedoom tiŋki. Ama bi bí disaŋkindi puee ní samaa wunti yɔ̄tì.

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ ki bíiĺ ti-Dindaan nì Mooyiisi yii: «Ba pu ní ni nyántìń-ti Eejipiti tiŋkin ki cáań-ti kuteeun kí kpɔ̀ ní? Nnyim kpá, tijin kpá, ní ti núutiǹ maana, falaa jinti tin ti jīǹ nee!»

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan dū ikoobu in looti pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki tɔ́ bi-pu, ní i júntìi kūū Isirayeel yab tikpil.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Ní samaa un kíǹee sáǹ ki cūtìi ká Mooyiisi ki bí-u yii: «Ti nín sòon̄ ki bíil̀ ti-Dindaan nì siiyee, ti ŋá ikpiti. Míǹ puee gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan ú kàkatī ikoobu nee kí wàatī-ti.» Ní Mooyiisi mēē samaa pu.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Á dū tasa kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ kukoonaŋu kí dūú lúntí ndɔ pu. Un ní ukoobu yaa ti júee, ú wáaǹ kí kpèè kukoonaŋuee kí ŋmátí.»

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ kukoonaŋu ki dūu lúntì ndɔ pu. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, un ní ukoobu yaa ti jú ní u wáaǹ ki kpēē kukoonaŋuee kaa ti kúù. Isirayeel yab nín cōom̀ pu ki tin bàn̄ Piisga joolee

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab yíkì Ɔɔr jool taapuee ní ki tin bàn̄ ki kāl̀ Oobooti tiŋkin.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Bi yíkì niinee ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ Seereedi buŋgbandi.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Bi yíkì Seereedee ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ Arinɔn buŋgbandi. Mbun gbanti nyēeń Amɔɔr tiŋkin ní kí dāá jītí kuteeun. Ŋúǹ di sá Moowaab nì Amɔɔr yab kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: An pu ní an lī ti-Dindaan jaaku gbɔŋkun yii: «Wayeeb bí Sufa nì u-buŋyin, ní Arinɔn

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: nì u-bùmbiyaamu nyim pùub̀ ki kpàkaǹ Aari tiŋki ki tin bàn̄ Moowaab kpaanyɔkɔ.»

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Bi yíkì niinee ki nín cá Beeyeer, taapu di sá <lɔkɔ>. Lɔkɔ gbanti ní ti-Dindaan nìn bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kpāfì Isirayeel yab doo ḿ tīī-bi nnyim bí nyɔ̀.»

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Niin ní Isirayeel yab nìn gāā nlan nee yii: «Nnyim ń nīn tòó ki nyēeń lɔkɔn! Nín̄ kpáafímaan abaal!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Lɔkɔ un bibɔtiibi gbìn̄ee dee, lɔkɔ un kitiŋ pu nikpaambi lùkū nì bi-kúti nì bi-kpandɔyee dee!» Bi yíkì kuteeunee ní ki bàn̄ Matana.

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: Bi yíkì Matanayee ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ Nayaliyeel.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Bi yíkì Nayaliyeelee ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ Bamooti. Bi yíkì Bamootee ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ ditantakal din dɔ̄ ki jítì Moowaab tiŋkin ki cá Piisga jool yilpuee. A yaa tɔ́kɔ́ niinee, a wāĺ kuteeu kɔkɔ. Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Siiwɔn nì Ɔɔgi

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Eesbɔn nìn sá ditiŋyil laakin Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu nìn kóòyee. U nìn jáń nì Moowaab bɔtiu ukpiki ní ki fōō u-timmu kɔkɔ áli ki tin cáa bàn̄ Arinɔn buŋŋu.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab tú bí mèè Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu Siiwɔn yii:

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: «Ti là kí jītí a-tiŋkin. Taa làá jītí ubɔ kpaabun, kaa làá kɔ́ ubɔ fiinyi sufii saakun, kaa làá nyɔ̀ ni-lɔkɔb nyim. Ti làá nīn pée nóó mbɔtisanjaa ní cáaa kí jītí a-tiŋki pu.»

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Ama ubɔti Siiwɔn yíì yii Isirayeel yab ń taa jītí. Ní u kpáfì u-janjakitil kɔkɔ bi nyáń ki túŋkì Isirayeel yab áli Yaasi, kuteeun ki jáń nì bi.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi ki kūū-bi ní ki fōō bi-timmu kɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ Arinɔn buŋŋu kí cáá sāā Yaabɔki buŋŋu, kí yòon̄ niin kí nīn cá áli Amɔn yab tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ, di sá Amɔn yab nìn máń digundi bi-kpaanyɔkɔ ní.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Bi nìn fōō Amɔɔr yab timmu kɔkɔ, ki kpáaǹ Eesbɔn nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-kèe. Bi fōō-muee ní ki kāl̀ mu-poon.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: An pu ní bilaŋkpaŋgaaliibi lī yii: «Dāam̄maan tí fàtīí mā Eesbɔn tiŋki. Tí fàtīí mā Siiwɔn tiŋki!

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: «Ŋŋmi ŋubɔ nyánní Eesbɔn, ŋŋmi fōoń Siiwɔn tiŋkin ki wùn̄ Aari nì Moowaab timmu, ki kpáaǹ bin sá bikpilib ki tɔ́kɔ́ Arinɔn buŋŋu yilpuee.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Mbusu kɔ́-si, Moowaab! Nimbi bin jáaḿ diwaal Keemoosee, ni wáŋkì! A-jipɔmbi sáǹ ki yàl̄ ní Amɔɔr bɔtiu Siiwɔn cúú a-bisalib kuyuŋu.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: «Ti jàkā-bi butɔbu ki yōoǹ Eesbɔn ki cáa sāā Diibɔn! Ti kūū ki céetì-bi ki yōoǹ Noofa ki cáa sāā Meedeeba!»

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab jíń Amɔɔr yab tiŋki ki kāl̀.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi tú binib bí cùú cɔ̄ŋkì Yaseer tiŋki, ní bi cūtìi jáń ki fōō ntimu mun māntìi tú-kèe, ní ki jìn̄ Amɔɔr yab bin nìn kóò mu-nee.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel yab fātìi kpántì bi nín bàà túĺ ki cá puee ní ki dūu dī Baasan saŋŋu. Ní Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi nì u-janjakitil kɔkɔ yíkìń ki túŋkì Isirayeel yab Eedreeyii tiŋki kí jáǹ-bi.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Taa fàŋkì-bi. M làá dū bi nì bi-janjaliibi nì bi-tiŋki kí ŋá a-ŋaan, ní á ŋá-bi kii a nín ŋá Amɔɔr bɔtiu Siiwɔn un nìn kóò Eesbɔn tiŋkinee puee.»

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-janjakitil kɔkɔ, ki kūū bi-kɔkɔ ubɔ kaa kíǹ, ní ki fōō u-tiŋki.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab yíkì niinee ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ Moowaab tantakalin, Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi lapu pu ki túĺ Jeeriikoo.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: ní dinyoondi kɔ́ u nì u-samaau Isirayeel yab nín wīikí tikpilee pu. Bi nín ká Isirayeel yabee, tifaandi cúú-bi tikpil.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Ní u bí Madiyan kpilib yii: «Binib nee làá ŋàfì tin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-ti nee kii inaa nín ŋmóò dinaapaal mooti pu nyíki nyikee ní.» Ŋyunti gbantee Siipɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaaki di nìn sá ubɔti Moowaab tiŋkin.

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: An puee ní Balaaki dū binib ki tú Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaam cee. U nìn kóò u-tiŋkin Peetɔɔr, dimɔɔl din bi yíì Eefiraatee caŋin. U nìn bí bí cùú tùkù-u yii: «Dinibul diba nyánní Eejipiti ki kpátì ki gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu, ní ki kóò ki pìlīǹ man.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee m gbàam̄-si, dāan̄ kí tɔ̄-bi mbusu, kun puee bi pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ-mi. A yaa kíí ki dɔ́mińee, án yaa yíì m ŋūǹ kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi ní kí jà-bi m-tiŋki pu. Di sá m nyí yii un pu ní a yaa bīiǹee kāntí dibiindi, ní un ní a yaa tɔ́ mbusuee, udaan kāntí mbusu.»

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Ní Moowaab nì Madiyan kpilib yíkìi yōoǹ tiwampɔkaal tin bi làá tin pɔ̄ Balaamee ki bàn̄ ki ká-u, ní ki dū Balaaki nín lī puee ki kàan̄.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Ní Balaam bí-bi yii: «Ní gbíntí m-cee doo kí dòon̄, ku yaa fu wúntì ti-Dindaan yaa sòon̄ nì mi puee, m làá fu tùkù-ni an nín sá puee.» Niinee ní Moowaab kpilibee gbíntì Balaam cee ki dōoǹ.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti dɔ́miń Balaam cee ní ki bí yii: «Binib bilab di bí a-cee nan ní?»

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Ní Balaam kíí Unimbɔti yii: «Siipɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaaki, Moowaab bɔtiu di túnní-bi, bí dāá tùkù-mi yii:

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: <Dinibul diba nyánní Eejipiti ki kpátìi gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu. An puee dāá tūtuǹ-mi kí tɔ̄-bi mbusu. Án yaa yíì m ŋūǹ kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi.>»

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti bí-u yii: «Á taa táá-bi kí cù, kí taa tɔ̄ dinibul gbanti mbusu kun puee m bīiǹ di-boon.»

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Ku wúntì Balaam fīntèe ní ki bí bikpilib bin Balaaki túnnée yii: «Ní nīn gítímaan, ti-Dindaan kaa pú-mi nsan ḿ táá-ni kí cù.»

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Ní Moowaab kpilib bin bi túee fātìi gítì ki tùkū Balaaki yii: «Balaam yíì yii waa làá táá-ti kí dāan̄.»

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Ní Balaaki gíti lēē bikpilib bin sá bikpaambi bi-wíiŋŋu mun jítiǹ bipeepeekaabee ki tú.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Ní bi bàn̄ Balaam cee ki dū tin pu ní Balaaki túnní-bee ki bíl̀ u-nimbiin yii: «Man Balaaki, Siipɔɔr jipɔɔn, m gbàam̄-si, á taa yíí yii aa làá dāan̄ m-cee.

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
