translation_verse: M làá tīī-si tinyool tikpil, ní tin kɔkɔ a yaa bālifèe, m làá ŋá míǹ! Míǹ puee m gbàam̄-si, dāan̄ kí tɔ̄ dinibul nee mbusu.»

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Ní Balaam kíí bin Balaaki túnnée yii: «Báà Balaaki yaa dū animbil nì sindaariya bin gbí u-beediiŋŋinee kɔkɔ ki tīī-mi, maa ŋūǹ kí yìntīǹ m-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu marau kí ŋá tiba fiii gba kí tīī-u.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Ama ni mun ń gbíntímaan kunyeeu nee kí dòon̄ doo, m làá fu béé tin ní ti-Dindaan làá fu tùkù-mee.»

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti dɔ́miń Balaam cee kunyeeu ki tùkū-u yii: «Kii binib nee nín gíti dáá dɔ́miń ki yíiń-see, yīkìí táá-bi ní cù. Ama man yaa tùkū-si yii á ŋá puee, tíǹ ní á ŋá.»

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Balaam kpàl̄ u-mansaliiki ki táá bikpilibee ní bi búntì. Balaam maŋki bɔti

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Balaam nóó-bi ki búntèe ní Unimbɔti fōō diŋuul. Ŋyunti ŋun Balaam kā u-mansaliiki pu u nì u-tɔntɔnliibi bili nóó ki cée, ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu kíntì ki yú nsanni ú taa ŋmā kí jītí.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Ní kimansalii ká ntuun yú nsan kansikin ki ŋúb́ njicál ŋu-ŋaan, ní kì gɔ́ntì ki kɔ́ bukpaan. Ní Balaam bíi gbáà-kì kí kíntí nsan.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nìkī nyɔkɔpu ki cūtìi yúl̀ nsan laakin kaa wāāyee fiinyi sufii kansikin digundi diba bí ŋŋaŋgan pú ní diba bí ŋŋaŋgiil pú.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Kimansalii ká ntuun mimmee ní kì còom̄ ki náká nì digundi. Balaam taal dūuǹ digundee, ní u kíĺ ki bíi gbáà-kì.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nìkī nyɔkɔpu laakin nsan mɔ́ɔb́ unil kaa ŋūǹ kí fàtī ŋgiilaaa, kaa ŋūǹ kí fàtī ŋganee.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Kimaŋ ká-ŋu mimmee ní ki dōoǹ Balaam taapu ní Balaam dàn̄ ki-pu. Balaam fōō diŋuul tiŋan pu ní ki dū ndɔ ki gbáń-kì tikpil.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan pú kimansalii ŋŋmam kí sòoǹ tibɔti, ní kì bí Balaam yii: «M baasii ŋá-si ba ní a gbáń-mi mita kɔkɔ?»

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Ní Balaam kíí-kì yii: «A kpēē-mi fám ní. M yaa bàà ŋúb́ kitàataajiki m-ŋaan doo, m bàà làá làntì-si!»

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Ní kimansalii kíí-u yii: «Man di kaa sá a-maŋki kin a kàal̀ baabadaleeee? M ŋá-si míǹ dalba ki káaa?» Ní Balaam kíí-u yii: «Aayee.»

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan ŋúbitì Balaam nimbiliŋ ní u ká ntuun yú nsan kansikin ki ŋúb́ njicál ŋu-ŋaan. Dicilpu niinee ní u tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun bālifì-u yii: «Ba pu ní a gbáń a-maŋki mita kɔkɔ? M nyáń kí pìin̄-si nsan á taa ŋmā kí cù laakin a cée ní, kun puee nsan ŋun a cá nee cáǹ-si mbusun ní.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Kimaŋ ká-mi ní ki gɔ́ntì-mi ŋfunyɔm mita, kì yaa kaa bàà gɔ́ntì-mi, naŋkɔnampu m bàà kūū-si ní kí yàntī kíǹ.»

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Ní Balaam bí ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu yii: «M yīntì, kun puee maa nyí yii an sá sii di kíntì ki yú nsanni m-nyɔkɔpu. An puee m-saŋŋu nee bɔti yaa kaa mɔ́ɔkiǹ-see, m kíí kí fàtī m-dumpu.»

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu bí Balaam yii: «Sii nì binib nee ń nīn cá, ama anyɔɔbun ŋin ní m làá dūú ŋá a-nyɔkɔnee, ŋíǹ ní a làá sòoǹ.» Ní Balaam nì binibee nìkī bi-saŋŋu ki búntì. Ubɔti Balaaki túŋkì Balaam nsanni

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Balaaki gbìl̄ yii Balaam dòońee ní u nyáń ki cūtì ki túŋkì-u áli Moowaab tiŋki kin bí ki pìlīǹ kikpaanyɔkɔ Arinɔn buŋŋu caŋinee.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Ní Balaaki bí Balaam yii: «Ba pu ní m nín tú binib mpeepeekaam a-cee bí yíiń-see, a yíì kaa dɔ́miń ní? A nyí yii maa ŋūǹ kí tīī-si tinyool níii?»

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Ní Balaam bí Balaaki yii: «Nì min kɔkɔ m dɔ́miń nee, maa ŋūǹ kí gāā m-bindi kí lì tiba, see tibɔti tin Unimbɔti yaa dūu ŋá m-nyɔkɔnee, tíǹ ní m làá sòoǹ.»

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Ní Balaam nóó Balaaki ní bi nín cá Kiiriyati-Usɔti.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Ní Balaaki dū inaa nì ipii kí ŋá saraabi, ní ki lēē tinan ki tīī Balaam nì bikpilib bin nóoń-uee, báà ŋma nì u-yati. Balaam mēē ki bīiǹ Isirayeel yab pu mpeepeekaam

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Kù wúntèe ní Balaaki yōoǹ Balaam bi nín jɔ́ḿ Bamooti-Baal. Niin ní bi kpēē ki wálìń Isirayeel yab biba.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balaam bí Balaaki yii: «Mā-mi laakin ti yú nee isaraafan iluli, kí cáań-mi doo inajaa iluli nì ipijaa iluli.»

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Ní Balaaki ŋá min Balaam bālifì yii ú ŋée. Ní bi-liitil dū unaja ubɔ nì upìja ubɔ kí ŋá saraawɔkaa nsaraafan kamaa pu.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Ní Balaam bí Balaaki yii: «Nín̄ yú ki kɔ́ĺ a-saraabi bin a ŋée, man làá kàkatī ŋkpaanceeti. Án yaa yíì ti-Dindaan làá dāan̄ m-cee. Tin ní u yaa lēē ki dàkā-mee, m làá tùkù-si.» U lī mimmee ní ki nín jɔ́ḿ kigbantaŋ kiba pu.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti dɔ́miń Balaam cee, ní Balaam bí-u yii: «M máń isaraafan iluli ki ŋá saraawɔkaa nsaraafan kamaa pu, unaja ubɔ nì upìja ubɔ.»

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Ní Balaam nín gítí Balaaki cee. U bàn̄ee Balaaki yú ki kɔ́ĺ saraa un u ŋée, u nì Moowaab kpilib.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Ní Balaam bíi gà-u alaŋkpaŋkpaka yii: «Balaaki yāntì m nyánní Aram tiŋkin ki dɔ́miń. Moowaab bɔtiu yāntì m nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú jooŋŋin ki dɔ́miń. Dāan̄ kí tɔ̄ Isirayeel yab, Jaakɔb naantiibi mbusu!

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: M tɔ́kɔ́ ataŋkpee pu ní ki wāĺ-bi, m tɔ́kɔ́ agbantan yilpu ní ki kpèé-bi. Bi sá dinibul din kɔŋkooŋŋu bí ŋu-bee ní, baa ŋmàl̄ atimbun kansikin.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ Jaakɔb nib? Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí lì Isirayeel yab wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm? M là kí kpú deedeedambi kúm ní, m-kúntitam ń nīn náań nì bi-kúntitam.»

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Niinee Balaaki bí Balaam yii: «A ŋá-mi ba dee? Man yíiń-si yii á dāan̄ kí tɔ̄ m-nannanliibi mbusu ní sii dɔ́miń ki yú ki mèé ki bìintí bi-puɔɔ!»

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Ní Balaaki bí Balaam yii: «Dāan̄ tí gíti cùú yūĺ mpaan ŋubɔ mun pu, niinee a làá ká Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ. Laakin ti yú nee, aa ŋūǹ kí wāl̀ bi-kɔkɔ. Ti yaa kpántì mpaanee, a làá wāl̀ bi-kɔkɔ ní kí tɔ̄-bi mbusu.»

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Ní u yōoǹ Balaam ki cáa cūnnì doooo laakin bi sīlifí sintilee, Piisga jool caŋin. Niinee ní u tí máń isaraafan iluli, ki dū unaja ubɔ nì upìja ubɔ ki ŋá saraawɔkaa nsaraafan kamaa pu.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Ní Balaam bí Balaaki yii: «Nín̄ yú ki kɔ́ĺ a-saraabi bin a ŋée, man làá cù nyɔkɔpu doo kí cīití ti-Dindaan.»

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan dɔ́miń Balaam cee, ní ki tīī-u tibɔti tin u làá sòoǹee, ní ki bí yii: «Nín̄ gíti Balaaki cee kí sòoǹ míǹ.»

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Ní Balaam fātìi nín gítí Balaaki cee. U nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ u-saraawɔkaabi u nì Moowaab kpilib. Ní Balaaki bālifì Balaam yii: «Ti-Dindaan lī yii ba?»

english_verse: Balaam answered: “Pay close attention to my words—
translation_verse: Ní Balaam gāā-u alaŋkpaŋkpaka nee yii: «Yīkì kí pīlifì Balaaki! Kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì, Siipɔɔr jipɔɔn!

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti kaa sá unil ki mɔ́ntí, waa sá nisaal ki kpántí ilandɔkɔ. Waa lì tiba fám kaa ŋá míǹ. U yaa pōoǹ puee, see ú ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: “My command from God was to bless these people, and there's nothing I can do to change what he has done.
translation_verse: U bí yii m bìin̄ bi-pu ní, úǹ di bīiǹ ní ki bí yii ḿ bìin̄, maa ŋūǹ kí kpántí tiba.

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan kaa ká ikpiti iba Jaakɔb nibul pu, waa ká mɔnaafiki Isirayeel yab pu. Úǹ ti-Dindaan di sá bi-Nimbɔtiu, ní ki bí bi-cee. Bíǹ di kpáafí abɔtibaal ki tìì-u.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti di nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin. U-pɔŋŋu sá-bi kii upɔɔnaa pɔŋŋuee ní.

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Kpèè, dinibul nee yíkì ki náká kii gbikintee. See ú cúú upeel un u làá ŋmɔ́ee kí cátí kí nyɔ̀ u-fatikuu kí wàatī ní kí nín dòon̄.»

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Balaaki bí Balaam yii: «A yaa kaa làá tɔ̄-bi mbusuee, taa ti mèè kí bìin̄ bi-puɔɔ!»

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Ní Balaam kíí-u yii: «M pée tùkū-si dooooyee ki yóoǹ yii: <Tibɔti tin ní m-Dindaan yaa dūu ŋá m-nyɔkɔnee, tíǹ ní m làá sòoǹ.>» Balaam mēē ki bīiǹ Isirayeel yab pu ntataatiim

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Ní Balaaki bí Balaam yii: «Dāan̄ tí gíti nìkī mpaan ŋubɔ pu. Án yaa yíì mpaan gbanti pu ní Unimbɔti làá kíí á tɔ̄ dinibul gbanti mbusu kí tīī-mi.»

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Niinee Balaaki yōoǹ Balaam ki cáa jɔ́ntiǹ Peewɔɔr jool din yú ki túliń kuteeuee pu.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Ní Balaam tí bí Balaaki yii: «Mā-mi isaraafan iluli doo kí cáań-mi inajaa iluli nì ipijaa iluli.»

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balaaki ŋá min kɔkɔ Balaam bālifèe, ní ki dū unaja ubɔ nì upìja ubɔ ki ŋá saraawɔkaa nsaraafan kamaa pu.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Min bí nee Balaam béè yii an ŋān̄ ti-Dindaan cee ú bìin̄ Isirayeel yab puee, waa ti lī yii u làá kàkatī ŋkpaanceeti kí kpèè ti-Dindaan nín làá tùkù-u puee kii u nín kpààa ŋáań puee, u fātì u-nimbiin ki túĺ kuteeu pú ní.

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: Balaam wáaǹ ki kpēēyee ki ká Isirayeel yab naakɔti bi-naapaal pu, ní Unimbɔti Fam kɔ́-u.

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Ní Balaam gāā-bi alaŋkpaŋkpaka nee yii: «Tin man Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaam sòon̄ee sèé. Kpèè tin man un wāĺee sòon̄ee.

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Kpèè man un gbìl̀ Unimbɔti nyɔkɔ poon bɔtee nín lī puee sèé. Man un di wālifí tin Mpɔŋkɔdaan lèekī ki dàkà ŋyunti ŋun ní an yōoǹ-mi m-nimbiliŋ ŋúbitèe.

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: «Jaakɔb naantiibi, ni-tantib ŋān̄eeee! Isirayeel yab, ni-kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋān̄ ní!

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: A lì kii ibun di pùub̀ee, kii bukpaa bun dɔ̄ mbun caŋinee, kii disaaweendi din ti-Dindaan cóoǹee, a lì kii isufi in bi yíì Seedir i yú ki nákáǹ ŋkpinee.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: A lì kii nnyim min gbéè dinyimbɔbil, ní ki yàantí u-wambɔlkaati an lòoǹee. Isirayeel yab bɔtiu yindi yíkì yilpu ki jítiǹ ubɔti Agaagi, ní bi-beel làá nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ abee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nyántì-u Eejipiti tiŋkin, ní u-pɔŋŋu sá-bi kii upɔɔnaa pɔŋŋuee, ní bi cáa pɔ̀fī atimbun ŋin sá bi-nannanliibee, ki wìil̄ bi-kpabiŋ, ní bi-piiŋyi kɔ̄ntí-bi tiweendi.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Bíǹ di tātìi dɔ̄ kii gbikintee, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí páb́-bi bí yīkì!» «Un di yaa bīiǹ Isirayeel boonee làá ká dibiindi. Un di yaa tí tɔ́-u mbusuee, mbusu làá gítí udaan pu!»

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Balaaki fōō Balaam pu diŋuul ní ki kpáafì u-ŋalii ki bí Balaam yii: «M yíiń-si á dāan̄ kí tɔ̄ m-nannanliibi mbusu, ní sii dɔ́miń ki mēē ki bīiǹ bi-pu mita kɔkɔɔ!

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Too fàtīí nīn kùǹ a-dumpu malaa! M bàà nìn pōoǹ-si yii m làá tīī-si tinyool, ama ní ti-Dindaan kaa pú-si nsan.» Balaam sòon̄ tinyool tin dɔ̄ ki cí Isirayeel yabee

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: <Báà Balaaki yaa yōoǹ animbil nì sindaariya bin gbí u-beediiŋŋinee kɔkɔ ki tīī-mi, maa làá yìntīǹ m-Dindaan. Di sá tibɔti tin ní m-Dindaan dūu ŋá m-nyɔkɔnee, tíǹ ní m làá sòoǹ.>

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Too, kɔŋkɔnnee m làá fàtīí gítí m-yab cee. Kí wàatī ḿ nīn cée, dāan̄ ḿ tùkù-si dalba Isirayeel yab nín làá dāá ŋá a-nibul puee.»

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Ní Balaam gāā-bi alaŋkpaŋkpaka nee yii: «Tin man Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaam sòon̄ee sèé, kpèè tin man un wāĺee sòon̄ee.

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Kpèè man un gbìl̀ Unimbɔti nyɔkɔ poon bɔtee nín lī puee sèé, man un di cáá Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu nyilee. Man un di wālifí tin Mpɔŋkɔdaan lèekī ki dàkà ŋyunti ŋun ní an yōoǹ-mi m-nimbiliŋ ŋúbitèe.

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: M wāĺ tiba, tì bí ki dòoń, ama an kaa nín sá kɔŋkɔnnee. M dáań ki ká tiba, ama taa làá bàń díǹ. Uŋmalbija ubɔ nyáń Jaakɔb maaliŋun, ubɔtikpaan ubɔ nyáń Isirayeel nibulin. U làá dāá fáá kí wīī Moowaab yab nyɔɔkpaweeŋyi, ní kí fáá kí wīī Seeti yab yiliŋ.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: U làá dāá fōō Eedoom tiŋki, u làá dāá fōō u-nannanliibi Seeyiir yab tiŋki. Isirayeel yab di yì dijajil.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Ubɔ làá nyānní Jaakɔb maaliŋun kí nīn tɔ́kɔ́ tikɔkɔ pu. U làá dāá kúntí bin bin nìn sáǹ ki nyáń ntimun ki ŋmátèe.» Isirayeel nannanliibi kúntitam

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Balaam ká Amaleeki yabee ní ki sòon̄ ki tɔ́ bi-pu yii: «Amaleeki, atimbun kɔkɔ poonee, sii di sá mbaa, ama tin dɔ̄ ki cí-see di sá a làá dāá kúntí ní kí nàan̄.»

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Ní u ká Keeni yab ní ki sòon̄ ki tɔ́ bi-pu yii: «Keeni yab, ni bí kitiŋ kin poon tiba kpá kí ŋá-nee, kii kunɔndii kun pá ditaŋkpal puee.

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Ama ŋŋmi di làá dāá wà ni-kɔŋkooŋyi, ní Asuur yab ń dāá cúú-ni kí cùnnì bi-tiŋkin kuyuŋu.»

english_verse: “No one can survive if God plans destruction.
translation_verse: Ní u gíti lī yii: «Unimbɔti yaa làá tɔ̄ u-tundi kí jītée, ŋma di làá kíń?

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Meelab túnní bijanjaliibi ki làá nyānní Siitiim tiŋkin kí dāá wɔ́b́ Asuur tiŋki yab, kí dāá wɔ́b́ Eebeer tiŋki yab, ní kíǹ ki-ba mun ń dāá céetí.»

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Balaam lī mimmee ní ki fātìi nín gítí u-dumpu ní Balaaki mun nín cá u-laŋki.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel yab dɔ́miń ki bí Siitiim tiŋkin. Ní samaa kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań tilaakpaal nì Moowaab yab sapɔmbi.

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: Moowaab yab sapɔmbi yaa làá nìn tòotī awaayee, bi nìn yíì Isirayeel yab ní bí cù bí tòotī. Bi nìn jīǹ tiwaatootijin, ní ki gbàantí bi-waaŋi nimbiin.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn kíĺ ki bíi tòotī Peewɔɔr waal din bi yíì yii Baalee. Ní ti-Dindaan fōō bi-pu diŋuul.

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Á cúú Isirayeel yab kpilib kɔkɔ kí lúntí idɔ pu m-nimbiin bí bíití ŋwìiń, kí wàatī ní m-ŋuul ń nín sɔ̀ŋkì Isirayeel yab pu.»

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi bí Isirayeel yab yidambi yii: «Ni-kansikin báà ŋma ń kpɔ̀ bin di cūtìi tōotì Peewɔɔr waal din bi yíì Baalee.»

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Niinee Isirayeel yab ubɔ jítì nì umadiyannimpu ubɔ, Mooyiisi nì u-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin. Bíǹ nìn bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ki sūǹ.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn naantiiu Fineeyaasi, Eeleeyasaar jipɔɔn ká mimmee ní ki yíkì samaa kansikin ki yōoǹ u-kpaŋki,

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: ní ki páaǹ uninjee boon ki tin kɔ́ u-tantiun ní ki sāā uisirayeeljee nì unimpuee pooŋi ki kūū-bi. Ní ditafadaaldi gbēeǹ Isirayeel yab kansikin.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: «Usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn naantiiu Fineeyaasi, Eeleeyasaar jipɔɔn yāntì m-ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkì Isirayeel yab pu, kun puee u yāntì m-poompooŋyi in m ŋáań Isirayeel yab puee kɔ́-u, ní m-ŋuul din m bàà fōō kí kúntí Isirayeel yabee dūu gbēeǹ.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: Dipoondi gbantee sá ki tīī úǹ nì u-naantiibi ní. Á dū-bi kí kpántí bisaraaŋaliibi kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Di sá u dàkā yii u dū u-pɔbil kɔkɔ ki tīī man u-Nimbɔtiu, an di yì-tì ní u ŋúń ki nyántì Isirayeel yab bi-kpitii poon.»

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yíì uisirayeelja un bi nìn kūū nì umadiyannimpuee yii Simrii, ní ki yíì u-baa Saluu. Úǹ nìn sá ukpil ubɔ ní Simeeyɔn naakookun.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Ní ki yíì umadiyannimpuee yii Koosbii, ní ki yíì u-baa Suur. U-baa gbanti nìn sá Madiyan naakooku kubɔ yab bɔtiu ní.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: Kun puee bi sá ni-nannanliibi ní. Di sá bi ŋá nciin ní ki dī tibɔti tin nìn jítì Peewɔɔr tiŋkinee nì tin nìn jítì Koosbii, niin yab bisal puee ki ŋúń-ni. Koosbii gbanti nìn sá bi-bɔtiu ubɔ bisal ní bi kūū-u Peewɔɔr waal bɔti tafadaaldi yuntiŋu.» Bi fātìi kàan̄ Isirayeel yab nliliitiim

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: «Ní kàaǹ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, kí nóó nì adican nib kí kíĺ bin cáá abin mmuŋku kí nín cáa cée, bin kɔkɔ ŋūǹ kí bàl̄ tijanjawanee.»

english_verse: years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Juuda naakooku dicaŋŋi ŋin kíǹee sèé. Seela dicaŋŋi yab naanja di sá Seela, Peereeki dicaŋŋi yab naanja di sá Peereeki ní Seera dicaŋŋi yab naanja sá Seera.

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi nì usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar sòon̄ nì samaa Moowaab tantakal din pìlīǹ Jɔɔdan ki túĺ Jeeriikoo tiŋkee, ní ki bí-bi yii:

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Palu jipɔɔn di sá Eeliyaab,

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: ní Eeliyaab jipɔmbi sá Neemuyeel nì Daatan nì Abiiram. Daatan nì Abiiram gbanti di nìn sá samaa kansikin bikpilib bin nìn yíkìi bíi kpākantí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔŋyee. Bi nìn dū Kooree yab ki kútì bi-ba pu bí jáǹ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: Kitiŋ nìn wāaǹ ki-nyɔkɔ ki dū-bi ki náĺ ki kpáaǹ Kooree. Ŋwiin gbantee, ŋŋmi nìn wùn̄ binib kulaafaau nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa, bi nì bi-nimbiliŋ án nīn sá kudaaŋŋu ki tīī samaa.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Ama Kooree jipɔmbi kaa nìn kpíì yaadal.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab gbanti kansikinee, baa nìn gíti ká bin ní Mooyiisi nì usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn nìn kàan̄ Siinaayi teekunee báà ubɔ.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Ní Aarɔn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu munaa: Nadaab nì Abiyuu nì Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: «Á yàkatī ntimu kí tīī tinaakɔti tin a kàan̄ee nib kí táá nì bi-wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: An tí sá ní tɔ̄ kasi ní án lēē laakin sá ní tīī bin nib wīikée nì bin yab kaa náaǹee.» Bi kàan̄ Leefii yab nliliitiim

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Leefii naakooku yab biba mun sɔ̀. Liibinii naakooku yab nì Eebrɔn yab nì Maalii yab nì Musii yab nì Kooree yab. Keeyaati di màl̄ Amiiraam,

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: ní u cáá Yookeebeedi, Leefii bisal un bi màl̄ Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ní úǹ màl̄ Amiiraam mbiyaamu muta: Aarɔn nì Mooyiisi nì bi-niisal Miiriyam.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ama Nadaab nì Abiyuu kpíì, kun puee bi nìn mɔ́fìń ŋŋmi laaba ki cáań kí ŋá ti-Dindaan nimbiin saraa.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nì usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar nín nìn kàan̄ Isirayeel yab Moowaab tantakal din pìlīǹ Jɔɔdan ki túĺ Jeeriikooyee, bi nín nìn nyáń puee dee.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: Di sá ti-Dindaan nìn tùkū-bi yii bi làá kpú kuteeun. Míǹ puee bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn gíti kíǹ, see Yeefunee jipɔɔn Kaaleeb nì Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa di nìn kíǹ.

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ti-baa kpíì kuteeun, ama an kaa nín sá yii u nìn kútì Kooree nikitil din nìn yíkì kí jáǹ ti-Dindaanee bɔti poon. U nìn pée kpíì úǹ u-ba kpitii kúm ní, ama waa cáá kibininjabiki.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Mimmee an ŋān̄ yii u nín kaa cáá kibininjabikee puee, u-yindi ń kúntí ti-naakooku maaliŋu yab kansikinaaa? An puee ní tīī ti mun difakal kii ni nín tīī ti-baa nabiyaamu puee.»

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Ní Mooyiisi cáá bi-bɔti gbanti ki bíl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin,

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: «Seeloofaadi bisalib cáá ibaamɔn! Tīī bi mun ditinjandi difakal kii a nín tīī bi-baa nabiyaamu puee. Dū bi-baa tinjandi kí tīī-bi difakal.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: U yaa kaa cáá bisalee, bí dūú tīī u-nabiyaamu.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: U yaa kaa cáá nnabiyaamuee, bí dūú tīī u-baa nabiyaamu.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: U-baa yaa kaa cáá nnabiyaamuee, bí dū u-fakal kí tīī u-dicaŋkun niliu u nì un pēē kubaabinaatoouee ń jī u-fakal.> Isirayeel yab máaǹ kí ŋúb́ mara un m tīī sii Mooyiisi nee kii m nín bí yii bí ŋá puee.» Joosuwa fōō Mooyiisi yil

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Jɔ̄m̀ Abariim joonɔbikaal nee pu, kí kpèè kitiŋ kin m làá dūú tīī Isirayeel yabee.

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: A yaa kpēē-kì ki dóòyee, a mun làá kpú kí cùú ŋàl̄ a-baabi kii a-maan Aarɔn nín kpíì puee ní.

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: Di sá ni yīntiǹ-mi Siini teekun ŋyunti ŋun ní samaa nìn bíi tákà-mi tibɔtee. Naa dàkā Isirayeel yii m sá circir ŋyunti ŋun m nìn bíi sòoǹ Siini teekun Kadeesi nnyiŋkum min nìn cúú-bee bɔti.» Bi dāa pú niin diyindi yii Meeriiba, an dàkà yii kujaau nyim.

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, sii un tīī tiwannáaŋkaal kɔkɔ kufoouee, lēē unil ubɔ ú lìntī samaa nee nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
