english_verse: If any of you are engaged to be married, you may go back home and get married. It isn't right for you to die in battle and for somebody else to marry the woman you are engaged to.
translation_verse: Ubɔ cáá bɔɔn kaa láá cáá-uaaa? Ubɔ yaa bée, ú gítí u-diikun. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, u ŋūǹ kí tin kpúń dikɔ̀ndin ní ubɔ fám ń dāá cáá u-bɔɔn gbanti.»

english_verse: Finally, if any of you are afraid, you may go home. We don't want you to discourage the other soldiers.
translation_verse: Ní bigbaŋŋmaliibee ń gíti bàlifì tin bí nee yii: «Ubɔ bí ki sá ufaantija u-mul kaa bōotí mmɔ́ɔnaaa? Udaan yaa bée, ú nīn gítí u-diikun, án nín làá ŋá pu ú taa yɔ̀tī u-nabiyaamu wuntee.»

english_verse: When the officials are finished giving these orders, they will appoint officers to be in command of the army.
translation_verse: Bigbaŋŋmaliibi yaa sòon̄ nì samaayee míǹ ki dóòyee ní bí lēē bijanjakpilib bin làá nīn līī samaa nyɔkɔpuee.

english_verse: Whenever you capture towns in the land the Lord your God is giving you, be sure to kill all the people and animals.
translation_verse: Ama an yaa kíǹ anibul ŋin timmu ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe poonee, ní kpɔ̀ tin kɔkɔ pée cáá kufoouee kí taa kíń tiba.

english_verse: He has commanded you to completely wipe out the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: An puee ní dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Eeti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Kanaan yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab kii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín kpáafì-ni puee.

english_verse: If you allow them to live, they will persuade you to worship their disgusting gods, and you will be unfaithful to the Lord.
translation_verse: An yaa kaa sá mimmee, ni làá fōō bi-waatootii tuuŋŋi ŋin sá ntimbiilee. Ni mun yaa ŋá mimmee, ni yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dee.

english_verse: When you are attacking a town, don't chop down its fruit trees, not even if you have had the town surrounded for a long time. Fruit trees aren't your enemies, and they produce food that you can eat, so don't cut them down.
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa bíi jáà nì kitiŋ kiba ní ki lùkū gíb́-kì, ní ki kpēē yii an sá ní kàl̄ niin kí yúntí ní kí nín ŋmā kí já kí fōō-kèe, ní taa yòon̄ ni-ceekub kí nīn gà isufi in sí niinee ki féeń, kun puee ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ i-biliŋ. Ní taa pée gāā-i kí fá. Isufi in yú akpaannee kaa sá binib ní nīn bíi jáà nì i!

english_verse: You may need wood to make ladders and towers to help you get over the walls and capture the town. But use only trees that you know are not fruit trees.
translation_verse: Ama ni ŋūǹ kí gàatì isufi in kaa lòoǹ abil ŋin bi ŋmóòyee kí dūú ŋá ni-jaaku tuuŋŋi kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní kitiŋ kin ni cūtì kí já kí fōōyee làá kɔ́ ni-ŋaanee.

english_verse: Suppose the body of a murder victim is found in a field in the land the Lord your God is giving you, and no one knows who the murderer is.
translation_verse: Tí dūú ŋmàntī yii kitiŋ kin ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-nee poonee, ni ká dinikpil dɔ̄ kusaau kubɔn, ní naa nyí un di kūū-uee.

english_verse: The judges and other leaders from the towns around there must find out what town is the closest to where the body was found.
translation_verse: Ni-tindaŋkpilib nì ni-bɔsoonliibi ń cù kí ŋmàntī kí yòon̄ dinikpilee nín dɔ̄ laakiŋyee kí cáá cùnnì ntimu mun māntìi tú-dèe,

english_verse: The leaders from that town will go to their cattle herds and choose a young cow that has never been put to work.
translation_verse: kí kpèè kitiŋ kin di pìlīǹ dinikpil gbantee. Niinee ní kitiŋ gbanti kpilib ń nyàab̀ kinasalii kin kaa láá kùn̄ tikpaal àá ki dáaĺ tɔrɔku ki kée,

english_verse: They and some of the priests will take this cow to a nearby valley where there is a stream, but no crops. Once they reach the valley, the leaders will break the cow's neck. The priests must be there, because the Lord your God has chosen them to be his special servants at the place of worship. The Lord has chosen them to bless the people in his name and to be judges in all legal cases, whether property or injury is involved.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibee ń nyā kí yūĺ nyɔkɔpu. Di sá yii bíǹ ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu lēē bí nīn tūǹ u-tundi ní kí nīn mèé-u ki bìintí binib pu. Bíǹ di máaǹ kí nīn sòoǹ kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu nì ubɔ yaa fáá u-juti ki tīī-u tiweendee bɔti.

english_verse: The town leaders will wash their hands over the body of the dead cow
translation_verse: Niinee ní kitiŋ kin pìlīǹ dinikpilee kpilib ń fíntí bi-ŋalii kí sìtī dinasapɔmbil din sil bi nyīī ki gííyee pu,

english_verse: and say, “We had no part in this murder, and we don't know who did it.
translation_verse: ní kí lì yii: «An kaa sá timbi di kūū unil nee. Ti-nimbiliŋ kaa ká un kūū-uee mun.

english_verse: From time to time, you men will serve as soldiers and go off to war. The Lord your God will help you defeat your enemies, and you will take many prisoners.
translation_verse: Ni yaa cūtì dikɔ̀ndi ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dū ni-nannanliibi ki ŋá ni-ŋaan ní ni jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi ki cúuń binib dikɔ̀ndin,

english_verse: One of these prisoners may be a beautiful woman, and you may want to marry her. But first you must bring her into your home, and have her shave her head, cut her nails, get rid of her foreign clothes, and start wearing Israelite clothes. She will mourn a month for her father and mother, then you can marry her.
translation_verse: ní kí lēē u-wampeeŋkaati tin u pēeń u-dumpuee kí bíĺ, ní kí nīn bí uninjee dumpu. Míǹ boonee ní ú dū uŋmamɔn kí sɔ̄ u-na nì u-baa pu. Unimpuee yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, udaan ŋūǹ kí dòon̄ nì u, ní kí dū-u kí kpántí u-nimpuu.

english_verse: Later on, if you are not happy with the woman, you can divorce her, and she can go free. But you have slept with her as your wife, so you cannot sell her as a slave or make her into your own slave. Rights of a First-Born Son Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ama boonee, udaan yaa ká yii unimpuee bɔti kaa ti mɔ̄ǹ-uee, ú yàntī-u ú búntí laakin u yaa lèe. Waa dāa ŋūǹ kí dū-u kí nyāfì, kaa dāa tí ŋūǹ kí dū-u kí kpántí u-yumbuu ŋyunti ŋun ní u cáá-u ki dóòyee. Ujipɔŋkpil fakal bɔti

english_verse: Suppose a man has two wives and loves one more than the other. The first son of either wife is the man's first-born son, even if the boy's mother is the wife the man doesn't love. Later, when the man is near death and is dividing up his property, he must give a double share to his first-born son, simply because he was the first to be born. A Son Who Rebels Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: U máaǹ kí béé yii unimpu un waa néeńee jipɔɔn di lafun sá u-jipɔŋkpiliu tiŋman pu, ní kí dū u nín làá yàkatī u-jipɔmbi kɔkɔ u-gaajawanti puee mili pu kí tīī-u. Di sá yii kibiki gbanti di sá u-biseebiki kin dàkā u-ninjatee, ní ki máaǹ kí fōō kibipeepeekaai fakal. Kibiki kin tafal pɔ̄ɔ̄yee bɔti

english_verse: A father and a mother may have a stubborn and rebellious son who refuses to obey them even after he has been punished.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa cáá kibiki ní kì cáá ntafapɔn nì ŋyipɔn, kaa tɔ́ ki-baa nì ki-na, ní báà min kɔkɔ bi sòon̄ nì kì tibɔn nì timan ki dáaĺ ki-tafalee kaa fātìi tɔ́ee,

english_verse: If a son is like that, his parents must drag him to the town gate, where the leaders of the town hold their meetings.
translation_verse: ki-baa nì ki-na ń cúú-kì kí cáá cùnnì bitindaŋkpilib bin kā bi-tiŋki punyɔkɔpuee cee.

english_verse: The parents will tell the leaders, “This son of ours is stubborn and never obeys. He spends all his time drinking and partying.”
translation_verse: Bí tùkù bitindaŋkpilibee yii: «Ti-jipɔɔn nee cáá ŋyipɔn nì ntafapɔn. Waa tɔ́-ti. Kun u pée ŋūǹee di sá binimpoobi dimɔnnil nì ndaam dinyɔl.»

english_verse: The men of the town will stone that son to death, because they must get rid of the evil he brought into the community. Everyone in Israel will be afraid when they hear how he was punished. The Body of a Criminal Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Niinee ní kitiŋ gbanti yab bin sá bininjabee ń yāŋkì-kì ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀. Ni máaǹ kí nyāntí ikpiti ni-kansikin. An yaa ŋá mimmee, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ làá gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní kí fàŋkì. Unil un bi lúntì ndɔ pu u kpíìyee bɔti

english_verse: If a criminal is put to death, and you hang the dead body on a tree,
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa yīntì ní u-yìntitam gbanti puee ni kūū-u ki dū u-wunti ki lúntì ndɔ puee,

english_verse: you must not leave it there overnight. Bury it the same day, because the dead body of a criminal hanging on a tree will bring God's curse on the land. The Lord your God is giving this land to you, so don't make it unclean by leaving the bodies of executed criminals on display.
translation_verse: ní taa yàntī kunyeeu ń mɔ́ dinikpilee ndɔ pu. Ní síb́-u ŋwiin ŋun ní ni kūū-uee, di sá yii un kamaa bi yaa lúntì ndɔ puee dátiń Unimbɔti busuu kitiŋ pu ní. Ní nīn nyí kí taa kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: If you see a cow or sheep wandering around lost, take the animal back to its owner.
translation_verse: A-nabiki naau yaa wáŋkì àá u-piiiu di wáŋkì ní a kée, á taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī. Péetí unaayee àá upiiyee kí cáá tīī u-dindaan.

english_verse: If the owner lives too far away, or if you don't know who the owner is, take the animal home with you and take care of it. The owner will come looking for the animal, and then you can give it back.
translation_verse: A-nabikee yaa kóò an dátiǹ-si àá saa pée nyí udaanee, á péetí-u kí cáá gbìn̄ a-dumpu kí nīn kpèé-u kí cáá sāā daliŋkin unaayee àá upiiyee dindaan làá dāan̄ kí nyàab̀ u-wantee, ní á gíiǹ kí tīī-u.

english_verse: That's what you should do if you find anything that belongs to someone else. Do whatever you can to help, whether you find a cow or sheep or donkey or some clothing.
translation_verse: An yaa tí sá a-nabiki maŋki àá u-bɔkutil àá u-wanti tin kamaa yaa pée wáŋkì ní a kée, a nín máaǹ kí ŋá puee dee. Á taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī a-juti wanti.

english_verse: Oxen and donkeys that carry heavy loads can stumble and fall, and be unable to get up by themselves. So as you walk along the road, help anyone who is trying to get an ox or donkey back on its feet. Don't Pretend To Be the Opposite Sex Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: A yaa tí ká a-nabiki maŋki àá u-naau lítì ki dɔ̄ nsan caŋinee, á taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī. Tūtuǹ udaan ú yòon̄ kuwaŋkuluuee kí síiń ku-taaŋi pu.

english_verse: Women must not pretend to be men, and men must not pretend to be women. The Lord your God is disgusted with people who do that. Don't Take a Mother Bird Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Unimpu kaa máaǹ kí lòon̄ tininjawan. Míǹ mbaantiim ní uninja mun kaa máaǹ kí lòon̄ tinimpuwan. Bin bin ŋáań mimmee sá bitiŋwiiliibi ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cee.

english_verse: If you build a house, make sure to put a low wall around the edge of the flat roof. Then if someone falls off the roof and is killed, it won't be your fault. Laws against Mixing Different Things Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: A yaa máń kudipɔŋuee, á bɔ̀b̄ ku-yilpu kí mā digundi kí màntīí tū yilpu laakin a bɔ̀b̄ee ubɔ ń taa láa nyā kudiiyee yilpu kí lítí kitiŋ kí dū u-kpuulool kí lúntí a-pu.

english_verse: If you plant a vineyard, don't plant any other fruit tree or crop in it. If you do plant something else there, you must bring to the place of worship everything you harvest from the vineyard.
translation_verse: A yaa kùn̄ bufiinyikpaayee, á taa dū busubu bubɔ biliŋ kí bɔ̄l̀ bukpaabaantiibuee poon. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, fiinyee nì asubil ŋin a búĺ ki kútèe yaa láa lòon̄ee, an kɔkɔ dāa sá ki tīī Unimbɔti ní.

english_verse: Don't hitch an ox and a donkey to your plow at the same time.
translation_verse: Á taa dū unaa nì kimaŋ kí kpāfì kí kpàl̄ bí kpɔ̀ tikpaal.

english_verse: When you weave cloth for clothing, you can use thread made of flax or wool, but not both together.
translation_verse: Aa máaǹ kí pèen̄ tiwan tin ní bi dū ipii kuti nì gulfa ki ŋmālim̀ ki lùn̄ee.

english_verse: Suppose a man starts hating his wife soon after they are married.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa cáá unimpu ní ki dōoǹ nì u, ní boonee kaa ti là-u,

english_verse: He might tell ugly lies about her, and say, “I married this woman, but when we slept together, I found out she wasn't a virgin.”
translation_verse: ní ki túǹ-u dibɔgabil ki bíil̀ u-yindi ki lī yii: «M nín cáá unimpu nee ki dōoǹ nì uee, maa ká kudaaŋŋu kun dàkà yii waa nìn nyí uninjee».

english_verse: If this happens, the bride's father and mother must go to the town gate to show the town leaders the proof that the woman was a virgin.
translation_verse: Niinee ní usapɔɔnee baa nì u-na ń cáań kudaaŋŋu kun dàkà yii bi-bisal kaa nìn nyí uninjee kí tīī bitindaŋkpilib bin kā kitiŋ punyɔkɔpuee.

english_verse: Her father will say, “I let my daughter marry this man, but he started hating her
translation_verse: Ní ubaati ń bí bitindaŋkpilibee yii: «M dū m-bisal ki tīī uninja nee ticati, ama waa ti là-u,

english_verse: and accusing her of not being a virgin. But he is wrong, because here is proof that she was a virgin!” Then the bride's parents will show them the bed sheet from the woman's wedding night.
translation_verse: ní ki bíi tūntí-u dibɔgabil ki lì yii m-bisal béè uninja ní ki nín mɔ́ǹ-u. Ama kpèèmaan kun dàkà yii m-bisal kaa nìn nyí uninjee.» Niinee ní ubaati ń kpátí sata un pu bi nìn dōoǹ kunyapeepeekaauee kí bíĺ bitindaŋkpilib nimbiin.

english_verse: The town leaders will beat the man with a whip
translation_verse: Ní bitindaŋkpilibee ń cúú uninjee kí dáaĺ u-tafal.

english_verse: But if the man was right and there is no proof that his bride was a virgin,
translation_verse: Ama uninjee nín lī puee yaa sá ibaamɔn ní baa lafun ká kudaaŋŋu kun dàkà yii usapɔɔnee kaa nìn lafun nyí uninjee,

english_verse: the men of the town will take the woman to the door of her father's house and stone her to death. This woman brought evil into your community by sleeping with someone before she got married, and you must get rid of that evil by killing her. Laws about Illegal Sex Moses said:
translation_verse: ní bí cáá-u kí cùnnì u-baa diiku punyɔkɔpu ní kitiŋ gbanti yab bin sá bininjabee ń yāŋkì-u ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀. Di sá yii u ŋá icoo bɔti Isirayeel tiŋkin ki kāl̀ u-baa dicaŋkun ki ŋá tilaakpaal. Míǹ ní ni máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí nyāntí ikpiti ni-kansikin.

english_verse: People of Israel, if a man is caught having sex with someone else's wife, you must put them both to death. That way, you will get rid of the evil they have done in Israel.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa dōoǹ nì u-juti nimpuu ní ni cúú-uee, ní kpɔ̀-u kí kpáaǹ unimpuee mun. Míǹ ní ni máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí nyāntí ikpiti ni-kansikin.

english_verse: If a man is caught in town having sex with an engaged woman who isn't screaming for help, they both must be put to death. The man is guilty of having sex with a married woman. And the woman is guilty because she didn't call for help, even though she was inside a town and people were nearby. Take them both to the town gate and stone them to death. You must get rid of the evil they brought into your community.
translation_verse: ní nyāntí bi-liitilee kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu kí yāŋkì-bi ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀. Bí kpɔ̀ usapɔɔnee, kun puee u bí kitiŋin kaa kúuǹ ki yíiń binib bí dāá fīī-u, ní kí kpɔ̀ uninjee, kun puee u dōoǹ nì ubɔ nimpuu. Míǹ ní ni máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí nyāntí ikpiti ni-kansikin.

english_verse: If an engaged woman is raped out in the country, only the man will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ama an yaa sá kusaaun ní ubɔ ká usapɔɔn un cáá bɔɔnee ki ŋá-u mpɔn ki dōoǹ nì uee, uninja un ŋá mimmee baba ní ni máaǹ kí kpɔ̀.

english_verse: Do not punish the woman at all; she has done nothing wrong, and certainly nothing deserving death. This crime is like murder,
translation_verse: Ní taa ŋá usapɔɔn tiba, di sá yii waa ŋá ikpiti in máaǹ ŋkúmee. Tibɔti gbantee náań nì ubɔ nín cútí u-juti kí kpɔ̀-u puee ní.

english_verse: because the woman was alone out in the country when the man attacked her. She screamed, but there was no one to help her.
translation_verse: Di sá yii uninjee ká usapɔɔn kusaaun ní. Báà usapɔɔnee yaa gbáń ibiilaaa, ubɔ kaa bí niin kí fīī-u.

english_verse: Suppose a woman isn't engaged to be married, and a man forces her to have sex with him. If he is caught,
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa tí ká usapɔɔn un kaa cáá bɔɔnee ní ki yaa ŋá mpɔn ki dōoǹ nì u ní bi yaa cúú-bee,

english_verse: If a man's private parts have been crushed or cut off, he cannot fully belong to the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Ubɔ ń taa cáá u-baa nimpoobi kansikin ubɔ. U yaa ŋá mimmee, u kpēē u-baa dooŋu fám. Bin kaa máaǹ kí nīn bí Unimbɔti samaau kansikinee

english_verse: No one born outside of a legal marriage, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can fully belong to the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Uninja un sá ufaalee àá un ninjati bi yaa gíí ki tūkutèe kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan samaau kansikin.

english_verse: No Ammonites or Moabites, or any of their descendants for ten generations, can become part of Israel, the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Unil un sá dikpacantibilee nì u-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ kí tin sāā saalaa pu gba kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan samaau kansikin.

english_verse: This is because when you came out of Egypt, they refused to provide you with food and water. And besides, they hired Balaam to put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì bi-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ kí tin sāā saalaa pu gba kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan samaau kansikin.

english_verse: But Edomites are your relatives, and you lived as foreigners in the country of Egypt. Now you must be kind to Edomites and Egyptians
translation_verse: Dalba dalba ní taa nyàab̀ atimbun ali gbanti nyɔkɔpu cùtam, kí taa píí-bi kubɔɔtiiu.

english_verse: and let their great-grandchildren become part of Israel, the Lord's people. Keep the Army Camp Acceptable Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ní taa nín kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ Eedoom yab kii bi sá ntimbiil nibee, di sá yii bi sá ni-nabiyaamu ní. Ní taa kpèè kí sìŋkīǹ Eejipiti yab mun, di sá yii ni kāl̀ bi-tiŋkin kunicaŋu.

english_verse: When you men go off to fight your enemies, make sure your camp is acceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi-naantitɔntɔkɔl ditataatiil ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan samaau kansikin. Dijanjanaapaal pu nyaŋkanti

english_verse: For example, if something happens at night that makes a man unclean and unfit for worship, he must go outside the camp and stay there
translation_verse: Ni yaa yíkì ki cá kí jáǹ ni-nannanliibi ní ki kóoǹ ki kpáfì laaba ki ŋātì dijanjanaapaalee, ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba kí taa ŋá tin kamaa kaa ŋān̄ee.

english_verse: until late afternoon. Then he must take a bath, and at sunset he can go back into camp.
translation_verse: Ni-kansikin ubɔ yaa dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ kunyeeu ní ki nyéem̀ tijati ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndinee, udaan ń nyā dinaapaalin kí taa kɔ́nní ŋwiin gbanti.

english_verse: Set up a place outside the camp to be used as a toilet area.
translation_verse: Ama kujoou yaa bíi jóotée, ú nyàab̀ nnyim kí fàl̀, ní ŋwìiń yaa jéetèe ú fàtīí gítiń bin kíǹee cee.

english_verse: You must keep your camp clean of filthy and disgusting things. The Lord is always present in your camp, ready to rescue you and give you victory over your enemies. But if he sees something disgusting in your camp, he may turn around and leave. Runaway Slaves from Other Countries Moses said:
translation_verse: Ujanjal kamaa máaǹ kí nīn cáá tigbakaal ní u yaa cūtì ataa puee, ú gbà mbòó kí sɔ́ntí, ní u yaa dóòyee ú kàfì ntam kí bìin̄.

english_verse: You can charge a foreigner interest. But if you charge other Israelites interest, the Lord your God will not let you be successful in the land you are about to take. Sacred Promises to the Lord Moses said:
translation_verse: Ni yaa pīnnì ni-nabiki animbil àá tijin àá tin ní an yaa pée sée, ní taa páb́-u ú téeǹ-ni kí páań.

english_verse: People of Israel, if you make a sacred promise to give a gift to the Lord, then do it as soon as you can. If the Lord has to come looking for the gift you promised, you will be guilty of breaking that promise.
translation_verse: Ni ŋūǹ kí pìnnì unicaan kí yàntī ú dāá téeǹ-ni kí páań, ama ní taa ŋá míǹ ni-nabiki Isirayeel niliu cee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá bìin̄ ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kitiŋ kin ni làá kɔ́ kí fōō ki nīn kíǹ ki yèe poon. Diwampoondi bɔti

english_verse: On the other hand, if you never make a sacred promise, you can't be guilty of breaking it.
translation_verse: Ni yaa pōoǹ kí ŋá tiba kí tīī ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiuee, ní pà ni-pɔndi malaa, di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá pée bàlifì-ni, ní ní dāá fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: If you go into a vineyard that belongs to someone else, you are allowed to eat as many grapes as you want while you are there. But don't take any with you when you leave.
translation_verse: Tin nyáń ni-nyɔkɔnee, see ní pɔ́ɔǹ kí ŋá míǹ, kun puee ni-ba nyɔkɔn ní an nyáń ní ni pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dipoondi. Nsan pú unil ń kìtī asubil kí ŋmɔ́

english_verse: In the same way, if you are in a grain field that belongs to someone else, you can pick heads of grain and eat the kernels. But don't cut down the stalks of grain and take them with you.
translation_verse: Ni yaa kɔ́ ni-nabiki fiinyi kpaabunee, ni ŋūǹ kí kìtī fiinyi biliŋ kí ŋmɔ́ ni nín là puee, ama ní taa kìtī kí ŋá ni-lookun.

english_verse: Suppose a woman was divorced by her first husband because he found something disgraceful about her. He wrote out divorce papers, gave them to her, and sent her away.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa cáá unimpu ní ki ká yii unimpuee bɔti kaa ti mɔ̄ǹ-u kun puee u ká u-pu tibee, ú ŋmà kugbɔŋu kun dàkà yii u jìn̄-uee kí ŋúbíǹ-u ní kí nín jà-u u-cindi.

english_verse: Since she has slept with her second husband, she cannot marry her first husband again. Their marriage would pollute the land that the Lord your God is giving you, and he would be disgusted. Newlyweds Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Niinee, u-cal peepeekaa un nìn jìn̄-uee kaa ti cáá nsan kí fàtīí cáá-u, di sá yii unimpuee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Waa ti ŋūǹ kí cáá-u. U yaa fātìi cáá-uee, an sá ntimbiil tundi ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Ní taa kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe tijɔkɔndi. Uninja un cáá unimpucaanee

english_verse: If a man and a woman have been married less than one year, he must not be sent off to war or sent away to do forced labor. He must be allowed to stay home for a year and be happy with his wife. Loans Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Uninja un cáá unimpucaanee kaa máaǹ kí cù kujaau. Baa máaǹ kí tīī-u ditundi diba mun ú tɔ̄. U cáá dibimmɔndi kí tɔ̄ u-ba kí kàl̄ mmɔŋki kí kɔ̀ntī unimpu un u cááyee nimbiliŋ. Toolima bɔti

english_verse: When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that they will pay back the loan. But don't take one or both of their millstones, or else they may starve. They need these stones for grinding grain into flour to make bread. Kidnapping Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa cáá-ni dipɔndee, ní taa cùú yòon̄ u-naaku toolima, kí taa yòon̄ u-namintidɔŋu gba. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, an bí kii ni fōō kun u ŋáań ki jīǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee ní toolima. Unil un bi cúú mpɔnee

english_verse: If you are guilty of kidnapping Israelites and forcing them into slavery, you will be put to death to remove this evil from the community. Skin Diseases Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ni yaa ká ubɔ cúú u-nabiki Isirayeel nib kansikin ubɔ ki dū-u ki kpántì u-yumbuu àá u dū-u ki nyáfèe, ní kpɔ̀ udaan. Ní ŋá míǹ kí nyāntí ikpiti ni-kansikin. Dinyaŋgbandi bɔti

english_verse: I have told the priests what to do if any of you have leprosy, so do exactly what they say.
translation_verse: An yaa sá dinyaŋgbandi weeŋŋu jandee, ní kpèè tiŋan kí ŋá kii Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibi nín dàkā yii ní ŋá puee deedee. Ni máaǹ kí ŋá tin m kpáafì-bi bí dūú dàkà-nee.

english_verse: And remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam after you left Egypt. Loans Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ní téetí ni nín nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dòoń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ŋá Miiriyam pu nsannee. Toolima bɔti tiba mun

english_verse: Wait outside, and they will bring out the item you have agreed on.
translation_verse: Ní nīn yú mmɔŋki ní ni-pɔnliu u-ba ń cáań-ni kun u làá dūú tīī-ni toolimee.

english_verse: Suppose someone is so poor that a coat is the only thing that can be offered as a guarantee on a loan. Don't keep the coat overnight.
translation_verse: Udaan yaa sá usoodaan ní ki yaa dū u-satabiiŋkaau ki tīī-ni toolimee, ní taa yàntī kutaa ń wúntí u-toolimau gbanti pu ni-dumpu.

english_verse: Instead, give it back before sunset, so the owner can keep warm and sleep and ask the Lord to bless you. Then the Lord your God will notice that you have done the right thing. Poor People's Wages Moses said:
translation_verse: Ní fàtīí gíiǹ u-satau kí tīī-u ní ŋwìiń ń nín jēetí, án nín làá ŋá pu ú ŋmā kí ká kí bìin̄ kunyeeuee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, u làá mèè kí bìin̄ ni-pu ní án nīn sá min kítì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ceeyee. Bí nīn tɔ́ usoodaan

english_verse: If you hire poor people to work for you, don't hold back their pay, whether they are Israelites or foreigners who live in your town.
translation_verse: Ní taa mùul̀ upaadaan un sá usoodaan kaa cáá tibee. An yaa sá ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab ubɔ àá binicambi bin kóò ni-tiŋkinee kansikin ubɔɔɔ, ní taa mùul̀ udaan.

english_verse: Pay them their wages at the end of each day, because they live in poverty and need the money to survive. If you don't pay them on time, they will complain about you to the Lord, and he will punish you. The Death Penalty Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ní pà u-paati ní ŋwìiń ń nín jēetí, di sá yii u sá usoodaan, ní animbil gbanti pu ní u máká. An yaa kaa sá mimmee, u làá tīminsì ti-Dindaan kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní ní kɔ́ ikpitin. Unil kamaa kpitii pu ní bi làá kpɔ̀-u

english_verse: Parents must not be put to death for crimes committed by their children, and children must not be put to death for crimes committed by their parents. Don't put anyone to death for someone else's crime. Don't Mistreat the Powerless Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Baa máaǹ kí kpɔ̀ bibaatiibi bi-biyaamu kpitii pu, kaa tí máaǹ kí kpɔ̀ mbiyaamu bi-baabi kpitii pu. Báà ŋma kpitii pu ní u máaǹ kí kpú. Bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá bisoodambi puee

english_verse: You were slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws. Leave Some of Your Harvest for the Poor Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Téetímaan yii ni nìn sá iyumbu ní Eejipiti tiŋkin ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dá-ni ki líì. An pu ní m kpáafí-ni ní ŋúb́ tibɔti nee.

english_verse: If you forget to bring in a stack of harvested grain, don't go back in the field to get it. Leave it for the poor, including foreigners, orphans, and widows, and the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
translation_verse: Ni yaa bíi cēē ni-kpaajinti ní ki yaa súntì dibɔ́ndi diba pu boonee, ní taa fàtīí gítí ni-boon kí yòon̄-dì. Ní yàntī-dì, binicambi nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi yaa bíi lúlifí ki tin kée, bí yòon̄ ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ń bìin̄ ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: When you harvest your olives, don't try to get them all for yourself, but leave some for the poor.
translation_verse: Ni yaa kītì ɔliifi biliŋee, ní taa fàtīí gítí kí lūlifì. Ní yàntī abil ŋin kíǹ ki lúń busubu puee kí tīī binicambi nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi.

english_verse: And when you pick your grapes, go over the vines only once, then let the poor have what is left.
translation_verse: Ni yaa tí kītì fiinyi biliŋee, ní taa fàtīí gítí kí lūlifì. Ní yàntī abil ŋin kíǹ ki lúńee kí tīī binicambi nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi.

english_verse: You lived in poverty as slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws.
translation_verse: Ní taa súntí yii nimbi ni-ba nìn sá iyumbu ní Eejipiti tiŋkin. An pu ní m kpáafí-ni ní ŋúb́ tibɔti nee.

english_verse: Suppose you and someone else each accuse the other of doing something wrong, and you go to court, where the judges decide you are guilty. If your punishment is to be beaten with a whip, one of the judges will order you to lie down, and you will receive the number of lashes you deserve.
translation_verse: An yaa sá bí gbá un jíń dibɔkpilee, ubɔsoonli ń yàntī ú dòon̄ kitiŋ u-nimbiin ní kí yàntī bí gbá-u anaalab. U-bɔkpil nín bàlifī bí gbá-u puee, míǹ ní bi máaǹ kí gbá-u.

english_verse: Forty lashes is the most that you can be given, because more than that might make other Israelites think you are worthless. Don't Muzzle an Ox Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ama ubɔsoonlee kaa máaǹ kí yàntī bí gbá-u kí jītí anaalab imuŋku ili pu. Kun puee bi yaa gbáń-u an jítì míǹ puee, ni kíǹ ki bíi kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ ni-nabiki dee. Unaa

english_verse: Don't muzzle an ox while it is threshing grain. A Son for a Dead Brother Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Ní taa bóob́ unaa un tà ki gbátí adibilee nyɔkɔ. Ukpiipu un kaa cáá kibikee bɔti

english_verse: But suppose the brother refuses to marry the widow. She must go to a meeting of the town leaders at the town gate and say, “My husband died without having a son to carry on his name. And my husband's brother refuses to marry me so I can have a son.”
translation_verse: Ama uninjee yaa kaa là kí fōō u-nabiki kpiipuuee, ukpiipuee ń cù kí ká bitindaŋkpilib, kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu ní kí tùkù-bi yii: «M-cal nabiki kaa là u-nabiki utaŋkpiil yindi ń nīn bí ki cá Isirayeel yab kansikin. M-cal nabiki yíì kaa là kí ŋá min u máaǹ kí ŋá kí tīī-mee.»

english_verse: The leaders will call the living brother to the town gate and try to persuade him to marry the widow. But if he doesn't change his mind and marry her,
translation_verse: Niinee ní bitindaŋkpilib ń yíiń-u tibuul ní kí sòoǹ nì u. U yaa gbíntìi tɔ́kɔ́ ki lì yii: «Maa là kí fōō ukpiipuee»,

english_verse: she must go over to him while the town leaders watch. She will pull off one of his sandals and spit in his face, while saying, “That's what happens to a man who won't help provide descendants for his dead brother.”
translation_verse: ní ukpiipuee ń còom̀ kí cù u-nimbiin bikpilib nín kā puee, ní kí tákatí u-naatakal diba ní kí tíiĺ kí pɔ̀l̄ u-nimbiin ní kí lì yii: «Bi nín ŋáań unil un kaa là kí màal̀ kí téeǹ u-nabiki yilee puee dee!»

english_verse: From then on, that man's family will be known as “the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off.” When Two Men Fight Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel tiŋki poonee bí pɔ̄ kijapaai gbanti dicaŋku diyindi yii: «Un taalin bi tákatì dinaatakalee dicaŋku.» Kujaau poon laakin baa máaǹ kí cúúyee

english_verse: If two men are fighting, and the wife of one man tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the other man's private parts,
translation_verse: Bininjab bili yaa bíi jáà ní un bi bíi gbáàyee nimpuu yaa bàà cūtì kí fīī u-cal un bíi gbáà-uee ŋaan, ní u yaa tāntì u-ŋal ki cúú un bíi gbáà u-calee ninjatee,

english_verse: you must cut off her hand. Don't have any mercy. Be Honest in Business Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: ní gāā kí gùutī u-ŋal. Ní taa sɔ̄ u-saai báà fiii pu. Nnyiŋfi nì mpúun ŋmàntitam bɔti

english_verse: Don't try to cheat people by having two sets of weights or measures, one to get more when you are buying, and the other to give less when you are selling.
translation_verse: Ní taa nín̄ tí cáá ni-dumpu asambiŋmantikaa mili pu, diba ń nīn sá dikpaandi, din kíǹee ń nīn sá kiwaai.

english_verse: If you weigh and measure things honestly, the Lord your God will let you enjoy a long life in the land he is giving you.
translation_verse: Ni máaǹ tikúti tin ni cáa ŋmàntī nnyiŋfee ń nīn sá deedee kúti, ní asambil ŋin ni cáa ŋmàntī tiwanee ń nīn sá deedee sambiliŋ. Mimmee ni làá kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá tīī-nee poon kí yúntí.

english_verse: But the Lord is disgusted with anyone who cheats or is dishonest. Wipe Out Amalek Moses said:
translation_verse: Di sá yii bin kɔkɔ ŋáań míǹ ki cáa mùul̄ee sá ntimbiil nib ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin. Bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá Amaleeki yab puee

english_verse: People of Israel, do you remember what the Amalekites did to you after you came out of Egypt?
translation_verse: Ní téetímaan Amaleeki yab nín nìn ŋá-ni pu ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dòońee.

english_verse: You were tired, and they followed along behind, attacking those who could not keep up with the others. This showed that the Amalekites have no respect for God.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn gīī kaa ti pée ŋūǹ kí ŋá tibee, ní bi cílìń ni-boon pú ki nāaǹ bin nìn pánní boonee. Baa nìn fāŋkì Unimbɔti báà fiii.

english_verse: The Lord your God will help you capture the land, and he will give you peace. But when that day comes, you must wipe out Amalek so completely that no one will remember they ever lived.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yaa láa nyántì-ni ni-nannanliibi bin māntì ki tú-nee ŋaan ki tīī-ni diŋuŋfil kitiŋ kin u làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe poonee, ní dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Amaleeki yab kitiŋ pu, án nín làá ŋá pu báà ubɔ ń taa ti téetí bi-puee. Ní taa súntí tibɔti gbanti!

english_verse: The Lord is giving you the land, and soon you will conquer it, settle down,
translation_verse: Ni làá kɔ́ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe poon. Ni yaa láa ká ŋkakaamɔnti ki kāl̀ee,

english_verse: and plant crops. And when you begin harvesting each of your crops, the very first things you pick must be put in a basket. Take them to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped,
translation_verse: báà ŋma ń dāá lēē tikpaajin tin kɔkɔ u kùn̄ kitiŋ gbantinee tipeekaal kí ŋá kukabikun, kí yòon̄ kí cùnnì mpaan ŋun pu ti-Dindaan lēē kí nīn bí ní nīn jáaḿ-uee.

english_verse: and tell the priest, “Long ago the Lord our God promised our ancestors that he would give us this land. And today, I thank him for keeping his promise and giving me a share of the land.”
translation_verse: Ni yaa bàn̄ee ní báà ŋma ń tùkù usaraaŋakpil un bí ŋyunti gbanti niinee yii: «M lì díǹ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin yii m bāań kitiŋ kin poon u nìn pōoǹ ti-naanjab yii u làá dūú tīī-tee.»

english_verse: The priest will take the basket and set it in front of the Lord's altar.
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋakpil ń fōō kukabikuee u-ŋaan kí dūú síiń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu saraafaŋŋu caŋin.

english_verse: Then, standing there in front of the place of worship, you must pray: My ancestor was homeless, an Aramean who went to live in Egypt. There were only a few in his family then, but they became great and powerful, a nation of many people.
translation_verse: Niinee ní udaan ń lì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin yii: «M-naanja nìn sá uaranja ní ki nìn tú ki yìiǹ, ní ki dāa yíkìi sīntì Eejipiti tiŋkin ki kāl̀ niin kunicaŋu. Bin nìn táá-uee kaa nìn náaǹ, ama boonee bi dāa dūu kpántì ditimbuŋkpaandi. Bi nìn cáá mpɔn ki wīikí mun.

english_verse: The Egyptians were cruel and had no pity on us. They mistreated our people and forced us into slavery.
translation_verse: Ama Eejipiti yab nìn wɔ́b́-ti ki sāaǹ-ti, ní ki nìn yāntì ti túń atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee.

english_verse: We called out for help to you, the Lord God of our ancestors. You heard our cries; you knew we were in trouble and abused.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan, ti-naanjab Nimbɔtiu ní u gbìl̄ ti-neen pu, ki ká ti-falaau nì ti-gìńdi nì bi nín wɔ́b́-ti puee.

english_verse: Then you terrified the Egyptians with your mighty miracles and rescued us from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn túń atuŋkpaan nì mpɔŋkpaan tuuŋŋi nì atuun ŋin kɔ̄ntí tifaandee

english_verse: You brought us here and gave us this land rich with milk and honey.
translation_verse: ki cáań-ti doo, ní ki dū kitiŋ kin pu ní nnaabiim nì tisiil dɔ̄ ki còol̀ nee ki tīī-ti.

english_verse: Now, Lord, I bring to you the best of the crops that you have given me. After you say these things, place the basket in front of the Lord's altar and bow down to worship him.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, m-Dindaan, m cáań-si tikpaajin tipeekaal tin m cáń kitiŋ kin ní a tīī-mee pu.» U yaa lī míǹ ki dóòyee ní ú dū kukabikuee kí síiń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin ní kí gbàan̄ kí jāam̀-u.

english_verse: Then you and your family must celebrate by eating a meal at the place of worship to thank the Lord your God for giving you such a good harvest. And remember to invite the Levites and the foreigners who live in your town. Ten Percent of the Harvest Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, ni nì Leefii yab nì binicambi bin kóò ni-puee ń dū tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī ni nì ni-dicaŋŋee kí jī kí fàal̀. Dibintataatiil poon tin bi lèekēe

english_verse: Every year you are to give ten percent of your harvest to the Lord. But every third year, this ten percent must be given to the poor who live in your town, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. That way, they will have enough to eat.
translation_verse: Dibintataatiil poonee, an dàkà yii tisaalaatiil bindi poonee, ni yaa láa lēē ni-kpaajinti kɔkɔ pu tisaalaatiil ki síiǹee, ní dāá dū-tì kí tīī Leefii yab nì binicambi bin kóò ni-puee nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi, án nín làá ŋá pu laakin ni kóòyee, bí ká kí jī kí díkée.

english_verse: Then you must pray: Our Lord and our God, you have said that ten percent of my harvest is sacred. I have obeyed your command and given this to the poor, including the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ní tùkù ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yii: «Ti nyántì ti-kpaajinti dijandi din bí circiree ti-dumpui ki dū-dì ki tīī Leefii yab nì binicambi nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi kii a nín kpáafì-ti yii tí ŋá puee. Taa fātì ti-boon ki tīī a-marab, kaa tí súntì bi-kansikin báà ubɔ mun pu.

english_verse: I have not eaten any of this sacred food while I was in mourning; in fact, I never touched it when I was unclean. And none of it has been offered as a sacrifice to the spirits of the dead. I have done everything exactly as you commanded.
translation_verse: Taa kāl̀ dikpool ki dū tisaalaatiil jandi ki jíń, kaa tí lēē-tì ŋyunti ŋun ní ti bí tijɔkɔndinee, kaa lēē mun ki ŋá saraa ki tīī utaŋkpiil ubɔ. Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, ti ŋá a nín kpáafì-ti yii tí ŋá puee deedee.

english_verse: Our Lord, look down from your temple in heaven and bless us and our land. You promised our ancestors that you would give us this land rich with milk and honey, and you have kept your promise. The Lord Is Your God, and You Are His People Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Míǹ puee gbóonní doooo yilpu laakin a kóòyee, kí bìin̄ a-niboolii Isirayeel yab nì kitiŋ kin ní a tīī-tee pu, kii a nín nìn pōoǹ ti-naanjab puee. Kitiŋ gbanti puee, nnaabiim nì tisiil di còol̀.» Isirayeel yab sá ti-Dindaan nibul

english_verse: Today the Lord your God has commanded you to obey these laws and teachings with all your heart and soul.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kpáafì-ni díǹ yii ní nīn ŋúb́ abɔkpaa nì akoobil nee. Ní pɔ́ɔm̀maan ni-ba kí ŋá kii ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ.

english_verse: In response, you have agreed that the Lord will be your God, that you will obey all his laws and teachings, and that you will listen when he speaks to you.
translation_verse: Ni lī díǹ yii ti-Dindaan sá ni-Nimbɔtiu ní ni làá nīn ŋáań u nín là puee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-marab nì u-koobiliŋ ní kí nīn tɔ́-u.

english_verse: Since you have agreed to obey the Lord, he has agreed that you will be his people and that you will belong to him, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan mun pōoǹ-ni ki lī díǹ yii ni sá u-nibul, binib bin u làá nīn yíì u-gaajawammɔntiitee kii u nín pōoǹ puee. Ní nīn ŋúb́ u-marab kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The Lord created all nations, but he will make you more famous than any of them, and you will receive more praise and honor. You will belong only to the Lord your God, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá yòon̄-ni yilpu, kí yàntī ní nīn jítiǹ atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ u náańee, kí tīī-ni tinyool, kí yàntī ní nyā diyindi kí jītíǹ ŋi-kɔkɔ. Di sá yii u là ní nīn sá u-circir nibul kii u nín lī puee ní.

english_verse: Moses stood together with the leaders and told the people of Israel: Obey all the laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
translation_verse: Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib nìn kútì Mooyiisi pu ki tīī Isirayeel yab mara nee yii: «Nín̄ ŋúb́maan marab bin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee.

english_verse: Soon you will enter the land that the Lord your God is giving to you. He is the God your ancestors worshiped, and he has promised that this land is rich with milk and honey. After you cross the Jordan River, go to Mount Ebal. Set up large slabs of stone, then cover them with white plaster and write on them a copy of these laws.
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki dóòyee, ní dāá dū ataŋkpee gbanti kí cóoń Eebaal jool pu kii m nín kpáafì-ni díǹ yii ní ŋá puee, ní kí dāá dū kaaluupiin kí pīil̀-ŋi.

english_verse: At this same place, build an altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God. But don't use stones that have been cut with iron tools.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní dū ataŋkpee ŋin baa dū kukúluu ki kpítèe kí mā ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nsaraafan niin.

english_verse: Look for stones that can be used without being cut. Then offer sacrifices to please the Lord, burning them completely on the altar.
translation_verse: Ni nín pée yōoǹ ataŋkpee ŋi bí pu amɔnee, ní dūú mā ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nsaraafan, ní kí ŋá ŋu-pu saraawɔkaa kí tīī ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Next, offer sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing, and serve the meat at a sacred meal where you will celebrate in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní dāá ŋá mpèé saraau mun, ní kí jī kí fàal̀ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin niin.

english_verse: Moses stood together with the priests and said, “Israel, be quiet and listen to me! Today you have become the people of the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Mooyiisi nì Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibee bí Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yii: «Isirayeel yab, ŋmīĺmaan kí pīlifì. Díǹ nee ni kpántì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nibul.

english_verse: So you must obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you.”
translation_verse: Nín̄ tɔ́maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, kí ŋá kii u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin m tīī-ni díǹ nee nín bí yii ní ŋá puee.»

english_verse: That same day, Moses gave them the following instructions:
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti mbaanti ní Mooyiisi tīī Isirayeel yab mara nee, yii:

english_verse: The Lord will make your businesses and your farms successful.
translation_verse: U làá bìin̄ ni-pu ntimun nì tisatin.

english_verse: You will have many children. You will harvest large crops, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats will produce many young.
translation_verse: U làá bìin̄ ni-maaliŋu pu ní bùtī, kí bìin̄ ni-kpaajinti pu, ní kí yàntī ni-naai nì ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui ń bùtī.

english_verse: You will have plenty of bread to eat.
translation_verse: U làá bìin̄ ni-pu kí gbéeǹ ni-kabiti tikpaajin ní ki gbéeǹ ni-yugutiliŋ ŋyim.

english_verse: The Lord will make you successful in your daily work.
translation_verse: U làá bìin̄ ni-nyātam nì ni-kɔ́tam pu.

english_verse: The Lord will help you defeat your enemies and make them scatter in all directions.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ ni-nannanliibi bin làá yīkì kí jáǹ-nee. Bi yaa láa dī nsambaanti pu ki dɔ́mińee, bi dāa dì isan iluli pu ní kí kpì.

english_verse: The Lord your God is giving you the land, and he will make sure you are successful in everything you do. Your harvests will be so large that your storehouses will be full.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá bìin̄ ni-pu ni-cakalaabi ń gbí tijin ní kí bìin̄ tin kamaa ní làá ŋée pu. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá bìin̄ ni-pu kitiŋ kin u làá tīī-nee poon.

english_verse: If you follow and obey the Lord, he will make you his own special people, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Ni yaa ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab, ki yaa ŋáań u nín là puee, u làá dū-ni kí kpántí u-circir nibul kii u nín pōoǹ-ni puee.

english_verse: Then everyone on earth will know that you belong to the Lord, and they will be afraid of you.
translation_verse: Ní kitiŋ pu nibuliŋ kɔkɔ ń dāa nīn kíǹ ki yíì-ni yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti yab, ní kí dāá fàŋkì-ni.

english_verse: The Lord will give you a lot of children and make sure that your animals give birth to many young. The Lord promised your ancestors that this land would be yours, and he will make it produce large crops for you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní nīn bí digbíl poon, ní màal̀ kí bùtī, ni-waŋkuti mun ń bùtī, ní ni-kpaajinti ń lòoǹ tiŋan kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan pōoǹ ni-naanjab yii u làá dūú tīī-nee poon.

english_verse: The Lord will open the storehouses of the skies where he keeps the rain, and he will send rain on your land at just the right times. He will make you successful in everything you do. You will have plenty of money to lend to other nations, but you won't need to borrow any yourself.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá pìitī kutagbɔŋu, laakin u kpáafì nnyim tiŋan puee, kí yàntī utaa ń nì ni-timmu pu ŋyunti ŋun an máaǹee, ní kí bìin̄ ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu. Atimbun tikpil dāa dòoń ni-cee, ní ní pìnnì-bi tin ni cááyee, ama nimbee, naa dāa cá ditimbundi diba cee kí pìnnì tiba.

english_verse: Obey the laws and teachings that I'm giving you today, and the Lord your God will make Israel a leader among the nations, and not a follower. Israel will be wealthy and powerful, not poor and weak.
translation_verse: Ni yaa ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab bin ní m tīī-ni díǹ nee ní ki yaa ŋáań kii bi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, ni làá nīn sá ditimbundi din làá nīn līī nyɔkɔpuee ní, ni kpá kí lūŋkì boon. Ni làá nīn pée yíkí yilpu ŋma ní, ni kpá kí sìntī taapu.

english_verse: and no one will disturb the birds and wild animals while they eat your dead bodies.
translation_verse: Ni-nikpiliŋ làá kpántí tijin ní kí tīī inoon in ŋàaǹ kutaa puee nì tiwaŋkuti tin bí kitiŋ puee, ubɔ dāa kpá kí jà-tì.

english_verse: Then everyone will look at you and your descendants and realize that the Lord has placed you under a curse.
translation_verse: Mbusub gbanti làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu nì atulim ní ki tīī nimbi nì ni-naantiibi ki nín cáa cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Israel, today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. And if you don't obey them all, he will put many curses on you.
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa kaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, ki yaa kaa ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee, mbusu un làá jēetí ni-puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: Your businesses and farms will fail.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̄-ni mbusu ntimun nì tisatin.

english_verse: You won't have enough bread to eat.
translation_verse: U làá tɔ̄-ni mbusu ni-kabiti ń lóó tikpaajin ní ni-yugutiliŋ ń lóó ŋyim.

english_verse: You'll have only a few children, your crops will be small, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats won't produce many young.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̄ ni-maaliŋu nì ni-kpaatanti nì ni-naai nì ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui mbusu.

english_verse: The Lord will make you fail in everything you do.
translation_verse: U làá tɔ̄ ni-nyātam nì ni-kɔ́tam mbusu.

english_verse: He will send dust and sandstorms instead of rain, and you will be wiped out.
translation_verse: An nín bàà sá ti-Dindaan ń yàntī utaa ń nì ni-tiŋki puee, dikpɔŋkpɔndi nì dibul ní u làá yàntī an nyēeń yilpu ki sìtīń ni-pu kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni.

english_verse: The Lord will let you be defeated by your enemies, and you will scatter in all directions. You will be a horrible sight for the other nations to see,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ni-nannanliibi ń já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-ni. Ni làá dī nsambaanti pu kí cù kí já nì bi, ama ní kí dī isan iluli pu kí sāǹ-bi. Tin làá bàn̄ ni-puee làá cúú kitiŋ pu beeŋi kɔkɔ tifaandi.

english_verse: The Lord will make you suffer with diseases that will cause oozing sores or crusty itchy patches on your skin or boils like the ones that are common in Egypt. And there will be no cure for you!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dū ibunsoon in u nìn tɔ́ Eejipiti yabee nì ncaapa nì digbàndi nì iwàlfi kí tɔ̄ ni-pu. Ni dāa kpá kí ká dicáaǹdi.

english_verse: that even in bright sunshine you will have to feel your way around like a blind person, who cannot tell day from night. For the rest of your life, people will beat and rob you, and no one will be able to stop them.
translation_verse: Ni dāa táfí an kɔkɔ kuwiŋkaŋu pu kii ujɔfu nín bí dibɔmbɔndin ki táfí puee ní. Tin kamaa ni yaa bíi ŋáańee, án kaa làá bútí-ni. Bi làá nīn wɔ́b̀-ni baabadal ní kí fūkul̀-ni. Báà ubɔ mun dāa kpá kí fīī-ni.

english_verse: Your cattle will be killed while you watch, but you won't get to eat any of the meat. Your donkeys and sheep will be stolen from you, and no one will be around to force your enemies to give them back.
translation_verse: Ni-nimbilaaliyin ní bi làá cúú ni-naai kí làntì, ama naa làá ká i-nanti kí dáká. Ni dāa sí ki kpèé ní bí yɔ̀ ni-mammu, ama baa làá fàtīí gíiǹní-mu kí tīī-ni. Bi dāa dù ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui kí tīī ni-nannanliibi, ama ubɔ kaa dāa bí kí jòó-ni.

english_verse: Your sons and daughters will be dragged off to a foreign country, while you stand there helpless. And even if you watch for them until you go blind, you will never see them again.
translation_verse: Ditimbundi diba yab làá cūtì ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib kuyuŋu, ní ní kpèè bi-saŋŋu pú kí gīī, ama kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiba nì tiba.

english_verse: You will work hard on your farms, but everything you harvest will be eaten by foreigners, who will mistreat you and abuse you for the rest of your life.
translation_verse: Dinibul din naa nyée di dāa yì ni-timmu jinti nì ni-tuntuŋku paatii kɔkɔ kí jī. Nimbee, bi dāa pée sàantí-ni ní, ki jīǹ ni-pu.

english_verse: What you see will be so horrible that you will go insane,
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin làá nīn jītí ni kāntée làá yàntī ní wáatí.

english_verse: The Lord will let you and your king be taken captive to a country that you and your ancestors have never even heard of, and there you will have to worship idols made of wood and stone.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá cáá ni nì ni-bɔtiu un ni kāaǹee kí cùnnì ditimbundi din ní nimbi nì ni-naanjab kaa nìn nyée poon. Niin ní ni dāa kíǹ ki tòotī awaa ŋin sá ataŋkpee nì idɔee.

english_verse: People of nearby countries will shudder when they see your terrible troubles, but they will still make fun of you.
translation_verse: Tin làá jītí ni-puee làá ŋá atimbun ŋin poon ní ti-Dindaan làá cáá-ni kí cùnnèe nib bitii, ní bi dāa kíǹ ki sòoǹ ni-bɔti ki bèel̄-ni.

english_verse: You will plant a lot of seed, but gather a small harvest, because locusts will eat your crops.
translation_verse: Ni làá kpɔ̀ tisati kí bɔ̄l̀ tikpil tikpil, ama ní kí cā fiii di sá yii inaakitoon làá kēefì kɔkɔ.

english_verse: You will plant vineyards and work hard at taking care of them, but you won't gather any grapes, much less get any wine, because the vines themselves will be eaten by worms.
translation_verse: Ni làá kpɔ̀ afiinyikpaan kí cóoń fiinyi sufii kí bɔ́ntí-i an nín máaǹ puee, ama naa dāa kāntí fiinyi gbanti subil báà diba kí kìtī ki dāa nín nyàab̀ ŋi-daam kí nyɔ̀. Di sá yii akoosibil di dāa dù kɔkɔ kí ŋmɔ́.

english_verse: Even if your olive trees grow everywhere in your country, the olives will fall off before they are ready, and there won't be enough olive oil for combing your hair.
translation_verse: Ni làá nīn cáá ɔliifi sufii ni-tiŋki kɔkɔ poon, ama naa dāa kāntí i-kpam kí ŋmìtī, di sá yii ni-ɔliifi sufii yaa láa lòon̄ee, abil kaa dāa bīī ní kí gbátí kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Locusts will eat your crops and strip your trees of leaves and fruit.
translation_verse: Inaakitoon dāa kpátí kí bìin̄ ni-sufii nì ni-kpaajinti pu ní kí kēefì kí céetí an kɔkɔ múb.

english_verse: Foreigners in your towns will become wealthy and powerful, while you become poor and powerless.
translation_verse: Unicaan un kóò ni-puee làá nīn jítiǹ-ni kpataaa, ní ki tɔ́kɔ́ ni-pu. Ama nimbee, ni dāa mɔ̀tīi sìntī taapu ní ki cá.

english_verse: You will be so short of money that you will have to borrow from those foreigners. They will be the leaders in the community, and you will be the followers. More Curses for Disobedience Moses said:
translation_verse: Úǹ di dāa cáá kí pìnnì-ni, ama nimbee, naa dāa cáá tiba kí pìnnì-u. U dāa sá usanliiti ní nimbi sá biboompaanliibi.

english_verse: Israel, if you don't obey the laws and teachings that the Lord your God is giving you, he will send these curses to chase, attack, and destroy you.
translation_verse: Mbusub nee kɔkɔ làá jēetí ni-pu ní kí nīn dī-ni míǹ kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni làá kpú kí céetée. Di sá yii naa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, ní kaa tí ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin u tīī-nee mun.

english_verse: If the Lord makes you wealthy, but you don't joyfully worship and honor him,
translation_verse: Ni yaa kaa jáam̀ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nì mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindin ŋyunti ŋun ní ni bí digbilinee,

english_verse: he will send enemies to attack you and make you their slaves. Then you will live in poverty with nothing to eat, drink, or wear, and your owners will work you to death.
translation_verse: ni làá kpántí ni-nannanliibi bin ti-Dindaan dāa cāabìń kí tɔ̄ ni-puee yumbui ní. Ŋkùm nì nnyinnyoo làá cúú-ni ní ní nīn kíǹ ki gàaǹ kaa ti pée cáá báà tiba. Ti-Dindaan làá dū tikúti kí bóob́ kí páań ni-gbigbipati pu kii bi nín kpàl̀ inaa in kù tikpaalee puee, kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni làá kpú kí céetí múbuee.

english_verse: Foreigners who speak a strange language will be sent to attack you without warning, just like an eagle swooping down.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá cáań ditimbundi din nyánní ndandati kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔee, ditimbundi din sooŋyi naa gbìl̀ee kí tɔ̄ ni-pu kii ukaabu nín tòó puee.

english_verse: They won't show any mercy, and they will have no respect for old people or pity for children.
translation_verse: An dāa sá ditimbundi din nib cáá inimbinaakulimee ní. Baa dāa kpèé utikpil nimbiinaaa, kaa dāa sūǹ binipɔmbi mun saai.

english_verse: All over the land that the Lord your God gave you, the enemy army will surround your towns. You may feel safe inside your town walls, but the enemy will tear them down,
translation_verse: Bi làá lùkù kí gíb́ ni-timmu kɔkɔ kí jáǹ-ni kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni-timmu mun ni máń aguŋfɔkɔ ki tú ki máká mu-pu yii ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ mu-nee ń lítí. Bi dāa lùkù kí gíb́ ntimu mun kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-nee poon ní kí jáǹ-ni.

english_verse: while you wait in horror. Finally, you will get so hungry that you will eat the sons and daughters that the Lord gave you.
translation_verse: Bi yaa láa lùkū ki gíb́ ni-timmu míǹ kí já kí fōō-muee, ni làá kɔ́ falaakpaŋkpaan poon, áli gba ni-poon biyaamu di làá kpántí ni-jinti. Tiŋman, ni làá ŋmɔ́ ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib bin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-nee nanti.

english_verse: Because of hunger, a man who had been gentle and kind will eat his own children and refuse to share the meal with his brother or wife or with his other children.
translation_verse: Di sá yii waa dāa là u nì bi-kansikin ubɔ ń yàkatī u-biyaamu nanti kí ŋmɔ́, kun puee mbiyaamuee di dāa kíǹ ki sá u-jikaati ŋyunti ŋun ní ni-nannanliibi yaa láa lùkū ki gíb́ ni-timmu kí jáǹ-nee. Ni-nannanliibee làá yàntī ni-nimbiliŋ ń mántí tikpil.

english_verse: A woman may have grown up in such luxury that she never had to put a foot on the ground. But times will be so bad that she will secretly eat both her newborn baby and the afterbirth, without sharing any with her husband or her other children. Disobedience Brings Destruction Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Di sá yii u dāa là kí ŋmɔ́ kibipɔŋ kin u dáá màl̄ee nì dibɔl dibalin u-baba, kun puee ni-nannanliibi nín lùkū ki gíb́ ni-timmu kɔkɔ pu kí jáǹ-nee làá kɔ́ǹ-ni dinimbinaamandin.

english_verse: You must obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Because if you don't respect the Lord,
translation_verse: Ni yaa kaa ŋúb́ marab bin bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee poon, kí nīn ŋáań bi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, kaa fāŋkì diyindi din cáá tinyool nì mpɔnee, an dàkà yii <Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu>,

english_verse: he will punish you and your descendants with incurable diseases,
translation_verse: ti-Dindaan làá dū maamaaci weeŋyi nì tiweeŋkpiil nì iween in pɔ̄ɔ̄ kaa pée ŋān̄ee kí tɔ̄ nimbi nì ni-naantiibi pu.

english_verse: Remember! If the Lord decides to destroy your nation, he can use any disease or disaster, not just the ones written in The Book of God's Law.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dū iween in kɔkɔ baa ŋmàn̄ marab gbɔŋku nee poonee gba kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní ní kpú kí céetí.

english_verse: There are as many of you now as the stars in the sky, but if you disobey the Lord your God, only a few of you will be left.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin nìn wīikí kii iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee dāa kīntí ní fiii, di sá yii naa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: The Lord is happy to make you successful and to help your nation grow while you conquer the land. But if you disobey him, he will be just as happy to pull you up by your roots.
translation_verse: Kii an nín nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ti-Dindaan u ŋá-ni tiŋan ki yāntì ni būtì ki bí mmɔnni puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní án làá tí fàtīí mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u ú nàan̄-ni kí kúntí-ni. U làá jà-ni kí nyāntí kitiŋ kin ni làá kɔ́ kí fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee poon.

english_verse: Those of you that survive will be scattered to every nation on earth, and you will have to worship stone and wood idols that never helped you or your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní yàl̄ kí kɔ́ atimbun kɔkɔn, kí yòon̄ kitiŋ kpaanyɔkɔ kiba kí cáá sāā kin kíǹee. Ni làá tòotī awaa ŋin sá idɔ nì ataŋkpee nimbi nì ni-naanjab kaa pée nyí ki kée.

english_verse: Each morning you will wake up to such terrible sights that you will say, “I wish it were night!” But at night you will be terrified and say, “I wish it were day!”
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin kɔkɔ làá nīn jītí ni kāntée làá bīil̀ ni-pɔbiliŋ tikpil. Kutaafaauee ní ní lì yii: «Ba dal ní ku làá jóotí dee!> ní ku yaa tí jóotèe ní ní lì yii: <Ba dal ní ku wúntí dee!>

english_verse: I told you never to go back to Egypt. But now the Lord himself will load you on ships and send you back. Then you will even try to sell yourselves as slaves, but no one will be interested.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní kɔ́ meelab kí fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin, nì min kɔkɔ u nìn lī yii: <Ni-taal gíti kpá kí tāā kitiŋ gbantinee>. Ni yaa láa bàn̄ niinee, ni dāa nyàab̀ kí dū ni-ba kí nyāfiǹ ni-nannanliibi kí bàà kpántí bi-yumbui, ama naa dāa kāntí udal.» MOOYIISI BƆJOOLKAATI (

english_verse: Moses called the nation of Israel together and told them: When you were in Egypt, you saw the Lord perform great miracles that caused trouble for the king, his officials, and everyone else in the country.
translation_verse: Ama kí dāá sāā díǹ nee, ti-Dindaan kaa tīī-ni nlandɔkɔ ní dàkafì kí béé, kaa tīī-ni animbil ní wāl̀, kaa tí tīī-ni atafal ní gbìl̄.»

english_verse: When we first camped here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan attacked, but we defeated them.
translation_verse: Ti nìn fōō bi-tiŋki ní ki dūu tīī Rubeen naakookun yab nì Gaadi naakookun yab nì Manasee naakookun yab dijandi, án nīn sá bi-kpaatanti.

english_verse: Then we captured their land and divided it among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. Keep the Agreement Moses said:
translation_verse: Nín̄ ŋúb́maan dipoondi nee koobiliŋ kí ŋá ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, ní án bútí-ni ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon.» Unimbɔti poondi bɔti páb́

english_verse: Israel, the Lord has made an agreement with you, and if you keep your part, you will be successful in everything you do.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab, díǹ nee, ni-kɔkɔ kpáfì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin, ni nì ni-kpootiliibi nì ni-naakɔti kpilib nì ni-tindaŋkpilib nì ni-bɔsoonliibi,

english_verse: Today everyone in our nation is standing here in the Lord's presence, including leaders and officials, parents and children, and even those foreigners who cut wood and carry water for us. We are at this place of worship to promise that we will keep our part of the agreement with the Lord our God.
translation_verse: kí dàkà yii ni sá u-nibul ní u mun sá ni-Nimbɔtiu kii u nín nìn pōoǹ-ni puee. Míǹ ní u nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ni-naanjab Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb mun.

english_verse: When we lived in Egypt, you saw the Egyptians worship disgusting idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. Then as we traveled through other nations, you saw those people worship other disgusting idols.
translation_verse: Bí taa ká ni-kansikin uninja àá unimpu àá kudicaŋu àá tinaakɔti tin bí doo díǹ nee kubɔ nib fātì bi-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ki cūtìi bíi tòotī atimbun gbanti waaŋi. Ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba ubɔ ń taa kpántí kii kisubiki kin cáá tiloolee.

english_verse: So make sure that everyone in your tribe remains faithful to the Lord and never starts worshiping gods of other nations. If even one of you worships idols, you will be like the root of a plant that produces bitter, poisonous fruit.
translation_verse: Ubɔ ń taa nyā ni-kansikin, ŋyunti ŋun ní u gbìl̄ dipoondi nyɔɔbuŋŋi ŋin bi sòon̄ ki pūtì nee, boonee kí gāā u-bindi kí lì yii: «Báà m yaa gbíntìi ŋáań min m lèe, m làá nīn pée bí ŋgbansɔŋfin». Yaa sá fám, unikpiti làá kpú kí kpáaǹ maanyiiba.

english_verse: You may be an Israelite and know all about the Lord's agreement with us, but he won't bless you if you rebel against him. You may think you can get away with it, but you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan kaa dāa kíikí kí dūú pɔ̄ udaan, see ú dāá yàntī u-ŋuul ń lítí u-pu ní mbusub bin kɔkɔ bi ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋu nee poonee ń jēetí u-pu. Ti-Dindaan làá kpìtī udaan yindi kitiŋ pu.

english_verse: The Lord will be furious, and instead of forgiving you, he will separate you from the other tribes. Then he will destroy you, by piling on you all the curses in The Book of God's Law, and you will be forgotten forever.
translation_verse: Ni-biyaamu mun làá dāá páanní ni-boonee nì binicambi bin làá dāá nyānní ntimu mun dátèe poon làá dāá ká asaluu un gbáń kitiŋ gbantee nì iween in ti-Dindaan dūu tɔ́ ki-puee ní kí lì yii:

english_verse: has become a scorching desert of salt and sulfur, where nothing is planted, nothing sprouts, and nothing grows. It will be as lifeless as the land around the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, after the Lord became angry and destroyed them.
translation_verse: Niinee ní atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee nib ń dāá bàlifì yii: «Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan nín ŋá kitiŋ nee míǹ dee? Ba pu ní u fōō mbum míǹ tikpil dee?»

english_verse: People from other nations will ask, “Why did the Lord destroy this country? Why was he so furious?”
translation_verse: Ní bí dāá kíí-bi yii: «Kun pu tin bí nee bāań-bee di sá yii bi fātì bi-boon ki tīī dipoondi din ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ-bi ŋyunti ŋun ní u nìn nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee.

english_verse: And they will be given this answer: Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, but after he brought them out of Egypt and made an agreement with them, they rejected the agreement
translation_verse: Bi cūtìi bíi tòotī awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapu. Awaa gbantee, baa nìn nyí-ŋaaa, ti-Dindaan mun kaa nìn pú nsan bí nín tòotī-ŋi.

english_verse: and decided to worship gods that had never helped them. The Lord had forbidden Israel to worship these gods,
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní ti-Dindaan gíí kitiŋ gbanti nib pu diŋuul ní ki yāntì mbusub bin kɔkɔ bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee poonee jéetì bi-pu.

english_verse: and so he became furious and punished the land with all the curses in The Book of God's Law. Then he pulled up Israel by the roots and tossed them into a foreign country, where they still are today.
translation_verse: Tin tin bí dibalinee, ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu di yì, ama tin nyáń ki pá mpaampiin puee, timbi nì ti-naantiibi di yì kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. Tíǹ di sá yii tí nīn ŋúb́ marab nee bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: I have told you everything the Lord your God will do for you, and I've also told you the curses he will put on you if you reject him. He will scatter you in faraway countries, but when you realize that he is punishing you,
translation_verse: Dibiindi nì mbusub bɔti tin m dūu bíl̀ ni-nimbiin nee làá dāá ŋá míǹ. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yaa láa yāntì ni yàl̄ ki búntì nnicantimunee, ní dāá dàkafì tibɔti gbanti pu tiŋan.

english_verse: return to him with all your heart and soul and start obeying the commands I have given to you today.
translation_verse: Nimbi nì ni-biyaamu làá fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cee kí nīn kíǹ ki tɔ́-u nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ, kí nóó nì tin kɔkɔ m dūu kpáafì-ni díǹ nee.

english_verse: Then he will stop punishing you and treat you with kindness. He may have scattered you to the farthest countries on earth, but he will bring you back
translation_verse: Báà ni yaa yàl̄ ki bínní kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá cù niin kí kóoǹní ni-kɔkɔ kí kpāfì kí fàtīí gíiǹní-ni.

english_verse: to the land that had belonged to your ancestors and make you even more successful and powerful than they ever were.
translation_verse: U làá dāá fàtīí gíiǹní-ni ni-naanjab tiŋkin, ní ní dāá fōō-kì kí nīn kíǹ ki yì. U làá dāá fàtīí tīī-ni mmɔn ní kí yàntī ní bùtī kí jītíǹ ni-naanjab.

english_verse: You and your descendants are stubborn, but the Lord will make you willing to obey him and love him with all your heart and soul, and you will enjoy a long life.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá kpántí ni nì ni-naantiibi pɔbiliŋ, án nín làá ŋá pu ní dāá nīn kíǹ ki néeń-u nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ, kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee.

english_verse: Then the Lord your God will remove the curses from you and put them on those enemies who hate and attack you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá dū mbusub nee kɔkɔ kí tɔ̄ ni-nannanliibi nì bin ná-ni ki sàantí-nee pu.

english_verse: You will again obey the laws and teachings of the Lord,
translation_verse: Nimbee, ní dāá fàtīí nīn tɔ́ ti-Dindaan kí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab bin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee.

english_verse: and he will bless you with many children, large herds and flocks, and abundant crops. The Lord will be happy to do good things for you, just as he did for your ancestors.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan ń dāá yàntī án bútí-ni ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon tikpil, kí bùtī ni-maaliŋu nì ni-waŋkuti ní kí yàntī ni-kpaajinti ń lòoǹ. Di sá yii án làá dāá fáatíǹ ti-Dindaan ú ŋá-ni tiŋan kii an nín nìn fáatiǹ-u u ŋá ni-naanjab puee.

english_verse: But you must decide once and for all to worship him with all your heart and soul and to obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Choose Life, Not Death Moses said to Israel:
translation_verse: Kí wàatī míǹ ń nín ŋée, asee ní nīn tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin bi ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá marab gbɔŋku nee poonee, ní kí fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan cee nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ. Dinyɔɔbundee dɔ̄ ki kɔ́ĺ-si

english_verse: His commands aren't in heaven, so you can't excuse yourselves by saying, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are in heaven, and no one can go up to get them, then bring them down and explain them to us.”
translation_verse: Baa bíń yilpu ní ní lì yii: «Ŋma di làá jɔ̄m̀ yilpu kí nyàab̀-bi kí cáań kí tùkù-ti, án nín làá ŋá pu tí ŋmā kí béé kí ŋá kii bi nín bí yii tí ŋá puee?»

english_verse: And you can't say, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are across the sea, and someone must go across, then bring them back and explain them to us.”
translation_verse: Baa tí bí tiŋku gbandi lapu yal ní ní lì yii: «Ŋma di làá dùtī tiŋku kí nyàab̀-bi kí cáań kí tùkù-ti, án nín làá ŋá pu tí ŋmā kí béé kí ŋá kii bi nín bí yii tí ŋá puee?»

english_verse: No, these commands are nearby and you know them by heart. All you have to do is obey!
translation_verse: Aayee, dinyɔɔbundee dɔ̄ ki kɔ́ĺ-ni. Di kā ni-nyɔkɔn ki kā ni-pɔbilin, án nín làá ŋá pu ní ŋmā kí ŋá kii di nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. Lēē dimaŋfal saŋŋu

english_verse: Today I am giving you a choice. You can choose life and success or death and disaster.
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan, díǹ nee, m dū dimaŋfal nì nnaam, ŋkúm nì nnaabu ki bíl̀ ni-nimbiin.

english_verse: Now I call the sky and the earth to be witnesses that I am offering you this choice. Will you choose for the Lord to make you prosperous and give you a long life? Or will he put you under a curse and kill you? Choose life!
translation_verse: Kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ sá-mi biseeradambi díǹ yii m dū dimaŋfal nì ŋkúm, dibiindi nì mbusu ki bíl̀ ni-nimbiin ní lēē. Ama ní lēē dimaŋfal án nín làá ŋá pu ni nì ni-naantiibi ń nīn bí dimaŋfalinee.

english_verse: Be completely faithful to the Lord your God, love him, and do whatever he tells you. The Lord is the only one who can give life, and he will let you live a long time in the land that he promised to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Nín̄ néeḿmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kí nīn tɔ́-u, kí dū ni-ba kí nákáǹ-u. Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní nīn bí dimaŋfalin, ní kí yàntī ní kàl̄ kitiŋ kin poon u nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ni-naanjab Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb yii u làá tīī-bee kí yúntí.

english_verse: Moses again spoke to the whole nation of Israel:
translation_verse: Mooyiisi cūtì ki dū tibɔti nee ki tùkū Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Be brave and strong! Don't be afraid of the nations on the other side of the Jordan. The Lord your God will always be at your side, and he will never abandon you.
translation_verse: Ní pɔ́ɔm̀maan ni-ba kí ká dipɔbil. Ní taa fàŋkìmaan-bi kí taa yàntī ni-pɔbiliŋ ń bīil̀ bi-nimbiin. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá nīn bí ni-cee. Waa làá yàntī-ni, kaa làá dū-ni kí fá mun.»

english_verse: Then Moses called Joshua up in front of the crowd and said: Joshua, be brave and strong as you lead these people into their land. The Lord made a promise long ago to Israel's ancestors that this land would someday belong to Israel. That time has now come, and you must divide up the land among the people.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi yíiń Joosuwa ki tùkū-u Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin yii: «Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil, di sá yii sii di làá cáá dinibul nee kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ní ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ kí tīī bi-naanjabee poon. Sii di làá yàkatī kitiŋ gbanti kí tīī bi-kɔkɔ an kpántí bi-kpaatanti.

english_verse: The Lord will lead you into the land. He will always be with you and help you, so don't ever be afraid of your enemies. Read These Laws
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di làá nīn līī a-nyɔkɔpu ní kí nīn bí a-cee. Waa làá yàntī-si, kaa làá dū-si kí fá mun. Míǹ puee á taa fàŋkì, kí taa yàntī a-wunti ń yɔ̀tī». Bi máaǹ kí nīn kàaǹ marab abin aluli kamaa

english_verse: Moses wrote down all of these laws and teachings and gave them to the priests and the leaders of Israel. The priests were from the Levi tribe, and they carried the sacred chest that belonged to the Lord.
translation_verse: Niinee Mooyiisi ŋmàn̄ Unimbɔti marab ki dūu tīī Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibi bin tūntí ti-Dindaan poondi dakaauee nì Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Moses told these priests and leaders: Each year the Israelites must come together to celebrate the Festival of Shelters at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. You must read these laws and teachings to the people at the festival every seventh year, the year when loans do not need to be repaid.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ làá cù ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin mpaan ŋun pu u làá dāá lēē kí nīn bí ní nīn jáaḿ-uee. Ní dāá kàaǹ marab nee Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin án kɔ́ bi-tafalin.

english_verse: Everyone must come—men, women, children, and even the foreigners who live in your towns. And each new generation will listen and learn to worship the Lord their God with fear and trembling and to do exactly what is said in God's Law. Israel Will Reject the Lord
translation_verse: Niinee, ni-biyaamu mun kaa nìn dá láá nyí marab gbantee ń gbìl̄, ní kí bīfì kí nīn kíǹ ki fàŋkí ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu iwiin in kɔkɔ ni cáá kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ní ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí cùú fōō kí nín kíǹ ki yì nee poonee.» Isirayeel kaa làá yūĺ nì Unimbɔti deedee

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “You will soon die, so bring Joshua to the sacred tent, and I will appoint him the leader of Israel.” Moses and Joshua went to the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kpèè, a-wiiŋyi kaa ti náaǹ, a-kúm wiiŋŋu tóobiń. Míǹ puee yíiń Joosuwa ni-kɔkɔ ń dāan̄ kí sīĺ dikpafindi tantiun ḿ tùkù-u tin ní u máaǹ kí ŋée.» Ní Mooyiisi nì Joosuwa cūtìi kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki síl̀.

english_verse: and the Lord appeared in a thick cloud right over the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Bi bí niinee ní ti-Dindaan dɔ́miń bi-cee ntagbanloon poon ní ntagbanloonee cūtì ki síl̀ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: The Lord said: Moses, you will soon die. But Israel is going into a land where other gods are worshiped, and Israel will reject me and start worshiping these gods. The people will break the agreement I made with them,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kpèè, a làá cùú dòon̄ kí ŋàl̄ a-naanjab dee. A-kúm boonee dinibul nee làá cù kí nīn tòotī awaa ŋin bin bí kitiŋ kin bi làá kɔ́ kí fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee tòotēe. Bi làá dāá dū-mi kí fá ní kí kpìtī dipoondi din m pōoǹ-bee.

english_verse: and I will be so furious that I will abandon them and ignore their prayers. I will send disasters and suffering that will nearly wipe them out. Finally, they will realize that the disasters happened because I abandoned them.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá gíí bi-pu diŋuul, kí dū-bi kí fá ní kí fàtī m-boon kí tīī-bi. Agìń tikpil nì dinimbinaamandi làá dāá jēetí bi-pu kí nàan̄-bi ní bi dāa kíǹ ki bàlifī bi-ba yii: <Agìń nee yaa bíi bàń-tee, mimmee an kaa sá ti-Nimbɔtiu nín kaa ti bí ti-kansikinee di yì-tàaa?>

english_verse: They will pray to me, but I will ignore them because they were evil and started worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Bi-kpitii in bi bíi ŋáań ŋyunti ŋun bi cūtìi bíi tòotī awaayee pu ní m làá dāá mɔ̀tīí fàtī m-boon kí tīī-bi.

english_verse: Moses and Joshua, I am going to give you the words to a new song. Write them down and teach the song to the Israelites. If they learn it, they will know what I want them to do, and so they will have no excuse for not obeying me.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ŋmàmaan nlan ŋun m làá dàkà-ni nee nyɔɔbuŋŋi kí síiń. Sii Mooyiisi, á cáá nlanee kí dàkà Isirayeel yab ní kí yàntī bí bīfì-ŋu kí nīn gà-ŋu. Di sá yii nlan gbanti di làá dāá nīn sá m-seeradaaŋwu Isirayeel yab cee.

english_verse: I am bringing them into the land that I promised their ancestors. It is a land rich with milk and honey, and the Israelites will have more than enough food to eat. But they will get fat and turn their backs on me and start worshiping other gods. The Israelites will reject me and break the agreement that I made with them.
translation_verse: M làá cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ní m pūtì ki pōoǹ kí tīī bi-naanjabee, kitiŋ kin pu ní nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee. Bi làá dāá jī kí díkí kí ŋá ŋkpam ní boonee bí dāá cù kí nīn tòotī awaa. Bi làá dāá kpèè-mi fám ní kí gbá kí kpìtī m-poondi.

english_verse: When I punish the Israelites and their descendants with suffering and disasters, I will remind them that they know the words to this song, so they have no excuse for not obeying me. I will give them the land that I promised, but I know the way they are going to live later on.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun agìń nì dinimbinaamandi yaa láa bàn̄-bee, nlan nee di làá dāá lēē seera kí kpɔ̀ bi-bɔti. Di sá ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu gba kaa làá dāá súntí nlan nee. Bi làá dāá nīn pée téetí ní ki gà-ŋu. M nyí kun bí binib nee pɔbiliŋinee kí wàatī gba ní ḿ nín cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin m nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ yii m làá tīī-bee poon.»

english_verse: Moses at once wrote down the words to the song, and he taught it to the Israelites.
translation_verse: Yaadal ní Mooyiisi ŋmàn̄ nlanee ní ki dū-ŋu ki dàkā Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua, “Be brave and strong! I will help you lead the people of Israel into the land that I have promised them.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan kpáafì Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa ní ki bí-u yii: «Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil, di sá yii sii di làá cáá Isirayeel yab kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin m pūtì ki pōoǹ kí tīī-bee poon. Mama m-ba làá nīn bí a-cee.»

english_verse: Moses wrote down all these laws and teachings in a book,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Mooyiisi ŋmàn̄ marab nee kɔkɔ ki ŋá kugbɔŋun ki dóòyee,

english_verse: then he went to the Levites who carried the sacred chest and said:
translation_verse: ní u kpáafì Leefii yab bin tūntí ti-Dindaan poondi daakaauee yii:

english_verse: This is The Book of God's Law. Keep it beside the sacred chest that holds the agreement the Lord your God made with Israel. This book is proof that you know what the Lord wants you to do.
translation_verse: «Yòom̄maan marab gbɔŋku nee kí dū-u kí bíĺ kí kɔ́ĺ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu poondi dakaau. Niin ní u làá nīn bí kí nīn sá seeradaan ki kù ni-bɔti.

english_verse: I know how stubborn and rebellious you and the rest of the Israelites are. You have rebelled against the Lord while I have been alive, and it will only get worse after I am gone.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m nyí ni-pu, m nyí ni-pɔɔpɔŋŋu pu. Ni yaa jáń nì ti-Dindaan ŋyunti ŋun ní m dá bí dimaŋfalin ki bí ni-cee nee, kin ataa aŋa pu ní, m-kúm boonee, naa dāa jáà nì u kí jītíǹ míǹ?

english_verse: So call together the leaders and officials of the tribes of Israel. I will bring this book and read every word of it to you, and I will call the sky and the earth as witnesses that all of you know what you are supposed to do.
translation_verse: Kóom̀maan ni-naakɔti kpilib nì ni-kpootiliibi kɔkɔ bí kpāfì m-cee, ḿ sòoǹ nì bi tibɔti nee bí gbìl̄ ní kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ mun ń nīn sá m-seeradambee.

english_verse: I am going to die soon, and I know that in the future you will stop caring about what is right and what is wrong, and so you will disobey the Lord and stop living the way I told you to live. The Lord will be angry, and terrible things will happen to you. The Song of Moses
translation_verse: Di sá yii m nyí yii m-kúm boonee ni làá dāá kɔ́ ikpitin ní kí dāá fàtī ni-boon kí tīī tibɔti tin m dūu kpáafì-ni nee. Ŋyunti gbantee, ni-kpitii in ni làá dāá ŋá ti-Dindaan nimbiinee nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ ŋin ni làá dāá ŋá kí yàntī ú gíí diŋuulee puee, digìńdi làá dāá kɔ́-ni.» Mooyiisi laŋŋu

english_verse: Moses called a meeting of all the people of Israel, so he could teach them the words to the song that the Lord had given him. And here are the words:
translation_verse: Niinee ní Mooyiisi dū nlan nee nyɔɔbuŋŋi ki sòon̄ mpɔn an kɔ́ Isirayeel nikitil kɔkɔ tafalin.

english_verse: Earth and Sky, listen to what I say!
translation_verse: Kutagbɔŋu, pīlifì m-bɔti, kitiŋ, pīlifì m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi.

english_verse: Israel, I will teach you. My words will be like gentle rain on tender young plants, or like dew on the grass.
translation_verse: M-bɔti tin m dàkèe yàantí kii utaayee, ní m-nyɔɔbundi tòó kii dimalindee, kii utaaja nín nì ki sɔ̀ŋkī kumɔsɔŋu puee, kii putipuuki nín yàantí kumoou pu puee.

english_verse: Join with me in praising the wonderful name of the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Di sá m làá nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan yindi. Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kpaanti.

english_verse: The Lord is a mighty rock, and he never does wrong. God can always be trusted to bring justice.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sá kutaŋkpanaakoou. Inaatuu kpá u-tuuŋŋi poon, u-saŋyi kɔkɔ tèen̄ ní. U sá deedee Nimbɔtiu ní, ikpiti kpá u-ni, ibaamɔn nì deedeedaan ní u sá.
