english_verse: But you lie and cheat and are unfaithful to him. You have disgraced yourselves and are no longer worthy to be his children.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin ŋáań ikpiti ki gáatèe, ni yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan. Án nīn cáá-ni icoo! Naa ti sá u-biyaamu!

english_verse: Israel, the Lord is your Father, the one who created you, but you repaid him by being foolish.
translation_verse: Dinibul din nib sá bigbaambi ki lóò dinyilee, mimmee tipaal tin ni làá dūú pà ti-Dindaanee deeee? Úǹ di kaa sá ni-baa ki tīī-ni dimaŋfalaaa? Úǹ di kaa náań-ni ki dū-ni ki kpántì u-nibulaaa?

english_verse: Think about past generations. Ask your parents or any of your elders. They will tell you
translation_verse: Téetímaan iyuntikpiki pu, dàkafìmaan ni-naanjab yuntii pu. Bàlifìmaan ni-baabi bí tùkù-ni! Ní bàlifì ni-tikpilib bí māafì-ni!

english_verse: that God Most High gave land to every nation. He assigned a guardian angel to each of them,
translation_verse: Yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu nín nìn tīī atimbun kɔkɔ bi-timmuee, ŋyunti ŋun u nìn cúú anibul kɔkɔ ki yākatì tɔbinee, u nìn tīī ditimbundi kamaa di-kpaanyɔkɔ ki nóó nì Isirayeel yab nyɔkɔm ní.

english_verse: but the Lord himself takes care of Israel.
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan nibul di sá u-fakal, Jaakɔb naantiibi ní u lēē kí nīn yì.

english_verse: Israel, the Lord discovered you in a barren desert filled with howling winds. God became your fortress, protecting you as though you were his own eyes.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn ká u-nibul kuteeun, laakin bi gbìl̀ jiiŋkpaaibi siim ŋmaniŋma puee. U nìn wúń bi-pu ki dàkà-bi, u nìn cí-bi kii u-nimbibuliiyee.

english_verse: The Lord was like an eagle teaching its young to fly, always ready to swoop down and catch them on its back.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá kii ukaalun nín ŋáań pu, kí yòon̄ u-biyaamu kí jɔ̄m̀ yilpu kí gíiǹ-mu kí líiń pu ní kí kpátiń u-feeŋyi kí nīn sìntīń pu ki cí mun yaa gīīyee ń dāá páań puee ní.

english_verse: Israel, the Lord led you, and without the aid of a foreign god,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan baba di nìn kpōotì u-nibul, unimbɔti ubɔ kaa nìn bí ki kútì u-pu.

english_verse: he helped you capture the land. Your fields were rich with grain. Olive trees grew in your stony soil, and honey was found among the rocks.
translation_verse: U nìn kāaǹ-bi ŋgbantamu pu, ní ki dū tikpaajin ki kpíiǹ-bi. U lēē tisiil ntaŋkpalɔkɔn ki tīī-bi bi ŋmɔ́, ní ki nyántì ŋkpam ditaŋkpayaabulin ki tīī-bi bi jíń.

english_verse: Your flocks and herds produced milk and yogurt, and you got choice meat from your sheep and goats that grazed in Bashan. Your wheat was the finest, and you drank the best wine.
translation_verse: U nìn tīī-bi waagaasii nì mpibiim, ki tīī-bi apibil nì iŋɔjaa nì ipijaa in bí màlmalee, ki tīī-bi bileemɔnti yim bi jíń, ní ki tīī-bi fiinyi damam bi nyùn̄.

english_verse: Israel, you grew fat and rebelled against God, your Creator you rejected the Mighty Rock, your only place of safety.
translation_verse: Yeesurun jíń ki díkí ki ŋá ŋkpamee, ní ki kíǹ ki bíi tòó igbeen. U gbīfiǹ ki ŋá ŋkpam ki ŋá gbàlgbalee, ní ki dū Unimbɔti un náań-uee ki fá, ki kíǹ ki kpèé un sá u-taŋkpanaakooku nì u-fiiliuee fám.

english_verse: You made God jealous and angry by worshiping disgusting idols and foreign gods.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ki yāntì Unimbɔti gíí diŋuul. Bi nìn dū bi-waatuuŋŋi ki gbítì u-ŋuul.

english_verse: You offered sacrifices to demons, those useless gods that never helped you, new gods that your ancestors never worshiped.
translation_verse: Bi nìn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì arasiniibi, kaa sá Unimbɔti. Bi nìn ŋáań ki tìì awaa ŋin baa nìn nyí ki kée, awaapɔɔn ŋin bi dáá nyántì bi-baabi kaa nìn nyí ŋi-pu gbee.

english_verse: You turned away from God, your Creator; you forgot the Mighty Rock, the source of your life.
translation_verse: «Isirayeel, a súntì a-taŋkpanaakooku pu, a súntì un màl̄-see pu, kaa ti dū Unimbɔti un tīī-si dimaŋfalee ki yíiń tiba.»

english_verse: You were the Lord's children, but you made him angry. Then he rejected you
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ká mimmee ní ki gíí diŋuul, u-jipɔmbi nì u-bisalib yīntiǹ-u ní u dū-bi ki fá.

english_verse: and said, “You are unfaithful and can't be trusted. So I won't answer your prayers; I'll just watch and see what happens to you.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan lī yii: «M làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-bi, ní kí kpèè án nín làá dāá kúntíǹ-bi puee. Kun puee bi sá binib bin gáatèe ní, binib bin pu baa ŋūǹ kí nīn mákée.

english_verse: You worshiped worthless idols, and made me jealous and angry! Now I will send a cruel and worthless nation to make you jealous and angry.
translation_verse: Bi yāntì kun kaa sá Unimbɔtee fōō m-paaŋŋu ki kɔ́ǹ-mi ipoompoon, ní ki dū bi-waaŋi ŋin kaa bí tibanee ki gbítì m-ŋuul. Ma mun làá dū dinibul din kaa sá m-yalee kí kɔ́ǹ-bi ipoompoon, ní kí yàntī bí fōō diŋuul binib bin kaa cáá iciinee pu.

translation_verse: Di sá m-ŋuul bíi fòol̄ lìblib kii ŋŋmee. Di wùn̄ ki tin bàn̄ ditaŋkpiil taapu, di wùn̄ ki kpáaǹ kitiŋ nì tin kɔkɔ ki lòon̄ee, ki làá póotí kí wà ajoon nyeel.

translation_verse: M làá tɔ̄-bi agìń tikpil poon, m làá tɔ̄-bi m-piiŋyi.

translation_verse: «M dākafì kí bàà nà-bi ní dúsi dusi, ní kí kúntí bi-yindi kitiŋ pu kpataaa.

translation_verse: Ama kun m fāŋkèe di sá bi-nannanliibi siibiliŋ. Bi ŋūǹ kí taa gbìl̄ taapu ní kí lì yii: <An sá ti-kpabil di tīī-ti dijajil, an kaa sá bi-Dindaan di ŋá tin bí nee.>

english_verse: When only a few of the Lord's people remain, when their strength is gone, and some of them are slaves, the Lord will feel sorry for them and give them justice.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan làá dāá sòoǹ kí pɔ̀ u-nibul, ní kí dāá sɔ̄ u-tɔntɔnliibi saai ŋyunti ŋun u yaa láa ká yii baa ti cáá mpɔn, ní uyumbu àá un tɔ́ u-bee kaa ti bée.

english_verse: But first the Lord will say, “You ran for safety to other gods— couldn't they help you?
translation_verse: U làá dāá bàlifì yii: <Bi-waaŋi ŋin nìn sá bi-taŋkpanaakooku bi sáń ki kóòyee bí la ní?

translation_verse: Awaa ŋin nìn ŋmóò bi-saraabi kpam, ki nyù ndaam min bi féeń-ŋee bí la? Ŋí yīkì kí dāá fīī-baa! Ŋí nyàab̀ kibalilaŋ kí tīī-baa!>

english_verse: Don't you understand? I am the only God; there are no others. I am the one who takes life and gives it again. I punished you with suffering. But now I will heal you, and nothing can stop me!
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ní béémaan díǹ yii, man baba di sá Unimbɔti, ubɔ kaa ti bí ki kútì man pu. Man di ŋūǹ kí lēē unil maŋfal, man di tí ŋūǹ kí tīī dimaŋfal. Man di tìì tiweendi, man di tí cāantí, ní ubɔ kaa bí ki ŋūǹ kí fīī un kā man ŋaanee.

english_verse: “I make this solemn promise: Just as I live forever,

english_verse: I will take revenge on my hateful enemies. I will sharpen my sword and let it flash like lightning.
translation_verse: M yaa lōoǹ m-tàataajiki kì jītí pámpam ki dū-kì ki tākaǹ m-ŋaan kí kíĺ ibɔsoonee, m làá tɔ̀ m-nannanliibi ipɔntoon, ní kí pà bin kɔkɔ ná-mee bi-kpitii paati.

english_verse: My arrows will get drunk on enemy blood; my sword will taste the flesh and the blood of the enemy. It will kill prisoners, and cut off the heads of their leaders.”
translation_verse: M-piiŋyi làá dāá nyɔ̀ fatiku kí gbí, ní m-tàataajiki ń dāá ŋmɔ́ bin fōō tiweendee nì bin bi cúú kuyuŋuee nanti, ki kpáaǹ binannanliibi kpilib yiliŋ.>

english_verse: Tell the heavens to celebrate and all gods to bow down to the Lord, because he will take revenge on those hateful enemies who killed his people. He will forgive the sins of Israel and purify their land.
translation_verse: Atimbun, ní pàkàmaan ti-Dindaan nikitil, di sá yii ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̀ u-tɔntɔnliibi bin bi kūūyee pɔntooŋyi, kí dáaĺ u-nannanliibi tafal, ní kí fíntí u-tiŋki nì u-nikitil kpitii.

english_verse: Later that day the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ŋwimbaanti gbantee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Mooyiisi yii:

english_verse: Go up into the Abarim Mountain range here in Moab across the Jordan River valley from Jericho. And when you reach the top of Mount Nebo, you will be able to see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to Israel.
translation_verse: «Cù Abariim jooŋŋi ŋin bí Moowaab tiŋkin, Jeeriikoo tiŋki nyɔkɔpuee kí jɔ̄m̀ Neeboo jool pu kí kpèè Kanaan tiŋki kin m làá dūú tīī Isirayeel yab bí nīn kíǹ ki yèe.

english_verse: Then you will die and be buried on the mountaintop, just as your brother Aaron died and was buried on Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Dijool din a làá jɔ̄m̀ee pu ní a làá tin kpú kí cùú ŋàl̄ a-naanjab, kii a-maan Aarɔn nín kpíì Ɔɔr jool pu ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-yab puee.

english_verse: Both of you were unfaithful to me at Meribah Spring near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. I am God, but there in front of the Israelites, you did not treat me with the honor and respect I deserve.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn bàn̄ Meeriiba Kadeesi, Siini teeku puee, ni-liitil kaa nìn ŋá Isirayeel yab nimbiin kii m nín nìn bí yii ní ŋá pu kí ká nnyimee, kaa nìn tí dàkā Isirayeel yab yii m sá circir.

english_verse: So I will give the land to the people of Israel, but you will only get to see it from a distance.

english_verse: Moses was a prophet, and before he died, he blessed the tribes of Israel by saying:
translation_verse: Kí wàatī Unimbɔti niliu Mooyiisi ń kpúee, u nìn mēē ki bīiǹ Isirayeel yab pu.

translation_verse: U nìn lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan nyánní Siinaayi jool pu, u nyáń ki páaǹní Seeyiir jool watil pú, ní ki ŋmíntì u-samaau pu doooo Paaran jool pu. U bāań Meeriiba Kadeesi. Niin ní u nìn ŋúbiń marab bin jìl̀ee u-ŋaan kí tīī-bi.

english_verse: The Lord loves the tribes of Israel, and he protects his people. They listen to his words and worship at his feet. *

translation_verse: Marab bin ní Mooyiisi tīī-tee, Jaakɔb naantiibi gaajawanti dee.

translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun samaa kpilib nìn kpáfì ki kpáaǹ Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔee, ti-Dindaan di nìn sá Yeesurun bɔtiu.»

english_verse: Tribe of Reuben, you will live, even though your tribe will always be small.

english_verse: At Massah and Meribah Spring, the Lord tested you, tribe of Levi. You were faithful, and so the priesthood belongs to the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: U sòon̄ Leefii naakooku pu yii: «Ti-Dindaan, a dū a-Tumiimuu nì a-Uriimuu ki tīī unil un fáatiǹ-see ní. A nìn cɔ́ŋkì-u Maasa, sii nì u nìn kpáká Meeriiba nyim laŋki.

english_verse: Protecting Israel's agreement with the Lord was more important to you than the life of your father or mother, or brothers or sisters, or your own children.
translation_verse: U dàkā a-pu dineendi ki jítiǹ u-baa nì u-na pu, ki jítiǹ u-nabiyaamu nì u-biyaamu pu. Di sá bi nìn ŋúb́ a-nyɔɔbundi, ní ki nìn ŋúb́ a-poondi.

english_verse: You teach God's laws to Israel, and at the place of worship you offer sacrifices and burn incense.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will bless everything you do, and make you strong enough to crush your enemies.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, mɔ̀tīí kūtì-bi mpɔn, yàntī bi-ŋaan tuuŋŋi ń fáatiǹ-si. Fáá kí tàtī bin yíkì kí jáǹ-bee cammu, bin ná-bee ń taa ti ŋmā kí yīkì.»

english_verse: The Lord Most High loves you, tribe of Benjamin. He will live among your hills and protect you.
translation_verse: U sòon̄ Beenjameen naakooku pu yii: «Ti-Dindaan bineeŋkaaki, ú nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin u-Nimbɔtiu cee. di sá úǹ di wúń u-pu baabadal, ní ki kóò u-gbantammu kansikin.»

english_verse: Descendants of Joseph, the Lord will bless you with precious water from deep wells and with dew from the sky.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi sòon̄ Jooseefi naakooku pu yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ u-tiŋki pu, kí tīī-kì dimalindi din nyēeń yilpuee, nì nnyim min nyēeń kitiŋ taapuee,

english_verse: Month by month, your fruit will ripen in the sunshine.
translation_verse: kí tí tīī-kì tikpaajin timɔntiil tin ŋwìiń yàntī an nyēēyee, nì asubimɔnti ŋin lòoǹ uŋmal kamaayee.

english_verse: Be happy, Zebulun, as your boats set sail; be happy, Issachar, in your tents.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi sòon̄ Sabulɔn nì Isakaar naakɔti pu yii: «Sabulɔn, án nīn mɔ̄ǹ-si a-saŋkindi poon. Isakaar, án nīn mɔ̄ǹ si mun a-tantib poon!

english_verse: The sea will make you wealthy, and from the sandy beach you will get treasure. So invite the other tribes to celebrate with you and offer sacrifices to God.

english_verse: Your leaders met together and chose the best land for your tribe, but you obeyed the Lord and helped the other tribes.
translation_verse: U lēē kitimmɔntii ki gāā u-bindi, u dū dijandi din sá ubɔti yalee kí síiǹ u-ba. U dɔ́miń ki kútì samaa kpilib pu ki ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín là puee, ní ki sòoǹ ti-Dindaan bɔkpaaŋi ŋin u nìn tīī Isirayeel yabee pu.»

english_verse: Tribe of Dan, you are like a lion cub, startled by a snake.

translation_verse: U sòon̄ Aseer naakooku pu yii: «Jaakɔb biyaamu kansikinee, Aseer ń nīn sá un boon ti-Dindaan bīiǹ tikpilee, u-nabiyaamu ń nīn néeń u-bɔti ní u-taaŋi ń nīn dēē ɔliifi kpamin.

english_verse: Israel, no other god is like ours— the clouds are his chariot as he rides across the skies to come and help us.

english_verse: The eternal God is our hiding place; he carries us in his arms. When God tells you to destroy your enemies, he will make them run.

english_verse: Israel, you will live in safety; your enemies will be gone. The dew will fall from the sky, and you will have plenty of grain and wine.
translation_verse: «Isirayeel yab bí ŋgbansɔŋfin, Jaakɔb naantiibi bí dibatɔlin. Bi tàkā bilee nì ndapɔm tiŋkin, kitiŋ kin pu dimalindi nyēeń yilpu ki tòóyee.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued you and given you more blessings than any other nation. He protects you like a shield and is your majestic sword. Your enemies will bow in fear, and you will trample on their backs.
translation_verse: «A bí mmɔnneeee Isirayeel! Ŋma di bí kii sii dinibul din ní ti-Dindaan fīīyee? Ti-Dindaan di sá a-gbampɔɔl, ki sá un tútúǹ-see. U sá kitàataajiki kin tìì-si dijajilee. A-nannanliibi làá dāá gbàan̄ a-nimbiin ní á dāá tāā bi-waapaaŋyi pùb.»

english_verse: He let Moses see the territories that would soon belong to the tribes of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, as far west as the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: ki kpáaǹ Neefitalii tiŋki kɔkɔ nì Eefiraayiim nì Manasee tiŋki nì Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔ ki tin cáa sāā tiŋku ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú,

translation_verse: nì Neegeeb tiŋki nì Jɔɔdan tantakal ki yōoǹ Jeeriikoo ibafi tiŋki, ki tin cáa sāā Soowaar.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, this is the land I was talking about when I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give land to their descendants. I have let you see it, but you will not cross the Jordan and go in.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū-u yii: «Kpèè, kitiŋ kin m nìn pōoǹ yii m làá tīī Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔbee dee. M nìn tùkū-bi yii: <M làá dāá dū-kì kí tīī ni-naantiibi ní.> M yāntì a wál̀ kitiŋ gbanti nì a-nimbiliŋ, ama aa làá nín kɔ́ ki-ni ní.»

english_verse: And so, Moses the Lord's servant died there in Moab, just as the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi kpíì Moowaab tiŋkin niin kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn lī puee.

english_verse: The Lord buried him in a valley near the town of Beth-Peor, but even today no one knows exactly where.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan síb́-u Moowaab tiŋkin ditantakalin, Beeti-Peewɔɔr tiŋki nyɔkɔpu. Ama báà ubɔ kaa nyí u-kaakul laŋki ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: The people of Israel stayed in the lowlands of Moab, where they mourned and grieved
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn súń Mooyiisi kpool iwiin mmuŋku nì saalaa ní Moowaab tantakalin. Míǹ boon ní Mooyiisi kpool kúntì.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he had placed his hands on Joshua, and the Lord had given Joshua wisdom. The Israelites paid attention to what Joshua said and obeyed the commands that the Lord had given Moses. Moses Was a Great Prophet
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn gbéeǹ Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa Ŋfam min tīī-u dinyilee, di sá yii Mooyiisi nìn dū u-ŋalii ki páaǹ u-pu ki mēē. An puee Isirayeel yab nìn pílifiǹ-u ní ki nìn ŋáań kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn kpáafì Mooyiisi yii bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: There has never again been a prophet in Israel like Moses. The Lord spoke face to face with him
translation_verse: Baa ti ká Isirayeel tiŋkin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ bí kii Mooyiisee. Mooyiisi nìn yūlifí ti-Dindaan nimbiin ní bi sòoǹ nì tɔb.

english_verse: and sent him to perform powerful miracles in the presence of the king of Egypt and his entire nation.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn tú-u Eejipiti tiŋkin u cūtìi ŋá maamaacikpaambi Faaroo nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì u-nib kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_verse: No one else has ever had the power to do such great things as Moses did for everyone to see.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn dàkā mpɔŋkpaan nì maamaaci tuuŋŋi Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, was dead. So the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been the assistant of Moses. The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi kúm boonee, ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa un nìn bí Mooyiisi cee ki tútúǹ-uee yii:

english_verse: My servant Moses is dead. Now you must lead Israel across the Jordan River into the land I'm giving to all of you.
translation_verse: «M-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi kpíì dee. Kɔŋkɔnnee, yīkì sii nì samaa nee kɔkɔ ní dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋun bí nee kí kɔ́ kitiŋ kin m làá dūu tīī Isirayeel yabee.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I'll give you that land, as I promised Moses.
translation_verse: M làá dū laakin kamaa ní ni-taaŋi yaa tāāyee kí tīī-ni kii m nín nìn tùkū Mooyiisi yii m làá ŋá puee.

english_verse: It will reach from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains in the north, and to the northeast as far as the great Euphrates River. It will include the land of the Hittites, and the land from here at the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea on the west.
translation_verse: Ni-tiŋki di làá nīn sá kí yòon̄ kuteeu ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Leebanɔn jooŋŋi, kí yòon̄ kí nīn cá dimɔɔkpaandi ŋgan pú, an dàkà yii Eefiraati mɔɔl, ní kí yòon̄ Eeti yab tiŋki kɔkɔ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kí tin cáá sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú.

english_verse: Joshua, I will always be with you and help you as I helped Moses, and no one will ever be able to defeat you.
translation_verse: A-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ kí tin cáá sāā a-kúmee, ubɔ kpá kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-si. M nín nìn bí Mooyiisi cee puee, míǹ ní m làá nīn bí si mun cee. Maa làá yàntī-si, kaa làá fá-si mun.

english_verse: Long ago I promised the ancestors of Israel that I would give this land to their descendants. So be strong and brave! Be careful to do everything my servant Moses taught you. Never stop reading The Book of the Law he gave you. Day and night you must think about what it says. If you obey it completely, you and Israel will be able to take this land.
translation_verse: Á yàntī kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmàn̄ Mara ki ŋée ń nīn bí ki kɔ́ĺ-si. Á nīn pée kàaǹ-ku ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu, án nín làá ŋá pu á ŋmā kí nīn ŋáań tikɔkɔ ki nóó nì tibɔti tin bi ŋmàn̄ ku-poonee. A yaa ŋáań mimmee ní a làá ŋmā kí bɔ́ntí a-sàmbiyaamu ní án bútí-si á ŋmā kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ a là kí ŋée.

english_verse: I've commanded you to be strong and brave. Don't ever be afraid or discouraged! I am the Lord your God, and I will be there to help you wherever you go. The Eastern Tribes Promise To Help
translation_verse: Maa kpáafì-si yii á ká dipɔbil kí taa fàŋkì báà tibaaa? Taa yàntī tifaandi ń cúú-si, kí taa yàntī a-wunti ń yɔ̀tī, kun puee man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu làá nīn bí a-cee laakin kamaa ní a làá cùee!» Joosuwa bɔ́ntì kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu

english_verse: Joshua ordered the tribal leaders
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa tīī Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib mara nee yii:

english_verse: to go through the camp and tell everyone: In a few days we will cross the Jordan River to take the land that the Lord our God is giving us. So prepare as much food as you'll need for the march into the land.
translation_verse: «Ní yìim̀maan dinaapaal kɔkɔ pu kí bāakì tibɔti nee kí tùkù samaa kɔkɔ. Ní lì yii: <Ní bɔ́ntímaan tijin kí yóoń, kun puee kí yòon̄ díǹ kí tin sāā iwiin itee, ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋun dɔ̄ nee kí cùú já kí fōō kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-ni, kí nīn sá ni-yakee.>»

english_verse: Joshua told the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
translation_verse: Boonee ní Joosuwa sòon̄ nì Rubeen naakookun yab, nì Gaadi naakookun yab, nì Manasee naakooku dijandi diba yab ki bí-bi yii:

english_verse: conquer the land that the Lord is giving them. The Lord will give peace to them as he has given peace to you, and then you can come back and settle here in the land that Moses promised you.
translation_verse: bí já kí tin cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá tīī-bi diŋuŋfil kii u nín tīī ni mun diŋuŋfil puee, ní bi mun ń ŋmā kí fōō kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-bee. Míǹ boonee ní ní gítiń kí dāá kàl̄ ni-tiŋki kin ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi tīī-ni Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi din bí doo pú nee, an dàkà yii dibuŋgbándi din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nee.»

english_verse: The men answered: We'll cross the Jordan River and help our relatives. We'll fight anywhere you send us.
translation_verse: Ní bi bí Joosuwa yii: «Ti kíí ki làá ŋá tin kɔkɔ a yaa bí yii tí ŋée. Laakin ní a yaa pée tú-tee, ti làá cù.

english_verse: If the Lord our God will help you as he helped Moses, and if you are strong and brave, we will obey you as we obeyed Moses. We'll even put to death anyone who rebels against you or refuses to obey you.
translation_verse: Unil un kamaa yaa ŋèen̄ nì a-marab, ki yíì kaa pílifì a-nyɔkɔ kí ŋá a nín lī puee, bí kpɔ̀ udaan! Siiyee, pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil!»

english_verse: Joshua chose two men as spies and sent them from their camp at Acacia with these instructions: “Go across the river and find out as much as you can about the whole region, especially about the town of Jericho.” The two spies left the Israelite camp at Acacia and went to Jericho, where they decided to spend the night at the house of a prostitute named Rahab.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab dáá bí Siitiim tiŋkin ní Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa lēē binib bili ki tú dibalin ki bí-bi yii: «Ní cùmaan kí yìiǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé Jeeriikoo tiŋki kɔkɔ.» Binibee bàn̄ee ní ki kɔ́ kinimpulaakpaai kiba dumpu ki dōoǹ. Bi yíì kinimpulaakpaai gbanti yii Rakaab.

english_verse: But someone found out about them and told the king of Jericho, “Some Israelite men came here tonight, and they are spies.”
translation_verse: Ní binib cūtìi nyá Jeeriikoo bɔtiu kuŋaŋŋaau yii: «Kpèè, Isirayeel yab biba kɔ́nní ti-tiŋki pu doo kunyeeu nee kí yìiǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé kitiŋ!»

english_verse: Rahab went back up to her roof. The spies were still awake, so she told them:
translation_verse: Kí wàatī Rakaab nicambi bin u bál̀ee ń dòon̄ee, ní u nín jɔ́ḿ bi-cee kudii yilpu.

english_verse: We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea so you could leave Egypt. And we heard how you destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan nín yāntì Tikati mɔɔl nyim fóotì ni-nimbiin ni dūtì ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Ti gíti gbìl̄ tin ní ni ŋá Amɔɔr yab bɔtiibi liitil Siiwɔn nì Ɔɔgi bin bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu lapu puee, nì ni nín nāaǹ bibɔtiibi gbanti liitil nì bi-wanti pílpil puee.

english_verse: Please promise me in the Lord's name that you will be as kind to my family as I have been to you. Do something to show
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee ní pùtī ti-Dindaan yii m nín ŋá-ni tiniti tin nee, ni mun làá ŋá m-baa dicaŋkun yab tiniti kí téeǹ, ní kí tīī-mi kudaaŋŋu yii ni làá lafun ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: that you won't let your people kill my father and mother and my brothers and sisters and their families.
translation_verse: Ní yàntī m-baa nì m-na nì m-niijab nì m-mambi nì m-naalib nì bi-dicaŋŋi nib kɔkɔ ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin. Ní taa yàntī bí kpɔ̀-ti».

english_verse: “Rahab,” the spies answered, “if you keep quiet about what we're doing, we promise to be kind to you when the Lord gives us this land. We pray that the Lord will kill us if we don't keep our promise!”
translation_verse: Ní bininjabee kíí-u yii: «Ti kíí kí kpú nimbi yil pu, sii dee taa pée yàntī ti-bɔti nee ń nyā ti nì si kansikin ubɔ ń gbìl̄-tì! Ti-Dindaan yaa láa yāntì kitiŋ nee kɔ́ ti-ŋaanee, ti làá dāá ŋá-si tiniti kí dàkà-si ti-baamɔŋyi.»

english_verse: Rahab's house was built into the town wall, and one of the windows in her house faced outside the wall. She gave the spies a rope, showed them the window, and said, “Use this rope to let yourselves down to the ground outside the wall.
translation_verse: Niinee Rakaab dū ŋŋmii ki tɔ́ tɔkɔla boon pú ní bininjabee dī ki kpákatì taapu, kitiŋ boon. Di sá yii kitiŋ gundi pu ní bi nìn máń kudii kun Rakaab kóòyee ki tɔ́kɔǹ.

english_verse: Then hide in the hills. The men who are looking for you won't be able to find you there. They'll give up and come back after a few days, and you can be on your way.”
translation_verse: Bi làá nīn nyēēyee ní Rakaab kpáafì-bi yii: «Ní túĺmaan dijool watil pú bin bíi jì kí cúú-nee ń taa ká-ni. Ní gbíntí dijool pu niin kí báĺ iwiin ita kí nīn cí binib gbanti ń fàtīí gítiń, boonee ní nín nìkī ni-saŋŋu kí nīn cá.»

english_verse: “I'll do exactly what you said,” Rahab promised. Then she sent them on their way and tied the red rope to the window.
translation_verse: Ní Rakaab kíí-bi yii: «Ni nín lī puee, án ŋá míǹ!» U lī mimmee ní ki pú-bi nsan bi nín cá, ní u nyàab̄ gulfaman ŋmiiŋu ki dūu kúĺ ki lúntì tɔkɔla pu.

english_verse: The spies hid in the hills for three days while the king's soldiers looked for them along the roads. As soon as the soldiers gave up and returned to Jericho,
translation_verse: Ní bininjab bilee nín cá dijool pu ki cūtìi bál̀ niin iwiin ita. Ubɔti naacimbi bin bíi jì kí cúú-bee nyàab̄-bi didandi pu ki gīī kaa ká-bee, ní ki fātìi nín gítí.

english_verse: the two spies went down into the Jordan valley and crossed the river. They reported to Joshua and told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bininjabee liitil kpákatì dijool, ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki cūtì Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa cee ní ki dū bi nín bàn̄ tin jítèe kɔkɔ ki máafì-u.

english_verse: “We're sure the Lord has given us the whole country,” they said. “The people there shake with fear every time they think of us.”
translation_verse: Bi bí Joosuwa yii: «Tiŋman pu, ti-Dindaan lafun dū kitiŋee kɔkɔ ki ŋá ti-ŋaan ní. Di sá yii timbi puee, tifaandi kɔ́ ki-nib kɔkɔ ní bi nyùn̄ ŋkpatim!»

english_verse: Early the next morning, Joshua and the Israelites packed up and left Acacia. They went to the Jordan River and camped there that night.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní Joosuwa yíkì Siitiim kaaŋun, u nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, ní bi cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi. Bi bàn̄ niinee ní ki gbíntì ki kāl̀ kí cīití ŋwiin ŋun bi làá dùtī mbunee.

english_verse: Two days later their leaders went through the camp,
translation_verse: Iwiin ita boonee ní Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib yìin̄ ki māntì dinaapaal kɔkɔ poon,

english_verse: shouting, “When you see some of the priests carrying the sacred chest, you'll know it is time to cross to the other side. You've never been there before, and you won't know the way, unless you follow the chest. But don't get too close! Stay about a kilometer back.”
translation_verse: Mimmee ni làá béé nsan ŋun ní ni máaǹ kí nóóyee, kun puee naa láá pée cōom̀ nsan nee pu ki ká. Ama ní yàntī mpaan ń nīn dɔ̄ ni nì Dipoondi dakaau kansikin kí bà kii ditaŋkpal diba, kí taa nín̄ pìl̄-u tikpil.»

english_verse: Joshua told the people, “Make yourselves acceptable to worship the Lord, because he is going to do some amazing things for us.”
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa tùkū samaa yii: «Ní bɔ́ntímaan ni-ba kí nīn bí circir, kun puee fool ti-Dindaan làá fu ŋá maamaaci tuuŋŋi ni-kansikin.»

english_verse: Then Joshua turned to the priests and said, “Take the chest and cross the Jordan River ahead of us.” So the priests picked up the chest by its carrying poles and went on ahead.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Joosuwa bí bisaraaŋaliibi yii: «Yòom̄maan Dipoondi dakaau kí lìntī samaa nyɔkɔpu!» Ní bi yōoǹ Dipoondi dakaau ki līntì samaa nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua, “Beginning today I will show the people that you are their leader, and they will know that I am helping you as I helped Moses.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Joosuwa yii: «Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee ní m làá kíĺ kí yàntī á nyā diyindi Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin ní bí béé yii m làá nīn bí a-cee kii m nín nìn bí Mooyiisi cee puee.

english_verse: Now, tell the priests who are carrying the chest to go a little way into the river and stand there.”
translation_verse: Tùkù bisaraaŋaliibi bin tú Dipoondi dakaauee yii bi yaa cōom̀ ki bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee, bí kɔ́ poon kí yūĺ nnyimin.»

english_verse: Joshua spoke to the people: Come here and listen to what the Lord our God said he will do!
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Ní sútiḿmaan doo kí dāá pīlifì tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cáá ki làá sòoǹee!»

english_verse: The Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites control the land on the other side of the river. But the living God will be with you and will force them out of the land when you attack. And now, God is going to prove that he's powerful enough to force them out.
translation_verse: Bi kóoǹní ki kpáfèe ní Joosuwa bí-bi yii: «Tin bí nee di làá yàntī ní béé yii Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee bí ni-kansikin ní ki làá lafun jà Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Eefi yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Giirgaasi yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Jeebusi yab kí wàatī-ni.

english_verse: Just watch the sacred chest that belongs to the Lord, the ruler of the whole earth. As soon as the priests carrying the chest step into the Jordan, the water will stop flowing and pile up as if someone had built a dam across the river. The Lord has also said that each of the twelve tribes should choose one man to represent it.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi bin bùkū ti-Dindaan, duulinya kɔkɔ Dindaan Poondi dakaauee dāa pée lì yii bi dù bi-tafati kí gbēē Jɔɔdan nyimee, nnyim min pùubìń yilpu puee làá gbèen̄ kaa làá ti pùub̀, ní kí kóoǹ kí ŋá dinyiŋgundi.»

english_verse: The Israelites packed up and left camp. The priests carrying the chest walked in front,
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab nyáń bi-tantibin kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, ní bisaraaŋaliibi bùkū Dipoondi dakaau ki līī samaa nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: until they came to the Jordan River. The water in the river had risen over its banks, as it often does in springtime. But as soon as the feet of the priests touched the water,
translation_verse: An nìn sá ŋyunti ŋun bi cēē tikpaajinee ní. Dibindi poonee, ŋyunti gbanti ní Jɔɔdan buŋŋu gbéè kí páań. Bisaraaŋaliibi bin bùkū Dipoondi dakaauee nín bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi ki tin pée dùŋfī bi-taaŋi kí gbēē nnyimee,

english_verse: the river stopped flowing, and the water started piling up at the town of Adam near Zarethan. No water flowed toward the Dead Sea, and the priests stood in the middle of the dry riverbed near Jericho while everyone else crossed over.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi bin bùkū ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaauee pée sí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin ŋkulimmi, ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ dāa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋkulimmi ki dóò.

english_verse: After Israel had crossed the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua:
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun samaa kɔkɔ dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki dóòyee, ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii:

english_verse: Tell one man from each of the twelve tribes to pick up a large rock from where the priests are standing. Then tell the men to set up those rocks as a monument at the place where you camp tonight.
translation_verse: kí tùkù-bi yii: <Ní kɔ́maan kí tòò ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin, dibɔbil din bisaraaŋaliibi yúl̀ee. Ní kpáaǹ-ŋi kí cáá bíĺ laakin ni làá dòon̄ kunyeeu neeyee.>»

english_verse: and said: Go to the middle of the riverbed where the sacred chest is, and pick up a large rock. Carry it on your shoulder to our camp. There are twelve of you, so there will be one rock for each tribe.
translation_verse: ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ní lìntīmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu Poondi dakaau nyɔkɔpu kí kɔ́ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin, ní báà ŋma ń yòon̄ ditaŋkpal diba diba kí dūú bùkun̄ u-gbigbil pu, kí nóó nì Isirayeel yab naakɔti nyɔkɔm nín sá puee.

english_verse: Someday your children will ask, “Why are these rocks here?” Then you can tell them how the water stopped flowing when the chest was being carried across the river. These rocks will always remind our people of what happened here today.
translation_verse: ní dāá kíí-bi yii: <Bi nín nìn túǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee, mi-nyim nìn cúu yākatì mili ní. Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi dùtī nì Dipoondi dakaauee, nnyim nìn cúu yākatì ní bi jítì. An puee, ataŋkpee nee sá kí nīn téetí Isirayeel yab an bɔti ní kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.>»

english_verse: The men followed the instructions that the Lord had given Joshua. They picked up twelve rocks, one for each tribe, and carried them to the camp, where they put them down.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab lafun ŋá kii Joosuwa nín yóoǹ-bi yii bí ŋá puee. Bi nìn lēē ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin, kunaakoou kamaa ditaŋkpal diba, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Joosuwa yii bí ŋá puee, ní ki cáa cūnnì ki bíl̀ laakin bi nìn dōoǹ kunyeeu gbantee.

english_verse: Joshua set up a monument next to the place where the priests were standing. This monument was also made of twelve large rocks, and it is still there in the middle of the river. The People of Israel Set Up Camp at Gilgal
translation_verse: Joosuwa nìn gíti yāntì bi tōō ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali aba mun ki cóoǹ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin, laakin bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn tú Dipoondi dakaauee nìn yúl̀ee. Ataŋkpee gbanti dáá gbíntìi bí niin ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: It was the tenth day of the first month of the year when Israel crossed the Jordan River. They set up camp at Gilgal, which was east of the land controlled by Jericho.
translation_verse: Uŋmapeepeekaa poon iwiin saalaa dal ní Isirayeel yab dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ laakin bi yíì yii Giilgaal, an bí Jeeriikoo tiŋki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee.

english_verse: The men who had carried the twelve rocks from the Jordan brought them to Joshua, and they made them into a monument.
translation_verse: Giilgaal niin ní Joosuwa yāntì bi cóoǹ ataŋkpee ŋin bi kɔ́ Jɔɔdan buŋŋun ki tōōyee.

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Years from now your children will ask you why these rocks are here.
translation_verse: Bi cóoǹ ki dóòyee ní u tùkū Isirayeel yab yii: «Fool boon ni-biyaamu yaa láa bālifì nimbi bibaatiibi yii ba taŋkpeeŋi sèéyee,

english_verse: Tell them, “The Lord our God dried up the Jordan River so we could walk across. He did the same thing here for us that he did for our people at the Red Sea,
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yāntì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nyim fóotì ni-nimbiin ní ni-kɔkɔ dūtì kii úǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín nìn yāntì Tikati mɔɔl nyim fóotì timbi nimbiin ki tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ti-kɔ dūtèe.

english_verse: because he wants everyone on earth to know how powerful he is. And he wants us to worship only him.”
translation_verse: U ŋá míǹ anibul ŋin bí kitiŋ puee kɔkɔ ń béé yii úǹ ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu di sá mpɔŋkpaan, ní nimbi ń nīn fàŋkí-u kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan!»

english_verse: The Amorite kings west of the Jordan River and the Canaanite kings along the Mediterranean Sea lost their courage and their will to fight, when they heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan River to let Israel go across. Israel Gets Ready To Celebrate Passover
translation_verse: Amɔɔr yab bin kóò Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee bɔtiibi, nì Kanaan yab bin kóò ki pìlīǹ tiŋkuee bɔtiibi nìn gbìl̄ yii ti-Dindaan yāntì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nyim fóotì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ŋúń ki dūtì. Niinee bi-pɔbiliŋ bíil̀, ní Isirayeel yab puee, bi nyùn̄ ŋkpatim. Bi gíí Isirayeel yab bininjab kɔkɔ Giilgaal

english_verse: While Israel was camped at Gilgal, the Lord said, “Joshua, make some flint knives and circumcise the rest of the Israelite men and boys.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Joosuwa yii: «Kpítí ntaŋkpajimu kí gíí Isirayeel yab bininjab bin dáá sá binipɔmbee akpancan.»

english_verse: This had to be done, because none of Israel's baby boys had been circumcised during the
translation_verse: Bi-jipɔmbi di yíkì ki fōō bi-yil. Bi-jipɔmbi gbanti ní Joosuwa nìn gíí akpancan, kun puee baa nìn gíiń-bi nsanni.

english_verse: Everyone who had been circumcised needed time to heal, and they stayed in camp.
translation_verse: Bi gíí-bi míǹ ki dóòyee ní samaa kɔkɔ gbíntì dinaapaal pu niin ki kāl̀ áli ibuun dāa kpíì.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua, “It was a disgrace for my people to be slaves in Egypt, but now I have taken away that disgrace.” So the Israelites named the place Gilgal, and it still has that name.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee, m cúú Eejipiti tiŋki cooi in nìn bí ni-puee ki lēē.» An di yì-tì ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Giilgaal, ní bi dáá gbíntìi yíì-ŋu míǹ ki dāa sāā díǹ. Dilákatil jiŋaaliu upeepeekaa un bi jíń Kanaaŋyee

english_verse: Israel continued to camp at Gilgal in the desert near Jericho, and on the fourteenth day of the same month, they celebrated Passover.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn kāl̀ Giilgaal niin, Jeeriikoo tantakalin ní ki jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu uŋmal poon ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal kujoou.

english_verse: The next day, God stopped sending the Israelites manna to eat each morning, and they started eating food grown in the land of Canaan. They ate roasted grain and thin bread made of the barley they had gathered from nearby fields. Israel Captures Jericho
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun bi jíń an jintee ní maana gbēeǹ kaa ti nyēeń kutaa pu ki lítiń. Dibindi gbanti ní Isirayeel yab kíĺ ki bíi jīǹ tijin tin lòoǹ Kanaan tiŋki puee. Joosuwa nì ti-Dindaan janjakitil kpiliu

english_verse: One day, Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing some distance in front of him. The man was holding a sword, so Joshua walked up to him and asked, “Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?”
translation_verse: Dalba Joosuwa nìn bí Jeeriikoo tiŋki caŋin. U dāa pée yáatèe ní ki ká uninja ubɔ yú u-nyɔkɔpu, ki ŋúb́ njicál u-ŋaan. Joosuwa cōom̀ ki cūtì u-cee ní ki bālifì-u yii: «Sii sá ti-yɔu ubɔ naaa, a sá ti-nannanliu ubɔ ní?»

english_verse: “Neither,” he answered. “I am here because I am the commander of the Lord's army.” Joshua fell to his knees and bowed down to the ground. “I am your servant,” he said. “Tell me what to do.”
translation_verse: Ní unaaciinee kíí Joosuwa yii: «Aayee, maa sá bi-kansikin báà ubɔ! Man di sá ti-Dindaan janjakitil kpiliu. Kɔŋkɔnnee ní m bāań!» Niinee ní Joosuwa tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ki jáam̀-u ní ki bí-u yii: «M-dindaan, ba ní a là yii man a-tɔntɔnliu ń ŋá ní?»

english_verse: “Take off your sandals,” the commander answered. “This is a holy place.” So Joshua took off his sandals.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan janjakitil kpiliuee bí Joosuwa yii: «Cúú a-naatakaŋ kí tákatí, kun puee laakin a yú nee sá circir paaŋŋu pu ní.» Ní Joosuwa ŋá min ní u tùkū-u yii ú ŋée.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Jericho had been locking the gates in their town wall because they were afraid of the Israelites. No one could go out or come in.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab puee, Jeeriikoo yab nìn dū bi-tiŋki punyɔmmu ki pīiǹ ki kpàl̄. Báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ɔɔ, kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí nyā mun.

english_verse: Take along the sacred chest and tell seven priests to walk in front of it, carrying trumpets. But on the seventh day, march slowly around the town seven times while the priests blow their trumpets.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi biluli ń nīn ŋúb́ ipijaa yiŋyi ki līī Dipoondi dakaau nyɔkɔpu. Ŋwinluluúti dalee, ní dāá còom̀ kí màntīí tū kitiŋ ŋfunyɔm miluli ní bisaraaŋaliibee ń dāá nīn búǹ iyin.

english_verse: Then the priests will blast on their trumpets, and everyone else will shout. The wall will fall down, and your soldiers can go straight in from every side.
translation_verse: Bi yaa láa búń upìja yiŋŋu ni gbìl̄ an súńee, samaa kɔkɔ ń dāá kúuǹ mpɔn mpɔn. Digundi din bi máń ki māntìi tú kitiŋee làá lítí niin niin. Niinee samaa kɔkɔ ń sāǹ kí kɔ́ kitiŋin, báà ŋma ń nīn pée túĺ u-nimbiin.»

english_verse: Joshua called the priests together and said, “Take the chest and tell seven priests to carry trumpets and march ahead of it.”
translation_verse: Ní Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa yíiń bisaraaŋaliibi ki bí-bi yii: «Yòom̄maan Dipoondi dakaau kí bùkun̄ ní bisaraaŋaliibi biluli ń nīn ŋúb́ ipijaa yiŋyi ki līī ti-Dindaan dakaau nyɔkɔpu.»

english_verse: They obeyed Joshua's orders and carried the chest once around the town before returning to camp for the night.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Joosuwa yāntì bi būkuǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau ki cōom̀ ki māntìi tú kitiŋee diba, ní ki fātìi gítì dinaapaal pu ki dōoǹ.

english_verse: On the seventh day, the army got up at daybreak. They marched slowly around Jericho the same as they had done for the past six days, except on this day they went around seven times.
translation_verse: Ŋwinluluúti dalee, bi péé ki yíkì ntaafaabɔmbɔmin ní ki cōom̀ ki māntìi tú kitiŋ, kii bi nín pée kpàà ŋáań puee miluli pu. Ŋwiin gbanti baba ní bi cōom̀ ki māntìi tú kitiŋ miluli.

english_verse: Then the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua yelled: Get ready to shout! The Lord will let you capture this town.
translation_verse: Bi nín māntì nluluútiim ní bisaraaŋaliibi búń iyinee, ní Joosuwa bí samaa yii: «Ní kúum̀maan, kun puee ti-Dindaan dū kitiŋ nee ki ŋá ni-ŋaan ní!

english_verse: But you must destroy it and everything in it, to show that it now belongs to the Lord. The woman Rahab helped the spies we sent, so protect her and the others who are inside her house. But kill everyone else in the town.
translation_verse: Ní nàan̄ kitiŋ gbanti nì tin kɔkɔ pée bí ki-poonee kí dàkà yii tì kpántì ti-Dindaan wanti ubɔ kaa ti máaǹ kí gbēē! Asee Rakaab kinimpulaakpaai baba di làá ŋmátí, ní kí kūtì binib bin kɔkɔ pée bí u-cee kudiinee. Kun puee úǹ di nìn bál̀ binib bin ti lēē ki tú bi cūtì ki cɔ́ŋkì ki béè kitiŋee.

english_verse: The priests blew their trumpets again, and the soldiers shouted as loud as they could. The walls of Jericho fell flat. Then the soldiers rushed up the hill, went straight into the town, and captured it.
translation_verse: Ní bisaraaŋaliibi búń iyin ní samaa kɔkɔ kúuǹ mpɔn. Ŋyunti ŋun samaa gbìl̄ iyin pu ki kúuǹ mpɔnee, ní digundi cúu wūtì. Niinee ní Isirayeel yab sáǹ ki nín jɔ́ḿ kitiŋin, báà ŋma túĺ u-nimbiin, ní bi jáń ki fōō kitiŋ.

english_verse: After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti ní Joosuwa nìn pūtì ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan yindi puee, mbusu ń kɔ́ unil un kamaa yaa mākaǹ yii u làá fàtīí mā Jeeriikoo tiŋki neeyee. Udaan jipɔŋkpiliu ní u làá dūú kíĺ kitiŋ gbanti dimal, ní kí dū u-jipɔnjoolkaau kí cóoń ki-punuubi!»

english_verse: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan nìn bí Joosuwa cee ní u-yindi nìn gbītì kitiŋ kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab yīntiǹ mara un sá yii bí taa gbēē tiwan tin kpántì ti-Dindaan wantee. Di sá yii Kaarmii jipɔɔn, Sabidii naantiiu nì Seera un sá Juuda naakookunee naantitɔntɔkɔl Akan lēē tiwanee poon tiba. An puee ní ti-Dindaan fōō mbum Isirayeel yab pu.

english_verse: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa nì Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib dáaĺ ki cátì bi-wanti tin bi pēēyee, ki cūtìi dōoǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau nyɔkɔpu dicincibil. Bi nìn dōoǹ ki tin sāā kujoou, ní ki kàfī ntam ki yàantí bi-yiliŋ pu.

english_verse: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa bí yii: «Áà, m-Dindaan Unimbɔti! Ba pu ní a cáá-ti ki dūtìń Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ní? A cáań-ti ki ŋá Amɔɔr yab ŋaan bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ti níii? Ti yaa bàà pūtì gbíntì Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi lapu pu tiŋki pu, an bàà sɔ́ɔ!

english_verse: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
translation_verse: Abàa, m-Dindaan! Kɔŋkɔnnee Isirayeel yab nannanliibi nín kpìl̄-bi bi sáǹ nee, m làá nín lì yii ba dee?

english_verse: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
translation_verse: Kanaan yab nì binib bin kɔkɔ kóò kitiŋ nee puee yaa gbìl̄ tin bí nee, asee bí gbáb́ kí bìin̄ ti-pu ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ti! Mimmee, mana ní a làá ŋá ní kí yàntī binib ń béé yii a-yindi sá dikpaandi?»

english_verse: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Yīkìm̄! Ba pu ní a dɔ̄ dicincibil míǹ?

english_verse: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab yīntì! Bi kpītì dipoondi din m pōoǹ-bee, ki lēē tiwan tin baa máaǹ kí gbēēyee poon tiba. Bi yùn̄-tì ki bál̀ bíǹ bi-ba wanti poon.

english_verse: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
translation_verse: An puee Isirayeel yab kaa làá ti ŋmā kí sútíí pìl̄ bi-nannanliibi. Bi-nannanliibi làá nīn pée sáń ki jì-bi ní, kun puee mbusu kɔ́-bi dikoobil din bi kōotèe pu. Ni yaa kaa nyántì tiwan tin naa máaǹ kí gbēēyee ni-kansikin, maa làá ti nín̄ bí ni-cee!

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
translation_verse: Yīkì kí bɔ́ntí samaa bí nīn bí circir man nì bi ń fu kpāfì. Á tùkù-bi yii bí bɔ́ntí bi-ba kí nīn bí circir kí cīití fool taaku, kun puee man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Isirayeel yab, tiwan tin naa máaǹ kí gbēēyee tiba bí ni-cee! Ni yaa kaa nyántì tiwan gbanti ni-kansikin, naa làá ti ŋmā kí sútí kí pìl̄ ni-nannanliibi.>

english_verse: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
translation_verse: An puee, fool kutaafaauee, ni-kɔkɔ ń fu dāan̄ m-cee, kí nīn sútiń kunaakoou kunaakoou. Kunaakoou kun ti-Dindaan yaa fu sāāyee ń fu kpāfì kí nīn sútiń mmaal mmaal. Mmaal ŋun ti-Dindaan yaa fu sāāyee ń fu kpāfì kí nīn sútiń kudicaŋu kudicaŋu. Ní kudicaŋu kun ti-Dindaan yaa fu sāāyee nib ń fu kpāfì kí nīn sútiń ubɔ ubɔ.

english_verse: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
translation_verse: Unil un an yaa fu sāā yii úǹ di ŋúb́ tiwan tin baa máaǹ kí gbēēyee, bí fu wà udaan ŋŋmi kí kpáaǹ tin pée sá u-wantee kɔkɔ. Kun puee udaan kpītì man ni-Dindaan Poondi ki ŋá icoo bɔti Isirayeel tiŋki poon!»

english_verse: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
translation_verse: Joosuwa fīntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ sútìń kunaakoou kunaakoou, ní an sāā Juuda naakooku.

english_verse: Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty.
translation_verse: Ní u yāntì Juuda naakookun yab sútìń, ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee, ní an sāā Seera maaliŋu. Ní Seera maaliŋu yab sútìń kudicaŋu kudicaŋu, ní an sāā Sabidii dicaŋku.

english_verse: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
translation_verse: U yāntì Sabidii dicaŋkun nib sútìń ubɔ ubɔ, ní an sāā Kaarmii jipɔɔn, Sabidii naantiiu, Seera un sá Juuda naakookunee naantitɔntɔkɔl Akan.

english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa bí Akan yii: «M-jipɔɔn, tīī ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu tinyool, kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-u. Māafì-mi tin a ŋée kɔkɔ kí taa báĺ-mi báà tiba!»

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Akan kíí Joosuwa yii: «Tiŋman, man di lafun yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. An nín jítì puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Ní bi kóoǹní tiwanee tanti poon ki cáań Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ cee, ki dūu bíl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa yāntì bi cúú Seera naantiiu Akan, ki yōoǹ animbil kútee nì dibɔkutikpaandee nì disindaariyakúndee. Bi nìn cúú ki kpáaǹ u-jipɔmbi nì u-bisalib, nì u-naai nì u-mammu nì u-piii nì tin kɔkɔ pée sá u-wantee, ní u nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ cáá-bi ki cūnnì Akɔɔr tantakalin.

english_verse: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ niinee ní Joosuwa bí Akan yii: «Ba pu ní a pàal̄ ŋŋmii ki léeǹ ti-pu míǹ? Too, díǹ wiiŋŋu nee ní ti-Dindaan làá pée gíiǹ-ŋu kí téeǹ-si!» Ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yáŋkì Akan ataŋkpee ki kūū. Bi nìn yáŋkì u-yab mun ataŋkpee ki kūū ní ki wùn̄ u-wanti kɔkɔ ŋŋmi.

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: Boonee ní bi kóoǹ ataŋkpee ki kpúkuǹ bi-pu dikpúkukpaandi. Ditaŋkpakpukul gbanti dáá gbíntìi bí niin díǹ pu nee. An pu ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Akɔɔr tantakal, ki dāa sāā díǹ. Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkì.

english_verse: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
translation_verse: Ti yaa bíi sáń ní bi yaa kùl̄ ki páaǹ ti-boonee, ní tí ŋmàtiǹ-bi kí dáaĺ-bi kí nyāntí kitiŋin. Bi làá dàkafì yii ti tí bíi sáń-bi, kii bi nín nìn jìn̄-ti ti sáǹ mpeekaam puee.

english_verse: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
translation_verse: Niinee ní nimbi ń nyānní laakin ní ni náká nákée, kí kɔ́ kí já kí fōō kitiŋee. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dū-kì kí ŋá ni-ŋaan.

english_verse: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
translation_verse: Ni yaa jáń ki fōō kitiŋ gbantee, ní sēē-kì ŋŋmi kí wà, kí nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín tùkū-ni yii ní ŋá puee. Man nín yóoǹ-ni yii ní ŋá puee, ní ŋámaan míǹ deedee!»

english_verse: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní Joosuwa yíkì ki yíiń bininjab bin bàn̄ kí cù kujaauee ki kpáfì kí kpèè bi nín bɔ́ntì puee, ní u nì Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib līntì bi-nyɔkɔpu bí cùú jáǹ Aayi tiŋki yab.

english_verse: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní bijanjaliibi tikpil nìn gāā dijanjanaapaal Aayi tiŋki ŋgan pú, ní bin kíǹee bíǹ náká náká kitiŋ boon, ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. Kunyeeu gbantee, Joosuwa nìn fātìi gítì ditantakalin.

english_verse: So he called out every man in Ai to go after Joshua's troops. They all rushed out to chase the Israelite army, and they left the town gates wide open. Not one man was left in Ai or in Bethel. Joshua let the men of Ai chase him and his army farther and farther away from Ai.
translation_verse: Báà uninja kaa nìn kíǹ Aayi nì Beeteel timmun kaa nyáń ki jìn̄ Isirayeel yab boon. Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bí ki jì Isirayeel yab mimmee, Aayi tiŋki punyɔkɔki nìn kíǹ ki wāā fám dee.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Tàntī kikpaŋ kin a ŋúb́ee kí dàkà Aayi tiŋki, kun puee m làá dū kitiŋ gbanti ki ŋá a-ŋaan!» Ní Joosuwa tāntì u-ŋal ki fātì kikpaŋ kin u ŋúb́ee ki túĺ Aayi tiŋki watil pú.

english_verse: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
translation_verse: U tin lì yii u tàntī u-ŋalee, bijanjaliibi bin u yóoǹ kitiŋ boonee kɔkɔ ŋá malaa ki nyánní laakin bi nìn náká nákée, ki sáǹ ki kɔ́ kitiŋin, ki jáń ki fōō-kì ní ki sēē-kì ŋŋmi niin niin.

english_verse: When Joshua and his troops saw smoke rising from the town, they knew that the other part of their army had captured it. So they turned and attacked. The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from their town. But they could not escape, because the soldiers they had been chasing had suddenly turned and started fighting.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab nín ká yii bi-yab bin náká náká kitiŋ boon púee kɔ́ ki jáń ki fōō kitiŋ, ki ká nnyiim nín bí ki nyēē kitiŋ gbanti poon jòooo ki jɔ́ḿ puee, ní bi fātìi lábitì Aayi yab pu ki kíĺ ki bíi kù-bi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn kūū Aayi janjaliibi tisatin, kuteeu poon laakin bi páaǹ bi-boonee ki dóò. Bi nìn dū ntàataajimu ki kūū ki kúntì bi-kɔkɔ kaa nìn kíǹ bi-kansikin báà ubɔ. Boonee ní Isirayeel yab fātìi nín gítiń Aayi tiŋkin ní ki dɔ́miń ki púntìi kūū Aayi yab bin kíǹ ki bí kitiŋinee kɔkɔ pílpil.

english_verse: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. Those rocks are still there, and the town itself has never been rebuilt. Joshua Reads the Blessings and Curses (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: U nìn lúntì Aayi bɔtiu úǹ busubu bubɔ pu, ní ki yāntì u lúń míǹ ki tin sāā kujoou. Ŋwìiń cá kí jéetée ní u yāntì bi cúú dinikpilee ki sākatìń busubu pu ki cáa lúkú kitiŋ punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní ki kóoǹ ataŋkpee ki nyīkiǹ u-pu ní an ŋá ditaŋkpakpukul dikpaandi. Ditaŋkpakpukul gbanti dáá dɔ̄ niin díǹ pu nee. Bi kàan̄ Unimbɔti marau Eebaal jool pu

english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Gabawɔn tiŋki yab mun nìn gbìl̄ Joosuwa nín ŋá Jeeriikoo nì Aayi timmu puee.

english_verse: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
translation_verse: Ama bíǹ nìn ŋá nciin ŋubɔ. Bi nìn lēē binib ki tú Joosuwa cee. Binib bin bi nìn túee nìn nyàab̄ bifɔltɔkpikib bin cátì cátée, nì tidalɔti tin púĺ ki kpíì yɔ́si yɔsi bi fātìi ŋáĺ ŋáĺee ki bóob́ ki túǹ bi-mammu.

english_verse: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū anaatakakpiŋkpiki ŋin bi nìn kpáá miŋa nì miŋa puee ki táká, ki nyàab̄ ikpalcati ki pēeǹ. Kpɔnɔb bin bi ŋúb́ yii tijikaalee kūń ki pɔ́ɔkì kaŋkaŋ ní boon pùl̄ ki wíiḿ.

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Bi bɔ́ntì mimmee ní ki nín cá Joosuwa cee Giilgaal naapaal pu, ní ki bàn̄ ki bí u nì Isirayeel yab yii: «Ti nyánní kitiŋ kin dátèe ni ní. Ti là yii ní yàntī ti nì ni ń pùtī kí pòon̄ tɔb kí ŋá ubaanti.»

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu pu ní, di sá ti yíkìń kitiŋ kin dátì tikpilee ni ki cōom̀ ki dāa bāań doo. Tiŋman, ti gbìl̄ bi sòon̄ u-bɔti, ki gbìl̄ tin kɔkɔ u ŋáaǹ Eejipiti tiŋkinee.

english_verse: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
translation_verse: Ti gbìl̄ tin u ŋá Amɔɔr yab bɔtiibi bili bin nìn kóò Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee mun, an dàkà yii Eesbɔn bɔtiu Siiwɔn nì Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi un nìn kóò Asitarooti tiŋkinee.

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Ti-tindaŋkpilib nì ti-tiŋki nib kɔkɔ nín gbìl̄ tibɔti gbantee ní bi bí-ti yii tí bɔ́ntí tijin tin ti làá nīn jīǹ nsannee kí dāá tūŋkì-ni. Ti yaa bāań ki ká-nee, tí tùkù-ni yii ti sá ni-tɔntɔnliibi ní. Ti là yii ní yàntī ti nì ni ń pùtī kí pòon̄ tɔb kí ŋá ubaanti!

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Ti-kpɔnɔb bin ti ŋúbiń nee, ŋwiin ŋun ti nìn dū-bi ki ŋá ti-waŋguliŋi poon ki kālìń nsan pu kí nīn dòoń ni-cee dooyee, bi nìn dáá pée tùm̀ ní ki pɔ̀fì làblab. Kpèèmaan kɔŋkɔnnee bi nín kūń ki wíiḿ ki wúkul̀ puee!

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: Tidalɔti nee, ti nín nìn kpíliń-tì ndaamee, tì nìn dáá pée pɔ̀ɔǹ ní kílkil. Ní kpèè kɔŋkɔnnee tì nín cátì cátì puee! Ti-wampeeŋkaati nì ti-naatakaŋ nee nín kpíì kpíì pu nee, nsan ŋun ti cōomìńee dandatiŋu di yì-tì ní an ŋá míǹ!»

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel yab kíí ki fōō binibee jinti tin bi lēē ki tīī-bee, kaa bālifì ti-Dindaan ki wāatì.

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nìn kíí ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí bi-kansikin, ní u nì bi pūtì ki pōoǹ tɔb kí ŋá ubaanti ú yàntī bí nīn bí dimaŋfalin. Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ-bi yii án làá ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: A couple of days later, the Israelites found out that these people actually lived in the nearby towns of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim. So the Israelites left the place where they had camped and arrived at the four towns two days later.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Isirayeel yab yíkì niin ki nìkī bi-saŋkindee ní ki dūu bàn̄ binib gbanti timmun ŋwintataati dal. Bi-timmu gbanti di sá Gabawɔn nì Keefiira nì Beerooti nì Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab kaa nìn kūū-bi, kun puee bi-tindaŋkpilib nìn gíti dáá pūtì ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ki pōoǹ binib gbanti yii baa làá kpɔ̀-bi. Ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ pée kíǹ ki gbùkum̄ ki wòoǹ bi-tindaŋkpilib.

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa yíiń-bi ki sòon̄ nì bi yii: «Ba ŋá ní ni mɔ́ntì-ti yii ni nyánní ndandati, kaa nyí yii ni pée kóò ki pìlīǹ-ti doo nee?

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Too, ni dáaĺ mbusu ki tɔ́ ni-ba pu ní nee! Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, ni-kɔkɔ làá nīn pée sá iyumbu ní kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. Nimbi di làá nīn kíǹ ki là idɔ ki lúù nnyim ki cāabìń man Nimbɔtiu diikun.»

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí Joosuwa yii: «Bi máafì timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi miŋa nì miŋa pu yii ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nìn kpáafì u-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi yii ú dū kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ kí tīī-ni ní ní kpɔ̀ kí céetí ki-nib kɔkɔ. Ti gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki fāŋkì tikpil yii ní taa kpɔ̀-ti. An pu ní ti ŋá min ti ŋá nee.

english_verse: and you are strong enough to do anything to us that you want. We just ask you to do what seems right.”
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee ti dū ti-ba ki ŋá a-ŋaan. Min ní sii yaa dākafì yii an kítì ki ŋān̄ á ŋá-tee, ŋá míǹ!»

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Joosuwa fīī binib gbanti Isirayeel yab ŋaan ní baa kūū-bi.

english_verse: but he did tell the Gibeonites that they would have to be servants of the nation of Israel. They would have to cut firewood and bring it for the priests to use for burning sacrifices on the Lord's altar, wherever the Lord decided the altar would be. The Gibeonites would also have to carry water for the priests. And that is still the work of the Gibeonites.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti ní Joosuwa yāntì bi kíǹ ki là idɔ ki lúù nnyim ki tìì Isirayeel samaau, ní ki cāabìń ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu pu ki dāa sāā díǹ pu nee, laakin kamaa ní ti-Dindaan yaa lēē bí nīn jáaḿ-uee.

english_verse: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem bɔtiu Adoonii-Seedeeki nìn gbìl̄ yii Joosuwa jáń ki fōō Aayi tiŋki, ki nāaǹ-kì kɔkɔ. U nín nìn pée ŋá Jeeriikoo tiŋki nì ki-bɔtiu puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní u nìn ŋá Aayi tiŋki nì ki-bɔtiu. U gbìl̄ mun yii Gabawɔn yab nì Isirayeel yab sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí bi-kansikin ní bi kíǹ ki kóò bi-kansikin.

english_verse: This frightened Adonizedek and his people. They knew that Gibeon was a large town, as big as the towns that had kings, and even bigger than the town of Ai had been. And all of the men of Gibeon were warriors.
translation_verse: U nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní tifaandi cúú u nì u-yab tikpil, kun puee Gabawɔn nìn sá kitiŋkpaaŋŋi ní kii ntimu mun cáá bibɔtiibee, ki nìn wīikí ki jítiǹ Aayi tiŋki, ní ki-ninjab kɔkɔ sá bibaatandambi ŋma.

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: An puee ní Jeerusaleem bɔtiu Adoonii-Seedeeki lēē binib ki tú Eebrɔn bɔtiu Ookam nì Yaarmuti bɔtiu Piiram nì Lakiisi bɔtiu Yafiya nì Eeglɔn bɔtiu Deebiir cee bi cūtìi tùkū-bi yii:

english_verse: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
translation_verse: «Ní dāam̄maan kí tūtuǹ-mi tí jáǹ Gabawɔn tiŋki yab, kun puee bi nì Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb ki ŋá mpèé.»

english_verse: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
translation_verse: Ní Gabawɔn yab lēē binib ki tú Giilgaal naapaal pu, ní bi cūtìi tùkū Joosuwa yii: «Taa dū timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi kí fá! Dāan̄ malaa kí jòò-ti! Dāá fīī-ti kun puee Amɔɔr yab bɔtiibi bin bin kóò ajoon puee kɔkɔ kpáfì kinyɔkɔ ki bíi jáà nì ti!»

english_verse: Joshua and his army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa yíkì Giilgaal ki nín jɔ́ḿ Gabawɔn, u nì Isirayeel yab janjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Taa pée fàŋkì-bi, kun puee m dū-bi ki ŋá a-ŋaan ní. Bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí yūĺ a-nimbiin.»

english_verse: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon and made a surprise attack on the Amorite camp.
translation_verse: Joosuwa kpáaǹ u-yab ki cōom̀ kunyamɔŋu ní ki dāa dūu cíl̀ binib gbanti pu baa nyí u-pu.

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan yāntì bi fāŋkì ní ki kíǹ ki sáń ajan kɔkɔ pu Isirayeel yab nimbiin. Bi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ Gabawɔn caŋin niin ki jìn̄-bi ki nóó nsan ŋun jɔ́ḿ Beeti-Oorɔn gbantaŋki puee. Bi nìn nàn̄-bi ki tin bàn̄ Aseeka nì Makeeda timmun.

english_verse: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
translation_verse: Bi nín bí ki sáń Isirayeel yab ki bíi wúntí Beeti-Oorɔn gbantaŋkee, ní ti-Dindaan yāntì ataanyiŋkumbil akpaan nyánní yilpu ki tābitì ki kūū-bi. Bi-kansikin bin ní ataanyiŋkumbil tābitì ki kūūyee nìn wīikí ki jítiǹ bin bin Isirayeel yab nìn dū ntàataajimu ki kūūyee.

english_verse: The Lord was helping the Israelites defeat the Amorites that day. So about noon, Joshua prayed to the Lord loud enough for the Israelites to hear: “Our Lord, make the sun stop in the sky over Gibeon, and the moon stand still over Aijalon Valley.” So the sun and the moon stopped and stood still until Israel defeated its enemies. This poem can be found in The Book of Jashar. The sun stood still and didn't go down for about a whole day.
translation_verse: Ní ŋwìiń yúl̀ kaa ti bíi còom̄ ní uŋmal mun gbíntì u-laŋki kaa ti bíi sútí, ki tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel nibul jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ bi-nannanliibee. An bɔti gbanti ŋmàn̄ ki kā Deedeedaan gbɔŋku poon míǹ. Ŋwiin gbantee, ŋwìiń nìn yúl̀ kutagbɔŋu kansikin nì kansikin ní kaa nìn jìkī yii ŋu làá jēetí, ki bàn̄ kii ŋwimmɔn.

english_verse: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
translation_verse: Dalba dalba ti-Dindaan kaa fōō unifoo nyɔkɔ kii yéè ki ká kii ŋwiin gbantee, ní ŋwiin gbanti boonee, an kaa tí jítì míǹ ki ká jaanjaan. Tiŋman, yaadalee, ti-Dindaan di nìn jáń kujaau ki tīī Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: After the battle, Joshua and the Israelites went back to their camp at Gilgal. Joshua Kills the Five Enemy Kings
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ fātìi nín gítí Giilgaal naapaal pu. Joosuwa kūū bibɔtiibi biŋmoo bin u jáń ki jíńee

english_verse: While the enemy soldiers were running from the Israelites, the five enemy kings ran away and hid in a cave near Makkedah.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi biŋmooyee bíǹ nìn sáǹ ki cūtìi bál̀ kutaŋkpanaakoou kubɔn, Makeeda tiŋkin.

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Binib biba nìn ká-bi niin ní ki cūtìi tùkū Joosuwa yii: «Ti ká bibɔtiibi biŋmooyee bál̀ kutaŋkpanaakoou kubɔ poon, Makeeda tiŋkin.»

english_verse: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa bí yii: «Ní bíntí ataŋkpakpaan kí pìin̄ kutaŋkpanaakoouee nyɔkɔpu, kí lēē binib biba bí nīn cí.

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: Ama nimbee, ní taa gbíntí niin. Ní jà ni-nannanliibi boon kí gāā kí kíntí-bi, kí taa yàntī bí fàtīí sāǹ kí kɔ́ bi-timmun. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di dū-bi ki ŋá ni-ŋaan!»

english_verse: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab nìn ŋman kūū ki kúntì bi-kɔkɔ ní. Binikaaŋkaabi di nìn ŋúń ki sáǹ ki kɔ́ ntimu mun bi máń agun ki māntìi túee poon.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nín gítí dijanjanaapaal pu nì ŋgbansɔŋfi Joosuwa cee, Makeeda tiŋkin. Báà unil kaa nìn pée gíti wàantí u-nyɔkɔ ní kaa nín múlifì tiba Isirayeel yab pu.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa bí yii: «Ní cúúmaan ataŋkpee kí lēē kí wàatī kutaŋkpanaakoouee nyɔkɔ, kí cúuń bibɔtiibi biŋmooyee kí cáań-mi doo!»

english_verse: The soldiers opened the entrance to the cave and brought out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
translation_verse: Ní bi lafun pīitìń bibɔtiibi biŋmooyee kutaŋkpanaakoouee poon ki cáań Joosuwa cee. An dàkà yii Jeerusaleem bɔtiu nì Eebrɔn bɔtiu nì Yaarmuti bɔtiu nì Lakiisi bɔtiu nì Eeglɔn bɔtiu.

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Bi nyántìń bibɔtiibi biŋmooyee ki cáań Joosuwa ceeyee, ní u yíiń Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki bí bijanjaliibi kpilib u nì bin nóóyee yii: «Ní sútiḿmaan doo, kí tāā bibɔtiibi nee silii kí nákáǹ kitiŋ.» Ní bi sútìń u-cee ki dū bi-taaŋi ki tāā bibɔtiibee silii ki nákáǹ kitiŋ.

english_verse: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa tùkū-bi yii: «Ní taa fàŋkìmaan, kí taa yàntī ni-wunti ń yɔ̀tī. Ní ká dipɔbil kí taa fàŋkì baa tiba, kun puee ti-Dindaan nín làá ŋá binannanliibi bin kɔkɔ ni nì bi làá jée puee dee.»

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: Joosuwa sòon̄ míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki kūū bibɔtiibee ŋmootil, ki yāntì bi dū-bi ki lúntì isufi iŋmoo pu ní bi lúń niin ki tin sāā kujoou.

english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń jéetèe ní Joosuwa pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí kpákatiń bibɔtiibee wunti isufee pu kí cáá tɔ̄ kutaŋkpanaakoou kun poon bi nìn bál̀ee. Bi dóòyee ní ki tōō ataŋkpakpaŋkpaan ki kpúkuǹ nyɔkɔpu. Ataŋkpee gbanti dáá gbíntìi kpúkú niin díǹ pu nee. Joosuwa jáń ki fōō ntimu mun bí ŋgiil púee

english_verse: Later that day, Joshua captured Makkedah and killed its king and everyone else in the town, just as he had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Ŋwimbaanti gbanti ní Joosuwa jáń ki fōō Makeeda tiŋki, ki kūū ki-bɔtiu nì ki-nib kɔkɔ, kaa kíǹ báà uniseen. U nìn ŋá Makeeda bɔtiu kii u nín nìn pée ŋá Jeeriikoo bɔtiu puee ní.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab yíkì Makeeda tiŋkinee ní ki nìkī ki cūtìi bíi jáà nì Liibina tiŋki yab.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn dū kitiŋ gbanti mun ki ŋá Isirayeel yab ŋaan ní bi kūū ki mun nib kɔkɔ, kaa kíǹ báà uniseen. Bi nìn ŋá ki mun bɔtiu kii bi nín nìn ŋá Jeeriikoo bɔtiu puee ní.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab yíkì Liibina tiŋkinee ní ki nín cá Lakiisi tiŋki. Bi bàn̄ee ní ki māntìi gíb́ kitiŋ gbanti ki bíi jáà nì ki-nib.

english_verse: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn dū Lakiisi tiŋki mun ki ŋá Isirayeel yab ŋaan ní bi jáń ki fōō-kì ŋwinliliiti dal, ki kūū ki-nib kɔkɔ kii bi nín nìn ŋá Liibina tiŋki puee.

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Geeseer bɔtiu Ooram yíkìń kí bàà dāá tíkiń Lakiisi tiŋki yab, ní Joosuwa kūū u nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ, báà uniseen kaa kíǹ.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yíkì Lakiisi tiŋkinee ní ki cūtìi māntìi gíb́ Eeglɔn tiŋki ki bíi jáà nì ki.

english_verse: captured it that same day, then killed everyone, as they had done at Lachish.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti mbaanti ní bi jáń ki fōō Eeglɔn tiŋki, ki kūū ki-nib kɔkɔ nì kitàataajiki kaa kíǹ báà uniseen, kii bi nín nìn ŋá Lakiisi tiŋki puee.

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: Bi nìn jáń ki fōō Deebiir tiŋki ki cúú ki-bɔtiu. Bi nìn fōō ntimu mun pìlīǹ-kèe ki kūū ki-nib kɔkɔ, báà uniseen kaa kíǹ. Kii Joosuwa nín nìn ŋá Eebrɔn tiŋki nì ki-bɔtiu nì Liibina tiŋki nì ki-bɔtiu puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní u ŋá Deebiir tiŋki mun.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Joosuwa nìn jáń ki fōō kitiŋ gbanti kɔkɔ, an dàkà yii ntimu mun bí ajoon puee, nì mun bí Neegeeb teekunee, nì mun bí Seefeelaa paal puee, nì ntimu mun nákáǹ ajoon tikiŋŋee kɔkɔ, ní ki cúú mu-bɔtiibi. Waa nìn yāntì báà uniseen kíǹ. U nìn kūū binifoobi kɔkɔ kii ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín nìn tīī mara bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ bi-kɔkɔ, ki yōoǹ Kadeesi-Baarneeya tiŋki ki tin cáa sāā Gaasaa tiŋki, ní ki yōoǹ Gooseen tiŋki kɔkɔ ki tin cáa sāā Gabawɔn tiŋki.

english_verse: King Jabin of Hazor heard about Joshua's victories, so he sent messages to many nearby kings and asked them to join him in fighting Israel. He sent these messages to King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
translation_verse: Asɔɔr bɔtiu Jabiini nín nìn gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní u lēē binib ki tú Maadoon bɔtiu Joobaab, nì Simroon bɔtiu nì Akisaafi bɔtiu cee.

english_verse: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
translation_verse: U nìn tú bibɔtiibi bin kóòń ŋgan pú ajoon puee, nì ditantakalin Kiineereeti mɔɔl ŋgiil pú, nì Seefeelaa paal puee, nì Dɔɔr tiŋki kin bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee cee.

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: U nìn gíti tú Kanaan yab bɔtiibi bin kóòń ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì ŋu-jeetilaŋki púee, nì Amɔɔr yab nì Eeti yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Jeebusi yab bin kóò ajoon puee, nì Eefi yab bin kóò Eermɔn jool taapu Miisipa tiŋkinee bɔtiibi cee.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Taa pée fàŋkì-bi, kun puee fool naŋkɔnampuee mama m-ba fu kūū bi-kɔkɔ ki tīī Isirayeel yab dee. Á fu gàatì ki gīfì bi-taamui taaŋi ní kí fu wà bi-janjatɔrɔkub ŋŋmi.»

english_verse: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
translation_verse: Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab nìn cūtìi túuǹ-bi Meeroom buŋŋu caŋin ní ki páatìi jéetì bi-pu.

english_verse: Up to this time, the king of Hazor had controlled the kingdoms that had joined together to attack Israel, so Joshua led his army back and captured Hazor. They killed its king
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, Joosuwa nìn fātìi gítì ki cūtìi jáń ki fōō Asɔɔr tiŋki kin nìn sá atimbun gbanti kɔkɔ tiŋyilee, ní ki kūū ki-bɔtiu.

english_verse: and everyone else, then they set the town on fire.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kūū binifoobi bin kóò kitiŋ gbantinee kɔkɔ. Báà uniseen kaa nìn kíǹ, ní ki sēē-kì ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Joshua captured all the towns where the enemy kings had ruled. These towns were built on small hills, and Joshua did not set fire to any of these towns, except Hazor. The Israelites kept the animals and everything of value from these towns, but they killed everyone who lived in them, including their kings.
