That's what the Lord had told his servant Moses to do, that's what Moses had told Joshua to do, and that's exactly what Joshua did.
translation_verse: Tin ti-Dindaan nìn tīī u-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi mara ú ŋée, tíǹ ní Mooyiisi mun nìn dūu tīī Joosuwa. Ní Joosuwa nìn ŋá tin ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara ú ŋée deedee, kaa bātì báà tiba ki fá. Isirayeel yab púntìi fōō Kanaan tiŋki kɔkɔ

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Joosuwa nìn jáń ki fōō kitiŋ gbanti kɔkɔ. U nìn fōō ntimu mun bí ajoon puee, nì Neegeeb teekun kɔkɔee, nì Gooseen timmu kɔkɔ, nì ntimu mun bí Seefeelaa paal puee nì mun bí Arabaa teekunee, nì mun bí Isirayeel jool nì ki-paal puee.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he wanted the towns in this region destroyed and their people killed without mercy. That's why the Lord made the people in the towns stubborn and determined to fight Israel. The only town that signed a peace treaty with Israel was the Hivite town of Gibeon. The Israelite army captured the rest of the towns in battle.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di nìn pɔ́ɔkì ntimu gbanti nib pɔbiliŋ ní bi kíí ki jáń nì Isirayeel yab, án nín làá ŋá pu ní bíǹ ń kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi kí taa sɔ̄ bi-saai kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ní Joosuwa cūtì ki jáń nì Anaaki yab bin nìn kóò ntimu mun bí ajoon puee, an dàkà yii Eebrɔn nì Deebiir nì Anaab timmu, nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ bí Juuda nì Isirayeel jooŋŋi puee. Joosuwa nìn kūū ki céetì binib gbanti ní ki nāaǹ bi-timmu kɔkɔ.

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Anaaki yab báà unil kaa nìn gíti kíǹ Isirayeel yab tiŋkin, asee Gaasaa nì Gaati nì Asidoodi timmun ní bikaaŋkaabi biba nìn kíǹ ki bí.

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nìn fōō kitiŋee kɔkɔ ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee, ní ki dū-kì ki yākatì ki tīī Isirayeel yab bí nīn kíǹ ki yì, ki nóó nì bi-naakɔti nín sá puee. Niinee ní ŋgbansɔŋfi dɔ́miń kitiŋee pu ní kujaau gbēeǹ.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ bibɔtiibi bili ki fōō bi-timmu Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, kí yòon̄ Arinɔn buŋŋu kí tin cáá sāā Eermɔn jool, ki kpáaǹ ditantakal din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki jandi púee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The first king that Moses and the Israelites defeated was an Amorite, King Sihon of Heshbon. The southern border of his kingdom ran down the middle of the Arnon River gorge, taking in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the gorge. The Jabbok River separated Sihon's kingdom from the Ammonites on the east. Then the Jabbok turned west and became his northern border, so his kingdom included the southern half of the region of Gilead.
translation_verse: Upeepeekaa di nìn sá Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu Siiwɔn un nìn kóò Eesbɔn tiŋkinee. U-beel nìn kífí kí yòon̄ Arooweer tiŋki kin nákáǹ Arinɔn buŋŋuee, nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ bí ki pìlīǹ mbun gbantee, nì Galaadi tiŋki dijandi diba, kí tin cáá sāā Yaabɔki buŋŋu ŋun sá Amɔn yab tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔee.

english_verse: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, u-tiŋki di sá kí yòon̄ ditantakal kí cáá bà Kiineereeti mɔɔl din bí ŋgan púee. Kí yòon̄ míǹ kí cáá bà Ditantakal mɔɔl din bi gíti yíì yii Ŋyaam mɔɔlee jandi din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, Beeti-Yeesimooti tiŋki watil pú, ní kí yòon̄ ŋgiil pú kí tin bà Piisga jooŋŋi nín wúntí puee taapu.

english_verse: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Uliliiti di nìn sá Baasan tiŋki bɔtiu Ɔɔgi un nìn sá Reefa yab bin pée kíǹ kitiŋ puee ubɔee. U nìn kóò Asitarooti nì Eedreeyii timmun ní.

english_verse: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
translation_verse: U-beel nìn jīǹ kí yòon̄ Eermɔn jool nì Saleeka tiŋki nì Baasan tiŋki kɔkɔ kí tin cáá sāā Geesuur yab nì Maaka yab kpaanyɔkɔ nì Galaadi tiŋki dijandi diba kí cáá sāā Eesbɔn bɔtiu Siiwɔn tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nì Isirayeel yab nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ bibɔtiibi gbanti liitil ní Mooyiisi nìn dū bi-tiŋki kɔkɔ ki tīī Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔti nì Manasee naakookun yab dijandi diba bí nīn kíǹ ki yì.

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Joosuwa dāa púĺ tikpilee ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «A-wiiŋyi kaa ti náaǹ, ama ní kitiŋ nee jandi din kíǹ ní fōōyee dáá gbíntìi wīikí tikpil.

english_verse: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Manasee naakookun yab dijandi diba nì Rubeen naakookun yab nì Gaadi naakookun yab nìn fōō bi-tinjandi din Mooyiisi nìn tīī-bee Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní. Ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi di nìn yākatì kitiŋ gbanti ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: Bi-tinjandi gbanti di sá kí yòon̄ Arooweer tiŋki kin bí Arinɔn buŋŋu caŋinee, nì kitiŋ kin bí Arinɔn tantakalinee kɔkɔ, nì Meedeeba tiŋki kin dɔ̄ ki tèen̄ee kí tin sāā Diibɔn tiŋki.

english_verse: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
translation_verse: Bi-tinjandi gbanti nìn nìkī kí yòon̄ Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu Siiwɔn un nìn kóò Eesbɔn tiŋkin, kí tin cáá sāā Amɔn yab tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab kaa nìn fōō Geesuur yab nì Maaka yab timmu. An pu ní Geesuur nì Maaka yab dáá gbíntìi kóò Isirayeel yab kansikin ki dāa sāā díǹ pu nee.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: Leefii naakookun yab baba ní baa nìn yākatì kitiŋ ki kpáaǹ. Bíǹ fakal di sá saraabi bin bi ŋáań ki tìì ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiuee, kii úǹ u-ba nín nìn pōoǹ-bi puee.

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn tīī Rubeen naakookun yab bi-tinjandi ki nóó nì bi nín nìn pēē mmaal puee ní.

english_verse: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
translation_verse: Bi-tiŋki di nìn sá kí yòon̄ Arooweer tiŋki kin pìlīǹ Arinɔn buŋŋuee, nì kitiŋ kin bí ditantakalinee, nì kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ ki tèen̄ ki gítí Meedeeba tiŋki watil púee,

english_verse: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ ki tèen̄ee puee, nì Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu Siiwɔn un nìn kóò Eesbɔn tiŋkinee timmu kɔkɔ. Úǹ ní Mooyiisi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ, ki kpáaǹ Maadiyan tiŋki bɔtiibi Eefi nì Reekeem nì Suur nì Kuur nì Reeba. Bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ nìn bí ubɔti Siiwɔn taapu ní ki nìn kóò kitiŋ gbanti pu.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaam un nìn sá ubɔɔyee mun nìn kútì binib bin Isirayeel yab nìn kūūyee poon.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Jɔɔdan buŋŋu di nìn sá Rubeen naakookun yab tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. Rubeen naakookun yab tinjandi timmu nì di-timbilimmu nín nìn sá puee dee, ki nóó nì bi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee.

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn tīī Gaadi naakookun yab mun bi-tinjandi ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee.

english_verse: It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Bíǹ tiŋki di nìn sá Yaseer tiŋki nì Galaadi timmu kɔkɔ nì Amɔn yab tiŋki dijandi diba, kí cáá sāā Arooweer tiŋki kin pìlīǹ Raaba tiŋkee.

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: Bi-timmu di nìn gíti sá kí yòon̄ Eesbɔn tiŋki kí cáá sāā Ramati-Miisipee tiŋki nì Beetooniim tiŋki, ní kí yòon̄ Maanayiim tiŋki ki cáá sāā Deebiir tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: Jɔɔdan buŋŋu tantakalinee, bi-timmu di nìn sá Beeti-Aram nì Beeti-Niimra nì Sukooti nì Safoon. Bíǹ di nìn gíti yì Eesbɔn bɔtiu Siiwɔn tiŋki kɔkɔ, an dàkà yii kí yòon̄ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kitiŋ kin pée dɔ̄ kansikin kí tin cáá sāā Kiineereeti mɔɔl kúntilaŋki ŋgan púee.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Gaadi naakookun yab tinjandi timmu nì di-timbilimmu nín nìn sá puee dee, ki nóó nì bi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee.

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi nìn tīī Manasee naakookun yab dijandi diba mun bi-tinjandi Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, ŋwìiń nyalaŋki jaaŋŋu pú.

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: Bíǹ di nìn gíti yì Galaadi tiŋki dijandi diba nì Baasan timmu Asitarooti nì Eedreeyii, laakin ubɔti Ɔɔgi nìn kóòyee. Ntimu mun bi nìn tīī Manasee jipɔɔn Makiir biyaamu ki nóó nì bi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee dee.

english_verse: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
translation_verse: Atinjan ŋin Mooyiisi nìn yākatì ki tīī Isirayeel yab Moowaab tantakalin, Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi lapu pu yal, Jeeriikoo tiŋki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee dee.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Ama Mooyiisi kaa nìn tīī Leefii naakooku yab bíǹ ditinjandi. Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu di nìn sá bíǹ fakal, kii úǹ u-ba nín nìn pōoǹ-bi puee.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Dalbee, Juuda naakookun yab biba dɔ́miń Joosuwa cee Giilgaal tiŋkin ní Yeefunee un sá Keeniisi maaliŋunee jipɔɔn Kaleeb bí Joosuwa yii: «A máaǹ ki téetí tin ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ man nì sii pu u-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi cee, Kadeesi-Baarneeya tiŋkinee.

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: Man nì m-nabiyaamu mun nìn cūtèe nìn bíil̀ samaa pɔbil, ama ní man nìn nóó ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu bɔti nì dipɔbil diba.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee Mooyiisi nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ-mi yii: <M pūtì yii kitiŋ kin a-taal tāā nee, kíǹ ní bi làá dūú tīī sii nì a-maaliŋu yab ní nīn kíǹ ki yì kí nīn cá jaanjaan, kun puee a ŋá ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu nín bí yii á ŋá puee deedee!>

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: An puee, dū dijool pu tiŋki kin ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ-mi ŋwiin gbantee kí tīī-mi. Ŋyuntee, m nìn tùkū-si yii Anaaki yab di kóò niin, ní bi-timmu sá ntiŋkpaamu bi máń agun ki māntìi tú-mu. An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan làá tíkiń-mi ḿ ŋmā kí já kí fōō kitiŋ gbanti bi-cee, kii úǹ u-ba nín nìn sòon̄ puee.»

english_verse: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa bīiǹ Yeefunee jipɔɔn Kaleeb pu, ní ki dū Eebrɔn tiŋki ki tīī-u ú nīn kíǹ ki yì.

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Njaminee, Eebrɔn yindi di nìn sá Kiiriyati-Ariba. Arba gbanti di nìn nyáń diyindi ki jítiǹ Anaaki yab bin kíǹee kɔkɔ. Míǹ boonee ní ŋgbansɔŋfi dɔ́miń Kanaan tiŋki pu ní baa ti bíi jáà.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ŋgiil pú púee, bi-kpaanyɔkɔ nìn kíĺ Ŋyaam mɔɔl gbeenlaŋki, laakin kitiŋ tin kóò dimɔɔlin ní an náań nì dilimbil ki túĺ Neegeeb teeku púee.

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: Ki yōoǹ niinee ki dūu dī Akrabiim gbantaŋki Siini teeku ŋgiil pú, ki nín jɔ́ḿ Kadeesi-Baarneeya tiŋki ŋgiil pú ki tin bàn̄ Eesirɔn tiŋkin. Ki yōoǹ niin ki nín jɔ́ḿ Adaar tiŋkin ní ki pɔ́ĺ ki cūtì Karka tiŋki watil pú,

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: ki jítì Asimɔn tiŋki pu ki tin bàn̄ Eejipiti buŋŋu ní ki tin sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu. Ŋgiil púee, Juuda yab tinjandi din bi fōōyee kpaanyɔkɔ dee.

english_verse: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, bi-tinjandi kpaanyɔkɔ kíĺ Ŋyaam mɔɔl ki cáa sāā Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nín kúntí puee. Ŋgan púee, kikpaanyɔkɔ kíĺ Ŋyaam mɔɔl laakin náań nì dilimbilee ki cáa sāā Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nín kúntí puee.

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Ki yōoǹ niinee ki nín jɔ́ḿ Beeti-Oogila tiŋki, ki dī Beeti-Arabaa ŋgan pú ki tin sāā laakin bi yíì yii Rubeen jipɔɔn Bookan taŋkpalee.

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: Kikpaanyɔkɔ yōoǹ niinee ní ki dūu dī Akɔɔr tantakalin ki tin bàn̄ Deebiir tiŋki. Ki pɔ́ĺ ŋgan pú ki nín cá Geeliilɔti tiŋki kin bí Adumiim gbantaŋki nimbiinee watil pú, mbun nín dɔ̄ puee ŋgiil pú. Ki nìkī ki nín cá Eeni-Seemeesi buŋŋu pú ní ki tin bàn̄ Eeni-Roogeel.

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Niinee ní kikpaanyɔkɔ fātìi nín jɔ́ḿ Been-Kiinoom tantakal pú, Jeebusi yab tiŋki kin bi gíti yíì yii Jeerusaleem tiŋkee caŋin. Niinee ní ki nín jɔ́ḿ dijool din bí Kiinoom tantakal nimbiin ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú, nì Reefayiim gbantaŋki kúntilaŋki ŋgan púee yilpu.

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: Kikpaanyɔkɔ yíkì dijool yilpuee ní ki sīntì Neefitoowa nyimbuliŋu watil pú ní ki nín nìkì Eefrɔn jool timmu pu, ki pɔ́ĺ ki nín cá Baala tiŋki kin bi gíti yíì yii Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋkee watil pú.

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: Kikpaanyɔkɔ yōoǹ Baala tiŋkee ní ki pɔ́ĺ ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ki nín cá Seeyiir jool watil pú, ki kpākaǹ Yaariim jool din bi gíti yíì yii Keesalɔn joolee ŋgan pú, ki nín sìntī Beeti-Seemeesi tiŋkin ki cūtìi pūntì Tiimina tiŋki.

english_verse: It continued along to the hillside north of Ekron, curved around to Shikkeron, and then went to Mount Baalah. After going to Jabneel, the border finally ended at the Mediterranean Sea,
translation_verse: Ki yōoǹ niinee ní ki cáa bàn̄ Eekrɔn tiŋki caŋin ŋgan pú, ní ki pɔ́ĺ ki nín cá Siikaroon tiŋki watil pú, ki nín nìkì Baala jool nì Yabineeyeel tiŋki watil pú ní ki tin cáa sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Boonee ní u nìkī ki cūtìi jáń nì Deebiir tiŋki kin bi nìn yíì dooooyee yii Kiiriyati-Seefeer tiŋkee yab.

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Yeefunee jipɔɔn Kaleeb mun nìn fōō kitiŋ Juuda yab tinjandi poon ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Joosuwa yii ú ŋá puee. Bi nìn tīī-u Kiiriyati-Ariba tiŋki kin nìn sá Anaaki yab tiŋki bi kíǹ ki yíì díǹ pu nee yii Eebrɔn tiŋkee ní. Arba di nìn sá Anaaki baa.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Kaleeb nìn jìn̄ Anaaki jipɔmbi taatil bin nìn bí niinee naantiibi. U-jipɔmbi gbanti yiŋŋi di nìn sá Seesayi nì Akiimaani nì Talimayi.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Niin ní Kaleeb bí yii: «Un di yaa ŋúń ki jáń nì Kiiriyati-Seefeer yab ki fōō bi-tiŋkee, m làá dū m-bisal Akisa kí tīī udaan ú cáá.»

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Akisa bàn̄ u-cal ceeyee ní ki sāal̀-u ú bàlifì u-baa ú tīī-u tikpaatan. Boonee ní u kpákatì u-maŋki pu ní u-baa Kaleeb bālifì-u yii: «A là ba ní?»

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: Ní u kii yii: «M là kí mèè-si tiba ní. Di sá yii a tīī-mi ntimu Neegeeb teekun ní, an puee á tīī-mi anyimbɔbil mun!» Ní Kaleeb tīī-u anyimbɔbil ŋin bí yilpu puee nì ŋin bí taapu puee.

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Ditinjandi din bi nìn tīī Juuda naakookun yab ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: nì Leebawɔti nì Siiliim nì Ayiin nì Riimɔn. Ntimu gbanti nìn kpáfì mmuŋku nì muwa ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: nì Saarayiim nì Aditayiim nì Geedeera tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu. Mu nìn kpáfì ntimu kiba kpá saalku ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: nì Geedeerooti nì Beeti-Daagɔn nì Naama nì Makeeda. Mu nìn kpáfì ntimu saalku nì kiba ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: The fifth region was located along the Mediterranean seacoast, and it had the following towns with their surrounding settlements and villages: Ekron and the towns between there and the coast, Ashdod and the larger towns nearby, Gaza, the towns from Gaza to the Egyptian Gorge, and the towns along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: nì Asidoodi tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu nì ntimbilimu mun bí ki-taapuee kɔkɔ. Kí kūtì Gaasaa tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu nì ntimbilimu mun bí ki-taapuee kɔkɔ ki tin cáa sāā Eejipiti buŋŋu nì Meediiteeranee tiŋkugbandi.

english_verse: The seventh region was located in the south-central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages: Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth-Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath-Arba, which is now called Hebron, and Zior.
translation_verse: nì Umita nì Kiiriyati-Ariba tiŋki kin bi gíti yíì yii Eebrɔn tiŋkee, nì Siiyɔɔr. Mu nìn kpáfì ntimu muwa ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: The eleventh region was located in the northern part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following two towns with their surrounding villages: Rabbah, and Kiriath-Baal, which is also called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: ní ki kútì Kiiriyati-Baal tiŋki kin bi gíti yíì yii Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋkee nì Arabaa tiŋki. Múǹ nìn sá ntimu muli ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab kaa nìn ŋúń ki jìn̄ Jeebusi yab bin nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee ki fōō bi-tiŋki. An pu ní díǹ pu nee Jeebusi yab dáá gbíntìi kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, Juuda naakookun yab kansikin.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Ditinjandi din bi nìn tīī Eefiraayiim naakookun yab bi yākatì ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee sèé. Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, kikpaanyɔkɔ yōoǹ Atarooti-Adaar tiŋki ki tin cáa sāā Beeti-Oorɔn yilpu tiŋki.

english_verse: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ntimu nì mu-timbilimmu mun nìn bí Manasee naakookun yab tinjandinee ki kútì-bi.

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Baa nìn jìn̄ Kanaan yab bin nìn kóò Geeseer tiŋkinee. An puee bíǹ dáá gbíntìi kóò Eefiraayiim yab kansikin ki dāa sāā díǹ pu nee. Ama ní Eefiraayiim yab nìn dū-bi ki kpántì iyumbu bi kíǹ ki tūǹ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki tìì-bi.

english_verse: The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring.
translation_verse: Manasee tinjandi kpaanyɔkɔ nìn kíĺ Aseer tiŋki ní ki tin sāā Miikimeetati tiŋki kin bí Siikeem tiŋki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee ní, ki nìkī ŋgiil pú ki tin sāā binib bin kóò Eeni-Tapuuwa tiŋkee.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Manasee yab di nìn yì Tapuuwa tiŋki, ama Eefiraayiim yab di nìn yì Tapuuwa tiŋki dijandi din bí Manasee yab tinjandi kpaanyɔkɔee.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Isakaar yab nì Aseer yab tinjaŋŋi poonee, Manasee yab di nìn gíti yì Beeti-Seeyan tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu, nì Yeebileeyam tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu, nì binib bin kóò Dɔɔr nì Eeni-Dɔɔr timmuee nì mu-timbilimmu, nì Taanaki nì Meegiidoo yab timmu nì mu-timbilimmu. Kitintataatii di sá Dɔɔr tiŋki.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Ama ní Manasee naantiibi kaa ŋúń ki jìn̄ ntimu gbanti nib ki nyántì, di sá yii Kanaan yab di yóoǹ yii bíǹ kpá ki làá yīkì ntimu gbanti pu.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín dāa pɔ́ɔkiǹ Kanaan yabee ní bi dū-bi ki kāaǹ bi-taapu ní ki yāntì bi kíǹ ki tūǹ-bi atuun kii iyumbuee. Ama baa nìn jìn̄-bi kitiŋee pu.

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Jooseefi naantiibi sòon̄ nì Joosuwa ní ki bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní a tīī-ti ditinjandi dibaba ja, timbi bin ti-Dindaan bīiǹ ti-boon ti būtì tiŋan pu ki wīikí tikpil nee?»

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa kíí-bi yii: «Ni yaa wīikí tikpil ní Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi kaa bàn̄ ní kàl̄ee, ní cù Peeriisi yab nì Reefa yab bambaŋkun kí ŋàtī kí kàl̄.»

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Ní Jooseefi naantiibi fātìi bí-u yii: «Tiŋman, dijool tiŋki nee kaa làá lafun bà-ti. Kí kūtèe, Kanaan yab bin kóò kitiŋ kin tèen̄ee cáá tikúti janjatɔrɔkub ní, ki kpáaǹ Beeti-Seeyan tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu yab, nì Jisirayeel tantakalin yab kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa bí Jooseefi naantiibi, an dàkà yii Eefiraayiim nì Manasee naakɔtin yab yii: «Ni lafun wīikí tikpil ní ki cáá mpɔn tiŋan pu, naa làá fōō ditinjandi dibaba ja.

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: Nimbi di làá nīn yì dijool pu tiŋki, nì min ní kì sá kubambaŋŋuee. Ní ŋàtī kí ŋāŋkì ki-kɔkɔ kí nīn kíǹ ki yì. Ni làá ŋmā kí jà Kanaan yab, báà nì bi nín cáá tikúti janjatɔrɔkub ki cáá mpɔŋkpaan nee!»

english_verse: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn jáń ki fōō kitiŋ kɔkɔ. Niinee ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì Siiloo tiŋkin, ní ki dū dikpafindi tantiu ki cóoǹ niin.

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
translation_verse: Ní binib bin bi lēēyee lafun yíkì ki nín cá. Kí wàatī bí búntí kí cùú ŋmà kitiŋ nín bí puee ní Joosuwa bí-bi yii: «Nín̄ cámaan kí cùú yìiǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu. Ní kpèè kì nín bí puee tiŋan kí fàtīí gítiń kí tùkù-mi. M làá tɔ̄ kasi ti-Dindaan nimbiin Siiloo tiŋkin doo, kí yàkatī-kì kí tīī kunaakoou kamaa ku-tinjandi.»

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Ní binibee nín cá ki cūtìi yìin̄ kitiŋee kɔkɔ pu. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ atinjan alulee nín bí puee nì ŋi-timmu. Míǹ boonee ní bi fātìi nín gítiń Joosuwa cee Siiloo naapaal pu.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Joosuwa nìn tɔ́ kasi Siiloo naapaalin niin ti-Dindaan nimbiin, ní ki yākatì kitiŋ ki tīī Isirayeel yab. U nìn tīī kunaakoou kamaa ku-tinjandi. Beenjameen naakookun yab tinjandi

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Bi nín nìn tɔ́ kasee, an nìn péé ki lēē Beenjameen naakookun yab tinjandi ní ki tīī-bi. Bi-tinjandi gbanti nìn sáká Juuda naakookun yab nì Jooseefi naakookun yab tinjaŋŋi kansikin ní.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Ŋgan púee, bi-kpaanyɔkɔ nìn kíĺ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ní, ki dūu dī Jeeriikoo tiŋki ŋgan pú, ki kpākaǹ dijool ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú, ki tin cáa gbēeǹ Beeti-Aween teeku.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Niinee ní kikpaanyɔkɔ nìn dūu pɔ́ĺ ki māntì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú, dijool din bí Beeti-Oorɔn tiŋki nyɔkɔpuee ŋgiil pú ní ki cáa gbēeǹ Kiiriyati-Baal àá Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋki kin sá Juuda yab tiŋkee. Ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, kikpaanyɔkɔ dee.

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Ŋgiil púee, kikpaanyɔkɔ nìn kíĺ doooo Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim nín kúntí puee ní, ki nìkī Ŋyaam mɔɔl watil pú ki tin cáa gbēeǹ Neefitoowa nyimbuliŋu.

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: Kikpaanyɔkɔ tí yōoǹ niinee ní ki nín sìntī dijool kúntilaŋki laakin bíitiǹ Been-Inɔɔm tantakalee, Reefa yab tantakal poon ki cá ŋgiil pú. Ki nìn nóó Inoom tantakal gbantee ki dūu dī Jeebusi yab tiŋki ŋgiil pú, ki tin cáa gbēeǹ Eeni-Roogeel tiŋki.

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Kikpaanyɔkɔ nìn yíkì niinee ní ki pɔ́ĺ ŋgan pú ki nín cá Eeni-Seemeesi tiŋki pú, ki nìkī Geeliilɔti tiŋki kin bí Adumiim gbantaŋki nyɔkɔpuee ní ki nín sìntī laakin bi yíì yii Rubeen Jipɔɔn Boowan taŋkpalee watil pú.

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Ki nìn yōoǹ niinee ní ki kpākaǹ kigbantaŋ kin bí Beeti-Arabaa tiŋki nyɔkɔpuee ŋgan pú, ní ki nín nìkì Arabaa tantakalin.

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ki nìn dūu dī Beeti-Oogila tiŋki ŋgan pú ki cáa gbēeǹ Ŋyaam mɔɔl nín kífí pu ŋgan púee, an dàkà yii Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kúntilaŋki ŋgiil pú. Ŋgan pú kpaanyɔkɔ nín nìn sá puee dee.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Jɔɔdan buŋŋu di nìn sá kikpaanyɔkɔ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki jaaŋŋu pú. Beenjameen yab tinjandi din bi yākatì ki tīī-bee nì di-kpaanyɔkɔ nín nìn sá puee dee, ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee.

english_verse: One region of Benjamin's tribal land had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Those towns were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, Emek-Keziz, Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Chephar-Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba.
translation_verse: nì Keefaar-Amɔna nì Oofinii nì Geeba. Mu nìn kpáfì ntimu saalaa nì muli ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Bi nín nìn tɔ́ kasi nliliitiimee, an nìn lēē Simeeyɔn naakookun yab tinjandi ní ki tīī-bi ki nóó nì bi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee. Bi-tinjandi gbanti nìn sáká Juuda naakookun yab timmu kansikin ní.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: nì Beeti-Leebawɔti nì Seeruyeen. Mu nìn nyáń ntimu saalaa nì muta ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Bi-timmu di nìn gíti sá Ayiin nì Riimɔn nì Eeteer nì Asaar. Mu nìn kpáfì ntimu munaa ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-muee kɔkɔ, kí tin cáá bà Balaati-Beer àá Ramati-Neegeeb tiŋkee, Simeeyɔn naakookun yab di nìn yì kɔkɔ, ki nóó nì bi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Juuda naakookun yab tinjandi ní bi nìn gíí ki tīī Simeeyɔn naakookun yab. Di sá yii bi nín nìn ŋmāntì ditinjandi din ki tīī Juuda naakookun yabee nìn wīikí tikpil ki jítiǹ-bi, an pu ní bi nìn gíí ki bātì ki dūu tīī Simeeyɔn naakookun yab. Sabulɔn naakookun yab tinjandi

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: Kikpaanyɔkɔ māntì Neeya tiŋki ŋgan pú ní ki tin bàn̄ Yiifita-Eel tantakalin.

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ditinjandi gbanti timmu di nìn sá Kataati nì Naalal nì Simroon nì Yideeyala nì Beetileem. Mu nìn nyáń ntimu saalaa nì muli ní, mu nì mu-timbilimmu.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Sabulɔn naakookun yab timmu nì mu-timbilimmu mun bi nìn tīī-bi bi yākatì ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee dee. Isakaar naakookun yab tinjandi

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Isakaar naakookun yab timmu nì mu-timbilimmu mun bi nìn tīī-bi bi yākatì ki nóó nì bi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee dee. Aseer naakookun yab tinjandi

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, kikpaanyɔkɔ nìn dūu túĺ Beeti-Daagɔn tiŋki watil pú ní ki tin sāā Sabulɔn naakookun yab tinjandi kpaanyɔkɔ nì Yiifita-Eel tantakal. Niinee ní kì nìkī ŋgan pú ki tin sāā Beeteemeeki nì Neeyeel. Kì yíkì niinee ní ki nín cá Kabuul,

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: nì Abidɔn nì Reewoob nì Amoon nì Kana ní ki tin sāā Siidɔn, kitiŋkpaaŋŋi.

english_verse: Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Aseer naakookun yab timmu nì mu-timbilimmu mun bi nìn tīī-bi bi yākatì ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee dee. Neefitalii naakookun yab tinjandi

english_verse: Naphtali was the sixth tribe chosen to receive land. The southern border for its clans started in the west, where the tribal lands of Asher and Zebulun meet near Hukkok. From that point it ran east and southeast along the border with Zebulun as far as Aznoth-Tabor. From there the border went east to Heleph, Adami-Nekeb, Jabneel, then to the town called Oak in Zaanannim, and Lakkum. The southern border ended at the Jordan River, at the edge of the town named Jehudah. Naphtali shared a border with Asher on the west.
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, kì nìn fātìi dūu dī Asinɔti-Tabɔɔr tiŋki watil pú, ki cāatì ki nín cá Ukooki tiŋki watil pú. Kì nìn gūū Sabulɔn yab kpaanyɔkɔ ŋgan pú, ní ki gūū Aseer yab kpaanyɔkɔ ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú, Yeewuuda tiŋkin. Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, Jɔɔdan buŋŋu di nìn sá kikpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar nì Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab naakɔti poon adican kpilib di nìn tɔ́ kasi ki yākatì ntimu gbanti. Siiloo tiŋkin, ti-Dindaan nimbiin, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ní bi nìn tɔ́ kasi gbanti. Bi nìn ŋá míǹ ní ki yākatì Kanaan tiŋki kɔkɔ ki dāa dóò.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Ntimu mun bi nìn lēē ki yóoǹ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nì binicambi bin kóò bi-kansikinee, un yaa kaa nyí ki kūū u-jutee ń sāǹ kí kɔ́ee dee. Mimmee unikpɔlee ŋūǹ kí ŋmátí un u kūūyee nabiki kin máaǹ kí kpɔ̀-u kí tɔ̀ ipɔntoonee ŋaan, kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní u làá dāá yūĺ samaa nimbiin bí sòoǹ u-bɔtee.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Joosuwa ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: «Tùkù Isirayeel yab yii bí lēē ntimu mun ubɔ yaa kaa nyí ki kūū unil ú sāǹ kí kɔ́ee. M nìn dī Mooyiisi pu ki sòon̄ nì ntimu gbanti bɔti.

english_verse: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
translation_verse: Unikpɔlee ń sāǹ kí cù ntimu gbanti kiba poon, kí sīĺ kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu kí dū tibɔti nín jítì puee kí kàaǹ kí tùkù niin tindaŋkpilib. Bitindaŋkpilibee ń fōō unikpɔlee bi-tiŋki gbanti poon, kí nyàab̀ ŋkɔŋkoon kí tīī-u u nì bi ń nīn kóò.

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Un bi kūūyee nabiki kin máaǹ kí kpɔ̀ unikpɔlee kí tɔ̀ ipɔntoonee yaa jìn̄ u-boonee, bí taa dū unikpɔlee kí ŋá u-ŋaan. Di sá yii unikpɔlee kaa là ní ki kūū-u, kaa tí sá mun yii u ná-u.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Unikpɔlee ń gbíntí kí nīn bí kitiŋ gbantin kí dāá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní u làá dāá yūĺ samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin bí sòoǹ u-bɔtee. Ú nīn bí niin kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní usaraaŋakpil un bi lēē ŋyunti gbantee yaa láa kpíìyee. Míǹ boonee, unikpɔlee ŋūǹ kí fàtīí gítí u-dumpu, kitiŋ kin poon u sáǹ ki kátèe.»

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Di sá ní bi nìn lēē Kadeesi tiŋki kin bí Galiilee tiŋkin Neefitalii jool puee, nì Siikeem tiŋki kin bí Eefiraayiim jool puee, nì Kiiriyati-Ariba tiŋki kin bi gíti yíì yii Eebrɔn tiŋki kì bí Juuda jool puee.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi lapu pu yal Jeeriikoo tiŋki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, bi nìn lēē Beeseer tiŋki kin bí kuteeunee Rubeen yab tiŋki kin tèen̄ee poon, ki nìn lēē Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkinee Gaadi yab timmu poon, ní ki lēē Goolan tiŋki kin bí Baasan tiŋkinee Manasee yab timmu poon.

english_verse: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
translation_verse: Siiloo, Kanaan tiŋkin. Bi nìn bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan nìn dī Mooyiisi pu ki tùkū-ni yii ní tīī-ti ntimu tí nīn kóò, ní kí tīī-ti ntimu gbanti kpaanceetii tí nīn kpàá ti-waŋkuti.»

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Di sá ní Isirayeel yab nìn lēē bi-timmu mun bi tīī-bi bí yàkatēe mubɔ, ki kpáaǹ mu-kpaanceetii kɔkɔ ki dūu tīī Leefii naakookun yab, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū-bi yii bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Bi nín nìn tɔ́ kasee, Leefii naakookun yab bin sá Keeyaati maaliŋunee di nìn péé ki fōō bi-timmu. Keeyaati yab gbanti kansikinee, bin nìn sá usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn maaliŋunee ní bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ki lēē ntimu saalaa nì muta ki tīī. Ntimu gbantee, bi nìn lēē-mu Juuda nì Simeeyɔn nì Beenjameen naakɔti yab timmu poon ní.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki lēē ntimu gbanti nì mu-kpaanceetii kɔkɔ ki tīī Leefii yab, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī Mooyiisi pu ki tīī-bi mara puee.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Ntimu mun bi nìn tīī Aarɔn naantiibi bisaraaŋaliibee nìn kpáfì ntimu saalaa nì muta ní, mu nì mu-kpaanceetii.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: Ntimu mun bi nìn tīī Geersɔn naantiibee dee. Mu nìn kpáfì ntimu saalaa nì muta ní, mu nì mu-kpaanceetii.

english_verse: The people of the Levi tribe had a total of
translation_verse: Bi nìn tīī ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ nì mu-kpaanceetii ní.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn lafun tīī Isirayeel yab kitiŋ kin u nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ kí tīī bi-naanjabee kɔkɔ. Ní Isirayeel yab fōō kitiŋ gbanti ki kíǹ ki yì ní ki kāl̀ ki-poon.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì bi ká diŋuŋfil ajan kɔkɔ pu, kii u nín nìn pōoǹ bi-naanjab puee. Bi-nannanliibi báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋúń ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn dū bi-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ki ŋá bi-ŋaan.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn ŋá Isirayeel yab tiŋan tin kɔkɔ u nìn pōoǹ yii u làá ŋá kí tīī-bee, báà tiba kaa nìn gbíntì waa ŋá.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa yíiń Rubeen naakookun yab nì Gaadi naakookun yab nì Manasee naakookun yab dijandi din bíń Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee ki kpáfì.

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Naa dū ni-nabiyaamu ki fá abin kupaau ŋin jítì nee ki dāa dūu sāā díǹ. Ni nóó ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín yóoǹ-ni mara puee deedee.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī ni-nabiyaamu diŋuŋfil din u nìn pōoǹ-bee. Ni ŋūǹ kí kpì ni-dumpui, kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nìn tīī-ni Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú jaaŋŋuee.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Ama ní nīn ŋúb́ marab bin ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi tīī-nee tiŋan. Ní nīn néeń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, kí nīn còom̄ u-saŋyi poon, kí nīn tɔ́ u-marab, kí dū ni-ba kí nákáǹ-u ní kí nīn nóó-u nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ».

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Ní bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee yii: «Kpèèmaan, Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔtin yab, nì Manasee naakooku dijandi dibee yab máń nsaraafan Kanaan tiŋkin, Jɔɔdan buŋŋu caŋin, timbi jandi pú».

english_verse: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab gbìl̄ mimmee, ní samaa kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì Siiloo tiŋkin, ki bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi kí cùú jáǹ-bi kujaau.

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn lēē usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar jipɔɔn Piinaasi ki tú Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔtin yab nì Manasee naakooku dijandi dibee yab cee Galaadi tiŋkin.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lēē bikpilib saalaa ki kútì u-pu. Kunaakoou kamaa ukpil ubɔ, ní ukpil kamaa sá u-dicaŋku poon uyidaan, ki nóó nì Isirayeel yab nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Bi nín cá Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔtin yab, nì Manasee naakooku dijandi dibee yab cee Galaadi tiŋkin. Bi bàn̄ee ní ki sòon̄ nì bi yii:

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan samaau kɔkɔ nyɔkɔpu ní ti sòoǹ nì ni nee. Ba yintikpaandi ní ni yīntiǹ Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu mimmee? Ba ŋá ní ni nyáń ti-Dindaan boon díǹ ki máń ni-ba nsaraafan ki bíi jáà nì u míǹ?

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Mimmee ikpiti in ti nìn ŋá Peewɔɔr tiŋkinee kaa ŋmāntàaa? Díǹ pu nee taa láá pàn̄ ikpiti gbanti pɔndi ki dóò, báà nì min kɔkɔ i-puee, ti-Dindaan dáaĺ u-samaau tafal ŋkpitim puee!

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Ní díǹ nee, nimbi bíi fàtī ni-boon ki tìì ti-Dindaanaaa? Díǹ nee, ni yaa bíi jáǹ ti-Dindaanee, fool boonee u-ŋuul làá dāá jēetí Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ pu ní.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Ni yaa ká yii kitiŋ kin bi tīī-nee kaa bí circiree, ní póotiń ti-Dindaan tiŋki pu doo, laakin u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu bée, kí dāan̄ ti nì ni ń nīn bí ki-pu. Ama ní taa jáǹ ti-Dindaan, kí taa jáǹ ti mun, kí mā ni-ba nsaraafan ŋubɔ kí kūtì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu saraafaŋŋu pu!

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Seera jipɔɔn Akan nín nìn yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan ki yùn̄ tiwan tin kpántì u-wantee tibee, ti-Dindaan ŋuul kaa nìn jéetì Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ pu níii? U-baba di kaa nìn kpíì u-kpitii pu!»

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔtikpaan! Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔtikpaan ní ki nyí kun pu ti ŋá mimmee, ní ki là yii Isirayeel yab mun ń béé. An yaa sá yii ti nín ŋá puee, ti bíi jáà nì ti-Dindaan àá ti yīntiǹ-uee, ú taa yàntī tí nīn gíti bí!

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Ti yaa máń nsaraafan yii tí fàtī ti-boon kí tīī ti-Dindaan, kí ŋá saraawɔkaa àá tijimpin saraau àá mpèé saraauee, ti-Dindaan u-ba ń bàlifì-ti!

english_verse: We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.” Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yóoǹ kikpaanyɔkɔ ti nì nimbi Rubeen nì Gaadi naantiibi kansikin, an di sá Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. An puee báà tiba kaa ti bí ni nì ti-Dindaan kansikin!> Niinee ní ni-naantiibi ń dāá yàntī timbi yab ń gbèen̄ kí taa ti nín̄ jáaḿ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti sòon̄ ki yóoǹ yii tí mā nsaraafan ŋubɔ kí yóoń ti-ba, án taa nín̄ sá yii ti làá nīn cáa ŋáań saraawɔkaa àá bisaraafantantiibi biba.

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Ní Usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar jipɔɔn Piinaasi tùkū Rubeen nì Gaadi nì Manasee yab yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee ti béè yii ti-Dindaan bí ti-kansikin, kun puee ni nín ŋá puee kaa sá yii ni jáń nì u. Mimmee ni fīī Isirayeel yab ti-Dindaan ŋaan ki líì dee.»

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋakpil Eeleeyasaar jipɔɔn Piinaasi nì bikpilibee yíkì Rubeen nì Gaadi nì Manasee yab cee Galaadi tiŋkin ki fātìi nín gítiń Kanaan tiŋkin Isirayeel yab cee, ní ki cáań an nín jítìń pu lapuee ki máafì-bi.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: An bɔtee mɔ́ɔkiǹ Isirayeel yab ní bi jáam̀ Unimbɔti, ní kaa ti sòon̄ yii bi làá cù kí jáǹ Rubeen nì Gaadi yab kí nàan̄ kitiŋ kin bi kóòyee.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Rubeen nì Gaadi yab nìn téeń ki lī yii: «Nsaraafan nee sá kudaaŋŋu ki dàkà yii ti-Dindaan baba di sá Unimbɔti!» Niinee ní bi pú nsaraafanee diyindi yii <Kudaaŋŋu>.

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ká diŋuŋfil abin kupaau bi-nannanliibi bin māntìi tú-bee cee. Ŋyunti gbantee Joosuwa nìn púĺ ki kpántì utikpil.

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nìn yíiń Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nì bi-tindaŋkpilib nì bi-yidambi nì bi-bɔsoonliibi nì bi-gbaŋŋmaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì. U nìn bí-bi yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee m púĺ tikpil.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Nimbi ni-ba ká, ni-puee, tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ŋá atimbun nee kɔkɔee. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu u-ba di jáń ki tīī-ni.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu u-ba di làá jà-bi kí wàatī-ni, kí yàntī bí sāǹ kí fá bi-timmu, ní ní fōō bi-timmu kí nīn kíǹ ki yì, kii úǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu u-ba nín nìn pōoǹ-ni puee.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: An puee nimbi kámaan dipɔbil tiŋan, kí pɔ́ɔǹ kí nīn nóó tin tin kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Mooyiisi Marab gbɔŋkunee. Ní nīn pée nóó-tì deedee, kí taa kpòotī kí cù ŋgiil púɔɔɔ, kí taa kpòotī kí cù ŋgan pú.

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: Ní taa dū ni-ba kí ŋmàlim̀ atimbun ŋin kíǹ ki dáá gbíntìi kóò ni-kansikin nee nib poon. Ní taa pée pútí bi-waaŋi yiŋŋi, kí taa yíiń ŋi-yiŋŋi kí pùtī, kí taa gbàan̄ ŋi-nimbiin kí jāam̀-ŋi.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan jìn̄ atimbun ŋin sá akpaan ki pɔ̄ɔ̄yee nib ni-nimbiin, ní báà unil kaa ŋúń ki yúl̀ ni-nimbiin ki dāa sāā díǹ pu nee.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Ni-kansikin unibaanti nìn ŋūǹ kí jà binib kutuku ubɔ, kun puee ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di nìn jáà ki tìì-ni, kii u nín nìn pōoǹ-ni puee.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: An puee ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba kí nīn néeń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: ní nīn nyí tiŋan yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kaa làá ti jà atimbun gbanti kí wàatī-ni. Ŋi làá dāá kpántí kii kutaliŋŋu àá kpaalaa ní kí tīī-ni, ní kí dāá kpántí mbambaan ŋun bi làá nīn cáa gbáà-nee, ní kí kpántí ikuŋkum ki sàatī ni-nimbiliŋ. An dāa pée kúntée, ni làá dāá wāŋkì kitimmɔntii kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dūu tīī-ni nee pu ní.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: Ní kpèè, díǹ pu nee man cá laakin unifoo kamaa cée dee. Nimbi ni-ba ń béé nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ yii tiŋan tin kɔkɔ ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nìn pōoǹ-nee, u ŋá ti-kɔkɔ pái ki tīī-ni, báà tiba kaa kíǹ waa ŋá.

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Joosuwa kpáfì Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ Siikeem tiŋkin, ní ki yíiń Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib nì bi-yidambi nì bi-bɔsoonliibi nì bi-gbaŋŋmaliibi ní bi-kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki kpáfì ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa bí Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: <Cannaakuee ni-naanjab Abraam nì Naakɔɔr baa Teera nìn kóòń Eefiraati mɔɔgbandi lapu jaaŋŋu pú ní, ní ki nìn tòotī awaa.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kin bí Eefiraati mɔɔgbandi lapu jaaŋŋu gbanti púee ní m nìn yōoǹní ni-naanja Abraam, ki nìn cáá-u ki yìin̄ ki māntì Kanaan tiŋki kɔkɔ, ki nìn yāntì u-maaliŋu būtì tiŋan, ní ki nìn tīī-u Isaaki.

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: M nìn tīī Isaaki mun Jaakɔb nì Eesayuu. M nìn dū Seeyiir jool ki tīī Eesayuu ú nīn yì, ama ní Jaakɔb nì u-jipɔmbi nìn sīntì Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: Ni-naanjab nìn kúuǹ ki yíiń man ni-Dindaan ḿ jòoń-bi, ní m nìn dū dibɔmbɔndi ki pītì ni nì Eejipiti yab kansikin ní ki nìn yāntì dimɔɔl nyim fātìi gítì ki bīiǹ bi-pu. Nimbi ni-ba nìn ká m nín nìn ŋá Eejipiti yab puee. Míǹ boonee, ni nìn kāl̀ kuteeun ki yúntì tikpil.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: M nìn cáá-ni ki cūnnì Amɔɔr yab bin nìn kóòń Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi lapu puee tiŋki pu. Binib gbanti nìn jáń nì ni. M nìn dū-bi ki ŋá ni-ŋaan ni ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō bi-tiŋki, ní m kúntì bi-kɔkɔ ni-nimbiin.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Siipɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaaki, Moowaab yab bɔtiu mun nìn yíkì kí jáǹ-ni ní ki nìn tú bi yíiń Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaam ú dāan̄ kí tɔ̄-ni mbusu.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Ama maa nìn kíí ki pílifiǹ Balaam. See u nín nìn líbitì ki bīiǹ ni-puee, ní m nìn fīī-ni ki nyántì Balaaki ŋaan.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: Ni nìn dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki bāań Jeeriikoo tiŋkin ní Jeeriikoo yab nìn jáń nì ni. Amɔɔr yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Giirgaasi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab mun nìn jáń nì ni. Ama m nìn dū bi-kɔkɔ ki ŋá ni-ŋaan.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: M nìn dū abaakati ní ki līntì ni-nyɔkɔpu ní ŋi sáǹ ki jìn̄ Amɔɔr yab bɔtiibi bilee. An kaa nìn sá ni-tàataajimmu nì ni-tɔfii ní ni nìn dūu jìn̄-bi.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: M nìn tīī-ni tikpaatan faalaa, ní naa nìn gīī digìńdi báà diba ti-pu. M nìn tīī-ni ntimu ni kāl̀, ama ní kaa máń-mu. M nìn tīī-ni fiinyi nì ɔliifi sufii in naa nìn cóoǹee, ama ní ki bí ki ŋmóò i-biliŋ.>»

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa kútì yii: «An puee, kɔŋkɔnnee ní fàŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan, kí nīn jáaḿ-u nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ibaamɔn poon. Ní dū awaa ŋin ni-naanjab nìn tòotī Eefiraati mɔɔgbandi lapu jaaŋŋu pú nì Eejipiti tiŋkinee kí fá, kí nīn kíǹ ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaan baba.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Ama an yaa kaa fáatì-ni yii ní nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaanee, ní lēē díǹ nee un ni làá nīn jáaḿee. Ni yaa là awaa ŋin ni-naanjab nìn tòotī ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíń Eefiraati mɔɔgbandi lapu jaaŋŋu púeeyaaa, ni yaa tí là Amɔɔr yab bin tiŋki ni kóò nee waaŋaaa, ní lēē. An yaa kíǹ kii man nì m-dicaŋkuee, timbi làá nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan ní!»

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní samaa kíí Joosuwa yii: «Unimbɔti ń cáá cùnnì ndan! Timbi kpá kí fàtī ti-boon kí tīī ti-Dindaan kí cùú nīn tòotī awaa aba fám!

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu di nìn nyántìń ti nì ti-naanjab kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkin, ní ki nìn ŋáaǹ atuŋkpaan ti-nimbiin ti kántì. Úǹ di bīiǹ ti-boon nsan ŋun ti nìn cōom̀ee poon nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ pu ti nìn jítì jítèe.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di nìn jìn̄ Amɔɔr yab nì anibul ŋin nìn kóò kitiŋ nee puee kɔkɔ ki wāatì-ti. An puee ti mun lēē yii ti-Dindaan ní ti làá nīn jáaḿ, kun puee úǹ di sá ti-Nimbɔtiu.»

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa bí samaa yii: «Naa làá ŋmā kí nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan, kun puee u sá Unimbɔti un bí circiree ní, ki sá Unimbɔti un cáá ipoompoonee. Waa làá dū ni-yìntitam nì ni-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ni.

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Ni yaa fātì ni-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan ki kíǹ ki bí ki tòotī awaayee, u làá bíkití ni-pu ní kí ŋá-ni tin kaa ŋān̄ee. Tiŋan tin u ŋá-nee boonee, u làá nàan̄-ni ní pílpil!»

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ní samaa kíí Joosuwa yii: «Kpataaa, ti-Dindaan ní ti làá nīn jáaḿ!»

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa bí-bi yii: «Nimbi ni-ba sá ni-seeradambi yii ni lēē kí nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan!» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Iiin, ti sá ti-seeradambi.»

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa bí-bi yii: «An yaa sée, kɔŋkɔnnee ní dū awaa ŋin kɔkɔ bí ni-ceeyee kí fá, ní kí dū ni-ba kí nákáǹ ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ!»

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Ní samaa kíí Joosuwa yii: «Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ní timbi làá nīn pée jáaḿ, ní kí nīn tɔ́-u.»

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti ní Joosuwa yāntì u nì samaa pūtì ki pōoǹ, ní u síiǹ Siikeem tiŋkin niin abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin ní bi máaǹ kí nīn nóóyee.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Ní Joosuwa dū an bɔtee kɔkɔ ki ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá Unimbɔti Marau gbɔŋku poon. U dóòyee ní ki dū ditaŋkpakpaandi diba ki cóoǹ niin, busubu bun bi yíì yii teereebinti bu yú mpaan ŋun pu bi jáaḿ ti-Dindaanee taapu.

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: U cóoǹ ki dóòyee ní ki bí samaa kɔkɔ yii: «Ní kpèèmaan! Ditaŋkpal nee di làá dāá nīn sá-ti seeradaan, kun puee di gbìl̄ anyɔɔbun ŋin kɔkɔ ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì tee. Dì làá nīn sá ni-seeradaaŋwu án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa fàtī ni-boon ki tīī ni-Nimbɔtiuee.»

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joosuwa pú samaa nsan yii báà ŋma ń nīn kùǹ, ní báà ŋma nín gítí u-tiŋki pu. Joosuwa kúm nì u-síbitam

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Tibɔti nee kɔkɔ jítì boonee ní Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa, ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu kpíì. U nìn cáá abin dilaataal nì saalaa ní.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Bi nìn síb́-u kitiŋ kin bi nìn tīī-u u kíǹ ki yèe poon ní, an dàkà yii Tiiminati-Seera tiŋki kin bí Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu, ki gítí Gaasi jool ŋgan púee.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan ŋyunti ŋun ní Joosuwa nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee nì u-kúm boon bikpilib bin nìn dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin, ki nìn ká atuŋkpaan ŋin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nìn ŋáaǹ ki tīī Isirayeel yabee.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn cáá Jooseefi kpabiŋ ŋin bi nìn kpáaǹní Eejipiti tiŋkinee ki síb́ Siikeem tiŋkin, ntampaan ŋun Jaakɔb nìn dá Siikeem baa Amɔɔr naantiibi cee ki pàn̄-u animbil jitɔmbi dilaataalee pu. Ntampaan gbanti mun nìn kútì Jooseefi naantiibi tinjandi poon.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Aarɔn jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar mun dāa kpíì, ní bi cáá-u ki síb́ u-jipɔɔn Piinaasi gbantaŋki kin bi nìn tīī-u Eefiraayiim jooŋŋinee pu.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Joosuwa kúm boonee ní Isirayeel yab bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «Ti-kansikin bilab di làá péé kí jɔ̄m̀ kí cùú jáǹ Kanaan yab ní?»

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kíí yii: «Juuda naakookun yab di làá jɔ̄m̀. Bíǹ ŋaan ní m dū kitiŋ gbanti ki ŋá.»

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Juuda naakookun yab bí bi-nabiyaamu Simeeyɔn naakookun yab yii: «Ní dāá céem̀maan-ti tí jɔ̄m̀ timbi tinjandi pu kí cùú jáǹ Kanaan yab, ní boonee ti mun ń dāá céeǹ-ni ni-tinjandi pu tí cùú já.» Niinee ní Simeeyɔn naakookun yab kútì Juuda naakookun yab pu ki búntì.

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Juuda naakookun yab nìkī ki cūtìi jáń nì Kanaan yab bin nìn kóò Eebrɔn tiŋkinee. Dooooyee bi nìn yíì Eebrɔn tiŋki yii Kiiriyati-Ariba ní. Niin ní Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Seesayi nì Ayiiman nì Talimayi naantiibi.

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Ubɔti Adoonii-Beeseeki nìn sáǹ ki kátì ní bi jìn̄ ki cúú-u ki gūutì u-ŋambijaliŋ nì u-taŋambijaliŋ.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Juuda naakookun yab nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Jeerusaleem yab ki fōō bi-tiŋki, ki dū ntàataajimu ki kūū binib kɔkɔ ní ki sēē Jeerusaleem tiŋki ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Juuda naakookun yab nín sìntī ki cūtìi jáń nì Kanaan yab bin nìn kóò ajoon pu timmuee, nì bin nìn kóò Neegeeb timmuee nì bin kóò Seefeelaa paal timmuee.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Juuda naakookun yab yíkì niinee ní ki cūtìi jáń nì Deebiir tiŋki yab. Deebiir tiŋki gbanti ní bi nìn yíì dooooyee yii Kiiriyati-Seefeer.

english_verse: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
translation_verse: Ní Kaleeb bí yii: «Un di yaa ŋúń ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Kiiriyati-Seefeer yab ki fōō kitiŋ gbantee, m làá dū m-bisal Akisa kí tīī udaan ú cáá.»

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Kaleeb naal Keenaasi jipɔɔn Ootiniyeel di ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō kitiŋ gbanti, ní Kaleeb dū u-bisal Akisa ki tīī-u u cáá.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Akisa bàn̄ u-cal Ootiniyeel ceeyee ní ki sāal̀-u ú bàlifì u-baa Kaleeb ú tīī-u tikpaatan. Akisa u-ba kpákatì kimaŋ puee ní Kaleeb bālifì-u yii: «A là ba ní?»

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí u-baa yii: «M là kí mèè-si tiba ní. Di sá yii tikpaatan tin a tīī-mee sá kuteeu ní, an puee á tīī-mi inyimbul mun!» Ní Kaleeb dū inyimbul in bí yilpu puee nì in bí taapu puee ki tīī-u.

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi coo un nìn sá Keeni maaliŋunee naantiibi yíkì Ibafi tiŋki ki nóó Juuda naakookun yab ní bi-kɔ nín jɔ́ḿ Juuda teeku dijandi din bí Araadi tiŋki ŋgiil púee. Bi bàn̄ ní ki kāl̀ dinibul din nìn kóò niinee yab kansikin.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Juuda nì u-maan Simeeyɔn naakɔtin yab nìkī ki cūtìi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Kanaan yab bin nìn kóò Seefaati tiŋkinee. Bi nìn kúntì kitiŋ gbanti kɔkɔ ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Ɔrima, taapu di sá yii <adigbun>.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí Juuda naakookun yab cee ki tútúǹ-bi ní bi ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō ntimu mun bí ajoon puee kɔkɔ. Ama baa nìn ŋúń ki jìn̄ binib bin nìn kóò laakin tèen̄ee timmuee, kun puee binib gbanti bíǹ nìn cáá janjatɔrɔkub bin bi nìn dū tikúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee ní.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū Eebrɔn tiŋki ki tīī Kaleeb ki nóó nì Mooyiisi nín nìn lī puee, ní Kaleeb jáń ki fōō kitiŋee Anaaki jipɔmbi taatil bin nìn kóò kitiŋ gbantee ŋaan.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Beenjameen naakookun yab kaa nìn ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki Jeebusi yab ŋaan. An pu ní Jeebusi yab pée gbíntìi kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, bi nì Beenjameen naakookun yab, ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: The Ephraim and Manasseh tribes were getting ready to attack Bethel, which at that time was called Luz. And the Lord helped them when they sent spies to find out as much as they could about Bethel.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lēē bi-nib biba ki tú bi cūtìi cɔ́ŋkì ki kpēē Beeteel tiŋki nín bí puee. Bi nìn dá láá yíì Beeteel tiŋki yii Luusi ní.

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Bicɔŋkiliibee nìn tú uninja ubɔ nyánní kitiŋin ní bi bí-u yii: «Dàkà-ti laakin bi dìŋfī kí kɔ́ kitiŋinee, ti làá dāá ŋá-si tiŋan kí téeǹ!»

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn dàkā-bi bi nín làá dī pu kí kɔ́ kitiŋinee, ní bi kɔ́ ki dū ntàataajimu ki kūū binib bin nìn kóò kitiŋ gbantee kɔkɔ. Ama bi nìn yāntì uninjee nì u-nabiyaamu búntì kaa ŋá-bi báà tiba.
