english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Ní kijapaayee nín cá Eeti yab tiŋkin ki bàn̄ ki náań kitiŋ niin ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Luusi. Diyindi gbanti ní bi pée gbíntìi yíì an tiŋkee ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: Canaanites lived in the towns of Beth-Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and all the villages nearby. The Canaanites were determined to stay, and the Manasseh tribe never did get rid of them. But later on, when the Israelites grew more powerful, they made slaves of the Canaanites.
translation_verse: Ama boonee, Isirayeel yab nín dāa fōō mpɔnee ní bi dū Kanaan yab ki ŋá bi-taapu, ki yāntì bi kíǹ ki tūǹ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki tìì-bi. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Isirayeel yab kaa nìn ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō ntimu gbanti Kanaan yab ŋaan.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim naakookun yab kaa nìn ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō Geeseer tiŋki Kanaan yab ŋaan. An pu ní Kanaan yab nìn pée gbíntìi kóò Geeseer tiŋki, Eefiraayiim yab kansikin.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Sabulɔn naakookun yab kaa nìn ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō Kiitirɔn tiŋki nì Naalɔɔl tiŋki Kanaan yab ŋaan. An pu ní Kanaan yab gbanti nìn pée gbíntìi kóò Sabulɔn yab kansikin. Ama ní Sabulɔn yab dū-bi ki ŋá bi-taapu, ki yāntì bi tūǹ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki tìì-bi.

english_verse: The Asher tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob, and the Asher tribe lived with Canaanites all around them.
translation_verse: Aseer naakookun yab nìn kóò Kanaan yab bin nìn bí ntimu gbantinee kansikin ní, kun puee baa nìn fōō ntimu gbanti Kanaan yab ŋaan.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Neefitalii naakookun yab kaa nìn ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō Beeti-Seemeesi nì Beeti-Anaati timmu Kanaan yab ŋaan. Bi nìn kóò Kanaan yab bin nìn bí ntimu gbantinee kansikin ní. Ama ní ki nìn dū Beeti-Seemeesi yab nì Beeti-Anaati yab ki ŋá bi-taapu, ki yāntì bi tūǹ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki tìì-bi.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amɔɔr yab nìn jìn̄ Daani naakookun yab ki tɔ́ ajoon pu ní, kaa pée pú-bi mpaan bi sīntìń mpɔfin.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Amɔɔr yab gbanti nìn gbíntì ki kóò Aari-Eereesi nì Ayalɔn nì Saalbiim timmu. Ama Eefiraayiim nì Manasee naakɔtin yab dāa fōō mpɔnee ní ki dū-bi ki ŋá bi-taapu, ki yāntì bi kíǹ ki tūǹ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki tìì-bi.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Amɔɔr yab tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ nìn kífí Akrabiim gbantandi ní, kí yòon̄ laakin bi yíì yii Seerayee kí nīn cáa jɔ́ḿ yilpu pú.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nyáń Giilgaal tiŋkin ki jɔ́m̀ Bookiim tiŋkin ki bí Isirayeel yab yii: «M nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin ní ki cáá-ni ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin m nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ yii m làá tīī ni-baabee. M nìn lī yii: <M kpá kí kpìtī mpèé ŋun m bóob́ nì nee.

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: Ni mun nì binib bin kóò kitiŋ nee ń taa ŋá mpèé. Ní gbá kí kpìtī bi-saraafaŋyi kɔkɔ.> Ama ní nimbi kaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ. Ba bɔti ní ni ŋá mimmee!

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní ma mun bí yii: <Maa làá jà binib bin kóò kitiŋ nee puee kí wàatī-ni. Binib gbanti làá nīn sá-ni kpaalaa, ní bi-waaŋi ń nīn sá-ni kutaliŋŋu.»

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: An pu ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Bookiim, taapu di sá yii <Bin sūǹee>, ní bi ŋá saraabi niin ki tīī ti-Dindaan. Joosuwa kúm

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Bi nìn síb́-u u-tinjandi din bi nìn tīī-u difakalee pu, Tiiminati-Eereesi tiŋkin, Eefiraayiim jool pu ki gítí Gaasi jool ŋgan pú.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Joosuwa yuntiŋu yab gbanti dāa kpíì ki dóò. Binipɔmbi nìn yíkì ki téeǹ bi-yil, ama bíǹ kaa nìn nyí ti-Dindaanaaa, kaa nìn nyí atuŋkpaan ŋin ní u nìn ŋáaǹ ki tīī Isirayeel yabee. Isirayeel yab fātì bi-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Ŋyunti kamaa bi yaa nìn gíti nyáń ki cūtì kujaauee, ti-Dindaan nìn dàkà u-pɔŋŋu ní ki yàntī bi jáà ki pɔ́ɔkíǹ-bi, kii úǹ ti-Dindaan u-ba nín nìn pée tùkū-bi ki pūtì yii u làá ŋá puee. An ŋá mimmee ní kunimbaau kɔ́ Isirayeel yab tikpil.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan u-ba lēē bibɔsoonliibi biba Isirayeel nibul poon ní bíǹ fìil̄ samaa kɔkɔ ki líikí digaŋgandambi bin nìn bí ki jàkà-bee ŋaan.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Isirayeel yab kaa nìn pílifì bi-bɔsoonliibi gbanti nyɔkɔ gba. Bi nìn bí ki nóó inimbɔticaan iba boon, ki gbàantí i-nimbiin ki jáaḿ-i. An kaa nìn pée súŋkì ní bi dū nsan ŋun bi-baabi bin nìn ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan marabee nìn nóóyee ki fá, kaa ti nóó-ŋu.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín nìn lèekī bibɔsoonliibi ki tìì Isirayeel yabee, úǹ ti-Dindaan u-ba nìn bí ubɔsoonli un kamaa u yaa nìn lēēyee cee, ní ki nìn fìil̄ Isirayeel yab bi-nannanliibi ŋaan ubɔsoonlee maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon. Di sá yii bi-nannanliibi yaa nìn bíi wɔ́b̀-bi ki sàantí-bi ní bi bíi sūǹ ki yáliŋkée, ti-Dindaan nìn sūǹ bi-saai.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Ama ubɔsoonlee tin lì yii u kúùyee, ní Isirayeel yab ń fàtīí tí gáatí kí jītíǹ bi-baabi nín nìn gáatí puee gba. Bi nìn nōotí inimbɔticaan, ki gbàantí i-nimbiin ki jáaḿ-i. Baa nìn féeń atuŋkpiti ŋin bi nìn ŋáańeeyaaa, kaa nìn yàntī mpɔɔgbifin ŋun bi nìn cááyee mun. Ti-Dindaan cɔ́ŋkì u-nibul Isirayeel yab

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan gíí diŋuul Isirayeel yab pu ki lī yii: «Ditimbundi nee nib kpītì m-pèéŋu ŋun m nìn bóob́ man nì bi-baabee, kaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ.

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: An puee ma mun kaa làá ti jà atimbun ŋin nib Joosuwa kaa nìn jìn̄ ní ki nín kpíìyee kí wàatī-bi.»

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn là kí dī atimbun gbanti pu ní kí cɔ̄ŋkì u-nibul Isirayeel yab kí kpèè yii bi làá nīn gbíntìi nóó úǹ ti-Dindaan saŋŋu kii bi-baabi nín nìn nóó pueeyaaa, baa làá nīn nóó.

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì atimbun gbanti nib gbíntìi bí Kanaan tiŋkin, kaa nìn jìn̄-bi malaayaaa, kaa nìn dū-bi ki ŋá Joosuwa ŋaan mun.

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: U nìn baasii là yii binipɔmbi bin kaa nìn pée jáń kujaau ki kée ń bīfì bi nín jáà kujaau puee ní.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: An nibee di nìn sá Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi biŋmooyee, nì Kanaan yab nì Siidɔn yab nì Eefi yab bin kɔkɔ nìn kóò Leebanɔn jool pu, kí yòon̄ Baal-Eermɔn jool kí tin cáá sāā Leeboo-Amaati tiŋkee.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn lēē binib gbanti kí dī bi-pu kí cɔ̄ŋkì Isirayeel yab kí kpèè yii bi làá nīn nóó marab bin úǹ ti-Dindaan nìn dī Mooyiisi pu ki tīī bi-baabeeyaaa, baa làá nīn nóó-bi.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Bi nìn cáá binib gbanti bisalib, ki nìn dū bi-bisalib ki tīī binibee jipɔmbi ticati, ní ki nìn bí ki jáaḿ bi-nimbɔtii. BIBƆSOONLIIBI BƆTI Ootiniyeel

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn ŋá min kaa kítì ti-Dindaan ceeyee, di sá yii bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu saŋŋu ki fá ní ki nìn kíǹ ki bí ki tòotī Baal nì Aseera.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn gíí Isirayeel yab pu diŋuul ní ki dū-bi ki ŋá Kusan-Riseeyatayiim, Aram-Naarayiim bɔtiu ŋaan. Isirayeel yab nìn kāl̀ Kusan-Riseeyatayiim taapu abin anii ní.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan, ní ti-Dindaan lēē bi-kansikin Ootiniyeel, Kaleeb naal Keenaasi jipɔɔn ní úǹ fīī-bi.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn fātìi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań min kaa kítì ti-Dindaan ceeyee. Bi nín nìn bíi ŋáań min kaa kítì ti-Dindaan ceeyee puee ní u yāntì Moowaab bɔtiu Eeglɔn pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Eeglɔn nìn dū Amɔn yab nì Amaleeki yab ki kútì u-ba pu ní bi cūtìi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Isirayeel yab, ní ki cúú Jeeriikoo, Ibafi tiŋki ki fōō bi-cee.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Eewuudi nín dū lampoo ki tīī ubɔtee ní u fātìi nín gítí ki cūtìi céeǹ binib bin nìn túǹ lampoo gbantee ki nyántì nsanni.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and the Lord chose Ehud from the Benjamin tribe to rescue them. They put Ehud in charge of taking the taxes to King Eglon, but before Ehud went, he made a double-edged dagger. Ehud was left-handed, so he strapped the dagger to his right thigh, where it was hidden under his robes.
translation_verse: Eewuudi nìn yāntì bi mɔ́ɔ́-u kitàataajiki kiba, kì jītí ajanliitil pu ní ki-fɔkɔŋŋu sá kii dimeetajandi nyɔkɔm. U nìn dū kitàataajikee ki gbìn̄ tiwan tin u pēēyee poon, ní an pá u-ŋaŋgiitapandi pu.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn kā u-diiku kun nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpu ki sɔ̀m̀ fílfil bi bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ úǹ babee poon ní Eewuudi sútìi pìl̄-u ki bí-u yii: «Tibɔti tin m cáá kí tùkù-see sá Unimbɔti bɔti ní.» Ní ubɔti yíkì u-beejal pu ki yáatìi yúl̀.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Niinee ní Eewuudi tāntì u-ŋaŋgan ki cúú kitàataajiki kin nìn pá u-ŋaŋgiitapandi puee ki dáaĺ ki nēetì ní ki dūu sāā ki cóoǹ ubɔti pool pu.

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: U nìn làá nyēe ní ki dáaĺ kudii kun tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee punyɔmmu ki pīiǹ ki kpàl̄ ubɔti pu ní ki dī boon pú ki nyáń.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Eewuudi nìn nín nyēē ubɔti tɔntɔnliibi dāa dɔ́mińee ní ki ká yii kudii kun tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee punyɔmmu pīī ki kpàl̄. Niinee ní bi lī yii: «An yaa yíì u máaǹ ki kɔ́ ataa pu u-diiku kun sɔ̀m̀ee poon ní.»

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Bi nìn cíitì ki tin gīī, waa bíi pìitī kudii kun tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee punyɔmmu. Bi dāa yōoǹ saafii ki cúú kudii ki pīitì ki kpēēyee, bi-kpiliu di dɔ̄ kitiŋ ki kpíìyee.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: U nìn bí-bi yii: «Páaḿmaan m-boon, kun puee ti-Dindaan dū ni-nannanliibi Moowaab yab ki ŋá ni-ŋaan!» Bi nìn lafun páaǹ u-boon ki sīntì ki cūtìi gāā ki kíntì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu laakin ní binib còom̄ ki dùtī Moowaab tiŋki jaaŋŋu púee, kaa nìn yāntì báà uniseen dūtì.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbanti ní Isirayeel yab nyīī Moowaab yab ki gùl̄ bi-taapu, ní Isirayeel tiŋki sɔ̄ŋkì ki tin sāā abin imuŋku inaa. Samgaar

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Eewuudi boonee, Anaati jipɔɔn Samgaar di nìn páaǹ. U nìn dū ndɔ ŋun nyɔkɔpu cáá mpiin bi cáa sàatī inaa kiŋkinti i tūǹ atuunee ki kūū Fiiliistii yab binib alaataa aluu ní. Min ní Samgaar nìn ŋá ki fīī Isirayeel yabee dee.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Eewuudi kúm boonee Isirayeel yab nìn fātìi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań min kaa kítì ti-Dindaan ceeyee.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn dū-bi ki ŋá ukaanaambɔti Jabiini un nìn kāl̀ Asɔɔr tiŋkin ki jíń dibeelee ŋaan. U-janjakitil kpiliu di nìn sá Siiseela, ama Siiseela úǹ nìn kóòń Arooseeti-Gooyiim tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Ní Siiseela gíti bí-u yii: «Á nīn yú tanti punyɔkɔpu, ubɔ yaa dɔ́miń ki bālifì-si yii: <Unil ubɔ bí doooo?> á kíí yii: <Aayee!>»

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: An yuntiŋuee, Lapiidɔti nimpuu Deeboora un nìn sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee di nìn sá Isirayeel bɔsoonliu.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: U nìn kóò Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu ní, Raama nì Beeteel timmu kansikin, laakin bi yíì yii Deeboora Babu taapuee, ní binib nìn cá u-cee u ŋáŋkí bi-bɔti.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: U nìn tú bi yíiń Abinoowaam jipɔɔn Baraaki, Keedeesi tiŋki kin bí Neefitalii tinjandinee. U bāańee ní Deeboora bí-u yii: «Kpèè, ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu u-ba di tīī-si mara nee yii: <Yīkì kí cùú lēē bijanjaliibi kii binib kutukub saalaa Neefitalii nì Sabulɔn naakɔti poon ní cùú kpāfì Tabɔɔr jool pu.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: M làá dáaĺ ubɔti Jabiini janjakpiliu Siiseela kí cáań a-cee Kiisɔn buŋŋu caŋin, kí dū-u kí ŋá a-ŋaan, u nì u-janjatɔrɔkub nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ.>»

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Ní Deeboora bí-u yii: «An yaa sée m làá céeǹ-si tí cù. Ama á nīn nyí yii kujaau kun a cá kí já nee nyooti kaa làá tin nín̄ sá a-yati. Di sá yii unimpu ŋaan ní ti-Dindaan làá tin dū Siiseela kí ŋá.» Niinee ní Deeboora yíkì ki céeǹ Baraaki ní bi búntì Keedeesi tiŋkin.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Eebeer un nìn sá Keeni maaliŋunee nìn dáaĺ u-ba ki nyántì Keeni yab, Mooyiisi coo Oobaab naantiibi kansikin. U nìn cūtìi cóoǹ u-tantiu seeni subu bun bí Sanayiim tiŋki ki pìlīǹ Keedeesi tiŋkee taapu.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Bi nìn cūtìi tùkū Siiseela yii Abinoowaam jipɔɔn Baraaki nín jɔ́ḿ Tabɔɔr jool pu.

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Ní Deeboora bí Baraaki yii: «Yīkì kí nīn cá, di sá yii díǹ wiiŋŋu ní ti-Dindaan dū Siiseela ki ŋá a-ŋaan. Ti-Dindaan u-ba di līī a-nyɔkɔpu.» Ní bijanjaliibi kutukub saalaayee páaǹ Baraaki boon bi nín sìntī Tabɔɔr jool taapu.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì fìkil fikil kɔ́ Siiseela nì u-janjatɔrɔkub nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ Baraaki nimbiin, ní bi dū ntàataajimu ki kūū-bi. Ní Siiseela nyáń u-janjatɔrɔkuun ki sáǹ ataa pu ki kátì.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Baraaki nì u-naacimbi nìn kùl̄ ki páaǹ janjatɔrɔkub nì bijanjaliibi boon, ki jìn̄-bi ki tin bàn̄ Arooseeti-Gooyiim tiŋkin. Bi nìn dū ntàataajimu ki kūū Siseela janjaliibi kɔkɔ múb, báà uniseen kaa kíǹ.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Nì mimmee Siiseela úǹ nìn bíi sáń ataa pu ki cá Eebeer un sá Keeni maaliŋunee nimpuu Jaayeel tantiu watil pú, di sá yii Asɔɔr bɔtiu Jabiini nì Keeni naantiiu Eebeer dicaŋku kansikin nìn mɔ̄.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Jaayeel nín wál̀ Siiseela páaǹnée, ní u nyáń ki túŋkì-u nsanni ki bí-u yii: «Dāá kɔ́ doo nee, m-dindaan, dāan̄ kí kɔ́ m-dumpu. Taa fàŋkì báà tiba!» Ní Siiseela nín kóò Jaayeel dumpu. U nìn kɔ́ ki bál̀ Jaayeel tantiun ní úǹ dū satakpaan ki bīiǹ u-pu.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Ní Siiseela bí-u yii: «Pɔ̄-mi nnyim ḿ nyɔ̀, nnyinnyoo cáá-mi.» Ní Jaayeel cúú kuloou kun poon u ŋáań nnaabiimee ki pīitì, ki bātì nnaabiim ki tīī Siiseela nyùn̄ ní u gíiǹ satakpaanee ki bīiǹ u-pu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee Baraaki mun nìn bíi yìiǹ ki nyàab̀ Siiseela dee! Ní Jaayeel nyáń ki túŋkì-u nsanni ní ki bí-u yii: «Dāan̄ ḿ dàkà-si unil un a nyàab̀ee.» Ní Baraaki nóó-u ki kɔ́ u-dumpu ki kpēēyee, Siiseela di dɔ̄ ki kpíìyee, dikpakpaal sāā ki bá u-taŋkpanjil.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, Unimbɔti nìn nyīī Kanaan bɔtiu Jabiini ki gùl̄ Isirayeel yab taapu.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel yab mɔ̄tìi múkú Kanaan bɔtiu Jabiini tiŋan pu, ní ki dāa ŋúń ki kūū-u.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, Deeboora nì Abinoowaam jipɔɔn Baraaki nìn gāā nlan nee yii:

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: «Isirayeel tiŋkinee, bijanjaliibi nín bɔ́ntì ki cūtì kujaau puee, samaa nín lēē nì dipɔbil diba ki cūtì kujaau puee, Jāam̀maan ti-Dindaan!

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi, pīlifìmaan! Biyidambi, kpòom̄maan ni-tafaliŋ! Man làá gāā ilan kí pàkà ti-Dindaan, m làá nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: Ajoon nìn wūtì sii Siinaayi jool Dindaaŋwu nimbiin, ŋi nìn wūtì sii ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nimbiin.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Anaati jipɔɔn Samgaar nì Jaayeel yuntiŋuee, binib kaa nìn gíti kàal̀ igutaamu ki còom̄ isanjaa pu, bisaŋkinliibi nìn kíǹ ki pāantí ipampa ní ki jītí.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn lēē inimbɔtipɔɔn ki jáaḿ, an di yì-tì ní kujaau bāań ki gūū bi-timmu punyɔmmu. Ama an nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ á ká digbampɔɔl àá kikpaŋ kí tīī binib kutukub imuŋku inaa Isirayeel tiŋkin.

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: M-pɔbil bí Isirayeel kpilib cee, bin dū bi-ba ki sú samaa kansikinee. Jāam̀maan ti-Dindaan!

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kàal̀ mmansapimu puee, nimbi bin kàal̀ tisatakampati puee, nimbi bin còom̄ adan puee, dàkafìmaan.

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Laakin bi cáǹ tiwaŋkuti ki nyùntī-tèe, biwaŋkpaaliibi bíi máafí ti-Dindaan deedee tuuŋŋi bɔti, deedee tuuŋŋi ŋin ní u ŋáaǹ Isirayeel tiŋkinee. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan nibul nyáń ki cūtìi kpáfì kitiŋ punyɔkɔpui.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: Deeboora, fìntim̄eeee, fìntīmaan! Fìntī malaa kí tóoń njanjalan. Baraaki, yīkìm̄! Kpáaǹ bin a cúú kuyuŋuee, Abinoowaam jipɔɔn.

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee kpáfì ki kpákatì abɔtibil cee. Ti-Dindaan nibul kpáfì nì bibaatandambi ki kpákatìń m-cee.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim naakookun yab kansikin ní bin jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Amaleeki yabee nyánní. Beenjameen naakookun yab páaǹ bi-boon ki kpákatì nì bi-janjaliibi. Makiir yab kansikin ní bi lēē bijanjakpilib, ní ki lēē Sabulɔn naakookun yab kansikin bikpootiliibi.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Isakaar kpilib bí Deeboora cee. Isakaar naakookun yab bí Baraaki jandi, ki páaǹ u-boon ki cūtì ditantakalin. «Ama Rubeen naakookun yab nín pēē pēē mmaal puee bíǹ kā ki kpákà an kaa kúntí.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Ba ŋá ní sii gbíntì awaŋgul ali kansikin ki pílifí bi nín búǹ awul ki yíì tiwaŋkuti puee? Rubeen naakookun yab nín pēē pēē mmaal puee bíǹ lafun kā ki kpákà an kaa kúntí.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Galaadi tiŋki bí Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní. Ba di ŋá ní Daani naakookun yab kóò meelabin ní? Aseer naakookun yab kāl̀ tiŋku caŋin, ki kóò ki pìlīǹ laakin meelab yūlifée.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Sabulɔn naakookun yab nì Neefitalii naakookun yab di sá binib bin kaa fāŋkì ŋkúm, ki jɔ́m̀ dikɔmbool pu ki jáń kujaauee.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi dɔ́miń ki jáń kujaau, Kanaan bɔtiibi jáń kujaau Taanaki tiŋkin, Meegiidoo nyiŋfii caŋin. Ama baa ká animbil kúti ki yōoǹ.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Iŋmalbijaa kālìń yilpu ki jáń kujaau, i kālìń i-laŋki kutagbɔŋu pu ki jáń nì Siiseela.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kiisɔn buŋŋu yōoǹ bi-kɔkɔ ki cáa búntì, cannaaku buŋŋu, Kiisɔn buŋŋu dee! M-naŋki, còom̀ nì tininjati!

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Niinee ní itaamu kíĺ ditaatandi i-taaŋi gbáà kitiŋ. i tòó ki tòó kii kpaŋkpakantiku taamuuyee.»

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu bí yii: «Ní tɔ̄ Meeroosi tiŋki mbusu, ní tɔ̄ kitiŋ gbanti nib mbusu ŋkpitim pu, kun puee baa nyáń ki tútúǹ ti-Dindaan, baa tútúǹ ti-Dindaan nì bibaatandambi.

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Binimpoobi kansikinee, bí nyɔ̄ŋkì Jaayeel, Eebeer un sá Keeni maaliŋunee nimpuu! Bí nyɔ̄ŋkì-u binimpoobi bin pée kóò tantibinee kɔkɔwoooo kansikin!

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Siiseela mēē-u nnyim, ama ní úǹ tīī-u nnaabiim. U bātì nnaabiim min kìl̄ee ki sītì-u bibɔtiibi sambinyɔkaakin.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Jaayeel tāntì u-ŋal ki cúú dikpakpaal, ki tāntì u-ŋaŋgiil ki dúkutì bitɔntɔnliibi kújal. U gbáń ki mátì Siiseela yil, u sāā u-taŋkpanjil ki cíl̀.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: «Siiseela na gbóoń tɔkɔla ki kpēē, tɔkɔla boon ní u bí yii: <Ba pu ní u-janjatɔrɔkuu kaa bíi bàń malaa ní? Ba pu ní u-janjatɔrɔkub còomìń soooo míǹ?>

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Binimpoobi bin bí u-ceeyee kansikin un cáá iciinee kíí-u, ní úǹ u-ba bí ki lì ki kùbitī yii:

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: <An yaa yíì bi tin jáń ki ká tiwan ki bíi yàkatī: ujanjal kamaa tin ká usapɔɔn ubɔ kii bili, Siiseela tin ká satab bin nyim bí miba mibee, ujajil tin ká ŋŋaabu ŋun bi gbáń mili puee kí dūú fìn̄ u-sil.>

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, yàntī a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ń kpú míǹ mbaantiim, ama bin sá a-bɔɔbee ń nīn bí kii ŋwìiń nín nyēeń nì ŋu-pɔŋŋu puee!» Ní Isirayeel tiŋki ká ŋgbansɔŋfi ki tin sāā abin imuŋku ili.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab tí ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan ceeyee. An pu ní ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki ŋá Madiyan yab ŋaan abin aluli.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: Madiyan yab nìn wɔ́b́ Isirayeel yab tikpil. Madiyan yab puee, Isirayeel yab nìn bɔ́ntì itaŋkpalɔkɔ nì titaŋkpanaakɔti nì ipaan in an pɔ̄ɔ̄ unil ń còom̀ kí bà sɔkɔmiiyee ajoon pu.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab yaa nìn búĺ bi-kpaajintee, Madiyan yab nì Amaleeki yab nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú timmu yab nìn jɔ́ḿ ki jáà nì bi.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Di sá yii binibee nìn yíkiń ní kí kpáaǹní bi-waŋkuti nì bi-tantib ní kí dāá bìin̄ Isirayeel yab tiŋki pu bɔ̀mmm kii inaakitoonee, kí bīil̀ tin bí kitiŋee puee kɔkɔ. Bi nì bi-gutaamui nìn wīikí an kaa cáá ŋkaan.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab nìn kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ú fīī-bi Madiyan yab ŋaanee,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: M nìn tùkū-ni yii man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. Ní taa jāam̀ Amɔɔr yab bin tiŋkin ni kóòyee nimbɔtii!> Ama ní naa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ!» Unimbɔti lēē Geedeeyɔn ú fīī Isirayeel yab

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nìn dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ teereebinti subu bubɔ taapu, Oofiraa tiŋkin. Joowaasi un sá Abiyeeseer maaliŋunee di nìn yì busubu gbanti. U-jipɔɔn Geedeeyɔn nìn bí ki gbáà bilee dibɔbil din poon bi tà fiinyi biliŋ ki lèekī ndamamee, Madiyan yab ń taa ká-u.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nìn lēē ŋu-ba ki dàkā-u ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan bí a-cee, ubaatandaan!»

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn bí-u yii: «M gbāam̀-si, m-kpiliu. An yaa sá yii ti-Dindaan lafun bí ti-ceeyee, ba pu ní tin bí nee kɔkɔ bāań-ti? Atuŋkpaan ŋin ti-baabi nìn máafì-ti yii ti-Dindaan nìn ŋáaǹ ki tīī-bi u nín nìn nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee bí la sɔ̀? Too, kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Dindaan fātì u-boon ki tīī-ti, ní ki dū-ti ki ŋá Madiyan yab ŋaan.»

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan fātì u-watil pú ní ki bí-u yii: «Nì mpɔn ŋun a cáá nee, cùú já kí fīī Isirayeel yab Madiyan yab ŋaan! Man di kaa tú-saaa?»

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn bí-u yii: «M gbāam̀-si, m-kpiliu, mana ní m làá ŋmā kí fīī Isirayeel yab? Manasee naakookun ti nín pēē pēē mmaal puee, man maaliŋun yab di pátì. Kí kūtèe, man di pée sá kiwaŋwaai m-baa dicaŋkun.»

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «M làá nīn bí a-cee ní á já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Madiyan yab kɔkɔ dicilpu kii bi sá unibambaantee.»

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn bí-u yii: «M yaa lafun ká diyimɔɔl a-ceeyee, á dàkà-mi kudaaŋŋu kubɔ ḿ béé yii tilafuŋman sii di bíi sòoǹ nì mi.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: M gbāam̀-si, taa búntí. Á cīití-mi doo ḿ cù kí bɔ́ntiń m-saraau kí cáań kí yóoń a-nimbiin.» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «M làá cīití-si á cùú gítiń.»

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn nín kóò u-dumpu ki cūtìi cúú diŋɔbil ki kūū ki tɔ́kɔǹ, ki lēē ŋyim kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa ki púĺ kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. U nìn bāaǹ tinan ki tākaǹ kukabikun, ki kpáatì tikun ki sītì dikumboolin ní ki yōoǹ kɔkɔ ki cáa nyántì teereebinti subu taapu ki yóoǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu bí Geedeeyɔn yii: «Dū tinan nì kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee kí páań ditaŋkpal nee pu, kí kpáatí tikun kí pɔ̀l̄ an pu.» Ní Geedeeyɔn ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee tāntì ŋkpandɔ ŋun ŋu ŋúb́ee nyɔkɔpu ki gbēē tinan nì kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee, ní ŋŋmi nyáń ditaŋkpal din pu an pée ki wùn̄ tinan nì kpɔnɔbee kɔkɔ múb. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee wáŋkì Geedeeyɔn nimbiin.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Niin ní Geedeeyɔn béè yii an sá ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu, ní u téeń yii: «Óo, m-bɔlii na, m-Dindaan Unimbɔti. Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu ní m lafun wál̀ nì m-nimbiliŋ kpìrrr naa!»

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí a-cee! Taa fàŋkì báà tiba, aa làá kpú.»

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn máń nsaraafan ŋubɔ mpaan gbanti pu ki tīī ti-Dindaan ní ki pú-ŋu diyindi yii <Ti-Dindaan sá ŋgbansɔŋfi>. Nì díǹ pu nee, nsaraafan gbanti dáá gbíntìi yú Oofiraa, Abiyeeseer tiŋki kiba poon. Geedeeyɔn wīī diwaal Baal saraafaŋŋu

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbanti ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Geedeeyɔn yii: «Cúú a-baa najau dimaaliliitiil yau un cáá abin alulee. Míǹ boonee, á cùú gbá kí wīī a-baa waal Baal saraafaŋŋu, kí gāā ŋwindɔ ŋun bi cóoǹ nsaraafanee caŋinee.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Boonee á mā man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nsaraafan ŋun sá mmɔntee kigbantaŋ nee pu. Á látí ŋwindɔ ŋun a gāāyee kí dūú kpāā ŋŋmi nsaraafan ŋun a máń-mi mpɔminee pu, ní kí dū dimaaliliitiil najauee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī-mi.»

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Geedeeyɔn nìn lēē u-tɔntɔnliibi kansikin binib saalaa ní bi cūtìi ŋá ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū-u yii ú ŋá puee. Ama u nín nìn fàŋkí u-baa dicaŋkun yab nì binib bin kíǹ kitiŋinee puee, waa nìn ŋá min ní ti-Dindaan bí yii ú ŋée ŋwiimpu, kunyeeu ní u ŋá.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl kitiŋin nib yíkèe ní ki dáań ki ká yii bi gbáń ki wīī diwaal Baal saraafaŋŋu, ki gāā ŋwindɔ ŋun nìn cɔ́ ŋu-caŋinee ní ki dū dimaaliliitiil najauee ki ŋá saraawɔkaa nsaraafan ŋun bi máń mpɔminee pu.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíǹ ki bí ki bàlifī tɔb yii: «Ŋma di kalin nín ŋá mimmee?» Bi bālifì bālifì, ki nyàab̄ nyàab̄ee ní an dāa nyáń yii Joowaasi jipɔɔn Geedeeyɔn di ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Ní kitiŋin nib bí Joowaasi yii: «Nyāntiń a-jipɔɔn doo tí kpɔ̀-u, kun puee u gbáń ki wīī diwaal Baal saraafaŋŋu ní ki gāā ŋwindɔ ŋun bi cóoǹ ŋu-caŋinee.»

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Ní Joowaasi kíí bin nìn yú u-cee niinee kɔkɔ yii: «Nimbi di làá sòoǹ diwaal Baal bɔti kí tīī-daaa? Nimbi di máaǹ kí jòoń-dàaa? Un kamaa di yaa mɔ́tì diwaal Baal puee máaǹ bí kpɔ̀-u ní kutaa ń nín wúntí. Diwaal Baal yaa lafun nyí yii di sá unimbɔtee, bi nín gbáń ki wīī di-saraafaŋŋuee, dí mɔ̄tì di-ba pu.»

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti ní bi nìn páaǹ Geedeeyɔn diyimpaaŋkaal yii <Yeerubaal> ki lī yii: «Diwaal Baal ń mɔ̄tì di-ba pu», kun puee u gbáń ki wīī di-saraafaŋŋu. Isirayeel yab bíi bɔ́ntí kí jáǹ Madiyan yab

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Madiyan yab nì Amaleeki yab nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú timmu yab sòon̄ ki ŋá kinyɔɔbaantii, ki kóoǹní ki kpáfì, ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ní ki dɔ́miń ki ŋātì dijanjanaapaal Jisirayeel tantakalin ki kāl̀.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Fam nìn gbí Geedeeyɔn ní u búń ŋyin ki yíiń Abiyeeseer maaliŋun yab ní bi-kɔkɔ yíkì ki páaǹ u-boon.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: U nìn lēē binib ki tú bi yíiń Manasee naakookun yab kɔkɔ ní bi mun yíkìń ki páaǹ u-boon. Boonee ní u tú ituun Aseer nì Sabulɔn nì Neefitalii naakɔtin yab cee ní bi mun jɔ́m̀ ki túŋkì-bi nsanni.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: m làá kpátí ipii kuti ŋaabuŋu ki bíĺ mmɔŋki dijanjanaapaal pu. Kutaa yaa wúntì ní dimalindi yaa sɔ̄ŋkì ipii kuti ŋaabuŋu ama ní kaa sɔ̄ŋkì dijanjanaapaal laakin kíǹeeyee, mimmee m béè yii a lafun là kí dī man pu kí fīī Isirayeel yab, kii a nín lī puee dee.»

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Ní an ŋá min Geedeeyɔn lēe. Di sá kutaa wúntì u fīntì kutaafaau ki yōoǹ ipii kuti ŋaabuŋuee ki ŋmáaḿee ní nnyim nyáń ki gbí kisambinyɔkaai kimɔŋ.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn bí Unimbɔti yii: «Á taa fōō m-pu diŋuul, m láa gíti sòoǹ nì si diba. Pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ gíti màkan̄ ipii kuti ŋaabuŋu makandee kí kpèè. Yàntī ipii kuti ŋaabuŋu ń nīn kūń ama ní dimalindi ń tɔ̄ kí sɔ̀ŋkì kitiŋ kɔkɔ dijanjanaapaal pu.»

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbantee Unimbɔti tí ŋá Geedeeyɔn nín lī puee. U nìn yāntì ipii kuti ŋaabuŋuee kūń ama ní dimalindi tɔ́ ki sɔ̄ŋkì kitiŋ kɔkɔ dijanjanaapaal pu.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní Geedeeyɔn un bi páaǹ diyindi yii Yeerubaalee yíkì u nì samaa kɔkɔ ki cūtìi ŋātì dijanjanaapaal Eeni Aroodi buŋŋu caŋin. Madiyan yab bíǹ naapaal nìn bínní ŋgan pú, Mooree gbantaŋki taapu, ditantakalin.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Geedeeyɔn yii: «Binib bin bí a-ceeyee wīikí tikpil ḿ dū Madiyan yab kí ŋá bi-ŋaan, kun puee Isirayeel yab dāa ŋūǹ kí gāā bi-bindi m-nimbiin kí lì yii: <Ti nì ti-pɔŋŋu ní ti jáń ki fīī ti-ba!>

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: An puee á bāakì kí tùkù diniwul kɔkɔ yii: <Ni-kansikin un di yaa fàŋkí u-wunti gbáàyee, udaan ń gbèen̄ Galaadi jool pu doo kí fàtīí nīn gítí!>» Ní binib kutukub mmuŋku nì bili bātì samaa poon ki fātìi nín gítí ní an kíǹ binib kutukub saalaa.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Ama a yaa fàŋkéee, sii nì a-tɔntɔnliu Puura ń dá láá nóó kí sìntī dijanjanaapaal watil pú dibalin.

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Geedeeyɔn yii: «Binib nee dáá gbíntìi wīikí tikpil! Yàntī bí sìntī mbunni ḿ lútí bin làá nóó-see kí tīī-si. Un kamaa ní m yaa bí yii ú nóó-si kí cùee, udaan ń nóó-si. Un ní m yaa tí bí yii ú taa nóó-si kí cùee, udaan ń taa nóó-si.»

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn yāntì binib nín sìntī mbunni ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Un kamaa làá dū u-limbil kí nyɔ̀ nnyim kii kibɔkɔ nín nyù puee, á gàntī udaan kí yóoń dijandi diba, ní kí gàntī un kamaa yaa gbāaǹ u-tabiŋyiliŋ pu ki nyùn̄ nnyimee kí yóoń dijandi diba mun.»

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Binib bin nìn dū bi-limbiliŋ ki nyùn̄ nnyim kii iboo nín nyù puee nìn kpáfì binib alaataa ata, ama binib bin nìn kíǹee kɔkɔ nìn gbāaǹ bi-tabiŋyiliŋ pu ní ki nyùn̄ nnyim.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Geedeeyɔn yii: «Binib alaataa ata bin dū bi-limbiliŋ ki nyùn̄ nnyim nee pu ní m làá dī kí fīī-ni ní kí dū Madiyan yab kí ŋá a-ŋaan. Binib bin kíǹee bimbee, báà ŋma ń nīn kùǹ u-dumpu.»

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbanti ní ti-Dindaan bí Geedeeyɔn yii: «Yīkì kí sìntī Madiyan yab naapaal pu kí jáǹ-bi, di sá yii m dū-bi ki ŋá a-ŋaan.

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: A yaa bàn̄ niinee, a làá gbìl̄ tin binib bí ki sòoǹee. Án làá tīī-si kunyannyaau ní á ŋmā kí sìntī Madiyan yab naapaal pu kí cùú jáǹ-bi.» Niinee Geedeeyɔn nì u-tɔntɔnliu cōom̀ ki tin gūū Madiyan yab naapaal.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Madiyan yab nì Amaleeki yab nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú timmu yab kɔkɔ nìn kpátìi gbí ditantakalin ní bɔ̀mmm, ki wīikí kii inaakitoonee. Baa nìn ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ bi-gutaamui gba, kun puee i nìn wīikí ní tikpil tikpil, kii tiŋku gbandi bul nín wīikí puee.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Geedeeyɔn bàn̄ee, uninja ubɔ nìn bí ki máafí u-bɔɔ kudamintiiu kun u dámintèe. U nìn bíi lì yii: «Kpèè, m dáá pée dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ dee. Kudamintiiu gbanti poonee, m ká ɔɔji kpɔnɔu ubɔ bí ki ŋàaǹ ki màntī Madiyan yab naapaal yilpu. Kpɔnɔee ŋàan̄ ki bàn̄ tanti ubɔ ní ki yá-u ki lúkú ní u lábitì ki cìb̄ kitiŋ.»

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Ní u-bɔɔ kíí-u yii: «Án sɔ̄ kí lā, an máaǹ ki pée sá uisirayeelja Joowaasi jipɔɔn Geedeeyɔn tàataajiki ní a dámintì. Unimbɔti dū Madiyan yab nì bi-janjanaapaal kɔkɔ ki ŋá u-ŋaan dee.»

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Geedeeyɔn nín gbìl̄ bi máafì kudamintiiuee pu nì bi nín lēē ku-taapu mun puee, ní u gbāaǹ u-tabiŋyiliŋ pu ki jáam̀ Unimbɔti. Boonee ní u yíkì ki nín gítí Isirayeel yab naapaal pu ki bàn̄ee ki bí-bi yii: «Ní yīkìmaan, kun puee ti-Dindaan dū Madiyan yab nì bi-naapaal ki ŋá ni-ŋaan!» Geedeeyɔn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Madiyan yab

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: M làá búń ŋyin, man nì bin làá nīn bí m-ceeyee kɔkɔ. Ni mun ń búń iyin míǹ mbaantiim, kí nīn còom̄ ki màntīi gɔ́ǹ dijanjanaapaal ki tátí ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan yindi pu nì Geedeeyɔn yindi pu!>»

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Geedeeyɔn nì u-yab binib dilaataal bin nìn nóó-uee nìn bàn̄ Madiyan yab naapaal caŋin kunyataasiiu búmbum ní. Ŋyunti gbantee bi nìn kpántì bijanjaliibi bin fōō bikpikib bin nìn dáá kpákatì sintil pu kpalaayee dee. Di sá ní Geedeeyɔn nì u-yab nìn kíĺ ki bíi búǹ iyin, ki fátí ki wìil̄ mbamu mun bi nìn ŋúb́ee.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Niinee ní akiti atee kíĺ ki bíi búǹ iyin ki fátí ki wìil̄ mbamu. Bi nìn ŋúb́ iŋminaapool ŋŋaŋgan ní ki ŋúb́ iyin ŋŋaŋgiil ki búǹ, ní ki nìn tátí mpɔn ki lì yii: «Tí jámaan ti-Dindaan yindi pu nì Geedeeyɔn yindi pu!»

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab māntìi gɔ́ń Madiyan yab naapaal míǹ, báà ŋma gbíntìi yú u-paaŋŋu. Dijanjanaapaal puee, báà ŋma nìn kíĺ ki bíi sáń ki tátí an kɔkɔ pu ki nyàab̀ kí ŋmátí.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab binib alaataa atee bí ki búǹ iyinee, ní ti-Dindaan yāntì dijanjanaapaal kɔkɔ puee báà ŋma kíǹ ki fàtī u-tàataajiki ki sàatī u-juti. Ní binib kɔkɔ sáǹ ki kátì ki tin bàn̄ Beeti-Siita tiŋki, ki gítí Seereera tiŋki watil pú, ní ki yōoǹ ki tin cáa gūū Abeel-Meewoola tiŋki, Tabaati tiŋki caŋin.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi yíiń Isirayeel yab bininjab bin sá Neefitalii nì Aseer nì Manasee naakɔtinee, ní bi kùl̄ ki páaǹ Madiyan yab boon.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Geedeeyɔn nìn lēē binib ki tú Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu bí cùú bāakì kí tùkù bin kóò niinee yii: «Ní sìntīmaan kí tūŋkì Madiyan yab, kí péeǹ-bi kí jī mpaan anyimbɔbil nì inyimbul kɔkɔn, kí yòon̄ kí tin cáá sāā Beeti-Baara tiŋki nì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu.» Míǹ ní bi yíiń Eefiraayiim yab bininjab kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní bi cūtìi jíń mpaan anyimbɔbil nì inyimbul kɔkɔn, ki yōoǹ ki tin cáa sāā Beeti-Baara tiŋki nì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Bi nìn cúú Madiyan kpilib bili. Bi nìn yíì ubɔ Ooreeb ní ki yíì un kíǹee Seeyeeb. Bi nìn kūū Ooreeb laakin bi yíì yii Ooreeb Taŋkpalee ní ki kūū Seeyeeb laakin bi yíì yii Seeyeeb Bɔbil din poon bi tà fiinyi biliŋ ki lèekī ndamamee. Bi kūū bikpilib gbanti liitil míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki nìkī ki jìn̄ Madiyan yab ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. Bi nìn ŋúbiń Ooreeb nì Seeyeeb yiliŋ ki nyánní lapu pu buŋgbandi ki cáań ki tīī Geedeeyɔn.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Eefiraayiim yab bālifì Geedeeyɔn yii: «Ba bɔti ní a ŋá-ti mimmee? A nín cá kí jáǹ Madiyan yabee, ba ŋá ní aa yíiń-ti?» Bi nìn nyáń u-pu an kaa kítì.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn kíí-bi yii: «Tin man ŋée kɔkɔ téé tin nimbi ŋá neeee? Nimbi Eefiraayiim yab nín ŋá tin nee, báà an yaa kaa pée náaǹ gba, an kaa jítiǹ man nì m-nabiyaamu Abiyeeseer yab nín ŋá tin kɔkɔee kpataaa puɔɔɔ?

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Nimbi ŋaan ní Unimbɔti dū Madiyan yab kpilib Ooreeb nì Seeyeeb ki ŋá. Ba ní man ŋúń ki ŋá kí dūú ŋmàntīǹ tin nimbi ŋée?» Geedeeyɔn nín sòon̄ an nyɔɔbundee ní bi-ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkì u-pu. Geedeeyɔn bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Sukooti tiŋkinee ní Geedeeyɔn bí niin yab yii: «M gbāam̀-ni, ní tīīmaan binib bin nóó-mi nee tijin bí jī, kun puee bi gīī tikpil. M bíi jì Madiyan yab bɔtiibi Seeba nì Salmuuna boon ní.»

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Sukooti kpilib kíí-u yii: «Seeba nì Salmuuna gíti dáá kɔ́ a-ŋaan ní timbi ń tīī a-janjaliibi tijin bí jāaa?»

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn bí-bi yii: «Too, an ŋān̄. Ní nīn nyí yii ti-Dindaan yaa dū Seeba nì Salmuuna ki ŋá m-ŋaanee, m làá dāá gítiń kí dū ikuŋkuŋfi in nyēē kuteeunee nì abɔjanaakun kí gbá-ni.»

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: U yíkì ki nín jɔ́ḿ Peenuyeel tiŋkin ki bàn̄ ki sòon̄ niin yab tibɔbaantiilee ní Peenuyeel yab mun kíí-u kii Sukooti yab nín kíí-u puee.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Ní u bí Peenuyeel yab mun yii: «M yaa fātìi gítìń nì laafiya, m làá gbá kí wīī ni-difɔkɔku kun bí nee!»

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn nín cá Sukooti tiŋki yab cee ki bàn̄ ki bí-bi yii: «Ni téetí yii ni nìn sīī-mi ki lī yii: <Seeba nì Salmuuna gíti dáá kɔ́ a-ŋaan ní timbi ń tīī a-janjaliibi bin gīīyee tijin bí jāaa?> Too, Seeba nì Salmuuna gbanti sɔ̀!»

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Seeba nì Salmuuna nìn sáǹ ki kátì, ama ní Geedeeyɔn kùl̄ ki páaǹ Madiyan bɔtiibi bili gbanti boon áli ki tin cúú-bi. U nìn yāntì dinyoondi kɔ́ bi-janjakitil kɔkɔ.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Joowaasi jipɔɔn Geedeeyɔn nín nìn nyánní kujaau ki fàtīi gítińee, u nìn dūu dīń Eereesi gbantaŋki pú ní.

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: U bāań Sukooti tiŋkinee ní ki cúú niin naacimpɔmbiki kiba ki yóoǹ ní ki bālifì-kì Sukooti yab kpilib nì bi-tindaŋkpilib yiŋŋi ní kinaacimpɔmbikee dūu ŋmàn̄ ŋgban pu ki tīī-u. Bi nìn sá binib imuŋku ita nì saalaa ní.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Geedeeyɔn lī mimmee ní ki cúú Sukooti yab kpilib, ní ki yōoǹ ikuŋkuŋfi in nyēē kuteeunee nì abɔjanaakun ki dūu dáaĺ Sukooti yab tafal ní an bàn̄-bi tiŋan pu.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: U nìn gbáń ki wīī Peenuyeel tiŋki mun difɔkɔku, ní ki pɔ̄fì ki-nib.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u bālifì Seeba nì Salmuuna yii: «Binib bin ni nìn kūū Tabɔɔr jool puee nìn bí mana ní?» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Bi nìn bí kii sii mun nín pée bí pu nan ní. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn bí kii bɔtiijabee ní.»

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Ní u bí-bi yii: «M-nabiyaamu pēē na ní ni kūūyee! M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalinee yii ní yaa kaa bàà lēē bi-maŋfal, maa bàà làá kpɔ̀-ni!»

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Geedeeyɔn lī mimmee ní ki bí u-jipɔŋkpiliu Yeeteer yii: «Yīkì kí kpɔ̀-bi!» Ama ní u-jipɔɔn kaa nìn fúutì u-tàataajiki kujitooun, kun puee u nìn dáá sá kinaacimpɔmbiki ní ki nìn fàŋkí.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Niinee ní Seeba nì Salmuuna bí-u yii: «Sisi a-ba yīkì kí kpɔ̀-ti, kun puee uninja máaǹ kí dàkà tininjati ní!» Ní Geedeeyɔn yíkì ki kūū Seeba nì Salmuuna ní ki cúú tiléeŋkaal tin bi nìn léeǹ bi-gutaamuyee ki léetì i-neeŋyi. Geedeeyɔn maŋfal wiiŋyi nín kúntì puee

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Isirayeel yab tùkū Geedeeyɔn yii: «Nín̄ sá ti-kpootiliu, ní a-kpátam boonee a-jipɔɔn ń dāá fōō a-yil ní a-jipɔɔn jipɔɔn mun ń dāá fōō, kun puee a fīī-ti ki líì Madiyan yab ŋaan.»

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn kíí-bi yii: «Man m-ba kaa làá kpòotī-naaa, m-jipɔɔn mun kaa làá kpòotī-ni. Ti-Dindaan u-ba di làá nīn kpòotī-ni.»

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Ní Geedeeyɔn nìkī ki bí-bi yii: «Ama tiba ní m là kí mèè-ni. M bàà là yii ni-kansikin báà ŋma ń lēē tiwan tin ní u ká kujaaunee poon kibɔmbiki kiba kí tīī-mi.» Di sá yii bi-nannanliibi bin bi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee kɔkɔ nìn cáá sindaariya bɔmbiyaamu bi-wunti pu ní, kii Isimaayeel naakookun yab kɔkɔ nín pée cáá puee.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Geedeeyɔn lī mimmee ní bi bí-u yii: «Iiin, ti kíí ki làá tīī-si nì dipɔbil diba!» Niinee ní bi kpátì dibɔkutipaaŋkaal diba ki bíl̀ kitiŋ ní báà ŋma lēē tiwan tin u ká kujaaunee poon kibɔmbiki kiba kiba ki tɔ́-u dibɔkutilee pu.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: U nìn gíti cáá ubɔnti ubɔ Siikeem tiŋkin. Unimpuee mun nìn màl̄-u kibininjabiki ní u pú-kì diyindi yii Abimeeleeki.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Joowaasi jipɔɔn Geedeeyɔn nìn kpíì titikpitin nì dipɔɔsɔŋkilin. Bi nìn síb́-u u-baa Joowaasi kaakul poon, Oofiraa tiŋki kin nìn sá Abiyeeseer maaliŋun timmu kibee poon ní.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Ama Geedeeyɔn kúm boonee ní Isirayeel yab fātìi tí kíĺ ki bíi tòotī Baal. Bi nìn dū Baal-Beeriiti ki ŋá bi-nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kaa nìn gíti téetì ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu un nìn fīī-bi ki líì bi-nannanliibi bin nìn māntìi tú-bee ŋaanee pu.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Baa nìn ŋá Yeerubaal-Geedeeyɔn dicaŋkun yab mun tiŋan ki téeǹ tiŋan tin kɔkɔ u nìn ŋá ki tīī bíǹ Isirayeel yabee.

english_verse: and told them to say to the leaders of Shechem, “Do you think it would be good to have all
translation_verse: «Ní tùkùmaan Siikeem tindambi kɔkɔ yii: <Ni là Yeerubaal jipɔmbi binib imuŋku ita nì saalaayee ní ń nīn kpòotī-naaa, ni là unibaanti ní ń nīn kpòotī-ni? Ní téetímaan yii man nì ni sá fatikubaanti ní!>»

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki na niijab nìn dū tibɔtee ki lī Siikeem tindambi kɔkɔ cee, ní bíǹ páaǹ Abimeeleeki boon, di sá bi nìn lī yii: «Ti-nabiki dee.»

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki nìn cūtì u-baa dumpu, Oofiraa tiŋkin ki cúú u-nabiyaamu Yeerubaal jipɔmbi binib imuŋku ita nì saalaayee ki kūū ditaŋkpabaantiil pu. Asee Yeerubaal jipɔnjoolkaau Yootam di nìn kíǹ, kun puee úǹ nìn sáǹ ki bál̀.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Siikeem tindambi kɔkɔ nì Beeti-Miiloo yab kɔkɔ kpáfì ní ki cūtìi kāaǹ Abimeeleeki dibeel seeni subu bun nìn yú ditaŋkpal din bi nìn cóoǹ Siikeem tiŋkinee caŋin. Yootam gāā Siikeem yab dilaŋkpandi

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Yootam nín gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní u jɔ́m̀ ki tɔ́kɔǹ Geerisiim jool pu ki téeń mpɔn ki tùkū-bi yii: «Siikeem tindambi, ní pīlifìmaan-mi ní Unimbɔti ń pīlifì ni mun.

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: «Isufi di nìn yíkì yii i làá kàan̄ i-bɔtiu. I nìn bí ɔliifi subu yii: <Sii nín̄ sá ti-bɔtiu!>

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ní ɔliifi subu kíí isufi in kíǹee yii: <Mimmee m yàntī ŋkpam min awaa nì binib néeńee kí cùú jī dibeel isufi pu deeyaa!>

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ní isufi in kíǹee bí fiigi subu yii: <Sii dāan̄ kí nīn sá ti-bɔtiu!>

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ní fiigi subu kíí in kíǹee yii: <Mimmee m yàntī m-subiliŋ ŋin ŋān̄ ki mɔ̄ cɔ́ncɔŋ nee kí cùú jī dibeel isufi pu deeyaa!>

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ní isufi in kíǹee bí fiinyi subu yii: <Sii dāan̄ kí nīn sá ti-bɔtiu!>

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ní fiinyi subu kíí in kíǹee yii: <Mimmee m yàntī m-damam min awaa nì binib nyù an nyàatī-bee kí cùú jī dibeel isufi pu deeyaa!>

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Niin ní isufi kɔkɔ bí kikuŋkumbɔŋ yii: <Sii dāan̄ kí nīn sá ti-bɔtiu!>

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Ní kikuŋkumbɔŋ bí isufi yii: <Tiŋman ní ni yaa lafun là kí kàan̄-mi dibeel ḿ nīn sá ni-bɔtiuee, ní sāǹnímaan kí dāá báĺ m-booŋŋu taapu. Ama an yaa kaa sá míǹ, ŋŋmi làá nyā man kikuŋkumbɔŋ poon kí wà kí kpáaǹ Leebanɔn sufii in bi yíì yii seediree!>

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Ama díǹ nee, ni fātìi lábitì m-baa dicaŋku pu, ki cúú u-jipɔmbi binib imuŋku ita nì saalaayee ki kūū ditaŋkpabaantiil pu. Míǹ boonee ní ni dū dibeel ki tīī u-yumbunimpuu jipɔɔn Abimeeleeki ú nīn kíǹ ki sá Siikeem tiŋki nì ki-tindambi bɔtiu, yii u nín sá ni-nabikee pu.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: An puee ni yaa lafun nyí yii min ni ŋá Yeerubaal nì u-dicaŋkuee, an sá nì dipɔbil diba nì tibulcinee, ní nīn fàal̀maan Abimeeleeki pu ní u mun ń nīn fàal̀ nimbi pu!

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: An yaa kaa sá mimmee, ŋŋmi ń nyā Abimeeleeki cee kí wà Siikeem nì Beeti-Miiloo tindambi, ní ŋŋmi ń nyā Siikeem nì Beeti-Miiloo tindambi mun cee kí wà Abimeeleeki!»

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Yootam nìn sòon̄ míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ Beeyeer tiŋkin. U nìn gbíntì niin, kun puee u nìn fàŋkí u-maan Abimeeleeki. Siikeem yab bíi jáà nì Abimeeleeki

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki nìn jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu abin ata ní.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Siikeem tindambi nìn nyēē Abimeeleeki boon ní ki nìn lèekī binib bi cá ki nākantí ajoon yilpu ki cí. Unil un kamaa yaa nìn jītí bi-caŋin didandi puee, bi nìn gà kí kíntí udaan ní kí fūkul̀ udaan wanti kɔkɔ. Ní bi cáá an bɔtee ki tùkū Abimeeleeki.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋubɔee, Eebeedi jipɔɔn Gaal nìn dɔ́miń Siikeem tiŋkin, u nì u-nabiyaamu. Siikeem tindambi nìn dū bi-mákal ki ŋá Gaal pu.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Siikeem tindambi nìn nyáń ki cūtì tisatin ní ki kītì bi-fiinyi sufii biliŋ ki tāā ki lēē ndamam ní ki bɔ́ntì agbiil. Bi nìn kɔ́ bi-nimbɔtiu un bi jáaḿee diikun ní ki jíń ki nyùn̄ ní ki mēē mbusu ki tɔ́ Abimeeleeki pu.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Eebeedi jipɔɔn Gaal nìn bí ki lì yii: «Abimeeleeki di sá ŋma, ní timbi Siikeem yab ń nīn bí u-taapu ní? Úǹ di kaa sá Yeerubaal jipɔɔn ní Seebuul sá u-kàliŋkpiliuaaa? An puee nín̄ bímaan Siikeem baa Amɔɔr nib taapu. Ba pu ní tí nīn bí Abimeeleeki taapu?

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Ŋma bàà dù binib nee ki ŋúbiǹ-mi, m bàà làá jà Abimeeleeki ní!» Ní ki lī Abimeeleeki yii: «Nyàab̀ bijanjaliibi kí kūtì a-yab pu kí nyānní tí ká tɔb!»

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Seebuul un nìn sá Siikeem tiŋki gɔminauee nìn gbìl̄ tin Eebeedi jipɔɔn Gaal bí ki sòoǹee ní ki fōō mbum.

english_verse: And so he sent some messengers to Abimelech. But they had to pretend to be doing something else, or they would not have been allowed to leave Shechem. Zebul told the messengers to say: Gaal the son of Ebed has come to Shechem along with his brothers, and they have persuaded the people to let Gaal rule Shechem instead of you.
translation_verse: Ní u lēē binib ki tú dibalin Abimeeleeki cee bi cūtìi tùkū-u yii: «Kpèè, Eebeedi jipɔɔn Gaal dɔ́miń Siikeem tiŋkin, u nì u-nabiyaamu, ní bi bí ki sòoǹ nì Siikeem yab kí bīil̀ sii nì bi kansikin.

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: An puee á yīkì kunyeeu nee kí yòon̄ a-janjaliibi ní dāan̄ kí nákań tisatin.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Kutaa yaa fu wúntì ŋwìiń nyáatèe, á fu dāan̄ malaa kí jáǹ kitiŋee. Gaal nì binib bin nóó-uee yaa fu nyáń kí já nì see, á fu ŋá-bi min máaǹee.»

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki lafun yíkì kunyeeu gbanti, ki cúú u-janjaliibi ki yākatì akiti anaa pu ní bi cūtìi nákáǹ nákáǹ tisatin ki pìlīǹ Siikeem tiŋki.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki nín ká yii Eebeedi jipɔɔn Gaal nyánní ki yú kitiŋ punyɔkɔpuee, ní u nì u-yab nyīī ki yíkì laakin bi náká nákée.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Gaal nín ká dinikitil gbantee ní u bí Seebuul yii: «Kpèè, dinikitil diba di nyánní ajoon yilpu ki sìntīńee.» Ní Seebuul bí-u yii: «An sá ajoon jiliŋku ní a cáa yíì binib.»

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Ní Gaal fātìi gíti bí yii: «Kpèè, dinikitil diba di nyánní dijool din bí kitiŋ kansikin nì kansikin watil pú ki sìntīńee, diba mun di dī seeni subu bun sá Bibɔɔbi subuee saŋŋu ki dòońee.»

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Seebuul bí-u yii: «A-nyɔkɔ kin a bàà bí ki lúǹee bí la? Sii di kaa bíi lì yii: <Ŋma di sá Abimeeleeki ní timbi ń nīn bí u-taapueeee?> U-janjaliibi bin ní a bí ki ŋèeǹee deeyaa! Kɔŋkɔnnee nyā sii nì u ń jáa!»

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ní Gaal nyáń ki līntì Siikeem tindambi nyɔkɔpu ki bíi jáà nì Abimeeleeki.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Ama Abimeeleeki nìn jìn̄-u ní u sáǹ ki kátì. Binib tikpil nìn kpíì ki dɔ̄ dɔ̄ ki tin sāā kitiŋ punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Abimeeleeki cūtì ki kíǹ ki kóò Aruuma tiŋkin, ní Seebuul jìn̄ Gaal nì u-nabiyaamu bí taa ti kàl̄ Siikeem tiŋkin.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Abimeeleeki gbìl̄ yii Siikeem yab bíi bɔ́ntí kí nyā tisatin.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Ní u cúú u-janjaliibi ki yākatì akiti ata, ní bi cūtìi nákáǹ nákáǹ tisatin. Ŋyunti ŋun Abimeeleeki ká yii Siikeem yab nyánní kitiŋinee ní u nì u-yab yíkì ki dūu túuǹ-bi ní ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki nì u-yab bin nìn bí u-ceeyee nìn ŋá malaa ki cūtìi yúl̀ kitiŋ punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ki pīiǹ nsan. Ní u-yab akiti ali ŋin kíǹee yíkì ki páatìi jéetì Siikeem yab bin nìn pée bí tisatinee kɔkɔ pu ní ki pɔ̄fì-bi.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki nìn dū ŋwimmɔn ní ki jáń nì Siikeem tiŋki ní ki dāa nín fōō-kì. U nìn kūū ki céetì ki-nib kɔkɔ, ki nàn̄-kì dúsi dusi ní ki dū ŋyaam ki yāaǹ ki-pu.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Miigidaal-Siikeem tindambi nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní bi yíkì ki nín cá Eel-Beeriiti waadiiku taŋkpalɔkɔŋun.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Ní bi cūtìi tùkū Abimeeleeki yii Miigidaal-Siikeem tindambi kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì dicilpu ntaŋkpalɔkɔn.

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Abimeeleeki nín jɔ́ḿ Saalmɔn jool pu, ki kpáaǹ u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ. Abimeeleeki nìn yōoǹ kicɔkɔ ki gāā disupandi diba ki dūu būkuǹ, ní ki tùkū binib bin nóó-uee yii: «Min ní ni ká m ŋá nee, ni mun ŋámaan míǹ malaa!»
