english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Abimeeleeki dūu túĺ Teebeesi tiŋki watil pú, ki cūtìi jáń ki fōō kitiŋ gbanti.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ gbanti kansikinee, kudifɔkɔu kun bi nìn máń agun ki māntìi túee kubɔ nìn yú. Kudifɔkɔu gbanti poon ní kitiŋee nib bininjab nì binimpoobi nì bitindambi kɔkɔ nìn sáǹ ki kɔ́ ki bál̀. Bi nìn dū kipunyɔkɔ ki pīiǹ ki kpàl̄ bi-ba pu, ní ki nín jɔ́ḿ kudii yilpu laakin bi bɔ̀b̄ee.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki nìn bàn̄ kudifɔkɔuee cee kí jáǹ binib bin sáǹ ki bál̀ ku-poonee, ki sútì ki pìl̄ kudii punyɔkɔki kí bàà sēē-kì ŋŋmi.

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: Niinee ní unimpu ubɔ dū kunaau ki lúkuń ní an dɔ́miń ki tàb̄ ki wīī Abimeeleeki yil.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ní Abimeeleeki yíiń u-tɔntɔnliu unaacimpɔɔn un pá u-boon ki ŋúb́-u tijanjawanee malaa ní ki bí-u yii: «Fúutí a-tàataajiki kí sāā kí kpɔ̀-mi. Maa là bi dāa máafí m-bɔti yii: <Unimpu di nìn kūū-u!>» Niinee ní u-naacimpɔɔŋwuee dū kitàataajiki ki sāā-u ní u kpíì.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín ká yii Abimeeleeki kpíìyee ní báà ŋma fātìi nín kùǹ u-dumpu.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Unimbɔti nìn téeǹ Abimeeleeki ikpiti in u nìn ŋá u-baa, ki nìn kūū u-nabiyaamu binib imuŋku ita nì saalaayee.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn téeǹ Siikeem yab mun ikpiti in bi mun nìn ŋée, ki nìn yāntì mbusu un ní Yeerubaal jipɔɔn Yootam nìn sòon̄ ki tɔ́ Siikeem yab puee nìn lafun bāań-bi míǹ.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Abimeeleeki kúm boonee, Puuwa jipɔɔn Toola, Doodoo naantiiu un nìn sá Isakaar naakookunee di nìn līntì Isirayeel yab nyɔkɔpu ki nìn fīī-bi bi-nannanliibi ŋaan. U nìn kóò Samiir tiŋki kin bí Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee ní.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Toola kúm boonee, Yayiir un nìn sá Galaadi tiŋkinee di nìn fōō-u. U nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin mmuŋku nì ali ní.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Yayiir nìn kpíì ní bi síb́-u Kamɔn tiŋkin. Amɔn yab bíi jáà nì Isirayeel yab

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn gíí diŋuul Isirayeel yab pu ní ki nìn dū-bi ki ŋá Fiiliistii yab nì Amɔn yab ŋaan.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Niin ní Isirayeel yab nì Galaadi tindaŋkpilib nìn bíi bàlifī tɔb yii: «Ŋma di làá nín kíĺ kujaau nì Amɔn yab dee? Udaan di bàà làá kpántí Galaadi tiŋki nib kɔkɔ kpiliu!»

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nìn dūtìń Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Juuda naakookun yab nì Beenjameen naakookun yab nì Eefiraayiim naakookun yab. Isirayeel yab nimbaaku kun poon bi nìn kíǹ ki bée nìn gíti nyāŋkì tikpil.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel yab kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ki lī yii: «Tilafuŋman ní ti yīntiǹ-si, kun puee ti dū sii un sá ti-Nimbɔtiuee ki fá ní ki bí ki tòotī Baal.»

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Ní cùmaan kí nīn kūuntí ki yíì awaa ŋin ni lēē yii ni là kí nīn tòotēe, ŋí fīī-ni ni-nimbaakun!»

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab fātìi bí ti-Dindaan yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ti yīntì ní. Ŋá-ti min di yaa pée ŋān̄ a-ceeyee, ama ti gbàam̄-si ní, fīī-ti díǹ wiiŋŋu nee!»

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn lī mimmee ní ki dū awaa ŋin nìn bí bi-ceeyee ki fá ní ki fātìi bíi jáaḿ ti-Dindaan. Niinee falaau un bi nìn bí ki jīǹee nìn kɔ́ ti-Dindaan tikpil.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nìn yíiń tɔb ki kpáfì ní ki ŋātì bi-janjanaapaal Galaadi tiŋkin, ní Isirayeel yab kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki ŋātì bi-janjanaapaal Miisipa tiŋkin.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bàn̄ee ní ki bí Jeefita yii: «Dāan̄ kí nīn sá ti-janjakpiliu tí ŋmā kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Amɔn yab.»

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Ní Jeefita bí Galaadi tindaŋkpilib yii: «Kéè ni nìn ná-mi ní ki jìn̄-mi m-baa dicaŋkunaa! Ba gíti ŋá ní ni dòoń m-cee kɔŋkɔnnee, ŋyunti ŋun ní dinimbinaamandi bāań-nee?»

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Ní Galaadi tindaŋkpilib kíí Jeefita yii: «Too, kɔŋkɔnnee ti yaa dɔ́miń a-ceeyee, ti là yii á kíí kí nóó-ti kí cùú jáǹ Amɔn yab, kí nīn sá timbi Galaadi yab kɔkɔ kpiliu ní.»

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Ní Jeefita bí Galaadi tindaŋkpilib yii: «Ni lafun kíí tiŋman yii m yaa nóó-ni ki gítì ki cūtìi jáń nì Amɔn yab ní ti-Dindaan yaa dū-bi ki ŋá m-ŋaan, man di làá nīn sá ni-kɔkɔ kpiliuaaa?»

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Ní Galaadi tindaŋkpilib bí Jeefita yii: «Ti-Dindaan sá ti-seeradaaŋwu, ti làá ŋá a nín lī puee.»

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jeefita kíí ki páaǹ Galaadi tindaŋkpilib boon bi nín cá, ní samaa tin kāaǹ-u ú nīn sá bi-kpiliu nì bi-janjakpiliu. Ní Jeefita fātìi sòon̄ anyɔɔbun ŋin u nìn pée sòon̄ee kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nimbiin Miisipa tiŋkin. Jeefita tú ituun Amɔn yab cee

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: An ŋá mimmee ní Jeefita lēē binib ki tú Amɔn yab bɔtiu cee bi cūtìi bālifì-u dinyɔɔbundi u-yil pu yii: «Man nì si yii ba ní a dɔ́miń m-tiŋki pu ki bíi jáà nì man nì m-yab?»

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Ní Amɔn yab bɔtiu kíí Jeefita tuuŋyi yii: «Kun pu m ŋá mimmee di sá yii, ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki jɔ́mińee, bi nìn fōō m-tiŋki kí yòon̄ Arinɔn buŋŋu kí tin cáá sāā Yaabɔki buŋŋu nì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. An puee, kɔŋkɔnnee á gíiǹ m-tiŋki gbanti kí tīī-mi soooo.»

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Ní Jeefita fātìi lēē binib ki tú Amɔn yab bɔtiu cee

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: bí tùkù-u tin Jeefita sòon̄ee yii: «Isirayeel yab kaa fōō Moowaab yab tiŋkaaa, kaa tí fōō Amɔn yab mun tiŋki.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn kā niin ní ki lēē binib ki tú Eedoom yab bɔtiu cee ki lī yii: <Ti mèé-si á pɔ̄-ti nsan tí jītí a-tiŋki poon!> Ama ní Eedoom yab bɔtiu kaa nìn pílifiǹ-bi. Bi nìn tú Moowaab yab bɔtiu mun cee ní u mun kaa nìn kíí ki pú-bi nsan. Di sá ní Isirayeel yab nìn gbíntì Kadeesi tiŋkin.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Boonee, bi nìn cōom̀ kuteeun, ki gɔ́ntì Moowaab tiŋki ki fātìi nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní ki dāa dūu nyáń Moowaab tiŋki pu. Bi nìn kāl̀ Arinɔn buŋgbandi lapu pu yal ní, kaa nìn kɔ́ Moowaab yab tiŋkin, di sá yii Arinɔn buŋŋu di nìn sá Moowaab tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn lēē binib ki tú Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu, an dàkà yii Eesbɔn tiŋki bɔtiu Siiwɔn cee bi cūtìi tùkū-u yii: <Ti mèé-si yii á pɔ̄-ti nsan tí jītí a-tiŋki poon kí cù laakin ti cée!>

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Ama ubɔti Siiwɔn kaa nìn cáá Isirayeel yab pu dimákal, di sá ní waa nìn kíí bi jítì u-tiŋkin. U nìn kóoǹ u-janjaliibi ki kpáfì Yakaasi tiŋkin ki kíĺ kujaau nì Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dū ubɔti Siiwɔn nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ ki ŋá Isirayeel yab ŋaan ní bi ŋúń ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Isirayeel yab nìn fōō Amɔɔr yab tiŋki kin bi nìn kóòyee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: Bi nìn fōō Amɔɔr yab tiŋki kɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ Arinɔn buŋŋu kí cáá sāā Yaabɔki buŋŋu ní kí yòon̄ kuteeu kí cáá sāā Jɔɔdan buŋŋu.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: An puee ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu di nìn yāntì timbi u-nibul ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō Amɔɔr yab tiŋki bi-cee, ní sii là kí cúú kitiŋ gbanti kí fōō ti-ceeee?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Man nyí a ŋúb́ tin kɔkɔ ní a-waal Keemoosi tīī-see naa! Kin ba pu ní timbi ń taa nín̄ yì tin ní ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu dūu ŋá ti-ŋaanee?

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: A dàkafī yii a jítiǹ Moowaab bɔtiu Balaaki, Siipɔɔr jipɔɔn níii? A ká u táká Isirayeel yab ki dāa nín lì yii u làá já nì baaa?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Mbaamɔn pu, man kaa yīntiǹ-si tiba. Ama a nín bí ki jáà nì mi kujaau min nee, á nīn nyí yii sii di yīntiǹ-mi. Ti-Dindaan baba di sá Ubɔsoonli, úǹ di làá sòoǹ Isirayeel yab nì Amɔn yab bɔti díǹ nee.>»

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Ama Amɔn yab bɔtiu kaa nìn pílifì tibɔti tin Jeefita nìn yāntì bi cáań ki tùkū-uee. Jeefita pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ipoon

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Fam nìn gbí Jeefita. U nìn yíkì ki dī Galaadi nì Manasee timmu pú, ki pɔ́ĺ ki dī Miisipa, Galaadi timbiliiki pú, ní ki dī niin ki kɔ́ Amɔn yab tiŋkin.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Jeefita nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ti-Dindaan yii: «A yaa lafun dū Amɔn yab ki ŋá m-ŋaan ki yāntì m jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bee,

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Jeefita nìn lafun kɔ́ Amɔn yab tiŋki pu ki jáń nì bi ní ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki ŋá u-ŋaan.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jeefita nìn fātìi bàn̄ Miisipa tiŋkin ki làá kɔ́ u-cindinee, ní u-bisal nyánní ki ŋúb́ kigaŋgaŋ ki bɔ̀ɔ́ ki ŋōoń ki túŋkí-u nsanni. Jeefita bisal gbanti di nìn pée sá u-bibaabil. Waa nìn gíti màl̄ kibininjabikaaa, kaa nìn màl̄ kibinimpubiki ki kútì u-bisal gbanti pu.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Jeefita nín nìn pée wál̀ u-bisal túŋkiń-uee, ní u dáaĺ ki cátì u-wanti tin u nìn pēēyee ní ki bí yii: «Óò, m-bisal, a kɔ́ǹ-mi kunimbaaun. Sii di yì nnaabu ŋun dòoń-mi nee. Di sá yii m gíti dáá pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ipoon ní kaa ti ŋūǹ kí yíí yii maa làá ŋá tin ní m pōoǹ-uee.»

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Ama ní u-bisal kíí-u yii: «M-baa, a nín gíti dáá pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ipoonee, ŋá tin ní a pōoǹ-u yii a làá ŋée. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di yāntì a ŋúń ki tɔ̀n̄ a-nannanliibi Amɔn yab ipɔntoon.»

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Ní u nìkī ki lī u-baa yii: «Ama kuwambaantiiu kun m làá mèè-see di sá yii, á pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ nīn bí dimaŋfalin kí gíti bà iŋmal ili man nì m-bɔɔbi ń nóó kí cù ajoonni kí sɔ̄ m nín làá kpú m-sapɔnti poon kaa béè uninjee pu.»

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Ní Jeefita pú u-bisal nsan ki yāntì u búntì ki cūtìi ŋá iŋmal ili ajoonni u nì u-bɔɔbi, ki súń u nín làá kpú u-sapɔnti poon kaa béè uninjee pu.

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: Dikoobil gbanti di sá yii dibindi kamaayee, Isirayeel sapɔmbi kɔkɔ ń cù kí kpāfì kí sɔ̄ ugalaadija Jeefita bisal pu iwiin inaa dibindi poon.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim yab kóoǹ ki kpáfì ní ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki cūtì Saafɔn tiŋkin ki bālifì Jeefita yii: «Ba pu ní a kɔ́ Amɔn yab tiŋkin a-baba ki cūtìi jáń nì bi kaa yíiń-ti ti nì si ń nóó kí cù? Ti làá wà a-dicaŋku ŋŋmi kí kpáaǹ sisi a-ba!»

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Ní Jeefita kíí-bi yii: «Man nì m-nib nìn bí kujaau pu an pɔ̄ɔ̄, ti nì Amɔn yab. M nín nìn yíiń-nee, naa nìn dɔ́miń ki fīī-mi bi-ŋaan.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: M nín nìn ká yii naa bíi dòoń kí fīī-mee, maa mɔ́tì m-maŋfal pu ní ki kɔ́ Amɔn yab tiŋkin ki jáń nì bi, ní ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki ŋá m-ŋaan. Too, ba gíti ŋá ní ni yíkìń díǹ nee kí dāá já nì mi?»

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jeefita kpáfì Galaadi janjaliibi kɔkɔ ní bi jáń nì Eefiraayiim naakookun yab ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Kun pu bi nìn jáń kujaau gbantee di sá yii Eefiraayiim yab nìn lī-bi yii: «Nimbi Galaadi yab, ni sá Eefiraayiim naakookun nib ní ki yíkì Eefiraayiim yab kansikin ki sáǹní ki dɔ́miń ki kā Manasee naakookun yab kansikin!»

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Galaadi yab nìn pīiǹ Eefiraayiim naakookun yab isan in bi nìn dìŋfī ki dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee. Ŋyunti ŋun ní Eefiraayiim naakookun yab bin nìn sáǹ ki ŋmátèe kansikin ubɔ yaa nìn bāań ki là kí dùtēe, ní Galaadi yab ń bàlifì-u yii: «A sá Eefiraayiim niliu níii?» Udaan yaa kíí yii: «Aayeeyee»,

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: ní Galaadi yab ń bí-u yii: «Lì yii: <Ciibooleeti>.» Ní udaan ń bí yii: <Siibooleeti>, kun puee Eefirayiim yab kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí lì an nín bàà sá bí lì puee. Niinee ní bí cúú udaan kí làntì kí bíĺ laakin ní bi dìŋfī ki dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee caŋin niin. An yuntiŋuee, bi nìn kūū Eefiraayiim janjaliibi binib kutukub imuŋku ili nì bili ní.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Ugalaadija Jeefita nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin aluu ní ki dāa nín kpíì, ní bi síb́-u Galaadi timmu kiba poon. Yibisan nì Eelɔn nì Abidɔn

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Jeefita kúm boonee, Yibisan un sá Beetileem tiŋkinee di nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Yibisan nìn kpíì ní bi síb́-u Beetileem tiŋkin.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Yibisan kúm boonee, Eelɔn un nìn sá Sabulɔn naakookunee di nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab. U nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin saalaa ní.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Eelɔn nìn kpíì ní bi síb́-u Eelɔn, Sabulɔn tiŋki poon.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Yileel un nìn sá Pireeyatɔn tiŋkinee jipɔɔn Abidɔn nìn kpíì ní bi síb́-u Pireeyatɔn tiŋki kin sá Eefiraayiim naakookun timmu kibee poon, Amaleeki yab jool pu.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn fātìi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan ceeyee ní ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki ŋá Fiiliistii yab ŋaan abin imuŋku ili.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Uninja ubɔ nìn bí ki nìn sá Sooreeya tiŋkin, Daani naakookun maaliŋu ŋubɔ poon, ní bi nìn yíì-u yii Manoowa. U-nimpuu nìn sá uŋmaŋŋmanti ní, waa nìn cáá kibiki.

english_verse: but one day an angel from the Lord appeared to her and said: You have never been able to have any children, but very soon you will be pregnant and have a son. He will belong to God from the day he is born, so his hair must never be cut. And even before he is born, you must not drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Your son will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines.
translation_verse: kibininjabiki kin a làá cáá dipool kí màal̀ee pu. Bɔlfi ń taa pée gbēē kibikee yil, di sá kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun ní a làá díkí u-poolee, u làá nīn sá un bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee ní. Úǹ di làá kíĺ kí fīī Isirayeel yab Fiiliistii yab ŋaan.»

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee nín kùǹ ki cūtìi máafì u-cal yii: «Unimbɔti niliu ubɔ dɔ́miń m-cee. U náań nì Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ní a yaa kpēē-uee, an cáá tifaandi. Maa bālifì laakin ní u sée, ní u mun kaa tùkū-mi u-yindi.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: U bí-mi yii: <Á nīn nyí yii a làá cáá dipool kí màal̀ kibininjabiki. Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, á taa ti nyɔ̀ ndamamaaa, kí taa ti nyɔ̀ ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Á taa jī tijin tin kaa bí circiree mun, kun puee kibininjabiki kin a làá màal̀ee, bi làá dū-kì kí sú Unimbɔti ní kí dāá sāā ki-kúm dal.>»

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Manoowa mēē ti-Dindaan ki lī yii: «M-Dindaan, m gbāam̀-si, yàntī Unimbɔti niliu un a túnní ti-ceeyee ń fàtīí gítiń kí dàkà-ti min ti máaǹ kí ŋá kí tīī kibikee bi yaa láa màl̄-kèe.»

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn fōō Manoowa wimmeem ní ki nìn yāntì u-tuuŋŋuee fātìi gítìń unimpuee cee. U nìn kā bukpaan ní, ama u-cal Manoowa kaa nìn bí u-cee.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Niin niin ní unimpuee yíkìi sáǹ ki cūtìi tùkū u-cal yii: «Kpèè, kijapaai kin nìn dɔ́miń m-cee yaadalee fātìi tí lēē u-ba ki dàkā-mi!»

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ní Manoowa yíkì ki páaǹ u-nimpuu boon ki nín cá kijapaayee cee ki bàn̄ ki bālifì-u yii: «Sii di sá kijapaai kin nìn sòon̄ nì unimpu neeyeeee?» Ní kijapaayee kíí yii: «Iiin, an sá man!»

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Ní Manoowa bālifì-u yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, a nín lī puee yaa láa ŋá mimmee, akoobil ŋilaŋ ní tí kòò kibikee maŋfal wiiŋyi nì ditundi din kì làá tɔ̄ee pu?»

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee kíí Manoowa yii: «Tin kɔkɔ ní m kōoǹ a-nimpuuee, ú kòò-tì.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Ú taa pée dáká tin kamaa ní bi yaa dū fiinyi subil ki ŋée. Ú taa nyɔ̀ ndamam àá ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Ú taa jī tijin tin kamaa kaa bí circiree, ní kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ ní m tùkū-u yii ú ŋée.»

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Manoowa bí ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee yii: «Yàntī tí tàan̄-si fiii. Ti làá kpɔ̀ diŋɔbil kí tɔ́kɔń kí cáań-si.»

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee kíí-u yii: «Báà a yaa tāaǹ-maaa, maa làá jī tijin tin a làá ŋá kí tīī-mee. Ama a yaa là kí ŋá saraawɔkaa, a ŋūǹ kí ŋá kí tīī ti-Dindaan.» Di sá yii Manoowa kaa nìn nyí yii u nì ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu di nìn bíi sòoǹ.

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Ní Manoowa bí ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee yii: «Bi yíì-si yii ba? Tùkù-ti án nín làá ŋá pu ní tibɔti tin a sòon̄ee yaa láa ŋée tí dāá nyɔ̄ŋkì-see.»

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní a baasii là kí béé m-yindi ní? Dì sá maamaaci yindi ní.»

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Manoowa nìn bɔ́ntì diŋɔbil nì saraa wanti ki dūu páaǹ ditaŋkpal pu ki ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan un ŋáań maamaaci tuuŋŋee. Manoowa nì u-nimpuu nìn kíǹ ki yú ki kpèé.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Bi dāa kpēēyee, ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee bí aŋmilimbil ŋin nìn nyēē nsaraafan pu ki jɔ́ḿee poon ki nín jɔ́ḿ yilpu. Manoowa nì u-nimpuu nín ká mimmee ní bi tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee kaa nìn gíti lēē ŋu-ba ki dàkā Manoowa nì u-nimpuu. Niin ní Manoowa nìn dūu béè yii kijapaayee nìn lafun sá ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Ní Manoowa bí u-nimpuu yii: «Ti nín pée ká Unimbɔti nì ti-nimbiliŋ nee, ti làá pée kpú ní.»

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Ama ní u-nimpuu kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan yaa bàà là kí kpɔ̀-tee, waa bàà fòol̄ ti-saraawɔkaau nì ti-saraau. Waa bàà làá dàkà-ti tin kɔkɔ ti ká nee, kaa bàà làá tùkù-ti tibɔti tin u tùkū-ti kɔŋkɔnnee.»

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Unimpuee nìn màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Samsɔn. Kibiki gbanti nìn wíiǹ, ní ti-Dindaan nìn bīiǹ ki-boon.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Maanee-Daani tiŋki kin bí Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmu kansikinee poon ní ti-Dindaan Fam nìn yāntì Samsɔn péé péé ki nyántì u-pɔŋŋu ki dàkā.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Dalbee Samsɔn sīntì Tiimina tiŋkin ní ki tin dūu ká Fiiliistii yab sapɔmbi kansikin usapɔnnyaan ubɔ.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: U nín nìn fātìi jɔ́m̀ u-tiŋkinee ní ki sòon̄ unimpuee bɔti u-baa nì u-na cee ki bí yii: «M nín cūtì Tiimina tiŋkinee, m ká usapɔɔn ubɔ Fiiliistii yab sapɔmbi kansikin. Kɔŋkɔnnee m là yii ní cáá úǹ ní kí tīī-mi.»

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Ní u-baa nì u-na bí-u yii: «Mimmee usapɔɔn kaa bí a-maaliŋu nì a-nibul kɔkɔ sapɔmbi poon á cááaaa? Ba di ŋá ní a là kí cáá Fiiliistii yab bin kaa gíí akpancan nee sapɔmbi ubɔ ní?» Ní Samsɔn bí u-baa yii: «Usapɔɔn gbanti ní m pée là yii á cáá kí tīī-mi, kun puee úǹ di kɔ́-mi!»

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Samsɔn baa nì u-na kaa nìn nyí yii ti-Dindaan di nìn bíi téekí bi-jipɔɔn ú lēē yii u là an nimpuuee. Ti-Dindaan nìn bíi nyàab̀ nsan ŋun ní u làá dī kí táká Fiiliistii yab tibɔtee ní, kun puee ŋyunti gbantee, u-nibul Isirayeel yab nìn bí Fiiliistii yab taapu ní.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Samsɔn nìn nín sìntī Tiimina tiŋkin, u nì u-baa nì u-na. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ fiinyi sufii in yú Tiimina tiŋki caŋinee, kpalaayee digbikintipɔmbil diba nyánní kumooun, ki mùuǹ ki túŋkí Samsɔn.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Niin ní ti-Dindaan Fam kɔ́ Samsɔn ní u cúú digbikintipɔmbilee ŋŋancal, ki dáaĺ ki tɔ̄ntì-dì kii bi nín dátí kí tɔ̀ntī kiŋɔbiki puee. Ama waa nìn tùkū u-baa nì u-na tin ní u nìn ŋée.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee u nìn nín sìntī Tiimina tiŋkin ki cūtìi sòon̄ nì usapɔɔnee. Usapɔɔnee nìn kɔ́-u tikpil.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Iwiŋkaaŋkaa boonee, Samsɔn nìn fātìi yíkì u-dumpu ki nín gítí Tiimina tiŋkin kí cùú cáá unimpuee. U bàn̄ laakin u nìn kūū gbikinti ki bíl̀ee ní ki pāatì kí kpèè digbikintikpilee. U nìn ká dinaŋgbansikitil kā gbikintee wunti poon nì tisiil.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Ní Samsɔn lēē tisiil ki ŋá u-ŋaan ki còom̄ ki ŋmóò ki cá. U cōom̀ ki fātìi cúú u-baa nì u-nee, ní ki lēē tisiil ki tīī-bi ní bi mun ŋmɔ́, ama waa nìn tùkū-bi yii digbikintikpil poon ní u lēeń tisiil. Samsɔn pɔ́ɔǹ Fiiliistii yab mpɔ́ɔn

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Samsɔn baa nìn sīntì unimpuee dumpu ní Samsɔn cūtìi bɔ́ntì dinimpucaal jiŋaaliu niin, kii binaacimpɔmbi nín nìn pée ŋáań puee.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nín nìn pée ká-uee, ní bi lēē binaacimpɔmbi mmuŋku nì saalaa bí nīn bí u-cee.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa kaa ŋúń ki lēē ŋu-taapu ki tùkū-mee, nimbi di làá tīī man abɔkutifɔkɔ mmuŋku nì saalaa nì abɔkutikpántikaa mun mmuŋku nì saalaa.» Ní bi bí-u yii: «Pɔ́ɔǹ a-pɔɔŋŋu gbanti tí pīlifì!»

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Ní Samsɔn bí-bi yii: «Un ŋmóò poon ní tiŋmɔkaal nyánní. Un pɔ̄ɔ̄yee poon ní mmɔn nyánní. An sá ba?» Iwiin ita dāa dūu jítì, binaacimpɔmbee kaa ŋúń ki lēē mpɔɔnee taapu ki tùkū Samsɔn.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Ŋwinluluúti dalee ní bi bí Samsɔn nimpuu yii: «Ŋmàtiǹ a-cal ú tùkù-ti mpɔɔnee taapu, an yaa sá fám ti làá wà-si ŋŋmi kí kpáaǹ a-baa dicaŋku kɔkɔ. Ni yíiń-ti kí fūkul̀-ti níii?»

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Samsɔn nimpuu bíi sūǹ lɔ̀lɔ ní ki bí-u yii: «A pée ná-mi ní, aa néeń-mi. A pɔ́ɔǹ m-dumpu yab mpɔ́ɔn, ama ní kaa lēē ŋu-taapu ki tùkū-mi.» Ní Samsɔn kíí-u yii: «Maa lēē mpɔ́ɔn gbanti taapu ki tùkū m-baa nì m-na gba, ní ki dāa cáa tùkū siii?»

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Samsɔn nimpuu nìn súń míǹ ní kinyɔmmɔŋ kin bi dūu jíń jiŋaalee kɔkɔ. Ŋwinluluúti dalee, Samsɔn nimpuu nìn páb́-u an gíti lákáǹee, ní Samsɔn lēē mpɔɔnee taapu ki tùkū-u. Ní unimpu yíkìi nín cá ki cūtìi lēē mpɔɔnee taapu ki tùkū u-yab.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Ŋwinluluúti gbanti dal kí wàatī ŋwìiń ń jēetée ní kitiŋee nib bí Samsɔn yii: «Ba gíti mɔ̄ ki jítiǹ tisiil? Ba gíti pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ gbikinti?» Ní Samsɔn kíí-bi yii: «Ni yaa kaa bàà dū m-nasaliu ki kùn̄ tikpaal, naa bàà làá ŋmā kí béé man pɔɔŋŋu nee taapu!»

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū unimpuee úǹ ki tīī Samsɔn bɔɔ u nì un nìn pée nóó u-nimpucaal jiŋaaliu yuntiŋuee ticati.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: U nìn bí Samsɔn yii: «Man dākafì yii aa ti pée là-u ní, an puee man dū-u ki tīī a-bɔɔ un nìn pée nóó-si a-nimpucaal jiŋaaliunee ticati. Ama u-naal bí, ki gíti ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ-u gba. A ŋūǹ kí yòon̄ úǹ kí téeǹ u-maan yil!»

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Ní Samsɔn bí-bi yii: «Min bí nee m yaa ŋá Fiiliistii yab inikpiti, ubɔ kaa làá kɔ̄kɔl̀-mi.»

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: U ŋá mimmee ní ki dū ŋŋmi ki sēē iŋminaapool, ki gíiǹ ŋŋɔkɔmu ki líì ní mu nín kóò Fiiliistii yab satin. Ŋŋmi nìn wùn̄ bilee un bi nìn cáń ki bíl̀ee nì un dáá gbíntìi yú baa láá cáńee, ki wùn̄ ki kpáaǹ fiinyi sufii nì ɔliifi sufii.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab bālifì yii: «Ŋma ŋá mimmee?» Ní binib kíí-bi yii: «An sá utiiminaja coo Samsɔn di ŋá míǹ, kun puee u-coo gbanti fōō u-nimpuu ní ki dūu tīī u-bɔɔ un nìn nóó-u u-nimpucaal jiŋaaliunee ticati.» Ní Fiiliistii yab nín jɔ́ḿ Tiimina tiŋkin ki cūtìi wùn̄ unimpu gbanti ŋŋmi, ki kpáaǹ u-baa.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Samsɔn tùkū-bi yii: «Too, ní béé yii ni nín ŋá min nee puee, m yaa kaa tɔ̀n̄-ni ipɔntoon maa làá dūú cà.»

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: U nìn cūtìi jáń nì Fiiliistii yab ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Míǹ boon ní u nín sìntī Eetaam tiŋkin ki cūtìi kɔ́ ntaŋkpalɔkɔ ŋubɔn. Samsɔn dū kimaŋ nyɔɔkpaweeŋŋu ki pɔ̄fì Fiiliistii yab

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn jɔ́m̀ Juuda tiŋkin ki ŋātì dijanjanaapaal, ki kāaǹ bi-janjaliibi ki tin sāā mpaan ŋun bi yíì yii Leeyiiyee.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Ní Juuda naakookun yab bālifì-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni jɔ́mìń kí jáǹ-ti ní?» Ní Fiiliistii yab kíí Juuda naakookun yab yii: «Ti jɔ́mìń kí cúú Samsɔn kí ŋá-u kii u nín ŋá-ti puee kí téeǹ ní.»

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Juuda naakookun yab bininjab kutukub bita yíkì ki nín sìntī Eetaam tiŋkin, ntaŋkpalɔkɔ ŋun poon Samsɔn nìn bée ki bí-u yii: «Saa nyí ti nín bí Fiiliistii yab taapueeee? Ba bɔti ní a ŋá-ti mimmee?» Ní Samsɔn kíí-bi yii: «Bi nín ŋá-mi puee, míǹ ní ma mun ŋá-bi ki téeǹ!»

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Ní bi bí-u yii: «Too, timbi sīntìń kí bóob́-si iŋmii kí cáá-si kí ŋúbiǹ Fiiliistii yab ní!» Ní Samsɔn bí-bi yii: «Ní pùtīmaan yii nimbi ni-ba kaa làá kpɔ̀-mi.»

english_verse: “We promise,” the men said. “We will only tie you up and turn you over to the Philistines. We won't kill you.” Then they tied up his hands and arms with two brand-new ropes and led him away from Etam Rock. When the Philistines saw that Samson was being brought to their camp at Jawbone, they started shouting and ran toward him. But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and Samson broke the ropes, as though they were pieces of burnt cloth.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u tóob́ kí bà mpaan ŋun bi yíì Leeyiiyee ní Fiiliistii yab túŋkì-u nsanni ki kūuntí mpɔn. Ama ti-Dindaan Fam nìn kɔ́-u ní iŋmii in nìn bóob́ u-ŋaliiyee dūu kpántì kii gulfa ní ŋŋmi wùn̄ee, ní ki gbátì u-ŋaliiyin ki lítì.

english_verse: Samson glanced around and spotted the jawbone of a donkey. The jawbone had not yet dried out, so it was still hard and heavy. Samson grabbed it and started hitting Philistines—he killed
translation_verse: Samsɔn kpēēyee kimaŋ kin bi kūū an kaa láá yúntèe nyɔɔkpaweeŋŋu di dɔ̄ee. Ní u yōoǹ-ŋu ki dūu fátì ki kūū binib kutuku ubɔ.

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Ní Samsɔn bí yii: «Kimaŋ nyɔɔkpaweeŋŋu ní m dūu pɔ̄fì-bi. M dū kimaŋ nyɔɔkpaweeŋŋu ki kūū binib kutuku ubɔ.»

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: U lī míǹ ki ŋmíl̀ee, ní ki dū nnyɔɔkpaweenee ki tɔ́ ki fá ndan, ní bi yíiń laakin ŋu tin lítèe yii Ramati Leeyii, taapu di sá yii <nnyɔɔkpaween gbantaŋki>.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee nnyinnyoo nìn bàn̄-u tikpil, ní u tíminsì ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ki lī yii: «Sii di yāntì ní man a-tɔntɔnliu ká dijajikpaandi din bí nee. Mimmee kɔŋkɔnnee nnyinnyoo làá kpɔ̀-mi, ḿ kɔ́ bin kaa gífí nee ŋaanaaa?»

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn yāntì ditaŋkpakpaandi din nìn bí Leeyii paaŋŋu pu ki cáá mbùńee cúu látì, ní nnyim nyánní. Samsɔn nìn nyùn̄ u-nimbiliŋ cúu ŋāatì ní u fātìi ká mpɔn. An pu ní bi nìn pú nnyimbul gbantee diyindi yii Eeni-Kooree, taapu di sá yii <un yíińee nyimbuliŋu>. Nnyimbul gbanti dáá gbíntìi bí Leeyii paaŋŋu pu ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab yuntiŋu gbantee, Samsɔn nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin mmuŋku ní.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Gaasaa yab nín nìn gbìl̄ yii Samsɔn bí bi-tiŋkinee, bi nìn cōom̀ ki māntì kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu ki cɔ́ŋkì-u kunyeeu gbanti kɔkɔ. Kunyeeu gbantee, baa nìn ŋá kìrikiri ní ki lī bi-neen yii: «Ti làá yàntī kutaa yaa fu wúntèe ní tí fu kpɔ̀-u.»

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, Samsɔn ká unimpu ubɔ ki néeń. U nìn kóòń Sooreeki tantakalin ní bi yíì-u yii Daliila.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi biŋmooyee nín béè mimmee ní ki cūtìi ká Daliila ki tùkū-u yii: «Ŋmàtiǹ Samsɔn kí béé an nín dī pu ní u baasii cáá mpɔŋkpaan ŋun u cáá nee, nì min ní ti máaǹ kí ŋá kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u kí ŋmā kí bóob́-u iŋmii ú taa ti ŋmā kí ŋá báà tibee. A yaa ŋúń ki ŋá mimmee, timbi ŋmootil báà ŋma làá tīī-si animbil kúti jitɔmbi kutuku ubɔ nì dilaataal dilaataal.»

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daliila bí Samsɔn yii: «M gbàam̄-si, tùkù-mi an nín dī pu ní a cáá mpɔŋkpaan ŋun a cáá nee, kí tùkù-mi min unil máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí ŋmā kí bóob́-si iŋmii á taa ti ŋmā kí ŋá báà tibee.»

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ní Samsɔn bí-u yii: «A yaa dū itaŋŋmii in dáá sɔ̀m̀ baa láá díntì-iee iluli ki dūu bóob́-mee, m-pɔŋŋu làá pèefì ní ḿ gítí kii unifantantee.»

english_verse: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní Fiiliistii yab kɔ́ ki nákáǹ nákáǹ Samsɔn diikunee, ní Daliila téeń yii: «Samsɔn, Fiiliistii yab dòoń kí cúú-seeee!» Ní Samsɔn dáaĺ ki tīfì itaŋŋmiiyee kii gulfa yaa pìl̄ ŋŋmi u nín tìfī puee. Ama binib kaa nìn béè laakin ní Samsɔn pɔŋkpaaŋŋu gbanti nìn nyánnée.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daliila bí Samsɔn yii: «Kpèè a ŋúb́-mi ki gbíilíǹ ki mɔ́ntí-mi inyimɔn. Kɔŋkɔnnee baasii tùkù-mi min ní unil máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí ŋmā kí bóob́-si iŋmiiyee.»

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ní Samsɔn bí-u yii: «A yaa dū iŋmipɔmpɔɔn in baa láá dūu ŋá báà tiba nì tibee ki gúĺ-mi mpɔnee, m-pɔŋŋu làá pèefì ní ḿ gítí kii unifantantee.»

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Ní Daliila nyàab̄ iŋmipɔmpɔɔn ki gúĺ Samsɔn ní ki téeń yii: «Samsɔn, Fiiliistii yab dòoń kí cúú-seeee!» Nì mimmee Fiiliistii yab nìn pée náká náká Samsɔn diikun niin dee. Ama Samsɔn nìn dáaĺ ki tīfì iŋmipɔmpɔɔn in nìn bóob́ u-ŋaliiyee, a lì kii gulfatɔkaayee.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ní Daliila bí Samsɔn yii: «Kí yòon̄ kí dāá sāā nee, a pée ŋúb́-mi ki gbíilíǹ ní ki mɔ́ntí-mi inyimɔn. Pée tùkù-mi min ní unil máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí ŋmā kí bóob́-see!» Ní Samsɔn bí-u yii: «A yaa dū bi nín lùn̄ m-yikpiti tifɔkɔl miluli puee ki lùn̄ ki nákáǹ kun bi cáa lù satabee pu ní ki dū mpiin ki cúúyee, m-pɔŋŋu làá pèefì ní ḿ gítí kii unifantantee.»

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: Ní Daliila ŋmáliŋkì ŋmáliŋkì Samsɔn ní u gèen̄. Samsɔn gèen̄ee ní Daliila cúú bi nín lùn̄ u-yikpiti tifɔkɔl miluli puee ki lùn̄ ki nákáǹ kun bi cáa lù satabee pu ní ki dū mpiin ki cúú. U dóòyee ní ki téeń yii: «Samsɔn, Fiiliistii yab dòoń kí cúú-seeee!» Ní Samsɔn fīntì ŋgeem pu ki cúú mpiin nì kun bi cáa lù satabee ki dáaĺ ki cóotì ki kpáaǹ gulfa un bi nìn dūu bóob́ u-yikpitee.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Ní Daliila bí Samsɔn yii: «Mana ní a ŋūǹ kí lì yii a néeń-mi, ama ní a-naŋki kaa kā m-pu? Kpèè, mita kɔkɔ ní a ŋúb́-mi ki gbíilíǹ kaa tùkū-mi laakin ní a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋuee nyánnée.»

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Baabadalee Daliila nìn pée páb́ Samsɔn nì tibɔbaantiil gbanti dibalifil kaa gbèentí. Samsɔn nìn ŋmēē ki ŋmēē ki tin gīī,

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: ní ki dāa lēē tin kā u-pɔbilinee ki tùkū Daliila yii: «Bɔlfi kaa láá gbēē m-yikpiti ki ká, kun puee doooo m-na poon ní bi dū-mi ki sú Unimbɔti. Bi yaa pée kōol̀ m-yikpitee, m-pɔŋŋu làá nyā m-ni ní m-wunti ń pèefì, ní ḿ gítí kii unifantantee.»

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Daliila nín ká yii kɔŋkɔnnee Samsɔn lafun lēē tin kā u-pɔbilinee ki tùkū-uee, ní u tú bí yíiń Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibee ki bí-bi yii: «Nín̄ dòoḿmaan, kun puee min bí nee u baasii lēē u-pɔbil poon bɔti ní ki tùkū-mi.» Niin ní Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibee yíkì ki nín jɔ́ḿ Daliila dumpu, ki ŋúb́ animbil ŋin bi nìn pōoǹ-uee.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Daliila nìn dū Samsɔn ki páaǹ u-taaŋi pu ki ŋmáliŋkì ŋmáliŋkì-u ní Samsɔn gèen̄, ní u yíiń uninja ubɔ dɔ́miń ki cúú Samsɔn yikpiti tin bi lùn̄ tifɔkɔl miluli puee ki kōol̀. Niin ní Samsɔn wunti kíĺ ki bíi yɔ̀tī, ní u-pɔŋŋu nyáń u-ni kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn cúú-u ní ki sāā ki cɔ́tì u-nimbiliŋ liitil. Boonee ní bi cáá-u ki sīntì Gaasaa tiŋkin ki tin dū ikusaka in bi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee ki pɔ́b́ mili ki dūu gbìn̄-u. Bi nìn yāntì u bí kusarkadiin ki màntī kunaau taŋkpeeŋi ŋin nà ŋyimee.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Ama Samsɔn yikpiti tin bi nìn cúu kōol̀ee nìn fātìi kíĺ ki bíi nyēē. Samsɔn tɔ̀n̄ u-pɔntooŋyi ijoolkaa ní ki nín kpíì

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Dalbee, Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibee kpáfì ki ŋá saraakpaan ki tīī bi-waal Daagɔn. Bi nìn bí ki fàal̀ ki lì yii: «Ti-waal dū ti-nannanliu Samsɔn ki ŋá ti-ŋaan!»

english_verse: Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!” The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god: Samson ruined our crops and killed our people. He was our enemy, but our god helped us capture him. They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní an bíi nyàatī-bee, ní bi bí yii: «Ní yíiḿmaan Samsɔn ú dāan̄ kí láaǹ-taa!» Ní bi lēē binib ki tú bi cūtìi nyántìń Samsɔn kusarkadiin, ní u dɔ́miń ki láaǹ-bi. Bi láń láń ki dóòyee ní ki cáá-u ki sákaǹ kuwaadii jaantalkub bili kansikin.

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Niin ní Samsɔn bí unaacimpɔɔn un nìn ŋúb́ u-ŋal ki dàtī-uee yii: «Cúú m-ŋal kí dàkà-mi ḿ ŋmā kí gbēē jaantalkub bin ŋúb́ kudiiyee. M là kí nyīī bi-pu ní.»

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Niinee Samsɔn mēē ti-Dindaan yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m mèé-si yii á pée téetí m-pu. M-baa Unimbɔti, fàtīí tīī-mi mpɔn, báà min bí nee baba, ḿ ŋmā kí téeǹ Fiiliistii yab bi nín sāā ki cɔ́tì m-nimbiliŋ liitil puee dibaba pu.»

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Samsɔn mēē míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki máań máań jaantalkub bili bin nìn cɔ́ kansikin ní ki ŋúb́ kudiiyee pɔŋŋuee. U nìn dū u-ŋaŋgiil ki nyīī jaantalkubee ubɔ ní ki dū u-ŋaŋgan ki nyīī un kíǹee.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: Samsɔn nyīī nyīī jaantalkub liitil mimmee ní ki téeń mpɔn yii: «Yàntī man nì Fiiliistii yab ń kpāfì kí kpú!» Niinee ní u gúkúǹ u-ba ki nyīī jaantalkubee nì u-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ, ní kudiiyee lítì ki tābitì ki kūū Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibee nì samaa un nìn pée kpáfì ki bí niinee kɔkɔ. Binib bin ní Samsɔn nìn kūū u-kúm wiiŋŋu gbanti dalee nìn jítiǹ bin kɔkɔ u nìn kūū ŋyunti ŋun u nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Samsɔn nabiyaamu nì u-baa dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ nìn sīntìń ki yōoǹ u-wunti ki cáa nín jɔ́ḿ bi-tiŋkin. Bi nìn síb́-u Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmu kansikin, u-baa Manoowa kaakul poon. Samsɔn nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin mmuŋku ní.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: An pu ní Miika nín fātìi gíiǹ animbilee ki tīī u-nee, u-na nìn lēē ŋi-poon jitɔmbi kulaafaau ki dūu tīī ucaa u mɔ́ɔ́ diwaal ki dūntì tikúti ki nyūntì-dì ní bi cáa yóoǹ Miika dumpu.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Too, Miika gbanti nìn cáá mpaan ŋun pu u jáaḿ inimbɔtee u-cindin. U nìn yāntì bi fātìi mɔ́ɔ́-u diwaal diba, ki kpítì-u awaa ŋin làá nīn cí u-cindee mun ní u dūu kútì, ní ki lēē u-jipɔɔn ubɔ ki kāaǹ ú nīn sá u-saraaŋaliu.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee bibɔtiibi kaa nìn dá láá bí Isirayeel tiŋkin. Báà ŋma nìn ŋáań min u lèe ní.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Unaacimpɔɔnee nìn yíkì Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkinee, ní ki nìn bíi yìiǹ ki nyàab̀ laaba kí gíti kàl̄ kunicaŋu. U nìn bíi yìiǹ ki tin kɔ́ Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi timmunee, ní ki tin nyáń Miika dicaŋku pu.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Ní Miika bālifì-u yii: «La ní a nyánní ní?» Ní u kíí Miika yii: «Man sá Leefii naakookun ní ki nyánní Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin. M bíi yìiǹ ki nyàab̀ laaba kí kàl̄ kunicaŋu ní.»

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Miika bí-u yii: «Yaa sée gbíntí m-cee doo kí nīn sá m-baa nì m-saraaŋaliu. M làá nīn tìì-si animbil jitɔmbi saalaa dibindi poon, kí nīn tìì-si tiwampeeŋkaal nì tijikaal.» Leefii naakookun naacimpɔɔŋwuee nìn kíí ki gbíntì niin.

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Miika nìn dū usaraaŋal tundi ki ŋúbiǹ Leefii naakookun naacimpɔɔŋwuee. U nìn kíǹ ki kóò Miika dumpu ní.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Miika lī yii: «Min bí nee, m nín ká Leefii naakookun niliu ú nīn sá m-saraaŋaliu nee, m lafun béè yii ti-Dindaan làá dàkà-mi u-ŋanti dee!»

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee bibɔtiibi kaa nìn dá láá bí Isirayeel tiŋkin. An yuntiŋuee Daani naakookun yab nìn bí ki nyàab̀ kitiŋ kin bi làá kàl̄ee dee, kun puee kí cáá sāā ŋyunti gbantee, baa nìn cáá ditinjandi Isirayeel naakɔti tin kíǹee kansikin.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Daani naakookun yab nìn lēē bi-maaliŋu poon bibaatandambi biŋmoo ki tú, bí yīkì Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmun kí yìiǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé kitiŋ tiŋan. Binib biŋmoo gbanti nìn yìin̄ ki bàn̄ Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi timmunee, kunyeeu mɔ́ ní bi kɔ́ Miika dumpu.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí Miika dumpu niin ní ki gbìl̄ unaacimpɔɔn un sá Leefii naakookunee neen, ní ki béè dinicil din u sée. Bi nìn cūtì u-cee ki bālifì-u yii: «Ŋma di cáań-si doo nee ní? Ba tundi ní a bí doo ki tūǹ? Ba di ŋúb́-si ní a kā doo nee?»

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí-bi yii: «An sá Miika di fōō-mi ditundi. U yāntì m sá u-saraaŋaliu ní u pà-mi.»

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Ní bi fātìi bí-u yii: «Bàlifì Unimbɔti kí kpèè yii nsan ŋun ti bíi còom̄ nee làá nīn sá nsammɔntaaa, ŋuaa làá nīn sá.»

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋalee kíí-bi yii: «Ní taa pée fàŋkìmaan báà tiba! Ti-Dindaan làá céeǹ-ni nsan ŋun ni bíi còom̄ nee poon!»

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Ní binib biŋmooyee nìkī bi-saŋŋu, ki cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Layiisi tiŋkin. Bi bàn̄ kitiŋ gbantinee ní ki ká yii binib bin nìn kóò niinee nì ubɔ kaa nìn cáá tɔb kujaau. Bi kā nì ŋgbansɔŋfi nì dipɔɔsɔŋkil kii Siidɔn yab nín nìn bí puee. Ubɔ kaa nìn bí ki páb́-baaa, ditimbundi diba mun nib kaa nìn bí ki cáá mpɔn bi-pu. Layiisi yab nìn kóò ki dátiǹ Siidɔn yab, ní kaa nìn bí báà ubɔ taapu.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní binib biŋmooyee fātìi nín gítí bi-dumpu Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmun, ní bi-nabiyaamu tin bālifì-bi yii: «Ni kánní yii ba?»

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Ni yaa bàn̄ niinee, ni làá ká yii binib bin kóò kitiŋ gbantee kā nì ŋgbansɔŋfi ní kaa dàkafī yii tiba ŋūǹ kí ŋá-bi. Bi-tiŋkee wāā tiŋan ní tikɔkɔ nì tikɔkɔ bí ki-poon. Ti nyí yii Unimbɔti làá dū kitiŋ gbanti kí tīī-ni!»

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daani naakookun yab binib alaataa aluu bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi ní ki yíkì Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmun ki nín cá.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Bi yíkì mimmee ní ki jɔ́m̀ ki cūtìi ŋātì dijanjanaapaal Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋki kin sá Juuda naakookun timmu kibee poon. An pu ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Maanee-Daani ki dāa sāā díǹ pu nee. Mpaan gbanti bí Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋkin, ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Bi yíkì niinee ní ki pūntì Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi, ki cōom̀ ki bàn̄ Miika dumpu.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní binib biŋmoo bin bi nìn lēē bi yìin̄ ki cɔ́ŋkì ki béè Layiisi tiŋkee fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki bí yii: «Ni nyí yii diwaal diba, nì kudicaŋu waaŋi, nì diwaal din bi mɔ́ɔ́ ki dūntì tikúti ki nyūntèe bí adican nee kubɔ poonaaa? Too, kɔŋkɔnnee ní dàkafìmaan kí kpèè ni nín làá ŋá puee!»

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Ŋmīĺ niin! Taa ti pée wàan̄ a-nyɔkɔ kí lì báà tiba! Dāan̄ kí nóó-ti kí nīn sá usaraaŋal ki tīī-ti. Dàkafì kí kpèè yii á nīn sá usaraaŋal ki tīī unibaanti dicaŋku nì á nīn sá usaraaŋal ki tīī Isirayeel naakooku kumɔŋu kɔkɔee, la di ŋān̄?»

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Tibɔti gbanti nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ usaraaŋalee tikpil, di sá ní u nìn fōō diwaalee, nì kudicaŋu waaŋi, nì diwaal din bi dūntì tikúti ki nyūntèe ki nóó-bi bi nín cá.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Daani naakookun yab nìn nìkī bi-saŋŋu, ki nìn dū mbiyaamu nì tiwaŋkuti nì awaŋgul ki līntì bi-nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Daani naakookun yab nìn cōom̀ ki kɔ́ ndan kaa ti pìlīǹ Miika dumpu ní Miika nì u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki bóob́ butɔbu ní ki yíkìi kùl̄ ki páaǹ bi-boon.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Daani naakookun yab nín gbìl̄ Miika nì u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb pánní bi-boon ki tátí ki yíì-bee ní bi fātì ki bālifì Miika yii: «Ba cáá-si ní? Ba yì-tì ní a kóoǹní dinikitil nee ki páaǹní a-boon mimmee?»

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Ní Miika kíí-bi yii: «Ni yōoǹ awaa ŋin m yāntì bi mɔ́ɔ́-mee, ki yōoǹ ki kpáaǹ m-saraaŋaliu, báà tiba nì tiba kaa ti kíǹ-mi ní ni gíti bàlifī-mi yii ba di cáá-maaa?»

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Ní Daani naakookun yab fātìi kpātì u-pu ki bí-u yii: «A yaa pée nyí nnyiimee, á ŋmīĺ a-nyɔkɔ laakin a yú nee, kí taa ti sòoǹ kí páb́ timbi! Yaa sá fám, a làá yàntī ti-kansikin biba ń dū bi-ŋuul kí nyìntī a-pu, kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí sii nì a-dicaŋku yab kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Daani naakookun yab kpātì Miika pu mimmee ní ki nìkī bi-saŋŋu. Miika nín ká yii bi cáá mpɔn ki jítiǹ-uee, ní u fātìi nín kùǹ u-dumpu. Daani naakookun yab kāl̀ Layiisi tiŋkin

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpántì kitiŋee diyindi, ki nìn kíǹ ki yíì-kì yii Daani, kii bi nín nìn yíì bi-naanja, Jaakɔb jipɔɔn puee. Njaminee, ki-yindi di nìn dáá láá sá Layiisi.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee bibɔtiibi kaa nìn dá láá bí Isirayeel tiŋkin. Leefii naakookun niliu ubɔ nìn kóòń Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi timmu mun bínní poon poon púee kiban. U nìn cáá ubɔnti ubɔ sá Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: U-bɔɔn gbanti nìn nyáń u-boon ní ki nìn yíkì-u ki nín kùǹ u-baa dumpu Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin. U nìn kāl̀ niin ki bàn̄ kii iŋmal inaa nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: U-cal nìn jìn̄ u-boon ki cūtì kí sɔ̀ŋkì u-pɔbil kí fàtīí gíiǹní-u u-cee. U nìn kpáaǹ u-tɔntɔnliu nì mmamu muli. U-bɔɔnee nìn cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ u-baa dumpu. U-baa nín nìn ká u-cooyee, an nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u tikpil ní u fōō-u nì dipɔɔpindi.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: U nìn cúú u-coo ki kāaǹ u-dumpu iwiin ita kɔkɔ. Iwiin ita gbantee, u nì u-tɔntɔnliu nìn jīǹ, ki nyù ní ki dɔ̀ niin.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Ŋwinnanaati dal bi fīntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, uleefiijee bíi bɔ́ntí bí yīkèe, ní unimpu baa bí-u yii: «Kāl̀ kí jī tijin kí tíkiń a-fam kí wàatī ní nín búntáa!»

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Ní u kíí ki kāl̀ ní bi-liitil jíń ki nyùn̄. Ní unimpu baa bí-u yii: «Gbíntí kí dòon̄ doo kunyeeu nee kí gíti ŋùŋfì fiiiyaa!»

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Uleefiijee nín bàà nìn yíkì kí nīn cée, ní u-coo kā u-pu yii ú gbíntí kí dòon̄, ní u dāa kíí ki lafun gbíntì niin ki dōoǹ kunyeeu gbanti.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Ŋwiŋŋmooŋmooti dal, u tí yíkì malaa ki bɔ́ntì kí bàà nín̄ cée, ní unimpu baa tí bí-u yii: «M gbāam̀-si, kàl̄ kí jī tijin, kí cīití ŋwìiń yaa sɔ̄ŋkèe á nīn cá!» Ní bi-liitil tí kāl̀ ki jíń tijin.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Uninjee nì u-bɔɔn nì u-tɔntɔnliu tí bɔ́ntì kí yīkèe, ní u-coo tí bí-u yii: «Kpèè ŋwìiń jéetì ní nee, kunyeeu bíi móotí! An puee ní pūtìi gbíntí kí dòon̄ á gíti ŋùŋfì fiii. Fool kutaafaauee, ní fu yīkì malaa kí nīn kùǹ a-dumpu.»

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ama uninjee nìn yíì kpataaa, kaa ti kíí kí dòon̄ niin kunyeeu gbanti. U nìn yíkì ki cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Jeebusi tiŋki kin bi gíti yíì yii Jeerusaleem tiŋkee. U nìn kpáaǹ u-mammu liitil mun u nìn túǹ awaŋgulee nì u-bɔɔn.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ Jeebusi tiŋki caŋinee, ŋwìiń ŋman nìn pée jéetì ki dóò, ní utɔntɔnlee bí u-kpiliu yii: «Ukpil, yàntī tí pàatī kí kɔ́ Jeebusi yab tiŋki nee poon kí dòon̄ kunyeeu nee!»

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ní u-kpiliu kíí-u yii: «Taa làá yūĺ binicambi tiŋki kin poon Isirayeel niliu báà ubɔ kaa bí nee. Ti làá nìkī kí bà Giibeeya tiŋkin ní.»

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lafun nìkī ki tin bàn̄ Giibeeya, Beenjameen tiŋkinee ŋwìiń nìn bíi jēetí.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Bi nìn pāatì Giibeeya tiŋkin niin kí dòon̄ kunyeeu gbanti. Bi nìn kɔ́ kitiŋin ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu, ama báà unil kaa nìn fōō-bi bí kɔ́ kí dòon̄ u-dumpu.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Bi dāa kpēēyee ujaŋkpil ubɔ di nyánní kusaau ki kùnnée. Ujaŋkpil gbanti nìn sá Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi timmu kiban ní, ama ní ki nìn kóò Giibeeya tiŋkin, Beenjameen naakookun yab kansikin.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Ujaŋkpil yáatì u-yil ki ká usaŋkinlee kā kitiŋ punyɔkɔpuee, ní u bālifì-u yii: «A nyánní la ní ki cá la?»

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí ujaŋkpilee yii: «Ti nyánní Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin ní ki cá Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi timmu mun bínní poon poon púee kiban. Niin ní m sá ní ki cūtì Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin ki bàà fàtīi kùǹ dee, ní báà ubɔ kaa fōō-mi ḿ dòon̄ u-dumpu.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ama timool nì tifaal bí tí kpíiǹ ti-mammu. Kpɔnɔ nì ndamam mun bí man nì m-nimpuu nì m-tɔntɔnliu un bíi cēentí-tee ń jī. Tiba nì tiba kaa lóò-ti.»

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Ní ujaŋkpilee bí-u yii: «Ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí a-cee! Man cáá tikɔkɔ ki làá ŋmā kí fōō-ni, ama ní taa pée gbíntí kí dòon̄ kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu doo.»

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ujaŋkpilee nìn cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ u-dumpu ki tīī bi-mammu timool mu ŋmɔ́. Bíǹ bi-ba nìn ká nnyim ki fíntì bi-taaŋi ní ki nìn jíń ki nyùn̄.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bí ki jīǹee ní kitiŋ gbanti nib bin kaa bí tibanee biba dɔ́miń ki māntìi tú dicindi, ki gāā kipunyɔkɔ mpɔn mpɔn ní ki téeń ki bí ujaŋkpilee yii: «Nyāntiń uninja un kɔ́ a-dumpuee doo timbi ń dòon̄ nì u!»

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Ní kudiidaan nyáń ki bí-bi yii: «Aayee, m-nabiyaamu m pée gbāam̀-ni ní, ní taa ŋá tikpitil gbanti. Uninja nee nín gíti dáá kɔ́ man nee, ní taa ŋá-u icoo bɔti gbanti!

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan, man bisal un kaa nyí uninjee bí ní kí kūtì unicaanee nimpuu. M làá nyāntí-bi kí tīī-ni ní dòon̄ nì bi, ní kí ŋá-bi min ni yaa lèe. Ama ní taa ŋá uninja nee pu icoo bɔti min ni là kí ŋá nee!»

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Ama binibee nìn yíì kaa pílifiǹ-u. Niinee ní uleefiijee nyántì u-bɔɔnee mmɔŋki ki tīī-bi. Bi nìn dōoǹ nì u, ki nìn sāaǹ-u míǹ ní kutaa dāa dūu wúntì. An nìn bíi cá kutaawuntuŋuee ní bi gíiǹ-u ki líì.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Kutaa nìn tóob́ kí wúntí ní unimpuee fātìi bāań ujaŋkpil un cee u-cal nìn bée dumpu, ní ki lítì dicindi punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. U nìn dōoǹ niin ní kutaa púntìi wúntì.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl u-cal yíkì ki cūtìi pīitì dicindi punyɔkɔki ki nyáń bí bàà nìkī u-saŋŋuee, u kpēēyee u-bɔɔnee di dɔ̄ee, u-ŋalii nyīī kipunyɔkɔ.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-u yii: «Yīkì tí nīn cá!» Ní an ŋmí kpíii. Niinee ní u bɔ́ ki mɔ̀kɔ̄-u ki dūu páaǹ u-maŋki pu ki cáa nín kùǹ.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: U bàn̄ u-dumpuee ní ki yōoǹ kitàataajiki ki cúú u-bɔɔnee wunti ki càkā anaŋkún saalaa nì ali, ní ki dūu tú bi cáa yākatì Isirayeel naakɔti saalaa nì tilee dinaŋkúndi diba diba.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Uleefiijee nìn tùkū binib bin u nìn túee yii bi yaa bàn̄ Isirayeel yab ceeyee bí lì yii: «Doooo Isirayeel yab nín nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, ni gíti dáá ká tibɔti nee juti jítì dalbaaa? Ní dàkafìmaan tibɔti gbanti pu, kí kpāfì kí sòoǹ kí kpèè ni nín làá ŋāŋkì-tì puee!» Unil un kamaa yaa nìn ká mimmee ní ú lì yii: «Kí pée yòon̄ doooo ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, tibɔti tin bí nee juti kaa láá pée jítì ŋwindal ti-nimbil ká!»

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Ní uleefiija un nimpuu bi nìn kūūyee fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki bí yii: «Man nì m-bɔɔn di nìn pāatì Giibeeya, Beenjameen tiŋkin kí dòon̄ kutaa ń wúntí tí nìkī ti-saŋŋu.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ní m yōoǹ m-bɔɔn dinikpilee ki càkā ki dūu yākatì ki tīī Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ, kun puee binib gbanti ŋá dijɔkɔntundi nì icoo bɔti Isirayeel tiŋkin.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: An puee, Isirayeel yab, ni-kɔkɔ nín kpáfì doo nee, ní sòoǹ kí kpèè ni nín làá ŋá puee.»

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yíkì kii unibaantee ki bí yii: «Ti-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa làá fàtīí gítí u-tantiun, ubɔ kpá ki làá fàtīí gítí u-dumpu.

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Isirayeel janjaliibi kɔkɔ nìn kíí kí kpāfì kii unibaantee kí cù kí já nì Giibeeya yab.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel naakɔti tin kíǹee yab lēē binib ki tú Beenjameen naakooku kɔkɔn bí bàlifì ku-nib yii: «Ba kpitii bulifi ní bi ŋá ni-kansikin mimmee?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní nyāntí binib bin kaa bí tiban ki bí Giibeeya tiŋkinee gbanti kí tīī-ti tí kpɔ̀-bi ní kí nyāntí ikpiti gbanti Isirayeel tiŋkin!» Ama Beenjameen naakookun yab kaa nìn pílifì bi-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee nyɔkɔ.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Beenjameen naakookun yab gbanti nìn yíkìń bi-timmu kɔkɔn ní ki kóoǹní ki kpáfì Giibeeya tiŋkin kí já nì Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní Isirayeel yab yíkì ki cūtìi ŋātì bi-janjanaapaal Giibeeya tiŋki caŋin.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Bi nyáń kí jáǹ Beenjameen naakookun yabee, ki bōoǹ dikɔmbool pu bi-nimbiin túĺ Giibeeya tiŋki.
