english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, Beenjameen naakookun yab nìn nyánní Giibeeya tiŋkin ní ki kūū Isirayeel yab binib kutukub mmuŋku nì bili.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: An yuntiŋuee Piinaasi, Eeliyeeseer jipɔɔn, Aarɔn naantiiu di nìn sá usaraaŋakpil. Isirayeel yab nìn bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «Tí fàtīí gítí kí jáǹ ti-nabiyaamu Beenjameen naakookun yabaaa, tí taa ti cù ní?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí yii: «Ní fàtīí gítímaan kí já nì bi, kun puee fool ní m làá fu dū-bi kí ŋá ni-ŋaan!»

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn lēē bi-janjaliibi biba ki nákáǹ nákáǹ Giibeeya tiŋki ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: but this time they had a different plan. They said, “When the men of Benjamin attack, we will run off and let them chase us away from the town and into the country roads.” The soldiers of Benjamin attacked the Israelite army and started pushing it back from the town. They killed about
translation_verse: Isirayeel janjaliibi nín ká mimmee ní ki fātìi lábitì Beenjameen naakookun yab pu. Beenjameen naakookun yab nín nìn ká nnaabu ŋun jéetì bi-puee, bi-pɔbiliŋ nìn bíil̀ tikpil.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: An puee ní bi nìn fātìi lábitì ki sáǹ ki kátì Isirayeel yab nimbiin, ki dūu túĺ kuteeu watil pú. Ama Isirayeel yab janjaliibi bin nìn bí dipaal puee nìn kā bi-pu, ní bin nìn nyánní kitiŋinee nìn túŋkiń-bi ki kùń-bi ki dòoń.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Isirayeel yab nìn māntìi tú Beenjameen naakookun yab, ki nìn jìn̄-bi kaa pée pú-bi mpaan, ní ki nìn pɔ̄fì-bi míǹ áli ki tin cáa sāā Giibeeya tiŋki nyɔkɔpu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Beenjameen naakookun yab janjaliibi bin Isirayeel yab nìn kūū ŋwiin gbantee nìn kpáfì bijanjaliibi kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo, bi-kɔkɔ bibaatandambi ŋma.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín nìn kpáfì Miisipa tiŋkinee, bi nìn pūtì yii: «Ti-kansikin báà ubɔ ń taa dū u-bisal kí tīī Beenjameen naakookun yab ubɔ ticati.»

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Isirayeel nibul nìn cūtì Beeteel circir paaŋŋu ki kāl̀ kitiŋ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki súń ki yáliŋkì tikpil tikpil áli kujoou dāa dūu jóotì.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí ki lì yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, ba pu ní díǹ pu nee Isirayeel naakɔti kansikin kubɔ ń kúntí míǹ?»

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Kutaa nìn wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, Isirayeel yab nìn máń nsaraafan mpaan gbanti pu ní ki ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bālifì yii: «Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ poonee, kunaakoou kulɔkɔ yab di kaa nìn dɔ́miń dikpafil din ti kpáfì ti-Dindaan nimbiin Miisipa tiŋkinee?» Kun pu bi nìn bālifì mimmee di sá yii bi-kɔkɔ nìn pée pūtì ki pōoǹ yii an sá bí kpɔ̀ unil un kamaa yaa yíì kaa dɔ́miń an kpafil gbantee ní.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Kí kūtì muee, Beenjameen naakookun yab nìn kɔ́ bi-nabiyaamu Isirayeel naakɔti tin kíǹee yab isaa. Bi nìn bí ki lì yii: «Díǹ pu nee Isirayeel naakɔti kansikin kubɔ di bíi wáŋkí nee.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Ti làá ŋá mana ní kí ká binimpoobi kí tīī Beenjameen naakookun yab bininjab bin ŋúń ki sáǹ ki ŋmátì kaa kpíìyee? Kun puee ti gíti dáá pūtì ti-Dindaan u-ba nimbiin ki lī yii taa làá dū ti-bisalib kí tīī-bi ticati.»

english_verse: Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?” After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead.
translation_verse: Bi nín nìn kàan̄ Isirayeel nibul din nìn kóoǹní ki kpáfèe kɔkɔee, bi nìn ká yii binib bin kóò Yabeesi, Galaadi tiŋkinee báà ubɔbɔ ja kaa nìn bí.

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Bi nìn kánní bisapɔmbi bin kaa nyí uninja ki kée binib alaataa anaa Yabeesi, Galaadi tiŋkin ní ki yōoǹní-bi ki cáań Siiloo naapaal pu, Kanaan tiŋkin.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Samaa kɔkɔ nìn lēē binib ki tú Beenjameen naakookun yab bin nìn bí laakin bi yíì yii Riimɔn Taŋkpalee cee. Bi nìn cūtìi tùkū-bi yii kujaau kúntì ŋgbansɔŋfi dōoǹ.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Beenjameen naakookun yab nìn fātìi gítì ki kāl̀ bi-timmu pu, ní Isirayeel naakɔti tin kíǹee yab dū Yabeesi, Galaadi tiŋki nimpoobi bin baa nìn kūūyee ki tīī-bi bi cáá cáá. Ama binimpoobi kaa nìn bàn̄ bi-kɔkɔ ń ká ubɔ ubɔ kí cáá.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nín nìn yāntì Beenjameen naakookun yab paaŋŋu dōoǹ fám Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ kansikinee, bi-bɔti nìn kɔ́ tinaakɔti tin kíǹee yab isaa tikpil.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: An puee ní samaa kɔkɔ kpilib kāl̀ ki sòon̄ ki bí yii: «Too, Beenjameen naakooku poon binimpoobi nín kúntì kɔkɔ pu nee, ti làá ŋá mana ní kí ká binimpoobi kí tīī bininjab bin kíǹee dee?

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: An máaǹ yii Beenjameen naakookun yab bin kíǹee ń fàtīí màal̀ kí bùtī ní bi-naakooku ń taa wāŋkì Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Ni pée nyí yii timbi kaa làá ŋmā kí dū ti-bisalib kí tīī-bi bí cáá, kun puee ti nìn pūtì yii un kamaa di yaa pée dū u-bisal ki tīī Beenjameen naakookun yab ubɔ ticatee, ti làá tɔ̄ udaan mbusu ní.»

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti ní bi nìn téetì yii dibindi kamaayee bi jīǹ ti-Dindaan jiŋaaliu Siiloo tiŋkin. Kitiŋ gbanti nìn bí Beeteel tiŋki ŋgan pú, nsan ŋun yíkí Beeteel tiŋkin ki cá Siikeem tiŋkinee ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, ní ki bí Leeboona tiŋki ŋgiil pú.

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi sáŋkì Beenjameen naakookun yab ki bí-bi yii: «Ní cù kí nákań nákaḿmaan fiinyi sufii boon kí nīn cí!

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa ká Siiloo tiŋki sapɔmbi nóoń tɔb ki nyánní kí kpāfì kí gāā ilan kí ŋɔ̄ diŋoolee, ní dāá nyānní ní ni-kansikin báà ŋma ń dāá cúú Siiloo sapɔmbee ubɔ ubɔ. Báà ŋma ń dāá cáá u-yɔu kí nīn kùǹ u-dumpu Beenjameen naakooku timmun kí dū-u kí kpántí u-nimpuu.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Bisapɔmbee baabi àá bi-niijab yaa dɔ́miń ki nyáfì-ni ti-ceeyee, timbi làá lì-bi yii: <Ní gbìl̄maan kí tīī nì Beenjameen naakookun yab, kun puee timbi kaa ŋúń ki fōō binimpoobi bin nyɔkɔm làá bà bi-kɔkɔ ń ká kí cááyee Yabeesi jaaku poon ki tīī-bi. Ní nimbi ni-ba nín kaa dū ni-bisalib ki tīī-bi bi cááyee, naa yīntì mara.>»

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Beenjameen naakookun yab nìn lafun ŋá bi nín nìn sáŋkì-bi yii bí ŋá puee. Bi nìn lēē binimpoobi bin nyɔkɔm làá tin bà bi-kɔkɔ ń ká ubɔ ubɔ kí cááyee Siiloo sapɔmbi bin nìn nyáń ki ŋɔ́ń ní bi cúú-bee kansikin ki cáa búntì. Bi nìn nín gítí bi-tinjandi pu ní, ki cūtì ki fātìi náań bi-timmu ki kāl̀.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee yíkì dikpafil laŋki ki nóó nì bi-naakɔti nì bi-dicaŋŋi ní bi-kɔkɔ nín gítí bi-tinjaŋŋin.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee bibɔtiibi kaa nìn dá láá bí Isirayeel tiŋkin. Báà ŋma nìn ŋáań min u lèe ní.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Bi nìn yíì uninjee yii Eeliimeeleeki, ki yíì u-nimpuu yii Nawoomii ní ki yíì u-jipɔmbee ubɔ yii Maalɔn ní ki yíì un kíǹee yii Kiiliyɔn. Bi nìn sá Eefiraata maaliŋun nib ní ki kóò Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin. Bi nìn bàn̄ Moowaab yab satinee ní ki gbíntì niin ki kāl̀.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Bi bí niin ní Eeliimeeleeki kpíì ki fá u-nimpuu Nawoomii nì u-jipɔmbi liitil.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Ní u-jipɔmbee cáá bimoowaabisapɔmbi. Bi nìn yíì ubɔ yii Ɔripa ní ki yíì un kíǹee yii Ruuti. Bi nìn kāl̀ Moowaab satin niin an bàn̄ kii abin saalaa nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: An puee ní u yíkì Moowaab tiŋki laakin u nìn kóòyee ki kpáaǹ u-coopoobi. Bi nìn kāl̀ nsan pu kí nīn gítí Juuda tiŋkin.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Bi nyáń nsannee ní Nawoomii bí u-coopoobi liitilee yii: «M-bisalib, nín̄ gítímaan! Báà ŋma ń nīn cá u-na cee. Ti-Dindaan ń ŋá-ni tiŋan kii ni mun nín ŋá man nì ni-calib bin kaa ti bí ti-cee nee tiŋan puee.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ń yàntī ní fàtīí ká ticamɔntiil, ni-kansikin báà ŋma ń ká diŋuŋfil kucadiin.» Nawoomii lī mimmee ní ki kpàl̄ u-coopoobi liitil ki kāaǹ-bi. Ama ní u-coopoobi kíĺ ki bíi sūǹ mpɔn,

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: ní ki bí-u yii: «Kpáb! Timbi làá nóó-si ní kí cù a-yab cee.»

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Ní Nawoomii bí-bi yii: «Nín̄ gítímaan, m-bisalib! Ba pu ní ní nīn gbíntìi nóó-mi? M nín bí pu nee, m gíti ŋūǹ kí màal̀ mbininjabiyaamu mú cáá-naaa?

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: ní ki yaa lafun ŋá míǹ, ni làá kíí kí kàl̄ kí cīití-mu mú dāá wíiǹaaa? Ni làá nīn kā ki cí-mu míǹ mú wíiǹ kí dāá cáá-ni, kaa làá nyàab̀ bininjab kí mɔ̄ǹaaa? Aayee, m-bisalib! Man falaau gíti lákatì tikpil nì nimbi yɔu, kun puee ti-Dindaan u-ba di gbáń-mi.»

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Ní Nawoomii bí-u yii: «Kpèè, a-yɔnti úǹ nín gítí u-yab nì u-nimbɔtii cee. Sii mun páań u-boon ní nīn gítí!»

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Ní Ruuti kíí-u yii: «Taa páb́-mi yii ḿ nīn cá kí dū-si kí fá. Laakin a làá cùee, niin ní ma mun làá cù. Laakin a làá kɔ́ee, niin ní ma mun làá kɔ́. A-nibul làá nīn sá m-nibul, ní a-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn sá m-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: Laakin a làá kpúee, niin ní ma mun làá kpú ní bí síb́-mi niin. Ŋkúm baba di làá yàkatī man nì sii kansikin. An yaa kaa ŋá míǹ, ti-Dindaan ń dáaĺ m-tafal kí gíti dáaĺ m-tafal.»

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Nawoomii nín ká yii Ruuti dáá pée gbíntìi cɔ́ yii u làá nīn nóó-u ki cée, ní u ŋmíl̀ kaa ti gātì-u báà tiba.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Ní Ruuti nì Nawoomii liitil nóó ki tin kɔ́ Beetileem tiŋkin. Bi nín bàn̄ ki kɔ́ Beetileem tiŋkin bi ká-bee ní an ŋá binib kɔkɔ yèeee, ní binimpoobi kíǹ ki bàlifī tɔb yii: «Mimmee Nawoomii lafun sɔ̀ɔɔ?»

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Ní Nawoomii bí-bi yii: «Ní taa ti yíiń-mi yii Nawoomii! Ní nīn kíǹ ki yíì-mi yii Maara, kun puee Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan yāntì m-nyɔkɔ túŋkì!

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Di sá yii nì digbíl ní m nìn búntì, ama ní ti-Dindaan fātìi gíiǹní-mi nì iŋaŋkulim. Ní taa ti yíiń-mi yii Nawoomii, kun puee ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ ki kūū m-bɔti ní ki yāntì m kpántì unandaan.»

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: An kútì fiiiyee ní Boowaasi nyánní Beetileem kitiŋin ki bāań, ní ki jáam̀ bijincaliibi yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń nīn bí ni-cee!» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ a-boon!»

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Ní Boowaasi bālifì u-tɔntɔnliu un kpèé bijincaliibee yii: «Kin unimpusapɔɔn nee úǹ sá ŋma?»

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔnli un kpèé bijincaliibee kíí-u yii: «An sá kimoowaabibiki kin nóoń Nawoomii ki nyánní Moowaab satinee.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: U dɔ́miń ní ki mēē nsan ki lī yii: <M bàà là kí páań bijincaliibi boon kí nīn lúlifí tijin tin kīntí bi-boonee.> Doooo kutaafaau u nín pée bāań ki yú puee ní u yú nee. Waa ŋman pée kɔ́ ki kāl̀ kibiŋ taapu kí ŋùŋfì gba!»

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Niinee ní Boowaasi bí Ruuti yii: «Pīlifì m-bisal! Á taa lì yii a làá gíti cù kusaau kubɔn kí lūlifì tijin, kí taa pée sútí kí cù laaba gba. Á gbíntí m-saakun doo kí dū a-ba kí nákáǹ m-sapɔmbi.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Nín̄ pée kpèé bijincaliibi nín cēē ki cá puee ní kí nīn pá bisapɔmbi boon ki lúlifí. M kpáafì m-naacimpɔmbi yii bí yàntī á nīn lúlifí, bí taa páb́-si! Nnyinnyoo yaa cáá-see, á cù kí jōō nnyim min bitɔntɔnliibi lúń ki sītì aboonnee kí nyɔ̀.»

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Ruuti gbāaǹ Boowaasi nimbiin ki tīntì u-yil taapu taapu ní ki bālifì-u yii: «Mana ní a kíí ki dàkā man un sá kinicambiki nee kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ki ŋá-mi tiŋan míǹ na?»

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Ní Boowaasi kíí-u yii: «Bi pée máafì-mi tiŋan tin kɔkɔ a ŋá ki tīī a-beel doooo a-cal nín lántì dimaŋfalee. M gbìl̄ a nín kíí ki fá a-baa nì a-na ki yíkìń kitiŋ kin pu bi màl̄-see, ki nóoń a-beel ki nín dòoń u-tiŋki kin ní saa láá pée nyí ki ká ŋwindalee poonee.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di làá pà-si tiŋan tin a ŋée paati! Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un a sáǹní ki dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ nee ń téeǹ-si tiŋan tin kɔkɔ a ŋá ki tīī a-beelee!»

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Ruuti fātìi bí-u yii: «Ukpil, a ŋá-mi tiŋan tikpilku. Á nīn pée ŋúb́-mi míǹ, á taa dū-mi kí fá! Di sá yii a sòon̄ nì man a-tɔntɔnliu an kɔ́-mi, ki tīī-mi kunyannyaau, ki sɔ̄ŋkì m-pɔbil. Ama maa kpáàa bàn̄ a-tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi kansikin báà ubɔ gba!»

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋmāntì bi làá jī tijinee ní Boowaasi bí Ruuti yii: «Dāan̄ kí kàl̄ tí jī tijin. Dāá gíí kpɔnɔ kí sēē tikun kí ŋmɔ́.» Niinee ní Ruuti cūtìi kāl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ bijincaliibi ní Boowaasi lēē ɔɔji fiŋyi in bi púĺee ki tīī-u. Ruuti fōō ki ŋmēem̀ ki ŋmɔ́ ki díkí ní an kíǹ, ní u dūu kpáafì.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Ruuti jíń tijin ki dóòyee ní ki yíkìi nìkī ki bíi lúlifí. Ní Boowaasi tīī u-naacimbi mara ki lī-bi yii: «Ní yàntī ú nīn lúlifí ki kpáaǹ ni nín cēē ɔɔji ki bīil̀ ipɔ̀n pu kí dāá nín kóoǹee kansikin, ní taa pée lì-u tiba an bīil̀ u-pɔbil.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Ní nīn lèekī ifin in ni cēē ki bīil̀ kí dāá nín kóoǹee iba gba ki bīil̀-u ú nīn yòontí, ní taa wòoǹ-u.»

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Ruuti gbíntì Boowaasi saakun ki lúlifì ní ŋwìiń dāa dūu jéetì. U nìn gbáń ɔɔji un u lúlifèe kɔkɔ ki cāatì ki ŋmāntì, ní ki ká kii asambil saalku nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: U yōoǹ ki túǹ ki cáa nín kùǹ mmɔŋki ní ki bàn̄ ki dūu dàkā u-beel Nawoomii, ní ki dū tijin tin u jíń ki kíǹee mun ki tīī-u.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Ní u-beel bālifì-u yii: «La ní a lúlifìń mimmee? La ní a cūtìi túń ditundi díǹ ní? Unimbɔti ń bìin̄ udaan un súń a-saayee boon!» Ní Ruuti tùkū u-beel unil un cee u cūtì ki túń ditundi yaadal gbantee ki lī yii: «Uninja un cee m túń ditundi díǹ neeyee yindi di sá Boowaasi.»

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Nawoomii bí u-coopu yii: «Ti-Dindaan un dàkà timbi binifoobi ki kpáaǹ bitaŋkpiibi u-ŋanti kaa gbèentée ń bìin̄ unil gbanti boon!» U lī mimmee ní ki kútì yii: «Uninja gbanti sá ti-niliu ubɔ ní. U sá ti-dicaŋku poon bin bin cáá nsan kí fōō-ti kí ŋúb́ee kansikin ubɔ ní.»

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Ní Ruuti kimoowaabibiki fātìi kūbitì ki bí yii: «U gíti lī-mi yii: <Á dū a-ba kí nákáǹ m-tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi kí taa pée sútí ki wàatī-bi kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun bi làá cā m-kpaajinti kɔkɔ kí dóóyee.>»

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Nawoomii bí u-coopu Ruuti yii: «Tiŋman ní, m-bisal! Pée dū a-ba kí nákáǹ u-tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi kí taa cù unifantanti ubɔ saakun bi dāa ŋáań-si ntoom.»

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ní Ruuti gbíntì Boowaasi tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi cee ki lúlifì tijin ní bi dāa cáń ɔɔji nì bilee ki dóò. U nìn pée gbíntìi kóò u-beel Nawoomii cee ní.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Ruuti beel Nawoomii bí-u yii: «M-bisal, m ká yii m máaǹ kí tūtuǹ-si á ká ŋkakaamɔnti kucadiin kí kàl̄ a-pɔbil ń nīn sɔ̀m̀.

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Kéè a téetí Boowaasi un kíí ki yāntì sii nì u-tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi kpáfì u-saakun ki túń ditundi, ti nì u pēēyeeyaa! Too, kunyeeu nee ní uninja gbanti làá càatī ɔɔji un bi cáń-uee u-naapaal pu.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: An puee á fàl̀ kí bɔ́ntí a-ba, kí dū a-wampeeŋkaati timɔntiil kí pèen̄, kí yàaǹ a-ba pu talaalu ní kí sìntī u-naapaal din pu u cēē u-jinti ki bīil̀ee. Ama á taa yàntī ú béé a-pu kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní u yaa jíń ki nyùn̄ ki dóòyee.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: U yaa dōoǹee á dáań tiŋan kí béé laakin u dɔ̄ee. U yaa gèen̄ee á ŋá soooo kí cùú wákatí sata kí bìitī u-taaŋi pu ní kí dòon̄ kí kɔ́ĺ-u u-taaŋi taapu niin. Úǹ u-ba làá tùkù-si a nín làá ŋá puee.»

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Ní Ruuti nín sìntī Boowaasi naapaal pu ki bàn̄ ki ŋá min min u-beel kpáafì-u yii ú ŋée deedeedee.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Boowaasi jíń ki nyùn̄ an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u tiŋanee ní u cūtìi dōoǹ tijikaal tin u kóoǹ ki kpúkuǹee caŋin. U dōoǹee ní Ruuti ŋá soooo ki cūtìi cúú sata ki wákatì ní ki dōoǹ u-taaŋi taapu.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Kunyataasiiuee ní an ŋá Boowaasi nyàaa ní u yùkū ki fīntì. U kpēēyee unimpu di dɔ̄ u-taaŋi taapuee.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Ní u bālifì yii: «An sá sii ŋma?» Ní Ruuti kíí-u yii: «An sá man a-tɔntɔnliu Ruuti. M dɔ́miń kí kɔ́-si ní. Kíí kí fōō-mi kí nīn ŋúb́. Di sá yii a sá m-cal nabiyaamu mun cáá nsan kí fōō-mi kí ŋúb́ee kansikin ubɔ ní.»

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Boowaasi fātìi bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ a-boon, m-bisal! Min a bíi ŋáań nee dàkà dineendi din a cáá a-cal dicaŋku puee ki jítiǹ min a nìn ŋá mpeepeekaamee. Di sá yii aa dū a-landɔkɔŋu ki tɔ́ binaacimpɔmbi bin cáá tigaajatee àá bin kaa cááyee pu.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Tiŋman ní m lafun sá a-niliu ki bàà cáá nsan kí fōō-si kí ŋúb́, ama kinabiki kiba bí u nì a-cal gíti pēē kiŋkiŋ ki jítiǹ mama.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Gbíntí doo kí dòon̄ kunyeeu nee, fool kutaafaauee m làá fu sòoǹ nì u kí kpèè. U yaa fu kíí kí fōō-saaa, an ŋān̄ ú fōō-si. Ama u yaa fu yíì yii waa làá fōō-see, nì Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee yindi pu, man làá fōō-si! An puee, gbíntí doo kí dòon̄ kutaa ń púntíí wúntí!»

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Ní Boowaasi bí Ruuti yii: «Lēē a-bɔkutipaaŋkaal kí cúú kpátí kí bíĺ yéè!» Ní Ruuti cúú u-bɔkutipaaŋkaal ki lēē ní ki kpátì ki bíl̀. Ní Boowaasi màkā ɔɔji biliŋ asambiŋmantikaa aluu pu ki sītì-u, ki yōoǹ ki túǹ-u ní u nín cá kitiŋin.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: U máafì ki dóòyee ní ki bí yii: «Úǹ di tīī-mi ɔɔji biliŋ asambiŋmantikaa aluu nee ki bí-mi yii: <Án kaa máaǹ yii á fàtīí gítí a-beel cee nì iŋaŋkulim.>»

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Nawoomii bí-u yii: «M-bisal, kàl̄ soooo kí kpèè tibɔti nee nín làá kúntí puee. Uninja gbanti yaa kaa kpēē tibɔti nee nín sá puee díǹ wiiŋŋu nee, u-pɔbil kaa làá sɔ̀ŋkì!»

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: An yuntiŋuee Boowaasi nìn nín jɔ́ḿ kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu ki cūtìi kāl̀ niin. Kpalaayee kinabiki kin nì Eeliimeeleeki pēē kiŋkiŋ, Boowaasi sòon̄ u-bɔtee di jītée. Ní u yíiń-u ki bí yii: «Kinabiki, pàatīń kí dāá kàl̄ yéèyaa!» Ní kijapaayee pāatì ki kāl̀.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Ní Boowaasi yíiń bitindaŋkpilib kansikin binib saalaa ní ki bí bi mun yii: «Ní kàl̄maan doo!» Ní bi mun kāl̀.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Ní u bí uninja un nì Eeliimeeleeki pēē kiŋkiŋee yii: «Nawoomii nyánní Moowaab satin ki fātìi bāań ki bíi nyáfí ti-nabiki Eeliimeeleeki kpaatanti.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Ní m bí yii m máaǹ kí yàntī á gbìl̄ ní kí kpáàá kpòotī-si yii á kíí kí fōō tikpaatan gbanti bitindaŋkpilib nì binib bin bí doo nee kɔkɔ nimbiin. A yaa kíí ki làá fōō, á fōō. A yaa tí nyí yii aa là kí fōō, á tùkù-mi ḿ nīn nyí, kun puee sii di sá upeekaa ki cáá nsan kí fōō tikpaatan gbanti, sii boonee man di pá.» Ní kijapaayee kíí Boowaasi yii: «Iiin, m kíí ki làá fōō!»

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Ní Boowaasi bí-u yii: «Daliŋkin ní a làá fōō kusaau gbanti Nawoomii ŋaanee, á nīn nyí yii a fōō ki kpáaǹ kimoowaabibiki Ruuti ukpiipu dee, u-cal un kaa ti bí ti-kansikinee yindi ń taa kúntí, ní u-kpaatanti tin sá u-fakalee ń gbíntí u-naakookun kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní kijapaayee bí Boowaasi yii: «An yaa sée man kaa làá ŋmā kí fōō. Di sá yii m-kpátam boonee, án dāa ŋūǹ kí cáań digìńdi mama m-ba fakal pu. Míǹ puee a ŋūǹ kí yūĺ man yil pu kí fōō ti-nabiki wanti tin man bàà cáá nsan ki jítiǹ sii kí fōōyee, man kaa ti làá ŋmā kí fōō-tì!»

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: An pu ní kijapaayee nín tùkū Boowaasi yii u ŋūǹ kí yūĺ úǹ yil pu kí fōō bi-nabiki wantee, u tákatì u-naatakal diba ki dūu tīī Boowaasi.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Boowaasi bí bitindaŋkpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ yii: «Ni-kɔkɔ sá biseeradambi díǹ wiiŋŋu nee yii m fōō Nawoomii ŋaan Eeliimeeleeki nì u-jipɔmbi Maalɔn nì Kiiliyɔn wanti kɔkɔ kí nīn ŋúb́.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: M fōō ki kpáaǹ Ruuti kimoowaabibiki, Maalɔn nimpuu ukpiipu, utaŋkpiil wanti ń gbíntí u-naakookun ní u-yindi ń taa wāŋkì u-nabiyaamu kansikin, kí taa wāŋkì u-tiŋki punyɔkɔpu mun. Ni sá biseeradambi díǹ wiiŋŋu nee yii m lafun ŋá mimmaaa?»

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ní bitindaŋkpilibee nì samaa un kpáfì kitiŋ punyɔkɔpuee kɔkɔ kíí-u yii: «Iiin, ti sá biseeradambi yii a ŋá míǹ! Ti-Dindaan ń yàntī unimpu un a làá fōō ú kɔ́ a-dicaŋkun nee ń nīn sá kii Raseel nì Leeya bin liitil náań Isirayeel nibulee. Ti mèé yii á kpántí unikpaan Eefiraata tiŋkin ní kí nyā diyiŋkpaandi Beetileem tiŋki kɔkɔn.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Mbiyaamu mun ní ti-Dindaan làá yàntī unimpusapɔɔn gbanti ń màal̀ kí tīī-see puee, a-naakooku ń nīn sá kii Peereesi un un Taamaar nìn màl̄ ki tīī Juudayee naakooku!» Ruuti màl̄ kibininjabiki ki tīī Nawoomii

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ní Beetileem nimpoobi bí Nawoomii yii: «Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan! Díǹ pu nee waa ŋmīntì-si un làá dāá ŋúb́-si fool boonee. U làá dāá nyā diyindi Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn!

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Úǹ di làá yàntī a-bimbim ń kpántí a-maŋfal wiiŋyi in poon a bí nee, ní kí dāá nīn kpèé-si a-puti poon fool boon. An sá a-coopu un néeń-si tikpil, ki jítiǹ jipɔmbi biluli puee di màl̄ naantiiu gbanti ki tīī-si.»

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Ní Nawoomii yōoǹ kibikee ki péé u-taaŋi pu ki kíĺ ki bíi lòó-kì.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Ní u-nimpujutiibi sòon̄ ki nāatì tɔb kibikee bɔti ki lī yii: «Bi màl̄ kibininjabiki ki tīī Nawoomii!» Bi nìn pú kibikee diyindi yii Oobeedi. Úǹ di dāa màl̄ Isayi, Daafiidi baa. Daafiidi naanjab yiŋŋi

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Uninja ubɔ nìn bí bi yíì-u yii Eelkana. U nìn kóò Raama Suufi tiŋkin, Eefiraayiim jooŋŋin. U nìn sá Eefiraayiim naakookun ní. Bi nìn yíì u-baa yii Jeeroowaam ní ki yíì u-naanjab yii Suufi nì Toowu nì Eeliiwuu.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: U nìn cáá binimpoobi bili: bi yíì ubɔ yii Aana ní ki yíì un kíǹee yii Peeniina. Peeniina nìn cáá mbiyaamu, ama Aana úǹ kaa nìn cáá.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Dibindi kamaayee, Eelkana nìn yíkí Raama kí cù Siiloo kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī-u. Eelii nìn cáá jipɔmbi bili, Oofinii nì Fineeyaasi. Bi nìn bí niin ki sá ti-Dindaan saraaŋaliibi.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Eelkana yaa nìn ŋá saraayee, u nín nìn ŋáań puee di sá u nìn lèekī u-nimpuu Peeniina yati kí tīī-u, ní kí lēē u-jipɔmbi nì u-bisalib yati kí tīī-bi.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Ama u nìn tìì Aana dijandi din ŋān̄ tikpilee, di sá yii u nìn néeń-u tikpil, nì min kamaa ti-Dindaan kaa nìn pú-u mmaalee.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: U-yɔnti Peeniina nìn pée nyàab̀-u tibɔti kí kɔ́ǹ-u diŋuul, kun puee Unimbɔti kaa nìn pú-u mmaal.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Abintil kɔkɔee, míǹ ní an nìn bí. Aana yaa nìn pée cūtì ti-Dindaan circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee, Peeniina nìn pée nyàab̀-u tibɔti ní. Bi tí cūtì dibindi dibee ní Aana bíi sūǹ kaa là tijin.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Ní u-cal bālifì-u yii: «Aana, ba ŋá-si ní a sūǹ kaa là tijin ní? Ba yì-tì ní a bí kunimbaaun míǹ? Mimmee maa jítiǹ jipɔmbi saalaa pu a-ceeee?»

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Bi jíń ki nyùn̄ míǹ ki dóò Siiloo tiŋkinee, ní Aana yíkì ki cūtìi bíi mèé. Usaraaŋakpil Eelii nìn kā u-jal pu circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Aana nìn bí kunimbaakpaaŋŋun. U nìn bíi mèé ti-Dindaan ki sūǹ lòoloo.

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: U nìn pōoǹ ti-Dindaan yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, kpèè man a-tɔntɔnliu falaau. Téetí m-pu, taa súntí m-pu. A yaa tīī-mi kibininjabikee, m làá dū-kì kí sú sii ti-Dindaan ní. Ki-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, bɔlfi kpá kí gbēē ki-yikpiti.»

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Aana kaa nìn sòoǹ anyɔɔbun nyēē. U-nyunculiŋ di nìn pée tábití, di sá yii u nìn mèé u-pɔbilin ní. Eelii nìn dākafì yii u gbí ndaam ní.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Eelii nìn bí-u yii: «Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a-daam nee làá cèetī-si ní? Kpáaǹ a-danyɔgbibɔtee kí nyā doo!» -

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Taa dū man a-tɔntɔnliu kí yíiń kunimpufaŋu. Kunimbaau nì takaasi di gíti lákatì m-pu, an pu ní m mēē ki yúntì míǹ.»

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Eelii kíí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá nì ŋgbansɔŋfi, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ń tīī-si tin a mēē-uee.» -

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Ní Aana kíí-u yii: «Ḿ pée ká diyimɔɔl a-cee di sá.» U lī mimmee ní ki kíĺ u-saŋŋu. U bàn̄ee ní ki jíń tijin ní u-nimbiin cúu kpántì.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Ku wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní Eelkana nì u-dicaŋku péé ki cūtì ki gbāaǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki jáam̀-u, ní ki nín fàtī bi-dumpu Raama tiŋkin. Samiyeel màaltam nì u-biyati Eelkana nì u-nimpuu Aana kpáfì ní ti-Dindaan fōō u-wimmeem.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Aana cáá dipool ní ki màl̄ kibininjabiki. U nìn pú-kì diyindi yii Samiyeel, di sá u lī yii: «M mēē-kì ti-Dindaan cee ní.»

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee Eelkana nì u-dicaŋku kɔkɔ gítì Siiloo kí cùú ŋá dibindi kamaa saraau, nì ipoon in u nìn pōoǹee saraau.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Ama min bí nee, Aana kaa nìn táá u-cal ki cūtì. U nìn tùkū-u yii: «M làá cīití m yaa gíí kibiki dibiilee ní ḿ cáá-kì kí cùnnì Siiloo kí tīī ti-Dindaan, ní kí nīn kíǹ ki bí niin jaanjaan.»

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Ní u-cal Eelkana kíí-u yii: «An ŋān̄, ŋá min a ká yii an ŋān̄ee. Kàl̄ doo kí cīití ŋyunti ŋun a yaa láa gíí-kì dibiilee. Tin bée di sá ti-Dindaan nín pōoǹ puee, ú ŋá míǹ.» Ní Aana kāl̀ Raama ki lōō u-biki áli ki dāa gíí-kì dibiil.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Aana nìn bí Eelii yii: «Ukpil m gbāam̀-si, ibaamɔn ní m làá sòoǹ, man di sá unimpu un nìn dɔ́miń dalba doo ki yú a-caŋin ki mèé ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Kibiki nee ní m nìn mèé ki nyàab̀ee. Ti-Dindaan tīī-mi kun m nìn mèé ki nyàab̀ee.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Ma mun dū-kì ki sú ti-Dindaan. Ki-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, kì làá nīn pée sá ti-Dindaan yɔu ní.» Ní Eelkana nì u-dicaŋku gbāaǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin niin ki jáam̀-u.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Niinee Aana mēē Unimbɔti yii: «Ti-Dindaan puee, m-pɔbil píil̀. Ti-Dindaan puee, m còom̄ m-yil gáań, m ŋūǹ kí lā m-nannanliibi. M bí ki fàal̀ dijajil din ti-Dindaan tīī-mee pu.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Ubɔ kpá ki bí circir ki bàn̄ ti-Dindaan. Ti-Nimbɔtiu boonee, ubɔ kaa ti bí. Ti-Nimbɔtiu baba di sá kutaŋkpanaakoou.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Ní taa nín̄ sòoǹ ki bùsī dibayoondi nyɔɔbuŋŋi. Timɔn nyɔɔbuŋŋi ń taa nín̄ nyēē ni-nyɔmmun. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan sá Unimbɔti un nyí tikɔkɔee ní, úǹ di ŋmàntī ki nyí báà ŋma tuuŋŋi nín sá puee.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Bin nìn jīǹ ki díkèe bíi nyàab̀ atuun kí tɔ̄ kí ká kí jī. Ama bin ŋkùm nìn cááyee kā ki ŋùŋfī. Uŋmaŋŋmanti màl̄ mbiyaamu mululi, ama un nìn màl̄ mbiyaamu tikpilee maaliŋu gúń.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di yàntī unil kúù, úǹ di tí tìì unil dimaŋfal. U yàntī unil ń sìntī ditaŋkpiilin, ki tí yàntī ú jɔ̄mìń.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di kɔ̄ntí unil disoolin, úǹ di tí tìì-u tigaajati. Úǹ di sìntī unil taapu, úǹ di tí yòontí-u yilpu.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: U yòontí unandaan ntampukumin, ki nyāntí ufalaadaan titampummoolin, kí cáá-bi kí kàan̄ bɔtiijab kansikin jilma paaŋŋu pu. Ti-Dindaan di yì kitiŋ kɔkɔ, úǹ di dū-kì ki tɔ́kɔǹ u-jaantalkub pu.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: U wúǹ bin yú nì u deedeeyee pu, ama binikpitib làá kpú dibɔmbɔndin. Kun puee an kaa sá unil pɔŋŋu pu ní u jáà ki jīǹ.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī utaa ń nyānní yilpu kí tɔ̄ kí yàaǹ u-nannanliibi. Ti-Dindaan làá dāá sòoǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ bɔti. U làá dāá tīī u-bɔtiu mpɔn, kí dāá yòon̄ ubɔti un u lēēyee yilpu.»

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Eelkana nín gítí u-dumpu Raama. Ama Samiyeel úǹ nìn gbíntì Siiloo, usaraaŋakpil Eelii cee, kí nīn tūǹ ti-Dindaan tundi. Eelii jipɔmbi bɔti

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi gbanti nín nìn ŋáań puee sèé. Ubɔ yaa nìn ŋá saraayee, usaraaŋal tɔntɔnliu nìn dòoń ŋyunti ŋun ní bi càkā tinan ki tɔ́kɔǹee, ki ŋúb́ kijiii kin cáá anyin atee.

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: U nìn dù kijiiyee kí sāā tinan tin kā disambitɔkɔŋkaalin àá dikumboolin àá sirban àá daanseeyee kí lēeń tinan tin an yaa pée sāāyee kí cáań usaraaŋal. Míǹ ní Eelii jipɔmbi nìn ŋáań Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn cá Siiloo Circir Kɔŋkooŋŋunee.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Tin bi nìn ŋáań an gíti lákatèe di sá baa láá dū tiwaŋkuti kpam ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki tīī ti-Dindaan ní usaraaŋal tɔntɔnliu ń bàń kí bí yii: «Tīī-mi tinan ḿ cáá ŋɔ̄fì kí tīī usaraaŋal. Waa làá kíí kí fōō a-cee tinantɔkɔŋkaal, see tikaal baba.»

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Bi yaa bí-u yii: «Yàntī tí dū ŋkpam kí wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaan kí wàatī á nín lēē tin a yaa lèe», ní utɔntɔnlee ń bí yii: «Kpataaa, an pée sá á tīī-mi kɔŋkɔnnee ní, an yaa kaa sá míǹ, m làá lēē-tì mpɔn ní.»

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Eelii jipɔmbee nìn ŋáań ikpitikpaan ti-Dindaan nimbiin, kun puee baa nìn tɔ́ saraabi bin bi nìn ŋáań ki tìì ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Samiyeel úǹ nìn pēē gulfa un bí fálfalee bɔkutipaaŋkaaki, ki bí ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki tūǹ u-tundi. Samiyeel dicaŋku bɔti

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Dibindi kamaayee, Samiyeel na nìn ŋál̀-u dibɔkutil ní. U nìn cáǹ-dì ki tìì-u ŋyunti ŋun ní u nì u-cal yaa nìn cá Siiloo kí ŋá dibindi kamaa saraauee.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Eelii nìn mèé ki bìintí Eelkana nì u-nimpuu pu. U nìn mèé yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń yàntī a-nimpuu nee ń gíti màal̀-si mbiyaamu kí téeǹ kin a dūu sú ti-Dindaanee.» Míǹ boonee ní bí fàtīí nín kùǹ bi-dumpu.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bīiǹ Aana boon ní u gíti màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muta nì nnimpubiyaamu muli. An yaa kíǹ Samiyeelee, u nìn bí ti-Dindaan tundin ní ki wīintí. Eelii wòon̄ u-jipɔmbi

english_verse: Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Eelii nìn púĺ tikpil. U nìn gbìl̄ u-jipɔmbi nín bí ki ŋáań Isirayeel yab puee. U nìn gíti gbìl̄ yii bi mɔ̀nnì binimpoobi bin dòoń ki tūǹ Circir Kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu atuunee.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: M-biyaamu, fámaan mbimbim gbanti! Tin m gbìl̀ ti-Dindaan nikitil sòoǹ ni-puee kaa ŋān̄ báà fiii.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Unil ubɔ yaa yīntiǹ u-jutee, Unimbɔti di pɔ̀, ama unil yaa yīntiǹ ti-Dindaanee, ŋma di làá pɔ̀?» Ama baa pée dū tin bi-baa sòon̄ nì bee ki túń ditundi. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn lēē kí kpɔ̀-bi ní.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Samiyeel nìn wīintí ní ki nìn mɔ̀tīi fáatiǹ ti-Dindaan nì binib. Eelii nì u-jipɔmbi tafadaaldi

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ dɔ́miń ki ká Eelii ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Ŋyunti ŋun a-naanjab nìn bí kuyuŋun Faaroo ŋaan Eejipiti tiŋkinee, m nìn lēē m-ba ki dàkā-bi.

english_verse: Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar. But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní ni kpèé tiwaŋkuti saraabi nì saraabi bin kíǹ m tīī mara yii bí nīn ŋáań m-kɔŋkooŋŋunee fám míǹ? Ba pu ní a tīī a-jipɔmbi jilma ki jítiǹ man? Di sá yii m-nibul Isirayeel yab nín cāabìń-mi tin kɔkɔ ki ŋáań saraayee, ni lēē dijandi din ŋān̄ee ki jíń ki gbīfiǹ.

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu lī yii: <M nìn pōoǹ yii a-dicaŋkun yab nì a-baa dicaŋkun yab làá nīn pée sá m-saraaŋaliibi ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, man ni-Dindaan sòon̄ yii an kaa ti sá míǹ. Di sá yii bin tìì-mi jilmee, m tìì-bi jilma ní, bin kpèé-mi fámee, ma mun kpèé-bi fám ní.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋubɔ dòoń m làá dāá kúntí kun sá sii nì a-baa dicaŋku pɔŋŋuee, ní taa ti ŋmā kí ká ujaŋkpil ni-cindin.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti kamaayee, a làá nīn bí kunimbaaun ní. Án làá bútí Isirayeel yab tikɔkɔ poon, ama a-dicaŋkun binicikitikaabi kaa làá nīn gíti bí.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m làá yàntī a-dicaŋkun yɔu ubɔ ń nīn gbíntìi bí ki tūǹ ditundi m-saraafaŋŋu pu. An dāa sá kí yàntī án nīn wù-si pɔ̀lpɔl kí kɔ́ kí dóó-si ní. Ama a-dicaŋkun yab bin kɔkɔ kíǹee làá dāá kpú.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: «Tin làá bàń a-jipɔmbi Oofinii nì Fineeyaasi puee di làá nīn sá-si kudaaŋŋu, bi-liitil làá kpú ŋwimbaanti ní.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Boonee, m làá dāá lēē usaraaŋal un bí deedeeyee. U làá dāá ŋá tin m-pɔbil fáatèe nì m nín là puee. Úǹ di làá dāá ŋá tin fáatì m-pɔbilee. M làá dāá yàntī u-naantiibi ń nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibi kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ní kí nīn bí ki kɔ́ĺ ubɔti un m làá dāá lēēyee.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Un làá dāá kíń a-dicaŋkun kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee làá dāá cù kí gbàan̄ usaraaŋal nimbiin ki nyàab̀ animbil jitɔn àá kikpɔnɔkatii. U làá dāá tùkù-u yii: <M gbàam̄-si, pée fōō-mi kí ŋá disaraaŋal tundi diba poon ḿ ŋmā kí nīn kāntí tiba poon fiii ki jīǹ.>»

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Samiyeel mun nìn dɔ̄ ti-Dindaan Diikun, laakin Unimbɔti dakaau yúee. Unimbɔti fitilau kaa nìn dáá kpíì.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yíiń Samiyeel, ní u kíí yii: «M sèé».

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Ní u sáǹ ki nín cá Eelii cee ki bí-u yii: «A nín yíiń-mee, m sèé.» Ní Eelii bí-u yii: «Maa yíiń-si, nín̄ gítí kí cùú dòon̄.» Ní Samiyeel nín gítí ki cūtìi dōoǹ.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan fātìi yíiń Samiyeel nliliitiim. Ní Samiyeel yíkì ki nín gítí Eelii cee, ki bí-u yii: «A nín yíiń-mee, m sèé.» Ní Eelii bí-u yii: «Maa yíiń-si m-biki, nín̄ gítí kí cùú dòon̄.»

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Samiyeel kaa nìn dáá nyí ti-Dindaan, di sá waa nìn dáá pée sòon̄ nì u ki ká.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan gíti yíiń Samiyeel ntataatiim ní Samiyeel yíkì ki nín cá Eelii cee ki bí-u yii: «A nín yíiń-mee, m sèé!» Niinee Eelii nín béè yii an sá ti-Dindaan di bíi yíì kibiki.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Ní Eelii bí Samiyeel yii: «Nín̄ gítí kí cùú dòon̄, u yaa ti yíiń-see, á lì yii: <Nín̄ sòoǹ, ti-Dindaan, man a-tɔntɔnliu pílifí!>» Ní Samiyeel nín gítí ki cūtìi dōoǹ laakin u pée dɔ̀ee.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn dɔ́miń ki lēē u-bítam ki dàkā. Kii u nín bàà pée bíi yíì-u puee, u nìn tí yíiń-u yii: «Samiyeel! Samiyeel!» Ní Samiyeel kíí-u yii: «Nín̄ sòoǹ, man a-tɔntɔnliu pílifí.»

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Samiyeel yii: «M làá ŋá tiba Isirayeel tiŋkin, ní án làá kɔ́ǹ un kamaa yaa gbìl̄-tèe dinyoondi.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: M tùkū Eelii ki síiǹ, m sòon̄ ki kūū u-dicaŋkun yab bɔti kí nīn pée cá, kun puee u nyí u-jipɔmbi nín bí ki kpèé man Unimbɔti fámee ní u ŋmí kaa dáaĺ bi-tafal.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: An pu ní m pūtì yii báà Eelii dicaŋkun yab yaa yāntì ki ŋá tiwaŋkuti saraabi àá saraabi bin kíǹee min min, án kpá kí pítí bi-kpitii.»

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Samiyeel gbíntìi dɔ̄ míǹ ní kutaa wúntì, ní u yíkìi pīitì ti-Dindaan diiku punyɔmmu. Samiyeel nìn fàŋkí kí tùkù Eelii tin u kée.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ní Eelii yíiń Samiyeel ní ki bí-u yii: «Samiyeel, m-jipɔɔn!» Ní u kíí-u yii: «M sèé!»

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Ní u bālifì-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan tùkū-si yii ba ní? Á taa báĺ-mi báà tiba! A yaa bál̀-mi kubɔbambaantiiu, Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ a-tafal ŋkpitim pu.»

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Niinee ní Samiyeel kàan̄ tibɔti kɔkɔ ki tùkū-u kaa bál̀-u báà tiba. Ní Eelii bí yii: «Úǹ di sá ti-Dindaan, ú ŋá min u ká yii an ŋān̄ee.»

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Samiyeel nìn wíiǹ. Ti-Dindaan nìn bí u-cee, ní kaa nìn yāntì tin u sòon̄ee tiba gbíntì fám kaa túń ditundi.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: An yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ Daani tiŋki kí cáá sāā Beerseeba tiŋkee, báà ŋma béè yii ibaamɔn Samiyeel baasii sá ti-Dindaan bɔnaatiliu.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn gbíntìi nìkì ki nyāntí u-ba Siiloo ki dàkà. Di sá yii Siiloo niin ní u nìn nyāntí u-ba ki dàkà Samiyeel ní ki tìì-u u-nyɔɔbundi,

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: ní u cáa nàatī Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ. Fiiliistii yab jáń ki fōō Unimbɔti dakaau Dalbee Isirayeel yab bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi kí já nì Fiiliistii yab. Bi nìn gāā bi-janjanaapaal Eebeen-Eeseer caŋin, ní Fiiliistii yab gāā bi-yal Afeeki tiŋkin.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Ní bi lēē binib ki tú Siiloo bí cùú yòon̄ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un kā keerubimbi puee Poondi dakaau. Eelii jipɔmbi Oofinii nì Fineeyaasi di nìn céeǹ Unimbɔti dakaau.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab fātìi gítì bi-janjanaapaal puee ní bikpilib bí yii: «Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan yāntì Fiiliistii yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-ti díǹ míǹ? Tí cùmaan Siiloo kí yòon̄ní ti-Dindaan dakaau, ú nīn bí ti-kansikin kí fīī-ti ti-nannanliibi ŋaan kí líí.»

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun dakaayee bàn̄ Isirayeel yab janjanaapaal puee, ní bi-kɔkɔ kúuǹ ikuŋkuunti mpɔn mpɔn ní kitiŋ cīŋkì.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab gbìl̄ ikuŋkuunti puee ní ki téeń yii: «Ba kuŋkuuntii di tùm̀ Eebru yab janjanaapaal pu míǹ ní?» Boonee ní bi béè yii an sá ti-Dindaan dakaau di bāań Isirayeel yab janjanaapaal pu.

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi fāŋkì ki lī yii: «Unimbɔti dɔ́miń Eebru yab janjanaapaal pu. Taa láá pée ká míǹ dalba dalba. Ti kpíì ní!

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: An dóò ti-pu ní. Ŋma di làá fīī-ti Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nee ŋaan kí líí? Úǹ di kɔ́ǹ Eejipiti yab agìń nín bí a-ba a-ba puee kuteeun.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab, kámaan kunyannyaau, nín̄ sámaan bininjab, án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa kpántí Eebru yab yumbui kii bíǹ nín sá nimbi yumbui puee. Nín̄ sámaan bininjab kí já nì bi!»

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn fōō Unimbɔti dakaau. Bi nìn kūū Eelii jipɔmbi liitil, Oofinii nì Fineeyaasi. Usaraaŋakpil Eelii nì u-coopu kúm

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti mbaantee, uninja ubɔ nìn nyánní kujaaun ki sáǹ ki cūtì Siiloo. U nìn sá Beenjameen naakookun ní. U nìn dáaĺ ki cátì u-bɔkutil, ki dū ntam ki pùkū u-yil kí dàkà yii u bí kunimbaaun.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Eelii nìn nyántì u-jal ki kā ki kpèé nsan pu, kun puee u-pɔbil kaa nìn sɔ̀m̀ Unimbɔti dakaau pu. Uninjee nìn bāań ki kɔ́ kitiŋin ní ki dū tin jítèe ki máafì. Niinee kitiŋin nib kɔkɔ kíĺ ki bíi gbáà ibiil ki kūuntí.

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Ní uninjee kíí-u yii: «Isirayeel yab sáǹ Fiiliistii yab. Bi pɔ̄fì ti-nibul yab tikpil. Bi kūū a-jipɔmbi liitil, Oofinii nì Fineeyaasi, ní ki fōō Unimbɔti dakaau.»

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Eelii nín pée gbìl̄ u pútì Unimbɔti dakaau yindi puee, ní u nyáń u-jal pu ki lítì u-boon pú, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki caŋin, ní u-sil gíì ní u kpíì, kun puee u nìn púĺ ní ki nyìm̀ mun. U nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin imuŋku ili ní.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: U-coopu Fineeyaasi nimpuu nìn cáá dipool ki tóob́ mmaal. U nín gbìl̄ yii bi fōō Unimbɔti dakaau ní u-cooja nì u-cal kpíìyee ní u tātìi kāl̀ ki núuĺ ki màl̄, di sá yii imatiŋween nìn cúú-u dikáal.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: U bíi sìntēe ní binimpoobi bin nìn bí u-ceeyee bí-u yii: «Taa fàŋkì, di sá yii kibininjabiki ní a màl̄.» Waa kíí tibaaa, kaa fātìi tɔ́ mun.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn fōō Unimbɔti dakaau. Bi nìn yōoǹ-u Eebeen-Eeseer ki cáa cūnnì Asidoodi tiŋkin.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl Asidoodi yab kpēēyee, diwaal Daagɔn lítì dicincibil ki dɔ̄ kitiŋ Unimbɔti dakaau nimbiin, ní bi yōoǹ-dì ki gíiǹ ki yóoǹ di-paaŋŋu.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Kù tí wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl bi kpēēyee, Daagɔn tí lítì dicincibil ki dɔ̄ kitiŋ Unimbɔti dakaau nimbiin. Diyil nìn cúu tūkutì ní iŋal liitil kɔ́fì ki dɔ̄ nsan pú. An nìn pée kíǹ dimuundi ní ki dɔ̄.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: An pu ní áli ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, diwaal Daagɔn tandambi nì bin kɔkɔ cá ki kóò kuwaadiin Asidoodi tiŋkinee taal kaa tà kuwaadii punyɔkɔpu kí kɔ́.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn kɔ́ǹ Asidoodi yab agìŋ́kpaan poon. U nìn kɔ́ǹ-bi dinyoondin, ki yāntì ncaapa cúú-bi, ki kpáaǹ bin nìn kóò ntimu mun māntìi tú-bee.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Asidoodi yab nín ká tin bíi jītí bi-puee, ní bi bí yii: «Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu dakaau kaa máaǹ kí yūĺ ti-cee doo. Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dàkā ti nì ti-waal Daagɔn u-pɔŋŋu.»

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Ní bi tú bi yíiń Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi bi dɔ́miń ki kpáfì bi-cee, ní bi bālifì-bi yii: «Ti làá ŋá Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dakaau nee mana?» Ní bíǹ kíí-bi yii: «Yòom̄maan-u kí cáá cùnnì Gaati tiŋkin.» Niinee ní bi yōoǹ Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu dakaau ki cáa yóoǹ Gaati tiŋkin.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Bi nín cáá Unimbɔti dakaau ki yóoǹ kitiŋ gbantinee, Unimbɔti nìn dáaĺ kitiŋ gbanti nib tafal, ki yāntì dinyoondi kɔ́-bi. U nìn dáaĺ bikpaambi nì ŋwaamu kɔkɔ tafal, ki yāntì ncaapa cútì-bi.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi yōoǹ Unimbɔti dakaau ki cūnnì Eekrɔn tiŋkin. Ama bi nín cáá Unimbɔti dakaau ki bàn̄ niinee ní Eekrɔn yab kíĺ ki bíi gbáà ibiil yii: «Bi cáań Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu dakaau ti-cee doo kí kpɔ̀ ti nì ti-nibul!»

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Ní bi mun yíiń Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ki bí-bi yii: «Ní fàtīí gíiǹ Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu dakaau u-tiŋkin, laakin u nìn bée, ú taa kpɔ̀ ti nì ti-nibul.» Di sá ŋkúm faanti nìn cúú Eekrɔn yab kɔkɔ, kun puee Unimbɔti nìn dàkā-bi u-pɔnŋu.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Bin ŋkúm kaa nìn kūūyee, ncaapa nìn cúú-bi, ní bi gbáń kunimbaau biilii áli an tin bàn̄ kutagbɔŋu.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan dakaau nìn ŋá Fiiliistii yab tiŋkin iŋmal iluli ní.

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn yíiń bitandambi nì bibɔɔbi, ní ki bālifì-bi yii: «Ti làá ŋá ti-Dindaan dakaau mana ní? Tùkùmaan-ti min ní an sá tí ŋá ní kí yòon̄-u kí gíiǹ u-tiŋkin laakin u nìn bée.»

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-bi yii: «Ni yaa làá gíiǹ Unimbɔti dakaau Isirayeel tiŋkinee, ní taa gíiǹ-u fám. Ama ní tīī tiwan tin bi làá tin dūú ŋá saraa kí ŋāŋkì ni-bɔkpilee. Niinee, ni làá ká dicáaǹdi ní kí béé kun pu u dátí ni-tafal kaa gbèentée.»

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Ní bi bālifì-bi yii: «Ba ní an sá tí tīī bí dūú ŋāŋkì?» Ní bitandambee nì bibɔɔbee bí-bi yii: «Ní dū sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan tiŋmoo kí nántíǹ ncaapa, nì inapul iŋmoo, di sá yii Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi bí biŋmoo ní. Ibaamɔnee, ŋweembaanti di cúú ni nì ni-bɔtiibi.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: An puee ní mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan kí nántíǹ ncaapa ŋun cúú-nee nì inapul in di kɔ́ ki bíil̀ ni-tiŋkee, ní kí tīī Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu tinyool. An yaa yíì, u làá gbèen̄ kaa ti làá dáaĺ ni nì ni-waaŋi nì ni-tiŋki tafal.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Ní taa pɔ̄ɔkì ni-pɔbil kii Eejipiti yab nì Faaroo nín nìn ŋá puee. Ní téetí Unimbɔti nín nìn sāaǹ-bi pu ní bi dāa nín yāntì Isirayeel yab nyáń ki búntèe.

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: An puee mɔ́ɔ́maan tɔrɔkupɔɔn ubɔ, kí nyàab̀ inasal ili in biyaamu ŋáaḿ baa kpàl̄-i i túń ditundi ki kée. Bí dū tɔrɔku kí nɔ̀b̄-i ní kí gíiǹ i-biyaamu laakin bi ŋáań inaa timool i ŋmóòyee.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Ní yòon̄ ti-Dindaan dakaau kí tàkan̄ tɔrɔkuee poon. Ní dū sindaariya wanti tin ni tīī bí dūú ŋāŋkì ni-bɔkpilee kí ŋá kidakaabiki kiba poon kí dūú yóoń kí kɔ́ĺ Unimbɔti dakaau, ní kí yàntī inaayee ń nīn cá.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Ní nīn yú ki kpèé, inasalee yaa túĺ Isirayeel yab tiŋki saŋŋu ki cá Beeti-Seemeesi watil púee, mimmee ti béè yii bi-Nimbɔtiu di yāntì mbusu nee jéetì ti-pu. Ama i yaa dūu túĺ laaba púee, mimmee ti béè yii an kaa nyánní u-cee, an sá yìkíl̄ yikil ní.»

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab ŋá min bi dàkā-bee. Bi nyàab̄ inasal ili in mbiyaamu ŋáaḿee ki kpàl̄-i ní ki dū tɔrɔku ki nɔ̀b̄-i, ní ki gíiǹ i-biyaamu laakin bi ŋáań inaa timool i ŋmóòyee.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan dakaau nì kidakaabiki kin poon inapul naŋku nì tiwan tin bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ ki nántiǹ ncaapee ki tākaǹ tɔrɔkuee poon.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Ní inasalee kíĺ Beeti-Seemeesi saŋŋu cáaa ki búntì. I pée tàkā nsan gbanti míǹ ní, kaa pāatì ŋganaaa, ŋgiil. I nìn pée sūǹ ní kaa gbèentí. Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi nìn pá i-boon áli i tin kɔ́ Beeti-Seemeesi tiŋkin.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Beeti-Seemeesi yab nìn bí ditantakalin ki cēē bilee. Bi yáatìi kpēēyee ki ká ti-Dindaan dakaau. Bi nín ká dakaayee ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii bɔtiibi bi-ŋmootil nín ká mimmee ní bi nín gítí Eekrɔn tiŋkin yaadal wiiŋŋu.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nín nìn tīī sindaariya wanti tin bi mɔ́ɔ́ ki nántiǹ ncaapa bí dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa kí ŋāŋkì bi-bɔkpilee nyɔkɔm sɔ̀: Asidoodi tiŋki yil pu kubɔ, Gaasaa tiŋki yil pu kubɔ, Asikeelɔn tiŋki yil pu kubɔ, Gaati tiŋki yil pu kubɔ ní Eekrɔn tiŋki yil pu kubɔ.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Sindaariya napulii in bi mɔ́ɔ́yee nìn sá ntimu mun Fiiliistii bɔtiibi biŋmooyee nìn kpòotēe nyɔkɔm ní, kí yòon̄ ntimu mun bi máń agun ki túee kí cáá sāā ntimbilimu mun baa máń agun ki túee. Fiiliistii yab timmu nìn dɔ̄ kí tin cáá sāā Ditaŋkpakpaandi din pu bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan dakaau ki tɔ́kɔǹee. Díǹ pu nee, ditaŋkpakpaandi gbanti dáá gbíntìi bí niin, Joosuwa un sá Beeti-Seemeesee saakun.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Ní Beeti-Seemeesi yab bí yii: «Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ ti-Dindaan un sá circir Nimbɔtiu nee nimbiin? Ŋma cee ní ti làá yòon̄ dakaa nee kí cùnnì kí yóoń kí wàatī ti-ba?»

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Ní bi tú binib bí cù Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim yab cee kí tùkù-bi yii: «Fiiliistii yab gíiǹní ti-Dindaan dakaau. Dāam̄maan kí yòon̄ kí cùnnì ni-cee.»

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim yab nìn dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ ti-Dindaan dakaau ki cáa cūnnì Abinadaab dumpu kigbantaŋ pu. Bi nìn lēē u-jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar ú nīn cí ti-Dindaan dakaau. Samiyeel Isirayeel kpootiliu. Bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Fiiliistii yab

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Samiyeel bí Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yii: «An yaa lafun sá nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ ní ni là kí gítiń ti-Dindaan ceeyee, ní nyāntí awaa Asitaartee nì awaa ŋin pée kíǹee kɔkɔ ni-cee. Ní dū ni-ba kí nákáǹ ti-Dindaan nì ni-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ kí nīn jáaḿ úǹ baba. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, u làá nyāntí-ni Fiiliistii yab ŋaan.»

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab nyántì awaa Baal nì Asitaartee bi-kansikin ki fá, ní ki kíǹ ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaan baba.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Samiyeel bí-bi yii: «Ní kpāfìmaan Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ Miisipa ḿ gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan ni-pu.»

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ní bi dɔ́miń ki kpáfì Miisipa, ki lúń nnyim ki pɔ̀l̄ kitiŋ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Bi nìn bóob́ kinyɔkɔ yaadal wiiŋŋu, ki bīitì bi-kpitii pu ki bí yii: «Ti yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan.» Miisipa niin ní Samiyeel kpántì Isirayeel yab kpootiliu.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab gbìl̄ yii Isirayeel yab kpáfì Miisipa. Niinee ní bi-bɔtiibi yíkì kí cùú jáǹ-bi. Isirayeel yab nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee ní bi fāŋkì Fiiliistii yab.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí Samiyeel yii: «Taa nín̄ kā ki ŋmí! Taa dū-ti kí fá! Kúuǹ kí yíiń ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ú fīī-ti Fiiliistii yab ŋaan.»
