english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Samiyeel bí ki ŋáań saraawɔkaayee, Fiiliistii yab tíibiń kí dāá já nì Isirayeel yab. Ŋyunti gbantee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì utaa téeń bi-pu ní bi-pɔbil bíil̀, ní Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nyáń Miisipa ki kùl̄ ki bīiǹ Fiiliistii yab boon ki kūū-bi ki tin cáa sāā Beeti-Kaar tiŋki poon.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn jáń ki fōō Isirayeel yab timmu, kí yòon̄ Eekrɔn kí cáá sāā Gaati. Bi nìn fātìi gíiǹ-mu ki tīī-bi ní Isirayeel yab fōō bi-tiŋki Fiiliistii yab ŋaan. Ŋgbansɔŋfi nìn dōoǹ Isirayeel yab nì Amɔɔr yab kansikin.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samiyeel nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab míǹ ki tin sāā u-kúm dal.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Dibindi kamaayee, u nìn cá Beeteel nì Giilgaal nì Miisipa ki sòoǹ Isirayeel yab bɔti ntimu gbantin.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ú fàtī Raama u-dumpu kí sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì Isirayeel yab kansikin bɔti. Raama niin ní u nìn tí máń ti-Dindaan nsaraafan.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yíì u-jipɔŋkpiliu yii Jooweel, ní ki yíì uliliiti yii Abiiya. Bi nìn kóò Beerseeba ní ki kpòotī samaa.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Ama bíǹ kaa nìn nóó bi-baa tabɔbiliŋ. Nnimbineel puee, bi nìn fòol̄ dinyɔɔŋeebil jim ní kaa sòoǹ tibɔti ti-pú.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: An pu ní Isirayeel yab kpilib kpáfì ki cūtìi ká Samiyeel Raama tiŋkin.

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí-u yii: «Kpèè, a púĺ ní nee, ní a-jipɔmbi mun kaa nóó a-tabɔbiliŋ. Míǹ puee, kàan̄-ti ubɔti ú nīn kpòotī-ti kii atimbun kɔkɔ poon an nín bí puee.»

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Tibɔtee kaa nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ Samiyeel bi nín bālifì yii bi là ubɔtee, ní u bíi mèé ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Pīlifì dinibul nín bālifì-si tiŋyee kí ŋá míǹ. Di sá yii an kaa sá sii ní baa ti là, an sá man! Baa ti là yii man ḿ nīn sá bi-bɔtiu.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ daliŋkin m nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, bi pée fàtī bi-boon ní ki tìì-mi ní ki nóó awaa. Míǹ mbaantiim ní bi bíi ŋáań si mun nee.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: An puee pīlifì tin bi bālifì-see kí ŋá míǹ. Ama á kpāafì-bi ubɔtee nín làá dāá jī dibeel bi-pu miŋyee.» Ubɔti nín cáá nsan kí ŋá tiŋyee

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Samiyeel cáań tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan lēe ki tùkū Isirayeel yab bin nìn bālifì-u yii bi là ubɔtee.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: U bí-bi yii: «Ubɔti un bi làá kàan̄ee nín dāa cáá nsan kí ŋá puee sɔ̀. Ni-jipɔmbi kansikin ní u làá dāá lēē bin làá nīn ŋàal̀ u-janjatɔrɔkubee nì bin làá nīn jàkà u-taamuuyee nì bin làá nīn sáń ki līī u-tɔrɔkuu nyɔkɔpuee.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: U làá dāá dū ni-bisalib kí kpántí bitalaaluŋaliibi nì bijiŋŋaliibi nì bikpɔnɔpuliliibi.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: U làá dāá fōō ni-sati nì ni-fiinyikpaaŋŋi nì ni-ɔliifikpaaŋŋi amɔnti kí tīī u-kàliŋkpilib.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: U làá dāá lēē ni-kpaajinti nì ni-fiinyib pu tisaalaatiil kí dūú tīī u-kpambaliŋ nì u-kàliŋkpilib.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: U làá dāá fōō ni-tɔntɔnliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi. U làá dāá lēē ni-nipɔmbi bin cáá mpɔnee, ki kpáaǹ ni-mammu gba bí nīn bí ki tūǹ u-tundi.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: U làá dāá lēē ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui saalaa kamaa puee ubɔ ubɔ. Mimmee nimbi ni-ba dāa kpántì u-yumbui dee.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ni làá dāá yāliŋkì, ama ti-Dindaan kaa làá dāá pīlifiǹ-ni.»

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: Ti mun là kí nīn bí kii atimbun ŋin kíǹee nín bí puee ní. Ti-bɔtiu làá nīn sòoǹ ti-bɔti, kí nīn līī ti-nyɔkɔpu ki jáà ti-jaaku.»

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samiyeel pílifì tibɔti tin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab sòon̄ee ní ki fātìi kàan̄ míǹ ki tùkū ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Samiyeel yii: «Pīlifiǹ-bi kí kàan̄-bi ubɔti.» Niinee ní Samiyeel bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Báà ŋma ń nīn kùǹ u-dumpu.»

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Beenjameen tiŋkinee, uninja ubɔ nìn bí ki sá ubaatandaan bi yíì-u yii Kiisi. Bi nìn yíì u-baa yii Abiyeel ní ki yíì u-naanja yii Seeroor. Bi nìn yíì Seeroor baa yii Beekoorati ní ki yíì u-naanja yii Afiya.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: U nìn cáá jipɔɔn ubɔ bi yíì-u yii Saayuul. U nìn ŋān̄ unaacimpɔɔn an kaa cáá bí lì. Isirayeel tiŋkinee, un nìn ŋān̄ ki bàn̄-uee kaa bí, ní u nìn fɔ̀kɔǹ bi-kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Dalbee, Saayuul baa Kiisi mansalii wáŋkì, ní u bí u-jipɔɔn yii: «Yòon̄ utɔntɔnli ubɔ kí páań a-boon ní cùú nyàab̀ imansal.»

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Saayuul nì utɔntɔnlee yìin̄ Eefiraayiim timmu mun bí ajoon puee, nì Salisaa timmun kaa ká-i. Boonee ki nín cá Saaliim timmun ki yìin̄ kaa ká-i, ní ki yìin̄ Beenjameen timmun kaa ká-i.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Bi bāań Suufi tiŋkinee ní Saayuul bí utɔntɔnlee yii: «Tí gítí mmɔŋki, an yaa sá fám m-baa làá súntí imansal pu kí nīn bíi yáliŋkí ti-pu.»

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔnlee kíí-u yii: «Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ bí kitiŋ nee poon! U sá unil un pu bi nyée ní. Tin u yaa lēe, see á ká míǹ deedee. Tí cùú ká-u, an yaa yíì, u làá dàkà-ti dijandi din sá tí túĺ kí nīn nyàab̀ee.»

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul kíí-u yii: «Too, tí cù. Kin ba ní ti làá tin pɔ̄ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu gbanti? Di sá yii ti-kpɔnɔb dóò kulooun, ní taa ti cáá tiwampɔkaal tiba mun kí tin pɔ̄-u, tiba nì tiba kaa ti kíǹ ti-cee.»

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔnlee bí yii: «Man cáá kijitɔŋwaai kiba m-cee doo. M làá dū-kì kí tīī Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ú dàkà-ti nsan ŋun sá tí túĺee.»

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí u-tɔntɔnliuee yii: «A nín lī puee ŋān̄, tí nīn cá.» Ní bi páaǹ tɔb pu ki búntì kitiŋ kin poon Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee kóòyee.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Bi bíi dàb̀ kí kɔ́ kitiŋinee ní ki tú bisapɔmbi cá ŋkpin, ní bi bālifì-bi yii: «Doo ní uninja un wāĺee báaa?»

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Ní bisapɔmbee kíí-bi yii: «U bāań an kaa yúntì ní ni mun dūu bāań nee. Ama ní ŋá malaa, u dɔ́miń kitiŋin díǹ. Di sá yii u cáá saraa ubɔ ki làá ŋá kí tīī samaa díǹ nsaraaŋapaan pu.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Ni yaa pée kɔ́ kitiŋin kpalaayee, ni làá ká-u kí wàatī ú nīn nín jɔ́ḿ nsaraaŋapaan laŋki kí jī tijin. Di sá yii u yaa kaa bāań, samaa kaa máaǹ kí jī, kun puee úǹ di mèé kí bìin̄ saraa jinti pu ní bin bi yíińee ń nín jī. Míǹ puee nín̄ cámaan kɔŋkɔnnee, ni làá tin yìkin̄-u.» Samiyeel nì Saayuul kpáfì

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ní bi nín jɔ́ḿ kitiŋin. Ŋyunti ŋun bi làá kɔ́ kitiŋinee, Samiyeel mun nyēē bi-nimbiin kí nīn cá nsaraaŋapaan pu dee.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Too, kutaa ń wúntí Saayuul ń bà Samiyeel ceeyee, ti-Dindaan tùkū Samiyeel yii:

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: «Fool ŋyunti nee deedeeyee, m làá fu yàntī Beenjameen naakookun niliu ubɔ ń dāan̄ a-cee. Á fu sìtī u-yil pu ŋkpam kí kàan̄-u m-nibul Isirayeel yab pu dibeel. U làá dāá fīī m-nibul Isirayeel yab Fiiliistii yab ŋaan. Di sá yii m ká m-nibul falaau ki gbìl̄ di-yaliŋkii.»

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Samiyeel ká Saayuul páaǹnée ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Kpèè uninja un bɔti m fu sòon̄ nì si yii u làá jī m-nibul pu dibeelee sèé.»

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Saayuul sútì ki pìl̄ Samiyeel kitiŋ punyɔkɔki caŋin ki bālifì yii: «M gbāam̀-si, dàkà-mi laakin un wāĺee kóòyee.»

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel kíí-u yii: «An sá man. Lìntī m-nyɔkɔpu tí jɔ̄m̀ nsaraaŋapaan laŋki. Ni làá jī man cee ní tijin díǹ, ní fool kutaafaauee ḿ fu tùkù-si tin kɔkɔ páb́-see, ní kí fu pɔ̄-si nsan á fàtī.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: An yaa kíǹ imansal in wáŋkì an ŋá díǹ iwiin itee bɔtee, taa ti yāliŋkì, di sá yii bi fātìi ká-i. Ŋma di yì tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ bí Isirayeel tiŋkinee ní? An kaa sá sii nì a-baa dicaŋkuaaa?»

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí yii: «Man sá Beenjameen naakookun naa! Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ poonee, kúǹ di sá kiwaai, ní Beenjameen naakookunee, man dicaŋku di kaa pée bí tiban! Kin ba pu ní a sòon̄ nì mi míǹ?»

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Ní u cūtìi cáań dinantaal nì dipugbindi ki yóoǹ Saayuul nimbiin, ní Samiyeel bí-u yii: «Dinaŋkúndi din m lēē ki yóoǹ-see dee. Sii di yì. Nín̄ ŋmóò. Dikpafil nee pu ní bi lēē-dì ki yóoǹ. Sii nì bin m yíińee ń kpāfì kí ŋmɔ́.» Ŋwiin gbantee Saayuul nì Samiyeel di nìn kpáfì ki jíń tijin.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Ní bi yíkìń nsaraaŋapaan laŋki ki sīntìń kitiŋin. Ní Samiyeel kāl̀ bi nín bɔ̀b̄ kudii yilpu puee u nì Saayuul gbáń mmaam.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Saayuul nì u-tɔntɔnliuee fīntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl. Kutaa wúntì ki dóòyee ní Samiyeel yíiń Saayuul kudii yilpu ki bí-u yii: «Yīkì ḿ nyāntí-si nsanni.» Ní bi yíkìi táá tɔb ki nín nyēē.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Bi nyáń kitiŋin ki dóòyee ní Samiyeel bí Saayuul yii: «Yàntī a-tɔntɔnliu ń lìntī nyɔkɔpu kí nīn cá.» Ní u-tɔntɔnliuee jítìi līntì ní Samiyeel bí Saayuul yii: «Sii yūĺ doo ḿ tùkù-si Unimbɔti nín lī puee.»

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Samiyeel nìn ŋúb́ kikpalbabiki ŋkpam kā poon, ní u bātì ki sītì Saayuul yil pu ki kpàl̄-u ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan u-ba di lēē-si á nīn sá u-nibul bɔtiu.»

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: A yaa yíkì m-cee doo díǹee, a làá tū binaacimpɔmbi bili Raseel kaakul caŋin Seelisaa, Beenjameen yab tiŋkin. Bi làá tùkù-si yii: «Bi ká imansal in a bíi nyàab̀ee. Kɔŋkɔnnee a-baa kaa ti dàkafī íǹ pu, ama nimbi bɔti di kíǹ ki páb́-u. U bíi bàlifī u-ba min ní u làá dī ní kí ká u-jipɔɔnee.»

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: A yaa nìkī a-saŋŋu ki cá ki tin bàn̄ busubu bun bi yíì Tabɔɔree, a làá ká bininjab bita niin, bi jɔ́ḿ Beeteel kí jāam̀ Unimbɔti. Ubɔ ŋúb́ aŋɔbil ata, uliliiti ŋúb́ kpɔnɔb bita ní utataati bàl̄ kuloou ndaam kā poon.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Bi làá jāam̀-si ní kí tīī-si kpɔnɔb bili. A làá fōō kpɔnɔb gbanti.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, a làá nìkī a-saŋŋu kí tin bà Giibeeya-Eelooyiim tiŋkin, laakin Fiiliistii yab yidambi kóòyee. A yaa tóob́ kí kɔ́ kitiŋinee, a làá tū Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nsanni bi nyánní nsaraaŋapaan pu ki sìntīń. Biwambɔɔliibi līiń bi-nyɔkɔpu ki bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati nì ŋgaŋgamu ki búǹ awul ki bɔ̀ɔ́ saŋgu. A làá ká-bi bi fītì ní ki nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan Fam làá kɔ́ a-ni ní á fìtī kii án nín fītì bi mun puee, ní á kpántí unipɔɔn.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: A yaa láa ká tidaandi nee jítì mimmee, á béé yii Unimbɔti bí a-cee tiŋman pu. Niinee tin yaa láa pée bāań á ŋée, ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Á lìntī kí sìntī Giilgaal. Boonee ma mun làá dāan̄ kí ká-si niin kí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi. Á kàl̄ niin iwiin iluli kí cīití-mi. M yaa láa bāańee, m làá tùkù-si tin sá á ŋée.

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Saayuul yíkì Samiyeel ceeyee ní Unimbɔti cúú u-pɔbil ki kpántì. Tin kɔkɔ Samiyeel sòon̄ee, ŋwimbaanti gbanti ní an jítì míǹ.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Saayuul nì u-tɔntɔnliuee bāań Giibeeyayee ní bi tú Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi dikitil. Unimbɔti Fam nìn dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ Saayuul ni, ní u fītì ki kútì dikitilee pu bi bíi nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ nìn pée nyí Saayuul dooooyee nín ká u bíi nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti kii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nín nàatī puee, ní bi bíi bàlifī tɔb yii: «Ba cáá Kiisi jipɔɔn ní? Saayuul mun kpántì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu níii?»

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Ní kitiŋ gbantin niliu ubɔ bí yii: «Ŋma di baasii sá bi-kpiliu ní?» Niin ní dilìmbil nee nyánní yii: «Saayuul mun kpántì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu níii?»

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: An cēetì Saayuul puee, ní u nín jɔ́ḿ nsaraaŋapaan pu.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Saayuul wee bālifì u nì u-tɔntɔnliu yii: «Ni cūtì la ní?» Ní Saayuul kíí-u yii: «Ti cūtìi nyàab̄ imansal ní. Ama taa ká-i ní ki nín cá Samiyeel cee.»

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Ní u-wee bí-u yii: «Māafì-mi tin Samiyeel tùkū-nee.»

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí u-wee yii: «Tin u pée tùkū-tee di sá yii bi fātìi ká imansal.» Ama waa tùkū-u Samiyeel nín sòon̄ nì u dibeel bɔti tiŋyee. Bi tɔ́ kasi ki lēē Saayuul ubɔti

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Samiyeel yíiń Isirayeel yab ki kpáfì Miisipa ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: U bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Man di nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin, ki fōō-ni Eejipiti yab nì abee ŋin yab nìn sàantí-nee ŋaan ki líì.>

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Ama díǹ nee nimbi dū ni-Nimbɔtiu ki fá, úǹ un fìil̄-ni ki nyāntí nnaabu nì animbinaaman kɔkɔ poonee. Ni bí-u yii: <Á tīī-ti ubɔti.> Too, dāá yūĺmaan ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí nóó nì ni-naakɔti nì ni-maaliŋu nín sá puee.»

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Samiyeel yāntì Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ sútìń. Bi tɔ́ kasee ní án lēē Beenjameen naakooku.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Ní u cáań bin sá Beenjameen yabee ki síiǹ ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee, ní án lēē Matirii maaliŋun yab. Mmaal gbanti poonee ní án lēē Kiisi jipɔɔn Saayuul. Ní bi nyàab̄-u ki gīī kaa ká-u.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Ní bi gíti bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «Uninja gbanti dɔ́miń doooo?» Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «U kɔ́ ki bál̀ tiwaŋkpiil kansikin.»

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Ní bi cūtì ki nɔ̄kɔtìń-u tiwaŋkpiilee kansikin ní u cūtì ki yúl̀ samaa kansikin. U nìn fɔ̀kɔǹ bi-kɔkɔ.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí samaa kɔkɔ yii: «Kpèèmaan un ti-Dindaan lēēyee. U-juti kaa bí samaa kansikin.» Niinee báà ŋma bíi kpáafí ki tátí yii: «Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn!»

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Samiyeel kàan̄ tin sá bí ŋá kí tīī ubɔtee samaa nimbiin, ní ki ŋmàn̄-tì ki ŋá kugbɔŋun ki cáa yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ní ki pú Isirayeel yab nsan bí kpì bi-dumpui.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul mun nín kùǹ u-dumpu Giibeeya. Unimbɔti nìn gbēē bibaatandambi biba pɔbiliŋ ní bíǹ nóó-u.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Ama bin kaa bí tibanee mun nìn lī yii: «Mana ní un bí nee ŋūǹ kí fīī-ti?» Bi nìn kpēē-u fám kaa cáań tiba ki jáam̀-u. Ama ní an kaa nìn ká Saayuul.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Amɔn yab bɔtiu Naasi nìn cūtì kí jáǹ Yabeesi tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkinee. Ní Yabeesi yab kɔkɔ bí ubɔti Naasi yii: «Á pòon̄-ti kí pùtī yii ti nì si ŋá ubaanti ní tí kpántí a-tɔntɔnliibi.»

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti Naasi kíí-bi yii: «Ni yaa là ḿ pòon̄-ni kí pùtī yii man nì ni ŋá ubaantee, see báà ŋma ń lúkutí u-ŋaŋgiinimbil kí kɔ́ǹ Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ icoo.»

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Ní Yabeesi tindaŋkpilib kíí-u yii: «Á pɔ̄-ti iwiin iluli. Ti làá tɔ̄ binib Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ poon kí kpèè. Ubɔ yaa kaa nín bí kí fīī-tee, ti làá dū ti-ba kí ŋá a-ŋaan.»

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Binibee nín cá Giibeeya, Saayuul tiŋkin ki dū tibɔtee ki máafì niin yab. Kitiŋ gbantin nib nìn súń ki yáliŋkì.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee Saayuul mun nyánní kusaau ki pá u-naai boon ki kùnní, ní u bālifì yii: «Ba di yì-tì ní samaa kɔkɔ bíi sūǹ míǹ?» Ní bi máafì-u tin Yabeesi yab lēe.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Saayuul nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee ní Unimbɔti Fam kɔ́ u-ni ní u fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Ní u cúú inaa ili ki kūū ki càkā. U nìn dūu tīī binib ń cáá yìiǹ Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn kí tùkù-bi yii: «Un kamaa yaa kaa páaǹ Saayuul nì Samiyeel boon ki cūtì kujaauee, bi nín làá ŋá udaan naai puee dee.» Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì dinyoondi kɔ́ samaa, ní bi-kɔkɔ kpáfì kii unibaantee.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū bin bi nìn túnnée yii: «Fool kuwiŋkuluuee, ni làá fu ká dijòońdi.» Bi nín cáá an bɔtee ki tùkū Yabeesi yabee ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi.

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: Niinee Yabeesi yab tùkū Amɔn yab yii: «Foolee ti làá fu cáań ti-ba kí ŋá ni-ŋaan, ni yaa fu là-ti puee ní ŋá.»

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Saayuul cúú u-janjaliibi ki yākatì akiti ata. Kutaa síitì ki cá diwuntilee ní bi kɔ́ bi-nannanliibi janjanaapaal pu ki kūū Amɔn yab ki tin sāā kuwiŋkuluu. Bin nìn kíǹee nìn sáǹ ki yàl̄ bi-ba bi-ba, baa ti kāntí biba nóó bili.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bí Samiyeel yii: «Bilab di nìn bí yii baa là Saayuul ń nīn sá ti-bɔtiuee? Bí nyāntiń-bi doo tí kpɔ̀-bi.»

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí yii: «Baa máaǹ kí kpɔ̀ ubɔ ŋwiin kii ŋu nee dal, kun puee ti-Dindaan tīī Isirayeel yab dijajil díǹ.»

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Boonee ní Samiyeel bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Dāam̄maan tí cù Giilgaal kí cùú mɔ̀tīí síití Saayuul beel.»

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Ní samaa kɔkɔ nín cá Giilgaal, ní bi kāaǹ Saayuul dibeel niin ti-Dindaan nimbiin, ní ki ŋá mpèé saraabi ki tīī ti-Dindaan. Niinee Saayuul nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ jíń jiŋaakpaan ki fàal̄.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Samiyeel bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Kpèèmaan m pílifì ni-nyɔkɔ ki ŋá tin kɔkɔ ni bālifì-mee ki tīī-ni. M kāaǹ-ni ubɔti.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee úǹ di làá nīn kpòotī-ni. Man púĺ m-yikpiti píil̀. M-biyaamu cíkitì ki bí ni-kansikin. Doooo m-naacimpɔntin ní m kpōotì-ni ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: An pu ní m yú ni-nimbiin díǹ. Tin m yaa ŋée, ní lì ti-Dindaan nì ubɔti un u lēēyee nimbiin. M fōō ubɔ naau àá u-maŋkaaa? M mūul̀ ubɔ àá m sāaǹ ni-kansikin ubɔɔɔ? Ubɔ tīī-mi tiba ki ŋéeb́ m-nyɔkɔ m sòon̄ ki bīiǹ u-kpitii puɔɔɔ? M yaa ŋá-ni míǹ, m làá téeǹ-ni.»

english_verse: “No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab kíí-u yii: «Aa mūul̀-ti, kaa sāaǹ ti-kansikin ubɔ, kaa fōō ubɔ mun cee tiba.»

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel fātìi bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan nì un u lēē ú nīn sá ni-bɔtiuee sá m-seeradambi díǹ yii naa pée ká m-pu tikpitil tiba.» Ní bi kíí yii: «Tiŋman ní an sá.»

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan un di lēē Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn ki yāntì bi nyántì ni-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkinee sá m-seeradaaŋwu.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee ní dāá yūĺ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. M làá kàaǹ-ni atummɔnti ŋin kɔkɔ u ŋá ki tīī ni nì ni-naanjabee.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nì u-yab nín nìn bàn̄ ki kóò Eejipitee, bi nìn sāaǹ-bi ní bi gbáń ibiil ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ú jòoń-bi. Ti-Dindaan nìn tú Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn bi nyántìń-bi ki cáań ki kāaǹ kitiŋ kin poon ni bí nee.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Ama ni-naanjab nìn súntì ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu pu. Niinee ní u dū-bi ki líiǹ Siisira un sá Asɔɔr janjaliibi kpiliuee nì Fiiliistii yab nì Moowaab bɔtiu.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ni-naanjab tí kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ú jòoń-bi. Bi nìn lī yii: <Ti ŋá ikpiti. Di sá yii ti dū-si ki fá ki cūtìi bíi tòotī awaa ŋin bi yíì Baal nì Asitaarteeyee. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee fīī-ti ti-nannanliibi ŋaan ní tí nīn kíǹ ki jáaḿ-si.>

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan túnní Geedeeyɔn nì Beedan nì Jeefita nì man Samiyeel kí fīī-ni ni-nannanliibi bin māntìi tú-nee ŋaan. An yāntì ni kāl̀ kitiŋ nee poon nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Ama ni nín ká yii Amɔn yab bɔtiu Naasi dòoń kí já nì nee, nì min kamaa ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu sá ni-bɔtiuee, ní ni bí-mi yii: <Ti là á kàan̄-ti ubɔti!>

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee kpèèmaan ni-bɔtiu un ni lēēyee sèé. Ni bālifì yii ni là ubɔti ní ti-Dindaan tīī-ni ubɔti.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Ni yaa fàŋkí ti-Dindaan, ki nóó-u, ki tɔ́-u, ki yaa kaa yíkìi jáń nì u-marab, ní ni nì ni-bɔtiu yaa nóó-uee, tikɔkɔ làá còom̀-ni tiŋan.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa kaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan, ki yaa yíkìi bíi jáà nì u-marabee, u làá dáaĺ ni-tafal ŋkpitim pu, kii u nín nìn dáaĺ ni-naanjab tafal puee.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní bɔ́ntí ni-ba. Ni làá ká nì ni-nimbiliŋ maamaacikpaan un ti-Dindaan làá ŋée.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Kudiceeu yuntiŋu poon ní taa bí naaa? M làá mèè ti-Dindaan ú yàntī utaa ń fáá didundi kí nì. Niinee ni làá béé yii ni nín bālifì yii ni là ubɔtee, an sá ikpitikpaan ní ni ŋá ti-Dindaan nimbiin.»

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel mēē ti-Dindaan ní ti-Dindaan yāntì utaa fáá didundi ki nìn̄. Yaadal wiiŋŋu gbantee, samaa kɔkɔ nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan nì Samiyeel tikpil.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ bí Samiyeel yii: «Gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ti-pu tí taa kpú. Di sá yii ti pée ŋá-u ikpiti, ní ti nín gíti bālifì yii ti là ubɔtee mun kpitii dɔ́miń ki kútì.»

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí-bi yii: «Taa fàŋkìmaan. Tiŋman ni lafun ŋá ikpitikpaan. Ama min bí nee, ní taa ti fàtī ni-boon kí tīī ti-Dindaan, ní nóó-u nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Ni yaa fātì ni-boon ki tīī-uee, ni làá cù kí nīn tòotī awaa dee. Too, awaa gbanti mun di kaa bí tiban, kaa tí ŋūǹ kí fīī unilee, kun puee ŋaa bí tiban.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Tiŋman ti-Dindaan di là ní ki dū-ni ki ŋá u-nibul. An puee waa làá fá-ni, di sá yii u là kí dàkà u nín sá ukpaan puee ní.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: An yaa kíǹ man jandee, maa làá yìntīǹ ti-Dindaan kí gbèen̄ kí taa ti nín mèé ni-pu. M làá nīn gbíntìi dàkà-ni nsammɔnti, nsan ŋun tèen̄ee.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Tin bée di sá ní fàŋkì ti-Dindaan, kí nīn nóó-u ibaamɔn poon nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ. Di sá yii ní kpèè maamaacikpaambi bin u ŋá ki tīī-nee.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee, u làá kúntí ni nì ni-bɔtiu.»

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ gbìl̄ yii Saayuul kūū Fiiliistii yab kɔmandaŋwu, ní Fiiliistii yab kaa ti là bi-nimbil ń ká Isirayeel yab. Niinee bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ cūtìi kpáfì Saayuul cee Giilgaal.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín ká yii bi wúkutìń bi-pu an pɔ́ɔkèe ní bi sáǹ ki kɔ́ itaŋkpalɔkɔn nì ibòó ni nì ntaŋkpafaŋfakamin nì adiin ŋin bi gbìn̄ taapu ki máńee nì afaginni nì anyimbɔbilin.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Biba nìn sáǹ ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki cūtìi bál̀ Gaadi nì Galaadi timmun. Ŋyunti gbantee, Saayuul úǹ nìn dáá bíń Giilgaal ní u-janjaliibi bin nìn bí u-ceeyee wunti gbáà kpàkpakpa.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Saayuul kāl̀ niin iwiin iluli ki cíitì Samiyeel. Di sá yii Samiyeel nìn bí-u yii ú kíntí-u Giilgaal, ama ní kaa cūtì ŋyunti ŋun u síiǹee. Niinee bijanjaliibi sáǹ ki yàl̄ ki wāatì Saayuul.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí yii bí cáań-u tiwaŋkuti tin bi làá dūú ŋá saraawɔkaa nì mpèé saraauee. Ní úǹ u-ba ŋá saraawɔkaa.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: U tin pée lì yii u ŋáań saraawɔkaa ki dóotée, Samiyeel mun dūu bāań. Ní u nyáń ki túŋkì-u ki jáam̀-u.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bālifì-u yii: «Ba ní a ŋée?» Ní Saayuul kíí-u yii: «M ká yii bijanjaliibi bíi sáń ki yàl̀, ní ŋyunti ŋun ti yóoǹee, aa bíi bàń ní Fiiliistii yab mun kpáfì Miikimaasi ki bɔ́ntì.

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: Niinee m lī m-ban yii: <Fiiliistii yab làá dāan̄ kí túuǹ-mi Giilgaal ŋyunti ŋun maa láá ŋá saraabi ki sɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbilee, an pu ní m fōō ditundi gbanti ki ŋá m-ba saraawɔkaa.>»

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí Saayuul yii: «A ŋá kii unil un yil lábitèe! Aa ŋúb́ mara un ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu tīī-see. A yaa bàà ŋúb́ mara gbantee, ti-Dindaan bàà làá yàntī a-dicaŋkun niliu ubɔ ń nīn pée kā dibeel Isirayeel tiŋkin kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: A nín kaa ŋúb́ mara un ti-Dindaan tīī-see puee, a-beel kaa làá ti yúntí. Ti-Dindaan lēē unil ubɔ un kā u-pɔbil puee ki dūu kāaǹ dibeel ú nīn sá u-nibul bɔtiu.»

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Samiyeel yíkì Giilgaal ki túĺ u-saŋŋu. Bijanjaliibi bin kíǹee táá Saayuul ki yíkì Giilgaal ki cūtì. Saayuul kàan̄ bijanjaliibi bin kíǹ u-ceeyee, bi nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Saayuul nì u-jipɔɔn Joonatan nì bijanjaliibi bin kíǹ u-ceeyee nìn gbíntì Giibeeya, Beenjameen tiŋkin. Fiiliistii yab bíǹ nìn ŋātì bi-janjanaapaal Miikimaasi.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Dalbee Fiiliistii yab janjaliibi bin bi bífì bí nīn ŋàfēe nyáń dijanjanaapaal pu ki cúu yākatì akiti ata. Dikitipeekaalee nìn túĺ Oofiraa, Suwaal tiŋki watil pú,

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: ní dikitililiitiilee túĺ Beeti-Oorɔn pú, ní dikititataatiilee túĺ kitiŋ kpaanyɔkɔ watil pú, laakin a yaa tɔ́kɔ́ a wāĺ Isaakpan Tantakal, an bí kuteeu watilee.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee baa nìn gíti kāntí ucaa báà ubɔ Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn. Di sá yii Fiiliistii yab kaa nìn là Eebru yab ń mɔ́ɔ́ ntàataajimu nì ŋkpamu.

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Bi yaa làá nìn lòoǹ akoo ŋin inaa cáa kùee nì akoo nì ŋgaamu, àá bi yaa làá nìn tā inyanyee, bi nìn fòol̄ bi yaa yākatì jitɔn mitee, mili pu ní.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: An puee kujaau dalee, Saayuul nì Joonatan janjaliibi kaa nìn cáá ntàataajimu nì ŋkpamu. See Saayuul nì u-jipɔɔn baba di nìn cáá.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab janjakitil nìn cūtìi yúl̀ Miikimaasi saŋŋu pu ntaŋkpafaŋfakamin.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Ditaŋkpapeekaalee nìn bí ŋgan pú ki túĺ Miikimaasi, ní din kíǹee bí ŋgiil pú ki túĺ Giibeeya.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Ní Joonatan bí u-tɔntɔnliu yii: «Dāan̄ tí cù Fiiliistii yab bin kaa gífì akpancanee janjakitil nee cee. An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan làá yūĺ ti-boon, di sá yii ti yaa wīikáaa, ti yaa kaa wīikáaa, tiba kaa lìkintí ti-Dindaan nsan ú tīī-ti dijajil.»

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Ní u-tɔntɔnliu kíí-u yii: «Tin yaa pée fáatiǹ-see, ŋá míǹ. Tí nīn cá, m pá a-boon.»

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Ní Joonatan bí yii: «Tí nīn cá binib gbanti cee kí cáá ti-ba kí dàkà-bi.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Bi yaa bí-ti yii: <Yūĺmaan niin, timbi làá dāan̄ ni-ceeyee>, ti làá yūĺ dibɔɔbaantiil, taa làá jɔ̄m̀ bi-cee.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Ama bi yaa bí-ti yii: <Jɔ̄mìḿmaan ti-ceeyee>, ti làá jɔ̄m̀, di sá yii án di làá dàkà yii ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki ŋá ti-ŋaan.»

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Ní Joonatan nín dàb̀ ki nyìitī u-ŋalii pu ki bàlim̄ ki cá u-tɔntɔnliu pá u-boon. Joonatan nìn fátí Fiiliistii yab ki bīil̀ ní u-tɔntɔnliu pá u-boon ki púntí-bi.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Samaa kɔkɔ yaa bàà lēē tin ti jáń ki fōō ti-nannanliibi ceeyee ki jíńee, ti nín bàà làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Fiiliistii yab puee bàà làá nīn sá ŋkpaamin ní.»

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul kpáfì u-janjakitil ní bi nín cá dikɔmbool pu. Bi bàn̄ee ki ká Fiiliistii yab bí ki kù tɔb. An nìn sá fìkilfikilkpaan di kɔ́-bi.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Niinee dinyoondi kɔ́ Fiiliistii yab janjaliibi bin nìn gbíntì dijanjanaapaal puee nì bin nìn bí tisatinee nì samaa kɔkɔ. Bijanjaliibi bin yūlifí sintilee nì bin bi bífì bí nīn ŋàfēe mun nìn kɔ́ dinyoondin. Kí kūtèe kitiŋ nìn cīŋkì. Unimbɔti u-ba di nìn kɔ́ǹ-bi dinyoondi gbantin.

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Giibeeya, Beenjameen tiŋkinee, Saayuul janjaliibi bin nìn yú sintilee nìn bí ki kpèé. Bi nìn ká Fiiliistii yab nín sáń ki pùntī an kɔkɔ puee.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí bin bí u-ceeyee yii: «Yíiḿmaan ayin tí kpèè ŋma di nyáń ti-kansikin ki cūtì bi-cee?» Bi yíińee ní ki ká yii Joonatan nì u-tɔntɔnliu kpá.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Saayuul bí usaraaŋal Ayiiya yii: «Cáań Unimbɔti dakaau doo.» Di sá yaadal wiiŋŋuee, Unimbɔti dakaau nìn bí Isirayeel yab janjanaapaalin bi-cee.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Saayuul bíi sòoǹ nì usaraaŋalee ní kuwoou mɔ̀tīi bíi pɔ́ɔkí Fiiliistii yab janjanaapaal pu. Ní Saayuul bí usaraaŋal yii: «Gbèen̄ dibalifil!»

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Eebru yab bin nìn bí Fiiliistii yab cee ki tūǹ-bi atuunee nìn céeǹ-bi kujaau. Bíǹ nìn fātìi gítì Isirayeel yab nì Saayuul nì Joonatan jandi pú.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin nìn sáǹ ki bál̀ Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee gbìl̄ yii Fiiliistii yab sáǹ. Niinee ní bi mun kùl̄ ki bīiǹ bi-boon ki jáà nì bi.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Yaadal wiiŋŋuee, samaa nìn jíń falaa, kun puee Saayuul nìn pūtìi tɔ́ báà ŋma pu ki lī yii: «Un ní ŋwìiń yaa kaa láá jéetì man tɔ̀n̄ m-nannanliibi ipɔntoon ní udaan jíń tijinee, mbusu ń lítí udaan pu.» Samaa poonee, báà ubɔ kaa nìn jíń tijin.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Bi nín kɔ́ kubambaŋŋunee, bi nìn ká tisiil dɔ̄ ki pùub̀ kitiŋ, ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn sēē ki dáká, kun puee bi nìn fàŋkí mbusu.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Ama Joonatan kaa nìn gbìl̄ u-baa nín yāntì samaa pūtèe. U nìn tāntì ŋkpandɔ ŋun u ŋúb́ee ki sēē tisiil ki dáká ní u-nimbiliŋ ŋāatì.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Ní bijanjaliibi kansikin ubɔ bí-u yii: «A-baa bàà pūtì ki tɔ́ samaa pu yii: <Un yaa jíń tijin díǹee, mbusu ń lítí udaan pu.» An pu ní báà ŋma gīī.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Joonatan bí yii: «M-baa cáań nnaabu ki tɔ́ kitiŋ pu. Kpèè m nín sēē tisiil ki ŋmɔ́ ki ká mpɔn puee!

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, Isirayeel yab nìn kūū Fiiliistii yab kí yòon̄ Miikimaasi kí cáá sāā Ayalɔn. Bi nìn gīī púb.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Niinee samaa páatìi jéetì tiwan tin bi jáń ki fōōyee pu. Bi nìn cúú ipii nì inaa nì anabil ki lāntì ní ki kāl̀ laakin fatiku dɔ̄ee ki ŋmɔ́.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū Saayuul yii u-samaau yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan. Bi ŋmɔ́ tinan laakin bi lāntì tiwaŋkuti fatiku dɔ̄ee. Ní Saayuul téeń yii: «Ni yīntiǹ mara! Bíntiḿmaan ditaŋkpakpaandi kí cáań doo.»

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí yii: «Ní yìiǹ samaa kansikin kí tùkù-bi yii: <Báà ŋma ń cáań u-naau àá u-piiiu man cee. Doo ní ni làá kpɔ̀ tiwaŋkuti gbanti kí ŋmɔ́-tì. Mimmee naa làá ti ŋmɔ́-tì fatiku caŋin kí yìntīǹ ti-Dindaan.>» Kujoou gbantee, báà ŋma nìn cáań u-waŋkuluku niin ní ki kūū-kù.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Saayuul máń ti-Dindaan nsaraafan. Ŋúǹ di sá mpeekaa ŋun u máń ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí yii: «Tí sìntī kunyeeu nee kí jà Fiiliistii yab boon kí fūkul̀-bi kí kpɔ̀ bi-kɔkɔ áli kutaa nì ku-wuntil.» Ní u-yab kíí-u yii: «A yaa pée ká min ŋān̄ee, ŋá míǹ.» Ní usaraaŋal bí yii: «Tí bàlifì ti-Dindaan kí wàatī.»

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «Ḿ sìntī kí jà Fiiliistii yab boonaaa? A làá dū-bi kí ŋá Isirayeel yab ŋaanaaa?» Ama ŋwiin gbantee Unimbɔti kaa pée kíí tiba.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Saayuul yíiń samaa kpilib kɔkɔ u-cee ki bí-bi yii: «Ní nyàab̀maan kí kpèè ikpiti in ní ti ŋá díǹee!

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: M pūtì ti-Dindaan un sá Isirayeel yab fiiliu ki bí dimaŋfalinee yii báà an yaa sá gba m-jipɔɔn Joonatan di ŋá ikpiti gbanti, see bí kpɔ̀-u.» Samaa kɔkɔ poon báà ubɔ kaa gātì-u.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Saayuul bí samaa yii: «Nimbi Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, ní gítímaan dijandi diba, ma mun nì m-jipɔɔn ń yūĺ dijandi diba.» Ní samaa kíí-u yii: «A yaa pée ká min ŋān̄ee, ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Saayuul mēē ti-Dindaan yii: «Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, ba pu ní aa kíí-mi díǹ ní? Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, an yaa sá man àá m-jipɔɔn Joonatan di yīntèe, án tāā Uriim, an yaa tí sá Isirayeel nibul di yīntèe, án tāā Tumiim.» Ní an tāā Joonatan nì Saayuul, ní samaa nyáń tibɔtin.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí yii: «Tɔ̄maan kasi kí kpèè man nì m-jipɔɔn Joonatan un ní an sée, ní an tāā Joonatan.»

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Saayuul bí-u yii: «Tùkù-mi tin a ŋée.» Ní Joonatan bí-u yii: «M ká tisiil ní ki dū m-kpandɔŋu ki sēē ki dáká. M bɔ́ntì kí kpú.»

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul téeń yii: «Joonatan, a yaa kaa kpíì díǹ, Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ m-tafal ŋkpitim pu!»

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ama ní samaa bí Saayuul yii: «Joonatan yāntì Isirayeel yab ká dijajikpaandi. Waa máaǹ kí kpú. Án làá nīn sá ntimbiil bɔti ní. Ti pūtì ti-Dindaan yii u-yikpilku báà kubɔ kaa làá lítí kitiŋ. Di sá yii Unimbɔti di tútúǹ-u ní u ŋúń ki ŋá míǹ díǹ.» Samaa nín ŋá pu ki fīī Joonatan baa kūū-uee dee.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Niin ní Saayuul gbēeǹ kaa ti jìn̄ Fiiliistii yab boon, ní Fiiliistii yab nín kùǹ bi-tiŋkin. Saayuul beel bɔti

english_verse: When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles. Saul's Family
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋubɔee, u dàkā tininjati ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Amaleeki yab. U nìn jáń ki fōō Isirayeel yab ki nyántì bin nìn dòoń ki fúkuĺ bi-tiŋkee ŋaan.

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Saayuul maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, u nìn jáń nì Fiiliistii yab nì dinimbinaamandi. An puee u yaa nìn ká ubɔ cáá dikpabil nì dibaatandee, u nìn cútí-u ú kpántí ujanjal ní.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Samiyeel bí Saayuul yii: «Man ní ti-Dindaan nìn tú ḿ kàan̄-si u-nibul Isirayeel yab pu dibeel. Kɔŋkɔnnee á pīlifì ti-Dindaan bɔti tin m làá sòoǹ nì si nee.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé yii: <Isirayeel yab nín nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dòońee, Amaleeki yab nìn pīiǹ-bi nsan. An puee m làá dáaĺ bi-tafal.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, cù kí já nì bi kí nàan̄ tin kɔkɔ bi cááyee pílpil, á taa sɔ̄ bi-saai. Á kpɔ̀ bininjab nì binimpoobi, mbiyaamu nì nnaŋgbammamu, inaa nì ipii, igutaamu nì mmamu.>»

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul kóoǹ u-janjaliibi ki kpáfì Teelayiim ki kàan̄-bi. Bijanjaliibi bin nìn còom̄ ataayee nìn nyáń kutukub alaataa ali, ní Juuda yab janjaliibi nyáń kutukub saalaa.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Samiyeel yii:

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Saayuul nì u-janjaliibi nìn bàn̄ Amaleeki yab tiŋki caŋin ní ki kɔ́ mbunni ki nákáǹ.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí Keeni yab yii: «Nyāmaan Amaleeki yab kansikin kí cù ndan. Maa là yii tin m làá ŋá-bee ń kpáaǹ-ni. Di sá yii Isirayeel yab nín nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ni nìn ŋá-bi tiŋan.» Niinee ní Keeni yab nyáń Amaleeki yab kansikin.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Saayuul kūū Amaleeki yab kí yòon̄ Awiila kí tin cáa sāā Suur, Eejipiti tiŋkin ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú.

english_verse: Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag.
translation_verse: U nìn kūū Amaleeki yab kɔkɔ. See bi-bɔtiu Agaagi ní waa nìn kūū.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Saayuul nì u-janjaliibi kaa nìn kūū Agaagi nì tiwaŋkuti tin ŋān̄ee, an dàkà yii ipii nì inaa nì tiwaŋkuti tin cáá laafiyee nì apibil. U nìn dū tin ŋān̄ee ki kpáafì kaa kūū-tì. U nìn kūū tin kaa bí tiban kaa ŋūǹ kí kèetēe ní.

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: «An wùn̄-mi m nín lēē Saayuul ki kāaǹ dibeelee. Di sá u fātì u-boon ki tīī-mi, kaa dū m-marab bin m tīī-uee ki túń ditundi.» Samiyeel nìn gíí diŋuul ní ki dū kunyamɔŋu ki mēē ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, Samiyeel péé kí cùú ká Saayuul. U bàn̄ee ní binib tùkū-u yii: «Saayuul cūtì Kaarmeel ki máń dikumpool. Míǹ boonee ní u kíĺ nsan ki nín sìntī Giilgaal.»

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Samiyeel bàn̄ ki ká Saayuul ní úǹ bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ a-boon! M ŋá tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan tīī-mi mara yii ḿ ŋée.»

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí yii: «Ipii nì inaa di kaa sūǹ ki kpáà m-tafaliŋ naaa?»

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul kíí-u yii: «An sá bijanjaliibi di cáań tiwaŋkuti gbanti Amaleeki yab cee. Samaa lēē ipii in ŋān̄ee nì inaa in bí màlmalee ki cáań kí dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu saraa. Ama ti kūū ki céetì tin kíǹee kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Samiyeel bí Saayuul yii: «An ŋmāntì. M làá tùkù-si ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì mi kunyeeu nee puee.» Ní Saayuul bí-u yii: «Nín̄ sòoǹ.»

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí-u yii: «Ŋyunti ŋun a nìn dàkafī yii aa bí tibanee, ŋyunti gbanti ní a kpántì Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ yidaaŋwu. Ti-Dindaan u-ba di nìn kāaǹ-si á nīn sá Isirayeel yab bɔtiu.

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di tú-si ki bí-si yii: <Nín̄ cá! Á kpɔ̀ Amaleeki yab binikpitib gbanti. Á kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi báà ubɔ ń taa kíń.>

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Ba pu ní aa pílifì ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔ? Ba pu ní a yōoǹ tin ni jáń ki fōōyee, ki ŋá tin kaa kítèe ti-Dindaan nimbiin míǹ?»

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ḿ ŋá puee míǹ deedee ní m ŋá. M cūtì laakin u tú-mee. M kūū ki céetì Amaleeki yab kɔkɔ, see bi-bɔtiu Agaagi baba ní m cúú ki cáań doo.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ama m-janjaliibi di lēē tin ti jáń ki fōōyee poon ipimɔnti nì inamɔnti in bàà sá tí kpɔ̀ kí céetée ki yóoǹ kí dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu saraa Giilgaal.»

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan néeń bisaraawɔkaabi nì saraabi bin kíǹee kii unil ń nīn tɔ́ u-nyɔɔbundaaa? Aayee kpataaa! Unil ń nīn tɔ́ ti-Dindaanee jítiǹ saraabi, ní kí sìntī a-ba kí tīī-uee jítiǹ upìja kpam min bi cáa wù ŋŋmi ki ŋáań saraayee.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii a yaa yíì kaa tɔ́ Unimbɔtee kpitii jítiǹ dibɔɔbɔl kpitii, ní a yaa jáà nì ti-Dindaanee kpitii jítiǹ iwaatooti kpitii. A nín dū ti-Dindaan bɔti ki fée, u mun dū-si ki fá, aa làá nīn gíti sá ubɔti.»

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí Samiyeel yii: «M ŋá ikpiti, m yīntì ti-Dindaan marab nì a-bɔkpaaŋi. Di sá yii m fāŋkì bijanjaliibi ní ki ŋá bi nín là puee.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee m gbāam̀-si dū m-kpitii kí pɔ̄-mi, kí céeǹ-mi ḿ cùú jāam̀ ti-Dindaan.»

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Samiyeel bí-u yii: «Kpataaa maa làá cù, kun puee a dū ti-Dindaan marab ki fá, ní ti-Dindaan mun dū-si ki fá, aa ti sá Isirayeel yab bɔtiu.»

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Samiyeel lī míǹ ki fātì kí nīn cée ní Saayuul cúú u-bɔkutil gbeeŋgbeeŋyi ní an cúu tīl̀ ki gbíntì u-ŋaan.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí-u yii: «Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan fōō Isirayeel beel a-ŋaan díǹ. U dū-dì ki tīī un jítiǹ-see.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Á nīn nyí yii ti-Dindaan un sá Isirayeel yab nyootee kaa mɔ́ntáaa, kaa kpántí nlandɔkɔ kii unilee.»

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul tí bí yii: «M ŋá ikpiti. Ama m gbāam̀-si, tīī-mi disíndi m-nibul kpilib nì Isirayeel yab nimbiin kí céeǹ-mi tí cù ḿ jāam̀ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu.»

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel kíí ki céeǹ-u u cūtì ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Samiyeel bí yii: «Cáaḿmaan-mi Amaleeki yab bɔtiu Agaagi.» Agaagi bāań ki yúl̀ an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u, ní u lī u-neen yii: «Báà an ŋá pu, baa ti làá kpɔ̀-mi.»

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ama ní Samiyeel bí-u yii: «A-tàataajiki yāntì bibinaatiibi lóò mbiyaamu, an puee si mun na làá lóó u-biki binimpoobi kansikin.» Ní Samiyeel kūū-u ti-Dindaan nimbiin Giilgaal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Samiyeel nín fàtī Raama, ní Saayuul mun nín kùǹ u-dumpu Giibeeya.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Samiyeel kaa ti ká Saayuul ní ki dāa kpáàa kpíì. U nìn sūǹ Saayuul pu, di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn yáliŋkì u nín lēē-u ú nīn sá Isirayeel yab bɔtiuee.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Samiyeel yii: «A làá nīn gbíntìi sūǹ Saayuul pu kí tin cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní? Man di dū-u ki fá ní waa ti làá nīn sá Isirayeel yab bɔtiu. Kpíĺ ŋkpam a-yiŋŋu poon, kí yīkì ḿ tɔ̄-si Beetileem Jeesee cee. U-jipɔmbi kansikin ní m lēē ubɔti un m lèe.»

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Samiyeel bí yii: «M làá ŋá mana ní kí ŋá míǹ? Saayuul yaa gbìl̄, u làá kpɔ̀-mi ní.» Ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Cúú dinajapɔmbil kí nīn cá. A bèe ní kí bí yii: <M dɔ́miń kí ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa ní.>

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: A yaa làá dāá ŋá saraa gbantee, á dāá yíiń Jeesee ú nīn bí. M làá dāá dàkà-si tin sá á ŋée. Á dāá bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī un man làá dāá dàkà-see yil pu.»

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samiyeel ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee. U bàn̄ Beetileem tiŋkinee ní bitindaŋkpilib pɔbiliŋ máĺ. Ní bi yíkìi túŋkì-u ki bālifì-u yii: «A-dāantam nee mɔ̄ deeee?»

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí-bi yii: «An mɔ̄! M dɔ́miń kí ŋá m-Dindaan saraa ní. Ní ŋámaan ni-ba circir kí dāam̄maan tí ŋá saraa.» Ní u bí Jeesee nì u-jipɔmbi mun yii: «Ní ŋámaan ni-ba circir kí dāan̄ tí ŋámaan saraa gbanti.»

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Jeesee nì u-jipɔmbi bāańee ní Samiyeel ká Eeliyaab ní ki lī u-neen yii: «Báà an ŋá pu, un bí nee ní ti-Dindaan lēē.»

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Ama ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Taa kpèè u-gbannyaaŋŋu nì u-fɔkɔŋŋu pu, maa lēē-u. Maa kpèé kii binib nín kpèé puee. Di sá yii tin unil nimbil wāĺee ní u kpèé. Ama ti-Dindaan úǹ kpèé dipɔbil poon ní.»

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Ní Jeesee yíiń Abinadaab, ki yāntì u dɔ́miń ki jítì Samiyeel nimbiin, ama ní u bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan kaa lēē un bí nee mun.»

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Jeesee yāntì Sama dɔ́miń ki jítì, ní Samiyeel bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan kaa lēē-u.»

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Jeesee yāntì u-jipɔmbi biluli dɔ́miń ki jítì Samiyeel nimbiin, ní u bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan kaa pée lēē báà ubɔ bi-kansikin.»

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí Jeesee yii: «A-jipɔmbi kɔkɔ dɔ́mińaaa?» Ní u bí yii: «Aayee, bi-kɔkɔ kaa yá, an kíǹ ujoolkaa, úǹ bíi kpàá ipii.» Ní Samiyeel bí Jeesee yii: «Tɔ̄ bí yíiń-u, see ú bàń ní tí nín jī saraa jinti.»

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Jeesee tú bi yíiń Daafiidi. Kinaacimpɔmbikee nìn máǹ ní púlpul ní u-nimbiin ŋān̄ an kaa cáá bí lì. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Samiyeel yii: «Úǹ dee! Yīkì kí bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī u-yil pu ú kpántí ubɔti.»

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Samiyeel yōoǹ ŋyin ŋun poon ŋkpam kēe ki bātì ki sītì Daafiidi yil pu u-nabiyaamu kansikin. Ki yōoǹ ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan Fam kpákatìń Daafiidi pu, ki bí u-cee. Míǹ boonee ní Samiyeel fātìi nín gítí Raama tiŋkin.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Fam nìn yíkì Saayuul cee, ní ti-Dindaan tūǹní ŋfaŋkpitim miba, mi dòoń ki sàantí-u.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Saayuul tɔntɔnliibi bí-u yii: «Ti ká yii ti-Dindaan tūǹní ŋfaŋkpitim miba mi dòoń ki sàantí-si.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Ti-baa, timbi bí ki tīī-si ní. An sá á pɔ̄ kinyɔkɔ ní timbi ń cùú nyàab̀-si un ŋūǹ ki bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeuee. Mimmee Unimbɔti yaa ti túnní ŋfaŋkpitimee a-puee, ú nīn bíi bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu ní an ŋá a-pu fòooo.»

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí u-tɔntɔnliibi yii: «An ŋān̄, nyàab̀maan ubeebɔɔmɔnti kí cáań-mi.»

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Ní u-tɔntɔnliibi kansikin ubɔ bí yii: «M nyí ubɔ, Jeesee un sá Beetileemee jipɔɔn. U ŋūǹ ki bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu tiŋan, ki cáá dibaatandi, ki sòoǹ tibɔti nì iciin ki ŋān̄ uninja, ní ti-Dindaan bí u-cee.»

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Saayuul dū binib ki tú Jeesee cee bí tùkù-u yii: «Yàntī a-jipɔɔn Daafiidi upikpaalee ń dāan̄ kí nīn bí m-cee.»

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Jeesee dū kpɔnɔb nì ndaam ntúun, nì diŋɔbil ki túǹ kimaŋ ní ki bí Daafiidi yii ú cáá tīī Saayuul.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Daafiidi bàn̄ Saayuul cee ní ki kpántì u-tɔntɔnliu. Saayuul nìn néeń-u tikpil. Úǹ di nìn tūntí u-janjawanti ki pá u-boon.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Saayuul tú bí tùkù Jeesee yii: «M néeń Daafiidi bɔti, an puee m là yii ú kpántí m-tɔntɔnliu.»

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, Unimbɔti yaa ti túnní ŋfaŋkpitim Saayuul puee, ní Daafiidi ń yòon̄ u-beeku ki bíi bɔ̀ɔ́. Niinee ní án ŋá Saayuul pu fòooo ní ú ŋùŋfì ní ŋfaŋkpitimee ń nyā kí wàatī-u.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab kpáfì bi-janjaliibi kí cù dikɔ̀ndi. Bi nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì Sookoo, Juuda tiŋki kiban, ní ki gāā bi-janjanaapaal Eefeesi-Damiim, Sookoo nì Aseeka kansikin.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn tɔ́kɔ́ dijool diba pu, ní Isirayeel yab mun tɔ́kɔ́ dijool din kíǹee pu ní ditantakal dɔ̄ bi-kansikin.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Unaaciin ubɔ nìn nyánní Fiiliistii yab janjanaapaalin. Bi nìn yíì-u yii Gooliyaati ní u sá Gaati tiŋkin. U-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn kíǹ fiii kí bà meetab bita.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: U nìn dū tasa kúti ki fúuń u-taaŋi, ki bàl̄ tasa kúti kpaŋki.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Daafiidi nín kūū ufiiliistiija ki fātìi bāańee, ní Abineer yōoǹ-u ki cūnnì Saayuul nimbiin. U nìn ŋúb́ ufiiliistiija yil u-ŋaan.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: U-kpaŋki dɔŋu gbìfì kii bisataluliibi dɔyee, ní kikpaŋ biim nyìm̀ ki jítì kiiloobi biluli pu. Un tú u-gbampɔɔlee līī u-nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: U nìn nyēē ŋkɔnjaloon pu kí túĺ Isirayeel yab janjanaapaal ki tátí yii: «Ba pu ní ni bɔ́ntìń dikɔ̀ndi ní? Man sá ufiiliistiija, ní nimbi sá Saayuul yumbui. Lēēmaan unil ubɔ ú nyānní m-cee doo.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: U yaa ŋúń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-mi ki kūū-mee, timbi làá kpántí ni-yumbui. Ama man di yaa pɔ́ɔkiǹ udaan ní ki kūū-uee, nimbi di làá kpántí ti-yumbui.»

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
