translation_verse: Ní unaaciinee gíti bí yii: «M nyáń ki fáá pɔ́ĺee díǹ, ní nyāntiń unil ubɔ man nì u ń já.»

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Saayuul nì u-naacimbi nín gbìl̄ ufiiliistiijee sòon̄ puee ní dinyoondi kɔ́-bi bi nyùn̄ ŋkpatim.

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Daafiidi baa nìn sá Eefiraata naakookun ní ki bí Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin. Bi nìn yíì-u yii Jeesee, ní u nìn cáá jipɔmbi binii. Saayuul yuntiŋuee, u nìn púĺ ní binib nìn tɔ́-u.

english_verse: the oldest was Eliab, the next was Abinadab, and Shammah was the third. The three of them had gone off to fight in Saul's army. David was Jesse's youngest son.
translation_verse: Daafiidi úǹ nìn sá ujoolkaa, ní u-mambi bitee bíǹ nìn nóó Saayuul ki cūtì kujaau.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn cáà Saayuul cee ní ki nìn fàtīi gítiń Beetileem ki kpèé u-baa piii.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Gooliyaati ufiiliistiija nìn pée dòoń ki yūlifí Isirayeel yab janjaliibi nimbiin, taafaau nì joou áli iwiin imuŋku ili.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Ní u yōoǹ u-kpandɔŋu ní ki lútì ataŋkpee ŋin jɔ̀m̀ee aŋmoo mbunni ki dūu ŋá u-naakpaagbeelkuun. U nìn yōoǹ u-jaataafuŋku ki ŋúb́, ní ki nín cá ufiiliistiijee cee.

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Jeesee bí Daafiidi yii: «Yòon̄ bilee biliŋ ŋin bi kìn̄ee nì kpɔnɔb saalaa nee. Sāǹ malaa kí cùnnì kí tīī a-mambi dijanjanaapaalin.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Á kpáaǹ waagaasiibi saalaa nee kí tīī un kpèé bijanjaliibi kutuku kitilee kpiliu. Á kpáàá kpèè yii a-mambi bí laafiyaa, ní kí fōoń ti-ba bi-cee ḿ béé yii bi lafun pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋan.

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Ku wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní Daafiidi dū u-piii ki kpāaǹ ubɔ, ní ki yōoǹ tijinee kii u-baa nín bí yii ú ŋá puee ki búntì. U bàn̄ dijanjanaapaal puee bijanjaliibi bíi fátí ukaabu kí bòon̄ dikɔmbool pu.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab tí nyáń ki yúl̀ ŋkɔnjaloon pu ki túĺ tɔb.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Daafiidi bàn̄ee ní ki túutì u-waŋgul ki kpāaǹ un kā ki cí awaŋgulee ní ki sáǹ ki nín cá kujaaun ki cūtìi jáam̀ u-mambi.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u dáá bíi sòoǹ nì u-mambee ní ufiiliistiija Gooliyaati, ujanjakpil un sá Gaati tiŋkinee tí nyánní u-yab kansikin ki fáá pɔ́ĺee. Daafiidi nìn gbìl̄ tin kɔkɔ u sòon̄ee.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab yaa ká unaaciinee nín bí miŋyee ní bi fàŋkí yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ ki túlifí boon.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn bí ki sòoǹ nì tɔb yii: «Kéè ni ká unaaciin neeyaa, u là kí táká Isirayeel yabee pu ní u tí nyánní nee. Ama ubɔ yaa ŋúń ki kūū-u, ubɔti làá tīī-u tigaajati tikpil. U làá dū u-bisal kí pɔ̄-u ticati, ní kí pɔ̄ u-dicaŋkun yab diyimɔɔl bí taa ti pà lampoo Isirayeel tiŋkin.»

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: Daafiidi bālifì binib bin yú u-caŋinee yii: «Ba ní bi làá tīī unil un yaa ŋúń ki kūū ufiiliistiija nee ki nyántì Isirayeel yab icoo poon ní? Ní ŋma di baasii sá ufiiliistiija un kaa gíí dikpancandi ní ki yú ki sìí Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee janjaliibi míǹ ní?»

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū Daafiidi kun bi pōoǹ kí tīī un di yaa ŋúń ki kūū unaaciin gbantee.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: U-maan Eeliyaab nín gbìl̄ u bíi sòoǹ nì bijanjaliibee, ní u fōō u-pu diŋuul, ní ki bí yii: «A nyàab̀ ba doo? Ŋma ní a dū a-pikitiiki ki kpāaǹ kuteeun niin? M nyí a-lambil nì a-pɔɔgbifiŋŋu pu! A pée là kí kpèè kujaauee pu ní a dɔ́miń.»

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «Ba ní m ŋá? Ḿ taa bàlifì tibɔtaaa?»

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Ní u yāntì u-maan ki cūtìi bālifì ujanjal ubɔ tibɔbaantiil, ní u mun gíiǹ ki téeǹ unipeekaa nín bàà lī puee.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Ama binib gbìl̄ tin Daafiidi sòon̄ee ní ki cūtìi dūu máafì ubɔti Saayuul ní úǹ yíiń-u.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: Daafiidi bí ubɔti yii: «Ubɔ pɔbil ń taa yīkì ufiiliistiija nee pu. Man a-tɔntɔnliu làá cùú já nì u.»

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Saayuul bí Daafiidi yii: «Saa ŋūǹ kí já nì ufiiliistiija nee. Sii dáá sá kibiki ní, ama doooo úǹ naacimpɔntin ní u pée sá ujanjal.»

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí Saayuul yii: «Man a-tɔntɔnliu yaa nìn bíi kpàá m-baa piii ní gbikinti àá digbiŋgbil yaa nìn dɔ́miń kí cúú dipibil dibee,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: m nìn jì di-boon ní kí fōō dipibil di-nyɔkɔn. Di yaa nìn fātìń kí cúú-mee ní ḿ cúú di-neen ní kí gbá kí kpɔ̀-dì.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Man a-tɔntɔnliu kūū gbikinti ki kūū digbiŋgbil. Míǹ ní m làá tí kpɔ̀ ufiiliistiija un kaa gíí dikpancandi nee, kii ipeel gbanti kansikin ubɔee, kun puee u sīī Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee.»

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi gíti bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan un fōō-mi gbikinti nì digbiŋgbil ŋaŋŋatin ki líìyee làá tí fōō-mi ufiiliistiija nee ŋaan kí líí.» Niinee ní Saayuul bí Daafiidi yii: «Too nín̄ cá ti-Dindaan ń nīn bí a-cee.»

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul dū úǹ u-ba janjawanti ki pēeǹ-u. U nìn dū tasa kúti fuuliiki ki cíkiǹ-u ní ki dū digbampɔɔl ki pēeǹ-u.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: Daafiidi pēeǹ míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki dū Saayuul tàataajiki ki gbìn̄. U nìn mākaǹ kí còom̀, ama ní an kaa cá. Di sá yii waa nìn mántiǹ tiwan gbanti. Niinee ní u bí Saayuul yii: «Maa ŋūǹ kí dū tiwanee kí còom̀, di sá yii an kaa mántiǹ-mi.» Niinee ní Daafiidi lēē Saayuul janjawanti ki bíl̀.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Niinee Gooliyaati bíi sútí ki mɔ̀tīi pìl̀ Daafiidi. Un nìn tú u-janjawantee nìn līī u-nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: Ufiiliistiija kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ Daafiidi, di sá u nìn ká yii u sá kinaacimpɔmbiki ki máǹ púlpul ní u-nimbiin ŋān̄ an kaa cáá bí lì.

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: Ní ufiiliistiija bí Daafiidi yii: «M sá kibɔkɔ a dòoń kí já nì mi ki ŋúb́ ŋkpandɔɔɔ?» Niinee ní u yíiń Daafiidi Fiiliistii yab waaŋi.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: Ní ufiiliistiijee bí Daafiidi yii: «Dāan̄ doo, m làá dū a-wunnanti kí tīī inoon nì ipeel í jī.»

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Daafiidi bí-u yii: «Sii ŋúbiń kitàataajiki nì kikpaŋ nì dicɔbil ní kí dāá jáǹ man. Ama ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab janjaliibi Nimbɔtiu un a sìíyee yindi ní m làá dūú jáǹ-si.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Díǹ nee gba, ti-Dindaan làá dū-si kí ŋá m-ŋaan. M làá kpɔ̀-si kí lēē a-yil. Díǹ gba ní m làá dū Fiiliistii yab janjaliibi nikpiliŋ kí tīī inoon nì ipeel í jī. Niin ní kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ làá béé yii Isirayeel yab cáá Unimbɔti.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ kpáfì ki yú doo nee ń béé yii an kaa sá kitàataajiki, kaa ti sá kikpaŋ ní ti-Dindaan cáa fìil̄. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di yì dikɔ̀ndi nee, ní ki dū-ni ki ŋá ti-ŋaan.»

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Daafiidi dū u-ŋal ki bɔ́ u-gbeelikuun ki lēeń ditaŋkpal diba ki ŋá u-jaataafuŋkun ki tɔ́, ní ditaŋkpal cūtìi cúú Gooliyaati yigbeel. Ditaŋkpalee nìn kɔ́ poon poon ní u lítì dicincibil.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Daafiidi nìn dū kujaataafuŋ nì ditaŋkpal ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ ufiiliistiija. U nìn yá-u ki lúkú ní ki kūū-u, kitàataajiki kaa kútì poon.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi sáǹ ki cūtìi tɔ́kɔǹ Gooliyaati pu, ní ki cúú u-tàataajiki ki fúutì kujitooun ki púntì-u ní ki lēē u-yil. Fiiliistii yab nín ká yii bi-janjakpiliu kpíìyee ní bi sáǹ.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab fáá ijanjakuŋkuunti ní ki fāā ki bīiǹ Fiiliistii yab boon áli ki tin bàn̄ Gaati nì Eekrɔn timmun. Fiiliistii yab nikpiliŋ nìn dɔ̄ Saarayiim dandi pu míǹ ní áli ki tin sāā Gaati nì Eekrɔn timmun.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab jìn̄ Fiiliistii yab boon míǹ ki fātìńee ní ki kɔ́ bi-janjanaapaalin ki fúkúl̀ bi-wanti.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn yōoǹ ufiiliistiija yil ki cáa cùnnì Jeerusaleem ní ki dū ufiiliistiijee janjawanti ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ úǹ u-ba bìŋ́ku poon. Bi cáá Daafiidi ki dàkā Saayuul

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Saayuul nìn ká Daafiidi cá kí já nì ufiiliistiijee ní u bālifì ujanjakpil Abineer yii: «Abineer, ŋma jipɔɔn di sá kinaacimpɔmbiki nee ní?» Ní Abineer kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, maa nyí.»

english_verse: “Then find out!” Saul told him.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Bàlifì kí béé un jipɔɔn ní u sée.»

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Saayuul bālifì-u yii: «Unaacimpɔɔn, ŋma jipɔɔn di sá-si ní?» Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «A-tɔntɔnliu Jeesee u sá Beetileemee jipɔɔn di sá-mi.»

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Saayuul kaa nìn yāntì Daafiidi fātì u-baa dumpu yaadal, ní u fōō-u u bí u-cee.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Joonatan nìn yāntì u nì Daafiidi pōoǹ ki pūtì kí nīn sá bibɔɔtiibi, kun puee u nìn néeń-u kii úǹ u-bee ní.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Joonatan nìn pēetì u-bɔkutikpaandi ki dūu tīī Daafiidi. U nìn tīī-u u-bɔkutiŋ mun, áli ki dū u-tàataajiki nì u-tɔbu nì u-gbajau ki tīī-u.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Ŋyunti kamaa Saayuul yaa nìn tú Daafiidi kujaauee, u nìn jáà ki jīǹ ní. An pu ní Saayuul nìn dū-u ki ŋá u-janjakpiliu. Samaa kɔkɔ nìn néeń u-bɔti, ki kpáaǹ Saayuul kàliŋkpilib. Saayuul bíi nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀ Daafiidi

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nín kūū ufiiliistiija Gooliyaati ki fātìi kùnnée, binimpoobi nìn nyánní Isirayeel yab timmu kɔkɔn ki túŋkì ubɔti Saayuul ki gà ilan ki ŋōō ki kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi ki bɔ̀ɔ́ ŋgaŋgamu nì cancakantib.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Bi nìn gà ilan ki kíikí tɔb yii: «Saayuul kūū binib kutuku, ní Daafiidi kūū binib cutimaanyi.»

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Saayuul nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní u fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu, di sá nlanee kaa nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u. U nìn bí yii: «Bi bí yii Daafiidi kūū binib cutimaanyi ní man kūū binib kutuku jaa! Mimmee tin pée kíǹ ú fōōyee di sá dibeelaa!»

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe Unimbɔti túnní ŋfaŋkpitim miba, mi dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ u-ni ní u fītì u-diikun. Daafiidi nìn bíi bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu kii u nín pée kpààa bɔ̀ɔ́ puee. Saayuul nìn ŋúb́ u-kpaŋki u-ŋaan.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Dicilpuee Saayuul dū kikpaŋ ki tɔ́ Daafiidi ki lī yii: «M làá pée yā Daafiidi kí nákań digundi ní.» U ŋá míǹ mba mbee mili, ní Daafiidi lóotì.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Saayuul nìn fāŋkì Daafiidi, kun puee u nìn béè yii ti-Dindaan bí Daafiidi cee ní ki dū úǹ ki fá.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Tin kɔkɔ Daafiidi yaa nìn ŋáańee, an nìn bútí-u ní, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn bí u-cee.

english_verse: This made Saul even more afraid of David.
translation_verse: Saayuul nín ká an bútì-u miŋyee ní u fāŋkì-u.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab nìn néeń Daafiidi, kun puee úǹ di nìn lìntī bi-nyɔkɔpu ní bi jáà ki jīǹ. Daafiidi kpántì ubɔti coo

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Saayuul bí Daafiidi yii: «M-biseekpiliu Meerab sɔ̀. M làá dū-u kí tīī-si á cáá. Ama a máaǹ kí dàkà difaŋgiil m-tundi poon ní kí já ti-Dindaan jaaku.» Di sá u nìn lī u-neen yii: «Maa làá kpɔ̀ Daafiidi m-ba, m làá yàntī Fiiliistii yab ní ń kpɔ̀-u.»

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí Saayuul yii: «Man di sá ŋma, ní tilati poon ní m-baa dicaŋku nì u-maaliŋu bí Isirayeel yab kansikin, ní man un bí nee ń nīn sá ubɔti coo?»

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Ama an ŋmāntì ubɔti Saayuul ń dū u-bisal Meerab kí tīī Daafiidi ticatee ní u dū-u ki tīī Adriyeel umeeyoolaaja.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Ama Saayuul bisal Miikaal nìn là Daafiidi. Saayuul nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul lī u-neen yii: «M làá dū-u kí tīī Daafiidi ń cáá án nín làá ŋá pu ú nīn sá-u kutaliŋŋu Fiiliistii yab ń ŋmā kí kpɔ̀-uee.» Niinee ní Saayuul bí Daafiidi nliliitiim yii: «Díǹ nee, a làá kpántí m-coo.»

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul kàliŋkpilibee cáá an bɔtee ki lī Daafiidi cee, ní úǹ bí-bi yii: «Ni dàkafī yii á nīn sá ubɔti cooyee, an sá gbaŋgbam níii? Man sá usoodaan ní kaa bí tiban.»

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Ubɔti kàliŋkpilib gíiǹní Daafiidi nín kíí puee ki tùkū ubɔti.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí yii: «Ni nín làá sòoǹ nì Daafiidi puee sèé: <Ubɔti kaa là á ŋá kucootiiu. Kun u bàlifī-see di sá á cáań-u Fiiliistii yab kuncooti dilaataal ú tɔ̀ u-nannanliibi ipɔntoon.» Saayuul nìn dàkafī yii u yaa ŋá mimmee, Daafiidi làá kɔ́ Fiiliistii yab ŋaan bí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Saayuul kàliŋkpilib cáań tibɔti tin u lēe ki tùkū Daafiidi. Daafiidi ká yii án nín sá ú ŋá pu kí kpántí ubɔti cooyee ŋān̄. Kí wàatī ŋyunti ŋun ubɔti yóoǹee ń bàńee,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Saayuul ká ki béè yii ti-Dindaan bí Daafiidi cee ní u-bisal Miikaal néeń-u.

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Niinee Saayuul mɔ̄tìi fāŋkì Daafiidi, ní ki kíǹ ki ná-u an kaa cáá digbèendi.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi nìn dòoń ki jáà nì Isirayeel yab. Kujaau kamaa poonee, Daafiidi nìn jáà ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ binannanliibi ki jítiǹ Saayuul janjaliibi bin kíǹee. An nìn yāntì u nyáń diyindi tikpil.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Saayuul nìn tùkū u-jipɔɔn Joonatan nì u-kàliŋkpilib kɔkɔ yii u là bí kpɔ̀ Daafiidi. Ama Saayuul jipɔɔn Joonatan nì Daafiidi nìn kɔ́ tɔbin tiŋan.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: M làá fu céeǹ m-baa tí cù kusaau laakin a làá cùú báĺee. M làá fu sòoǹ nì m-baa a-pu. U yaa fu sòon̄ puee, m làá tùkù-si.»

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: U nìn dū u-maŋfal ki sú ní ki kūū ufiiliistiija. Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ dijajikpaandi. Sii a-ba nìn ká ki fāal̀. Kin ba pu ní a làá ŋá ikpiti kí kpɔ̀ Daafiidi un kaa ŋá tibee fám.»

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Niinee Saayuul gbìl̄ ki tīiǹ Joonatan ní ki pūtì yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan yii baa làá kpɔ̀ Daafiidi.»

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Niinee Joonatan yíiń Daafiidi ní ki tùkū-u tin jítèe kɔkɔ. U nìn cáań Daafiidi Saayuul cee, ní Daafiidi fātìi kíĺ ki bíi tūǹ u-tundi kii u nín nìn pée bí ki tūǹ pu dooooyee. Miikaal fīī Daafiidi

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nì Isirayeel yab jaaku fātìi tí kíĺ. Daafiidi cūtì ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ, ní bi sáǹ-u.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Saayuul dū binib ki tú Daafiidi dumpu bí cɔ̄ŋkì-u kutaa yaa wúntì kutaafaauee bí kpɔ̀-u. U-nimpuu gbìl̄ ní ki tùkū-u yii: «A yaa kaa sáǹ kunyeeu nee, fool bi làá fu kpɔ̀-si!»

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Ní u-nimpuu yōoǹ-u ki dī tɔkɔla pu ki nāatì boon ní u sáǹ ki ŋmátì.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Miikaal yōoǹ diwaal ki bíl̀ Daafiidi dooŋu pu, ní ki dū ŋŋɔgban ki bíl̀ diyil pú, ní ki dū dibɔkutikpaandi ki bīiǹ di-pu múlmul.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Bininjab bin Saayuul túnní bí dāá cúú Daafiidee bāańee ní u-nimpuu bí-bi yii: «U būǹ.»

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul fātìi gíiǹ-bi ki tú bí cùú ká Daafiidi. U bí-bi yii: «Yòon̄nímaan-u kí kpáaǹ u-dooŋu ḿ kpɔ̀-u!»

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Binibee fātìi bàn̄ Daafiidi dumpu ki kpēēyee diwaal di pá ndoo pu, ŋŋɔgban dɔ̄ diyil púee.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí Miikaal yii: «Ba pu ní a kíil̀-mi ki yāntì m-nannanliu sáǹ ki ŋmátì.» Ní Miikaal kíí-u yii: «Úǹ di bí-mi yii: <A yaa kaa yāntì m sáǹ ki ŋmátì, m làá kpɔ̀-si.>» Saayuul nì Daafiidi bí Raama

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Daafiidi sáǹ mimmee ní ki búntì Samiyeel cee Raama, ki máafì-u Saayuul nín ŋá-u tiŋyee kɔkɔ. Ní u nì Samiyeel cūtìi kóò Nayooti.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Bi cūtìi tùkū Saayuul yii: «Kpèè Daafiidi cūtìi bí Nayooti tiŋkin, Raama caŋin.»

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul tú binib bí cùú cúuń-u. Bi bàn̄ee ki ká Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi dikitil, bi-kpiliu Samiyeel līī bi-nyɔkɔpu bi fītì ki bí ki nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti. Ní Unimbɔti Fam kɔ́ binib bin Saayuul túnnée ni ní bi mun fītì.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Saayuul ní u dū biba mun ki tú, bi mun bàn̄ee ki fītì. Ní u dū bitataatiibi ki tú, bi mun tí bàn̄ee ní ki fītì.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Saayuul yíkìi nín cá u-ba Raama. U bàn̄ Seeku nyimbɔbikpaandee ní ki bālifì yii: «Samiyeel nì Daafiidi bí la pú ní?» Ní bi bí-u yii: «Bi bí Nayooti, Raama caŋin.»

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: U cá ki bàn̄ nsannee ní Unimbɔti Fam kɔ́ u mun ní u fītì ní u nìkī u-saŋŋu ki tin bàn̄ Nayooti, Raama caŋin.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Niin ní u mun pēetì u-bɔkutiŋ ní ki fītì Samiyeel nimbiin. U nìn lítì ki dɔ̄ dicancaŋgbeel ŋwiin gbanti nì kunyeeu kɔkɔ. An pu ní bi lì yii: «Saayuul mun kpántì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu níii?»

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Daafiidi yíkì Nayooti Raama caŋin ki sáǹ ki cūtìi ká Joonatan ki bí-u yii: «M baasii ŋá a-baa ba ní? Ba kpitii ní m ŋá-u àá tilati poon ní m yīntiǹ-u ní u nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-mi ní?»

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Ní Joonatan kíí-u yii: «Mbusu ń cù ndan, aa làá kpú. M-baa kaa ŋáań tiba kaa tùkū-mi. Ba pu ní u bál̀-mi tibɔti nee? An kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Daafiidi pée cɔ́ yii: «M pūtì yii an sá míǹ ní. A-baa nyí man nì sii nín bɔ́ɔtée. An pu ní u máaǹ ki tin lī u-neen yii: <Joonatan ń taa béé tibɔti nee án nín làá ŋá pu án taa páb́-uee.> Ama nì ti-Dindaan un bí nee, nì sii un mun bí nee, m làá tùkù-si yii maa ti dátì nì ŋkúm.»

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joonatan bí Daafiidi yii: «Tin a yaa pée lèe, m làá ŋá míǹ kí tīī-si.»

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Daafiidi bí Joonatan yii: «Fool di fu sá uŋmapɔɔn. An bàà sá yii ḿ kàl̄ kí kɔ́ĺ ubɔti ní tí jī tijin. Ama a yaa kíí, m làá cùú báĺ kusaaun áli kujoou.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: A-baa yaa fu dáań ki ká yii m kpá ní u bíi bàlifī m-puee, á tùkù-u yii: <Daafiidi mēē-mi nsan kí sāǹ kí cù Beetileem u-dumpu, u nì u-dicaŋkun yab ń ŋá dibindi kamaa saraau.>

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: A-baa yaa fu kíí yii: <Too an ŋān̄.> Mimmee man a-tɔntɔnliu pɔbil làá nīn sɔ̀m̀, ama u yaa fu fōō diŋuulee, á béé yii u baasii là kí kpɔ̀-mi ní.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee á dàkà-mi dineembaamɔndi, kun puee a pūtì ki pōoǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii man nì si làá nīn sá bibɔɔtiibi. Báà kun ní m yaa pée ŋá ki yīntèe, kpɔ̀-mi a-ba. Taa cáá-mi kí tīī a-baa.»

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Niinee Joonatan fáá mbiil yii: «M kpá kí ŋá míǹ jaanjaan! M yaa béè yii m-baa baasii nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-see, m pūtì yii m làá tùkù-si.»

english_verse: “How will you do that?” David asked.
translation_verse: Daafiidi bí Joonatan yii: «A-baa yaa kpātì a-pu mpɔnee, ŋma di làá dāá tùkù-mi?»

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Joonatan bí Daafiidi yii: «Dāan̄ tí nyā kí cù kusaaun!» Ní bi-liitil nyáń ki búntì.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Joonatan bí yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu yii fool àá daapudal naŋkɔnampuee, m bālifì m-baa ki béè nlandɔkɔ ŋun u cáá a-puee dee. U yaa cáá a-pu nlandɔkɔmɔntee, maa làá tɔ̄ń ubɔ ń tùkù-si.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Ama m-baa yaa bíi nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-si ní m ŋmí kaa tùkū-see, ti-Dindaan ń dáaĺ m-tafal ŋkpitim pu. M làá yàntī á búntí nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. Unimbɔti ń nīn bí a-cee kii u nín nìn bí m-baa cee puee.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: á dāá dàkà m-dicaŋkun yab kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu, ki kpáaǹ ŋyunti ŋun ní ti-Dindaan làá dāá kúntí a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ubɔ ubɔ kitiŋ puee.»

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joonatan pūtì ki pōoǹ Daafiidi nì u-dicaŋkun yab ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń dāá tɔ̀ Daafiidi nannanliibi ipɔntoon.»

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Joonatan bí Daafiidi yii ú pùtī kí pòon̄ kubɔɔtiiu kun bi cáá tɔb puee pu. Di sá yii Joonatan nìn néeń Daafiidi kii u nín néeń u-ba puee ní.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Ní Joonatan fātìi bí yii: «Fool di fu sá uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaaliu. Bi làá fu béé yii a kpá, kun puee a-jal làá fu nīn yú fám.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Daapudalee, á dāá cù laakin tibɔti nee nín kíĺ a nìn cūtì ki bál̀ee. Á yūĺ Eeseel taŋkpal caŋin.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Man làá dāan̄ kí bíití mpaan ŋubɔ pu kí tɔ̄ ipiin ita.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, m làá tɔ̄ m-naacimpɔmbiki ú cùú nyàabìń-i. M yaa bí-u yii: <Ipiin bí a-nyɔkɔpu fiii, cùú cóotiń-iee!>, an dàkà yii an sá á gítiń mmɔŋki ní tiba kaa làá ŋá-si. Nì ti-Dindaan puee, á taa fàŋkì.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Ama m yaa téeń ki tùkū m-naacimpɔmbikee yii: <Ipiin bí ndan a-nyɔkɔpuee!>, mimmee á nīn cá, di sá yii ti-Dindaan di là á búntí.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Ama an yaa kíǹ man nì si nín pūtì ki pōoǹ tiŋyee, ti-Dindaan di làá tūtuǹ-ti tí nīn yú deedee kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi cūtìi bál̀ kusaaun. Uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaaliu dalee, ní ubɔti kāl̀ bí jī tijin.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: U nìn kāl̀ u-jal din pu u pée kpààa kàal̀ee. Di nìn yú ki nákáǹ digundi. Joonatan nìn kā ki túĺ-u, ní Abineer kā ki kɔ́ĺ-u. Ama Daafiidi jal nìn yú fám.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Yaadalee Saayuul kaa nìn lī tiba, di sá u nìn lī u-neen yii: «An yaa yíì, waa nyí ní ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi tiban. Báà an ŋá pu, u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ní.»

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Ama uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaaliu ŋwinliliiti dalee, Daafiidi jal tí dɔ̄ fám waa bí. Ní Saayuul bālifì u-jipɔɔn Joonatan yii: «Ba pu ní Jeesee jipɔɔn kaa dɔ́miń fool nì díǹ ki jíń tijin ní?»

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: U bí-mi yii: <M gbāam̀-si, pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ cù m-dumpu, di sá yii ti cáá kudicaŋu saraa ubɔ ki làá ŋá ti-tiŋkin, ní m-maan bí yii an pée sá ḿ dāan̄ ní. An puee, pɔ̄-mi diyimɔɔl ḿ cùú ká m-mambi.> An pu ní waa dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ ubɔti cee bí jī tijin.»

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Saayuul fōō u-jipɔɔn Joonatan pu diŋuul ní ki téeń yii: «Kibɔpimpiŋ kin bí nee! M nyí a nín yú Jeesee jipɔɔn boonee. Si nì a-na cooi dee.

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jeesee jipɔɔn bí dimaŋfalinee, a pée kpá kí kpántí ubɔti ní a-beel kpá kí kàl̄ kí báań. Kɔŋkɔnnee, yàntī bí cùú cúuń-u kí cáań-mi doo, di sá yii u máaǹ bí kpɔ̀-u ní.»

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Ní Joonatan kíí u-baa yii: «Ba pu ní u máaǹ kí kpú ní? Ba ní u baasii ŋá ní?»

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul dúkutì kikpaŋ kí bàà fáá-u. Niinee Joonatan béè yii u-baa baasii lēē kí pée kpɔ̀ Daafiidi ní.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Joonatan yíkì tijin pu nì diŋuul ki yíì kaa ti jíń tiba jiŋaal gbanti winliliitiŋu dal, kun puee u-baa nín nìn sīī Daafiidi miŋyee nìn kɔ́ǹ-u kunimbaau.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Joonatan nín cá kusaaun laakin u nì Daafiidi nìn sòon̄ ki yóoǹ yii bi làá ká tɔbee. Kinaacimpɔmbiki kiba nìn céeǹ-u.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Joonatan bí kinaacimpɔmbikee yii: «Á sāǹ kí cùú cóotiń-mi ipiin in m làá tɔ̄ nee.» Ní kinaacimpɔmbikee sáǹ ki búntì, ní Joonatan tɔ́ mpiin an cāatì ki-pu.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Kinaacimpɔmbikee nín bàn̄ laakin mpiinee cɔ́ee ní Joonatan téeń yii: «Mpiinee kaa cɔ́ ndan a-nyɔkɔpuɔɔɔ?

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Nín̄ cá malaa, taa yūĺ!» Ní kinaacimpɔmbikee cūtìi cóotìń mpiin ki nín gítiń u-kpiliu cee.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Kinaacimpɔmbikee kaa nìn nyí tin nìn bíi jītée. See Joonatan nì Daafiidi baba di nìn nyí.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Joonatan nìn dū u-tɔbu nì ipiin ki tīī kinaacimpɔmbikee, ní ki bí-kì yii: «Cáá kpìnnì.»

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Kinaacimpɔmbikee nín kùǹee ní Daafiidi nyánní ditaŋkpakpukul boon laakin u nìn bál̀ee. U nìn gbāaǹ Joonatan nimbiin u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ ŋfunyɔm mita. Boonee ní bi kpàl̄ tɔb ní bi-liitil súń tikpil ki yúntì.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Ní Joonatan bí Daafiidi yii: «Nín̄ cá nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. Di sá yii ti-liitil pūtì ki pōoǹ tɔb ti-Dindaan yindi pu. Ti-Dindaan ń nīn sá man nì sii nì ti-maaliŋun yab seeradaaŋwu kí nīn cá jaanjaan.>»

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi kíĺ nsan ki nín cá, ní Joonatan mun nín gítiń mmɔŋki. Daafiidi bí Noob tiŋki usaraaŋakpil Ayiimeeleeki cee

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Daafiidi búntì Noob tiŋkin usaraaŋakpil Ayiimeeleeki cee. Ní úǹ sáǹní u-wunti jìkì ki dɔ́miń ki túŋkì-u, ki bālifì-u yii: «Ba ŋá ní a nóoń a-baba ubɔ kaa céeǹní-si?»

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí usaraaŋakpil yii: «Ubɔti tú-mi ní ki tīī-mi mara ki lī yii: <Ubɔ ń taa béé tibɔti tin pu m tú-see.> An puee m dàkā m-naacimbi laakin bi làá kíntí-mee.

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Too, ba jinti di bí a-cee á tīī-mi? Tīī-mi kpɔnɔb biŋmoo àá tin a yaa pée kée.»

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋakpil kíí-u yii: «Maa cáá kpɔnɔfantanti, see kpɔnɔb bin bi cáań ki ŋá saraayee. M ŋūǹ kí dū-bi kí tīī-si a-naacimbi yaa kaa gbēē binimpoobi.»

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «Taa gbēē binimpoobi, kii ti nín yaa cá kujaau, taa cáá nsan kí gbēē binimpoobi puee ní. Kí kūtèe, m-naacimbi janjawanti bí circir. Báà ti yaa kaa bíi jáà kujaau nee nì Unimbɔti yindi puɔɔɔ, tijanjawan nín pée gíti dáá bí circiree, ku mun kpántì circir dee.»

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Niinee usaraaŋakpil dū kpɔnɔb bin bi cáań ki ŋá saraayee ki tīī-u, kun puee kpɔnɔb biba mun kaa nìn gíti bí. An nìn sá kpɔnɔb bin bi nìn páatì ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí fàtīí dū bipɔmbi bin bi dáá púĺee kí páańee ní.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: Yaadal wiiŋŋuee, Saayuul tɔntɔnliu ubɔ nìn bí usaraaŋakpil Ayiimeeleeki cee kí ŋá saraa. Bi nìn yíì-u yii Dooweegi, u sá ueedoomja ní ki nìn sá Saayuul naakpaakpiliu.

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Daafiidi gíti bālifì usaraaŋakpil yii: «Aa cáá kikpaŋ àá kitàataajiki kiba a-cee doo kí tīī-maaa? Ubɔti bɔti tin pu u tú-mee nín páb́ puee, maa ti ká mpaan kí yòon̄ m-tàataajiki àá tijanjawan.»

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Yaadal wiiŋŋu ní Daafiidi yíkì niin ki sáǹ kaa ti pìlīǹ Saayuul. U nìn dūu bàn̄ Gaati yab bɔtiu Akiisi cee.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi gíiǹ u-ba kii uwaatee, ki sòoǹ fám fam, ní ki yú ki lùtī mpunyɔmu pu, ki yàntī timɔtan kɔ̀tifī u-nyimpul pu.

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Akiisi bí u-kàliŋkpilib yii: «Ni ká yii unil nee sá uwaati ní. Kin ba pu ní ni cáań-u m-cee?

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daafiidi yíkì Gaati tiŋkin ki cūtìi bál̀ Adulaam taŋkpanaakookun. U-nabiyaamu nì u-dicaŋkun yab gbìl̄ mimmee ní bi yíkìi dɔ́miń ki kíǹ ki bí u-cee.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Binib bin nìn bí agìń poonee, nì bin nìn jíń apɔɔnee, nì bin nyɔmmu túŋkèe kɔkɔ nìn dɔ́miń ki bí u-cee. Binib nìn kpáfì kii binib alaataa anaa ki bí u-cee, ní u kpántì bi-kpiliu.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi yíkì niin ki nín cá Miisipa, Moowaab yab tiŋkin, ní ki bí Moowaab bɔtiu yii: «M gbāam̀-si, á yàntī m-baa nì m-na ń dāá nīn kóò a-cee doo, kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun m làá béé Unimbɔti nín làá ŋá-mi puee.»

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Ní u yōoǹní u-baa nì u-na ki cáań ki kāaǹ Moowaab bɔtiu cee. Niin ní bi kāl̀ kí yòon̄ iyunti in kɔkɔ Daafiidi nìn bí dibalinee.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Gaadi bí Daafiidi yii: «Taa nín̄ kā kibalilaŋ nee poon. Yīkì kí nīn cá Juuda tiŋkin.» Ní Daafiidi yíkì ki nín cá Eereeti bambaŋku poon. Saayuul yāntì bi pɔ̄fì Noob saraaŋaliibi kɔkɔ

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Saayuul gbìl̄ yii bi ká Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi. U nìn kā Giibeeya gbantaŋki pu, busubu bun bi yíì tamariisee taapu ki ŋúb́ u-kpaŋki u-ŋaan. U-tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ nìn yú ki māntìi tú-u.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Saayuul bí u-tɔntɔnliibee yii: «Nimbi Beenjameen naakookun yab, ní pīlifìmaan-mi. Ni dàkafī yii Jeesee jipɔɔn làá tīī ni-kɔkɔ tisati nì fiinyi kpaaŋŋaaa? U làá kàan̄ ni-kɔkɔ ní nīn sá binib kutukub kpilib nì binib alaataa kpilibaaa?

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní ni-kɔkɔ nyáń m-boon míǹ. Ni-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nyá-mi kuŋaŋŋaau yii m-jipɔɔn nì Jeesee jipɔɔn pūtì ki pōoǹ tɔb kí nīn sá bibɔɔtiibi. M-bɔti kaa pée ká ni-kansikin báà ubɔ. Ubɔ kaa ŋúń ki tùkū-mi yii m-jipɔɔn sāal̀ m-tɔntɔnliu ú píĺ-mi titalindi, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nee!»

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Dooweegi, ueedoomja nìn bí Saayuul tɔntɔnliibi kansikin. U nìn bí-u yii: «Man ká Jeesee jipɔɔn. U nìn dɔ́miń Noob, Akituub jipɔɔn Ayiimeeleeki cee.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Ayiimeeleeki nìn bālifì ti-Dindaan u-yil pu, ki tīī-u tijin. U nìn dū ufiiliistiija Gooliyaati tàataajiki ki tīī-u.»

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti tú bi yíiń Akituub jipɔɔn Ayiimeeleeki nì u-dicaŋkun yab bin sá bisaraaŋaliibi ki bí Noobee kɔkɔ. Ní bi-kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki yúl̀ ubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí Ayiimeeleeki yii: «Akituub jipɔɔn, á pīlifì tiŋan». Ní u kíí-u yii: «M-dindaan m pílifí.»

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní sii nì Jeesee jipɔɔn ŋá kinyɔkɔ kí já nì mi ní? A tīī-u tijin nì kitàataajiki, ní ki kɔ́ ki bālifì Unimbɔti u-yil pu ú já nì mi kí píĺ-mi titalindi, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nee.»

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Ní Ayiimeeleeki kíí ubɔti yii: «A-tɔntɔnliibi kansikin ubɔ bí ki sá deedee ki bàn̄ Daafiidaaa? Sii ti-baa ubɔti coo dee, ní ki sá bijanjaliibi bin cí-see kpiliu. Úǹ ní dibɔticindin nib kɔkɔ tìì jilma.

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: M yaa bālifì Unimbɔti u-yil puee, an kaa sá mpeepeekaam. Maa pée ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá nyā a-boon kí já nì si. An puee, ti-baa ubɔti, taa dū tibɔti nee kí túń man nì m-dicaŋkun niliu ubɔ pu. Di sá man a-tɔntɔnliu kaa pée nyí tiba tibɔti nee poon.»

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí Ayiimeeleeki yii: «Sii nì a-dicaŋkun nib kɔkɔ làá kpú ní, man di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní u bí bijanjaliibi bin yú ki kɔ́ĺ-uee yii: «Kpɔ̀maan ti-Dindaan saraaŋaliibi nee, kun puee bi yú Daafiidi boon. Bi nyí u nín bíi sáńee ní baa tùkū-mi.» Ama bijanjaliibi yíì kaa kūū ti-Dindaan saraaŋaliibi.

english_verse: Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!” On that same day, Doeg killed
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí Dooweegi yii: «Sii, cùú kpɔ̀ bisaraaŋaliibi nee!» Ní ueedoomja Dooweegi u-ba kūū-bi. Yaadalee, u nìn kūū bisaraaŋaliibi bin pèentí asaraaŋabɔkutee imuŋku inaa nì binib biŋmoo ní.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Saayuul nìn yāntì bi dū ntàataajimu ki kūū Noob, bisaraaŋaliibi tiŋkin nib kɔkɔ. U nìn yāntì bi kūū bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu nì mbipɔmu nì inaa nì mmamu nì ipii.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Ayiimeeleeki jipɔɔn, Akituub naantiiu ubɔbɔ di nìn ŋúń ki sáǹ ki ŋmátì. Bi nìn yíì-u Abiyataar. U nìn sáǹ ki cūtìi bí Daafiidi cee.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Abiyataar di tùkū Daafiidi yii Saayuul kūū ti-Dindaan saraaŋaliibi.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí Abiyataar yii: «M nín nìn ká ueedoomja Dooweegi Noob tiŋkin ŋwiin gbantee, m nìn béè yii u làá tùkù Saayuul tin kɔkɔ jítèe. Míǹ puee man di yì a-baa dicaŋkun nib kɔkɔ kúm.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: An puee nín̄ kā m-cee, á taa fàŋkì tiba. Man nì sii nannanliu sá ubaanti ní. Ama a yaa bí man ceeyee, tiba nì tiba kaa làá ŋá-si.»

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Daafiidi yii Fiiliistii yab dòoń ki tákà Keeyiila yab, ki cá bi-naapaaŋi pu ki kōontí tijin.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «Ḿ cù kí já nì Fiiliistii yabaaa?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «Cù kí já nì bi kí fōō Keeyiila yab bi-ŋaan ki líí.»

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi naacimbi bí-u yii: «Ti dá láá kā Juuda tiŋkin doo nì tifaandi. Ti yaa cūtì ki jáń nì Fiiliistii yab, an kaa làá púntáaa?»

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi gíti bālifì ti-Dindaan nliliitiim, ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá Keeyiila. M làá dū Fiiliistii yab kí ŋá a-ŋaan.»

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi yíkìi nín cá Keeyiila ki jáń nì Fiiliistii yab ki cútì bi-waŋkuti, ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ, ní ki fōō Keeyiila yab bi-ŋaan ki líí.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi gbìl̄ nlandɔkɔkpiti ŋun Saayuul bíi bɔ́ntí u-puee, ní u bí usaraaŋal Abiyataar yii ú cáań eefoodi.

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu, man a-tɔntɔnliu gbìl̄ yii Saayuul bɔ́ntì kí dāá kúntí Keeyiila tiŋki man pu.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Keeyiila tindaŋkpilib làá nyāntí-mi kí tīī-uaaa? Saayuul làá lafun dāan̄ kii man a-tɔntɔnliu nín gbìl̄ bi lī pueeee? M-Dindaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu, an yaa sá puee, tùkù man a-tɔntɔnliu.» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «Saayuul làá dāan̄.»

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi gíti bí yii: «Keeyiila tindaŋkpilib làá nyāntí man nì m-naacimbi kí tīī-uaaa?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «Iiin, bi làá nyāntí-ni kí tīī.»

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Daafiidi bàn̄ Siifi teekun ki kóò ajoon pu titaŋkpanaakɔtin. Ní Saayuul bí ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu ki nyàab̀-u, ama Unimbɔti kaa dū-u ki ŋá u-ŋaan.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nín béè yii Saayuul bíi nyàab̀-u kí lēē u-maŋfalee ní u gbíntì Siifi teekun, Ooreesa tiŋkin.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Saayuul jipɔɔn Joonatan cūtì Ooreesa Daafiidi cee ki tīī-u kunyannyaau ú nīn gbíntìi máká Unimbɔti pu.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: U bí-u yii: «Taa fàŋkì tiba! M-baa Saayuul kaa làá ŋmā kí dū u-ŋal kí máań a-pu. Sii di làá jī dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu, ní man ń nīn sá a-taapu yɔu. M-baa u-ba nyí míǹ tiŋan.»

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Ní bi-liitil pūtì ki pōoǹ tɔb kí nīn sá bibɔɔtiibi ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Ní Daafiidi gbíntì Ooreesa niin ki bí, ní Joonatan fātìi nín kùǹ u-dumpu. Daafiidi ŋmátì Saayuul ŋaan

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Siifi yab cūtì Giibeeya ki tùkū Saayuul yii: «Daafiidi dɔ́miń ki bál̀ timbi tiŋkin, Ooreesa taŋkpanaakɔtin, Akiila jool pu kitimpiliŋ kin sá kuteeuee ŋgiil pú.

english_verse: If you come, we will help you catch him.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ti-baa, a yaa pée là ŋyunti ŋuŋyee, á dāan̄ timbi di làá cúú-u kí ŋúbíǹ-si.»

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul kíí-bi yii: «Nimbi bin súń man saayee, ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ ni-boon.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Ní cù kí mɔ̀tīí nyàab̀ kí béé laakin u baasii bée, kí béé un di ká-u dibɔbil gbantee, di sá bi tùkū-mi yii u sá uŋmatinli ní.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Ní kpèè kí béé ipaan in pu ní u cá ki bāal̀ee kɔkɔ. Ni yaa cúú ibaamɔnee ní gítiń kí tùkù-mi, ní man nì ni ń táá kí cù. U yaa bí Juuda tiŋkinee, m làá fíkití kitiŋee jaaŋŋi kɔkɔ poon nyíki nyiki kí tin ká-u.»

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Niinee Siifi yab yíkì Saayuul cee ki līntì ki nín kùǹ. Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi nìn bí Maawɔn teeku kun bí kitimpiliŋ ŋgiil púee.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Saayuul yōoǹ u-nib bi nín cá kí nyàab̀-u. Ní bi tùkū Daafiidi, ní u yíkì ki nín cá Maawɔn teekun kigbantaŋ kiba pu. Saayuul gbìl̄ u-pu niinee ní ki nín jì u-boon.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Saayuul nì u-nib nìn bí dijool dijandi diba pú, ní Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi bí dijandi din kíǹee pu ki sáń. Daafiidi nìn bíi ŋáań malaa malaa kí sāǹ Saayuul. Di sá yii an nìn kíǹ fiii Saayuul nì u-janjaliibi ń bàà màntī kí tú-bi kí cúú-bi.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Niin kpalaayee ntuun ŋubɔ dɔ́miń ki tùkū Saayuul yii: «Dāan̄ malaa malaa, di sá Fiiliistii yab bíi jáà nì ti-tiŋki.»

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Dicilpu niin ní Saayuul gbēeǹ Daafiidi bɔti pu ki nín cá kí cùú jáǹ Fiiliistii yab. An pu ní bi pú niin diyindi yii: «Diyakatil taŋkpal.»

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Daafiidi yíkì niin ní ki cūtì ki kíǹ ki bí Eeni-Geedii gbantaŋki pu.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Tinaabakal tiba nìn bí nsan caŋin ipii bí poon. Kutaŋkpanaakoou kubɔ nìn bí niin. Bi bàn̄ niinee, Saayuul kɔ́ ataa pu. Asee Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi nìn kɔ́ ki bál̀ poon poon niin.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Daafiidi bí u-naacimbi yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń cúú-mi ḿ taa dū m-ŋal kí gbēē m-kpiliu un Unimbɔti lēēyee. Di sá ti-Dindaan u-ba di lēē-u ú nīn sá ubɔti.»

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: An nyɔɔbuŋŋi ní Daafiidi nìn dūu tātì u-naacimbi lammi. Waa nìn pú-bi nsan bí ŋá Saayuul tiba. Ní ubɔti nyáń kutaŋkpanaakooun ki nìkī u-saŋŋu.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee Daafiidi mun nyánní kutaŋkpanaakoouee poon ki kúuǹ ki yíiń-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔteeee!» Saayuul fātìi kpēēyee ní Daafiidi gbāaǹ u-nimbiin u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Sii a-ba ká nì a-nimbil díǹ yii ti-Dindaan bàà dū-si ki ŋá m-ŋaan kutaŋkpanaakoou nee poon. Bi bí-mi yii ḿ kpɔ̀-si, ama ní m súń a-saai ki bí yii: <Maa làá dū m-ŋal kí gbēē m-kpiliu un Unimbɔti lēēyee, di sá úǹ ní ti-Dindaan lēē ubɔti.>

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Kpèè m-baa, kpèè kun kā m-ŋaanee, a-bɔkutil juti dee. M nín gíí a-bɔkutil juti kaa kūū-si nee, á béé yii maa pée cáá a-pu nlandɔkɔkpiti ŋubɔ, kaa bíi jáà nì si, kaa yīntiǹ-si tiba mun poon. Ama sii di bíi jì-mi ki là kí lēē m-maŋfal.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di làá sòoǹ man nì si kansikin bɔti. Úǹ di làá tɔ̀ m-pɔntooŋyi ikpiti in a ŋá-mee pu. Ama man kaa làá dū m-ŋal kí gbēē-si.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Kii dooooyee laŋkpandi nín lī puee yii: <Utɔŋfiti cee ní ntoom nyēeń.> Ama maa làá dúkutí m-ŋal ní kaa nín gbēē-si.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Ŋma ní Isirayeel yab bɔtiu cá kí jáǹ ní? Ŋma ní a sáń ki jì ní? Man sá kii kibɔkɔ kin kpíìyee, ní ki sá kii dikambabilee!

english_verse: “David, my son—is that you?” Saul asked. Then he started crying
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di sá ubɔsoonli kí sòoǹ man nì si bɔti. U làá kpèè-tì, kí mɔ̄tì m-pu, kí pɔ̀-mi ní kí fīī-mi a-ŋaan.»

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: Daafiidi sòon̄ nì Saayuul míǹ ki dóòyee, ní Saayuul bí-u yii: «Sii m-jipɔɔn Daafiidi neen ní m gbìl̀ naaa?» U lī mimmee ní ki bíi sūǹ tikpil.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul nìkī ki lī yii: «A sá deedeedaan ki jítiǹ man, di sá yii sii ŋá man tiŋan ní man ŋá-si tikpitil.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: A dàkā-mi díǹ nee tiŋan tin a dàkafī m-puee, di sá yii ti-Dindaan bàà dū-mi ki ŋá a-ŋaan ní aa kūū-mi.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Unil yaa yīkiǹ u-pulincɔnti nsanni, u yàntī ú nìkī u-saŋŋu nì ŋgbansɔŋfaaa? Unimbɔti ń pà-si tin a ŋá ki tīī-mi díǹ nee pu.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee m béè yii sii di làá dāá nīn sá ubɔti, ní Isirayeel beel pɔŋŋu dāa kā a-ŋaan.

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, pùtī ti-Dindaan kí pòon̄-mi yii m-kúm boonee, aa làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí m-dicaŋkun nib. Mimmee bi làá dāá téetí man nì m-dicaŋkun nib pu.»

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Ní tùkù-u yii: <Ti nì dibàl! Án bútí si nì a-dicaŋku nì tin kɔkɔ a cááyee!

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Daafiidi gbìl̄ yii a bíi cēē a-piii kuti. Ŋyunti ŋun a-pikpaaliibi nìn bí ti-cee Kaarmeelee, taa nìn pée ŋá-bi digìńdi diba, ní bi-wanti báà kubɔbɔ kaa wáŋkì.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Bàlifì a-tɔntɔnliibi bi làá tùkù-si. Daafiidi gbàam̄-si yii á dàkà-ti kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu díǹ jiŋaal wiiŋŋu nee. Ti pée gbàam̄-si ní, tīī timbi nì a-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi kun a yaa pée ŋūǹee.>»

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Binib bin Daafiidi túee bàn̄ ki dū u nín tùkū-bi puee ki lī Nabaal cee, ki kíǹ ki yú ki cí.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Ní Nabaal bí yii: «Ŋma di sá Daafiidi ní? Ŋma di sá Jeesee jipɔɔn gbanti ní? Ti-yuntii nee bitɔntɔnliibi tikpil yíkí bi-kpilib cee ki sáń.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Ní man ḿ yòon̄ m-jinti nì m-nyim nì m-nanti tin m ŋāaǹ kí fōō bin m mēē dikpaameelee kí dūú tīī nimbi bin maa nyí laakin pú ni nyánnéeee?»

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Daafiidi naacimpɔmbee fātìi nín gítí, ki tin dū Nabaal nín sòon̄ puee kɔkɔ ki máafì-u.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, dàkafì kí kpèè min ní a máaǹ kí ŋée, di sá bi bɔ́ntì kí cáań mbusu kí tɔ̄ ti-kpiliu nì u-dicaŋku pu. An yaa kíǹ úǹ ti-kpiliuee, u-bimbim kaa ŋān̄, an puee ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ nì u.»

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: ní ki bí u-tɔntɔnliibi yii: «Lìntīmaan, ḿ páań ni-boon.» Ama waa pée tùkū u-cal Nabaal tiba.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: U jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ kimaŋ pu ki bíi pɔ́tí kigbantaŋee, Daafiidi mun nì u-yab sìntīń ki túliń-u, ní bi dāa dūu tú tɔb.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn bí ki lì u-ban yii: «Mimmee, m pée wúń kijapaai nee wanti kuteeu nee pu tiba kaa wáŋkì fám deeyaa! M ŋá-u tiŋan ní u dū tikpitil ki pàn̄-mi!

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti ń tīī m-nannanliibi mpɔn kí bìin̄ bi-pu gba, m yaa fu yāntì uninja bambaanti u-dicaŋkun kaa kūū-u fool kutaafaau.»

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Abiigayiil nín ká Daafiidi páaǹee, ní u kpákatì kimaŋ pu malaa ki tātìi gbāaǹ Daafiidi nimbiin u-yil tūū kitiŋ.

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: M-kpiliu, taa fàtīí tɔ̄ Nabaal un kaa bí tiban nee. Di sá yii u fōō u-yindi didandi ní. Nabaal taapu di sá yii: <Kinaatuui>, ní inaatuu lafun bí u-ni. Ama man a-yumbuu kaa nìn ká binaacimpɔmbi bin a nìn túnnée.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: M gbāam̀-si, dū man a-yumbuu yìntitam kí pɔ̄-u. Di sá yii m cáá dimákal yii ti-Dindaan làá dū dibeel kí tīī a-dicaŋkun yab kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan, kun puee m-dindaan jáń ti-Dindaan jaaku. A-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, bí taa pée ká tikpitil tiba a-ni.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Unil ubɔ yíkì ki bíi jì m-kpiliu ki là kí lēē u-maŋfal. Ama ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu làá wúń a-maŋfal pu kí dū-dì kí kpāafì u-cee. U làá dū a-nannanliibi maŋfal kí tɔ̄ kí fá ndandati kii bi nín dù ditaŋkpal kí ŋá kujaataafuŋ poon kí tɔ̄ puee ní.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ti-Dindaan yaa láa ŋá tiŋan tin u pōoǹ yii u làá ŋá kí tīī-see, u làá dāá dū-si kí kàan̄ dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu.

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: Taa kpɔ̀ unil fám kí tɔ̀ a-ba ipɔntoon. Mimmee a-pɔbil kaa dāa máfí. M-kpiliu, ti-Dindaan yaa láa bīiǹ a-boonee, á dāá téetí man a-yumbuu pu.»

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí Abiigayiil yii: «M jáaḿ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu un túnní-si díǹ á dāá tūŋkìń-mi nsannee.

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: M jáam̀ si mun, a-landɔkɔmɔntiŋu di nyántì-mi nnikpaakoon nì man m-ba nín bàà làá tɔ̀ ipɔntoon iŋyee poon.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Ibaamɔn an sá ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu di pīiǹ-mi nsan ḿ taa ŋá-si tikpitil. Ama m pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee yii a yaa kaa bàà túŋkìń-mi malaa, báà uninja kaa bàà fu kīntí fool kutaafaau Nabaal dicaŋkun.»

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi fōō tiwampɔkaal tin u cáań-uee ní ki bí-u yii: «Nín̄ kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. Kpèè, m gbìl̄ tin a lēe, ki fōō-tì nì kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.» Nabaal kpíì, Daafiidi cáá Abiigayiil

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Abiigayiil fātìń mmɔŋkee, Nabaal bí ki jīǹ jiŋaal mmɔntiimin kii ubɔtee, ki bí dipɔɔpindi poon ki gbí púb. An puee waa pée tùkū-u tiba áli kutaa dāa wúntì.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì ndaam cēetì-uee, ní u máafì-u tin jítèe. Niinee ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ ní u dūu fàl̄.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Iwiin saalaa boonee ní ti-Dindaan fáá-u ní u kpíì.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Ní u yíkì malaa ki tātìi gbāaǹ u-yil tūū kitiŋ, ní ki bí yii: «M bɔ́ntì kí nīn sá u-yumbuu, kí nīn fíntí m-dindaan tɔntɔnliibi taaŋi.»

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Ní u yíkì kpalaa ki kāl̀ kimaŋ pu ki nóó Daafiidi tɔntɔnliibee. Bitɔntɔnliibi biŋmoo nìn táá-u. An nín dī pu u kpántì Daafiidi nimpuuee dee.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn cáá unimpu ubɔ mun bi yíì-u yii Akiinoowam, u sá Jisirayeel tiŋkin, ki dūu kútì Abiigayiil pu bi ŋá binimpoobi bili.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Saayuul nìn dū u-bisal Miikaal, Daafiidi nimpuu, ki pú Layiisi jipɔɔn Paltii un sá Galiim tiŋkinee ticati.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Siifi tiŋki yab cūtì Saayuul cee Giibeeya ki tùkū-u yii: «Aa nyí yii Daafiidi cūtìi bál̀ Akiila gbantaŋki pu kuteeu caŋinaaa?»

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Saayuul nìn gāā u-janjanaapaal Akiila gbantaŋki pu, didandi caŋin. Daafiidi úǹ nìn bí kuteeun. U nìn gbìl̄ yii Saayuul dɔ́miń niin ki nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi tú binib biba cūtìi kpēē ní ki ká yii tiŋman Saayuul bāań ki bí niin.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Ní u yíkìi nín cá niin ki tin bàn̄ Saayuul janjanaapaal pu. U nìn dáań ki ká laakin Saayuul nì u-janjakpiliu Abineer, Neer jipɔɔn dɔ̄ee. Saayuul nìn dɔ̄ dijanjanaapaal kansikin ní bijanjaliibi dɔ̄ ki māntìi tú-u.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi yíiń Ayiimeeleeki uitiija nì Abisayi, Joowaab nabiki bin na bi yíì yii Seeruyee ki bí-bi yii: «Ŋma di làá nóó-mi tí cù Saayuul janjanaapaal pu?» Ní Abisayi kíí yii: «M làá nóó-si tí cù.»

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Kunyeeuee, Daafiidi nì Abisayi ŋá soooo ki bàn̄ Saayuul janjaliibi cee. Saayuul nìn dɔ̄ dijanjanaapaal kansikin ki gèeǹ. U-kpaŋki nìn cɔ́ u-yil caŋin. Abineer nì bijanjaliibi nìn dɔ̄ ki māntìi tú-u ki gèeǹ.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Abisayi bí Daafiidi yii: «Unimbɔti baasii dū a-nannanliu ki ŋá a-ŋaan díǹ ní. Yàntī ḿ pée dū kikpaŋ kí sāā-u dibaja kí nákań kitiŋ, maa làá sāā mili.»

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí-u yii: «Á taa kpɔ̀-u. Un di yaa dū u-ŋal ki gbēē un ti-Dindaan lēē ú nīn sá ubɔtee kaa lóotí ditafadaaldi.

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee yii ti-Dindaan u-ba di làá dāá kpɔ̀-u. An dāa ŋūǹ kí nīn sá yii u-wiiŋŋu di bàn̄ ní u kpíì, àá u cūtì kujaau ní bi kūuń-u.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ń cúú-mi ḿ taa dū m-ŋal kí gbēē ubɔti un u lēēyee maŋfal. Tí pée yòon̄ u-kpaŋki kin cɔ́ u-yil caŋinee nì u-túuŋŋu ŋun poon nnyim kēe kí nīn cá.»

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi yōoǹ kikpaŋ nì ntúun ŋun poon nnyim kā ŋu yú u-yil caŋinee ki búntì. Báà ubɔ kaa fīntì, kaa ká tin jítèe, kaa béè tin ŋée mun. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì ŋgeembiim miba cúú-bi.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
