translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi nín cá lapu pu jandi ki cūtìi tɔ́kɔǹ dijool diba pu. U nìn dátiǹ Saayuul janjanaapaal.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn téeń bijanjaliibi watil pú ki yíiń Neer jipɔɔn Abineer yii: «Abineer, á pīlifì!» Ní Abineer bí-u yii: «Ŋma di bí niin ki kūuntí ki kpáàa ubɔti tafal ní?»

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí-u yii: «A sá uninja ní, kaa sá mimmaaa? A-juti kaa bí Isirayeel tiŋkin. Kin ba pu ní aa cíitì ubɔti un sá a-kpiliuee tiŋan? Ubɔ dɔ́miń kí kpɔ̀ ubɔti un sá a-kpiliuee.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Min a ŋá nee kaa ŋān̄. Aa cíitì a-kpiliu ubɔti un ti-Dindaan lēēyee tiŋan. Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee, a máaǹ ŋkúm. Ubɔti kpaŋki nì u-túuŋŋu ŋun poon nnyim kā ki yú u-yil caŋinee bí la?»

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Niinee Saayuul béè Daafiidi neen, ní ki bālifì-u yii: «Sii m-jipɔɔn Daafiidi neen pu ní m gbìl̄ naaa?» Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, an sá man Daafiidi.»

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kútì ki lī yii: «Ba pu ní m-dindaan jì man a-tɔntɔnliu míǹ? Ba ní m ŋá-si ní? Tikpitil tilati ní m baasii ŋá ní?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-baa ubɔti, pīlifì tin man a-tɔntɔnliu làá sòoǹee. An yaa sá ti-Dindaan di yaa lùkutī-si ní a kā m-pu mimmee, ú yàntī m-saraau ń sɔ̀ŋkì u-pɔbil. Ama an yaa nyánní binib ceeyee, ti-Dindaan ń yàntī mbusu ń jēetí bi-pu. Di sá yii bi jìn̄-mi díǹ pu nee m-naanjab tiŋki kin ti-Dindaan tīī-tee pu kaa là ḿ kàl̄. An bí kii bi bíi tùkù-mi yii: <Cùú nīn jáaḿ awaayee> ní.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Ama man kaa làá kpú kinicantiŋin kí nīn dátiǹ m-Dindaan. Di sá yii sii Isirayeel bɔtiu bíi jì man un kaa bí tiban kii dikambabilee. A bíi jì-mi kii bi nín jì ujikpal ajoon pu puee ní.»

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Saayuul téeń yii: «M yīntì! M-jipɔɔn Daafiidi, fàtīí gítiń. Maa ti làá ŋá-si tikpitil tiba, kun puee a dàkā díǹ yii m-maŋfal cáá kunyampoou a-cee. M ŋá ŋwaatiyaamin ní, m kíil̀ m-ba tikpil.»

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, kpèè a-kpaŋki sèé, a-janjaliibi kansikin ubɔ ń dāan̄ kí fōō.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di làá pà báà ŋma deedee tuuŋŋi nì u-baamɔŋyi paati. Díǹ nee, ti-Dindaan bàà dū-si ki ŋá m-ŋaan, ama m yíì yii maa làá dū m-ŋal kí gbēē-si, kun puee a sá ubɔti un ti-Dindaan lēēyee ní.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: A-maŋfal yaa cáá kunyampoou m-ceeyee, ma mun maŋfal ń nīn cáá kunyampoou ti-Dindaan cee, ú nyāntí-mi agìń kɔkɔ poon.»

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Saayuul bí Daafiidi yii: «Unimbɔti ń bìin̄ a-boon m-jipɔɔn Daafiidi. Tiŋman, án làá bútí-si ní á tɔ̄ atuŋkpaan.» Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi búntì u-laŋki, ní Saayuul mun fātìi nín gítí u-dumpu.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Boonee ní Daafiidi lī u-neen yii: «Ŋwiin bí Saayuul làá dāá ŋmā kí lēē m-maŋfal. Kun m pée ŋūǹ kí ŋée di sá ḿ sāǹ kí cùú báĺ Fiiliistii yab tiŋkin. Mimmee, Saayuul làá gbèen̄ kí taa ti nín̄ nyàab̀-mi Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn, ní ḿ ŋmátí u-ŋaan.»

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Saayuul nín gbìl̄ yii Daafiidi sáǹ ki cūtìi bál̀ Gaatee ní u gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi jì-u.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Daafiidi bí Akiisi yii: «A yaa kíikí kí bàà pɔ̄-mi diyimɔɔl ḿ nīn kóò kitimbilii kiban. Kun puee an kaa máaǹ yii man a-tɔntɔnliu ń nīn kóò kitiŋ kin poon sii ubɔti kóòyee.»

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Yaadal gbanti ní Akiisi dū Siikilaagi tiŋki ki tīī-u. An pu ní áli nì díǹ, Juuda yab bɔtiibi gbíntìi yì Siikilaagi tiŋki.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Daafiidi kāl̀ Fiiliistii yab tiŋkin dibindi diba nì iŋmal inaa ní.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Daafiidi bí niinee ní u nì u-naacimbi jɔ́m̀ ki jáń nì Geesuur yab nì Giirsi yab nì Amaleeki yab. Di sá yii bíǹ di nìn pée kóò kitiŋ gbantin doooodooooyee kí pée yòon̄ Suur tiŋki kí tin cáá sāā Eejipiti tiŋki.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Bi nìn kūū kitiŋ gbanti nib kɔkɔ, bininjab nì binimpoobi, ní ki cúuń inaa nì ipii nì iŋoobu nì mmamu nì igutaamu, ki kóoǹní tiwampeeŋkaal. U fātìi gítìńee ní ki cūtì Akiisi cee.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Akiisi yaa nìn bālifì Daafiidi yii: «Bilab ní a cūtìi jáń kujaau díǹ ní?» Ní Daafiidi ń kíí-u yii: «M cūti jáń nì Juuda tiŋki ŋgiil pú yab», àá «Yeerameel yab tiŋki ŋgiil pú», àá «Keeni yab tiŋki ŋgiil pú ní.»

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Daafiidi kaa nìn cútiń uninja àá unimpu nì u-nimbiliŋ kí cáań Gaati tiŋkin. U nìn lī u-neen yii: «Binib làá nīn sòoǹ ki kɔ́kɔĺ-mi yii: <Kpèè Daafiidi nín ŋáań puee sèé.>» Ŋyunti ŋun kɔkɔ Daafiidi dūu kāl̀ Fiiliistii yab tiŋkinee, u nín nìn ŋáań puee dee.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: An pu ní Akiisi nìn cáá Daafiidi pu dimákal tikpil. U nìn lī u-ban yii: «Daafiidi dàkā kináŋ Isirayeel yab bin sá u-nibulee pu tikpil. An puee u làá nīn pée bí m-cee ki tūǹ m-tundi kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Dalbee Fiiliistii yab kpáfì bi-janjaliibi ki gāā bi-janjanaapaal Suneem tiŋkin. Ní Saayuul mun kpáfì Isirayeel yab janjaliibi, ní ki gāā bi-janjanaapaal Giilboowa.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Saayuul nín ká Fiiliistii yab janjanaapaalee ní dinyoondi kɔ́-u ní u-wunti kíĺ ki bíi gbáà kpàkpakpa.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bālifì ti-Dindaan ní waa kíí-u tiba. Waa kíí-u tidamintiil poonaaa, kaa dī Uriim pu àá ubɔnaatil ubɔ pu ki kíí-u.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí u-tɔntɔnliibi yii: «Nyàab̀maan-mi unimpu ubɔ un sá ubɔɔyee ḿ cù u-cee kí bɔ̄ tibɔɔl.» Ní u-tɔntɔnliibi bí-u yii: «Unimpu ubɔ sá ubɔɔ ki bí Eeni-Dɔɔr.»

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Saayuul kpántì u-wampeeŋkaati ní bininjab bili céeǹ-u, ní bi bàn̄ unimpuee cee kunyeeu. Ní Saayuul bí-u yii: «M làá dàkà-si utaŋkpiil ubɔ, m là á yíiń-u ḿ sòoǹ nì u.»

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee kíí-u yii: «Kéè sii a-ba nyí yii Saayuul kúntì dibɔɔbɔl tundi kitiŋ nee poonaa! Ba pu ní a pīil̀-mi ŋkúm taliŋku míǹ?»

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee yii tiba kaa làá ŋá-si tibɔti nee poon.»

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Unimpuee bí-u yii: «Ŋma ní a là ḿ yíiń kí tīī-si ní?» Ní Saayuul bí-u yii: «Yíiń-mi Samiyeel.»

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Unimpuee nín ká Samiyeelee ní u fáá mbiil, ní ki bí Saayuul yii: «Sii di sá Saayuul, ba pu ní a kíil̀-mi míǹ?»

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Taa fàŋkì, ama tùkù-mi un ní a kée?» Ní unimpuee bí-u yii: «M ká ŋfam miba nyánní kitiŋ taapu taapu ki jɔ́miń.»

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Ní u bālifì yii: «U bí mana?» Ní u bí yii: «An sá ujaŋkpil ubɔ di jɔ́miń ki pēē dibɔkutikpaandi.» Niinee Saayuul béè yii an sá Samiyeel ní u tātìi gbāaǹ u-yil tūū kitiŋ.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí Saayuul yii: «Ba pu ní a páb́-mi ki yíiń-mi?» Ní Saayuul kíí-u yii: «M bí dinimbinaamandi poon ní. Fiiliistii yab dɔ́miń ki bíi jáà nì mi, ní Unimbɔti fātì u-boon ki tīī-mi. Waa ti dì ubɔnaatil ubɔ pu àá kudamintiiu kubɔ pu ki sòoǹ nì mi. An pu ní m yíiń-si á dàkà-mi min sá ḿ ŋée.»

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Ní Samiyeel bí yii: «Ba pu ní a gíti bíi bàlifī-mi? Sii a-ba ká yii Unimbɔti fātì u-boon ki tīī-si ní ki kpántì a-nannanliu.

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ŋá kii u nín nìn dī m-pu ki sòon̄ a-pu miŋyee ní. U fōō a-cee dibeel ki dūu tīī ubɔ, an dàkà yii Daafiidi.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: A yíì kaa pílifì ti-Dindaan bɔkpaaŋi kí bàà kpɔ̀ kí céetí Amaleeki yab. An pu ní ti-Dindaan bíi dàkà-si míǹ díǹ.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dū si nì a-nibul Isirayeel yab kí ŋá Fiiliistii yab ŋaan. Fool, sii nì a-jipɔmbi làá fu nīn bí m-cee doo ditaŋkpiilin, ní ti-Dindaan ń fu dū a-janjaliibi kí ŋá Fiiliistii yab ŋaan.»

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Saayuul nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee, tifaandi nìn kɔ́-u ní u lítì ki dōoǹ kitiŋ mɔ̀rrr. Kun nìn gíti púntì-uee di sá waa nìn jíń tiba ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu, an puee mpɔn kaa nìn gíti bí-u.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Unimpuee sútìi pìl̄ Saayuul ki ká u-pɔbil nín bíil̀ puee ní u bí-u yii: «Sii a-ba ká man a-yumbuu nín pílifiǹ-see. Maa mɔ́tì m-maŋfal pu, ama m ŋá min a bí yii ḿ ŋée.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, si mun pīlifì tin man a-yumbuu là kí sòoǹ nì see. Yàntī ḿ cáań-si tijin fiii á jī kí ká mpɔn kí wàatī kí nín kíĺ nsan kí nīn kùǹ.»

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Ní u yíì yii waa làá jī. Ní u-tɔntɔnliibi nì unimpuee páb́-u ní u dāa kíí ki jíń tijin. Niinee ní u yíkì kitiŋ ki kāl̀ kilambaŋ pu.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Unimpuee nìn cáá dinajapɔmbil din bí màlmalee. U nìn ŋá malaa ki kūū-dì. Míǹ boonee ní u búuń ŋyim ki púĺ kpɔnɔ un baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: U nìn cáań ki tīī Saayuul nì u-tɔntɔnliibi ní bi jíń. Bi jíń ki dóòyee ní ki fātìi kíĺ nsan ki nín gítí kunyeeu gbanti.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn gíí diŋuul Akiisi pu ki bí-u yii: «Jà uninja nee ú nīn gítí laakin a pú-u u kóòyee. Ú taa kūtì ti-pu tí cù kujaau. U dāa ŋūǹ kí lábití kí nīn bíi jáà nì ti kujaaun. U nín làá ŋá pu ní u nì u-kpiliu ń mɔ̄ɔkèe di sá ú tìl̄ ti-janjaliibi yiliŋ kí tīī u-kpiliu.

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: An kaa sá Daafiidi gbanti pu ní bi nìn gà ilan ki ŋōō ki lì yii: <Saayuul kūū binib kutuku, ní Daafiidi kūū binib cutimaanyeeee?>»

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Niinee Akiisi yíiń Daafiidi ki bí-u yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí nee yii a sá unil un pu bi ŋūǹ kí nīn mákée ní. Man ká yii an ŋān̄ á bàà céeǹ-ti tí cù kujaau, di sá doooo a nín bāań ki bí m-cee ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, maa ká a-pu tikpitil tiba. Ama a-bɔti kaa mɔ̄ǹ Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi bin kíǹee.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee nín̄ gítí nì ŋgbansɔŋfi, kí taa ŋá tin baa lèe.»

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bālifì yii: «Mimmee ba ní m ŋá? Doooo m nín kpántì a-tɔntɔnliu ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, tibɔkpitil tilati ní a ká m-pu ní an sá yii maa ŋūǹ kí cùú já nì a-nannanliibi?»

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti Akiisi kíí Daafiidi yii: «Tiŋman pu, a-bɔti fáatì man kii Unimbɔti tuuŋŋuee ní. Ama an sá Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi di bí yii baa là á cù kujaau.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: An puee á fu yīkì fool kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl si nì a-naacimbi bin céeǹní-see. Ní fu yīkì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl, ku tin pée lì yii ku wúntée, ni yíkì.»

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaauee Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi yíkìi nín gítí Fiiliistii yab tiŋkin. Ní Fiiliistii yab nín cá Jisirayeel tiŋkin.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Winta dalee, Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi fātìi bàn̄ Siikilaagi tiŋkin. Amaleeki yab nìn dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Juuda tiŋki ŋgiil pú yab nì Siikilaagi yab. Bi nìn nāaǹ Siikilaagi tiŋki ki tūū-kì ŋŋmi.

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì u-yab bāańee ki ká yii bi-tiŋki wùn̄ ŋŋmi, ní bi cúú bi-nimpoobi nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ki kpáàa búntì.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi kíĺ ki bíi gà dituweel mpɔn, ki súń áli kaa ti gíti cáá mpɔn gba kí sɔ̄.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: Bi nìn cúú Daafiidi nimpoobi liitil mun, Akiinoowam un sá Jisirayeelee nì Nabaal nimpuu Abiigayiil un sá Kaarmeelee.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Tibɔtee nìn kɔ́ǹ Daafiidi kunimbaau tikpil, di sá yii u-naacimbi nìn bíi sòoǹ yii bi làá yāŋkì-u ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀. Báà ŋma nyɔkɔ nìn túŋkì bi nín bíi dàkafī bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-nimpoobi pu puee. Ama Daafiidi nìn fātìi ká kunyannyaau ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu pu.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi bí usaraaŋakpil Abiyataar, Ayiimeeleeki jipɔɔn yii: «M gbāam̀-si, cáań-mi eefoodi.» Ní Abiyataar yōoǹ ki cáań-u.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «M yaa jìn̄ dinikitil nee boon, m làá tin cúú-dàaa?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «Yīkìi jà bi-boon, a làá cúú-bi ní kí fōō a-yab bi-ŋaan.»

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Bi bí ki jì binibee boonee ní ki ká ueejipitija ubɔ kusaaun ní bi cáań-u Daafiidi cee, ní ki tīī-u kpɔnɔ u ŋmɔ́, ki tīī-u nnyim u nyùn̄.

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: Bi nìn tīī-u fiigi kalaau nì fiinyi biliŋ akulim asaka ali. U jíń ki dóòyee ní ki fātìi ká mpɔn, di sá waa nìn jíń tiba kaa nyùn̄ tiba áli iwiin ita ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Daafiidi bālifì-u yii: «Ŋma di yì-si, ní a nyánní la?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «M sá ueejipitija ní, Amaleeki yab ubɔ yumbuu ní m sá. M-kpiliu dū-mi ki fá díǹ nee iwiin ita sɔ̀, kun puee m búŋkì.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Timbi di cūtì ki jáń nì Keereeti yab nì Juuda yab nì Kaaleeb yab bin kóò ŋgiil púee. Timbi di tí tūū Siikilaagi tiŋki ŋŋmi.»

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí-u yii: «A làá cùnnì-mi binib gbanti ceeee?» Ní u bí-u yii: «Pùtī Unimbɔti yii aa làá kpɔ̀-mi, àá aa làá gíiǹ-mi kí ŋúbiǹ m-kpiliu, mimmee m làá cùnnì-si dinikitil gbanti cee.» Daafiidi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Amaleeki yab

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: Ní kijapaayee cáá Daafiidi ki cūnnì. Bi bàn̄ee Amaleeki yab yàl̄ ki gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔn ki cáá tin bi jáń ki kūliŋkìń Fiiliistii nì Juuda yab timmunee ki jīǹ ki nyù ki jīǹ jiŋaal.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíĺ kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl ki jàkā-bi butɔbu áli kutaa wúntì ki dāa sāā kujoou. Báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋmátì, see binaacimpɔmbi alaataa anaa di ŋúń ki kāl̀ igutaamu pu ki sáǹ ki ŋmátì.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn fīī binib bin kɔkɔ Amaleeki yab nìn cúúyee ki kpáaǹ tiwan tin bi nìn yōoǹee. Cilinjee u nìn fīī u-nimpoobi liitil.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: Binib bin kɔkɔ bi nìn cúúyee, ŋwaamu nì bikpaambi, bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib nì tin kɔkɔ bi nìn yōoǹee, báà tiba nì tiba kaa nìn fɔ́tì. Daafiidi nìn fōō kɔkɔ ki gíiǹní.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: U nìn fōoń ipii nì iŋoobu nì inaa, ní bin nìn péetiń-iee lì yii: «Kpèèmaan Daafiidi nín jáń ki fōoń tiwan tiŋyee.»

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Daafiidi janjaliibi kansikin binikpitib nì bin kaa bí tibanee bí yii: «Kii bi nín kaa nóó-ti ti cūtì kujaauee, baa làá ká tin ti fōoń kujaaunee báà tiba. Asee bi-nimpoobi nì bi-biyaamu ní ti làá dūú tīī-bi ní bí nīn cá.»

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Ama ní Daafiidi bí yii: «M-nabiyaamu, taa dūmaan tiwan tin ti-Dindaan dūu tīī-tee kí ŋá míǹ. Úǹ di wúń ti-pu, ní ki dū dinikitil din dɔ́miń ki jáń nì tee ki ŋá ti-ŋaan.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa làá pīlifì tin ni sòoǹee. Báà ŋma làá pée fōō u-jandi ní. Bin kāl̀ ki cíitì awaŋgulee nì bin cūtì kujaauee, bi-kɔkɔ làá yàkatī án nīn ŋmà ní.>»

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Ki yōoǹ yaadal wiiŋŋu ní Daafiidi dū tibɔti gbanti ki kpántì mara nì dikoobil ki tīī Isirayeel yab. An bí míǹ ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Bi fātìi bāań Siikilaagee ní Daafiidi lēē tin bi jáń ki fōońee poon tiba ki cáa tīī Juuda yab kpilib u-bɔɔbi ní ki bí-bi yii: «Kpèèmaan ni-wampɔkaati sèé, ti fōoń-tì ti-Dindaan nannanliibi cee ní.»

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn jáń nì Isirayeel yab Giilboowa jool pu. Isirayeel yab nìn sáǹ ní Fiiliistii yab kūū-bi tikpil.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi pu kàtì kati. Bi nìn kūū ubɔti jipɔmbi Joonatan nì Abinadaab nì Malkisuwa.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Niinee dikɔ̀ndi kóoǹ ki nyīŋfì Saayuul pu. Bipintɔliibi nín dāa ká-uee ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ ní u-wunti kíǹ ki gbáà kpàkpakpa.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí un ŋúb́ u-janjawantee yii: «Fúutí a-tàataajiki ki sāā kí kpɔ̀-mi. Maa là yii Fiiliistii yab bin kaa gíí akpancan nee ń kpɔ̀-mi kí nīn cáa bèel̄-mi.» Ama ní un ŋúb́ u-janjawantee fāŋkì ní ki yíì. Niinee ní Saayuul yōoǹ úǹ u-ba tàataajiki ki cóoǹ ki lítì ki-pu.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Un ŋúb́ u-janjawantee ká yii u-kpiliu kpíìyee, ní u mun dū u-tàataajiki ki cóoǹ ki lítì ki-pu ki kpíì.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: An nín dī min ní Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi taatil nì un ŋúb́ u-janjawantee kpíì ŋwimbaantee dee.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin kóò ditantakal lapu pu gbandee nì bin kóò Jɔɔdan buŋŋu lapu pu gbantee nín gbìl̄ yii Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi taatil kpíì ní Isirayeel yab sáǹee, ní bi yíkìi sáǹ ki fá bi-timmu, ní Fiiliistii yab dɔ́miń ki kāl̀.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Ku wúntì Fiiliistii yab dɔ́miń kí fūkul̀ bin bi kūūyee wantee ní ki ká yii Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi taatil kpíì ki dɔ̄ Giilboowa jool pu.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Bin kóò Yabeesi Galaadi tiŋkinee gbìl̄ Fiiliistii yab nín ŋá Saayuul puee.

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: Ní bininjab bin cáá dibaatandee yíkì ki cōom̀ kunyamɔŋu ki tin bàn̄ Beeti-Seeyan gundi ki yōoǹní anikpil, Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi. Bi cáá-bi ki bāań Yabeesee ní ki dū-bi ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Boonee ní bi kóoǹ bi-kpabiŋ ki dūu síb́ busubu bun bi yíì tamariisee taapu Yabeesi tiŋkin, ní ki bóob́ kinyɔkɔ iwiin iluli.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Saayuul kúm boonee, Daafiidi nìn cūtìi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Amaleeki yab. U nìn gítìń ki kāl̀ Siikilaagi tiŋkin iwiin ili.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Ŋwintataati dalee, u bí yii ú kpèèyee, unaacimpɔɔn ubɔ di nyánní Saayuul janjanaapaal pu ki páaǹnée. U-wampeeŋkaati nìn cátì ní ntam pùkū u-yil. U bāań Daafiidi ceeyee ní ki tātìi gbāaǹ u-nimbiin dicincibil u-yil tūū kitiŋ.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn bālifì-u yii: «A nyánní la?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «M nyánní Isirayeel yab janjanaapaal pu ní ki sáǹní.»

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi bí-u yii: «Tùkù-mi tin jítì niinee.» Ní u bí-u yii: «Isirayeel yab sáǹ kujaaun ní bi kūū bi-kansikin binib tikpil. Áli gba bi kūū Saayuul nì u-jipɔɔn Joonatan.»

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bālifì unaacimpɔɔnee yii: «A ŋá mana ní ki béè yii Saayuul nì u-jipɔɔn Joonatan kpíì?»

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ní unaacimpɔɔnee bí-u yii: «M pée bí Giilboowa jool pu yìkíl̄ yikil ní. M bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, Saayuul di ŋúb́ u-kpaŋki ki nyìitēe. Janjatɔrɔkub nì bitanjakaliibi nìn kā u-pu kàti kati.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: U fātèe ki ká-mi, ní ki yíiń-mi, ní m kíí-u yii: <Ti-baa, m sèé.>

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Ní u bālifì-mi yii: <Sii di sá ŋma ní?> Ní m kíí-u yii: <M sá uamaleekija ní.>

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní u bí-mi yii: <M gbàam̄-si, dāá kpɔ̀-mi, di sá yii m-nimbiliŋ bɔ̀ntī, nì min kamaa m dáá gbíntìi fòotēe.>

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Niinee, m sútì ki pìl̄-u ní ki kūū-u, kun puee m nyí yii u yaa lítì, waa làá pée ŋmátí. Míǹ boonee ní m cíkitì u-beefuuliiki ní ki fúutì dibɔmbil din u fúuńee ki cáań doo kí tīī-si.»

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi dáaĺ tiwan tin u pēēyee ki cátì, ní u-naacimbi kɔkɔ mun dáaĺ ki cátì bi-yati.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kāl̀ Saayuul nì u-jipɔɔn Joonatan nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ sá ti-Dindaan nibul bi kūū kujaaunee kpool. Bi nìn súń ki bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ki cáa sāā kujoou.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi gíti bí unaacimpɔɔn un cáań tibɔti ki tùkū-uee yii: «A bí yii a sá la naaa?» Ní u bí-u yii: «Amaleeki yab bin kóò ni-puee ubɔ jipɔɔn ní m sá.»

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí-u yii: «A-kpuulool làá báatí a-yil pu ní, di sá sii a-ba nyɔkɔ di sòon̄ ki kūū a-bɔti ki lī yii: <Man di kūū ubɔti un Unimbɔti lēēyee.>» Ŋkpiisilan ŋun Daafiidi gāā Saayuul nì Joonatan puee

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Daafiidi gāā ŋkpiisilan nee Saayuul nì u-jipɔɔn Joonatan pu.

english_verse: and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
translation_verse: U nìn tīī mara yii bí dū-ŋu kí dàkà Juuda yab. An sá Butɔbu kpiisilaŋŋu ŋun bi ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá deedeedambi gbɔŋkunee ní.

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: Isirayeel, a-janjamɔntiibi kpíì a-gbantammu pu! Ba pu ní a-baatandambi kpíì ní?

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Taa gbìitīmaan-tì Gaati tiŋkin, taa mūlifìmaan-tì Asikeelɔn daŋŋi pu. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, Fiiliistii yab nimpoobi làá nīn fàal̀, bin kaa gíí akpancan nee sapɔmbi làá nīn bí dipɔɔpindin.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Giilboowa jooŋŋi, dimalindi ń taa ti tɔ̄ ni-pu, utaa ń taa ti nì ni-pu, bí taa ti ká tisati tin lòoǹee ni-pu. Di sá yii niin ní bi kɔ́ǹ bibaatandambi gbampɔɔŋi icoo. An kaa sá ŋkpam ní bi cáa nùkù Saayuul gbampɔɔl.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Kí yàntī fatiku ń nyā kí pùub̀ee, kí jáǹ binannanliibi bin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee, Joonatan tɔbu kaa nìn gítí bu-boon, míǹ ní Saayuul mun tàataajiki kaa nìn nyēē kí gítiń fám.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Saayuul nì Joonatan nìn néeń tɔb tiŋan, ki kpáaǹ bi-kúm poon baa yākatì tɔbin. Bi nìn yáb̀ ki jítiǹ ikaabu, ní ki nìn cáá dibaatandi ki jítiǹ gbikintib.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Isirayeel sapɔmbi, sɔ̄maan Saayuul pu. Úǹ di nìn pēentí-ni abɔkutinyaan, ní ki nìn cáá sindaariya wanti ki nyɔ̀kɔntí-ni.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Bibaatandambi kpíìń dikɔ̀ndin, Joonatan kpíì ki dɔ̄ ŋgbantamu pu.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: M-nabiki Joonatan, m wíì a-pu, maa mɔ̄ a-pu. A néeń-mi ki jítiǹ unimpu nín néeń u-cal puee.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Bibaatandambi kpíìń dikɔ̀ndin, tijanjawan kaa ti bí tiban.

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Tíǹ jítèe ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «M ŋūǹ kí cùú kàl̄ Juuda yab timmu kiba poonaaa?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «A ŋūǹ kí cù.» Ní Daafiidi gíti bālifì yii: «Kitiŋ kilaka poon ní ḿ cù?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-u yii: «Eebrɔn tiŋkin.»

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi yōoǹ u-nimpoobi liitil, Ayiinoowaam un sá Jisirayeel tiŋkinee, nì Naabaal un kpíìyee nimpuu Abiigayiil un sá Kaarmeel tiŋkinee ki nín cá.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn kpáaǹ u-nib bin kɔkɔ nìn bí u-ceeyee nì bi-dicaŋŋi, ní bi cūtìi kāl̀ Eebrɔn tiŋkin.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Juuda yab dɔ́miń Eebrɔn ki bātì ŋkpam ki sītì Daafiidi yil pu ki kāaǹ-u dibeel Juuda yab pu. Bi nìn tùkū Daafiidi yii Yaabeesi tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkinee yab di síb́ Saayuul.

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi tú binib bi-cee bí cùú jāam̀-bi kí tùkù-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ ni-boon ni nín dàkā ni-dindaan Saayuul dineeŋkpaandi din ki píí-u ki síb́ee pu.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan mun ń dàkà-ni u-neeŋkpaandi kí ŋá-ni tiŋan. Tin ni ŋá nee puee, ma mun làá ŋá-ni tiŋan.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee ní pɔ́ɔm̀maan ni-ba kí ká dipɔbil. Ni-kpiliu Saayuul kpíì, ama ní béé yii Juuda yab bātì ŋkpam ki sītì m-yil pu ḿ nīn sá bi-bɔtiu.» Isirayeel yab kāaǹ Isi-Booseeti dibeel

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Neer jipɔɔn Abineer, Saayuul janjakpiliu yōoǹ Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti ki cūnnì Maanayiim.

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: Niin ní u kāaǹ-u dibeel ú nīn kpòotī Galaadi nì Aseer nì Jisirayeel nì Eefiraayiim nì Beenjameen timmu, an dàkà yii Isirayeel naakɔti tin bí ŋgan púee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Úǹ nìn kāl̀ Eebrɔn tiŋkin ki jíń Juuda naakookun yab pu dibeel abin aluli nì iŋmal iluu. Juuda yab nì Isirayeel yab jaaku

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Neer jipɔɔn Abineer nì Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti nib nyáń Maanayiim ki búntì Gabawɔn.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Joowaab un na bi yíì Seeruyee nì Daafiidi nib mun kíĺ nsan ki nín cá, ní akiti alee cūtìi kpáfì Gabawɔn nyimbɔbil caŋin. Biba nìn bí dinyimbɔbil jandi diba pú ní bin kíǹee mun bí dijandi din kíǹee pú.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Ní Abineer bí Joowaab yii: «Ti-naacimpɔmbi ń nyā kí mɔ̀ bili bili ti-nimbiin dooyaa!» Ní Joowaab kíí yii: «Too!».

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Ní Beenjameen naakookun binaacimpɔmbi saalaa nì bili nyáń ki yúl̀ Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti jandi pú, ní saalaa nì bili nyáń ki yúl̀ Daafiidi jandi pú.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Báà ŋma nìn cúú u-juti yil ní ki dū kitàataajiki ki sāā u-takakal, ní bi-kɔkɔ tin lítì dicilpu. Bi nìn pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Ataŋkpee Saaku. Ŋu bí Gabawɔn tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti mbaantee, kujaau nìn pōō ki píĺ ki pɔ́ɔkì. Daafiidi yab nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Abineer nì Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Joowaab nì Abisayeel nì Asayeel bin na nìn sá Seeruyee nìn bí. Asayeel nìn tóotí kii ukɔniiyee ní.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Ní Abineer fātìi bālifì-u yii: «An sá sii Asayeel níii?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «Iiin, an sá man.»

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Ní Abineer bí-u yii: «Kpèè ŋgiil pú àá ŋgan pú kí jà kí cúú ujanjal ubɔ kí fōō u-wanti.» Ama ní Asayeel kaa kíí kí gbèen̄, ní ki gbíntìi kā u-pu.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Ní Abineer gíti bí-u yii: «Asayeel, páatí m-boon. Ba pu ní a là kí páb́-mi ḿ kpɔ̀-si ní? M yaa ŋá míǹ, mana ní m gíti ŋūǹ kí kpèè a-maan Joowaab nimbiin?»

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Ama ní u yíì ki gbíntìi dī-u. Niinee ní Abineer dū u-kpaŋki yil ki sāā u-pool ní an tin nyáń u-boon, ní u lítì dibɔbil pu niin ki kpíì. Bin kɔkɔ yaa nìn bāań laakin Asayeel nìn kpíì ki dɔ̄ee nìn sàatī kí yūĺ ní.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Niinee Joowaab nì Abisayi nìn kùl̄ ki bīiǹ Abineer boon. Ŋwìiń tin lì yii ŋu jēetée, bi bàn̄ Amma gbantaŋki pu. Mpaan gbanti bí Giiya tiŋki, ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, Gabawɔn teeku saŋŋu pu.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Beenjameen naakookun yab nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki yúl̀ Abineer boon. Bi nìn dūu kpáfì ki ŋá dikitil ki cūtìi yúl̀ kigbantaŋ kiba yilpu.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Ní Abineer kúuǹ ki bí Joowaab yii: «Ti làá nīn pée jáà yéè ki cáaa? Aa nyí yii án làá dāá kúntí nì kunimbaauaaa? Kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá tùkù a-yab bí gbèen̄ kí taa ti jà bi-nabiyaamu ní?»

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab bí yii: «Nì Unimbɔti un bí nee pu, a yaa kaa bàà lī min a lī nee, m-naacimpɔmbi bàà làá nīn jì bi-nabiyaamu míǹ ní áli kutaa ń wúntí.»

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Niinee Joowaab búń ŋyin ní u-janjaliibi gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi jì Isirayeel yab janjaliibi ní kujaau gbēeǹ.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Abineer nì u-janjaliibi nìn dū kunyamɔŋu ki cōom̀ Jɔɔdan tantakalin. Bi nìn dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, ki cōom̀ kutaafaau ki tin cáa sāā kuwiŋkuluu ní ki tin bàn̄ Maanayiim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Joowaab nín nìn gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi jì Abineer ki fātìi gítìńee, u nìn kóoǹ u-naacimbi ki kpáfì. Daafiidi janjaliibi ubɔ kpá mmuŋku di nìn fɔ́tì kí kūtì Asayeel pu.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yōoǹ Asayeel ki cáa síb́ u-baa kaakulin Beetileem. Míǹ boonee Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi nìn cōom̀ kunyamɔŋu. Bi nìn bāań Eebrɔn tiŋkinee, ŋwiin nyáń.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Saayuul yab nì Daafiidi yab nìn bí ki jáàyee, Abineer úǹ nìn mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn Saayuul yab kansikin.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Saayuul nìn cáá ubɔnti ubɔ bi yíì-u yii Riispa ní ki yíì u-baa yii Aaya. Ní Isi-Booseeti bí Abineer yii: «Ba pu ní a dōoǹ nì m-baa bɔɔn ní?»

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: An bɔtee nìn yāntì Abineer fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu, ní ki bí Isi-Booseeti yii: «M sá kibɔkɔ ki pá Juuda yab boonaaa? Doooo nee, maa pée nyáń a-baa cindin yab nì u-nabiyaamu nì u-bɔɔbi boon. M mɔ̀n̄ a-pu á taa kɔ́ Daafiidi ŋaan, ní díǹ nee, a bí ki wòoǹ-mi unimpu nee puɔɔ!

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ m-tafal ŋkpitim pu, m yaa kaa ŋá min ti-Dindaan pōoǹ yii u làá ŋá kí tīī Daafiidee!

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan pūtì yii u làá fōō Saayuul dicaŋkun yab ŋaan dibeel. U làá wàan̄ Daafiidi beel Isirayeel nì Juuda timmu pu, kí yòon̄ Daani ŋgan pú kí cáá sāā Beerseeba ŋgiil pú.»

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Isi-Booseeti kaa nìn ŋúń ki gātì Abineer báà dinyɔɔbundi, kun puee u nìn fàŋkí-u. Abineer gítì Daafiidi jandi pú

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Ní Abineer tú binib Daafiidi cee bí tùkù-u yii: «Ŋma di yì kitiŋ nee ní? Ŋá mpèé nì man, ní ḿ tūtuǹ-si á kóoǹ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kí páań a-boon.»

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «M làá ŋá mpèé nì si, ama kí wàatī á dāan̄ kí ká-mee, á péé péé kí dū m-nimpuu Miikaal, Saayuul bisal kí tīiń-mi.» Niinee a ŋūǹ kí dāan̄ kí ká-mi.

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi tú binib Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti cee bí tùkù-u yii: «Dū m-nimpuu Miikaal kí tīiń-mi, di sá yii m dū Fiiliistii yab kuncooti dilaataal ní ki pàn̄ u-pu kucootiiu.»

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Ní u-cal céeǹ-u ki pá u-boon ki sūǹ ki tin bàn̄ Bawuriim. Niinee Abineer bí-u yii ú nīn gítí u-dumpu ní u nín gítí.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Abineer kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib yii: «An yúntì ni nín bíi nyàab̀ yii Daafiidi ń nīn sá ni-bɔtiuee.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Toooo, ŋyunti bāań ní ŋá tiba. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Daafiidi pu yii: <M-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi pu ní m làá dī kí fīī Isirayeel m-nibul kí nyāntí Fiiliistii yab nì bi-nannanliibi bin kɔ kíǹee ŋaan.>»

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Abineer nìn sòon̄ nì Beenjameen naakookun yab mun. Boonee ní u nín cá Eebrɔn ki tùkū Daafiidi u nì Isirayeel yab nì Beenjameen naakookun yab kɔkɔ nín sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb ki yóoǹ miŋyee.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Bininjab mmuŋku di nìn céeǹ Abineer ní bi dūu bàn̄ Daafiidi cee Eebrɔn tiŋkin. Daafiidi nìn ŋá tican ki fōō-bi.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Ní Abineer bí-u yii: «M làá cùú kóoǹ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kí páań sii ti-baa ubɔti boon. Bi làá ŋá mpèé nì si, ní á jī dibeel an kɔkɔ pu kii a nín là puee.» U sòon̄ míǹ ki dóòyee ní Daafiidi pú-u nsan ú nīn kùǹ, ní u nín kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. Joowaab kūū Abineer

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee Joowaab nì Daafiidi janjaliibi dūu bāań. Bi nìn cūtì kujaau ki jáń ki fōoń tigaajawan tikpil. Ŋyunti gbantee, Abineer kaa nìn gíti bí Daafiidi cee Eebrɔn, di sá yii Daafiidi nìn yāntì u fātìi nín kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ nín nyánní kujaau ki bāańee, ní bi tùkū-u yii: «Neer jipɔɔn Abineer dɔ́miń ki ká ubɔti ní u yāntì u nín kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.»

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab nín cá ubɔti cee ki bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní a ŋá mimmee? Abineer dɔ́miń a-cee ní a yāntì u fātìi nín kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfaaa?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Kéè sii a-ba nyí Neer jipɔɔn Abineer gbantaa! U dɔ́miń ki kíil̀-si, kí béé a-filiŋfeetii kɔkɔ ní.»

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Joowaab nyáń ubɔti ceeyee ní ki tú binib bí jà Abineer boon. Bi nìn jìn̄ ki cúú-u Siira nyimbɔbil caŋin ní ki fātìi gíiǹní-u Daafiidi kaa nyí.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Abineer fātìi gítìń Eebrɔn tiŋkinee, ní Joowaab cáá-u ki kākatì ŋkpaanceeti kitiŋ punyɔkɔ poon pú kii u là kí lɔ̄kɔfì-u tibee. Niin ní u sāā u-pool kitàataajiki ki kūū-u ki tɔ̀n̄ u-nabiki Asayeel kúm pɔntooŋyi.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Boonee Daafiidi nín dāa gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní u fáá mbiil yii: «Ti-Dindaan nyí yii man nì m-beel kaa kútì Neer jipɔɔn Abineer kúm bɔti poon.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Abineer kúm kpuulool ń lítí Joowaab nì u-dicaŋku yil pu. U-dicaŋku poonee, bin wunti làá nīn yàkà, àá bin dinyaŋgbandi làá cúúyee, àá bin làá nīn sá bideembi ki ŋúb́ ŋkpandɔ ki nyìitēe, àá bin bi làá dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀ee, àá bin ŋkùm làá cúúyee ń taa lóó.»

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Joowaab nì u-nabiki Abisayi nìn sāā ki kūū Abineer, kun puee u nìn kūū bi-nabiki Asayeel kujaaun Gabawɔn tiŋkin.

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn tùkū Joowaab nì bijanjaliibi bin kɔkɔ bí u-ceeyee yii: «Cátímaan tiwan tin ni pēēyee, kí dū kutukub kí gbìn̄ kí dàkà yii ni bí kunimbaaun kí sɔ̄ Abineer kpool.» Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn còom̄ ki pá utaŋkpiil boon ní.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Eebrɔn ní bi síb́ Abineer. Ubɔti nìn súń ki yíkintì Abineer kaakul pu, ní samaa kɔkɔ bíi sūǹ.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti gāā Abineer kúm pu ŋkpiisilan nee yii: Abineer, ba pu ní a kpíì kii ugbaan nín kúù puee?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Baa nìn bóob́ a-ŋalii, kaa bá a-taaŋi abaa. Ama ní bi kūū-si kii unil un kɔ́ binikpɔliibi ŋaanee. Ní samaa kɔkɔ mɔ̄tìi bíi sūǹ u-pu.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní ŋwìiń dáá bée ní samaa dɔ́miń ki páb́ Daafiidi yii ú jī tijin fiii. Ní Daafiidi pūtì ki lī yii: «Ŋwìiń yaa kaa jéetì ní m yaa ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔ àá m jíń tibee, Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ m-tafal ŋkpitim pu.»

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Samaa kɔkɔ nìn dáań ki ká míǹ ní an nìn ŋān̄ bi-cee. Tin kɔkɔ ubɔti nìn ŋáańee nìn ŋān̄ samaa cee ní.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Juuda nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn béè yaadal wiiŋŋu yii ubɔti kaa nìn nyí Neer jipɔɔn Abineer kúm poon tiba.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi gíti bí u-naacimbi yii: «Naa nyí yii dibɔtibil, unikpaan di kpíì díǹ wiiŋŋu Isirayeel tiŋkinaaa?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Nì min kamaa bi sītì m-yil pu ŋkpam m kpántì ubɔtee, maa ŋūǹ kí dàkà mpɔn kii binib bin na bi yíì yii Seeruya nee nín ŋá puee. Ti-Dindaan ń téeǹ utɔŋfiti u-toom paati nín sá puee.»

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti nín gbìl̄ yii Abineer kpíì Eebrɔn tiŋkinee, ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ ní tifaandi kɔ́ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti nìn cáá bijanjakpilib bili bi kpòotī ajanjakiti. Bi nìn yíì ubɔ yii Baana ní ki yíì un kíǹee yii Reekaab. Bi nìn sá Beerooti tiŋkin, ní bi nìn yíì bi-baa yii Riimɔn, u sá Beenjameen naakookun. - Beerooti nìn sá Beenjameen naakookun yab timmu kiba ní.

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: Beerooti yab nìn sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ Giitayiim tiŋkin, ní ki gbíntì niin ki kāl̀ ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Di sá Saayuul jipɔɔn Joonatan nìn cáá jipɔɔn ubɔ u-taaŋi wɔ̀b̄. U nìn cáá abin aŋmoo ŋyunti ŋun binib nìn nyánní Jisirayeel tiŋkin ki dɔ́miń ki lī yii Saayuul nì Joonatan kpíìyee. Un nìn lòó-uee nìn kpáaǹ-u kí sāǹ. U nín bíi nyàab̀ malaa puee ní kibiki nyáń ki lítì ní ki kpántì udeen. Bi nìn yíì-u yii Meefiibooseeti ní.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Riimɔn un sá Beerooti tiŋkinee jipɔmbi Reekaab nì Baana nìn nín cá Isi-booseeti dumpu kuwiŋkuluu. Úǹ nìn dɔ̄ u-diikun ki ŋùŋfī.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kɔ́ u-dumpu ŋyunti ŋun ní úǹ nìn dɔ̄ u-dooŋu pu u-didooŋkaakun ki gèeǹee. Bi nìn kūū-u ki lēē u-yil ki dūu dī Jɔɔdan tantakal saŋŋu ki cōom̀ kunyamɔŋu.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Bi yōoǹ Isi-Booseeti yil ki cáa tīī Daafiidi Eebrɔn tiŋkin ní ki bí-u yii: «Kpèè, Saayuul un nìn sá a-nannanliu ki nìn nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-see jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti yil sɔ̀. Ti-Dindaan kūū Saayuul nì u-maaliŋun yab ki tɔ̀n̄ a-pɔntooŋyi díǹ.»

english_verse: David answered: I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble!
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí Riimɔn un sá Beerooti tiŋkinee jipɔmbi Rakaab nì u-nabiki Baana yii: «Ti-Dindaan un nyántì-mi animbinaaman kɔkɔ poonee bí dimaŋfalin!

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: Unil un nìn dɔ́miń ki tùkū-mi yii Saayuul kpíìyee nìn dākafì yii u nìn cáań-mi dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi ní. Ama m nìn yāntì bi cúú-u ki kūū-u Siikilaagi tiŋkin ki pàn̄ u-nyɔɔbummɔɔndi paati.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Kin ataa aŋa pu ní maa làá pà binikpitib bin sāā ki kūū maanyiiba un dɔ̄ u-dooŋu pu u-diikunee. M làá dáaĺ ni-tafal nnikpaakoon gbanti pu ní kí kúntí-ni kitiŋ pu.»

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daafiidi pú u-naacimpɔmbi kinyɔkɔ yii bí kpɔ̀-bi. Bi nìn kūū-bi ní boonee ki gūutì bi-ŋalii nì bi-taaŋi ki dūu lúntì Eebrɔn nyimbɔbil caŋin. Bi nìn yōoǹ Isi-Booseeti yil ki cáa síb́ Abineer kaakulin, Eebrɔn tiŋkin.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Tiir yab bɔtiu Iram nìn túnní binib Daafiidi cee. Bi nìn cáań-u busubu bun bi yíì seediree dɔi nì kapintab nì bitaŋkpakpitiliibi bí mā-u dibeecindi.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi nì u-yab bóob́ kí já nì Jeebusi yab bin kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee. Binib gbanti nìn bí Daafiidi yii: «Aa làá kɔ́nní kitiŋ nee poon! Bijɔfub nì bideembi saaleen di làá jà-si kí gíiǹ.» Bi nìn là kí lì yii Daafiidi kaa làá ŋmā kí kɔ́.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn ki cá, ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nìn bí u-cee.

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Niinee, Daafiidi nìn béè yii ti-Dindaan u-ba di kāaǹ-u Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel, ní Isirayeel u-nibul puee, u bíi yòontí u-beel yilpu. Daafiidi jipɔmbi bin u màl̄ Jeerusaleemee (Kpèè

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nín nìn yíkì Eebrɔn ki cūtìi kíǹ ki bí Jeerusaleemee, u nìn gíti cáá binimpoobi tikpil ki kútì, binimpukpilib nì nnimpuwaamu, ní bi nìn màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu.

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nín nìn gbìl̄ yii bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì Daafiidi yil pu ki kāaǹ-u dibeelee, ní bi-kɔkɔ nín cá kí nyàab̀-u kí cúú-u. Daafiidi gbìl̄ an bɔtee ní ki nín sìntī kibalilaŋin.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab bàn̄ee ní ki yàl̄ ki gbí Reefayiim tantakalin.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «Ḿ cùú já nì Fiiliistii yabaaa? A làá dū-bi kí ŋá m-ŋaanaaa?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí Daafiidi yii: «Cùú já nì bi, m làá dū-bi kí ŋá a-ŋaan.»

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi nín cá áli Baal Peerasiim ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi niin. Ní ki bí yii: «Kii nnyim nín cífí nnyimbilkaam gundi dibùndi puee, míǹ ní m-Dindaan cátì nsan m-nimbiin m-nannanliibi kansikin!» An pu ní bi pú niin diyindi yii Baal-Peerasiim. Taapu di sá yii: «Un cífí dibùndee Kpiliu.»

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn sáǹ ki fá bi-waaŋi niin, ní Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab fātìi tí gítìń ki yàl̄ ki gbí Reefayiim kí já nì Daafiidi.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan ní úǹ kíí-u yii: «Á taa bíití bi-nimbiin pú kí já nì bi! Màntī bi-boon pú, ní kí dāá nyā bi-pu isufi taapu.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: A yaa láa gbìl̄ bi-tagbiŋŋi pu isufee yilpuee, á yáb́ malaa. Ti-Dindaan di līntì a-nyɔkɔpu kí já nì Fiiliistii yab janjakitil.»

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín bí ú ŋá puee, ní ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ki jìn̄-bi kí yòon̄ Geeba ki tin cáa sāā Geeseer kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní bin tú ti-Dindaan dakaauee yaa dāatì ataa aluuyee ní bí yūĺ kí dū unaja nì dinabil din bí màlmalee kí ŋá saraa.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn baasii bíi ŋōō nì u-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin. U nìn pée pēē bisaraaŋaliibi bɔkutil din bí fálfalee ní.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn yōoǹ ti-Dindaan dakaau ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem nì dipɔɔpindi kuŋkuuntii ki búǹ ŋyin.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi cáá ti-Dindaan dakaau ki kɔ́ǹ Daafiidi Tiŋkinee, Saayuul bisal Miikaal gbóoń tɔkɔlee ki ká ubɔti Daafiidi nín pée yùkufī ki tìintí pu ki ŋōō ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U-ŋool gbanti puee, u nìn kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ-u u-pɔbilin.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū Unimbɔti dakaau ki tākaǹ tɔrɔkupɔɔn poon. Bi nìn yōoǹní-u Abinadaab dumpu kigbantaŋ pu. Abinadaab jipɔɔn Usa nì Ayiiyoo di nìn kpòotī inaa in dàtī tɔrɔkupɔɔn gbantee.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì binibee nìn nín cá Baala tiŋki kin bí Juuda tiŋkinee kí gíiǹní mpèé Dakaau. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un kā keerubimbi puee yindi ní bi nìn dūu pú Dakaa gbanti.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: Bi nín yōoǹ Unimbɔti dakaau Abinadaab dumpu kigbantaŋ pu mimmee, ní Ayiiyoo līī u-nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn bí ki fàal̀ nì dipɔɔpindi ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki bɔ̀ɔ́ tiwambɔɔkaal tin bi dū siipreesi dɔi ki kpítèe kɔkɔ nì ti-bulifi, nì kubeeu nì saŋgu nì ŋgaŋgamu nì icaal nì cancakantib.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Naakɔn tuulool caŋinee ní inaa gbéetì ní Usa tāntì u-ŋal ki cúú Unimbɔti dakaau.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn fōō Usa pu diŋuul, ní ki fáá-u niin u nín yīntèe pu. Usa nìn kpíì Unimbɔti dakaau caŋin niin.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi fōō diŋuul, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn dáaĺ Usa tafal. Ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Peereesi-Usa. Bi dáá gbítìi yíì mpaan gbanti míǹ ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan yaadal wiiŋŋu, ní ki bí yii: «Maa làá ŋmā kí cùnnì ti-Dindaan dakaau m-dumpu!»

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Daafiidi kaa nìn gíti là kí yòon̄ ti-Dindaan dakaau kí cùnnì Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U nìn yāntì bi cáa yóoǹ Oobeedi-Eedoom dumpu. Kijapaai gbanti nìn sá Gaati tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dɔ́miń ki tùkū Daafiidi yii: «Unimbɔti dakaau puee, ti-Dindaan bīiǹ Oobeedi-Eedoom pu ki yāntì u-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ bíi còom̄-u tiŋan.» Niinee Daafiidi cūtì Oobeedi-Eedoom dumpu ki yōoǹ Unimbɔti dakaau ki cáa cūnnì Daafiidi Tiŋkin ifaal poon.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn gāā tanti dakaa gbanti pu. Bi nìn yōoǹní dakaayee ki kɔ́ǹ tantee poon ki yóoǹ mpaan ŋun Daafiidi nìn lēē kí síiń-uee. Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi ki tīī ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: U ŋá saraabi míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki mēē ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan ki bīiǹ samaa pu.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u yākatì Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ tijin. Uninja kamaa nì unimpu kamaa nìn fōō kpɔnɔ nì dinaŋkúndi nì fiinyi subiliŋ akulim kalaau. Míǹ boonee ní báà ŋma fātìi nín kùǹ.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi fātì u-dumpu kí cùú mèè kí bìin̄ u-dicaŋku yab pu, ní Miikaal nyáń ki túŋkì-u ki bí-u yii: «Bi baasii tīī sii Isirayeel bɔtiu díǹ tinyool ní. A lēē a-cancaŋgbeel ki dàkā a-kàliŋkpilib tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi kii unil un kaa bí tibanee nín ŋáań puee!»

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «An sá kí tīī m-Dindaan tinyool pu ní m ŋɔ́ń míǹ. Úǹ di lēē-mi, kun puee m-bɔti fáatiǹ-u ki jítiǹ a-baa nì a-dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ, ní ki kāaǹ-mi dibeel Isirayeel u-nibul pu. U-nimbiin ní m làá nīn fàal̀.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: M làá gíti sìntī m-ba taapu kpataaa kí taa nín̄ sá tiba kí jītíǹ min bí nee. Míǹ gba di làá yàntī bitɔntɔnliibi bin bɔti a sòoǹ nee ń tīī-mi tinyool.»

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Ama maa làá cúú m-laŋŋaŋfitiiku kí fōō u-cee kii m nín fōō-ku Sayuul cee puee. M nìn dū Sayuul ki fá ní ki dū sii ki kāaǹ u-paaŋŋu pu.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: Dalbee ní u bí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan yii: «Kpèè, man kóò dibeecindi din bi dū idɔmɔnti in bi yíì seediree ki kpááyee. Ama ní Unimbɔti dakaau yú tanti un poon bi dū iŋoobu kuti satab ki gāāyee.»

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Ní Naatan bí ubɔti yii: «Tin kā a-pɔbilin a là kí ŋée, cùú ŋá míǹ, di sá yii ti-Dindaan bí a-cee.»

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Ama kunyeeu gbantee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Naatan yii:

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: «Cùú tùkù m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi yii man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Sii di kaa làá mā-mi Kudii ní ḿ kɔ́.

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ daliŋkin m nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, ubɔ kaa máń-mi kudii m kɔ́ ki ká. M nìn sá kii usaŋkinlee ní ki nìn kàal̀ ntimu ki nìkì, ní ki nìn kóò tantin.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Kí kūtèe, ŋyunti ŋun m dūu céeǹ Isirayeel yab bi-saŋkindi poonee, m nìn kāaǹ bikpilib tikpil. Bíǹ di nìn kpāā Isirayeel yab m-nibul. Maa láá pée bālifì-bi dalba dalba yii: <Ba pu ní naa dū seedir dɔi ki máń-mi kudii?>

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee á tùkù m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi yii: <Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di páatì-si ipii boon kupikpaaun ki dū-si ki kāaǹ dibeel m-nibul Isirayeel yab pu.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Laakin kamaa a cūtèe, m bí a-cee. M kúntì a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ a-nimbiin. M làá yòon̄ a-yindi yilpu kii binikpaambi bin kāl̀ kitiŋ puee.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: M làá tīī Isirayeel m-nibul mpaan ŋun pu m làá kàan̄-bee. Bi làá nīn kóò niin kaa làá fàŋkì tiba. Binikpitib biba kaa làá ti dāan̄ kí wɔ́b́-bi kii dooooyee,

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: ŋyunti ŋun ní m nìn kāaǹ bibɔsoonliibi m-nibul Isirayeel puee. M làá fīī-si a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ŋaan kí líí ní á ŋùŋfì. Di sá man ni-Dindaan bíi tùkù-si yii m làá náań-si dicindi.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní sii yuntiŋu yaa láa sāā a cūtìi dōoǹ ki ŋàl̄ a-baabee, m làá dāá lēē a-maaliŋun ubɔ, un sá a-poon naŋuee kí kàan̄ dibeel a-yil pu. M làá dāá yàntī u-beel ń nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Úǹ di làá dāá mā-mi Kudii kí tīī m-yindi tinyool, ní ḿ dāá yàntī u-beel ń nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Man làá nīn sá-u ubaati, ní úǹ ń nīn sá-mi ujipɔnti. U yaa yīntèe, m làá dáaĺ u-tafal kii ubaati nín dátí u-jipɔɔn tafal puee ní.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: An puee ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu, sii a-ba di tùkū man a-tɔntɔnliu yii: <M làá náań-si dicindi>. An pu ní man a-tɔntɔnliu ká kunyannyaau kí mèè-si ŋwimmeem nee.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Daafiidi cūtì ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki mēē-u yii: «M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, ba ní m sá, ní m-dicaŋku bí tilatin ní a cáá-mi ki bàn̄ laakin m bí nee ní?

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people?
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, a wāĺ yii tin a ŋá nee pátì a-cee. Di sá a gíti pōoǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu dicaŋku ipoon iba in bɔti dáá dátìńee. M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, tin a ŋá nee máaǹ unilaaa?

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a nyí man a-tɔntɔnliu tiŋan. Too tilati ní m làá gíti lì kí kūtì.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Kii a nín pōoǹ ki lī yii a làá ŋá pu a-pɔbilinee ní a túń atuŋkpaan nee ki nyántì-ŋi ki dàkā man a-tɔntɔnliu.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a lafun baasii sá ukpaan ní! Aa cáá juti! Sii boonee, Unimbɔti ubɔ gíti kpá, kii ti nín gbìl̀ bi sòoǹ puee.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Dinibul diba gíti bí kitiŋ pu doo ki bí kii Isirayeel nibuleeee? A cūtìi dá-dì ki nyántì Eejipiti yab nì bi-waaŋi ŋaan ki dū-dì ki kpántì a-nibul. A yōoǹ di-yindi yilpu, ki túń atuŋkpaan nì maamaaci tuuŋŋi ki tīī-dì a-tiŋkin. Ditimbundi diba gíti bí ki náań nì a-timbundi din a dá ki nyántì Eejipiti yab timbundi nì bi-waaŋi ŋaaneeee?

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a dū Isirayeel yab ki kpántì a-nibul kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ní a kpántì bi-Nimbɔtiu.
