english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: Bí yòon̄ a-yindi yilpu kí nīn pée cá jaanjaan, binib ń lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan di sá Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu!> Ní man a-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi dicaŋku ń nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ a-nimbiin.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, sii di sá Unimbɔti. A yaa lī puee, míǹ ní a ŋáań, ní a pōoǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu nnaam!

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, bìin̄ man a-tɔntɔnliu naantiibi pu bí nīn pée bí a-nimbiin ki cá jaanjaan. Di sá yii sii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di pōoǹ míǹ. A-biindi puee, man a-tɔntɔnliu dicaŋku làá fōō dibiindi kí nīn cá jaanjaan!»

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Yeeyooda jipɔɔn Beenaya di nìn bí ki kpèé Keereeti nì Peeleeti yab. Daafiidi jipɔmbi mun nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi ní.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: U nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Moowaab yab, ní ki yāntì bi dōoǹ kitiŋ ipɔ̀n ita pu. U nìn kūū bin nìn dɔ̄ ipɔ̀n ili ipeepeekaa puee ní ki kíǹ bin dɔ̄ mpɔ̀nluŋkikaa puee. Míǹ boonee ní Moowaab yab kpántì Daafiidi yumbui ki kíǹ ki pà lampoo ki tìì-u.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn tí jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Reewoob jipɔɔn Adadeeseer, Sooba yab bɔtiu, ŋyunti ŋun úǹ nìn bíi bɔ́ntí kí já kí fōō Eefiraata tiŋki kí ŋá u-taapuee.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Siirii yab bin kóò Damaasee nìn dɔ́miń ki tíkiǹ Adadeeseer, Sooba yab bɔtiu, ní Daafiidi kūū bi-kansikin binib kutukub mmuŋku nì bili.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn kāaǹ kɔmandambi Siirii yab bin kóò Damaasi tiŋkinee ní ki dū-bi ki kpántì u-yumbui, ní bi kíǹ ki pà lampoo ki tìì-u. Laakin kamaa ní Daafiidi yaa nìn pée cūtèe, ti-Dindaan nìn tìì-u dijajil ní.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn jáń ki fōō sindaariya gbampɔɔŋi ŋin Adadeeseer janjaliibi nìn ŋúb́ee, ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: U nìn fōō tasa kúti tikpil ubɔti Adadeeseer timmu Beeta nì Beerootayi poon.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: Ní Tooyi dū u-jipɔɔn Yooram ki tú ú cùú jāam̀ Daafiidi kí pàkà-u u nín jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Adadeeseeree. Di sá Tooyi pulincɔnti mbaa di nìn sá Adadeeseer. Yooram nìn cáá sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti wanti ki tīī Daafiidi.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn dū tiwan gbanti mun ki sú ti-Dindaan, kii u nín nìn dū sindaariya nì tikúti nimbiliŋ tin u nìn jáń ki fōoń atimbun ŋin u nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee ki sú puee.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Ayiituub jipɔɔn Saadooki nì Abiyataar jipɔɔn Ayiimeeleeki di nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi ní Seeraya sá ugbaŋŋmal.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Joowaab un na bi yíì Seeruyee di nìn sá ujanjakpil ní Ayiiluudi jipɔɔn Joosafaati sá ubɔti kpambal.

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Daafiidi bālifì yii: «Unil ubɔ kaa kíǹ Saayuul dicaŋkun ki bí dimaŋfalinaaa? Joonatan puee, ḿ bàà ŋá-u tiŋan.»

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Uninja ubɔ nìn bí Saayuul cindin ki sá u-tɔntɔnliu bi yíì-u yii Siiba. Bi nìn cáań uninjee ubɔti cee, ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Sii ní bi yíì Siibaaa?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «Iiin, ti-baa an sá man.»

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Unil ubɔ kaa kíǹ Saayuul dicaŋkun ḿ ŋá udaan tiŋan kii m nín nìn pōoǹ Unimbɔti nimbiin yii m làá ŋá pueeee?» Ní Siiba kíí-u yii: «Joonatan jipɔɔn ubɔ kíǹ, u-taaŋi wɔ̀b̄.»

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «U bí la?» Ní Siiba kíí-u yii: «U bí Amiyeel jipɔɔn Maakiir cee Loo-Deebaar.»

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Joonatan jipɔɔn Meefiibooseeti, Saayuul naantiiu bāań Daafiidi ceeyee ní ki tātìi dōoǹ Daafiidi nimbiin dicincibil. Ní Daafiidi bālifì-u yii: «Sii di sá Meefiibooseetaaa?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «Iiin ti-baa, an sá man.»

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí-u yii: «Taa fàŋkì. A-baa Joonatan puee, m làá ŋá-si tiŋan. M làá gíiǹ a-naanja Saayuul timmu kɔkɔ ki tīī-si, ní man nì si ń nīn pēē disambibaantiil ki jīǹ baabadal.»

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Ní Meefiibooseeti tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ní ki bí yii: «Ti-baa, ba pu ní a dū man a-tɔntɔnliu un kaa pée bí tiban kii kibɔkɔ kin kpíìyee bɔti ki páb́ a-ba?»

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Ubɔti yíiń Saayuul tɔntɔnliu Siiba ní ki bí-u yii: «M dū tin kɔkɔ sá Saayuul nì u-dicaŋku wantee ki tīī Meefiibooseeti, a-kpiliu naantiiu.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Adadeeseer taapuee nìn ká yii Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Niinee ní bi nì Isirayeel yab sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí bi-kansikin, ní ki sīntì bi-ba taapu ki tīī-bi. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, Siirii yab kíǹ ki fàŋkí kí jòò Amɔn yab.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi bí yii: «M làá ŋá Naasi jipɔɔn Anuun tiŋan kii u-baa nín nìn ŋá-mi tiŋan puee.» Ní Daafiidi lēē u-kàliŋkpilib ki tú bí cùú jāam̀-u u-baa kpool. Bikàliŋkpilib bin Daafiidi nìn túee nìn dūu bàn̄ Amɔn yab tiŋkin.

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: Amɔn yab bɔtibiliŋ bí bi-kpiliu ubɔti Anuun yii: «A dàkafī yii Daafiidi là kí tīī a-baa jilmee pu ní u túnní binib bí dāá jāam̀-si u-kpoolaaa? An kaa sá bí cɔ̄ŋkì kitiŋ kí béé ki-filiŋfeetii kí dāá já kí fōō-kì dalba pu ní bi dɔ́mińaaa?»

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Anuun yāntì bi cúú Daafiidi kàliŋkpilib, ki kōol̀ bi-nyimpuliŋ dijandi, ki gíí bi-bɔkutiŋ ki ŋāatì bi-kpiliŋ pu, ní ki gíiǹ-bi ki líì.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn gbìl̄ tin jítèe. Niinee ní u lēē binib bí cùú tūŋkì u-kàliŋkpilibee, di sá yii bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-bi icoo tikpil. Ní ubɔti bí bí tùkù-bi yii: «Ní kàl̄maan Jeeriikoo ni-nyimpuliŋ ń túkú, boonee ní nīn nín kùnní.» Daafiidi jáń nì Amɔn yab nì Siirii yab (Kpèè

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nín béè yii bi kɔ́ Daafiidi poon ki lēē baadakamee ní bi nyàab̄ binib ki tú Siirii yab bin kóò Beeti-Reeyoob nì Soobayee cee ki pàn̄ bijanjaliibi kutukub mmuŋku, ki pàn̄ ubɔti Maaka janjaliibi kutuku, ní ki pàn̄ Toob yab janjaliibi kutukub saalaa nì bili.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Dàkà dibaatandi, tí dàkà dibaatandi kí fīī ti-nibul nì ti-Nimbɔtiu timmu. Ti-Dindaan ń ŋá min u lèe.»

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: Daafiidi gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki dū Joowaab nì bijanjaliibi bin kɔkɔ cáá dibaatandee ki tú bí cùú já nì bi.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nìn nyáń ki yúl̀ mpɔ̀n pu kitiŋ punyɔkɔki caŋin ki cí kí já. Ní Siirii yab bin kóò Sooba nì Beeti-Reeyoobee nì Toob yab nì Maaka yab náká náká tisatin.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Joowaab dáań ki ká yii an sá anikiti ali ní u làá jáǹ, diba bí nyɔkɔpu diba bí boon pú. Niinee ní u lútì Isirayeel janjaliibi kansikin bimɔntiibi ní ki dū-bi ki yóoǹ ki bíitì Siirii yab.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ní ki dū bin kíǹee ki ŋúbiǹ u-nabiki Abisayi, ki bíitiǹ Amɔn yab.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Joowaab tùkū u-nabiki yii: «Siirii yab yaa bíi pɔ́ɔkíǹ-mee, á dāá tíkiń-mi. M yaa tí ká yii Amɔn yab bíi pɔ́ɔkíǹ-see, ma mun làá dāan̄ kí tíkiń-si.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Niinee Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi nín cá kí já nì Siirii yab, ní bíǹ sáǹ-bi.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nín ká yii Siirii yab sáǹee, ní bi mun sáǹ Abisayi, ki kɔ́ kitiŋin. Niinee Joowaab gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi jì Amɔn yab, ní ki nín fàtī Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Siirii yab nín ká yii Isirayeel yab pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bee, ní bi kóoǹ bi-janjaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Adadeeseer tú binib Siirii yab bin kóò Eefiraati mɔɔl lapu puee cee, ní bíǹ yíkìń ki dūu bāań Eelam. Adadeeseer janjakpiliu Soobaaki di nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū Daafiidi an bɔti, ní u kóoǹ Isirayeel yab janjaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì, ní bi nín cá ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki dūu bàn̄ Eelaam. Siirii yab nìn yúl̀ mpɔ̀n pu ki tātìi gbāaǹ dikɔmbool pu kí já nì Daafiidi.

english_verse: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Dibindi tú, ŋyunti ŋun bibɔtiibi jáà kujaauee, ní ubɔti Daafiidi tú ujanjakpil Joowaab nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì Isirayeel janjaliibi kɔkɔ bí cùú já nì Amɔn yab. Bi nìn pɔ̄fì Amɔn yab, ní ki māntìi tú bi-tiŋyil Raaba kí já nì kì. Daafiidi úǹ nìn gbíntì ki kā Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
translation_verse: Beetiseeba gbíntì uŋmal gbanti poon. Ní u tú bi tùkū Daafiidi yii: «M cáá dipool.»

english_verse: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
translation_verse: Niinee ubɔti Daafiidi tú bí tùkù Joowaab yii: «Yàntī uyitiija Urii ń dāan̄ kí ká-mi.» Ní Joowaab dū Urii ki tú Daafiidi cee.

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Urii dūu bāań ubɔti Daafiidi ceeyee, ní u bālifì-u Joowaab nì bijanjaliibi pu, nì kujaau nín bíi còom̄ puee.

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ubɔti bí Urii yii: «Nín̄ cá a-dumpu kí dòon̄ kí ŋùŋfì.» Urii nìn nyáń ubɔti dumpu ní ubɔti nyàab̄ tiwampɔkaal ki tú bí cáá tīī-u.

english_verse: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
translation_verse: Ama Urii kaa nìn cūtì u-dumpu. U nìn gbíntì dibeecindi punyɔkɔpu ki dōoǹ, u nì ubɔti janjaliibi.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Daafiidi gbìl̄ yii Urii kaa fu cūtìi dōoǹ u-dumpu. Ní ubɔti yíiń-u ki bālifì-u yii: «A nyánní nsan ŋun fɔ̀kɔ̀ee ní. Ba pu ní aa fu cūtì a-dumpu?»

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Ní Urii kíí Daafiidi yii: «Dipoondi dakaau yú tantin, ní Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab kóò tantin. Ujanjakpil Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi dɔ̄ mpaampiin pu dijanjanaapaal pu. Ní man ń nīn cá m-dumpu kí jī kí nyɔ̀ kí dòon̄ m-nimpuu ceeee? M pūtì yii m kpá kí ŋá míǹ jaanjaan.»

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí Urii yii: «Too, gíti kàl̄ díǹ, foolee ḿ fu yàntī á nīn gítí.» Ní Urii gbíntì Jeerusaleem yaadal wiiŋŋu nì kutaa kun gíti wúntèe.

english_verse: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi yíiń-u ú dāan̄ u-dumpu kí jī tijin. Daafiidi nìn yāntì u nyùn̄ ndaam ki gbí. Ama Urii nyáńee ki gbíntì ubɔti janjaliibi cee ki dōoǹ, kaa cūtì u-dumpu.

english_verse: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
translation_verse: Ku wúntì kutaafaauee, Daafiidi ŋmàn̄ Joowaab kugbɔŋu ki dūu ŋúbiǹ Urii ú cáá tīī-u.

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: Tin u nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poonee sèé: «Laakin dikɔ̀ndi yaa píĺ ki pɔ́ɔkèe, á dū Urii kí lìntī nyɔkɔpu. Míǹ boonee bí sútí kí wàatī-u bí kpɔ̀-u.» Daafiidi yāntì bi kūū Batiseeba cal Urii

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Joowaab di nìn cí kitiŋ kin bi nìn māntìi tú kí já kí fōōyee. U nìn dū Urii ki síiǹ laakin u nyí yii binannanliibi baatandambi bée.

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: Kitiŋee yab nìn nyáń ki jáń nì Joowaab nì u-yab. Bi nìn kūū Daafiidi janjaliibi biba. Bi nìn kūū uyitiija Urii mun.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab tú ntuun cūtìi máafì Daafiidi tin jítì kujaaunee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: U nìn tīī ntuunee mara yii: «A yaa máafì-u tin jítì kujaaunee kɔkɔ ki dóò,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Ŋma di kūū Yeerubaal jipɔɔn Abimeeleeki Teebeesi tiŋkin ní? An kaa sá unimpu ubɔɔɔ? U nìn dū kunaau ki tɔ́ an lákatì digundi boon ní ki yá ki kūū-u! Kin ba pu ní nimbi sútì ki pìl̄ digundi ní?> Ubɔti yaa lī mimmee, á kíí-u yii: <A-janjakpiliu Urii, uyitiija mun kpíì.>»

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Ní ntuunee búntì ki bàn̄ ki dū Joowaab nín tùkūń-u pu ú dāá tùkù Daafiidee ki máafì-u.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: U bí Daafiidi yii: «Binannanliibee nìn pɔ́ɔkiǹ-ti. Bi nyáń ki kpìlìń-ti, ama ní ti téé-bi ki cáa gūū bi-tiŋki punyɔkɔki.

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bipintɔliibi yúl̀ digundi poon pú ki tòoń ki lákatí digundi ní an cúú ti-janjaliibi biba ní bi kpíì. A-janjakpiliu Urii, uyitiija mun kpíì.»

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí ntuunee yii: «Á tùkù Joowaab yii: <Taa dū tibɔti nee kí páb́ a-ba. Kujaau poonee, ŋkúm kù ní kaa gàntī. Pɔ́ɔǹ kí já kí fōō kitiŋ gbanti kí kpēelikì-kì.> Á tīī-u kunyannyaau míǹ.»

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Beetiseeba nín gbìl̄ yii u-cal Urii kpíìń kujaaunee ní u kāl̀ u-kpool.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Dikpool jítèe ní Daafiidi yāntì bi cūtìi cáań-u u-dumpu. U nìn dū-u ki kpántì u-nimpuu, ní u màl̄-u kibininjabiki. Ama tin Daafiidi nìn ŋée kaa nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Ugaajee nìn cáá ipii nì iŋoobu nì inaa tikpil.

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Dalbee unicaan ubɔ kɔ́ ugaajee. Ama ugaajee kaa là kí cúú u-piii àá u-ŋoobui àá u-naai kansikin ubɔ kí ŋá u-nicaaŋwu tijin. Ama ní ki cúú usoodaan pisaliiki ki kūū ki ŋá u-nicaaŋwu tijin.»

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi fōō ugaajee pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu, ní ki bí Naatan yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí nee yii unil un ŋá mimmee máaǹ bí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: U nín ŋá pu kaa súń u-juti saayee, ú pà mpisalimu munaa kí téeǹ kipisaliiyee pu.»

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Ní Naatan bí Daafiidi yii: «Unil un ŋá mimmee, sii dee! Kpèè ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: <Man di lēē-si á nīn sá Isirayeel yab bɔtiu. Man di fīī-si ki nyántì Saayuul ŋaan.

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: M dū a-kpiliu Saayuul dicaŋku ki tīī-si, ki dū u-nimpoobi ki ŋá a-ŋaan. M dū-si ki kāaǹ á jī dibeel Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab pu. An yaa bàà pátì, m bàà ŋūǹ kí kūtì-si tin jítiǹ mimmee.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní a kpēē man a-Dindaan fám ki ŋá min kaa fáatiǹ-mee? A kūū uyitiija Urii. A yāntì Amɔn yab kūū-u, ní sii fōō u-nimpuu ki cáá.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: An puee kí yòon̄ kɔŋkɔnnee kí nīn cée, nnikpaakoon pée kpá kí lóó a-dicaŋkun, di sá yii a kpēē-mi fám ki fōō uyitiija Urii nimpuu ki cáá.

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. M làá yàntī mbusu ń jēetí a-pu, ní mbusu gbantee làá nyānní sii a-ba dicaŋkun ní. A-nimbilaaliyin ní m làá fōō a-nimpoobi kí tīī a-yab ubɔ ní ú dòon̄ nì bi ŋwiimpu.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii sii ŋá dibalin ní, ama man làá nyāntí tin a ŋée Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbilaaliyin ŋwiimpu ní.»

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Ama tibɔti nee poonee, a kpēē ti-Dindaan fám. An puee kibininjabiki kin bi màl̄-si nee làá kpú.»

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Naatan nín kùǹ. Batiseeba biki kúm Ti-Dindaan yāntì iween iba dɔ́miń ki cúú Urii nimpuu Batiseeba biki kin u màl̄ Daafiidee.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn mēē Unimbɔti kibiki gbanti pu. U nìn bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ, ní u yaa nìn kɔ́ u-diikunee, u dɔ̀ kitiŋ fám ní.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: U-kàliŋkpilib bin bí u-cindinee dɔ́miń u-cee ki gbāam̀-u ú yīkì kitiŋ ní u yíì, ní kaa là kí jī tijin bi-cee.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: An dāa tú kinyɔŋee, kibikee kpíì. Daafiidi tɔntɔnliibi nìn fàŋkí kí tùkù-u yii kibiki kpíì. Bi nìn bíi lì yii: «Ŋyunti ŋun kibikee dáá bée, ti nìn sòon̄ nì u waa pílifiǹ-ti. Kɔŋkɔnnee ti làá ŋá mana kí tùkù-u yii kì kpíì. U ŋūǹ kí ŋá u-ba tin kaa ŋān̄ee!»

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Daafiidi gbìl̄ bi nín bí ki mùkufī bi-ŋmaniŋmee, ní u béè yii kibikee kaa ti bí. Ní u bālifì-bi yii: «Kibikee kpíì níii?» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Iiin, kì kpíì.»

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: U-tɔntɔnliibi bālifì-u yii: «Ti-baa, tin a bíi ŋáań nee là kí lì yii ba dee? Di sá ŋyunti ŋun kibiki dáá bée, a nìn bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ ní ki sūǹ. Kɔŋkɔnnee kì nín kpíìyee ní a yíkìi kāl̀ ki bíi jīǹ tijin.»

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí-bi yii: «Ŋyunti ŋun kibiki dáá bée, m nìn bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ ki sūǹ, di sá m nìn dàkafī yii an yaa yíì ti-Dindaan làá sɔ̄ m-saai kí cáaǹ-kì.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee kì kpíì, ba pu ní m nín gíti bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ? M ŋūǹ kí gíiǹní-kì dimaŋfalinaaa? Man di làá dāá cù ki-cee, kíǹ kaa ti ŋūǹ kí gítiń m-cee.» Bi màl̄ Saloomɔn

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Daafiidi ŋméeǹ u-nimpuu Batiseeba. Boonee ní u nì u kpáfì ní u cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Saloomɔn. Ti-Dindaan nìn néeń-kì.

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: U nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Naatan pu ní ki tùkū Daafiidi míǹ. Ní Naatan pú-kì diyindi yii Yeediidiya, an taapu di sá yii: «Un ti-Dindaan néeńee.» Daafiidi jáń ki fōō Raaba tiŋki (

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ujanjakpil Joowaab nìn cūtìi jáń nì Amɔn yab tiŋki Raaba ki fōō laakin ubɔti kóòyee.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Joowaab nìn tú binib bí tùkù Daafiidi yii: «M bíi jáà nì Raaba tiŋkin yab, ki fōō bi-tiŋki laakin bi bíl̀ nnyimee.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: An puee kpāfì bijanjaliibi bin kíǹee, sii a-ba ń dāan̄ kí já kí fōō-kì. Maa là kí já kí fōō-kì m-ba kí fōō diyindi.»

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kpáfì bijanjaliibi bin kíǹee ní bi dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Raaba ki fōō-kì.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn cúú kitiŋ gbanti nib kuyuŋu bi tūǹ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Biba nìn sèekì ki kpítí ataŋkpee, ní biba gà isufi, ní biba mun māā brikisib. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋá Amɔn yab bin bí ntimu mun kɔkɔ kíǹee poon. U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní u nì u-janjaliibi nín gítí Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee tin jítèe sèé. Daafiidi jipɔɔn Abisaloom nìn cáá niisal ubɔ bi yíì-u Taamaar. U nìn cáá kunyaaŋŋu tikpil. Usapɔɔnee nìn kɔ́ Daafiidi jipɔɔn Aminɔn tikpil.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Aminɔn niisal Taamaar nín nìn kɔ́-u puee nìn yāntì an dūu ŋá-u iween. U-niisalee nín kaa nìn nyí uninjee puee, an nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ú ŋmā kí sútí kí pìl̄-u.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Aminɔn nìn cáá bɔɔ ubɔ bi yíì-u Yoonadaab. U nìn sá Daafiidi maan Simeeya jipɔɔn ní. Kijapaayee nìn wálifì tikpil.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: U nìn bālifì Aminɔn yii: «Sii sá ubɔti jipɔɔn ní, ba pu ní kutaafaau kamaa a pée kā kunandaŋu míǹ? Tiba yaa bí tùkù-maa!» Ní Aminɔn kíí-u yii: «An sá m-naal Abisaloom niisal Taamaar di kɔ́-mi tikpil.»

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yoonadaab bí-u yii: «Dòon̄ a-dooŋu pu kí ŋá kii a būǹee. A-baa yaa dɔ́miń kí màntì a-puee ní á bí-u yii: <Yàntī m-niisal Taamaar ń dāan̄ kí ŋá-mi tijin. Ú nīn kā m-nimbiin ki ŋáań tijin m wāĺ-u. U yaa dóòyee, úǹ u-ba ń cáań kí tīī-mi ḿ jī.>»

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Niinee Aminɔn dōoǹ ki ŋá kii u būǹee. Ubɔti dɔ́miń kí màntì u-puee ní Aminɔn bí-u yii: «Yàntī m-niisal Taamaar ń dāan̄ kí kàl̄ m-nimbiin kí tɔ̄-mi kalaabi bili pu yéè kí tīī-mi ḿ ŋmɔ́.»

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi tú ubɔ Taamaar dumpu ú tùkù-u yii: «Cù a-niija Aminɔn cee kí ŋá-u tijin.»

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Ní Taamaar nín cá u-niija Aminɔn cee, ki bàn̄ ki ká-u u dɔ̄ ndoo pu. Ní u kāl̀ u-nimbiin niin ki búuń ŋyim ki tɔ́-u kalaabi.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: U wūutì kalaayee ní ki cáa yóoǹ u-nimbiin ú ŋmɔ́, ní u yíì. Ní Aminɔn bí yii: «Nyāntímaan binib kɔkɔ doo». Ní bin kɔkɔ nìn bí u-ceeyee nyáń.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Ní u bí Taamaar yii: «Cáań-mi kalaabee m-diikun, kí lēē kí tīī-mi ḿ ŋmɔ́.» Ní Taamaar yōoǹ kalaabi bin u tɔ́ee ki cáa kɔ́ǹ u-niija Aminɔn diikun.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u lēē kalaa ki tīī-u ú ŋmɔ́ee ní u cúú-u ki bí yii: «M-niisal, yàntī ḿ dòon̄ nì si.»

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Ní Taamaar fáá mbiil yii: «M-niija, taa bīil̀-mi. Baa ŋáań míǹ Isirayeel yab tiŋkin. A taa ŋá icoo bɔti gbanti.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: A yaa ŋá mimmee, la ní m làá cáá m-cooi gbanti kí báĺ? A làá kpántí kpayiliku Isirayeel tiŋkin. Míǹ puee, sòoǹ nì ubɔti, waa làá yíí yii á taa cáá-mi.»

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Aminɔn kaa pée là kí pīlifiǹ-u. U cúú-u mpɔn ní ki dōoǹ nì u.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, Aminɔn nìn kíǹ ki ná Taamaar. Kináŋ kin u nìn kíǹ ki cáá u-puee nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ dineendi din u nìn bí yii u néeń-uee. Ní Aminɔn bí-u yii: «Yīkìí nyā doo!»

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Ní Taamaar kíí-u yii: «A yaa jìn̄-mee kpitii làá nyàŋkiǹ in a dáá ŋá nee.» Ama ní Aminɔn kaa ti pée là kí pīlifiǹ-u.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: Ní u yíiń u-tɔntɔnliu ki bí yii: «Jà usapɔɔn nee kí nyāntí doo kí dū kudii kí pìin̄ kí kpàl̄.»

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔnlee jìn̄ Taamaar ki nyántì ki dū kudii ki pīiǹ ki kpàl̄. Taamaar nìn pēē dibɔkutifɔkɔl dimɔntiil diba, di sá yii bɔtiisalib bin kaa nìn nyí uninjee nín nìn pèentí puee dee.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Ní Taamaar dū ŋfantam ki pùkū u-yil, ki dáaĺ ki cátì dibɔkutimɔntiil din u pēēyee, ní ki dū u-ŋalii ki túǹ u-yil pu ki còom̄ ki cá ki gbáà ibiil.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Ní u-niija Abisaloom bālifì-u yii: «A-niija Aminɔn bíil̀-si níii? Taa ti lì tiba, m-niisal, a-niija dee. Taa dūú páb́ a-ba.» Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, Taamaar nìn kíǹ ki bí u-niija Abisaloom cee icoo poon.

english_verse: When David heard what had happened to Tamar, he was very angry. But Amnon was his oldest son and also his favorite, and David would not do anything to make Amnon unhappy.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn gbìl̄ tin jítèe kɔkɔ ní ki fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. Ama waa nìn wòon̄ Aminɔn, di sá yii úǹ di nìn sá u-jipɔŋkpiliu ní u nìn néeń-u tikpil.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Ama Abisaloom kaa nìn gíti sòoǹ nì Aminɔn. U nìn kíǹ ki ná-u, kun puee u nìn bíil̀ u-niisal Taamaar. Abisaloom yāntì bi kūū Aminɔn ní ki sáǹ

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Tíǹ jítì abin ali boonee, bi bíi cēē Abisaloom piii kuti Baal-Asɔɔr, Eefiraayiim tiŋki caŋin. Abisaloom nìn yíiń ubɔti jipɔmbi kɔkɔ bí jī bi nín bíi cēē u-piii kutee jiŋaaliu.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Abisaloom cūtìi ká u-baa Daafiidi ki bí-u yii: «Ti-baa, bi bíi cēē man a-tɔntɔnliu piii kuti. M gbāam̀-si, si nì a-kàliŋkpilib ń céeǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu tí cùú jī jiŋaal gbanti.»

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «Aayee m-jipɔɔn, ti-kɔkɔ kaa máaǹ kí cù, án làá nīn sá-si digìŋ́kpaandi ní.» Ní Abisaloom pée gbíntìi cɔ́ yii bí cù, ní ubɔti yíì, ama ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ u-pu.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Ní Abisaloom bí yii: «Mimmee sii yaa kaa làá cùee, pɔ̄ nsan m-maan Aminɔn ń céeǹ-ti.» Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «Ba pu ní ú céeǹ-si?»

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Ní Abisaloom gbíntìi cɔ́. Ubɔti dāa gīīyee ní ki yāntì Aminɔn nì u-jipɔmbi bin kíǹee cūtì. Ní Abisaloom bɔ́ntì tijin mbɔtiyaamin.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Abisaloom tīī u-tɔntɔnliibi mara nee yii: «Ní nīn cɔ́ŋkí Aminɔn. U yaa láa nyùn̄ ndaam ki bál̀ an nyāatì-u ní m yaa láa bí-ni yii: <Kpɔ̀maan Aminɔŋyee!> Ní kpɔ̀-u! Ní taa fàŋkì tiba, man di tīī-ni mara yii ní kpɔ̀-u. Kámaan dipɔbil kí dàkàmaan tininjati.»

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Ní Abisaloom tɔntɔnliibi kūū Aminɔn kii u nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. Niinee ubɔti jipɔmbi bin kíǹee yíkìi yōoǹ bi-mambooŋyi ki sáǹ ki kátì.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Bi dáá bí nsanni ki sáń ki cá ní Daafiidi gbìl̄ yii: «Abisaloom kūū ubɔti jipɔmbi kɔkɔ pílpil báà ubɔ kaa kíǹ.»

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Niinee ubɔti cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki cátì ní ki dōoǹ kitiŋ. Ní u-kàliŋkpilib mun cátì bi-wanti tin bi pēēyee ki yú ki gɔ́ń-u.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daafiidi maan Simeeya jipɔɔn Yoonadaab bí yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a taa dàkafì yii bi kūū a-jipɔmbi kɔkɔ. Aminɔn baba ní bi kūū. Doooo ŋyunti ŋun Aminɔn bíil̀ u-niisalee ní Abisaloom nìn lī ki yóoǹ yii u làá kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: An puee, á taa dàkafì yii bi kūū a-jipɔmbi kɔkɔ, Aminɔn baba ní bi kūū.

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Abisaloom úǹ sáǹ.» Un nìn sí sintilee kpēē ndanee ki ká dinikitikpaandi diba tàkāń Ooroonayiim dandi ki kpàkaǹ dijool ki dòoń.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Ní Yoonadaab bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa, kpèè a-jipɔmbi di dòońee! M nín bàà pée tùkū-si puee, míǹ ní ti wāĺ nee.»

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: U sòon̄ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ ní ubɔti jipɔmbi dūu bāań. Bi nìn kíĺ nsiim, ní ubɔti nì u-kàliŋkpilib mun bíi sūǹ lɔ̀lɔlɔ.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn bíi súntí Aminɔn kúm pu fiii fiii, ní diŋuul din u nìn gíí Abisaloom puee mun sɔ̄ŋkì.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Joowaab un na bi nìn yíì Seeruyee nìn dáań ki ká yii ubɔti dáá gbíntìi dàkafī Abisaloom pu.

english_verse: and he sent someone to bring in the wise woman who lived in Tekoa. Joab told her, “Put on funeral clothes and don't use any makeup. Go to the king and pretend you have spent a long time mourning the death of a loved one.” Then he told her what to say.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, á cù kí ká ubɔti kí sòoǹ nì u tin m làá tùkù-si nee.» Niinee ní Joowaab dàkā-u tin u làá tin sòoǹ nì ubɔtee.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Unimpuee yíkì ki nín cá ubɔti cee. U bàn̄ee ní ki tātìi dōoǹ ubɔti nimbiin dicincibil ní ki bí yii: «Ti-baa, pée fīī-mi!» -

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Ba ní a là ní?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa, m sá ukpiipu ní. M-cal kpíì.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: M nìn cáá jipɔmbi bili, ní bi jáń kusaaun. Báà ubɔ nìn kpá niin kí pàtī-bi ní ubɔ fáá ki kūū u-juti.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-maaliŋun yab kɔkɔ yíkìi kāl̀ m-pu ki bí-mi yii: <Nyāntí unikpɔlee kí ŋúbíǹ-ti tí kpɔ̀-u kí téeǹ u-nabiki kin u kūūyee yil pu. - Ti yaa ŋá mimmee, ti kúntì un làá jī difakalee dee.> - Mimmee bi púntìi gbíntì dimɔsiŋkɔndi din bàà pée kíǹ-mee dee. Baa là kí kíń m-cal mmaabool bí nīn téetí u-yindi kitiŋ pu.»

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Nín̄ kùǹ. M làá yóoń mara ubɔ a-pu bí taa ŋá-si tiba.» -

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee fātìi bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, tin kɔkɔ làá bàń tibɔti nee poonee kpuulool ń lítí man nì m-dicaŋku pu. An taa lítí sii nì a-tiŋki pu.»

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Ubɔ yaa gíti sòon̄ an bɔti a-ceeyee, á cáań udaan m-cee. Waa làá ti sòoǹ-tì a-cee ŋwindal.»

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee bí yii: «Ti-baa, pée pùtī ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu, án nín làá ŋá pu un làá kpɔ̀ m-jipɔɔn kí tɔ̀ ipɔntoonee ń taa kpɔ̀-u kí yàntī m-nimbinaamandi ń gíti lákatíǹ-mee.» - Ní ubɔti bí yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan yii a-jipɔɔn yil pu kuyikpiliu kubɔbɔ kaa làá lítí kitiŋ.»

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee gíti bí yii: «Ti-baa, a kíikí m gíti sòoǹ nì si tibaaa?» Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: - «Sòoǹ.»

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee bí ubɔti yii: «Kin a nyí míǹ dee, ba pu ní a ŋá Unimbɔti nibul kii bi nín là kí ŋá m-jipɔɔn puee? Kii a nín dáá sòon̄ pu nee, a kūū a-bɔti, di sá yii aa nyántìń Abisaloom kitiŋ kin poon u sáǹ ki kɔ́ee ki gíiǹní.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Ti-kɔkɔ làá dāá pée kpú ŋwindal ní. Ti bí kii nnyim min bi yaa dūu fá, baa ti ŋūǹ kí fāā-mèe ní. Ama an kaa sá míǹ ní Unimbɔti bɔ́ntì Abisaloom pu. U lēē yii ú taa nín̄ bí ki dátiǹ-u.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, m yaa dɔ́miń sii ti-baa ubɔti cee ki sòon̄ nì si tibɔti neeyee, an sá yii samaa nín sòoǹ puee di fāaǹ-mi. Niinee ní m dākafì yii: <M yaa sòon̄ nì ubɔti, an yaa yíì u làá gbìl̄ kí tīiǹ-mi.>

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ubɔti làá kíí kí nyāntí-mi un bàà là kí kúntí man nì m-jipɔɔn, Unimbɔti nibul kansikinee ŋaan.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Ní man a-tɔntɔnliu lī m-neen yii: <Tin ti-baa ubɔti làá sòoǹee làá cáań ŋgbansɔŋfi. Di sá yii ti-baa ubɔti sá kii Unimbɔti tuuŋŋuee ní, u nyí kí gàntī tin ŋān̄ee nì tin kaa ŋān̄ee. Ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn bí a-cee.>»

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti bí unimpuee yii: «M làá bàlifì-si tibɔti tiba. Á kíí-mi-tì ibaamɔn.» - Ní unimpuee kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, m gbāam̀-si, sòoǹ tin a cááyee.»

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Joowaab nyɔkɔ kaa cēē tibɔti nee poonaaa?» - Ní unimpuee kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, ibaamɔn ní m làá sòoǹ. A nín sòon̄ puee, a sòon̄ ki tɔ́ kufaaun ní. Tiŋman, a-tɔntɔnliu Joowaab di sáŋkì-mi ḿ sòoǹ tin kɔkɔ m sòon̄ nee.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: A-tɔntɔnliu Joowaab ŋá míǹ kí kpántí tibɔti tin poon ti bí nee ní. Ama sii ti-baa ubɔti cáá iciin kii Unimbɔti tuuŋŋuee ní, a nyí tin kɔkɔ pée jītí kitiŋ puee.»

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti ká Joowaab ki bí-u yii: «A nín lī puee m làá ŋá míǹ. Cùú gíiǹní Abisaloom doo.»

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab tātìi dōoǹ ubɔti nimbiin dicincibil ní ki jáam̀-u ki lī yii: «Ti-baa, kɔŋkɔnnee man a-tɔntɔnliu béè yii m cáá diyimɔɔl a-cee, di sá yii a kíí ki fōō m-nyɔkɔ.»

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab yíkìi kíĺ nsan ki búntì Geesuur tiŋkin. U nìn gíiǹní Abisaloom Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Ama ní ubɔti bí yii: «Abisaloom ń taa dāan̄ m-cee, ú nīn kùǹ u-dumpu.» Niinee Abisaloom nín kùǹ u-dumpu ubɔti kaa fōō-u. Daafiidi nì Abisaloom kansikin fātìi mɔ́ɔkì

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Dibintil kamaayee, u nìn cēē u-yikpiti, di sá yii an nìn nyìm̀ u-pu. Bi yaa nìn cáń u-yikpitee, bi nìn ŋmàntī kiiloobi bili nì ipaa ki nóó nì ubɔti nín yóoǹ nnyiŋfi ŋun bí nīn ŋmàntēe.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Abisaloom nìn cáá mbininjabiyaamu muta nì kinimpubiki kiba. Bi nìn yíì-kì yii Taamaar. U nìn ŋān̄ usapɔɔn an kaa cáá bí lì.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Abisaloom nìn kāl̀ Jeerusaleem abin ali, u-baa kaa kíí u gbóoń u-cee.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, Abisaloom tú bí yíiń Joowaab ú tɔ̄-u u-baa cee, ní Joowaab yíì kaa dɔ́miń. Ní u fātìi tí tú unil nliliitiim Joowaab cee, ní u yíì kaa dɔ́miń.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u bí u-tɔntɔnliibi yii: «Kéè ni ká ɔɔji saaku kun dɔ̄ ki pìlīǹ-mee yaa! Joowaab saaku dee. Ní cùú tūū-kù ŋŋmi.» Ní u-tɔntɔnliibi cūtìi tūū kusaau gbanti ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab cūtì Abisaloom cee ki bālifì-u yii: «Ba pu ní a-tɔntɔnliibi cūtìi tūū m-saaku ŋŋmi ní?»

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Ní Abisaloom kíí-u yii: «M nìn tú bi yíiń-si ní a yíì kaa dɔ́miń. M bàà nìn là kí tɔ̄-si ubɔti cee á bàlifì-u yii: <Ba pu ní m yíkìń Geesuur tiŋkin ki dɔ́miń doo ní? An bàà sɔ́ ḿ nīn gbíntìi bí niinaa! Kɔŋkɔnnee m là kí cùú ká ubɔti, m yaa ŋá ikpiti iba, ú kpɔ̀-mi!>»

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab nín cá ubɔti cee ki máafì-u Abisaloom nín lī puee. Ní ubɔti yíiń Abisaloom. U bàn̄ u-ceeyee ní ki tātìi dōoǹ ubɔti nimbiin dicincibil. Niinee ní ubɔti kpàl̄-u.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Abisaloom nyàab̄ janjatɔrɔku nì itaamu, ní bijanjaliibi imuŋku ili nì saalaa sáń ki līī u-nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Abisaloom nìn péetí kutaafaau ní kí cùú kàl̄ kitiŋ punyɔkɔ nsan caŋin. Ŋyunti ŋun kamaa ubɔ yaa nìn cáá tiba ki cá ubɔti dumpu ki là ubɔti ń sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì kí tīī-uee ní ú yíiń udaan kí bàlifì-u yii : «A nyánní kitiŋ kilakan ní?» Ní úǹ ń kíí-u yii : «Man a-tɔntɔnliu nyánní Isirayeel yab naakooku kubɔ poon ní.»

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Ní Abisaloom ń bí-u yii: «A-bɔti ŋān̄ ki túĺ nsan, ama ubɔ kaa bí ubɔti cee ki làá gbìl̄ kí tīiǹ-si.»

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa nìn bāań ki gbāaǹ kí jāam̀-uee, ní ú cúú u-ŋal kí yáatí-u kí yóoń ní kí kpàl̄-u.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Abisaloom nìn ŋáań bin kɔkɔ nìn cá ubɔti cee ú sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì bi-bɔtee. U nìn ŋá míǹ ní ki ŋmātiǹ Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Abin anaa boonee, ní Abisaloom bí ubɔti yii: «Pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ cù Eebrɔn kí pà ipoon in m nìn pōoǹ ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun m nìn bí Geesuur, Siirii yab tiŋkinee, man a-tɔntɔnliu nìn pōoǹ yii: <M-Dindaan, a yaa yāntì m fātìi gítì Jeerusaleemee, m làá cù Eebrɔn kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī-si.>»

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.» Ní u yíkìi kíĺ nsan ki búntì Eebrɔn.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Unil ubɔ nìn dɔ́miń ki tùkū Daafiidi yii: «Isirayeel yab gítì Abisaloom jandi pú.»

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí u-kàliŋkpilib bin nìn bí u-cee Jeerusaleemee yii: «Tí yīkì kí sām̀maan malaa, an yaa sá fám, Abisaloom kaa làá tàan̄ ti-kansikin báà ubɔ. Yáb́maan, an yaa kaa sá míǹ, u làá cúú-ti malaa, kí kpɔ̀ binib kɔkɔ kí cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ kitiŋ nee pu.»

english_verse: The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Ní u-kàliŋkpilib kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a yaa pée lēē puee, míǹ ní ti làá ŋá.»

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Ní u-yab còom̄ ki jītí. Bíǹ di sá Keereeti yab kɔkɔ nì Peeleeti yab kɔkɔ bin cí ubɔtee, nì Gaati yab binib alaataa aluu bin nìn nóoń-u doooo Gaati tiŋkinee. Bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ nìn cōom̀ ki jítì ubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Ubɔti bí Gaati yab janjakpiliu Itaayii yii: «Ba pu ní a nóoń-ti? Gítí kí cùú nīn bí ubɔtipɔɔn cee, di sá yii a sá unicaan ní, ní bi jìn̄-si gba a-tiŋkin.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: A dáá pée bàń dee ní ḿ kpáaǹ-si tí nīn tú ki yìiǹaaa? Maa kpáàa nyí laakin m cée. Míǹ puee kpáaǹ a-nabiyaamu kí gítí. Ti-Dindaan ń dàkà-si u-poommɔŋŋu nì u-laŋŋaŋfitiiku.»

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Itaayii kíí ubɔti yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan nì sii ubɔti yii, laakin ti-baa ubɔti làá nīn bée, án yaa sá kí kpúɔɔɔ, án yaa tí sá kí ŋmátáaa, niin ní man a-tɔntɔnliu mun làá nīn bí.»

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «An ŋān̄, dāá lìntī nyɔkɔpu.» Niinee ní Itaayii nì u-janjaliibi nì bi-dicaŋŋi jítìi līntì nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bijanjaliibi nìn còom̄ ki jītí Daafiidi nimbiinee, samaa nìn gà dituweel ní. Ní ubɔti dūtì Seedrɔn bùmbiki nì u-yab kɔkɔ, ní ki dūu túĺ kuteeu saŋŋu.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Saadooki nì Leefii yab bin tūntí Mpèé dakaauee mun nìn bí bi-kansikin. Leefii yab nìn túutì dakaayee ki yóoǹ ní Abiyataar kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań saraabi áli binib kɔkɔ dāa sáǹ ki nyáń kitiŋin ki dóò.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Ubɔti bí Saadooki yii: «Gíiǹ Unimbɔti dakaau kitiŋin. Ti-Dindaan yaa súń m-saai, u làá fàtīí gíiǹní-mi. U làá yàntī ḿ fàtīí ká Unimbɔti dakaau nì u-kɔŋkooŋŋu.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Ama u yaa tí bí yii maa ti fáatiǹ-u, ú ŋá-mi min ní u lèe.»

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti gíti bí usaraaŋakpil Sadooki yii: «Aa káaa? Nín̄ gítí mmɔŋki nì ŋgbansɔŋfi sii nì a-jipɔɔn Ayiimaasi nì usaraaŋakpil Abiyataar nì u-jipɔɔn Yoonatan.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Man làá nīn bí kuteeun laakin Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kaa nyóò binib còom̄ ki dùtēe ki cí ni-kansikin ubɔ ń dāan̄ kí tùkù-mi tin bíi jītée.»

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Saadooki nì Abiyataar fātìi gíiǹ Unimbɔti dakaau Jeerusaleem ní ki gbíntì niin. Daafiidi tú Ayiimaasi ú cùú cɔ̄ŋkì Abisaloom

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn dàb̀ ɔliifi sufii jool pu ki sūǹ. U nìn dū ŋŋaabu ki bīiǹ u-nimbiin kí dàkà u-nimbaaku, ní ki còom̄ fám kaa táká anaataka. U nì bin nìn nóóyee mun nìn dū iŋaabu ki bīiǹ bi-nimbiiŋyi ki dàb̀ dijool ki sūǹ.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Daafiidi yii: «Ayiitoofeel kútì Abisaloom nì u-yab bin fōō dibeelee pu.» Ní Daafiidi mēē yii: «M gbāam̀-si m-Dindaan, yàntī Ayiitoofeel saŋkii kɔkɔ ń taa tɔ̄ ditundi.»

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Daafiidi dàb̄ ki bàn̄ dijool yilpu kúnti kunti laakin bi jáaḿ Unimbɔtee, ní u ká uarkitiija Usayii, u-saŋkiliu còom̄ ki túŋkí-u. Tiwan tin u nìn pēēyee nìn cátì ní u-yil táká ntam.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí-u yii: «A yaa dɔ́miń m-cee, a làá kpántí-mi digìńdi ní.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Ama nín̄ gítí kitiŋin Abisaloom cee kí tùkù-u yii: <Ti-baa ubɔti, m dɔ́miń kí nīn kíǹ ki bí a-cee ní. Dooooyee m nìn tūǹ ditundi ki tìì a-baa ní, ama kɔŋkɔnnee sii ní m làá tɔ̄ ditundi kí tīī.>» Niinee a ŋūǹ kí pìin̄ Ayiitoofeel saŋkii kí tūtuǹ-mi.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋakpilib Saadooki nì Abiyataar bí niin kí tūtuǹ-si. Tin kɔkɔ yaa bíi jítì dibeecindinee, á māafì-bi.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Saadooki jipɔɔn Ayiimaasi nì Abiyataar jipɔɔn Yoonatan bí bi-cee niin. Tin yaa pée bíi jītée, ní tɔ̄ń-bi bí dāá tùkù-mi.

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Daafiidi saŋkiliu Usayii cá kí kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, Abisaloom mun dòoń kí kɔ́ dee.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Daafiidi cōom̀ ki jítì dijool yilpu kpalaayee ní ki tú Meefiibooseeti tɔntɔnliu Siiba nsanni u dòoń u-cee. U nìn kpàl̄ mmamu muli mu túń kpɔnɔb alaataa ali nì fiinyi subiliŋ akulim asaka dilaataal, nì fiigi subiliŋ dilaataal, nì ndamam kuloou.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti bālifì Siiba yii: «Tin kɔkɔ ní a tú nee, a làá ŋá nì ba?» Ní Siiba kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, mmamu nee sá ki tīī a-dicaŋkun yab ń nīn cáa kàal̀, ní kpɔnɔb nì asubilee sá a-naacimpɔmbi jikaati, ní bin cōom̀ kuteeun ki gīīyee ń nīn cáá ndaamee ki sɔ̀ŋkī bi-neen.»

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Kin a-kpiliu Saayuul naantiiu Meefiibooseeti bí la?» Ní Siiba kíí-u yii: «U bí Jeerusaleem niin. Di sá u lī yii: <Kɔŋkɔnnee, Isirayeel yab làá gíiǹ m-naanja beel kí tīī-mi.>»

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Too, an ŋān̄. Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, m fōō Meefiibooseeti fakal kɔkɔ ki tīī-si.» Niinee ní Siiba tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ní ki bí yii: «Ti-baa, m jáam̀-si diyimɔɔl din a pú-mee pu.» Simeeyii nì Daafiidi bɔti

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi bàn̄ Bawuriim timbiliikinee, uninja ubɔ nìn nyēeń ki-ni bi yíì-u Simeeyii, Geera jipɔɔn. U nì Saayuul nìn pēē mmaal ní u kíĺ ki bíi tòó Daafiidi mbusu.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: U nìn bí ki tòó Daafiidi nì u-kàliŋkpilib kɔkɔ ataŋkpee, min kamaa samaa nì bijanjaliibi nìn bí u-ŋaŋgiil pú nì u-ŋaŋgan pú bi còom̄ ki cée.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: U nín nìn tòó-u mbusu ki lì puee di sá yii: «Nyā doo, nyā doo, unikpɔl un bí nee, aa pée bí tiban!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yāntì binib bin kɔkɔ a kūū Saayuul dicaŋkunee fatikuu fātìi lítì a-pu nín̄ nee. A fōō Saayuul ŋaan dibeel, an pu ní ti-Dindaan fōō-dì a-ŋaan ki dūu tīī a-jipɔɔn Abisaloom. Kɔŋkɔnnee, a kɔ́ nnaabun, kun puee a sá unikpɔl ní.»

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Abisayi un na bi yíì Seeruyee bí ubɔti yii: «Ba pu ní dibɔkpil nee tòó ti-baa ubɔti mbusu míǹ? Yàntī ḿ cùú lēē u-yil.»

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Seeruya jipɔmbi Abisayi nì Joowaab, tíǹ ká-ni la? Kijapaai nee yaa bíi tòó-mi mbusuee, an yaa yíì ti-Dindaan di bí yii ú ŋá míǹ. Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí kpákáǹ-u?»

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí Abisayi nì u-kàliŋkpilib kɔkɔ yii: «Un sá m-jipɔɔn, man m-ba poon naŋuee nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-mi. Ŋma nín kàlaasì un sá Beenjameen naakookun nee. Ti-Dindaan di yaa pú-u nsan ú tɔ̄-mi mbusuee, yàntīmaan-u.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan làá kpèè m-falaau kí cúú mbusu un u tòó-mi díǹ nee kí kpántí dibiindi.»

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì u-yab nìn bí ki còom̄ ki cá. Simeeyii nìn bí ki kpàkaǹ dijool ki nóó-bi kaa dátiǹ Daafiidi. U nìn gbíntìi tòó mbusub, ki tòó ataŋkpee, ní ki kàfī ntam ki yàantí.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Boonee ubɔti nì u-yab dūu bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi. Bi nìn gīī ní ki kāl̀ niin ki ŋūŋfì. Abisaloom bāań ki kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Abisaloom nì Isirayeel yab dinikitikpaandi bāań ki kɔ́ Jeerusaleem. Ayiitoofeel nìn bí u-cee.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun uarkitiija Usayii un nìn bí Daafiidi cee ki sá u-saŋkiliuee bāań Abisaloom ceeyee ní u téeń yii: «Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn! Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn!»

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Ní Abisaloom bālifì-u yii: «A nín yú nì a-bɔɔ Daafiidi deedee puee deeee? Ba pu ní aa nóó-u?»

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Ní Usayii kíí-u yii: «Un ní ti-Dindaan nì Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ lēē ú nīn sá ubɔtee, úǹ ní man làá nóó kí nīn bí u-cee.

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Abisaloom bí Ayiitoofeel yii: «Kàl̄maan ni-ŋmaniŋma kí kpèèmaan min sá tí ŋée.»

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Niinee Ayiitoofeel bí Abisaloom yii: «Cùú dòon̄ nì a-baa nimpoobi bin u kāaǹ bí nīn kpèé dibeecindee. Niinee, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ làá béé yii a kɔ́ a-baa poon ki lēē baadakam, ní bin bí a-jandi púee ń ká kunyannyaau.»

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi gāā tanti bi nín bɔ̀b̄ dibeecindi puee yilpu ki tīī Abisaloom. Ní Abisaloom dōoǹ nì u-baa nimpoobi mpaampiin pu Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbilin.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Ayiitoofeel yaa nìn pée tīī isaŋkee, an nìn bí kii Unimbɔti di sòon̄ee ní. An puee, an yaa sá Daafiidaaa, Abisaloomaaa, Ayiitoofeel yaa nìn pée lī puee, míǹ ní bi nìn ŋáań.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Báà laakin ní u yaa bée, see tí bà-u ní kí kpátí kí bìin̄ u-pu kii dimalindi nín bìintí kitiŋ pu puee. Taa làá yàntī úǹ Daafiidi nì u-nib ubɔbɔ ń ŋmátí.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: M làá cùú túuǹ-u ŋyunti ŋun u gīī mpɔn kaa ti bí-uee, ní ḿ fàaǹ-u ní u-yab bin nóó-uee ń sāǹ kí wàatī-u. Niinee ubɔti yaa kíǹ u-babee ní ḿ kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: M yaa ŋá mimmee ní ḿ gíiǹní samaa kɔkɔ a-jandi pú. Di sá yii unil un a nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀ee yaa kpíìyee, binib kɔkɔ làá fàtīí gítiń a-jandi pú ní kí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.»

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Abisaloom nì Isirayeel yab kpilib kɔkɔ nìn ká yii nlandɔkɔee sá mmɔnti.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Ní Abisaloom bí yii: «Yíiḿmaan uarkitiija Usaayii tí pīlifì u mun nín cáá tin ki làá tùkù-tee.»

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Ní Usaayii nín cá Abisaloom cee, ní Abisaloom bí-u yii: «Kpèè Ayiitoofeel nín lī puee sèé. Tí ŋá u nín lī pueeyaaa, tí taa ŋá? Sii dàkafī yii ba?»

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Ní Usaayii kíí Abisaloom yii: «Min bí nee, Ayiitoofeel saŋkii kaa làá tɔ̄ ditundi.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Sii a-ba nyí a-baa nì u-naacimbi pu. Bi sá bibaatandambi ní. Bi fōō mbum kii digbiŋgbil din biki an cúú kupɔɔunee ní. A-baa sá ujanjal ní. Waa làá kíí kí dòon̄ u-yab cee kunyeeu nee.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Kɔnampu nee, u kɔ́ ki bál̀ mbòó ŋubɔn, àá laaba. Kujaau yaa kíĺ ní bi bíi kù ti-yabee, samaa làá gbìl̄ ní kí lì yii: <Bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Abisaloom janjaliibi.>

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Niinee, báà ujanjal yaa cáá dipɔbil kii gbikintee, see u-wunti ń yɔ̀tī. Kun puee Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nyí a-baa nín sá ujanjakpaanee, ní u-janjaliibi mun sá bibaatandambi.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Kpèè tin m cáá ki làá sāŋkì-see. Kpāfì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ a-cee kí yòon̄ Daani tiŋki ŋgan pú kí cáá sāā Beerseeba tiŋki ŋgiil pú. Bi máaǹ kí nīn wīikí kii tiŋku gbandi bulee, ní sii a-ba ń lìntī nyɔkɔpu ní cù kujaau.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: U yaa sáǹ ki kɔ́ kitiŋ kibanee, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ làá cáań iŋmii ní tí dáaĺ kitiŋee kí cáá tɔ̄ mbunni. Niinee baa dāa gíti kāntí kitaŋkpalii kitiŋ gbantin.»

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Abisaloom nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ lī yii: «Usaayii saŋkii ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ Ayiitoofeel yai.» Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn lēē ki yóoǹ yii Ayiitoofeel saŋkii ń ŋá fám, i mun di bàà ŋān̄. U nìn ŋá míǹ kí cáań mbusu kí tɔ̄ Abisaloom pu ní. Daafiidi dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Ní Usaayii tùkū bisaraaŋakpilib Saadooki nì Abiyataar yii: «Kpèè Ayiitoofeel nín sáŋkì Abisaloom nì Isirayeel kpilib puee, nì ma mun nín sáŋkì-bi puee.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, tɔ̄maan bí tùkù Daafiidi malaa yii ú taa dòon̄ Jɔɔdan tantakalin. U máaǹ kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, an yaa kaa sá míǹ, Abisaloom làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí u nì u-yab.»

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Joonatan nì Ayiimaasi nìn yú Eeni-Roogeel ki cí. Usapɔɔn ubɔ nìn cāabìń tibɔti tin bi làá dūú nàatī ubɔti Daafiidee. Di sá yii bíǹ kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ kitiŋin bí ká-bi.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Ama kinaacimpɔmbiki kiba nìn ká-bi ní ki cūtìi tùkū Abisaloom. Ní binib bilee búntì malaa malaa ki bàn̄ Bawuriim tiŋkin ki kɔ́ uninja ubɔ pu. U nìn cáá lɔkɔ u-cindi, ní bi kɔ́ lɔkɔee poon.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Kudiidaan nimpuu nìn dū tanti ki bīiǹ lɔkɔee pu ki dū asubil ki díntì, bí taa béé yii tiba bí niin.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ní bin Abisaloom túnnée bāań ki kɔ́ unimpuee dumpu ki bālifì-u yii: «Ayiimaasi nì Joonatan bí la?» Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Bi dūtì kibùmbiki ki búntì.» Ní bi cūtìi nyàab̄-bi kaa ká-bi, ní ki fātìi nín gítí Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Bi búntèe ní Yoonatan nì Ayiimaasi nyáń lɔkɔn ki cūtìi tùkū Daafiidi yii: «Yīkìmaan kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu malaa, di sá yii Ayiitoofeel nín tīī isaŋkee, bi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee dee.»

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Dicilpu niinee ní Daafiidi nì u-yab kíĺ ki bíi dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. Kutaa tin lì yii kù wúntée, bi-kɔkɔ dūtì ki dóò, báà uniseen kaa kíǹ.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ayiitoofeel nín ká yii baa dū u-saŋkii ki túń ditundee, ní u dū dimaŋgakal ki páaǹ u-maŋki pu ki jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ ki nín kùǹ u-tiŋkin. U bàn̄ee ki tīī u-dicaŋkun yab marab, ní ki lúntì u-ba ŋŋmii ki kpíì. Bi nìn síb́-u u-baa kaakulin. Daafiidi bí Maanayiim

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn dūu bàn̄ Maanayiim. Ŋyunti gbantee, Abisaloom nì Isirayeel yab janjaliibi kɔkɔ nìn bíi dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Abisaloom nìn lēē Amasaa ki dū-u ki kpántì bijanjaliibi kpiliu ú fōō Joowaab yil. Amasaa gbanti baa nìn sá uisirayeelja ní bi yíì-u Yeeteer. U nìn cáá Naaki bisal Abiigal, Seeruya naal, Joowaab na.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Abisaloom nì Isirayeel yab nìn gāā bi-janjanaapaal Galaadi tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nín bāań Maanayiim tiŋkinee, Naasi jipɔɔn Soobii un nyánní Amɔn yab tiŋyil Raabee nìn dɔ́miń ki kútì u-pu. Bin nìn nóó-uee di sá Amiyeel jipɔɔn Makiir un nyánní Loo-Deebaar tiŋkinee nì ugalaadija Baarsilaayi un nyánní Roogeeliim tiŋkinee.

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: nì tisiil nì nnaabiim nì inaa nì ipii waagaasiibi ki cáań ki tīī Daafiidi nì u-yab bin nìn nóó-uee bí jī. Di sá bi nìn lī bi-neen yii: «Kɔnampu, digìńdi nì ŋkùm nì nnyinnyoo bàn̄ binib nee kuteeun.»

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: U nìn cúú ajanjakitee ki yākatì mita pu, ki dū diba ki ŋúbiǹ Joowaab un na bi yíì Seeruyee, ní ki dū diba mun ki ŋúbiǹ Joowaab nabiki Abisayi, ní ki dū din kíǹee ki ŋúbiǹ ugaatija Itaayii. U nìn tùkū bijanjaliibi yii: «Ma mun làá nóó-ni tí cù kujaau.»

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Ama ní bijanjaliibi kíí-u yii: «Kpataaa, a kpá kí nóó-ti! Di sá yii bi yaa tāā ki bíikì ti-pu ní ti bíi sáńee, an kaa làá nīn ká ti-nannanliibi.
