Báà bi yaa kūū timbi dijandi, an kaa làá nīn ká-bi. Ama siiyee, a jítiǹ timbi janjaliibi kutukub saalaa pu. An puee an sɔ́ sii ń gbíntí kitiŋin ní an yaa píĺ ki pɔ́ɔkèe, á jòoń-ti.»

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Daafiidi janjaliibi ubɔ nìn ká-u ní ki cūtìi tùkū Joowaab yii: «M ká Abisaloom lúń busubu bubɔ pu.»

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Kujaau nìn yàl̄ ki gbí kitiŋ gbanti jaŋŋi kɔkɔn. Binib bin nìn kpíì kubambaŋŋunee nìn jítiǹ binib bin bi nìn kūū nì ntàataajimuee. Joowaab kūū Abisaloom

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Bi pée bíi jáà ki sāā ŋyunti ŋubɔee Abisaloom dūu túuǹ Daafiidi janjaliibi. U nìn kā umamboon pu ní umamboon bàà sáń kí gúutí asupan taapuee, ní u-yil fákáǹ asupan kansikin, ní umamboon gúutì taapu ki búntì. Abisaloom nìn gbíntì niin ki lúń.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab bí-u yii: «A ká-uaa! Ba pu ní aa kūū-u niin niin? M bàà làá pɔ̄-si animbil jitɔmbi saalaa nì dambala.»

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Báà m yaa ŋá kii maa nyí ki kūū-uaaa, tiba kaa bí ubɔti kaa nyí. U làá dāá béé yii m mɔ́ntí, ní sii dāa yú kaa làá mɔ̄tì m-pu.»

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab bí-u yii: «Maa làá kúntíǹ-si kí bīil̀ ŋyunti!» Ní u yōoǹ ikpaa ita ki búntì. U bàn̄ee Abisaloom lúń busubu pu ki dáá wāĺ ní u dū ikpaayee ki sāā u-pɔbil.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Ní ajanjapɔmbil saalaa ŋin nìn tūntí Joowaab janjawantee māntìi tú Abisaloom ní ki púntì-u.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joowaab búń ŋyin bí gbèen̄ kujaau. Ní Daafiidi janjaliibi gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi jì Abisaloom janjaliibi.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yōoǹ Abisaloom ki dūu tɔ́ kubookpaaŋŋu kubɔn kubambaŋŋun niin, ní ki tōō ataŋkpee ki nyīkiǹ u-pu ní an dūu kpántì ditaŋkpakpukul. Ŋyunti gbantee, Abisaloom janjaliibi sáǹ báà ŋma nín kùǹ u-dumpu.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Abisaloom dáá bée, u nìn dū ditaŋkpal diba ki cóoǹ ubɔti tantakalin. U nìn lī yii: «Maa cáá jipɔɔn bí nīn téetí m-pu.» An pu ní u dū úǹ u-ba yindi ki pú ditaŋkpalee. Bi gbíntìi yíì-dì nì díǹ yii: «Abisaloom taŋkpal.» Daafiidi gbìl̄ Abisaloom kúm pu

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Saadooki jipɔɔn Ayiimaasi bí Joowaab yii: «Yàntī ḿ sāǹ kí cùú tùkù ubɔti yii ti-Dindaan pɔ̀n̄-u ki fīī-u ki nyántì binannanliibi ŋaan.»

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab bí-u yii: «Aayee, si di kaa làá nīn sá un làá sòoǹ dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi bɔti díǹee. A dāa cáǹ-u dalba dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi, ama díǹ nee, taa cù, kun puee ubɔti jipɔɔn di kpíì.»

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab bí ueetiiyoopiija ubɔ yii: «Sii, nín̄ cá kí tùkù ubɔti tin a kée!» Ní u dɔ́miń ki gbāaǹ Joowaab nimbiin ní ki yíkìi sáǹ ki nín cá.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Ní Saadooki jipɔɔn Ayiimaasi gíti tí bí Joowaab yii: «Báà tin yaa pée bāań-mee, míǹ dee. M làá jà ueetiiyoopiija nee boon ní.» Ní Joowaab bí-u yii: «M-bɔɔ, ba pu ní a là kí jà u-boon ní? Tibɔti tin bí yéèyee juti kaa cáá ipaati.»

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ní Ayiimaasi kíí Joowaab yii: «An kaa cáá tiba, m làá cù.» Ní Joowaab bí-u yii: «Too, nín̄ cá.» Ní u dūu dī Jɔɔdan tantakalin saŋŋu ki sáǹ ki jítì ueetiiyoopiija pu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn kā mmɔŋki pú punyɔkɔki nì poon pú yaka kansikin. Ucɔŋkil nìn tɔ́kɔ́ bi nín bɔ̀b̄ kipunyɔkɔ yilpu puee digundi pu ki cɔ́ŋkí. Kpalaayee ní u ká ubɔ páaǹní ndan ki sánní u-baba.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Ní ucɔŋkilee téeń ki tùkū ubɔti yii ubɔ dòoń. Ní ubɔti bí yii: «U yaa nóoń u-babee, mimmee u cāabìń dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi dee.» Ŋyunti ŋun kijapaayee tóobińee,

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: ní ucɔŋkilee tí ká uninja ubɔ mun sánní ki dòoń ní u téeń ki tùkū upunyɔɔciitil yii: «Kpèè, ubɔ di dòoń ki sánní u-babee.» Ní ubɔti bí yii: «U mun cāabìń dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi ní.»

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Ucɔŋkilee lī yii: «Unipeekaa nín sáń puee yāntì m béè yii an sá Saadooki jipɔɔn Ayiimaasi.» Ní ubɔti bí yii: «U sá unaacimpɔmmɔnti ní. U cāabìń dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi ní.»

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ayiimaasi bāańee ní ki téeń ki bí ubɔti yii: «Tikɔkɔ pée cōom̀ ki ŋān̄ ní.» Ní u gbāaǹ ubɔti nimbiin ní ki bí yii: «Ti-baa, ti jáam̀ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu un dū bin yíkìi jáà nì see ki ŋá a-ŋaanee.»

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «M-naacimpɔɔŋwu Abisaloom bí mana?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «Ŋyunti ŋun Joowaab dū man nì a-tɔntɔnliu ubɔ mun ki túnní a-ceeyee, ní m dáań ki ká yii binib sáń lìbiti libiti, ama maa nín béè tin di yaa ŋée ní.»

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Sii kàkatī kí yūĺ ŋkpaanceeti yéè.» Ní u kākatì ki cūtìi yúl̀ ŋkpaanceeti.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Dicilpu kpalaa niin ní ueetiiyoopiija mun dūu bāań ní ki bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa, dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi ní m cáań-si, di sá yii ti-Dindaan pɔ̀n̄-si díǹ ki fīī-si ki nyántì a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ŋaan.»

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «M-naacimpɔɔŋwu Abisaloom bí mana?» Ní ueetiiyoopiija kíí-u yii: «Tin jítì Abisaloom puee, tíǹ tibaantiil ń jītí a-nannanliibi nì bin kaa là a-bɔtee pu.»

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔ cūtìi tùkū Joowaab yii: «Daafiidi bí ki sūǹ ki yáliŋkí Abisaloom pu.»

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, dijajil nìn dūu kpántì kunimbaau ki tīī bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ. Di sá bi mun nìn gbìl̄ yii ubɔti jipɔɔn kúm nìn kɔ́-u tikpil.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Bijanjaliibi nìn nɔ̄ntì ní ki kɔ́ kitiŋin. Bi nìn ŋá kii bijanjaliibi bin cūtì kujaau bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi bi fātìi gítìń nì icooyee ní.

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn dū ŋŋaabu ki bīiǹ u-nimbiin ní ki tátí mpɔn yii: «M-jipɔɔn Abisaloom! Abisaloom, m-jipɔɔn, m-jipɔɔn!»

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Joowaab kɔ́ ubɔti cee kudiin ki bí-u yii: «A bíi kɔ̄ntí a-janjaliibi bin fīī si nì a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib nì a-nimpukpilib nì a-nimpuwaamu kɔkɔ ki líí díǹ nee icoo dee.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Di sá yii a néeń bin ná-see, ní ki ná bin néeń-see. A dàkā díǹ yii a-janjakpilib nì binib bin kɔkɔ tíkí-see kaa sá tiba a-cee dee. Díǹ nee, m béè yii timbi di yaa bàà kpíì ní Abisaloom bí dimaŋfalin nee, an bàà ŋān̄ a-cee ní.

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: An puee cúú a-ba kí nyā kí tīī a-janjaliibi kunyannyaau nyɔɔbundi. M pūtì ti-Dindaan yii a yaa kaa ŋá míǹ, aa ti làá ká báà uniseen kunyeeu nee a-cee. Doooo a-naacimpɔntin ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, a láá pée ká nnaabu ŋubɔ kii ŋunee juti.»

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Abisaloom un ti nìn lēē ki kāaǹ dibeelee kpíì kujaaun. Ti gíti kā ki cí ba kí gíiǹní ubɔti Daafiidi ní?»

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi úǹ nìn tú bí tùkù bisaraaŋaliibi Saadooki nì Abiyataar yii: «Cùú sòoǹ nì Juuda yab kpilib yii: <Ubɔti nyí Isirayeel yab landɔkɔŋu. Ní nīn sá bipeekaabi kí gíiǹní ubɔti u-dumpu.

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Nimbi di sá ubɔti nabiyaamu kiŋkiŋ ki sá fatikubaanti. Ní nīn sá bipeekaabi kí gíiǹní ubɔti u-dumpu.>

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ní tùkù Amasaa yii: <Sii di kaa sá man nabiki kiŋkiŋaaa? Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ m-tafal kí gíti dáaĺ m-tafal m yaa kaa yāntì a kpántì ujanjakpil ki fōō Joowaab yil.»

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Niinee ubɔti yíkìi kíĺ nsan ki nín gítí, ki tin bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi. Daafiidi dū Simeeyii bɔkpil ki pú-u Juuda yab kɔkɔ cūtì Giilgaal kí tūŋkì ubɔti kí cáá-u kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: U nìn bí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, taa dū m-yìntitam kí ŋá tibɔti! Á taa téetí ikpiti in man a-tɔntɔnliu nìn ŋá-si ŋwiin ŋun a nìn nyēē Jeerusaleemee pu! Ubɔti, á taa pée díkí m-pu.

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: U nì Beenjameen naakookun yab binib kutuku di nìn nóó. Siiba un sá Saayuul tɔntɔnliuee nì u-jipɔmbi saalku, nì u-tɔntɔnliibi mmuŋku nìn kútì bi-pu. Bi nìn bíi ŋáań malaa malaa kí bà Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí tūŋkì ubɔti. Bi máaǹ kí nīn bí niin

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: kí ká buŋalimbu bun làá yòon̄ ubɔti nì u-dicaŋku kí dùtēe, ní kí ŋá min u lèe. Simeeyii nìn dɔ́miń ki lítì ubɔti nimbiin ŋyunti ŋun u nìn bíi bɔ́ntí kí dùtēe.

english_verse: But Abishai shouted, “You should be killed for cursing the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Ti-baa, man m-ba béè yii m ŋá-si ikpiti. Ama díǹ nee, sii a-ba ká yii m sá unipeekaa Jooseefi naakookun ki dɔ́miń ki túŋkì-si.»

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Abisayi un na bi yíì Seeruyee fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki lī yii: «Simeeyii tɔ́ un ti-Dindaan lēē ki kāaǹ dibeelee mbusu. Tibɔti tin u ŋá nee kaa máaǹ bí kpɔ̀-uaaa?»

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: Saayuul naantiiu Meefiibooseeti mun nìn cūtìi túŋkì ubɔti Daafiidi. Kí yòon̄ daliŋkin ubɔti nyáń Jeerusaleem ki dāa sāā ŋwiin ŋun u fātìi gítìń nì ŋgbansɔŋfee, Meefiibooseeti kaa fíntì u-taaŋi, kaa kōol̀ u-nyimpul, kaa fíntì u-wampeeŋkaati mun.

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: U nín bàn̄ ubɔti nimbiinee ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Ba ŋá ní aa nìn nóó-mi ti yíkì ní?»

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, m-tɔntɔnliu di kíil̀-mi. Di sá m nìn lī m-neen yii: <M nín kaa ŋūǹ kí còom̀ee, m làá dū digakal kí páań m-mansaliiki pu kí kàl̄ kí nīn nóó ubɔti.>

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Ama ní m-tɔntɔnliu cūtì a-cee ki kúŋfì m-boon. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ti-baa ubɔti sá kii Unimbɔti tuuŋŋuee ní. Ŋá min ŋān̄ a-ceeyee.

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «A sòon̄ tikpil! M lēē yii sii nì Siiba ń yàkatī Saayuul kpaatanti.»

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Ní Meefiibooseeti bí yii: «Siiba ŋūǹ kí yòon̄ tikpaatan kɔkɔ! Tin páb́ee di sá ubɔti nín fātìi gítìń u-dumpu nì ŋgbansɔŋfee.» Daafiidi pàn̄ Barsilayii tipaal

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Barsilayii nìn sá unil un púĺ tikpilee. U nìn cáá abin imuŋku inaa. Úǹ di nìn ŋúb́ ubɔti Daafiidi ŋyunti ŋun u nìn bí Maanayiim tiŋkinee, di sá yii u nìn sá ugaaja.

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Ubɔti bí-u yii: «Barsilayii, nóó-mi tí cù Jeerusaleem m-cee, m làá kpèè-si.»

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Tin m ŋūǹ kí ŋée di sá ḿ pée céeǹ-si tí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. Ba ní m ŋá gba ní sii ubɔti làá pà-mi tipaal ní?

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Yàntī man a-tɔntɔnliu ń gítí m-tiŋkin. Niin ní m làá kpú kí nīn pìlīǹ m-baa nì m-na kaakul. Ama kpèè m-jipɔɔn Kimaam sèé. Úǹ ŋūǹ kí céeǹ-si. A ŋūǹ kí ŋá min fáatì a-pɔbilee kí tīī-u.»

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «An ŋān̄, Kimaam ń céeǹ-mi. Min a lèe, míǹ ní m làá ŋá kí tīī-u. Tin kɔkɔ a yaa là ní ki mēē-mee, m làá tīī-si kudɔŋu.»

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Binib kɔkɔ nìn dūtì Jɔɔdan, ní ubɔti u-ba mun dūtì. Ubɔti nìn cūtìi kpàl̄ Barsilayii, ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ u-pu, ní u fātìi nín gítí u-dumpu.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti nìkī u-saŋŋu ki nín cá Giilgaal ní Kimaam nóó-u. Juuda yab nì Isirayeel yab jaaku Juuda yab kɔkɔ nì Isirayeel yab dijandi nìn céeǹ ubɔti ki cáá-u ki dūtì mbun.

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Niinee Isirayeel yab dɔ́miń ki ká ubɔti ki bālifì-u yii: «Ba pu ní ti-nabiyaamu Juuda yab dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ si nì a-dicaŋku yab ki cáa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, ama ní a-janjaliibi bí a-cee?»

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ní Juuda yab kɔkɔ kíí-bi yii: «Kun pu ti ŋá mimmee di sá yii timbi nì ubɔti di pēē. Ba pu ní an bɔti kɔ́ǹ-ni diŋuul ní? Ba ní ubɔti tīī-ti ti jíń ní? Ba ní u pú-ti?»

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Unifan ubɔ nìn bí niin bi yíì-u Seeba. U nìn sá Beenjameen naakookun ní bi yíì u-baa Biikirii. Kijapaayee nìn búń ŋyin ki lī yii: «Tiba kaa bí ti nì Daafiidi kansikin! Mpèé ŋubɔ kaa bí ti nì Jeesee jipɔɔn nee kansikin! Isirayeel yab, báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-dumpu.»

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Niinee Isirayeel yab yíkìi dū Daafiidi ki fá ní ki kíǹ ki nóó Seeba. Ama Juuda yab nìn gbíntì ki bí Daafiidi cee. Bi nìn céeǹní-u doooo Jɔɔdan áli Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Daafiidi bàn̄ ki kɔ́ u-beecindin Jeerusaleem. U nìn yíiń u-nimpuwaamu saalaa mun u nìn dūu kāaǹ bí nīn kpèé dibeecindee ki cáá-mu ki kɔ́ǹ kudii kubɔn bi cí-bi. U nìn tìì-bi tin kɔkɔ pée máaǹee, ama waa nìn gíti dɔ̀ bi-cee. Bi nìn pīī míǹ ní ki dāa sāā bi-kúm dal. Bi nìn bí kii bikpiipoobee, ama ní bi-cal kaa kpíì. Joowaab sāā ki kūū Amasaa

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Ubɔti bí Amasaa yii: «Á kpāfì Juuda janjaliibi kɔkɔ. M tīī-si iwiin ita a nì bi ń dāan̄ m-cee doo.»

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Amasaa búntì kí ŋá kii ubɔti nín bí yii ú ŋá puee, ama ní ki jítì iwiin in ubɔti yóoǹ-uee pu.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí Abisayi yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, Biikirii jipɔɔn Seeba làá kɔ́ǹ-ti digìńdi kí jītíǹ Abisaloom. Yòon̄ bijanjaliibi bin cí-mee kí jà Seeba boon, ú taa sāǹ kí kɔ́ ntimu mun poon bi máń digundi ki māntìi túee kí ŋmátí.»

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab janjaliibi nì Keereeti yab nì Peeleeti yab, nì bibaatandambi kɔkɔ nyáń ki páaǹ Abisayi boon kí jà Biikirii jipɔɔn Seeba boon.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ ki yú ditaŋkpakpaandi din bí Gabawɔn caŋinee, ní Amasaa bāań bi-cee. Joowaab nìn yú ki pēē u-janjawanti ki gbìn̄ gbaja kitàataajiki fúuń kijitooun ki lúń. Ŋyunti ŋun Joowaab bíi sútíi pìl̀-uee ní u-tàataajiki nyáń ki lítì.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab jáam̀ Amasaa yii: «M-nabiki, a pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋanaaa?» Ní u dū u-ŋaŋgiil ki cúú Amasaa nyimpul ki kpàl̄-u.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Amasaa kaa nìn gíiǹ u-landɔkɔŋu kitàataajiki kin nìn kā Joowaab ŋaŋganee pu. Joowaab nìn dū kitàataajikee ki sāā Amasaa pool ní ina nyáń ki dɔ̄ kitiŋ ní u kpíì. Waa nìn gíti kútì-u nliliitiim. Joowaab yāntì bi kūū Seeba Míǹ boonee ní Joowaab nì u-nabiki Abisayi nìkī ki bíi jì Biikirii jipɔɔn Seeba boon.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Joowaab janjaliu ubɔ nìn kā ki kɔ́ĺ utaŋkpiil Amasaa ki lì yii: «Un kamaa bí Joowaab nì Daafiidi jandee ń páań Joowaab boon.»

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Amasaa nìn dōoǹ ki bíntì u-fatikuu poon nsan kansikin. Ujanjalee nìn ká yii binib dòoń ki yūlifí niin. Niinee ní u fùn̄ dinikpilee ki cáa bíl̀ kusaau kubɔn, ní ki dū sata ki bīiǹ di-pu.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: U nín ŋá mimmee ní binib kíǹ ki dòoń ki jītí kaa ti yūlifí, ki nóó Joowaab ki jì Biikirii jipɔɔn Seeba boon.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Joowaab nìn yìin̄ Isirayeel naakɔti timmu kɔkɔn ki tin bàn̄ Abeel-Beeti-Maaka. Beerii yab kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì ki nóó-u.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi nìn māntìi tú Abeel-Beeti-Maaka tiŋki kin poon Seeba nìn bée. Bi nìn fāā ntam ki kpúkuǹ ki tin sāā digundi, ní bijanjaliibi kíĺ ki bíi gbì ki tíkití digundee nyeel dí lítí.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Unimpu ubɔ nìn bí kitiŋ gbanti poon ki cáá iciin ní ki téeń yii: «Pīlifìmaan, pīlifìmaan. Tùkùmaan Joowaab yii ú sútiń kí pìlīń-mi ḿ sòoǹ nì u tiba.»

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab sútìi pìl̄-u ní u bālifì-u yii: «Sii di sá Joowaabaaa?» Ní Joowaab kíí-u yii: «Iiin, an sá man.» Ní unimpuee bí-u yii: «Á pīlifì tibɔti tin man a-tɔntɔnliu làá sòoǹ nì see.» Ní Joowaab bí-u yii: «M pílifí.»

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Ní u bí yii: «Bi lì dilìmbil diba yii: <Bàlifì isaŋki Abeel-Beeti-Maaka yab cee, a-bɔti kɔkɔ làá ŋāŋkì.>

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Ti sá ŋgbansɔŋfi nib ní ki yú deedee Isirayeel tiŋkin. Ní sii dɔ́miń kí kúntí kitiŋ kin sá Isirayeel tiŋkpaammu kansikin kibee! Ba pu ní a nyàab̀ kí kúntí tiwan tin ti-Dindaan yèe?»

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab bí yii: «Kpataaa, maa pée cáá nlandɔkɔ kí nàan̄ àá kí kúntí tiba nì tiba!

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Kaa sá kitiŋ ní m là kí kúntí, ama unil ubɔ ní m nyàab̀. U sá Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu timmu kiban, bi yíì-u Seeba, Biikirii jipɔɔn. U yíkì ki bíi jáà nì ubɔti Daafiidi. Ní nyāntímaan úǹ baba kí tīī-mi ní ḿ yàntī ni-tiŋki.» Ní unimpuee bí yii: «An ŋān̄, ti làá tìl̄ u-yil kí dūú lúkuń-si digundi boon.»

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Unimpuee nín gítí u-yab cee ki tīī-bi isaŋkimɔnti. Ní bi tīl̀ Seeba yil ki dūu lúkuń Joowaab. Ní u búń ŋyin ní bi yāntì kitiŋee, ní báà ŋma nín kùǹ u-dumpu. Joowaab úǹ nìn nín gítí Jeerusaleem ubɔti cee. Daafiidi kàliŋkpilib

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Joowaab di nìn sá Isirayeel yab janjaliibi kɔkɔ kpiliu. Yooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenaya di nìn sá Keereeti nì Peeleeti yab kpiliu.

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Adooram di nìn kpòotī ayumbutuun ŋin ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee, Joosafaati jipɔɔn Ayiiluudi di nìn sá ubɔti soobaabuu.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Seeba di nìn sá ugbaŋŋmal. Saadooki nì Abiyataar di nìn sá bisaraaŋakpilib.

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti yíiń Gabawɔn yab ki sòon̄ nì bi. Gabawɔn yab kaa nìn sá Isirayeel yab, ama bi sá Amɔɔr yab bin Isirayeel yab nìn kūū ki kíǹee ní. Isirayeel yab nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ-bi yii baa làá kpɔ̀-bi. Dineendi din Sayuul nìn cáá Isirayeel nì Juuda yab puee nìn yāntì u nyàab̄ kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi.

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: Daafiidi bālifì-bi yii: «Ni là ḿ ŋá ba kí tīī-ni ní? Ḿ ŋá mana kí ŋāŋkì tikpitil tin Saayuul ŋá-nee, án nín làá ŋá pu ní mèè kí bìin̄ ti-Dindaan nibul puee ní?»

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi bí ubɔti yii: «Saayuul nìn là kí kúntí-ti. U nìn bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ti báà ubɔ ń taa kíń Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn.

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: Bí cúú u-dicaŋku poon binib biluli kí tīī-ti ní tí cáá-bi kí cɔ̀b̄ ti-Dindaan nimbiin, Giibeeya tiŋkin. Niin ní Sayuul un ti-Dindaan nìn lēēyee nìn kóò.» Ní ubɔti kíí-bi yii: «M làá cáań an nibee kí tīī-ni.»

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Ama ubɔti nìn fīī Joonatan jipɔɔn Meefiibooseeti, Sayuul naantiiu. Daafiidi nìn pūtì ti-Dindaan ki pōoǹ u nì Joonatan bɔɔtiiku pu.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: U nìn dū-bi ki tīī Gabawɔn yab, ní bíǹ cáá-bi ki cɔ̀b̄ dijool pu ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Binib bilulee nìn kpíì dicilpu. Ŋwimpeepeekaa ŋun bi bōoǹ ki bíi cēē ɔɔjee ní bi nìn kūū-bi.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Aya bisal Riispa nìn dū kpɔsata un u nìn lōōyee ki dāntì ditaŋkpakpaandi pu, ní ki kā niin kí yòon̄ ŋyunti ŋun bi kíĺ ki bíi cēē ɔɔjee kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun utaa kpákatìńee. Ŋwiimpuee, u nìn jì inoon ń taa jī bi-nanti, ní kunyeeuee, u jì ipeel.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi yāntì bi yōoǹní Sayuul nì u-jipɔɔn Joonatan kpabiŋ Yaabeesi yab cee Galaadi tiŋkin. Di sá yii Fiiliistii yab nín nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Saayuul Giilboowa tiŋkinee, bi nìn cáá Saayuul nì Joonatan ki lúntì Beeti-Seeyan paaŋŋu pu, ní Yaabeesi yab cūtìi sākatìń bi-wunti.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Ní bi cáá bi-kpabiŋ nì Saayuul nì Joonatan yaŋ ki bíl̀ Saayuul baa Kiisi kaakulin, Seera timbiliikin, Beenjameen tiŋkin. Bi ŋá kii ubɔti nín tīī mara bí ŋá puee ki dóòyee ní Unimbɔti súń kitiŋ gbanti saai. Isirayeel nì Fiiliistii yab kɔndi (Kpèè

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Dikɔ̀ndi diba mun nìn tí nyáń Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab kansikin Gaati tiŋkin. Kujawɔkɔu kubɔ nìn bí ki sá Arafa dicaŋkun. Ku nìn cáá ŋŋambiyaamu muluu ŋŋal kamaa pu nì ntaŋambiyaamu muluu ditaal kamaa pu, mu-kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì mmuŋku nì munaa.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Kujaau kubɔ gíti nyáń Fiiliistii yab nì Isirayeel yab kansikin. Daafiidi nì u-janjaliibi nìn sīntì kí já nì Fiiliistii yab. Bi bí dikɔ̀ndi poonee ní Daafiidi gīī.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Iseebi-Beenoobi un sá Arafa naakookunee bíi pùlifī ki lì yii u làá kpɔ̀ Daafiidi. U nìn gbìn̄ kijipɔŋ ki ŋúb́ kikpaŋ. Kikpaŋee nyɔkɔpu nìn sá tasa kúti ní ki nyìm̀ kii kiiloobi bita nì ipaa.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Ama Abisayi un na bi yíì Seeruyee dɔ́miń ki jòoń ubɔti ní ki kūū ufiiliistiija. Niinee Daafiidi janjaliibi pūtì ki bí Daafiidi yii: «Aa ti làá pée nóó-ti tí cù dikɔ̀ndi, án nín làá ŋá pu ní Isirayeel walifiŋu ń taa kpúee.»

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: An yúntì boonee ní dikɔ̀ndi diba nyáń Fiiliistii yab nì Isirayeel yab kansikin Goobi tiŋkin. Niin ní Sibeekayii un sá Usa tiŋkinee kūū Saafi un sá Arafa dicaŋkunee.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Dikɔ̀ndi diba tí pōō Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab kansikin, Goobi tiŋkin. Min bí nee, Yaarii jipɔɔn Eelanan un sá Beetileem tiŋkinee kūū Gooliyaati ugaatija. U-kpaŋki dɔŋu nìn gbìfì kii tikúti tin bisataluliibi cōontí ki lù satabee ní.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: U nìn kpēē ki sɔ́kɔ́ Isirayeel yab. Ní Daafiidi maan Sama jipɔɔn Yiinatan kūū-u.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì u-janjaliibi nìn kūū Fiiliistii janjaliibi binaa gbanti. Bi nìn sá Arafa dicaŋkun, Gaati tiŋkin.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: U fōō-mi m-nannanliu un pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ŋaan, m-pulincɔntiibi bin pɔ̄ɔǹ-mee ŋaan.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Daafiidi dū anyɔɔbun nee ki gāā nlan ki nyɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan ŋyunti ŋun u nyántì-u u-nannanliibi kɔkɔ, cilinjee Saayuul ŋaanee.

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: An pu ní, m-Dindaan, m làá nyɔ̄ŋkì-si atimbun kansikin, ní kí gāā ilan kí pàkà a-yindi.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: U lī yii: Ti-Dindaan di sá man taŋkpanaakooku, úǹ di sá man guŋkpaandi lɔkɔl nì man fiiliu.

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: U sá man Nimbɔtiu ní ki sá ntaŋkpalɔkɔ ŋun poon m sáń ki kóòyee. Úǹ di sá man gbampɔɔl ní ki sá man jajil pɔŋŋu, ti-Dindaan di sá man balilaŋki. Úǹ ní m sáń ki kóò ní u fìil̄-mi tipɔmbɔti dambi ŋaan.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan! M kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ní u yāntì m jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ m-nannanliibi.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Ŋkúm kusakai nìn fìn̄-mi, dinàandi nyiŋgbeeŋŋu nìn yōoǹ-mi ki dóò.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Ditaŋkpiilin laaŋku nìn māntìi tú-mi, ní ŋkúm talinti píĺ ki dɔ̄ m-nimbiin.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: M kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan m-nimbinaamandi poon. M fáá mbiil m-Nimbɔtiu ń jòoń-mi. U gbìl̄ m-neen pu doooo u-diikun ní m-kuŋkuuntii kɔ́ u-tafalin.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Niinee ní kitiŋ fōō dijinjikil ki cīŋkì, ní ajoon nyeel cīŋkì. Di sá yii Unimbɔti gíí diŋuul.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Ŋŋminyiim nìn nyēē u-maŋfataabuŋyin, ní aŋmilimbil ŋin nàantée nì amɔsiŋkoon nyēē u-nyɔkɔn.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: Ní u cúú kutagbɔŋu ki cátì ní ki kpákatìń, ní ditagbandi din bɔ̀ǹee bí u-taaŋi taapu.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: U kāl̀ tiwannáaŋkaal tin cáá ifeenee pu ki ŋàan̄, ní ki dū kubuŋu ki kpántì ifeen ki kíǹ ki dàn̄.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: Dibɔmbɔndi ní u dūu bīiǹ u-ba pu ní atagban ŋin gbìfì nnyim gbí ŋi-poonee māntìi tú-u.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Ŋwalifi nìn bí u-nimbiin, ní atagban jītí ki sá ataanyiŋkumbil nì amɔsiŋkoon.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ní doooo yilpu kii ntaateenteenee, Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu yāntì bi gbìl̄ u-nyɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tāā ki bíikì u-nannanliibi pu, ní ki fōō bi-pu diŋuul, an pu ní tiŋku poon nyim fóotì, ní kitiŋ nyeel cúu bīitì ki dɔ̄.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kāl̀ doooo yilpu ki tāntì u-ŋal ki cúú-mi ki nyántì inyiŋfi taapu.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: M-nimbinaamandi dal ní bi dɔ́miń ki jáń nì mi, ama ti-Dindaan dɔ́miń ki tíkiǹ-mi.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: U nyántì-mi digìńdin ki tīī-mi dibatɔl. U fīī-mi, kun puee u néeń-mi.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di pàn̄-mi, kun puee m ŋá tin bí deedeeyee. U bīiǹ m-pu kun puee tikpitil tiba kaa táká m-ŋal.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: M nóó ti-Dindaan saŋŋu nì mbaamɔn, ní kaa fātì m-boon ki tīī m-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: M ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan marab kɔkɔ, kaa fātì m-kpaŋkpamboon ki tīī u-bɔkpaaŋi.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: Waa ká m-pu tiba kí wòoǹ-mi, ní m pɔ́ɔǹ m-ba kí taa ŋá ikpiti.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan pàn̄-mi, kun puee m ŋá tin bí deedeeyee, ní u nyí mun yii m-ŋalii kaa táká ikpiti.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, bin nóó-si nì dipɔbil dibee, a sí nì bi dipɔbil diba mun ní. Bin bí deedeeyee, a sí nì bi deedee ní.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: A ŋáań bin pɔbiliŋ pīiǹee tiŋan, ama ní ki dàkà bikpitiŋaliibi yii a nyíǹ-bi.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Di sá yii a fìil̄ dinibul din sīntiǹ di-ba taapuee, ama ní ki sìntīǹ bilambidambi taapu.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, sii di sá m-fitilau, sii di ŋmíntí-mi ní m-bɔmbɔndi ń wāŋkì.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Tin kɔkɔ Unimbɔti ŋáańee ŋān̄, ní unil ŋūǹ kí nīn máká u-nyɔɔbundi pu. U sá digbampɔɔl ní ki tīī bin kɔkɔ sáń ki kóò-uee.

english_verse: You alone are God! Only you are a mighty rock.
translation_verse: Ŋma di sá Unimbɔti, an yaa kaa sá ti-Dindaan? Ŋma di sá timbi taŋkpanaakooku, an yaa kaa sá ti-Nimbɔtiu?

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Úǹ di sá Unimbɔti un tìì-mi mpɔnee, ní ki cátí nsammɔnti ki tìì-mi m còom̄.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: U yàntī m-taaŋi yáb̀ m sáń kii ucaŋkpalimee, ní ki yàntī ḿ jɔ̄m̀ kí tɔ́kɔń ajoon pu tiba ń taa ŋá-mi.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: Waa bífí-mi bi nín jáà puee ŋmaniŋma, ama u yàntī ḿ ŋmā kí dáaĺ butɔbu bun bi dū tasa kúti ki píĺee.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a tìì-mi digbampɔɔl din fìil̄-mee, ní a-ŋaŋgiil tíkí-mi, ní a nín tútúǹ-mi puee yāntì m nyáń diyindi.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: Sii puee m ŋūǹ kí dàatī malaa malaa, ní maa tà ki pántí.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: M jì m-nannanliibi ní kí cúú-bi, m yaa kaa nāaǹ-bi maa fàtī m-boon.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: Ní ḿ pɔ̀fì pɔ̀fì-bi ní baa ti ŋūǹ kí yīkì, ní ki kíǹ ki dɔ̄ m-taaŋi taapu fìlfil.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: A tìì-mi mpɔn ḿ já kujaau, ní ki dù bin yíkíi jáà nì mee ki ŋáań m-taaŋi taapu.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: A yàntī m-nannanliibi sáń kukunsaŋu, ní ki nàantí bin ná-mee.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Bi kūuntí ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi, ní ubɔ kpá kí fīī-bi. Bi kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan gba, ama waa kíí-bi.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: M jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi ki nàn̄-bi dúsi dusi kii ŋkpɔŋkpɔm min kubuŋu yòontée, ki tà-bi ki ŋmàtifī kii nsanni kpatee.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: A fīī-mi ki nyántì anibul ŋin nib nìn yíkì ki jáà nì mee ŋaan, ní ki dū-mi ki ŋá atimbun yidaaŋwu. Anibul ŋin maa nìn nyée kpántì m-naacimbi ki tūǹ ditundi ki tìì-mi.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Bi-wunti kúù, ní bi nyēeń bi-balilaŋki tiwun jìkì.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí dimaŋfalin! Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan m-taŋkpanaakooku! Tí pàkàmaan Unimbɔti un di sá m-fiiliuee!

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti tútuǹ-mi m jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ m-nannanliibi, ní ki dū atimbun ki ŋá m-taaŋi taapu.

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: U fīī-mi ki nyántì m-nannanliibi ŋaan. Tiŋman u yāntì m jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ bin jáà nì mee, ní ki fīī-mi ki nyántì tipɔmbɔti dambi ŋaan.

english_verse: You give glorious victories to your chosen king. Your faithful love for David and for his descendants will never end.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti tìì u-bɔtiu ajajil ŋin sá akpaanee. U dàkà ubɔti un úǹ u-ba lēēyee nì Daafiidi nì u-naantiibi dineeŋkpaandi kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Fam dī m-pu ki sòon̄, u-nyɔɔbundi kā m-nyɔkɔn.

english_verse: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
translation_verse: Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu sòon̄, Isirayeel taŋkpanaakooku bí-mi yii: «Ubɔti un di ŋúb́ binib deedee, ki cáá Unimbɔti faaŋku ki kpòotī-bee

english_verse: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”
translation_verse: bí kii ntaafaawìiń nín nyēē pu ki wāĺ bɔ́iii kutaa kun pu atagban kpée ní. Utaa yaa nìn̄ boonee, ŋu-tuntuŋku yàntī kumɔsɔŋu nyēē.»

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Unimbɔti ŋá m-dicaŋku, di sá u pōoǹ-mi ipoon kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan, ní ki síiǹ marab bin làá nīn wúń ipoon gbanti puee. U tīī-mi dijajil ijaan kɔkɔ pu, ní ki ŋá tin kɔkɔ m lèe ki tīī-mi.

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Ama bin kɔkɔ kaa bí tibanee bí kii ikuŋkum in bi féeńee ní. Baa cútí-i mɔ̀b.

english_verse: but with a sharp spear and are burned on the spot. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: Un yaa là kí gbēē-iee, see udaan ń dū kikpaŋ àá ndɔ kí kùl̄-i kí tūū ŋŋmi dibɔbilin niin. Daafiidi baatandambi (Kpèè

english_verse: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: Ama Eelasaar nìn yúl̀ ki cíitì-bi, ki kūū Fiiliistii yab, áli u-ŋal dūu mɔ́ɔb́ ki nákáǹ dijigbandi. Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ká dijajikpaandi ŋwiin gbanti. Bijanjaliibi dāa fātìi gítìń Eelasaar ceeyee, an sá bí fūkul̀ anikpil wanti ní.

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: Áli gba u ká jilma ki jítiǹ bitee ní ki kpántì bi-kpiliu. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, waa kɔ́ bitee kitil poon.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: Daafiidi janjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee yiŋŋi sèé. Yooseeb-Baseebeeti uakimoonja nìn kútì bijanjakpilib bin nìn cí ubɔtee pu. Úǹ di nìn kūū binib alaataa anii kujabambaantiiu poon.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee Doodoo jipɔɔn Eelasaar di nìn pá. U-naanja nìn sá Ayooya tiŋkin ní. U nìn bí bibaatandambi bita bin nìn nóó Daafiidi bi cūtìi jáń nì Fiiliistii yab kujaau kubɔ poonee. Bíǹ nìn kpáfì kí já kujaau ní Isirayeel yab sáǹ.

english_verse: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
translation_verse: Ama Sama úǹ nìn gbíntì bukpaayee kansikin, ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi ki fōō-bu. Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan nìn dī ki tīī Isirayeel yab dijajikpaandi.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Kuceeu yuntiŋuee, bijanjakpilib bin cí ubɔtee bita nìn cūtìi ká Daafiidi Adulaam taŋkpalɔkɔlin. Di sá yii Fiiliistii janjakitil diba nìn cūtìi gāā bi-janjanaapaal Reefayiim tantakalin.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn bí laakin u sáǹ ki bál̀ee, ní Fiiliistii yab fōō Beetileem ki kā niin.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ní kpɔkɔsi ubɔ cúú Daafiidi ní u bí yii: «Ŋma di làá cùú cáań-mi lɔkɔ un bí Beetileem punyɔkɔki caŋinee nyim ḿ nyɔ̀ dee?»

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Niinee bijanjaliibi bitee kɔ́ Fiiliistii yab janjanaapaalin, ki lúnní nnyim lɔkɔ un dɔ̄ Beetileem punyɔkɔki caŋinee ki cáań ki tīī Daafiidi. Ama u nìn yíì kaa nyùn̄-mì. U nìn dū-mi ki fá ti-Dindaan un máaǹ-mee ní.

english_verse: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: Ní u bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń cúú-mi ḿ taa nyɔ̀ nnyim nee! Mi sá-mi kii binib bin kaa mɔ́tì bi-ba pu ki cūtìi nyàabìń-mèe fatikuu ní.» Ní u yíì kaa nyùn̄-mì. Bibaatandambi bitee nín nìn túń dituŋkpaandi diŋyee dee.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa, ukabiseelja jipɔɔn Beenayawuu nìn sá ubaatandaan ubɔ naantiiu ní. Úǹ di nìn kūū bibaatandambi bili Moowaab tiŋkin. Ŋwiin ŋubɔ ntaayim bíi lítí ní u kɔ́ dinyimbɔbilin ki kūū gbikinti nsɔnsɔm yuntiŋu gbantin. U nìn túń atuŋkpaan kujaaun.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: Úǹ di nìn tí kūū ueejipitija ubɔ. Kijapaayee nìn yáà unil. U nìn ŋúb́ kikpaŋ, ní úǹ ŋúb́ ndɔ ki nín cá u-cee, ki bàn̄ ki fōō u-kpaŋki ki gíiǹ ki sāā ki kūū-u.

english_verse: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
translation_verse: Áli gba u nìn ká jilma ki jítiǹ bibaatandambi mmuŋku nì saalaayee. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, waa kɔ́ bitee kitil poon. An puee Daafiidi yōoǹ-u u kíǹ ki cí úǹ ubɔti.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?” David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
translation_verse: Ní ki bālifì yii: «Ba pu ní sii ti-baa ubɔti dòoń man a-tɔntɔnliu cee ní?» Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «M dɔ́miń kí dā a-bileegbanaapaal kí mā m-Dindaan nsaraafan ní. Ti yaa ŋá mimmee, bìlbil kúm min bíi kù samaa nee làá gbèen̄.»

english_verse: They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon.
translation_verse: Bi kɔ́ Galaadi tiŋkin ní ki nín cá Itii yab tiŋkin Seedeesi. Bi nìkī ki nín cá Daani-Yaan tiŋkin nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-kèe. Míǹ boonee ní bi kàan̄ Siidɔn yab.

english_verse: So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti bí ujanjakpil Joowaab un bí u-ceeyee yii: «Á yìiǹ Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔn, kí yòon̄ Daani ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Beerseeba ŋgan pú kí kàaǹ binib kɔkɔ ḿ béé bi-wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm.»

english_verse: But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee ubɔti nín pée tīī Joowaab nì bijanjakpilib mara uŋyee, míǹ ní u pée ŋúb́. Niinee ní bíǹ kíĺ nsan kí cùú kàaǹ Isirayeel nib.

english_verse: They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, ní ki kíĺ ki bíi kàaǹ Arooweer tiŋkin yab nì kitiŋ kin bí ditantakalinee yab. Bi cōom̀ ki jítì Gaadi ki nìkī kí nīn cá Yaseer.

english_verse: After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them
translation_verse: Bi dū iŋmal iwa nì iwiin mmuŋku ní ki yìin̄ Isirayeel nì Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔn ki kàan̄ binib, ní ki fātìi gítìń Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Araafina kpēēyee ki ká Daafiidi nì u-kàliŋkpilib dòoń u-cee. Ní u nyáń ki túŋkì-bi ní ki tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Daafiidi nín ká ntuun bíi kù binib mimmee ní u bí ti-Dindaan yii: «Man di ŋá ikpiti, man di yīntì, m-nibul mun ŋá ba? An sá man nì m-dicaŋku tafal ní á dáaĺ.» Daafiidi máń ti-Dindaan nsaraafan (Kpèè

english_verse: After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Daafiidi nín kàan̄ binib míǹ ki dóòyee ní u-pɔbil bíi máfí. Ní u bí ti-Dindaan yii: «M ŋá ikpitikpaan. M-Dindaan, dūú pɔ̄-mi. M ŋá kii m sá uwaatee ní!»

english_verse: Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì Daafiidi fīntì kutaafaauee, ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Gaadi un sá Daafiidi saŋkiliuee yii:

english_verse: to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him: You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? Or will your enemies chase you and make you run from them for three months? Or will there be three days of horrible disease in your land? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God, who sent me.
translation_verse: Ní Gaadi cūtì Daafiidi cee ki dū tibɔtee ki tùkū-u, ní ki bí-u yii: «A là ŋkùm ń jēetí a-tiŋki pu abin alulaaa, a-nannanliibi ń sāǹ kí jà-si iŋmal itaaa, bìlbil kúm ń jēetí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu iwiin ita? Dàkafì kí tùkù-mi tin m làá tin tùkù un túnní-mee.»

english_verse: David was really frightened and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí Gaadi yii: «M bí kunimbaakpaaŋŋu poon ní... Ama an sɔ́ ḿ kɔ́ ti-Dindaan ŋaan ki jítiǹ ḿ kɔ́ unil ŋaan, di sá yii ti-Dindaan úǹ poon mɔ̄ ní.»

english_verse: So that morning, the Lord sent an angel to spread a horrible disease everywhere in Israel, from Dan to Beersheba. And before it was over,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ntuun bàà tāntì ŋu-ŋal ki túĺ Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí nàan̄-kèe, ní ti-Dindaan kpántì u-landɔkɔŋu ní ki bí ntuun ŋun bíi kù binibee yii: «An ŋmāntèe, gbèen̄ee.» Ŋyunti gbantee ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nìn yú ujeebusja Araafina bileegbanaapaal caŋin.

english_verse: Araunah said, “Take whatever you want and offer your sacrifice. Here are some oxen for the sacrifice. You can use the threshing-boards and the wooden yokes for the fire.
translation_verse: Ní Araafina bí Daafiidi yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti ń yòon̄ tin kɔkɔ fáatì-uee kí dūú ŋá saraabi. Kpèè inaa sèé á dūú ŋá saraawɔkaa. Tɔrɔku dɔkpalkaai mun sèé á dūú kpāā ŋŋmi kí wà saraabi.

english_verse: Take them—they're yours! I hope the Lord your God will be pleased with you.”
translation_verse: M dū tikɔkɔ ki tīī-si! Ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ń fōō a-saraabi.»

english_verse: But David answered, “No! I have to pay you what they're worth. I can't offer the Lord my God a sacrifice that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing place and the oxen for
translation_verse: Ama ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Aayee, m làá dā a-bileegbanaapaal ní kí pà-si kunimbiŋmiiu nín sá puee. Maa là kí dū faalaa wanti kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī m-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu.» Ní Daafiidi pàn̄-u animbil jitɔmbi imuŋku ili nì saalaa dibileegbanaapaal nì inaa pu.

english_verse: Then he built an altar for the Lord. He offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. The Lord answered the prayers of the people, and no one else died from the terrible disease.
translation_verse: Niin ní Daafiidi máń ti-Dindaan nsaraafan, ní ki ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan súń kitiŋee saai, ní bìlbil kúm min jéetì Isirayeel tiŋki puee gbēeǹ.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we will look for a young woman to take care of you. She can lie down beside you and keep you warm.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní u-tɔntɔnliibi bí-u yii: «Ti làá nyàab̀ kisapɔmbiki kin kaa nyí uninjee kí tīī ti-baa ubɔti. Kisapɔmbikee làá nīn bí ubɔti cee ki tūǹ ditundi ki tìì-u, ki kpèé-u, ní kí nīn dɔ̀ ki kɔ́l̀-u án nīn tùm̀ u-pu.»

english_verse: They looked everywhere in Israel until they found a very beautiful young woman named Abishag, who lived in the town of Shunem. They brought her to David, and she took care of him. But David did not have sex with her. Adonijah Tries To Become King
translation_verse: Kisapɔmbikee nìn ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu an kaa cáá bí lì. Kì nìn bí ubɔti cee ki tūǹ ditundi ki tìì-u ki kpèé-u. Ama ubɔti kaa nìn béè-u.

english_verse: Adonijah was the son of David and Haggith. He was Absalom's younger brother and was very handsome. One day, Adonijah started bragging, “I'm going to make myself king!” So he got some chariots and horses, and he hired
translation_verse: U nín bée, dalba dalba u-baa kaa wòon̄-u ki lī yii: «Ba pu ní a ŋáań míǹ?» Kí kūtì muee, u nìn ŋān̄ unaacimpɔɔn ní úǹ di nìn sá un pá Abisaloom boon u-na maaliŋu poonee.

english_verse: Adonijah met with Joab the son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest and asked them if they would help him become king. Both of them agreed to help.
translation_verse: Adooniyasi nìn sòon̄ nì ujanjakpil Joowaab, Seeruya jipɔɔn nì usaraaŋakpil Abiyataar, ní bíǹ kíí ki kútì u-pu.

english_verse: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's bodyguards all refused.
translation_verse: Ama usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nì Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan nì Simeeyii nì Reeyii nì Daafiidi baatandambi kaa nìn kíí ki kútì Adooniyasi pu. Naatan nì Batiseeba páaǹ Saloomɔn boon

english_verse: Adonijah invited his brothers and David's officials from Judah to go with him to Crawling Rock near Rogel Spring, where he sacrificed some sheep, cattle, and fat calves.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Adooniyasi kūū ipii nì inajaa nì anabil ŋin cáá ŋkpamee ki ŋá saraa <Ditaŋkpal din ŋàtī> ki bí ki pìl̄ Eeni-Roogeelee caŋin. U nìn yíiń ubɔti jipɔmbi u-naalib kɔkɔ nì Juuda nikpaambi bin bí ubɔti tundinee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: But he did not invite Nathan, Benaiah, David's bodyguards, or his own brother Solomon.
translation_verse: Ama waa nìn yíiń Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan nì Beenayawuu nì ubɔti baatandambi nì u-naal Saloomɔn.

english_verse: When Nathan heard what had happened, he asked Bathsheba, Solomon's mother: Have you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has made himself king? But David doesn't know a thing about it.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Naatan cūtìi ká Saloomɔn na Baatiseeba ki bí-u yii: «Sii kaa gbìl̄ yii Agiiti jipɔɔn Adooniyasi kpántì ubɔti ní ti-baa Daafiidi kaa kpáàa nyáaa?

english_verse: You and your son Solomon will be killed, unless you do what I tell you.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, isaŋki in m cáá kí tīī-see sɔ̀, fīī a-ba kí kpáaǹ a-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn mun.

english_verse: While you are still talking to David, I'll come in and tell him that everything you said is true.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní a dáá bí ubɔti cee ki bíi sòoǹ nì uee ní man m-ba ḿ kɔ́nní kí nyīī tin a bíi sòoǹee pu ŋŋal.»

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was in his bedroom where Abishag was taking care of him because he was so old. Bathsheba went in
translation_verse: Niinee, Baatiseeba nín kóò ubɔti cee u-diikun. Ubɔti nìn púĺ tikpil ní kisuneembiki Abiisaagi bí u-cee ki kpèé-u.

english_verse: and bowed down. “What can I do for you?” David asked.
translation_verse: Baatiseeba nìn tātìi gbāaǹ ubɔti nimbiin ní úǹ bālifì-u yii: «Ba ní a là ní?»

english_verse: Bathsheba answered: Your Majesty, you promised me in the name of the Lord your God that my son Solomon would be the next king.
translation_verse: Ní Baatiseeba kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a nìn pūtì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ki pōoǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu ki lī yii: <M-kpátam boonee, a-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn di làá kpántí ubɔti kí kàl̄ m-beejal pu.>

english_verse: But Adonijah has already been made king, and you didn't know anything about it.
translation_verse: Ama kpèè, Adooniyasi kpántì ubɔti ní sii ti-baa ubɔti kaa kpáàa nyí!

english_verse: He sacrificed a lot of cattle, calves, and sheep. And he invited Abiathar the priest, Joab your army commander, and all your sons to be there, except Solomon, your loyal servant.
translation_verse: U kūū inajaa nì anabil ŋin cáá ŋkpamee nì ipii tikpil ki ŋá saraa, ní ki yíiń a-jipɔmbi kɔkɔ ki kpáaǹ usaraaŋakpil Abiyataar nì ujanjakpil Joowaab, ama waa yíiń a-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn.

english_verse: Your Majesty, everyone in Israel is waiting for you to announce who will be the next king.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-baa ubɔti, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiliŋ kíǹ ki cɔ́ a-pu ki cí un ní a làá lēē ú kpántí ubɔti a-kpátam boonee ní nee.

english_verse: Someone told David that he was there, and Nathan came in. He bowed with his face to the ground
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū ubɔti yii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan bāań, ní Naatan nín cá ubɔti cee ki tātìi gbāaǹ u-nimbiin u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ.

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, did you say that Adonijah would be king?
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u lī yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, mimmee sii di lēē yii a-kpátam boonee Adooniyasi ń kpántí ubɔti kí kàl̄ a-beejal puɔɔɔ?

english_verse: But he didn't invite me or Zadok the priest or Benaiah or Solomon.
translation_verse: Ama waa yíiń man a-tɔntɔnliuaaa, kaa yíiń usaraaŋakpil Sadookaaa, kaa yíiń Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuuyaaa, kaa yíiń a-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn mun.

english_verse: Did you say they could do this without telling the rest of us who would be the next king? Solomon Becomes King
translation_verse: Mimmee ti-baa ubɔti, sii di lafun lēē míǹ ní kaa kpáàa tùkū timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi tí béé un di làá kpántí ubɔti a-kpátam booneeee?» Daafiidi lēē Saloomɔn ú fōō u-yil

english_verse: David said, “Tell Bathsheba to come here.” She came and stood in front of him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Daafiidi bí yii: «Yíiḿmaan-mi Baatiseeba!» U bāańee ní ki yúl̀ ubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: Then he said, “The living Lord God of Israel has kept me safe. And so today, I will keep the promise I made to you in his name: Solomon will be the next king!”
translation_verse: kii m nín nìn pūtì ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ki pōoǹ-si yii: <M-kpátam boonee, a-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn di làá kpántí ubɔti kí kàl̄ m-beejal puee,> díǹ nee gba m làá ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and said, “Your Majesty, I pray that you will live a long time!”
translation_verse: Niinee Baatiseeba tātìi gbāaǹ ubɔti nimbiin u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ ní u lī yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti Daafiidi ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin kí nīn cá jaanjaan!»

english_verse: Then David said, “Tell Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to come here.” When they arrived,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti Daafiidi bí yii: «Yíiḿmaan-mi usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan nì Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu!» Ní bi yíiń-bi ní bíǹ bāań ki síl̀ ubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: he told them: Take along some of my officials and let Solomon ride my own mule to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-bi yii: «Kóom̀maan m-tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ kí kpāfì, ní kí dū m-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn kí kàan̄ mama m-ba mambooŋwu pu, kí cáá-u kí sìntī Giiyɔn nyimbuliŋun.

english_verse: When you get there, Zadok and Nathan will pour olive oil over Solomon's head to show that he is the new king of Israel. Then order someone to blow a trumpet and tell everyone to shout, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Ni yaa bàn̄ niinee, usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan ń bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī u-yil pu kí kàan̄-u ubɔti Isirayeel tiŋki pu. Míǹ boonee ní búń dikantándi ní kí kúuǹ mpɔn kí lì yii: <Ubɔti Saloomɔn ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn!>

english_verse: Bring him back here, and he will take my place as king. He is the one I have chosen to rule Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, ní fàtīí táá-u kí gítiń kitiŋin, ní ú dāá kàl̄ m-beejal pu. Úǹ di làá fōō m-yil kí kpántí ubɔti, di sá yii úǹ ní m kāaǹ ú kpántí Isirayeel nì Juuda ubɔti.»

english_verse: Benaiah answered, “We will do it, Your Majesty. I pray that the Lord your God will let it happen.
translation_verse: Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu kíí ubɔti yii: «Án ŋá míǹ! Ti-Dindaan, ti-baa ubɔti Nimbɔtiu di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: The Lord has always watched over you, and I pray that he will now watch over Solomon. May the Lord help Solomon to be an even greater king than you.”
translation_verse: Kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn bí sii ti-baa ubɔti cee puee, ú nīn bí Saloomɔn mun cee, ní kí tīī Saloomɔn beel tinyool tin jítiǹ sii ti-baa ubɔti Daafiidi yalee.» Saloomɔn kpántì ubɔti (Kpèè

english_verse: Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah left and took along the two groups of David's special bodyguards. Solomon rode on David's mule as they led him to Gihon Spring.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan nì Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu nì Keereeti nì Peeleeti yab nín cá Saloomɔn cee, ki yōoǹ-u ki kāaǹ ubɔti Daafiidi mambooŋwu pu, ní ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Giiyɔn nyimbuliŋun.

english_verse: Zadok the priest brought some olive oil from the sacred tent and poured it on Solomon's head to show that he was now king. A trumpet was blown and everyone shouted, “Long live King Solomon!”
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nìn yōoǹ ti-Dindaan circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ŋyin, ŋkpam kā ŋu-poon, ní ki bātì ŋkpamee ki sītì Saloomɔn yil pu ki kāaǹ-u tibɔtiil. Niinee ní bi búń dikantándi ní bin kɔkɔ bí niinee kúuǹ mpɔn ki lī yii: «Ubɔti Saloomɔn ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn!»

english_verse: Then they played flutes and celebrated as they followed Solomon back to Jerusalem. They made so much noise that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Ní samaa kɔkɔ táá-u ki gítìń kitiŋin. Binib nín nìn bí ki búǹ ŋwulimu ki fàal̀ puee, an nìn bí kii bi-kuŋkuuntii nìn yāntì kitiŋ bíi cìŋkēe ní. Saloomɔn dū Adooniyasi yìntitam ki pú-u

english_verse: Adonijah and his guests had almost finished eating when they heard the noise. Joab also heard the trumpet and asked, “What's all that noise about in the city?”
translation_verse: Adooniyasi nì bin kɔkɔ u nìn yíińee nìn jíń tijin ki dóò ní ki gbìl̄ ikuŋkuunti pu. Joowaab úǹ nìn gbìl̄ dikantándi pu gba ní ki bí yii: «Ba pu ní kitiŋin an tùm̀ dàii míǹ?»

english_verse: Just then, Jonathan son of Abiathar came running up. “Come in,” Adonijah said. “An important man like you must have some good news.”
translation_verse: U bíi sòoǹ míǹ u-nyɔkɔ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ ní usaraaŋakpil Abiyataar jipɔɔn Yoonatan dūu bāań. Ní Adooniyasi bí-u yii: «Kɔ́nní, a sá tinyooldaan ní, báà an ŋá pu, a cáań-ti tibɔmɔntiil ní.»

english_verse: Jonathan answered: No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king.
translation_verse: Ní Yoonatan kíí Adooniyasi yii: «An kaa sá míǹ báà fiii! Ti-baa ubɔti Daafiidi dū Saloomɔn ki kāaǹ ubɔti.

english_verse: Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki kāaǹ-u ubɔti Giiyɔn nyimbuliŋu caŋin. Míǹ boonee ní samaa kɔkɔ nín gítí kitiŋin nì dipɔɔpindi ní kitiŋin nib kɔkɔ kɔ́ ifaalin. An pu ní ni gbìl̄ kuwoou puee.

english_verse: Solomon is now king.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ dibeejal pu gba.

english_verse: And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!” David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed
translation_verse: Áli gba ubɔti kàliŋkpaambi dɔ́miń ki pàkā ti-baa ubɔti Daafiidi ki lī yii: <Unimbɔti ń yàntī Saloomɔn yindi ń nīn nyìm̀ ki jítiǹ a-yal ní kí tīī u-beel tinyool tin jítiǹ a-yatee.> Niinee ní ubɔti gbāaǹ u-lambaŋki pu,

english_verse: and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
translation_verse: ní ki lī yii: <Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu u nín tīī-mi díǹ ubɔ ú kàl̄ m-beejal puee, nì u nín yāntì m-nimbil wál̀ tin bíi jītí neeyee.>»

english_verse: Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ Adooniyasi nìn yíińee nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní bi-pɔbiliŋ bíil̀, ní báà ŋma yíkìi túĺ u-laŋki.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
translation_verse: Ní bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Saloomɔn yii: «Kpèè, Adooniyasi fāŋkì sii ubɔti Saloomɔn ní ki sáǹ ki cūtìi cúú nsaraafan yiŋyi ki bí yii: <Ubɔti Saloomɔn yaa kaa pūtì ki pōoǹ-mi yii waa làá kpɔ̀-mee, m kpá kí yīkì doo.>»

english_verse: Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.”
translation_verse: Ní Saloomɔn kíí yii: «U yaa làá nīn sá ubulcinnil, maa làá ŋá-u tiba, ama u yaa cáá tibɔkpitil u-ni, u làá kpú.»

english_verse: Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah. After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti Saloomɔn tú binib bi kpákatìń-u nsaraafan pu. U bāańee ní ki gbāaǹ ubɔti Saloomɔn nimbiin. Niinee ní Saloomɔn bí-u yii: «Nín̄ kùǹ a-dumpu!»

english_verse: My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave.
translation_verse: «M làá dòon̄ m-ŋaliŋu pu dee, á pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká kunyannyaau.

english_verse: Do what the Lord your God commands and follow his teachings. Obey everything written in the Law of Moses. Then you will be a success, no matter what you do or where you go.
translation_verse: Nín̄ ŋúb́ tin ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu yāntì bi ŋmàn̄ ki yóoǹee. Nín̄ pée ŋáań min u lèe, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-marab nì u-koobiliŋ nì u-dàkatam, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ ki kā Mooyiisi Marau poon puee. A yaa ŋá míǹ, án làá bútí-si a-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ nì tin kɔkɔ a bɔ́ntì kí ŋée poon.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always faithfully obey the Lord. If you do, he will keep the solemn promise he made to me that someone from our family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Niinee, ti-Dindaan làá ŋá kii u nín nìn pōoǹ-mi ki lī puee yii: <A-naantiibi yaa ŋáań min m lèe, ki yaa nóó-mi ibaamɔn poon nì bi-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ nì bi-naŋki kɔkɔee, a-kpátam boonee, a-naantiibi kansikin ubɔ làá nīn pée sá ubɔti ní Isirayeel tiŋkin.>

english_verse: Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him
translation_verse: Tiba mun gíti sɔ̀. A téetí Seeruya jipɔɔn Joowaab nín nìn ŋá-mi tikpitil tiŋyee kɔkɔɔ! Úǹ di nìn kūū Neer jipɔɔn Abineer nì Yeeteer jipɔɔn Amasaa, Isirayeel janjakpilib bilee. U nìn kūū-bi ŋgbansɔŋfi yuntiŋu, a lì kii kujaau poonee, ní ki làá túń bi-kúm kpuulool.

english_verse: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, dàkà iciin kí taa yàntī ú púĺ kí nīn sìntī ditaŋkpiilin nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.

english_verse: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
translation_verse: Kí kúntée, á taa súntí Geera jipɔɔn Simeeyii un sá Beenjameen naantiu ubɔ ki kóò Bawuriim tiŋkinee pu. Ŋwiin ŋun m nìn sáń ki cá Mayanayiim tiŋkinee, u nìn tɔ́-mi mbusu an kaa cáá bí lì. Ama m nín gítińee, u nìn sīntì Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi ki túŋkìń-mi, ní m nìn pūtì ti-Dindaan ki pōoǹ-u yii maa làá kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee á taa yàntī ú nīn bí kii u sá maanyiibee. Di sá yii a sá uciŋfiti, míǹ puee a nyí a nín làá ŋá-u puee. Á kpɔ̀-u ú kpáaǹ u-yikpipinti kí sìntī ditaŋkpiilin.» Daafiidi kpíì, Saloomɔn fōō u-yil (Kpèè

english_verse: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ní Simeeyii yíkì ki kpàl̄ u-maŋki ki nín cá Akiisi cee Gaati tiŋkin kí nyàabìń u-yumbui. Simeeyii nìn pée cūtì Gaati tiŋkin ki gíiǹní u-yumbui ní.

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
translation_verse: Bi-fatikuu ń gítí Joowaab nì u-naantiibi pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Ama ti-Dindaan ń yàntī Daafiidi nì u-naantiibi nì u-dicaŋku nì u-beel ń nīn bí mmɔnni kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Niinee ní Saloomɔn kāl̀ u-baa Daafiidi beejal pu, ní u-beel báaǹ inyaan tiŋan. Saloomɔn yāntì bi kūū Adooniyasi

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Agiiti jipɔɔn Adooniyasi cūtìi ká Saloomɔn na Baatiseeba. Baatiseeba ká u dòońee ní u bālifì-u yii: «An mɔ̄ deeee?» Ní úǹ kíí-u yii: «Iiin, an mɔ̄!»

english_verse: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
translation_verse: Ní ki gíti kútì yii: «M cáá tiba kí tùkù-si ní.» Ní Baatiseeba bí-u yii: «Sòoǹ tin a cááyee!»

english_verse: “You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed.
translation_verse: Ní u kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ yii: «Kii a nín nyí puee, man di bàà baasii yì dibeel, ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn kíǹ ki kā ki cí yii man nín kpántí ubɔti. Ama ní dibeel ŋmábitì m-ŋalin ní m-naal fōō, di sá yii ti-Dindaan di là yii úǹ ní kpántí ubɔti.

english_verse: Would you do me a favor?” “What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, m cáá kuwambambaantiiu ní kí mèè-si. M gbàam̄-si, á taa yííyee.» Ní Baatiseeba bí-u yii: «Nín̄ sòoǹ!»

english_verse: “Please ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag. He won't say no to you.”
translation_verse: Ní Adooniyasi nìkī ki bí yii: «M gbàam̄-si, tùkù ubɔti Saloomɔn ú dū kisuneembiki Abiisaagi kí tīī-mi ḿ cáá. Kéè waa làá yííyeeee!»

english_verse: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Baatiseeba nín cá ubɔti Saloomɔn cee kí sòoǹ nì u tin Adooniyasi cáań ki tùkū-uee. Ubɔti nín ká-uee ní u yíkì u-beejal pu ki nín túŋkí-u ní ki gbāaǹ u-nimbiin. U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki gítì ki kāl̀ u-beejal pu ní ki nyàab̄ diba mun ki síiǹ u-ŋaŋgiil pú ní u-na mun kāl̀ díǹ pu.

english_verse: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
translation_verse: Ní Baatiseeba bí-u yii: «M cáá tiba fiii ní ki là kí mèè-si, á taa yííyeeee.» Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «M-na, mèè kun ní a yaa lèe, m làá ŋá kí tīī-si.»

english_verse: “Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ní Baatiseeba bí yii: «Mimmee baa ŋūǹ kí dū kisuneembiki Abiisaagi kí tīī a-maan Adooniyasi ú cááaaa?»

english_verse: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti Saloomɔn kíí u-na yii: «Ba pu ní a bàlifī bí dū kisuneembiki Abiisaagi ŋmaniŋma kí tīī Adooniyasi? Bàlifì bí dū dibeel mun kí tīī-uaa, kun puee u sá m-maan ní! Bàlifì bí dū-dì kí tīī u nì u-naacimbi usaraaŋakpil Abiyataar nì ujanjakpil Joowaab, Seeruya jipɔɔn!»

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti Saloomɔn pūtì ti-Dindaan ki lī yii: «Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ m-tafal kí gíti kūtì m yaa kaa yāntì Adooniyasi dū u-maŋfal ki pàn̄ tin u sòon̄ee pɔndi!

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin ki yāntì m kāl̀ m-baa Daafiidi beejal pu, ní ki pōoǹ-mi yii dibeel làá nīn sá ki tīī man nì m-naantiibee yindi puee, m pūtì yii díǹ díǹ ní Adooniyasi làá kpú.»

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Saloomɔn tú Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu, ní úǹ cūtìi kūū Adooniyasi. Saloomɔn jìn̄ Abiyataar Jeerusaleem tiŋkin
