english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí usaraaŋakpil Abiyataar yii: «Nín̄ cá Anatooti tiŋkin, a-kpaatantin, di sá yii a máaǹ ŋkúm. Ama maa làá kpɔ̀-si díǹ, kun puee a túǹ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti dakaau m-baa Daafiidi yuntiŋu, ní a nì m-baa kpáfì ki jíń falaa.»

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Saloomɔn lēē Abiyataar ú taa ti nín̄ sá ti-Dindaan saraaŋakpiliu. Mimmee u ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn sòon̄ tin usaraaŋakpil Eelii dicaŋku pu Siilooyee dee. Saloomɔn yāntì bi kūū Joowaab

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní Joowaab gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní u sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ ti-Dindaan tantiun ki cúú nsaraafan yiŋyi. Di sá yii Joowaab nìn kíí ki kútì Adooniyasi pu, ama waa nìn páaǹ Abisaloom boon.

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Ní bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū ubɔti Saloomɔn yii: «Joowaab sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ ti-Dindaan tantiun ki bí nsaraafan caŋin.» Niinee ní Saloomɔn tú Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu ú cùú kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Beenayawuu kɔ́ ti-Dindaan tantiu poonee ní ki bí Joowaab yii: «Ubɔti bí yii á nyānní niin.» Ama ní Joowaab kíí yii: «Kpáb, doo ní m làá kpú.» Ní Beenayawuu nín gítí ubɔti cee ki dū Joowaab nín kíí-u puee ki tùkū-u.

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, Isirayeel janjakpiliu, Neer jipɔɔn Abineer nì Juuda janjakpiliu, Yeeteer jipɔɔn Amasaa nìn sá deedeedambi ki jítiǹ Joowaab. Ama u nìn kūū-bi m-baa kaa kpáàa nyí. Ti-Dindaan ń yàntī u-nikpaakooŋu gbanti kpuulool ń gítí u-pu.

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu nín gítí Joowaab cee ki kūū-u. Bi nìn síb́ Joowaab u-dumpu kuteeun ní.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn dū Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu ki téeǹ u-yil u kpántì ujanjakpil, ní ki yāntì usaraaŋakpil Sadooki fōō Abiyataar yil.

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn yāntì bi yíiń Simeeyii ní u bí-u yii: «Mā a-diiku Jeerusaleem tiŋkin doo kí nīn kóò. Aa cáá nsan kí nyā kí cù laaba.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋwiin ŋun ní a yaa nyáń ní a-taal lákatì Seedrɔn bùmbiki puee, á béé yii a làá pée kpú ní, ní a-fatikuu kpuulool ń gítí a-pu.»

english_verse: “That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
translation_verse: Ní Simeeyii bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a nín lī puee ŋān̄ tikpil. A nín bí yii man a-tɔntɔnliu ń ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá.» Simeeyii nìn kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki yúntì.

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Ama abin ata boonee ní Simeeyii yumbui ili sáǹ ki nín cá Gaati bɔtiu, Maaka jipɔɔn Akiisi cee, ní bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Simeeyii yii: «A-yumbui bí Gaati tiŋkin.»

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū Saloomɔn yii Simeeyii nyáń Jeerusaleem ki cūtì Gaati tiŋkin ki fātìi gítìń.

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti yāntì bi yíiń Simeeyii ní u bí-u yii: «M nìn yāntì a pūtì ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii aa làá nyā kitiŋee ni ní man m-ba kpáafì-si yii: <Ŋwiin ŋun a yaa nyáń kitiŋ nee ni ki cūtì laabee, a làá kpɔ́ɔ>! Kéè a nìn kíí-mi yii tin m sòon̄ee ŋān̄aa!

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Kin ba pu ní aa tɔ́ dipoondi din a nìn pōoǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiinee nì mara un m nìn tīī-see?»

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti gíti bí Simeeyii yii: «Sii a-ba nyí tiŋan tikpitil tin ní a ŋá m-baa Daafiidee. Too, ti-Dindaan làá yàntī a-toonam ń gítí a-pu.

english_verse: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
translation_verse: Ama man ubɔti Saloomɔn, ti-Dindaan làá bìin̄ m-pu, ní kí tīī Daafiidi beel mpɔn kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti pú Yeewooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu kinyɔkɔ ú nyāntí Simeeyii ní úǹ nyántì-u ki kūū-u. Min ní Saloomɔn nìn ŋá ki mɔ̄tìi ká mpɔn u-beel báaǹ inyaanee dee.

english_verse: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
translation_verse: M làá tīī-si gba tin ní aa mēēyee, m làá tīī-si tigaajati nì tinyool a-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon. Báà ubɔti ubɔ juti kaa làá nīn sá-si.

english_verse: Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn néeń ti-Dindaan ní ki nìn ŋáań min u-baa Daafiidi nìn kpáafì-uee. Ama ŋgbantamu pu awaa saraafaŋyi pu ní u mun nìn kù tiwaŋkuti ki ŋáań saraabi ní ki tùutī talaalub. Saloomɔn mēē Unimbɔti ú tīī-u iciin (Kpèè

english_verse: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: U bí Gabawɔn niin kunyeeuee ní ti-Dindaan lēē u-ba ki dàkā-u ní ki bí-u yii: «Bàlifì kun ní a là ḿ tīī-see.»

english_verse: Solomon answered: My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king.
translation_verse: Ní Saloomɔn kíí yii: «A dàkā a-tɔntɔnliu m-baa Daafiidi kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu tikpil, kun puee u nìn nóó-si nì ibaamɔn nì deedee ní u-pɔbil nìn bí diba nì si. A gíti dàkā-u a-laŋŋaŋfitiiku ki tīī-u jipɔɔn u kpántì díǹ pu nee ubɔti.

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: Too kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu, sii di yāntì man a-tɔntɔnliu fōō m-baa Daafiidi yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Ma mun di dá láá sá campɔnti kaa nyí dibeel bɔti tibee.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: Man a-tɔntɔnliu bí a-nibul din a lēēyee nib kansikin kí nīn kpòotī-bi. Dinibul gbanti nib wīikí tikpil áli baa kpáàa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ-bi.

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee tīī man a-tɔntɔnliu dinyil ḿ dūú kpòotī a-nibul, kí ŋmā kí béé kí gàntī tin ŋān̄ee nì tin kaa ŋān̄ee. Di sá yii ŋma di ŋūǹ kí gāā u-bindi kí lì yii u ŋūǹ kí kpòotī a-nibul dikpaandi nee?»

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bí-u yii: «Aa mēē yii ḿ tīī-si mmaŋfafɔkɔn, àá tigaajati, àá ḿ nàan̄ a-nannanliibi. Ama ní ki mēē yii ḿ tīī-si dinyil á ŋmā kí dūú kpòotī m-nibul nì ibaamɔn. A nín mēē mimmee puee,

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: A yaa ŋáań min m lèe, ki yaa tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab kii a-baa Daafiidee, m làá gbéeǹ a-maŋfal wiiŋyi pu.»

english_verse: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials. Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
translation_verse: Saloomɔn fīntèe ní ká yii an sá kudamintiiu. Míǹ boonee ní u nín kùǹ u-dumpu Jeerusaleem ní ki cūtìi yúl̀ ti-Dindaan Dakaau nimbiin. U nìn ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi, ní ki ŋá jiŋaal ki yíiń u-tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ bi jíń. Saloomɔn sòon̄ tibɔti nì iciin

english_verse: One day two women came to King Solomon,
translation_verse: Dalbee nnimpulaakpaamu muli mubɔ dɔ́miń ubɔti Saloomɔn cee.

english_verse: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
translation_verse: Bi-kansikin ubɔ bí yii: «Ti-baa, m gbàam̄-si ní. Man nì unimpu nee di kóò kudibaantiiun. M màl̄ kibiki kudii gbantinee, u mun nìn bí niin.

english_verse: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
translation_verse: Kunyeeuee ní unimpu nee biki kpíì, kun puee u nyīkiǹ ki-pu.

english_verse: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
translation_verse: Ní u yíkì kunyataasiiu ki yōoǹ m-biki m-cee ŋyunti ŋun man a-tɔntɔnliu dɔ̄ ki gèeǹee. U yōoǹ m-bikee ní ki dū-kì kí bíl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ u-ba, ní ki dū u-yaka kin kpíìyee ki bíl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ-mi.

english_verse: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
translation_verse: M fīntì kutaafaau kí tīī m-biki dibiilee, m ká yii kì kpíì. Kutaa wúntì ki dóò m kpēē-kì tiŋanee ní ki ká yii an kaa sá m-biki.»

english_verse: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
translation_verse: Unimpuliliitee nìn bí yii: «An kaa sá mbaamɔn! Man biki di bí dimaŋfalin, kin kpíìyee, a-yaka dee.» Ama ní unimpupeepeekaayee bí yii: «Aayee! Sii biki di kpíì, man yaka di bí dimaŋfalin.» Bi nín nìn sí ubɔti nimbiin ki sòoǹ puee dee.

english_verse: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
translation_verse: An yaa sée, ní cáaḿmaan-mi kitàataajiki.» Ní bi cūtìi cáań-u kitàataajiki.

english_verse: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Pùtīmaan kibiki kin bí dimaŋfalinee mili, kí dū dijandi kí tīī ubɔ kí dū dijandi din kíǹee kí tīī un kíǹee.»

english_verse: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
translation_verse: Ama unimpu un biki bí dimaŋfalinee bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa, m gbàam̄-si, dū kibiki kin bí dimaŋfalinee kí tīī unimpu nee, ní taa kpɔ̀-kì!» Di sá yii dineendi din unimpuee nìn cáá u-biki puee nìn fòol̄ u-ni lìblib kii ŋŋmee ní. Ama ní unimpu un kíǹee bí yii: «Ní taa dū-kì kí tīī ti-kansikin báà ubɔ. Ní pùtī-kì mili!»

english_verse: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti bí yii: «Ní taa kpɔ̀ kibikee. Dūmaan-kì kí tīī unimpupeekaayee, di sá yii úǹ di sá kibikee na!»

english_verse: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn gbìl̄ ubɔti nín sòon̄ tibɔti gbanti puee, ní bi kíǹ ki tɔ́-u tikpil. Bi nìn ká yii Unimbɔti ciiŋyi bí u-ni ú nīn cáa sòoǹ tibɔti.

english_verse: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn gíti cáá kɔmandambi saalaa nì bili bin u kāaǹ Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ puee. Bíǹ di nìn nyàab̀ tijin ki tìì ubɔti nì u-dicaŋkun yab. Bi-kansikin báà ŋma nìn cáá uŋmal ubɔ dibindi poon kí nyàab̀ tijin kí tīī ubɔti nì u-dicaŋku.

english_verse: These were the twelve officers: The son of Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Kɔmandambi gbanti yiŋŋi sɔ̀. Uur jipɔɔn di nìn kpèé Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi,

english_verse: The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
translation_verse: ní Deekeeri jipɔɔn kpèé Makaasi nì Saalbiim nì Beeti-Seemeesi nì Eeloon-Beeti-Anaani,

english_verse: The son of Abinadab was in charge of Naphath-Dor and was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath.
translation_verse: ní Abinadaab jipɔɔn kpèé Dɔɔr tiŋki kɔkɔ. Úǹ di nìn cáá Saloomɔn bisal Tafaati,

english_verse: The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had
translation_verse: Geebeer jipɔɔn di nìn kpèé Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadee nì Manasee jipɔɔn Yayiir timbilimmu mun bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee nì Argoob tiŋki kin bí Baasan tiŋkpaaŋkinee. Kitiŋkpaaŋŋi gbanti nìn cáá ntimu imuŋku ita bi máń agun ki tú-mu. Mu nìn cáá punuubi bin bi cáá tasa kúti kpàlkaati ki kpàl̀ee,

english_verse: Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of the territory of Mahanaim.
translation_verse: ní Idoo jipɔɔn Ayiinadaab kpèé Mayanayiim tiŋkpaaŋki,

english_verse: Ahimaaz was in charge of the territory of Naphtali and was married to Solomon's daughter Basemath.
translation_verse: ní Ayiimaasi kpèé Neefitalii tiŋkpaaŋki. U mun nìn tí cáá Saloomɔn bisal ubɔ ní, bi yíì-u Basmaati.

english_verse: Baana son of Hushai was in charge of the territory of Asher and the town of Bealoth.
translation_verse: Usayii jipɔɔn Baana di nìn kpèé Aseer nì Beeyalooti timmu,

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in charge of the territory of Issachar.
translation_verse: ní Paruuya jipɔɔn Yeewoosafaati kpèé Isakaar tiŋkpaaŋki,

english_verse: Shimei son of Ela was in charge of the territory of Benjamin.
translation_verse: ní Eela jipɔɔn Simeeyii kpèé Beenjameen tiŋkpaaŋki,

english_verse: Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived. And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah. The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
translation_verse: ní Urii jipɔɔn Geebeer kpèé Galaadi tiŋki nì Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu Siiwɔn nì Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi timmu. Kɔmandan ubɔ mun nìn gíti bí Juuda tiŋkin.

english_verse: The Lord God promised my father that when his son became king, he would build a temple for worshiping the Lord. So I've decided to do that.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, Juuda yab nì Isirayeel yab nìn kā ŋgbansɔŋfin ní, kí yòon̄ Daani ŋgan pú kí cáá sāā Beerseeba ŋgiil pú. Báà ŋma nìn cáá u-fiinyi sufii nì u-fiigi sufii ní ki nìn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_verse: I'd like you to send your workers to cut down cedar trees in Lebanon for me. I will pay them whatever you say and will even have my workers help them. We both know that your workers are more experienced than anyone else at cutting lumber.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn gíti cáá itaamu kutukub saalaa nì bili nì tinaabakal tin poon itaamu in dátí tɔrɔkubee bée. Tinaabakal gbanti poonee, inaa kutukub imuŋku ili nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́.

english_verse: Hiram was so happy when he heard Solomon's request that he said, “I am grateful that the Lord gave David such a wise son to be king of that great nation!”
translation_verse: Kɔmandambi saalaa nì bili bin ubɔti nìn lēēyee nìn cāabìń tijin ki tìì ubɔti Saloomɔn nì bin kɔkɔ jīǹ u-dumpuee. Kɔmandan kamaa nìn cáá dibindi poonee uŋmal un ní u cāabìń tijinee ní. Baa nìn yàntī tiba nì tiba ń lóó-u.

english_verse: Then he sent back his answer: I received your message and will give you all the cedar and pine logs you need.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti cāabìń ɔɔji nì timool ki tìì itaamu in dátí tɔrɔkubee nì itaamu in kíǹee laakin ubɔti kóòyee, ki nóó nì báà ŋma nín fōō mara kí ŋá puee. Saloomɔn cáá iciin ki jítiǹ binib kɔkɔ

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise and made Solomon wise. Hiram and Solomon signed a treaty and never went to war against each other. Solomon's Workers
translation_verse: U nìn náań alaŋkpan kutukub bita nì ilan kutuku ubɔ nì ilan iŋmoo.

english_verse: The windows were narrow on the outside but wide on the inside.
translation_verse: U nìn lēē tɔkɔlab kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi pu. Tɔkɔlabee nìn cáá tifukuŋkaal nì nlaamu.

english_verse: Solomon put them next to each other in the most holy place. Their wings were spread out and reached across the room.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū keerubimbi gbanti ki síiǹ Circir páaa laŋki poon ní. Bi nìn kpátì bi-feeŋyi, upeekaayee feeŋŋu ŋubɔ nìn tùutī digundi ní uliliitee feeŋŋu ŋubɔ tùutī digundi din kíǹee, ní bi-feeŋyi in kíǹee tùutī tɔb.

english_verse: The roof of the temple was made out of beams and cedar boards. The workers finished building the outside of the temple.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nín nìn máń Unimbɔti diiku ki dóòyee, u nìn dū seedir dɔi ní ki bɔ̀b̄ yilpu.

english_verse: If you obey my commands and do what I say, I will keep the promise I made to your father David. I will live among my people Israel in this temple you are building, and I will not desert them.
translation_verse: M làá dāan̄ kí nīn kóò Isirayeel yab kansikin kudii nee poon. M kpá kí dū m-nibul Isirayeel yab kí fá jaanjaan.» Bi nín nyɔ̄kɔntì kunimbɔtidii poon puee

english_verse: Along the sides and back of the temple, there were three levels of storage rooms. The rooms on the bottom level were just over two meters wide, the rooms on the middle level were over two and a half meters wide, and those on the top level were just over three meters wide. There were ledges on the outside of the temple that supported the beams of the storage rooms, so that nothing was built into the temple walls.
translation_verse: Aditɔntɔkɔ gbanti kun bí taapuee waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní kun bí kansikinee waaŋŋu sá meetab bita, ní kun tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee waaŋŋu sá meetab bita nì dijandi. Di sá yii kunimbɔtidii boon pú gundi gbifiŋŋu kaa nìn sá mbaanti ki tin kátì yilpu. An puee bi nín nìn bɔ̀b̄ aditɔntɔkɔ yilpu puee kaa nìn kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi poon.

english_verse: Solomon did not want the noise of hammers and axes to be heard at the place where the temple was being built. So he gave orders for the workers to shape the blocks of stone at the quarry.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lēē laaba ní ki kpítíi ŋáŋkí ataŋkpee. Ataŋkpee ŋin bi nìn kpítíi ŋáŋkée ní bi nìn dūu máń kunimbɔtidii. An puee bi nín nìn bíi māāyee, baa nìn gbìl̀ aama puɔɔɔ, kicɔkɔ puɔɔɔ, tikúti tɔntɔŋwanti tiba pu.

english_verse: Storage rooms just over two meters high were all around the temple, and they were attached to the temple by cedar beams.
translation_verse: Aditɔntɔkɔ ŋin u nìn máń ki tú kunimbɔtidii kɔkɔee, kudii kamaa fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní bi dū seedir dɔjaliŋ ki páaǹ yilpu ní an dāa tɔ́kɔǹ kunimbɔtidii gundi pu.

english_verse: The Lord told Solomon:
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Saloomɔn yii:

english_verse: The floor of the temple was made out of pine, and the walls were lined with cedar from floor to ceiling.
translation_verse: u nìn látì seedir dɔpampaŋŋi ki nákáǹ ku-poon ki yōoǹ ku-taapu ki cáa sāā yilpu, ní ki dū siipreesi dɔi in bi látèe ki bíl̀ ku-taapu.

english_verse: The most holy place was in the back of the temple, and it was nine meters square. Cedar boards standing from floor to ceiling separated it from the rest of the temple.
translation_verse: Bi nìn tí dū seedir dɔi in bi látì apampanee ki nákáǹ poon diiku guŋŋi ki yōoǹ taapu ki cáá sāā yilpu. Kudii gbanti fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalaa ní. Bi nìn bɔ́ntì-ku ki dū-ku ki ŋá kunimbɔtidii pɔ̀ti pu, circir páaa laŋki.

english_verse: The inside walls were lined with cedar to hide the stones, and the cedar was decorated with carvings of gourds and flowers.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lēē koolookinti subiliŋ nì nsupumpukum min mātèe ki nákáǹ seedir dɔpampaŋŋi ŋin bi nìn dūu nákáǹ kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi puee. Seedir dɔi ní bi nìn dūu bīiǹ tikɔkɔ pu, an puee baa nìn wāĺ báà ditaŋkpal.

english_verse: The sacred chest was kept in the most holy place.
translation_verse: Bi nìn bɔ́ntì kudikpaaŋŋu poon circir diiku kubɔ ní ki dū ti-Dindaan poondi dakaau ki síiǹ.

english_verse: Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made from olive wood to put in the most holy place. Each creature was four and a half meters tall
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ɔliifi dɔŋu ki kpítì keerubimbi bili ki síiǹ Circir páaa laŋki diikun, keerubim kamaa fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab biŋmoo ní.

english_verse: and four and a half meters across. They had two wings, and the wings were just over two meters long.
translation_verse: Keerubimpeekaayee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab biŋmoo, míǹ mbaantiim ní uliliitee mun fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá.

english_verse: The creatures were also covered with gold.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki nyūntì keerubimbi liitil.

english_verse: The walls of the two rooms were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpítì keerubimbi nì ibafi nì nsupumpukum min mātèe ki nákáǹ kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi poon nì boon ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: Even the floor was covered with gold.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki ŋàl̄ adiin liitil poon.

english_verse: The two doors to the most holy place were made out of olive wood and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures. The doors and the carvings were covered with gold. The door frame came to a point at the top.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpítì punuubi bilee pu keerubimbi nì ibafi nì nsupumpukum min mātèe, ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki nyūntì keerubimbi nì ibafee mun.

english_verse: The doors were covered with gold and were decorated with carvings of palm trees, flowers, and winged creatures.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti kpítì punuubee pu keerubimbi nì ibafi nì nsupumpukum min mātèe ki nyɔ̄kɔntì, ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì laakin bi kpítèe.

english_verse: The inner courtyard of the temple had walls made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u máń poon cindi. Bi nín nìn máń dicindi gundi puee sɔ̀. Bi nìn máń ataŋkpee ikuul ita nì seedir dɔi ŋkuul ŋubɔ.

english_verse: Work began on the temple during Ziv, the second month of the year, four years after Solomon became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nín kāl̀ dibeelee, dibinnanaatiil ŋmaliliitiu poon, an dàkà yii uŋmal un bi yíì Siifee poon ní bi bíl̀ ti-Dindaan diiku nyeel.

english_verse: Seven years later the workers finished building it during Bul, the eighth month of the year. It was built exactly as it had been planned.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nín kāl̀ dibeelee abin saalaa nì diba ŋmaniniitiu poon, an dàkà yii uŋmal un bi yíì yii Buulee poon ní bi dóò kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pái. Saloomɔn nìn dū abin aluli ní ki máń-ku.

english_verse: a large bowl; twelve bulls that held up the bowl;
translation_verse: nì kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundee, nì inajaa saalaa nì ili in tú kusɔŋu gbantee,

english_verse: -centimeter strip, and there were four braces attached to the corners of each stand. The panels and the supports were attached to the stands,
translation_verse: Bi nìn ŋá jaantalkubee yilpu kii nsupumpukumee ní. Míǹ ní Yiiram nìn mɔ́ɔ́ jaantalkubee ki dóò. Bi dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu (Kpèè

english_verse: Hiram made two bronze columns eight meters tall and almost two meters across.
translation_verse: U nìn dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ jaantalkub bili. Bi-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab biwa ní kí màntīí tūee sá meetab biluu.

english_verse: pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls. Hiram made these bronze things for Solomon
translation_verse: nì asambil nì peelab nì asambil ŋin poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki cáa yàantée. Tasa kúmɔntiiti ní Yiiram nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn ú dūú síiń ti-Dindaan Diikun.

english_verse: The section of the palace where Solomon lived was behind Justice Hall and looked exactly like it. He had a similar place built for his wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt.

english_verse: Forgive your people no matter how much they have sinned against you. Make the enemies who defeated them be kind to them.
translation_verse: Dū a-nibul kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi. Dū bi nín jáà nì si puee kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí yàntī bin ŋúb́-bi kuyuŋuee ń sɔ̄ bi-saai kí dàkà-bi kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.

english_verse: Remember, they are the people you chose and rescued from Egypt that was like a blazing fire to them.
translation_verse: Di sá yii bi sá a-nibul ní. Sii di yì-bi ní ki nyántìń-bi Eejipiti yab paaki ŋmiŋun.

english_verse: I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So listen when any of us pray and cry out for your help.
translation_verse: «Ŋúbití a-nimbiliŋ, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti. Pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu gbaamii nì a-nibul Isirayeel gbaamii. Pīlifiǹ-ti ŋyunti ŋun kamaa ní ti yaa pée kúuǹ ki yíiń-see.

english_verse: When you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, you told your servant Moses to say to them, “From all people on earth, the Lord God has chosen you to be his very own.” Solomon Blesses the People
translation_verse: Di sá yii sii di lútì-ti kitiŋ pu nibuliŋ kɔkɔ kansikin tí nīn sá difakal ki tīī-si, kii a nín nìn dī a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu ki sòon̄ pu ŋyunti ŋun a nìn nyántì ti-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkinee.» Saloomɔn mēē Unimbɔti ń bìin̄ samaa pu

english_verse: When Solomon finished his prayer at the altar, he was kneeling with his arms lifted toward heaven. He stood up,
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn gbāaǹ u-tabiŋyiliŋ pu ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu nyɔkɔpu, ki yōoǹ u-ŋalii yilpu, ní ki mēē ki gbāam̀ ti-Dindaan. U nìn mēē míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki yíkì

english_verse: turned toward the people, blessed them, and said loudly:
translation_verse: ki síl̀ ki mēē mpɔn ki bīiǹ Isirayeel samaau pu ki lī yii:

english_verse: Praise the Lord! He has kept his promise and given us peace. Every good thing he promised to his servant Moses has happened.
translation_verse: «Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan un di tīī u-nibul Isirayeel ŋgbansɔŋfi kii u nín nìn pōoǹ puee. Di sá yii u nín nìn dī u-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu ki pōoǹ-ti ipoon iŋyee, báà iba kaa gbíntì waa ŋá.

english_verse: The Lord our God was with our ancestors to help them, and I pray that he will be with us and never abandon us.
translation_verse: Tin m mèé ti-Dindaan Unimbɔtee di sá ú nīn bí ti-cee kii u nín nìn bí ti-naanjab cee puee. Ú taa dū-ti kí fá, kí taa fàtī u-boon kí tīī-ti.

english_verse: May the Lord help us obey him and follow all the laws and teachings he gave our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ú gíiǹní ti-pɔbiliŋ u-cee! Niinee ti làá ŋmā kí nīn bí kii u nín là tí nīn bí puee, ní tí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-koobiliŋ ŋin u nìn dūu tīī ti-naanjabee.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord our God will remember my prayer day and night. May he help everyone in Israel each day, in whatever way we need it.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn téetí m-gbaamii in m dūu bíl̀ u-nimbiin nee pu ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Ú pɔ̀ man u-tɔntɔnliu nì u-nibul Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: Then every nation will know that the Lord is the only true God.
translation_verse: An yaa ŋá mimmee, kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ làá béé yii ti-Dindaan baba di sá Unimbɔti, ubɔ kaa ti bí.

english_verse: Obey the Lord our God and follow his commands with all your heart, just as you are doing today. Solomon Dedicates the Temple (
translation_verse: Nín̄ símaan nì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu deedee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-bɔkpaaŋi kí nīn tɔ́ u-marab, kii ni nín bíi ŋáań pu díǹ nee.» Saraabi bin bi ŋá ki tīī ti-Dindaanee (Kpèè

english_verse: On that day, Solomon dedicated the courtyard in front of the temple and made it acceptable for worship. He offered the sacrifices there because the bronze altar in front of the temple was too small.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti mbaanti ní ubɔti dū dicindi din bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee ki sú ti-Dindaan. Di sá yii tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu ŋun nìn bí kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki caŋinee kaa nìn náaǹ bí ŋmā kí wà saraabi kɔkɔ. An puee kunimbɔtidii cindin ní u nìn dū saraawɔkaa nì tijin saraabi nì mpèé saraabi kpam ki wùn̄ ki ŋá saraa.

english_verse: Solomon and the huge crowd celebrated the Festival of Shelters at the temple for seven days. There were people from as far away as the Egyptian Gorge in the south and Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní Saloomɔn nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kpáfì ki jíń tibìń jiŋaaliu. An nìn sá dinikitikpaandi ní, binib nìn nyánní doooo Leeboo-Amaati kitiŋ yilpu pú ki cáá sāā Eejipiti buŋŋu kitiŋ taapu pú. Bi nìn jíń jiŋaal gbanti iwiin iluli ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin, ní ki gíti kútì iwiin iluli, an kpáfìi ŋá ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku.

english_verse: Then on the eighth day, he sent everyone home. They said goodbye and left, very happy, because of all the good things the Lord had done for his servant David and his people Israel.
translation_verse: Kinyɔnliliitii iwiin inii dalee ní Saloomɔn yāntì Isirayeel yab nín gítí bi-dumpui. Samaa nìn jáam̀ ubɔti ní ki nín kóò bi-tantibin nì mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn dàkā u-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi nì u-nibul Isirayeel kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.

english_verse: I will no longer let my people Israel live in this land I gave them. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped. Then people everywhere will think this nation is only a joke and will make fun of it.
translation_verse: m làá jà Isirayeel yab kitiŋ kin m tīī-bee pu. M làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī kudii kun m dūu sú m-ba nee. Anibul kɔkɔ làá nīn kíǹ ki bèel̄ Isirayeel yab ní ki lāā-bi.

english_verse: The Lord said: I heard your prayer and what you asked me to do. This temple you have built is where I will be worshiped forever. It belongs to me, and I will never stop watching over it.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-u yii: «M gbìl̄ a-wimmeem nì a-gbaamii in a dūu bíl̀ m-nimbiinee. M ŋá kudii kun a máńee circir, ní m kíí bí nīn jáaḿ m-yindi ku-poon kí nīn cá jaanjaan. M-nimbikpeeŋu làá nīn pée cɔ́ ku-pu, ní m làá nīn wúń ku-pu baabadal.

english_verse: You must obey me, as your father David did, and be honest and fair. Obey my laws and teachings,
translation_verse: Ama siiyee, nín̄ nóó-mi nì dipɔbil diba nì ibaamɔn poon kii a-baa Daafiidee. Nín̄ ŋáań tin m kpáafì-see, ní kí nīn ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-koobiliŋ.

english_verse: But if you or any of your descendants disobey my commands or start worshiping foreign gods,
translation_verse: Ama sii nì a-jipɔmbi yaa kaa ŋúb́ m-marab nì m-koobiliŋ ŋin m tīī-nee, ní ki yaa fātì ni-boon ki tīī-mi ki cūtìi nóó awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapuee,

english_verse: Then they will answer, “We know why the Lord did this. The people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.” Other Things Solomon Did (
translation_verse: Niinee ní bí dāá kíí-bi yii: <Kun yì-tèe di sá yii Isirayeel yab dū ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu un di nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee ki fá. Bi dū bi-ba ki tīī awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapu ki jáaḿ-ŋi. An pu ní ti-Dindaan yāntì nnaabu nee bāań-bi.>» Saloomɔn nín túń atuun ŋiŋyee (Kpèè

translation_verse: Niinee ní Yiiram nyánní Tiir tiŋkin ki dɔ́miń kí kpèè ntimu mun Saloomɔn tīī-uee, ama ntimuee bɔti kaa nìn fáatì-u.

english_verse: He said, “Solomon, my friend, are these the kind of towns you want to give me?” So Hiram called the region Cabul because he thought it was worthless.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u bí yii: «M-nabiki, ba timmu ní a nín tīī-mi nan dee!» An pu ní nìn díǹ, bi yíì ntimu gbanti yii Kabuul timmu.

english_verse: After Solomon's workers had finished the temple and the palace, he ordered them to fill in the land on the east side of Jerusalem, to build a wall around the city, and to rebuild the towns of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
translation_verse: Diwɔ́bil tundi ní Saloomɔn nìn dūu máń ti-Dindaan Diiku nì úǹ u-ba diiku nì kudii kun bi yíì Miilooyee nì digundi din bi máń ki tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee nì Asɔɔr nì Meegiidoo nì Geeseer timmu.

english_verse: Earlier, the king of Egypt had captured the town of Gezer; he burned it to the ground and killed the Canaanite people living there. Then he gave it to his daughter as a wedding present when she married Solomon.
translation_verse: Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo nìn cūtìi jáń ki fōō Geeseer tiŋki. U nìn kūū Kanaan yab bin nìn kóò niinee kɔkɔ ní ki tūū adiin ŋŋmi, ní ki dū kitiŋee ki pàn̄ u-bisal un mɔ́ǹ Saloomɔŋyee cootiiku.

english_verse: So Solomon had the town rebuilt. Solomon ordered his workers to rebuild Lower Beth-Horon,
translation_verse: An pu ní an nìn bālifì yii Saloomɔn ń fàtīí mā Geeseer tiŋki gbanti. Saloomɔn nìn gíti máń Beeti-Oorɔn-Taapu,

english_verse: They also built towns where he could keep his supplies and his chariots and horses. Solomon ordered them to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere in his kingdom.
translation_verse: nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon ní bi nìn bīil̀ u-jintee, nì ntimu mun poon ní u-janjatɔrɔkub nìn sīlifée, nì mun poon ní u-taamui nìn bée. Saloomɔn nìn gíti máń kun ní u nìn lèe Jeerusaleem tiŋkin nì Leebanɔn jool pu nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ nìn pée bí u-taapuee.

english_verse: Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the older part of Jerusalem to her new palace. Then Solomon had the land on the east side of Jerusalem filled in.
translation_verse: Faaroo bisal nín jɔ́m̀ Daafiidi Tiŋkin ki kɔ́ kudii kun Saloomɔn nìn máń ki tīī-uee, boonee ní u nín máń Miiloo diiku.

english_verse: Three times a year, Solomon burned incense and offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built. Solomon had now finished building the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi nsaraafan ŋun u nìn máń ti-Dindaanee dibindi poonee mita pu ní. U nìn gíti tùutī talaalub nsaraafan pu ki tìì ti-Dindaan. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋáań ki dàkà kun pu kunimbɔtidii bée.

english_verse: He also had a lot of ships at Ezion-Geber, a town in Edom near Eloth on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn kpáá meelab Eesiiyɔn-Geebeer tiŋkin Eelaati tiŋki caŋin. Eelaati tiŋki gbanti bí Tikati Mɔɔl gbandi, Eedoom tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: King Hiram let some of his experienced sailors go to the country of Ophir with Solomon's own sailors, and they brought back about
translation_verse: Bimeelaŋaaliliibi gbanti nìn cūtì Oofiiri tiŋkin ki nyàab̄ sindaariya tɔnnib saalaa nì bili ki cáa cūnnì ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn.

english_verse: The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, his servants in their uniforms, the people who served his food, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: nì tijin tin tɔ́kɔ́ u-teebiliu puee nì u-tɔntɔnliibi kɔŋkooŋyi nì u-tɔntɔnliibi bin tìì-u tijin u jīǹ nì nnyim u nyùee wampeeŋkaati nì saraabi bin u nìn ŋáań kunimbɔtidiinee ní an ŋá-u bitii waa ti nyí tin poon u bée.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u bí ubɔti yii: «Tin m gbìl̄ m-tiŋkin a-tuuŋŋi pu nì a-ciiŋyi puee lafun sá mbaamɔn ní.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are wiser and richer than I was told.
translation_verse: Ama maa nìn fōō ki kíí, see m nín dɔ́miń m-ba ki ká nì m-nimbilee. Tin bi máafì-mee kaa bàn̄ tin m ká nee dijandi gba. A-ciiŋyi nì a-gaajati jítiǹ tin m gbìl̄ee pu kpataaa.

english_verse: Your wives and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: A-nib nì a-tɔntɔnliibi bin bí a-nimbiin baabadal ki pílifí a-ciiŋyi nyɔɔbuŋŋee bí mmɔnneeee!

english_verse: The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, many jewels, and more spices than anyone had ever brought into Israel.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Sabaa tiŋki nimpubɔtiu tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn sindaariya tɔnnib bita nì dijandi nì talaalub tikpil nì ataŋkpamɔnti. Sabaa nimpubɔtiu nín nìn tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn talaalub puee, baa ti pée ká an talaalub bulifi kɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋkin dalba dalba.

english_verse: He was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn jítiǹ kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi kɔkɔ tigaajati poon nì iciin poon.

english_verse: The merchants and traders, as well as the kings of Arabia and rulers from Israel, also gave him gold.
translation_verse: ní kí nín kūtì bibantiliibi nì binyampoobi nín nìn cāabìń sindaariya un ki pà patantibee, nì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú bɔtiibi nì Isirayeel tiŋgbammu nín lèekī pu ki cāabìń ki pà lampoobee.

english_verse: His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn gíti kpítì dibeejal dikpaandi diba ní ki dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì ní ki dū kunti nyiŋŋi ki nákáǹ nákáǹ.

english_verse: Since silver was almost worthless in those days, everything was made of gold, even the cups and dishes used in Forest Hall.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Saloomɔn kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi kɔkɔ nìn sá sindaariya ŋma ní, ní asambil ŋin bí <Leebanɔn Pɔɔku> diikunee nìn sá sindaariyamɔnti ŋma. Baa nìn dù animbil kúti kí ŋá tiba, di sá yii Saloomɔn yuntiŋuee, animbil kúti kaa nìn cáá kunyampoou.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ubɔti nìn cáá meelab Taarsiisi tiŋkin bin tūntí binyampoobee bi cá ki gítiń bi nì Yiiram meelab. Abin ata poon diba puee, meelab gbanti nìn cāabìń sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì kunti nyiŋŋi nì ilantan nì ikooŋaan.

english_verse: People from every nation wanted to hear the wisdom God had given him.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ nìn nyàab̀ kí ká Saloomɔn kí ŋmā kí pīlifì iciin in Unimbɔti nìn tīī-uee.

english_verse: Year after year people came and brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, or mules.
translation_verse: Bi yaa nìn dòońee, báà ŋma nìn cāabìń animbil kúti wanti nì sindaariya wanti nì tiwampeeŋkaal nì tijanjawan nì talaalub nì itaamu nì imamboon ki pūǹ-u. Dibindi kamaayee, binib nìn pée ŋáań míǹ ní.

english_verse: While he was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn yāntì animbil gbí Jeerusaleem kii ataŋkpeeyee ní, ní seedir dɔi wīikí kii Seefeelaa tiŋkin sufii in bi yíì siikoomɔɔree.

english_verse: Seven hundred of his wives were daughters of kings, but he also married
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun Saloomɔn púĺee ní u-nimpoobee yāntì u cūtìi bíi tòotī awaa. Waa nìn gíti sí nì ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu deedee kii u-baa Daafiidee.

english_verse: Solomon also worshiped Astarte the goddess of Sidon, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn kíǹ ki tòotī Siidɔn yab waal Asitaartee, nì Amɔn yab timbiiliwaal Miilkɔm.

english_verse: Solomon's father had obeyed the Lord with all his heart, but Solomon disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn ŋá tin kaa nìn kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, di sá yii waa nìn nóó ti-Dindaan nì dipɔbil diba kii u-baa Daafiidee.

english_verse: Solomon built shrines on a hill east of Jerusalem to worship Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Molech the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Áli gba Saloomɔn máń kuwaadii dijool din bí ki bíitiǹ Jeerusaleemee ki tīī Moowaab yab timbiiliwaal Keemoosi nì Amɔn yab timbiiliwaal Mooleeki.

english_verse: In fact, he built a shrine for each of his foreign wives, so all of them could burn incense and offer sacrifices to their own gods.
translation_verse: U nìn pée ŋá míǹ ní ki tīī u-nicannimpoobi kɔkɔ. Bi nìn tùutī talaalub ki kù tiwaŋkuti ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì bi-waaŋi.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel had appeared to Solomon two times and warned him not to worship foreign gods. But Solomon disobeyed and did it anyway. This made the Lord very angry,
translation_verse: U nìn kpáafì-u ú taa nóó awaayee, ama Saloomɔn kaa nìn ŋá kii Unimbɔti nín nìn kpáafì-u puee.

english_verse: and he said to Solomon: You did what you wanted and not what I told you to do. Now I'm going to take your kingdom from you and give it to one of your officials.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Saloomɔn yii: «A nín ŋá pu ní ki ŋá míǹ kaa ŋúb́ m-poondi nì m-marab bin m tīī-see, m làá fōō dibeel a-ŋaan, ní kí dū-dì kí tīī a-tɔntɔnliibi kansikin ubɔ.

english_verse: But because David was your father, you will remain king as long as you live. I will wait until your son becomes king, then I will take the kingdom from him.
translation_verse: Ama a-baa Daafiidi puee, maa làá ŋá m nín bí yii m làá ŋá puee a-maŋfal wiiŋyi poon. M làá dāá fōō dibeel a-jipɔɔn ŋaan ní.

english_verse: When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city. Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Ama maa làá fōō dibeel kɔkɔ, Daafiidi m-tɔntɔnliu pu nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin m lēēyee puee, m làá kíń kunaakoou kubɔ kí tīī a-jipɔɔn.» Saloomɔn pulincɔntiibi

english_verse: Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì ueedoomja Adaadi, u sá Eedoom yab beecindin ubɔee yíkì ki bíi jáà nì Saloomɔn.

english_verse: Some time earlier, when David conquered the nation of Edom, Joab his army commander went there to bury those who had died in battle. Joab and his soldiers stayed in Edom six months, and during that time they killed every man and boy who lived there.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Joowaab nì Isirayeel yab bin nìn táá-uee nìn kāl̀ Eedoom tiŋkin iŋmal iluu ní áli ki dāa kūū ki céetì bi-ninjab nì bi-bininjabiyaamu kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
translation_verse: Tapaneesi naal màl̄ Adaadi kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Geenubaati. Tapaneesi nìn yāntì kì bí dibeecindi ubɔti biyaamu kansikin ní u kpēē-kì.

english_verse: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
translation_verse: Adaadi bí Eejipiti mimmee ní ki gbìl̄ yii Daafiidi kpíì, ní ujanjakpil Joowaab mun kpíì. Niinee ní u bí Faaroo yii: «Yàntī ḿ nīn gítí m-tiŋkin.»

english_verse: “Why?” asked the king. “Do you want something I haven't given you?” “No, I just want to go home.” Rezon Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Ní Faaroo bālifì-u yii: «Ba di lóò-si m-cee doo ní a nyàab̀ kí nīn gítí a-tiŋkin?» Ní u kíí yii: «Tiba kaa lóò-mi, sii dee yàntī ḿ nín cá.»

english_verse: Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon: Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn gíti yāntì Eeliyadaa jipɔɔn Reesɔn jáń nì Saloomɔn. Reesɔn gbanti nìn sáǹ u-kpiliu Adadeeseer, Sooba bɔtiu ní.

english_verse: He formed his own small army and became its leader after David had defeated Hadadezer's troops. Then Rezon and his army went to Damascus, where he became the ruler of Syria and an enemy of Israel. Both Hadad and Rezon were enemies of Israel while Solomon was king, and they caused him a lot of trouble. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jeroboam
translation_verse: Saloomɔn maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, Reesɔn nìn pée sá Isirayeel nannanliu ní, ní kí nín kūtì inikpiti in Adaadi nìn ŋá Isirayeel yabee. U nìn jíń dibeel Aram tiŋkin ní u-nimbil kaa nìn pée là kí wāl̀ Isirayeel yab. Jeerooboowaam yíkìi jáń nì Saloomɔn (

english_verse: Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon.
translation_verse: Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn sá Eefiraayiim naakookun ní ki kóò Seereeda. U-na nìn sá ukpiipu ní bi yíì-u yii Seeruya. U nìn sá Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliu ní ki yíkìi bíi jáà nì ubɔti.

english_verse: Here is how it happened: While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls,
translation_verse: Kun pu u nìn yíkì ki bíi jáà nì ubɔtee sɔ̀. Saloomɔn nìn bíi māā Miiloo diiku ní ki yāntì bi ŋéeb́ mbùń ŋun nìn bí u-baa Daafiidi Tiŋki gundi puee.

english_verse: Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Jeerooboowaam gbanti nìn dáá sá kinaacimpɔmbiki ki cáá difaŋgiil ki ŋūǹ ditundi tiŋan. Saloomɔn nìn ká yii u tūǹ ditundi tiŋan ní u lēē-u ú nīn kpèé Eefiraayiim nì Manasee naakɔti tɔntɔnliibi.

english_verse: But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
translation_verse: M-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin m lēē Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ kansikinee puee, m làá pée kíń-u kunaakɔbambaantiiu ní.

english_verse: “Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
translation_verse: M làá ŋá míǹ kun puee Isirayeel yab dū-mi ki fá, ní ki cūtìi bíi jáaḿ Siidɔn yab waal Asitaartee nì Moowaab yab waal Keemoosi nì Amɔn yab waal Miilkɔm. Baa nóó m-saŋŋu kí nīn ŋáań tin kítì m-nimbiinee, kaa tí ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-koobiliŋ kii u-baa Daafiidee.

english_verse: “Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee maa làá fōō dibeel Saloomɔn ŋaan, di sá yii m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi un m lēē ní u nìn ŋúb́ m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋee puee, m dū-u ki kāaǹ ú nīn sá ubɔti u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon ní.

english_verse: Then I will give you ten tribes to rule,
translation_verse: Ama m làá fōō dibeel u-jipɔɔn ŋaan ní kí dū tinaakɔti saalaa kí tīī-si.

english_verse: but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: M làá kíń u-jipɔɔn kunaakoou kubɔ. Mimmee m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi làá nīn pée cáá naantiiu ubɔ kā dibeel pu Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Di sá yii kitiŋ kin ní m lēē kí nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkèe dee.

english_verse: “You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want.
translation_verse: Siiyee, m làá tīī-si dibeel kii a nín là puee. A làá jī Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel.

english_verse: I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
translation_verse: A yaa pílifì tin ní m làá tùkù-see, ki yaa nóó m-saŋŋu, ki yaa ŋáań tin kítèe m-nimbiin, ki ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab kii m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi nín nìn ŋúb́ puee, m làá nīn bí a-cee, ní kí yàntī a-kpátam boonee, a-naantiibi ń nīn pée kā dibeel kii Daafiidi yab nín bí puee. M làá dū Isirayeel tiŋki kí ŋá a-ŋaan.

english_verse: “I will punish the descendants of David, but not forever.”
translation_verse: M làá dáaĺ Daafiidi naantiibi tafal, ama maa làá dáaĺ bi-tafal kí nīn cá jaanjaan.>»

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom.
translation_verse: Bi ŋmàn̄ Saloomɔn maam, tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u-ciiŋyi bɔti kɔkɔ ki ŋá Saloomɔn Tuuŋŋi Gbɔŋku poon.

english_verse: he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-naanjab ní bi síb́-u u-baa Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Rooboowaam di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Ama ní bi tú binib bi cūtìi yíiń-u. U bāańee ní u nì Isirayeel beel samaau kɔkɔ bí Rooboowaam yii:

english_verse: “Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Nín̄ cámaan, iwiin ita dalee ní fàtīí gítiń.» U lī mimmee ní samaa nín cá.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Rooboowaam bālifì bitindaŋkpilib bin nìn bí u-baa Saloomɔn tundin ŋyunti ŋun u nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee yii: «Ni sáŋkí-mi ḿ kíí binib nee yii ba?»

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Ní bikpilibee bí-u yii: «Díǹ nee, a yaa kíí kí nīn sá binib nee tɔntɔnliu ní ki kíí-bi kinyɔɔmɔɔyee, bi làá nīn sá a-tɔntɔnliibi kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Ama ní Rooboowaam kaa dū bikpilibee saŋkii ki túń ditundi, ní ki yíiń binipɔmbi u nì bin jíń tinaacimpɔn dicilpu bi bí u-tundinee.

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: U nìn bí bíǹ yii: «Nimbi fáà, ni sáŋkí-mi yii ba? Ḿ kíí binib bin bíi bàlifī-mi ḿ bàtī diwaŋgul din m-baa nìn dūu túǹ-bee nyiŋfiŋu pu yii ba?»

english_verse: He spoke bluntly and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: Binipɔmbee nín nìn sáŋkì-u puee, míǹ ní u dūu sòon̄ nì binibee. U bí-bi yii: «M-baa yaa nìn túǹ-ni diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, man làá gíti kūtì diwaŋgul gbanti nyiŋfiŋu pu. M-baa nìn dū anaalab ní ki dáaĺ ni-tafal, mamee, m làá dū anaalab ŋin cáá agatee ní kí dáaĺ ni-tafal.»

english_verse: When the Israelites heard that Jeroboam was back, they called everyone together. Then they sent for Jeroboam and made him king of Israel. Only the people from the tribe of Judah remained loyal to David's family. Shemaiah Warns Rehoboam (
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ kóò ŋgan pú beelinee gbìl̄ yii Jeerooboowaam fātìi gítìńee, ní bi kóoǹ samaa kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki tú ki yíiń-u ní ki dū-u ki kāaǹ bi-pu ubɔti. Juuda naakooku baba yab di nìn pée síl̀ nì Daafiidi dicaŋku deedee.

english_verse: After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and take control of the whole country. So he called together
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Rooboowaam bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee ní u kóoǹ Juuda nì Beenjameen naakɔti janjaliibi bimɔmmɔntiibi kutukub imuŋku ili nì saalaa ki kpáfì kí cùú já nì Isirayeel yab, án nín làá ŋá pu úǹ Saloomɔn jipɔɔn ń fàtīí fōō dibeelee.

english_verse: Meanwhile, God told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Ama ní Unimbɔti bí u-bɔnaatiliu Seemaya yii:

english_verse: to give Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin this warning:
translation_verse: «Tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Rooboowaam, Saloomɔn jipɔɔn nì Juuda nì Beenjameen naakɔtin yab nì samaa un kɔkɔ pée kíǹee yii,

english_verse: “Don't go to war against the people from Israel—they are your relatives. Go home! I am the Lord, and I made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord and went home. Jeroboam Makes Religious Changes
translation_verse: ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Naa máaǹ kí cùú já nì ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab. Báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-dumpu, di sá yii man di yāntì tin bíi jītí nee bāań.>» Niinee ní bi gbìl̄ ki tīī nì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi ní ki nín gítí bi-dumpui.

english_verse: Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in Ephraim and made it a stronger town, then he moved there. He also fortified the town of Penuel.
translation_verse: Jeerooboowaam nìn máń digundi ki tú Siikeem tiŋki kin bí Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee, ki kíǹ ki kóò niin. Boonee ní u dāa yíkì niin ki cūtìi máń digundi ki tú Peenuyeel tiŋki. Jeerooboowaam kpitii

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii binib nee yaa gbíntìi cáà Jeerusaleem ki ŋáań saraabi ti-Dindaan Diikunee, bi-pɔbiliŋ làá fàtīí gítí bi-kpiliu Juuda bɔtiu Rooboowaam cee. Bi làá dāá kpɔ̀-mi ní kí fàtīí gítí Juuda bɔtiu Rooboowaam cee.»

english_verse: Jeroboam asked for advice and then made two gold statues of calves. He showed them to the people and said, “Listen everyone! You won't have to go to Jerusalem to worship anymore. Here are your gods who rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Jeerooboowaam ká nlandɔkɔ ní ki yāntì bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́-u anabil ali, ní u bí samaa yii: «Ni jɔ́m̀ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ki gīī Isirayeel yab, kpèèmaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee.»

english_verse: Then he put one of the gold calves in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan.
translation_verse: U ŋá mimmee ní ki dū dinabil diba ki síiǹ Beeteel tiŋkin ní ki dū din kíǹee ki síiǹ Daani tiŋkin.

english_verse: The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
translation_verse: U nín ŋá pu ki yāntì samaa ŋá ikpitee dee. Di sá yii binib tikpil nìn pá dinabililiitiil boon ki tin bàn̄ Daani tiŋkin.

english_verse: Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests.
translation_verse: Jeerooboowaam nìn gíti yāntì bi máń awaadiin ŋgbantamu pu, ní ki nìn lēē bin kaa sá Leefii yabee bí nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibi.

english_verse: He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
translation_verse: Dibindi poon ŋmaniniitiu, iwiin saalku dalee ní u yíiń samaa kɔkɔ bí jī jiŋaal Beeteel. Ŋwiin gbantee, úǹ di gāā u-bindi ki lēē-ŋu. Jiŋaal gbanti yuntiŋuee, úǹ u-ba di nìn pée ŋá saraa nsaraafan ŋun u nìn yāntì bi máńee pu.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted: The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
translation_verse: U bāańee ní ki sòon̄ ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi nee ki tɔ́ nsaraafan pu yii: «Nsaraafan! Nsaraafan! Pīlifì tin ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹee! Bi làá dāá màal̀ kibininjabiki kiba Daafiidi dicaŋkun. Bi làá dāá pɔ̄-kì diyindi yii Joosiyaasi. U làá dāá kpɔ̀ ŋgbantamu pu saraaŋaliibi bin tùutī a-pu talaalutuukaabee kí ŋá saraa a-pu. Bi làá dāá dū anikpab kí páań a-pu kí wà ŋŋmi.»

english_verse: You will know that the Lord has said these things when the altar splits in half, and the ashes on it fall to the ground.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti mbaantee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee gíti lī yii: «Kudaaŋŋu kun ti-Dindaan tīīyee sɔ̀. Nsaraafan làá wīī, ní ŋkpam min pá ŋu-puee ń lítí kitiŋ.»

english_verse: Jeroboam pointed at the prophet and shouted, “Grab him!” But at once, Jeroboam's hand became stiff, and he could not move it.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ubɔti gbìl̄ tin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee sòon̄ ki tɔ́ Beeteel saraafaŋŋuee puee, ní u tāntì u-ŋal nsaraafan pu ki bí yii: «Cúúmaan-u!» Ama ní u-ŋal ŋun u tāntèe dūu fáká, waa ti ŋúń ki gúkúǹ-ŋu.

english_verse: The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
translation_verse: Dibòol pu niin niin ní nsaraafan wīī ní ŋkpam min pá ŋu-puee lítì kitiŋ kii Unimbɔti nín bàà yāntì u-bɔnaatiliu sòon̄ puee.

english_verse: “Please pray to the Lord your God and ask him to heal my hand,” Jeroboam begged. The prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti bí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee yii: «M gbàam̄-si, mèè ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ú dū m-kpitii kí pɔ̄-mi kí cáaǹ m-ŋal kí tīī-mi.» Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee nìn mēē ti-Dindaan ní ubɔti ŋal fātìi ŋáŋkì ki gítì kii ŋu nín nìn bí puee.

english_verse: “Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti bí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee yii: «Dāan̄ tí cù man dumpu á jī tijin, ḿ kpáàa pɔ̄-si tiba.»

english_verse: “No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either.
translation_verse: Ama ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee bí ubɔti yii: «Báà a yaa yākatì a-gaajawanti mili ki dū dijandi ki tīī-mi, maa làá kɔ́ a-dumpuɔɔɔ, kaa làá jī tijinaaa, kaa làá nyɔ̀ nnyim mpaan nee pu.

english_verse: The Lord said I can't eat or drink anything and that I can't go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nín tùkū-mi puee dee yii: <A taa jī tibaaa, kí taa nyɔ̀ tibaaa, kí taa fàtīí dī nsan ŋun pu a dī ki cūtèe kí gítiń.>»

english_verse: At that time an old prophet lived in Bethel, and one of his sons told him what the prophet from Judah had said and done.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ nìn kóò Beeteel tiŋkin ki púĺ. U-jipɔmbi nìn dɔ́miń ki máafì-u tin kɔkɔ ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee ŋá ŋwiin gbanti Beeteel tiŋkin nì tin u tùkū ubɔtee.

english_verse: “Show me which way he went,” the old prophet said, and his sons pointed out the road.
translation_verse: Niinee bi-baa bālifì-bi yii: «Nsan ŋulɔŋu ní u dī ki nín gítí?» Ní u-jipɔmbi dàkā-u nsan ŋun Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu un nyánní Juuda tiŋkin ki dɔ́mińee dēe.

english_verse: “Put a saddle on my donkey,” he told them. After they did, he got on the donkey
translation_verse: Ní u bí u-jipɔmbi yii: «Kpàl̄maan m-maŋki kí tīī-mi.» Ní u-jipɔmbee kpàl̄ kimaŋ ki tīī-u ní u máĺ ki kāl̀ ki-pu.

english_verse: and rode off to look for the prophet from Judah. The old prophet found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the prophet from Judah?” “Yes, I am.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní u nín jì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee boon ní ki tin ká-u u kā teereebinti subu bubɔ taapu, ní u bālifì-u yii: «Sii di sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu un nyánní Juuda tiŋkineeee?» Ní u kíí yii: «An sá man.»

english_verse: “Come home with me,” the old prophet said, “and have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu un kóò Beeteelee bí-u yii: «Dāan̄ tí cù man dumpu á ká tiba kí jī.»

english_verse: “I can't go back with you,” the prophet replied, “and I can't eat or drink anything with you.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí-u yii: «Maa ŋūǹ kí táá-si kí gítáaa, kaa tí máaǹ kí jī tijinaaa, kí nyɔ̀ tiba doo.

english_verse: The Lord warned me not to eat or drink or to go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: <A taa jī tibaaa, kí taa nyɔ̀ tibaaa, kí taa fàtīí dī nsan ŋun pu a dī ki cūtèe kí gítiń.>»

english_verse: The old prophet said, “I'm a prophet too. One of the Lord's angels told me to take you to my house and give you something to eat and drink.” The prophet from Judah did not know that the old prophet was lying,
translation_verse: Ama ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu utikpilee bí-u yii: «Ma mun sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu kii siiyee ní. Ntuun ŋubɔ di dɔ́miń ki dū ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi nee ki tùkū-mi yii ḿ fàtīí gíiǹní-si á jī tijin kí nyɔ̀ nnyim.» Ama Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu utikpilee nìn bíi mɔ́ntí-u ní.

english_verse: During the meal the Lord gave the old prophet
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi-liitil kā ki jīǹee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu un fātìi gíiǹní un béeyee.

english_verse: a message for the prophet from Judah: Listen to the Lord's message. You have disobeyed the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Niinee ní úǹ dūu nāatì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu un nyánní Juuda tiŋkinee. U nìn bí-u yii: «A yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan. Aa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu marau un u tīī-see.

english_verse: He told you not to eat or drink anything here, but you came home and ate with me. And so, when you die, your body won't be buried in your family tomb.
translation_verse: A gítìń Beeteel ki jíń tijin ki nyùn̄ nnyim. Ama ti-Dindaan mun nìn bí-si yii a taa ŋá míǹ. A nín ŋá mimmee puee, a làá kpú ní baa làá síb́-si a-naanjab kaakulin.>»

english_verse: After the meal the old prophet got a donkey ready,
translation_verse: Bi jíń ki nyùn̄ ki dóòyee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu utikpilee kpàl̄ u-maŋki ki tīī Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu un u fātìi gíiǹnée

english_verse: and the prophet from Judah left. Along the way, a lion attacked and killed him, and the donkey and the lion stood there beside his dead body.
translation_verse: ní u nín cá. U cée ní gbikinti ubɔ kíntì-u nsanni ki kūū-u. U nìn dɔ̄ nsanni ní kimaŋ nì gbikintee yú ki kɔ́ĺ-u.

english_verse: Some people walked by and saw the body with the lion standing there. They ran into Bethel, telling everyone what they had seen.
translation_verse: Bisanjitiliibi nìn ká dinikpilee dɔ̄ nsanni gbikinti yú ki kɔ́ĺ, ní bi dɔ́miń ki dū tibɔtee ki máafì kitiŋin, laakin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu utikpilee nìn kóòyee.

english_verse: When the old prophet heard the news, he said, “That must be the prophet from Judah. The Lord warned him, but he disobeyed. So the Lord sent a lion to kill him.”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu un nìn cūtì ki gíiǹní-uee nín gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní u bí yii: «Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu un nyánní Juuda tiŋkinee dee, úǹ di yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan maraauee. Ti-Dindaan dū-u ki tīī gbikinti ní u cúú-u ki kūū, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū-u puee.»

english_verse: The old prophet told his sons to saddle his donkey, and when it was ready,
translation_verse: U lī mimmee ní ki bí u-jipɔmbi yii: «Kpàl̄maan-mi kimaŋ!» Ŋyunti ŋun bi kpàl̄ kimaŋ ki dóòyee,

english_verse: he left. He found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and lion standing there. The lion had not eaten the body or attacked the donkey.
translation_verse: ní u nín cá ki bàn̄ ki ká dinikpilee dɔ̄ nsanni, kimaŋ nì gbikinti yú ki kɔ́ĺ. Gbikintee kaa nìn ŋmɔ́ dinikpileeyaaa, kaa ŋá kimaŋ mun tiba.

english_verse: The old prophet picked up the body, put it on his own donkey, and took it back to Bethel, so he could bury it and mourn for the prophet from Judah.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu utikpilee yōoǹ dinikpilee ki dūu páaǹ kimaŋ pu ki gíiǹní Beeteel. U nìn súń u-kpool, ní ki síb́-u.

english_verse: He buried the body in his own family tomb and cried for the prophet.
translation_verse: U nìn dū-u ki ŋá úǹ u-ba kaakulin, ní ki gāā nlan yii: «Áù, m-nabiki kpíì!» ki súń u-kpool.

english_verse: I'm sure that everything he said about the altar in Bethel and the shrines in Samaria will happen.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan bɔti tin u dī u-pu ki sòon̄ ki tɔ́ Beeteel saraafaŋŋu pu nì awaadiin ŋin bí ŋgbantamu pu Samaarii timmunee làá lafun ŋá míǹ.»

english_verse: But Jeroboam kept on doing evil things. He appointed men to be priests at the local shrines, even if they were not Levites. In fact, anyone who wanted to be a priest could be one.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Jeerooboowaam kaa nìn fá u-bimbikpitim. U nìn gbíntìi nìkì ki lèekī binib samaa kansikin ki kàantí-bi bisaraaŋaliibi ŋgbantamu pu. Ubɔ yaa nìn lèe, u nìn bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī udaan yil pu ní kí kàan̄-u ú nīn sá usaraaŋal ŋgbantamu pu waadiiŋŋin.

english_verse: She got ready and left for Ahijah's house in Shiloh. Ahijah was now old and blind,
translation_verse: Ní Jeerooboowaam nimpuu lafun ŋá míǹ. U nìn yíkì ki nín cá Abiiya dumpu. Too, tiputi puee, Abiiya kaa nìn gíti wāĺ.

english_verse: But when Ahijah heard her walking up to the door, he said: Come in! I know you're Jeroboam's wife—why are you pretending to be someone else? I have some bad news for you.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Abiiya gbìl̄ u-taaŋi pu u bāań kipunyɔkɔpuee ní u bí yii: «Jeerooboowaam nimpuu, kɔ́nní! Ba pu ní a kpántì a-ba bí taa béé-si? Tin m cáá kí tùkù-see gba kaa sá tibɔmɔntiil.

english_verse: Give your husband this message from the Lord God of Israel: “Jeroboam, you know that I, the Lord, chose you over anyone else to be the leader of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Nín̄ gítí kí tùkù Jeerooboowaam yii ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bí-u yii: <Man di lēē-si samaa kansikin ki dū-si ki kāaǹ m-nibul Isirayeel pu ubɔti.

english_verse: I even took David's kingdom away from his family and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He always obeyed me and did what was right.
translation_verse: M fōō Daafiidi dicaŋkun dibeel ki dūu tīī-si, ama aa dī m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi un nìn ŋúb́ m-marab, ki nóó-mi nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔ, ki ŋáań tin kítì m-nimbiinee tabɔbiliŋ.

english_verse: “You have made me very angry by rejecting me and making idols out of gold. Jeroboam, you have done more evil things than any king before you.
translation_verse: A gíti ŋá ikpiti ki jítiǹ bin līntiǹ-see kɔkɔ. A mɔ́ɔ́ awaa ki gbítì m-ŋuul ní ki fātì a-boon ki tīī-mi.

english_verse: “Because of this, I will destroy your family by killing every man and boy in it, whether slave or free. I will wipe out your family, just as fire burns up trash.
translation_verse: An puee m làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ a-dicaŋku pu. M làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí a-dicaŋkun iyumbu nì bin tɔ́ bi-ba ki sá bininjab ki bí Isirayeel tiŋkinee. M làá nàan̄ a-naantiibi kii bi nín ŋàtī timool puee ní.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel will mourn at his funeral. But he will be the last one from Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial, because he's the only one the Lord God of Israel is pleased with.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ làá kàl̄ ki-kpool ní kí síb́-kì, di sá yii Jeerooboowaam dicaŋkunee, un baba bi làá pée ŋmā kí síb́ee dee. Jeerooboowaam dicaŋkunee, un baba bɔti fáatiǹ ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiuee dee.

english_verse: The Lord will soon choose a new king of Israel, who will destroy Jeroboam's family. And I mean very soon.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá kàan̄ ubɔtipɔɔn ubɔ Isirayeel tiŋki pu. Úǹ di làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Jeerooboowaam dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ. Díǹ gba ní an sá. M bí yii an sá kɔŋkɔnnee bɔti ní!

english_verse: The people of Israel have made the Lord angry by setting up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. So the Lord will punish them until they shake like grass in a stream. He will take them out of the land he gave to their ancestors, then scatter them as far away as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dáaĺ Isirayeel yab tafal. Bi-wunti làá dāá nīn jìkì kii tikati tin sí nnyiminee nín jìkì puee ní. U làá dāá fùkù Isirayeel yab kí nyāntí kitimmɔntii kin u nìn dūu tīī bi-naanjabee poon ní kí cáá-bi kí yàl̄ Babiloon mɔɔl Eefiraati gbandi lapu pu yal, kun puee bi kpítì idɔcɔbikaa ki gbítì ti-Dindaan ŋuul.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jeerooboowaam nimpuu yíkì ki nín kùǹ ki tin bàn̄ Tiirsa tiŋkin. U nín pée dū u-taal ki tāā u-cindee ní u-bikee sīntì.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said. Jeroboam Dies
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn síb́-kì ní ki súń ki-kpool kii ti-Dindaan nín dī u-bɔnaatiliu Abiiya pu ki lī pu ki síiǹee.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including the battles he won, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Jeerooboowaam tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, u nín jáń tijáti nì u nín jíń dibeel puee bɔti kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔnti poon.

english_verse: The people of Judah disobeyed the Lord and made him even angrier than their ancestors had.
translation_verse: Juuda yab nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Bi nìn ŋá ikpiti ki gbítì u-ŋuul ki jítiǹ bi-naanjab nín nìn ŋá puee.

english_verse: They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Bi mun nìn máń awaadiin ŋgbantamu pu, ki cóoǹ ataŋkpee nì idɔ in pu bi cɔ̀b̀ ticɔbikaalee ŋgbantamu pu nì isuboon kɔkɔ taapu.

english_verse: Even worse, they allowed prostitutes at the shrines, and followed the disgusting customs of the foreign nations that the Lord had forced out of Canaan.
translation_verse: Bininjab nì binimpoobi nìn bí niin gba ki ŋáań alaakpaatuun ki jáaḿ awaa. Atimbun ŋin ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ki fōō bi-timmu ki tīī Isirayeel yabee nín nìn ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔee, míǹ deedee ní bi mun nìn ŋáań.

english_verse: After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Rooboowaam nín kāl̀ dibeel dibiŋŋmooŋmootiil poonee ní Eejipiti bɔtiu Siisaaki dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Rooboowaam dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ agbampɔɔ ki téeǹ ŋin bi yōoǹee pu, ní ki dū-ŋi ki ŋá bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔti naakooku punyɔmmuee kpiliu ŋaan ú nīn kpèé.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he was finished.
translation_verse: Ubɔti yaa nìn pée yíkì ki kóò kunimbɔtidiinee, bijanjaliibi nìn yòontí agbampɔɔ gbanti ní ki līī ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-ŋi.

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Atuun ŋin kɔkɔ Rooboowaam nìn túńee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: He and Jeroboam were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Kujaau nìn pée bí Rooboowaam nì Jeerooboowaam kansikin ní kaa gbèentí.

english_verse: Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_verse: Rooboowaam kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u u-baabi kaakulin Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-na nìn sá uamɔnnimpu ní bi yíì-u yii Naama. Rooboowaam jipɔɔn Abiyaam di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: U nìn lēē u-na Maaka tinimpubɔtiilin, kun puee u nìn kpítì diwaal ki nántiǹ ntimbiil waal Aseera. Asaa nìn gāā diwaalee ki lúkú ní ki cáá-dì ki cūnnì Seedrɔn buŋgbandi ki tūū ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Asaa yíiń Juuda yab kɔkɔ kaa gāntì báà ubɔ. U nìn yāntì bi cáań ataŋkpee nì idɔ in Bayeesa nìn cáa bíi māā Raama gundee. Ubɔti Asaa nìn yāntì bi dū ataŋkpee nì idɔ gbanti ki máń digundi ki tú Beenjameen tiŋki Geeba nì Miisipa timmu.

english_verse: Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam.
translation_verse: U nìn pée ŋá ikpitibaanti in u-baa nìn ŋée ní. U-pɔbil kaa nìn bí diba nì ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu kii u-naanja Daafiidee.

english_verse: David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Daafiidi nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee, ní u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, waa nìn fātì u-boon ki tīī tin u nìn kpáafì-uee, see ueetija Urii bɔtee baba.

english_verse: The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king. Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Abiyaam tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ u túńee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔntin. Kujaau nìn pée tí bí u nì Jeerooboowaam kansikin ní.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Abiyaam kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabee ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Asaa di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Juuda bɔtiu Asaa bɔti (Kpèè

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: U nìn cáań ti-Dindaan Diikun tin kɔkɔ ní úǹ u-ba nì u-baa nìn dūu sú Unimbɔtee, an dàkà yii animbil nì sindaariya nì asambil.

english_verse: Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel.
translation_verse: Kujaau nìn pée bí Asaa nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Bayeesa kansikin ní.

english_verse: Asa obeyed the Lord, as David had done.
translation_verse: Asaa nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee, kii u-naanja Daafiidee.

english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
translation_verse: Jeerooboowaam nín kāl̀ Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel abin mmuŋku poonee, ní Asaa kpántì Juuda bɔtiu.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: U nìn jìn̄ bininjab nì binimpoobi bin nìn bí awaadiinni ki ŋáań alaakpaatuunee, ní ki kúntì awaa ŋin u-naanjab nìn mɔ́ɔ́yee.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Ama waa nìn kúntì laakin bi tòotī awaa ŋgbantamu puee. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Asaa maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, u-pɔbil nìn bí diba nì ti-Dindaan ní.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔtiu Bayeesa dɔ́miń dalba kí já nì Juuda tiŋki, ní ki máń digundi ki tú Raama timbiliiki kí pìin̄ Juuda bɔtiu Asaa nsan.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Niinee ní Asaa kɔ́tì animbil nì sindaariya un kɔkɔ nìn bí kunimbɔtidii nimbikpaafidiikun nì ubɔti nimbikpaafidiikunee ki tīī u-tɔntɔnliibi bí cáá cùnnì Damaasi kí tīī Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi, Tabirimɔn jipɔɔn nì Eesiyɔn naantiiu. U nìn bí bí tùkù-u yii:

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: «Yàntī mpèé ń nīn bí man nì sii kansikin kii an nín nìn bí man baa nì sii baa kansikin puee. Kpèè animbil nì sindaariya ní m dūu tú bí cáań kí tīī-si nee. Míǹ puee cùú kpìtī mpèé ŋun bí si nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Bayeesa kansikinee ú taa ti dāan̄ kí já nì mi.»

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Been-Adaadi nìn gbìl̄ ki tīī nì ubɔti Asaa ní ki dū u-janjakpilib ki tú bí cùú já nì Isirayeel timmu. Bi nìn jáń ki fōō Iyɔn nì Daani nì Abeel-Beeti-Maaka timmu nì Kiineereeti tiŋki kɔkɔ nì Neefitalii timmu kɔkɔ.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Bayeesa nín gbìl̄ tibɔti gbantee ní u gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi māā Raama timbiliiki gundi ní ki nín gítí ki cūtìi kāl̀ Tiirsa.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Atuun ŋin kɔkɔ ní Asaa nìn túńee nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam nì ntimu mun u máń agun ki túee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun. Ama u-puti poonee, u nìn búŋkì ní u-taaŋi dūu fàl̄.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Asaa nín kāl̀ dibeel, dibinliliitiil poonee, ní Jeerooboowaam jipɔɔn Nadaab kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu abin ali ní.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. U nìn dī u-baa saŋŋu ní ki nóó u-baa nín nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitin puee tabɔbiliŋ.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: U nín pée kpántì ubɔtee ní u kūū Jeerooboowaam dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ kaa kíǹ báà unibaanti. U nìn kūū ki céetì bi-kɔkɔ ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu usiilooja Ayiiya pu ki sòon̄ puee ní.

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: An nìn jítì míǹ kun puee Jeerooboowaam nìn ŋá ikpiti ní ki yāntì Isirayeel nibul mun ŋá ikpiti, ki gbítì ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ŋuul.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Nadaab tuuŋŋi ŋin u túńee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Asaa maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, kujaau nìn pée bí u nì Bayeesa kansikin ní. Isirayeel bɔtiu Bayeesa bɔti

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
