translation_verse: Asaa nín kpántì Juuda bɔtiu dibintataatiil poonee ní Ayiiya jipɔɔn Bayeesa kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kóò Tiirsa ní ki jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì anaa.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. U nìn dī Jeerooboowaam saŋŋu ní ki nóó u nín nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitin puee tabɔbiliŋ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Ananii jipɔɔn Jeewuu, u-bɔnaatiliu ú tùkù Bayeesa yii:

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: «Aa nìn bí tiban, ama ní m lēē-si ki dū-si ki kāaǹ m-nibul Isirayeel pu ubɔti. Díǹ pu nee, a nóó Jeerooboowaam tabɔbiliŋ, ki yāntì Isirayeel yab ŋá ikpiti ki gbítì m-ŋuul.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: An puee m làá kúntí sii nì a-dicaŋku, m làá ŋá-ni kii m nín ŋá Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam dicaŋku puee ní.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: A-dicaŋkun unil un yaa kpíì kitiŋinee, iboo di làá ŋmɔ́-u, ní un yaa kpíì tisatinee, inoon ń jī u-nanti.»

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Ananii jipɔɔn Jeewuu pu ní ki sòon̄ nì Bayeesa nì u-dicaŋku pu. Di sá yii mpeepeekaamee u nìn yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan. U nìn gbítì ti-Dindaan ŋuul kun puee u nìn ŋá ikpiti kii ubɔti Jeerooboowaam nín nìn ŋá puee ní. Nliliitiimee, u nìn kūū ki céetì Jeerooboowaam dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ. Isirayeel bɔtiu Eela bɔti

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Asaa nín kāl̀ dibeel abin mmuŋku nì aluu poonee ní Bayeesa jipɔɔn Eela kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Tiirsa ní ki jíń dibeel abin ali.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Oomirii nìn ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. U nìn gíti ŋá tin jítiǹ bibɔtiibi bin līntiǹ-uee.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Ama u-janjakpiliu Simrii, ujanjakpil un kpèé janjatɔrɔkubee bɔ́ntì ki jáń nì u. Ubɔti nìn bí Tiirsa tiŋkin un kpèé kubɔtinaakoouee dumpu ki nyù ndaam ki gbéè.

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Niin ní Simrii kɔ́ ki kūū-u. Tíǹ jítì ŋyunti ŋun ní Juuda bɔtiu Asaa jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì aluli poonee ní. Simrii nìn fōō Eela yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: U kpántì ubɔti ki kāl̀ dibɔtijal puee ní ki kūū Bayeesa dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ, waa nìn kíǹ-u uninjaaa, kaa kíǹ-u kinabikaaa, kaa kíǹ-u bɔɔ mun.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: Simrii nìn kūū ki céetì Bayeesa dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Jeewuu pu ki sòon̄ puee ní.

english_verse: Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
translation_verse: An nìn jítì míǹ kun puee Bayeesa nì u-jipɔɔn nìn ŋá ikpiti ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab mun ŋá ikpiti, ki dū bi-waaŋi ki gbítì ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ŋuul.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Eela tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, nì tin u ŋée kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. Isirayeel bɔtiu Simrii bɔti

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Bijanjaliibi bin nìn bíń kujaauee nín gbìl̄ yii Simrii bɔ́ntì ki jáń nì ubɔti ki kpáàa kūū-uee, ní bi ŋá kinyɔɔbaantii dijanjanaapaal pu niin ki lēē ujanjakpil Oomirii ú kpántí Isirayeel bɔtiu.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Niinee Oomirii nì u-janjakitil yíkìń Giibeetɔn ki dɔ́miń ki māntìi tú Tiirsa tiŋki.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Simrii nín ká yii bi ŋman fōō kitiŋ ki dóòyee ní u nín kóò ubɔti dibiki kiban. U nìn gāā ŋŋmi ki tūū ní an wùn̄ ki kūū-u.

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: An nìn jítì míǹ kun puee Simrii nìn ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. U nìn ŋá ikpiti, ki nóó Jeerooboowaam tabɔbiliŋ ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitin.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Simrii tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì u nín bɔ́ntì pu ki kūū ubɔtee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Simrii kúm boonee ní Isirayeel yab cúu yākatì mili: dijandi diba nìn là Giinaati jipɔɔn ń nīn sá ubɔti ní dijandi din kíǹee lēē Oomirii.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Asaa nín jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì diba poonee, ní Oomirii kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì ali ní. U nìn dáá kóò Tiirsa tiŋkin ní ki jíń dibeel abin aluu.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: U nìn pée dī Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam un nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ŋá ikpiti ki dū iwaatooti ki gbítì ti-Dindaan ŋuulee tabɔbiliŋ ní.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Oomirii tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹ u túńee nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: U kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabee ní bi síb́-u Samaarii tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Akaab di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab bɔti

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Asaa nín jíń dibeel abin ali kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní Oomirii jipɔɔn Akaab kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Ama Oomirii jipɔɔn Akaab nìn ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee ki jítiǹ bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ līntiǹ-uee.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: U nín nìn nóó Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam kpitii tabɔbiliŋee kaa bàn̄-uee, ní u gíti cūtìi cáá Siidɔn yab bɔtiu Eetibaal bisal Jeesabeel. U nìn cūtìi bíi gbàantí diwaal Baal nimbiin ki jáaḿ-dì.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: Kudii kun u nìn máń Samaarii tiŋkinee poonee, u nìn máń nsaraafan ki tīī diwaal.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Akaab nìn kpítì ndɔ ŋun pu bi cɔ̀b̀ ticɔbikaalee ki cóoǹ. U nìn gíti ŋá tin jítiǹ mimmee ki gbítì ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ŋuul ki jítiǹ Isirayeel bɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ nìn līntiǹ-uee.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: U-beel yuntiŋu ní ubeeteelja Yiil máń digundi ki tú Jeeriikoo tiŋki. Ama kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa pu ki sòon̄ puee, míǹ ní an nìn jítì. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi gbì kí bíĺ kitiŋee nyeelee ní u-jipɔŋkpiliu Abiiram kpíì, ní ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi cōontí kitiŋee punuubee ní u-jipɔnjoolkaau Seeguub mun kpíì.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ nìn bí bi yíì-u yii Eelii. U nìn sá Tiisbee timbiliikin, Galaadi tiŋkin. U nìn bí ubɔti yii: «Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin m sá u-tɔntɔnliu nee yindi puee, dimalindi àá utaa gíti kpá kí jōō kitiŋ pu abin ŋin làá páanní nee poon, see m yaa láa bí yii dimalindi àá utaa ń nì.» Eelii bí Keeriiti bùmbiki gbandi

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Eelii yii:

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: «Yīkì doo, nín̄ cá ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kí báĺ Keeriiti bùmbiki kin bí Jɔɔdan ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee caŋin.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Mimmee a ŋūǹ kí nīn kāntí nnyim mbunee poon ki nyù. M làá tīī agaliŋgaa mara bí nīn cāabìń-si tijin niin.»

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Agaliŋgaa nìn cāabìń-u tijin nì tinan kutaafaau nì kujoou, ní u nyù kibùmbikee nyim. Eelii cūtì ki kíǹ ki bí Sareepita ukpiipu ubɔ cee

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Ama an dāa bàn̄ ŋyunti ŋubɔee, kibùmbikee nyim fóotì, kun puee utaa kaa nìn gíti nìn̄ kitiŋee pu.

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan bí Eelii yii:

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: «Yīkìm̄, nín̄ cá Sareepita tiŋki kin bí Siidɔn tiŋgbaŋkinee kí nīn kíǹ ki kóò niin. Di sá yii m tīī unimpukpiipu ubɔ niin mara ú kpíiǹ-si.»

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Ní Eelii kíĺ nsan ki nín cá Sareepita. U bàn̄ kí kɔ́ kitiŋee ní ki ká unimpukpiipu ubɔ bíi píikí idɔ. U nìn yíiń-u ki bí-u yii: «M gbàam̄-si ní, cùú jōoń diboolin nnyim fiii kí pɔ̄-mi ḿ nyɔ̀.»

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun unimpuee nín cá kí jōō nnyim kí cáań-uee ní u fātìi yíiń-u ki bí-u yii: «M gbàam̄-si, á kpáàa cáań-mi tijin mun.»

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee kíí-u yii: «Nì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu un bí dimaŋfalin nee puee, m pūtì-si yii maa ŋá tijin tiba ki síiǹ. Kun pée kíǹ-mee di sá ŋyim diŋaaŋkul an kā kulɔŋŋun nì ŋkpam fiii mun kā kibaŋŋin. M nín dɔ́miń ki tōō idɔ nee, m làá kɔ́ ní kí dū tin pée kíǹee kí ŋá tijin man nì m-jipɔɔn tí jī kí nīn kíǹ ki kā ki cí ŋkúm.»

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Ní Eelii bí-u yii: «Taa fàŋkì! Nín̄ cá kí ŋá kii a nín lī puee. Ama dū tin a cááyee kí ŋá tijin fiii kí cáań man kí wàatī. Boonee á ŋá kí tīī sii nì a-jipɔɔn mun.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ŋyim kpá kí lóó kulɔŋŋuee poon, ní ŋkpam mun kpá kí fóotí kibaŋŋee ni kí cáá sāā ŋwiin ŋun ní ti-Dindaan làá yàntī utaa ń nèe.»

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee nín kóò ki ŋá kii Eelii nín bí yii ú ŋá puee. An ŋá mimmee ní úǹ nì Eelii nì u-jipɔɔn ká ki jíń iwiin kupaau.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Ŋyim kaa nìn dóò kulɔŋŋun ní ŋkpam mun kaa fóotì kibaŋŋin, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī Eelii pu ki sòon̄ puee. Eelii fīkitì unimpukpiipuee jipɔɔn

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Míǹ boon an kaa yúntì ní unimpukpiipu un fōō Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eelii u-dumpuee jipɔɔn búŋkì. U-weeŋyee nìn pɔ́ɔkì áli u dāa lántì dimaŋfal.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee bí Eelii yii: «Unimbɔti niliu, ba pu ní a ŋá-mi míǹ? A dɔ́miń kí téetí Unimbɔti ikpiti in ní m ŋée kí kpɔ̀ m-jipɔɔn níii?»

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Ní Eelii kíí-u yii: «Cáań-mi a-jipɔɔn!» U fōō unaacimpɔɔnee unimpuee ŋaan ní ki cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ kudii kun poon u dɔ̀ee aditɔntɔkɔ yilpu, ní ki dū-u ki bíl̀ u-lambaŋki pu.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u mēē Unimbɔti mpɔn ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu, mimmee a là kí kɔ́ǹ unimpukpiipu un pu m kóò nee dinimbinaamandin ki kūū u-jipɔɔnaaa?»

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Eelii lī mimmee ní ki dōoǹ kibikee pu ŋfunyɔm mita, ní ki mēē ti-Dindaan yii: «Ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu, gíiǹ kibiki nee fooku kí ŋá ki-ni.»

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn fōō Eelii wimmeem ní ki gíiǹ kibikee fooku ki tīī-kì, ní kì kíĺ ki bíi fòotī.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Eelii yōoǹ kibikee ki nyáń u-diikun ki kpákatì, ní ki dū-kì ki tīī ki-na ki lī yii: «Kpèè, a-jipɔɔn bí dimaŋfalin.»

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee bí Eelii yii: «Tiŋman, m béè kɔŋkɔnnee yii a lafun sá Unimbɔti niliu, ní tin ti-Dindaan dì a-pu ki sòoǹee mun sá mbaamɔn.»

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ŋyunti ŋun Jeesabeel nìn yāntì bi kūū ti-Dindaan bɔnaatiliibee, Oobadiya nìn fīī bi-kansikin dilaataal ní. U nìn kpáfì-bi akiti ali pu ní dikitil kamaa cáá binib imuŋku ili nì saalaa ní ki nìn dū-bi ki bál̀ itaŋkpalɔkɔ ili poon. U nìn tìì-bi tijin bi jīǹ nì nnyim bi nyù. -

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Akaab bí Oobadiya yii: «Yàntī tí cù kí kpèè inyimbul nì ibun kɔkɔn ti yaa kāntí timool kí cáań kí tīī itaamu nì imamboon í taa kpú. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, ti làá dāá kpɔ̀ ti-waŋkuti.»

english_verse: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi sòon̄ ki bɔ́ntì báà ŋma nín làá túĺ laakiŋyee. Akaab nìn túĺ laaba pú ní Oobadiya mun dūu túĺ laaba pú.

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Oobadiya tàkā u-saŋŋu ki cée, u bí yii ú kpèèyee, Eelii dee. Oobadiya béè-uee ní ki tātìi dōoǹ u-nimbiin dicincibil ní ki bí yii: «Sii ní an lafun sáa, m-dindaan Eelii?»

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Ní Oobadiya bí yii: «Tikpitil tilati ní m ŋá ní a là kí dū man a-tɔntɔnliu kí ŋá Akaab ŋaan ú kpɔ̀-mi ní?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: M pūtì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu un bí dimaŋfalin nee yii ditimbundi àá dibeel diba kaa kíǹ m-kpiliu Akaab kaa tú binib bí nyàab̀-si. Ditimbundi àá dibeel diba nib yaa bí yii baa ká-see, see ubɔti ń gíti yàntī bí pùtī yii baa lafun ká-si.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Ní kɔŋkɔnnee, sii bíi lì yii ḿ cùú tùkù m-kpiliu yii: <Eelii dòońaa!>

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Ama m yíkí a-cee doo kí cùú tùkù Akaab yii a dòońee ní ti-Dindaan Fam ń yòon̄-si kí cáá búntí laaba, ní u nín dɔ́miń doo kaa ká-see, ní ú kpɔ̀-mi. Man a-tɔntɔnliu mun, doooo m-naacimpɔntin ní m fàŋkí ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Eelii bí-u yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un tundin m bí nee yii díǹ nee gba, m làá cù kí sīĺ Akaab nimbiin.» Eelii dū u-ba ki dàkā Akaab

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Oobadiya nín cá Akaab cee ki dūu máafì-u, ní Akaab nín cá kí tūŋkì Eelii.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Akaab ká Eeliiyee ní u bí-u yii: «Sii un cáań agìń ki tɔ́ Isirayeel yab puee, sii deeee?»

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Akaab tú bi yíiń Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nì bibɔnaatiliibee, ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì Kaarmeel jool pu.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Eelii nìn sútì ki pìl̄ samaa kɔkɔ ní ki bí-bi yii: «Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní ni làá lēē kí nóó nlandɔkɔbaanti ní? Ti-Dindaan di yaa sá Unimbɔti, nín̄ nóómaan-u. Diwaal Baal di yaa tí sá Unimbɔtee, ní nóó-dì!» Ama samaa kansikinee, báà ubɔ kaa nìn wāaǹ kinyɔkɔ ní kaa nín kíí tiba.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Ní tīī-ti inajaa ili: diwaal Baal bɔnaatiliibi ń lēē ubɔ, kí càkà kí dūú páań idɔ pu kí ŋá saraa, ama bí taa kpāā ŋŋmi. Ma mun làá yòon̄ unaja un kíǹee kí bɔ́ntí kí páań idɔ pu, ma mun kaa làá kpāā ŋŋmi.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Boonee bí mèè bi-waal ní ma mun ḿ mèè ti-Dindaan. Un Nimbɔtiu yaa kíí ki yāntì ŋŋmi fōō saraayee di lafun sá Unimbɔti.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ kíí yii: «Ti kíí míǹ.»

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Eelii bí diwaal Baal bɔnaatiliibi yii: «Lēēmaan unaja ubɔ kí bɔ́ntí-u, di sá yii nimbi di wīikí. Ní mèè ni-waal, ama ní taa kpāā ŋŋmi.»

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ní bi lēē inajaa in bi cáańee ubɔ ki bɔ́ntì saraa, ní ki kúuǹ ki yíiń Baal ki yōoǹ kutaafaau ki cáa sāā kuwiŋkuluu ki lì yii: «Baal, kíí-ti!» Ama baa nìn gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ puɔɔɔ, ubɔ mun kaa nìn kíiń-bi. Bi nìn ŋōō ki màntī nsaraafan ŋun bi nìn máńee.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Kuwiŋkuluuee ní Eelii kíĺ ki bíi bèel̄-bi ki lì yii: «Nín̄ kūuntímaan mpɔn! U sá unimbɔti ní! An yaa yíì u bíi dàkafī tiba pu àá waa bí, àá u cūtì nsan. An yaa yíì u dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ ní an sá ní fìntī-u.»

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi bíi kūuntí mpɔn, kii bi-koobiliŋ poon nín sá puee. Bi nìn cáá njimu nì ŋkpamu ki gífí bi-ba áli fatiku dāa kíǹ ki pùub̀ bi-wunti pu.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Kuwiŋkuluu gbáń ki jítèe ní an fītì-bi yam ní bi kíǹ ki tátí mpɔn áli kuwiŋkuluu saraau yuntiŋu dāa sāā, ama baa nìn gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ puɔɔɔ, ubɔ kaa nìn kíiń-baaa, baa nìn ká báà kudaaŋŋu mun.

english_verse: Elijah told everyone to gather around him while he repaired the Lord's altar.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Eelii bí samaa kɔkɔ yii: «Ní sútiń kí pìl̄maan-mi!» Ní samaa kɔkɔ sútì ki pìl̄-u. Ní u ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu ŋun nìn lítèe.

english_verse: Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about
translation_verse: Ataŋkpee gbanti ní Eelii nìn fātìi dūu máń nsaraafan ki dū-ŋu ki sú ti-Dindaan. U nìn gbìn̄ dibɔbil din poon nnyim liitirib mmuŋku nì saalaa ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ee ki tú nsaraafan.

english_verse: He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood. He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this,
translation_verse: U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki bɔ́ntì idɔ ki páaǹ nsaraafanee pu, ní ki càkā unajee ki bɔ́ntìi páaǹ idɔee pu.

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Nnyim nìn kíǹ ki pùub̀ nsaraafan pu ní áli dibɔbil din bi gbìn̄ee gba gbí.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi ŋáań kuwiŋkuluu saraauee bàn̄ee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eelii sútìi pìl̄ nsaraafan ní ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu, yàntī bí béé díǹ yii sii di sá Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ní man sá a-tɔntɔnliu, ní sii di bí yii ḿ ŋá tin kɔkɔ m ŋá nee.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Kíí-mi, ti-Dindaan, kíí-mi kí yàntī samaa nee ń béé yii sii ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔti, ní a là kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi a-cee.»

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan yāntì ŋŋmi nyánní yilpu ki wùn̄ saraayee nì idɔee nì ataŋkpeeyee nì ŋkpɔŋkpɔm, ní ki yāntì nnyim min kā dibɔbilinee fóotì.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Samaa nín ká mimmee ní bi-kɔkɔ tātìi dōoǹ kitiŋ dicincibil ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan di lafun sá Unimbɔti! Ti-Dindaan di lafun sá Unimbɔti!»

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Ní Eelii bí-bi yii: «Ní cúúmaan diwaal Baal bɔnaatiliibee! Ní taa yàntī báà ubɔ ń ŋmátí!» Ní bi cúú-bi, ní Eelii cáá-bi ki sīntì Kiisɔn buŋgbandi ki lāntì bi-kɔkɔ niin. Utaa fātìi nìn̄

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Boonee ní Eelii bí Akaab yii: «Jɔ̄m̀ kí jī kí nyɔ̀, di sá yii m gbìl̄ ditaadundi pu.»

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Ní Akaab nín jɔ́ḿ kí jī kí nyɔ̀, ní Eelii úǹ nín jɔ́ḿ Kaarmeel jool yilpu, ki tātìi gbāaǹ ki dū u-yil ki fákáǹ u-tabiŋyiliŋ kansikin.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u bí u-tɔntɔnliu yii: «Jɔ̄m̀ kí kpèè tiŋku watil pú.» Ní utɔntɔnlee jɔ́m̀ ki kpēē ní ki fātìi gítìń ki bí yii: «Tiba kpá.» Ŋfunyɔm miluli pu ní Eelii bí-u yii: «Gítí kí kpèè.»

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Ŋfunyɔm miluli puee ní utɔntɔnlee bí yii: «Kpèè, kitagbambilii kiba nyánní tiŋku watil pú ki jɔ́miń. Kaa gbìfì ki bàn̄ unil ŋaŋfaau gba.» Ní Eelii bí-u yii: «Jɔ̄m̀ kí tùkù Akaab yii: <Kpàl̄ a-taamuu kí kpákatí utaa ń taa cúú-si nsanni.>»

english_verse: A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Eelii mpɔn ní úǹ gbìn̄ u-dambalau ki sáǹ ki līntì Akaab tɔrɔkuu nyɔkɔpu ki tin kɔ́ Jisirayeel tiŋkin.

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Akaab máafì u-nimpuu Jeesabeel tin kɔkɔ ní Eelii ŋée nì u nín kūū diwaal Baal bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ puee.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jeesabeel tú bí cùú tùkù Eelii yii: «Fool naŋkɔnampu, m yaa kaa fu ŋá-si kii a nín ŋá bibɔnaatiliibi nee puee, awaa ń dáaĺ m-tafal kí gíti kūtì!»

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Eelii gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki yíkìi kátì kí fīī u-ba. U bàn̄ Beerseeba, Juuda yab tiŋkinee ní ki dū u-tɔntɔnliu ki kāaǹ niin.

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: Ama ní úǹ u-ba dū ŋwimmɔn ki cōom̀ kuteeun, ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ kisugbooi kiba taapu ki mèé yii ŋkúm ń dāá dū-u. U nìn bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan, kɔŋkɔnnee an gíti lákatì! Lēē m-maŋfal, di sá yii maa jítiǹ m-naanjab.»

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: U lī mimmee ní ki tātìi dōoǹ kisugbooyee taapu ki dūu gèen̄. Kpalaayee ntuun ŋubɔ gbēē-u ní ki bí-u yii: «Yīkìm̄ kí jī tijin.»

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: U kpēē u-yil púee, kantaalku nì dinyimbool di sée. U jíń ki nyùn̄ ki dóòyee ní ki fātìi dōoǹ.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Eelii yíkèe ní ki jíń ki nyùn̄ ní ki ká mpɔn ki cōom̀ iwiin imuŋku ili ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu ki tin nyáń Unimbɔti jool Ooreeb pu. Unimbɔti fātìi tīī Eelii kunyannyaau

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Eelii bàn̄ Ooreebee ní ki kɔ́ ki dōoǹ ntaŋkpalɔkɔ ŋubɔn kunyeeu. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-u yii: «Eelii, ba ní a tūǹ doo?»

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ní Eelii kíí yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ipɔn kɔkɔ Nimbɔtiu, m cáá a-pu difaŋgiil, ní an páb́-mi Isirayeel yab nín fātì bi-boon ki tīī a-poondee. Bi gbáń ki wīī a-saraafaŋyi, ki kūū a-bɔnaatiliibi. M pée kíǹ m-baba ní, ní bi bíi nyàab̀ kí lēē ma mun maŋfal.»

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Nyānní kí sīĺ dijool pu m-nimbiin yéèyaa, m làá jītí.» Kpalaayee kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kubɔ dɔ́miń ki jítì, kubuŋuee nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki yàntī ajoon fátí iween ki wìil̄ ataŋkpee. Ama ti-Dindaan kaa nìn bí kubuŋuee poon. Kubuŋu jítì ki dóòyee ní kitiŋ cīŋkì. Ama ti-Dindaan kaa nìn bí kitiŋ nín cīŋkì puee poon.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Kitiŋ cīŋkì míǹ ki dóòyee ní ŋŋmi dɔ́miń, ama ti-Dindaan kaa nìn bí ŋŋmee poon. Ŋŋmi boonee ní u gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ pu ŋu bí dìmmm.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Eelii gbìl̄ nneenee puee ní u dū u-bɔkutikpaandi ki bīiǹ u-nimbiin, ní ki nyáń ki sí ntaŋkpalɔkɔee nyɔkɔpu. Niinee ní nneen ŋubɔ gíti sòon̄ nì u yii: «Eelii, ba ní a ŋáań doo ní?»

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ní u kíí yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ipɔn kɔkɔ Nimbɔtiu, m cáá a-pu difaŋgiil, ní an páb́-mi Isirayeel yab nín fātì bi-boon ki tīī a-poondee. Bi gbáń ki wīī a-saraafaŋyi, ki kūū a-bɔnaatiliibi. Man baba di pée kíǹ, ní bi bíi nyàab̀ kí lēē ma mun maŋfal.»

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-u yii: «Nín̄ gítí, yòon̄ Damaasi teeku saŋŋu. A yaa bàn̄ee, á bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī Asayeel yil pu kí kàan̄-u Siirii bɔtiu.

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: A yaa dóòyee, á bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī Nimisii jipɔɔn Jeewuu yil pu kí kàan̄-u Isirayeel bɔtiu, ní kí bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī Safaati jipɔɔn Eeliisee un sá Afeel-Meewoola tiŋkinee yil pu ú fōō a-paaŋŋu kí kpántí m-bɔnaatiliu.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Unil un yaa ŋúń ki sáǹ ki ŋmátì ní Asayeel kaa kūū-uee, Jeewuu làá kpɔ̀-u, ní un yaa ŋúń ki ŋmátì Jeewuu kaa kūū-uee, Eeliisee làá kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Niinee Eelii kíĺ nsan ki nín cá. U cée ní ki ká Safaati jipɔɔn Eeliisee ŋúb́ inaa in bi kpàl̄ i kù tikpaalee mmuŋku nì inaa ki bíi kù tikpaal. Eelii jítì u-ceeyee ní ki tɔ́ u-bɔkutikpaandi ki páaǹ Eeliisee pu.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Niinee Eeliisee yāntì u-naayee ki nín cá Eelii cee ki bí-u yii: «Yàntī ḿ cùú kpàl̄ m-baa nì m-na kí kàan̄-bi ní kí dāan̄ kí nīn nóó-si.» Ní Eelii bí-u yii: «Nín̄ gítí a-tundi pu, m lī-si tibaaa?»

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Eeliisee nín gítí u-saakun. U bàn̄ee ní ki cúú inaa ili ki ŋá saraa. Idɔ in bi nìn dūu kpàl̄-iee ní u nìn dūu kpāā ŋŋmi ki tɔ́kɔǹ tinan ki tīī u-yab. U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki yíkìi páaǹ Eelii boon ní ki kpántì u-tɔntɔnliu.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi nyàab̄ kutukub ki pēeǹ, ní ki dū iŋmii ki kúĺ ki léeǹ bi-silii ní ki nín cá Isirayeel bɔtiu cee. Bi bàn̄ee ní ki bí-u yii: «A-tɔntɔnliu Been-Adaadi gbàam̄-si yii á fīī u-maŋfal.» Ní Akaab bí yii: «U dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalinaaa? U sá m-nabiki naa!»

english_verse: Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel,
translation_verse: U nìn tú binib bí tùkù Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab yii:

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Ahab replied, “everything I have is yours, including me.”
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a nín lī puee míǹ dee. Man nì tin kɔkɔ m cááyee, sii di yì.»

english_verse: Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children.
translation_verse: Ama ní ituunee fātìi gítìń nliliitiim ki bí-u yii: «Man Been-Adaadi di bíi sòoǹ. M tú bí tùkù-si yii: <Á dū a-nimbiliŋ nì a-sindaariyau nì a-nimpoobi nì a-jipɔmbi kí tīiń-mi.>

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii fool naŋkɔnampuee, m làá fu tɔ̄ m-kàlimbi bí fūkul̀ a-naakookun nì a-kàliŋkpilib diiŋŋin. Kun bi yaa fu ká an cáá a-cee kunyampoou aa mɔ̄ ti-puee, bi làá fu yòon̄.»

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bitindaŋkpilibee nì samaa kɔkɔ bí-u yii: «Á taa pīlifiǹ-uaaa, kí taa kíí u nín bālifì-si tiŋyee.»

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: Ní u bí Been-Adaadi tuuŋyee yii: «Ní tùkù ti-baa ubɔti yii: <Tin a bàà bí yii man a-tɔntɔnliu ń ŋá kí tīī-si mpeepeekaamee, m làá ŋá míǹ kí tīī-si, ama tin a bālifì kɔŋkɔnneeyee, maa làá ŋmā kí ŋá míǹ.>» Ituunee nìn búntì ki cūtìi tùkū Been-Adaadi Isirayeel bɔtiu nín kíí puee.

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Been-Adaadi fātìi dū u-tɔntɔnliibee kí tú ntataatiim bí tùkù-u yii: «Awaa ń dáaĺ m-tafal kí gíti kūtì m yaa kaa yāntì Samaarii tiŋki kpántì ntam min kaa làá gbí bin kɔkɔ cēentí-mi nee ŋaantiliŋinee!»

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu kíí yii: «Ní tùkù Been-Adaadi yii: <Un cá kujaauee kaa máaǹ kí nīn pùlifī kii u nyánní kujaauee.>»

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Been-Adaadi nì bibɔtiibi bin kíǹee nìn bí tantibin ki nyù idafi ní bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū-u tibɔti gbanti. U nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní u bí u-janjakpilib yii: «Dikɔ̀ndi ń kíĺ!» Ní bi bɔ́ntì kí kíĺ dikɔ̀ndi. Ubɔti Akaab jáń ki jíń

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ dɔ́miń ki ká Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Kéè a ká bijanjaliibi cutimaanyi nee yaa! M làá dū-bi kí ŋá a-ŋaan díǹ ní á béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.>»

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.
translation_verse: Ní Akaab bí yii: «Kí dūú dī ŋma pu ní a làá dū-bi kí ŋá m-ŋaan ní?» Ní ubɔnaatilee kíí-u yii: «Kpèè ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ntiŋgbamu kpilib janjaliibi bin sá binipɔmbee pu ní m làá dūú dī.>» Ní Akaab gíti bālifì yii: «Ŋma di làá kíĺ dikɔ̀ndi ní?» Ní u kíí yii: «An sá sii.»

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Ntiŋgbamu janjapɔmbee di nìn péé péé ki nyáń. Been-Adaadi nìn tú binib bí kpèè kun bíi jītée ní bíǹ dɔ́miń ki tùkū-u yii: «Binib nyánní Samaarii ki dòoń.»

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
translation_verse: Ní Been-Adaadi bí yii: «Bi yaa dòoń nì ŋgbansɔŋfee, ní cúú-bi kí taa kpɔ̀-bi, bi yaa tí dòoń nì kujaauaa, ní tí cúú-bi kí taa kpɔ̀-bi!»

english_verse: The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle,
translation_verse: Ama bijanjapɔmbee nìn nyáń kitiŋin dijanjakitil pá bi-boon.

english_verse: and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses,
translation_verse: Báà ŋma nìn kūū u nì un bíi jáàyee. Siirii yab nìn sáǹ ní Isirayeel yab jìn̄-bi. Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi nìn ŋúń ki kāl̀ utaamu pu kí sáǹ ki ŋmátì ki kpáaǹ bitanjakaliibi biba.

english_verse: but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots. Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔtiu nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Siirii yab kpataaa. U nìn kūū ki céetì itaamu ki nāaǹ janjatɔrɔkub.

english_verse: Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.” Syria Attacks Israel Again
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu dɔ́miń ki ká Isirayeel bɔtiu ní ki bí-u yii: «Ká kunyannyaau, ama á dàkafì tiŋan kí kpèè a nín máaǹ kí ŋá puee, di sá yii jiil naŋkɔnampuee, Siirii bɔtiu làá dāá fàtīí gítiń kí já nì si.» Akaab fātìi jáń ki jíń

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained: Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
translation_verse: Siirii bɔtiu naacimbi bí-u yii: «Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu sá ajoon pu Nimbɔtiu ní, an pu ní bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-ti. Ama yàntī tí já nì bi laakin kitiŋ tèen̄ee, niinee ti làá pée pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi ní.

english_verse: Here's what you should do. First, get rid of those
translation_verse: An nín máaǹ tí ŋá puee sɔ̀. Kpákatí bibɔtiibi kɔkɔ kí dū kɔmandambi kí téeǹ bi-yil pu

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: ní kí fàtīí fōō bijanjaliibi bin wīikí ki jítiǹ bin sáǹ-see, ní kí nyàab̀ itaamu nì tɔrɔkub ń nīn wīikí kii mpeepeekaamee. A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, timbi làá cùú já nì Isirayeel yab laakin kitiŋ tèen̄ee, báà an ŋá pu ti làá pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi.» Been-Adaadi nìn pílifiǹ-bi ní ki ŋá kii bi nín bí yii ú ŋá puee.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.
translation_verse: Dibindi páaǹee ní Been-Adaadi kóoǹ Siirii janjaliibi ki kpáfì, ní ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì Afeeki tiŋkin bí já nì Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee nìn tí dɔ́miń ki sòon̄ nì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Siirii yab nín bí yii man ni-Dindaan, m sá ajoon pu Nimbɔtiu kaa sá laakin kitiŋ tèen̄ee Nimbɔtiuee puee, m làá dū bi-janjakitikpaandi nee kí ŋá a-ŋaan, ní ní béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.>»

english_verse: For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed
translation_verse: Bi nìn gāā bi-janjanaapaaŋi ki túĺ tɔb áli iwiin iluli. Ŋwinluluútee ní dikɔ̀ndi kíĺ. Isirayeel yab nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Siirii yab ní ki kūū ŋwimbambaanti bi-janjaliibi bin còom̄ kitiŋ ki jáàyee kutukub dilaataal.

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
translation_verse: U-tɔntɔnliibi nìn bí-u yii: «Pīlifì doo, ti gbìl̄ yii Isirayeel bɔtiibi cáá kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu tikpil. Míǹ puee yàntī tí dū kutukub kí pèen̄, kí dū iŋmii kí kúĺ kí léeń ti-silii, ní kí nyā kí tūŋkì Isirayeel bɔtiu. An yaa yíì u làá yàntī-si kí taa kpɔ̀-si.»

english_verse: Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.” “Go get him,” Ahab said. When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
translation_verse: Bin Been-Adaadi nìn túnnée nìn ká yii an sá kudaaŋŋu kun ŋān̄ee ní bi kpáàa fātìi lī malaa yii: «Tiŋman, Been-Adaadi lafun sá a-nabiki!» Ní Akaab bí yii: «Cùú cáaḿmaan-u.» Niinee ní Been-Adaadi nyánní laakin u bál̀ee ní ki nín dòoń Akaab cee, úǹ dū-u ki kāaǹ u-tɔrɔkuu pu.

english_verse: Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.” Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go. A Prophet Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Been-Adaadi bí-u yii: «M làá fàtīí gíiǹ ntimu mun m-baa nìn jáń ki fōō a-baa ŋaanee kí tīī-si. A ŋūǹ kí nīn kíǹ ki nyáfí a-wanti Damaasi tiŋkin kii m-baa nín nìn ŋūǹ kí nyāfì ti-wanti Samaarii tiŋkin puee.» Ní Akaab kíí-u yii: «See tí pòon̄ tɔb kí ŋá mpèé ní ḿ nín yàntī á nīn cá.» Niinee ní bi pōoǹ tɔb ki ŋá mpèé ní Akaab yāntì u búntì. Akaab nín ŋá puee kaa mɔ́ɔkiǹ ti-Dindaan

english_verse: About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliibi kitil poon ubɔ ní úǹ bí u-juti yii: «M gbàam̄-si, fáá-mi!» Ama ní u-jutee yíì kaa fáá-u.

english_verse: and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní un bàà bí yii ú fáá-uee bí-u yii: «A nín ŋá pu kaa pílifiǹ ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔee, a yaa pée nyáń dooyee, gbikinti di làá kpɔ̀-si.» Ŋyunti ŋun kijapaayee lafun nyánnée ní gbikinti kíntì-u ki kūū-u.

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee ti ká unil ubɔ mun ní ki bí-u yii: «M gbàam̄-si fáá-mi!» Ní úǹ fáá-u ki ŋá-u tiweendi.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee cūtìi kāl̀ nsan caŋin ki cí ubɔti. U nìn dū ŋŋaabu ki fìn̄ u-nimbiin bí taa ŋmā kí béé-u.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ubɔti bíi jītée ní u téeń yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, man a-tɔntɔnliu bí dikɔ̀ndin ki bíi jáàyee ní ujanjal ubɔ cáań-mi unil ubɔ ní ki bí-mi yii: <Nín̄ kpèé-mi unil nee yaa! U yaa sáǹ ki ŋmátì, sii ní bi làá dūú téeǹ u-yil pu, àá a làá pà animbil jitɔmbi kutukub bita>.

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Ama m nín là doo ki là dooyee, maa ti ká mpaan kí kpèè-u ní u sáǹ ki ŋmátì!» Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu kíí-u yii: «Too sii a-ba di sòon̄ ki kūū a-bɔti.»

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔnaatilee cúú ŋŋaabu ŋun u dūu fìn̄ u-nimbiinee ki lēē malaa, ní Isirayeel bɔtiu béè yii an sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kansikin ubɔ.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín bí puee sèé: <A nín yāntì unil un m kūū u-bɔti yii bí kpɔ̀-uee ŋmátèe, sii ní bi làá kpɔ̀ kí téeǹ u-yil pu, ní kí kpɔ̀ a-nibul kí téeǹ u-nibul yil pu.>»

english_verse: Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu nín gítí u-dumpu Samaarii nì kunimbaau nì diŋuul.

english_verse: One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Akaab cūtìi ká Nabooti ní ki bí-u yii: «Dū a-fiinyikpaabu kí tīī-mi ḿ dūú ŋá tikuŋfaal kpaabu, di sá yii bu dɔ̄ ki pìlīǹ m-dumpu, ní ḿ tīī-si bufiinyikpaa bun ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ bu neeyee. A yaa tí là ḿ pà-si bu-daaku nimbiliŋ nín sá pueeyaaa, m làá pà.»

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Nabooti kíí-u yii: «Maa cáá nsan ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí dū bufiinyikpaa bun m fōō difakal m-naanjab ceeyee kí tīī-si.»

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Ní Akaab nín kùǹ nì kunimbaau nì diŋuul, kun puee ujiseeraayeelja Nabooti bí-u yii: «Maa làá dū m-naanjab fakal kí tīī-si.» U dōoǹ u-lambaŋki pu, ní ki fātì u-nimbiin ki túĺ digundi kaa là tijin kí jī.

english_verse: Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
translation_verse: U-nimpuu Jeesabeel dɔ́miń ki ká-uee ní ki bālifì-u yii: «Ba pu ní a-nimbiin wíiḿ míǹ aa là tijin kí jī na?»

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «Kun bée di sá yii m cūtìi ká ujiseeraayeelja Nabooti ki bí-u yii: <Dū a-fiinyikpaabu kí nyāfiǹ-mi, a yaa tí làa, ḿ dū m-fiinyi kpaabu bubɔ kí kpántí-si.> Ní u kíí-mi yii: <Maa làá tīī-si m-fiinyikpaabu.>»

english_verse: “Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jeesabeel bí-u yii: «Sii di kaa sá Isirayeel bɔtiuaa? Yīkìm̄! Jī tijin kí nīn fàal̀. Man di làá dū ujiseeraayeelja Nabooti kpaabu kí tīī-si.»

english_verse: After receiving her letters, they did exactly what she had asked.
translation_verse: Nabooti nín kóò kitiŋ kin poonee kpilib nì ki-kpambaliŋ ŋá kii Jeesabeel nín ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu poon ki bí yii bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front.
translation_verse: Bi bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ní ki kóoǹ samaa kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki yāntì Nabooti kpōotì.

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Bininjab bili bin kaa bí tibanee dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ Nabooti nimbiin ní ki kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nnyimɔn seerau ki tūntí Nabooti pu, samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin ki lì yii: «Nabooti sòon̄ ki bíil̀ Unimbɔti nì ubɔti.» Niinee ní bi nyántì-u kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu ki yáŋkì-u ataŋkpee ki kūū.

english_verse: The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
translation_verse: Ní bi tú bí cùú tùkù Jeesabeel yii: «Bi yáŋkì Nabooti ataŋkpee ki kūū-u.»

english_verse: As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.”
translation_verse: Jeesabeel nín gbìl̄ yii bi yáŋkì Nabooti ataŋkpee ki kūū-uee ní u bí Akaab yii: «Cùú fōō ujiseeraayeelja Nabooti fiinyikpaabu bun u nìn yíì yii waa làá dūú nyāfiǹ-see kí nīn kíǹ ki yì, di sá yii Nabooti kaa ti bí, u kpíì.»

english_verse: Ahab got up and went to take over the vineyard. Elijah Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Akaab nín gbìl̄ yii Nabooti kpíìyee, ní u nín sìntī u-kpaabun, kí fōō-bu kí nīn kíǹ ki yì. Unimbɔti sòon̄ ki kūū Akaab nì Jeesabeel bɔti

english_verse: The Lord said to Elijah the prophet,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí ubɔnaatil Eelii utiiseebeeja yii:

english_verse: “King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over.
translation_verse: «Yīkì kí cù Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab un kóò Samaarii tiŋkinee cee. U bí Nabooti fiinyi kpaabun. U cūtì kí fōō bukpaayee kí nīn kíǹ ki yì.

english_verse: Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ” When Elijah found him,
translation_verse: Á tùkù-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. A kūū unil ki dóòyee ki dɔ́miń kí fōō u-wantaa!> Á gíti kūtì-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín gíti sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Laakin ní iboo líntì Nabooti fatikuee, niin ní i làá líntí si mun yɔu.>»

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Ní Eelii dū tibɔtee ki tùkū Akaab ní Akaab bí-u yii: «M-nannanliu, a tí nyàab̄-mi ki ká-maa!» Ní Eelii kíí-u yii: «M tí nyàab̄ ki ká-si, kun puee an pée mɔ̄ǹ-si á nīn ŋáań tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee dee.

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Kpèè ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <M làá yàntī dinimbinaamandi ń kɔ́-si. M làá kúntí a-dicaŋkun yab. M làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí a-dicaŋkun bininjab kɔkɔ, uyumbuee, un tɔ́ u-beeee, báà ubɔ kaa làá kíń.

english_verse: Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: M làá ŋá a-dicaŋku kii m nín nìn ŋá Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nì Ayiiya jipɔɔn Bayeesa dicaŋŋi puee ní. Di sá yii a gbítì m-ŋuul ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitin.>

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ Jeesabeel bɔti ki lī yii: <Iboo di làá ŋmɔ́ Jeesabeel nanti Jisirayeel gundi taapu.

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: A-dicaŋkun un yaa kpíì kitiŋinee, iboo di làá ŋmɔ́ udaan nanti. Un di yaa kpíì tisatinee, inoon di làá jī u-nanti.>»

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: ní kí tùkù-bi yii: <Man ubɔti di bí yii, ní dū kijapaai nee kí tɔ̄ sarka, kí tīī-u tijin ŋwaam pu nì nnyim kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun m làá fàtīí gítiń nì ŋgbansɔŋfee.>»

english_verse: Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.”
translation_verse: Akaab nìn tùkū u-kàliŋkpilib yii: «Kéè ni nyí yii timbi di yì Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee yaa! Kin ba pu ní ti gíti gùgufī kaa làá cùú fōō-kì Siirii bɔtiu ŋaan?»

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Ní u bālifì Joosafaati yii: «A làá céeǹ-mi ḿ cùú já kí fōō Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkineeee?» Ní Joosafaati kíí Isirayeel bɔtiu yii: «Man nì si sá unibaanti ní. A-nibul sá m-nibul ní a-taamui sá man taamui.» Nnyimɔn bɔnaatiliibi sòon̄ dijajil pu

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Ama ní Joosafaati gíti bālifì yii: «Mimmee báà ti-Dindaan bɔnaatiliu ubɔ gíti kpá doo tí ŋmā kí cù u-cee kí bàlifì kí béé ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ pueeee?»

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel bɔtiu yíiń u-kàlinjau ubɔ ní ki bí-u yii: «Cùú cáań Yiimila jipɔɔn Miika doo malaa!»

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.

translation_verse: U yōoǹ dibɔkutikpaandee ní ki dūu fáá mbunee nyim ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan Eelii Nimbɔtiuee bí la ní?» U fáá nnyim mimmee ní mi cúu yākatì mili ní nsan dōoǹ ní u jítì.

english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kitil din bí Jeeriikoo ki nìn yúní kudandaŋu ki túĺ-bee nín ká Eeliisee ŋá kuŋyee, ní bi bí yii: «Ŋfam min nìn bí Eelii puee kíǹ ki bí Eeliisee mun pu.» Bi lī mimmee ní ki dɔ́miń ki túŋkì-u ní ki tātìi gbāaǹ u-nimbiin bi-yigbeeŋi tūū kitiŋ

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Ama bi nìn pée gbíntìi cɔ́ ki páb́ Eeliisee ní úǹ dāa gīī kí bí-bi yii: «An yaa sée, tɔ̄maan-bi!» Bi nìn dū binib imuŋku ili nì saalaayee ki tú ní bíǹ dū iwimmɔn ita ki nyàab̄ Eelii kaa ká-u.

english_verse: They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.” Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi gítìńee, Eeliisee nìn dáá bí Jeeriikoo ní úǹ bí-bi yii: «Kéè m nìn pée tùkū-ni yii ní taa cùeeee!» Eeliisee ŋáŋkì Jeeriikoo nyimbuliŋu nyim

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Ní Jeeriikoo yab bí Eeliisee yii: «Ti-dindaan, kii sii a-ba nín wāĺ puee, ti-tiŋki bàà mɔ̄ ŋkaa, ama nnyim kaa ŋān̄ ní kitiŋ mun kaa lòoǹ tikpaajin.»

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí yii: «Dūmaan ŋyaam kí ŋá disambipɔndin kí cáań-mi!» Ní bi cáań-u.

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee nín cá dinyimbunimbilin ní ki dū ŋyaamee ki ŋá nnyimin ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M yāntì nnyim nee ŋáŋkì, màa ti làá yàntī binib ń kpúɔɔɔ, kaa ti làá bīil̀ ntiŋkpam mun.>»

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Tiŋman nnyimee nìn ŋáŋkì, ní ki gbíntìi ŋān̄ ki dāa sāā díǹ kii Eeliisee nín nìn sòon̄ puee. Eeliisee dáaĺ mbiyaamu mun bēel̀-uee tafal

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Eeliisee nyáń Jeeriikooyee ní ki nín cá Beeteel. Nsannee ní mbiyaamu nyánní kitiŋin ki bíi bèel̄-u ki lì yii: «Nín̄ cá-mi, uyiŋatifu! Nín̄ cá-mi, uyiŋatifu!»

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Ní u fātì ki kpēē-mu ní ki tɔ́-mu mbusu nì ti-Dindaan yindi pu. Niinee agbiŋgbil ali nyánní kupɔɔun ní ki cúú mbiyaamuee kansikin imuŋku ili nì muli ki tɔ̄ntì.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Eeliisee nín cá Kaarmeel jool pu. U nyánní niinee ní ki nín gítiń Samaarii tiŋkin.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nín kāl̀ dibeel abin saalku nì ata poonee ní Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii tiŋkin ní ki jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì ali.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, ama waa nìn bàn̄ u-baa nì u-na, di sá yii u nìn kpéelikì diwaal Baal taŋkpeeŋi ŋin u-baa nìn cóoǹ bi tòotēe.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: Ama u nìn dū u-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ ikpiti in Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee. Waa nìn fātì u-boon ki tīī-i. Isirayeel yab cūtì ki jáń nì Moowaab yab

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Moowaab bɔtiu Meesaa nìn kpàá tiwaŋkuti ní. Dibintil kamaayee, u nìn pà Isirayeel bɔtiu lampoo apibil kutukub dilaataal nì ipii in cáá tikuti tin bi cáa lù satabee kutukub dilaataal.

english_verse: One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Jooram yíkì Samaarii tiŋkin ki kàan̄ Isirayeel janjaliibi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u tú binib bí tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati yii: «Moowaab yab bɔtiu kaa kíí u-ba pu ki bíi jáà nì mi. Mimmee a kíí kí dāá kūtì m-pu tí já nì u-tiŋkaaa?» Ní Juuda bɔtiu kíí-u yii: «M kíí kí cù, di sá yii man nì si sá unibaanti ní, ní man nib sá a-nib ní man taamui sá a-yai.»

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔtiu nì Juuda bɔtiu nì Eedoom bɔtiu kíĺ nsan ki nín cá. Bi cōom̀ iwiin ilulee, bijanjaliibi nì tiwaŋkuti tin bí bi-ceeyee kaa ti cáá nnyim kí nyɔ̀.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Niinee Isirayeel bɔtiu téeń yii: «Ti kpíì ní! Ti-Dindaan di cáań timbi bibɔtiibi bita nee doo kí dū-ti kí ŋá Moowaab yab ŋaan!»

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Joosafaati bālifì yii: «Ti-Dindaan bɔnaatiliu ubɔ kaa bí doo tí dī u-pu kí bàlifì ti-Dindaanaaa?» Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu janjaliu ubɔ bí yii: «Safaati jipɔɔn Eeliisee bí doo, úǹ di nìn tútúǹ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eelii.»

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Ní Joosafaati bí yii: «An yaa sée u làá ŋmā kí tùkù-ti tin ti-Dindaan cáá kí tùkù-tee.» Dicilpu niinee ní Isirayeel bɔtiu nì Juuda bɔtiu nì Eedoom bɔtiu nín cá Eeliisee cee.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ee ní Eeliisee bí Isirayeel bɔtiu yii: «Ba di bí man nì sii kansikin ní? Nín̄ cá a-baa nì a-na bɔnaatiliibi cee kí bàlifì-bi.» Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «Aayee! Ti-Dindaan di cáań timbi bibɔtiibi bita nee doo kí dū-ti kí ŋá Moowaab yab ŋaan.»

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí yii: «Nì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un bí dimaŋfalin m nóó-u nee puee, m pūtì yii an yaa kaa bàà sá Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati pu, maa bàà làá pée fàtīí kpèè-si gba ní kaa nín pílifiǹ-si.

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Too kɔŋkɔnnee, cáaḿmaan-mi ubeebɔɔl.» Ŋyunti ŋun ní ubeebɔɔlee bíi bɔ̀ɔ́yee ní ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu kpákatì Eeliisee pu,

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: ní u bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀ yii: <Ní gbàmaan kibùmbiki kin nyim fóotì nee poon abɔbil án nīn náaǹ.

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan, man di lī yii naa làá wāl̀ kubuŋu, kaa làá wāl̀ utaa mun, ama nnyim làá gbí kibùmbiki nee, ní ni nì ni-janjaliibi nì ni-waŋkuti ń ká kí nyɔ̀.>»

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee nìkī ki lī yii: «Tíǹ kaa sá tiba ti-Dindaan cee. U làá dū Moowaab yab mun kí ŋá ni-ŋaan.

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: Ni làá nàan̄ bi-timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee nì mun sá ŋkpaamuee. Ní gàatì isufi in lòoǹ abilee kɔkɔ, kí gbīŋkì bi-nyimbɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ ní kí tòò ataŋkpee kí gbéeǹ bi-kpaaŋŋi ŋin bi kùn̄ee kɔkɔn kí bīil̀-ŋi.»

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì ŋyunti ŋun bi ŋáań kutaafaau saraauee, bi kpēēyee nnyim di pùub̀ ki nyánní Eedoom tiŋkin ki bīiǹ kitiŋ puee.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Moowaab yab gbìl̄ yii bibɔtiibee dòoń kí já nì bee ní bi yíiń bin kɔkɔ ŋūǹ kí gbìn̄ gbajabee ní ki cáá-bi ki síiǹ bi-tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau Moowaab yab fīntèe, ŋwìiń nyáń nnyim pu. Bi nín ká nnyim gbanti ndanee, mi máǹ kii fatikuee

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: ní bi téeń yii: «Fatiku dee! Báà an ŋá pu, bibɔtiibee nì bi-janjaliibi di gbáń ki kūū tɔb. Kɔŋkɔnnee, Moowaab yab, yīkìmaan tí cùú fūkul̀-bi!»

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun bi sútì ki pìl̄ Isirayeel yab janjanaapaalee ní bíǹ nyáń ki kpìlìń-bi. Niinee Moowaab yab dū itaaci ní Isirayeel yab kùl̄ ki bīiǹ bi-boon áli ki tin kɔ́ bi-tiŋkin ki kūū-bi.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpéelikì ntimuee ní báà ŋma tɔ́ tisati tin bi kùn̄ee poon ditaŋkpal ní ataŋkpee dūu gbí tisatee. Bi nìn gbíŋkì anyimbɔbil kɔkɔ ní ki gāatì isufi in lòoǹ abilee kɔkɔ ki fá. An dāa kúntèe, digundi din bi máń ki tú Kiiri-Eereesee baba ní baa gbēē, ama bijanjaliibi bin tòó tijaataafunee nìn māntìi tú-kì kí já nì kì.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u cúú u-jipɔŋkpiliu un bàà làá fōō u-yil kí kpántí ubɔtee ki kūū ki ŋá saraawɔkaa digundi pu. An ŋá mimmee ní Isirayeel yab fāŋkì tikpil ní ki yíkì niin ki nín gítí bi-tiŋkin.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kitil kansikin ubɔ nimpuu dɔ́miń ki ká Eeliisee ki bí-u yii: «Ukpil, sii a-ba nyí yii a-tɔntɔnliu m-cal nìn fàŋkí ti-Dindaan. Kɔŋkɔnnee u kpíì ní ti-pɔnliu dɔ́miń yii u làá yòon̄ m-jipɔmbi liitil kí ŋá u-yumbui kí téeǹ dipɔndi din ti cáá-uee.»

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Ba ní a là ḿ ŋá kí tīī-si ní? Tùkù-mi kun ní a cáá an bí a-dumpuee?» Ní u kíí yii: «Man a-tɔntɔnliu kaa pée cáá tiba m-dumpu, an yaa kaa sá ŋkpam min m cáa ŋmìtēe fiiiyee.»

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá a-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb cee kí càà tilɔn tin poon tiba kpée, á càà an nīn náaǹ.

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee sii nì a-jipɔmbi ní kɔ́ kudiin kí dūú pìin̄, ní kí bàtī ŋkpam kí ŋá tilɔnee poon. Kulɔŋŋu kun yaa gbée, á dū-ku kí síiń ku-ba.»

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Niinee unimpuee yíkì ki nín kùǹ. U bàn̄ mmɔŋkee ní ki dū dikampiil ki pīiǹ u nì u-jipɔmbi pu. U-jipɔmbee nìn cáá tilɔnee ki nàatī-u ní úǹ bàtī ŋkpam ki sìtī ki gbēentí.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: U bíi ŋáań míǹ an bàn̄ ŋyunti ŋubɔee ní u bí u-jipɔmbi kansikin ubɔ yii: «Dū kulɔŋŋu kubɔ mun kí nàatīń-mi!» Ní úǹ kíí-u yii: «Tilɔn kaa ti bí.» Niinee ŋkpamee gúń kaa tí bíi còol̀.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee cūtìi máafì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu tin jítèe ní úǹ bí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá kí dū ŋkpamee kí nyāfì kí lēē kí pà a-pɔndi. A-nimbil ŋin yaa kíǹee, á dūú kpíiǹ sii nì a-jipɔmbi.» Eeliisee bí Suneem timbiliikin

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Dalba muee, Eeliisee yíkì ki cūtì Suneem. Upíja ubɔ nìn bí niin ki páb́-u yii ú dāan̄ u-dumpu kí jī tijin. Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbantee, Eeliisee yaa ti pée jītí kitimbilii gbantinee, u nìn pàatī u-cee ní ki jīǹ tijin.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: An bée ní unimpuee dāa tùkū u-cal yii: «M dáań ki béè yii kijapaai kin pée dòoń ti-cee doo nee sá Unimbɔti circir niliu ní.

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee yàntī tí mā kidibiki kí tɔ́kɔń bi nín bɔ̀b̄ kudii puee yilpu, ní kí nyàab̀ kilambaŋ nì teebil nì dijal nì fitila kí síiń ki-poon. U yaa ti dɔ́miń ti-ceeyee, ú dòon̄ niin.»

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Dalbee Eeliisee tí dɔ́miń binibee cee ní ki nín kóò kidibikee ni kí dòon̄.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí u-tɔntɔnliu yii: «Tùkù-u yii: <A tīī a-ba digìńdi ki ŋá tin bí nee kɔkɔ ki tīī-ti. Ba ní ti ŋūǹ kí ŋá kí tīī-si ní? A là tí sòoǹ a-pu ubɔti nì ujanjakpil ceeee?» Ní unimpuee kíí yii: «Aayee! Man nì m-yab pée bí nì ŋgbansɔŋfi ní.»

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí Geeyaasii yii: «Ba ní ti ŋūǹ kí ŋá kí tīī-u ní?» Ní Geeyaasii kíí yii: «Toooo! Waa cáá kibiki ní u-cal mun púĺ.»

english_verse: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí yii: «Fàtīí yíiń-u.» U yíiń unimpuee ní u dɔ́miń ki síl̀ kipunyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Jiil naŋkɔnampuee, a làá dāá nīn ŋúb́ kibiki.» Ní unimpuee téeń yii: «Aayee, m-dindaan, Unimbɔti niliu, taa mɔ̄ntì man a-tɔntɔnliu.»

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Ama unimpuee dūu cáá dipool ní dibindi tú deedeeyee, u dūu màl̄ kibininjabiki, kii Eeliisee nín nìn tùkū-u puee. Eeliisee fīkitì un fōō-u kunicaŋuee jipɔɔn

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Kibikee nìn cíkitì. Dalbee, u-baa bí bijincaliibi cee ki tūǹ ditundi ní kibikee nín cá u-cee.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Dicilpuee ní u kíĺ ki bíi kūuntí ki lì yii: «M-baa! M-yil! M-yil!» Ní ubaati bí u-tɔntɔnliu ubɔ yii: «Yòon̄-kì kí lìb̄ kí cáá tīī ki-na!»

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Ní utɔntɔnlee yōoǹ kibikee ki lìb̄ ki cáa tīī ki-na. Unimpuee yōoǹ u-biki ki làl̄, ama kuwiŋkuluu nyɔkɔmee ní kì sīntì.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Niinee ní unimpuee yōoǹ kibikee ki jɔ́m̀ Unimbɔti tɔntɔnliu Eeliisee diikun ní ki dū-kì ki bíl̀ u-lambaŋki pu. U ŋá mimmee ní ki nyáń ki dū kudii ki pīiǹ.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u yíiń u-cal ní ki bí-u yii: «Cáań-mi utɔntɔnli ubɔ nì kimansalii kiba. M làá sāǹ kí cù Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu cee kí gítiń.»

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ní u-cal bālifì-u yii: «Ba ŋá ní a là kí cùú ká-u díǹ? Díǹ kaa sá uŋmapɔɔn kaa tí sá ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa mun.» Ní u kíí u-cal yii: «Taa fàŋkì, tiba kpá!»

english_verse: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.”
translation_verse: U lī mimmee ní ki kpàl̄ kimansaliiyee ní ki bí u-tɔntɔnliuee yii: «Tí nīn cá, nín̄ dàtī kimansalii kí taa sīĺ nsanni, see m yaa bí-si yii á sīĺ baba.»

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: U yíkèe ní ki nín cá Eeliisee cee Kaarmeel jool pu. Ŋyunti ŋun Eeliisee ká-u ndanee ní u bí u-tɔntɔnliu Geeyaasii yii: «Kpèè usuneennimpuee!

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Sāǹ kí tūŋkì-u kí bàlifì-u yii: <A pɔ̄ɔ̄ mana? A-cal ní? A-biki pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋanaaa?» Geeyaasii bālifì-u mimmee ní u kíí-u yii: «Tikɔkɔ pée còom̄ tiŋan ní!»

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun u bàn̄ Eeliisee cee dijool puee ní u tātìi gbāaǹ u-nimbiin ki cúú u-taal. Geeyaasii bàà sútì ki pìl̄-u kí téé-u, ama ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Yàntī-u, di sá yii u bí kunimbaaun ní maa nyí kun yì-tèe. Unimbɔti kaa lēē-tì ki dàkā-mi.»

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee bí yii: «Man nìn bālifì sii m-dindaan yii á tīī-mi kibikaaa? Maa nìn tùkū-si yii: <Á taa tīī-mi dimákakulindaaa?>»

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí Geeyaasii yii: «Bɔ́ntí a-ba kí yòon̄ m-kpandɔŋu kí tàb̄ kí nīn cá! A yaa tú ubɔ nsanni, á taa jāam̀-u. A yaa bàn̄ee, á dū m-kpandɔŋu kí páań kibikee nimbiin.»

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Ama ní kibikee na bí Eeliisee yii: «Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee nì sii a-ba maŋfal puee, m pūtì yii m kpá kí yàntī-si!» Niinee ní Eeliisee yíkì ki páaǹ u-boon.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Geeyaasii nìn péeǹ-bi ki bàn̄. U dū ŋkpandɔee ki páaǹ kibikee nimbiin, ama waa nìn gbìl̄ kibikee neen puɔɔɔ, kaa ká yii kì cīŋkì ki-ba mun. Niinee ní Geeyaasii fātìi nín gítí Eeliisee cee ki bí-u yii: «Kibikee kaa fīntì.»

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Eeliisee dūu bàn̄ dicindee, kibikee di kpíì ki dɔ̄ u-lambaŋki puee.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: Eeliisee kɔ́ kudiinee ní ki dūu pīiǹ ní ki kíĺ ki bíi mèé ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
