translation_verse: U mēē ki dóòyee ní ki dōoǹ kibikee pu ní ki dū u-nyɔkɔ ki tūū ki-nyɔkɔ, ní ki dū u-nimbiliŋ ki tūū ki-nimbiliŋ ní ki dū u-ŋalii ki páaǹ ki-ŋalii pu. U dɔ̄ kibikee pu mimmee ní ki-wunti píĺ.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Eeliisee yíkì kibikee pu ní ki bíi còom̄ ki pùntī kudiin, ní ki fātìi gítìń ki dōoǹ ki-pu. Niinee kibikee cíiǹ ŋfunyɔm miluli pu ní ki cúú ki-nimbiliŋ ki ŋúbitì.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Eeliisee yíiń Geeyaasii ní ki bí-u yii: «Yíiń-mi usuneennimpuee yaa!» Geeyaasii cūtìi yíiń-u u bāańee ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Yòon̄ a-jipɔɔn!»

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee gbāaǹ Eeliisee taaŋi taapu u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ. U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki yíkìi yōoǹ u-biki ki nín nyēē. Tikun tin tū kaa bí dijilee bɔti

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Tíǹ jítì boonee ní Eeliisee nín gítiń Giilgaal. Ŋkùm nìn bí kitiŋee pu. Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kitil nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì u-cee ní u bí u-tɔntɔnliu yii: «Dū daanseekpaan kí tɔ́kɔń kí ŋàan̄-ti tikun.»

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bibɔnaatiliibee kansikin ubɔ nín cá kusaaun kí nyàabìń tikuŋfaal. U bàn̄ee ki ká kumooun fiinyi subu lòon̄ abil ní u kītì ki gbéeǹ u-wampeeŋkaatin. U fātìi bāańee ní ki càkā ki ŋá daanseeyee poon, di sá yii baa nìn nyí kun ní an sée.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Bi tɔ́kɔǹ an bīńee ní bi lēē ki ŋá binib bin bí niinee. Ama ŋyunti ŋun ní bi dákée ní bi kíĺ ki bíi gbáà ibiil ki lì yii: «Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu, ŋkúm bí daansee poon!» Baa nìn ŋúń ki jíń tijinee.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Niinee ní Eeliisee bí yii: «Cáaḿmaan ŋyim!» Bi cáańee ní u dūu ŋá daanseeyee poon ní ki bí yii: «Lēē kí ŋá binib bí jī!» Tijin tin nìn kā daanseeyee poonee nìn ŋáŋkì bi kíǹ ki ŋūǹ kí jī-tì. Eeliisee kpíiǹ binib dilaataal

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Niinee ní utɔntɔnlee dū kpɔnɔbee ki yākatì ki tīī binibee. Bi nìn ŋmɔ́ an kíǹ kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn sòon̄ puee.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Siirii tiŋki bɔtiu janjakpiliu ní bi yíì Naama. U-kpiliu nìn pàkà-u ki dàkà-u kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu. Di sá yii u-pu ní ti-Dindaan nìn dī ki tīī Aram yab dijajil. Ama ubaatandaan nì ujanjakpaan gbantee nìn sá unyaŋgbanti.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Siirii yab janjaliibi biba nìn nyáń ki kɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋkin ki fúkúl̀ bi-wanti ní ki kpáàa cúuń kisapɔmbiki kiba uyumbu. Kì nìn bí Naama nimpuu cee ní ki tūǹ-u ditundi.

english_verse: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Naama cūtì u-kpiliu ubɔti cee ki dū tin kisirayeelsapɔmbikee tùkū-uee ki máafì-u.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Bɔ́ntí a-ba kí nīn cá, m làá tīī-si kugbɔŋu á cáá tīī Isirayeel bɔtiu.» Niinee Naama yōoǹ animbil kiiloobi alaataa ata nì sindaariya kiiloobi imuŋku ita nì jiŋaal bɔkutiŋ saalaa ki kíĺ nsan ki nín cá.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: U bàn̄ee ní ki dū kugbɔŋuee ki tīī Isirayeel bɔtiu. Kugbɔŋuee poonee, bi nìn ŋmàn̄ yii: «Man di túnní m-janjakpiliu Naama un ŋúb́ kugbɔŋu nee yii á cáaǹ-u u-nyaŋgbandi.»

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Eeliisee nìn tú ubɔ ú tùkù-u yii: «Cù Jɔɔdan buŋŋun kí múĺ ŋfunyɔm miluli pu. A yaa ŋá míǹ, a làá pɔ̄ɔkì ní a-wunti ń ŋāŋkì.»

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti nín pée kàan̄ kugbɔŋu ki dóòyee ní ki cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki cátì ní ki bí yii: «M sá Unimbɔtaaa? M cáá mpɔn kí kpɔ̀ unil àá kí yàntī unil ń nīn bí dimaŋfalinaaa? Kin ba pu ní Siirii bɔtiu dū ubɔ ki túnní m-cee ḿ cáaǹ-u dinyaŋgbandi? Ni káa, u bíi tákà-mi tibɔti ní!»

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee nín gbìl̄ yii Isirayeel bɔtiu dáaĺ tiwan tin u pēēyee ki cátèe, ní u tú bí tùkù-u yii: «Ba pu ní a dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin a pēēyee? Yàntī Naama ń dāan̄ m-cee, u làá béé yii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ bí Isirayeel tiŋkin.»

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Niinee Naama jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ u-tɔrɔkuu un u-taamui dátée poon, ki nín cá ki cūtìi síl̀ Eeliisee diiku nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Naama gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki gíí diŋuul ki nín cá ki lī yii: «Man bàà dàkafī yii u làá nyānní kí sīĺ m-nimbiin kí mèè ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu, ní kí dū u-ŋal kí càab̀ m-wunti laakin dinyaŋgbandi tɔ́ee ní kí cáaǹ-mi.

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Damaasi buŋyi Albana nì Paarpaar kaa jítiǹ ibun in kɔkɔ bí Isirayeel tiŋkineeee? Maa bàà ŋūǹ kí múĺ íǹ poon m-wunti ń ŋāŋkàaa?» U lī mimmee ní ki fātì kí nīn kùǹ nì diŋuul.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Ama ní u-tɔntɔnliibi sútì ki pìl̄-u ní ki bí-u yii: «Ukpil! Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu nee yaa bàà bí-si yii á ŋá tiba tin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee, aa bàà làá ŋáaa? Kin ŋma nín kàlaasì u nín bí-si yii: <Cùú dū a-ba kí múĺ nnyimin a-wunti ń ŋāŋkì na!>»

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Niinee Naama nín sìntī Jɔɔdan buŋŋun ki múĺ nnyimin ŋfunyɔm miluli pu kii Eeliisee nín bí yii ú ŋá puee, ní u-wunti ŋáŋkì kii kibiki wunti nín bí puee.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Dicilpu niinee ní u nì u-naacimbi nín gítí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu cee. U bàn̄ee ní ki kɔ́ ki síl̀ u-nimbiin ní ki bí-u yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee ní m nín béè yii Unimbɔti ubɔ kaa ti bí kitiŋ pu laaba an yaa kaa sá Isirayeel tiŋkin. M gbàam̄-si, fōō tiwampɔkaal tin man a-tɔntɔnliu cáań-si nee.»

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Ama ní Eeliisee kíí yii: «Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin m sá u-tɔntɔnliu nee yindi puee, m pūtì yii m kpá kí fōō tiba.» Naama pée páb́-u yii ú fōō, ama ní Eeliisee yíì.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Naama bí yii: «Kii a nín yíì kaa fōō m-wampɔkaatee, pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ yáfí a-tiŋki pu tam kí túń imamboon ili. Di sá yii man a-tɔntɔnliu kaa ti làá ŋá saraawɔkaa àá saraa ubɔ fám kí tīī awaa, see ti-Dindaan baba.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Ama m mèé yii ti-Dindaan ń dū tin bí nee kí pɔ̄-mi. Di sá yii m-kpiliu Siirii bɔtiu yaa kɔ́ u-waal Riimɔn diikun ki gbāaǹ kí jāam̀-dì ní ma mun gbāaǹee, an sá yii m-ŋaliŋu pu ní u nyìitī. M yaa gbāā diwaal Riimɔn diikun mimmee, ti-Dindaan ń dūú pɔ̄ man a-tɔntɔnliu an pu.»

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee kíí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.» Ní Naama nín cá. Geeyaasii yìntitam Naama búntì kaa láá kɔ́ ndan

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: ní Eeliisee tɔntɔnliu Geeyaasii lī u-neen yii: «M-kpiliu ŋá u-ba kaa fōō tin usiiriija Naama cáań kí pɔ̄-uee tiba. Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee yindi puee, m làá sāǹ kí páań u-boon kí fōoń tiba u-cee!»

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Ní Geeyaasii kùl̄ ki bīiǹ Naama boon. Naama nín ká-u u sáń ki dòoń u-ceeyee ní u kpákatì u-tɔrɔkuu pu malaa ki túŋkì-u ní ki bālifì-u yii: «Ba ŋá?»

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Ní Geeyaasii kíí-u yii: «Tiba kaa ŋá. M-kpiliu di túnní-mi ḿ tùkù-si yii: <A nín pée búntì kpalaayee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kitil poon binib bili nyánní Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu ki bāań m-cee. An puee m gbàam̄-si, tīī-mi animbil kúti kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa nì jiŋaal bɔkutiŋ ali.>»

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Ní Naama bí-u yii: «Yòon̄ animbil kúti kiiloobi imuŋku ita.» U pée páb́-u míǹ ní ki dū animbil kúti kiiloobi imuŋku ita nì tiwampeeŋkaal tili ki ŋá kutukub bili poon ki kúĺ ki dūu túǹ u-tɔntɔnliibi bili bí túń kí cáá céeǹ Geeyaasii.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Oofeelee ní Geeyaasii fōō kutukubee ki dūu bíl̀ u-cee ní ki bí Naama tɔntɔnliibee yii bí nīn gítí, ní bíǹ nín cá.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Geeyaasii nín kóò u-kpiliu Eeliisee cee ní úǹ bālifì-u yii: «Geeyaasii, a nyánní la ní?» Ní u kíí yii: «Man a-tɔntɔnliu kaa pée cūtì laabaa!»

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Ama ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «A nyí yii maa bí a-cee ŋfamin ŋyunti ŋun uninja ubɔ kpákatì malaa u-tɔrɔkuu pu ki túŋkìń-see niin? Mimmee ŋyunti ŋun an sá á fōō animbil kúti nì tiwampeeŋkaal nì ɔliifi nì fiinyi nì ipii nì iŋoobu nì inaa nì bitɔntɔnliibi bininjab nì binimpoobee deeee?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Too Naama nyaŋgbandi làá gítí sii nì a-naantiibi pu ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan!» Geeyaasii nyáń Eeliisee ceeyee, dinyaŋgbandi píń u-wunti pu ki pīiǹ kii ntaayimee.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Dalbee Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kitil bí bi-kpiliu Eeliisee yii: «Kudii kun poon ti nì si kpáfí nee kaa wāā ki bàn̄-ti.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: An puee á pɔ̄-ti nsan tí cù Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi kí gāań idɔ kí cáań kí mā ti-kpafidiiku.» Ní Eeliisee kíí-bi yii: «Nín̄ cámaan!»

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Ní bibɔnaatiliibee kansikin ubɔ bí yii: «Ti gbàam̄-si ní ukpil, pée kíí kí céeǹ timbi a-tɔntɔnliibaa!» Ní Eeliisee kíí yii: «Too, m làá cù.»

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: U lī mimmee ní ki yíkì ki táá-bi. Bi bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋgbandee ní ki gāā isufi.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bālifì-u yii: «La pú ní ncɔkɔbiimee tɔ́ ní?» Ní kijapaayee dàkā-u laakin pú ní mi tɔ́ee. Niinee Eeliisee gāā didɔgindi ki dūu tɔ́ nnyimin laakin ncɔkɔbiimee tɔ́ee. Dicilpu niin ní ncɔkɔbiimee yíkì dēeǹ nnyim pu.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Dèetīń-mì!» Ní kijapaayee dēetìń-mì. Eeliisee cúú Siirii janjaliibi

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Siirii bɔtiu nìn bí ki jáà nì Isirayeel yab. U nì u-janjakpilib yaa nìn kpáfì ki lī yii: «M-janjaliibi làá cùú gāā dijanjannaapaal dooyee»,

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: ní Eeliisee ń tɔ̄ bí cùú tùkù Isirayeel bɔtiu yii: «Á nīn nyí kí taa dī mpaan nee pu, di sá yii Siirii yab janjaliibi bí niin»,

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: An ŋá mimmee ní Siirii bɔtiu kaa ti nyí tin poon u bée, ní u yíiń u-janjakpilib ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ni-kansikin ubɔ bí Isirayeel bɔtiu jandi pú. Ní tùkùmaan-mi un ní an sée.»

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Ní u-janjakpilib kansikin ubɔ bí yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, ubɔ kaa bí ki nyēē a-boon! Ama an sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee un bí Isirayeel tiŋkinee di ŋáań míǹ. Báà tin ní a yaa sòon̄ a-didooŋkaaku poonee, u ŋūǹ kí béé-tì kí dūú tùkù Isirayeel bɔtiu.»

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Niinee Siirii bɔtiu bí yii: «Ní cùú nyàab̀ kí béémaan laakin u bée ḿ ŋma kí tɔ̄ binib bí cùú cúuń-u!» Ní bi tùkū-u yii Eeliisee bí Dootan.

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Niinee ubɔti dū dijanjakitikpaandi nì itaamu nì janjatɔrɔkub ki tú kunyeeuee bi cūtìi māntìi tú kitiŋ kin poon Eeliisee kóòyee.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee Eeliisee tɔntɔnliu péé ki yíkì ki nyáń kitiŋinee ki ká dijanjakitikpaandi nì itaamu nì janjatɔrɔkub māntìi tú kitiŋ. Ní u bí Eeliisee yii: «Ukpil, ti kpíì ní! Ti làá nín ŋá mana dee?»

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee kíí-u yii: «Taa pée fàŋkì! Bin bí ti-ceeyee wīikíǹ bin bí bíǹ ceeyee.»

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Eeliisee lī mimmee ní ki mēē yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ŋúbití u-nimbiliŋ ú wāl̀!» Ti-Dindaan cúú utɔntɔnlee nimbiliŋ ki ŋúbitèe ní u wál̀ itaamu nì janjatɔrɔkub bin sá ŋŋmee gbí dijool pu ki māntìi tú Eeliisee.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Siirii janjaliibee nìn bíi còom̄ ki cá Eeliisee cee ní úǹ mēē ti-Dindaan yii: «Yàntī bijanjaliibi nee kɔkɔ ń kpántí bijɔfub!» Ní ti-Dindaan lafun yāntì bi kpántì bijɔfub kii Eeliisee nín mēē puee.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Niinee Eeliisee bí-bi yii: «Ni yīntì nsan, kitiŋ kin poon ni cée kaa sɔ̀. Páaḿmaan m-boon ḿ cáá-ni kí cùnnì unil un ni nyàab̀ee cee.» Ama Eeliisee yōoǹ-bee ní ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì Samaarii tiŋkin.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ Samaariiyee ní Eeliisee mēē yii: «Ti-Dindaan ŋúbití binib nee nimbiliŋ bí wāl̀!» Ti-Dindaan ŋúbitì bi-nimbiliŋee ní bi ká yii bi bí Samaarii tiŋki poon táb.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔtiu nín ká-bee ní u bālifì Eeliisee yii: «M-baa, ḿ kpɔ̀-baaa?»

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee kíí-u yii: «Taa kpɔ̀-bi! Mimmee a yaa cūtì kujaau ní ki cúuń binib bi kpántì a-yumbuuyee, a kù-bi níii? Tīī-bi tijin bí jī kí tīī-bi nnyim bí nyɔ̀ ní kí yàntī bí nīn gítí bi-kpiliu cee.»

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Niinee Isirayeel bɔtiu ŋá-bi tican ní bi jíń ki nyùn̄. Bi jíń ki nyùn̄ míǹ ki dóòyee ní u yāntì bi nín gítí bi-kpiliu cee. Kí yòon̄ yaadal wiiŋŋuee, Siirii yab bin dòoń ki fúkuĺ binib Isirayeel tiŋkinee kaa ti pée dɔ́miń. Ŋkùm nyáń Samaarii tiŋkin

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋubɔ boonee Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi kóoǹ u-janjakitiŋ kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki cūtìi māntìi tú Samaarii tiŋki kí já nì kì.

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: An ŋá mimmee ní ŋkùm dūu nyáń Samaarii tiŋkin. Bin nìn māntìi tú kitiŋee nìn cí-kì tiŋan, an puee bi nìn kíǹ ki dāā kimaŋ yil animbil kúti jitɔmbi imuŋku inaa ní ki dāā atùun disambijandi animbil kúti jitɔmbi biŋmoo.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Dalbee Isirayeel bɔtiu tɔ́kɔ́ digundi din bi máń ki māntìi tú kitiŋee pu ki jītí ní unimpu ubɔ téeń ki yíiń-u ní ki bí yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, dāá fīī-mi!»

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Ama ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan yaa kaa fīī-si, man làá ŋá mana ní kí fīī-si! Tijin kaa ti báaa, ndamam mun kaa ti bí.»

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Ubɔti gíti nìkī ki bí-u yii: «Ba ní a là ní?» Ní unimpuee kíí-u yii: «A ká unimpu nee yaa! Yaadalee u dɔ́miń ki ká-mi ní ki bí-mi yii: <Yàntī tí ŋmɔ́ a-biki díǹ, foolee tí fu ŋmɔ́ man yaka.>

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti cúú m-biki ki kūū ki tɔ́kɔǹ ní ti ŋmɔ́. Kutaa wúntèe ní m bí-u yii: <Cáań a-biki tí ŋmɔ́>, ama ní úǹ yōoǹ u-biki kí cáa bál̀.»

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nín gbìl̄ unimpuee nín sòon̄ puee ní u cúú u-wanti tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì. Ubɔti còom̄ digundi pu ki jītée ní binib ká yii u dū kutuku ki ŋá poon bɔkutil ki pēeǹ.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Díǹ nee, m yaa kaa lēē Safaati jipɔɔn Eeliisee yil, Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ m-tafal kí gíti kūtì!» Eeliisee sòon̄ yii ŋkùm làá kúntí

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Eeliisee nìn kā u-dumpu ní bitindaŋkpilib kā ki kɔ́ĺ-u. Ubɔti nìn dū ubɔ ki tú u-cee. Ama udaan kaa láá bāań u-cee ní Eeliisee bí bikpilibee yii: «Ni káa! Unikpɔl nee túnní ubɔ ú dāá lēē m-yil. Udaan yaa láa bāańee, ní dū kudii kí kpàl̄ kí taa pɔ̄-u nsan. Pīlifìmaan, m gbìl̀ u-kpiliu pu u pánní u-boon ki dòoń.»

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Eeliisee nìn dáá bíi sòoǹ u-nyɔkɔ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ ní ubɔti tuuŋŋuee dūu bāań u-cee ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan di yāntì digìńdi nee bāań-ti! Ba ní m gíti ŋūǹ kí nīn kā ki cí ú ŋá kí tīī-mi?»

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Eeliisee kíí yii: «Ní pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii: <Fool naŋkɔnampuee, bi làá fu dā ŋyim kiiloobi saalaa nì bili àá ɔɔji yim kiiloobi mmuŋku nì binaa animbil kúti jitɔn ubɔ ní Samaarii nyɔŋkin.>»

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti kpambal un nìn cēentí-u laakin kamaa ní u yaa nìn cée bí yii: «Báà ti-Dindaan yaa cúú kutagbɔŋu tɔkɔlab ki pīitì, tin a sòon̄ nee ŋūǹ kí bàń mimmaaa?» Ní Eeliisee bí yii: «Too! A-nimbil làá ká tin m sòon̄ nee, ama a kpá kí dáká tijin gbanti.» Siirii yab sáǹ ki fá bi-janjanaapaal

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Binyaŋgbantiibi binaa biba nìn bí kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu kaa dátiǹ kipunyɔkɔ. Ní bi bí tɔb yii: «Ba pu ní tí nīn kā doo ki cí ŋkúm?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Ti yaa bí yii ti làá kɔ́ kitiŋin, ti làá kpú kun puee tijin kaa ti bí niin. Ti yaa tí kā dooyaaa, ti làá kpú. Mimmee taa pùtì cá Siirii yab janjanaapaal puɔɔɔ? Bi yaa kaa kūū-ti ki yāntì ti bí dimaŋfalinaaa, ti-yimɔɔl dee. Bi yaa ti kūū-taaa, tí kpú.»

english_verse: That evening the four men got up and left for the Syrian camp. As they walked toward the camp, the Lord caused the Syrian troops to hear what sounded like the roar of a huge cavalry. The soldiers said to each other, “Listen! The king of Israel must have hired Hittite and Egyptian troops to attack us. Let's get out of here!” So they ran out of their camp that night, leaving their tents and horses and donkeys. When the four men with leprosy reached the edge of the Syrian camp, no one was there. They walked into one of the tents, where they ate and drank, before carrying off clothes, as well as silver and gold. They hid all this, then walked into another tent; they took what they wanted and hid it too.
translation_verse: Binyaŋgbantiibee yìin̄ dinaapaal pu míǹ ki dóòyee ní bi jítìi kɔ́ tanti ubɔ poon ní ki jíń ki nyùn̄. Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki kóoǹ animbil nì sindaariya nì tiwampeeŋkaal tin bí niinee ki cáa cūnnì ki bál̀ laaba. Bi gítìńee ní ki kɔ́ tanti ubɔ mun poon ki tí kóoǹ tin kɔkɔ bí u-poonee ki cáa cūnnì ki bál̀. Bijanjaliibi bin māntìi tú kitiŋee yíkì ŋkùm mun kúntì

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi lì tɔb cee yii: «Kun ti bíi ŋáańee kaa kítì. Díǹ wiiŋŋu sá tibɔmɔntiil wiiŋŋu ní. Ti yaa kaa lī tiba ní ki cíitì kutaa wúntèe, taa làá lóó ditafadaaldi. Tí nīn cámaan. Tí kɔ́maan kitiŋin kí dū tibɔti nee kí māafì ubɔti cindin yab.»

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Bi lī mimmee ní ki nín gítiń kitiŋin ní ki yíiń bin cí kitiŋ punyɔkɔkee ki dū tibɔtee ki máafì-bi. Bi bí-bi yii: «Ti cūtì Siirii yab janjanaapaal pu kaa ká báà uniseen, kaa gbìl̄ báà unil neen pu. Kun ti pée kée di sá itaamu nì mmamu gbìn̄ ní tantib sí fám.»

english_verse: The guards reported the news to the king's palace.
translation_verse: Niinee bipunyɔɔciitiliibee yíiń ubɔ ú dū tibɔtee kí māafì ubɔti cindin yab.

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti yíkì kunyeeuee ní ki bí u-kàliŋkpilib yii: «M làá tùkù-ni kun ní Siirii yab bíi bɔ́ntí ti-puee. Bi nyí ŋkùm nín cáá-tee, an pu ní bi yíkì bi-janjanaapaal pu ki cūtìi bál̀ tisatin ki lī tɔb cee yii: <Bin bí kitiŋinee làá nyānní ní tí cúú-bi binifoobi ní kí kɔ́ bi-tiŋkin.>»

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti kàliŋkpilibee kansikin ubɔ fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki lī yii: «Tí yòon̄ itaamu in kíǹ kitiŋinee poon iŋmoo, di sá yii báà i yaa pée báaa, i làá pée kpú kii kitiŋ nee nib kɔkɔee ní. Ti yaa lēē-i mimmee ní tí dū binikaaŋkaabi kí tɔ̄ bí cùú kpèè tin di bíi jītí niinee.»

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi yōoǹ tɔrɔkub bili ki dūu kpàl̄ bi-taamui ní ubɔti lēē bijanjaliibi ki dū-bi ki tú bí cùú nyàab̀ Siirii yab janjaliibi nín bí laakiŋyee kí kpáàa kpèè tin di bíi jītée.

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Bi páaǹ bi-boon ki tin bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. Bi nín cée bi ká tiwampeeŋkaal nì tiwan tin Siirii yab dūu fá fá kí ŋmā kí sāǹ malaa malaayee. Ituunee gítìńee ní ki dū tin bi kée ki dūu máafì ubɔti.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Niinee Samaarii yab nyáń ki cūtìi fúkúl̀ Siirii yab janjanaapaal. Kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn lī puee, bi nìn dá ŋyim kiiloobi saalaa nì bili àá ɔɔji yim kiiloobi mmuŋku nì binaa animbil jitɔn ubɔ ní.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn dū kitiŋ punyɔkɔki ki ŋá u-janjakpiliu un nìn cēentí-u laakin kamaa u yaa nìn cée ŋaan yii ú nīn kpèé. Ama binib nìn tàn̄ tàn̄-u ki nákáǹ kipunyɔkɔ ní u kpíì kii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee nín nìn lī puee. Ubɔti nín nìn dɔ́miń u-ceeyee, tin ní u nìn lēe dee.

english_verse: Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, Eeliisee nìn sòon̄ nì ubɔti ki bí-u yii: «Fool naŋkɔnampu, bi làá fu dā ŋyim kiiloobi saalaa nì bili àá ɔɔji yim kiiloobi mmuŋku nì binaa animbil kúti jitɔn ubɔ ní Samaarii nyɔŋkin.»

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: Ubɔti janjakpiliuee nìn kíí Eeliisee yii: «Báà ti-Dindaan yaa cúú kutagbɔŋu tɔkɔlab ki pīitì, tin a sòon̄ nee ŋūǹ kí bàń mimmaaa?» Ní Eeliisee nìn kíí yii: «Too! A-nimbil làá ká tin m sòon̄ nee, ama a kpá kí dáká tijin gbanti.»

english_verse: Then she returned to Israel and immediately begged the king to give back her house and property.
translation_verse: Abin aluli boonee ní unimpuee nyánní Fiiliistii yab tiŋkin ki fātìi gítìń. U bāańee ní ki cūtìi ká ubɔti ní ki mēē-u yii ú fōō u-diiku nì u-kpaatanti kí tīī-u.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ubɔti nì Eeliisee tɔntɔnliu Geeyaasii di nìn bíi sòoǹ. Ubɔti nìn bí-u yii: «Māafì-mi atuŋkpaan ŋin kɔkɔ ní Eeliisee ŋáaǹee!»

english_verse: While Gehazi was telling him that Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman and her son arrived. “Here's the boy, Your Majesty,” Gehazi said. “And this is his mother.”
translation_verse: Geeyaasii nìn bíi máafí ubɔti Eeliisee nín fīkitì utaŋkpiil ubɔ puee, kpalaayee unimpu un biki Eeliisee nìn fīkitèe dūu kɔ́ní ubɔti cee kí gbàam̀-u ú fōō u-diiku nì u-kpaatanti kí tīī-u. Niinee Geeyaasii téeń yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, kpèè unimpu un jipɔɔn Eeliisee nìn fīkitèe nì u-jipɔɔnee sɔ̀!»

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Dalbee Eeliisee yíkì ki nín cá Damaasi tiŋkin. Ŋyunti gbantee Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi būǹ. Ní bi tùkū-u yii: «Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu dɔ́miń doo.»

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Ní Asayeel yíkì ki nín cá ki cūtìi ká Eeliisee. U nìn yōoǹ tiwammɔntiil tin bí Damaasi tiŋkinee ki túǹ igutaamu imuŋku ili kí cáá pɔ̄ Eeliisee. U bàn̄ ki síl̀ Eeliisee nimbiinee ní ki bí-u yii: «A-tɔntɔnliu Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi di túnní-mi a-cee ḿ bàlifì-si yii u làá pɔ̄ɔkàaa, waa làá pɔ̄ɔkì.»

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Ní Eeliisee kíí-u yii: «Cùú tùkù-u yii u làá pɔ̄ɔkì. Ama tiŋman puee ti-Dindaan lēē ki dàkā-mi yii u bàà làá kpú ní.»

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Kpalaayee Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee kíĺ ki bíi kpèé Asayeel címmm áli icoo dāa kpáàa cúú-u, ní Eeliisee kíĺ ki bíi sūǹ.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Ní Asayeel bālifì-u yii: «M-kpiliu, ba pu ní a bíi sūǹ ní?» Ní Eeliisee kíí yii: «M sūǹ kun puee m nyí inikpiti in a làá dāá ŋá Isirayeel yabee. A làá dāá tūū bi-timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee ŋŋmi, kí dāá làntī bi-naacimpɔmbiyaamu, ní kí dāá tāā tāā kí mátí bi-biyaamu ní kí dāá pùtī bi-nimpoobi bin sá bipɔdambee.»

english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Ní Asayeel bí yii: «Mana ní man a-tɔntɔnliu un bí kii kibɔgbaŋfii nee làá dāá ŋmā kí ŋá míǹ?» Ní Eeliisee kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan lēē ki dàkā-mi yii a làá dāá kpántí Siirii bɔtiu.»

english_verse: Hazael went back to Benhadad and told him, “Elisha said that you will get well.”
translation_verse: Asayeel yíkì Eeliisee ceeyee ní ki nín gítí u-kpiliu cee. U bàn̄ee ní u-kpiliu bālifì-u yii: «Eeliisee tùkūń-si yii ba?» Ní u kíí yii: «U bí-mi yii a làá ŋmátí.»

english_verse: But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Ama kutaa wúntèe ní Asayeel yōoǹ ŋŋaabu ki dūu ŋá nnyimin ní ki dūu bīiǹ ubɔti nimbiin waa ti ŋūǹ kí fòotī. Ubɔti kpíìyee ní Asayeel fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Juuda bɔtiu Jooram bɔti (

english_verse: So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes.
translation_verse: Jooram nìn yíkì ki nín cá Sayiir tiŋkin ki kpáaǹ u-janjatɔrɔkub kɔkɔ. Kunyeeuee ní u nì u-janjatɔrɔkub kpootiliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedoom yab bin nìn māntìi tú-bee. Ama Juuda janjaliibi nìn sáǹ ki nín kóò bi-tantibin.

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: Jooram beel yuntiŋu ní Eedoom yab yíkì kaa kíí bi-ba pu kí nīn gbíntìi bí Juuda yab taapu ní ki kāaǹ bi-ba nì bi-bɔtiu.

english_verse: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
translation_verse: Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram nín kāl̀ Isirayeel beelin tibɔtiil dibiŋŋmooŋmootiil poonee, ní Joosafaati jipɔɔn Jooram kpántì Juuda beelin ubɔti.

english_verse: Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel.
translation_verse: U nìn pée nóó Isirayeel bɔtiibi tabɔbiliŋ ní, a lì kii Akaab dicaŋkun yab nín nìn bí puee, di sá yii u nìn cáá Akaab bisal ubɔ ní. U nìn ŋá tin kaa nìn kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi puee, waa nìn là kí nàan̄ Juuda tiŋki, kun puee u nìn pōoǹ Daafiidi yii u-jipɔmbi làá nīn pée kā dibeel pu Jeerusaleem ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Jooram tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king. King Ahaziah of Judah (
translation_verse: Jooram kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Akasiyasi di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi bɔti (Kpèè

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram nín kāl̀ Isirayeel tibɔtiil abin saalaa nì ali poonee ní Juuda bɔtiu Jooram jipɔɔn Akasiyasi kpántì Juuda beelin ubɔti.

english_verse: Since Ahaziah was related to Ahab's family, he acted just like them and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong.
translation_verse: U nìn nóó Akaab dicaŋkun yab tabɔbiliŋ ní ki nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee kii Akaab dicaŋkun yabee, di sá yii u nìn sá Akaab dicaŋkun yab coo ní.

english_verse: Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: U nì Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram nìn cūtì ki jáń nì Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee ni. Ama kujaaunee ní Siirii yab tīī Jooram tiweendi.

english_verse: One day, Elisha called for one of the other prophets and said: Take this bottle of olive oil and get ready to go to the town of Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee yíiń bibɔnaatiliibi kitil kansikin unaacimpɔɔn ubɔ ní ki bí-u yii: «Bɔ́ntí a-ba kí yòon̄ circir kpam kpalba kí nīn cá Ramooti tiŋkin Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkin.

english_verse: then pour olive oil on his head to show that he is the new king. Say to him, “The Lord has chosen you to be king of Israel.” Then leave quickly—don't wait around for anything!
translation_verse: Kudiin niinee ní á yòon̄ ŋkpam kpalbee kí bàtī kí sìtī u-yil pu kí tùkù-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nì ŋkpam min m bātì ki sītì a-yil pu nee, m kāaǹ-si Isirayeel beelin ubɔti dee!> A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, ní á pìitī kudii kí sāǹní kí taa ti tàan̄.»

english_verse: When he arrived, the army officers were meeting together. “Sir, I have a message for you,” he said. “For which one of us?” Jehu asked. “You, sir,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u bàn̄ee, Isirayeel janjakpilib bíi ŋáań dikpafil. Ní unaacimpɔɔnee bí yii: «Ukpil, m cáá tiba ki làá tùkù-si!» Ní Jeewuu bí yii: «Ti-kansikin ŋma ní a là kí sòoǹ nì ní?» Ní kinaacimpɔmbikee kíí yii: «Ukpil, sii ní an sá!»

english_verse: So Jehu got up and went inside. The prophet poured olive oil on Jehu's head and told him: The Lord God of Israel has this message for you: “I am the Lord, and I have chosen you to be king of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Niinee Jeewuu yíkì ki nín kóò dicindin, ní kinaacimpɔmbikee bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Nì ŋkpam min m bātì ki sītì a-yil pu nee, m dū-si ki kāaǹ man ni-Dindaan nibul Isirayeel pu ubɔti.

english_verse: As for Jezebel, her body will be eaten by dogs in the town of Jezreel. There won't be enough left of her to bury.” Then the young prophet opened the door and ran out.
translation_verse: An yaa kíǹ Jeesabeel úŋ̀wuee, baa làá síb́-u, di sá yii iboo di làá ŋmɔ́-u tisatin.>» U lī mimmee ní ki pīitì kudii ki sáǹ ki kátì.

english_verse: Jehu went back to his officers, and one of them asked, “What did that crazy prophet want? Is everything all right?” “You know him and how he talks,” Jehu answered.
translation_verse: Jeewuu nyánnée ní ki nín gítí ubɔti janjakpilib bin kíǹee cee ní bíǹ bālifì-u yii: «An mɔ̄ deeee? Uwaati gbanti nyàab̀ ba ní a-cee ní?» Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Nimbi ni-ba, ni pée nyí bibɔnaatiliibi nee nì tin bi sòoǹee.»

english_verse: “No, we don't. What did he say?” they asked. “He had a message from the Lord,” Jehu replied. “He said that the Lord has chosen me to be the next king of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ní bin kíǹee bí-u yii: «A mɔ́ntí, māafì-ti tin jítèe!» Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Too, u bí-mi yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nì ŋkpam min m bātì ki sītì a-yil pu nee, m kāaǹ-si ubɔti Isirayeel beelin dee.>»

english_verse: They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!” Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
translation_verse: Bijanjakpilibee gbìl̄ mimmee ní báà ŋma ŋá malaa ki kpátì u-wanti tin u pēēyee ki bíl̀ dikɔl pu ki dū Jeewuu ki kāaǹ. Bi nìn búń ŋyin ní bi-kɔkɔ kíĺ ki kíǹ ki tátí yii: «Ubɔti Jeewuu ń ká mmaŋfafɔkɔn!» Jeewuu bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀ Isirayeel bɔtiu Jooram

english_verse: When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.” Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
translation_verse: Un nìn sí sintil Jisirayeel tiŋkinee nín ká Jeewuu nì dijanjakitil din nìn táá-uee dòońee ní u bí ubɔti yii: «M wāĺ dijanjakitil diba dòoń.» Ní ubɔti Jooram bí yii: «Nyàab̀ utanjakal ubɔ kí tɔ̄ ú cùú tūŋkì-bi kí bàlifì-bi yii bi dòoń nì ŋgbansɔŋfaaa?»

english_verse: One of the soldiers rode out and said to Jehu, “King Joram wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just stay behind me with the rest of my troops!” About the same time the guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back.”
translation_verse: Ní utanjakalee nín cá kí tūŋkì-bi. U bàn̄-bee ní ki bí yii: «Ubɔti bí yii ḿ bàlifì-ni yii an mɔ̄ deeee?» Ní Jeewuu kíí yii: «Ŋgbansɔŋfi bɔti ká-si la? Páań m-boon!» Ní un sí sintilee bí yii: «Ntuunee bàn̄ bi-cee, ama ŋuaa ti gítìń.»

english_verse: So Joram sent out another rider, who rode up to Jehu and said, “The king wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just get behind me with the rest of my troops!”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti gíti lēē utanjakal uliliiti ki tú ní u mun bàn̄ bi-cee ki bí yii: «Ubɔti bí yii ḿ bàlifì-ni yii an mɔ̄ deeee?» Ní Jeewuu kíí yii: «Ŋgbansɔŋfi bɔti ká-si la? Páań m-boon!»

english_verse: The guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back either. Wait a minute! That one man is a reckless chariot driver—it must be Jehu!”
translation_verse: Ní un sí sintilee bí yii: «Ntuun nliliitee bàn̄ bi-cee, ama ŋuaa ti gítìń. Bi nín jàkāń puee m béè un ní an sée. An sá Nimisii naantiu Jeewuu, di sá yii u jàkāń kii uwaatee ní.»

english_verse: Joram commanded, “Get my chariot ready.” Then he and Ahaziah got in their chariots and rode out to meet Jehu. They all met on the land that had belonged to Naboth.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti Jooram yāntì bi kpàl̄ u-taamuu ní u jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀, ní Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi mun jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ u-taamuu pu ní bi-liitil nín túŋkí Jeewuu, ní ki tin dūu tú-u ujiseeraayeelja Nabooti kpaatantin. Isirayeel bɔtiu Jooram kúm

english_verse: “Ahaziah, let's get out of here!” Joram yelled. “It's a trap!” As Joram tried to escape,
translation_verse: Niinee Jooram fātìi lábitì u-ba ki bíi sáń, ní ki bí Akasiyasi yii: «Á nīn nyí nì a-ba Akasiyasi, bi nyáń ti-boon ní!»

english_verse: Jehu shot an arrow. It hit Joram between his shoulders, then it went through his heart and came out his chest. He fell over dead in his chariot.
translation_verse: Niinee Jeewuu lēē mpiin ki páaǹ u-tɔbu pu ki dáaĺ ní an cūtìi cúú Jooram gbigbipati kansikin ki kɔ́ ki pūutì diŋuul ní ki tin nyáń ki lítì. Úǹ u-ba nìn nyáń u-tɔrɔkuu poon ki lítì.

english_verse: Jehu commanded his assistant Bidkar, “Get Joram's body and throw it in the field that Naboth once owned. Do you remember when you and I used to ride side by side behind Joram's father Ahab? It was then that the Lord swore to Ahab that he would be punished in the same field where he had killed Naboth and his sons. So throw Joram's body there, just as the Lord said.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-u yii: <Fool a nín fu kūū Nabooti nì u-jipɔmbee, man a-Dindaan, m fu ká kɔkɔ. Bukpaa bun poon a fu kūū-bee, bukpaa gbanti bubaantiiu poon ní m làá dáaĺ a-tafal, man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ!> An puee nyāntí Jooram kí dū-u kí tɔ̄ bukpaayee poon, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn sòon̄ puee.» Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi kúm (Kpèè

english_verse: Ahaziah saw all of this happen and tried to escape to the town of Beth-Haggan, but Jehu caught up with him and shouted, “Kill him too!” So his troops shot Ahaziah with an arrow while he was on the road to Gur near Ibleam. He went as far as Megiddo, where he died.
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi nín ká mimmee, ní u cúú Beeti-Gan saŋŋu ki sáń ki cá, ama ní Jeewuu kùl̄ ki páaǹ u-boon. Jeewuu nìn tīī u-naacimbi mara yii bí kpɔ̀ u mun! Ŋyunti ŋun u kā u-tɔrɔkuun ki bíi dàb̀ Guur gbantaŋki kin kaa dátì nì Ibileeyamee ní bi yá u mun mpiin. Ama u nìn pɔ́ɔǹ ki sáǹ ki bàn̄ Meegiidoo tiŋkin ní ki kpíì niin.

english_verse: Ahaziah's officers put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried him beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: U-tɔntɔnliibi nìn dū-u ki ŋá u-tɔrɔkuun ní ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Jeerusaleem, ní ki tin síb́-u u-baabi kaakulin, Daafiidi Tiŋkin.

english_verse: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of the rule of Ahab's son Joram. Jehu Kills Jezebel
translation_verse: Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram nín jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì diba poonee ní Akasiyasi kpántì ubɔti Juuda tiŋkin. Jeesabeel kúm

english_verse: Jehu headed toward Jezreel, and when Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye shadow and brushed her hair. Then she stood at the window, waiting for him to arrive.
translation_verse: Jeewuu nìn kíǹ fiii kí kɔ́ Jisirayeel tiŋkin ní Jeesabeel gbìl̄ tin jítèe kɔkɔ. Ní u nyàab̄ culoo ki bɔ̄ntì ní ki nyáantì u-ba ní ki cūtìi kíǹ ki ŋōō tɔkɔla pu.

english_verse: As he walked through the city gate, she shouted down to him, “Why did you come here, you murderer? To kill the king? You're no better than Zimri!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jeewuu lákatì kitiŋ punyɔkɔki kí kɔ́ee ní Jeesabeel téeń yii: «Simrii, sii un kūū a-kpiliuee, an mɔ̄ deeee?»

english_verse: He looked up toward the window and asked, “Is anyone up there on my side?” A few palace workers stuck their heads out of a window,
translation_verse: Jeewuu wáaǹ ki kpēē tɔkɔla watil púee ní ki bí yii: «Ŋma bí m-jandi púee?» Niinee ubɔti cindin bifaabi bili kii bita ŋɔ̄ntìń tɔkɔlabin.

english_verse: and Jehu shouted, “Throw her out the window!” They threw her down, and her blood splattered on the walls and on the horses that trampled her body.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-bi yii: «Téeḿmaan-u kí lúkuń kitiŋ!» Ní bíǹ téeń-u ki lúkú kitiŋ. U lítèe ní u-fatikuu yāaǹ kitiŋ gundi nì itaamu pu, ní Jeewuu dū u-tɔrɔkuu ki tāā-u ki jítì.

english_verse: Jehu left to get something to eat and drink. Then he told some workers, “Even though she was evil, she was a king's daughter, so make sure she has a proper burial.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Jeewuu nín cá dibeecindin ki jíń ki nyùn̄, ní ki bí u-naacimbi yii: «Ní bɔ́ntímaan unimpusoopu nee kí síb́-u, di sá yii u sá ubɔti bisal ní.»

english_verse: But when they went out to bury her body, they found only her skull, her hands, and her feet.
translation_verse: Niinee bi nyáń kí síb́-u, ama kun bi pée kée di sá kuyikpabiku nì ataa nì iŋal.

english_verse: They reported this to Jehu, and he said, “The Lord told Elijah the prophet that Jezebel's body would be eaten by dogs right here in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Ní bi fātìi gítìń ki tùkū Jeewuu ní úǹ bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Eelii, utiiseebeeja pu ki sòon̄ tiŋyee dee yii: <Iboo làá dāá ŋmɔ́ Jeesabeel wunti Jisirayeel satin,

english_verse: And he warned that her bones would be spread all over the ground like manure, so that no one could tell who it was.”
translation_verse: ní u-wunti ń yàl̄ tisatin kii tinaabin tin bi bīil̀ kitiŋ tì yàntī tiwan lòoǹee, áli gba baa dāa gíti ŋūǹ kí lì yii: Jeesabeel sèé!>»

english_verse: choose the best person for the job and make him the next king. Then be prepared to defend Ahab's family.
translation_verse: ní kpèè ubɔti jipɔmbi kansikin kí lēē un kítì ki máaǹ kí nīn sá ubɔtee kí dū-u kí kàan̄ tibɔtiil ú fōō u-baa yil. Ni yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, ní bɔ́ntí ni-ba kí já kí mɔ̄tì ni-kpiliu dicaŋku pu.»

english_verse: The officials and leaders read the letters and were very frightened. They said to each other, “Jehu has already killed King Joram and King Ahaziah! We have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki fāŋkì tikpil ki kíǹ ki lì tɔb cee yii: «Bibɔtiibi bili kaa ŋúń ki síl̀ u-nimbiin, kin mana ní timbi nee làá ŋmā kí já nì u?»

english_verse: The prime minister, the mayor of the city, as well as the other leaders and Ahab's supporters, sent this answer to Jehu, “We are your servants, Your Majesty, and we will do whatever you tell us. But it's not our place to choose someone to be king. You do what you think is best.”
translation_verse: Niinee ukpil un kpèé ubɔti cindee nì ujanjakpil un kpèé kitiŋ gbantee nì bitindaŋkpilib nì bin kpèé mbiyaamuee tú bí cùú tùkù Jeewuu yii: «Timbi sá a-tɔntɔnliibi ní. Kun a yaa pée bí yii tí ŋée, ti làá ŋá. Taa làá lēē báà ubɔ kí kàan̄ tibɔtiil. Míǹ puee ŋá min di ŋān̄ a-ceeyee.»

english_verse: Jehu then wrote another letter which said, “If you are on my side and will obey me, then prove it. Bring me the heads of the descendants of Ahab! And be here in Jezreel by this time tomorrow.” The
translation_verse: Ní Jeewuu fātìi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu kuliliitiiu ki tùkū-bi yii: «Ni yaa bí m-jandi pú ní ki yaa làá pīlifì m-nyɔkɔee, ní lēēmaan ni-kpiliu Akaab jipɔmbi nì u-naantiibi kɔkɔ yiliŋ kí fu cáań-mi fool naŋkɔnampu Jisirayeel tiŋkin.» Ubɔti jipɔmbi nì u-naantiibi imuŋku ita nì saalaa gbantee nìn kā Samaarii nikpaambi cee ní bi kpèé-bi.

english_verse: The next morning, Jehu went out and stood where everyone could hear him, and he said, “You people are not guilty of anything. I'm the one who plotted against Joram and had him killed. But who killed all these men?
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Jeewuu nyáń ki síl̀ samaa nimbiin ki lī yii: «Nimbee, ni sá deedeedambi! Man di bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀ m-kpiliu ubɔti ní ki lafun kūū-u mun. Ama ŋma di kūū bin bí nee kɔkɔ?

english_verse: Then Jehu killed the rest of Ahab's relatives living in Jezreel, as well as his highest officials, his priests, and his closest friends. No one in Ahab's family was left alive in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Niinee Jeewuu kūū bin kɔkɔ nìn kíǹ Akaab dicaŋkun ki bí dimaŋfalin ki kóò Jisirayeelee kɔkɔ. U nìn kūū ki kpáaǹ bikpilib bin kɔkɔ nìn pá u-boonee nì u-bɔɔbi nì u-tandambi. Waa nìn yāntì bi-kansikin ubɔ ŋmátì. Jeewuu kūū Juuda bɔtibiliŋ (Kpèè

english_verse: Jehu left for Samaria, and along the way, he met some relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah at a place where shepherds meet. He asked, “Who are you?” “We are relatives of Ahaziah,” they answered. “We're going to visit his family.”
translation_verse: ní ki tú Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi nabiyaamu. Ní u bālifì-bi yii: «Ni sá bilab ní?» Ní bi kíí yii: «Ti sá Akasiyasi nabiyaamu ní. Ti dɔ́miń kí jāam̀ ubɔti nimpuu Jeesabeel biyaamu nì bin kíǹ ki bí ubɔti dicaŋkunee ní.»

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Jehu said to his officers. So they grabbed them and led them to the well near the shepherds' meeting place, where they killed all
translation_verse: Ní Jeewuu téeń yii: «Ní cúúmaan-bi nì bi-nimbiliŋ!» Ní u-naacimbi cúú-bi nì bi-nimbiliŋ ki lāntì ní ki dū-bi ki tɔ́ Beeti-Eekeedi lɔkɔun. Binib gbanti nìn sá binib imuŋku ili nì bili ní. Bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋmátì. Jeewuu tú Yoonadaab nsanni

english_verse: As Jehu went on, he saw Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him, then said, “Jehonadab, I'm on your side. Are you on mine?” “Yes, I am.” “Then give me your hand,” Jehu answered. He helped Jehonadab into his chariot
translation_verse: U nyáń niin kí nīn cée ní ki dūu tú Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab, u mun nìn còom̄ ki túŋkí-u. Jeewuu jáam̀-uee ní ki bí-u yii: «A sí m-boon kii ma mun nín sí a-boon pueeee?» Ní Yoonadaab kíí yii: «Iiin!» Ní Jeewuu gíti bí-u yii: «An yaa sée, tīī-mi kuboou!» Ní Yoonadaab tīī-u kuboou. Niinee ní Jeewuu cúú u-ŋal ki cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ u-cee tɔrɔkun,

english_verse: and said, “Come with me and see how faithful I am to the Lord.” They rode together in Jehu's chariot
translation_verse: ní ki bí-u yii: «Dāan̄ tí cù á kpèè man nín cáá ti-Dindaan pu difaŋgiil puee!» U lī mimmee ní ki yōoǹ-u u-tɔrɔkuu pu ki cáá-u ki búntì.

english_verse: to Samaria. Jehu killed everyone there who belonged to Ahab's family, as well as all his officials. Everyone in his family was now dead, just as the Lord had promised Elijah. Jehu Kills All the Worshipers of Baal
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Samaarii tiŋkinee ní Jeewuu kūū Akaab dicaŋkun yab bin kɔkɔ nìn kíǹ ki bí kitiŋin niinee. U nìn nāaǹ bi-kɔkɔ ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī ubɔnaatil Eelii pu ki sòon̄ puee. Jeewuu nāaǹ diwaal Baal tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ

english_verse: Jehu called together the people in Samaria and said: King Ahab sometimes worshiped Baal, but I will be completely faithful to Baal.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Jeewuu kóoǹ samaa kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ubɔti Akaab tōotì diwaal Baal, man làá gíti tòotī-dì kí jītíǹ-u.

english_verse: I'm going to offer a huge sacrifice to him. So invite his prophets and priests, and be sure everyone who worships him is there. Anyone who doesn't come will be killed. But this was a trick—Jehu was really planning to kill the worshipers of Baal.
translation_verse: An puee ní yíiń Baal bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ nì bin kɔkɔ tòotī-dèe nì di-tandambi kɔkɔ bí kpāfì m-cee. Ubɔ ń taa kíń, di sá yii m làá ŋá saraakpaŋkpaan ní kí tīī diwaal Baal. Un yaa kaa dɔ́mińee, bi làá kpɔ̀-u ní.» Jeewuu nìn bíi ŋmàtíǹ-bi kí ŋmā kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí bin nìn tòotī diwaal Baalee ní.

english_verse: He said, “Announce a day of worship for Baal!” After the day had been announced,
translation_verse: An pu ní u nìn bí yii bí kóoǹ kí kpāfì kí jāam̀ diwaal Baal. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn

english_verse: Jehu sent an invitation to everyone in Israel. All the worshipers of Baal came, and the temple was filled from one end to the other.
translation_verse: ki yākatì ki tīī Isirayeel beel kɔkɔn. Bin kɔkɔ nìn pée tòotī diwaal Baalee nìn dɔ́miń ní. Ubɔ kaa nìn kíǹ kaa dɔ́miń. Bi nìn kɔ́ diwaal Baal diikun ní an gbí.

english_verse: Jehu told the official in charge of the sacred robes to make sure that everyone had a robe to wear.
translation_verse: Ní Jeewuu bí un kpèé diwaal wampeeŋkaatee yii: «Nyāntí tiwampeeŋkaal kí yàkatīí tīī bin kɔkɔ pée tòotī Baalee!» Ní úǹ nyántì tiwampeeŋkaal ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: Jehu and Jehonadab went into the temple, and Jehu said to the crowd, “Look around and make sure that only the worshipers of Baal are here. No one who worships the Lord is allowed in.”
translation_verse: Jeewuu nì Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab nìn kɔ́ diwaal Baal diikun ní ki bí bin tòotī Baalee yii: «Ní kpèèmaan ni-kansikin tiŋan kí kpèè yii bin jáaḿ ti-Dindaanee yaa bí doo, di sá yii ti pée là bin tòotī Baalee ŋmaniŋma ní.»

english_verse: As soon as Jehu finished offering the sacrifice, he told the guards and soldiers, “Come in and kill them! Don't let anyone escape.” They slaughtered everyone in the crowd and threw the bodies outside. Then they went back into the temple
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jeewuu ŋá saraabi ki dóòyee ní u bí bijanjaliibi nì bi-kpilib yii: «Ní kɔ́ kí kpɔ̀ binib nee! Ní taa yàntī ubɔbɔ ń ŋmátí.» Ní bi kɔ́ ki dū ntàataajimu ki kūū bi-kɔkɔ. Bi kūū-bi ki dóòyee ní ki nyántì-bi ki tɔ́ ki fá kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu. Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki nín gítiń diwaal Baal diikun,

english_verse: and carried out the image of Baal. They burned it
translation_verse: ní ki nyántìń ditaŋkpal din nìn cɔ́ diwaal Baal diikun bi tòotēe ki tūū ŋŋmi.

english_verse: and broke it into pieces, then they completely destroyed Baal's temple. And since that time, it's been nothing but a public toilet.
translation_verse: Bi nín wùn̄ Baal taŋkpal míǹ ki dóòyee ní bi gbáń ki wīī di-diiku ki dūu ŋá kupɔɔndii. Ku bí ki dāa sāā díǹ. Jeewuu kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu

english_verse: But he did not stop the worship of the gold statues of calves at Dan and Bethel that Jeroboam had made for the people to worship.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì ikpiti in ní Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ŋá ki cūtìi bíi jáaḿ sindaariya nabiliŋ ŋin bi nìn mɔ́ɔ́ an bí Beeteel nì Daanee.

english_verse: Later the Lord said, “Jehu, you have done right by destroying Ahab's entire family, just as I had planned. So I will make sure that the next four kings of Israel will come from your own family.”
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan bí Jeewuu yii: «A ŋá an ŋān̄, a ŋá tin fáatiǹ-mee. A ŋá Akaab dicaŋkun yab kii m nín là puee. An puee a-naantiibi làá kàl̄ Isirayeel tiŋki pu tibɔtiil kí cáá sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ anaa pu.»

english_verse: But Jehu did not completely obey the commands of the Lord God of Israel. Instead, he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam had caused the Israelites to do. Jehu Dies
translation_verse: Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Jeewuu kaa nìn ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu marab nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔ, waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì ikpiti in Jeerooboowaam nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ŋée.

english_verse: In those days the Lord began to reduce the size of Israel's territory. King Hazael of Syria defeated the Israelites and took control
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ti-Dindaan nìn kíĺ ki bíi bàtī Isirayeel tiŋki pu. U nìn yāntì Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Isirayeel yab bi-tiŋki kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: of the regions of Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan River and north of the town of Aroer near the Arnon River. This was the land where the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh had once lived.
translation_verse: Siirii yab nìn jáń ki fōō kitiŋ kin bí Jɔɔdan ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee nì Arooweer tiŋki kin bí Arinɔn buŋŋu ŋgan púee, an dàkà yii Galaadi nì Baasan timmu. Ntimu gbanti poon ní Rubeen nì Gaadi nì Manasee naakɔti yab nìn kóò.

english_verse: Everything else Jehu did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Jeewuu tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Jehu died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz became king.
translation_verse: Jeewuu kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Samaarii tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Joowakaasi di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Jehoiada brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David and gave them to the commanders.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil nìn dū ubɔti Daafiidi kpaŋki nì u-gbampɔɔŋi ŋin nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki tīī bijanjakpilib.

english_verse: Jehoiada brought Joash outside, where he placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, while the crowd clapped and shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Niinee Yooyadaa nyántì Joowaasi, ki dū kibeefuulii ki cíkiǹ-u ní ki dū dipoondi taŋkpapilinti ki ŋúbiǹ-u. Boonee ní u bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki kāaǹ-u tibɔtiil ní samaa kɔkɔ kpáafì abaal ki kíǹ ki tátí yii: «Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn!»

english_verse: Joash hid in the temple with Jehosheba for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah. Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah (
translation_verse: Kibikee nì ki-bilooliu nìn bál̀ ti-Dindaan diikun niin áli abin aluu. Ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔee, Atalii di nìn kā dibeel pu. Bi kpántì ubɔti (Kpèè

english_verse: Joash son of Ahaziah had hidden in the Lord's temple six years. Then in the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of the king's special bodyguards and the commanders of the palace guards. They met him at the temple, and he asked them to make a promise in the name of the Lord. Then he brought out Joash
translation_verse: Dibinluluútiil poonee, ní Yooyadaa tú bi cūtìi yíiń Karii yab janjakpilib nì bijanjaliibi bin cīití dibeecindi nì ti-Dindaan diikuee. Bi bāańee ní u cáá-bi ki cūnnì ti-Dindaan Diikun ní u nì bi ŋá kinyɔkɔbaantii. U nìn yāntì bi pūtì ní u dū ubɔti jipɔɔnee ki dàkā-bi.

english_verse: and said to them: Here's what I want you to do. Three of your guard units will be on duty on the Sabbath. I want one unit to guard the palace.
translation_verse: Boonee ní u tīī-bi mara nee yii: «Ni nín làá ŋá puee sɔ̀. Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa nee, ni-kitil diba làá tɔ̄ ditundi. Dikitipeekaal làá cīití dibeecindi kii di nín kpàà ŋáań puee,

english_verse: Another unit will guard Sur Gate, and the third unit will guard the palace gate and relieve the palace guards.
translation_verse: ní dikitililiitiil ń nīn cí Suur punyɔkɔki ní ditataatiil ń nīn cí kipunyɔkɔ kin bí biciitiliibi boonee. Akiti ata gbanti làá nīn cīití dibeecindi ní ki fòol̄ tɔb.

english_verse: The other two guard units are supposed to be off duty on the Sabbath. But I want both of them to stay here at the temple and protect King Joash.
translation_verse: Akiti ali ŋin kaa làá nīn bí ditundin ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee ń dāá dāan̄ ti-Dindaan Diikun kí nīn cí ubɔti.

english_verse: Make sure they follow him wherever he goes, and tell them to keep their swords ready to kill anyone who tries to get near him.
translation_verse: Ní dāá màntīí tū ubɔti báà ŋma ń nīn ŋúb́ u-janjawanti u-ŋaan. Un yaa là kí ŋá mpɔn kí kɔ́née, ní kpɔ̀-u. Laakin kamaa ubɔti yaa cée, ní nīn bí u-cee.»

english_verse: The commanders followed Jehoiada's orders. Each one called together his guards—those coming on duty and those going off duty.
translation_verse: Bijanjakpilibee nìn ŋá kii usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. Báà ŋma nìn yōoǹ u-janjaliibi, bin tundi nìn kífí ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee nì bin tundi nìn kúntí ŋwiin gbanti dalee, ní bi nín cá usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa cee.

english_verse: Then they gave the weapons to their guards, who took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect Joash on every side.
translation_verse: Bijanjaliibee nìn māntìi tú ubɔti ti-Dindaan Diiku nì nsaraafan nimbiin kí yòon̄ ŋgiil pú ki cáa sāā ŋgan pú. Bi nìn ŋúb́ tijanjawan ní ki lūtìi gíb́ ubɔti.

english_verse: Queen Athaliah heard the crowd and went to the temple.
translation_verse: Atalii nín gbìl̄ samaa nì bijanjaliibi wooku puee ní u nín cá ti-Dindaan Diiku watil pú diniwulee cee.

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns, which was the usual place for the king. The singers and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the people were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: U kpēēyee, ubɔtipɔɔn di tɔ́kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diiku kɔl pu kii bi nín kpààa ŋáań puee, bijanjakpilib nì bikantámbunliibi sí ki kɔ́ĺ-u. Samaa kɔkɔ nìn bí mmɔnni ní bikantámbunliibi búǹ akantán. Niinee Atalii cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì ní ki téeń yii: «Bi nyáń m-boon ní! Bi nyáń m-boon ní!»

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Kill her! But don't do it anywhere near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops and kill anyone who is with her!”
translation_verse: Ní usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa tīī bijanjakpilib bin nìn kpèé bijanjaliibi bin bí ti-Dindaan diikunee mara yii: «Nyāntímaan-u doo! Un di yaa páaǹ u-boonee, bí kpɔ̀-u!» Di sá yii usaraaŋakpil nìn lī yii: «Bí taa kpɔ̀-u ti-Dindaan Diikun doo.»

english_verse: So the commanders dragged her to the gate where horses are led into the palace, and they killed her there.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dáaĺ-u ki cūnnì kubɔtinaakoou watil pú, ní ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ Itaamu punyɔkɔkee ní bi kūū-u niin.

english_verse: Jehoiada the priest asked King Joash and the people to promise that they would be faithful to each other and to the Lord.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nìn ŋá mpèé ti-Dindaan nì ubɔti nì samaa kansikin bí nīn kíǹ ki sá ti-Dindaan nibul. U nìn yāntì ubɔti nì samaa mun ŋá mpèé.

english_verse: Then the crowd went to the temple built to honor Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal right in front of the altars. After Jehoiada had placed guards around the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Niinee ní samaa kɔkɔ nín cá diwaal Baal diikun ki gbáń ki wīī-ku. Bi nìn gbáń ki wīī Baal saraafaŋyi nì ataŋkpee ŋin nìn bí niin bi tòotēe. Bi nìn kūū Baal tandaaŋwu Matan ki bíl̀ isaraafan caŋin. Boonee ní usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa lēē binib bí nīn cí ti-Dindaan Diiku.

english_verse: he called together all the commanders, the king's special bodyguards, the palace guards, and the people. They led Joash from the temple, through the Guards' Gate, and into the palace. He took his place on the throne and became king of Judah.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nìn kóoǹ bijanjakpilib nì Karii yab nì bijanjaliibi bin nìn sá biciitiliibee nì samaa kɔkɔ ní bi yōoǹ ubɔti ti-Dindaan Diikun, ki dūu dī biciitiliibi saŋŋu ki céeǹ-u ki cáa cūnnì ubɔti dumpu. Joowaasi nìn kāl̀ dibeejal pu,

english_verse: Joash became king of Judah in Jehu's seventh year as king of Israel, and he ruled
translation_verse: Joowaasi nìn cáá abin aluli ní ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: The fines that had to be paid along with the sacrifices to make things right and the sacrifices for sin did not go to the temple. This money belonged only to the priests.
translation_verse: Binib bin bi nìn cáá animbil gbanti ki tìì bí nīn cáa pà bitɔntɔnliibee, baa nìn bàlifī-bi yii bí gbá akɔntaa bí kpèè bi nín jíń animbil gbanti puee, di sá yii bi nìn sá bibulcinnib ní.

english_verse: But even Joash did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Joowaasi maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, u nìn ŋá tin kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ní, kun puee usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nìn dàkā-u tiŋan.

english_verse: But the priests never started repairing the temple. So in the twenty-third year of his rule,
translation_verse: nimbi ni-ba ń fōō an nimbiliŋee bin ni nyée cee kí dūú ŋāŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku laakin bíil̀ee.»

english_verse: When the box was full of money, the king's secretary and the chief priest would count the money and put it in bags.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nìn nyàab̄ dakaa ubɔ ní ki sāā ki cíl̀ yilpu ki dūu síiǹ nsaraafan caŋin, a yaa kóò ti-Dindaan Diikunee, ŋŋaŋgiil pú. Bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn cīití kipunyɔkɔee nìn cáá animbil ŋin kɔkɔ ní binib nìn cāabìń ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki ŋáań poon ní.

english_verse: Then they would give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. Some of the money was used to pay the builders, the woodworkers,
translation_verse: Bi yaa nìn ká yii animbil bí dakaayee poon ki náaǹee, ní ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu nì usaraaŋakpil ń dāan̄ kí yòon̄ animbil gbanti kí kàaǹ.

english_verse: the stonecutters, and the men who built the walls. And some was used to buy wood and stone and to pay any other costs for repairing the temple.
translation_verse: Bi yaa nìn kàan̄ animbil gbanti ki dóòyee ní bí dūú tīī bin nìn tūǹ atuunee nì bin nìn kpèé ti-Dindaan Diiku tuuŋŋee. Bíǹ yaa fōōyee ní bí lēē kí pà bitɔntɔnliibi bin nìn bí ki ŋáŋkée nì kapintab bin nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikun ki tūǹ ditundee,

english_verse: While the repairs were being made, the money that was given to the temple was not used to make silver bowls, lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or anything gold or silver for the temple.
