translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Asariyasi nín jíń dibeel dibindi diba kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní Gaadi jipɔɔn Meenayeem kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii ní ki jíń dibeel abin saalaa.

english_verse: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, waa nìn kākatì ki wāatì Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam kpitii in u nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee.

english_verse: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu Puul nìn kɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋkin kí já nì Meenayeem, ama ní u ŋá malaa ki nyàab̄ animbil tɔɔnib mmuŋku nì saalaa ki tīī-u ú tūtuǹ-u ú ká mpɔn kí mɔ̀tīí kàan̄ u-beel.

english_verse: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. U nìn pée ŋá kii u-baa Oosiyasi nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedee.

english_verse: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Meenayeem tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king. King Pekahiah of Israel
translation_verse: Meenayeem kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní u-jipɔɔn Peekaya fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Peekaya, Isirayeel bɔtiu

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam kpitii in u nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam kpitii in u nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee.

english_verse: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔtiu Peekaa beel yuntiŋuee ní Asuur bɔtiu Tiigilaati-Piilneeseer dɔ́miń ki jáń ki fōō Yoon nì Abeel-Beeti-Maaka nì Yanoowa nì Keedeesi nì Asɔɔr nì Galaadi nì Galiilee timmu ki kpáaǹ Neefitalii yab timmu kɔkɔ. U nìn kóoǹ ntimu gbanti nib kɔkɔ ki cáa cūnnì Asuur tiŋkin.

english_verse: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Eela jipɔɔn Oosee nìn bɔ́ntì Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa pu ní ki kūū-u ní ki fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Oosiyasi jipɔɔn Yootam nín jíń dibeel Juuda tiŋkin abin mmuŋku poonee ní tíǹ jítì.

english_verse: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
translation_verse: Peekaa tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. Yootam, Juuda bɔtiu (

english_verse: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa nín jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋkin abin ali poonee ní Oosiyasi jipɔɔn Yootam kpántì Juuda bɔtiu.

english_verse: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ama waa nìn kúntì isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu puee. Samaa nìn gbíntìi cáà niin ki ŋáań saraabi ki tùutī talaalub. Úǹ di nìn máń ti-Dindaan Diiku punyɔkɔki kin bí Yilpu púee.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Yootam tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
translation_verse: Yootam beel yuntiŋuee, ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Siirii bɔtiu Reesiin nì Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa dòoń ki jáà nì Juuda yab.

english_verse: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Yootam kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u u-baabi kaakulin, u-naanja Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Akaasi di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa nín jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋkin abin saalku nì ali poonee ní Yootam jipɔɔn Akaasi kpántì Juuda bɔtiu.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_verse: Akaasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Eeseekiyaasi di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Uriya nìn ŋá ubɔti nín tīī-u mara ú ŋá puee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: Ama u nìn dī Isirayeel yab bɔtiibi saŋŋu ní, áli gba u nìn dū u-jipɔɔn ubɔ ki tōotì. Ntimbiil tuuŋŋi gbanti ní atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ki fōō bi-tiŋki ki dūu tīī Isirayeel yabee nìn ŋáań.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá saraabi ki tūutì talaalub awaa saraafaŋyi nì ŋgbantamu pu nì isufi in cáá tifaalee taapu.

english_verse: While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there. About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti ní Siirii bɔtiu Reesiin fōō Eelaati tiŋki Juuda yab ŋaan ki gíiǹ ki tīī Eedoom yab ní bíǹ fātìi gítìń ki kíǹ ki kóò niin áli ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
translation_verse: Akaasi nìn tú binib bí cù Asuur bɔtiu Tiigilaati-Piilneeseer cee kí tùkù-u yii: «M sá a-tɔntɔnliu nì a-jipɔɔn ní. Siirii nì Isirayeel bɔtiibi dɔ́miń kí já nì mi, dāan̄ kí fīī-mi kí nyāntí bi-ŋaan!»

english_verse: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
translation_verse: Ní Akaasi yōoǹ animbil nì sindaariya un nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee nì tigaajawan tin bí dibeecindinee ki tú bí cáá pɔ̄ Asuur bɔtiu.

english_verse: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu nìn pílifiǹ-u ní ki cūtì u-ba ki jáń nì Damaasi yab ní ki fōō bi-tiŋki. U nìn kóoǹ binib bin kɔkɔ nìn bí kitiŋee poonee ki cáa cūnnì Kiiri tiŋkin ní ki kūū ubɔti Reesiin.

english_verse: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Akaasi nìn yíkìi cūtì Damaasi tiŋkin kí ká Asuur bɔtiu Tiigilaati-Piilneeseer. U bàn̄ee ní ki ká nsaraafan ŋubɔ niin, ní u lēē nsaraafanee nín bí puee kɔkɔ ki tú bi cáa cūnnì ki tīī usaraaŋal Uriya ú mā míǹ deedeedee.

english_verse: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
translation_verse: Uriya nìn máń nsaraafanee ki nóó nì ubɔti Akaasi nín bí yii ú mā-ŋu puee. U nìn máń-ŋu ki dóò ki wāatì ní ubɔti nín nyánní Damaasi ki fātìi gítìń.

english_verse: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ubɔti nyánní Damaasi ki fātìi gítìń ki ká nsaraafanee ní u sútìi pìl̄-ŋu,

english_verse: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
translation_verse: ní úǹ u-ba ŋá nsaraafanee pu saraawɔkaa nì tijin saraau, ní ki fá ŋu-pu ndaam. U nìn gíti ŋá mpèé saraau nsaraafanee pu ní ki dū saraayee fatikuu ki yāaǹ ŋu-pu.

english_verse: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
translation_verse: Boonee ní ubɔti Akaasi tīī usaraaŋakpil Uriya mara nee yii: «Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, nsaraafan ŋkpaan nee pu ní a làá nīn kíǹ ki ŋáań saraawɔkaa un a ŋáań kutaafaau kamaayee nì tijimpin saraau un a ŋáań kujoou kamaayee, nì ubɔti saraawɔkaabi nì tijimpin saraabi, nì samaa kɔkɔ nín ŋáań tijimpin saraabi biŋyee nì ndaam min bi féeńee. Saraabi gbanti kɔkɔ fatikubee, á kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafanee pu. An yaa kíǹ tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu ŋúǹ bɔtee, m làá dàkafì kí kpèè m nín làá ŋá-ŋu puee.»

english_verse: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn gíí ki lēē adɔpampan ŋin bi nìn dūu kpáá tasa kúti tɔrɔkub bin nìn sí ti-Dindaan Diikunee, ní ki cúú kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu kun nìn tɔ́kɔ́ tɔrɔkubee puee nì kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundi kun nìn tɔ́kɔ́ inajaa saalaa nì ili puee ki tɔ́kɔtì tɔ́kɔtì ki dūu síiǹ kitiŋ ataŋkpee pu.

english_verse: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
translation_verse: Kí fáatiǹ Asuur bɔtiuee, ubɔti nìn kpītì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dikpaaŋku kun bi nìn máń ti-Dindaan Diikunee, nì nsan ŋun ubɔti nìn dìŋfī kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Akaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Akaasi nín jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì ali poonee ní Eela jipɔɔn Oosee kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii tiŋkin ní ki jíń dibeel abin awa.

english_verse: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, ama waa nín bàn̄ Isirayeel bɔtiibi bin nìn līntiǹ-uee ní.

english_verse: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu Salmanasaar nìn dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Oosee, ní úǹ kíí ki sīntì u-ba ki tīī-u kí nīn bí u-taapu kí nīn pà lampoo ki tìì-u.

english_verse: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
translation_verse: Ama an dāa kúntèe, ní Oosee yíkì kaa kíí u-ba pu. U nìn tú binib Eejipiti bɔtiu Soo cee ní ki yíì yii waa ti làá pà lampoo kí tīī Asuur bɔtiu. Ubɔti Salmanasaar dāa béè mimmee ní ki cúú Oosee ki pīiǹ kudii.

english_verse: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
translation_verse: U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki cáań u-janjaliibi Samaarii tiŋkin ki māntìi tú-kì. Ki yōoǹ abin ata,

english_verse: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: an dàkà yii Oosee nín jíń dibeel abin awa poonee, ní Asuur bɔtiu jáń ki fōō Samaarii tiŋki ní ki cúú Isirayeel yab kí cáa cūnnì kuyuŋu Asuur tiŋkin. U nìn dū-bi ki kāaǹ Alaa tiŋkpaaŋkin nì Abɔɔr tiŋkpaaŋki kin poon ní Goosan buŋŋu pùub̀ee, nì Meedii timmun. Kun pu ní Isirayeel tiŋki kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋmee

english_verse: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
translation_verse: Kun pu ní agìń nee nìn bāań Isirayeel yabee di sá yii bi nìn yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu un nìn fīī-bi ki nyántì Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo ŋaan ki nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Di sá yii bi nìn kíǹ ki tòotī awaa,

english_verse: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
translation_verse: ní ki nìn nóó atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ki fōō bi-tiŋki ki dūu tīī Isirayeel yabee koobiliŋ, nì akoobil ŋin ní Isirayeel bɔtiibi nìn cáań ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋinee.

english_verse: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn ŋáań ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu tin ní baa máaǹ kí ŋée. Bi nìn máń awaa saraafaŋyi bi-timmu kɔkɔn nì sintil difɔkɔŋin nì bi-timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee poon.

english_verse: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
translation_verse: Bi nìn cóoǹ awaa taŋkpeeŋi nì iwaadɔ ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ pu nì busubu bun kamaa pée cáá tifaapɔnee taapu.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
translation_verse: Bi nìn ŋá saraabi awaa saraafaŋyi gbanti kɔkɔ pu kii atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ní ki cáań bíǹ ki kāaǹee nín nìn ŋáań puee. Bi nìn ŋá atuŋkpiti ŋin gíti lákatèe ki gbítì ti-Dindaan ŋuul.

english_verse: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
translation_verse: Bi nìn tōotì awaa, min kamaa ti-Dindaan nìn bí-bi yii bí taa ŋá mimmee.

english_verse: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ pu nì bin wāĺee kɔkɔ pu ki kpáafì Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab. U nìn bí-bi yii: «Fámaan ni-saŋkpitii kí nīn ŋúb́maan m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin kā marab gbɔŋkun m nìn dūu tīī ni-naanjabee. M nìn dūu dī m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi pu ki yāntì ni béè marab gbanti.»

english_verse: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab kaa nìn pílifì tin bi nìn sòon̄ nì bee. Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ kii bi-naanjab nín nìn ŋá pu kaa fōō ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu ki kíí puee ní.

english_verse: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn tīī-bi marab, ki nìn pōoǹ bi-naanjab dipoondi ní ki nìn tīī-bi isaŋki, ama bi nìn dū tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ ki fá. Bi nìn dū bi-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ awaa ŋin kaa bí tibanee, ní bíǹ bi-ba mun kpántì binib bin kaa ti bí tibanee, ní ki fōō atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-bee bimbim, min kamaa ti-Dindaan nìn kpáafì-bi yii bí taa ŋá mimmee.

english_verse: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu marab kɔkɔ ki fá. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ anabil ali kí nīn jáaḿ. Bi nìn nyàab̄ ŋwindɔ ki cóoǹ ki tīī diwaal Aseera. Bi nìn gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ iŋmalbi in bí kutaa puee ki tōotì diwaal Baal.

english_verse: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan nìn gíí Isirayeel yab pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu ní kaa nìn gíti là u-nimbil ń wāl̀-bi. Juuda naakooku yab baba di nìn pée kíǹ ki bí.

english_verse: but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab mun kaa nìn ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu marab. Bi nìn fōō Isirayeel yab bimbim ní.

english_verse: So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan nìn dū Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ki fá ní ki sīntiǹ-bi taapu. U nìn dū-bi ki ŋá anibul ŋin fúkuĺ binib wantee ŋaan. Kí kúntée, u dāa yāntì bi cúú-bi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu ní.

english_verse: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín nìn cúú Isirayeel tiŋki ki nyántì Daafiidi beelinee, Isirayeel yab nìn dū Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam ní ki kāaǹ ubɔti. Jeerooboowaam nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab fātì bi-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan ní ki nìn cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ ikpitikpaan poon.

english_verse: until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets. That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained. Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
translation_verse: An di yāntì ti-Dindaan kaa nìn gíti là kí wāl̀-bi ní ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu Asuur tiŋkin. Niin ní bi gbíntìi bí ki dāa sāā díǹ. Ti-Dindaan nín dī pu ki ŋá kii u nín nìn dī u-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi pu ki sòon̄ ki síiǹee dee. Samaarii yab nyeeŋu

english_verse: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu nìn cáań Babiloon yab nì Kuuta yab nì Afa yab nì Amaati yab nì Seefarfayiim yab ki kāaǹ Samaarii timmun bi fōō Isirayeel yab paaŋŋu. Bíǹ nìn fōō Samaarii tiŋkpaaŋki ní ki kíǹ kóò ki-timmun.

english_verse: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
translation_verse: Bi nín bāań Samaarii tiŋkin ŋkilkaaminee, baa nìn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan. An puee ti-Dindaan nìn dū gbikintib ki tɔ́ bi-pu ní bíǹ kūū bi-kansikin binib tikpil.

english_verse: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi cūtìi ká Asuur bɔtiu ní ki bí-u yii: «Binib bin ní a cáań ki kāaǹ Samaarii timmunee kaa nyí bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá pu ní kí jāam̀ kitiŋ gbanti nimbɔtiuee. An puee unimbɔti gbanti dū gbikintib ki tɔ́ bi-pu ní bíǹ bíi kù-bi, di sá yii baa nyí bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá pu ní kí jāam̀ kitiŋ gbanti nimbɔtiuee.»

english_verse: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
translation_verse: Niinee Asuur bɔtiu tīī mara nee yii: «Ní gíiǹní bisaraaŋaliibi bin ni cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee kansikin ubɔ Samaarii tiŋkin. Ú cù kí nīn kíǹ ki kóò niin kí ŋmā kí dàkà-bi bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá pu ní kí nīn jáaḿ kitiŋ gbanti nimbɔtiuee.»

english_verse: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní an ŋá ní bisaraaŋaliibi bin bi nìn cúú Samaarii tiŋkin ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee kansikin ubɔ gítìń ki kíǹ ki kóò Beeteel. U nìn dàkà-bi bi nín máaǹ kí nīn ŋáań pu kí nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, binicambi bin bi nìn cáań ki kāaǹee kɔkɔ nìn kpítì bi-waaŋi ŋin bi jáaḿee ní. Bi nìn dū bi-waaŋi gbanti ki síiǹ ŋwaadibiyaamu mun Isirayeel yab bin nìn kóò Samaariiyee nìn máń ŋgbantamu puee ní. Kitiŋ kin kamaa poon ní binibee nìn kóòyee, bi nìn pée ŋá míǹ ní.

english_verse: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
translation_verse: Bin nìn nyánní Babiloonee nìn kpítì diwaal Suukooti-Beenooti, ní bin nyánní Kuutee kpítì diwaal Neergaal, ní bin nyánní Amaatee kpítì diwaal Asima,

english_verse: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
translation_verse: ní Afa yab kpítì awaa Niibaasi nì Taartaki. Seefarfayiim yab bíǹ nìn gbíntìi nìkì ki cáá bi-biyaamu ki tòotī bi-waaŋi Adirameeleeki nì Anameeleeki.

english_verse: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
translation_verse: Bi nìn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan, ní ki nìn tòotī bíǹ bi-ba waaŋi mun, ki nóó nì ntimu mun poon bi nyánnée nín ŋáań puee.

english_verse: Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel.
translation_verse: Áli nì díǹ, bi gbíntìi ŋúb́ bi-koobiliŋ gbanti ní. Baa fàŋkí ti-Dindaan. Baa ŋúb́ bíǹ bi-ba marab nì bi-koobiliŋaaa, kaa ti ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan marab bin u nìn tīī Jaakɔb naantiibee mun. Jaakɔb gbanti ní ti-Dindaan nìn gíti páaǹ diyindi yii Isirayeel.

english_verse: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ Jaakɔb naantiibi dipoondi ní ki nìn tīī-bi mara nee yii: «Ní taa jāam̀ awaa, kí taa gbàan̄ ŋi-nimbiin, kí taa tòotī-ŋi ní kaa nín ŋá saraabi ki tīī-ŋi.

english_verse: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan un di dū mpɔŋkpaan ki nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee baba ní ni máaǹ kí jāam̀. Man baba nimbiin ní ni máaǹ kí gbàan̄, ní man baba nì m-baba ní ni máaǹ kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī.

english_verse: and remember the solemn agreement between us. I will say it again: Do not worship any god
translation_verse: Ní taa súntí dipoondi din m pōoǹ-nee, ní m gíti bíi bùsī ki tùkù-ni yii ní taa jāam̀ báà diwaal.

english_verse: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu baba ní ni máaǹ kí jāam̀, di sá yii man baba di ŋūǹ kí fīī-ni kí nyāntí ni-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ŋaan.»

english_verse: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
translation_verse: Ama binib gbanti kaa nìn pílifì. Bi nìn gbíntìi ŋúb́ bi-yaajakoobiliŋ ní.

english_verse: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee bi nìn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan ní ki nìn gbíntìi tòotī bi-waaŋi. Bíǹ boonee bi-biyaamu nì bi-naantiibi nìkī ki ŋá míǹ mbaantiim ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: Ní taa pīlifì Eeseekiyaasi, ama ní pīlifì tin Asuur bɔtiu bí ki sòoǹee, yii: <Píímaan-mi kubɔɔtiiu, ní sāǹ kí kɔ́maan-mi! Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, báà ŋma làá ŋmɔ́ u-fiinyi subu nì u-fiigi subu biliŋ ní ki nyɔ̀ u-lɔkɔu poon nyim,

english_verse: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
translation_verse: A dàkafī yii ti-Dindaan kaa là ní m dɔ́miń kí jáǹ kitiŋ nee kí nàan̄-kàaa? Ti-Dindaan u-ba di bí-mi yii: <Cùú já nì kitiŋ nee kí nàan̄-kì!>»

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin fáatì ti-Dindaanee kii u-naanja Daafiidi nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedee.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
translation_verse: U nìn kúntì ŋgbantamu pu saraabi, ki gbáń ki wīī ataŋkpee ŋin bi kpítì ki dūu ŋá awaayee, ki gāatì ŋwindɔ ŋun bi nìn dūu cóoǹ ki tīī diwaal Aseerayee. U nìn tí gbáń ki wīī kukoonaŋu kun Mooyiisi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee, di sá yii kí cáá sāā ŋyunti gbantee, Isirayeel yab nìn tùutī talaalub ki tìì kukoonaŋu gbanti ní. Bi nìn yíì-ku yii Neeyuusitan.

english_verse: Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn dū u-mákal ki páaǹ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu pu. Juuda bɔtiibi bin nìn līntiǹ-uee nì bin dāa páaǹní u-boonee, bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa bàn̄-u.

english_verse: He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people.
translation_verse: U nìn dū u-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ ti-Dindaan, kaa fātì u-boon ki tīī-u. U nìn ŋúb́ marab bin kɔkɔ ní ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Mooyiisee.

english_verse: The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant.
translation_verse: An puee ti-Dindaan nìn bí u-cee, ní tin kɔkɔ u nìn ŋáańee bútí-u. Waa nìn kíí u-ba pu Asuur bɔtiu cee ní kaa nìn gíti bí u-taapu.

english_verse: and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule.
translation_verse: Abin ata boon, an dàkà yii Eeseekiyaasi beel binluluutiil poon nì Oosee beel biŋwawatiil poon ní Asuur yab jáń ki fōō Samaarii tiŋki.

english_verse: The king of Assyria took the Israelites away as prisoners; he forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu nìn cúú Isirayeel yab kí cáa cūnnì kuyuŋu Asuur tiŋkin. U nìn dū-bi ki kāaǹ Alaa tiŋkpaaŋkin nì Abɔɔr tiŋkpaaŋki kin poon ní Goosan buŋŋu pùub̀ ki jītée, nì Meedii timmun.

english_verse: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there. Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him.

english_verse: One of the Assyrian commanders told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
translation_verse: Ní un nìn ŋúb̀ Asuur bɔtiu janjawanti kujaaunee bí-bi yii: «Ní tùkù Eeseekiyaasi yii: Ubɔtikpaan, Asuur bɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ba pu ní a máká ní?

english_verse: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
translation_verse: An yaa yíì a làá lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu pu ní timbi máká!> Kin an kaa sá sii Eeseekiyaasi ubaantee di kúntì ŋgbantamu pu saraabi nì mu-saraafaŋyi ní ki bí Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab yii nsaraafan ŋun bí Jeerusaleemee baba nimbiin ní bí nīn gbàantí ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaanaaa?

english_verse: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nín jíń dibeel dibindi diba kpá saalku poonee ní Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Juuda yab timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee ki fōō mu-kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.” Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Juuda bɔtiu tú bí cùú tùkù Asuur bɔtiu Lakiisi tiŋkin yii: «M yīntì! Taa ti já nì mi. A yaa gíí-mi dipɔndi diŋyee, m kíí kí pà.» Asuur bɔtiu nìn gíí Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi dipɔndi animbil kúti kiiloobi kutukub biwa nì sindaariya kiiloobi alaataa awa.

english_verse: So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Ní Eeseekiyaasi yōoǹ animbil ŋin kɔkɔ bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee nì ŋin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti nimbikpaafidiikunee ki tīī Asuur bɔtiu.

english_verse: The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu nìn bí Lakiisi tiŋkin ní ki dū u-janjakpiliu nì un sá bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ yidaaŋwuee nì un bi yaa cūtì kujaau u ŋúb̀ ubɔti janjawantee ki tú ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi cee, bi nì dijanjakitikpaandi diba nóó. Bi bàn̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee ní ki jɔ́m̀ ki síl̀ kunyiŋfuŋu kun bi cátì nnyim dì ki kóò dinyimbɔbil din bí yilpu púee. Dinyimbɔbil gbanti nìn dɔ̄ didandi din cá biwaŋfintiliibi kpaabunee watil pú ní.

english_verse: They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: Bi síl̀ niinee ní ki téeń yii bi là kí sòoǹ nì ubɔti. Bin kpèé ubɔti cindee kpiliu Eeliyaakiim, Yiilkiyaawuu nì ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Seebina nì Asafi jipɔɔn Yoowa un kpáafí ubɔti gbɔntee di nìn nyáń ki túŋkì-bi nsanni.

english_verse: Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: A dàkafī yii anyɔɔbun fám ŋūǹ kí fōō kujaau bɔ́ntitam nì dibaatandi paaŋŋu kí já kujaauaaa? Ŋma pu ní a baasii máká ní ki yíkì kaa kíí a-ba pu m-cee na?

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Eejipiti pu ní a mákáaa? Saa nyí yii Eejipiti sá kii kukaluu kun gíìyee ní un yaa dū u-ŋal ki nyīī ku-puee, an gíí-uaaa? Too, míǹ ní Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo sá ki tīī un kamaa yaa dū u-mákal ki páaǹ u-puee!

english_verse: The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people. He will give you
translation_verse: A yaa là sii nì m-kpiliu Asuur bɔtiu ń kpáká kí kpèè. A yaa ŋúń ki ká bitanjakaliibi, m làá tīī-si itaamu kutukub bili mun!

english_verse: How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
translation_verse: Á kpáàa ŋūǹ kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ m-kpiliu tɔntɔnliibi kansikin kiwaai gba! Kin ba pu ní a nín máká Eejipiti pu ú tīī-si janjatɔrɔkub nì itaamu na!

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
translation_verse: Niinee Yiilkiyaawuu jipɔɔn Eeliyaakiim nì Seebina nì Yoowa bí Asuur janjakpiliuee yii: «Ti gbāam̀-si ní, sòoǹ nì timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi Aram yab sooŋyi poon, di sá yii ti gbìl̀-i. Taa ti sòoǹ nì ti eebru sooŋyi poon, di sá yii binib tɔ́kɔ́ digundi pu ki pílifí.»

english_verse: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Asuur janjakpiliuee kíí-bi yii: «A dàkafī yii sii nì a-bɔtiu baba cee ní m-kpiliu túnní-mi ḿ cáań tibɔti nee kí sòoǹaaa? Tibɔti gbanti sá ki tīī binib bin kɔkɔ bí digundi pu nee mun ní. An kaa làá ti yúntí, bi làá ŋmɔ́ bi-binti ní kí nyɔ̀ bi-nyeem kii ni muee.»

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Asuur yab janjakpiliuee yíkìi síl̀, ní ki téeń mpɔn eebru sooŋyi poon yii: «Ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti tin ubɔtikpaan, Asuur bɔtiu cáá kí sòoǹee!

english_verse: Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Ní taa yàntī Eeseekiyaasi ń kīil̀-ni ní dū ni-mákal kí páań ti-Dindaan pu, u bí ki lì yii báà an ŋá pu, ti-Dindaan làá fīī-ni. Kitiŋ nee kpá kí kɔ́ Asuur bɔtiu ŋaan!>

english_verse: Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Atimbun ŋin kíǹee waaŋi ŋúń ki fīī ŋi-timmu ki nyántì Asuur bɔtiu ŋaanaaa?

english_verse: What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?
translation_verse: Amaati nì Aripaadi yab waaŋi bí la? Seefarfayiim nì Eena nì Afa yab waaŋi bí la? Awaa gbanti ŋúń ki fīī Samaarii tiŋkaaa?

english_verse: None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
translation_verse: Ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ waaŋi dilal di ŋúń ki fīī di-tiŋki ki nyántì m-ŋaan? Kin án làá dī mana ní ti-Dindaan ń pìin̄-mi nsan ḿ taa fōō Jeerusaleem?»

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Yiilkiyaawuu jipɔɔn Eeliyaakiim nì ugbaŋŋmal Seebina nì Asafi jipɔɔn Yoowa un kpáafí ubɔti gbɔntee nín gítí ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi cee. Bi nìn dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin bi pēēyee, ní ki dū tibɔti tin ujanjakpilee sòon̄ee ki máafì-u.

english_verse: One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_verse: Dalba u gbāā u-waal Niisrooki diikun ki jáaḿ-dèe, ní u-jipɔmbi Adirameeleeki nì Sareeseer dū kitàataajiki ki gāā ki kūū-u ní ki sáǹ ki nín cá Ararati tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Asaradɔn di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi nín gbìl̄ tin bi máafì-uee ní u cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì, ní ki dū kutuku ki pēeǹ ní ki nín cá ti-Dindaan Diikun.

translation_verse: Amaati bɔtiu nì Aripaadi bɔtiu nì Layiir nì Seefariim nì Eena nì Iwa bɔtiibi bí la díǹ pu na?» Ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi wimmeem

english_verse: These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born.
translation_verse: U nìn bí-bi bí tùkù-u yii: «Eeseekiyaasi nín bí tí tùkù-si puee sɔ̀. Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá-ti kunimbaau nì ditafadaaldi nì icoo wiiŋŋu ní! A lì kii kibiki di bīń ki-na poon ki ŋmāntì bí bàà màal̀-kì, ama ní unaati kaa ti cáá ŋfam kí núuĺ kibiki ń nyānnée!

english_verse: Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
translation_verse: An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu tin máaǹ ki gbìl̄ tibɔti tin Asuur bɔtiu janjakpiliu sòon̄ee kí dáaĺ u-tafal. U-kpiliu túnní-u u dɔ́miń ki sīī Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee. An puee, sii Yeesaya, mèè ti-Dindaan kí tīī a-nibul yab bin kíǹee.»

english_verse: When these leaders went to Isaiah,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi tɔntɔnliibi bin u túee nín cá Yeesaya cee.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah: I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ee ní Yeesaya tùkū-bi yii: «Ní gítí kí tùkù ni-kpiliu yii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Taa fàŋkì anyɔɔbun ŋin a gbìl̄ Asuur bɔtiu janjakpiliu sòon̄ee, u nín sòon̄ ki bíil̀-mi puee.

english_verse: I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
translation_verse: Bi làá cáań tibɔti tiba kí tùkù ubɔti ní ḿ yàntī ú nīn gítí u-tiŋkin. U-tiŋkin niin ní m làá yàntī bí dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀-u.» Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi tí bíikì Jeerusaleem pu (Yees

english_verse: Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
translation_verse: Ujanjakpilee nín gbìl̄ yii u-kpiliu Asuur bɔtiu yíkì Lakiisi tiŋki ki cūtìi bíi jáà nì Liibina tiŋkee, ní u mun nín cá niin ki cūtìi ká-u.

english_verse: About this same time the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu nìn gbìl̄ yii Eejipiti bɔtiu Tiiraka un sá Kuusi tiŋkinee dòoń kí já nì u. Niinee ní u tí tú binib Eeseekiyaasi cee ki bí yii:

english_verse: Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me.
translation_verse: «Ní cùú tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi yii: <A-Nimbɔtiu un pu ní a dū a-mákal ki páaǹee ń taa kīil̀-si kí lì yii Jeerusaleem tiŋki kaa làá kɔ́ Asuur bɔtiu ŋaan.

english_verse: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?
translation_verse: Sisi a-ba gbìl̄ Asuur bɔtiibi nín ŋáaǹ ntimu mun kíǹee kɔkɔ pu ki nāaǹ-muee, ní sii dàkafī yii a làá ŋmátáa!

english_verse: The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them?
translation_verse: Goosan nì Karan nì Reeseefi timbuŋŋi nì Eedeen yab bin nìn kóò Teelasaar tiŋkin ní m-naanjab nìn nāaǹ bi-kɔkɔee, bi-waaŋi nìn ŋúń ki fīī-baaa?

english_verse: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn fōō kugbɔŋu kun Asuur bɔtiu túnní bí cáań kí tīī-uee ki kàan̄. U kàan̄ ki dóòyee ní ki nín jɔ́ḿ ti-Dindaan Diikun, ní ki kpátì kugbɔŋuee ki bíl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Isaiah went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said: Hezekiah, I heard your prayer about King Sennacherib of Assyria.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Amɔtisi jipɔɔn Yeesaya tú bi cūtìi tùkū Eeseekiyaasi yii: «A nín mēē Seenakeeriibi pu puee, ti-Dindaan nín kíiń a-wimmeem puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: He prayed: Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world.
translation_verse: U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki mēē ŋwimmeem nee yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un beejal tɔ́kɔ́ keerubimbi puee. Sii baba di sá kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu beeŋi Nimbɔtiu. Sii di náań kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ.

english_verse: It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, an lafun sá tiŋman ní yii Asuur bɔtiibi kūū ki céetì atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib ki nāaǹ bi-timmu.

english_verse: They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū atimbun gbanti waaŋi ki tɔ́ ŋŋmin ki kúntì-ŋi, di sá yii bi-waaŋi gbanti kaa nìn sá Unimbɔti, idɔ nì ataŋkpee ní binib nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́-ŋi.

english_verse: But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God. The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Ama sii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, fīī-ti kí nyāntí Seenakeeriibi ŋaan ní kitiŋ pu beeŋi kɔkɔ ń béé yii sii, ti-Dindaan baba di sá Unimbɔti.» Yeesaya dū ti-Dindaan nín kíí ubɔti puee ki nāatì-u (Kpèè Yees

english_verse: That same night the Lord sent an angel to the camp of the Assyrians, and he killed
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbantee ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu dɔ́miń Asuur yab janjanaapaal pu ki kūū binib kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku inaa nì kutukub biŋmoo. Kutaa wúntì bin kaa kpíìyee fīntèe, ki ká anikpil dɔ̄ an kɔkɔ fìlfilfil.

english_verse: You let your officials insult me, the Lord. And this is how you bragged about yourself: “I led my chariots to the highest heights of Lebanon's mountains. I went deep into its forest, cutting down the best cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: A dī a-tuuŋyi pu ki sīī man ni-Dindaan. A lī yii: <Man Seenakeeriibi, m cáá janjatɔrɔkub náaǹ, an pu ní m ŋúń ki jɔ́m̀ ki tin bàn̄ ajoon yilpu, m jɔ́m̀ ki tin bàn̄ Leebanɔn jool yilpu. M gāatì ki-seedir sufii in pée fɔ̀kɔ̀ee, ki gāatì ki-siipreesi sufii in pée ŋān̄ee. M jɔ́m̀ ki bàn̄ ki-jooŋŋi ŋin fɔ̀kɔ̀ee yilpu, ki kɔ́ ki-bambaŋku kun múkúee poon.

english_verse: I dried up every stream in the land of Egypt, and I drank water from wells I had dug.”
translation_verse: M gbìn̄ lɔkɔb ntincamun ki nyùn̄ bi-nyim niin. M dū m-taaŋi ki tāā Eejipiti tiŋki, ní ki-buŋyi kɔkɔ fóotì.>

english_verse: Sennacherib, now listen to me, the Lord. I planned all this long ago. And you don't even realize that I alone am the one who decided that you would do these things. I let you make ruins of fortified cities.
translation_verse: «Mimmee Seenakeeriibi, saa nyí yii an sá man di bɔ́ntì tin bíi jītí nee kɔkɔ ki yóoǹ doooodooooyeeee? Saa nyí yii an yúntì tikpil m nín bɔ́ntì-tèeee? Kɔŋkɔnnee ní m yāntì tin m bɔ́ntèe bíi jītí. Man di lēē-si á nà ntimu mun bi máń agun ki māntìi túee kɔkɔ dúsi dusi.

english_verse: Their people became weak, terribly confused. They were like wild flowers or tender young grass growing on a flat roof, scorched before it matures.
translation_verse: Binib bin kóò ntimu gbantinee ŋalii jòon̄ fám ní, dinyoondi kɔ́-bi ní icoo cúú-bi. Bi bí kii timool tin bí tisatinee, kii kumɔsɔŋu kun dáá pɔ̀fèe, kii timool tin nyēē kudii yilpuee, àá tin nyēē tisatin kaa láá bīńee.

english_verse: I know all about you, even how fiercely angry you are with me.
translation_verse: «A yaa kāaa, a yaa yúɔɔɔ, a yaa nyēēyaaa, a yaa kóòyaaa, a yaa tí gíí m-pu diŋuulaaa, m nyí.

english_verse: I have seen your pride and the tremendous hatred you have for me. Now I will put a hook in your nose, a bit in your mouth, then I will send you back to where you came from.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, a lafun gíí m-pu diŋuul, ní tibɔfan tin a sòon̄-mee kɔ́ m-tafalin. An pu ní m làá dū dibɔmbil kí túuń a-maŋfal, kí dū tikúti kí kpàl̄ a-nyɔkɔ kí ŋmā kí kpòotī-si. Nsan ŋun a dī ki dɔ́miń dooyee, nsan gbanti ní a làá fàtīí dī kí kpì.

english_verse: Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest.
translation_verse: «Eeseekiyaasi, kudaaŋŋu kun m tīī-see sɔ̀. Dun bindi nee, ni làá jī dibindi din jítèe jinti tin sá aleenee, ní jiilee ní dāá tí jī míǹ. Ama dibintataatiil poonee, ni làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí bɔ̄l̀ kí cā ni-kpaajinti, ní kí dāá kpɔ̀ afiinyikpaan kí dāá kìtī abil kí ŋmɔ́.

english_verse: Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit.
translation_verse: Juuda beel nib bin làá dāá ŋmátée làá dāá nìn bí kii disupɔmbilee ní. Bi làá dāá tɔ̄ inyaampɔɔn kitiŋ poon ní kí dāá lòoǹ abil yilpu.

english_verse: As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nsan ŋun u dī ki dɔ́mińee, nsan gbanti ní u làá fàtīí dī kí gítí. U-taal kpá kí tāā kitiŋ nee poon. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I will protect it for myself and for my servant David. The Death of King Sennacherib (Isaiah
translation_verse: M làá wúń Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu kí fīī-kì. Mama m-ba nì m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi pu ní m làá ŋá míǹ.>» Asuur yab nín kùǹ, ní bi kūū Seenakeeriibi (Kpèè Yees

english_verse: After this King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi yíkì dinaapaalee pu ki nín gítí Niiniifi tiŋkin ki cūtìi gbíntì niin.

english_verse: Hezekiah died, and his son Manasseh became king.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-naanjab ní u-jipɔɔn Manasee fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: “Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried bitterly.
translation_verse: «M-Dindaan, m gbāam̀-si ní. Téetí yii m nóó-si nì ibaamɔn nì dipɔbil diba ní ki ŋá tin fáatiǹ-see.» U mēē mimmee ní ki súń tikpil.

english_verse: Before Isaiah got to the middle court of the palace,
translation_verse: Yeesaya kaa nìn dá láá nyáń diciŋkpaandin ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message: Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple.
translation_verse: «Gítí kí tùkù m-nibooliŋu kpootiliu Eeseekiyaasi yii: <Ti-Dindaan, a-naanja Daafiidi Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M gbìl̄ a-wimmeem ki ká a-nyinnyim. Béé yii m làá cáaǹ-si. Nì iwiin ita dal, a làá ŋmā kí fàtīí kíĺ kí nīn cáà ti-Dindaan Diikun.

english_verse: “What did you show them?” Isaiah asked. Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ní Yeesaya gíti nìkī ki bālifì-u yii: «Ba ní bi ká a-beecindin?» Ní Eeseekiyaasi kíí yii: «Bi pée ká tin kɔkɔ pée bí m-beecindinee ní. Tiba kaa kíǹ m-nimbikpaafidiikun maa dūu dàkā-bi.»

english_verse: Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
translation_verse: Ní Yeesaya tīī mara nee yii: «Nàmaan fiigi biliŋ kí cáań!» Ní bi nàn̄ ki cáań ki nákáǹ ubɔti wunti laakin wùee pu ní u pɔ́ɔkì.

english_verse: Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
translation_verse: Ní Yeesaya kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan làá tīī-si kudaaŋŋu kí dàkà-si yii u nín pōoǹ puee u làá ŋá míǹ. Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī mboon ŋun lítì Akaasi kɔliŋ puee ń fàtīí sútí kí jɔ̄m̀ akɔl saalaa pu. A là mboon ń cù nyɔkɔpu puɔɔɔ, boon pú ní?»

english_verse: “It's normal for the sun to go forward,” Hezekiah answered. “But how can it go back?”
translation_verse: Ní Eeseekiyaasi kíí yii: «An sá sɔkɔmii ki tīī mboon ŋú cù nyɔkɔpu ki jítiǹ ŋú sútí boon.»

english_verse: Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow go back ten steps on the stairway built for King Ahaz. The Lord Is Still with Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Niinee Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya mēē ti-Dindaan ní úǹ yāntì mboon sútì ki jɔ́m̀ Akaasi kɔliŋ pu, akɔl saalaa ŋin pu ŋu bàà lítèe pu. Babiloon bɔtiu Meeroodaki-Baladan tú binib Eeseekiyaasi cee (Kpèè Yees

english_verse: Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah had been sick, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Babiloon bɔtiu Baladan jipɔɔn Meeroodaki-Baladan nìn gbìl̄ yii Eeseekiyaasi búŋkì. Niinee ní u ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki nyàab̄ tiwampɔkaal ki tú bí cáá cùnnì kí tīī-u.

english_verse: Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
translation_verse: Bin bi túee nín bàn̄ee, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ Eeseekiyaasi ní u yōoǹ-bi ki kɔ́ǹ kudii kun poon ní u nìn kpáafí u-gaajawanti nì animbil nì sindaariya nì talaalub nì ikpafi in sɔ́fèe ki dàkā-bi. U nìn dàkā-bi laakin u nìn kpáafí u-janjawanti mun nì tijanjawan kɔkɔee. Tiba kaa nìn kíǹ Eeseekiyaasi cindin nì u-beelin waa dūu dàkā-bi.

english_verse: Isaiah asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?” “They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
translation_verse: Tíǹ boonee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya dɔ́miń ki ká ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi ní ki bālifì-u yii: «Binib nee tùkū-si yii ba, ní la ní bi nyánní?» Ní Eeseekiyaasi kíí yii: «Bi nyánní ndan ní. Doooo Babiloon tiŋkin ní bi nyánní.»

english_verse: Then Isaiah told Hezekiah: I have a message for you from the Lord.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yeesaya bí Eeseekiyaasi yii: «Pīlifì tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ee:

english_verse: One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left.
translation_verse: <Ŋwiin ŋubɔ bí ki dòoń, tin kɔkɔ bí a-dumpu nee nì tin kɔkɔ a-baabi kpáafì ki síiǹee, bi làá dāá kóoǹ kɔkɔ kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. Tiba kaa làá dāá kíń doo, ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá cúú a-jipɔmbi tikpil bin sisi a-ba màl̄ee, kí cùnnì Babiloon bɔtiu cee kí dū-bi kí ŋá bifaabi bí nīn tūǹ atuun ki tìì-u.>»

english_verse: Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told Isaiah, “The message you brought me from the Lord is good.” Hezekiah Dies (
translation_verse: Ní Eeseekiyaasi kíí Yeesaya yii: «Tibɔmɔntiil ní ti-Dindaan tùkū-si a cáań ki nāatì-mi nee.» Di sá yii u nìn lī u-neen yii: «Ti làá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfi nì dibatɔlin m-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon.»

english_verse: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he made the upper pool and tunnel bring water into Jerusalem, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam kɔkɔ nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u nín gbìn̄ dinyimbɔbil nì u nín cátì nnyinsan pu ki dáaĺ nnyim ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋin puee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa nìn kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee kii u-baa Manasee nín nìn ŋá puee.

english_verse: Now I, the Lord God of Israel, will destroy both Jerusalem and Judah! People will hear about it but won't believe it.
translation_verse: An puee man ni-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá cáań nnaabukpaan ŋubɔ kí tɔ̄ Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem pu. Án làá dāá ŋá un yaa láa gbìl̄ nnaabu gbanti puee bitii.

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah, just as King Ahab of Israel had done. And he faithfully worshiped the stars in heaven.
translation_verse: U nìn fātìi máń isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu pu u-baa Eeseekiyaasi nìn kúntèe. U nìn máń diwaal Baal nsaraafan, ní ki nyàab̄ ŋwindɔ ki cóoǹ kii Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab nín nìn ŋá puee, ní ki nìn gbàantí ki jáaḿ iŋmalbi.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: U nìn máń isaraafan iba mun ti-Dindaan Diikun, min kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nìn lī yii: «Jeerusaleem niin ní m làá nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkèe.»

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courts of the temple,
translation_verse: U nìn gíti máń isaraafan ti-Dindaan Diiku ciŋŋi liitilin ki tīī iŋmalbi in bí kutaa puee.

english_verse: and even set up the pole for Asherah there. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own son. He did many sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago the Lord had told David and his son Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there I will be worshiped forever.
translation_verse: U nìn máń Aseera waal ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diikun. Ama ti-Dindaan nìn tùkū Daafiidi nì u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn yii: «Kudii nee poon nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin m lēē Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ kansikinee poon ní m làá nīn pée lèekī m-ba ki dàkà.

english_verse: If my people will faithfully obey all the commands in the Law of my servant Moses, I will never make them leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
translation_verse: M-nibooliŋu yaa tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ nì m-marab bin kɔkɔ m-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi tīī-bee, m kpá kí yàntī bí nīn tú ki yìiǹ kí wàatī kitiŋ kin ní m tīī bi-naanjabee.»

english_verse: But the people of Judah disobeyed the Lord. They listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab kaa nìn pílifì ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔ. Ubɔti Manasee nìn yāntì bi gáatì ki ŋá tin kaa kítèe ki jítiǹ atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn kūū ki céetì ki cáań Isirayeel yab ki kāaǹee.

english_verse: One day the Lord said to some of his prophets:

translation_verse: U nìn dū Yooyakiin baawaai Mataniya ki kāaǹ ubɔti u fōō u-yil, ní ki kpántì u-yindi. Bi nìn kíǹ ki yíì-u yii Seedeesiyasi ní. Seedeesiyasi, Juuda bɔtiu (Kpèè Yeer

english_verse: Zedekiah disobeyed the Lord, just as Jehoiakim had done.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, kii Yooyakiin nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedeedee.

english_verse: It was Zedekiah who finally rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar. The people of Judah and Jerusalem had made the Lord so angry that he turned his back on them. That's why these horrible things were happening.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín nìn gíí diŋuul diŋyee puee di nìn yì-tì ní nnaabu gbanti jéetì Jeerusaleem nì Juuda yab pu, áli gba u dāa fātì u-boon ki tīī-bi. Neebukadineesaar janjaliibi māntìi tú Jeerusaleem kí já nì kì (Kpèè Yeer

english_verse: Each column had been eight meters tall with a bronze cap over one meter high. These caps were decorated with bronze designs—some of them like chains and others like pomegranates.
translation_verse: Jaantalkub kamaa fɔkɔŋŋu yilpu nìn sá meetab biwa ní. Bi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ dikɔl yam, di-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meeta ubɔ nì dijandi ki tɔ́kɔǹ jaantalku kamaa yilpu. Bi nìn dū tasa ki lēē tilaandi yam nì greenaadi biliŋ ki nyɔ̄kɔntì ki māntìi tú-bi. Jaantalkub liitilee nì bi-laanti nìn sá tiwambaantiil ní.

english_verse: near Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar had them killed. Most of the people of Judah had been carried away as captives from their own country. Gedaliah Is Made Ruler of the People Left in Judah (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ní Babiloon bɔtiu kūū bi-kɔkɔ Riibila tiŋkin, Amaati tiŋkpaaŋkin. An nín dī pu ní bi cúú Juuda yab kuyuŋu ki jìn̄-bi bi-tiŋki puee dee. Geedaliyasi, Juuda tiŋki gɔminau (Kpèè Yeer

english_verse: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbanti kí tin sāā Yooyakiin kúm dalee, Babiloon bɔtiu di nìn tìì-u tin u máaǹ kí nīn cáá ki bí dimaŋfalinee.

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the desert,
translation_verse: Babiloon yab lùkū dibundi digundi din nìn māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee. Kunyeeuee, min kamaa Babiloon janjaliibi māntìi tú-kèe, Juuda janjaliibi dūu dī kipunyɔkɔ kin bi dìŋfī ki cá ubɔti kuŋfaati kpaabun, kì bí agunlɔkɔ ali kansikinee ki sáǹ. Ubɔti Seedeesiyasi nìn kíĺ nsan ŋun cá Jɔɔdan tantakalinee ki nín cá.

english_verse: but the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah, but his soldiers scattered in every direction.
translation_verse: Ama Babiloon janjaliibi nìn kùl̄ ki bīiǹ ubɔti boon ní ki jìn̄ ki tin cúú-u Jeeriikoo tantakalin. Niinee ní u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ sáǹ ki yàl̄ ki dū-u ki fá.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Babiloon yab nìn cúú ubɔti ní ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon bɔtiu cee, Riibila tiŋkin. Niin ní bi sòon̄ u-bɔti.

english_verse: About a month later, in Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king, Nebuzaradan, who was his official in charge of the guards, arrived in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nín jíń dibeel dibindi diba kpá mmuŋku, uŋmaŋmooŋmooti winluluútiŋu poonee, ní Neebusaradan kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. U nìn sá Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpiliu ubɔ ní ki nìn sá bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Babiloon yab janjaliibi bin nìn céeǹní ujanjakpilee nìn gbáń ki wīī digundi din bi nìn máń ki tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee.

english_verse: He led away as prisoners the people left in the city, including those who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Neebusaradan nìn cúú bin kɔkɔ nìn kíǹ ki gbíntìi bí Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, an dàkà yii bin nìn sáǹ ki kɔ́ Babiloon yabee nì bin kɔkɔ nìn pée kíǹ ki bí niinee.

english_verse: Only some of the poorest people were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
translation_verse: Ama u nìn yāntì biwɔfib kansikin biba bíǹ ń nīn bí ki kù fiinyib nì tikpaajin tisatin.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers took the two bronze columns that stood in front of the temple, the ten movable bronze stands, and the large bronze bowl called the Sea. They broke them into pieces so they could take the bronze to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Babiloon yab nìn gbáń ki wīī ti-Dindaan Diiku jaantalkub bin bi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee. Bi nìn gbáń ki wīī tɔrɔkub nì kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu kun bi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ an bí ti-Dindaan Diiku cindinee. Bi nìn yōoǹ kusɔŋu gbanti ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin.

english_verse: They carried off the bronze things used for worship at the temple, including the pans for hot ashes, and the shovels, snuffers, and also the dishes for incense,
translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti yōoǹ ŋfantam kumbɔbiyaamu nì peelab nì njimu nì kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi nìn pée dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ bi cáa tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan Diikunee.

english_verse: as well as the fire pans and the sprinkling bowls. Nebuzaradan ordered his soldiers to take everything made of gold or silver.
translation_verse: Bijanjaliibi bin cīití ubɔtee kpiliu nìn gíti yōoǹ kisambiki kin poon ní bi nìn tùutī talaalubee nì kisambiki kin poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki cáa yàantée. Tiwan gbanti kɔkɔee, sindaariya àá animbil kúti ní bi nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́-tì.

english_verse: The pile of bronze from the columns, the stands, and the large bowl that Solomon had made for the temple was too large to be weighed.
translation_verse: Tasa kúti tin ní Saloomɔn nìn yāntì bi dūu mɔ́ɔ́ jaantalkub liitil nì kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì tɔrɔkub ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diikunee nyiŋfiŋu kaa nìn cáá bí dūú ŋmàntī.

english_verse: Then he arrested one of the army commanders, the king's five personal advisors, and the officer in charge of gathering the troops for battle. He also found
translation_verse: U nìn gíti cúú ukàlinjakpaan un nìn kpèé bijanjaliibi bɔtee nì ubɔti saŋkiliibi biŋmoo bin nìn bí kitiŋinee. U nìn gíti cúú ujanjakpil un nìn fòol̄ bijanjaliibi ki gíti sá ugbaŋŋmalee nì Juuda yab binib imuŋku ita kitiŋin niin.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam to rule the few people still living in Judah.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn yāntì binib biba gbíntì Juuda tiŋkin. U nìn lēē Ayiikaam jipɔɔn, Cafan naantiiu Geedaliyasi ki kāaǹ gɔmina ú nīn kpòotī-bi.

english_verse: When the army officers and troops heard that Gedaliah was their ruler, the officers met with him at Mizpah. These men were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, and Jaazaniah from Maacah.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní Juuda yab janjakpilib nì bi-janjaliibi bin kaa nìn dū bi-ba ki tīī Babiloon yab kí kpántí bi-yumbuuyee nín gbìl̄ yii Babiloon bɔtiu dū Geedaliyasi ki kāaǹ gɔminee ní bi cūtìi ká-u Miisipa. Bijanjakpilib bin nìn cūtèe di sá Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nì Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì Taneewumeeti jipɔɔn Seeraya nì Neetoofa nì Yasaniyawuu nì Maaka.

english_verse: Gedaliah said to them, “Everything will be fine, I promise. We don't need to be afraid of the Babylonian rulers, if we live here peacefully and do what Nebuchadnezzar says.”
translation_verse: Geedaliyasi nìn tùkū bi-kɔkɔ yii: «Ní taa fàŋkì Babiloon yab. Nimbi dee, ní kàl̄maan kitiŋ nee poon kí sìntī ni-ba kí tīī Babiloon bɔtiu ní an kɔkɔ ń còom̀ tiŋan kí tīī-ni.»

english_verse: Ishmael was from the royal family. And about two months after Gedaliah began his rule, Ishmael and ten other men went to Mizpah. They killed Gedaliah and his officials, including those from Judah and those from Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ama dibindi poon ŋmaluluútiu poonee, Neetaniya jipɔɔn, Eeliisama naantiiu Isimaayeel un gíti sá Juuda bɔtiu dicaŋkun ubɔee nì binib saalaa táá ki cūtì Miisipa. Bi bàn̄ee ní ki kūū Geedaliyasi nì Juuda yab nì Babiloon yab bin nìn bí u-ceeyee.

english_verse: After that, the army officers and all the people in Mizpah, whether important or not, were afraid of what the Babylonians might do. So they left Judah and went to Egypt. Jehoiachin Is Set Free (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Niinee kí yòon̄ kibiki kí cáá sāā ukpaan nì bijanjakpilibee kɔkɔ kíĺ nsan ki nín cá Eejipiti, di sá yii bi nìn fāŋkì Babiloon yab. Babiloon bɔtiu nyántì ubɔti Yooyakiin kusaarkadiin (Kpèè Yeer

english_verse: Evil-Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: U nìn sòoǹ nì u kubɔɔtiiu poon ní ki nìn kāaǹ-u mpaan ŋun jítiǹ bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí u-cee Babiloon tiŋkinee yai.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was even allowed to wear regular clothes, and he ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: U nìn yāntì Yooyakiin kaa ti pèentí disarkabɔkutil. Yooyakiin nì Babiloon bɔtiu di nìn kíǹ ki jīǹ disambibaantiilin baabadal.

english_verse: Japheth was the father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras, and they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
translation_verse: Jafeeti jipɔmbi di sá Goomeer nì Maagoogi nì Madayi nì Yafan nì Tubaal nì Meeseeki nì Tiiraasi.

english_verse: Abraham and his slave woman Keturah had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan.
translation_verse: Keetura, Abraam nimpuwaaki di màl̄ Siimran nì Yɔkisan nì Meedan nì Madiyan nì Yiisbaaki nì Suuwa. Yɔkisan jipɔmbi di sá Seeba nì Deedan.

english_verse: Ethiopia was also the father of Nimrod, the world's first mighty warrior.
translation_verse: Kuusi di màl̄ Neemiroodi un sá ubaatandaan upeekaa kitiŋ puee.

english_verse: Egypt was the ancestor of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
translation_verse: Miisirayiim di màl̄ Luudi yab nì Anam yab nì Leeyaab yab nì Nafituu yab,

english_verse: Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
translation_verse: Goomeer jipɔmbi di sá Asikeenaasi nì Diifaati nì Toogarma.

english_verse: Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
translation_verse: Yafan jipɔmbi di sá Eeliisa nì Taarsiisi nì Kiitiim nì Roodaniim.

english_verse: Ham was the father of Ethiopia, Egypt, Put, and Canaan, and they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
translation_verse: Kaam jipɔmbi di sá Kuusi nì Miisirayiim nì Puuti nì Kanaan.

english_verse: Ethiopia was the ancestor of Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah was the ancestor of Sheba and Dedan.
translation_verse: Kuusi jipɔmbi di sá Seeba nì Afiila nì Sabita nì Rama nì Sabiteeka. Rama jipɔmbi di sá Keeba nì Deedan.

english_verse: Canaan's oldest son was Sidon; his other son was Heth.
translation_verse: Kanaan màl̄ u-jipɔŋkpiliu Siidɔn, ní ki dū Eeti ki páaǹ.

english_verse: Shem was the ancestor of Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech; they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
translation_verse: Seem jipɔmbi di sá Eelam nì Asuur nì Aripakisaadi nì Luudi nì Aram nì Usi nì Kuul nì Geeteer nì Meeseeki.

english_verse: Arpachshad was Shelah's father and Eber's grandfather.
translation_verse: Aripakisaadi màl̄ Seera, ní Seera màl̄ Eebeer.

english_verse: Eber named his first son Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided into tribal regions. Eber's second son was Joktan,
translation_verse: Eebeer màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muli ní. Bi yíì ujipɔŋkpil yii Peeleegi, taapu di sá yii <diyakatil>, kun puee úǹ yuntiŋu ní binib nìn cúu yākatì tɔbin kitiŋ pu. U-naal ní bi nìn yíì Yɔkitan.

english_verse: the ancestor of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Ebal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab.
translation_verse: nì Oofiiri nì Afiila nì Yoobaab. Yɔkitan jipɔmbi di sá bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Shem's descendants included Arpachshad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, and Abram, later renamed Abraham. Abraham's Family (Genesis
translation_verse: ní Teera màl̄ Abram. Abram ní bi gíti yíì Abraam.

english_verse: Abraham was the father of Isaac and Ishmael.
translation_verse: Abraam jipɔmbi di sá Isaaki nì Isimaayeel.

english_verse: Midian was the father of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. Esau's Family (Genesis
translation_verse: Madiyan jipɔmbi di sá Eefa nì Eefeer nì Anɔki nì Abiida nì Eeldaa. Keetura naantiibi di sá bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Abraham's son Isaac was the father of Esau and Jacob.
translation_verse: Abraam di màl̄ Isaaki. Isaaki jipɔmbi di sá Eesayuu nì Jaakɔb.

english_verse: Esau was the father of Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Eesayuu jipɔmbi di sá Eeliifaasi nì Reewuyeel nì Yeewusi nì Yalaam nì Koora.

english_verse: Reuel was the father of Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. The First Edomites and Their Kings (Genesis
translation_verse: Reewuyeel jipɔmbi di sá Nakati nì Seera nì Sama nì Miisa.

english_verse: Before kings ruled in Israel, Bela son of Beor ruled the country of Edom from its capital of Dinhabah.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi bin nìn kāl̀ abee Eedoom tiŋki pu ki wāatì ní Isirayeel yab nín kíĺ ki kàantí bibɔtiibee yiŋŋi sɔ̀. Upeepeekaa di sá Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn Beela un sá Diinaba tiŋkinee.

english_verse: Seir was the father of Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
translation_verse: Seeyiir jipɔmbi di sá Lootan nì Soobaal nì Siibeeyɔn. Siibeeyɔn di nìn sá Ana baa nì Diisɔn nì Eeseer nì Diisan naanja.

english_verse: Lotan was the father of Hori and Homam; Lotan's sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lootan jipɔmbi di sá Oori nì Ɔmam. Lootan niisal di sá Tiimina.

english_verse: Shobal was the father of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon was the father of Aiah and Anah.
translation_verse: Soobaal jipɔmbi di sá Aliyan nì Manakaati nì Eebaal nì Seefii nì Oonam. Siibeeyɔn jipɔmbi di sá Aya nì Ana.

english_verse: Anah was the father of Dishon and the grandfather of Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Ana jipɔɔn di sá Diisɔn. Diisɔn jipɔmbi di sá Amiiran nì Eesban nì Yiitiran nì Keeran.

english_verse: Ezer was the father of Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan was the father of Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Eeseer jipɔmbi di sá Biiliyan nì Saafan nì Yaakan. Diisɔn jipɔmbi di gíti sá Usi nì Aran. Eedoom yab bɔtiibi nì bi-yidambi yiŋŋi (Kpèè Diny

english_verse: After Bela's death, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah became king.
translation_verse: Beela kpíì ní Seera jipɔɔn Joobaab un sá Boosiraa tiŋkinee fōō dibeel.

english_verse: After Jobab's death, Husham from the land of Teman became king.
translation_verse: Joobaab kpíì ní Usaam un sá Teeman yab tiŋkinee fōō dibeel.

english_verse: After Husham's death, Hadad son of Bedad became king and ruled from Avith. Earlier, Bedad had defeated the Midianites in the territory of Moab.
translation_verse: Usaam kpíì ní Beedaadi jipɔɔn Adaadi fōō dibeel. Úǹ di nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Madiyan yab Moowaab satinee. U-tiŋki yindi di sá Afiiti.

english_verse: After Hadad's death, Samlah from Masrekah became king;
translation_verse: Adaadi kpíì ní Samla un sá Masireeka tiŋkinee fōō dibeel.

english_verse: after Samlah's death, Shaul from the town of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River became king;
translation_verse: Samla kpíì ní Sawuul un sá Reewoobooti, kitiŋ kin bí Eefiraati mɔɔkpaandi caŋinee fōō dibeel.

english_verse: and after Shaul's death, Baal Hanan son of Achbor became king.
translation_verse: Sawuul kpíì ní Akibɔɔr jipɔɔn Baal-Anan fōō dibeel.

english_verse: After Baal Hanan's death, Hadad ruled from Pai. His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab.
translation_verse: Baal-Anan kpíì ní Adaadi fōō dibeel. U-tiŋki yindi di sá Payii. U-nimpuu di sá Meetabeel un sá Matireedi bisal nì Meesayaab naantiiuee.

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: nì Ooliibama nì Eela nì Piinɔn,

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: nì Keenaasi nì Teeman nì Miibsaar,

english_verse: Jacob was the father of twelve sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
translation_verse: nì Daani nì Jooseefi nì Beenjameen nì Neefitalii nì Gaadi nì Aseer.

english_verse: Judah and his Canaanite wife Bathshua had three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah. But the Lord had Er put to death, because he disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Juuda jipɔmbi di sá Eer nì Oonan nì Seera. U-nimpuu, Suuwa bisal un sá Kanaan tiŋkinee di màl̄ u-jipɔmbi gbanti taatil. Ama ní u-jipɔŋkpiliu Eer nìn ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee ní úǹ yāntì u kpíì.

english_verse: Judah and his daughter-in-law Tamar also had two sons: Perez and Zerah.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Juuda coopu Taamaar dāa gíti màl̄-u Peereesi nì Seera. U-jipɔmbi kɔkɔ nìn nyáń biŋmoo dee.

english_verse: Perez was the father of Hezron and Hamul.
translation_verse: Peereesi jipɔmbi di sá Eesirɔn nì Amuul.

english_verse: Zerah was the father of Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda.
translation_verse: Seera jipɔmbi di sá Simrii nì Eetan nì Eeman nì Kaalkool nì Daara. Bi mun nyáń binib biŋmoo dee.

english_verse: Achan, who was a descendant of Zerah and the son of Carmi, caused trouble for Israel, because he kept for himself things that belonged only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Kaarmii jipɔɔn di sá Akaar. Úǹ di nìn cáań nnaabu ki tɔ́ Isirayeel yab pu. Di sá yii u nìn yōoǹ tiwan tin bi jáń ki fōō kujaaun bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee.

english_verse: Ethan's son was Azariah. The Ancestors of King David
translation_verse: Eetan jipɔɔn di sá Asariya.

english_verse: Hezron was the father of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
translation_verse: Eesirɔn jipɔmbi di sá Yeerameeyeel nì Raam nì Kaleeb un bi gíti yíì yii Keelubaayee.

english_verse: Ram was the father of Amminadab and the grandfather of Nahshon, a tribal leader of Judah.
translation_verse: Raam di màl̄ Amiinadaab ní Amiinadaab màl̄ Naasɔn un sá Juuda yab kpiliuee.

english_verse: Nahshon's descendants included Salma, Boaz,
translation_verse: Naasɔn di màl̄ Salima ní Salima màl̄ Boowaasi.

english_verse: Jesse also had two daughters: Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah was the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
translation_verse: Bi-niisalib di sá Seeruya nì Abiigayiil. Seeruya jipɔmbi di sá Abisayi nì Joowaab nì Asayeel. Bi nyáń bita dee.

english_verse: Abigail's husband was Jether, who was a descendant of Ishmael, and their son was Amasa. The Descendants of Hezron
translation_verse: Abiigayiil di màl̄ Amaasa. Amaasa baa di sá Yeeteer un sá Isimaayeel maaliŋunee.

english_verse: Hezron's son Caleb married Azubah, and their daughter was Jerioth, the mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
translation_verse: Eesirɔn jipɔɔn Kaleeb nimpoobi Asuuba nì Jeeriyɔɔti màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu muta. Bíǹ di sá Jeeseer nì Soobaab nì Ardɔn.

english_verse: After the death of Azubah, Caleb married Ephrath. Their son Hur
translation_verse: Asuuba kúm boonee ní Kaleeb cáá Eefiraati ní úǹ màl̄-u Uur.

english_verse: was the father of Uri and the grandfather of Bezalel.
translation_verse: Uur màl̄ Urii ní Urii màl̄ Beesaleel.

english_verse: was the father of Jair, who ruled
translation_verse: Seeguub di màl̄ Yayiir un nìn ŋúb́ ntimu mmuŋku nì muta Galaadi tiŋkinee.

english_verse: After the death of Hezron, Caleb married Ephrath, his father's wife. Their son was Ashhur, who later settled the town of Tekoa. The Descendants of Jerahmeel
translation_verse: Eesirɔn kúm boonee, Kaleeb nìn kpáfì nì u-baa Eesirɔn nimpuu Abiiya, Eefiraata tiŋkin ní ki màl̄ Aseekuur un náań Teekoowa tiŋkee.

english_verse: Jerahmeel, Hezron's oldest son, was the father of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
translation_verse: Eesirɔn jipɔŋkpiliu Jeerameeyeel jipɔmpeekaau di sá Raam. Bin kíǹee di sá Buuna nì Ooreen nì Ooseem nì Akiya.

english_verse: Jerahmeel had a second wife, Atarah, who gave birth to Onam.
translation_verse: Jeerameeyeel gíti cáá unimpu ubɔ bi yíì-u yii Atara. Úǹ di sá Oonam na.

english_verse: Ram was the father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
translation_verse: Jeerameeyeel jipɔmpeekaau Raam jipɔmbi di sá Maasi nì Yamiini nì Eekeer.

english_verse: Onam was the father of Shammai and Jada. Shammai was the father of Nadab and Abishur.
translation_verse: Oonam jipɔmbi di sá Samayii nì Yaada, ní Samayii jipɔmbi sá Nadaab nì Abiisuur.

english_verse: Abishur married Abihail, and their two sons were Ahban and Molid.
translation_verse: Abiisuur nimpuu Abiyayiil màl̄-u Akiban nì Mooliidi.

english_verse: Nadab was the father of Seled and Appaim. Seled had no children;
translation_verse: Nadaab jipɔmbi di sá Seeleedi nì Apayiim. Ní Seeleedi kpíì kaa màl̄.

english_verse: Appaim's son was Ishi, the father of Sheshan and the grandfather of Ahlai.
translation_verse: Apayiim jipɔɔn di sá Yiseeyi. Yiseeyi jipɔɔn di sá Seesan. Seesan jipɔɔn di sá Alayi.

english_verse: Jada was the father of Jether and Jonathan. Jether had no children,
translation_verse: Samayii naal Yaada jipɔmbi di sá Yeeteer nì Joonatan. Yeeteer kaa màl̄ ní ki kpíì.

english_verse: but Jonathan had two sons: Peleth and Zaza.
translation_verse: Joonatan jipɔmbi di sá Peeleeti nì Saasa. Yeerameel naantiibi dee.

english_verse: Sheshan had no sons, and so he let one of his daughters marry Jarha, his Egyptian slave. Their son was Attai,
translation_verse: Ní Seesan lēē u-bisalib ubɔ ki tīī u-yumbuu gbanti u cáá, ní ki màl̄ Atayii.

english_verse: the father of Nathan and the grandfather of Zabad.
translation_verse: Atayii di màl̄ Naatan ní Naatan màl̄ Sabaadi.

english_verse: Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, had the following descendants: Mesha, Ziph, Mareshah, Hebron,
translation_verse: Jeerameeyeel naal Kaleeb naantiibi di sá u-jipɔŋkpiliu Meesa, Siifi baa biyaamu nì Mareesa, Eebrɔn baa naantiibi.

english_verse: and Hebron's four sons, Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
translation_verse: Eebrɔn jipɔmbi di sá Koora nì Tapuuwa nì Reekeem nì Seema.

english_verse: Shema was the father of Raham and the grandfather of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai,
translation_verse: Seema di màl̄ Rakam ní Rakam màl̄ Jɔɔrkeeyam. Reekeem di màl̄ Samayii.

english_verse: the grandfather of Maon, and the great-grandfather of Bethzur.
translation_verse: Samayii màl̄ Mawɔn ní Mawɔn màl̄ Beeti-Suur.

english_verse: Ephah was one of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran named his son after his brother Gazez.
translation_verse: Kaleeb gíti cáá unimpu ubɔ bi yíì-u yii Eefa. Eefa di màl̄ Aran nì Moosa nì Gaseesi. Aran mun màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Gaseesi.

english_verse: Ephah was the daughter of Jahdai, who was also the father of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, and Shaaph.
translation_verse: Yaadayi jipɔmbi di sá Reegeem nì Jootam nì Geesan nì Peeleeti nì Eefa nì Saafi.

english_verse: Maacah was another of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Sheber and Tirhanah.
translation_verse: Kaleeb gíti cáá unimpu ubɔ bi yíì-u yii Maaka. Maaka di màl̄ Seebeer nì Tiirana.

english_verse: Later, they had two more sons: Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Maaka dāa gíti màl̄ Madimana baa Saafi, ní ki kútì Makibeena nì Giibeeya baa Seefa. Kaleeb cáá bisal ubɔ, bi yíì-u yii Akisa.

english_verse: Shobal, who settled the town of Kiriath-Jearim, was the ancestor of Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth clan,
translation_verse: Soobaal un náań Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋkee naantiibi di sá binib bin kóò Aroowee tiŋkinee nì bin kóò Meenuwɔti tiŋkinee dijandi,

english_verse: and the clans that lived near Kiriath-Jearim; they were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zorathites and the Eshtaolites were descendants of the Mishraites.
translation_verse: nì Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim yab nín pēē pēē mmaal puee, an dàkà yii Yitirii yab nì Puuti yab nì Suuma yab nì Miisiraa yab. Binib gbanti kansikin biba di sá Soora tiŋki yab nì Eesitawool tiŋki yab.

english_verse: Salma settled the town of Bethlehem and was the ancestor of the Netophathites, the people of Atroth-Bethjoab, half of the Manahathite clan, and the Zorites.
translation_verse: Salima naantiibi di sá Beetileem tiŋki yab nì Neetoofa tiŋki yab nì Atarooti-Beeti-Joowaab tiŋki yab nì Manaati tiŋki yab dijandi nì Koora yab,

english_verse: Salma was also the ancestor of the clans in Jabez that kept the court and government records; they were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These clans were the descendants of Hammath the Kenite, who was also the ancestor of the Rechabites.
translation_verse: nì bigbannyiliibi bin kóò Jabeesi tiŋkin ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee, an dàkà yii Tiirati yab nì Simeeya yab nì Suuka yab. Bíǹ di sá Keen yab bin nyánní Amaati maaliŋun, ki sá Reekaab yab naanjee.

english_verse: David's other sons included Ibhar, Elishua, Eliphelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
