translation_verse: nì Eeliisama nì Eeliyadaa nì Eeliifeeleeti. Bi nyáń binib biwa dee.

english_verse: David's other wives also gave birth to sons. Tamar was his daughter. The Descendants of King Solomon
translation_verse: Daafiidi jipɔmbi di sá bi-kɔkɔ, ní kí nín kūtì bin ní u-nimpuwaamu mun màl̄ màl̄-uee. Bi-niisal di sá Taamaar.

english_verse: Solomon's descendants included the following kings: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah, Azariah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, and Josiah and his four sons, Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Joosiyaasi jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Yoowanan, u-jipɔnliliitiu di sá Yooyakiim, utataati di sá Seedeekiyasi, ní unanaati sá Saluum.

english_verse: Jehoiakim was the father of Jehoiachin and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: Yooyakiim jipɔɔn di sá Jeekooniya ní u-naantiiu sá Seedeekiyasi.

english_verse: Jehoiachin, who was taken to Babylon as a prisoner, had seven sons: Shealtiel,
translation_verse: Jeekooniya un bi nìn cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee jipɔɔn di sá Saltiyeel,

english_verse: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
translation_verse: ní u-naantiibi sá Malkiiraam nì Peedaya nì Seenasaar nì Jeekamiya nì Oosama nì Neebadiya.

english_verse: Pedaiah had two sons: Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel was the father of Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister.
translation_verse: Peedaya jipɔmbi di sá Sooroobabeel nì Simeeyii. Sooroobabeel jipɔmbi di sá Meesulam nì Ananiya, ní bi-niisal sá Seeloomiiti.

english_verse: He also had five other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushabhesed.
translation_verse: U-jipɔmbi di gíti sá Asuuba nì Ookeel nì Beereekiya nì Asadiya nì Jusaab-Eeseedi. Bíǹ nyáń binib biŋmoo dee.

english_verse: Hananiah's descendants were Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah,
translation_verse: Ananiya jipɔɔn di sá Peelatiya ní u-naantiibi sá Jeesaya nì Arinan nì Oobadiya nì Seekaniya.

english_verse: the father of Shemaiah and the grandfather of Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
translation_verse: Seekaniya jipɔmbi di sá Seemaya nì Atuusi nì Igaal nì Bariya nì Neeyariya nì Safaati. Bi nyáń binib biluu dee.

english_verse: Neariah was the father of Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
translation_verse: Neeyariya jipɔmbi di sá Eeliyooweenayi nì Isikiya nì Asiirikam. Bi nyáń binib bita dee.

english_verse: Elioenai was the father of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
translation_verse: Eeliyooweenayi jipɔmbi di sá Ɔdafiya nì Eeliyasiib nì Peelaya nì Akuub nì Yoowanan nì Deelaya nì Ananii. Bi nyáń binib biluli dee.

english_verse: Judah was the father of five sons: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
translation_verse: Juuda naantiibi di gíti sá Peereesi nì Eesirɔn nì Kaarmii nì Uur nì Soobaal.

english_verse: Shobal was the father of Reaiah, the grandfather of Jahath, and the great-grandfather of Ahumai and Lahad. These men all belonged to the Zorathite clan.
translation_verse: Soobaal jipɔɔn Raaya di màl̄ Yakaati, ní Yakaati màl̄ Akumayi nì Lakaadi. Bíǹ di sá Soora tiŋki yab naanjab ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee.

english_verse: Ashhur, who settled the town of Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.
translation_verse: Aseewuur di náań Teekoowa tiŋki. U nìn cáá binimpoobi bili ní. Bi yíì ubɔ Eela ní ki yíì un kíǹ Naara.

english_verse: daughters. But his brothers did not have as many children, so the Simeon tribe was smaller than the Judah tribe.
translation_verse: Naara nìn màl̄-u Awusam nì Eefeer nì Teeminii nì Akastarii. Naara jipɔmbi dee.

english_verse: Ashhur and Helah were the parents of Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
translation_verse: Eela jipɔmbi di sá Seereeti nì Soowaar nì Eetinan.

english_verse: Koz, the father of Anub and Zobebah, was also the ancestor of the clans of Aharhel, the son of Harum.
translation_verse: Kɔɔsi di màl̄ Anuub nì Soobeeba ní ki sá Aruum jipɔɔn Areeyeel maaliŋun yab naanja.

english_verse: Jabez was a man who got his name because of the pain he caused his mother during birth. But he was still the most respected son in his family.
translation_verse: Jabeesi nìn cáá tinyool ki jítiǹ u-mambi nì u-naalib bin kíǹee kɔkɔ. Di sá yii u-na nín màl̄-uee, u pú-u diyindi yii Jabeesi ki lī yii: «An píĺ-mi ní m nín màl̄-u.»

english_verse: One day he prayed to Israel's God, “Please bless me and give me a lot of land. Be with me so I will be safe from harm.” And God did just what Jabez had asked.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Jabeesi mēē Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ki lī yii: «A yaa lafun yú m-boon, á yàntī m-tinjandi ń wàan̄ kí kūtì. Wúń m-pu, ní kí jà nnaabu nì dinimbinaamandi kí wàatī-mi.» Unimbɔti nìn kíí ki ŋá tin Jabeesi mēē-uee ki tīī-u.

english_verse: Chelub was the brother of Shuhah and the father of Mehir. Later, Mehir had a son, Eshton,
translation_verse: Suuwa naal Keeluub di màl̄ Meekiir ní Meekiir màl̄ Eesitɔn.

english_verse: whose three sons were Bethrapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. It was Tehinnah who settled the town of Nahash. These men and their families lived in the town of Recah.
translation_verse: Ní Eesitɔn màl̄ Beeti-Raafa nì Paseeya nì Teekiina un náań Iir-Naasi tiŋkee. Bi-naantiibi nìn kāl̀ Reeka tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: Kenaz was the father of Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel had two sons: Hathath and Meonothai,
translation_verse: Keenaasi jipɔmbi di sá Ootiniyeel nì Seeraya. Ootiniyeel jipɔmbi di sá Ataati nì Meeyɔnootayi.

english_verse: who was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, who settled a place called “Valley of Crafts” because the people who lived there were experts in making things.
translation_verse: Meeyɔnootayi di màl̄ Oofiraa. Seeraya di màl̄ Joowaab un sá binib bin tūǹ ŋŋal pu tundi ki kóò Iŋal pu tɔntɔnliibi tantakalinee naanja.

english_verse: Caleb son of Jephunneh had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah was the father of Kenaz.
translation_verse: Yeefunee jipɔɔn Kaleeb jipɔmbi di sá Iruu nì Eela nì Naam. Eela jipɔɔn di sá Keenaasi.

english_verse: Ezrah was the father of Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered was married to Bithiah the daughter of the king of Egypt. They had a daughter named Miriam and two sons: Shammai and Ishbah. It was Ishbah who settled the town of Eshtemoa. Mered was also married to a woman from the tribe of Judah, and their sons were Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel. Jered settled the town of Gedor; Heber settled the town of Soco; and Jekuthiel settled the town of Zanoah.
translation_verse: Eesiraasi jipɔmbi di sá Yeeteer nì Meereedi nì Eefeer nì Yalɔn. Meereedi nìn cáá Eejipiti bɔtiu bisal Biitiya. Biitiya nìn màl̄-u Miiriyam nì Samayii nì Iseeba un náań Eesiteemoowa tiŋkee. Meereedi nìn gíti cáá unimpu ubɔ, u sá kijuudabiki. Úǹ di màl̄-u Yeereedi un náań Geedɔɔr tiŋkee, nì Eebeer un náań Sookoo tiŋkee, nì Yeekutiyeel un náań Sanoowa tiŋkee.

english_verse: A man named Hodiah was married to the sister of Naham. Hodiah's descendants included Keilah of the Garmite clan and Eshtemoa of the Maacathite clan.
translation_verse: Oodiya nìn cáá Naam niisal ubɔ. U-niboolii di sá Garimii maaliŋun yab bin kóò Keeyiila tiŋkinee nì Maaka maaliŋun yab bin kóò Eesteemoowa tiŋkinee.

english_verse: Shimon was the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. Ishi was the father of Zoheth and Benzoheth.
translation_verse: Siimɔn jipɔmbi di sá Aminɔn nì Riina nì Been-Anaani nì Tiilɔn. Iseeyii jipɔmbi di sá Sooweeti nì Been-Sooweeti.

english_verse: The members of these clans were the potters who lived in the towns of Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king. The Descendants of Simeon
translation_verse: Bi-naantiibi nìn sá biyɔɔmaatiibi ní. Bi nìn kóòń Neetayiim nì Geedeera timmun ní ki tūǹ ditundi ki tìì ubɔti. Simeeyɔn naantiibi

english_verse: Simeon had five sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
translation_verse: Simeeyɔn jipɔmbi di sá Neemuyeel nì Yamiini nì Yariib nì Seera nì Saayuul.

english_verse: The descendants of Shaul included his son Shallum, his grandson Mibsam, and his great-grandson Mishma.
translation_verse: Saayuul maaliŋun yab di sá Saluum nì Miibsam nì Miisima.

english_verse: The descendants of Mishma included his son Hammuel, his grandson Zaccur, and his great-grandson Shimei.
translation_verse: Miisima maaliŋun yab di sá Miiseema jipɔɔn Amuyeel nì Amuyeel jipɔɔn Sakuur nì Sakuur jipɔɔn Simeeyii.

english_verse: Before David became king, the people of the Simeon tribe lived in the following towns: Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazarsusim, Bethbiri, and Shaaraim.
translation_verse: nì Beeti-Markabooti nì Asaar-Susiim nì Beeti-Biirii nì Saarayiim. Ntimu gbantin ní bi nìn kóò áli Daafiidi dāa kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: They also lived in the five villages of Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan,
translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti kóò Eetaam nì Ayiin nì Riimɔn nì Tookeen nì Asaan timbilimmun. Mu nìn nyáń ntimbilimu muŋmoo ní,

english_verse: as well as in the nearby villages as far as the town of Baal. These are the places where Simeon's descendants had settled, according to their own family records.
translation_verse: ki kpáaǹ ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-muee, ki tin cáa sāā Balaati tiŋki. Ntimu gbantin ní bi nìn kóò. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ bi-dicaŋŋi kpilib yiŋŋi ki ŋá dikàandi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: As their families and clans became larger, the people of Simeon had the following leaders: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah, Joel, Jehu, Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza.
translation_verse: Bin yiŋŋi bi dáá yíiń nee nìn sá bi-maaliŋu poon kpilib, ní bi-dicaŋŋi nib nìn būtì tiŋan tiŋan pu.

english_verse: When the people needed more pastureland for their flocks and herds, they looked as far as the eastern side of the valley where the town of Gerar is located,
translation_verse: An pu ní bi nìn kpátìi gbí an kɔkɔ áli ki tin dūu gūū Geedɔɔr tiŋki, ditantakal ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, ki nyàab̀ kupikpaapɔɔu kí kpàà bi-piii.

english_verse: and they found a lot of good pastureland that was quiet and undisturbed. This had once belonged to the Hamites,
translation_verse: Niin ní bi ká kupikpaapɔɔu kumɔntiiu timool bí ki sɔ̀m̀ fílfil. Kitiŋ gbanti nìn wāā ní ŋgbansɔŋfi bí ki-pu. Cannaakuee, Kaam naantiibi di nìn kóò niin.

english_verse: Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob, but he lost his rights as the first-born son because he slept with one of his father's wives. The honor of the first-born son was then given to Joseph,
translation_verse: Jaakɔb biseebiki Rubeen jipɔmbi sèé. Rubeen di sá Jaakɔb jipɔŋkpiliu. Ama u nìn dōoǹ nì u-baa nimpoobi kansikin ubɔ. Míǹ boonee ní bi cúú tijipɔŋkpiti ki fōō u-cee ki dūu tīī Jooseefi jipɔmbi. Jooseefi mun nìn sá Isirayeel jipɔmbi kansikin ubɔ ní. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, baa nìn gíti dū Rubeen ki yíiń ujipɔŋkpil.

english_verse: Reuben had four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb jipɔŋkpiliu Rubeen jipɔmbi di sá Anɔki nì Palu nì Eesirɔn nì Kaarmii.

english_verse: The descendants of Joel included Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, Baal, and Beerah, a leader of the Reuben tribe. Later, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria took Beerah away as prisoner.
translation_verse: nì Baal jipɔɔn Beera. Beera nìn sá Rubeen naakookun yab kpiliu ubɔ ní Asuur bɔtiu Tiigilaati-Piilneeseer nìn cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋu.

english_verse: The family records also include Jeiel, who was a clan leader, Zechariah, and Bela son of Azaz and grandson of Shema of the Joel clan. They lived in the territory around the town of Aroer, as far north as Nebo and Baal-Meon,
translation_verse: ní ki páaǹ Asaasi jipɔɔn Beela. Beela sá Seema naantiiu nì Jooweel naantitɔntɔkɔl ní. Rubeen yab nìn kóò kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ kí yòon̄ Arooweer tiŋki ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Neeboo jool nì Baal-Meeyɔn tiŋki ŋgan púee ní.

english_verse: and as far east as the desert just west of the Euphrates River. They needed this much land because they owned too many cattle to keep them all in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, bi nìn kóò kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ ki tin cáa sāā kuteeu kun yākatì bi nì Eefiraati mɔɔlee nín kífí púee ní, kun puee bi-waŋkuti nìn būtì Galaadi tiŋki pu tikpilku.

english_verse: When Saul was king, the Reuben tribe attacked and defeated the Hagrites, then took over their land east of Gilead. The Descendants of Gad
translation_verse: Ubɔti Saayuul yuntiŋuee, bi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Agaar maaliŋun yab ní ki fōō mpaan ki kāl̀ Galaadi tiŋki kin dɔ̄ ŋgan púee kɔkɔ. Gaadi naantiibi

english_verse: The tribe of Gad lived in the region of Bashan, north of the Reuben tribe. Gad's territory extended all the way to the town of Salecah.
translation_verse: Gaadi naakookun yab nìn kóò Rubeen yab tiŋki ŋgan pú ní, Baasan tiŋki kí tin cáá sāā Salka tiŋki.

english_verse: Some of the clan leaders were Joel, Shapham, Janai, and Shaphat.
translation_verse: Baasan tiŋkin niinee, bi-kpiliu upeepeekaa di nìn sá Jooweel, uliliiti di sá Safan, ní ki páaǹ Jaanayi nì Safaati.

english_verse: They were all descendants of Abihail, whose family line went back through Huri, Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz.
translation_verse: Urii jipɔɔn Abiikayiil niboolii di sá bikpilib gbanti. Abiikayiil naanjab di sá Jaroowa nì Galaadi nì Miikayeel nì Jeesisaayi nì Jaadoo nì Buusi.

english_verse: Ahi, the son of Abdiel and the grandson of Guni, was the leader of their clan.
translation_verse: Abidiyeel jipɔɔn nì Guuni naantiiu Akii di nìn sá Gaadi naakookun yab gbanti kɔkɔ kpiliu.

english_verse: The people of Gad lived in the towns in the regions of Bashan and Gilead, as well as in the pastureland of Sharon.
translation_verse: Gaadi dicaŋkun yab nìn kóò Galaadi nì Baasan tiŋkpaammun ní. Bi nìn gíti kóò ntimu mun bí mu-taapuee nì Saarɔn naakpaapɔɔkun kí tin cáá sāā mu-kpaanyɔmmu.

english_verse: Their family records were written when Jotham was king of Judah and Jeroboam was king of Israel.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kàan̄ binib gbanti kɔkɔ ki ŋmàn̄ bi-yiŋŋi ki ŋá dikàandi gbɔŋkun ŋyunti ŋun Jootam nìn sá Juuda bɔtiu ní Jeerooboowaam sá Isirayeel bɔtiuee ní.

english_verse: They fought against the Hagrites and the tribes of Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
translation_verse: Bi nìn jáń nì Agrii yab nì Jeetuur nì Nafiisi nì Noodaab dicaŋŋi yab.

english_verse: Whenever these soldiers went to war against their enemies, they prayed to God and trusted him to help. That's why the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh defeated the Hagrites and their allies.
translation_verse: Kujaau gbanti poonee, bi nìn dū bi-mákal ki páaǹ Unimbɔti pu ní ki mēē-u yii ú tūtuǹ-bi. Unimbɔti nìn fōō bi-wimmeem ní ki tútuǹ-bi. Míǹ ní bi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Agrii yab nì bin nìn pá bi-boonee.

english_verse: Many of the Hagrites died in battle, because God was fighting this battle against them. The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh lived in that territory until they were taken as prisoners to Assyria. The Tribe of East Manasseh
translation_verse: ní ki kūū binannanliibi tikpil. Di sá yii Unimbɔti di nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpu ní bi jáń kujaau gbanti. Niinee ní bi gbíntì Agrii yab tiŋki gbantin ki kāl̀ ki dāa sāā ŋyunti ŋun bi dāa cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee. Manasee naantiibi bin kóòń Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee

english_verse: East Manasseh was a large tribe, so its people settled in the northern region of Bashan, as far north as Baal-Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: Manasee naakooku dijandi diba yab nìn dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ kí yòon̄ Baasan tiŋki ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Baal-Eermɔn tiŋki nì Seeniir nì Eermɔn jool ŋgan púee ní.

english_verse: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel were their clan leaders; they were well-known leaders and brave soldiers. The Tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh Are Defeated
translation_verse: Bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee, bi-kpilib yiŋŋi di sá Eefeer nì Iseeyii nì Eeliyeel nì Asiriyeel nì Irimeeya nì Oodafiya nì Yaadiyeel. Bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ nìn sá bibaatandambi nì bin nyáń diyindee ní.

english_verse: The people of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh were unfaithful to the God their ancestors had worshiped, and they started worshiping the gods of the nations that God had forced out of Canaan.
translation_verse: Ama Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔtin yab nì Manasee naakooku dijandi din bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee yab nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu ní ki nìn bí ki tòotī atimbun ŋin nib Unimbɔti nìn jìn̄ ki nyántì ki wāatì-bi kitiŋee waaŋi.

english_verse: So God sent King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria to attack these Israelite tribes. The king led them away as prisoners to Assyria, and from then on, he forced them to live in Halah, Habor, Hara, and near the Gozan River.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu sāal̀ Asuur bɔtiibi Puul nì Tiigilaati-Piilneeseer ní bíǹ dɔ́miń ki cúú-bi ki cūnnì Alaa nì Abɔɔr nì Ara timmun nì Goosan mɔɔl caŋin timmun kuyuŋu. Bi dáá gbíntìi bí niin ki dāa sāā díǹ. Leefii naantiibi

english_verse: Kohath was the father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Geersɔm jipɔmbi di sá Liibinii nì Simeeyii.

english_verse: Amram was the father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Keeyaati jipɔmbi di sá Amiiraam nì Isaar nì Eebrɔn nì Usiyeel.

english_verse: Kohath's descendants included Amminadab, Korah, Assir, Elkanah, Ebiasaph, Assir, Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.
translation_verse: Eeman nabiki kin yūlifí u-ŋaŋgiil pú bi gà ilanee di sá Beereekiya jipɔɔn Asaafi. Úǹ naanjab di sá Simeeya,

english_verse: Elkanah was the father of Amasai and Ahimoth.
translation_verse: nì Miikayeel nì Baseeya nì Maalkiya,

english_verse: Ahimoth's descendants included Elkanah, Zophai, Nahath, Eliab, Jeroham, and Elkanah.
translation_verse: nì Eetan nì Siima nì Simeeyii,

english_verse: Samuel was the father of Joel and Abijah, born in that order.
translation_verse: nì Yaati nì Geersɔm nì Leefii.

english_verse: Ethan was also Heman's relative and served as his assistant. Ethan belonged to the Merari clan, and his ancestors included Kishi, Abdi, Malluch, Hashabiah, Amaziah, Hilkiah, Amzi, Bani, Shemer, Mahli, Mushi, Merari, and Levi.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lēē Isakaar nì Aseer nì Neefitalii naakɔtin nì Manasee naakookun yab dijandi din nìn kóò Baasan tiŋkinee poon ntimu saalaa nì muta ki tīī Geersɔm naantiibi.

english_verse: The rest of the Levites were appointed to work at the sacred tent. The Descendants of Aaron
translation_verse: Bi gíti tɔ́ kasi ní ki lēē Rubeen nì Gaadi nì Sabulɔn naakɔti yab tinjaŋŋi poon ntimu saalaa nì muli ki tīī Meerarii naantiibi.

english_verse: They received the town of Hebron in the territory of Judah and the pastureland around it.
translation_verse: Manasee naakooku dijandi din bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee tinjandi poonee, bi nìn tīī-bi Aneer tiŋki nì ki-sati, nì Biileeyam tiŋki nì ki-sati.

english_verse: So Aaron's descendants received the following Safe Towns and the pastureland around them: Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, Hilen, Debir, Ashan, and Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Aseer naakookun yab tinjandi poonee, bi nìn tīī-bi Masaal tiŋki nì ki-sati, nì Abidɔn tiŋki nì ki-sati,

english_verse: The rest of the Levite clan of Kohath received ten towns from West Manasseh.
translation_verse: Neefitalii naakookun yab tinjandi poonee, bi tīī-bi Keedeesi tiŋki kin bí Galiilee tiŋkinee nì ki-sati, nì Amɔn tiŋki nì ki-sati, nì Kiiriyatayiim tiŋki nì ki-sati.

english_verse: The Levite clan of Gershon received thirteen towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and East Manasseh in Bashan.
translation_verse: Sabulɔn naakookun yab tinjandi poonee, bi nìn tīī Meerarii maaliŋun yab bin kíǹee Riimoonoo tiŋki nì ki-sati, nì Tabɔɔr tiŋki nì ki-sati.

english_verse: The Levite clan of Merari received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, Jeeriikoo tiŋki caŋinee, bi nìn tīī-bi Rubeen naakooku yab tinjandi poon Beeseer tiŋki kin bí kuteeunee nì ki-sati, nì Yaasa tiŋki nì ki-sati,

english_verse: So the people of Israel gave the Levites towns to live in and the pastureland around them.
translation_verse: nì Keedeemooti tiŋki nì ki-sati, nì Meefaati tiŋki nì ki-sati.

english_verse: All the towns were chosen with the Lord's help, including those towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: Gaadi naakookun yab tinjandi poonee, bi nìn tīī-bi Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkinee nì ki-sati, nì Maanayiim tiŋki nì ki-sati,

english_verse: Some of the families of the Kohath clan received their towns from the tribe of Ephraim.
translation_verse: nì Eesbɔn tiŋki nì ki-sati, nì Jaseer tiŋki nì ki-sati.

english_verse: Issachar was the father of four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
translation_verse: Isakaar nìn cáá jipɔmbi binaa ní. Bíǹ di sá Toola nì Puuwa nì Jasuub nì Simroon.

english_verse: Tola was the father of Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, who were all brave soldiers and family leaders in their clan. There were
translation_verse: Toola jipɔmbi di sá Usii nì Reefaya nì Jeeriyeel nì Yaamayi nì Yibisam nì Seemiyeel. Bíǹ di sá Toola maaliŋun dicaŋŋi kpilib, ní ki nìn sá bibaatandambi bi-dicaŋŋi poon. Ubɔti Daafiidi yuntiŋuee, Toola maaliŋun yab gbanti nìn sá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì bili nì binib alaataa aluu ní.

english_verse: Ephraim mourned for his sons a long time, and his relatives came to comfort him.
translation_verse: Bi-baa Eefiraayiim súń bi-kpool ki yúntì tikpil, ní u-nabiyaamu dɔ́miń ki sɔ̄ŋkì u-pɔbil.

english_verse: Uzzi was the father of Izrahiah and the grandfather of Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, who were also family leaders.
translation_verse: Usii jipɔɔn di sá Isiraya ní Isiraya jipɔmbi sá Miikayeel nì Oobadiya nì Jooweel nì Isiya. Bi-ŋmootil nìn sá adican kpilib ní.

english_verse: Zophah was the father of Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
translation_verse: Soofa jipɔmbi di sá Suuwa nì Arineefeer nì Suwaal nì Beerii nì Imira,

english_verse: In fact, according to family records, the tribe of Issachar had a total of
translation_verse: Bi nín kàan̄ Isakaar naakookun yab bin sá bibaatandambee, bi nìn nyáń binib kutukub imuŋku inaa nì biluli ní. Beenjameen nì Neefitalii naakɔtin yab

english_verse: Benjamin was the father of three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
translation_verse: Beenjameen nìn cáá jipɔmbi bita ní. Bíǹ di sá Beela nì Beekeer nì Yeediyeel.

english_verse: Bela was the father of Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were all brave soldiers and family leaders in their father's clan. The number of soldiers in their clan was
translation_verse: Beela naantiibi di sá Eesbɔn nì Usii nì Usiyeel nì Yeereemooti nì Irii. Bibaatandambi gbanti kɔkɔ nìn sá bi-dicaŋŋi kpilib ní. Bi nín kàan̄-bee, bi-kɔkɔ nìn nyáń binib kutukub mmuŋku nì bili nì binib mmuŋku nì saalaa nì binaa ní.

english_verse: Becher was the father of Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth.
translation_verse: Beekeer naantiibi di sá Seemiira nì Joowaasi nì Eeliyeeseer nì Eeliyooweenayi nì Oomirii nì Jeereemooti nì Abiiya nì Anatooti nì Aleemeeti. Beekeer dicaŋkun yab di sá bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Ephraim was the father of Shuthelah and the ancestor of Bered, Tahath, Eleadah, Tahath,
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim naakookun yab di sá u-jipɔɔn Suteela nì u-naantiibi Beereedi nì Taati nì Eelaada nì Taati,

english_verse: Jediael was the father of Bilhan and the grandfather of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
translation_verse: Yeediyeel jipɔɔn di sá Biilan ní Biilan jipɔmbi sá Jeewusi nì Beenjameen nì Eewuudi nì Keenaana nì Seetan nì Taarsiisi nì Ayiisakaar.

english_verse: Ulam was the father of Bedan. These were all descendants of Gilead, the son of Machir and the grandson of Manasseh.
translation_verse: ní Ulam màl̄ Beedan. Makiir jipɔɔn Manasee naantiiu Galaadi maaliŋun yab dee.

english_verse: Ir was the father of Shuppim and Huppim, who also belonged to this clan. Dan was the father of Hushim. The Descendants of Naphtali
translation_verse: Iir jipɔmbi di sá Supiim nì Upiim, ní Ayeer jipɔɔn sá Usiim.

english_verse: Naphtali's mother was Bilhah, and he was the father of Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. The Descendants of Manasseh
translation_verse: Neefitalii jipɔmbi di sá Yaasiyeel nì Gunii nì Saluum. Bi-na di sá Biila. Manasee naantiibi bin bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee

english_verse: Manasseh and his Syrian wife were the parents of Asriel and Machir the father of Gilead.
translation_verse: Manasee jipɔmbi di sá Asiriyeel nì Makiir bin u-nimpuwaaki kin sá Aram tiŋkinee nìn màl̄-uee. Makiir di màl̄ Galaadi.

english_verse: Machir found a wife for Huppim and one for Shuppim. Machir had a sister named Maacah. Zelophehad was also a descendant of Manasseh, and he had five daughters.
translation_verse: Makiir nìn cáá unimpu ki tīī Upiim nì Supiim. Makiir nìn cáá niisal ubɔ bi yíì-u Maaka. U nìn gíti cáá jipɔnliliiti bi yíì-u Seeloofaadi, ama úǹ nìn pée màl̄ mbinimpubiyaamu ŋma ní.

english_verse: Machir and his wife Maacah were the parents of Peresh and Sheresh. Peresh was the father of Ulam and Rekem.
translation_verse: Makiir nimpuu Maaka nìn màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Peereesi. U nìn gíti màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki pú kíǹ diyindi yii Seereesi. Seereesi di màl̄ Ulam nì Reekeem,

english_verse: Gilead's sister Hammolecheth was the mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
translation_verse: Galaadi niisal Amɔleekeeti di màl̄ Isoodi nì Abiyeeseer nì Maala.

english_verse: Shemida, another descendant of Manasseh, was the father of Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam. The Descendants of Ephraim
translation_verse: Seemiida jipɔmbi di sá Ayan nì Seekeem nì Liikii nì Aniiyam. Eefiraayiim naakookun yab

english_verse: Zabad, and Shuthelah. Ephraim had two other sons, Ezer and Elead. But they were killed when they tried to steal livestock from the people who lived in the territory of Gath.
translation_verse: nì Sabaadi nì Suteela nì Eeseer nì Eelaadi. Eefiraayiim jipɔmbi Eeseer nì Eelaadi nìn cūtì kí gbìntī Gaati yab waŋkuti ní bíǹ kūuń-bi.

english_verse: Some time later his wife gave birth to another son, and Ephraim named him Beriah, because he was born during a time of misery.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Eefiraayiim nì u-nimpuu fātìi kpáfì ní u-nimpuu màl̄ kibininjabiki ní u pú-kì diyindi yii Beeriya, di sá yii «nnaabu nìn jéetì u-dicaŋku pu.»

english_verse: Ephraim's daughter was Sheerah. She built the towns of Lower Beth-Horon, Upper Beth-Horon, and Uzzen-Sheerah.
translation_verse: U-bisal Seera di náań Beeti-Oorɔn yilpu tiŋki nì taapu tiŋki, ní ki náań Useen-Seera tiŋki mun.

english_verse: Ephraim also had a son named Rephah, and his descendants included Resheph, Telah, Tahan,
translation_verse: U-naantiibi di gíti sá Reefa nì Reeseefi nì Teela nì Tayan,

english_verse: Nun, and Joshua.
translation_verse: nì Nuuni nì Joosuwa.

english_verse: The descendants of Ephraim took over the territory as far south as Bethel, as far east as Naaran, and as far west as Gezer. Their territory included all the villages around these towns, as well as Shechem, Ayyah, and the nearby villages.
translation_verse: Ditinjandi din Eefiraayiim yab fōō kí nīn kóòyee di sá Beeteel tiŋki nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe, nì Naaran tiŋki kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, nì Geeseer tiŋki kin bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe, nì Siikeem nì Aya timmu nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-muee.

english_verse: The descendants of Manasseh settled in the territory that included Beth-Shan, Taanach, Megiddo, Dor, and the nearby villages. The descendants of Joseph lived in these towns and villages. The Descendants of Asher
translation_verse: Manasee naakookun yab di yì Beeti-Seeyan nì Taanaki nì Meegiidoo nì Dɔɔr timmu, ki yì ki kpáaǹ ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-muee kɔkɔ. Ntimu gbanti ní Jaakɔb jipɔɔn Jooseefi naantiibi nìn kóò. Aseer naakookun yab

english_verse: Asher had four sons, Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and one daughter, Serah.
translation_verse: Aseer jipɔmbi di sá Imina nì Isifa nì Isifii Beeriya, bi-niisal di sá Seera.

english_verse: Beriah was the father of Heber and Malchiel the father of Birzaith.
translation_verse: Beeriya jipɔmbi di sá Eebeer nì Malkiyeel. Malkiyeel di sá Biirisayiiti baa.

english_verse: Heber was the father of three sons, Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and one daughter, Shua.
translation_verse: Eebeer di màl̄ Jafileeti nì Soomeer nì Ootam nì bi-niisal Suuwa.

english_verse: Japhlet was the father of Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.
translation_verse: Jafileeti jipɔmbi di sá Pasaki nì Biimaal nì Asifaati.

english_verse: Shomer was the father of Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
translation_verse: Seemeer jipɔmbi di sá Ayii nì Rooga nì Uba nì Aram.

english_verse: And Japhlet's brother Hotham was the father of Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
translation_verse: U-nabiki Eeleem jipɔmbi di sá Soofa nì Irima nì Seeleesii nì Amaal.

english_verse: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
translation_verse: nì Beeseer nì Oodi nì Sama nì Siileesa nì Itiran nì Beera.

english_verse: Jether was the father of Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
translation_verse: Jeeteer jipɔmbi di sá Jeefunee nì Piispa nì Eera.

english_verse: Ulla was the father of Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
translation_verse: Ula jipɔmbi di sá Ara nì Aniiyeel nì Riisiya.

english_verse: These were the descendants of Asher, and they were all respected family leaders and brave soldiers. The tribe of Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Aseer naantiibi di sá binib nee kɔkɔ. Bi nìn sá adican kpilib nì bibaatandambi bin nyáń diyindee. Bi nín kàan̄ bi-nib kɔkɔee, bin nìn bàn̄ kí cù kujaauee nìn sá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì biluu ní.

english_verse: Benjamin had five sons, who were born in the following order: Bela, Ashbel, Aharah,
translation_verse: Beenjameen màl̄ u-jipɔŋkpiliu Beela ní ki páaǹ uliliiti Asibeel nì utataati Aara,

english_verse: Nohah, and Rapha.
translation_verse: nì unanaati Noora nì uŋmooŋmooti Raafa.

english_verse: Bela was the father of Addar, Gera, Abihud,
translation_verse: Beela jipɔmbi di sá Adaar nì Geera nì Abiiwuudi,

english_verse: Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
translation_verse: nì Abiisuwa nì Naaman nì Ayooya,

english_verse: Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
translation_verse: nì Geera nì Seefufan nì Uraam.

english_verse: Ehud was the father of Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera. They were clan leaders in the town of Geba, but were later forced to move to the town of Manahath, and Gera led the way. He had two sons: Uzza and Ahihud.
translation_verse: Bíǹ di sá Naaman nì Aaya nì Geera. Geera di nìn cáá-bi ki cūnnì niin. U-jipɔmbi di sá Usa nì Ayiiwuudi.

english_verse: Elpaal was the father of Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who settled the towns of Ono and Lod, as well as the nearby villages.
translation_verse: Eelpaal jipɔmbi di sá Eebeer nì Miisaam nì Seemeedi. Seemeedi di máń Oonoo nì Loodi timmu nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-muee.

english_verse: Beriah and Shema were family leaders in the clan that lived in the town of Aijalon and that forced out the people of Gath.
translation_verse: Beeriya nì Seema bin sá bin kóò Ayalɔnee dicaŋŋi kpilib di nìn jìn̄ Gaati yab.

english_verse: Beriah's descendants included Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth, Zebadiah, Arad, Eder, Michael, Ishpah, and Joha.
translation_verse: nì Miikayeel nì Isipa nì Joowa di sá Beeriya jipɔmbi.

english_verse: Elpaal's descendants included Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab.
translation_verse: nì Isimeerayi nì Isiliya nì Joobaab di sá Eelpaal jipɔmbi.

english_verse: Shimei's descendants included Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath.
translation_verse: nì Adaaya nì Beeraya nì Siimrati di sá Simeeyii jipɔmbi.

english_verse: Shashak's descendants included Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Abdon, Zichri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah, Iphdeiah, and Penuel.
translation_verse: nì Ifideeya nì Peeniyeel di sá Sasaaki jipɔmbi.

english_verse: Jeroham's descendants included Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri.
translation_verse: nì Jaareesiya nì Eeliya nì Sikirii di sá Jeeroowaam jipɔmbi.

english_verse: These were the family leaders in their ancestor's clan, and they and their descendants lived in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Bin bí nee di sá adican kpilib, ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee. Bi nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: Jeiel settled the town of Gibeon. He and his wife Maacah lived there
translation_verse: Unil un nìn náań Gabawɔn tiŋkee nìn kóò kitiŋ gbantin ní. U-nimpuu ní bi yíì yii Maaka.

english_verse: along with their sons, who were born in the following order: Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
translation_verse: U-jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Abidɔn ní u-jipɔmbi bin kíǹee sá Suur nì Kiisi nì Baal nì Nadaab,

english_verse: Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,
translation_verse: nì Geedɔɔr nì Aayoo nì Seekeer,

english_verse: and Mikloth the father of Shimeah. Some of them went to live in Jerusalem near their relatives. The Descendants of King Saul
translation_verse: nì Siima baa Miikilooti. Binib nee nì bi-yab mun nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní, bi nì bi-nabiyaamu mubɔ mun. Sayuul naantiibi (Kpèè

english_verse: Ner was the father of Kish and the grandfather of King Saul. Saul had four sons: Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
translation_verse: Neer di màl̄ Kiisi, ní Kiisi màl̄ Saayuul, ní Saayuul màl̄ Joonatan nì Malkisuwa nì Abinadaab nì Eesbaal.

english_verse: Jonathan was the father of Meribbaal, the grandfather of Micah,
translation_verse: Joonatan jipɔɔn di sá Meeriibaal. Meeriibaal di màl̄ Miika.

english_verse: and the great-grandfather of Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
translation_verse: Miika jipɔmbi di sá Piitɔn nì Meeleeki nì Tareeya nì Ayaasi.

english_verse: Saul's other descendants were Jehoaddah, Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri, Moza,
translation_verse: Ayaasi di màl̄ Yooyadaa, ní Yooyadaa màl̄ Aleemeeti nì Asimafeeti nì Simrii, ní Simrii màl̄ Moosa,

english_verse: as well as Azel's six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
translation_verse: Aseel jipɔmbi sá biluu ní. Bi-yiŋŋi di sá Asiirikam nì Bookiru nì Isimaayeel nì Seeyara nì Oobadiya nì Anan.

english_verse: Azel's brother Eshek was the father of Ulam, Jeush, and Eliphelet.
translation_verse: Aseel nabiki Eeseeki jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Ulam, u-jipɔnliliitiu di sá Jeewusi ní utataati sá Eeliifeeleeti.

english_verse: Ulam's sons were brave soldiers who were experts at using a bow and arrows. They had a total of
translation_verse: Ulam jipɔmbi sá bibaatandambi ní ki sá bipintɔliibi. U nìn cáá jipɔmbi nì naantiibi tikpil. Bi nìn nyáń binib dilaataal nì binib imuŋku ili nì saalaa. Beenjameen naakookun yab di sá binib bin bí nee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: And the first people to return to their towns included priests, Levites, temple workers, and other Israelites.
translation_verse: Bi nín dāa gítìń kuyuŋu púee, bi-kansikin bin nìn péé péé ki fātìi kāl̀ bi-timmu pu bi-tinjaŋŋi poonee di sá Isirayeel yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì kunimbɔtidiin tɔntɔnliibi.

english_verse: People from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh settled in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab nì Eefiraayiim yab nì Manasee yab di nìn gítìń ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: Here is a list of priests who settled in Jerusalem: Jedaiah; Jehoiarib; Jachin; Azariah, who was a temple official, and whose ancestors included Hilkiah, Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub; Adaiah son of Jeroham, whose ancestors included Pashhur and Malchijah; Maasai son of Adiel, whose ancestors included Jahzerah, Meshullam, Meshillemith, and Immer.
translation_verse: Adaaya mun nìn bí. U-naanjab di sá Yeeroowaam nì Pasuur nì Maalkiya. Masayi mun nìn bí. U-naanjab di sá Adiyeel nì Jaseera nì Meesulam nì Meesileemiiti nì Imeer.

english_verse: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives were the guards at the temple gates. Shallum was the leader of this clan,
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kansikinee, Saluum un sá ukpilee nì u-nabiyaamu Akuub nì Talmɔn nì Ayiiman nìn bí.

english_verse: and for a long time they had been the guards at the King's Gate on the east side of the city. Before that, their ancestors guarded the entrance to the Levite camp.
translation_verse: Bi-naantiibi dáá gbíntìi cí kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, bi yíì-kì yii ubɔti punyɔkɔkee. Bi-naanjab di nìn sá Leefii yab naapaal punyɔɔciitiliibi.

english_verse: Shallum son of Kore, as well as the other men in the Korahite clan, guarded the entrance to the temple, just as their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Saluum nìn sá Kooree jipɔɔn nì Abiyasafi naantiiu nì Kooree naantitɔntɔkɔl ní. U nì Kooree dicaŋkun yab bin kíǹee di nìn cí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki. Bi-naanjab di nìn cí ti-Dindaan nibul naapaal.

english_verse: Phinehas son of Eleazar had supervised their work because the Lord was with him.
translation_verse: Njaminee, Eelasaar jipɔɔn Piinaasi di nìn sá bi-kpiliu, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn bí u-cee.

english_verse: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was also one of the guards at the temple.
translation_verse: Meeseeleemiyawuu jipɔɔn Seekariya mun nìn sá dikpafindi tantiu ciitiliu ubɔ ní.

english_verse: and now they guarded the temple gates.
translation_verse: Ní bi nì bi-naantiibi gbíntìi bí ki kpèé ti-Dindaan Diiku, ki cí ki-punyɔmmu.

english_verse: There was one full-time guard appointed to each of the four sides of the temple.
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nìn bí ki cí mpunyɔmu naatil, an dàkà yii ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú.

english_verse: The four full-time guards were Levites, and they supervised the other guards and were responsible for the rooms in the temple and the supplies kept there.
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi bikpilib naatil nìn pée bí niin ní. Bíǹ di sá Leefii yab bin cí Unimbɔti diiku dibiyaamu nì ku-gaajawantee.

english_verse: They guarded the temple day and night and opened its doors every morning. The Duties of the Levites
translation_verse: Bi nìn màntīí tū kunimbɔtidii áli kutaa ń dāá wúntí, kun puee bi-tundi di nìn sá bí nīn cí-ku ní kí nīn pìitī ku-punyɔmmu kutaafaau kamaa.

english_verse: Some of the Levites were responsible for the equipment used in worship at the temple, and they had to count everything before and after it was used.
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi biba tundi di nìn sá bí nīn kpèé tiwan tin bi cáa ŋáań saraabee. Bi yaa nìn nyántì-tèe, bi nìn kàaǹ-tì ní ní bi yaa làá kɔ́ǹ-tèe, bí fàtīí kàaǹ-tì.

english_verse: But only the priests could mix the spices.
translation_verse: Ama ní bisaraaŋaliibi di nìn bɔ́ntí tiwan tin bi ŋmàlintí ki cáa ŋáań talaalubee.

english_verse: Mattithiah, Shallum's oldest son, was a member of the Levite clan of Korah, and he was in charge of baking the bread used for offerings.
translation_verse: Leefii yab kansikinee, Saluum un sá Kooree maaliŋunee jipɔŋkpiliu Matatiya tundi di nìn sá ú nīn pūul̀ ŋkpɔnɔbiyaamu mun bi cáa ŋáań saraabee.

english_verse: The Levites from the Kohath clan were in charge of baking the sacred loaves of bread for each Sabbath.
translation_verse: Leefii yab bin sá Keeyaati maaliŋunee biba tundi di nìn sá bí nīn pūul̀ kpɔnɔb bin bi cáa ŋáań Unimbɔti saraa ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa kamaayee.

english_verse: The Levite family leaders who were the musicians also lived at the temple. They had no other responsibilities, because they were on duty day and night.
translation_verse: Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib bin nìn sá bilaŋgaaliibee bíǹ nìn bí bíǹ bi-ba diiŋŋin ní. Baa nìn gíti cáá ditundi diba ki kútì, kun puee bíǹ nìn pée bí ditundin ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu ní.

english_verse: All of these men were family leaders in the Levi tribe and were listed that way in their family records. They lived in Jerusalem. King Saul's Family (
translation_verse: Leefii yab kpilib dee, ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee. Bi nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní. Saayuul dicaŋku yab (Kpèè

english_verse: the father of Shimeam. Some of them went to live in Jerusalem near their relatives.
translation_verse: Miikilooti di màl̄ Simeeyam. Ama bíǹ nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní, bi nì bi-nabiyaamu.

english_verse: Jeiel had settled the town of Gibeon, where he and his wife Maacah lived.
translation_verse: Yeeyeel un náań Gabawɔn tiŋkee kóò Gabawɔn tiŋki gbantin ní, u nì u-nimpuu Maaka,

english_verse: They had ten sons, who were born in the following order: Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
translation_verse: nì u-jipɔŋkpiliu Abidɔn nì u-jipɔmbi bin kíǹee, an dàkà yii Suur nì Kiisi nì Baal nì Neer nì Nadaab,

english_verse: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth
translation_verse: nì Geedɔɔr nì Ayiiyoo nì Seekariya nì Miikilooti.

english_verse: Ner was the father of Kish and the grandfather of King Saul. Saul had four sons: Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
translation_verse: Neer di màl̄ Kiisi, ní Kiisi màl̄ Saayuul, ní Saayuul màl̄ Joonatan nì Malkisuwa nì Abinadaab nì Eesbaal.

english_verse: The descendants of Ahaz included Jarah, Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri, Moza, Binea, Rephaiah, Eleasah, and Azel and his six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
translation_verse: Aseel màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muluu ní. Bi-yiŋŋi di sá Asiirikam nì Bookiru nì Isimaayeel nì Seeyariya nì Oobadiya nì Anan. Aseel jipɔmbi dee.

english_verse: The Philistines fought against Israel in a battle at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Dalba Fiiliistii yab jáń kujaau nì Isirayeel yab Giilboowa jool pu. Isirayeel yab nìn sáǹ ní Fiiliistii yab kūū binib tikpil.

english_verse: Saul died because he was unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord. He even asked advice from a woman who talked to spirits of the dead,
translation_verse: Kun pu Saayuul nìn kpíìyee di sá yii waa nìn yúl̀ nì ti-Dindaan deedee. Waa nìn tɔ́ u-marab. Áli gba u cūtì un kàal̀ dibɔɔjal pu ki yíì bitaŋkpiibee cee dibalifil,

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons and killed three of them: Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi pu kàti kati. Bi nìn kūū Joonatan nì Abinadaab nì Meelkiisuwa.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Niinee dikɔ̀ndi kóoǹ ki nyīŋfì Saayuul pu. Bipintɔliibi nín dāa ká-uee ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ ní u-wunti kíǹ ki gbáà kpàkpakpa.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want those godless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Then Saul stuck himself in the stomach with his own sword and fell on the blade.
translation_verse: Ní Saayuul bí un ŋúb́ u-janjawantee yii: «Fúutí a-tàataajiki ki sāā kí kpɔ̀-mi. Maa là yii Fiiliistii yab bin kaa gíí akpancan nee ń kpɔ̀-mi kí nīn cáa bèel̄-mi.» Ama ní un ŋúb́ u-janjawantee fāŋkì ní ki yíì. Niinee ní Saayuul yōoǹ úǹ u-ba tàataajiki ki cóoǹ ki lítì ki-pu.

english_verse: When the soldier realized that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Un ŋúb́ u-janjawantee nín ká yii u-kpiliu kpíìyee, ní u mun dū u-tàataajiki ki cóoǹ ki lítì ki-pu ki kpíì.

english_verse: Saul, three of his sons, and all his male relatives were dead.
translation_verse: An nín dī min ní Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi taatil kpíìyee dee. Mimmee ubɔti dicaŋku kúntì mun dee.

english_verse: The Israelites who lived in Jezreel Valley learned that their army had run away and that Saul and his sons were dead. They ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites left behind.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin kóò ditantakalinee ká yii Isirayeel yab sáǹ ní Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi taatil kpíì. Niinee ní bi yíkìi sáǹ ki fá bi-timmu, ní Fiiliistii yab dɔ́miń ki kāl̀.

english_verse: The next day the Philistines came back to the battlefield to carry away the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers. When they found the bodies of Saul and his sons on Mount Gilboa,
translation_verse: Ku wúntì Fiiliistii yab dɔ́miń kí fūkul̀ bin bi kūūyee wantee ní ki ká yii Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi taatil kpíì ki dɔ̄ Giilboowa jool pu.

english_verse: they took Saul's weapons, pulled off his armor, and cut off his head. Then they sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the news among their people and to thank the idols of their gods.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lēē u-yil, ki pēetì u-janjawanti, ní ki tú ki yìiǹ Fiiliistii yab timmu kɔkɔn nì awaadiinni nì aniwulin ki sòoǹ nì báà ŋma bi-jajil pu.

english_verse: They put Saul's armor in the temple of their gods and hung his head in the temple of their god Dagon.
translation_verse: Boonee ní bi cáá u-janjawanti ki yóoǹ bi-waadiiku kubɔn. Bi nìn dū u-yil ki lúntì bi-waal Daagɔn diikun.

english_verse: When the people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
translation_verse: Bin kóò Yabeesi Galaadi tiŋkinee gbìl̄ Fiiliistii yab nín ŋá Saayuul puee.

english_verse: some brave men went to get his body and the bodies of his three sons. The men brought the bodies back to Jabesh, where they buried them under an oak tree. Then for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Bininjab bin cáá dibaatandee yíkì ki cūtìi yōoǹní Saayuul nì u-jipɔmbi. Bi nín cáá-bi ki bāań Yabeesee ní bi dū bi-kpabiŋ ki síb́ teereebinti subu bubɔ taapu Yabeesi tiŋkin, ki bóob́ kinyɔkɔ iwiin iluli.

english_verse: instead of asking the Lord. So the Lord had Saul killed and gave his kingdom to David, the son of Jesse.
translation_verse: kaa mēē ti-Dindaan ú kpòotī-u. An pu ní Unimbɔti yāntì Saayuul kpíì ní u dū dibeel ki tīī Isayi jipɔɔn Daafiidi.

english_verse: The Jebusites said, “You won't be able to get in here!” But David captured the fortress of Mount Zion, which is now called the City of David.
translation_verse: Jeebusi yab nìn bí Daafiidi yii: «Ni kpá kí kɔ́nní ti-tiŋkin!» Ama ní Daafiidi jáń ki fōō Siiyɔn tiŋki laakin bi nìn máń digundi ki túee. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti ní bi kíǹ ki yíì niin yii Daafiidi Tiŋki.

english_verse: Israel's leaders met with David at Hebron and said, “We are your relatives,
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nibul kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì Daafiidi cee Eebrɔn tiŋkin ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti baasii pēē dinabiil ní.

english_verse: So we have come to crown you king of Israel.” David made an agreement with the leaders and asked the Lord to be their witness. Then the leaders poured olive oil on David's head to show that he was now king of Israel. This happened just as the Lord's prophet Samuel had said. David Captures Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kpilib kɔkɔ nìn dɔ́miń Eebrɔn tiŋkin Daafiidi cee. Niin ní u nì bi ŋá mpèé ti-Dindaan nimbiin, ní bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ú nīn sá Isirayeel yab bɔtiu kí nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī Samiyeel pu ki sòon̄ tiŋyee. Daafiidi jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki (Kpèè

english_verse: David had told his troops, “The first soldier to kill a Jebusite will become my army commander.” And since Joab son of Zeruiah attacked first, he became commander.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn lī yii: «Unil un làá péé kí já nì Jeebusi yabee di làá nīn sá bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ kpiliu.» Seeruya jipɔɔn Joowaab di nìn līntì nsan ki cūtìi jáń nì Jeebusi yab, ní ki kpántì bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ kpiliu.

english_verse: The Lord had promised that David would become king, and so everyone in Israel gave David their support. Certain warriors also helped keep his kingdom strong.
translation_verse: Daafiidi janjakpilib bin nìn tíkí-uee sèé. Bíǹ nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ di nìn kāaǹ-u dibeel kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn sòon̄ u-nibul pu puee.

english_verse: Jerusalem was called Jebus at the time, and David led Israel's army to attack the town.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn cūtì kí já nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Bi nìn gíti yíì kitiŋ gbanti yii Jeebusi tiŋki, di sá yii Jeebusi yab di nìn kóò niin.

english_verse: Later, David moved to the fortress—that's why it's called the City of David.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn cūtìi kāl̀ kitiŋ pɔ̀ti pu laakin bi máń diguŋkpaandi ki túee ní ki pú niin diyindi yii <Daafiidi Tiŋki>.

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn ki cá, ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nìn bí u-cee. Daafiidi janjaliibi (Kpèè

english_verse: Another time he killed an Egyptian who was over two meters tall and was armed with a spear. Benaiah only had a club, so he grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: U nìn tí kūū ueejipitija ubɔ u fɔ̀kɔ̀ ki bàn̄ kii meetab bili nì dijandi nyɔkɔm. Kikpaŋ kin unaaciinee nìn ŋúb̀ee nìn gbìfì kii ndɔfɔkɔ ŋun bi cáa lù satabee ní. Beenaya nìn ŋúb́ ditambɔndi ní ki kpìl̄ unaaciinee, ki cúú u-kpaŋki ki fōō u-ŋaan ní ki gíiǹ ki kūū-u.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm very thirsty. I wish I had a drink of water from the well by the gate to Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ní kpɔkɔsi ubɔ cúú Daafiidi ní u bí yii: «Ŋma di làá cùú cáań-mi lɔkɔ un bí Beetileem punyɔkɔki caŋinee nyim ḿ nyɔ̀ dee?»

english_verse: The first of these warriors was Jashobeam the son of Hachmoni, the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle he killed
translation_verse: Daafiidi janjakpilib gbanti yiŋŋi sèé: Uakimoonja Iseebaal di nìn sá bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu. Dalba úǹ di dū u-kpaŋki ki jáń ki kūū bijanjaliibi alaataa ata kɔkɔ dikɔmbaantiil poon.

english_verse: Another one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite.
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee, Doodoo un nìn sá Ayooya tiŋkinee jipɔɔn Eelasaar di nìn pá. U nìn kútì <bibaatandambi Bitee kitil> poon.

english_verse: except Eleazar, who stayed with David. They took their positions in a nearby barley field and defeated the Philistines! The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: Eelasaar nì u-naacimbi nìn síl̀ bukpaayee kansikin ní ki jáń ki fōō-bu ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Fiiliistii yab. Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Isirayeel yab dijajikpaandi.

english_verse: One time the Three Warriors went to meet David among the rocks at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Dalba Fiiliistii yab ŋātì bi-janjanaapaal Rafayii yab tantakalin. Niinee bijanjaliibi bimɔntiibi Mmuŋku nì Saalaa bin cīití ubɔtee kitil poon bita dɔ́miń ki ká Daafiidi Adulaam taŋkpalɔkɔlin.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in a fortress,
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn bál̀ kutaŋkpanaakoouee poon, ní Fiiliistii yab gɔminau nìn bí Beetileem tiŋkin.

english_verse: and said, “Drinking this water would be like drinking the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: Ní u bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń cúú-mi ḿ taa nyɔ̀ nnyim nee! Mì sá-mi kii binib bin kaa mɔ́tì bi-ba pu ki cūtìi nyàabìń-mèe fatikuu ní.» Ní u yíì kaa nyùn̄-mì. Bibaatandambi bitee nín nìn túń dituŋkpaandi diŋyee dee.

english_verse: Joab's brother Abishai was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and in one battle he killed
translation_verse: Joowaab naal Abisayi di nìn sá <Bibaatandambi Bitee kitil> kpiliu. Dalba úǹ di dū u-kpaŋki ki jáń nì binannanliibi alaataa ata, ki kūū-bi ní ki nyáń diyindi Bibaatandambi Bitee kitil poon.

english_verse: and was more famous than the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was their commander, but he never became one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: U nìn nyáń diyindi mili pu ki jítiǹ bibaatandambi bili bin kíǹee. Úǹ di nìn kpántì bi-kpiliu gba. Waa cáá juti bíǹ Bitee kitil poon.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. One time he killed two of Moab's best fighters, and one snowy day he went into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenaya un sá Kabiseeyeel tiŋkinee nìn sá ubaatandaan un dàkā tininjati ŋfunyɔm kupaauee. Úǹ di nìn kūū Moowaab tiŋkin janjakpaambi bili. Dalba mun ntaayim nìn lítì ki bīī kitiŋ pu ní u kɔ́ mbòó ŋubɔ poon ki kūū gbikinti.

english_verse: Benaiah did things like that; he was just as brave as the Three Warriors,
translation_verse: Beenaya nín nìn ŋá puee dee. Míǹ ní u nyáń diyindi kii bibaatandambi bitee.

english_verse: even though he never became one of them. And he was certainly as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. So David made him the leader of his own bodyguard.
translation_verse: Dikitil mmuŋku nì saalaayee kansikinee, úǹ di nìn nyáń diyindi ki jítiǹ bin kíǹee, ama waa nín kútì <Bibaatandambi Bitee kitil> poon ní. Daafiidi nìn dū-u ki ŋá bijanjaliibi bin cí-uee kpiliu ní.

english_verse: Several of these warriors were from King Saul's own tribe of Benjamin. They were experts at using a bow and arrows, and they could shoot an arrow or sling a stone with either hand.
translation_verse: Bi nìn ŋúb̀ itɔfi nì tijaataafun, ki nìn ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ ataŋkpee nì ipiin ŋŋaŋgiil nì ŋŋaŋgan kɔkɔ. Beenjameen naakookun, an dàkà yii Saayuul u-ba naakookunee, bin nìn bée di sá:

english_verse: Earlier, they had crossed the Jordan River when it flooded, and they chased out the people who lived in the valleys on each side of the river. Warriors from the Benjamin and Judah tribes
translation_verse: Gaadi yab gbanti nìn sá bijanjakpilib ŋma ní. Bi-kansikin un kaa nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄yee pɔŋŋu nìn sá kii bijanjaliibi dilaataalee ní, ní upɔɔl pɔŋŋu nìn sá kii bijanjaliibi kutukuee.

english_verse: One time a group of men from the tribes of Benjamin and Judah went to the fortress where David was staying.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋubɔee, bíǹ di nìn dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu dibindi poon uŋmapeekaa, ŋyunti ŋun ní nnyim gbéè kí páań dibuŋgbándi an kɔkɔ puee. Bi nìn cūtìi jìn̄ binib bin nìn kóò atantakan ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee.

english_verse: Some of the warriors who joined David were from the tribe of Manasseh. They had earlier gone with David when he agreed to fight on the side of the Philistines against King Saul. But as soon as the Philistine rulers realized that David might turn against them and rejoin Saul, they sent David away to the town of Ziklag.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti Fam nìn gbí Amasaayi un nìn sá bibaatandambi bin nìn bí Mmuŋku nì Saalaa kitil poonee kpiliu ní u bí yii: «Ti bí ki tīī-si, ti bí a-jandi pú, Isayi jipɔɔn Daafiidi. Ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí a-cee, kí nīn bí bin di tíkí-see mun cee. Di sá yii a-Nimbɔtiu di tútúǹ-si!» Niinee ní Daafiidi fōō-bi ní ki dū-bi ki ŋá u-janjakitil kpilib.

english_verse: and brave soldiers, and so David made them officers in his army. They fought on his side when enemy troops attacked.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Daafiidi nìn fàtīi gítí Siikilaagi tiŋkinee ní Manasee yab biba nìn cūtìi kútì u-pu. Bi-yiŋŋi di sá Adina nì Joosabaadi nì Yeediyeel nì Miikayeel nì Joosabaadi nì Eeliiwuu nì Siileetayi. Bi nìn sá Manasee janjaliibi kutuku kutuku kitiŋi kpilib ní.

english_verse: All of these soldiers voluntarily came to Hebron because they wanted David to become king of Israel. In fact, everyone in Israel wanted the same thing.
translation_verse: Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔti yab nì Manasee naakooku dijandi diba yab bin kóòń Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee janjaliibi nìn kpáfì binib kutukub dilaataal nì mmuŋku ní, ki ŋúb́ tijanjawan kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Then he led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They went there to get the sacred chest and bring it to Jerusalem, because it belonged to the Lord God, whose throne is above the winged creatures on the lid of the chest.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nín jɔ́ḿ Baala, an dàkà yii Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋki kin bí Juuda naakookunee, kí cùú yòon̄ní Unimbɔti Dakaau. Ti-Dindaan un kā keerubimbi kansikinee yindi ní bi dūu pú Dakaa gbanti.

english_verse: David was afraid what the Lord might do to him, and he asked himself, “Should I really be the one to take care of the sacred chest?”
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan yaadal wiiŋŋu, ní ki bí yii: «Maa làá ŋmā kí cùnnì ti-Dindaan dakaau m-dumpu!»

english_verse: The sacred chest was still at Abinadab's house, and when David and the crowd arrived there, they brought the chest outside and placed it on a new ox cart. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio guided the cart,
translation_verse: U nìn yú Abinadaab dumpu ní. Bi nìn dū-u ki tākaǹ tɔrɔkupɔɔn poon ní. Usa nì Ayiiyoo di nìn kpòotī inaa in dàtī tɔrɔkupɔɔn gbantee.

english_verse: while David and the crowd danced and sang praises to the Lord with all their might. They played music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn bí ki fàal̀ nì dipɔɔpindi Unimbɔti nimbiin ki gà ilan ní ki bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati nì saŋgub nì ŋgaŋgamu, ki cákafí cancakantib, ki búǹ akantán.

english_verse: But when they came to Chidon's threshing place, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of the chest to stop it from falling.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Kiidɔn tuulool caŋinee ní inaa gbéetì ní Usa tāntì u-ŋal kí cúú Unimbɔti dakaau.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Niin ní ti-Dindaan gíí Usa pu diŋuul. U nìn fáá ki kūū-u, kun puee u nìn gbēē dakaa. Usa nìn kpíì Unimbɔti dakaau caŋin niin.

english_verse: David then got angry with God for killing Uzzah. So he named that place “Attack on Uzzah,” and it's been called that ever since.
translation_verse: Niinee Daafiidi fōō diŋuul, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn fáá ki kūū Usa. Bi nìn pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Peereesi-Usa. Bi dáá gbíntìi yíì mpaan gbanti míǹ ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: So instead of taking it to Jerusalem, David decided to take it to the home of Obed-Edom, who lived in the town of Gath.
translation_verse: Daafiidi kaa nìn gíti là kí yòon̄ ti-Dindaan dakaau kí cùnnì Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U nìn yāntì bi cáa yóoǹ Oobeedi-Eedoom dumpu. Kijapaai gbanti nìn sá Gaati tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-Edom, his family, and everything he owned.
translation_verse: Dakaayee nìn yúl̀ Oobeedi-Eedoom dumpu iŋmal ita, ní ti-Dindaan bīiǹ u nì tin kɔkɔ u cááyee pu.

english_verse: David and his army marched to Baal-Perazim, where they attacked and defeated the Philistines. He said, “I defeated my enemies because God broke through them like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Niinee Fiiliistii yab nín cá áli Baal Peerasiim ní Daafiidi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi niin. U nìn bí yii: «Kii nnyim nín cífí nnyimbilkaam gundi dibundi puee, míǹ ní m-Dindaan cátì nsan m-nimbiin m-nannanliibi kansikin!» An pu ní bi pú niin diyindi yii Baal-Peerasiim. Taapu di sá yii: «Un cífí dibundee Kpiliu.»

english_verse: David obeyed God and he defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Gibeon to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín bí ú ŋá puee, ní ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ki jìn̄-bi kí yòon̄ Gabawɔn kí tin cáá sāā Geeseer kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. They brought along carpenters and stone workers, and enough cedar logs to build David a palace.
translation_verse: Tiir yab bɔtiu Iram nìn túnní binib Daafiidi cee. Bi nìn cáań-u busubu bun bi yíì seediree dɔi nì kapintab nì bitaŋkpakpitiliibi bí mā-u dibeecindi.

english_verse: After David moved to Jerusalem, he married more women and had more sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Daafiidi gíti cáá binimpoobi biba Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Binimpoobi gbanti màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu ki kútì.

english_verse: His children born there were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet. David Defeats the Philistines (
translation_verse: nì Eeliisama nì Beelyadaa nì Eeliifeeleeti. Daafiidi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Fiiliistii yab (Kpèè

english_verse: From then on, David became even more famous, and the Lord made all the nations afraid of him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daafiidi yindi dūu gbītì ntimu kɔkɔ poon ní báà ŋma kíǹ ki sòoǹ u-bɔti, ní ti-Dindaan yāntì atimbun kɔkɔ nib fāŋkì-u.

english_verse: When the Philistines heard that David had become king of Israel, they came to capture him. But David heard about their plan and marched out to meet them in battle.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nín nìn gbìl̄ yii bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì Daafiidi yil pu ki kāaǹ-u dibeelee, ní bi-kɔkɔ nín cá kí nyàab̀-u kí cúú-u. Daafiidi gbìl̄ an bɔtee ní ki nyáń ki túŋkì-bi nsanni.

english_verse: The Philistines had already camped in Rephaim Valley and were raiding the nearby villages.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab bàn̄ee ní ki yàl̄ ki gbí Reefayiim tantakalin.

english_verse: David asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help me win?” The Lord told David, “Yes, attack them! I will give you victory.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «Ḿ cùú já nì Fiiliistii yabaaa? A làá dū-bi kí ŋá m-ŋaanaaa?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí Daafiidi yii: «Cùú já nì bi, m làá dū-bi kí ŋá a-ŋaan.»

english_verse: Then David ordered his troops to burn the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab nìn sáǹ ki fá bi-waaŋi niin, ní Daafiidi yāntì bi wùn̄-ŋi ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab fātìi tí gítìń ki yàl̄ ki gbí Reefayiim tantakal kí já nì Daafiidi.

english_verse: David asked God what he should do, and God answered, “Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind them where the balsam trees are.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan ní úǹ kíí-u yii: «Á taa bíití bi-nimbiin pú kí já nì bi! Màntī bi-boon pú, ní kí dāá nyā bi-pu isufi taapu.

english_verse: Wait there until you hear the treetops making the sound of marching troops. That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army. So you must then attack quickly!”
translation_verse: A yaa láa gbìl̄ bi-tagbiŋŋi pu isufee yilpuee, á yáb́ malaa. Ti-Dindaan di līntì a-nyɔkɔpu kí já nì Fiiliistii yab janjakitil.»

english_verse: David had several buildings built in Jerusalem, and he had a tent set up where the sacred chest would be kept.
translation_verse: Daafiidi máń u-ba adiin laakin bi yíì yii Daafiidi Tiŋkee, ní ki bɔ́ntì mpaan ŋubɔ ki cóoǹ tanti bí cáań Unimbɔti dakaau kí síiń poon.

english_verse: Next, David invited everyone to come to Jerusalem and watch the sacred chest being carried to the place he had set up for it.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daafiidi yíiń Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin bí yòon̄ní Unimbɔti dakaau kí cùnnì laakin u bɔ́ntì kí yóoń-uee.

english_verse: He also sent for Aaron's descendants and for the Levites. The Levites that came were:
translation_verse: U kpáfì Aarɔn naantiibi bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab mun.

english_verse: Uriel, the leader of the Kohath clan, and
translation_verse: Keeyaati maaliŋunee, Uriyeel di nìn sá ukpil u nì u-nabiyaamu binib dilaataal nì mmuŋku.

english_verse: Joel, the leader of the Gershon clan, and
translation_verse: Geersɔm maaliŋunee, Jooweel di sá ukpil u nì u-nabiyaamu binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì saalaa.

english_verse: Shemaiah, the leader of the Elizaphan clan, and
translation_verse: Eeliisafan maaliŋunee, Seemaya di sá ukpil, u nì u-nabiyaamu binib alaataa ali.

english_verse: Eliel, the leader of the Hebron clan, and
translation_verse: Eebrɔn maaliŋunee, Eeliyeel di sá ukpil u nì u-nabiyaamu binib imuŋku inaa.

english_verse: Amminadab, the leader of the Uzziel clan, with
translation_verse: Usiyeel maaliŋunee, Amiinadaab di sá ukpil, u nì u-nabiyaamu binib dilaataal nì binib saalaa nì bili.

english_verse: David called together these six Levites and the two priests, Zadok and Abiathar.
translation_verse: Daafiidi yíiń bisaraaŋakpilib Sadooki nì Abiyataar, nì Leefii yab Uriyeel nì Asaaya nì Jooweel nì Seemaya nì Eeliyeel nì Amiinadaab u-cee.

english_verse: The first time we tried to bring the chest to Jerusalem, we didn't ask the Lord what he wanted us to do. He was angry with us, because you Levites weren't there to carry the chest.”
translation_verse: Mpeekaamee, ni nín kaa nìn bí puee di nìn yāntì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nìn fōō mbum ti-pu. Di sá yii taa nìn kpēē dakaayee kii an nín máaǹ puee.»

english_verse: The priests and the Levites made themselves clean. They were now ready to carry the sacred chest
translation_verse: Ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab bɔ́ntì ki ŋá bi-ba circir kí cùú yòon̄ní ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dakaau.

english_verse: on poles that rested on their shoulders, just as the Lord had told Moses to do.
translation_verse: Niinee Leefii yab dū idɔ ki bɔ́ Unimbɔti dakaau buŋyin ki yōoǹ ki būkuǹ ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Mooyiisi bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: David then told the leaders to choose some Levites to sing and play music on small harps, other stringed instruments, and cymbals.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn tùkū Leefii yab kpilib yii bí lēē bi-dicaŋŋi yab poon bilaŋgaaliibi bí nīn gà ilan ki bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati nì saŋgub nì cancakantib, kí nīn fàal̀ nì dipɔɔpindi.

english_verse: Four Levites were then appointed to guard the sacred chest. They were Berechiah, Elkanah, Obed-Edom, and Jehiah. Finally, David chose priests to walk in front of the sacred chest and blow trumpets. They were Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer. The Sacred Chest Is Brought to Jerusalem (
translation_verse: bi nì Oobeedi-Eedoom nì Jeeya. Bisaraaŋaliibi Seebaniya nì Joosafaati nì Neetaneeyeel nì Amasaayi nì Seekariyawuu nì Beenayawuu nì Eeliyeeseer di nìn búǹ akantán ki līī Unimbɔti dakaau nyɔkɔpu. Bi cáań ti-Dindaan dakaau Jeerusaleem (Kpèè

english_verse: David, the leaders of Israel, and the army commanders were very happy as they went to Obed-Edom's house to get the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib nì bijanjakpilib nìn nín cá kí yòon̄ní ti-Dindaan dakaau Oobeedi-Eedoom dumpu. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn bí mmɔŋkpaan poon.

english_verse: God gave the Levites the strength they needed to carry the chest, and so they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn wúń Leefii yab bin nìn tú Dakaayee pu. Niinee ní bi kūū inajaa iluli nì ipijaa iluli ki ŋá Unimbɔti saraa.

english_verse: While the sacred chest was being carried into Jerusalem, everyone was celebrating by shouting and playing music on horns, trumpets, cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn cáá ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau ki cūnnì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ki gbáà iwiliili, ki búǹ iyin nì akantán, ki cákafí cancakantib ní ki bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati nì saŋgub an tùm̀ dàii.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing in honor of the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní bi cáá ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau ki bàn̄ <Daafiidi Tiŋkinee>, Saayuul bisal Miikaal gbóoń tɔkɔla ki kpēē ní ki ká Ubɔti Daafiidi bí ki ŋōō nì dipɔɔpindi. Niinee ní u kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ-u u-pɔbilin.

english_verse: After David had finished, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord
translation_verse: U ŋá saraabi gbanti ki dóòyee ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ samaa pu ti-Dindaan yindi pu.

english_verse: and gave every person in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins.
translation_verse: Boonee ní u yākatì tijin ki tīī Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ. Uninjaaa, unimpuɔɔɔ, báà ŋma nìn fōō kpɔnɔ ubɔ nì daati subiliŋ kalaau nì fiinyi subikuliŋ kalaau. Leefii yab gāā ilan ki pàkā ti-Dindaan (Kpèè Ilan

english_verse: David appointed some of the Levites to serve at the sacred chest; they were to play music and sing praises to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn dū Leefii yab bin bí ditundin ŋyunti gbantee biba ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Dakaau nyɔkɔpu bí gāā ilan kí pàkà ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, kí jāam̀-u ní kí nyɔ̄ŋkì u-yindi.

english_verse: Asaph was their leader, and Zechariah was his assistant. Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and another man named Jeiel were appointed to play small harps and stringed instruments. Asaph himself played the cymbals,
translation_verse: Asaafi di nìn kpòotī-bi ní Seekariyawuu tútúǹ-u. Yeeyiyeel nì Seemiiramooti nì Yeekiyeel nì Maatitiyawuu nì Eeliyaab nì Beenayawuu nì Oobeedi-Eedoom nì Yeeyiyeel bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati nì saŋgub ní Asaafi cákafí cancakantib.

english_verse: and the two priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to blow trumpets every day in front of the sacred chest. David's Song of Praise (Psalms
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi Beenayawuu nì Yasiyeel di nìn yú Unimbɔti Dakaau nyɔkɔpu ki búǹ akantán kaa gbèentí.

english_verse: We must never forget his agreement and his promises, not in thousands of years. *
translation_verse: Ní taa pée súntí u-poondi pu dalba dalba, tibɔti tin u sòon̄ ki tīī anaantitɔntɔkɔ kutuku puee.

english_verse: You belong to the family of Israel, his servant; you are his chosen ones, the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: Nimbi u-tɔntɔnliibi Isirayeel naantiibi, nimbi Jaakɔb naantiibi, nimbi bin u lútèe, téetímaan.

english_verse: That same day, David instructed Asaph and his relatives for the first time to sing these praises to the Lord:
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti sá mpeekaa ŋun Daafiidi tīī Asaafi nì u-nabiyaamu ditundi bí nīn gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: Praise the Lord and pray in his name! Tell everyone what he has done.
translation_verse: Nlan ŋun bi nìn gāāyee sèé: Ní nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan kí yòon̄ u-yindi yilpu, ní yàntīmaan anibul kɔkɔ ń gbìl̄ atuŋkpaan ŋin u ŋáaǹee pu.

english_verse: Sing praises to the Lord! Tell about his miracles.
translation_verse: Ní gāāmaan ilan kí pàkà-u, ní bɔ̀ɔ̀maan tibɔɔkaal kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-u. Ní māafìmaan atuŋkpaan ŋin kɔkɔ u túńee.

english_verse: Celebrate and worship his holy name with all your heart.
translation_verse: Ní nīn fàal̀maan u-circir yindi pu, nín̄ bímaan mmɔnni, nimbi bin nyàab̀ ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: Trust the Lord and his mighty power. Worship him always.
translation_verse: Nyàab̀maan ti-Dindaan nì u-pɔŋŋu, pée nyàab̀maan kí wāl̀ u-nimbiin.

english_verse: Remember his miracles and all his wonders and his fair decisions.
translation_verse: Ní téetímaan maamaacib bin kɔkɔ u ŋée, nì atulim nì ibɔsoon in nyáń u-nyɔkɔnee pu.

english_verse: The Lord is our God, bringing justice everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Úǹ di sá ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, úǹ di sá duulinya kɔkɔ bɔsoonliu.

english_verse: when he said, “I'll give you the land of Canaan.”
translation_verse: ki lī yii: «M làá dū Kanaan tiŋki kí tīī-si, án nīn sá si nì a-naantiibi fakal».

english_verse: At the time there were only a few of us, and we were homeless.
translation_verse: Ti-naanjab kaa nìn náaǹ báà fiii, bi nìn pée sá binicambi bikaaŋkaabi yéè ní kitiŋ nee pu.

english_verse: We wandered from nation to nation, from one country to another.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kàal̀ atimbunni ní ki kpántí, ní kí kàl̄ dibeel diban kí póotí din kíǹ.

english_verse: God did not let anyone mistreat our people. Instead he protected us by punishing rulers
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti kaa kíí báà unil ń sàaǹ-bi. Bi-puee, Unimbɔti dáaĺ bibɔtiibi tafal ki lī yii:

english_verse: and telling them, “Don't touch my chosen leaders or harm my prophets!”
translation_verse: «Ní taa gbēē bin m lútèe, kí taa ŋá m-bɔnaatiliibi tikpitil tiba.»

english_verse: Everyone on this earth, sing praises to the Lord. Day after day announce, “The Lord has saved us!”
translation_verse: Duulinya kɔkɔ nib, gāāmaan ilan kí pàkà ti-Dindaan. Ŋwiin kamaayee, ní nīn báakí ki lì yii úǹ di sá Ufiil.

english_verse: Tell every nation on earth, “The Lord is wonderful and does marvelous things!
translation_verse: Māafìmaan atimbun kɔkɔ nib u-nyooti, kí māafìmaan duulinya kɔkɔn u-maamaaci tuuŋŋi.

english_verse: The Lord is great and deserves our greatest praise! He is the only God worthy of our worship.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di sá ukpaan ní ki máaǹ inyɔŋki. U sá kuwambiiu ní ki jítiǹ awaa kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Other nations worship idols, but the Lord created the heavens.
translation_verse: Anibul ŋin kíǹee waaŋi kaa bí tiban, ama ní ti-Dindaan di náań yilpu.

english_verse: Give honor and praise to the Lord, whose power and beauty fill his holy temple.”
translation_verse: U-nimbiin ní tikpaandi nì dibeel bí, mpɔn nì mmɔn gbí u-kɔŋkooŋŋun.

english_verse: Tell everyone of every nation, “Praise the glorious power of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ntimu kɔkɔ nibuliŋ, dāá tīīmaan ti-Dindaan tinyool, ní bāakìmaan u-nyooti nì u-pɔŋŋu.

english_verse: He is wonderful! Praise him and bring an offering into his temple. Worship the Lord, majestic and holy.
translation_verse: Dāá nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan u-yiŋkpaandi. Cáaḿmaan ni-saraabi u-nimbiin. Bòom̄maan taapu ti-Dindaan nimbiin, ŋyunti ŋun u yaa lēē u-ba ki dàkēe.

english_verse: Everyone on earth, now tremble!” The world stands firm, never to be shaken.
translation_verse: Duulinyan kɔkɔ nib, ni-wunti ń nīn gbáà kpàkpakpa u-nimbiin! Tiŋman kitiŋ bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄, ní kì kpá kí lábití kí cìb̄.

english_verse: Tell the heavens and the earth to be glad and celebrate! And announce to the nations, “The Lord is King!”
translation_verse: Kutagbɔŋu, nín̄ fàal̀, kitiŋ, nín̄ bí dipɔɔpindin! Lìmaan atimbun kɔkɔ nib cee yii: «Ti-Dindaan di sá ubɔti!»

english_verse: Command the ocean to roar with all of its creatures and the fields to rejoice with all of their crops.
translation_verse: Tiŋku ń nīn wòoǹ ki kpáaǹ tin kɔkɔ bí u-poonee! Tisati ń nīn fàal̀ ki kpáaǹ tin kɔkɔ bí ti-poonee!

english_verse: Then every tree in the forest will sing joyful songs to the Lord. He is coming to judge all people on earth.
translation_verse: Kubambaŋŋun sufii ń nīn gbáà iwiliili ti-Dindaan nimbiin, di sá yii u dòoń kí sòoǹ duulinya bɔti.

english_verse: Praise the Lord because he is good to us, and his love never fails.
translation_verse: Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan, di sá yii u ŋān̄, ní u-neeŋkpaandi bí ki cá jaanjaan!

english_verse: Say to him, “Save us, Lord God! Bring us back from among the nations. Let us celebrate and shout in praise of your holy name.
translation_verse: Ní lìmaan yii: «Unimbɔti ti-Fiiliu, fīī-ti, kóoǹ-ti kí kpāfì, ní kí fīī-ti kí nyāntí atimbun ŋin kíǹee ŋaan. A-yindi sá circir yindi ní. Niinee ti làá ŋmā kí tùkù-si yii si nì ditundi, ní án nīn mɔ̄ǹ-ti tí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si.»

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you deserve to be praised forever and ever.” After David finished, the people shouted, “Amen! Praise the Lord!” David Appoints Worship Leaders at Jerusalem and Gibeon
translation_verse: Ní jāam̀maan ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, kí nīn cá abin abin. Ní samaa kɔkɔ kíí yii «Ameeni! Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan!»

english_verse: David chose Asaph and the Levites in his clan to be in charge of the daily worship at the place where the sacred chest was kept.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Daafiidi tīī Asaafi nì u-nabiyaamu mara yii bí gbíntí ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau cee. Niin ní bi làá nīn bí ki tūǹ bi-tundi baabadal kí nóó nì ŋwiin kamaa koobil nín sá puee.

english_verse: David also chose Zadok the priest and his relatives who were priests to serve at the Lord's sacred tent at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn dū ti-Dindaan circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun bí Gabawɔn tiŋkinee tundi ki ŋúbiǹ usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nì u-nabiyaamu.

english_verse: They were to offer sacrifices on the altar every morning and evening, just as the Lord had commanded in the Law he gave Israel.
translation_verse: Niin ní bi làá nīn ŋáań kutaafaau nì kujoou bisaraawɔkaabi. Bíǹ di làá nīn ŋáań tin kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā marab bin ti-Dindaan nìn dūu tīī Isirayeelee gbɔŋku poon.

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were their assistants, as well as the other men who had been chosen to praise the Lord for his never-ending love.
translation_verse: Binib bin nìn kútì bi-puee di sá Eeman nì Yeedutun nì bin bi nìn pée lēē bí nīn gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaanee. Di sá yii u-ŋanti bí ní ki cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were also responsible for blowing the trumpets, and for playing the cymbals and other instruments during worship at the tent. The Levites in Jeduthun's clan were the guards at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Eeman nì Yeedutun di nìn kpèé akantán nì cancakantib nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi nìn cáa bɔ̀ɔ́ ki gà ilanee. Yeedutun dicaŋkun yab di nìn cí kipunyɔkɔ.

english_verse: After that, everyone went home, and David went home to his family.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní báà ŋma nín kùǹ, ní Daafiidi mun nín gítí kí cùú màntì u-dicaŋku yab pu.

english_verse: Soon after David moved into his new palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest is kept in a tent.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi kāl̀ u-beecindin. Dalbee ní u bí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan yii: «Kpèè, man kóò kudii kun ní bi dū seedir dɔi ki máńee, ama ní ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau yú tanti un bi dū satab ki ŋée poon.»

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more for my descendants. You are treating me as if I am a very important person.
translation_verse: Ama sii m-Nimbɔtiu ceeyee, tíǹ kɔkɔ kaa sá tiba, ní a gíti pōoǹ m-dicaŋku yab dipoondi fool boon pu. Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a dū-mi ki yíiń unikpaan un nyáń diyindee dee.

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Ama kunyeeu gbantee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Naatan ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: to go to David and tell him: David, you are my servant, so listen carefully: You are not the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: «Cùú tùkù m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi yii man ni-Dindaan di lī yii: <Sii di kaa làá mā-mi kudii ḿ nīn kóò.

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Doooo ŋwiin ŋun ní m nyántìń Isirayeel nibul Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹee, maa láá kɔ́ kudii poon ki ká. Ama tantib poon ní m pée kóò ki yìiǹ ki kpántí ikaa.

english_verse: I chose special leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Kí kūtèe, abin ŋin kɔkɔ m céeǹ Isirayeel nibulee, m lēē bibɔsoonliibi tikpil bí nīn kpòotī m-nib. Ama maa láá bālifì bi-kansikin báà ubɔ yii: <Ba pu ní aa dū seedir dɔi ki máń-mi kudii?>»

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: M nìn bí a-cee laakin kamaa ní a yaa nìn cée. M kūū ki céetì a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ a-nimbiin. M làá yàntī á nyā diyindi kii kitiŋ pu bɔtikpaambee.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace. They will no longer have to tremble with fear—evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: M làá tīī m-nibul Isirayeel yab laakin ní bi làá nīn kóò kí taa ti nín̄ fàŋkí báà tibee. Binikpitib kaa ti làá dāan̄ kí sàaǹ-bi kii bi nín nìn ŋáań pu njamin,

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people, and I will keep your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that like you, your descendants will be kings.
