translation_verse: ŋyunti ŋun m nìn lēekì bibɔsoonliibi bi nìn ŋúb́-bee. M làá yàntī á pɔ̄ɔkiǹ a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ, ní ki kpáàa bíi tùkù-si yii man a-Dindaan làá náań-si dicindi.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried beside your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun a-maŋfal wiiŋyi yaa láa dóò a cūtìi ŋàl̄ a-baabee, m làá dāá lēē sisi a-ba jipɔɔn ubɔ ní ú fōō a-yil kí jī dibeel. M làá dāá yàntī u-beel ń báań kí nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Úǹ di làá dāá mā-mi Kudii ní ḿ dāá yàntī u-beel ń báań kí nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: I will be like a father to him, and he will be like a son to me. I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: M làá dāá nīn sá ubaati ki tīī-u ní úǹ ń dāá nīn sá man jipɔɔn. M kpá kí dāá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-u kii m nín ŋá ubɔti un līntì a-nyɔkɔpuee puee.

english_verse: I will make sure that your son and his descendants will rule my people and my kingdom forever.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī ú nīn pée sá m-nibul nì m-beel kpootiliu ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ní kí yàntī u-beel ń báań inyaan kí nīn cá talku.>»

english_verse: Nathan told David exactly what the Lord had said. David Gives Thanks to the Lord (
translation_verse: Ní Naatan cáá tin kɔkɔ ní Unimbɔti tùkū-u dileedakal gbanti poonee ki nāatì Daafiidi. Daafiidi wimmeem (Kpèè

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts. What else can I say, except that you have honored me?
translation_verse: Ba ní man Daafiidi gíti ŋūǹ kí lì kí kūtì tinyool tin a tīī-mi nee pu? A nyí man a-tɔntɔnliu ki cíl̀.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. He sat there and prayed: Lord God, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Daafiidi kɔ́ ki kāl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ní ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, ŋma ní m sá ní m-dicaŋku bí tilatin ní a cáá-mi ki bàn̄ laakin m bí nee?

english_verse: It was your choice to do these wonderful things for me and to make these promises.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a nín néeń man a-tɔntɔnliu nì an nín fáatiǹ-see pu ní a túń atuŋkpaan nee kɔkɔ, kí dàkà a nín sá ukpaan puee.

english_verse: No other god is like you, Lord—you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, ubɔ kaa ti bí laaba kii siiyee! Unimbɔti ubɔ mun kaa ti bí ki bàn̄-si, ki nóó nì tin ti-tafaliŋ gbìl̄ee.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so that your people could live here.
translation_verse: Dinibul diba pée gíti bí kitiŋ pu doo ki náań nì Isirayeel nibulaaa? A cūtì ki fīī-dì ki nyántì Eejipiti yab ŋaan ní ki dū-dì ki ŋá a-nibul. A túń atuŋkpaan nì titumbilindi ki tīī-bi ki nyáń diyindi. A jìn̄ anibul a-nibul din a fīī ki nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee nimbiin.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a dū Isirayeel yab ki kpántì a-nibul kí nīn cá jaanjaan ní ki kpántì di-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord All-Powerful rules Israel and is their God.” My kingdom will be strong,
translation_verse: Tiŋman yàntī án ŋá míǹ! Niinee a làá nyā diyindi kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ní binib ń lì yii: <Duulinya kɔkɔ Dindaan di sá Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, Unimbɔti un bí ki tīī Isirayeelee.> Yàntī dibeel ń gbíntí m-dicaŋkun kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: because you are my God, and you have promised that my descendants will be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Di sá yii, m-Nimbɔtiu, sii di yāntì m béè a-landɔkɔŋu ŋun sá yii a làá tīī-mi naantiibi bin làá dāá jī dibeel m-kpátam boonee. An pu ní man a-tɔntɔnliu ká dipɔbil ki gbāā a-nimbiin ki mèé-si nee.

english_verse: You are the Lord God, and you have made this good promise to me.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Dindaan, sii un di sá Unimbɔtee, sii di pōoǹ yii a làá ŋá-mi tiŋaŋkpaandi gbanti!

english_verse: Now please bless my descendants forever, and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already blessed my family, and I know you will bless us forever.
translation_verse: A lēē kí bìin̄ m-dicaŋku pu án nín làá ŋá pu m-naantiibi ń nīn pée sá bibɔtiibi a-nimbiin kí nīn cá jaanjaanee. An nín sá yii sii ti-Dindaan di bīiǹ bi-puee, bi làá pée ká dibiindi ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan!»

english_verse: While King Hadadezer of Zobah was trying to gain control of the territory near the Euphrates River, David met him in battle at Hamath and defeated him.
translation_verse: U nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Adadeeseer. Siirii tiŋki Sooba kin bí Amaati watil púee bɔtiu dee. Ŋyunti gbantee, Adadeeseer nìn bíi mɔ̀ kí wàan̄ u-beel kí tin cáá sāā Eefiraati mɔɔl ní.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried gold shields, but David took these shields and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn kóoǹ Adadeeseer janjaliibi gbampɔɔŋi ŋin sá sindaariyee ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: Then David stationed some of his troops in Damascus, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn kāaǹ gɔminab Damaasi tiŋki pu. Aram yab nìn kíǹ ki bí Daafiidi taapu ní ki pà lampoo ki tìì-u. Laakin kamaa Daafiidi yaa nìn cūtèe, ti-Dindaan nìn tìì-u dijajil ní.

english_verse: King Tou of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Tou heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David on his victory. Hadoram also brought him gifts made of gold, silver, and bronze.
translation_verse: U nìn dū u-jipɔɔn Adooram ki tú yii ú cùú jāam̀ ubɔti Daafiidi. Adooram nìn jáam̀ ubɔti ki pàkā-u, kun puee u nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Adadeeseer. Di sá yii Toowu nì Adadeeseer nìn jáà ní. Adooram nìn kpáàa tú sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti wanti ki cáań ki pú Daafiidi.

english_verse: David gave these gifts to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold he had captured from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn dū an wanti gbanti kɔkɔ ki sú ti-Dindaan, kii u nín nìn dū animbil nì sindaariya un u nìn fōoń Eedoom yab nì Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab nì Fiiliistii yab nì Amaleeki yab cee ki sú puee.

english_verse: Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed
translation_verse: Seeruya jipɔɔn Abiisayi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedoom yab Ŋyaam tantakalin. U nìn kūū bi-kansikin binib kutukub saalku nì bita.

translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn kāaǹ gɔminab Eedoom tiŋki pu ní ki dū ki-nib ki ŋá u-taapu. Laakin kamaa Daafiidi yaa nìn cūtèe, ti-Dindaan nìn tìì-u dijajil ní. Daafiidi kàlimbi yiŋŋi (Kpèè

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Seeruya jipɔɔn Joowaab di nìn sá bijanjaliibi kpiliu ukpaan. Ayiiluudi jipɔɔn Yoosafaati di nìn sá ubɔti taapu yɔu.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests. Shavsha was the secretary.
translation_verse: Ayiituub jipɔɔn Sadooki nì Abiyataar jipɔɔn Abimeeleeki di nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi. Safeesa di nìn sá ugbaŋŋmal.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were his highest-ranking officials.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu di nìn kpèé Keereeti yab nì Peeleeti yab bin cí ubɔtee. Ubɔti Daafiidi u-ba jipɔmbi di sá u-kàliŋkpilib bin nìn pée bí ki kɔ́ĺ-uee.

english_verse: Joab saw that the enemy troops were lined up on both sides of him. So he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Syrians.
translation_verse: Joowaab ká yii kujaau làá nīn bí u-nyɔkɔpu nì u-boon pú. Di sá ní u lēē Isirayeel janjaliibi bimɔntiibi ki yāntì bi yúl̀ mpɔn pu ki bíitiǹ Aram yab.

english_verse: Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋubɔ boonee ní Amɔn yab bɔtiu Naasi kpíì ní u-jipɔɔn fōō u-yil ki kāl̀ dibeel.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and accepted him as their new ruler. The Syrians never helped the Ammonites again.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Adadeeseer taapuee nìn ká yii Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Niinee ní bi nì Daafiidi sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí bi-kansikin. Bi nìn kíǹ ki bí u-taapu ní. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, Siirii yab kíǹ ki fàŋkí kí jòò Amɔn yab.

english_verse: the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, “Do you really believe King David is honoring your father by sending these men to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our country, so he can come and destroy it.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Amɔn yab yidambi bí Anuun yii: «A dàkafī yii Daafiidi nín là kí tīī a-baa tinyool kí sɔ̀ŋkì a-pɔbil puee ní u túnní binib a-ceeee? Waa túnní u-nib bí dāan̄ kí yìiǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé kitiŋ filiŋfeetii níii?»

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off and their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Anuun yāntì bi cúú Daafiidi kàliŋkpilib ki kōol̀ bi-nyimpuliŋ, ki cátì bi-bɔkutiŋ ki ŋmāntiǹ bi-kpiliŋ ní ki jìn̄-bi.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message that told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Ní bi cūtìi máafì Daafiidi binibee bɔti. U nìn lēē binib ki tú bi cūtìi túŋkì-bi nsanni kun puee bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-bi icoo tikpil. english_verse: David heard what was happening, and he sent out Joab with his army.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nín gbìl̄ mimmee, ní u dū ujanjakpil Joowaab nì bijanjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee ki tú.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops marched to the entrance of the city and prepared for battle, while the Syrian troops took their positions in the open fields.
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nìn cūtì ki yúl̀ mpɔn pu bi-tiŋyil punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu kí já kujaau. Ama bibɔtiibi bin nìn dɔ́miń kí tūtuǹ-bee bíǹ nìn yúl̀ tisatin laaba.

english_verse: Then he put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and told them to fight against the Ammonites.
translation_verse: U nìn dū u-janjaliibi bin kíǹee ki ŋúbíǹ u-naal Abisayi ní ki yāntì bi yúl̀ mpɔn pu ki bíitiǹ Amɔn yab.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Syrians are too much for me to handle, come and help me. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Joowaab tùkū u-nabiki yii: «Siirii yab yaa bíi pɔ́ɔkíǹ-mee, á dāá tíkiń-mi. M yaa tí ká yii Amɔn yab bíi pɔ́ɔkíǹ-see, ma mun làá dāan̄ kí tíkiń-si.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the towns of our Lord God. I pray he will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Dàkà dibaatandi, tí dàkà dibaatandi kí fīī ti-nibul nì ti-Nimbɔtiu timmu. Ti-Dindaan ń ŋá min u lèe.»

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them.
translation_verse: Niinee Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi nín cá kí já nì Siirii yab, ní bíǹ sáǹ-bi.

english_verse: When the Ammonite troops saw that the Syrians had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab then returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nín ká yii Siirii yab sáǹee, ní bi mun sáǹ Abisayi, ki kɔ́ kitiŋin. Niinee ní Joowaab nín gítí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: As soon as the Syrians realized they had been defeated, they sent for their troops that were stationed on the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led these troops to Ammon.
translation_verse: Siirii yab nín ká yii Isirayeel yab pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bee, ní bi tú binib bí cùú yíiń Siirii yab janjaliibi bin kóò Eefiraati mɔɔl lapu púee. Adadeeseer janjakpiliu Soobaaki di nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: David found out what the Syrians were doing, and he brought Israel's entire army together. They crossed the Jordan River, and he commanded them to take their positions facing the Syrian troops. Soon after the fighting began,
translation_verse: Ní bi tùkū Daafiidi an bɔti, ní u kóoǹ Isirayeel yab janjaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì, ní bi nín cá ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki cūtìi yúl̀ ŋkɔnjaloon pu. Siirii yab nìn yúl̀ mpɔ̀n pu ki tātìi gbāaǹ dikɔ̀ndi pu kí já nì Daafiidi.

english_verse: The next spring, the time when kings go to war, Joab marched out in command of the Israelite army and destroyed towns all over the country of Ammon. He attacked the capital city of Rabbah and left it in ruins. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Dibindi tú an bàn̄ ŋyunti ŋun bibɔtiibi nyēē ki cáà kujaauee, ní Joowaab līntì Isirayeel janjaliibi nyɔkɔpu ki cūtìi nāaǹ Amɔn yab tiŋki kɔkɔ. U nìn bíi bɔ́ntí kí já nì bi-tiŋyil Raaba kí fōō-kì. Ama Daafiidi úǹ nìn gbíntì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Joowaab nìn jáń ki fōō Raaba tiŋki ki nāaǹ-kì.

english_verse: He forced the people of Rabbah to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He also did the same thing with the people in all the other Ammonite towns. David then led Israel's army back to Jerusalem. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn cúú kitiŋee nib ki cūnnì ki tɔ́ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee poon: bi nìn sèekì idɔ, ki kpítí ataŋkpee ní ki gàatī isufi. Míǹ ní Daafiidi ŋá Amɔn yab timmu mun kíǹee kɔkɔ poon. Boonee ní u fātìi nín gítí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, u nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ. Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab jaaku (Kpèè

english_verse: Some time later, Israel fought a battle against the Philistines at Gezer. During this battle, Sibbecai from Hushah killed Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were defeated.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee kujaau kubɔ nyáń Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab kansikin Geeseer tiŋkin. An jaaku poon ní Siibkayi un sá Usa tiŋkinee kūū Siipayi un sá Reefa naantiiu ubɔee. Bi nìn dū Fiiliistii yab ki ŋá bi-taapu.

english_verse: In another battle against the Philistines, Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
translation_verse: Kujaau kubɔ mun nìn gíti nyáń Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab kansikin ní Yayiir jipɔɔn kūū Gooliyaati un sá Gaati tiŋkinee naal Laamii. Laamii kpaŋki kin u nìn ŋúb́ee dɔŋu nìn gbìfì kii nsataludɔee ní.

english_verse: Another one of the Philistine soldiers who was a descendant of the Rephaim was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. During a battle at Gath,
translation_verse: Kujaau kubɔ mun dāa gíti nyáń Gaati tiŋkin. Ku-poonee unaaciin ubɔ nìn bí ki cáá ŋŋambiyaamu muluu kuŋaŋfaau kamaa pu nì ntaŋambiyaamu muluu kutafaau kamaa mun pu. U-ŋambiyaamu nì u-taŋambiyaamu kɔkɔ nìn nyáń mmuŋku nì munaa dee. U mun nìn sá Arafa maaliŋun ní.

english_verse: he made fun of Israel, so David's nephew Jonathan killed him.
translation_verse: U nìn sīī Isirayeel yab. Niinee Sama jipɔɔn Joonatan, Daafiidi wee kūū-u.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these three men from Gath who were descendants of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nì u-janjaliibi di nìn kūū Fiiliistii yab janjaliibi gbanti. Bi nìn sá Gaati tiŋkin Arafa dicaŋkun ní.

english_verse: But David replied, “No! I want to pay you what they're worth. I can't just take something from you and then offer the Lord a sacrifice that cost me nothing.”
translation_verse: Ama ní ubɔti Daafiidi bí Ɔrinan yii: «Aayee, m làá dā a-bileegbanaapaal ní kí pà-si kunimbiŋmiiu nín sá puee. Maa là kí dū tin sá a-wantee nì faalaa wanti kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī m-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu.»

english_verse: The Lord said to Gad, one of David's prophets,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì ubɔnaatil Gaadi un di kpòotī Daafiidee ní ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: Joab answered, “Your Majesty, even if the Lord made your kingdom a hundred times larger, you would still rule everyone in it. Why do you need to know how many soldiers there are? Don't you think that would make the whole nation angry?”
translation_verse: Ní Joowaab kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, m mèé yii ti-Dindaan ń yàntī u-nibul Isirayeel yab ń bùtī ŋfunyɔm dilaataal pu. Bi-kɔkɔ bí díǹ pu nee sii ti-baa ubɔti taapu ní. Kin ba pu ní a baasii nyàab̀ kí kàaǹ Isirayeel yab kí yàntī bí yìntī míǹ?»

english_verse: But David would not change his mind. And so Joab went everywhere in Israel and Judah and counted the people. He returned to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee ubɔti marau nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ Joowaab nín nìn dàkafī puee, ní úǹ dāa gīī ki ŋá míǹ. Joowaab nìn cúú nsan ki yìin̄ Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn ní ki fātìi gítìń Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: Joab refused to include anyone from the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he still disagreed with David's orders. God Punishes Israel (
translation_verse: Joowaab kaa nìn kàan̄ Leefii naakookun yab nì Beenjameen naakookun yab ki kútì bin kíǹee pu. Di sá yii ubɔti marauee kaa nìn kāliǹ-u báà fiii. Unimbɔti dáaĺ Daafiidi tafal (Kpèè

english_verse: “Tell David that I will punish him in one of three ways. But he will have to choose which one it will be.”
translation_verse: «Cùú tùkù Daafiidi yii man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Man ni-Dindaan, m dū tiwan tita ní ki bíl̀ u-nimbiin ú lēē tin u là ḿ dūú dáaĺ u-tafalee.>»

english_verse: and David prayed, “It's my fault! I sinned by ordering the people to be counted. They have done nothing wrong—they are innocent sheep. Lord God, please punish me and my family. Don't let the disease wipe out your people.” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí Unimbɔti yii: «Man di kaa bí yii bí kàaǹ binibaaa? Man di ŋá ikpiti, man di yīntì, m-nibul mun ŋá ba? An sá man nì m-dicaŋku tafal ní á dáaĺ? Ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu, an sá man nì m-dicaŋku yab tafal ní á dáaĺ. Taa dū iween nee kí tɔ̄ a-nibul pu.» Daafiidi máń ti-Dindaan nsaraafan (Kpèè

english_verse: David's order to count the people made God angry, and he punished Israel.
translation_verse: Tibɔti gbanti kaa nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ Unimbɔti, ní u dáaĺ Isirayeel yab tafal.

english_verse: David prayed, “I am your servant. But what I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí Unimbɔti yii: «Ikpitikpaan ní m ŋá nee. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee m mèé-si yii á dū m-yìntitam gbanti kí pɔ̄-mi, kun puee m lafun ŋá kii m sá uwaatee ní.»

english_verse: Gad went to David and told him: You must choose how the Lord will punish you:
translation_verse: Ní Gaadi cūtì Daafiidi cee ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé. Ba ní a là ḿ dūú dáaĺ a-tafal ní?

english_verse: Will there be three years when the land won't grow enough food for its people? Or will your enemies constantly defeat you for three months? Or will the Lord send a horrible disease to strike your land for three days? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God who sent me.
translation_verse: Ŋkùm ń nyā a-tiŋki pu abin ataaa, binannanliibi ń já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-si iŋmal itaaa, bìlbil kúm ń jēetí kitiŋ nee pu ní ntuun ń dū ti-Dindaan tàataajiki kí pɔ̀fì binib Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn iwiin ita? Kɔŋkɔnnee, dàkafì tiŋan kí tùkù-mi tin m làá tin kíí un túnní-mee.»

english_verse: David was miserable and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí Gaadi yii: «M bí kunimbaakpaaŋŋu poon ní. Ama an sɔ́ ḿ kɔ́ ti-Dindaan ŋaan ki jítiǹ ḿ kɔ́ unil ŋaan, di sá yii ti-Dindaan úǹ poon mɔ̄ ní.»

english_verse: Then he sent an angel to destroy the city of Jerusalem. But just as the angel was about to do that, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused the people, and he told the angel, “Stop! They have suffered enough.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn tú ntuun ŋú cùú nàan̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Ama ti-Dindaan nín ká ntuunee bí ki nà binib puee, ní an gíti kɔ́-u falaa nnaabu gbanti pu. Di sá ní u bí ntuunee yii: «An ŋmāntèe, gbèen̄ee!» Ŋyunti gbantee ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nìn yú ujeebusja Araafina bileegbanaapaal caŋin.

english_verse: David saw the Lord's angel in the air, holding a sword over Jerusalem. He and the leaders of Israel, who were all wearing sackcloth, bowed with their faces to the ground,
translation_verse: Daafiidi wáaǹ ki kpēēyee ní ki ká ntuunee yú yilpu nì taapu kansikin ki fɔ́fì kitàataajiki ki túĺ Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Niinee ní Daafiidi nì bitindaŋkpilib tātìi gbāaǹ bi-yigbeeŋi tūū kitiŋ ki pēē kutukub.

english_verse: The Lord's angel told the prophet Gad to tell David that he must go to Araunah's threshing place and build an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu bí Gaadi ń tùkù Daafiidi yii: «Jɔ̄m̀ ujeebusja Araafina bileegbanaapaal pu kí mā ti-Dindaan nsaraafan.»

english_verse: Araunah and his four sons were threshing wheat at the time, and when they saw the angel, the four sons ran to hide.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee Ɔrinan nìn bí u-naapaal pu ki gbáà bilee. U fātèe ní ki ká ntuun, ní u-jipɔmbi binaa bin nìn bí u-cee niinee sáǹ ki bál̀.

english_verse: Just then, David arrived, and when Araunah saw him, he stopped his work and bowed down.
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi cōom̀ ki nín cá Ɔrinan cee. Ɔrinan kpēēyee Daafiidi dee ní u nyáń ki túŋkì-u ní ki tātìi gbāaǹ u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ ubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: David said, “Would you sell me your threshing place, so I can build an altar on it to the Lord? Then this disease will stop killing the people. I'm willing to pay whatever you say it's worth.”
translation_verse: Ní Daafiidi bí Ɔrinan yii: «Dū a-naapaal nee kí tīī-mi. M là kí mā ti-Dindaan nsaraafan ŋu-pu. Mimmee nnaabu ŋun jéetì dinibul pu nee làá gbèen̄. Dū-ŋu kí tīī-mi ḿ pà-si ŋu-daaku nín sá puee.»

english_verse: Araunah answered, “Take it, Your Majesty, and do whatever you want with it. I'll even give you the oxen for the sacrifice and the wheat for the grain sacrifice. And you can use the threshing-boards for the fire. It's all yours!”
translation_verse: Ní Ɔrinan kíí Daafiidi yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, yòon̄ tin kɔkɔ fáatì-see kí dūú ŋá saraabi. Kpèè inaa sèé á dūú ŋá saraawɔkaa. Tɔrɔku dɔkpalkaai mun sèé á dūú kpāā ŋŋmi kí wà saraabi, bilee mun sèé á dūú ŋá tijimpin saraau. M dū kɔkɔ ki tīī-si.»

english_verse: David built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. David prayed, and the Lord answered him by sending fire down on the altar.
translation_verse: Daafiidi máń ti-Dindaan nsaraafan niin ní ki ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi. U nìn mēē ti-Dindaan ní úǹ kíí-u ki yāntì ŋŋmi nyánní yilpu ki wùn̄ bisaraawɔkaabi bin pá ŋfan puee.

english_verse: Then the Lord commanded the angel to put the sword away.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū ntuunee yii ŋú gíiǹ kitàataajiki kí fúuń kujitooun.

english_verse: When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayer, he offered more sacrifices there at the threshing place,
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn ká yii ti-Dindaan kíí ki fōō u-wimmeem Ɔrinan un sá Jeebusi tiŋkinee bileegbanaapaal pu. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee ní u kíǹ ki cáà niin múlmul ki ŋáań saraabi.

english_verse: David said, “The temple of the Lord God must be built right here at this threshing place. And the altar for offering sacrifices will also be here.” David Prepares To Build the Temple
translation_verse: An di yì-tì ní Daafiidi nìn lī yii: «Doo di sá ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti diiku, ní doo di làá nīn kíǹ ki sá Isirayeel yab saraawɔkaabi faŋŋu.» Daafiidi bɔ́ntì kunimbɔtidii mātam

english_verse: David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to come to Jerusalem. Then he assigned some to cut blocks of stone for building the temple.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn yāntì bi kóoǹ binicambi bin kóò Isirayeel tiŋkinee ki kpáfì ní u lēē bi-kansikin bin làá kpítí ataŋkpee bí dūú mā Unimbɔti diikuee.

english_verse: He also brought an endless supply of cedar logs from the cities of Sidon and Tyre.
translation_verse: U nìn bɔ́ntì seedir dɔi an kaa cáá ŋkaan ki kpúkuǹ, di sá yii Tiir nì Siidɔn yab nìn cáań-u seedir dɔi tikpil tikpil.

english_verse: He said, “The temple for the Lord must be great, so that everyone in the world will know about it. But since my son Solomon is young and has no experience, I will make sure that everything is ready for the temple to be built.” That's why David did all these things before he died. David Instructs Solomon To Build the Temple
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn lī u-ban yii: «M-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn dáá pɔ̀ɔǹ, kaa láá nyí tiba. Ama kudii kun u làá mā ti-Dindaanee máaǹ kí nīn sá kukpaaŋŋu kí nīn cáá kunyaaŋŋu binib ń gbìl̄ ku-pu ntimu kɔkɔ poon. An puee m làá bɔ́ntí ku-mātam kí yóoń-u.» Di sá ní Daafiidi lafun bɔ́ntì tiwan tikpil ki síiǹ ki wāatì ní ki nín kpíì. Daafiidi tīī Saloomɔn mara yii ú mā kunimbɔtidii

english_verse: David sent for his son Solomon and told him to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Daafiidi yíiń u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn ní ki tīī-u mara yii ú mā ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu kudii.

english_verse: He said: My son, I wanted to build a temple where the Lord my God would be worshiped.
translation_verse: Daafiidi tùkū Saloomɔn yii: «M-jipɔɔn, mama m-ba nìn lēē m-pɔbilin yii m làá mā ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu kudii.

english_verse: But some time ago, he told me, “David, you have killed too many people and have fought too many battles. That's why you are not the one to build my temple.
translation_verse: Ama ní ti-Dindaan tùkū-mi yii: <A jáń tijakpaandi tikpil ki kūū binib tikpil. Fatiku un kɔkɔ nyáń ki fá kitiŋ man nimbiinee puee, an kaa sá sii di làá mā kudii kun poon binib làá nīn dòoń ki jáaḿ-mee.

english_verse: But when your son becomes king, I will give him peace throughout his kingdom. His name will be Solomon, because during his rule I will keep Israel safe and peaceful.
translation_verse: Kpèè, a làá màal̀ kibininjabiki kiba, kì làá nīn sá ŋgbansɔŋfi niliu ní. M làá yàntī ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí u nì binannanliibi bin māntìi tú-uee kansikin. U-yindi di làá nīn sá Saloomɔn, taapu di sá yii <Ŋgbansɔŋfi daan>. U-beel yuntiŋuee, m làá dāá yàntī ŋgbansɔŋfi nì dibatɔl ń nīn bí Isirayeel tiŋki pu.

english_verse: Solomon will build my temple. He will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. In fact, one of his descendants will always rule in Israel.”
translation_verse: Úǹ di làá dāá mā-mi kunimbɔtidii. U làá dāá nīn sá-mi ujipɔnti ní ḿ dāá nīn sá-u ubaati. M làá yàntī u-beel ń báań inyaan Isirayeel tiŋki pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan.>»

english_verse: Solomon, my son, I now pray that the Lord your God will be with you and keep his promise to help you build a temple for him.
translation_verse: «Míǹ puee kɔŋkɔnnee, m-jipɔɔn, ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn bí a-cee á ŋmā kí mā-u kudii, kii u nín nìn pōoǹ a-pu puee.

english_verse: May he give you wisdom and knowledge, so that you can rule Israel according to his Law.
translation_verse: U yaa láa dū Isirayeel tiŋki pɔŋŋu ki ŋúbiǹ-see, ú dāá tīī-si iciin nì dinyil á ŋmā kí nīn tɔ́ úǹ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu marau.

english_verse: If you obey the laws and teachings that the Lord gave Moses, you will be successful. Be strong and brave and don't get discouraged or be afraid of anything.
translation_verse: A yaa tɔ́ abɔkpaa nì marab bin u dī Mooyiisi pu ki tīī Isirayeel yabee, ki cáá-bi ki tūǹ ditundee, án làá bútí-si tikɔkɔ poon. Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba, kí ká dipɔbil, a-wunti ń taa yɔ̀tī, ní kí taa fàŋkì báà tiba.

english_verse: I have also assigned men who will cut and lay the stone. And there are carpenters and people who are experts in working with
translation_verse: Bitɔntɔnliibi tikpil bí ki làá tɔ̄-si atuun. Bitaŋkpakpitiliibi bí, bidɔkpitiliibi bí, kapintab bí, ní atuun ŋin kíǹee kɔkɔ tɔntɔnliibi bí ki nyí bi-tuuŋŋi tiŋan pu.

english_verse: gold, silver, bronze, and iron. You have plenty of workers to do the job. Now get started, and I pray that the Lord will be with you in your work.
translation_verse: Sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti nì tikúmɔntiil bí tikpil tikpil, baa ŋūǹ kí ŋmàntī kí béé ti-nyɔkɔm gba. An puee yīkì kí kíĺ ditundi ní ti-Dindaan ń nīn bí a-cee!»

english_verse: David then gave orders for the leaders of Israel to help Solomon.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi tīī Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ kɔkɔ mara yii bí tūtuǹ u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn.

english_verse: David said: The Lord our God has helped me defeat all the people who lived here before us, and he has given you peace from all your enemies. Now this land belongs to the Lord and his people.
translation_verse: U bí-bi yii: «Kéè ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu bí ni-ceeyaa! U tīī-ni diŋuŋfil ajan kɔkɔ pu. U dū binib bin nìn kóò kitiŋ nee puee ki ŋá m-ŋaan. Díǹ pu nee bi kíǹ ki bí ti-Dindaan nì u-nibul taapu ní.

english_verse: Obey the Lord your God with your heart and soul. Begin work on the temple to honor him, so that the sacred chest and the things used for worship can be kept there.
translation_verse: An puee ní nyàab̀maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ. Ní yīkì kí kíĺ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti circir kɔŋkooŋŋu mātam. Niinee, ni dāa ŋūǹ kí yòon̄ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau nì tiwan tin bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee kí yóoń kudii kun ni làá mā ti-Dindaan yindi puee poon.»

english_verse: David was old when he chose his son Solomon to be king of Israel.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn púĺ tikpil tikpil. U nìn dū u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn ki kāaǹ dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu.

english_verse: Some time later, David called together all of Israel's leaders, priests, and Levites.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u tú bi yíiń Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ kɔkɔ ki kpáfì u-cee, ki kpáaǹ bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab.

english_verse: Every morning and evening, the Levites are to give thanks to the Lord and sing praises to him.
translation_verse: Leefii yab máaǹ kí nīn bí kunimbɔtidiin taafaau nì joou ki gà ilan ki pàkà ti-Dindaan ki nyɔ́ŋkí-u.

english_verse: David then divided the Levites into three groups according to the clans of Levi's sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
translation_verse: U nìn yākatì Leefii yab akiti akiti ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal pu Leefii jipɔmbi Geersɔn nì Keeyaati nì Meerarii dicaŋŋinee.

english_verse: Gershon had two sons: Ladan and Shimei.
translation_verse: Geersɔn jipɔmbi Laadan nì Simeeyii dicaŋŋi di nìn náań Geersɔn kitil.

english_verse: Ladan was the father of Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel.
translation_verse: Laadan nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muta ní, ujipɔŋkpil di sá Yeeyiyeel ní bin kíǹee sá Seetam nì Jooweel.

english_verse: They were all family leaders among their father's descendants. Shimei was the father of Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran.
translation_verse: Simeeyii mun nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muta ní. Múǹ di sá Seeloomiiti nì Asiyeel nì Aran ní ki sá Laadan yab dicaŋŋi kpilib.

english_verse: Later, Shimei had four more sons, in the following order: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah. But Jeush and Beriah didn't have many children, so their descendants were counted as one family.
translation_verse: Yakaati di sá ujipɔŋkpil ní Siisa pá. Yeewusi nì Beeriya bíǹ kaa màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu tikpil. Di sá ní bi dū bi-nib ki kpáfì ki tīī-bi kudicambaantiiu tundi.

english_verse: Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Keeyaati nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu munaa. Múǹ di sá Amiiraam nì Isaar nì Eebrɔn nì Usiyeel.

english_verse: Amram was the father of Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were chosen to be in charge of all the sacred things. They served the Lord by offering sacrifices to him and by blessing the people in his name.
translation_verse: Amiiraam jipɔmbi di sá Aarɔn nì Mooyiisi. Bi nìn gāntì Aarɔn ki yóoǹ ú dū u-ba kí sú kí nīn tūǹ circir páaa laŋki tuuŋŋi kí nīn cá jaanjaan. U nì u-naantiibi tundi di sá bí nīn ŋáań talaalutuukaa saraabi ki tìì ti-Dindaan, kí nīn tūǹ Unimbɔti tundi ní kí nīn tìì binib dibiindi ti-Dindaan yindi pu.

english_verse: Gershom's oldest son was Shebuel.
translation_verse: Geersɔm jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Seebuyeel.

english_verse: Hebron, the third son of Kohath, was the father of Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
translation_verse: Eebrɔn jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Yeeriya, uliliiti di sá Amaariya, utataati di sá Yasiyeel ní unanaati sá Yeekamam.

english_verse: Merari had two sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish.
translation_verse: Meerarii jipɔmbi di sá Maalii nì Musii. Maalii jipɔmbi di sá Eelasaar nì Kiisi.

english_verse: Eleazar had no sons, only daughters, and they married their uncle's sons.
translation_verse: Eelasaar kaa màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki kpíì. U màl̄ mbinimpubiyaamu ŋma ní, ní bi-niijab Kiisi jipɔmbi fātìi cáá-bi bi kpántì bi-nimpoobi.

english_verse: Mushi the second son of Merari, was the father of Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
translation_verse: Musii nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muta ní. Múǹ di sá Maalii nì Eedeer nì Yeereemooti.

english_verse: David said: The Lord God of Israel has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Daafiidi nìn bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu tīī u-nibul diŋuŋfil. Úǹ u-ba kíǹ ki kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: And so, the Levites won't need to move the sacred tent and the things used for worship from place to place.
translation_verse: Mimmee an kaa ti cáá yii Leefii yab làá gíti túń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-poon ditundee.»

english_verse: will serve the Lord by helping Aaron's descendants do their work at the temple, by keeping the courtyards and rooms of the temple clean, and by making sure that everything used in worship stays pure.
translation_verse: Bi máaǹ kí nīn tɔ́ Aarɔn naantiibi marab ní ki nīn tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan diikun. Bíǹ di kpèé kunimbɔtidii ciŋŋi nì ku-dibiyaamu, ní ki ŋáań tiwan tin bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee circir, ní ki bí kunimbɔtidiin ki tūǹ ditundi.

english_verse: They will also be in charge of the sacred loaves of bread, the flour for the grain sacrifices, the thin wafers, any offerings to be baked, and the flour mixed with olive oil. These Levites will weigh and measure these offerings.
translation_verse: Bíǹ di làá nīn pūul̀ kpɔnɔb bin bi pāantí teebil pu Unimbɔti nimbiinee, kí nīn bɔ́ntí ŋyim min bi cáa ŋáań tijimpin saraabee, kí nīn pūul̀ ŋkpɔnɔbiyaamu mun poon baa ŋáań ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nì kalaabi bin bi pūul̀ ataŋkpee puee, nì kalaabi bin kíǹee. Bíǹ di tí kpèé tiwan tin bi cáa ŋmàntī tiwan nyifiŋŋu nì ti-púuŋŋuee.

english_verse: They must also give thanks and sing praises when sacrifices are offered on each Sabbath, as well as during New Moon Festivals and other religious feasts. There must always be enough Levites on duty at the temple to do everything that needs to be done.
translation_verse: Bi máaǹ kí nīn bí ŋyunti ŋun kamaa binib yaa dɔ́miń kí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabee, nì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa kamaa, nì uŋmal kamaa wimpeepeekaaŋu dal, nì jiŋaalib wiiŋyi kɔkɔ. Bi máaǹ kí tɔ̄ ditundi gbanti ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan, kí nīn wīikí kii mara nín bālifì puee.

english_verse: They were once in charge of taking care of the sacred tent; now they are responsible for the temple and for helping Aaron's descendants.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní bi làá nīn tūǹ Unimbɔti Tantiu nì dikpafindi tantiu tuuŋŋi. Bi làá nīn tútúǹ bi-nabiyaamu Aarɔn naantiibi bi tūǹ ditundi kunimbɔtidii poon.

english_verse: Aaron's descendants were then divided into work groups. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yākatì Aarɔn naantiibi akiti akiti. Aarɔn jipɔmbi di sá Nadaab nì Abiyuu nì Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu died long before their father, without having any sons. That's why Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
translation_verse: Nadaab nì Abiyuu nìn péeǹ bi-baa ki kpíì kaa nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu. Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar baba di nìn kpántì bisaraaŋaliibi.

english_verse: David divided Aaron's descendants into groups, according to their assigned work. Zadok, one of Eleazar's descendants, and Ahimelech, one of Ithamar's descendants, helped David.
translation_verse: Eeleeyasaar naantiiu Sadooki nì Itamaar naantiiu Ayiimeeleeki nìn tútúǹ Daafiidi u yākatì bisaraaŋaliibi kɔkɔ akiti akiti, ki nóó nì ditundi din bi tūǹee.

english_verse: groups, and Ithamar's were divided into eight groups, because Eleazar's family included more family leaders.
translation_verse: ní saalaa nì uwawati sá Peetaya, ní un pá saalaa nì uwawati sá Yeesikeel,

english_verse: However, both families included temple officials and priests, and so to make sure the work was divided fairly, David asked God what to do.
translation_verse: Bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki yākatì yākatì akiti gbanti. Di sá yii an yaa sá Eeleeyasaar naantiibi poonaaa, Itamaar naantiibi poonaaa, «circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tɔntɔnliibi» nì «Unimbɔti tɔntɔnliibi» nìn bí ní.

english_verse: As each group was assigned their duties, Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the Levite wrote down the name of the family leader in charge of that group. The witnesses were David and his officials, as well as Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the family leaders from the clans of the priests and the Levites.
translation_verse: Neetaneeyeel jipɔɔn Seemaya, un sá ugbaŋŋmal Leefii naakookunee ŋmàn̄ bi-yiŋŋi ubɔti nì abɔtibil nì usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nì Abiyataar jipɔɔn Ayiimeeleeki, nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib kɔkɔ nimbiin. Bi yaa nìn tɔ́ kasi mili pu ki lēē Eeleeyasaar maaliŋun bikpilib bilee, ní bí tɔ̄ kasi diba pu kí lēē Itamaar maaliŋun kudicaŋu kpiliu ubɔ.

english_verse: These men were assigned their duties at the temple, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded their ancestor Aaron. The Rest of the Levites Are Assigned Their Duties
translation_verse: Akiti gbanti nìn nóó bi nín pá pá tɔb pu puee ní ki tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan Diikun. Bi nìn tūǹ ditundi niin ki nóó nì bi-naanja Aarɔn nín nìn tīī marab biŋyee ní. Úǹ nìn fōō marab gbanti ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee ní. Leefii yab bin kíǹee yiŋŋi

english_verse: Here is a list of the other descendants of Levi: Amram was the ancestor of Shubael and Jehdeiah.
translation_verse: Leefii kpilib bin kíǹee yiŋŋi sèé. Un nìn sá Amiiraam naantiibi poon ukpilee di sá Suubayeel, ní un sá Suubayeel naantiibi poon ukpilee di sá Yeediya.

english_verse: Rehabiah was the ancestor of Isshiah, the oldest son in his family.
translation_verse: Un nìn sá Reekabiya naantiibi poon ukpilee di sá Isiya un sá u-dicaŋkun ujipɔŋkpilee.

english_verse: Izhar was the father of Shelomoth and the grandfather of Jahath.
translation_verse: Isaar naantiibi poonee, Seeloomiiti di nìn sá ukpil, ní Seeloomiiti naantiibi poonee, Yakaati sá ukpil.

english_verse: Hebron had four sons, in the following order: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
translation_verse: Eebrɔn jipɔmbi sèé. Upeekaa di sá Yeeriya ní uliliiti sá Amaariya, ní utataati sá Yasiyeel ní unanaati sá Yeekamam.

english_verse: Uzziel was the father of Micah and the grandfather of Shamir.
translation_verse: Usiyeel jipɔɔn di sá Miika. Miika naantiibi poonee, Samiir di nìn sá ukpil.

english_verse: Isshiah, Micah's brother, was the father of Zechariah.
translation_verse: Miika naal Isiya naantiibi poonee, Seekariyawuu di nìn sá ukpil.

english_verse: Merari was the father of Mahli, Mushi, and Jaaziah.
translation_verse: Meerarii jipɔmbi di sá Maalii nì Musii nì Yaasiyawuu.

english_verse: Jaaziah had three sons: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
translation_verse: Meerarii naantiibi bin u-jipɔɔn Yaasiyawuu màl̄ee di sá Sooyam nì Sakuur nì Ibirii.

english_verse: Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish. Eleazar had no sons, but Kish was the father of Jerahmeel.
translation_verse: Uliliiti di sá Kiisi. Úǹ nìn màl̄ kibininjabiki bi yíì-kì Yeerameel.

english_verse: Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the descendants of Levi, according to their clans.
translation_verse: Musii jipɔmbi di sá Maalii nì Eedeer nì Yeereemooti. Bininjab gbanti kɔkɔ nìn sá Leefii naakookun ní. Báà ŋma nìn sá u-dicaŋkun ukpil ní.

english_verse: Each one was assigned his duties in the same way that their relatives the priests had been assigned their duties. David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the family leaders of the priests and Levites were the witnesses.
translation_verse: Kii bi-nabiyaamu Aarɔn naantiibi nín ŋá puee, bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki lēē bi nín làá nīn tūǹ ditundi ki pá pá tɔb pu puee. Ubɔti Daafiidi nì Sadooki nì Ayiimeeleeki, nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib nimbiin ní bi nìn ŋá míǹ gbanti kɔkɔ. Mimmee bi ŋá ujipɔŋkpil dicaŋku mbaantiim kii bi nín ŋá kiwaai mun dicaŋku puee dee.

english_verse: David and the temple officials chose the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to be in charge of music. They were to praise the Lord by playing cymbals, harps and other stringed instruments. Here is a list of the musicians and their duties:
translation_verse: Akiti ŋin tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan Diikunee kpilib nìn tútúǹ Daafiidi bi gāntì Asaafi nì Eeman nì Yeedutun naantiibi bí nīn kpèé dilaŋgaal tundi. Bi nìn bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati nì saŋgub, ki cákafí cancakantib ní ki gà ilan ki nàatī binib Unimbɔti bɔti. Binib bin tūǹ ditundi gbantee yiŋŋi sèé.

english_verse: Asaph's four sons, Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, were under the direction of their father and played music whenever the king told them to.
translation_verse: Asaafi jipɔmbi di sá Sakuur nì Jooseefi nì Neetaniya nì Asaareela. Bi-baa un nìn gà ilan ki nàatī Unimbɔti bɔtee di nìn kpòotī-bi kii ubɔti nín tīī mara puee.

english_verse: His sons were under his direction and played cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments during times of worship at the temple. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman took their orders directly from the king.
translation_verse: Binib gbanti kɔkɔ nìn bí bi-baa taapu ní ki tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan diikun. Bi nìn cákafí cancakantib, ní ki bɔ̀ɔ́ saŋgub nì tibati. Bi nìn bí ubɔti tundin ní Asaafi nì Yeedutun nì Eeman kpòotī-bi.

english_verse: David assigned them their duties by asking the Lord what he wanted. Everyone was responsible for something, whether young or old, teacher or student.
translation_verse: Bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki lēē bi nín làá nīn tūǹ ditundi ki fòol̄ tɔb puee. Digàntil kaa nìn bí kiwaayaaa, ukpil kansikin, àá un bífì ki nyí dilaŋgaal tiŋanee nì un dáá bíi bífée kansikin.

english_verse: Elam, Jehohanan, and Eliehoenai.
translation_verse: Eelam nì Yeewoowanan Eeliyooweenayi.

english_verse: Obed-Edom had been blessed with eight sons: Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai.
translation_verse: nì Amiyeel nì Isakaar nì Peewuleetaayi. Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan nìn lafun bīiǹ Oobeedi-Eedoom boon.

english_verse: Shemaiah was the father of Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, Elihu, and Semachiah. They were all respected leaders in their clan.
translation_verse: Seemaya jipɔmbi di sá Ɔtinii nì Reefayeel nì Oobeedi nì Eelsabaadi, ní kí kūtì bi-nabiyaamu Eeliiwuu nì Seemakiya. Bíǹ liitil nìn sá bibaatandambi ní.

english_verse: Eighteen descendants of Meshelemiah were chosen for this work.
translation_verse: Meeseeleemiyawuu nìn cáá jipɔmbi nì nnabiyaamu, bi nìn nyáń bibaatandambi saalku nì bita ní.

english_verse: Hosah, from the Merari clan, was the father of Shimri, Hilkiah, Tebaliah, and Zechariah. Hosah had made Shimri the family leader, even though he was not the oldest son. Thirteen men from Hosah's family were chosen to be temple guards.
translation_verse: Koosa jipɔnliliitiu di sá Ilikiyawuu, ní utataati sá Teebaaliyawuu ní unanaati sá Seekariyawuu. Koosa jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu kɔkɔ nìn nyáń binib saalaa nì bita ní.

english_verse: The guards were divided into groups, according to their family leaders, and they were assigned duties at the temple, just like the other Levites.
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitiŋi nee kpilib nì bi-yab nìn tūǹ bi-tundi dicilpu ti-Dindaan Diikun ní.

english_verse: Each group, no matter how large or small, was assigned a gate to guard, and they let the Lord show them what he wanted done.
translation_verse: Binipɔmbaaa, binicikitikaabaaa, bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki yākatì mpunyɔmu mun bi làá nīn cīitée ki nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋi.

english_verse: Shelemiah was chosen to guard the East Gate. Zechariah his son was a wise man and was chosen to guard the North Gate.
translation_verse: Bi nín tɔ́ kasee, an nyáń yii Seeleemiyawuu di làá nīn cīití kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. Bi gíti tɔ́ee ní an nyáń yii u-jipɔɔn Seekariyawuu un sá usaŋkimɔntee di làá nīn cīití kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgan púee.

english_verse: Obed-Edom was then chosen to guard the South Gate, and his sons were chosen to guard the storerooms.
translation_verse: Oobeedi-Eedoom di làá nīn cīití kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgiil púee, ní u-jipɔmbi ń nīn cīití adiin ŋin poon bi yōontí tijikaalee.

english_verse: Shuppim and Hosah were chosen to guard the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road. The guards were assigned the following work schedule:
translation_verse: Supiim nì Koosa di làá nīn cīití kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee nì Saleekeeti punyɔkɔki kin bí yilpu dandi púee. Bi nín làá nīn cīití ki fòol̄ tɔb puee sèé.

english_verse: Each day six guards were on duty on the east side of the temple, four were on duty on the north side, and four were on duty on the south side. Two guards were stationed at each of the two storerooms,
translation_verse: Ŋwiinee, Leefii yab binib biluu di làá nīn cīití ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔki, ní binib binaa ń nīn cīití ŋgan pú yaka, ní binib binaa ń nīn cīití ŋgiil pú punyɔkɔki, ní akiti ali ń nīn cīití adiin ŋin poon bi yōontí tijikaalee, dikitil kamaa cáá binib bili bili.

english_verse: four were stationed along the road leading to the west courtyard, and two guards stayed in the court itself.
translation_verse: Kudii kun bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, binib binaa làá nīn yú didandi pu ki cí ní bili ń nīn bí kudiin.

english_verse: These were the guard duties assigned to the men from the clans of Korah and Merari. Guards Are Assigned to the Treasury
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitiŋi ŋin bi nìn lēē Kooree nì Meerarii maalii poonee dee. Bi dū atuun aba ki ŋúbiǹ Leefii yab biba

english_verse: The Levites who were relatives of the Korahites and the Merarites were in charge of guarding the temple treasury and the gifts that had been dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Leefii yab biba mun nìn sá bin kpèé kunimbɔtidii gaajawanti nì tiwan tin bi cáań ki ŋá Unimbɔti saraayee.

english_verse: Ladan was from the Gershon clan and was the father of Jehieli. Many of his other descendants were family leaders in the clan.
translation_verse: Laadan naantiibi bin sá Geersɔn maaliŋunee nì bi-dicaŋŋi kpilib di sá Yeeyeelii,

english_verse: Jehieli was the father of Zetham and Joel, and they were responsible for guarding the treasury.
translation_verse: nì Yeeyeelii jipɔmbi nì Seetam nì u-naal Jooweel. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé ti-Dindaan Diiku gaajawanti.

english_verse: Other guards at the treasury were from the Kohathite clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
translation_verse: Amiiraam nì Isaar nì Eebrɔn nì Usiyeel maaliŋunee,

english_verse: Shebuel was a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses. He was the chief official in charge of the temple treasury.
translation_verse: Mooyiisi jipɔɔn, Geersɔm naantiiu Seebuyeel di sá ukpikpaan un kpèé tigaajawan kɔkɔee.

english_verse: The descendants of Gershom's brother Eliezer included Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomoth.
translation_verse: U-nabiyaamu kansikinee, Geersɔm maan Eeliyeeseer naantiibi nìn bí. Bíǹ di sá Eeliyeeseer jipɔɔn Reekabiya nì Yeesaya nì Yooram nì Sikirii nì Seeloomiiti.

english_verse: Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the gifts that were dedicated to the Lord. These included the gifts that King David had dedicated, as well as those dedicated by the family leaders, army officers, and army commanders.
translation_verse: Seeloomiiti gbanti nì u-nabiyaamu di nìn kpèé tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ ubɔti Daafiidi nì adican kpilib nì bijanjakpilib bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutuku kutukuee nì bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee nì bijanjakpilib bin kíǹee nìn dūu sú Unimbɔtee.

english_verse: And whenever valuable things were captured in battle, these men brought back some of them to make repairs to the temple.
translation_verse: Binib gbanti nìn lēē tiwan tin bi jáń kujaau ki fōōyee tiba ki dūu sú Unimbɔti bí nīn cáa ŋáŋkí ti-Dindaan Diiku.

english_verse: Shelomoth and his relatives were responsible for any gifts that had been given to the temple, including those from Samuel the prophet, King Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah. Other Officers Are Assigned Their Duties
translation_verse: Seeloomiiti nì u-nabiyaamu ní bi nìn dū tiwan tin kɔkɔ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Samiyeel, nì Kiisi jipɔɔn Saayuul, nì Neer jipɔɔn Abineer, nì Joowaab un na bi yíì Seeruyee nìn dūu sú Unimbɔtee ki ŋúbíǹ bí nīn kpèé.

english_verse: Chenaniah from the Izhar clan and his sons were government officials and judges. They did not work at the temple.
translation_verse: Keenaniyawuu nì u-jipɔmbi bin sá Isaar maaliŋunee di nìn kpèé Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn tin kaa sá tinimbɔtibɔtee bɔti. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé akàlintuun bɔti, ní ki sá bibɔsoonliibi mun.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah had begun to count the people, but he stopped when the Lord began punishing Israel. So the total number was never included in David's official records. Officials in Charge of the King's Property
translation_verse: Seeruya jipɔɔn Joowaab nìn kíĺ ki bíi kàaǹ Isirayeel yab, ama waa nìn púntì. Unimbɔti nìn gíí Isirayeel yab pu diŋuul dikàandi gbanti pu. An pu ní Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ nyɔkɔm kaa ŋmàn̄ ki kā Daafiidi Tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. Binib bin kpèé ubɔti gaajawantee

english_verse: who was the leader of the Thirty Warriors, and whose son Ammizabad was also an army commander;
translation_verse: Beenayawuu gbanti nìn kútì Bibaatandambi Mmuŋku nì Saalaa kitil pu ní ki nìn sá di-kpiliu. U-janjakitil poonee u-jipɔɔn Amiisafaadi nìn bí.

english_verse: in the fourth month, Asahel the brother of Joab, whose son Zebadiah took over command after him;
translation_verse: Dijanjakitil dinanaatiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmananaati poonee kpilib di nìn sá Joowaab naal Asayeel nì u-jipɔɔn Seefadiya. Bi-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní.

english_verse: years of age, because the Lord had promised long ago that Israel would have as many people as there are stars in the sky.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim naakookunee, Asasiyawuu jipɔɔn Ooseeya di sá ukpil. Manasee naakooku dijandi din bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, Peedaya jipɔɔn Jooweel di sá ukpil.

english_verse: Azmaveth the son of Adiel was in charge of the king's personal storage rooms. Jonathan the son of Uzziah was in charge of the king's other storerooms that were in the towns, the villages, and the defense towers in Israel.
translation_verse: Adiyeel jipɔɔn Asimafeeti di nìn sá un kpèé ubɔti gaajawantee. Oosiyasi jipɔɔn Yoowanan di nìn kpèé tikpaajin tin bi kpáafì ntiŋkpaamun nì ntimbilimun nì laakin sintil difɔkɔŋi bée.

english_verse: Ezri the son of Chelub was in charge of the workers who farmed the king's land.
translation_verse: Keeluub jipɔɔn Eesirii di nìn sá bikpaabi kpiliu Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn.

english_verse: Shimei from Ramah was in charge of the vineyards, and Zabdi from Shepham was in charge of storing the wine.
translation_verse: Simeeyii un sá Raama tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé fiinyi sufii kpaaŋŋi kɔkɔ. Sabidii un sá Seefam tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé ndamam min nyánní akpaan gbantin bi cāabìń ki kpáafée.

english_verse: Baal Hanan from Geder was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the western foothills, and Joash was in charge of storing the olive oil.
translation_verse: Baal-Anan un sá Beeti-Geedeer tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé ɔliifi sufii nì siikoomɔɔr sufii kpaaŋŋi ŋin bí Seefeelaayee. Yoowasi di nìn kpèé ŋkpam min bi cāabìń ki kpáafée.

english_verse: Shitrai from Sharon was responsible for the cattle that were kept in Sharon Plain, and Shaphat son of Adlai was responsible for those kept in the valleys.
translation_verse: Siitirayi un sá Saarɔn tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé tinacaŋkpun tin bi kpàá Saarɔn naakpaapɔɔkunee. Adilayi jipɔɔn Safaati di nìn kpèé tinacaŋkpun tin bi kpàá ditantakalinee.

english_verse: Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels, Jehdeiah from Meronoth was in charge of the donkeys, and Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Ɔbiil un sá Isimaayeel maaliŋunee di nìn kpèé igutaamu. Yeediya un sá Meerɔnɔti tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé mmansalimu.

english_verse: These were the men in charge of David's royal property. David's Personal Advisors
translation_verse: Yasiisi un sá Agaar maaliŋunee di nìn kpèé ipii nì iŋoobu. Binib bin nìn kpèé ubɔti Daafiidi gaajawantee dee. Binib bin pìlīǹ ubɔti Daafiidee

english_verse: David's uncle Jonathan was a wise and intelligent advisor. He and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni taught David's sons.
translation_verse: Daafiidi wee Joonatan nìn sá unyil ki ŋá sukul. Úǹ di nìn sá ubɔti saŋkiliu. Yeeyeel un baa nìn sá Akimoonii tiŋkee di nìn kpèé ubɔti jipɔmbi.

english_verse: Jehoiada the son of Benaiah was the king's advisor after Ahithophel, and later, Abiathar was his advisor. Joab was commander of Israel's army.
translation_verse: Ayiitoofeel kúm boonee, Beenayawuu jipɔɔn Yooyadaa nì Abiyataar di nìn fōō u-yil. Joowaab di nìn sá ubɔti janjakitil kpiliu.

english_verse: David called a meeting in Jerusalem for all of Israel's leaders, including the tribal leaders, the government officials, the army commanders, the officials in charge of the royal property and livestock, the palace officials, and the brave warriors.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn yíiń Isirayeel yab kpilib kɔkɔ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. U nìn yíiń tinaakɔti kpilib nì ajanjakiti kpilib bin bí u-tundinee, nì bijanjakpilib bin sá bijanjaliibi kutuku kutuku nì dilaataal dilaataal kpilibee. U nìn gíti kpáfì bikàlimbi bin kpèé ubɔti nì u-jipɔmbi gaajawanti nì bi-waŋkutee, nì bifaabi nì bibaatandambi nì binikpaambi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: After everyone was there, David stood up and said: Listen to me, my people. I wanted to build a place where the sacred chest would be kept, so we could go there and worship the Lord our God. I have prepared all the supplies for building a temple,
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn yíkì ní ki bí-bi yii: «M-nibul yab, m-nabiyaamu, pīlifìmaan-mi! M nìn ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá mā kudii kun poon ní ti-Dindaan poondi dakaau làá nīn yúee, laakin ti-Nimbɔtiu taaŋi làá nīn yūlifée. An puee m bɔ́ntì kí mā kudii gbanti.

english_verse: but the Lord has refused to let me build it, because he said I have killed too many people in battle.
translation_verse: Ama ní Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: <Sii di kaa làá mā-mi kudii kun poon binib làá nīn dòoń ki jáaḿ-mee. Di sá yii a jáń tijáti tikpil ki yāntì binib tikpil fatikuu nyáń.>

english_verse: The Lord God chose Judah to be the leading tribe in Israel. Then from Judah, he chose my father's family, and from that family, he chose me to be the king of Israel, and he promised that my descendants will also rule as kings.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee man ní ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu lēē m-baa dicaŋku kɔkɔ poon. U lēē man nì m-jipɔmbi nì m-naantiibi tí jī dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Dooooyee m-naanja Juuda ní u nìn lēē ú nīn sá uyidaan. Míǹ boonee, Juuda naakookunee ní u lēē m-baa dicaŋku. An dāa kúntèe, man ní u lēē m-baa jipɔmbi kansikin ḿ nīn sá Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ pu ubɔti.

english_verse: The Lord has blessed me with many sons, but he chose my son Solomon to be the next king of Israel.
translation_verse: Mbininjabiyaamu kupaau mun ti-Dindaan tīī-mee kansikinee, Saloomɔn ní u lēē yii ú kàl̄ úǹ ti-Dindaan beel Isirayeel pu tibɔtiil.

english_verse: The Lord said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my temple, and it will honor me. Solomon will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tùkū-mi yii: <A-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn di làá mā m-Diiku nì ku-ciŋŋi. Tiŋman úǹ ní m lēē. U làá nīn sá-mi ujipɔnti ní man ń nīn sá-u ubaati.

english_verse: If he continues to obey my laws and commands, his kingdom will never end.”
translation_verse: U yaa gbíntìi nìkì ki tɔ́ m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi kii díǹ neeyee, m làá yàntī u-beel ń báań inyaan kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.>

english_verse: My friends, you are the Lord's people. And now, with God as your witness, I want you to promise that you will do your best to obey everything the Lord God has commanded us. Then this land will always belong to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee m-nabiyaamu, ti-Dindaan nibul Isirayeel kɔkɔ nimbiinee, nì ti-Nimbɔtiu un gbìl̀ tin ti bíi sòoǹee nimbiinee, ní lēē kí bīfì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu marab kɔkɔ kí nīn tɔ́-bi. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni làá nīn pée gbíntìi yì kitimmɔntii kin pu ni kā nee, ní kí dāá dū-kì kí tīī ni-naantiibi án nīn sá bi-tindaŋwanti kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Solomon, my son, worship God and obey him with all your heart and mind, just as I have done. He knows all your thoughts and your reasons for doing things, and so if you turn to him, he will hear your prayers. But if you ignore him, he will reject you forever.
translation_verse: Sii m-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn, nyàab̀ kí béé man a-baa Nimbɔtiu un m jáaḿee tiŋan, kí nīn jáaḿ-u nì dipɔbil diba nì a-naŋki kɔkɔ. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan kpèé ki wāĺ tin bí binib pɔbiliŋ poon poon kábuee ní ki nyí bi nín dàkafī puee kɔkɔ. A yaa nyàab̀-u, u làá yàntī á ká-u. Ama a yaa dū-u ki fá, u mun làá dū-si kí fá ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: The Lord has chosen you to build a temple for worshiping him. Be confident and do the work you have been assigned.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee sii a-ba wāĺ, sii ní ti-Dindaan lēē yii á mā-u kudii kun làá nīn sá u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋuee. An puee, ká dipɔbil kí kíĺ ditundi gbanti!» Daafiidi tùkū Saloomɔn kunimbɔtidii nín làá nīn bí puee

english_verse: After David finished speaking, he gave Solomon the plans for building the main rooms of the temple, including the porch, the storerooms, the rooms upstairs and downstairs, as well as the most holy place.
translation_verse: Daafiidi nìn tīī u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn kugbɔŋu kun poon bi lēē kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋku nì ku-dibiyaamu, nì adiin ŋin poon bi kpáafí tiwanee nì aditɔntɔkɔ nì poon pú diiŋŋi nì circir dakaau diiku.

english_verse: He gave Solomon his plans for the courtyards and the open areas around the temple, and for the rooms to store the temple treasures and gifts that had been dedicated to God.
translation_verse: Daafiidi gíti tīī Saloomɔn kugbɔŋu kun poon ní bi lēē tin kɔkɔ u dākafì kí mā kí kūtèe, an dàkà yii kunimbɔtidii ciŋŋi nì adiin ŋin māntìi tú-ŋee, nì adiin ŋin poon bi làá nīn kpáafí kunimbɔtidii gaajawanti nì tiwan tin bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee.

english_verse: David also gave Solomon his plans for dividing the priests and the Levites into groups, as well as for the work that needed to be done at the temple and for taking care of the objects used for worship.
translation_verse: U nìn dū bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab kitiŋi yiŋŋi gbɔŋku ki tīī-u, ki kpáaǹ bi nín máaǹ kí nīn tūǹ atuun ŋin ti-Dindaan Diikunee. U nìn gíti dū kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmàn̄ tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi làá nīn cáa tūǹ kunimbɔtidiin tuuŋŋee ki ŋée ki tīī-u.

english_verse: the gold table which held the sacred loaves of bread, the tables made of silver,
translation_verse: U nìn dàkā-u sindaariya teebilib bin pu bi làá nīn pāantí kpɔnɔb bin bi dūu ŋá Unimbɔti saraayee nyiŋfiŋu, ki dàkā-u animbil kúti teebilib nyiŋfiŋu,

english_verse: the gold incense altar, and the gold statue of a chariot for the winged creatures which were on the lid of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: U nìn dàkā-u sindaariyamɔnti saraafaŋŋu ŋun pu bi làá nīn tùutī talaalubee nyiŋfiŋu. Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi dàkā-u min bi máaǹ kí mɔ́ɔ́ circir janjatɔrɔkuuee, nì keerubimbi bin bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ bi kpátì bi-feeŋyi ki bīiǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau puee nyiŋfiŋu.

english_verse: But you must see that everything is done according to these plans. Be confident, and never be afraid of anything or get discouraged. The Lord my God will help you do everything needed to finish the temple, so it can be used for worshiping him.
translation_verse: U lī mimmee ní ki kútì yii: «M-jipɔɔn, pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil. Kíĺ atuun gbanti kí taa fàŋkì báà tiba, ní a-wunti ń taa yɔ̀tī mun! Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu làá nīn bí a-cee. Waa làá dū-si kí fá, ní ki kpá kí fàtī u-boon kí tīī-si kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun a làá tɔ̄ úǹ Unimbɔti diiku mātam tuuŋŋi kí dóóyee.

english_verse: The priests and Levites have been assigned their duties, and all the skilled workers are prepared to do their work. The people and their leaders will do anything you tell them.
translation_verse: Kpèè, bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab yākatì akiti akiti ki cí kí tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidiin tuuŋŋi. Kí kūtèe, binib bin cáá nlammɔntiimee nì bin cáá kí tɔ̄ atuun kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifee, nì Isirayeel kpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ bí a-cee kí ŋá a nín là puee.»

english_verse: and to make the gold and silver objects. Now, who else will show their dedication to the Lord by giving gifts for building his temple?
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee ni-kansikin ŋma di kíí nì dipɔbil diba kí tīī ti-Dindaan sindaariya nì animbil kúti? Mimmee bitɔntɔnliibi làá dāá dūú mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan tin kɔkɔ máaǹ bí dū sindaariya nì animbil kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́yee.»

english_verse: After David finished speaking, the family leaders, the tribal leaders, the army commanders, and the government officials voluntarily gave gifts
translation_verse: Niinee ní adican kpilib, nì Isirayeel naakɔti kpilib, nì bijanjakpilib bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutuku kutukuee, nì bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee nì anikiti ŋin tūǹ ubɔti tuuŋŋee kpilib kɔkɔ kíí ki tīī tiwan nì dipɔbil diba.

english_verse: Everyone who owned precious stones also donated them to the temple treasury, where Jehiel from the Levite clan of Gershon guarded them.
translation_verse: Binib bin kɔkɔ nìn cáá ataŋkpamɔntee nìn dū-ŋi ki tīī Yeeyeel un sá Geersɔn maaliŋunee ú dūú ŋá Unimbɔti diiku gaajawanti poon.

english_verse: David and the people were very happy that so much had been given to the Lord, and they all celebrated. David Praises the Lord
translation_verse: Binib gbanti nìn dū bi-gaajawanti ki tīī ti-Dindaan nì dipɔbil diba ní ki nìn bí mmɔnni. An nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ubɔti Daafiidi mun tikpil. Daafiidi wimmeem

english_verse: Then, in front of everyone, David sang praises to the Lord: I praise you forever, Lord! You are the God our ancestor Jacob worshiped.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daafiidi jáam̀ ti-Dindaan samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin ki lī yii: «Bí nyɔ̄ŋkì sii ti-Dindaan, ti-naanja Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Your power is great, and your glory is seen everywhere in heaven and on earth. You are king of the entire world,
translation_verse: Sii ti-Dindaan di sá ukpaan ki yì mpɔn nì tinyool nì jilma nì dibeel! Tiŋman, sii ti-Dindaan di yì tin kɔkɔ bí yilpu nì taapuee. Sii di sá ubɔti, sii un tɔ́kɔ́ tin kɔkɔ cáá kufoouee puee.

english_verse: We thank you, our God, and praise you.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti jáaḿ sii ti-Nimbɔtiu, ní ki nyɔ́ŋkí a-yinnyaandi.

english_verse: But why should we be happy that we have given you these gifts? They belong to you, and we have only given back what is already yours.
translation_verse: Maa sá tibaaa, m-nibul yab mun kaa sá tiba. An kaa sá timbi ti-ba di cáá mpɔn kí tīī-si tiwan tin ti bíi tìì-si nee. Sii di tīī-ti an wanti kɔkɔ. Tin a tīī-tee ní timbi fàtīi gīintí ki tìì-si nee.

english_verse: We are only foreigners living here on earth for a while, just as our ancestors were. And we will soon be gone, like a shadow that suddenly disappears.
translation_verse: Timbi sá binicambi nì binikɔkaabi ní a-nimbiin, kii ti-naanjab kɔkɔ nín nìn bí puee. Ti-maŋfal wiiŋyi kitiŋ nee pu sá kii mboon nín jītí puee ní, dimákal kpá.

english_verse: Our Lord God, we have brought all these things for building a temple to honor you. They belong to you, and you gave them to us.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, ti kóoǹ tiwan tikpil ki kpúkuǹ kí dūú mā kudii kí tīī a-circir yindi tinyool. Too, tikɔkɔ nyánní a-cee ní ki sá a-wanti.

english_verse: But we are happy, because everyone has voluntarily given you these things. You know what is in everyone's heart, and you are pleased when people are honest.
translation_verse: M-Nimbɔtiu, m nyí yii a kóò unil pɔbilin kí nyɔ̀kɔfì kí kpèè, ní ki néeń tin bí deedeeyee. Mamee nì dipɔbil diba ní m dū m-gaajawanti ki ŋá-si nlammɔntiim saraau. Ní m gíti ká díǹ mun nì dipɔɔpindi yii a-nibul din kóoǹ ki kpáfì doo nee mun ŋá míǹ mbaantiim.

english_verse: Always make us eager to give, and help us be faithful to you, just as our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob faithfully worshiped you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, ti-naanjab Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu, yàntī a-nibul ń nīn cáá dipɔɔmɔntiil gbanti, ní bi-landɔkɔŋu kɔkɔ ń nīn pée bí sii baba pu kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: And give Solomon the desire to completely obey your laws and teachings, and the desire to build the temple for which I have provided these gifts.
translation_verse: Tīī m-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn tibulcin pɔbil ú nīn nóó a-marab nì a-dàkatam nì a-bɔkpaaŋi, kí nīn tɔ́-ŋi. Ú mā a-Circir Diiku kun pu m bɔ́ntì tikɔkɔ ki yóoǹee.»

english_verse: David then said to the people, “Now it's your turn to praise the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped!” So everyone praised the Lord, and they bowed down to honor him and David their king. Solomon Is Crowned King
translation_verse: Boonee ní Daafiidi bí samaa yii: «Ní jāam̀maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu!» Ní samaa kɔkɔ jáam̀ ti-Dindaan, bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu. Bi nìn tātìi gbāaǹ bi-yigbeeŋi tūū kitiŋ Unimbɔti nì ubɔti nimbiin. Bi nín kāaǹ Saloomɔn dibeel puee nì Daafiidi kúm bɔti

english_verse: The people were very happy, and they ate and drank there at the Lord's altar. That same day, Solomon was again crowned king. The people celebrated and poured olive oil on Solomon's head to show that he would be their next king. They also poured oil on Zadok's head to show that he was their priest.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, Isirayeel yab nìn jíń ki nyùn̄ ti-Dindaan nimbiin nì dipɔɔpindi nì ifaal. Ŋwiin gbanti ní bi kāaǹ Daafiidi jipɔɔn Saloomɔn ubɔti nliliitiim. Bi nìn bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki kāaǹ-u tibɔtiil ú nīn bí ti-Dindaan tundin. Bi nìn bātì ŋkpam ki sītì Saadooki mun yil pu ú kpántí usaraaŋakpil.

english_verse: So Solomon became king after David his father. Solomon was successful, and everyone in Israel obeyed him.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn kāl̀ ti-Dindaan beejal pu ki fōō u-baa Daafiidi yil ki kpántì ubɔti. An nìn bútì-u tikpil ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn tɔ́-u tiŋan pu.

english_verse: Every official and every soldier, as well as all of David's other sons, were loyal to him.
translation_verse: Bijanjakpilib kɔkɔ nì bibaatandambi kɔkɔ, ki kpáaǹ Daafiidi jipɔmbi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ nìn sīntì bi-ba taapu ki tīī Saloomɔn ki tɔ́-u.

english_verse: The Lord made Solomon a great king, and the whole nation was amazed at how famous he was. In fact, no other king of Israel was as great as Solomon. David Dies
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Saloomɔn yindi yíkì yilpu tikpil Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin. U nìn yāntì Saloomɔn ká jilma tiŋan tiŋan pu, ní u-nyooti nìn jítiǹ Isirayeel bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ līntiǹ-uee.

english_verse: David the son of Jesse was king of Israel
translation_verse: Isayi jipɔɔn Daafiidi nìn jíń dibeel Isirayeel kɔkɔ pu ní.

english_verse: David was rich and respected and lived to be an old man. Then he died, and his son Solomon became king.
translation_verse: U nìn púĺ tiŋan ní ki nín kpíì. U nìn cáá tigaajati tikpil, ki nìn nyáń diyindi mun. U nín kpíìyee, u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Everything David did while he was king is included in the history written by the prophets Samuel, Nathan, and Gad.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daafiidi tuuŋŋi, kí yòon̄ ŋi nín kíĺ puee kí tin sāā ŋi nín kúntì puee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Samiyeel tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun, nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Gaadi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: They wrote about his powerful rule and about the things that happened not only to him, but also to Israel and the other nations.
translation_verse: Tigbɔn gbantin ní bi ŋmàn̄ tin jítì Daafiidi pu ŋyunti ŋun u sá ubɔtee nì u nín dàkā dibaatandi puee nì agìń ŋin u kée nì tin jítì Isirayeel tiŋki puee nì tin jítì abee ŋin kíǹee puee.

english_verse: and there at the bronze altar, Solomon offered a thousand animals as sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn jɔ́m̀ tasa saraafaŋŋu ŋun nìn bí ti-Dindaan nimbiin, dikpafindi tantiu nyɔkɔpuee ki ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi. U nìn kūū tiwaŋkuti kutuku ní ki dū ti-kɔkɔ ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Solomon answered: Lord God, you were always loyal to my father David, and now you have made me king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ní Saloomɔn kíí Unimbɔti yii: «Ti-Dindaan, a dàkā m-baa Daafiidi kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu tikpil, ki yāntì kɔŋkɔnnee m kpántì ubɔti ki fōō u-yil.

english_verse: God replied: Solomon, you could have asked me to make you rich or famous or to let you live a long time. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom and knowledge to rule my people.
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti kíí Saloomɔn yii: «Aa bālifì tigaajati àá tigaajawan àá tinyool àá a-nannanliibi kúm, ní kaa bālifì mun yii ḿ tīī-si mmaŋfafɔkɔn. Ama a bālifì kí nīn cáá iciin nì dinyil kí ŋmā kí dūú kpòotī m-nibul din pu m kāaǹ-si dibeelee. A nín bālifì mimmee puee,

english_verse: Solomon decided to build a temple where the Lord would be worshiped, and also to build a palace for himself.
translation_verse: U nìn fōō binib kutukub imuŋku ita nì saalaa bí nīn tūntí tiwan nì binib kutukub imuŋku inaa bí nīn bí dijool pu ki kpítí ataŋkpee, ní ki fōō binib kutukub bita nì alaataa aluu bí nīn kpèé bitɔntɔnliibi.

english_verse: No one can ever build a temple large enough for God—even the heavens are too small a place for him to live in! All I can do is build a place where we can offer sacrifices to him.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, á tīiń-mi unil un ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ sindaariya nì animbil nì tasa nì tikúti tundi tiŋanee. Udaan máaǹ kí nīn nyí bi nín bɔ́ntí satab bí nīn cáá nnyim min máǹee nì nnyim min máǹ cínciŋee nì nnyim min máǹ gùŋgumee, ní kí nīn gíti nyí tikpiŋkpiil bɔti. Udaan làá kūtì man m-ba tɔntɔnliibi bin m-baa Daafiidi nìn lēē bi bí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin nì Juuda timmunee pu kí tɔ̄ ditundi.

english_verse: Send me a worker who can not only carve, but who can work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, as well as make brightly colored cloth. The person you send will work here in Judah and Jerusalem with the skilled workers that my father has already hired.
translation_verse: Á tīiń-mi seedir nì siipreesi nì santaal dɔi in bí Leebanɔn jooŋŋi puee, di sá yii m nyí a-tɔntɔnliibi di ŋūǹ ki gà Leebanɔn sufii tiŋanee. M-tɔntɔnliibi làá dāá kūtì bi-pu.

english_verse: I know that you have workers who are experts at cutting lumber in Lebanon. So would you please send me some cedar, pine, and juniper logs? My workers will be there to help them,
translation_verse: Bi làá bɔ́ntí-mi idɔ an nīn náaǹ, di sá yii Unimbɔti diiku kun m làá mēe làá nīn sá kukpaaŋŋu ní kí nīn ŋān̄.

english_verse: Hiram sent his answer back to Solomon: I know that the Lord must love his people, because he has chosen you to be their king.
translation_verse: Ní Yiiram gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Tí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un di náań kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋee. Tiŋman u tīī ubɔti Daafiidi kibininjabiki kin cáá iciin nì dinyil nì nlandɔkɔee. U làá mā kudii kí tīī ti-Dindaan ní kí mā úǹ u-ba diiku.

english_verse: Go ahead and send the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine you promised to pay my workers.
translation_verse: Ti làá cùú gāań isufi Leebanɔn kii a nín pée là puee, ní kí bóob́ kí dūú tɔ̄ń tiŋkun kí cáań-si Jafaa tiŋkin. Niinee ní á dāá yòon̄-i kí cùnnì Jeerusaleem.»

english_verse: I will tell them to start cutting down trees in Lebanon. They will cut as many as you need, then tie them together into rafts, and float them down along the coast to Joppa. Your workers can take them to Jerusalem from there. Solomon's Work Force
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn kàan̄ binicambi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Isirayeel tiŋki puee, kii u-baa Daafiidi nín nìn kàan̄-bi pu ŋyunti ŋun u nìn sá ubɔtee. Bi nìn nyáń binib kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì bita nì binib alaataa aluu.

translation_verse: U nìn lēē bi-kansikin binib kutukub imuŋku ita nì saalaa bí nīn tūntí tiwan, ní ki lēē binib kutukub imuŋku inaa bí nīn kpítí ataŋkpee dijool pu, ní ki lēē binib kutukub bita nì alaataa aluu bí nīn kpèé bitɔntɔnliibi gbanti ditundi ń còom̀.

english_verse: He used precious stones to decorate the temple, and he used gold imported from Parvaim
translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti dū ataŋkpamɔnti ní ki nyɔ̄kɔntì kudii gbanti. Sindaariya un bi nìn dūu túń ku-pu ditundee nìn nyánní Paarwayiim tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: Five hundred and seventy grams of gold was used to cover the heads of the nails. The walls of the small storage rooms were also covered with gold.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ ipiin ní i-nyiŋfiŋu nìn sá graambi alaataa aŋmoo. Ki kpáaǹ adiin ŋin nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee, bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki nyūntì ki bīiǹ ŋi-guŋŋi pu.

english_verse: Solomon had the inside walls of the temple's main room paneled first with pine and then with a layer of gold, and he had them decorated with carvings of palm trees and designs that looked like chains.
translation_verse: U nìn dū siipreesi dɔi in bi látì apampan ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntèe ki nákáǹ kudikpaaŋŋuee poon. Bi nìn lēē ibafi nì ikusaka ki nákáǹ adɔpampanee pu.

translation_verse: Bi nìn dūntì tikúti ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ keerubimbi bili. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-bi, ní ki dū-bi ki síiǹ circir páaa diikun.

translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti ŋá tinyɔkɔntikaal ikusaka yam ki dūu sākaǹ jaantalkubee yilpu. Bi nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ greenaadi biliŋ ki sākaǹ ikusakee pu.

english_verse: Solomon had one of the columns placed on the south side of the temple's entrance; it was called Jachin. The other one was placed on the north side of the entrance; it was called Boaz.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū jaantalkubee ki cóoǹ kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu, ubɔ bí ŋgan pú ní un kíǹee bí ŋgiil pú. Bi nìn yíì un bí ŋgiil púee yii Yakiin, taapu sá yii: <Unimbɔti di tìì mpɔn>, ní ki yíì un bí ŋgan púee yii Boowaasi, taapu sá yii: <Unimbɔtin ní mpɔn bí>.

english_verse: Ten gold lampstands were also made according to the plans. Solomon placed these lampstands inside the temple, five on each side of the main room.
translation_verse: Uram nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati saalaa ki nóó nì bi nín síiǹ mara bí mɔ́ɔ́-bi puee. U nìn dū-bi ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin, biŋmoo bí ŋŋaŋgiil pú ní biŋmoo bí ŋŋaŋgan pú.

english_verse: He also made ten small bowls and put five on each side of the large bowl. The small bowls were used to wash the animals that were burned on the altar as sacrifices, and the priests used the water in the large bowl to wash their hands.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ nsampeemu saalaa ní ki dū muŋmoo ki síiǹ kusɔŋuee gaŋŋu pú ní ki dū muŋmoo mun kíǹee ki síiǹ ŋgiil pú. Nnyim min nìn kā nsampeemu gbanti poonee ní bi nìn cáa fíntí ki ŋáań tiwan circir.
