english_verse: He also made ten tables and placed them in the main room, five on each side. And he made
translation_verse: U nìn kpáá teebilib saalaa ki dūu síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin, biŋmoo ŋŋaŋgiil pú ní biŋmoo mun ŋŋaŋgan pú. U nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsambiyaamu dilaataal ki ŋáań mu-poon fatiku kí nīn cáa yàantí.

english_verse: Solomon gave orders to build two courtyards: a smaller one that only priests could use and a larger one. The doors to these courtyards were covered with bronze.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá kiciŋwaai ki tīī bisaraaŋaliibi ní ki ŋá diciŋkpaandi. Diciŋkpaandi gbanti nìn cáá mpunyɔmu ní u dū tasa ki nyūntì-mu.

english_verse: The large bowl called the Sea was placed near the southeast corner of the temple.
translation_verse: U nìn dū kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundee ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidii ŋŋaŋgiil pú, ki nákáǹ ŋgan pú nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki faŋfakam.

english_verse: Huram made shovels, sprinkling bowls, and pans for hot ashes. Here is a list of the other furnishings he made for God's temple:
translation_verse: Uram nìn ŋá asambil nì peelab nì nsambiyaamu mun poon bi ŋáań tiwan ki cáa yàantée. U nìn túń ditundi din ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn tīī-u ú tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidiinee ki dóò, an dàkà yii:

english_verse: two columns, two bowl-shaped caps for the tops of these columns, two chain designs on the caps,
translation_verse: jaantalkub bili, nì akɔl akuŋkun ŋin bi làá dūú páań jaantalkubee yilpuee, nì tilaandi tili tin bi làá dūú bìin̄ akɔl ŋin pá jaantalkubee puee,

english_verse: the stands and the small bowls,
translation_verse: nì tɔrɔkub nì tisɔn tin tɔ́kɔ́ tɔrɔkub gbanti puee,

english_verse: the large bowl and the twelve bulls that held it up,
translation_verse: nì kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundee, nì inajaa saalaa nì ili in tú kusɔŋu gbantee,

english_verse: by pouring melted bronze into the clay molds he had set up near the Jordan River, between Succoth and Zeredah.
translation_verse: Jɔɔdan tantakalin, Sukooti nì Saartan timbilimmu kansikin ní ubɔti nìn yāntì bi dūntì tasa, kuyɔkɔu paamun ki mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: There were so many bronze furnishings that no one ever knew how much bronze it took to make them.
translation_verse: Tiwan tin Saloomɔn nìn ŋée nìn wīikí tikpil, an puee baa nìn gíti nyàab̀ kí béé tasa kúti tin bi dūu ŋá an tuuŋŋi gbanti kɔkɔee nyiŋfiŋu.

english_verse: Solomon also gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar, the tables that held the sacred loaves of bread,
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn gíti yāntì bi dū sindaariya ki ŋá ti-Dindaan Diiku wanti tin an bàlifēe. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalubee, ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ teebil un pu bi pāantí kpɔnɔb kí dūú sú Unimbɔtee,

english_verse: the lampstands and the lamps that burned in front of the most holy place,
translation_verse: ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì bi-fitilab ki síiǹ Circir páaa laŋki nyɔkɔpuee bí nīn tùutī-bi ki nóó nì bi nín síiǹ puee,

english_verse: lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, ladles, fire pans, and the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
translation_verse: ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ bɔlfitantab nì asambil ŋin poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki yàantée nì kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi nì nfantansamu. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ kunimbɔtidii punyɔmmu nì mpunyɔmu mun bi dì kí kɔ́ Circir páaa laŋkee nì kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋku.

english_verse: The priests of every group had gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable to the Lord. The Levite musicians, including Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives, were wearing robes of fine linen. They were standing on the east side of the altar, playing cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments. One hundred and twenty priests were with these musicians, and they were blowing trumpets. They were praising the Lord by playing music and singing: “The Lord is good, and his love never ends.” Suddenly a cloud filled the temple as the priests were leaving the holy place.
translation_verse: Bikantámbunliibee nì biwambɔɔliibee nìn bíi bɔ̀ɔ́ dicilpu ki nyɔ́ŋkí ki pàkà ti-Dindaan. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi búǹ akantán ki bɔ̀ɔ́ cancakantib nì tiwambɔɔkaal tin kíǹee ki gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan yii: «Di sá yii u ŋān̄, ní u-neendi bí kí nīn cá talkuee», ní ditagbandi diba dɔ́miń ki gbí ti-Dindaan Diikun.

english_verse: Then the priests and the Levites picked up the sacred chest, the sacred tent, and the objects used for worship, and they carried them to the temple.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi Leefii yabee nìn yōoǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bí ku-poonee ki túǹ.

english_verse: Solomon and a crowd of people stood in front of the chest and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Saloomɔn nì Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì u-cee ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau nimbiin ní bi kūū ipii nì inaa ki ŋá saraabi an kaa cáá ŋkaan.

english_verse: The priests carried the chest into the most holy place and put it under the winged creatures,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nín dū Dipoondi Dakaau ki kɔ́ǹ Circir Páaa laŋki diikun ki síiǹ u-paaŋŋu, keerubimbi feeŋyi taapu.

english_verse: The poles were so long that they could be seen from just outside the most holy place, but not from anywhere else. And they stayed there from then on.
translation_verse: Dakaa dɔi gbanti nìn fɔ̀kɔ̀ tiŋan, an puee a yaa nìn bí Circir laŋkee, a nìn wāĺ i-nyɔkɔ ní, ama a yaa nìn bí mmɔŋkee, an kaa nìn wāĺ. Idɔee dáá gbíntìi bí ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: The only things kept in the chest were the two flat stones Moses had put there when the Lord made his agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, after bringing them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Tiba kaa nìn bí Dipoondi Dakaau poon an yaa kaa sá ataŋkpee pilinti tili tin Mooyiisi nìn dūu ŋée. Ti-Dindaan nín nìn nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin u nì bi ŋá mpèéyee ní Mooyiisi dū ataŋkpee pilinti gbanti ki ŋá poon Ooreeb jool pu.

english_verse: The Lord's glory was in that cloud, and the light from it was so bright that the priests could not stay inside to do their work.
translation_verse: Ditagbandee puee, bisaraaŋaliibi kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí sīĺ poon kí tɔ̄ bi-tundi, di sá yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí u-diiku poon.

english_verse: When my father wanted to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel,
translation_verse: M-baa Daafiidi nìn cáá nlandɔkɔ kí mā kudii kí dū-ku kí sú ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: But you're not the one to do it. Your son will build the temple to honor me.”
translation_verse: Tin bée di sá yii an kaa sá sii di làá mā kudii gbanti, ama sii a-ba jipɔɔn un a màl̄ee di làá mā-mi kudii gbanti.>

english_verse: The Lord has done what he promised. I am now the king of Israel, and I've built a temple for the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan nín nìn pōoǹ puee u ŋá míǹ. Di sá yii m fōō m-baa Daafiidi yil ki jíń Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn lī puee. M máń kudii nee ki dū-ku ki sú ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: There's not enough room in all of heaven for you, Lord God. How could you possibly live on earth in this temple I have built?
translation_verse: «Mimmee Unimbɔti ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ kitiŋ pu u nì binibaaa? Áli gba kutagbɔŋu nín wāā pu nee kaa bàn̄-si á kɔ́, ki dāa nín kàaǹ kudii kun m máń nee.

english_verse: This is the temple where you have chosen to be worshiped. Please watch over it day and night and listen when I turn toward it and pray.
translation_verse: A-nimbikpeeŋu ń nīn pée cɔ́ kudii nee pu ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Ŋú nīn pée cɔ́ mpaan ŋun pu a nìn sòon̄ yii: <M-yindi làá nīn bí niin> nee pu. Pīlifì ŋwimmeem min m bí doo ki mèé-si nee.

english_verse: Listen from heaven and decide who is right. Then punish the guilty person and let the innocent one go free.
translation_verse: á pīlifì doooo yilpu kí kpèè tibɔti gbanti kí sòoǹ a-tɔntɔnliibi bɔti. Á kpɔ̀ dibɔkpil daan bɔti kí dáaĺ u-tafal, ní kí pɔ̀ un bɔti ŋān̄ee báà ŋma ń béé yii u sá maanyiiba.

english_verse: Suppose your people Israel sin against you, and then an enemy defeats them. If they come to this temple and beg for forgiveness,
translation_verse: «Isirayeel yab a-nibul yaa yīntiǹ-si ní bi-nannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ní bi fātìi gítìń a-cee, ki nyɔ́ŋkì-si, ki mēē-si ní ki gbāam̀-si kudii nee poonee,

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven. Forgive them and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.
translation_verse: sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifì a-nibul Isirayeel yab doooo yilpu, kí dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi kitiŋ kin a nìn dūu tīī bi-naanjabee poon.

english_verse: Suppose your people sin against you, and you punish them by holding back the rain. If they stop sinning and turn toward this temple to pray in your name,
translation_verse: «A-nibul yaa yīntiǹ-si ní a dū kutaa ki pīiǹ utaa kaa ti bíi nì, ní bi fātì bi-ba ki túĺ mpaan nee pú, ki mēē ki nyɔ́ŋkì a-yindi, ní ki fātì bi-boon ki tīī bi-kpitii a nín dáaĺ bi-tafal pueeyee,

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven and forgive them. The people of Israel are your servants, so teach them to live right. And send rain on the land you promised them forever.
translation_verse: sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ a-tɔntɔnliibi Isirayeel yab doooo yilpu. Á dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, kí dàkà-bi nsammɔnti ŋun bi máaǹ kí nóóyee, ní kí yàntī utaa ń nì a-tiŋki nee pu, kitiŋ kin ní a dūu tīī a-nibul án nīn sá bi-fakalee.

english_verse: Sometimes the crops may dry up or rot or be eaten by locusts or grasshoppers, and your people will be starving. Sometimes enemies may surround their towns, or your people will become sick with deadly diseases.
translation_verse: «Ŋkùm àá bìlbil kúm yaa jéetì kitiŋ nee pu, àá tikpaajin kaa láá bīń ní ki kūń àá ki sūū, àá inaakitoon nì inaaki di ŋmɔ́ ki bíil̀ tikpaajin, àá bi-nannanliibi di māntìi tú bi-timmu kí já nì bi, àá an yaa pée sá tibumbun àá igbaŋween iŋyee,

english_verse: Please listen when anyone in Israel truly feels sorry and sincerely prays with arms lifted toward your temple.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kansikin ubɔ àá a-nibul Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ di yaa béè tin bāań-bee, ki yōoǹ bi-ŋalii ki túĺ Kudii nee watil pú ki mēē-si àá ki gbāam̀-see,

english_verse: You know what is in everyone's heart. So from your home in heaven answer their prayers, according to what they do and what is in their hearts.
translation_verse: sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ-bi doooo yilpu laakin a kóoǹnée kí dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí ŋá kí tīī báà ŋma kii an nín máaǹ puee, di sá yii a nyí báà ŋma pɔbil poon bɔti.

english_verse: Then your people will worship you and obey you for as long as they live in the land you gave their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ŋá míǹ án nín làá ŋá pu ní Isirayeel yab ń fàŋkì-si iwiin in kɔkɔ bi cáá kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin a tīī bi-naanjabee puee.

english_verse: Foreigners will hear about you and your mighty power, and some of them will come to live among your people Israel. If any of them pray toward this temple,
translation_verse: «Unicaan un kaa sá a-nibul Isirayeel yab kansikin ubɔee yaa nyánní kitindandatiin ki dɔ́miń a-yindi pu, di sá yii u gbìl̄ bi sòon̄ a-yiŋkpaandi nì a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu pu, ní ki dɔ́miń míǹ ki mēē-si kudii nee poonee,

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven and answer their prayers. Then everyone on earth will worship you, just as your own people Israel do, and they will know that I have built this temple in your honor.
translation_verse: sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ-u doooo yilpu laakin a kóoǹnée. Á ŋá u nín bālifì-si puee kí tīī-u. A yaa ŋá míǹ, kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ làá béé a-yindi, kí fàŋkì-si kii Isirayeel yab nín fàŋkí-si puee, ní bí béé yii a lafun bí kudii kun m máń nee ni.

english_verse: Sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you.
translation_verse: «A yaa tīī a-nibul Isirayeel yab mara yii bí cù kí já nì bi-nannanliibi, ní bi fātì bi-ba ki túĺ kitiŋ kin a lēē nee nì kudii kun m máń-si nee watil pú ki mēēyee,

english_verse: Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
translation_verse: á pīlifiǹ bi-wimmeem nì bi-gbaamii doooo yilpu, ní kí tīī-bi dijajil.

english_verse: Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries.
translation_verse: «An ŋūǹ kí ŋá yii Isirayeel yab yīntiǹ-si, di sá yii unil ubɔ kpá kaa yìntī. Bi yaa ŋá míǹ ní a gíí bi-pu diŋuul ki yāntì bi-nannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi ki cúú-bi ki cūnnì bi-tiŋki kin dátèe àá kin kaa dátèe ni kuyuŋu,

english_verse: Lord God, hear us when we pray in this temple.
translation_verse: «Ŋúbití a-nimbiliŋ, m-Nimbɔtiu. Pīlifì m-wimmeem min m bíi mèé-si mpaan nee puee.

english_verse: Come to your new home, where we have already placed the sacred chest, which is the symbol of your strength. I pray that when the priests announce your power to save people, those who are faithful to you will celebrate what you've done for them.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, yīkìm̄, dāan̄ kí nīn bí a-ŋuŋfil paaŋŋu pu, sii nì a-dakaau un poon a-pɔŋŋu bée. Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, yàntī a-saraaŋaliibi ń dū difiil kí pèen̄ kii tiwampeeŋkaalee! Yàntī bin yú nì si deedeeyee ń nīn fàal̀ a-ŋanti pu.

english_verse: Always remember the love you had for your servant David, so that you will not reject your chosen kings.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, taa dū ubɔti un sii a-ba lēēyee kí fá. Téetí tiŋan tin kɔkɔ a ŋá ki tīī a-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidee pu!»

english_verse: When the crowd of people saw the fire and the Lord's glory, they knelt down and worshiped the Lord. They prayed: “The Lord is good, and his love never ends.”
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee nìn ká ŋŋmi nyánní yilpu ki kpákatìń ní ti-Dindaan nyooti jìliŋkī kunimbɔtidiin. Niinee ní bi tātìi gbāaǹ bi-nimbiiŋyi tūū kitiŋ ki jáaḿ-u ki nyɔ́ŋkí-u ki lì yii: «U ŋān̄ ní u-neendi bí kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: Then they will answer, “It was because the people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.”
translation_verse: Ní bí dāá kíí-bi yii: <Kun yì-tèe di sá yii Isirayeel yab dū ti-Dindaan bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu un di nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee ki fá. Bi dū bi-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ awaa ki gbāaǹ ŋi-taapu ki jáam̀-ŋi. An pu ní ti-Dindaan yāntì nnaabu nee jéetì bi-pu.>»

english_verse: Everybody stood up during the ceremony. The priests were in their assigned places, blowing their trumpets. And the Levites faced them, playing the musical instruments that David had made for them to use when they praised the Lord for his never-ending love.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yú bi-tundi laŋki. Leefii yab nìn ŋúb́ tiwambɔɔkaal tin ubɔti Daafiidi nìn yāntì bi kpítì ki tīī-bee ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan ki lì yii: «Di sá yii u-neendi bí ní ki cá jaanjaan.» Daafiidi di nìn ŋmàn̄ nlan gbanti ki tīī-bi. Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yú ki túĺ-bi ki búǹ akantán ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yíkìi yúl̀.

english_verse: If my own people will humbly pray and turn back to me and stop sinning, then I will answer them from heaven. I will forgive them and make their land fertile once again.
translation_verse: M-nibul din pu bi yíì m-yindee nib yaa sīntì bi-ba taapu, ki mēē, ki nyàab̄-mi ní ki dū bi-saŋkpitii ki fée, man làá pīlifiǹ-bi doooo yilpu, kí dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí fàtīí tīī bi-tiŋki ki-gaajati.

english_verse: Then on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent everyone home. They left very happy because of all the good things the Lord had done for David and Solomon, and for his people Israel. The Lord Appears to Solomon Again (
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, uŋmaluluúti iwiin mmuŋku nì ita dalee ní Saloomɔn yāntì Isirayeel yab nín kùǹ bi-dumpu. english_verse: The Lord's temple and Solomon's palace were now finished. In fact, everything Solomon had planned to do was completed.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn máń ti-Dindaan Diiku nì úǹ u-ba naakooku nì tin u nìn pée là kí mēe ki dóò.

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream and said: I heard your prayer, and I have chosen this temple as the place where sacrifices will be offered to me.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-u kunyeeu ní ki bí-u yii: «M gbìl̄ a-wimmeem ní ki lēē kudii nee kú nīn sá mpaan ŋun pu bi làá nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì-mee.

english_verse: because it belongs to me, and this is where I will be worshiped forever. I will never stop watching over it.
translation_verse: Too, m lēē kudii nee ki dū-ku ki sú m-ba kí nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkà ku-poon kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. M-nimbikpeeŋu làá nīn cɔ́ ku-pu, ní m-pɔbil ń nīn kā ku-pu baabadal.

english_verse: Your father David obeyed me, and now, Solomon, you must do the same. Obey my laws and teachings,
translation_verse: Ama siiyee, nín̄ nóó-mi kii a-baa Daafiidee. Nín̄ ŋáań tin kɔkɔ m kpáafì-see, ní kí nīn ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-koobiliŋ.

english_verse: and I will keep my solemn promise to him that someone from your family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: A yaa ŋá míǹ, m làá tīī a-beel mpɔn kii m nín nìn pōoǹ a-baa Daafiidi puee. M nìn bí-u yii: <A-kpátam boonee, a-naantiibi kansikin ubɔ làá nīn pée sá ubɔti ní Isirayeel tiŋkin.>

english_verse: But if you or any of the people of Israel disobey my laws or start worshiping foreign gods,
translation_verse: Ama sii nì a-nibul yaa fātì ni-boon ki tīī-mi, ní kaa ŋúb́ m-marab nì m-koobiliŋ ŋin m tīī-nee, ní ki cūtìi nóó awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapuee,

english_verse: I will pull you out of this land I gave you. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped, so that people everywhere will think it is only a joke and will make fun of it.
translation_verse: m làá jà-ni kitiŋ kin pu m tīī-nee. M làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī kudii kun m dūu sú m-ba nee. Anibul kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn ŋúb́ Isirayeel ki lāā ki bèel̄.

english_verse: This temple is now magnificent. But when these things happen, everyone who walks by it will be shocked and will ask, “Why did the Lord do such a terrible thing to his people and to this temple?”
translation_verse: Kudii nee sá díǹ pu nee kukpaaŋŋu. Ama binib bin làá dāá jītí kudii nee caŋinee làá dāá bàkatī ní kí bàlifì yii: <Ba yì-tì ní ti-Dindaan nín ŋá kitiŋ nee nì kudii nee míǹ?>

english_verse: After that, Solomon had his workers rebuild the towns that Hiram had given him. Then Solomon sent Israelites to live in those towns.
translation_verse: U nìn fātìi máń ntimu mun Tiir bɔtiu Yiiram nìn tīī-uee. U nìn cáań Isirayeel yab ki kāaǹ ntimuee ni.

english_verse: Solomon attacked and captured the town of Hamath-Zobah.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Saloomɔn cūtìi jáń ki fōō Amati-Sooba tiŋki.

english_verse: He ordered his workers to build the town of Tadmor in the desert and some towns in Hamath where he could keep his supplies.
translation_verse: U nìn fātìi máń Tadimɔɔr tiŋki kuteeun nì ntimu mun nìn bí Amati tiŋkpaaŋkin bi kpáafí u-jintee.

english_verse: He strengthened Upper Beth-Horon and Lower Beth-Horon by adding walls and gates that could be locked.
translation_verse: U nìn fātìi máń Beeti-Oorɔn tiŋki kin bí yilpu púee nì Beeti-Oorɔn tiŋki kin bí taapu púee. U nìn máń agun ki tú ntimu gbanti ní mu cáá punuubi nì tikpàlkaal.

english_verse: He did the same thing to the town of Baalath and to the cities where he kept supplies, chariots, and horses. Solomon ordered his workers to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere else in his kingdom.
translation_verse: U nìn gíti ŋá Balaati tiŋki nì ntimu mun poon u nìn kpáafí u-jinti nì u-janjatɔrɔkub nì u-taamuuyee míǹ ní. Saloomɔn nìn pée máń tin ní u nìn lèe ní Jeerusaleem tiŋkin nì Leebanɔn jool pu nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ nìn bí u-taapuee.

english_verse: Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the part of Jerusalem called David's City to her new palace that Solomon had built. The sacred chest had been kept in David's City, which made his palace sacred, and so Solomon's wife could no longer live there.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn yāntì u-nimpuu Faaroo bisal nyáń Daafiidi Tiŋkin ki cūtìi kɔ́ kudii kun u nìn máń ki tīī-uee ni. Di sá u nìn lī yii: «M-nimpuu kaa máaǹ kí nīn kóò Isirayeel bɔtiu Daafiidi cindin. Di sá yii adiin ŋin poon bi dū ti-Dindaan Dakaau ki yóoǹee sá circir diiŋŋi ní.»

english_verse: Solomon offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built in front of the temple porch.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn nìn ŋáań ti-Dindaan bisaraawɔkaabi nsaraafan ŋun u nìn máń ki tīī-u ŋu bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee ní.

english_verse: He followed the requirements that Moses had given for sacrifices offered on the Sabbath, on the first day of each month, the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters.
translation_verse: Kii Mooyiisi nín nìn síiǹ mara bí nīn ŋáań ŋwiin kamaa puee, u nìn ŋáań ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa saraabi, ki ŋáań uŋmal kamaa wimpeekaaŋu saraabi nì bijiŋaakpaambi bita bin bi nìn jīǹee saraabi. Jiŋaalib gbanti di sá jiŋaal un bi jīǹ ki ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nì Pantikooti jiŋaaliu nì Tibìń jiŋaaliu.

english_verse: Solomon then assigned the priests and the Levites their duties at the temple, and he followed the instructions that his father, the man of God, had given him. Some of the Levites were to lead music and help the priests in their duties, and others were to guard the temple gates
translation_verse: Kii u-baa Daafiidi nín nìn lēē pu ki síiǹee, Saloomɔn nìn tīī bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab bi-tuuŋŋi nín sá pu kunimbɔtidiinee, ki nóó nì bi-kitiŋi. Leefii yab biba tundi di nìn sá bí nīn nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan baabadal, àá kí tūtuǹ bisaraaŋaliibi bi-tuuŋŋi poon. U nìn yāntì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitiŋi ŋin nìn cí kunimbɔtidii punyɔmmuee mun kíĺ bi-tundi. Unimbɔti niliu Daafiidi nín nìn síiǹ mara bí ŋá puee dee.

english_verse: Everything Solomon had planned to do was now finished—from the laying of the temple's foundation to its completion.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Saloomɔn nìn túń u-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ ki dóò, kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun u bíl̀ kunimbɔtidii nyeelee ki cáa sāā bi nín máń-ku ki dóòyee. Saloomɔn nìn máń kunimbɔtidii ki dóò.

english_verse: Solomon went to Ezion-Geber and Eloth, two Edomite towns on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Niinee Saloomɔn nín cá Eesiiyɔn-Geebeer nì Eelaati timmun. Eelaati tiŋki gbanti nìn bí Tikati Mɔɔl gbandi, Eedoom tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: Hiram sent him ships and some of his experienced sailors. They went with Solomon's own sailors to the country of Ophir and brought back more than
translation_verse: Yiiram nìn dū u-tɔntɔnliibi bimeelaŋaaliliibi bin nyí tiŋku bɔti tiŋanee ki tú bí tūtuǹ Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi. Bimeelaŋaaliliibi gbanti nì Saloomɔn yab nìn cūtì Oofiiri tiŋkin ki nyàab̄ sindaariya tɔnnib saalaa nì bili ki cáa cūnnì ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u bí ubɔti yii: «Tin m gbìl̄ m-tiŋkin a-tuuŋŋi pu nì a-ciiŋyi puee lafun sá mbaamɔn ní.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are greater than I was told.
translation_verse: Ama maa nìn fōō ki kíí, see m nín dɔ́miń m-ba ki ká nì m-nimbilee. Tin bi máafì-mee kaa bàn̄ tin m ká nee dijandi gba. A-ciiŋyi jítiǹ tin m gbìl̄ee pu kpataaa.

english_verse: Your people and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: A-nib nì a-tɔntɔnliibi bin bí a-nimbiin baabadal ki pílifí a-ciiŋyi nyɔɔbuŋŋee bí mmɔnneeee!

english_verse: I praise the Lord your God. He is pleased with you and has made you king of Israel. God loves the people of this country and will never desert them, so he has given them a king who will rule fairly and honestly.
translation_verse: Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu un di lēē-si á kàl̄ Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeelee! Kun puee u néeń Isirayeel kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan ní, an pu ní u dū-si ki kāaǹ dibeel á yàntī tin bí deedeeyee nì ibaamɔn ń nīn bí.»

english_verse: The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, a large amount of jewels, and the best spices anyone had ever seen.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Sabaa tiŋki nimpubɔtiu tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn sindaariya tɔnnib bita nì dijandi nì talaalub tikpil nì ataŋkpamɔnti. Sabaa nimpubɔtiu nín nìn tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn talaalub puee, baa ti pée ká an talaalub bulifi kɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋkin ki ká.

english_verse: not counting what the merchants and traders brought him. The kings of Arabia and the leaders of Israel also gave him gold and silver.
translation_verse: ní kí nín kūtì bibantiliibi nì binyampoobi nín nìn cāabìń sindaariya un ki pà patantibee. Arabii bɔtiibi kɔkɔ nì Isirayeel tiŋkpaammu gɔminab nìn cāabìń sindaariya nì animbil ki tìì Saloomɔn.

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the records of Nathan the prophet, Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh, and Iddo the prophet who wrote about Jeroboam son of Nebat.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, kí yòon̄ tin u péé ki ŋée nì tin u ŋá ki lúŋkèe, ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan gbɔŋkun nì Ayiiya, ubɔnaatil un nyánní Siiloo tiŋkinee gbɔŋkun nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Idoo leedakal gbɔŋkun. Kugbɔŋu gbanti sòoǹ Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam mun pu.

english_verse: His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn gíti kpítì dibeejal dikpaandi diba ní ki dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì ní ki dū kunti nyiŋŋi ki nákáǹ nákáǹ.

english_verse: It had a gold footstool attached to it and armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on each side of the throne,
translation_verse: Dibeejalee nìn cáá akɔl ŋin pu bi tà ki jɔ́ḿ-dèe aluu, ní ki cáá laakin ataa tɔ̄kɔntée an sá sindaariya. Bi nìn kpítì gbikintib bili ki síiǹ laakin bi pāantí iŋalee.

english_verse: and there were two lion statues on each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
translation_verse: Gbikintib nìn bí saalaa nì bili ní ki bí akɔl aluuyee nín kúntí puee. Baa nìn pée kpítì dibeejal diba míǹ dibeel diba poon ki ká.

english_verse: Solomon's cups and dishes in Forest Hall were made of pure gold, because silver was almost worthless in those days.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Saloomɔn kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi kɔkɔ nìn sá sindaariya ŋma ní, ní asambil ŋin bí <Leebanɔn Pɔɔku> diikunee nìn sá sindaariyamɔnti ŋma. Baa nìn dù animbil kúti kí ŋá tiba, di sá yii Saloomɔn yuntiŋuee, animbil kúti kaa nìn cáá kunyampoou.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ubɔti nìn cáá meelab Taarsiisi tiŋkin. Yiiram meelaŋaaliliibi di nìn ŋàal̀-bi. Abin ata poon diba puee, meelab gbanti nìn cāabìń sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì kunti nyiŋŋi nì ilantan nì ikooŋaan.

english_verse: Solomon was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn jítiǹ kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi kɔkɔ tigaajati poon nì iciin poon.

english_verse: Year after year, other kings came to hear the wisdom God had given him. And they brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Bi yaa nìn dòońee, báà ŋma nìn cāabìń animbil kúti wanti nì sindaariya wanti nì tiwampeeŋkaal nì tijanjawan nì talaalub nì itaamu nì imamboon ki pūǹ-u. Dibindi kamaayee, binib nìn pée ŋáań míǹ ní.

english_verse: He ruled all the nations from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of Philistia in the south, as far as the border of Egypt.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi bin nìn bí kí yòon̄ Eefiraati mɔɔl kí cáá sāā Fiiliistii yab tiŋki nì Eejipiti tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔee kɔkɔ nìn bí Saloomɔn taapu ní.

english_verse: While Solomon was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as the sycamore trees in the western foothills.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn yāntì animbil gbí Jeerusaleem kii ataŋkpeeyee ní, ní seedir dɔi wīikí kii Seefeelaa tiŋki sufii in bi yíì siikoomɔɔree.

english_verse: Solomon's horses were brought in from other countries, including Musri. Solomon Dies (
translation_verse: Saloomɔn taamui nìn nyēeń Eejipiti nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ kíǹee poon ní. Saloomɔn kúm (

english_verse: he died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn kpíì ki cūtì ki ŋàl̄ u-naanjab ní bi síb́-u u-baa Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Rooboowaam di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he returned from Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon.
translation_verse: Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn dáá gbíntìi bíń Eejipiti tiŋkin, laakin u nìn sáǹ ubɔti Saloomɔn ki cūtìi kāl̀ee. U nín gbìl̄ Siikeem kooŋyi gbanti puee ní u yíkì Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dɔ́miń.

english_verse: The people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Bi nìn tú binib bi cūtìi yíiń-u. U bāańee ní u nì Isirayeel beel samaau kɔkɔ cūtì Rooboowaam cee ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: “Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
translation_verse: «A-baa nìn túǹ-ti ditúndi din nyìm̀ee. Siiyee, ti là yii á bàtī-ti ditumpɔɔl din a-baa nìn yāntì ti túńee nì diwaŋgul din u nìn dūu nyīkiǹ ti-puee. A yaa ŋá míǹ ti kíí kí nīn sá a-tɔntɔnliibi.»

english_verse: Rehoboam replied, “Come back in three days for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Nín̄ cámaan, iwiin ita dalee ní fàtīí gítiń.» U lī mimmee ní samaa nín cá.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Rooboowaam bālifì bitindaŋkpilib bin nìn bí u-baa Saloomɔn tundin ŋyunti ŋun u nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee yii: «Ni sáŋkí-mi ḿ kíí binib nee yii ba?»

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should be kind and promise to make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Ní bikpilibee bí-u yii: «A yaa dàkā binib nee kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ki ŋá bi nín là puee ní ki yaa kíí-bi kinyɔɔmɔɔyee, bi làá nīn sá a-tɔntɔnliibi kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Ama ní Rooboowaam kaa dū bikpilibee saŋkii ki túń ditundi, ní ki yíiń binipɔmbi u nì bin jíń tinaacimpɔn dicilpu bi bí u-tundinee.

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: U nìn bí bíǹ yii: «Nimbi fáà, ni sáŋkí-mi yii ba? Ḿ kíí binib bin bíi bàlifī-mi ḿ bàtī diwaŋgul din m-baa nìn dūu túǹ-bee nyiŋfiŋu pu yii ba?»

english_verse: His younger advisors said: Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak.
translation_verse: Ní binipɔmbi u nì bin kpáfìi jíń tinaacimpɔnee kíí-u yii: «Kpèè a nín làá kíí binib bin dɔ́miń ki bí-si yii: <A-baa nìn túǹ-ti diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, siiyee bàtī di-nyiŋfiŋu pu kí tīī-ti> puee sɔ̀: <M-ŋambikpakpalii gbìfiǹ m-baa ŋal.

english_verse: He made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: M-baa yaa nìn túǹ-ni diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, man làá gíti kūtì diwaŋgul gbanti nyiŋfiŋu pu. M-baa nìn dū anaalab ní ki dáaĺ ni-tafal, mamee, m làá dū anaalab ŋin cáá agatee ní kí dáaĺ ni-tafal.>»

english_verse: Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. He spoke bluntly
translation_verse: Bikpilib nín nìn sáŋkì u-bɔti puee, waa dūu túń ditundi, ní ki sòon̄ nì samaa an pɔ̄ɔ̄.

english_verse: and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested. He said: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: Binipɔmbee nín sáŋkì-u puee, míǹ ní u dūu sòon̄ nì binibee. U nìn bí-bi yii: «M-baa yaa nìn túǹ-ni diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, man làá gíti kūtì diwaŋgul gbanti nyiŋfiŋu pu. M-baa nìn dū anaalab ní ki dáaĺ ni-tafal, mamee, m làá dū anaalab ŋin cáá agatee ní kí dáaĺ ni-tafal.»

english_verse: After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and regain control of the whole country. So he called together
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Rooboowaam bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee ní u kóoǹ Juuda nì Beenjameen naakɔtin janjaliibi bibaamɔmbi kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku inaa ki kpáfì kí cùú já nì Isirayeel yab, án nín làá ŋá pu úǹ Rooboowaam ń fàtīí fōō dibeelee.

english_verse: as well as with shields and spears. He used these fortified cities to keep control of Judah and Benjamin. The Priests and the Levites Support Rehoboam
translation_verse: Agbampɔɔ nì ŋkpamu nìn bí ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ poon. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋá ní ki ŋúń ki jíń Juuda nì Beenjameen timmu pu dibeel. Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab páaǹ Rooboowaam boon

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Lord had told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Ama ní ti-Dindaan bí u-bɔnaatiliu Seemaya yii:

english_verse: “The Lord warns you not to go to war against the people from the northern tribes—they are your relatives. Go home! The Lord is the one who made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord's message and did not attack Jeroboam and his troops. Rehoboam Fortifies Cities in Judah
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Naa máaǹ kí cùú já nì ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab. Báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-dumpu, di sá yii man di yāntì tin bíi jītí nee bāań.>» Niinee ní bi gbìl̄ ki tīī nì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi ní ki yāntì kaa ti cūtìi jáń nì Jeerooboowaam. Rooboowaam máń agun ki tú ntimu kupaau

english_verse: Rehoboam ruled from Jerusalem, and he had several cities in Judah turned into fortresses so he could use them to defend his country. These cities included
translation_verse: Rooboowaam nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní ki máń agun ki tú Juuda timmu. Ntimu gbanti di sá:

english_verse: Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
translation_verse: Beetileem nì Eetaam nì Teekoowa

english_verse: Beth-Zur, Soco, Adullam,
translation_verse: nì Beeti-Suur nì Sookoo nì Adulaam

english_verse: Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
translation_verse: nì Gaati nì Mareeka nì Siifi

english_verse: Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
translation_verse: nì Adoorayiim nì Lakiisi nì Aseeka

english_verse: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. After he had fortified these cities in the territories of Judah and Benjamin,
translation_verse: nì Soora nì Ayalɔn nì Eebrɔn. Ntimu mun bi nìn máń agun ki tú gbantee nìn bí Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab timmu poon ní.

english_verse: he assigned an army commander to each of them and stocked them with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine,
translation_verse: An nìn sá agun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋanee ní Rooboowaam nìn máń ki tú-mu. U nìn nyàab̄ gɔminab ki kāaǹ mu-pu, ní bi nìn kpáafí tijin nì ɔliifi kpam nì ndamam niin.

english_verse: The priests and Levites from the northern tribes of Israel gave their support to King Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn nyáń Isirayeel timmu kɔkɔn ki dɔ́miń ki páaǹ Rooboowaam boon.

english_verse: And since Jeroboam and the kings of Israel that followed him would not allow any Levites to serve as priests, most Levites left their towns and pasturelands in Israel and moved to Jerusalem and other towns in Judah.
translation_verse: Leefii yab nìn yíkìi fá bi-timmu nì bi-kpaatanti ki nín cá Juuda beelin nì Jeerusaleem. Di sá yii Jeerooboowaam nì u-jipɔmbi kaa nìn pú-bi nsan bí nīn gbíntìi sá ti-Dindaan saraaŋaliibi.

english_verse: Jeroboam chose his own priests to serve at the local shrines in Israel and at the places of worship where he had set up statues of goat-demons and of calves.
translation_verse: Jeerooboowaam nìn lēē úǹ u-ba saraaŋaliibi, ní bíǹ bí ŋgbantamu pu ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì iŋɔjaa nì anabil ŋin u nìn máń ki síiǹee.

english_verse: But some of the people from Israel wanted to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done. So they followed the priests and Levites to Jerusalem, where they could offer sacrifices to the Lord.
translation_verse: Isirayeel beel naakɔti kɔkɔnee, binib bin nìn nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nì bi-pɔbil kɔkɔee nìn táá Leefii yab ki dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Bi nìn là kí nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì ti-Dindaan, bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: For the next three years, they lived in Judah and were loyal to Rehoboam and his kingdom, just as they had been loyal to David and Solomon. Rehoboam's Family
translation_verse: Bíǹ nìn gíti kútì Juuda beel mpɔn ní ki nìn tútúǹ Saloomɔn jipɔɔn Rooboowaam abin ata. Di sá yii abin ata gbanti poonee, u nìn nóó Daafiidi nì Saloomɔn tabɔbiliŋ. Rooboowaam dicaŋku

english_verse: Rehoboam and Mahalath had three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
translation_verse: U nìn màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu muta: Yeewusi nì Seemariya nì Sayam.

english_verse: Then Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom. Their sons were Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Rooboowaam cáá Abisaloom bisal Maaka. U nìn màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu munaa: Abiiya nì Atayii nì Siisa nì Seeloomiiti.

english_verse: Rehoboam was wise enough to put one of his sons in charge of each fortified city in his kingdom. He gave them all the supplies they needed and found wives for every one of them.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá iciin ní ki yāntì u-jipɔmbi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ yàl̄ ki tin bíń Juuda nì Beenjameen timmu mun bi nìn máń agun ki túee poon. U nìn tīī-bi tijin tikpil ní ki nyàab̄ binimpoobi kupaau ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: but he still did wrong and refused to obey the Lord.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, di sá yii waa nìn dū u-pɔbil kɔkɔ ki nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: So in the fifth year of Rehoboam's rule, the Lord punished them for their unfaithfulness and allowed King Shishak of Egypt to invade Judah.
translation_verse: Rooboowaam nín kāl̀ dibeel dibiŋŋmooŋmootiil poonee ní Eejipiti bɔtiu Siisaaki dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Jeerusaleem, di sá yii baa nìn gíti yú nì ti-Dindaan deedee.

english_verse: He captured every one of the fortified cities in Judah and then marched to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: U nìn jáń ki fōō Juuda timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee, ní ki nìkī ki dāa bāań áli Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah had gone to Jerusalem to escape Shishak's invasion. And while they were there, Shemaiah the prophet told them, “The Lord says that because you have disobeyed him, he has now abandoned you. The Lord will not help you against Shishak!”
translation_verse: Siisaaki nìn tóobiń ní Rooboowaam nì Juuda kpilib kóoǹ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem. Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Seemaya nìn cūtìi ká-bi ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀: <Ni dū man ni-Dindaan ki fá! Too, ma mun dū-ni ki ŋá Siisaaki ŋaan.>»

english_verse: Rehoboam and the leaders were sorry for what they had done and admitted, “The Lord is right. We have deserted him.”
translation_verse: Isirayeel kpilibee nì ubɔti nìn lafun béè yii bi yīntì ní ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan cáá mbaamɔn.»

english_verse: When the Lord heard this, he told Shemaiah: The people of Judah are truly sorry for their sins, and so I won't let Shishak completely destroy them. But because I am still angry,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín ká bi sīntì bi-ba taapuee, ní u tùkū Seemaya yii: «Bi nín béè bi-yìntitamee puee, maa làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi. Ama an kaa ti làá yúntí, m làá fīī-bi, di sá yii maa làá dī Siisaaki pu ní kí yàntī m-ŋuul ń jēetí Jeerusaleem pu.

english_verse: he will conquer and rule them. Then my people will know what it's like to serve a foreign king instead of serving me.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m làá yàntī bí kpántí u-tɔntɔnliibi. Niinee bi làá béé yii bi yaa sá man tɔntɔnliibi di sɔ́ɔɔ, bi yaa sá ntimu mubɔ bɔtiibi tɔntɔnliibi di sɔ́.»

english_verse: Shishak attacked Jerusalem and took all the valuable things from the temple and from the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: Eejipiti bɔtiu Siisaaki nìn jáń nì Jeerusaleem yab. U nìn yōoǹ tigaajawan tin bí ti-Dindaan Diikun nì kubɔtinaakoounee. U nìn pée yōoǹ kɔkɔ ní, ki kpáaǹ agbampɔɔ ŋin Saloomɔn nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́yee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Rooboowaam dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ agbampɔɔ ki téeǹ ŋin bi yōoǹee yil pu, ní ki dū-ŋi ki ŋá bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔti naakooku punyɔmmuee kpiliu ŋaan ú nīn kpèé.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he had finished worshiping.
translation_verse: Ubɔti yaa nìn pée yíkì ki kóò kunimbɔtidiinee, bijanjaliibi nìn yòontí agbampɔɔ gbanti ní ki līī, ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-ŋi biciitiliibi diikun.

english_verse: Rehoboam turned back to the Lord, and so the Lord did not let Judah be completely destroyed, and Judah was prosperous again. Rehoboam's Rule in Judah (
translation_verse: Rooboowaam nín nìn sīntì u-ba taapu puee, ti-Dindaan nìn páatì u-ŋuul u-pu kaa nāaǹ-u kɔkɔ. Kí kūtì muee, tiwammɔntiil nìn dáá bí Juuda tiŋkin. Rooboowaam maŋfal wiiŋyi kúntitam (

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king, including a history of his family, is written in the records of the two prophets, Shemaiah and Iddo. During Rehoboam's rule, he and King Jeroboam of Israel were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Rooboowaam tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, kí yòon̄ tin u péé ki ŋée nì tin u ŋá ki lúŋkèe, ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Seemaya gbɔŋkun nì Idoo un wāĺee gbɔŋkun. Kujaau nìn pée bí Rooboowaam nì Jeerooboowaam kansikin ní kaa gbèentí.

english_verse: When Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah became king.
translation_verse: Rooboowaam kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Abiiya di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Now you and your powerful army think you can stand up to the kingdom that the Lord has given to David's descendants. The only gods you have are those gold statues of calves that Jeroboam made for you.
translation_verse: Too kɔŋkɔnnee, ni bíi lì yii ni làá já nì dibeel din ti-Dindaan dūu ŋá Daafiidi naantiibi ŋaanee. Tiŋman ni wīikí ní ki cáá sindaariya nabil din Jeerooboowaam mɔ́ɔ́ ki tīī-ni dí nīn sá ni-nimbɔtiuee.

english_verse: and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah. Some time later, Abijah and King Jeroboam of Israel went to war against each other.
translation_verse: U nìn jíń dibeel Jeerusaleem abin ata ní. U-na nìn sá ugiibeeyaja Uriyeel bisal ní bi yíì-u yii Miikaya. Abiiya nì Jeerooboowaam nìn pée jáà ní kaa gbèentí.

english_verse: Abijah went to the top of Mount Zemaraim in the hills of Ephraim and shouted: Listen, Jeroboam and all you Israelites!
translation_verse: Abiiya nìn jɔ́m̀ Seemarayiim jool din bí Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee ní ki bí yii: «Jeerooboowaam nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, ní pīlifìmaan.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has made a solemn promise that every king of Israel will be from David's family.
translation_verse: Naa nyí yii ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dū Isirayeel beel ki tīī Daafiidi nì u-naantiibi ní ki nīn cáa cá jaanjaanaaa? An sá dipoondi din bí kaa kpìtēe ní.

english_verse: But Jeroboam, you were King Solomon's official, and you rebelled.
translation_verse: Ama Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam un nìn sá Daafiidi jipɔɔn Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliuee yíkì ki jáń nì u-kpiliu.

english_verse: Then right after Rehoboam became king, you and your bunch of worthless followers challenged Rehoboam, who was too young to know how to stop you.
translation_verse: Naayeekub nì binib bin kaa bí tibanee yíkìi páaǹ u-boon ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Saloomɔn jipɔɔn Rooboowaam. Rooboowaam mun nìn dáá sá kinaacimpɔmbiki, kaa nìn dáá nyí tiba ní kaa nìn ŋúń ki síl̀ bi-nimbiin.

english_verse: But we have not turned our backs on the Lord God! Aaron's own descendants serve as our priests, and the Levites are their assistants.
translation_verse: Ama timbee, ti-Dindaan di sá timbi Nimbɔtiu, ní taa dū-u ki fá. Bisaraaŋaliibi bin tūǹ ti-Dindaan tundee sá Aarɔn naantiibi ní, ní Leefii yab mun bí ki tūǹ bi-tundi.

english_verse: That's why God is on our side and will lead us into battle when the priests sound the signal on the trumpets. It's no use, Israelites. You might as well give up. There's no way you can defeat the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, Unimbɔti u-ba di līī timbi nyɔkɔpu. U-saraaŋaliibi mun bí ki bɔ́ntì kí búń bi-yiŋyi ti kíĺ nì ni kujaau. Míǹ puee Isirayeel yab, ní taa já nì ti-Dindaan, ni-naanjab Nimbɔtiu! Naa làá ŋmā kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u.»

english_verse: But while Abijah was talking, Jeroboam had sent some of his troops to attack Judah's army from behind, while the rest attacked from the front.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Jeerooboowaam nìn lēē u-janjaliibi biba bi cūtìi bál̀ Juuda yab janjaliibi boon pú kí túuǹ-bi. An ŋá mimmee ní Isirayeel janjaliibi biba bí Juuda yab nyɔkɔpu ní bin bál̀ee mun bí bi-boon pú.

english_verse: Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
translation_verse: Abiiya nìn kùl̄ ki páaǹ Jeerooboowaam boon. U nìn jáń ki fōō u-cee Beeteel nì Yeesana Eefrɔn timmu nì ntimbilimu mun pìl̄-muee.

english_verse: Jeroboam never regained his power during the rest of Abijah's rule. The Lord punished Jeroboam, and he died, but Abijah became more powerful.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Abiiya sá ubɔtee, Jeerooboowaam kaa nìn gíti ká mpɔn. An dāa kúntèe ní ti-Dindaan fáá-u ní u kpíì.

english_verse: Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
translation_verse: Abiiya tuuŋŋi ŋin u túńee, tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì tin u lēe ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Idoo gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines and the altars to foreign gods. He smashed the stone images of gods and cut down the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah.
translation_verse: U nìn kpáafì Juuda yab yii bí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu, kí nīn tɔ́ u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-marab.

english_verse: Then he told everyone in Judah to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done, and to obey his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: U nìn kúntì iwaatootipaan nì isaraafan in pu bi nìn tùutī talaalubee Juuda timmu kɔkɔn. An puee, u-beel yuntiŋuee, Juuda beel nìn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin ní.

english_verse: He said to the people, “Let's build walls and defense towers for these towns, and put in gates that can be locked with bars. This land still belongs to us, because we have obeyed the Lord our God. He has given us peace from all our enemies.” The people did everything Asa had suggested.
translation_verse: Juuda naakookunee, Asaa nìn cáá bijanjaliibi kutukub alaataa ata, bi ŋúb̀ agbampɔɔ akpaan nì ŋkpamu. U nìn cáá Beenjameen naakookun bijanjaliibi kutukub alaataa ali nì imuŋku inaa, bi ŋúb̀ agbampɔɔ ŋwaamu ki ŋūǹ ki tòó itɔfi. Bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ nìn sá bibaatandambi ní.

english_verse: but Asa and his troops chased them as far as Gerar. It was a total defeat—the Ethiopians could not even fight back! The soldiers from Judah took everything that had belonged to the Ethiopians.
translation_verse: Bi nìn jáń ki fōō ntimu mun kɔkɔ nìn bí ki pìlīǹ Geeraar tiŋkee. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì dinyoondi kɔ́-bi. Juuda yab nìn fúkúl̀ ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ yab wanti, kun puee tigaajawan tikpil nìn bí niin bí fūkul̀.

english_verse: The people who lived in the villages around Gerar learned what had happened and were afraid of the Lord. So Judah's army easily defeated them and carried off everything of value that they wanted from these towns.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gāatì bipikpaaliibi naabakati ní ki nìn kóoǹ bi-piii nì bi-gutaamui tikpil. Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki nín gítí Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: Some time later, God spoke to Azariah son of Oded.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti Fam nìn kpákatì Oodeedi jipɔɔn Asariyawuu pu.

english_verse: At once, Azariah went to Asa and said: Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
translation_verse: U nìn cūtìi túŋkì Asaa ní ki bí-u yii: «Asaa nì Juuda nì Beenjameen yab kɔkɔ, ní pīlifìmaan-mi! Ni yaa bí ti-Dindaan ceeyee, u mun bí ni-cee ní. Ni yaa nyàab̄-uee, u làá yàntī ní ká-u, ama ni yaa dū-u ki fée, see u mun ń dū-ni kí fá.

english_verse: For a long time, the people of Israel did not worship the true God or listen to priests who could teach them about God. They refused to obey God's Law.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn dū iyunti tikpil ki kāl̀ ibaamɔn Nimbɔtiu kpá bi-ceeyaaa, usaraaŋal ubɔ kpá kí dàkà-baaa, ní mara ubɔ mun nìn kpá.

english_verse: But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
translation_verse: Ama bi-nimbinaamandi poonee, bi fātìi gítìń ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee, ki nyàab̄-u, ní úǹ yāntì bi ká-u.

english_verse: There was so much confusion in those days that it wasn't safe to go anywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, unil kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí nyā kí fàtīí kɔ́nní nì ŋgbansɔŋfi, di sá yii kitiŋ kamaa pu nib nìn bí dinyoondin ní.

english_verse: Nations were destroying each other, and cities were wiping out other cities, because God was causing trouble and unrest everywhere.
translation_verse: Ditimbundi diba nìn jáà nì di-juti, ní kitiŋ kiba jáà nì ki-juti, di sá yii Unimbɔti di nìn cáań animbinaaman gbanti kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifi ki tɔ́ bi-pu.

english_verse: As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Asariyawuu, Oodeedi jipɔɔn dū tibɔti gbanti ki nāatì Asaayee, ní u ká kunyannyaau. U nìn kúntì awaa ŋin kɔkɔ nìn bí Juuda nì Beenjameen timmunee. U nìn kúntì ŋin mun nìn bí ntimu mun u nìn jáń ki fōō Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee. U nìn ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu ŋun nìn bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee.

english_verse: Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
translation_verse: U nìn kóoǹ Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab kɔkɔ nì Isirayeel yab bin nìn nyánní Eefiraayiim nì Manasee nì Simeeyɔn naakɔtin ki dɔ́mińee ki kpáfì. Di sá yii Isirayeel yab tikpil nìn dɔ́miń ki páaǹ u-boon ŋyunti ŋun ní bi ká yii ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu bí u-ceeyee.

english_verse: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Asaa nín jíń dibeel abin saalku ŋmatataatiu poonee, ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: They made a solemn promise to faithfully worship the Lord God their ancestors had worshiped,
translation_verse: Bi nìn pōoǹ kí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu nì bi-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ nì bi-nammu kɔkɔ.

english_verse: and to put to death anyone who refused to obey him.
translation_verse: Bi nìn pōoǹ yii kibikeeee, unikpaaneeee, uninjeeee, unimpueeee, un kamaa yaa kaa nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiuee, bí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: The crowd solemnly agreed to keep their promise to the Lord, then they celebrated by shouting and blowing trumpets and horns.
translation_verse: Ní bi téeń mpɔn ki fáá iwiliili, ní ki búń akantán nì iyin ki pūtì ki pōoǹ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Everyone was happy because they had made this solemn promise, and in return, the Lord blessed them with peace from all their enemies.
translation_verse: Juuda yab kɔkɔ nìn bí mmɔnni, kun puee bi nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ nì bi-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ ní. Bi nìn lēē bi-ban kí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, ní ti-Dindaan mun nìn yāntì bi ká-u. Ti-Dindaan nìn tīī-bi ŋgbansɔŋfi ijaan kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Asaa nìn lēē u-naan Maaka tinimpubɔtiilin, kun puee u nìn kpítì diwaal ki nántiǹ ntimbiil waal Aseera. Asaa nìn gāā diwaalee ki lúkú, ní ki càkā càkā-dì ki dūu tɔ́ ŋŋmin Seedrɔn tantakalin.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel.
translation_verse: Ama ŋgbantamu pu waatootipaaŋyi kaa nìn kúntì Isirayeel tiŋkin. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Asaa pɔbil nìn bí diba nì ti-Dindaan ní u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
translation_verse: U nìn cáań animbil nì sindaariya nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ u-baa nì úǹ u-ba nìn dūu sú Unimbɔtee ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin.

english_verse: There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
translation_verse: Asaa nín jíń dibeel ki cáá sāā abin aŋmoo kpá imuŋku ili poonee, baa ti gbìl̄ kujaau pu.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Niinee ní Asaa lēē animbil nì sindaariya un nìn bí kunimbɔtidii nimbikpaafidiikun nì ubɔti nimbikpaafidiikunee ki tīī u-tɔntɔnliibi bí cáá cùnnì Damaasi kí tīī Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi, kí tùkù-u yii:

english_verse: “I think we should sign a peace treaty, just as our fathers did. This silver and gold is a present for you. Would you please break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: «Yàntī mpèé ń nīn bí man nì sii kansikin kii an nín nìn bí man baa nì sii baa kansikin puee. Kpèè animbil nì sindaariya ní m tú bí cáań kí tīī-si nee. Míǹ puee cùú kpìtī mpèé ŋun bí si nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Bayeesa kansikinee ú taa ti dāan̄ kí já nì mi.»

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept.
translation_verse: Been-Adaadi nìn gbìl̄ ki tīī nì ubɔti Asaa ní ki dū u-janjakpilib ki tú bi cūtìi jáń nì Isirayeel timmu. Bi nìn jáń ki fōō Iyɔn nì Daani nì Abeel-Mayiim-Maaka timmu nì Neefitalii naakookun timmu mun kɔkɔ poon bi nìn sīintí tijinee.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
translation_verse: Bayeesa nín gbìl̄ tibɔti gbantee ní u gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi māā Raama timbiliiki gundi.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood. Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Asaa yōoǹ Juuda yab kɔkɔ ní bi cūtìi kóoǹ ataŋkpee nì idɔ in Bayeesa nìn cáa bíi māā Raama gundee ki cáań. Ubɔti Asaa nìn dūu máń digundi ki tú Geeba nì Miisipa timmu. Asaa pīiǹ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananii kudii

english_verse: Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said: You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananii dɔ́miń ki ká Juuda bɔtiu Asaa ní ki bí-u yii: «An nín bàà sá á nyàab̀ dijòońdi ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ceeyee, a cūtìi nyàab̄ dijòońdi Siirii bɔtiu cee. A nín ŋá mimmee puee, Siirii bɔtiu janjaliibi ŋmátìi nyáń a-ŋaan.

english_verse: Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them.
translation_verse: Eetiiyoopii yab nì Liibii yab janjaliibi nì bi-tɔrɔkub nì bi-tanjakaliibi nìn wīikí ní tikpil tikpil. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, a nín nìn dū a-mákal ki páaǹ ti-Dindaan puee, u nìn dū-bi ki ŋá a-ŋaan.

english_verse: The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nimbiliŋ làaǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu kí tíkiń bin néeń-u nì bi-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔee ní. Min bí neeyee, a ŋá kii ugbaanee, ní kí yòon̄ kɔŋkɔnnee kí nīn cée, kujaau poon ní a làá nīn kíǹ ki bí.»

english_verse: When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people. Asa Dies (
translation_verse: Asaa nìn gíí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu pu diŋuul ní ki cúú-u ki pīiǹ kudii. Di sá yii tin Ananii nìn sòon̄ee nìn yāntì u gíí diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. Ŋyunti gbanti ní Asaa kíĺ ki kíǹ ki wɔ́b́ samaa kansikin binib biba. Asaa beel nín kúntì puee (Kpèè

english_verse: Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Atuun ŋin kɔkɔ Asaa túńee kí yòon̄ apeekaa kí cáá sāā aluŋkikaayee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi nì Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔntin.

english_verse: In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Asaa nín jíń dibeel dibindi diba kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní u búŋkì ní u-taaŋi dūu fàl̄. Ama u-weeŋyi gbanti poonee, waa nìn nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan jòońdi, see binyɔɔdambi.

english_verse: Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_verse: Bi nìn síb́-u dikaakul din úǹ u-ba yāntì bi gbìn̄ Daafiidi Tiŋkinee poon ní. Bi nìn bɔ́ntì talaalub ki páaǹ kilambaŋ kin pu bi dū-u ki bíl̀ee, ní ki nyàab̄ ikpafi in sɔ́fèe ki ŋmītì u-wunti an taa sūū. Bi nìn tūū talaalub tikpil ki tīī-u tinyool.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king and strengthened his defenses against Israel.
translation_verse: Asaa jipɔɔn Joosafaati fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn bɔ́ntì u-janjaliibi kí ŋmā kí jáǹ Isirayeel beel.

english_verse: He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
translation_verse: U nìn dū bijanjaliibi ki síiǹ Juuda timmu mun bi nìn máń agun ki túee kɔkɔ poon, ní ki nìn kāaǹ gɔmina Juuda nì Eefiraayiim timmu mun u-baa nìn jáń ki fōōyee.

english_verse: and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Joosafaati beel mpɔn ní Juuda yab kɔkɔ nìn cāabìń tiwan ki pūǹ-u. U nìn dūu kpántì ugaajakpaan ki ká tinyool tikpil.

english_verse: he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
translation_verse: U nìn dū u-pɔbil kɔkɔ ki tīī ki nóó ti-Dindaan, ní ki nìn kúntì iwaatootipaan in pu bi nìn tòotī awaayee nì diwaal Aseera ŋgbantamu puee nì iwindɔ Juuda tiŋkin.

english_verse: Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along.
translation_verse: U nìn yāntì Leefii yab biba céeǹ-bi. Bíǹ di sá Seemayawuu nì Neetaniyawuu nì Seebadiyawuu nì Asayeel nì Seemiiramooti nì Yoonatan nì Adooniyasi nì Toobiyawuu nì Toob-Adooniya. Bisaraaŋaliibi bili biba mun nìn kútì bi-pu, bíǹ di sá Eeliisama nì Yooram.

english_verse: They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yōoǹ ti-Dindaan Marau gbɔŋku ní ki yìin̄ Juuda timmu kɔkɔn ki dàkā mu-nib ti-Dindaan marau. Joosafaati pɔŋŋu

english_verse: The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat.
translation_verse: Abee ŋin nìn bí ki māntìi tú Juuda tiŋkee nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan, ní báà ubɔ kaa nìn kíikí kí jáǹ Joosafaati.

english_verse: Philistines brought him silver and other gifts to keep peace. Some of the Arab people brought him
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab gba nìn cāabìń tiwampɔkaal nì animbil nì patantib ki tìì Joosafaati. Bilaalibub mun nìn cāabìń tiwaŋkuti ki pūǹ-u. Bi nìn cáań ipijaa kutukub biluli nì alaataa aluli nì iŋɔjaa kutukub biluli.

english_verse: where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers
translation_verse: U nìn kpáafì tijin tikpil tikpil Juuda timmun. U nìn dū bijanjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee ki kāaǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans. Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had
translation_verse: U nìn yākatì bijanjaliibi gbanti akiti akiti ki nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋi. Juuda naakookunee, bin nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutukub kutukubee sɔ̀. Ujanjakpil Adina nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee kutukub alaataa ata,

english_verse: Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with
translation_verse: Utataati di sá Sikirii jipɔɔn Amaseeyaawuu. Úǹ nìn dū u-ba ki tīī kí tɔ̄ ti-Dindaan tundi. U nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutukub alaataa ali ní.

english_verse: Eliada was a brave warrior who commanded the troops from Benjamin. He had
translation_verse: Beenjameen naakookunee, ubaatandaan ubɔ nìn bí bi yíì-u Eeliyadaa. Úǹ di nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi bin jáà nì abaatan nì agbampɔɔyee binib kutukub alaataa ali.

english_verse: These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
translation_verse: Bijanjaliibi bin nìn bí ubɔti tundin Jeerusaleemee dee. Bijanjaliibi bin ubɔti nìn dūu kāaǹ Juuda timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee poon kaa kútì.

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab nì Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nín cá kí já nì Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee.

english_verse: One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead,
translation_verse: Abin aba boonee ní Joosafaati cūtìi māntì Akaab pu Samaarii tiŋkin. Akaab nìn kūū ipii nì inaa kupaau ki fōō u nì bin céeǹní-uee kucaŋu. U nìn páb́-u yii ú kūtì u-pu bí cùú já nì Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadee.

english_verse: But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Joosafaati gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Tí bàlifì ti-Dindaan kí wàatī.»

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Ama ní Joosafaati gíti bālifì yii: «Mimmee báà ti-Dindaan bɔnaatiliu ubɔ gíti kpá doo tí ŋmā kí cù u-cee kí bàlifì kí béé ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ pueeee?»

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel bɔtiu yíiń u-kàlinjau ubɔ ní ki bí-u yii: «Cùú cáań Yiimila jipɔɔn Miika doo malaa!»

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔtiu nì Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nìn kā báà ŋma u-beejal pu Samaarii tiŋki punyɔkɔki caŋin ki pēē bi-beebɔkutiŋ. Bibɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ nìn bí ki nàatī tibɔti bi-nimbiin.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Keenaana jipɔɔn Siideekiyawuu nìn dū tikúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ ŋyin. U nìn bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Nì ŋyin nee ní a làá dūú jáǹ Siirii yab kí céetí-bi múb.>»

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Un bi tú ú cùú yíiń Miikayee bàn̄ee ní ki bí-u yii: «Kpèè, Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ ŋá kinyɔɔbaantii ki sòoǹ ki nàatī ubɔti tiŋan ŋma ní. Si mun yaa bàn̄ee, á sòoǹ kí nàatī ubɔti tin ŋān̄ee ŋma kii bin béeyee.»

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Ama ní Miika kíí-u yii: «Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee puee, tin ti-Dindaan yaa tīī-mi ḿ nàatēe, tíǹ ní m làá nàatī.»

english_verse: Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
translation_verse: U bāań ubɔti ceeyee ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Miika, tí cùú já kí fōō Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkineeyaaa, tí taa cù?» Ní Miika kíí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá! A làá já kí fōō-kì! Ti-Dindaan dū kitiŋ gbanti ki ŋá a-ŋaan.»

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Ama ní ubɔti gíti bí-u yii: «Ŋfunyɔm miŋa ní m máaǹ kí yàntī á pùtī kí tùkù-mi ibaamɔn ti-Dindaan yindi pu ní á nín tùkù-mi ní?»

english_verse: Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Miika bí yii: «M ká Isirayeel nibul yàl̄ ki gbí ajoon pu kii ipii in kaa cáá ukpaalee Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Baa ti cáá ukpil. Báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-dumpu nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.>»

english_verse: Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu bí Joosafaati yii: «M bàà tùkū-si yii bee! Waa pée nàatī tin ŋān̄ee kí tīī-mi, see tikpitil!»

english_verse: Micaiah replied: I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Ama ní Miika gíti bí-u yii: «Too! Pīlifì tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ee. M ká ti-Dindaan kā u-beejal pu ní yilpu janjaliibi yú ki kɔ́ĺ-u, biba yú u-ŋaŋgiil pú ní bin kíǹee yú u-ŋaŋgan pú.

english_verse: The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?” They talked about it for a while,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Ŋma ní m làá nín ká ú cùú ŋmàtiǹ Akaab kí yàntī ú cùú já nì Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee bí kpɔ̀-u ní?> Niinee ní ubɔ ń bí yii tina, ní un kíǹee ń bí yii tina.

english_verse: then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.” “How?” the Lord asked.
translation_verse: An ŋá mimmee ní ŋfam miba dɔ́miń ki síl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ní ki bí yii: <Man di làá cù kí ŋmàtiǹ-u.> Ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-mì yii: <A làá ŋá mana ní?>

english_verse: “I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.” “Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
translation_verse: Ní mì kíí yii: <M làá cù kí kɔ́ bibɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔn ní kí yàntī bí sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti kí tùkù ubɔti.> Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mì yii: <A làá cùú ŋmàtiǹ-u ní m nyí yii a làá ŋmā. Nín̄ cá kí ŋá míǹ.>

english_verse: Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Keenaana jipɔɔn Siideekiyawuu sútì ki pìl̄ Miika ní ki fáá-u ntampa ki lī yii: «La pú ní ti-Dindaan Fam nyáń m-ni ki cūtìi bíi sòoǹ nì si?»

english_verse: Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
translation_verse: Ní Miika kíí yii: «Tiŋman, ŋwiin ŋun ní a yaa láa sáń ki póotí adiin ki bāal̀ee, a làá dāá gbìl̄ taapu.»

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Isirayeel bɔtiu tīī mara yii: «Ní cúúmaan Miika kí cùnnì kí tīī Amɔn tiŋki kɔmandaŋwu nì ubɔti jipɔɔn Yoowasi,

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: ní kí tùkù-bi yii: <Man ubɔti di bí yii, ní dū kijapaai nee kí tɔ̄ sarka. Ní tīī-u tijin ŋwaam pu nì nnyim kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun m làá fàtīí gítiń nì ŋgbansɔŋfee.>»

english_verse: Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!” Ahab Dies at Ramoth (
translation_verse: Ní Miika bí-u yii: «A yaa fātìi gítìń nì laafiyee, mimmee ti-Dindaan kaa dī m-pu ki sòon̄ dee.» Ní u gíti kútì yii: «Nimbi samaa kɔkɔ, pīlifìmaan!» Bi kūū ubɔti Akaab dikɔ̀ndin (Kpèè

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu bí Joosafaati yii: «M làá kpántí m-wampeeŋkaati bí taa béé-mi ní kí cùú já kujaau. Ama siiyee, dū a-beebɔkutil kí pèen̄.» Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu lafun kpántì u-wampeeŋkaati bí taa béé-u ní ki cūtìi bíi jáà.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop.
translation_verse: An pu ní bin kpèé janjatɔrɔkub kpilibee nín ká Joosafaatee, bi bí yii: «Báà an ŋá pu, Isirayeel bɔtiu dee», ní bi fātì bi-ba ki túĺ-u ki bíi jáà nì u, ní Joosafaati kíĺ ki bíi kūuntí.

english_verse: And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bijanjakpilibee nín béè yii an kaa sá Isirayeel bɔtiu ní bi yāntì-u kaa tí bíi jì-u.

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Ama Siirii yab janjaliu ubɔ pée tɔ́ mpiin yìkíl̄ yikil ní an cūtìi yá Isirayeel bɔtiu laakin u-gbampɔɔl janliitiliŋ tūū tɔbee. Ní ubɔti bí un ŋàal̀ u-tɔrɔkuuee yii: «Fàtīí gítí a-boon tí nyā dikɔmbool pu, di sá m ká tiweendi.»

english_verse: The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_verse: Ama ŋwiin gbantee, kujaau nín nìn pɔ́ɔkì puee, bi nìn yāntì ubɔti yú u-tɔrɔkuu poon ki túĺ Siirii yab áli kujoou, ní u kpíì.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nìn fātìi gítì Jeerusaleem nì ŋgbampɔn.

english_verse: But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said: By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you!
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeewuu, Ananii jipɔɔn nìn túŋkì-u nsanni ní ki bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní a cūtìi tútúǹ unikpiti? Mimmee sii néeń bin ná ti-Dindaaneeee? Kun ní a ŋée puee, ti-Dindaan gíí a-pu diŋuul.

english_verse: But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord. Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee a túń atummɔnti. A wùn̄ diwaal Aseera windɔi Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔn ní ki nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan nì dipɔbil diba.»

english_verse: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
translation_verse: Joosafaati nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní. Ama u nìn yìiǹ Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔ pu kí yòon̄ Beerseeba kí tin cáá sāā Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu. U nìn sòoǹ nì binib bí fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu cee.

english_verse: He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah
translation_verse: Juuda timmu mun bi nìn máń agun ki túee kɔkɔ poonee, u nìn kāaǹ bibɔsoonliibi.

english_verse: and told them: Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide.
translation_verse: U nìn bí-bi yii: «Ní tɔ̄maan ni-tundi tiŋan. Di sá yii an kaa sá nniyaamin ní ni làá dūú sòoǹ tibɔti, ama nì ti-Dindaan yindi pu ní ni làá dūú sòoǹ. Ni yaa láa bíi sòoǹ tibɔtee, úǹ u-ba làá dāá nīn bí ni-cee.

english_verse: So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, ní yàntī ti-Dindaan faaŋku ń nīn bí ni-ni. Ní nīn ŋúb́ tin m tùkū-ni nee kí ŋámaan míǹ. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kaa gèetíǹ bin kaa sòoǹ tibɔti nì ibaamɔnee, àá bin pɔ̀ gandee, àá bin fòol̄ dinyɔɔŋeebil jim kí sòoǹ kí pɔ̀ ubɔee.»

english_verse: Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ki kpáaǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, Joosafaati nìn lēē Leefii yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib biba ki kāaǹ bí nīn sòoǹ tibɔti ti-Dindaan yindi pu, ní kí nīn ŋáŋkí Jeerusaleem yab bɔti.

english_verse: The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
translation_verse: Tí dūú ŋmàntī yii ni-nabiyaamu nyánní ntimu mun poon ní bi kóòyee ki cáań-ni tibɔti ní sòoǹ. An ŋūǹ kí nīn sá nnikpaakoon bɔti, àá mara bɔti, àá abɔkpaa bɔti, àá akoobil bɔti tiba. Too an yaa pée sá tiŋyee, ní dàkà-bi tin bi máaǹ kí ŋée. Mimmee baa làá yìntīǹ ti-Dindaan ní waa nín gíí ni-pu àá ni-nabiyaamu pu diŋuul. Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, naa làá fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Amariyawuu di làá nīn kpèé dinimbɔtinool bɔti ki tìì-ni. Juuda beel kàlinjakpiliu Seebadiyawuu, Isimaayeel jipɔɔn di làá nīn kpèé dibeel pu bɔti. Leefii yab làá nīn bí ni-cee ki tútúǹ-ni ni kpèé kitiŋ pu bɔti. Ní kámaan dipɔbil kí tɔ̄ ni-tundi! Ti-Dindaan ń nīn bí bin ŋáań tiŋanee cee.»

english_verse: Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
translation_verse: Ní bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Joosafaati yii: «Dijanjakitikpaandi diba dòoń kí jáǹ-si. Dì nyánní Ŋyaam Mɔɔgbandi lapu yal pú, an dàkà yii Eedoom tiŋkin. Dì bāań Asasɔn-Tamaar, an dàkà yii Eeni-Geedii.»

english_verse: Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Joosafaati nìn fāŋkì, ní ki nìn lēē yii u làá mēē ti-Dindaan. U nìn tīī mara yii Juuda beel kɔkɔn bí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ.

english_verse: They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
translation_verse: Juuda yab nìn nyánní Juuda timmu kɔkɔn ki kóoǹ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem kí mèè ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard
translation_verse: Joosafaati nìn yíkìi yúl̀ Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab kansikin, ti-Dindaan Diikun ki túĺ Dicimpɔndi.

english_verse: and prayed: You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you.
translation_verse: U nìn bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ti-baabi Nimbɔtiu, sii di bí yilpu ní ki jīǹ atimbun kɔkɔ pu dibeel. Sii di cáá mpɔn nì dikpabil ní ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí sīĺ a-nimbiin kí jáǹ-si.

english_verse: Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever.
translation_verse: Sii ti-Nimbɔtiu di nìn jìn̄ kitiŋ nee pu nib ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab, a-nibul nìn dòońee. A dū kitiŋ nee ki tīī a-bɔɔ Abraam naantiibi kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kāl̀ kitiŋee poon ní ki máń-si ŋkɔŋkoon ki lī yii:

english_verse: They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
translation_verse: <Nnaabu ŋubɔ yaa jéetì ti-pu, an ŋūǹ kí nīn sá yii kujaau, àá ditafadaaldi diba àá bìlbil kúm àá ŋkùm, ti làá dāan̄ kí yūĺ ŋkɔŋkoon nee nyɔkɔpu, an dàkà yii a-nimbiin, di sá yii niin ní a lèekī a-ba ki dàkà. Ti làá kúuǹ kí yíiń-si ti-nimbinaamandi poon. Niinee, a làá pīlifiǹ-ti ní kí fīī-ti.>

english_verse: You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed.
translation_verse: Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì Eedoom yab dɔ́miń kí já nì ti. Ti-naanjab nín nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dòońee, aa nìn pú-bi nsan bí dī bi-tiŋki pu. An puee ti-baabi nìn dūu dī nsan ŋubɔ fám ní ki yāntì-bi kaa kūū ki céetì-bi.

english_verse: Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us.
translation_verse: Ama kpèè binib gbanti nín bíi pà-ti tipaal tiŋyee! Bi dɔ́miń kí jà-ti kitiŋ kin a dūu tīī-tee pu.

english_verse: Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
translation_verse: Ti-Nimbɔtiu, mimmee aa làá dáaĺ bi-tafalaaa? Di sá yii binib bin dòoń kí já nì ti nee wīikí tikpil ní taa cáá mpɔn kí ŋmā kí sīĺ bi-nimbiin. Taa nyí ti nín làá ŋá puee, ama ti-nimbikpeeŋu cɔ́ a-pu ní.»

english_verse: While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple,
translation_verse: Juuda yab kɔkɔ, ki kpáaǹ bi-nimpoobi nì bi-biyaamu nìn yú ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Ti-Dindaan tīī Juuda yab dijajil

english_verse: Then Jahaziel said: Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side!
translation_verse: Yasiyeel nìn bí yii: «Nimbi Juuda yab, Jeerusaleem yab nì sii ubɔti Joosafaati, ní pīlifìmaan! Ti-Dindaan nín bíi sòoǹ nì ni puee sèé: <Ni-pɔbiliŋ ń taa bīil̀, kí taa fàŋkì dijanjakitikpaandi nee, di sá yii kujaau nee kaa sá ni-jaaku, ama an sá man ni-Nimbɔtiu jaaku ní.

english_verse: So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley.
translation_verse: Foolee, ní fu cùú já nì bi. Bi bíi dàb̀ Nsupumpukum gbantaŋki. Ni làá fu ká-bi ditantakal nín kúntí puee, Yeeruweel teeku nyɔkɔpu.
