english_verse: You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
translation_verse: An kaa fu bàlifī ní já nì bi. Nimbi dee, ní fu nyā kí yūĺ kí kpèè dijajil din ti-Dindaan làá fu tīī-nee. Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab, ni-pɔbiliŋ ń taa bīil̀, ní taa fàŋkì! Foolee, ní fu nyā kí tūŋkì-bi, man ni-Dindaan làá fu nín̄ bí ni-cee.>»

english_verse: Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Leefii yab bin sá Keeyaati nì Kooree maaliŋunee yíkìi yúl̀. Bi nìn gāā ilan mpɔn ki nyɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.”
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní bi-kɔkɔ kíĺ nsan ki nín cá Teekoowa teekun. Kí wàatī bí yīkèe ní Joosafaati bí-bi yii: «Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab, ní pīlifìmaan. Ní nīn máká ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu pu, ní ubɔ kaa làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-ni! Ní nīn máká u-bɔnaatiliibi pu ní kí ká dijajil!»

english_verse: Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing: “Praise the Lord! His love never ends.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u nì samaa sòon̄ ki bɔ́ntì ní ki lēē bilaŋgaaliibi ki dū circir bɔkutiŋ ki pēeǹ-bi ní bíǹ līī dijanjakitil nyɔkɔpu ki gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan u nín sá circir ki sá ukpaan puee ki lì yii: «Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan, di sá yii u-neendi bí ní ki cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
translation_verse: Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nìn bíi jáà nì Seeyiir jool yab ní ki kūū ki céetì-bi múb. Míǹ boonee ní bi nyáń tɔb pu ki kūū ki céetì tɔb.

english_verse: When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Juuda yab jɔ́m̀ laakin bi ŋūǹ kí tɔ́kɔń kí wāl̀ kuteeu puee ki kpēē dijanjakitikpaandi watil púee, anikpil ŋmaniŋma di dɔ̄ kitiŋ fìlfilee. Uniseen kaa nìn kíǹ.

english_verse: Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
translation_verse: Ŋwinnanaati dalee ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì Beeraka tantakalin kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan. An pu ní bi pú ditantakal gbanti diyindi yii Beeraka, taapu sá yii «si nì ditundi».

english_verse: When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid
translation_verse: Atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee beeŋi nìn gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín jáń nì Isirayeel nannanliibi puee, bi nìn fāŋkì tikpil.

english_verse: to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace. Jehoshaphat Dies (
translation_verse: Joosafaati beel nìn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin, di sá yii u-Nimbɔtiu nìn tīī-u diŋuŋfil ijaan kɔkɔ pu. Joosafaati beel nín kúntì puee (Kpèè

english_verse: While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel.
translation_verse: Kí kūtèe, Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nìn ŋá mpèé nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Akasiyasi. Ubɔti gbanti bimbim kaa nìn ŋān̄.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done,
translation_verse: U nìn nóó u-baa Asaa tabɔbiliŋ ní deedee, ní ki nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ama waa nìn gbáń ki kpītì isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu puee, ní samaa kaa nìn nóó bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu nì dipɔbil diba.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Joosafaati tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee kí yòon̄ ŋi nín kíĺ puee kí cáá sāā ŋi nín kúntì puee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Ananii jipɔɔn Yeewuu gbɔntin. Bi nìn dū tigbɔn gbanti ki sákaǹ Isirayeel bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliyeeseer, Doodafa jipɔɔn un sá Mareesa tiŋkinee nìn fōō tibɔti ki nāatì Joosafaati yii: «A nín ŋá pu ní a nì Akasiyasi ŋá mpèéyee, ti-Dindaan bíil̀ ditundi din ní a túńee.» Tiŋman míǹ ní an lafun jítì, meelabee nìn bíil̀ kaa ŋúń ki cūtì Taarsiisi.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Joosafaati kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabee ní bi síb́-u ki kɔ́ĺ-bi, Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Jooram di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Jooram beel (Kpèè

english_verse: King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah.
translation_verse: Joosafaati jipɔɔn Jooram nìn cáá naalib pēē baa. Bíǹ di sá Asariya nì Yeeyiyeel nì Seekariyawuu nì Asariyawuu nì Miikayeel nì Seefatiyawuu.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_verse: Jooram beel yuntiŋu ní Eedoom yab yíkì kaa kíí bi-ba pu kí nīn gbíntìi bí Juuda yab taapu ní ki kāaǹ bi-ba nì bi-bɔtiu.

english_verse: The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram.
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan yāntì Fiiliistii yab nì Bilaalibub bin kóò ki pìlīǹ Kuusi yabee dɔ́miń kí já nì Jooram.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
translation_verse: Bi-baa Joosafaati nìn púb́-bi animbil nì sindaariya nì tiwan tin cáá kunyampoouee tikpil. U nìn gíti tīī-bi Juuda timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee bí nīn kpòotī. Ama Jooram ní u nìn lēē ú fōō u-yil kí kpántí ubɔti, di sá yii úǹ di nìn sá ujipɔŋkpil.

english_verse: After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders.
translation_verse: Jooram nìn fōō u-baa beel ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki báaǹ inyaan. Míǹ boonee ní u cúú u-naalib kɔkɔ ki lāntì, ki kpáaǹ Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ aba.

english_verse: Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong,
translation_verse: U nìn pée nóó Isirayeel bɔtiibi tabɔbiliŋ ní, a lì kii Akaab dicaŋkun yab nín nìn bí puee, di sá u nìn cáá Akaab bisal ubɔ ní. U nìn ŋá tin kaa nìn kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee.

english_verse: but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi puee, waa nìn là kí nàan̄ Juuda tiŋki, kun puee u nìn pōoǹ Daafiidi yii u-jipɔmbi làá nīn pée kā dibeel pu Jeerusaleem ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night,
translation_verse: Jooram nìn yíkì ki nín cá Seeyiir tiŋkin ki kpáaǹ u-janjatɔrɔkub kɔkɔ. Ama kunyeeuee ní u nì u-janjatɔrɔkub kpootiliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedoom yab bin nìn māntìi tú-bee.

english_verse: but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time. Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ yaadal wiiŋŋu gbanti ní Eedoom yab fōō bi-ba kaa ti bí Juuda yab taapu. Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní Liibina yab mun kaa kíí bi-ba pu.

english_verse: Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
translation_verse: Jooram u-ba nìn máń iwaatootipaan Juuda jooŋŋi pu, ní ki yāntì Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda yab kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ki dū Unimbɔti ki fá.

english_verse: One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said: I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ŋmàn̄-u kugbɔŋu ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan, a-naanja Daafiidi Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Aa dī a-baa Joosafaati tabɔbiliŋ kaa ti dī a-naanja Asaa, Juuda bɔtiu tabɔbiliŋ.

english_verse: Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
translation_verse: Ama a dī Isirayeel yab bɔtiibi saŋŋu ki yāntì Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda yab bíi tòotī awaa kii Akaab dicaŋkun yab nín ŋáań puee. Áli gba a kūū a-naalib bin nìn sɔ́ǹ-see.

english_verse: Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan làá cáań atulim ki tɔ̄ a-nibul nì a-jipɔmbi nì a-nimpoobi nì a-gaajawanti kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
translation_verse: Sii a-bee, tiweeŋkpiil di làá cúú-si, iween in làá ŋmɔ́ kí bà a-nai ní kí nīn púntí-si baabadal áli a-nai ń dāá nyā mpaampiin puee.»

english_verse: They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
translation_verse: Bi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Juuda yab ní ki kɔ́ kitiŋin ki kóoǹ tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ nìn bí ubɔti dicaŋkunee. Bi nìn kpáaǹ u-jipɔmbi nì u-nimpoobi. U-jipɔŋwaaliu Akasiya baba ní bi nìn kíǹ-u.

english_verse: After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì ina weeŋyi in baa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹee dɔ́miń ki cúú-u.

english_verse: About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
translation_verse: An pée bí míǹ ki cá abin ali boonee, iweenee píĺ-u ní u-nai nyáń, ní u dāa kpíì nsansaaŋkúm. U-naacimbi kaa nìn kpāā ŋŋmi ki súń u-kpool kii bi nín nìn ŋá pu ki tīī u-naanjab tinyoolee.

english_verse: and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní Jeewuu bíi dátí Akaab dicaŋku yab tafalee ní ki ká Juuda bɔtibiliŋ nì Akasiyasi nabiyaamu mun bí ubɔti tundinee ní u kūū ki céetì-bi.

english_verse: then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord. There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah. Queen Athaliah of Judah (
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u yāntì bi nyàab̄ Akasiyasi. Bi nìn ká-u u cūtìi bál̀ Samaarii tiŋkin, ní bi cúú-u ki cáań Jeewuu cee ní úǹ kūū-u. Bi nìn síb́-u, di sá yii bi nìn lī yii: «Joosafaati un nìn nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔee jipɔɔn dee.» Ubɔ kaa nìn gíti kíǹ Akasiyasi dicaŋkun kí ŋmā kí kpántí ubɔti. Atalii fōō dibeel mpɔn (Kpèè

english_verse: In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors. Their advice led to his downfall.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee kii Akaab dicaŋkun yabee, di sá yii u-baa kúm boonee, bíǹ di kpántì u-saŋkiliibi ní bi-sansaŋkii gbanti nāaǹ-u.

english_verse: He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Bíǹ di sáŋkì-u ní u nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Jooram, Akaab jipɔɔn cūtìi jáń nì Aram bɔtiu Asayeel, Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee. Ama bi bíi jáàyee ní Aram yab tīī Jooram tiweendi.

english_verse: It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death. When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family,
translation_verse: Akasiyasi nín nìn cūtìi māntì Jooram pu puee ní ti-Dindaan dī an pu ki nāaǹ-u. Di sá u bàn̄ee ní u nì Jooram nyáń kí já nì Nimisii jipɔɔn Jeewuu. Tin waa nyée di sá yii ti-Dindaan di nìn yāntì Jeewuu kpántì ubɔti kí nàan̄ Akaab dicaŋku.

english_verse: but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah.
translation_verse: Ama ubɔti Jooram bisal Yooseeba nìn ŋúń ki yōoǹ Akasiyasi jipɔɔn Joowaasi u-mambi kansikin baa ŋúń ki kūū-u. U nìn cáá kibikee nì ki-bilooliu ki bál̀ kunimbɔtidii didooŋkaaku kubɔn. Míǹ ní ubɔti Jooram bisal Yooseeba un nìn sá usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nimpuu, ki gíti sá Akasiyasi niisalee nìn ŋúń ki fīī kibikee Atalii ŋaan waa kūū-kì.

english_verse: As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that,
translation_verse: Akasiyasi na Atalii nín ká yii u-jipɔɔn kpíìyee ní u lēē yii u làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí ubɔti naantiibi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_verse: Joowaasi nìn bál̀ ti-Dindaan Diikun niin áli abin aluu, ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔee, Atalii di nìn kā dibeel pu.

english_verse: These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Bi nìn yìin̄ Juuda timmu kɔkɔn ki kóoǹ Leefii yab nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib ki kpáfì. Míǹ boonee ní bi nì bi táań ki gítì Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Niinee Yooyadaa nì u-jipɔmbi nyántì Joowaasi. Bi nìn dū kibeefuulii ki cíkiǹ-u ní ki dū dipoondi taŋkpapilinti ki ŋúbiǹ-u. Boonee ní bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki kāaǹ-u tibɔtiil ní ki téeń mpɔn yii: «Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn!»

english_verse: Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple,
translation_verse: Ni nín làá ŋá puee sɔ̀. Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab yaa dɔ́miń kí tɔ̄ ditundi ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaayee, bí ŋá akiti ata ní diba ń nīn cí kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki.

english_verse: Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_verse: ní samaa kɔkɔ kíĺ ki bíi fàal̀. Bi nín kūū Atalii míǹ boonee ní kitiŋ kɔ́ ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_verse: After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
translation_verse: Dibinluluútiil poonee, ní Yooyadaa dàkā tininjati. U nì bijanjakpilib bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee nìn ŋá kunyɔɔbaantii. Bíǹ di sá Yeeroowaam jipɔɔn Asariyawuu nì Yoowanan jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nì Oobeedi jipɔɔn Asariyawuu nì Adaaya jipɔɔn Maaseeyawuu nì Sikirii jipɔɔn Eeliisafaati.

english_verse: and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash. Jehoiada said to them: Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king.
translation_verse: Samaa kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì ti-Dindaan Diikun ní bi nì ubɔti ŋá mpèé. Yooyadaa nìn bí-bi yii: «Ubɔti jipɔɔn sèé. U máaǹ kí jī dibeel kí nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn pōoǹ Daafiidi naantiibi puee.

english_verse: one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards.
translation_verse: Dikitililiitiil làá nīn cí dibeecindi ní ditataatiil ń nīn cí Dinyeel punyɔkɔki. Samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee làá nīn bí ti-Dindaan Diiku cindin.

english_verse: Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa cáá nsan kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diikun, see bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab baba. Bíǹ ŋūǹ kí kɔ́, di sá yii bi dū-bi ki sú ti-Dindaan ní. Samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ puee kí nīn yú mmɔŋki.

english_verse: You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
translation_verse: Leefii yab làá màntīí tū ubɔti báà ŋma ń nīn ŋúb́ u-janjawanti u-ŋaan. Un yaa là kí ŋá mpɔn kí kɔ́née, bí kpɔ̀-u. Laakin kamaa ubɔti yaa cée, bí nīn bí u-cee.»

english_verse: The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty.
translation_verse: Leefii yab nì Juuda yab nìn ŋá kii usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nín nìn tīī-bi mara puee. Ukpil kamaa nìn yōoǹ u-nib, bin tundi nìn kífí ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee nì bin tundi nìn kúntí ŋwiin gbanti dalee, di sá yii Yooyadaa kaa nìn tīī báà dikitil diŋuŋfil.

english_verse: Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders.
translation_verse: U nìn tīī bijanjakpilib bin kpèé bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee ŋkpamu nì ubɔti Daafiidi gbampɔɔŋi ŋin bí a-ba a-ba ki nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee.

english_verse: They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
translation_verse: U nìn yāntì bijanjaliibee kɔkɔ māntìi tú ubɔti ki ŋúb́ bi-janjawanti, ki kíĺ ti-Dindaan Diiku ŋgiil pú ki cáa sāā ŋgan pú, nsaraafan nì kunimbɔtidii caŋin.

english_verse: As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple.
translation_verse: Atalii nín gbìl̄ samaa wooku puee ní u nín cá ti-Dindaan Diiku watil pú, diniwul cee.

english_verse: There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
translation_verse: U kpēēyee, ubɔti di tɔ́kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diiku nyɔkɔpu kɔl puee. Bijanjakpilib nì bikantámbunliibi nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ-u. Samaa kɔkɔ nìn bí mmɔnni ní bikantámbunliibi búǹ akantán, ní bi bɔ̀ɔ́ tiwan ní bilaŋgaaliibi gà ilan. Niinee Atalii cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì ní ki téeń yii: «Bi nyáń m-boon ní! Bi nyáń m-boon ní!»

english_verse: At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!”
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nìn nyántì bijanjakpilib bin kpèé bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee ki bí-bi yii: «Nyāntímaan-u doo! Un di yaa páaǹ u-boonee, bí kpɔ̀-u!» Di sá yii usaraaŋakpil nìn lī yii bí taa kpɔ̀-u ti-Dindaan Diikun doo.

english_verse: She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
translation_verse: Bi nìn cúú Atalii ní ki dáaĺ-u ki cūnnì kubɔtinaakoou watil pú, ní ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ Itaamu punyɔkɔkee ní bi kūū-u niin.

english_verse: Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed,
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nì samaa nì ubɔti nìn ŋá mpèé ki pōoǹ kí nīn kíǹ ki sá ti-Dindaan nibul.

english_verse: then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
translation_verse: Niinee ní samaa kɔkɔ nín cá diwaal Baal diikun ki gbáń ki wīī-ku. Bi nìn gbáń ki wīī Baal saraafaŋyi nì ataŋkpee ŋin nìn bí niin bi tòotēe. Bi nìn kūū Baal tandaaŋwu Matan ki bíl̀ isaraafan nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nìn dū ti-Dindaan Diiku ki ŋúbiǹ bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá Leefii yabee bí nīn cí. Daafiidi nìn kpáfì-bi akiti akiti bí nīn ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ti-Dindaan Diikun, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ ki kā Mooyiisi marau poon puee. U nìn gíti kpáafì-bi yii bí nīn tūǹ ditundi gbanti ki gà ilan nì mmɔn.

english_verse: Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nìn dū bipunyɔɔciitiliibi ki síiǹ bí nīn cí ti-Dindaan Diiku, án nín làá ŋá pu unil un yaa bí tijɔkɔndinee ń taa kɔ́ ku-nee.

english_verse: Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nìn kóoǹ bijanjakpilib nì akpambal nì bikàliŋkpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ ní bi yōoǹ ubɔti ti-Dindaan Diikun, ki dū-u ki dī mpunyɔɔjaati ki cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ dibeecindi. Bi nìn dū-u ki kāaǹ dibeejal pu,

english_verse: and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple. Joash Turns Away from the Lord
translation_verse: Bi nìn síb́-u bibɔtiibi kaakuliŋ diban, Daafiidi Tiŋkin. Di sá yii u nìn ŋá tin ŋān̄ee ki tīī Isirayeel yab nì Unimbɔti nì u-diiku.

english_verse: And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii Atalii, unikpitee nì u-jipɔmbi yāntì kunimbɔtidii bíil̀, áli gba bi yōoǹ circir wanti tin bí kunimbɔtidiinee ki dūu ŋá diwaal Baal tundi.»

english_verse: Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nìn cáá binimpoobi bili ki tīī Joowaasi ní bíǹ màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu.

english_verse: Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Joowaasi lēē u-pɔbilin yii u làá ŋāŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku.

english_verse: He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.” But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders.
translation_verse: U nìn kóoǹ bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab ki kpáfì ní ki bí-bi yii: «Nín cámaan Juuda timmun kí fōō Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ cee animbil kí nīn cáa ŋáŋkí dibindi kamaa ni-Nimbɔtiu Diiku. Ní yáb́ kí tɔ̄ ditundi gbanti.» Ama Leefii yab kaa nìn yáb́ ditundi gbanti pu.

english_verse: So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti yíiń usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa ní ki bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní aa páb́ Leefii yab bí fōō Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab cee lampoo un ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nì Isirayeel samaau nìn gíí bí nīn cáa ŋáŋkí Circir Tantiuee ní?

english_verse: Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn yāntì bi kpáá dakaa ubɔ ki síiǹ a yaa làá kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diikunee caŋin.

english_verse: He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u yāntì bi báakì Juuda nì Jeerusaleem timmun yii: «Ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nìn yóoǹ kuteeun yii Isirayeel yab ń nīn pà lampoo ubɔ. Báà ŋma máaǹ kí cáań lampoo gbantee kí tīī ti-Dindaan.»

english_verse: The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box.
translation_verse: An nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ abɔtibil kɔkɔ nì samaa kɔkɔ ní bi cáań tin bi máaǹ kí cáańee ki ŋá dakaayee poon áli an tin gbí.

english_verse: Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside. This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected.
translation_verse: Bi yaa nìn cáań dakaayee Leefii yab cee bí yūĺ ubɔti yil pu kí kpèèyee, bi nìn kāntí animbil kā poon ki wīikí. Niinee ní bí yíiń ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu nì un kpèé usaraaŋakpil wantee, ní bíǹ ń yòon̄ dakaayee kí kpáatí kí gíiǹ kí síiń u-paaŋŋu. Míǹ ní bi nìn pée ŋáań baabadal ní ki ká animbil tikpil tikpil.

english_verse: These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new.
translation_verse: Bitɔntɔnliibee nìn dūu gùl̄ ditundi pu, ní ditundi nìn bíi cá malaa malaa. Bi nìn fātìi ŋáŋkì Unimbɔti diiku ní ku fātìi ká mpɔn.

english_verse: They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple. Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku ki dóòyee ní bitɔntɔnliibi kpilibee cáań animbil ŋin kíǹee ki tīī ubɔti nì Yooyadaa. Bi nìn dū animbil gbanti ki ŋá ti-Dindaan Diiku wanti tiba mun. Bi nìn dūu ŋá tiwan tin bi cáa tūǹ ti-Dindaan Diikun ditundee nì tin bi cáa ŋáań saraawɔkaayee nì asambil nì sindaariya nì animbil kúti wanti. Yooyadaa maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, bi nìn pée ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ní ti-Dindaan Diikun. Joowaasi kaa ti yú nì Unimbɔti deedee

english_verse: He died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: Yooyadaa nìn púĺ. U nìn cáá abin dilaataal nì mmuŋku nì saalaa ní ki nín kpíì.

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa kúm boonee ní Juuda bɔtibiliŋ dɔ́miń ki tātìi gbāaǹ ubɔti Joowaasi nimbiin ki tīī-u tinyool. Ubɔti nìn pílifiǹ-bi.

english_verse: but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ti-Dindaan nìn tú u-bɔnaatiliibi bi-cee bí sāŋkì-bi kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi nsammɔnti pu, ama baa nìn pílifiǹ-bi.

english_verse: God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti Fam kpákatìń usaraaŋakpil Seekariya, Yooyadaa jipɔɔn pu, ní úǹ nyáń samaa pu ki bí-bi yii: «Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ba pu ní ni bíi yìntī ni-Dindaan marab? An kaa làá bútí-ni! Kii ni nín dū Unimbɔti ki fée puee, u mun dū-ni ki fá!>»

english_verse: In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus.
translation_verse: Dibindi dāa fātìi túee ní Aram yab janjaliibi dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Joowaasi. Bi nìn jáń ki fōō Juuda timmu nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Bi nìn sákatì abɔtibilee kɔkɔ samaa kansikin ki kūū, ní ki dū tiwan tin bi fúkúl̀ee kɔkɔ ki tú bi cáa cūnnì ki tīī bi-bɔtiu Damaasi tiŋkin.

english_verse: The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
translation_verse: Aram janjaliibi bin nìn dɔ́mińee kaa nìn pée náaǹ, ama ti-Dindaan nìn dū Juuda yab janjakitil dikpaandee ki ŋá bi-ŋaan, di sá yii bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu ki fá. Bi nìn ŋá míǹ kí dáaĺ Joowaasi tafal ní.

english_verse: The History of the Kings also tells more about the sons of Joash, what the prophets said about him, and how he repaired the temple. Amaziah son of Joash became king after his father's death.
translation_verse: Joowaasi jipɔmbi nì bi nín fōō Unimbɔti cee tibɔti tin ki nāatì-uee nì u nín ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku puee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā bibɔtiibi gbɔŋkun. U-jipɔɔn Amasiyaawuu di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: One of God's prophets said, “Your Majesty, don't let these Israelite soldiers march into battle with you. The Lord has refused to help anyone from the northern kingdom of Israel,
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ nìn dɔ́miń ki tùkū-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, taa yàntī Isirayeel janjaliibi ń táá-si kí cù kujaau, di sá yii ti-Dindaan kaa bí Isirayeel yab bin bi gíti yíì yii Eefiraayiim yab nee cee.

english_verse: Amaziah replied, “What am I supposed to do about all the silver I paid those troops?” “The Lord will give you back even more than you paid,” the prophet answered.
translation_verse: Ní Amasiyaawuu bālifì Unimbɔti niliuee yii: «Kin animbil kúti tɔɔnib bita bin m dūu tīī Isirayeel janjaliibee làá kúntí nì yii ba?» Ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan làá tīī-si tin jítiǹ mimmee kpataaa pu!»

english_verse: After Amaziah got his courage back, he led his troops to Salt Valley, where he killed
translation_verse: Amasiyaawuu nìn ká kunyannyaau ní ki yōoǹ u-janjaliibi ki cūnnì Ŋyaam tantakalin. Niin ní bi jáń ki kūū Seeyiir yab binib kutukub saalaa.

english_verse: But before the prophet finished speaking, Amaziah interrupted and said, “You're not one of my advisors! Don't say another word, or I'll have you killed.” The prophet stopped. But then he added, “First you sinned and now you've ignored my warning. It's clear that God has decided to punish you!” Israel Defeats Judah (
translation_verse: U dáá bíi sòoǹ u-nyɔkɔ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «Ti lēē-si á nīn sá ubɔti saŋkiliuaaa? A yaa kaa là bí gbá-see, á ŋmīĺ niin.» Ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee ŋmíl̀, ama ní ki lī yii: «M nyí yii Unimbɔti lēē kí nàan̄-si, kun puee a ŋá tin bí nee kaa pílifì m-saŋkii.»

english_verse: King Amaziah of Judah talked with his officials, then sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Amasiyaawuu fōō u-saŋkiliibi cee tin u máaǹ kí ŋée ní ki tú binib bí cùú tùkù Isirayeel bɔtiu Joowaasi un gíti sá Joowakaasi jipɔɔn nì Jeewuu naantiiuee yii: «Dāan̄, man nì si tí já!»

english_verse: Jehoash sent back a reply that said: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon arranged the marriage between his son and the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu Joowaasi tú bí cùú tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Amasiyaawuu yii: «Bukuŋkumbu subiki kiba di nìn bí Leebanɔn jool pu. Dalbee ní kì cūtìi ká seedir subu ní ki bí-bu yii: <Dū a-bisal kí tīī m-jipɔɔn ú cáá!> Ama upeel ubɔ nyánní Leebanɔn joolee puee ní ki tāā ki mátì bukuŋkumbuee.

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. But stay at home and do your celebrating. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Tiŋman a jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedoom yabee ní an yòontí-si. Nín̄ kā a-dumpu soooo kí nīn fàal̀ a-jajil gbanti pu. Ba pu ní a là kí kíĺ kujaau kun poon ní bi làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ sii nì Juuda janjaliibee?»

english_verse: so Jehoash led his army to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Niinee Isirayeel bɔtiu Joowaasi yíkìń kujaau pu ki bāań ki dūu sìkī nì Juuda bɔtiu Amasiyaawuu Beeti-Seemeesi tiŋkin, Juuda tiŋki kiban.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Juuda yab, ní bíǹ sáǹ ki nín kùǹ.

english_verse: and Jehoash captured Amaziah. Jehoash took Amaziah with him when he went to attack Jerusalem. Jehoash broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔtiu nìn cúú Juuda bɔtiu, Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn, Yoowakasi naantiiu Amasiyaawuu kuyuŋu Beeti-Seemeesi tiŋkin. U nìn gíiǹ-u Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. U nìn gbáń ki wīī digundi an wāā kii meetab alaataa ali kí yòon̄ Eefiraayiim punyɔkɔki kí cáá sāā Ŋfaŋfakam punyɔkɔki.

english_verse: He carried away the gold, the silver, and all the valuable furnishings from God's temple where the descendants of Obed-Edom stood guard. He robbed the king's treasury, took hostages, then returned to Samaria. Amaziah Is Killed (
translation_verse: U nìn yōoǹ sindaariya nì animbil nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikun Oobeedi-Eedoom kpèéyee, nì tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ nìn bí dibeecindinee. U nìn cúú binib biba mun ki kpáàa búntì Samaarii tiŋkin. Amasiyaawuu beel nín kúntì puee (Kpèè

english_verse: Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Amasiyaawuu tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, apeekaa kí cáá sāā aluŋkikaa, ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi nì Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah started disobeying the Lord, some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti ŋun ní Amasiyaawuu fātì u-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaanee, ní bi bɔ́ntì u-pu kí kpɔ̀-u Jeerusaleem ní u sáǹ ki nín cá Lakiisi. Bi nìn tú binib jìn̄ u-boon ki tin kūuń-u niin.

english_verse: His body was taken to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
translation_verse: Boonee ní bi dū-u ki ŋá tɔrɔku un itaamu dátée ki gíiǹní Jeerusaleem, ní bi dū-u ki síb́ u-baabi kaakulin, Daafiidi Tiŋkin.

english_verse: Uzziah supplied his army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and stones used for slinging.
translation_verse: Bi yaa nìn cá kujaau kamaayee, ubɔti nìn tìì-bi agbampɔɔ nì ŋkpamu nì njanjafuulimu nì ajanjabɔkuti nì itɔfi nì tijaataafun taŋkpeeŋi.

english_verse: Uzziah had leprosy the rest of his life. He was no longer allowed in the temple or in his own palace. That's why his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Oosiyasi nìn kpántì unyaŋgbanti áli u-kúm dal. U-nyaŋgbandi gbanti puee, u nìn kóò kudii kubɔn laaba ní u-jipɔɔn Yootam un nìn sá bin kpèé dibeecindi kpiliuee kpòotī kitiŋ.

english_verse: Everything else Uzziah did while he was king is in the records written by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya, Amɔtisi jipɔɔn nìn ŋmàn̄ u-tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee kí yòon̄ tipeekaal kí cáá sāā tiluŋkikaal.

english_verse: After the death of King Amaziah, the people of Judah crowned his son Uzziah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Oosiyasi nìn cáá abin saalku nì diba ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel abin imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì ali. U-na nìn sá Jeerusaleem ní bi yíì-u yii Yeekooliya.

english_verse: Uzziah became proud of his power, and this led to his downfall. One day, Uzziah disobeyed the Lord his God by going into the temple and burning incense as an offering to him.
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun ní Oosiyasi ká mpɔn mimmee ní dilambil jítìi kɔ́ ki nāaǹ-u. Waa nìn gíti yú nì ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu deedee. Dalbee ní u jítìi kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diikun kí tūū talaalutuukaa talaalu saraafaŋŋu pu.

english_verse: He obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee, kii u-baa Amasiyaawuu nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedee. Oosiyasi yúl̀ Unimbɔti deedee, ní ki dāa yīntiǹ-u

english_verse: While Uzziah was king, he started a war against the Philistines. He smashed the walls of the cities of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, then rebuilt towns around Ashdod and in other parts of Philistia.
translation_verse: Oosiyasi nìn cūtìi jáń nì Fiiliistii yab. U nìn gbáń ki wīī agun ŋin bi nìn máń ki tú Gaati nì Yabinee nì Asidoodi timmuee. Míǹ boonee ní u fātìi máń agun ki tú ntimu mun bí Asidoodi kpaanceetiiyee nì Fiiliistii yab tiŋki laakin kíǹee.

english_verse: Even the Ammonites paid taxes to Uzziah. He became very powerful, and people who lived as far away as Egypt heard about him.
translation_verse: Meewun yab nìn pà lampoo ki tìì Oosiyasi. Oosiyasi nìn ká mpɔn ní u-yindi gbītì ki tin bàn̄ áli Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: In Jerusalem, Uzziah built fortified towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and the place where the city wall turned inward.
translation_verse: Oosiyasi nìn máń Jeerusaleem sintil difɔkɔŋi Ŋfaŋfakam punyɔkɔki yilpu nì Ditantakal punyɔkɔki yilpu nì digundi faŋfakam yilpu.

english_verse: He also built defense towers out in the desert. He owned such a large herd of livestock in the western foothills and in the flatlands, that he had cisterns dug there to catch the rainwater. He loved farming, so he had crops and vineyards planted in the hill country wherever there was fertile soil, and he hired farmers to take care of them.
translation_verse: U nìn gíti máń adifɔkɔ kuteeu pu ní ki gbìn̄ anyimbɔbil kupaau, di sá yii u nìn cáá tiwaŋkuti tikpil Seefeelaa nì kitimpiliŋ pu. U nìn cáá bikpaabi bí ajoon pu nì Kaarmeel ki kù u-satin nì u-fiinyi kpaaŋŋin, di sá yii u nìn néeń tikpaal bɔti.

english_verse: Uzziah's army was always ready for battle. Jeiel and Maaseiah were the officers who kept track of the number of soldiers, and these two men were under the command of Hananiah, one of Uzziah's officials.
translation_verse: Oosiyasi nìn cáá bijanjaliibi bin nìn ŋūǹ kí cù kujaau kí jée. Ubɔti janjakpilib kansikin un bi yíì Ananiyawuuyee di nìn kpēē bigbaŋŋmaliibi Yeeyiyeel nì Maaseeyawuu ní bi kàan̄-bi ki yākatì-bi akiti akiti.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty, this isn't right! You are not allowed to burn incense to the Lord. That must be done only by priests who are descendants of Aaron. You will have to leave! You have sinned against the Lord, and so he will no longer bless you.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn pīiǹ ubɔti Oosiyasi nsan ní ki bí-u yii: «An kaa pú nsan, sii Oosiyasi ń tūū talaalu kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Aarɔn naantiibi bisaraaŋaliibi bin bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee tundi dee. Nyā circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nee poon, di sá yii a yīntì. Á béé yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nimbiinee, saraa nee kaa làá tīī-si tinyool.»

english_verse: Uzziah, who was standing next to the incense altar at the time, was holding the incense burner, ready to offer incense to the Lord. He became very angry when he heard Azariah's warning, and leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead!
translation_verse: Oosiyasi nìn ŋúb́ u-ŋaan kisambiki kin poon bi tùutī talaaluee. U nìn gíí bisaraaŋaliibi pu diŋuul, dicilpu niinee dinyaŋgbandi tɔ́ u-yigbeel kunimbɔtidiin niin, nsaraafan caŋin, bi-saraaŋaliibi nimbiin.

english_verse: Azariah and the other priests saw it and immediately told him to leave the temple. Uzziah realized that the Lord had punished him, so he hurried to get outside.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Asariyawuu nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin kɔkɔ kíǹee kpēē-uee, dinyaŋgbandi di tɔ́ u-yigbeelee. Bi nìn ŋá malaa ki nyántì-u. Úǹ u-ba mun nìn pée ŋá malaa kí nyā, di sá yii u ká yii ti-Dindaan di nìn dáaĺ u-tafal. Oosiyasi beel nín kúntì puee (Kpèè

english_verse: Since Uzziah had leprosy, he could not be buried in the royal tombs. Instead, he was buried in a nearby cemetery that the kings owned. His son Jotham then became king.
translation_verse: Oosiyasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u ki kɔ́ĺ u-naanjab bibɔtiibi ceekun. Ama u nín nìn sá unyaŋgbantee puee, baa nìn síb́-u u-dicaŋku kaakulin. U-jipɔɔn Yootam di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Jotham obeyed the Lord and did right. He followed the example of his father Uzziah, except he never burned incense in the temple as his father had done. But the people of Judah kept sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. U nìn pée ŋá kii u-baa Oosiyasi nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedee. Ama úǹ kaa nìn kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin kii u-baayee. Samaa úǹ nìn pée gbíntì nìkì ki ŋáań ikpiti.

english_verse: During his rule he attacked and defeated the Ammonites. Then every year for the next three years, he forced them to pay
translation_verse: Yootam nìn jáń nì Amɔn yab bɔtiu ní ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-u. Dibindi gbantee, Amɔn yab nìn pàn̄-u lampoo animbil kúti tɔɔnib bita nì bilee tɔɔnib kutukub bita nì ɔɔji tɔɔnib kutukub bita. Dibinliliitiil nì dibintataatiilee, bi nìn gíti pàn̄-u lampoo míǹ mbaantiimin ní.

english_verse: Jotham remained faithful to the Lord his God and became a very powerful king.
translation_verse: Yootam nìn ká mpɔn gbanti, kun puee u nìn yúl̀ nì ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu deedee.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king, including the wars he fought, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Yootam tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tijáti tin kɔkɔ u jáńee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋáaǹee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: He was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Yootam kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Akaasi di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees. Syria and Israel Attack Judah (
translation_verse: U nìn ŋáaǹ saraabi, ki tūutì talaalub ŋwaadibiyaamu poon nì ŋgbantamu pu nì bususɔmbu kamaa taapu.

english_verse: So Tiglath Pileser came to Judah, but instead of helping, he made things worse.
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu Teegilaati-Falasaar bāań, ní an nín bàà sá ú tūtuǹ Akaasee, ní u bíi jáà nì u.

english_verse: and he offered sacrifices in Hinnom Valley. Worst of all, Ahaz sacrificed his own sons, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: Úǹ u-ba nìn tūū talaalub ki ŋá saraa Been-Inɔɔm tantakalin, ní ki dū u-jipɔmbi ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki ŋá saraa. U nìn pée ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin atimbun ŋin ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ki fōō ŋi-timmu ki tīī Isirayeel yabee nìn ŋáańee ní deedee.

english_verse: Ahaz and the people of Judah sinned and turned away from the Lord, the God their ancestors had worshiped. So the Lord punished them by letting their enemies defeat them. The king of Syria attacked Judah and took many of its people to Damascus as prisoners. King Pekah of Israel later defeated Judah and killed
translation_verse: Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa nìn kūū Juuda yab janjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku ili ŋwimbambaanti. Tíǹ nìn bāań-bi, kun puee bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu ki fá.

english_verse: If you make slaves of the people of Judah and Jerusalem, you will be as guilty as they are of sinning against the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní ki gíti là kí dū Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab kí ŋá ni-yumbui. Mimmee naa nyí yii nimbi ni-ba yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiuaaa?

english_verse: Send these prisoners back home—they are your own relatives. If you don't, the Lord will punish you in his anger.
translation_verse: Ní pīlifiǹ-mi! Ní fàtīí gíiǹ ni-nabiyaamu mun ni cúú kuyuŋu nee kí líí, di sá yii nimbi pu ní ti-Dindaan gíí diŋuul kɔŋkɔnnee.»

english_verse: About the same time, four of Israel's leaders arrived. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai. They agreed with Oded that the Israelite troops were wrong,
translation_verse: Niinee Eefiraayiim tindaŋkpilib biba yíkìi nyáń bin cūtì kujaauee pu. Bíǹ di sá Yoowanan jipɔɔn Asariyawuu nì Meesileemooti jipɔɔn Beereekiya nì Saluum jipɔɔn Yeeyisikiya nì Adilayi jipɔɔn Amasaa.

english_verse: and they said: If you bring these prisoners into Samaria, that will be one more thing we've done to sin against the Lord. And he is already angry enough with us.
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí-bi yii: «Ní taa cáań bisarkadambi nee doo! An yaa kaa sá míǹ, ni làá yàntī tí ŋá ikpitikpaan ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Ni là kí gíti kūtì ti-kpitii nì ti-yìntitam pu níii? Di sá yii ti-kpitii náaǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ní u-ŋuul dàn̄ Isirayeel yab pu.»

english_verse: So in front of the leaders and the crowd, the troops handed over their prisoners and the property they had taken from Judah.
translation_verse: Niinee bijanjaliibee yāntì bisarkadambee nì tiwan tin bi nìn fúkúl̀ ki yōoǹee samaa kɔkɔ nì bi-kpilib nimbiin.

english_verse: The four leaders took some of the stolen clothes and gave them to the prisoners who needed something to wear. They later gave them all a new change of clothes and shoes, then fixed them something to eat and drink, and cleaned their wounds with olive oil. They gave donkeys to those who were too weak to walk, and led all of them back to Jericho, the city known for its palm trees. The leaders then returned to Samaria. Ahaz Asks the King of Assyria for Help (
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi lēē binib biba ní bíǹ tīī bisarkadambee kunyannyaau ki sɔ̄ŋkì bi-pɔbiliŋ. Bi nìn lēē tiwan tin bi fúkúl̀ee poon tiwampeeŋkaal ki pēeǹ bin nìn gàaǹee. Bi nìn tīī-bi tiwampeeŋkaal nì anaataka nì tijin nì tinyɔkaal nì ŋkpam min bi cáa cāantí ibuunee. Bi nìn dū bin pɔ̀fì kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí còom̀ee ki kāaǹ mmamu pu ní ki fātìi gíiǹ-bi bi-nabiyaamu cee, Jeeriikoo, ibafi tiŋkin. Míǹ boonee ní bi fātìi nín gítí Samaarii. Akaasi mēē Asuur yab bí dāá tūtuǹ-u (Kpèè

english_verse: Some time later, the Edomites attacked the eastern part of Judah again and carried away prisoners. And at the same time, the Philistines raided towns in the western foothills and in the Southern Desert. They conquered the towns of Beth-Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, including the villages around them. Then some of the Philistines went to live in these places. Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria and begged for help.
translation_verse: Fiiliistii yab mun nìn dɔ́miń ki jàkā Juuda tiŋkpaammu Seefeelaa nì Neegeeb. Bi nìn fōō Beeti-Seemeesi nì Ayalɔn nì Geedeerooti timmu nì Sookoo tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu, nì Tiimina tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu, nì Giimsoo tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu ki kíǹ ki kā niin.

english_verse: But God was punishing Judah with these disasters, because Ahaz had disobeyed him and refused to stop Judah from sinning.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, ubɔti Akaasi puee, ti-Dindaan nìn sīntiǹ Juuda beel taapu. Di sá yii Akaasi nìn yāntì Juuda yab ŋá ikpiti kaa yúl̀ nì ti-Dindaan deedee.

english_verse: Ahaz gave him gifts from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, as well as from the homes of Israel's other leaders. The Assyrian king still refused to help Ahaz. The Final Sin of Ahaz and His Death
translation_verse: Akaasi nìn yōoǹ tigaajawan tin nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee dijandi nì tin nìn bí dibeecindin nì u-kpambaliŋ ciŋŋinee ki tīī Asuur bɔtiu, ama tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kaa nìn kēetì-u.

english_verse: Even after all these terrible things happened to Ahaz, he sinned against the Lord even worse than before.
translation_verse: Agìń gbanti kɔkɔ poonee, ubɔti Akaasi kaa nìn gbíntìi yú nì ti-Dindaan deedee.

english_verse: He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá saraabi ki tīī Damaasi waaŋi ŋin nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-uee. Di sá yii u nìn lī yii: «Asuur yab waaŋi nín tútúǹ Asuur bɔtiibi puee, m làá ŋá saraa kí tīī-ŋi ŋí tūtuǹ ma mun.» Ama awaa gbanti di nìn mɔ̄tìi nāaǹ u nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Niinee Akaasi kóoǹ tiwan tin kɔkɔ bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki gbáń ki wīī. U nìn dū ti-Dindaan Diiku gbanti ki kpàl̄ ní ki máń isaraafan asaŋkaŋkpil kɔkɔ pu Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.
translation_verse: Juuda tiŋki kamaa poonee, u nìn máń awaadiin ní bi tùutī talaalub ki tìì awaa. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋá ní ki gbítì ti-Dindaan u-baabi Nimbɔtiu ŋuul.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Akaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee, tin u ŋée kí yòon̄ tipeepeekaal kí cáá sāā tiluŋkikaal kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda nì Isirayeel yab bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs. His son Hezekiah then became king.
translation_verse: Akaasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, ama baa nìn dū-u ki bíl̀ Isirayeel bɔtiibi kaakuliŋin. U-jipɔɔn Eeseekiyaasi di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord by doing right, just as his ancestor David had done. The Temple Is Purified
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee kii u-naanja Daafiidi nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedee.

english_verse: they went back to Hezekiah and said: Your Majesty, we have finished our work. The entire temple is now pure again, and so is the altar and its utensils, as well as the table for the sacred loaves of bread and its utensils.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Leefii yab nín cá ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi cee ki bí-u yii: «Ti ŋá ti-Dindaan Diiku kɔkɔ circir ki dóò, ki kpáaǹ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu nì teebil un pu bi pāantí kpɔnɔb bin bi cáa ŋáań ti-Dindaan saraabee, nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ u-pu ditundee.

english_verse: Next, Hezekiah assigned the Levites to their places in the temple. He gave them cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments, according to the instructions that the Lord had given King David and the two prophets, Gad and Nathan.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn dū Leefii yab ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin ní bi ŋúb́ cancakantib nì tibati nì saŋgub ki nóó nì Daafiidi nì ubɔti bɔnaatiliibi Gaadi nì Natan nín nìn yóoǹ puee. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliibi gbanti pu ní ki tīī mara nee.

english_verse: After that, Hezekiah and the crowd of worshipers bowed down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi ŋá saraabi ki dóòyee ní ubɔti nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí u-cee niinee tātìi gbāaǹ bi-yigbeeŋi tūū kitiŋ ki jáam̀ Unimbɔti.

english_verse: Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple
translation_verse: U nìn yíiń bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì kunimbɔtidii cindin ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú,

english_verse: and said: It's time to purify the temple of the Lord God of our ancestors. You Levites must first go through the ceremony to make yourselves clean, then go into the temple and bring out everything that is unclean and unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: ní u bí-bi yii: «Leefii yab, ní pīlifìmaan! Ŋámaan ni-ba circir kí ŋámaan ti-Dindaan, ni-baabi Nimbɔtiu Diiku circir. Nyāntímaan tin kɔkɔ pée sá tijɔkɔndi wantee circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.

english_verse: Some of our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed the Lord our God. Not only did they turn their backs on the Lord, but they also completely ignored his temple.
translation_verse: Ti-baabi nìn yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ní ki ŋá tin kaa kítì u-nimbiinee. Bi nìn fātì bi-kpaŋkpamboon ki tīī ti-Dindaan Kɔŋkooŋŋu ní ki fātì bi-boon ki tīī-u.

english_verse: They locked the doors, then let the lamps go out and stopped burning incense and offering sacrifices to him.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan Diiku punuubi ki pīiǹ ní ki yāntì fitilab gbíntì. Bi nìn gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi tùutī talaalutuukaabi, ní kaa nìn gíti ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki tìì Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: The Lord became terribly angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and everyone was shocked and horrified at what he did to punish them. Not only were
translation_verse: An di yāntì ti-Dindaan fōō Juuda nì Jeerusaleem timmu pu diŋuul. Kun u yāntì bi kpántèe fàantí binib ní bi kíǹ ki cáa bèel̄ kii nimbi ni-ba nín wāĺ an bí pu díǹ nan ní.

english_verse: our ancestors killed in battle, but our own children and wives were taken captive.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-baabi kpíì kujaaun, ní bi cúú ti-jipɔmbi nì ti-bisalib nì ti-nimpoobi kuyuŋu.

english_verse: So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee m là kí ŋá mpèé nì ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, án nín làá ŋá pu u-ŋuul ń sútí kí wàatī-tee.

english_verse: Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
translation_verse: Nimbee, m-jipɔmbi, ní taa dū tibɔti nee kí ŋá bugbambu. Di sá yii nimbi ní ti-Dindaan lēē ní nīn yú u-nimbiin ki tūǹ u-tundi ki tùutī talaalu ki tìì-u.»

english_verse: These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kóoǹ bi-nabiyaamu ki kpáfì, ki ŋá bi-ba circir ní ki dɔ́miń ki ŋá ti-Dindaan Diiku circir ki nóó nì ubɔti nín tīī mara uŋyee nì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi nín bí yii bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: The priests went into the temple and carried out everything that was unclean. They put these things in the courtyard, and from there, the Levites carried them outside the city to Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diiku poon kí ŋá-kù circir. Bi nìn nyántì tin kɔkɔ nìn pée bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki sá tijɔkɔndi wantee dicindin. Leefii yab nìn nyántì tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ ki cáa fá Seedrɔn tantakalin.

english_verse: The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month
translation_verse: Uŋmapeekaa wimpeepeekaaŋu dal ní bi kíĺ kunimbɔtidii ŋāŋkitam kí ŋá-ku circir. Iwiin inii dalee bi nìn ŋáŋkì ki bàn̄ kunaakoou kun bí kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋku nyɔkɔpuee. Bi nìn gíti dū iwiin inii ní ki túń ditundi ki ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku kɔkɔ. Uŋmapeekaa, iwiin saalku nì ŋubɔ dal ní bi dóò atuun kɔkɔ.

english_verse: And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar. Worship in the Temple
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Akaasi nìn sá ubɔti ki fātì u-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan ki nyántì tiwan tiŋyee, ti fātìi gíiǹní-tì ki ŋá-tì circir. Tiwan gbanti bí nsaraafan nyɔkɔpu.» Eeseekiyaasi yāntì bi fātìi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań saraabi

english_verse: At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi kóoǹ kitiŋin bɔtibiliŋ ki kpáfì ní u nì bi nín jɔ́ḿ kunimbɔtidiin.

english_verse: They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
translation_verse: U nìn yāntì bi cáań inajaa iluli nì ipijaa iluli nì apibil aluli nì iŋɔjaa iluli bí dūú ŋá ubɔti cindin yab nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì Juuda yab pu ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau. Ubɔti nìn tīī bisaraaŋaliibi Aarɔn naantiibee mara yii bí dū tiwaŋkutee kí ŋá saraabi ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu pu.

english_verse: They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi cáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam ŋɔjaayee ubɔti nì samaa nimbiin. Bíǹ nìn dū bi-ŋalii ki páaǹ i-pu.

english_verse: The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn lāntì-i ní ki dū fatiku ki yāaǹ nsaraafan pu, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ń ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam. Di sá yii ubɔti nìn tīī mara bí ŋá saraawɔkaa nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau kí tīī Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.
translation_verse: Leefii yab nìn cūtìi yúl̀ bi-paaŋŋu pu ki ŋúb́ tiwambɔɔkaal tin Daafiidi nìn kpítèe. Bisaraaŋaliibi mun nìn cūtìi yúl̀ ki ŋúb́ bi-kantáŋŋi.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments,
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí tūū saraawɔkaa nsaraafan pu. Ŋyunti ŋun bi kíĺ ki bíi tùutī saraawɔkaayee ní bilaŋgaaliibi kíĺ ki bíi gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan. Bi nìn búǹ akantán nì tibɔɔkaal tin Isirayeel bɔtiu Daafiidi nìn kpítèe.

english_verse: and everyone worshiped the Lord. This continued until the last animal was sacrificed.
translation_verse: Samaa kɔkɔ nìn tātìi gbāaǹ ki bíi jáaḿ Unimbɔti ní bilaŋgaaliibi gà ilan ní bikantámbunliibi búǹ míǹ áli bi dāa ŋá saraawɔkaa ki dóò.

english_verse: Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi nì abɔtibilee bí Leefii yab yii bí dū Daafiidi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Asafi laŋyi in bi nìn náańee kí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan. Leefii yab nìn gāā ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan nì dipɔɔpindi. Míǹ boonee ní bi mun tātìi gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ Unimbɔti.

english_verse: Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.” The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Eeseekiyaasi yōoǹ dinyɔɔbundi ki bí yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee nimbi bin ŋúbiń saraabi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, ní cáaḿmaan ni-saraabi nì ni-wampɔkaati tí dūú ŋá saraabi kunimbɔtidiin kí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan.» Niinee ní samaa cáań tiwaŋkuti ní bi dūu ŋá saraabi ki nyɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan. Bin nìn gíti cáá tinitee nìn cáań tiwaŋkuti bi dūu ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi.

english_verse: There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi kaa nìn náaǹ kí ŋmā kí lēē tiwaŋkuti tin bi nìn dūu ŋá bisaraawɔkaabee gbaŋyi, an puee bi-nabiyaamu Leefii yab nìn tútuǹ-bi ní bi túń ditundi gbanti ki dāa dóò. Ŋyunti gbanti muee, bisaraaŋaliibi bin kíǹee mun ŋá bi-ba circir ki dóò, di sá yii Leefii yab nìn gíti yáb́ ki ŋá bi-ba circir ki jítiǹ bisaraaŋaliibi.

english_verse: Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar. So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Kí kūtì muee, bisaraawɔkaabi nìn wīikí ní an nìn gíti bàlifī yii bí wà mpèé saraabi kpam ní kí fá ndaam min bi nìn cāabìń nì bisaraawɔkaabi waŋkutee. Míǹ ní bi nìn ŋá ní ki fātìi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań saraabi kunimbɔtidiin.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
translation_verse: An nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ Eeseekiyaasi nì samaa kɔkɔ Unimbɔti nín nìn tútuǹ-bi bi ŋúń ki ŋá kuŋyee, di sá yii atuun nìn pée cōom̀ ní malaa malaa.

english_verse: Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
translation_verse: Bi nìn tú binib Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ cee, kí yòon̄ Beerseeba kí cáá sāā Daani, bí yíiń-bi bí dāan̄ Jeerusaleem kí jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. Binib tikpil kaa nìn gíti jíń jiŋaal gbanti kii an nín ŋmàn̄ ki síiǹ bí nīn jīǹ-u puee.

english_verse: Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter: People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. If you do this, he will stop being angry.
translation_verse: Binib bin bi nìn túee nìn yōoǹ tigbɔn tin ní ubɔti nì u-kpambaliŋ ŋmàn̄ee ki yìin̄ Isirayeel nì Juuda timmu kɔkɔn, ki báakì ki nóó nì ubɔti nín síiǹ mara uŋyee yii: «Isirayeel yab, nimbi bin ŋmátì ki nyáń Asuur bɔtiu ŋaanee, ní fàtīí gítiḿmaan ti-Dindaan, Abraam nì Isaaki nì Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee, ní u mun ń fàtīí gítiń ni-cee.

english_verse: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry,
translation_verse: Ní taa ŋá mpɔɔgbifin kii ni-naanjabee. Ama ní sìntī ni-ba taapu kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Dāam̄maan u-saraafaŋŋu ŋun ní u ŋá circir kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaanee poon, ní kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, án nín làá ŋá pu u-ŋuul ń sɔ̀ŋkì ni-puee.

english_verse: and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
translation_verse: Ni yaa fātìi gítìń ti-Dindaan ceeyee, bin cúú ni-nabiyaamu kuyuŋuee làá dàkà-bi tiniti ní kí yàntī bí fàtīí gítiń kitiŋ nee poon. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cáá tiniti ní ki sūǹ isaa. Ni yaa lafun fātìi gítìń u-cee, waa làá fàtī u-boon kí tīī-ni.»

english_verse: Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Aseer nì Manasee nì Sabulɔn naakɔtin binib biba nìn sīntiǹ bi-ba taapu ki kíí ki dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded. Passover Is Celebrated
translation_verse: Juuda tiŋkinee, Unimbɔti nìn yāntì binib kɔkɔ ŋá kii unibaantee, ki kíí ki ŋá kii ubɔti nì u-kpambaliŋ nín bí yii bí ŋá puee, ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ puee. Eeseekiyaasi jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu

english_verse: In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: Dinikitikpaandi di nìn kpáfì Jeerusaleem dibindi ŋmaliliitiu poon kí jī jiŋaal un poon ní bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. Binib bin nìn kpáfèe nìn baasii náaǹ ní.

english_verse: They took all the foreign altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and threw them into Kidron Valley.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gbáń ki wīil̀ isaraafan in nìn bí Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee. Bi nìn kpīkitì isaraafan in pu bi nìn tùutī talaalutuukaayee, ní ki kóoǹ ki cáa fá Seedrɔn tantakalin.

english_verse: The Lord answered Hezekiah's prayer and did not punish them.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn fōō Eeseekiyaasi wimmeem ní ki wúń u-nibul pu.

english_verse: The worshipers in Jerusalem were very happy and celebrated the Festival for seven days. The Levites and priests sang praises to the Lord every day and played their instruments.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin nìn bí Jeerusaleemee nìn dū iwiin iluli ki jíń jiŋaal un poon bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nì dipɔɔpiŋkpaandi. Baabadalee Leefii yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nìn gà ilan ki bɔ̀ɔ́ tibɔɔkaal ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration. The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn sòon̄ ki tīī Leefii yab kunyannyaau, ní bíǹ mun dū nlammɔntiim ki túń ti-Dindaan tundi nì dipɔbil diba. Iwiin iluli gbanti kɔkɔ poonee, bi nìn jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu jinti, ki ŋá mpèé saraabi ní ki nyɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Everyone was very happy, including those from Judah and Israel, the priests and Levites, and the foreigners living in Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Juuda yab kɔkɔ nìn bí dipɔɔpindin, ki kpáaǹ bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bin nìn nyánní Isirayeel beelinee, nì bin nìn dɔ́miń ki kíǹ kóò Juuda beelinee.

english_verse: It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David.
translation_verse: Dipɔɔpiŋkpaandi di nìn bí Jeerusaleem, di sá yii kí yòon̄ Isirayeel bɔtiu Daafiidi jipɔɔn Saloomɔn yuntiŋuee, baa ti pée jíń jiŋaal gbanti míǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn yíkìi yúl̀ ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ samaa pu. Unimbɔti nìn fōō bi-wimmeem, di sá yii mì nìn bàn̄ yilpu, u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu laŋki.

english_verse: Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn yākatì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab akiti akiti, ní ki tīī báà ŋma u-tundi dikitil din poon ní u bée. Biba nìn ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi, ní biba mun bí kunimbɔtidiin ki gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kàan̄-bi ki kpáaǹ bi-nimpoobi nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib nì bin māntìi tú-bee ní, di sá yii bi nìn pée bɔ́ntí bi-ba ŋyunti kamaa kí nīn bí circir ní.

english_verse: He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn bí bin kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee yii bí nīn tìì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab kun bi máaǹ kí tīī-bee, án nín làá ŋá pu bí ŋmā kí dū bi-ba kɔkɔ kí sú ti-Dindaan marabee.

english_verse: After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. They destroyed all the local shrines and foreign altars in Judah, as well as those in the territories of Benjamin, Ephraim, and West Manasseh. Then everyone went home. Offerings for the Priests and Levites
translation_verse: Bi jíń jiŋaal ki dóòyee ní Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee yìin̄ Juuda timmun ki gbáń ki wīī ataŋkpee ŋin bi nìn cóoǹ awaayee. Bi nìn gāatì iwindɔ, ki wīil̀ ŋwaadibiyaamu nì isaraafan. Bi nìn ŋá míǹ Juuda nì Beenjameen timmun, ki kpáaǹ Eefiraayiim nì Manasee timmun. Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní báà ŋma nín gítí u-tiŋkin, laakin u kóòyee.

english_verse: Hezekiah provided animals from his own herds and flocks to use for the morning and evening sacrifices, as well as for the sacrifices during the Sabbath celebrations, the New Moon Festivals, and the other religious feasts required by the Law of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ubɔti gaajawanti poon ní u nìn lèekī ki tìì bi cáa ŋáań kutaafaau nì kujoou saraawɔkaabi nì iwiŋŋuŋfikaa saraawɔkaabi, nì saraabi bin bi ŋáań uŋmal kamaa wimpeekaaŋu dalee, nì saraabi bin bi ŋáań jiŋaalib yuntiŋuee, ki nóó nì an nín ŋmàn̄ pu ki kā ti-Dindaan marau gbɔŋkunee.

english_verse: As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops.
translation_verse: Daliŋkin ní bi nyántì mara gbantee, Isirayeel yab nìn cāabìń bilee nì ndamam nì ŋkpam nì tisiil nì tikpaajin tin kíǹee jincɔ̀fikaati. Bi nìn gíti cāabìń tin kɔkɔ bi cááyee saalaatiiti tikpil.

english_verse: The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Isirayeel beelin yab nì Juuda beelin yab bin nìn kóò Juuda timmunee mun nìn cāabìń bi-naai nì bi-piii nì bi-ŋoobui saalaatiiti, ki kpáaǹ tiwan tin ní bi nìn dūu sú ti-Dindaanee saalaatiiti. Bi nìn kóoǹ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ ki kpúkuǹ akpuku akpuku.

english_verse: The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later.
translation_verse: Bi nín kíĺ uŋmatataati poon ki bīil̀ akpuku akpukuee, uŋmaluluúti poon ní bi dāa bíl̀ ki dóò.

english_verse: When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nì u-kpambaliŋ dɔ́miń ki kpēē akpukuee ní ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaan nì u-nibul Isirayeel.

english_verse: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn bālifì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab akpuku ŋin bi cáańee pu,

english_verse: The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
translation_verse: ní usaraaŋakpil Asariyawuu un sá Sadooki maaliŋunee kíí-u yii: «Daliŋkin binib kíĺ ki bíi cāabìń tin bi lēē bi-kpaajinti poonee, ti ká ki jíń ki díkí an kíǹ, di sá yii ti-Dindaan bīiǹ u-nibul pu. Akpuku ŋin kíǹ nee, tijin tin kíǹee dee.»

english_verse: So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed,
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí ŋāŋkì adiin ŋin poon bi kpáafí tijin ŋi bí kunimbɔtidii caŋinee, ní bi lafun ŋáŋkì-ŋi.

english_verse: all the extra offerings were taken there. Hezekiah and Azariah then appointed Conaniah the Levite to be in charge of these storerooms. His brother Shimei was his assistant, and the following Levites worked with them: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi nì usaraaŋakpil Asariyawuu un nìn gíti sá un kpèé kunimbɔtidiiyee nìn lēē bin làá nīn bí Koonaniyawuu nì Simeeyii taapu ki cīití tiwan gbantee. Bíǹ di nìn sá Yeeyiyeel nì Asasiyawuu nì Nayati nì Asayeel nì Yeereemooti nì Yoosabaadi nì Eeliyeel nì Isimakiyawuu nì Mayaati nì Beenaya.

english_verse: Kore son of Imnah was assigned to guard the East Gate, and he was put in charge of receiving the offerings voluntarily given to God and of dividing them among the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Uleefiija Kooree, Imina jipɔɔn di nìn cīití ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔki. Úǹ ní bi nìn lēē ú nīn fòol̄ nlammɔntiim saraabi bin bi nìn cāabìń ki tìì Unimbɔtee, ní ki nìn yàkatī tin bi lèekī tikpaajin pu ki tìì ti-Dindaanee nì tiwan tin bi nìn cāabìń kí sú-uee.

english_verse: He had six assistants who were responsible for seeing that all the priests in the other towns of Judah also got their share of these offerings. They were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah. Every priest and every Levite over
translation_verse: Kí kūtì muee, kaa sá bininjab bin yiŋŋi bi nìn ŋmàn̄ bi cáá abin ata kí nīn cée ŋmaniŋma ní bi nìn yàkatī tijin ki tìì, ama bi nìn tìì bin nìn dòoń kunimbɔtidiin baabadal ki tūǹ ditundi ki nóó nì bi-kitiŋi nín sá puee mun.

english_verse: Hezekiah also appointed other men to take food and supplies to the priests and Levites whose homes were in the pastureland around the towns of Judah. But the priests had to be descendants of Aaron, and the Levites had to be listed in the official records.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá Aarɔn naantiibi ki kóò tisati tin māntìi tú bi-timmunee, bi nìn lēē binib kitiŋ kamaa poon bí nīn yàkatī tijin ki tìì bininjab kɔkɔ nì Leefii yab bin nìn ŋmàn̄ bi-yiŋŋee.

english_verse: Everything Hezekiah did while he was king of Judah, including what he did for the temple in Jerusalem, was right and good. He was a successful king, because he obeyed the Lord God with all his heart.
translation_verse: U nìn túń atuun tikpil kí ŋmā kí ŋāŋkì kunimbɔtidii ní kí nīn tɔ́ ti-Dindaan marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi. U nìn ŋá míǹ ki nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔ ní an nìn bútì-u tikɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: The officials said all these things in Hebrew, so that everyone listening from the city wall would understand and be terrified and surrender.
translation_verse: Seenakeeriibi tɔntɔnliibi nìn tátí mpɔn eebru sooŋyi poon kí ŋmā kí fàaǹ binib bin nìn bí digundi puee kí yɔ̀tī bi-wunti, án nín làá ŋá pu bí ŋmā kí fōō kitiŋee.

english_verse: You've heard what my ancestors and I have done to other nations. Were the gods of those nations able to defend their land against us?
translation_verse: Naa nyí m-naanjab nì man m-ba nín ŋá duulinya nibuliŋ kɔkɔ pueeee? Atimbun gbanti diba waal ŋúń ki fīī di-tiŋki ki nyántì m-ŋaanaaa?

english_verse: The Lord rescued Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib and also protected them from other enemies.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan ŋá ní ki fīī Eeseekiyaasi nì Jeerusaleem yab ki nyántì Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi ŋaan nì bi-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ŋaan. U nìn wúń bi-pu ijaan kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: he and his officials worked out a plan to cut off the supply of water outside the city, so that the Assyrians would have no water when they came to attack. The officials got together a large work force that stopped up the springs and streams near Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ní samaa nyáń ki náaǹ ní ki dū inyimbul kɔkɔ nì kibùmbiki kin pùub̀ kitiŋ gundi boonee ki ŋéeb́ ki lī yii: «Asuur yab ń taa dāan̄ doo kí ká nnyim tikpil.»

english_verse: Hezekiah's workers also repaired the broken sections of the city wall. Then they built defense towers and an outer wall to help protect the one already there. The landfill on the east side of David's City was also strengthened. He gave orders to make a large supply of weapons and shields,
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn ká dipɔbil ki fātìi bíi māā digundi din bi nìn máń ki tú kitiŋee laakin bátì bátì ki lítèe. U nìn máń ndibiyaamu mun poon bi kàal̀ sintilee ki tɔ́kɔǹ digundi pu. U nìn gíti máń digundi diba dipeekaalee boon, ní ki ŋáŋkì kudii kun bi yíì Miiloo, ku bí Daafiidi Tiŋkinee. U nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ ŋkpamu nì agbampɔɔ tikpil.

english_verse: and he appointed army commanders over the troops. Then he gathered the troops together in the open area in front of the city gate and said to them:
translation_verse: U nìn lēē bijanjakpilib bin làá nīn kpòotī samaayee. U nìn kóoǹ bi-kɔkɔ ki kpáfì u-cee kitiŋ punyɔkɔki caŋin ní ki tīī-bi kunyannyaau yii:

english_verse: Be brave and confident! There's no reason to be afraid of King Sennacherib and his powerful army. We are much more powerful,
translation_verse: «Ní pɔ́ɔǹ ni-ba kí ká kunyannyaau! Ní taa fàŋkì tiba. Ní taa fàŋkì Asuur bɔtiu nì dijanjakitikpaandi din táá-u nee. Di sá yii mpɔn bí ti-cee ki jítiǹ u-cee.

english_verse: When Sennacherib and his troops were camped at the town of Lachish, he sent a message to Hezekiah and the people in Jerusalem. It said:
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi nì u-janjakitil kɔkɔ cūtìi māntì ki tú Lakiisi tiŋki kí já nì kì. Niin ní u tú u-janjakpilib biba ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi cee Jeerusaleem nì Juuda yab bin kóò Jeerusaleemee ki bí-bi yii:

english_verse: I am King Sennacherib of Assyria, and I have Jerusalem surrounded. Do you think you can survive my attack?
translation_verse: «Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ba pu ní ni máká ní ki gbíntìi kā Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin bi māntìi tú kí jáǹ-kì nee ní?

english_verse: The Assyrian officials said terrible things about the Lord God and his servant Hezekiah.
translation_verse: Seenakeeriibi tɔntɔnliibi nìn gíti nìkī ki sòon̄ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nì u-tɔntɔnliu Eeseekiyaasi tibɔfan. Seenakeeriibi sīī ti-Dindaan

english_verse: Sennacherib's letter even made fun of the Lord. It said, “The gods of other nations could not save their people from Assyria's army, and neither will the God that Hezekiah worships.”
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn mun ki sīī ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. U nìn sòon̄ tigbɔn gbantin yii: «Kii duulinya timbuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee waaŋi nín kaa ŋúń ki fīī ŋi-nib ki nyántì m-ŋaan puee, míǹ ní Eeseekiyaasi mun Nimbɔtiu kaa làá ŋmā kí fīī u-nibul kí nyāntí m-ŋaan.»

english_verse: People brought offerings to Jerusalem for the Lord and expensive gifts for Hezekiah, and from that day on, every nation on earth respected Hezekiah. Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies (
translation_verse: Binib tikpil nìn cáań saraabi Jeerusaleem ki tīī ti-Dindaan ní ki cáań tiwampɔkaal ki pú Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti kí nīn cée ní atimbun kɔkɔ nib kíǹ ki tɔ́-u. Eeseekiyaasi beel nín kúntì puee (Kpèè

english_verse: About this same time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. He prayed, and the Lord gave him a sign that he would recover.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Eeseekiyaasi nìn búŋkì ki làá kpú. U nìn mēē ti-Dindaan ní úǹ tīī-u kudaaŋŋu yii u làá ká dicáaǹdi.

english_verse: But Hezekiah was so proud that he refused to thank the Lord for everything he had done for him. This made the Lord angry, and he punished Hezekiah and the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ama u nìn kɔ́ dilambilin kaa béè tiŋan tin ní Unimbɔti ŋá ki tīī-uee. An puee ti-Dindaan ŋuul nìn jéetì u nì Jeerusaleem nì Juuda yab pu.

english_verse: Hezekiah and the people later felt sorry and asked the Lord to forgive them. So the Lord did not punish them as long as Hezekiah was king. Hezekiah's Wealth (
translation_verse: Min kamaa Eeseekiyaasi nìn kɔ́ dilambilinee, u nìn sīntì u-ba taapu, u nì Jeerusaleem yab. An puee ti-Dindaan ŋuul kaa nìn jéetì bi-pu ŋyunti ŋun Eeseekiyaasi dáá bí dimaŋfalinee.

english_verse: Hezekiah was very rich, and everyone respected him. He built special rooms to store the silver, the gold, the precious stones and spices, the shields, and the other valuable possessions.
