translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn ká tigaajati tikpil tikpil nì tinyool mun. U nìn kpáafì animbil nì sindaariya nì ataŋkpamɔnti nì talaalub nì agbampɔɔ nì tigaajawan kɔkɔ nì ti-bulifi.

english_verse: Storehouses were also built for his supply of grain, wine, and olive oil; barns were built for his cattle, and pens were put up for his sheep.
translation_verse: U nìn máń adiin ki kpáafì tijimpin nì ndamam nì ŋkpam. U nìn gíti ŋá tinaabakal ki tīī u-naai nì u-piii.

english_verse: God made Hezekiah extremely rich, so he bought even more sheep, goats, and cattle. And he built towns where he could keep all these animals.
translation_verse: U nìn máń ntimu ní ki nìn cáá tipicaŋkpun nì tiŋɔcaŋkpun nì tinacaŋkpun tikpil, di sá yii Unimbɔti nìn tīī-u tigaajati tikpil.

english_verse: It was Hezekiah who built a tunnel that carried the water from Gihon Spring into the city of Jerusalem. In fact, everything he did was successful!
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi di nìn ŋéeb́ Giiyɔn nyimbulnimbil din nìn bí digundi boonee ní ki cátì nnyinsan ki dáaĺ nnyim ki kɔ́ǹ Daafiidi Tiŋkin, ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. An nìn pée bútì Eeseekiyaasi u-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon ní.

english_verse: Even when the leaders of Babylonia sent messengers to ask Hezekiah about the sign God had given him, God let Hezekiah give his own answer to test him and to see if he would remain faithful. Hezekiah Dies (
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun ní Babiloon kpootiliibi nìn tú binib bí dāan̄ kí bàlifì kí mɔ̀tīí béé maamaaci tuuŋŋi ŋin jítì u-tiŋki puee, Unimbɔti nìn kākatì u-ba ki yāntì-u kí ŋmā kí cɔ̄ŋkì-u kí kpèè kun di bí u-pɔbilinee.

english_verse: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including how faithful he was to the Lord, is included in the records kept by Isaiah the prophet. These are written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee nì u nín yúl̀ Unimbɔti deedee puee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya, Amɔtisi jipɔɔn leedakal gbɔŋkun nì Juuda yab nì Isirayeel yab bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: When Hezekiah died, he was buried in the section of the royal tombs that was reserved for the most respected kings, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem honored him. His son Manasseh then became king.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi naantiibi kaakuliŋin yilpu pú. Juuda yab kɔkɔ nì Jeerusaleem yab nìn súń u-kpool ki tīī-u tinyool. U-jipɔɔn Manasee di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_verse: But the people of Judah and Jerusalem listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Ama Manasee nìn yāntì Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab gáatì, áli gba bi gíti ŋá ikpiti ki jítiǹ atimbun ŋin ti-Dindaan nìn kúntì ki fōō bi-tiŋki ki tīī Isirayeel yabee.

english_verse: The people obeyed Manasseh, but they worshiped the Lord at their own shrines.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, binib nìn gbíntìi ŋáań saraabi iwaatootipaan pu, ama bi nìn ŋáań ki tìì ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu ní.

english_verse: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his prayer to the Lord God and the warnings from his prophets, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Manasee tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, u nín mēē u-Nimbɔtiu nì anyɔɔbun ŋin ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi fōō ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee ki dūu nāatì-uee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: While Manasseh was held captive there, he asked the Lord God to forgive him and to help him.
translation_verse: U nìn nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu u-nimbinaamandi poon ní ki sīntiǹ u-ba u-baabi Nimbɔtiu nimbiin.

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. And he continued to worship the stars.
translation_verse: U nìn fātìi ŋáŋkì iwaatootipaan in u-baa nìn gbáń ki bíil̀ee, ní ki máń isaraafan bí nīn ŋáań i-pu saraabi ki tìì diwaal Baal. U nìn cóoǹ iwindɔ ní ki gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ iŋmalbi in kɔkɔ bí kutaa puee.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: U nìn máń isaraafan iba mun ti-Dindaan Diikun, min kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nìn lī yii: «Jeerusaleem niin ní m làá nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkèe.»

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courtyards of the temple
translation_verse: U nìn gíti máń isaraafan ti-Dindaan Diiku ciŋŋi aliitilin bí nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì iŋmalbi in bí kutaa puee.

english_verse: and even set up a stone image of a foreign god. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own sons in Hinnom Valley. He did many other sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago, God had told David and Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there in the temple I will be worshiped forever.
translation_verse: U nìn máń diwaal ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diikun. Ama ti-Dindaan nìn tùkū Daafiidi nì u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn yii: «Kudii nee poon nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin m lēē Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ kansikinee poon ní m làá nīn pée lèekī m-ba ki dàkà.

english_verse: If my people will faithfully obey all the laws and teaching I gave to my servant Moses, I will never again force them to leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
translation_verse: M-nibooliŋu yaa tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ nì m-marab bin kɔkɔ m-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi tīī-bee, m kpá kí yàntī bí nīn tú ki yìiǹ kí wàatī kitiŋ kin ní m tīī bi-naanjabee».

english_verse: The Lord tried to warn Manasseh and the people about their sins, but they ignored the warning.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Manasee nì u-nibul, ama baa nìn fātìi tɔ́.

english_verse: So he let Assyrian army commanders invade Judah and capture Manasseh. They put a hook in his nose and tied him up in chains, and they took him to Babylon.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan cáań Asuur bɔtiu janjakpilib ki tɔ́ bi-pu. Bi nìn cúú Manasee ní ki dū abɔmbil ki kpàl̄ u-nyɔɔkpaweeŋyi, ní ki dū tasa kusakai ki bóob́-u mili pu ní ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Manasseh's prayer and saw how sorry he was, and so he let him go back to Jerusalem and rule as king. Manasseh knew from then on that the Lord was God.
translation_verse: U nìn mēē-u ní an gbēē Unimbɔti ní u pílifì u-wimmeem ní ki yāntì u fātìi gítì Jeerusaleem u-beelin. Niinee ní Manasee nín béè yii ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔti.

english_verse: Later, Manasseh rebuilt the eastern section of Jerusalem's outer wall and made it taller. This section went from Gihon Valley north to Fish Gate and around the part of the city called Mount Ophel. He also assigned army officers to each of the fortified cities in Judah.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, ní u máń Daafiidi Tiŋki boonee diguŋfɔkɔl diba. Digundi gbanti nìn dī Giiyɔn nyimbuliŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní ki kpākaǹ Seedrɔn tantakal ki cáa sāā Ijɔm punyɔkɔki, ní ki fātìi pɔ́ĺ ki māntì Oofeel gbantaŋki ki tú. U nìn kāaǹ bijanjakpilib Juuda timmu mun kɔkɔ bi nìn máń agun ki túee poon.

english_verse: Manasseh also removed the idols and the stone image of the foreign god from the temple, and he gathered the altars he had built near the temple and in other parts of Jerusalem. He threw all these things outside the city.
translation_verse: U nìn nyántì awaa ŋin u nìn cáań ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiinee nì kunaŋu kun u nìn máń ki síiǹ niinee. U nìn gbáń ki wīī isaraafan in u nìn máń ti-Dindaan gbantaŋki pu nì Jeerusaleemee kɔkɔ, ní ki nyántìi fá kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu.

english_verse: Then he repaired the Lord's altar and offered sacrifices to thank him and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He gave orders that everyone in Judah must worship the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: U nìn fātìi máń ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu ní ki ŋá mpèé saraabi nì ijaam saraabi ŋu-pu. U nìn tīī Juuda yab mara yii bí nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Manasseh died and was buried near the palace, and his son Amon became king. King Amon of Judah (
translation_verse: Manasee kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabee ní bi síb́-u u-cindin. U-jipɔɔn Amɔn nín nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Amɔn, Juuda bɔtiu (Kpèè

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done, and he worshiped and offered sacrifices to the idols his father had made.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee kii u-baa Manasee nín nìn ŋá puee. U nìn ŋá saraabi ki tīī awaa ŋin ní u-baa nìn máńee ki jáam̀-ŋi.

english_verse: Manasseh had turned back to the Lord, but Amon refused to do that. Instead, he sinned even more than his father.
translation_verse: Ama úǹ kaa nìn sīntiǹ u-ba taapu ti-Dindaan nimbiin kii u-baa Manasee nín nìn sīntiǹ u-ba taapu puee. Úǹ nìn gíti ŋá ikpiti ki jítiǹ u-baa gba.

english_verse: Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
translation_verse: U-tɔntɔnliibi nìn bɔ́ntì u-pu ní ki kūū-u u-naakookun.

english_verse: But the people of Judah killed the murderers of Amon and made his son Josiah king.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab nìn kūū bin kɔkɔ nìn kūū Amɔŋyee ní ki dū u-jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi ki kāaǹ ubɔti u-yil pu.

english_verse: In the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah, after he had removed all the sinful things from the land and from the Lord's temple, he sent three of his officials to repair the temple. They were Shaphan son of Azaliah, Governor Maaseiah of Jerusalem, and Joah son of Joahaz, who kept the government records.
translation_verse: Joosiyaasi nín jíń dibeel abin saalku nì ata poon ki fíntì Isirayeel tiŋki nì kunimbɔtidii ki nyántì tijɔkɔndin ki dóòyee, ní u tú Asaliya jipɔɔn Safan nì Jeerusaleem Gɔminau Maaseeyawuu nì Joowakaasi jipɔɔn Yoowa, ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu bí cùú ŋāŋkì ti-Dindaan, u-Nimbɔtiu Diiku.

english_verse: After Josiah had finished reading, he stood in the place reserved for the king. He promised in the Lord's name to faithfully obey the Lord and to follow his laws and teachings that were written in the book.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn yú u-paaŋŋu ní ki pōoǹ kí nīn yú nì ti-Dindaan deedee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-dàkatam nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì u-naŋki kɔkɔ. U nìn gíti pōoǹ kí nīn tɔ́ tin kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā dipoondi taŋkpapilintinee.

english_verse: He watched as the altars for the worship of the god Baal were torn down, and as the nearby incense altars were smashed. The Asherah poles, the idols, and the stone images were also smashed, and the pieces were scattered over the graves of their worshipers.
translation_verse: U-nimbiin ní bi gbáń ki wīī diwaal Baal saraafaŋyi nì talaalutuukaa saraafaŋyi in nìn tɔ́kɔ́ i-puee. Bi nìn gāatì iwindɔ ki fá ní ki nàn̄ awaa ŋin bi kpítèe nì ŋin bi dūntèe dúsi dusi ki dūu yāaǹ bin nìn ŋá saraabi ki tīī-bee kaakuliŋ pu.

english_verse: Josiah then had the bones of the pagan priests burned on the altars. And so Josiah got rid of the worship of foreign gods in Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: U nìn dū awaa gbanti saraaŋaliibi kpabiŋ ki tūū bi-saraafaŋyi pu ŋŋmi. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋá ki fíntì Juuda nì Jeerusaleem ki nyántì tijɔkɔndin.

english_verse: He did the same things in the towns and ruined villages in the territories of West Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as the border of Naphtali.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá míǹ mbaantiim Manasee nì Eefiraayiim nì Simeeyɔn ki kpáaǹ Neefitalii timmun nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-muee.

english_verse: Everywhere in the northern kingdom of Israel, Josiah tore down pagan altars and Asherah poles; he crushed idols to dust and smashed incense altars. Then Josiah went back to Jerusalem. Hilkiah Finds The Book of God's Law (

english_verse: These three men went to Hilkiah the high priest. They gave him the money that the Levite guards had collected from the people of West Manasseh, Ephraim, and the rest of Israel, as well as those living in Judah, Benjamin, and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Binibee nìn nín cá usaraaŋakpil Yilkiya cee. Bi nìn dū animbil ŋin bi cáań kunimbɔtidiinee ki tīī-u. Leefii yab bin nìn cí kipunyɔkɔee di nìn fōō animbil gbanti Manasee yab nì Eefiraayiim yab nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ kíǹee nì Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab bin nìn kóò Jeerusaleemee cee.

english_verse: Then the money was turned over to the men who supervised the repairs to the temple. They used some of it to pay the workers,
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū animbilee ki ŋúbiǹ bin bi nìn lēē bí nīn kpèé ditundi ti-Dindaan Diikunee, ní bíǹ cáa pà bin bí niin ki ŋáŋkí ti-Dindaan Diikuee.

english_verse: The workers were honest, and their supervisors were Jahath and Obadiah from the Levite clan of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the Levite clan of Kohath. Other Levites, who were all skilled musicians,
translation_verse: Binibee nìn túń ditundee deedee. Leefii yab Yayati nì Oobadiya bin sá Meerarii maaliŋunee nì Seekariya nì Meesulam bin sá Keeyaati maaliŋunee di nìn kpèé-bi. Leefii yab bin nìn ŋūǹ tibɔɔkaal tiŋanee biba

english_verse: were in charge of carrying supplies and supervising the workers. Other Levites were appointed to stand guard around the temple.
translation_verse: nìn kpèé bin tūntí tiwanee nì bitɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ, báà udaan tundi yaa nìn sá diŋyee. Leefii yab kansikinee, biba mun nìn sá bigbaŋŋmaliibi ní biba sá bikàliŋkpilib ní bin kíǹ sá bipunyɔɔciitiliibi.

english_verse: While the money was being given to these supervisors, Hilkiah found the book that contained the laws that the Lord had given to Moses.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi nyāntí animbil ŋin bi nìn cáań ti-Dindaan Diikunee ní usaraaŋakpil Yiilkiyaawuu ká ti-Dindaan marau un u nìn dūu tīī Mooyiisee gbɔŋku.

english_verse: Hilkiah handed the book to Shaphan the official and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.”
translation_verse: Yiilkiyaawuu nìn bí ugbaŋŋmal Safan yii: «M ká Marab gbɔŋku ti-Dindaan Diikun.» U lī mimmee ní ki dū kugbɔŋuee ki tīī-u.

english_verse: They have collected the money from the temple and have given it to the men supervising the repairs.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi yōoǹ animbil ŋin bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki dūu tīī bin bíi kpèé ditundee nì bitɔntɔnliibi.»

english_verse: But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it aloud.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Safan kútì ki tùkū ubɔti yii: «Usaraaŋakpil Yiilkiyaawuu dū kugbɔŋu kubɔ ki tīī-mi.» Safan nìn kàan̄ kugbɔŋuee ubɔti nimbiin. Joosiyaasi yāntì bi cūtì Ulda cee dibalifil (Kpèè

english_verse: When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nín gbìl̄ tin kā Marab gbɔŋkuee poonee ní u cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì.

english_verse: “The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Israel and Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
translation_verse: «Ní cùú bàlifì ti-Dindaan kí tīī man nì Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee nì Juuda yab. Ní bàlifì-u tin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee pu. Di sá yii ti-naanjab kaa pílifì u-nyɔkɔ. Baa ŋá tin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee. An pu ní ti-Dindaan gíí ti-pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu.»

english_verse: “Josiah, I am the Lord! And I intend to punish this country and everyone in it, just as this book says.
translation_verse: <M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì bin kɔkɔ kóò ki-nee pu, kí nóó nì mbusub bin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu kun ni kàan̄ Juuda bɔtiu nimbiinee.

english_verse: The people of Judah and Israel have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I can't stand it any longer. I am furious.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem yab dū-mi ki fá ní ki tūutì talaalub ki tīī awaa ŋin bíǹ bi-ba dū bi-ŋalii ki ŋée ki gbítì m-ŋuul. An pu ní m gíí kitiŋ nee pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu, ní m-ŋuulee kpá kí sɔ̀ŋkì!>

english_verse: “Josiah, listen to what I am going to do. I noticed how sad you were when you heard that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry.
translation_verse: ní tibɔtee gbēē-si. A nín gbìl̄ tin m sòon̄ yii an làá bàń Jeerusaleem nì ki-nib puee, a sīntiǹ a-ba m-nimbiin, ní ki dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin a pēēyee ní ki súń m-nimbiin. An puee ma mun gbìl̄ a-wimmeem. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: King Josiah called together the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti tú bi yíiń Juuda nì Jeerusaleem tindaŋkpilib ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì u-cee.

english_verse: Then he went to the Lord's temple, together with all the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, and the Levites. Finally, when everybody was there, he read aloud The Book of God's Law that had been found in the temple.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u nì Juuda yab nì bin kóò Jeerusaleemee nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì samaa kɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ bikpaambi kí cáá sāā mbiyaamu nín jɔ́ḿ kunimbɔtidiin. Niinee ní ubɔti kàan̄-bi tin kɔkɔ bi ŋmàn̄ an kā dipoondi gbɔŋku kun bi ká ti-Dindaan Diikunee.

english_verse: Then he asked the people of Jerusalem and Benjamin to make that same promise and to obey the God their ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn yāntì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Jeerusaleem nì Beenjameen timmunee pōoǹ míǹ mbaantiim. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, bin nìn kóò Jeerusaleemee nìn ŋá ki nóó nì dipoondi din bi nìn pōoǹ bi-baabi Nimbɔtiuee.

english_verse: Josiah destroyed all the idols in the territories of Israel, and he commanded everyone in Israel to worship only the Lord God. The people did not turn away from the Lord God of their ancestors for the rest of Josiah's rule as king.
translation_verse: Joosiyaasi nìn kúntì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ ní bi nìn ŋáań Isirayeel tiŋkinee, ní ki páb́ bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Isirayeelee bí nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan, bi-Nimbɔtiu. An puee, u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, Isirayeel yab kaa nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: During the battle an Egyptian soldier shot Josiah with an arrow. Josiah told his servants, “Get me out of here! I've been hit.”
translation_verse: Bi bíi jáà mimmee ní bin tòó ipiinee tɔ́ ipiin ki yá-u ní u bí u-tɔntɔnliibi yii: «Yòom̄maan-mi kí cùnnì, di sá yii m fōō tiweendi.»

english_verse: Neco sent the following message to Josiah: I'm not attacking you, king of Judah! We're not even at war. But God has told me to quickly attack my enemy. God is on my side, so if you try to stop me, he will punish you.
translation_verse: Ama ní Neekoo tú binib bí tùkù-u yii: «Juuda bɔtiu, tilati di bí man nì sii kansikin? An kaa sá sii ní m dòoń kí já kujaau díǹ, ama m-nannanliu ubɔ mun ní m dòoń kí jáǹ. Unimbɔti bí-mi yii ḿ yáb́. Unimbɔti bí m-cee. An puee á taa jáǹ Unimbɔti, yaa sá fám, u làá kpɔ̀-si.»

english_verse: Josiah commanded that Passover be celebrated in Jerusalem to honor the Lord. So, on the fourteenth day of the first month, the lambs were killed for the Passover celebration.
translation_verse: Joosiyaasi nìn jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu Jeerusaleem ki tīī ti-Dindaan tinyool. Uŋmapeekaa, ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dalee, ní bi kūū Dilákatil jiŋaaliu waŋkuti.

english_verse: Get ready to do the work that David and Solomon assigned to you, according to your clans.
translation_verse: Ní bɔ́ntímaan ni-ba kí nóó nì ni-maalii nì ni-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ pu ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiu Daafiidi nì u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn gbɔntin puee.

english_verse: When the people bring you their Passover lamb, you must kill it and prepare it to be sacrificed to the Lord. Make sure the people celebrate according to the instructions that the Lord gave Moses, and don't do anything to make yourselves unclean and unacceptable.
translation_verse: Kpɔ̀maan Dilákatil jiŋaaliu waŋkuti, ŋámaan ni-ba circir ní kí tūtuǹ ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab bí ŋá ti-Dindaan nín dī Mooyiisi pu ki sòon̄ pu ki síiǹee.»

english_verse: Josiah's officials also voluntarily gave some of their animals to the people, the priests, and the Levites as sacrifices. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, who were the officials in charge of the temple, gave the priests
translation_verse: U-kàliŋkpilib mun nìn tīī samaa nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab tiwaŋkuti nì nlammɔntiim. Ilikiya nì Seekariyawuu nì Yeeyiyeel nín nìn kpèé kunimbɔtidii. Bíǹ nìn tīī bisaraaŋaliibi apibil kutukub bili nì alaataa aluu nì inajaa alaataa ata bí dūú ŋá Dilákatil jiŋaaliu saraabi.

english_verse: Conaniah, his two brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, as well as Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad were leaders of the Levites, and they gave the other Levites
translation_verse: Leefii yab kpilib Koonaniyawuu nì u-naalib Seemayawuu nì Neetaneeyeel nì Asabiya nì Yeeyiyeel nì Yoosabaadi nìn tīī Leefii yab apibil kutukub biŋmoo nì inajaa alaataa aŋmoo bí dūú ŋá Dilákatil jiŋaaliu saraabi.

english_verse: When everything was ready to celebrate Passover, the priests and the Levites stood where Josiah had told them.
translation_verse: Bi nín nìn bɔ́ntì jiŋaal gbanti puee sɔ̀. Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yú bi-paaŋŋu ní Leefii yab mun yúl̀ akiti akiti ki nóó nì ubɔti nín nìn síiǹ-bi puee.

english_verse: Then the Levites killed and skinned the Passover lambs, and they handed some of the blood to the priests, who splattered it on the altar.
translation_verse: Bi nìn làntī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu waŋkuti ní bisaraaŋaliibi tīkintí fatiku ki cáa yàantí nsaraafan pu ní Leefii yab lèekī igban.

english_verse: The Levites set aside the parts of the animal that the worshipers needed for their sacrifices to please the Lord, just as the Law of Moses required. They also did the same thing with the bulls.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gāntì tiwaŋkuti tin bi làá dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan saraawɔkaayee, cilinjee inajaayee. Bi nìn yākatì ki tīī samaa ki nóó nì bi-maalii kii an nín ŋmàn̄ pu ki kā Mooyiisi gbɔŋkun puee.

english_verse: They sacrificed the Passover animals on the altar and boiled the meat for the other offerings in pots, kettles, and pans. Then they quickly handed the meat to the people so they could eat it.
translation_verse: Bi nìn púĺ Dilákatil jiŋaaliu pibiliŋ kii dikoobil nín sá puee, ní ki dū saraabi bin kíǹee nanti ki tɔ́kɔǹ daanseebin nì ŋkumbɔbiyaamun nì sirbabin. Bi nìn ŋáań malaa ki cáa yàkatī ki tìì samaa kɔkɔ.

english_verse: All day long, the priests were busy offering sacrifices and burning the animals' fat on the altar. And when everyone had finished, the Levites prepared Passover animals for themselves and for the priests.
translation_verse: Leefii yab nìn ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki bɔ́ntì bíǹ bi-ba nì bisaraaŋaliibi yati, di sá yii bisaraaŋaliibi, Aarɔn naantiibee kaa nìn cáá mpaan. Bi nìn bí ki ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki cáá ŋkpam ki wù ŋŋmi áli kunyeeu dāa mɔ́. An pu ní Leefii yab nìn bɔ́ntì bíǹ bi-ba nì bisaraaŋaliibi jinti.

english_verse: During the celebration some of the Levites prepared Passover animals for the musicians and the guards, so that the Levite musicians would not have to leave their places, which had been assigned to them according to the instructions of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's prophet. Even the guards at the temple gates did not have to leave their posts.
translation_verse: Asafi naantiibi bilaŋgaaliibi nìn yú bi-paaŋŋu ki nóó nì Daafiidi nì Asafi nì Eeman nì Yeedutun, ubɔti saŋkiliu nín nìn síiǹ puee. Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi mun nìn yú ki cí kipunyɔkɔ kamaa. Báà ŋma nìn pée bí u-tundin ní, di sá yii bi-nabiyaamu Leefii yab nìn bɔ́ntì bi mun jinti ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: So on that day, Passover was celebrated to honor the Lord, and sacrifices were offered on the altar to him, just as Josiah had commanded.
translation_verse: Kii ubɔti Joosiyaasi nín nìn tīī mara puee, bi nìn bɔ́ntì atuun kɔkɔ ŋwiin gbanti kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan, kí jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu ní kí ŋmā kí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu pu.

english_verse: People from Jerusalem and from towns all over Judah and Israel were there. Passover had not been observed like this since the days of Samuel the prophet. In fact, this was the greatest Passover celebration in Israel's history!
translation_verse: Baa nìn gíti jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu ubɔ míǹ Isirayeel tiŋkin kí yòon̄ doooo Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Samiyeel yuntiŋu. Isirayeel bɔtiu ubɔ mun kaa nìn jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu ubɔ kii un ní Joosiyaasi nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì Juuda yab nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee nì Jeerusaleem yab jíńee.

english_verse: All these things happened in the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah. Josiah Dies in Battle (
translation_verse: Joosiyaasi nín jíń dibeel abin ali kpá mmuŋku poonee ní bi jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu gbanti. Joosiyaasi maŋfal wiiŋyi nín kúntì puee (Kpèè

english_verse: Some time later, King Neco of Egypt led his army to the city of Carchemish on the Euphrates River. And Josiah led his troops north to meet the Egyptians in battle.
translation_verse: Tin bí nee kɔkɔ boonee, ŋyunti ŋun ní Joosiyaasi ŋáŋkì kunimbɔtidii ki dóòyee ní Eejipiti bɔtiu Neekoo nín cá Kaarkeemiisi, Eefiraati mɔɔl caŋin kí já kujaau. Joosiyaasi nìn túŋkì-u kí bàà pìin̄-u nsan.

english_verse: But Josiah ignored Neco's warning, even though it came from God! Instead, he disguised himself and marched into battle against Neco in the valley near Megiddo.
translation_verse: Ama Joosiyaasi kaa nìn kpántì u-landɔkɔŋu. Di sá yii waa nìn pílifiǹ Neekoo bɔti tin nìn nyánní Unimbɔti u-ba ceeyee. U nìn cúú u-beebɔkutil ki pēetì bí taa béé-u ní ki cūtìi bíi jáà kujaau Meegiidoo tantakalin.

english_verse: They carried Josiah out of his chariot, then put him in the other chariot he had there and took him back to Jerusalem, where he soon died. He was buried beside his ancestors, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem mourned his death.
translation_verse: Ní u-tɔntɔnliibi kpákatì-u janjatɔrɔku poon ní ki yōoǹ-u ki ŋá u-tɔrɔkuliliitiu poon ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Jeerusaleem. Niin ní u kpíì ní bi síb́-u u-baabi kaakuliŋin. Bin kɔkɔ nìn kóò Jeerusaleemee nì Juuda yab nìn súń u-kpool.

english_verse: Jeremiah the prophet wrote a funeral song in honor of Josiah. And since then, anyone in Judah who mourns the death of Josiah sings that song. It is included in the collection of funeral songs.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii nìn gāā Joosiyaasi ŋkpiisilan. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti kí cáá sāā díǹ, bilaŋgaaliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi gà ikpiisilan ki téetí Joosiyaasi kúm pu. An nìn dūu kpántì dikoobil ní Isirayeel tiŋkin. Bi ŋmàn̄ ilan gbanti nyɔɔbuŋŋi ki ŋá Iyaliŋki gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Everything else Josiah did while he was king, including how he faithfully obeyed the Lord,
translation_verse: Joosiyaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, u-deedee tuuŋŋi ŋin u túń ki nóó nì tin ŋmàn̄ ki kā ti-Dindaan marab gbɔŋkunee,

english_verse: is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: nì ubɔti nín kíĺ pu ki dāa kúntì puee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel nì Juuda bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: The message said: I am King Cyrus of Persia. The Lord God of heaven has made me the ruler of every nation on earth. He has also chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over any of his people who want to go back to Judah.
translation_verse: «Peeriisi bɔtiu Siirusi nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ti-Dindaan, yilpu Nimbɔtiu dū abee ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee ki ŋá m-ŋaan ní ki lēē-mi yii ḿ mā-u kudii Jeerusaleem, Juuda tiŋkin. Ni-kansikin un sá u-nibul yɔuee, ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn bí udaan cee ú jɔ̄m̀ Jeerusaleem!»

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar also carried off many of the valuable things in the Lord's temple, and he put them in his palace in Babylon.
translation_verse: Neebukadineesaar nìn gíti yōoǹ kunimbɔtidii poon tiwan tikpil ki cáa cūnnì ki síiǹ úǹ u-ba beecindin Babiloon.

english_verse: During Jehoiakim's rule, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia invaded Judah. He arrested Jehoiakim and put him in chains, and he sent him to the capital city of Babylon.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn dɔ́miń ki jáń nì u. U nìn dū tasa kusakai ki bóob́-u tiŋan ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon.

english_verse: The Lord sent King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to attack Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar killed the young men who were in the temple, and he showed no mercy to anyone, whether man or woman, young or old. God let him kill everyone in the city.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn cáań Babiloon yab bɔtiu ki tɔ́ bi-pu. Úǹ nìn dū kitàataajiki ki kūū bi-naacimpɔmbi áli gba circir kɔŋkooŋŋun. Waa nìn súń unaacimpɔɔnaaa, usapɔɔnaaa, utikpilaaa, unicikitikaa saai. Unimbɔti nìn dū tikɔkɔ ki ŋá u-ŋaan.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar carried off everything that was left in the temple; he robbed the treasury and the personal storerooms of the king and his officials. He took everything back to Babylon.
translation_verse: U nìn yōoǹ tiwan tin sá tikpaandi nì ŋwaamu ki nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee kɔkɔ ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. U nìn yōoǹ ki kpáaǹ tigaajawan tin bí kunimbɔtidiinee nì tin bí dibeecindinee nì u-kàliŋkpilib yati.

english_verse: The survivors were taken to Babylonia as prisoners, where they were slaves of the king and his sons, until Persia became a powerful nation.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu nìn yōoǹ bin nìn kíǹ kaa kpíìyee ki cūnnì Babiloon ní bi kpántì úǹ nì u-jipɔmbi yumbui ki cáa sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní Peeriisi yab fōō dibeelee.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord his God and refused to change his ways, even after a warning from Jeremiah, the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan, u-Nimbɔtiu nimbiinee. Waa nìn sīntiǹ u-ba Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii un nìn bíi nàatī-u ti-Dindaan bɔtee nimbiin.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had forced Zedekiah to promise in God's name that he would be loyal. Zedekiah was stubborn and refused to turn back to the Lord God of Israel, so he rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Neebukadineesaar nìn yāntì u pūtì ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti yindi pu, ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, waa nìn kíí u-ba pu ní ki yíkìi bíi jáà nì u. U nìn ŋá ntafapɔn ní ki pɔ́ɔkì u-pɔbil, ní ki yíì kaa kpántì u-ba ki fātìi gítìń ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee.

english_verse: The people of Judah and even the priests who were their leaders became more unfaithful. They followed the disgusting example of the nations around them and made the Lord's holy temple unfit for worship.
translation_verse: Abɔtibil nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì samaa kɔkɔ kaa nìn yúl̀ nì Unimbɔti deedee. Bi nìn ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin ní atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-bee ŋáańee ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidii kun bí Jeerusaleem ti-Dindaan dūu sú u-bee tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: But the Lord God felt sorry for his people, and instead of destroying the temple, he sent prophets who warned the people over and over about their sins.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu nìn túnní binib ŋfunyɔm kupaau bí kpāafì-bi, di sá yii u-nibooliŋu nì u-saraafaŋŋu nìn gbí-u inimɔɔn.

english_verse: But the people only laughed and insulted these prophets. They ignored what the Lord God was trying to tell them, until he finally became so angry that nothing could stop him from punishing Judah and Jerusalem. Jerusalem Is Destroyed (
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab nìn bēel̀ Unimbɔti tuuŋyi gbanti, ki kpēē u-nyɔɔbundi fám ní ki láń u-bɔnaatiliibi. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan ŋuul jéetì u-nibul pu nnyɔkɔ gíti kpá.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's troops burned down the temple and destroyed every important building in the city. Then they broke down the city wall.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gāā ŋŋmi ki tūū kunimbɔtidii ní ki gbáń ki wīī digundi din bi nìn máń ki tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee. Bi nìn gāā ŋŋmi ki tūū adimɔnti kɔkɔ ní ki gbáń ki bíil̀ tiwan tin cáá kunyampoouee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: In the first year that Cyrus was king of Persia, the Lord had Cyrus send a message to all parts of his kingdom. This happened just as Jeremiah the Lord's prophet had promised.
translation_verse: Peeriisi bɔtiu Siirusi nín jíń dibeel dibimpeepeekaal poonee, ní ti-Dindaan lēē kí ŋá kii u nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii pu ki sòon̄ pu ki síiǹee. Ti-Dindaan nìn gbēē Siirusi pɔbil ní ki yāntì u báakì u-beel kɔkɔ poon, ki ŋmàn̄ mun ki síiǹ yii:

english_verse: Everyone else must provide what is needed. They must give money, supplies, and animals, as well as gifts for rebuilding God's temple.
translation_verse: Laakin kamaa ní u-nibul din kíǹee yaa bée, niin yab ń tīī-bi animbil kúti nì sindaariya nì tigaajawan nì tiwaŋkuti nì nlammɔntiim saraabi bí dūú tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidii kun bí Jeerusaleemee tundi.»

english_verse: The others helped by giving silver articles, gold, personal possessions, cattle, and other valuable gifts, as well as offerings for the temple.
translation_verse: Bi-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb nìn cáań animbil kúti nì sindaariya wanti nì tigaajawan nì tiwaŋkuti nì tiwan tin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee kí tūtuǹ-bi, ní kí nín kūtì tiwan tin bi nìn tīī-bi nì dipɔbil dibee.

english_verse: King Cyrus gave back the things that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the Lord's temple in Jerusalem and had put in the temple of his own gods.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Siirusi nìn kóoǹ tiwan tin kɔkɔ ubɔti Neebukadineesaar nìn yōoǹ kunimbɔtidiin Jeerusaleem ki cáań ki yóoǹ u-waadiiŋŋinee ki kpáfì.

english_verse: Cyrus placed Mithredath, his chief treasurer, in charge of these things. Mithredath counted them and gave a list to Sheshbazzar, the governor of Judah.
translation_verse: Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi nìn yāntì Miitireedati un kpèé animbil bɔtee dū an wantee ki ŋúbiǹ Seesbasaar, Juuda yab kpiliu.

english_verse: Here is how many people returned whose ancestors had come from the following towns:
translation_verse: Seenaa tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib kutukub bita nì alaataa aluu nì binib mmuŋku nì saalaa.

english_verse: Here is a list of how many returned from each family of priests:
translation_verse: Ariim maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì binib saalku nì bili.

english_verse: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until we find out if you really are priests.”
translation_verse: Ní bi-gɔminau bí-bi yii bí taa ti jī tijin tin bi dūu ŋá saraa tì bí circir páaayee kí nīn cí usaraaŋakpil ubɔ ń dāá dū Uriim nì Tumiim kí bàlifì dibalifil.

english_verse: When the people came to where the Lord's temple had been in Jerusalem, some of the family leaders gave gifts so it could be rebuilt in the same place.
translation_verse: Bi nín fātìi bāań Jeerusaleem laakin ti-Dindaan diiku nìn bée, ní adican kpilib biba ŋá nlammɔntiim saraabi, bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii laakin ku nìn pée yú ŋkpikimee.

english_verse: Everyone returned to the towns from which their families had come, including the priests, the Levites, the musicians, the temple guards, and the workers.
translation_verse: Niinee bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì samaa kansikin biba, nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì kunimbɔtidiin tɔntɔnliibi cūtìi kāl̀ bi-timmun. Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee mun nìn cūtìi kāl̀ bi-naanjab timmun.

english_verse: During the seventh month of the year, the Israelites who had settled in their towns went to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Dibindi poon ŋmaluluútiu bāańee, Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn gítìń ki kāl̀ bi-timmunee nìn kóoǹ ki cūtìi kpáfì kii unibaantee Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: The priest Joshua son of Jozadak, together with the other priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives rebuilt the altar of Israel's God. Then they were able to offer sacrifices there by following the instructions God had given to Moses, the man of God.
translation_verse: Niinee ní usaraaŋakpil Joosuwa, Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn nì u-nabiyaamu bisaraaŋaliibi nì Saltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel nì u-dicaŋkun yab yíkìi kíĺ ki bíi māā Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu saraafaŋŋu kí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi kii Unimbɔti niliu Mooyiisi nín yóoǹ mara yii bí nín ŋáań puee.

english_verse: And they built the altar where it had stood before, even though they were afraid of the people who were already living around there. Then every morning and evening they burned sacrifices and offerings to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nì min kɔkɔ bi nìn fàŋkí binib bin nìn bí niinee, bi nìn fātìi máń nsaraafan ŋu-paaŋkpikiŋu pu, ní ki kíǹ ki ŋáań kutaafaau nì kujoou saraabi ki tìì ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: The people followed the rules for celebrating the Festival of Shelters and offered the proper sacrifices each day.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi jíń tantib jiŋaaliu kii bi nín síiǹ mara bí nīn jīǹ-u puee, ní ki ŋáań kutaa kamaa saraabi bin nyɔkɔm bi máaǹ kí ŋée.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices to please the Lord, sacrifices at each New Moon Festival, and sacrifices at the rest of the Lord's festivals. Every offering the people had brought voluntarily was also presented to the Lord.
translation_verse: Boonee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań baabadal saraabi nì saraabi bin bi ŋáań uŋmapɔɔn kamaayee, nì bin bi ŋáań ti-Dindaan jiŋaalib yuntiŋuee nì saraabi bin kɔkɔ binib nìn cāabìń ki tìì ti-Dindaanee.

english_verse: Although work on the temple itself had not yet begun, the people started offering sacrifices on the Lord's altar on the first day of the seventh month of that year. The Rebuilding of the Temple Begins
translation_verse: Uŋmaluluúti wimpeekaaŋu dalee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki tìì ti-Dindaan, nì min kɔkɔ baa nìn dáá bíl̀ ti-Dindaan diiku kun bi làá mēe nyeelee.

english_verse: King Cyrus of Persia had said the Israelites could have cedar trees brought from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. So they sent grain, wine, and olive oil to the cities of Tyre and Sidon as payment for these trees, and they gave money to the stoneworkers and carpenters.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi tīī bin kpítí ataŋkpeeyee nì kapintab animbil, ní ki tīī Siidɔn yab nì Tiir yab tijin nì ndaam nì ŋkpam bí bóob́ seedir dɔi kí dūú tɔ̄ń tiŋkun doooo Leebanɔn tiŋkin án dāá nyā Jafaa tiŋkin. Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi di pú-bi kinyɔkɔ ní bi ŋúń ki ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: During the second month of the second year after the people had returned from Babylonia, they started rebuilding the Lord's temple. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jozadak, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned started working. Every Levite over
translation_verse: Bi nín fātìi bāań Jeerusaleem laakin kunimbɔtidii nìn bée, dibinliliitiil ŋmaliliitiu poon ní Samiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel, nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa, nì bi-nabiyaamu mun kíǹee, an dàkà yii bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki kūnnée, kíĺ ki bíi bɔ́ntí Leefii yab bin nìn cáá abin mmuŋku kí nīn cáa cée bí kpòotī kunimbɔtidii mātam tuuŋŋi.

english_verse: The Levites in charge of the whole project were Joshua and his sons and relatives and Kadmiel and his sons from the family of Hodaviah. The family of Henadad worked along with them.
translation_verse: Joosuwa nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu, nì Kadimiyeel nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu Juuda naakookun yab di nìn kpáfì dicilpu kí kpòotī bin kɔkɔ làá nīn bí kunimbɔtidii mātam tuuŋŋi poonee. Eeniyadaadi maaliŋun yab nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-nabiyaamu Leefii yab nìn kútì bi-pu.

english_verse: When the builders had finished laying the foundation of the temple, the priests put on their robes and blew trumpets in honor of the Lord, while the Levites from the family of Asaph praised God with cymbals. All of them followed the instructions given years before by King David.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bidimaliibi nìn kíĺ ki bíi bīil̀ kunimbɔtidii nyeelee, bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yú ki pēē bi-saraaŋabɔkutiŋ ki ŋúb́ akantán, ní Leefii yab bin sá Asaafi maaliŋunee ŋúb́ cancakantib, ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan kii Isirayeel yab bɔtiu Daafiidi nín nìn yóoǹ mara pu bi ŋmàn̄ ki síiǹee.

english_verse: They praised the Lord and gave thanks as they took turns singing: “The Lord is good! His faithful love for Israel will last forever.” Everyone started shouting and praising the Lord because work on the foundation of the temple had begun.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gà ilan ki tìì tɔb ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan yii: «Tiŋman, u ŋān̄ ní u-neendi bí Isirayeel yab pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ kūuntí mpɔn ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan, kun puee bi nìn kíĺ kunimbɔtidii nyeel ki bíi māā.

english_verse: Many of the older priests and Levites and the heads of families wept bitterly because they remembered seeing the first temple years before. But others were so happy that they celebrated with joyful shouts.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi tikpil nì Leefii yab nì adican kpilib kansikin bin nìn púĺ ki ká dooooyee Nimbɔtidiiku nín nìn bí puee, nìn bíi sūǹ mpɔn bi nín ká bi bíi bīil̀ kupɔŋu nyeelee. Ama ní tikpil mun nìn bíi kūuntí mpɔn nì dipɔɔpindi.

english_verse: Their shouting and crying were so noisy that it all sounded alike and could be heard a long way off.
translation_verse: An ŋá mimmee binib kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí gàntī bin nìn bí ki kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindee nì bin nìn bí ki sūǹ mpɔnee, kun puee bi nìn kūuntí mpɔn mpɔn ní an gbìl̀ ndan.

english_verse: The enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people had come back to rebuild the temple of the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Juuda nì Beenjameen yab nannanliibi nìn gbìl̄ yii bin nyánní kuyuŋu ki gítìńee bíi māā bi-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu diiku.

english_verse: So they went to Zerubbabel and to the family leaders and said, “Let us help! Ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here, we have worshiped your God and offered sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi sútì ki pìl̄ Sooroobabeel nì adican kpilib ki bí-bi yii: «Ti làá kūtì ni-pu ní mā kunimbɔtidii nee, di sá yii ti mun pée nóó Unimbɔtibaantee ní. Kí yòon̄ daliŋkin Asuur bɔtiu Asaradɔn yōoǹní-ti ki cáań dooyee, ti pée ŋáań saraabi ní ki tìì Unimbɔti.»

english_verse: But Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the family leaders answered, “You cannot take part in building a temple for the Lord our God! We will build it ourselves, just as King Cyrus of Persia commanded us.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Sooroobabeel nì Joosuwa nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib bin kíǹee kíí-bi yii: «An kaa kítì yii ní kūtì ti-pu tí mā ti-Nimbɔtiu kudii. An sá timbi baba ní ń mā ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu kudii, kii Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi nín tīī-ti mara yii tí ŋá puee.»

english_verse: Then the neighboring people began to do everything possible to frighten the Jews and to make them stop building.
translation_verse: Niinee ní binib bin kóò kitiŋ gbantinee yɔ̄tì Juuda yab wunti ki kɔ́ǹ-bi tifaandi bí gbèen̄ kí taa ti mā kunimbɔtidii.

english_verse: During the time that Cyrus was king and even until Darius became king, they kept bribing government officials to slow down the work. Trouble Rebuilding Jerusalem
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti ŋun Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi kā dibeel ki tin cáa sāā ŋyunti ŋun Daariyusi dāa kāl̀ dibeelee, bi nìn pée tìì kitiŋ gbanti kàliŋkpilib animbil yii bíǹ ń pìin̄ Juuda yab nsan atuun ń gbèen̄ ní. Bi ŋmàn̄ tigban ki mɔ́ntì Juuda yab nyɔkɔpu

english_verse: In the first year that Xerxes was king, the neighboring people brought written charges against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Asuweerusi nín kāl̀ dibeel pu kpalaayee, ní Juuda yab nannanliibi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki túǹ Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab pu dibɔgaandi.

english_verse: Later, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their advisors got together and wrote a letter to Artaxerxes when he was king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic and had to be translated.
translation_verse: Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Aritaseerseesi yuntiŋuee ní Biseelam nì Miitireedati nì Taabeel nì u-jutiibi mun ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī ubɔti. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poon Aram yab ŋmaŋmabiti nì bi-sooŋyin ní.

english_verse: This letter said: Your Majesty King Artaxerxes, we are your servants from everywhere in Western Province, and we send you our greetings.
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poonee sèé: «Ubɔti Daariyusi, an sá timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi bin kóò ntimu mun bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee di ŋmàn̄-si kugbɔŋu nee.

english_verse: You should know that the Jews who left your country have moved back to Jerusalem and are now rebuilding that rebellious city. In fact, they have almost finished rebuilding the walls and repairing the foundations.
translation_verse: «Ti-baa ubɔti, ti là á béé yii Juuda yab bin nyánní a-cee ki fātìi bāań timbi cee Jeerusaleem dooyee kíĺ ki fātìi bíi māā kitiŋ kin kaa ŋān̄ ní ki-nib sá pɔɔgaatibee. Bi ŋáŋkì digundi din māntìi tú-kèe nyeel ki bíi māā ki tɔ̄kɔntí.

english_verse: You should also know that if the walls are completed and the city is rebuilt, the Jews won't pay any kind of taxes, and there will be less money in your treasury.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ti-baa ubɔti, ti là á béé yii bi yaa fātìi máń kitiŋ nee ki yōoǹ ki-gundee, baa làá gíti pà lampoobi nì patantib nì animbil ŋin bisaŋkinliibi pèe, an di làá dāá cáań sii ubɔti agìń.

english_verse: We are telling you this, because you have done so much for us, and we want everyone to respect you.
translation_verse: An puee timbi bin ká diyimɔɔl a-cee ki sá a-tɔntɔnliibee kaa ŋūǹ kí nīn kā ki kpèé bí nīn kpèé sii ubɔti fám míǹ. An pu ní ti bíi tùkù-si tibɔti nee

english_verse: If you look up the official records of your ancestors, you will find that Jerusalem has constantly rebelled and has led others to rebel against kings and provinces. That's why the city was destroyed in the first place.
translation_verse: á yàntī bí nyàab̀ bibɔtikpikib gbɔnti poon. Sii a-ba làá ká yii kitiŋ gbanti nib pée sá pɔɔgaatib ní, ki kɔ̄ntí bibɔtiibi nì ntimu yidambi agìń. Laakin kamaa ní bi yaa bée, bi pée cāabìń agìń ŋma ní. An pu gba ní bi dāa nāaǹ kitiŋ gbanti.

english_verse: King Artaxerxes answered: Greetings to Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and to your advisors in Samaria and other parts of Western Province.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki kíí-bi yii: «Gɔmina Reewum nì ugbaŋŋmal Simsayi nì bi-tɔntɔnjutiibi bin bí Samaarii nì ntimu mun kíǹ ki bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, «m jáam̀-ni.

english_verse: After your letter was translated and read to me,
translation_verse: «M fōō kugbɔŋu kun ni ŋmàn̄ní-mee, bi kàan̄-ku m-nimbiin ní ki nāatì.

english_verse: I had the old records checked. It is true that for years Jerusalem has rebelled and caused trouble for other kings and nations.
translation_verse: M yāntì bi nyàab̄ tibɔkpikil gbɔnti poon ní ki lafun ká yii doooo cannaakuee, Jeerusaleem yab nìn pée jáà nì bibɔtiibi ní, kaa nìn kíikí bi-ba pu, ní ki nìn gáatí binib.

english_verse: I want you to command the people to stop rebuilding the city until I give further notice.
translation_verse: An puee ní yóoń mara yii binib gbanti ń gbèen̄ bi-tuuŋŋi, kí tùkù-bi yii bí taa fàtīí mā tiba kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní man làá dāá pɔ̄ kinyɔkɔee.

english_verse: Do this at once, so that no harm will come to the kingdom.
translation_verse: Ní kpèèmaan tiŋan kí taa ŋá bugbambu tibɔti nee poon, án nín làá ŋá pu án taa láa kpántí tibɔkpaandi kí dāá cáań bibɔtiibi agìńee.»

english_verse: As soon as this letter was read, Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and their advisors went to Jerusalem and forced everyone to stop rebuilding the city. Work on the Temple Starts Again
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní bi fōō ubɔti Aritaseerseesi gbɔŋkuee ki kàan̄-ku Reewum nì ugbaŋŋmal Simsayi nì bi-tɔntɔnjutiibi bin kíǹee nimbiinee, dicilpu niin ní bi nín cá Jeerusaleem, ki tin dàkā Juuda yab mpɔn bí gbèen̄ atuun. Bi fātìi kíĺ kunimbɔtidii mātam

english_verse: The Jews were forced to stop work on the temple and were not able to do any more building until the year after Darius became king of Persia.
translation_verse: Niin ní bi gbēeǹ Unimbɔti diiku mātam tuuŋŋi Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, ki tin cáa sāā Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Daariyusi nín kāl̀ dibeelee binliliitiil poon.

english_verse: Then the Lord God of Israel told the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to speak in his name to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. And they did.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Agaayi nì Idoo jipɔɔn Sakari sòon̄ nì Juuda yab bin bí Jeerusaleemee nì bin bí Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔnee, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un nìn bí bi-nee yindi pu.

english_verse: So Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the priest urged the people to start working on the temple again, and God's prophets encouraged them.
translation_verse: Niinee Sooroobabeel jipɔɔn Saltiyeel nì Joosuwa jipɔɔn Yoosadaaki yíkì ki kíĺ ki bíi māā Unimbɔti diiku Jeerusaleem. Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nìn kútì bi-pu ki tútúǹ-bi.

english_verse: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and his assistant Shethar Bozenai got together with some of their officials. Then they went to Jerusalem and said to the people, “Who told you to rebuild this temple?
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ní Tateenaayi un nìn sá gɔmina Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki timmunee nì Seetaar-Boosinayi nì bi-tɔntɔnjutiibi dɔ́miń bi-cee ki bālifì-bi yii: «Ŋma di pú-ni kinyɔkɔ yii ní fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii nee nì ku-guŋŋi ní?

english_verse: Give us the names of the workers!”
translation_verse: Ní tīī-ti binib bin bíi māā kunimbɔtidii neeyee yiŋŋi.»

english_verse: But God was looking after the Jewish leaders. So the governor and his group decided not to make the people stop working on the temple until they could report to Darius and get his advice.
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti nìn wúń Juuda yab kpilib pu. Baa nìn ŋúń ki pīiǹ-bi nsan bí taa ti mā, kí nīn cí tibɔti gbanti ń bà ubɔti Daariyusi, ní úǹ ń kíiń ní bí nín béé bi nín làá ŋá puee. Bi kúŋfì Juuda yab boon ubɔti cee

english_verse: Governor Tattenai, Shethar Bozenai, and their advisors sent a report to Darius,
translation_verse: Gɔmina Tateenaayi nì Seetaar-Boosinayi nì u-tɔntɔnjutiibi nì bikàliŋkpilib bin sá Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmu kpilibee nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī ubɔti Daariyusi.

english_verse: which said: King Darius, we wish you the best!
translation_verse: Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ yii: «Ubɔti Daariyusi, Unimbɔti ń yàntī á nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_verse: We went to Judah, where the temple of the great God is being built with huge stones and wooden beams set in the walls. Everyone is working hard, and the building is going up quickly.
translation_verse: «Ti là ti-baa ubɔti ń béé yii ti cūtì Juuda tiŋkin áli ki bàn̄ Unimbɔtikpaan diiku laŋki. Bi fātìi kíĺ ki bíi māā kunimbɔtidii. Ataŋkpakpaan ní bi kpítì ní ki cáá idɔjaa ki kútí ki māā agun. Bi baasii bíi tūǹ ditundi mmɔntiimin, ní an bíi cá malaa malaa mun.

english_verse: We asked those in charge to tell us who gave them permission to rebuild the temple.
translation_verse: Ní ti bālifì bi-kpilib yii: <Ŋma di pú-ni kinyɔkɔ yii ní fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii nee nì ku-guŋŋi ní?>

english_verse: We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down for you.
translation_verse: Boonee ní ti fōō bi-yiŋŋi ki ŋmàn̄ kí dūú tīiń-si á béé bikpilib bin di bíi kpòotī atuunee.

english_verse: They claimed to be servants of the God who rules heaven and earth. And they said they were rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago by one of Israel's greatest kings.
translation_verse: Kpèè binib gbanti nín kíí-ti tibɔti tiŋyee sèé: «<Timbi sá Unimbɔti un náań yilpu nì taapuee tɔntɔnliibi ní ki fātìi bíi māā kunimbɔtidii kun Isirayeel bɔtikpaaŋwu ubɔ nìn máń ki dóò dooooyee.

english_verse: We were told that their people had made God angry, and he let them be captured by Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king who took them away as captives to Babylonia. Nebuchadnezzar tore down their temple,
translation_verse: Ama ti-naanjab nìn kɔ́ǹ Unimbɔti un náań yilpuee diŋuul ní u dū-bi ki líiǹ Babiloon tiŋki bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar, ní úǹ dɔ́miń ki gbáń ki wīī kunimbɔtidii ní ki cúú-bi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu Babiloon tiŋkin.

english_verse: Sheshbazzar then went to Jerusalem and laid the foundation for the temple, and the work is still going on.
translation_verse: Di sá ní Seesbasaar gbanti dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem doo ki bíl̀ Unimbɔti diiku nyeel. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti kí dāá sāā díǹ ti pée bí ku-pu dimal ní an kaa láá dóò.

english_verse: Your Majesty, please order someone to look up the old records in Babylonia and find out if King Cyrus really did give orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem. We will do whatever you think we should.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-baa ubɔti, a yaa là, a ŋūǹ kí yàntī bí nyàab̀ Babiloon niin, bibɔtiibi gbɔnti poon kí kpèè yii ubɔti Siirusi yaa nìn lafun pú kinyɔkɔ bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii Jeerusaleem. Boonee sii ti-baa ubɔti ń yàntī tí gbìl̄ a nín síiǹ-ti puee.»

english_verse: King Darius ordered someone to go through the old records kept in Babylonia.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Daariyusi tīī mara yii bí nyàab̀ Babiloon yab gbɔnti tin bí adiin ŋin poon bi kpáafí bi-gaajawantee poon kí kpèè.

english_verse: Finally, a scroll was found in Ecbatana, the capital of Media Province, and it said: This official record will show
translation_verse: Ama Eekibataani, kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki māntìi tú kì bí Meedi tiŋkpaaŋki poonee ní bi tin ká kugbɔŋu kubɔ. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ ku-poon yii: «Tibɔti tin bi ŋmàn̄ ki yóoǹ fool boon puee.

english_verse: that in the first year Cyrus was king, he gave orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem, so that sacrifices and offerings could be presented there. It is to be built
translation_verse: «Ubɔti Siirusi nín nìn kāl̀ dibeel dibimpeepeekaalee, u nìn pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii Jeerusaleem, án nīn sá laakin bi làá nīn ŋáań saraabee. Bí fàtīí gíiǹ-ku kí mā kí tɔ́kɔń kukpikuu nyeel pu. Ku-fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab mmuŋku nì saalaa, ku-waaŋŋu mun ń nīn sá meetab mmuŋku nì saalaa.

english_verse: with one row of wooden beams for each three rows of large stones. The royal treasury will pay for everything.
translation_verse: Bí kpítí ataŋkpakpaan kí dūú mā ikuul ita ní kí dū idɔ kí páań ŋkuul ŋubɔ. Dibeel nimbiliŋ poon ní bi làá lēē kí dūú tɔ̄ atuun gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Then the gold and silver things that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple and brought to Babylonia are to be returned to their proper places. King Darius Orders the Work To Continue
translation_verse: Kí kūtèe, bí gíiǹ sindaariya wanti nì animbil kúti wanti tin Neebukadineesaar nìn yōoǹ kunimbɔtidiin Jeerusaleem ki cáa cūnnì Babiloonee. Bí cáá-tì kí yóoń kunimbɔtidiin Jeerusaleem, tikɔkɔ ń nīn yú ti-laŋki.»

english_verse: King Darius sent this message: Governor Tattenai of Western Province and Shethar Bozenai, you and your advisors must stay away from the temple.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, sii Tateenaayi, Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmu gɔminau nì Seetaar-Boosinayi nì ni-tɔntɔnjutiibi nì bikàliŋkpilib bin bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmunee: «Ní taa ti bɔ̄ ni-nyɔkɔ kunimbɔtidii gbanti mātam bɔti poon.

english_verse: Let the Jewish governor and leaders rebuild it where it stood before. And stop slowing them down!
translation_verse: Yàntīmaan Juuda yab ń tɔ̄ bi-ba kí mā kunimbɔtidii. Juuda yab gɔminau nì bi-kpilib ń fàtīí gíiǹ kunimbɔtidii gbanti kí mā kí tɔ́kɔń ku-nyeel ŋkpiki pu.

english_verse: Starting at once, I am ordering you to help the leaders by paying their expenses from the tax money collected in Western Province.
translation_verse: M tīī-ni mara ní tūtuǹ Juuda yab kpilib bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii. Ní dū lampoo nimbiliŋ ŋin binib bin bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee pà ki tìì ubɔtee kí dūú tīī-bi bí nīn cáa pà bitɔntɔnliibi, ditundi ń taa gbèen̄.

english_verse: And don't fail to let the priests in Jerusalem have whatever they need each day so they can offer sacrifices to the God of heaven. Give them young bulls, rams, sheep, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil.
translation_verse: Ní tīī-bi tin kɔkɔ pée máaǹee, an dàkà yii anajapɔmbil nì ipijaa nì apibil bí nīn cáa ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki tìì Unimbɔti un náań yilpu nì taapuee, ní kí tīī bilee nì ŋyaam nì ndamam nì ŋkpam kí nóó nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin bí Jeerusaleemee nín síiǹ puee bí nīn cáa ŋáań baabadal saraau an taa lóó ŋwindal.

english_verse: I want them to be able to offer pleasing sacrifices to God and to pray for me and my family.
translation_verse: Mimmee bi làá ŋmā kí nīn ŋáań saraabi bin sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī Unimbɔti un náań yilpuee pɔbil, ní kí mèè kí tīī ubɔti nì u-jipɔmbi ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin.

english_verse: If any of you don't obey this order, a wooden beam will be taken from your house and sharpened on one end. Then it will be driven through your body, and your house will be torn down and turned into a garbage dump.
translation_verse: Un kamaa di yaa yīntì mara gbantee, bí lēē u-diiku dɔjaatiŋu kí cóoń kí dū-u kí lúntí ŋu-pu, ní u-cindi ń kpántí ditampundi.

english_verse: I ask the God who is worshiped in Jerusalem to destroy any king or nation who tries either to change what I have said or to tear down his temple. I, Darius, give these orders, and I expect them to be followed carefully. The Temple Is Dedicated
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi nì atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ yaa yīntì mara un m yóoǹ nee, ki tāntì bi-ŋal kí wīī kunimbɔtidii kun bi bíi māā Jeerusaleem nee, Unimbɔti un bí niin bi yíì u-yindee ń lábití bi-beeŋi kí cìb̄. Man ubɔti Daariyusi di yóoǹ mara nee, bí ŋá m nín lī puee deedee.»

english_verse: With great success the Jewish leaders continued working on the temple, while Haggai and Zechariah encouraged them by their preaching. And so, the temple was completed at the command of the God of Israel and by the orders of kings Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes of Persia.
translation_verse: Juuda yab kpilib nìn nìkī kunimbɔtidii mātam an cōom̀ tiŋan, kii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Agaayi nì Idoo jipɔɔn Sakari nín nìn sòon̄ puee. Bi nìn máń kunimbɔtidii ki dóò kii Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nì Peeriisi yab bɔtiibi Siirusi nì Daariyusi nì Aritaseerseesi nín nìn yóoǹ mara yii bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: On the third day of the month of Adar in the sixth year of the rule of Darius, the temple was finished.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Daariyusi beel dibinluluutiil, uŋmal un bi yíì Adaaree wiiŋyi ita dal ní bi máń kunimbɔtidii ki dóò.

english_verse: The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned from exile were happy and celebrated as they dedicated God's temple.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee nìn jíń kunimbɔtidii gbanti jiŋaaliu ki dū-ku ki sú Unimbɔti nì dipɔɔpindi.

english_verse: One hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs were offered as sacrifices at the dedication. Also twelve goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū inajaa dilaataal nì ipijaa alaataa ali nì apibil alaataa anaa ní ki ŋá saraa kunimbɔtidii jiŋaaliu gbanti poon. Bi nìn dū iŋɔjaa saalaa nì ili ki ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ pu ki nóó nì Isirayeel naakɔti saalaa nì tilee nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: Then the priests and Levites were assigned their duties in God's temple in Jerusalem, according to the instructions Moses had written. The Passover
translation_verse: Bi nìn kāaǹ bisaraaŋaliibi ki nóó nì bi-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee, ní ki yākatì Leefii yab akiti akiti ki nóó nì bi-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee bí nīn tūǹ Unimbɔti tundi Jeerusaleem, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ pu Mooyiisi marab gbɔŋkunee. Juuda yab jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu

english_verse: Everyone who had returned from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
translation_verse: Bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki bāańee nìn jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu uŋmapeepeekaa poon ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal ní.

english_verse: The priests and Levites had gone through a ceremony to make themselves acceptable to lead in worship. Then some of them killed Passover lambs for those who had returned, including the other priests and themselves.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nín nìn kpáfì dicilpu ki ŋá akoobil ŋin bi ŋáań kí nyā tijɔkɔndinee, bi-kɔkɔ nìn bí circir dee. An pu ní bi nìn lāntì Dilákatil jiŋaaliu pibiliŋ ki tīī bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee, nì bi-nabiyaamu bisaraaŋaliibi nì bíǹ bi-ba mun.

english_verse: The sacrifices were eaten by the Israelites who had returned and by the neighboring people who had given up the sinful customs of other nations in order to worship the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí kitiŋin niin ní ki dū bin kaa nyí Unimbɔtee jɔkɔntuuŋŋi ki fée nìn kpáfì ki jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu. Binib gbantee nìn bí ki nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: For seven days they celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread. Everyone was happy because the Lord God of Israel had made sure that the king of Assyria would be kind to them and help them build the temple.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi jíń jiŋaal un bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee iwiin iluli nì dipɔɔpindi. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì dipɔɔpindi gbí-bi u nín kpántì Asuur yab bɔtiu pɔbil ki yāntì bi ká diyimɔɔl u-ceeyee pu. An nìn tīī-bi kunyannyaau bi ŋúń ki túń Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu diiku mātam tuuŋŋi.

english_verse: Much later, when Artaxerxes was king of Persia, Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylonia. Ezra was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Azariah. His other ancestors were Hilkiah, Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub, Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki, Abishua, Phinehas, Eleazar, and Aaron, the high priest. Ezra was an expert in the Law that the Lord God of Israel had given to Moses, and the Lord made sure that the king gave Ezra everything he asked for.
translation_verse: Eesiraasi gbanti nìn nyánní Babiloon ní. U nìn sá unil un nyí Mooyiisi marab bin ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nìn tīī u-nibul Isirayeel yabee tiŋan. Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nìn yú u-boon, an puee tin u yaa nìn bālifì ubɔtee, u nìn tìì-u ní.

english_verse: Other Jews, including priests, Levites, musicians, the temple guards, and servants, came to Jerusalem with Ezra. This happened during the seventh year that Artaxerxes was king.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Aritaseerseesi beel dibinluluútiil poon ní Isirayeel yab kansikin bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì biwambɔɔliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bin bí kunimbɔtidiin ki tútúǹ atuunee biba nìn yíkì ki nín gítí Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: God helped Ezra, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month of that seventh year, after leaving Babylonia on the first day of the first month.
translation_verse: U nìn bɔ́ntì ki yíkìń Babiloon uŋmapeepeekaa wimpeekaaŋu dal, ní ki dāa dūu bāań Jeerusaleem uŋmaŋmooŋmooti wimpeekaaŋu dal, kun puee u-Nimbɔtiu nìn yú u-boon.

english_verse: Ezra was a priest and an expert in the laws and commands that the Lord had given to Israel. One day King Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter which said:
translation_verse: Kugbɔŋu kun ubɔti Aritaseerseesi nìn ŋmàn̄ ki tīī Eesiraasi un sá usaraaŋal ki sá un nyí ti-Dindaan marab nì u-koobiliŋ tiŋan pu ki cáa dàkà Isirayeel yabee sèé:

english_verse: Greetings from the great King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and expert in the teachings of the God of heaven.
translation_verse: «Man Aritaseerseesi, bibɔtiibi kɔkɔ bɔtiu di ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee ki tīī sii usaraaŋal Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti un bí yilpuee marabee.

english_verse: Any of the people of Israel or their priests or Levites in my kingdom may go with you to Jerusalem if they want to. My seven advisors and I agree that you may go to Jerusalem and Judah to find out if the laws of your God are being obeyed.
translation_verse: Man ubɔti nì m-saŋkiliibi bilulee di tú-si á cù Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee poon kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí kpèè yii binib nóó a-Nimbɔtiu marab bin kā a-ŋaanee mana.

english_verse: When you go, take the silver and gold that I and my advisors are freely giving to the God of Israel, whose temple is in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Sii ní man nì m-saŋkiliibi tú á cáá animbil nì sindaariya un ti ŋá saraa kí tīī Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiuee kí cùnnì Jeerusaleem laakin Unimbɔti kɔŋkooŋŋu bée.

english_verse: Take the silver and gold that you collect from everywhere in Babylonia. Also take the gifts that your own people and priests have so willingly contributed for the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Á kpáaǹ animbil nì sindaariya nì tin kɔkɔ Babiloon timmu kɔkɔ yab tɔ́ ki tīī-see, nì Unimbɔti nibul nì bisaraaŋaliibi nín ŋá nlammɔntiim saraabi bin kí tūtuǹ bi-Nimbɔtiu diiku kun bí Jeerusaleemee tuuŋŋee.

english_verse: Use the money carefully to buy the best bulls, rams, lambs, grain, and wine. Then sacrifice them on the altar at God's temple in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Á tin dū animbil ŋin bi tɔ́ ki tīī-see kí dā inajaa nì ipijaa nì apibil nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa ŋáań saraayee nì ndaam min bi làá fée, kí dūú ŋá saraabi ni-Nimbɔtiu diiku saraafaŋŋu pu Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: If any silver or gold is left, you and your people may use it for whatever pleases your God.
translation_verse: Sii nì a-nabiyaamu ń kpèè kí dū animbil nì Sindaariya un kíǹee kí ŋá min ŋān̄ ni-ceeyee kí nóó ni-Nimbɔtiu nín là puee.

english_verse: Give your God the other articles that have been contributed for use in his temple.
translation_verse: Tiwan tin bi tīī-si bí nīn cáa tūǹ kunimbɔtidii poon tuuŋŋee, á cáá-tì kí yóoń Jeerusaleem Nimbɔtiu nimbiin.

english_verse: If you need to get anything else for the temple, you may have the money you need from the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Á dāá lēē lampoo nimbiliŋ ŋin ntimu pà ki tìì ubɔtee kí pà atuun ŋin kíǹ ki sá á púntí kí tɔ̄ a-Nimbɔtiu Diikunee.

english_verse: Ezra, you are a priest and an expert in the laws of the God of heaven, and I order all treasurers in Western Province to do their very best to help you.
translation_verse: «Man ubɔti Aritaseerseesi, m yóoǹ mara ntimu mun bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee nimbiŋubiliibi yii usaraaŋal Eesiraasi un dàkà Unimbɔti un bí yilpuee marabee yaa bālifì tiŋyee, bí ŋá míǹ kí tīī-u deedee.

english_verse: tons of silver,
translation_verse: Seeraya nì Usii nì Bukii nì

english_verse: They must provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that he won't be angry with me and with the kings who rule after me.
translation_verse: Tin kɔkɔ Unimbɔti un náań yilpuee bālifèe, ŋámaan míǹ deedee, án nín làá ŋá pu ú taa fōō diŋuul m-beel nì m-jipɔmbi puee.

english_verse: We want you to know that no priests, Levites, musicians, guards, temple servants, or any other temple workers will have to pay any kind of taxes.
translation_verse: Ti gíti là ní béé yii mara kaa pú yii bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bitɔntɔnliibi nì bin tūǹ kunimbɔtidii poon atuunee ń pà lampoo nì patantib nì animbil ŋin bisaŋkinliibi pèe.

english_verse: Ezra, use the wisdom God has given you and choose officials and leaders to govern the people of Western Province. These leaders should know God's laws and have them taught to anyone who doesn't know them.
translation_verse: «An yaa kíǹ sii Eesiraasee, á dū iciin in Unimbɔti marau un kā a-ŋaanee dàkèe kí kàan̄ bibɔsoonliibi bí dū ibaamɔn kí sòoǹ ntimu mun bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee nib bin kɔkɔ nyí a-Nimbɔtiu marabee bɔti, ní kí dàkà bin kaa nyí marabee bí béé-bi.

english_verse: Everyone who fails to obey God's Law or the king's law will be punished without pity. They will either be executed or put in prison or forced to leave their country, or have all they own taken away. Ezra Praises God
translation_verse: Un sá kamaa kaa tɔ́ a-Nimbɔtiu marau kaa tɔ́ ubɔti marauee, bí dáaĺ udaan tafal. An yaa sá bí kpɔ̀-uee, bí kpɔ̀-u. An yaa sá bí jà-u kí nyāntí kitiŋ puee, bí jà-u. An yaa sá bí gíí-u dipɔndee, bí gíí-u, an yaa tí sá bí pìin̄-u sarkee, bí pìin̄-u.» Eesiraasi jáam̀ Unimbɔti

english_verse: Because King Artaxerxes was so kind, Ezra said: Praise the Lord God of our ancestors! He made sure that the king honored the Lord's temple in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: «Ti jáam̀ ti-Dindaan ti-naanjab Nimbɔtiu un gbēē ubɔti pɔbil ki yāntì u tīī ti-Dindaan Diiku kun bí Jeerusaleemee tinyoolee.

english_verse: God has told the king, his advisors, and his powerful officials to treat me with kindness. The Lord God has helped me, and I have been able to bring many Jewish leaders back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nì u-saŋkinliibi nì u-kàliŋkpilib nimbiin ní ti-Dindaan dàkā-mi u-ŋanti yii u bí m-cee. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu ŋal nìn pá m-pu ní m ŋúń ki kpáfì Isirayeel yab kpilib biba ní man nì bi yíkìń Babiloon.»

english_verse: Artaxerxes was king of Persia when I led the following chiefs of the family groups from Babylonia to Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Ubɔti Aritaseerseesi beel yuntiŋu bin nìn nóoń-mi ti yíkìń Babiloonee dicaŋŋi kpilib nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee sèé.

english_verse: Gershom of the Phinehas family; Daniel of the Ithamar family; Hattush son of Shecaniah of the David family; Zechariah and
translation_verse: ní Utayii nì Sakuur sá Biigifayi maaliŋun yab kpilib. Bi-nib nìn nyáń bininjab imuŋku ita nì saalaa. Eesiraasi yíkìi ki nín cá Jeerusaleem

english_verse: I said to the priests: You belong to the Lord, the God of your ancestors, and these things also belong to him. The silver and gold were willingly given as gifts to the Lord.
translation_verse: M nìn bí-bi yii: «Ni sá binib bin dū bi-ba ki sú ti-Dindaanee ní. Tiwan nee mun sá tin bi dūu súee ní. Animbil nì sindaariya nee sá nlammɔntiim saraau ní bi ŋá ki tīī ni-baabi Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: I brought everyone together by the river that flows to the town of Ahava where we camped for three days. Not one Levite could be found among the people and priests.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m yíiń binib gbanti ki kpáfì mbun ŋun pùub̀ ki cá Aafa watil púee. Ti nìn kāl̀ niin iwiin ita. M nìn dáań ki ká yii bisaraaŋaliibi dikitil gbanti poon, Leefii yab báà ubɔ nìn kpá.

english_verse: So I sent for the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were very wise counselors.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m yíiń adican kpilib Eeliyeeseer nì Ariyeel nì Seemaya nì Eelnatan nì Yariib nì Eelnatan nì Naatan nì Seekariya nì Meesulam nì Yooyariib nì Eelnatan bimaradakaliibi bilee.

english_verse: Then I sent them to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, and I told them to ask him and his temple workers to send people to serve in God's temple.
translation_verse: M nìn tú-bi Kasfiya timbiliiki bɔtiu Idoo cee, ní ki tùkū-bi bi nín làá tin sòoǹ tin Idoo nì u-nabiyaamu bin bí Kasfiya tiŋkin ki sá kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibee pu bí tīiń-ti bitɔntɔnliibi bí nīn bí ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku poon ki tūǹ atuunee.

english_verse: God was kind to us and caused them to send a skillful man named Sherebiah, who was a Levite from the family of Mahli. Eighteen of his relatives came with him.
translation_verse: Kii ti-Nimbɔtiu ŋal nín nìn wúń ti-pu puee, bi nìn cáań-ti uninja ubɔ bi yíì-u Seereebiya. U nìn cáá dinyil ní ki nìn sá Malii maaliŋun, Jaakɔb jipɔɔn Leefii naakookun, u nì u-nabiyaamu nì u-jipɔmbi saalku nì bita.

english_verse: We were also sent Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the family of Merari along with
translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti cáań Meerarii maaliŋun yab Asabiya nì u-nabiki Yeesaya nì bi-jipɔmbi. Bi nìn kpáfì binib mmuŋku.

english_verse: Beside the Ahava River, I asked the people to go without eating and to pray. We humbled ourselves and asked God to bring us and our children safely to Jerusalem with all of our possessions.
translation_verse: Aafa buŋŋu caŋin niin ní m lēē yii tí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ kí sìntī ti-ba taapu ti-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin kí mèè-u ú pɔ̄-ti diyimɔɔl tí còom̀ disaŋkimmɔntiil ti nì ti-biyaamu nì tin kɔkɔ ti cááyee.

english_verse: So we went without food and asked God himself to protect us, and he answered our prayers. The Gifts for the Temple
translation_verse: An pu ní ti bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ki mēē ti-Nimbɔtiu ú yūĺ ti-boon, ní u fōō ti-wimmeem.

english_verse: I chose twelve of the leading priests—Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their relatives.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní m lēē bisaraaŋaliibi saalaa nì bili, ní ki dū Seereebiya nì Asabiya nì bi-nabiyaamu saalaa mun ki kútì bi-pu.

english_verse: Be sure to guard them and keep them safe until you reach Jerusalem. Then weigh them inside God's temple in the presence of the chief priests, the Levites, and the heads of the Israelite families.
translation_verse: Ní kpèè tiwan gbanti mmɔntiim, kí ŋúb́-tì tiŋan kí cáá-tì kí bànnì Jeerusaleem bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib nimbiin kunimbɔtidii dibiyaamun.»

english_verse: The priests and Levites then took charge of the gifts that had been weighed, so they could take them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem. The Return to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Niinee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yabee yōoǹ sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tigaajawan tin bi ŋmāntì ki tīī-bee ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem ki yóoǹ ti-Nimbɔtiu diikun. Eesiraasi nì u-yab bàn̄ Jeerusaleem

english_verse: On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River and started for Jerusalem. Our God watched over us, and as we traveled along, he kept our enemies from ambushing us.
translation_verse: Ti nìn yíkì uŋmapeepeekaa poon iwiin saalaa nì ili dal Aafa buŋŋu caŋin ki nín cá Jeerusaleem. Ti-Nimbɔtiu nìn bīiǹ ti-saŋkindi gbanti pu, binannanliibi kaa táká-taaa, biyipɔɔdambi mun kaa kíntì-ti nsanni ki fúkúl̀-ti.

english_verse: After arriving in Jerusalem, we rested for three days.
translation_verse: Ti nìn bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee ní ki dū iwiin ita ki kāl̀ ki ŋūŋfì.

english_verse: Then on the fourth day we went to God's temple, where the silver, the gold, and the other things were weighed and given to the priest Meremoth son of Uriah. With him were Eleazar son of Phinehas and the two Levites, Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
translation_verse: Ŋwinnanaatee ní ti ŋmāntì animbil kúti nì sindaariya nì tigaajawanee ti-Nimbɔtiu diikun ki dūu tīī usaraaŋal Uriya jipɔɔn Meereemooti. U nì Piinaasi jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar nì Leefii yab Joosuwa jipɔɔn Yoosabaadi nì Binuyii jipɔɔn Noowadiya di nìn bí.

english_verse: goats were sacrificed for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Akatan jipɔɔn Yoowanan sá Asigaadi maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab dilaataal nì saalaa.

english_verse: Some of those who had returned took the king's orders to the governors and officials in Western Province. Then the officials did what they could for the people and for the temple of God.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi dū kugbɔŋu kun ubɔtikpaan ŋmàn̄née ki tīī ubɔti kàliŋkpilib nì gɔminab bin bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmunee, ní bi-kɔkɔ tútúǹ Isirayeel yab bi máń Unimbɔti diiku.

english_verse: Later the Jewish leaders came to me and said: Many Israelites, including priests and Levites, are living just like the people around them. They are even guilty of some of the horrible sins of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Tíǹ jítì boonee ní Isirayeel kpilib biba dɔ́miń ki tùkū-mi yii: «Isirayeel nibul nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab kaa gāntì bi-ba nì kitiŋ nee pu nibuliŋ ŋin kíǹee. Bi mun bí ki ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi kii Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Jeebusi yab nì Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì Eejipiti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nín ŋáań puee ní.

english_verse: Some Israelite men have married foreign women and have let their sons do the same thing. Our own officials and leaders were the first to commit this disgusting sin, and now God's holy people are mixed with foreigners.
translation_verse: Bíǹ bi-ba cáá niin tiŋkin binimpoobi, ní ki cáá ki tīī bi-jipɔmbi mun ní dinibul din bí circiree dūu ŋmālim̀ niin tiŋki nibin. Adican kpilib nì abɔtibil di péé péé ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi gbantin.»

english_verse: This news made me so angry that I ripped my clothes and tore hair from my head and beard. Then I just sat in shock
translation_verse: M nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee ní m dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin m pēēyee, ní ki dáaĺ ki fùkū m-yikpiti nì m-nyimpul, ní ki kíǹ ki kā nì kunimbaau.

english_verse: until the time for the evening sacrifice. Many of our people were greatly concerned and gathered around me, because the God of Israel had warned us to stay away from foreigners. Ezra's Prayer
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ nìn tɔ́ Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bɔtee nín gbìl̄ atuŋkpiti ŋin bin nyánní kuyuŋuee ŋée, ní bi kóoǹní ki dɔ́miń ki kpáfì m-cee. Ama mamee, m nìn pée kā nì kunimbaau míǹ ní áli kujoou saraau yuntiŋu. Eesiraasi mēē ki tīī Juuda yab bin yīntèe

english_verse: At the time of the evening sacrifice, I was still sitting there in sorrow with my clothes all torn. So I got down on my knees, then lifted my arms,
translation_verse: Kujoou saraau yuntiŋu ní m nyáń m-nimbaaku poon. M nìn gbíntìi pēē m-wanti tin m nìn dáaĺ ki cátèe, ní ki gbāaǹ m-tabiŋyiliŋ pu, ní ki yōoǹ m-ŋalii ki túĺ ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu watil pú.

english_verse: and prayed: I am much too ashamed to face you, Lord God. Our sins and our guilt have swept over us like a flood that reaches up to the heavens.
translation_verse: M nìn mēē-u yii: «M-Nimbɔtiu, icoo cúú-mi ní m bākatì, maa ŋūǹ kí wáaǹ kí kpèè sii m-Nimbɔtiu watil pú gba. Di sá ti-kpitii wíiǹ ki lákatì ti-yil pu ní ti-yìntitam kpúkú ki tin sāā kutagbɔŋu.

english_verse: Since the time of our ancestors, all of us have sinned. That's why we, our kings, and our priests have often been defeated by other kings. They have killed some of us and made slaves of others; they have taken our possessions and made us ashamed, just as we are today.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ti-naanjab yuntiŋu kí dāá sāā díǹ nee, ti yīntiǹ-si ŋkpitim pu. Ti-kpitii puee a dū timbi nì ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-saraaŋaliibi ki líiǹ kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi nì kujaau, ki yāntì bi cúú-ti kuyuŋu ki fúkúl̀-ti ki kɔ́ǹ-ti icoo, kii an nín bí-ti díǹ pu nan ní.

english_verse: But for now, Lord God, you have shown great kindness to us. You made us truly happy by letting some of us settle in this sacred place and by helping us in our time of slavery.
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, a dàkā-ti kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ki yāntì ti-kansikin biba dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin ki gítìń ki kāl̀ a-circir tiŋkin. Ti-Nimbɔtiu, a ŋá míǹ ki yāntì ti-nimbiliŋ ŋāatì ní ti ká dimaŋfapɔndi ti-yuŋku poon.

english_verse: We are slaves, but you have never turned your back on us. You love us, and because of you, the kings of Persia have helped us. It's as though you have given us new life! You let us rebuild your temple and live safely in Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti nìn sá iyumbu ní, ama ti-yuŋku gbanti poonee, sii ti-Nimbɔtiu kaa nìn dū-ti ki fá. A yāntì Peeriisi yab bɔtiibi dàkā-ti kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu. A tīī-ti dimaŋfal ti ŋúń ki fātìi máń sii ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku, ní ki ŋáŋkì ku-digbuŋŋi ní ki ŋúń ki máń agun ki tú Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee.

english_verse: Our God, what can we say now? Even after all this, we have disobeyed the commands
translation_verse: «Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Nimbɔtiu, tilati ní ti cáá kí lì tin bāań nee pu? Di sá yii ti fātì ti-boon ki tīī a-marab

english_verse: that were given to us by your servants the prophets. They said the land you are giving us is full of sinful and wicked people, who never stop doing disgusting things.
translation_verse: bin ní a nìn dī a-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi pu ki tīī-tee. A nìn kpáafì-ti ki lī yii: <Kitiŋ kin ni làá cùú fōō kí nīn kóò nee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi binib bin kóò ki-nee jɔkɔntuuŋŋi pu. Di sá yii kí yòon̄ laakin kitiŋ nee kífée kí cáá kúntí ki-gbeennyɔkɔee, an sá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi tūǹee ŋma ní bi dūu gbéeǹ-kì.

english_verse: And we were warned not to let our daughters and sons marry their sons and daughters. Your prophets also told us never to help those foreigners or even let them live in peace. You wanted us to become strong and to enjoy the good things in the land, then someday to leave it to our children forever.
translation_verse: An puee ní taa dū ni-bisalib kí tīī bi-jipɔmbi ticati, kí taa cáá bi-bisalib kí tīī ni-jipɔmbi.
