Ni yaa là kí nīn cáá mpɔn kí jī kitiŋ gbanti naam, ni-biyaamu mun ń dāá yīkì kí tɔ́kɔń kí nīn pée jīǹ ki cá jaanjaanee, ní taa dī isaŋkpiti in pu bíǹ bí an bútì-bee pu, kí taa nyàab̀ bi-gbansɔŋfiŋu juti ŋwindal.>

english_verse: You punished us because of our terrible sins. But you did not punish us nearly as much as we deserve, and you have brought some of us back home.
translation_verse: Tin kɔkɔ pée bāań-ti nee nyánní ti-tuŋkpitiŋ nì ikpitikpaan in ti ŋée pu ní. Óò ti-Nimbɔtiu, nì míǹ kɔkɔee, aa dáaĺ ti-tafal ki bàn̄ ti-kpitii nín sá puee nyɔkɔm, ní ki yāntì ti-nibul poon biba kíǹ kaa kpíì.

english_verse: Why should we disobey your commands again by letting our sons and daughters marry these foreigners who do such disgusting things? That would make you angry enough to destroy us all!
translation_verse: Tinee boonee, ti bàà gíti cáá nsan kí tí kíĺ kí nīn yìntīǹ a-marab ti nì anibul ŋin ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋee ń ŋá ubaanti, ti cāab̀ tɔbaaa? Aa fòol̄ ti-pu diŋuul áli kí kúntí-ti ubɔ ń taa kíń, àá ubɔ ń taa ŋmátáaa?

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you have been more than fair by letting a few of us survive. But once again, our sins have made us ashamed to face you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, a sá deedeedaan ní. Díǹ pu nee a yāntì ti-kansikin biba kíǹ kaa kpíì. Kpèè timbi di yú a-nimbiin ti nì ti-kpitii nee, ama ubɔ kpá ki bí tin poon timbi bí nee kí ŋmā kí yūĺ a-nimbiin.»

english_verse: While Ezra was down on his knees in front of God's temple, praying with tears in his eyes and confessing the sins of the people of Israel, a large number of men, women, and children gathered around him and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Eesiraasi gbāā ki sūǹ kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu ki mèé Unimbɔti bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam puee, Isirayeel yab dinikitikpaandi, bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu dɔ́miń ki māntì tú-u ní ki bíi sūǹ tikpil.

english_verse: Shecaniah son of Jehiel from the family of Elam said: Ezra, we have disobeyed God by marrying these foreign women. But there is still hope for the people of Israel,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yeeyiyeel jipɔɔn Seekaniya un sá Eelaam maaliŋunee bí Eesiraasi yii: «Taa yúliǹ ti-Nimbɔtiu deedee ki cáá binicannimpoobi bin sá kitiŋ nee poon nimpubiyaamuee. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, dimákal diba gbíntìi dáá bí ki tīī Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: if we follow your advice and the advice of others who truly respect the laws of God. We must promise God that we will divorce our foreign wives and send them away, together with their children.
translation_verse: Tí lēēmaan ti-pɔbiliŋ poon kɔŋkɔnnee kí ŋá mpèé nì ti-Nimbɔtiu yii ti làá jà binicannimpoobi gbanti kɔkɔ ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu, kii sii ti-kpiliu nì bin kɔkɔ fàŋkí ti-Nimbɔtiu marabee nín sáŋkì-ti puee. Ti làá ŋá kí nóó nì mara.

english_verse: Ezra, it's up to you to do something! We will support whatever you do. So be brave!
translation_verse: Yīkìm̄, kun puee sii di làá ŋāŋkì tibɔti nee. Timbi yú a-boon, ká kunyannyaau kí ŋá min máaǹee kí taa gùgufì.»

english_verse: Ezra stood up and made the chief priests, the Levites, and everyone else in Israel swear that they would follow the advice of Shecaniah.
translation_verse: Niinee Eesiraasi yíkì ní ki yāntì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ pūtì yii bi làá ŋá kii Seekaniya nín sòon̄ puee, ní bi-kɔkɔ pūtì.

english_verse: Then Ezra left God's temple and went to spend the night in the living quarters of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He felt sorry because of what the people had done, and he did not eat or drink a thing.
translation_verse: Ní Eesiraasi nyáń kunimbɔtidii cindin ki cūtìi kɔ́ Eeliyasiib jipɔɔn Yoowanan diikun ki dōoǹ, ama waa nìn jíń báà tiba kaa nìn nyùn̄ mun. Di sá yii bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee nín nìn ŋá ikpitikpaan iŋyee nìn sá-u kii dikpoolee ní u kā.

english_verse: The officials and leaders sent a message to all who had returned from Babylonia and were now living in Jerusalem and Judah. This message told them to meet in Jerusalem within three days, or else they would lose everything they owned and would no longer be considered part of the people that had returned from Babylonia.
translation_verse: Adican kpilib nì abɔtibil nìn sòon̄ ki yóoǹ yii nì iwiin ita poonee, un yaa kaa dɔ́mińee, bí fōō u-wanti tin kɔkɔ u cááyee, ní kí jà úǹ u-ba kí nyāntí bin nyánní kuyuŋuee kansikin.

english_verse: Three days later, on the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem and sat in the temple courtyard. It was a serious meeting, and they sat there, trembling in the rain.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab bininjab kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin iwiin ita gbanti poon. An nìn sá uŋmawawati poon iwiin mmuŋku dal ní. Binib kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì kunimbɔtidii mɔŋkiŋu tiwun jìkì tin poon bi bée pu. Kí kūtèe utaa nín bíi nì.

english_verse: Ezra the priest stood up and said: You have broken God's Law by marrying foreign women, and you have made the whole nation guilty!
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal Eesiraasi nìn yáatìi yúl̀ ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ni nín cáá binicannimpoobee, naa yúliǹ Unimbɔti deedee, ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab bɔkpil gíti nyāŋkì.

english_verse: Now you must confess your sins to the Lord God of your ancestors and obey him. Divorce your foreign wives and don't have anything to do with the rest of the foreigners who live around here.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní tīīmaan ti-Dindaan ni-baabi Nimbɔtiu tinyool, kí ŋámaan min u lèe. Ni nì kitiŋ nee pu yab ń yàkatī tɔbin ní ní jà binicannimpoobi bin ni cááyee.»

english_verse: Everyone in the crowd shouted: You're right! We will do what you say.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì niinee nìn kíí mpɔn yii: «A cáá mbaamɔn! Án pée sá tí ŋá kii a nín lī pu nee ní.

english_verse: But there are so many of us, and we can't just stay out here in this downpour. A lot of us have sinned by marrying foreign women, and the matter can't be settled in only a day or two.
translation_verse: Ama ti wīikí ní an sá kuseeun mun. Taa ŋūǹ kí nīn yú mpaampiin pu míǹ. Kí wàatī muee taa ŋūǹ kí dū ŋwiin ŋubɔ àá ili gba kí ŋāŋkì tibɔti nee, kun puee ti-kansikin tikpil bí ki ŋá ikpiti tibɔti nee poon.

english_verse: Why can't our officials stay on in Jerusalem and take care of this for us? Let everyone who has sinned in this way meet here at a certain time with leaders and judges from their own towns. If we take care of this problem, God will surely stop being so terribly angry with us.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ti-kpilib ń gbíntí doo samaa kɔkɔ yil pu. Bí yóoń bin kɔkɔ cáá binicannimpoobee iyunti ní báà ŋma ń nīn dòoń ŋyunti ŋun bi yóoǹ-uee, u nì u-tiŋki kpilib nì ki-bɔsoonliibi, ní bí kpèè tibɔti gbanti kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní Unimbɔti ŋuul làá sɔ̀ŋkì timbi puee.»

english_verse: Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were the only ones who objected, except for the two Levites, Meshullam and Shabbethai.
translation_verse: Asayeel jipɔɔn Joonatan nì Tiisfa jipɔɔn Yasiya baba di kaa nìn kíí ki tɔ́kɔǹ nlandɔkɔ ŋun bi cáańee pu. Meesulam nì uleefiija Sabeetayi mun nìn yú bi-boon.

english_verse: Everyone else who had returned from exile agreed with the plan. So Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of the families, and he listed their names. They started looking into the matter on the first day of the tenth month,
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee nìn fōō an bɔtee ki làá ŋá míǹ. Usaraaŋal Eesiraasi nìn sāā kudicaŋu kamaa poonee bininjab kansikin ubɔ diŋambil, ki lēē-u ú nīn sá kudicaŋu kpiliu. An nibee nìn kpáfì uŋmaliliiti wimpeekaaŋu dal ki kíĺ kí kpèè tibɔti gbanti.

english_verse: and they did not finish until the first day of the first month of the next year. The Men Who Had Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Bi dāa ŋáŋkì bininjab bin kɔkɔ cáá binicannimpoobee bɔti ki dóò dibindi poon uŋmapeepeekaa wimpeepeekaaŋu dal ní. Bininjab bin nìn ŋá ikpitee yiŋŋi

english_verse: Hanani and Zebadiah from the family of Immer;
translation_verse: Imeer maaliŋun yab kansikinee, Ananii nì Seebadiya.

english_verse: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah from the family of Harim;
translation_verse: Ariim maaliŋun yab kansikinee, Maseeyawuu nì Eeliya nì Seemaya nì Yeeyiyeel nì Usiyasi.

english_verse: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah from the family of Pashhur.
translation_verse: Pasuur maaliŋun yab kansikinee, Eeliyooweenayi nì Maseeyawuu nì Isimaayeel nì Neetaneeyeel nì Yoosabaadi nì Eeleeyasa.

english_verse: Those Levites who had foreign wives were: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah , Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
translation_verse: Bi-kansikinee bin sá Leefii naakookun yabee di sá Yoosabaadi nì Simeeyii nì Keedaya, nì Peetayia nì Yeewuda nì Eeliyeeseer.

english_verse: Eliashib, the musician, had a foreign wife. These temple guards had foreign wives: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
translation_verse: Biwambɔɔliibi kansikinee, Eeliyasiib. Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kansikinee, Saaluum nì Teeleem nì Uurii.

english_verse: Here is a list of the others from Israel who had foreign wives: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah from the family of Parosh;
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee kansikinee, Pareeyoosi maaliŋun yab di sá Ramiya nì Yiisiya nì Maalkiya nì Miiniyaamiini nì Eeleeyasaar nì Maalkiya nì Beenaya.

english_verse: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah from the family of Elam;
translation_verse: Eelaam maaliŋun yab di sá Mataniya nì Seekariya nì Yeeyiyeel nì Abidii nì Yeereemooti nì Eeliya.

english_verse: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza from the family of Zattu;
translation_verse: Satu maaliŋun yab di sá Eeliyooweenayi nì Eeliyasiib nì Mataniya nì Yeereemooti nì Sabaadi nì Asiisa.

english_verse: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai from the family of Bebai;
translation_verse: Beebaayi maaliŋun yab di sá Yoowanan nì Ananiya nì Sabaayi nì Atilayi.

english_verse: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth from the family of Bani;
translation_verse: Banii maaliŋun yab di sá Meesulam nì Maluuki nì Adaaya nì Akuub nì Seeyal nì Yeereemooti.

english_verse: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh from the family of Pahath Moab;
translation_verse: Paati-Moowaab maaliŋun yab di sá Adina nì Keelaal nì Beenaya nì Maseeyawuu nì Mataniya nì Beesaleel nì Binuyii nì Manasee.

english_verse: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei from the family of Hashum;
translation_verse: Asuum maaliŋun yab di sá Mateenayi nì Mataata nì Sabaadi nì Eeliifeeleeti nì Yeereemayi nì Manasee nì Simeeyii.

english_verse: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah from the family of Nebo.
translation_verse: Neeboo maaliŋun yab di sá Yiyeel nì Matitiya nì Sabaadi nì Seebina nì Yadidayi nì Jooweel nì Beenaya.

english_verse: These men divorced their foreign wives, then sent them and their children away.
translation_verse: Bininjab gbanti kɔkɔ di nìn cáá binicannimpoobi, ní bi-kansikin tikpil nìn màl̄ mbiyaamu.

english_verse: I am Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and in this book I tell what I have done. During the month of Chislev in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes ruled Persia, I was in his fortress city of Susa,
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin Akaliya jipɔɔn Neeyeemiya máafèe. Bi máafì Neeyeemiya tin bíi jītí Jeerusaleemee Ubɔti Aritaseerseesi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin mmuŋku, Kiisileewu ŋmaliu poonee, m nìn bí Suusi ditiŋyil,

english_verse: when my brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped from being captives in Babylonia. I also asked them about the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: ní Ananii m-nabiyaamu kansikin ubɔ, u nì Juuda yab dikitil diba dɔ́miń m-cee. M nìn bālifì-bi Juuda yab bin nyáń kuyuŋu ki kùn̄ee nì Jeerusaleem pu.

english_verse: They told me, “Those captives who have come back are having all kinds of troubles. They are terribly disgraced, Jerusalem's walls are broken down, and its gates have been burned.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-mi yii: «Bin ŋmátì kaa kpíì kuyuŋun ní ki kóò Juuda timmunee bí falaakpaan nì icoo poon ní. Jeerusaleem gundi bátì bátì ki lítì, abun dōoǹ dōoǹ ní punuubi wùn̄ ŋŋmi.» Neeyeemiya mēē ki tīī Juuda yab

english_verse: When I heard this, I sat down on the ground and cried. Then for several days, I mourned; I went without eating to show my sorrow, and I prayed:
translation_verse: M nín nìn gbìl̄ an bɔtee, m nìn kāl̀ ní ki bíi sūǹ. M nìn kāl̀ kunimbaaun iwiin kupaau, ki bóob́ kinyɔkɔ, ki gbāaǹ yilpu Nimbɔtiu nimbiin ki mēē.

english_verse: Lord God of heaven, you are great and fearsome. And you faithfully keep your promises to everyone who loves you and obeys your commands.
translation_verse: M nìn mēē yii: «Too, m-Dindaan yilpu Nimbɔtiu, Unimbɔti un sá ukpaan ki sá kuwambiiuee, sii di kaa súntí jaanjaan a nín pōoǹ bin néeń-si ki ŋúb́ a-marabee pu ní ki ŋáań-bi tiŋan.

english_verse: I am your servant, so please have mercy on me and answer the prayer that I make day and night for these people of Israel who serve you. I, my family, and the rest of your people have sinned
translation_verse: Kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì, kí ŋúbití a-nimbiliŋ kí wāl̀ man a-tɔntɔnliu nín bí ki mèé-si iyunti nee poon ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu a-tɔntɔnliibi Isirayeel yab pu puee. M bí ki bìitī ikpiti in ní timbi Isirayeel yab ŋá-see. Ti yīntiǹ-si, tiŋman man nì m-naanjab yīntiǹ-si.

english_verse: by choosing to disobey you and the laws and teachings you gave to your servant Moses.
translation_verse: Tiŋman ti baasii yīntiǹ-si ní, kun puee taa ŋúb́ marab nì abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin a nìn tīī a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi u dūu tīī-tee.

english_verse: Please remember the promise you made to Moses. You told him that if we were unfaithful, you would scatter us among foreign nations.
translation_verse: Téetí anyɔɔbun ŋin a nìn dī a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu ki sòon̄ee. A nìn bí yii: <Ni yaa kaa yúliǹ-mi deedee, m làá dāá jà-ni ní yàl̄ kí kɔ́ atimbun aban.

english_verse: But you also said that no matter how far away we were, we could turn to you and start obeying your laws. Then you would bring us back to the place where you have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa láa fātìi gítìń m-cee, ki ŋúb́ m-marab, ki ŋáań bi nín bí ní ŋá puee, báà ni yaa láa bíń kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ, m làá dāá kóoǹní-ni kí kpāfì kí yàntī ní dāan̄ laakin m làá lēē bí nīn jáaḿ-mee.>

english_verse: Our Lord, I am praying for your servants—those you rescued by your great strength and mighty power.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, bi sá a-tɔntɔnliibi ní ki sá a-nibul din a dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì a-kpabil ki dée.

english_verse: Please answer my prayer and the prayer of your other servants who gladly honor your name. When I serve the king his wine today, make him pleased with me and let him do what I ask.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, m gbàam̄-si, kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu nì a-tɔntɔnliibi bin an mɔ̄ǹ bí nīn fàŋkí-see wimmeem. Yàntī án kàlīǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu tiŋan díǹ ubɔti ń fōō-mi nì tiniti.» Ŋyunti gbantee, m nìn sá un tìì ubɔti ndaamee ní.

english_verse: During the month of Nisan in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king, I served him his wine, as I had done before. But this was the first time I had ever looked depressed.
translation_verse: Dalba Niisan ŋmaliu poon, ubɔti Aritaseerseesi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin mmuŋku poonee, ndaam nìn yú u-nimbiin ní m yōoǹ ki tīī-u. Doooo nee, maa láá pée yúl̀ u-nimbiin nì kunimbaau míǹ ki ká.

english_verse: So the king said, “Why do you look so sad? You're not sick. Something must be bothering you.” Even though I was frightened,
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn bālifì-mi yii: «Ba pu ní a-nimbiin bóob́ míǹ? A būǹ níii? Kunimbaau di cáá-saaa?» Niinee ní tifaandi tiba cúú-mi tikpil.

english_verse: I answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! I feel sad because the city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”
translation_verse: Ní m bí ubɔti yii: «Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn baabadal! Mana ní m-nimbiin kaa làá nīn bóob́, ŋyunti ŋun ní kitiŋ kin poon bi síb́ m-naanjabee kpántì adigbun ní ŋŋmi wùn̄ ki-punuubee?»

english_verse: The king asked, “What do you want me to do?” I prayed to the God who rules from heaven.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bālifì-mi yii: «Ba ní a là ḿ ŋá kí tīī-si?» Ní m mēē yilpu Nimbɔtiu,

english_verse: Then I told the king, “Sir, if it's all right with you, please send me back to Judah, so that I can rebuild the city where my ancestors are buried.”
translation_verse: ní ki bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, an yaa ŋān̄ a-cee ní man a-tɔntɔnliu bɔti yaa fáatiǹ-si, á tɔ̄-mi Juuda tiŋkin laakin bi síb́ m-naanjabee, ḿ cùú fàtīí mā-kì.»

english_verse: The queen was sitting beside the king when he asked me, “How long will it take, and when will you be back?” The king agreed to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
translation_verse: Unimpubɔti nìn kā ki kɔ́ĺ ubɔti ní u bālifì-mi yii: «A-saŋŋu gbanti làá fōō iwiin iŋa? Ní ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá fàtīí gítiń?» An nìn kítì ubɔti cee ú yàntī ḿ cù, ní m yóoǹ-u ŋyunti ŋun m làá gítińee.

english_verse: Then I asked, “Your Majesty, would you be willing to give me letters to the governors of the provinces west of the Euphrates River, so that I can travel safely to Judah?
translation_verse: Ní m gíti bí ubɔti yii: «A yaa bàà kíikí kí tīī-mi kugbɔŋu ḿ cáá tīī ntimu mun bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee gɔminab, bí pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ jītí bi-timmun kí cù Juuda tiŋkin.

english_verse: I will need timber to rebuild the gates of the fortress near the temple and more timber to construct the city wall and to build a place for me to live. And so, I would appreciate a letter to Asaph, who is in charge of the royal forest.” God was good to me, and the king did everything I asked.
translation_verse: Á bàà gíti tīī-mi kugbɔŋu kubɔ mun ḿ cáá tīī sii ubɔti saakpeeliu Asaafi ú tīī-mi idɔ ḿ cáá kpáá sintil difɔkɔku kun yú ki pìl̄ kunimbɔtidiiyee punyɔmmu nì kitiŋ gundi nì kudii kun m làá nīn kóòyee.» Ubɔti nìn tīī-mi kugbɔŋu gbanti, kun puee Unimbɔti nìn yú m-boon.

english_verse: The king sent some army officers and cavalry troops along with me, and as I traveled through the Western Provinces, I gave the letters to the governors.
translation_verse: M nìn cūtì ntimu mun bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee gɔminab cee, ní ki dū tigbɔn tin ubɔti nìn tīī-mee ki tīī-bi. Ubɔti nìn yāntì bijanjakpilib nì bitanjakaliibi céeǹ-mi.

english_verse: But when Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about what had happened, they became very angry, because they didn't want anyone to help the people of Israel. Nehemiah Inspects the Wall of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Sambalati un sá Oorɔn tiŋkinee nì uamɔnja Toobiya, u-taapu yɔu nín gbìl̄ yii m bāańee, an kaa mɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi yii ubɔ dɔ́miń ki nyàab̀ Isirayeel yab ŋanti. Neeyeemiya yìin̄ ki kpēē Jeerusaleem guŋŋi

english_verse: Three days after arriving in Jerusalem,
translation_verse: M bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee, m kāl̀ iwiin ita ní.

english_verse: I got up during the night and left my house. I took some men with me, without telling anyone what I thought God wanted me to do for the city. The only animal I took was the donkey I rode on.
translation_verse: Kunyeeuee, man nì bininjab biba nìn yíkì, ama maa nìn pée tùkū báà ubɔ tin Unimbɔti nìn dūu ŋá m-pɔbilin ḿ ŋá kí tīī Jeerusaleemee. Maa nìn cáá kuwaŋkuluu kubɔ ki kútì kimaŋ kin m nìn kēe pu.

english_verse: I went through Valley Gate on the west, then south past Dragon Spring, before coming to Garbage Gate. As I rode along, I took a good look at the crumbled walls of the city and the gates that had been torn down and burned.
translation_verse: M nìn dūu dī Ditantakal punyɔkɔki ki nyáń ki cūtì Draagɔn nyimbuliŋu nì titampuntan punyɔkɔki. M nìn kpēē Jeerusaleem gundi ki tin kátì ní ki ká yii ajan bátì bátì ki lítì, ní punuubi wùn̄ ŋŋmi.

english_verse: On the east side of the city, I headed north to Fountain Gate and King's Pool, but then the trail became too narrow for my donkey.
translation_verse: Ní m nìkī ki nín cá Nnyimbul punyɔkɔki watil, ki jítì ubɔti bɔɔku caŋin, ní nsan nìn gíti kpá kimaŋ kin m kēe ń dī.

english_verse: So I went down to Kidron Valley and looked at the wall from there. Then before daylight I returned to the city through Valley Gate.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbanti ní m fātìi tí dī ki nín jɔ́ḿ Seedrɔn bùmbiki watil pú ki pée bí ki kpèé Jeerusaleem tiŋki gundi, ní ki fātìi gítì m-boon ki dī Ditantakal punyɔkɔki ki kɔ́.

english_verse: None of the city officials knew what I had in mind. And I had not even told any of the Jews—not the priests, the leaders, the officials, or any other Jews who would be helping in the work.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ pu bɔsoonliibi kaa nìn nyí laakin m cūtèe, kaa nyí tin mun m ŋée. Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti gbantee, maa nìn tùkū Juuda yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì akpambal nì bibɔsoonliibi nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí ki kpèé atuunee kun pu ní m dɔ́mińee.

english_verse: But when I got back, I said to them, “Jerusalem is truly in a mess! The gates have been torn down and burned, and everything is in ruins. We must rebuild the city wall so that we can again take pride in our city.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bí-bi yii: «Nimbi ni-ba ká nnaabu ŋun poon ti kɔ́ee. Jeerusaleem tiŋki kpántì adigbun ní ki-punuubi wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Yīkìmaan tí fàtīí mā Jeerusaleem tiŋki guŋŋi kí nyā icoo ni.»

english_verse: Then I told them how kind God had been and what the king had said. Immediately, they replied, “Let's start building now!” So they got everything ready.
translation_verse: Ní m máafì-bi m-Nimbɔtiu nín bīī m-pu puee, nì ubɔti nín sòon̄ nì mi puee. Niinee ní bi téeń yii: «Tí yīkì kí māmaan.» Ní bi yíkì nì kunyannyaau ki kíĺ ditummɔntiil gbanti.

english_verse: When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about our plans, they started insulting us and saying, “Just look at you! Do you plan to rebuild the walls of the city and rebel against the king?”
translation_verse: Sambalati un sá Oorɔn tiŋkinee nì u-taapu yɔu Toobiya uamɔnja, nì ulaalibuja Geeseem nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ní bi kíĺ ki bíi bèel̄-ti, ní ki kpèé-ti fám ki lì yii: «Ba ní ni bíi ŋáań nan ní? Ni là kí já nì ubɔti deeyaaa?»

english_verse: I answered, “We are servants of the God who rules from heaven, and he will make our work succeed. So we will start rebuilding Jerusalem, but you have no right to any of its property, because you have had no part in its history.”
translation_verse: Ní m kíí-bi yii: «Yilpu Nimbɔtiu u-ba di làá tīī-ti ŋŋmam. Timbi u-tɔntɔnliibi làá yīkì kí fàtīí mā ti-tiŋki. Ama nimbee, naa cáá nsan kí fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki wanti tiba. Naa tí cáá ki-pu mpɔn ŋubɔ, ní ubɔ kpá kí dāá téetí ni-pu dalba!»

english_verse: These are the people who helped rebuild the wall and gates of Jerusalem: The high priest Eliashib and the other priests rebuilt Sheep Gate and hung its doors. Then they dedicated Sheep Gate and the section of the wall as far as Hundred Tower and Hananel Tower.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Eeliyaasiib nì u-nabiyaamu bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yíkì ki kíĺ ditundi. Bíǹ di nìn máń Apibil punyɔkɔki. Bi nìn dū-kì ki sú Unimbɔti ní ki cóoǹ ki-punuubi. Bi nìn dū digundi ki sú Unimbɔti ní ki ŋáŋkì-dì ki cáa sāā bijanjaliibi Dilaataal difɔkɔku, ní ki yōoǹ niin ki cáa sāā Ananeeyeel difɔkɔku.

english_verse: The people of Jericho rebuilt the next section of the wall, and Zaccur son of Imri rebuilt the section after that.
translation_verse: Jeeriikoo yab nìn bí bi-cee ki tūǹ ditundi, nì Imirii jipɔɔn Sakuur.

english_verse: The family of Hassenaah built Fish Gate. They put the beams in place and hung the doors, then they added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
translation_verse: Aseena yab di nìn máń Ijɔm punyɔkɔki. Bíǹ di nìn kpáá punuubi dɔcooŋkaai ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal.

english_verse: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, completed the next section of the wall. Meshullam, son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel, rebuilt the next section, and Zadok son of Baana rebuilt the section beside that.
translation_verse: Bin nìn bí bi-caŋin ki tūǹ ditundee di sá Uriya jipɔɔn Meereemooti, Akoosi naantiiu nì Beereekiya jipɔɔn Meekulaam, Meeseesaabeel naantiiu nì Tiisaadooki jipɔɔn Baana.

english_verse: The next section was to be repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their town leaders refused to do the hard work they were assigned.
translation_verse: Bin nìn dī bi muee di sá Teekoowa yab. Ama bi-kpilib nìn yíì yii baa là kí nīn bí bi-tɔntɔŋkpilib taapu kí tɔ̄ ditundi.

english_verse: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah restored Ancient Gate. They put the beams in place, hung the doors, and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
translation_verse: Paseeya jipɔɔn Yooyadaa nì Beesoodiya jipɔɔn Meekulaam di nìn ŋáŋkì Yeesana punyɔkɔki. Bíǹ di nìn kpáá punuubi dɔcooŋkaai ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal.

english_verse: Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the men from Gibeon and Mizpah rebuilt the next section of the wall. This section reached as far as the house of the governor of West Euphrates Province.
translation_verse: Bin nìn bí bi-caŋin ki tūǹ ditundee di sá ugabaawɔnja Meelatiya nì umeeroonootija Yaadɔn nì Gabawɔn yab nì Miisipa yab bin nìn bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmu gɔminau cee ki sòoǹ tibɔtee.

english_verse: Uzziel son of Harhaiah the goldsmith rebuilt the next section. Hananiah the perfume maker rebuilt the section next after that, and it went as far as Broad Wall.
translation_verse: Bin nìn bí bi mun caŋin ki tūǹ ditundee di sá Araya jipɔɔn Usiyeel un sá goosimiitee, ní úǹ caŋinee, utalaaluŋal Ananiya nìn bí. Bi nìn túń ditundi Jeerusaleem ki cáa sāā laakin ní digundi wāāyee ní ki gbēeǹ.

english_verse: Rephaiah son of Hur ruled half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Bíǹ caŋinee, Uur jipɔɔn Reefaya, Jeerusaleem jandi diba bɔtiu di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi.

english_verse: The section after that was close to the home of Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and he rebuilt it. Hattush son of Hashabneiah constructed the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: U mun caŋinee, Arumaafi jipɔɔn Yeedaya di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi dijandi din túĺ u-mɔŋkiŋu watilee. U mun caŋinee, Asabineeya jipɔɔn Atuusi di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi.

english_verse: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath Moab rebuilt the section after that, and they also built Oven Tower.
translation_verse: Ariim jipɔɔn Maalkiya nì Paati-Moowaab jipɔɔn Akuub di nìn ŋáŋkì digundi janliliitiil, nì Mpaamu difɔkɔku.

english_verse: Shallum son of Hallohesh ruled the other half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. Shallum's daughters also worked with him.
translation_verse: Bíǹ caŋinee, Alooweesi jipɔɔn Saaluum un sá Jeerusaleem tiŋki jandi din kíǹee bɔtiu di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi, u nì u-bisalib.

english_verse: Hanun and the people who lived in the town of Zanoah rebuilt Valley Gate. They hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. They also rebuilt the wall for
translation_verse: Anuun nì Saamoowa yab di nìn ŋáŋkì Ditantakal punyɔkɔki. Bíǹ di nìn kpáá punuubi dɔcooŋkaai ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal. Bíǹ di tí máń digundi mpúun cáá meetab alaataa aŋmoo ki tin cáa sāā Titampuntan punyɔkɔki.

english_verse: Malchijah son of Rechab ruled the district of Beth-Haccherem, and he rebuilt Garbage Gate. He hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
translation_verse: Reekaab jipɔɔn Maalkiya, Beeti-Akeereem tiŋki bɔtiu di nìn ŋáŋkì Titampuntan punyɔkɔki. U nìn fātìi máń-kì ki kpáá punuubi dɔcooŋkaai ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal.

english_verse: Shallum son of Colhozeh ruled the district of Mizpah, and he rebuilt Fountain Gate. He put a cover over the gateway, then hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. He also rebuilt the wall at Shelah Pool. This section was next to the king's garden and went as far as the stairs leading down from David's City.
translation_verse: Kool-Ooseeya jipɔɔn Saaluum, Miisipa tiŋki bɔtiu di nìn ŋáŋkì Nnyimbul punyɔkɔki. U nìn fātìi máń-kì ki píń ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal. Úǹ di nìn tí fātìi máń Siiloowee nyimbɔbil gundi, kí yòon̄ ubɔti kpaabu kí cáá sāā nsan ŋun jɔ́ḿ Daafiidi Tiŋkinee.

english_verse: Nehemiah son of Azbuk ruled half of the district of Beth-Zur, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. It went as far as the royal cemetery, the artificial pool, and the army barracks. Levites Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee, Asibuki jipɔɔn Neeyeemiya, Beeti-Suur tiŋki bɔtiu di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi kí yòon̄ dijandi din dɔ̄ ki cáa gūū Daafiidi ceekuee, ki nìkī ki tin sāā nnyimbilkaam nì ubɔti janjaliibi dumpu.

english_verse: The Levites who worked on the next sections of the wall were Rehum son of Bani; Hashabiah, who ruled half of the district of Keilah and did this work for his district;
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee, Leefii yab di nìn pá ki tūǹ ditundi. Banii jipɔɔn Reewum nìn bí, ní Keeyiila tiŋki dijandi bɔtiu Asabiya nìn bí u-caŋin ki tūǹ ditundi u-tinjandi pu.

english_verse: Binnui son of Henadad, who ruled the other half of the district of Keilah;
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee, bi-nabiyaamu Eenadaadi jipɔɔn Bafayi, Keeyiila tiŋki jandi din kíǹee bɔtiu,

english_verse: Ezer son of Jeshua, who ruled Mizpah, rebuilt the section of the wall that was in front of the armory and reached to the corner of the wall;
translation_verse: nì Yeesuwa jipɔɔn Eeseer, Miisipa bɔtiu di nìn pá. Eeseer di nìn ŋáŋkì dijanliliitiil din nìn túĺ laakin bi yōontí tijanjawan digundi lɔ́kɔ́ee.

english_verse: Baruch son of Zabbai eagerly rebuilt the section of the wall that went all the way to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest;
translation_verse: Sabaayi jipɔɔn Baruuki di nìn bí u-caŋin ki tūǹ ditundi nì difaŋgiil ki yōoǹ dijandi din bí digunlɔkɔl laŋki kí cáá sāā usaraaŋakpil Eeliyasiib diiku nyɔkɔpuee.

english_verse: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, built up to the far end of Eliashib's house. Priests Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee, Uurii jipɔɔn Meereemooti, Akoosi naantiiu di nìn yōoǹ dijandi din bí usaraaŋakpil Eeliyasiib diiku nyɔkɔpuee ki ŋáŋkì ki cáa tin kátì.

english_verse: Here is a list of the priests who worked on the wall: Priests from the region around Jerusalem rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Ní úǹ boonee, bisaraaŋaliibi bin māntìi tú Jeerusaleemee di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi.

english_verse: Benjamin and Hasshub rebuilt the wall in front of their own houses. Azariah, who was the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah, rebuilt the section in front of his house.
translation_verse: Bíǹ boonee, Beenjameen nì Asuub di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí dijandi din túĺ bi-diiŋŋee. Bíǹ boonee, Maseeyawuu jipɔɔn Asariya, Ananiya naantiiu di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí laakin pìlīǹ u-diikuee.

english_verse: Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section of the wall from Azariah's house to the corner of the wall.
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee, Eenadaadi jipɔɔn Binuyii di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí dijandi din bí kí yòon̄ Asariya dumpu kí cáá sāā digunlɔkɔlee.

english_verse: Palal son of Uzai rebuilt the next section, which began at the corner of the wall and the tower of the upper palace near the court of the guard. Pedaiah son of Parosh rebuilt the next section of the wall.
translation_verse: Paalali jipɔɔn Usaayii di ŋáŋkì diguŋkpindi nyɔkɔpu nì kudifɔkɔu kun lībitì ubɔti diiŋŋi puee ki tin sāā bisarkadambi mɔŋkiŋu. Úǹ boonee, Paaneeyoosi jipɔɔn,

english_verse: He stopped at a place near the Water Gate on the east and the tower guarding the temple. This was close to a section in the city called Ophel, where the temple workers lived. Other Builders Who Worked on the Wall
translation_verse: nì bin bí ki tútúǹ kunimbɔtidii poon tuuŋŋi ki kóò Oofeel tiŋgbaŋkinee túń ditundi ki tin sāā kudifɔkɔu kun bí Nnyim punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee.

english_verse: Some priests rebuilt the next section of the wall. They began working north of Horse Gate, and each one worked on a section in front of his own house.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi di nìn yōoǹ kí kíĺ Itaamu punyɔkɔki yilpu pú, ní báà ŋma túń ditundi ki cáá sāā u-diiku nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the wall in front of his house. Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who looked after the East Gate, rebuilt the section after that.
translation_verse: Boonee, Saadooki jipɔɔn Imeer di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí digundi laakin túĺ u-diikuee. Úǹ boonee, Seekaniya jipɔɔn Seemaya un nìn cí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔkee di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi.

english_verse: Hananiah and Hanun rebuilt the next section, which was the second section for them. Meshullam son of Berechiah rebuilt the next section, which happened to be in front of his house.
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee Seeleemiya jipɔɔn Ananiya, nì Salafi jipɔnluluutiu Anuun di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí dijanliliitiil. Úǹ boonee, Beereekiya jipɔɔn Meesulam di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí dijandi din túĺ u-diikuee.

english_verse: Malchijah, a goldsmith, rebuilt the next section, as far as the house used by the temple workers and merchants. This area was across from Gathering Gate, near the room on top of the wall at the northeast corner.
translation_verse: Úǹ boonee, goosimiiti Maalkiya di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi kí cáá sāā kunimbɔtidiin tɔntɔnliibi nì bibantiliibi diiŋŋi ŋin túĺ Miifkaadi watilee, ní ki yōoǹ niin ki tin cáa sāā sintil diiku kun tɔ́kɔ́ digunlɔkɔl puee.

english_verse: The goldsmiths and merchants rebuilt the last section of the wall, which went from the corner room all the way to Sheep Gate.
translation_verse: Goosimiitib nì bibantiliibi di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí sintil diiku kun tɔ́kɔ́ digunlɔkɔl puee nì Apibil punyɔkɔki kansikin. Binannanliibi kaa kíí bí mā digundi

english_verse: When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Sambalati nì Toobiya nì bilaalibub nì Amɔn yab nì Asidoodi yab gbìl̄ yii Jeerusaleem gundi mātam bíi cá nyɔkɔpu, ní bi fātìi bíi māā ki ŋēeb̀ digundi jaŋŋi ŋin lítèe, ní bi fōō mbum tiŋan pu.

english_verse: Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti mēē ti-Nimbɔtiu, ní bi-puee, ti lēē binib ki yóoǹ sintil bí nīn cí-ti ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu.

english_verse: But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war.
translation_verse: Ama ní Juuda yab bíi gbùkum̄ yii: «Ndigbuntam kpúkú tikpil, ní bin bíi fèe gīī an dáá gbíntìi dɔ̄. Taa làá ŋmā kí fàtīí mā digundi nee.»

english_verse: The people worked hard, and we built the walls of Jerusalem halfway up again.
translation_verse: Juuda yab bin nìn kóò bi-kansikinee dɔ́miń ki tùkū-ti ŋfunyɔm saalaa pu yii: «Laakin kamaa ní ni yaa pée fātèe, bi kā ti-pu ní.»

english_verse: But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry
translation_verse: Niinee ní m dū binib ki yóoǹ digundi boon laakin tàkēe. M nìn yóoǹ-bi ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee ní bi ŋúb́ ntàataajimu nì ŋkpamu nì itɔfi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song: “So much rubble for us to haul! Worn out and weary, will we ever finish this wall?”
translation_verse: Ama kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbantee, m-tɔntɔnliibi bininjab dijandi di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi ní dijandi din kíǹee ŋúb́ ŋkpamu nì agbampɔɔ nì itɔfi ní ki pēē ajanjabɔkuti. Bikpilib nìn yú Juuda yab kɔkɔ boon.

english_verse: Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
translation_verse: Bin nìn bíi māā digundee nì bin nìn tūntí awaŋgulee nìn cáá ŋŋal ŋubɔ ní ki tūǹ ditundi, ní ŋun kíǹee ŋúb́ tijanjawan.

english_verse: On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side,
translation_verse: Bimaliibi nìn gbìn̄ bi-tàataajimmu bi-cammu ní ki māā, ní uninja un búǹ ŋyinee yú m-tikindi.

english_verse: and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Ní m bí abɔtibil nì bibɔsoonliibi nì samaa un kíǹee kɔkɔ yii: «Digundi tundi din kíǹee dáá náaǹ ki wīikí, ní ajancuku ŋin pu ti bí ki tūǹ ditundee dátiǹ tɔb.

english_verse: Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee laakin kamaa ni yaa bí ní ki gbìl̄ bi búń ŋyinee, ní dāá kpāfì m-cee. Ti-Nimbɔtiu làá já kí tīī-ti!»

english_verse: Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
translation_verse: Ti nìn tūǹ ditundi kí kíĺ kutaafaau kí dāá sāā kunyeeu iŋmalbijaa nyātam, ní ti-kansikin dijandi ŋúb́ ŋkpamu.

english_verse: From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní m tùkū samaa yii: «Kunyeeuee, utɔntɔŋkpil kamaa nì u-tɔntɔnliibi ń cù Jeerusaleem kí cīití sintil, kutaa yaa wúntèe, bí dāá tɔ̄ ditundi.

english_verse: who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon.
translation_verse: Man m-ba nì m-nabiyaamu nì m-tɔntɔnliibi nì m-janjaliibi bin cí-mee, ti-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn pèetī u-wanti, see ti yaa làá fàl̀ baba.»

english_verse: Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋubɔ poonee ní samaa poon bininjab biba nì bi-nimpoobi dɔ́miń ki bíi yáliŋkí tikpil bi-nabiyaamu Juuda yab bimbim pu.

english_verse: and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
translation_verse: Biba nìn bí ki lì yii: «Timbi nì ti-jipɔmbi nì ti-bisalib wīikí tikpil. Ti là tijin kí jī kí ŋmátí.»

english_verse: Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
translation_verse: Bin kíǹee nìn lì yii: «Timbi dù ti-sati nì ti-fiinyi sufii nì ti-diiŋŋi ní kí yóoń toolima ŋkùm yuntiŋu ní kí nín ká kí jī.»

english_verse: Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Ní biba mun nìn lì yii: «Kí ŋmā kí pà lampoo kí tīī gɔminee, see tí pìnnì animbil kí dū ti-sati nì ti-fiinyi sufii kí yóoń toolima.

english_verse: We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
translation_verse: Ti nì bi bàà sá binibaantiibi, ní bi-jipɔmbi nì ti-jipɔmbi sá bibaantiibi. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, see timbi ń dū ti-jipɔmbi nì ti-bisalib kí tīī bí kpántí iyumbu. Ti-bisalib biba gba pée kpántì iyumbu ki dóò. Taa ŋūǹ kí ŋá mbamin. Ti-sati nì ti-fiinyi sufii kpántì bin ti jíń apɔɔnee wanti ní.»

english_verse: When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun m gbìl̄ bi nín bíi yáliŋkí puee nì tin bi sòoǹee ní an kɔ́ǹ-mi diŋuul tikpil.

english_verse: So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?” Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders
translation_verse: Niinee ní m ká yii an máaǹ ḿ wòoǹ abɔtibil nì bibɔsoonliibi. M nìn bí-bi yii: «Ni bíi wɔ́b̀ ni-nabiyaamu dee yaa!» Niinee ní m yíiń dikpafikpaandi kí kpèè tibɔti gbanti.

english_verse: by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
translation_verse: M nìn bí-bi yii: «Timbi ti-ba nì ti-ŋmam ní ti fātìi dūu dá ti-nabiyaamu Juuda yab bin bi nìn dūu nyáfiǹ binicambee. Ama ní nimbi fàtīi cáá ni-nabiyaamu ki nyáfí, ní timbi ti-ba di fàtīi bíi dāā-bi!» Ní bi ŋmí fɔ́ŋfɔŋ, kaa pée ká dinyɔɔbundi ki gātì.

english_verse: I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us.
translation_verse: M nìn nìkī ki lī yii: «Ni nín ŋá puee kaa ŋān̄! Ni máaǹ kí fàŋkì ti-Nimbɔtiu ní ti-nannanliibi ń taa ká nsan kí sìì-ti.

english_verse: My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return.
translation_verse: Man nì m-nabiyaamu nì m-tɔntɔnliibi, ti mun pīnnì binib animbil nì tijin. An puee ti-kɔkɔ ń dū ti-pɔnliibi pɔɔŋŋi kí pɔ̄-bi.

english_verse: Now give back the fields, vineyards, olive orchards, and houses you have taken and also the interest you have been paid.”
translation_verse: Ní gíiǹ bi-sati nì bi-fiinyi sufii nì bi-ɔliifi sufii nì bi-diiŋŋi kí tīī-bi díǹ. Ní dū tin kɔkɔ ni nìn pīnnì-bi bí dāá pà kí páańee, an yaa sá animbilaaa, tijinaaa, ŋkpamaaa, ní dūú yàntī kí taa ti fōō ipaati.»

english_verse: The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.” So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property.
translation_verse: Ní bi bí yii: «Ti làá gíiǹ tin kɔkɔ ti fōōyee kí tīī, kaa làá bàlifì tiba pu, kii a nín lī puee.» Ní m yíiń bisaraaŋaliibi ní ki yāntì bin kɔkɔ bi cáá apɔɔnee pūtì kí ŋá bi nín lī yii bi làá ŋá puee.

english_verse: Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.” The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised. Nehemiah Is Generous
translation_verse: Ní m gbáfì m-bɔkutil lɔbiki ki bí-bi yii: «Míǹ ní Unimbɔti làá gbāfì un di kaa ŋá min tibɔti nee bí yii bí ŋée kí fá ndandati kí wàatī u-dicaŋku nì u-gaajati, ú taa nín̄ gíti cáá báà tiba.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ kíí yii: «Ameeni, án ŋá míǹ.» Samaa kɔkɔ nìn nyɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan, ní ki ŋá min bi lī yii bi làá ŋée.

english_verse: I was governor of Judah from the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king until the thirty-second year. And during these entire twelve years, my relatives and I refused to accept the food that I was allowed.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti ŋun bi lēē-mi ḿ nīn sá Juuda tiŋkin gɔmina, ubɔti Aritaseerseesi beel yuntiŋu abin mmuŋku kí cáá sāā abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì alee, an dàkà yii abin saalaa nì alee, man nì m-yab kaa lēē gɔmina lampoou nimbiliŋ, kii án nín bàà sá tí lēē puee.

english_verse: Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them.
translation_verse: Gɔminab bin nìn kāl̀ ní man nín bāańee nìn sàantí samaa tikpil. Bi nìn fòol̄-bi tijin nì ndaam ní kí kūtì animbil jitɔmbi imuŋku ili. Bi-tɔntɔnliibi mun nìn wɔ́b́ samaa. Ama man nín fàŋkí Unimbɔtee puee, maa ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing.
translation_verse: Kí kūtèe, man m-ba túń digundi nee mātam tundi. Maa dá kusaau kubɔ, ní man tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì niin ki bíi tūǹ ditundi.

english_verse: Each day one ox, six of the best sheep, and lots of chickens were prepared. Then every ten days, a large supply of wine was brought in. I knew what a heavy burden this would have been for the people, and so I did not ask for my food allowance as governor.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin kamaayee, m nìn kù unaa ubɔ nì ipii in yáàyee iluu nì ikɔl ní. Man m-ba nimbiliŋ ní m nìn cáa dāā, ní iwiin saalaa kamaayee, m nìn yàntī bi cāabìń-mi ndaam tikpil tikpil. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, maa nìn bālifì yii bí tīī tin sá bí tīī-mi yii m nín sá gɔminee pu, di sá yii atuun ŋin samaa nìn bíi tūǹee nìn sá kii diwaŋgulee ní ki nyìm̀ bi-pu.

english_verse: I pray that God will bless me for everything I have done for my people.
translation_verse: «M-Nimbɔtiu, téetí tin kɔkɔ m ŋá ki tīī samaa neeyee pu, kí ŋá-mi tiniti.»

english_verse: Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and our other enemies learned that I had completely rebuilt the wall. All I lacked was hanging the doors in the gates.
translation_verse: Sambalati nì Toobiya nì Geeseem ulaalibuja nì ti-nannanliibi bin kíǹee nìn gbìl̄ yii m fātìi máń digundi dibùndi diba kaa ti bí. Ŋyunti gbantee, punuubi di nìn kíǹ maa láá dūu cóoǹ.

english_verse: Then Sanballat and Geshem sent a message, asking me to meet with them in one of the villages in Ono Valley. I knew they were planning to harm me in some way.
translation_verse: Sambalati nì Geeseem nìn túnní binib bí tùkù-mi yii ḿ dāan̄ tí kpāfì Keefiriim tiŋkin Oonoo tantakalin. Bi nìn cáá nlandɔkɔ kí ŋá-mi tikpitil.

english_verse: So I sent messengers to tell them, “My work is too important to stop now and go there. I can't afford to slow down the work just to visit with you.”
translation_verse: M nìn tú binib bí cùú tùkù-bi yii: «Atuun ŋin m bíi tūǹ dooyee wīikí tikpil, an pɔ̄ɔ̄ ḿ ŋmā kí dāan̄ ni-cee. M yaa yíkì ki nín dòoń ni-cee, ditundi làá gbèen̄.»

english_verse: They invited me four times, but each time I refused to go.
translation_verse: Bi túnní bi yíí-mi míǹ ŋfunyɔm minaa pu, ní m kíí-bi tibɔbaantiil.

english_verse: Finally, Sanballat sent an official to me with an unsealed letter,
translation_verse: Sambalati nìn gíti túnní u-tɔntɔnliu ubɔ ŋŋmooŋmootiim, u ŋúbiń kugbɔŋu ncal an kaa fúuń tiba poon.

english_verse: which said: A rumor is going around among the nations that you and the other Jews are rebuilding the wall and planning to rebel, because you want to be their king. And Geshem says it's true!
translation_verse: Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poon yii: «Atimbun kɔkɔ poonee, bi sòoǹ ní Geeseem mun lī yii sii nì a-nabiyaamu Juuda yab cáá nlandɔkɔ kí nyā ni-ba. An pu ní a fātìi bíi māā digundi. Bi lī gba yii a là kí kpántí bi-bɔtiu ní.

english_verse: You even have prophets in Jerusalem, claiming you are now the king of Judah. You know the Persian king will hear about this, so let's get together and talk it over.
translation_verse: Bi bí yii a lēē Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Jeerusaleem bí bāakì yii a kpántì Juuda tiŋkin ubɔti. Tibɔti gbanti làá bà Peeriisi yab bɔtiu cee, an puee dāan̄ man cee tí kpāfì kí sòoǹ.»

english_verse: I sent a message back to Sanballat, saying, “None of this is true! You are making it all up.”
translation_verse: Ní m tú bí tùkù-u yii: «Tin kɔkɔ a sòon̄ nee, mbaamɔn ŋubɔ kpá poon, sii a-ba di náań-tì.»

english_verse: Our enemies were trying to frighten us and to keep us from our work. But I asked God to give me strength.
translation_verse: Binib gbanti kɔkɔ nìn nyàab̀ kí fàaǹ-ti ní. Bi nìn dàkafī yii ti-wunti làá yɔ̀tī tí gbèen̄ ditundi ní. «Kɔŋkɔnnee m-Dindaan, tīī-mi mpɔn!»

english_verse: One day I went to visit Shemaiah. He wasn't supposed to leave his house, but he said, “Let's hurry to the holy place of the temple and hide there. We will lock the temple doors, because your enemies are planning to kill you tonight.”
translation_verse: Dalbee man nìn cūtì ki ká Deelaya jipɔɔn Seemaya, Meetabeel naantiiu, kun puee waa nìn ŋūǹ kí nyā. Ní u bí-mi yii: «Tí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin, poon poon diikun kí kpāfì. Tí pìin̄ mpunyɔmu kí kpàl̄, di sá bi là kí kpɔ̀-si. Kunyeeu ní a-nannanliibi làá dāan̄ kí kpɔ̀-si.»

english_verse: I answered, “Why should someone like me have to run and hide in the temple to save my life? I won't go!”
translation_verse: Ní m kíí-u yii: «Kii man nee di sáńaaa? Àá unil ulɔu di bí kii man nee ní kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin kí taa kpú? Maa làá cù.»

english_verse: Suddenly I realized that God had not given Shemaiah this message. But Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to trick me
translation_verse: M nìn béè yii an kaa sá Unimbɔti di nìn tīī-u dinyɔɔbundi ú dūú nàatī-mi, ama an sá Sambalati nì Toobiya di nìn tīī-u animbil ú sòoǹ nì mi míǹ.

english_verse: Then I asked God to punish Tobiah and Sanballat for what they had done. I prayed that God would punish the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who, together with her, had tried to frighten me. The Work Is Finished
translation_verse: «M-Nimbɔtiu, taa súntí tin Toobiya nì Sambalati nì Noowadiya, unimpu un nàatī a-bɔtee, nì a-bɔnaatiliibi bin kíǹee nín ŋá tin ki nyàab̀ kí fàan̄-mee pu.»

english_verse: On the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, the wall was completely rebuilt. It had taken
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū iwiin imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì ili ní ki máń ki dóò digundi, uŋmal un bi yíì Eeluulee wiiŋyi mmuŋku nì iŋmoo dal.

english_verse: When our enemies in the surrounding nations learned that the work was finished, they felt helpless, because they knew that our God had helped us rebuild the wall.
translation_verse: Ti-nannanliibi kɔkɔ nín gbìl̄ mimmee, tifaandi nìn kɔ́ atimbun ŋin nìn māntìi tú-tee kɔkɔ ní bíǹ bi-ba nìn ká yii bi sīntì taapu. Niinee bi béè yii an sá ti-Nimbɔtiu di tútúǹ-ti ní ti túń ditundi gbanti ki dóò.

english_verse: All this time the Jewish leaders and Tobiah had been writing letters back and forth.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔ mun poonee, Juuda yab bɔtibiliŋ nìn ŋmà Toobiya tigban ní úǹ kíikí-bi.

english_verse: Many people in Judah were loyal to Tobiah for two reasons: Shecaniah son of Arah was his father-in-law, and Tobiah's son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
translation_verse: Di sá u nì Juuda yab tikpil nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ tɔb, kun puee u nìn sá Araa jipɔɔn Seekaniya coo, ní úǹ u-ba jipɔɔn Yeewoowanan nìn cáá Beereekiya jipɔɔn Meesulam bisal.

english_verse: The people would always tell me about the good things Tobiah had done, and then they would tell Tobiah everything I had said. So Tobiah kept sending letters, trying to frighten me.
translation_verse: Bi nìn sòoǹ ki pàkà-u m-nimbiin, ní ki cáǹ ma mun bɔti ki máafí-u. Toobiya nìn ŋmà-mi tigban kí fàaǹ-mi.

english_verse: Although Jerusalem covered a large area, not many people lived there, and no new houses had been built.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem nìn sá kitiŋkpaaŋŋi ki dɔ̄ ki cá ajan liitil pú, ní ki-nib kaa nìn náaǹ. Baa nìn dá láá fātìi máń adiin aba.

english_verse: This is a list of how many returned from each family group:
translation_verse: Gabawɔn tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib biŋmoo kpá dilaataal.

english_verse: This is a list of how many returned whose ancestors had come from the following towns:
translation_verse: Seenaa tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib kutukub bita nì alaataa awa nì binib mmuŋku nì saalaa.

english_verse: This is a list of how many returned from the families of Levites:
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitilinee, Saaluum nì Ateer nì Talmɔn nì Akuub nì Atiita nì Soobayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib bili kpá imuŋku ili.

english_verse: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until he lets us know if you really are priests.”
translation_verse: Ní bi-gɔminau bí-bi yii bí taa ti jī tijin tin bi dūu ŋá saraa tì bí circir páaayee kí nīn cí usaraaŋakpil ubɔ ń dāá dū Uriim nì Tumiim kí bàlifì dibalifilee.

english_verse: bowls to be used in the temple, and
translation_verse: nì Reeyaya nì Reesiin nì Neekooda

english_verse: Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this occasion. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah were standing to his right, while Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash Baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam were standing to his left.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū idɔ ní ki ŋá dikɔl dikpafil gbanti pu, ní Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti marab tiŋanee tɔ́kɔ́ di-pu. Bin nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ-u ŋŋaŋgiil púee di sá Matatiya nì Seema nì Anaaya nì Uriya nì Ilikiya nì Maseeyawuu. Bin nìn yú u-ŋaŋgan púee di sá Peedaya nì Miikayeel nì Maalkiya nì Asuum nì Aseebadana nì Seekariya nì Meesulam.

english_verse: Ezra was up on the high platform, where he could be seen by everyone, and when he opened the book, all the people stood up.
translation_verse: Eesiraasi nìn kpátì kugbɔŋu samaa kɔkɔ nimbilin, kun puee úǹ nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpu. Ŋyunti ŋun ní u kpátì kugbɔŋuee, samaa kɔkɔ nìn yíkìi yúl̀.

english_verse: Ezra praised the great Lord God, and they lifted their hands, shouting “Amen! Amen!” Then they bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní Eesiraasi jáam̀ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti un sá ukpaanee, ní samaa kɔkɔ kíí yii: «Ameeni! Ameeni!» ki yōoǹ bi-ŋalii yilpu. Bi nìn gbāaǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki jáam̀-u.

english_verse: After this, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah went among the people, explaining the meaning of what Ezra had read.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kàaǹ Unimbɔti marau gbɔŋku ki lèekī ajan kɔkɔ taapu ki cántí, án nín làá ŋá pu báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ tin bi kàan̄ee taapuee.

english_verse: The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
translation_verse: Bi nín kàan̄ Unimbɔti marau gbɔŋku samaa gbìl̄ee, ní bi bíi sūǹ. Niinee, Neeyeemiya un sá gɔminee nì Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti marab tiŋanee nì Leefii yab bin nìn bí ki lèekī taapu ki dàkèe bí yii: «Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu wiiŋŋu ní. Ní taa nín̄ sūǹ kí nīn bí kunimbaaun.»

english_verse: Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
translation_verse: Eesiraasi nìn gíti bí-bi yii: «Nín̄ kùm̀maan kí cùú ŋá tijimmɔntiil kí jī, kí nyɔ̀maan ndamɔntiim. Ní pɔ̄maan bin kaa ŋúń ki ŋá tijinee bí jī, kun puee díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu ní. Ní taa nín̄ bí kunimbaaun, kun puee dipɔɔpindi din ti-Dindaan tììyee di sá ti-pɔŋŋu!»

english_verse: The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!”
translation_verse: Ní Leefii yab bí ki ŋmēentí samaa ki lì yii: «Ní ŋmīĺmaan! Díǹ wiiŋŋu sá ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu ní. Ní taa nín̄ bímaan kunimbaaun!»

english_verse: When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them. Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
translation_verse: Niinee ní samaa kɔkɔ nìn nín kùǹ ki cūtìi jíń ki nyùn̄. Bi nìn tīī biwɔfib mun jíń ní ki ŋá jiŋaakpaan, kun puee bi nìn gbìl̄ tibɔti tin bi sòon̄ nì bee taapu. Tibìń jiŋaaliu

english_verse: On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe, Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab kóoǹ ki kpáfì Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti marab tiŋanee cee kí mɔ̀tīí bīfì marabee taapu mmɔntiim.

english_verse: that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year.
translation_verse: Bi nìn ká marab bin Unimbɔti yāntì Mooyiisi nìn ŋmàn̄ ki tīī-bee poon yii, tibìń jiŋaaliu un bi jīǹ uŋmaluluúti poonee, Isirayeel yab máaǹ kí nīn kóò tibìń poon ní, jiŋaal gbanti wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: They also learned that they were to go into the woods and gather branches of leafy trees such as olives, myrtles, and palms for making these shelters.
translation_verse: An puee bi nìn báakì Jeerusaleem timmu kɔkɔ poon yii: «Nyāmaan kí jɔ̄m̀ ajoon pu kí bátímaan ɔliifi un bi kùn̄ee nì un nyáń kumoounee faati nì miirti faati nì tikpakpati nì isufi in cáá tifaapɔnee kí cáań tí gāā tibìń kii an nín ŋmàn̄ puee.»

english_verse: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
translation_verse: Niinee ní samaa nyáń ki cūtìi cáań nsupamu nì tifaal ki gāā tibìń bi-diiŋŋi nyɔkɔpu nì bi-mɔŋkii, nì kunimbɔtidii mɔŋkiŋu nì Inyiŋfi punyɔkɔki paaŋŋu pu, nì Eefiraayiim punyɔkɔki paaŋŋu pu.

english_verse: Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì niinee, an dàkà yii bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki fātìńee nìn gāā tibìń ki kɔ́ ki bí niin. Doooo Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa yuntiŋu ní Isirayeel yab kaa nìn gíti jíń jiŋaal gbanti. An puee bi nìn jíń jiŋaal gbanti ŋkpaamin nì ifaal ní.

english_verse: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ jiŋaal wimpeekaaŋu kí cáá sāā ŋwinjoolkaa dalee, Eesiraasi nìn pée kàaǹ marab gbɔŋku ní baabadal. Bi jíń jiŋaal gbanti iwiin iluli, ní winnii dalee bi ŋá dikpafikpaandi, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ mara poon puee.

english_verse: On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel went without eating, and they dressed in sackcloth and threw dirt on their heads to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Uŋmabaanti gbanti poon iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dal ní Isirayeel yab dū kutukub ki pēeǹ, ki dū ntam ki pùkū bi-yiliŋ ní ki kpáfì ki bóob́ kinyɔkɔ.

english_verse: They refused to let foreigners join them, as they met to confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Bin nìn sá Isirayeel yabee nìn gāntì bi-ba nì bin kaa sée ní ki yúl̀ ki bīitì bi-kpitii nì bi-naanjab yìntitam pu.

english_verse: For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yíkìi yúl̀. Báà ŋma yú u-paaŋŋu pu mimmee, ní bi kàan̄ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu marau gbɔŋku áli tikúti tita. Bi nìn dū tikúti tita mun ki gbāaǹ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin ki bīitì bi-kpitii pu.

english_verse: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Leefii yab kɔl puee, Yeesuwa nì Banii nì Kaadimiyeel nì Seebaniya nì Bunii nì Seereebiya nì Banii nì Keenanii nìn yíkì ki mēē ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu mpɔn.

english_verse: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: “Stand and shout praises to your Lord, the eternal God! Praise his wonderful name, though he is greater than words can express.” The People Pray
translation_verse: Leefii yab Yeesuwa nì Kaadimiyeel nì Banii nì Asabineeya nì Seereebiya nì Oodiya nì Seebaniya nì Peetaya nìn téeń mpɔn yii: «Yīkìmaan! Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan-u ŋyunti kamaa!» Neeyeemiya mēē samaa nimbiin «Ti-Dindaan, báà ŋma ń nyɔ̄ŋkì a-yindi din cáá tinyoolee! A sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ ijaam nì inyɔŋki in ŋūǹ kí nyā unil nyɔkɔnee.

english_verse: You alone are the Lord, Creator of the heavens and all the stars, Creator of the earth and those who live on it, Creator of the ocean and all its creatures. You are the source of life, praised by the stars that fill the heavens.
translation_verse: Sii baba di sá ti-Dindaan! Sii di náań yilpu, yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ nì iŋmalbijaa kɔkɔ. Sii di náań tiŋkub nì tin kɔkɔ bí bi-poonee. Sii di tīī tin kɔkɔ pée bée kufoou, ní iŋmalbijaa gbàantí a-nimbiin.

english_verse: You are the Lord our God, the one who chose Abram— you brought him from Ur in Babylonia and named him Abraham.
translation_verse: Sii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lēē Abram. Sii di nyántìń-u Uur, Kaaldee yab tiŋkin ní ki pú-u diyindi yii Abraam.

english_verse: Because he was faithful, you made an agreement to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, and of the Jebusites and Girgashites. Now you have kept your promise, just as you always do.
translation_verse: A ká yii u yú nì si deedee nì dipɔbil diba, ní a pūtì ki pōoǹ-u yii a làá dū Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Jeebusi yab nì Giirgaasi yab timmu kí tīī u-naantiibi. A lafun ŋá míǹ, kun puee a sá deedeedaan.

english_verse: When our ancestors were in Egypt, you saw their suffering; when they were at the Red Sea, you heard their cry for help.
translation_verse: «A nìn ká falaa un poon ní ti-naanjab nìn bí Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ki nìn gbìl̄ bi nín nìn yúl̀ Tikati mɔɔl gbandi ki kúuǹ ki yíiń-si á dāá jòoń-bee.

english_verse: You knew that the King of Egypt and his officials and his nation had mistreated your people. So you worked fearsome miracles against the Egyptians and earned a reputation that still remains.
translation_verse: A nìn ŋá maamaaci daanti nì atuŋkpaan ki dàkā Faaroo nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì u-tiŋki kɔkɔ nib, kun puee a nìn nyí bi nín nìn sāaǹ ti-naanjab dilambil poon puee. Míǹ pu ní a nìn nyáń diyiŋkpaandi, di bí ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_verse: You divided the deep sea, and your people walked through on dry land. But you tossed their enemies in, and they sank down like a heavy stone.
translation_verse: A nìn búkutì tiŋku nyim mili ti-naanjab nimbiin ní bi dūtì ŋkulimmi. A nìn téé bin nìn jìń-bee ki tɔ́ nnyimin, ní bi múĺ taapu taapu kii ditaŋkpalee.

english_verse: Each day you led your people with a thick cloud, and at night you showed the way with a flaming fire.
translation_verse: A nìn yāntì ditagbancancaal kpòotī a-nibul ŋwiimpu, ní kunyeeuee ditagbancancaalee kpántí ŋŋmi ki ŋmíntí nsan ŋun pu bi nìn còom̄ee.

english_verse: At Sinai you came down from heaven, and you gave your people good laws and teachings that are fair and honest.
translation_verse: A nìn kpákatìń Siinaayi jool pu ki sòon̄ní-bi doooo yilpu. A nìn tīī-bi abɔkpaa ŋin tèen̄ee, a-dàkatam min sá ibaamɔnee nì akoobil nì marab bin sá bimɔntiibee.

english_verse: You commanded them to respect your holy Sabbath, and you instructed your servant Moses to teach them your laws.
translation_verse: A nìn dī a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu ki yāntì bi béè ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun bi dūu sú-see. A nìn dàkā-bi marab nì akoobil nì a-dàkatam.

english_verse: When they were hungry, you sent bread from heaven, and when they were thirsty, you let water flow from a rock. Then you commanded them to capture the land that you had solemnly promised. *
translation_verse: A nìn yāntì tijin nyánní yilpu bi jíń ki díkí, ki nìn yāntì nnyim nyáń ditaŋkpakpaandin bi nyùn̄ nnyinnyoo kpíì. A nìn bí-bi yii bí nīn cá kí fōō kitiŋ kin a pūtì ki pōoǹ yii a làá tīī-bee.

english_verse: Our stubborn ancestors refused to obey— they forgot about the miracles you had worked for them, and they were determined to return to Egypt and become slaves again.
translation_verse: «Ama bíǹ ti-naanjab nìn yōoǹ bi-ba yilpu. Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ ní kaa nìn tɔ́ a-marab.

english_verse: not even when they made an idol shaped like a calf and insulted you by claiming, “This is the god who rescued us from Egypt.”
translation_verse: ki kpáaǹ gba ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn dūntì tikúti ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ dinabil ki bí yii: <Kpèè a-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-si Eejipiti tiŋkinee sèéyee,> bi nìn ŋá-si ikpitikpaan.

english_verse: Because of your great mercy, you never abandoned them in the desert. And you always guided them with a cloud by day and a fire at night.
translation_verse: Ama sii poon nín mɔ̄ee puee, aa nìn dū-bi ki fá kuteeun. Ditagbancancaal din nìn dàkà-bi nsan ŋwiimpuee kaa nìn kākatì ki wāatì-bi, ní ditagbancancaal din nìn kpántí ŋŋmi kunyeeu ki ŋmíntí nsan ŋun bi nìn còom̄ee mun nìn gbíntìi bí ki ŋmíntí-bi.

english_verse: Your gentle Spirit instructed them, and you gave them manna to eat and water to drink.
translation_verse: A nìn tīī-bi a-fammɔntiim bí nīn nyí ki gàntī. Aa nìn ŋmīntì-bi maana bí dūú kpíiǹ bi-ba, kaa nìn tí ŋmīntì-bi nnyim bí dūú kpɔ̀ nnyinnyoo.

english_verse: You took good care of them, and for forty years they never lacked a thing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet were never swollen.
translation_verse: Abin imuŋku ili ŋin bi nìn ŋá kuteeunee, baa tiba kaa nìn lóò-bi. Bi-wampeeŋkaati kaa nìn cátàaa, bi-taaŋi mun kaa nìn díkí.

english_verse: You let them conquer kings and take their land, including King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan.
translation_verse: «A nìn dū abee nì anibul ki ŋá bi-ŋaan. A nìn yāntì bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ ntimu mun nì bi nìn cáá ŋkpaanyɔmuee, an dàkà yii Eesbɔn bɔtiu Siiwɔn tiŋki nì Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi tiŋki.

english_verse: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
translation_verse: A nìn yāntì bi-naantiibi būtì kii iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee ní ki cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin poon a nìn bí bi-naanjab yii bí cùú fōō án kpántí bi-tiŋkee.

english_verse: Then their descendants conquered the land. You helped them defeat the kings and nations and treat their enemies however they wished.
translation_verse: Bi-naantiibi gbanti nìn cūtì ki fōō-kì kì kpántì bi-tiŋki. A nìn yāntì Kanaan yab nìn sīntì bi-ba taapu ki tīī-bi ní ki nìn dū-bi ki ŋá bi-ŋaan, bi nì bi-bɔtiibi nì bi-samaau. Ti-naanjab nìn ŋá-bi bi nín là puee.

english_verse: They captured strong cities and rich farmland; they took furnished houses, as well as cisterns, vineyards, olive orchards, and numerous fruit trees. They ate till they were satisfied, and they celebrated your abundant blessings.
translation_verse: Bi nìn fōō ntimu mun bi nìn máń agun ki māntìi túee nì tikpaatan tin cáá ntiŋkpamee. Bi nìn fōō adiin ŋin poon tigaajati gbée, nì lɔkɔb bin baa gbìn̄ee, nì fiinyi nì ɔliifi sufii nì isufi in lòoǹ asubiŋmɔkaayee tikpil. A-ŋanti puee, bi nìn jíń ki bál̀ bi nín là puee, bi nìn jíń ki díkí, ki nɔ́ĺ ní ki nìn kíǹ ki bí nnaam poon.

english_verse: In spite of this, they rebelled and disobeyed your laws. They killed your prophets, who warned them to turn back to you, and they cursed your name.
translation_verse: «Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, bi nìn yíkì kaa kíí bi-ba pu, ki nìn jáń nì si ní ki fātì bi-boon ki tīī a-marab. Bi nìn kūū a-bɔnaatiliibi bin nìn bí ki sáŋkí-bi yii bí gítiń a-ceeyee. Bi nìn ŋá-si ikpitikpaan.

english_verse: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
translation_verse: An puee a nìn dū-bi ki líiǹ bi-nannanliibi bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Bi-nimbinaamandi poonee, bi nìn fáá mbiil yii á jòoń-bi, ní a kāl̀ doooo yilpu ki gbìl̄. A-neeŋkpaandi puee, a nìn tīiń-bi binib bin nìn nyāntí-bi bi-nannanliibi ŋaanee.

english_verse: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
translation_verse: Ama bi yaa nìn fīī-bi míǹ bi-wunti sɔ̄ŋkèe, ní bí fàtīí kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań-si ikpiti, ní á fàtīí tí dū-bi ki líiǹ bi-nannanliibi. Niinee ní bí tí fáá mbiil yii á jòoń-bi ní á kàl̄ yilpu kí gbìl̄. A-neeŋkpaandi puee, a nìn fīī-bi míǹ ki líí ŋfunyɔm tikpil.

english_verse: You warned them to turn back and discover true life by obeying your laws. But they stubbornly refused and continued to sin.
translation_verse: A nìn kpáafì-bi bí gítiń kí nóó a-marab, ama bi nìn ŋá dilambil kaa tɔ́ a-marab. Bi nìn yīntiǹ abɔkpaa ŋin unil máaǹ kí nóó kí ŋmátée. Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ ki kpáá bi-tafaliŋ kaa nìn pée là kí gbìl̄ tiba.

english_verse: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
translation_verse: «A nìn dū abin kupaau ki jíń kimɔtii bi-pu. A nìn tīī a-bɔnaatiliibi a-Fam bi kpáafì-bi, ama baa nìn pílifì. An puee a nìn dū-bi ki líiǹ ntincamu nib.

english_verse: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔ, a-neeŋkpaandi puee, aa nìn yāntì bi nāaǹ-bi kɔkɔ, kaa nìn dū-bi ki fá, kun puee a sá Unimbɔti un poon mɔ̄ ki cáá kulaŋŋaŋfitiiuee ní.

english_verse: Our God, you are powerful, fearsome, and faithful, always true to your word. So please keep in mind the terrible sufferings of our people, kings, leaders, priests, and prophets, from the time Assyria ruled until this very day.
translation_verse: «Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Nimbɔtiu, Unimbɔti un sá ukpaan, ki cáá mpɔn, ki sá kuwambiiuee, sii un di ŋúb́ ipoon in a pūtì ki pōoǹ-tee nì deedeeyee, taa lì yii kí yòon̄ Asuur yab bɔtiibi yuntiŋu ki cáa sāā ti-yuntiŋu nee, falaa un ti nì ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-kpootiliibi nì ti-saraaŋaliibi nì ti-bɔnaatiliibi nì ti-naanjab nì a-nibul kɔkɔ jíńee kaa ká-si.

english_verse: You have always been fair when you punished us for our sins.
translation_verse: Tin kɔkɔ bāań-ti nee, a ŋá-tì deedee nì mbaamɔn ní, ama ní timbi ŋá tin kaa kítèe.

english_verse: Our kings and leaders, our priests and ancestors have never obeyed your commands or heeded your warnings.
translation_verse: Ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-kpootiliibi nì ti-saraaŋaliibi nì ti-naanjab kaa nìn dū a-dàkatam ki túń ditundi, kaa nìn fātìi tɔ́ a-marab nì a-bɔti tin a nìn dūu kpáafì-bee.

english_verse: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
translation_verse: Bíǹ bin nìn kā bi-beelin, ki cáá tiwammɔntiil tin kɔkɔ a nìn tīī-bee, nì kitiŋ kin wāā ki cáá ntiŋkpam a nìn cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ poonee, baa nìn nóó-si, kaa nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī bi-tuŋkpitiŋ.

english_verse: Now we are slaves in this fruitful land you gave to our ancestors.
translation_verse: Díǹ pu nee, ti kpántì iyumbu! Ti kpántì iyumbu kitiŋ kin a nìn dūu tīī ti-naanjab bí jī tiwammɔntiil tin kɔkɔ kì lòoǹee poon.

english_verse: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Ti-kpitii puee, bin a kāaǹ bí nīn sá ti-bɔtiibee di yì tijimmɔntiil tin kitiŋ gbanti lòoǹ tikpilee. Bíǹ di yì timbi ti-ba nì ti-waŋkuti ki ŋáań min bi lèe. Ti bí kunimbaakpaaŋŋu poon ní!»

english_verse: The Levites who signed were: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the clan of Henadad, Kadmiel,
translation_verse: nì Maasiya nì Biiligayi nì Seemaya. Bíǹ kɔkɔ nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi ní. -

english_verse: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
translation_verse: nì Miika nì Reewoob nì Asabiya,

english_verse: Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
translation_verse: nì Sakuur nì Seereebiya nì Seebaniya,

english_verse: The leaders who signed were: Parosh, Pahath Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
translation_verse: nì Oodiya nì Banii nì Beeniinuu.

english_verse: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
translation_verse: nì Buunii nì Asigaadi nì Beebaayi,

english_verse: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
translation_verse: nì Adooniya nì Biigifayi nì Adiini,

english_verse: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
translation_verse: nì Ateer nì Isikiya nì Asuur,

english_verse: Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,
translation_verse: nì Oodiya nì Asuum nì Beesayi,

english_verse: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
translation_verse: nì Ariifi nì Anatooti nì Neebaayi,

english_verse: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
translation_verse: nì Magipiyaasi nì Meesulam nì Eesiir,

english_verse: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
translation_verse: nì Meeseesaabeel nì Saadooki nì Yaduwa,

english_verse: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
translation_verse: nì Peelatiya nì Anan nì Anaaya,

english_verse: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
translation_verse: nì Ooseeya nì Ananiya nì Asuub,

english_verse: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
translation_verse: nì Alooweesi nì Piileeya nì Soobeeki,

english_verse: Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
translation_verse: nì Reewum nì Asaabina nì Maseeyawuu

english_verse: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah. The Agreement
translation_verse: nì Ayiiya nì Anan nì Aanan

english_verse: All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin nìn kíǹee nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi, nì bin kɔkɔ nìn gāntì bi-ba nì ntimu mun kíǹee nib ki nóó Unimbɔti marabee, ki kpáaǹ bi-nimpoobi nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib nì bin kɔkɔ nìn ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tibɔti taapuee nìn kútì bi-pu.

english_verse: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
translation_verse: An puee taa ti làá dū ti-bisalib kí tīī kitiŋ nee nib ticati, míǹ ní kaa làá tí yòon̄ bi-bisalib kí tīī ti-jipɔmbi ticati.

english_verse: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
translation_verse: Animbilee ní bi làá nīn cáa dāā kpɔnɔb bin bi pāantí ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, nì tijimpin saraabi bin bi ŋáań kutaa kamaayee, nì saraawɔkaa un bi ŋáań kutaa kamaayee, nì saraabi bin bi ŋáań ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal nì uŋmapɔɔn nì jiŋaalib bin kíǹee wiiŋyee, nì tin kɔkɔ bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee, nì Isirayeel yab kpitii pɔ̄tam saraabi, nì tin kɔkɔ pée sá bí nīn cáa kpèé ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku ŋāŋkitamee.

english_verse: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ti làá nīn tí cāabìń ti-tiŋki jincɔ̀fikaati nì busubu kamaa nín lòoǹ abil ŋiŋyee apeekaa dibintil kamaa ti-Dindaan diikun.

english_verse: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
translation_verse: Ti làá gíti cáań ti-biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu nì ti-waŋkuti biseemaliŋ, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ marab gbɔŋkun poon puee. Ti làá cáá ti-naai nì ti-piii nì ti-ŋoobui biseemaliŋ kí cùnnì ti-Nimbɔtiu diikun kí tīī bisaraaŋaliibi bin bí niin ki tūǹ ti-Dindaan tundee.

english_verse: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Leefii yab yaa cá kí fōoń tisaalaatiilee, usaraaŋal un sá Aarɔn maaliŋu poonee ń céeǹ-bi. Leefii yab làá lēē tisaalaatiil gbanti saalaatiiti kí tīī ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku bí cáań kí síiń kunimbɔtidii dibiyaamu mun poon bi yōontí tijinee.

english_verse: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
translation_verse: Samaa kpilib nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní. Bi nìn tɔ́ kasi samaa un kíǹee pu kí lēē binib saalaa kamaa poonee, unil ubɔ ú cùú nīn kóò Jeerusaleem, circir tiŋkin, ní binib biwa bin kíǹee ń gbíntí kí nīn kóò ntimu mun kíǹee poon.

english_verse: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Samaa nìn mēē ki bīiǹ bin kɔkɔ nìn lēē bi-pɔbilin yii bi làá cù kí nīn kóò Jeerusaleemee pu.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì kunimbɔtidiin tɔntɔnliibi nì Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi naantiibi di nìn kóò Juuda tiŋkin. Báà ŋma nìn kóò u-tiŋkin laakin u nìn yèe ní. Juuda timmu mun kíǹee kpilib bin nìn dɔ́miń ki kóò Jeerusaleemee yiŋŋi sɔ̀.

english_verse: From the Judah tribe, two leaders settled in Jerusalem with their relatives. One of them was Athaiah son of Uzziah. His ancestors were Zechariah, Amariah, Shephatiah, Mahalalel, and Perez, the son of Judah. From the descendants of Perez,
translation_verse: Peereesi maaliŋun yab bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn dɔ́miń ki kóò Jeerusaleemee nìn nyáń binib alaataa anaa nì imuŋku ita nì binib binii.

english_verse: From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were
translation_verse: Bin kíǹee di sá Gabayi nì Salayi. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn nyáń binib alaataa awa nì binib mmuŋku nì binii.

english_verse: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
translation_verse: Sikirii jipɔɔn Jooweel di nìn sá bi-kpiliu, ní Aseenuwa jipɔɔn Juuda sá kitiŋee kpiliu taapu yɔu.

english_verse: Four priests settled in Jerusalem. The first was Jedaiah; he was the son of Joiarib and the uncle of Jachin.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi kansikinee, bin nìn bée di sá Yooyariib jipɔɔn Peedaya, nì Yakiin

english_verse: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
translation_verse: nì Ilikiya jipɔɔn Seeraya. Seeraya gbanti naanjab di sá Meesulam nì Sadooki nì Meerayooti nì bin kpèé kunimbɔtidiiyee kpiliu Ayiituub,

english_verse: Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
translation_verse: Leefii yab kansikinee, bin nìn bée ubɔ di sá Asuub jipɔɔn Seemaya. U-naanjab di sá Asiirikam nì Asabiya nì Bunii

english_verse: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
translation_verse: nì Sabeetayi nì Yoosabaadi bin nìn sá Leefii yab kpilib kansikin biba ní ki nìn kpèé kunimbɔtidii boon tuuŋŋee mun nìn bí.

english_verse: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
translation_verse: Miika jipɔɔn Mataniya mun nìn bí. U-naanjab di sá Sabidii nì Asaafi un di nìn tōontí inyɔŋki laŋyi ŋwimmeem yuntiŋuee, nì u-nabiki Bakibukiya un nìn sá u-taapu yɔuee nì Samuwa jipɔɔn Abidaa. Úǹ naanjab di sá Galaal nì Yeedutun.
