english_verse: One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kansikinee, bi nìn bée di sá Akuub nì Talmɔn nì bi-dicaŋŋin yab. Bi nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib binii kpá imuŋku inaa.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn cūtìi kāl̀ bi-tinjaŋŋin Juuda timmu mun kíǹee poon.

english_verse: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
translation_verse: Kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi nìn kóò Oofeel, Jeerusaleem tiŋgbaŋkin ní. Siiya nì Giiseepa di nìn sá bi-kpilib.

english_verse: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
translation_verse: Un nìn sá Leefii yab kpiliu Jeerusaleemee di sá Banii jipɔɔn Uusi. U-naanjab di sá Asabiya nì Mataniya nì Miika. U nìn sá kunimbɔtidiin laŋgaaliibi ubɔ ní Asaafi maaliŋun.

english_verse: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn yóoǹ bilaŋgaaliibi gbanti mara ní ki nìn bɔ́ntì bi nín làá nīn tūǹ dilaŋgaal tundi pu ŋwiin kamaa puee ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
translation_verse: Meeseesaabeel jipɔɔn Peetaya un sá Juuda jipɔɔn, Seera maaliŋunee di nìn bí Peeriisi yab bɔtiu cee ki kpèé Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ bɔti. Juuda yab bin kaa nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee

english_verse: Some of the people of Judah lived in the following towns near their farms: Kiriath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel,
translation_verse: Ntimbilimu mun bí tisatinee jaaŋŋu púee, Juuda yab biba nìn kóò Kiiriyati-Ariba nì ki-timbilimmun nì Diibɔn nì ki-timbilimmun nì Yeekabiseel nì ki-timbilimmun,

english_verse: Jeshua, Moladah, Beth-Pelet,
translation_verse: nì Yeesuwa nì Moolada nì Beeti-Peeleeti,

english_verse: Enrimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
translation_verse: nì Eeni-Riimɔn nì Soora nì Yaarmuti,

english_verse: Zanoah, Adullam, Lachish, and Azekah. In fact, they settled the towns from Beersheba in the south to Hinnom Valley in the north.
translation_verse: nì Sanoowa nì Adulaam nì ki-timbilimmu nì Lakiisi nì ki-timbilimmun nì Aseeka nì ki-timbilimmun. Bi nìn kāl̀ kí yòon̄ Beerseeba kí cáá sāā Inoom tantakalin.

english_verse: The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages,
translation_verse: Beenjameen naakookun yab nìn kāl̀ kí yòon̄ Geeba kí nīn cá doooo Miikimaasi nì Aya nì Beeteel nì ki-timbilimmun,

english_verse: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
translation_verse: nì Anatooti nì Noob nì Ananiya

english_verse: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
translation_verse: nì Asɔɔr nì Raama nì Giitayiim,

english_verse: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
translation_verse: nì Adiidi nì Seebooyiim nì Neebalati,

english_verse: Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley.
translation_verse: nì Loodi nì Oonoo nì Iŋal pu tɔntɔnliibi tantakal.

english_verse: Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Leefii yab kansikinee, biba nìn yíkì Juuda yab timmun ki cūtìi kóò Beenjameen yab cee.

english_verse: Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab bin nìn nóoń Saltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel nì Yeesuwa ki nyánní kuyuŋu ki fātìńee di sá Seeraya nì Yiirmeeya nì Eesiraasi,

english_verse: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
translation_verse: nì Amariya nì Maluuki nì Atuusi,

english_verse: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
translation_verse: nì Seekaniya nì Reewum nì Meereemooti,

english_verse: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
translation_verse: nì Idoo nì Giineetɔyi nì Abiiya,

english_verse: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
translation_verse: nì Miiniyaamiini nì Maadiya nì Biiliga,

english_verse: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
translation_verse: nì Seemaya nì Yooyariib nì Yeedaya,

english_verse: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
translation_verse: nì Saluu nì Amooki nì Ilikiya nì Yeedaya. Yeesuwa yuntiŋuee, bíǹ nì bi-nabiyaamu di nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi kpilib.

english_verse: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,
translation_verse: Leefii yab kansikinee, bin nìn bée di sá Yeesuwa nì Binuyii nì Kadimiyeel nì Seereebiya nì Yeewuda nì Mataniya. Mataniya nì u-nabiyaamu di nìn kpòotī inyɔŋki laŋyi.

english_verse: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
translation_verse: Bakibukiya nì Unii, bi-nabiyaamu di nìn yú ki túĺ-bi ki kíikí ilan.

english_verse: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
translation_verse: Yeesuwa di màl̄ Yooyakiim, ní Yooyakiim màl̄ Eeliyasiib, ní Eeliyasiib màl̄ Yooyadaa,

english_verse: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
translation_verse: ní Yooyadaa màl̄ Joonatan, ní Joonatan màl̄ Yaduwa.

english_verse: When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Yooyakiim sá usaraaŋakpilee, bin nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi dicaŋkpilibee sɔ̀. Seeraya dicaŋkunee, Meeraya di nìn sá ukpil. Yiirmeeya dicaŋkunee, Ananiya di nìn sá ukpil.

english_verse: Shammua of Bilgah, Jehonathan of Shemaiah,
translation_verse: Biiliga dicaŋkunee, Samuwa. Seemaya dicaŋkunee, Joonatan di nìn sá ukpil.

english_verse: Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah. The Priestly and Levite Families
translation_verse: Ilikiya dicaŋkunee, Asabiya di nìn sá ukpil. Ní Yeedaya dicaŋkunee, Neetaneeyeel di nìn sá ukpil.

english_verse: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
translation_verse: Eeliyasiib nì Yooyadaa nì Yoowanan nì Yaduwa yuntiŋu ní bi nìn ŋmàn̄ Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib nì bisaraaŋaliibi yiŋŋi ki tin cáa sāā Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Daariyusi yuntiŋu.

english_verse: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
translation_verse: Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib yiŋŋi ki ŋá kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmà tin jītí ŋwiin kamaayee ki tin sāā Eeliyasiib naantiiu Yoowanan yuntiŋu.

english_verse: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
translation_verse: Leefii yab kpilib di nìn sá Asabiya nì Seereebiya nì Kadimiyeel jipɔɔn Yeesuwa. Bi-nabiyaamu nìn yú ki túĺ-bi, ní ki gà ilan ki fòol̄ tɔb ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan ki pàkà-u, kii Unimbɔti niliu Daafiidi nín nìn síiǹ mara bí nīn ŋáań puee.

english_verse: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi Mataniya nì Bakibukiya nì Oobadiya nì Meesulam nì Talmɔn nì Akuub di nìn cí adiin ŋin nìn yú ki nákáǹ kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki bi yōontí tijin poonee.

english_verse: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
translation_verse: Bíǹ di nìn tūǹ kunimbɔtidii poon ditundi Yeesuwa jipɔɔn Yooyakiim un nìn sá Yoosadaaki naantiiu nì Gɔmina Neeyeemiya nì Eesiraasi un sá usaraaŋal nì umaradakalee yuntiŋu. Bi jíń Jeerusaleem gundi jiŋaaliu

english_verse: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem gundi jiŋaaliu puee, bi nìn yíiń Leefii yab bin nìn kóò ijaan kɔkɔ puee bí dāan̄ Jeerusaleem bí jī digundi jiŋaaliu nì dipɔɔpindi. Bi nìn gà inyɔŋki laŋyi, ki cákafí cancakantib ní ki bɔ̀ɔ́ saŋgub nì tibati.

english_verse: The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth.
translation_verse: nì Beeti-Giilgaal, nì Geeba nì Asimafeeti timbilimmun yab. Di sá yii bilaŋgaaliibi nìn náań ntimbilimu ki māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋki ní ki kóò.

english_verse: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn ŋá akoobil nín sá puee ki ŋá bíǹ bi-ba nì samaa kɔkɔ nì mpunyɔmu nì digundi circir.

english_verse: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
translation_verse: M nìn yāntì Juuda yab kpilib jɔ́m̀ digundi pu. M nìn náań alaŋgakitikpaan ali. Dikitipeekaalee nìn búntì ŋŋaŋgiil pú ki tɔ́kɔ́ digundi pu ki còom̄ ki cá Titampuntan punyɔkɔki watil pú.

english_verse: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
translation_verse: Bin nìn pá bilaŋgaaliibi gbanti boonee di sá Oosaya nì Juuda yab kpilib dijandi,

english_verse: Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
translation_verse: an dàkà yii Asariya nì Eesiraasi nì Meesulam,

english_verse: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
translation_verse: nì Yeewuda nì Beenjameen nì Seemaya nì Yiirmeeya.

english_verse: all of them blowing trumpets. Next, there was Zechariah of the Asaph clan
translation_verse: Bíǹ boon ní bisaraaŋaliibi bin ŋúb́ akantánee pá. Bíǹ di sá Joonatan jipɔɔn Seekariya. U-naanjab di sá Seemaya nì Mataniya nì Miikaya nì Sakuur nì Asaafi.

english_verse: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
translation_verse: U-nabiyaamu Seemaya nì Asareeyeel nì Miilalayi nì Giilalayi nì Maayi nì Neetaneeyeel nì Yeewuda nì Ananii nìn pá bi-boon ki ŋúb́ tiwambɔɔkaal tin Unimbɔti niliu Daafiidi nìn kpítèe. Umaradakal Eesiraasi di nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Nnyimbul punyɔkɔkee, laakin dàb̀ ki jɔ́ḿ Daafiidi Tiŋkee bí bi-nimbiin. Bi nìn dàb̄ akɔl ki jɔ́m̀ ki tɔ́kɔǹ digundi pu, ní Daafiidi diiŋŋi bí taapu. Bi nìn cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Inyiŋfi punyɔkɔki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú.

english_verse: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
translation_verse: Dilaŋgakitil dililiitiil nìn dī ŋŋaŋgan pú. Man nì samaa kpilib bin kíǹee nìn pá bi-boon ki tɔ́kɔǹ digundi pu. Ti nìn cōom̀ ki jítì Mpaamu difɔkɔku pu, ní ki tin bàn̄ laakin pú digundi wāāyee.

english_verse: Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard,
translation_verse: Ti nìn nìkī ki nín cá Eefiraayiim punyɔkɔki yilpu pu nì Yeesana punyɔkɔki nì Ijɔm punyɔkɔki, nì Ananeeyeel difɔkɔku nì Dilaataal difɔkɔku ki tin cáa sāā Apibil punyɔkɔki ní ki tin gbēeǹ Sintil punyɔkɔki.

english_verse: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
translation_verse: Alaŋgakiti alee nìn kɔ́ ki yúl̀ kunimbɔtidiin. Man nì samaa kpilib dijandi din nìn nóó-mee mun nìn kɔ́ ki yúl̀.

english_verse: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi Eeliyaakiim nì Maseeyawuu nì Miiniyaamiini nì Miika nì Eeliyooweenayi nì Seekariya nì Ananiya nìn bí ki búǹ akantán.

english_verse: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
translation_verse: Bin mun nìn bée di sá Maseeyawuu nì Seemaya nì Eeleeyasaar nì Uusi nì Yoowanan nì Maalkiya nì Eelaam nì Eeseer. Isiraya di nìn kpòotī bilaŋgaaliibi ní bi gà ilan.

english_verse: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
translation_verse: Yaadalee, bi nìn ŋá saraabi tikpil ní ki nìn bí dipɔɔpindi poon, kun puee Unimbɔti nìn tīī-bi dipɔɔpiŋkpaandi. Binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu mun nìn bíi fàal̀, ní binib nìn bíń ndan ki gbìl̄ dipɔɔpindi faalii pu Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Tin sá bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab yatee

english_verse: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti ní bi nìn lēē binib biba bí nīn cí adiin ŋin poon bi yōontí saraabi nì tisaalaatiil nì tijincɔ̀fikaalee. An nibee di làá nīn fòolìń ntimu mun bí ikpaanceetee yab cee mara nín yóoǹ yii bí nīn tìì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab dijandi diŋyee. Ditundi din bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn bí ki tūǹee nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ Juuda yab.

english_verse: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí ki tūǹ bi-Nimbɔtiu tundi ní ki nìn ŋáań circir tin kɔkɔ sá bí ŋá circiree. Bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi mun nìn bí ki tūǹ bi-tuuŋŋi deedee, kii Daafiidi nì u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn nín nìn yóoǹ mara yii bí nīn ŋáań puee.

english_verse: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
translation_verse: Di sá yii doooo ubɔti Daafiidi nì Asaafi yuntiŋuee, bilaŋgaaliibi kpilib nìn kpòotī bilaŋgaaliibi ní bi gà inyɔŋki nì ipampaka laŋyi ki tìì Unimbɔti tinyool.

english_verse: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_verse: Sooroobabeel nì Neeyeemiya yuntiŋuee, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn tìì bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi dijandi din nìn pée sá bí nīn tìì-bi baabadalee ní. Bi nìn dùŋfī dijandi din sá circiree ní kí tīī Leefii yab, ní Leefii yab mun ń dū tin bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee kí tīī Aarɔn maaliŋun yab.

english_verse: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, bi nìn bí ki kàaǹ Mooyiisi gbɔŋkun Isirayeel yab nimbiin, ní ki ká an ŋmàn̄ yii Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab kaa máaǹ kí cèeǹ Unimbɔti nibul poon.

english_verse: This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
translation_verse: Di sá yii baa nìn túŋkì Isirayeel yab ki tīī-bi tijin nì nnyim. Kí kūtèe, Moowaab yab nìn tīī Balaam animbil ú tɔ̄ Isirayeel yab mbusu, ama ní ti-Nimbɔtiu nìn dū mbusuee ki kpántì dibiindi.

english_verse: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nín gbìl̄ bi kàan̄ mara gbantee, ní bi nyántì binicambi kɔkɔ Isirayeel nibul kansikin.

english_verse: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī bí nìn lēē nlandɔkɔ neeyee, usaraaŋal Eeliyasiib ní bi nìn lēē ú nīn kpèé ndibiyaamu mun nákáǹ ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku bi yōontí saraabi wantee. U nì Toobiya nín nìn pēē kunabitiiuee puee,

english_verse: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
translation_verse: u nìn tīī-u kudii kun poon wāā tiŋan bi nìn cāabìń saraabi nì talaalutuukaa nì asambil nì bilee nì ndapɔm nì ŋkpam saalaatiiti ki yōontée. An dàkà yii tin kɔkɔ mara nìn lī yii bí nīn cāabìń ki tìì Leefii yab nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibee, ki kpáaǹ tin bi nìn lèekī ki tìì bisaraaŋaliibee.

english_verse: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun tibɔti nee jítèe, maa nìn bí Jeerusaleem, di sá m nìn fātìi gítì Babiloon bɔtiu Aritaseerseesi cee u nín jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ali poonee. Boonee ní m mēē ubɔti nsan,

english_verse: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
translation_verse: ní ki gítìń Jeerusaleem. Niin ní m ká ikpiti in Eeliyasiib ŋá ki dū kudii kun bí kunimbɔtidii cindinee ki tīī Toobiya kóòyee.

english_verse: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
translation_verse: M nìn fōō diŋuul tikpil ní ki kɔ́ kudiin ki kóoǹ Toobiya wanti kɔkɔ ki tɔ́ ki fá kudii boon.

english_verse: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
translation_verse: M nìn yāntì bi fíntì kudii gbanti ki ŋá-ku circir, ní m fātìi dū kunimbɔtidiin sambiliŋ nì saraabi nì talaalutuukaa ki síiǹ ti-laŋki.

english_verse: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
translation_verse: M nìn gbìl̄ mun yii baa nìn tìì dijandi din sá bí nīn tìì Leefii yabee, an puee Leefii yab nì bilaŋgaaliibi bin nìn bí kunimbɔtidiin ki tūǹ atuunee nìn dū bi-tuuŋŋi ki fá ki gítì ki bíi kù tikpaal.

english_verse: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
translation_verse: M nìn wòon̄ bibɔsoonliibi ki bí-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni dū Unimbɔti diiku ki fá míǹ?» Niinee ní m fātìi kpáfì Leefii yab nì bilaŋgaaliibi ní ki dū bi-tuuŋŋi ki gíiǹ ki ŋúbiǹ-bi.

english_verse: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee Juuda yab kɔkɔ nìn cáań bilee nì ndapɔm nì ŋkpam saalaatiiti ki dūu yóoǹ kudii kun poon bi nìn yōontí saraabi jintee.

english_verse: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
translation_verse: M nìn lēē usaraaŋal Seeleemiya nì umaradakal Saadooki nì uleefiija Peedaya, ní ki dū Saakuur jipɔɔn, Mataniya naantiiu Anan ki ŋàl̄-bi bí nīn kpèé tijin tin bi cāabìń ki yōontée bɔti. Di sá yii báà ŋma nìn máká binib gbanti pu ní. Bíǹ ní bi nìn lēē bí nīn yàkatī bi-nabiyaamu tijin.

english_verse: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
translation_verse: «Óò m-Nimbɔtiu, taa súntí tin kɔkɔ m ŋée pu! Taa súntí m nín túń kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋi nì deedee ki bɔ́ntì dinimbɔtinool puee pu.»

english_verse: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní m nìn ká Juuda yab tiŋkinee, binib nìn bí ki tà ki fɔ́bití asubil ndaam còol̀ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. Biba mun nìn bíi tūntí bi-mammu bilee nì ndamam nì fiinyi subiliŋ nì fiigi subiliŋ nì awaŋgul aba mun ki cáa cáǹ Jeerusaleem ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. M nìn wòon̄-bi ŋwiin ŋun bi nìn bíi nyáfí bi-wantee.

english_verse: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Tiir yab bin nìn kóò Jeerusaleemee nìn cāabìń ijɔm nì tinyampuwan ki nyáfíǹ Juuda yab Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal.

english_verse: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
translation_verse: M nìn wòon̄ Juuda yab bɔtibiliŋ ki bí-bi yii: «Ba kpitii bulifi ní ni ŋá míǹ, ki kpēē ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun bí circiree fám mimmee?

english_verse: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ti-naanjab nìn ŋá. An pu ní Unimbɔti nìn yāntì mbusub nín bí puee nì bi-nyɔkɔm dɔ́miń ki jéetì ti nì ti-tiŋki pu. Ni nín bí ki kpèé ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun fám nee, ni bíi kùtī Unimbɔti ŋuul Isirayeel yab pu dee!»

english_verse: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: M nìn pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí pìin̄ Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu kujoou kun ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa kífée, kí taa pìitī kí nīn cí ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ń jītí. Ní m lēē m-tɔntɔnliibi biba bí cīití mpunyɔmu báà ubɔ ń taa túnní tinyampuwan kí kɔ́ǹní ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal.

english_verse: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
translation_verse: An puee binyampoobi nì biwannyafiliibi bin nyáfí tiwan nín bí ti-ba ti-ba puee nìn gbíntì Jeerusaleem guŋŋi boon ki dōoǹ diba kii mili pu.

english_verse: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ní m kpáafì-bi ki bí-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni dɔ̀ digundi nyɔkɔpu kunyeeu ní? Ni yaa gbíntìi dɔ̀ míǹ, m làá yàntī bí cúú-ni.» Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee ní bi gbēeǹ kaa ti dòoń ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal.

english_verse: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
translation_verse: Ní m bí Leefii yab yii bí ŋá bi-ba circir kí cùú cīití mpunyɔmu bí ŋmā kí nīn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa. «Kii míǹ mun puee, taa súntí m-pu m-Nimbɔtiu. A-laŋŋaŋfitiiku nín wīikí miŋyee puee, sɔ̄ m-saai!»

english_verse: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní m dáań ki ká yii Juuda yab nìn cáá Asidoodi nì Amɔn nì Moowaab yab bisalib.

english_verse: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
translation_verse: Bi-biyaamu dijandi nìn sòoǹ Asidoodi yab sooŋyi ní biba mun sòoǹ ntimu mubɔ yab sooŋyi. Bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn gbìl̀ Juuda yab sooŋyi.

english_verse: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: M nìn wòon̄-bi, ki mēē mbusu ki tɔ́-bi. M nìn gbáń bi-kansikin biba ki dátì ki fùkū bi-yikpiti, ní ki yāntì bi pūtì Unimbɔti yindi pu. M nìn bí-bi yii: «Ní taa ti dū ni-bisalib kí tīī-bi ticati, ní ni nì ni-jipɔmbi ń taa cáá bi-bisalib.

english_verse: God dearly loved King Solomon of Israel and made him the greatest king on earth, but Solomon's foreign wives led him into sin.
translation_verse: An kaa sá tibɔti gbanti juti di nìn dáaĺ Isirayeel yab bɔtiu Saloomɔn ki kɔ́ǹ ikpitinaaa? Waa nìn cáá juti atimbuŋkpaan bɔtiibi kansikin. Unimbɔti nìn néeń-u, ki nìn dū-u ki kāaǹ dibeel Isirayeel kɔkɔ pu. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, úǹ ní binicannimpoobi nìn dáaĺ ki tɔ́ ikpitin.

english_verse: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
translation_verse: Bí dāá gíti gbìl̄ ni mun cee yii ni ŋá ikpitikpaan gbanti kaa yúliǹ Unimbɔti deedee, ki cáá binicannimpoobaaa?»

english_verse: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
translation_verse: Yooyadaa jipɔɔn ubɔ, usaraaŋakpil Eeliyasiib naantiu coo di nìn sá Sambalati un sá Oorɔn tiŋkinee. An pu ní m nìn jìn̄-u ki nyántì Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: «Óò m-Nimbɔtiu, taa súntí binib bin di bíil̀ disaraaŋal tundee nì mpèé ŋun a ŋá si nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yabee pu.»

english_verse: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: M nìn yāntì bi ŋá Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ circir bi nì binicambi nín kpáfèe pu, ki nìn fātìi síiǹ marab bin ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab làá nīn nóó báà ŋma ń nīn tūǹ u-tundi tiŋanee.

english_verse: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_verse: M nìn fātìi síiǹ idɔkpaakaa saraabi bin sá bí nīn cāabìń ŋwiin ŋun bi yóoǹ bí cáańee nì tijincɔ̀fikaal tin bi péetí kí lēē kitiŋ puee saraabi. «Óò m-Nimbɔtiu, nì a-laŋŋaŋfitiiku puee, taa súntí m-pu.»

english_verse: King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti ní ubɔti Asuweerusi kāl̀ u-beejal pu Suusi ditiŋyil.

english_verse: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
translation_verse: U-beel bintataatiil poonee ní u ŋá tican ki yíiń u-kàliŋkpilib nì u-tɔntɔnliibi nì Peeriisi nì Meedi yab janjakpilib nì ntimu yidambi nì mu-kàliŋkpilib.

english_verse: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
translation_verse: Iwiin gbanti boonee ní ubɔti ŋá binib bin kɔkɔ bí Suusi ditiŋyilinee tican ubɔti mɔŋkiŋu, kí yòon̄ binikpaambi kí tin cáá sāā ŋwaamu bi jíń áli iwiin iluli.

english_verse: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū gulfa ki lùn̄ bisatapimbi nì bimambi gàaa, ní ki dū gulfaman ki lùn̄ iŋmii ki dūu bɔ́ tikúti bɔmbiyaamun, ki dū satabee ki sākaǹ jaantalkub bin bi dū kaaluubi ki nákáǹee pu. Ní ki dū kaaluubi nì tin jìl̀ee nì bikaaluubɔmbi ki ŋàl̄ kitiŋ, ní ki dū sindaariya lambammu nì tikúti lambammu ki yóoǹ an pu.

english_verse: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
translation_verse: Sindaariya kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi poon ní bi nìn tìì binib ndaam, ní kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabee nìn bí tɔbin. Mbɔtidaamee nìn pùub̀ ní. Nì tiniti ní bi nìn bàtī ndaamee ki tìì binib.

english_verse: and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn pú nsan yii báà ŋma ń nyɔ̀ ndaam u nín là puee, di sá yii u nìn síiǹ u-tɔntɔnliibi mara yii bí ŋá min un sá kamaa lèe kí tīī udaan.

english_verse: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
translation_verse: Unimpubɔti Fastii mun nìn bɔ́ntì tican dibɔticindi poon ki yíiń binimpoobi. Ubɔti jìn̄ unimpubɔti Fastii

english_verse: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
translation_verse: Bi bí jiŋaal poon míǹ iwiin iluli dalee, ndaam nyāatì ubɔti. Niinee ní u yíiń Meewuman nì Biisita nì Arboona nì Biigita nì Abagita nì Seetaar nì Karkasi, u-tɔntɔnliibi biluli bin sá bifaabi ki bí u-cindinee.

english_verse: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-bi yii bí cùú yíiń unimpubɔti Fastii ú dāan̄ kí nīn cíkiń u-beefuuliiki. U nìn là kí dū u-nyaaŋku kí dàkà abɔtibil nì bikàliŋkpilib bin u nìn yíiń ticanee, di sá unimpubɔtee nìn ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu tikpil.

english_verse: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
translation_verse: Bifaabi cūtìi tùkū unimpubɔti Fastii ubɔti nín lī puee, ama ní u yíì kaa cūtì. Niinee ubɔti fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu.

english_verse: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
translation_verse: Bikpootiliibi biluli bin nìn bí ki nákáǹ ubɔtee di nìn sá Kaarseena nì Keetaar nì Adimata nì Taarsiisi nì Meereesi nì Maarseena nì Meemukan. Binib biluli gbanti di nìn sá Peeriisi nì Meedi kàliŋkpilib bin pu ubɔti nìn mákée, bíǹ di nìn kā ipaaŋkpaan ubɔti gɔminau poon.

english_verse: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí-bi yii: «Man ubɔtikpaan, m tú m-faabi unimpubɔti Fastii cee ki tīī-bi dinyɔɔbundi yii bí yíiń-u, ní u yíì kaa dɔ́miń. Mara poonee ditafadaaldi dilal ní u máaǹ ní?»

english_verse: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
translation_verse: Ní Meemukan fōō dinyɔɔbundi ubɔti kàliŋkpilib nimbiin ki bí yii: «An kaa sá ubɔti baba ní unimpubɔti Fastii kpēē fám, ama an sá ki kpáaǹ bikàliŋkpilib nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti Asuweerusi tiŋki jaaŋŋi kɔkɔnee ní.

english_verse: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
translation_verse: Di sá yii binimpoobi làá gbìl̄ tibɔti tin unimpubɔti ŋá nee, ní ki mun dāa kíǹ ki kpèé bi-calib fám, ní kí dūú kpáĺ yii: <Ubɔtikpaan nìn tú bí yíiń unimpubɔti Fastiiyee, u nìn yíì ní kaa cūtì.>

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Díǹ gba Peeriisi nì Meedi kàliŋkpilib nimpoobi làá gbìl̄ unimpubɔti nín ŋá tiŋyee. Míǹ mbaantiim ní bi mun làá kpèè timbi a-kàliŋkpilib bin sá bi-calibee fám, kun làá dāá yàntī bininjab ń fōō aŋuuyee dee.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: A yaa bàà kíikée, ti-baa ubɔti, á bàà síiń mara yii Fastii ń taa ti gbóonní a-cee, ní kí fàtīí lēē unimpubɔti un jítiǹ-uee. Mara gbantee, bí ŋmà-u Peeriisi nì Meedi yab marabin ubɔ ń taa ŋmā kí kpìtī-u.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun mara un sii ubɔti yóoǹee yaa bàn̄ a-beekpaandi jaaŋŋi kɔkɔnee, binimpoobi kɔkɔ, bikpaambi nì ŋwaamu dāa kíǹ ki tɔ́ bi-calib ní.»

english_verse: King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said,
translation_verse: Nlandɔkɔee nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ubɔti nì u-kàliŋkpilib, ní ubɔti ŋá kii Meemukan nín kpōotì-u puee.

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn ki tīī u-beel tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔ, kitiŋ kamaa nì ki-ŋmaŋmabiti nì ki-sooŋyi poon. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ yii uninja kamaa ń nīn sá uyidaan u-dicaŋkun, kí páb́ bí nīn sòoǹ u-nibul sooŋyi.

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Míǹ jítì boon, ubɔti Asuweerusi ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkèe, ní u téetì Fastii nín nìn ŋá-u miŋyee, nì u mun nín nìn síiǹ-u laakiŋyee.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bin sá ubɔti kpambaliŋee bí-u yii: «An máaǹ tí nyàab̀ bisapɔmbi bin ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu tikpil kaa nyí uninjee kí tīī ubɔti.

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: An puee ubɔti ń lēē u-tiŋki jaaŋŋi kɔkɔn bikàlimbi bí nyàab̀ bisapɔmbi bin ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu tikpil kaa nyí uninjee. Bí cáań-bi Suusi ditiŋyil, kí kɔ́ǹ-bi binimpoobi diiŋŋin. Bí dū-bi kí ŋúbiǹ Eegee, ubɔti faaliu un cí u-nimpoobee, ní úǹ ń tīī-bi ikpafi in ŋáŋkí tiwunee bí nīn ŋmìtī.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Ní usapɔɔn un yaa fáatì ubɔtee ń kpántí unimpubɔti kí fōō Fastii yil.» Tibɔti gbantee nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ubɔti ní u yāntì bi ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ujuudaja ubɔ nìn bí Suusi tiŋki kin sá ditiŋyilee poon, bí yíì-u Maardoosee. U sá Beenjameen naakookun. U-naanjab di sá Yaayiir nì Simeeyii nì Kiisi.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Kijapaayee nìn kútì binib bin Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn cúuń kuyuŋu Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ki kpáaǹ Juuda yab bɔtiu Yookooniyayee poon.

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Maardoosee nìn fōō u-baawaai bisal u kā u-cee, bi yíì-u Adaasa àá Eesiteer. U-na nì u-baa nìn kpíì, ní Maardoosee fōō-u ki ŋúb́ kii u-bisalee. Usapɔɔnee nìn ŋān̄ tikpil.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Bi nín dū ubɔti nín lī puee nì u-marau ki báakì ntimu poon yii ubɔti nyàab̀ bisapɔmbee, ní bi kóoǹní bisapɔmbi tikpil ki cáań ki kpáfì Suusi tiŋki kin sá ditiŋyilee poon, ní Eegee kpèé-bi. Bi cáań Eesiteer mun ubɔti cindi, ki dū-u ki ŋúbiǹ Eegee un cí ubɔti nimpoobee.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Eesiteer nìn kɔ́ kijapaayee, ki ká diyimɔɔl u-cee, ní u nyàab̄ ikpafi in u làá nīn ŋmìtī u-wunti ń nīn ŋān̄ee nì tin u làá nīn jīǹee malaa ki tīī-u. U nìn lēē bisapɔmbi bin bí ubɔti cindinee biluli ki tīī-u bí nīn bí u-cee ki tútúǹ-u, ní ki kpēē ubɔti diiŋŋi kudimɔntiiu ki cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ niin.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Eesiteer kaa nìn nyántì u-ba ki dàkā yii u sá dinibul dinee àá u-nyeeŋŋu sá doo, kun puee Maardoosee nìn kpáafì-u yii ú taa pée tùkù ubɔ u-nyeeŋŋu.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Baabadalee, Maardoosee pée cá binimpoobi diiŋŋi mɔŋkiŋu ní ki kpèé yii Eesiteer bí mana àá bi ŋúb́-u mana.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní usapɔɔn yaa dū ikpafi ki ŋmītì u-wunti iŋmal saalaa nì ili ki dóò kii an nín bàlifī unimpu ń dū ŋyunti ŋun kí bɔ́ntí u-bee, ní ú nín cù ubɔti Asuweerusi cee. Di sá bi nìn dù ŋkpam min bi yíì miiree ní kí nùkù bi-wunti iŋmal iluu, ní kí dū iŋmal iluu mun kí ŋmìtī binimpoobi kpafii in ŋáŋkí tiwunee.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Usapɔɔn un yuntiŋu yaa bāań ú cù ubɔti ceeyee, bi tìì-u tin kɔkɔ u yaa là kí ŋúb́ kí cù ubɔti cindinee ní.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: U nìn cá kujoou ní kutaa yaa wúntì kutaafaauee ní ú fàtīí gítiń kí kɔ́ binimpoobi bililiitiibi diikun, ní ufaal Saakigaasi un cí ubɔti bɔmbee cí-bi. Baa ti gítí ubɔti cee, see un di yaa kɔ́-u ní u yíiń u-yindi yii ú dāan̄ee baba di gítí.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Ubɔti naŋki nìn kɔ́ Eesiteer tikpil ki jítiǹ binimpoobi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ. U nìn ká ubɔti cee diyimɔɔl nì kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ki jítiǹ bisapɔmbi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ. Ubɔti nìn dū kibeefuulii ki cíkiǹ-u, ní ki dū-u ki kpántì unimpubɔti Fastii paaŋŋu.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti ŋá tican Eesiteer pu, ní ki yíiń u-tɔntɔŋkpilib nì u-kàliŋkpilib, ní ki pú u-tiŋki jaaŋŋi kɔkɔ lampoo, ní ki ŋá binib tiniti mbɔtiyaamin.

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Bi nìn gíti nyàab̄ bisapɔmbi nliliitiim ki kpáfì ubɔti dumpu. Ŋyunti gbantee, Maardoosee bí ubɔti cindi ki sá ukàlinja.

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: Eesiteer kaa nìn yāntì bi béè u-nyeeŋŋu nì dinibul din u sée, kii Maardoosee nín nìn kpáafì-u puee. Eesiteer pée gbíntìi ŋúb́ tin Maardoosee nìn dàkā-uee kii u nín nìn pée bí u-cee ki ŋúb́-tì puee ní. Maardoosee cúú binib bin là kí kpɔ̀ ubɔtee

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Maardoosee bí ubɔti cindin ki tūǹ u-kàlintundee, ní bifaabi bili Bigitan nì Teereesi bin nìn cí ubɔti punyɔkɔkee fōō ubɔti pu diŋuul ki nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Ama ní Maardoosee gbìl̄ an bɔti, ní ki dūu tùkū unimpubɔti Eesiteer, ní úǹ dū an bɔtee ki nāatì ubɔti.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Bi cɔ́ŋkì ki kpēēyee, tibɔtee lafun sá mbaamɔn, ní bi cúú bi-liitil ki lúntì idɔ pu bi kpíì. Ní bi dū an bɔtee ki ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmà tibɔti ki cáa kpáafée ubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti Asuweerusi kāaǹ Ameedata jipɔɔn Amaani u-tɔntɔŋkpilib kɔkɔ pu tikpiti. Amaani gbanti nìn sá Agaagi naakookun ní.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn yóoǹ bikàlimbi bin bí u-cindin ki tūǹ atuunee mara yii Amaani yaa jītée, báà ŋma ń gbàan̄ u-nimbiin kí tīī-u jilma. Ama Maardoosee nìn yíì kaa gbàantí, kaa tàtīi dòontí dicincibil Amaani nimbiin.

english_verse: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
translation_verse: Ní bikàlimbi bin kɔ kíǹ ubɔti cindinee bālifì Maardoosee yii: «Ba pu ní sii kaa tɔ́ ubɔti marau un u yóoǹee ní?»

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Bi pée dāantí tibɔbaantiil gbanti ní ki tùkù Maardoosee ní waa fātìi tɔ́. Ní u bí-bi yii úǹ sá ujuudaja ní. An pu ní bi dūu tùkū Amaani kí kpèè u yaa làá nīn gbíntì ki ŋáań míǹ.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Amaani nín lafun dáań ki ká yii Maardoosee kaa gbàantí u-nimbiin kaa tí tàtīi dòontí dicincibil ki tìì-u jilmee, ní u fōō diŋuul u-pu.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: U nín béè yii Maardoosee sá ujuudajee, ní u ká nlandɔkɔ yii Maardoosee baba maŋfal ní waa làá lēē, ama u làá kúntí Maardoosee nì u-yab Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti Asuweerusi tiŋki kɔkɔnee ní.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Asuweerusi nín jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì ali, uŋmapeepeekaa un bi yíì Niisaŋyee poon ní bi tɔ́ Puur, an dàkà yii bi tɔ́ kasi Amaani nimbiin ŋwiin kamaa pu nì uŋmal kamaa pu kí kpèè ŋwiin àá uŋmal un di máaǹ ú kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yabee. Ní an dūu lítì uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti pu, uŋmal gbanti ní bi yíì Adaar. Amaani bíi bɔ́ntí kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yab

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Ní Amaani bí ubɔti yii: «Dinibul diba bí ki yàl̄ ki kɔ́ a-tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔn, ki nyáń di-ba nì anibul ŋin kíǹee. Di-marab nyáń bi-ba nì anibul kɔkɔ marab, ní bíǹ kaa tɔ́ ubɔti marab. Aa cáá ipaati iba bi-pu kí yàntī bí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Ti-baa ubɔti, an yaa bàà ŋān̄ a-ceeyee, á bàà ŋmà kugbɔŋu kí pɔ̄ kinyɔkɔ bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi. Man làá ŋmàntī animbil kúti kutukub saalaa kí tīī a-kàlimbi bin bí a-cindin ki tūǹ atuunee bí dūú ŋá ubɔti nimbiliŋ dakaau poon.»

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti fúutì u-bɔmbiki kin cáá u-daaŋkuee u-ŋaan ki dūu tīī Juuda yab pulincɔnti Amaani un sá Ameedata jipɔɔn ki sá Agaagi naakookunee.

english_verse: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «M gíiǹ a-nimbiliŋ ki kpáaǹ dinibulee ki tīī-si á ŋá-bi min a lèe.»

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Ní bi yíiń ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliibi uŋmapeepeekaa iwiin saalaa nì ita dal. Ní Amaani yāntì bi ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn ki tīī atinjan kɔkɔ bɔtibiliŋ nì ŋi-gɔminab nì dinibul kamaa bɔtiu. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī dinibul kamaa di-sooŋyin nì di-ŋmaŋmabiti ní. Ubɔti Asuweerusi yindi pu ní bi ŋmàn̄, ki dū u-bɔmbiki kin cáá u-daaŋkuee ki nyīī tigbɔnee pu.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti tuuŋyi yōoǹ tigbɔnee ki yākatì ubɔti tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔn. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔnee poon yii: «Bi pú kinyɔkɔ yii uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti poon, Adaar ŋmaliu iwiin saalaa nì ita dalee, bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yab kɔkɔ, binipɔmbi nì bitikpilib nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu. An sá ŋwimbaanti ní bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi kí yòon̄ bi-wanti.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii u-tuuŋyi ń yòon̄ tigbɔnee kí cáá yàkatī malaa malaa, ní bi cáa yākatì, ní maree dūu gbītì Suusi ditiŋyil poon. Ŋyunti gbantee Amaani nì ubɔti cūtìi kāl̀ ki bíi nyù ndaam, ní Suusi tiŋki kɔkɔ kɔ́ dinimbinaamandin.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Maardoosee nín gbìl̄ tin kɔkɔ jítèe, ní u dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin u pēēyee, ki dū kutukub ki pēeǹ, ki dū ŋfantam ki pùkū u-ba, ní ki nyáń kitiŋin ki gbáà ibiil mpɔn ki yáliŋkí.

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: U bàn̄ ubɔti mɔŋkiŋuee ní ki yúl̀, kun puee ubɔ kaa cáá nsan kí nīn pēē kutuku kí kɔ́ ubɔti cindi.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní kitiŋ jaaŋŋi laakin kamaa ní mara un ubɔti yóoǹee yaa bàn̄ee, an sá dikpool ní Juuda yab cee. Bi nìn bōob̀ nnyɔmu, ní binib tikpil sūǹ ki yáliŋkí, ní ki pēē kutukub ki dɔ̄ ŋfantamin ki bíntí.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Eesiteer tɔntɔnliibi bisapɔmbi nì u-faabi cūtìi tùkū-u tin bi kée, ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ tikpil. Ní u nyàab̄ abɔkuti ki tīī-bi bí cáá tīī-u, ú pèetī kutukub bin u pēēyee kí dū abɔkuti ŋin u tīī-uee kí pèen̄, ama ní Maardoosee yíì.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Niinee Eesiteer yíiń Ataaki, ufaal un ubɔti nìn tīī-u ú nīn bí ki tútúǹ-uee ki tú ú cùú bàlifì Maardoosee kí béé kun di yì-tì ní u bíi ŋáań mimmee.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Ní Ataaki nín cá ki bàn̄ ki ká-u u yú mmɔŋkijaa, ubɔti naakooku nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Ní Maardoosee máafì-u tin kɔkɔ jítèe, nì animbil ŋin nyɔkɔm Amaani pōoǹ ubɔti yii bi yaa kūū ki céetì Juuda yab u làá cáá ŋá ubɔti nimbiliŋ dakaaunee.

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: Ní u dū kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋmàn̄ Suusi an gbītì an kɔkɔ yii bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yabee ki tīī-u ú cáá dàkà Eesiteer, ú béé tin poon bi bée, kí ká ubɔti kí gbàam̀-u ú sɔ̄ u-nibul Juuda yab saai.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Ní Ataaki cáá tibɔti tin Maardoosee sòon̄ee ki tùkū Eesiteer.

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: «Ubɔti tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti tinjaŋŋi poonee nyí yii ubɔti yaa kaa yíiń sii ubɔ ní a jítìi kɔ́ u-cindinee, see bí kpɔ̀-si, an sá mara ní. Ama sii un ní ubɔti yaa tāntì u-bɔtikpandɔŋu ŋun sá sindaariyee ki túĺee, sii di ŋmátí. Man ŋá iwiin mmuŋku nì saalaa dee ubɔti kaa yíiń-mi m cūtì u-cee.»

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Ní Ataaki cáá Eesiteer nín lī puee ki tùkū Maardoosee.

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Ní Maardoosee kíí Eesiteer yii: «Á taa dàkafì yii a nín bí dibeecindinee puee, sii baba di làá ŋmátí Juuda yab kɔkɔ kansikin.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: A yaa kaa ŋá tiba agìń yuntii in poon ti bí nee, Unimbɔti làá jòò Juuda yab kí fīī-bi, ama ní sii nì a-baa dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ ń kpú. Ŋma tin ká an yaa kaa sá tin bí nee pu ní a kpántì unimpubɔti?»

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Ní Eesiteer kíí Maardoosee yii:

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: «Á cù kí kpāfì Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bí Suusi tiŋkinee, bí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ kí mèè Unimbɔti kí tīī-mi. Ní taa jī kí taa nyɔ̀ iwiin ita ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Ma mun nì m-tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi làá bóob́ kinyɔkɔ míǹ mbaantiim. Boonee ní ḿ cùú ká ubɔti nì min kɔkɔ mara yú yii ubɔ kaa cée, ní an yaa sá ŋkúmaaa, ḿ kpú.»

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Ní Maardoosee cūtìi ká u-yab ní ki ŋá kii Eesiteer nín bālifì yii bí ŋá puee.

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Bi bóob́ kinyɔkɔ míǹ winta dalee, ní Eesiteer dū unimpubɔti bɔkutiŋ ki pēeǹ ki nín cá ubɔti cee. U bàn̄ee ní ki kɔ́ ki yú ubɔti beecindin ki bíitiǹ kunaakoou. Ubɔti kā u-naakookun u-beejal pu ní u-nimbiin túĺ mmɔŋki punyɔkɔki.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: U nín ká unimpubɔti Eesiteer yú dibeecindinee, ní u pú-u diyimɔɔl ki tāntì u-bɔtikpandɔŋu ŋun sá sindaariyee, ní Eesiteer sútìń ki gbēē nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Unimpubɔti Eesiteer, ba ŋá? Ba ní a là ní? Báà an yaa sá m-beel dijandi ní a là, m làá tīī-si.»

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Ní Eesiteer kíí-u yii: «An yaa bàà fáatì ti-baa ubɔti u nì Amaani ń bàà dāan̄ m-cee díǹ kí jī tican tin m bɔ́ntì kí ŋá kí tīī-uee.»

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti tú unil dicilpu niin ú tùkù Amaani yii ú bɔ́ntí malaa malaa kí dāan̄ bí cùú jī tican tin Eesiteer bɔ́ntì ki yíiń-bee. Ní Amaani dɔ́miń ki céeǹ ubɔti bí cùú jī tican tin Eesiteer bɔ́ntì ki yíiń-bee.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Bi jíń tijin ki dóòyee ní ubɔti bālifì Eesiteer yii: «Ba ní a là ní? Báà an yaa sá m-beel dijandi ní a yaa là, m làá tīī-si.»

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: Ti-baa ubɔti, m yaa ká diyimɔɔl a-cee, ní an yaa fáatì-si yii á ŋá tin páb́-mi m là kí mèè-si á tīī-mee, sii nì Amaani ń fu gítiń fool kí dāá jī tican tin m làá fu tí bɔ́ntí kí tīī-nee. Niin ní m làá fu tùkù ti-baa ubɔti tin m là ú ŋá kí tīī-mee.» Amaani bɔ́ntì ndɔ kí lúntí Maardoosee

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Yaadalee Amaani nìn nyáń unimpubɔti dumpu an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u u-pɔbil píil̀. Niinee ní u ká Maardoosee ubɔti naakooku nyɔkɔpu, ama ní úǹ kaa cīŋkì u-ba báà fiii ní kaa nín tīī-u disíndi. Niinee Amaani fōō Maardoosee pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: Ní u cúú u-ba kaa lī tiba ní ki nín kùǹ. U bàn̄ee ní ki yíiń u-bɔɔbi nì u-nimpuu Seereesi.

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Amaani bíi dàkà u-ba ki sòoǹ nì bi u nín cáá tigaajati tikpil nì jipɔmbi kupaau puee nì jilma un ubɔti tīī-u ki dū-u ki kāaǹ mpaan ŋun pu u jítiǹ u-kàliŋkpilib kɔkɔee.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Amaani nìn gíti bí yii: «Unimpubɔti Eesiteer nín ŋá tican ki yíiń ubɔtee, man baba ní u yíiń ḿ céeǹ ubɔti, ní ti cūtì díǹ ki jíń. U gíti tí yíiń-ti fool man nì ubɔti tí fu cù u-cee kí jī.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Ama tin bí nee kaa pée tìì-mi mmɔn ŋubɔ, ŋyunti ŋun ní Maardoosee ujuudaja gbíntìi kā u-paaŋŋu dibeecindi nyɔkɔpu m wāĺ-uee.»

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbantee, ŋgeem nìn sáǹ ubɔti nimbiliŋ pu, ní u yāntì bi cáań kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin nìn jítì bibɔtiibi pu dooooyee ki kàan̄ u-nimbiin.

english_verse: When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king,
translation_verse: Bi kàan̄ee ki ká laakin ubɔti Asuweerusi faabi bili, Bagitan nì Teereesi bin nìn cí ubɔti punyɔkɔkee nìn nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀ ubɔtee, nì Maardoosee nín nìn bīitì bi-pu puee.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Maardoosee nín nìn ŋá mimmee, ba nyooti nì ba paati ní bi nìn tīī-u?» Ní ubɔti kpambaliŋ bí yii: «Baa nìn tīī-u tiba.»

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Ni ubɔti bí yii: «Ŋma di bí dicindi?» Ŋyunti gbantee Amaani kóoń ubɔti cindi kí bàà tùkù-u yii u bɔ́ntì ndɔ ki cáań kí dūú lúntí Maardoosee dee.

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti kpambaliŋ kíí-u yii: «Amaani di bí dicindi.» Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Tùkùmaan-u yii ú kóoń.»

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Ní Amaani kɔ́, ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Ubɔti yaa là kí tīī unil ubɔ jilmee, u ŋáań-u mana ní?» Amaani nìn dākafì yii: «Ŋma di gíti bí ubɔti là kí tīī-u jilma an yaa kaa sá man?»

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
translation_verse: Ní Amaani kíí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a yaa là kí tīī unil ubɔ jilmee,

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: an sá bí cáań dibeebɔkutil din ubɔti pēeǹee, nì ubɔti taamuu un pu u kāl̀ee, ní kí dū ubɔti beefuuliiki kí cíkiń-u.

english_verse: Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
translation_verse: Ní bí lēē bikàliŋkpilib kansikin ubɔ, kí dū dibeebɔkutilee nì utaamu kí dūú ŋúbiǹ udaan ń dūú pèen̄ unil un ubɔti là kí tīī jilmee ní kí dū-u kí kàan̄ utaamuee pu. Ní ú cáá-u kí nīn yìiǹ kitiŋin, ní binib ń nīn līī u-nyɔkɔpu ki tátí yii: <Kpèèmaan, bi nín ŋáań unil un ubɔti là kí tīī jilmee puee sèé!>»

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí Amaani yii: «Too, malaa cùú yòon̄ dibeebɔkutil nì utaamu kí ŋá kii a nín pée sòon̄ pu nee kí tīī Maardoosee ujuudaja un kā dibeecindi punyɔkɔpuee. A nín pée lī puee, á ŋá míǹ deedee kí taa bàtī tiba.»

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Ní Amaani cūtìi nyàab̄ dibeebɔkutil nì utaamu, ní ki dū dibeebɔkutilee ki pēeǹ Maardoosee, ní ki dū-u ki kāaǹ utaamu pu, ní ki cáá-u ki yìin̄ kitiŋin, ní ki līī u-nyɔkɔpu ki tátí yii: «Kpèèmaan, bi nín ŋáań unil un ubɔti là kí tīī jilmee puee sèé!»

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, ní Maardoosee fātì dibeecindi punyɔkɔpu, ní Amaani nín kùǹ malaa u-dumpu nì icoo, u-yil tīī.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Amaani bàn̄ee ní ki máafì u-nimpuu Seereesi nì u-bɔɔbi tin jítèe kɔkɔ. Niinee ní u-bɔɔbi bin kpòotī-uee nì u-nimpuu Seereesi bí-u yii: «Maardoosee un nimbiin a kíĺ ki bíi gbàantí nee sá ujuudaja ní. An puee a pée gíti kpá kí ŋmā-u, sii làá mɔ̀tīí nīn sìntī taapu ní ki cá.»

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Bi bí ki sòoǹee ní ubɔti faabi dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ Amaani malaa, bi búntì tican tin Eesiteer bɔ́ntì ki yíiń-bee laŋki.

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Ubɔti nì Amaani búntì unimpubɔti Eesiteer cee kí jī tican.

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Ŋwinliliiti dal bi jíń ki nyùn̄ ki dóòyee ní ubɔti bālifì unimpubɔti Eesiteer yii: «Ba ní a là ní? Báà an yaa sá m-beel dijandi ní a yaa bālifì-mi, m làá tīī-si.»

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Ní unimpubɔti bí yii: «Too ti-baa ubɔti, m yaa ká diyimɔɔl a-cee ní an yaa fáatì-see, á dā man nì m-nibul maŋfal kí líí. Tin páb́-mi m là kí mèè-see dee, ti-baa ubɔti.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii bi dū man nì m-nibul ki nyáfì bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ti. An yaa bàà sá yii bi dū-ti ki nyáfì tí bàà kpántí iyumbu, maa bàà lì tiba a-cee, kun puee tíǹ kaa bàn̄ tibɔti ḿ cáań kí páb́ ubɔti.»

english_verse: “Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti bālifì unimpubɔti Eesiteer yii: «Ŋma di sá-u ní ki cáá nlandɔkɔ gbanti? Udaan bí la?»

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Ní Eesiteer kíí-u yii: «Un páb́-ti ki sá ti-nannanliuee di sá Amaani unikpiti nee!» Niinee ní dinyoondi kɔ́ Amaani ubɔti nì unimpubɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti fōō diŋuul ní ki yíkì ki yāntì tijin ki nyáń ki yú mmɔŋki. Ní Amaani gbíntì Eesiteer cee ki bíi gbàam̄-u kí fīī u-maŋfal, kun puee u nìn ká yii ubɔti nín yíkì miŋyee, an sá ŋkúm di dɔ̄ ki cí-u.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Ní u lítì kilambaŋ kin pu Eesiteer nìn kēe taapu ki bíi gbàam̄-u. Ubɔti nyánní mmɔŋki ki fātìi kóońee ki ká Amaani kudii kun poon bi bàà bíi jīǹ ticanee, u dɔ̄ dicincibil laakin Eesiteer kēe, ní ubɔti téeń mpɔn yii: «Kijapaai nee là kí dòon̄ nì Eesiteer mpɔn man nimbiin m-diikunaaa?» Ubɔti tin pée lì míǹ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ee bi dɔ́miń ki cúú Amaani ki dū tiwan ki bīiǹ u-nimbiin.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Ní bi dū Amaani ki lúntì ndɔ ŋun u nìn bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ bí dū Maardoosee kí lúntée. Niinee ní ubɔti ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkì.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti dal ní ubɔti Asuweerusi dū Juuda yab nannanliu Amaani gaajawanti kɔkɔ ki tīī unimpubɔti Eesiteer. Míǹ boonee ní Eesiteer cáá Maardoosee ki dàkā ubɔti ki tùkū-u yii úǹ di sá u-baa.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti fúutì u-bɔmbiki kin cáá u-daaŋku u nìn fōō Amaani ceeyee ki dūu tīī Maardoosee. Ní unimpubɔti Eesiteer dū Maardoosee ki kāaǹ tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ Amaani nìn cááyee pu. Ubɔti nyántì mara kí mɔ̄tì Juuda yab pu

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Ní Eesiteer lítì ubɔti nimbiin nì nnyinnyim ki fātìi sòon̄ nì u ki gbāam̀-u yii ú kpìtī mbusu un Amaani un sá Agaagi naakookunee nìn nyàab̄ kí kɔ́ǹ-bee, nì u nín lēē nsàmbiyaamu mun kí céetí Juuda yabee.

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, m yaa ká diyimɔɔl a-cee, ní an yaa ŋān̄ a-cee m-bɔti fáatì-see, á ŋmà kí kpìtī mara un Ameedata jipɔɔn Amaani un sá Agaagi naakookunee ŋmàn̄ yii bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ kóò a-tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔnee.

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti kíí unimpubɔti nì Maardoosee, ujuudaja yii: «Kpèè, m dū Amaani gaajati kɔkɔ ki tīī Eesiteer ní ki yāntì bi lúntì-u ndɔ pu, kun puee u bàà là bí kpɔ̀ Juuda yab.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Di sá kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋmàn̄ ubɔti yindi pu, ki dū ubɔti jaliiki ki nyīīyee, nsan kpá ubɔ ń kpìtī tibɔti tin bi ŋmàn̄ee. Míǹ puee, ni mun ŋmàmaan min làá tūtuǹ Juuda yab bí mɔ̄tì bi-ba puee ubɔti yindi pu, kí dū ubɔti jaliiki kí nyīī.»

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Bi ŋmàn̄ tigbɔnee ubɔti Asuweerusi yindi pu, ní ki dū u-bɔmbiki kin cáá u-daaŋkuee ki nyīī ní ki dūu tīī bitanjakaliibi, bí yòon̄ ubɔti taamui in sá itammɔntee kí cáá tigbɔnee kí yàkatī.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Niinee Maardoosee nyánní ubɔti dumpu ki pēē dibeebɔkutil din ŋmàl̄ mmam gàaa nì mpimee, ki dū iŋaaman in bí fálfalee bɔkutifɔkɔl ki páaǹ ní ki cíkí sindaariya beefuuliiki kikpaaŋŋi. Suusi yab nìn kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi ki fàal̀.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: An nìn sá dipɔɔpindi nì ifaal nì dinyandi ní Juuda yab cee.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Atinjan nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon ní ubɔti marauee nìn bàn̄ee, an nìn sá dipɔɔpindi nì ifaal nì jiŋaal ní Juuda yab cee. Ní dinyoondi kɔ́ anibul ŋin kɔ kíǹee, ní an yāntì binib tikpil kpántì Juuda yab.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti poon, Adaar ŋmaliu iwiin saalaa nì ita dal, ŋwiin ŋun bi nìn yóoǹ yii bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yabee dūu bāań. Juuda yab nannanliibi dākafì yii bíǹ di làá pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi ŋwiin gbanti, ama ní an cúu lábitì ní Juuda yab pɔ́ɔkiǹ bin kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ-bee.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Juuda yab nìn kpáfì ntimu mun poon bi bée ubɔti Asuweerusi tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔn ki cíitì bin kɔkɔ làá táká-bee. Ama báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋúń ki yúl̀ bi-nimbiin, kun puee dinyoondi nìn cúú bi-nannanliibi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Atinjan kɔkɔ kàliŋkpilib nì abɔtibil nì gɔminab nì ubɔti tɔntɔŋkpilib kɔkɔee nìn yú Juuda yab boon ní, kun puee bi nìn fàŋkí Maardoosee ní yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Di sá Maardoosee nìn kā ŋkakaakpaan pu ní ubɔti beecindin, ní ki nìn nyáń diyindi kitiŋ jaaŋŋi kɔkɔn. Maardoosee yindi nìn mɔ̀tīi yíkí yilpu ní ki cá.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Juuda yab nìn dū ntàataajimu ki kūū ki nāaǹ bi-nannanliibi kɔkɔ. Bíǹ bin nìn kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ Juuda yabee, Juuda yab ŋá-bi bi nín là puee.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Ŋwimbaanti gbanti ní bi tùkū ubɔti bininjab bin nyɔkɔm bi kūū Suusi ditiŋyilinee.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí unimpubɔti Eesiteer yii: «Suusi ditiŋyil ní Juuda yab kūū bininjab alaataa aŋmoo ki kpáaǹ Amaani jipɔmbi saalaayee, mimmee m-tinjaŋŋi ŋin kíǹee poonee, bi ŋá mana? A yaa gíti là tiba ḿ ŋá kí tīī-si, bàlifì-mi m làá tīī-si kudɔŋu. Ba ní a là ní?»

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Ní Eesiteer kíí yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a yaa bàà kíikée, á pɔ̄ kinyɔkɔ fool marauee ń nìkī díǹ Juuda yab bin bí Susee ń nìkī kujaau, ní kí dū Amaani jipɔmbi saalaayee kí lúntí ndɔ pu.»

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí ŋá míǹ, ní bi báakì maree Suusi tiŋkin. Ní bi dū Amaani jipɔmbi saalaa bin bi kūūyee ki lúntì ndɔ pu.

english_verse: Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed
translation_verse: Ní Juuda yab bin bí Suusee kpáfì Adaar ŋmaliu ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal Suusi tiŋkin, ní ki kūū bininjab alaataa ata. Ama baa nìn gbēē bin bi kūūyee wanti báà kubɔ.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
translation_verse: Uŋmal gbanti ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal ní bi gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi kù binib, ní bi dū ŋwiin gbanti ki kpántì jiŋaal nì dipɔɔpindi wiiŋŋu.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab bin nìn bí Suusi ki nìn kpáfì iwiin saalaa nì ita, nì ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal ki tɔ̀n̄ bi-nannanliibi pu ipɔntoonee nìn kāl̀ iwiin saalku dal ní ki ŋūŋfì. Bíǹ nìn dū ŋwiin gbanti ní ki kpántì jiŋaal nì dipɔɔpindi wiiŋŋu.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: An pu ní Juuda yab bin nìn kóò ntiŋgbamu poonee nìn dū Adaar ŋmaliu ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal ki kpántì jiŋaal nì dipɔɔpindi wiiŋŋu, ki ŋáań tijin ki pūǹ tɔb. Bi yóoǹ kí nīn kíǹ ki jīǹ Puuriim jiŋaaliu

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Maardoosee nìn ŋmàn̄ tin kɔkɔ jítèe ki bíl̀. U nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn ki tīī Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti Asuweerusi tinjaŋŋi ŋin pìl̄ee nì ŋin dátèe kɔkɔn.

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: U nìn tùkū-bi yii dibintil kamaa, Adaar ŋmaliu ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku nì iwiin saalku dalee, bí nīn jīǹ jiŋaal gbanti.

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: Di sá yii iwiin gbanti poon ní Juuda yab fōō bi-ba ki ŋūŋfì bi-nannanliibi pu. Adaar ŋmaliu poon ní mpɔn nìn cúu lábitì ní kunimbaau kpántì dipɔɔpindi ní dikpool kpántì jiŋaal. Iwiin gbantin ní Juuda yab ŋáań tijin ki tìì tɔb ní ki pūǹ biwɔfib tiwan.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Ní Juuda yab fōō Maardoosee nyɔkɔ, ní ki dū jiŋaal un bi jíńee ki kpántì diyaajakoobil kí nīn kíǹ ki ŋáań míǹ.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Di sá Ameedata un sá Agaagi naakookunee jipɔɔn Amaani, Juuda yab nannanliu nìn bóob́ yii bí kúntí Juuda yab. U nìn tɔ́ Puur, an dàkà yii u tɔ́ kasi kí béé ŋwiin ŋun máaǹ bí kpɔ̀ kí kúntí-bee.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Ama Eesiteer nìn cūtì ki ká ubɔti tibɔti gbanti pu, ní ubɔti yāntì bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu yii ntoom tafadaaldi din Amaani bɔ́ntì Juuda yab puee ń fàtīí lítí u-pu, ní bi dū u nì u-jipɔmbi ki lúntì idɔ pu.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: An pu ní bi nìn pú jiŋaal gbanti wiiŋyi yii Puuriim, kí dàkà yii bi nìn tɔ́ Puur ní ki lēē iwiin gbanti. Maardoosee nín nìn ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin kugbɔŋu poonee nì Juuda yab bi-ba nín nìn ká tiŋyee nì tin nìn jítì bi-puee,

english_verse: Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do.
translation_verse: ní bi dūu kpántì bi-yaajakoobil. Bíǹ nì bi-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ nì bin kɔkɔ làá dāá páanní bi-boonee làá nīn jīǹ jiŋaal gbanti dibintil kamaa iwiin ili gbanti poon, kii bi nín ŋmàn̄ ki yóoǹ yii bí nīn jīǹ-u puee.

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Unimpubɔti Eesiteer, Abiikayiil bisal nì ujuudaja Maardoosee ŋmàn̄ kugbɔnliliitiiu kí tīī kugbɔŋu kun bi nìn ŋmàn̄ Puuriim puee mpɔn.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: ní ki kpáafì-bi bí nīn jīǹ Puuriim jiŋaaliu iwiin gbanti. Án nīn sá-bi dinyɔɔboobil nì itiminsi wiiŋyi, kii Maardoosee ujuudaja nì unimpubɔti Eesiteer nín yóoǹ yii bíǹ bi-ba nì bi-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ ń nīn ŋáań puee.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Ní bi dū Eesiteer nín yóoǹ mara un Puuriim puee bɔti ki ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋun.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Asuweerusi nìn wɔ́b́ u-tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔ nib, ki kpáaǹ bin kóò ntimu mun tiŋku māntìi túee bi pà lampoo.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: Dibaatandi din u cááyee nì atuŋkpaan ŋin u ŋáaǹee nì u nín yōoǹ Maardoosee yilpu u-beelin puee, bi ŋmàn̄ an bɔti kɔkɔ Meedi nì Peeriisi yab bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, Maardoosee ujuudaja nìn sá unikpaan ní. Ubɔtikpaan Asuweerusi yaa nìn līntèe, Maardoosee di nìn pá. U-yab Juuda yab nìn néeń-u ní ki nìn tɔ́-u. U nìn pée mɔ̀ ki nyàab̀ bi-ŋanti ŋma ní, ní ki nìn mɔ́tí u-nibul kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Uninja ubɔ nìn bí Uusi tiŋkin bi yíì-u Yoob. Baa nìn kāntí u-pu tikpitil tiba ní u-pɔbil nìn bí diba nì Unimbɔti. U nìn fàŋkí Unimbɔti ní ki nìn fàtī u-boon ki tìì ikpiti.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bālifì Sitaan yii: «La ní a nyánní ní?» Ní Sitaan kíí ti-Dindaan yii: «M cūtìi yìin̄ yìin̄ ki māntì kitiŋ pu ní.»

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
