translation_verse: Kii u nín nyánní u-na poon dicancaŋgbeel puee, míǹ ní u làá fàtīí gítí. Waa pée páatì u-tundi pu, kaa làá ŋmā kí kpáaǹ báà tiba.

english_verse: They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work.
translation_verse: An sá nnaabukpaan ní ki tīī-u. U làá yīkì kitiŋ nee pu kii u nín dɔ́miń puee. U túń ditundi ki tīī kubuŋu dee.

english_verse: That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind.
translation_verse: Kí kūtèe, u-maŋfal wiiŋyi poonee, u ká agìń tikpil nì kunimbaau nì diŋuul nì diwuŋyɔtil.

english_verse: What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti yaa pú unil diyimɔɔl ú nīn cáá animbil nì tigaajawanee, ú jī tin Unimbɔti tīī-uee pu, an dàkà yii u-tundi paati. Unimbɔti di pú-u.

english_verse: Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ú súntí yii u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kaa náaǹ, kun puee Unimbɔti tīī-u dipɔɔpindi.

english_verse: There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth.
translation_verse: M gíti tí dáań ki ká nnaabu ŋubɔ mun kitiŋ pu doo, an sá nnaabukpaan ní ki tīī unil.

english_verse: God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
translation_verse: Unil di bí ní Unimbɔti tīī-u tigaajati nì tigaajawan nì tinyool. Tin kɔkɔ pée kā unil gbanti naŋki puee, u cáá-tì. Ama ní Unimbɔti kaa pú-u ú jī an wantee pu, ní unifantanti ubɔ ń dāá jī-tì. Tíǹ gbanti mun sá kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee ní, ki sá falaakpaan.

english_verse: You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial.
translation_verse: Unil ŋūǹ kí màal̀ mbiyaamu dilaataal, kí kàl̄ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí. U nín kāl̀ ki yúntì mimmee, u yaa kaa jíń nnaam ní baa kpáàa síb́-u mmɔntiimee, u páatì ba? Man ká yii kibiki kin bi màl̄ kaa yōoǹee sɔ́ǹ udaan.

english_verse: That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you,
translation_verse: Kí kūtèe, kàa pée ká ŋwìiń gba ní kaa nín béè-ŋu. An puee kíǹ cáá diŋuŋfil ki jítiǹ un kāl̀ ki yúntì kitiŋ pu doo fámee.

english_verse: even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
translation_verse: Báà udaan yaa kāl̀ kitiŋ pu doo abin kutukub bili, ama ní kaa jíń mmɔnee, u páatì ba? Di sá yii kufoou kamaa làá kúntíǹ ŋkúm ní.

english_verse: We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied.
translation_verse: Unil tūǹ ditundi u-pool pu ní, ama ní kaa díkì dalba dalba.

english_verse: We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right.
translation_verse: Kin ba ní uciŋfiti cáá ki jítiǹ ugbaan? Unandaan un còom̄ disaŋkimmɔntiil binifoobi kansikinee úǹ páatì ba?

english_verse: It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_verse: Tiwan tin a cáá a-nimbil wāĺee sɔ́ǹ tin a là kí nīn cááyee. Niin mun pée sá fám ní, a lì kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee. Uciŋfiti saŋkii

english_verse: Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us.
translation_verse: Tin kɔkɔ pée bée, bi nìn pée nyí-tì dooooyee ní, ní ti nyí kun unil sée. Waa ŋūǹ kí yíiń un pɔ̄ɔǹ-uee ibeeyiin.

english_verse: The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk?
translation_verse: A yaa sòoǹ tikpilee, a sòoǹ tibɔti tin kaa cáá taapuee mun tikpil ní. Ipaati ilai di bí poon.

english_verse: Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_verse: Unil maŋfal jītí malaa kii mboonee ní. Ŋma di nyí tin ŋān̄ ki tīī unil u-maŋfal wiiŋyi in kaa kpáàa náaǹ nee poon? Ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí tùkù-u tin làá bàń kitiŋ nee pu u-kpátam boonee.

english_verse: A good reputation at the time of death is better than loving care at the time of birth.
translation_verse: Diyimmɔntiil sɔ́ǹ talaalumɔnti, ní unil kúm dal sɔ́ǹ ŋwiin ŋun bi màl̄-uee.

english_verse: It's better to go to a funeral than to attend a feast; funerals remind us that we all must die.
translation_verse: Á kɔ́ dikpɔcindin sɔ́ǹ á kɔ́ dicindi din poon binib bí ki jīǹ jiŋaalee. Di sá yii unil sá kamaa kúntilaŋki di sá ŋkúm, ní an ŋān̄ yii unifoo kamaa ń nīn téetí an pu.

english_verse: Choose sorrow over laughter because a sad face may hide a happy heart.
translation_verse: Kunimbaau sɔ́ǹ tilaal, di sá yii binib ŋūǹ kí nīn wāĺ yii a bí kunimbaaun, ama ní a-pɔbil bí mmɔnni.

english_verse: A sensible person mourns, but fools always laugh.
translation_verse: Dikpɔcindin ní a kāntí uciŋfiti, ama ugbaan úǹ néeń dijiŋaacindin ní.

english_verse: Correction from someone wise is better by far than praise from fools.
translation_verse: Á kíí uciŋfiti ń wòoǹ-si sɔ́ǹ á nīn bí ki pílifí ugbaan gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí-si.

english_verse: Corruption makes fools of sensible people, and bribes can ruin you.
translation_verse: Uciŋfiti un cáá mpɔn ki wɔ́b̀ binibee ŋūǹ kí kpántí ugbaan, ní dinyɔɔŋeebil jim ŋūǹ kí yàntī u-pɔbil ń gáatí.

english_verse: Something completed is better than something just begun; patience is better than too much pride.
translation_verse: Tiwan kúntitam sɔ́ǹ ti-kíltam. An sɔ́ á nīn cáá kimɔtii ki jítiǹ á nīn cáá dibayoondi.

english_verse: Only fools get angry quickly and hold a grudge.
translation_verse: Taa nín̄ gífí diŋuul malaa malaa, di sá yii ugbaan di kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ diŋuul digiil.

english_verse: It isn't wise to ask, “Why is everything worse than it used to be?”
translation_verse: Taa lì yii: «Ba ŋá ní dooooyee nìn ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ kɔŋkɔnnee?» Un bàlifī mimmee kaa sá uciŋfiti.

english_verse: Having wisdom is better than an inheritance.
translation_verse: Iciin cáá kudapɔɔu kii difakalee ní, i kèetī báà ŋma ní.

english_verse: Wisdom will protect you just like money; knowledge with good sense will lead you to life.
translation_verse: Iciin wúǹ unil pu kii animbilee ní. Bin cáá-iee kàal̀ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí ní. An pu ní an páb́ yii unil ń béé-i.

english_verse: Think of what God has done! If God makes something crooked, can you make it straight?
translation_verse: Kpèè ditundi din Unimbɔti túńee kɔkɔ. Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí tàntī tiwan tin u nyīī ki pɔ́ĺee?

english_verse: When times are good, you should be cheerful; when times are bad, think about what it means. God makes them both to keep us from knowing what will happen next. Some of Life's Questions
translation_verse: Tikɔkɔ yaa còom̄ nì si tiŋanee, nín̄ bí dipɔɔpindin. An yaa kaa ti ŋān̄ee, á dàkafì. Unimbɔti di yàntī nnaam nì nnaabu dòoń, mimmee taa làá béé tin làá dāan̄ee.

english_verse: I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper.
translation_verse: M-maŋfal din kaa bí tiban nee poonee, m ká tikɔkɔ. M dáań ki ká yii deedeedaan kúù u-deedeeu pu, ní ukpitiŋal bí dimaŋfalin u-kpitii pu.

english_verse: So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart!
translation_verse: Taa nín̄ dàkafī yii a sá deedeedaan tikpil, kí taa nín̄ yíì a-ba uciŋfiti. Ba pu ní a là kí bīil̀ a-ba?

english_verse: Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool.
translation_verse: Taa dū a-ba kí líiǹ ikpiti diŋál, kí taa nín̄ sá ugbaan. Ba pu ní a là kí kpú kaa bàn̄ a-wiiŋŋu?

english_verse: Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
translation_verse: An ŋān̄ á nīn ŋúb́ isaŋki gbanti liitil, di sá yii unil un fàŋkí Unimbɔtee di ŋūǹ kí ŋá tibɔti gbanti liitil.

english_verse: Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
translation_verse: Iciin yàntī uciŋfiti cáá mpɔn ki jítiǹ gɔminab saalaa bin kpáfì ki kpòotī kitimbaantiiyee.

english_verse: Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you.
translation_verse: Taa nín̄ pílifí tin kɔkɔ binib sòoǹee. Mimmee aa dāa gbìl̀ a-tɔntɔnliu sòoǹ ki bíiĺ-si.

english_verse: I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me.
translation_verse: Tin bí nee kɔkɔee, m dū iciin ki mākaǹ ki kpēē. M lī yii: «M làá nīn cáá iciin», ama ní i dáá gbíntìi dátiǹ-mi.

english_verse: The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep.
translation_verse: Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tin nyáń ki bée taapu? An dátiǹ-ti ní ki nyóò lúkú luku.

english_verse: So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
translation_verse: Niinee m dū m-ba ki tīī kí nyàab̀ kí béé kun di sá iciinee. M nyàab̄ kí gbìl̄ kun pu ní tiwan dòoń ki jītée. M bífì ki béè mun yii ntoom nì digbaandi kɔkɔ sá kuwaatiiu ní.

english_verse: Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for.
translation_verse: M dáań ki ká tin bí nee: unimpu un sàtī bininjabee cāabìń ntuntun kii ŋkúmee ní. U-neendi sá kii kutaliŋŋuee ní, ní u-ŋalii sá kii ikusakee. Unil un bɔti fáatiǹ Unimbɔtee ŋmátí kí nyā u-ŋaan, ama un yaa sá unikpitee, asee ú ŋmā udaan.

english_verse: With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together,
translation_verse: Uciŋfiti lī yii: M cɔ́ŋkì ki kpēē tiwan kɔkɔ kubɔ kubɔ kí béé ti-taapu.

english_verse: but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman.
translation_verse: M nyàab̄ ki tin gīī kaa ŋúń ki béè. Bininjab kutuku poonee, m ká yii ubɔbɔ di pée sá uŋman. Ama binimpoobi kɔkɔ poonee, maa ká báà ubɔ.

english_verse: I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_verse: Tin man dáań ki kée di sá yii Unimbɔti náań unil u bí deedee, ama ní unil nyàab̄ agìń tikpil ki tɔ́ u-ba pu.

english_verse: Who is smart enough to explain everything? Wisdom makes you cheerful and gives you a smile. Obey the King
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa sá uciŋfiti, ubɔ kaa nyí kí lēē tin dòońee taapu kí lì. Ama unil ciiŋyi yàntī u-nimbiin ń bútí ní u-nimbiin nín bàà kūń puee ń cúú kpántí. Un tɔ́ ubɔtee sá uciŋfiti

english_verse: If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise.
translation_verse: Ubɔti yaa lī puee, á ŋá míǹ kii ti nín pūtì ki pōoǹ Unimbɔti nimbiin puee.

english_verse: Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind.
translation_verse: Á taa kàkatī a-ba kí wàatī-u malaa. Taa nín̄ nìkì ki ŋáań tin kaa fáatiǹ-uee, di sá yii u ŋáań u nín là puee ní.

english_verse: The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?”
translation_verse: Ubɔti nyɔɔbundi cáá mpɔn, ní ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí bàlifì-u yii: «Ba ní a ŋáań nee?».

english_verse: If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it.
translation_verse: Un yaa tɔ́ ubɔtee kpá kí kɔ́ tibɔtin. Ama uciŋfiti úǹ nyí tiŋan yii ibɔsoon yuntiŋu bí ki dòoń.

english_verse: Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything,
translation_verse: Tiŋman, ŋwindal bí, Unimbɔti làá dāá sòoǹ unil bɔti kí nóó nì atuun ŋin u túńee, ama nnaabukpaan dɔ̄ ki cí unil.

english_verse: though no one can tell the future.
translation_verse: Unil kaa nyí tin bí ki dòońee, kaa nyí ŋyunti ŋun tì làá dāan̄ee.

english_verse: We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil.
translation_verse: Unil kaa yì u-maŋfal kí cúú-dì kí taa kpú. Ubɔ kaa tí cáá mpɔn kí sútí u-kúm wiiŋŋu. Kujaau yaa nyáńee, kuaa gàntī ubɔ, ní inikpiti kaa fìil̄ ukpitiŋal. Nisaal falaau

english_verse: I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another? Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
translation_verse: M ká tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ: m kpēē tin kɔkɔ pée bí ki jītí kitiŋ pu dooyee tiŋan. An sá laakin ní binib tɔ́kɔ́ bi-jutiibi pu ki ŋáań-bi tikpitilee.

english_verse: I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense.
translation_verse: M ká binikpitib kpíì bi bíi ŋáań bi-kpool. Binib gbanti nìn cáà kunimbɔtidiin múlmul. Bi nìn súntì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ bi ŋée. Tíǹ mun pée tí sá kii bi nín jì kubuŋu puee ní.

english_verse: When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime.
translation_verse: Unil yaa ŋá ikpitee, waa fòol̄ ditafadaaldi dicilpu niin. An pu ní binib néeń ki tūǹ atuŋkpiti tikpil.

english_verse: They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying: Everyone who lives right and respects God will prosper,
translation_verse: Unikpiti ŋūǹ kí ŋá ikpiti ŋfunyɔm dilaataal pu, ama ní kí kàl̄ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí. Ama m gíti nyí mun yii bin fàŋkí Unimbɔtee bí mmɔnni, kun puee bi cáá Unimbɔti faaŋku.

english_verse: but no one who sins and rejects God will prosper or live very long.
translation_verse: Unikpiti kaa làá nīn bí nnaamin. U làá jītí malaa kii mboonee, u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kaa làá nīn náaǹ, kun puee waa cáá Unimbɔti faaŋku.

english_verse: There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens.
translation_verse: Tiba gíti bí kitiŋ pu doo kaa cáá taapu. Binib bí ki sá deedeedambi, ki fòol̄ binikpitib paati. Ní binikpitib bí ki fòol̄ deedeedambi nín máaǹ tipaal tiŋyee. M lī ki gíti bíi bùsī ki lì yii tíǹ sá kii bi nín jì kubuŋu puee ní.

english_verse: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
translation_verse: An puee m tìì kunyannyaau kí jī mmɔn. Di sá yii kun pée ŋūǹ kí nīn sá nnaam ki tīī unil kitiŋ nee puee di sá ú jī, kí nyɔ̀ kí gbìl̄ mmɔn. Tíǹ di ŋūǹ kí céeǹ unil u-tundi poon iwiin in Unimbɔti tīī-u ú dūú kàl̄ kitiŋ pu dooyee.

english_verse: Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world.
translation_verse: M lēē m-pɔbil poon yii m làá nyàab̀ kí béé iciin, ní kí kpèè atuun ŋin kɔkɔ binib tūǹ kitiŋ pu doo kaa gèeǹ ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeuee soooo.

english_verse: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m ká Unimbɔti tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ. Unil kaa ŋūǹ kí nyàab̀ kí ká atuun ŋin bi tūǹ kitiŋ pu dooyee kɔkɔ. Min kamaa unil gì ki nyàab̀ee, u pée kpá kí ká. Baa gba uciŋfiti yaa bí yii u nyí, waa làá ŋmā kí ká.

english_verse: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
translation_verse: M dākafì tin bí nee kɔkɔ pu ní tin m kée sèé: deedeedambi nì biciŋfitiibi nì bi-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ kā Unimbɔti ŋaan ní. Binib kaa kpáàa nyí bi yaa làá ká dineendi àá kináŋ. Baa nyí kun dɔ̄ ki cí-bee.

english_verse: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
translation_verse: Tibɔbaantiilee di dɔ̄ ki cí báà ŋma. Tin làá bàń deedeedaanee, tíǹ di làá bàń ukpitiŋal. Tin làá bàń unimɔntee, tíǹ di làá bàń unikpiti. Tin làá bàń circirdaanee, tíǹ di làá bàń un kaa bí circiree. Tin làá bàń un ŋáań saraabee, tíǹ di làá bàń un kaa ŋáańee. Digàntil diba kaa bí unimɔnti nì unikpiti kansikin, un pòontí Unimbɔti ipoonee nì un fàŋkí kí pòon̄ee.

english_verse: It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die.
translation_verse: Tibɔbaantiil di bàń báà ŋma, ní tin an cāabìńee kaa ŋān̄ kitiŋ pu doo. An di yì-tì ní ikpiti gbí binib pɔbiliŋin ní bi tūǹ agbaantuun, ní boonee bí kpú.

english_verse: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
translation_verse: Ama unil un bí dimaŋfalinee ŋūǹ kí nīn cáá dimákal, kun puee kibɔkɔ kin bí dimaŋfalinee sɔ́ǹ gbikinti un kpíìyee.

english_verse: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
translation_verse: Binifoobi di nyí yii bi bí ki làá kpú ŋwindal, ama bitaŋkpiibi bíǹ kaa ti nyí báà tiba pu. Baa ti cí kí fōō tipaal tiba, kun puee bi súntì bi-pu.

english_verse: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
translation_verse: Tin bi nìn néeńee nì tin bi nìn née nì bi-poompooŋyi kɔkɔ wáŋkì. Baa ti pée bí kí kūtì tin bí ki jītí kitiŋ pu dooyee poon.

english_verse: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
translation_verse: An puee jī a-jinti nì mmɔn, kí nyɔ̀ a-daam nì dipɔɔpindi, di sá yii a-tuuŋŋi fáatiǹ Unimbɔti dooooyee.

english_verse: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
translation_verse: Á nīn pée pèentí ajiŋaabɔkuti, kí taa súntí kí yàaǹ a-yil pu talaalu.

english_verse: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
translation_verse: Sii nì unimpu un a néeńee ń jī mmɔn a-maŋfal wiiŋyi in kaa náaǹ Unimbɔti tīī-si á dūú kàl̄ kitiŋ nee puee. Tiŋman, a-maŋfal wiiŋyi kaa náaǹ ní ditundi din a túń kitiŋ nee puee paati dee.

english_verse: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
translation_verse: Ditundi din kamaa a pée ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ee, tɔ̄-dì nì a-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ. Di sá yii ditaŋkpiilin laakin a cée, aa ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ dibaaa, kaa ŋūǹ kí dàkafàaa, dinyil kpáaa, iciin mun kpá. Kaa sá tikɔkɔ poon ní iciin tūǹ ditundi

english_verse: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
translation_verse: M gíti dáań ki ká kitiŋ pu doo nee tiba. An kaa sá ŋyunti kamaa ní bin yáb̀ee sáń kí jī ditaatandi kpaŋkpakantikuu. Bibaatandambi kaa tí jáà ki jīǹ ŋyunti kamaa. Biciŋfitiibi kaa tí kāntí ki jīǹ sɔkɔmii. Binyiliibi kaa tí sá bin cáá tigaajati ki jítiǹ bin kíǹee. Bin yiliŋ poon tūǹ ditundi tikpilee kaa tí sá bin ní bi tìì jilmee. Di sá yii bi-kɔkɔ kāntí nnaam nì nnaabu.

english_verse: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
translation_verse: Tiŋman, unil kaa nyí tin làá bàń-uee. Kii kulaaŋŋu nín sàtī ijɔm pu, àá kii bi nín pīil̀ kí sàl̄ unoon puee, míǹ ní unil kā ní nnaabu ń dāá túuǹ-u.

english_verse: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
translation_verse: M gíti dáań ki ká tiba kitiŋ nee pu ní an yāntì m gíti dākafì iciin pu.

english_verse: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
translation_verse: Kitimbilii kiba di bí ní ki-nib kaa náaǹ báà fiii. Ní ubɔtikpaan ubɔ dɔ́miń kí já nì kì. U nìn píĺ píĺ kujaau talinti ki māntìi tú-kì.

english_verse: But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten.
translation_verse: Unandaan ubɔ nìn kóò kitimbiliiyee poon ki sá uciŋfiti. U bàà nìn ŋūǹ kí dū u-ciiŋyi kí fīī kitimbiliiyee, ama ní báà ubɔ kaa nìn téetì u-pu.

english_verse: So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
translation_verse: An pu ní man lī yii iciin sɔ́ǹ mpɔn, ama uciŋfiti yaa sá unandaanee, binib ŋèeǹ nì u ní, kaa pílifí tin u sòoǹee.

english_verse: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
translation_verse: Bi pílifí uciŋfiti un sòoǹ sooooyee nyɔɔbuŋŋi ki jítiǹ ubɔti un tìì bigbaambi marab ki tátée.

english_verse: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
translation_verse: Iciin sɔ́ǹ tijanjawan, ama ní ukpitiŋal ubaanti bíiĺ tiwammɔntiil tikpil.

english_verse: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
translation_verse: Isii yaa jéetì talaalu kpam poonee, i yàntī mí nūukì ní kí bīil̀. Míǹ ní digbaandi fiii bíiĺ iciin nì tinyool.

english_verse: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
translation_verse: Uciŋfiti dàkafī tiŋan ní, ama ugbaan úǹ kaa gbìl̀ tibɔti taapu.

english_verse: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
translation_verse: Ugbaan yaa bíi còom̄ didandi puee, kii nlandɔkɔmɔnti nín kaa bí u-yilin puee, un kamaa yaa ká-uee béetí yii u sá ugbaan ní.

english_verse: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
translation_verse: A-kpiliu yaa gíí a-pu diŋuulee, taa dū a-tundi kí fá. A yaa cúú a-ba, an yàntī á taa kɔ́ diyintikpaandi poon.

english_verse: Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair:
translation_verse: Ubɔti mun ŋūǹ kí yìntī. Míǹ ní m dáań ki ká dimuuldi kitiŋ nee pu.

english_verse: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
translation_verse: M ká iyumbu kā itaamu pu ama ní binikpaambi còom̄ ataa pu fám kii iyumbuee.

english_verse: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
translation_verse: Unil yaa bíi gbì mbòóyee, u ŋūǹ kí dāá jēetí ŋu-poon, ukoobu ŋūǹ kí jú un bíi wìil̄ digundee.

english_verse: You could even get hurt by chiseling a stone or chopping a log.
translation_verse: Unil yaa bíi kpìkitī ataŋkpeeyee, ŋi ŋūǹ kí tīī-u tiweendi, míǹ ní un bíi látí idɔee, an ŋūǹ ki cáań-u in bí iwa.

english_verse: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
translation_verse: Kicɔkɔ yaa gbītì ní baa lōoǹ-kì, ní a cáa bíi tūǹ ditundee, asee á mɔ̀tīí dàkà dikpabil ní kí ŋmā kí dūú gāā tiba. Di sá yii iciin di yàntī tin unil bíi ŋáańee ń nyā nnyim.

english_verse: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
translation_verse: Un cáá nnyɔkɔ ki cútí ikoobuee yaa yāntì ukoobu péé-u dijulee, u páatì u-nyɔkɔŋuee pu ba? Taa nín̄ sòoǹ tikpil

english_verse: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
translation_verse: Uciŋfiti yaa sòoǹee, an mɔ̄ dipilifil ní. Ama ugbaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi yàntī u wáŋkí ní.

english_verse: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
translation_verse: U kífí kí sòoǹ tigbaambɔti ní kí dāá kúntíǹ tinifambɔti tin kaa cáá taapuee.

english_verse: They never tire of talking, but none of us really know what the future will bring.
translation_verse: Ugbaan di sòoǹ ki sòoǹ kaa ŋmīlifí. Ama unil úǹ kaa nyí tin bí ki dòońee. Ŋma ŋūǹ kí tùkù u-juti tin bí ki dòoń udaan kpátam boonee?

english_verse: Fools wear themselves out— they don't know enough to find their way home.
translation_verse: Ugbaan di gì digìńdi fám. Waa kpáàa nyí gba u nín làá túĺ pu kí cù kitiŋinee.

english_verse: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí kitiŋ kin bɔtiu sá campɔnti ní ki-kàliŋkpilib nyēē ki jīǹ jiŋaalib baabadalee!

english_verse: But a nation will prosper when its ruler is mature, and its leaders don't party too much.
translation_verse: Án nīn mɔ̄ǹ kitiŋ kin bɔtiu nyánní dibeecindin àá akpambal dicaŋkunee, ki-kàliŋkpilib jīǹ bi-jinti ŋyunti ŋun ní an máaǹ bí jēe ní. Bi jīǹ kí ká mpɔn ní, kaa sá kí nyɔ̀ kí gbí.

english_verse: Some people are too lazy to fix a leaky roof— then the house collapses.
translation_verse: Uwutijoodaan diiku bɔ̀b̀ ní. Unil un kpàl̄ iŋal kaa tūǹ dibee, utaa nì u-diikun ní.

english_verse: Eating and drinking make you feel happy, and money can buy everything you need.
translation_verse: Bigaajab jīǹ jiŋaal kí kɔ̀ntī bi-nimbiliŋ ní. Ndaam tìì-bi mmɔn, ní animbil yàntī bí ká tin kɔkɔ bí lèe.

english_verse: Don't let yourself think about cursing the king; don't curse the rich, not even in secret. A little bird might hear and tell everything.
translation_verse: Á taa tɔ̄ ubɔti mbusu, báà a-pɔbilin. Á taa kpákáǹ binikpaambi, báà a-didooŋkaakun. Unoon ŋūǹ kí yòon̄ tin a sòon̄ee, kí dū tin a lēe kí māafì.

english_verse: Be generous, and someday you will be rewarded.
translation_verse: Dū a-kpɔnɔu kí tɔ̄ nnyimin, di sá yii a làá dāá fàtīí ká-u iwiin iba boon.

english_verse: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
translation_verse: Dū a-gaajati kí yóoń binib biluli kii binii cee, di sá yii aa nyí mbusu un di ŋūǹ kí dāá bàń kitiŋ puee.

english_verse: If you worry about the weather and don't plant seeds, you won't harvest a crop.
translation_verse: Ukpaal un fàŋkí kubuŋuee kaa kù kí bɔ̄l̀. Un fàŋkí utaayee kaa dāa kāntí kí cā.

english_verse: No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
translation_verse: Aa ŋūǹ kí béé an nín ŋáań pu ní kibiki ń náań ki-na poonee, kaa tí nyí laakin kufoou nyēeńee. Míǹ mbaantiim ní aa làá ŋmā kí gbìl̄ Unimbɔti nín tūǹ u-tundi puee taapu, úǹ un náań tikɔkɔee.

english_verse: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
translation_verse: An puee á kíĺ kutaafaau kí kpɔ̀ kí bɔ̄l̀ a-wamboolii kí tɔ̄ ditundi kí jóotí-ku. Di sá yii aa nyí a-tuuŋŋi kansikin din làá bútí-see. An yaa yíì a ŋūǹ kí páatí a-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
translation_verse: Ŋwalifi mɔ̄ dikpeel, ní an ŋān̄ unil ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin.

english_verse: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
translation_verse: Unil yaa kāl̀ kitiŋ pu ki yúntèe, u máaǹ kí jī abin gbanti kɔkɔ pu. Tí téetí tin bí nee pu: dinimbinaamandi wiiŋyi di làá nīn wīikí, ní tin kɔkɔ dòońee sá kii kubuŋuee. Tí jīmaan nnaam án taa nà-ti

english_verse: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
translation_verse: Unaacimpɔɔn, jī a-naacimpɔnti kí nīn bí mmɔnni ŋyunti gbanti poon. Pée ŋá tin a lèe nì tin fáatiǹ-see. Ama á nīn nyí ŋwindal Unimbɔti làá dāá sòoǹ a-bɔti ki nóó nì tin kɔkɔ a ŋée.

english_verse: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_verse: Gɔ́ntí tin kamaa ŋūǹ kí yàntī á kɔ́ kunimbaaunee, kí kàkatī tin kɔkɔ pée ŋūǹ kí cáań-si igbaŋweenee. Di sá yii tinaacimpɔn nì tiyikpibɔn yuntiŋu jītí malaa ní.

english_verse: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
translation_verse: Taa súntí a-náanliu pu ŋyunti ŋun ní a dáá pɔ̀ɔǹee. Téetí u-pu kí wàatī ní iwiŋkpiti ń bàń, ŋyunti ŋun ní a làá dāá lì yii: «An kaa ti mɔ̄ǹ-mi ḿ nín bí dimaŋfalin.»

english_verse: Someday the light of the sun and the moon and the stars will all seem dim to you. Rain clouds will remain over your head.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ŋwìiń nì ŋwalifi làá dāá dūú kpántí dibɔmbɔndi, ní uŋmal nì iŋmalbijaa kaa dāa gíti wāĺ, ní utaa tin lì yii u nì ki báatée atagban fātìi lúntì.

english_verse: The noisy grinding of grain and the voices of singers will be shut out by your deaf ears, but even the song of a bird will keep you awake.
translation_verse: Niinee kudii kun punyɔkɔki túĺ didandi púee dūu pīiǹ, ní baa ti gbìl̀ tinàti pu. Kinɔmbiki gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi sūǹ, ní baa ti gbìl̀ ilan pu.

english_verse: You will be afraid to climb up a hill or walk down a road. Your hair will turn as white as almond blossoms. You will feel lifeless and drag along like an old grasshopper. We each go to our eternal home, and the streets here are filled with those who mourn.
translation_verse: Binib kíǹ ki fàŋkí kí dàb̄ kigbantaŋ pu, ní dinyoondi bí nsan pu. Tiyikpiti píil̀ kii nsupumpukumee, ní tiwun dūu nyīŋfì kii unaakitoon di nyáń ki lítèe, ní unil maŋfal ń lítí kii disubil di kītì ki lítèe. Tiŋman ŋwiin bí ki dòoń báà ŋma làá kɔ́ dikaakulin laakin sá u-kɔŋkooŋŋu njoolkaayee. Ŋyunti gbantee, binib lālim̀ ki gbí didandi pu kí sɔ̄ u-kpool.

english_verse: The silver cord snaps, the golden bowl breaks; the water pitcher is smashed, and the pulley at the well is shattered.
translation_verse: Niinee ní animbil kúti ŋmibiki ń cúú tìl̄, ní sindaariya sambil ń cúú yàaǹ, ní dibool din poon nnyim gbée ń lítí kí wīī, ní guuka ŋmiiŋu ń kútí ní ú jēetí lɔkɔn.

english_verse: So our bodies return to the earth, and the life-giving breath returns to God.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ntam ń fàtīí gítí kitiŋin laakin mì nyánnée, ní kufoou ń fàtīí gítí Unimbɔti un tīī-kuee cee.

english_verse: Nothing makes sense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense. Respect and Obey God
translation_verse: Uciŋfiti di lī yii: <Kubuŋu fám, kubuŋu fám, tikɔkɔ pée sá kii kubuŋuee ní. Tibɔkuntikaal

english_verse: I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied.
translation_verse: Tin ti làá dūú kūtì tin bí nee puee di sá yii Uciŋfiti kaa dàkā yii u sá uciŋfiti ŋmaniŋma, ama u dàkā binib kun u nyée. U bɔ́ntì alaŋkpan tikpil, ki dākafì tiŋan ki nyàab̄ ŋi-taapu ki dɔ́ntì-ŋi.

english_verse: Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
translation_verse: Uciŋfiti pɔ́ɔǹ u-ba ki nyàab̄ anyɔɔbummɔɔn ní ki dūu ŋmàn̄ tibɔŋman.

english_verse: Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together.
translation_verse: Biciŋfitiibi nyɔɔbuŋŋi sá kii inyanyee ní, a lì kii akpakpaa ŋin bin ŋmàn̄ tigbɔnee dūu cóoǹee. Unimbɔti un sá upikpaabaantee di tìì tikɔkɔ.

english_verse: My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these. There is no end to books, and too much study will wear you out.
translation_verse: M-jipɔɔn, á taa pée kūtì tiba. Á ŋmà tigbɔnee sá ditundi din kaa kúntée ní, ní kí bīfì tikpil muee gì tiwun.

english_verse: Everything you were taught can be put into a few words: Respect and obey God! This is what life is all about.
translation_verse: Kí kúntí tin kɔkɔ bi sòon̄ neeyee, tin ti làá lèe sèé: Nín̄ fàŋkí Unimbɔti kí nīn tɔ́ u-marab. Tin unifoo kamaa máaǹ kí ŋée dee.

english_verse: God will judge everything we do, even what is done in secret, whether good or bad.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Unimbɔti làá dāá sòoǹ tin kɔkɔ ti ŋée bɔti, ki kpáaǹ atummɔnti nì atuŋkpiti ŋin ti ŋá dibalinee.

english_verse: This is Solomon's most beautiful song. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ilan kɔkɔ poonee, ŋunee di mɔ̄. Saloomɔn di ŋmàn̄-ŋu. Bibɔntiibi bili Usapɔɔn

english_verse: Kiss me tenderly! Your love is better than wine,
translation_verse: Kpàl̄-mi kí nákań a-ba, móotí-mi! A-neendi yàntī m gbéè kii m nyùn̄ ndaamee,

english_verse: and you smell so sweet. All the young women adore you; the very mention of your name is like spreading perfume. *
translation_verse: ki mɔ̄ ki jítiǹ a-talaalub sɔnsɔfiŋu. A bí kii talaalumɔntee ní. An pu ní bisapɔmbi kɔkɔ là-si!

english_verse: Hurry, my king! Let's hurry. Take me to your home. The Young Women Speak: We are happy for you! And we praise your love even more than wine. She Speaks: Young women of Jerusalem, it is only right that you should adore him.
translation_verse: Kpáaǹ-mi kí cùnnì, tí sāǹ dicilpu! M-bɔtiu, cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ a-diikun. Niinee, sii puee, ti làá nīn bí mmɔŋkpaanni. Ti làá nyɔ̄ŋkì a-neendi din nyàatī kii ndaamee. Bisapɔmbi lafun cáá mbaamɔn kí nīn néeń-si!

english_verse: My skin is dark and beautiful, like a tent in the desert or like Solomon's curtains.
translation_verse: M sá unibɔn, ama m cáá kunyaaŋŋu. M-wunti bɔ̀ǹ jíbjib kii Keedaar yab tantibee, ki ŋān̄ kii iŋaamɔnti in sàkā kubɔtinaakoou punyɔkɔpuee. Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi,

english_verse: Don't stare at me just because the sun has darkened my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they made me work in the vineyard, and so I neglected my complexion.
translation_verse: ní taa kpèè m-wunti nín bɔ̄ntì puee, an sá ŋwìiń di gbáń-mi. M-niijab di fōō m-pu diŋuul, ní ki ŋá-mi mpɔn ḿ cīití bi-fiinyib. Ama man m-ba fiinyibee, maa cíitì!

english_verse: My darling, I love you! Where do you feed your sheep and let them rest at noon? Don't let the other shepherds think badly of me. I'm not one of those women who shamelessly follow after shepherds. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Sii un m néeńee, tùkù-mi la ní a kpàá a-picaŋkpuŋku ní? Tùkù-mi ŋwìiń yaa píĺee laakin a cáǹ-i i dɔ̀ ki ŋùŋfēe? Mimmee maa làá nīn gíti tú ki yìiǹ a-bɔɔbi picaŋkpunti cee. Bipikpaaliibi

english_verse: My dearest, if you don't know, just follow the path of the sheep. Then feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
translation_verse: Unimpunyannyaan, a yaa kaa nyée, nín̄ nóó ipii taaŋi, kí kpàà a-ŋɔbiliŋ bipikpaaliibi bimmu caŋin. Unaacimpɔɔn

english_verse: You move as gracefully as the pony that leads the chariot of the king.
translation_verse: M-bɔɔn, m dū-si ki ŋmāntiǹ utannyaan un dátí Faaroo tɔrɔkuee ní.

english_verse: Earrings add to your beauty, and you wear a necklace of precious stones.
translation_verse: Falfatib bin a túuńee tìì a-taŋkpunti kunyaaŋŋu. A-leeŋkaati máaǹ a-neen. Bipikpaaliibi

english_verse: Let's make you some jewelry of gold, woven with silver. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ti làá dū sindaariya ní kí mɔ́ɔ́-si falfatib, ní kí dū animbil kúti kí nyùntī. Usapɔɔn

english_verse: My king, while you were on your couch, my aroma was a magic charm.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun m-bɔtiu kā ki jīǹee, ní m-talaaluu sɔnsɔfiŋu ń gbìtī.

english_verse: you are flower blossoms from the gardens of En-Gedi. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Un m néeńee bí kii nsupumpukum min sɔ́fì ki bí Eeni-Geedii fiinyi sufii kansikinee ní. Unaacimpɔɔn

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— your eyes are those of a dove. She Speaks:
translation_verse: M-bɔɔn, a ŋān̄, a baasii ŋān̄ ní! A-nimbiliŋ bí kùlkul kii dibeenanjilee! Usapɔɔn

english_verse: My love, you are handsome, truly handsome— the fresh green grass will be our wedding bed
translation_verse: Sii un m néeńee, a ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu. Man nì sii dooŋu sɔ̀m̀ kii kumɔsɔŋuee ní.

english_verse: I am merely a rose from the land of Sharon, a lily from the valley. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Man sá Sarɔn timpiliŋki supumpukum ní, nsupumpukum min yú atantakanee. Unaacimpɔɔn

english_verse: My darling, when compared with other young women, you are a lily among thorns. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Kii nsupumpukum min ŋān̄ ki yú ikuŋkum kansikinee, míǹ ní m-bɔɔn bí bisapɔmbi kansikin. Usapɔɔn

english_verse: And you, my love, are an apple tree among trees of the forest. Your shade brought me pleasure; your fruit was sweet.
translation_verse: Kii pɔɔmi subu nín yú kubambaŋŋu sufii kansikin puee, míǹ ní m-bɔɔn bí binaacimpɔmbi kansikin. M yaa kā u-booŋŋu taapuee an mɔ̄ǹ-mi, u-biliŋ mɔ̄ m-nyɔkɔn.

english_verse: You led me to your banquet room and showered me with love.
translation_verse: U cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ jiŋaal diikun. Bi ŋmàn̄ m nín kā puee yilpu yii <Dineendi>.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: U-ŋaŋgan tíkí m-yil, ní u-ŋaŋgiil pá m-caŋ pu. Unaacimpɔɔn

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles never to awaken love before it is ready. Winter Is Past She Speaks:
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi, m dū ipeeman nì ikɔnii ki gbāam̀-ni, ní taa fìntī m-neendi kí taa páb́-dì kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun dì yaa lèe. Úǹ di dòońee Usapɔɔn

english_verse: I hear the voice of the one I love, as he comes leaping over mountains and hills
translation_verse: M gbìl̄ un m néeńee pu. Kpèè úǹ di dòońee. Úǹ di yùkufī ajoon nì ŋgbantamu yilpuee.

english_verse: like a deer or a gazelle. Now he stands outside our wall, looking through the window
translation_verse: Un m néeńee bí kii upeeman àá dikɔniipɔmbilee ní. Kpèè u bāań ki yúl̀ ti-diiku boon. U lɔ́kɔtí ki kpèé tɔkɔla watil pú, u gbōontí tɔkɔla laaŋkin ki kpèé.

english_verse: and speaking to me. He Speaks: My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: U bí-mi yii: «Yīkìm̄, m-bɔɔn unyaan kí dāan̄.

english_verse: Winter is past, the rain has stopped;
translation_verse: Kuseeu jítì, utaa yúl̀ kutaa kɔ́ ndan.

english_verse: flowers cover the earth, it's time to sing. The cooing of doves is heard in our land.
translation_verse: Ti ká ti-satin mpumpukum bíi màtī. Ilan yuntiŋu bāań. Ti gbìl̄ nnanjimamu siim pu ti-satin.

english_verse: Fig trees are bearing fruit, while blossoms on grapevines fill the air with perfume. My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
translation_verse: Fiigi subipeepeekaaŋi bíi mántí. Fiinyi pumpukum gbītì mi-sɔnsɔfiŋu. Yīkìń, m-bɔɔn unyaan kí dāan̄.

english_verse: You are my dove hiding among the rocks on the side of a cliff. Let me see how lovely you are! Let me hear the sound of your melodious voice.
translation_verse: Man beenanjil din páaǹ di-diiku ntaŋkpalɔkɔnee, ki bál̀ ntaŋkpafaŋfakaminee, yàntī ḿ wāl̀ a-nimbiin, yàntī ḿ gbìl̄ a-neen pu di sá yii a-neen sɔ̀m̀ ki mɔ̄, ní a-nimbiin ŋān̄.» Ubinaati

english_verse: Our vineyards are in blossom; we must catch the little foxes that destroy the vineyards. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Ní cúúmaan-ti iŋɔkɔ nee, ŋŋɔkɔbiyaamu mun bí ki ŋmóò ki bíiĺ fiinyibee. Di sá yii ti-fiinyib bàà púkuḿ dee! Usapɔɔn

english_verse: My darling, I am yours, and you are mine, as you feed your sheep among the lilies.
translation_verse: Un m néeńee bí ki tīī-mi, ní ma mun bí ki tīī-u. U kpàá u-picaŋkpuŋku mpumpukum kansikin ní.

english_verse: Pretend to be a young deer dancing on mountain slopes until daylight comes and shadows fade away.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī kutaa ń ŋàatī, ní ibóon ń wāŋkèe, fàtīí gítiń, sii un man néeńee. Sāǹní kii upeemanee, kii ukɔnii biki di sánní ajoon ŋin yākatèe pu puee.

english_verse: While in bed at night, I reached for the one I love with heart and soul. I looked for him, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu m-dooŋu puee m nyàab̀ un m néeńee, m nyàab̄-u, ama kaa ká-u.

english_verse: So I searched through the town for the one I love. I looked on every street, but he wasn't there.
translation_verse: M làá yīkì kí yìiǹ kitiŋin nì adan pu nì sampaambi pu. M nyàab̀ un m néeńee. M nyàab̄-u, ama kaa ká-u.

english_verse: I even asked the guards patrolling the town, “Have you seen the one I love so much?”
translation_verse: M tūŋkí bijanjaliibi bin màntī ki kpèé kitiŋee ki bàlifī-bi yii: «Ni ká un m néeńeeee?»

english_verse: Right after that, I found him. I held him and would not let go until I had taken him to the home of my mother.
translation_verse: M pūtì pée jítì bi-pu kpalaayee ní ki dūu tú un m néeńee. M cúú u-ŋal kaa ti líì-ŋu, see m nín cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ m-na diikun laakin u cáá m-poolee.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles, never to awaken love before it is ready. The Groom and the Wedding Party Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: «Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi, m dū ipeeman nì ikɔnii ki gbāam̀-ni. Ní taa fìntī m-neendi kí taa páb́-dì kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun dì yaa láa lèe.» Usapɔɔn

english_verse: What do we see approaching from the desert like a cloud of smoke? With it comes the sweet smell of spices, including myrrh and frankincense.
translation_verse: Ŋma di nyánní kuteeun ki dòoń kii ŋŋmi tagbanlooŋŋuee? U sɔ́fìń miiri talaaluu nì bitalaalutuukaabi nì talaalub bin kɔkɔ nyánní laaba nì bi-bulifee.

english_verse: It is King Solomon carried on a throne, surrounded by sixty of Israel's best soldiers.
translation_verse: An sá ubɔti Saloomɔn di pá u-lambaŋki pu. Bijanjaliibi bin cáá dipɔbilee imuŋku ita māntìi tú-u. Isirayeel baatandambi dee.

english_verse: Each of them wears a sword. They are experts at fighting, even in the dark.
translation_verse: Bi-kɔkɔ ŋúb́ kitàataajiki ki bɔ́ntì dikɔ̀ndi. Báà ŋma gbìn̄ u-gbajau, kí mɔ̄tì u-ba pu kunyeeu jaaku pu.

english_verse: The throne is made of trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn yāntì bi dū Leebanɔn dɔi ki kpáá-u dijakpatikaal.

english_verse: Its posts are silver, the back is gold, and the seat is covered with purple cloth. You women of Jerusalem have taken great care to furnish the inside.
translation_verse: Idɔ in tɔ́kɔ́ di-puee sá animbil kúti ní laakin u dìntēe sá sindaariya, ní ki dū bisatamambi binyannyaambi ki ŋáĺ ki tākaǹ dijalee poon. Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi dū nì dineendi ní ki lùn̄ iŋaabu ki nyáantì di-poon.

english_verse: Now come and see the crown given to Solomon by his mother on his happy wedding day.
translation_verse: «Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi, nyānnímaan kí dāá kpèè ubɔti Saloomɔn. U cíkí kibeefuulii kin u-na nìn tīī-u u-nimpucaal dalee! Ŋwiin gbantee, u nìn bí dipɔɔpindin ní.»

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— as you look through your veil, your eyes are those of a dove. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: A ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu, m-bɔɔn, a ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu! A yaa dū a-ŋaabiiŋkaaŋu ki bīiǹee, a-nimbiliŋ ŋān̄ kii dibeenanjilee ní. A-yikpiti nín dɔ̄ puee bí kii kuŋɔcaŋkpuŋu di kpákatiń Galaadi jool puee.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: A-nyiŋŋi pīiǹ káŋkaŋ kii ipii in bi dáá cáń i-kuti ki fùl̄-iee. Dinyindi kamaa cáá di-ŋaliŋu ní, báà dibaba kaa fúkutì.

english_verse: Your lips are crimson cords, your mouth is shapely; behind your veil are hidden beautiful rosy cheeks.
translation_verse: A-nyunculiŋ ŋān̄ kii kiŋaamaŋee, ní a-nyɔkɔ cáá kunyaaŋŋu. A yaa dū a-ŋaabiiŋkaaŋu ki bīiǹee, a-taŋkpunti bí kii kpakpaapu un bi búkutì milee poon nín bí puee ní.

english_verse: Your neck is more graceful than the tower of David, decorated with thousands of warriors' shields.
translation_verse: A-sil bí kii Daafiidi difɔkɔku kun bi máń ku yú ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ jìbuee ní. Niin ní agbampɔɔ kutuku sàkā. Bibaatandambi kɔkɔ janjawanti dee.

english_verse: Your breasts are perfect; they are twin deer feeding among lilies.
translation_verse: A-biiŋi bí kii aŋɔbil alee, a lì kii ipeeman in bi màl̄ ŋwimbaanti, i yú nsupumpukum kansikin ki jīǹee.

english_verse: I will hasten to those hills sprinkled with sweet perfume and stay there till sunrise.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī kutaa ń ŋàatī, ní mboon ń lítí kitiŋ puee, m làá cù miiri jool pu, ní kí cù talaalu tūukaa gbantaŋki pu.

english_verse: My darling, you are lovely in every way.
translation_verse: M-bɔɔn, a baasii ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu ní, a-laaba kaa pée wɔ̀b̄.

english_verse: My bride, together we will leave Lebanon! We will say goodbye to the peaks of Mount Amana, Senir, and Hermon, where lions and leopards live in the caves.
translation_verse: M-bɔɔn, nyānní Leebanɔn jooŋŋi pu kí dāan̄ m-cee, dāan̄ m-cee. Kpákatiń Arimina nì Seeniir nì Eermɔn jooŋŋi pu. Nyā gbikintib kɔŋkooŋyin nì igbii jooŋŋi pu.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you have stolen my heart! With one glance from your eyes and the glow of your necklace, you have stolen my heart.
translation_verse: A yāntì maa ti yì m-ba m-niisal, m-bɔɔn, a yaa pée fātìi kpēē-mi yéè ní m yaa ká a-leeŋkaati dimbil diba jee, maa ti yì m-ba.

english_verse: Your love is sweeter than wine; the smell of your perfume is more fragrant than spices.
translation_verse: A-neendi tìì-mi mmɔn, m-niisal, m-bɔɔn! Dì mɔ̄ m-cee ki jítiǹ ndaam pu gba! A-talaalub sɔ́fì ki jítiǹ talaalumɔntiibi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Your lips are a honeycomb; milk and honey flow from your tongue. Your dress has the aroma of cedar trees from Lebanon.
translation_verse: M-bɔɔn, m yaa móotí a-nyunculiŋee, an mɔ̄ kii tisiilee ní. Tisiil nì nnaabiim bál̀ ki kā a-limbil pu. A-wampeeŋkaati sɔ́fì kii Leebanɔn bambaŋku sɔnsɔfiŋuee ní.

english_verse: My bride, my very own, you are a garden, a fountain closed off to all others.
translation_verse: M-niisal, m-bɔɔn, a sá bukpaa bun man baba yèe ní, man baba nyimbulnimbil, nnyimbul ŋun m pīiǹ ki kpàl̄ kpálkpalee.

english_verse: Your arms are vines, covered with delicious fruits and all sorts of spices— henna, nard,
translation_verse: A sɔ̀m̀ fílfil kii yilpu beel sufii in biliŋ mɔ̄ cɔ́ncɔŋee. Niin ní isufi in sɔ́fèe nyēē. Íǹ di sá eenee nì naar,

english_verse: You are a spring in the garden, a fountain of pure water, and a refreshing stream from Mount Lebanon. She Speaks:
translation_verse: A sá nnyimbul ŋun dɔ̄ bukpaa kansikinee ní, dinyimbunimbil din nyim wāĺ kílkil ki pùubìń Leebanɔn jooŋŋi puee. Usapɔɔn

english_verse: Let the north wind blow, the south wind too! Let them spread the aroma of my garden, so the one I love may enter and taste its delicious fruits.
translation_verse: Fìntim̄, ŋgan pú buŋku! Dāan̄ malaa ŋgiil pú buŋku! Dāá jītí m-kpaabu pu bú gbìtī bu-sɔnsɔfiŋu! Sii un m néeńee, kɔ́ a-kpaabun kí ŋmɔ́ bu-subimɔntiŋ!

english_verse: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
translation_verse: M kɔ́ m-kpaabun m-niisal, m-bɔɔn. M kītì m-subu bun bi yíì miiree nì talaalu sufii iba mun. M ŋmɔ́ m-sigbandi nì m-siiti, ki nyùn̄ m-daam nì m-naabiim. Bibɔɔtiibi «M-bɔɔbi, jī kí nyɔ̀maan kí gbímaan dineendi. Waa pīitì-u kipunyɔkɔ malaa Usapɔɔn

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”

english_verse: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
translation_verse: M kɔ́ m-kpaabun m-niisal, m-bɔɔn. M kītì m-subu bun bi yíì miiree nì talaalu sufii iba mun. M ŋmɔ́ m-sigbandi nì m-siiti, ki nyùn̄ m-daam nì m-naabiim. Bibɔɔtiibi «M-bɔɔbi, jī kí nyɔ̀maan kí gbímaan dineendi. Waa pīitì-u kipunyɔkɔ malaa Usapɔɔn

english_verse: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
translation_verse: M dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ, ama m-pɔbil kaa gèeǹ. M gbìl̄ kuwoou kubɔ pu, an sá un m néeńee di bíi fátí kipunyɔkɔ. Unaacimpɔɔn Pìitī-mi, m-niisal, m-bɔɔn, m-beenanjil, unyaan. Dimalindi tɔ́ ki sɔ̄ŋkì m-yil gbàtii, ní kunyeeu sɔnsɔm sɔ̄ŋkì m-yikpiti. Usapɔɔn

english_verse: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
translation_verse: M pēetì m-bɔkutil, maa là kí gíiǹ-dì kí pèen̄! M fíntì m-taaŋi, maa là kí kɔ́ǹ-ŋi tijɔkɔndi.»

english_verse: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
translation_verse: Un m néeńee dū u-ŋal ki bɔ́ dikampiil buŋŋun ní m-pɔbil máĺ.

english_verse: When I rose to open the door, my hands and my fingers dripped with perfume.
translation_verse: M yíkì kí pìitī-u. Talaalu kpam min bi yíì miiree nìn gbí m-ŋaan ní ŋkpamee mèetī m-ŋambiyaamu pu ki tōontí dikampiil kpàlkaati pu.

english_verse: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.
translation_verse: M pīitì un m néeńee, ama ní u fātì u-boon ki tīī-mi, ki búntì. M nyáń kí nyàab̀-u. M nyàab̄-u ama kaa ká-u, ki yíiń-u ama waa kíí-mi.

english_verse: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
translation_verse: Ama m tú bijanjaliibi bin cí kitiŋ ki màntī ki kpèé-kèe kitiŋ gundi pu. Bi cúú-mi ki gbáń ki ŋá-mi tiweendi, bi cúú ŋŋaabu ŋun pá m-gbigbil puee ki fōō.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi m gbāam̀-ni: ni yaa ká un m néeńee, ni làá tùkù-u yii ba dee? Ní tùkù-u yii m būǹ dineendi weeŋŋu. Bisapɔmbi

english_verse: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
translation_verse: Sii unimpunyaan, ba pu ní a bàlifī-ti tin bí nee? Un a néeńee, ba ní u cáá ki jítiǹ bin kíǹee ní? Ba ní u baasii cáá ki jítiǹ-bi ní? Usapɔɔn

english_verse: He is handsome and healthy, the most outstanding among ten thousand.
translation_verse: Un m néeńee yaa sáká bininjab kutukub saalaa kansikin, bi béetí-u ní. Di sá yii u-wunti máǹ ní ki jìl̀.

english_verse: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
translation_verse: U-yikpiti bí kii sindaariyee ní, ní ki gɔ́liḿ gɔ́liḿ kii tikpakpatee, ní ki bɔ̀ǹ kii kunaambɔŋŋuee.

english_verse: His eyes are a pair of doves bathing in a stream flowing with milk.
translation_verse: U-nimbiliŋ jìl̀ kii dibeenanjil di bí mbun caŋinee. Di tɔ́kɔ́ kusampeeu nyɔɔgbandi ki fùul̀ nnaabiim poon.

english_verse: His face is a garden of sweet-smelling spices; his lips are lilies dripping with perfume.

english_verse: His arms are branches of gold covered with jewels; his body is ivory decorated with sapphires.

english_verse: My darling has gone down to his garden of spices, where he will feed his sheep and gather lilies.

english_verse: I am his, and he is mine, as he feeds his sheep among the lilies. He Speaks:
translation_verse: M sá ki tīī un m néeńee, ní u mun sá ki tīī-mi. Laakin mpumpukum bée, niin ní u kpàá u-waŋkuti. Un bi néeńee nín bí puee Unaacimpɔɔn

english_verse: My dearest, the cities of Tirzah and Jerusalem are not as lovely as you. Your charms are more powerful than all of the stars in the heavens.
translation_verse: M-bɔɔn, a ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu, kii Tiirsa tiŋkee. A ŋān̄ ki mɔ̄ nnimbikpee kii Jeerusaleem tiŋkee, ama a kɔ̄ntí binib tifaandi kii dijanjakitil di bí dikɔmbool puee.

english_verse: Turn away your eyes— they make me melt. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Fàtī a-nimbiin kí taa ti kpèè-mi, di sá yii a-nimbiliŋ sàtī-mi. A-yikpiti fɔ̀kɔ̀ ki bí kii kuŋɔcaŋkpuŋu di kpákatiń Galaadi jool puee.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: A-nyiŋŋi pīiǹ káŋkaŋ kii ipii in bi dáá cáń i-kuti ki fùl̄-iee ní. Dinyindi kamaa cáá di-ŋaliŋu ní, báà dibaba kaa fúkutì.

english_verse: What if I could have sixty queens, eighty wives, and thousands of others!
translation_verse: Ubɔti ŋūǹ kí nīn cáá binimpoobi imuŋku ita, bibɔntiibi imuŋku inaa, nì bisapɔmbi kupaau.

english_verse: You would be my only choice, my flawless dove, the favorite child of your mother. The young women, the queens, and all the others tell how excited you are as they sing your praises:
translation_verse: Man ceeyee, unimpubambaanti di bí. Úǹ di sá man beenanjil, unyaan. U sá u-na bibaabil ní, kibiki kin u nìn néeń tikpilkuee. Bisapɔmbi yaa wál̀-uee, bi pàkà-u ní, ní ubɔti nimpoobi nì u-bɔmbi nyɔ́ŋkí-u ki lì yii:

english_verse: “You are as majestic as the morning sky— glorious as the moon— blinding as the sun! Your charms are more powerful than all the stars above.” She Speaks:
translation_verse: «Batii nimpuu di bí kii kutaawuntuŋu walifiŋu na! U ŋān̄ kii uŋmalee, ki jìl̀ kii ŋwìińee, ki kɔ̄ntí binib tifaandi kii dijanjakitil di bí dikɔmbool puee.»

english_verse: I went down to see if blossoms were on the walnut trees, grapevines, and fruit trees.
translation_verse: M sīntì m-sufii kpaabun. M là kí kpèè asupɔmbil ŋin bí ditantakalinee. Fiinyi sufii púkuḿaaa? Greenaadi mun púkuḿaaa?

english_verse: But in my imagination I was suddenly riding on a glorious chariot. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Maa tí gbìl̀ taapu, ubɔtiisal, a yāntì maa ti nyí tin poon m bée.

english_verse: Most beautiful of women, tell us where he has gone. Let us help you find him. She Speaks:
translation_verse: Unimpunyannyaan, un a néeńee bí la ní? La ní u túĺ ní?. Ti làá tūtuǹ-si á nyàab̀-u. Usapɔɔn

english_verse: My darling has gone down to his garden of spices, where he will feed his sheep and gather lilies.
translation_verse: Un m néeńeee sīntì u-kpaabun, mpumpukum min sɔ́fèe watil. Niin ní u kāntí u-jinti, ki kìtī mpumpukum.

english_verse: I am his, and he is mine, as he feeds his sheep among the lilies. He Speaks:
translation_verse: M sá ki tīī un m néeńee, ní u mun sá ki tīī-mi. Laakin mpumpukum bée, niin ní u kpàá u-waŋkuti. Un bi néeńee nín bí puee Unaacimpɔɔn

english_verse: My dearest, the cities of Tirzah and Jerusalem are not as lovely as you. Your charms are more powerful than all of the stars in the heavens.
translation_verse: M-bɔɔn, a ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu, kii Tiirsa tiŋkee. A ŋān̄ ki mɔ̄ nnimbikpee kii Jeerusaleem tiŋkee, ama a kɔ̄ntí binib tifaandi kii dijanjakitil di bí dikɔmbool puee.

english_verse: Turn away your eyes— they make me melt. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
translation_verse: Fàtī a-nimbiin kí taa ti kpèè-mi, di sá yii a-nimbiliŋ sàtī-mi. A-yikpiti fɔ̀kɔ̀ ki bí kii kuŋɔcaŋkpuŋu di kpákatiń Galaadi jool puee.

english_verse: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
translation_verse: A-nyiŋŋi pīiǹ káŋkaŋ kii ipii in bi dáá cáń i-kuti ki fùl̄-iee ní. Dinyindi kamaa cáá di-ŋaliŋu ní, báà dibaba kaa fúkutì.

english_verse: What if I could have sixty queens, eighty wives, and thousands of others!
translation_verse: Ubɔti ŋūǹ kí nīn cáá binimpoobi imuŋku ita, bibɔntiibi imuŋku inaa, nì bisapɔmbi kupaau.

english_verse: You would be my only choice, my flawless dove, the favorite child of your mother. The young women, the queens, and all the others tell how excited you are as they sing your praises:
translation_verse: Man ceeyee, unimpubambaanti di bí. Úǹ di sá man beenanjil, unyaan. U sá u-na bibaabil ní, kibiki kin u nìn néeń tikpilkuee. Bisapɔmbi yaa wál̀-uee, bi pàkà-u ní, ní ubɔti nimpoobi nì u-bɔmbi nyɔ́ŋkí-u ki lì yii:

english_verse: “You are as majestic as the morning sky— glorious as the moon— blinding as the sun! Your charms are more powerful than all the stars above.” She Speaks:
translation_verse: «Batii nimpuu di bí kii kutaawuntuŋu walifiŋu na! U ŋān̄ kii uŋmalee, ki jìl̀ kii ŋwìińee, ki kɔ̄ntí binib tifaandi kii dijanjakitil di bí dikɔmbool puee.»

english_verse: I went down to see if blossoms were on the walnut trees, grapevines, and fruit trees.
translation_verse: M sīntì m-sufii kpaabun. M là kí kpèè asupɔmbil ŋin bí ditantakalinee. Fiinyi sufii púkuḿaaa? Greenaadi mun púkuḿaaa?

english_verse: But in my imagination I was suddenly riding on a glorious chariot. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Maa tí gbìl̀ taapu, ubɔtiisal, a yāntì maa ti nyí tin poon m bée.

english_verse: You are a princess, and your feet are graceful in their sandals. Your thighs are works of art, each one a jewel;
translation_verse: Gítiń, gítiń usulamiitinimpu, gítiń tí ŋmā kí kpèè-si. Ba pu ní ni kpèé usulamiitinimpu un bí akiti ali kansikin ki ŋōōyee? Unaacimpɔɔn

english_verse: your navel is a wine glass filled to overflowing. Your body is full and slender like a bundle of wheat bound together by lilies.
translation_verse: Bɔtiisal, anaataka ŋin a tákée ŋān̄ ki máaǹ-si! A-caŋ gíí ki ŋān̄ kii tiwanléeŋkaal tin bi mɔ́ɔ́yee.

english_verse: Your head is held high like Mount Carmel; your hair is so lovely it holds a king prisoner.
translation_verse: A-sil bí kii dikuntinyindi difɔkɔkuee. A-nimbiliŋ bí kii a yaa nyēē Eesbɔn tiŋkpaaŋkin anyimbɔbil ŋin bí niinee. A-maŋfal tɔ́kɔ́ kii Leebanɔn sintil difɔkɔku kun bí ki túĺ Damaasee.

english_verse: You are tall and slender like a palm tree, and your breasts are full.
translation_verse: A ŋān̄ ki bí gbàlgbal. M-neeŋkaau, sii di sá man pɔɔpindi.

english_verse: Kissing you is more delicious than drinking the finest wine. How wonderful and tasty! She Speaks:
translation_verse: M lī yii: «M làá jɔ̄m̀ bubabu nee kí gāā bu-sakaŋ!» A-biiŋi ń nīn sá ki tīī-mi kii fiinyi sakaŋee. A-fooku sɔnsɔfiŋu ń nīn náań nì asubil sɔnsɔfiŋu!

english_verse: Let's stroll through the fields and sleep in the villages.
translation_verse: M bí ki tīī un m néeńee, man ní u baasii là. Un bi néeńee bí mmɔnni Usapɔɔn

english_verse: Perfume from the magic flower fills the air, my darling. Right at our doorstep I have stored up for you all kinds of tasty fruits.
translation_verse: Kù yaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, ti làá cù fiinyi kpaaŋŋin kí kpèè yii an púkuḿaaa, an mātì. Ti làá kpèè yii greenaadi mun yaa púkuḿ. Niin ní m làá ŋmāliŋkì-si.

english_verse: If you were my brother, I could kiss you whenever we happen to meet, and no one would say I did wrong.
translation_verse: A yaa bàà sá m-niija, man nì un ŋáam̀ dibiibaantiilee! M yaa tú-si mmɔŋki laabee, m bàà kpàl̀-si, ní ubɔ kaa làá cɔ́kɔ́-mi.

english_verse: I could take you to the home of my mother, who taught me all I know. I would give you delicious wine and fruit juice as well.
translation_verse: M bàà cáǹ-si m-na cee ní á bīfì-mi dineendi. M bàà tìì-si ndaam min sɔ́fèe á nyɔ̀, asubiman ŋin m ŋmáaḿee nyim.

english_verse: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
translation_verse: U-ŋaŋgan tíkí m-yil, ní u-ŋaŋgiil pá m-caŋ pu.

english_verse: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me never to awaken love before it is ready. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi, m gbàam̄-ni, ní taa fìntī m-neendi, kí taa páb́-dì kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní di yaa láa lèe. Bisapɔmbi

english_verse: Who is this young woman coming in from the desert and leaning on the shoulder of the one she loves? She Speaks: I stirred up your passions under the apple tree where you were born.
translation_verse: Unimpu ulɔu di nyánní kuteeun u-ŋal nyīī un u néeńee pu na? Dineendi pɔŋŋu Usapɔɔn Dineendi subu taapu ní m fīntì-si laakin a-na cáá a-pool, laakin u màl̄-see.

english_verse: Always keep me in your heart and wear this bracelet to remember me by. The passion of love bursting into flame is more powerful than death, stronger than the grave.
translation_verse: Dū-mi kí nákań a-pɔbil pu kii kijalii kin a cáa nyìitī a-wanti puee. Yàntī ḿ nīn pée bí ki lɔ́kɔ́-si kii ditaŋkpal din pu bi kpítì a-yindi a dūu fúuń a-ŋalee. Tiŋman, dineendi pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii ŋkúmee ní, ní kpɔkɔsi pɔ̄ɔ̄ kpaŋkpam kii ditaŋkpiilinee, tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí pèefì-dì. Di fòol̄ kii ŋŋmee ní ki tòó kii utaayee.

english_verse: Love cannot be drowned by oceans or floods. It cannot be bought— any offer would be scorned no matter how great. Their Friends Speak:
translation_verse: Nnyiŋkpaam kɔkɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí gbíntí dineendi ŋmiŋu. Amɔɔ kɔkɔ nyim kaa ŋūǹ kí bìin̄ di-pu. Ubɔ yaa dū u-diikun gaajati kɔkɔ yii u làá dūú dā dineendee, u làá kúntíǹ ibeel ní.

english_verse: We have a little sister whose breasts are not yet formed. If someone asks to marry her, what should we do?
translation_verse: Ti cáá naal ubɔ, ama waa láá nyáń abii. Ti-naal gbanti yaa bàn̄ dicamɔndee, ba ní ti làá dāá ŋá kí tīī-u?

english_verse: She isn't a wall that we can defend behind a silver shield. Neither is she a room that we can protect behind a wooden door. She Speaks:
translation_verse: U yaa bàà sá kii digundee, ti bàà dù animbil kúti ní kí mā sintil difɔkɔŋi kí wúń u-pu. U yaa bàà sá kipunyɔkɔee, ti bàà làá dū seedir dɔi ní kí kpáá punuu kí pìin̄-u. Usapɔɔn

english_verse: I am a wall around a city, my breasts are towers, and just looking at me brings him great pleasure.
translation_verse: Man sá digundi ní, ní m-biiŋi sá adifɔkɔ. An puee, u-ceeyee, m sá un tìì-u dipɔɔpindee ní. Unaacimpɔɔn

english_verse: Solomon has a vineyard at Baal-Hamon, which he rents to others for a thousand pieces of silver each.
translation_verse: Saloomɔn cáá bufiinyikpaa Baal-Amɔn tiŋkin. U dū-bu ki kpāaǹ bipaadambi ní. Kí kìtī fiinyi gbanti biliŋee, báà ŋma máaǹ kí pà animbil kúti jitɔmbi kutuku ní.

english_verse: My vineyard is mine alone! Solomon can keep his silver and the others can keep their share of the profits. He Speaks:
translation_verse: Saloomɔn, animbil jitɔmbi kutukuee, sii di yì, ní kí dū jitɔmbi kulaafaau kí tīī bipaadambi bin cí kusaauee. An yaa kíǹ man fiinyi kpaabuee, m làá nīn cí-bu m-ba ní.

english_verse: You are in the garden with friends all around. Let me hear your voice! She Speaks:
translation_verse: Sii un kóò bukpaa kansikinee, a-bɔɔbi kpōoǹ bi-tafal kí pīlifì tin a làá sòoǹee. Ama man ní a máaǹ kí lì yii:

english_verse: Hurry to me, my darling! Run faster than a deer to mountains of spices.
translation_verse: «Sii un m néeńee, sāǹ kí kátí malaa! sāǹ kii upeemanee, àá kii kikɔniibikee ajoon ŋin sɔ́fèe pu.»

english_verse: I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz. And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah: A Guilty Nation
translation_verse: Yeesaya, Amɔtisi jipɔɔn nín nìn ká tibɔti tin Juuda beel nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki puee sèé. Ŋyunti gbantee, Oosiyasi nì Yootam nì Akaasi nì Eeseekiyaasi nìn kāl̀ kāl̀ Juuda beel pu tibɔtiil ki fōol̀ tɔb. Ti-Dindaan nibul kaa nyí di-Nimbɔtiu

english_verse: The Lord has said, “Listen, heaven and earth! The children I raised have turned against me.
translation_verse: Kutagbɔŋu, pīlifì! Kitiŋ, kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì! Ti-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ nee. «M lōō mbiyaamu, ki kpēē-mu mu cíkitì, ní mu kíǹ ki bíi jáà nì mi.

english_verse: Israel, you are a sinful nation loaded down with guilt. You are wicked and corrupt and have turned from the Lord, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni, nimbi ditimbundi din ŋáań ikpitee, dinibul din yīntèe, nnibool ŋun ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee, mbiyaamu mun yiliŋ gáatèe. Ni dū ti-Dindaan ki fá, ki kpēē Isirayeel Circir Nimbɔtiu fám, ki fātì ni-boon ki tīī-u.

english_verse: Why be punished more? Why not give up your sin? Your head is badly bruised, and you are weak all over.
translation_verse: Ni nín gbíntìi jáà nì u nee, ni-la ní u làá gíti fáá ní? Diyil kɔkɔ fōō tiweendi, dipɔbil kɔkɔ gīī ki yúl̀.

english_verse: From your head to your toes there isn't a healthy spot. Bruises, cuts, and open sores go without care or oil to ease the pain. A Country in Ruins
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ titafati kí cáá sāā diyilee, laaba kaa ti bí mmɔm. Tiwun kɔkɔ fōō tiweendi, ki lākatì lākatì, ki kpántì ibuun. Ubɔ kaa fíntì-i, kaa póob́-i, kaa ŋá-i ŋkpam kí bàtī iween pu.

english_verse: Your country lies in ruins; your towns are in ashes. Foreigners and strangers take and destroy your land while you watch.
translation_verse: Ni-tiŋki kpántì kuteeu, ni-timmu wùn̄ ŋŋmi kɔkɔ múb. Ni-nimbilaaliyin ní binicambi bí ki ŋàfī ni-kpaajinti. An kpéelikì ni-sati nyíki nyiki kii binannanliibi di jítèe.

english_verse: Enemies surround Jerusalem, alone like a hut in a vineyard or in a cucumber field.
translation_verse: Siiyɔn tiŋki baba di pée kíǹ, kii kibiŋ di yú fiinyi kpaabunee, kii uciitil bìŋ́ki di yú aputaajul kpaabunee, kii kitiŋ ní bijanjaliibi māntìi túee.

english_verse: Zion would have disappeared like Sodom and Gomorrah, if the Lord All-Powerful had not let a few of its people survive. Justice, Not Sacrifices
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan yaa kaa bàà yāntì ti-kansikin binikaaŋkaabi ŋmátèe, ti bàà làá nīn bí kii Soodoom yabee ní, kí nīn náań nì Goomoora yab. Ti-Dindaan ná binikpitib saraabi

english_verse: You are no better than the leaders and people of Sodom and Gomorrah! So listen to the Lord God:
translation_verse: Pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi, Soodoom kpilib. Ní ŋátí ni-tafal kí pīlifì ti-Nimbɔtiu dàkatam, Goomoora nibul.

english_verse: “Your sacrifices mean nothing to me. I am sick of your offerings of rams and choice cattle; I don't like the blood of bulls or lambs or goats.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ba ní m làá ŋá nì saraabi bin ni ŋáań tikpil nee? M núutiǹ ipijaa saraawɔkaabi nì anabil kpam. M gīī nì inajaa nì apibil nì iŋoobu fatikuu.

english_verse: “Who asked you to bring all this when you come to worship me? Stay out of my temple!
translation_verse: Ni nín dòoń ki yūlifí m-nimbiinee, man di bí yii ni-taal ń tāā m-cindinaaa?

english_verse: Your sacrifices are worthless, and your incense disgusting. I can't stand the evil you do on your New Moon Festivals or on your Sabbaths and other times of worship.
translation_verse: Ní taa ti cáań-mi saraabi, an kaa kèetī tiba. M ná talaalub bin ni tùutēe nyiim! Ni jīǹ uŋmapɔɔn nì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa jiŋaalib ki kpáfí ki jīǹ jiŋaalib ki ŋáań ikpiti. Maa ti là kí ká míǹ.

english_verse: I hate your New Moon Festivals and all others as well. They are a heavy burden I am tired of carrying.
translation_verse: M ná uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaalib bin ni jīǹee, ni-kpafiŋ kpántì diwaŋgul ní ki tīī-mi, ní m túǹ ki gīī m-naŋki nyáń.

english_verse: “No matter how much you pray, I won't listen. You are too violent.
translation_verse: Ni yaa tāntì ni-ŋalii kí mèèyee, m fàtī m-kpaŋkpamboon ní kí tīī-ni. Báà ní mèè kí gíti mèè, maa làá pīlifì-ni, kun puee ni-ŋalii táká fatiku.

english_verse: Wash yourselves clean! I hate your filthy deeds. Stop doing wrong
translation_verse: Ní fàl̀maan, kí ŋámaan ni-ba circir. Ní nyāntí ni-tuŋkpitiŋ m-nimbiin, kí gbèen̄ kí taa ti ŋá ikpiti.

english_verse: and learn to live right. See that justice is done. Defend widows and orphans and help the oppressed.” An Invitation from the Lord
translation_verse: Ní bīfì kí nīn ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee. Ní nyàab̀ kí nīn nóó deedee saŋŋu. Ní nīn kpòotī bin wɔ́b̀ bi-jutiibee. Ní sòoǹ kí pɔ̀ ditaŋkpiibil, kí sòoǹ kí mɔ̄tì ukpiipu pu.» Ní taa ti já nì ti-Dindaan

english_verse: I, the Lord, invite you to come and talk it over. Your sins are scarlet red, but they will be whiter than snow or wool.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ní dāam̄maan tí sòoǹ kí gbìlīǹ tɔb. Báà ni-kpitii yaa yāntìi máǹ cíncinciŋ kii fatikuee, i làá pīil̀ káŋkaŋkaŋ kii ntaayimee. Báà i yaa máǹ kii ŋwɔmee, i làá pīil̀ kii upipiin kutee ní.

english_verse: If you willingly obey me, the best crops in the land will be yours.
translation_verse: Ni yaa kíí ki pílifì m-nyɔkɔ, ni làá jī tijin tin kitiŋ nee lòon̄ee.

english_verse: But if you turn against me, your enemies will kill you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa yíì kaa pílifì, ní ki gbíntìi jáà nì mee, kitàataajiki ní bi làá dūú kúntí-ni.» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ. Ti-Dindaan làá ŋá Jeerusaleem tiŋki circir

english_verse: Jerusalem, you are like an unfaithful wife. Once your judges were honest and your people lived right; now you are a city full of murderers.
translation_verse: An ŋá mana ní kitiŋ kin kaa nìn cáá tijɔkɔndee dūu kpántì kii kinimpulaakpaayee ní? Dooooyee, ki-nib nìn nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu, ní ki nìn bí deedee. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, binikpɔliibi di kíǹ ki gbí ki-ni.

english_verse: Your silver is fake, and your wine is watered down.
translation_verse: A-nimbiliŋ kúti kaa ti nyìm̀, ní bi cēeǹ a-damɔmmɔntiimin nnyim!

english_verse: Your leaders have rejected me to become friends of crooks; your rulers are looking for gifts and bribes. Widows and orphans never get a fair trial.
translation_verse: A-bɔtiibi sá pɔɔgaatib ní, bi nì binaayub di pēē kinyɔkɔ. Bi-kɔkɔ néeń tiwampɔkaal, ki jòó ki pá dinyɔɔŋeebil jim boon. Baa pɔ̀ ditaŋkpiibil, kaa mɔ́tí ukpiipu pu.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the mighty ruler of Israel, and I make you a promise: You are now my enemy, and I will show my anger by taking revenge on you.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan un di sá Isirayeel Nimbɔtikpaaŋwuee lī yii: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni! M làá téeǹ nimbi bin ná-mee! M làá tɔ̀ nimbi m-nannanliibi ipɔntoon!

english_verse: I will punish you terribly and burn away everything that makes you unfit to worship me.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem, m làá tāā kí bīikì a-pu. M làá dū kaŋwa kí fàl̀-si á nyā, m làá nyāntí-si a-jɔkɔnti kɔkɔn.

english_verse: Jerusalem, I will choose judges and advisors like those you had before. Your new name will be “Justice and Faithfulness.” The Lord Will Save Jerusalem
translation_verse: M làá yàntī a-bɔsoonliibi ń kpántí kii njamin yabee, kí yàntī a-saŋkiliibi ń nīn bí kii cannaaku yabee. Ní bí dāá nīn kíǹ ki yíì-si yii <Ibaamɔn Tiŋki, Kitiŋ kin yú nì Unimbɔti deedeeyee>».

english_verse: Jerusalem, you will be saved by showing justice; Zion's people who turn to me will be saved by doing right.
translation_verse: Ibaamɔn làá fīī Siiyɔn tiŋki, ní deedee ń yàntī ki-nib bin kpántì bi-bee ń ŋmátí.

english_verse: But those rebellious sinners who turn against me, the Lord, will all disappear.
translation_verse: Ama pɔɔgaatib nì bikpitiŋaliibi làá nàan̄, ní bin dū ti-Dindaan ki fée ń kúntí.

english_verse: You will be made ashamed of those groves of trees where you worshiped idols.
translation_verse: Icoo làá cúú-ni iwaasufi in ni néeń tikpilee pu. Ni-wunti làá yɔ̀tī ni-kpaaŋŋi ŋin ni lēē kí nīn tòotī awaayee poon.

english_verse: You will be like a grove of trees dying in a drought.
translation_verse: Kun puee ni làá dāá nīn sá kii buwaasubu bun faati yɔ́ĺee ní, kii bukpaa bun poon ní nnyim fóotèe.

english_verse: Your strongest leaders will be like dry wood set on fire by their idols. No one will be able to help, as they all go up in flames.
translation_verse: Upɔɔl làá dāá nīn sá usá, ní u-tuuŋŋi dāa sá kii ŋŋmiyatiyaalee. Bi-liitil làá dāá fōō ŋŋmi, ní ubɔ kaa dāa bí kí gbíntí.

english_verse: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills; every nation will rush to it.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń, dijool din pu ti-Dindaan diiku tɔ́kɔ́ee làá dāá lìbitī ajoon kɔkɔ pu. Di làá dāá nīn fɔ̀kɔǹ ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ. Anibul kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn bìtifī ki dòoń di-cee.

english_verse: Many people will come and say, “Let's go to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
translation_verse: Anibul tikpil làá dāá tàkan̄ nsan ki cá ki lì yii: «Dāam̄maan! Tí jɔ̄m̀maan ti-Dindaan jool pu, tí jɔ̄m̀maan Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu diikun. U làá tin dàkà-ti tin ní u là tí ŋée, ní tí nóó u-sàmbiyaamu pu.» Tiŋman, Siiyɔn ní Mara làá nyānní, u-nyɔɔbundi làá nyānní Jeerusaleem ní.

english_verse: He will settle arguments between nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never make war or attack one another.
translation_verse: U làá dāá sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì atimbun kansikin bɔti, kí dāá pàtī anibul tikpil bí taa ti já. Bi làá dāá dū bi-tàataajimmu kí mɔ́ɔ́ akoo, ní kí dāá dū bi-kpammu kí mɔ́ɔ́ igɔti. Ditimbundi diba kaa dāa gíti jáà nì di-juti, ní binib kaa dāa gíti bífí bi nín jáà kujaau puee.

english_verse: People of Israel, let's live by the light of the Lord. Following Sinful Customs
translation_verse: Jaakɔb naantiibi, dāam̄maan tí còom̀ ti-Dindaan walifiŋun. Ti-Dindaan bɔsooŋyi wiiŋŋu

english_verse: Our Lord, you have deserted your people, Israel, because they follow customs of nations from the east. They worship Philistine gods and are close friends of foreigners.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a dū a-nibul Jaakɔb naantiibi ki fá. Kun puee ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú bɔɔbi di kíǹ ki gbí bi-tiŋkin. Bin kpèé iŋmalbijaa ki cáa būū tibɔɔlee gbóotì kii Fiiliistii yab ceeyee. A-nibul nì binicambi di kíǹ ki sòoǹ ki ŋàatī tɔb pu.

english_verse: They have endless treasures of silver and gold; they have countless horses and war chariots.
translation_verse: Animbil kúti nì sindaariya gbí bi-tiŋkin, ní ki-gaajawanti wīikí tikpil an kaa cáá bí lì. Itaamu gbí bi-tiŋkin, ní bi-janjatɔrɔkub wīikí tikpil.

english_verse: Everywhere in the country they worship the idols they have made.
translation_verse: Awaa gbí bi-tiŋkin, bi gbàantí ki jáaḿ awaa, tiwan tin bi dū bi-ŋalii ki mɔ́ɔ́yee.

english_verse: And so, all of them will be ashamed and disgraced. Don't forgive them! A Day of Judgment
translation_verse: An pu ní binib kɔkɔ làá nīn dɔ̄ kitiŋ ki fìlim̀, ama ti-Dindaan, á taa yòon̄-bi kí síiń.

english_verse: Every one of you, go hide among the rocks and in the ground, because the Lord is fearsome, marvelous, and glorious.
translation_verse: Kɔ́maan kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔ poon, ní kɔ́ kitiŋ taapu kí báĺ kí sāǹ ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi, kí sāǹ u-kpaanti nín ŋmóò pu nyàlibuee nimbiin.

english_verse: When the Lord comes, everyone who is proud will be made humble, and the Lord alone will be honored.
translation_verse: Unil un yòontí u-ba yilpuee làá dāá tìntī u-yil, bilambidambi làá dāá sìntī bi-ba taapu. Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan baba ní bi làá dāá tīī tinyool.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has chosen a day when those who are proud and conceited will be put down.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan lēē ŋwiin ŋun ní u làá dāá sòoǹ bilambidambi nì bin dàkà bi-bee nì binib bin yòontí bi-ba yilpuee bɔti, ní kí dāá sìntī-bi taapu.

english_verse: The tall and towering cedars of Lebanon will be destroyed. So will the oak trees of Bashan,
translation_verse: U làá dāá sòoǹ Leebanɔn tiŋki sufii in bi yíì seedir i fɔ̀kɔ̀ tikpilee bɔti, kí dāá sòoǹ Baasan tiŋki waasufii in bi yíì seenee bɔti,

english_verse: all the seagoing ships, and every beautiful boat.
translation_verse: kí dāá sòoǹ Taarsiisi tiŋkin meelab kɔkɔ bɔti, ní kí dāá sòoǹ meelanyaambi kɔkɔ bɔti.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone who is proud will be put down. Only the Lord will be honored.
translation_verse: Unil un yòontí u-ba yilpuee làá dāá tìntī u-yil, bilambidambi làá dāá sìntī bi-ba taapu. Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan baba ní bi làá dāá tīī tinyool.

english_verse: Idols will be gone for good.
translation_verse: Awaa kɔkɔ làá dāá wāŋkì.

english_verse: You had better hide in caves and holes— the Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth.
translation_verse: Kɔ́maan kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔ poon, ní kɔ́maan kí báĺ afaginni kí sāǹ ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi, kí sāǹ u-kpaanti nín ŋmóò pu nyàlibuee nimbiin, u yaa láa yíkì ki bíi kɔ̄ntí kitiŋ kɔkɔ dinyoondee.

english_verse: On that day everyone will throw to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold they made to worship.
translation_verse: Yaadalee, binib làá dāá dū awaa ŋin bi dū animbil kúti nì sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ ki gbàantí ŋi-nimbiin ki jáaḿee kí lúkú isiiboo nì tinanjin.

english_verse: The Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth— they will hide in caves and in the hills.
translation_verse: Binib làá kɔ́ kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔ poon, kí kɔ́ kí báĺ ntaŋkpafaŋfakamin kí sāǹ ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi, kí sāǹ u-kpaanti nín ŋmóò pu nyàlibuee nimbiin, u yaa láa yíkì ki bíi kɔ̄ntí kitiŋ kɔkɔ dinyoondee.

english_verse: Stop trusting the power of humans. They are all going to die, so how can they help?
translation_verse: Ní taa nín̄ máká nisaaleen pu, kufoou kun u cááyee pu ní u bí. An yaa sá fám, unil sá ba?

english_verse: The mighty Lord All-Powerful is going to take away from Jerusalem and Judah everything you need— your bread and water, *
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá ŋmìntī Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì Juuda beel tijikaal nì nnyim. U làá ŋmìntī-bi tin máaǹ kí nīn tíkí-bee kɔkɔ:

english_verse: soldiers and heroes, judges and prophets, leaders and army officers,
translation_verse: an dàkà yii ubaatandaan nì ujanjal, ubɔsoonli nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu, ubɔɔ nì utindaŋkpil,

english_verse: officials and advisors, fortunetellers and others who tell the future.
translation_verse: ujanjakpil nì dibɔtibil, usaŋkil nì ukpaŋkpanti nì usoopu.

english_verse: You will each be cruel to friends and neighbors. Young people will insult their elders; no one will show respect to those who deserve it.
translation_verse: Binib làá nīn ŋáań tɔb tipɔmbɔti, báà ŋma làá nīn ŋáań u-juti tipɔmbɔti. Kibiki làá jɔ̄m̀ utikpil pu, ní unifan ń jɔ̄m̀ unikpaan pu.

english_verse: Some of you will grab hold of a relative and say, “You still have a coat. Be our leader and rule this pile of ruins.”
translation_verse: Unil làá dāá cúú u-nabiki kin u nì un pēē kubaabinaatoouee kí lì-u yii: «Sii cáá dibɔkutil kí pèen̄ee, kpántí ti-kpiliu kí nīn kpòotī-ti fikil fikil yuntiŋu nee poon!»

english_verse: But the answer will be, “I can't do you any good. Don't make me your leader. There's no food or clothing left in my house.”
translation_verse: Ní udaan ń dāá kíí yaadal gbanti yii: «Maa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiba kí tīī-ni. M-dumpuee, tijikaal kaa báaa, tiwampeeŋkaal mun kpá. Naa ŋūǹ kí lēē-mi ḿ nīn sá ukpil!»

english_verse: Jerusalem and Judah, you rebelled against your glorious Lord— your words and your actions, made you stumble and fall.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem tiŋki gbéetì, ní Juuda beel lítì. Di sá yii bi jáà nì ti-Dindaan bi-sòontam nì bi-ŋáaǹtam poon, ki kpèé-u fám.

english_verse: The look on your faces shows that you are sinful as Sodom, and you don't try to hide it. You are in for trouble, and you have brought it all on yourselves. The Wrong Kind of Leaders
translation_verse: Bi-nimbikpeeŋu di sòoǹ ki kù bi-bɔti. Bi sòoǹ bi-kpitii pu mpaampiin pu kii Soodoom tiŋki yab nín nìn ŋáań puee, baa bāal̀ i-pu binib cee. Bíǹ bi-ba naabuŋu ní bi bíi bɔ́ntí!

english_verse: Tell those who obey God, “You're very fortunate— you will be rewarded for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Lìmaan yii deedeedambi bí mmɔnneeee! Di sá yii bi làá dāá páatí tin ní bi ŋée pu.

english_verse: Tell those who disobey, “You're in big trouble— what you did to others will come back to you.”
translation_verse: Ama mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí binikpitib, tiba pée kpá kí nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī-bi. Di sá yii bi-tuuŋŋi paati ní bi làá fōō.

english_verse: Though you are God's people, you are ruled and abused by women and children. You are confused by leaders who guide you down the wrong path.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M-nibul, mbiyaamu di wɔ́b́-si, binimpoobi di ŋúb́ a-tiŋki ki kpòotī. M-nibul, a-tindaŋkpilib kíiĺ-si ní, bi kpòotī-si ki cáǹ nsaŋkpiti pu ní.» Ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ u-nibul kpilib bɔti

english_verse: The Lord is ready to accuse and judge all nations.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì kí sòoǹ ibɔsoon, u yíkìi yúl̀ kí sòoǹ anibul bɔti.

english_verse: He will even judge you rulers and leaders of his own nation. You destroyed his vineyard and filled your houses by robbing the poor.
