translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ u-nibul kpootiliibi nì bi-tindaŋkpilib bɔti yii: «Nimbi di bíil̀ m-fiinyi sufii kpaabu. Ni jíitì biwɔfib wanti ki gbéeǹ ni-diiŋŋi.»

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says, “You have crushed my people and rubbed in the dirt the faces of the poor.” The Women of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, duulinya kɔkɔ Nimbɔtiu bí yii: «Ba ŋá ní ni bí ki nà m-nibul, ki wɔ́b́ biwɔfib míǹ?» Jeerusaleem nimpunyaambi

english_verse: The Lord says: The women of Jerusalem are proud and strut around, winking shamelessly. They wear anklets that jingle and call attention to the way they walk.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Jeerusaleem nimpoobi mɔ̀ɔǹ tikpil. Bi còom̄ bi-silii tèen̄, ki cáá bi-nimbikpeeŋu ki sàtī bininjab. Bi còom̄ diba diba, ní ki yàntī abɔmbil ŋin bi fúuń bi-taaŋee gbáà tɔb ki sūǹ.»

english_verse: But I, the Lord, will cover their heads with sores, and I will uncover their private parts.
translation_verse: An puee ti-Dindaan làá yàntī digbàndi ń cúú bi-yiliŋ bi-yikpiti ń kùfì ní bi-yigbeeŋi ń kpántí akulim.

english_verse: In place of perfume, there will be a stink; in place of belts, there will be ropes; in place of fancy hairdos, they will have bald heads. Instead of expensive clothes, they will wear sackcloth; instead of beauty, they will have ugly scars.
translation_verse: Tiwansuundi nunuŋu di làá dāá fōō talaalu sɔnsɔfiŋu, ŋŋmii di làá dāá fōō dambala paaŋŋu, dibaakpandi di làá dāá fōō tiyikpilukaal tin nyáń ti-bee paaŋŋu, kpɔsatab di làá dāá fōō tiwannyaandi paaŋŋu, ní icoo daaŋku ń dāá fōō kunyaaŋŋu paaŋŋu. Jeerusaleem kpiipoobi

english_verse: The fighting men of Jerusalem will be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem, a-nib làá gbíntí kujaau poon, a-janjaliibi làá kpúń dikɔ̀ndi poon.

english_verse: The city will mourn and sit in the dirt, emptied of its people.
translation_verse: Niinee a-tiŋki nib kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn sūǹ ki yáliŋkí, kii unimpu un kaa ti cáá báà tiba ki gbíntì ki kā kitiŋee.

english_verse: When this happens, seven women will grab the same man, and each of them will say, “I'll buy my own food and clothes! Just marry me and take away my disgrace.” The Lord Will Bless His People Who Survive
translation_verse: Yaadalee, binimpoobi biluli làá dāá tɔ̄ kí kíĺ uninjabaanti ní kí lì yii: «Timbi di làá nīn kpèé ti-ba ti-jītam nì ti-pèentam. Kun ti pée nyàab̀ a-ceeyee di sá á kíí kí cáá-ti kí nyāntí-ti ti-cooin.» Binib bin làá kíń Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee

english_verse: The time is coming when the Lord will make his land fruitful and glorious again, and the people of Israel who survive will take great pride in what the land produces.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, tin ti-Dindaan làá yàntī án nyēe làá nīn cáá jilma nì tinyool. Tin Isirayeel tiŋki làá dāá lòoǹee làá dāá nīn sá ki-nib bin ŋmátèe faalii nì bi-nyooti.

english_verse: after the Lord sends a fiery judgment to clean the city and its people of their violent deeds.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī kubuŋu kun ŋáań binib deedee nì circiree ń jītí ní kí fíntí Siiyɔn nimpunyaambi jɔkɔnti. U làá fíntí Jeerusaleem tiŋki fatiku un u nyántèe pu.

english_verse: Then the Lord will cover the whole city and its meeting places with a thick cloud each day and with a flaming fire each night. God's own glory will be like a huge tent that covers everything.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, Siiyɔn jool kɔkɔ pu nì bin kɔkɔ làá dāá kóoǹ kí kpāfì niinee puee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá yàntī ditagbandi diba ń nyā ŋwiimpu ní ŋŋminyiim nì aŋmilimbil ń nīn ŋmíntí kunyeeu. Ní ti-Dindaan nyooti ń dāá nīn dàn̄ yilpu kii kadantikuee,

english_verse: It will provide shade from the heat of the sun and a place of shelter and protection from storms and rain.
translation_verse: a lì kii kadantiku un bi dū tifaal ki píń án tìì mboon kutuntuŋkpaaŋŋu yuntiŋuee. Kubuŋkpaaŋŋu nì utaa yuntiŋuee, u làá dāá kpántí kibalilaŋ nì laakin binib sáń ki kóòyee.

english_verse: My friend dug the ground, removed the stones, and planted the best vines. He built a watchtower and dug a pit in rocky ground for pressing the grapes. He hoped they would be sweet, but bitter grapes were all it produced.
translation_verse: M-bɔɔ yɔ̄kɔtì kitiŋ gbanti, ki lēē ataŋkpee kɔkɔ ki fá, ní ki cóoǹ ifiinyisumɔnti. U gāā isupaa bukpaayee kansikin, ki gbìn̄ mbòó ŋun ni u làá nīn ŋmāam̀ isufee biliŋee. U bàà nìn cɔ́tí yii bukpaayee làá lòoǹ asubimɔnti, ama ní bu dūu lòon̄ asubikpiti.

english_verse: Listen, people of Jerusalem and of Judah! You be the judge of me and my vineyard.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m-bɔɔ bí yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, nimbi bin kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee nì nimbi bin sá Juuda tiŋkin yabee, ní sòom̀maan man nì m-fiinyi kpaabu bɔti kí tīī-mi!

english_verse: Now I will let you know what I am going to do. I will cut down the hedge and tear down the wall. My vineyard will be trampled and left in ruins.
translation_verse: «Too, m làá tùkù-ni m nín làá ŋá m-kpaabu gbanti puee. M làá bàkatī bu-naabakaku ní tiwaŋkuti ń kɔ́ kí ŋmɔ́ fiinyee faati. M làá téé digundi din māntìi tú-buee kí lúkú ní bisanjitiliibi ń tāā tāā kí bīil̀-i.

english_verse: It will turn into a desert, neither pruned nor hoed; it will be covered with thorns and briars. I will command the clouds not to send rain.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī bú kpántí kupɔɔu, maa ti làá ŋāŋkì fiinyi sufii gbanti ní kaa nín kɔ̄tì-i. Ikuŋkuŋfi nì abɔjanaakun di làá nyā i-ni, ní ḿ yàntī utaa ń taa ti nì i-pu.»

english_verse: You are in for trouble! You take over house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone else in all the land.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí binib bin di māā adiin ki kútí adiin pu, ki fòol̄ tisati ki kútí tisati puee. Án dāa pée kúntíǹ yii bíǹ di jíń mpaan kɔkɔ, ki kíǹ ki kóò kitiŋ nee pu bi-baba.

english_verse: None of them are tired. They don't sleep or get drowsy, and they run without stumbling. Their belts don't come loose; their sandal straps don't break.
translation_verse: Di-nib kansikinee, báà ubɔ kaa gīī, báà ubɔ kaa gbéetì, báà ubɔ kaa gèen̄ ki yīntì, báà ubɔ kaa dōoǹ ki gèen̄, báà ubɔ kaa gbīntì u-dambalau ní kaa nín kútì u-naataaŋmiii.

english_verse: You are in for trouble! The lies you tell are like ropes by which you drag along sin and evil.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí binib bin nyimɔŋyi sá kii iŋmii ki bóob́-bi ki nákáǹ bi-kpitiiyee! Bi còom̄ ikpiti pá bi-boon kii tɔrɔku ní bi dàtēe.

english_verse: You are in for trouble! You get up early to start drinking, and you keep it up late into the night.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí binib bin fìntī kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl kí dūú gùl̄ ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee pu dinyɔlee, nì bin yìiǹ kunyeeu ki nyù ndamam an nyàatī-bee!

english_verse: At your drinking parties you have the music of stringed instruments, tambourines, and flutes. But you never even think about all the Lord has done,
translation_verse: Bi kpáfí ki nyù idafi ní bi bɔ̀ɔ́-bi tibati nì saŋgub, ki cákafí-bi cancakantib ní ki búǹ-bi awul. Ama baa wāĺ tin ti-Dindaan bíi ŋáańee, kaa kpèé gba tin ní u ŋée.

english_verse: and so his people know nothing about him. That's why many of you will be dragged off to foreign lands. Your leaders will starve to death, and everyone else will suffer from thirst.
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní bi làá cúú m-nibul kí cùnnì kuyuŋu bi nín kaa là kí nīn nyí tibee pu. Bi-kpilib làá kpú ŋkùm, ní samaa ń kpú nnyinnyoo.

english_verse: The world of the dead has opened its mouth wide and is eagerly waiting for the leaders of Jerusalem and for its noisy crowds, especially for those who take pride in that city.
translation_verse: An puee ditaŋkpiil wāaǹ kinyɔkɔ bàaa, di wāaǹ di-nyɔɔkpaaŋku. Jeerusaleem kpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ làá kɔ́ poon, bi nì bi-jiŋaalib wooku kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Its citizens have been put down, and its proud people have been brought to shame.
translation_verse: An pu ní binib kɔkɔ làá nīn dɔ̄ kitiŋ ki fìlim̀, ní bilambidambi ń tìntī bi-yiliŋ.

english_verse: But the holy Lord God All-Powerful is praised, because he has shown who he is by bringing justice.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá sòoǹ tibɔti ibaamɔn kí dàkà u-kpaanti. Circir Nimbɔtiu làá sòoǹ tibɔti deedee kí dàkà yii u sá circirdaan.

english_verse: His people will be like sheep grazing in their own pasture, and they will take off what was left by others.
translation_verse: Ipii làá dāá ŋmɔ́ timool niin kii kupikpaapɔɔunee, ní ŋŋɔbiyaamu mun bi là mú gbìfiǹee ń dāá jī niin.

english_verse: And you say, “Let the holy God of Israel hurry up and do what he has promised, so we can see it for ourselves.”
translation_verse: Bi bí ki lì yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń yáb́, ú ŋá tin u là kí ŋée malaa timbi ń ká. Tin ní Isirayeel Circir Nimbɔtiu bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ yii u làá ŋée, ú ŋá, timbi là kí béé.»

english_verse: And you are great at drinking and mixing drinks. But you are in for trouble.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí bin dàkà dibaatandi ki nyù ndaam, ki cáá tininjati kí dū idafi in pɔ̄ɔ̄yee kí ŋmàlim̀ kí nyɔ̀ee.

english_verse: You accept bribes to let the guilty go free, and you cheat the innocent out of a fair trial.
translation_verse: Bi fòol̄ dinyɔɔŋeebil jim kí pɔ̀ dibɔkpil daan, ama baa kíikí kí pɔ̀ ibaamɔndaan.

english_verse: You will go up in flames like straw and hay! You have rejected the teaching of the holy Lord God All-Powerful of Israel. Now your roots will rot, and your blossoms will turn to dust.
translation_verse: An pu ní kii ŋŋmi nín wù timool pu, timɔkulindi ń wà búkú buku puee, míǹ ní bi-nyaaŋyi làá sūū ní bi-pumpukum ń kpántí kii ŋkpɔŋkpɔmee kubuŋu ń yòon̄, kun puee bi fá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan marau, kaa fātìi tɔ́ Isirayeel Circir Nimbɔtiu bɔti. Ti-Dindaan gíí diŋuul u-nibul pu (B.

english_verse: You are the Lord's people, but you made him terribly angry, and he struck you with his mighty arm. Mountains shook, and dead bodies covered the streets like garbage. The Lord is still angry, and he is ready to strike you again. Foreign Nations Will Attack
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan fōō u-nibul pu mbum ki tāntì u-ŋal ki fáá-dì. Ajoon cīŋkì ní anikpil dɔ̄ adan pu fìlfilfil kii timool tin bi ŋātì ki fée. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee u-ŋuul kaa sɔ̄ŋkì, ní u-ŋal dáá pée gbíntìi tèen̄.

english_verse: The Lord has signaled for the foreign nations to come and attack you. He has already whistled, and they are coming as fast as they can.
translation_verse: U cóoǹ kudaaŋŋu kubɔ ki dàkā ndandati nibul diba, ki búń ŋfoon ki yíiń-dì doooo kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ ní di yáb́ malaa ki bāań.

english_verse: Their arrows are sharp, and their bows are ready. The hoofs of their horses are hard as flint; the wheels of their war chariots turn as fast as a whirlwind.
translation_verse: Bi lōoǹ bi-piiŋyi, ki píĺ bi-tɔfii ki páaǹ ipiin ki cí. Bi-taamui tafuŋfukuti pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii ataŋkpacancalee, ní bi-tɔrɔkub taaŋi màntī kii kunaakpaabuŋŋuee.

english_verse: They roar and growl like fierce young lions as they grab their victims and drag them off where no one can rescue them.
translation_verse: Bi mùuǹ kii ugbikintinaatee, ki gà kuwoou kii ŋgbikintibiyaamu nín sūǹ puee. Bi mùuǹ kí cúú bi-jinti kí kpáàá cáá búntí, ní báà ubɔ kpá ki làá cúú-tì kí fōō bi-ŋaan.

english_verse: On the day they attack, they will roar like the ocean. And across the land you will see nothing but darkness and trouble, because the light of day will be covered by thick clouds.
translation_verse: Ama ŋwindalee, bi làá dāá téeń ditimbundi gbanti pu kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋu nín yàntī tiŋku wòoǹ puee. A yaa láa gbóoń ki kpēē kitiŋee, dibɔmbɔndi nì dinimbinaamandi ní a dāa pée kíǹ ki wāĺ, ní atagban ń dāá dūú bìin̄ ŋwalifi pu.

english_verse: In the year that King Uzziah died, I had a vision of the Lord. He was on his throne high above, and his robe filled the temple.
translation_verse: Dibindi din ubɔti Oosiyasi kpíìyee, an nìn lēē ki dàkā-mi. M nìn ká ti-Dindaan kā dibeejafɔŋfɔkɔl diba pu. U-bɔkutil gbeeŋgbeeŋyi nìn gbí kunimbɔtidii kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Flaming creatures with six wings each were flying over him. They covered their faces with two of their wings and their bodies with two more. They used the other two wings for flying,
translation_verse: Seerafiimbi nìn yú u-yilpu ki cáá ifeen iluu iluu. Seerafiim kamaa feeŋyi ili nìn bīī u-nimbiin, ní ili bīī u-wunti pu ní u cáá ili in kíǹee ki ŋàaǹ.

english_verse: as they shouted, “Holy, holy, holy, Lord All-Powerful! The earth is filled with your glory.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn bí ki kūuntí ki lì tɔb yii: «Circir, circir, circir! Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sá circirdaan! U-nyooti gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ!»

english_verse: As they shouted, the doorposts of the temple shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
translation_verse: Bi bíi kūuntí mimmee ní kunimbɔtidii punyɔmmu cīŋkì doooo mu-nyeel, ní nnyiim yíkì ki gbí kunimbɔtidiin.

english_verse: Then I cried out, “I'm doomed! Everything I say is sinful, and so are the words of everyone around me. Yet I have seen the King, the Lord All-Powerful.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní m lī yii: «Mbusu kɔ́-mi! M-bɔti dóò ní nee, kun puee tijɔkɔndi nyɔɔbuŋŋi ŋma di nyēē m-nyɔkɔn, ní m kóò binib bin nyɔmmun tijɔkɔndi nyɔɔbuŋŋi nyēēyee kansikin. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m-nimbiliŋ baasii ká Ubɔti, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan.»

english_verse: One of the flaming creatures flew over to me with a burning coal that it had taken from the altar with a pair of metal tongs.
translation_verse: Niinee ní seerafiimbee ubɔ dū kubabiku ki bábiń dimɔsiŋkɔndi diba nsaraafan pu ní ki ŋàan̄ ki nín dòoń m-cee.

english_verse: It touched my lips with the hot coal and said, “This has touched your lips. Your sins are forgiven, and you are no longer guilty.”
translation_verse: U bāań ki dū dimɔsiŋkɔndee ki gbēē m-nyunculiŋ ní ki bí-mi yii: «Dimɔsiŋkɔndi nín gbēē a-nyunculiŋ nee, bi pítì a-yìntitam, ki dū a-kpitii ki pú-si.»

english_verse: After this, I heard the Lord ask, “Is there anyone I can send? Will someone speak for us?” “I'll go,” I answered. “Send me!”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní m gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan bālifì yii: «Ŋma ní m làá tɔ̄ ní? Ŋma làá nīn sá ti-bɔnaatiliu?» Ní m kíí yii: «M sèé, tɔ̄-mi!»

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to go and speak this message to the people: “You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.” The Lord also said,
translation_verse: Ní u bí yii: «Cù kí tùkù dinibul nee yii: <Ni làá pīlifì kí pīlifì, ama naa làá gbìl̄ taapu. Ni làá kpèè kí kpèè, ama naa làá wāl̀ tiba.>

english_verse: “Make these people stubborn! Make them stop up their ears, cover their eyes, and fail to understand. Don't let them turn to me and be healed.”
translation_verse: Yàntī binib gbanti pɔbiliŋ ń tìlifì, bi-tafaliŋ ń kpáá ní bi-nimbiliŋ ń ŋúb́. Yàntī bí taa ti wāl̀, kí taa ti gbìl̄, kí taa ti béé tibɔti taapu. Án nín làá ŋá pu bí taa kpántí bi-bimbim kí fàtīí gítiń m-cee ḿ cáaǹ-bee.»

english_verse: Then I asked the Lord, “How long will this last?” The Lord answered: Until their towns are destroyed and their houses are deserted, until their fields are empty,
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bālifì yii: «Ti-Dindaan, án làá nīn bí míǹ kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu?» Ní u kíí-mi yii: «Kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní bi làá nàan̄ ntimu, binib ń taa ti nín̄ kóò mu-poon, adiin ń nīn kíǹ ki yú fám ní tikpaatan ń kpántí kii kuteeuee.»

english_verse: and I have sent them far away, leaving their land in ruins.
translation_verse: Iiin, ti-Dindaan làá jà binib kí nyāntí kitiŋ nee poon kí cùnnì ndan, ní tikpaatan dāa kíǹ ki dɔ̄ fám.

english_verse: If only a tenth of the people are left, even they will be destroyed. But just as stumps remain after trees have been cut down, some of my chosen ones will be left.
translation_verse: Báà binib saalaa poon ubaanti di yaa kíǹ kitiŋ nee ni, ŋŋmi làá wà-u kii busubu bun bi gāā ki lúkúee ní. Kun làá dāá pée kíńee di sá disuyil, ama disuyil gbanti di làá dāá nīn sá circir wambooliŋu.

english_verse: When news reached the royal palace that Syria had joined forces with Israel, King Ahaz and everyone in Judah were so terrified that they shook like trees in a windstorm.
translation_verse: Bi tùkū Akaasi un sá Daafiidi naantiiuee yii: «Aram yab bāań ki bí Eefiraayiim tiŋki pu.» Ubɔti nì u-yab nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní an cīŋkì-bi kii kubuŋu nín cìŋkī kubambaŋŋun sufii puee.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to me: Take your son Shearjashub and go see King Ahaz. You will find him on the road near the cloth makers' shops at the end of the canal that brings water from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Yeesaya yii: «Sii nì a-jipɔɔn Seeyaar-Yasuub ń nóó á cù kí ká ubɔti Akaasi. U bíń kunyiŋfuŋu kun bi cátì nnyim dì ki kóò dinyimbɔbil din bí yilpu púee kúntilaŋki, didandi din cá biwaŋfintiliibi kpaabunee watil pú.

english_verse: Tell Ahaz to stop worrying. There's no need for him to be afraid of King Rezin and King Pekah. They are very angry, but they are nothing more than a dying fire. Ahaz doesn't need to fear
translation_verse: Á tùkù-u yii: <Kàl̄ soooo, taa fàŋkì báà tiba. Taa yàntī diŋuul din uaranja Reesiin nì Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn gííyee ń bīil̀ a-pɔbil. Bi sá kii aŋmisaatee ali ŋin bí ki dùkù ŋŋminyiimee ní.

english_verse: to invade and defeat Judah and Jerusalem and to let the son of Tabeel be king in his place.
translation_verse: 'Tí cù kí já nì Juuda beel yab kí fàaǹ-bi. Tí páb́-bi bí kūtì ti-pu, ní tí dū Taabeel jipɔɔn kí kàan̄ dibeel bi-tiŋki pu.'

english_verse: I, the Lord, promise that this will never happen.
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī yii: 'Án kpá kí ŋá míǹ jaanjaan!

english_verse: Damascus is just the capital of Syria, and King Rezin rules only in Damascus. Samaria is just the capital of Israel, and King Pekah rules only in Samaria. But in less than
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim tiŋyil di sá Samaarii, ní Peekaa sá Samaarii bɔtiu. Ni yaa kaa máká ti-Dindaan pu, naa làá ŋmā kí yūĺ.>» Eemanuyeel daaŋku

english_verse: “Ask me for proof that my promise will come true. Ask for something to happen deep in the world of the dead or high in the heavens above.”
translation_verse: «Bàlifì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ú tīī-si kudaaŋŋu kubɔ. Kú nyānní taapu ditaŋkpiilin àá kutagbɔŋu yilpu.»

english_verse: Then I said: Listen, every one of you in the royal family of David. You have already tried my patience. Now you are trying God's patience by refusing to ask for proof.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yeesaya bí-u yii: «Pīlifìmaan, Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab. Kéè ni nyántì binib naŋki an kaa ŋmāntiǹ-ni ní ni là kí nyāntí man Nimbɔtiu mun naŋkaa!

english_verse: But the Lord will still give you proof. A virgin is pregnant; she will have a son and will name him Immanuel.
translation_verse: Too, ti-Dindaan u-ba làá tīī-ni kudaaŋŋu kubɔ. Usapɔɔnee làá dāá cáá dipool kí màal̀ kibininjabiki ní kí dāá pɔ̄-kì diyindi yii Eemanuyeel, taapu di sá yii <Unimbɔti bí ti-cee>.

english_verse: Even before the boy is old enough to know how to choose between right and wrong, he will eat yogurt and honey, and the countries of the two kings you fear will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī kibiki gbanti ń béé kí gàntī tin kaa ŋān̄ee nì tin ŋān̄eeyee, bibɔtiibi bili bin a fàŋkí nee nib làá dāá yīkì kí fá bi-timmu.

english_verse: But the Lord will make more trouble for your people and your kingdom than any of you have known since Israel broke away from Judah. He will even bring the king of Assyria to attack you. The Threat of an Invasion
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̄ sii nì a-nibul nì a-dicaŋkun yab pu nnaabu ŋun naa láá ká ki ká doooo ŋyunti ŋun ní Eefiraayiim beel cúu yākatì nì Juuda beelee. Asuur bɔtiu di làá dāá ŋá míǹ.» Binannanliibi làá lúuń-ni kí jī ni-tiŋki

english_verse: When that time comes, the Lord will whistle, and armies will come from Egypt like flies and from Assyria like bees.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá búń kiwulii kí yíiń isii in bíń laakin Niil mɔɔl cá ki kóò tiŋkunee, nì inaŋgbansii in bíń Asuur tiŋkinee.

english_verse: They will settle everywhere—in the deep valleys and between the rocks, on every thornbush and all over the pastureland.
translation_verse: I-kɔkɔ làá dāan̄ kí nákań nákań atantaka bɔbiliŋ poon, nì itaŋkpalɔkɔ poon, nì nsugboomu kɔkɔ pu, nì anyimbɔbil kɔkɔ poon.

english_verse: The Lord will pay the king of Assyria to bring a razor from across the Euphrates River and shave your head and every hair on your body, including your beard.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá fōoń bɔlfi Eefiraati mɔɔgbandi lapu pu yal cee. Asuur bɔtiu dee. U làá dāá kòol̀-ni abaakpan nì ni-wunti kɔkɔ kuti ki kpáaǹ ni-nyimpuliŋ.

english_verse: Anyone who is able to save only one young cow and two sheep,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, báà ŋma làá dāá pée kpàà unasal ubɔ nì iŋɔsal ili ja ní.

english_verse: will have enough milk to make yogurt. In fact, everyone left in the land will eat yogurt and honey.
translation_verse: I làá dāá tīī nnaabiim tikpil unil ń ká kí nyɔ̀. Bin kɔkɔ làá dāá kíń kitiŋ nee puee, nnaabiim nì tisiil ní bi dāa jīǹ.

english_verse: You will go there to hunt with your bow and arrows, because the whole country will be covered with thornbushes.
translation_verse: Bi dāa ŋúbiń butɔbu nì ipiin ní kí dāá kɔ́ bu-poon kí kpāŋkì, di sá yii kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ dāa kpántí ikuŋkum nì abɔjanaakun ŋma ní.

english_verse: The hills where you once planted crops will be overgrown with thorns and thistles. You will be afraid to go there, and your cattle, sheep, and goats will be turned loose on those hills.
translation_verse: Ikuŋkum nì abɔjanaakun puee, ubɔ kaa dāa gíti cá ŋgbantamu mun pu bi nìn kù nì akooyee. Mu làá dāá kpántí laakin bi dāa gbìntī inaa kí líí, ní ipii tɔ́ i-ba ki yìiǹee ní.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Isaiah, get something to write on. Then write in big clear letters the name, MAHER-SHALAL-HASH-BAZ.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Yòon̄ kupiliŋkpaaŋŋu kí ŋmà tibɔti nee ku-pu yii: <Makeer-Salaal-Aasi-Basi>, taapu di sá yii <Yáb́-tigaajati-malaa-difukuldi>.

english_verse: I will tell Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah to serve as witnesses to this.”
translation_verse: Ní m dūu dàkā binib bin pu bi cáá dimákalee seera. Bíǹ di sá usaraaŋal Uriya nì Yeebeereekiyawuu jipɔɔn Seekariyawuu.

english_verse: Sometime later, my wife and I had a son, and the Lord said, “Name him Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz.
translation_verse: Boonee ní man nì m-nimpuu un mun sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee kpáfì. Ní u cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii ḿ pɔ̄-kì diyindi yii <Makeer-Salaal-Aasi-Basi>.

english_verse: Because before he can say ‘Mommy’ or ‘Daddy,’ the king of Assyria will attack and take everything of value from Damascus and Samaria.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii, kí wàatī kibikee ń ŋmā kí lì yii m-baa àá m-nee, bi làá yòon̄ Damaasi tiŋkin gaajati nì tin kɔkɔ bi fúkúl̀ Samaarii tiŋkinee kí cùnnì kí bíĺ Asuur bɔtiu nimbiin.» Aram yab làá kpátí kí bìin̄ Juuda tiŋki pu

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me again and said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan fātìi gíti bí-mi yii:

english_verse: These people have refused the gentle waters of Shiloah and have gladly gone over to the side of King Rezin and King Pekah.
translation_verse: «Dinibul nee yíì Siiloowee nyim min pùub̀ sooooyee, ní ki fàal̄ Reesiin nì Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn pu.

english_verse: Now I will send the king of Assyria against them with his powerful army, which will attack like the mighty Euphrates River overflowing its banks.
translation_verse: An puee ti-Dindaan làá yàntī Eefiraati mɔɔkpaandi nyim min pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki wīikí tikpilee, an dàkà yii Asuur bɔtiu nì u-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu kɔkɔ ń dāá léeń bi-pu. Eefiraati mɔɔkpaandi nyim làá gbí kí jɔ̄m̀ kí páań.

english_verse: Enemy soldiers will cover Judah like a flood reaching up to your neck. But God is with us. He will spread his wings and protect our land.
translation_verse: Mì làá dāá bà Juuda beelin, kí gbí kí léeń kí jɔ̄m̀ kí tin sāā nneen. Mi-mɔɔgbaŋŋi làá wàan̄ kí jī a-tiŋki waaŋŋu kɔkɔ, Eemanuyeel.» Anibul ŋin kíǹee ŋáań fám ní

english_verse: All of you foreign nations, go ahead and prepare for war, but you will be crushed.
translation_verse: Anibul, nín̄ jìkìmaan nì tifaandi! Pīlifìmaan tiŋan, nimbi ndandati timmu yab. Báà ni yaa bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi, see bí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-ni! Tiŋman, báà ni yaa bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi, see bí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-ni!

english_verse: The Lord took hold of me with his powerful hand and said: I'm warning you! Don't act like these people.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan cúú-mi ní ki kpáafì-mi yii ḿ taa nóó nsan ŋun ní binib nee nóóyee. U lī-mi yii:

english_verse: Don't call something a rebellious plot, just because they do, and don't be afraid of something, just because they are.
translation_verse: «Binib nee yaa bíi bɔ́ntí kí ŋá tiŋyee, ní taa kūtì bi-pu. Ní taa fàŋkì tin bíǹ fàŋkée, ní taa pée fàŋkì-bi.»

english_verse: I am the one you should fear and respect. I am the holy God, the Lord All-Powerful!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan baba ní ni máaǹ kí yíiń circirdaan. Úǹ ní ni máaǹ kí nīn tɔ́, úǹ baba ní ni máaǹ kí fàŋkì.

english_verse: Run to me for protection. I am a rock that will make both Judah and Israel stumble and break their bones. I am a trap that will catch the people of Jerusalem—they will be captured and dragged away. Isaiah and His Followers
translation_verse: Binib tikpil làá dāá gbéetí, bi làá dāá lítí ní kí kɔ̄fì. Kutaliŋŋu làá dāá sàl̄-bi kí kíkí-bi. Yeesaya kā ki cí ki kpèé ti-Dindaan pú

english_verse: My message and my teachings are to be sealed and given to my followers.
translation_verse: M kpáafì tibɔti nee nì didàkal nee. M làá dū-tì kí dàkà m-boonnooliibi baba ní.

english_verse: Meanwhile, I patiently trust the Lord, even though he is no longer pleased with Israel.
translation_verse: M kā ki cí ti-Dindaan. U dá láá fātì u-boon ki tīī Jaakɔb naantiibi, ama m máká u-pu.

english_verse: My children and I are warning signs to Israel from the Lord All-Powerful, who lives on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: Man nì mbiyaamu mun ti-Dindaan tīī-mee sá kudaaŋŋu ní Isirayeel tiŋki poon. Timbi pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un kóò Siiyɔn jool puee dī ki kpáafì u-nibul.

english_verse: Someone may say to you, “Go to the fortunetellers who make soft chirping sounds or ask the spirits of the dead. After all, a nation ought to be able to ask its own gods
translation_verse: Biba làá lì-ni yii: «Ní cùú ká bin kàal̀ abɔɔjal ki yíì bitaŋkpiibee, bibɔɔbi bin kpántí nneen ki sòoǹ tin bí ki dòońee. An kítì yii dinibul ń bàlifì ditaŋgbandi, kí yíiń bitaŋkpiibi binifoobi puɔɔ!» Bi yaa lī-ni mimmee,

english_verse: what it should do.” None of those who talk like that will live to see the light of day!
translation_verse: ní kíí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan dàkal nì u-bɔti ní ni máaǹ kí pīlifì.» Un kamaa yaa kaa sòon̄ mimmee kaa làá ká ntaafaawalifi. Dibɔmbɔndi poon saŋkindi

english_verse: They will go around in great pain and will become so hungry that they will angrily curse their king and their gods. And when they try to find help in heaven
translation_verse: Binib làá dāá còom̀ kí jītí kitiŋ nee pu. Bi làá dāá gīī ŋkùm ń bà-bi. Ŋkùm nín làá dāá bà-bi puee, bi làá dāá nīn kíǹ ki tòó bi-bɔtiu nì bi-Nimbɔtiu mbusu. Bi làá dāá wáaǹ kí kpèè kutaa,

english_verse: and on earth, they will find only trouble and darkness, terrible trouble and deepest darkness.
translation_verse: kí dāá fàtīí kpèè kitiŋ. Kun bi làá dāá pée kée di sá dinimbinaamandi nì dibɔmbɔndi nì nnaabu nì kunyeeu kun bɔ̀ǹ kpìmmee.

english_verse: Those who walked in the dark have seen a bright light. And it shines upon everyone who lives in the land of darkest shadows.
translation_verse: A yāntì bi ká dipɔɔpiŋkpaandi, ki yāntì an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi tikpil. Bi bí ki fàal̀ a-nimbiin kii bi nín yaa bíi cēē bi-kpaajinti bi fàal̀ puee, ní ki kūuntí nì ifaal kii bi bíi yàkatī tin bi jáń ki fōō kujaaunee.

english_verse: Our Lord, you have made your nation stronger. Because of you, its people are glad and celebrate like workers at harvest time or like soldiers dividing up what they have taken.
translation_verse: Di sá yii a túutì-bi diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ bi nìn túee, ki kɔ́fì ndɔ ŋun nìn pá bi-gbigbipati puee nì ditambɔndi din utɔntɔŋkpil nìn ŋúb́ bi-puee, kii a nín nìn ŋá pu ŋwiin ŋun a nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Madiyan yabee.

english_verse: You have broken the power of those who abused and enslaved your people. You have rescued them just as you saved your people from Midian.
translation_verse: Anaataka ŋin bi nìn táká ki tà kitiŋ cìŋkēe, nì bi-bɔkutikpaaŋŋi ŋin nìn máǹ fatikuee kɔkɔ làá fōō ŋŋmi kí wà.

english_verse: and all of them knew it, including everyone in the capital city of Samaria. But they were proud and stubborn and said,
translation_verse: «Ti-diiŋŋi ŋin ti máń nì brikisibee lítì, ama timbi làá dū ataŋkpee ŋin bi kpítèe ní kí fàtīí mā-ŋi. Bi gāatì ti-siikoomɔɔr sufii, ama timbi làá cóoń seedir sufii kí téeǹ.»

english_verse: “Houses of brick and sycamore have fallen to the ground, but we will build houses with stones and cedar.”
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan dū Reesiin nannanliibi ki tɔ́ Isirayeel yab pu. U tīī bi-nannanliibi kunyannyaau.

english_verse: He sent the Arameans from the east and the Philistines from the west, and they swallowed up Israel. But even this did not stop him from being angry, so he kept on punishing them.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Isirayeel nibul kaa fātìi gítì un di bíi dátí bi-tafalee cee, baa nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan.

english_verse: The people of Israel still did not turn back to the Lord All-Powerful and worship him.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, ŋwimbaanti ní ti-Dindaan làá gāā kí tìl̄ Isirayeel tiŋki yil nì ki-juul, kukpakpaliu nì kukaluu.

english_verse: In one day he cut off their head and tail, their leaves and branches.
translation_verse: Bitindaŋkpilib nì akpambal di sá diyil, ní inyimɔn bɔnaatiliibi sá dijuul.

english_verse: Their rulers and leaders were the head, and the lying prophets were the tail.
translation_verse: Dinibul nee kpootiliibi yāntì bi wáŋkì, ní binib bin bi kpòotēe yīntì nsan.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with his people and kept punishing them, because they had turned against him. They were evil and spoke foolishly. That's why he did not have pity on their young people or on their widows and orphans.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ntoom fòol̄ kii ŋŋmee, ki wù ikuŋkum nì abɔjanaakun, ki wù nsugboomu kubambaŋŋun, ní ŋu-nyiim yíkí ki jɔ́ḿ kutaa.

english_verse: Evil had spread like a raging forest fire sending thornbushes up in smoke.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan ŋuukpaandi puee, kitiŋ nee fōō ŋŋmi. An bí kii ŋŋmi bíi wù dinibulee. Ubɔ kaa ti sūǹ u-nabiki saai.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful was angry and used the people as fuel for a fire that scorched the land. They turned against each other
translation_verse: Unil fàtī ŋgiil pú kí gíí kí jī ama ní ŋkùm dáá gbíntìi cáá-u, ní kí fàtī ŋgan pú kí gíí kí ŋmɔ́ ama ní kaa díkì. Báà ŋma gífí u-ba ŋal nanti ki ŋmóò.

english_verse: You people are in for trouble! You have made cruel and unfair laws
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí binib bin yōontí marab bin kaa bí deedeeyee, binib bin ŋmà marab bin kɔ̄ntí bi-jutiibi falaayee ki yōontée.

english_verse: that let you cheat the poor and needy and rob widows and orphans.
translation_verse: Baa tìì biwɔfib dinyɔɔbundi ibɔsoon laŋki ki ŋmìntī m-nibul nandambi tin sá bi-yatee. Bi fìkì bikpiipoobi, ki fúkuĺ ataŋkpiibil wanti.

english_verse: But what will you do when you are fiercely attacked and punished by foreigners? Where will you run for help? Where will you hide your valuables?
translation_verse: Mimmee ditafadaaldi wiiŋŋu dal, ni yaa láa ká kubuŋkpaaŋŋu páaǹnée, ni làá dāá nín ŋá mana dee? Ŋma ní ni làá dāá sāǹ kí kɔ́ kí ká dijòońdi dee? La ní ni làá dāá yóoń ni-gaajati dee?

english_verse: How will you escape being captured or killed? The Lord is still angry, and he isn't through with you yet! The Lord's Purpose and the King of Assyria
translation_verse: Kun ni dāa pée ŋūǹ kí ŋée di sá ní nīn bōō bisarkadambi kansikin, àá ní lítí kí nīn dɔ̄ anikpil kansikin. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ti-Dindaan ŋuul kaa sɔ̄ŋkì, u-ŋuul dáá gbíntìi dàn̄ bi-pu. Asuur yab kpitii jítì mara pu

english_verse: The Lord says: I am furious! And I will use the king of Assyria as a club
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí Asuur tiŋki kin sá m-ŋuul bambaaŋŋuee. Ndɔ ŋun kā u-ŋaan nee ní m làá dūú dàkà m-bum.

english_verse: to beat down you godless people. I am angry with you, and I will send him to attack you. He will take what he wants and walk on you like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: M dū-kì ki tú kí cùú já nì ditimbundi din kaa dū Unimbɔti ki yíiń tibee. M tīī-kì ditundi kí cùú já nì dinibul din gbítí m-ŋuulee, kí fūkul̀-kì kí kóoǹ ki-gaajawanti, kí tāā-kì kii didandi pu kpatee.

english_verse: He has even bigger plans in mind, because he wants to destroy many nations.
translation_verse: Ama Asuur tiŋki kíǹ kaa dàkafī míǹ, ki-landɔkɔŋu nyáń ŋu-ba. Di sá yii kíǹ pée dàkafī dinàandi pu ní, kí kúntí atimbun tikpil tikpil.

english_verse: The king of Assyria says: My army commanders are kings!
translation_verse: Kì lì yii: <M-janjakpilib kɔkɔ kaa sá bibɔtiibi níii?

english_verse: The gods of Jerusalem and Samaria are weaker than the gods of those powerful nations. And I will destroy Jerusalem, together with its gods and idols, just as I did Samaria.
translation_verse: M nín ŋá Samaarii nì ki-waaŋi pu nee, maa làá ŋmā kí ŋá Jeerusaleem nì ki-waaŋi mimmaaa?>»

english_verse: The Lord will do what he has planned against Jerusalem and Mount Zion. Then he will punish the proud and boastful king of Assyria,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yaa láa dóò ditundi din u cáá kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì Siiyɔn jool puee, u làá dāá dáaĺ Asuur bɔtiu tafal u nín cáá dilambil ki dàkà u-bee pu.

english_verse: who says: I did these things by my own power because I am smart and clever. I attacked kings like a wild bull, and I took the land and the treasures of their nations.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ubɔti gbanti lī yii: «An sá m-ŋal pɔŋŋu nì m-ciiŋyi pu ní m ŋá tin bí nee kɔkɔ, kun puee man cáá dinyil ní. M kpītì ŋkpaanyɔmu mun nìn bí anibul kansikinee, ki fúkúl̀ bi-wanti tin bi kpáafèe. M kpákatì bi-bɔtiibi bi-beeŋi pu kii ubaatandaanee ní.

english_verse: I have conquered the whole world! And it was easier than taking eggs from an unguarded nest. No one even flapped a wing or made a peep.
translation_verse: Kii unil nín dàatī u-ŋal kí páatí kunɔndii puee, míǹ ní m kóoǹ anibul gaajati. Kii bi nín wúkutí ajin ŋin unoon yíkìi fée puee, míǹ ní m kóoǹ tiwan kɔkɔ kitiŋ pu, ní báà unil kaa cīŋkì u-baaa, kaa wāaǹ kinyɔkɔ ní kaa nín múlifì.»

english_verse: King of Assyria, can an ax or a saw overpower the one who uses it? Can a wooden pole lift whoever holds it?
translation_verse: Kicɔkɔ mun ŋūǹ kí dàkà ki-ba un di ŋúb́-kì ki cáa gàatēe ceeee? Kijiseekikaai ŋūǹ kí gúntí ki-ba un cáá-kì ki tūǹ ditundee puɔɔɔ? Mbambaan kaa ŋūǹ kí fíiǹ un ŋúb́-ŋuee ŋal, míǹ ní ndɔ kaa tí ŋūǹ kí dúkutí un ŋúb́-ŋuee ŋal.

english_verse: The mighty Lord All-Powerful will send a terrible disease to strike down your army, and you will burn with fever under your royal robes.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá yàntī u-nib bin gbìfèe ń dúntí. Ŋŋmi làá pōō u-nyooti taapu.

english_verse: The holy God, who is the light of Israel, will turn into a fire, and in one day you will go up in flames, just like a thornbush.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan un sá Isirayeel tiŋki walifiŋuee làá kpántí kii ŋŋmee ní, circir Nimbɔtiu ŋmilimbiliŋ kí fōō ikuŋkum nì abɔjanaakun, kí wà kɔkɔ múb ŋwimbaanti.

english_verse: The Lord will make your beautiful forests and fertile fields slowly rot.
translation_verse: U làá wà kí bīil̀ u-bambannyaaŋku nì u-subiŋmɔkaaŋi kpaabu kɔkɔ. U làá dāá nīn náań nì unil un iween ŋmɔ́ ki bíil̀ee ní.

english_verse: There will be so few trees that even a young child can count them. Only a Few Will Come Back
translation_verse: Án làá dāá pée kíń isufi fiii yéè ní Asuur bambaŋkun áli gba campɔnti dāa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ-i. Isirayeel yab biba làá dāá kíń

english_verse: A time is coming when the survivors from Israel and Judah will completely depend on the holy Lord of Israel, instead of the nation that defeated them.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Isirayeel yab bin làá dāá nīn bí dimaŋfalinee, Jaakɔb nibul bin làá dāá kíńee kaa dāa gíti cɔ́tí un di bí ki gbáà-bee pu. Bi làá dāá nīn kíǹ ki cɔ́tí ti-Dindaan pu, Isirayeel circir Nimbɔtiu pu ní.

english_verse: There were as many people as there are grains of sand along the seashore, but only a few will survive to come back to Israel's mighty God. This is because he has threatened to destroy their nation, just as they deserve.
translation_verse: Isirayeel, báà a-naantiibi yaa wīikí kii dibul din dɔ̄ tiŋku gbandee, bi-kansikin biba di làá fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan cee. Ti-Dindaan nín lēē ki síiǹ yii u làá nàan̄-kèe, see ú ŋá míǹ, ní deedee ń dāá gbí kitiŋ pu kii mbunee.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has promised that everyone on this earth will be punished.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ ki yóoǹ pu yii u làá nàan̄ kitiŋ kɔkɔee, see u nāaǹ-kì. Ní taa fàŋkìmaan Asuur yab

english_verse: Now the Lord God All-Powerful says to his people in Jerusalem: The Assyrians will beat you with sticks and abuse you, just as the Egyptians did. But don't be afraid of them.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan lī yii: «M-nibul yab bin kóò Siiyɔn jool puee, ní taa fàŋkì Asuur yab bin ŋúb́ mbambaan ki gbáà-ni, ki ŋúb́ ni-boon ndɔ kii Eejipiti yab nín nìn ŋáań-ni pu dooooyee.

english_verse: Soon I will stop being angry with you, and I will punish them for their crimes.
translation_verse: Ama an kíǹ ŋyunti fiii nàanyɔkɔ diŋuul din m gíí ni-puee ń sɔ̀ŋkì ní ḿ fōō Asuur yab pu mbum kí nàan̄-bi.»

english_verse: I will beat the Assyrians with a whip, as I did the people of Midian near the rock at Oreb. And I will show the same mighty power that I used when I made a path through the sea in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá dúkutí u-bambaaŋŋu kí fáá Asuur yab kii u nín nìn fáá Madiyan yab pu Ooreeb jool puee, ní kí tàntī u-kpandɔŋu dimɔɔl pu kii u nín nìn ŋá pu Eejipitee.

english_verse: Then they will no longer rule your nation. All will go well for you, and your burden will be lifted.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, u làá dāá páatí diwaŋgul din pá ni-gbigbipati puee, ní kí túutí-ni ditúndi din u túǹ-ni ni-silii gīīyee. Diwaŋgul làá dāá wāŋkì ní án bútí-ni. Binannanliibi tóobiń Jeerusaleem tiŋki Unannanli nín jɔ́ḿ Samaarii tiŋkin,

english_verse: Enemy troops have reached the town of Aiath. They have gone through Migron, and they stored their supplies at Michmash,
translation_verse: bi bāań Ayaati tiŋkin. Bi cōom̀ ki jítì Miigirɔn tiŋki pu, ní ki cáá bi-wanti ki yóoǹ Miikimaasi tiŋkin.

english_verse: before crossing the valley and spending the night at Geba. The people of Ramah are terrified; everyone in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, has run away.
translation_verse: Bi cōom̀ ki jítì ntaŋkpafaŋfakamin ki bí yii: «Tí gbíntí kí dòom̄maan Geeba tiŋkin.» Niinee dinyoondi kɔ́ Raama tiŋkin yab, ní binib bin kóò Giibeeya, Sayuul tiŋkinee sáǹ ki kátì.

english_verse: Loud crying can be heard in the towns of Gallim, Laishah, and sorrowful Anathoth.
translation_verse: Galiim tiŋkin yab, nín̄ tátímaan! Layiisa tiŋkin yab, ní pīlifì. Anatooti yab gbí isaa!

english_verse: No one is left in Madmenah or Gebim.
translation_verse: Madimeena tiŋki yab bíi sáń kí ŋmátí, ní bin kóò Geebiim tiŋkinee bíi nyàab̀ kibalilaŋ.

english_verse: Today the enemy will camp at Nob and shake a threatening fist at Mount Zion in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee binannanliibi làá dāá yūĺ Noob tiŋkin, ní ki dāa sòoǹ ki dàkà Siiyɔn jool, Jeerusaleem gbantaŋki ŋŋal.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will use his fearsome might to bring down the tallest trees and chop off every branch.
translation_verse: Kpèè, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan di kɔ́fí asupan nì mpɔnee. U gāatì isukpaan ki lúkufì, isufi in fɔ̀kɔ̀ee dɔ̄ kitiŋ.

english_verse: With an ax, the glorious Lord will destroy every tree in the forests of Lebanon.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dāá dū kicɔkɔ kí gàatì kubambaŋŋun sugboomu, ní Leebanɔn seedir sufii in ŋān̄ee lítì ki dɔ̄ kitiŋ.

english_verse: Like a branch that sprouts from a stump, someone from David's family will someday be king.
translation_verse: Disubambil diba làá dāá kpìtī Jeesee sunyeel pu, disupɔmbil diba làá cɔ́tí u-nyaaŋyi pu.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will be with him to give him understanding, wisdom, and insight. He will be powerful, and he will know and honor the Lord.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Fam làá dāá nīn bí u-pu. Mì làá dāá tīī-u iciin nì mpɔn ú gàntī tin ŋān̄ee nì tin kaa ŋān̄ee. Mì làá dāá tīī-u isaŋki nì dibaatandi. Mì làá dāá yàntī ú béé ti-Dindaan kí nīn fàŋkí-u.

english_verse: His greatest joy will be to obey the Lord. This king won't judge by appearances or listen to rumors.
translation_verse: Kun dāa mɔ̄ǹ-uee di sá ú nīn fàŋkí ti-Dindaan. Waa làá kpèè unil nimbiin ní kí sòoǹ u-bɔti, kaa làá tí pīlifì tin binib sòoǹee ní kí sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì tibɔti.

english_verse: The poor and the needy will be treated with fairness and with justice. His word will be law everywhere in the land, and criminals will be put to death.
translation_verse: U làá dāá sòoǹ binandambi bɔti nì deedee, ní kí dāá sòoǹ kitiŋ nee pu wɔfib bɔti nì ibaamɔn. U-nyɔɔbundi dāa gbáà kitiŋ nee pu nib kii mbambaanee ní, ní tibɔti tin dāa nyēē u-nyɔkɔnee dāa kù bin sá bitɔŋfitiibee.

english_verse: Honesty and fairness will be his royal robes.
translation_verse: Deedee di làá dāá nīn sá-u dambala, ní ibaamɔn dāa sá-u gbaja u gbìn̄ u-caŋ.

english_verse: Leopards will lie down with young goats, and wolves will rest with lambs. Calves and lions will eat together and be cared for by little children.
translation_verse: Sinsiŋku nì dipibil di dāa kóò dicilpu, ní ugbii ń dāá dòon̄ kí kɔ́ĺ kiŋɔbiki. Dinabil nì digbikintipɔmbil dāa kpáfí dibɔɔbaantiil ki jīǹ, ní kinaacimpɔmbiki dāa kpàá bi-kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Cows and bears will share the same pasture; their young will rest side by side. Lions and oxen will both eat straw.
translation_verse: Unasal nì digbiŋgbil dāa pēē kunaakpaapɔɔu, ní bi-biyaamu dāa pēē ŋkɔŋkoon. Gbikinti dāa ŋmóò timool kii unaayee ní.

english_verse: Little children will play near snake holes. They will stick their hands into dens of poisonous snakes and never be hurt.
translation_verse: Kibipɔŋ dāa kā ukoobu faliŋu pu ki gbíiĺ, ní campɔnti ń dāá dū u-ŋal kí bɔ̄ ukoowaati faliŋun.

english_verse: Nothing harmful will take place on the Lord's holy mountain. Just as water fills the sea, the land will be filled with people who know and honor the Lord. God's People Will Come Back Home
translation_verse: Baa dāa gíti ŋáań tikpitil, kaa dāa gíti bíiĺ tiba ti-Dindaan circir jool kɔkɔ pu, kun puee bi làá dāá béé ti-Dindaan kitiŋee kɔkɔ pu kii nnyim nín gbéè tiŋku puee.

english_verse: The time is coming when one of David's descendants will be the signal for the people of all nations to come together. They will follow his advice, and his own nation will become famous.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, Jeesee naantiiu di dāa sá kudaaŋŋu ki tīī duulinya nibuliŋ kɔkɔ. Atimbun kɔkɔ làá dāá nyàab̀-u, ní laakin u dāa bée, tinyool làá dāá nīn jìliŋkī. Bin bínní kuyuŋuee gítintam

english_verse: When that day comes, the Lord will again reach out his mighty arm and bring home his people who have survived in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Ethiopia, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the land along the coast.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá tàntī u-ŋal nliliitiim kí fīī u-nib bin kíǹee kí líí. An dàkà yii bin ŋmátì ki bíń Asuur tiŋki nì Eejipiti tiŋki nì Paatroosi tiŋki nì Kuusi tiŋki nì Eelaam tiŋki nì Sineeyaar tiŋki nì Amaati tiŋki nì ntimu mun ní tiŋku māntìi túee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: He will give a signal to the nations, and he will bring together the refugees from Judah and Israel, who have been scattered all over the earth.
translation_verse: U làá dāá tīī atimbun kɔkɔ kudaaŋŋu, kí kpāafì-ŋi yii u làá fàtīí kóoǹní Isirayeel yab bin bi cūnnì kuyuŋuee, kí kpāfì Juuda naakookun yab bin kpátìi gbí duulinya jaaŋŋi kɔkɔnee.

english_verse: Instead, they will get together and attack the Philistines in the west. Then they will defeat the Edomites, the Moabites, and the Ammonites in the east. They will rule those people and take from them whatever they want.
translation_verse: Bi làá lúuń Fiiliistii yab ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú, kí kpāfì kí fūkul̀ bin kóò ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. Bi làá dāá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Eedoom nì Moowaab yab, ní Amɔn yab ń dāá nīn bí bi-taapu.

english_verse: The Lord will dry up the arm of the Red Sea near Egypt, and he will send a scorching wind to divide the Euphrates River into seven streams that anyone can step across.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī Eejipiti mɔɔl ń kpā, kí dàkà Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋŋal kí kpàtī di-pu. U làá púfí di-pu kí cúú-dì kí yàkatī abuntaa aluli, ní unil dāa ŋūǹ kí táká anaataka kí dùtī.

english_verse: Then for his people who survive, there will be a good road from Assyria, just as there was a good road for their ancestors when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Didandi dāa bí u-nibul din kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin Asuur tiŋkinee ń dī. Án dāa bí kii bi-naanjab nín nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin puee ní.

english_verse: At that time you will say, “I thank you, Lord! You were angry with me, but you stopped being angry and gave me comfort.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, sii dinibul din ká difiilee làá dāá lì yii: «M nyɔ́ŋkí-si, ti-Dindaan! Di sá yii a nìn gíí m-pu diŋuul, ama ní a-ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkì m-pu ní a sɔ̄ŋkì m-pɔbil.

english_verse: I trust you to save me, Lord God, and I won't be afraid. My power and my strength come from you, and you have saved me.”
translation_verse: Kpèè Unimbɔti di fīī-mi, m cáá dimákal ní kaa ti fàŋkí. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di sá m-pɔŋŋu nì m-laŋŋu. Úǹ di sá m-fiiliu.»

english_verse: With great joy, you people will get water from the well of victory.
translation_verse: Ni làá dāá lúń nnyim difiil nyimbulii poon nì dipɔɔpindi.

english_verse: At that time you will say, “Our Lord, we are thankful, and we worship only you. We will tell the nations how glorious you are and what you have done.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, ni làá dāá lì yii: «Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan! Ní sòoǹ mpɔn kí dàkà u nín sá uŋyee. Ní yàntī anibul kɔkɔ ń béé u-tuŋkpaaŋŋi. Māafìmaan kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ min ní u-yindi sá dikpaandee.

english_verse: Because of your wonderful deeds we will sing your praises everywhere on earth.”
translation_verse: Gāāmaan ilan kí pàkà ti-Dindaan, di sá yii u túń atuŋkpaŋkpaan. Ní yàntī duulinya kɔkɔ ń béé ŋi-pu!»

english_verse: Sing, people of Zion! Celebrate the greatness of the holy Lord of Israel. God is here to help you.
translation_verse: Sii un kóò Siiyɔn jool puee, fáá ŋwiliili nì dipɔɔpindi kí nīn nyàkantī, di sá yii Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un bí a-cee ki bí circiree, sá ukpaan ní!

english_verse: This is the message that I was given about Babylon:
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Babiloon tiŋki pu ní Amɔtisi jipɔɔn Yeesaya ká dileedakal poonee sèé.

english_verse: From high on a barren hill give a signal, shout the orders, and point the way to enter the gates of Babylon's proud rulers.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ní cóoḿmaan kudaaŋŋu ŋaabiki dijool din kūń isufi nì timool kpée yilpu. Ní kúum̀maan mpɔn kí yíiń bijanjaliibi. Ní kábitiń-bi bí dī akpambal punyɔmmu pu kí kɔ́.

english_verse: The Lord has commanded his very best warriors and his proud heroes to show how angry he is.
translation_verse: M tīī binib bin dū bi-ba ki sú-mee mara. M yíiń m-janjaliibi bin sá bimɔntiibee, bin di fàal̀ m-jajil puee, bí dāan̄ kí lēē m-ŋuul kí dàkà.»

english_verse: Listen to the noisy crowds on the mountains! Kingdoms and nations are joining forces. The Lord All-Powerful is bringing together an army for battle.
translation_verse: Ní pīlifì kuwoou nín gàń ajoon pu puee, a lì kii dinikitikpaandi di bí ki wòoǹee. Ní pīlifì an nín tùm̀ pu dàii abee poonee, anibul ŋin kóoǹ ki kpáfèe kansikinee. An sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di bí ki kpèé bijanjaliibi bin làá cù kujaauee.

english_verse: From a distant land the Lord is coming fierce and furious— he brings his weapons to destroy the whole earth.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nì bin làá lēē u-ŋuul kí dàkèe nyánní ndandati, kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ. Bi làá nàan̄ kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Cry and weep! The day is coming when the mighty Lord will bring destruction. *
translation_verse: Nín̄ sūm̀maan ki yáliŋkí, kun puee ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu tóobiń! Ŋu dòoń kí nàan̄ tikɔkɔ, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan di túnní-ŋu.

english_verse: All people will be terrified. Hands will grow limp; courage will melt away.
translation_verse: An pu ní binib kɔkɔ ŋalii jòon̄, tiwun yɔ̄tì.

english_verse: Everyone will tremble with pain like a woman giving birth; they will stare at each other with horror on their faces. There Will Be No Mercy
translation_verse: Dinyoondi làá kɔ́-bi ní iwàlfi nì ŋwunnyaŋfi ń cúú-bi. Bi làá nīn bí ki yáliŋkí nì bi-ba, kii upɔdaan di kā imatiŋween puee. Bi làá nīn kíǹ ki kpèé tɔb nì bitii, ní bi-nimbiliŋ ń mántí cínciŋ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will show no mercy or pity when that time comes. In my anger I will destroy the earth and every sinner who lives on it.
translation_verse: Kpèè, ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu di dòońee, ŋwiin ŋun disaasɔl kaa dāa bée, ŋwiin ŋun di sá u-ŋuukpaandi wiiŋŋuee. U làá dāá yàntī kitiŋ ń kpántí kuteeu, kí dāá céetí bikpitiŋaliibi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Light will disappear from the stars in the sky; the dawning sun will turn dark, and the moon will lose its brightness.
translation_verse: Iŋmalbijaa nín kpáfì kpáfì pu ki bí yilpuee kaa làá ti nín̄ wāĺ. Ŋwìiń tin lì yii ŋu nyēēyee, an fātìi bɔ̄ntì, ní uŋmal mun kaa dāa gíti pīiǹ.

english_verse: I will punish this evil world and its people because of their sins. I will crush the horrible pride of those who are cruel.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá dáaĺ duulinya nib tafal bi-tuŋkpitiŋ pu, m làá dáaĺ binikpitib tafal bi-kpitii pu. M làá kúntí bin dàkà bi-bee bi-lambil pu, kí sìntī bin tɔ́kɔ́ bi-jutiibi puee taapu.

english_verse: Survivors will be harder to find than the purest gold.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī binifoobi ń taa ti nín̄ gbōō kii sindaariyamɔntee, ń taa ti nín̄ gbōō kii Oofiiri tiŋkin sindaariyauee.»

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, am terribly angry— I will make the sky tremble and the earth shake loose.
translation_verse: M làá cìŋkì yilpu ní kitiŋ nyeel ń jìkì màkà maka, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan ŋuul pu, ŋwiin ŋun dì làá fōō lìblib kii ŋŋmee pu.

english_verse: Everyone will run to their homelands, just as hunted deer run, and sheep scatter when they have no shepherd.
translation_verse: Niinee, kii upeeman un bi bíi jèe, àá ipii in kaa cáá upikpaalee nín sáń puee, míǹ ní báà ŋma làá dāá sāǹ kí gítí u-nibul cee, báà ŋma làá dāá gítí u-tiŋki pu.

english_verse: They will see their children beaten against rocks, their homes robbed, and their wives abused.
translation_verse: Bi-nimbilaaliyin ní bi làá dāá tāā kí mátí bi-biyaamu, kí dāá fūkul̀ bi-wanti tin bí bi-diiŋŋinee, kí dāá cūtì bi-nimpoobi mpɔn kí dòon̄ nì bi.

english_verse: The Medes can't be bought off with silver or gold, and I'm sending them to attack Babylonia.
translation_verse: M làá lùkutī Meedeesi yab kí dū-bi kí tɔ̄ bi-pu. Binib gbanti tafal kpá nì animbil, áli gba bi kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ sindaariya ní.

english_verse: Their arrows will slaughter the young men; no pity will be shown to babies and children. The Lord Will Destroy Babylon
translation_verse: Bi làá tɔ̄ binaacimpɔmbi ipiin kí kpɔ̀, kaa làá gàntī mbipɔmu, kaa làá sɔ̄ mbiyaawaamu mun saai.

english_verse: The city of Babylon is glorious and powerful, the pride of the nation. But it will be like the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah after I, the Lord, destroyed them.
translation_verse: Babiloon tiŋki kin di ŋān̄ abee kansikinee, kitiŋ kin di ŋān̄ Kaaldee yab cee kii dibeedimbilee làá kpántí kii Soodoom nì Goomoora timmu mun Unimbɔti nìn nāaǹee ní.

english_verse: Only desert creatures, hoot owls, and ostriches will live in its ruins, and goats will leap about.
translation_verse: Ilambunti di dāa kíǹ ki kóò kitiŋ gbantin, ní atulinjoo ń dāá gbí ki-diiŋŋin. Kì làá dāá kpántí laakin taataabi kóòyee, ní iŋɔjaa dāa yùkufī ki-digbuŋŋi pu.

english_verse: Hyenas and wolves will howl from Babylon's fortresses and beautiful palaces. Its time is almost up!
translation_verse: Isaakpan dāa kpátí kí gbí ki-dikpaaŋŋi poon, ní sinsiŋkub ń gbí ki-beeciŋŋi amɔntee poon. Babiloon tiŋki kúntitam tóobiń, an bāań gba, báà ŋwimbaanti kaa làá gbéeǹ.

english_verse: The Lord will have mercy on Israel and will let them be his chosen people once again. He will bring them back to their own land, and foreigners will join them as part of Israel.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá sɔ̄ Jaakɔb naantiibi saai. U làá fàtīí lēē Isirayeel nibul dí nīn sá u-yal. U làá fàtīí kàan̄-bi bi-tiŋki pu. Binicambi làá kūtì bi-pu ní bi nì Jaakɔb naantiibi ń ŋá ubaanti.

english_verse: Other nations will lead them home, and Israel will make slaves of them in the land that belongs to the Lord. Israel will rule over those who once governed and mistreated them. Death to the King of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Anibul aba làá dāá yòon̄ní Isirayeel yab kí fàtīí gíiǹní bi-tiŋki pu. Ti-Dindaan tiŋki pu niinee, Isirayeel yab làá dāá dū binicambi gbanti, bininjab nì binimpoobi kɔkɔ kí kpántí bi-yumbui. Bi làá dāá cúú binib bin nìn cúú-bi kuyuŋuee kuyuŋu. Bin nìn wɔ́b́-bee làá dāá nīn kíǹ ki bí bi-taapu. Babiloon bɔtiu kpiisilaŋŋu

english_verse: The Lord will set you free from your sorrow, suffering, and slavery.
translation_verse: Isirayeel nibul, a-gìńdi nì a-yaliŋkii nì kuyuŋu kun bi cúú-see boonee, ti-Dindaan làá tīī-si diŋuŋfil.

english_verse: Then you will make fun of the King of Babylonia by singing this song: That cruel monster is done for! He won't attack us again.
translation_verse: Niinee a dāa gà nlan nee kí bèel̀ Babiloon bɔtiu yii: «An kúntiǹ uwɔ́bilee mana ní? U-lambilee bí la ní?

english_verse: The Lord has crushed the power of those evil kings,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan cúú bitɔŋfitiibi tambɔndi ki gíì, u cúú biwɔ́biliibi kpandɔŋu ki kɔ́fì.

english_verse: Now all the world is at peace; its people are celebrating with joyful songs.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee kitiŋ kɔkɔ ŋūŋfì ki ká dipɔɔsɔŋkil. Báà ŋma kíǹ ki fàal̀.

english_verse: King of Babylonia, even the cypress trees and the cedars of Lebanon celebrate and say, “Since you were put down, no one comes along to chop us down.”
translation_verse: A-puee, ki kpáaǹ siipreesi sufii bí ifaal poon, ní a nín lítì ki dɔ̄ee, Leebanɔn seedir sufii lì yii: <Un nìn jɔ́miń ki gàatī-tee kaa ti làá jɔ̄mìń.>»

english_verse: The world of the dead eagerly waits for you. With great excitement, the spirits of ancient rulers hear about your coming.
translation_verse: Taapu taŋkpiilin yab nín gbìl̄ yii a dòońee, ní bi bí ki bɔ́ntí bi-ba ki cí yii á dāan̄. A-puee bi fīkitì bitaŋkpiibi bin nìn sá bikpaambi kitiŋ puee, ní ki yāntì atimbun kɔkɔ bɔtiibi yíkì bi-beejaliŋ pu ki yúl̀ a-pu.

english_verse: Each one of them will say, “Now you are just as weak as any of us!
translation_verse: Bi-kɔkɔ làá sòoǹ kí lì yii: «Si mun kaa ti cáá mpɔn kii timbee dee, ti nì si ŋá ubaanti dee!»

english_verse: Your pride and your music have ended here in the world of the dead. Worms are your blanket, maggots are your bed.”
translation_verse: Bi bíi bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati ní ki téé a-kpaanti ki tɔ́ ditaŋkpiilin. Akoosibil di kíǹ ki sá-si kilambaŋ, ní ijiliŋkpaam sá-si satabiiŋkaa.

english_verse: You, the bright morning star, have fallen from the sky! You brought down other nations; now you are brought down.
translation_verse: Sii utaafaaŋmalbija un wāĺ kílkilee, an dī mana ní a nyánní yilpu ki lítìń ní? Sii un nìn jáà ki pɔ́ɔkíǹ atimbunee, an dī mana ní bi téé-si ki lúkú míǹ?

english_verse: You said to yourself, “I'll climb to heaven and place my throne above the highest stars. I'll sit there with the gods far away in the north.
translation_verse: A nìn bí ki lì a-ban yii: «Man làá jɔ̄m̀ kutaa pu, m làá jɔ̄ntiǹ m-beejal yilpu kí nīn bí Unimbɔti ŋmalbijaai yilpu. M làá kàl̄ dibeel dijool yilpu, laakin ní inimbɔti kàal̀ ki kpáfí, ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kúntilaŋkee.

english_verse: I'll be above the clouds, just like God Most High.”
translation_verse: M làá jɔ̄m̀ atagban yilpu kúntí kunti, m làá nīn bí kii Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiuee ní.»

english_verse: But now you are deep in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Ama a sīntì ki bàn̄ ditaŋkpiilin, kubookpaaŋŋu taapu taapu.

english_verse: Those who see you will stare and wonder, “Is this the man who made the world tremble and shook up kingdoms?
translation_verse: Bin ká-see kpèé-si dímmm ní ki lì yii: «Mimmee unil un nìn yàntī kitiŋ pu nib jìkì, ní abee cìŋkēe sèéee?

english_verse: Did he capture every city and make earth a desert? Is he the one who refused to let prisoners go home?”
translation_verse: Úǹ di kaa nìn nàantí ntimu, ki nìn yàntī kitiŋ kpántí kuteeu kaa líikí bisarkadambeeee?»

english_verse: When kings die, they are buried in glorious tombs.
translation_verse: Atimbun bɔtiibi kɔkɔ yaa kpíìyee, báà ŋma dɔ̀ u-kaakulin nì tinyool ní kí ŋùŋfì.

english_verse: But you will be left unburied, just another dead body lying underfoot like a broken branch. You will be one of many killed in battle and gone down to the deep rocky pit.
translation_verse: Ama siiyee, bi dū-si ki fá, kaa síb́-si a-kaakulin. A bí kii kibiki kin bi màl̄ kaa yōoǹ kì dɔ̄ kaa bí ŋkpèéyee ní. A dɔ̄ binib bin bi kūūyee nyìkī a-pu. Bi dū kitàataajiki ki sāatì ki cífì cífì-si, ki téé-si ki tɔ́ kubookpaaŋŋun ataŋkpee pu, kii dinikpil din dɔ̄ binib tà ki jītée.

english_verse: You won't be buried with kings; you ruined your country and murdered your people. You evil monster! We hope that your family will be forgotten forever.
translation_verse: Baa làá kpāfì sii nì bi kuceeu, kun puee a nāaǹ a-tiŋki, ní ki kūū sisi a-ba nibul. Dalba dalba baa làá ti pútí a-nibooliŋu binikpitib nee yindi.

english_verse: We will slaughter your sons to make them pay for the crimes of their ancestors. They won't take over the world or build cities anywhere on this earth.
translation_verse: Ní bɔ́ntí kí kpɔ̀ mbininjabiyaamu inikpiti in mu-baabi ŋáaǹee pu! Án nín làá ŋà pu bí taa láa yīkì kí já kí fōō kitiŋ kí náań ntimu kí gbéeǹ duulinya kɔkɔnee.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has promised to attack Babylonia and destroy everyone there, so that none of them will ever be remembered again.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii: «M làá jáǹ Babiloon yab. M làá kúntí Babiloon yindi nì ki-nib bin kíǹee, nì bi-biyaamu nì bi-naantiibi kɔkɔ.» Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: The Lord will sweep out the people, and the land will become a swamp for wild animals. Assyria Will Be Punished
translation_verse: «M làá yàntī Babiloon tiŋki ń kpántí kubɔɔu, laakin ní jɔmbaaŋkib kóòyee. M làá dū dinàandi ŋaaŋŋu kí ŋàtī-kì.» Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ. Ti-Dindaan làá nàan̄ Asuur pɔŋŋu

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has made this promise: Everything I have planned will happen just as I said.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di pūtì ki lī yii: «Tiŋman pu, tin m bɔ́ntì kí ŋée, see án ŋá míǹ, m nín lēē kí ŋá puee, see án ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: I will wipe out every Assyrian in my country, and I will crush those on my mountains. I will free my people from slavery to the Assyrians.
translation_verse: M làá kúntí Asuur yab pɔŋŋu m-tiŋki pu, m làá tāā kí mátí-bi m-jooŋŋi pu. M làá léetí kpancikil un bi léeǹ m-nibee pu, kí túutí-bi ditúndi din bi túee.

english_verse: I have planned this for the whole world, and my mighty arm controls every nation.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tin ki yóoǹ duulinya kɔkɔ puee dee, u nín bɔ́ntì pu ki yóoǹ kí dáaĺ atimbun kɔkɔ tafal puee dee.»

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have made these plans. No one can stop me now! The Philistines Will Be Punished
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan yaa lēē kí ŋá puee, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí lì yii ú taa ŋá míǹ? U yaa gúntì u-ŋal, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí cúú-ŋu? Ti-Dindaan bíi kpáafí Fiiliistii yab

english_verse: This message came from the Lord in the year King Ahaz died:
translation_verse: Dibindi din ubɔti Akaasi kpíìyee ní bi báakì tibɔti tin bí nee.

english_verse: Philistines, don't be happy just because the rod that punished you is broken. That rod will become a poisonous snake, and then a flying fiery dragon.
translation_verse: Nimbi Fiiliistii yab kɔkɔ, án taa nín̄ mɔ̄ǹ-ni yii ndɔ ŋun bi dūu gbáń-nee nín gíìyee. Di sá yii ukoobu un kpíìyee poon ní ukoowaati làá nyānní, ní ukoowaatee ń màal̀ kukoobiliŋŋu kun ŋàaǹee.

english_verse: The poor and needy will find pastures for their sheep and will live in safety. But I will starve some of you, and others will be killed.
translation_verse: Binandambi làá dāá ká kí jī kí díkí, biwɔfib làá dāá ŋùŋfì nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. Ama m làá yàntī sii biyaamu ń kpú ŋkùm, ní kí yàntī bí kpɔ̀ mun kíǹee.

english_verse: Cry and weep in the gates of your towns, you Philistines! Smoke blows in from the north, and every soldier is ready.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ punyɔkɔki, nín̄ yáliŋkí, ntimu, nín̄ sūǹ ki tátímaan. Fiiliistii yab kɔkɔ wunti yɔ̄tì, di sá yii nnyiim miba nyánní ŋgan pú ki dòoń. Binannanliibi gbanti kansikinee, báà unil kaa sáǹ ki wāatì dijanjakitil.

english_verse: If a messenger comes from a distant nation, you must say: “The Lord built Zion. Even the poorest of his people will find safety there.”
translation_verse: Ti làá dāá kíí ditimbundee tuuŋyi yii ba? Yii: «Ti-Dindaan u-ba di náań Siiyɔn tiŋki. Niin ní u-nibul yab bin sá biwɔfibee làá dāá sāǹ kí kɔ́.»

english_verse: This is a message about Moab: The towns of Ar and Kir were destroyed in a night. Moab is left in ruins!
translation_verse: Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Moowaab tiŋki puee sɔ̀. Kunyabambaantiiu ní bi nāaǹ Aari tiŋki kin bí Moowaabee, an pée dóò ki-pu dee! Kunyabambaantiiu ní bi nāaǹ Kiiri tiŋki kin bí Moowaabee, an pée dóò ki-pu dee!

english_verse: Everyone in Dibon has gone up to the temple and the shrines to cry and weep. All of Moab is crying. Heads and beards are shaved because of what happened at Nebo and Medeba.
translation_verse: Diibɔn tiŋkin yab jɔ́m̀ bi-waatootipaaŋyi pu kí sɔ̄. Moowaab yab jɔ́m̀ Neeboo jool pu nì Meedeeba tiŋkin kí yāliŋkì. Bi-kɔkɔ kōol̀ abaakpan ní ki cáń bi-nyimpuliŋ.

english_verse: In the towns and at home, everyone wears sackcloth and cries loud and long.
translation_verse: Bi pēē kpɔsatab ki còom̄ adan pu. Adiin ŋin bi bɔ̀b̄ee yilpu nì kpacantib puee, bi gà ikpiisilan ní báà ŋma sūǹ.

english_verse: From Heshbon and Elealeh, weeping is heard in Jahaz; Moab's warriors scream while trembling with fear. Pity Moab
translation_verse: Eesbɔn nì Eelalee timmu yab bíi gbáà ibiil, bi tin gbìl̀ bi-neen pu doooo Yakaasi tiŋkin ní. An pu ní Moowaab janjaliibi bí ki kūuntí, bi-wunti yɔ̄tì.

english_verse: I pity Moab! Its people are running to Zoar and to Eglath-Shelishiyah. They cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they tell of disasters.
translation_verse: M bíi nyàab̀ un làá jòoń Moowaab tiŋkee. Ki-nib biba sáǹ ki bàn̄ Soowaar tiŋkin, ní biba bàn̄ Eegilati Seeliisiya tiŋkin. Bi sūǹ ki dàb̀ Luwiiti gbantaŋki, ki gbáà ibiil nì kunimbaau ki tàkā Ooroonayiim saŋŋu pu.

english_verse: The streams of Nimrim and the grasslands have dried up. Every plant is parched.
translation_verse: Niimriim buŋŋu fóotì. Timool kūń kaa ti nyēē, timɔsɔn kaa ti pée bí.

english_verse: The people of Moab are leaving, crossing over Willow Creek, taking everything they own and have worked for.
translation_verse: An pu ní binib kóoǹ bi-wanti tin kíǹ-bee ki kpáàa sáǹ ki dūtì peepiliiyee sufii buŋŋu.

english_verse: In the towns of Eglaim and of Beerelim and everywhere else in Moab mournful cries are heard.
translation_verse: Ibiil di pée tùm̀ dàii Moowaab tiŋki kɔkɔn. Bi gbìl̀ iyaliŋki pu Eegilayiim tiŋkin, bi gbìl̀ i-pu doooo Beer-Eeliim.

english_verse: The streams near Dimon are flowing with blood. But the Lord will bring even worse trouble to Dimon, because all in Moab who escape will be attacked by lions.
translation_verse: Mbun ŋun jītí Dimɔn tiŋkinee máǹ fatiku, ní m làá kūtì Dimɔn yab nnaabu ŋubɔ mun. Gbikinti ubɔ làá cūtì Moowaab yab bin kíǹ bi-tiŋkin kaa kpíìyee.

english_verse: Send lambs as gifts to the ruler of the land. Send them across the desert from Sela to Mount Zion.
translation_verse: «Ní yòom̄maan dipibil doooo Seera tiŋki kin bí kuteeu watil púee kí cùnnì kí tīī Juuda bɔtiu un kóò Siiyɔn jool puee.»

english_verse: The women of Moab crossing the Arnon River are like a flock of birds scattered from their nests.
translation_verse: Moowaab yab nimpoobi bí Arinɔn buŋŋu laakin bi ŋūǹ kí còom̀ kí dùtēe. Bi náań nì inoon in bi jìn̄ ki nyántì i-diikun i yàl̄ee.

english_verse: Moab's messengers say to the people of Judah, “Be kind and help us! Shade us from the heat of the noonday sun. Hide our refugees! Don't turn them away.
translation_verse: Bi bí ki lì Jeerusaleem yii: «Tùkù-ti kun ti máaǹ kí ŋée, ŋá tiba kí tīī-ti. Wúń ti-pu kuwiŋkaŋu nee pu, kii kunyeeu, dibɔmbɔndi nín bīī puee. Dū ti-yab bin sáǹ ki kɔ́-see kí báĺ, taa bìitī bin bíi sáńee pu.

english_verse: Let our people live in your country and find safety here.” Moab, your cruel enemies will disappear; they will no longer attack and destroy your land.
translation_verse: Yàntī Moowaab yab bin sáǹ ki kɔ́-see ń kàl̄ a-cee, nín̄ sá-bi kibalilaŋ unàanli cee. Diwɔ́bil bɔti làá gbèen̄, tipɔmbɔti làá kúntí. Unàanli làá yīkì ti-tiŋki pu.

english_verse: Then a kingdom of love will be set up, and someone from David's family will rule with fairness. He will do what is right and quickly bring justice. Moab's Pride Is Destroyed
translation_verse: Niinee a-ŋanti puee, ubɔti beel làá nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄. U làá dāá kpòotī Daafiidi beel nì deedee. U làá dāá nīn bí kii ubɔsoonli un deedee bɔti máǹ u-nimbiliŋ, ní u néeń ibaamɔn bɔti tikpilee.» Jeerusaleem kaa làá ŋmā kí tūtuǹ Moowaab

english_verse: Tell everyone in Moab to mourn for their nation. Tell them to cry and weep for those fancy raisins of Kir-Hareseth.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee Moowaab yab bíi sūǹ bi-tiŋki pu, bi-kɔkɔ bíi sūǹ. Bi yaa téetì fiinyi subiliŋ kalaabi bin bi nìn ŋmóò Kiiri-Areeseeti tiŋki puee, bi yáliŋkí ní. Bi-wunti yɔ̄tì kpataaa!

english_verse: Vineyards near Heshbon and Sibmah have turned brown. The rulers of nations used to get drunk on wine from those vineyards that spread to Jazer, then across the desert and beyond the sea.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Eesbɔn tiŋki sati kɔkɔ bíil̀ kii Siibima tiŋki fiinyi sufiiyee. Ŋyunti puee, isufi gbanti damam di nìn gbéè bin nìn sá atimbun kpilibee. I nìn yú ki tin bàn̄ Yaseer tiŋkin, ki nìn nyēē kuteeun an kɔkɔ pu. I nìn tɔ́ apan an lákatì Ŋyaam mɔɔl pu.

english_verse: Now I mourn like Jazer for the vineyards of Sibmah. I shed tears for Heshbon and for Elealeh. There will be no more harvest celebrations
translation_verse: An pu ní m kútì Yaseer yab pu ki bíi sūǹ Siibima fiinyi sufii pu. Eesbɔn nì Eelalee, m làá dū m-nyinnyim kí yàaǹ-ni ní sɔ̀ŋkì. Kun puee ni nín nìn kìtī ni-subiliŋ, ki cēē ni-jikaati nì dipɔɔpindi ki fàal̀ puee kɔkɔ kúntì.

english_verse: or joyful and happy times, while bringing in the crops. Singing and shouting are gone from the vineyards. There are no joyful shouts where grapes were pressed. God has silenced them all.
translation_verse: Dipɔɔpindi nì ifaal kúntì ni-kpaaŋŋin. Naa ti gà ilan ki kūuntí ni-fiinyi kpaaŋŋin. Kubɔbiku kun poon ni nìn tà fiinyi biliŋ ndamam còol̀ee kūń. Dipɔɔpindi faalii kúntì.

english_verse: It's useless for Moab's people to wear themselves out by going to their altars to worship and pray.
translation_verse: Moowaab yab làá gīī kí dàb̄ ŋgbantamu pu. Bi làá cùú kɔ́ bi-waadiikun kí tīminsì, ama tiba kaa làá kpántí.

english_verse: The Lord has already said all of this about Moab.
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ Moowaab tiŋki pu dooooyee dee.

english_verse: Now he says, “The contract of a hired worker is good for three years, but Moab's glory and greatness won't last any longer than that. Only a few of its people will survive, and they will be left helpless.”
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí cáá sāā abin ata deedeeyee, Moowaab tindaŋkpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ kaa dāa gíti bí tiban. Bin làá dāá kíńee kaa làá dāá nīn náaǹ, ní kaa dāa pɔ̄ɔ̄ mun.»

english_verse: This is a message about Damascus: Damascus is doomed! It will end up in ruins.
translation_verse: Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Damaasi tiŋki puee sɔ̀. Damaasi tiŋki kaa làá nīn gíti sá kitiŋ ki bí, kì làá kpántí adigbun ŋma ní.

english_verse: The villages around Aroer will be deserted, with only sheep living there and no one to bother them.
translation_verse: Binib làá yīkì kí fá Arooweer timmu. Tiwaŋkuti di làá jī mpaan mu-poon kí nīn bí ní báà uniseen kaa dāa bí ki páb̀-tì.

english_verse: Israel will lose its fortresses. The kingdom of Damascus will be destroyed; its survivors will suffer the same fate as Israel. The Lord All-Powerful has promised this. Sin and Suffering
translation_verse: Ntimu mun bi máń agun ki túee kaa ti làá nīn bí Eefiraayiim beelin. Damaasi tiŋki kaa dāa gíti cáá ubɔti. Aram yab bin làá dāá kíńee nì Isirayeel yab wíiŋŋu làá dāá nīn ŋmà ní. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: When that time comes, the glorious nation of Israel will be brought down; its prosperous people will be skin and bones.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, Jaakɔb nyooti làá bàtī, ní u-wunti tin nìn bí màlmalee ń sāǹ.

english_verse: It will be like an olive tree beaten with a stick, leaving two or three olives or maybe four or five on the highest or most fruitful branches. The Lord God of Israel has promised this.
translation_verse: <Án làá dāá pée kíń tijinlulifikaal ní, tin ní bi lúlifèe, kii bi nín yaa kītì ɔliifi subiliŋ, an nín kīntí abil ali kii ata pu ki lúń yilpuee, àá abil anaa kii aŋmoo ŋin kīntí asupan puee. Tibɔti tin ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu sòon̄ee dee.

english_verse: At that time the people will turn and trust their Creator, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: Yaadalee, binib làá dāá dū bi-nimbikpeeŋu kí báań bi-náanliu pu, bi làá dāá fàtī bi-nimbiin kí túĺ Isirayeel circir Nimbɔtiu cee.

english_verse: They have built altars and places for burning incense to their goddess Asherah, and they have set up sacred poles for her. But they will stop worshiping at these places.
translation_verse: Baa dāa gíti fàtīí kpèè isaraafan in bíǹ bi-ba máńee. Baa dāa gíti fàtīí kpèè diwaal Aseera windɔi àá isaraafan in pu bi tùutī talaalubee watil pú.

english_verse: Israel captured powerful cities and chased out the people who lived there. But these cities will lie in ruins, covered over with weeds and underbrush.
translation_verse: Yaadalee bi làá dāá sāǹ kí fá bi-timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee, kii dooooyee Eefi yab nì Amɔɔr yab nín nìn sáǹ ki fá bi-timmu pu Isirayeel yab nimbiinee ní. Bi-timmu gbanti làá dāá kpántí kii kuteeuee.

english_verse: Israel, you have forgotten the God who saves you, the one who is the mighty rock where you find protection. You plant the finest flowers to honor a foreign god.
translation_verse: Isirayeel, a súntì Unimbɔti un fīī-see pu. Aa ti téetí ditaŋkpal din a sáǹ ki kɔ́ee pu. An pu ní a cóoǹ isufi in cáá kunyaaŋŋuee, ní ki búĺ asubil ŋin di nyánní ntincamunee.

english_verse: The plants may sprout and blossom that very same morning, but it will do you no good, because you will suffer endless agony. God Defends His People
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun a cóoǹ-iee, ní i yíkì ki wíiǹ, kutaafaauee ní iwambool in a búĺee ń púkuḿ. Ama ní nnaabu wiiŋŋu dalee, tin a cáńee kɔkɔ ń wāŋkì a-cee, ní án kaa dāa cáá dicáaǹdi. Anibul wooku

english_verse: But even if they roar like a fearsome flood, God will give the command to turn them back. They will be like dust, or like a tumbleweed blowing across the hills in a windstorm.
translation_verse: Atimbun gbanti wooku náań nì nnyiŋkpaam wooku ní. Ti-Dindaan kpìl̄-mì ní mì sáǹ ki nín cá ndandati, a lì kii dijool pu buŋku nín yòontí timɔkulindi ki féeń puee, kii kubuŋu nín yòontí kikuŋkumbɔŋ biliŋ puee, a lì kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋu nín yòontí kukpɔŋkpɔŋu puee.

english_verse: In the evening their attack is fierce, but by morning they are destroyed. This is what happens to those who raid and rob us.
translation_verse: Kujoouee, an sá dinyoondi ní, ama ku dāa lì yii ku wúntée, bi wáŋkì. Binib bin dòoń ki fúkuĺ-ti ki gbákaĺ-tee, kun dɔ̄ ki cí-bee dee.

english_verse: Downstream from Ethiopia lies the country of Egypt, swarming with insects.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí sii kitiŋ kin ŋaliŋfii cáá ifeen ili, ki dɔ̄ ki nóó Kuusi buŋyee.

english_verse: Egypt sends messengers up the Nile River on ships made of reeds. Send them fast to Ethiopia, whose people are tall and have smooth skin. Their land is divided by rivers; they are strong and brutal, feared all over the world.
translation_verse: A tūǹ ituun i kàal̀ tikati ŋaliŋfii poon ki còom̄ Niil mɔɔl pu. Nimbi ituun in yáb̀ee, nín̄ gítímaan. Ní gítímaan ni-nibul din nib fɔ̀kɔ̀ bi-wunti jɔ̀m̀ee cee, dinibul din bi fàŋkí duulinyanee cee, dinibul din pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki tà ki mátí di-nannanliibee cee. Ní fàtīí gítí ni-tiŋki kin ní ibun yākatèe cee.

english_verse: Everyone on this earth, listen with care! A signal will be given on the mountains, and you will hear a trumpet.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kɔkɔ kóò duulinyanee, nimbi bin kɔkɔ kpátìi gbí kitiŋ puee, bi yaa láa cóoǹ kiŋaabiki ajoon puee, ní dāá kpèèmaan, bi yaa láa búń ŋyinee, ní dāá pīlifìmaan!

english_verse: The Lord said to me, “I will calmly look down from my home above— as calmly as the sun at noon or clouds in the heat of harvest season.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di tùkū-mi yii: «M làá nīn kā m-kɔŋkooŋŋun yilpu ní ki kpèeń tin bíi jītí taapuee soooo, kii ŋwìiń nín ŋmíntí ŋu-walifiŋu tùm̀ puee, kii dimalindi nín tòó kudiceeu yuntiŋu puee.»

english_verse: Those Ethiopians are tall and their skin is smooth. They are feared all over the world, because they are strong and brutal. But at that time they will come from their land divided by rivers, and they will bring gifts to the Lord All-Powerful, who is worshiped on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, bi làá dāá cáań tiwampɔkaal kí tīī ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan. Án dāa sá dinibul din yab fɔ̀kɔ̀ ní bi-wunti jɔ̀m̀ pɔ́lpɔlee ní. Kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ fàŋkí-bi ní yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ. Dinibul gbanti nib cáá mpɔn ní ki tà ki mátí bi-nannanliibi, ní ibun cúú bi-tiŋki ki yākatì. Bi làá dāá cáań an wampɔkaatee Siiyɔn jool pu, laakin ní bi jáaḿ ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaanee ní.

english_verse: This is a message about Egypt: The Lord comes to Egypt, riding swiftly on a cloud. The people are weak from fear. Their idols tremble as he approaches and says,
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin Unimbɔti sòon̄ Eejipiti tiŋki puee sèé. Kpèè, ti-Dindaan di kāń ditagbandi din yáb̀ee pu ki jàkà ki dòoń Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Tifaandi kɔ́ Eejipiti waaŋi u-nimbiin, ní Eejipiti yab bi-ba pɔbil bíil̀ tikpil.

english_verse: “Egypt will be discouraged when I confuse their plans. They will try to get advice from their idols, from the spirits of the dead, and from fortunetellers.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī Eejipiti yab wunti ń yɔ̀tī, kí yàntī tin bi bɔ́ntì kí ŋée ń gbíntí fám. Niinee bi làá cù bi-waaŋi nì bin yíì bitaŋkpiibee nì bi-bɔɔbi cee dibalifil.

english_verse: I will put the Egyptians under the power of a cruel, heartless king. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have promised this.” Trouble along the Nile
translation_verse: M làá dū Eejipiti yab kí ŋá bikpilib bin bɔti pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ŋaan. Ubɔti un cáá mpɔnee di làá jī dibeel bi-pu.» Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: The Nile River will dry up and become parched land.
translation_verse: Niil mɔɔl làá fóotí, dimɔɔl gbanti làá kpā.

english_verse: Its streams will stink, Egypt will have no water, and the reeds and tall grass will dry up.
translation_verse: Ibun làá dāá nūukì, Niil buntaaŋi poonee, nnyim làá dāá fóotí ní ŋí kpā, ní tikati nì dikal ń dāá yɔ́ĺ.

english_verse: None of the cloth makers will know what to do, and they will turn pale.
translation_verse: Icoo cúú bin bɔ́ntí gulfapiin un bí fálfalee, nì bin cáa lùee.

english_verse: Weavers will be confused; paid workers will cry and mourn. Egypt's Helpless Leaders
translation_verse: Bisataluliibi naŋki làá nyā nì bi-ba, ní bitɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ wunti ń yɔ̀tī.

english_verse: The king's officials in Zoan are foolish themselves and give stupid advice. How can they say to him, “We are very wise, and our families go back to kings of long ago?”
translation_verse: Soowan bɔtibiliŋ sá bigbaambi ŋma ní. Biciŋfitiibi bin sáŋkí Faarooyee kaa nyí tiba. Mana ní ni ŋūǹ kí tùkù Faaroo yii: «Ti sá biciŋfitiibi naantiibi, ti sá dooooyee bɔtiibi naantiibi ní?»

english_verse: Where are those wise men now? If they can, let them say what the Lord All-Powerful intends for Egypt.
translation_verse: Faaroo, a-ciŋfitiibee bí la sɔ̀? Bí lēē kí dàkà-si á béé tin ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bɔ́ntì kí ŋá Eejipiti tiŋkee!

english_verse: The royal officials in Zoan and in Memphis are foolish and deceived. The leaders in every state have given bad advice to the nation.
translation_verse: Soowan yab bɔtibiliŋ kpántì bigbaambi, ní Nɔfi yab kpilib bíi kíiĺ bi-ba. Bíǹ bin bàà sá yii bí kpòotī Eejipiti tiŋkee, bíǹ di bíi gáatí-kì.

english_verse: The Lord has confused Egypt; its leaders have made it stagger and vomit like a drunkard.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan dū kunyiŋfuŋfuŋu fam ki tɔ́ bi-pu, ki yāntì Eejipiti yab kaa bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄, kii udanyɔgbil nín kpìntī ki wùliŋkī puee.

english_verse: No one in Egypt can do a thing, no matter who they are.
translation_verse: Diyileeee, dijuuleeee, kukpakpaliueeee, kukaluueeee, ubɔ kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiba kí tīī Eejipiti. Kun làá dāá jītí Eejipiti tiŋki puee

english_verse: When the Lord All-Powerful punishes Egypt with his mighty arm, the Egyptians will become terribly weak and will tremble with fear.
translation_verse: Ŋwindalee, Eejipiti yab làá dāá nīn bí kii binimpoobee ní. Dinyoondi làá dāá kɔ́-bi ní bi-wunti jìkì ŋyunti ŋun bi yaa láa ká ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan tāntì u-ŋal kí dáaĺ bi-tafalee.

english_verse: They will be so terrified of Judah that they will be frightened by the very mention of its name. This will happen because of what the Lord All-Powerful is planning against Egypt. The Lord Will Bless Egypt, Assyria, and Israel
translation_verse: Juuda tiŋki làá dāá yàntī dinyoondi ń kɔ́ Eejipiti yab. Bi yaa láa pée pútì Juuda tiŋki yindi bi-ceeyee, ní bí kíĺ ki bíi jìkì tin ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ ki yóoǹ kí ŋá-bee pu.

english_verse: The time is coming when Hebrew will be spoken in five Egyptian cities, and their people will become followers of the Lord. One of these cities will be called City of the Sun.
translation_verse: Ŋwindalee, binib làá dāá sòoǹ eebru sooŋyi Eejipiti timmu muŋmoo poon ní, kí dāá pùtī kí pòon̄ yii bi làá nīn kíǹ ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan baba. Ntimu gbanti kiba ní bi dāa yíì yii Iir-Ayeereesi, taapu di sá yii «ŋwìiń tiŋki».

english_verse: In the heart of Egypt an altar will be set up for the Lord; at its border a shrine will be built to honor him.
translation_verse: Ŋwindalee, bi làá dāá mā ti-Dindaan nsaraafan Eejipiti tiŋki pɔ̀ti pu, ní kí dāá cóoń ditaŋkpal Eejipiti tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔki kí nīn téetí ti-Dindaan pu.

english_verse: These will remind the Egyptians that the Lord All-Powerful is with them. And when they are in trouble and ask for help, he will send someone to rescue them from their enemies.
