translation_verse: Án di dāa sá kudaaŋŋu yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí Eejipiti tiŋkin. Eejipiti yab yaa láa kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan bin bíi wɔ́b̀-bee puee, u làá dāá tɔ̄ ufiil ubɔ ú cùú mɔ̄tì bi-pu ní kí fīī-bi kí líí.

english_verse: The Lord will show the Egyptians who he is, and they will know and worship the Lord. They will bring him sacrifices and offerings, and they will keep their promises to him.
translation_verse: Niinee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá lēē u-ba kí dàkà Eejipiti yab, ní bíǹ ń dāá béé-u. Bi làá dāá ŋá saraabi kí cáań tiwampɔkaal kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan. Bi làá dāá pòon̄ ti-Dindaan ipoon ní kí dāá ŋá tin ní bi pōoǹee.

english_verse: After the Lord has punished Egypt, the people will turn to him. Then he will answer their prayers, and the Egyptians will be healed.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dāá dáaĺ Eejipiti yab tafal. U làá dāá fáá-bi, ama ní kí cáaǹ-bi. Bi làá dāá fàtīí gítí ti-Dindaan cee, ní ú fōō bi-wimmeem kí cáaǹ-bi.

english_verse: At that time a good road will run from Egypt to Assyria. The Egyptians and the Assyrians will travel back and forth from Egypt to Assyria, and they will worship together.
translation_verse: Ŋwindalee, didandi làá dāá nyā Eejipiti tiŋkin kí cù Asuur tiŋkin. Asuur yab làá dāá dāan̄ Eejipiti yab tiŋkin, ní Eejipiti yab mun ń cù Asuur yab tiŋkin. Eejipiti yab nì Asuur yab làá dāá kpāfì kí jāam̀ Unimbɔti.

english_verse: Israel will join with these two countries. They will be a blessing to everyone on earth,
translation_verse: Ŋwindalee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá bìin̄ duulinya pu: Isirayeel tiŋki làá dāá nīn sá kitintataatii kin pu u làá bìin̄ee, kí kūtì Eejipiti nì Asuur timmu pu.

english_verse: then the Lord All-Powerful will bless them by saying, “The Egyptians are my people. I created the Assyrians and chose the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá dāá bìin̄ duulinya pu kí lì yii: «M bīiǹ Eejipiti yab m-nibul pu, ki bīiǹ Asuur yab bin m náań nì m-ŋaliiyee pu, ní ki bīiǹ Isirayeel yab bin ní m gāntì ki yóoǹ m-bee pu.»

english_verse: King Sargon of Assyria gave orders for his army commander to capture the city of Ashdod.
translation_verse: An nìn sá dibindi din ní Asuur bɔtiu Saargɔn nìn tú u-janjakpiliu u cūtì ki jáń nì Asidoodi tiŋki ki fōō-kèe ní.

english_verse: About this same time the Lord had told me, “Isaiah, take off everything, including your sandals!” I did this and went around naked and barefoot
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti ní ti-Dindaan nìn tùkū Amɔtisi jipɔɔn Yeesaya yii: «Nín̄ cá, á gbìntī kutuku un a gbìn̄ a-caŋee, kí cúú a-naatakaŋ mun kí tákatí.» Ní Yeesaya ŋá míǹ, ki kíǹ ki còom̄ kaa lōō tiba, kaa táká anaataka mun.

english_verse: for three years. Then the Lord said: What Isaiah has done is a warning to Egypt and Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M-tɔntɔnliu Yeesaya nín cōom̀ kaa lōō tiba, kaa táká anaataka mun abin ata nee, an sá kudaaŋŋu nì tibɔkpaafikaal ní kí tīī Eejipiti nì Kuusi timmu yab.

english_verse: Everyone in these two countries will be led away naked and barefoot by the king of Assyria. Young or old, they will be taken prisoner, and Egypt will be disgraced.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní Asuur bɔtiu làá dāá cúú Eejipiti yab sarka ní kí cúú Kuusi yab, binipɔmbi nì bitikpilib kí cùnnì kuyuŋu. Bi làá dāá nīn còom̄ kaa lōō tiba, kaa táká anaataka ní bi-kpiliŋ ń nīn dɔ̄ fám. Án dāa sá icoo ní ki tīī Eejipiti yab.

english_verse: They will be confused and frustrated, because they depended on Ethiopia and bragged about Egypt.
translation_verse: Binib bin nìn máká Kuusi yab pu, ki nìn fàal̀ Eejipiti yab puee wunti làá dāá yɔ̀tī ní icoo ń dāá cúú-bi.»

english_verse: When this happens, the people who live along the coast will say, “Look what happened to them! We ran to them for safety, hoping they would protect us from the king of Assyria. But now, there is no escape for us.”
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, binib bin kóò ditiŋkugbandee làá dāá lì yii: «Kpèèmaan tin bāań bin pu timbi mákée! Ti bàà nìn cɔ́tí yii ti làá sāǹ kí kɔ́-bi ní bí jòoń-ti kí fīī-ti Asuur bɔtiu ŋaan. Mimmee ti làá nín ŋá mana ní kí ŋmátí dee?»

english_verse: This is a message about a desert beside the sea: Enemies from a hostile nation attack like a whirlwind from the Southern Desert.
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ní Unimbɔti sòon̄ <tiŋku caŋin teeku> puee sèé. Kii kunaakpaabuŋŋu nín jītí Neegeeb tiŋki pu puee, míǹ ní unannanli nyánní kuteeu pú tiŋki, kitiŋ kin báà ŋma fàŋkée poon.

english_verse: What a horrible vision was shown to me— a vision of betrayal and destruction. Tell Elam and Media to surround and attack the Babylonians. The Lord has sworn to end the suffering they caused.
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin m ká dileedakal poonee pɔ̄ɔ̄ tikpil. U nì un nìn pēē kinyɔkɔee nyáń u-boon, ní un nàantée bíi nàantí. Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «Eelam yab, cùú já nì kì! Meedii yab, cùú màntīí tū-kì! M làá kúntí iyaliŋki kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: I'm in terrible pain like a woman giving birth. I'm shocked and hurt so much that I can't hear or see.
translation_verse: M nín ká mimmee ní tiwool kɔ́-mi. M gbìl̄ iwàlfi pu kii imatiŋweenee. Kunimbaau kɔ́-mi ki yāntì m-tafaliŋ kpáá, dinyoondi kɔ́-mi ki yāntì maa ti wāĺ.

english_verse: My head spins; I'm horrified! Early evening, my favorite time, has become a nightmare.
translation_verse: M-pɔbil bíil̀ ní tifaandi kɔ́-mi m-wunti kíǹ ki jìkì. M nín bàà kā ki cí yii án sɔ̀ŋkì m-pu kujoouee, ní an dūu kpántì-mi dinyoondi.

english_verse: In Babylon the high officials were having a feast. They were eating and drinking, when someone shouted, “Officers, take your places! Grab your shields.”
translation_verse: Bi síiǹ teebilib ki kpátì iŋaabu ki bīiǹ, ní binib kíĺ ki bíi jīǹ ki nyù. Kpalaayee ní ubɔ téeń yii: «Bijanjakpilib, yīkìmaan, ŋmìtī ni-gbampɔɔŋi ŋkpam!»

english_verse: The Lord said to me, “Send guards to find out what's going on.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄-mi puee sèé: «Cùú yóoń un làá nīn cí sintilee, tin ní u làá kée, ú dūú bāakì.

english_verse: When they see cavalry troops and columns of soldiers on donkeys and camels, tell them to be ready!”
translation_verse: U yaa láa ká janjatɔrɔku páaǹní itaamu ili dátée, ki ká binib kā mmamu pu àá binib kā igutaamu puee, ú dāá kpèè tiŋan, kí gíti kpèè tiŋan!»

english_verse: Now I see column after column of cavalry troops.” At once someone shouted, “Babylon has fallen! Every idol in the city lies broken on the ground.”
translation_verse: Kpèè, unil ubɔ di dòońee. U kāń janjatɔrɔku pu itaamu ili dátí-u. U bí ki sòoǹ ki lì yii: <Kitiŋee lítì ní, Babiloon tiŋki lítì. Awaa ŋin ki-nib jáaḿee kɔkɔ dɔ̄ kitiŋ ki wīil̀.>

english_verse: Then I said, “My people, you have suffered terribly, but I have a message for you from the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel.” How Much Longer?
translation_verse: «M-nibul, sii un ní ti-Dindaan gbáń kii bi nín gbáà bilee dinaapaal pu puee, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee ní m gbìl̄ an bɔti, ní ki cáa bíi nàatī-si. Kunyeeu dáá dátàaa?

english_verse: This is a message about Dumah: From the country of Seir, someone shouts to me, “Guard, how much longer before daylight?”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti sòon̄ Duuma tiŋki pu. Ubɔ sòon̄ní-mi doooo Seeyiir tiŋkin ki lī yii: «Uciitil, kunyeeu dáá dátàaa? Uciitil, kunyeeu dáá dátàaa?»

english_verse: From my guard post, I answered, “Morning will soon be here, but night will return. If you want to know more, come back later.”
translation_verse: Ní uciitil kíí yii: «Kutaa bíi wúntí, ama kunyeeu làá gíti mɔ́. Ni yaa là bí kíí-nee, ní fàtīí gítiń kí bàlifì.» Deedan nì Keedaar timmu yab bíi sáń

english_verse: This is a message for Arabs who live in the barren desert in the region of Dedan: You must order your caravans
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin Unimbɔti sòon̄ Bilaalibub tiŋki puee sèé. Nimbi Deedan yab bin kā igutaamu ki jītée, bilaalibub tiŋki bambaŋkun ní ni làá dòon̄ díǹ nyeeku!

english_verse: to bring water for those who are thirsty. You people of Tema must bring food for the hungry refugees.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kóò Teema tiŋkinee, tīīmaan bin nnyinnyoo cááyee nnyim bí nyɔ̀, kí tīī bin sáń kí ŋmátée tijin bí jī.

english_verse: They are worn out and weary from being chased by enemies with swords and arrows.
translation_verse: Kun puee bi bíi sáń ntàataajimu mun bi dáaĺ ki fúutì kujitoounee, ki bíi sáń itɔfi in bi dáaĺ ki làá tɔ̄ee, ki bíi sáń kujaau nín yíkìi pɔ́ɔkì puee.

english_verse: The Lord said to me: A year from now the glory of the people of Kedar will all come to an end, just as a worker's contract ends after a year.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nín lī-mi puee sèé: «Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí cáá sāā dibindi deedeeyee, Keedaar yab nyooti kɔkɔ làá kúntí.

english_verse: Only a few of their warriors will be left with bows and arrows. This is a promise that I, the Lord God of Israel, have made.
translation_verse: Keedaar yab kansikin bibaatandambi bin tòó ipiinee kaa làá dāá kíń ki náaǹ.» Ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu di lī míǹ.

english_verse: This is a message about Vision Valley: Why are you celebrating on the flat roofs of your houses?
translation_verse: Tin Unimbɔti lī Dileedakal Tantakal puee sèé. Jeerusaleem, ba ŋá ní a-nib kɔkɔ jɔ́m̀ adiin yilpu ní?

english_verse: Your city is filled with noisy shouts. Those who lie drunk in your streets were not killed in battle.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní a sá kitiŋ kin poon kuwoou bí, an tùm̀ dàii, ki bí jiŋaal poonee ní? Kitàataajiki ní baa dūu kūū a-nib bin kpíìyee, an kaa sá kujaau poon ní bi kūū-bi.

english_verse: Your leaders ran away, but they were captured without a fight. No matter how far they ran, they were found and caught.
translation_verse: A-janjakpilib kɔkɔ sáǹ ki kátì pílpil, bijanjaliibi bin tòó ipiinee dū-bi ki kpántì bisarkadambi. Bi nìn cúú bin kɔkɔ bi nìn pée kée dicilpu, ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi sáńee.

english_verse: Then I said, “Leave me alone! Let me cry bitter tears. My people have been destroyed, so don't try to comfort me.”
translation_verse: An pu ní m bí-ni yii: «Ní yàntīmaan ḿ sɔ̄ lɔ̀lɔ. Bi nāaǹ m-nibul, ama ní taa màkan̄ kí sɔ̀ŋkì m-pɔbil.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful had chosen a time for noisy shouts and confusion to fill Vision Valley, and for everyone to beg the mountains for help.
translation_verse: Di sá yii díǹ wiiŋŋu nee, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan dū fìkil fikil nì dilitil nì dinyoondi ki tɔ́ń ti-pu.» Dileedakal Tantakal poonee, bi wīī digundi din māntìi tú kitiŋee, ní ibiil fōō ki píĺ bin bí ajoon puee ń jòoń-bi.

english_verse: The people of Elam and Kir attacked with chariots and carried shields.
translation_verse: Eelaam yab yōoǹ abaatan ki bàl̄. Bijanjaliibi bin nìn kā janjatɔrɔkub puee nìn bí ní bitanjakaliibi mun bí. Kiiri janjaliibi bɔ́ntì bi-gbampɔɔŋi.

english_verse: Your most beautiful valleys were covered with chariots; your cities were surrounded by cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem, janjatɔrɔkub gbí a-tantakaŋ ŋin ŋān̄ee poon, ní bitanjakaliibi yú a-punyɔkɔpu kí já nì si.

english_verse: Judah was left defenseless. At that time you trusted in the weapons you had stored in Forest Palace.
translation_verse: Juuda beel kaa ti cáá diwundi. Yaadalee, ni fātì ni-nimbikpeeŋu ki túĺ tijanjawan tin bí <Kubambaŋŋu diikunee>.

english_verse: You saw the holes in the outer wall of Jerusalem, and you brought water from the lower pool.
translation_verse: Digundi din māntìi tú Daafiidi Tiŋkee, ni ká laakin bátì bátì ki lítèe nín wīikí puee. Ni kpáafì nnyim dinyimbɔbil din bí taapu púee poon.

english_verse: You counted the houses in Jerusalem and tore down some of them, so you could get stones to repair the city wall.
translation_verse: Ni kàan̄ Jeerusaleem diiŋŋi, ni wīil̀ aba kí mɔ̀tīí tīī kitiŋ gundi mpɔn.

english_verse: Then you built a large tank between the walls to store the water. But you refused to trust the God who planned this long ago and made it happen. A Time To Weep
translation_verse: Ni gbìn̄ dinyimbɔbil agun ali kansikin kí ŋmā kí dáaliń dikpikilee nyim. Ama naa fātì ni-nimbikpeeŋu ki túĺ un ŋá tíǹ kɔkɔee, kaa béè un di túń an tundi ki síiǹ dooooyee.

english_verse: When all of this happened, the Lord All-Powerful told you to weep and mourn, to shave your heads, and wear sackcloth.
translation_verse: Yaadalee, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nìn yíiń-ni ní sɔ̄ kí yāliŋkì, kí kòol̀ ni-yiliŋ ní kí dū kpɔsatab kí pèen̄.

english_verse: But instead, you celebrated by feasting on beef and lamb and by drinking wine, because you said, “Let's eat and drink today! Tomorrow we may die.”
translation_verse: Ama kpèèmaan, ni bí ifaal nì mmɔnni! Ni bí ki kù inaa, ki làntī ipii, ki ŋmóò tinan ní ki nyù ndamam ki lì yii: «Tí jī kí nyɔ̀maan, kun puee fool ti làá fu kpú.»

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has spoken to me this solemn promise: “I won't forgive them for this, not as long as they live.” Selfish Officials Are Doomed
translation_verse: Ama ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ tibɔti nee an kɔ́ m-tafalin yii: «M pée kpá kí dū ikpiti nee kí pɔ̄-ni kí tin sāā ni-kúm dal.» Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee dee. Ubɔti tɔntɔŋkpiliu Seebina làá fá u-paaŋŋu

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful is sending me with this message for Shebna, the prime minister:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí-mi yii: «Cù kí tùkù ubɔti tɔntɔŋkpiliu Seebina un kpèé dibeecindi tuuŋŋee yii:

english_verse: Shebna, what gives you the right to have a tomb carved out of rock in this burial place of royalty? None of your relatives are buried here.
translation_verse: <Ba ní a cáá doo nee ní? A-yaaja ulɔu di bí doo ní a yāntì bi gbìn̄-si dikaakul doo? Bi gbìn̄-si dikaakul kigbantaŋ yilpu, ki lùkū ditaŋkpal ki bɔ́ntì-si ŋkɔŋkoon.

english_verse: You may be powerful, but the Lord is about to snatch you up and throw you away.
translation_verse: Kpèè, ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̄-si kí fá ndan, u làá gúĺ-si kí bíĺ.

english_verse: He will roll you into a ball and throw you into a wide open country, where you will die and your chariots will be destroyed. You're a disgrace to those you serve.
translation_verse: U làá kúntí-si á kpántí kii dinantaŋkulee, kí dū-si kí tɔ̄ á tin lítí kitiŋ kin wāāyee poon. Niin ní a làá tin kpú, niin mun ní a-janjatɔrɔkub bin yì a-nyootee làá tin gbíntí, sii un sá icoo ki tīī a-kpiliu dicaŋkuee!>

english_verse: He will give your official robes and your authority to his servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah. Eliakim will be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the royal family of Judah.
translation_verse: M làá dāá dū a-bɔkutil poon yal kí pèen̄-u, kí dāá dū ŋŋaabu dambalau un a gbìǹee kí gbìn̄-u, ní kí dū mpɔn ŋun ní a cááyee kí tīī-u. U làá dāá nīn sá ubaati ní ki tīī Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda beel kɔkɔ yab.

english_verse: The Lord will put him in charge of the key that belongs to King David's family. No one will be able to unlock what he locks, and no one will be able to lock what he unlocks.
translation_verse: M làá dāá dū Daafiidi beel saafiiu kí ŋúbiǹ-u. U yaa láa pīitì kipunyɔkɔee, ubɔ dāa kpá kí pìin̄, u yaa láa tí dūu pīiǹee, ubɔ dāa kpá kí pìitī.

english_verse: The Lord will make him as firm in his position as a tent peg hammered in the ground, and Eliakim will bring honor to his family.
translation_verse: M làá dāá cóoń-u kii dikpakpaalee, mpaan ŋun pu u làá nīn cɔ́ ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋanee. U-pu ní u-baa dicaŋku kɔkɔ làá dāá ká tinyool.»

english_verse: His children and relatives will be supported by him, like pans hanging from a peg on the wall.
translation_verse: U-baa dicaŋkun nyooti kɔkɔ làá nīn lúń úǹ baba pu ní, kii bi nín dù tisamɔŋwan kí yòon̄ asambil kí cáá sāā aboon kí lúntí dikpakpaal pu puee ní.

english_verse: That peg is fastened firmly now, but someday it will be shaken loose and fall down. Then everything that was hanging on it will be destroyed. This is what the Lord All-Powerful has promised.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin ŋubɔee, dikpakpaal din bi cóoǹ laakin pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋanee làá gíí kí kɔ̄fì ní kí lítí kitiŋ, ní diwaŋgul din nìn lúń di-puee kɔkɔ ń bīil̀.» Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee dee.

english_verse: This is a message from distant islands about the city of Tyre: Cry, you seagoing ships! Tyre and its houses lie in ruins.
translation_verse: Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Tiir tiŋki puee sɔ̀. «Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan, Taarsiisi meelab! Bi nāaǹ Tiir tiŋki kɔkɔ, báà kudii kaa kíǹ.» Bi bàn̄ Kiitiim tiŋkinee ní ki gbìl̄ an bɔti gbanti.

english_verse: Mourn in silence, you shop owners of Sidon, you people on the coast. Your sailors crossed oceans, making your city rich.
translation_verse: Ní ŋmīĺmaan fɔ́ŋfɔŋ nimbi bin kóò ditiŋkugbandee, nimbi Siidɔn nyampoobi bin tūǹ binib bi dùtī tiŋkuee.

english_verse: Your merchants sailed the seas, making you wealthy by trading with nation after nation. They brought back grain that grew along the Nile.
translation_verse: Tin bi būul̀ Niil mɔɔl puee, nì tin bi cēē di-gbándee di sá Siidɔn gaajati. Kíǹ di nìn kpántì atimbun kɔkɔ nyɔŋki.

english_verse: Sidon, you are a mighty fortress built along the sea. But you will be disgraced like a married woman who never had children.
translation_verse: Siidɔn tiŋki, icoo ń cúú-si, sii un di sá tiŋku balilaŋkee. Di sá yii tiŋku sòon̄ yii: «Maa làá yāliŋkì imatiŋween ní kaa nín màl̄ kibiki. Maa làá kpàà binaacimpɔmbi, ní kaa nín kpēē bisapɔmbi bi cíkitì.»

english_verse: All of you along the coast had better cry and sail far across the ocean.
translation_verse: Ní dùtīmaan tiŋku kí cù Taarsiisi tiŋkin, yāliŋkìmaan, nimbi bin kóò ditiŋkugbandee!

english_verse: Can this be the happy city that has stood for centuries? Its people have spread to distant lands;
translation_verse: Ni-tiŋki kin nìn nyìm̀ ki sá kitiŋkpiŋkpikiiyee sɔ̀ɔɔ? Kitiŋ kin nìn cūtì ndandati ki jáń ki fōō ntimu ki kāl̀ee sɔ̀ɔɔ?

english_verse: its merchants were kings honored all over the world. Who planned to destroy Tyre?
translation_verse: Tiir tiŋki nìn yàkatī mbeefuulimu ní. Ki-nyampoobi sá kii abɔtibilee, ní ki-wannyafiliibi sá binikpaambi kitiŋ pu. Ŋma di lēē ki síiǹ yii bí bīil̀ kitiŋ gbanti ní?

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful planned it to bring shame and disgrace to those who are honored by everyone on earth.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di sòon̄ ki yóoǹ míǹ, kí bīil̀ bin bi tìì jilmee lambil, kí sìntī kitiŋ nee pu nikpaambi taapu.

english_verse: People of Tyre, your harbor is destroyed! You will have to become farmers just like the Egyptians. Tyre Will Be Forgotten
translation_verse: Tiir yab, cùú nīn kùmaan ni-kpaatanti, kii bi nín kù Niil mɔɔgbandi puee, di sá yii naa ti cáá laakin meelab sīlifée.

english_verse: The Lord's hand has reached across the sea, upsetting the nations. He has given a command to destroy fortresses in the land of Canaan.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tāntì u-ŋal tiŋku pu ki yāntì abee cīŋkì. U tīī mara yii bí kpìtī Kanaan tiŋki laakin bi wúń tiŋanee.

english_verse: The Lord has said to the people of Sidon, “Your celebrating is over— you are crushed. Even if you escape to Cyprus, you won't find peace.”
translation_verse: U bí yii: «Siidɔn yab, ni kpá kí gíti jī jiŋaal, ni bí kii usapɔɔn un bi bíil̀ee ní! Báà ni yaa kíĺ nsan ki cūtìi póotì Kiitiim tiŋki, naa làá ŋmā kí ká niin mun diŋuŋfil.

english_verse: Look what the Assyrians have done to Babylonia! They have attacked, destroying every palace in the land. Now wild animals live among the ruins.
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan Kaldee yab tiŋki, dinibul gbanti kaa ti bí kitiŋ pu. Asuur yab dū-kì ki kpántì laakin ní ilambunti kóòyee. Bi máń adifɔkɔ ŋin pu bi yūlifí sintilee, ki wīil̀ ki-dinyaaŋŋi ní ki yāntì kì kpántì adigbun ŋma.

english_verse: Not a fortress will be left standing, so tell all the seagoing ships to mourn.
translation_verse: Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan, Taarsiisi meelab, di sá yii bi wīī ni-balilaŋki.»

english_verse: You're gone and forgotten, you evil woman! So strut through the town, singing and playing your favorite tune to be remembered again.
translation_verse: Sii kinimpulaakpaai kin pu bi súntèe, yòon̄ kubeeu kí yìiǹ kí màntī kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ! Bɔ̀ɔ̀ kubeeu tiŋan, gāā a-laŋyi kí fàtīí gāā, án nín làá ŋá pu binib ń téetí a-puee.

english_verse: but none of what is earned will be kept in the city. That money will belong to the Lord, and it will be used to buy more than enough food and good clothes for those who worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Ama bi làá dū ki-paatii nì ki-paati kɔkɔee kí sú ti-Dindaan ní. Baa làá dāá kóoǹ-tì kí kpāfì, kaa làá dāá kpāafì-tì mun. Bi-paati ní bi làá dāá nīn cáa dāā tijin ki kpīintí binib bin bí ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki tūǹ u-tundee bí jī kí díkí, ní kí kíń kí dā tiwannyaandi kí pèen̄-bi.

english_verse: The Lord is going to twist the earth out of shape and turn it into a desert. Everyone will be scattered,
translation_verse: Kpèè, ti-Dindaan làá nàan̄ kitiŋ kí bīil̀-kì, u làá kpēelikì-kì ní ki-nib kɔkɔ ń yàl̄.

english_verse: including ordinary people and priests, slaves and slave owners, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, the rich and the poor.
translation_verse: Tin làá bàń usaraaŋalee di làá bàń unifantanti, ukpil nì u-tɔntɔnliu, unimpu nì u-yumbusapɔɔŋwu, uwandal nì unyampu, un pìntée nì un bi pìntée, un bi cáá dipɔndee nì u-pɔ̀nliu.

english_verse: The earth will be stripped bare and left that way. This is what the Lord has promised.
translation_verse: Bi làá nàan̄ kitiŋ ní kí fūkul̀ ki-wanti pílpil. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ an bɔti ki yóoǹ.

english_verse: The earth is polluted because its people disobeyed the laws of God, breaking their agreement that was to last forever.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ pu doo nib kɔ́ǹ-kì tijɔkɔndi, di sá yii baa nóó Unimbɔti marab, kaa dū u-bɔkpaaŋi ki yíiń tiba, ní ki kpītì u-poondi din bí ki cá talkuee.

english_verse: Grapevines have dried up: wine is almost gone— mournful sounds are heard instead of joyful shouts.
translation_verse: Ndapɔm bɔti dūu pɔ́ɔkì, fiinyi sufii kɔkɔ yɔ́ĺ yɔ́ĺ, ní bin nìn fàal̀ee kíǹ ki yáliŋkí.

english_verse: No one plays tambourines or stringed instruments; all noisy celebrating has come to an end.
translation_verse: Bi nín bɔ̀ɔ́ agaŋgan an mɔ̄ puee kaa ti bí, binib nín jīǹ jiŋaal ki tátí puee gbēeǹ, ní bi nín bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati an mɔ̄ puee kúntì.

english_verse: They no longer sing as they drink their wine, and it tastes sour.
translation_verse: Binib kaa ti nyù ndamam ki gà ilan, ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee kíǹ ki tū ní binyɔliibi cee.

english_verse: Towns are crushed and in chaos; houses are locked tight.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kin kaa bí tibanee kpántì adigbun ŋma, adiin kɔkɔ pīī báà ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí kɔ́.

english_verse: Happy times have disappeared from the earth, and people shout in the streets, “We're out of wine!”
translation_verse: Binib bí adan pu ki yáliŋkí yii ndaam kpá. Mmɔn kaa ti bí, ní dipɔɔpindi kúntì kitiŋ nee pu.

english_verse: Cities are destroyed; their gates are torn down.
translation_verse: Adigbun di kíǹ ki yú kitiŋee poon, ní bi gbáń ki wīī ki-punyɔkɔki kɔkɔ pílpil.

english_verse: Nations will be stripped bare, like olive trees or vineyards after the harvest season. Praise the God of Justice
translation_verse: Kitiŋ nee puee, án làá nīn bí anibul kansikin kii bi nín yaa kītì ɔliifi biliŋ, àá bi nín yaa kītì fiinyi biliŋ ki dóò ŋin kīntí isufi pu bí lūlifèe ní. Binib bíi jìkì ifaal pu

english_verse: People in the west shout; they joyfully praise the majesty of the Lord.
translation_verse: Binib bin ŋmátèe bíi tátí ki fàal̀, bi bíi gà ilan ki sòoǹ ti-Dindaan kpaanti pu. Bi nyánní ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ki kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi.

english_verse: And so, everyone in the east and those on the islands should praise the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: «Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan, nimbi bin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. Nimbi bin kóò ntimu mun nnyim māntìi túee, nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu yindi.»

english_verse: From all over the world songs of praise are heard for the God of justice. But I feel awful, terribly miserable. Can anyone be trusted? So many are treacherous! There's No Escape
translation_verse: Ti gbìl̀ ilan tùm̀ kitiŋ kúntilaŋki ki lì yii: «Deedeedaan ń ká tinyool!» Ama man bí yii: «An dóò m-pu ní! An dóò m-pu ní! Nnaabu ŋulɔŋu dee!» Binib bin nyēē bi-jutiibi boonee bí ki nyēē, bi nyēē bi-jutiibi boon an kaa cáá yii bi gbēeǹ.

english_verse: Terror, traps, and pits are waiting for everyone.
translation_verse: Tifaandi nì mbòó nì kulaaŋŋu dɔ̄ ki cí nimbi bin kóò kitiŋ puee.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; if you crawl out of the pit, you will get caught in a trap. The sky has split apart like a window thrown open. The foundations of the earth have been shaken;
translation_verse: Un yaa láa sáǹ ki nyáń tifaandi ŋaanee, làá dāá jēetí mbòó poon ní. Un yaa láa ŋúń ki nyáń mbòó poonee, kulaaŋŋu poon ní u làá dāá kɔ́. Di sá yii yilpu tɔkɔlab cúu pīitì, ní kitiŋ nyeel cīŋkì.

english_verse: the earth is shattered, ripped to pieces.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ fáá fáá iwèeń, kì cīŋkì ki wīī.

english_verse: It staggers and shakes like a drunkard or a hut in a windstorm. It is burdened down with sin; the earth will fall, never again to get up.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ bíi kpìntī kii udanyɔgbilee, kì cìŋkī kii kibiŋ ní kubuŋu cìŋkēe. Ki-kpitii nyìm̀ ki-pu, kì lítì ní kaa ti ŋūǹ kí yīkì. Duulinya beeŋi làá kúntí ní Unimbɔti beel ń kíĺ

english_verse: On that day the Lord will punish the powers in the heavens and the kings of the earth.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan làá já nì ipɔn in kɔkɔ pée bí yilpuee, nì bibɔtiibi bin bí kitiŋ puee.

english_verse: He will put them in a pit and keep them prisoner. Then later on, he will punish them.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì dicilpu kubòóun. Bi làá dāá dū-bi kí pìin̄ kusaarkadiin. Bi làá dāá kàl̄ niin kí yúntí ní bí dāá sòoǹ bi-bɔti.

english_verse: Both the moon and sun will be embarrassed and ashamed. The Lord All-Powerful will rule on Mount Zion in Jerusalem, where he will show its rulers his wonderful glory.
translation_verse: Icoo làá cúú uŋmal nì ŋwìiń. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá nīn sá ubɔti Siiyɔn jool pu, an dàkà yii Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu. U-nyooti làá nīn jìl̀ bitindaŋkpilib nimbiin.

english_verse: You, Lord, are my God! I will praise you for doing the wonderful things you had planned and promised since ancient times.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, sii di sá m-Nimbɔtiu. M làá yòon̄-si yilpu ní kí nyɔ̄ŋkì a-yindi. Di sá yii a ŋáaǹ maamaaci tuuŋŋi ŋin a bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ dooooyee, ŋi pée bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kaa kpántí.

english_verse: You have destroyed the fortress of our enemies, leaving their city in ruins. Nothing in that foreign city will ever be rebuilt.
translation_verse: A dū kitiŋee ki kpántì ditaŋkpakpukul. Kitiŋ kin bi nìn máń digundi ki túee kpántì adigbun. Binicambi tiŋki kin nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄yee kaa ti sá kitiŋ, bi kpá ki làá gíti náań-kì dalba dalba.

english_verse: Now strong and cruel nations will fear and honor you.
translation_verse: An pu ní dinibul din cáá mpɔnee tìì-si tinyool, bin néeń tipɔmbɔti tiŋkinee, binib fàŋkí-si.

english_verse: You have been a place of safety for the poor and needy in times of trouble. Brutal enemies pounded us like a heavy rain or the heat of the sun at noon, but you were our shelter.
translation_verse: Di sá yii sii ní binandambi nìn sáń ki kóò, bifalaadambi nìn sáń ki kóò-si ní dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu. Utaa yaa bíi nèe, sii di sá kibalilaŋ, ŋwìiń yaa tùm̀ee, sii di sá mboon. Di sá yii bin néeń tipɔmbɔtee bum sá kii utaakpaan nín gbáà digundi puee ní,

english_verse: Those wild foreigners struck like scorching desert heat. But you were like a cloud, protecting us from the sun. You kept our enemies from singing songs of victory. The Lord Has Saved Us
translation_verse: a lì kii ŋwìiń nín gbáà kitiŋkuliŋŋi puee ní. A yāntì binicambi wooku ŋmíl̀, kii ditagbandi nín lìkintí ŋwìiń pu án sɔ̀ŋkèe ní. A yàntī bin néeń tipɔmbɔtee laŋyi ŋmīlifí. Ti-Dindaan làá bɔ́ntí jiŋaal kí tīī anibul kɔkɔ

english_verse: On this mountain the Lord All-Powerful will prepare for all nations a feast of the finest foods. Choice wines and the best meats will be served.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá bɔ́ntí jiŋaal ubɔ dijool nee pu kí tīī anibul kɔkɔ. An dāa sá tijimmɔntiil nì ndamɔntiim ní jiŋaal gbantin, jiŋaal un poon bi dāa ŋmóò tinan tin mèeǹ, ki nyù ndaam min dōoǹ ki wāĺ kílkilee.

english_verse: Here the Lord will strip away the burial clothes that cover the nations.
translation_verse: Dijool gbanti puee, u làá cúú kpɔsata un anibul kɔkɔ lōōyee kí lēē, ŋŋaabu ŋun bīī atimbun kɔkɔ puee.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful will destroy the power of death and wipe away all tears. No longer will his people be insulted everywhere. The Lord has spoken!
translation_verse: U làá kúntí ŋkúm kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti làá pítí báà ŋma nyinnyim kí nyāntí u-nibul icoo in cúú-bi kitiŋ nee poonee. Úǹ ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Isirayeel bí dipɔɔpindin ní Moowaab kɔ́ nnaabun

english_verse: At that time, people will say, “The Lord has saved us! Let's celebrate. We waited and hoped— now our God is here.”
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, báà ŋma làá dāá lì yii: «Úǹ di sá ti-Nimbɔtiu! Ti nìn máká u-pu ní u fīī-ti. Úǹ ti-Dindaan pu ní ti nìn máká. Án nīn mɔ̄ǹ-ti tí nīn fàal̀ u nín fīī-tee pu.

english_verse: The powerful arm of the Lord will protect this mountain. The Moabites will be put down and trampled on like straw in a pit of manure.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ŋal làá nīn bīī dijool nee pu!» Ama u làá tāā tāā Moowaab tiŋki kii bi nín tà timool kí ŋmàlim̀ tinaabin poon puee ní.

english_verse: They will struggle to get out, but God will humiliate them no matter how hard they try.
translation_verse: Niinee, kì làá kpátí ki-ŋalii kii unyiŋwaŋkil nín kpátí u-ŋalii puee. Ama nì min kɔkɔ u bíi pɔ̄ɔntée, ti-Dindaan làá sìntī u-lambil taapu.

english_verse: The walls of their fortresses will be knocked down and scattered in the dirt.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá téé a-guŋŋi kí lúkú, aguŋfɔkɔ ŋin bi máń ki māntìi tú-see, u làá téé-ŋi ní ŋí lítí ntampukumin.

english_verse: The time is coming when the people of Judah will sing this song: “Our city is protected. The Lord is our fortress, and he gives us victory.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, bi làá dāá gāā nlan nee Juuda tiŋkin: «Ti cáá kitiŋ kin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Kí ŋmā kí wúń ti-puee, ti-Dindaan dū agun ali ní ki māntìi tú-kì.

english_verse: Open the city gates for a law-abiding nation that is faithful to God.
translation_verse: Pìitīmaan mpunyɔmu kí wàan̄ ditimbundi din nib sá ibaamɔn dambi, ki yú nì Unimbɔti deedeeyee ń jītí kí kɔ́.

english_verse: The Lord gives perfect peace to those whose faith is firm.
translation_verse: Un di yaa nóó-si nì dipɔbil dibee, sii ti-Dindaan tìì udaan ŋgbansɔŋfi, kun puee sii baba pu ní u máká.

english_verse: So always trust the Lord because he is forever our mighty rock.
translation_verse: Nín̄ mákámaan ti-Dindaan pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ti-Dindaan un di sá talku taŋkpalee.

english_verse: God has put down our enemies in their mountain city and rubbed it in the dirt.
translation_verse: U téé bin nìn kóò ajoon yilpuee ki lúkú, ki nāaǹ kitiŋ kin báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí já kí fōōyee. U téé-kì ki lúkú, ki dū-kì ki tɔ́ ntampukumin.

english_verse: Now the poor and abused trample all over that city.” The Lord Can Be Trusted
translation_verse: Binib bin kaa bí tibanee, bin sá biwɔfibee, bíǹ di kíǹ ki tà ki-pu ki còom̄ bi nín là puee.» Iyuntijoolkaa wimmeem

english_verse: Our Lord, you always do right, and you make the path smooth for those who obey you.
translation_verse: Deedeedaan saŋŋu tèen̄ ní, ti-Dindaan, a tàntī u-saŋŋu ní an kaa cáá disampɔl.

english_verse: You are the one we trust to bring about justice; above all else we want your name to be honored.
translation_verse: Ti tàkā nsan ŋun a tīī-ti mara yii tí nóóyee pu, ti-Dindaan, sii pu ní ti máká. Tin ti lèe di sá tí yíiń a-yindi, kí dàkafì a-pu.

english_verse: Throughout the night, my heart searches for you, because your decisions show everyone on this earth how to live right.
translation_verse: Kunyeeuee, m-naŋki fèefī ki nyàab̀-si ní, m nyàab̀-si nì m-pɔbil kɔkɔ. Di sá yii a yaa bíi sòoǹ kitiŋ pu nib bɔtee, ní duulinya nib béetí tin di sá deedee bɔtee.

english_verse: Even when the wicked are treated with mercy in this land of justice, they do wrong and are blind to your glory, our Lord.
translation_verse: Ama unil yaa súń binikpitib saayee, baa béetí tin bi máaǹ kí ŋá án fáatíǹ-see. Báà gba kitiŋ kin poon binib ŋáań tiŋanee, bíǹ ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee ní, kaa wāĺ sii ti-Dindaan nín sá ukpaan puee.

english_verse: Your hand is raised and ready to punish them, but they don't see it. Put them to shame! Show how much you care for us and throw them into the fire intended for your enemies.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a dúkutì a-ŋal kí dáaĺ bi-tafal, ama bíǹ kaa wāĺ-ŋu. Bi làá dāá ká a nín mɔ́tí a-nibul pu nì dineendee, ní icoo ń dāá cúú-bi. Ŋŋmi ŋun a bɔ́ntì ki síiǹ a-nannanliibee di làá dāá wà-bi.

english_verse: You will give us peace, Lord, because everything we have done was by your power.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a tìì-ti dipɔɔsɔŋkil, ní tin kɔkɔ ti bɔ́ntì kí ŋée, sii di fōō ki ŋá ki tīī-ti.

english_verse: Others have ruled over us besides you, our Lord God, but we obey only you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, bikpilib bin kaa sá siiyee di nìn kpōotì-ti, ama sii baba yindi ní ti yíì.

english_verse: Those enemies are now dead and can never live again. You have punished them— they are destroyed, completely forgotten.
translation_verse: Bin kpíìyee kaa ti làá gítiń. Bin kaa ti bée kpántì kii mboonee ní, baa ti làá yīkì. Sii di dáaĺ bi-tafal ki nāaǹ-bi pílpil, ubɔ ń taa ti téetí bi-pu dalba dalba.

english_verse: Our nation has grown because of you, our Lord. We have more land than before, and you are honored. The Lord Gives Life to the Dead
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a yāntì ti-timbundi wíiǹ, a yāntì ti-timbundi wíiǹ ki dàkā a-nyooti, a yāntì ti-tiŋki wāaǹ.

english_verse: When you punished our people, they turned and prayed to you, our Lord.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, dinimbinaamandi poonee, sii watil pú ní ti fàtī ti-nimbikpeeŋu kí túĺ. A yaa dáaĺ ti-tafalee ní ti kíǹ ki bí ki mèé-si.

english_verse: Because of what you did to us, we suffered like a woman about to give birth.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, ti nìn bí a-nimbiin kii upɔdaan di làá màal̀ee. U yáliŋkí imatiŋween ní ki gbáà ibiil.

english_verse: But instead of having a child, our terrible pain produced only wind. We have won no victories, and we have no descendants to take over the earth.
translation_verse: Ti mun nìn cáá dipool, ki yáliŋkì imatiŋween, ama ní ki dāa dūu màl̄ kubuŋu. Taa nìn ŋúń ki cáań difiil kitiŋ pu, kaa tí ŋúń ki cáań binib duulinyan. Bitaŋkpiibi fìkititam nì ikpiti tafadaaldi

english_verse: Your people will rise to life! Tell them to leave their graves and celebrate with shouts. You refresh the earth like morning dew; you give life to the dead.
translation_verse: A-yab bin kpíìyee làá fàtīí ká dimaŋfal, a-taŋkpiibi làá fìkitī. Binib bin dɔ̄ ntampukuminee làá fìntī ní kí nīn tátí nì dipɔɔpindi. Ti-Dindaan làá dāá tīiń-si ŋwalifi malindi, di-puee, kitiŋ ń dāá yàntī bitaŋkpiibi ń fìkitī.

english_verse: Go inside and lock the doors, my people. Hide there for a little while, until the Lord is no longer angry. The Earth and the Sea Will Be Punished
translation_verse: M-nibul, yīkì kí kɔ́ a-dumpu, kí dáaĺ a-kampiiŋi liitil kí pìin̄ a-ba pu. Kɔ́ kí báĺ ŋyunti ŋubɔ poon kí nīn cí ti-Dindaan ŋuul ń sɔ̀ŋkì.

english_verse: The Lord will come out to punish everyone on earth for their sins. And when he does, those who did violent crimes will be known and punished.
translation_verse: Kpèè, ti-Dindaan di nyánní u-kɔŋkooŋŋunee. U làá cùú dáaĺ kitiŋ pu nib tafal bi-kpitii pu. Kitiŋ làá nyāntí fatiku un bi yāaǹee mpaampiin pu, kàa ti làá báĺ binib bin bi nìn kūū kūūyee pu.

english_verse: On that day, Leviathan, the sea monster, will squirm and try to escape, but the Lord will kill him with a cruel, sharp sword. Protection and Forgiveness The Lord said:
translation_verse: Yaadalee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá yòon̄ u-tàataajiki kin jītí, ki sá kikpaŋkpaaŋŋi, ki cáá mpɔnee kí dáaĺ Leefiyatan, ukoobu un sáńee, Leefiyatan, ukoobu un nyí diŋmatindee tafal. U làá dāá kpɔ̀ tiŋkun peebilinti gbanti. Ti-Dindaan nì u-fiinyi sufii kpaabu bɔti

english_verse: At that time you must sing about a fruitful vineyard.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, ní dāá gāā fiinyi sufii kpaabu bun damam mɔ̄ee nlan.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will protect it and always keep it watered. I will guard it day and night to keep it from harm.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan di sá bukpaa gbanti ciitiliu. M yàantí-bu nnyim ní ŋyunti sá kamaa. Ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeuee, m cí-bu ubɔ ń taa pée ŋá-bu ikpiti iba.

english_verse: I am no longer angry. But if it produces thorns, I will go to war against it and burn it to the ground.
translation_verse: Maa ti gíí diŋuul bu-pu. M yaa ká abɔjanaakun nì ikuŋkum bu-poonee, m làá gāā-i kí dū-i kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin í wà.

english_verse: Yet if the vineyard depends on me for protection, it will become my friend and be at peace with me.
translation_verse: Ama un yaa sáǹ ki kɔ́-mee, man nì udaan làá sòoǹ kí gbìlīǹ tɔb ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí ti-kansikin.» Ti-Dindaan làá dū Isirayeel yab kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi

english_verse: Someday Israel will take root like a vine. It will blossom and bear fruit that covers the earth.
translation_verse: Iyunti in bí ki dòoń nee poonee, Jaakɔb nibul làá dāá báań inyaan, Isirayeel làá dāá tɔ̄ mpamu kí púkuḿ, ní kí lòoǹ abil kí gbéeǹ duulinya kɔkɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, didn't punish and kill the people of Israel as fiercely as I punished and killed their enemies.
translation_verse: Ni ká ti-Dindaan dáaĺ u-nibul yab tafal kii u nín nìn dáaĺ bin sàantí-bee tafal pueeee? Ni ká u kūū-bi kii u nín nìn kūū bin nìn kù-bee pueeee?

english_verse: I carefully measured out Israel's punishment and sent the scorching heat to chase them far away.
translation_verse: Aayee, u dáaĺ bi-tafal ní ki jìn̄-bi ki tɔ́ kuyuŋun ntincamun. Kii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú buŋku nín jītí puee, míǹ ní u yāntì u-buŋkpaaŋku yōoǹ-bi ki cáa búntì.

english_verse: There's only one way that Israel's sin and guilt can be completely forgiven: They must crush the stones of every pagan altar and place of worship. The Lord Will Bring His People Together
translation_verse: Jaakɔb nibul kpitii nín làá pítí puee sèé, dikpántil din ní bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam làá cáańee sèé: Bi làá nà isaraafan taŋkpeeŋi dúsi dusi, kii bi nín nà kaluu taŋkpeeŋi ŋí kpántí ŋyim puee. Iwindɔ nì talaalutuukaa saraafaŋyi kaa ti làá nīn cɔ́.

english_verse: Fortress cities are left like a desert where no one lives. Cattle walk through the ruins, stripping the trees bare.
translation_verse: Báà uniseen kaa ti kóò kitiŋ kin ní bi máń digundi ki māntìi túee. Kì kíǹ ki bí fám ní kii kuteeuee. Anabil làá nīn dòoń niin ní ki jīǹ, ki dɔ̀ niin ki ŋùŋfī, ní ki ŋmóò tifaapibiti.

english_verse: When broken branches fall to the ground, women pick them up to feed the fire. But these people are so stupid that the God who created them will show them no mercy.
translation_verse: Tikpaŋkpaal yaa kūń ki kɔ́fì kɔ́fèe, ní binimpoobi ń dāan̄ kí dū ŋŋmi kí sēē. Tiŋman ní, dinibul nee kaa gbìl̀ tibɔti taapu. An pu ní Unimbɔti un náań-bee kaa làá sɔ̄ bi-pu, un di máń-bee kaa làá sɔ̄ bi-saai. Bin kɔkɔ cūtì kuyuŋuee làá fàtīí gítiń

english_verse: The time is coming when the Lord will shake the land between the Euphrates River and the border of Egypt, and one by one he will bring all of his people together.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá gbá u-jimpinti, kí yòon̄ Eefiraati mɔɔl kí tin cáá sāā Eejipiti buŋŋu. U làá dāá kóoǹ nimbi Isirayeel yab ubɔ ubɔ kii idifinee.

english_verse: A loud trumpet will be heard. Then the people of Israel who were dragged away to Assyria and Egypt will return to worship the Lord on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, bi làá dāá búń ŋyiŋkpaan. Niinee, bin nìn wáŋkì ki bíń Asuur tiŋkinee, bin bi nìn jìn̄ ki tɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee ń dāá tíntiń. Bi-kɔkɔ làá dāá dāan̄ kí gbàan̄ ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí jāam̀-u u-circir jool pu, Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: The city of Samaria above a fertile valley is in for trouble! Its leaders are drunkards, who stuff themselves with food and wine. But they will be like flowers that dry up and wilt.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí Samaarii tiŋki, kitiŋ kin di náań nì kibeefuulii ní Eefiraayiim danyɔgbiliibi cáá ki-pu dilambilee! Kì tɔ́kɔ́ digbantandi pu, ditantakal din kpaatanti cáá ntiŋkpamee yilpu, ní bi nyɔ̄kɔntì-kì ní kì ŋān̄. Ama kì náań nì mpumpukum min yɔ́ĺ, ki pá bidanyɔgbiliibi bin gbí ki dɔ̄ ki gèeǹee yil puee ní.

english_verse: Only the Lord is strong and powerful! His mighty hand will strike them down with the force of a hailstorm or a mighty whirlwind or an overwhelming flood.

translation_verse: Awaa ŋin a kpítì ki dū animbil kúti ki nyūntèe, nì ŋin a mɔ́ɔ́ ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntèe làá dāá kpántí ni-cee tijɔkɔŋwan. A làá dāá dū-ŋi kí fá kii titampummoolee ní kí lì-ŋi yii: «Nyāmaan doo!»

english_verse: The Lord will send rain to water the seeds you have planted—your fields will produce more crops than you need, and your cattle will graze in open pastures.
translation_verse: U làá dāá yàntī utaa ń nì iwambool in a búĺee pu. Tijin tin làá lòoǹ a-tiŋki puee làá dāá nīn wīikí tikpil kí nīn ŋān̄. Ŋwiin gbantee, a-waŋkuti làá cù kunaakpaapɔɔu kun wāāyee poon kí jī.

english_verse: Even the oxen and donkeys that plow your fields will be fed the finest grain.
translation_verse: Inaa nì mmamu mun kù a-satee dāa ŋmóò timool tin bi ŋmālim̀ ŋyaamee ní. Bi làá dāá nīn cáá peela nì adɔpantampal ní ki kàfī timool gbanti ki yàantí kitiŋ.

english_verse: On that day people will be slaughtered and towers destroyed, but streams of water will flow from high hills and towering mountains.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun bi làá dāá bɔ̀fì binibee, sintil difɔŋfɔkɔŋi yaa láa lítèe, mbùmbiyaamu làá dāá pùub̀ ajoon nì ŋgbantamu pu.

english_verse: Then the Lord will bandage his people's injuries and heal the wounds he has caused. The moon will shine as bright as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter than usual. It will be like the light of seven days all at once. Assyria Will Be Punished
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun ti-Dindaan làá dāá póob́ u-nibul buuŋyi kí cáaǹ tiweendi tin bi fōōyee, uŋmal làá dāá nīn wāĺ kii ŋwìińee ní, ní ŋwìiń walifiŋu ń dāá nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄ miluli pu kii iwìiń iluli walifiŋuee. Ti-Dindaan làá dāan̄ kí dáaĺ Asuur tiŋki tafal

english_verse: The Lord is coming from far away with his fiery anger and thick clouds of smoke. His angry words flame up like a destructive fire;
translation_verse: Kpèè, ti-Dindaan di páaǹní ndanee. U-ŋuul fòolìń lìblib ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kpaŋkpam. U yaa sòoǹee, diŋuul bí u-nyunculiŋ pu, ní u-limbil bí kii ŋŋmi ŋun wù ki céetí tikɔkɔee.

english_verse: he breathes out a flood that comes up to the neck. He sifts the nations and destroys them. Then he puts a bridle in every foreigner's mouth and leads them to doom.
translation_verse: U-fooku bí kii mbun ŋun gbí ki sāā unil neenee. U dòoń kí cìŋkì atimbun ŋkpitim pu. U làá kpàl̄ anibul nyɔmmu tikúti kí nīn cáá-bi ki yìiǹ laakin baa lèe.

english_verse: The Lord's people will sing as they do when they celebrate a religious festival at night. The Lord is Israel's mighty rock, and his people will be as happy as they are when they follow the sound of flutes to the mountain where he is worshiped.
translation_verse: Nimbi Jeerusaleem yab, ni làá nīn bí ki gà ilan kii ni bí jiŋaal poon kunyeeuee. Ni làá dāá nīn bí dipɔɔpindin kii bi búǹ awul ní ni còom̄ ki yìkintí ki cá ti-Dindaan jool pu, Isirayeel Taŋkpanaakooku ceeyee.

english_verse: The Lord will get furious. His fearsome voice will be heard, his arm will be seen ready to strike, and his anger will be like a destructive fire, followed by thunderstorms and hailstones.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī bí gbìl̄ u-neel ŋun sá ŋkpaanee pu, ní kí yàntī bí ká u-ŋal pɔŋŋu. U làá dàkà u-ŋuukpaandi aŋmilimbil ŋin wù ki céetí tikɔkɔee poon, ní kí yàntī utaa ń tɔ̄, utaaja ń nì ní ataanyiŋkumbil ń lítí.

english_verse: When the Assyrians hear the Lord's voice and see him striking with his iron rod, they will be terrified.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan neel làá yàntī dinyoondi ń kɔ́ Asuur yab, u làá dāá dū u-dɔŋu kí fáá-bi.

english_verse: He will attack them in battle, and each time he strikes them, it will be to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yaa láa fáá-bi ndɔee, ní bí dāá bɔ̀ɔ̀ ŋgaŋgamu nì tibati. U làá dāá yòon̄ u-ŋal yilpu ní kí já nì bi.

english_verse: Long ago the Lord got a place ready for burning the body of the dead king. The place for the fire is deep and wide, the wood is piled high, and the Lord will start the fire by breathing out flaming sulfur.
translation_verse: Bi pée bɔ́ntì ŋŋmi dooooyee, ŋŋmi gbanti sá ki tīī ubɔti mun. Mbòó ŋun wāā ki nyóòyee poonee, bi dū idɔ tikpil ki bíl̀ dikuŋkundi kí kpāā ŋŋmi. Ti-Dindaan fooku kun bí kii farwata ŋmiŋuee di làá dāá fōō idɔee kii farwata di kpáatìi sītì di-puee.

english_verse: You are in for trouble if you go to Egypt for help, or if you depend on an army of chariots or a powerful cavalry. Instead you should depend on and trust the holy Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí binib bin sìntī Eejipiti tiŋkin ki nyàab̀ dijòońdee! Bi máká itaamu pu, ki máká janjatɔrɔkub pu, kun puee bi wīikí tikpil, ki máká bitanjakaliibi pu, bi nín cáá mpɔŋkpaanee pu. Ama baa fātì bi-nimbikpeeŋu Isirayeel circir Nimbɔtiu watil pú, kaa nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: The Lord isn't stupid! He does what he promises, and he can bring doom. If you are cruel yourself, or help those who are evil, you will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ama u mun cáá iciin ki ŋūǹ kí cáań nnaabu. U yaa lī puee, míǹ ní u ŋáań. U jáà nì binikpitib kitil, ki jáà nì dijòońdi din nyánní binikpitib ceeyee.

english_verse: The Egyptians are mere humans. They aren't God. Their horses are made of flesh; they can't live forever. When the Lord shows his power, he will destroy the Egyptians and all who depend on them. Together they will fall.
translation_verse: Eejipiti yab sá binib ní, baa sá inimbɔti. Bi-taamui cáá tiwunnan ní, iaa sá ŋfam. Ti-Dindaan yaa tāntì u-ŋalee, un bàà sá kí jòòyee lítí ní, ní un bālifì dijòońdee ń lítí, ní bi-liitil ń kpāfì kí kpú. Ti-Dindaan un mɔ́tí Jeerusaleem puee

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful said to me, “I will roar and attack like a fearless lion not frightened by the shouts of shepherds trying to protect their sheep. That's how I will come down and fight on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín tùkū-mi puee sèé: «Gbikinti àá kigbikintibiki yaa cúú kuwaŋkuluu ki mùuǹ ki mɔ́tí ku-puee, bi yíì bipikpaaliibi kupaau ní kí kpāfì. Ama ní úǹ kaa fàŋkí bi-tantatii, ní bi-kuŋkuuntii kaa tùkù-u tiba. Míǹ ní man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan yaa láa sīntìń Siiyɔn jool pu kí já kujaauee, án làá dāá nīn bí.»

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will protect Jerusalem like a mother bird circling over her nest.” Come Back to the Lord
translation_verse: Kii unoon nín kpátí u-feeŋyi kí bìin̄ u-biyaamu pu puee, míǹ ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá dāá wúń Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu. U làá dāá wúń ki-pu kí fīī-kì, u làá dāá mɔ̄tì ki-pu kí fōō-kì kí líí.

english_verse: People of Israel, come back! You have completely turned from the Lord.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab, ni fātì ni-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan tikpil. Fàtīí gítiḿmaan u-cee.

english_verse: The time is coming when you will throw away your idols of silver and gold, made by your sinful hands.
translation_verse: Di sá yii yaadalee, báà ŋma làá dāá fá animbil kúti nì sindaariya waaŋi ŋin ni dū ni-ŋalii in sá ikpiti ŋaliiyee ki mɔ́ɔ́yee.

english_verse: The Assyrians will be killed, but not by the swords of humans. Their young men will try to escape, but they will be captured and forced into slavery.
translation_verse: Kitàataajiki ní bi làá dūú kpɔ̀ Asuur yab, ama an kaa làá nīn sá unil yaka. Kitàataajiki di làá nàan̄-bi, ama án kaa dāa sá nisaal tàataajiki. Asuur yab làá dāá sāǹ kitàataajiki gbanti, ní bí dāá cúú bi-janjaliibi bin pɔ̀ɔǹee kí dāá yàntī bí nīn tūǹ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee.

english_verse: Their fortress will fall when terror strikes; their army officers will be frightened and run from the battle. This is what the Lord has said, the Lord whose fiery furnace is built on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: Dinyoondi làá dāá kɔ́ bin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii ditaŋkpalee bí sāǹ, ní kufaaŋŋu ń kɔ́ bi-janjakpilib ní bí sāǹ kí fá bi-ŋaabiki. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ, úǹ un ŋmilimbil bí Siiyɔn jool pu, ní u-ŋmiŋu fòol̄ lìblib Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee.

english_verse: A king and his leaders will rule with justice.
translation_verse: Ubɔti ubɔ làá dāá jī dibeel nì deedee, ní abɔtibil ń dāá ŋúb́ kitiŋ ibaamɔn saŋŋun.

english_verse: They will be a place of safety from stormy winds, a stream in the desert, and a rock that gives shade from the heat of the sun.
translation_verse: Bi-kansikin báà ŋma làá dāá nīn sá kii laakin kubuŋu yaa bíi jītí binib sáń kí báĺee, kii laakin utaaja yaa bíi nì binib sáń ki kóòyee, kii mbun ŋun di pùub̀ kitiŋkuliŋŋi puee, kii ditaŋkpal din tìì mboon kitiŋ kin tùm̀ee poonee.

english_verse: Then everyone who has eyes will open them and see, and those who have ears will pay attention.
translation_verse: Bin nimbiliŋ wāĺee kaa dāa gíti jɔ̀b̀, bin tafaliŋ gbìl̀ee dāa ŋátí bi-tafaliŋ kí pīlifì.

english_verse: All who are impatient will take time to think; everyone who stutters will talk clearly.
translation_verse: Nnaatuumu làá dāá dàkafì kí gbìl̄ tibɔti taapu, binib bin sòoǹ dibeebeelee dāa kíǹ ki sòoǹ cábcab.

english_verse: Fools will no longer be highly respected, and crooks won't be given positions of honor.
translation_verse: Baa dāa gíti tìì ugbaan jilma, kaa dāa gíti yíì ukiildi yii unimɔnti.

english_verse: Fools talk foolishness. They always make plans to do sinful things, to lie about the Lord, to let the hungry starve, and to keep water from those who are thirsty.
translation_verse: Ugbaan sòoǹ tigbaambɔti ŋma ní, ní u-pɔbilinee, u dàkafī tikpitil ŋma. U tūǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi, ní ki sòoǹ ki bíiĺ ti-Dindaan. Waa pūǹ un ŋkùm cááyee ú jī, kaa pūǹ un nnyinnyoo cááyee ú nyɔ̀.

english_verse: Cruel people tell lies— they do evil things, and make cruel plans to destroy the poor and needy, even when they beg for justice.
translation_verse: Ukiildi úǹ tūǹ atuŋkpiti ŋma ní. U bɔ́ntí atuŋkpiti ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn kí nàan̄ uwɔfi. Ama kun uwɔfi gbanti pée nyàab̀ee di sá bí pɔ̀-u.

english_verse: But helpful people can always be trusted to make helpful plans. Punishment for the Women of Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ama unimɔnti úǹ cáá ilandɔkɔmɔnti ní, ní atuun ŋin u tūǹee sá atummɔnti. Bi kpáafì Jeerusaleem nimpoobi

english_verse: Listen to what I say, you women who are carefree and careless!
translation_verse: Nimbi binimpoobi bin kaa dàkafī tiba puee, yīkìmaan kí pīlifìmaan-mi. Nimbi bisapɔmbi bin máká ni-ba puee, kpòom̄maan ni-tafaliŋ kí pīlifì.

english_verse: You may not have worries now, but in about a year, the grape harvest will fail, and you will tremble.
translation_verse: Nì dibindi diba boonee, nimbi bin máká ni-ba puee, ni-wunti làá dāá jìkì. Di sá yii bi dāa kìtī fiinyi biliŋ kí dóó, ní tiba kaa dāa gíti bí bí kìtī.

english_verse: Shake and shudder, you women without a care! Strip off your clothes— put on sackcloth.
translation_verse: Nín̄ jìkìmaan, nimbi binimpoobi bin kaa dàkafī tiba puee, nín̄ yáliŋkímaan, nimbi bisapɔmbi bin máká ni-ba puee. Pèetīmaan ni-wampeeŋkaati, lòotīmaan dicancaŋgbeel kí dū kpɔsatab kí cúú ni-cammu.

english_verse: Slap your breasts in sorrow because of what happened to the fruitful fields and vineyards,
translation_verse: Nín̄ fátímaan ni-biŋŋi nì kunimbaau kí nīn yáliŋkí tisati tin ŋān̄ee nì fiinyi kpaaŋŋi ŋin lòoǹ sàka sakee pu.

english_verse: and to the happy homes in Jerusalem. The land of my people is covered with thorns.
translation_verse: Nín̄ sūm̀maan m-nibul tiŋki kin pu ikuŋkum nyáńee pu, nín̄ sūm̀maan adiin ŋin kɔkɔ poon dipɔɔpindi bí, ní kitiŋ bí jiŋaal poonee pu.

english_verse: The palace will be deserted, the crowded city empty. Fortresses and towers will forever become playgrounds for wild donkeys and pastures for sheep. God's Spirit Makes the Difference
translation_verse: Bi dū dibeecindi ki fá, ubɔ kaa ti bí kitiŋ kin poon an nìn tùm̀ee. Oofeel tincaliiki nì sintil difɔkɔku làá dòon̄ kikuliŋŋi kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. Niin ní kumooun mammu dāa bí ki léelikí, ní tipicaŋkpun dāa ŋmóò timool. Dikpántikpaandi bí ki dòoń

english_verse: When the Spirit is given to us from heaven, deserts will become orchards thick as fertile forests.
translation_verse: Ŋwindalee, ŋfam làá dāá kpákatiń ti-pu. Niinee ní kuteeu làá dāá kpántí asubiŋmɔkaa kpaabu, ní asubiŋmɔkaa kpaabu ń dāá kpántí kubambaŋŋu.

english_verse: You, the Lord's people, will live in peace, calm and secure,
translation_verse: M-nibul làá dāá nīn kóò laakin ŋgbansɔŋfi bée, ikɔŋkoon in poon unil bí kaa fàŋkí tibee, laakin diŋuŋfil nì dipɔɔsɔŋkil bée.

english_verse: even if hailstones flatten forests and cities.
translation_verse: Ama ataanyiŋkumbil làá dāá lítí kubambaŋŋuee pu, ní kitiŋee ń dāá sìntī taapu taapu.

english_verse: You will have God's blessing, as you plant your crops beside streams, while your donkeys and cattle roam freely about.
translation_verse: Án dāa sá-ni mmɔn ní dāá ŋmā kí bɔ̄l̀ ni-wamboolii laakin kamaa nnyim bée caŋin, ní kí dāá gbìntī unaa nì kimaŋ kí líí.

english_verse: You defeated my people. Now you're in for trouble! You've never been destroyed, but you will be destroyed; you've never been betrayed, but you will be betrayed. When you have finished destroying and betraying, you will be destroyed and betrayed in return.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí sii un bíiĺ, ama ní ubɔ kaa bíil̀ siiyee, sii un nyēē a-jutiibi boon, ama ní ubɔ kaa nyēē a-boonee. A yaa láa bíil̀ ki dóòyee, bi làá dāá bīil̀ si mun. A yaa láa nyáń a-jutiibi boon ki dóòyee, bi làá dāá nyā sii mun boon.

english_verse: Please, Lord, be kind to us! We depend on you. Make us strong each morning, and come to save us when we are in trouble.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, dàkà-ti a-ŋanti! Sii pu ní timbi máká. Nín̄ sá ti-pɔŋŋu kutaafaau kamaa, ní kí nīn sá ti-fiiliu dinimbinaamandi poon.

english_verse: Nations scatter when you roar and show your greatness.
translation_verse: A yaa téeńee, anibul sáń kí kátí ní, a yaa yáatì ki yúl̀ee, atimbun yàl̀ ní.

english_verse: We attack our enemies like swarms of locusts; we take everything that belongs to them.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bí kíĺ ki bíi fúkuĺ-ni, a lì kii inaakitoon nín gbáb̀ kí bìin̄ tiwan pu puee. Bi làá gbáb́ kí bìin̄ tigaajawan pu bɔ̀mmm kii inaakee.

english_verse: You, Lord, are above all others, and you live in the heavens. You have brought justice and fairness to Jerusalem;
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tɔ́kɔ́ tikɔkɔ pu, kun puee u kóòń yilpu ní. U yāntì deedee nì ibaamɔn kíǹ ki bí Siiyɔn jool pu.

english_verse: you are the foundation on which we stand today. You always save us and give true wisdom and knowledge. Nothing means more to us than obeying you. The Lord Will Do Something
translation_verse: Sii ti-Dindaan nibul, a làá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin. Iciin nì dinyil sá tigaajati tin fìil̄ee ní. Á nīn fàŋkí ti-Dindaanee sá tigaajawan ní. Ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̄ u-tundi

english_verse: Listen! Our bravest soldiers are running through the streets, screaming for help. Our messengers hoped for peace, but came home crying.
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan Ariyeel yab bí ki kūuntí adan pu. Ŋgbansɔŋfi tuuŋyi bí ki sūǹ lɔ̀lɔlɔ.

english_verse: No one travels anymore; every road is empty. Treaties are broken, and no respect is shown to any who keep promises.
translation_verse: Adan kíǹ ki dɔ̄ fám ní, binib kaa ti còom̄ isan pu. Bi kpītì mpèé, ki fá ntimu, kaa ti pée fātìi tɔ́ báà unil.

english_verse: Fields are dry and barren; Mount Lebanon wilts with shame. Sharon Valley is a desert; the forests of Bashan and Carmel have lost their leaves.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kɔ́ kunimbaaun ki bí ki kōō. Leebanɔn jool sufii bíi yɔ́l̀, ní icoo kɔ́-dì. Saarɔn tiŋki kpántì kii kuteeuee. Baasan tiŋki nì Kaarmeel jool kaa ti cáá isufi.

english_verse: But the Lord says, “Now I will do something and be greatly praised.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee m làá tɔ̄ m-tundi, kɔŋkɔnnee m làá yáatí kí yūĺ, m làá dàkà m-pɔŋŋu.

english_verse: Your deeds are straw that will be set on fire by your very own breath.
translation_verse: Ni nín bɔ́ntí kí ŋá tiŋyee sá kii timɔkulindee ní. Ni-fooku di sá ŋŋmi ŋun làá dāá wà-nee.

english_verse: Everyone, both far and near, come look at what I have done. See my mighty power!” Punishment and Rewards
translation_verse: Nimbi bin bíń ndandatee, ní pīlifìmaan tin ní m ŋée. Ní nimbi bin bí ki pìlīǹ dooyee, ní béémaan m-pɔŋŋu nín sá ŋuŋyee.»

english_verse: Those terrible sinners on Mount Zion tremble as they ask in fear, “How can we possibly live where a raging fire never stops burning?”
translation_verse: Dinyoondi kɔ́ bikpitiŋaliibi bin bí Siiyɔn jool puee, binikpitib wunti fōō dijinjikil. Bi kíǹ ki bàlifī yii: «Ti-kansikin ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ ŋŋmi ŋun wù ki céetí nee caŋin? Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ kí kɔ́ĺ aŋmilimbil ŋin kaa kúù jaanjaan nee?»

english_verse: But there will be rewards for those who live right and tell the truth, for those who refuse to take money by force or accept bribes, for all who hate murder and violent crimes.
translation_verse: - See unil un nóó deedee saŋŋu, ki sòoǹ ibaamɔnee. An niliuee kaa ŋáań tipɔmbɔti kí ká ipaati, úǹ kaa kíikí kí fōō dinyɔɔŋeebil jim. Bi yaa bíi sòoǹ nnikpaakoon bɔtee, u ŋēeb̀ u-tafaliŋ ní kí taa gbìl̄. U ŋúb̀ u-nimbiliŋ kí taa wāl̀ tikpitil.

english_verse: They will live in a fortress high on a rocky cliff, where they will have food and plenty of water. The Lord Is Our King
translation_verse: Udaan làá nīn kóò ajoon yilpu. Kutaŋkpanaakoou di làá nīn sá u-balilaŋki. U làá nīn kāntí tijin ki jīǹ, ní nnyinyɔkaam kpá kí lóó-u. Jeerusaleem tiŋki làá ká difiil

english_verse: With your own eyes you will see the glorious King; you will see his kingdom reaching far and wide.
translation_verse: A-nimbil làá dāá ká ubɔti u-nyaaŋku kɔkɔ poon, ní kí dāá ká kitiŋ nín pée dɔ̄ ki wāā puee.

english_verse: Then you will ask yourself, “Where are those officials who terrified us and forced us to pay such heavy taxes?”
translation_verse: A làá dāá dàkafì tin nìn kɔ̄ntí-si dinyoondee pu ní kí bàlifì a-ba yii: «Bin nìn kàaǹ lampoo nimbiliŋee bí la? Bin nìn kpèé lampoobee bí la? Bin nìn kpèé sintil difɔkɔŋee bí la?»

english_verse: You will never again have to see the proud people who spoke a strange and foreign language you could not understand.
translation_verse: Aa làá dāá gíti ká dinibul din cáá dilambilee, dinibul din sooŋyi unil kaa gbìl̀ taapuee, isooncaan in báà ubɔ kaa gbìl̀ee.

english_verse: Look to Mount Zion where we celebrate our religious festivals. You will see Jerusalem, secure as a tent with pegs that cannot be pulled up and fastened with ropes that can never be broken.
translation_verse: Kpèè Siiyɔn tiŋki kin poon ti kpáfí ki jīǹ jiŋaalibee, a-nimbil làá dāá ká Jeerusaleem, dipɔɔsɔŋkil tiŋki. Kì dāa sá tanti un ní baa làá ti sútée, tanti un kpakpaaŋi baa làá ti cóotée, tanti un ŋmiii baa làá ti kútí dalba dalbee.

english_verse: Our wonderful Lord will be with us! There will be deep rivers and wide streams safe from enemy ships. The Lord Is Our Judge
translation_verse: Niin ní ti-Dindaan làá dàkà-ti u-pɔŋŋu. Án dāa sá laakin ní amɔɔ nì ibun in wāāyee bée, baa dāa ŋàal̀ niin iŋaliŋfi, meelab bin sá bikpaambee kaa làá dāá dùtī niin.

english_verse: The Lord is our judge and our ruler; the Lord is our king and will keep us safe.
translation_verse: Tiŋman pu, ti-Dindaan di sá ti-bɔsoonliu, úǹ di sá ti-marayóonliu. Ti-Dindaan di sá ti-bɔtiu, úǹ di sá ti-fiiliu.

english_verse: But your nation is a ship with its rigging loose, its mast shaky, and its sail not spread. Someday even you that are lame will take everything you want from your enemies.
translation_verse: A-ŋmiii cúu kútì ní nee, iaa ti ŋúb́ ndɔ ŋun pu meela ŋaabuŋu sàkantée, baa ti ŋūǹ kí sàkan̄ meela ŋaabuŋu ndɔ pu. An pu ní ti làá dāá yàkatī tigaajawan tikpil. Ki kpáaǹ gba bin tà bi-taaŋi puee làá dāá kūtì ti-pu tí fūkul̀.

english_verse: The Lord will forgive your sins, and none of you will say, “I feel sick.”
translation_verse: Binib bin kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, ubɔ kaa dāa gíti lì yii: «M būǹ!» Binib bin kóò niinee làá dāá ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam.

english_verse: Everyone of every nation, the entire earth, and all its creatures, come here and listen!
translation_verse: Atimbun, sútiḿmaan doo kí dāá pīlifì, anibul, ní kpòom̄maan ni-tafal kí pīlifì. Kitiŋ nì tin kɔkɔ bí ki-poonee ń pīlifì, duulinya nì tin kɔkɔ nyáń u-nee ń pīlifì.

english_verse: The Lord is terribly angry with the nations; he has condemned them to be slaughtered.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan fōō mbum atimbun kɔkɔ nib pu, u gíí diŋuul tikpil bi-janjakitiŋi kɔkɔ pu. U lēē ki síiǹ bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi, u dū-bi ki tīī bí bɔ̀fì kí kúntí-bi.

english_verse: Their dead bodies will be left to rot and stink; their blood will flow down the mountains.
translation_verse: Bi-nib bin bi kūūyee dɔ̄ kitiŋ fìlfil, bi-nikpiliŋ sūū ki núukì, ní bi-fatikuu pùub̀ ajoon pu ki sìntī.

english_verse: Each star will disappear— the sky will roll up like a scroll. Everything in the sky will dry up and wilt like leaves on a vine or fruit on a tree. Trouble for Edom
translation_verse: Iŋmalbijaa kitil làá dāá yàl̄. Kutagbɔŋu làá kpáb́ kii kugbɔŋuee, ní tin kɔkɔ pée bí ku-puee ń kìtī kí lítiń kitiŋ, kii fiinyi subu àá fiigi subu faati nín gbátí kí lítí puee.

english_verse: After the sword of the Lord has done what it wants to the skies above, it will come down on Edom, the nation that the Lord has doomed for destruction.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan tàataajiki nyáń ki páaǹní kutagbɔŋu pu. Kì lítì Eedoom tiŋki pu, dinibul din ní u lēē kí kpɔ̀ kí céetée.

english_verse: The sword of the Lord is covered with blood from lambs and goats, together with fat from kidneys of rams. This is because the Lord will slaughter many people and make a sacrifice of them in the city of Bozrah and everywhere else in Edom.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tàataajiki nyùn̄ fatiku ki bál̀, kì ŋmɔ́ ŋkpam ki díkí, a lì kii apibil nì iŋɔjaa fatikuuee, a lì kii ŋkpam min bīī ipijaa ceebiliŋ puee. Bɔsiraa, ditiŋyilinee, ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì kí ŋá saraa ubɔ. Bi làá pɔ̀fì binib tikpil Eedoom tiŋkin.

english_verse: Edom's leaders are wild oxen. They are powerful bulls, but they will die with the others. Their country will be soaked with their own blood, and its soil made fertile with their own fat.
translation_verse: Bi nì ipɔɔnaa nì anabil nì inajaa di làá kpāfì kí lítí. Bi-tiŋki làá nyɔ̀ fatiku kí báĺ, ní bi-tam ń nyɔ̀ ŋkpam kí díkí.

english_verse: The Lord has chosen the year and the day, when he will take revenge and come to Zion's defense.
translation_verse: Án sá ŋwiin ŋun ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̀ Eedoom yab ipɔntoonee ní, dibindi din ní u làá mɔ̄tì Siiyɔn pu kí pà Eedoom yab bi-tuuŋŋi paatee ní.

english_verse: Edom's streams will turn into tar and its soil into sulfur— then the whole country will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Eedoom tiŋki buŋyi làá kpántí aŋɔ, ní ki-tam ń kpántí farwata. Kì làá kpántí kii aŋɔ un bí ki wùee ní.

english_verse: It will burn night and day and never stop smoking. Edom will be a desert, generation after generation; no one will ever travel through that land.
translation_verse: An yaa sá kunyeeuaaa, ŋwiimpuɔɔɔ, ŋu kpá ki làá kpú. Ŋu-nyiim làá nīn jɔ́ḿ kutaa pu ní ki cá jaanjaan. Kitiŋ gbanti làá kpántí kii kuteeuee ní ki cá abin abin, báà uniseen kaa dāa gíti còom̄ ki jītí niin.

english_verse: Owls, hawks, and wild animals will make it their home. God will leave it in ruins, merely a pile of rocks. The End of Edom
translation_verse: Ditulinjool nì kilabinsaŋ di làá dāá nīn kíǹ ki yì-kì, kitulinjakpatibooi nì digaliŋgaal di làá dāá nīn kóò ki-ni. Ti-Dindaan làá dāá tàntī dinàandi ŋmiiŋu Eedoom tiŋki pu, u làá dāá kpátí-kì ní tiba nì tiba kaa dāa gíti bí ki-pu.

english_verse: Edom will be called “Kingdom of Nothing.” Its rulers will also be nothing.
translation_verse: Akpambal kaa dāa gíti bí kí kàan̄ ubɔti, abɔtibil kɔkɔ dāa kpíì ki dóò dee.

english_verse: Its palaces and fortresses will be covered with thorns; only wolves and ostriches will make their home there.
translation_verse: Ikuŋkum làá dāá nyā ki-beeciŋŋin, sintil difɔkɔŋi dāa kpántí abɔjanaakun nì ŋkuŋkumbɔmu ŋma ní. Niin làá dāá kpántí sinsiŋkub kɔŋkooŋŋu, kí dāá kpántí atulinjoo dumpu.

english_verse: Wildcats and hyenas will hunt together, demons will scream to demons, and creatures of the night will live among the ruins.
translation_verse: Ilambunti dāa tūŋkí isaakpan nsanni, ní iŋɔjaa ń dāá kóoǹ kí kpāfì niin. Niin ní Liliiti, kunyeeu faŋfantiu dāa kóò. Niin ní u dāa kāntí diŋuŋfil.

english_verse: Owls will nest there to raise their young among its shadows, while families of vultures circle around.
translation_verse: Niin ní ukoobu làá dāá ŋá u-diiku, kí tɔ̄ ajin, kí wùkun̄ ŋi-pu, kí wúń ŋi-pu ŋí dāá kákatí. Niin mun ní kaajiikub dāa kpáfí, kaajiiku kamaa nì u-ŋàliŋu.

english_verse: In The Book of the Lord you can search and find where it is written, “The Lord brought together all of his creatures by the power of his Spirit. Not one is missing.”
translation_verse: Ni yaa nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan gbɔŋkunee, ni làá ká bi ŋmàn̄ yii: «Bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa làá fɔ́tí, báà ubɔ kpá kí fá u-juti, di sá ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔn ní mara nyáń, u-Fam di kóoǹ-bi ki kpáfì.

english_verse: Thirsty deserts will be glad; barren lands will celebrate and blossom with flowers.
translation_verse: Án nīn mɔ̄ǹ kuteeu nì kitiŋkuliŋŋi, kitiŋ kin pu nnyim kpée ń nīn fàal̀ kí púkuḿ.

english_verse: Deserts will bloom everywhere and sing joyful songs. They will be as majestic as Mount Lebanon, as glorious as Mount Carmel or Sharon Valley. Everyone will see the wonderful splendor of the Lord our God. God Changes Everything *
translation_verse: Tisatin pumpukum ń bìin̄ ki-pu. Nín̄ fàal̀, nín̄ fàal̀ kí nīn fátí iwiliili. Ti-Dindaan làá tīī-si Leebanɔn jooŋŋi nyooti juti, kí tīī-si Kaarmeel jool nì Saarɔn timpiliŋki nyaaŋku. Niinee báà ŋma làá dāá ká ti-Dindaan nyooti, ti-Nimbɔtiu nyaaŋku.

english_verse: Here is a message for all who are weak, trembling, and worried:
translation_verse: Ní pɔ̄ɔkìmaan iŋal in gīīyee, kí pɔ̄ɔkì atabiŋyil ŋin yɔ̄tèe.

english_verse: “Cheer up! Don't be afraid. Your God is coming to punish your enemies. God will take revenge on them and rescue you.”
translation_verse: Tùkùmaan bin pɔbiliŋ bíil̀ee yii: <Ní kámaan dipɔbil, ní taa fàŋkìmaan. Kpèèmaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. U dòoń kí tɔ̀-ni ipɔntoon kí téeǹ ni-nannanliibi tikpitil tin bi ŋá-nee. Ni-Nimbɔtiu u-ba di dòoń kí fīī-ni nee.>

english_verse: The blind will see, and the ears of the deaf will be healed.
translation_verse: Niinee, bijɔfub nimbiliŋ làá ŋúbití, ní bitafakpaafub tafaliŋ ń ŋátí.

english_verse: Those who were lame will leap around like deer; tongues once silent will shout for joy. Water will rush through the desert.
translation_verse: Niinee, udeen làá dāá nīn yùkufī kii upeemanee, ní umuun ń dāá nīn kíǹ ki tátí mpɔn ki fàal̀. Nnyim làá dāá cɔ́tí kuteeu pu, ní ibun pùub̀ kitiŋkuliŋŋi pu.

english_verse: Scorching sand will turn into a lake, and thirsty ground will flow with fountains. Grass will grow in deserts, where packs of wild dogs once made their home. God's Sacred Highway
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kin tùm̀ kpaŋkpamee làá kpántí mbúun, inyimbul làá cɔ́tí nnyinnyoo tiŋki poon. Laakin ní sinsiŋkub nìn dɔ̀ee, niin làá kpántí kupuu ní tikati ń nyā.

english_verse: A good road will be there, and it will be named “God's Sacred Highway.” It will be for God's people; no one unfit to worship God will walk on that road. And no fools can travel on that highway.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá tɔ̄ didandi diba niin, kí dāá nīn yíì-dì yii <circir saŋŋu>. Unil un kaa bí circiree kaa dāa dì-ŋu, ŋu dāa sá ki tīī ti-Dindaan nibul ní. Báà ugbaan ubɔ kaa dāa yìntī kí dī-ŋu.

english_verse: No lions or other wild animals will come near that road; only those the Lord has saved will travel there.
translation_verse: Gbikinti ubɔ dāa kpá niin, upeecuncuti ubɔ kaa dāa jītí niin. Baa dāa kāntí tíǹ gbanti báà tiba niin. Binib bin ti-Dindaan fōō ki líìyee baba di dāa dì nsan gbanti.

english_verse: The people the Lord has rescued will come back singing as they enter Zion. Happiness will be a crown everyone will always wear. They will celebrate and shout because all sorrows and worries will be gone far away.
translation_verse: Niin ní bin ti-Dindaan dá ki líìyee làá dī kí fàtīí gítiń. Bi làá bàń Siiyɔn jool pu ki gà ilan ki fàal̀. Bi làá dāá gbí mmɔn ŋun kaa kúntée. Mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi làá dāá céeǹ-bi ní kunimbaau nì iyaliŋki ń gbèen̄.

english_verse: Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him. Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ní taa yàntī Eeseekiyaasi ń mɔ̄ntì-ni. U bí ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan làá fīī-ti!> Atimbun ŋin kíǹee waaŋi ŋúń ki fīī ŋi-timmu ki nyántì Asuur bɔtiu ŋaanaaa?

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted out in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Asuur yab janjakpiliuee yíkìi síl̀ ní ki téeń mpɔn Juuda yab sooŋyin yii: «Ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti tin ubɔtikpaan, Asuur bɔtiu cáá kí sòoǹee!

english_verse: What happened to the gods of Hamath, Arpad, and Sepharvaim? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?
translation_verse: Amaati nì Aripaadi yab waaŋi bí la? Seefarfayiim yab waaŋi bí la? Ŋi ŋúń ki fīī Samaarii tiŋki ki nyántì m-ŋaanaaa?

english_verse: Three of the king's highest officials came out of Jerusalem to meet him. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: Ní Yiilkiyaawuu jipɔɔn Eeliyaakiim un kpèé ubɔti cindee, nì ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Seebina nì Asaafi jipɔɔn Yoowa un kpáafí ubɔti gbɔntee nyáń ki túŋkì ujanjakpilee.

english_verse: The Assyrian commander told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ee ní ujanjakpilee bí-bi yii: «Ní cùú tùkù Eeseekiyaasi yii tibɔti tin ní Ubɔtikpaan, Asuur bɔtiu sòon̄ee sèé: <Ba pu ní a máká ní?

english_verse: Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: A dàkafī yii anyɔɔbun fám ŋūǹ kí fōō kujaau bɔ́ntitam nì dibaatandi paaŋŋu kí já kujaauaaa? Ŋma pu ní a baasii máká ní ki yíkì kaa kíí aba pu man cee na?

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Eejipiti tiŋki kin sá kii kukaluu kun gíìyee pu ní a mákáaa? Saa nyí yii unil un yaa dū u-ŋal ki nyīī ku-puee, ku gífí udaan níii! Too, míǹ ní Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo sá ki tīī bin kɔkɔ dū bi-mákal ki páaǹ u-puee.>

english_verse: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord, your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
translation_verse: An yaa yíì a làá lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu pu ní timbi máká.> An kaa sá sii di kúntì ipaan in bí ŋgbantamu pu bi jáaḿ Unimbɔtee nì u-saraafaŋyaaa? M nyí sii di bí Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab yii: <An sá nsaraafan ŋun bí Jeerusaleem tinkin doo nee baba nimbiin ní ní nīn gbàantí ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaanaa!>

english_verse: The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people! He will give you
translation_verse: A yaa là sii nì m-kpiliu Asuur bɔtiu ń kpáká kí kpèè. A yaa ŋúń ki ká bitanjakaliibi, man làá tīī-si itaamu kutukub bili.

english_verse: How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
translation_verse: Aa kpáàa ŋūǹ kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ m-kpiliu tɔntɔnliibi kiwaai gba. Kin ba pu ní a nín máká Eejipiti pu ú tīī-si janjatɔrɔkub nì itaamu na!

english_verse: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
translation_verse: A dàkafī yii ti-Dindaan kaa là ní m dɔ́miń kí já nì kitiŋ nee kí nàan̄-kàaa? Ti-Dindaan u-ba di bí-mi yii: <Cùú já nì kitiŋ nee kí nàan̄-kì!>»

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Eeliyaakiim nì Seebina nì Yoowa bí Asuur janjakpiliuee yii: «Ti gbāam̀-si ní, sòoǹ nì timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi Aram yab sooŋyi poon, di sá yii ti gbìl̀-i. Taa ti sòoǹ nì ti eebru sooŋyi poon, kun puee binib tɔ́kɔ́ digundi pu ki pílifí.»

english_verse: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you!”
translation_verse: Ama ní ujanjakpilee kíí yii: «A dàkafī yii a-kpiliu nì sii baba ní m-kpiliu túnní-mi yii ḿ cáań tibɔti nee kí sòoǹaaa? Tibɔti gbanti sá ki tīī binib bin kɔkɔ bí agun pu nee mun ní. An kaa làá ti yúntí, ni nì bi làá ŋmɔ́ ni-binti kí nyɔ̀ ni-nyeem.»

english_verse: Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Ní taa yàntī Eeseekiyaasi ń kīil̀-ni ní dū ni-mákal kí páań ti-Dindaan pu. U bí ki lì yii: <Báà án ŋá pu, ti-Dindaan làá fīī-ti, kitiŋ nee kpá ki kɔ́ Asuur bɔtiu ŋaan!>

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah. Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: Ní taa pīlifì Eeseekiyaasi, ama ní pīlifì tin Asuur bɔtiu bí ki sòoǹ-ni nee. Píímaan-mi kubɔɔtiiu, ní sāǹ kí kɔ́maan-mi! Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, báà ŋma làá ŋmɔ́ u-fiinyi nì u-fiigi subiliŋ, ní kí nyɔ̀ u-lɔkɔu nyim,

english_verse: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards and raise your own grain.
translation_verse: kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun m làá dāan̄ kí yòon̄-ni kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin bí kii ni-yaka nee poonee. Kitiŋ gbanti poonee, bilee nì ndamam bí, ní tikpaajin nì fiinyi sufii sati bí.

english_verse: None of those gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord, your God, can do any better?
translation_verse: Ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ waaŋi poonee, dilal di ŋúń ki fīī di-tiŋki ki nyántì m-ŋaan? Kin án làá dī mana ní ti-Dindaan ń fīī Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí nyāntí m-ŋaan?»

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Yiilkiyaawuu jipɔɔn Eeliyaakiim un kpèé ubɔti cindee, nì ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Seebina nì Asaafi jipɔɔn Yoowa un kpáafí ubɔti gbɔntee nín gítí ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi cee. Bi nìn dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin bi pēēyee, ní ki dū tibɔti tin ujanjakpilee sòon̄ee ki máafì-u.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi nín gbìl̄ tin bi máafì-uee ní u cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì, ki dū kutuku ki pēeǹ ní ki nín cá ti-Dindaan diikun.

english_verse: The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared. Hezekiah Prays (
translation_verse: Amaati bɔtiu nì Aripaadi bɔtiu nì Layiir nì Seefarfayiim nì Eena nì Iwa bɔtiibi bí la díǹ pu na?» Ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi wimmeem (Kpèè

english_verse: Isaiah, these are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Yeesaya ceeyee ní ki bí-u yii: «Eeseekiyaasi nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá-ti dinimbinaamandi nì ditafadaaldi nì icoo wiiŋŋu ní. A lì kii kibiki di bīń ki-na poon ki ŋmāntì bí bàà màal̀-kì, ama ní unaati kaa cáá ŋfam kí núuĺ kibiki ń nyānnée.

english_verse: Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
translation_verse: An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu tin máaǹ ki gbìl̄ tibɔti tin Asuur bɔtiu janjakpiliu sòon̄ee. U-kpiliu túnní-u u dɔ́miń ki sīī Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee. An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu tin gbìl̄ tibɔti tin u sòon̄ee, ki làá dáaĺ u-tafal. An puee mèè kí tīī u-nibul din kíǹee.>»

english_verse: When these leaders came to me,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi tɔntɔnliibi bin u túee nín cá Yeesaya cee.

english_verse: I told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah: I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ee ní Yeesaya tùkū-bi yii: «Ní gítí kí tùkù ni-kpiliu yii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Taa fàŋkì anyɔɔbun ŋin a gbìl̄ Asuur bɔtiu janjakpiliu sòon̄ee, u nín sòon̄ ki bíil̀-mi puee.

english_verse: I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
translation_verse: Bi làá cáań tibɔti tiba kí tùkù ubɔti ní ḿ yàntī ú nīn gítí u-tiŋkin. U-tiŋkin niin ní m làá yàntī bí dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀-u.>» Seenakeeriibi fātìi kpìl̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋki (Kpèè

english_verse: Meanwhile the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
translation_verse: Ujanjakpilee nín gbìl̄ yii u-kpiliu Asuur bɔtiu yíkì Lakiisi tiŋki ki cūtìi bíi jáà nì Liibina tiŋkee, ní u mun nín cá niin ki cūtìi ká-u.

english_verse: About this same time, the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu nìn gbìl̄ yii Eejipiti bɔtiu Tiiraka un sá Kuusi tiŋkinee dòoń kí já nì u. Niinee ní u tí tú binib Eeseekiyaasi cee ki bí yii:

english_verse: Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me.
translation_verse: «Ní cùú tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi yii: <A-Nimbɔtiu un pu ní a dū a-mákal ki páaǹee ń taa kīil̀-si kí lì yii Jeerusaleem tiŋki kaa làá kɔ́ Asuur bɔtiu ŋaan.

english_verse: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?
translation_verse: Sisi a-ba gbìl̄ Asuur bɔtiibi nín ŋáaǹ ntimu mun kíǹee kɔkɔ pu ki nāaǹ-muee, ní sii dàkafī yii a làá ŋmátáa!

english_verse: The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them?
translation_verse: Goosan nì Karan nì Reeseefi timbuŋŋi nì Eedeen yab bin nìn kóò Teelasaar tiŋkin ní m-naanjab nìn nāaǹ bi-kɔkɔee, bi-waaŋi nìn ŋúń ki fīī-baaa?

english_verse: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
translation_verse: Eeseekiyaasi nìn fōō kugbɔŋu kun Asuur bɔtiu túnní bí cáań kí tīī-uee ki kàan̄. U kàan̄ ki dóòyee ní ki nín jɔ́ḿ ti-Dindaan diikun, ní ki kpátì kugbɔŋuee ki bíl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Lord God All-Powerful of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world.
