translation_verse: Báà ubɔ kaa ti pée yíì a-yindi, ubɔ kaa fìntī kí dū u-ba kí nákáǹ-si. Di sá yii a fātì a-boon ki tīī-ti, ní ki dū-ti ki líiǹ ti-yìntitam.

english_verse: No one worships in your name or remains faithful. You have turned your back on us and let our sins melt us away.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ti-Dindaan, sii di sá ti-Baa. Timbi sá kuyɔkɔu, ní a sá uyɔɔmaati. Sii di máń timbi kɔkɔ nì a-ŋalii.

english_verse: You, Lord, are our Father. We are nothing but clay, but you are the potter who molded us.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, taa gíí diŋuul kí jītí mara pu. Taa nín̄ téetí ti-kpitii pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Ti gbàam̄-si, fàtīí kpèè-ti, ti-kɔkɔ sá a-nibul ní.

english_verse: Don't be so furious or keep our sins in your thoughts forever! Remember that all of us are your people.
translation_verse: Báà ubɔ kaa ti kóò a-circir timmun, Siiyɔn jool kpántì kuteeu, Jeerusaleem tiŋki kpántì adigbun ŋma.

english_verse: Every one of your towns has turned into a desert, especially Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ti-circir Nimbɔtidiiku kun nìn ŋān̄, ti-baabi nìn gà ilan ku-poon ki nyɔ́ŋkí-see, bi sēē-ku ŋŋmi. Tin kɔkɔ ti nìn néeńee kpántì adigbun ŋma.

english_verse: Zion's glorious and holy temple where our ancestors praised you has been destroyed by fire. Our beautiful buildings are now a pile of ruins.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, tin kɔkɔ pée jítì nee kaa sòoǹ nì si tibaaa? Mimmee a làá nīn kā ki ŋmí kí sìntīǹ-ti taapu án gíti lákatí mara puɔɔɔ?

english_verse: I, the Lord, was ready to answer even those who were not asking and to be found by those who were not searching. To a nation that refused to worship me, I said, “Here I am!”
translation_verse: M yāntì bin kaa nìn bàlifī m-puee kíǹ ki bàlifī m-pu, m yāntì bin kaa nìn nyàab̀-mee ká-mi. Ditimbundi din kaa nìn yíì m-yindee, m kíí-dì yii: «M sèé, m sèé!»

english_verse: All day long I have reached out to stubborn and sinful people going their own way.
translation_verse: M tāntì m-ŋalii iwiin kɔkɔ ki túĺ dinibul din sá pɔɔgaatee watil, dinibul din nìn nóó nsan ŋun kaa ŋān̄, ní ki ŋáań tin dì pée lèe.

english_verse: They keep making me angry by sneering at me, while offering sacrifices to idols in gardens and burning incense to them on bricks.
translation_verse: An sá dinibul din di gbítí m-ŋuul kaa gbèentée ní. Bi ŋáań saraabi akpaanni, ki tùutī talaalub brikisib pu,

english_verse: They spend their nights hiding in burial caves; they eat the meat of pigs, cooked in sauces made of stuff unfit to eat.
translation_verse: ki dɔ̀ akaakulin, ki dɔ̀ titaŋkpanaakɔti poon, ki ŋmóò tigbeetinan ní tinan tin kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee kā bi-kumbooŋi poon.

english_verse: And then they say to others, “Don't come near us! We're dedicated to God.” Such people are like smoke, irritating my nose all day.
translation_verse: Bi lì yii: «Nín̄ nyí nì a-ba, taa sútí kí pìl̄-mi, an yaa sá fám a làá túń a-kpuulool, di sá m dū m-ba ki sú Unimbɔti ní.» M yaa kpēē ni-ŋáaǹtamee, m-ŋuul fòol̄ ní lìblib ní ki fòol̄ kaa gbèentí, ní ki wù áli ŋwimmɔn.

english_verse: I have written this down; I won't keep silent. I'll pay them back just as their sins deserve.
translation_verse: Ama an ŋmàn̄ ki dɔ̄ m-nimbiin. Maa làá nīn kā ki ŋmí, see m téeǹ-bi bi-tuuŋŋi paati.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will make them pay for their sins and for those of their ancestors— they have disgraced me by burning incense on mountains.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan di lī yii: m làá téeǹ nimbi ni-ba kpitii nì ni-baabi yai dicilpu. Bíǹ di nìn tùutī talaalub ajoon pu, ní ki nìn sìí-mi ŋgbantamu pu. M làá téeǹ-bi an nín máaǹ puee, m làá ŋmàntī bi nín nìn ŋáaǹ puee ní kí dāá téeǹ-bi míǹ deedee.

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says: A cluster of grapes that produces wine is worth keeping! So, because of my servants, I won't destroy everyone.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di lī yii: «Binib yaa ká fiinyi subiliŋ disakal bīń tiŋanee, bi lì yii: <Taa bīil̀-dì, di làá tīī ndamɔntiim.> Míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá ŋá m-tɔntɔnliibi pu. Maa làá nàan̄ bi-kɔkɔ.

english_verse: I have chosen the people of Israel and Judah, and I will bless them with many descendants. They will settle here in this land of mountains, and it will be theirs.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī nnibool ŋubɔ ń nyā Jaakɔb maaliŋun. M làá yàntī Juuda ń jī m-jooŋŋi pu difakal. Bíǹ bin m lēēyee di làá nīn yì-ŋi, m-tɔntɔnliibi di làá nīn kóò ŋi-pu.

english_verse: My people will worship me. Then the coastlands of Sharon and the land as far as Achor Valley will turn into pastureland where cattle and sheep will feed and rest.
translation_verse: M-nibul nì bin làá dāá fàtī bi-ba kí túliń-mee ceeyee, Saarɔn tantakal di làá dāá kpántí kupikpaapɔɔu ki tīī bi-piii ní Akɔɔr tantakal ń dāá kpántí kunaabakau ki tīī bi-naai.

english_verse: What will I, the Lord, do if any of you reject me and my holy mountain? What will happen to you for offering food and wine to the gods you call “Good Luck” and “Fate”?
translation_verse: «Ama nimbi bin dū man ni-Dindaan ki fée, nimbi bin di súntì m-circir jool puee, ni tòotī diwaal Gaadi, ki ŋmàlintí idafi ki féeń diwaal Meenii.

english_verse: Your luck will end! I will see to it that you are slaughtered with swords. You refused to answer when I called out; you paid no attention to my instructions. Instead, you did what I hated, knowing it was wrong.
translation_verse: Too, m làá dū-ni kí líiǹ ni-nannanliibi. Ni-kɔkɔ làá dāá gbàan̄ kitiŋ ní bí làntì-ni. Di sá yii m yíiń ní naa kíí, m sòon̄ ní naa pílifì. Ni ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee m-cee, ní ki lēē kí ŋá tin di kaa fáatiǹ-mee!

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will give food and drink to my servants, and they will celebrate. But all of you sinners will go hungry and thirsty, overcome with disgrace.
translation_verse: An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín lī puee sɔ̀. Ní kpèè, m-tɔntɔnliibi làá dāá ká kí jī ama ní ŋkùm ń dāá cúú nimbi. M-tɔntɔnliibi làá dāá ká kí nyɔ̀, ama ní nnyinnyoo ń dāá kpɔ̀-ni. M-tɔntɔnliibi làá dāá nīn fàal̀, ama ní icoo ń dāá cúú-ni.

english_verse: My servants will laugh and sing, but you will be sad and cry out in pain.
translation_verse: M-tɔntɔnliibi làá dāá nīn fàal̀ ní bi-pɔbiliŋ ń nīn pīiǹ, ama nimbi làá dāá nīn sūǹ ki yáliŋkí ní ni-pɔbiliŋ ń nīn bí kunimbaaun.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, promise to see that you are killed and that my chosen servants use your names as curse words. But I will give new names to my servants.
translation_verse: Bin m lēēyee, bi làá dāá nīn cáá ni-yiŋŋi ní ki tòó mbusu ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti ń yàntī á kpú kii ŋmɔŋŋmɔkɔ àá waaniiyee>. Ama an yaa sá m-tɔntɔnliibee, diyindi diba ní bi làá nīn cáa yíì-bi.

english_verse: I am God! I can be trusted. Your past troubles are gone; I no longer think of them. When you pray for someone to receive a blessing, or when you make a promise, you must do it in my name. I alone am the God who can be trusted. The Lord's New Creation
translation_verse: Un kamaa yaa láa là kí mèè kí bìin̄ ubɔ pu kitiŋ gbanti puee, udaan dāa dù ibaamɔn Nimbɔtiu yindi ní kí mèè kí bìin̄. Un kamaa yaa láa là kí pùtī kí pòon̄ kitiŋ gbanti puee, udaan dāa dù ibaamɔn Nimbɔtiu yindi ní kí pùtī kí pòon̄.» Kutagbɔmpɔŋu nì kitimpɔŋ Di sá yii binib làá dāá súntí animbinaaman ŋin jítèe pu, ŋi làá dāá wāŋkì m-nimbiin.

english_verse: I am creating new heavens and a new earth; everything of the past will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m làá fàtīí náań kutagbɔmpɔŋu nì kitimpɔŋ. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti téetí tin jítèe pu, unil kaa dāa gíti dàkafī tíǹ pu gba.

english_verse: I will celebrate with Jerusalem and all its people; there will be no more crying or sorrow in that city.
translation_verse: Án làá mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-mi Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu ní ḿ nīn bí dipɔɔpindin ki fàal̀ m-nibul pu. Kí yòon̄ kí nīn cée, baa làá ti gbìl̄ nsiim pu, kaa làá ti gbìl̄ ibiil pu.

english_verse: No child will die in infancy; everyone will live a very long life. Anyone a hundred years old will be considered young, and to die younger than that will be considered a curse.
translation_verse: Baa làá ti ká mbipɔmu kaa yúntì ki kpíì, kaa làá ti ká utikpil kaa púĺ ki bál̀ ki kpíì. Un kaa pée yúntì pílpilee di sá un cáá abin dilaataal ki kpíìyee. Unil yaa kaa láá bàn̄ abin dilaataal ní ki kpíìyee, mimmee, bi tɔ́-u mbusu dee.

english_verse: My people will live in the houses they build; they will enjoy grapes from their own vineyards.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá mā adiin ní kí ká-ŋi kí kɔ́, bi làá dāá cóoń fiinyi sufii ní kí dāá ká i-biliŋ kí ŋmɔ́.

english_verse: No one will take away their homes or vineyards. My chosen people will live to be as old as trees, and they will enjoy what they have earned.
translation_verse: Baa làá ti mā adiin kí yóoń biba ń dāá kɔ́, kaa làá ti cóoń fiinyi sufii biba ń dāá kìtī abil kí ŋmɔ́. Di sá yii m-nibul làá dāá yúntí kii isufee. Bin m lútèe làá dāá jī ditundi din bi túńee pu.

english_verse: Their work won't be wasted, and their children won't die of dreadful diseases. I will bless their children and their grandchildren.
translation_verse: Baa làá ti gīī digìńdi fám, kaa làá ti màal̀ mbiyaamu kí tīī ŋkúm. Di sá yii bíǹ di dāa sá dinibul din boon ti-Dindaan bīiǹee, bíǹ nì bi-biyaamu.

english_verse: Wolves and lambs will graze together; lions and oxen will feed on straw. Snakes will eat only dirt! They won't bite or harm anyone on my holy mountain. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Sinsiŋku nì kipibiki di dāa kpáfí ki ŋmóò timool, gbikinti dāa ŋmóò timool kii unaa nín ŋmóò puee ní. Ukoobu làá dāá nīn jīǹ ntam ní. Tiweendi dāa gíti kpáaa, dinàandi mun dāa gíti kpá m-circir jool kɔkɔ pu. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: The Lord said: Heaven is my throne; the earth is my footstool. What kind of house could you build for me? In what place will I rest?
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Yilpu di sá m-beejal ní kitiŋ sá m-taaŋi tɔkɔnlaŋki. Kudii kulɔkɔ ní ni làá gíti mā-mi? Mpaan ŋulɔŋu pu ní m làá ŋmā kí ŋùŋfì?

english_verse: I have made everything; that's how it all came to be. I, the Lord, have spoken. The people I treasure most are the humble— they depend only on me and tremble when I speak.
translation_verse: Nì m-ŋalii ní m dūu náań tin kɔkɔ bí nee. Man di yì tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Ama unil un m làá fàtīí kpèèyee di sá ufalaadaan un sīntiǹ u-ba taapuee, unil un di yaa gbìl̄ m-nyɔɔbundi, dì cáá-u tifaandi u jìkèe.

english_verse: You sacrifice oxen to me, and you commit murder; you sacrifice lambs to me and dogs to other gods; you offer grain to me and pigs' blood to idols; you burn incense to me and praise your idols. You have made your own choice to do these disgusting things that you enjoy so much.
translation_verse: «Unil làntī unaja kí ŋá saraa, ama ní kí fáá kí kpɔ̀ u-nijuti. Unil làntī upii, ama ní kí dū kibɔkɔ kí ŋá saraa. Unil cāabìń-mi tijimpin saraau, ní kí cáań ugbeeti fatikuu mun kí ŋá saraa. Unil tùutī talaalutuukaa kí ŋá-mi saraa, ama ní ki bí ki jáaḿ awaa. Binib gbanti lēē kí ŋá tin fáatiǹ bíǹ bi-bee, ní an mɔ̄ǹ-bi bí nīn tūǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi gbanti.

english_verse: You refused to answer when I called out; you paid no attention to my instructions. Instead, you did what I hated, knowing it was wrong. Now I will punish you in a way you dread the most. The Lord Will Help Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ma mun lēē kí dū-bi kí líiǹ bi-landɔkɔkpitii. M làá cáań dinyoondi kí tɔ̄ bi-pu. Di sá yii m yíiń ní báà ubɔ kaa kíí, m sòon̄ ní baa ubɔ kaa pílifì. Bi ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ m-ceeyee, bi lēē kí ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ-mee.» Tin ti-Dindaan làá ŋá kí lūŋkèe

english_verse: If you tremble when the Lord speaks, listen to what he says: “Some of your own people hate and reject you because of me. They make fun and say, ‘Let the Lord show his power! Let us see him make you truly happy.’ But those who say these things will be terribly ashamed.”
translation_verse: Pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi, nimbi bin fòol̄ u-nyɔɔbundi nì kufaaŋŋuee: Ni-nabiyaamu biba ná-ni, ní ki jìn̄-ni man pu. Bi sòoǹ ki bèel̄-ni yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń dàkà u-nyooti ní tí ká ni nín làá nīn fàal̄ puee!» Ama bíǹ ní icoo làá cúú gbòooo.

english_verse: Do you hear that noise in the city and those shouts coming from the temple? It is the Lord shouting as he punishes his enemies.
translation_verse: Pīlifìmaan kuwoou kun nyánní kitiŋinee, kuwoou kun di nyánní kunimbɔtidiinee. An sá ti-Dindaan di bíi pà u-nannanliibi tipaal tin bi máaǹee.

english_verse: Have you ever heard of a woman who gave birth to a child before having labor pains?
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem màl̄ kibiki ki dóò ní ki nín gbìl̄ imatiŋween pu, u màl̄ kibininjabiki ní kí nín gbìl̄ iween pu.

english_verse: Who ever heard of such a thing or imagined it could happen? Can a nation be born in a day or come to life in a second? Jerusalem is like a mother who gave birth to her children as soon as she was in labor.
translation_verse: Ŋma pée gbìl̄ an bɔti ki ká dalba? Ŋma di pée ká an wanti gbanti dalba? Bi ŋūǹ kí màal̀ kitiŋ ŋwimbaantaaa? Bi ŋūǹ kí màal̀ ditimbundi dicilpuɔɔɔ? Ama Siiyɔn úǹ nín ŋá puee dee. Waa láá kíĺ imatiŋween ní ki pūtì kpáàa dūu màl̄ u-jipɔmbi!

english_verse: The Lord is the one who makes birth possible. And he will see that Zion has many more children. The Lord has spoken.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di bālifì dinyɔɔbundi nee yii: «Man yaa pú nsan unimpu ń cáá dipool iŋmal iwee, m làá pìin̄-u nsan ú taa màal̀aaa? Man di yaa yàntī unimpu màal̀, m làá gíti pìin̄ nsan kibiki ń taa nyānnáaa?»

english_verse: If you love Jerusalem, celebrate and shout! If you were in sorrow because of the city, you can now be glad.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin di néeń Jeerusaleem tiŋkee, ni nì kì ń kpāfì kí fàal̀, ní nīn bí dipɔɔpindin ki-pu. Nimbi bin nìn kāl̀ dikpool ki súń ki-puee, ni nì kì ń kpāfì kí làntì.

english_verse: She will nurse and comfort you, just like your own mother, until you are satisfied. You will fully enjoy her wonderful glory.
translation_verse: Án nín làá ŋá pu ní ní ŋāam̀ ki-biil din tìì dipɔɔsɔŋkilee kí díkí, kii mbiyaamu nín ŋáaḿ mu-na biil din cáá mbiimee nì mmɔn puee.

english_verse: The Lord has promised: “I will flood Jerusalem with the wealth of nations and make the city prosper. Zion will nurse you at her breast, carry you in her arms, and hold you in her lap.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di lī yii: «M làá yàntī ŋgbansɔŋfi ń pùubìń kii mbunee kí dāan̄ kí kɔ́ ki-ni, kí yàntī atimbun nyooti ń fùntīń kii ŋkpin ŋun gbée kí dāan̄ ki-ni. M làá kpèè-ni tiŋan kii ubinaati nín kpèé kibiki kin u tìì dibiilee puee. U dù-kì kí lìb̄ ní kí dū-kì kí páań u-taaŋi pu ki càab̀-kì.

english_verse: I will comfort you there like a mother comforting her child.”
translation_verse: Kii ubinaati nín ŋmēentí u-biki puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní ma mun làá dāá ŋméeǹ-ni. M làá ŋméeǹ-ni Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: When you see this happen, you will celebrate; your strength will return faster than grass can sprout. Then everyone will know that the Lord provides help for his servants, but he is angry with his enemies.
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa ká mimmee, ni-pɔbil làá dāá pīil̀ ní ni-kpabiŋ ń dāá fàtīí pɔ̀ntī kii timɔsɔnee.» Ti-Dindaan làá dāá dàkà u-pɔŋŋu ama ní kí dāá dàkà u-nannanliibi u-ŋuul.

english_verse: The Lord will come down like a whirlwind with his flaming chariots. He will be furiously angry and punish his enemies with fire.
translation_verse: Ní kpèèmaan, ti-Dindaan di kāń ŋŋmi poon ki dòońee, u-janjatɔrɔkub náań nì kunaakpaabuŋŋu ní. U dòoń kí dàkà u-ŋuukpaandi, ní kí dū aŋmilimbil kí tāā kí bīikì binib pu.

english_verse: The Lord's fiery sword will bring justice everywhere on this earth and execute many people. A Threat and a Promise
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan làá dāá dū ŋŋmi nì kitàataajiki kí sòoǹ inifunaan kɔkɔ bɔti. Binib tikpil làá dāá kpú.

english_verse: Some of you get yourselves ready and go to a garden to worship a foreign goddess. You eat the meat of pigs, lizards, and mice. But I, the Lord, will destroy you for this.
translation_verse: M sòoǹ nì bin ŋáań bi-ba circir, ní kí nín kɔ́ circir kpaaŋŋinee, nì bin pāantí unil ubɔ un bí bukpaa kansikinee boonee ní. Bi ŋmóò ugbeeti àá usiibɔ àá ntimbiil wanti. Binib gbanti kɔkɔ làá dāá kpú dicilpu ní. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Dikpafikpaandi diluŋkikaal

english_verse: I know everything you do and think! The time has now come to bring together the people of every language and nation and to show them my glory
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Man nyí bi-tuuŋŋi nì bi-landɔkɔi kɔkɔ. M dòoń kí kóoǹ atimbun kɔkɔ nì isoon kɔkɔ nib kí kpāfì. Bi làá dāan̄ kí ká m-nyooti.

english_verse: by proving what I can do. I will send the survivors to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Meshech, Tubal, Javan, and to the distant islands. I will send them to announce my wonderful glory to nations that have never heard about me.
translation_verse: M làá dāá ŋá kudaaŋŋu kubɔ bi-kansikin. M-bɔsooŋyi boon bin yaa láa kíǹ kaa kpíìyee, m làá dāá dū-bi kí tɔ̄ Taarsiisi nì Puul nì Luudi yab bin sá bipintɔliibee timmun. M làá dāá dū-bi kí tɔ̄ Tubaal nì Yafan timmun nì ntimu mun nnyim māntìi túee poon, laakin binib bin kaa gbìl̄ bi sòon̄ m-puee, laakin baa ká m-nyooti ki kée. Bíǹ di làá dāá yàntī atimbun gbanti ń béé m-nyooti.

english_verse: They will bring your relatives from the nations as an offering to me, the Lord. They will come to Jerusalem, my holy mountain, on horses, chariots, wagons, mules, and camels. It will be like the people of Israel bringing the right offering to my temple.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá cáań ni-nabiyaamu mun kɔkɔ bí bi-ceeyee: bi làá dāá nīn kāń itaamu nì janjatɔrɔkub pu nì tɔrɔkub bin bi bɔ̀b̄ee poon nì imamboon pu nì igutaamu pu kí dāan̄ m-Circir jool pu, Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Án di dāa sá saraabi bin bi ŋá ki tīī-mee. M làá dāá fōō-bi kii m nín fòol̄ Isirayeel yab nín cāabìń saraabi bin m-diikun bi kā asambil ŋin bí circiree poonee ní.

english_verse: I promise that some of them will be priests and others will be helpers in my temple. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M làá dāá lēē bi-kansikin biba ń nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I also promise that you will always have descendants and will never be forgotten, just as the new heavens and the new earth that I create will last forever.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kutagbɔmpɔŋu nì kitimpɔŋ kin m bíi nāantée làá nīn bá m-nimbiin ki pɔ̄ɔ̄. Míǹ mbaantiim ní ni-yiŋŋi nì ni-naantiibi yaŋ làá nīn bí m-nimbiin ki cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: On the first day of each month and on each Sabbath, everyone will worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ kí nīn cée, uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaaliu kamaa nì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa kamaayee, kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ làá dāan̄ kí gbàan̄ man bi-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: My people will go out and look at the dead bodies of those who turned against me. The worms there never die, the fire never stops burning, and the sight of those bodies will be disgusting to everyone.
translation_verse: Binib yaa láa nyēē kitiŋinee, bi dāa ŋūǹ kí ká bin nìn jáń nì mee nikpiliŋ. Akoosibil ŋin dāa ŋmóò-ŋee kaa dāa kúù jaanjaan, ní ŋŋmi ŋun dāa wù-bee mun kaa dāa kúù. Án làá dāá nīn cáá kitiŋ kɔkɔ nib titantan ní.

english_verse: My name is Jeremiah. I am a priest, and my father Hilkiah and everyone else in my family are from Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. This book contains the things that the Lord told me to say.
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin Ilikiyawuu jipɔɔn Yeereemii sòon̄ee sɔ̀. Yeereemii nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi bin kóò Anatooti tiŋkin, Beenjameen naakookun yab tinjandinee dicaŋkun ní.

english_verse: The Lord first spoke to me in the thirteenth year that Josiah was king of Judah,
translation_verse: Amoon jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi nín kāl̀ dibeel Juuda tiŋki pu abin saalaa nì ditataatiil poonee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti nee.

english_verse: and he continued to speak to me during the rule of Josiah's son Jehoiakim. The last time the Lord spoke to me was in the fifth month of the eleventh year that Josiah's son Zedekiah was king. That was also when the people of Jerusalem were taken away as prisoners. The Lord Chooses Jeremiah
translation_verse: U nìn gíti sòon̄ nì u ŋyunti ŋun Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yooyakiim nìn kāl̀ Juuda tiŋki pu dibeelee. U nìn gíti tí sòon̄ nì u njoolkaam Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Seedeesiyasi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin saalaa nì dipeepeekaal poon ŋmaluluutiu poonee. Ŋyunti gbanti ní bi cúú Jeerusaleem yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu. Unimbɔti yíiń Yeereemii ú nīn sá u-bɔnaatiliu

english_verse: “Jeremiah, I am your Creator, and before you were born, I chose you to speak for me to the nations.”
translation_verse: «Kí wàatī ḿ mā-si kí tàkan̄ a-na poonee, m nìn pée nyí-si ní. Kí wàatī á nyā a-na poonee, m nìn gāntì-si ki síiǹ á nīn bí m-tundin. M dū-si ki kpántì m-bɔnaatiliu atimbun cee.»

english_verse: I replied, “I'm not a good speaker, Lord, and I'm too young.”
translation_verse: Ní m kíí yii: «Too, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m dáá sá campɔnti ní, maa nyí isoon.»

english_verse: “Don't say you're too young,” the Lord answered. “If I tell you to go and speak to someone, then go! And when I tell you what to say, don't leave out a word!
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-mi yii: «Taa lì yii: <M sá campɔnti.> Laakin m yaa pée tú-see, á cù. M yaa pée tīī-si mara á sòoǹ puee, á sòoǹ míǹ.

english_verse: I promise to be with you and keep you safe, so don't be afraid.”
translation_verse: Á taa fàŋkì binib gbanti nimbiin, di sá yii m làá nīn bí a-cee kí fīī-si.» Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì mi puee dee.

english_verse: The Lord reached out his hand, then he touched my mouth and said, “I am giving you the words to say,
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan tāntì u-ŋal ki gbēē m-nyɔkɔ ní ki bí-mi yii: «Kpèè, m dū m-bɔti ki ŋá a-nyɔkɔn.

english_verse: and I am sending you with authority to speak to the nations for me. You will tell them of doom and destruction, and of rising and rebuilding again.”
translation_verse: Á béé díǹ yii m tīī-si mpɔn atimbun nì abee pu. A làá kpìkitī kí lábití kí cìb̄, kí bīil̀ kí kpēelikì, ní kí fàtīí mā kí cóoń.» Amandi supandi nì dikumbool din nùuǹee bɔti

english_verse: The Lord showed me something in a vision. Then he asked, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I answered, “A branch of almonds that ripen early.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti sòoǹ nì mi yii: «Yeereemii, ba ní a wāĺ?» Ní m kíí-u yii: «Amandi supandi ní m wāĺ.»

english_verse: “That's right,” the Lord replied, “and I always rise early to keep a promise.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «A lafun wál̀-dì tiŋman. Di sá yii m cí kí ŋá tin m sòon̄ee.»

english_verse: Then the Lord showed me something else and asked, “What do you see now?” I answered, “I see a pot of boiling water in the north, and it's about to spill out toward us.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ nì mi nliliitiim yii: «Ba ní a gíti wāĺ?» Ní m kíí yii: «M wāĺ dikumbool tɔ́kɔ́ ki nùuǹ di-nyɔkɔ túĺ ŋgan pú.»

english_verse: The Lord said: I will pour out destruction all over the land.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Ŋgan pú ní nnaabu làá nyānní kí dūú pɔ̀l̄ kitiŋ kɔkɔ nib pu.

english_verse: Just watch while I send for the kings of the north. They will attack and capture Jerusalem and other towns, then set up their thrones at the gates of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Di sá m nín lī puee sèé. M làá yíiń adican nì abee ŋin kɔkɔ bí ŋgan púee nib. Bi làá dāá dāan̄, ní báà ŋma bɔtiu ń dū u-beejal kí síiń Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu nyɔkɔpu. Bi làá dāá màntīí tū ki-gundi, ní kí dāá já nì Juuda timmu kɔkɔ nib.

english_verse: Jeremiah, get ready! Go and tell the people what I command you to say. Don't be frightened by them, or I will make you terrified while they watch.
translation_verse: Siiyee, yòon̄ a-gbajau kí gbìn̄. Yīkìí yūĺ kí cùú sòoǹ nì bi tin kɔkɔ m tīī-si mara á sòoǹ nì bee. Á taa fàŋkì-bi, yaa sá fám, man m-ba di làá fàaǹ-si bi-nimbiin.

english_verse: My power will make you strong like a fortress or a column of iron or a wall of bronze. You will oppose all of Judah, including its kings and leaders, its priests and people.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, m làá dū-si kí kpántí kii kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee. A làá nīn bí kii tikúti jaantalkuee, àá tasa kúti gundee kitiŋee kɔkɔ nimbiin, nì Juuda tiŋki bɔtiibi nì ki-bɔtibiliŋ nì ki-saraaŋaliibi nì kitiŋee nibul kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_verse: They will fight back, but they won't win. I, the Lord, give my word— I won't let them harm you.
translation_verse: Bi làá já nì si, ama baa làá ŋmā kí ŋá-si tiba. Di sá yii m bí a-cee kí fīī-si. Man a-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: The Lord told me
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: to go to Jerusalem and tell everyone that he had said: When you were my young bride, you loved me and followed me through the barren desert.
translation_verse: «Cù kí sòoǹ nì Jeerusaleem yab án kɔ́ bi-tafaliŋin. Man bi-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. M téetí a-pɔntinee, a nín nìn cáá m-pu dineeŋkpaandi diŋyee. Dineendi gbanti nìn bí kii unil nín néeń u-bɔɔn puee ní. A nìn nóó-mi kuteeun laakin tiba nì tiba nìn kpée.

english_verse: You belonged to me alone, like the first part of the harvest, and I severely punished those who mistreated you.
translation_verse: Di sá yii sii Isirayeel, a nìn sá ki tīī man a-Dindaan baba ní, a lì kii tijincɔ̀fikaalee. Bin yaa nìn lámintì ki gbēē-see nìn kóò m-bɔtin ní ḿ yàntī nnaabu ń jēetí bi-pu.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: and I, the Lord, will speak. I was never unfair to your ancestors, but they left me and became worthless by following worthless idols.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Diyìntil dilal ní ni-naanjab ká m-pu, ní ki sáǹ ki wāatì-mi ní? Bi sáǹ ki jòó ki pá tin kaa bí tibanee boon, ní bíǹ bi-ba kpántì tin kaa bí tibanee.

english_verse: Your ancestors refused to ask for my help, though I had rescued them from Egypt and led them through a treacherous, barren desert, where no one lives or dares to travel.
translation_verse: Baa bālifì yii: <Ti-Dindaan un nyántìń-ti Eejipiti tiŋkinee, úǹ un kpōotì-ti kuteeun laakin kūń ki sá mbuŋgalimuee, ŋweel nì dibɔmbɔndi tiŋkee, kitiŋ kin báà ubɔ kaa kóòyee bí la?>

english_verse: I brought you here to my land, where food is abundant, but you made my land filthy with your sins.
translation_verse: M nìn cáá-ni ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin cáá ntiŋkpamee poon, ní ŋmɔ́ ki-subiliŋ kí jī ki-gaajawanti. Ama ni bàn̄ee ní ki kɔ́ǹ m-tiŋkee tijɔkɔndi, ní ki dū m-gaajawammɔntiiti ki kpántì ntimbiil wanti.

english_verse: The priests who teach my laws don't care to know me. Your leaders rebel against me; your prophets give messages from Baal and worship false gods. The Lord Accuses His People
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi kaa bālifì yii: <Ti-Dindaan bí la?> Bimaradakaliibi kaa nyí-mi, ní bikpootiliibi jáà nì mi. M-bɔnaatiliibi bí ki nàatī diwaal Baal bɔti, bi jòó ki pá tin kaa bí tibanee boon.

english_verse: I will take you to court and accuse you and your descendants *
translation_verse: An pu ní m làá cùnnì-ni ibɔsoon, ní kí cùnnì ni-naantiibi mun ibɔsoon.» Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: of a crime that no nation has ever committed before. Just ask anyone, anywhere, from the eastern deserts to the islands in the west.
translation_verse: «Dùtīmaan Kitiim buŋyi kí cùú kpèè! Tɔ̄maan binib bí cù Keedaar tiŋkin kí bàlifì kí béé tiŋan. Ni làá ká yii baa ŋáań tin ni ŋáań nee niin.

english_verse: You will find that no nation has ever abandoned its gods even though they were false. I am the true and glorious God, but you have rejected me to worship idols.
translation_verse: Dinibul diba kpántì di-waaŋi ni káaa? Nì min kɔkɔ awaa gbanti kaa kpáàa sá Unimbɔtee! Ama m-nibul díǹ dū di-nyooti ki kpántì tin kaa bí tibanee.

english_verse: You, my people, have sinned in two ways— you have rejected me, the source of life-giving water, and you've tried to collect water in cracked and leaking pits dug in the ground.
translation_verse: M-nibul ŋá ikpiti mili pu: bi dū man un sá nnyimbul ŋun tìì dimaŋfalee ki fá, ki cūtìi gbìn̄ anyimbɔbil ŋin tátì nnyim kaa ŋūǹ kí dòon̄ poonee.» Unil yaa fá Unimbɔtee, an kpántí ntuntun ní

english_verse: People of Israel, you weren't born slaves; you were captured in war.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab kpántì iyumbu naaa, bi màl̄-bi kuyuŋun ní? Kin ba pu ní bi fúkúl̀-bi míǹ?

english_verse: Enemies roared like lions and destroyed your land; towns lie burned and empty.
translation_verse: Bíǹ pu ní gbikintib mùuǹ ki tátée. Bi yāntì bi-tiŋki kpántì adigbun. Bi sēē bi-timmu ŋŋmi ní báà ubɔ kaa ti kóò mu-ni.

english_verse: Soldiers from the Egyptian towns of Memphis and Tahpanhes have cracked your skulls.
translation_verse: Áli gba Meemifiisi yab nì Dafinee yab kōol̀-bi diyibaakpandi.

english_verse: It's all your own fault! You stopped following me, the Lord your God,
translation_verse: Isirayeel, tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kaa nyánní a-ceeee? Man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nìn ŋúb́-si ní ti còom̄, ama ní a dū-mi ki fá.

english_verse: Your own sins will punish you, because it was a bitter mistake for you to reject me without fear of punishment. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Fōō ikpiti in a ŋée tafadaaldi! A nín kaa yúl̀ nì mi deedeeyee kpuulool ń gítí a-pu! english_verse: Long ago you left me and broke all ties between us, refusing to be my servant. Now you worship other gods by having sex on hilltops or in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Isirayeel, dooooyee ní a yíkì kaa kíí a-ba pu. A kpītì mpèé ŋun nìn bí man nì si kansikinee ní ki bí yii: <Maa ti là kí nīn sá uyumbu>. Di sá yii ŋgbantamu mun fɔ̀kɔ̀ee kɔkɔ pu nì isufi in cáá tifaasɔnee taapu ní sii dɔ̀ ki ŋáań a-laakpaatuuŋŋi.

english_verse: You were a choice grapevine, but you have become a wild, useless vine. Israel Is Stained with Guilt
translation_verse: M nìn cóoǹ-si á nīn sá bufiinyisumɔntiibu bun pu bi ŋūǹ kí nīn mákée ní. Kpèè a kpántì difiinyileendi din biliŋ gàm̀ee, an ŋá mana ní ki ŋá míǹ?

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel, you are stained with guilt, and no soap or bleach can wash it away.
translation_verse: Báà a yaa dū njeem ki fíntì a-ba, ní ki dū fɔfɔb tikpil tikpil ki fùl̄, a-yìntitam daaŋku làá nīn gbíntìi dɔ̄ m-nimbiin ní.» Man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu di lī míǹ.

english_verse: You deny your sins and say, “We aren't unclean. We haven't worshiped Baal.” But think about what you do in Hinnom Valley. You run back and forth like young camels, as you rush to worship one idol after another.
translation_verse: Mana ní a ŋūǹ kí lì yii: <Maa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, maa tōotì diwaal Baal>? Kpèè kun a ŋá ditantakalinee! Béé tin a ŋée. A náań nì ugutansal un sáń ajan kɔkɔ puee ní.

english_verse: Your shoes are worn out, and your throat is parched from running here and there to worship foreign gods. “Stop!” I shouted, but you replied, “No! I love those gods too much.”
translation_verse: <Isirayeel yab, kpèèmaan tiŋan! Ni làá gbéetí kí fōō tiweendi ní ni-neen ń kpā.> Ama ní ni kíí yii: <Taa ti ŋūǹ kí gítí boon! M néeń awaa ní ki làá nīn jòó ki pá ŋi-boon.>

english_verse: You and your leaders are more disgraceful than thieves— you and your kings, your priests and prophets
translation_verse: Kii bi nín cútí unaayuu icoo ń cúú-u puee, míǹ ní icoo làá dāá cúú nimbi Isirayeel yab, ni nì ni-bɔtiibi nì ni-kàliŋkpilib nì ni-saraaŋaliibi nì ni-bɔnaatiliibi.

english_verse: worship stone idols and sacred poles as if they had created you and had given you life. You have rejected me, but when you're in trouble, you cry to me for help.
translation_verse: Ni tùkù ndɔ ŋun ni dūu kpítì diwaalee yii: <Sii di sá man baa.> Ní kí bí ditaŋkpal yii: <Sii di màl̄-mi!> An nín bàà sá ní fàtī ni-nimbiin kí túĺ-mee, ní ni fātì ni-boon ki tīī-mi. Ama ni yaa kɔ́ dinimbinaamandi poonee ní ní bí-mi yii: <Yīkì malaa kí dāá fīī-ti.>

english_verse: Go cry to the gods you made! There should be enough of them to save you, because Judah has as many gods as it has towns. Israel Rebels against the Lord
translation_verse: Awaa ŋin ni kpítèe bi la? Ŋí yīkì tí kpèè ŋi yaa ŋūǹ kí fīī-ni kí nyāntí-ni ni-nimbinaamandi poon! Di sá yii nimbi Juuda yab waaŋi wīikí ki jítiǹ ni-timmu nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: The Lord said to Israel: You accuse me of not saving you, but I say you have rebelled.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní ni bí ki wòoǹ-mi? Ni-kɔkɔ yíkì ki jáń nì mi. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I tried punishing you, but you refused to come back to me, and like fierce lions you killed my prophets.
translation_verse: M fáá-ni ama an kaa ŋá-ni tiba, kaa cíikì-ni, ní gbìl̄ kí béé tin m ŋée taapu. Ni dū ntàataajimu ki kūū ni-bɔnaatiliibi kii gbikinti nín bìliŋkī ipeel puee.

english_verse: Now listen to what I say! Did I abandon you in the desert or surround you with darkness? You are my people, yet you have told me, “We'll do what we want, and we refuse to worship you!”
translation_verse: «Nimbi waanee nib, ní pīlifìmaan tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nee tiŋan. M kpántì kuteeu ní ki tīī Isirayeel yabaaa, dibɔmbɔndi tiŋki ní? Kin ba pu ní m-nibul yab lì yii: <Ti làá cù laakin ti yaa lèe, taa làá fàtīí gítiń a-cee?>

english_verse: A bride could not forget to wear her jewelry to her wedding, but you have forgotten me day after day.
translation_verse: Usapɔɔn ŋūǹ kí súntí u-wanléeŋkaati puɔɔɔ? Unimpucaan ŋūǹ kí súntí u-nimpucambɔkutil puɔɔɔ? Ama nimbi man nibul súntì man pu an yúntì tikpil tikpil.» *

english_verse: You are so clever at finding lovers that you could give lessons to a prostitute.
translation_verse: «Óooo! A nyí bi nín dì pu kí nyàab̀ kí ká dineendi pueeyeeee! An yāntì a mántiǹ ikpiti diŋál.

english_verse: You killed innocent people for no reason at all. And even though their blood can be seen on your clothes,
translation_verse: Bi kāntí a-wampeeŋkaati pu bisoodambi nì maanyiibab fatikuu. Ama aa cúú-bi bi bíi wìil̄ a-diiku punyɔkɔki. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee,

english_verse: you claim to be innocent, and you want me to stop being angry with you. So I'll take you to court, and we'll see who is right.
translation_verse: ní a lì yii: <Maa ŋá tiba. Báà an ŋá pu, ti-Dindaan làá páatí u-ŋuul m-pu.> Ama a nín lì yii: <Maa ŋá tikpitil tibee puee>, m làá sòoǹ a-bɔti. *

english_verse: When Assyria let you down, you quickly ran to Egypt, but you'll find no help there,
translation_verse: A kpántì ubɔɔti sɔkɔmii! Ama á béé yii Eejipiti tiŋki làá kɔ́ǹ-si icoo kii Asuur tiŋki nín kɔ́ǹ-si icoo puee ní.

english_verse: The Lord said to the people of Israel: If a divorced woman marries, can her first husband ever marry her again? No, because this would pollute the land. But you have more gods than a prostitute has lovers. Why should I take you back?
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lī yii: Unil yaa jìn̄ u-nimpuu ní u yīkìi cūtìi mɔ́ǹ ubɔee, udaan gíti cáá nsan kí fàtīí fōoń-uaaa? Aayee! Di sá yii atuun gbanti pu ní kitiŋ kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. english_verse: Just try to find one hilltop where you haven't gone to worship other gods by having sex. You sat beside the road like a robber in ambush, except you offered yourself to every passerby. Your sins of unfaithfulness have polluted the land.
translation_verse: Wáaǹ kí kpèè ŋgbantamu yilpu. Kigbantaŋ kiba pée bí si nì a-bɔɔn ubɔ kaa jɔ́m̀ ki-pu ki dōoǹaaaa? A kàal̀ isan caŋin ki cīití-bi kii ulaalibuja un kóò kuteeunee. A dū a-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi nì a-laakpaatuuŋŋi ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: So I, the Lord, refused to let the spring rains fall. But just like a prostitute, you still have no shame for what you have done.
translation_verse: An puee maa yāntì utaa nìn̄, maa yāntì a ká utaa kuseeun. Ama a ŋá mpɔɔgbifin ki gbíntìi nìkì ki ŋáań a-laakpaatuuŋŋi, ní ki yíì kaa béè a-bɔkpil.

english_verse: You call me your father or your long-lost friend;
translation_verse: Ní kɔŋkɔnnee a cáá dipɔbil ki kūuntí ki yíì-mi yii: «M-baa, sii un sá m-bɔɔ doooo m-biyatinee!

english_verse: you beg me to stop being angry, but you won't stop sinning. The Lord Asks Israel To Come Back to Him

english_verse: This nation will eat your crops and livestock; they will leave no fruit on your vines or fig trees. And although you feel safe behind thick walls, your towns will be destroyed and your children killed. Israel Refused To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá jī kí céetí ni-kpaajinti nì ni-jikaati, kí kpɔ̀ ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib, kí làntì ni-naai nì ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui, kí nàan̄ ni-fiinyi nì ni-fiigi sufii. Bi làá dāá kpēelikì ni-timmu mun ni máń agun ki tú ki dàkafī yii tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋá-nee kujaau poon.»

english_verse: The Lord said: Jeremiah, the enemy army won't kill everyone in Judah.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, maa làá dāá kúntí-ni nyíki nyiki.

english_verse: And the people who survive will ask, “Why did the Lord our God do such terrible things to us?” Then tell them: I am the Lord, but you abandoned me and worshiped other gods in your own land. Now you will be slaves in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Binib yaa láa bālifì yii: <Ba ní ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ŋá-ti mimmee?>, sii Yeereemii, á dāá kíí-bi yii: <Ni dū-u ki fá ki nóó anicaŋwaa ni-tiŋki poon. Míǹ mbaantiim ní ni làá cù kinicantiŋin kí cùú tɔ̄ ditundi kí tīī binicambi.>» Binib kaa ti nyí Unimbɔti tuuŋŋi

english_verse: Tell these things to each other, you people of Judah, you descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ní sòoǹ tibɔti nee kí tùkù Jaakɔb yab, ní bāakì-tì Juuda tiŋkin.

english_verse: that you should worship me with fear and trembling? I'm the one who made the shore to hold back the ocean. Waves may crash on the beach, but they can come no farther.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Naa fàŋkí-maaa? Naa yɔ́tifí m-nimbiinaaa? Man di kaa dū dibul ki bíl̀ án nīn sá tiŋku kpaanyɔkɔki, kikpaanyɔkɔ kin waa máaǹ kí lákatéeee? U-nyiŋgbanti ŋūǹ kí yīkì, ama tàa cáá mpɔn, tì gà kuwoou, nì míǹ kɔkɔee tàa ŋūǹ kí jītí.

english_verse: You stubborn people have rebelled and turned your backs on me.
translation_verse: Ama nimbi dinibul nee pɔbil nyìm̀ ki gáatì, ni fātì ni-boon ki tīī-mi ki búntì.

english_verse: You refuse to say, “Let's worship the Lord! He's the one who sends rain in spring and autumn and gives us a good harvest.”
translation_verse: Baa lì bi-pɔbilin yii: <Tí fàŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu. Úǹ di tìì-ti utaa ŋyunti ŋun an máaǹee, utaapeekaa nì ujoolkaa. Dibindi kamaayee, u síiǹ-ti nnyɔmu mun ti làá nīn cēē tikpaajinee.>

english_verse: A hunter traps birds and puts them in a cage, but some of you trap humans and make them your slaves.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m-nibul kansikinee, binikpitib bí. Kii un kpáŋkí inoonee nín bí puee, míǹ ní bi bāal̀ ki cí. Bi píĺ titalindi ki sātì binib.

english_verse: You are evil, and you lie and cheat to make yourselves rich. You are powerful
translation_verse: Kii inoon nín gbí anɔndiinni puee, míǹ ní tiwan tin bi fìkēe gbí bi-diiŋŋin. Bi nín dī pu ki kpántì binikpaambi nì bigaajab,

english_verse: and prosperous, but you refuse to help the poor get the justice they deserve.
translation_verse: ki gbīfiǹ ki ŋá ŋkpamee dee. Bi ŋá ikpiti an lákatì. Baa sòoǹ tibɔti ti-pú, kaa mɔ́tí ditaŋkpiibil pu, ama ní an bútí-bi. Baa pɔ̀ uwɔfi.

english_verse: Look at the terrible things going on in this country. I am shocked!
translation_verse: «Ntimbiil nì atulim bɔti bíi jītí kitiŋ nee pu.

english_verse: Prophets give their messages in the name of a false god, my priests don't want to serve me, and you—my own people— like it this way! But on the day of disaster, where will you turn for help?
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nàatī tinyimɔmbɔti, ní bisaraaŋaliibi kāntí ipaati, ní m-nibul ká yii míǹ ŋān̄! Mimmee tin bí nee kɔkɔ yaa láa kúntèe, ni làá dāá ŋá mana dee?»

english_verse: Run for your lives, people of Benjamin. Get out of Jerusalem. Sound a trumpet in Tekoa and light a signal fire in Beth-Haccherem. Soon you will be struck by disaster from the north.
translation_verse: Beenjameen yab, sām̀maan kí nyā Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Ní cùú báĺmaan laaba. Búḿmaan ŋyin Teekoowa tiŋkin, kí cóoḿmaan kudaaŋŋu ŋaabiki Beeti-Keereem tiŋkin, di sá yii mbusu ubɔ, nnaabukpaan ŋubɔ làá nyānní ŋgan pú kí dāan̄.

english_verse: Jerusalem is a lovely pasture,
translation_verse: Siiyɔn tiŋki kin ŋān̄ dándanee, bi nāaǹ-kì ní nee.

english_verse: but shepherds will surround it and divided up, then let their flocks eat all the grass.
translation_verse: Binib làá dāan̄ kí bìin̄ ki-pu, kii bipikpaaliibi nì bi-picaŋkpuntee. Bi làá gāā bi-bìńti kí màntīí tū-kì. Báà ŋma làá nīn cáá u-jandi.

english_verse: Kings will tell their troops, “If we reach Jerusalem in the morning, we'll attack at noon. But if we arrive later,
translation_verse: Bi téeń yii: «Yīkìmaan! Tí bɔ́ntímaan kujaau. Tí cùú já nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki diwiŋkaŋkambil pu. Timbi bɔlii na! Ŋwìiń bíi jēetí, njooboon bíi lítí.

english_verse: we'll attack after dark and destroy its fortresses.”
translation_verse: Yīkìmaan tí cùú jáǹ-bi kunyeeu nee, tí wīīmaan bi-dinyaaŋŋi!»

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I will command these armies to chop down trees and build a ramp up to the walls of Jerusalem. People of Jerusalem, I must punish you for your injustice.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé: «Gàatìmaan isufi kí kpúkuń kí nákáǹ Jeerusaleem gundi.» M làá dáaĺ kitiŋ gbanti tafal, kun puee tipɔmbɔti ŋma di gbí ki-poon.

english_verse: Evil pours from your city like water from a spring. Sounds of injustice and violence echo within your walls; victims are everywhere, wounded and dying.
translation_verse: Kii nnyimbul nín tòoń di-nyim puee, míǹ ní kì tòó ki-toom ki yàantí. Ki-ceeyee, bi pée sòoǹ tipɔmbɔti nì dinàandi pu ní. Falaabi nì tiweendi di pée dɔ̄ m-nimbiin baabadal.

english_verse: Listen to me, you people of Jerusalem and Judah. I will abandon you, and your land will become an empty desert.
translation_verse: «Jeerusaleem, kpèè tiŋan, an yaa kaa sá míǹ, m làá cúú m-ba kí nákatí kí wàatī-si, kí nàan̄-si á kpántí kuteeu, kitiŋ kin báà ubɔ kaa ti kóòyee.» Isirayeel yab yíì kaa pílifiǹ ti-Dindaan

english_verse: I will tell your enemies to leave your nation bare like a vine stripped of grapes. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken. Jeremiah's Anger
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé. «Kóom̀maan bin kɔkɔ kíǹ ki bí Isirayeel tiŋkinee kii bi nín kōontí fiinyi subiliŋ sakaŋ bukpaan puee. Fàtīí dūmaan ni-ŋalii kí máań máań afiinyipan pu ŋfunyɔm kupaau, kii bufiinyikpaa dindaan nín ŋáań puee.» Yeereemii

english_verse: I have told the people that you, Lord, will punish them, but they just laugh and refuse to listen.
translation_verse: Tibɔti nee, ŋma cee ní m làá sòoǹ-tì? Ŋma ní m làá kpāafì ní ú gbìl̄ ní? Bi-tafaliŋ kpáá baa ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄. Ti-Dindaan bɔti kpántì bi-cee ibeel ní, baa pée là kí gbìl̄-tì.

english_verse: Your anger against Judah flames up inside me, and I can't hold it in much longer. The Lord's Anger Will Sweep Everyone Away The Lord answered: Don't hold back my anger! Let it sweep away everyone— the children at play and all adults, young and old alike.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ŋuul fòol̄ m-ni lìblib, maa ti ŋūǹ kí ŋmèè. ti-Dindaan «Kpáatí diŋuul gbanti kí sìtī mbiyaamu mun còom̄ adan puee nì binipɔmbi kɔkɔ pu. Bi-kɔkɔ làá kpántí bisarkadambi, bininjab nì binimpoobi, bijaŋkpilib nì bin púĺ sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔee.

english_verse: I'll punish the people of Judah and give to others their houses and fields, as well as their wives. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Biba di làá dāá jī bi-diiŋŋi nì bi-sati nì bi-nimpoobi. M làá tàntī m-ŋal kí gbēē kitiŋ nee nib, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ!

english_verse: Everyone is greedy and dishonest, whether poor or rich. Even the prophets and priests cannot be trusted.
translation_verse: Di sá yii kí yòon̄ bikpaambi kí tin sāā ŋwaamuee, bi-kɔkɔ bìǹ ki nyàab̀ njim ní. Kí yòon̄ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kí cáá sāā bisaraaŋaliibee, bi-kɔkɔ cáá inaamuul ní.

english_verse: All they ever offer to my deeply wounded people are empty hopes for peace.
translation_verse: Bi cáá m-nibul naabuŋu ki ŋáań bugbambu ní ki lì yii: <Ŋgbansɔŋfi bí! Ŋgbansɔŋfi bí!> Ama ní ŋgbansɔŋfi kpá.

english_verse: They should be ashamed of their disgusting sins, but they don't even blush. And so, when I punish Judah, they will end up on the ground, dead like everyone else. I, the Lord, have spoken. The People of Judah Rejected God's Way of Life
translation_verse: Ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi tūǹee, an kɔ́ǹ-bi icoooo? Aayee, kpataaa! Baa kpáàa nyí gba yii bi ŋá tiba. Ti-Dindaan bí yii: An pu ní bi làá kūtì bin bíi lítée pu bí lítí. M yaa láa tāā ki bíikì bi-puee, bi làá dāá ká yii bi dɔ̄ kitiŋ ní.

english_verse: The Lord said: My people, when you stood at the crossroads, I told you, “Follow the road your ancestors took, and you will find peace.” But you refused.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: Gbèem̄maan nsan ŋun ni dēe pu kí dàkafì. Bàlifìmaan bí tùkù-ni njamin saŋyi bɔti. Nyàab̀maan nsammɔnti kí nóó-ŋu. Niin ní ni ŋūǹ kí ká dipɔɔsɔŋkil kí ŋùŋfì. Ama ní bi kíí yii: <Taa làá nóó-ŋu.>

english_verse: I also sent prophets to warn you of danger, but when they sounded the alarm, you paid no attention.
translation_verse: M yóoǹ binib sintil bí kpāafì-bi yii: <Ni yaa gbìl̄ bi búń ŋyinee, ní nīn nyí nì ni-ba!> Ama ní bi kíí yii: <Taa làá nīn nyí nì ti-ba.>

english_verse: So I tell all nations on earth, “Watch what I will do!
translation_verse: An puee nimbi atimbun, pīlifìmaan! Báà ŋma ń béé tin làá bàń bi-puee.

english_verse: My people ignored me and rejected my laws. They planned to do evil, and now the evil they planned will happen to them.”
translation_verse: Anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí duulinyanee, pīlifìmaan. M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ binib nee pu. Án làá nīn sá bi-tuŋkpitiŋ paati. Baa dū m-bɔti ki yíiń tiba, ní ki kpèé m-marab fám.

english_verse: People of Judah, you bring me incense from Sheba and spices from distant lands. You offer sacrifices of all kinds. But why bother? I hate these gifts of yours!
translation_verse: Ba ní ni làá ŋá nì talaalutuukaa un ni cāabìń Seeba tiŋkin, nì kukaluu kun sɔ́fì ni cáań kitiŋ kin dátèe poonee? Maa là bisaraawɔkaabi bin ni ŋáań ki tìì-mee. Ni-saraabi kaa fáatì-mi.

english_verse: So I will put stumbling blocks in your path, and everyone will die, including parents and children, neighbors and friends. An Army from the North
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: M làá dū tiwaŋgbeetikaal kí bíĺ dinibul nee nyɔkɔpu dí gbéetí kí lítí. Bibaatiibi nì bi-jipɔmbi, bi-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb nì bi-bɔɔbi kɔkɔ làá kpú dicilpu.» Binannanliibi làá nyānní ŋgan pú kí dāan̄

english_verse: The Lord said, “Look toward the north, where a powerful nation has prepared for war.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé. «Dinibul diba làá nyānní ŋgan pú kí dāan̄. Ditimbuŋkpaandi diba kālìń nsan pu ki nyánní kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ ki dòoń.

english_verse: Its well-armed troops are cruel and never show mercy. Their galloping horses sound like ocean waves pounding on the shore. This army will attack you, lovely Jerusalem.”
translation_verse: Bi-bijanjaliibi ŋúb́ itɔfi nì ŋkpamu. Bi cáá ntoom kaa cáá disaasɔl. Bi-bìntindi bí kii tiŋku wookuee ní. Bi kā itaamu pu, ki lūtì mpɔn pu kí já nì sii Siiyɔn tiŋki.» Isirayeel nibul

english_verse: Then the people said, “Just hearing about them makes us tremble with fear, and we twist and turn in pain like a woman giving birth.”
translation_verse: «Ti nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ti-wunti yɔ̄tì. Dinimbinaamandi kɔ́-ti fíŋfiŋ ní ti bíi jīǹ falaa kii unimpu un kā imatiŋween puee.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Don't work in your fields or walk along the roads. It's too dangerous. The enemy is well armed
translation_verse: Ní taa nyā kí cù tisatin, kí taa nyā kí còom̀ adan pu, di sá yii unannanli bí ki kù binib. Dinyoondi bí an kɔkɔ pu.» ti-Dindaan

english_verse: and attacks without warning. So mourn, my people, as though your only child had died. Wear clothes made of sackcloth and roll in the ash pile.” The Lord's People Must Be Tested The Lord said:
translation_verse: «Sii man nibul, dū kpɔsata kí pèen̄ kí nīn dɔ̄ ŋfantam poon ki bíntí. Kíĺ kí nīn bíi ŋáań dikpool koobiliŋ kii bi nín ŋáań dijipɔmbaabil kpool puee. Nín̄ gà ikpiisilan ki yáliŋkí. Di sá yii unannanli un làá nàan̄-see làá páatí kí jēetí a-pu dicilpu dicilpu.» Tikúti tin baa ŋūǹ kí lēē tijɔkɔndee

english_verse: And you'll find they are hard like bronze and iron. They are stubborn rebels, always spreading lies. *
translation_verse: Bi-kɔkɔ gáatì, baa ti ŋūǹ kí gíiǹní-bi, bi kúŋfí bi-jutiibi boon. Bi pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii tasa kúti àá kii tikúbɔnee ní. Bi-kɔkɔ sá binàanliibi ní.

english_verse: Silver can be purified in a fiery furnace, but my people are too wicked to be made pure, and so I have rejected them.
translation_verse: Bi yíì binib gbanti yii, <Animbil ŋin kaa ti bí tibanee.> Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki fá.

english_verse: But you have ignored me and become even more stubborn and sinful than your ancestors ever were! Slaughter Valley The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ama ní naa pílifiǹ-mi. Naa kpōoǹ ni-tafal kí pīlifì. Ni ŋá ŋyipɔn, ki ŋá tin jítiǹ ni-naanjabee.>

english_verse: Stop taking advantage of foreigners, orphans, and widows. Don't kill innocent people. And stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Ní taa mùul̀ unicaan nì ditaŋkpiibil nì ukpiipu. Ní taa kpɔ̀ maanyiiba kitiŋ nee pu. Ní taa nín̄ jòó ki pá awaa ŋin làá cáá-ni kí kɔ́ǹ mbusunee boon.

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves! My temple is here in Jerusalem, but that doesn't mean I will protect you.
translation_verse: Ní taa nín̄ kùbitī ki lì yii: <Doo di sá ti-Dindaan Diiku, doo di sá ti-Dindaan Diiku, doo di sá ti-Dindaan Diiku.> Ní taa dū ni-mákal kí páań anyɔɔbuŋkiilkaa gbanti pu.

english_verse: I will keep you safe only if you change your ways and are fair and honest with each other.
translation_verse: Ní kpántí ni-bimbim nì ni-ŋáaǹtam. Ni nì ni-jutiibi kansikinee, ubɔ ń taa mùul̀ u-juti.

english_verse: Then I will let you enjoy a long life in this land I gave your ancestors.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ḿ yàntī ní kàl̄ kitiŋ kin m nìn tīī ni-naanjab kí nīn cá abin abinee pu.

english_verse: But just look at what is happening! You put your trust in worthless lies.
translation_verse: «Ama ní ni dū ni-mákal ki ŋá tinyimɔmbɔti tin kaa bí tiba nee ni.

english_verse: You steal and murder; you lie in court and are unfaithful in marriage. You worship idols and offer incense to Baal, when these gods have never done anything for you.
translation_verse: Baaa! Ni yù, ki kù binib, ki ŋáań tilaakpaal, ki pùtī fám, ki tùutī talaalu ki tìì diwaal Baal, ki sáń ki pá awaa ŋin ni nì ŋi kaa cáá mpèé ŋubɔee boon.

english_verse: And then you come into my temple and worship me! Do you think I will protect you so that you can go on sinning?
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ní dāan̄ kí gbàan̄ m-nimbiin, kudii kun bi dūu sú-mee poon ki lì yii: <Ti ká difiil!> ní boonee ki gbíntìi nìkì ki tūǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi.

english_verse: You are thieves, and you have made my temple your hideout. But I've seen everything you have done.
translation_verse: Kunimbɔtidii kun bi dūu sú-mee ní ni dūu kpántì kunaayudii naaa? Too man nín wāĺ-ku puee dee.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Go to Shiloh, where my sacred tent once stood. Take a look at what I did there. My people Israel sinned, and so I destroyed Shiloh!
translation_verse: «Cùmaan Siiloo circir paaŋŋu pu kí kpèè. Dooooyee, niin ní m nìn kóò. Ní kpèè, Isirayeel m-nibul toom puee, m nín ŋá mpaan gbanti puee.

english_verse: While you have been sinning, I have been trying to talk to you, but you refuse to listen.
translation_verse: Too, man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ni mun yīntì kii bimbee. M yōoǹ ŋyunti ki kpáafì-ni, ama ní naa pílifì, m yíiń-ni ní naa kíí-mi.

english_verse: Don't think this temple will protect you. Long ago I told your ancestors to build it and worship me here, but now I have decided to tear it down, just as I destroyed Shiloh.
translation_verse: Kpèè ni dū ni-mákal ki páaǹ kunimbɔtidii nee pu. Bi dū-ku ki sú-mi, ní man dū-ku ki tīī ni nì ni-naanjab. Too, m làá ŋá-ku kii m nín nìn ŋá Siiloo circir paaŋŋu puee ní.

english_verse: And as for you, people of Judah, I'm going to send you away from my land, just as I sent away the people of Ephraim and the other northern tribes. Punishment for Worshiping Other Gods
translation_verse: M làá dū-ni kí fá ndan kii m nín fá ni-nabiyaamu Eefiraayiim naantiibi puee ní.» Ŋwimmeem min Unimbɔti kaa pílifée

english_verse: Do you see what the people of Judah are doing in their towns and in the streets of Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Saa wāĺ tin kɔkɔ bi bí ki ŋáań Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pueeee?

english_verse: Children gather firewood, their fathers build fires, and their mothers mix dough to bake bread for the goddess they call the Queen of Heaven. They even offer wine sacrifices to other gods, just to insult me.
translation_verse: Mbiyaamu là idɔ ní bibaatiibi kpà ŋŋmi, ní binaatiibi nùkù ŋyim kí ŋá kalaabi kí tīī yilpu Nimpubɔtiu. Ni féeń awaa nnyim ki gbítí m-ŋuul.

english_verse: But they are not only insulting me; they are also harming themselves by doing these shameful things.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bālifì yii: <Mimmee man ní bi dàkafī yii bi ŋáań ikpitaaa? Bi ŋáań bi-ba ní, ní an sá bi-cooi!>»

english_verse: And now, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will flood Judah with my fiery anger until nothing is left—no people or animals, no trees or crops. It Is Useless To Offer Sacrifices
translation_verse: «Too, m làá kpáatí m-ŋuukpaandi kí sìtī mpaan nee nì binib nì ipeel nì tisatin sufii nì tikpaajin pu. Di làá nīn bí kii ŋŋmi ŋun kaa kúùyee ní.» Ditimbundi din kaa pílifí di-Nimbɔtiuee

english_verse: At the time I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I didn't command them to offer sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: M nín nìn nyántì ni-naanjab kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee, maa nìn tùkū-bi yii bí ŋá tiba. Maa nìn bí-bi yii bí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi àá saraabi biba kí tīī-mi.

english_verse: Instead, I told them, “If you listen to me and do what I tell you, I will be your God, you will be my people, and all will go well for you.”
translation_verse: Ama m nìn kpáafì-bi yii: <Ní pīlifìmaan m-nyɔkɔ. Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, m làá nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu, ní nimbi ń nīn sá man nibul. Nóómaan nsan ŋun m cátì ki bíl̀-nee ní án nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī-ni.

english_verse: But your ancestors refused to listen. They were stubborn, and whenever I wanted them to go one way, they always went the other.
translation_verse: Ama baa nìn pílifiǹ-mi, kaa kpōoǹ bi-tafal ki pílifì. Bi lēē kí nóó bi-landɔkɔkpitii. An nìn bàà sá bí fàtī bi-nimbiin kí túĺ-mee, ní bi fātì bi-boon ki tīī-mi.

english_verse: Ever since your ancestors left Egypt, I have been sending my servants the prophets to speak for me.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun m nyántì ni-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkin kí dāá sāā díǹee, m pée tūǹ baabadal m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi ni-cee ní kaa gbèentí.

english_verse: So you must say to them: People of Judah, I am the Lord your God, but you have refused to obey me, and you didn't change when I punished you. And now, you no longer even pretend to be faithful to me.
translation_verse: Tùkù-bi yii: <Kpèèmaan, ni sá ditimbundi din kaa pílifí di-Dindaan di-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ, ní kaa fòol̄ u-saŋkiiyee ní. Tin bí deedeeyee kpíì ni-cee, ní ubɔ kaa ti sòoǹ ti-pu.>» Laakin bi pɔ̄fì binibee tantakal

english_verse: Shave your head bald and throw away the hair. Sing a funeral song on top of a barren hill. You people have made me angry, and I have abandoned you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Juuda nibul, Cā a-yikpiti tin dàkà yii a dū a-ba ki sú-mee kí fá, kí tóoń ŋkpiisilan ajoon ŋin yilpu kaa cáá timoolee pu. Di sá yii a sá dinibul din kɔ́ǹ man ni-Dindaan diŋuulee ní. An pu ní maa ti là kí wāl̀-si ki dū-si ki fá.»

english_verse: You have disobeyed me by putting your disgusting idols in my temple, and now the temple itself is disgusting to me.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Juuda yab ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee m-nimbiin. Bi cáá bi-waaŋi ŋin sá ntimbiilee ki kɔ́ǹ Kudii kun bi dūu sú-mee poon ki kɔ́ǹ-ku tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: At Topheth in Hinnom Valley you have built altars where you kill your children and burn them as sacrifices to other gods. I would never think of telling you to do this.
translation_verse: Been-Inɔɔm tantakalinee, bi bɔ́ntì ŋwaapaan ŋun bi yíì Toofeetee. Niin ní bi cáá bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ki tòotī ki wù ŋŋmi ki ŋáań saraabi. Maa pée tīī-bi mara yii bí ŋá míǹ dalba dalba, kaa kpáàa dākafì an pu ŋwindal.»

english_verse: So watch out! Someday that place will no longer be called Topheth or Hinnom Valley. It will be called Slaughter Valley, because you will bury your dead there until you run out of room,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Iwiin bí ki dòoń, baa dāa gíti yíì mpaan gbanti yii: <Toofeeti> àá <Been-Inɔɔm tantakal>, ama <dipɔ̀fil tantakal>. Niin ní bi làá dāá síb́ anikpil, di sá yii mpaan kaa dāa gíti bí laaba bí síb́-ŋi.

english_verse: and then bodies will lie scattered on the ground. Birds and wild animals will come and eat, and no one will be around to scare them off.
translation_verse: Inoon nì ipeel làá dāá gbáb́ kí bìin̄ anikpil gbanti pu ki jīǹ, ní ubɔ dāa kpá kí jà-i.

english_verse: When I am finished with your land, there will be deathly silence in the empty ruins of Jerusalem and the towns of Judah—no happy voices, no sounds of parties or wedding celebrations.
translation_verse: M làá dāá yàntī Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu ifaal nì dipɔɔpindi laŋyi ń ŋmīĺ. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti gbìl̀ animpucaŋgbiil pu. Di sá yii kitiŋ làá dāá kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma ní.

english_verse: Then the bones of the dead kings of Judah and their officials will be dug up, along with the bones of the priests, the prophets, and everyone else in Jerusalem
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Ŋyunti gbantee, bi làá dāá nyāntiń Juuda yab bɔtiibi nì bi-kàliŋkpilib nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì bin kóò Jeerusaleemee kpabiŋ akaakul poon.

english_verse: who loved and worshiped the sun, moon, and stars. These bones will be scattered and left lying on the ground like trash, where the sun and moon and stars can shine on them.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá dū akpab gbanti kí yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu ŋwìiń nì uŋmal nì iŋmalbijaa in bitaŋkpiibi gbanti nìn néeń, ki jáaḿ, ki nóó ní ki bàlifēe nimbiin. An pu ní ubɔ kaa dāa gíti kōontí akpab gbanti kí gíiǹ-ŋi kí ŋá akaakulin. Ama ŋi làá dāá dòon̄ kitiŋ kí kpántí ntiŋkpam.

english_verse: Some of you people of Judah will be left alive, but I will force you to go to foreign countries, and you will wish you were dead. I, the Lord God All-Powerful, have spoken. The People Took the Wrong Road
translation_verse: Binikpitib nee kansikin bin yaa láa kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee dāa lì yii ŋkúm sɔ́ǹ dimaŋfal.> Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.» Ti-Dindaan nibul kaa ti là kí gítiń u-cee

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Jerusalem, when you stumble and fall, you get back up, and if you take a wrong road, you turn around and go back.
translation_verse: «Á tùkù-bi yii, ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Unil yaa lítèe, waa ti yíkáaa? Unil yaa yīntì nsanee, waa gítiń u-boonaaa?

english_verse: So why do you refuse to come back to me? Why do you hold so tightly to your false gods?
translation_verse: Ama ba pu ní Jeerusaleem yab yīntì nsan, ní ki gbíntìi nìkì ki fàtī bi-boon ki tìì man ní? Binib gbanti dū bi-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ awaa ní ki yíì kaa là kí fàtīí gítiń m-cee.

english_verse: Storks, doves, swallows, and thrushes all know when it's time to fly away for the winter and when to come back. But you, my people, don't know what I demand.
translation_verse: Áli gba naakpaapiimbi bin ŋàaǹ kutaa puee nyí ŋyunti ŋun sá bí yīkì kí búntée. Ananjil nì jikpaasib nì ŋkoosiyaakpaamu nyí bi-yuntii kí gítiń. Ama m-nibul kaa nyí kí nóó man bi-Dindaan marab bin m síiǹ-bee.»

english_verse: You say, “We are wise because we have the teachings and laws of the Lord.” But I say that your teachers have turned my words into lies!
translation_verse: Mana ní ni ŋūǹ kí lì yii: «Ti sá biciŋfitiibi, ti-Dindaan marab bí ti-cee?» Di sá yii bimaradakaliibi bin fàtīi ŋmà marabee sá binyimɔndambi ní ki kpántí marab gbanti.

english_verse: Your wise men have rejected what I say, and so they have no wisdom. Now they will be trapped and put to shame; they won't know what to do.
translation_verse: Biciŋfitiibi gbanti dū ti-Dindaan marab ki fá. Mimmee bi-ciiŋŋu gbanti gíti bí tilatin? Icoo cúú-bi gbòooo. Dinyoondi kɔ́-bi ní an sàl̄-bi kii kutaliŋŋuee. Binib bí ki sòoǹ yii tikɔkɔ còom̄ tiŋan (Kpèè Yeer

english_verse: I'll give their wives and fields to strangers. Everyone is greedy and dishonest, whether poor or rich. Even the prophets and priests cannot be trusted.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá dū bi-nimpoobi kí tīī biba, kí dū bi-sati kí tīī bin làá dāá fōō-tèe. Di sá yii kí yòon̄ bikpaambi kí tin sāā ŋwaamuee, bi-kɔkɔ bìǹ ki nyàab̀ njim ní. Kí yòon̄ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kí cáá sāā bisaraaŋaliibee, bi-kɔkɔ cáá inaamuul ní.

english_verse: All they ever offer to my deeply wounded people are empty hopes for peace.
translation_verse: Bi cáá m-nibul naabuŋu ki ŋáań bugbambu ní ki lì yii: <Ŋgbansɔŋfi bí! Ŋgbansɔŋfi bí!> Ama ní ŋgbansɔŋfi kpá.

english_verse: They should be ashamed of the way they live, but they don't even blush. And so, when I punish Judah, they will end up on the ground, dead like everyone else.
translation_verse: Ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi tūǹee, an kɔ́ǹ-bi icoooo? Aayee, kpataaa! Baa kpáàa nyí gba yii bi ŋá tiba.» Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «An pu ní bi làá kūtì bin bíi lítée pu bí lítí. M yaa láa tāā ki bíikì bi-puee, bi làá dāá ká yii bi dɔ̄ kitiŋ ní.» Dimákal kaa ti bí ti-Dindaan

english_verse: I will wipe them out. They are vines without grapes; fig trees without figs or leaves. They have not done a thing that I told them! I, the Lord, have spoken. The People and Their Punishment
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «An yaa ŋmāntì ḿ kìtī asubil bi-ceeyee, maa kāntí fiinyi pu abilaaa, kaa kāntí fiigi pu abil. Tifaal gba kūń, m làá dū-bi kí fìtīǹ bisanjitiliibi.» Isirayeel nibul

english_verse: The people of Judah say to each other, “What are we waiting for? Let's run to a town with walls and die there. We rebelled against the Lord, and we were sentenced to die by drinking poison.
translation_verse: «Ba pu ní tí nīn kā kaa cìŋkī? Tí kóoǹ kí kpāfì, kí cùú kɔ́ ntimu mun bi máń digundi ki túee poon, kí nīn kíǹ ki kā ki cí ŋkúm. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu yāntì taa ti ŋūǹ kí cìŋkì ti-ba, ní ki yàntī ti nyù nnyim min cáá ndabiimee, kun puee ti yīntiǹ-u.

english_verse: We had hoped for peace and a time of healing, but all we got was terror.
translation_verse: Ti bàà kā ki cí ŋgbansɔŋfi, ama kaa ká tiwammɔntiil tiba. Ti bàà kā ki cí kí ká dicáaǹdi, ama tifaandi di dɔ́miń.

english_verse: Our enemies have reached the town of Dan in the north, and the snorting of their horses makes us tremble with fear. The enemy will destroy Jerusalem and our entire nation. No one will survive.”
translation_verse: Binannanliibi bāań Daani tiŋkin ki dóò. Ti gbìl̄ itanjaa nín fèefī doooo kitiŋ gbantinee. Kuwoou kun bi ŋáańee yāntì kitiŋ kɔkɔ cīŋkì. Bi dòoń kí nàan̄ kitiŋ nì ki-nib, kitiŋee nì bin kóò ki-puee.» ti-Dindaan

english_verse: “Watch out!” the Lord says. “I'm sending poisonous snakes to attack you, and no one can stop them.” Jeremiah Mourns for His People
translation_verse: «M làá dū ikoobu in cáá tilool ubɔ kaa cáá i-naajuukee ní kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní í jūntì-ni», ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Yeereemii timinsii Yeereemii

english_verse: I'm burdened with sorrow and feel like giving up.
translation_verse: Tiba kaa bí ki ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ m-nimbaaku, m-poon kaam cɔ́tì.

english_verse: In a foreign land my people are crying. Listen! You'll hear them say, “Has the Lord deserted Zion? Is he no longer its king?” I hear the Lord reply, “Why did you make me angry by worshiping useless idols?”
translation_verse: Pīlifìmaan, m-nibul di kūuntí ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi doooo kitindandatii poonee. Ti-Dindaan kaa ti bí Siiyɔn tiŋkinaaa? Siiyɔn kaa ti cáá ubɔtaaa? ti-Dindaan Ba pu ní bi cáá bi-waaŋi ki gbítí m-ŋuul, awaa ŋin kaa bí tiban ki nyánní laabee?

english_verse: The people complain, “Spring and summer have come and gone, but still the Lord hasn't rescued us.”
translation_verse: Tijincakaal yuntiŋu jítì, dipeel jítì, ama nì díǹ, taa láá ká difiil.

english_verse: My people are crushed, and so is my heart. I am horrified and mourn.
translation_verse: M-nibul nín kɔ́ dinimbinaamandi din poonee cɔ́tì m-poon kaam. Kunimbaau kɔ́-mi, maa ti nyí tin poon m bée.

english_verse: If medicine and doctors may be found in Gilead, why aren't my people healed?
translation_verse: Isufi in bi cáa cāantí iweenee kaa bí Galaadi tiŋkinaaa? Ucaanli ubɔ kaa bí niinaaa? Kin ba pu ní nì díǹ m-nibul buuŋŋu kaa bíi kúù?

english_verse: I wish that my eyes were fountains of tears, so I could cry day and night for my people who were killed.
translation_verse: M bàà là kí nīn bí kuteeun laakin bisaŋkinliibi túutée! M bàà làá dū m-nibul nee kí fá kí cùú nīn bí niin ki dátiǹ-bi. Di sá bi-kɔkɔ sá bilaakpaadambi, ki nyēē binib boon.

english_verse: I wish I could go into the desert and find a hiding place from all who are treacherous and unfaithful to God. The Lord Answers Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Bi-limbiliŋ bí kii butɔbu bun bi dáaĺee ní. Bi dū nnyimɔn ní ki jíń dibeel kitiŋ pu, kaa sá mbaamɔn. Bi ŋáań ikpiti ní kaa gbèentí, ama baa nyí-mi.

english_verse: The Lord replied: Lies come from the mouths of my people, like arrows from a bow. With each dishonest deed their power increases, and not one of them will admit that I am God.
translation_verse: Báà ŋma ń nīn nyí nì u-ba nì u-bɔɔ. Ubɔ ń taa nín̄ máká u-nabiki pu, di sá yii kì ŋūǹ kí kīil̀-u ní ubɔɔti mun ŋūǹ kí kūŋfì u-boon.

english_verse: Jeremiah, all your friends and relatives tell lies about you, so don't trust them.
translation_verse: Báà ŋma kíiĺ u-juti, ubɔ kaa sòoǹ ibaamɔn. Bi mántì kí nīn mɔ́ntí. Bi-tuŋkpitiŋ puee baa ti ŋūǹ kí gítiń m-cee.»

english_verse: They wear themselves out, always looking for a new way to cheat their friends.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: Bi ŋáań tipɔmbɔti kaa gbèentí, ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn ki bùsī. Bi yíití kaa là kí béé-mi.

english_verse: And so I will purify the hearts of my people just as gold is purified in a furnace. I have no other choice.
translation_verse: Bi-limbiliŋ bí kii nlɔpiinee ní, tinyimɔmbɔti ŋma di nyēē bi-nyɔmmun. Bi-nyunculiŋ pu ní bi sòoǹ nì bi-juti yii ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí u-cee, ama ní bi-pɔbiliŋ poonee, bi pīil̀ udaan kutaliŋŋu.

english_verse: They say they want peace, but this lie is deadly, like an arrow that strikes when you least expect it.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kii tin bí nee kɔkɔ puee, m taa dáaĺ bi-tafalaaa? M taa tɔ̀ ditimbundi din bí kii di neeyee ipɔntoonaaa?» Nsiim nì iyaliŋki yuntiŋu

english_verse: Give me one good reason not to punish them as they deserve. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken. Jeremiah Weeps for His People
translation_verse: M bí ajoon pu ki sūǹ ki yáliŋkí, m bí ki gà kunaakpaapɔɔu ikpiisilan. Baa ti gbìl̀ tiwaŋkuti siim pu. Inoon nì tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ sáǹ. Báà tiba kaa ti bí.

english_verse: I weep for the pastureland in the hill country. It's so barren and scorched that no one travels there. No cattle can be found there, and birds and wild animals have all disappeared.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī Jeerusaleem ń kpántí ataŋkpakpuku, laakin sinsiŋkub làá nīn kóòyee, ní kí yàntī Juuda timmu ń kpántí kuteeu, laakin binib kaa làá nīn gíti kóòyee.

english_verse: I heard the Lord reply, “When I am finished, Jerusalem and the towns of Judah will be piles of ruins where only jackals live.” Why the Land Was Destroyed
translation_verse: Unil ubɔ bí ki cáá iciin ki ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tibɔti nee taapuɔɔɔ? Ti-Dindaan yaa sòon̄ nì udaanee, ú tùkū-ti kun pu ní bi nāaǹ kitiŋ nee, ki wùn̄-kì ŋŋmi kì kpántì kii kuteeu ubɔ kaa ti jītí niinee.

english_verse: I said to the Lord, “None of us can understand why the land has become like an uncrossable desert. Won't you explain why?”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kun pu tin bí nee bāań-bee di sá yii bi dū marab bin m tīī-bee ki fá. Baa pílifiǹ-mi kaa nóó-mi.»

english_verse: The Lord said: I destroyed the land because the people disobeyed me and rejected my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ama bi nóó bíǹ bi-ba landɔkɔi ní. Bi-baabi nìn dàkā-bi awaa ŋin bi yíì Baalee, ní awaa gbanti ní bi nóó.

english_verse: So I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, promise them poison to eat and drink.
translation_verse: M làá jà-bi bí yàl̄ kí kɔ́ atimbun ŋin bíǹ bi-ba kaa nyáaa, bi-naanjab mun kaa nìn nyée poon. M làá dū ajanjakiti kí páań bi-boon, ŋí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi.

english_verse: I'll scatter them in foreign countries that they and their ancestors have never even heard of. Finally, I will send enemy soldiers to kill every last one of them. The Women Who Are Paid To Weep
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii: Isirayeel nibul «Bɔ́ntímaan kí yíiń binimpoobi bin sūǹee bí dāan̄ kí sɔ̄. Ní nyàab̀ bimɔmmɔntiibi!

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful said, “Make arrangements now for the women who are paid to weep at funerals, especially the women who can cry the loudest.”
translation_verse: Bí yáb́ malaa. Bí gāā-ti ikpiisilan! Nnyinnyim ń gbí ti-nimbiliŋin. Ti-niŋgbunti ń díkí nnyinnyim ń nīn pùub̀!» Yeereemii

english_verse: The people answered, “Let them come quickly and cry for us, until our own eyes are flooded with tears.
translation_verse: Ti gbìl̄ Siiyɔn pú ikpiisilan pu. Bi nāaǹ-ti! «Ba cooi bulifi poon ní ti bí na! Ti làá yīkì kí fá ti-tiŋki, di sá yii bi kpéelikì ti-diiŋŋi.»

english_verse: Now those of us on Zion cry, ‘We are ruined! We can't stand the shame. Our homes have been destroyed, and we must leave our land.’
translation_verse: Nimbi binimpoobee, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi nee. Ní ŋátí ni-tafal kí pīlifì u-nyɔɔbundi! Ní dàkà ni-bisalib ŋkpiisilan nee, báà ŋma ń dàkà u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔ iyaliŋki laŋŋu nee:

english_verse: “We ask you women to pay attention to what the Lord says. We will teach you a funeral song that you can teach your daughters and friends:
translation_verse: «Di sá yii ŋkúm dàb̄ ti-tɔkɔlab ki kɔ́ ti-pu, mì kɔ́ ti-dinyaaŋŋin. Mì yōoǹ ti-biyaamu adan pu, ki yōoǹ binipɔmbi sampaambi pu.» ti-Dindaan

english_verse: ‘We were in our fortress, but death sneaked in through our windows. It even struck down children at play and our strongest young men.’
translation_verse: «Sii Yeereemii, gíti sòoǹ tin ti-Dindaan lēe yii: <Anikpil dɔ̄ kitiŋ fìlfil kii tinaabin ní bi bíl̀ kusaaunee. Ŋi náań nì idifin in bicaliibi cáń ki bíl̀ ubɔ kaa pá bi-boon ki kōontée.>» Iciin in sá tiŋman pu yayee

english_verse: “The Lord has told us the ground will be covered with dead bodies, like ungathered stalks of grain or manure in a field.” What the Lord Likes Best
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Uciŋfiti ń taa nín̄ yòontí u-ba u-ciiŋyi pu. Upɔndaan ń taa nín̄ yòontí u-ba u-pɔŋŋu pu. Ugaaja ń taa nín̄ yòontí u-ba u-gaajati pu.

english_verse: If you feel you must brag, then have enough sense to brag about worshiping me, the Lord. What I like best is showing kindness, justice, and mercy to everyone on earth.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋwiin ŋubɔ dòoń m làá tāā kí bīikì bin gíí dikpancandi ŋwuŋgban pu gíitamee pu,

english_verse: The Lord said: Listen to me, you people of Israel. Don't follow the customs of those nations who become frightened when they see something strange happen in the sky.
translation_verse: U bí yii: «Ní taa nín̄ túŋkíǹ atimbun ŋin kíǹee! Ní taa fàŋkì tidaandi tin nyēē ki pāantí kutagbɔŋu puee. Atimbun ŋin kíǹee di fàŋkí an wanti.

english_verse: Their religion is worthless! They chop down a tree, carve the wood into an idol,
translation_verse: Di sá yii anibul ŋin kíǹee koobiliŋ kaa bí tiban! Bi gà ndɔ kubambaŋŋun, ní ukpiŋkpiiti ń dū kicɔkɔ kí kpítí diwaal.

english_verse: cover it with silver and gold, and then nail it down so it won't fall over.
translation_verse: U dù animbil kúti nì sindaariya kí nyɔ̀kɔntì-dì, ní kí dū dikújal nì mpiin kí kpáá-dì kí nákań, dí nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄ kí taa nín̄ cìŋkī.

english_verse: An idol is no better than a scarecrow. It can't speak, and it has to be carried, because it can't walk. Why worship an idol that can't help or harm you? Jeremiah Praises the Lord
translation_verse: Awaa gbanti náań nì tiwan tin bi sākaǹ diputaajul kpaabun ki fàantí inoonee ní. Awaa gbanti kaa sòoǹ. Bi tūntí-ŋi ní, di sá yii ŋaa ŋūǹ kí còom̀. Taa fàŋkìmaan-ŋi, di sá yii ŋaa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tikpitilaaa, kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiŋan mun.»

english_verse: Our Lord, great and powerful, you alone are God.
translation_verse: Sii, ti-Dindaan, ubɔ kaa bí kii siiyee! A sá ukpaan, ní a-yindi sá dikpaandi ki cáá mpɔn.

english_verse: You are King of the nations. Everyone should worship you. No human anywhere on earth is wiser than you.
translation_verse: Ŋma di kaa fàŋkí sii atimbun bɔtiu? Kun puee sii ní bi máaǹ kí fàŋkì. Di sá yii duulinya ciŋfitiibi kansikin, nì abee kɔkɔ poonee, ubɔ kaa bí kii siiyee.

english_verse: Idols are made by humans. A carver shapes the wood. A metalworker hammers out a covering of gold from Uphaz or of silver from Tarshish. Then the idol is dressed in blue and purple clothes.
translation_verse: Ukpiŋkpiiti di kpítì-ŋi, ní ukúduntil dūu tikúti ki dūntì ki nyūntì-ŋi ní ki dū animbil kúti tin nyánní Taarsiisi tiŋkinee, nì sindaariya un nyánní Ufasi tiŋkinee ki nyɔ̄kɔntì-ŋi. Míǹ boonee ní bi dū iŋaaman cínciŋ nì in máǹ wèeeeyee ki ŋáĺ dibɔkutil ki pēeǹ-ŋi. Bin nyí iŋal pu tundi tiŋanee di mɔ́ɔ̀ an wanti.

english_verse: You, Lord, are the only true and living God. You will rule for all time. When you are angry the earth shakes, and nations are destroyed.
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔti tiŋman pu yɔu. U sá Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee, ki sá ubɔti kí nīn cá jaanjaan. U yaa fōō diŋuulee, kitiŋ cìŋkī ní, ní atimbun kaa ŋūǹ kí yūĺ u-bum nimbiin.

english_verse: You told me to say that idols did not create the heavens and the earth, and that you, the Lord, will destroy every idol.
translation_verse: Kpèè ni nín làá sòoǹ nì bi puee sèé: Bi máaǹ kí kúntí awaa ŋin kaa náań yilpu nì taapuee, ŋi máaǹ kí wāŋkì kutagbɔŋu taapu.

english_verse: With your wisdom and power you created the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di dū u-pɔŋŋu ki ŋá kitiŋ, ki dū u-ciiŋŋu ki náań duulinya, ki dū u-nyil ki kpátì kutagbɔŋu ki dāntì.

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at your command. You make clouds appear— you send the winds from your storehouse and make lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: U yaa téeńee, inyiŋfi kōontí ní kí kpāfì kutagbɔŋu pu. U yàntī atagbaŋkpaan ń nyānní kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ kí jɔ̄m̀. U yàntī utaa ń ŋmɔ́ kí cáań utaa, ní ki nyāntiń kubuŋu ku-walimbookun.

english_verse: People who make idols are so stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods are not alive.
translation_verse: Binib kɔkɔ bākatì sèee, kaa ti nyí tin poon bi bée. Awaa ŋin bikúduntiliibi mɔ́ɔ́yee cáá-bi icoo. Awaa gbanti sá tinyimɔmbɔti ní. Ŋaa cáá kufoou.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ŋì sá tiwan tin kaa bí tibanee, ki mɔ̄ tilaal. Ŋwiin ŋun ti-Dindaan làá yīkì ŋi-puee, ŋì làá wāŋkì ní.

english_verse: But you, Israel's God, created all things, and you chose Israel to be your very own. Your name is the Lord All-Powerful. Judah Will Be Thrown from Its Land
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti un sá Jaakɔb gaajawantee, kaa bí kii ŋíǹ nín bí puee. Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu di náań duulinya kɔkɔ, ní Isirayeel naakooku sá u-fakal. U-yindi di sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan. Nnaabu tóobiń

english_verse: I said to the people of Judah, “Gather your things; you are surrounded.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem, sii un bi māntìi túee, kóoǹ a-waŋguliŋ ŋin dɔ̄ kitiŋee!

english_verse: The Lord said these troubles will lead to your capture, and he will throw you from this land like a rock from a sling.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Min bí nee, m làá dū kitiŋ nee nib kí tɔ̄ ndan kii kujaataafuŋ taŋkpalee. M làá cáań dinimbinaamandi kí tɔ̄ bi-pu áli ubɔ ń taa ŋmátí.»

english_verse: The people answered, “We are wounded and doomed to die. Why did we say we could stand the pain?
translation_verse: Ba busuu dee! Nnaabu ŋulɔŋu ŋúǹ dee!, Tiweendi tin m fōōyee kaa cáá dicáaǹdi! M lī m-ban yii: «An kaa páb́, m làá ŋmā kí túń m-gìńdi.

english_verse: Our homes are destroyed; our children are dead. No one is left to help us find shelter.”
translation_verse: Bi nāaǹ m-tantiu, u-ŋmiii kɔkɔ tīfì. M-biyaamu yíkì-mi, muaa ti bí. Ubɔ kaa ti bí kí cóoń m-tantiu, kí ŋāŋkì m-kɔŋkooŋŋu.»

english_verse: But I told them, “Our leaders were stupid failures, because they refused to listen to the Lord. And so we've been scattered like sheep.
translation_verse: Tin yì-tèe di sá yii bikpootiliibi ŋá digbaandi. Baa nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan. An pu ní an kaa bútì-bi, ní bin bi nìn kpòotēe yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: “Sounds of destruction rumble from the north like distant thunder. Soon our towns will be ruins where only jackals live.” Jeremiah Prays
translation_verse: Ti gbìl̄ kuwoou kubɔ pu, ku tóobiń. Kukunsaŋu kubɔ nyánní ŋgan pú tiŋkin. Ku làá yàntī Juuda tiŋki ń kpántí kuteeu, laakin sinsiŋkub làá nīn kóòyee. Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu wimmeem

english_verse: I know, Lord, that we humans are not in control of our own lives.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, m nyí yii, unil kaa yì u-ba. Unil un còom̄ee kaa ŋūǹ kí kpòotī u-ba.

english_verse: Correct me, as I deserve, but not in your anger, or I will be dead.
translation_verse: Dáaĺ m-tafal, ama á taa lákatí marab pu. Taa fōō diŋuul, an yaa sá fám, a làá nàan̄-mi.

english_verse: Our enemies refuse to admit that you are God or to worship you. They have wiped out our people and left our nation lying in ruins. So get angry and sweep them away!
translation_verse: Kpáatí a-ŋuul kí sìtī atimbun ŋin kaa nyí-see pu, kí sìtī anibul ŋin kaa jáaḿ-see pu. Kun puee bi tɔ̄ntì a-nibul Jaakɔb naantiibi, bi fúkúl̀-bi ki púntì-bi, ní ki nāaǹ bi-tiŋki.

english_verse: My commands haven't changed since I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, a nation that seemed like a blazing furnace where iron ore is melted. I told your ancestors that if they obeyed my commands, I would be their God, and they would be my people.
translation_verse: M nìn nyántì ni-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkin, kipaai ŋmiŋun. Ŋyunti gbanti ní man nì bi nìn ŋá mpèé nee. M nìn bí-bi yii: <Ní pīlifì m-nyɔkɔ kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ m bí yii ní ŋée. Niinee, ni làá nīn sá m-nibul, ní ma mun ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu.>

english_verse: Then I did what I had promised and gave them this wonderful land, where you now live. “Yes, Lord,” I replied, “that's true.”
translation_verse: Niinee, m làá ŋá m nín nìn pōoǹ ni-naanjab puee kí tīī-bi. M nìn pōoǹ-bi yii m làá dū kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee kí tīī-bi. Kitiŋ gbanti poon ní ni bí díǹ nee.» Ní m kíí yii: «An sá míǹ ní ti-Dindaan.»

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to everyone on the streets of Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah: Pay attention to the commands in my agreement with you.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Dū an bɔti gbanti kɔkɔ kí bāakì Juuda timmu nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu yii: <Ní pīlifìmaan mpèé nee bɔti, kí ŋá tì nín bí yii ní ŋá puee.

english_verse: Ever since I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I have been telling your people to obey me. But you and your ancestors
translation_verse: M nín nìn nyántì ni-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, m nìn pée kpáafí-bi ní kaa gbèentí, kii m nín bíi kpáafí ni mun díǹ pu nee ní. M lì ki bùsī yii bí pīlifì m-nyɔkɔ.

english_verse: have always been stubborn. You have refused to listen, and instead you have done whatever your sinful hearts have desired. You have not kept the agreement we made, so I will make you suffer every curse that goes with it.
