translation_verse: Ama baa pílifàaa, kaa fātìi tɔ́. Bi-landɔkɔkpitii ní bi nóó. Niinee ní m yāntì agìń ŋin m nìn tùkū-bi yii bi yaa kaa ŋúb́ mpèé nee bɔti bi làá kée, bāań-bi.>»

english_verse: The Lord said to me: Jeremiah, the people of Judah and Jerusalem are plotting against me.
translation_verse: Boonee ní ti-Dindaan gíti bí-mi yii: «Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab ŋá kinyɔkɔ kí já nì mi.

english_verse: They have sinned in the same way their ancestors did, by turning from me and worshiping other gods. The northern kingdom of Israel broke the agreement I made with your ancestors, and now the southern kingdom of Judah has done the same.
translation_verse: Bi fātìi gítì ikpiti in bi-naanjab bin nìn yíì kaa pílifì m-bɔtee nìn ŋée pu. Bi nóó awaa ki tòotī-ŋi. Isirayeel nì Juuda yab bíil̀ mpèé ŋun nìn bí man nì bi-naanjab kansikinee.

english_verse: Here is what I've decided to do. I will bring suffering on the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and no one will escape. They will beg me to help, but I won't listen to their prayers.
translation_verse: «Too, an pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: <M làá cáań nnaabu ŋubɔ kí tɔ̄ bi-pu, ní baa làá ŋmā kí ŋmátí. Bi làá dāá kúuǹ kí yíiń-mi ḿ jòò-bi, ama maa làá dāá pīlifiǹ-bi.

english_verse: Then they will offer sacrifices to their other gods and ask them for help. After all, the people of Judah have more gods than towns, and more shameful altars for Baal than there are streets in Jerusalem. But those gods won't be able to rescue the people of Judah from disaster.
translation_verse: Juuda yab timmu nín wīikí puee, míǹ ní bi-waaŋi mun wīikí. Jeerusaleem daŋŋi nín wīikí puee, míǹ ní ki-saraafaŋyi mun wīikí. Bi tùutī i-pu saraabi ki tìì diwaal Baal din sá-bi icooyee.>

english_verse: Jeremiah, don't pray for these people or beg me to rescue them. If you do, I won't listen, and I certainly won't listen if they pray!
translation_verse: Sii Yeereemii, á taa pée mèè dinibul nee pu. Á taa sɔ̄ di-pu, kí taa gbàam̀ di-pu. Di sá yii dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu poonee, bi làá dāá mèè-mi, ama maa làá dāá pīlifiǹ-bi.» Ti-Dindaan làá gāā ɔliifi subu kí lúkú

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah: You are my chosen people, but you have no right to be here in my temple, doing such evil things. The sacrifices you offer me won't protect you from disaster, so stop celebrating.
translation_verse: «Ba ní dinibul din m néeńee nib dòoń kí ŋá m-Diikun ní? Bi ŋá bi-landɔkɔkpitii nín sá puee. Bi dàkafī yii ipoon nì tiwaŋkuti tin bi cáa ŋáań-mi saraayee ŋūǹ kí kpàà bi-naabuŋu kí cùnnì ndan kí wàatī-bi ní. Mimmee míǹ ní bi làá ŋá kí ŋmátáaa?

english_verse: Once you were like an olive tree covered with fruit. But soon I will send a noisy mob to break off your branches and set you on fire.
translation_verse: M nìn pú-bi diyindi yii: <Ɔliifi subu bun faati pée sɔ̀m̀ bu-biliŋ ŋān̄ee ní.> Ama dibintiŋkpaandi poonee, m gāā ŋŋmi ki tūū bu-faati ní bu-paŋŋi wáŋkì.»

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful. You people of Judah were like a tree that I had planted, but you have made me angry by offering sacrifices to Baal, just as the northern kingdom did. And now I'm going to pull you up by the roots. The Plot To Kill Jeremiah *
translation_verse: An sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di cóoǹ-si. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, u bíi tùkù-si yii u làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ a-pu Isirayeel nì Juuda yab kpitii pu. Di sá yii bi tūutì talaalub ki tīī diwaal Baal ki gbítì ti-Dindaan ŋuul. Yeereemii dicaŋkun yab nyáń u-pu

english_verse: Some people plotted to kill me. And like a lamb being led to the butcher, I knew nothing about their plans.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lēē ki dàkā-mi, ní m béè tin m-nannanliibi bíi búkù m-puee.

english_verse: But then the Lord told me that they had planned to chop me down like a tree— fruit and all— so that no one would ever remember me again.
translation_verse: Mamee, m nìn bí kii dipibil din pɔ̀fì bi cáǹ-dì kí kpɔ̀ee ní. Maa nìn nyí tin bi nìn bíi bɔ́ntí m-puee. Bi nìn lì yii: «Tí gāā busubu bun dáá sɔ̀m̀ee kí lúkú. Tí lēē-u binifoobi tiŋkin bí taa ti téetí u-yindi pu.»

english_verse: I prayed, “Lord All-Powerful, you always do what is right, and you know every thought. So I trust you to help me and to take revenge.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, a sòoǹ tibɔti nì deedee ní. Sii di nyí unil pɔbilin nì u-landɔkɔi. M dū m-ba ki líiǹ-si á sòoǹ m-bɔti kí tīī-mi. Niinee ní ḿ ká a nín làá pɔ̀-mi puee.

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Jeremiah, some men from Anathoth say they will kill you, if you keep on speaking for me.
translation_verse: Too, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Anatooti yab bin là kí kpɔ̀-see puee sèé. Bi lì yii: «Taa ti nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti ti-Dindaan yindi pu, an yaa kaa sá míǹ, ti làá kpɔ̀-si.»

english_verse: But I will punish them. Their young men will die in battle, and their children will starve to death.
translation_verse: Too, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M làá tāā kí bīikì bi-pu. Bi làá kpɔ̀ bi-nipɔmbi kujaaun, ní bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ń kpú ŋkùm.

english_verse: And when I am finished, no one from their families will be left alive.
translation_verse: Dibindi din m làá tāā kí bīikì Anatooti yab pu kí cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-puee, báà uniseen kaa làá ŋmátí.»

english_verse: Whenever I complain to you, Lord, you are always fair. But now I have questions about your justice. Why is life easy for sinners? Why are they successful?
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, a baasii sá deedeedaan ní, maa ŋūǹ kí kpákáǹ-si. Ama m là kí sòoǹ nì si tin bí deedeeyee pu. Ba pu ní an bútí binikpitib ní? Ba pu ní bin kaa bí deedeeyee bí ŋgbansɔŋfin ní?

english_verse: You plant them like trees; you let them prosper and produce fruit. Yet even when they praise you, they don't mean it.
translation_verse: A cóoǹ-bi bi báaǹ inyaan áli ki lòon̄ abil. A-yindi pée kā bi-nyɔkɔn, ama ní bi-pɔbiliŋ dátiǹ-si.

english_verse: But you know, Lord, how faithful I've always been, even in my thoughts. So drag my enemies away and butcher them like sheep!
translation_verse: Ama mamee, m-Dindaan, a nyí-mi, a wāĺ-mi ki nyí m-landɔkɔi, i dɔ̄ a-nimbiin. Gàntī binikpitib kí síiń kii bi nín lèekī ipii in bi làá kpɔ̀ee kí síiń puee. Kpāafì-bi kí síiń ŋwiin ŋun a làá kpɔ̀-bee.

english_verse: How long will the ground be dry and the pasturelands parched? The birds and animals are dead and gone. And all of this happened because the people are so sinful. They even brag, “God can't see the sins we commit.” The Lord Answers Jeremiah
translation_verse: Kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní kitiŋ nee làá nīn bí kunimbaaun ní? Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní akpaan làá nīn dɔ̄ ki kūń ní? Kitiŋ nee peelii nì ki-nooŋyi bíi kúù bin kóò ki-puee kpitii pu. Bi lì yii: «Yeereemii kaa ti làá nīn bí kí ká tin làá bàń-tee.»

english_verse: Jeremiah, if you get tired in a race against people, how can you possibly run against horses? If you fall in open fields, what will happen in the forest along the Jordan River?
translation_verse: «Sii nì binib yaa bíi sáń ní a gīīyee, kin mana ní si nì itaamu ŋūǹ kí sāǹ kí kpáká? An yaa sá kitiŋ kin cáá ŋgbansɔŋfee poon ŋmaniŋma ní a ŋūǹ kí nīn bí a-pɔbil sɔ̀m̀ee, kin mana ní a làá ŋá a yaa láa kɔ́ Jɔɔdan mɔgbaakin?

english_verse: Even your own family has turned against you. They act friendly, but don't trust them. They're out to get you, and so is everyone else. The Lord Is Furious with His People
translation_verse: «Di sá yii, a-nabiyaamu, a-dicaŋkun yab nyēē a-boon. Bi kóoǹ binib ki kpáfì bí já nì si ní saa nyí. Bi yaa bíi sòoǹ nì si nì anyɔɔbummɔntee, á taa nín̄ máká bi-pu.» Ti-Dindaan dū u-diiku nì u-nibul ki fá

english_verse: I loved my people and chose them as my very own. But now I will reject them and hand them over to their enemies.
translation_verse: «M dū m-Diiku ki fá, m fātì m-boon ki tīī tin sá m-yatee. M dū dinibul din m néeńee ki líiǹ di-nannanliibi.

english_verse: My people have turned against me and roar at me like lions. That's why I hate them.
translation_verse: Bin nìn sá man yabee kpántì kii gbikinti di bí kupɔɔunee. Bi gbùkum̄ ki tátí m-pu, an puee ní maa ti là bi-bɔti.

english_verse: My people are like a hawk surrounded and attacked by other hawks. Tell the wild animals to come and eat their fill.
translation_verse: Bin nìn sá man yabee kpántì kii kinɔmbiki kin ŋān̄, ní ikaabu gbáb́ ki bīiǹ ki-puee. Ní cùmaan kí kóoǹ ipeel kí kpāfì, í dāan̄ kí jī jiŋaal.

english_verse: My beautiful land is ruined like a field or a vineyard trampled by shepherds and stripped bare by their flocks.
translation_verse: Bipikpaaliibi tikpil dɔ́miń ki bíil̀ m-fiinyi kpaabu, bi tāā m-tiŋki kì ŋá púb, ki dū m-tinjandi din ŋān̄ee ki kpántì kunimbaau teeku.

english_verse: A destroying army marches along desert roads and attacks everywhere. They are my deadly sword; no one is safe from them.
translation_verse: Binàanliibi páaǹní kuteeu jooŋŋi pu ki dòoń. Ti-Dindaan tàataajiki bíi pɔ̀fī tikɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ kitiŋ kílilaŋki ki tin sāā ki-kúntilaŋki. Báà uniseen kaa ti bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_verse: My people, you planted wheat, but because I was furious, I let only weeds grow. You wore yourselves out and gained only shame! The Lord Will Have Pity on Other Nations
translation_verse: Bi nìn búĺ bilee ní ki dāa cáń ikuŋkum, bi bìn̄ ki gīī púb, ama kaa ká ipaati. Ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi din u fōō ni-puee di yì-tì ní tin ni cáńee cáá-ni icoo. Ti-Dindaan nì Isirayeel yab kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb bɔti

english_verse: The Lord said: I gave this land to my people Israel, but enemies around it have attacked and robbed it. So I will uproot them from their own countries just as I will uproot Judah from its land.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M-kɔŋkɔnaatɔb bin kɔkɔ sá binikpitib ki gbēē kitiŋ kin m dūu tīī m-nibul Isirayeelee, m làá jà-bi bi-tiŋki pu. Ama m làá cúú Juuda nibul kí nyāntí bi-kansikin.

english_verse: But later, I will have pity on these nations and bring them back to their own lands.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, m làá sɔ̄ bi-saai, ní kí gíiǹní-bi bi-tiŋkin, báà ŋma nì u-kpaatanti pu.

english_verse: They once taught my people to worship Baal. But if they admit I am the only true God, and if they let my people teach them how to worship me, these nations will also become my people.
translation_verse: Bi nìn bífì m-nibul bí nīn pùtī Baal yindi pu. Ama bíǹ bi-ba yaa kíǹ ki cáá m-nibul bimbim, ki kíǹ ki cáá m-yindi ki pùtī ki lì yii: <M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalinee>, m làá dāá fōō-bi m-nibul kansikin.

english_verse: However, if they don't listen to me, I will uproot them from their lands and completely destroy them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ama atimbun gbanti diba yaa yíì kaa pílifiǹ-mee, m làá kpìkitī-dì kii bi nín kpìkitī busubu puee ní kí dū-dì kí líiǹ ŋkúm, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: The Lord told me, “Go and buy a pair of linen shorts. Wear them for a while, but don't wash them.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín tùkū-mi puee sèé: «Cùú dā ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee dambalau kí gbìn̄ a-caŋ, ama á taa dū-u kí tɔ̄ nnyimin.»

english_verse: So I bought a pair of shorts and put them on.
translation_verse: Ní m cūtìi dá dambala kii ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ḿ ŋá puee, ki dūu gbìn̄ m-caŋ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn gíti sòon̄ nì mi nliliitiim yii:

english_verse: “Take off the shorts. Go to Parah and hide the shorts in a crack between some large rocks.”
translation_verse: «Yòon̄ dambala un ní a dá ki gbìn̄ a-caŋee kí nīn cá Eefiraati mɔɔl caŋin kí dū-u kí báĺ ntaŋkpaween ŋubɔn.»

english_verse: I went back and dug the shorts out of their hiding place, but the cloth had rotted, and the shorts were ruined.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m nín cá Eefiraati mɔɔl caŋin. M bàn̄ee ní ki nyàab̄ dambalee ki lēeń-u laakin m nìn dū-u ki bál̀ee. Ama m nìn ká yii dambalee nìn bíil̀ kaa ti pée bí tiban.

english_verse: Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Jeremiah, I will use Babylonia to destroy the pride of the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Míǹ ní m làá bīil̀ Juuda yab lambil nì Jeerusaleem yab lambikpaandi.

english_verse: The people of Judah are evil and stubborn. So instead of listening to me, they do whatever they want and even worship other gods. When I am finished with these people, they will be good for nothing, just like this pair of shorts.
translation_verse: Di sá yii an sá dinibul din nib kaa ŋān̄ee ní. Bi yíì kaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ, ki nóó bíǹ bi-ba nín là puee saŋŋu. Bi jòó ki pá awaa boon ki tòotī-ŋi. Too, dinibul nee ń kpántí kii dambala un bíil̀ kaa ti bí tiban nee.»

english_verse: These shorts were tight around your waist, and that's how tightly I held onto the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. I wanted them to be my people. I wanted to make them famous, so that other nations would praise and honor me, but they refused to obey me. Wine Jars The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Kii unil nín dù dambala kí gbìn̄ u-caŋ puee, míǹ ní m nìn dū Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab ki bóob́ ki nákáǹ m-ba. M nín nìn là puee di sá bí nīn sá man nibul, kí nyā diyindi, kí nīn sá m-jilmau nì m-nyooti. Ama ní baa gbìl̄ ki tīiǹ-mi.» Ndamam nì ti-Dindaan ŋuul

english_verse: Jeremiah, tell the people of Judah, “The Lord God of Israel orders you to fill your wine jars with wine.” They will answer, “Of course we fill our wine jars with wine! Why are you telling us something we already know?”
translation_verse: «Á tùkù-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sɔ̀. Tilɔn bí bí nīn fūuntí ndaam ní>. Bi yaa kíí-si yii: <Mimmee timbi kaa nyí tilɔn nín bí bí nīn fūuntí ndaameeee?>

english_verse: Then say to them: I am the Lord, and what I'm going to do will make everyone in Judah and Jerusalem appear to be full of wine. And the worst ones will be the kings of David's family and the priests and the prophets.
translation_verse: Niinee ní á tùkù-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá yàntī kitiŋ nee pu nib nì bibɔtiibi bin kā Daafiidi beejal puee, nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì m-bɔnaatiliibi nì Jeerusaleem yab kɔkɔ ń gbí.

english_verse: Then I will smash them against each other like jars. I will have no pity on the young or the old, and they will all be destroyed. I, the Lord, have spoken. The People of Judah Will Be Taken Away
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan di bí yii m làá dū-bi kí yāŋkì tɔb kí kɔ̄fì, bibaatiibi nì mbiyaamu dicilpu. Maa làá tàan̄ báà ubɔ. Maa làá dàkà kulaŋŋaŋfitiiuaaa, kaa làá sɔ̄ isaa mun. Tiba nì tiba kaa làá cúú-mi ḿ taa nàan̄-bi.>» Ti-Dindaan bíi kpáafí u-nibul

english_verse: People of Judah, don't be too proud to listen to what the Lord has said.
translation_verse: Pīlifìmaan, kpòom̄maan ni-tafal, taa nín̄ sámaan bilambidambi. Ti-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ.

english_verse: You hope for light, but God is sending darkness. Evening shadows already deepen in the hills. So return to God and confess your sins to him before you trip and fall.
translation_verse: Tīīmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tinyool kí wàatī ní dibɔmbɔndi wiiŋŋu ń nín bàń, án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa láa gbéetí ajoon ŋin pu kunyeeu mɔ́ee. Ni bàà kā ki cí ŋwalifi dee, ama ní u dūu kpántì ŋkúm bɔmbɔndi, ki dūu kpántì ditagbambɔndi.

english_verse: If you are too proud to listen, I will weep alone. Tears will stream from my eyes when the Lord's people are taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Ni yaa kaa pílifì tibɔkpaafikaal nee, m làá nīn sūǹ dibalin ni-lambil pu. Nnyinnyim làá gbí m-nimbiliŋ kí nīn bàtifī, kun puee bi cúú ti-Dindaan picaŋkpuŋku ki cūnnì kuyuŋu.

english_verse: The Lord told me to tell you that your king and his mother must surrender their thrones and remove their crowns.
translation_verse: Tùkù ubɔti nì u-na yii: «Kàl̄maan kitiŋ, di sá ni-beefuunyaaŋki nyáń ni-yil pu ki lítì kitiŋ.

english_verse: The cities in the Southern Desert are surrounded; no one can get in or out. Everyone in Judah will be taken away.
translation_verse: Bi pīiǹ Neegeeb timmu punyɔmmu, ubɔ kaa ti pìitī-mu. Bi cúú Juuda yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu, bi-kɔkɔ búntì ubɔ kaa kíǹ. Jeerusaleem tiŋki fá ki-nyooti

english_verse: Jerusalem, you were so proud of ruling the people of Judah. But where are they now? Look north, and you will see your enemies approaching.
translation_verse: Wáaǹ kí kpèè bin nyánní ŋgan pú ki dòońee. Kupicaŋkpuŋu kun m nìn kpāaǹ-see bí la? Apibil ŋin nìn tìì-si tinyoolee bí la?

english_verse: You once trusted them to help, but now I'll let them rule you. What do you say about that? You will be in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: A yāntì biba kpántì a-bɔɔbi. An nib gbanti yaa láa yíkì ki bíi jáà nì si kí jī a-pu dinyandee, a làá dāá lì yii ba dee? A làá dāá jī falaa kii unimpu di kāl̀ imatiŋween puee.

english_verse: Do you know why your clothes were torn off and you were abused? It was because of your terrible sins.
translation_verse: Niinee, a làá dāá bàlifì yii: <Ba di yì-tì ní nnaabu nee bāań-mi míǹ?> Too, bi yaa láa kóoǹ a-wɔndoou, ki bíi ŋáań-si tipɔmbɔtee, an sá a-kpitii nín wīikée pu.

english_verse: Can you ever change and do what's right? Can people change the color of their skin, or can a leopard remove its spots? If so, then maybe you can change and learn to do right.
translation_verse: «Unibɔn ŋūǹ kí kpántí u-wuŋgbaŋŋuɔɔɔ? Ugbii ŋūǹ kí pítí u-tàmaaa? Míǹ mbaantiim ní nimbi bin mántiǹ ikpiti diŋálee, naa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiŋan.

english_verse: I will scatter you, just as the desert wind blows husks from grain tossed in the air.
translation_verse: M làá jà-ni kí yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu kii kuteeun buŋku nín yòontí timool puee ní.»

english_verse: I won't change my mind. I, the Lord, have spoken. You rejected me and worshiped false gods. *
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Jeerusaleem, tin dɔ̄ ki cí-see dee. Dijandi din m kpáafì ki yóoǹ-see dee. Di sá yii a súntì man pu, ní ki dū a-mákal ki páaǹ awaa pu.

english_verse: You were married to me, but you were unfaithful. You even became a prostitute by worshiping disgusting gods on hilltops and in fields.
translation_verse: An puee ma mun làá kóoǹ a-wɔndoou kí cáá sāā a-nimbiin pu, ní bí wāl̀ a-cooi.

english_verse: So I'll rip off your clothes and leave you naked and ashamed for everyone to see. You are doomed! Will you ever be worthy to worship me again?
translation_verse: Yéēee! A-laakpaati nì a-mɔŋŋu biilii nì a-laakpaatuuŋŋi ŋin kɔ̄ntí-si icoo na! M ká a-gbantammu pu nì a-satin a-waaŋi ŋin sá ntimbiil wantee. Ba naabuŋu ŋúǹ bulifi dee, Jeerusaleem, aa là kí ŋá a-ba circir. Án làá nīn bí míǹ kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní?»

english_verse: Rulers send their servants to the storage pits for water. But there's none to be found; they return in despair with their jars still empty.
translation_verse: Akpambal tú bi-tɔntɔnliibi bí cùú nyàabìń nnyim. Bi bàn̄ dinyimbɔbilinee, nnyim fóotì. Bi fātìi gítìń nì abɔkulim. Bi-wunti yɔ̄tì kunimbaau kɔ́-bi ní bi kíǹ ki tīī bi-yil.

english_verse: There has been no rain, and farmers feel sick as they watch cracks appear in the dry ground.
translation_verse: Utaa nín yúl̀ee puee, kitiŋ fáá iwèeń. Niinee bikpaabi wunti yɔ̄tì, bi-yil kíǹ ki tīī.

english_verse: A deer gives birth in a field, then abandons her newborn fawn and leaves in search of grass.
translation_verse: Kipeewuŋ gba màl̄ tisatin ki dū ki-biki ki fá, kun puee timool kaa ti bí.

english_verse: Wild donkeys go blind from starvation. So they stand on barren hilltops and sniff the air, hoping to smell green grass. The Lord's People Pray
translation_verse: Kumooun mammu tɔ́kɔ́ ajoon pu ki tíkì kubuŋu kii sinsiŋkubee. Mu nyàab̄ timool mu-nimbiliŋ tin kpáàa lóoĺ, ama ní muaa ká báà tiba.» Isirayeel nibul

english_verse: We rejected you and did evil, so we deserve to be punished. But if you rescue us, Lord, everyone will see how great you are.
translation_verse: «Báà ti-kpitii yaa bíi kɔ́kɔĺ-ti, ti-Dindaan, a-yindi puee, ŋá tiba kí tīī-ti. Tiŋman ti nyáń a-boon, ti yīntiǹ-si.

english_verse: You're our only hope; you alone can save us now. You help us one day, but you're gone the next.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, sii un pu Isirayeel yab mákée, a nìn fīī-bi dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu poon. Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, a sá kii unicaanee ní kitiŋ nee poon, a lì kii usaŋkinli nín dɔ́miń kí dòon̄ kunyabambaantiiu kutaa ń wúntí ú nìkēe ní.

english_verse: Did this disaster take you by surprise? Are you a warrior with your hands tied? You have chosen us, and your temple is here. Don't abandon us! The Lord's Answer
translation_verse: Ba pu ní a bí kii unil un wunti kpíìyee, a lì kii ubaatandaan un kaa ti ŋūǹ kí fīī bin kíǹee? Ama ní a bí ti-kansikin ti-Dindaan, bi dū-ti ki sú-si ní, taa dū-ti kí fá.» *

english_verse: My people, you love to wander away; you don't even try to stay close to me. So now I will reject you and punish you for your sins. I, the Lord, have spoken. Lying Prophets
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ dinibul nee pu tiŋyee: «Tiŋman, bi néeń ki sáń ki póotí an kɔkɔ kii bi nín là puee.» Ama tíǹ kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaan. Kɔŋkɔnnee u làá téetí bi-yìntitam nì bi-kpitii pu ní kí dáaĺ bi-tafal.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Jeremiah, don't ask me to help these people.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Á taa gbàam̀ dinibul nee yab pu, á taa mèè kí nyàab̀ bi-ŋanti.

english_verse: They may even go without eating and offer sacrifices to please me and to give thanks. But when they cry out for my help, I won't listen, and I won't accept their sacrifices. Instead, I'll send war, starvation, and disease to wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Báà bi yaa bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ki mēē-mi, maa làá pīlifiǹ-bi. Báà bi yaa cáań-mi bisaraawɔkaabi nì saraabi bin kíǹee, maa làá fōō. Ama m làá kpɔ̀-bi kujaaun ní kí yàntī ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi.»

english_verse: I replied, “The other prophets keep telling everyone that you won't send starvation or war, and that you're going to give us peace.”
translation_verse: Ní m kíí yii: «Too, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, bibɔnaatiliibi bí-bi yii: <Naa làá ká kujaauaaa, ŋkùm mun kaa làá jēetí ni-pu, ama Unimbɔti làá tīī-ni mbaamɔn gbansɔŋfiŋu mpaan nee pu.>»

english_verse: The Lord answered: They claim to speak for me, but they're lying! I didn't even speak to them, much less choose them to be my prophets. Their messages come from worthless dreams, useless fortunetelling, and their own imaginations.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Tin bibɔnaatiliibi gbanti sòoǹ m-yindi puee sá nnyimɔn ní. Maa tú-bi, kaa tīī-bi mara ubɔ, kaa tí sòon̄ nì bi tiba. Bi-leedakaŋ sá tinyimɔmbɔti, ní tin bi sòoǹee kaa bí tiban. Bíǹ bi-ba di pée kāl̀ ki náań tinyimɔmbɔti gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Those lying prophets say there will be peace and plenty of food. But I say that those same prophets will die from war and hunger.
translation_verse: An puee man ni-Dindaan nín cáá tin kí sòoǹ bibɔnaatiliibi gbanti pu puee sèé: <Maa tú-bi, ama ní bi sòoǹ m-yindi pu yii kujaau àá ŋkùm kaa làá jēetí kitiŋ nee pu. Too, kujaau nì ŋkùm di làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí bi-kɔkɔ.

english_verse: And everyone who listens to them will be killed, just as they deserve. Their dead bodies will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem, because their families will also be dead, and no one will be left to bury them.
translation_verse: Ní kujaau nì ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀ binib bin bi nāatì tinyimɔmbɔti ki tīīyee kí bíĺ Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu an kɔkɔ fìlfil. Ubɔ dāa kpá kí síb́ bi nì bi-nimpoobi nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib. M làá yàntī ikpiti in bi ŋée ń gítí bi-pu.

english_verse: Jeremiah, go and tell the people how you feel about all this. So I told them: “Tears will flood my eyes both day and night, because my nation suffers from a deadly wound.
translation_verse: «Á tùkù-bi tibɔti nee yii: «Nnyinnyim ń nyā m-nimbiliŋ kí nīn bàtifī kí taa gbèen̄ ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu! Di sá yii asaluukpaan kɔ́ m-nibul. Tiweendi tin di fōōyee kaa cáá dicáaǹdi.

english_verse: In the fields I see the bodies of those killed in battle. And in the towns I see crowds dying of hunger. But the prophets and priests go about their business, without understanding what has happened.” Jeremiah Prays to the Lord
translation_verse: M yaa nyáń ki cá kusaauee, m kāntí binib bin bi kūū kujaaunee dɔ̄ dɔ̄. M yaa tí nín kóò kitiŋinaaa, m tí kāntí bin ŋkùm kūū kūūyee. Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì bisaraaŋaliibi tú ki yìiǹ kitiŋee ni, baa bíi gbìl̀ tin bíi jītée taapu.» Isirayeel nibul

english_verse: Have you rejected Judah, Lord? Do you hate Jerusalem? Why did you strike down Judah with a fatal wound? We had hoped for peace and a time of healing, but all we got was terror.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan, a lafun dū Juuda yab ki fá níii? A núutiǹ Siiyɔn yab níii? Ba pu ní a ŋáań-ti tiweendi tin ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹee ní? Ti bàà kā ki cí ŋgbansɔŋfi, ama ní tiwammɔntiil tiba kaa bíi dòoń. Ti bàà kā ki cí kí ká dicáaǹdi, ama ní dinyoondi bāań.

english_verse: We and our ancestors are guilty of rebelling against you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, ti nyí ti nín ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee. Ti béè mun yii ti-naanjab yīntiǹ-si. Tiŋman, ti baasii yīntiǹ-si ní.

english_verse: If you save us, it will show how great you are. Don't let our enemies disgrace your temple, your beautiful throne. Don't forget that you promised to rescue us.
translation_verse: A-yindi puee, taa kpèè kí sìŋkīǹ a-beejal din cáá tinyoolee, taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī-dì. Taa súntí mpèé ŋun a nìn ŋá nì tee pu, taa kpìtī-ŋu.

english_verse: Idols can't send rain, and showers don't fall by themselves. Only you control the rain, so we put our trust in you, the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Atimbun ŋin kíǹee waaŋi kansikinee, diba ŋūǹ kí yàntī utaa ń nàaa? Kutagbɔŋu ku-ba di yàntī utaa nàaa? An kaa sá sii ti-Dindaanaaa? Ti-Dindaan, sii pu ní timbi máká, di sá yii sii di ŋáań tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: The Lord said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel were here, praying with you, I wouldn't change my mind. So send the people of Judah away.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Báà gba Mooyiisi nì Samiyeel yaa gbāam̀-mi dinibul nee yab pu, maa làá pée sɔ̄ bi-saai. Jà-bi kí nyāntí bí búntí kí wàatī-mi.

english_verse: And when they ask where they are going, tell them that I, the Lord, have said: Some of you are going to die of horrible diseases. Others are going to die in war or from starvation. The rest will be led away to a foreign country.
translation_verse: Ní bi yaa bālifì-si yii: <La ní ti làá cù ní?> Á kíí-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. «Bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ un sá bìlbil kúm yɔuee! Un máaǹ kí kpú kujaaunee ń kpú kujaaun! Ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀ un sá ŋkùm yɔuee! Ní un sá kuyuŋun yɔuee ń búntí kuyuŋu!»

english_verse: I will punish you in four different ways: You will be killed in war and your bodies dragged off by dogs, your flesh will be eaten by birds, and your bones will be chewed on by wild animals.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá jáǹ-bi minaa pu ní: kitàataajiki làá kpɔ̀-bi, ní iboo ń fù-bi kí cùnnì ndan, ní kaajiikub ń jī-bi ní sinsiŋkub ń ŋmɔ́ kí tɔ̀ntī-bi.

english_verse: This punishment will happen because of the horrible things your King Manasseh did. And you will be disgusting to all nations on earth.
translation_verse: Mimmee, kitiŋ pu beeŋi kɔkɔ yaa ká-bee, bi làá kɔ́ dinyoondin. Kun pu m làá ŋá mimmee di sá Eeseekiyaasi jipɔɔn Manasee, Juuda yab bɔtiu nín ŋáaǹ atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee.» Ti-Dindaan gīī kí sɔ̄ isaa

english_verse: People of Jerusalem, who will feel sorry for you? Will anyone bother to ask if you are well?
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Jeerusaleem, ŋma di làá gíti sɔ̄ a-saai? Ŋma di làá sɔ̄ a-pu? Ŋma di làá dūú páb́ u-ba kí bàlifì kí kpèè tin poon a bée?»

english_verse: My people, you abandoned me and walked away. I am tired of showing mercy; that's why I'll destroy you
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Sii di dū-mi ki fá, ní ki fātì a-boon ki tīī-mi. An pu ní ma mun jáń nì si ki nāaǹ-si. Di sá yii m gīī kí nīn sūǹ a-saai.

english_verse: by scattering you like straw blown by the wind. I will punish you with sorrow and death, because you refuse to change your ways.
translation_verse: Kitiŋee timmu kɔkɔ poonee, m yōoǹ ndɔ ŋun m cáa gbáà tijimpinee ki gbáń ki yāaǹ-bi. M nāaǹ-bi ki yāntì baa ti cáá mbiyaamu, ama ní baa kpántì bi-bimbim.

english_verse: There will be more widows in Judah than grains of sand on a beach. A surprise attack at noon! And the mothers in Jerusalem mourn for their children.
translation_verse: M yāntì bikpiipoobi wíiǹ ki jítiǹ tiŋku gbandi bul. M cáań nnaabu ki tɔ́ unipɔɔn un sá ujanjalee na pu kuwiŋkaŋu pu. Dibɔbil pu niinee ní m yāntì dinyooŋkpaandi jéetì u-pu.

english_verse: A mother is in deep despair and struggles for breath. Her daylight has turned to darkness— she has suffered the loss of her seven sons. I will kill anyone who survives. I, the Lord, have spoken. Jeremiah Complains
translation_verse: Unimpu un nìn cáá jipɔmbi bilulee kaa ti bí tiban. U fìkī ki dɔ̄. Úǹ wìiŋ́ŋu jéetì kuwiŋkaŋu pu. Icoo cúú-u, u fá u-jilmau. Bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee, m làá yàntī bí kpú kujaaun bi-nannanliibi nimbiin.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Yeereemii bíi yáliŋkí, Unimbɔti dàkā-u u-tundi Yeereemii

english_verse: I wish I had never been born! I'm always in trouble with everyone in Judah. I never lend or borrow money, but everyone curses me just the same.
translation_verse: M-na, mbusu kɔ́-mi a nín màl̄-mee pu! Kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ poonee, binib jáà nì mi ní kaa là kí wāl̀-mi. Ma mun kaa pīnnì ubɔ animbil, kaa tí cūtì ubɔ mun cee ki pīnnì animbil. Ama ní báà ŋma tòó-mi mbusu.

english_verse: Then the Lord replied, “I promise to protect you, and when disaster comes, even your enemies will beg you for help.” The Enemy Cannot Be Defeated The Lord told me to say:
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii: «M pūtì yii m làá fīī-si kí kɔ́ǹ-si nnaamin. Nnaabu nì dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋuee, m làá yàntī a-nannanliibi ń dāá gbàan̄ a-nimbiin.

english_verse: People of Judah, just as you can't break iron mixed with bronze, you can't defeat the enemies that will attack from the north.
translation_verse: Ubɔ ŋūǹ kí kóoĺ tikútaaa, tikúti tin nyánní ŋgan púee nì tasa kútaaa?» ti-Dindaan

english_verse: I will give them everything you own, because you have sinned everywhere in your country.
translation_verse: «Juuda yab, m làá yàntī bí fūkul̀ ni-gaajawanti nì ni-gaajati, ní an kaa cáá yii ubɔ làá téeǹ-ni. Ikpiti in kɔkɔ ni ŋá ni-tiŋki kɔkɔnee paati dee.

english_verse: My anger is a fire that cannot be put out, so I will make you slaves of your enemies in a foreign land. Jeremiah Complains Again
translation_verse: M làá yàntī ní kpántí ni-nannanliibi yumbui kitiŋ kin a nyée poon. Di sá yii m-ŋuul sēē ŋŋmi ŋun di làá wà-see.» Yeereemii

english_verse: You can see how I suffer insult after insult, all because of you, Lord. Don't be so patient with my enemies; take revenge on them before they kill me.
translation_verse: Sii ti-Dindaan nyí tikɔkɔ! Dàkafì m-pu kí téetí m-pu. Tɔ̀ bin kā m-puee ipɔntoon. Kimɔtii kin a cáá bi-puee puee, á taa yàntī ḿ jī falaa. Béé yii sii pu ní man bíi jīǹ takaasi.

english_verse: When you spoke to me, I was glad to obey, because I belong to you, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: M yaa nìn ká a-nyɔɔbundee, m dù-dì kí ŋmɔ́ ní kí náĺ. Di nìn tìì-mi mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi ní. Di sá yii bi dū-mi ki sú sii m-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan ní.

english_verse: I don't go to parties and have a good time. Instead, I keep to myself, because you have filled me with your anger.
translation_verse: Maa kāl̀ bibeeliliibi kansikin ki kɔ̄ntì m-nimbiliŋ. Ama a ŋá-mi mpɔn m kākatì m-baba, di sá yii a yāntì m díkí a-ŋuul ki gbí.

english_verse: I am badly injured and in constant pain. Are you going to disappoint me, like a stream that goes dry in the heat of summer? The Lord Replies
translation_verse: Ba pu ní m-falaau kaa cáá dikúntil ní? Ba pu ní m-buuŋŋu kaa kúù ki kpántì taagbunjaanjaan ní? Ibaamɔn, a kpántì m-cee kii mbun ŋun kíiĺ binib, baa ŋūǹ kí nīn máká ŋu-pu yii ŋu cáá nnyimaaa, ŋuaa cááyee ní.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me: Stop talking like a fool! If you turn back to me and speak my message, I will let you be my prophet once again. I hope the people of Judah will accept what you say. But you can ignore their threats, *
translation_verse: Too, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. «A yaa fātìi gítìń m-cee, m làá fàtīí fōō-si á nīn bí m-tundin ní á dāá yūĺ m-nimbiin. A yaa ŋūǹ kí lì tibɔti tin cáá kudapɔɔuee kí yàntī tibɔfanee, m làá fàtīí dū-si kí kpántí kii m-nyɔkɔee. An sá Juuda yab nín fàtīí gítiń a-cee, an kaa sá sii di làá fàtīí gítí bi-cee.

english_verse: I will be there to rescue you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M làá fīī-si kí nyāntí bitɔŋfitiibi ŋaan, m làá fōō-si bin dàkà tipɔmbɔtee ŋaan kí líí.»

english_verse: The Lord said to me:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti nee yii:

english_verse: Jeremiah, don't get married and have children—Judah is no place to raise a family.
translation_verse: «Á taa cáá unimpu, kí taa màal̀ mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu kitiŋ nee poon.

english_verse: I'll tell you what's going to happen to children and their parents here.
translation_verse: Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu mun bi làá màal̀ kitiŋ nee poonee, nì bibinaatiibi nì bibaatiibi bin làá màal̀-muee puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: They will die of horrible diseases and of war and starvation. No one will give them a funeral or bury them, and their bodies will be food for the birds and wild animals. And what's left will lie on the ground like manure.
translation_verse: Tigbaŋweeŋkpiil di làá kpɔ̀-bi. Ubɔ kaa làá sɔ̄ bi-kpool, ní ubɔ mun kaa dāa bí kí síb́-bi. Bi làá dāá dòon̄ kitiŋ kí sūū ní kí dāá kpántí ntiŋkpam. Kujaaun ní bi làá kpú àá ŋkùm di làá kpɔ̀-bi. Kaajiikub nì sinsiŋkub di làá ŋmɔ́ bi-nanti.»

english_verse: When someone dies, don't visit the family or show any sorrow. I will no longer love or bless or have any pity on the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti bí-mi yii: «Á taa kɔ́ dicindi din poon ní binib kpáfì ki kā dikpoolee, kí taa cù dikpool. Á taa ŋá ubɔ fɔ̀ɔ́, di sá yii m cúú m-saasɔl nì m-ŋanti nì m-poommɔŋŋu ki fōō dinibul nee cee. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Rich and poor alike will die and be left unburied. No one will mourn and show their sorrow by cutting themselves or shaving their heads.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ nee poonee, binikpaambi nì ŋwaamu làá kpú. Ubɔ kaa làá síb́-bi. Ubɔ kaa làá cāfì u-wunti kí dàkà kunimbaau ní kaa nín kōol̀ diyibaakpandi.

english_verse: No one will bring food and wine to help comfort those who are mourning the death of their father or mother.
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa làá mɔ̄ǹ bukpɔsaa kí cùnnì dikpool kí ŋméeǹ-bi. Ubɔ mun kaa làá dā un baa kpíì àá u-na kpíìyee ndaam.

english_verse: Don't even set foot in a house where there is eating and drinking and celebrating.
translation_verse: «Taa kɔ́ kudicaŋu kun poon bi bíi jīǹ jiŋaalee. Taa kàl̄ si nì bi ń jī kí nyɔ̀.

english_verse: Warn the people of Judah that I, the Lord All-Powerful, will put an end to all their parties and wedding celebrations.
translation_verse: Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ni-maŋfal wiiŋyi poon nì ni-nimbilaaliyin ní m làá kúntí kitiŋ nee pu ni-jiŋaalib gbiiliŋ nì ni-pɔɔpindi faalii nì animpucaŋgbiil.>

english_verse: They will ask, “Why has the Lord our God threatened us with so many disasters? Have we done something wrong or sinned against him?”
translation_verse: «A yaa láa dū tibɔti nee ki tùkū dinibul nee yab ní bi yaa láa bālifì-si yii: <Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan cáań nnaabu nee ki tɔ́ ti-pu? Ba ní ti ŋá ki yīntì ní? Ba kpitii ní ti baasii ŋá ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ní?>

english_verse: Then tell them I have said: People of Judah, your ancestors turned away from me; they rejected my laws and teachings and started worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Á dāá kíí-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kun pu m ŋá mimmee di sá yii ni-naanjab nìn dū-mi ki fá ki cūtìi nóó awaa ki tōotì-ŋi ní ki gbāaǹ ŋi-taapu. Mamee, bi dū-mi ki fá ní kaa ŋúb́ m-marab.

english_verse: And you have done even worse! You are stubborn, and instead of obeying me, you do whatever evil comes to your mind.
translation_verse: Nimbee, ni-kpitii gíti nyāŋkì nì ni-naanjab yai. Báà ŋma nóó u-landɔkɔkpitii kaa pílifiǹ-mi.

english_verse: So I will throw you into a land that you and your ancestors know nothing about, a place where you will have to worship other gods both day and night. And I won't feel the least bit sorry for you.
translation_verse: M làá jà-ni kí nyāntí kitiŋ nee poon kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin poon ni nì ni-naanjab kaa nyí ki kée. Niinee, ni làá ŋmā kí nīn tòotī awaa ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Di sá yii maa ti làá dàkà-ni m-laŋŋaŋfitiiku.>» Ti-Dindaan fātìi gíiǹní bin u nìn jìn̄ee bi-tiŋki pu

english_verse: A time will come when you will again worship me. But you will no longer call me the Living Lord who rescued Israel from Egypt.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii: «Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń baa làá dāá gíti lì yii: <M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin ki nyántìń Isirayeel yab kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee!>,

english_verse: Instead, you will call me the Living Lord who rescued you from that country in the north and from the other countries where I had forced you to go. Someday I will bring you back to this land that I gave your ancestors.
translation_verse: ama bi làá dāá lì yii: <nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin, ki nyántìń Isirayeel yab kitiŋ kin bí ŋgan púee nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon u nìn jìn̄-bi ki kɔ́ǹee.> Tiŋman m làá fàtīí gíiǹní-bi kitiŋ kin m nìn dūu tīī bi-naanjabee poon.» Unimbɔti làá fàtīí fōō bin jíń dibɔkpilee

english_verse: But for now, I am sending enemies who will catch you like fish and hunt you down like wild animals in the hills and the caves.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá tɔ̄ bijɔncuuliibi tikpil bí cùú cúuń-bi. Míǹ boonee ní ḿ tɔ̄ bikpambi kupaau bí cù ajoon kɔkɔ pu nì ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ pu nì itakpalɔkɔn kí kpāŋkì-bi.

english_verse: I can see everything you are doing, even if you try to hide your sins from me.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m wāĺ tin kɔkɔ bi ŋáańee. Bi-tuuŋŋi báà dibaba kaa bál̀-mi, ní tiba kaa lìkī bi-kpitii m-nimbiin.

english_verse: I will punish you double for your sins, because you have polluted my own land. You have filled it with lifeless idols that remind me of dead bodies. The Lord Gives Strength I prayed to the Lord:
translation_verse: M làá yàntī bí pà bi-kpitii paati mili pu nì bi-yìntitam. Di sá yii bi dū bi-waaŋi ŋin sá ntimbiil wanti kaa cáá dimaŋfalee ki kɔ́ǹ m-tiŋki tijɔkɔndi. Bi dū bi-waaŋi ŋin m-nimbil kaa là kí wāl̀ee ki gbéeǹ m-tiŋki kin sá m-gaajawantee.» Báà ŋma béè Unimbɔti un sá tiŋman pu yɔuee

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who gives me strength and protects me like a fortress when I am in trouble. People will come to you from distant nations and say, “Our ancestors worshiped false and useless gods,
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, sii di sá man pɔŋŋu nì m-balilaŋki, dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋuee, sii ní m sáń ki kóò. Atimbun làá nyānní kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ kí dāan̄. Bi làá dāá lì yii: «Difakal din ti-naanjab fōōyee di sá tinyimɔmbɔti, tiwan tin kaa bí tiban kaa kèetēe.

english_verse: worthless idols made by human hands.”
translation_verse: Unil ŋūǹ kí mɔ́ɔ́ inimbɔtaaa? Tin bi māāyee kaa sá inimbɔti.»

english_verse: Then the Lord replied, “That's why I will teach them about my power, and they will know that I truly am the Lord.”
translation_verse: «Too, min bí nee m làá dàkà-bi m-kpabil nì m-pɔŋŋu. Niinee bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_verse: People of Judah, your sins cannot be erased. They are written on your hearts like words chiseled in stone or carved on the corners of your altars. *
translation_verse: «Juuda yab kpitiiyee, bi dū kigaai ní ki cáká ki ŋmàn̄, àá ataŋkpanyaan ní bi dūu ŋmàn̄-i. Bi ŋmàn̄-i ki ŋá bi-pɔbiliŋin, ní ki ŋmàn̄-i ki nákáǹ nsaraafan kpiŋŋi pu.

english_verse: One generation after another has set up pagan altars and worshiped the goddess Asherah everywhere in your country— on hills and mountains, and under large trees.
translation_verse: Kii bi nín dàkafī bi-jipɔmbi pu puee, míǹ ní bi dàkafī bi-saraafaŋyi nì bi-windɔi nì isufi in cáá tifaasɔn ki bí ŋgbantamu puee pu.

english_verse: You will lose the land that I gave you, and I will make you slaves in a foreign country, because you have made my anger blaze up like a fire that won't stop burning. Trust the Lord
translation_verse: Ni làá yīkì kí dū kitiŋ kin m nìn tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe kí fá. M làá yàntī ní kpántí ni-nannanliibi yumbui kitiŋ kin naa nyée poon. Di sá yii ni tūū m-ŋuul ŋmiŋu, ní ŋu làá nīn pée wù míǹ ní ki cá jaanjaan. Ibaamɔn wundi nì inyimɔn wundi

english_verse: I, the Lord, have put a curse on those who turn from me and trust in human strength.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «An sá mbusu ní ki tīī unil un máká nisaal pu, ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi nisaaleen cee, ní ki fàtī u-boon ki tìì ti-Dindaanee.»

english_verse: But I will bless those who trust me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Ama unil un di máká man pu ki fōō-mi ki kíí nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔee, man u-Dindaan làá bìin̄ u-pu.

english_verse: They will be like trees growing beside a stream— trees with roots that reach down to the water, and with leaves that are always green. They bear fruit every year and are never worried by a lack of rain.
translation_verse: Udaan bí kii busubu bun yú mbun caŋin, bu-nyaaŋyi lālim̀ ki kɔ́ mbunee ní. Kutuntuŋu yuntiŋuee, buaa fàŋkí tiba, ní bu-faati pée sɔ̀m̀ ŋma. Báà ŋweel yaa yúl̀ dibimmɔndi, bu pée lòoǹ abil ní kaa gbèentí.

english_verse: You people of Judah are so deceitful that you even fool yourselves, and you can't change.
translation_verse: Unil pɔbil ŋmàtíǹ ki jítiǹ tikɔkɔ! Ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ-dì. Ubɔ mun kaa ŋūǹ kí béé-dì.

english_verse: But I know your deeds and your thoughts, and I will make sure you get what you deserve.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaanee, m wāĺ tin kā unil pɔbil poon poon kábuee, ní ki nyí u-landɔkɔi kɔkɔ nín sá puee. An pu ní m ŋūǹ kí pà báà ŋma bimbim nì u-tuuŋŋi paati.

english_verse: You cheated others, but everything you gained will fly away, like birds hatched from stolen eggs. Then you will discover what fools you are. Jeremiah Prays to the Lord
translation_verse: Kii ujikpal nín nākantí ajin ŋin waa tɔ́ee puee, míǹ ní unil un dī isaŋkpiti pu ki ká tigaajatee bí. U-maŋfal wiiŋyi kansikin nì kansikinee ní u-gaajati ń wāŋkì, ní ú dūú kpántí kii kinaatuuyee.» Ti-Dindaan baba di sá dimaŋfal nyeel

english_verse: Our Lord, your temple is a glorious throne that has stood on a mountain from the beginning.
translation_verse: Tinyool beejal din tɔ́kɔ́ yilpu doooo ŋkilkaaminee, míǹ ní ti-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu bí.

english_verse: You are a spring of water giving Israel life and hope. But if the people reject what you have told me, they will be swept away like words written in dust.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, sii un pu Isirayeel mákée, icoo ń cúú bin kɔkɔ dū-si ki fée! Bin kɔkɔ fātì bi-boon ki tīī-see, bí nīn bí kii ayin ŋin bi ŋmàn̄ ntaminee. Di sá yii bi dū sii ti-Dindaan un sá dimaŋfal nyimbuliŋuee ki fá. Yeereemii bíi mèé ti-Dindaan

english_verse: You, Lord, are the one I praise. So heal me and rescue me! Then I will be completely well and perfectly safe.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, cáaǹ-mi ní ḿ ká dicáaǹdi, fīī-mi ní ḿ ká difiil. Di sá yii sii di sá m-nyɔŋkii.

english_verse: The people of Judah say to me, “Jeremiah, you claimed to tell us what the Lord has said. So why hasn't it come true?”
translation_verse: Bi lì-mi yii: «Ti-Dindaan bɔti tin u sòon̄ee bí la? Tibɔti gbanti ń ŋá míǹ tí kpèèyaa!»

english_verse: Our Lord, you chose me to care for your people, and that's what I have done. You know everything I have said, and I have never once asked you to punish them.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, man di kaa páb́-si á cáań nnaabu. Maa tí mēē kí ká nnaabu wiiŋŋu, sii a-ba nyí míǹ. Tin m sòon̄ee, a-nimbiin ní m sòon̄-tì.

english_verse: I trust you for protection in times of trouble, so don't frighten me.
translation_verse: Taa kpántí dinyoondi kí tīī-mi, sii ní m sáń ki kóò dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu.

english_verse: Keep me from failure and disgrace, but make my enemies fail and be disgraced. Send destruction to make their worst fears come true. Resting on the Sabbath
translation_verse: Icoo ń cúú bin sàantí-mee kí taa cúú man. Tifaandi ń cúú-bi, ama kí taa cúú man. Cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu, kí nàan̄-bi dúsi dusi. Ti-Dindaan wiŋŋuŋfikaaŋu bɔti

english_verse: The Lord said: Jeremiah, stand at each city gate in Jerusalem, including the one the king uses, and speak to him and everyone else. Tell them I have said: I am the Lord, so pay attention.
translation_verse: Á tùkù Juuda yab bɔtiibi nì Juuda yab kɔkɔ nì Jeerusaleem yab bin kɔkɔ dì mpunyɔmu gbantee yii: <Pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi.

english_verse: If you value your lives, don't do any work on the Sabbath. Don't carry anything through the city gates or through the door of your house, or anywhere else. Keep the Sabbath day sacred! I gave this command to your ancestors, but they were stubborn and refused to obey or to be corrected. But if you obey,
translation_verse: «<Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nimbee, ní pīlifiǹ-mi. Ní taa túń diwaŋgul ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal kí dī kitiŋ nee punyɔmmu kí kɔ́. Ní dū ŋwiin gbanti kí sú-mi kí taa tɔ̄ ditundi diba ŋwiin gbanti.

english_verse: then Judah and Jerusalem will always be ruled by kings from David's family. The king and his officials will ride through these gates on horses or in chariots, and the people of Judah and Jerusalem will be with them. There will always be people living in Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Niinee, bibɔtiibi nì abɔtibil bin kā Daafiidi beejal puee làá nīn kàal̀ itaamu nì tɔrɔkub pu kí nīn pée dì kitiŋ nee punyɔmmu pu ki kóò ki nyēē. Bi-kàliŋkpilib nì Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab làá nīn dì niin, ní binib ń nīn pée kóò kitiŋ nee ni kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: and others will come here from the nearby villages, from the towns of Judah and Benjamin, from the hill country and the foothills to the west, and from the Southern Desert. They will bring sacrifices to please me and to give me thanks, as well as offerings of grain and incense.
translation_verse: Binib làá nyānní Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem kpaanceetii nì Beenjameen tiŋkin nì Seefeelaa tiŋkin nì ajoon pu timmun nì Neegeeb. Bi làá dāá ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì saraabi biba mun nì tijimpin saraabi nì talaalutuukaa nì ijaam saraabi ti-Dindaan diikun.

english_verse: But if you keep on carrying things through the city gates on the Sabbath and keep treating it as any other day, I will set fire to these gates and burn down the whole city, including the fortresses.
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa kaa pílifiǹ-mi kaa dū ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ki sú-mi, ki túǹ diwaŋgul ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal ki dī Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu pu ki kɔ́ee, m làá tūū ki-punyɔmmu ŋŋmi. Ŋu làá wà Jeerusaleem beeciŋŋi, ní kaa làá kpú.>»

english_verse: The Lord told me,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti nee yii:

english_verse: “Jeremiah, go to the pottery shop, and when you get there, I will tell you what to say to the people.”
translation_verse: «Yīkìí sìntī uyɔɔmaati cee. Niin ní m làá sòoǹ nì si tin m cááyee.»

english_verse: I went there and saw the potter making clay pots on his pottery wheel.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m nín sìntī uyɔɔmaati cee. M bàn̄ee u bíi māā dibool kupiliŋu kun pu bi māā abookuŋkunee.

english_verse: And whenever the clay would not take the shape he wanted, he would change his mind and form it into some other shape.
translation_verse: Ama dibool din u nìn bíi māāyee kaa nìn kāl̀ kii iyunti iba án nín pée bàń uyɔɔmaati puee. Niinee ní u fātìi máń dibool diba din fáatiǹ-uee.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say:
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti nee yii:

english_verse: People of Israel, I, the Lord, have power over you, just as a potter has power over clay.
translation_verse: «Mimmee Isirayeel yab, maa ŋūǹ kí ŋá-ni kii uyɔɔmaati nee nín ŋá pueeee? Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ. Kii kuyɔkɔu nín kā uyɔɔmaati ŋaan puee, míǹ ní nimbi Isirayeel yab mun kā m-ŋaan.

english_verse: If I threaten to uproot and shatter an evil nation,
translation_verse: Iyunti ibee m sòoǹ yii m làá cóotí ditimbundi àá dibeel diba kí lábití-dì kí cìb̄ ní kí nàan̄-dì.

english_verse: and that nation turns from its evil, I will change my mind.
translation_verse: Ama ditimbundi gbanti yaa fá di-tuŋkpitiŋee, ma mun kpántí m-landɔkɔŋu ní kí taa ti ŋá-dì tin m bàà bɔ́ntì kí ŋá-dèe.

english_verse: If I promise to make a nation strong,
translation_verse: Iyunti ibee m tí sòoǹ ditimbundi àá dibeel diba pu yii bí fàtīí náań-dì kí mā-dì.

english_verse: but its people start disobeying me and doing evil, then I will change my mind and not help them at all.
translation_verse: Ama ditimbundi gbanti yab yaa kaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ ní ki bíi ŋáań min maa lèe, m kpántí m-landɔkɔŋu ní kí taa ti ŋá-bi tiŋan tin m bàà bɔ́ntì kí ŋá-bee.

english_verse: So listen to me, people of Judah and Jerusalem! I have decided to strike you with disaster, and I won't change my mind unless you stop sinning and start living right.
translation_verse: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, Yeereemii, á tùkù Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M bíi bɔ́ntí nnaabu kí tɔ̄ ni-pu, m bíi dàkafī min m làá ŋá-nee. An puee báà ŋma ń fá u-saŋkiŋkpitil. Ní ŋāŋkì ni-bítam nì ni-ŋáaǹtam.>»

english_verse: But I know you won't listen. You might as well answer, “We don't care what you say. We have made plans to sin, and we are going to be stubborn and do as we please!”
translation_verse: Ama bi làá lì-si yii: «Tin a sòoǹ nee sá fám ní! Ti nín pée lēē kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní ti làá ŋá, ti làá nóó ti-landɔkɔkpitii ní.» Isirayeel yab súntì bi-Dindaan pu

english_verse: So I, the Lord, command you to ask the nations, and find out if they have ever heard of such a horrible sin as what you have done.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii: «Ní bàlifìmaan atimbun ŋin kíǹee yab. Ni pée gbìl̄ tibɔti nee juti ki káaa?> Isirayeel un bí kii usapɔɔn un kaa nyí uninjee túń ntimbiil tuuŋŋi tikpil.

english_verse: The snow on Lebanon's mountains never melts away, and the streams there never run dry.
translation_verse: Ntaayim kaa bìintí Leebanɔn jooŋŋi taŋkpeeŋi puɔɔɔ? Ibun in nyim sìntī ajoon pu ki sɔ̀m̀ee ŋūǹ kí gbèen̄ kí taa ti pùub̀aaa? Aayee!

english_verse: But you, my people, have turned from me to burn incense to worthless idols. You have left the ancient road to follow an unknown path where you stumble over idols.
translation_verse: Ama man nibul súntì m-pu! Bi tòotī awaa ŋin kaa bí tibanee. Awaa gbanti di líikí-bi bi-saŋŋu poon. Ŋi yàntī bi féeń dooooyee saŋyi kí cùú nóó nsan ŋun baa cátèe.

english_verse: Your land will be ruined, and every passerby will look at it with horror and make insulting remarks.
translation_verse: M-nibul yāntì di-tiŋki kpántì ataŋkpakpuku, ki yàntī binib gbáà inimɔɔn biilii kaa gbèentí. An ŋáań bisanjitiliibi bitii, ní bi gbēentí bi-yiliŋ.

english_verse: When your enemies attack, I will scatter you like dust blown by an eastern wind. Then, on that day of disaster, I will turn my back on you. The Plot against Jeremiah
translation_verse: Binannanliibi yaa láa bāańee, m làá gbá kí yàaǹ m-nibul kii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki buŋku nín kpàá ntam ki féeń puee ní. Bi-nimbinaamandi dalee, án nín bàà sá ḿ fàtī m-nimbiin kí tīī-bee, m-boon ní m làá fàtī kí tīī-bi.» Binib bíi bɔ́ntí kí kpɔ̀ Yeereemii

english_verse: Some of the people said, “Let's get rid of Jeremiah! We will always have priests to teach us God's laws, as well as wise people to give us advice, and prophets to speak the Lord's messages. So, instead of listening to Jeremiah any longer, let's accuse him of a crime.” Jeremiah Prays about His Enemies
translation_verse: Binib biba bí yii: «Tí cùmaan kí bɔ́ntí kí jáǹ Yeereemii! An kaa sá ti lóò bisaraaŋaliibi bin làá dàkà-ti marabee àá biciŋfitiibi bin làá tīī-ti isaŋkee. Taa tí lóò bibɔnaatiliibi bin làá nàatī-ti Unimbɔti bɔtee. Tí cùmaan kí jáǹ-u kí sòoǹ kí bīil̀-u. Ti taa pīlifì tin u sòoǹee.»

english_verse: Please, Lord, answer my prayer. Make my enemies stop accusing me of evil.
translation_verse: Ama sii m-Dindaan, gíiǹní a-landɔkɔŋu m-cee, pīlifì tibɔti tin bin bíi kɔ́kɔĺ-mee sòoǹee.

english_verse: I tried to help them, but they are paying me back by digging a pit to trap me. I even begged you not to punish them.
translation_verse: Bi dù tikpitil kí pà tiŋan puɔɔɔ? Bi gbìn̄ mbòó ḿ jēetí poon. Ti-Dindaan, téetí yii m yúl̀ a-nimbiin ki gbāam̀-si binib nee pu yii á páatí a-ŋuul bi-pu.

english_verse: But now I am asking you to let their children starve or be killed in war. Let women lose their husbands and sons to disease and violence.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee yàntī ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀ bi-biyaamu, bí dū ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀-mu! Bi-nimpoobi ń kpántí biŋmaŋŋmantiibi nì bikpiipoobi! Bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ bi-calib! Bi-naacimpɔmbi ń kpúń kujaaun.

english_verse: These people have dug pits and set traps for me, Lord. Make them scream in fear when you send enemy troops to attack their homes.
translation_verse: A yaa láa dū binannanliibi ki tɔ́ bi-puee, bí dāá gbìl̄ ibiil pu bi-dumpui! Di sá yii bi gbìn̄ mbòó ḿ jēetí poon, ki píĺ-mi titalindi kí sàl̄-mi.

english_verse: You know they plan to kill me. So get angry and punish them! Don't ever forgive their terrible crimes.
translation_verse: Ama sii ti-Dindaanee, a nyí tin kɔkɔ bi bíi búkù m-pu ki là kí kpɔ̀-mee. Á taa dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi! Taa kpìtī bi-yìntitam a-nimbiin! Bí lítí a-nimbiin. A-ŋuul wiiŋŋu dalee, á dāá jáǹ-bi.

english_verse: The Lord said: Jeremiah, go to the pottery shop and buy a clay jar. Then take along some of the city officials and leading priests
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Cù uyɔɔmaati cee kí dā kulɔŋŋu. A yaa cée, á kpáaǹ bitindaŋkpilib biba nì bisaraaŋaliibi kpilib.

english_verse: and go to Hinnom Valley, just outside Potsherd Gate. Tell the people that I have said:
translation_verse: Á dī abɔkati punyɔkɔki kí cù Inɔɔm tantakalin. Niin ní á bāakì tibɔti tin m làá sòon̄ nì si nee.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and you kings of Judah and you people of Jerusalem had better pay attention. I am going to bring so much trouble on this valley that everyone who hears about it will be shocked.
translation_verse: Á dāá lì yii: <Juuda yab bɔtiibi nì Jeerusaleem yab, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá cáań nnaabukpaan ŋubɔ kí tɔ̄ mpaan nee pu. Bin yaa láa gbìl̄-tèe làá fàŋkì.

english_verse: The people of Judah stopped worshiping me and made this valley into a place of worship for Baal and other gods that have never helped them or their ancestors or their kings. And they have committed murder here, burning their young, innocent children as sacrifices to Baal. I have never even thought of telling you to do that.
translation_verse: Bi ŋātì iwaatootipaan kí nīn tòotī diwaal Baal. Niin ní bi cáǹ bi-jipɔmbi ki tòotī diwaal Baal ki wù ŋŋmi. Maa tīī-bi mara yii bí nīn ŋáań míǹ, maa sòon̄ an pu, kaa dākafì míǹ pu gba.>

english_verse: So watch out! Someday this place will no longer be called Topheth or Hinnom Valley. It will be called Slaughter Valley!
translation_verse: «An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: Ŋwiin ŋubɔ bí ki dòoń, baa làá dāá ti yíiń mpaan nee yii <Toofeeti> àá <Been-Inɔɔm tantakal>, ama bi làá dāá nīn yíì-ŋu yii <Dipɔ̀fil tantakal>.

english_verse: You people of Judah and Jerusalem may have big plans, but here in this valley I'll ruin those plans. I'll let your enemies kill you, and I'll tell the birds and wild animals to eat your dead bodies.
translation_verse: Mpaan nee puee, m làá dāá nàan̄ Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab nín bɔ́ntì kí ŋá tiŋyee. M làá yàntī bi-nannanliibi ń kpɔ̀-bi kujaaun. M làá dūú dī bin nyàab̀-bi ŋkúmee pu ní kí ŋá míǹ. M làá dū bi-nikpiliŋ kí tīī inoon ń jī ní ipeel ń ŋmɔ́.

english_verse: I will turn Jerusalem into a pile of rubble, and every passerby will be shocked and horrified and will make insulting remarks.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī kitiŋ nee ń kpántí adigbun ŋma kí yàntī báà ŋma ń nīn gbáà ki-pu ibiil. Bin kɔkɔ làá dāá jītí niinee làá dāá fàŋkì ní kí nīn búǹ ifoon tin bāań-kèe pu.

english_verse: And while your enemies are trying to break through your city walls to kill you, the food supply will run out. You will become so hungry that you will eat the flesh of your friends and even of your own children.
translation_verse: Binannanliibi bin là kí kúntí-bee làá dāá màntīí tū bi-tiŋki kí jáǹ-bi. Bi làá dāá nīn bí falaakpaan poon áli kí dāá ŋmɔ́ bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib nanti ní kí dāá ŋmɔ́ tɔb.

english_verse: Jeremiah, as soon as you have said this, smash the jar while the people are watching.
translation_verse: «Míǹ boonee ní á gbá kí wīī kulɔŋŋuee bin nóó-see nimbiin,

english_verse: Then tell them that I have also said: I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warn you that I will shatter Judah and Jerusalem just like this jar that is broken beyond repair. You will bury your dead here in Topheth, but so many of you will die that there won't be enough room.
translation_verse: ní kí tùkù-bi yii: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá wīī dinibul nee nì kitiŋ nee kii bi nín wìil̄ uyɔɔmaati lɔŋku puee ní. An kaa dāa gíti cáá diŋaŋkil. «Bi làá dāá síb́ anikpil Toofeeti tantakalin gba, kun puee mpaan kaa dāa gíti bí laaba bí síb́-ŋi.»

english_verse: I will make Jerusalem as unclean as Topheth, by filling the city with your dead bodies. I will do this because you and your kings have gone up to the roofs of your houses and burned incense to the stars in the sky, as though they were gods. And you have given sacrifices of wine to foreign gods. Jeremiah Speaks in the Temple Courtyard
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem diiŋŋi nì Juuda bɔtiibi diiŋŋi làá kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kii Toofeetee ní. Di sá yii bi tūutì talaalub adiin kɔkɔ yilpu bi nín bɔ̀b̄ puee ki tīī iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee, ki fá awaa ndaam.

english_verse: I went to Topheth, where I told the people what the Lord had said. Then I went to the temple courtyard and shouted to the people,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Yeereemii nyánní Toofeeti tantakalin, laakin ti-Dindaan nìn tú-u ú cù kí sòoǹ u-bɔtee. U nìn cūtì ki kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii cindin, ní ki bí samaa kɔkɔ yii:

english_verse: “Listen, everyone! Some time ago, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, warned you that he would bring disaster on Jerusalem and all nearby villages. But you were stubborn and refused to listen. Now the Lord is going to bring the disaster he promised.”
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá cáań nnaabu ŋun m nìn sòon̄ ki tɔ́ kitiŋ nee nì ki-timbilimmu kɔkɔ puee. Di sá yii kitiŋ nee nib yiliŋ pɔ̄ɔ̄, ní bi yíì kaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ.>»

english_verse: Pashhur son of Immer was a priest and the chief of temple security. He heard what I had said,
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil Pasuur, Imeer jipɔɔn, di nìn sá ti-Dindaan Diiku pilisikpiliu. U nìn gbìl̄ Yeereemii nín nāatì ti-Dindaan bɔti puee.

english_verse: and so he hit me. Then he had me arrested and put in chains at the Benjamin Gate in the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u fáá Yeereemii ntampa ní ki yāntì bi bóob́-u ki nákáǹ ndɔ Beenjameen punyɔkɔki yilpu pú yaka kin bi dì ki kóò ti-Dindaan Diikunee.

english_verse: The next day, when Pashhur let me go free, I told him that the Lord had said: No longer will I call you Pashhur. Instead, I will call you Afraid-of-Everything.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì Pasuur yāntì bi bútì Yeereemiiyee, ní Yeereemii bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan kaa ti làá yíiń-si Pasuur, ama u làá nīn kíǹ ki yíì-si yii: <Tifaandi bí an kɔkɔ pu.>

english_verse: You will be afraid, and you will bring fear to your friends as well. You will see enemies kill them in battle. Then I will let the king of Babylonia take everyone in Judah prisoner, killing some and dragging the rest away to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá kɔ́ǹ sii a-ba nì a-bɔɔbi tifaandi ní fàŋkì yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ. A-nimbilaaliyin ní bi-nannanliibi làá kpɔ̀-bi. M làá dū Juuda yab kɔkɔ kí líiǹ Babiloon yab bɔtiu. U làá cúú-bi kí cùnnì u-tiŋkin kuyuŋu ní kí kpɔ̀ bin kíǹee.

english_verse: Pashhur, you are guilty of telling lies and claiming they were messages from me. That's why I will let the Babylonians take you, your family, and your friends as prisoners to Babylonia, where you will all die and be buried. Jeremiah Complains to the Lord
translation_verse: Sii Pasuur nì a-dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔee, bi làá cúú-ni kí cùnnì kuyuŋu. A yaa láa bàn̄ Babiloon tiŋkinee, a làá kpú. Bi làá síb́-si niin, ki kpáaǹ a-bɔɔbi bin a nì bi nāatì tinyimɔmbɔtee kɔkɔ.>» Yeereemii timinsii

english_verse: You tricked me, Lord, and I was really fooled. You are stronger than I am, and you have defeated me. People never stop sneering and insulting me.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, a kíil̀-mi ní ma mun lafun fōō ki kíí míǹ. A cúú-mi mpɔn, ní ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-mi. Binib lāā-mi baabadal, báà ŋma bèel̄-mi ní.

english_verse: You have let me announce only injustice and death. Your message has brought me nothing but insults and trouble.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti kamaa m yaa làá sòoǹee, see ḿ téeń kí bāakì yii: Tipɔmbɔti nì dinàandi! Tiŋman baabadalee, sii ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi puee, binib sìí-mi ki bèel̄-mi.

english_verse: Sometimes I tell myself not to think about you, Lord, or even mention your name. But your message burns in my heart and bones, and I cannot keep silent.
translation_verse: M yaa bí yii: «Maa làá ti dàkafì ti-Dindaan pu, maa làá ti nàatī u-nyɔɔbundi.» Ama ní m-pɔbil poonee, an wù kii ŋŋmee. M bíi pɔ̄ɔntí fám kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u, ama ní kaa ŋūǹ.

english_verse: I heard the crowds whisper, “Everyone is afraid. Now's our chance to accuse Jeremiah!” All of my so-called friends are just waiting for me to make a mistake. They say, “Maybe Jeremiah can be tricked. Then we can overpower him and get even at last.”
translation_verse: M gbìl̄ binib tikpil sòoǹ ki bíiĺ-mi. Bi yíì-mi yii: «Tifaandi bí an kɔkɔ pu». Biba lì yii: «Tí bìitī u-pu!» ní bin kíǹee kíikí yii: «Tiŋman, tí lafun bìitī u-pu.» M-bɔɔbi gba kā ki cí yii ḿ lítí ní. Bi lì yii: «An yaa yíì u làá yàntī án túuǹ-u. Niinee ti làá pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u ní kí tɔ̀-u ipɔntoon.»

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you test those who do right, and you know every heart and mind. I have told you my complaints, so let me watch you take revenge on my enemies.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, a nyí unil un yú nì si deedeeyee. A nyí kun ti lèe nì ti-landɔkɔi. M cí kí ká a nín làá tɔ̀-bi ipɔntoon puee, di sá yii sii ŋaan ní m dū m-bɔti ki ŋá.

english_verse: I sing praises to you, Lord. You rescue the oppressed from the wicked.
translation_verse: Tí gāāmaan ilan kí pàkà ti-Dindaan! Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan, di sá yii u fìil̄ uwɔfi ki nyāntí binikpitib ŋaan! *

english_verse: Put a curse on the day I was born! Don't bless that day.
translation_verse: Mbusu ń kɔ́ ŋwiin ŋun bi màl̄-mee! Ŋwiin ŋun m-na núuĺ-mi ki bíl̀ee ń taa ká diyimɔɔl!

english_verse: Put a curse on the man who told my father, “Good news! You have a son.”
translation_verse: Mbusu ń kɔ́ un di nìn cūtìi tùkū m-baa yii: «Bi màl̄-si kibininjabiki!» ní ki yāntì an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-uee!

english_verse: May that man be like the towns you destroyed without pity. Let him hear shouts of alarm in the morning and battle cries at noon.
translation_verse: An niliuee ń nīn bí kii ntimu mun ti-Dindaan lábitì ki cìb̄ kaa súń isaayee. Udaan làá nīn bí iyaliŋki pu kutaafaau ní kí nīn gbìl̀ ijanjakuŋkuunti pu ŋwiimpu.

english_verse: He deserves to die for not killing me before I was born. Then my mother's body would have been my grave.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní Unimbɔti kaa yāntì m kpíì m-na poon ní? Kéè m-na poon bàà kpántì m-kaakul deeyaa! M bàà làá nīn pée kā u-poon míǹ ní kí nīn pée cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Why did I have to be born? Was it just to suffer and die in shame?
translation_verse: Ba pu ní m nyáń m-na poon ki jéetì kunimbaau nì falaa poon, kí kúntí m-maŋfal wiiŋyi icoo poon míǹ?

english_verse: King Zedekiah of Judah sent for Pashhur son of Malchiah and for a priest named Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. Then he told them, “Talk with Jeremiah for me.” So they came to me and said,
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Yeereemii ú dūú nàatī ubɔti Seedeesiyasee sɔ̀. Ubɔti nìn tú Maalkiya jipɔɔn Paasuur nì usaraaŋal Seefaniya, Maaseeyawuu jipɔɔn bí tùkù-u yii:

english_verse: “King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked Judah. Please ask the Lord to work miracles for our people, as he has done in the past, so that Nebuchadnezzar will leave us alone.”
translation_verse: «Bàlifì ti-Dindaan kí kpèè ti-yil pu bɔti, di sá yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar bíi jáà nì ti. An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan làá tí ŋá u-maamaacikpaambee ubɔ kí yàntī ú búntí kí wàatī-ti.»

english_verse: Then I told them that the Lord had said: People of Jerusalem, I, the Lord, give you the choice of life or death.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti tin ú dūú nàatī samaayee sèé: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M dū dimaŋfal saŋŋu nì ŋkúm saŋŋu ki bíl̀ ni-nimbiin.

english_verse: The Babylonian army has surrounded Jerusalem, so if you want to live, you must go out and surrender to them. But if you want to die because of hunger, disease, or war, then stay here in the city.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ làá gbíntí Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm di làá kpɔ̀-bi. Ama bin làá nyā kí cáá bi-ba kí tīī Babiloon yab bin bíi jáà nì nee làá ŋmátí. Tin an nibee páatèe di sá bi nín kaa kpíìyee.

english_verse: I have decided not to rescue Jerusalem. Instead, I am going to let the king of Babylonia burn it to the ground. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Warns the King of Judah *
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá fàtī kí já nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí ŋá-kì tikpitil, kaa sá tiŋan. M làá dū kitiŋ nee kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan ní úǹ ń tūū-kì ŋŋmi.» Tin làá bàń Juuda yab bɔtiu dicaŋku puee

english_verse: Pay attention, you that belong to the royal family.
translation_verse: Tibɔti nee sá ki tīī Juuda bɔtiu dicaŋkun yab ní. Ní pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi,

english_verse: Each new day, make sure that justice is done, and rescue those who are being robbed. Or else my anger will flame up like a fire that never goes out.
translation_verse: Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab! Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ní kíĺ kutaafaau kí sòoǹ tibɔti ibaamɔn. Ní fōōmaan bin bi mùul̄ee bimuuliliibi ŋaan. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, m-ŋuul làá pōō kí yàaǹ ni-pu kii ŋŋmee. Di làá wà tikɔkɔ ní ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí gbíntí-dì.

english_verse: and I will punish you as you deserve. I'll set your palace on fire, and everything around you will go up in smoke.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá dáaĺ ni-tafal kí nóó nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ nín sá puee. M làá tūū Jeerusaleem bambaŋku ŋŋmi ní an wà tin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-kuee.»

english_verse: King Zedekiah of Judah sent for Pashhur son of Malchiah and for a priest named Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. Then he told them, “Talk with Jeremiah for me.” So they came to me and said,
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Yeereemii ú dūú nàatī ubɔti Seedeesiyasee sɔ̀. Ubɔti nìn tú Maalkiya jipɔɔn Paasuur nì usaraaŋal Seefaniya, Maaseeyawuu jipɔɔn bí tùkù-u yii:

english_verse: “King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked Judah. Please ask the Lord to work miracles for our people, as he has done in the past, so that Nebuchadnezzar will leave us alone.”

english_verse: Jehoahaz became king of Judah after his father King Josiah died. But Jehoahaz was taken as a prisoner to a foreign country. Now I, the Lord, promise that he will die there without ever seeing his own land again. King Jehoiakim The Lord told me to say: *
translation_verse: Bi nín cúú-u ki cūnnì kitiŋ kin poon kuyuŋuee, niin ní u làá tin kpú, waa làá ti ká u-tiŋki.» Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ ubɔti Yoowakiim pu miŋyee

english_verse: You put in big windows and used cedar paneling and red paint. But you were unfair and forced the builders to work without pay. *
translation_verse: U lì u-ban yii: <M làá mā kudikpaaŋŋu kí mā adiin kí tɔ́kɔń ku-yilpu. M làá lèekì tɔkɔlab, ní kí dū seedir dɔi kí nákań agun pu ní kí dū peentaman kí ŋmìtī-ku.

english_verse: More cedar in your palace doesn't make you a better king than your father Josiah. He always did right— he gave justice to the poor and was honest.
translation_verse: A dàkafī yii a nín néeń seedir dɔyee pu ní a sá ubɔtaaa? A-baa nìn jīǹ ki nyù kii báà ŋmee ní. U nìn nóó mara saŋŋu ki nìn dàkà mbaamɔn ní tikɔkɔ nìn còom̄-u tiŋan.

english_verse: That's what it means to truly know me. So he lived a comfortable life and always had enough to eat and drink.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. A-baa nìn mɔ́tí binandambi nì bisoodambi pu ní tikɔkɔ nìn còom̄-u tiŋan. Unil un ŋáań mimmee dàkà yii u lafun nyí-mi ní.

english_verse: But all you think about is how to cheat or abuse or murder some innocent victim.
translation_verse: Ama tin sii nyàab̀ee di sá a-baba paatii kaa dàkafī bin kíǹee pu. A pée nyàab̀ kí nīn kù maanyiibab ŋma ní ki dàkà binib tipɔmbɔti ki mùul̄-bi.

english_verse: People of Jerusalem, the nations you trusted have been crushed. Go to Lebanon and weep; cry in the land of Bashan and in Moab.

english_verse: When times were good, I warned you. But you ignored me, just as you have done since Israel was young.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun a nìn bí nsɔŋfinee, m nìn sòon̄ nì si, ama ní a kíí-mi yii: <Maa làá pīlifiǹ-si!> Tin a ŋá doooo a-sapɔntinee dee, aa pée pílifíǹ-mi dalba dalba.

english_verse: Now you will be disgraced because of your sins. Your leaders will be swept away by the wind, and the nations you trusted will be captured and dragged to a foreign country.
translation_verse: Kubuŋu làá yòon̄ a-kpootiliibi kɔkɔ. An yōoǹ a-bɔmbi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu. Ikpiti in kɔkɔ a ŋée puee, a làá fá a-jilmau ní icoo ń cúú-si gbòooo.

english_verse: King Jehoiachin, son of Jehoiakim, even if you were the ring I wear as the sign of my royal power, I would still pull you from my finger.
translation_verse: Á sòoǹ nì Yoowakiim jipɔɔn Yeekooniya Juuda bɔtiu yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M bí dimaŋfalin, m pūtì yii báà a yaa bàà sá kii kibɔmbiki ki fúuń m-ŋambiki m cáa nyìitī m-daaŋkuee, m làá fúutí-si kí fá.

english_verse: I would hand you over to the enemy you fear, to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army, who want to kill you.
translation_verse: M làá dū-si kí ŋá bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-si a fàŋkí yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔee ŋaan, an dàkà yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nì u-janjaliibi ŋaan.

english_verse: You and your mother were born in Judah, but I will throw both of you into a foreign country, where you will die,
translation_verse: M làá dū si nì a-na un màl̄-see kí tɔ̄ ndandati, kitincaŋ kin poon baa màl̄-nee. Niin ní ni làá tin kpú.

english_verse: Jehoiachin, you are unwanted like a broken clay pot. So you and your children will be thrown into a country you know nothing about.
translation_verse: Binib bàlifī yii: «Kooniya gbanti kpántì kii disambil din wīī kaa ti bí tibanee, àá tiwan tin kaa ti kèetēe níii? Ba pu ní bi jìn̄-u ki cáań kitiŋ kin poon ní u nì u-biyaamu kaa nyée poon ní?»

english_verse: Erase the names of Jehoiachin's children from the royal records. He is a complete failure, and so none of them will ever be king. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Bí ŋmà Kooniya nee pu kii unil un kaa màl̄ ki kée. U bíil̀ u-maŋfal. U-dicaŋkun ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí kàl̄ Daafiidi beejal pu kí kpòotī Juuda tiŋki.»

english_verse: You leaders of my people are like shepherds that kill and scatter the sheep.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí m-nibul kpootiliibi bin bí kii bipikpaaliibi bikpitibee. Bi féeń m-piii ní ki gbáà ki yàantí-i.»

english_verse: You were supposed to take care of my people, but instead you chased them away. So now I'll punish you severely and make you pay for your crimes!
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bíi sòon̄ bipikpaaliibi gbanti pu yii: «Ni yāntì m-piii wáŋkì ki yàl̄. Naa kpēē-i tiŋan. Too, mama m-ba làá kpèè ni-bɔti nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ bɔti, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I will bring the rest of my people home from the lands where I have scattered them, and they will grow into a mighty nation.
translation_verse: «Míǹ boonee, mama m-ba làá kóoǹ m-piii in kíǹ ki yàl̄ ki bí ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon m jìn̄-bi ki kɔ́ǹee kí kpāfì. M làá fàtīí gíiǹní-i i-pikpaapɔɔkun. Niinee, i làá bùtī kí wíiǹ.

english_verse: I promise to choose leaders who will care for them like real shepherds. All of my people will be there, and they will never again be frightened.
translation_verse: M làá tīī-i bipikpaamɔntiibi bin làá kpàà-iee. Niinee, iaa ti làá fàŋkì, kaa ti làá nyɔ̀ ŋkpatim, ní báà ubɔ kaa ti làá wāŋkì, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: Someday I will appoint an honest king from the family of David, a king who will be wise and rule with justice.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Iwiin bí ki dòoń m làá yàntī bí màal̀ Daafiidi jipɔɔn tiŋman pu yɔu. U làá dū dinyil ní kí jī dibeel. U làá yàntī bí nīn tɔ́ mbaamɔn saŋŋu nì tin bí deedeeyee kitiŋ nee pu.

english_verse: As long as he is king, Israel will have peace, and Judah will be safe. The name of this king will be “The Lord Gives Justice.”
translation_verse: U-yuntiŋuee, Juuda beel làá ká difiil ní Isirayeel yab ń nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin. Bi làá dāá nīn yíì-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan di sá ti-baamɔŋŋu.>

english_verse: A time will come when you will again worship me. But you will no longer call me the Living God who rescued Israel from Egypt.
translation_verse: «An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii, ŋwiin bí ki dòoń baa làá dāá gíti lì yii: <M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin ki nyántìń Isirayeel yab kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee!>,

english_verse: Instead, you will call me the Living God who rescued you from the land in the north and from all the other countries where I had forced you to go. And you will once again live in your own land. Jeremiah Thinks about Unfaithful Prophets
translation_verse: ama bi làá dāá lì: <Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin, ki nyántìń Isirayeel yab kitiŋ kin bí ŋgan púee nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon u nìn jìn̄-bi ki kɔ́ǹ bi fātìi gítìń ki kíǹ ki kóò bi-tiŋkinee pu.>» Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bin kaa bàà máaǹ kí nīn sée

english_verse: When I think of the prophets, I am shocked, and I tremble like someone drunk, because of the Lord and his sacred words.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ u-bɔnaatiliibi pu puee sèé: M-pɔbil bíil̀ m-wunti kɔkɔ jìkì. M bí kii udanyɔgbilee, a lì kii unil un nyùn̄ ndaam ki bál̀ee. An sá ti-Dindaan circir Nimbɔtiu nì tin u sòon̄ nì mee pu.

english_verse: Those unfaithful prophets misuse their power all over the country. So God turned the pasturelands into scorching deserts. The Lord Will Punish Unfaithful Prophets
translation_verse: U bí yii: «Kitiŋ nee poonee, binib kɔkɔ sá bilaakpaadambi ní. Bi-kɔkɔ sáń ki cá tikpitil laŋki ní, bi cáá tininjati kí ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee. Mbusu ubɔ puee, kitiŋ nee kā dikpool. Kitiŋ nee naakpaapɔɔku kɔkɔ kūń nyíki nyiki.»

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: You prophets and priests think so little of me, the Lord, that you even sin in my own temple!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M-bɔnaatiliibi nì bisaraaŋaliibi mun sá bikpitib ní. Áli gba m kāntí bi-tuŋkpitiŋ m-Diikun.

english_verse: Now I will punish you with disaster, and you will slip and fall in the darkness. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee bi-saŋŋu ń kpántí dijɔnjɔndi. Bí wāŋkì dibɔmbɔndin kí lítí. M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu dibindi din bi làá dāá sòoǹ bi-nyɔkɔpu yayee.» Samaarii bɔnaatiliibi sɔ́ǹ Jeerusaleem yab

english_verse: The prophets in Samaria were repulsive to me, because they preached in the name of Baal and led my people astray.
translation_verse: Samaarii bɔnaatiliibi ceeyee, m ká tiwan tin cáá titantanee. Diwaal Baal bɔti ní bi nìn nàatī, ní ki gáatí m-nibul Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: And you prophets in Jerusalem are even worse. You're unfaithful in marriage and never tell the truth. You even lead others to sin instead of helping them turn back to me. You and the people of Jerusalem are evil like Sodom and Gomorrah.
translation_verse: Ama tin m ká Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bin bí Jeerusaleemee ceeyee di sá ntimbiil bɔti. Bi ŋáań tilaakpaal, ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn, ki tìì bikpitiŋaliibi kunyannyaau, an yāntì báà ubɔ kaa ti ŋūǹ kí fá u-kpitii. Bi-kɔkɔ bí m-cee kii Soodoom yabee ní. Jeerusaleem yab náań nì Goomoora yab ní.

english_verse: You prophets in Jerusalem have spread evil everywhere. That's why I, the Lord, promise to give you bitter poison to eat and drink. The Lord Gives a Warning The Lord said:
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ u-bɔnaatiliibi pu yii: «M làá tīī-bi kisubiki kin tūee bí ŋmɔ́, kí tīī-bi nnyim min cáá ndabiimee bí nyɔ̀. Di sá yii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bin bí Jeerusaleemee cee ní ikpiti nyánní ki tīntì kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: Don't listen to the lies of these false prophets, you people of Judah! The message they preach is something they imagined; it did not come from me, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii: «Ní taa pīlifì tibɔti tin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi sòoǹee, bi mɔ́ntí-ni ní. Bíǹ bi-ba di nāantí tin bi sòoǹee, taa nyánní man ni-Dindaan nyɔkɔn.»

english_verse: These prophets go to people who refuse to respect me and who are stubborn and do whatever they please. The prophets tell them, “The Lord has promised everything will be fine.”
translation_verse: Bi lì bin kpèé-mi fámee cee yii: <Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii ni làá ká ŋgbansɔŋfi.> Bi tùkù bipɔɔgbifindambi yii: «Nnaabu ŋubɔ kaa làá bàń-ni.»

english_verse: But I, the Lord, tell you that these prophets have never attended a meeting of my council in heaven or heard me speak.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋma di cūtì laakin man ni-Dindaan kàal̀ ki lèekī ilandɔkɔee? Ŋma di ká m-bɔti ki gbìl̄-tì? Ŋma di fōotì ki yīkiǹ m-nyɔɔbundi ki gbìl̄ di-taapu. Yeereemii

english_verse: They are evil! So in my anger I will strike them like a violent storm.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan buŋkpaaŋku dòoń, u-ŋuul làá pōō. Kunaakpaabuŋkpaaŋŋu kubɔ bíi jītí, ku bí binikpitib yiliŋ pu ki màntī.

english_verse: I won't calm down, until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday you will understand exactly what I mean.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yaa kaa ŋá u nín lēē kí ŋá puee, u-ŋuul kpá kí sɔ̀ŋkì. Boon kpataaayee, ni làá dāá gbìl̄ taapu. ti-Dindaan

english_verse: I did not send these prophets or speak to them, but they ran to find you and to preach their message.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi gbantee, maa tú-bi, ama ní bi sáń ki cá. Maa sòon̄ nì bi, ama ní bi bí ki nàatī m-bɔti.

english_verse: If they had been in a meeting of my council in heaven, they would have told you people of Judah to give up your sins and come back to me.
translation_verse: Bi yaa bàà nìn bí laakin m kāl̀ ki lēē ilandɔkɔee, bi bàà sòoǹ nì m-nibul bí béé m-bɔti. Bi bàà nyāntí binib bi-bimbikpitim poon, nì ikpiti in bi ŋáańee poon. Ti-Dindaan bí duulinya kɔkɔn

english_verse: These unfaithful prophets claim that I have given them a dream or a vision, and then they tell lies in my name.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan, m gbìl̄ tin m-bɔnaatiliibi sòoǹee. Bi lì yii bi sòoǹ m-yindi pu ní, ama an kaa sá míǹ. Bi lì yii: <M dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ, m dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ.>

english_verse: But everything they say comes from their own twisted minds. How long can this go on?
translation_verse: Kí tin cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu dee? Ba di kalin kā bibɔnaatiliibi gbanti yiliŋin ní bi nàatī tinyimɔmbɔti ní? An sá bibɔnaatiliibi bin di nāantí tibɔti bi-ba ki nàatēe ní.

english_verse: They tell each other their dreams and try to get my people to reject me, just as their ancestors left me and worshiped Baal.
