translation_verse: Nì bi-damintiiti tin bi cáa sòoǹ tɔb ceeyee, bi dàkafī yii m-nibul làá súntí m-pu, kii bi-naanjab nín nìn dī diwaal Baal pu ki súntì m-pu puee ní.

english_verse: Their dreams and my truth are as different as straw and wheat. But when prophets speak for me, they must say only what I have told them.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu kansikin un yaa dámintèe ń sòoǹ tin u kée. Ama un fōō m-nyɔɔbundee ń nàatī-dì deedee! Idi nì tifin kaa sá ubaanti. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: My words are a powerful fire; they are a hammer that shatters rocks.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: M-bɔti sá kii ŋŋmee ní, a lì kii dikújal din bi cáa wìil̄ ditaŋkpakpaandee ní.

english_verse: These unfaithful prophets claim I give them their dreams, but it isn't true. I didn't choose them to be my prophets, and yet they babble on and on, speaking in my name, while stealing words from each other. And when my people hear these liars, they are led astray instead of being helped. So I warn you that I am now the enemy of these prophets. I, the Lord, have spoken. News and Nuisance The Lord said to me:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <M làá jáǹ-bi. Bi-damintiiti sá tinyimɔmbɔti ní. Bi yaa sòoǹ bi-damintiiti gbanti puee, bi cáá tinyimɔmbɔti nì nyɔɔmálmal ki kíiĺ m-nibul. Man kaa tú-bi, kaa dū dinyɔɔbundi diba ki ŋúbíǹ-bi. Baa pée ŋūǹ kí kèetī m-nibul tiba poon, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.>» Unimbɔti nyɔɔbundi sá diwaŋgulaaa?

english_verse: Jeremiah, when a prophet or a priest or anyone else comes to you and asks, “Does the Lord have news for us?” tell them, “You people are a nuisance to the Lord, and he will get rid of you.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí Yeereemii yii: «Dinibul nee niliu ubɔ, àá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ àá usaraaŋal ubɔ yaa bālifì-si yii: <Ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi sá dilal? Diwaŋgul dilal ní u làá tí túń-ti ní?> Á kíí-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan bí yii nimbi di sá diwaŋgul, ní m làá túutí-ni kí fá kí wàatī m-ba, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.>

english_verse: If any of you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” I will punish you and your families, even if you are a prophet or a priest.
translation_verse: M-nibul niliu ubɔ àá m-bɔnaatiliu ubɔ àá usaraaŋal ubɔ di yaa lī yii: <Ti-Dindaan di túǹ-mi diwaŋgulee,> m làá dáaĺ udaan nì u-dicaŋku tafal.

english_verse: Instead, you must ask your friends and relatives, “What answer did the Lord give?” or “What has the Lord said?”
translation_verse: Ni máaǹ ki bàlifì tɔb yii: <Ti-Dindaan kíí-ti yii ba ní? Ti-Dindaan bí yii ba ní.>

english_verse: It seems that you each have your own news! So if you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” you are twisting my words into a lie. Remember that I am your God, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ama ní taa ti sòoǹ yii ti-Dindaan túǹ-ti diwaŋgul dilal ní? Mimmee ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi sá diwaŋgulaaa? Ni yaa bíi lì mimmee ni bíi kpántí ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan un bí dimaŋfalinee bɔti taapu dee.

english_verse: If you go to a prophet, it's all right to ask, “What answer did the Lord give to my question?” or “What has the Lord said?”
translation_verse: Kpèè tin a máaǹ kí bàlifì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee sèé: <Ti-Dindaan kíí-si yii bá ní? Ti-Dindaan tùkū-si yii ba ní?>

english_verse: But if you disobey me and say, “Here is news from the Lord,”
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa gbíntìi lì yii ti-Dindaan túǹ-ti diwaŋgulee, min kamaa ti-Dindaan bí yii ní taa ti lì mimmee, man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: I will pick you up and throw you far away. And I will abandon this city of Jerusalem that I gave to your ancestors.
translation_verse: M làá yòon̄-ni kí túń kí cáá ni nì ni-tiŋki kin m nìn tīī ni-naanjabee kí tɔ̄ kí fá ndandati.

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me in a vision after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had come to Judah and taken King Jehoiachin, his officials, and all the skilled workers back to Babylonia. In this vision I saw two baskets of figs in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì m ká tikabiti tili tin poon fiigi subiliŋ kēe yú ti-Dindaan kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu. An nìn sá ŋyunti ŋun Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn cúú Yooyakiim jipɔɔn Yeekooniya, Juuda bɔtiu nì Juuda yab kàliŋkpilib nì bicaabi nì bin tūǹ ŋŋal pu tundee Jeerusaleem ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee ní.

english_verse: One basket was full of very good figs that ripened early, and the other was full of rotten figs that were not fit to eat.
translation_verse: Fiigi biliŋ ŋin ŋān̄ kii asubipeekaayee nìn kā kukabiku kubɔ poon ní fiigi biliŋ ŋin bíil̀ unil kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ee kā kukabiku kun kíǹee poon.

english_verse: “Jeremiah,” the Lord asked, “what do you see?” “Figs,” I said. “Some are very good, but the others are too rotten to eat.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-mi yii: «Yeereemii, ba ní a wāĺ?» Ní m kíí-u yii: «M wāĺ fiigi subiliŋ ní. Amɔntee ŋān̄ tikpilku, ama ní akpilee ŋíǹ baasii bíil̀. Ŋi nín bíil̀ puee, unil kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́-ŋi.»

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say:
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: where I am watching over them. Then someday I will bring them back to this land. I will plant them, instead of uprooting them, and I will build them up, rather than tearing them down.
translation_verse: M làá kpèè-bi nì kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ní kí gíiǹní-bi kitiŋ nee poon. Maa ti làá gbá kí kpìtī-bi, ama m làá fàtīí mā-bi ní, maa ti làá cóotí-bi, ama m làá fàtīí cóoń-bi ní.

english_verse: I will give them a desire to know me and to be my people. They will want me to be their God, and they will turn back to me with all their heart.
translation_verse: M làá dāá tīī-bi dipɔbil din làá yàntī bí béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaanee. Bi làá nīn sá m-nibul, ní man ń nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu, di sá yii bi làá fàtīí gítiń m-cee nì bi-pɔbil kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The rotten figs stand for King Zedekiah of Judah, his officials, and all the others who were not taken away to Babylonia, whether they stayed here in Judah or went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: «Ama kii bi nín ŋáań asubil ŋin bíil̀ kaa bí diŋmɔlee puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì binib bin kíǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee nì bin kóò kɔŋkɔnnee Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I will punish them with a terrible disaster, and everyone on earth will tremble when they hear about it. I will force the people of Judah to go to foreign countries, where they will be cursed and insulted.
translation_verse: Duulinya beeŋi kɔkɔ yaa láa ká mimmee, ŋi làá dāá kɔ́ dinyoondin. Bi yaa láa là kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icoo àá kí bèel̀ ubɔ àá kí sìì ubɔ àá kí tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon m làá dāá jà-bi kí kɔ́ǹee, bíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika.

english_verse: War and hunger and disease will strike them, until they finally disappear from the land that I gave them and their ancestors.
translation_verse: M làá dāá dū kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm kí tɔ̄ bi-pu áli bí dāá wāŋkì kitiŋ kin m tīī bi nì bi-naanjabee poon.»

english_verse: The Lord has sent prophets to you time after time, but you refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan túnní u-tɔntɔnliibi u-bɔnaatiliibi ni-cee kaa gbēeǹ, ama naa kpōoǹ ni-tafal ki pílifì-bi.

english_verse: They told you that the Lord had said: Change your ways! If you stop doing evil, I will let you stay forever in this land that I gave your ancestors.
translation_verse: Bi nìn tùkū-ni yii: <Báà ŋma ń fá u-bimbikpitim nì u-tuŋkpitiŋ. Niinee ni làá ŋmā kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin man ni-Dindaan tīī ni nì ni-naanjabee poon kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: I don't want to harm you. So don't make me angry by worshiping idols and other gods.
translation_verse: Ní taa nín̄ jòó ki pá awaa boon kí nīn jáaḿ-ŋi, kí taa gbàan̄ ŋi-nimbiin kí tòotī-ŋi. Ní taa mā àá kí kpítí awaa kí gbítí m-ŋuul. Mimmee maa làá ŋá-ni tikpitil tiba.

english_verse: But you refused to listen to my prophets. So I, the Lord, say that you have made me angry by worshiping idols, and you are the ones who were hurt by what you did.
translation_verse: Ama ní naa pílifiǹ-mi, ní ki kpítì àá ki mɔ́ɔ́ awaa ŋin sá ni-naabuŋuee ki gbítì m-ŋuul. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.>

english_verse: and now I will let you be attacked by nations from the north, and especially by my servant, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. You and other nearby nations will be destroyed and left in ruins forever. Everyone who sees what has happened will be shocked, but they will still make fun of you.
translation_verse: m làá tɔ̄ bí cáań ŋgan pú nibuliŋ. M làá yíiń m-tɔntɔnliu Neebukadineesaar, Babiloon bɔtiu. M làá cáań bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kí tɔ̄ kitiŋ nee nì ki-nib nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-kèe pu. M làá nàan̄ ni nì bi kɔkɔ. M làá yàntī kitiŋ nee ń kpántí ntimbiil paaŋŋu, adigbun kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Binib làá dāá nīn gbáà inimɔɔn biilii, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I will put an end to your parties and wedding celebrations; no one will grind grain or be here to light the lamps at night.
translation_verse: M làá kúntí ifaal nì dipɔɔpindi kuŋkuuntii nì inimpucanlan bi-cee. M làá kúntí tinàti tin nà idee wooku ní kí kpɔ̀ fitila ŋmiŋu.

english_verse: This country will be as empty as a desert, because I will make all of you the slaves of the king of Babylonia for
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kɔkɔ làá kpántí adigbun, mpaan ŋun kaa làá nīn bí ŋkpèéyee. Anibul nee kɔkɔ làá nīn bí Babiloon bɔtiu taapu abin imuŋku ita nì saalaa ní>.»

english_verse: When that time is up, I will punish the king of Babylonia and his people for everything they have done wrong, and I will turn that country into a wasteland forever.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Abin imuŋku ita nì saalaayee yaa láa jítèe, m làá dāá dáaĺ Babiloon bɔtiu nì u-yab tafal ikpiti in bi ŋée pu. M làá kúntí Babiloon tiŋki ní kí yàntī kí kpántí kuteeu kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: My servant Jeremiah has told you what I said I will do to Babylonia and to the other nations, and he wrote it all down in this book. I will do everything I threatened.
translation_verse: M làá cáań inaabu in kɔkɔ m nìn sòon̄ bi ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá tigbɔn poonee kitiŋ nee pu. Tíǹ ní m nìn yāntì Yeereemii sòon̄ ki nāatì atimbun kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: I will pay back the Babylonians for every wrong they have done. Great kings from many other nations will conquer the Babylonians and force them to be slaves. The Cup Full of God's Anger
translation_verse: Di sá yii ntimu mun cáá mpɔnee nì bibɔtikpaambi mun làá dāá nyīī Babiloon yab kí gùl̄ bi-taapu. Niinee ní ḿ pà-bi bi-tuŋkpitiŋ nì bi-ŋáaǹtam paati.» Unimbɔti làá dáaĺ atimbun tafal

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel showed me a vision in which he said, “Jeremiah, here is a cup filled with the wine of my anger. Take it and make every nation drink some.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu bí-mi yii: «Fōō ndamam kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaau un poon m-ŋuul kā nee, kí cáá nyùntī atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ cee m làá tɔ̄-si nee yab.

english_verse: They will vomit and act crazy, because of the war this cup of anger will bring to them.”
translation_verse: Bi yaa láa ká m tú binib bi dū kitàataajiki ki pɔ̄fì binib bi-kansikinee, bi làá dāá nyɔ̀ kí gbí ní ki kíǹ ki kpìntī, ní bi-yiliŋ ń lábití.»

english_verse: I took the cup from the Lord's hand, and I went to the kings of the nations and made each of them drink some.
translation_verse: Ní m fōō ndamam kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaauee ti-Dindaan ŋaan ki cáa nyūntì atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ cee u tú-mee nib.

english_verse: I started with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and the king and his officials were removed from power in disgrace. Everyone still makes insulting jokes about them and uses their names as curse words.
translation_verse: M nyūntì Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda timmun yab nì bibɔtiibi nì bikàliŋkpilib, ní ntimu gbanti kpántì adigbun, ki kíǹ ki fàantí. An yāntì binib gbáà mu-pu ibiil ní ki yāntì mu kpántì ŋabika bi cáa tòó mbusu.

english_verse: The second place I went was Egypt, where everyone had to drink from the cup, including the king and his officials, the other government workers, the rest of the Egyptians,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní m tīī Eejipiti yab bɔtiu Faaroo nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì u-bɔtibiliŋ nì u-nibul kɔkɔ bi nyùn̄,

english_verse: and all the foreigners who lived in the country. Next I went to the king of Uz, and then to the four kings of Philistia, who ruled from Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what was left of Ashdod.
translation_verse: nì nyaaŋmaliŋku nibuliŋ ŋin kóò Eejipiti tiŋkinee, nì Uusi tiŋki bɔtiibi nì Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi an dàkà yii Asikeelɔn yab bɔtiibi nì Gaasaa yab bɔtiibi nì Eekrɔn yab bɔtiibi nì Asidoodi yab bin kíǹee.

english_verse: Then I went to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon,
translation_verse: M nìn tīī Eedoom yab nì Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab,

english_verse: and to the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and their colonies across the sea.
translation_verse: nì Tiir yab bɔtiibi nì Siidɔn yab bɔtiibi nì ntimu mun bí tiŋku gbandee,

english_verse: After this, I went to the kings of Dedan, Tema, Buz, the tribes of the Arabian Desert,
translation_verse: nì Bilaalibub tiŋki bɔtiibi kɔkɔ nì nyaaŋmaliŋku nibuliŋ ŋin kóò kuteeunee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: and the countries in the north, both near and far. I went to all the countries on earth, one after another, and finally to Babylonia.
translation_verse: nì bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ bí ŋgan púee, bin pìl̄ee nì bin bí ndandatee kɔkɔ. Abee ŋin kɔkɔ bí duulinyanee máaǹ kí nyɔ̀ kɔŋkɔn gbanti kí kíǹ kí tīī tɔb. Bíǹ kɔkɔ yaa láa nyùn̄ ki dóòyee ní Seesaki bɔtiu ń nín nyɔ̀.

english_verse: The Lord had said to tell each king, “The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, commands you to drink from this cup that is full of the wine of his anger. It will make you so drunk that you will vomit. And when the Lord sends war against the nations, you will be completely defeated.”
translation_verse: Á tùkù-bi yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: «Nyɔ̀maan! Gbímaan kí wùliŋkì! Lítímaan kí taa yīkì kí kpèè kitàataajiki kin m làá dūú pɔ̀fì binib ni-kansikinee.

english_verse: The Lord told me that if any of them refused to drink from the cup, I must tell them that he had said, “I, the Lord All-Powerful, command you to drink.
translation_verse: Biba yaa yíì kaa làá fōō a-ŋaan ndamam kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaauee kí nyɔ̀ee, á tùkù-bi yii: <Ni làaa, naa làaa, ni làá fōō-u kí nyɔ̀, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Starting with my own city of Jerusalem, everyone on earth will suffer from war. So there is no way I will let you escape unharmed.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii m dū nnaabu ki tɔ́ mama m-ba tiŋki pu, ní nimbi dàkafī yii m làá yàntī-naaa? Aayee, maa làá yàntī-ni fám. M làá dū kujaau kí tɔ̄ kitiŋ nee nib kɔkɔ pu, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.>»

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: From my sacred temple I will roar like thunder, while I trample my people and everyone else as though they were grapes.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan gíti bí-mi yii: «Dū tibɔti nee kí nàatī kí tùkù-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan kāl̀ yilpu ki téenní. U kāl̀ u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki yāntì bi gbìl̄ u-neen pu. U tátí u-tiŋki pu, u bíi kūuntí kí jáǹ kitiŋ nib kɔkɔ, kii bin bí ki tà fiinyi biliŋ kí nyāntí ndaamee.

english_verse: My voice will be heard everywhere on earth, accusing nations of their crimes and sentencing the guilty to death. Disaster Is Coming
translation_verse: Kuwoou kun u ŋáańee bàn̄ kitiŋgbeennyɔkɔ. Ti-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ anibul bɔti, u yíiń inifunaan kɔkɔ u-bɔsoondiikun. U làá yàntī bí pɔ̀fì bikpitiŋaliibi.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says: You can see disaster spreading from far across the earth, from nation to nation like a horrible storm.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Nnaabu ŋubɔ jéetì ditimbundi diba pu ki tin póotì din kíǹ pu, kubuŋkpaaŋŋu nyánní kitiŋgbeennyɔkɔ ki bíi jītí.»

english_verse: When it strikes, I will kill so many people that their bodies will cover the ground like manure. No one will be left to bury them or to mourn. The Leaders of Judah Will Be Punished
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, bin ti-Dindaan làá dāá kpɔ̀ee làá dāá nīn bí kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ kiba kí tin sāā kin kíǹee. Tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ yaa láa bāańee, ubɔ kaa dāa sūǹ bi-pu, kaa dāa kōontí bi-nikpiliŋ ki dāa nín nyàab̀ kí síb́-ŋi. Ŋi làá dāá dòon̄ kitiŋ ní kí kpántí ntiŋkpam.

english_verse: The Lord's people are his flock, and you leaders were the shepherds. But now it's your turn to be butchered like sheep. You'll shatter like fine pottery dropped on the floor. So roll on the ground, crying and mourning.
translation_verse: Bikpootiliibi, gāāmaan ikpiisilan, nín̄ gbáàmaan ibiil kí dòon̄ kitiŋ kí nīn bíliŋkí. Di sá yii ŋyunti bāań bí kpɔ̀ ni mun dee. Ni làá lítí ní kí wīī kii disambil din pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee.

english_verse: You have nowhere to run, nowhere to hide. *
translation_verse: Bikpootiliibi kaa làá ká kibalilaŋ, ní bipikpaaliibi kaa làá ŋmā kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí.

english_verse: Like a lion leaving its den, the Lord has abandoned his people to the destruction of war.
translation_verse: Gbikinti nyáń u-mɔgbaakin. Kujaau kun poon baa sūǹ ubɔ saayee nì ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi puee, bi-tiŋki kpántì kuteeu.

english_verse: The priests, the prophets, and everyone else in the temple heard what I said,
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì samaa kɔkɔ gbìl̄ tibɔti tin Yeereemii sòon̄ kunimbɔtidii cindinee.

english_verse: Soon after Jehoiakim became king of Judah, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yoowakiim, Juuda bɔtiu beel nín kíĺ puee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti nee yii:

english_verse: But if you put me to death, you and everyone else in Jerusalem will be guilty of murdering an innocent man, because everything I preached came from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ama ni máaǹ kí béé yii nimbi nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì ki-nib yaa kūū-mee, maanyiiba fatikuu kpuulool làá lítí ni-pu. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di lafun túnní-mi ni-cee ḿ sòoǹ nì ni tibɔti nee kɔkɔ ní gbìl̄.»

english_verse: Jeremiah, I have a message for everyone who comes from the towns of Judah to worship in my temple. Go to the temple courtyard and speak every word that I tell you.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Cùú yūĺ kunimbɔtidii cindin. Á sòoǹ nì bin kɔkɔ nyēeń Juuda yab timmun ki dòoń ki jáaḿ-mee. Tibɔti tin kɔkɔ m tīī-si mara á tùkù-bee, dūú tùkù-bi, á taa báĺ-bi báà tiba.

english_verse: Maybe the people will listen this time. And if they stop doing wrong, I will change my mind and not punish them for their sins.
translation_verse: An yaa yíì bi làá pīlifiǹ-si ní báà ŋma ń fá u-bimbikpitim. Bi-tuŋkpitiŋ puee, m bàà lēē kí dū nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu. Ama bi yaa pílifì, m làá kpántí m-landɔkɔŋu.

english_verse: Tell them that I have said: You have refused to listen to me and to obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Á dāá tùkù-bi yii, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Nín̄ nóómaan marab bin m tīī-nee.

english_verse: I will destroy this temple, just as I destroyed the town of Shiloh. Then everyone on earth will use the name “Jerusalem” as a curse word. Jeremiah on Trial
translation_verse: Ni yaa kaa pílifèe, m làá wīī kunimbɔtidii nee kii m nín nìn wīī Siiloo yɔkɔ puee. Niinee atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ bí duulinyanee poonee, m làá dū Jeerusaleem ní kí ŋá ŋabika bí nīn cáa tòó tɔb mbusu.>»

english_verse: and as soon as I finished, they all crowded around me and started shouting, “Why did you preach that the Lord will destroy this temple, just as he destroyed Shiloh? Why did you say that Jerusalem will be empty and lie in ruins? You ought to be put to death for saying such things in the Lord's name!” Then they had me arrested.
translation_verse: A cáá dipɔbil ki nāatì ti-Dindaan bɔti yii: <Bi làá wīī kunimbɔtidii nee kii Siiloo yɔkɔee! Bi làá kpēelikì Jeerusaleem tiŋki ní ubɔ ń taa nín̄ gíti kóò ki-ni!» Ní bin kɔkɔ nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee kóoǹ ki múkuǹ Yeereemii pu.

english_verse: The royal officers heard what had happened, and they came from the palace to the new gate of the temple to be the judges at my trial.
translation_verse: Juuda yab kàliŋkpilib nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ní bi yíkì dibeecindi ki nín cá kunimbɔtidii laŋki. Míǹ boonee ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki Kipɔŋ nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bí bikàliŋkpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ yii: «Kijapaai nee máaǹ ŋkúm, di sá yii u sòon̄ ki tɔ́ Jeerusaleem pu, nimbi ni-ba tafal gbìl̄ míǹ.»

english_verse: Then I told the judges and everyone else: The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní kpántí ni-bimbim kí nīn ŋáań min kítèe, kí pīlifì ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ. Niinee u làá kpántí u-landɔkɔŋu. Waa làá ti dū nnaabu kí tɔ̄ ni-pu kii u nín sòon̄ puee.

english_verse: You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right.
translation_verse: Mamee, m bí ni-ŋaan. Ŋámaan-mi min ni ká yii an máaǹee.

english_verse: The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bikàliŋkpilib nì samaayee bí bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi yii: «Kijapaai nee kaa máaǹ ŋkúm, di sá yii tin ti-Dindaan tùkū-uee ní u dūu nāatì-ti.»

english_verse: Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bitindaŋkpilib kansikin biba yíkì ki bí samaa kɔkɔ yii:

english_verse: years ago when Hezekiah was king of Judah, a prophet named Micah from the town of Moresheth had said: “I, the Lord All-Powerful, say Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.”
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti ŋun Eeseekiyaasi nìn sá Juuda bɔtiuee, Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ nìn bí bi yíì-u Miisee, u sá Mooreeseeti tiŋkin. U nín tùkū Juuda nibul kɔkɔ puee sɔ̀. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Siiyɔn tiŋki làá dāá kpántí kii bukpaa bun bi kùn̄ee ní, Jeerusaleem làá dāá kpántí adigbun ŋma, ní kunimbɔtidii gbantaŋki ń kpántí kimɔgbaai.>

english_verse: Then the leaders continued: No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. Then the Lord decided not to destroy Jerusalem, even though he had already said he would. People of Judah, if Jeremiah is killed, we will bring a terrible disaster on ourselves.
translation_verse: Mimmee Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi nì Juuda yab nìn kūū Miiseeee? Aayee, ama bi nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan ní ki nìn pɔ́ɔǹ kí ŋá min fáatiǹ-uee. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì kaa ti cáań nnaabu ŋun u nìn sòon̄ kí cáań kí tɔ̄ bi-puee. Too timbi yaa kūū uninja nee, timbi ti-ba ní ti làá ŋá tikpitil.» Yooyakiim yāntì bi kūū Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Uriya

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me: Jeremiah, make a wooden yoke with leather straps, and place it on your neck.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Nyàab̀ iŋmii nì idɔ kí bóob́ kii bi nín bōob̀ pu kí dūú kpàl̄ inaa in kù tikpaalee. Míǹ boonee, á dūú páań a-gbigbipati pu.

english_verse: Then send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Some officials from these countries are in Jerusalem, meeting with Zedekiah.
translation_verse: A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, á dūú tīī ituun in Eedoom yab bɔtiu nì Moowaab yab bɔtiu nì Amɔn yab bɔtiu nì Tiir yab bɔtiu nì Siidɔn yab bɔtiu túnní Jeerusaleem bi dɔ́miń Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi ceeyee.

english_verse: So have them tell their kings that I have said: I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel,
translation_verse: Á tīī-bi mara bí cùú tùkù bi-kpilib yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé:

english_verse: and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth,
translation_verse: «Man di náań kitiŋ nì binib nì tiwaŋkuti tin bí kitiŋ puee. M dū m-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì m-kpabil ní ki náań tíǹ kɔkɔ ní ki tìì un ní m yaa lèe.

english_verse: and I have chosen my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to rule all nations, including yours. I will even let him rule the wild animals. All nations will be slaves of Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his grandson. Then many nations will join together, and their kings will make slaves of the Babylonians.
translation_verse: Atimbun kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn bí u nì u-jipɔɔn nì u-naantiiu taapu, kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní úǹ u-ba tiŋki làá dāá sìntī kí nīn bí atimbun ŋin pɔ̄ɔǹ-kèe nì bibɔtikpaambi taapuee.

english_verse: This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease.
translation_verse: «Ditimbundi diba àá dibeel diba yaa yíì kaa sīntì di-ba ki tīī Neebukadineesaar, Babiloon bɔtiu, kaa dū u-kpancikiliu ki léeǹee, m làá dū kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ní kí tɔ̄ di-pu. M làá dī Babiloon bɔtiu pu ní kí nàan̄ ditimbundi gbanti, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: You might have people in your kingdom who claim they can tell the future by magic or by talking with the dead or by dreams or messages from a god. But don't pay attention if any of them tell you not to obey Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: «Míǹ puee, nimbi ń taa pīlifì ni-bɔnaatiliibi nì ni-bɔɔbi nì bin lèekī tidamintiil taapuee nì bin kpèé kutagbɔŋu ki būū tibɔɔlee nì bikpaŋkpantiibi. Bi tùkù-ni yii ni kpá kí kɔ́ Babiloon bɔtiu taapu.

english_verse: If you listen to such lies, I will have you dragged far from your country and killed.
translation_verse: Ama tin bi nàatī-nee sá tinyimɔmbɔti ní. Ni yaa pílifiǹ-bee, bi làá jà-ni ní búntí kí wàatī ni-tiŋki. Tiŋman ní, m làá jà-ni ní yàl̄ kí túĺ an kɔkɔ pu, ní kí kpú.

english_verse: But if you and your nation are willing to obey Nebuchadnezzar, I will let you stay in your country, and your people will continue to live and work on their farms.
translation_verse: «Ama ditimbundi diba yab yaa kíí ki sīntì biba taapu ki tīī Babiloon bɔtiu ki fōō u-kpancikiliu ki léeǹee, m làá yàntī bí nīn bí bi-tiŋkin, kí kpɔ̀ ki-pu tikpaal ní kí nīn kóò ki-pu, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said: Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians.
translation_verse: «Mama Yeereemii, m sòon̄ nì Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi tibɔbaantiil gbanti. M tùkū-u yii: <Sii nì a-nibul, ní kíí kí sìntī ni-ba taapu kí nīn bí Babiloon bɔtiu taapu ní kí fōō u-kpancikiliu kí léeń. Ní sìntī ni-ba taapu kí nīn bí u nì u-nibul taapu, niinee ni làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin.

english_verse: But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní sii nì a-nibul là kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀-ni ní? Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ yii tin làá bàń atimbun ŋin nib kaa làá sìntī bi-ba taapu kí tīī Babiloon bɔtiuee dee.

english_verse: Your prophets have told you that you don't need to obey Nebuchadnezzar, but don't listen to their lies.
translation_verse: Ní taa pīlifiǹ bibɔnaatiliibi bin lì-ni yii ni kpá kí kɔ́ Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaanee. Tin bi sòoǹ nì nee sá tinyimɔmbɔti ní.>

english_verse: Those prophets claim to be speaking for the Lord, but he didn't send them. They are lying! If you do what they say, he will have both you and them dragged off to another country and killed. The Lord has spoken.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Man kaa túnní-bi. Bi lì yii bi nàatī m-bɔti, ama an sá inyimɔn ní. Ni yaa pílifiǹ-bee, m làá jà-ni doo, ní ni nì bibɔnaatiliibi bin nàatī an bɔtee ń kpú.>»

english_verse: When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said: Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying!
translation_verse: Yeereemii nìn gíti sòon̄ nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee. U nìn bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ní taa pīlifì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bin bí ki nàatī-ni yii an kaa ti làá yúntí bi làá gíiǹní tiwan tin bi nìn yōoǹ kunimbɔtidiin ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkinee. Tin bi sòoǹee sá inyimɔn ní.

english_verse: If you choose to obey the king of Babylonia, you will live. But if you listen to those prophets, this whole city will be nothing but a pile of rubble.
translation_verse: Ní taa pīlifiǹ-bi, sìntīmaan ni-ba taapu kí tīī Babiloon bɔtiu ní kí nīn bí dimaŋfalin. Ba pu ní ni làá yàntī kitiŋ nee ń kpántí adigbun ŋma ní?>»

english_verse: If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: «Binib gbanti yaa lafun sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi, bi yaa lafun nàatī ti-Dindaan bɔti, bí gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan ú taa yàntī bí yòon̄ kí púntí tiwan tin kíǹ kunimbɔtidiinee nì tin bí Juuda bɔtiu beecindinee nì tin bí Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee kí cùnnì!

english_verse: will be taken to Babylonia, where they will remain until I decide to bring them back to Jerusalem. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: <Bi làá yòon̄ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. Tì làá nīn bí niin kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāá tɔ̄ m-tundi kí gíiǹní-tèe.>» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening,
translation_verse: Dibimbaantiil gbanti poon, an dàkà yii Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nín kāl̀ dibeel dibinnanaatiil poon uŋmaŋmooŋmooti poonee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananiya, Asuur jipɔɔn un sá Gabawɔn tiŋkinee nìn bí kunimbɔtidiin. U nìn kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì Yeereemii nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin. U nìn bí yii:

english_verse: And within two years, I will bring back to Jerusalem everything that he took from my temple and carried off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn yōoǹ kunimbɔtidii poon wanti ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. Too an kíǹ abin ali deedee m làá fàtīí gíiǹní tiwan gbanti doo.

english_verse: King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
translation_verse: M làá fàtīí gíiǹní Juuda bɔtiu Yeekooniya, Yooyakiim jipɔɔn doo, ki kpáaǹ bin kɔkɔ bi cúú ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Tiŋman, m làá léetí kpancikil un Babiloon bɔtiu dūu léeǹ-nee.>»

english_verse: The priests and the others were still standing there, so I said:
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii kíí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananiya nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee nimbiin yii:

english_verse: Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home.
translation_verse: «Ameeni! Ti-Dindaan ń ŋá kii a nín dá láá nāatì tin nee kí gíiǹní kunimbɔtidiin wanti tin kɔkɔ bi yōoǹee nì bin kɔkɔ bi cúú ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee doo.

english_verse: But let me remind you and everyone else
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, sii nì samaa kɔkɔ ń pīlifì tibɔti tin m làá sòoǹ nee tiŋan.

english_verse: Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ yaa nāatì yii ŋgbansɔŋfi làá nīn bée, mana ní bi ŋūǹ kí béé yii ti-Dindaan di lafun túnní-u? See tin u sòon̄ee yaa láa ŋá mimmee ní bí béé.»

english_verse: Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananiya cúú kpancikil un Yeereemii nìn lée ki léetì ki gbáń ki wīī.

english_verse: Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.” I left the temple,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u bí samaa kɔkɔ yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Abin ali deedeeyee, m làá cúú kpancikil un Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar dūu léeǹ atimbun kɔkɔee kí léetí.>» Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii búntì u-laŋki.

english_verse: and a little while later, the Lord told me
translation_verse: Ananiya nín léetì Yeereemii neen kpancikil ki gbáń ki wīīyee boon ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: to go back and say to Hananiah: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. I will put iron yokes on all the nations, and they will have to do what King Nebuchadnezzar commands. I will even let him rule the wild animals.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M làá dū tikúti kpancikiliu ní kí léeń atimbun nee kɔkɔ. Niinee bi làá nīn bí Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar taapu kí nīn sá u-tɔntɔnliibi. M làá dū ipeel gba kí ŋá u-ŋaan.»

english_verse: Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii: <M làá jà-si kitiŋ nee pu. A làá kpú dun bindi, di sá yii a téé samaa bí já nì ti-Dindaan.>»

english_verse: Two months later, Hananiah died.
translation_verse: Ní Ananiya lafun kpíì dibindi gbanti ŋmaluluútiu poon.

english_verse: I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote
translation_verse: Yeereemii nìn dū kugbɔŋuee ki ŋúbiǹ Safan jipɔɔn Eeleeyasa nì Ilikiya jipɔɔn Geemariya. Di sá yii Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nìn tú-bi Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar cee. Tin bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poonee sèé:

english_verse: that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu di bíi sòoǹ nì bin kɔkɔ u yāntì bi cúú Jeerusaleem ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee.

english_verse: to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them.
translation_verse: Māmaan adiin kí nīn kóò. Kpɔ̀maan akpaan kí lēē tijikaal kí jī.

english_verse: Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
translation_verse: Ní cáá binimpoobi kí màal̀ mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu. Ní cáá binimpoobi kí tīī ni-jipɔmbi, kí dū ni-bisalib kí pɔ̄ ticati bí màal̀ mbiyaamu. Ní màal̀ kí bùtī niin, ni-wíiŋŋu ń taa bàtī.

english_verse: Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
translation_verse: Ní nyàab̀maan kitiŋ kin poon ti-Dindaan jìn̄-ni ki kɔ́ǹee nyɔkɔpu cùtam, di sá yii kitiŋ gbanti yaa bí ŋgbansɔŋfinee, ni mun làá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_verse: You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Niinee, ni làá dāá dāan̄ kí yíiń-mi kí mèè-mi, ní ḿ dāá pīlifiǹ-ni.

english_verse: You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you
translation_verse: Ni làá dāá nyàab̄-mi ní kí dāá ká-mi, di sá yii ni làá dāá nyàab̀-mi nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ ní.

english_verse: You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ nì ni míǹ, di sá yii ni lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan tīī-ti Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Babiloon tiŋkin doo.>

english_verse: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now.
translation_verse: «Nimbi bin m jìn̄ Jeerusaleem ki tɔ́ Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee, ní pīlifì man ni-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi.

english_verse: You think Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah are prophets because they claim to speak for me. But they are lying! I haven't told them anything. They are also committing other horrible sins in your community, such as sleeping with the wives of their friends. So I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will put them to death while the rest of you watch. And in the future, when you want to put a curse on someone, you will say, “I pray that the Lord will kill you in the same way the king of Babylonia burned Zedekiah and Ahab to death!” A Message for Shemaiah
translation_verse: Tíǹ bāań-bi kun puee bi ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi Isirayeel tiŋkin ki dōoǹ nì bi-jutiibi nimpoobi. Bi nìn lì yii bi nàatī m-bɔti ama ní an kaa sá míǹ, di sá yii maa nìn tīī-bi mara bí ŋá míǹ. M nyí tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ ní ki sá useeradaan», man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Kugbɔŋu kun Seemayawuu ŋmàn̄ee

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
translation_verse: ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. A gāā a-bindi ki ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī Jeerusaleem yab kɔkɔ nì usaraaŋakpil Seefaniya, Maaseeyawuu jipɔɔn nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin kɔkɔ kíǹee yii:

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan di lēē-si á nīn sá usaraaŋakpil kí fōō Yooyadaa yil. Á nīn kpèé kunimbɔtidii poon biwaatiibi bin yíì bi-ba Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibee. Á bóob́-bi ikusaka ní kí bā-bi abaa.

english_verse: Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him?
translation_verse: Ba pu ní aa wòon̄ Yeereemii uanatootija un bí ni-kansikin ki nàatī-ni Unimbɔti bɔtee?

english_verse: He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
translation_verse: U ŋmàn̄-ti kugbɔŋu ki tīiń-ti Babiloon doo yii: Ni làá kàl̄ niin kí yúntí. An puee, māmaan adiin kí nīn kóò, kí kpɔ̀maan akpaan kí lēē tijikaal kí jī.»

english_verse: When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me.
translation_verse: Ama usaraaŋakpil Seefaniya kàan̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti ki tùkū Yeereemii.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said: I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name.
translation_verse: «Á tɔ̄ bí cùú tùkù bin kɔkɔ bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ Seemayawuu uneelamja puee sɔ̀. Seemayawuu nāatì-ni m-bɔti, ama maa túnní-u ni-cee. U dū tinyimɔmbɔti ní ki sɔ̄ŋkì ni-pɔbil.

english_verse: He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Too man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá dáaĺ Seemayawuu uneelamja nì u-biyaamu nì u-naantiibi tafal. U-dicaŋkun yab ubɔ kpá kí ká tiŋan tin m làá ŋá m-nibulee. Di sá Seemayawuu lūkutì m-nibul yab bí já nì mi. Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee dee.>»

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ŋmà tibɔti tin kɔkɔ m tùkū-see kí ŋá kugbɔŋun.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah: Screams of terror are heard, with no word of peace.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii: «Bi gbìl̀ dipɔɔbiildi biilii pu, an sá dinyoondi ní, kaa sá ŋgbansɔŋfi.

english_verse: Can men give birth? Then why do I see them looking so pale and clutching their stomachs like women in labor?
translation_verse: Ní bàlifì binib kí kpèèmaan, uninja màal̀ kibikaaa? Ama m wāĺ bininjab kɔkɔ yú ki nyīī bi-cammu kii unimpu di kā imatiŋween puee. Ba pu ní binib kpèé fáaa míǹ?

english_verse: My people, soon you will suffer worse than ever before, but I will save you.
translation_verse: Mbusu! Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá ŋwiŋkpaan ní, ŋwiin nee ŋúǹ kaa cáá juti. An sá dinimbinaamandi wiiŋŋu ní ki tīī Jaakɔb naantiibi, ama bi làá dāá ŋmátí.» *

english_verse: Now you are slaves of other nations, but I will break the chains and smash the yokes that keep you in slavery.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ŋyunti yaa láa bàn̄ee, m làá dāá léetí bi-neen kpancikiliu. Niinee baa dāa gíti sá binicambi yumbui.

english_verse: Then you will be my servants, and I will choose a king for you from the family of David. *
translation_verse: Ama bi làá dāá nīn sá man bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nì Daafiidi un m làá dāá dūú kàan̄ bi-pu ubɔtee tɔntɔnliibi.» *

english_verse: Israel, you belong to me, so don't be afraid. You deserved to be punished; that's why I scattered you in distant nations. But I am with you, and someday I will destroy those nations.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M-tɔntɔnliu Isirayeel, taa fàŋkì. Sii un naanja sá Jaakɔbee, taa kɔ́ dinyoondin! Di sá yii m làá nyāntí-si ntindandatimu nee ni kí fīī-si, ní kí gíiǹní a-biyaamu mun bíń kuyuŋuee. Isirayeel, a làá fàtīí gítiń ní kí nīn bí dipɔɔsɔŋkilin. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti bí kí páb́-si.

english_verse: Then I will bring you and your descendants back to your land, where I will protect you and give you peace. Then your fears will be gone. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
translation_verse: M bí a-cee kí fīī-si, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. M làá kúntí anibul ŋin cee m nìn jìn̄-si ki kɔ́ǹee kɔkɔ. Ama siiyee, maa làá kúntí-si. An sá mbaamɔn yii m dáaĺ a-tafal, ama nì deedee poon ní m ŋá míǹ. Di sá yii maa bàà ŋūǹ kí yàntī-si kii a sá maanyiibee.» *

english_verse: The Lord said: My people, you are wounded and near death.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Tiweendi tin a fōōyee kaa cáá dicáaǹdi, baa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ a-buuŋŋu.

english_verse: You are accused of a crime with no one to defend you, and you are covered with sores that no medicine can cure. *
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa bí ki mɔ́tí a-pu. Unil yaa fōō tiweendee, bi cāantí-u ní, ama sii ceeyee, an kaa cáá nnyɔkɔ.

english_verse: Your friends have forgotten you; they don't care anymore. Even I have acted like an enemy. And because your sins are horrible and countless, I will be cruel as I punish you.
translation_verse: A-bɔmbi kɔkɔ súntì a-pu, ubɔ kaa ti dàkafī a-pu. Jeerusaleem, m fáá-si kii a sá m-nannanliuee. M dáaĺ a-tafal ŋkpitim pu, kun puee a-kpitii wīikí ní a-yìntitam náaǹ.

english_verse: But if your enemies try to rob or destroy you, I will rob and destroy them, and they will be led as captives to foreign lands.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ cátikì-see, bi làá cātikì bi mun. Bi làá cúú a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ pái kí cùnnì kuyuŋu. Bin yùn̄-see, bi làá dāá yɔ̀ bi mun, bin fúkúl̀-see, bi làá dāá fūkul̀-bi.

english_verse: No one wants you as a friend or cares what happens to you. But I will heal your injuries, and you will get well. The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Bi yíì-si yii <un bi jìn̄ee>, <Siiyɔn un bɔti kaa ti ká ubɔee>. Ama mama ni-Dindaan, m bí yii: M làá cáaǹ tiweendi tin a fōōyee, m làá yàntī a-buuŋyi ń kpú. *

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I will be kind to you and let you come home. Jerusalem now lies in ruins, but you will rebuild it, complete with a new palace.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá fàtīí mā Jaakɔb diiŋŋi, m làá sɔ̄ bi-kɔŋkooŋyi saai. Bi làá fàtīí mā ntimu mun bi nìn nāaǹee kí tɔ́kɔń mu-digbuŋŋi pu, ní adinyaan ń fàtīí ká ipaan in pu ŋi nìn yúee.

english_verse: Other nations will respect and honor you. Your homes will be filled with children, and you will celebrate, singing praises to me.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá gbìl̄ ilan nì ifaal kuŋkuuntii pu bi-kansikin. M làá dāá yàntī bí bùtī, bi-wíiŋŋu kaa làá dāá bàtī. Baa làá dāá gíti kpèè-bi fám, di sá yii m làá dāá tīī-bi tinyool.

english_verse: It will be just like old times. Your nation will worship me, and I will punish anyone who abuses you.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb naantiibi làá dāá nīn bí kii bi nín nìn bí pu njaminee ní. Bi làá dāá fàtīí tí kóoǹ kí kpāfì m-nimbiin, ní ḿ dāá jáǹ bi-wɔ́biliibi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: One of your own people will become your ruler. And when I invite him to come near me at the place of worship, he will do so. No one would dare to come near without being invited.
translation_verse: Ni-kansikin ubɔ di làá dāá nīn sá ni-kpiliu, tiŋman ni-kansikin ubɔ di làá dāá kpòotī-ni. M làá dāá pɔ̄ udaan diyimɔɔl ú sútí kí pìl̄-mi. Di sá yii ŋma di sá-u kí sútí kí pìl̄-mi? Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: You will be my people, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ní dāá nīn sá m-nibul, ní man ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu.>» *

english_verse: I am furious! And like a violent storm I will strike those who do wrong.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan buŋkpaaŋku dòoń, u-ŋuul di pōō. Kunaakpaabuŋkpaaŋŋu bíi jītí ki fīintí kí dāá lítí binikpitib pu, ku bí binikpitib yiliŋ pu ki màntī.

english_verse: I won't calm down until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday, you will understand what I mean.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yaa kaa ŋá u nín lēē kí ŋá puee, u-ŋuul kpá kí sɔ̀ŋkì. Boon kpataaayee, ni làá dāá gbìl̄ taapu.

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I promise that someday all your tribes will again be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋyunti gbantee, man di làá dāá nīn sá Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kɔkɔ Nimbɔtiu, ní ŋí dāá nīn sá m-nibul.» Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee gítintam

english_verse: In the desert I was kind to those who escaped death. I gave them peace, and when the time is right, I'll do the same for you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Kuteeunee, m dàkā dinibul din ŋmátì ki nyáń ŋkúm ŋaanee m-laŋŋaŋfitiiku. M làá tīī Isirayeel diŋuŋfil dee.

english_verse: Some time ago, the Lord appeared to me and told me to say: Israel, I will always love you; that's why I've been so patient and kind.
translation_verse: Dinibulee nìn lì yii: <Doooo ndandati ní ti-Dindaan lēē u-ba ki dàkā-mi.> Ní m kíí-u yii: <Dooooyee ní m néeń-si ní ki làá nīn pée néeń-si. An pu ní m dū m-ba ki nákáǹ-si kiŋkiŋ.

english_verse: You are precious to me, and so I will rebuild your nation. Once again you will dance for joy and play your tambourines.
translation_verse: Sii Isirayeel un m néeńee, m làá fàtīí yòon̄-si kí yóoń, ní bí fàtīí mā-si. A làá fàtīí yòon̄ a-gaŋgammu nnyaammuee kí cùú kūtì bin bí ki jīǹ jiŋaalee pu ní ŋɔ̄.

english_verse: You will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria and enjoy the grapes.
translation_verse: A làá dāá fàtīí cóoń fiinyi sufii Samaarii jooŋŋi pu. Bin cóoǹ-iee di làá dāá kìtī abil.

english_verse: Someday those who guard the hill country of Ephraim will shout, “Let's go to Zion and worship the Lord our God.” Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋwiin ŋubɔ bí ki dòoń biciitiliibi làá dāá tɔ́kɔń Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu kí téeń yii: Yīkìmaan tí jɔ̄m̀ Siiyɔn <jool, ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu cee.>»

english_verse: The Lord says: Celebrate and sing for Israel, the greatest of nations. Offer praises and shout, “Come and rescue your people, Lord! Save what's left of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nín̄ tátímaan nì dipɔɔpindi kí tīī Isirayeel, nín̄ fàal̀maan ditimbundi din tɔ́kɔ́ atimbun kɔkɔ puee. Nín̄ gàmaan ilan mpɔn ki lì yii: «Ti-Dindaan, fīī a-nibul, fīī bin kíǹ Isirayeel tiŋkin ki bí dimaŋfalinee.»

english_verse: I, the Lord, will bring my people back from Babylonia and everywhere else on earth. The blind and the lame will be there. Expectant mothers and women about to give birth will come and be part of that great crowd.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m làá nyāntiń-bi ŋgan pú timmun kí gíiǹní, ní kí kóoǹní-bi ntindandatimun kí kpāfì. Bi-kansikinee, bijɔfub nì bideembi, bipɔdambi nì bimatimpɔmbi làá nīn bí. An dāa sá dinikitikpaandi di làá fàtīí gítiń.

english_verse: They will weep and pray as I bring them home. I will lead them to streams of water. They will walk on a level road and not stumble. I am a father to Israel, my favorite children.
translation_verse: Bi fàtīi gítiń ki sūǹ, ní m cēentí-bi ki ŋmēentí-bi. M làá dāá cáá-bi kí cùnnì ibun in pùub̀ee ni. M làá dāá dū-bi kí dī nsan ŋun tèen̄ baa làá gbéetée pu. Di sá yii m sá kii ubaatee ní ki tīī Isirayeel, ní Eefiraayiim sá m-jipɔŋkpiliu. *

english_verse: Listen to me, you nations nearby or across the sea. I scattered the people of Israel, but I will gather them again. I will protect them like a shepherd guarding a flock;
translation_verse: Nimbi atimbun, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. Ní cáá-dì kí nàatī ntimu mun dátì nnyim māntìi tú-muee ni. Ní lì yii: «Ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ Isirayeel yab bi yàl̄ ki gbí an kɔkɔ. Kɔŋkɔnnee u kóoǹ-bi ki kpáfì, ki wúń bi-pu kii upikpaal nín wúǹ u-piii pu puee.»

english_verse: I will rescue them from enemies who could overpower them.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan fīī Isirayeel yab, u nyántì-bi unannanli un pɔ̄ɔǹ-bee ŋaan.

english_verse: My people will come to Mount Zion and celebrate; their faces will glow because of my blessings. I'll give them grain, grapes, and olive oil, as well as sheep and cattle. Israel will be prosperous and grow like a garden with plenty of water.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá bàń Siiyɔn gbantaŋki pu ki kūuntí dipɔɔpindi kuŋkuuntii. Bi fāā mɔ̀ɔɔ ki cá ti-Dindaan wammɔntiiti cee, an dàkà yii bilee nì ndapɔm nì ŋkpam nì ipii nì iŋoobu nì inaa. Bi làá dāá nīn bí kii bukpaa bun bi yāaǹ nnyim tiŋanee ní. Bi-pɔŋŋu pée gíti kpá kí bàtī.

english_verse: Young women and young men, together with the elderly, will celebrate and dance, because I will comfort them and turn their sorrow into happiness.
translation_verse: Niinee bisapɔmbi dāa ŋōō nì dipɔɔpindi ní binaacimpɔmbi nì bijaŋkpilib fàal̀ dicilpu. M làá dāá yàntī bi-nimbaaku ń kpántí-bi jiŋaal, m làá ŋméeǹ-bi bi-nimbinaamandi poon, ní kí yàntī bi-pɔbil ń sɔ̀ŋkì.

english_verse: I will bless my people with more food than they need, and the priests will enjoy the choice cuts of meat. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Offers Hope
translation_verse: M làá dāá tīī bisaraaŋaliibi tinan tin cáá ŋkpamee tikpil. M làá dāá gbéeǹ m-nibul tiwammɔntiil, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. *

english_verse: In Ramah a voice is heard, crying and weeping loudly. Rachel mourns for her children and refuses to be comforted, because they are dead. *
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Bi gbìl̀ Raama tiŋkin dituweel nì nsiim pu. An sá Raaseel di bíi sūǹ u-biyaamu pu. Waa kíí ubɔ ń ŋméeǹ-u, di sá yii muaa ti bí.»

english_verse: But I, the Lord, say to dry your tears. Someday your children will come home from the enemy's land. Then all you have done for them will be greatly rewarded.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Taa ti sɔ̄ kí yīkintì, pítí a-nyinnyim! Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ, m làá pà a-gìńdi paati. A-biyaamu làá nyānní binannanliibi tiŋkin kí gítiń.

english_verse: So don't lose hope. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Dimákal bí ki tīī a-naantiibi, a-biyaamu làá fàtīí gítiń bi-tiŋkin.»

english_verse: The people of Israel moan and say to me, “We were like wild bulls, but you, Lord, broke us, and we learned to obey. You are our God— please let us come home.
translation_verse: M gbìl̄ Eefiraayiim yab yáliŋkí ki lì yii: «Ti-Dindaan, a dáaĺ ti-tafal ŋkpitim pu kii bi nín tìŋkī dinajapɔmbil din bɔti pɔ̄ɔ̄yee puee. Ama á fàtīí gíiǹní-ti a-cee tí bàà fàtīí gítiń a-cee tiŋman pu. Di sá yii sii ti-Dindaan di sá ti-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: When we were young, we strayed and sinned, but then we realized what we had done. We are ashamed and disgraced and want to return to you.”
translation_verse: Ti nìn fātì ti-boon ki tīī-si, ama kɔŋkɔnnee, ti kpántì ti-ba. Ti béè ti-yìntitam, ní ki fátí ti-biŋŋi ki yáliŋkí. Ti fá ti-jilmau ní icoo cúú-ti gbòooo. Tiŋman ti ŋá tin kaa kítèe ti-naacimpɔntin, ní ki bíi fòol̄ an paati.

english_verse: People of Israel, you are my own dear children. Don't I love you best of all? Though I often make threats, I want you to be near me, so I will have mercy on you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim di sá m-bineeŋkaaki, m néeń-u ki jítiǹ bin kɔkɔ kíǹee. An pu ní ŋyunti ŋun kamaa m yaa bíi sòoǹ ki kù u-bɔtee, m gbíntìi dàkafī u-pu. M-pɔ̀ti kaa fù u-pu. Maa pée ŋūǹ kí gbèen̄ kí taa sɔ̄ u-saai.» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ. *

english_verse: With rock piles and signposts, mark the road well, my dear people. The road by which you left by will now lead you home.
translation_verse: Cóoń kikpaanyɔkɔ taŋkpeeŋi kí nóó nì a-daanti, cóoń tidaandi nsan pu. Nín̄ nyí nì a-ba nì didandi din a dēe, nì nsan ŋun a cōom̀ee. Isirayeel un bí kii usapɔɔnee, fàtīí gítiń, fàtīí gítiń ntimu mun sá a-yaka nee poon! Fàtīí gítiń a-timmun.

english_verse: Will you ever decide to be faithful? I will make sure that someday things will be different, as different as a woman protecting a man. The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
translation_verse: Usapɔɔn un gáatèe, a làá nīn sáń ki lábití yéè kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní? Di sá yii ti-Dindaan náań tiwampɔn tiba kitiŋ pu: Unimpu di làá nīn kíǹ ki mɔ̀nnì uninja. * Bi làá fàtīi mā Juuda nì Jeerusaleem timmu

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say, “We pray that the Lord will bless his home, the sacred hill in Jerusalem where his temple stands.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M yaa láa fātìi gíiǹní bin bínní kuyuŋuee, bi làá dāá tí lì Juuda tiŋki nì ki-timmu pu yii: «<Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ a-boon, sii Siiyɔn gbantaŋki kin bí circiree, laakin difiil bée.>

english_verse: The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds.
translation_verse: «Niinee Juuda yab bin kóò tisatinee nì bin kóò ntimunee, bikpaabi nì biwaŋkpaaliibi kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn kóò kitiŋ nee pu dicilpu.

english_verse: Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy,
translation_verse: M làá dāá tīī bin gīīyee nnyim bí nyɔ̀ ní kí tīī bin kaa ti cáá mpɔnee kunyannyaau.

english_verse: and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní m fīntì ní ki ká yii ŋgeem min m gèen̄ee mɔ̄.

english_verse: Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Iwiin iba bí ki dòoń, m làá dāá yàntī binib nì tiwaŋkuti ń kpátí kí gbí Isirayeel nì Juuda beeŋin kii iwamboolee.

english_verse: In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow.
translation_verse: Kii m nín tāā ki bíikì bi-pu, ki fùkū, ki gāatì ki lúkú, ki kpéelikì, ki nāaǹ ní ki ŋá tikpitil puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá ŋá kí tīī-bi bí fàtīí mā kí cóoń, man bi-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: No longer will anyone go around saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ubɔ kaa dāa gíti lì yii: <Bibaatiibi ŋmɔ́ asubigaan, ama mbiyaamu nyiŋŋi di nyāŋfì.>

english_verse: When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death. The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Un di yaa ŋmɔ́ asubigaanee, udaan nyiŋŋi di làá nyàŋfì. Un di yaa ŋá ikpitee, udaan di kúù.»

english_verse: The Lord said: The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan di lī yii iwiin iba bí ki dòoń, m làá fàtīí pòon̄ Isirayeel nì Juuda yab dipoompɔndi.

english_verse: It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
translation_verse: Díǹ kaa dāa sá kii din m nìn pōoǹ bi-naanjab ŋwiin ŋun m nìn cúú bi-ŋal ki nyántì Eejipiti tiŋkin kuyuŋunee. Nì min kɔkɔ man di nìn sá bi-Dindaanee, bi nìn kpītì dipoondi gbanti, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel: “I will write my laws on their hearts and minds. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Dipoompɔndi din m làá dāá líí Isirayeel yab ŋwiin gbantee sɔ̀. M làá dāá dū m-marab kí ŋmà kí ŋá bi-landɔkɔyin, kí ŋmà-bi kí ŋá bi-pɔbilin. Man làá dāá nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu ní bíǹ ń nīn sá m-nibul.

english_verse: “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti dàkà u-juti àá u-nabiki ú nīn nyí ti-Dindaan. Di sá yii kí yòon̄ bi-kansikin mbiyaawaamu kí tin cáá sāā bikpaambee, báà ŋma làá dāá béé-mi, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Di sá yii m làá dāá dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi ní kaa làá ti téetí bi-yìntitam pu.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful. I command the sun to give light each day, the moon and stars to shine at night, and ocean waves to roar.
translation_verse: Ŋma di dū ŋwìiń ki kāaǹ ŋú nīn ŋmíntí ŋwiimpu ní? Ŋma di tīī uŋmal nì iŋmalbijaa mara í nīn ŋmíntí kunyeeu ní? Ŋma di kùtī tiŋku ní ki yàntī u-nyiŋgbanti yíkí ki gà kuwoou ní? An sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan. U-yindi dee.»

english_verse: I will never forget to give those commands, and I will never let Israel stop being a nation. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Daliŋkin ní m yaa kíí yii marab bin kpòotī duulinya nee kaa ti bée, mimmee m kíí yii Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ mun kaa ti kpáfì ki ŋá ditimbundi dee!»

english_verse: Can you measure the heavens? Can you explore the depths of the earth? That's how hard it would be for me to reject Israel forever, even though they have sinned. I, the Lord, have spoken. Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Unil yaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmàntī kutagbɔŋu kun dàn̄ee, ki yaa tí ŋūǹ kí béé kitiŋ nyóoŋŋuee, mimmee ma mun làá dū Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kí fá, ikpiti in kɔkɔ bi ŋée pu, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.» *

english_verse: The Lord said: Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Iwiin bí ki dòoń m làá fàtīí mā Jeerusaleem kí tīī m-ba, kí yòon̄ Ananeeyeel difɔkɔku Dikpindi punyɔkɔki.

english_verse: From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá dū ŋŋmiiŋmantikaa kí tɔ̄ kí ŋmàntī kitiŋ kpaanyɔkɔ kí nīn cá Gareeb gbantaŋki, ní kí yòon̄ niin kí pɔ́ĺ kí nīn cá Goowa tiŋki watil pú.

english_verse: Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá dū anikpil nì ŋfantam tantakal nì mpaan ŋun kɔkɔ dɔ̄ kí tin sāā Seedrɔn buŋŋuee nì Dikpindi punyɔkɔki kin sá Itaamu punyɔkɔki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee kí sú-mi. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti fùkù tiba ki dāa nín bíiĺ tiba mpaan gbanti pu.»

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin disaalaatiil poonee, Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar úǹ nìn ŋá abin saalku nì ata dee dibeel pu. Ŋyunti gbanti ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii.

english_verse: At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee Babiloon janjaliibi nìn māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí já nì kì. Bi nìn cúú Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii ki pīiǹ kudii bijanjaliibi dumpu, Juuda bɔtiu beecindin.

english_verse: Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said: I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi di nìn yāntì bi pīiǹ-u niin. Di sá yii u nìn wòon̄ Yeereemii u nín nāatì ti-Dindaan bɔti yii: «M làá dū Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan ú fōō-kèe.

english_verse: King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face.
translation_verse: Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi kaa làá ŋmátí kí nyā Babiloon yab ŋaan, di sá yii m lēē kí dū-u kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan. U làá cùú yūĺ Neebukadineesaar nimbiin ní bí nīn sòoǹ ki kpèé tɔb.

english_verse: Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Bi làá cúú Seedeesiyasi kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin, ní ú nīn bí niin kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāá kpèè u-bɔtee, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Ni yaa gbíntìi bíi jáà nì Babiloon yab, naa làá ŋmā-bi.»

english_verse: Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Yeereemii bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì mi puee sèé:

english_verse: Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
translation_verse: <A-wee Anameeyeel, Saaluum jipɔɔn làá dāan̄ a-cee kí bí-si yii á dā u-kpaabu bun bí Anatootee. Di sá yii sii nì u di pēē. An puee, sii di cáá nsan kí dā bukpaa gbanti.>»

english_verse: Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.” The Lord had told me to buy it
translation_verse: Kii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì mi puee, m-wee Anameeyeel nìn lafun dɔ́miń m-cee bijanjaliibi mɔŋkiŋu ki bí-mi yii: «Dā m-kpaabu bun bí Anatooti, Beenjameen tiŋkinee. Di sá yii man nì sii di pēē. Míǹ puee, mara poonee, sii di cáá nsan kí dā-bu.» Niin ní m béè yii ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ nì mi.

english_verse: Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything.
translation_verse: «Too, ti-Dindaan, sii di dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì a-kpabil ki náań kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ. Tiba kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ a-cee.

english_verse: And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
translation_verse: M nìn dū tigbɔnliitilee ki tīī Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki, Maaseeyawuu naantiiu. M-wee Anameeyeel nì biseeradambi bin nìn nyīī ŋŋal kugbɔŋuee puee, nì Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí bijanjaliibi mɔŋkiŋuee nìn bí.

english_verse: I told Baruch that the Lord had said: Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: <Yòon̄ tigbɔnliitil tin dàkà yii m dá bukpaayee, kun pu m nyīī ŋŋal ki kpáb́ee nì kun maa kpáb́ee. Á dū-tì kí ŋá diboolin kí kpāafì an nīn bí kí yúntí.>»

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country. Jeremiah Questions the Lord
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: <Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń, bi làá dāá fàtīí dā kitiŋ nee poon adiin nì akpaan nì fiinyi kpaaŋŋi.>» Yeereemii wimmeem

english_verse: You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Sii di dàkà binib kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu kí tin sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ kutuku pu. Ama bibaatiibi yaa yīntèe, bi-biyaamu tafal ní a dátí kí tɔ̀ ipɔntoon. A sá Unimbɔtikpaan, ní ki cáá mpɔn. Sii yindi di sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan.

english_verse: With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
translation_verse: A nín lēē kí ŋá puee sá ŋkpaami ní a cáá mpɔn kí ŋá míǹ. A kpèé ki wāĺ tin kɔkɔ nnibiyaamu bí ki ŋáańee. A pà báà ŋma paati ki nóó nì u-bimbim nì u-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee ní.

english_verse: You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well.
translation_verse: «Sii di nìn túń atuŋkpaan nì maamaacib Eejipiti tiŋkin. Áli nì díǹ, a dàkà un ní a sée Isirayeel nibul nì inifunaan kɔkɔ kansikin, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nee ní.

english_verse: You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt.
translation_verse: A nìn túń atuŋkpaan nì maamaacib ki dàkā mpɔŋkpaan nì dikpabil ki nyántì a-nibul Isirayeel Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
translation_verse: A nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ti-naanjab yii a làá dū kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil pùub̀ee kí tīī-bi ní a lafun ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: But when our ancestors took over the land, they did not obey you. And now you have punished Israel with disaster.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lafun kɔ́ ki fōō kitiŋ gbanti ki kāl̀. Ama baa pílifiǹ-si, kaa nóó a-dàkatam, kaa tɔ́ a-marab. Niinee ní a yāntì inaabu in kɔkɔ bíi bàń-ti díǹ nee jéetì bi-pu.

english_verse: Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
translation_verse: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, Babiloon yab dɔ́miń ki gūū kitiŋee ki bíl̀ ataŋkpuku kí fōō-kì. Bi bíi jáà nì kì ní kì làá pée kɔ́ bi-ŋaan ní kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm pu. Tin a nìn sòon̄ ki síiǹee bāań ní sii a-ba wāĺ míǹ.

english_verse: So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians? The Lord Explains about the Field
translation_verse: Too, Jeerusaleem làá kɔ́ bi-ŋaan dee! Kin ba pu ní a tīī-mi mara yii ḿ dā bukpaa Anatooti kí pà biseeradambi nimbiin?» Ti-Dindaan kíí Yeereemii tibɔti

english_verse: The Lord explained:
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kíí Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
translation_verse: «Man di sá tin kɔkɔ cáá kufoouee Nimbɔtiu. Tiba bí ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ-maaa?

english_verse: It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: An pu ní man ni-Dindaan bí yii m làá dū kitiŋ nee kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nì u-janjaliibi ŋaan. U làá fōō-kì.

english_verse: The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
translation_verse: Babiloon yab bin bíi jáà nì kitiŋ nee làá kɔ́ ki-ni, kí nàan̄-kì ní kí tūū-kì ŋŋmi. Adiin aba yilpu bi nín bɔ̀b̄ puee, binib tūutì talaalub ki tīī diwaal Baal ní ki fá awaa aba mun ndaam. Bi ŋá míǹ ki gbítì m-ŋuul. Too, Babiloon yab làá tūū adiin gbanti ŋŋmi.

english_verse: They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me.
translation_verse: Bi cáá bi-waaŋi ŋin sá ntimbiil tuuŋŋee ki kɔ́ǹ Kudii kun bi dūu sú-mee poon ki kɔ́ǹ-ku tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
translation_verse: Inɔɔm tantakalinee, bi ŋātì mpaan kí nīn tòotī diwaal Baal. Niin ní bi dū bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ki tūū ŋŋmi ki tīī diwaal Mooleeki. Maa pée tīī-bi dalba dalba mara bí ŋá míǹ, kaa kpáàa dākafì míǹ ŋwindal. Bi nín ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi gbantee, bi téé Juuda yab ki yāntì bi ŋá ikpiti.

english_verse: Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: «Ni sòoǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu yii: <Kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm di dū-kì ki ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan.> Kɔŋkɔnnee, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ kitiŋ nee pu puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety.
translation_verse: M nìn gíí bi-pu diŋuul ki fōō bi-pu mbum ŋkpitim pu. M nìn jìn̄-bi bi yàl̄ ki kɔ́ ntimu kɔkɔn. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m làá kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì doo bí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_verse: They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Niinee bi làá fàtīí nīn sá man nibul, ní man ń nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ yii: «Man di cáań nnaabukpaan nee ki tɔ́ Juuda nibul pu. Man ubaantee di làá tí cáań nnaam min m pōoǹ-bee kí tīī-bi.

english_verse: Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals.
translation_verse: Binib lì yii: <Bi dū kitiŋ nee ki ŋá Babiloon yab ŋaan. Kɔŋkɔnnee kì kpántì kuteeu ní binib nì tiwaŋkuti kaa ti bí ki-pu. Ama kitiŋ nee poonee, binib làá dāá fàtīí dā akpaan.

english_verse: But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Tiŋman bi làá dāá fàtīí dā akpaan Beenjameen tiŋkin nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kpaanceetii nì Juuda timmun nì ntimu mun bí ajoon puee nì mun bí Seefeelaayee nì mun bí Neegeebee. Binib làá dāá ŋmà tigbɔn tin dàkà yii bi nyáfì bi-kpaatantee ní kí dāá dū kijalii kí nyīī ti-pu ŋŋal ní kí kpáb́ biseeradambi nimbiin. Di sá yii m làá fàtīí gíiǹní bi-yab bin bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee», ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me: I am the Lord, and I created the whole world.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan un di ŋá tin bí nee kɔkɔee, ti-Dindaan un di bɔ́ntì-tì ki yāntì tì bée nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Úǹ ní bi yíì ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
translation_verse: Kúuǹ ki yíiń-mi, m làá kíí-si. M làá lēē tiwaŋkpaandi tin bí dibalin aa nyée kí dàkà-si.

english_verse: Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace.
translation_verse: «Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔ, m làá dāá cáaǹ-kì kí pɔ̄ɔkì. M làá cáaǹ-kì ní ki-nib ń ká dipɔɔsɔŋkil kí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_verse: I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before.
translation_verse: M làá fàtīí gíiǹní Juuda nì Isirayeel yab bin bi nìn cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee, m làá fàtīí gíiǹ-bi mpaan ŋun pu bi nìn bí dooooyee.

english_verse: They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt.
translation_verse: M làá dāá ŋá-bi circir kí nyāntí ikpiti in kɔkɔ bi ŋée. Bi nín jáń nì mi puee, m làá dūú pɔ̄-bi.

english_verse: When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
translation_verse: An làá dāá nīn mɔ̄ǹ-mi ḿ yíiń Jeerusaleem yindi. Kitiŋ gbanti làá dāá tīī-mi jilma ní ḿ dāá nīn fàal̀ ki-pu kitiŋ pu nibuliŋ kɔkɔ nimbiin. Anibul gbanti kɔkɔ làá dāá béé tiŋan tin kɔkɔ m làá dāá ŋá-kèe. Bi yaa láa ká nnaam nì ŋgbansɔŋfi ŋun kɔkɔ m làá tīī-kèe, bi làá dāá nīn jìkì nì kufaaŋŋu ní kí kɔ́ dinyoondin.» *

english_verse: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Nimbi Juuda yab, ni lì yii: <Kitiŋ nee kpántì adigbun binib nì tiwaŋkuti kaa ti kóò ki-pu.> Tiŋman, Juuda timmu nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi kíǹ ki dɔ̄ fám binib nì tiwaŋkuti kaa ti kóò ntimu gbantin. Too, kitiŋ nee poonee, bi làá fàtīí gbìl̄

english_verse: happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say: “We praise you, Lord All-Powerful! You are good to us, and your love never fails.” The land will once again be productive.
translation_verse: jiŋaal wooku nì dipɔɔpindi laŋyi nì animpucaŋgbiil pu. Bi làá dāá fàtīí tí gbìl̄ bin cāabìń inyɔŋki saraabi kunimbɔtidiinee laŋyi pu ki lì yii: <Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, di sá yii u ŋān̄ ní u-neendi bí ki cá jaanjaan.> Di sá yii m làá fàtīí ŋāŋkì kitiŋ nee ní kí fàtīí gítí kii kì nín nìn bí pu dooooyee, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.» *

english_verse: Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord's Wonderful Promise
translation_verse: Dijool pu timmun nì Seefeelaa nì Neegeeb nì Beenjameen timmu nì Jeerusaleem kpaanceetii nì Juuda timmunee, ipii nì iŋoobu làá dāá tí jītí un kàaǹ-iee nimbiin», ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Tin Unimbɔti pōoǹee, u làá ŋá míǹ

english_verse: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Iwiin iba bí ki dòoń, m nín pōoǹ Isirayeel nì Juuda yab nibul kí ŋá-bi tiŋan tiŋyee, m làá ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti yaa láa sāāyee, m làá yàntī bí màal̀ Daafiidi naantiiu tiŋman pu yɔu. Úǹ di làá dāá yàntī binib ń ŋá tin dɔ̄ nsanee nì tin bí deedeeyee kitiŋ nee pu.

english_verse: In those days, Judah will be safe; Jerusalem will have peace and will be named, “The Lord Gives Justice.”
translation_verse: Iwiin gbantinee Juuda beel làá dāá ká difiil ní Jeerusaleem beel ń dāá nīn bí dipɔɔsɔŋkilin. Bi làá nīn yíì Jeerusaleem yii: <Ti-Dindaan ti-baamɔŋŋu.>»

english_verse: The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Daafiidi maaliŋu poon kpá kí lóó un làá kàl̄ Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeelee.

english_verse: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
translation_verse: Míǹ mbaantiim Leefii yab bin sá bisaraaŋaliibee kpá kí lóó binib bin làá nīn yú m-nimbiin ki ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi, ki tùutī saraabi ki ŋáań baabadal saraabee.» *

english_verse: Then the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them,
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ni ŋūǹ kí kpìtī mpèé ŋun di bí man nì ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kansikineeee? Ni ŋūǹ kí pìin̄ nsan ŋwiimpu ń taa páań kunyeeu boon, àá kunyeeu ń taa páań ŋwiimpu boonaaa?

english_verse: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Míǹ mbaantiim ní mpèé ŋun bí man nì m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi kansikinee kaa làá kpìtī. An pu ní u-naantiibi kansikin ubɔ làá nīn pée sá ubɔti Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Míǹ mbaantiim ní bisaraaŋaliibi làá nīn pée bí Leefii dicaŋkun ki tūǹ m-tundi. Ubɔ kaa làá pée ŋmā kí pìin̄ nsan míǹ ń taa ŋá.

english_verse: and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
translation_verse: Unil kaa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee, kaa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ tiŋku gbandi bul. Míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá bùtī Daafiidi maaliŋun yab nì Leefii maaliŋun bin sá m-tɔntɔnliibee.» *

english_verse: The Lord also said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
translation_verse: «Aa gbìl̀ binib nín sòoǹ pueeee? Bi lì yii m dū Isirayeel nì Juuda, adican ali ŋin m lēēyee ki fá. Bi sòoǹ mimmee ní ki kpèé m-nibul fám. Bíǹ ceeyee, ŋaa ti kpáàa sá ditimbundi gba.

english_verse: Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands.
translation_verse: Tin man ni-Dindaan lēe sɔ̀. M ŋá mpèé nì ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. M síiǹ marab bin kpòotī kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋee.

english_verse: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_verse: Mimmee m ŋūǹ kí dū Jaakɔb dicaŋkun yab nì m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi maaliŋun yab kí fáaa? M ŋūǹ kí yíí kí taa lēē bin làá nīn kpòotī Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb nibuleeee? «Aayee, kpataaa! M làá sɔ̄ bi-saai ní kí fàtīí yàntī án bútí-bi.»

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me
