translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn bíi jáà nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee. U-janjakitil kɔkɔ nì kitiŋ pu beeŋi janjaliibi kɔkɔ nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí u-taapuee janjaliibi nìn kútì u-pu. Ŋyunti gbanti ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: to say to King Zedekiah: I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Cùú ká Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi kí tùkù-u yii man ni-Dindaan bí yii m làá dū kitiŋ nee kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan ú wà-kì ŋŋmi.

english_verse: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Sisee, aa làá ŋmátí kí nyā u-ŋaan. Bi làá cúú-si kí dū-si kí ŋá u-ŋaan. A làá cùú yūĺ u-nimbiin ní ní nīn sòoǹ ki kpèé tɔb. Míǹ boonee ní ú cáá-si kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin.

english_verse: You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
translation_verse: A làá kpú ŋgbansɔŋfin ní. Bi làá ŋá a-kpool kii bi nín ŋá a-naanjab bin nìn sá bibɔtiibi ki wāatì ní sii nín kpántì ubɔtee puee ní. Bi làá dāá tūū talaalub kí tīī-si jilma ní kí gāā-si icaalan yii: <Áù, ti-baa ubɔti kpíì!> Man a-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_verse: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii nìn dū an bɔtee ki nāatì Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured. The People Break a Promise
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee Babiloon bɔtiu nì u-janjakitil nìn bíi jáà nì Jeerusaleem nì u-timmu nì Juuda timmu mun bi nìn máń agun ki túee, múǹ di sá Lakiisi nì Aseeka timmu, ntimu muli gbanti di nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄. Juuda yab tīī iyumbu dibatɔl ki fātìi cúú-i

english_verse: King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
translation_verse: Niinee ní biyidambi kɔkɔ nì samaa kɔkɔ ŋá mpèé yii bi làá tīī bi-yumbui bininjab nì binimpoobi dibatɔl, kí taa ti yàntī bí tɔ̄ ditundi kii iyumbuee.

english_verse: But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Ama míǹ boonee ní bi kpántì nlandɔkɔ ki fātìi fōō iyumbu bininjab nì binimpoobi bin bi nìn tīī dibatɔlee, ki fātìi yāntì bi kpántì iyumbu.

english_verse: That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M nìn ŋá mpèé ŋubɔ nì ni-naanjab ŋyunti ŋun m nìn nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin laakin bi nìn bí ki sá iyumbuee.

english_verse: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Ama míǹ boonee ní ni kpántì nlandɔkɔ ki kpēē-mi fám. Báà ŋma fātìi cūtìi gíiǹní u-yumbuu uninja àá unimpu un u tīī dibatɔlee. Ni ŋá-bi mpɔn bí fàtīí kpántí ni-yumbui.»

english_verse: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Too, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. An bàà sá yii báà ŋma ń tīī u-yumbuu eebru niliu un sá u-nabiki nì u-jutee dibatɔl ní. Ama naa ŋá kii m nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. An pu ní man ni-Dindaan sòon̄ yii m làá cáań kujaau nì bìlbil kúm nì ŋkùm kí tɔ̄ ni-pu. Niinee kitiŋ pu beeŋi nib yaa láa ká mimmee, bi làá dāá kɔ́ dinyoondin.

english_verse: You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf.
translation_verse: «Binib gbanti nyáń mpèé ŋun bi ŋée boon. Baa ŋá kii bi nín yúl̀ m-nimbiin ki pōoǹ puee. M làá ŋá-bi kii dinabil din bi gíí ki nābitì mili ki cōom̀ ki jítì ajan alee kansikinee ní.

english_verse: These enemies are King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia and his army. They have stopped attacking Jerusalem, but they want to kill King Zedekiah and his high officials. So I will command them to return and attack again. This time they will conquer the city and burn it down, and they will capture Zedekiah and his officials. I will also let them destroy the towns of Judah, so that no one can live there any longer.
translation_verse: Ama m làá tīī-bi mara bí gítiń kí jáǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Bi làá fōō kitiŋ nee ní kí wà-kì ŋŋmi. M làá yàntī Juuda timmu ń kpántí kii kuteeuee ubɔ ń taa ti nín̄ kóò mu-ni.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yooyakiim sá Juuda bɔtiuee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
translation_verse: «Cùú ká Reekaab maaliŋun yab, kí sòoǹ nì bi, kí cáań-bi kunimbɔtidii dibiyaamu kiba poon. Niinee á tīī-bi ndaam bí nyɔ̀.»

english_verse: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m cūtìi nyàab̄ Yaasaniya, Irimeeya jipɔɔn Abasiniya naantiu nì u-nabiyaamu kɔkɔ nì u-jipɔmbi, an dàkà yii Reekaab maaliŋun yab kɔkɔ.

english_verse: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
translation_verse: M nìn cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidiin, Igidaliya jipɔɔn Anan, Unimbɔti niliu dibikin. Kidibiki gbanti nìn bí ki kɔ́ĺ abɔtibil dibiki, Saluum jipɔɔn Maaseeyawuu un sá usaraaŋal ki kpèé kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔkee yaka yilpu pú ní.

english_verse: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
translation_verse: M nìn dū aboon ŋin poon ndaam gbée nì tidayuti ki yóoǹ Reekaab maaliŋun yab nimbiin ní ki bí-bi yii: «Bàtīmaan ndaam kí nyɔ̀.»

english_verse: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
translation_verse: Ama ní bi kíí yii: «Taa nyù ndaam. Ti-naanja Yoonadaab, Reekaab jipɔɔn yóoǹ-ti mara yii: <Nimbi nì ni-naantiibi, ní taa pée nyɔ̀ ndaam dalba dalba.

english_verse: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
translation_verse: Ní taa mā adiin, kí taa kpɔ̀ tikpaal, kí taa cóoń fiinyi sufii, ní kí taa nín̄ cáá an wanti báà tiba. Ama ní nīn kóò tantibin ni-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon, ní kí ŋmā kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ni kóò kii binicambi nee pu kí yúntí.>»

english_verse: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar bíi jáà nì kitiŋ neeyee ní ti dākafì yii: <An sɔ́ tí sāǹ kí kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin Babiloon janjakitil nì Siirii janjakitil ń taa cúú-ti. Ŋyunti gbantee ní ti dɔ́miń ki kíǹ ki kóò kitiŋin doo.>»

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Cùú tùkù Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab yii: <Naa bàà máaǹ kí fōō m-bɔkpaafikaati kí pīlifì tin m sòoǹeeee?> Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
translation_verse: Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab tīī u-naantiibi mara yii bí taa pée nyɔ̀ ndaam, ní baa lafun nyùn̄ ndaam ki dāa sāā díǹ, kun puee bi tɔ́ bi-naanja marau. Ama man sòon̄ nì ni ki gíti sòon̄ nì ni ní naa pílifiǹ-mi.

english_verse: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
translation_verse: M túnní m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi ni-cee ŋfunyɔm kupaau kaa gbēeǹ bí tùkù-ni yii: <Báà ŋma ń dū u-saŋkiŋkpitil kí fá, kí ŋá min kítèe. Taa nín̄ jòó ki pámaan awaa boon ki tòotī-ŋi. Niinee ni làá ŋmā kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin m tīī ni nì ni-naanjabee poon.> Ama naa kpōoǹ ni-tafal ní kaa nín pílifì.

english_verse: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
translation_verse: Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab naantiibi ŋúb́ marab bin bi-naanja nìn yóoǹ-bee, ama ní man nibul kaa pílifiǹ man.

english_verse: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
translation_verse: «An puee ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá cáań inaabu in bɔti m nìn sòon̄ee kí tɔ̄ Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab pu. Di sá yii m sòon̄ nì bi, ama ní baa pílifiǹ-mi. M yíiń-bi, ama ní baa kíí-mi.>»

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Yeereemii bí Reekaab maaliŋun yab yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ni tɔ́ ni-naanja Yoonadaab marau, ki ŋúb́ tin kɔkɔ u tīī-ni mara ní ŋée.

english_verse: so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_verse: An puee Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab maaliŋun yab pée kpá kí lóó unil un làá nīn yú m-nimbiin ki tūǹ m-tundee.> «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee dee.»

english_verse: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Yooyakiim jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi nín kpántì Juuda bɔtiu dibinnanaatiil poonee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
translation_verse: «Yòon̄ kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋūǹ kí kpáb́ee. Á ŋmà ku-pu tibɔti tin kɔkɔ m yāntì a sòon̄ Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab nì atimbun kɔkɔ puee, kí yòon̄ ubɔti Joosiyaasi yuntiŋu tin m sòon̄ nì see kí dāá sāā díǹ nee.

english_verse: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
translation_verse: An yaa yíì Juuda yab yaa gbìl̄ inaabu in m bíi bɔ́ntí kí cáań kí tɔ̄ bi-puee, báà ŋma làá fá u-bimbikpitim. Niinee ní ḿ dū bi-yìntitam nì bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi.»

english_verse: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yeereemii yíiń Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki, ní ki kàan̄-u tibɔti tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì uee, ní Baruuki dūu ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋun.

english_verse: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii tùkū Baruuki yii: «Tiba cúú-mi, an puee man m-ba kaa làá ŋmā kí cù kunimbɔtidiin.

english_verse: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
translation_verse: Ama, sii làá cù dinyɔɔboobil wiiŋŋu dal, ní kí kàaǹ mpɔn ti-Dindaan bɔti tin m kàan̄-si a ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋunee. Á kàaǹ bin kɔkɔ bí kunimbɔtidiinee ń gbìl̄, ki kpáaǹ bin kɔkɔ nyánní Juuda timmun ki dɔ́mińee.

english_verse: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
translation_verse: An yaa yíì bi làá kíĺ kí nīn bíi gbàam̄ ti-Dindaan, ní báà ŋma ń fá u-bimbikpitim. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan bí yii u-ŋuukpaandi di dàn̄ dinibul nee pu.»

english_verse: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Geemariya jipɔɔn Miikayeewu, Safan naantiiu gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan bɔti tin kā kugbɔŋu poon Baruuki kàan̄ee.

english_verse: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u nín sìntī ubɔti beecindin ki bàn̄ ki kɔ́ ugbaŋŋmal tɔntɔndiikun. Bikàliŋkpilib kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì ki bí niin. Bin nìn bí niinee di sá ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Eelsama nì Seemayawuu jipɔɔn Deelaya nì Akibɔɔr jipɔɔn Eelnatan nì Safan jipɔɔn Geemariyawuu nì Ananiyawuu jipɔɔn Seedeesiyasi nì bikàliŋkpilib bin kɔkɔ kíǹee.

english_verse: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
translation_verse: Ní Miikayeewu dū tibɔti tin kɔkɔ Baruuki kàan̄ kugbɔŋu poon samaa kɔkɔ nimbiinee ki máafì-bi.

english_verse: Then the officials sent Jehudi and Shelemiah to tell Baruch, “Bring us that scroll.” When Baruch arrived with the scroll,
translation_verse: Niinee ní bikàliŋkpilibee dū Neetaniyawuu jipɔɔn Yeewuudi, Seeleemiyawuu naantiiu nì Kuusii naantitɔntɔkɔl ki tú Baruuki cee ú tùkù-u yii: «Dāan̄ kí kpáaǹ kugbɔŋu kun a kàan̄ samaa nimbiinee.» Niinee ní Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki yōoǹ kugbɔŋuee ki cūnnì bi-cee.

english_verse: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
translation_verse: U bàn̄ee ní bi bí-u yii: «Kàl̄ kí kàaǹ-ti tin kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee.» Ní Baruuki kàan̄ ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
translation_verse: Bi nín gbìl̄ tibɔti gbanti kɔkɔee, ní tifaandi kɔ́-bi. Bi nìn kíǹ ki kā ki fàtī ki kpèé tɔb, ní ki bí Baruuki yii: «See tí cáá tibɔti nee kɔkɔ kí māafì ubɔti.»

english_verse: “Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
translation_verse: Boonee ní bi bālifì Baruuki yii: «Māafì-ti a nín ŋá pu ki ŋúń ki ŋmàn̄ tibɔti nee kɔkɔee?»

english_verse: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
translation_verse: Ní Baruuki kíí-bi yii: «Yeereemii u-ba nyɔkɔn ní u kàan̄ tibɔti nee kɔkɔ, ní man dū ŋŋmamɔɔn ki ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee pu.»

english_verse: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bikàliŋkpilib bí Baruuki yii: «Si nì Yeereemii ń sāǹ kí báĺ. Ubɔ kaa máaǹ kí béé laakin ni bée!»

english_verse: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn tīī u-jipɔɔn Yeerameeyeel nì Asiriyeel jipɔɔn Seeraya nì Abideeyeel jipɔɔn Seeleemiyawuu mara yii bí cúú ugbaŋŋmal Baruuki nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii. Ama ní Unimbɔti dū-bi ki bál̀.

english_verse: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn dū kugbɔŋu kun poon Baruuki nìn ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin Yeereemii nìn kàan̄-uee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
translation_verse: «Cùú nyàab̀ kugbɔŋu kubɔ kí fàtīí ŋmà tibɔti tin kɔkɔ nìn ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔmpeepeekaau poon, Juuda yab bɔtiu Yooyakiim dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmee.

english_verse: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee á sòoǹ Juuda bɔtiu Yooyakiim pu yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: Yeereemii nìn ŋmàn̄ yii Babiloon bɔtiu làá dāan̄ kí nàan̄ kitiŋ nee kí kpɔ̀ binib nì tiwaŋkuti. Ama ní Yooyakiim wòon̄-u ní ki wùn̄ kugbɔŋuee ŋŋmi.

english_verse: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
translation_verse: Too, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Yooyakiim kpátam boonee, u-maaliŋu poon báà ubɔ kaa làá kàl̄ Daafiidi beejal pu. U yaa láa kpíìyee, bi làá dū-u kí fá mmɔŋki ní ŋwìiń ń gbá-u ŋwiimpu, ní nsɔnsɔm ń tɔ̄-u kunyeeu.

english_verse: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
translation_verse: M làá dáaĺ u nì u-maaliŋun yab nì u-kàliŋkpilib tafal ikpiti in bi ŋée pu. M làá cáań inaabu in bɔti m nìn sòon̄ baa pílifiǹ-mee kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda yab pu.>»

english_verse: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yeereemii nyàab̄ kugbɔmpɔŋ ki tīī ugbaŋŋmal Baruuki, Neeriya jipɔɔn, ní Yeereemii fātìi kàan̄-u tibɔti tin nìn kā kugbɔŋu kun Juuda bɔtiu Yooyakiim dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmee poonee. U nìn gíti kútì tibɔti tin náań nì tíǹ gbantee.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn dū Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Seedeesiyasi ki kāaǹ Juuda beel pu ubɔti. Seedeesiyasi di nìn fōō Yooyakiim jipɔɔn Kooniya yil.

english_verse: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn pílifì tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn dī Yeereemii pu ki kpáafì-bee. Ubɔti u-baaa, u-kàliŋkpilibaaa, Juuda yabaaa, ubɔ kaa nìn fōotì ki yīkiǹ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ní cùú tùkù Juuda bɔtiu un túnní-ni ní dāan̄ kí bàlifèe yii: Faaroo janjaliibi bin nìn nyáń ki tútúǹ-nee fātìi nín gítí bi-tiŋkin Eejipiti.

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Babiloon yab làá fàtīí gítiń kí dāá já nì kitiŋ nee. Bi làá fōō-kì kí wà-kì ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ní taa mɔ̄ntì ni-ba kí lì yii Babiloon yab yíkì ti-cee ki búntì. Baa búntì.

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Tí lì yii ni ŋúń ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Babiloon yab janjaliibi bin bí ki jáà nì nee kɔkɔ ní an kíǹ bin fōō tiweendee. Bíǹ gbanti làá nyānní bi-tantibin kí tūū kitiŋ nee ŋŋmi.>» Bi cúú Yeereemii ki pīiǹ kudii

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Ubɔti Faaroo janjaliibi pu ní Babiloon janjaliibi sútì ki wāatì Jeerusaleem tiŋki.

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: Yeereemii nìn là kí nyā Jeerusaleem tiŋkin kí cù Beenjameen tiŋkin kí fōō bi nín yākatì yākatì atinjan u-dicaŋkunee u-jandi.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Ama u nín bàn̄ Beenjameen tiŋki punyɔkɔpuee ní u ká bijanjaliibi bin cīití kipunyɔkɔee kpiliu ubɔ. Bi nìn yíì-u Yiiriya, u sá Seeleemiya jipɔɔn nì Ananiya naantiiu. Úǹ nìn cúú Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii ní ki bí-u yii: «A cáǹ a-ba kí tīī Babiloon yabaa!»

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii kíí-u yii: «Aayee, maa cáǹ m-ba kí tīī Babiloon yab.» Ama Yiiriya kaa nìn pīlifiǹ-u. U nìn cúú-u ki cáa cūnnì u-kpilib cee.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Dalbee ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi tú unil ú cùú cáań-u. U nìn là kí bàlifì-u tiba dibalin u-beecindin. Ubɔti nìn bālifì-u yii: «Mimmee ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì si tiba m-pu á tùkù-maaa?» Ní Yeereemii kíí yii: «Iiin! Bi làá dū-si kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan.»

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii gíti bí ubɔti Seedeesiyasi yii: «Ba ní m yīntiǹ sii nì a-kàliŋkpilib nì dinibul nee ní ni cúú-mi ki pīiǹ sarka ní?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Ni-bɔnaatiliibi nìn tùkū-ni yii Babiloon bɔtiu kaa làá dāan̄ kí já ni nì ni-tiŋki kujaau. Bibɔnaatiliibi gbanti bí la díǹ?»

english_verse: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii kútì ki lī yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-baa ubɔti, pīlifiǹ-mi. Yàntī m-gbaamii ń kɔ́-si fíŋfiŋ. Taa ti gíiǹ-mi a-gbaŋŋmaliu Yoonatan dumpu, yaa sá fám m làá kpú.»

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi tīī mara yii bí dū Yeereemii kí pìin̄ bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu kudii. Bí nīn tìì-u ŋwiin kamaa kikpɔnɔkatii. Bí nīn cāabìń kpɔnɔ gbanti kpɔnɔb bin bi kāntí bikpɔnɔpuliliibi daŋŋi puee kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní kpɔnɔ làá dóó kitiŋee nee. Míǹ ní Yeereemii nìn gbíntì bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu.

english_verse: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi kíí yii: «U bí ni-ŋaan, m sá ubɔti, ama maa cáá mpɔn kí pìin̄-ni nsan ni ŋá ni nín là puee.»

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: Bikàliŋkpilibee nìn cúú Yeereemii ki cáá-u ki tɔ́ ubɔti jipɔɔn Maalkiya nyimbɔbilin. Bi nìn dū iŋmii ní ki cúú Yeereemii ki cáa sīntì dinyimbɔbilin. Dinyimbɔbil gbanti nìn bí bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu ní, ama nnyim nìn kpá di-poon, asee tikpati. An puee bi nín nìn dū Yeereemii ki tɔ́ee, u nìn nín sìntī tikpatin ní.

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: «Ti-baa ubɔti, binib nee nín ŋá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii puee kaa ŋān̄. Bi dū-u ki tɔ́ dinyimbɔbilin. U làá kpú ŋkùm dinyimbɔbil gbantin, di sá yii tijin kaa ti bí kitiŋin.»

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Eebeedi-Meeleeki nìn yōoǹ bininjab mmuŋku nì saalaa. U nìn kɔ́ dibeecindin kudii kun bí kunimbikpaafidii taapuee. Niinee ní u yōoǹ ticaliŋkpun. U nìn dūu kúĺ iŋmii pu ki cáa lāaǹ Yeereemii dinyimbɔbilin.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: ) Bi nín jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋkee, tin jítèe sèé:

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ní bi dáaĺ iŋmiiyee ki nyántìń-u dinyimbɔbilin. Míǹ boonee ní Yeereemii gbíntì bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee cee. Ubɔti bíi sòoǹ nì Yeereemii dibalin

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti Seedeesiyasi nìn tú bi yíiń Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii, ní u cáá-u ki cūnnì kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki kitataatii poon. U nìn bí-u yii: «M làá bàlifì-si tibɔti, á taa báĺ-mi báà tiba.»

english_verse: “Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii kíí Seedeesiyasi yii: «M yaa tùkū-si ibaamɔn, a làá yàntī bí kpɔ̀-mi. M yaa tí tīī-si isaŋkaaa, aa làá dū-i kí tɔ̄ ditundi.»

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii bí Seedeesiyasi yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <A yaa nyáń ki dū a-ba ki tīī Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilibee, si nì a-dicaŋkun yab làá ŋmátí, ní baa làá wà Jeerusaleem tiŋki ŋŋmi.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Ama a yaa kaa nyáń ki dū a-ba ki tīī Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilibee, Jeerusaleem tiŋki làá kɔ́ Babiloon yab ŋaan. Bi làá sēē-kì ŋŋmi, ní siiyee, aa làá ŋmátí bi-ŋaan.>»

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti Seedeesiyasi bí Yeereemii yii: «M fàŋkí Juuda yab bin kɔ́ Babiloon yab ŋaanee. Babiloon yab ŋūǹ kí dū-mi kí ŋá bi-ŋaan bíǹ ń sàaǹ-mi.»

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Ama ní Yeereemii kíí-u yii: «Baa làá dū-si kí ŋá bi-ŋaan. Pīlifì tin ti-Dindaan dī m-pu ki sòon̄ nì see. A yaa ŋá míǹ, án làá nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī-si ní á ŋmátí.

english_verse: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
translation_verse: Ama a yaa yíì kaa cáá a-ba ki tīīyee, ti-Dindaan nín lēē tin làá bàń a-pu ki dàkā-mee sɔ̀.

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: Binimpoobi bin kɔkɔ kíǹ ki bí a-beecindinee, bi làá cúú-bi kí cùnnì kí tīī Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilib. Bi làá dāá gāā-si nlan yii: «<A-bɔɔmɔmmɔntiibi baasii kíil̀-si ní! A cáá a-taaŋi ki múĺ tikpatin, ní bíǹ sáǹ ki fá-si!>

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá cúú a-nimpoobi nì a-jipɔmbi kí cùnnì kí tīī Babiloon yab. Sii a-ba kaa làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā bi-ŋaan. Di sá yii Babiloon bɔtiu làá dāá cúú-si ní kí sēē a-tiŋki ŋŋmi.»

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi bí Yeereemii yii: «Ubɔ yaa pée gbìl̄ tibɔti nee, see m kūū-si.

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: Á kíí-bi yii: <M gbāam̀ ubɔti yii ú taa gíiǹ-mi Joonatan dumpu ḿ tin kpú niin.>»

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní bikàliŋkpilib kɔkɔ lafun dɔ́miń Yeereemii cee ki bālifì-u tibɔti. Ama Yeereemii kíí-bi kii ubɔti nín tīī-u mara yii ú kíí puee ní. Niinee ní bi yāntì-u soooo kaa ŋá-u tiba, kun puee báà ubɔ kaa gbìl̄ tin u nì ubɔti sòon̄ee.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Niinee Yeereemii gbíntì bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu ki tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun bi jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋkee. Babiloon yab jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki (Kpèè

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nì u-janjaliibi ká-bee ní bi dū itaaci. Kunyeeu ní bi nìn sáǹ ki nyáń Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Bi nìn dūu dī ubɔti kpaabun ki tin nyáń kipunyɔkɔ kin bí agun ali kansikinee ní ki fōō nsan ŋun cá Jɔɔdan tantakalinee.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: «Cùú tùkù ueetiiyoopiija Eebeedi-Meeleeki yii: <Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: M nìn sòon̄ yii an kaa sá nnaam ní m làá cáań kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem yab pu ama nnaabu. Too, m nín nìn sòon̄ puee, m làá ŋá míǹ. An kaa làá sūŋkì, sii a-ba nimbil làá ká.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: «Á cùú nyàab̀-u kí wúń u-pu ubɔ ń taa ŋá-u tikpitil tiba. U yaa bālifì-si tiŋyee, á ŋá míǹ kí tīī-u.»

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: Ama Babiloon janjaliibi nìn kùl̄ ki bīiǹ bi-boon, ní ki tin cúú Seedeesiyasi Jeeriikoo tantakalin. Bi nìn cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar cee, Riibila, Amati tiŋkin. Niin ní Neebukadineesaar sòon̄ Seedeesiyasi bɔti.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
translation_verse: Riibila niin ní Babiloon bɔtiu kūū Seedeesiyasi jipɔmbi bi-baa nimbilaaliyin ki kpáaǹ Juuda yab bɔtibiliŋ kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi sāā ki cɔ́tì Seedeesiyasi nimbiliŋ, ní ki dū tasa kúti kusakai ki bóob́-u ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Ní Babiloon yab tūū dibeecindi nì binib diiŋŋi ŋŋmi. Bi nìn gbáń ki wīī Jeerusaleem gundi.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nìn cúú binib bin nìn kíǹ ki kā Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋu. U nìn cáá bin nìn dū bi-ba ki tīī Babiloon bɔtiuee nì ŋŋal pu tɔntɔnliibi bin kíǹee ki cūnnì.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Ama u nìn yāntì bisoodambi nì bin kaa pée cáá tibee Juuda tiŋkin, ní ki nìn dū fiinyi kpaaŋŋi nì tisati ki yākatì-bi. Bi nyántì Yeereemii sarkan

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan:
translation_verse: Ubɔti Neebukadineesaar nìn tīī bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan mara Yeereemii pu yii:

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: Bi nìn tú binib bí cùú nyàabìń Yeereemii bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu. Bi nìn dū-u ki ŋúbiǹ Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu. Geedaliyasi nìn pú-u nsan ú kpì u-dumpu. Míǹ ní Yeereemii nìn gbíntì samaa kansikin ki kóò. Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tin Eebeedi-Meeleeki puee

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Yeereemii nìn dáá pīī bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔti dumpuee, ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì u yii:

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, m làá fīī a-maŋfal. Aa làá kpú kujaaun. Kun a làá páatée dee, kun puee a dū a-mákal ki páaǹ m-pu. Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.>»

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Yeereemii nìn bí binib bin bi nìn cúú Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmun kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee poon. Bi nìn bóob́ u mun ikusaka. Ama bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nìn nyántì-u bisarkadambee kansikin ní ki yāntì u búntì Raama tiŋkin.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Too, m làá bútí-si ikusaka in kā a-ŋaan nee díǹ. A yaa tí là kí nóó-mi tí cù Babiloon tiŋkinaaa, a ŋūǹ kí dāan̄, m làá wúń a-pu. Ama a yaa kaa tí là kí dāan̄aaa, á taa dāan̄. Kpèè, kitiŋ kɔkɔ di dɔ̄ a-nimbiinee, a ŋūǹ kí cù laakin a yaa lèe.»

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Niinee Yeereemii nín cá Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi cee Miisipa tiŋkin. U nìn kɔ́ binib bin nìn kíǹ ki kóò kitiŋee poonee kansikin. Juuda yab kóoǹ ki kpáfì Geedaliyasi cee (Kpèè

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Ní Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu bí bijanjakpilib nì bi-bijanjaliibi yii: «Taa fàŋkìmaan kí nīn bí Babiloon yab taapu. Kàl̄maan kitiŋ nee ni kí nīn tūǹ ditundi ki tìì Babiloon yab. Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, an làá nīn sɔ̀m̀ nì ni, man di tùkū-ni míǹ.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Man kā Miisipa tiŋkin doo nimbi yil pu Babiloon yab bin dòoń ti-ceeyee cee. Ama nimbee, ní kìtīmaan fiinyi biliŋ nì isufi in kíǹee biliŋ nì ŋkpam subiliŋ. Ní kpāafì ni-kpaajinti kí nīn kā ntimu mun poon ni kóòyee.»

english_verse: Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year. Gedaliah Is Murdered
translation_verse: Niinee ní Juuda yab kɔkɔ nyánní laakin bi nìn sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ee ki gítìń. Bi nìn dūu bāań Juuda tiŋkin Miisipa, Geedaliyasi cee. Bi nìn kītì niin fiinyi biliŋ nì asubil aba mun tikpil. Bi kūū Geedaliyasi (Kpèè

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Dalbee ní Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì ajanjakiti kpilib bin nìn bí tisatinee dɔ́miń ki ká Geedaliyasi Miisipa tiŋkin.

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: U nìn bí-u yii: «Mimmee aa nyí yii Amɔn yab bɔtiu Baliisi lēē Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel ú kpɔ̀-saaa?» Ama Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi kaa nìn fōō ki kíí.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nìn dɔ́miń Miisipa ki ká-u dibalin ní ki nìn bí-u yii: «Yàntī ḿ cù kí kpɔ̀ Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel dibalin. Ubɔ kaa làá béé. Àá a là yii úǹ nín kpɔ̀-si ní? U yaa kūū-see, Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bàà kóoǹ ki kpáfì a-ceeyee làá fàtīí tí yàl̄, ní tin bàà kíǹ Juuda beelinee ń wāŋkì.»

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Ama ní Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi kíí Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan yii: «Taa ŋá míǹ, kun puee tin a sòoǹ Isimaayeel pu nee kaa sá ibaamɔn.»

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Ama dibindi poon ŋmaluluútiuee ní Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel, Eeliisama naantiiu dɔ́miń Miisipa Geedaliyasi cee. Isimaayeel nìn sá ubɔti dicaŋkun niliu ní ki nìn sá ubɔti kàliŋkpilib ubɔ. U nì bininjab saalaa di nìn táá ki dɔ́miń. Ŋyunti ŋun bi kā u-cee ki jīǹee,

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: ní Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nì bininjab saalaa bin nóoń-uee yíkì dicilpu, ní ki dū bi-tàataajimmu ki gāatì ki kūū Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu. Unil un Babiloon bɔtiu nìn kāaǹ Juuda tiŋki pu gɔminee, bi nín kūū-u puee dee.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Isimaayeel kūū Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Geedaliyasi cee Miisipa tiŋkinee. U nìn kūū ki kpáaǹ Babiloon janjaliibi bin nìn bí niinee. Isimaayeel kūū bisaŋkinliibi imuŋku inaa

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Bi kūū Geedaliyasi iwiin ili jítì báà ubɔ kaa gbìl̄ u-kúm pu.

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nìn nyáń Miisipa tiŋkin ki túŋkì-bi nsanni ki sūǹ. U bàn̄ bi-ceeyee, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Dāam̄maan Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi cee.»

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun bi kɔ́ kitiŋinee ní Isimaayeel nì u-yab kūū-bi ní ki dū-bi ki tɔ́ dinyimbɔbil diban.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Bi-kansikinee binib saalaa nìn bí Isimaayeel yii: «Taa kpɔ̀-ti, di sá yii ti cáá bilee nì ɔɔji nì ŋkpam nì tisiil ki bál̀ tisatin.» Niinee ní Isimaayeel yāntì-bi kaa kūū-bi kii u nín kūū bi-jutiibi puee.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Dinyimbɔbil din poon Isimaayeel nìn dū binib bin u kūūyee nìn sá dinyimbɔbil din ubɔti Asaa nìn yāntì bi gbìn̄ ŋyunti ŋun u nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Basaa nìn bí kujaaunee ní. Dinyimbɔbilee nìn sá dikpaandi. Dinyimbɔbil gbantin ní Neetaniya jipɔɔn nìn dū binib bin u kūūyee ki gbéeǹ.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Isimaayeel cúú bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Miisipa tiŋkinee nì ubɔti sapɔmbi ki pīiǹ kudii. U nìn cúú bin kɔkɔ bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nìn dūu ŋúbiǹ Geedaliyasee. Míǹ boonee ní u kpáaǹ bisarkadambee ki búntì Amɔn yab cee. Bi fīī bin Isimaayeel cúú kuyuŋuee

english_verse: Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done.
translation_verse: Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì ajanjakiti kpilib bin nìn bí u-ceeyee gbìl̄ nnikpaakoon ŋun Neetaya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel ŋée.

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi kóoǹ bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì kí cùú jáǹ-u. Bi nìn jìn̄ ki tin cúú-u Gabawɔn puuku caŋin.

english_verse: When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy
translation_verse: Binib bin Isimaayeel nìn cúúyee nín ká Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib bin nìn nóó-uee, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Ama Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nín ká Yoowanan tóobiń-bee ní u sáǹ ki nín cá Amɔn yab cee.

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Niinee bijanjakpilib kɔkɔ, cilinjee Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì Oosaya jipɔɔn Asariya nì samaa kɔkɔ, bikpaambi nì ŋwaamu kɔkɔ cūtìi ká

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii. Bi nìn bí-u yii: «Ti gbàam̄-si, fōō tin ti là kí mèè-si nee: Gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu timbi bin ŋmátì ki kíǹ nee pu. Di sá yii taa ti náaǹ kii sii a-ba nín wāĺ pu nee.

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee bàlifì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ú dàkà-ti nsan ŋun sá tí dēe, nì kun ti máaǹ kí ŋée.»

english_verse: “All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii kíí-bi yii: «M gbìl̄, m làá mèè ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kii ni nín bālifì-mi puee. Míǹ boonee, m làá tùkù-ni ti-Dindaan nín kíí puee, maa làá báĺ-ni báà tiba.»

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says,
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí Yeereemii yii: «Ti pōoǹ kí ŋá tin ti-Dindaan làá tùkù-si á dūú nàatī-tee deedeedee. Ti-Dindaan ń nīn sá ibaamɔn seeradaaŋwu ki tīī-ti.

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Timbi di tú-si á bàlifì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu. Tin u yaa lēe yaa ŋān̄aaa, an yaa kaa ŋān̄aaa, ti làá ŋá míǹ. Niinee, án làá nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī-ti, di sá yii ti làá pīlifì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ.»

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Iwiin saalaa boonee, ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii.

english_verse: Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together
translation_verse: Niinee ní u yíiń Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib bin nìn bí u-ceeyee, nì samaa kɔkɔ, bikpaambi nì ŋwaamu.

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: U nìn bí-bi yii: «Ni lēē-mi yii ḿ mèè ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ni-pu. U nín lī puee sèé:

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: «<Ni yaa kíí kí nīn kā kitiŋ nee poonee, maa ti làá nàan̄-kì, ama m làá mā m-nibul. M làá cóoń-ni kii bi nín cōontí busubu puee, maa ti làá cóotí-ni dalba dalba. M làá ŋāŋkì tikpitil tin kɔkɔ m ŋá-nee.

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī ní ká diyimɔɔl u-cee, ní ú sɔ̄ ni-saai, kí yàntī ní gítiń ni-tiŋki pu.>»

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa bí yii: «Taa làá kàl̄ kitiŋ nee poon! ní ki yíì kaa pílifì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ»,

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee nimbi Juuda yab bin kíǹee, ní pīlifì ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ni yaa gbíntìi cɔ́ yii ni làá cù Eejipiti, ni yaa lafun sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ niinee,

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ làá lēē kí cùú nīn kóò Eejipiti tiŋkinee, kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm di làá kpɔ̀-bi. Báà ubɔ kaa làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā nnaabu ŋun m làá dāá dūú tɔ̄ bi-puee ni.

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii gíti bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M kpáatì m-ŋuul nì mbum ki pɔ̀l̄ Jeerusaleem yab pu. Míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá dāá kpáatí m-ŋuul nì mbum kí pɔ̀l̄ nimbi bin làá cùú kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee pu. Niinee bi yaa làá dāá tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu àá kí sòoǹ kubɔbiiu kubɔ pu àá tibɔti tin cáá tifaandee pu àá kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icooyee, bíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika. Ni pée gíti kpá kí ká kitiŋ nee.>»

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii kútì ki lī yii: «Nimbi Juuda nibul din kíǹee, m bíi kpáafí-ni díǹ. Ti-Dindaan di bíi tìì-ni mara yii ní taa cù Eejipiti, ní béé míǹ.

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: Ni tīī-mi ditundi yii ḿ bàlifì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dibalifil. Ni bí-mi yii: <Mèè ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kí tīī-ti. Tùkù-ti tin kɔkɔ u làá tùkù-see, ti làá ŋá míǹ.> Ŋwiin gbantee, an nìn sá nì bugbambu ní ni sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Di sá yii díǹ nee, m bíi tùkù-ni tin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kíí-nee. Ama naa bíi pílifí tin ti-Dindaan dī m-pu ki sòon̄ee.

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Oosaya jipɔɔn Asariya nì Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bilambidambi gbanti kɔkɔ bí Yeereemii yii: «A mɔ́ntí ní! Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kaa pée tùkū-si á nàatī-ti yii: <Ní taa cù Eejipiti tiŋkin kí kàl̄.>

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: An sá Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki di bíi sàal̄-si á sòoǹ ti-pu míǹ. Di sá yii u là kí dū-ti kí ŋá Babiloon yab ŋaan bíǹ ń kpɔ̀-ti, àá kí cúú-ti kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋu ní.»

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: An puee Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib nì samaa un nìn dī-bee nìn yíì kaa pílifì ti-Dindaan kí kàl̄ Juuda tiŋkin.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Niinee Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib yōoǹ Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ kíǹee. Bíǹ di nìn sá bin nìn yàl̄ ki bíń ntimu kɔkɔn ki fātìi gítìń Juuda tiŋkinee.

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: Bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu nì ubɔti bisalib nì binib bin kɔkɔ bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nìn dūu kāaǹ Juuda tiŋkin Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu ń nīn kpèéyee. Bi nìn kpáaǹ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii nì Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki.

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: Bi nìn yíì kaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan nín lī puee. Bi nìn yíkì ki búntì Eejipiti tiŋkin, ki dūu bàn̄ Tapaneesi. Yeereemii nāatì yii Neebukadineesaar làá fōō Eejipiti

english_verse: when the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Tapaneesi tiŋkin niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: «Yòon̄ ataŋkpakpaan kí gbà kí síb́ kasarka un bí Eejipiti bɔtiu beecindi nyɔkɔpu Tapaneesee. Á ŋá míǹ Juuda yab nimbilaaliyin.»

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u bí-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá tɔ̄ bí cùú nyàabìń m-tɔntɔnliu Neebukadineesaar, Babiloon bɔtiu. M làá dū u-beejal kí tɔ́kɔń ataŋkpee ŋin a síb́ nee pu ní. Niin ní u làá cóoń u-beecindi tantiu.

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti ú dūú nàatī Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ nìn cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkin, ki bí Miigidool nì Tapaneesi nì Meemifiisi nì bin kóò Patroosi tinjaaŋŋinee.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Ni ká inaabu in kɔkɔ m cáań ki tɔ́ Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee puee. Díǹ pu nee, ntimu gbanti kpántì adigbun, ní báà uniseen kaa ti kóò mu-poon.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: M túnní m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ ni-cee kaa gbēeǹ. Bi nìn bí-ni yii: <Ní taa tɔ̄ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin m ná nee.>

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m kpáatì m-bum nì m-ŋuul ki sītì ni-pu, ní an wùn̄ Juuda timmu nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi kii ŋŋmee. Ntimu gbanti kpántì adigbun ŋma nì kuteeu kii ni nín wāĺ an bí pu díǹ nee ní.>»

english_verse: Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies.
translation_verse: Ní Yeereemii nìkī ki lī yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ba pu ní ni bíi kɔ̄ntí ni-ba agìŋ́kpaan poon míǹ? Ni là kí kúntí Juuda nibulin, bininjab nì binimpoobi nì binipɔmbi nì mbipɔmu níii? Naa pée là ni-kansikin biba ń kíń níii?

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ni-tuuŋŋi gbítí m-ŋuul. Ni tùutī talaalub ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì Eejipiti tiŋki kin ni cūtìi kɔ́ee waaŋi. Ni baasii là kí kúntí ni-ba, kí kpántí mbusu nì icoo ŋabikau kí tīī duulinya timbuŋŋi kɔkɔ níii?

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Ni súntì ikpiti in bi ŋá Juuda tiŋkin nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pueeee? Ni-naanjab nì Juuda bɔtiibi nì bi-nimpoobi nì nimbi ni-ba nì ni-nimpoobi di ŋá ikpiti gbanti.

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Áli nì díǹ, an kaa ŋá ubɔ nyàaa yii u ŋá tiba. Naa fāŋkì-mi, kaa tɔ́ m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin m tīī ni nì ni-naanjabee.>»

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: M làá kpèè Juuda yab bin kíǹ ki cūtìi kóò Eejipiti tiŋkinee bɔti. Bi-kɔkɔ làá kpú ní. Kitiŋ gbantin ní kujaau àá ŋkùm làá kpɔ̀ bi-kɔkɔ, ŋwaamu nì bikpaambi. Míǹ ní bi làá kpú ní bi yaa làá dāá tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu àá kí sòoǹ kubɔbiiu kubɔ pu àá tibɔti tin cáá tifaandee pu àá kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icooyee, bíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: M làá jáǹ bin cūtìi kóò Eejipiti tiŋkinee, kii m nín jáń nì Jeerusaleem yab puee. M làá dū kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm kí tɔ̄ bi-pu.

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Juuda yab bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin, ní ki dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ubɔ kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí kí nyā ŋkúm ŋaan. Ubɔ kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí gítiń Juuda tiŋki kin bi bàà cáá nlandɔkɔ kí gítiń kí kàl̄ee poon. Baa làá dāá ŋmā kí gítiń, asee bikaaŋkaabi bin làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā ŋkúm ŋaanee.>» Juuda yab ŋá saraabi ki tīī yilpu Nimpubɔtiu

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Bininjab bin kɔkɔ nìn nyí yii bi-nimpoobi ŋáań saraabi ki tìì awaayee nì binimpoobi bin kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki dūu ŋá dikitikpaandee, an dàkà yii bin kɔkɔ nìn cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkin Patroosee nìn kíí Yeereemii yii:

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: «Nì min kɔkɔ an sá ti-Dindaan yindi pu ní a sòoǹ nì tee, taa làá pīlifiǹ-si.

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Ti làá nīn nìkì ki ŋáań ti nín lēē yii ti làá ŋá puee. Ti làá nīn tùutī talaalutuukaabi ki tìì diwaal Asitaartee, yilpu Nimpubɔtiu ní kí fá-u ndaam. Timbi nìn pée ŋáań míǹ ní, ki kpáaǹ ti-naanjab nì ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-kàliŋkpilib Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu. Ti nín nìn ŋáań mimmee, ti nìn kāntí ki jīǹ ní, ní an nìn bútì-ti ní taa nìn nyí kun bi yíì nnaabuee.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Ama kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun ti gbēeǹ kaa ti tùutī talaalub ki tìì diwaal yilpu Nimpubɔtiu, kaa ti féeń-dì ndaamee, ti lóò tikɔkɔ, ní kujaau nì ŋkùm bíi kù-ti»

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Ní binimpoobi gíti lī yii: «Ti nín nìn tùutī talaalub ki tìì diwaal yilpu Nimpubɔtiu ki féeń-dì nnyimee, ti-calib kaa nìn nyáaa? Ti yaa nìn ŋáań kalaabi bin náań nì dèe ki féeń-dì ndaamee, bi nìn nyáaa!»

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: «An sá tiŋman, ni nì ni-baabi nì ni-bɔtiibi nì ni-kàliŋkpilib nì Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ kíǹee nìn tùutī talaalub Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu. Ti-Dindaan dáá gbíntìi téetí an pu, waa súntì.

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: Ama ní ti-Dindaan gīī nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin ni ŋáańee. An pu ní ni-tiŋki kpántì adigbun, mpaan ŋun kíǹ ki fàantée, ní binib kaa ti kóò niin. Ni-tiŋki gbanti di kpántì ŋabika bi cáa tòó mbusu, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nee ní.

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Kun pu nnaabu gbanti jéetì ni-puee di sá yii ni tūutì talaalub ki tīī awaa ki yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan. Naa pílifiǹ-u ní kaa nóó u-dàkatam nì u-marab nì u-saŋkii, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nan ní.»

english_verse: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ni nì ni-nimpoobi, ni lī yii: <Ti pōoǹ yii ti làá nīn tùutī talaalub ki tìì diwaal yilpu Nimpubɔtiu ki féeń-dì ndaam. Ti nín pōoǹ puee, míǹ ní ti làá ŋá!> Too, nín̄ ŋúb́ ni-pooŋyi, ŋámaan ni nín pōoǹ puee.

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: Nimbi Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ní pīlifì tin man ni-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ nì ni nee tiŋan: Man ni-Dindaan, m pūtì m-yiŋkpaandi yii ujuudanil ubɔ pée gíti kpá kí pùtī kí yíiń m-yindi Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔn. Ubɔ gíti kpá kí lì yii: <Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee.>

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Kun m làá nyàab̀ kí cáań kí tɔ̄ ni-puee, an kaa làá nīn sá nnaam, ama nnaabu ní. Kujaau nì ŋkùm di làá kpɔ̀ Juuda yab bin cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Báà uniseen kaa làá kíń.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Bi-kansikin binikaaŋkaabi di làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā kujaaun. Bi làá dāá nyānní Eejipiti kí gítiń Juuda tiŋkin. Niinee Juuda yab bin kíǹ ki sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee làá béé man nì bíǹ un di cáá mbaamɔnee.

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: M dū Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi ki ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar un nìn nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-uee ŋaan. Too, míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá dū Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo Oofiraa kí ŋá u-nannanliibi bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-uee ŋáań. Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee dee.>»

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
translation_verse: Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yoowakiim nín kāl̀ Juuda beel pu tibɔtiil dibinnanaatiilee ní Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu kàan̄-uee ki ŋá kugbɔŋun. Dibindi gbantee, Yeereemii nín nìn tùkū Baruuki tibɔti tiŋyee sèé:

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ tin sii Baruuki puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: A lì yii: <Man bɔlii na! M nìn pée bí falaa poon ní ti-Dindaan gíti dū kunimbaau ki kútì-mi. M yáliŋkì ki tin gīī, kaa kpáà ká diŋuŋfil.>

english_verse: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
translation_verse: Too, ti-Dindaan nín tùkū-mi tin ḿ dūú nàatī-see sèé: <M làá gbá kí kpìtī tin m nìn máńee, m làá fùkù tin m nìn cóoǹee. M làá ŋá míǹ ntimu kɔkɔn.

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ní siiyee, a nyàab̀ kí tɔ̄ atuŋkpaan. Taa ti pée bàlifì tiba! Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan, m nín sòon̄ puee sèé: M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ tin kɔkɔ cáá kufoouee pu. Ama siiyee, dimaŋfal ní m làá tīī-si án nīn sá a-paati, laakin kamaa a làá cùee.>»

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Yeereemii atimbun pu puee sɔ̀. Bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eejipiti yab Kaarkeemiisi

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: U sòon̄ Eejipiti tiŋki nì Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo Neekoo janjakitil pu. Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yooyakiim nín kpántì Juuda bɔtiu dibinnanaatiilee, Eejipiti bɔtiu nìn bí Kaarkeemiisi, Eefiraati mɔɔgbandi. Ŋyunti gbantee, Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-u.

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: Bijanjakpilib nìn kūuntí yii: «Bɔ́ntímaan agbampɔɔ akpaan nì ŋwaamu. Ní cùú jámaan kujaau.

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: Ní kpàl̄maan itaamu! Bitanjakaliibi, máĺmaan ni-taamui! Dūmaan ni-janjafuulimmu kí cíkiń! Ní páaḿmaan ipɔ̀n pu! Bɔ́ntímaan ni-kpammu! Dūmaan ni-gbampɔɔŋi kí pèen̄!»

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Un ŋūǹ ki yáb̀ee kaa ŋúń ki sáǹ ki ŋmátì, ubaatandaan kaa ŋūǹ kí fīī u-ba. Ŋgan pú Eefiraati mɔɔgbaŋŋee, bi gbéetì ki lítì.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: «Ŋma náań nì Niil mɔɔl din gbée, a lì kii dimɔɔl din nyim gbí ki páaǹee?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: An sá Eejipiti di jɔ́ḿ kii Niil mɔɔlee. Kì nìn lì yii: <Kii Niil mɔɔl nín gbí puee, a lì kii di-nyim nín gbí ki páaǹ puee, míǹ ní m làá gbí kí léeń kitiŋ pu ní kí nàan̄ kitiŋ kí kpáaǹ mu-timmu.

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Itaamu, kpàtīí líímaan! Janjatɔrɔkub, dūmaan ni-yil kí bɔ̄! Bijanjaliibi ń dū bi-ba kí bíĺ, an dàkà yii Eetiiyoopii yab nì Puuti yab, bin tūntí agbampɔɔyee nì Luudi yab bin bàl̀ abaatanee!

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Atimbun gbìl̄ a-cooi pu, bi gbìl̀ a-yaliŋkii pu an kɔkɔ pu. Di sá yii ubaatandaan kpéetì ubaatandaan, ní bi-liitil gbéetì ki lítì dicilpu.>» Neebukadineesaar lúuń Eejipiti tiŋki

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: «Ní bāakì tibɔtee Eejipiti tiŋkin, ní yàntī bí gbìl̄-tì Miigidool tiŋkin, bí gbìl̄-tì Meemifiisi nì Tapaneesi timmun. Lìmaan yii: Yīkìí yūĺmaan kí bɔ́ntí ni-ba, di sá yii kujaau bíi nà ni-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb.

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní a-waal din sá unajee lítì kaa ŋúń ki yúl̀ ní? Ti-Dindaan nín kpìb̄-dèe,

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: dì kpīntì ní ŋkpitim pu. Bijanjaliibi lítì ki dɔ̄ tɔb pu. Bi lì tɔb cee yii: <Tí yīkì kí kpì ti-tiŋkin kí sāǹ kí wàatī kujaau kun nàantí nee.

english_verse: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
translation_verse: Diyindi din bi làá pɔ̄ Eejipiti bɔtiu Faarooyee sɔ̀. Kufuu, kufuu, ama kufuu fám!

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: «Ubɔti un bi yíì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaanee nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M pūtì m-ba maŋfal yii unannanli làá dāan̄.> Kii Tabɔɔr nín sá dijool ní Kaarmeel jool bí tiŋku caŋinee, míǹ ní u làá dāan̄.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: «Eejipiti yab, bɔ́ntímaan ni-wanti kí nīn cá kuyuŋu. Meemifiisi tiŋki làá kpántí kuteeu. Bi làá nàan̄-kì ní báà uniseen kaa ti làá nīn kóò ki-ni.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: «Eejipiti nìn sá unasal un ŋān̄ee ní! Ama dinaagandi diba nyánní ŋgan pú ki dɔ́miń ki báaǹ u-pu.

english_verse: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
translation_verse: Bijanjaliibi bin kì nìn dée nìn bí ní màlmal kii dinajapɔmbilee. Ama bi mun fātì bi-boon ki tīī-kì, bi-kɔkɔ sáǹ dicilpu, baa ŋúń ki yúl̀. Di sá yii nnaabu wiiŋŋu dòoń bi-pu, ŋwiin ŋun m làá dáaĺ bi-tafalee.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: Binannanliibi fāā mɔ̀ɔɔ ki dòoń kí léeń Eejipiti tiŋki pu kii bidɔgaaliibi di ŋúb́ ncɔkɔmu kí dāá gāā isufee. Niinee Eejipiti yab janjaliibi sáń kii ukoobu nín sáń pu kaa ŋáań kuwoouee ní.

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Bi bíi gà ki-bambaŋku, kubambaŋŋu kun poon ubɔ kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ee. Di sá yii bi nìn wīikí ki jítiǹ inaakitoon, ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ-bi.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Icoo kɔ́ Eejipiti kitinnyanyaaŋŋi, bi dū-kì ki ŋá ŋgan pú nibuliŋ ŋaan.>»

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu bí yii: «M làá dáaĺ Tabeesi yab waal Amɔn nì Eejipiti yab nì bi-waaŋi nì bi-bɔtiibi ní Faaroo nì bin kɔkɔ máká u-puee tafal.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: M làá dū-bi kí ŋá bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-bee ŋaan, an dàkà yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nì u-janjaliibi ŋaan. «Ama boonee, binib làá dāá fàtīí kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋki kii dooooyee.» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ. Ti-Dindaan làá fīī Isirayeel yab (Kpèè Yeer

english_verse: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
translation_verse: «Sii m-tɔntɔnliu Jaakɔb, taa fàŋkì, Isirayeel, taa yàntī a-pɔbil ń bīil̀. M làá fīī-si kí nyāntí ntindandatimun, ní kí gíiǹní a-biyaamu mun bí kuyuŋunee. Jaakɔb, a làá fàtīí gítiń nì dimákal kí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti páb̀-si.

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Sii Jaakɔb m-tɔntɔnliu, taa fàŋkì. Man a-Dindaan di lī yii m bí a-cee. M làá kúntí atimbun ŋin poon m nìn jìn̄-si a yàl̄ ki kɔ́ee. Ama siiyee, maa làá kúntí-si. An sá tiŋman yii m dáaĺ a-tafal, ama an sá kí sāŋkì-si ní. Di sá yii maa ŋūǹ kí yàntī-si kii a sá maanyiibee.»

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii Fiiliistii yab pu. An nìn sá kí wàatī Faaroo ń já nì Gaasaa yabee ní.

english_verse: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Tinyiŋgbaŋkpaandi nyánní ŋgan pú. Tì kpántì mbuŋkpaan ki gbí ki páaǹ. Tì gbí ki léeǹ kitiŋee nì tin kɔkɔ bí ki-poonee, ntimu nì mu-nib pu. Binib gbáà ibiil ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi, kitiŋee nib bíi gà ikpiisilan.

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̀ itaamu tagbíŋŋi pu. Janjatɔrɔkub wàkalìń, bi-taaŋi ŋáań kuwookpaaŋŋu. Bibaatiibi kaa ti wāĺ bi-biyaamu, bi-ŋalii kpíì.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋwiin di bāań bí nàan̄ Fiiliistii yab. Ubɔ kaa ti bí kí tūtuǹ Tiir nì Siidɔn timmu. Án taa kíń báà uniseen. Ti-Dindaan bíi nàantí Fiiliistii yab kɔkɔ, bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin Kafitoor tiŋki kin nnyim māntìi túee poonee.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Gaasaa yab kōol̀ abaakpan! Asikeelɔn yab ŋmíl̀ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ díkí diki. Nimbi tijawɔkɔl tin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee, ni làá nīn cáá njimu ki gífí ni-wunti pu yéè kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: Ni lì yii: <Abàa, ti-Dindaan tàataajiki, kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá ŋùŋfì ní? Kɔ́ a-jitookun! Kàl̄ niin soooo!>

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Mana ní kì ŋūǹ kí ŋùŋfì? Ti-Dindaan tīī-kì mara yii kí cù áli Asikeelɔn nì tiŋku gbandi. U nín síiǹ-kì kí ŋá puee dee.»

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ Moowaab pu puee sèé: «Ba naabuŋu di jéetì Neeboo tiŋki pu míǹ? Bi nāaǹ-kì múb! Icoo cúú Kiiriyatayiim tiŋki, bi jáń ki fōō-kì! Kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee, ba cooi íǹ bulifi dee, kì lítì.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Kun nìn sá Moowaab nyootee kúntì. Binib bɔ́ntì kí cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ Eesbɔn tiŋki pu ki lì yii: <Tí cùmaan kí kúntí kitiŋ nee atimbun kansikin!> Si mun Madimeeni, bi làá pée nàan̄-si ní, kujaau jìn̄ ki cúú-si dee.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̀ ibiil pu doooo Ooroonayiim tiŋkin yii: <Bi nāaǹ tikɔkɔ. Ba naabukpaaŋŋu ŋúǹ dee!>

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Bi wīī Moowaab tiŋki. Bi gbìl̀ ki-biyaamu biilii pu.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Binib dàb̀ Luwiiti gbantaŋki ki sūǹ. A yaa sìntī Ooroonayiimee, a gbìl̀ kunimbaau biilii pu.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Sām̀maan kí fīī ni-ba! Ní gbíntí kuteeun kii kumooun maŋkee.

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Moowaab, a nìn máká a-tuuŋŋi nì a-gaajati pu ní. Ama bi làá já kí fōō si mun. Bi làá cúú a-waal Keemoosi nì a-tandambi nì a-kpilib kí cùnnì kuyuŋu dicilpu.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: Un nàantí tikɔkɔee làá yìiǹ ntimu kɔkɔn, waa làá súntí báà kibaba pu. Bi làá nàan̄ ditantakal, ní kí bīil̀ laakin tɔ́kɔ́ee,» kii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ pu ki síiǹee.

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: Tīīmaan Moowaab tiŋki ifeen, kí ŋmā kí yīkì kí ŋàaǹ! Ki-timmu làá kpántí kuteeu ubɔ kaa ti làá nīn kóò mu-ni.

english_verse: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
translation_verse: An sá mbusu ní ki tīī un tūǹ ti-Dindaan tundi nì bugbambuee. Mbusu sá ki tīī un kaa là fatiku ń táká u-tàataajikee. *

english_verse: Moab, you are like wine left to settle undisturbed, never poured from jar to jar. And so, your nation continues to prosper and improve.
translation_verse: Doooo Moowaab biyatin ní u bí ŋgbansɔŋfin. Baa cúú-u ki cūnnì kuyuŋu ki ká. U nìn pée dɔ̄ soooo kii ndaam min baa tóoń ki lēē tidacaal, kaa kpáatì-mì ki ŋá dibool diban ki kpáal̀ee ní. An puee ní u-mɔŋŋu nì u-sɔnsɔfiŋu kaa kpántì.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá nīn cáá diwaal Keemoosi pu icoo. Kii Isirayeel yab nín nìn cáá diwaal Beeteel din pu bi nìn mákée pu puee.

english_verse: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
translation_verse: «Moowaab yab, mana ní ni ŋūǹ kí lì yii: <Ti sá bibaatandambi, bijanjaliibi bimɔmmɔntiibi.>

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Bi nāaǹ Moowaab tiŋki, bi dàb̄ kí jáǹ ki-timmu. Bi cúú ki-nipɔmbi bin cáá laafiyee ki cáǹ kí kpɔ̀.» Ubɔti un bi yíì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaanee di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: An kaa làá sūŋkì, bi làá nàan̄ Moowaab tiŋki, nnaabu làá jēetí ki-pu kpalaa.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: Nimbi ki-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb bin nyí-kì tiŋanee, ní cùú ŋámaan-kì fɔ̀ɔ́. Baa! Mpɔn ŋun kaa cáá juti nee, mbɔtikpandɔ ŋun cáá tinyool nee cúu kɔ́fàa! *

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: Diibɔn nibul, kpákatí a-nyooti beejal pu, kí dāá kàl̄ titampummool pu. Un nāaǹ Moowaab tiŋkee dòoń kí já nì si, u bíi wìil̄ digundi din māntìi tú-see.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Arooweer nibul, cùú yūĺ didandi pu kí nīn cɔ́ŋkí ki kpèé. Ní bàlifì bin sáń kí ŋmátée yii: «Ba di ŋá ní?»

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Bi làá kíí yii: Bi nàn̄ Moowaab tiŋki dúsi dusi! An puee icoo kɔ́-kì. Ní fáámaan ibiil bí jòò-ni. Ní bāakìmaan Arinɔn buŋgbandi pu yii bi nāaǹ Moowaab tiŋki.

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: Ditafadaaldi lítì ditantakal timmu pu nì Oolɔn nì Yaasa nì Meefaati

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: «Moowaab pɔŋŋu wáŋkì, u-kpabil kɔ́fì», ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
