english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: Moowaab dākafì yii u sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ ti-Dindaan ní! Bí nyùntī-u ndaam ú gbí áli kí wùliŋkì. Ŋyunti bāań bí bèel̀ u mun dee!

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: Moowaab yab, yīkìí fámaan ni-timmu. Ní cùú nīn kóòmaan itaŋkpalɔkɔn! Nín̄ bímaan kii dibeenanjilee. Di pāantí di-diiku nsitim watil pú laakin unil kaa ŋūǹ kí bèe ní. *

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: An pu ní m bíi yáliŋkí Moowaab pu. M gbáà ibiil bí jòò Moowaab tiŋki kɔkɔ. M bíi tíminsí Kiiri-Eereesi yab pu.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: M sūǹ sii Sibima nibul pu ki jítiǹ Yaseer yab nín sūǹ a-pu puee. A nìn sá kii fiinyi subuee ní. A nìn tɔ́ apan an lákatì Ŋyaam mɔɔl pu, ŋi nìn lālim̀ ki tin bàn̄ Yaseer tiŋki. Ama unàanli páatìi jéetì a-fiinyi biliŋ nì a-kpaajinti pu.

english_verse: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
translation_verse: Ifaal nì dipɔɔpindi kúntì asubiŋmɔkaa kpaaŋŋi nì Moowaab tiŋkin. Ndaam dóò tilɔn poon, bininjab bin tà ki fɔ́bití fiinyi biliŋ ki nyāntí ndaamee kaa ti bí. Dipɔɔpindi kuŋkuuntii kúntì.

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: Eesbɔn yab bíi gbáà ibiil bí jòò-bi. Bi gbìl̀ bi-pu Eeleeyalee nì Yaasa, ní kí yòon̄ Soowaar kí tin sāā Ooroonayiim nì Eegilati-Seelisiya. Áli gba Niimriim buŋŋu fóotì.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá kúntí Moowaab tiŋkin bin di cá ŋgbantamu pu ki ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki tùutī talaalub ki tìì awaayee.»

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: M bí ki sūǹ Moowaab yab nì Kiiri-Eeseesi yab pu. M-yaliŋkii bí kii kiwulii nín sūǹ puee ní, kun puee tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ bi nìn kóoǹ ki kpúkuǹee wáŋkì.

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Moowaab diiŋŋi yilpu bi nín bɔ̀b̄ puee nì kpacantib kɔkɔ puee, bi gbìl̀ ikpiisilan pu ní. «M wīī Moowaab kii bi nín wìil̄ dibool din kaa ti bí tibanee puee ní.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Baa! Bi nùkū Moowaab tiŋki púb! Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan! Moowaab sáǹ ki kátì, ba cooi dee! Ki-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb kɔkɔ bèel̄-kì ní kì kɔ́ dinyoondin. *

english_verse: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Binannanliibi kpántì kii kaajiikuee ki ŋàaǹ ki kpátí u-feeŋyi Moowaab tiŋki pu.»

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: Bi jáń ki fōō ntimu, ki gbáń ki wīī sintil difɔkɔŋi. Yaadalee, Moowaab baatandambi fāŋkì kii unimpu un kā imatiŋween puee ní.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi nāaǹ Moowaab tiŋki, an kaa ti sá dinibul. U nìn dākafì yii u sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ ti-Dindaan ní.

english_verse: Terror, pits, and traps are waiting for you.
translation_verse: Dinyoondi nì mbòó nì kulaaŋŋu dɔ̄ ki cí nimbi Moowaab yab. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Un yaa láa bíi sáń dinyoondee làá dāá jēetí mboon. Un yaa láa nyáń mboonee làá cùú kɔ́ kulaaŋŋun. Tiŋman, dibindi din m làá dāá dáaĺ bi-tafalee, m làá dāá yàntī tíǹ gbanti ń jēetí Moowaab yab pu. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: Bin bíi sáńee kaa ti cáá mpɔn. Bi sáǹ ki kɔ́ Eesbɔn tiŋkin. Ama ŋŋmi ŋubɔ nyánní Eesbɔn tiŋkin, Siiwɔn bɔtiu beecindin. Ŋu dɔ́miń ki wùn̄ dinibul din cáá kufuu nee tiŋki kí yòon̄ ki-kpaanyɔkɔ kí cáá sāā ki-kansikin.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Moowaab, an sá nnaabu ní ki tīī-si! Keemoosi nibul, an dóò a-pu dee! Bi cúú a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib ki cūnnì kuyuŋu.

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Amɔn yab pu. Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Ba pu ní diwaal Mooleeki jíń Gaadi tiŋki mpaan míǹ? Ba pu ní Amɔn yab fōō Isirayeel timmu míǹ? Isirayeel kaa cáá jipɔɔn un làá fōō ntimu gbanti difakaleeee?»

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: An puee ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Iwiin iba bí ki dòoń m làá yàntī bí gbìl̄ Amɔn yab tiŋyil Raaba poon ijanjakuŋkuunti. Kitiŋ gbanti làá dāá kpántí adigbun, bi làá wà ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe ŋŋmi. Ŋyunti gbantee Isirayeel yab làá fàtīí fōō bin nìn jìn̄-bee cee bi-wanti.»

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: Eesbɔn yab, nín yáliŋkímaan! Di sá yii bi nāaǹ Ayi tiŋki. Ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú Raaba tiŋkee, gbámaan ibiil bí jòò-ni. Dūmaan kpɔsatab kí pèen̄, gāāmaan ikpiisilan! Yìim̀maan tinaabakalin. Bi cúú diwaal Mooleeki ki cáǹ kuyuŋu, ki kpáaǹ di-tandambi nì di-kpilib dicilpu.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: Raaba tiŋki, kisapɔmbiki kin gáatèe, ba pu ní a nìn dàkà a-ba a-tantakal nì a-kpaaŋŋi ŋin lòoǹ tiŋanee pu míǹ? A nìn máká a-gaajati pu. A nìn bàlifī a-ba yii: «Ŋma di sá-u ní kí já nì mi?»

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: «M làá cáań dinyoondi kí tɔ̄ ni-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb kɔkɔ pu, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. M làá jà ni-kɔkɔ ní sāǹ báà ŋma ń nīn pée túĺ u-nimbiin cáaa, ní báà ubɔ dāa kpá kí kóoǹ bin bíi sáńee kí kpāfì.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: «Míǹ boonee, m làá fàtīí gíiǹní Amɔn yab bin bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee.» Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee dee. Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Eedoom yab puee

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says about Edom: Wisdom and common sense have vanished from Teman.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Eedoom yab pu. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Biciŋfitiibi kaa ti bí Teeman tiŋkin níii? Binyiliibi kaa ti nyí níii? Bi-ciiŋyi wáŋkì níii?

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Deedan yab, sām̀maan! Fàtīmaan ni-boon kí tīī. Sām̀maan kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔn! M làá cáań dinàandi kí tɔ̄ Eesayuu naantiibi pu, di sá yii ŋyunti bāań bí dáaĺ bi-tafal.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Bin kìtī fiinyi subiliŋee yaa láa bāań ni-ceeyee, baa làá dāá kíǹ disubil dibaba. Binaayub yaa láa dɔ́miń ni-cee kunyeeuee, bi làá dāá nàan̄ tin kɔkɔ bi dāa ŋūǹee.

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Di sá yii man di làá fūkul̀ Eesayuu naantiibi. M làá nyāntí ni-balilammu kí páań mpaampiin pu. Naa dāa gíti ŋūǹ kí cù kí báĺ niin. Ni-naantiibi nì ni-nabiyaamu nì ni-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb làá nàan̄. Ubɔ dāa kpá kí tùkù-ni yii:

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: <Yàntīmaan ni-taŋkpiibiliŋ, ti làá kpèè-ŋi kí tīī-ni, ní ni-kpiipoobi ŋūǹ kí nīn máká m-pu.>»

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Pīlifì, bin maa nìn páb́ yii bí nyɔ̀ m-ŋuul kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaaunee nyùn̄ kaa là. Ní sii Eedoom, a dàkafī yii baa làá dáaĺ a-tafalaaa? A làá nyɔ̀ m-ŋuul kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaaun kaa bál̀.

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan di pūtì yii m sá Unimbɔti ní ki làá yàntī a-tiŋyil Boosiraa ń kpántí adigbun ŋma, ntimbiil paaŋŋu. Bi yaa làá dāá tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu àá kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icooyee, kíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika. Ki-timmu kɔkɔ làá dāá kpántí adigbun ŋma kí nīn cá jaanjaan.» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti tiba, ní ntuun ŋubɔ cáań-tì ki nāatì atimbun kɔkɔ: «Kóom̀maan kí kpāfì! Cùú jámaan Eedoom tiŋki. Yīkìmaan! Jámaan-kì!»

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: A nìn fàantí báà ŋma, a nìn dàkafī yii a tɔ́kɔ́ bin kíǹee kɔkɔ pu, ama a nìn bíi kíiĺ a-ba ní. A kóò itaŋkpalɔkɔn ki lúń yilpu yilpu. Ama báà a yaa máń a-diiku ki tɔ́kɔǹ yilpu kii ukaabɔnee, m làá dū-si kí tɔ̄ń taapu.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: People passing by your country will be shocked and horrified to see a disaster
translation_verse: «Eedoom tiŋki làá kpántí adigbun ŋma ní. Bisanjitiliibi kɔkɔ yaa láa ká bi nín nāaǹ-si puee, án làá dāá ŋá-bi bitii ní bí nīn búǹ ifoon.

english_verse: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
translation_verse: An dāa bí kii Soodoom nì Goomoora timmu nì ntimu mun nìn māntìi tú-muee nín nìn nāaǹ puee ní, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Ubɔ kaa làá dāá gíti kɔ́ niin, uniseen kaa dāa gíti kíikí kí kàl̄ niin.»

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá dāá nīn bí kii gbikinti nín nyēē kimɔgbaayin Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi ki cá laakin timɔsɔn bée puee ní. Kii dinimbil nín kábití puee, m làá yàntī báà ŋma ń búntí. Míǹ boonee ní ḿ lēē un m lèe kí kàan̄ Eedoom tiŋki pu ubɔti. Di sá yii ŋma di bí kii mamee? Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yíiń-mi tibuul? Uyidaan ulɔu di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ m-nimbiin?»

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: Bi nín lítì puee wooku yāntì kitiŋ cīŋkì. Bi gbìl̀ bi-biilii pu áli Tikati mɔɔl.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Unannanli bí kii ukaabɔn nín jɔ́ḿ kutaa pu, ki ŋàaǹ ki kpátí u-feeŋyi Boosiraa tiŋki puee ní. Yaadalee, Eedoom yab baatandambi pɔbiliŋ làá dāá bīil̀ kii imatiŋween nín cútí upɔdaan puee ní. Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Damaasi yab puee

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tibɔti tin Damaasi yab puee sèé. «Amaati nì Aripaadi timmu nín gbìl̄ kubɔbiiu gbanti puee, ní icoo cúú-mu. Bi-pɔbil yíkì kii tiŋku un pu kubuŋkpaaŋŋu jītí waa ŋūǹ kí dòon̄ sooooyee ní.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damaasi yab wunti yɔ̄tì ní bi bíi bɔ́ntí kí sāǹ. Tifaandi cúú-bi. Dinyoondi kɔ́-bi ní bi bíi yáliŋkí kii imatiŋween di cúú upɔdaanee.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: An ŋá mana ní bi dū kitiŋ kin nyáń diyindee ki fá míǹ, kitiŋ kin nìn tīī-mi dipɔɔpindee.

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. An pu ní ŋwiin gbantee, bi-nipɔmbi làá lítí mpaan nee pu ní bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ ń kpú.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: M làá tūū digundi din māntìi tú Damaasi tiŋkee ŋŋmi ní ŋú wà ubɔti Been-Adaadi beecindi. Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Bilaalibub nibul puee

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tibɔti tin bilaalibub nì Asɔɔr beeŋi ŋin Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee sèé: «Yīkìmaan kí cùú jáǹ Keedaar yab! Ní nàan̄ bin kóò kuteeunee wanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: His fearsome army will surround you, taking your tents and possessions, your sheep and camels.
translation_verse: Ní fōōmaan bi-tantib nì bi-waŋkuti, nì bi-kɔŋkooŋyi nì tin kɔkɔ bi cááyee. Ní kpáaǹ bi-gutaamui, ní kí nīn kūuntí mpɔn bi-pu yii: Dinyoondi bí an kɔkɔ pu.»

english_verse: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Asɔɔr yab, sām̀maan, yīkìmaan malaa kí fīī ni-ba Ní sāǹ kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔn. Di sá yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar bɔ́ntì ni-pu min u làá ŋá-nee.»

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Yīkìmaan kí cùú jáǹ ditimbundi din kā ŋgbansɔŋfin kaa dàkafī yii tiba ŋūǹ kí ŋá-dèe. Bi-punyɔmmu kaa cáá punuubi, kaa cáá tikpàlkaal, ní ki kóò bi-baba ŋkpaanceeti.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Binannanliibi làá yɔ̀ bi-gutaamui, ní kí fūkul̀ bi-picaŋkpunti tin náaǹ nee. Ti-Dindaan bí yii: M làá jà binib bin kōol̀ jamba nee. M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu laakin kamaa bi yaa pée bée.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Asɔɔr tiŋki làá kpántí iŋɔkɔ kɔŋkooŋŋu, kunimbaau teeku kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Ubɔ kaa làá nīn gíti kóò ki-ni, báà uniseen.» Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Eelam tiŋki puee

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M làá kóoĺ Eelam yab tɔbu bun pu bi pɔ̄ɔ̄yee.

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M làá kúntí Eelam tiŋkin ubɔti nì u-kàliŋkpilib, ní kí cáań m-beejal kí yóoń kitiŋ gbantin.>» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: Ama míǹ boonee, m làá fàtīí gíiǹní Eelam yab bin bi nìn cūnnì kuyuŋuee bi-tiŋkin. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii Babiloon tiŋki, an dàkà yii Kaldee yab tiŋki pu puee sèé:

english_verse: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
translation_verse: «Bāakìmaan tibɔti nee kí tùkù atimbun kɔkɔ, ní cóoḿmaan tidaandi kí yàntī bí béé-tì. Yàntīmaan bí béé-tì, ní taa báĺ tiba. Lìmaan yii: <Bi jáń ki fōō Babiloon tiŋki, icoo cúú diwaal Beeli, diwaal Maarduuki lítì. Icoo cúú u-waaŋi gbanti, bi kúntì u-jɔkɔŋwanti gbanti.

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: Di sá yii ditimbundi diba nyánní ŋgan pú ki dòoń kí já nì kì kí yàntī kí kpántí kunimbaau teeku. Ubɔ kaa ti làá kɔ́ ki-pu. Binibaaa, tiwaŋkutaaa, bi-kɔkɔ làá sāǹ kí wāŋkì.>»

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋyunti gbantee, Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab làá dāá nóoń dicilpu kí dāan̄. Bi làá dāá nīn còom̄ ki sūǹ ki nyàab̀ man bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: M-nibul yab nìn bí kii ipii in wáŋkèe ní. Bi-kpàaliibi nìn yāntì bi wáŋkì ní ki yāntì bi tú ki yìiǹ ajoon pu. Bi nìn yìiǹ ajoon pu ki póotí ŋgbantamu pu, ní ki súntì bi-naabakati pu.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ yaa nìn ká-bee nìn cútí-bi ní kí tɔ̀ntī ní bi-nannanliibi lì yii: <Taa bíi ŋáań tikpitil tibaa! Tiŋman puee, binib gbanti yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan un di sá difiil kɔŋkooŋŋu, ní bi-naanjab nìn máká u-puee.>»

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: Sām̀maan kí nyā Babiloon tiŋki, yīkìmaan Kaldee yab tiŋki! Lìntīmaan kupicaŋkpuŋu nyɔkɔpu kii iŋɔjaayee.

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m làá lùkutī atimbuŋkpaan dikitil ní kí tɔ̄-ŋi ŋí já nì Babiloon tiŋki. Atimbun gbanti làá nyānní ŋgan pú ní kí tàtīí gbàan̄ dikɔ̀ndi pu kí já kí fōō kitiŋ gbanti. Bi-piiŋyi bí kii ubaatandaan un kaa fàtīi gítí mmɔŋki iŋaŋkulimee ní.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Bi làá fūkul̀ Kaldee yab tiŋki, ní bin kɔkɔ làá fūkul̀-bee làá kóoǹ tigaajawan kí báĺ, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: Nín̄ fàal̀maan kí nīn bí dipɔɔpindin, nimbi bin dɔ́miń ki fúkúl̀ man gaajawantee. Nín̄ yùkufīmaan kii dinabil di yú kumɔsɔŋunee. Nín̄ sūm̀maan kii itaamuee!

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: Icoo cúú ni-tiŋki kin sá kii ni-nee, un di màl̄-nee fá u-jilmau. Kɔŋkɔnnee, ni-tiŋki di sá kin lúŋkèe ntimu kɔkɔ kansikin. Kì kpántì kuteeu, kitiŋkuliŋŋi.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Diŋuul din ti-Dindaan fōōyee puee, binib kaa ti kóò ni-tiŋkin, kì kpántì kuteekpaaŋŋu ní. An ŋáań bin kɔkɔ jītí Babiloon tiŋkinee bitii. Bi yaa ká nnaabu ŋun jéetì kitiŋee puee, bi fátí dipɔɔbiildi biilii ní.

english_verse: Babylon has rebelled against me. Archers, take your places. Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
translation_verse: Nimbi bipintɔliibi kɔkɔ, màntīí tūmaan Babiloon tiŋki kí já nì kì. Ní tɔ̄maan ni-piiŋyi, ní taa mɔ̄tì i-pu, di sá yii kì yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Ijaan kɔkɔ puee, nín̄ kūuntímaan ki-pu ijanjakuŋkuunti! Bi yōoǹ bi-ŋalii yilpu ki sáǹ ki kɔ́ bi-nannanliibi. Digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee lítì. Ti-Dindaan di bíi tɔ̀ ipɔntoon! Tɔ̀maan Babiloon tiŋki ipɔntoon, ŋámaan-kì kii kì nín ŋá bin kíǹee puee.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Ní kúntímaan Babiloon tiŋkin, bin būul̀ee nì bin cēēyee. Báà ŋma ń sāǹ kujaau kun nàantí nee kí gítí u-nibul cee, báà ŋma ń sāǹ kí gítí u-tiŋkin.

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab nìn bí kii dipibil din wáŋkì ní gbikintib sáń ki jèe ní. Gbikintipeepeekaa un cúú-bi ki ŋmɔ́ee di sá Asuur bɔtiu. Míǹ boonee ní Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar mun dɔ́miń ki kɔ́fì bi-kpabiŋ.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bí yii: «M làá jáǹ Babiloon bɔtiu nì u-tiŋki, kii m nín jáń nì Asuur bɔtiu puee ní.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: «M làá fàtīí gíiǹní Isirayeel yab bi-pikpaapɔɔkun. Bi làá ká kí jī Kaarmeel jool pu nì Baasan timpiliŋki pu, nì Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu nì Galaadi tiŋkin kí díkí.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ yii ŋyunti gbantee, bi làá dāá nyàab̀ Isirayeel yìntitam ama baa làá dāá ká. Bi làá dāá nyàab̀ Juuda kpitii kaa làá dāá ká. Di sá yii m làá dāá dū bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: «Bóob́maan dikɔ̀ndi kí cùú jáǹ Maratiim tiŋki. Ní cùú já kì nì Peekoodi yab! Ní pɔ̀fì-bi kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí bi-kɔkɔ múb. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Á ŋá m nín tīī-si mara á ŋá puee deedee.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Ti gbìl̄ dikɔ̀ndi wooku nì dibintiŋkpaandi pu kitiŋee ni!

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Babiloon tiŋki nìn bí kii dikújal din gbáà ki mátí kitiŋ kɔkɔee ní. Kin an dī mana ní bi gbáń ki wīil̀-kì kì kíǹ ki dɔ̄ akati akati míǹ? Babiloon tiŋki kpántì dinyoondi paaŋŋu atimbun kansikin.

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babiloon, m píĺ-si kutaliŋŋu ní a sàl̄ kaa kpáàa béè. Bi bīitì a-pu ki cúú-si, kun puee a jáń nì man ni-Dindaan»

english_verse: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan pīitì u-janjawanti diiku ní ki lēeń u-ŋuul janjawanti. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan cáá ditundi kí tɔ̄ Kaaldee yab tiŋkin.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Nyānnímaan ajan kɔkɔ pu kí dāan̄ kitiŋ nee ni! Ní pìitī ki-cakalaabi kí kóoǹ ki-gaajawanti kí kpúkuń ní kí nàan̄-kì. Tiba nì tiba kaa máaǹ kí kíń.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Kpɔ̀maan ki-janjaliibi bimɔntiibi kɔkɔ, cùnnìmaan-bi nnaŋkpɔpaan pu! Dinimbinaamandi kɔ́-bi, di sá yii ŋyunti bāań ti-Dindaan ń dáaĺ bi-tafal.

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: Pīlifìmaan, bin bíi sáń Babiloon tiŋkee, bin dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalinee di dɔ́miń ki máafí Siiyɔn tibɔmɔntiil yii: «Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu tɔ̀n̄-ti, u tɔ̀n̄ u-diiku pɔntooŋyi.

english_verse: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
translation_verse: Kóom̀maan bipintɔliibi, bin kɔkɔ pīil̀ itɔfee kí kpāfì bí jáǹ Babiloon tiŋki. Lùkù kí gíb́maan-kì ijaan kɔkɔ pu, ní taa yàntī báà ubɔ ń sāǹ kí ŋmátí. Ní pàmaan-kì kí nóó ki-tuŋkpitiŋ. Ŋámaan-kì kii kì nín ŋá bin kíǹee puee. Di sá yii kì yōoǹ ki-ba yilpu ti-Dindaan Isirayeel circir Nimbɔtiu nimbiin.

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: «An pu ní bi-nipɔmbi làá lítí mpaan nee pu ŋwiin gbanti, ki-janjaliibi kɔkɔ làá kpú.» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: «Babiloon ulambidaan, man nì sii dee, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ. A-wiiŋŋu bāań díǹ dee, ŋyunti ŋun m làá dáaĺ a-tafalee dee.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Kilambidaŋ gbéetì ki lítì, ubɔ kaa bí kí yòon̄-kì kí yóoń. M tūū ki-timmu ŋŋmi, an làá wà tin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-kèe.»

english_verse: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Bi ŋúb́ Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab ki sàantí. Bin cúú-bi kuyuŋuee ŋúb́-bi kaa là kí gíiǹ-bi kí líí.

english_verse: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Bí já nì Kaaldee yab, bí já nì Babiloon yab, bí já nì Babiloon bɔtibiliŋ nì ki-ciŋfitiibi!

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Bí já nì bibɔɔbi, bi-yiliŋ ń lábití! Bí já nì bibaatandambi, bi-wunti ń yɔ̀tī.

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Bí já nì ki-taamui nì ki-janjatɔrɔkub, nì nyaaŋmaliŋku nib bin kóò bi-kansikinee, bí kpántí kii binimpoobee! Bí já nì laakin ki kpáafí ki-gaajatee.

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Bí já nì ki-buŋyi í kpā! Di sá yii kì sá awaa tiŋki ní. Ntimbiil wanti gbanti yāntì bi-yiliŋ lábitì.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kii m nín nìn nāaǹ Soodoom nì Goomoora timmu nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-muee puee, míǹ ní ubɔ kaa ti làá kɔ́ Babiloon tiŋkin, uniseen kaa làá ti kàl̄ niin.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: Dinibul diba nyánní ŋgan pú, an sá ditimbuŋkpaandi ní. Atimbun kupaau nyánní doooo kitiŋgbeennyɔkɔ ki dòoń.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Bi-janjaliibi ŋúb́ itɔfi nì ŋkpamu. Bi cáá nnimbinaakulim kaa sūǹ isaa. Dibintindi din bi gèe náań nì tiŋku nín ŋáań kuwoou puee ní. Bi jɔ́m̀ ki kā itaamu pu. Bi páaǹ ipɔ̀n pu tiŋan kí já nì sii Babiloon tiŋki.

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu gbìl̄ bi-pu. U-wunti yɔ̄tì ní dinyoondi cúú-u, ní u bíi gbìl̀ tiweendi pu kii imatiŋween di cúú upɔdaanee.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: M làá nīn bí kii gbikinti un di nyánní kimɔgbaayin ki kpàkaǹ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki cá kumɔsɔŋu laŋkee ní. Kii dinimbil nín kábití puee, míǹ ní m làá yàntī ki-nib ń yīkì. Míǹ boonee ní ḿ kàan̄ Babiloon tiŋkin ubɔti un m lēēyee. Di sá yii ŋma di bí kii mamee? Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yíiń-mi tibuul? Uyidaan ulɔu di ŋūǹ kí já nì mi?»

english_verse: Listen to my plans for you, people of Babylonia. Your children will be dragged off, and your country destroyed.
translation_verse: Ní pīlifìmaan tin ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì kí ŋá Babiloon tiŋkee, tin u lēē kí ŋá Kaaldee yabee. Tiŋman, bi làá dāá dàtī-bi mpɔn ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu kii tiwaŋkutee. Bi-puee, bi làá nàan̄ bi-naabakati, an kaa cáá digbíntil.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Bi nín gbìl̄ yii: «Bi jáń ki fōō Babiloon tiŋkee», kitiŋ cīŋkì ní, ní ibiil fōō ki píĺ dàii atimbun kɔkɔn.

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M làá cáań kubuŋu kun nàantée kú jītí Babiloon tiŋki nì ki-nib pu.

english_verse: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
translation_verse: M làá cáań binicambi kí tɔ̄ ki-pu ní bí jà ki-nib kí yàl̄ kii kubuŋu nín yòontí tifeel kí fá puee ní. Bi làá nàan̄ kitiŋee. Dinimbinaamandi dalee, bi làá màntī kí tū-kì ijaan kɔkɔ pu.»

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Bipintɔliibi ń tɔ̄ binannanliibi pintɔliibi. Binannanliibi ń taa nín̄ pùlifī bi-gbampɔɔŋi pu! Ní taa yàntī bi-janjapɔmbi ubɔ ń ŋmátí! Ní nàan̄ bi-janjakitil kɔkɔ!

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ikpiti in bi ŋá Isirayeel circir Nimbɔtiuee gbí bi-tiŋki. Ama Isirayeel nì Juuda Nimbɔtiu un sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaanee kaa kpíì ki fá-bi.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Sāǹ kí nyāmaan Babiloon tiŋkin, báà ŋma ń sāǹ kí fīī u-ba! Niinee naa làá kpú ki-kpitii pu. Di sá yii ŋyunti bāań ti-Dindaan ń tɔ̀ ipɔntoon, u làá pà bi-paati nín máaǹ puee.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babiloon nìn sá kii sindaariya kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaau ní ki kā ti-Dindaan ŋaan. Kì nìn yàntī kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ nyù ki gbéè. Atimbun nib nìn nyù ki-daam ní bi-yiliŋ ń lábití.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Ama dicilpu dicilpu ní Babiloon lítì ki wúkul̀. Yāliŋkìmaan ki-pu! Nyàab̀maan ŋkpam kí ŋá ki-buuŋyi, an yaa yíì kì làá pɔ̄ɔkì.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ti pɔ́ɔǹ kí bàà cáaǹ Babiloon tiŋki, ama ní kàa pɔ́ɔkì. An puee tí yàntī-kì! Báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-tiŋkin. Tiŋman, ditafadaaldi din lítì ki-puee nyìm̀ tikpil, di jɔ́m̀ ki tin tūū kutagbɔŋu, di tūū atagban.

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì kí nàan̄ Babiloon tiŋki. An pu ní u tīī Meedi yab bɔtiibi kunyannyaau bí ŋá u nín bɔ́ntì puee. Ti-Dindaan bíi tɔ̀ ipɔntoon, u bíi tɔ̀ u-diiku pɔntooŋyi. Lòom̄maan ni-piiŋyi, ní gbéem̀maan ni-baataŋŋi.

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Sii Babiloon un di kóò dimɔɔkpaandi gbandee, sii un di cáá tigaajati tikpilee, an dóò a-pu dee.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan pūtì úǹ u-ba ki lī yii: «M làá yàntī binib bin wīikí kii inaakitoonee ń gbáb́ kí bìin̄ a-pu. Bi làá kúuǹ a-pu ijanjakuŋkuunti.»

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: U tīī mara ní inyiŋfi kóoǹ ki kpáfì yilpu, ní atagban nyánní kitiŋ kúntinyɔkɔ ki jɔ́m̀. U yāntì utaa ŋmɔ́ ní ki nìn̄. U yāntì kubuŋu nyánní ku-walimbookun.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan dū u-pɔŋŋu ní ki náań kitiŋ, ní ki dū u-ciiŋŋu ki bíl̀ duulinya ní u bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄, ní ki dū u-nyil ki kpátì kutagbɔŋu ki dāntì kutaa pu.

english_verse: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
translation_verse: Án làá dāá ŋá binib bitii, ní bí nīn yú kaa gbìl̀ taapu. Icoo cúú bin dùntī tikúti ki mɔ́ɔ̀ awaayee. Bi-waaŋi gbanti sá tinyimɔŋwan ní, ŋaa cáá kufoou ŋi-ni.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ŋaa pée bí tiban, ki mɔ̄ tilaal, ditafadaaldi wiiŋŋu dalee, ŋi làá dāá wāŋkì.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti un sá Jaakɔb gaajatee, kaa bí kii ŋi nín bí puee. Úǹ di sá duulinya kɔkɔ náanliu, ní Isirayeel sá-u difakal. Úǹ ní bi yíì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan Babiloon kúntitam

english_verse: Babylonia, you were my hammer; I used you to pound nations and break kingdoms,
translation_verse: Sii Babiloon nìn sá-mi kii dikújalee ní, a nìn sá-mi tijanjawan ní. M dī a-pu ki nàn̄ atimbun dúsi dusi ki nāaǹ abee.

english_verse: as well as men and women, young and old,
translation_verse: M dī a-pu ki nàn̄ bininjab nì binimpoobi, binipɔmbi nì bitikpilib, binaacimpɔmbi nì bisapɔmbi kunaau.

english_verse: shepherds and their flocks, farmers and their oxen, and governors and leaders.
translation_verse: M dī a-pu ki nàn̄ bipikpaaliibi nì bi-picaŋkpunti, bikpaabi nì bi-naai in bi cáa kù tikpaalee, gɔminab nì kɔmandambi.

english_verse: But now, my people will watch, while I repay you for what you did to Zion.
translation_verse: Ama ni-nimbilaaliyin ní m làá pà Babiloon tiŋki nì Kaaldee yab tikpitil tin bi ŋá Siiyɔŋyee paati, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, m làá já nì sii Babiloon tiŋki, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Kí nàan̄ee, a nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii dijoolee, ní ki nìn nàantí duulinya kɔkɔ. M làá tàntī m-ŋal kí túĺ a-watil pú. M làá téeń-si á gàaǹ ataŋkpee pu kí lítí, ní kí yàntī á kpántí dijool din fòol̄ lìblibee.

english_verse: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
translation_verse: Baa ti làá ká a-cee ditaŋkpajal àá ataŋkpee ŋin bi dūu bíl̀ a-nyeelee, di sá yii a làá kpántí kuteeu ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Signal the nations to get ready to attack. Raise a flag and blow a trumpet. Send for the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Choose a commander; let the cavalry attack like a swarm of locusts.
translation_verse: Ní cóoḿmaan kujaau daaŋku ŋaabiki kitiŋin, ní búń ŋyin atimbun nib ń gbìl̄. Kóom̀maan atimbun kí kpāfì ŋí jáǹ Babiloon tiŋki, yíiḿmaan Ararati nì Miini nì Asikeenaasi beeŋi ŋí jáǹ-kì. Ní lēēmaan bijanjakpilib bí fōō bijanjaliibi bí jáǹ-kì. Dūmaan itaamu in wīikí kii inaakitoonee kí tɔ̄ ki-pu í jáǹ-kì.

english_verse: Tell the kings and governors, the leaders and the people of the kingdoms of the Medes to prepare for war!
translation_verse: Kóom̀maan atimbun kí kpāfì ŋí jáǹ-kì, cilinjee Meedi bɔtiibi nì bi-gɔminab nì bi-kɔmandambi nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ bi kpòotēe.

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ cīŋkì màkà maka ki kɔ́ dinyoondin, ŋyunti ŋun ti-Dindaan ŋá u nín bɔ́ntì kí ŋá Babiloon tiŋki puee. U yāntì Babiloon tiŋki kpántì kuteeu báà unil kaa ti kóò ki-ni.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Babiloon baatandambi gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi jáà, bi sáǹ ki kɔ́ ki bál̀ bi-balilammun. Baa ti cáá dipɔbil, bi kpántì binimpoobi ní. Kitiŋ punyɔmmu pīitì ki wāā, bi tūū ki-diiŋŋi ŋŋmi.

english_verse: One messenger after another announces to the king, “Babylon has been captured!
translation_verse: Ituun sáń ki fòol̄ tɔb. Bi sáń malaa malaa ki cá Babiloon bɔtiu cee kí cùú tùkù-u yii bi jáń ki fōō u-tiŋki kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The enemy now controls the river crossings! The marshes are on fire! Your army has panicked!”
translation_verse: Bi pīiǹ laakin unil ŋūǹ kí còom̀ kí dùtī mbunee, digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee wùn̄ ŋŋmi, ní tifaandi cúú bijanjaliibi.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bí yii: «Babiloon tiŋki náań nì didigbanaapaal din bi ŋātèe ní. An kaa ti làá sūŋkì kudiceeu yuntiŋu làá bàń ki-pu.» Ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̀ u-nibul pɔntooŋyi Jeerusaleem

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar, cátikì-mi ki tɔ̄ntì-mi. U dū-mi ki fá kii disambikulindee. U dū-mi ki náĺ kii kupeebiliŋŋuee, u jíń m-jimmɔntiiti ki gbéeǹ u-pool, míǹ boonee ní u jìn̄-mi.

english_verse: The people of Babylonia harmed some of us and killed others. Now, Lord, make them pay!” The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
translation_verse: Babiloon ń fōō nnaabu nì falaabi bin kì kɔ́ǹ-tee tafadaaldi! Siiyɔn yab ń lì yii: «Tiŋman Kaaldee yab ń túń ti-fatikuu kpuulool.» *

english_verse: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Jeerusaleem pu puee sèé: «Mama m-ba di làá mɔ̄tì a-pu, man di làá tɔ̀ a-pɔntooŋyi. M làá yàntī Babiloon buŋyi ń kpā ní kí yàntī u-nyimbulii ń gúń.

english_verse: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī Babiloon tiŋki ń kpántí adigbun ŋma. Iŋɔkɔ di làá nīn kíǹ ki kóò niin, ní an kpántí mpaan ŋun fàantée. Bi làá dāá nīn gbáà inimɔɔn biilii, ní báà uniseen kaa dāa gíti kíikí kí kɔ́ niin.

english_verse: The Babylonians roar and growl like young lions.
translation_verse: Babiloon yab mùuǹ dicilpu kii gbikintibee, bi gbùkum̄ kii agbikintipɔmbilee.

english_verse: And since they are hungry, I will give them a banquet. They will celebrate, get drunk, then fall asleep, never to wake up!
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní kpɔkɔsi cúú-bee ní ḿ bɔ́ntí tijimmɔntiil kí tīī-bi. M làá yàntī bí nyɔ̀ kí gbí, bi làá gèeǹ ŋgeem min kaa kúntée, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I will lead them away to die, like sheep, lambs, and goats being led to the butcher.
translation_verse: M làá péetí-bi kí cùnnì laakin bi làá kpɔ̀-bee kii bi nín péetí apibil nì ipijaa nì iŋɔjaa ki cáǹ kí kpɔ̀ puee ní.» Bi bíi yáliŋkí Babiloon tiŋki pu

english_verse: All nations now praise Babylon, but when it is captured, those same nations will be horrified.
translation_verse: Bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Seesaki tiŋki ki fōō-kì. An dī mana ní ki bāań míǹ? Babiloon tiŋki kpántì kuteeu kun gbí inimɔɔnee atimbun kansikin.

english_verse: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
translation_verse: Tiŋku gbí ki bīiǹ Babiloon tiŋki pu, u-nyiŋgbanti yíkìi léeǹ ki-pu.

english_verse: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
translation_verse: Ki-timmu kpántì kuteeu kun gbí inimɔɔnee. Kitiŋee kpántì kitiŋkuliŋŋi, mpaan ŋun pu báà ubɔ kaa kóò, ní báà uniseen kaa ti jītée ní.

english_verse: I will punish Marduk, the god of Babylon, and make him vomit out everything he gobbled up. Then nations will no longer bring him gifts, and Babylon's walls will crumble. The Lord Offers Hope to His People
translation_verse: M làá jáǹ diwaal Beeli Babiloon tiŋkin. M làá dáaĺ kí lēē kun kā ki-nyɔkɔnee, atimbun kaa làá nīn gíti bìtifī ki cá ki-cee. Babiloon gundi gba lítì.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon, my people, and run for your lives, before I strike the city in my anger!
translation_verse: M-nibul, sāǹ kí nyā kitiŋ gbantin! Báà ŋma ń sāǹ kí fīī u-ba ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi ń taa kpáaǹ-u.

english_verse: Don't be afraid or lose hope, though year after year there are rumors of leaders fighting for control in the city of Babylon.
translation_verse: Ni-wunti ń taa yɔ̀tī! Ní taa yàntī tin bi sòoǹ kitiŋee ni ń fàaǹ-ni. Dibindi dibee bi sòoǹ tiba, ní dibindi dibee, bí tí sòoǹ tiba mun. Tipɔmbɔti jíń dinyandi kitiŋee ni, ní ubɔ ń yīkì kí já nì ubɔti un kēe kí fōō u-yil.

english_verse: The time will come when I will punish Babylon's false gods. Everyone there will die, and the whole nation will be disgraced,
translation_verse: Too, iwiin bí ki dòoń, m làá jáǹ Babiloon waaŋi. Kitiŋee kɔkɔ làá kɔ́ icoo ni. Ki-nikpiliŋ kɔkɔ làá nīn dɔ̄ kitiŋ kansikin fìlfil.

english_verse: when an army attacks from the north and brings destruction. Then the earth and the heavens and everything in them will celebrate.
translation_verse: Bin làá nàan̄ Babiloon tiŋkee làá nyānní ŋgan pú ní. Niinee yilpu nì taapu nì tin kɔkɔ bí bi-puee làá dāá nīn kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi ki-pu. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Ubɔnaatil

english_verse: Babylon must be overthrown, because it slaughtered the people of Israel and of many other nations.
translation_verse: Duulinya kɔkɔnee, binib tikpil kpíì Babiloon pu. Míǹ mbaantiim ní Babiloon mun làá kpú Isirayeel yab bin kpíì u-puee pu. Unimbɔti nibul

english_verse: My people, you escaped death when Jerusalem fell. Now you live far from home, but you should trust me and think about Jerusalem. Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
translation_verse: Nimbi bin ŋmátì kaa kpíìyee, nín̄ cámaan, taa nín̄ kāmaan doo. Ni yaa bí ndanaaa, ní nīn dàkafī ti-Dindaan pu, kí nīn téetí Jeerusaleem pu.

english_verse: You feel ashamed and disgraced, because foreigners have entered my sacred temple.
translation_verse: Ti yaa nìn gbìl̀ bi sìí-tee, an nìn wù-ti ní. Icoo nìn cútí-ti, di sá yii binicambi nìn kɔ́ ti-Dindaan circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.

english_verse: Soon I will send a war to punish Babylon's idols and leave its wounded people moaning everywhere.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń m làá jáǹ Babiloon waaŋi. Kitiŋee kɔkɔ poonee, bin fōō tiweendee làá dāá nīn yáliŋkí.

english_verse: Although Babylon's walls reach to the sky, the army I send will destroy that city. I, the Lord, have spoken. Babylon Will Be Destroyed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Báà Babiloon yaa jɔ́m̀ ki tin tūū kutagbɔŋu, báà kì yaa máń digundi din ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí dàb̄ee ki tú ki-ba, m làá tīī mara ní bin làá nàan̄-kèe ń bàń-kì, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: Listen to the cries for help coming from Babylon. Everywhere in the country the sounds of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Binib gbáà ibiil Babiloon tiŋkin ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi, bi gbìl̀ bi nín bíi nàantí Babiloon tiŋkee.

english_verse: The shouts of the enemy, like crashing ocean waves, will drown out Babylon's cries as I level the city.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di bíi nàantí Babiloon tiŋki, u yāntì u-wookpaaŋku ŋmíl̀. Binannanliibi janjakitil bíi gà dibintindi kii tiŋku nyiŋgbantee. Kuwoou kun bi ŋáańee náań nì ditaadundee ní.

english_verse: An enemy will attack and destroy Babylon. Its soldiers will be captured and their weapons broken, because I am a God who takes revenge against nations for what they do.
translation_verse: Di sá yii un làá nàan̄-kèe bāań-kì. U làá jáǹ Babiloon tiŋki. U làá cúú ki-baatandambi kí cùnnì kuyuŋu, u làá kɔ̄fì ki-tɔfii. Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan sá Unimbɔti un tɔ̀ ipɔntoonee ní. U làá pà báà ŋma u nín máaǹ tipaal tiŋyee ní.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the true King, promise that the officials and advisors, the governors and leaders, and the soldiers of Babylon will get drunk, fall asleep, and never wake up.
translation_verse: M làá nyùntī ki-kàliŋkpilib nì ki-ciŋfitiibi nì ki-gɔminab nì ki-kɔmandambi nì ki-baatandambi ndaam bí gbí. Bi làá gèeǹ talku geem, bi pée gíti kpá kí fìntī. Ubɔti un bi yíì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaanee di lī míǹ.

english_verse: The thick walls of that city will be torn down, and its huge gates burned. Everything that nation worked so hard to gain will go up in smoke. Jeremiah Gives Seraiah a Scroll
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii: «Babiloon guŋkpaaŋŋi kpéelikì kɔkɔ múb, ki-punuufɔkɔbee wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Anibul pée bíi ŋáań falaa fám deeyaa, atimbun pée bíi gì ki tìì ŋŋmi deeyaa!» Dinyɔɔbundi din bi dūu tɔ́ Eefiraati mɔɔlinee

english_verse: During Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah, he went to Babylon. And Baruch's brother Seraiah went along as the officer in charge of arranging for places to stay overnight.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii nìn tīī Neeriya jipɔɔn Seereeya, Meeseeya naantiiu mara ŋyunti ŋun u nì Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nìn cūtì Babiloon tiŋkinee. Ŋyunti gbantee, Seedeesiyasi nìn kā dibeel an ŋá abin anaa dee. Seereeya di nìn sá ubɔti kpambal din bɔ́ntí u-bɔti kɔkɔee.

english_verse: Before they left, I wrote on a scroll all the terrible things that would happen to Babylon.
translation_verse: Yeereemii nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔmbaantiiu poon inaabu in kɔkɔ làá jēetí Babiloon tiŋki puee, anyɔɔbun ŋin di jáǹ Babiloon tiŋkee.

english_verse: I gave the scroll to Seraiah and said: When you get to Babylon, read this scroll aloud,
translation_verse: Yeereemii nìn bí Seeraya yii: «A yaa bàn̄ Babiloon tiŋkinee, á kàaǹ tibɔti tin kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee.

english_verse: then pray, “Our Lord, you promised to destroy this place and make it into a desert where no people or animals will ever live.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní á lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan, sii a-ba di sòon̄ ki síiǹ yii bi làá nàan̄ Babiloon tiŋki, ní báà unilaaa, kuwaŋkuluaaa, tiba kaa ti làá nīn bí ki-pu. Kì làá kpántí kuteeu kun gbí inimɔɔnee kí nīn cá jaanjaan.>

english_verse: When you finish praying, tie the scroll to a rock and throw it in the Euphrates River. Then say,
translation_verse: A yaa láa kàan̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti ki dóòyee, á nyàab̀ ditaŋkpal kí páań kí bóob́ ní kí cáá tɔ̄ Eefiraati mɔɔlin.

english_verse: “This is how Babylon will sink when the Lord destroys it. Everyone in the city will die, and it won't have the strength to rise again.” The End of Jeremiah's Writing Jeremiah's writing ends here.
translation_verse: A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní á lì yii: <Míǹ ní Babiloon tiŋki làá wāŋkì. Ti-Dindaan di làá cáań nnaabu ŋun kí tɔ̄ ki-pu boonee, kàa ti làá ŋmā kí yīkì.>» «Yeereemii bɔti nín kúntí laakiŋyee dee.»

english_verse: Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials.
translation_verse: Bijanjaliibi bin cīití ubɔtee kpiliu nìn cúú usaraaŋakpil Seeraya nì u-taapu yɔu Seefaniya nì bisaraaŋaliibi bita bin nìn cí kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔkee.

english_verse: meters around. They were hollow, but the bronze was about
translation_verse: Bi nìn māntìi tú kitiŋ míǹ ki tin sāā Seedeesiyasi nín kpántì ubɔtee abin saalaa nì diba.

english_verse: After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ŋkùm nìn píĺ ki pɔ́ɔkì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní binib kaa nìn gíti cáá tiba kí jī. Uŋmananaati iwiin iwa dalee

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley,
translation_verse: ní Babiloon yab sāā ki cíl̀ digundi din nìn māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee. Kunyeeuee ní Juuda janjaliibi kɔkɔ sáǹ. Babiloon yab nìn māntìi tú kitiŋ. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, bijanjaliibi nìn dūu dī kipunyɔkɔ kin bí agun ali kansikin, ki bí ubɔti kpaabu caŋinee ki nyáń kitiŋin. Míǹ boonee ní bi kíĺ Jɔɔdan tantakal saŋŋu ki nín cá.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Babiloon yab nìn cúú-u kuyuŋu ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Riibila, Amaati tiŋkin, Babiloon bɔtiu cee. Niin ní úǹ sòon̄ u-bɔti

english_verse: Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia. About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan,
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nín kpántì ubɔtee abin diba kpá mmuŋku poon, uŋmaŋmooŋmooti iwiin saalaa dalee ní Neebusaradan kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. U nìn sá bijanjaliibi bin cí Babiloon bɔtiuee kpiliu ní ki nìn sá ubɔti kpambal kansikin ubɔ.

english_verse: and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses.
translation_verse: U nìn tūū kunimbɔtidii nì Juuda bɔtiu beecindi nì adikpaan ŋin nìn bí kitiŋee nee kɔkɔ ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Babiloon janjaliibi bin nìn bí bin cīití ubɔtee kpiliu ceeyee nìn gbáń ki wīī digundi din bi nìn máń ki tú Jeerusaleemee.

english_verse: He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Neebusaradan cúú bin nìn kíǹ kitiŋee nee ki cūnnì kuyuŋu. Bíǹ di sá bisoodambi kansikin biba nì bin nìn sáǹ ki kɔ́ Babiloon bɔtiuee nì bin tūǹ ŋŋal pu tundee.

english_verse: Only the very poorest were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
translation_verse: Ama u nìn yāntì bisoodambi biba kitiŋee ni bí nīn kù fiinyib nì akpaan.

english_verse: Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: U nìn sòoǹ nì u kubɔɔtiiu poon ní ki nìn kāaǹ-u mpaan ŋun jítiǹ bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí u-cee Babiloon tiŋkinee yai.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: U nìn yāntì Yooyakiim kaa ti pèentí disarkabɔkutil. Yooyakiim nì Babiloon bɔtiu di nìn kíǹ ki jīǹ disambibaantiilin.

english_verse: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbanti kí tin sāā Yooyakiim kúm dalee, Babiloon bɔtiu di nìn tìì-u tin u máaǹ kí nīn cáá kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee.

english_verse: Jerusalem, once so crowded, lies deserted and lonely. This city that was known all over the world is now like a widow. This queen of the nations has been made a slave.
translation_verse: Ba di yì-tì ní kitiŋ kin poon binib nìn nyìkēe ŋá kii ukpiipu un bi dūu fée. Kíǹ di nìn nyáń diyindi atimbun kɔkɔ kansikin, kpèè, kì kpántì uyumbu. Kíǹ di nìn sá kii bɔtiisal ki tɔ́kɔ́ ntimu kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: Each night, bitter tears flood her cheeks. None of her former lovers are there to offer comfort; her friends have betrayed her and are now her enemies.
translation_verse: Kì cáá tinyati kɔkɔ ki sūǹ ní, ní nnyinnyim pùub̀ ki-taŋkpunti. Bin nìn néeń-kèe kansikin báà ubɔ kaa ŋméeǹ-kì. Ki-bɔɔbi kɔkɔ dū-kì ki fá ní ki kpántì ki-nannanliibi.

english_verse: The people of Judah are slaves, suffering in a foreign land, with no rest from sorrow. Their enemies captured them and were terribly cruel.
translation_verse: Bi cúú Juuda tiŋki yab kɔkɔ ki cūnnì kuyuŋu kinicantiŋin, isaa jíń-bi tikpil niin. Bi cūtìi kɔ́ dinibul diba pu ní kaa ká laaba kí kàl̄. Bin bí ki jì bi-boonee tin cúú-bi nsanni bi bí kunimbaau poon.

english_verse: The roads to Zion mourn because no one travels there to celebrate the festivals. The city gates are deserted; priests are weeping. Young women are raped; Zion is in sorrow!
translation_verse: Isan in bi dì ki cá Siiyɔn tiŋkinee kā dikpool, kun puee báà ubɔ kaa ti cá ki jīǹ jiŋaalib. Ki-punyɔmmu bíil̀, ní ki-saraaŋaliibi bí iyaliŋki poon. Ki-sapɔmbi bin kaa nyí uninjee bí kunimbaaun. Tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kpántì ntuntun ní ki tīī Siiyɔn yab.

english_verse: Enemies now rule the city and live as they please. The Lord has punished Jerusalem because of her awful sins; he has let her people be dragged away.
translation_verse: Bi-nannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, bi-pulincɔntiibi kā nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. Bi-kpitii wíiŋŋu puee, ti-Dindaan yāntì takaasi bíi jīǹ-bi. Bi cúú bi-biyaamu ki cūnnì unannanli nimbiin kuyuŋu ní ki wɔ́b́-bi.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared. Her leaders are like deer that cannot find pasture; they are hunted down till their strength is gone.
translation_verse: Siiyɔn kā ki wāĺ ní bi yōoǹ tin sá u-nyootee ki cáa búntì. U-kàliŋkpilib kpántì kii ipeel in kaa ti kāntí kumoou kí ŋmɔ́ee. Baa ti ŋūǹ kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí bikpambi bin bíi jì-bee ŋaan.

english_verse: Her people recall the good life that once was theirs; now they suffer and are scattered. No one was there to protect them from their enemies who sneered when their city was taken.
translation_verse: Nnaabu jéetì Jeerusaleem pu ní kàa ti nyí laakin kì làá cùee, ní ki téetí tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ kì nìn cáá dooooyee pu. Ŋyunti ŋun ki-niwul kɔ́ binannanliibi ŋaanee, báà ubɔ kaa dɔ́miń kí jòoń-kì. U-nannanliibi nín ká kì lítì míǹ kaa ti bí tibanee ní bi bí ki lāā.

english_verse: Jerusalem's horrible sins have made the city a joke. Those who once admired her now hate her instead— she has been disgraced; she groans and turns away.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem yab ŋá ikpitikpaan ní, an pu ní kì kpántì titampummool. Bin kɔkɔ nìn tīī-kì disíndee kíǹ ki kpèé-kì fám, kun puee bi ká ki-cooi. Ní kíǹ ki-ba sūǹ ki yáliŋkí ki fātì ki-boon ki tīī.

english_verse: Her sins had made her filthy, but she wasn't worried about what could happen. And when Jerusalem fell, it was so tragic. No one gave her comfort when she cried out, “Help! I'm in trouble, Lord! The enemy has won.”
translation_verse: Ikpiti jɔkɔnti táká ki-bɔkutil, kaa dākafì kun ní an làá cáań boonee. An ŋá-kì maamaaci kì nín lítì miŋyee pu, ní ubɔ kaa bí kí ŋméeǹ-kì. U bí yii: «M-Dindaan, kpèè isaa in poon m bée, m-nannanliu bí ki gà u-bindi u-pɔŋŋu pu.»

english_verse: Zion's treasures were stolen. Jerusalem saw foreigners enter her place of worship, though the Lord had forbidden them to belong to his people.
translation_verse: Binannanliibi fúkúl̀ Jeerusaleem gaajawanti kɔkɔ pílpil. Jeerusaleem yab ká anibul aba yab dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun. Ama ti-Dindaan, a nìn yíì an nibuliŋee bí taa kɔ́ a-nikitil kansikin.

english_verse: Everyone in the city groans while searching for food; they trade their valuables for barely enough scraps to stay alive. Jerusalem Speaks: Jerusalem shouts to the Lord, “Please look and see how miserable I am!”
translation_verse: Ki-nib bí ki yáliŋkí ki nyàab̀ tijin. Bi ŋúb́ bi-gaajawammɔntiiti kí kpántí tijin kí jī kí ŋmátí. «M-Dindaan kpèè takaasi un poon m bée.» *

english_verse: No passerby even cares. Why doesn't someone notice my terrible sufferings? You were fiercely angry, Lord, and you punished me worst of all.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin còom̄ ki jītí dooyee, kpèèmaan ubɔ naabuŋu bàn̄ man yɔu nee jutaaa? Ubɔ naabuŋu bàn̄ ŋun poon ti-Dindaan kɔ́ǹ-mi u-ŋuul wiiŋŋu dal naaa?

english_verse: From heaven you sent a fire that burned in my bones; you set a trap for my feet and made me turn back. All day long you leave me in shock from constant pain.
translation_verse: Yilpu ní u tɔ́ń ŋŋmi, ní an kɔ́-mi ki tin bàn̄ m-kpabiŋ. U píĺ kutaliŋŋu m-saŋŋu pu, u gíiǹ-mi boon. U nyántì-mi m kíǹ ki bí m-baba, baabadalee m bí iween poon ní.

english_verse: You have tied my sins around my neck, and they weigh so heavily that my strength is gone. You have put me in the power of enemies too strong for me.
translation_verse: U kpáfì m-kpitii ki dūu bóob́ kpancikil, nì u-ŋalii ní u dūu bóob́, ní ki dūu léeǹ m-neen. Ti-Dindaan bātì m-pɔŋŋu pu, ní ki dū-mi ki líiǹ binib bin nimbiin maa ŋūǹ kí fālifèe ŋaan.

english_verse: You, Lord, have turned back my warriors and crushed my young heroes. Judah was a woman untouched, but you let her be trampled like grapes in a wine pit.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nyántì bibaatandambi bin nìn bí m-ceeyee. U bɔ́ntì dijanjakitil ki tɔ́ m-pu bí dāá nà m-nipɔmbi kunaau. Ní bi dɔ́miń ki nàn̄-bi kii bi nín nà asubil ki còol̀ ŋkpam puee. Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan nàn̄ Juuda yab bin bí kii usapɔɔn un kaa nyí uninjee.

english_verse: Because of this, I mourn, and tears flood my eyes. No one is here to comfort or to encourage me; we have lost the war— my people are suffering. The Prophet Speaks:
translation_verse: Tí nee kɔkɔ pu ní m bí ki sūǹ m-nimbiliŋ dēē nnyinnyimin. Kun puee un bàà làá ŋméeǹ-mi, kí tīī-mi dimaŋfalee dū-mi ki fá. M-biyaamu wáŋkì m-ŋaan, kun puee m-nannanliu pɔ́ɔkiǹ-mi. *

english_verse: Zion reaches out her hands, but no one offers comfort. The Lord has turned the neighboring nations against Jacob's descendants. Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag to her neighbors. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Siiyɔn tāntì u-ŋalii ki gbāam̀ ki gīī, ama ubɔ kaa bí kí cúú-u kí sɔ̄ŋkì u-pɔbil. Ti-Dindaan tīī mara yii Jaakɔb nannanliibi ń màntīí gíb́-u ajan kɔkɔ pu. Jeerusaleem kpántì kii titampummoolee binib kansikin. *

english_verse: The Lord was right, but I refused to obey him. Now I ask all of you to look at my sufferings— even my young people have been dragged away.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín ŋá puee sá deedee, di sá yii bi-marab ní waa là. Anibul kɔkɔ pīlifìmaan! Kpèèmaan iween in poon m bée. Bi cúú m-naacimpɔmbi nì m-bisalib ki cūnnì kuyuŋu.

english_verse: I called out to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and my leaders died while searching the city for scraps of food.
translation_verse: M bàà yíiń bin m nìn néeńee, ní bíǹ kaa ti là m-bɔti. M-saraaŋaliibi nì m-kpilib kpíì kitiŋin, ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi nyàab̀ tijin kí jī kí ŋmátée.

english_verse: Won't you look and see how upset I am, our Lord? My stomach is in knots, and my heart is broken because I betrayed you. In the streets and at home, my people are slaughtered.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, kpèè mbusu un kɔ́-mee, an cúú m-poon nai ki kūtì. M-naŋki nyáń nì m-ba, kun puee m jáń nì si an gíti lákatì. Kitàataajiki kūū m-biyaamu mmɔŋki ní kudiinee, a lì kii bitaŋkpiibi dumpuee.

english_verse: Everyone heard my groaning, but no one offered comfort. My enemies know of the trouble that you have brought on me, and it makes them glad. Hurry and punish them, as you have promised.
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̄ m nín dùǹee, ama ubɔ kaa dòoń kí sɔ̀ŋkì m-pɔbil. M-nannanliibi kɔkɔ gbìl̄ nnaabu ŋun jéetì m-puee, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi a nín ŋá-mi puee pu. A yāntì ŋwiin ŋun a yóoǹee bāań, yàntī tin poon m bí nee ń bàń bi mun pu míǹ.

english_verse: Don't let their evil deeds escape your sight. Punish them as much as you have punished me because of my sins. I never stop groaning— I've lost all hope!
translation_verse: Kpèè ntoom min kɔkɔ bi ŋée, kí ŋá-bi kii man kpitii puee, a nín ŋá-mi puee! Di sá yii m bí iyaliŋki poon ní an kaa cáá digbèendi.

english_verse: The Lord was angry! So he disgraced Zion though it was Israel's pride and his own place of rest. In his anger he threw Zion down from heaven to earth.
translation_verse: Mana ní ti-Dindaan fōō diŋuul ki kpátì dibɔmbɔndi ki bīiǹ Siiyɔn tiŋki pu míǹ. U téeń doooo yilpu Isirayeel yab nyooti ki lúkuń kitiŋ pu. U nín fōō siiyɔn pu mbum miŋyee, waa ti kpáàa nyí laakin u-taaŋi tɔ̄kɔntée pu.

english_verse: The Lord had no mercy! He destroyed the homes of Jacob's descendants. In his anger he tore down every walled city in Judah; he toppled the nation together with its leaders, leaving them in shame.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nyīī u-nibul Jaakɔb yab ki múĺ kaa súń bi-saai. U nín fōō mbum miŋyee yāntì u kpéelikì Juuda yab timmu mun bi máń agun ki māntìi túee. U lábitì abee nì bikpootiliibi ki cìb̄ kitiŋ, ki kpēē-bi fám.

english_verse: The Lord was so furiously angry that he wiped out the whole army of Israel by not supporting them when the enemy attacked. He was like a raging fire that swallowed up the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: U nín fōō mbum miŋyee yāntì u nāaǹ Isirayeel yab pɔŋyi kɔkɔ. Ti-Dindaan kaa ti fìil̄-bi binannanliibi ŋaan. Ama u tūū ŋŋmi ní an wùn̄ ki māntìi tú-u.

english_verse: He attacked like an enemy with a bow and arrows, killing our loved ones. He has burned to the ground the homes on Mount Zion.
translation_verse: U píĺ u-tɔbu ki tāntì kí tɔ̄ kii unannanlee. U tɔ́ ki kūū tin kɔkɔ nìn pée ŋān̄ nnimbikpeeyee. U fīitì u-bum kii ŋŋmee ki pɔ̀l̄ Siiyɔn nimbɔtidiiku kun cáá kunyaaŋŋuee pu.

english_verse: The Lord was like an enemy! He left Israel in ruins with its palaces and fortresses destroyed, and with everyone in Judah moaning and weeping.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ŋá Isirayeel tiŋki kii kì sá u-pulincɔntee. U gbáń ki wīī ki-beeciŋŋi kɔkɔ ki kpīkitì ki-guŋŋi ŋin kì máń ki dūu cíitì ki-bee, ní ki dū nnaabu nì dinimbinaamandi ki yàl̄ Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: He shattered his temple like a hut in a garden; he completely wiped out his meeting place, and did away with festivals and Sabbaths in the city of Zion. In his fierce anger he rejected our king and priests.
translation_verse: U ŋá mpɔn ki kɔ́ u-naabakakun ki kpītì u-paaŋŋu ŋun pu ti nì u kpáfée. Ti-Dindaan yāntì bi súntì Siiyɔn tiŋkin mpaan ŋun pu ti kpáfée nì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa pu. U nín fōō mbum miŋyee yāntì u kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ ubɔti nì bisaraaŋaliibi.

english_verse: The Lord abandoned his altar and his temple; he let Zion's enemies capture her fortresses. Noisy shouts were heard from the temple, as if it were a time of celebration.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan fá u-saraafaŋŋu, waa ti là u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu. U dū dibeecindi guŋŋi ki ŋá unannanli ŋaan, ní bi kūuntí kunimbɔtidiin kii jiŋaal wiiŋŋuee.

english_verse: The Lord had decided to tear down the walls of Zion stone by stone. So he started destroying and did not stop until walls and fortresses mourned and trembled.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lēē yii u làá wīī agun ŋin wúń Siiyɔn tiŋki yab puee. Waa làá tàan̄, u làá kpēelikì-ŋi ŋí taa ti nín̄ bí. U fáá agunliitil ní ŋi lítì.

english_verse: Zion's gates have fallen facedown on the ground; the bars that locked the gates are smashed to pieces. Her king and royal family are prisoners in foreign lands. Her priests don't teach, and her prophets don't have a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Kitiŋee gundi punyɔmmu lítì, ti-Dindaan wīī mpunyɔmu kpàlkaati. Bi cáá ki-bɔtiu nì ki-yidambi ki cūnnì nnicantimun kuyuŋu. Ubɔ kaa ti bí kí dàkà marab. Ti-Dindaan kaa ti lèekī tiba ki dàkà u-bɔnaatiliibi.

english_verse: Zion's leaders are silent. They just sit on the ground, tossing dirt on their heads and wearing sackcloth. Her young women can do nothing but stare at the ground.
translation_verse: Siiyɔn tindaŋkpilib tātìi kā kitiŋ dikru. Bi kā ki pēē kpɔsatab ntam pùkū bi-yiliŋ. Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi yiliŋ tīī kitiŋ. *

english_verse: My eyes are red from crying, my stomach is in knots, and I feel sick all over. My people are being wiped out, and children lie helpless in the streets of the city.
translation_verse: M wīī nnyinnyim ki gīī, m yaa kpēē tin bāań m-nibul puee ní an cúú m-poon kí kùtī, m-poon kaami cɔ́tì. Di sá yii mbiyaamu nì nnaŋgbammamu bí ki kúù imɔŋkijaa pu.

english_verse: A child begs its mother for food and drink, then blacks out like a wounded soldier lying in the street. The child slowly dies in its mother's arms.
translation_verse: Mu bàlifī mu-nab yii: «La ní ti làá nín ká tijin kí jī kí ká nnyim kí nyɔ̀ dee?» Mu kúù mu-nab ŋaan kii bin fōō tiweendi kujaaunee nín kúù puee. *

english_verse: Zion, how can I comfort you? How great is your pain? Lovely city of Jerusalem, how can I heal your wounds, gaping as wide as the sea?
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem, maa ti nyí tin m làá sòoǹ nì see! Tiba kaa bí ń dūú ŋmàntīǹ tin poon a bí nee kí dūú sɔ̀ŋkì a-pɔbil, Siiyɔn yab. Nnaabu ŋun jéetì a-puee sá ŋkpaan ki jítiǹ tiŋku. Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ-si.

english_verse: Your prophets deceived you with false visions and lying messages— they should have warned you to leave your sins and be saved from disaster.
translation_verse: Bibɔnaatiliibi cáá tinyimɔmbɔti tin kaa bí tibanee ní ki nàatī-si. Baa bìitī a-bɔɔŋŋi pu á bàà kpántí a-bimbim. Tin an lēē ki dàkā-bi a-puee sá nnyimɔn ní, bíǹ di náań-tì.

english_verse: Those who pass by shake their heads and sneer as they make fun and shout, “What a lovely city you were, the happiest on earth, but look at you now!”
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem, bin kɔkɔ jītí a-ceeyee kpáafí abaal bi nín nàn̄-si kunaauee pu, ní ki búǹ ifoon ki gbákafí diyil. Bi sòoǹ Jeerusaleem pu yii: «Kitiŋ kinyannyaaŋŋi dándan kin tìì duulinya kɔkɔ dipɔɔsɔŋkilee deeee?»

english_verse: Zion, your enemies curse you and snarl like wild animals, while shouting, “This is the day we've waited for! At last, we've got you!”
translation_verse: Sii pu ní a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ sòoǹ ki bèel̄, ki ŋmóò bi-nyiŋŋi nyànya ki lì yii: «Ti nyīī-u ki múĺ, ŋwiin ŋun ti nyàab̀ee bāań dee, ti bí ki wāĺ-ŋu.»

english_verse: The Lord has done everything that he had planned and threatened long ago. He destroyed you without mercy and let your enemies boast about their powerful forces.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ŋá min u nìn sòon̄ ki yóoǹ doooodooooyee yii u làá ŋée, u kpéelikì kaa súń isaa. Nnaabu ŋun poon u kɔ́ǹ-nee pu ní unannanli bí ki fàal̀ ní ki gbéeǹ ni-nannanliibi mpɔn. *

english_verse: Zion, deep in your heart you cried out to the Lord. Now let your tears overflow your walls day and night. Don't ever lose hope or let your tears stop.
translation_verse: Siiyɔn nib, kúum̀maan nì iyaliŋki ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Digundi din bi máń ki māntìi tú kitiŋee, yàntī a-nyinnyim ń nīn pùub̀ ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kii mbunee. Á taa ŋùŋfì, kí taa gbèen̄ nsiim.

english_verse: Get up and pray for help all through the night. Pour out your feelings to the Lord, as you would pour water out of a jug. Beg him to save your people, who are starving to death at every street crossing. Jerusalem Speaks:
translation_verse: Yīkì kunyeeu kí nīn tíminsí, kí sòoǹ a-pɔbilin bɔti kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Yòon̄ a-ŋalii kí túĺ u-watil, kí fīī a-biyaamu mun di bí isantaan kɔkɔ pu ki kúù ŋkùmee. *

english_verse: Think about it, Lord! Have you ever been this cruel to anyone before? Is it right for mothers to eat their children, or for priests and prophets to be killed in your temple?
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, kpèè tibɔti nee soooo! Ŋma ní a ŋá kii a nín ŋá man pu na? Ubinaati ŋmóò u-poon biki kinaŋgbammaŋ kin u néeńeeee? A kíikí bí kpɔ̀ bisaraaŋaliibi nì a-bɔnaatiliibi a-circir kɔŋkooŋŋunaaa?

english_verse: My people, both young and old, lie dead in the streets. Because you were angry, my young men and women were brutally slaughtered.
translation_verse: Bijaŋkpilib nì mbiyaamu dɔ̄ adan pu tàb tab. Bi dū ntàataajimu ki kūū m-sapɔmbi nì m-naacimpɔmbi. A-bum wiiŋŋu dalee, aa súń bi-saai, a pɔ̄fì-bi ki lāntì-bi.

english_verse: When you were angry, Lord, you invited my enemies like guests for a party. No one survived that day; enemies killed my children, my own little ones.
translation_verse: A yíiń m-kɔŋkɔnaatɔb bin m fàŋkí yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔee ki kpáfì kii jiŋaal wiiŋŋuee. Ní daliŋkin ti-Dindaan fīitì u-bumee, báà ubɔ kaa ŋmátì. Uniseen kaa kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin. M-nannanliu dɔ́miń ki kúntì bin m kpāā, ki néeń-bi tiŋanee.

english_verse: I have suffered much because God was angry.
translation_verse: M sá unil un di ká dinimbinaamandi mbum min ti-Dindaan fōōyee puee ní.

english_verse: He chased me into a dark place, where no light could enter.
translation_verse: Man ní u téé ki līntì u-nyɔkɔpu ḿ còom̀ dibɔmbɔndin, kaa sá ŋwalifin.

english_verse: I am the only one he punishes over and over again, without ever stopping.
translation_verse: Man baba tafal ní u dátí baabadal taafaau nì joou.

english_verse: God caused my skin and flesh to waste away, and he crushed my bones.
translation_verse: U fóofì-mi m-wunti dóò dáká daka, ní ki wīī m-kpabiŋ.

english_verse: He attacked and surrounded me with hardships and trouble;
translation_verse: U dū ntuntun nì agìń ki māntìi gíb́-mi kii digundee.

english_verse: he forced me to sit in the dark like someone long dead.
translation_verse: U cáá-mi ki kāaǹ dibɔmbɔndi paaŋŋun a lì kii bin kpíì ki dɔ̄ doooodooooyee.

english_verse: God built a fence around me that I cannot climb over, and he chained me down.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan dū digundi ki māntìi tú-mi ḿ taa ŋmā kí nyā, ki túǹ-mi tikúti tin nyìm̀ee.

english_verse: Even when I shouted and prayed for help, he refused to listen.
translation_verse: M kúuǹ ki yíiń-u ú dāá jòoń-mi ní u kpáá u-tafaliŋ kaa pílifì m-wimmeem.

english_verse: God put big rocks in my way and made me follow a crooked path.
translation_verse: U dū ataŋkpakpaan ki pīiǹ m-saŋŋu ní ki dū-mi ki dī nsaŋkpiti pu.

english_verse: God was like a bear or a lion waiting in ambush for me;
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí m-cee kii digbiŋgbil di wúliń m-puee, kii gbikinti di nɔ̀kɔ̄ kubambaŋŋun ki cí-mee.

english_verse: he dragged me from the road, then tore me to shreds.
translation_verse: U yāntì m fá m-saŋŋu, ní u cúú-mi ki tɔ̄ntì, ki nāaǹ-mi.

english_verse: God took careful aim and shot his arrows
translation_verse: U píĺ u-tɔbu ki páaǹ mpiin ki bíitìń-mi.

english_verse: I am a joke to everyone— no one ever stops making fun of me.
translation_verse: Man ní m-nibul kɔkɔ lāā, baabadalee man ní bi gà ilan ki bèel̄.

english_verse: God has turned my life sour.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan yāntì m-nyɔkɔ túŋkì, u nyūntì-mi ndabiim.

english_verse: He made me eat gravel and rubbed me in the dirt.
translation_verse: U tīī-mi itaŋkpabiiti m jú ki wīil̀, ní ki dū ŋfantam ki pùkū-mi.

english_verse: I cannot find peace or remember happiness.
translation_verse: U lēē m-gbansɔŋfiŋu, m súntì nnaam pu.

english_verse: I tell myself, “I am finished! I can't count on the Lord to do anything for me.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bí yii: an dóò man pu ní, maa ti cáá dimákal diba ti-Dindaan pu. *

english_verse: Just thinking of my troubles and my lonely wandering makes me miserable.
translation_verse: Téetí nnaabu ŋun poon m bée nì takaasi un bíi jīǹ-mee pu. An sá tilool tin tūee ní m bíi nyù.

english_verse: That's all I ever think about, and I am depressed.
translation_verse: M téetí múlmul, ní an jákatí m-pɔbil.

english_verse: Then I remember something that fills me with hope.
translation_verse: Ama tin pu m téetí ki cáá dimákalee sèé:

english_verse: The Lord's kindness never fails! If he had not been merciful, we would have been destroyed.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ŋanti kaa dóò, u-neendi kaa kúntì.

english_verse: The Lord can always be trusted to show mercy each morning.
translation_verse: U-deedeeu pɔ̀ntī ní kutaafaau sá kamaa!

english_verse: Deep in my heart I say, “The Lord is all I need; I can depend on him!”
translation_verse: M lī m-ban yii: ti-Dindaan di sá man gaajati, úǹ saŋŋu pú ní m kpèé.

english_verse: The Lord is kind to everyone who trusts and obeys him.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ŋān̄ bin kpèé u-saŋŋu púee nì bin nyàab̀-uee cee.

english_verse: It is good to wait patiently for the Lord to save us.
translation_verse: An ŋān̄ á nīn kā diŋmiŋŋmil ki cí ti-Dindaan jòońtam.

english_verse: When we are young, it is good to struggle hard
translation_verse: An ŋān̄ uninja ń léeń kpancikil u-naacimpɔntin.

english_verse: and to sit silently alone, if this is what the Lord intends.
translation_verse: U yaa bíi dàkà-u min waa lèe, ú cùú kàl̄ ŋkpaanceeti kí nīn ŋmí fɔ́ŋfɔŋ.

english_verse: Being rubbed in the dirt can teach us a lesson;
translation_verse: Ú gbàan̄ u-nimbiin ń cìb̄ dibulin, an yaa yíì u làá ká dimákal.

english_verse: The Lord won't always reject us!
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan kaa féeń unil kpataaa pu.

english_verse: He causes a lot of suffering, but he also has pity because of his great love.
translation_verse: Báà u yaa bíi sàantí unil, u làá dāá sɔ̄ u-saai, kun puee u-neendi wīikí tikpil.

english_verse: The Lord doesn't enjoy sending grief or pain.
translation_verse: An kaa sá yii u-pɔbil poonee an mɔ̄ǹ-u ú sàaǹ inifunaan kí sìntī-bi taapu. *

english_verse: Don't trample prisoners under your feet
translation_verse: Bi yaa bíi tà ki mátí kitiŋ pu yumbui kɔkɔee,

english_verse: or cheat anyone out of what is rightfully theirs. God Most High sees everything,
translation_verse: bi yaa bíi kpèé unil nì u-baamɔŋyi fám un bí yilpu yilpuee nimbilaaliyinee,

english_verse: and he knows when you refuse to give someone a fair trial.
translation_verse: bi yaa kūū ubɔ bɔti digàndee, ti-Dindaan kaa wāĺaaa?

english_verse: No one can do anything without the Lord's approval.
translation_verse: Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí lì dinyɔɔbundi tiba ń nyā kí nīn bí? Ti-Dindaan di lèekī ní án bàńaaa?

english_verse: Good and bad each happen at the command of God Most High.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di kaa lì ní tikpitil nì tiŋan kɔkɔ ŋáańaaa?

english_verse: We're still alive! We shouldn't complain when we are being punished for our sins.
translation_verse: Too, ba pu ní unil un bí dimaŋfalin min kamaa u sá unikpitee yáliŋkí?

english_verse: Instead, we should think about the way we are living, and turn back to the Lord.
translation_verse: Tí nyɔ̀kɔfì kí kpèè ti-bimbim kí dàkafì tiŋan, kí gítiḿmaan ti-Dindaan cee.

english_verse: When we lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we should offer him our hearts and say,
translation_verse: Tí yòom̄maan ti-ŋalii yilpu kí túĺ Unimbɔti un bí yilpuee kí mèè nì ti-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ.

english_verse: “We've sinned! We've rebelled against you, and you haven't forgiven us!
translation_verse: Taa yúliǹ-si deedee, ti-Dindaan, ti jáń nì si, ní saa dūu pú-ti.

english_verse: Anger is written all over you, as you pursue and slaughter us without showing pity.
translation_verse: A kɔ́ a-ŋuul poon ki yíkìi jìn̄ ti-boon ki kūū-ti kaa súń isaa.

english_verse: You are behind a wall of clouds that blocks out our prayers.
translation_verse: A dū ditagbandi ki bīiǹ a-ba pu ti-wimmeem ń taa bàń-si.

english_verse: You allowed nations to treat us like garbage;
translation_verse: A dū-ti ki ŋá anibul kansikin kii titampummool nì tiwan tin bi dūu fée.

english_verse: our enemies curse us.
translation_verse: Timbi ní ti-nannanliibi kɔkɔ sòoǹ ki bíiĺ.

english_verse: We are terrified and trapped, caught and crushed.”
translation_verse: Tin dɔ̄ ki cí-tee di sá dinyoondi nì nnaabu, dinàandi nì sámbu.

english_verse: My people are destroyed! Tears flood my eyes,
translation_verse: M-nimbiliŋ pùub̀ nnyinnyim sámbu un kɔ́ m-nibulee pu.

english_verse: and they won't stop
translation_verse: M sūǹ kaa ŋmīlifí, an kaa cáá digbèendi,

english_verse: until the Lord looks down from heaven and helps.
translation_verse: kí nīn cí ti-Dindaan ń kàlīń yilpu kí kpèè kí wāl̀.

english_verse: I am horrified when I see what enemies have done to the young women of our city.
translation_verse: M yaa bíi kpèé tin bāań m-nibulee, an wù m-nimbiliŋ ní. *

english_verse: No one had reason to hate me, but I was hunted down like a bird.
translation_verse: Bin ná-mi fám maa ŋá-bi tibee jì-mi kii m sá kinɔmbikee.

english_verse: Then they tried to kill me by tossing me into a pit and throwing stones at me.
translation_verse: Man nì m-nimbiliŋ yéè ní bi dū-mi ki tɔ́ dilɔkɔgindin ki dū ditaŋkpal ki tɔ́nní-mi.

english_verse: Water covered my head— I thought I was gone.
translation_verse: Ní nnyim jɔ́m̀ ki bīiǹ m-yil pu ní m bí yii an dóò man pu dee.

english_verse: From the bottom of the pit, I prayed to you, Lord.
translation_verse: Kubɔbiku gbanti poonee, m kúuǹ ki yíiń sii ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: I begged you to listen. “Help!” I shouted. “Save me!” You answered my prayer
