translation_verse: A gbìl̄ m-nyɔkɔ pu m nín lī yii: «Taa kpáá a-tafal, pīlifì m-kuŋkuuntii nì diniindi din m fátée.»

english_verse: and came when I was in need. You told me, “Don't worry!”
translation_verse: M nín kúuǹ ki yíiń-see, a sútìń ki pìl̄-mi ní ki bí-mi yii: «Taa fàŋkì.»

english_verse: You rescued me and saved my life.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan a mɔ́tì m-pu ní ki fīī-mi ki líì.

english_verse: You saw them abuse me, Lord, so make things right.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, a ká agìń ŋin poon binib kɔ́ǹ-mee, pɔ̀-mi!

english_verse: You know every plot they have made against me.
translation_verse: A ká ipɔntoon in bi tɔ̀n̄-mee, ki ká bi nín búkú m-pu tiŋyee.

english_verse: Yes, you know their insults and their evil plans.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, a gbìl̄ bi nín sìí-mi puee, nì bi nín sòon̄ ki búkú m-pu puee.

english_verse: All day long they attack with words and whispers.
translation_verse: M-nannanliibi dàkafī m-pu tibɔkpitil ŋma ní, ní ki sòoǹ ki tòó m-pu baabadal.

english_verse: No matter what they are doing, they keep on mocking me.
translation_verse: Kpèè, bi yaa kāaa, bi yaa yúɔɔɔ, man bɔti di sá-bi ilan bi gà.

english_verse: Pay them back for everything they have done, Lord!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, pà-bi tin bi ŋá-mee paati.

english_verse: Put your curse on them and make them suffer.
translation_verse: Kí pɔ̄ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ mbusu ń kɔ́-bi.

english_verse: Get angry and go after them until not a trace is left under the heavens.
translation_verse: Nì a-ŋuul poon ní a làá jà bi-boon, kí céetí-bi kitiŋ pu.

english_verse: The purest gold is ruined and has lost its shine; jewels from the temple lie scattered in the streets.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní sindaariya bɔ̄ntì míǹ kaa ti jìl̀? Ba pu ní sindaariyamɔnti gáń míǹ? Ba pu ní ataŋkpee ŋin bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee dɔ̄ ki yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu míǹ?

english_verse: These are Zion's people, worth more than purest gold; yet they are counted worthless like dishes of clay.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní Siiyɔn bɔtiijab bin náań nì sindaariyamɔntee kpántì kii kuyɔkɔu booŋŋi ŋin uyɔɔmaati dū u-ŋalii ki máńee míǹ?

english_verse: Even jackals nurse their young, but my people are like ostriches that abandon their own.
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan iŋɔkɔ, i tìì i-biyaamu dibiil i ŋáaḿ. Ama man nibul sá ubinaati un cáá ntoomee, àá kii taataabi bin bí kuteeunee ní.

english_verse: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues are stuck to the roof of the mouth. Children go begging for food, but no one gives them any.
translation_verse: Nnyinnyoo cúú kinaŋgbammaŋ ki-limbil nákáǹ ki-nyɔkɔ poon ki kūń. M-biyaamu bàlifī tijin pu ubɔ kaa tìì-mu.

english_verse: All who ate expensive foods lie starving in the streets; those who grew up in luxury now sit on trash heaps.
translation_verse: Bin nìn jīǹ tijimmɔntiilee bí ki kúù ŋkùm adan pu. Bin bi nìn lōō nì bisatamɔntiibee dɔ̄ titampummoolin.

english_verse: My nation was punished worse than the people of Sodom, whose city was destroyed in a flash without the help of human hands.
translation_verse: M-nibul yab kpitii wīikí ki jítiǹ Soodoom yab yai. Bi nìn nāaǹ kitiŋ gbanti dicilpu dicilpu ní ubɔ kaa ŋúń ki ŋá tiba.

english_verse: The leaders of Jerusalem were purer than snow and whiter than milk; their bodies were healthy and glowed like jewels.
translation_verse: Siiyɔn yab bɔtiijab nìn jìl̀ kii ntaayimee ní, ní bi-wuŋgbaŋŋu pīiǹ káŋkaŋ kii nnaabiimee. Bi-wunti nìn jɔ̀m̀ kii ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì kɔrayee ní bi-nimbiiŋyi jìl̀ kii ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì safiiree.

english_verse: Now they are blacker than tar, and no one recognizes them; their skin clings to their bones and is drier than firewood.
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee bi-nimbiiŋyi bɔ̄ntì kútí kuti kii dinaŋkansimbɔndee. Bi yaa ká-bi adan puee baa ti nyí-bi, bi-wuŋgbaŋŋu kūń kii ndɔee ní.

english_verse: Being killed with a sword is better than slowly starving to death.
translation_verse: Á kpú dikɔ̀ndin sɔ́ǹ ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀-si, á páĺ tijin kpátam pu.

english_verse: Life in the city is so bad that loving mothers have boiled and eaten their own children.
translation_verse: Dinimbinaamandi din jéetì m-nibul puee yāntì binimpoobi bin kaa mɔ̄ bi-biyaamu puee tɔ́kɔǹ-mu ki ŋmɔ́. *

english_verse: The Lord was so fiercely angry that he burned the city of Zion to the ground.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan kpáatì u-ŋuukpaandi kɔkɔ, ki tūū Siiyɔn tiŋkin ŋŋmi ní an wùn̄ ki tin kpáaǹ ki-nyeel.

english_verse: Not a king on this earth or the people of any nation believed enemies could break through her gates.
translation_verse: Ubɔti ubɔ àá unil ubɔ kitiŋ pu kaa fōō ki kíí yii unannanli ŋūǹ kí dī Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu pu kí kɔ́.

english_verse: Jerusalem was punished because her prophets and her priests had sinned and caused the death of innocent victims.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kpitii nì bisaraaŋaliibi yìntitam di yì nnaabu gbanti, kun puee bi kūū bi-timmun maanyiibab.

english_verse: Yes, her prophets and priests were covered with blood; no one would come near them, as they wandered from street to street.
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, bi còom̄ ki táfí kii bijɔfubee, fatiku táká-bi. An puee ubɔ kaa máaǹ kí gbēē bi-wampeeŋkaati.

english_verse: Instead, everyone shouted, “Go away! Don't touch us! You're filthy and unfit to belong to God's people!” So they had to leave and become refugees. But foreign nations told them, “You can't stay here!”
translation_verse: Bi tátí ki sòoǹ bi-pu yii: «Kàkatīmaan kí wàatī-bi, bi kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi! Kàkatīmaan! Kàkatīmaan! Ní taa gbēēmaan-bi.» Bi bíi sáń kaa nyí laakin bi cée. Ama ní atimbun ŋíǹ kíǹee lì yii: «Baa ŋūǹ kí kàl̄ timbi cee doo!»

english_verse: The Lord is the one who sent them scattering, and he has forgotten them. No respect or kindness will be shown to the priests or leaders.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan u-ba kaa ti là kí wāl̀-bi ní ki jìn̄-bi ki yàl̄ an kɔkɔ. Niinee baa ti dū bisaraaŋaliibi ki yíiń tiba, kaa súń bijaŋkpilib mun saai. *

english_verse: Our eyes became weary, hopelessly looking for help from a nation that could not save us.
translation_verse: Ti kpēē a-pu á dāá jòoń-ti ti-nimbiliŋ lóoĺ. Ti gāā isupaa ki kāl̀ ki cíitì ditimbundi din kaa ŋūǹ kí fīī-tee ń bàà dāan̄.

english_verse: Enemies hunted us down on every public street. Our time was up; our doom was near.
translation_verse: Ti-nannanliibi cɔ́ŋkí ki kpèé ti-tabɔbiliŋ, taa ti ŋūǹ kí nyā ti-mɔŋkijaai pu. Ti-kúntitam tóobiń tiŋman, ti-wiiŋŋu sāā.

english_verse: They swooped down faster than eagles from the sky. They hunted for us in the hills and set traps to catch us out in the desert.
translation_verse: Bin jì-tee yáb̀ ki jítiǹ ukaabu un ŋàaǹ yilpuee. Bi pá ti-boon ki jì-ti ajoon pu, ki cūtìi nɔ̄kɔǹ kuteeun ki cí-ti.

english_verse: The Lord's chosen leader was our hope for survival! We thought he would keep us safe somewhere among the nations, but even he was caught in one of their traps.
translation_verse: Un ti-Dindaan lēē ki kāaǹ ú nīn sá ti-bɔtiuee, un di yì ti-maŋfalee, bi cúú-u. Úǹ pu ní ti nìn sòoǹ yii: «Un pu ti làá ŋùŋfì atimbun kansikinee sèé.» *

english_verse: You people of Edom can celebrate now! But your time will come to suffer and stagger around naked.
translation_verse: Eedoom yab, nimbi bin kóò Uusi tiŋkinee, ni ŋūǹ kí nīn fàal̀ ki ŋōō! Ama ni mun làá nyɔ̀ ti-Dindaan ŋuul kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaau poon. Ni làá gbí ní kí lòotī ki dɔ̄ dicancaŋgbeel.

english_verse: The people of Zion have paid for their sins, and the Lord will soon let them return home. But, people of Edom, you will be punished, and your sins exposed.
translation_verse: Siiyɔn tiŋki, a-tafadaaldi kúntì, baa làá ti cùnnì-si kuyuŋu. Ama nimbi Eedoom yab, ti-Dindaan làá dáaĺ ni-tafal ni-yìntitam pu, ní kí nyāntí ni-kpitii kí páań mpaampiin pu.

english_verse: Our Lord, don't forget how we have suffered and been disgraced.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, taa súntí tin bāań-ti nee pu. Kpèè kí wāl̀ bi nín bí ki sìí-ti puee.

english_verse: Foreigners and strangers have taken our land and our homes.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kin a tīī-tee kpántì binicambi yaka, biba di kíǹ ki yì ti-diiŋŋi.

english_verse: We are like children whose mothers are widows.
translation_verse: Ti-baabi kaa ti bí, ti kpántì ataŋkpiibil. Ti-nab kpántì bikpiipoobi.

english_verse: The water we drink and the wood we burn cost far too much.
translation_verse: Ti dāā ti-nyim ní kí nín ká kí nyɔ̀, ti dāā ti-dɔi ní kí nín ká kí kpāā.

english_verse: We are terribly mistreated; we are worn out and can find no rest.
translation_verse: Bin bí ki sàantí-tee kā ti-pu ní kàti kati, ti-fam tīl̀, taa pée cáá diŋuŋfil báà fiii.

english_verse: We had to surrender to Egypt and Assyria because we were hungry.
translation_verse: Ti tàntī ŋŋal Eejipiti nì Asuur timmun watil pú ní kí wàatī kí nín ká tin ti làá jēe.

english_verse: Our ancestors sinned, but they are dead, and we are left to pay for their sins.
translation_verse: Ti-baabi bin nìn ŋá ikpitee kaa ti bí, ní bi-kpitii gìńdi dɔ́miń ki nyīkiǹ timbi pu.

english_verse: Slaves are now our rulers, and there is no one to set us free.
translation_verse: Iyumbu di jíń ti-pu dinyandi ní ubɔ kpá kí jòoń-ti.

english_verse: We are in danger from brutal desert tribes; we must risk our lives just to bring in our crops.
translation_verse: Biyipɔɔdambi bin bí kuteeunee puee, ti dù ti-maŋfal kí ŋá awoo ní kí nín ká tijin.

english_verse: Our skin is scorched from fever and hunger.
translation_verse: Ŋkùm nín cúú-ti tikpil puee, ti-wunti píĺ ní kpaŋkpam kii ti kā dibubulinee.

english_verse: On Zion and everywhere in Judah our wives and daughters are being raped.
translation_verse: Bi dōoǹ nì binimpoobi mpɔn Siiyɔn tiŋkin, ki dōoǹ nì bisapɔmbi Juuda timmun.

english_verse: Our rulers are strung up by their arms, and our nation's advisors are treated shamefully.
translation_verse: Bi cúú bikàliŋkpilib ki lúntì idɔ pu, kaa dū bijaŋkpilib ki yíiń tiba.

english_verse: Young men are forced to do the work of slaves; boys must carry heavy loads of wood.
translation_verse: Binaacimpɔmbi tú tinàti ní mbiyaamu tú idɔbɔɔ ki còom̄ ki gbéetí.

english_verse: Our leaders are not allowed to decide cases in court, and young people no longer play music.
translation_verse: Bikpilib kaa ti kpáfí ki kàal̀ kitiŋ punyɔkɔ nyɔkɔpu ní binipɔmbi gbēeǹ ilan digaal.

english_verse: Our hearts are sad; instead of dancing, we mourn.
translation_verse: Dipɔɔpindi wáŋkì ti-pɔbiliŋin, ti-ŋool kpántì dikpool.

english_verse: Zion's glory has disappeared! And we are doomed because of our sins.
translation_verse: Ti-beefuuliiki nyáń ti-yil pu ki lítì kitiŋ. An sá-ti mbusu ní, kun puee ti ŋá ikpiti.

english_verse: We feel sick all over and can't even see straight;
translation_verse: An di yì-ti ní ti-pɔbiliŋ fōō tiweendi, ní nnyinnyim yāntì ti kíǹ ki kpèé pùuu.

english_verse: our city is in ruins, overrun by wild dogs.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Siiyɔn jool kpántì kuteeu laakin ŋŋɔkɔmu tú ki yìiǹee.

english_verse: You will rule forever, Lord! You are King for all time.
translation_verse: Ama sii, ti-Dindaan, doooo jaanjaan ní a sá ubɔti, ní a-beejal bí ní ki cá abin abin.

english_verse: Or do you despise us so much that you don't want us?
translation_verse: A lafun dū-ti ki fá kɔkɔ kpataaa níii? A lafun gíí ti-pu diŋuul tikpil míǹ níii?

english_verse: I saw a windstorm blowing in from the north. Lightning flashed from a huge cloud and lit up the whole sky with a dazzling brightness. The fiery center of the cloud was as shiny as polished metal,
translation_verse: M bíi kpèéyee ní ki ká kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kubɔ nyánní ŋgan pú ki kpáaǹní ditagbaŋkpaandi diba din poon ní ŋŋmi nìn bée. Ŋwalifi nìn māntì tú ditagbandee. Di-kansikin nìn fòol̄ ní lìblib ní ki jìliŋkī kii tikúti tin bi dūu púĺ ŋŋminee.

english_verse: and in that center I saw what looked like four living creatures. They were somewhat like humans,
translation_verse: Kansikinee, an gíti bí kii tiwan tinaa tin cáá kufoouee bée. Tiwan tinaa gbanti nìn náań nì binib ní.

english_verse: except that each one had four faces and four wings.
translation_verse: Tiwan tinaa gbanti kɔkɔ nìn cáá inimbiin inaa inaa nì ifeen inaa inaa ní.

english_verse: Their legs were straight, but their feet looked like the hoofs of calves and sparkled like bronze.
translation_verse: Ti-tapaŋŋi nìn tèen̄, ní ti-taaŋi náań nì dinapɔmbil tafuŋfukuti, ní ki gíti jìl̀ kii tasa kúti tin bi jɔ̄lifèe.

english_verse: The four creatures were standing back to back with the tips of their wings touching. They moved together in every direction, without turning their bodies.
translation_verse: Ti-feeŋyi nyɔkɔpuee nìn tùutī tɔb. Báà ŋma nìn pée còom̄ ní ki cá u-nyɔkɔpu kaa fàtī u-ba.

english_verse: Each creature had the face of a human in front, the face of a lion on the right side, the face of a bull on the left, and the face of an eagle in back.
translation_verse: Tiwan tinaa tin cáá kufoouee kɔkɔ nìn cáá inimbiin inaa inaa: nnimbiin ŋun bí nyɔkɔpuee sá unil nimbiin, ŋun bí ŋgiil púee sá gbikinti nimbiin, ŋun bí ŋgan púee sá unaja nimbiin ní ŋun bí boon púee sá ukaalun nimbiin.

english_verse: Two wings of each creature were spread out and touched the wings of the creatures on either side. The other two wings of each creature were folded against its body.
translation_verse: Ti-feeŋyi ili kpátì kutaa ní ki tùutī tɔb ní ifeen ili in kíǹee bīī ti-wunti pu.

english_verse: The four living creatures went wherever the Spirit led them, and they moved together without turning their bodies, because each creature faced straight ahead.
translation_verse: Báà ŋma nìn còom̄ ní ki cá ku-nyɔkɔpu. Tì nìn ŋūǹ kí cù laakin kamaa ŋfam yaa là tí cùee kí taa fàtī ti-ba.

english_verse: The creatures were glowing like hot coals, and I saw something like a flaming torch moving back and forth among them. Lightning flashed from the torch every time its flame blazed up.
translation_verse: Tiwan tinaa gbanti kansikinee, an nìn bí kii amɔsiŋkoon ŋin fòol̄ lìblibee, ní an gíti bí kii iŋminaapool yamee ní an yìiǹ an kɔkɔ pu. Ŋŋmi nìn jìliŋkī ní utaa nín ŋmóò puee nyēē ŋŋmee poon.

english_verse: The creatures themselves moved as quickly as sparks jumping from a fire.
translation_verse: Tiwanee nìn cá ki gítiń malaa malaa, a lì kii utaa nín tòó puee ní.

english_verse: I then noticed that on the ground beside each of the four living creatures was a wheel,
translation_verse: M pée bíi kpèé tiwan tin cáá kufoou gbantee ní ki ká tiba bí kii ataayee sí kitiŋ ki kɔ́ĺ-tì.

english_verse: shining like chrysolite. Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
translation_verse: Ataayee nìn jìl̀ kii ataŋkpamɔntee ní. Ŋì nìn sá abaanti ní ki gíti bí kii ŋi kóò tɔbinee.

english_verse: so that they could move in any direction without turning.
translation_verse: Ŋi nìn ŋūǹ kí còom̀ kí cù ajannaatil kɔkɔ pu kí taa màntī.

english_verse: The rims of the wheels were large and frightening, and they had eyes all the way around them.
translation_verse: Ŋi-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn cáá tifaandi ní animbil ŋin jìl̀ee bí ŋi-pu ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: The creatures controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the four creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels were beside them.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, tì yaa bíi còom̄aaa, tì yaa yúl̀aaa, tì yaa tí yíkìi jɔ́m̀ yilpuɔɔɔ, ataayee mun nìn ŋáań míǹ ní mbaantiim, di sá yii tiwan tin cáá kufoouee fam nìn bí ataayee poon ní.

english_verse: Above the living creatures, I saw something that was sparkling like ice, and it reminded me of a dome. Each creature had two of its wings stretched out toward the creatures on either side, with the other two wings folded against its body.
translation_verse: Kugbɔŋu gbanti taapuee, tiwan tin cáá kufoouee kamaa nìn cáá ifeen ili kpátì ki túĺ tɔb, ní ifeen ili in kíǹee nìn bīī ti-wunti pu.

english_verse: Whenever the creatures flew, their wings roared like an ocean or a large army or even the voice of God All-Powerful. And whenever the creatures stopped, they folded their wings against their bodies.
translation_verse: Tì yaa nìn ŋàaǹ ki cée, m gbìl̀ ti-feeŋyi wooku pu. Kuwoou gbanti nìn náań nì tiŋku wooku àá ditaadundi din sá Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan neenee àá dijanjakitikpaandi wookuee ní. Tì yaa nìn síl̀ee, tì nìn kpáb̀ ti-feeŋyi ní.

english_verse: I then saw what looked like a throne made of sapphire, and sitting on the throne was a figure in the shape of a human.
translation_verse: Yilpu niinee ní tiba bí kii safiir taŋkpalee ki náań nì dibeejal. An beejalee yilpu kúntí kuntee, kunaŋu kubɔ nìn tɔ́kɔ́ ki náań nì unil.

english_verse: From the waist up, it was glowing like metal in a hot furnace, and from the waist down it looked like the flames of a fire. The figure was surrounded by a bright light,
translation_verse: M nìn ká yii kunaŋuee jìl̀ kii tikúmanee ní an gíti bí kii ŋŋmi māntìi tú-kùee. Kí yòon̄ tin bí ki náań nì ku-caŋ yilpu nì taapuee, m nìn ká tiba bí ki náań nì ŋŋmi ní ki wāĺ bɔ́iii ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: as colorful as a rainbow that appears after a storm. I realized I was seeing the brightness of the Lord's glory! So I bowed with my face to the ground, and just then I heard a voice speaking to me.
translation_verse: Ŋwalifi ŋun nìn māntìi túee nìn náań nì dikuntinyindi nín gà ditagbandin ntaawìiń puee ní. Ŋwalifi gbanti nìn dàkà ti-Dindaan nyooti bítam ní. M nín ká mimmee ní m tātìi gbāaǹ m-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ. Niinee ní m gbìl̄ ubɔ bíi sòoǹ nì mi.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, I want you to stand up and listen.”
translation_verse: U nìn bíi sòoǹee nìn bí-mi yii: «Sii nisaaleen, yīkìí sīĺ ḿ sòoǹ nì si.»

english_verse: After he said this, his Spirit took control of me and lifted me to my feet. Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u bíi sòoǹ nì mi mimmee ní Unimbɔti Fam kɔ́ m-ni ní ki yōoǹ-mi ki síiǹ. Niinee ní m pílifì un bíi sòoǹ nì mee.

english_verse: Ezekiel, I am sending you to the people of Israel. They are just like their ancestors who rebelled against me and refused to stop.
translation_verse: U bí-mi yii: «Sii nisaaleen, m làá tɔ̄-si Isirayeel yab cee, bíǹ bin sá pɔɔgaatib ki yíkìi jáń nì mee. Bi pée jáà nì mi kaa gbèentí kii bi-naanjabee ní.

english_verse: They are stubborn and hardheaded. But I, the Lord God, have chosen you to tell them what I say.
translation_verse: Binib bin yiliŋ pɔ̄ɔ̄ bi-pɔbiliŋ gbìfì gbanti cee ní m bíi tūǹ-si nee. Á tùkù-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bíi sòoǹ puee sèé>.

english_verse: Those rebels may not even listen, but at least they will know that a prophet has come to them.
translation_verse: Niinee pɔɔgaatib gbanti yaa pílifiǹ-saaa, bi yaa kaa pílifiǹ-saaa, bi làá béé yii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ bí bi-kansikin.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of them or of anything they say. You may think you're in the middle of a thorn patch or a bunch of scorpions. But be brave
translation_verse: «Ama sii nisaaleen, á taa fàŋkì-bi kí taa fàŋkì bi-nyɔɔbuŋŋi. Bi làá kpákáǹ-si. Án làá nīn bí kii ikuŋkum di māntìi tú-si àá a kā inoom puee ní. Taa yàntī bi-nyɔɔbuŋŋi ń fàaǹ-si kí taa fàŋkì bi-nimbiiŋyi, di sá yii bi sá pɔɔgaatib ní.

english_verse: and preach my message to them, whether they choose to listen or not.
translation_verse: Bi yaa bíi pílifíǹ-saaa, bi yaa kaa bíi pílifiǹ-saaa, á dū m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi kí tùkù-bi, di sá yii pɔɔgaatib ní bi sá.

english_verse: Ezekiel, don't rebel against me, as they have done. Instead, listen to everything I tell you. And now, Ezekiel, open your mouth and eat what I am going to give you.
translation_verse: «Ama sii nisaaleen, á pīlifì tin m cáá kí tùkù-see, á taa nín̄ sá pɔɔgaati kii bimbee. Wàan̄ a-nyɔkɔ ní kí dū tin m làá tīī-see kí ŋmɔ́.»

english_verse: Just then, I saw a hand stretched out toward me. And in it was a scroll.
translation_verse: Niinee, m bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, ŋŋal ŋubɔ tāntì ki túĺ m-watil pú. Ŋu nìn ŋúb́ kugbɔŋu kubɔ an kpáb́.

english_verse: The hand opened the scroll, and both sides of it were filled with words of sadness, mourning, and grief.
translation_verse: Ŋu cúú kugbɔŋuee ki kpátì. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ ajanliitil pu. Tin bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋuee poonee nìn sá iyaliŋki nì nsiim nì dinimbinaamandi bɔti ŋma ní.

english_verse: He handed me the scroll and said, “Eat this and fill up on it.” So I ate the scroll, and it tasted sweet as honey.
translation_verse: U nìn kútì ki lī yii: «Sii nisaaleen, dū kugbɔŋu kun m cáa bíi tìì-si nee kí ŋmɔ́ a-pool ń díkí.» Niinee ní m dū-ku ki ŋmɔ́ ní an gíti mɔ́ɔkì m-nyɔkɔn kii tisiilee.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, I am sending you to your own people.
translation_verse: Niin ní u nín bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, nín̄ cá Isirayeel yab cee kí dū m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi kí nàatī-bi.

english_verse: They are Israelites, not some strangers who speak a foreign language you can't understand. If I were to send you to foreign nations, they would listen to you.
translation_verse: M yaa bàà tú-si anibul akpaan ŋin sòoǹ isooncaan in pɔ̄ɔ̄ aa ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ taapuee cee gba, bi bàà làá pīlifiǹ-si.

english_verse: But the people of Israel will refuse to listen, because they have refused to listen to me. All of them are stubborn and hardheaded,
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab kaa làá pīlifiǹ-si, di sá yii baa là kí pīlifiǹ-mi ní. Kun yì-tèe di sá yii bi-yiliŋ pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní bi-pɔbiliŋ mun dūu tīlifì.

english_verse: so I will make you as stubborn as they are.
translation_verse: Ama m làá pɔ̄ɔkì a-pɔbil kii bi-yalee, ní kí pɔ̄ɔkì a-yil kii bi-yaŋee!

english_verse: Then go to the people who were brought here to Babylonia with you and tell them you have a message from me, the Lord God. Do this, whether they listen to you or not.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee á cù a-yab bin ní bi cúú kuyuŋuee cee. Á sòoǹ nì bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín lī puee sɔ̀>. Bi yaa bíi pílifíǹ-saaa, bi yaa kaa bíi pílifíǹ-saaa, sii dee sòoǹ nì bi.»

english_verse: The Spirit lifted me up, and as the glory of the Lord started to leave, I heard a loud, thundering noise behind me.
translation_verse: Niinee Unimbɔti Fam yōoǹ-mi ki cáa jɔ́m̀, ní m gbìl̄ m-boon pú dibintiŋkpaandi pu yii: «Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan laakin u lèekī u-nyooti ki dàkèe.»

english_verse: It was the sound made by the creatures' wings as they brushed against each other, and by the rumble of the wheels beside them.
translation_verse: M nìn gbìl̄ tiwan tin cáá kufoouee feeŋyi nín gbáà tɔb ki ŋáań kuwoou kuŋyee mun pu, ní ki gbìl̄ ataa ŋin nìn bí ki kɔ́ĺ-tèe wooku mun pu. An nìn sá dibintiŋkpaandi ní.

english_verse: Then the Spirit carried me away. The Lord's power had taken complete control of me, and I was both annoyed and angry.
translation_verse: Ŋfam min bàà yōoǹ-mi ki jɔ́m̀ee kpáaǹ-mi ki búntì. Ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu nìn dɔ́miń m-pu tikpil, ní m nín cá nì kunimbaaun, kaa ti nyí tin poon m bée.

english_verse: When I was back with the others living at Abib Hill near the Chebar River, I sat among them for seven days, shocked at what had happened to me. The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch (Ezekiel
translation_verse: M nìn bàn̄ Teel-Abiibi bin bi cúú kuyuŋu bi bí Keebaar mɔɔgbandee cee. M nìn kāl̀ bi-kansikin iwiin iluli, ní ki bākatiǹ m-ba sèeee. Eeseekiyeel làá nīn sá Isirayeel nibul ciitiliu (Kpèè

english_verse: Seven days after I had seen the brightness of the Lord's glory, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Iwiin iluli gbanti jítèe ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
translation_verse: «A sá nisaaleen ní, ama m dū-si ki kpántì uciitil á nīn wàal̀ Isirayeel nibul. Á pīlifì m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi ní kí dū m-bɔkpaafikaati nee kí nàatī Isirayeel yab.

english_verse: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways so they won't be punished. If you refuse, you are responsible for their death.
translation_verse: M yaa tùkū unikpiti yii: <A làá kpú>, ní aa kpáafì-u àá kaa sòon̄ nì u ú kpántí u-bimbikpitim kí ŋmátée, unikpitee làá kpú u-kpitii pu, ama sii pu ní m làá dū udaan kúm kpuulool kí lúntí.

english_verse: However, if you do warn them, and they keep on sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
translation_verse: Ama a yaa kpáafì unikpiti ní waa fātì u-boon ki tīī u-kpitii nì u-bimbikpitimee, u làá kpú u-kpitii pu, ní sii ń fīī a-ba.

english_verse: Now suppose faithful people start sinning, and I decide to put stumbling blocks in their paths to make them fall. They deserve to die because of their sins. So if you refuse to warn them, I will forget about the times they were faithful, and I will hold you responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Deedeedaan yaa fātì u-boon ki tīī u-deedeetuuŋŋi ní ki kíǹ ki bíi ŋáań tin kaa bí deedeeyee, m làá yàntī ú gbéetí kí lítí ní kí kpú. A yaa kaa kpáafì-u, u làá kpú u-kpitii pu. Baa ti làá téetí u-tunnyaaŋŋi ŋin u nìn ŋá njaminee pu, ama sii pu ní m làá dū u-kúm kpuulool kí lúntí.

english_verse: But if you do warn them, and they listen to you and stop sinning, I will let them live. And you will be innocent. Ezekiel Cannot Talk
translation_verse: Ama a yaa kpáafì deedeedaan gbanti yii ú taa ŋá ikpiti, ní u lafun yāntì kaa ŋá ikpitee, u làá ŋmátí, di sá yii a kpáafì-u, ní siiyee, a làá ká difiil.» Unimbɔti yāntì Eeseekiyeel ŋmíl̀

english_verse: The Lord took control of me and said, “Stand up! Go into the valley, and I will talk with you there.”
translation_verse: M gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan bítam pu m-ni, ní u bí-mi yii: «Yīkìm̄, nín̄ cá ditantakalin, m làá sòoǹ nì si niin.»

english_verse: I immediately went to the valley, where I saw the brightness of the Lord's glory, just as I had seen it near the Chebar River, and I bowed with my face to the ground.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m cúú ditantakal saŋŋu ki nín cá. Ti-Dindaan tí lēē u-nyooti ki dàkā niin kii m nín nìn tí ká Keebaar mɔɔgbandi pu puee. M ká mimmee ní ki tātìi gbāaǹ m-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ.

english_verse: His Spirit took control of me and lifted me to my feet. Then the Lord said: Go back and lock yourself in your house!
translation_verse: Niinee Unimbɔti Fam kɔ́ m-ni ní ki yōoǹ-mi ki síiǹ m-taaŋi pu. U bí yii: «Nín̄ kùǹ kí dūú pìin̄ kí kpàl̄ a-ba pu.

english_verse: and I will make you unable to talk or to warn those who have rebelled against me.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī a-nyɔkɔ ń kpú ní á kpántí umuun, án nín làá ŋá pu á taa ti ŋmā kí wòoǹ-bee, di sá yii pɔɔgaatib ní bi sá.

english_verse: But the time will come, when I will tell you what to say, and you will again be able to speak my message. Some of them will listen; others will be stubborn and refuse to listen.
translation_verse: Ama m yaa sòon̄ nì see, á wàan̄ a-nyɔkɔ kí tùkù-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé>. Un yaa làá pīlifèe ń pīlifì, un kaa làá pīlifèe ń taa pīlifì, di sá yii pɔɔgaatib ní bi sá.»

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, find a brick and sketch a picture of Jerusalem on it.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, pīlifì, yòon̄ kuyɔkɔu brikisiu kí dūú bíĺ a-nimbiin. Lēē brikisee pu Jeerusaleem tiŋki.

english_verse: Then prepare to attack the brick as if it were a real city. Build a dirt mound and a ramp up to the top and surround the brick with enemy camps. On every side put large wooden poles as though you were going to break down the gate to the city.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, á lēē kí dàkà yii bi māntìi tú-kì: gbà abɔbil kí gbà ntam kí kpúkuń digundi caŋin. Lēē bijanjaliibi tantib ní kí lēē tijanjawan kí màntīí tū-kì.

english_verse: The brick stands for Jerusalem, so attack it! Stare at it and shout angry warnings.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, á fàtīí kpèè Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin bi māntìi tú kí jáǹ-kèe. Á tàntī a-ŋaliŋu ncal ní kí sòoǹ m-nyɔɔbundi kí tɔ̄ ki-pu.

english_verse: Get a large bowl. Then mix together wheat, barley, beans, lentils, and millet, and make some bread. This is what you will eat for the
translation_verse: «Yòon̄ bilee nì ɔɔji nì atuun nì ikpintumpu nì iyoo nì bilee un pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Dū kɔkɔ kí ŋá disambibaantiilin kí ŋmàlim̀ kí dūú ŋá kpɔnɔ. Iwiin saalaa kpá alaataa anaa in a làá dūú dòon̄ a-takakal puee, tijin tin a làá nīn jīǹee dee.

english_verse: Use dried human waste to start a fire, then bake the bread on the coals where everyone can watch you.
translation_verse: Bi nín cáá ɔɔji ki ŋáań kalaabi bi bí puee, míǹ ní a-jinti làá nīn bí. Á dū binib binti kí kpāā ŋŋmi kí púĺ kpɔnɔb gbanti báà ŋma nimbiin.»

english_verse: When I scatter the people of Israel among the nations, they will also have to eat food that is unclean, just as you must do.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kútì ki lī yii: «Míǹ ní Isirayeel yab làá jī tijin tin kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee nnicantimu mun poon m làá jà-bi kí cùnnèe.»

english_verse: I said, “Lord God, please don't make me do that! Never in my life have I eaten food that would make me unacceptable to you. I've never eaten anything that died a natural death or was killed by a wild animal or that you said was unclean.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní m téeń yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, maa kɔ́ǹ m-ba tijɔkɔndi ki ká! Doooo m-biyatin, maa láa pée ŋmɔ́ kuwaŋkuluu kun kpíìyee àá kuwaŋkuluu kun ní upeecuncuti cúúyee. Báà kunaŋu kun kòóyee kaa láa pée kɔ́ m-nyɔkɔn.»

english_verse: The Lord replied, “Instead of human waste, I will let you bake your bread on a fire made from cow manure.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-mi yii: «An yaa sée, m pú-si nsan á dū tinaabin kí kpāā ŋŋmi kí púĺ a-kpɔnɔu kí yàntī tinibin.»

english_verse: Ezekiel, the people of Jerusalem will starve. They will have so little food and water that they will be afraid and hopeless.
translation_verse: Ní u gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Nisaaleen, m làá kúntí kpɔnɔb bin bi dūu kpáafì Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee. Binib làá dāá ŋmàntī bi-jinti ní kí ŋmɔ́ kunimbaaun, ní kí dāá ŋmàntī nnyim kí nyɔ̀ kufaaŋŋun.

english_verse: Everyone will be shocked at what is happening, and, because of their sins, they will die a slow death.”
translation_verse: Di sá kpɔnɔ nì nnyim làá dāá lóó-bi, ní báà ŋma dāa kíǹ ki bí dinyoondin. Bi làá dāá dúntí ní kí kpú bi-kpitii pu.»

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, get a sharp sword and use it to cut off your hair and beard. Weigh the hair and divide it into three equal piles.
translation_verse: «Sii nisaaleen, yòon̄ bɔlfi kí dūú ŋá kijikoolkaai. Á dū-kì kí kòol̀ a-yil nì a-nyimpul. Míǹ boonee, á ŋmàntī tiyikpiti tin a kōol̀ee saniya pu ní kí cúú yàkatī mita pu.

english_verse: After you attack the brick that stands for Jerusalem, burn one pile of your hair on the brick. Chop up the second pile and let the small pieces of hair fall around the brick. Throw the third pile into the wind, and I will strike it with my own sword.
translation_verse: Bi nín māntìi tú kitiŋ kí jáǹ-kì puee yaa láa kúntèe, á dāá dū dijandi diba kí wà ŋŋmi kitiŋ kansikin. Á dāá yòon̄ dijanliliitiil kí dū a-tàataajiki kí fáá kí màntīí tū kitiŋ. Á dāá dū dijantataatiil din kíǹee kí yàaǹ kubuŋu ń yòon̄ ní man ń dāá dū m-tàataajiki kí páań di-boon.

english_verse: Keep a few of the hairs and wrap them in the hem of your clothes.
translation_verse: Ama á dāá kíń tikutee fiii kí dūú fúuń a-wampeeŋkaati lookun.

english_verse: Then pull out a few of those hairs and throw them in the fire, so they will also burn. This fire will spread, destroying everyone in Israel.
translation_verse: Á dāá lēē pooki kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin án wà. Ŋŋmi gbanti làá dāá nyàtī kí bà Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ cee.

english_verse: I am the Lord God, and I have made Jerusalem the most important place in the world, and all other nations admire it.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi sòoǹ yii: Kpèèmaan Jeerusaleem tiŋki! M dū-kì ki ŋá atimbun kansikin, ní ntimu māntìi tú-kì.

english_verse: But the people of Jerusalem rebelled and refuse to obey me. They ignored my laws and have become even more sinful than the nations around them.
translation_verse: Ama Jeerusaleem yab dū marab bin m tīī-bee ki fá. Bi yíì kaa nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi. Bi gíti ŋá ikpiti ki jítiǹ atimbun nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-bee nib. Di sá yii bi dū m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab ki fá kaa tɔ́-ŋi.

english_verse: So tell the people of Jerusalem: I am the Lord God! You have refused to obey my laws and teachings, and instead you have obeyed the laws of the surrounding nations. You have become more rebellious than any of them!
translation_verse: An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii: Ni jáń nì mi ki jítiǹ atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-nee, ní kaa tɔ́ m-marabaaa, kaa tí ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi mun, ní kaa kpáàa dī atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-nee marab gba.

english_verse: Now all those nations will watch as I turn against you and punish you
translation_verse: An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii: m làá jáǹ nimbi Jeerusaleem yab. M làá dáaĺ ni-tafal atimbun ŋin kíǹee nimbiin ŋi-nib ń wāl̀.

english_verse: for your sins. Your punishment will be more horrible than anything I've ever done or will ever do again.
translation_verse: Ni-timbiilituuŋŋi puee, m làá jáǹ-ni kii m nín kaa láá pée jáń nì ni dalba dalba puee ní. Maa làá ti pée jáǹ-ni míǹ mun jaanjaan.

english_verse: Parents will be so desperate for food that they will eat their own children, and children will eat their parents. Those who survive this horror will be scattered in every direction.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, bibaatiibi làá dāá ŋmɔ́ bi-biyaamu nanti ní mbiyaamu ń dāá ŋmɔ́ bi-baabi nanti. M làá dāá dáaĺ ni-tafal ní kí jà bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee kí yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: Your sins have disgusted me and made my temple unfit as a place to worship me. So I swear by my own life that I will cut you down and show you no pity.
translation_verse: «An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee nín lī yii, ni nín ŋá pu ki dū ni-waaŋi nì ni-timbiilituuŋŋi ki kɔ́ǹ m-Diiku tijɔkɔndee, ma mun làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-ni. M làá dàkà-ni nnimbinaakulim kaa làá sɔ̄ ni-saai.

english_verse: A third of you will die here in Jerusalem from disease or starvation. Another third will be killed in war. And I will scatter the last third of you in every direction, then track you down and kill you.
translation_verse: Bi yaa cúú-ni ki yākatì mita puee, bìlbil kúm àá ŋkùm làá kpɔ̀ dijandi diba kitiŋin, ní bí dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀ dijandi diba kitiŋ gundi boon. Dijandi din kíǹee, m làá jà-bi kí yàl̄ ijaan kɔkɔ pu ní kí dū m-tàataajiki kí kùl̄ kí páań bi-boon.

english_verse: You will feel my fierce anger until I have finished taking revenge. Then you will know that I, the Lord, was furious because of your disobedience.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi. M làá yàntī m-bum ń tɔ̄ mi-tundi kí cáá kátí ní ḿ tɔ̀ m-pɔntooŋyi. Niinee, ni làá béé yii man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, di sá yii ni nín kaa yú nì mi deedeeyee kaa mɔ̄ǹ-mi.

english_verse: will insult you and make fun of you, but they will also be shocked and terrified at what I did in my anger.
translation_verse: M làá dū m-ŋuul kí sòoǹ Jeerusaleem yab bɔti ní kí wòoǹ-bi tikpil. Atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-kèe làá nīn bèel̄-kì ki sìí-kì, ama kì làá nīn sá mun kii ŋabikee ní ki tīī-bi ní bí fàŋkì. Man ni-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ nì ni.

english_verse: I will destroy your crops until you starve to death, and disasters will strike you like arrows.
translation_verse: «M làá dū ŋkùm kí tɔ̄ ni-pu mí kpɔ̀-ni. Mi làá tīī-ni tiweendi kii ipiinee ní. M làá bīil̀ ni-jiŋkpaafikaati ní kí yàntī ní kpú ŋkùm.

english_verse: Starvation and wild animals will kill your children. I'll punish you with horrible diseases, and your enemies will strike you down with their swords. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M làá dū ŋkùm nì ipeecuncuti kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní í kpɔ̀ ni-biyaamu. Bìlbil kúm nì tipɔmbɔti nì kujaau làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ nì ni.»

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, face the hills of Israel and tell them:
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbikpeeŋu kí túĺ Isirayeel jooŋŋi kí sòoǹ m-nyɔɔbundi kí tɔ̄ ŋi-pu.

english_verse: Listen, you mountains and hills, and every valley and gorge! I, the Lord, am about to turn against you and crush all the places where foreign gods are worshiped.
translation_verse: Lì yii: Isirayeel jooŋŋi, pīlifì anyɔɔbun ŋin ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti cáá kí tùkù bin kóò ni-puee nì bin kóò ŋgbantamu pu nì igalin nì atantaka poonee. U bí yii: <Kpèè, m làá cáań kujaau kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní kí nàan̄ ni-waatootipaaŋyi.

english_verse: Every altar will be smashed, and in front of the idols I will put to death the people who worship them.
translation_verse: Bi làá gbá kí wìil̀ ni-saraafaŋyi nì ni-sambiyaamu mun poon ni tùutī talaalubee. M làá kpɔ̀ ni-kansikin biba kí bíĺ ni-waaŋi gbanti nimbiin.

english_verse: Dead bodies and bones will be lying around the idols and the altars.
translation_verse: M làá dū Isirayeel yab bin kpíìyee wunti kí bíĺ bi-waaŋi nimbiin ní kí kàfì bi-kpabiŋ kí yàaǹ bi-saraafaŋyi pu kí màntīí tū.

english_verse: All over the country, your people will die. And those who survive will know that I, the Lord, did these things.
translation_verse: Ni-kansikin tikpil làá lítí kí kpú. Niinee ní ní béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: I will let some of the people live through this punishment, but I will scatter them among the nations,
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m làá yàntī ni-kansikin biba ń ŋmátí kí taa kpú kujaaun. Bíǹ gbanti di làá dāá yàl̄ kí cù nnicantimun.

english_verse: where they will be prisoners. And when they think of me, they will realize that they disgraced me by rebelling and by worshiping idols. They will hate themselves for the evil things they did,
translation_verse: Bin ŋmátì gbantee làá dāá téetí m-pu bin cúú-bi kuyuŋuee kansikin. Bi làá dāá téetí m nín nāaǹ-bi miŋyee pu. Di sá yii bi nyáń m-boon: bi fātì bi-boon ki tīī-mi ní ki dū bi-nimbikpeeŋu ki báaǹ awaa pu. Niinee bi-naŋki làá dāá nyā nì bi-ba ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi ŋée pu.

english_verse: and they will know that I am the Lord and that my warnings must be taken seriously.
translation_verse: Bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan, ní m nín nìn sòon̄ yii nnaabu làá jēetí bi-puee, maa nìn sòon̄ fám!>»

english_verse: The Lord God then said: Ezekiel, beat your fists together and stomp your feet in despair! Moan in sorrow, because the people of Israel have done disgusting things and now will be killed by enemy troops, or they will die from starvation and disease.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Kpāafì a-ŋalii, fáá a-taaŋi ní kí lì yii: <An bàn̄ an laŋki!>, ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin Isirayeel yab ŋée bàn̄ an laŋki. An kíǹ kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi dee.

english_verse: Those who live far away will be struck with deadly diseases. Those who live nearby will be killed in war. And the ones who are left will starve to death. I will let loose my anger on them!
translation_verse: Bìlbil kúm làá kpɔ̀ bin bínní ndandatee, kujaau làá kpɔ̀ bin bí ki pìl̄ee ní bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee ń kpú ŋkùm. M làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi ní kí cáá kátí.

english_verse: These people used to offer incense to idols at altars built on hills and mountaintops and in the shade of large oak trees. But when they see dead bodies lying around those altars, they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi-nikpiliŋ làá dāá nīn dɔ̄ an kɔkɔ pu fìlfil bi-waaŋi kansikin ki māntìi tú bi-saraafaŋyi nì ajoon nì ŋgbantamu yilpu, nì isuboon nì iwaasufi taapu laakin bi nìn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì bi-waaŋee. Niinee, bi làá dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.

english_verse: I will make their country a barren wasteland, from the Southern Desert to the town of Diblah in the north. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: M làá dàkà-bi m-pɔŋŋu ní kí nàan̄ bi-tiŋki. M làá jà bin kóò ki-puee kí yòon̄ kuteeu ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Riibila tiŋki ŋgan pú. Bi làá dāá béé niin yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that I am saying: Israel will soon come to an end! Your whole country is about to be destroyed
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, pīlifì tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì Isirayeel yabee: An dóò! Nnaabu kpátì ki bàn̄ kitiŋ jannaatiliŋ.

english_verse: as punishment for your disgusting sins. I, the Lord, am so angry
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee an dóò ni-pu: m làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń jēetí ni-pu. Ni-bimbim ní m làá dūú sòoǹ ni-bɔti ní kí pà-ni ni-timbiilituuŋŋi paati.

english_verse: that I will show no pity. I will punish you for the evil you've done, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M làá dàkà-ni nnimbinaakulim kaa làá sɔ̄ ni-saai báà fiii. M làá pà-ni ni-bimbim paati ní kí nyāntí ni-timbiilituuŋŋi kí páań mpaampiin pu. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: There's never been anything like the coming disaster.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀: Nnaabu dòoń, nnaabu ŋun baa láá pée kée dòoń!

english_verse: And when it comes, your life will be over.
translation_verse: An dóò, an dóò ní, nnaabu bíi bɔ́ntí kí jēetí ni-pu, ŋu dòoń!

english_verse: You people of Israel are doomed! Soon there will be panic on the mountaintops instead of celebration.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kóò kitiŋ nee puee, dinàandi dòoń ni-pu! Ŋyunti dòoń, ibɔsoon wiiŋŋu tóobiń. Dipɔɔbiildi làá fōō dipɔɔpindi paaŋŋu ajoon pu.

english_verse: I will let loose my anger and punish you for the evil things you've done. You'll get what you deserve.
translation_verse: An kaa ti làá tàan̄, kɔŋkɔnnee m làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī ni-pu ní kí yàntī m-bum ń tɔ̄ mi-tundi kí cáá kátí. Ni-bimbim ní m làá dūú sòoǹ ni-bɔti ní kí pà-ni ni-timbiilituuŋŋi paati.

english_verse: Your sins are so terrible, that you'll get no mercy from me. Then you will know that I, the Lord, have punished you.
translation_verse: M làá dàkà-ni nnimbinaakulim kaa làá sɔ̄ ni-saai. M làá pà ni-bimbim paati ní kí nyāntí ni-timbiilituuŋŋi kí páań mpaampiin pu. Ni làá dāá béé niinee yii man ni-Dindaan di bíi dátí ni-tafal.

english_verse: Disaster is near! Injustice and arrogance are everywhere,
translation_verse: «Ibɔsoon wiiŋŋu sèé! Ŋu bāań ki dóò. Ipɔŋkpiti bí an kɔkɔ pu, dilambil yíkì tiŋan pu.

english_verse: and violent criminals run free. None of you will survive the disaster, and everything you own and value will be shattered.
translation_verse: Tipɔmbɔti bí kii ndɔ ní bi dūu cóoǹ kí ŋá ikpitee. Ni-wanti tiba kaa ti làá kíń ni-cee, ni-gaajati kaa làá kíńaaa, ni-wíiŋŋu kaa làá kíńaaa, ni-nyooti mun kaa làá tí kíń.

english_verse: and people who sell property will never get it back, because all of you must be punished for your sins. And I won't change my mind!
translation_verse: Báà uwannyafil yaa ŋmátì kaa kpíìyaaa, waa ti làá ŋmā kí gítí kí yòon̄ u-wanti tin u nyáfée. Di sá yii dileedakal din sòoǹ án nín làá nàan̄ samaa kɔkɔ puee kaa làá gbíntí fám. Báà ŋma bí ikpitin, an pu ní báà ubɔ kaa làá ti ká mpɔn.

english_verse: A signal has been blown on the trumpet, and weapons are prepared for battle. But no one goes to war, because in my anger I will strike down everyone in Israel. Israel Is Surrounded The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Bi dāa ŋūǹ kí búń ŋyin kí bɔ́ntí kí cù kujaau, ama báà unibambaanti kaa làá cù. Di sá yii m gíí samaa kɔkɔ pu diŋuul ní.» Ditafadaaldi dɔ̄ ki cí báà ŋma

english_verse: War, disease, and starvation are everywhere! People who live in the countryside will be killed in battle, and those who live in towns will die from starvation or deadly diseases.
translation_verse: An làá nīn sá kujaau ní mmɔŋki, ní bìlbil kúm nì ŋkùm bí adiinni ki nà. Bin bí tisatinee làá kpú kujaaun, ní bin bí kitiŋinee, ŋkùm nì iween ń kpɔ̀-bi.

english_verse: Anyone who survives will escape into the hills, like doves who leave the valleys to find safety. All of you will moan because of your sins.
translation_verse: Bin làá dāá kíń ki bí dimaŋfalinee làá dāá sāǹ kí cù ajoonni. Kii abeenanjil nín yáliŋkí puee, míǹ ní bi làá dāá yāliŋkì bi-kpitii pu.

english_verse: Your hands will tremble, and your knees go limp.
translation_verse: Bi-ŋalii kaa dāa gíti cáá mpɔn, ní bi-tabiŋyiliŋ ń dāá yɔ̀tī.

english_verse: You will put on sackcloth to show your sorrow, but terror will overpower you. Shame will be written all over your faces, and you will shave your heads in despair.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá nīn lōō kpɔsatab, ní bi-wunti ń dāá sāǹ yàrrr. Icoo làá dāá cúú-bi ní gbòooo, ní bí dāá kòol̀ ayibaakpan.

english_verse: Your silver and gold will be thrown into the streets like garbage, because those are the two things that led you into sin, and now they cannot save you from my anger. They are not even worth enough to buy food.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá dū bi-nimbiliŋ kí fá adan pu, bi-sindaariyau làá dāá kpántí kii titampummoolee ní kí tīī-bi. Di sá yii ŋwiin ŋun ti-Dindaan làá dāá gíí diŋuulee, bi-nimbiliŋ àá bi-sindaariyau kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí fīī-bi. Baa làá dāá ká tijin kí jī, ní bi-pooŋyi ń dāá dūú fáká. Di sá yii animbil nì sindaariya di sá bi-yìntitam nyeel.

english_verse: You took great pride in using your beautiful jewelry to make disgusting idols of foreign gods. So I will make your jewelry worthless.
translation_verse: Bi-gaajati nyaaŋku di nìn yòontí-bi ní bi dūu mɔ́ɔ́ awaa ŋin sá ntimbiil wanti nì titantaŋwanee. An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá dū bi-gaajati gbanti kí kpántí titampummool.

english_verse: They will break into my temple and leave it unfit as a place to worship me, but I will look away and let it happen.
translation_verse: Bi yaa láa bíi kɔ̄ntí m-Diiku kun sá m-gaajawantee tijɔkɔndee, maa làá pée ŋá tiba. Digaŋgandambi làá dāá dāan̄ kí kɔ́ǹ-ku tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: Your whole country is in confusion! Murder and violence are everywhere in Israel,
translation_verse: Mɔ́ɔ́ ikusaka, di sá yii binikpɔliibi gbí kitiŋin, ní tipɔmbɔti gbí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.

english_verse: so I will tell the most wicked nations to come and take over your homes. They will put an end to the pride you have in your strong army, and they will make your places of worship unfit to use.
translation_verse: M làá cáań anibul ŋin cáá nnimbinaakulimee ŋí dāan̄ kí fōō bi-diiŋŋi. M làá kúntí bi-pɔndambi lambil, ní kí bīil̀ bi-waatootipaaŋyi.

english_verse: You will be terrified and will desperately look for peace—but there will be no peace.
translation_verse: Dinyoondi bí ki dòoń. Bi làá dāá nyàab̀ ŋgbansɔŋfi kaa làá dāá ká-ŋu.

english_verse: One tragedy will follow another, and you'll hear only bad news. People will beg prophets to give them a message from me. Priests will stop teaching my Law, and wise leaders won't be able to give advice.
translation_verse: Inaabu làá dāá nīn dī tɔb, ní atulim bɔti ń dāá nīn dòoń kaa gbèentí. Binib làá dāá gbàam̀ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu yii ú ká dileedakal. Usaraaŋakpil kaa dāa gíti cáá tiba kí dàkà, ní bitindaŋkpilib kaa dāa gíti cáá isaŋki kí tīī.

english_verse: Even your king and his officials will lose hope and cry in despair. Your hands will tremble with fear. I will punish you for your sins and treat you the same way you have treated others. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ubɔti làá dāá nīn kā dikpool, dibɔtibil kaa dāa gíti cáá dimákal, ní kitiŋee nib báà ŋma wunti dāa gbáà kpàkpakpa. M làá dāá dū bi-bimbim ní kí sòoǹ bi-bɔti, ní kí sòoǹ bi-bɔti kii an nín máaǹ puee. Niinee bi làá dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_verse: Six years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the leaders of Judah were meeting with me in my house. On the fifth day of the sixth month, the Lord God suddenly took control of me,
translation_verse: Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab kuyuŋu ki cùnnì Babiloon abin aluu poon, iŋmal iluu wiŋŋmooŋmootiŋuee, m nìn kā m-dumpu ní Juuda yab tindaŋkpilib kā m-nimbiin. Dicilpu niinee ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti pɔŋŋu kpákatìń m-pu.

english_verse: and I saw something in the shape of a human. This figure was like fire from the waist down, and it was bright as polished metal from the waist up.
translation_verse: M bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, tiwan tiba nìn bí ki náań nì unil. Kí yòon̄ tin bí ki náań nì u-caŋ yamee taapuee, an sá ŋŋmi ní. Kí yòon̄ u-caŋ gbanti kí nīn jɔ́ḿee, an bí kii ŋwalifee ní ki jìl̀ kii sindaariya un bi dūu ŋá ŋŋmin an mántèe.

english_verse: It reached out what seemed to be a hand and grabbed my hair. Then in my vision the Lord's Spirit lifted me into the sky and carried me to Jerusalem. The Spirit took me to the north gate of the temple's inner courtyard, where there was an idol that disgusted the Lord and made him furious.
translation_verse: U nìn tāntì tiba bí kii ŋŋalee ní ki cúú m-yikpiti. Niinee, dileedakal din nìn nyánní Unimbɔti cee gbanti poonee, Ŋfam nìn yōoǹ-mi m kíǹ ki bí yilpu nì taapu kansikin ní ki cáá-mi ki cūnnì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. M ká yii m bí kitiŋ punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋgan púee poon pú, laakin bi nìn dū diwaal din bí ki kùtī Unimbɔti poonee ki síiǹee.

english_verse: Then I saw the brightness of the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen it near the Chebar River.
translation_verse: Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nìn tí nyántì u-nyooti ki dàkā-mi niin, kii m nín nìn ká dileedakal poon pu ditantakalinee.

english_verse: God said to me, “Ezekiel, son of man, look north.” And when I did, I saw that repulsive idol by the altar near the gate.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kpèè ŋgan pú.» Ní m wáaǹ ki kpēē. Kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgan púee, nsaraafan ŋubɔ nìn bí niin. Diwaal din nìn bí ki kùtī Unimbɔti poonee nìn bí nsan ŋun cá nsaraafan gbanti ceeyee.

english_verse: God then said, “Do you see the terrible sins of the people of Israel? Their sins are making my holy temple unfit as a place to worship me. Yet you will see even worse things than this.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, a wāĺ tin bi bíi ŋáańeeee? Isirayeel yab baasii dū bi-ba ki líiǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi kí jà-mi kí wàatī m-circir Kɔŋkooŋŋu ní. Ama a làá gíti ká ntimbiil tuuŋŋi aba mun.»

english_verse: Next, I was taken to the entrance of the courtyard, where I saw a hole in the wall.
translation_verse: Ŋfamee nìn yōoǹ-mi ki cūnnì dicindi punyɔkɔpu. M bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, dibundi diba bí digundin.

english_verse: God said, “Make this hole bigger.” And when I did, I realized it was a doorway.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, lùkù kí cíĺ digundi.» Niinee ní m lùkū ki cíl̀ ní dibundi dōoǹ.

english_verse: “Go in,” God said, “and see what horrible and evil things the people are doing.”
translation_verse: Ní u bí-mi yii: «Kɔ́ kí kpèè ntimbiil nì titantan tuuŋŋi ŋin binib bí doo ki tūǹeee.»

english_verse: Inside, I saw that the walls were covered with pictures of reptiles and disgusting, unclean animals, as well as with idols that the Israelites were worshiping.
translation_verse: M nín kɔ́ee, kun m kée sɔ̀: m nín kpēē ki māntìi túee, m ká bi lēē ikoobu nì tiwaŋkuti tin cáá titantanee digundi kɔkɔ pu. Bi nìn lēē awaa ŋin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab tòotēe di-pu.

english_verse: Seventy Israelite leaders were standing there, including Jaazaniah son of Shaphan. Each of these leaders was holding an incense burner, and the smell of incense filled the room.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib imuŋku ita nì saalaa nìn yú awaayee nimbiin. Bi-kansikinee, Safan jipɔɔn Yasaniya nìn bí. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn ŋúb́ kisambiki kin poon bi tùutī talaalubee ní talaalu un bi tūūyee nyiim nìn jɔ́ḿ kutaa.

english_verse: God said, “Ezekiel, do you see what horrible things Israel's leaders are doing in secret? They have filled their rooms with idols. And they say I can't see them, because they think I have already deserted Israel.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bālifì-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, a wāĺ kun dinibul nee tindaŋkpilib bíi ŋáań dibalineeee? Báà ŋma yú mpaan ŋun pu u-waal bée ní. Bi bí ki pɔ̀ bi-ba ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan kaa wāĺ-ti, u dū u-tiŋki ki fá.>»

english_verse: But I will show you something even worse than this.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti gíti bí-mi yii: «A làá gíti ká bi bíi ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi aba mun.»

english_verse: He took me to the north gate of the temple, where I saw women mourning for the god Tammuz.
translation_verse: Niinee ní u yōoǹ-mi u-diiku punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋgan púee. Binimpoobi biba nìn kā niin ki sūǹ diwaal Tamuusi kpool.

english_verse: God asked me, “Can you believe what these women are doing? But now I want to show you something even worse.”
translation_verse: U bālifì-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kéè a káa! A làá gíti ká ntimbiil tuuŋŋi aba mun.»

english_verse: God said, “Ezekiel, it's bad enough that the people of Judah are doing these disgusting things. But they have also spread violence and injustice everywhere in Israel and have made me very angry. They have disgraced and insulted me in the worst possible way.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bālifì-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kéè a káa! An kaa sá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin Juuda yab bí doo ki ŋáań nee ŋmaniŋma ní bi ŋáań, ama bi gíti bí ní ki ŋáań tipɔmbɔti ki gbítí m-ŋuul. Kɔŋkɔnnee, bíǹ di bátì kisupaŋŋi ki cáa cáǹ bi-maŋfal watil púee.

english_verse: So in my fierce anger, I will punish them without mercy and refuse to help them when they cry out to me.”
translation_verse: An puee, ma mun làá tɔ̄ m-tundi nì m-ŋuul poon. M làá dàkà-bi nnimbinaakulim kaa làá fīī-bi. Bi làá dāá kúuǹ mpɔn kí yíiń-mi, ama maa làá pīlifiǹ-bi.»

english_verse: After that, I heard the Lord shout, “Come to Jerusalem, you men chosen to destroy the city. And bring your weapons!”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, m gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan yíiń mpɔn yii: «Nimbi bin di làá jáǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkee, ní dāam̄maan! Báà ŋma ń nīn ŋúb́ u-janjawanti u-ŋaan kí dāá nàan̄-kì.»

english_verse: I saw six men come through the north gate of the temple, each one holding a deadly weapon. A seventh man dressed in a linen robe was with them, and he was carrying things to write with. The men went into the temple and stood by the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Niinee m ká bininjab biluu nyánní kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki yilpu pú yaka ki ŋúb́ bi-janjawanti. Uninja ubɔ nìn yú bi-kansikin ki pēē ŋŋaapiin bɔkutil ki gbìn̄ kun pu u làá ŋmèe u-caŋ. Bi táá dicilpu ki dɔ́miń ní ki yúl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu.

english_verse: The brightness of God's glory then left its place above the statues of the winged creatures inside the temple and moved to the entrance. The Lord said to the man in the linen robe,
translation_verse: Ní Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nyooti yíkìi dāntì keerubimbi bin pu tì nìn bée ki nín cá kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔpu. Ní ti-Dindaan yíiń uninja un pēē ŋŋaapiin bɔkutil, ki gbìn̄ tipilindi tin pu u làá ŋmèe u-caŋ,

english_verse: “Walk through the city of Jerusalem and mark the forehead of anyone who is truly upset and sad about the terrible things that are being done here.”
translation_verse: ní ki bí-u yii: «Yìiǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki kɔkɔn. Un kamaa bíi yáliŋkí an páb́-u bi nín bíi tūǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋee puee, á dáań udaan yigbeel.»

english_verse: He turned to the other six men and said, “Follow him and put to death everyone who doesn't have a mark on their forehead. Show no mercy or pity! Kill men and women, parents and children. Begin here at my temple, but be sure not to harm those who are marked.” The men immediately killed the leaders who were standing there.
translation_verse: Ní kpɔ̀ kí céetí bitikpilib kí kpáaǹ nnaacimpɔmbiyaamu nì nsapɔmbiyaamu nì mbiyaamu nì binimpoobi. Ama ní taa gbēē bin cáá kudaaŋŋu bi-yigbeel puee. Ní kíĺ m-Diikun doo.» Niinee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi kù bitindaŋkpilib bin nìn bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Pollute the temple by piling the dead bodies in the courtyards. Now get busy!” They left and started killing the people of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-bi yii: «Dūmaan anikpil kí gbéeǹ kunimbɔtidii cindi kí kɔ́ǹ-ku tijɔkɔndi. Nín̄ cámaan!» Ní bi nyáń kunimbɔtidiin ki cūtìi pɔ̄fì binib kitiŋin.

english_verse: I was then alone, so I bowed down and cried out to the Lord, “Why are you doing this? Are you so angry with the people of Jerusalem that everyone must die?”
translation_verse: Bi nín bíi kù binib mimmee, m kíǹ m-baba niin ní m tātìi gbāaǹ kitiŋ m-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ ki téeń yii: «Abàa, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a nín kpáatì a-ŋuul ki sītì Jeerusaleem pu minee, a làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee níii?»

english_verse: The Lord answered, “The people of Israel and Judah have done horrible things. Their country is filled with murderers, and Jerusalem itself is filled with violence. They think that I have deserted them, and that I can't see what they are doing.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí-mi yii: «Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab nín ŋá ikpiti iŋyee wīikí tikpil. Bi yāntì nnikpaakoon gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu ní Jeerusaleem tiŋki gbí ikpiti. Binib bí ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan dū kitiŋ nee ki fá ní kaa wāĺ-ti.>

english_verse: And so I will not have pity on them or forgive them. They will be punished for what they have done.”
translation_verse: An puee m làá dàkà-bi nnimbinaakulim kaa làá sɔ̄ bi-saai. M làá yàntī kun bi ŋée ń fàtīí lítí bi-yil pu.»

english_verse: I saw the dome that was above the four winged creatures, and on it was the sapphire throne.
translation_verse: M bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, kugbɔŋu kubɔ bí keerubimbi yilpu. Kugbɔŋuee puee, Safiir taŋkpal bí ki náań nì dibeejal.

english_verse: The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, “Walk among the four wheels beside the creatures and pick up as many hot coals as you can carry. Then scatter them over the city of Jerusalem.” I watched him as he followed the Lord's instructions.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bí unil un pēē dibɔkutipindee yii: «Kɔ́ ataa ŋin bí keerubimbi taapuee. Yáfí amɔsiŋkoon ŋin bí keerubimbi kansikinee kí gbéeǹ a-ŋaan kí cáá cùnnì kí yàaǹ kitiŋee pu.» M-nimbilaaliyin ní uninjee nín cá.

english_verse: The winged creatures were standing south of the temple when the man walked among them. A cloud filled the inner courtyard,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u nín cée, keerubimbee nìn bí kunimbɔtidii ŋŋaŋgiil pú ní ditagbandi diba gbí dicindi poon pú yalin.

english_verse: and the brightness of the Lord's glory moved from above the creatures and stopped at the entrance of the temple. The entire temple was filled with his glory, and the courtyard was dazzling bright.
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan nyooti yíkì ki dāntì keerubimbee yilpu ki nín cá kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔpu. Ditagbandee nìn gbí kunimbɔtidii ní ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn ŋmíntí dicindi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The sound of the creatures' wings was as loud as the voice of God All-Powerful and could even be heard in the outer courtyard.
translation_verse: A yaa nìn bí dicindi boon púee, a nìn gbìl̀ keerubimbi feeŋyi nín nìn ŋáań kuwoou kuŋyee pu. An nìn bí kii Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan yaa bíi sòoǹ u-neel nín bí puee ní.

english_verse: One of the four creatures reached its hand into the fire among them and gave him some of the hot coals. The man took the coals and left.
translation_verse: Keerubimbee kansikinee, unil ubɔ nìn tāntì u-ŋal ki túĺ ŋŋmi ŋun bí bi-kansikinee. U lēē amɔsiŋkoon ki gbéeǹ uninjee ŋaaŋyi ní úǹ cáa búntì.

english_verse: I noticed again that each of the four winged creatures had what looked like human hands under their wings,
translation_verse: Niinee tiba nyáń keerubimbee feeŋyi taapu ki náań nì nniŋal.

english_verse: and I saw the four wheels near the creatures. These wheels were shining like chrysolite.
translation_verse: M gíti bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, ataa anaa dee, ditaal diba bí ki kɔ́ĺ keerubimbee ubɔ. Ataayee nìn jìl̀ kii ditaŋkpamɔntiil din bi yíì Kriistooliitee ní.

english_verse: Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
translation_verse: Ataayee nìn náań ní ki bí kii ŋi kɔ́ tɔbinee.

english_verse: so that they could move in any direction without turning. The wheels moved together whenever the creatures moved.
translation_verse: Ŋi nìn ŋūǹ kí cù ajannaatil pú kaa māntì. Keerubimbee yaa fātì bi-nimbiiŋyi ki túĺ laakiŋyee, niin ní ŋi cá kaa fàtī ŋi-ba.

english_verse: I also noticed that the wheels and the creatures' bodies, including their backs, their hands, and their wings, were covered with eyes.
translation_verse: Keerubimbee wunti kɔkɔ nì bi-boon nì bi-ŋalii nì bi-feeŋyi nìn sá animbil ŋma ní ki jìl̀, míǹ mbaantiim ní ataayee mun nìn bí.

english_verse: And I heard a voice calling these “the wheels that spin.”
translation_verse: M nìn gbìl̄ bi yíiń ataayee yii «kunaakpaabuŋŋu.»

english_verse: Each of the winged creatures had four faces: the face of a bull, the face of a human, the face of a lion, and the face of an eagle.
translation_verse: Keerubim kamaa nìn cáá inimbiin inaa: Mpeekaa nìn sá Keerubim nimbiin, ní nliliiti sá unil nimbiin, ní ntataati sá gbikinti nimbiin ní nnanaati sá ukaalun nimbiin.

english_verse: These were the same creatures I had seen near the Chebar River. They controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels stayed beside them.
translation_verse: Bi yaa nìn yúl̀ee, ataayee mun nìn yūlifí ní. Bi yaa nìn yíkì ki dāntèe, ŋi mun nìn yíkí kí dàntī ní, di sá yii tiwan tin cáá kufoouee di nìn kpāantí-ŋi ki còom̄. Ti-Dindaan yíkì kunimbɔtidiin

english_verse: Then I watched the brightness of the Lord's glory move from the entrance of the temple and stop above the winged creatures.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn yíkì kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔpu ní ki cūtì ki kíǹ ki bí keerubimbi pu.

english_verse: They spread their wings and flew into the air with the wheels at their side. They stopped at the east gate of the temple, and the Lord's glory was above them.
translation_verse: Niinee keerubimbi kpátì bi-feeŋyi ní m ká bi yíkì kitiŋ, bi nì ataayee dicilpu ki nín cá. Bi cūtìi yúl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nyooti nìn bí bi-pu ki jìl̀.

english_verse: I knew for sure that these were the same creatures I had seen beneath the Lord's glory near the Chebar River.
translation_verse: Keebaar mɔɔgbaŋŋi puee, m nìn ká tiwannáaŋkaal tibaantiil gbanti yú Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu taapu. Niinee ní m béè yii an sá keerubimbi.

english_verse: They had four wings with hands beneath them, and they had the same four faces as those near the River. Each creature moved straight ahead without turning.
translation_verse: Bi-nimbiiŋyi nìn náań nì bin m bàà ká Keebaar mɔɔl caŋinee. Keerubimbee nìn còom̄ ní ki túĺ bi-nimbiin cáaa.

english_verse: and I told them everything the Lord had shown me.
translation_verse: M nìn tùkū bin bi cúú kuyuŋuee tin ti-Dindaan lēē ki dàkā-mee.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, these men are making evil plans and giving dangerous advice to the people of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ŋfamee nìn tùkū-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kpèè binib bin di bɔ́ntí atuŋkpiti ki tìì isaŋkikpiti kitiŋ nee poonee sɔ̀.

english_verse: They say things like, ‘Let's build more houses. This city is like a cooking pot over a fire, and we are the meat, but at least the pot keeps us from being burned in the fire.’
translation_verse: Bi bí ki lì yii: <Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋubɔ poonee, baa ti làá mā adiin doo! Kitiŋ nee sá kii daanseeyee ní, ní timbi sá kii tinan tin bi làá dūú tɔ́kɔń u-poonee.>

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of me and told me to tell these leaders: I, the Lord God, know what you leaders are saying.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan Fam kpákatìń m-pu ní ki kpáafì-mi ḿ sòoǹ yii: «Lì yii ti-Dindaan nín bí puee sɔ̀. Ni nín sòoǹ puee dee, Isirayeel yab! M nyí ni-landɔkɔi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: You have murdered so many people that the city is filled with dead bodies!
translation_verse: Ni kūū binib tikpil kitiŋ nee poon. Ni yāntì anikpil dɔ̄ ki-saŋkakpiliŋ fìlfil.

english_verse: This city is indeed a cooking pot, but the bodies of those you killed are the meat. And so I will force you to leave Jerusalem,
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii: Kitiŋ nee sá kii daanseeyee ní, ama bin ni kūū kitiŋ nee poonee di sá tinan. Ama nimbee, m làá jà-ni kí nyāntí kitiŋ nee poon.

english_verse: and I'll send armies to attack you, just as you fear.
translation_verse: Ni fàŋkí kujaauaa! Too m làá cáań kujaau kí tɔ̄ ni-pu, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: You will be killed in your own country, but not before you realize that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī ní kpú kujaaun ní kí sòoǹ ni-bɔti Isirayeel tiŋkin táb. Niinee ní ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: You leaders claim to be meat in a cooking pot, but you won't be protected by this city. No, you will die at the border of Israel.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ nee kaa ti làá nīn sá kii daanseeyee ní nimbi mun kaa ti làá nīn sá tinan kin kā u-poon. Isirayeel tiŋki poon ní m làá sòoǹ ni-bɔti.

english_verse: You will realize that while you were following the laws of nearby nations, you were disobeying my laws and teachings. And I am the Lord!
translation_verse: Niinee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan. Naa nóó m-marab kaa tí ŋúb́ m-koobiliŋ mun. Ama ni nóó atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-nee koobiliŋ ní.»

english_verse: Before I finished speaking, Pelatiah dropped dead. I bowed down and cried out, “Please, Lord God, don't kill everyone left in Israel.” A Promise of Hope
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun m bíi nàatī Unimbɔti bɔtee ní Peelatiya jipɔɔn Beenaya kpíì. Niinee ní m tātìi gbāaǹ m-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ ní ki téeń mpɔn yii: «Áù, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee níii?» Unimbɔti làá kóoǹ u-nibul din yàl̄ee kí kpāfì

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in Jerusalem claim that you and the other Israelites who were taken to Babylonia are too far away to worship me. They also claim that the land of Israel now belongs only to them.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, a-nabiyaamu dee, a-nabiyaamu mun a nì bi pēē mmaalee, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, bin ní bin kóò Jeerusaleemee lì yii: <Ní taa sútí kí pìl̄ ti-Dindaan, di sá yii timbi ní u dū kitiŋ nee ki tīī tí nīn yì.>

english_verse: But here is what I want you to tell the Israelites in Babylonia: It's true that I, the Lord God, have forced you out of your own country and made you live among foreign nations. But for now, I will be with you wherever you are, so that you can worship me.
translation_verse: An puee á tùkù-bi ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee yii: <M dū-ni ki tɔ́ atimbun ŋin dátèe poon, ní ki yāntì ni yàl̄ ki bí nnicantimun, ama niin muee, m bí ni-kansikin kii m nín bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun puee>.

english_verse: And someday, I will gather you from the nations where you are scattered and let you live in Israel again.
translation_verse: An puee, á tùkù-bi yii tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì bee sèé: <M làá nyāntí-ni anibul kansikin kí kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì. M làá cáań-ni ntimu mun poon ni yàl̄ee kí kpāfì ní kí dū Isirayeel tiŋki kí tīī-ni.

english_verse: When that happens, I want you to clear the land of all those idols I hate so much.
translation_verse: Niin ní ni làá nyānní ní kí kúntí ntimbiil tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ nì ajɔkɔntuun kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Then I will take away your stubbornness and make you eager to be completely faithful to me. You will want to obey me
translation_verse: M làá tīī ni-kɔkɔ dipɔbil diba ní kí tīī-ni ŋfampɔm. M làá lēē ni-wuntin dipɔbil din pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii ditaŋkpalee ní kí tīī-ni dipɔbil din pɔ̀fèe.

english_verse: and all my laws and teachings. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Án nín làá ŋá pu ní nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi kí nīn ŋúb́ m-koobiliŋ kí ŋá kii ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. Ni làá nīn sá m-nibul ní man ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: But those who worship idols will be punished and get what they deserve. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord's Glory Leaves Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ama bin pɔbiliŋ fáatiǹ bi-timbiilituuŋŋi nì bi-jɔkɔntuuŋŋee, m làá yàntī bi-tuuŋŋi ń gítí bíǹ bi-ba pu.> Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.» Unimbɔti nyooti yíkì Jeerusaleem

english_verse: After the Lord had finished speaking, the winged creatures spread their wings and flew into the air, and the wheels were beside them. The brightness of the Lord's glory above them
translation_verse: Niinee keerubimbee kpátì bi-feeŋyi ki kpáaǹ ataayee ní Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nyooti nìn bí bi-pu ki ŋmíntí.

english_verse: left Jerusalem and stopped at a hill east of the city.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn yíkì kitiŋ kansikin ní ki cūtìi yúl̀ dijool din bí kitiŋ ŋgan púee.

english_verse: Then in my vision, the Lord's Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to the other exiles in Babylonia. The vision faded away,
translation_verse: Ŋfam nìn yōoǹ-mi ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon, bin bi cúú kuyuŋuee cee. Unimbɔti Fam di nìn lēē ki dàkā-mi. Dileedakal din m nìn ká gbantee nìn wáŋkì.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, you are living among rebellious people. They have eyes, but refuse to see; they have ears, but refuse to listen.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, a kóò pɔɔgaatib kansikin ní. Bi cáá animbil ní kaa wāĺ, ní ki cáá atafal kaa gbìl̀. Di sá yii bi sá pɔɔgaatib ní.

english_verse: So before it gets dark, here is what I want you to do. Pack a few things as though you were going to be taken away as a prisoner. Then go outside where everyone can see you and walk around from place to place. Maybe as they watch, they will realize what rebels they are.
translation_verse: Sii, nisaaleen, bɔ́ntí a-tɔkɔl kii a cá kuyuŋuee ní kí búntí kuyuŋu ŋwiimpu bi-nimbilaaliyin! Yīkì laakin a bée kí nīn cá laaba kuyuŋu bi-nimbilin. An yaa yíì bi làá gbìl̄ taapu yii bi sá pɔɔgaatib.

english_verse: After you have done this, return to your house. Later that evening leave your house as if you were going into exile.
translation_verse: Nyāntí a-tɔkɔl din a bɔ́ntì ki cáa cá kuyuŋuee mmɔŋki ŋwiimpu báà ŋma ń wāl̀. Kujoou yaa jóotèe, á nyā kii bin bi cúú kuyuŋuee nín nyēē puee bi-nimbilaaliyin.

english_verse: Dig through the wall of your house and crawl out, carrying the bag with you. Make sure everyone is watching.
translation_verse: Á lùkù kí cíĺ digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee bi-nimbilaaliyin ní kí dī niin kí nyā.

english_verse: Lift the bag to your shoulders, and with your face covered, take it into the darkness, so that you cannot see the land you are leaving. All this will be a warning for the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Á yòon̄ ditɔkɔl kí páań a-gbigbipeeu pu bí nīn wāĺ-si ní á nyāntí-dì dibɔmbɔndin. Á dū tiwan kí bìin̄ a-nimbiin kí taa kpèè kitiŋ nee. Di sá yii a làá nīn sá kii kudaaŋŋuee ní ki tīī Isirayeel yab.»

english_verse: I did everything the Lord had said. I packed a few things. Then as the sun was going down, and while everyone was watching, I dug a hole through one of the walls of my house. I pulled out my bag, then lifted it to my shoulders and left in the darkness.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì-mi puee. M nyántì ditɔkɔl din m bɔ́ntì kii uyumbu tɔkɔlee ŋwiimpu. Kujoouee ní m dū m-ŋal ki lùkū ki cíl̀ digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee ní ki nyántì ditɔkɔl dibɔmbɔndi poon ní ki yōoǹ ki páaǹ m-gbigbipeeu pu bi-nimbilaaliyin niin.

english_verse: The next morning, the Lord
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntì kutaafaauee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: reminded me that those rebellious people didn't even ask what I was doing.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, mimmee Isirayeel yab pɔɔgaatib nee kaa bālifì-si yii ba ní a ŋáańaaa?

english_verse: So he sent me back to tell them: The Lord God has a message for the leader of Jerusalem and everyone living there!
translation_verse: Tùkù-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Tibɔti nee sá ki tīī dibɔtibil din bí Jeerusaleemee nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ bí ki kóò kitiŋ nee poonee ní.>

english_verse: I have done these things to show them what will happen when they are taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Tùkù-bi yii a ŋá míǹ kí tīī kudaaŋŋu ní. Kun a ŋá nee, kun làá bàń bi-puee dee, di sá yii bi làá cúú-bi kí cùnnì kuyuŋu.

english_verse: The leader of Jerusalem will lift his own bag to his shoulders at sunset and leave through a hole that the others have dug in the wall of his house. He will cover his face, so he can't see the land he is leaving.
translation_verse: Dibɔtibil din bí bi-kansikinee làá dāá yòon̄ u-wanti kí páań u-gbigbipeeu pu ní kí nyā dibɔmbɔndin. Bi làá dāá sāā kí cíĺ digundi ní ú dī niin kí nyā. U làá dāá dū tiwan kí bìin̄ u-nimbiin án nín làá ŋá pu ú taa ti ká kitiŋ nee nì u-nimbiliŋee.

english_verse: The Lord will spread out a net and trap him as he leaves Jerusalem. He will then be led away to the city of Babylon, but will never see that place, even though he will die there.
translation_verse: M làá dāá dū m-laaŋku kí tɔ̄ u-pu ní m-taliŋku ń sàl̄-u. M làá cùnnì-u Babiloon, Kaldee yab tiŋkin. Ama waa làá ká kitiŋ gbanti ní kí kpú.

english_verse: His own officials and troops will scatter in every direction, and the Lord will track them down and put them to death.
translation_verse: M làá yàaǹ bin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-uee nì u-tɔntɔnliibi nì u-janjaliibi ijaan kɔkɔ pu. Míǹ boonee ní ḿ dū kitàataajiki kí jà-bi.

english_verse: The Lord will force the rest of the people in Jerusalem to live in foreign nations, where they will realize that he has done all these things.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá béé yii m sá bi-Dindaan, ŋyunti ŋun m yaa láa jìn̄-bi ki yàl̄ atimbun kɔkɔn nì ntimu kupaau poonee.

english_verse: Some of them will survive the war, the starvation, and the deadly diseases. That way, they will be able to tell foreigners how disgusting their sins were, and that it was the Lord who punished them in this way. A Sign of Fear
translation_verse: Ama m làá dāá kíń bi-kansikin binikaaŋkaabi bin làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā kujaaun nì ŋkùmin nì bìlbil kúminee. Bíǹ làá dāá māafì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ bi ŋée. Ŋyunti gbantee, bin kóò niinee làá dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, shake with fear when you eat, and tremble when you drink.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, a làá dāá jī a-jinti ní a-wunti jìkì, ní kí nyɔ̀ a-nyim nì dipɔɔbiildi nì inimɔɔn poon.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that I, the Lord, say that someday everyone in Jerusalem will shake when they eat and tremble when they drink. Their country will be destroyed and left empty, because they have been cruel and violent.
translation_verse: Á dāá tùkù kitiŋ nee nib yii: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ nì bin kóò Jeerusaleem ki bí Isirayeel tiŋkinee pu puee sɔ̀. Bi làá dāá jī bi-jinti inimɔɔn poon ní kí nyɔ̀ bi-nyim dipɔɔbiildi poon. Di sá yii bi làá dāá nàan̄ bi-tiŋki. Tiba nì tiba kaa làá dāá gíti kíń doo, di sá yii bin kóò kitiŋ nee dū tipɔmbɔti ki gbéeǹ-kì.

english_verse: Every town will lie in ruins, and the land will be a barren desert. Then they will know that I am the Lord. The Words of the Lord Will Come True
translation_verse: Ntimu mun poon binib nìn kóòyee làá kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma, ní kitiŋ nee ń kpántí kuteeu. Niinee ni làá dāá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.» Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee, án làá ŋá míǹ

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, you've heard people in Israel use the saying, “Time passes, and prophets are proved wrong.”
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, ba pu ní ni gà Isirayeel tiŋki dilaŋkpandi nee yii: <Iwiin fɔ̀kɔntí ki cá, ama ní an kaa ŋáań kii an nín lēē ki dàkā puee ní>?

english_verse: Now tell the people that I, the Lord, am going to prove that saying wrong. No one will ever be able to use it again in Israel, because very soon everything I have said will come true!
translation_verse: Too tùkù-bi yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá kúntí dilaŋkpandi gbanti. Baa làá ti gāā dilaŋkpandi gbanti Isirayeel tiŋkin. Ama á tùkù-bi yii: <Iwiin tóobiń, míǹ ní an nín lēē ki dàkā puee kɔkɔ làá ŋá.>

english_verse: I will give them my message, and what I say will certainly happen. Warn those rebels that the time has come for them to be punished. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m sá ni-Dindaan ní. M sòoǹ tin m cáá kí sòoǹee, ní án lafun làá ŋá míǹ kaa làá tàan̄. Tiŋman pɔɔgaatib, ni-yuntii nee poon ní m làá sòoǹ ní kí ŋá m nín sòon̄ puee. Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_verse: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are also saying that your visions and messages are only about things in the future.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, Isirayeel yab nín bí ki sòoǹ tiŋyee sèé: <Kijapaai nee leedakaŋ sá iwiin iba poon bɔti ní. U bíi sòoǹ ki nàatī iwiin in dátèe poon bɔti ní.>

english_verse: So tell them that my words will soon come true, just as I have warned. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: An pu ní an sá á tùkù-bi yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Tin m sòon̄ee, m làá yàntī án ŋá míǹ kaa làá tàan̄.> Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the prophets of Israel who say they speak in my name, but who preach messages that come from their own imagination. Tell them it's time to hear my message.
translation_verse: «Sii nisaaleen, fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī bin yíì bi-ba yii bi sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Isirayeel tiŋkin ní ki nàatī tin bíǹ bi-ba lèe. Tùkù-bi yii bí pīlifì m-nyɔɔbundi.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, say those lying prophets are doomed! They don't see visions—they make up their own messages!
translation_verse: Mama ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi lì yii nnaabu làá jēetí bibɔnaatiliibi bin kaa nyí tiba gbantee pu! Bi nóó tin bíǹ bi-ba bɔ́ntì kí sòoǹee ní ki nāantí bíǹ bi-ba leedakaŋ.

english_verse: Israel's prophets are no better than jackals that hunt for food among the ruins of a city.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab, ni-bɔnaatiliibi bí kii ŋŋɔkɔmu mun tú ki yìiǹ adigbunnee ní.

english_verse: They don't warn the people about coming trouble or tell them how dangerous it is to sin against me.
translation_verse: Baa jɔ́m̀ ki ŋéeb́ abun ŋin bí digundi puee, kaa tí máń digundi din làá wúń ni-pu ní ŋmā kí já kujaau ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dalee.

english_verse: Those prophets lie by claiming they speak for me, but I have not even chosen them to be my prophets. And they still think their words will come true.
translation_verse: Bi cáá inyimɔn leedakaŋ ní tin bi sòoǹ yii án làá dāan̄ee kaa sá ibaamɔn. Bi lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé>, ama ní man ni-Dindaan kaa tú-bi. Ní bi kā ki cí yii ḿ ŋá tin bi sòon̄ee kí tīī-bi!

english_verse: So I am going to punish those lying prophets for deceiving the people of Israel with false messages.
translation_verse: Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ yii: ni nín ŋá pu ki yāntì inyimɔn nyɔɔbuŋŋi nì inyimɔn leedakaŋee gbītì an kɔkɔ puee, m làá jáǹ-ni.> Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee dee!

english_verse: I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. They will not be allowed to call themselves Israelites or even to set foot in Israel. Then they will realize that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: «M làá dàkà bibɔnaatiliibi bin kántì inyimɔn leedakaŋ ki sòon̄ tinyimɔmbɔtee m-pɔŋŋu. Baa ti làá nīn cáá mpaan m-samaau kansikin. Baa làá ŋmà bi-yiŋŋi Isirayeel nibul gbɔŋkun ní baa ti làá gítí bi-tiŋkin mun. Niinee bi làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti.

english_verse: Those prophets refuse to be honest. They tell my people there will be peace, even though there's no peace to be found. They are like workers who think they can fix a shaky wall by covering it with paint.
translation_verse: «Bibɔnaatiliibi bí ki kíiĺ m-nibul ki lì yii ŋgbansɔŋfi bí, ama ní ŋgbansɔŋfi kaa bí. M-samaau bíi māā digundi ní bíǹ bí ki pōontí-dì.

english_verse: But when I send rainstorms, hailstones, and strong winds, the wall will surely collapse.
