translation_verse: Too, tùkù bin bíi pōontí gbanti yii: Digundi làá lítí! Utaakpaan ubɔ làá nì ní ataanyiŋkumbil ń lítí ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋu ń jītí.

english_verse: People will then ask the workers why the paint didn't hold it up.
translation_verse: Digundee yaa láa lítèe, bi làá dāá bàlifì-ni yii: <Ni nín póoń digundi puee bí la?>

english_verse: That wall is the city of Jerusalem. And I, the Lord God, am so angry that I will send strong winds, rainstorms, and hailstones to destroy it.
translation_verse: An ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nìn bíi tùkù-nee yii: M-ŋuul poonee, m làá cáań kubuŋkpaaŋŋu, ní m-bum ń cáań utaakpaan ní ataanyiŋkumbil ń lítí kí nàan̄ tikɔkɔ.

english_verse: The lying prophets have tried to cover up the evil in Jerusalem, but I will tear down the city, all the way to its foundations. And when it collapses, those prophets will be killed, and everyone will know that I have done these things.
translation_verse: M làá kpēelikì digundi din ni póońee. M làá téé-dì kí lúkú kitiŋ ní di-nyeel ń nyā kí páań mpaampiin pu. Di làá lítí ní kí nà-ni dúsi dusi ní ní béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: The city of Jerusalem and its lying prophets will feel my fierce anger. Then I will announce that the city has fallen and that the lying prophets are dead,
translation_verse: M làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi digundi nee nì bin póoń-dèe pu kí cáá kátí. Bi làá dāá tùkù-ni yii: <Digundee kaa ti bí! Ubɔ kaa ti bí kí póoń-dì!

english_verse: because they promised my people peace, when there was no peace. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Women Who Wear Magic Charms The Lord said:
translation_verse: Isirayeel bɔnaatiliibi bin nìn sòoǹ ki nàatī Jeerusaleem puee kaa ti bí. Bi nìn kāntí aleedaka ki lì yii ŋgbansɔŋfi bí, ama ní ŋgbansɔŋfi kaa bí! Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.» Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí bikpaŋkpantiibi

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, now condemn the women of Israel who preach messages that come from their own imagination.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, pīlifì, sòoǹ nì Isirayeel nimpoobi bin bɔ́ntí tin bi lèe ki cáa nàatēe, fōō Unimbɔti nyɔɔbundi kí dūú nàatī-bi.

english_verse: Tell them they're doomed! They wear magic charms on their wrists and scarves on their heads, then trick others into believing they can predict the future. They won't get away with telling those lies.
translation_verse: Tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee yii: Nnaabu làá jēetí ni-pu! Ni cáá igban ki lù abɔmbil ki fūuntí, ní ki lù iŋaabu nì i-bulifi ki tìì binib kɔkɔ kí ŋmā kí nīn cáá mpɔn bi-pu. Ni là kí fōō m-nibul maŋfal kí gāā ni-bindi ní ki kpáafí nimbi ni-ba yal.

english_verse: They charge my people a few handfuls of barley and a couple pieces of bread, and then give messages that are insulting to me. They use lies to sentence the innocent to death and to help the guilty go free. And my people believe them!
translation_verse: Ni bíiĺ-mi m-nibul nimbiin kí ŋmā kí ká ɔɔji aŋaŋkul akaaŋkaa nì kpɔnɔb bikaaŋkaabi. Ni nín bíi mɔ́ntí m-samaau un di néeń ki pílifí tinyimɔmbɔtee, ni bíi kù bin kaa bàà máaǹ ŋkúmee ní ki yàntī bin kaa bàà máaǹ kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee bí dimaŋfalin dee.

english_verse: I hate the magic charms they use to trick people into believing their lies. I will rip those charms from their wrists and set free the people they have trapped like birds.
translation_verse: An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi lì yii m làá jáǹ ni-bɔmbiliŋ ŋin ni cáa sàl̀ bin kíǹee. M làá dáaĺ-ŋi kí tìfì kí fúutí ni-ŋaliyin ní kí fīī bin ni cúúyee kí líí.

english_verse: I will tear the scarves from their heads and rescue my people from their power once and for all. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: M làá dáaĺ ni-ŋaabui kí cátí ní kí fīī m-samaau kí nyāntí ni-ŋaan. Naa ti làá ŋmā kí dū-bi kí kpántí ni-wanti tin ni cúúyee ní ní béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: They do things I would never do. They lie to good people and encourage them to do wrong, and they convince the wicked to ruin their own lives by not turning from sin.
translation_verse: Ni dū ni-nyimɔŋyi ki yɔ̄tì deedeedambi wunti ŋyunti ŋun ní maa bàà là bi-wunti ń yɔ̀tēe. Ni tīī binikpitib kunyannyaau, ki pīiǹ-bi nsan bí fá bi-bimbikpitim kí ŋmátí.

english_verse: I will no longer let these women give false messages and use magic, and I will free my people from their control. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, naa ti làá ká inyimɔn leedakaŋ kaa ti làá sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti. M làá fīī m-nibul kí nyāntí ni-ŋaan. Mimmee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_verse: While they were there, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these men have started worshiping idols, though they know it will cause them to sin even more. So I refuse to give them a message!
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, binib nee tú bi-waaŋi bi-pɔbiliŋin ní. Bi-nimbikpeeŋu pée cɔ́ kun di yàntī bi ŋáań ikpitee pu ní. A dàkafī yii m làá yàntī bí bàlifì-mi tiba ḿ kíí-baaa?

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that if they sin by worshiping idols and then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will give them the answer their sins deserve.
translation_verse: An puee sòoǹ nì bi kí tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti lēe yii: Tí dūú ŋmàntī kii Isirayeel yab kansikin ubɔ tú u-waaŋi u-pɔbilin ní u-nimbikpeeŋu pée cɔ́ tin di yàntī u ŋáań ikpitee pu, ní boonee ki dɔ́miń kí bàlifì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu, man ni-Dindaan di làá kíí-u m-ba. M làá kíí-u kí nóó nì awaa ŋin nyɔkɔm u cááyee ní.

english_verse: When they hear my message, maybe they will see that they need to turn back to me and stop worshiping those idols.
translation_verse: M làá ŋá míǹ ní kí gbēē Isirayeel yab bin dū-mi ki fá ki kíǹ ki nóó awaayee pɔbil.

english_verse: Now, Ezekiel, tell everyone in Israel: I am the Lord God. Stop worshiping those idols I hate so much and come back to me.
translation_verse: An pu ní á tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti bí-ni yii ní kpántí ni-bimbim. Fàtīmaan ni-boon kí tīī ni-waaŋi ní kí dū ni-timbiilituuŋŋi kɔkɔ kí fá.>

english_verse: Suppose one of you Israelites or a foreigner living in Israel rejects me and starts worshiping idols. If you then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will answer
translation_verse: «Isirayeel niliu ubɔ àá unicaan un kóò Isirayeel tiŋkinee yaa dū-mi ki fá ní ki yāntì tiwaabɔti jíń u-pɔbil ní kaa fātì u-boon ki tīī tin di yàntī u ŋáań ikpitee, udaan yaa dɔ́miń m-bɔnaatiliu cee kí bàlifì kí béé m-lammee, man ni-Dindaan di làá kíí-u m-ba.

english_verse: by turning against you. I will make you a warning to anyone who might think of doing the same thing, and you will no longer belong to my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord and that you have sinned against me.
translation_verse: M làá jáǹ unil gbanti. M làá yàntī ú kpántí ŋabika bí nīn kíǹ ki cáa gà ilan. M làá nyāntí-u m-samaau kansikin ní ní béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: If a prophet gives a false message, I am the one who caused that prophet to lie. But I will still reject him and cut him off from my people,
translation_verse: «Ama ubɔnaatil yaa yāntì an ŋmātiǹ-u ní u gāā u-bindi ki kíí udaan tibee, mimmee an dàkà yii man ni-Dindaan di ŋmātiǹ ubɔnaatil gbanti. M làá dàkà udaan m-pɔŋŋu ní kí nyāntí-u m-nibul Isirayeel yab kansikin.

english_verse: and anyone who goes to that prophet for a message will be punished in the same way.
translation_verse: Ubɔnaatil gbanti nì un dɔ́miń ki bālifèe kɔkɔ ŋá ikpitibaanti ní bi làá túń bi-kpitii kpuulool.

english_verse: I will do this, so that you will come back to me and stop destroying yourselves with these disgusting sins. So turn back to me! Then I will be your God, and you will be my people. I, the Lord God, make this promise. Judgment on a Sinful Nation
translation_verse: An yaa ŋá mimmee, Isirayeel yab kaa ti làá gáatí kí wàatī-mi. Baa ti làá ŋá ikpiti kí kɔ́ǹ bi-ba tijɔkɔndi. Ama bi làá nīn sá m-nibul ní man ḿ nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu. Man bi-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.» Tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí pìin̄ Unimbɔti bɔsooŋyi nsan

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, suppose an entire nation sins against me, and I punish it by destroying the crops and letting its people and livestock starve to death.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, kitiŋ kiba pu nib yaa kaa yúl̀-mi deedee ki ŋá ikpitee, m làá dàkà-bi m-pɔŋŋu. M làá bīil̀ bi-kpaajinti tin bi kpáafèe ní kí yàntī ŋkùm ń nyā, ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí kitiŋee nib nì ki-waŋkuti.

english_verse: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living in that nation, their faithfulness would not save anyone but themselves.
translation_verse: Báà binib bita nee, Noowa nì Daniyeel nì Yoob yaa bí kitiŋ gbanti nib kansikin, bi-deedeeu làá fīī bíǹ ŋmaniŋma ní. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Or suppose I punish a nation by sending wild animals to eat people and scare away every passerby, so that the land becomes a barren desert.
translation_verse: «Àá tí lì yii m dū ipeecuncuti ki tɔ́ kitiŋ gbanti nib pu. Kitiŋee làá kpántí kii kuteeuee ní, di sá ipeel làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí ki-nib ní ipeel puee, ubɔ mun kaa ti làá kíí kí dī niin.

english_verse: As surely as I live, I promise that even if these three men lived in that nation, their own children would not be spared. The three men would live, but the land would be an empty desert.

translation_verse: Samaarii tiŋki kíǹ kaa ŋá ikpiti in a ŋá nee dijandi gba! A ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi tikpil ki jítiǹ-kì. Bi yaa dū a-maan Samaarii nì a-naal Soodoom ki ŋmāntiǹ siiyee, bíǹ sá deedeedambi ní!

english_verse: So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins. Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed The Lord said to Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, an kíǹ á túń a nín fá a-jilmau puee cooi dee. A tīī a-naal nì a-maan ibaamɔn, di sá yii ikpiti in a ŋée nyāŋkì ki jítì bi-yai, ní ki yāntì bi kpántì deedeedambi ki jítiǹ-si. Icoo ń nīn cáá-si ní á jī falaa a nín fá a-jilmauee pu.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you.
translation_verse: An yaa ŋá mimmee, icoo làá cúú-si ní á fá a-jilmau tin kɔkɔ a ŋée pu. An di làá ŋméeǹ-mu.

english_verse: When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
translation_verse: Án làá fàtīí bútí Soodoom nì Samaarii nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-muee. Án làá fàtīí bútí si mun nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-see.

english_verse: Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun a nìn cáá dilambilee, a nìn kpèé a-naal Soodoom fám ní.

english_verse: But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks.
translation_verse: An sá ŋyunti ŋun ní a-kpitii nìn dáá bí dibalinee ní. Sii mun yuntiŋu bāań Eedoom timmu nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-muee ń bèel̀-si dee. Fiiliistii yab timmu làá kpèè-si fám ijaan kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Icoo nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin a ŋée paati dee. Man a-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever.
translation_verse: Ama mamee, maa làá súntí dipoondi din ní m pōoǹ-si a-sapɔnti yuntiŋuee. M làá yàntī dipoondi gbanti ń kpántí talku poondi.

english_verse: When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement.
translation_verse: A làá dāá téetí a-bimbim pu ní icoo ń cúú-si ŋyunti ŋun ní a yaa láa fōō a-mambi nì a-naalib a-ceeyee. M làá dāá dū-bi kí ŋá a-taapu bí kpántí kii a-bisalibee, min kamaa an kaa bí dipoondi din m pōoǹ-see poonee.

english_verse: I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M làá fàtīí pɔ̀ntī dipoondi din ní m pōoǹ-see, niinee a làá béé yii m sá a-Dindaan.

english_verse: I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: A làá téetí tin jítèe pu ní icoo ń cúú-si ní a-nyɔkɔ ń kpú, kun puee a fá a-jilmau. Ama mamee, m làá dū tin kɔkɔ a ŋée kí pɔ̄-si.» Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, pɔ́ɔǹ Isirayeel yab ipɔɔn nee kí dū tibɔti nee kí ŋmàntī-bi.

english_verse: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
translation_verse: Tùkù-bi yii man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi sòoǹ yii: <Ukaaluŋkpaan ubɔ di nìn bí ki cáá ifeeŋkpaan ní u-kuti fɔ̀kɔ̀ ki náaǹ ki cáá inyiŋfi kupaau. U nìn ŋàan̄ ki bāań Leebanɔn jooŋŋi. U nìn yá ki kɔ́fì seedir subu bubɔ yilpu.

english_verse: then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities.
translation_verse: U nìn bátì bu-pandi din fɔ̀kɔǹ ŋi-kɔkɔ kíǹee ní ki yōoǹ-dì ki cáa cūnnì binyampoobi tiŋkin ki dū-dì ki bíl̀ bibantiliibi tiŋkin.

english_verse: The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u yōoǹ Isirayeel tiŋkin subu bubɔ ki cáa cóoǹ kitiŋ kin bi yɔ̄kɔtèe ni. U nìn cóoǹ-bu mbun ŋun cáá nnyim tikpilee gbandi, a lì kii busubu bun néeń nnyimee.

english_verse: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
translation_verse: Busubuee cɔ́tì ní ki pɔ̄kɔtì ki kpántì bufiinyisubu ki lālim̀. Bu nìn tòó bu-paŋŋi ki cá ukaalunee watil pú ní bu-nyaaŋyi wīintí u-feeŋyi taapu. Busubuee nìn dūu kpántì bufiinyisubu ki cɔ́tì cɔ́tì ní ki tɔ́ tɔ́ mpamu.

english_verse: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.
translation_verse: Ama ní ukaaluŋkpaan uliliiti ubɔ mun dūu bāań. U-feeŋyi nìn sá ikpaan ní ki cáá tikuti tikpil. Niinee ní bufiinyisubuee tɔ́ bu-nyaaŋyi ki túĺ ukaalunee cee ní ki fātì bu-paŋŋi u-watil pú. Bu nìn dàkafī kí ká u-cee nnyim kí jītíǹ laakin bu cɔ́ee.

english_verse: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
translation_verse: Ama bi nìn cóoǹ-bu kitiŋ kin ŋān̄ee poon ní, mbun ŋun cáá nnyim tikpilee gbandi, bú ŋmā kí tɔ̄ apan, kí lòoǹ abil kí kpántí bufiinyisubu bunyaambu.>

english_verse: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
translation_verse: «Dū tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee kí nàatī yii: <Bufiinyisubu gbanti ŋūǹ kí wíiǹaaa? Ukaalumpeekaayee kaa làá cúú bu-nyaaŋyi kí fùkù, kí bīil̀ bu-biliŋ ní kí yàntī bu nín cɔ́tì cɔ́tì pu mpɔminee ń kpāaa? Kí fùkù-buee, an kaa làá bàlifì ú ŋá mpɔn àá ú nyàab̀ binib tikpil.

english_verse: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
translation_verse: Bi baasii cóoǹ bufiinyisubuee ní, ama bu làá ŋmā kí pɔ̀kɔtāaa? Kubuŋu yaa nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki jítì bu-puee, buaa làá kpā dicilpu dicilpu niinaaa? Laakin bi cóoǹ-bu bú bàà wíiǹee, niin ní bu làá kpā!>» Tibɔŋmantikaalee taapu

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
translation_verse: «Bàlifì pɔɔgaatib nee yii bi gbìl̄ tibɔŋmantikaal nee taapuɔɔɔ? Tùkù-bi yii Babiloon bɔtiu dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem ki cúú ubɔti nì bitindaŋkpilib ki cūnnì u-tiŋkin.

english_verse: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
translation_verse: U nìn yōoǹ ubɔti dicaŋkun niliu ubɔ, ní u nì u ŋá mpèé ní ki yāntì u pūtì yii waa làá nyā mpèéyee boon. U nìn yōoǹ kitiŋee pu bɔtibiliŋ

english_verse: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
translation_verse: án nín làá ŋá pu kitiŋee ń sìntī ki-ba taapu kí taa ti ŋmā kí yīkì, ní kí nīn tɔ́ mpèéyee deedeeyee.

english_verse: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
translation_verse: Ama ní ubɔtipɔɔnee yíkìi bíi jáà nì Babiloon bɔtiu. U tú ituun Eejipiti án nín làá ŋá pu Eejipiti ń tīī-u itaamu nì bijanjaliibi tikpilee. Án làá ŋmā kí bútí-uaaa? U nín bíi ŋáań mimmee, u làá ŋmā kí fīī u-baaa? Waa làá ŋmā kí fīī u-ba, di sá yii u nyáń mpèé boon!

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, ubɔti gbanti làá kpú Babiloon bɔtiu un di kāaǹ-u dibeelee tiŋkin ní. Di sá yii u kpēē dipùtil din u pūtèe fám ki nyáń mpèéyee boon. Míǹ puee Babiloon tiŋkin ní u làá kpú.

english_verse: Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people.
translation_verse: Báà Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo yaa cáań bijanjaliibi bin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee tikpil gba, waa làá ŋmā kí mɔ̄tì u-pu, kun puee Babiloon yab làá mā ŋgumu mun boon bi làá nīn bāal̀ee, ní kí gbà ibòó kí pɔ̀fì binib tikpil.

english_verse: The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
translation_verse: U nín kpēē dipùtil din u pūtèe fámee, u nyáń mpèéyee boon dee. U nín ŋá pu ki kíí ki nyīī ŋŋal ní ki ŋá tin bí nee kɔkɔee, waa làá ŋmátí!

english_verse: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalin nee nín bíi sòoǹ puee sɔ̀. Isirayeel bɔtiu nín ŋá pu ki nyáń mpèé ŋun ní u nìn pūtì m-nimbiin ki nyīī ŋŋalee boonee, m làá dáaĺ u-tafal.

english_verse: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
translation_verse: M làá píĺ-u kutaliŋŋu ní kí cúú-u. M làá cùnnì-u Babiloon tiŋkin ní kí sòoǹ u-bɔti niin, di sá yii waa yúl̀ nì mi deedee.

english_verse: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Bi làá kpɔ̀ u-janjamɔntiibi kujaaun ní bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee ń sāǹ kí yàl̄ ijaan kɔkɔ pu. Niinee ni làá béé yii man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄.» Ti-Dindaan pooŋyi

english_verse: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Man m-ba làá lēē seedir subu yilpu dipampɔmbil din túkú bu-paŋkpaaŋŋi nyɔkɔpuee ní kí cáá cóoń dijoofɔŋfɔkɔl diba yilpu.

english_verse: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
translation_verse: M làá dū-dì kí cóoń Isirayeel jool din fɔ̀kɔ̀ee yilpu. Di làá wíiǹ kí tɔ̄ apan, kí lòoǹ abil ní kí kpántí buseedirisubu bunyannyaambu. Inoon kɔkɔ nì i-bulifi làá páań i-diiŋi bu-paŋŋi pu, ní kí nīn ŋùŋfī bu-booŋŋu taapu.

english_verse: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
translation_verse: Niinee tisatin sufii kɔkɔ làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. M gùutī isufi in fɔ̀kɔ̀ee pu ní kí yàntī in kaa fɔ̀kɔ̀ee ń wíiǹ. M làá yàntī isufi in sɔ̀m̀ee ń kpā ní kí tīī in kūńee ŋkpiim. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, ní tin m yaa lēe, m ŋáań míǹ ní.»

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: «Isirayeel tiŋkinee, ba pu ní bi gà nlan nee yii: <Bibaatiibi ŋmɔ́ ayeeŋgaan, ama ní mbiyaamu nyiŋŋi nyāŋfì ní?>

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalin nee di bíi sòoǹ yii, naa ti làá gāā nlan gbanti Isirayeel tiŋkin.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, unil kamaa maŋfal kā man ŋaan ní. Bibaatiibi nì mbiyaamu kɔkɔ maŋfal kā man ŋaan ní. Un yaa ŋá ikpitee, udaan di kúù.

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: «Tí dūú ŋmàntī kii deedeedaan di bí ní ki ŋáań tin kítèe nì tin bí deedeeyee.

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: Waa jīǹ tiwaajin awaajoon pu, kaa tòotī Isirayeel yab waaŋi. Waa mɔ̀nnì u-juti nimpuu, ní kaa dɔ̀ nì unimpu un bíi fùul̀ ŋkpinee.

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: Waa mùul̄ u-juti kaa yù u-juti wanti mun. U gīintí u-pɔ̀nliu nín dū tin ki síiǹ u-cee toolimee ki tìì-u. U tìì un ŋkùm cááyee tijin, ki tìì un kaa cáá tiba kí pèen̄ee tiwampeeŋkaal.

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: Waa pìntí u-nimbiliŋ bí dāá téeǹ-u kí páań àá ki nyàab̀ ipaati. U fàtī u-boon ki tìì tin kaa bí deedeeyee ní ki sòoǹ binib bɔti nì ibaamɔn.

english_verse: and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
translation_verse: U tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab ní ki nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu. Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi sòoǹ yii an niliuee sá deedeedaan ní ki làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin.

english_verse: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
translation_verse: «Tí tí dūú ŋmàntī kii an niliuee cáá jipɔɔn ní u-jipɔɔnee fìkì binib wanti ki kù binib ní ki ŋáań atuŋkpiti kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifi.

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: U-baa kaa pée ŋá míǹ ki ká. U jīǹ tiwaajin awaajoon pu, ki mɔ̀nnì u-juti nimpuu.

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: U mùul̄ usoodaan nì unandaan, ki yù u-juti wanti, kaa gīintí u-pɔnliibi nín dù tin ki sīintí u-cee toolimee ki tìì-bi. U tòotī awaa ní ki ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi.

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: U pìntí u-nimbiliŋ bí dāá téeǹ-u kí páań àá ki nyàab̀ ipaati. An niliu gbanti làá nīn bí dimaŋfalinaaa? Aayee, kpataaa! U ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi nee kɔkɔ, see ú kpú, ní u-kúm kpuulool làá gítí úǹ u-ba pu ní.

english_verse: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
translation_verse: «Tí tí dūú ŋmàntī kii u cáá jipɔɔn. U-jipɔɔn gbanti ká u-baa tuŋkpitiŋ, ama ní kaa nóó u-tabɔbiliŋ.

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: Waa jīǹ tiwaajin awaajoon pu, kaa tòotī Isirayeel yab waaŋi. Waa mɔ̀nnì u-juti nimpuu kí kɔ́ǹ u-ba tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: Waa mùul̄ u-juti kaa yù u-juti wanti. U gīintí u-pɔ̀nliu nín dū tin ki síiǹ u-cee toolimee ki tìì-u. U tìì un ŋkùm cááyee tijin nì un kaa cáá tiba kí pèen̄ee tiwampeeŋkaal.

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: U fàtī u-boon ki tìì tin kaa bí deedeeyee ní kaa pìntí u-nimbiliŋ bí dāá téeǹ-u kí páań àá ki nyàab̀ ipaati. U tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab ní ki nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu. An niliuee kaa làá kpú u-baa kpitii pu. U làá nīn pée bí dimaŋfalin ní.

english_verse: It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
translation_verse: U-baa nín mūul̀ binib, ki yùn̄ u-nabiki wanti ki sāaǹ bin māntìi tú-uee, úǹ di máaǹ kí kpú u-kpitii pu.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: «Ama ní ni bàlifī yii ba pu ní ujipɔnti kaa máaǹ kí fōō u-baa yìntitam tafadaaldi? Too, kun di yì-tèe di sá yii ujipɔntee ŋá tin bí deedee ki kítèe ní ki tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ. An puee u làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Un ŋá ikpitee di kúù. Mbiyaamu kaa cáá kí pà mu-baabi kpitii pɔndi, ní bibaatiibi mun kaa cáá kí pà bi-biyaamu kpitii pɔndi. Bi làá pà deedeedaan u-deedeetuuŋŋi paati ní, ní kí pà unikpiti u-kpitii tuuŋŋi paati. Nín̄ ŋáaḿmaan tiŋan

english_verse: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
translation_verse: «Unikpiti yaa gbēeǹ kaa tí bíi ŋáań u-tuŋkpitiŋ ní ki kíǹ ki tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi ki ŋáań tin bí deedee ki kítèe, waa làá kpú, u làá pée ŋmátí ní.

english_verse: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
translation_verse: Bi làá súntí u-yìntitam kɔkɔ pu, ní ú nīn kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin u-deedee tuuŋŋi ŋin u kíǹ ki bíi ŋáańee pu.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: Ni dàkafī yii an mɔ̄ǹ-mi ḿ ká unikpiti ń kpú níii? Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi tùkù-ni yii kun m lèe di sá unikpiti ń kpántí u-bimbim kí nīn kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin.

english_verse: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
translation_verse: Ama deedeedaan yaa gbēeǹ kaa tí bíi ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi, ní ki kíĺ ki kíǹ ki bíi ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin binikpitib ŋáańee, ni dàkafī yii an niliuee làá nīn bí dimaŋfalinaaa? Aayee, kpataaa! Bi làá súntí u-deedee tuuŋŋee kɔkɔ pu. U làá kpú, di sá yii waa yúl̀ deedee ní ki bíi ŋáań ikpiti.

english_verse: You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are!
translation_verse: Ni lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín ŋáań puee kaa kítì!> Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan-mi tiŋan. Man di ŋáań tin kaa kítèeee? An kaa sá nimbaaa?

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Deedeedaan yaa gbēeǹ kaa tí bíi ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi ní ki bíi ŋáań ikpitee, see ú kpú. Ikpiti in u bíi ŋáańee pu ní u làá kpú.

english_verse: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Ama unikpiti yaa fātì u-boon ki tīī u-tuŋkpitiŋ ní ki kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi nì tin kítèe, u làá fīī u-maŋfal.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: U yaa dáań ki ká yii u bíi ŋáań atuŋkpiti ní ki fātì u-boon ki tīī-ŋee, u làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin, waa làá kpú.

english_verse: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
translation_verse: Ama ní nimbi Isirayeel yab bí ki lì yii: <Tin ti-Dindaan ŋáańee kaa kítì!> Mimmee man nín ŋáań puee di kaa kítàaa? Nimbi nín ŋáań puee di kaa kítàa!

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Fámaan atuŋkpiti ŋin ni ŋáańee, kpántímaan ni-pɔbiliŋ nì ni-landɔkɔi. Isirayeel yab, ba pu ní ni là kí kpú ní?

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m bíi lì yii maa là ubɔ kúm. Fàtīmaan ni-boon kí tīī ikpiti ní kí nīn bí dimaŋfalin!»

english_verse: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii ḿ gāā iyaliŋki laŋŋu nee kí tīī Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ:

english_verse: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
translation_verse: «Ni-na nìn sá ugbikintinaati ní ki bí gbikintib kansikin. U nìn dɔ̀ agbikintipɔmbil kansikin ní ki kpīintí u-biyaamu.

english_verse: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
translation_verse: U nìn péé u-biki kiba. Kíǹ kpántì digbikintipɔmbilee, ní ki bífì ki kíǹ ki ŋūǹ kí tɔ̀ntī kuwaŋkuluu, ní ki cútì binib ki ŋmɔ́.

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Binicambi nìn gbìl̄ u-pu. Bi nìn gbìn̄ mbòó ki sàl̄-u ní ki dū dibɔmbil ki túuń u-maŋfal ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: Ugbikintinaati kāl̀ ki cíitì ki gīī. Ŋyunti ŋun u ká yii dimákal kaa ti bée, ní u lēē u-biyaamu kansikin kiba. U nìn dū-kì ki kpántì digbikintipɔmbil din cáá mpɔnee.

english_verse: He destroyed fortresses and ruined towns; his mighty roar terrified everyone.
translation_verse: U nìn gbáń ki wīil̀ bi-gunlɔkɔŋ ní ki nāaǹ bi-timmu. Kitiŋee pu nib yaa nìn gbìl̄ u sūǹee, dinyoondi nìn cútí-bi ní.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Niinee atimbun nib kpáfì kí jáǹ-u, anibul nìn nyánní an kɔkɔ pu. Bi nìn dū kulaaŋŋu ki cúú-u ní ki dū-u ki tɔ́ mbòó poon.

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Bi dū dibɔmbil ki lɔ̀kɔ̄-u ní ki dū-u ki tɔ́ dikantandin ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon bɔtiu cee. Bi nìn dū-u ki tɔ́ sarkan kí taa ti gbìl̄ u-pu yii u gbùkum̄ Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu.» Bufiinyisubu yaliŋkii

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: «Ni-na nìn náań nì bufiinyisubu bun bi cóoǹ mbun caŋinee ní. Bu nìn lòoǹ tiŋan ní ki cáá tifaal tikpil, kun puee bu nìn kāntí nnyim tiŋan pu.

english_verse: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
translation_verse: Bu-paŋŋi nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋan, ní ki kpántì bibɔtiibi kpandɔŋu. Bu nìn wíiǹ ki fɔ̄kɔǹ ki páaǹ isufi pu. Bu-fɔkɔŋŋu nì bu-paŋŋi puee, báà ŋma nìn wāĺ-bu ní.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Ama ní bi fùkū-bu nì diŋuul poon ki lúkú kitiŋ. Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú buŋku yāntì bu-biliŋ kūń ki lítì. Bu-paŋŋi ŋin nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄yee kūń ní ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi.

english_verse: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, bi dū bufiinyisubu ki cóoǹ kuteeun, kitiŋ kin kūń nnyim kpée.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Ŋŋmi ŋubɔ nyáń bu-dɔŋu poon, ŋu wùn̄ bu-paŋŋi nì bu-biliŋ. Buaa ti cáá dipandi din pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki ŋūǹ kí kpántí ubɔti kpandɔŋuee.» Bí nīn gà nlan nee kii bi nín gà ŋkpiisilan puee.

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin aluli boon, uŋmaŋmooŋmooti iwiin saalaa dalee, ní Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib biba dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ m-nimbiin kí bàlifì kí béé Unimbɔti lammi.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, tùkù Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib yii man bi-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kéè ni dɔ́miń kí bàlifì kí béé m-lammi naa! Too, m nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, maa làá yàntī ní bàlifì-mi tiba, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: «Sii un sá nisaaleenee, a bɔ́ntì kí sòoǹ bi-bɔtaaa? Māafì-bi bi-baabi nín túń ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋiŋyee.

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: Á tùkù-bi yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M nín lēē Isirayeelee, m nìn yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu ki pūtì ki pōoǹ Jaakɔb naantiibi. M nìn yāntì bi béè-mi Eejipiti tiŋkin. M nìn yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu ki pūtì ki lī yii: <Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.>

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, m nìn yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu ki pūtì kí nyāntí-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin kí cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin poon m nyàab̄ kí tīī-bee. Kitiŋ kin di ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ ntimu kɔkɔ nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee.

english_verse: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
translation_verse: M nìn tīī-bi mara nee yii: <Ni-kɔkɔ ń dū ntimbiil waaŋi ŋin dátí-ni nee kí fá. Ní taa ti tòotī Eejipiti yab waaŋi nee kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi. Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu>

english_verse: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
translation_verse: «Ama ní bi yíkìi jáń nì mi, ní kaa kíí kí pīlifiǹ-mi. Báà ubɔ kaa dū ntimbiil waaŋi ŋin nìn dátí-bee ki fá. Baa nìn dū Eejipiti waaŋee ki fá. M nìn ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī bi-pu, kí ŋá kii m nín bí yii m làá ŋá puee kí cáá kátí Eejipiti tiŋkin niin.

english_verse: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama man m-ba yindi puee ní maa nìn ŋá míǹ. Maa nìn là yii atimbun ŋin kansikin bi nìn kóòyee nib ń kpèè-mi fám. Di sá yii m nìn lēē m-ba ki dàkā-bi atimbun gbanti nimbiin ní ki pōoǹ yii m làá nyāntí-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì kuteeun.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: M nìn dàkā-bi m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab bin ní un yaa dūu túń ditundee kāntí dimaŋfalee.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: M nìn tīī-bi ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa án nīn sá kudaaŋŋu kí nīn bí man nì bi kansikin, án nín làá ŋá pu bí béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan un di ŋáań-bi circiree.

english_verse: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab nìn yíkìi jáń nì mi kuteeun. Baa nìn ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi ní ki dū m-marab bin tìì un ŋúb́-bee dimaŋfalee ki fá. Baa nìn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. M nìn tí ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī bi-pu kuteeun niin kí céetí-bi.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama ní m tí kpēē m-yindi pu, án nín làá ŋá pu atimbun ŋin nib nìn ká m nín nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee ń taa kpèè m-yindi fámee.

english_verse: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
translation_verse: Ama, kuteeun niinee ní m pūtì yii maa làá cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin poon m bàà bí yii m làá tīī-bee, kitiŋ kin poon ní nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee.

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: M nìn pūtì kun puee bi nìn dū m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ki fá ní kaa nìn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. Di sá yii bi nìn baasii dū bi-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ bi-waaŋee ní.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: Ama m nìn súń bi-saai ní kaa kūū ki céetì-bi kuteeun. Isirayeel gbíntìi nìkì ki yìntīǹ Unimbɔti

english_verse: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
translation_verse: «M nìn tīī bi-biyaamu abɔkpaa nee kuteeun yii: <Ní taa nín̄ nóó abɔkpaa nì marab bin ni-baabi bi-ba mɔ́ɔ́yee. Ní taa tòotī awaa kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu! Ní nīn nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi kí nīn tɔ́ m-marab kí dū-bi kí tɔ̄ ditundi.

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ní dūmaan ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal kí sú-mi kí dàkà mpèé ŋun di bí man nì ni kansikinee, ní kí téetí yii man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.>

english_verse: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
translation_verse: Ama bíǹ mun yíkì ki jáń nì mi. Baa nìn nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi ní kaa ŋúb́ m-marab bin ní unil máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́ kí ŋmátée. Baa nìn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa. Niinee ní m ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá kpáatí m-bum kí sìtī bi-pu kuteeun, kí yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi kí tin cáá kátí.

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama m nìn tí cúú m-ba m-yindi pu, án nín làá ŋá pu atimbun ŋin nib ká-mi m nín nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee ń taa kpèè-mi fámee.

english_verse: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
translation_verse: Kuteeun niinee ní m yōoǹ m-ŋal ki pūtì yii m làá jà-bi kí yàl̄ atimbun aban nì ntincamun.

english_verse: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Di sá yii baa nìn ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab, ní kaa tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa, ama ní ki nìn yāntì bi-baabi waaŋi dáaĺ-bi.

english_verse: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
translation_verse: M nìn yāntì bi kɔ́ǹ bi-ba tijɔkɔndi. Di sá yii bi nìn cáá bi-jipɔŋkpilib ki wù ŋŋmi ki ŋáań saraabi. M nìn là kí kɔ́ǹ-bi agìń poon bí béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan ní. Unimbɔti làá kúntí Isirayeel yab waatootii

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me
translation_verse: «An puee, nisaaleen, sòoǹ nì Isirayeel yab kí tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee. Ni-baabi nìn sīī-mi kaa nìn yúl̀ nì mi deedee.

english_verse: by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them!
translation_verse: M nìn cáań-bi kitiŋ kin ní m nìn pōoǹ kí tīī-bee poon. Bi bāań ki kpēē ŋgbantamu puee ki ká isufi cáá tifaasɔn ní bi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań saraabi niin. Bi nìn ŋá saraabi ki tūutì talaalub ní ki fá idafi ki gbítì m-ŋuul.

english_verse: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bālifì-bi yii: <Ba di sá iwaatootipaan in pu ni cá nee ní?> Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti ní bi kíǹ ki yíì ipaan gbanti yii iwaatootipaan.

english_verse: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
translation_verse: Too kɔŋkɔnnee, ni yaa bíi ŋáań ni-saraabi ki yaa bíi wù ni-biyaamu ŋŋmi ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì awaayee, ni bíi kɔ̄ntí ni-ba tijɔkɔndi dee. Ní ni dàkafī yii m làá kíí ní bàlifì-maaa, Isirayeel yab? Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, maa làá kíí ní bàlifì-mi.

english_verse: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Ni lì yii: <Ti là kí nīn bí kii atimbun ŋin kíǹee nín bí puee, a lì kii ntimu mun kíǹee nib nín bí puee. Ti là kí nīn tòotī isufi nì ataŋkpee. Ama an kaa làá ŋá kii ni nín dàkafī puee.

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, m nín lī puee sɔ̀. M làá dàkà-ni m-pɔŋŋu nì m-kpabil ní kí kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī ni-pu ní kí nín ŋmā kí jī ni-pu dibeel.

english_verse: and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered
translation_verse: M làá dàkà-ni m-pɔŋŋu nì m-kpabil nì m-ŋuul ní kí ŋmā kí nyāntí-ni atimbun nì ntimu mun poon ni yàl̄ee, ní kí kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì.

english_verse: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
translation_verse: M làá cùnnì-ni kuteeun kí kàkatī-ni kí wàatī atimbun ŋin kíǹee, ní kí sòoǹ ni-bɔti niin.

english_verse: and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt.
translation_verse: Kii m nín nìn sòon̄ ni-bɔti Eejipiti teekun puee, míǹ ní m làá sòoǹ ni-bɔti. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: M làá dū m-kpandɔŋu ní kí kpàà-ni, ní kí yàntī ní nīn tɔ́ m-poondi.

english_verse: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M làá nyāntí bin jáń nì mi kaa tɔ́-mee ni-kansikin. M làá nyāntiń-bi ntimu mun poon bi kóòyee, ama bi-taal kaa làá tāā Isirayeel tiŋkin. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.>

english_verse: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Isirayeel yab, báà ŋma ŋūǹ kí tòotī u-waaŋi, ama míǹ boonee, ni là kaa là, ní làá dāá nīn tɔ́-mi ní. Ní taa kpèè m-circir yindi fám kí nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì ni-waaŋi.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Isirayeel yab, ni-kɔkɔ làá dāá jāam̀-mi m-circir jool pu, Isirayeel joofɔkɔl pu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. Niin ní m làá dāá fōō-ni nì iŋal ili ní kí dāá fōō tin ni dūu sú-mee, ni-wampɔkaati nì ni-saraamɔntiibi.

english_verse: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
translation_verse: M yaa láa nyántìń-ni atimbun kansikin nì ntimu mun poon ni yàl̄ee ki kóoǹ-ni ki kpáfì ki dóòyee ní ḿ dāá fōō ni-saraabi bí nīn sɔ́fì ki sɔ̀ŋkī m-pɔbil. M yaa ŋá-ni mimmee, m dàkā atimbun ŋin kíǹee yii m sá circir Nimbɔtiu dee.

english_verse: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: M làá dāá gíiǹní-ni Isirayeel tiŋkin, kitiŋ kin ní m yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu ki pūtì kí tīī ni-baabee. Ŋyunti gbantee, ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
translation_verse: Niinee, ni làá dāá téetí ni-bimbim nì atuun ŋin kɔkɔ ni ŋá ki kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndee pu. Atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ ni ŋée puee, ni-naŋki làá dāá nyā nì ni-ba.

english_verse: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab, an kaa sá ni-bimbikpitim nì ni-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi ní m làá kpèè, ama m-yindi pu ní m làá ŋá míǹ kí tīī-ni. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.>»

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbiin kí túĺ ŋgiil pú. Sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ dijandi gbanti pu, ní kí dū m-bɔti kí nàatī binib bin kóò Neegeeb bambaŋkunee.

english_verse: My sword has been polished; it's sharp and ready to kill.
translation_verse: An puee, sii nisaaleen, nín̄ yáliŋkí. Nín̄ yáliŋkí nì dipɔɔbiildi poon nì ntuntun bi-kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_verse: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī. Tùkù binib tin man ni-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ nì bee. Kitàataajiki kiba sɔ̀, kitàataajiki kin jītí ki jìl̀ pàlpalee.

english_verse: They will lose all courage and stumble with fear. My slaughtering sword is waiting at every gate, flashing and ready to kill.
translation_verse: Bi lōoǹ-kì kí pɔ̀fì binib ní, bi pítì-kì kí nīn jìl̀ ní.

english_verse: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
translation_verse: Nisaaleen, fáá dinimbinaamandi biilii! Bi tāntì kitàataajiki gbanti m-nibul nì abɔtibil ŋin kɔkɔ kpòotī Isirayeel tiŋkee pu ní. Bi làá kpɔ̀-bi kí kpáaǹ m-nibul. Fáá a-bindi kí dàkà a-nimbaaku.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
translation_verse: Sii nisaaleenee, fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī. Kpāafì abaal, diba, mili, mita pu, di sá yii ŋkúm tàataajiki dee, kitàataajiki kin di làá pɔ̀fì binib ki māntìi tú-bi an kɔkɔ puee.

english_verse: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
translation_verse: Kì làá bīil̀ bi-pɔbil kí yàntī bí lítí tikpil. M dū ŋkúm tàataajiki ki bíl̀ mpunyɔmu kɔkɔ pu. Bi bɔ́ntì-kì kí nīn jìl̀ ní, bi lōoǹ-kì kí ŋmā kí pɔ̀fì binib ní.

english_verse: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
translation_verse: Kitàataajiki kin jītí pámpamee, pɔ̀fì binib ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú. Fàtī a-nyɔkɔ kin cɔ́m̀ee an kɔkɔ pú.

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, cátí adan ali ŋin pu ní Babiloon bɔtiu tàataajiki làá ŋmā kí dī kí dāan̄ee. Adan alee làá nyānní kitimbaantiin ní. Didandi kamaa kílilaŋkee, ní ŋmà kupiliŋu pu kitiŋ kin poon ní di cée yindi.

english_verse: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
translation_verse: Cátí didandi din pu ní Babiloon janjaliibi làá dī kí cù Amɔn yab tiŋki Raabee, ní didandi din kíǹee ń nīn cá Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin bi máń digundi ki tú kì bí Juuda tiŋkinee.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
translation_verse: Babiloon bɔtiu síl̀ isampuyakati, laakin adan alee kífée kí bɔ̄ tibɔɔl. U cīkifì ipiin, ki bālifì awaa ki kpēē tiwaŋkuti pɔɔŋi címmm.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
translation_verse: Jeerusaleem yab dākafì yii bi nín bālifì an cúú Jeerusaleemee kaa sá tiba, di sá yii bi pūtì yii bi làá wúń bi-pu. Ama ní Babiloon bɔtiu bíi téetí-bi bi nín kaa yúl̀ nì ti-Dindaan deedeeyee pu. An puee u làá cúú-bi kí cùnnì kuyuŋu.

english_verse: You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
translation_verse: An puee man bi-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì bi tin bí nee yii: <Ni pée téetí-mi ni-yìntitam nì ni-kpitii pu ní kaa gbèentí. Ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poonee, ni-kpitii pée nyáń ní ki pá mpaampiin pu. Too, ni nín kaa yàntī bí súntí ni-puee puee, ni làá kɔ́ unannanli ŋaan.

english_verse: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
translation_verse: «Sii dibɔtibil din di kā Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel kaa yú deedee ki sá unikpitee, ŋwiin ŋun ní a-kpitii làá gbèen̄ee dòoń.

english_verse: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.
translation_verse: Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Bi làá fōō ŋŋaabu ŋun dàkà yii a sá ubɔtee ní kí cíkití a-beefuuliiki. Tiwan làá kpántí ti-paaŋyi! Bi làá yòon̄ un nìn sīntì u-ba taapuee yilpu, ní kí sìntī un nìn yōoǹ u-ba yilpuee taapu.

english_verse: You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Adigbuŋkati, adigbuŋkati ŋma! M làá yàntī Jeerusaleem ń kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma. M tīī ubɔ mpɔn ú jáǹ-kì. Bi làá yàaǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki kɔkɔ, ama see un m tīī mpɔn gbantee ń bàń kí wàatī.» Bi làá jáǹ Amɔn yab

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, bɔ́ntí a-ba kí sòoǹ Jeerusaleem, nnikpaakoon tiŋki nee bɔti, á taa gùgufì! Yàntī kí béé ki-tuŋkpitiŋ.

english_verse: and tell them I am saying: Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished!
translation_verse: Dū tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti tùkū-see kí nàatī-kì yii: <A sá kitiŋ kin nib kù binibee. Bi nín bíi ŋáań mimmee, bi bíi bɔ́ntí a-nàantam yuntiŋu dee. Bi bí ki māā awaa ki kɔ̄ntí-si tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks,
translation_verse: Binib bin bi kūūyee puee, a jíń dibɔkpil. Binib bin kóò a-nee nín máń awaa ŋiŋyee puee, a kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Bi nín ŋá mimmee puee, a sútìń a-bɔsooŋyi wiiŋŋu dee, bi làá nàan̄-si án kaa ti làá yúntí! An pu ní m làá kɔ́ǹ-si icoo anibul ŋin kíǹee nimbiin, ntimu kɔkɔ nib làá bèel̀-si.

english_verse: and people far and near will make fun of your misery.
translation_verse: A sá tijɔkɔndi nì fikil fikil tiŋki ní. An puee bin pìlīǹ-see nì bin dátiǹ-see làá bèel̀-si.>

english_verse: Your own leaders use their power to murder.
translation_verse: «Sii cee ní Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ cáá mpɔn ŋun bi cááyee ki kù binib.

english_verse: None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Sii cee ní unil kpèé u-baa nì u-na fám, ki mùul̄ unicaan ní ki wɔ́b̀ ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi.

english_verse: You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day.
translation_verse: Baa dū tin bi dūu sú-mee ki yíiń tiba, ní kaa tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa.

english_verse: Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things.
translation_verse: Sii cee ní binib tūntí bi-jutiibi abɔgabil kí ŋmā kí kpɔ̀-bi. A-nib jīǹ tiwaajin ajoon pu ní ki ŋáań ajɔkɔntuun.

english_verse: Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period
translation_verse: Biba dɔ̀ nì bi-baa nimpoobi, ní biba mun dɔ̀ nì binimpoobi ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi fùul̀ ŋkpinee.

english_verse: or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister.
translation_verse: Biba ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ki dɔ̀ nì bi-jutiibi nimpoobi, biba mun ŋáań mpɔn ki dɔ̀ nì bi-jipɔmbi nimpoobi, àá bi-niisalib pēē baa.

english_verse: Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
translation_verse: Sii cee ní unil kíikí bí tīī-u animbil ú kpɔ̀ u-juti. Unil yaa pīnnì u-juti animbilee, u nyàab̀ udaan ń dāá téeǹ-u kí páań ní. Binib bí ki fìkì bi-jutiibi wanti kí ŋmā kí kpántí bigaajab ní kí súntí man pu kpataaa. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes.
translation_verse: «Ma mun làá kpāafì abaal kí jáǹ-ni ni-paatii in kaa sá tibulcin paatiiyee, nì nnikpaakoon tuuŋŋi ŋin ni ŋáaǹee pu.

english_verse: When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāá jáǹ-nee, ni làá dāá ká mpɔn nì dipɔbil kí yūĺ m-nimbiinaaa? Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, ní m yaa sòon̄ puee, míǹ ní m ŋáań.

english_verse: I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways.
translation_verse: M làá jà-ni kí yàl̄ atimbun ŋin kíǹee poon ntincamun, ní kí kúntí ni-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. Jerusalem Must Be Purified
translation_verse: Ni làá fá ni-jilmau atimbun ŋin kíǹee cee, ama ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, pīlifì. Isirayeel kpántì m-cee kii agɔŋgɔŋkpilee ní. Bi bí kii animbil nì tasa kúti nì tikúnyuntikaal nì tikúti nì tikúbɔn tin nyìm̀ ki kā ucaa ŋmiŋunee ní.

english_verse: I will be like a metalworker who collects that metal from the furnace and melts it down. I will collect the Israelites and blow on them with my fiery anger. They will melt inside the city of Jerusalem
translation_verse: M làá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin táb ní kí yàntī m-ŋuul ŋmiŋu ń wà-ni ní dùntī kii tikútee.

english_verse: like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger. Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
translation_verse: Ni làá nīn bí kii animbil kúti tin bi dūntì kipaai poonee ní. Niinee ni làá dāá béé yii man ni-Dindaan di kpáatì m-ŋuul ki sītì ni-pu.>»

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious!
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, tùkù Jeerusaleem tiŋki yii kì sá kitiŋ kin kaa ŋá ki-ba circiree ní, kitiŋ kin pu utaa kaa nìn̄ m-ŋuul dalee.

english_verse: Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
translation_verse: A-bɔnaatiliibi bí kii gbikinti un nimbiliŋ máǹ ú cúú kuwaŋkuluu kí tɔ̀ntēe ní. Míǹ ní bi tɔ̀ntī binib, ki fòol̄ bi-gaajati nì bi-wammɔntiiti, ní ki yāntì bi-kpiipoobi wíiǹ kitiŋ nee poon.

english_verse: The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
translation_verse: Bi-saraaŋaliibi nyēē m-marab boon ní kaa tɔ́ m-circir paaŋyi. Baa gàntī tin bí circiree nì tin kaa bí circiree. Baa dàkà binib bí ŋmā kí gàntī tin sá tijɔkɔndee nì tin kaa sá tijɔkɔndee. Baa pée fātìi tɔ́ iwiŋŋuŋfikaa. Bi-puee baa tìì-mi tinyool.

english_verse: Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
translation_verse: Bitindaŋkpilib bí kii agbiŋgbil ŋin di cúú kuwaŋkuluu kí tɔ̀ntēe ní. Bi kù binib kí kpántí bigaajab.

english_verse: And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me.
translation_verse: Bi-bɔnaatiliibi bìintí tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ pu kii bi nín pōontí digundi puee ní. Bi kāntí aleedaka ŋin kaa sá ibaamɔn leedakaŋee ní ki sòoǹ ki nàatī tinyimɔmbɔti. Bi lì yii bi fòol̄ man cee tibɔti ní ki cáa nàatī, ama ní man ni-Dindaan kaa sòon̄ nì bi.

english_verse: The people themselves cheat and rob; they abuse the poor and take advantage of foreigners.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ poonee, binib dàkà dikpabil ní ki yù. Bi mùul̄ usoodaan nì unandaan ní ki wɔ́b̀ unicaan, kaa nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu.

english_verse: I looked for someone to defend the city and to protect it from my anger, as well as to stop me from destroying it. But I found no one.
translation_verse: M nyàab̄ bi-kansikin ubɔ ń bàà mā digundi, kí yūĺ laakin digundi bátìi lítì dibundi dōoǹee kí mɔ̄tì kitiŋ nee pu m-ŋuul ń taa bīil̀-kèe, ama maa ká báà ubɔ.

english_verse: So in my fierce anger, I will punish the Israelites for what they have done, and they will know that I am furious. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m kpáatì m-ŋuul ki sītì bi-pu. M nāaǹ-bi m-ŋuul ŋmiŋu poon ní ki pàn̄-bi bi-tuŋkpitiŋ paati. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, listen to this story about two sisters.
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, binimpoobi bili di bí ki pēē na.

english_verse: The older one was named Oholah, which stands for Samaria; the younger one was Oholibah, which stands for Jerusalem. They became my wives and gave birth to my children.
translation_verse: Bi nìn yíì ukpil yii Ooyoola ní ki yíì uwaal yii Ooyooliiba. Ukpilee, Samaarii dee, ní uwaal sá Jeerusaleem. Man di nìn cáab́-bi ní bi màl̄-mi mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu.

english_verse: Even though Oholah was my wife, she continued to be a prostitute and chased after Assyrian lovers.
translation_verse: Min kamaa man di yì Ooyoolayee, u nìn kpántì kinimpulaakpaai. U nìn cáá kukpeeu ki néeń u-bɔmbi, Asuur yab bijanjaliibi

english_verse: She offered herself to soldiers in purple uniforms: handsome, high-ranking officers and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: bin pēē abɔkutiman cínciŋee nì gɔminab nì kɔmandambi nì binaacimpɔmbi bin ŋān̄ee nì bitanjakaliibi.

english_verse: She had sex with all the important Assyrian officials and even worshiped their disgusting idols.
translation_verse: Ooyoola nìn néeń Asuur yab kàliŋkpaambi gbanti ní ki nìn kɔ̄ntí u-ba tijɔkɔndi ki tòotī bin kɔkɔ u nìn pée néeńee waaŋi.

english_verse: Once she started doing these things in Egypt, she never stopped. Men slept with her, and she was always ready for sex.
translation_verse: U nín nìn bí Eejipiti tiŋkin ki kíĺ alaakpaatuun ŋiŋyee, ŋíǹ ní u gbíntìi nìkì. U nín nìn bí niin ki sá usapɔɔnee, bininjab nìn dɔ̀ nì u ní ki ŋúb́ u-sapɔmbiiŋi ki ŋmáliŋkí ní ki kɔ́ǹ-u ajɔkɔntuun poon.

english_verse: So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m dū-u ki ŋá u-bɔmbi, Asuur yab bin u nìn lèe ŋaan.

english_verse: They ripped off her clothes, then captured her children and killed her. Women everywhere talked about what had happened to Oholah.
translation_verse: Bíǹ cúú-u ki pēetì ní ki yōoǹ u-jipɔmbi nì u-sapɔmbi ní ki dū kitàataajiki ki kūū-u. Míǹ ní bi nìn dáaĺ u-tafal ní u kpántì ŋabika ki tīī binimpoobi bin kíǹee.» Jeerusaleem ŋá tilaakpaal

english_verse: Oholibah saw all this, but she was more sinful and wanted sex more than her sister Oholah ever did.
translation_verse: «U-naal Ooyooliiba ká tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ. Ama u-kpeeku poonee, úǹ gíti kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ki jítiǹ Ooyoola. Úǹ gíti ŋá alaakpaatuun ki jítiǹ u-maan gba.

english_verse: Oholibah also chased after good-looking Assyrian officers, uniformed soldiers, and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: U mun nìn néeń Asuur yab ní, gɔminab nì kɔmandambi nì bijanjaliibi bin pēē tiwannyaandee nì bitanjakaliibi nì binaacimpɔmbi bin ŋān̄ee.

english_verse: Just like her sister, she did vulgar things.
translation_verse: U mun nìn dū u-ba ki múĺ tijɔkɔndin. M nìn ká yii bi-liitil dī nsambaanti ní.

english_verse: But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red.
translation_verse: Ama Ooyooliiba úǹ nìn gíti ŋá tilaakpaal kí jítiǹ u-maan. Dalbee ní u ká bi lēē bininjab ki nákáǹ digundi pu ki dū peentaman ki kɔ̀l̄-bi. Bininjab gbanti nìn sá Babiloon yab ní.

english_verse: They had belts around their waists and large turbans on their heads, and they reminded her of Babylonian cavalry officers.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū dambalab ki gbìn̄ bi-cammu ní ki dū ŋŋaabu ki fìn̄ bi-yiliŋ. Bin nìn náań nì bibaatandambi binyaambi. Babiloon yab nín pée bí pu bi-dumpuee ní bi nìn lēē ki nákáǹ.

english_verse: As soon as she looked at them, she wanted to have sex with them. And so, she sent messengers to bring them to her.
translation_verse: Ooyooliiba nín pée wál̀-bi yéèyee ní bi kɔ́-u ní u tú binib bi-cee bi-tiŋkin.

english_verse: Men from Babylonia came and had sex with her so many times that she got disgusted with them.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Babiloon yab dɔ́miń ki dōoǹ nì u. Bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-u tijɔkɔndi. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bíil̀-u kpataaayee, ní u kíǹ ki ná-bi.

translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, aa làá sòoǹ Ooyoola nì Ooyooliiba bɔtaaa? Dū ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi ŋée kí bíĺ bi-nimbiin.

translation_verse: Di sá yii ŋwiin ŋun bi kūū bi-jipɔmbi ki ŋá saraa ki tīī awaayee, ŋwiin gbanti ní bi kɔ́ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki kɔ́ǹ-ŋu tijɔkɔndi. Tin ní bi ŋá man m-ba diikunee dee.

translation_verse: Kí kūtèe, bi tú binib bí yíiń bininjab bin nyánní ndandati timmunee. Bíǹ tin pée lì yii bi fòol̄ bi-nyɔɔbundee, bi kpáàa bāań bi-cee. Bi nìn fùl̄ ki bɔ̄ntì culoo ki nyɔ̄kɔntì bi-ba ki kíǹ ki kā ki cí-bi.

translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní bi tātìi dōoǹ nlambanyaamu pu. Nlambamuee nyɔkɔpuee, teebil un pu talaalutuukaa nì ŋkpam min sɔ́fì m nìn tīī-uee tɔ́kɔ́.

english_verse: Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:

translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

translation_verse: M sòon̄ nì samaa kutaafaauee, ní m-nimpuu kpíì kujoou. Kutaa wúntì ní m ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì-mi yii ḿ ŋá puee.

translation_verse: Ní binib bālifì-mi ḿ tùkù-bi kun ní m ŋée taapu.

translation_verse: Ní m kíí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan tīī-mi dinyɔɔbundi nee

english_verse: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
translation_verse: Ní dū iŋaabu kí fìn̄ ni-yiliŋ kí nīn táká anaataka. Ní taa yāliŋkì kí taa sɔ̄. Ama, ni-kpitii puee, ni làá dúntí ní báà ŋma làá nīn yáliŋkí u-juti pu.

translation_verse: Eeseekiyeel làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu ní ki tīī-ni. Tin bi sòon̄ ki síiǹ yii án làá bàńee yaa láa bāańee, ní dāá ŋámaan kii úǹ nín ŋá puee deedee. Niinee, ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti.>»

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well.
translation_verse: «Sii nisaaleen, pīlifì, m làá yòon̄ bi-kansikin circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun di sá bi-balilaŋki, ki sá bi-pɔɔpindi bi kpèé, ŋkɔŋkoon ŋun pu bi fàal̀ ní ki dū bi-mákal ki páaǹee. M làá dāá yòon̄ bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib.

translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, un ŋmátì ki nyáń nnaabu gbantinee làá dāá māafì-ni tin jítèe.

translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, a làá dāá ŋmā kí sòoǹ. A làá dāá ká kinyɔkɔ kí sòoǹ nì un ŋmátì ki nyáń nnaabun ki dɔ́mińee. A làá dāá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu ní ki tīī m-nibul ní bí dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon
translation_verse: Nisaaleen, fàtī a-ba kí túĺ Amɔn yab cee kí sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ bi-pu.

english_verse: and tell them: You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners.

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: An puee, m làá yàntī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú yab ń fōō ni-tiŋki. Bi làá gāā bi-janjanaapaaŋi ni-tiŋki pu ní kí cóoń bi-tantib niin. Bíǹ di làá ŋmɔ́ ni-sufii biliŋ ní kí nyɔ̀ ni-waŋkuti naabiim.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī ni-tiŋyil Raaba ń kpántí kunaakpaapɔɔu kí tīī igutaamu, ní kí yàntī Amɔn tiŋki ń kpántí ipii naabakati. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: An puee m làá dàkà-ni m-pɔŋŋu ní kí dū-ni kí líiǹ atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib bí fūkul̀-ni pílpil. M làá kúntí-ni anibul kansikin, naa ti làá nīn cáá kitiŋ ní kí kúntí-ni múb. Niinee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.» Ti-Dindaan làá jáǹ Moowaab yab

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Moowaab yab lī yii Juuda yab kpántì kii atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib nín bí puee ní.

english_verse: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: An puee m làá yàntī bí jáǹ ntimu mun wúń Moowaab tiŋkpaanyɔmmuee. Binannanliibi làá nàan̄-mu kiba kiba ki kpáaǹ ntinnyaammu kii Beeti-Yeesimooti nì Baal-Meeyɔn nì Kiiriyatayiimee.

english_verse: The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever,
translation_verse: M làá yàntī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú yab ń já kí fōō Moowaab tiŋki kii bi nín jáń ki fōō Amɔn tiŋki puee. An yaa ŋá mimmee, baa ti làá téetí Amɔn yab pu atimbun kansikin.

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: M làá dáaĺ Moowaab yab tafal ní bí béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.» Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Eedoom yab pu

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Eedoom yab tɔ̀n̄ Juuda yab ipɔntoon, an pu ní bi fōō dibɔkpil.

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá dàkà Eedoom yab m-pɔŋŋu. M làá kúntí kitiŋ gbanti nib nì ki-waŋkuti. M làá yàntī kí kpántí kuteeu kí yòon̄ Teeman tiŋki kí cáá sāā Deedan tiŋki. Bi làá kpɔ̀ bin kóò Eedoom tiŋkinee kujaaun ní.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: M làá yàntī m-nibul Isirayeel yab nín tɔ̀ m-pɔntooŋyi Eedoom yab pu. M-ŋuukpaandi nín bàlifī puee, míǹ ní Isirayeel yab làá ŋá-bi. Mimmee, Eedoom yab làá béé kun di sá m-pɔntooŋyee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.» Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Fiiliistii yab pu

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Fiiliistii yab tɔ̀n̄ ipɔntoon. Bi dū nnimbidiki ki tɔ̀n̄ bi-nannanliibi bin sá talku nannanliibee ipɔntoon ní ki céetì-bi.

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: An puee, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá dàkà-bi m-pɔŋŋu. M làá kúntí-bi, bíǹ bin kɔkɔ nyánní Kafitoor ki dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ ditiŋkugbandee.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: M làá tɔ̀-bi ipɔntoon in sá ikpaanee ní kí dáaĺ bi-tafal ŋkpitim pu. Niinee bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin saalaa nì diba boon, uŋmal wimpeekaaŋuee, ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, pīlifì, Tiir yab bíi bèel̄ Jeerusaleem yab ki lì yii: <An nāaǹ Jeerusaleem, kitiŋ kin pu báà ŋma nìn jītée. An māaǹ-kì! Ti mun yuntiŋu bāań tí kpántí bigaajab deeyaa! Di sá yii kì kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋma ní!>

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii m làá jáǹ sii Tiir tiŋki. M làá cáań atimbun kupaau kí léeń a-pu kii tiŋku nín yòontí u-nyiŋgbanti yilpu puee.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Bi làá kpēelikì agun ŋin a máń ki tú a-tiŋkee ní kí wìil̀ a-sintil difɔkɔŋi. M làá kɔ́tí kitiŋ tam ní kí pée kíń ditaŋkpal dí nīn dɔ̄ fám.

english_verse: where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed
translation_verse: Tiir làá kpántí tiŋku kansikin mpaan ŋun pu bijɔncuuliibi làá nīn díntí bi-laantee ní. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ ní ki làá ŋá míǹ. Atimbun aba làá dāan̄ kí fūkul̀ Tiir tiŋki.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi làá kpēelikì ki-timbilimmu mun bí ditiŋkugbandee. Niinee báà ŋma làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: «Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii: <M làá cáań ŋgan pú bɔtiu un pɔ̄ɔ̄yee, an dàkà yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar ú jáǹ-si. U làá cáań itaamu nì janjatɔrɔkub nì bitanjakaliibi nì dijanjakitikpaandi kí jáǹ-si.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: U làá kpēelikì a-timbilimu mun bí ditiŋkugbandee. Míǹ boonee, bijanjaliibi bin dɔ́miń kí jáǹ-see làá gbà gɔtab bin poon bi làá nīn kàal̀ ki jáà nì see ní kí mā ŋgumu mun boon bi làá nīn bí ki jáà nì see, ní kí mā digundi din làá nīn sá kii digbampɔɔlee kí jáǹ-si.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Bi làá dū bi-janjamasiimbi kí gbá kí wìil̀ a-guŋŋi ŋin māntìi tú-see ní kí dū jikab kí kpēelikì a-sintil difɔkɔŋi.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Bi-taamui nín làá nīn wīikí puee kpɔŋkpɔŋku di làá bìin̄ a-pu, ní bi-tanjakaliibi wooku nì bi-tɔrɔkub taaŋi nín màntī puee làá yàntī a-guŋŋi ń cìŋkì. Di sá yii bi làá dī a-punyɔmmu kí kɔ́ kii bi nín wìil̄ digundi pu kí dī kí kɔ́ puee ní.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Bi-taamui taaŋi làá tāā tāā a-daŋŋi kɔkɔ pu ní bí dū ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀ a-nib ní kí téé a-jantalkukpaambee kí lúkú.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Bi làá yòon̄ a-gaajati ní kí fūkul̀ a-wanti. Bi làá wìil̀ a-guŋŋi ní kí kpēelikì a-dinyaaŋŋi. Bi làá yòon̄ ŋi-taŋkpeeŋi nì ŋi-dɔi nì ŋi-tam kí cáá tɔ̄ tiŋkun.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: M làá kúntí ilan in a gèe, baa ti làá gbìl̄ a-bati pu.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī á kpántí kii ditaŋkpal din pu tiba kaa bīīyee ní bijɔncuuliibi ń nīn díntí bi-laanti di-pu. Baa ti làá fàtīí náań kitiŋ gbanti dalba dalba. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ ní tin m sòon̄ee, tíǹ ní m làá ŋá.>

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ Tiir pu tiŋyee sɔ̀. Bi yaa láa nāaǹ sii Tiir tiŋki ki kūū a-nib ní ki gbìl̄ bin fōō tiweendee yaliŋkii puee, bin kóò ntimu mun poon nnyim māntìi túee wunti làá dāá fōō dijinjikil.

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Atimbun ŋin kóò atiŋkugbánee bɔtiibi làá kpákatí bi-beejaliŋ pu kí pèetī bi-bɔkutikpaaŋŋi nì bi-bɔkutiŋ ŋin bi gbáńee. Bi làá nyɔ̀ ŋkpatim ní kí kàl̄ kitiŋ. Bi-wunti làá nīn gbíntìi jìkì, ní bí kɔ́ dinyoondin a-pu.

english_verse: and sing this funeral song: “The great city beside the sea is destroyed! Its people once ruled the coast and terrified everyone there.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá gāā-si ŋkpiisilan nee yii: <Bi nāaǹ kitiŋ kin nyáń diyindee, bi kúntì-si tiŋkub kansikin! Ki-nib nìn cáá tiŋkub pu mpɔn, ní báà ŋma nìn fàŋkí-bi.

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, bi nín nāaǹ-kì nee atimbun ŋin bí tiŋkub kansikinee wunti bíi jìkì, bin kóò atiŋkugbánee nyùn̄ ŋkpatim, kun puee aa ti bí.>

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii m làá yàntī á kpántí kii ntimu mun kpántì adigbuŋkati ubɔ nì ubɔ kaa ti kóò mu-poonee. M làá yàntī tiŋku taapu nyim ń yīkì kí bìin̄ a-pu.

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī á cùú ŋàl̄ taapu taŋkpiibi pu, bin bí niin cannaakuee. M làá yàntī á cùú nīn kóò kitiŋ taapu taapu, kí nīn bí kii jaanjaan digbuŋkatiŋ ŋin bí niinee. Sii nì bitaŋkpiibi bin līntiǹ-see di làá nīn bí. Aa ti làá ŋmā kí jɔ̄mìń kaa ti làá nīn cáá mpaan binifoobi tiŋki pu.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
