english_verse: Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people.
translation_verse: Bi làá lì yii: <Kitiŋ kin bi nìn dūu fée fātìi kpántì kii Eedeen kpaabuee. Ntimu mun poon bi nìn gbáń ki wīil̀ adiin an kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋmee, bi fātìi máń adiin binib kíǹ ki kóò mu-ni.

english_verse: Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Niinee atimbun ŋin dáá gbíntìi bí ki māntìi tú-nee làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan, un di fàtīi māā ntimu mun poon bi gbáń ki wīil̀ adiinee, ní ki fàtīi cōontí tin bi fùkū ki fée. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ ní tin m yaa sòon̄ee, tíǹ ní m ŋáań.

english_verse: I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá yàntī Isirayeel yab ń mèè-mi ní ḿ kíí-bi ní kí yàntī bí bùtī kii ipiiyee.

english_verse: The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Dooooyee, binib yaa nìn kpáfì kí jī jiŋaalibee, ipii in bi nìn cáa ŋáań saraabee nìn gbéè Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní. Bi nìn cāabìń-i tipicaŋkpun tipicaŋkpun ní. Míǹ ní binib bin làá dāan̄ kí kɔ́ ni-timmu mun kpántì adigbuŋkati nee làá nīn wīikí. Niinee, báà ŋma làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_verse: Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones.
translation_verse: M nìn gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu m-ni ní u-Fam yōoǹ-mi ki cáa yóoǹ ditantakal diba kansikin. Akpab di nìn gbí ditantakalee poon.

english_verse: The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì m māntìi tú akpabee ditantakalee poon. Akpabee nìn wīikí tikpilku ní ki nìn kūń.

english_verse: He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?” I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, mimmee akpab nee ŋūǹ kí fàtīí ká dimaŋfalaaa?» Ní m kíí yii: «M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, sii baba di nyí.»

english_verse: He then told me to say: Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you,
translation_verse: Ní u bí-mi yii: «Fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī akpab nee. Tùkù-ŋi yii: <Akpakulim, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi!

english_verse: “I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bíi sòoǹ nì ni puee sɔ̀. M làá cáań dimaŋfal fooku kí ŋá ni-ni, ní ní fàtīí ká dimaŋfal.

english_verse: I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: M làá dū igiin kí páań ni-pu ní kí yàntī tiwunnan ń nyā ni-pu ní kí dū ŋwuŋgban kí bìin̄. M làá dū dimaŋfal fooku kí ŋá ni-ni, ní ní fàtīí ká dimaŋfal. Niinee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.>»

english_verse: I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together!
translation_verse: Ní m dū tibɔtee ki sòon̄ nì akpabee kii ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì-mi puee. Ŋyunti ŋun m bíi sòoǹee ní m gbìl̄ kuwoou kubɔ pu ní akpabee kíĺ ki bíi sútí ki pìl̀ tɔb.

english_verse: I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
translation_verse: M bíi kpèéyee ní ki ká yii igiin páaǹ ŋi-pu, ní tiwunnan nyáń ki páaǹ ní ŋwuŋgban dūu bīiǹ. Ama dimaŋfal fooku kaa nìn dáá bí ŋi-ni.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, fōō m-nyɔɔbundi kí dūú sòoǹ nì dimaŋfal fooku yii: <Dimaŋfal fooku, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nyānní kitiŋ jannaatiliŋ pú kí dāan̄ kí fáá anikpil nee pu ŋí ká dimaŋfal.>»

english_verse: As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
translation_verse: Ní m dū ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi ki nāatì kii u nín kpáafì-mi ḿ ŋá puee. Dimaŋfal fookuee dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ anikpilee ni ní ŋi fātìi ká dimaŋfal ní ki nìn yíkìi yúl̀. Bi nìn dūu ŋá dijanjakitikpaŋkpaandi ní.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, akpab nee sá Isirayeel nibul ní. Bi bí ki lì yii: <Ti bí kii akpakulimee, ti-mákal dóò, an dóò ti-pu dee.>

english_verse: So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel,
translation_verse: An puee dū m-nyɔɔbundi kí nàatī-bi kí tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì bee yii: <M làá cúú ni-kaakuliŋ kí pìitī ní kí cúú nimbi, man nibul kí nyāntiń. M làá fàtīí gíiǹ-ni ni-tiŋki pu.

english_verse: and when that happens, you will realize that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M yaa láa pīitì ni-kaakuliŋ ki nyántìń-nee, ni làá dāá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.” Judah and Israel Together Again
translation_verse: M làá dū m-Fam kí ŋá ni-ni, ní ní nīn bí dimaŋfalin. M làá dū-ni kí kàan̄ ni-tiŋkin. Niinee ni làá béé yii man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, ní tin m yaa lēe, tíǹ ní m ŋáań. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.» Ti-Dindaan làá dū Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ kí kpāfì

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.”
translation_verse: «Sii nisaaleen, yòon̄ didɔgindi kí ŋmà di-pu yii: <Juuda nì Isirayeel yab bin bí dibeel nee poonee>. Míǹ boonee, á gíti yòon̄ didɔgindi diba mun kí ŋmà di-pu yii: <Jooseefi àá Eefiraayiim nì Isirayeel yab bin bí dibeel nee poonee.>

english_verse: Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick.
translation_verse: Dū adɔgin ali gbanti nyɔmmu kí bíĺ kí tūū tɔb án kpántí kii didɔgimbaantiilee a-ŋaan.

english_verse: And when your people ask you what this means,
translation_verse: A-nibul yab làá bàlifì-si á cántí taapu kí tùkù-bi.

english_verse: tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
translation_verse: Á tùkù-bi yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ nì bi puee sɔ̀. M làá yòon̄ didɔgindi din di sá Jooseefi nì Isirayeel yabee kí dūú túkuń Juuda dɔgindi pu. Adɔgin alee làá kpántí didɔgimbaantiil ní m-ŋaan.

english_verse: Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone
translation_verse: «Á nīn ŋúb́ adɔgin ŋin pu ní a ŋmàn̄ee a-ŋaan báà ŋma ń wāl̀.

english_verse: and then say: I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, á dū tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee kí nàatī-bi yii: <Isirayeel yab, m làá nyāntiń-ni atimbun ŋin cee ni cūtèe ŋaan. M làá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-ni ni-tiŋkin.

english_verse: I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī ní kpántí ditimbumbaantiil Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu. Ni-kɔkɔ làá nīn cáá ubɔtibaanti ní. Naa ti làá nīn sá atimbun ali ní baa làá ti yàkatī-ni abee ali pu.

english_verse: They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Naa ti làá tòotī awaa, kaa ti làá ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi àá kí yìntīǹ-mi kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi. M làá nyāntí-ni laakin kɔkɔ ni cūtì ki yīntiǹ-mee ní kí fíntí-ni kí nyāntí ni-jɔkɔnti kɔkɔn. Ni làá nīn sá m-nibul ní man ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Ni làá nīn kóò kitiŋ kin ní m tīī m-tɔntɔnliu Jaakɔb ní ni-naanjab kāl̀ ki-poonee. Ni làá nīn kíǹ ki kóò niin ní jaanjaan, ni nì ni-biyaamu nì ni-naantiibi. Man tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi di làá nīn sá ni-bɔtibil kí nīn cá talku.

english_verse: I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time,
translation_verse: M làá pòon̄-ni ŋgbansɔŋfi poondi din làá nīn bí ki cá jaanjaanee. M làá dū-ni kí kàan̄ kitiŋ nee poon ní kí bùtī ni-maaliŋu. M làá dū m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kí síiń ni-kansikin ŋú nīn bí ki cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: and I will live among my people and be their God.
translation_verse: M làá nīn kóò ni-kansikin. M làá nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu ní nimbi ń nīn sá m-nibul.

english_verse: Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_verse: M yaa láa dū m-kɔŋkooŋŋu ki síiǹ ni-kansikin kí nīn cá jaanjaanee ní atimbun ŋin kíǹee làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan ní ki dū Isirayeel ki sú ú nīn bí m-tundin kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
translation_verse: «Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbiin kí túĺ Gɔɔgi un bí Maagoogi tiŋkin, ki sá Meeseeki nì Tubaal bɔtibilee. Dū m-bɔti kí nàatī-u.

english_verse: and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords.
translation_verse: M làá dū tikúti kí kpàl̄ a-nyɔɔkpaween ní kí dáaĺ-si mpɔn kí nyāntí. M làá nyāntí-si mpɔn a-tiŋkin, sii nì a-janjaliibi kɔkɔ nì a-taamui nì a-tanjakaliibi bin pēē tiwannyaandee nì a-janjakitikpaandi din ŋúb́ agbampɔɔ nì ntàataajimuee.

english_verse: as well as from Gomer and Beth-Togarmah in the north. Your army is enormous!
translation_verse: Goomeer tiŋki janjakitiŋ kɔkɔ nì Beeti-Toogarima tiŋki kin bí ŋgan púee janjakitiŋ kɔkɔ nì atimbun tikpil mun làá táá-si kí búntí.

english_verse: because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land.
translation_verse: Abin kupaau boon kpataaayee, m làá dāá tɔ̄-si á cùú jáǹ Isirayeel tiŋki. Ŋyunti gbantee, ki-nib ŋmátì ki nyáń kujaaun, ki nyáń ntimu mun poon bi nìn kóòyee ki kóoǹ ki kpáfì Isirayeel jooŋŋi ŋin kpántì adigbuŋkati an yúntèe pu dee. Bi nín nyáń atimbun ŋin kíǹee kansikinee, bi kíǹ ki bí ŋgbansɔŋfin ní.

english_verse: But you and your army will attack them like a fierce thunderstorm and surround them like a cloud.
translation_verse: Sii nì a-janjakitil nì atimbun kupaau ŋin kútì a-puee làá jáǹ-bi. Ni làá jēetí bi-pu kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee, ní ní kpátí kí bìin̄ bi-tiŋki pu kii ditagbandee.

english_verse: When that day comes, I know that you will have an evil plan
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii, ŋyunti gbanti yaa láa bāańee, ilandɔkɔ tikpil làá dāan̄ a-ni ní á bɔ́ntí kí tɔ̄ dituŋkpitil diba.

english_verse: to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks.
translation_verse: A làá lì yii a làá cùú jáǹ kitiŋ kin di kaa cáá ubɔ ń mɔ̄tì ki-puee. A làá jáǹ binib bin di bí ŋgbansɔŋfin tiba kaa páb́-bee. Binib gbanti kóò ntimu mun baa máń agun ki tú, muaa cáá mpunyɔmuɔɔ kaa cáá tikpàlkaalee.

english_verse: You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property.
translation_verse: A làá dāan̄ kí fūkul̀-bi kí kóoǹ bi-gaajawanti. Binib bin fātìi kɔ́ kitiŋ kin nìn kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋmee, a làá jáǹ-bi. Bi nyánní ntincamun ki kóoǹ ki kpáfì. Bi cáá tipicaŋkpun nì tigaajati ní ki kóò duulinya kansikin nì kansikin.

english_verse: The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
translation_verse: Binib bin kóò Sabaa nì Deedaŋyee nì Taarsiisi nyampoobi nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-nee làá bàlifì-si yii: <Mimmee kí fūkul̀ binib wanti pu ní a dɔ́mińaaa? Kí kóoǹ tigaajawan kí kpúkuńee pu ní a kóoǹ a-janjakitil ki kpáfàaa? A dɔ́miń kí fōō animbil nì sindaariya nì tipicaŋkpun nì tigaajawan kí kpúkuń níii?>

english_verse: You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy. Judgment on Gog
translation_verse: A làá dāan̄ kí jáǹ m-nibul Isirayeel yab ní kí gbá kí bìin̄ bi-tiŋki pu kii ditagbandi nín bìintí kitiŋ pu puee. Iyuntijoolkaa poon ní tíǹ làá jītí. M làá tɔ̄ sii Gɔɔgi á cù kí fōō m-tiŋki kí ŋmā kí dàkà anibul ŋin kíǹee yii man di sá Unimbɔti Circirdaan. Kun ní m làá dī a-pu kí dàkà-bee dee.

english_verse: The Lord said to Gog: Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Dooooyee, m nìn dūu dī m-tɔntɔnliibi Isirayeel bɔnaatiliibi pu ki sòon̄ a-pu. Bi dū abin kupaau ki sòon̄ yii m làá tɔ̄-si á jáǹ m-nibul.

english_verse: and in my anger I will send a terrible earthquake to shake Israel.
translation_verse: M pūtì yii m-ŋuukpaandi gbanti poonee, kitiŋ làá cìŋkì Isirayeel tiŋkin.

english_verse: Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse.
translation_verse: Ijɔm in bí tiŋkunee nì inoon in ŋàaǹ kutaa puee nì ipeel nì ikoobu in fù kitiŋee nì binib bin bí kitiŋ puee kɔkɔ làá nyɔ̀ ŋkpatim m-nimbiin. Ajoon làá wùtī ní ataŋkpee ń lítí kitiŋ ní agun ŋin bi máń ki tú ntimuee ń lítí.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other.
translation_verse: Gɔɔgi, m làá jáǹ-si m-jooŋŋi kɔkɔ pu, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ. A-janjaliibi làá kpɔ̀ tɔb.

english_verse: I will strike you with diseases and punish you with death. You and your army will be pounded with rainstorms, hailstones, and burning sulfur.
translation_verse: M làá dū bìlbil kúm weeŋŋu kí tɔ̄ a-pu ní kí yàntī á kpú kí dáaĺ a-tafal. M làá yàntī utaakpaan nì ataanyiŋkumbil nì farwata un fòol̄ lìblibee ń nì sii nì a-janjaliibi nì bin kɔkɔ kútì a-pu ni cūtì kujaauee pu.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him: You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy!
translation_verse: «Sii nisaaleen, dū m-nyɔɔbundi kí nàatī Gɔɔgi kí tùkù-u man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee yii: <Sii Gɔɔgi, Meeseeki nì Tuubaal bɔtibikpiliu, m làá jáǹ-si.

english_verse: I will turn you around and drag you from the north until you reach the mountains of Israel.
translation_verse: M làá nyāntí-si a-tiŋkin. M làá ŋá-si mpɔn á nyā a-tiŋki kin bí ŋgan púee kí jáǹ Isirayeel jooŋŋi.

english_verse: I will knock the bow out of your left hand and the arrows out of your right hand,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ḿ fáá-si ní butɔbu ń ŋmátí kí nyā a-ŋaŋgan poon kí lítí, ní ipiin ń ŋmátí kí nyā a-ŋaŋgiil poon kí lítí.

english_verse: and you and your army will die on those mountains. Then birds and wild animals will eat the flesh
translation_verse: Niinee, sii nì a-janjakitil nì a-bɔɔbi bin kútì a-puee ń kpú Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu. M làá yàntī kaajiikub nì ipeel ń ŋmɔ́ ni-nanti.

english_verse: of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: A làá lítí kitiŋ kí kpú, di sá yii man di sòon̄, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M làá sēē Maagoogi tiŋki ŋŋmi nì bin kóòń ntimu mun nnyim māntìi tú bi bí ŋgbansɔŋfinee. Niinee báà ŋma làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: My people Israel will know me, and they will no longer disgrace my holy name. Everyone on earth will know that I am the holy Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī m-nibul Isirayeel ń béé m nín bí circir puee. Maa làá ti yàntī bí kpèè m-circir yindi fám ní atimbun ŋin kíǹee ń béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan, Isirayeel circir Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: When that day comes, the people in the towns of Israel will collect the weapons of their dead enemies. They will use these shields, bows and arrows, spears, and clubs as firewood, and there will be enough to last for seven years.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab làá dāá nyā bi-timmun. Bi làá dāá kpāā ŋŋmi ní kí dū bi-nannanliibi janjawanti kí ŋá poon án wà. Agbampɔɔ, akpaan nì ŋwaamu nì itɔfi nì ipiin nì ŋkpamu nì ntàataajimu làá nīn bí ŋŋmee poon ki wù áli abin aluli.

english_verse: They will burn these weapons instead of gathering sticks or chopping down trees. That's how the Israelites will take revenge on those who robbed and abused them. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Burial of Gog The Lord said:
translation_verse: Binib kaa dāa gíti cá kusaau idɔpu àá kí cù kupɔɔun kí gāā isufi, di sá yii tijanjawan gbanti ní bi làá nīn cáa kpà ŋŋmi. Bin nìn fúkúl̀-bee, bi làá dāá fūkul̀-bi kí téeǹ. Bin nìn kóoǹ ni-wantee, ni làá dāá kóoǹ bi-wanti kí téeǹ. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.

english_verse: After Gog has been destroyed, I will bury him and his army in Israel, in Travelers' Valley, east of the Dead Sea. That graveyard will be so large that it will block the way of anyone who tries to walk through the valley, which will then be known as “The Valley of Gog's Army.”
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin gbantee, m làá dāá tīī Gɔɔgi ntaŋkpiifal ŋun poon bi làá síb́-uee Isirayeel tiŋkin. Bisanjitiliibi tantakalin, Ŋyaam mɔɔl ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní án làá nīn sá, ní ntaŋkpiifal gbanti làá pìin̄ bisanjitiliibi nsan. Niin ní bi làá síb́ Gɔɔgi nì u-janjakitil kɔkɔ. Bi làá nīn yíì mpaan gbanti yii <Gɔɔgi Nipaaku Tantakal>.

english_verse: The Israelites will spend seven months burying dead bodies and cleaning up their land.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab làá dāá dū iŋmal iluli ní kí síb́-bi, ní kí fíntí kitiŋ kí nyāntí tijɔkɔndin.

english_verse: Everyone will help with the burial, and they will be honored for this on the day the brightness of my glory is seen.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ nee nib kɔkɔ làá dāá síb́-bi, ní kí dāá nīn bí dipɔɔpindin daliŋkin m làá lēē m-nyooti kí dàkèe. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: After those seven months, the people will appoint a group of men to look for any dead bodies left unburied. This must be done for seven months to make sure that the land is no longer unclean.
translation_verse: Iŋmal iluli gbanti boonee, bi làá dāá lēē bininjab biba. Bíǹ tundi di làá nīn sá bí nīn yìiǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu, kí nyàab̀ anikpil ŋin dáá gbíntìi dɔ̄ kitiŋee kí síb́, kí ŋá kitiŋ circir.

english_verse: Whenever they find a human bone, they will set up a marker next to it. Then the gravediggers will bury it in “The Valley of Gog's Army”
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá yìiǹ kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ pu. Bi-kansikin ubɔ yaa ká anikpabee ní ú tòò ataŋkpee kí kpúkuń ŋi-caŋin. An di làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu. Niinee ní bin gbì itaŋkpiifalee ń dāan̄ kí yòon̄ akpabee kí cáá síb́ Gɔɔgi Nipaaku Tantakalin.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to hold a feast on Israel's mountains and offer sacrifices there. So invite all the birds and wild animals to come from every direction and eat the meat of sacrifices and drink the blood. The birds and animals
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti gíti bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, tùkù inoon kɔkɔ nì i-buluku nì ipeel kɔkɔ yii í nyānní an kɔkɔ pu kí dāá kpāfì kí jī saraa un m làá ŋá kí tīī-bee jinti. Án làá nīn sá saraakpaan ní m làá ŋá Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu. Ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ tinan kí nyɔ̀ fatiku.

english_verse: will feast on the bodies of warriors and foreign rulers that I will sacrifice like sheep, goats, and bulls.
translation_verse: Ni làá ŋmɔ́ bibaatandambi nanti kí nyɔ̀ abɔtibil fatikuu, bibaatandambi nì abɔtibil ŋin bi dūu ŋá saraa ipijaa nì apibil nì iŋɔjaa nì Baasan nabiliŋ ŋin cáá ŋkpamee yil puee.

english_verse: I want the birds and animals to eat until they are full and drink until they are drunk.
translation_verse: Saraa gbanti pu ní m yíì-ni, ni làá ŋmɔ́ ŋkpam kí díkí ní kí nyɔ̀ fatiku kí gbí.

english_verse: They will come to my table and stuff themselves with the flesh of horses and warriors of every kind. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Israel Will Be Restored The Lord said:
translation_verse: Jiŋaakpaan gbanti poonee, ni làá ŋmɔ́ itaamu nì bitanjakaliibi nì bijanjaliibi nì bijanjaliibi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ nì bi-bulifi kii ni nín là puee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: When I punish the nations of the earth, they will see the brightness of my glory.
translation_verse: «M làá dàkà atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib m-nyooti. Bi-kɔkɔ làá ká m nín cáá m-pɔŋŋu ki tūǹ ditundi ki sòoǹ binib bɔti puee.

english_verse: The people of Israel will know from then on that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbantee, Isirayeel yab làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan, bi-Nimbɔtiu.» Bi nín kúlifì Eeseekiyeel bɔti puee

english_verse: Foreign nations will realize that the Israelites were forced to leave their own land because they sinned against me. I turned my back on my people and let enemies attack and kill them.
translation_verse: «Atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib làá béé yii bi cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu bi-yìntitam pu ní, di sá yii baa yúl̀ man bi-Dindaan deedee. An pu ní m fātì m-boon ki tīī-bi. M dū-bi ki ŋá bi-nannanliibi ŋaan ní ki yāntì bi kūū-bi kujaaun.

english_verse: Their lives were wicked and corrupt, and they deserved to be punished.
translation_verse: M nín fātì m-boon ki tīī-bee, m dàkā-bi bi-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi nì bi-yìntitam nín máaǹ kuŋyee ní.

english_verse: Now I will show mercy to the people of Israel and bring them back from the nations where they are living. They are Jacob's descendants, so I will bless them and show that I am holy.
translation_verse: «Ama man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kɔŋkɔnnee, m làá sɔ̄ Isirayeel yab, Jaakɔb naantiibi saai. M làá nyāntí-bi kuyuŋun kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi ní kí yàntī bi-kɔkɔ ń nīn kíǹ ki tɔ́ m-circir yindi kii an nín máaǹ puee.

english_verse: They will live safely in their own land, but will be ashamed when they remember their evil ways and how they disgraced me.
translation_verse: Niinee bi làá súntí bi-cooi nì bi nín yīntiǹ-mi puee. Bi làá kàl̄ bi-tiŋkin ŋgbansɔŋfi ní ubɔ kaa làá ti fàaǹ-bi.

english_verse: Foreign nations will watch as I take the Israelites from enemy lands and bring them back home, and those nations will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: M làá nyāntí-bi bi-nannanliibi tiŋkin ní kí kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì ní kí gíiǹní-bi bi-dumpu. M làá dī bi-pu ní kí dàkà atimbun tikpil yii man di sá Unimbɔti circirdaan.

english_verse: My people will realize that I, the Lord their God, sent them away as prisoners and now will bring them back to their own land.
translation_verse: M yaa láa kóoǹ Isirayeel yab ki kpáfì bi-tiŋkin kaa yāntì ubɔbɔ gbíntì kinicantiŋin kuyuŋunee, bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Never again will I turn my back on the people of Israel, and my Spirit will live in them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Maa làá ti fàtī m-boon kí tīī Isirayeel yab, kun puee m làá tīī-bi m-Fam. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_verse: Twenty-five years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, and
translation_verse: Dileedakal diba poonee ní Unimbɔti yōoǹ-mi ki cáa cūnnì Isirayeel tiŋkin. U nìn dū-mi ki tɔ́kɔ́ǹ dijoofɔŋfɔkɔl diba yilpu kúntí kunti. Dijoolee jandi ŋgiil púee, adiin aba bí ki náań nì kitiŋ kiba.

english_verse: He measured the entrance room at the far end of the passageway, and it was ten meters wide.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋmāntì kudii kun ní bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu. Kunimbɔtidii cindi nìn māntìi tú-ku an kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: In my vision the Lord took me closer, and I saw a man who was sparkling like polished bronze. He was standing near one of the gates and was holding a tape measure in one hand and a measuring stick in the other.
translation_verse: U cáá-mi ki cūnnì niinee ní m ká uninja ubɔ. Uninjee nìn náań nì tasa kúti ní ki yú ki kɔ́ĺ kipunyɔkɔ kiba. U nìn ŋúb́ u-ŋaan ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee ŋmiiŋu nì kukaluu kun bi cáa ŋmàntēe.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay close attention to everything I'm going to show you—that's why you've been brought here. Listen carefully, because you must tell the people of Israel what you see.” The East Gate
translation_verse: U bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kpítí a-nimbiliŋ kí ŋátí a-tafaliŋ. Á kpèè tin kɔkɔ m làá dàkà-si nee tiŋan, di sá yii an sá á kpèè-tèe pu ní bi cáań-si doo. Míǹ boonee, a làá dū tin kɔkɔ a ká dooyee kí māafì Isirayeel yab ní.» Mmɔŋki cindi nì di-punyɔmmu

english_verse: at the end of the passageway. The man measured this room: It was four meters from the doorway to the opposite wall, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one meter.
translation_verse: Ku-nyooŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu minii pu, ní ku-jaantalkub nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mili pu. Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ gbantee nìn bí poon pú ní.

english_verse: The three guardrooms on each side of the passageway were the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same thickness.
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi ŋin nìn bí kunimbɔtidii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee nìn ŋmà ní. Adiin ata nìn bí nsanjaati ŋgan pú, ní ata mun bí ŋgiil pú. Agun ŋin nìn pītì ŋi-kansikinee kɔkɔ gbifiŋŋu nìn ŋmà ní.

english_verse: Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔee punuu nín pìitī puee waaŋŋu ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu saalaa pu. Nsanjaatee waaŋŋu nìn nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu saalaa nì mita pu.

english_verse: The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì kí yòon̄ kudii kubɔ poon gundi kí cáá sāā kun bíitiǹ-kuee poon gundi ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu.

english_verse: Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was
translation_verse: Kipunyɔkɔ kin bi dì kí kɔ́ kì bí boon pú gundi pu nì poon pú cindi punyɔkɔki kansikinee nìn nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa.

english_verse: The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. The Outer Courtyard
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpáá tilaandi ki nákáǹ tɔkɔlab ki māntìi tú bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi nì ŋi-jaantalkub nì kipunyɔkɔ poon pú nì agun ŋin pītì adiinee. Tɔkɔlab bin bi kpáá tilaandi ki nákáǹee mun nìn bí kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee guŋŋi pu. Bi nìn lēē ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì agun gbanti pu.

english_verse: The man then led me through the passageway and into the outer courtyard of the temple, where I saw
translation_verse: Uninjee cáá-mi ki cūnnì kunimbɔtidii boon cindi. Bi nìn bɔ̀b̄ dicindi gbanti yilpu ní ki máń adiin mmuŋku nì saalaa ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was
translation_verse: Adiin nìn māntìi tú kipunyɔkɔ gbanti. Kudii kubɔ púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu, ní ki-waaŋŋu sá kukaluuee miŋmoo pu.

english_verse: This was known as the lower sidewalk, and it was
translation_verse: Bi nìn ŋàl̄ ki māntìi tú mpunyɔmu kɔkɔ. Adiinee nìn gíti bí taapu ki jítiǹ poon pú cindi.

english_verse: I saw the gates that led to the inner courtyard of the temple and noticed that they were higher than those leading to the outer courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gates, and it was
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì digundi din bi máń ki tú kunimbɔtidii boon cindi kipunyɔkɔ bí bi dì ki kóò kunimbɔtidiinee nì digundi din bi máń ki tú kunimbɔtidii poon cindee ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú dee. Ŋgan púee,

english_verse: Next, the man measured the north gate that led to the outer courtyard.
translation_verse: u ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgan pú bi dì ki kóò kunimbɔtidii boon cindinee.

english_verse: This gate also had three guardrooms on each side of a passageway. The measurements of these rooms, the walls between them, and the entrance room at the far end of the passageway were exactly the same as those of the east gate. The north gate was also
translation_verse: A yaa dī kipunyɔkɔ ki kóò kunimbɔtidiinee, bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi ata bí ŋgan pú ní ata bí ŋgiil pú. Agun nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee púuŋŋu pú nì ku-waaŋŋu ŋwiin nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔkee púuŋŋu pú nì ki-waaŋŋu ŋmà ní. Ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki púuŋŋu pú nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu ní ki-waaŋŋu sá mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu.

english_verse: and the windows, the entrance room, and the carvings of palm trees were just like those in the east gate. The entrance room also faced the courtyard of the temple and had seven steps leading up to it.
translation_verse: Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nì tɔkɔlab nì ibafi in bi nìn dūu nyɔ̄kɔntèe nì kipunyɔkɔ kin béeyee nìn ŋmà mpúun pú nì ŋwaan pu ní. Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl aluli pu ní kí nín bà ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki, ní nyɔkɔpuee, kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poonee bí.

english_verse: Directly across the outer courtyard was a gate that led to the inner courtyard, just as there was for the east gate. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was
translation_verse: Ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee, kipunyɔkɔ kiba gíti bí. Kíǹ ní bi dì kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. An pée bí kii ŋgan pú nín bí puee ní. Uninjee ŋmāntì mpunyɔmu mulee kansikin ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu.

english_verse: The man then took me to the south gate. He measured the walls and the entrance room of this gate, and the measurements were exactly the same as those of the other two gates.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u cáá-mi ki cūnnì ŋgiil pú ní m ká kipunyɔkɔ kiba mun niin. U nìn ŋmāntì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi nì agun nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee ní ki ká yii an nì mpunyɔmu mun kíǹee ŋmà mpúun pú nì ŋwaan pu.

english_verse: Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl aluli pu ní kí nín bà ŋgiil pú punyɔkɔki, ní nyɔkɔpuee, kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poonee bí. Bi nìn dū ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì poon pú guŋŋi gbanti ŋgan nì ŋgiil kɔkɔ pú.

english_verse: And directly across the outer courtyard was a gate on the south side of the inner courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was also
translation_verse: Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti nyɔkɔpuee, kiba mun nìn gíti bí. Kíǹ ní bi nìn dì kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì mpunyɔmu gbanti kansikin ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. Kunimbɔtidii poon cindi nì ki-punyɔmmu

english_verse: We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki ní ti kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. U nìn ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔ gbanti ní ki ká yii kì nì mpunyɔmu mun bí boon pú gundi puee ŋmà.

english_verse: The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti diiku kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nìn bíitiǹ kunimbɔtidii boon cindi ní. Bi nìn lēē ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì ki-jaantalkub. Bi nìn tà akɔl anii pu ní kí kɔ́ ku-ni.

english_verse: Next, we went through the east gate to the inner courtyard. The man measured this gate, and it was the same size as the others.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔki ki kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. U nìn ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔ gbanti ní ki ká yii ki nì mun kíǹee ŋmà.

english_verse: The guardrooms, the walls separating them, and its entrance room had the same measurements as the other gates. The guardrooms and the entrance room had windows, and the gate was
translation_verse: Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi nì agun ŋin pītèe nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee nì mpunyɔmu mun kíǹee púuŋŋu nì ŋwaan nìn pée ŋmà ní. Tɔkɔlab nìn bí ki māntìi tú kipunyɔkɔee nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee. Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti kɔkɔ fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu, ní ki-waaŋŋu sá kukaluee mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu.

english_verse: The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti diiku kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nìn bíitiǹ kunimbɔtidii boon cindi ní. Bi nìn lēē ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì ki-jaantalkub. Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl anii pu ní kí kɔ́.

english_verse: Then the man took me to the north gate. He measured it, and it was the same size as the others,
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki ní ki ŋmāntì-kì. Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti nì mun kíǹee ŋmà ní.

english_verse: and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate. The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
translation_verse: Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti diiku kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nìn bíitiǹ kunimbɔtidii boon cindi ní. Bi nìn lēē ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì ki-jaantalkub. Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl anii pu ní kí kɔ́.

english_verse: Inside the entrance room of the north gate, I saw four tables, two on each side of the room, where the animals to be sacrificed were killed. Just outside this room was a small building used for washing the animals before they were offered as sacrifices to please the Lord or sacrifices for sin or sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti diiku kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee poonee, teebilib bili nìn sí dijandi diba pú ní bili mun sí dijandi din kíǹee. Teebilib gbanti pu ní bi nìn làntī bisaraawɔkaabi nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam nì dibɔkpil saraabi waŋkuti.

english_verse: Four more tables were in the outer courtyard, two on each side of the steps leading into the entrance room.
translation_verse: Kudii gbanti boonee, teebilib binaa nìn bí. A yaa jɔ́ḿ ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki watil púee, bili bí ŋgan pú ní bili bí ŋgiil pú.

english_verse: So there was a total of eight tables, four inside and four outside, where the animals were killed,
translation_verse: Teebilib nìn kpáfì binii ní bi làntī saraabi waŋkuti bi-pu, binaa bí kipunyɔkɔee dijandi diba pú ní binaa mun bí dijandi din kíǹee pú.

english_verse: and where the meat was placed until it was sacrificed on the altar. Next to the tables in the entrance room were four stone tables
translation_verse: Bi nìn cátì inyinsan ki māntìi tú teebilibee, ní inyinsanee waaŋŋu nìn sá kii kuŋaŋfaau waaŋŋuee. Teebilib gbanti pu ní bi nìn cáá saraabi nanti ki pāantí.

english_verse: The man then took me to the inner courtyard, where I saw two buildings, one beside the inner gate on the north and the other beside the inner gate on the south.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. Niin ní bilaŋgaaliibi diiŋŋi nìn bí. Kubɔ nìn bí ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki caŋin ní bi pìitī-ku ŋgiil watil pú, ní kun kíǹee bí ŋgiil watil pú punyɔkɔki caŋin ní bi pìitī-ku ŋgan pú.

english_verse: He said, “The building beside the north gate belongs to the priests who serve in the temple,
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn bí-mi yii: «Kudii kun nimbiin túĺ ŋgiil pú nee, bisaraaŋaliibi bin tūǹ ditundi kunimbɔtidiinee diiku dee.

english_verse: and the building beside the south gate belongs to those who serve at the altar. All of them are descendants of Zadok and are the only Levites allowed to serve as the Lord's priests.” The Inner Courtyard and the Temple
translation_verse: Kudii kun nimbiin túĺ ŋgan pú nee, bisaraaŋaliibi bin tūǹ ditundi nsaraafan puee diiku dee. Leefii naakookun yab kansikinee, Sadooki naantiibi baba di ŋūǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄ ti-Dindaan kí tɔ̄ ditundi kí tīī-u.» Kunimbɔtidii nín bí puee

english_verse: We walked to the porch of the temple, and the man measured the doorway of the porch: It was seven meters long, two and a half meters wide, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one and a half meters.
translation_verse: U nìn cáá-mi kí kɔ́ǹ kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee. U nìn ŋmāntì ki-jaantalkub ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miŋmoo pu dijandi kamaa pú, ní kipunyɔkɔ ki-ba waaŋŋu sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba kpá saalku pu. Agun ŋin bi nìn máń ki pūntèe gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mita pu.

english_verse: The porch itself was ten meters by six meters, with steps leading up to it. There was a column on each side of these steps.
translation_verse: Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu, ní ku-waaŋŋu sá saalaa nì mili pu. Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl saalaa pu ní kí kɔ́ ku-poon. Kipunyɔkɔee janliitiliŋ puee, jaantalkub nìn bí ní.

english_verse: Next we went into the main room of the temple. The man measured the doorway of this room: It was
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋkun ní ki ŋmāntì-ku. Bi nìn máń agun ali ní agunee kansikinee, nsan ŋun bi dì ki kóò kudikpaaŋŋu gbantinee nìn bí. Digundi kamaa gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluu pu.

english_verse: and the nearest buildings ten meters away.
translation_verse: nì adiin ŋin kíǹee kansikin nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu ki māntìi tú.

english_verse: Then the man walked to the far end of the temple's main room and said, “Beyond this doorway is the most holy place.” He first measured the doorway: It was one meter wide,
translation_verse: U nìn ŋmāntì kudii ku-ba ní ki ká mpúun pú kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu, ní ki ká ŋwaan pú mmuŋku pu. Niinee ní u tùkū-mi yii niin di sá <Circir páaa laŋki>. Ndibiyaamu mun kútì kunimbɔtidii puee

english_verse: The walls of the temple were thicker at the bottom than at the top, which meant that the storage rooms on the top level were wider than those on the bottom level. Steps led from the bottom level, through the middle level, and into the top level.
translation_verse: Dicindi kamaa puee, bi nìn bàtī digundi gbifiŋŋu pu, ní ndibiyaamu wàantí ki cá, míǹ ní an nìn bí ki māntì kunimbɔtidii ki tú. An puee, yilpu dibiyaamu nìn wāā ki jítiǹ taapu yamu. A yaa nìn kíĺ taapuee, a nìn jɔ́ḿ adiin ŋin tɔ́kɔ́ taapu yaŋ puee ní kí nín bà ŋin mun gíti tɔ́kɔ́ kansikin yaŋ puee.

english_verse: The temple rested on a stone base three meters high, which also served as the foundation for the storage rooms.
translation_verse: M nìn gíti ká yii ndibiyaamu mun bi nìn máń ki tú kunimbɔtidiiyee nìn lībitì adiin ŋin kíǹee kɔkɔ. Mu nìn lībitì-ŋi kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluu pu ní.

english_verse: The outside walls of the storage rooms were two and a half meters thick; there was nothing between these walls
translation_verse: Ndibiyaamu gundi din bí boonee gbifiŋŋu sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miŋmoo pu. Adiin ŋin bi nìn máń ki nákáǹ kunimbɔtidii boon gundi

english_verse: One door led into the storage rooms on the north side of the temple, and another door led to those on the south side. The stone base extended two and a half meters beyond the outside wall of the storage rooms. The West Building and the Measurements of the Temple
translation_verse: Ndibiyaamuee punyɔmmu muli nìn túĺ mpaan ŋun bí fám gbanti watil pú. Kipunyɔkɔ kiba nìn bí ŋgan pú ní kiba mun bí ŋgiil pú. Digundi din bi nìn máń ki tú mpaan gbantee gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluu pu.

english_verse: The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also
translation_verse: Kunimbɔtidii jandi din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee nì mpaan ŋun dɔ̄ fámee waaŋŋu nìn nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu.

english_verse: Finally, the man measured the length of the west building, including the side rooms on each end, and it was also
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn tí ŋmāntì kudii kun bí kunimbɔtidii boonee. Kudiiyee nì isan in bí ku-jaŋŋi liitil puee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. Kunimbɔtidii poon Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poonee nì kudikpaaŋŋuee nì kudii kun bí poonee

english_verse: were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood.
translation_verse: nì kipunyɔkɔ nì tɔkɔlab bin bi dū tilaandi ki kpáá ki nákáǹee nì isan in bí ki māntìi tú aditɔntɔkɔee, bi nìn dū ndɔpampamu ní ki bīiǹ ki māntìi tú kí yòon̄ kitiŋ kí cáá sāā tɔkɔlab. Bi nìn dū ndɔpampamu ní ki bīiǹ tɔkɔlab bi-ba.

english_verse: The paneling stopped just above the doorway. These walls were decorated
translation_verse: Kunimbɔtidii boon nì ku-poon, kí yòon̄ kipunyɔkɔ kí cáá sāā poon poon diikuee, bi nìn bɔ́ntì mpaan ŋubɔ

english_verse: The doorframe to the temple's main room was in the shape of a rectangle. The Wooden Altar In front of the doorway to the most holy place was something that looked like
translation_verse: Idɔ in pu kudikpaaŋŋu punuu nìn sàkēe jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní. <Circir páaa laŋki> nyɔkɔpuee, tiba nìn bí niin ki náań nì

english_verse: Both the doorway to the main room of the temple and the doorway to the most holy place had two doors,
translation_verse: Kunimbɔtidii nì circir laŋki nìn cáá mpunyɔmu muli ní. Bi dì kiba pu ní kí kɔ́ kudikpaaŋŋun ní kí dī kin kíǹee pu kí kɔ́ circir páaa laŋki.

english_verse: and each door had two sections that could fold open.
translation_verse: Mpunyɔmu gbanti nìn cáá punuubi bili bili ní.

english_verse: The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpítì keerubimbi nì ibafi ki nákáǹ kudikpaaŋŋu punuubi pu, kii bi nín ŋá agun pu puee ní.

english_verse: The walls on each side of this porch had small windows and were also decorated with carvings of palm trees.
translation_verse: Kipunyɔkɔ pu guŋŋi puee, tɔkɔlab bin pu bi kpáá tilaandi ki nákáǹee nìn bí, ní bi kpítì ibafi ki nákáǹ nákáǹ.

english_verse: After the man and I left the temple and walked back to the outer courtyard, he showed me a set of rooms on the north side of the west building. This set of rooms was
translation_verse: Adiin ŋin nìn bí niin gbantee kɔkɔ púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu ní ŋi-waaŋŋu sá imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu.

english_verse: and at the east end of this wall was the door leading from the courtyard to these rooms. There was also a set of rooms on the south side of the west building.
translation_verse: Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti nìn bí laakin dicindi gundi kífée ní. Ŋgiil púee, adiin aba nìn bí ki túĺ dicindi nì kudii kun bí kunimbɔtidii boonee.

english_verse: with doors that opened toward the north, and in front of them was a walkway five meters wide and
translation_verse: Adiinee nyɔkɔpu, poon cindi watil púee, nsan ŋubɔ nìn dɔ̄ ŋwaan sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu saalaa pu, ní mpúun sá dilaataal pu. Bi nìn dì ŋgan pú ní kí kɔ́ kudii gbantin.

english_verse: The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level.
translation_verse: Adiin ŋin nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee kaa nìn wāā ki bàn̄ ŋin bí taapuee, di sá yii isan nìn fōō mpaan yilpu diiŋŋi pu ki jítiǹ kansikin nì taapu yaŋ pu.

english_verse: The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Adiin gbanti nìn tɔ́kɔ́ tɔb pu mita pu ní kaa nìn cáá jaantalkub kii kunimbɔtidii cindin diiŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nín cáá puee. An pu ní adiin ŋin nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee nìn sá ŋwaamu ki jítiǹ ŋin bí taapuee nì ŋin bí kansikinee.

english_verse: These rooms were exactly like those on the north side, and they also had a walkway in front of them.
translation_verse: Adiin gbanti nyɔkɔpuee, nsan ŋubɔ nìn bí. Adiin gbanti púuŋŋu nì ŋi-waaŋŋu nì ŋin bí ŋgan púee yaŋ nìn ŋmà ní. Ŋi-punyɔmmu nì bi nín máń-ŋi puee nì bi-punuubi sá tiwambaantiil ní.

english_verse: The man then said to me: These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn bí-mi yii: «Adiin ŋin bí ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú ki túĺ dicindee, bi dū-ŋi ki sú Unimbɔti ní. Niin ní bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ circir páaa laŋkee nìn jīǹ saraabi bin bí circir páaayee jinti. Niin ní bi máaǹ kí dū tiwan tin bí circir páaayee nì saraabi nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabi nì dibɔkpil saraabi kí bíĺ, di sá yii mpaan gbanti bí circir ní.

english_verse: When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people. The Size of the Temple Area
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi bin yaa kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee kaa ŋūǹ kí nyānní boon pú cindin dicilpu. Bi máaǹ kí dū bi-circir wampeeŋkaati tin bi pēeǹ ki túń ti-Dindaan tundee kí bíĺ adiin gbantin, ní kí dū abɔkuti aba kí pèen̄ ní kí nín nyā laakin samaa kpáfèe.» Boon pú gundi ŋmàntitam

english_verse: After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area.
translation_verse: Uninjee nín ŋmāntì adiin ŋin bí kunimbɔtidiinee ki dóòyee ní u dū-mi ki dī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki punyɔkɔ pú ki nyántì. Niinee ní u kíĺ ki bíi ŋmàntī mpaan ŋun māntìi tú kunimbɔtidiiyee.

english_verse: He used his measuring stick to measure the east side of this wall; it was
translation_verse: U nìn dū kukaluu kun u cáa ŋmàntēe ki ŋmāntì ní ki ká yii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, mpúun sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu alaataa aŋmoo pu.

english_verse: Then he measured the north side, the south side, and the west side of the wall, and they were each
translation_verse: Ní u fātì u-ba ki túĺ ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ki dū kukaluuee ki ŋmāntì ŋgan pú jandi ní ki ká alaataa aŋmoo pu.

english_verse: and so the temple area was a perfect square. The wall around this area separated what was sacred from what was ordinary.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní u nìn ŋmāntì digundi din māntìi tú kunimbɔtidiiyee jannaatiliŋ. Digundee jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní ki nìn pītì mpaan ŋun bí circiree nì ŋfantanti kansikin.

english_verse: The man took me back to the east gate of the temple,
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn cáá-mi ki cūnnì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú.

english_verse: meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side. The Dedication of the Altar
translation_verse: Niinee ní m ká Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nyooti nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki dòoń. Tinyoolee nín nìn ŋáań kuwoou kuŋyee nìn náań nì tiŋku wookuee ní, ní ki nìn cáá tì-walifiŋu ki ŋmíntí kitiŋ.

english_verse: This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River. I immediately bowed with my face to the ground,
translation_verse: Dileedakal nee náań nì din m bàà ká ŋyunti ŋun ní Unimbɔti dɔ́miń kí nàan̄ Jeerusaleem nì ŋyunti ŋun m bí Keebaar buŋgbandee ní. Niinee ní m tātìi gbāaǹ m-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ.

english_verse: and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nyootee nìn dīń ŋwìiń nyalaŋki punyɔkɔki ki kɔ́nní kunimbɔtidiin.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti Fam yōoǹ-mi ní ki cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ poon cindin. M nìn ká yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí kunimbɔtidii poon.

english_verse: But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, Isirayeel yab làá gbèen̄ kí taa ti nín̄ bí tijɔkɔndin. Bi làá yòon̄ bi-bɔtiibi bin kpíìyee wunti kí wàatī-mi, ní ḿ nīn kíǹ ki kóò bi-kansikin kí nīn cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it,
translation_verse: «Sii nisaaleen, tùkù Isirayeel yab kunimbɔtidii nee nín bí puee. Icoo ń cúú-bi bi-tuŋkpitiŋ pu, ní bí bīfì kí béé bi nín lēē kudii nee ku bí puee tiŋan.

english_verse: then if they are truly sorry, describe for them the design and shape of the temple, the gates, the measurements, and how the buildings are arranged. Explain the regulations about worshiping there, then write down these things, so they can study and obey them.
translation_verse: Atuun ŋin bi ŋée yaa lafun kɔ́ǹ-bi icooyee, á dū kunimbɔtidii nee footau kí dàkà-bi nì adiin nín bí puee nì mpunyɔmu nì bi nín bɔ́ntì-ku pu ki dāa máń-kuee. Á ŋmà marab nì akoobil ŋin bi máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́ bi yaa bí mpaan nee puee kí dūú bíĺ bi-nimbiin. A yaa ŋá mimmee, bi làá nīn ŋúb́-bi kí nīn tɔ́-bi.

english_verse: The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple. The Altar
translation_verse: Kunimbɔtidii nee bɔkpaal dipeekaal sɔ̀. Mpaan ŋun kɔkɔ māntìi tú-ku dijool yilpuee sá ki tīī Unimbɔti ní.» Nsaraafan nì saraabi

english_verse: Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Iwiin iluli in làá páannée, á dū uŋɔja kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ŋwiin kamaa, ní kí dū unaja nì upìja in laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá míǹ mbaantiim.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do:
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Bi yaa láa máń nsaraafan kí nīn ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi, kí nīn yàantí saraabi waŋkuti fatikuuee, akoobil ŋin bi làá dāá ŋée sɔ̀.

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Á dū unaja kí tīī Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá Sadooki maaliŋunee bí sútí kí pìl̄-mi kí tɔ̄ ditundi kí tīī-mi. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. Bí dāá dū unajee kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau.

english_verse: Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: Á dāá yòon̄ u-fatikuu kí dūú ŋmìtī nsaraafan yiŋyi naatil nì ŋu-nyeel gbiŋŋi anaatil nì ŋu-nyɔɔgbandi kí màntīí tū. A yaa ŋá mimmee, a ŋá nsaraafanee circir ki dū-ŋu ki sú-mi dee.

english_verse: Then take the body of the bull outside the temple area and burn it at the special place.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, á yòon̄ unaja un bi dūu ŋá saraayee kí cáá wà ŋŋmi mpaan ŋun bi bɔ́ntì kí nīn ŋáań mimmee, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kpaanceetiŋu.

english_verse: The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
translation_verse: Kutaa yaa wúntèe, á yòon̄ uŋɔja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau kí ŋá nsaraafan circir, kii a nín bàà dū unaja ki ŋá puee.

english_verse: Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them,
translation_verse: A yaa dóò saraa gbantee ní á yòon̄ unaja nì upìja in laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee

english_verse: and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: kí cáań man a-Dindaan nimbiin. Bisaraaŋaliibi làá dū ŋyaam kí yàaǹ i-pu ní kí dū-bi kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī-mi.

english_verse: The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use.
translation_verse: Iwiin iluli ní ni làá ŋá nsaraafan circir kí dū-ŋu kí sú-mi ní bí nín kíĺ ŋu-pu ditundi.

english_verse: From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Iwiin iluli gbanti yaa kúntèe, ŋwinniniiti dal nì iwiin in làá páannée, bisaraaŋaliibi ń ŋá ni-saraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi bin ni cáańee nsaraafan pu. Niinee, m làá dàkà-ni kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_verse: The Lord said: I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii: «Kipunyɔkɔ nee làá nīn pée pīī ní, baa máaǹ kí pìitī-kì. Ubɔ ń taa dī ki-poon kí jītí, di sá yii man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dī niin ní ki kɔ́nní. Ŋú nīn pée pīī.

english_verse: The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate. People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
translation_verse: Ama dibɔtibil din kā dibeelee díǹ ŋūǹ kí kàl̄ niin kí jī circir jinti m-nimbiin. Ú dāá dī kipunyɔkɔee kí jītí kuditaakaau kun bí niinee kí kɔ́ ní kí fàtīí dī niin kí nyā.» Binicambi kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin

english_verse: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki ki cūtìi nyáń kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu. M nìn ká yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí kunimbɔtidii. Niinee ní m tātìi gbāaǹ m-nimbiin tūū kitiŋ.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, ŋá ŋká. Kpítí a-nimbiliŋ kí ŋátí a-tafaliŋ. Á pīlifì marab nì akoobil ŋin m cáá kí tīī-si m-Diiku puee. Á cúú marab bin sòoǹ bi nín máaǹ kí kɔ́ circir laŋki pu kí fàtīí nyā puee tiŋan.

english_verse: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
translation_verse: «Á tùkù Isirayeel yab, pɔɔgaatib nee tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹee. Isirayeel yab, m gīī nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin ni ŋáańee.

english_verse: My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ni cáá m-jandi, ni-saraabi kpam nì bi-fatikuu ki tìì-mee, ni cáá binicambi bin kaa gíí dikpancandi kaa tɔ́-mee ki kɔ̄ntí circir laŋki. Ni ŋáań míǹ ní ki kɔ̄ntí m-Diiku tijɔkɔndi. Ni ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi gbanti ki kpītì mpèé ŋun bí man nì nimbi kansikinee.

english_verse: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
translation_verse: Nimbi ni-ba kaa túń m-tundi m-circir paaŋŋu pu, ama ní ki yāntì binicambi fōō ni-paaŋŋu ki túń.

english_verse: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ yii báà unicaan yaa kóò Isirayeel yab kansikin, ní kaa gíí dikpancandi kaa tɔ́-mee, ú taa kɔ́ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.» Marab bin sá ki tīī Leefii yabee

english_verse: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel gáatì ki cūtìi nóó awaayee, Leefii yab nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī-mi ní ki dū-mi ki fá. An puee, m làá dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-kpitii pu.

english_verse: They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers.
translation_verse: Bi làá nīn gbíntìi bí m-tundin circir kɔŋkooŋŋun kí nīn cīití m-Diiku punyɔmmu ki tūǹ atuun nín pée bí pu a-ba a-ba m-Diikunee. Bi ŋūǹ kí làntì tiwaŋkuti tin bi làá dūú ŋá bisaraawɔkaabee nì saraabi bin kíǹee. Bi làá nīn tūǹ ditundi ki tìì m-nibul.

english_verse: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun m-nibul nìn bí ki tòotī awaayee, bi nìn túń ditundi ki tīī-bi ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitin. An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá jáǹ-bi ní bi-kpitii tafadaaldi ń gítí bi-pu.

english_verse: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
translation_verse: Baa làá ti ŋmā kí sútí kí pìl̄-mi kí tɔ̄ disaraaŋal tundi, kaa làá ti sútí kí pìl̄ tiwan tin bi dūu sú-mee. Baa máaǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄ circir páaa laŋki. Min ní bi làá túń icoo tuuŋŋi nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi ŋée tafadaaldee dee.

english_verse: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
translation_verse: M làá dū kunimbɔtidii poon tundi kí ŋá bi-ŋaan ní bí nīn tūǹ atuun ŋin kɔkɔ bí ku-poon bí tɔ̄ee.» Marab bin sá ki tīī bisaraaŋaliibee

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī man ni-Dindaanee, Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá Saadooki maaliŋunee nìn túń ditundi m-circir paaŋŋu pu an nín máaǹ puee. Bíǹ baba di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ m-nimbiin kí tɔ̄ m-tundi kí dū tiwaŋkuti tin bi dūu ŋá saraabee kpam nì ti-fatikuu kí ŋá-mi saraa. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
translation_verse: Bíǹ baba di làá kɔ́ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ní kí sútí kí pìl̄ m-teebiliu un pu bi tūǹ m-tundee. Bi làá nīn ŋúb́ m-tundi koobiliŋ.

english_verse: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī bí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindinee, bi máaǹ kí dū bi-wampeeŋkaati tin bi dū iŋaabu in bí fálfal ki jàkēe kí pèen̄. Bí taa dū ipii kuti wampeeŋkaati kí pèen̄ ŋyunti ŋun bi bí kunimbɔtidiin nì ku-cindi poon ki tūǹ ditundee.

english_verse: Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work.
translation_verse: Bí dū ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee kí yíĺ ní kí dū fálfal ŋaabuŋu kí cúú kicaŋ. Kutuntuŋu puee, bí taa cúú dambala.

english_verse: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī bí nyā kí kɔ́ boon pú cindin, laakin samaa bée, bí pèetī tiwan tin bi pēeǹ ki túń ditundee. Bí dū tiwampeeŋkaal gbanti kí síiń adiin ŋin bí circir laŋkee, ní kí kpántí tiwan, kí taa nín pēē tiwan tin bí circiree kí gbēē samaa.

english_verse: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
translation_verse: «Bisaraaŋaliibi kaa máaǹ kí kòol̀ diyibaakpandi, kaa tí máaǹ kí yàntī bi-yikpiti ń wíiǹ tikpil, ama bí cā bi-yikpiti tiŋan.

english_verse: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal ubɔ kaa máaǹ kí nyɔ̀ ndaam kí kɔ́ poon cindin.

english_verse: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋal kaa máaǹ kí cáab́ ukpiipu àá unimpu un bi jìn̄ee. Ú cáab́ Isirayeel sapɔmbiki kin kaa nyí uninja ki kée kiba àá usaraaŋal ubɔ kpiipuu.

english_verse: Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean.
translation_verse: «Bisaraaŋaliibi máaǹ kí dàkà m-nibul bí béé kí gàntī tin bí circiree nì tin kaa bí circiree, tin sá tijɔkɔndee nì tin kaa sá tijɔkɔndee.

english_verse: They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Bíǹ di làá nīn sòoǹ binib bɔti ní kí sòoǹ kí nóó nì m-marab. Bí nīn jīǹ jiŋaalib kí nóó nì akoobil nì abɔkpaa ŋin m tīī-bee. Bi máaǹ kí dū m-wiŋŋuŋfikaai kí sú-mi.

english_verse: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
translation_verse: «Usaraaŋal kaa máaǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄ dinikpil kí kɔ́ǹ u-ba tijɔkɔndi. Ama an yaa sá u-baa àá u-na àá u-biyaamu kansikin kiba àá u-naal àá u-maan àá u-niisal un kaa láá mɔ́ǹee, u ŋūǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄.

english_verse: If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, ú ŋá u-ba circir ní kí cīití iwiin iluli ní kí nín kíĺ ditundi.

english_verse: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun u yaa fātìi gítì kunimbɔtidii poon cindinee, ú ŋá u-kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi làá nīn cáá diyimɔɔl kí nīn bí m-tundin. Bí taa tīī-bi tikpaatan Isirayeel tiŋkin. Man di sá bi-fakal.

english_verse: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Bi làá nīn jīǹ saraabi nì tiwaŋkuti tin bi cáa ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabee. Isirayeel tiŋkin tin kɔkɔ bi dūu sú-mee kpántì bi-wanti ní.

english_verse: The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi di tí yì tijincɔ̀fikaal kɔkɔ nì tin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab lèekī bi-gaajawanti pu ki tìì-mee. Binib yaa púĺ kpɔnɔee, bí lēē un ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ bi-kɔkɔee kí tīī-bi ní ḿ bìin̄ bi-dicaŋŋi pu.

english_verse: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_verse: Ama bisaraaŋaliibi kaa máaǹ kí ŋmɔ́ unoon àá kuwaŋkuluu kun kpíì àá upeel ubɔ cúúyee nanti.»

english_verse: So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures.
translation_verse: «Ni-saniyab ń nīn sá deedee saniyab ní ni-waŋŋmantikaati ń nīn sá deedee yab.

english_verse: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_verse: «Uŋmaluluúti poon iwiin saalku dal, bi yaa bíi jīǹ tibìń jiŋaaliuee, dibɔtibil ń pée ŋá kii u nín ŋá Dilákatil jiŋaaliu puee. Iwiin iluli in bi làá dūú jī jiŋaal gbanti kɔkɔee, ú ŋá saraabaantiibi kí ká ikpiti pɔ̄tam, nì bisaraawɔkaabi bibaantiibi nì bilee nì ŋkpam saraabi bibaantiibi.»

english_verse: kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem. Land for Israel's Ruler The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kunimbɔtidii tinjandi poonee, bí ŋmàntī dijandi diba mpúun nì ŋwaan ń nīn ŋmà. Mpúun ń nīn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo pu ní ŋwaan ń nīn sá kutukub saalaa pu. Niin ní circir kɔŋkooŋŋu, <circir páaa laŋki> làá nīn bí.

english_verse: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Nimbi abɔtibil ŋin kā Isirayeel beel puee, ni gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu! Fámaan tipɔmbɔti nì diwɔ́bil, kí nóómaan tin tèen̄ee nì tin bí deedeeyee. Ní taa ti fìkì m-nibul gaajawanti. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄!

english_verse: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
translation_verse: Ni-sambiliŋ ŋin ni cáa ŋmàntī tijimpin ni yíì eefa nì ni-wanti tin ni cáa ŋmàntī inyiŋfi bi yíì baatee ń nīn ŋmà, an dàkà yii bi yaa yākatì oomeer saalaa puee, diba pu. Ni-waŋŋmantikaati ń nīn nóó nì oomeer gbanti.

english_verse: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
translation_verse: Iwiin iluli dalee, bí fàtīí ŋá tiwambaantiil kí tīī un kaa là àá kaa nyí ki ŋá ikpitee. Bi yaa ŋá mimmee, bi làá ŋá kunimbɔtidii circir.

english_verse: Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me.
translation_verse: «Ni nín làá nīn lèekī ni-saraabi puee sɔ̀. Ni yaa cáń ni-bileeu àá ni-ɔɔjiuee, ní cúú kí yàkatī imuŋku ita pu

english_verse: They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor.
translation_verse: ní kí yàkatī ni-kpam dilaataal pu kí dū diba pu kí tīī. Ní dū ni-wanti tin bi yíì bati bi yaa yākatì oomeer saalaa pu an sá diba puee kí ŋmàntī ŋkpam. Oomeer nì kɔɔr ŋmà ní.

english_verse: The people of Israel will bring you these offerings.
translation_verse: «Bin kɔkɔ kóò Isirayeel tiŋkinee máaǹ kí cáań bi-jandi kí tīī dibɔtibil din kā Isirayeel beel puee.

english_verse: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. The Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Di sá yii dibɔtibil nín máaǹ kí tīī tiwan tin bi làá dūú ŋá bisaraawɔkaabee nì tijimpin saraabee nì ndaam min bi féeń jiŋaalib yuntiŋuee, cilinjee uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaaliu nì iwiŋŋuŋfikaa nì iyunti in kíǹ Isirayeel yab kpáfée. Dibɔtibil di làá nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam nì tijimpin saraabi nì bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi. U yaa ŋá mimmee, Isirayeel nibul làá ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam.»

english_verse: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Iwiin iluli in bi làá dūú jī jiŋaalee kamaayee, ú dū inajaa iluli nì ipijaa iluli in laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí dūú ŋá saraawɔkaa. Ŋwiin kamaayee, ú dū uŋɔja ubɔ kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau.

english_verse: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti gíti sòon̄ yii: «Uŋmapeekaa wimpeekaaŋuee, ní dū unaja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraa kí ŋá circir kɔŋkooŋŋu circir.

english_verse: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil ń yòon̄ kuwaŋkuluu kun bi dūu ŋá saraayee fatikuu kí dūú ŋmìtī idɔ in pu kunimbɔtidii punuu sàkēe pu nì nsaraafan kpiŋŋi anaatil pu nì idɔ in pu kunimbɔtidii poon cindi punuubi sàkēe.

english_verse: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dalee, ní kíĺ kí jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu. Jiŋaal gbanti làá fōō iwiin iluli, ní iwiin iluli gbanti poonee, ní taa ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee.

english_verse: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Dilákatil jiŋaaliu wimpeekaaŋuee, dibɔtibil ń dū unaja ubɔ kí ŋá saraa úǹ u-ba nì samaa kɔkɔ kpitii pɔ̄tam pu.

english_verse: He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
translation_verse: Kí kúntée, bi yaa dū unaja ubɔ nì upìja ubɔ ki ŋá saraayee, ú dū bilee kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ŋkpam liitirib biluu kí kūtì.

english_verse: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Kunimbɔtidii poon cindi punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee máaǹ kí nīn pīī iwiin iluu in binib tūǹ ditundee, ama ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal nì uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaalibee, bí pìitī-kì.

english_verse: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
translation_verse: Dibɔtibil làá nyānní kunimbɔtidii boon cindi ní kí dī kudii kun bí ki pìl̄ kipunyɔkɔee kí kɔ́. Ú yūĺ idɔ in pu punuu sàkēe poon ŋyunti ŋun ní bisaraaŋaliibi bíi ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabee. Kipunyɔkɔpu niinee, ú tàtīí gbàan̄ kí dū u-yigbeel kí tūū kitiŋ ní kí fàtīí nīn gítí. Baa máaǹ kí pìin̄ kipunyɔkɔee kí cáá sāā kujoou.

english_verse: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
translation_verse: Di sá yii iwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal nì uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaalibee, kitiŋ nee pu nib máaǹ kí dāan̄ kipunyɔkɔee caŋin kí jāam̀ man ni-Dindaan.

english_verse: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee, dibɔtibil ń dū apibil aluu nì uŋɔja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa.

english_verse: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Ú dū bilee kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa kí ŋá saraa kí kūtì upìja kamaa pu ní kí dū bilee un u yaa lèe kí ŋá saraa kí kūtì ipii pu. Ú dāá dū ŋkpam liitirib biluu kí kūtì bilee kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaayee pu.

english_verse: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaaliu wiiŋyi dalee, ú dū unaja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee nì apibil aluu ŋin laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee nì upìja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraa.

english_verse: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Unaja kamaa nì upìja kamaa puee, ú dū bilee kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa kí kūtì kí ŋá saraa nì bilee min nyɔkɔm u lèe kí kūtì apibil pu kí ŋá saraa. Ú dāá dū ŋkpam liitirib biluu kí kūtì bilee kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa kamaa pu.

english_verse: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
translation_verse: Nsan ŋun dibɔtibil yaa dī ki kɔ́ee, ú fàtīí dī nsan gbanti kí nyānní kí jītí kuditaakaau kun pìlīǹ kipunyɔkɔee.

english_verse: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
translation_verse: Ama kitiŋ nee nib yaa dòoń kí jāam̀ man ni-Dindaan jiŋaakpaambi wiiŋyi poonee, bin dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki ki kɔ́nnée ń dī ŋgiil pú punyɔkɔki kí nyā. Bin dī ŋgiil pú punyɔkɔki ki kɔ́nnée ń dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki kí nyā. Ubɔ ń taa fàtīí dī kipunyɔkɔ kin u dī ki kɔ́nnée kí nyā, ama báà ŋma ń dī kipunyɔkɔ kin bíitiǹ kin u dī ki kɔ́nnée kí nyā.

english_verse: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
translation_verse: Dibɔtibil yaa kóòyee, samaa mun ń kɔ́, u yaa nyēēyee, samaa mun ń nyā.» Saraabi bin kíǹee marab

english_verse: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: «Jiŋaalib nì iwiŋkpaan dalee, bí dū bilee kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa kí kūtì unaja àá upìja kamaa pu kí ŋá saraa, ní kí dū bilee un nyɔkɔm bi yaa lèe kí kūtì apibil pu kí ŋá saraa. Bilee kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa kamaa puee, bí dū ŋkpam liitirib biluu kí kūtì kí ŋá saraa.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: «Dibɔtibil yaa là kí ŋá nlammɔntiim saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaan ní an yaa sá saraawɔkaa àá mpèé saraauee, bí pìitī-u ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔki ú dī kí kɔ́. Ú ŋá u-saraabi kii bi nín ŋáań ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa saraabi puee. U yaa nyánnée, bí fàtīí gíiǹ kipunyɔkɔee kí pìin̄.

english_verse: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin kamaayee, bí dū dibindi diba pibil din laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Kutaafaau ní bi máaǹ kí ŋá saraa gbanti.

english_verse: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
translation_verse: Kutaafaau kamaa muee, bí dū ŋkpam liitirib bili kí búuń ŋyim kiiloobi biŋmoo kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Baabadal saraau marab gbanti làá nīn bí ní ki cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Dibɔtibil yaa lēē u-tinjandi poon dijandi ki pú u-jipɔmbi kansikin ubɔee, dijandi gbanti kpántì u-jipɔɔnee fakal dee. U-jipɔɔn gbanti biyaamu di dāa yì kí jī ditinjandi gbanti difakal. An kpántì bi-wanti, kun puee bi fōō-dì difakal ní.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: Ama dibɔtibil yaa dū u-tinjandi dijandi ki tīī u-tɔntɔnliibi kansikin ubɔee, dijandi gbanti làá nīn sá ki tīī utɔntɔnlee kí cáá sāā dibatɔl bindi, ní dibɔtibil ń fàtīí fōō u-wanti. Di sá yii dibɔtibil u-ba biyaamu di yì u-wanti kí jī difakal.

english_verse: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
translation_verse: Dibɔtibil kaa máaǹ kí fìkì binib bin pu u kā dibeelee ubɔ wanti tiba kí gbākal̀-u kí fōō u-kpaatanti. U yaa làá tīī u-jipɔmbi ubɔ difakalee, ú lēē u-tinjandi poon, án nín làá ŋá pu bí taa jà m-nibul poon ubɔ u-kpaatanti puee.» Kunimbɔtidii samɔndiiŋŋi

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní uninjee dū-mi ki dī kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgan pú punuu caŋinee ki cáá-mi ki cūnnì bisaraaŋaliibi diiŋŋi ŋin bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu caŋinee. U dàkā-mi mpaan ŋubɔ, ŋu bí poon niin ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú.

english_verse: We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u cáá-mi ki cūnnì kunimbɔtidii boon cindin ní ki dū-mi ki dī dicindee kpiŋŋi anaatil. Dikpindi kamaa puee, dicindi nìn bí.

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dū ataŋkpee ki máń digundi ki tú dicindi kamaa ní bi máń ifan digundee taapu.
