english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn bí-mi yii: «An sá asamɔndiin ŋin poon bininjab bin tūǹ ditundi kunimbɔtidiinee làá nīn tɔ̄kɔntí tiwaŋkuti tin samaa cāabìń ki ŋáań saraayee nantee ní.»

english_verse: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn cáá-mi ki cūnnì kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔpu. Niinee ní m ká nnyim tòoń ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔki taapu. Kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu nìn túĺ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní. Nnyim nìn pùub̀ kunimbɔtidii giiliŋu pú ki jītí nsaraafan giiliŋu pú.

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki ki nyáń ní ki yāntì m māntì boon pú ki tú ki cáa sāā ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú punyɔkɔki. Nnyim nìn pùub̀ kipunyɔkɔ gbanti giiliŋu pú.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: Niinee ní u bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, a kpēē tiŋanaaa?» U cáá-mi ki kākatì ŋyunti ŋubɔ poon laaba ní ki fātìi gíiǹní-mi mbunee caŋin.

english_verse: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
translation_verse: M nìn dáań ki ká yii isufi tikpil nìn yú mbunee gbaŋŋi.

english_verse: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
translation_verse: Uninjee nìn bí-mi yii: «Mbun nee pùub̀ ki cá kitiŋ nee ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní. Ŋu sìntī Jɔɔdan tantakalin ní kí tin kɔ́ Ŋyaam mɔɔlin. Ŋu yaa bàn̄ dimɔɔlinee ní ŋú pɔ̀ntī di-nyim ní mí fàtīí kpántí nnyimmɔntiim.

english_verse: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Laakin kamaa ní mbunee nyim yaa pùub̄ ki bàn̄ee, tin kamaa pée cáá kufoouee làá nīn kóò niin ní kí bùtī. Ijɔm mun làá bùtī tikpilku. Di sá yii nnyim gbanti kpántí dimɔɔl nnyim, ní ki tìì dimaŋfal laakin kamaa mì yaa pùub̄ ki bàn̄ee.

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, kí yòon̄ Eeni-Geedii bùmbiki kí cáá sāā Eeni-Eegilaayiim bùmbikee, bijɔncuuliibi làá nīn kíǹ ki bí ní. Bi làá nīn díntí bi-laanti dimɔɔgbandi ní. Bi làá ká niin ijɔm kɔkɔ nì i-bulifi kii Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu poonee ní.

english_verse: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
translation_verse: Ama tipúti nì anyimbɔbil ŋin bí dimɔɔgbandee kaa làá ŋāŋkì, ŋíǹ nyim làá nīn sá ŋyaam ŋma ní.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Dibuŋgbándi kamaa puee, isufi in lòoǹ abilee làá nyā. I-faati kpá kí yɔ́ĺ jaanjaan ní i làá nīn lòoǹ abil kaa gbèentí. I làá nīn lòoǹ uŋmal kamaa ní, di sá yii nnyim min nyēeń circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee di làá nīn sɔ̀ŋkī-i. I-biliŋ di làá kpántí tijin ní i-faati ń nīn sá nnyɔkɔ ki cāantí iween.» Ti-Dindaan síiǹ Isirayeel tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ

english_verse: The Lord God said to the people of Israel: When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
translation_verse: Ní yàkatī kitiŋ an nīn ŋmà. Di sá yii m pūtì ki pōoǹ kí dū Isirayeel tiŋki kí tīī ni-naanjab, ní kì kpántì díǹ pu nee ni-fakal.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
translation_verse: Ŋgiil púee, kitinnyɔkɔ làá kíĺ Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu ní kí nóó didandi din jītí Eeltɔn nì Leeboo-Amaati nì Seedaad timmunee.

english_verse: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní kí dūú dī Beeroota nì Siibiraayiim timmu mun bí Damaasi nì Amaati timmu kansikinee. Kí kúntée, kitinnyɔkɔee ń nóó didandi din cá Aseer-Tikɔn tiŋki kin pìlīǹ Ooran tinnyɔkɔkee.

english_verse: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
translation_verse: Kitinnyɔkɔ gbanti làá kíĺ Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu kí cáá sāā Asaar-Eenam tiŋki ní. Ŋgan púee, kitinnyɔkɔee làá cùú sāā Damaasi nì Amaati timmun ní. Ŋgan pú jandi di làá nīn bí puee dee.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, kitinnyɔkɔ làá kíĺ dijandi din bí Damaasi nì Ooran timmu kansikinee ní kí dūú dī Jɔɔdan tantakal din bí Galaadi tiŋki nì Isirayeel tiŋki kansikinee ní kí cáá sāā Tamaar tiŋki kin bí Ŋyaam mɔɔl caŋinee. Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki jandi di làá nīn bí puee dee.

english_verse: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ŋgiil púee, kitinnyɔkɔ làá kíĺ Tamaar kí cáá sāā kibùmbiki kin bí Meeriiba Kadeesi tiŋkinee, ní kí dūú kpàkaǹ Eejipiti buŋŋu kí cáá sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu. Ŋgiil jandi di làá nīn bí puee dee.

english_verse: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń jeetilaŋkee, Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu di làá nīn sá kitinnyɔkɔ kí yòon̄ ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Leeboo Aamaati tiŋki kin bí ŋgan púee. Ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki jandi di làá nīn bí puee dee.

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: «Ní yàkatī kitiŋ gbanti kí tīī Isirayeel naakɔti.

english_verse: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
translation_verse: Ní tɔ̄ kasi kí yàkatī-kì kí tīī ni-ba nì binicambi bin kóò ni-kansikin ki màl̄ mbiyaamu kitiŋ nee poonee. An nicambee kpántì kii Isirayeel yabee ní ki kíǹ ki sá m-nibul yab. Bi mun máaǹ kí fōō ditinjandi Isirayeel yab naakɔti kansikin.

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Unicaan yaa kóò kunaakoou kun poonee, niin ní bi máaǹ kí gíí kitiŋ dijandi kí tīī-u. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_verse: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
translation_verse: «Juuda naakooku jandi púuŋŋu nín bí pu kí yòon̄ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki kí cáá sāā ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, bí kíń dijandi diba, di-púuŋŋu nì kunaakoou kamaa jandi ń nīn ŋmà ní ŋwaan ń nīn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo pu. Kansikin ní bi làá mā circir kɔŋkooŋŋu.

english_verse: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Dijandi din ni làá lēē kí tīī ti-Dindaanee púuŋŋu ń nīn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo pu ní ŋwaan ń nīn sá kutukub mmuŋku pu.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
translation_verse: Ní gíí kitiŋ gbanti dijandi kí tīī bisaraaŋaliibi. Dijandi gbanti púuŋŋu kí yòon̄ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kí cáá sāā ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ń nīn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo pu, ní kí yòon̄ ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā ŋgan pú ń nīn sá kutukub saalaa pu. Kansikinee ní bí mā ti-Dindaan circir kɔŋkooŋŋu.

english_verse: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
translation_verse: Dijandi gbantee, bisaraaŋaliibi Sadooki naantiibi di yì. Bi túń ti-Dindaan tundi deedee. Isirayeel yab di nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī Unimbɔtee, bíǹ kaa nìn dū-u ki fá kii Leefii yab nín ŋá puee.

english_verse: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
translation_verse: An pu ní bi làá fōō ditinjandi din bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee poon dijandi. Bi-jandi làá nīn nákáǹ Leefii yab yal ní.

english_verse: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
translation_verse: Leefii yab jandi làá nīn bí kii bisaraaŋaliibi jandee ní. Bi-liitil jandi púuŋŋu ń nīn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo pu, ní ŋwaan ń nīn sá kutukub saalaa pu.

english_verse: South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland.
translation_verse: «Ditinjandi din bi lēē ki bíl̀ gbanti poonee, an làá kíń kijaŋ kin làá nīn cáá ŋwaan kii ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub biŋmoo pu, ní mpúun ń nīn sá kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo puee. Kijaŋ gbanti kaa sá circir tiŋki. Bi ŋūǹ kí mā adiin kí nīn kóò, ní kí nīn kpàá tiwaŋkuti kitiŋ ń nīn bí kansikin.

english_verse: The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long,
translation_verse: Kitiŋ gbanti jannaatiliŋ làá nīn ŋmà, ní dijandi diba púuŋŋu ń nīn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub binaa nì alaataa aŋmoo pu.

english_verse: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Ditinjandi din bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee púuŋŋu puee, mpaan ŋubɔ làá kíń kitiŋ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kii ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub saalaa pu, ní kí kíń ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú míǹ mbaantiim. Bí dū tijin tin bi làá cā niinee kí kpíiǹ binib bin tūǹ kitiŋee poon ditundee.

english_verse: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
translation_verse: Kitiŋee poon tɔntɔnliibi bin làá kpɔ̀ kitiŋ gbanti puee làá nyānní Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔn ní.

english_verse: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
translation_verse: Atinjan ŋin bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee jannaatiliŋ làá nīn ŋmà ní, ní dijandi diba púuŋŋu ń nīn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo pu. Bí cúú kí yàkatī minaa pu ní kí dū dijandi diba kí yóoń an kpántí kitiŋ wanti.

english_verse: The regions east and west of this square of land will belong to the ruler of Israel. His property will run east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea. In the very center of his property will be my sacred land, as well as the temple,
translation_verse: Dijandi din kíǹee, dibɔtibil di yì. U-tinjandi ń nīn bí kitiŋ kin bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee jandi púɔɔ, kí nīn bí kitiŋ mun tinjandi pú. Dí nóó atinjan ŋin kíǹee púuŋŋu kí cáá sāā kii ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub mmuŋku nì biŋmoo pu, kí yòon̄ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kí cáá sāā kitiŋ kpaanyɔkɔ, ní kí yòon̄ ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú kí cáá sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu. Kitiŋ kin bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ń nīn bí ditinjandi gbanti kansikin.

english_verse: together with the share belonging to the Levites and the city of Jerusalem. The northern border of the ruler's property will be the land that belongs to Judah, and the southern border will be the land that belongs to Benjamin. The Division of Land among Tribes in the South The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Leefii yab timmu nì kitiŋ tinjandi ń nīn bí dibɔtibil tinjandi kansikin. Dibɔtibil tiŋki ń nīn bí Juuda naakooku jandi ŋgiil pú nì Beenjameen naakooku jandi ŋgan pú kansikin.» Tinaakɔti tin bí ŋgiil púee jandi

english_verse: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Gaadi naakooku ŋgan pú kpaanyɔkɔ di làá nīn sá kitiŋ kpaanyɔkɔ. Kì làá kíĺ Tamaar tiŋki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kí cáá sāā kibùmbiki kin bí Meeriiba, Kadeesi tiŋkinee, ní kí nìkī kí kpàkaǹ Eejipiti buŋŋu kí cáá sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu.

english_verse: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kin ni làá tɔ̄ kasi kí yàkatī kí tīī Isirayeel yab naakɔti án kpántí bi-fakalee dee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.» Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu saalaa nì mulee bɔti

english_verse: and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
translation_verse: Digundi din māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee púuŋŋu kɔkɔ làá nyā ndɔŋmantikaayee kutukub saalku nì bita pu ní. «Kí yòon̄ ŋwìiń gbanti kí nīn cée, bi làá nīn kíǹ ki yíì kitiŋ gbanti yii: <Ti-Dindaan bí>».

english_verse: In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yooyakiim nín jíń dibeel Juuda tiŋki pu abin ata poonee ní Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar dɔ́miń kí já nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki ní ki māntìi tú-kì.

english_verse: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Neebukadineesaar janjaliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Yooyakiim yab ní ki yāntì bi kóoǹ kunimbɔtidii poon wanti dijandi diba. U nìn cúú binib biba ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋu ní ki dū tiwan tin u yōoǹ kunimbɔtidiinee ki síiǹ u-waadiikun, laakin bi kpáafí u-waaŋi gaajawantee.

english_verse: One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families.
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn tīī Asipeenaasi un sá u-tɔntɔnliibi kpiliuee mara yii ú lēē Isirayeel yab bin bi cúuń kuyuŋuee kansikin binaacimpɔmbi biba bin nyánní ubɔti dicaŋkun àá akpambal dicaŋkunee.

english_verse: The king said, “They must be healthy, handsome, smart, wise, educated, and fit to serve in the royal palace. Teach them how to speak and write our language
translation_verse: Binaacimpɔmbi gbanti laaba ń taa nín̄ wɔ̀b̄. Bí nīn ŋān̄, kí nīn cáá iciin, kí nīn sá bin ŋá sukul ki nyée. Mimmee bi làá ŋmā kí nīn bí dibeecindin ki tūǹ ditundi. Bí dàkà-bi Babiloon yab sooŋyi nì bi-ŋmaŋmabiti.

english_verse: and give them the same food and wine that I am served. Train them for three years, and then they can become court officials.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti nìn síiǹ yii ŋwiin kamaayee, bí nīn tìì-bi tijin nì ndaam min úǹ u-ba jīǹ ki nyùee, ní kí dàkà-bi abin ata. Abin ata gbanti boonee, bí kíĺ ditundi dibeecindin.

english_verse: Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah.
translation_verse: Juuda naakookun binaacimpɔmbi binaa nìn bí bin bi nìn lēēyee kansikin. Bíǹ di sá Daniyeel nì Ananiya nì Miikayeel nì Asariya.

english_verse: But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
translation_verse: Ubɔti tɔntɔŋkpiliu nìn fātìi pú-bi ayin. U nìn pú Daniyeel yii Baltasaar ní ki pú Ananiya yii Sadraaki ní ki pú Miisayeel yii Meesaki ní ki pú Asariya yii Abeedi Neegoo.

english_verse: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
translation_verse: Daniyeel nìn lēē u-pɔbilin yii waa làá jī tijin tin ubɔti jīǹee nì ndaam min u nyùee kí kɔ́ǹ u-ba tijɔkɔndi. An puee u nìn gbāam̀ utɔntɔŋkpil yii ú taa ŋá-u mpɔn ú jī tijin gbanti kí kɔ́ǹ u-ba tijɔkɔndi.

english_verse: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn yāntì Daniyeel ká utɔntɔŋkpilee cee diyimɔɔl nì kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.

english_verse: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
translation_verse: Ama Asipeenaasi nìn tùkū Daniyeel yii: «An sá ti-baa ubɔti di síiǹ kun ni máaǹ kí jī kí nyɔ̀ee. M fàŋkí yii ú dāá ká ni dúntì kaa bí kii ni-naacimpɔnjutiibee. Ubɔti yaa ká mimmee, see ni-puee, ú lēē m-yil.»

english_verse: The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daniyeel tùkū un ní utɔntɔŋkpil lēē ú nīn kpèé úǹ Daniyeel nì Ananiya nì Miisayeel nì Asariyayee yii:

english_verse: “For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime.
translation_verse: «M gbàam̄-si, cɔ̄ŋkì-ti iwiin saalaa ja kí kpèè. Iwiin saalaa gbanti poonee, á nīn pée tìì-ti tikuŋfaal ti ŋmóò nì nnyim ti nyù.

english_verse: When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.”
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, á dāá kpèè ti-nimbiiŋyi nì binaacimpɔmbi bin nì ubɔti jīǹ tijimbaantiilee nimbiiŋyi, ní kí dāá ŋá min kítì a-ceeyee kí dī nì a nín ká ti bí puee.»

english_verse: The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
translation_verse: Niinee kijapaayee kíí ki ŋá bi nín bālifì-u puee ki cɔ́ŋkì-bi míǹ iwiin saalaa.

english_verse: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
translation_verse: Iwiin saalaa gbanti dāa jítèe, bi-nimbiiŋyi ŋáŋkì ní bi ká tiwun ki cáá ŋgbampɔn ki jítiǹ binaacimpɔmbi bin nì ubɔti jīǹ tijimbaantiilee.

english_verse: After this, the guard let them eat vegetables instead of the rich food and wine.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee un nìn cí-bee nìn gbíntìi tìì-bi tikuŋfaal ŋma, ki yāntì tijin nì ndaam min bàà sá ú nīn tìì-bee.

english_verse: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn yāntì binaacimpɔmbi binaa gbanti kpántì bigbannyiliibi nì biciŋfitiibi. Daniyeel úǹ nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí lēē aleedaka nì tidamintiil taapu kí lì.

english_verse: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
translation_verse: Abin ata ŋin ubɔti Neebukadineesaar yóoǹee bàn̄ee, ní utɔntɔŋkpil yōoǹ binaacimpɔmbee kɔkɔ ki cūnnì ubɔti cee.

english_verse: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti sòon̄ nì bi-kɔkɔ, ama Daniyeel nì Ananiya nì Miisayeel nì Asariya nìn nyí ki jítiǹ bin kɔkɔ kíǹee. Míǹ puee bi nìn kíĺ ki bíi tūǹ ditundi dibeecindin.

english_verse: From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians.
translation_verse: Ubɔti yaa nìn pée bālifì-bi iciin nì dinyil bɔti tiŋyee, u nìn kāntí yii bi nìn jítiǹ bikpaŋkpantiibi nì bibɔɔbi bin kɔkɔ bí u-beelinee kɔkɔ saalaa pu.

english_verse: Daniel served there until the first year of King Cyrus.
translation_verse: Daniyeel nìn gbíntì dibeecindin ki dāa sāā ŋyunti ŋun ubɔti Siirusi kāl̀ Babiloon tiŋki pu dibeelee.

english_verse: During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep.
translation_verse: Neebukadineesaar nín kāl̀ dibeel dibinliliitiil poonee, ní u dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ. Kudamintiiuee bɔti nìn páb́-u tikpil áli gba waa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí gèeǹ.

english_verse: and said, “I am disturbed by a dream that I don't understand, and I want you to explain it.”
translation_verse: ní u bí-bi yii: «M dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ. Kudamintiiuee bɔti páb́-mi tikpil, ní m là yii ní tùkù-mi m nín dámintì puee.»

english_verse: They answered in Aramaic, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! We are your servants. Please tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí ubɔti Aram yab sooŋyi poon yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, Unimbɔti ń tīī-si mmaŋfafɔkɔn! Tùkù-ti a nín dámintì puee, ní timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi ń lēē ku-taapu kí tùkù-si.»

english_verse: But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti kíí-bi yii: «M nín lēē puee sɔ̀. Ni yaa kaa tùkū-mi m nín dámintì puee ki lēē taapu ki tùkū-mee, m làá yàntī bí tɔ̀ntī-ni, ní kí yàntī bí kpēelikì ni-diiŋŋi ŋí kpántí adigbuŋkati.

english_verse: However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Ama ni yaa ŋúń ki tùkū-mi m nín dámintì puee ki lēē taapu ki tùkū-mee, m làá tīī-ni tiwampɔkaal tikpil nì tinyool. An puee ní tùkù-mi m nín dámintì puee kí lēē taapu kí tùkù-mi.»

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
translation_verse: Ní bi fātìi kíí ubɔti nliliitiim yii: «Ti-baa, tùkù-ti a nín dámintì puee ní ti mun ń ŋmā kí lēē taapu kí tùkù-si.»

english_verse: because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
translation_verse: Ni yaa kaa pée tùkū-mi m nín dámintì puee, ditafadaaldi dibaantiil di dɔ̄ ki cí ni-kɔkɔ. Ni tí bíi bɔ́ntí tiba dicilpu kí dāá mɔ̄ntì-mi kí kīil̀-mi kí nīn cɔ́tí yii m-landɔkɔŋu làá kpántí dee. An puee ní tùkù-mi m nín dámintì puee. Mimmee m béè yii ni làá ŋmā kí lēē taapu mun kí tùkù-mi dee.»

english_verse: His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing.
translation_verse: Ní bi tí bí ubɔti yii: «Báà unil kpá kitiŋ pu ki làá ŋmā kí ŋá tin sii ti-baa ubɔti bālifì yii tí ŋá nee. Báà ubɔti ubɔ, u sá ukpaan ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ min min kaa láá pée bālifì bikpaŋkpantiibi nì bibɔɔbi nì bin wāĺee bí ŋá tin ní a bālifì yii tí ŋá nee.

english_verse: It can't be done, except by the gods, and they don't live here on earth.”
translation_verse: Tin ní a bàlifēe pɔ̄ɔ̄ tikpil ní ubɔ mun kpá kí ŋmā kí tùkù-si tin a bālifèe, see inimbɔti. Too i mun di kaa kóò timbi binib kansikinee.»

english_verse: This made the king so angry that he gave orders for every wise man in Babylonia to be put to death, including Daniel and his three friends. God Tells Nebuchadnezzar's Dream to Daniel
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti nyīī ŋŋal ní an gbītì an kɔkɔ yii bí kpɔ̀ binyiliibi, ní bi tú binib bí cùú nyàab̀ Daniyeel nì u-bɔɔbi mun kí kpɔ̀. Unimbɔti lēē ubɔti nín dámintì puee ki dàkā Daniyeel

english_verse: Arioch was the king's official in charge of putting the wise men to death. He was on his way to have it done, when Daniel very wisely went to him
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Ariyɔɔki un sá ubɔti janjaliibi bin cí-uee kpiliu nyáń kí bàà kíĺ Babiloon nyiliibi dikpɔ̀lee, ní Daniyeel kíntì-u nsanni ní ki dū dinyil nì iciin ki sòon̄ nì u.

english_verse: and asked, “Why did the king give such cruel orders?” After Arioch explained what had happened,
translation_verse: Daniyeel nìn bālifì-u yii: «Ba pu ní ubɔti yóoǹ ditafadaaldi di baasii pɔ̄ɔ̄ míǹ ní.» Niinee ní Ariyɔɔki nín dū tibɔti ki máafì-u.

english_verse: Daniel rushed off and said to the king, “If you will just give me some time, I'll explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Daniyeel gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki nín kóò ubɔti cee dicilpu ní ki gbāam̀-u yii ú pée pɔ̄-u ŋyunti fiii ú ŋmā kí tùkù-u u nín dámintì puee nì an taapu.

english_verse: Then he said, “Pray that the God who rules from heaven will be merciful and explain this mystery, so that we and the others won't be put to death.”
translation_verse: U nìn bí-bi yii bí nīn mèé yilpu Nimbɔtiu ú sɔ̄ bi-saai kí lēē maamaaci damintiiku gbanti kí dàkà-bi, án nín làá ŋá pu bí taa kpɔ̀ Babiloon nyiliibi kí kpáaǹ bi muee.

english_verse: In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbantee ní Unimbɔti lēē abɔɔn gbanti ki dàkā Daniyeel dileedakal poon. Niinee ní Daniyeel nyɔ́ŋkì yilpu Nimbɔtiu,

english_verse: “Our God, your name will be praised forever and forever. You are all-powerful, and you know everything.
translation_verse: ki lī yii: «Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔti baabadal kí taa gbèen̄, úǹ di yì iciin nì mpɔn.

english_verse: You control human events— you give rulers their power and take it away, and you are the source of wisdom and knowledge.
translation_verse: Iyunti nì tibɔti nín dòoń ki kpántí puee kā u-ŋaan, úǹ di kpákatí bibɔtiibi ní ki tí kàantí-bi dibeel. Úǹ di tìì biciŋfitiibi iciin, ní ki tìì binyiliibi dinyil.

english_verse: “You explain deep mysteries, because even the dark is light to you.
translation_verse: Úǹ di bìitī maamaaci bɔɔŋŋi pu. U nyí tin bál̀ dibɔmbɔndinee, ní ŋwalifi māntìi tú-u.

english_verse: You are the God who was worshiped by my ancestors. Now I thank you and praise you for making me wise and telling me the king's dream, together with its meaning.” Daniel Interprets the Dream
translation_verse: «Sii m-naanjab Nimbɔtiu, m jáaḿ-si ki nyɔ́ŋkí-si, di sá yii a tīī-mi iciin nì mpɔn, ní ki yāntì m ká kun ní ti mēē-see. A yāntì ti béè tin di páb́ ubɔtee.»

english_verse: Daniel went back to Arioch, the official in charge of executing the wise men. Daniel said, “Don't kill those men! Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning of his dream.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daniyeel yíkìi nín cá Ariyɔɔki cee. Ariyɔɔki gbanti ní ubɔti nìn tīī mara yii ú kpɔ̀ Babiloon nyiliibee. Daniyeel bàn̄ u-ceeyee ní ki bí-u yii: «Taa kpɔ̀ Babiloon nyiliibi! Cáá-mi kí cùnnì ubɔti cee, m làá tùkù-u u-damintiiku taapu.»

english_verse: Arioch rushed Daniel to the king and announced, “Your Majesty, I have found out that one of the men brought here from Judah can explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Dicilpu dicilpu niin ní Ariyɔɔki yōoǹ Daniyeel ki cáa cūnnì ubɔti cee ki bí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, Juuda yab bin ti cúuń kuyuŋuee kansikin ubɔ ŋūǹ kí tùkù-si a-damintiikuee taapu.» Dikumpool din taaŋi sá kuyɔkɔuee

english_verse: The king asked Daniel, “Can you tell me my dream and what it means?”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bālifì Daniyeel un bi gíti yíì yii Baltasaaree yii: «A lafun ŋūǹ kí tùkù-mi m nín dámintì puee nì an taapuɔɔɔ?»

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, not even the smartest person in all the world can do what you are demanding.
translation_verse: Ní Daniyeel kíí-u yii: «Ubɔti, báà unyil àá ukpaŋkpanti àá ubɔɔ àá un kpèé iŋmalbijaa kí béé tin dòońee ubɔ kpá ki làá ŋmā kí lēē maamaaci bɔti tin pu a bíi sòoǹ nee taapu kí tùkù-si.

english_verse: But the God who rules from heaven can explain mysteries. And while you were sleeping, he showed you what will happen in the future.
translation_verse: Ubɔti, ŋyunti ŋun ní a dɔ̄ a-dooŋu puee ní a kíĺ ki bíi dàkafī tin làá dāá dāan̄ fool boonee pu. Niinee ní un bìitī abɔɔn puee lēē tin dòoń fool boonee ki dàkā-si.

english_verse: However, you must realize that these mysteries weren't explained to me because I am smarter than everyone else. Instead, it was done so that you would understand what you have seen.
translation_verse: Ama mamee, bi yaa bīitì abɔɔn gbanti pu ki dàkā-mee, an kaa dàkà yii m cáá iciin ki jítiǹ binib kɔkɔ, ama an sá yii ubɔ ń ŋmā kí tùkù-si a-damintiiku taapu, ní kí yàntī á béé kun di páb́ a-pɔbilee.

english_verse: Your Majesty, what you saw standing in front of you was a huge and terrifying statue, shining brightly.
translation_verse: Ubɔti, a pée bíi kpèéyee ní ki dāa ká unil naŋku kubɔ sí a-nimbiin. Kunaŋuee nìn sá kukpaaŋŋu, ki jìl̀ pàlpal ní ki cáá tifaandi.

english_verse: Its head was made of gold, its chest and arms were silver, and from its waist down to its knees, it was bronze.
translation_verse: Kunaŋuee yil nìn sá sindaariyamɔnti, ní ku-bindi nì ku-ŋalii sá animbil kúti, ní ku-pool nì ku-tapaŋŋi sá tasa kúti,

english_verse: From there to its ankles it was iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: ní ku-taaŋi sá tikúti, ní ku-tafati dijandi sá tikúti ní dijandi din kíǹee sá kuyɔkɔu.

english_verse: As you watched, a stone was cut from a mountain—but not by human hands. The stone struck the feet, completely shattering the iron and clay.
translation_verse: A pée bíi kpèé kunaŋuee ní ditaŋkpal diba nyánní dijool pu, ubɔ mun kaa gbēē-dì, ní dì dɔ́miń ki yá kunaŋuee tafati tin jandi diba sá tikúti, din kíǹee sá kuyɔkɔuee ki nàn̄-dì dúsi dusi.

english_verse: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed and blown away without a trace, like husks of wheat at threshing time. But the stone became a tremendous mountain that covered the entire earth.
translation_verse: Dicilpu niinee ní dì nàn̄ tikúti nì kuyɔkɔu nì tasa kúti nì animbil kúti nì sindaariyee dúsi dusi ní kubuŋu yōoǹ, a lì kii dipeel pu bi nín yaa bíi càatī idi dinaapaal pu kubuŋu yòontí tifeel puee, kaa yāntì báà tiba nì tiba. Ama ditaŋkpal din yá kunaŋuee díǹ kpántì dijookpaŋkpaandi ní ki jíń mpaan kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: That was the dream, and now I'll tell you what it means.
translation_verse: «Ubɔti, kpèè a nín dámintì puee dee. Too, kɔŋkɔnnee kudamintiiuee taapu sɔ̀.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings, and God has highly honored you with power
translation_verse: Ubɔti, sii di sá bibɔtiibi kɔkɔ kansikin ukpaan. Di sá yii yilpu Nimbɔtiu tīī-si dibeel nì mpɔn nì tinyool.

english_verse: After you are gone, another kingdom will rule, but it won't be as strong. Then it will be followed by a kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole world.
translation_verse: Sii boonee, dibeel din kaa cáá mpɔn kii a-yalee làá dāá nyā. Díǹ boonee dibeetataatiil diba mun làá dāá nyā kí nīn cáá kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu mpɔn. Díǹ di sá tasa kútee.

english_verse: This fourth kingdom will be divided—it will be both strong and brittle, just as you saw that the feet and toes were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Kii ntaŋambiyaamu dijandi diba di sá tikúti, din kíǹee sá kuyɔkɔu puee, míǹ ní dibeelee dijandi diba dāa pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní din kíǹee dāa pɔ̀fì.

english_verse: This kingdom will be the result of a marriage between kingdoms, but it will crumble, just as iron and clay don't stick together.
translation_verse: A ká yii tikúti nì kuyɔkɔu ŋmālim̀ tɔbin. Bibɔtiibi làá dāá ŋá mpèé kí nīn cāab̀ tɔb biyaamu, ama mpèéyee kaa làá dāá nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄, a lì kii tikúti nì kuyɔkɔu nín kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmàlim̀ kí kɔ́ tɔbin puee.

english_verse: During the time of those kings, the God who rules from heaven will set up an eternal kingdom that will never fall. It will be like the stone that was cut from the mountain, but not by human hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. Your Majesty, in your dream the great God has told you what is going to happen, and you can trust this interpretation. Daniel Is Promoted
translation_verse: Ditaŋkpal din a ká di nyáń dijool pu di-ba pu ubɔ kaa gbēē-dì, dì dɔ́miń ki nàn̄ tikúti nì tasa kúti nì kuyɔkɔu nì animbil kúti nì sindaariya dúsi dusee taapu dee. Ubɔti, Unimbɔtikpaan di nyántì tin bí nee ki dàkā-si á béé tin dòoń fool boonee. A-damintiiku nee sá tiŋman damintiiku ní, ní a ŋūǹ kí nīn máká m nín lēē ku-taapu miŋyee pu.»

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar bowed low to the ground and worshiped Daniel. Then he gave orders for incense to be burned and a sacrifice of grain to be offered in honor of Daniel.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Neebukadineesaar tātìi gbāaǹ kitiŋ Daniyeel nimbiin ki tīī-u tinyool, ní ki tīī mara yii bí ŋá saraabi kí tūū talaalub bin sɔ́fèe kí tīī Daniyeel.

english_verse: The king said, “Now I know that your God is above all other gods and kings, because he gave you the power to explain this mystery.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bí Daniyeel yii: «Ibaamɔn, ni-Nimbɔtiu di tɔ́kɔ́ inimbɔti kɔkɔ pu ní ki sá bibɔtiibi Dindaan ní ki bìitī abɔɔn pu, an pu ní a ŋúń ki lēē abɔɔn nee taapu ki tùkū-mi.»

english_verse: The king then presented Daniel with a lot of gifts; he promoted him to governor of Babylon Province and put him in charge of the other wise men.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti kāaǹ Daniyeel mpaaŋkpaan pu ní ki pú-u tiwan tikpil. U nìn dū-u ki kāaǹ ú nīn sá ukpikpaan Babiloon tiŋki kɔkɔ pu ní kí nīn sá Babiloon ciŋfitiibi kɔkɔ kpiliu.

english_verse: At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high positions in Babylon Province, and he let Daniel stay on as a palace official.
translation_verse: Daniyeel nìn mēē ubɔti ú yàntī Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo ń kɔ́ Babiloon gɔminau poon kí nīn kpòotī kitiŋ. Daniyeel úǹ nìn bí dibeecindin ki tūǹ ditundi.

english_verse: and the king's high officials, governors, and advisors all crowded around them. The men were not burned, their hair wasn't scorched, and their clothes didn't even smell like smoke.
translation_verse: Ní ntiŋgbamu kpilib nì Kɔmandambi nì ntiŋgbamu gɔminab nì ubɔti kpambaliŋ cīī ki kpèé-bi, ní ki dáań ki ká yii ŋŋmi kaa wùn̄ bi-wuntaaa, kaa wùn̄ bi-yikpitaaa, kaa wùn̄ bi-wampeeŋkaati mun, ní baa kpáàa gbìl̀ bi-pu ŋŋminyiim nunuŋu.

english_verse: and he commanded his governors, advisors, treasurers, judges, and his other officials to come from everywhere in his kingdom to the dedication of the statue.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u tú bí cù kí yíiń ntiŋgbamu kpilib nì Kɔmandambi nì ntiŋgbamu gɔminab nì akpambal nì binimbiŋubiliibi nì bibɔsoonliibi nì bimaramɔtiliibi nì ntiŋgbamu kàliŋkpilib bin kíǹee kɔkɔ bí dāan̄ kí jī dikumpoolee jiŋaaliu.

english_verse: Then an official stood up and announced: People of every nation and race, now listen to the king's command!
translation_verse: Ní un kpòotī jiŋaal tuuŋŋee téeń mpɔn yii: «Nimbi, anibul nì atimbun nì isoon kɔkɔ nib, bi nín síiǹ-ni mara uŋyee sɔ̀:

english_verse: Trumpets, flutes, harps, and all other kinds of musical instruments will soon start playing. When you hear the music, you must bow down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
translation_verse: <Ŋyunti ŋun ni yaa pée gbìl̄ ŋyin nì diwul nì kubeeu nì saŋgu nì túmba nì dikantándi nì tibɔɔkaal tin pée kíǹee kɔkɔ puee, ní gbàan̄ kitiŋ kí jāam̀ sindaariya kumpool din ubɔti Neebukadineesaar yāntì bi máńee.

english_verse: Some Babylonians used this as a chance to accuse the Jews to King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Míǹ boon kpalaayee ní Babiloon yab biba cūtìi nyáfì Juuda yab ubɔti cee.

english_verse: They said, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Bi tùkū ubɔti Neebukadineesaar yii: «Ubɔti, Unimbɔti ń tīī-si mmaŋfafɔkɔn!

english_verse: And you said that anyone who did not bow down and worship it would be thrown into a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Ní ki gíti lī yii un yaa yíì kaa gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ dikumpoolee, bí dū udaan kí tɔ̄ kipaai ŋmiŋu ŋun poon ŋŋmi fòol̄ lìblib ki pɔ̄ɔ̄yee neeee?>

english_verse: Sir, you appointed three men to high positions in Babylon Province, but they have disobeyed you. Those Jews, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, refuse to worship your gods and the statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Too ubɔti, Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo bin sá Juuda yab a dū-bi ki kɔ́ǹ Babiloon tiŋgbaŋki gɔminau poon bí nīn kpòotēe kaa fātìi tɔ́ gba yii a síiǹ mara. Kpèè, bíǹ kaa tòotī a-waaŋaaa, kaa jáaḿ sindaariya kumpool din a yāntì bi máń ki síiǹee mun.»

english_verse: “I hear that you refuse to worship my gods and the gold statue I have set up.
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti bālifì-bi yii: «Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo, mimmee an lafun sá tiŋman yii naa tòotī m-waaŋi, kaa jáaḿ sindaariya kumpool din m yāntì bi máń ki síiǹeeee?

english_verse: Now I am going to give you one more chance. If you bow down and worship the statue when you hear the music, everything will be all right. But if you don't, you will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace. No god can save you from me.”
translation_verse: Ní bɔ́ntímaan ni-ba kɔŋkɔnnee, ŋyunti ŋun ni yaa gbìl̄ ŋyin nì diwul nì kubeeu nì saŋgu nì túmba nì dikantándi nì tibɔɔkaal tin pée kíǹee puee, ní gbàan̄ kí jāam̀ dikumpool din m máń nee. Ama ni yaa yíì kaa jáam̀-dèe, ataa pu doo ní bi làá dū-ni kí tɔ̄ kipaai kin poon ŋŋmi fòol̄ lìblib ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ nee poon. Ní m kpèé unimbɔti un di làá fōō-ni kí nyāntí m-ŋaanee?»

english_verse: But even if he doesn't, we still won't worship your gods and the gold statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Báà u yaa kaa làá fīī-ti, ubɔti, á béé yii timbi kaa làá tòotī a-waaŋaaa, kaa làá gbàan̄ kí jāam̀ sindaariya kumpool din a yāntì bi máń ki síiǹ nee mun.»

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's face twisted with anger at the three men. And he ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than usual.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Neebukadineesaar fōō Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo pu mbum ní u-nimbiin cúu kpántì. Ní u tīī mara bí mɔ̀tīí kpāā kipaayee poon ŋŋmi an píĺ ŋfunyɔm miluli pu kí jītíǹ an nìn kpààa píl̀ puee.

english_verse: Next, he commanded some of his strongest soldiers to tie up the men and throw them into the flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Ní u tīī u-janjaliibi bin cáá dikpabilee mara yii bí bóob́ Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo kí cáá tɔ̄ kipaayee poon.

english_verse: The king wanted it done at that very moment. So the soldiers tied up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and threw them into the flaming furnace with all of their clothes still on, including their turbans. The fire was so hot that flames leaped out and killed the soldiers.
translation_verse: Ama bi nín pée bóob́ Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo puee, míǹ ní bi bí ki cūtìi jéetì kipaai ŋmiŋu ŋun fòol̄ lìblibee poon. Unimbɔti fīī bibɔɔtiibi bitee ki nyántì kipaai ŋmiŋun

english_verse: Suddenly the king jumped up and shouted, “Weren't only three men tied up and thrown into the fire?” “Yes, Your Majesty,” his officers answered.
translation_verse: Niinee ní tifaandi cúú ubɔti Neebukadineesaar ní u nyīī yíkì malaa ki bālifì u-kpambaliŋ yii: «An kaa sá binib bita ní ti yāntì bi bóob́ ki dūu tɔ́ ŋŋmi poonaaa?» Ní akpambalee kíí-u yii: «An sá míǹ, ti-baa ubɔti.»

english_verse: “But I see four men walking around in the fire,” the king replied. “None of them is tied up or harmed, and the fourth one looks like a god.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti fātìi bālifì yii: «Kin ba pu ní m wāĺ binib binaa còom̄ ŋŋmi poon tiba kaa bóob́-bi? Tiweendi tiba kaa bí bi-wunti pu, ní uninanaatee náań nì Unimbɔti biki.»

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar went closer to the flaming furnace and said to the three young men, “You servants of the Most High God, come out at once!” They came out,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Neebukadineesaar sútìi pìl̄ kipaayee punyɔkɔ ní ki téeń yii: «Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo, Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu tɔntɔnliibi, nyānnímaan kí dāan̄ doo.» Niinee ní Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo nyáń ŋŋmee poon.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar said: Praise their God for sending an angel to rescue his servants! They trusted their God and refused to obey my commands. Yes, they chose to die rather than to worship or serve any god except their own.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti Neebukadineesaar téeń yii: «Bí nyɔ̄ŋkì Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo Nimbɔtiu! Úǹ di túnní u-tuuŋŋu ní ŋu dɔ́miń ki fīī u-tɔntɔnliibi bin dū bi-mákal ki páaǹ u-pu kaa fātìi tɔ́ man ubɔti marabee. Bi kíí bí kpɔ̀-bi ki jítiǹ bí gbàan̄ kí jāam̀ diwaal diba, an yaa kaa sá bi-Nimbɔtiu baba.

english_verse: And I won't allow people of any nation or race to say anything against their God. Anyone who does will be chopped up and their houses will be torn down, because no other god has such great power to save.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee m síiǹ mara yii dinibul àá ditimbundi àá isoon in kamaa niliu di yaa sòon̄ ki bíil̀ Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo Nimbɔtiuee, m làá yàntī bí tɔ̀ntī udaan, ní kí kúntí u-dicaŋku kú kpántí adigbuŋkati. Di sá yii unimbɔti ubɔ gíti kpá ki ŋūǹ kí tīī difiil din bí nee juti.»

english_verse: After this happened, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in Babylon Province.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti mɔ̄tìi kāaǹ Sadraaki nì Meesaki nì Abeedi Neegoo ipaan in sá ikpaanee pu Babiloon tiŋgbaŋkin. Ubɔti dámintì busukpaambu bubɔ

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar sent the following letter to the people of all nations and races on the earth: Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: «Mama, Neebukadineesaar, m nìn bí m-beecindin nì mmɔn ní tiba nì tiba kaa nìn páb́-mi.

english_verse: I am glad to tell about the wonderful miracles God Most High has done for me.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu kubɔ, m dɔ̄ m-dooŋu pu ní ki dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ. M nìn fāŋkì tikpil. Di sá yii tin m nìn kée nìn kɔ́ǹ-mi dinyoondi.

english_verse: His miracles are mighty and marvelous. He will rule forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: M nìn yāntì bi cáań Babiloon ciŋfitiibi kɔkɔ m-nimbiin bí lēē kudamintiiuee taapu kí tùkù-mi.

english_verse: Then I commanded every wise man in Babylonia to appear in my court, so they could explain the meaning of my dream.
translation_verse: <Baltasaar, bikpaŋkpantiibi kpiliu, m nyí yii inimbɔti in bí circiree fam bí a-pu ní tibɔbalkaal tiba kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ a-cee. Tùkù-mi m nín dámintì ki ká tiŋyee taapu.

english_verse: After they arrived, I told them my dream, but they were not able to say what it meant.
translation_verse: M nín dɔ̄ m-dooŋu puee, m nín dámintì puee sɔ̀. M pée dɔ̄ m-dooŋu puee, m dāa bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, busukpaŋkpaambu bubɔ nyáń ki yúl̀ kitiŋ kansikin.

english_verse: Finally, a young man named Daniel came in, and I told him the dream. The holy gods had given him special powers, and I had renamed him Belteshazzar after my own god.
translation_verse: Busubuee nìn mɔ̄tìi wíiǹ ki ŋá busukpaŋkpaambu ní bu-yilpu tūū kutagbɔŋu. Unil yaa nìn pée bí kitiŋ jandi diŋyee, u nìn ŋūǹ kí wāl̀ busubu gbanti.

english_verse: I said, “Belteshazzar, not only are you the wisest of all advisors and counselors, but the holy gods have given you special powers to solve the most difficult mysteries. So listen to what I dreamed and tell me what it means:
translation_verse: Bu-faati nìn cáá kunyaaŋŋu. Bu nìn lòoǹ abil tikpil, ki nìn ŋūǹ kí kpíiǹ binib kɔkɔ. Ipeel nìn dòoń ki dɔ̀ bu-booŋŋu taapu, ní inoon mun pāantí i-diti bu-paŋŋi pu. Tin kɔkɔ pée cáá kufoouee nìn kāntí bu-pu ti-jinti.

english_verse: In my sleep I saw a very tall tree in the center of the world.
translation_verse: «M dáá gbíntìi dɔ̄ m-dooŋu pu ki dàkafī tin m kée puee, m bí yii ḿ kpèèyee circir tuuŋŋu ŋubɔ dee. Ŋu nyánní yilpu ki kpákatìń

english_verse: It grew stronger and higher, until it reached to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: ní ki téeń mpɔn yii: <Gāāmaan busubuee kí lúkú, kpākal̀maan bu-paŋŋi, lòol̀maan bu-faati kí kàfì bu-biliŋ kí yàaǹ. Ipeel ń nyā bu-taapu kí sāǹ, ní inoon ń yīkì bu-paŋŋi.

english_verse: It was covered with leaves and heavy with fruit— enough for all nations. Wild animals enjoyed its shade, birds nested in its branches, and all creatures on earth lived on its fruit.
translation_verse: Ama ní yàntī busubuee nyeel nì bu-nyaaŋyi ń nīn gbíntìi síb́ kitiŋ. Ní nyàab̀ tikúti nì tasa kusakai kí tɔ̄ dinyeelee ní kí yàntī-dì kusaaun timool kansikin. Dimalindi ń sɔ̀ŋkì-dì ní dí nīn ŋmóò timool kii ipeelee.

english_verse: “While I was in bed, having this vision, a holy angel came down from heaven
translation_verse: Di-pɔbil làá kpántí dí taa ti nín̄ cáá nnibimbim, ní dí nīn kíǹ ki cáá mpeebimbim! Míǹ boonee, dí nīn bí míǹ áli abin aluli.

english_verse: and shouted: ‘Chop down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Make the animals leave its shade and send the birds flying from its branches.
translation_verse: «Unimbɔti tuuŋyi in cí duulinyee di bíi lèekī tibɔti nee ki dàkà. Mimmee binib kɔkɔ làá béé yii Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu di cáá binib beeŋi kɔkɔ pu mpɔn. Úǹ di kàantí un u yaa lèe dibeel ní ki yòontí unil un sīntiǹ u-ba taapuee yilpu.»

english_verse: But leave its stump and roots in the ground, surrounded by grass and held by chains of iron and bronze. ‘Make sure that this ruler lives like the animals out in the open fields, unprotected from the dew.
translation_verse: Too kudamintiiu kun man, ubɔti Neebukadineesaar dámintèe dee. Kɔŋkɔnnee sii, Baltasaar, tùkù-mi ku-taapu. Di sá yii m-beel poon ciŋfitiibi báà ubɔ kaa ŋúń ki tùkū-mi ku-taapu. Ama siiyee, m nyí yii a ŋūǹ, kun puee inimbɔti in bí circiree fam bí a-pu. Daniyeel lēē kudamintiiu taapu ki tùkū ubɔti

english_verse: This punishment is given at the command of the holy angels. It will show to all who live that God Most High controls all kingdoms and chooses for their rulers persons of humble birth.’
translation_verse: A ká busubu bubɔ, ní bu wíiǹ ki ŋá busukpaambu ní bu-yilpu tūū kutagbɔŋu, ní binib ŋūǹ kí nīn wāĺ-bu ilaan kɔkɔ kitiŋ jaaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: “Daniel, that was the dream that none of the wise men in my kingdom were able to understand. But I am sure that you will understand what it means, because the holy gods have given you some special powers.”
translation_verse: Busubu gbanti faati nìn cáá kunyaaŋŋu ki lòoǹ abil tikpil, ki nìn cáá tijin kí kpíiǹ binib kɔkɔ, ní ipeel nìn dòoń ki dɔ̀ bu-booŋŋu taapu, ní inoon mun nìn pāantí i-diti bu-paŋŋi pu.

english_verse: For a while, Daniel was terribly confused and worried by what he was thinking. But I said, “Don't be bothered either by the dream or by what it means.” Daniel replied: Your Majesty, I wish the dream had been against your enemies.
translation_verse: Busubu gbantee, ubɔti, an sá sii. Di sá yii a kpántì ukpaan nì mpɔndaan. A-yindi yíkì yilpu áli ki tin tūū kutagbɔŋu, ní a-bɔtiiti tālim̀ ki bàn̄ ilaan kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Its leaves were beautiful, and it produced enough fruit for all living creatures; animals lived in its shade, and birds nested in its branches.
translation_verse: «Ubɔti, kpèè kudamintiiuee taapu sɔ̀. Yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu di lēē tin làá bàń sii ubɔti maŋfal wiiŋyi puee ki dàkā-si.

english_verse: Then you saw a holy angel come down from heaven and say, “Chop down the tree and destroy it! But leave its stump and roots in the ground, fastened there by a chain of iron and bronze. Let it stay for seven years out in the field with the wild animals, unprotected from the dew.”
translation_verse: Bi gíti tīī mara yii bí yàntī disunyeelee nì di-nyaaŋyi. An dàkà yii bi làá dāá fàtīí gíiǹ a-beel kí tīī-si ŋyunti ŋun ní a yaa láa béè yii Unimbɔti un bí yilpuee di sá tiwan kɔkɔ kpiliuee.

english_verse: But he gave orders not to disturb the stump and roots. This is to show that you will be king once again, after you learn that the God who rules from heaven is in control.
translation_verse: Iŋmal saalaa nì ili boonee, ubɔti nìn tɔ́kɔ́ ki còom̄ bi nín bɔ̀b̄ dibeecindi din bí Babiloon tiŋkinee yilpu.

english_verse: Your Majesty, please be willing to do what I say. Turn from your sins and start living right; have mercy on those who are mistreated. Then all will go well with you for a long time. The Rest of Nebuchadnezzar's Letter about His Second Dream
translation_verse: U nìn téeń yii: «Babiloon kitiŋkpaaŋŋi kin m dū m-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu ki máń án nīn sá mama ubɔti beecindi kí dàkà m-kpaanti nyootee kaa nín sɔ̀ɔɔ?»

english_verse: About twelve months later, I was walking on the flat roof of my royal palace and admiring the beautiful city of Babylon, when these things started happening to me. I was saying to myself, “Just look at this wonderful capital city that I have built by my own power and for my own glory!”
translation_verse: Ataa pu niin ní tin bi sòon̄ yii án làá bàń Neebukadineesaar puee bāań-u. Bi jìn̄-u binib kansikin ní u kíĺ ki bíi ŋmóò timool kii unaayee. Dimalindi sɔ̄ŋkì u-wunti, ní u-yikpiti fɔ̄kɔǹ kii ikaabu kutee ní u-ŋaŋŋati mun fɔ̄kɔǹ kii inoon ŋaŋŋatee. Ubɔti Neebukadineesaar ká dicáaǹdi

english_verse: You will be forced to live with the wild animals, away from people. For seven years you will eat grass, as though you were an ox, until you learn that God Most High is in control of all earthly kingdoms and that he is the one who chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ kaa sá tiba u-cee. U yaa là puee ní u ŋáań ki tìì bin bí yilpuee nì bin bí kitiŋ puee. Ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí cúú u-ŋal kí bàlifì-u yii: «Ba ní a ŋáańee?»

english_verse: This was no sooner said than done—I was forced to live like a wild animal; I ate grass and was unprotected from the dew. As time went by, my hair grew longer than eagle feathers, and my fingernails looked like the claws of a bird.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee ní m fātìi ká m-nilandɔkɔŋu. Bi nìn fātìi gíiǹ m-beel nyooti nì m-bɔtiiti jilmau nì m-pɔŋŋu ki tīī-mi. M-kpambaliŋ nì m-kàliŋkpaambi nìn nyàab̄-mi ní ki fātìi gíiǹ m-beel ki tīī-mi ní m gíti fōō tinyool ki jítiǹ mpeepeekaamin.

english_verse: Finally, I prayed to God in heaven, and my mind was healed. Then I said: “I praise and honor God Most High. God lives forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, mama Neebukadineesaar, m nyɔ́ŋkí ki dàntī ní ki pàkà yilpu bɔtiu! Tin kɔkɔ u ŋáańee kítì, ní u-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ sá deedee tuuŋŋi. Úǹ di cáá mpɔn kí sìntī un yòontí u-ba yilpuee taapu.

english_verse: One evening, King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his highest officials, and he drank wine with them.
translation_verse: Dalbee, ubɔti Baltasaar ŋá jiŋaakpaan ubɔ ki yíiń u-kàliŋkpaambi binib kutuku, ní u kíĺ ki bíi nyù ndaam bi-nimbiin.

english_verse: He got drunk and ordered his servants to bring in the gold and silver cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted the cups, so that he and all his wives and officials could drink from them.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Baltasaar nyùn̄ ndaam an nyāatì-uee ní u tīī mara yii bí cù kí yòon̄ sindaariya nì animbil kúti kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi bin u-baa Neebukadineesaar nìn yōoǹní Jeerusaleem kunimbɔtidiinee kí cáań. U nìn là u nì u-kàliŋkpaambi nì u-nimpoobi nì u-bɔmbi ń nīn bàtī ndaam ki ŋáań poon ki nyù.

english_verse: When the gold cups were brought in, everyone at the banquet drank from them and praised their idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
translation_verse: Bi nyùn̄ ndaam míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki nyɔ́ŋkì awaa ŋin sá sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti nì tikúti nì idɔ nì ataŋkpeeyee.

english_verse: Suddenly a human hand was seen writing on the plaster wall of the palace. The hand was just behind the lampstand, and the king could see it writing.
translation_verse: Bi bíi ŋáań míǹ kpalaayee, unil ŋaliŋu ŋubɔ nyáń ki kíĺ ki bíi ŋmà dibeecindi gundi pu laakin fitila nìn tɔ́kɔ́ ki ŋmíntée. Ubɔti nìn ká ŋŋalee nín nìn bíi ŋmà puee.

english_verse: He was so frightened that his face turned pale, his knees started shaking, and his legs became weak.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti nimbiin cúu kpántì ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ ŋkpitim pu ní u-wunti kɔkɔ fōō dijinjikil ní u-tabiŋyiliŋ kíǹ ki gbáà tɔb kpàkpa.

english_verse: The king called in his advisors, who claimed they could talk with the spirits of the dead and understand the meanings found in the stars. He told them, “The man who can read this writing and tell me what it means will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. He will wear robes of royal purple and a gold chain around his neck.”
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti téeń mpɔn yii bí cáań bikpaŋkpantiibi nì bibɔɔbi nì bin kpèé iŋmalbijaa kí béé tin dòońee. Ŋyunti ŋun Babiloon ciŋfitiibi gbanti kɔkɔ kpáfèe ní ubɔti bí-bi yii: «Un yaa ŋúń ki kàan̄ tiŋmaŋmabiti nee ki lēē ti-taapu ki tùkū-mee, m làá yàntī bí dū dibeebɔkutil din máǹ cínciŋee kí pèen̄-u, kí dū sindaariya léeŋkaati kí léeń-u, ní udaan ń kūtì bikàliŋkpaambi pu bí nīn kpòotī dibeel.»

english_verse: All of King Belshazzar's highest officials came in, but not one of them could read the writing or tell what it meant,
translation_verse: Ubɔti ciŋfitiibi kɔkɔ kɔ́, ama baa ŋúń ki kàan̄ tiŋmaŋmabitee kpaŋkpan ki dāa nín lèekī ti-taapu ki tùkù ubɔti.

english_verse: and they were completely puzzled. Now the king was more afraid than ever before, and his face turned white as a ghost.
translation_verse: An ŋá mimmee ní ubɔti Baltasaar pɔbil mɔ̄tìi bíil̀ ní u-nimbiin gíti cúu kpántì, ní an bākatì u-kàliŋkpilib sèeee, ní bi mun kaa ti nyí tin poon bi bée. Daniyeel lēē maamaaci ŋmaŋmabitee taapu

english_verse: When the queen heard the king and his officials talking, she came in and said: Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! Don't be afraid or look so pale.
translation_verse: Ubɔti na gbìl̄ ubɔti nì u-kàliŋkpilib biilii puee ní u kɔ́ kudii kun poon bi kā ki jīǹ jiŋaalee ki lī yii: «Ubɔti, Unimbɔti ń tīī-si mmaŋfafɔkɔn! Taa yàntī a-landɔkɔi ń bīil̀ a-pɔbil míǹ kí taa yàntī a-nimbiin ń cúú kpántí míǹ.

english_verse: In your kingdom there is a man who has been given special powers by the holy gods. When your father Nebuchadnezzar was king, this man was known to be as smart, intelligent, and wise as the gods themselves. Your father put him in charge of all who claimed they could talk with the spirits or understand the meanings in the stars or tell about the future.
translation_verse: A-beel poonee, uninja ubɔ bí inimbɔti in bí circiree fam bí u-ni. A-baa yuntiŋuee, bi nìn dáań ki ká yii u wāĺ ki cáá dinyil nì iciin in náań nì awaa ciiŋyee. An puee ní a-baa, ubɔti Neebukadineesaar nìn dū-u ki kpántì bibɔɔbi nì bikpaŋkpantiibi nì bikpaŋkpalib nì bin kpèé iŋmalbijaa kí béé tin dòońee kɔkɔ kpiliu.

english_verse: He also changed the man's name from Daniel to Belteshazzar. Not only is he wise and intelligent, but he can explain dreams and riddles and solve difficult problems. Send for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Daniyeel gbanti un ní ubɔti nìn páaǹ diyindi yii Baltasaaree nìn cáá ŋfam min nyáń mi-bee nì dinyil nì iciin ní ki nìn ŋūǹ kí lēē tidamintiil taapu, ki nìn nyí ipɔɔn kɔkɔ taapu kí tùkù unil, ní ki nìn tí ŋūǹ kí lēē tibɔti tin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee taapu. Míǹ puee tɔ̄ bí yíiń Daniyeel gbanti, u làá tùkù-si tiŋmaŋmabiti nee taapu.»

english_verse: When Daniel was brought in, the king said: So you are Daniel, one of the captives my father brought back from Judah!
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi cūtìi cáań Daniyeel ubɔti nimbiin ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Sii di lafun sá Daniyeel, Juuda yab yumbui in m-baa ubɔti nìn cáań Juuda tiŋkinee ubɔeeee?

english_verse: I was told that the gods have given you special powers and that you are intelligent and very wise.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m gbìl̄ a-pu yii inimbɔti fam bí a-ni ní a wāĺ ki cáá dinyil nì iciin in nyáń i-bee.

english_verse: Neither my advisors nor the men who talk with the spirits of the dead could read this writing or tell me what it means.
translation_verse: Bi dáá pée cáań-mi biciŋfitiibi nì bikpaŋkpantiibi bí bàà kàaǹ tiŋmaŋmabiti nee kí tùkù-mi taapu dee, ama baa ŋúń.

english_verse: But I have been told that you understand everything and that you can solve difficult problems. Now then, if you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. You will wear royal purple robes and have a gold chain around your neck.
translation_verse: Ní m gbìl̄ yii a ŋūǹ kí lēē ipɔɔn nì tibɔti tin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee taapu. Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, a yaa ŋúń ki kàan̄ tiŋmaŋmabiti nee ki lēē taapu ki tùkū-mee, m làá yàntī bí dū dibeebɔkutil din máǹ cínciŋee kí pèen̄-si, ní kí dū sindaariya léeŋkaati kí léeń-si, ní á kūtì bikàliŋkpaambi pu ní nīn kpòotī dibeel.»

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, I will read the writing and tell you what it means. But you may keep your gifts or give them to someone else.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Daniyeel kíí ubɔti yii: «Ubɔti, yòon̄ a-wampɔkaati kí dū tipaal tin a bàà làá pà-mee kí tīī ubɔ. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m làá kàaǹ tiŋmaŋmabitee kí lēē taapu kí tùkù-si.

english_verse: Sir, the Most High God made your father a great and powerful man and brought him much honor and glory.
translation_verse: Ti-baa ubɔti, Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu nìn yāntì a-baa Neebukadineesaar kpántì ubɔtikpaan. U nìn cáá tinyool nì mpɔŋkpaan.

english_verse: God did such great things for him that people of all nations and races shook with fear. Your father had the power of life or death over everyone, and he could honor or ruin anyone he chose.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nín nìn yāntì u kpántì ukpaan miŋyee, anibul nì atimbun nì isoon kɔkɔ nib nìn fàŋkí ní yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ u-nimbiin. Ubɔti yaa nìn là kí kpɔ̀ uŋyee u kù ní, ní un u yaa nìn tí là ú nīn bí dimaŋfalinee, ní ú yàntī udaan. U nìn yòontí un u yaa nìn là kí yòon̄ yilpuee, ní ki nìn sìntī un u yaa nìn là kí sìntī taapuee.

english_verse: But when he became proud and stubborn, his glorious kingdom was taken from him.
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun u yōoǹ u-ba yilpu ki kɔ́ dilambilinee, bi nìn kpákatì-u u-beejal pu ní u fá u-nyooti.

english_verse: His mind became like that of an animal, and he was forced to stay away from people and live with wild donkeys. Your father ate grass like an ox, and he slept outside where his body was soaked with dew. He was forced to do this until he learned that the Most High God rules all kingdoms on earth and chooses their kings.
translation_verse: Bi jìn̄-u binib kansikin ní u kpántì kii upeelee. U nìn bí kumooun mammu kansikin, ní ki nìn ŋmóò timool kii unaayee. U nìn fùul̀ dimalindi ki cáa sāā ŋyunti ŋun u béè yii Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu di cáá binib beeŋi kɔkɔ pu mpɔn, ní un u yaa lèe, u kàantí dibeelee.

english_verse: King Belshazzar, you knew all of this, but you still refused to honor the Lord who rules from heaven.
translation_verse: Ní sii, u-jipɔɔn Baltasaar, min kamaa a nyí tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔee, aa sīntiǹ a-ba taapu,

english_verse: Instead, you turned against him and ordered the cups from his temple to be brought here, so that you and your wives and officials could drink wine from them. You praised idols made of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, even though they cannot see or hear or think. You refused to worship the God who gives you breath and controls everything you do.
translation_verse: ní ki yíkì kí já nì ti-Dindaan un bí yilpuee. A yāntì bi cūtìi cáań u-diiku poon kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi ní sii nì a-kàliŋkpaambi nì a-nimpoobi nì a-bɔmbi bātì ndaam ki ŋá poon ki nyùn̄. Míǹ boonee, a nyɔ́ŋkì awaa ŋin sá animbil kúti nì sindaariya nì tasa kúti nì tikúti nì idɔ nì ataŋkpeeyee, awaa ŋin kaa wāĺaaa, kaa gbìl̀aaa, kaa nyí tiba muee. A ŋá míǹ kaa nyɔ́ŋkì Unimbɔti un ŋaan ní a-maŋfal nì tin kɔkɔ ŋūǹ kí bàń-see kēe.

english_verse: That's why he sent the hand to write this message on the wall.
translation_verse: An pu ní Unimbɔti túnní ŋŋal nee ŋú dāan̄ kí ŋmà tiŋmaŋmabiti nee.

english_verse: Belshazzar gave a command for Daniel to be made the third most powerful man in his kingdom and to be given a purple robe and a gold chain.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Baltasaar tīī mara yii bí dū dibeebɔkutil din máǹ cínciŋee kí pèen̄ Daniyeel, kí dū sindaariya léeŋkaati kí léeń-u ní kí bāakì yii Daniyeel làá kūtì bikàliŋkpaambi pu bí nīn kpòotī dibeel.

english_verse: That same night, the king was killed.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu gbanti ní bi kūū Baltasaar, Babiloon bɔtiu.

english_verse: In order to make sure that his government was run properly, Darius put three other officials in charge of the governors. One of these officials was Daniel.
translation_verse: Daariyusi nìn ká yii an kítì ú kàan̄ ntiŋgbamu kpilib binib dilaataal nì mmuŋku bí nīn kpòotī kitiŋ kɔkɔ.

english_verse: And he did his work so much better than the other governors and officials that the king decided to let him govern the whole kingdom.
translation_verse: U nìn gíti lēē bikàliŋkpilib bita bí nīn kpèé ntiŋgbamu kpilib nín kpòotī kitiŋ puee, án nín làá ŋá pu ubɔti tuuŋŋi ń nīn còom̄ tiŋanee. Daniyeel nìn sá bikàliŋkpilib bita gbanti kansikin ubɔ.

english_verse: The other men tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel did his work for the king. But they could not accuse him of anything wrong, because he was honest and faithful and did everything he was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Ama Daniyeel gbantee nìn jítiǹ bikàliŋkpilib bili bin kíǹee nì ntiŋgbamu kpilib kɔkɔ. Di sá yii ŋfam min nìn bí u-nee nyáń mi-ba, an pu ní ubɔti nìn bíi màkafī kí dū-u kí kàan̄ u-beel kɔkɔ pu ukpil.

english_verse: All of your officials, leaders, advisors, and governors agree that you should make a law forbidding anyone to pray to any god or human except you for the next
translation_verse: Niinee ní bikàliŋkpilibee nì ntiŋgbamu kpilibee yíkì malaa ki nín cá ubɔti cee ki bí-u yii: «Ubɔti Daariyusi, Unimbɔti ń tīī-si mmaŋfafɔkɔn.

english_verse: They went back to the king and said, “Didn't you make a law that forbids anyone to pray to any god or human except you for the next
translation_verse: Niinee ní binibee nóó dikitil ki bìl̄ ki kɔ́ Daniyeel pu ní ki ká-u u gbāā ki mèé ki gbàam̄ u-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: The men then told the king, “That Jew named Daniel, who was brought here as a captive, refuses to obey you or the law that you ordered to be written. And he still prays to his god three times a day.”
translation_verse: Bi ká mimmee ní ki nín cá ubɔti cee ki bí-u yii: «Ubɔti, an kaa sá sii di nyīī mara nee pu ŋŋal yii kí yòon̄ kí cáá sāā iwiin mmuŋku nì saalaayee, un yaa mēē diwaal àá unil ubɔ tiba ŋwimmeem poon ní an kaa sá siiyee, bí cáá udaan kí tɔ̄ mbòó ŋun poon bi kpàá gbikintibeeee?» Ní ubɔti kíí yii: «Míǹ deedee ní an sá, kii Meedeesi yab nì Peeriisi yab marau nín kaa kpántí puee.»

english_verse: The king was really upset to hear about this, and for the rest of the day he tried to think how he could save Daniel.
translation_verse: Ní binibee fātìi bí ubɔti yii: «Toooo! Daniyeel un sá bin ti cáań Juuda tiŋkin kuyuŋuee kansikin ubɔee kaa fātìi tɔ́-si, ki dāa nín kàaǹ mara un pu a nyīī ŋŋalee. Kpèè, u pée mèé ní ŋfunyɔm mita ŋwiin.»

english_verse: At sunset the men returned and said, “Your Majesty, remember that no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed, not even by the king.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti nín gbìl̄ tibɔti gbantee ní an kɔ́ǹ-u kunimbaau ní u lēē u-pɔbilin kí fīī Daniyeel. U pée mɔ̀n̄ míǹ ní áli ŋwìiń dāa jéetì ki pée bíi nyàab̀ nsan ŋun pu u làá dī kí fīī-uee.

english_verse: So Darius ordered Daniel to be brought out and thrown into a pit of lions. But he said to Daniel, “You have been faithful to your God, and I pray that he will rescue you.”
translation_verse: Ama ní binibee fātìi gítìń malaa ubɔti cee ki bí-u yii: «Ubɔti, a pée nyí yii Meedeesi yab nì Peeriisi yab marau poonee, ubɔti yaa ŋmàn̄ mara ki nyīī ŋŋalee, baa ti ŋūǹ kí kpántí-u.»

english_verse: A stone was rolled over the pit, and it was sealed. Then Darius and his officials stamped the seal to show that no one should let Daniel out.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti tīī mara yii bí cáań Daniyeel kí dū-u kí tɔ̄ mbòó ŋun poon bi kpàá gbikintibee. Ní ubɔti bí Daniyeel yii: «See a-Nimbɔtiu un a jáaḿ kaa gbèentée baba di ŋūǹ kí fīī-si.»

english_verse: All night long the king could not sleep. He did not eat anything, and he would not let anyone come in to entertain him.
translation_verse: Bi nìn cáań ditaŋkpakpaandi diba ki pīiǹ mbòóyee nyɔkɔ pu ní ubɔti yōoǹ úǹ u-ba jaliiki nì u-kàliŋkpilib jaliiki ki nyīī ditaŋkpalee pu, án nín làá ŋá pu ubɔ ń taa ŋmā kí kpántí Daniyeel pu tibee.

english_verse: He was anxious and shouted, “Daniel, you were faithful and served your God. Was he able to save you from the lions?”
translation_verse: Ntaafaabɔmbɔminee ní ubɔti yíkì malaa ki nín cá mbòó ŋun poon bi kpàá gbikintibee.

english_verse: The king was relieved to hear Daniel's voice, and he gave orders for him to be taken out of the pit. Daniel's faith in his God had kept him from being harmed.
translation_verse: M-Nimbɔtiu túnní u-tuuŋŋu ní ŋu dɔ́miń ki pīiǹ gbikintib nyɔmmu ní baa ŋá-mi tiba. Di sá Unimbɔti ká yii m síl̀ nì u deedee kaa yīntiǹ-u tiba, ní kaa yīntiǹ sii, ubɔti mun tiba.»

english_verse: And the king ordered the men who had brought charges against Daniel to be thrown into the pit, together with their wives and children. But before they even reached the bottom, the lions ripped them to pieces.
translation_verse: Niinee ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ ubɔti ní u tīī mara yii bí nyāntí Daniyeel mbòóyee poon. Ní bi nyántì Daniyeel mbòó poon, ama baa nìn ká u-pu báà tiweendi, di sá yii u nìn máká u-Nimbɔtiu pu.

english_verse: King Darius then sent this message to all people of every nation and race in the world: “Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: Ní ubɔti yāntì bi cáań bin nìn kúŋfì Daniyeel boonee ki tɔ́ mbòó ŋun poon bi kpàá gbikintibee, ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu nì bi-nimpoobi. Bi tin pée lì yii bi dù-bi kí tɔ̄ee, baa bàn̄ kitiŋ ní gbikintib kíntì-bi ki tɔ̄ntì ki wīil̀ bi-kpabiŋ kɔkɔ.

english_verse: I command everyone in my kingdom to worship and honor the God of Daniel. He is the living God, the one who lives forever. His power and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti Daariyusi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī anibul nì atimbun nì isoon kɔkɔ nib bin kóò u-tiŋki kɔkɔ puee yii: «Ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí ni-cee.

english_verse: All went well for Daniel while Darius was king, and even when Cyrus the Persian ruled.
translation_verse: Úǹ di jòoń unil ki fìil̄-u, u ŋáań maamaaci tuŋkpaaŋŋi yilpu nì kitiŋ pu. Úǹ di fīī Daniyeel ki nyántì gbikintib ŋaan.»

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the first year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had some dreams and visions while I was asleep one night, and I wrote them down. The four winds were stirring up the mighty sea,
translation_verse: Daniyeel nín lī puee sèé: «Kunyeeuee, ní an lēē ki dàkā-mi. M kpēēyee, ní ki ká kubuŋu nyánní yilpu jannaatiliŋ pu ki jītí tiŋkukpaan pu mpɔn.

english_verse: when suddenly four powerful beasts came out of the sea. Each beast was different.
translation_verse: Ní tipeebilindi tinaa tiba nyánní tiŋkun. Tì nìn nyáń ti-ba ti-ba.

english_verse: The first was like a lion with the wings of an eagle. As I watched, its wings were pulled off. Then it was lifted to an upright position and made to stand on two feet, just like a human, and it was given a human mind.
translation_verse: Upeepeekaa náań nì gbikinti, ní ki cáá ukaabu feeŋyi. M bíi kpèé-uee ní bi cúú u-feeŋyi ki lēē ní ki yōoǹ-u kitiŋ ki síiǹ u-boon taaŋi alee pu kii unilee, ní bi tīī-u dinipɔbil ní u kíǹ ki cáá nnibimbim.

english_verse: The second beast looked like a bear standing on its hind legs. It held three ribs in its teeth, and it was told, “Attack! Eat all the flesh you want.”
translation_verse: M tí bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, upeeliliiti dee. Úǹ náań nì digbiŋgbil. Úǹ kaa nìn yáatì ki yúl̀. U nìn bàb̄ u-nyɔkɔn atakakalkpab ata u-nyiŋŋi kansikin. Ní bi tùkū-u yii: <Yīkìí yūĺ, ŋmɔ́ tinan tikpil.>

english_verse: The third beast was like a leopard—except that it had four wings and four heads. It was given authority to rule.
translation_verse: Míǹ boon, m gbíntìi bíi kpèéyee ní ki ká upeel ubɔ mun. Upeel gbanti úǹ náań nì uguloobu ní u-boon cáá unoon feeŋyi inaa. Upeelee nìn gíti cáá ayil anaa ní bi dū mpɔn ki tīī-u.

english_verse: The fourth beast was stronger and more terrifying than the others. Its huge teeth were made of iron, and what it didn't grind with its teeth, it smashed with its feet. It was different from the others, and it had horns on its head—ten of them.
translation_verse: Míǹ boon m gbíntìi bíi kpèé an nín bí ki lèekī ki dàkà-mi kunyeeu puee. M bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, upeenanaati dee. Kupeebiliŋŋu dee ku-baba, ki cáá tifaandi ní ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ an kaa cáá bí lì. Upeelee cáá tinyiŋkpaandi tin sá tikútee ní ki ŋmóò ki tɔ̀ntī tin u yaa pée ká u-saŋŋu puee, ní ki tà ki ŋmàlintí tin kīntí waa ŋmɔ́ee. Upeel gbanti úǹ nìn pée nyáń u-ba nì ipeepeekaa itee ní, ní ki nìn cáá iyin saalaa.

english_verse: Just as I was thinking about these horns, a smaller horn appeared, and three of the other horns were pulled up by the roots to make room for it. This horn had the eyes of a human and a mouth that spoke with great arrogance. Judgment Daniel wrote:
translation_verse: Ní m kíĺ ki bíi kpèé iyinee, m tí bí yii ḿ kpèèyee ŋyin kiwaai kiba cɔ́tìń in béeyee kansikin ní ki cúú ipeepeekaa gbantee kansikin ita ki fùkū. Ŋyin ŋun nyáń ki lúŋkì gbanti nìn cáá animbil kii unilee, ní ki cáá kinyɔkɔ kin sòoǹ tilambibɔti ŋmee.» Unimbɔti bɔsooŋyi

english_verse: Thrones were set up while I was watching, and the Eternal God took his place. His clothing and his hair were white as snow. His throne was a blazing fire with fiery wheels,
translation_verse: «M bíi kpèé ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi sīintí abeejalee ní utikpil ubɔ dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ abeejalee diba pu. U-wampeeŋkaati nìn pīiǹ káŋkaŋ ní u-yikpiti mun pīiǹ kii ipii kuti tin bi fíntèe. U-beejal nìn sá aŋmilimbil ŋma ní, ní ki nìn cáá ataa. Ataa gbanti mun nìn sá ŋŋmi ŋma ní.

english_verse: and flames were dashing out from all around him. Countless thousands were standing there to serve him. The time of judgment began, and the books were opened.
translation_verse: Mbun ŋun poon ŋŋmi pùub̀ee nìn jītí u-nimbiin. Binib kutukub kutukub nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi ki tìì-u ní binib kutukub cutimaanyi nìn yú u-nimbiin. Niinee bibɔsoonliibi kāl̀ ní bi cúú tigbɔn ki kpátì.

english_verse: I watched closely to see what would happen to this smaller horn because of the arrogant things it was saying. Then before my very eyes, the fourth beast was killed and its body destroyed by fire.
translation_verse: «M nìn gbíntìi bíi kpèé, kun puee ŋyinee nìn bíi sòoǹ tilambibɔti ki ŋáań kuwoou. Ŋyunti ŋun m bíi kpèéyee ní ki ká bi kūū upeelee. Bi nìn dū u-wunti ki tɔ́ ŋŋmin án wà kí nàan̄.

english_verse: The other three beasts had their authority taken from them, but they were allowed to live a while longer.
translation_verse: Ní bi cúú ipeel in kíǹee pɔŋyi ki fōō i-cee, ama ní ki yāntì i dáá bí dimaŋfalin kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋubɔ poon.

english_verse: As I continued to watch the vision that night, I saw what looked like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven, and he was presented to the Eternal God.
translation_verse: «M gbíntìi bíi kpèé an nín bí ki lèekī pu ki dàkà-mi kunyeeuee. Kpalaayee tiwan tiba di páaǹní atagbanni ki dòoń ki náań nì unilee. U còom̄ ki cá utikpilee cee ní bi cáá-u ki cūnnì u-nimbiin.

english_verse: He was crowned king and given power and glory, so that all people of every nation and race would serve him. He will rule forever, and his kingdom is eternal, never to be destroyed. The Meaning of Daniel's Vision
translation_verse: Ní bi dū dibeel nì tinyool nì mpɔn ki tīī-u. Niinee anibul kɔkɔ nì atimbun kɔkɔ nì isoon kɔkɔ nib gbāaǹ ki jáam̀-u. U-pɔŋŋu làá nīn bí ní ki cá jaanjaan, ŋu kpá kí kúntí. U-beel kpá kí nàan̄.» Dileedakal dipeepeekaal taapu

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I was terrified by these visions, and I didn't know what to think.
translation_verse: «Mama Daniyeel, kunimbaau nìn kɔ́-mi tikpil, ní an nín lēē ki dàkā-mi puee fàantí-mi.

english_verse: But God Most High will give his kingdom to his chosen ones, and it will be theirs forever and ever.”
translation_verse: Ama bi làá dāá dū dibeel kí tīī Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu circir nib, ní bí dāá fōō-dì kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan jaanjaan.>

english_verse: I wanted to know more about the fourth beast, because it was so different and much more terrifying than the others. What was the meaning of its iron teeth and bronze claws and of its feet that smashed what the teeth and claws had not ground and crushed?
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní m nyàab̄ kí béé upeenanaatee nín baasii sá uŋyee. Upeel gbanti di nyáń u-ba nì bin kɔkɔ kíǹee. U cáá tifaandi tikpil, ki cáá anyin ŋin sá tikútee nì tiŋaŋŋati tin sá tasee, ní ki ŋmóò ki tɔ̀ntī tin u yaa pée kée ní ki tà tin kíǹee ki ŋmàlintí.

english_verse: I also wanted to know more about all ten of those horns on its head. I especially wanted to know more about the one that took the place of three of the others—the horn that had eyes and spoke with arrogance and seemed greater than the others.
translation_verse: M gíti bālifì kí béé iyin saalaa in u tú u-yil puee nì ŋun mun gíti nyáń ki cúú iyin ita ki fùkū in béeyee kansikinee taapu. Ŋyin gbanti di cáá animbil, ki cáá kinyɔkɔ kin sòoǹ tilambibɔti, ki wíiǹ ki jítiǹ in kɔkɔ kíǹee.

english_verse: While I was looking, this horn attacked God's chosen ones and was winning the battle.
translation_verse: M bíi kpèéyee ní ki ká yii ŋyin gbanti bíi jáà nì circirdambi áli gba ŋu jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi.

english_verse: Then God Most High, the Eternal God, came and judged in favor of his chosen ones, because the time had arrived for them to be given the kingdom.
translation_verse: Ama utikpilee nìn dɔ́miń ki pɔ̀n̄ Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu circir nibul, ní ŋyunti bàn̄ ní circirdambi fōō dibeel.

english_verse: Then I was told by the one standing there: “The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom to appear on earth. It will be different from all the others— it will trample the earth and crush it to pieces.
translation_verse: «Niinee ní un m bàà bālifèe kíí-mi yii: <Upeenanaatee sá dibeenanaatiil din làá dāá nyā kitiŋ puee ní. Dibeel gbanti làá dāá nyā di-ba nì ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee. Dì làá dāá ŋmɔ́ tin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee, kí tāā tikɔkɔ kí ŋmàliŋkì ní kí tɔ̀ntī kɔkɔ.

english_verse: All ten of those horns are kings who will come from this kingdom, and one more will follow. This horn will be different from the others, and it will conquer three other kings.
translation_verse: Iyin saalaayee sá bibɔtiibi saalaa mun ní. Bi làá dāá kàl̄ dibeel gbanti ní ki fòol̄ tɔb. Bíǹ boonee, ubɔti ubɔ mun làá dāá kàl̄. Úǹ làá dāá nyā u-ba nì bipeepeekaabee ní kí dāá jà bibɔtiibi bita dibeejal pu.

english_verse: “This king will speak evil of God Most High, and he will be cruel to God's chosen ones. He will try to change God's Law and the sacred seasons. And he will be able to do this for a time, two times, and half a time.
translation_verse: U làá dāá sòoǹ Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu tibɔfan, ní kí dāá wɔ́b́ Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu circir nibul. U dāa màkantí gba kí kpántí jiŋaalib wiiŋyi nì marab, ní bí dāá dū circirdambi kí ŋá u-ŋaan abin ata nì dijandi.

english_verse: “Then the greatest kingdom of all will be given to the chosen ones of God Most High. His kingdom will be eternal, and all others will serve and obey him.”
translation_verse: Ní bí dū abee ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee bɔtiiti nì ŋi-pɔŋyi nì ŋi-kpaanti kí tīī yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu circir nibul. Bi-beel dāa sá talku beel ní, ní duulinya pɔŋyi kɔkɔ dāa kpántí bi-tɔntɔnliibi ní ki tɔ́-bi.>

english_verse: That was what I saw and heard. I turned pale with fear and kept it all to myself.
translation_verse: «Tibɔtee nín kúntì laakiŋyee sɔ̀. Mama Daniyeel, m dākafì tibɔtee pu, ní an cúú-mi tifaandi tikpil, ní m-nimbiin cúu kpántì ní m dū tibɔtee ki kpáafì m-pɔbilin.»

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the third year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had a second vision
translation_verse: «An nín nìn lēē ki dàkā-mi mpeepeekaam puee, boonee ní an tí fātìi lēē ki dàkā mama Daniyeel, ubɔti Baltasaar nín jíń dibeel dibintataatiil poonee.

english_verse: when I looked up and saw a ram standing there with two horns on its head—both of them were long, but the second one was longer than the first.
translation_verse: M yáatì m-yil ki kpēēyee, upìja yú mbunee caŋin. Upìjee cáá iyin ili. Iyinee fɔ̀kɔ̀ ama ŋubɔ fɔ̀kɔǹ ŋun kíǹee ní ŋun fɔ̀kɔ̀ gbantee mun di nyáń ki lúŋkì.

english_verse: The ram went charging toward the west, the north, and the south. No other animals were strong enough to oppose him, and nothing could save them from his power. So he did as he pleased and became even more powerful.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, m ká upìjee dū u-yiŋyi ki bìl̄ ki cūtì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú nì ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú, ama báà upeel kaa ŋúń ki yúl̀ u-nimbiinaaa, ubɔ mun kaa ŋūǹ kí fōō u-juti u-ŋaan. U yaa là puee, míǹ ní u ŋáań ní ki mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn ki cá.

english_verse: I kept on watching and saw a goat come from the west and charge across the entire earth, without even touching the ground. Between his eyes was a powerful horn,
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti ŋun m pée bíi dàkafī tin m kée puee, kpalaayee uŋɔja ubɔ nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki bāań. U nìn bíi yìiǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu, ama ní u-taaŋi kaa gbèetī kitiŋ. Uŋɔja gbanti nìn cáá ŋyiŋkpaan ŋubɔ u-nimbiliŋ kansikin.

english_verse: and with tremendous anger the goat started toward the ram that I had seen beside the river.
translation_verse: U nìn nín cá upìja un cáá iyin ili m bàà ká u yú mbun caŋinee cee. U nìn sáǹ mpɔn ní ki nín cá u-cee.

english_verse: The goat was so fierce that its attack broke both horns of the ram, leaving him powerless. Then the goat trampled on the ram, and no one could do anything to help.
translation_verse: M ká u sáǹ ki tóob́ upìjee nín yú puee ní ki fōō mbum u-pu. U nìn gūū-u ní upìjee yiŋyi ilee cúu gíì. Upìjee kaa nìn ká mpɔn ki yúl̀ u-nimbiin. U nìn yōoǹ upìjee ki yá kitiŋ ki tàn̄ tàn̄. Ubɔ kaa nìn bí kí ŋmā kí fīī upìjee u-ŋaan.

english_verse: After this, the goat became even more powerful. But at the peak of his power, his mighty horn was broken, and four other mighty horns took its place—one pointing to the north and one to the east, one to the south and one to the west.
translation_verse: Uŋɔjee nìn mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn ki cá. Ama ŋyunti ŋun u bàà ká mpɔn páaayee ní ŋyiŋkpaanee cúu gíì, ní iyiŋkpaan inaa nyáń ki téeǹ ŋun béeyee yil pu ki túĺ kitiŋ jannaatiliŋ.

english_verse: A little horn came from one of these, and its power reached to the south, the east, and even to the holy land.
translation_verse: «Ní ŋyin ŋubɔ cɔ́tì iyinee kansikin ŋun sá kiwaayee pu ní ki fɔ̄kɔǹ ki túĺ ŋgiil pú nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì kitinnyaaŋŋi watil pú.

english_verse: It became so strong that it attacked the stars in the sky, which were heaven's army. Then it threw some of them down to the earth and trampled on them.
translation_verse: Ní ŋu mɔ̄tìi wíiǹ ní ki yíkìi bíi jáà nì yilpu janjakitil. Ŋu nìn téé dijanjakitilee dijandi nì iŋmalbijaa ki lúkú kitiŋ ní ki tàn̄ tàn̄-bi.

english_verse: It humiliated heaven's army and dishonored its leader by keeping him from offering the daily sacrifices. In fact, it was so terrible that it even disgraced the temple and wiped out true worship. It also did everything else it wanted to do.
translation_verse: Atuŋkpiti gbanti puee, bi dū dijanjakitilee nì saraa un bi ŋáań baabadalee ki ŋá ŋu-ŋaan. Ŋyinee líì fookiimɔnti, ní tin kɔkɔ u ŋáańee bútí-u.
