english_verse: Then one of the holy angels asked another, “When will the daily sacrifices be offered again? What about this horrible rebellion? When will the temple and heaven's army no longer be trampled in the dust?”
translation_verse: «Niinee ní m gbìl̄ ntuun ŋubɔ bíi sòoǹ. Ní ntuun ŋubɔ mun bālifì-ŋu yii: <Tibɔti tin ní dileedakal nee sòoǹee làá yúntí kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní? Kí dāá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní saraabi bin bi ŋáań baabadalee làá gbèen̄ ní? Atuŋkpiti ŋin bíiĺ tikɔkɔee làá nīn bí kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu? Bi làá tāā tāā yilpu janjakitil nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní?>

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I was trying to figure out the meaning of the vision, when someone suddenly appeared there beside me.
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti ŋun mama Daniyeel, m bíi kpèé an nín lèekī pu ki dàkà-mi m nyàab̀ kí gbìl̄ taapuee ní ubɔ, u náań nì unil yam, dɔ́miń ki yúl̀ m-nimbiin.

english_verse: And from beside the Ulai River, a voice like that of a human said, “Gabriel, help him understand the vision.”
translation_verse: Ní m gbìl̄ unil ubɔ téeń Ulayii buŋŋu poon yii: <Gabriyeel, tùkù uninja nee dileedakal nee taapu.>

english_verse: Gabriel came over, and I fell to the ground in fear. Then he said, “You are merely a human, but you need to understand that this vision is about the end of time.”
translation_verse: Ní u nín dòoń laakin m sée. U tóobiń-mee ní m-pɔbil bíil̀ ní m tātìi dōoǹ kitiŋ dicincibil. Ní u tùkū-mi yii: <Nisaaleen, á béé yii dileedakal nee sá ŋyuntijoolkaa bɔti ní.>

english_verse: While he was speaking, I fell facedown in a deep sleep. But he lifted me to my feet
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun u bíi sòoǹ nì mee, ní m fìkī ki gbíntìi dɔ̄ dicincibil. Ní u gbēē-mi ní ki yōoǹ-mi kí síiǹ m-taaŋi pu.

english_verse: and said: Listen, and I will tell you what will happen at the end of time, when God has chosen to show his anger.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u tùkū-mi yii: <M làá yàntī á béé tin làá dāá dāan̄ Unimbɔti ŋuul boonee, di sá yii bi síiǹ ŋyunti ŋun ní tikɔkɔ làá kúntée.

english_verse: The two horns of the ram are the kings of Media and Persia,
translation_verse: Upìja un a ká u cáá iyin ilee sá Meedeesi nì Peeriisi yab bɔtiibi ní.

english_verse: the goat is the kingdom of Greece, and the powerful horn between his eyes is the first of its kings.
translation_verse: Uŋɔja un bàà cáá tikuti sùuuyee, Greesi bɔtiu dee. Ŋyiŋkpaan ŋun bí u-nimbiliŋ kansikinee, ubɔtipeekaa dee.

english_verse: After this horn is broken, four other kingdoms will appear, but they won't be as strong.
translation_verse: Ŋyinee nín gíìyee, inaa in nyáń ki téeǹ ŋu-yil puee sá abee anaa ŋin làá dāá nyā ditimbundee poonee ní, ama ŋaa làá dāá ká ŋu-pɔŋŋu juti.

english_verse: When these rulers have become as evil as possible, their power will end, and then a king who is dangerous and cannot be trusted will appear.
translation_verse: Abee gbanti yaa láa kúntì ní binikpitib mun kpitii yaa láa wíiǹee, ubɔti un dāa cáá dilambil ki nyí diŋmatindee làá dāá nyā.

english_verse: He will gain strength, but not on his own, and he will cause terrible destruction. He will wipe out powerful leaders and God's people as well.
translation_verse: U-pɔŋŋu làá dāá nīn wīintí ní ki cá, ama mpɔnee kaa dāa nyēeń u-cee. U làá dāá ŋá asaluu tikpil ní tin kɔkɔ u dāa ŋáańee dāa bútí-u. U làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí bipɔndambi nì circir nibul gba.

english_verse: His deceitful lies will make him so successful, that he will think he is really great. Suddenly he will kill many people, and he will even attack God, the Supreme Ruler. But God will crush him!
translation_verse: U nín dāa ŋūǹ ki yáb̀ puee, u làá dāá ŋmàtiǹ binib tikpil. U-lambil poonee, u làá dāá kpɔ̀ binib bin dàkafī yii bi bí ŋgbansɔŋfinee, ní kí dāá yīkì kí já nì abɔtibil kɔkɔ kpiliu. Ama ubɔ kaa làá dāá gbēē-u ní án nàan̄-u.

english_verse: This vision about the evenings and mornings is true, but these things won't happen for a long time, so don't tell it to others.
translation_verse: An yaa sá bi nín sòon̄ kujoou nì kutaafaau leedakal poon puee, an sá tiŋman ní. Siiyee, kpāafì dileedakal gbanti dibalin, kun puee dì sòoǹ ŋyunti ŋun dá láá dátèe pu ní.>

english_verse: After this, I was so worn out and weak that it was several days before I could get out of bed and go about my duties for the king. I was disturbed by this vision that made no sense to me.
translation_verse: Niinee, mama Daniyeel, m-wunti kpíì ní m búŋkì iwiin kupaau. Míǹ boonee ní m yíkì ki bíi tūǹ ubɔti tundi. Dileedakalee bɔti nìn páb́-mi tikpil, di sá yii maa nìn gbìl̀ di-taapu.»

english_verse: Daniel wrote: Some years later, Darius the Mede, who was the son of Xerxes, had become king of Babylonia. And during his first year as king, I found out from studying the writings of the prophets that the Lord had said to Jeremiah, “Jerusalem will lie in ruins for
translation_verse: mama Daniyeel, m nyàab̄ tigbɔn poon kí béé abin ŋin nyɔkɔm Jeerusaleem làá nīn gbíntìi sá adigbuŋkati, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii puee. An nìn nyáń abin imuŋku ita nì saalaa ní.

english_verse: Then, to show my sorrow, I went without eating and dressed in sackcloth and sat in ashes. I confessed my sins and earnestly prayed to the Lord my God: Our Lord, you are a great and fearsome God, and you faithfully keep your agreement with those who love and obey you.
translation_verse: M nìn mēē ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu ní ki nìn bīitì ti-kpitii pu ki lī yii: «Áù, ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti un sá ukpaan ki sá kuwambiiuee, a ŋúb̀ a-poondi din a pōoǹ bin ŋúb́ a-marabee, ki néeń bin néeń-see.

english_verse: But we have sinned terribly by rebelling against you and rejecting your laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ti ŋá ikpiti, ti yīntì, ti ŋá tin kaa kítèe ki jáń nì si. Ti fātì ti-boon ki tīī a-marab nì a-bɔkpaaŋi.

english_verse: We have ignored the message your servants the prophets spoke to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and everyone else.
translation_verse: Taa pílifiǹ a-tɔntɔnliibi, a-bɔnaatiliibi. Bi sòon̄ ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-kpilib nì ti-baabi nì ti-tiŋki pu nib kɔkɔ a-yindi pu.

english_verse: and even our kings, our officials, and our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, icoo jíń ti nì ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-kpilib nì ti-baabi, kun puee ti yīntiǹ-si.

english_verse: Lord God, you are merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against you
translation_verse: Ama sii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu poon mɔ̄ ní a pūǹ ti-kpitii, min kamaa ti yíkì ki jáń nì see.

english_verse: and rejected your teachings that came to us from your servants the prophets.
translation_verse: Taa pílifiǹ sii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ kí nóó a nín dī a-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi pu ki tīī-ti marab biŋyee.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel has stubbornly refused to obey your laws, and so those curses written by your servant Moses have fallen upon us.
translation_verse: Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ yīntì a-marau. Bi fātì bi-boon ki tīī-si kaa pílifiǹ-si. Ti yīntiǹ sii ti-Nimbɔtiu. Niinee mbusub bin kɔkɔ bi nìn ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi marabinee jéetì ti-pu.

english_verse: You warned us and our leaders that Jerusalem would suffer the worst disaster in human history, and you did exactly as you had threatened.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti, a yāntì tin a nìn pée sòon̄ yii án làá bàń ti nì ti-kpilib bin kpòotī-tee bāań. A yāntì nnaabukpaan jéetì ti-pu Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Ubɔ kaa láá pée ká nnaabu gbanti juti kitiŋ pu doo laaba.

english_verse: We have not escaped any of the terrible curses written by Moses, and yet we have refused to beg you for mercy and to remind ourselves of how faithful you have always been.
translation_verse: Kii an nín pée ŋmàn̄ Mooyiisi marab poon puee, míǹ ní nnaabu nee jéetì ti-pu. Ama timbi kaa gbāam̀ sii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu yii á sɔ̀ŋkì a-pɔbil, tí bàà dū ti-kpitii kí fá kí nyàab̀ kí nīn nóó ibaamɔn.

english_verse: And when you finally punished us with this horrible disaster, that was also the right thing to do, because we deserved it so much.
translation_verse: An pu ní sii ti-Dindaan yāntì nnaabu nee jéetì ti-pu, di sá yii sii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu bí deedee a-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon ní, ama timbi kaa pílifiǹ-si.

english_verse: Our Lord God, with your own mighty arm you rescued us from Egypt and made yourself famous to this very day, but we have sinned terribly.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, a nín nìn dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu ki nyántì a-nibul Eejipiti tiŋkinee, a nyáń diyindi ki dāa sāā díǹ. Ama ti ŋá ikpiti, ki ŋá tin kaa kítèe.

english_verse: In the past, you treated us with such kindness, that we now beg you to stop being so terribly angry with Jerusalem. After all, it is your chosen city built on your holy mountain, even though it has suffered public disgrace because of our sins and those of our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a-deedeeu puee, páatí a-ŋuukpaandi Jeerusaleem, a-tiŋki, a-circir jool pu. Di sá yii ti-kpitii nì ti-baabi yìntitam puee, bin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-tee sìí Jeerusaleem nì a-nibul.

english_verse: I am your servant, Lord God, and I beg you to answer my prayers and bring honor to yourself by having pity on your temple that lies in ruins.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, m-Nimbɔtiu, á pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu wimmeem nì u-gbaamii. Sii a-ba yindi puee, m-Dindaan, sɔ̄ a-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun bi bíil̀ee saai.

english_verse: Forgive us! Hurry and do something, not only for your city and your chosen people, but to bring honor to yourself. The Seventy Weeks Daniel wrote:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, pīlifì-ti! Ti-Dindaan, dūú pɔ̄-ti! Ti-Dindaan, pīlifì soooo! A-yindi puee, m-Nimbɔtiu, jòoń a-tiŋki nì a-nibul.» Nnyɔmu imuŋku ita nì saalaa taapu

english_verse: I was still confessing my sins and those of all Israel to the Lord my God, and I was praying for the good of his holy mountain,
translation_verse: «M nìn gbíntìi bíi mèé m-kpitii nì m-nibul Isirayeel yab kpitii pu, ki gbàam̄ ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu ú sɔ̀ u-circir jool saai.

english_verse: when Gabriel suddenly came flying in at the time of the evening sacrifice. This was the same Gabriel I had seen in my vision,
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun m gbíntìi bíi mèéyee, ntuun Gabriyeel un m bàà pée ká dileedakal poonee, ŋàan̄ní malaa malaa ki bāań m-cee. An nìn sá ŋyunti ŋun bi ŋáań kujoou saraauee ní.

english_verse: and he explained: Daniel, I am here to help you understand the vision.
translation_verse: Ní ŋu sòon̄ nì mi ki bí-mi yii: <M dɔ́miń kí yàntī á ŋmā kí gbìl̄ tibɔti taapu ní.

english_verse: God thinks highly of you, and at the very moment you started praying, I was sent to give you the answer.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun a kíĺ ki bíi gbàam̄ Unimbɔtee ní u sòon̄ tibɔti tiba ní m dɔ́miń kí dūú tùkù-si, di sá yii u néeń-si. Míǹ puee á gbìl̄ tin m làá tùkù-si nee tiŋan kí béé dileedakal nee taapu.

english_verse: For one week this foreigner will make a firm agreement with many people, and halfway through this week, he will end all sacrifices and offerings. Then the “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction will be put there. And it will stay there until the time God has decided to destroy this one who destroys.
translation_verse: Ukpilee làá dāá dū mpɔn kí ŋá mpèé nì binib tikpil abin aluli. Abin ata nì dijandee, u làá dāá kúntí tiwaŋkuti nì tijimpin saraabi. Unàanlee làá dāá tɔ̄ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi malaa kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun án làá nàan̄ úǹ u-bee, kii an nín sòon̄ pu ki síiǹee.>»

english_verse: In the third year of Cyrus the king of Persia, a message came to Daniel from God, and it was explained in a vision. The message was about a dreadful war, and it was true.
translation_verse: Peeriisi bɔtiu Siirusi nín kāl̀ dibeel dibintataatiil poonee, ní an lēē ki dàkā Daniyeel un bi gíti páaǹ diyindi yii Baltasaaree. Dinyɔɔbundee nìn sá mbaamɔn ní ki nìn sòoǹ agìŋ́kpaan pu. Daniyeel nìn dākafì tibɔtee pu tikpil ní án lēē ki dàkā-u ní u gbìl̄ taapu.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: For three weeks I was in sorrow.
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti gbantee, mama Daniyeel, m nìn kɔ́ kunimbaaun nnyɔmu muta ní.

english_verse: I ate no fancy food or meat, I drank no wine, and I put no olive oil on my face or hair.
translation_verse: Maa nìn jíń tijimmɔntiil tibaaa, tinan nì ndaam kaa nìn kɔ́ m-nyɔkɔnaaa, maa nìn càatī mun gba áli nnyɔmu muta gbanti dāa jítì.

english_verse: Then, on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing on the banks of the great Tigris River,
translation_verse: Dibindi ŋmapeekaau, iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dalee, m nìn bí dimɔɔl din bi yíì Tiigiree gbandi.

english_verse: when I looked up and saw someone dressed in linen and wearing a solid gold belt.
translation_verse: M yáatì ki kpēēyee, uninja ubɔ dee. U pēē ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee bɔkutil ki gbìn̄ sindaariyamɔnti dambalau.

english_verse: His body was like a precious stone, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming fires, his arms and legs like polished bronze, and his voice like the roar of a crowd.
translation_verse: U-wunti nìn bí kii ditaŋkpamɔntiil disɔndi din bi yíì kriistooliitee, ní u-nimbiin jìl̀ kii utaa nín ŋmóò puee. U-nimbiliŋ nìn bí kii iŋminaapoolee, ní u-ŋalii nì u-taaŋi bí kii tasa kúti tin bi jɔ̄lifèe nín bí puee. U yaa sòoǹee, an bí kii kunipaauee ní.

english_verse: Although the people who were with me did not see the vision, they became so frightened that they scattered and hid.
translation_verse: Mama, Daniyeel baba ní an nìn pée lēē ki dàkā. Binib bin nìn bí m-ceeyee kaa nìn wál̀ tiba, ama tifaandi nìn kɔ́-bi ní bi sáǹ ki bál̀.

english_verse: and at the sound of his voice, I fell facedown in a deep sleep.
translation_verse: M nìn gbìl̄ kijapaayee bíi sòoǹ. Ŋyunti ŋun m gbìl̄ u-nyɔkɔ puee ní m fìkī ní ki lítì kitiŋ dicincibil.

english_verse: and then said, “Daniel, your God thinks highly of you, and he has sent me. So stand up and pay close attention.” I stood trembling, while the angel said:
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní u tùkū-mi yii: <Daniyeel, sii un ní Unimbɔti néeńee, gbìl̄ tibɔti tin m làá tùkù-si nee taapu. Yīkìí yūĺ, kun puee sii cee ní bi túnní-mi.> Ŋyunti ŋun u sòon̄ nì mi mimmee, ní m yíkìi yúl̀ tiwun gbíntìi jìkì.

english_verse: Daniel, don't be afraid! God has listened to your prayers since the first day you humbly asked for understanding, and he has sent me here.
translation_verse: Ní u gíti bí-mi yii: <Daniyeel, taa fàŋkì, di sá yii kí yòon̄ ŋwimpeekaa dal ŋun ní a lēē a-pɔbilin kí sìntī a-ba taapu kí tīī Unimbɔti kí gbìl̄ tin bíi jītée taapuee, Unimbɔti nìn gbìl̄ a-wimmeem, ní a-wimmeem gbanti pu ní m dɔ́miń.

english_verse: I will tell you what is written in The Book of Truth. But first, you must realize that no one except Michael, the guardian angel of Israel, is on my side.
translation_verse: Ama m làá tùkù-si tin bi ŋmàn̄ an kā ibaamɔn gbɔŋku poonee. Ubɔ kaa pée bí kí bɔ̄-mi ŋŋal ḿ já nì bi, asee Miikayeel, ntuun ŋun cí-nee baba.

english_verse: Now I have come here to give you another vision about what will happen to your people in the future.
translation_verse: Too, kɔŋkɔnnee m dɔ́miń kí yàntī á gbìl̄ tin làá bàń a-nibul pu fool boonee taapu ní, di sá yii iyunti gbanti pu leedakal diba gíti bí.>

english_verse: While this angel was speaking to me, I stared at the ground, speechless.
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti ŋun u bíi sòoǹ nì mi mimmee ní m tīntì m-yil ki kíǹ ki kpèé kitiŋ ki ŋmí.

english_verse: Then he appeared in human form and touched my lips. I said, “Sir, this vision has brought me great pain and has drained my strength.
translation_verse: Ama unaaciin ubɔ, u bí kii unilee dɔ́miń ki gbēē m-nyunculiŋ. Niinee m wāaǹ m-nyɔkɔ ní ki kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ. Ní m bí un yú m-nimbiinee yii: <M-dindaan, dileedakal nee puee, kunimbaau kɔ́-mi ní m-wunti kpíì.

english_verse: I am merely your servant. How can I possibly speak with someone so powerful, when I am almost too weak to get my breath?”
translation_verse: Mana ní mama, a-tɔntɔnliu ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ nì si, m-dindaan, ŋyunti ŋun ní maa ti cáá mpɔnaaa, kaa ti cáá ŋfam muee?>

english_verse: The angel touched me a second time and said, “Don't be frightened! God thinks highly of you, and he intends this for your good, so be brave and strong.” At this, I regained my strength and replied, “Please speak! You have already made me feel much better.”
translation_verse: ní ki bí-mi yii: <Taa fàŋkì, sii un ní Unimbɔti néeńee. Ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí a-cee! Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká kunyannyaau.> Ŋyunti ŋun u bíi sòoǹ nì mi mimmee ní m ká mpɔn ní ki bí-u yii: <M-dindaan, a ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ kɔŋkɔnnee, di sá yii a tīī-mi mpɔn.>

english_verse: Then the angel said: Now do you understand why I have come? Soon I must leave to fight against the guardian angel of Persia. Then after I have defeated him, the guardian angel of Greece will attack me.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-mi yii: <A nyí kun pu m dɔ́miń a-ceeyeeee? M làá fàtīí gítí kɔŋkɔnnee ki já nì ntuun ŋun cí Peeriisi tiŋkee. M yaa búntèe, ntuun ŋun cí Greesi tiŋkee mun làá dāan̄.

english_verse: You also need to know that I protected and helped Darius the Mede in his first year as king. The Angel's Message to Daniel Part One: The Four Kings and Their Successors
translation_verse: «Úǹ ní mama m-ba nìn bɔ́ ŋŋal ki tútúǹ-u Daariyusi, umeedija nín kāl̀ dibeelee bimpeepeekaal poon.

english_verse: What I am going to tell you is certain to happen. Four kings will rule Persia, one after the other, but the fourth one will become much richer than the others. In fact, his wealth will make him so powerful that he will turn everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, m làá tùkù-si mbaamɔn. Ŋgan nì ŋgiil pú bɔtiibi jaaku «Bibɔtiibi bita láa gíti kàl̄ Peeriisi tiŋki pu dibeel. Bíǹ boonee, unanaati làá kàl̄ ní kí kóoǹ tigaajati tikpil kí kpāafì kí jītíǹ bipeepeekaabee kɔkɔ. U-gaajatee yaa láa yāntì u ká mpɔnee, u làá dāá yīkì kí bóob́ Greesi tiŋki pu dikɔ̀ndi.

english_verse: Then a mighty king will come to power and will be able to do whatever he pleases.
translation_verse: Ama ubɔti un cáá dibaatandee làá dāá kàl̄ Greesi tiŋki pu. Kitiŋ kin u làá dāá nīn kpòotēe làá dāá nīn wāā, ní u dāa ŋáań u nín là puee.

english_verse: But suddenly his kingdom will be crushed and scattered to the four corners of the earth, where four more kingdoms will rise. But these won't be ruled by his descendants or be as powerful as his kingdom.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, u yaa láa kāl̀ dibeel ki cúú mpɔnee ní u-beel gbanti ń dāá wīī kí yàkatī minaa pu kitiŋ jannaatiliŋ kɔkɔ pu. U-naantiibi kaa làá dāá fōō u-yil kí kàl̄ dibeel. Bi làá dāá fōō dibeel u-ŋaan kí tīī biba fám, ama bíǹ kaa làá dāá ká u-pɔŋŋu juti.

english_verse: The king of the south will grow powerful. Then one of his generals will rebel and will rule an even larger kingdom.
translation_verse: «Ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiu làá dāá ká mpɔn. Ama u-janjakpilib kansikin ubɔ làá dāá nīn cáá mpɔn ki jítiǹ-u ní u-beel ń dāá nīn jítiǹ úǹ yal.

english_verse: Years later the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom will make a treaty, and the daughter of the king of the south will marry the king of the north. But she will lose her power. Then she, her husband, their child, and the servants who came with her will all be killed. After this,
translation_verse: Abin aba boonee ní bí dāá ŋá mpèé. Ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu bisal làá dāá mɔ̄ǹ ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiu kí dàkà mpèé ŋun bí bi-kansikinee, ama waa làá ŋmā kí ká mpɔn kí tin kátí-ku. U-cal u-ba kaa làá ŋmátí, kibiki kin bi màl̄ee mun làá kpú. U làá kpú kí kpáaǹ u-baa nì u-cal nì bin cūnnì-u niinee.

english_verse: one of her relatives will become the ruler of the southern kingdom. He will attack the army of the northern kingdom and capture its fortresses.
translation_verse: U-dicaŋku poon ubɔ làá dāá fōō u-baa yil ní kí bóob́ ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu pu dikɔ̀ndi. U làá dāá ŋmā kí kɔ́ ubɔtee tiŋki kin bi máń digundi ki māntìi túee poon kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u.

english_verse: Then he will carry their idols to Egypt, together with their precious treasures of silver and gold, but it will be a long time before he attacks the northern kingdom again. Some years later
translation_verse: U làá dāá yòon̄ bi-waaŋi nì bi-gaajawammɔntiiti tin sá animbil kúti nì sindaariyee kí kpáàá cùnnì Eejipiti tiŋkin. Míǹ boon abiŋkaaŋkaa poonee, waa làá ti táká ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiu.

english_verse: the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom, but he will be forced back to his own country.
translation_verse: Ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu làá dāá cù ŋgan pú tiŋkin ní boonee kí dāá fàtīí gítí úǹ u-ba tiŋkin.

english_verse: The sons of the king of the north will gather a huge army that will sweep down like a roaring flood, reaching all the way to the fortress of the southern kingdom.
translation_verse: «Ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu jipɔmbi làá dāá bɔ́ntí kujaau ní kí dāá kóoǹ ajanjakiti tikpil kí kpāfì. U-jipɔmbee kansikin ubɔ làá dāá yīkì u nì u-janjakitil kí jītí kitiŋ kpaanyɔkɔ kii mbun ŋun gbée. U yaa fàtīi kùǹee, u làá já nì unannanli timmu mun bi máń digundi ki túee kiba.

english_verse: But this will make the king of the south angry, and he will defeat this large army from the north.
translation_verse: Niinee ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu làá gíí diŋuul ní kí cùú já nì ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiu. Ubɔti gbanti làá dāá kóoǹ ajanjakiti kupaau kí kpāfì, ama ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu làá dāá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-ŋi.

english_verse: The king of the south will feel proud because of the many thousands he has killed. But his victories won't last long,
translation_verse: U yaa láa pée jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bee, ní ú dāá kɔ́ dilambilin. U làá dāá kpɔ̀ bijanjaliibi kutukub kutukub, ama waa làá já kí jī.

english_verse: because the king of the north will gather a larger and more powerful army than ever before. Then in a few years, he will start invading other countries.
translation_verse: Ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiu làá dāá fàtīí kóoǹ ajanjakiti ŋin wīikí ki jítiǹ apeepeekaayee kí kpāfì. Abiŋkaaŋkaa aba boonee, u làá fàtīí gítiń nì dijanjakitikpaandi gbanti nì tijanjawan tikpil.

english_verse: At this time many of your own people will try to make this vision come true by rebelling against the king of the south, but their rebellion will fail.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, binib tikpil làá dāá yīkì kí já nì ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu. Daniyeel, ki kpáaǹ a-nibul kansikin, binib bin néeń tipɔmbɔtee làá dāá já nì u. Bi làá nyàab̀ kí bàà ŋá kii an nín sòon̄ dileedakal diban puee, ama baa làá dāá ŋmā-u.

english_verse: Then the army from the north will surround and capture a fortress in the south, and not even the most experienced troops of the southern kingdom will be able to make them retreat.
translation_verse: Ŋgan pú bɔtiu làá dāá já nì kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee. Bi làá dāá cáań ntam kí kpúkuń digundi boon kí ŋmā kí tɔ́kɔń kí já nì kì. Ŋgan pú bɔtiu janjaliibi kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí yūĺ u-nimbiin, ki kpáaǹ u-janjaliibi bin tòó kaa lántée. Baa làá dāá ká mpɔn kí yūĺ kí já.

english_verse: The king who invaded from the north will do as he pleases, and he will even capture and destroy the holy land.
translation_verse: Ŋgan pú bɔtiu gbantee dāa ŋáań u nín là puee ní, ní ubɔ mun kaa dāa bí kí yūĺ u-nimbiin. U dāa bí kitinnyaaŋŋin ní ki ŋúb́ dinàandi pɔŋŋu u-ŋaan.

english_verse: In fact, he will decide to invade the south with his entire army. Then he will attempt to make peace by giving the king of the south a bride from the northern kingdom, but this won't be successful.
translation_verse: U làá dāá cù ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu cee nì u-beel pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ. U làá dāá dū u-bisal kí tīī-u ticati ki bàà dàkafī yii án nàan̄-u, ama án kaa làá ŋá kii u nín bàà dàkafī puee.

english_verse: Afterwards, this proud king of the north will invade and conquer many of the nations along the coast, but a military leader will defeat him and make him lose his pride.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ú fàtī u-nimbikpeeŋu kí túĺ ntimu mun dɔ̄ dimɔɔgbandee ní kí já kí fōō mu-kansikin tikpil. Ama ujanjakpil ubɔ un sá unicaanee làá dāá kúntí u-lambil, ní kí yàntī u-bimbim gìŋ́ŋi ń lítí u-pu.

english_verse: He will retreat to his fortresses in his own country, but on the way he will be defeated and never again be seen.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ú dāá fàtīí gítí u-timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee poon, ama u làá dāá gbéetí kí lítí ní baa ti làá ká-u.

english_verse: The next king of the north will try to collect taxes for the glory of his kingdom. However, he will come to a sudden end in some mysterious way, instead of in battle or because of someone's anger. Part Two: The Evil King from the North
translation_verse: Un làá dāá fōō u-yilee làá dāá tɔ̄ń ubɔ ú fūkul̀ dibeel poon kudii kun pée ŋān̄ee. Ama iwiŋkaaŋkaa boonee, bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ ubɔti gbanti, an kaa dāa sá kujaaun, ama dibalin.

english_verse: The successor of this king of the north will be a worthless nobody, who doesn't even come from a royal family. He will suddenly appear and gain control of the kingdom by treachery.
translation_verse: «Un baa pée dūu yíiń tiba baa kāaǹ dibeelee làá dāá fōō u-yil. Ŋgbansɔŋfi yuntiŋu ní u làá dāan̄ kí dū biibii kí fōō dibeel.

english_verse: Then he will destroy armies and remove God's chosen high priest.
translation_verse: Dijanjakitil diba kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u. U làá dāá nà bi-kɔkɔ ní kí kpáàa kpɔ̀ dipoondi nibul kpiliu ubɔ.

english_verse: He will make a treaty, but he will be deceitful and break it, even though he has only a few followers.
translation_verse: U làá dāá dī mpèé ŋun u nì bin kíǹee ŋée pu kí ŋmàtiǹ binib, ní u-pɔŋŋu dāa wīintí ki cá, min kamaa binib bin dī u-boonee kaa náaǹee.

english_verse: Without warning, he will successfully invade a wealthy province, which is something his ancestors never did. Then he will divide among his followers all of its treasures and property. But none of this will last very long.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ní kitiŋ bí ŋgbansɔŋfinee, u làá dāá cù ntimu mun cáá ntiŋkpamee poon kí ŋá tin ní u-baabi nì u-naanjab kaa nìn pée ŋá ki kée. U làá dāá fūkul̀ kitiŋee ní kí dū tin u fúkúl̀ee nì tigaajawan kí yàkatī u-naacimbi. U làá dāá màkan̄ gba kí já nì ntimu mun bi máń digundi ki túee. Ama tíǹ kaa làá yúntí.

english_verse: He will gather a large and powerful army, and with great courage he will attack the king of the south. The king of the south will meet him with a much stronger army, but he will lose the battle, because he will be betrayed
translation_verse: «U làá dāá nīn máká u-pɔŋŋu nì u-nyannyaaku pu ní kí dāá yòon̄ dijanjakitikpaandi diba kí cùú já nì ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu. Ubɔtee mun làá dāá yīkì kujaau pu nì dijanjakitil din sá dikpaandi ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋanee, ama waa làá dāá ŋmā kí yūĺ ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiu nimbiin, di sá yii bi làá dāá bɔ́ntí u-pu kí já nì u.

english_verse: by members of the royal court. He will be ruined, and most of his army will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: U nì bin dāa kpáfí ki jīǹ disambibaantiilinee di làá dāá dū-u kí nyāfì. Bi làá dāá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ u-janjakitil ní u-janjaliibi tikpil ń dāá kpú.

english_verse: The two kings will meet around a table and tell evil lies to each other. But their plans will fail, because God has already decided what will happen.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi bilee làá dāá nīn kā ki jīǹ disambibaantiil poon, ama, bi-pɔbiliŋ poonee, bi dāa nyàab̀ kí ŋá tɔb tikpitil. Bi dāa kā ní ki mɔ́ntí tɔb. Bi nín kāl̀ ki bóob́ puee kaa làá tɔ̄ ditundi, di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun bi síiǹee kaa láá bàn̄.

english_verse: Then the king of the north will return to his country with great treasures. But on the way, he will attack the religion of God's people and do whatever else he pleases.
translation_verse: Ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiuee làá dāá kpáaǹ tigaajawan tikpil kí gítí u-tiŋkin. U yaa kùǹee, u làá já nì dinibul din nì Unimbɔti ŋá dipoondee, kii u nín lēē u-pɔbilin puee. Míǹ boonee ní ú nīn nín kùǹ.

english_verse: At the time God has decided, the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom again, but this time, things will be different.
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti ŋun bi síiǹee yaa bàn̄ee, ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiu làá dāá gítí ŋgiil pú tiŋkin kí já nì kì, ama min bí nee, an kaa làá ŋá kii mpeepeekaaminee.

english_verse: Ships from the west will come to attack him, and he will be discouraged. Then he will start back to his own country and take out his anger on the religion of God's faithful people, while showing kindness to those who are unfaithful.
translation_verse: Binib làá nyānní ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ki kāń meelabin kí já nì u. U-wunti làá yɔ̀tī ní ú fàtīí nīn kùǹ. U làá dāá gíí diŋuul ŋkpitim pu ní kí dū u-ŋuul kí nyìntī dinibul din nì Unimbɔti ŋá dipoondee. U làá gbìl̄ kí tīī nì bin fá Unimbɔti poondee.

english_verse: He will send troops to pollute the temple and the fortress, and he will stop the daily sacrifices. Then he will set up that “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction.
translation_verse: U làá dāá tɔ̄ń u-janjaliibi bí dāá yūĺ digundi din māntìi tú kunimbɔtidiiyee. Bi làá dāá kɔ́ circir páaa laŋki kí kɔ́ǹ-kì tijɔkɔndi. Bi làá dāá kúntí saraa un bi ŋáań baabadal ki tìì Unimbɔtee ní kí dāá dū kuwaŋkpitiu kun cāabìń ntimbiilee kí síiń circir paaŋŋu pu.

english_verse: The king will use deceit to win followers from those who are unfaithful to God, but those who remain faithful will do everything possible to oppose him.
translation_verse: Ubɔti u-ba làá dāá dū biibii kí ŋmàtiǹ binib bí fá dipoondi. Ama dinibul poon bin nyí bi-Nimbɔtiuee làá dāá nīn ŋúb́ an píkí ní kí já nì u.

english_verse: Wise leaders will instruct many of the people. But for a while, some of these leaders will either be killed with swords or burned alive, or else robbed of their possessions and thrown into prison.
translation_verse: Bíǹ gbanti kansikinee, bin yaa láa cáá dinyilee di dāa dàkà binib tikpil. Ama iwiŋkaaŋkaa poonee, bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ biba ní kí wà biba mun ŋŋmi, ní kí cūtì biba kí tɔ̄ sarkan ní kí dāá gbākal̀ biba mun bi-gaajawanti kɔkɔ.

english_verse: They will receive only a little help in their time of trouble, and many of their followers will be treacherous.
translation_verse: Agìń yuntiŋu gbanti poonee, bi làá dāá pée ká dijòońdi fiii ní. Di sá yii binib tikpil làá dāá kūtì bi-pu nì mili mili pɔbil.

english_verse: Some of those who are wise will suffer, so that God will make them pure and acceptable until the end, which will still come at the time he has decided.
translation_verse: Biciŋfitiibi gbanti kansikin biba làá dāá kpú, án nín làá ŋá pu bi-kúmee ń fíntí Unimbɔti nibul kí ŋá-bi circir bí pīil̀ káŋkaŋ kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní tikɔkɔ làá kúntée, di sá yii ŋyuntijoolkaa kaa láá bāań.

english_verse: This king will do as he pleases. He will proudly claim to be greater than any god and will insult the only true God. Indeed, he will be successful until God is no longer angry with his people.
translation_verse: «Ubɔti làá dāá nīn ŋáań min ní u lèe. U làá dāá yòon̄ u-ba yilpu ní ki dāa dàkafī yii u jítiǹ awaa kɔkɔ gba. U làá dāá sòoǹ nì inimbɔti kɔkɔ Nimbɔtiu tibɔti tin baa máaǹ kí sòoǹee. Án làá dāá bútí-u kí cáá sāā Unimbɔti ŋuul dal. Niinee ní Unimbɔti ń ŋá tin u sòon̄ ki síiǹee.

english_verse: This king will reject the gods his ancestors worshiped and the god preferred by women. In fact, he will put himself above all gods
translation_verse: Ubɔtee kaa dāa fātìi tɔ́ awaa ŋin u-baabi nìn tòotēeyaaa, kaa dāa fātìi tɔ́ ŋin binimpoobi néeń ki jáaḿee. Waa dāa pée fātìi tɔ́ diwaal dibaba gba, di sá yii u làá dāá pée yòon̄ u-ba kí tɔ́kɔń tikɔkɔ nì tikɔkɔ pu ní.

english_verse: and worship only the so-called god of fortresses, who was unknown to his ancestors. And he will honor it with gold, silver, precious stones, and other costly gifts.
translation_verse: Awaa gbanti paaŋŋuee, u làá dāá nīn tìì diwaal din cí ntimuee tinyool, diwaal din u-naanjab kaa pée nyí ki kée. U dāa dù sindaariya nì animbil nì ataŋkpamɔnti nì tiwan tin cáá kudapɔɔuee ní kí ŋá-dì saraa.

english_verse: With the help of this foreign god, he will capture the strongest fortresses. Everyone who worships this god will be put in a position of power and rewarded with wealth and land. Part Three: The Time of the End
translation_verse: U làá dāá já nì ntimu mun bi máń digundi ki túee nì diwaacandi gbanti tūtuntam. U làá dāá tīī bin kíí kí jāam̀-dèe tinyool, ní kí dāá dū-bi kí kàan̄ binib tikpil pu bí nīn sá bi-kpootiliibi, ní kí dāá pɔ̄-bi ntimu án nīn sá bi-paatii.

english_verse: At the time of the end, the king of the south will attack the kingdom of the north. But its king will rush out like a storm with war chariots, cavalry, and many ships. Indeed, his forces will flood one country after another,
translation_verse: «Ŋyuntijoolkaa poonee, ŋgiil pú tiŋki bɔtiu làá dāá yīkì kí já nì ŋgan pú tiŋki bɔtiu. Ama úǹ dāa yíkí kí bīikì u-pu nì kujaau tɔrɔkub nì u-janjaliibi bin jàkà itaamuee nì meelab tikpil. U làá dāá kɔ́ ntimun ní kí kpátíí gbí an kɔkɔ.

english_verse: and when they reach the holy land, tens of thousands will be killed. But the countries of Edom and Moab and the ruler of Ammon will escape.
translation_verse: U làá dāá kɔ́ kitinnyaaŋŋi poon ní binib tikpil làá dāá kpú. Bin làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā u-ŋaanee di sá Eedoom yab nì Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab kpilib.

english_verse: The king of the north will invade many countries, including Egypt,
translation_verse: Ntimu mubɔ mun làá dāá kɔ́ u-ŋaan, ki kpáaǹ Eejipiti tiŋki gba kaa làá ŋmátí kí nyā u-ŋaan.

english_verse: and he will take its rich treasures of gold and silver. He will also conquer Libya and Ethiopia.
translation_verse: U làá dāá fōō Eejipiti gaajawanti kɔkɔ, an dàkà yii sindaariya nì animbil nì tin kɔkɔ pée pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee. Liibii yab nì Eetiiyoopii yab làá dāá nīn bí u-taapu.

english_verse: But he will be alarmed by news from the east and the north, and he will become furious and cause great destruction.
translation_verse: Ama u làá dāá gbìl̄ tin bíi jītí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì ŋgan púee ní tifaandi ń cúú-u. U làá dāá gíí diŋuul ŋkpitim pu ní kí búntí kí cùú kpɔ̀ kí céetí binib tikpil.

english_verse: After this, he will set up camp between the Mediterranean Sea and Mount Zion. Then he will be destroyed, and no one will be able to save him.
translation_verse: U làá dāá gāā u-beecindi tantib tiŋku nì kitinnyaaŋŋi circir jool kansikin. Niin ní u làá kpú, ní ubɔ dāa kpá kí jòoń-u.>»

english_verse: Many of those who lie dead in the ground will rise from death. Some of them will be given eternal life, and others will receive nothing but eternal shame and disgrace.
translation_verse: Binib tikpil bin kpántì ntam ki dɔ̄ dikaakulin ki gèeǹee làá dāá fìntī, ní bi-kansikin biba ń kɔ́ dimaŋfal din kaa cáá dikúntilee poon, ní bin kíǹee ń dāá kɔ́ icoo nì nnaabu ŋun kaa cáá dikúntilee poon.

english_verse: Everyone who has been wise will shine as bright as the sky above, and everyone who has led others to please God will shine forever like the stars.
translation_verse: Binib bin cáá dinyilee dāa jìl̀ ní pàlpal kii kutagbɔŋuee. Bin yaa dàkā binib tikpil bi kpántì deedeedambee, bi dāa jìl̀ kii iŋmalbijaayee ní ki cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: Daniel, I now command you to keep the message of this book secret until the end of time, even though many people will go everywhere, searching for the knowledge to be found in it. The End of Time
translation_verse: «<Sii, Daniyeel, á kpāafì tibɔti nee dibalin kí kpáb́ kugbɔŋu nee kí cáá sāā ŋyuntijoolkaa. Tikpil làá dāá kàaǹ kugbɔŋu gbanti ní bi-nyil ń wíiǹ.>» Ŋyuntijoolkaa bɔti sá tibɔbalkaal ní

english_verse: Daniel wrote: I looked around and saw two other people—one on this side of the river and one on the other side.
translation_verse: «Mama Daniyeel, m bíi kpèéyee ní ki ká binib bili biba nyáń ki yú. Ubɔ yú dibuŋgbándi diba pu, ní un kíǹee mun yú dibuŋgbándi din kíǹee pu.

english_verse: The angel who had spoken to me was dressed in linen and was standing upstream from them. So one of the two beside the river asked him, “How long before these amazing things happen?”
translation_verse: Ní bi-kansikin ubɔ bí uninja un pēē ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee bɔkutil ki tɔ́kɔ́ mbunee nyim puee yii: <Ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní maamaaci tuuŋŋi nee làá nín kúntí dee?>

english_verse: The angel then raised both hands toward heaven and said, “In the name of the God who lives forever, I solemnly promise that it will be a time, two times, and half a time. Everything will be over, when the suffering of God's holy people comes to an end.”
translation_verse: Ní uninja un pēē ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee bɔkutil ki bàà tɔ́kɔ́ mbunee nyim puee yōoǹ u-ŋaŋgiil nì u-ŋaŋgan ki túĺ yilpu ní m gbìl̄ u lī yii: <M pūtì Unimbɔti un bí ki cá jaanjaanee yii atuun gbanti làá ŋá abin ata nì dijandi ní kí nín kúntí. Unimbɔti nibul pɔŋŋu yaa láa nāaǹ kɔkɔ múbuee ní tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ làá kúntí.>

english_verse: I heard what the angel said, but I didn't understand. So I asked, “Sir, how will it all end?” The angel in my vision then replied:
translation_verse: «M gbìl̄ tin bi sòon̄ee ama ní kaa gbìl̄ ti-taapu. An pu ní m bālifì yii: <M-dindaan, tin bí nee kɔkɔ làá dāá pée kúntí nì mana dee?>

english_verse: Daniel, go about your business, because the meaning of this message will remain secret until the end of time.
translation_verse: Ní u kíí-mi yii: <Nín̄ cá, Daniyeel, di sá yii tibɔti nee sá bí kpāafì-tì dibalin án nīn kpáb́ ki bīī múlmul kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní tikɔkɔ làá kúntée ní.

english_verse: Many people will have their hearts and lives made pure and clean, but those who are evil will keep on being evil and never understand. Only the wise will understand.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá fíntí binib tikpil kí ŋá-bi circir bí nīn pīiǹ káŋkaŋ. Binikpitib kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí gbìl̄ taapu ní ki dāa nìkì ki ŋáań ikpiti, ama binyiliibi bíǹ dāa gbìl̀ taapu.

english_verse: So, Daniel, be faithful until the end! You will rest, and at the end of time, you will rise from death to receive your reward.
translation_verse: Sii Daniyeel, á pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí tin kátí-ku. A làá dāá ŋùŋfì ní kí dāá yīkì kí fōō a-paati iyuntijoolkaa dal.>»

english_verse: I am Hosea son of Beeri. When Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah, and when Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel, the Lord spoke this message to me. Hosea's Family
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Beerii jipɔɔn Ooseeya iyunti in ní Oosiyasi nì Yootam nì Akaasi nì Eeseekiyaasi nìn kāl̀ kāl̀ Juuda beel pu dibeelee. Iyunti gbanti ibaanti poon ní Joowaasi jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam mun nìn kāl̀ Isirayeel beel pu dibeel. Ooseeya nimpuu nì u-biyaamu bɔti

english_verse: So I married Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, and we had a son.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Ooseeya cáab́ Diibilayiim bisal Goomeer ní Goomeer cáá dipool ki màl̄-u kibininjabiki.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Hosea, name your son Jezreel, because I will soon punish the descendants of King Jehu of Israel for the murders he committed in Jezreel Valley. I will destroy his kingdom,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Ooseeya yii: «Pɔ̄ kibikee diyindi yii Jisirayeel, di sá yii an kaa ti làá yúntí, Jeewuu nín kūū binib bin Jisirayeel tantakalinee puee, m làá dáaĺ u-naantiibi tafal ní kí kúntí Isirayeel beel.

english_verse: and in Jezreel Valley I will break the power of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, m làá dāá kɔ̄fì Isirayeel tɔbu Jisirayeel tantakalin.»

english_verse: Later, Gomer had a daughter, and the Lord said, “Name her Lo-Ruhamah, because I will no longer have mercy and forgive Israel.
translation_verse: Ní Goomeer gíti cáá dipool ní ki màl̄ kibinimpubiki ní ti-Dindaan bí Ooseeya yii: «Pɔ̄ kibikee diyindi yii Loo Ruwama, taapu di sá yii, Baa Là-mi, di sá yii maa ti làá dàkà Isirayeel beel yab dineendi, maa ti làá nīn pée néeń-bi.

english_verse: But I am the Lord God of Judah, and I will have mercy and save Judah by my own power—not by wars and arrows or swords and cavalry.”
translation_verse: Ama m làá nīn néeń Juuda yab. Man di sá bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu, m làá fīī-bi, ama kaa sá nì butɔbu àá kitàataajiki àá tijanjawan tin kíǹee àá nì itaamu àá nì bitanjakaliibi.»

english_verse: After Gomer had stopped nursing Lo-Ruhamah, she had another son.
translation_verse: Goomeer gíí Loo-Ruwama dibiil boonee ní ki tí cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Name him Lo-Ammi, because these people are not mine, and I am not their God.” Hope for Israel
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí Ooseeya yii: «Pɔ̄ kibikee diyindi yii Loo-Amii, an dàkà yii naa sá m-nibul. Di sá yii naa ti sá m-nibul ní ma mun kaa ti sá ni-Nimbɔtiu.»

english_verse: So let your brothers be called “My People” and your sisters be called “Shown Mercy.” The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
translation_verse: Ama Isirayeel yab làá dāá nīn wīikí kii tiŋku gbandi bul din baa ŋūǹ kí ŋmàntāaa, kaa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹee ní. Laakin ní Unimbɔti nìn tùkū-bi yii: «Naa ti sá m-nibulee», niin ubaanti ní u làá dāá yíiń-bi yii: «Dimaŋfal Nimbɔtiu biyaamu.»

english_verse: Accuse! Accuse your mother! She is no longer my wife, and now I, the Lord, am not her husband. Beg her to give up prostitution and stop being unfaithful,
translation_verse: Juuda beel yab nì Isirayeel beel yab làá dāá fàtīí ŋá ubaanti. Bi làá dāá lēē ubɔtibaanti ú nīn kpòotī-bi, ní bí dāá bùtī kí gbí bi-tiŋki kɔkɔ. Di sá yii an dāa sá Jisirayeel wiŋkpaaŋŋu dal ní.

english_verse: or I will strip her naked like the day she was born. I will make her barren like a desert, and she will die of thirst.
translation_verse: Ní yíiń ni-mambi nì ni-naalib yii «M-nibul» ní kí yíiń ni-niisalib yii «Bi là-mi». Isirayeel, unimpu un nyáń u-cal boonee

english_verse: Your mother was unfaithful. She was disgraceful and said, “I'll run after my lovers. Everything comes from them— my food and drink, my linen and wool, my olive oil and wine.”
translation_verse: An yaa kaa sá mimmee, m làá lòotī-u dicancaŋgbeel, ú gítí kii u nín nìn bí pu ŋwiin ŋun bi màl̄-uee. M làá yàntī u-tiŋki ń kpántí kii kuteeuee, ní kí dū-kì kí kpántí kitiŋkuliŋŋi. M làá yàntī nnyinnyoo ń kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will build a fence of thorns to block her path.
translation_verse: Maa làá nīn là u-biyaamu bɔti, di sá yii u ŋá tilaakpaal ní ki màl̄-mu.

english_verse: She will run after her lovers, but not catch them; she will search, but not find them. Then she will say, “I'll return to my first husband. Life was better then.”
translation_verse: Tiŋman, mu-na dū u-ba ki líì nì alaakpaatuun. Un di màl̄-muee ŋá ticoobɔti. Di sá u lī yii: «M làá nóó m-bɔmbi bin tìì-mi m-jinti nì m-nyɔkaati, nì ipii kuti nì gulfamɔnti wampeeŋkaati nì m-kpam nì m-daamee.»

english_verse: She didn't know that her grain, wine, and olive oil were gifts from me, as were the gold and silver she used in worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: «An pu ní m làá dū ikuŋkum kí pìin̄-u nsan, ní kí mā digundi kí màntīí tū-u ú taa ti ká nsan kí nyā.

english_verse: Then I'll strip her naked in the sight of her lovers. No one can rescue her.
translation_verse: «Waa nìn béè yii an sá man di nìn tìì-u bilee nì ndaam nì ŋkpam. Man di nìn tìì-u animbil nì sindaariya, ama ní u dūu ŋá saraabi ki tīī diwaal Baal.

english_verse: She said, “My lovers gave me vineyards and fig trees as payment for sex.” Now I, the Lord, will ruin her vineyards and fig trees; they will become clumps of weeds eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, m làá dāá bìitī u-cooi pu kí dàkà u-bɔmbi, ní báà ubɔ mun dāa kpá kí fōō-u m-ŋaan.

english_verse: I'll punish her for the days she worshiped Baal and burned incense to him. I'll punish her for the times she forgot about me and wore jewelry and rings to attract her lovers. I, the Lord, have spoken! The Lord Will Help Israel
translation_verse: M làá dāá kúntí u-faalii, nì u-jiŋaalib nì u-jiŋaalib bin u jīǹ uŋmapɔɔn yaa páaǹee, nì u-wiŋŋuŋfikaai nì u-jiŋaalib bin kɔkɔ pée kíǹ u jīǹee.

english_verse: I will return your vineyards, and then Trouble Valley will become Hopeful Valley. You will say “Yes” to me as you did in your youth, when leaving Egypt.
translation_verse: M làá dáaĺ u-tafal ŋyunti ŋun u dūu nóó diwaal Baalee pu. U nìn tùutī talaalub ki ŋáań saraabi. U nìn cáá abɔmbil nì tiléeŋkaal ki nyāantí u-ba. U nìn sáń ki pá u-bɔmbi boon, ki nìn súntì man pu! Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: I promise from that day on, you will call me your husband instead of your master.
translation_verse: An pu ní m làá gíiǹní u-landɔkɔŋu m-cee. M làá cáá-u kí cùnnì kuteeun ní kí sòoǹ án kɔ́ u-pɔbilin.

english_verse: And I will agree to let you live in peace—you will no longer be attacked by wild animals and birds or by weapons of war.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ yii ŋwiin gbantee u làá dāá yíiń-mi yii <m-cal> ní kaa làá ti yíiń-mi yii <m-waal Baal, an dàkà yii m-kpiliu>.

english_verse: I will accept you as my wife forever, and instead of a bride price I will give you justice, fairness, love, kindness,
translation_verse: M làá lēē awaa Baal yindi u-nyɔkɔn, ní ubɔ gíti kpá kí téetí diyindi gbanti pu.

english_verse: and it will produce grain, grapes, and olives in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: M làá dāá dū deedee ní kí pà a-cootiiku pu, ní á béé yii m sá a-Dindaan.

english_verse: I will scatter the seeds and show mercy to Lo-Ruhamah. I will say to Lo-Ammi, “You are my people,” and they will answer, “You are our God.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Ŋwiin gbantee, m làá dāá nīn sá Unimbɔti un fòol̄ ŋwimmeemee. M làá dāá tīī kutagbɔŋu kun ku nyàab̀ m-ceeyee, ní kutagbɔŋu mun ń dāá tīī kitiŋ ntaanyim min kì nyàab̀ ku-ceeyee.

english_verse: Once again the Lord spoke to me. And this time he said, “Hosea, fall in love with an unfaithful woman who has a lover. Do this to show that I love the people of Israel, even though they worship idols and enjoy the offering cakes made with fruit.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tùkū-mi yii: «Nín̄ gbíntìi néeń unimpu un nyáń a-boon ki cáá bɔɔnee. Nín̄ néeń-u kii man ni-Dindaan nín néeń Isirayeel yab puee, nì min kɔkɔ bi dū bi-ba ki tīī awaa ki néeń fiinyi biliŋ kalaabee.»

english_verse: Then I said, “Now you are mine! You will have to remain faithful to me, though it will be a long time before we sleep together.”
translation_verse: Ní m tùkū-u yii: «Á kàl̄ m-cee doo kí yúntí, kí taa ti ŋá tilaakpaal, ní kaa nín dōoǹ nì uninja ubɔ. Ma mun làá ŋá míǹ mbaantiim kí tīī-si.»

english_verse: It will also be a long time before Israel has a king or before sacrifices are offered at the temple or before there is any way to get guidance from God.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Isirayeel yab làá dāá kàl̄ kí yúntí, kaa cáá ubɔtaaa, kaa cáá ukpootilaaa, kaa ti ŋáań saraayaaa, kaa ti cáá ditaŋkpacooŋkaal àá tiwambalifikaal tin bi cáa bàlifī kí béé Unimbɔti lammee mun.

english_verse: But later, Israel will turn back to the Lord their God and to David their king. At that time they will come to the Lord with fear and trembling, and he will be good to them.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, Isirayeel yab làá dāá fàtīí gítiń. Bi làá dāá nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nì Daafiidi naantiiu un sá bi-bɔtiuee. Bi làá dāá fàtīí gítiń nì kufaaŋŋu ti-Dindaan cee kí nyàab̀ u-ŋanti.

english_verse: Israel, listen as the Lord accuses everyone in the land! No one is faithful or loyal or truly cares about God.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan bɔti, di sá yii ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ bin kóò kitiŋ nee puee bɔti. Kitiŋ nee puee, mbaamɔn gíti kpáaa, dineendi gíti kpáaa, bin nyí Unimbɔtee gíti kpá.

english_verse: Cursing, dishonesty, murder, robbery, unfaithfulness— these happen all the time. Violence is everywhere.
translation_verse: Bi tòó tɔb mbusu, ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn, ki kù binib, ki yù bunaayubu, ki ŋáań tilaakpaal, ki ŋáań tipɔmbɔti, ní ki cáá nnikpaakoon.

english_verse: And so your land is a desert. Every living creature is dying— people and wild animals, birds and fish. The Lord Warns the Priests
translation_verse: An pu ní kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ làá kpā, ní bin kɔkɔ kóò ki-puee ń yɔ̀l̄, kí kpáaǹ ipeel nì inoon. Áli gba tiŋkun jɔmii làá céetí. Bisaraaŋaliibi kpitii

english_verse: Don't accuse just anyone! Not everyone is at fault. My case is against you, the priests.
translation_verse: Ama ubɔ ń taa kɔ̄kɔl̀ ubɔ, ubɔ ń taa wòoǹ u-juti. An sá man nì nimbi bisaraaŋaliibi di cáá tɔb tibɔti.

english_verse: You and the prophets will stumble day and night; I'll silence your mothers.
translation_verse: Ni làá dāá gbéetí kuwiŋkaŋu pu, bibɔnaatiliibi mun làá gbéetí kunyeeu kii nimbee, ní ḿ kpɔ̀ ni-na Isirayeel.

english_verse: You priests have rejected me, and my people are destroyed by refusing to obey. Now I'll reject you and forget your children, because you have forgotten my Law.
translation_verse: M-nibul kúù kun puee di lóò dinyil. Kii ni nín fātì ni-boon ki tīī dinyilee puee, ma mun làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-ni ní naa ti làá nīn sá m-saraaŋaliibi. Ni súntì mama, ni-Nimbɔtiu marau puɔɔ! Ma mun làá súntí ni-jipɔmbi pu.

english_verse: By adding more of you priests, you multiply the number of people who sin. Now I'll change your pride into shame.
translation_verse: Kii bisaraaŋaliibi nín būtì tikpil tikpil puee, míǹ ní bi yīntiǹ-mi mun. M làá yàntī tin nìn tìì-bi tinyoolee ń kpántí-bi ticoobɔti

english_verse: You encourage others to sin, so you can stuff yourselves on their sin offerings.
translation_verse: M-nibul nín ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabi biŋyee di kpīintí-bi. An pu ní bi tìì m-nibul kunyannyaau bí nīn mɔ̀tīi ŋáań ikpiti.

english_verse: That's why I will punish the people for their deeds, just as I will punish you priests.
translation_verse: Tin dɔ̄ ki cí bisaraaŋaliibee di dɔ̄ ki cí samaa un kíǹee. M làá dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-bimbikpitim pu, ní kí pà-bi bi-tuŋkpitiŋ paati.

english_verse: You expect wooden idols and other objects of wood to give you advice. Lusting for sex at pagan shrines has made you unfaithful to me, your God.
translation_verse: M-nibul bàlifī awaa ŋin sá idɔee ní bi-yil pu bɔti, ní mbɔɔkpandɔ tùkù-bi tin bi là kí bééyee. Di sá yii alaakpaatuun fam gáatì-bi. Bi dū bi-ba ki líì nì awaa, ki dū man bi-Nimbɔtiu ki fá.

english_verse: You offer sacrifices on mountaintops and hills, under oak trees, and wherever good shade is found. Your own daughters and daughters-in-law sell themselves for sex.
translation_verse: Ajoon yilpu kúntí kunti ní bi ŋáań bi-saraabi. Ŋgbantamu pu ní bi tùutī talaalub ki ŋáań saraa. Iwaasufi in bi yíì yii seeni nì peepiliiyee nì teereebintee taapu ní bi kàal̀, di sá yii i-booŋyi sɔ̀m̀. An pu ní ni-bisalib ŋáań alaakpaatuun ní ni-coopoobi nyēē bi-calib boon.

english_verse: Israel, you are unfaithful, but don't lead Judah to sin. Stop worshiping at Gilgal or at sinful Bethel. And quit making promises in my name—the name of the living Lord.
translation_verse: Báà nimbi Isirayeel beel yab yaa nyáń m-boonaaa, Juuda beel yab ń taa ŋá míǹ mbaantiim. Ní taa cùmaan Giilgaal circir paaŋŋu pu, kí taa cù Beeti Aween, kí taa tí pùtī kí lì yii: «Nì Unimbɔti un bí nee pu!»

english_verse: You are nothing more than a stubborn cow— so stubborn that I, the Lord, cannot feed you like lambs in an open pasture.
translation_verse: Kii unapɔɔl nín bí puee, míǹ ní Isirayeel beel yab tafaliŋ pɔ̄ɔ̄. Mimmee, kɔŋkɔnnee ní ti-Dindaan làá nín ŋá u-nibul kii apibil ŋin bi cáǹ kupikpaaueeee?

english_verse: You people of Israel are charmed by idols. Leave those people alone!
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim yab nì awaa ŋá mpèé. Yàntī-bi.

english_verse: You get drunk, then sleep with prostitutes; you would rather be vulgar than lead a decent life.
translation_verse: Bi yaa nyùn̄ ki gbée ní bí kɔ́ alaakpaatuun poon. Bi-kpootiliibi néeń tin kɔ̄ntí-bi icooyee ní.

english_verse: And so you will be swept away in a whirlwind for sacrificing to idols.
translation_verse: Kubuŋu làá dāá yòon̄-bi kí páań ku-feeŋyi pu, ní icoo ń dāá cúú-bi saraabi bin bi ŋáańee pu.

english_verse: Listen, you priests! Pay attention, Israel! Listen, you members of the royal family. Justice was your duty. But at Mizpah and Mount Tabor you trapped the people.
translation_verse: «Bisaraaŋaliibi, pīlifìmaan tin bí nee, Isirayeel beel yab kpootiliibi, ní pīlifìmaan. Ubɔti dicaŋkun yab, kpòom̄maan ni-tafal kí pīlifì. An bàà sá nimbi nín sòoǹ binib bɔti nì mbaamɔn. Ama ní ni kpántì kutaliŋŋu ki tīī m-nibul Miisipa tiŋkin, ní ki kpántì kulaaŋŋu kun bi píĺ Tabɔɔr jool puee.

english_verse: At the place of worship you were a treacherous pit, and I will punish you.
translation_verse: Bi gbìn̄ kubookpaaŋŋu Siitiim tantakalin. M bíi bɔ́ntí bi-kɔkɔ tafadaaldi.

english_verse: Israel, I know all about you, and because of your unfaithfulness, I find you unacceptable.
translation_verse: «Mamee, m nyí Eefiraayiim naakookun yab tiŋan, Isirayeel beel yab mun kaa lìkī m-nimbiin. Eefiraayiim yab kɔ́ alaakpaatuun poon, ní ki yāntì Isirayeel beel yab kɔkɔ kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin.»

english_verse: Your evil deeds are the reason you won't return to me, your Lord God. And your constant craving for sex keeps you from knowing me.
translation_verse: Isirayeel beel yab tuŋkpitiŋ kaa pūǹ-bi nsan bí ŋmā kí fàtīí gítí bi-Nimbɔtiu cee. Di sá yii alaakpaatuun fam miba bí bi-ni, ní baa nyí ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: You offer sheep and cattle as sacrifices to me, but I have turned away and refuse to be found.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá cáań bi-piii nì bi-naai kí ŋá saraa kí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, ama baa làá dāá ká-u. Di sá yii u dū-bi ki fá.

english_verse: You have been unfaithful to me, your Lord; you have had children by prostitutes. So at the New Moon Festival, you and your crops will be destroyed. The Lord Warns Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Bi nyáń ti-Dindaan boon ki màl̄ mbiyaamu mun kaa sá u-yɔmuee. Too, an kaa ti làá bà uŋmal, án làá nàan̄ bi nì bi-tiŋki. Juuda beel yab nì Isirayeel beel yab jaaku

english_verse: Give a warning on the trumpet! Let it be heard in Gibeah, Ramah, and sinful Bethel. Benjamin, watch out!
translation_verse: Búḿmaan ŋyin Giibeeya jool pu, búḿmaan dikantándi Raama tiŋkin! Kpāafìmaan Beeti-Aween yab! Beenjameen naakookun yab, bi bíi jáà nì ni ni-boon pú.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will punish and wipe out Israel. This is my solemn promise to every tribe of Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāá dáaĺ Eefiraayiim naakooku tafalee, kì làá dāá kpántí kuteeu ní. Tin m bíi sòoǹ Isirayeel naakɔti pu nee sá tibɔŋman ní.

english_verse: Judah's leaders are like crooks who move boundary markers; that's why I will flood them with my anger.
translation_verse: Juuda beel kpootiliibi náań nì bin cóotí bi-sati kpaanyɔmmu taŋkpeeŋi ki nìkèe ní. An pu ní m làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kii nnyimee kí sìtī bi-pu.

english_verse: Israel was brutally crushed. They got what they deserved for worshiping useless idols.
translation_verse: «Bi sāaǹ Eefiraayiim yab, ibɔsoon nàn̄-bi, di sá yii bi sáń ki pá tin kaa bí tibanee boon.

english_verse: Now I, the Lord, will fill Israel with maggots and make Judah rot.
translation_verse: Too, m làá dāá kpántí kii dinalee ní Eefiraayiim yab cee, ní kí kpántí kii taagbunjaanjaanee Juuda beel yab cee.

english_verse: When Israel and Judah saw their sickness and wounds, Israel asked help from Assyria and its mighty king. But the king cannot cure them or heal their wounds.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Eefiraayiim yab ká yii bi būǹ ní Juuda beel yab ká bi-bunsooŋyee, ní Eefiraayiim yab nín cá Asuur tiŋkin ní ki tú binib bí cùú ká ubɔtikpaan. Ama u mun kaa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ-naaa, kaa tí cáá ni-bunsooŋyi nyɔkɔŋu.

english_verse: So I'll become a fierce lion attacking Israel and Judah. I'll snatch and carry off what I want, and no one can stop me.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m làá nīn sá kii gbikintee ní Eefiraayiim yab cee, ní kí nīn sá kii digbikintipɔmbilee Juuda beel yab cee. Mama m-ba di làá tɔ̀ntī-ni, ní kí kpáaǹ-ni kí búntí, ní ubɔ mun dāa kpá kí fīī-ni m-ŋaan.» Unimbɔti fātì u-boon ki tīī u-nibul

english_verse: Then I'll return to my temple until they confess their guilt and worship me, until they are desperate and beg for my help.
translation_verse: «M làá búntí, m làá nīn gítí m-dumpu kí dāá sāā ŋyunti ŋun bi làá béé bi-bɔkpil kí nyàab̀-mee. Bi-nimbinaamandi poonee, bi làá dāá nyàab̀-mi.»

english_verse: Let's return to the Lord. He has torn us to shreds, but he will bandage our wounds and make us well.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ni lī yii: «Dāam̄maan, tí gítímaan ti-Dindaan cee. Úǹ di ŋá-ti tiweendi, úǹ di làá cáaǹ-ti. Úǹ di gbáń-ti, úǹ di làá tí póob́ ti-buuŋyi.

english_verse: In two or three days he will heal us and restore our strength that we may live with him.
translation_verse: Nì iwiin ili boonee, u làá tīī-ti dimaŋfal, iwiin ita poonee, u làá yáatí-ti kí yóoń ní tí nīn bí dimaŋfalin u-nimbiin.

english_verse: Let's do our best to know the Lord. His coming is as certain as the morning sun; he will refresh us like rain renewing the earth in the springtime. The Lord Speaks to Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Tí béé yii ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔti. Tí nyàab̀ kí béé-u. U-dāantam sá mbaamɔn kii ku nín yaa mɔ́ ku wúntí puee ní. U làá dāan̄ ti-cee kii utaayee ní, kii utaajoolkaa nín nì ki sɔ̀ŋkī kitiŋ puee ní.»

english_verse: People of Israel and Judah, what can I do with you? Your love for me disappears more quickly than mist or dew at sunrise.
translation_verse: Ama ní ti-Dindaan kíí yii: «Ḿ ŋá-si mana ní, Eefiraayiim? A là ḿ ŋá-si mana ní, Juuda? Dineendi din ni cáá m-puee bí kii ditaafaapɔ̀ńdee ní, a lì kii ditaafaamalindee, an kaa pée súŋkí ní kí wāŋkì.

english_verse: That's why I slaughtered you with the words of my prophets. That's why my judgments blazed like the dawning sun.
translation_verse: An pu ní m dī m-bɔnaatiliibi pu ki jáń nì ni, m dū anyɔɔbun ŋin nyáń m-nyɔkɔnee pu ki pɔ̄fì-ni. M-bɔsooŋyi tòoń kii ŋwalifee ní.

english_verse: I'd rather for you to be faithful and to know me than to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Kun fáatiǹ-mee di sá dineendi, kaa sá saraabi. Kí nīn nyí man Unimbɔtee jítiǹ bisaraawɔkaabi.» Ntimbiil tuuŋŋi Isirayeel tiŋkin

english_verse: At a place named Adam, you betrayed me by breaking our agreement.
translation_verse: «Ama kii Adamee, ni nyáń m-poondi boon, naa yúl̀ nì mi deedee.

english_verse: Everyone in Gilead is evil; your hands are stained with the blood of victims.
translation_verse: Giilaadi sá binikpitib tiŋki ní, fatiku daanti gbí ki-poon.

english_verse: You priests are like a gang of robbers in ambush. On the road to Shechem you murder and commit other horrible crimes.
translation_verse: Kii digaŋgam dambi nín bāal̀ nsan caŋin ki cí binib kí kpɔ̀ puee, míǹ ní bisaraaŋaliibi kitil diba kù binib Siikeem saŋŋu pu. Ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi tūǹee dee!

english_verse: I have seen a terrible thing in Israel— you are unfaithful and unfit to worship me.
translation_verse: M ká ntimbiil tuuŋŋi Isirayeel beel tiŋkin. Niin ní Eefiraayiim naakookun yab ŋáań alaakpaatuun ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin.

english_verse: People of Judah, your time is coming too. The Lord Wants To Help Israel I, the Lord, would like to make my nation prosper again
translation_verse: «Nimbi Juuda beel yab mun, m bíi bɔ́ntí ni-bɔsooŋyi yuntiŋu kí cīití-ni.» Fikil fikil nì nnaabu ŋun dòońee «Ŋyunti ŋun m làá dāá gíiǹní m-nibul din bi nìn cúú kuyuŋuee,

english_verse: and to heal its wounds. But then I see the crimes in Israel and Samaria. Everyone is deceitful; robbers roam the streets.
translation_verse: m yaa baa là kí cáaǹ Isirayeelee, ní Eefiraayiim yab kpitii nì Samaarii yab tuŋkpitiŋ ń nyā kí páań mpaampiin pu. Di sá yii bi kíiĺ tɔb, ní binaayub kóò adiinni ki yù, ní digaŋgam daan bí adan pu ki bìlim̄.

english_verse: No one realizes that I have seen their sins surround them like a flood.
translation_verse: Ama an kaa sòoǹ nì bi-pɔbiliŋin yii m téetí bi-kpitii in bi ŋáańee kɔkɔ pu. Kɔŋkɔnnee bi-kpitii gbanti di māntìi tú-bee. I dɔ̄ m-nimbiin ní baabadal.

english_verse: The king and his officials take great pleasure in their sin and deceit.
translation_verse: Bi cáá bi-tuŋkpitiŋ ki kɔ̀ntī ubɔti nimbiliŋ, ní ki cáá bi-nyimɔŋyi ki kɔ̀ntī bikàliŋkpilib yaŋ.

english_verse: Everyone burns with desire— they are like coals in an oven, ready to burst into flames.
translation_verse: Bi-kɔkɔ sá bilaakpaadambi ní. Bi náań nì dikpɔnɔbubul din píĺ kpaŋkpam ní ukpɔnɔŋal kaa ti bíi pàá án nyàtī kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní bukpɔnɔsaa làá jɔ̄m̀ee ní.

english_verse: On the day their king was crowned, his officials got him drunk, and he joined in their foolishness.
translation_verse: Ubɔti maaliwiiŋŋu jiŋaaliu dalee, abɔtibil nyù ndaam áli kí tin būŋkì. Ubɔti tàntī u-ŋal ki tìì bin bèel̄-uee kuboou.

english_verse: They are flames destroying their leaders. And their kings are powerless; none of them trust me.
translation_verse: Bi-kɔkɔ píĺ ní kpaŋkpam kii dikpɔnɔbubulee, bi kù ki céetí bi-kpootiliibi. Bi kpákatì bi-bɔtiibi kɔkɔ, ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ mun kaa kúuǹ ki yíiń-mi.

english_verse: The people of Israel have mixed with foreigners; they are a thin piece of bread scorched on one side.
translation_verse: «Eefiraayiim dū u-ba ki ŋmālim̀ anibul ŋin kíǹee poon. U náań nì kalaa un bi tɔ́ kaa lábitèe ní.

english_verse: They don't seem to realize how weak and feeble they are; their hair has turned gray, while foreigners rule.
translation_verse: Binicambi fóofì u-pɔŋŋu, ní waa kpáàa nyí gba. Tiyikpipin nyáń u-yil pu ní waa kpáàa béè.

english_verse: I am the Lord, their God, but in all of their troubles their pride keeps them from returning to me. No Help from Foreign Nations The Lord said:
translation_verse: Isirayeel beel yab badakal di lèekī bi-pu mmɔ́ɔn. Isirayeel beel yab kaa fātìi gítìń man bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu cee. Min kamaa tin bí nee kɔkɔ jítèe, baa nyàab̄-mi.

english_verse: Israel is a senseless bird, fluttering back and forth between Egypt and Assyria.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim sá kii dibeenanjil din kaa nyí tiba kaa dàkafēe ní. U yíì Eejipiti tiŋki ń dāá jòoń-u, ní ki sáń ki cá Asuur tiŋkin.

english_verse: But I will catch them in a net as hunters trap birds; I threatened to punish them, and indeed I will.
translation_verse: Ama ŋyunti ŋun u tú ki lábití mimmee, ní ḿ dū m-laaŋku kí tɔ̄-u, ní kí cúuń-u kii bi nín cútí inoon puee. M làá dáaĺ u-tafal kii m nín sòon̄ pu bi-kpafil poonee.

english_verse: Trouble and destruction will be their reward for rejecting me. I would have rescued them, but they told me lies.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-bi, di sá yii bi sáǹ-mi! Án làá nàan̄-bi, di sá yii bi yíkìi bíi jáà nì mi! M bàà nyàab̄ kí fīī-bi dee, ama ní bi bí ki sòoǹ m-pu tinyimɔmbɔti!

english_verse: They don't really pray to me; they just howl in their beds. They have rejected me for Baal and slashed themselves, in the hope that Baal will bless their crops.
translation_verse: Baa kūuntí ki yíì-mi mbaamɔm, ama ní bi dɔ̄ bi-dooŋu pu ki yáliŋkí. Bi cáá njimu ki gífí bi-ba kí ŋmā kí ká tijin nì ndaam. Baa nyí yii bi yaa bíi ŋáań mimmee, bi bíi jáà nì man dee.

english_verse: I taught them what they know, and I made them strong. Now they plot against me
translation_verse: Man di kpōotì-bi ki tīī-bi mpɔn, ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, bi dàkafī m-pu ilandɔkɔkpiti ŋma ní.

english_verse: and refuse to obey. They are more useless than a crooked arrow. Their leaders will die in war for saying foolish things. Egyptians will laugh at them.
translation_verse: Bi yaa gítìńaaa, an kaa sá man cee ní bi gítìń. Bi náań nì butɔbu bun gíì ki gbàkēe ní. Ama bi-kpilib nín sòoǹ ki bíiĺ-mi puee, kujaaun ní bi làá kpú, ní binib ń nīn bèel̄-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin.»

english_verse: Sound a warning! Israel, you broke our agreement and ignored my teaching. Now an eagle is swooping down to attack my land.
translation_verse: Búḿmaan ŋyin kí kpāafì binib! Kii ukaabu nín tòó puee, míǹ ní mbusu làá jēetí ti-Dindaan tiŋki pu. Di sá yii Isirayeel beel yab kaa tɔ́ m-poondi ní kaa yúl̀ deedee m-marab poon.

english_verse: Israel, you say, “We claim you, the Lord, as our God.”
translation_verse: Bi kūuntí fám ki lì yii: <Ti-Nimbɔtiu, timbi Isirayeel yab, ti nyí-si!>

english_verse: But your enemies will chase you for rejecting our good agreement.
translation_verse: Isirayeel beel yab dū tin ŋān̄ee ki fá. An pu ní unannanli bíi jì-bi.

english_verse: You chose kings and leaders without consulting me; you made silver and gold idols that led to your downfall.
translation_verse: Bi kāaǹ bi-bɔtiibi kaa bālifì m-pu. Bi lēē bi-kpilib kaa tùkū-mi. Bi dū bi-nimbiliŋ nì bi-sindaariyab ki mɔ́ɔ́ awaa ŋin làá nàan̄-bee.

english_verse: City of Samaria, I'm angry because of your idol in the shape of a calf. When will you ever be innocent again?
translation_verse: Samaarii yab, maa là m-nimbil ń ká ni-nabil. Ni yāntì m gíí ni-pu diŋuul. Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní m làá ká yii naa ti bí ikpitin?

english_verse: Someone from Israel built that idol for you, but only I am God. And so it will be smashed to pieces.
translation_verse: Ni-nabil gbantee nyánní Isirayeel beelin ní. Unil di máń-dì, dàa sá Unimbɔti. Tiŋman, Samaarii nabil gbanti làá nà ní dúsi dusi.

english_verse: If you scatter wind instead of wheat, you will harvest a whirlwind and have no wheat. Even if you harvest grain, enemies will steal it all.
translation_verse: Kii ni nín búĺ kubuŋuee, kubuŋkpaaŋŋu ní ni làá cā. <Didikakal yaa kaa cáá ŋfinee, ŋyim mun kpá dee.> Báà di yaa lòon̄aaa, binicambi di dāa yì kí jī.

english_verse: Israel, you are ruined, and now the nations consider you worthless.
translation_verse: «Bi dū Isirayeel beel ki náĺ. Dì kíǹ ki bí atimbun kansikin kii kuyukpuŋuee ní.

english_verse: You are like a wild donkey that goes its own way. You've run off to Assyria and hired them as allies.
translation_verse: Di sá yii bi yíkìi cūtì Asuur tiŋkin, bi bí kii kumooun maŋki kin tú ki yìiǹ ki-babee ní. Eefiraayiim yab dá bibɔntiibi.

english_verse: You can bargain with nations, but I'll catch you anyway. Soon you will suffer abuse by kings and rulers.
translation_verse: Báà bi yaa yākatì tiwan ki pú atimbun ŋin kíǹee, ŋyunti bāań ḿ kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì. Án kaa làá ti sūŋkì bi làá jī falaa abɔtibil bɔtiu ŋaan.

english_verse: Israel, you have built many altars where you offer sacrifices for sin. But these altars have become places for sin.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim yab máń isaraafan tikpil kí nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabi. - Ama isaraafan gbanti di yàntī bi mɔ̀tīi ŋáań ikpiti. -

english_verse: My instructions for sacrifices were written in detail, but you ignored them.
translation_verse: Báà m yaa ŋmàn̄ m-marab nee bɔkpaaŋi ŋfunyɔm kutuku pu, án làá nīn bí-bi kii tibɔcan tibee ní.

english_verse: You sacrifice your best animals and eat the sacrificial meals, but I, the Lord, refuse your offerings. I will remember your sins and punish you. Then you will return to Egypt.
translation_verse: Bi ŋáań saraabi ki tìì-mi, kun puee tinan ní bi nyàab̀ kí ŋmɔ́. Ama man bi-Dindaan, maa làá fōō saraabi gbanti. Too m làá téetí bi-yìntitam pu, m làá dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-kpitii pu. Bi làá fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin.

english_verse: Israel, I created you, but you forgot me. You and Judah built palaces and many strong cities. Now I will send fire to destroy your towns and fortresses.
translation_verse: «Isirayeel beel yab máń adinyaan ní ki súntì bi-náanliu pu. Juuda beel yabee, bíǹ máń agun ní ki tú bi-timmu. Ama m làá yàntī ŋŋmi ń wà bi-timmu gbanti, ní kí wà bi-dinyaaŋŋi mun.»

english_verse: Israel, don't celebrate or make noisy shouts like other nations. You have been unfaithful to your God. Wherever grain is threshed, you behave like prostitutes because you enjoy the money you receive.
translation_verse: Isirayeel, taa nín̄ fàal̀ kí lákatí mara pu kii atimbun ŋin kíǹee nín ŋáań puee. Di sá yii alaakpaatuun puee, a dū a-Nimbɔtiu ki fá, ki ŋá alaakpaatuun. A néeń kí fōō a-laakpaatuuŋŋi paati laakin kamaa ní bilee naapaaŋi bée.

english_verse: and you will have to leave the land of the Lord. Some of you will go to Egypt; others will go to Assyria and eat unclean food.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim yab kaa làá ŋmā kí nīn gbíntìi kóò ti-Dindaan tiŋkin. Bi làá fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin, ní kí jī tijin tin bi kòóyee Asuur tiŋkin.

english_verse: You won't be able to offer sacrifices of wine to the Lord. None of your sacrifices will please him— they will be unclean like food offered to the dead. Your food will only be used to satisfy your hunger; none of it will be brought to the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Baa dāa gíti féeń ndaam kí ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa, bi-saraabi kaa làá dāá nīn fáatiǹ-u. Bi-jinti làá dāá kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kii dikpoolin jintee, un kamaa yaa jíń-tèe kóò tijɔkɔndin ní. Bi làá dāá ká tijin kí jī kí díkí, ama baa dāa ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ǹ-tì ti-Dindaan diikun.

english_verse: You will no longer be able to celebrate the festival of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni làá dāá ŋá mana dikpafil wiiŋŋu dal, ti-Dindaan jiŋaaliu wiiŋŋu dal?

english_verse: Even if you escape alive, you will end up in Egypt and be buried in Memphis. Your silver treasures will be lost among weeds; thorns will sprout in your tents.
translation_verse: Ni yaa láa yíkì ni-tiŋki kin bi nāaǹee nee, Eejipiti tiŋki làá dāá fōō-ni, ama Meemifiisi tiŋkin ní bi làá dāá síb́-ni. Abɔjanaakun di làá dāá jī bi-gaajawammɔntiiti fakal, ní ikuŋkum ń dāá nyā bi-diiŋŋin.

english_verse: Israel, the time has come. You will get what you deserve, and you will know it. “Prophets are fools,” you say. “And God's messengers are crazy.” Your terrible guilt has filled you with hatred.
translation_verse: Ditafadaaldi yuntiŋu bāań dee, ŋyunti ŋun báà ŋma làá sòoǹ u-nyɔkɔpu yayee bāań. Isirayeel beel yab máaǹ kí béé míǹ! Ni lì yii: «Ubɔnaatil nee wáatì ní, unil un pu Ŋfam bí nee yil lábitì.» Tiŋman, m yaa wáatèe, an sá ni-kpitii nín wīikí puee, nì ni nín bí ki jáà nì mi mpɔn nì mpɔnee pu.

english_verse: Israel, the Lord sent me to look after you. But you trap his prophets and flood his temple with your hatred.
translation_verse: Man ubɔnaatil, man di sá un cí Eefiraayiimee, man nì m-Nimbɔtiu di bí. Ama binib pīil̀-mi titalindi laakin kamaa ní m yaa cée. Bi jáà nì mi áli m-Nimbɔtiu diikun.

english_verse: You are brutal and corrupt, as were the men of Gibeah. But God remembers your sin, and you will be punished. Sin's Terrible Results
translation_verse: Bi pée kɔ́ ikpiti poon poon ní kábu, a lì kii bi nín nìn ŋá pu Giibeeya tiŋkinee. Ama Unimbɔti kpá kí súntí bi-kpitii pu, asee u pée dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-kpitii gbanti pu. Tin nìn jítì Baal-Peewɔree

english_verse: Israel, when I, the Lord, found you long ago it was like finding grapes in a barren desert or tender young figs. Then you worshiped Baal Peor, that disgusting idol, and you became as disgusting as the idol you loved.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «Dooooyee, m nìn ká Isirayeel yab kii ɔliifi biliŋ ŋin bi kītì kuteeunee nín mɔ̄ puee ní. M nìn ká ni-naanjab kii difiigibipeepeekaal din bi kāntí bufiigisubu puee ní. Ama ni-naanjab nín nìn bāań Beeti-Peewɔɔree, bi nìn dū bi-ba ki líiǹ ticoobɔti. Bi ŋá mimmee ní m kíǹ ki ná-bi kii m nín ná diwaal din bi néeńee puee.

english_verse: And so, Israel, your glory will fly away like birds— your women will no longer be able to give birth.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim yab, kun tìì-ni tinyoolee làá yīkì kí ŋàaǹ kii unoonee ní. Binimpoobi kaa dāa gíti màal̀ mbiyaamuɔɔɔ, baa dāa gíti cāab̀ apooyaaa, mbiyaamu kaa dāa gíti nāantí bi-pooŋŋin.

english_verse: Even if you do have children, I will take them all and leave you to mourn. I will turn away, and you will sink down in deep trouble.
translation_verse: Báà bi yaa cáá mbiyaamu mu cíkitàaa, maa làá yàntī mú nīn bí kí kpántí binib. Ama m yaa fātì m-boon ki tīī-bi, dinimbinaamandi làá kɔ́-beeee!

english_verse: Israel, when I first met you, I thought of you as palm trees growing in fertile ground. Now you lead your people out, only to be slaughtered. Hosea's Advice
translation_verse: M wāĺ Eefiraayiim kii Tiir tiŋki kin nìn bí laakin timool múkú an sɔ̀m̀ fílfilee ní, nì míǹ kɔkɔee Eefiraayiim làá dāá dū u-biyaamu kí tīī bí kpɔ̀.»

english_verse: Our Lord, do just one thing for your people— make their women unable to have children or to nurse their babies. The Lord's Judgment on Israel
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, a yaa làá dáaĺ binib nee tafalee, ba ní a làá dūú dáaĺ ní? Yàntī bi-nimpoobi ń kpántí biŋmaŋŋmantiibi, bi-biiŋi ń fáká.

english_verse: Israel, I first began to hate you because you did evil at Gilgal. Now I will chase you out of my house. No longer will I love you; your leaders betrayed me.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti bí yii: «Bi-tuŋkpitiŋ kɔkɔ kíĺ Giilgaal ní. Niin ní m kíĺ ki kíǹ ki ná-bi. Ikpiti in ní bi ŋée puee, m làá jà-bi kí nyāntí m-diikun. Maa ti làá nīn néeń-bi. Bi-kpootiliibi kɔkɔ sá pɔɔgaatib ní.

english_verse: Israel, you are a vine with dried-up roots and fruitless branches. Even if you had more children and loved them dearly, I would slaughter them all. Hosea Warns Israel
translation_verse: Bi gbáń Eefiraayiim yab an bàn̄-bi. Bi-nyaaŋyi kūń. Baa ti làá lòoǹ abil. Báà binimpoobi yaa dáá gbíntìi cáá mbiyaamuɔɔɔ, m làá fáá kí kpɔ̀ bi-poon naŋu biyaamu mun bi néeńee.»

english_verse: Israel, you disobeyed my God. Now he will force you to roam from nation to nation.
translation_verse: M-Nimbɔtiu làá dū-bi kí fá di sá yii baa pílifiǹ-u. Bi làá nīn kíǹ ki tú ki yìiǹ atimbun ŋin kíǹee kansikin ní.

english_verse: You were a healthy vine covered with grapes. But the more grapes you grew, the more altars you built; the better off you became, the better shrines you set up for pagan gods.
translation_verse: Isirayeel beel nìn sá bufiinyisubu bun nìn lòoǹ abil tikpilee ní. U yaa nìn lòon̄ abil tikpilee, míǹ ní u nìn māā isaraafan mun tikpil. An yaa nìn bútì u-tiŋkee, míǹ ní u nìn nyāantí u-taŋkpacooŋkaaŋi.

english_verse: You are deceitful and disloyal. So you will pay for your sins, because the Lord will destroy your altars and images.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab sá milimilidambi ní. Too, ŋyunti bāań bí fōō bi-kpitii paati. Ti-Dindaan u-ba di làá wìil̀ bi-saraafaŋyi, ní kí kpēelikì bi-taŋkpacooŋkaaŋi.

english_verse: “We don't have a king,” you will say. “We don't fear the Lord. And what good are kings?”
translation_verse: Bi bí ki lì kɔŋkɔnnee yii: «Taa cáá ubɔti, di sá yii taa fāŋkì ti-Dindaan. Báà ti yaa cáá ubɔti, ba ní u ŋūǹ kí ŋá kí tīī-ti?»

english_verse: Israel, you break treaties and don't keep promises; you turn justice into poisonous weeds where healthy plants should grow.
translation_verse: Bi sòoǹ tikpil, ki pùtī fám, bi nì binib ŋáań mpèé, ama bi-baamɔŋyi bí kii ujil nín nyēē adan pu bukpaan puee ní.

english_verse: All who live in Samaria tremble with concern for the idols at sinful Bethel. The idol there was the pride of the priests, but it has been put to shame; now everyone will cry.
translation_verse: Samaarii yab fàŋkí tin làá bàń Beeti-Aween nabil puee. Dinabilee nibul nì di-saraaŋaliibi bíi ŋáań di-kpool. Bi nìn fàal̀ di-nyaaŋku pu, too, bi yōoǹ-dì ki cáa búntì.

english_verse: It will be taken to Assyria and given to the great king. Then Israel will be disgraced for worshiping that idol.
translation_verse: Bi làá yòon̄ dinabilee kí cáá cùnnì Asuur tiŋkin kí pɔ̄ kitiŋ gbanti bɔtikpaaŋwu. Icoo làá dāá cúú Eefiraayiim yab, tiŋman, icoo làá dāá cúú Isirayeel beel yab tin bi bɔ́ntì kí ŋée pu.

english_verse: Like a twig in a stream, the king of Samaria will be swept away.
translation_verse: An dóò Samaarii yab pu dee. Bi-bɔtiu sá kii didɔjal din dēē nnyim puee ní.

english_verse: The altars at sinful Bethel will be destroyed for causing Israel to sin; they will be grown over with thorns and thistles. Then everyone will beg the mountains and hills to cover and protect them. The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá kpìtī Aween saraaŋapaaŋyi, íǹ in pu Isirayeel yab nìn ŋáań ikpitee. Abɔjanaakun nì ikuŋkum làá dāá nyā kí múkuǹ i-saraafaŋyi pu. Samaarii yab làá dāá tùkù ajoon yii: «Bìim̄maan ti-pu!» ní kí dāá lì ŋgbantamu yii: «Lítímaan ti-pu!»

english_verse: Israel, you have never stopped sinning since that time at Gibeah. That's why you will be attacked at Gibeah.
translation_verse: Doooo Giibeeya ní Isirayeel yab yīntiǹ-mi, ní doooo nee, baa kpántì bi-ba. An pu ní bi làá já nì bíǹ binikpitib gbanti Giibeeya jool pu.

english_verse: Your sins have doubled, and you are rebellious. Now I have decided to send nations to attack and put you in chains.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «M làá dáaĺ bi-tafal. Atimbun làá dāá kpāfì kí já nì bi kí dáaĺ bi-tafal ikpiti in bi ŋáań kaa gbèentée pu.

english_verse: Once you were obedient like a calf that loved to thresh grain. But I will put a harness on your beautiful neck; you and Judah must plow and cultivate the ground.
translation_verse: «Eefiraayiim nìn sá kii dinabil din nìn néeń ki tà ki gbátí adibilee ní. Ŋyunti ŋun m ká u-sil nyaaŋkuee, ní m kpàl̄-u ú nīn kù tikpaal. Juuda làá nīn dátí akoo ŋin cátí adanee ní Isirayeel ń nīn dátí akoo ŋin kpátée.

english_verse: Plow your fields, scatter seeds of justice, and harvest faithfulness. Worship me, the Lord, and I will send my saving power down like rain.
translation_verse: Bɔ̄l̀maan tin bí deedeeyee kí dāá cā tiniti. Ní bēel̀maan kusapɔŋu, di sá yii ŋyunti bāań ní nyàab̀ man ni-Dindaan kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāan̄ kí dū tin bí deedeeyee kí yàaǹ ni-puee.

english_verse: You have planted evil, harvested injustice, and eaten the fruit of your lies. You trusted your own strength and your powerful forces.
translation_verse: Ama ní ni búĺ tikpitil ní ki bíi cēē ikpiti. Ni ŋmɔ́ disubil din ni-nyimɔŋyi lòon̄ee. «Di sá yii ni nìn máká ni-ba pɔŋŋu nì ni-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu pu.

english_verse: So war will break out, and your fortresses will be destroyed. Your enemies will do to you what Shalman did to the people of Beth-Arbel— mothers and their children will be beaten to death against rocks.
translation_verse: An pu ní kujaau làá pōō ni-nibul kansikin, ní bí dāá nàan̄ ni-timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee kɔkɔ. Ŋi làá dāá kpántí kii Beeti Arbeel tiŋkee ní. Ubɔti Calman nín nìn jáń nì kitiŋ gbantee, u nìn kūū bibinaatiibi ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu ní.

english_verse: Bethel, this will be your fate because of your evil. Israel, at dawn your king will be killed.
translation_verse: Kun ni ŋá Beeteelee nín cáań-ni kuŋyee dee, di sá yii ni-kpitii gíti jítì mara pu. Kutaa tin lì yii ku wúntée, an dóò Isirayeel bɔtiu pu dee.»

english_verse: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and I called my son out of Egypt.
translation_verse: «Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel nìn sá kibikee ní m nìn kíĺ ki néeń-u, ní ki yíiń úǹ, m-jipɔɔn ki nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkin.»

english_verse: But as the saying goes, “The more they were called, the more they rebelled.” They never stopped offering incense and sacrifices to the idols of Baal.
translation_verse: Ama míǹ boonee, m yaa gíti yíiń-uee, u kíǹ ki sáń-mi ní. Bi ŋáań saraabi ki tìì awaa ŋin bi yíì Baalee, ní ki tùutī talaalub ki tìì awaakpitikaa.

english_verse: I took Israel by the arm and taught them to walk. But they would not admit that I was the one who had healed them.
translation_verse: Min kamaa man di ŋúb́ Eefiraayiim ŋalii, ki dātì-u tàatáa u cōom̀ee, waa béè gba yii man di lōō-u.

english_verse: I led them with kindness and with love, not with ropes. I held them close to me; I bent down to feed them.
translation_verse: Nì mpoommɔn nì dineendi ní m dūu kpēē-u. M nìn sá kii ubinaati nín yòontí u-biki kí nákań u-ba pu, kí bòon̄ kí tīī-kì dibiil kí ŋāam̀ puee ní.

english_verse: But they rejected me, and so must return to Egypt; now Assyria will rule them.
translation_verse: «Baa làá fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin, ama Asuur yab di làá dāá nīn cáá bi-pu mpɔn, di sá yii bi yíì kaa fātìi gítìń m-cee.

english_verse: My people are determined to reject me for a god they think is stronger, but he can't help.
translation_verse: M-nibul lafun lēē bi-pɔbilin kí dū-mi kí fá. Bi yíì-bi doooo yilpu, ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa yíkì.

english_verse: Israel, I can't let you go. I can't give you up. How could I possibly destroy you as I did the towns of Admah and Zeboiim? I just can't do it. My feelings for you are much too strong.
translation_verse: «Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí fàtī m-boon kí tīī-si ní, Eefiraayiim? Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí dū-si kí fá ní, Isirayeel? Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí ŋá-si kii m nín ŋá Adima tiŋki puee, àá kí ŋá-si kii m nín ŋá Seebooyiim tiŋki puee? M yaa ŋá míǹ, an làá páb́-mi tikpil. An gbí-mi isaa.
