english_verse: Israel, I won't lose my temper and destroy you again. I am the Holy God— not merely some human, and I won't stay angry.
translation_verse: Maa làá dū m-ŋuukpaandi kí tɔ̄ ditundi. Maa ti làá nàan̄ Eefiraayiim, di sá yii m sá Unimbɔti ní, maa sá unil. M sá circirdaan ní ki bí ni-kansikin, maa làá dāan̄ nì diŋuul poon.»

english_verse: I, the Lord, will roar like a lion, and my children will return, trembling from the west.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá páań ti-Dindaan boon. Ti-Dindaan làá dāá mùuǹ kii gbikintee. U yaa láa bíi mùuǹee, u-biyaamu làá dāá nyānní ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú bi-wunti gbáà kí dāan̄.

english_verse: They will come back, fluttering like birds from Egypt or like doves from Assyria. Then I will bring them back to their homes. I, the Lord, have spoken! Israel and Judah Compared
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá nyānní Eejipiti tiŋkin bi-wunti gbáà kpàkpa kii idiyaalee, ní kí dāá nyānní Asuur tiŋkin kii abeenanjilee. M làá dāá yàntī bí gítí bi-diiŋŋi poon. Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄.

english_verse: All day long Israel chases wind from the desert; deceit and violence are found everywhere. Treaties are made with Assyria; olive oil is taken to Egypt. Israel and Judah Condemned
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim yab dū inyimɔn ki māntìi tú-mi, ní Isirayeel beel yab dū diŋmatindi ki fìn̄-mi. Ama Juuda beel yab bíǹ dá láá gbíntìi còom̄ nì Unimbɔti, ní ki dáá gbíntìi yú nì circirdaan deedee.

english_verse: The Lord also brings charges against the people of Judah, the descendants of Jacob. He will punish them for what they have done.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim yab jīǹ kubuŋu ní kí díkí, ní ki jì ki bīī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki boon kaa gbèentí. Bi yāntì inyimɔn nì tipɔmbɔti gbóotì. Bi nì Asuur yab ŋá mpèé, ní ki tìì Eejipiti yab ŋkpam.

english_verse: Even before Jacob was born, he cheated his brother, and when he grew up, he fought against God.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nì Juuda yab cáá ibɔsoon. U làá dáaĺ Jaakɔb nibooliŋu tafal bi-bimbikpitim pu, ní kí pà-bi bi-tuuŋŋi paati.

english_verse: At Bethel, Jacob wrestled with an angel and won; then with tears in his eyes, he asked for a blessing, and God spoke to us there.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb bí u-na poon ní ki fōō u-maan paaŋŋu. U cíkitì muee ní u nì Unimbɔti mɔ̀n̄.

english_verse: So return to your God. Patiently trust him, and show love and justice.
translation_verse: Niin ní Ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, un bi yíì yii <ti-Dindaanee> lī yii:

english_verse: You say to yourself, “I'm rich! I earned it all on my own, without committing a sin.” The Lord Is Still the God of Israel
translation_verse: «Kii Kanaan yab nín bí puee, míǹ ní sii Eefiraayiim mun bí, a ŋúb́ saniya un kaa sá umɔntee. A néeń ki mùul̄ binib

english_verse: Israel, I, the Lord, am still your God, just as I have been since the time you were in Egypt. Now I will force you to live in tents once again, as you did in the desert.
translation_verse: ki lì yii: <M kpántì ugaaja, m ká tigaajati tikpil. M-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poonee, maa ŋá tikpitil tiba, maa pée yīntì báà tiba poon.>

english_verse: I spoke to the prophets— often I spoke in visions. And so, I will send my prophets with messages of doom.
translation_verse: Ama mamee, doooo Eejipiti tiŋkin ní m sá a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu. M làá yàntī á fàtīí nīn kíǹ ki kóò tibìń ni, kii ŋwiin ŋun man nì sii nìn kpáfèe.

english_verse: Gilead is terribly sinful and will end up ruined. Bulls are sacrificed in Gilgal on altars made of stones, but those stones will be scattered in every field.
translation_verse: M nìn sòon̄ nì bibɔnaatiliibi, ní ki nìn yāntì bi kántì aleedaka tikpil. M làá gíti dī bibɔnaatiliibi pu kí gāā alaŋkpan.

english_verse: I sent the prophet Moses to lead Israel from Egypt and to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb sáǹ ki cūtì Aram tantakalin. Isirayeel cūtìi túń ditundi unimpu pu. Unimpu puee, u nìn kpántì un kpàá tiwaŋkutee.

english_verse: Israel, I will make you pay for your violent crimes and for insulting me.
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan dī ubɔnaatil ubɔ pu ní ki nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin. U làá yàntī ubɔnaatil ń kpàà u-nibul.

english_verse: When your leaders spoke, everyone in Israel trembled and showed great respect. But you sinned by worshiping Baal, and you were destroyed.
translation_verse: Njaminee, Eefiraayiim yaa nìn sòoǹee, báà ŋma nìn fàŋkí ní. Isirayeel naakɔti kansikinee, úǹ di nìn līī. Ama u nóó diwaal Baal ki fōō dibɔkpil, ní ki kpíì an pu.

english_verse: Now you continue to sin by designing and making idols of silver in the shape of calves. You are told to sacrifice to these idols— yes, even to kiss them.
translation_verse: Díǹ pu nee, bi dáá gbíntìi nìkì ki ŋáań ikpiti. Bi dūntì bi-nimbiliŋ ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ awaa, awaa ŋin ní bíǹ bi-ba dākafì ki mɔ́ɔ́yee. An sá uwammɔ́ɔl tuuŋŋi aba ní, awaa gbanti pu ní bi lì yii: «Tí ŋámaan saraabi kí tīī-ŋi!» Binib móotí anabil ki ŋáań saraabi.

english_verse: And so, all of you will vanish like the mist or the dew of early morning, or husks of grain in the wind or smoke from a chimney.
translation_verse: An pu ní bi làá nīn bí kii ditaafaapɔ̀ńdee, a lì kii ditaafaamalindi nín wáŋkí pu malaayee. Bi làá nīn bí kii tifeel nín yíkí pu kí cù ndandati kí wàatī dibileenaapaal puee ní, àá kii ŋŋminyiim nín nyēē mbùń ŋubɔ poon puee ní.

english_verse: I, the Lord, have been your God since the time you were in Egypt. I am the only God you know, the only one who can save.
translation_verse: Doooo Eejipiti tiŋkin ní man sá a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu. Aa ti nyí Unimbɔti ubɔ ki kútì man pu, ufiil ubɔ mun kaa ti bí laaba, asee man baba.

english_verse: I took care of you in a thirsty desert.
translation_verse: Mamee, kuteeun, ŋweel tiŋkin ní m béè-si.

english_verse: I fed you till you were satisfied, then you became proud and forgot about me.
translation_verse: A pée bàn̄ kunaakpaapɔɔunee ní a jíń ki díkí. Ama ŋyunti ŋun a jíń ki díkée ní a kɔ́ dilambilin. An pu ní a súntì man pu.

english_verse: Now I will attack like a lion, ambush you like a leopard,
translation_verse: Niinee ní m kpántì kii gbikintee ki tīī-si, a lì kii ugbii un di náká nsan caŋin ki cée.

english_verse: and rip you apart like a bear robbed of her cubs. I will gnaw on your bones, as though I were a lion or some other wild animal.
translation_verse: M làá kpìl̄-si kii digbiŋgbil din ní bi cúú di-biyaamuee. M làá yā kí cátí a-bindi. M làá cúú-si kí tɔ̀ntī kii ugbikintinaatee dibɔbil pu niin, ní ipeel ń cúú-si kí tɔ̀ntī tɔ̀ntī.

english_verse: Israel, you are done for. Don't expect help from me.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee Isirayeel, an nāaǹ-si! Too, man baba di bàà ŋūǹ kí jòoń-si?

english_verse: You wanted a king and rulers. Where is your king now? What cities have rulers?
translation_verse: A-bɔtiuee bí la ní kaa làá dāan̄ kí fīī-si a-timmu poon ní? A-kpootiliibee bí là ní? Ŋyuntee, a nìn bí-mi yii: <Tīī-mi ubɔti nì bikpootiliibi.>

english_verse: In my anger, I gave you a king; in my fury, I took him away. Israel's Terrible Fate The Lord said:
translation_verse: Tiŋman m nìn tīī-si ubɔti m-ŋuul poon, ní ki fātìi fōō-u m-bum poon.

english_verse: Israel, your terrible sins are written down and stored away.
translation_verse: M ŋmàn̄ Eefiraayiim yab yìntitam ki síiǹ. M dū bi-kpitii ki kpáafì tiŋan.

english_verse: You are like a senseless child who refuses to be born at the proper time.
translation_verse: Imatiŋween làá jēetí bi-pu. Ama kibikee sá kibigbaaŋŋi ní. Ŋyunti bàà bàn̄ dee, ama kì yíì kaa là kí nyā ki-na poon.

english_verse: Should I, the Lord, rescue you from death and the grave? No! I call death and the grave to strike you like a plague. I refuse to show mercy.
translation_verse: Mimmee mama bi-Dindaan, m máaǹ kí dā-bi kí nyāntí ditaŋkpiil ŋaanaaa? Ḿ fīī-bi kí nyāntí ŋkúm ŋaanaaa? Too, ŋkúm, a-pɔŋŋu bí la? Too, ditaŋkpiil, a-looti bí la? Disaasɔl nyáń m-nimbiliŋin.

english_verse: No matter if you prosper more than the other tribes, I, the Lord, will wipe you out, just as a scorching desert wind dries up streams of water. I will take away your precious treasures.
translation_verse: Min kamaa an bútì Eefiraayiim yab bi-nabiyaamu kansikinee, ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú buŋku dòoń, ti-Dindaan buŋku làá nyānní kuteeu pú. Ku làá fáá nnyimbul pu ní ŋú fóotí ní dinyimbɔbil ń kpā, ní bí fūkul̀ laakin bi dū bi-gaajawammɔntiiti ki kpáafèe.

english_verse: Return to the Lord and say, “Please forgive our sins. Accept our good sacrifices of praise instead of bulls.
translation_verse: Isirayeel, fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu cee, di sá yii a-kpitii di yāntì a gbéetì ki lítì.

english_verse: Assyria can't save us, and chariots can't help. So we will no longer worship the idols we have made. Our Lord, you show mercy to orphans.” The Lord Promises To Forgive
translation_verse: Gítiḿmaan ti-Dindaan cee kí kpáaǹ anyɔɔbun nee kí tin tùkù-u yii: «Dū ti-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ti, ní kí fōō tin ŋān̄ ti cáa ŋáań-si saraayee. An nín bàà sá tí dū anabil kí ŋá-si saraayee, ti làá dū ti-nyɔmmu poon nyɔɔbuŋŋi ní kí ŋá-si saraa.

english_verse: I will be like the dew— then you will blossom like lilies and have roots like a tree.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá cáaǹ Isirayeel u nín kaa yúl̀ nì mi deedeeyee pu. M làá nīn néeń-u nì dipɔbil diba, di sá yii diŋuul din m gíí u-puee sɔ̄ŋkì.

english_verse: Your branches will spread with the beauty of an olive tree and with the aroma of Lebanon Forest.
translation_verse: M làá nīn bí kii dimalindee ní ki tīī Isirayeel. U làá púkuḿ kii nsupumpukumee ní kí báań inyaan kii Leebanɔn tiŋkin isufi in bi yíì Seediree.

english_verse: You will rest in my shade, and your grain will grow. You will blossom like a vineyard and be famous as the wine from Lebanon.
translation_verse: U làá dāá tɔ̄ apan kí làlim̀ ní kí nīn cáá kunyaaŋŋu kii ɔliifi subuee, ní kí nīn sɔ́fì kii Leebanɔn satin sufiiyee.

english_verse: Israel, give up your idols! I will answer your prayers and take care of you. I am that glorious tree, the source of your fruit.
translation_verse: Bin nìn kóò u-booŋŋu taapuee làá dāá fàtīí gítiń. Bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ bilee kpaaŋŋi. Bi làá dāá púkuḿ kii fiinyi subuee, ní kí dāá nyā diyindi kii Leebanɔn daamee.

english_verse: If you are wise, you will know and understand what I mean. I am the Lord, and I lead you along the right path. If you obey me, we will walk together, but if you are wicked, you will stumble.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim, mpèé ŋulɔŋu di bí man nì awaa kansikin ní? Man di fòol̄ a-wimmeem ní ki wúǹ a-pu. M sá kii siipreesi susɔmbuee ní, man di yì-tì ní a-kpaajinti lòoǹ.»

english_verse: I am Joel the son of Pethuel. And this is the message the Lord gave to me. Locusts Cover the Land
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ nì Peetuweel jipɔɔn Jooweel tibɔti nee. Inaakitoon nì ŋweel bɔti

english_verse: Listen, you leaders and everyone else in the land. Has anything like this ever happened before?
translation_verse: Nimbi bikpilibee, ní pīlifìmaan! Ní ŋátímaan ni-tafaliŋ kí pīlifì, Juuda yab kɔkɔ! Tin bí nee juti jítì ni-yuntii nee poon ni káaa, àá tì jítì ni-naanjab yuntii ni gbìl̄ ní?

english_verse: Tell our children! Let it be told to our grandchildren and their children too.
translation_verse: Ní dūú māafìmaan ni-biyaamu. Ni-biyaamu mun ń dāá dūú māafì bi-biyaamu, ní bi-biyaamu ń dāá dūú māafì bi-boon yab.

english_verse: Sober up, you drunkards! Cry long and loud; your wine supply is gone.
translation_verse: Bidanyɔgbiliibi, fìntīmaan kí nīn sūǹ. Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan, nimbi bidanyɔliibi kɔkɔ. Di sá yii naa ti làá ká ndapɔm kí nyɔ̀.

english_verse: A powerful nation with countless troops has invaded our land. They have the teeth and jaws of powerful lions.
translation_verse: Ditimbundi diba nib bíi jáà nì m-tiŋki. Bi pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní ki wīikí baa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ-bi. Bi-nyiŋŋi bí kii gbikinti nyiŋŋee ní, ní bi-nyɔɔkpaweeŋyi bí kii ugbikintisal yaŋee.

english_verse: Grieve like a young woman mourning for the man she was to marry.
translation_verse: Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan kii usapɔɔn un dáá pée mɔ́ǹ ní u-cal kpíì u kā dikpoolee.

english_verse: Offerings of grain and wine are no longer brought to the Lord's temple. His servants, the priests, are deep in sorrow.
translation_verse: Baa ti cáǹ tijimpin saraau nì ndaam saraau ti-Dindaan diikun. Bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliibee kā dikpool.

english_verse: Barren fields mourn; grain, grapes, and olives are scorched and shriveled.
translation_verse: Bi bíil̀ tisati, kitiŋ kɔ́ kunimbaaun. Tijin gíti kpáaa, ndapɔm gíti kpáaa, ŋkpam mun gúń.

english_verse: Mourn for our farms and our vineyards! There's no wheat or barley growing in our fields.
translation_verse: Bikpaabi wunti yɔ̄tì. Bin kù fiinyee yáliŋkí ɔɔji nì bilee pu, di sá yii tikpaajin kpá bí cā.

english_verse: Grapevines have dried up and so has every tree— figs and pomegranates, date palms and apples. All happiness has faded away. Return to God
translation_verse: Fiinyi kūń, ní fiigi sufii fáaḿ. Greenaadi sufii nì ibafi nì pɔɔmi sufii, an dàkà yii kusaaun sufii kɔkɔ kūń. Dipɔɔpindi wáŋkì binib kansikin. Binib ń bóob́ kinyɔkɔ kí gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan

english_verse: Mourn, you priests who serve at the altar of my God. Spend your days and nights wearing sackcloth. Offerings of grain and wine are no longer brought to the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Bisaraaŋaliibi, dūmaan kpɔsatab kí pèen̄ kí nīn sūm̀maan. Nimbi bin tūǹ nsaraafan pu tundee, nín̄ yáliŋkímaan! Nimbi bin sá m-Nimbɔtiu tɔntɔnliibee, dūmaan kutuku kí pèen̄ kutaa ń wúntí. Di sá yii baa ti cāabìń tijimpin nì ndamam saraau ni-Nimbɔtiu diikun.

english_verse: Tell the leaders and people to come together at the temple. Order them to go without eating and to pray sincerely.
translation_verse: Bɔ́ntímaan ni-ba kí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ, yíiḿmaan binib bí kóoǹ kí kpāfì. Ní kóom̀maan bitindaŋkpilib nì bin kɔkɔ kóò Juuda tiŋkinee kí kpāfì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu diikun, ní kí kúuǹ kí yíiń ti-Dindaan. Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dal

english_verse: We are in for trouble! Soon the Lord All-Powerful will bring disaster.
translation_verse: Óooo! Ba wiiŋŋu ŋúǹ bulifi dee! Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋuee tóobiń. Ŋu dòoń kí nàan̄ tikɔkɔ, ŋu làá nyānní Mpɔŋkɔdaan cee ní kí dāan̄.

english_verse: Our food is already gone; there's no more celebrating at the temple of our God.
translation_verse: An kaa sá ti-nimbilaaliyin ní tijin wáŋkì, ní mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi yíkì ti-Nimbɔtiu diikunaaa?

english_verse: Seeds dry up in the ground; no harvest is possible. Our barns are in bad shape, with no grain to store in them.
translation_verse: Iwambool in bi búĺee dōoǹ kitiŋin ki sūū. Cakalaabi poon kūń, adiin ŋin poon bi kpáafí tijinee lítì, di sá yii bilee kaa ti bí.

english_verse: I cry out to you, Lord. Grasslands and forests are eaten by the scorching heat.
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, sii ní m kūuntí ki yíì! Di sá yii ŋŋmi wùn̄ kuteeu pu mooti, aŋmilimbil wùn̄ kusaau sufii kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Wild animals have no water because of you; rivers and streams are dry, and pastures are parched.
translation_verse: Ipeel gba fèefī ki nyàab̀-si, di sá yii ibun fóotì. Ŋŋmi wùn̄ kuteeu pu mooti.

english_verse: Sound the trumpet on Zion, the Lord's sacred hill. Warn everyone to tremble! The judgment day of the Lord is coming soon.
translation_verse: Ní búḿmaan dikantándi Siiyɔn tiŋkin, kúum̀maan mpɔn m-circir jool pu. Kitiŋee pu nib kɔkɔ wunti ń fáá dijinjikil, di sá yii ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dòoń, ŋu tóobiń gba.

english_verse: It will be dark and gloomy with storm clouds overhead. Troops will cover the mountains like thunderclouds. No army this powerful has ever been gathered before or will be gathered again.
translation_verse: Dibɔmbɔŋkpaandi wiiŋŋu dee ŋu-baba, atagbambɔn nì dipɔ̀ńdi wiiŋŋu dee. Inaaki janjakitil dòoń. I pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní ki wīikí bɔ̀m, a lì kii kunyeeu di mɔ́ ki bīiǹ ajoon puee. Baa láá pée ká míǹ ki ká ní ki pée gíti kpá kí ká míǹ jaanjaan kí nīn cáá cá abin abin.

english_verse: Fiery flames surround them; no one escapes. Before they invaded, the land was like Eden; now only a desert remains.
translation_verse: I-nyɔkɔpuee, ŋŋmi di wù, ní i-boon púee, aŋmilimbil nàantí. Kí wàatī í jītée, kitiŋ nìn sɔ̀m̀ kii Eedeen kpaabuee ní, ama i nín jítì ki dóòyee, an kpántì kii kuteeuee. Tiba nì tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmátí kí nyā i-ŋaan.

english_verse: They look like horses and charge like cavalry.
translation_verse: I yaa páaǹnée, a lì kii itaamuee ní, ní i sáń kii bitanjakaliibee.

english_verse: They roar over mountains like noisy chariots, or a mighty army ready for battle. They are a forest fire that feasts on straw.
translation_verse: I gà kuwoou kii janjatɔrɔkub di dàb̀ ki póotí ajoonee, a lì kii ŋŋmi di yaa wù timool, an pòol̄ puee. I dòoń kii dijanjakitil din pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki tātìi gbāaǹ dikɔ̀ndi puee.

english_verse: The very sight of them is frightening.
translation_verse: I yaa páaǹnée, anibul kɔkɔ kóò dinyoondin ní, ní ŋi-nimbiiŋyi ń cúú kpántí.

english_verse: They climb over walls like warriors; they march in columns and never turn aside.
translation_verse: I sáń kii bibaatandambee, ní ki dàb̀ agun kii bijanjaliibee. Báà ŋma pée túĺ u-saŋŋu ní cáaa ki cá, kaa kpèetī kí dī laaba pú.

english_verse: They charge straight ahead, without pushing each other; even arrows and spears cannot make them retreat.
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa pìkil̄ u-juti, di sá yii báà ŋma tàkā u-saŋŋu ní. Laakin aganlaka bée, niin ní bi cátí bi-saŋyi, ní tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí cúú-bi kí síiń.

english_verse: They swarm over city walls and enter our homes; they crawl in through windows, just like thieves.
translation_verse: I gbáb̀ kí bìin̄ kitiŋ pu, ki tɔ̄kɔntí digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee pu ki sáń, ní ki dìŋfī tɔkɔlabin ki kóò adiinni kii unaayuuyee.

english_verse: They make the earth tremble and the heavens shake; the sun and moon turn dark, and stars stop shining.
translation_verse: I yaa bāańee, kitiŋ cìŋkī ní, ní an bí kii kutagbɔŋu làá kìtī kí lítée. Uŋmal nì ŋwìiń kpántí dibɔmbɔndi, ní iŋmalbijaa kaa ti wāĺ.

english_verse: The Lord God leads this army of countless troops, and they obey his commands. The day of his judgment is so terrible that no one can stand it. The Lord's Invitation
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan līī u-janjakitil nyɔkɔpu ki téeń. U-janjakitiŋ ŋin tɔ́ u-marabee wīikí tikpil ní ki pɔ̄ɔ̄. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dal sá ŋwiŋkpaan ní, ŋwiinee nyāŋkì ní ŋma di dāa ŋūǹ kí ŋmátí? Tí fàtīí gítiḿmaan ti-Dindaan cee

english_verse: The Lord said: It isn't too late. You can still return to me with all your heart. Start crying and mourning! Go without eating.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋyunti bāań ní fàtīí gítiń m-cee nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ. Bóob́maan kinyɔkɔ, kí sɔ̄maan ní kí gbàam̀-mi.

english_verse: Don't rip your clothes to show your sorrow. Instead, turn back to me with broken hearts. I am merciful, kind, and caring. I don't easily lose my temper, and I don't like to punish.
translation_verse: An kaa sá ni-wampeeŋkaati ní ní cátí, ama an sá ni-pɔbiliŋ ní ní kpántí.» Fàtīí gítiḿmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cee. U sá ulaŋŋaŋfiti ní u-poon mɔ̄, waa gífí diŋuul malaa, ama ní u-ŋanti wīikí tikpil, ní ki bɔ́ntì kí yàntī ditafadaaldi din pu u sòon̄ee.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God. Perhaps I will change my mind and treat you with mercy. Then you will be blessed with enough grain and wine for offering sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: An yaa yíì, u ŋūǹ kí kpántí u-landɔkɔŋu ní kí bìin̄ ni-pu. Niinee, ni dāa ŋūǹ kí cáań tijimpin nì ndaam saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. Tí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ kí gbàam̀ Unimbɔti

english_verse: Sound the trumpet on Zion! Call the people together. Show your sorrow by going without food.
translation_verse: Búḿmaan dikantándi Siiyɔn tiŋkin, bóob́maan kinyɔkɔ. Yíiḿmaan dikpafikpaandi.

english_verse: Make sure that everyone is fit to worship me. Bring adults, children, babies, and even bring newlyweds from their festivities.
translation_verse: Yíiḿmaan samaa kɔkɔ bí kpāfì circir kpafil. Kpāfìmaan bitikpilib nì binipɔmbi, kí kpáaǹ mbipɔmu mun ŋáaḿee. Unimpucaan nì u-cal ń nyānní kunimpucandiin.

english_verse: Tell my servants, the priests, to cry inside the temple and to offer this prayer near the altar: “Save your people, Lord God! Don't let foreign nations make jokes about us. Don't let them laugh and ask, ‘Where is your God?’ ” The Lord Will Bless the Land
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliibi bisaraaŋaliibi ń yūĺ kunimbɔtidiin kipunyɔkɔ nì nsaraafan kansikin kí nīn sūǹ. Bí nīn lì yii: «Ti-Dindaan, sɔ̄ timbi a-nibul saai. Taa yàntī icoo ń cúú a-nibooliŋu. Taa yàntī anibul ŋin kíǹee ń nīn bèel̄-ti ki lì yii: <Bi-Nimbɔtiuee bí là?>» Ti-Dindaan fōō u-nibul wimmeem

english_verse: The Lord was deeply concerned about his land and had pity on his people.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan cáá u-tiŋki pu dineeŋkpaandi, u súń u-nibul saai.

english_verse: In answer to their prayers he said, “I will give you enough grain, wine, and olive oil to satisfy your needs. No longer will I let you be insulted by the nations.
translation_verse: U fōō u-nibul wimmeem ki bí-bi yii: «Too, m làá tīī-ni tijin nì ndamam nì ŋkpam. Ni làá dāá jī kí díkí. Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, maa ti làá dū-ni kí líiǹ atimbun ŋin kíǹee ŋí nīn bèel̄-ni.

english_verse: An army attacked from the north, but I will chase it into a scorching desert. There it will rot and stink from the Dead Sea to the Mediterranean.” The Lord works wonders
translation_verse: M làá jà ni-nannanliibi bin nyánní ŋgan pú puee kí cùnnì kuteeu pu laakin kūńee. M làá jà bin līī nyɔkɔpuee kí tɔ̄ Ŋyaam mɔɔl poon, ní kí jà bin kíǹ ki pá boonee kí tɔ̄ Meediiteeranee tiŋkuun. Niin ní bijanjaliibi bin kpíìyee làá sūū kí nūukì, di sá yii bi ŋá-ni inikpiti tikpil.

english_verse: and does great things. So tell the soil to celebrate
translation_verse: Sii kitiŋ, taa fàŋkì! Yàntī án nīn mɔ̄ǹ-si á nīn fàal̀, di sá yii ti-Dindaan túń atuŋkpaan.

english_verse: and wild animals to stop being afraid. Grasslands are green again; fruit trees and fig trees are loaded with fruit. Grapevines are covered with grapes.
translation_verse: Ipeel, ní taa fàŋkìmaan. Kuteeu pu mooti bíi túkù ki sɔ̀m̀ fílfil. Isufi bíi lòoǹ, ní fiigi nì fiinyi sufii mun lòon̄ sàka saka.

english_verse: People of Zion, celebrate in honor of the Lord your God! He is generous and has sent the autumn and spring rains in the proper seasons.
translation_verse: Nín̄ bímaan mmɔnni, Siiyɔn yab, nín̄ fàal̀maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu pu, di sá yii u tīī-ni ukpaasiitaa kí fīī-ni. U yāntì ukpaasiitaa nì useetaa nìn̄ tiŋan kii dooooyee.

english_verse: Grain will cover your threshing places; jars will overflow with wine and olive oil. The Lord Will Rescue His People
translation_verse: Tijimpin gbí dinaapaal pu, ní ndamam nì ŋkpam gbí tilɔn ki féeń.

english_verse: I, the Lord your God, will make up for the losses caused by those swarms and swarms of locusts I sent to attack you.
translation_verse: M làá fàtīí téeǹ-ni ni-kpaajinti tin ní anaakitɔmbil nì inaakitoon nì inaakicaan nì inaaki dūu ŋmɔ́ee. Man di nìn dū dijanjakitil gbanti ki tɔ́ ni-pu.

english_verse: My people, you will eat until you are satisfied. Then you will praise me for the wonderful things I have done. Never again will you be put to shame.
translation_verse: Ni làá jī kí díkí, ní kí nyɔ̄ŋkì man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un di túń atunnyaan ki tīī-nee. Icoo pée gíti kpá kí jī m-nibul jaanjaan.

english_verse: Israel, you will know that I stand at your side. I am the Lord your God— there are no other gods. Never again will you be put to shame. The Lord Will Work Wonders The Lord said:
translation_verse: Niin ní nimbi Isirayeel yab làá béé yii m bí ni-kansikin. Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, ní maa cáá juti. Icoo pée gíti kpá kí jī m-nibul jaanjaan.»

english_verse: and gambled to see who would get my people; they sold boys and girls to pay for prostitutes and wine.
translation_verse: M làá dāá yàntī maamaacikpaambi ń nyā kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ pu. Fatiku nì ŋŋmi nì nnyiim tagbaŋŋi làá dāá nyā.

english_verse: You people of Tyre and Sidon and you Philistines, why are you doing this? Are you trying to get even with me? I'll strike back before you know what's happened.
translation_verse: Ŋwìiń dāa kpántí dibɔmbɔndi ní uŋmal ń dāá mántí kii fatikuee, kí wàatī ní ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu ń nín bàń. Dinyoondi nì ŋwiŋkpaan dal dee ŋu-baba.

english_verse: I am Amos. And I raised sheep near the town of Tekoa when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel. Two years before the earthquake, the Lord gave me several messages about Israel,
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin Amoosi upikpaal un sá Teekoowa tiŋkinee sòon̄ee sɔ̀. Abin ali kí wàatī kitiŋ ń cìŋkèe, ti-Dindaan nìn lēē tin u làá sòoǹ Isirayeel beel puee bɔti ki dàkā-u. Ŋyunti gbantee, Oosiyasi di nìn sá Juuda tiŋki bɔtiu ní Joowaasi jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn sá Isirayeel tiŋki bɔtiu.

english_verse: and I said: When the Lord roars from Jerusalem, pasturelands and Mount Carmel dry up and turn brown. Judgment on Syria
translation_verse: Amoosi nìn lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan téeń mpɔn doooo Siiyɔn jool pu, u yāntì bi gbìl̄ u-nyɔkɔ pu doooo Jeerusaleem. Niinee kupikpaau mooti fáaḿ, ní Kaarmeel jool pu mooti kūń.» Ti-Dindaan wòon̄ Isirayeel yab nì abee ŋin pìlīǹ-bee Siirii yab

english_verse: The Lord said: I will punish Syria for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They dragged logs with spikes over the people of Gilead.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Damaasi yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil, bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu. An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá. Bi dū apinjal ŋin inaa dátí ki kpátí atannaapikee ki nàn̄ Galaadi yab.

english_verse: Now I will burn down the palaces and fortresses of King Hazael and of King Benhadad.
translation_verse: An puee m làá sēē Asayeel beecindi ŋŋmi, Been-Adaadi beecindi làá wà kí lítí.

english_verse: I will break through the gates of Damascus. I will destroy the people of Wicked Valley and the ruler of Beth-Eden. Then the Syrians will be dragged as prisoners to Kir. I, the Lord, have spoken! Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: M làá wīī Damaasi tiŋki punyɔkɔki kpàlkaati. M làá kúntí ikpiti tantakal tiŋki bɔtiu, nì un kā mmɔn tiŋki pu dibeelee, ní kí yàntī bí cúú Aram yab kí cùnnì Kiiri tiŋkin kuyuŋu.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Fiiliistii yab

english_verse: The Lord said: I will punish Philistia for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They dragged off my people from town after town to sell them as slaves to the Edomites.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Gaasaa yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil, bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu. An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá. Bi cáá ditimbummɔndi nib ki nyáfiǹ Eedoom tiŋkin yab.

english_verse: That's why I will burn down the walls and fortresses of the city of Gaza.
translation_verse: M làá sēē Gaasaa tiŋki gundi ŋŋmi, ní ki-beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí.

english_verse: I will destroy the king of Ashdod and the ruler of Ashkelon. I will strike down Ekron, and that will be the end of the Philistines. I, the Lord, have spoken! Judgment on Phoenicia
translation_verse: M làá kúntí Asidoodi tiŋki bɔtiu, nì un sá Asikeelɔn tiŋki bɔtiuee. M làá dū m-ba kí bíití Eekrɔn yab, kí yàntī Fiiliistii yab ń kúntí.» Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ. Tiir yab

english_verse: The Lord said: I will punish Phoenicia for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They broke their treaty and dragged off my people from town after town to sell them as slaves to the Edomites.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Tiir yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil, bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu. An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá. Bi cáá ditimbummɔndi nib ki nyáfiǹ Eedoom tiŋki yab, kun puee baa dū kunabitiiu poondi ki yíiń tiba.

english_verse: That's why I will send flames to burn down the city of Tyre along with its fortresses. Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: M làá sēē Tiir tiŋki ŋŋmi, ní ki-beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí.» Eedoom yab

english_verse: The Lord said: I will punish Edom for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They killed their own relatives and were so terribly furious that they showed no mercy.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Eedoom yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil, bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu. An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá. Bi kùl̄ ki bīiǹ bi-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab boon nì ntàataajimu. Baa pée súń bi-saai báà fiii. Bi fōō mbum an kaa kúntí, bi-ŋuul kaa cáá yii an sɔ̄ŋkì.

english_verse: Now I will send fire to wipe out the fortresses of Teman and Bozrah. Judgment on Ammon
translation_verse: M làá sēē Teeman tiŋki ŋŋmi, ní Bɔsiraa beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí.» Amɔn yab

english_verse: The Lord said: I will punish Ammon for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. In Gilead they ripped open pregnant women, just to take the land.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Amɔn yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil, bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu. An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá. Kun puee bi pūtì Galaadi tiŋkin pɔdambi kí ŋmā kí wàan̄ bi-tiŋki.

english_verse: Now I will send fire to destroy the walls and fortresses of Rabbah. Enemies will shout and attack like a whirlwind.
translation_verse: M làá sēē Raaba tiŋki gundi ŋŋmi, ní ki-beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí. An dāa sá ikuŋkuunti nì kujaau wiiŋŋu dal, utaa nì kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kun pɔ̄ɔ̄yee wiiŋŋu ní.

english_verse: Ammon's king and leaders will be dragged away. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá cúú bi-bɔtiu, kí kpáaǹ u-kàliŋkpilib kí cùnnì kuyuŋu.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: The Lord said: I will punish Moab for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They made lime from the bones of the king of Edom.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Moowaab yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil, bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu. An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá. Bi wùn̄ Eedoom bɔtiu kpabiŋ an kpántì ŋfantam.

english_verse: Now I will send fire to destroy the fortresses of Kerioth. Battle shouts and trumpet blasts will be heard as I destroy Moab
translation_verse: M làá sēē Moowaab tiŋki ŋŋmi, ní Keeriyooti beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí. Moowaab yab làá kpú kuwookpaaŋŋu nì ijanjakuŋkuunti nì iyin dibúndi poon.

english_verse: with its king and leaders. I, the Lord, have spoken! Judgment on Judah
translation_verse: M làá kpɔ̀ bi-bɔtiu, kí kpáaǹ u-kàliŋkpilib dicilpu.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Juuda yab

english_verse: The Lord said: I will punish Judah for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They have rejected my teachings and refused to obey me. They were led astray by the same false gods their ancestors worshiped.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Juuda yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil, bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu. An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá. Bi fá m-marab, kaa nóó m-koobiliŋ. Kii bi-naanjab nín nìn nóó awaa ŋi kíil̀-bi puee, míǹ ní bi yāntì awaa gbanti mun kíil̀-bi.

english_verse: Now I will send fire on Judah and destroy the fortresses of Jerusalem. Judgment on Israel
translation_verse: M làá sēē Juuda tiŋki ŋŋmi, Jeerusaleem beeciŋŋi làá wà kí lítí.» Isirayeel yab

english_verse: The Lord said: I will punish Israel for countless crimes, and I won't change my mind. They sell honest people for money, and the needy are sold for the price of sandals.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Isirayeel yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil, bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu. An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá. Bi nyáfí deedeedaan kí ká animbil, ki nyáfí usoodaan kalaa nimbiliŋ

english_verse: They smear the poor in the dirt and push aside those who are helpless. My holy name is dishonored, because fathers and sons sleep with the same young women.
translation_verse: Bi nyìitī uwɔfi yil ki gùl̀ ntamin, kaa sòoǹ unandaan bɔti deedee. Unil nì u-jipɔɔn kpáfí usapɔɔn pu, ki ŋáań míǹ ki bíiĺ man circir yindi.

english_verse: They lie down beside altars on clothes taken as security for loans. And they drink wine in my temple, wine bought with the money they received from fines.
translation_verse: Ipaan in kɔkɔ pu bi jáaḿ Unimbɔtee, abɔkuti ŋin bi fōol̀ toolima bisoodambi ceeyee pu ní bi dɔ̀, ki nyù ndaam min bi fìkēe bi-Nimbɔtiu diikun.

english_verse: Israel, the Amorites were there when you entered Canaan. They were tall as cedars and strong as oaks. But I wiped them out— I destroyed their branches and their roots.
translation_verse: Ama bi-puee m nìn kúntì Amɔɔr yab. Binib gbanti nìn kpílifì ní ki yáà kii seedir nì seeni sufiiyee. M kúntì bi-kɔkɔ pílpil.

english_verse: I had rescued you from Egypt, and for forty years I had led you through the desert. Then I gave you the land of the Amorites.
translation_verse: Man di nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin, ki kpōotì-ni abin imuŋku ili kuteeun ní ŋmā kí fōō Amɔɔr yab tiŋki.

english_verse: I chose some of you to be prophets and others to be Nazirites. People of Israel, you know this is true. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: M lēē ni-jipɔmbi biba bí nīn sá m-bɔnaatiliibi, ki lēē ni-naacimpɔmbi biba bí dū bi-ba kí sú-mi. An kaa sá mimmaaa, Isirayeel yab?» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: But you commanded the prophets not to speak their message, and you pressured the Nazirites into drinking wine.
translation_verse: Ama ni nyūntì bin dū bi-ba ki sú-mee ndaam, ki pīiǹ m-bɔnaatiliibi nsan yii bí taa ti nàatī m-bɔti.

english_verse: And so I will crush you, just as a wagon full of grain crushes the ground.
translation_verse: «An puee m làá tāā kí mátí-ni, kii tɔrɔku un tú tiwan tikpilee nín tà ki mátí tin kɔkɔ dɔ̄ u-saŋŋu pu puee ní.

english_verse: No matter how fast you run, you won't escape. No matter how strong you are, you will lose your strength and your life.
translation_verse: Binib bin yáb̀ee kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí, bipɔɔbi pɔŋŋu kaa làá kèetī-bi, bijanjamɔntiibi kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí fīī bi-maŋfal.

english_verse: Even if you are an expert with a bow and arrow, you will retreat. And you won't get away alive, not even if you run fast or ride a horse.
translation_verse: Upintɔl kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí yūĺ kí tɔ̄. Un ŋūǹ ki sáńee kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí. Utanjakal kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí fīī u-maŋfal.

english_verse: You may be brave and strong, but you will run away, stripped naked. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Ujanjal un cáá dibaatandee làá dāá dū u-janjawanti kí fá, kí sāǹ kí kátí ŋwiin gbanti». Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: People of Israel, I rescued you from Egypt. Now listen to my judgment against you.
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab, nimbi bin di sá kudicaŋu kun ti-Dindaan nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee, pīlifìmaan tin ti-Dindaan cáá kí sòoǹ ni-puee.

english_verse: Of all nations on earth, you are the only one I have chosen. That's why I will punish you because of your sins. The Work of a Prophet
translation_verse: «Kitiŋ pu dicaŋŋi kɔkɔ poonee, nimbi baba ní m lēē ki kpèé. An pu ní m làá dáaĺ ni-tafal ikpiti in kɔkɔ ni ŋáaǹee pu.» Unimbɔti yaa sòon̄ee, u-bɔnaatiliu kaa ŋūǹ kí nīn ŋmí

english_verse: Can two people walk together without agreeing to meet?
translation_verse: Binib bili cá nsan kaa kpáfì ki sòon̄ ki bɔ́ntàaa?

english_verse: Does a lion roar in the forest unless it has caught a victim? Does it growl in its den unless it is eating?
translation_verse: Gbikinti yaa kaa ká upeel kí cúú, u làá nīn sūǹ kupɔɔun fámaaa? Kigbikintibiki yaa kaa cúú tiba, kì làá nīn bí ki-kɔŋkooŋŋun ki mùuǹaaa?

english_verse: How can anyone catch a bird without using a net? Does a trap spring shut unless something is caught?
translation_verse: Kutaliŋŋu sàtī unoon fám baa dū tiba kí píĺaaa? Kutaliŋŋu mun tòó fám kaa pée sàl̄ báà tibaaa?

english_verse: Isn't the whole city frightened when the trumpet signals an attack? Isn't the Lord the one who brings disaster on a city?
translation_verse: Bi búǹ dibaŋwul kitiŋin tifaandi kaa cútí binibaaa? Dinimbinaamandi kóòń kitiŋin kaa nyánní ti-Dindaan ceeee?

english_verse: Whatever the Lord God plans to do, he tells his servants, the prophets.
translation_verse: Míǹ mbaantiim ní ti-Dindaan kaa ŋáań tiba kaa lēē ki dàkā u-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi.

english_verse: Everyone is terrified when a lion roars— and ordinary people become prophets when the Lord God speaks. Samaria Is Doomed
translation_verse: Gbikinti yaa téeńee, ŋma sá-u ní kaa làá fàŋkì? Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti yaa sòon̄ee, ŋma làá yíí kaa làá nàatī? Samaarii bɔsooŋyi

english_verse: Here is a message for the leaders of Philistia and Egypt— tell everyone to come together on the hills of Samaria. Let them see the injustice and the lawlessness in that city.
translation_verse: Asidoodi tiŋki beeciŋŋi yilpu nì Eejipiti tiŋki beeciŋŋi yilpuee, ní bāakìmaan kí lì yii: «Kóoǹ kí kpāfìmaan Samaarii jooŋŋi pu kí kpèè fìkil fikil un bí kitiŋ gbantinee, nì tipɔmbɔti tin ŋáań ki-nee!»

english_verse: The Lord has said that they don't even know how to do right. They have become rich from violence and robbery.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di lī yii: «Samaarii yab kaa nyí kí tɔ̄ ditummɔntiil. Tiwaŋfìkikaal nì tinaayuwan ní bi kùl̄ ki gbéeǹ bi-dimɔntiŋ poon.»

english_verse: And so the Lord God has sworn that they will be surrounded. Enemies will break through their defenses and steal their treasures.
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ sii Samaarii tiŋki pu ki lī yii: «Unannanli làá dāá màntīí tū a-tiŋki, kí gbākal̀ a-pɔŋŋu ní kí fūkul̀ a-dimɔntiŋ wanti.» Difiil nín bí la dee?

english_verse: The Lord has promised that only a few from Samaria will escape with their lives and with some broken pieces of their beds and couches. It will be like when a shepherd rescues two leg bones and part of a sheep's ear from the jaws of a lion. The Altars at Bethel
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Gbikinti yaa cúú upiiyee, upikpaal dátí ayaka ali nì kitafakatii ní kí fōō u-nyɔkɔn. Míǹ mbaantiim ní bi làá dāá fīī Isirayeel yab bin kóò Samaarii tiŋkin, ki dɔ̄ dijal pu àá ndoo puee.» Ti-Dindaan kpáafì Isirayeel yab

english_verse: The Lord God All-Powerful told me to speak this message against Jacob's descendants:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Ní pīlifìmaan kí dū tibɔkpaafikaal nee kí nàatī Jaakɔb naantiibi.

english_verse: When I, the Lord, punish Israel for their sins, I will destroy the altars at Bethel. Even the corners of the altar will be left in the dirt.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāá dáaĺ Isirayeel yab tafal bi-kpitii puee, m làá dāá gbá kí wìil̀ isaraafan in bí Beeteel tiŋkinee kɔkɔ. M làá dāá gbá kí kéetí nsaraafan yiŋyi ní í nīn kíǹ ki dɔ̄ kitiŋ.

english_verse: I will tear down winter homes and summer homes. Houses decorated with ivory and all other mansions will be gone forever. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: M làá dāá wìil̀ bi-dikpaaŋŋi, nì bi-diwaammu. M làá dāá wìil̀ adiin ŋin pu bi nákáǹ akuntinyin ki nyáantì-ŋee, adikpaan kɔkɔ làá dāá lítí.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ!

english_verse: You women of Samaria are fat cows! You mistreat and abuse the poor and needy, then you say to your husbands, “Bring us more drinks!”
translation_verse: Nimbi Samaarii yab nimpoobi, nimbi bin jíń ki gbīfiǹ kii Baasan tiŋkin nasaliiyee, ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti nee. Ni mùul̄ biwɔfib, ki sàantí binandambi ní ki lì ni-calib yii: «Ní cáań ndaam tí nyɔ̀!»

english_verse: I, the Lord God, have sworn by my own name that your time is coming. Not one of you will be left— you will be taken away by sharp hooks.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí circiree, pūtì ki lī yii: «Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń, bi làá dāá dū ipiin kí lɔ̀kɔ̄-ni, kí dáaĺ-ni kí kpáàá búntí kii njɔmpiin nín cútí ujɔm puee ní.

english_verse: You will be dragged through holes in your city walls, and you will be thrown toward Harmon. I, the Lord, have spoken! Israel Refuses To Obey The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kitiŋ guŋŋi laakin bátì bátìi lítèe ní bi làá dī kí cáá-ni kí nyāntí, báà ŋma ń nīn kpèé u-nimbiin. Bi làá dāá cáá-ni kí tɔ̄ ŋgan pú.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ! Inyimɔn nimbɔtinool

english_verse: Come to Bethel and Gilgal. Sin all you want! Offer sacrifices the next morning and bring a tenth of your crops on the third day.
translation_verse: «Ní cùmaan Beeteel tiŋkin kí já nì mi, kí cù Giilgaal tiŋkin kí mɔ̀tīí já nì mi tikpil. Ni yaa bàn̄ kutaafaauee, ní cáań kuwaŋkuluu kí ŋá-mi saraa, ní ŋwintataatee ní cáań ni-saalaatiiti.

english_verse: Bring offerings to show me how thankful you are. Gladly bring more offerings than I have demanded. You really love to do this. I, the Lord God, have spoken! How the Lord Warned Israel
translation_verse: Ní wà kpɔnɔb bin bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nsaraafan pu kí ŋá ijaam saraabi. Ní bāakì kí tùkù báà ŋma nlammɔntiim saraabi bin ni ŋá ki tīī-mee, kun puee nimbi Isirayeel yab nín là puee dee!» Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ. Ti-Dindaan kpáafì Isirayeel yab ki gīī

english_verse: I, the Lord, took away the food from every town and village, but still you rejected me.
translation_verse: «Ni-tiŋkpaammu kɔkɔnee, m yāntì ŋkùm cúú-ni, ki ŋmīntì-ni tijin ni-timbilimmun, ama ní naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Three months before harvest, I kept back the rain. Sometimes I would let it fall on one town or field but not on another, and pastures dried up.
translation_verse: «Maa yāntì utaa jōō ni-satin ki tin sāā iŋmal ita kudiceeu ń bàń. M yāntì utaa nìn̄ kitiŋ kiban kaa yāntì u nìn̄ kin kíǹee poon, ki yāntì utaa nìn̄ bukpaa bubɔn, ní bun ni u nìn̄ee kpaajinti kūń.»

english_verse: People from two or three towns would go to a town that still had water, but it wasn't enough. Even then you rejected me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: «Ntimu tikpil nib yíkì ki cūtì kitiŋ kiban ki kpìntī ki nyàab̀ nnyim kí nyɔ̀, ama kaa ká ki nyùn̄ ki bál̀, nì míǹ kɔkɔee, naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I dried up your grain fields; your gardens and vineyards turned brown. Locusts ate your fig trees and olive orchards, but even then you rejected me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: «M dū iween ki tɔ́ ni-kpaajinti, di sá tì dáá yú tisatin kaa láá bīń ní ki bíi kōō àá ki bíi sù. M yāntì inaakitoon ŋmɔ́ ki bíil̀ ni-kuŋfaati nì fiinyi sufii kpaaŋŋi, nì ni-fiigi sufii nì ni-ɔliifi sufii, ama ní naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I did terrible things to you, just as I did to Egypt— I killed your young men in war; I let your horses be stolen, and I made your camp stink with dead bodies. Even then you rejected me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: «M dū bìlbil kúm ki tɔ́ ni-waŋkuti pu kii m nín nìn ŋá pu Eejipiti tiŋkinee. M yāntì binannanliibi kūū ni-nipɔmbi, ki cútì ni-taamui ki cáa búntì. M yāntì ni-nikpiliŋ sūū ki núukì ki kɔ́-ni fíŋfiŋ ni-naapaal pu, ama ní naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I destroyed many of you, just as I did the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. You were a burning stick I rescued from the fire. But even then you rejected me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: «M nāaǹ ni-kansikin biba, a lì kii m nín nìn nāaǹ Soodoom nì Goomoora timmu puee. Ni-kansikin bin ŋmátèe sá kii kisanteei kin bi tātèe ní, ama ní naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Now, Israel, I myself will deal with you. Get ready to face your God!
translation_verse: «An puee Isirayeel, kpèè m nín làá ŋá-si puee sɔ̀. Kii tin m làá ŋá-see puee, á bɔ́ntí a-ba kí cīití man a-Nimbɔtiu.»

english_verse: I created the mountains and the wind. I let humans know what I am thinking. I bring darkness at dawn and step over hills. I am the Lord God All-Powerful!
translation_verse: Di sá yii úǹ di náań ajoon, ki náań kubuŋu, ki lèekī tin u làá ŋée ki dàkà unil. U dù ŋwiimpu kí kpántí kunyeeu ní ki tɔ́kɔ́ kitiŋ kɔkɔ yilpu ki còom̄. Úǹ ní bi yíì yii: <Ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan>.

english_verse: Listen, nation of Israel, to my mournful message:
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan tibɔti nee, ŋkpiisilan ŋun m làá gāā ni-pu nee.

english_verse: You, dearest Israel, have fallen, never to rise again— you lie deserted in your own land, with no one to help you up.
translation_verse: Isirayeel bí kii usapɔɔn un kpíì ki dɔ̄ gbàlaayee ní. U lítì ki dɔ̄ ki gíti kpá kí yīkì. U pée gbíntì ki dɔ̄ u-tiŋki pu ní báà ubɔ kaa bí kí yòon̄-u!

english_verse: The Lord God has warned, “From every ten soldiers only one will be left; from a thousand troops, only a hundred will survive.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ Isirayeel nibul pu puee sèé: «Kitiŋ kiba yaa tú bijanjaliibi kutuku, bijanjaliibi dilaataal di làá kínní. Kitimbilii kiba yaa tú bijanjaliibi dilaataal, bijanjaliibi saalaa di làá kínní.» Unil yaa kaa kpántì u-ba, u kpá kí ká difiil

english_verse: The Lord keeps saying, “Israel, turn back to me and you will live!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Isirayeel yab puee sèé: «Ni yaa là kí nīn bi dimaŋfalinee, nyàab̀maan-mi.

english_verse: Don't go to Gilgal or Bethel or even to Beersheba. Gilgal will be dragged away, and Bethel will end up as nothing.”
translation_verse: Ama ní taa nyàab̀-mi Beeteel tiŋkin, kí taa cù Giilgaal tiŋkin, ni-taal ń taa tāā Beerseeba tiŋkin. Giilgaal yab kɔkɔ làá búntí kuyuŋu, ní Beeteel, Unimbɔti diiku ń kpántí kuwaadii.»

english_verse: Turn back to the Lord, you descendants of Joseph, and you will live. If you don't, the Lord will attack like fire. Bethel will burn to the ground, and no one can save it.
translation_verse: Ni yaa là kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee, nyàab̀maan ti-Dindaan. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, u làá dāá jēetí Jooseefi yab pu kii ŋŋmee. U làá wà ti-kɔkɔ Beeteel tiŋkin, ní báà uniseen dāa kpá kí gbíntí-ŋu.

english_verse: You people are doomed! You twist the truth and trample on justice.
translation_verse: Ni yāntì ibaamɔn túŋkì kátí kati, ní kaa dū tin bí deedeeyee ki yíiń tiba!

english_verse: But the Lord created the stars and put them in place. He turns darkness to dawn and daylight to darkness; he scoops up the ocean and empties it on the earth.
translation_verse: Úǹ di náań kuŋmalbicukuu kɔkɔ. Úǹ di yàntī dibɔmbɔndi ń kpántí ntaafaawalifi, ki yàntī ŋwiimpu kpántí kunyeeu. Úǹ di yíì tiŋku nyim ní ki cáá-mì ki yàantí kitiŋ pu. Úǹ ní bi yíì yii <Ti-Dindaan>.

english_verse: God destroys mighty soldiers and strong fortresses. Choose Good Instead of Evil! The Lord said:
translation_verse: Úǹ di yàntī bí nàan̄ upɔɔl, ní kí nàan̄ kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee.

english_verse: You people hate judges and honest witnesses;
translation_verse: Bi ná un sòoǹ tibɔti ti-puee, kaa là bi-nimbil ń wāl̀ bin sòoǹ ibaamɔnee.

english_verse: you abuse the poor and demand heavy taxes from them. You have built expensive homes, but you won't enjoy them; you have planted vineyards, but you will get no wine.
translation_verse: Ni mùul̄ binandambi, ki fòol̄ bi-kpaajinti dijandi. An puee naa làá kɔ́ adinyaan ŋin ni máń ki yóoǹee poon, kaa làá nyɔ̀ ni-fiinyi sufimɔntiŋ ŋin ni kùn̄ee damam.

english_verse: I am the Lord, and I know your terrible sins. You cheat honest people and take bribes; you rob the poor of justice.
translation_verse: M nyí ni-kpitii nín wīikí tikpil puee, nì ni-yìntitam nín gíti lákatì mara pu puee. Ni sá deedeedambi nannanliibi, ki fòol̄ tiwampɔkaal tin bi cáa ŋēeb̀ ni-nyɔmmuee. Ni pìintí nsan ibɔsoon laŋki bí taa sòoǹ biwɔfib bɔti.

english_verse: Times are so evil that anyone with good sense will keep quiet.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti sá mbusu yuntiŋu ní, an pu ní un sá uciŋfitee kíǹ ki ŋmí.

english_verse: If you really want to live, you must stop doing wrong and start doing right. I, the Lord God All-Powerful, will then be on your side, just as you claim I am.
translation_verse: Ní nyàab̀maan kí nīn ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee, kí fàtī ni-boon kí tīī ikpiti. Niinee ni làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin, ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan ń lafun nín̄ bí ni-cee, kii nimbi ni-ba nín lì puee.

english_verse: Choose good instead of evil! See that justice is done. Maybe I, the Lord All-Powerful, will be kind to what's left of your people. Judgment Is Coming
translation_verse: Nín̄ námaan tikpitil, kí nīn néeń tiŋan. Ní nīn sòoǹ tibɔti ti-pu ibɔsoon laŋki. An yaa yíì, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá sɔ̄ nimbi Jooseefi yab bin kíǹ nee saai.

english_verse: This is what the Lord has sworn: Noisy crying will be heard in every town and street. Even farmers will be told to mourn for the dead, together with those who are paid to mourn.
translation_verse: An puee ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Bi làá dāá nīn gbìl̀ nsiim pu imɔŋkijaa kɔkɔ pu, dituweel làá dāá nīn gà adan kɔkɔ pu. Bi làá dāá bòotīń bikpaabi kusaau bí dāan̄ dinisibil, ní kí yíiń bin gà ikpiisilanee bí dāá gāā.

english_verse: Your vineyards will be filled with crying and weeping, because I will punish you. I, the Lord, have spoken! When the Lord Judges
translation_verse: M yaa láa jítì ni-kansikinee, binib làá dāá nīn gà ikpiisilan ni-fiinyi sufii satin.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dal

english_verse: You look forward to the day when the Lord comes to judge. But you are in for trouble! It won't be a time of sunshine; all will be darkness.
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí bin kā ki cí ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋuee! Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu gbanti làá dāá nīn sá ba ní ki tīī-ni ní? Ŋu làá dāá nīn sá dibɔmbɔndi wiiŋŋu ní, kaa sá ŋwalifi wiiŋŋu.

english_verse: You will run from a lion, only to meet a bear. You will escape to your house, rest your hand on the wall, and be bitten by a snake.
translation_verse: Ŋu sá kii unil nín sáń gbikinti kí cùú tū digbiŋgbil nsanni puee ní. Àá u nín kùǹ u-dumpu ki dū u-ŋal ki nyīī digundi ní ukoobu jú-uee ní.

english_verse: The day when the Lord judges will be dark, very dark, without a ray of light. What the Lord Demands
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dāa sá ŋwalifi níii? Aayee, ŋu dāa sá dibɔmbɔndi ní, ŋu dāa bɔ̀ǹ ní kpìmm, ŋuaa dāa wāĺ báà fiii. Unimbɔti kaa là Isirayeel yab jaamii

english_verse: I, the Lord, hate and despise your religious celebrations and your times of worship.
translation_verse: M ná ni-jiŋaalib, maa pée là kí wāl̀-bi. Ni-kpafiŋ kóò m-poon ki lèekī baadakam.

english_verse: I won't accept your offerings or animal sacrifices— not even your very best.
translation_verse: Bisaraawɔkaabi nì tijimpin saraabi bin ni ŋáań ki tìì-mee kaa fáatiǹ-mi. Ni-waŋkuti tin bí màlmal ni cáa ŋáań-mi saraayee, maa fàtīi kpèé gba.

english_verse: No more of your noisy songs! I won't listen when you play your harps.
translation_verse: Ní kpáaǹ ni-laŋyi wookuee kí nyā niin. Maa ti là kí gbìl̄ ni-bati pu.

english_verse: But let justice and fairness flow like a river that never runs dry.
translation_verse: Ama ní yàntī ibaamɔn ń nīn pùub̀ kii nnyimee, ní tin bí deedeeyee ń nīn bí kii mbun ŋun kaa fóotée.

english_verse: Israel, for forty years you wandered in the desert, without bringing offerings or sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: «Isirayeel yab, ni nín nìn ŋá abin imuŋku ili kuteeunee, ni nìn ŋá tiwaŋkuti nì tijimpin saraabi ki tīī-maaa?

english_verse: Now you will have to carry the two idols you made— Sakkuth, the one you call king, and Kaiwan, the one you built in the shape of a star.
translation_verse: Ama díǹ pu nee, ni tūntí awaa ŋin nimbi ni-ba kpítèe, din ni yíì Siikuuti di sá ni-bɔtiu nì ni-nimbɔtiuee, nì din ni yíì Kiiyuuni di sá ni-ŋmalbijau nì ni-nimbɔtiuee.

english_verse: I will force you to march as captives beyond Damascus. I, the Lord God All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_verse: An puee m làá cáá-ni kí cùnnì kuyuŋu laakin dátì ki jítiǹ Damaasee.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. U-yindi di sá Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan.

english_verse: Do you rulers in Jerusalem and in the city of Samaria feel safe and at ease? Everyone bows down to you, and you think you are better than any other nation. But you are in for trouble!
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí nimbi bin kóò Siiyɔn jool pu ni-pɔbiliŋ sɔ̀m̀ee, nimbi bin kóò Samaarii jool pu kaa fàŋkí yii tiba ŋūǹ kí ŋá-nee. Binib lì yii atimbun kɔkɔ kansikinee, nimbi di līī, ní ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab kpèé ni-pú!

english_verse: Look what happened to the cities of Calneh, powerful Hamath, and Gath in Philistia. Are you greater than any of those kingdoms?
translation_verse: Ní cùmaan Kalnee tiŋkin kí kpèè! Niinee ní cù Amaati kitiŋkpaaŋŋin kí kpèè. Míǹ boonee, ní sìntī Gaati tiŋkin Fiiliistii yab cee. Ni sɔ́ǹ ntimu gbantaaa? Ni-tiŋki wāā ki jítiǹ bi-tiŋkaaa?

english_verse: You are cruel, and you forget the coming day of judgment.
translation_verse: Ni nín bíi téekí mbusu wiiŋŋu ń taa bàń kɔŋkɔnnee, ni bíi yíì tipɔmbɔti wiiŋŋu ń bàń malaa dee.

english_verse: You rich people lounge around on beds with ivory posts, while dining on the meat of your lambs and calves.
translation_verse: Ni dɔ̄ idoomɔnti in pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee pu ki dɔ̄ ni-lambammu pu ki ŋmóò ni-picaŋkpunti pibiliŋ nì ni-nacaŋkpunti nabiliŋ nanti.

english_verse: You sing foolish songs to the music of harps, and you make up new tunes, just as David used to do.
translation_verse: Ni bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu ki gà ilan. Ni mɔ́ɔ́ tiwambɔɔkaal tipɔn kii Daafiidee.

english_verse: You drink all the wine you want and wear expensive perfume, but you don't care about the ruin of your nation.
translation_verse: Ni nyù ndamam asambikpaan poon, ki ŋmìtī ikpafi in sɔ́fèe, ama naa bí ki sūǹ mbusu un dòoń Jooseefi yab puee pu.

english_verse: So you will be the first to be dragged off as captives; your good times will end.
translation_verse: An pu ní kɔŋkɔnnee, nimbi di làá nīn sá bipeepeekaabi bin bi làá cúú kí cùnnì kuyuŋuee. Ní nimbi biwutijoodambi kitil nee ń kúntí. Samaarii tiŋki làá wīī

english_verse: The Lord God All-Powerful has sworn by his own name: “You descendants of Jacob make me angry by your pride, and I hate your fortresses. And so I will surrender your city and possessions to your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan pūtì ki lī yii: «Isirayeel yab lambil kóò ki dóotí-mi, m ná bi-dimɔntiŋ. An puee m làá dū Samaarii tiŋki kí ŋá ki-nannanliibi ŋaan.»

english_verse: If only ten of you survive by hiding in a house you will still die.
translation_verse: Binib saalaa di yaa kíǹ kudicaŋu poon, bi làá kpú.

english_verse: As you carry out a corpse to prepare it for burial, your relative in the house will ask, “Are there others?” You will answer, “No!” Then your relative will reply, “Be quiet! Don't dare mention the name of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Bi-nabiki làá nyāntí bi-wuntee kí wà ŋŋmi. Ubɔ yaa kíǹ ki bí poon diikunee, kinabikee làá dāá bàlifì udaan yii: «Ubɔ gíti bí ki kútì a-pu niinaaa?» Ní úǹ ń dāá kíí yii: «Aayee, ubɔ gíti kpá.» Ní kinabikee ń dāá lì yii: «Ŋmīĺ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ! Ubɔ ń taa ti pútí ti-Dindaan yindi!»

english_verse: At the Lord's command, houses great and small will be smashed to pieces.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan yaa pée tīī maree, adikpaan wùtī ní kí lítí, ní ndiwaamu ń fáá iwèeń. Dijajil mili pu fám

english_verse: Horses can't gallop on rocks; oceans can't be plowed. But you have turned justice and fairness into bitter poison.
translation_verse: Itaamu sáń ataŋkpajal puɔɔɔ? Inaa kù ataŋkpajal puɔɔɔ? Kin ba ŋá ní ni dū ibaamɔn ki kpántì tilool, ki dū tin bí deedeeyee ki kpántì ntuntun?

english_verse: But the Lord God All-Powerful will send a nation to attack you people of Israel. They will capture Lebo-Hamath in the north, Arabah Creek in the south, and everything in between.
translation_verse: Ama man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé: «Isirayeel yab, m làá yàntī ditimbundi diba ń jáǹ-ni ní kí nà-ni, kí yòon̄ Leeboo-Amaati tiŋki ŋgan pú kí tin cáá bà Arabaa buŋŋu ŋgiil pú.»

english_verse: The Lord God showed me that he is going to send locusts to attack your crops. It will happen after the king has already been given his share of the grain and before the rest of the grain has been harvested.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín nìn lēē tin ki dàkā-mee sɔ̀. U nìn bíi nāantí inaakitoon. An nìn sá ŋyunti ŋun bi gāā ubɔti taamui mooti ki dóò ní timool fātìi kíĺ ki bíi túkùee.

english_verse: In my vision the locusts ate every crop in the land, and I said to the Lord, “Please forgive your nation. It's so weak. How can it survive?”
translation_verse: Inaakitoonee nín dāa ŋmɔ́ kitiŋee pu mɔsɔnti kɔkɔee ní m bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m gbāam̀-si ní, dū a-nibul kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, mana ní bi làá ŋmátí, bíǹ bin kaa pée náaǹ nee?»

english_verse: Then the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.” A Vision of Fire
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kpántì nlandɔkɔ ní ki bí yii: «Án kaa làá bàń míǹ!» Dileedakal dililiitiil: ŋŋmi

english_verse: The Lord showed me that he is going to send a ball of fire to burn up everything on earth, including the ocean.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti gíti lēē tibɔti tiba ki dàkā-mi. U nìn cáá ŋŋmi ki sòoǹ u-nibul bɔti. Ŋŋmifaam nìn yāntì nnyim min dɔ̄ kitiŋ taapuee fóotì ní ki wùn̄ Isirayeel tiŋki búkú buku.

english_verse: Then I said, “Won't you please stop? How can our weak nation survive?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m gbāam̀-si, yàntēe! Yaa sá fám, mana ní a-nibul Isirayeel yab bin kaa náaǹ nee làá ŋmátí?»

english_verse: Again the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.” A Vision of a Measuring Line
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan kpántì nlandɔkɔ ní ki bí yii: «Tin bí nee mun kaa làá bàń míǹ!» Dileedakal ditataatiil: ŋŋmiiŋmantikaa

english_verse: The Lord showed me a vision of himself standing beside a wall and holding a string with a weight tied to the end of it. The string and weight had been used to measure the straightness of the wall.
translation_verse: Tin ti-Dindaan nìn gíti lēē ki dàkā-mee sɔ̀. U nìn yú digundi diba caŋin ki ŋúb́ ŋŋmii ŋun bi cáa ŋmàntī kí kpèè yii digundi tèen̄aaa, dàa tèen̄ee.

english_verse: Then he asked, “Amos, what do you see?” “A measuring line,” I answered. The Lord said, “I'm using this measuring line to show that my people Israel don't measure up, and I won't forgive them any more.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bālifì-mi yii: «Amoosi, ba ní a wāĺ?» Ní m kíí yii: «M wāĺ ŋŋmii ŋun bi cáa ŋmàntī kí kpèè yii digundi tèen̄aaa, dàa tèen̄ee ní.» Ní ti-Dindaan nìkī ki bí yii: «Kpèè, m làá dū ŋŋmii nee kí ŋmàntī kí kpèè yii m-nibul Isirayeel yab tèen̄aaa, baa tèen̄, di sá yii maa làá ti dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi.

english_verse: Their sacred places will be destroyed, and I will send war against the nation of King Jeroboam.” Amos and Amaziah
translation_verse: M làá kúntí ipaan in pu ní Isaaki naantiibi ŋáań saraabee, kí nàan̄ Isirayeel yab circir paaŋyi, ní kí já nì ubɔti Jeerooboowaam dicaŋkun yab.» Bi jìn̄ Amoosi Beeteel tiŋkin

english_verse: Amaziah the priest at Bethel sent this message to King Jeroboam of Israel, “Amos is plotting against you in the very heart of Israel. Our nation cannot put up with his message for very long.
translation_verse: Amasiya un nìn sá Beeteel tiŋkin usaraaŋakpilee nìn tú bí tùkù Isirayeel bɔtiu Jeerooboowaam yii: «Amoosi bí Isirayeel yab kansikin ki bíi gbì a-taapu. Binib gīī nì tibɔti tin u bí ki sòoǹee.

english_verse: Here is what he is saying: ‘Jeroboam will be put to death, and the people will be taken to a foreign country.’ ”
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin Amoosi sòon̄ee sèé: <Bi làá kpɔ̀ Jeerooboowaam kujaaun, ní bí dāá cáá Isirayeel yab kí cùnnì kuyuŋu bí nīn dátiǹ bi-tiŋki.>»

english_verse: Then Amaziah told me, “Amos, take your visions and get out! Go back to Judah and earn your living there as a prophet.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Amasiya bí Amoosi yii: «Sii un wāĺee, yīkì doo kí nīn gítí Juuda tiŋkin. Niinee, a ŋūǹ kí nīn nàatī tibɔti kí nīn kāntí ki jīǹ.

english_verse: Don't do any more preaching at Bethel. The king worships here at our national temple.”
translation_verse: Ama á taa ti nàatī tibɔti Beeteel tiŋkin doo! Di sá yii doo sá ubɔti circir paaŋŋu laŋki, dibeel nimbɔtidiiku ní.»

english_verse: I answered: I'm not a prophet! And I wasn't trained to be a prophet. I am a shepherd, and I take care of fig trees.
translation_verse: Ní Amoosi kíí Amasiya yii: «Maa sá ubɔnaatil, kaa tí nyánní bibɔnaatiliibi kitil diban. M sá upikpaal ní ki kpèé siikoomɔɔr sufii.

english_verse: But the Lord told me to leave my herds and preach to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ama ní ti-Dindaan cúú-mi ki páatì m-piii boon ní ki bí yii: <Cáá m-bɔti kí nàatī m-nibul Isirayeel yab.>

english_verse: Now, listen to what the Lord says about you: Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, your sons and daughters will be killed in war, and your land will be divided among others. You will die in a country of foreigners, and the people of Israel will be dragged from their homeland.
translation_verse: A-nimpuu làá kpántí kilaakpaai kitiŋin. Bi làá kpɔ̀ a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib. Bi làá ŋmàntī a-kpaatanti kí dūú yàkatī kí tīī biba. Sisi a-ba làá kpúnní kitiŋ kin yab kaa nyí Unimbɔtee ni, ní bí cùnnì Isirayeel yab kuyuŋu bí nīn dátiǹ bi-tiŋki.»

english_verse: The Lord God showed me a basket of ripe fruit
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nìn lēē asubil ŋin mántèe kukabiku ki dàkā-mi.

english_verse: and asked, “Amos, what do you see?” “A basket of ripe fruit,” I replied. Then he said, “This is the end for my people Israel. I won't forgive them again.
translation_verse: U nìn bālifì-mi yii: «Amoosi, ba ní a wāĺ?» Ní m kíí-u yii: «Kukabiku nì asubil ŋin mántèe.» Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «M-nibul Isirayeel mántì ki bàn̄ dikúntil. Maa ti làá dūú pɔ̄-bi.»

english_verse: Instead of singing in the temple, they will cry and weep. Dead bodies will be everywhere. So keep silent! I, the Lord, have spoken!” Israel Is Doomed The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī yii: «Yaadalee ilan in bi gà dibeecindee làá dāá kpántí ikpiisilan. Anikpil làá dāá nīn wīikí tikpilku. Bi làá dāá dū anikpil kí fá an kɔkɔ pu. Án làá dāá ŋmīĺ an kɔkɔ pu fɔ́ŋfɔŋ!» Binyampoobi nimbineeliŋu

english_verse: You say to yourselves, “How much longer before the end of the New Moon Festival? When will the Sabbath be over? Our wheat is ready, and we want to sell it now. We can't wait to cheat and charge high prices for the grain we sell. We will use dishonest scales
translation_verse: Ni kā ki lì yii: «Ba dal ní uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaaliu làá nín jītí tí ŋmā kí nyāfì ti-kpaajinti dee? Ba dal ní ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa làá nín jītí tí ŋmā kí nyāfiǹ binib bilee dee?» Ti làá bàtī tiwaŋŋmantikaal wíiŋŋu pu, kí gbéeǹ animbil ŋmàntikaati nyiŋfiŋu pu, kí tútí ti-saniyab bí taa tí nín̄ ŋmàntī tiwan deedee.

english_verse: and mix dust in the grain. Those who are needy and poor don't have any money. We will make them our slaves for the price of a pair of sandals.”
translation_verse: Ti làá dū animbil kí dā unandaan ní kí dū kalaa nimbiliŋ kí dā usoodaan. Ti làá nyāfì kí kpáaǹ tijaliŋgbiti.

english_verse: I, the Lord, won't forget any of this, though you take great pride in your ancestor Jacob.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan pūtì ní ki lī yii: «Kitiŋ kin pu Jaakɔb naantiibi gúntí bi-bee puee, m kpá kí súntí tin kɔkɔ bi ŋáańee pu.»

english_verse: Your country will tremble, and you will mourn. It will be like the Nile River that rises and overflows, then sinks back down.
translation_verse: An puee kitiŋ nee làá cìŋkì, ní ki-nib kɔkɔ ń kàl̄ dikpool. Kii Eejipiti mɔɔl Niil nín yaa gbí an yíkí puee, míǹ ní kitiŋ nee làá yīkì yilpu, ní kí fàtīí lítí bɔ̀b.

english_verse: On that day, I, the Lord God, will make the sun go down at noon, and I will turn daylight into darkness.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti lī yii: «Ŋwiin gbantee, m làá dāá yàntī ŋwìiń ń jēetí kuwiŋkaŋu pu, ní kí yàntī kitiŋ kɔkɔ ń kɔ́ dibɔmbɔndin ŋwiimpu.

english_verse: Your festivals and joyful singing will turn into sorrow. You will wear sackcloth and shave your heads, as you would at the death of your only son. It will be a horrible day.
translation_verse: M làá yàntī ni-jiŋaalib ń kpántí akpoo ní kí yàntī ni-laŋyi kɔkɔ ń kpántí ikpiisilan. Báà ŋma làá dāá nīn pēē kpɔsatab ní. Báà ŋma làá dāá pée kòol̀ diyibaakpandi kii unil jipɔmbaabil nín yaa kpíì u kòol̄ puee. Ŋwiin gbanti làá dāá kúntí nì ntuntun ní.»

english_verse: You will search everywhere— from north to south, from east to west. You will go all over the earth, seeking a message from me, the Lord. But you won't find one.
translation_verse: Binib làá dāá nīn tú ki yìiǹ an kɔkɔ pu, kí yīkì tiŋku ubɔ kí cáá sāā un kíǹee, kí yòon̄ ŋgan pú kí cù ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, ki bàà pée nyàab̀ kí gbìl̄ man ni-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi ama kaa làá dāá ká.

english_verse: Your beautiful young women and your young men will faint from thirst.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin gbantee, bisapɔnnyaambi nì binaacimpɔmbi làá dāá kpú nnyinnyoo.

english_verse: You made promises to the goddess Ashimah at Samaria; you made vows to other gods at the shrines of Dan and Beersheba. So now you will fall and never get up.
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ pùtī Samaarii waal yindi, bin lì yii: <Nì Daani waal yindi pu!> àá <nì Beerseeba waasaŋŋu yindi puee>, bi-kɔkɔ làá dāá lítí kaa làá ti yīkì.»

english_verse: I saw a vision of the Lord standing by the temple altar, and he said, “Shake the columns until the tops fall loose, and the doorposts crumble. Then make the pieces fall on the people below. I will take a sword and kill anyone who escapes.
translation_verse: M ká ti-Dindaan yú nsaraafan pu ki lì yii: «Gbá kí wìil̀ jaantalkub yilpu ní taapu ń cìŋkì! Gbá kí wìil̀-bi bí lítí kí tàbitì bi-yiliŋ. Bi-kansikin bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee, m làá dū ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀-bi. Báà unil kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí sāǹ, ní uniseen kaa làá dāá ŋmátí.

english_verse: “If they dig deep into the earth or climb to the sky, I'll reach out and get them.
translation_verse: Báà bi yaa pɔ́ɔǹ kí kɔ́ ditaŋkpiilinaaa, m làá dāá cù niin kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi. Bi yaa láa tí jɔ́m̀ yilpuɔɔɔ, m làá dāá cù niin kí sìntīń-bi.

english_verse: If they escape to the peaks of Mount Carmel, I'll search and find them. And if they hide from me at the bottom of the ocean, I'll command a sea monster to bite them.
translation_verse: Bi yaa láa bál̀ Kaarmeel jool yilpu kúntí kuntaaa, m làá dāá cù niin kí cúuń-bi. Bi yaa láa sáǹ ki bál̀ tiŋku taapu ḿ taa ká-baaa, m làá dāá tɔ̄ tiŋkun koobuu ú jūntì-bi.

english_verse: I'll send a sword to kill them, wherever their enemies drag them off as captives. I'm determined to hurt them, not to help them.” His Name Is the Lord
translation_verse: Bi-nannanliibi yaa láa jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi ní ki cúú-bi kuyuŋu ki cūnnì bi-tiŋkinee, m làá dāá tīī-bi mara bí pɔ̀fì-bi. M-nimbil làá dāá nīn cɔ́ bi-pu, kí ŋá-bi tikpitil, kaa sá tiŋan.»

english_verse: When the Lord God All-Powerful touches the earth, it melts, and its people mourn. God makes the earth rise and then fall, just like the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan yaa gbēē kitiŋee, kì cìŋkī ní, ní ki-nib kɔkɔ ń kàl̄ dikpool. Kii Eejipiti mɔɔl Niil nín yaa gbí an yíkí puee, míǹ ní kitiŋ nee làá yīkì yilpu, ní kí fàtīí lítí bɔ̀b.

english_verse: He built his palace in the heavens and let its foundations rest on the earth. He scoops up the ocean and empties it on the earth. His name is the Lord. The Lord Is God
translation_verse: U máń u-kɔŋkooŋŋu yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ ki dū kutagbɔŋu ki dāntì kitiŋ pu. Úǹ di yíì tiŋku nyim ní ki cáá-mì ki yàantí kitiŋ pu. Úǹ ní bi yíì yii <Ti-Dindaan>. Dibɔkpil dambi bɔsooŋyi

english_verse: Israel, I am the Lord God, and the Ethiopians are no less important to me than you are. I brought you out of Egypt, but I also brought the Philistines from Crete and the Arameans from Kir.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «Isirayeel yab, ni pɔ̄ɔ̄ m-cee kudaau ki jítiǹ Kuusi yabaaa? M nyántì-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin, ama ki nyántì Fiiliistii yab Kafitoor tiŋkin, ní ki nyántì Aram yab Kiiri tiŋkin.»

english_verse: My eyes have seen what a sinful nation you are, and I'll wipe you out. But I will leave a few of Jacob's descendants. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nimbil cɔ́ Isirayeel beel din fōō dibɔkpil nee pu. U lī yii: «M làá kúntí-dì kitiŋ pu. Ama maa làá nàan̄ Jaakɔb naantiibi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: At my command, all of you will be sifted like grain. Israelites who remain faithful will be scattered among the nations. And the others will be trapped like trash in a sifter.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m làá tīī mara ní bí jáká Isirayeel timbundi atimbun ŋin kíǹee kɔkɔ poon, kii bi nín dù kidicaai kí jáká tiwan pu, báà kitaŋkpalii kaa lùntī kí lítée.

english_verse: Some of you are evil, and you deny that you will ever get caught. But you will be killed. The Lord's Promise to Israel
translation_verse: M-nibul kansikin bikpitiŋaliibi làá kpú kujaaun, bíǹ bin lì yii: <Nnaabu ŋubɔ kpá kí làá dāan̄, u làá sútiń kí pìlīń-ti!>» Nnaabu yaa láa jítèe bɔti

english_verse: In the future, I will rebuild David's fallen kingdom. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again, just as it used to be.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin gbantee m làá dāá yòon̄ Daafiidi bìŋ́ku kun bíi lítée kí yóoń, ní kí ŋéeb́ ku-digbuŋweeŋyi kɔkɔ, kí mā ku-guŋŋi ŋin lítì ki dɔ̄ee, dí fàtīí gítí di nín nìn bí puee.

english_verse: Then you will capture Edom and the other nations that are mine. I, the Lord, have spoken, and my words will come true.
translation_verse: Án nín làá ŋá pu Isirayeel yab ń dāá fàtīí fōō Eedoom yab cee nì atimbun ŋin kíǹee kɔkɔ yab cee ntimu mun di nìn sá man yɔmuee. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, ní ki làá yàntī án ŋá míǹ!»

english_verse: You will have such a harvest that you won't be able to bring in all of your wheat before plowing time. You will have grapes left over from season to season; your fruitful vineyards will cover the mountains.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti lī yii: «Ŋwiin dòoń bi làá dāá cā tikpaajin tikpil án nīn dɔ̄ kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun bi làá kpɔ̀ tipɔnee. Míǹ mbaantiim, bi làá dāá kìtī fiinyi biliŋ án nīn dɔ̄ kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní bi làá bɔ̄l̀ bileeyee. Niinee ndapɔm dāa pùub̀ ajoon pu ní ki còol̀ ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: I'll make Israel prosper again. You will rebuild your towns and live in them. You will drink wine from your own vineyards and eat the fruit you grow.
translation_verse: M làá fàtīí gíiǹní m-nibul Isirayeel yab bi-tiŋkin bí fàtīí mā bi-timmu mun wīil̀ee kí kàl̄. Bi làá dāá cóoń fiinyi sufii kí nyɔ̀ i-daam. Bi làá kpɔ̀ tikuŋfaal kpaaŋŋi kí dāá ká kí jī.

english_verse: I'll plant your roots deep in the land I have given you, and you won't ever be uprooted again. I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_verse: M làá dāá fàtīí gíiǹ m-nibul kí kàan̄ bi-tiŋki pu. Baa làá ti jà-bi kitiŋ kin m tīī-bee pu jaanjaan. Man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di lī míǹ!»

english_verse: The Lord God gave Obadiah a message about Edom, and this is what we heard: “I, the Lord, have sent a messenger with orders for the nations to attack Edom.”
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti lēē ki dàkā Oobadiyee. U nín sòon̄ Eedoom tiŋki pu puee sɔ̀. Ti-Dindaan yāntì ti gbìl̄ tibɔti nee, bi tú ntuun ŋubɔ atimbun kɔkɔn ŋu lì yii: «Yīkìmaan! Tí cùú já nì Eedoom tiŋki!»

english_verse: The Lord said to Edom: I will make you the weakest and most despised nation.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «Eedoom, atimbun kɔkɔnee, m làá yàntī á kpántí kiwaŋwaai. Báà ŋma làá nīn kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ-si.

english_verse: You live in a mountain fortress, because your pride makes you feel safe from attack, but you are mistaken.
translation_verse: A-lambikpaandi di kíiĺ-si! A kóò itaŋkpalɔkɔn, ní ki máń a-diiŋŋi ki tɔ́kɔǹ ajoon yilpu, ní ki lì yii: <Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí kpákatí-mi taapu?>

english_verse: I will still bring you down, even if you fly higher than an eagle or nest among the stars. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Báà a yaa là kí ŋàaǹ kí kɔ́ kutaa kii ukaalunee, kí mā a-diiku iŋmalbijaa kansikin, see m kpákatìń-si taapu!

english_verse: If thieves break in at night, they steal only what they want. And people who harvest grapes always leave some unpicked. But, Edom, you are doomed!
translation_verse: Binaayub àá kunyeeu fukuliliibi yaa kɔ́ a-puee, bi yòontí tin kɔkɔ bi ŋūǹee ní, baa kīntí-si báà tiba. Bitɔntɔnliibi bin kìtī fiinyi subiliŋee yaa kɔ́ a-saakunee, tin làá pée kíńee di sá tilulifikaal.

english_verse: Everything you treasure most will be taken from you.
translation_verse: Bi fúkúl̀ nimbi Eesayuu naantiibi pílpil, bi bīitì ni-gaajawanti tin bí dibalinee pu!

english_verse: Your allies can't be trusted. They will force you out of your own country. And your best friends will trick and trap you, even before you know it.
translation_verse: Bi jìn̄-si ki nyántì a-tiŋkin, si nì bin pēē kinyɔkɔee nyáń a-boon. A-bɔɔmɔntiibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-si. Si nì bin nìn jīǹ disambibaantiilinee bíi pīil̀-si titalindi taapu taapu. Bi sòoǹ ni-pu yii: <Waa ti cáá diyil!>

english_verse: Edom, when this happens, I, the Lord, will destroy all your marvelous wisdom.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. M-ŋuul wiiŋŋu dalee, m làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí biciŋfitiibi Eedoom tiŋkin, maa làá kíń Eesayuu jool pu unyil ubambaanti.

english_verse: Warriors from the city of Teman will be terrified, and you descendants of Esau will be wiped out. The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
translation_verse: Teeman tiŋki, dinyoondi làá dāá kɔ́ a-janjaliibi, án nín làá ŋá pu bí kpɔ̀ kí kúntí unil sá kamaa Eesayuu jool puee. Eedoom yìntitam

english_verse: You were cruel to your relatives, the descendants of Jacob. Now you will be destroyed, disgraced forever.
translation_verse: A fúkúl̀ ki kūū a-nabiki, Jaakɔb naantiibi. An pu ní icoo làá cúú-si tikpil ní bí kúntí-si kí nīn pée cá jaanjaan.

english_verse: You stood there and watched as foreigners entered Jerusalem and took what they wanted. In fact, you were no better than those foreigners.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun a nìn yú ki kpèé binannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ u-janjaliibi ki kɔ́ u-tiŋkin, ki tɔ́ Jeerusaleem pu kasee, a mun nìn bí kii bi-kansikin ubɔee dee.

english_verse: Why did you celebrate when such a dreadful disaster struck your relatives? Why were you so pleased when everyone in Judah was suffering?
translation_verse: Eedoom, aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn fàal̀ ŋyunti ŋun a-nabiki kɔ́ dinimbinaamandinee. Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn fàal̀ ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi nàantí Juuda yabee. Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn bíi lāā-bi ŋyunti ŋun bi kɔ́ dinimbinaamandi poonee.

english_verse: They are my people, and you were cruel to them. You went through their towns, sneering and stealing whatever was left.
translation_verse: Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí kɔ́ m-nibul tiŋkin, ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi nàantí-kèe. Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn fàal̀ u-nimbinaamandi wiiŋŋu dal. Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí yòon̄ u-gaajawanti ŋwiin ŋun bi nìn bíi fúkuĺ-uee.

english_verse: In their time of torment, you ambushed refugees and handed them over to their attackers. The Lord Will Judge the Nations
translation_verse: Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn yú isampuyakati pu ki kù bin nìn sáń kí ŋmátée, kaa bàà nìn tí máaǹ kí dū bin baa kūūyee kí ŋá binannanliibi ŋaan nnaabu wiiŋŋu gbanti dal.

english_verse: The day is coming when I, the Lord, will judge the nations. And, Edom, you will pay in full for what you have done.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu ŋun u làá sòoǹ atimbun kɔkɔ bɔtee tóobiń. A nín ŋá bin beeyee puee, míǹ ní bi làá téeǹ-si. A-tuŋkpitiŋ làá dāá fàtīí gítí a-pu ní.» Isirayeel làá tɔ̀ Eedoom ipɔntoon

english_verse: I forced the people of Judah to drink the wine of my anger on my sacred mountain. Soon the neighboring nations must drink their fill— then vanish without a trace. Victory for Israel
translation_verse: «Nimbi Isirayeel yab, kii ni nín nìn nyùn̄ m-ŋuul kii ndaamee m-circir jool puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní atimbun kɔkɔ làá dāá nyɔ̀-dì kí taa gbèen̄. Ŋi làá dāá nyɔ̀-dì kí gbí, ní boonee kí wāŋkì.

english_verse: The Lord's people who escape will go to Mount Zion, and it will be holy. Then Jacob's descendants will capture the land of those who took their land.
translation_verse: Ama bin yaa láa bí kaa kpíìyee làá dāá sāǹ kí kɔ́ Siiyɔn jool. Dì làá fàtīí kpántí circir jool. Jaakɔb naantiibi làá dāá fàtīí fōō bi-tiŋki bin nìn fōō-kèe ŋaan.

english_verse: Israel will be a fire, and Edom will be straw going up in flames. The Lord has spoken!
translation_verse: Jaakɔb naantiibi làá dāá nīn sá kii ŋŋmee ní, Jooseefi naantiibi làá dāá nīn sá kii diŋmilimbilee. Ama Eesayuu naantiibi làá dāá nīn sá kii timoolee ní. Bi làá dāá wà Eesayuu naantiibi ní kɔkɔ múb.»

english_verse: The people of Israel who live in the Southern Desert will take the land of Edom. Those who live in the hills will capture Philistia, Ephraim, and Samaria. And the tribe of Benjamin will conquer Gilead.
translation_verse: Bin kóò ŋgiil pú tiŋkee di làá dāá nīn yì Eesayuu jool nì Seefeelaa tiŋki kin pu Fiiliistii yab kóòyee. Bi làá dāá nīn yì Eefiraayiim tiŋki nì Samaarii tiŋki mun, ní Beenjameen ń dāá nīn yì Galaadi tiŋki.

english_verse: Those who return from captivity will control Phoenicia as far as Zarephath. Captives from Jerusalem who were taken to Sepharad will capture the towns of the Southern Desert.
translation_verse: Isirayeel beel ŋgan pú yab bin bi nìn cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee làá dāá kpántí dijanjakitikpaandi. Bi làá dāá já kí fōō Kanaan yab tiŋki kí tin sāā Sareepita tiŋki. Jeerusaleem yab bin bi nìn cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋu bi bí Seefaradee làá dāá já kí fōō ntimu mun bí ŋgiil púee.

english_verse: Those the Lord has saved will live on Mount Zion and rule over Edom. Then the kingdom will belong to the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi nín jáń ki jíń mimmee ní bí jɔ̄m̀ Siiyɔn jool pu. Niin ní bi làá dāá nīn bí ní kí jī Eedoom jool pu dibeel. Ti-Dindaan di dāa sá ubɔti!

english_verse: One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai,
translation_verse: Dalba ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Amiitaayi jipɔɔn Yoona ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
translation_verse: «Yīkì kí cù Niiniifi kitiŋkpaaŋŋi poon kí bāakì kí tùkù kitiŋ gbanti nib yii bi-kpitii nyāŋkì, di sá yii m-nimbil ká ikpiti in bi bí ki ŋáańee.»

english_verse: Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
translation_verse: Ama ní Yoona yíkì ki dūu túĺ Taarsiisi tiŋki pú, kí sāǹ kí cù ndandati ti-Dindaan ń taa ti ká-u. U yíkèe ní ki nín sìntī Jaafa tiŋkin ki bàn̄ ki ká meela ubɔ bɔ́ntì ki cá Taarsiisi tiŋkin, ní u pàn̄ ki kɔ́ ki kāl̀ meelan bí cáá-u kí nīn cá Taarsiisi tiŋkin ú cùú báĺ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan dū kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kubɔ ki tɔ́ tiŋku pu. Kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee bíi fīintí tiŋku mpɔn mpɔn ní ki bàà làá wīī meela.

english_verse: The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter. All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep.
translation_verse: Niinee tifaandi kɔ́ meela tɔntɔnliibi, ní báà ŋma kíǹ ki bíi tíminsí ki yíì u-nimbɔtiu. Ní bi yōoǹ tiwan tin bi tākaǹ meelanee kɔkɔ ki tɔ́ tiŋkun kí ŋmā kí bàtī meela nyiŋfiŋu pu. Nì mimmee, Yoona úǹ pée kɔ́ meela poondiikun ki dōoǹ ki bíi gèeǹ fɔ̀rtititi!

english_verse: The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
translation_verse: Ní meelan tɔntɔnliibi kpiliu sútì ki pìl̄-u ní ki bí-u yii: «Sii dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ níii? Yīkì kí tīminsì kí yíiń a-nimbɔtiu. An yaa yíì úǹ làá sɔ̄ ti-saai kí jòoń-ti tí taa kpú.»

english_verse: Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
translation_verse: Ní meelan tɔntɔnliibi bí tɔb yii: «Ní yàntī tí tɔ̄maan kasi kí béé udaan un pu ní dinimbinaamandi nee dī ki bāań-tee.» Bi tɔ́ kasee ní an dūu tāā Yoona.

english_verse: They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
