translation_verse: Ní bi bālifì Yoona yii: «Too, sii un pu dinimbinaamandi nee dī ki bāań-ti nee, a-tundi baasii sá dilal ní doo ní? La pu ní a nyánní ní? A sá kitiŋ kilakan ní? A sá dinibul dilal niliu ní?»

english_verse: Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
translation_verse: Ní Yoona kíí-bi yii: «Man sá ueebruja ní. Ti-Dindaan yilpu Nimbɔtiu un náań tiŋku nì kitiŋee ní m jáaḿ!»

english_verse: When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
translation_verse: Binibee nín ká yii Yoona u-ba nín lī puee dàkà yii ti-Dindaan ní u bíi sáńee ní bi fāŋkì tikpil tikpil, ki bí-u yii: «Batii bɔti ní a ŋá mimmee!»

english_verse: The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
translation_verse: Bi lī mimmee ní ki bālifì Yoona yii: «Mana ní ti máaǹ kí ŋá-si ní tiŋku ń ŋmīĺ án ŋá ti-pu fòooo dee?» Di sá yii kubuŋu nìn dáá pée gbíntìi jītí mpɔn ní tiŋku nyim nìn mɔ̀tīi yíkí mpɔn.

english_verse: Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
translation_verse: Ní Yoona kíí-bi yii: «Ní yòom̄maan-mi kí tɔ̄ tiŋkun, tiŋku làá ŋmīĺ ní án ŋá ni-pu fòooo! Mama m-ba pée nyí yii man pu ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋu nee bí ki jītí tiŋku pu ki páb́-ni míǹ.»

english_verse: The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute.
translation_verse: Binibee pɔ́ɔǹ bi-ba kí bàà ŋàal̀ meela kí fàtīí bà tiŋku gbandi ama baa ŋúń, kun puee tiŋku nyim nìn mɔ̀tīi jɔ́ḿ ní ki páb́-bi.

english_verse: So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi tíminsì ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ní ki bí yii: «Áù, ti-Dindaan, ti gbàam̄-si! Taa yàntī tí kpú kijapaai nee pu. Taa dū kijapaai nee kpuulool kí lúntí ti-pu, waa ŋá-ti tiba. Ti-Dindaan, sisi a-ba nín là puee, míǹ ní a ŋá.»

english_verse: The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
translation_verse: Binibee nín ká mimmee, bi fāŋkì ti-Dindaan tikpil tikpil ní ki ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan ní ki pōoǹ-u ipoon.

english_verse: You threw me down to the bottom of the sea. The water was churning all around; I was completely covered by your mighty waves.
translation_verse: «M nìn bí dinimbinaamandin, ki tíminsì ki yíiń sii ti-Dindaan ní a kíí-mi. M nìn sīntì taapu taŋkpiilin ki kúuǹ ki yíiń-si á dāá jòoń-mi ní a gbìl̄ m-timinsii.

english_verse: I thought I was swept away from your sight, never again to see your holy temple.
translation_verse: A dū-mi ki tɔ́ tiŋku poon m nín sìntī nnyimbuun taapu taapu ní nnyim māntìi tú-mi an kɔkɔ pu, ní a yāntì tinyiŋgban kɔkɔ nì nnyinjil dòoń ki jītí m-pu.

english_verse: I was almost drowned by the swirling waters that surrounded me. Seaweed had wrapped around my head.
translation_verse: Ní m lī m-neen yii: <Man nì sii yākatì tɔbin ní nee, m pée gíti kpá kí ká-si! Nì míǹ kɔkɔee m gbíntìi bíi kpèé a-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu watil pú>.

english_verse: I had sunk down deep below the mountains beneath the sea. I knew that forever, I would be a prisoner there. But, you, Lord God, rescued me from that pit.
translation_verse: Nnyim jɔ́m̀ ki tin sāā m-neen, m mɔ̄tìi nín sìntī tiŋku taapu taapu, ní timool tin bí nnyiminee dūu lùl̄ m-yil.

english_verse: When my life was slipping away, I remembered you— and in your holy temple you heard my prayer.
translation_verse: M sīntì doooo taapu taapu ki tin nyáń ajoon nyeel pu, ditaŋkpiil dū di-punyɔmmu ki pīiǹ m-pu kí nīn pée cá jaanjaan. Ama ní sii ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu fātìi nyántìń-mi m dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin.

english_verse: But with shouts of praise, I will offer a sacrifice to you, my Lord. I will keep my promise, because you are the one with power to save.
translation_verse: Bin dū awaa ŋin kaa bí tibanee ki yíĺ bi-yilee, bíǹ kaa ti cáá diyimɔɔl kí ká difiil dee!

english_verse: Once again the Lord told Jonah
translation_verse: An ŋá mimmee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yoona nliliitiim ki bí-u yii:

english_verse: to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
translation_verse: «Yīkì kí cù Niiniifi kitiŋkpaaŋŋi poon kí dū tibɔti tin m dūu ŋúbiǹ-see kí bāakì kí tùkù niin yab.»

english_verse: Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yoona yíkì ki nín cá Niiniifi tiŋkin, ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ú ŋá puee. Niiniifi tiŋki gbanti nìn sá kitiŋkpaŋkpaaŋŋi ní, an kaa cáá bí lì. Iwimmɔn ita kɔkɔ ní unil nìn dùŋfī ní kí còom̀ kí pùntī-kì.

english_verse: After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
translation_verse: Yoona kɔ́ kitiŋin ki kíĺ ki cōom̀ ŋwiin ŋubɔ ní ki báakì ki lī yii: «An gíti kíǹ iwiin imuŋku ili Niiniifi tiŋki làá kúntí!»

english_verse: They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
translation_verse: Niiniifi yab nìn fōō Unimbɔti bɔti tin u sòon̄ee ki kíí, ní bi yóoǹ yii báà ŋma ń bóob́ kinyɔkɔ. Di sá kí yòon̄ bikpilib kí tin cáá sāā ŋwaamuee, báà ŋma nìn dū kutuku ki pēeǹ kí dàkà yii bi fá bi-kpitii ki kpántì bi-ba.

english_verse: When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust.
translation_verse: Tibɔti dūu bàn̄ Niiniifi bɔtiu ceeyee ní u yíkì u-beejal pu, ki cúú dibeebɔkutil din u pēēyee ki pēetì, ki dū kutuku ki pēeǹ ní ki kāl̀ ŋfantamin.

english_verse: When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nín ká yii Niiniifi yab pɔ́ɔǹ bi-ba ki dū isaŋkpiti in bi nóóyee ki fée, ní u kpántì u-landɔkɔŋu kaa ti dáaĺ bi-tafal kii u nín bàà là kí ŋá puee.

english_verse: Jonah was really upset and angry.
translation_verse: An bɔtee kaa mɔ́ɔkiǹ Yoona báà fiii ní u fōō mbum.

english_verse: So he prayed: Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
translation_verse: Ní Yoona mēē ti-Dindaan ki bí yii: «Áù, ti-Dindaan! Tibɔti tin m nìn lī ŋyunti ŋun m nìn bí m-tiŋkinee kaa sɔ̀ɔɔ? Kun pu m nìn yíkì ki bàà nìn sáń ki cá Taarsiisi tiŋkinee deeyaa! M pée nyí yii a sá Unimbɔti un poon mɔ̄, ki cáá disaasɔl nì kimɔtii tikpil ki ŋáań tiŋan ní unil yaa yīntiǹ-si ki bàà máaǹ á dáaĺ u-tafalee, á kpántí a-landɔkɔŋu malaa kí dūú pɔ̄ udaanee.

english_verse: The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-u yii: «A cáá nsan kí gíí diŋuulaaa?»

english_verse: Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
translation_verse: Ní Yoona yíkì ki nyáń Niiniifi tiŋkin ki cūtì ki kāl̀ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú. U gāā kibiŋ kiba niin ní ki kāl̀ ki-booŋŋu taapu ki cí kí kpèè tin làá jītí Niiniifi tiŋki poonee.

english_verse: The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine,
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti yāntì digbumbitiki subiki nyáń ki wíiǹ, ki-booŋŋu bīiǹ Yoona yil ŋwìiń, kí sɔ̀ŋkì u-pɔbil. Kisubiki gbanti bɔti mɔ́ɔkiǹ Yoona tikpil.

english_verse: but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up.
translation_verse: Ama kutaa wúntì an dáá bɔ̀ǹ gúuuyee, ní Unimbɔti lēē dikoosibil diba ki tú di ŋmɔ́ digbumbitiki subikee ní kì kūń.

english_verse: During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ŋwìiń jɔ́m̀ee ní Unimbɔti túnní kubuŋu, kù tùm̀ kpaŋkpam, ki nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki jítì. Ŋwìiń wùn̄ Yoona yil ŋkpitim pu áli u bàà làá fìkī. Ní u mēē yii ŋkúm ń dāá dū-u ki lī yii: «M yaa pūtì kpíì an sɔ́ nì ḿ nīn bí dimaŋfalin.»

english_verse: But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?” “Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti bālifì Yoona yii: «A cáá nsan kí gíí diŋuul digbumbitiki subiki nee puɔɔɔ?» Ní u kíí yii: «Iiin, m cáá nsan kí gíí diŋuul tikpil áli kí tin nyàab̀ ŋkúm.»

english_verse: But the Lord said: You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kpèè, sii bí ki sūǹ digbumbitiki subiki nee pu dee. Ama sii di kaa cóoǹ-kì, ní kaa tí kpēē-kì ní ki wíiǹ. Kunyeeu kubɔ ní kì nyáń ki wíiǹ, kunyeeu fātìi mɔ́ee ní kì kpíì.

english_verse: I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah. Judgment on Samaria
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Miika un sá Mooreeseeti timbiliikin iyunti in ní Yootam nì Akaasi nì Eeseekiyaasi nìn kāl̀ kāl̀ dibeel Juuda tiŋki puee. Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn lēē ki dàkā-u Samaarii nì Jeerusaleem timmu puee sɔ̀. Ti-Dindaan bíi wòoǹ u-nibul

english_verse: Listen, all of you! Earth and everything on it, pay close attention. The Lord God accuses you from his holy temple.
translation_verse: Anibul kɔkɔ nib, ní pīlifìmaan! Kitiŋ nì bin kɔkɔ kóò ki-puee, ní kpòom̄maan ni-tafal kí pīlifì. Ti-Dindaan làá sòoǹ ni-tuŋkpitiŋ pu doooo u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.

english_verse: And he will come down to crush underfoot every pagan altar.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan nyánní u-kɔŋkooŋŋun. U sìntìń ki còom̄ ŋgbantamu yilpu kúntí kunti.

english_verse: Mountains will melt beneath his feet like wax beside a fire. Valleys will vanish like water rushing down a ravine.
translation_verse: Ajoon ŋin pu u tɔ́kɔ́ee dùntī kii tikaliŋkpun di kā ŋŋminee, ní atantaka fátí iwèeń kii nnyim nín pùub̀ dijool pu puee.

english_verse: This will happen because of the terrible sins of Israel, the descendants of Jacob. Samaria has led Israel to sin, and pagan altars at Jerusalem have made Judah sin.
translation_verse: Tin bí nee kɔkɔ bāań kun puee Jaakɔb naantiibi ŋá ikpiti, Isirayeel yab kaa yúl̀ deedee. Ŋma yàntī Jaakɔb naantiibi ŋáań ikpiti ní? An kaa sá Samaarii tiŋkaaa? Ŋma yàntī Juuda yab kóò iwaatootin ní? An kaa sá Jeerusaleem tiŋkaaa?

english_verse: So the Lord will leave Samaria in ruins— merely an empty field where vineyards are planted. He will scatter its stones and destroy its foundations.
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. An puee m làá yàntī Samaarii tiŋki ń kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma kitiŋ kin pu bi dāa ŋūǹ kí kpɔ̀ fiinyi sufiiyee. M làá yàntī bí bíntí u-diiŋŋi taŋkpeeŋi kí tɔ̄ nsitimin, ní kí bìitī bi-tiŋki nyeel pu án nīn wāĺ.

english_verse: Samaria's idols will be smashed, and the wages of temple prostitutes will be destroyed by fire. Silver and gold from those idols will then be used by foreigners as payment for prostitutes. Judah Is Doomed
translation_verse: M làá gbá kí wīī bi-waaŋi kɔkɔ, ní kí dū tiwampɔkaal tin bi pú-ŋee kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin. M làá nà awaa gbanti dúsi dusi, di sá yii nlaakpaamu paati ní bi dūu ká tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ, ní tiwan gbanti làá fàtīí kpántí nlaakpaamu paati.» Nnaabu bāań áli Jeerusaleem

english_verse: Because of this tragedy, I go barefoot and naked. My crying and weeping sound like howling wolves or ostriches.
translation_verse: «Miika nín lī puee sɔ̀. M làá sɔ̄ kí yāliŋkì. M làá nīn còom̄ kaa táká anaataka, kaa pēē tiba. M làá gāā dituweel kii jiiŋkpaai nín sūǹ puee, kí nīn yáliŋkí kii taataayee.

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath! Don't even cry. Instead, roll in the dust at Beth-Leaphrah.
translation_verse: Ní taa māafì an bɔti Gaati tiŋkin, taa sɔ̄maan. Beeti-Leeyafiira tiŋkin yab, ní dòom̄maan ntampukumin kí nīn bíntí.

english_verse: Depart naked and ashamed, you people of Shaphir. The town of Bethezel mourns because no one from Zaanan went out to help.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kóò Safiir tiŋkinee, kíĺmaan kuyuŋu saŋŋu nì icoo nì dicancaŋgbeel. Bin kóò Saanan tiŋkinee kaa kíikí kí nyā bi-tiŋkin.

english_verse: Everyone in Maroth hoped for the best, but the Lord sent disaster down on Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Bin kóò Marɔti tiŋkinee kíǹ ki sūǹ bi-ba pu ki mèé yii mbusu ń cù ndan. Di sá yii nnaabu ŋun nyánní ti-Dindaan ceeyee bāań ki gūū Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu.

english_verse: Get the war chariots ready, you people of Lachish. You led Jerusalem into sin, just as Israel did.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kóò Lakiisi tiŋkinee, ní dū janjatɔrɔkub kí kúĺ kí lúntí itaamu. Naa yúl̀ nì Unimbɔti deedee kii Isirayeel yabee, ní ki dáaĺ Jeerusaleem yab ki kɔ́ǹ ni-tuŋkpitiŋin.

english_verse: Now you will have to give a going-away gift to Moresheth. Israel's kings will discover that they cannot trust the town of Achzib.
translation_verse: An pu ní ni máaǹ ni nì Mooreeseeti-Gaati tiŋkin yab ń yàkatī tɔbin. Akisiib tiŋkin yab kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí jòò Isirayeel yab bɔtiibi.

english_verse: People of Mareshah, the Lord will send someone to capture your town. Then Israel's glorious king will be forced to hide in Adullam Cave.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kóò Mareesa tiŋkinee, ti-Dindaan làá dū ujanjapɔɔl ubɔ kí tɔ̄ ni-pu. Isirayeel nigaakaabi làá dāá sāǹ kí cù Adulaam taŋkpalɔkɔŋun kí báĺ.

english_verse: Judah, shave your head as bald as a vulture and start mourning. Your precious children will be dragged off to a foreign country.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kóò Jeerusaleemee, ní cāmaan ni-yikpiti, ní kòol̀maan dibaakpandi ni-biyaamu mun ni néeń tikpilee pu. Ní nīn tú dibaakpandi kii kaajiikuee, kun puee bi làá cùnnì ni-biyaamu kuyuŋu kitiŋ kin dátiǹ-nee poon.

english_verse: Doomed! You're doomed! At night you lie in bed, making evil plans. And when morning comes, you do what you've planned because you have the power.
translation_verse: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí bin dɔ̄ kunyeeu ki dàkafī kí ŋá tibɔkpitil ki bɔ́ntí kí tɔ̄ atuŋkpitee! Kutaa tin pée lì yii ku wúntéee, bi ŋá bi nín bɔ́ntì puee, di sá yii bi cáá an pɔŋŋu.

english_verse: You grab any field or house that you want; you cheat families out of homes and land.
translation_verse: Biba kpaatanti yaa kɔ́-bi nnimbitaataamee, bi cútí ní kí fōō. Bi yaa tí ká adiin fáatiǹ-bee, ní bí cúú kí fōō. Bi fìkì kudiidaan nì u-dicaŋku, unil nì u-fakal.

english_verse: But here is what the Lord says: “I am planning trouble for you. Your necks will be caught in a noose, and you will be disgraced in this time of disaster.”
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan lī yii: <M bíi bɔ́ntí nnaabu kí tɔ̄ nimbi bin tūǹ an tuuŋŋee pu. Naa làá dāá ŋmā kí ŋmátí. Naa làá dāá nīn gíti còom̄ ni-yiliŋ gáań, di sá yii an dāa sá dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu ní.>

english_verse: When that happens, this sorrowful song will be sung about you: “Ruined! Completely ruined! The Lord has taken our land and given it to traitors.”
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, bi làá dāá gāā-ni nlan, bi làá dāá nīn gà ŋkpiisilan nee yii: <Bi fúkúl̀-ti pílpil. Ti-nibul kaa ti cáá kitiŋ. Bin bíi fúkuĺ-tee dū ti-sati ki yākatì.»

english_verse: And so you will never again own property among the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Too, ti-Dindaan nibul yaa làá dāá fàtīí yàkatī tikpaatanee, ni-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa dāa cáá kí fōō dijandi. Bin jáà nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bɔtee

english_verse: “Enough of your preaching!” That's what you tell me. “We won't be disgraced, so stop preaching!”
translation_verse: Biba sòoǹ nì mi yii: «Taa ti sòoǹ tin a sòoǹ nee. Aa máaǹ kí nīn lì yii: Icoo làá jī-ti.

english_verse: Descendants of Jacob, is it right for you to claim that the Lord did what he did because he was angry? Doesn't he always bless those who do right?
translation_verse: Bi ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ mimmaaa, Isirayeel yab? Ti-Dindaan kaa ti cáá kimɔtii níii? Míǹ ní u tūǹ u-tuuŋŋaaa?» Mamee, m cáá dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi kí tīī un bí deedeeyee.

english_verse: My people, you have turned against one another! You have even stolen clothes right off the backs of innocent neighbors who pass by in peace.
translation_verse: Nimbi pu ní an lī yii: «Ni dū m-nibul ki kpántì m-nannanliibi. Ni fòol̄ bin nyánní kujaau ki còom̄ ki cá nì ŋgbansɔŋfee bɔkutikpaaŋŋi.

english_verse: You take over lovely homes that belong to the women of my nation. Then you cheat their children out of the inheritance that comes from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ni jì m-nibul nimpoobi ki nyāntí bi-diiŋŋi ŋin bi néeńee poon. Ni fòol̄ bi-biyaamu cee tinyool tin m tīī-bi kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaanee.

english_verse: Get out of here, you crooks! You'll find no rest here. You're not fit to belong to the Lord's people, and you will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Yīkìmaan! Nín̄ cámaan! An kaa sá diŋuŋfil yuntiŋu! Ni-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi puee, nnaabukpaan dɔ̄ ki cí-ni.»

english_verse: The only prophet you want is a liar who will say, “Drink and get drunk!” A Promise of Hope
translation_verse: Binib yaa bí ki cáá kubɔcaau, ki nāantí tinyimɔmbɔti ki lì yii: «Ni làá ká ndamam nì ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee kí nyɔ̀.» Kubɔcaau gbanti dambi gíti lì yii:

english_verse: I, the Lord, promise to bring together the people of Israel who have survived. I will gather them, just as a shepherd brings sheep together, and there will be many.
translation_verse: «M làá kóoǹ ni-kɔkɔ kí kpāfì, Jaakɔb naantiibi. M làá kóoǹ Isirayeel yab bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee kí kpāfì ubaanti. M làá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì ubaanti kii ipii nín kpáfí pu kupikpuŋkpuŋunee. Ni làá dāá bùtī kí ŋá dinikitikpaandi bí gbìl̄ ni-pu.

english_verse: I will break down the gate and lead them out— then I will be their king.
translation_verse: Un pìitī nsanee làá nīn līī ni-nyɔkɔpu. Ni tɔ́ ni-ba, dīmaan kipunyɔkɔ kí nyā. An sá ti-Dindaan ni-bɔtiu di līī ni-nyɔkɔpu ki kpòotī-ni.»

english_verse: but you prefer to do evil instead of what is right. You skin my people alive. You strip off their flesh,
translation_verse: Ama nimbi di ná tin ŋān̄ee ní ki néeń tin kaa ŋān̄ee. Ni cátí binib gbaŋŋu ki bìitī tiwunnan nì akpab pu.»

english_verse: Someday you will beg the Lord to help you, but he will turn away because of your sins.
translation_verse: An pu ní bi yaa láa kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaanee, waa làá dāá kíí-bi. Ŋyunti gbantee, u làá dāá fàtī u-kpaŋkpamboon kí tīī-bi, atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ bi ŋée pu. Inyimɔn bɔnaatiliibi bɔkpaaŋi

english_verse: You lying prophets promise security for anyone who gives you food, but disaster for anyone who refuses to feed you. Here is what the Lord says to you prophets:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ bibɔnaatiliibi bin mɔ́ntí m-nibulee pu puee sèé: «Bin yaa tīī-bi njimee, bi lì yii Unimbɔti ń tīī-bi ŋgbansɔŋfi. Ama bin kaa tìì-bi tiba bí jēe, bi jáà nì bi.

english_verse: “You will live in the dark, far from the sight of the sun, with no message from me.
translation_verse: An puee kunyeeu làá mɔ́ ni-pu, naa làá ti ká aleedaka. Dibɔmbɔndi làá jēetí ni-pu, naa làá ti ká tiba kí sòoǹ. Ŋwìiń làá jēetí ni-pu, ní ŋwiimpu ń dūú kpántí dibɔmbɔndi.»

english_verse: You prophets and fortunetellers will all be disgraced, with no message from me.”
translation_verse: Icoo làá cúú bin wāĺee nì bin būūyee. Bi làá bìin̄ bi-nyɔɔkuti pu, kun puee Unimbɔti kaa ti kíikí-bi.

english_verse: But the Lord has filled me with power and his Spirit. I have been given the courage to speak about justice and to tell you people of Israel that you have sinned.
translation_verse: Ama mamee, nì ti-Dindaan Fam puee, m cáá mpɔn, ki nyí tin bí deedeeyee, ki cáá dipɔbil. M ŋūǹ kí yàntī Jaakɔb naantiibi, Isirayeel nibul ń béé bi-yìntitam nì bi-kpitii. Jeerusaleem tiŋki làá wīī

english_verse: So listen to my message, you rulers of Israel! You hate justice and twist the truth.
translation_verse: Pīlifìmaan tin bí nee, nimbi Jaakɔb naantiibi kpootiliibi, nimbi Isirayeel nibul bɔsoonliibi. Ni ná tin bí deedeeyee, kaa sòoǹ tibɔti ibaamɔn.

english_verse: You make cruelty and murder a way of life in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ni kù binib ki kāntí animbil ki cáa nyāantí Siiyɔn tiŋki. Ni wɔ́b̀ binib ki kāntí animbil ki cáa nyāantí Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: You leaders accept bribes for dishonest decisions. You priests and prophets teach and preach, but only for money. Then you say, “The Lord is on our side. No harm will come to us.”
translation_verse: Bibɔsoonliibi fòol̄ tiwampɔkaal ní ki sòoǹ binib bɔti, bisaraaŋaliibi dàkà Unimbɔti marab ní bi pà-bi, ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi fòol̄ animbil ní kí nín nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti. Ti-Dindaan yindi pu ní bi tɔ́kɔ́ ki ŋáań tíǹ kɔkɔ ki lì yii: «Ti-Dindaan bí ti-cee. Nnaabu ŋubɔ kpá ki làá jēetí ti-pu.»

english_verse: And so, because of you, Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.
translation_verse: Too, ni-puee, bi làá kpɔ̀ Siiyɔn tiŋki kii bi nín kù bukpaa puee, ní Jeerusaleem tiŋki ń kpántí adigbun ŋma, ní ikuŋkum ń nyā kí múkúǹ dijool din pu bi máń kunimbɔtidii ki tɔ́kɔ́ǹee.

english_verse: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills, and every nation will rush to it.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń, dijool din pu ti-Dindaan Diiku tɔ́kɔ́ee làá dāá nīn tɔ́kɔ́ ajoon kɔkɔ pu, di làá dāá nīn fɔ̀kɔǹ ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ. Anibul làá dāá nīn bìtifī ki dòoń di-cee.

english_verse: People of many nations will come and say, “Let's go up to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
translation_verse: Atimbun tikpil làá dāá tàkan̄ nsan ki cá ki lì yii: <Dāam̄maan tí jɔ̄m̀ ti-Dindaan jool pu, tí jɔ̄m̀maan Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu Diikun! U làá dàkà-ti kun u là tí ŋée ní tí nóó u-sàmbiyaamu.> Tiŋman, Siiyɔn ní Mara làá nyānní, u-nyɔɔbundi làá nyānní Jeerusaleem ní.

english_verse: He will settle arguments between distant and powerful nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never again make war or attack one another.
translation_verse: U làá dāá sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì anibul tikpil kansikin bɔti, kí dāá ŋāŋkì atimbun ŋin cáá mpɔn ki bínní ndandatee kansikin bɔti. Binib làá dāá dū bi-tàataajimmu kí dūú mɔ́ɔ́ akoo, ní kí dāá dū bi-kpammu kí mɔ́ɔ́ igɔti. Ditimbundi diba kaa dāa gíti jáà nì di-juti, ní binib kaa dāa bífí kujaau.

english_verse: Everyone will find rest beneath their own fig trees or grape vines, and they will live in peace. This is a solemn promise of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Báà ŋma dāa kíǹ ki kā u-fiinyi nì u-fiigi sufii taapu, ní ubɔ kaa dāa bí kí páb́-u.» Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_verse: Others may follow their gods, but we will always follow the Lord our God. The Lord Will Lead His People Home
translation_verse: Ditimbundi kamaa ŋáań tin làá fáatíǹ di-waaŋee ní, ama timbi làá nīn ŋáań tin làá fáatíǹ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiuee ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Ti-Dindaan làá jī dibeel Jeerusaleem tiŋkin

english_verse: The Lord said: At that time I will gather my people— the lame and the outcasts, and all others into whose lives I have brought sorrow.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá kóoǹní bin fōō tiweendee kí kpāfì, m làá gíiǹní bin tafal m dáaĺ ki yāntì bi yàl̄ ki bínní kuyuŋuee.

english_verse: Then the lame and the outcasts will belong to my people and become a strong nation. I, the Lord, will rule them from Mount Zion forever.
translation_verse: Bin fōō tiweendi gbantee, m làá dū-bi kí náań dinibul din bí dimaŋfalinee. Bin bínní kuyuŋunee, m làá dū-bi kí kpántí ditimbundi din pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Man bi-Dindaan di làá dāá nīn sá bi-bɔtiu Siiyɔn jool pu, kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan!

english_verse: Jerusalem, why are you crying? Don't you have a king? Have your advisors gone? Are you suffering like a woman in childbirth?
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee Jeerusaleem yab, ba pu ní ni sūǹ ki tátí míǹ? Ba pu ní ni bí ki yáliŋkí kii imatiŋween di bāań-nee? Naa ti cáá ubɔti níii? Ni-saŋkiliibi kpíì níii?

english_verse: Keep on groaning with pain, you people of Jerusalem! If you escape from your city to the countryside, you will still be taken as prisoners to Babylonia. But later I will rescue you from your enemies.
translation_verse: Nín̄ yáliŋkí nì ni-ba, kí nīn kūuntí kii upɔdaan di bíi màal̀ee. Di sá yii kɔŋkɔnnee ni làá nyā kitiŋin kí tin nín̄ kóò tisatin, áli kí tin bà Babiloon tiŋkin. Niin ní bi làá dā-ni kí líí, niin ní ti-Dindaan làá fīī-ni kí nyāntí ni-nannanliibi ŋaan.

english_verse: Zion, because of your sins you are surrounded by many nations who say, “We can hardly wait to see you disgraced.”
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee Jeerusaleem, atimbun tikpil kóoǹ ki kpáfì kí já nì si. Ŋi lì yii: «Tí bīil̀-kì! Bi yaa nāaǹ Siiyɔn tiŋki, án làá nīn mɔ̄ǹ-teeee!»

english_verse: Smash them to pieces, Zion! I'll let you be like a bull with iron horns and bronze hoofs. Crush those nations and bring their wealth to me, the Lord of the earth.
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, yīkìmaan kí gbá idi. M làá yàntī ní nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii unaa un yiŋyi sá tikúti ní u-tafuŋfukuti sá tasa kútee. Ni làá nàan̄ anibul tikpil. Tigaajawan tin ni làá fōō bi-ceeyee, ní dū-tì kí sú man ni-Dindaan, duulinya kɔkɔ kpiliu.

english_verse: Jerusalem, enemy troops have surrounded you; they have struck Israel's ruler in the face with a stick.
translation_verse: Sii Beetileem Eefiraata, Juuda timmu kansikinee, sii di sá kitiŋwaŋwaai. Ama sii poon ní m làá yàntī ubɔti un làá kpòotī m-nibul Isirayeelee ń nyānní. U-nyeeŋŋu kíliń doooo cannaaku ní, iyunti kpiŋkpiki poon.

english_verse: Bethlehem Ephrath, you are one of the smallest towns in the nation of Judah. But the Lord will choose one of your people to rule the nation— someone whose family goes back to ancient times.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dū u-nibul kí fá ŋyunti ŋubɔ poon, kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní unimpu un làá màal̀-uee ń dāá màal̀-u. Ŋyunti gbantee, u-nabiyaamu mun làá dāá kíń kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee làá dāá dāan̄ kí kūtì Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee pu.

english_verse: The Lord will abandon Israel only until this ruler is born, and the rest of his family returns to Israel.
translation_verse: Ubɔti gbantee làá dāá yīkì kí dū ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu, ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu yiŋkpaandi kí kpàà-bi. U-nibul làá dāá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin. Di sá yii u-kpaanti làá dāá gbìtī kí bà ilaan kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Like a shepherd taking care of his sheep, this ruler will lead and care for his people by the power and glorious name of the Lord his God. His people will live securely, and the whole earth will know his true greatness,
translation_verse: Úǹ di làá dāá cáań ŋgbansɔŋfi! Asuur yab yaa láa kɔ́nní ti-tiŋkin, bi-taaŋi yaa láa tāā ti-beeciŋŋinee, ti làá dāá lēē ti-kpilib kupaau bí já nì bi.

english_verse: because he will bring peace. Assyria Will Be Defeated Let Assyria attack our country and our palaces. We will counterattack, led by a number of rulers
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá dū kitàataajiki kí já nì Asuur tiŋki kí dāá dū kijisaakaai kí já nì Niimroodi tiŋki. Asuur yab yaa láa dòoń kí já nì ti ní ki kɔ́nní ti-tiŋkinee, ti-bɔtiuee làá dāá fīī-ti. Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee pɔŋŋu

english_verse: whose strong army will defeat the nation of Assyria. Yes, our leaders will rescue us, if those Assyrians dare to invade our land. The Survivors Will Be Safe
translation_verse: Jaakɔb naantiibi bin làá dāá kíń kí nīn bí anibul tikpil kansikinee làá dāá nīn náań nì dimalindi din nyánní ti-Dindaan ceeyee ní, kii utaa nín nì ki sɔ̀ŋkī timool puee. Baa làá nīn kā ki máká unil pu, kaa làá nīn kā ki cɔ́tí nisaal pu.

english_verse: A few of Jacob's descendants survived and are scattered among the nations. But the Lord will let them cover the earth like dew and rain that refreshes the soil.
translation_verse: Jaakɔb naantiibi bin làá dāá kíń kí nīn bí atimbunni, anibul kupaau kansikinee, bi làá dāá nīn bí kii gbikintee ní kupɔɔun peelii kansikin, kii digbikintipɔmbil din bí tipicaŋkpun kansikinee ní. U yaa pée jítì laakin kamaayee, u cútí ipeel ní ki tɔ̀ntī, ní ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí fīī-i.

english_verse: they will be helpless, completely destroyed. Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
translation_verse: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Tin làá dāá bàń ŋwiin gbantee sèé: <M làá dāá nàan̄ a-taamui, ní kí dāá kúntí a-janjatɔrɔkub.

english_verse: The Lord said: At that time I will wipe out your cavalry and chariots,
translation_verse: M làá dāá nàan̄ a-timmu, ní kí dāá wīī agun ŋin a máń ki tú a-timmuee.

english_verse: as well as your cities and your fortresses.
translation_verse: M làá dāá kúntí kusoou tuuŋŋi ni-kansikin. Baa dāa gíti kāntí u-kpaŋkpanti ni-kansikin.

english_verse: You will no longer worship the idols or stone images you have made— I will destroy them,
translation_verse: M làá dāá cóotí ni-windɔi, ní kí kúntí ni-timmu.

english_verse: together with the sacred poles and even your towns.
translation_verse: Nì mbum nì diŋuul poon ní m làá dāá tɔ̀ atimbun ŋin kaa tɔ́-mee ipɔntoon.»

english_verse: The Lord said to his people: Come and present your case to the hills and mountains.
translation_verse: Ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ee. Yīkì kí sòoǹ kí mɔ̄tì m-pu ajoon nimbiin, kí mɔ̄tì m-pu ŋgbantamu nimbiin.

english_verse: Israel, I am bringing charges against you— I call upon the mountains and the earth's firm foundation to be my witnesses.
translation_verse: Nimbi ajoon nì dinyeel din pu kitiŋ tɔ́kɔ́ kaa cìŋkēe, pīlifìmaan. Ti-Dindaan yíiń u-nibul ibeeyiin, u bíi sòoǹ Isirayeel yab bɔti.

english_verse: My people, have I wronged you in any way at all? Please tell me.
translation_verse: U bí yii: «M-nibul, ba ní m ŋá-si ní? Digìńdi dilal poon ní m kɔ́ǹ-si ní? Á kíí-mi!

english_verse: I rescued you from Egypt, where you were slaves. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to be your leaders.
translation_verse: M nín nyántìń-si Eejipiti tiŋkineeyaaa, m nín dá-si ki nyántì kuyuŋuneeyaaa, m nín tú Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì Miiriyam bí kpòotī-see ní m yīntì ní.

english_verse: Don't forget the evil plans of King Balak of Moab or what Balaam son of Beor said to him. Remember how I, the Lord, saved you many times on your way from Acacia to Gilgal. True Obedience
translation_verse: M-nibul, á téetí tin bí nee! Moowaab bɔtiu Balaaki nìn bɔ́ntì kí ŋá-si tikpitil. Téetí tin Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn Balaam nìn kíí-uee. Míǹ boonee, a yíkì Siitiim tantakalin ki cūtì Giilgaal paaŋŋu pu. A nìn ŋúń ki ká tiŋaŋkpaandi tin man a-Dindaan ŋá ki tīī-see.» Unimbɔti nín là unil ń nīn bí puee

english_verse: What offering should I bring when I bow down to worship the Lord God Most High? Should I try to please him by sacrificing calves a year old?
translation_verse: Ti yaa dɔ́miń kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaanee, ba ní ti máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́ kí cáań kí ŋá saraa kí tīī Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu dee? Ti kalin cāabìń dibindi diba nabil kí ŋá saraa kí tīī-uaaa?

english_verse: Will thousands of sheep or rivers of olive oil make God satisfied with me? Should I sacrifice to the Lord my first-born child as payment for my terrible sins?
translation_verse: U là ipijaa kutukub naaa, ŋkpam ń nīn pùub̀ ibun kutukub kutukub poon ní? Tí dū ti-jipɔŋkpilib kí ŋá saraa ti-yìntitam puɔɔɔ, ti nín dù ti-poon naŋu kí ŋá saraa ti-kpitii pu ní?

english_verse: The Lord God has told us what is right and what he demands: “See that justice is done, let mercy be your first concern, and humbly obey your God.” Cheating and Violence
translation_verse: Unil, ti-Dindaan dàkā-si tin ŋān̄ee. Kun u bàlifī-see di sá á nīn ŋáań tin bí deedeeyee, kí nīn néeń ki ŋáań tikɔkɔ nì tiniti ní kí nīn nóó a-Nimbɔtiu nì dibasintil. Inaamuul dambi nì bi ŋáań tipɔmbɔtee tafadaaldi

english_verse: I am the Lord, and you are wise to respect my power to punish. So listen to my message for the city of Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ nì bin kóò kitiŋ nee poonee! U làá fīī bin fàŋkí-uee. «Pīlifìmaan, Juuda naakookun yab, nimbi bin kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì kitiŋ nee poonee!

english_verse: Because of your sins, I will wound you and leave you ruined and defenseless.
translation_verse: An pu ní m dū falaa ki gbáń-ni, ki làá nàan̄-ni ni-kpitii pu.

english_verse: You will eat, but still be hungry; you will store up goods, but lose everything— I, the Lord, will let it all be captured in war.
translation_verse: Ni làá jī ama kaa làá díkì, ŋkùm làá nīn pée bí ni-dicaŋŋin ní. Ni làá dāá kpāafì ni-kpaajinti, ama tì làá bùkū. Báà ni yaa láa kpáafì ni-wanti tibaaa, m làá dāá bīil̀-tì kujaaun.

english_verse: You won't harvest what you plant or use the oil from your olive trees or drink the wine from grapes you grow.
translation_verse: Ni làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí bɔ̄l̀, ama kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí cā. Ni làá dāá ŋmáaḿ kí lēē ɔliifi subiliŋ kpam, ama kaa làá dāá ká-mì kí ŋmìtī. Ni làá dāá ŋàan̄ ndaam, ama kaa làá dāá nyɔ̀-mì.

english_verse: Jerusalem, this will happen because you followed the sinful example of kings Omri and Ahab. Now I will destroy you and your property. Then the people of every nation will make fun and insult you.
translation_verse: Ni nóó ubɔti Oomirii nì u-jipɔɔn Akaab dicaŋkun yab bimbikpitim. Ni ŋáań kii binib gbanti nín ŋáań puee. An pu ní m làá nàan̄ ni-tiŋki, ní kí yàntī bin kíǹee ń nīn bèel̄ nimbi bin kóò ki-nee. Icoo in jíń m-nibulee làá jī ni mun.»

english_verse: No one is loyal to God; no one does right. Everyone is brutal and eager to deceive everyone else.
translation_verse: Bin yú nì Unimbɔti deedeeyee kúntì kitiŋ nee pu, báà ubulcinnil ubɔbɔ kaa ti bí. Báà unil kaa ti bí ki-ni ki yú deedee nì Unimbɔti. Bi-kɔkɔ pée dàkafī nnikpaakoon pu ní. Báà ŋma pīil̀ u-juti kutaliŋŋu.

english_verse: People cooperate to commit crime. Judges and leaders demand bribes, and rulers cheat in court.
translation_verse: Bi yáb̀ kí ŋá ikpiti. Kí wàatī bí ŋá tiŋanee, bibɔtiibi sīintí bi nín là puee, ní bibɔsoonliibi sīintí kunimbiŋmiiu, ní akpambal lì bi nín là puee.

english_verse: The most honest of them is worse than a thorn patch. Your doom has come! Lookouts sound the warning, and everyone panics.
translation_verse: Bi-kansikin un pée sá unimɔntee bí kii abɔjanaakunee ní, un pée sá deedeedaanee jítiǹ kukuŋkuncikuu pu. Ni-tafadaaldi yuntiŋu bāań dee. Ni-bɔnaatiliibi bin cí-nee nìn sòon̄ an pu. Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, naa ti nyí tin poon ni bée.

english_verse: Don't trust anyone, not even your best friend, and be careful what you say to the one you love.
translation_verse: Ní taa fōō ni-jutiibi bɔti kí kíí, kí taa nín̄ máká ni-bɔɔbi pu. Báà sii a-ba nimpuu nimbiin gba, á nīn nyí nì a-ba nì tin a sòoǹee.

english_verse: Sons refuse to respect their own fathers, daughters rebel against their own mothers, and daughters-in-law despise their mothers-in-law. Your family is now your enemy.
translation_verse: Di sá yii kibininjabiki sìí ki-baa, ní kinimpubiki jáà nì ki-na, ní unimpu nì u-beel kaa kpí. Báà ŋma nannanliu sá u-dicaŋkun yɔu ní.

english_verse: But I trust the Lord God to save me, and I will wait for him to answer my prayer. The Nation Turns to God
translation_verse: Ama mamee, ti-Dindaan watil pú ní m kpèé, Unimbɔti un làá fīī-mee pu ní m máká. M-Nimbɔtiu làá pīlifiǹ-mi. Isirayeel yab máká Unimbɔti pu

english_verse: My enemies, don't be glad because of my troubles! I may have fallen, but I will get up; I may be sitting in the dark, but the Lord is my light.
translation_verse: Nimbi ti-nannanliibi, ní taa nín̄ fàal̀maan tin bāań-ti nee pu. Báà ti yaa lítì, ti làá fàtīí yīkì. Báà ti yaa bí dibɔmbɔndin, ti-Dindaan di sá ti-walifiŋu.

english_verse: I have sinned against the Lord. And so I must endure his anger, until he comes to my defense. But I know that I will see him making things right for me and leading me to the light.
translation_verse: Diŋuul din ti-Dindaan gíí ti-puee, ti máaǹ kí fōō-dì, kun puee ti yīntiǹ-u. Ama ŋyunti bí ki dòoń, u làá sòoǹ ti-bɔti kí pɔ̀-ti. U làá dāá nyāntí-ti kí gíiǹ ŋwalifin, kí gbéeǹ-ti u-ŋanti.

english_verse: You, my enemies, said, “The Lord God is helpless.” Now each of you will be disgraced and put to shame. I will see you trampled like mud in the street. A Bright Future
translation_verse: Ti-nannanliibi yaa láa ká mimmee, bi làá dāá kɔ́ icoo ni. Bíǹ bin nìn bàlifī-ti yii: «Ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiuee bí lee?» Bi làá dāá tāā-bi kí ŋmàtifì kii adan pu kpatee. Ti làá dāá ká míǹ nì ti-nimbibulii.

english_verse: Towns of Judah, the day is coming when your walls will be rebuilt, and your boundaries enlarged.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń, bi làá dāá fàtīí mā digundi kí tū ni-tiŋyil. Ŋwiin gbantee, ni-tiŋki làá dāá wàan̄ kí kūtì.

english_verse: Those nations will suffer disaster because of what they did. Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
translation_verse: Kitiŋ laakin kɔkɔ kíǹee làá dāá kpántí kuteeu binib bin kóò ki-puee kpitii pu.

english_verse: Lead your people, Lord! Come and be our shepherd. Grasslands surround us, but we live in a forest. So lead us to Bashan and Gilead, and let us find pasture as we did long ago.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, dū a-pikpaadɔŋu kí kpàà a-nibul din sá a-fakalee. Dì bí kuteeun di-baba isufi in lòoǹ abilee māntìi tú-dì. Péetí-dì kí cùnnì Baasan pikpaakun nì Galaadi tiŋkin kii dooooyee.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will work miracles just as I did when I led you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kii ŋyunti ŋun a nìn nyántìń-ti Eejipiti tiŋkinee, gíti ŋá a-maamaaci tuuŋŋi kí dàkà-ti.

english_verse: Nations will see this and be ashamed because of their helpless armies. They will be in shock, unable to speak or hear,
translation_verse: Atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib làá dāá ká míǹ ní icoo ń dāá cúú-bi, min kamaa bi cáá mpɔnee. Bi làá dāá cúú bi-nyɔmmu, ní bi-tafaliŋ ń kpáá baa ti gbìl̀.

english_verse: because of their fear of me, your Lord and God. Then they will come trembling, crawling out of their fortresses like insects or snakes, lapping up the dust. No One Is Like God The people said:
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá bàlim̀ ntampukumin kii ikoobu nì ipeel in fù i-biŋŋi puee. Bi làá dāá nyānní bi-balilaŋki bi-wunti jìkì kí dāan̄ sii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu cee. Bi làá dāá fàŋkì-si.

english_verse: Our God, no one is like you. We are all that is left of your chosen people, and you freely forgive our sin and guilt. You don't stay angry forever; you're glad to have pity
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti ulɔu di gíti bí kii sisee? A lèekī a-nibul din kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee yìntitam, ki pūǹ di-kpitii. Aa fòol̄ diŋuul kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ama an mɔ̄ǹ-si á nīn dàkà-ti a-ŋanti.

english_verse: and pleased to be merciful. You will trample on our sins and throw them in the sea.
translation_verse: A làá fàtīí tí sɔ̄ ti-saai, a làá tāā ti-yìntitam kí múĺ, ní kí dū ti-kpitii kí tɔ̄ tiŋku taapu taapu.

english_verse: You will keep your word and be faithful to Jacob and to Abraham, as you promised our ancestors many years ago.
translation_verse: A làá dàkà Jaakɔb naantiibi a-deedeeu, kí dàkà Abraam naantiibi a-laŋŋaŋfitiiku, kii a nín nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ti-baabi dooooyee puee.

english_verse: I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh. The Fierce Anger of the Lord
translation_verse: Kugbɔŋu nee poonee, tibɔti tin sòoǹ Niiniifi tiŋki puee kā. Tibɔti gbantee, Unimbɔti lēē-tì ki dàkā Nawum un sá ueelikoosjee. Ti-Dindaan gíí Niiniifi tiŋki pu diŋuul

english_verse: The Lord is powerful, yet patient; he makes sure that the guilty are always punished. He can be seen in storms and in whirlwinds; clouds are the dust from his feet.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan kaa fòol̄ diŋuul malaa ní ki cáá mpɔŋkpaan, ama waa yàntī dibɔkpil daan fám kaa dáaĺ u-tafal. Kunaakpaabuŋŋu nì kubuŋkpaaŋŋu poon ní u còom̄. Atagban di sá u yaa tà, kukpɔŋkpɔŋu kun yíkée.

english_verse: At the Lord's command, oceans and rivers dry up. Bashan, Mount Carmel, and Lebanon wither, and their flowers fade.
translation_verse: U kpàtī tiŋku pu ní ú kpā, ní ki yàntī ibun kɔkɔ nyim fóotí. Baasan pɔɔku nì Kaarmeel jool mooti fáaḿ, ní Leebanɔn pumpukum yɔ́ĺ.

english_verse: At the sight of the Lord, mountains and hills tremble and melt; the earth and its people shudder and shake.
translation_verse: U yaa dòońee, ajoon cìŋkī ní, ní ŋgbantamu kpìkitī. U yaa páaǹnée kitiŋ cìŋkī, ní binib bin kɔkɔ bí ki-puee jìkì.

english_verse: Who can stand the heat of his furious anger? It flashes out like fire and shatters stones. The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
translation_verse: U yaa fōō diŋuulee, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí ŋmátí? U yaa fōō mbumee, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ? U-ŋuul fòol̄ bìlbil kii ŋŋmee ní, ataŋkpee gba wìil̄ u-nimbiin ní.

english_verse: The Lord is good. He protects those who trust him in times of trouble.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan ŋān̄! U sá kibalilaŋ ní dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu poon. U wúǹ bin di sáń ki kóò-uee pu,

english_verse: So don't plot against the Lord! He wipes out his enemies, and they never revive.
translation_verse: Ba ní ni bíi bɔ́ntí ti-Dindaan pu? Úǹ di nàantí u-nannanliibi, ní baa ti làá wɔ́b́-ni nliliitiim.

english_verse: They are like drunkards overcome by wine, or like twisted thornbushes burning in a fire.
translation_verse: Di sá yii bi bí kii abɔjanaakun ŋin sɔ̀kɔ̄ee ní, bíǹ bin nyù idafi ki gbéèyee. Ŋŋmi làá wà-bi múb kii timɔkulindee ní.

english_verse: Assyria, one of your rulers has made evil plans against the Lord.
translation_verse: Unil un bíi bɔ́ntí kí já nì ti-Dindaanee, unil un di cáá ilandɔkɔkpitee nyánní sii Niiniifi tiŋkin ní.

english_verse: But the Lord says, “Assyria, no matter how strong you are, you will be cut down! My people Judah, I have troubled you before, but I won't do it again.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Báà ni-nannanliibi yaa wīikí ki pɔ̄ɔ̄, m làá nàan̄-bi ní bí kúntí múb. M sīntiǹ-ni taapu, maa ti làá ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: I'll snap your chains and set you free from the Assyrians.”
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, m làá nyìkitī diwaŋgul din bi dūu nyīkiǹ ni-puee, ní kí tìl̄ ni-kusakai.»

english_verse: Assyria, this is what else the Lord says to you: “Your name will be forgotten. I will destroy every idol in your temple, and I will send you to the grave, because you are worthless.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tin nimbi Niiniifi yab puee sèé: «Naa ti làá màal̀ mbiyaamu mun làá dāá fōō ni-yindee. M làá kúntí awaakpitikaa nì amɔɔkaa ŋin bí ni-waadiikunee. M bíi bɔ́ntí ni-kaakul, di sá yii naa bí tiban.»

english_verse: Nineveh, someone is coming to attack and scatter you. Guard your fortresses! Watch the road! Be brave! Prepare for battle!
translation_verse: Juuda yab, ntuun ŋun cāabìń tibɔmɔntiilee di dòoń ajoon puee, ŋu sòoǹ ŋgbansɔŋfi bɔti ní! Jīmaan ni-jiŋaalib, cáaḿmaan ni-pooŋyi saraabi kí tīī Unimbɔti. Kun puee, ukpitee kaa ti làá dāan̄ kí fōō ni-tiŋki, bi pée nāaǹ-u ní múb.

english_verse: Judah and Israel are like trees with branches broken by their enemies. But the Lord is going to restore their power and glory. *
translation_verse: Niiniifi, bi dòoń kí jáǹ-si dee. Bijanjaliibi, jɔ̄m̀maan sintil difɔkɔŋi pu kí nīn cí, nín̄ cɔ́ŋkímaan adan pu ki kpèé, yòom̄maan ni-gbajab kí gbìn̄, kámaan kunyannyaau kí pɔ́ɔǹ ni-ba.

english_verse: Their horses prance, and their armored chariots dart around like lightning or flaming torches.
translation_verse: Bi-nannanliibi janjaliibi gbampɔɔŋi máǹ, ní bi pēē tiwamman cínciŋ. Bi yaa gbāaǹ dikɔ̀ndi puee, bi-tɔrɔkub kúti ŋmóò ní làka laka kii ŋŋmee, ní bi fīintí bi-kpammu.

english_verse: An officer gives a command. But his soldiers stumble, as they hasten to build a shelter to protect themselves against rocks thrown down from the city wall.
translation_verse: Janjatɔrɔkub dū bi-ba ki bíl̀ adan pu, bi kpátìi gbí kitiŋ jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu a lì kii iŋminaapoolee. Bi yáb̀ kii utaa nín ŋmóò puee ní.

english_verse: Nineveh is disgraced. The queen is dragged off. Her servant women mourn; they moan like doves, and they beat their breasts in sorrow.
translation_verse: Bi gbáń ki pīitì mpunyɔmu mun bíitiǹ ibunee mpɔn, bi jáń ki fōō dibeecindi.

english_verse: Nineveh is like a pond with leaking water. Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!” can be heard everywhere. But everyone is leaving.
translation_verse: Binannanliibi yōoǹ diwaal ki cáa cūnnì kuyuŋu. Binimpoobi bin nìn jáaḿ-dèe bíi sūǹ ki yáliŋkí kii abeenanjilee, ní ki fátí bi-biŋŋi nì kunimbaau.

english_verse: Enemy soldiers shout, “The city is full of treasure and all kinds of wealth. Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
translation_verse: Niiniifi yab sá kii nnyimbilkaam min nnyim nyáń ki dóòyee ní. Bi nìn kūuntí ki yíì-bi yii: «Sīĺmaan! Sīĺmaan,» ama báà ubɔ kaa fātìi kpēē u-boon gba.

english_verse: Nineveh is doomed! Destroyed! Her people tremble with fear; their faces turn pale.
translation_verse: Fūkul̀maan kitiŋee nimbiliŋ nì ki-sindaariyau! Ki-gaajawanti kaa cáá dikúntil, tiwammɔntiil kɔkɔ nì ti-bulifi gbí ki-ni.

english_verse: What happened to this city? They were safer there than powerful lions in a den, with no one to disturb them.
translation_verse: Bi fúkúl̀-kì ki gbákal̀-kì ki nāaǹ-kì. Un cáá dipɔbilee gíti kpá, bi-taaŋi yɔ̄tì, tiwun kɔkɔ gbáà kpàkpakpa ní inimbiin cúu kpántì. Niiniifi bí kii gbikinti un bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee ní

english_verse: These are the same lions that ferociously attacked their victims, then dragged away the flesh to feed their young.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kin poon gbikintib nìn kóòyee bí la? Niin ní agbikintipɔmbil nìn kāntí ki jīǹ. Ugbikintija yaa nìn búntì dijinnyaabilee, ubɔ kaa nìn gbèetī u-biyaamu.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful is against you, Nineveh. God will burn your chariots and send an army to kill those young lions of yours. You will never again make victims of others or send messengers to threaten everyone on this earth.
translation_verse: Ugbikintija nìn cútí tinan ní ki tìì u-biyaamu. U nìn kù ipeel ki tìì ugbikintinaati, u nìn gbēentí laakin u kóòyee ipeel in u cúú ki tɔ̄ntèe.

english_verse: here is your fate— cracking whips, churning wheels; galloping horses, roaring chariots;
translation_verse: Pīlifìmaan! Anaalab di nìiǹnée! Tɔrɔkub taaŋi di wàkalìńee! Itaamu di tòó càlib calibee! Kujaau tɔrɔkub di jàkànée!

english_verse: You were nothing more than a prostitute using your magical charms and witchcraft to attract and trap nations.
translation_verse: Niiniifi tiŋki ŋá alaakpaatuun ŋfunyɔm kutuku kutuku pu. Kì nìn ŋān̄ ki bí gbàlgbalgbal, ní ki nìn sàtī binib. Kì nìn cáá ki-laakpaati ki cútí atimbun tikpil kuyuŋu, ní kì nìn cáá ki-nyɔkɔŋu ki sàtī anibul.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, am now your enemy. I will pull up your skirt and let nations and kingdoms stare at your nakedness.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. M làá já nì si. M làá kóoǹ a-wɔndoou kí bìitī a-cancaŋgbeel pu kí dàkà atimbun, ní kí bìitī a-cooi pu kí dàkà abee ŋin kíǹee.

english_verse: I will cover you with garbage, treat you like trash, and rub you in the dirt.
translation_verse: M làá dū titampummool kí bìin̄ a-pu kí kɔ́ǹ-si icoo, ní kí nyāntí-si kí páań mpaampiin pu.

english_verse: Everyone who sees you will turn away and shout, “Nineveh is done for! Is anyone willing to mourn or to give her comfort?” Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔ làá dāá ká-see dāa sáń-si ní ki lì yii: «Niiniifi tiŋki pée nāaǹ ní múb, ŋma làá yāliŋkì ki-pu dee? La ní m làá nín ká binib bí dāá ŋméeǹ-kì dee?» Bi làá ŋá Niiniifi kii bi nín ŋá Teebeesi puee ní

english_verse: Nineveh, do you feel safer than the city of Thebes? The Nile River was its wall of defense.
translation_verse: Niiniifi tiŋki, a dàkafī yii a sɔ́ǹ Teebeesi tiŋki kin bí Niil buntaaŋi kansikinee níii? Nnyim di nìn māntìi tú-kì, ní dimɔɔl cí-kì, ní nnyim sá ki-guŋŋi.

english_verse: Thebes trusted the mighty power of Ethiopia and Egypt; the nations of Put and Libya were her allies.
translation_verse: Eetiiyoopii nì Eejipiti di nìn sá ki-pɔŋŋu ŋun kaa cáá dikúntilee. Puuti yab nì Liibii yab di nìn sá ki-bɔɔbi.

english_verse: But she was captured and taken to a foreign country. Her children were murdered at every street corner. The members of her royal family were auctioned off, and her high officials were bound in chains.
translation_verse: Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, bi cúú Teebeesi yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu. Bi nìn nàn̄ bi-bipɔmmu asaŋkaŋkpil kɔkɔ pu. Bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ki yākatì bi-kpambaliŋ ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu, ní ki bóob́ ki-kpootiliibi ikusaka.

english_verse: Nineveh, now it's your turn! You will get drunk and try to hide from your enemy.
translation_verse: Sii Niiniifi tiŋki, digìńdi làá dāá kɔ́ si mun, a làá dāá nyàab̀ kí báĺ. Sii mun làá dāá nyàab̀ kibalilaŋ a-nannanliibi ń taa cúú-si. Niiniifi tiŋki làá lítí

english_verse: Your fortresses are fig trees with ripe figs. Merely shake the trees, and fruit will fall into every open mouth.
translation_verse: A-sintil difɔkɔŋi sá kii fiigi biliŋ ŋin lúń busubu pu ki mántèe ní. Bi yaa pée yáká-buee, abil gbátí ní kí kɔ́ un là kí ŋmɔ́-ŋee nyɔkɔn.

english_verse: Your army is weak. Fire has destroyed the crossbars on your city gates; now they stand wide open to your enemy.
translation_verse: Kpèè a-janjaliibi bí kii binimpoobee ní, a-nannanliibi yaa páaǹnée, a-tiŋki punyɔmmu cútí kí pìitī ní bàaa bí kɔ́, di sá yii ŋŋmi wùn̄ mu-kpàlkaati.

english_verse: Your city is under attack. Haul in extra water! Strengthen your defenses! Start making bricks! Stir the mortar!
translation_verse: Niiniifi yab, lúḿmaan nnyim kí yóoń, di sá yii binannanliibi làá màntīí tū ni-tiŋki. Mɔ̀tīí ŋāŋkìmaan ni-sintil difɔkɔŋi, tāāmaan kuyɔkɔu, ní kí yòon̄ ni-brikisi gaŋgammu!

english_verse: You will still go up in flames and be cut down by swords that will wipe you out like a field attacked by grasshoppers. So, go ahead and increase like a swarm of locusts!
translation_verse: Ama niin ní ŋŋmi làá wà-ni ní kpú, kujaaun ní ni làá kpú kí céetí. Bi làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni kii inaakitoon nín ŋmóò ki céetí tikɔkɔ puee ní. Báà ubɔ kaa ti kóò Niiniifi tiŋkin Niiniifi, a-nib nìn wīikí kii inaakitoonee ní!

english_verse: More merchants are in your city than there are stars in the sky— but they are like locusts that eat everything, then fly away.
translation_verse: Ni-nyampoobi nìn wīikí ki jítiǹ iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee. Kɔŋkɔnnee bi wáŋkì kii inaakicaan nín yíkí kí búntí puee.

english_verse: Your guards and your officials are swarms of locusts. On a chilly day they settle on a fence, but when the sun comes out, they take off to who-knows-where.
translation_verse: A-ciitiliibi nìn būtì kii inaakicaanee ní, ní a-kàlimbi mun nìn wīikí kii kunaakicikuee. An yaa dá láá sɔ̀m̀ee, inaaki náká an pu. Ama ŋwìiń yaa nyáńee, i yíkí ní kí búntí ní ubɔ kaa nyí laakin i túĺee. I nín bí la dee? Asaluu un baa ŋūǹ kí ŋāŋkèe

english_verse: King of Assyria, your officials and leaders are sound asleep, while your people are scattered in the mountains. Yes, your people are sheep without a shepherd.
translation_verse: Asuur bɔtiu, a-kpootiliibi gèen̄ kaa fīntì! A-baatandambi kaa ti bíi cìŋkī bi-ba! A-janjaliibi yàl̄ ki gbí ajoon pu, ní ubɔ kaa bí kí kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì.

english_verse: You're fatally wounded. There's no hope for you. But everyone claps when they hear this news, because your constant cruelty has caused them pain.
translation_verse: Asaluu un gbáń-see kaa ti cáá diŋaŋkil. Nnyɔkɔ kaa bí kí cáaǹ tiweendi tin a fōōyee. Bin kɔkɔ gbìl̄ tin bāań-see kpáafí bi-ŋalii nnaabu ŋun bāań-see pu, di sá yii a ŋá ntoom ki kíǹ ŋma? A-toom kaa cáá kikuntilaŋ.

english_verse: I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me. Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔti tin ní u lēē ki dàkā u-bɔnaatiliu Abakuukee. Abakuuki bíi yíì Unimbɔti ú jòoń-u

english_verse: Our Lord, how long must I beg for your help before you listen? How long before you save us from all this violence?
translation_verse: M-Dindaan, kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní m làá nīn yíì-si á jòoń-mi ní á nín pīlifì-mi ní? M bíi kūuntí yii tipɔmbɔti gbóotì, ama ní aa bíi fìil̄-ti.

english_verse: Why do you make me watch such terrible injustice? Why do you allow violence, lawlessness, crime, and cruelty to spread everywhere?
translation_verse: Ba pu ní a yàntī m kāntí atuŋkpiti ní? Ba pu ní unil wɔ́b̀ u-juti ní a kpèé ki ŋmí ní? Diwɔ́bil nì tipɔmbɔti di māntìi tú-mi. Kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu nì kujaau di kíǹ ki bí an kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Laws cannot be enforced; justice is always the loser; criminals crowd out honest people and twist the laws around. The Lord Answers Habakkuk
translation_verse: Mara wɔ̀b̄ kaa ti cáá mpɔn, ní an kaa ti sá un bɔti ŋān̄ee ní bi pɔ̀. Unikpiti nyīī deedeedaan ki múĺ, an pu ní ibɔsoon poonee, ibaamɔn kaa ti bí. Ti-Dindaan kíí Abakuuki: Babiloon yab cīiń

english_verse: Look and be amazed at what's happening among the nations! Even if you were told, you would never believe what's taking place now.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kpèèmaan tin bíi jītí atimbun ŋin kíǹee kansikin tiŋan. Yàntīmaan án bàkatīǹ-ni sèeee! Di sá yii m làá ŋá maamaaci tundi diba ni-yuntii nee poon. Ubɔ di yaa bàà máafì-ni tibɔti gbanti, naa bàà làá fōō-tì kí kíí.

english_verse: I am sending the Babylonians. They are fierce and cruel— marching across the land, conquering cities and towns.
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan, m làá yàntī Babiloon yab ń dāan̄, dinibul gbanti kaa sūǹ isaa ní ki néeń tipɔmbɔti. Bi yìiǹ duulinya kɔkɔn ki fòol̄ binib timmu ki cáa gà bi-biŋŋi.

english_verse: How fearsome and frightening. Their only laws and rules are the ones they make up.
translation_verse: Bi sá tinibilindi ní ki cáá tifaandi. Bíǹ bi-ba di sīintí bi-marab nì bi-pɔŋŋu.

english_verse: Their cavalry troops are faster than leopards, more ferocious than wolves hunting at sunset, and swifter than hungry eagles suddenly swooping down.
translation_verse: Bi-taamui yáb̀ ki jítiǹ iguloobu, ki cáá ntoom ki jítiǹ digbiŋgbil din cá kukpɔŋu kujoouee. Bi-tanjakaliibi nyánní ndan ki dòoń bi-taamui yùkufìń. Bi ŋàaǹ kii ukaalun nín tòó pu kí cúú tiba kí jēe ní.

english_verse: They are eager to destroy, and they gather captives like handfuls of sand.
translation_verse: Bi-kɔkɔ dòoń kí fūkul̀, ní bi-nimbikpeeŋu pée cɔ́ bi-nyɔkɔpu. Bi kóoǹ iyumbu ki kpáfì i wīikí kii dibulee.

english_verse: Then suddenly they disappear like a gust of wind— those sinful people who worship their own strength. Habakkuk Complains Again
translation_verse: Bi jītí kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee ní ki nìkì bi-saŋŋu. Kun pée páb́-bee di sá bi-pɔŋŋu, ŋúǹ di sá bi-nimbɔtiu.» Ubɔnaatil tí bíi kūuntí ki yíì Unimbɔti

english_verse: Holy Lord God, mighty rock, you are eternal, and we are safe from death. You are using those Babylonians to judge and punish others.
translation_verse: Doooo ŋkilkaaminee, sii di sá ti-Dindaan, sii di sá m-Nimbɔtiu, ki sá circirdaan ní kaa kúù. M-Dindaan, sii di lēē dinibul nee dí sòoǹ ti-bɔti. M-taŋkpanaakooku, a tīī-dì mpɔn dí dáaĺ ti-tafal.

english_verse: The people you put on this earth are like fish or reptiles without a leader.
translation_verse: Di sá yii a yāntì binib bí kii tiŋkun jɔmiiyee, a lì kii tin fù ti-pool pu kaa cáá ukpootilee.

english_verse: Then an enemy comes along and takes them captive with hooks and nets. It makes him so happy
translation_verse: Babiloon yab cútí binib kii ujɔm un bi tɔ́ njɔmpiin ki cúúyee ní. Kulaaŋŋu ní bi dù kí cúú-bi, ní kí dū bi-naanyaaŋŋu kí kóoǹ-bi. Niinee ní an kíǹ ki mɔ̄ǹ-bi ní bi fàal̀.

english_verse: that he offers sacrifices to his fishing nets, because they make him rich and provide choice foods.
translation_verse: Bi ŋáań saraabi ki tìì bi-laanti, ní ki tùutī talaalub ki tìì bi-naanyaaŋyi. Di sá yii bi-laanti nì bi-naanyaaŋyi pu ní bi-jinti mèeǹ ki mɔ̄.

english_verse: Will he keep hauling in his nets and destroying nations without showing mercy?
translation_verse: Mimmee bi làá nīn gbíntìi fúutí bi-tàataajimmu kujitooun ki kù atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib nì inimbinaakulimaaa?

english_verse: While standing guard on the watchtower, I waited for the Lord's answer, before explaining the reason for my complaint.
translation_verse: M làá yūĺ sintil, m làá jɔ̄m̀ kí tɔ́kɔń digunlɔkɔl pu kí kpèè tin Unimbɔti làá tùkù-mee, nì m nín bíi yáliŋkée, u nín làá kíí-mi puee. Kun dɔ̄ ki cí deedeedaan nì un wɔ́b̀ u-jutiibee

english_verse: Then the Lord told me: “I will give you my message in the form of a vision. Write it clearly enough to be read at a glance.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-Dindaan kíí-mi yii: «Ŋmà tin m bíi lèekī ki dàkà-si nee. Ŋmà kí nákań tipilindi pu, binib ń ŋmā kí kàaǹ sɔkɔmii.

english_verse: At the time I have decided, my words will come true. You can trust what I say about the future. It may take a long time, but keep on waiting— it will happen!
translation_verse: Dileedakal nee cí di-yuntiŋu ní kí ŋá kii an nín lēē ki dàkā puee. Di-yuntiŋu tóobiń, dàa làá gbíntí. Báà an yaa yúntàaa, cīití-dì. Tin m lēē ki dàkā-si nee, án làá pée ŋá míǹ ní. An pée kpá kí gbíntí.

english_verse: “I, the Lord, refuse to accept anyone who is proud. Only those who live by faith are acceptable to me.” Trouble for Evil People
translation_verse: Kpèè, unil un kaa bí deedeeyee yòontí u-ba yilpu, ama deedeedaan kāntí dimaŋfal u-deedeeu pu ní.

english_verse: Wine is treacherous, and arrogant people are never satisfied. They are no less greedy than death itself— they open their mouths as wide as the world of the dead and swallow everyone.
translation_verse: Tiŋman ndaam kíiĺ unileeee! Ulambidaan kaa cáá diŋuŋfil. U wàatī u-nyɔkɔ bàaa kii ditaŋkpiilee, waa díkì kii ŋkúmee. U jáà ki fòol̄ atimbun kɔkɔ, ní ki cáá anibul kɔkɔ pu mpɔn.

english_verse: But they will be mocked with these words: You're doomed! You stored up stolen goods and cheated others of what belonged to them.
translation_verse: Ama, binib gbanti kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn gà alaŋkpan ki bèel̄-u ní ki lāā-u.» Mbusub bɔti Bi dāa lì yii: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni! Ni bí ki fìkì binib wanti kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu? Ni mɔ̀tīi kútí ni-pɔɔŋŋi nyiŋfiŋu pu dee!

english_verse: But without warning, those you owe will demand payment. Then you will become a frightened victim.
translation_verse: Bin pīnnì-ni animbilee làá dāá cíliń ni-pu ní dicilpu dicilpu. Bi làá dāá yīkì kí cìŋkì cìŋkì-ni. Bi làá dāá fūkul̀-ni kí téeǹ.

english_verse: You robbed cities and nations everywhere on earth and murdered their people. Now those who survived will be as cruel to you.
translation_verse: Ni fúkúl̀ atimbun tikpil. Anibul ŋin kíǹee mun làá dāá fūkul̀-ni míǹ mbaantiim. Di sá yii ni kūū binib, ki ŋá Juuda tiŋki nì ki-timmu nì bin kóò mu-nee tipɔmbɔti!

english_verse: You're doomed! You made your family rich at the expense of others. You even said to yourself, “I'm above the law.”
translation_verse: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni! Ni nyàab̀ dulim gaajati kí dūú kpāafì kí síiń ni-dicaŋŋi yab, ní ki māā ni-diiŋŋi ki tɔ̄kɔntí yilpu, nnaabu yaa páaǹnée, án taa gbēē-ni.

english_verse: But you will bring shame on your family and ruin to yourself for what you did to others.
translation_verse: Tin ni bɔ́ntì kí ŋée làá cáań icoo kí tɔ̄ ni-dicaŋŋi yab pu ní. Ni nín nāaǹ anibul tikpil puee, nimbi ni-ba maŋfal ní ni nāaǹ.

english_verse: The very stones and wood in your home will testify against you.
translation_verse: Ataŋkpee ŋin bi dūu máń agunee gba làá nīn kūuntí ki kɔ́kɔĺ-ni, ní idɔ in bi dūu tɔ́kɔǹ kudiiyee ń kíí-ŋi.

english_verse: You're doomed! You built a city on crime and violence.
translation_verse: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni! Ni māā ni-timmu ki tɔ̄kɔntí nnikpaakoon nì tin kaa bí deedeeyee pu ní.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful sends up in flames what nations and people work so hard to gain.
translation_verse: An pu ní anibul gìńdi kúntí ŋŋmin, ní atimbun bí ki bìǹ fám. Tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kaa nyánní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan cee níii?

english_verse: Just as water fills the sea, the land will be filled with people who know and honor the Lord.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, báà ŋma làá béé ti-Dindaan nyooti, tì làá dāá gbí kitiŋ pu kii nnyim nín gbí tiŋku poon puee ní.

english_verse: Now you will be disgraced instead of praised. The Lord will make you drunk, and when others see you naked, you will lose their respect.
translation_verse: Ama icoo làá cúú-ni gbòooo, kaa sá tinyool! Ni mun, nyɔ̀maan kí gbí bí ká ni-cancaŋgbeeŋi. Ti-Dindaan làá páb́-ni ní nyɔ̀ u-ŋuul din kā u-yukubilinee. Ni-jilmau làá kpántí icoo.

english_verse: You destroyed trees and animals on Mount Lebanon; you were ruthless to towns and people everywhere. Now you will be terrorized. Idolatry Is Foolish
translation_verse: Di sá yii tipɔmbɔti tin ni ŋá Leebanɔn tiŋkinee làá fàtīí gítiń ni-pu. Ni pɔ̄fì tiwaŋkuti. Too tiwaŋkuti gbanti di làá kɔ́ǹ-ni dinyoondin. Di sá yii ni kūū binib, ki ŋá Juuda tiŋki nì ki-timmu nì bin kóò mu-nee tipɔmbɔti!

english_verse: What is an idol worth? It's merely a false god. Why trust a speechless image made from wood or metal by human hands?
translation_verse: Ba ní bi làá dū diwaal kí ŋá ní ukpiŋkpiiti kpítí-dì ní? An sá tikúti ní bi dūntì ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ ní an dàkà tinyimɔmbɔti. Ukpiŋkpiiti di kpítì-dì ní dàa ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ. Kin ba pu ní u gíti máká di-pu nan dee?

english_verse: What can you learn from idols covered with silver or gold? They can't even breathe. Pity anyone who says to an idol of wood or stone, “Get up and do something!”
translation_verse: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni! Ni tùkù didɔgindi yii: <Yīkì!> ki tùkù ditaŋkpal din kaa ŋūǹ kí sòoǹee yii: <Fìntī.> Ditaŋkpal kaa ŋūǹ kí dàkà-si tiba. Báà bi yaa dūntì sindaariya nì animbil ki nákaǹ-dàaa, dàa cáá kufoou!

english_verse: Let all the world be silent— the Lord is present in his holy temple.
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan úǹ kóò u-circir diikun ní. Kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu nib ń ŋmīĺ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ u-nimbiin!»

english_verse: I know your reputation, Lord, and I am amazed at what you have done. Please turn from your anger and be merciful; do for us what you did for our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, m gbìl̄ atuŋkpaan ŋin a ŋée pu. An cúú-mi tifaandi gba. Ti-Dindaan, fàtīí ŋá a-tuuŋŋi gbanti ti-wiiŋyi nee poon, yàntī báà ŋma ń béé-ŋi ti-yuntii nee poon. Báà a yaa fōō ti-pu diŋuulaaa, téetí a-poommɔŋŋu pu.

english_verse: You are the same Holy God who came from Teman and Paran to help us. The brightness of your glory covered the heavens, and your praises were heard everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nyánní Teeman tiŋkin ki dòoń, circir Nimbɔtiu páaǹní Paaran jooŋŋi pu. U nín sá ukpaan puee bīī kutagbɔŋu pu, ní u-nyɔŋkii gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu.

english_verse: Your glory shone like the sun, and light flashed from your hands, hiding your mighty power.
translation_verse: U wāĺ bɔ́iii kii ŋwalifee, ní itaaŋmɔŋmɔ nyēeń u-ŋaan ki jìl̀ pàlpal. Niin ní u-pɔŋŋu mun kā.

english_verse: Dreadful diseases and plagues marched in front and followed behind.
translation_verse: Bìlbil kúm līī u-nyɔkɔpu ní nnaanyeem tēentí u-tabɔbiliŋ.

english_verse: When you stopped, the earth shook; when you stared, nations trembled; when you walked along your ancient paths, eternal mountains and hills crumbled and collapsed.
translation_verse: U yaa sāā ki yúl̀ee, kitiŋ cìŋkī ní. U yaa fātìi kpēē atimbun nibee, bi-wunti gbáà ní kpàkpakpa. Jaanjaan jooŋŋi fáá iwèeń, ní cannaaku gbantammu lábitì ki cìb̄, ŋíǹ mun di nìn sá njaminee u-saŋŋu.

english_verse: The tents of desert tribes in Cushan and Midian were ripped apart.
translation_verse: M ká Kusan yab tantib kaa ti bí tiban. Madiyan yab kɔŋkooŋyi cīŋkì nì tifaandi.

english_verse: Our Lord, were you angry with the monsters of the deep? You attacked in your chariot and wiped them out.
translation_verse: Mimmee ti-Dindaan, ibun pu ní a fōō diŋuulaaa? Ibun pu ní a fōō mbum naaa? Tiŋku pu ní a-ŋuul gà lìblib yéèee? A jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ atagban pu kii dijajil tɔrɔkubee.

english_verse: Your arrows were ready and obeyed your commands. You split the earth apart with rivers and streams;
translation_verse: A bɔ́ntì a-tɔbu, ní dinyɔɔbundi din a sòon̄ee sá kii ipiinee. A dū ibun ki búkutì kitiŋ.

english_verse: mountains trembled at the sight of you; rain poured from the clouds; ocean waves roared and rose.
translation_verse: Ajoon wál̀-si ní ki fāŋkì ki fōō dijinjikil. Utaakpaan nìn̄ nì mpɔn, ní tiŋku yāntì bi gbìl̄ u-bintindi pu. U tòó u-nyiŋgbanti yilpu.

english_verse: In your furious anger, you trampled on nations
translation_verse: A-ŋuul poonee, a yìiǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu, a-bum poonee, a tà ki mátí atimbun.

english_verse: to rescue your people and save your chosen one. You crushed a nation's ruler and stripped his evil kingdom of its power.
translation_verse: A nyáń kí fīī a-nibul kí fīī ubɔti un a lēēyee. A líì un sá uyidaan binikpitib dicaŋkunee, ki nāaǹ u-yab kɔkɔ múb.

english_verse: His troops had come like a storm, hoping to scatter us and glad to gobble us up. To them we were refugees in hiding— but you smashed their heads with their own weapons.
translation_verse: A dū úǹ u-ba piiŋyi ní ki sāatìi cífì u-janjaliibi yiliŋ. Bi bàà sáń ki dòoń kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee kí dāá yàaǹ-ti. Bi nìn kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi, a lì kii bi kpáàa cúú uwɔfi ki bíi tɔ̀ntī dibalinee.

english_verse: Then your chariots churned the waters of the sea. Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
translation_verse: A cátì nsan tiŋkun laakin tinyiŋgban pɔ̄ɔ̄yee a-taamui cōom̀ ki jítì.

english_verse: When I heard this message, I felt weak from fear, and my lips quivered. My bones seemed to melt, and I stumbled around. But I will patiently wait. Someday those vicious enemies will be struck by disaster. Trust in a Time of Trouble
translation_verse: M gbìl̄ kuwoou nee kɔkɔ pu ní m-poon kaam cɔ́tì. M-nyunculiŋ bíi jìkì ní m-kpabiŋ bíi bùkù. M-taaŋi yɔ̄tì maa ti ŋūǹ kí yūĺ. M ŋmíl̀ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ ki cí dinimbinaamandi wiiŋŋu kí cùú já nì anibul ŋin bíi jáà nì tee.

english_verse: Fig trees may no longer bloom, or vineyards produce grapes; olive trees may be fruitless, and harvest time a failure; sheep pens may be empty, and cattle stalls vacant—
translation_verse: Fiigi subu kaa ti púkuḿ, fiinyi subu kaa ti lòoǹ, ɔliifi subu kaa ti lòoǹ, ní tisati mun kaa ti lòoǹ tikpaajin. Ipii kaa ti bí kupikpuŋkpuŋun, ní inaa mun kaa ti bí kunaabakaun.

english_verse: but I will still celebrate because the Lord God is my Savior.
translation_verse: Ama mamee, m làá nīn fàal̀ ti-Dindaan pu, m làá nīn bí mmɔnni Unimbɔti un di fīī-mee pu.

english_verse: The Lord gives me strength. He makes my feet as sure as those of a deer, and he helps me stand on the mountains. To the music director: Use stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sá m-pɔŋŋu. U yàntī m tóotí kii upeemanee, ní ki yàntī m tɔ́kɔ́ yilpu ki còom̄. Bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee. Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu ní ki gà-ŋu.

english_verse: I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah. When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message. Judgment on Judah
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Seefaniya ŋyunti ŋun Amɔn jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi nìn sá ubɔti Juuda tiŋkinee sɔ̀. Seefaniya gbanti nìn sá Kuusi naakookun, Geedaliya jipɔɔn, ki sá Amariya naantiiu, ní ki sá Eeseekiyaasi naantitɔntɔkɔl. Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab tafadaaldi

english_verse: I, the Lord, now promise to destroy everything on this earth—
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá kúntí tin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee.

english_verse: people and animals, birds and fish. Everyone who is evil will crash to the ground, and I will wipe out the entire human race.
translation_verse: M làá kúntí binib nì tiwaŋkuti, nì inoon in bí kutaa puee nì ijɔm in bí dimɔɔlinee. M làá kúntí bitɔŋfitiibi nì tin yàntī bi tūǹ atuŋkpitee. M làá kúntí binib kɔkɔ kitiŋ pu. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Unimbɔti làá jáǹ Juuda nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki

english_verse: I will reach out to punish Judah and Jerusalem— nothing will remain of the god Baal; nothing will be remembered of his pagan priests.
translation_verse: M làá já nì Jeerusaleem nì Juuda yab kɔkɔ. M làá kúntí awaatuun ŋin kíǹee mpaan nee pu, ní kí kúntí awaa tɔntɔnliibi nì ŋi-tandambi.

english_verse: Not a trace will be found of those who worship stars from their rooftops, or bow down to the god Milcom, while claiming loyalty to me, the Lord.
translation_verse: M làá kúntí bin tɔ̄kɔntí adibɔ̀bikaa yilpu ki jáaḿ iŋmalbijaayee. M làá kúntí bin gbàantí man bi-Dindaan nimbiin, ní ki gíti pùtī diwaal Mooleeki yindee.

english_verse: Nothing will remain of anyone who has turned away and rejected me.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan, m làá kúntí bin fàtī bi-boon ki tìì-mi kaa nyàab̀-mi ní kaa bàlifī-mi isaŋkee.»

english_verse: Be silent! I am the Lord God, and the time is near. I am preparing to sacrifice my people and to invite my guests.
translation_verse: Ní ŋmīĺmaan díkí diki ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nimbiin, di sá yii u-ŋuul wiiŋŋu tóobiń. Ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì saraa, kí ŋá bin u yíińee circir.

english_verse: On that day I will punish national leaders and sons of the king, along with all who follow foreign customs.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M-saraau wiiŋŋu gbanti dalee, m làá dāá já nì bikàliŋkpilib nì abɔtibil, nì bin di pèentí tiwan kii binicambee.

english_verse: I will punish worshipers of pagan gods and cruel palace officials who abuse their power.
translation_verse: Yaadal wiiŋŋuee m làá dāá dáaĺ bin di yùkufī ki lákatí kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔkee tafal. M làá dāá dáaĺ bin kɔkɔ fìkì binib ki mùul̄-bi ki fòol̄ tiwan ki gbēentí bi-waadiikuee.

english_verse: I, the Lord, promise that on that day noisy crying will be heard from Fish Gate, New Town, and Upper Hills.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii, ŋwiin gbantee, Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, bi dāa gbìl̀ ibiil Ijɔm punyɔkɔ watil, ní ikuŋkuunti tùm̀ kitimpɔŋ watil, ní kuwookpaaŋŋu gà ŋgbantamu pu.

english_verse: Everyone in Lower Hollow will mourn loudly, because merchants and money changers will be wiped out.
translation_verse: Makteesi yab, nín̄ kūuntímaan! Di sá yii binyampoobi kɔkɔ làá kpú, bin ŋmàntī animbilee làá kúntí.

english_verse: Their possessions will be taken, their homes left in ruins. They won't get to live in the houses they build, or drink wine from the grapes in their own vineyards. A Terrible Day
translation_verse: Too, bi làá dāá fūkul̀ bi-gaajawanti ní kí kpēelikì bi-diiŋŋi. Bi māā adiin, ama baa làá kɔ́-ŋi. Bi kù fiinyi sufii kpaaŋŋi, ama baa làá ká i-daam kí nyɔ̀.» Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dal

english_verse: The great day of the Lord is coming soon, very soon. On that terrible day, fearsome shouts of warriors will be heard everywhere.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan wiŋkpaaŋŋu tóobiń, ŋu tóobiń, ŋu dòoń malaa malaa. Ŋwiin gbantee, binib làá dāá gbá ibiil nì dinimbinaamandi. Bibaatandambi gba làá dāá gbá ibiil ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi.

english_verse: It will be a time of anger— of trouble and torment, of disaster and destruction, of darkness and despair, of storm clouds and shadows,
translation_verse: An dāa sá diŋuul wiiŋŋu ní, dinimbinaamandi nì kufaaŋŋu wiiŋŋu, asaluu nì ŋkúm wiiŋŋu, kunyeeu nì dibɔmbɔndi wiiŋŋu, atagbambɔn nì dipɔ̀ńdi wiiŋŋu ní an dāa sá.

english_verse: The Lord warns everyone who has sinned against him, “I'll strike you blind! Then your blood and your insides will gush out like vomit.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá dāá kɔ́ǹ binib dinimbinaamandin, ní bí nīn còom̄ kii bijɔfubee, kun puee bi yīntiǹ man bi-Dindaan. Bi-fatikuu làá dāá kpáatí kí fá kitiŋ kii dibulee, ní bí cáá bi-wunti kí fá kii titampummoolee.»

english_verse: Not even your silver or gold can save you on that day when I, the Lord, am angry. My anger will flare up like a furious fire scorching the earth and everyone on it.”
translation_verse: Bi-nimbiliŋ nì bi-sindaariyab kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí fīī-bi. Ti-Dindaan ŋuul dalee, u-ŋuukpaandi ŋmiŋu dalee, kitiŋ kɔkɔ làá dāá wà kí céetí. Tiŋman, u làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí binib kɔkɔ kitiŋ pu.

english_verse: before it's too late. The Lord has set a time when his fierce anger will strike like a storm and sweep you away.
translation_verse: kí wàatī ní ní nín kpántí kii timool tin kubuŋu yòontí ki féeń ŋwimbaantee. Ti-Dindaan bum làá dāá jēetí ni-pu. Ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi wiiŋŋu làá dāá jēetí ni-pu.

english_verse: If you humbly obey the Lord, then come and worship him. If you do right and are humble, perhaps you will be safe on that day when the Lord turns loose his anger. Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ nee pu ki sīntiǹ ni-ba taapu, ki tɔ́ ti-Dindaan marabee, nyàab̀maan ti-Dindaan. Nín̄ ŋáaḿmaan tin bí deedeeyee, kí sìntīmaan ni-ba taapu Unimbɔti nimbiin. An yaa yíì u-ŋuul wiiŋŋu dalee, u làá dāá fīī-ni. Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú nibuliŋ pu

english_verse: Gaza and Ashkelon will be deserted and left in ruins. Ashdod will be emptied in broad daylight, and Ekron uprooted.
translation_verse: Binib làá dāá yīkì kí fá Gaasaa tiŋki, ní bí nàan̄ Asikeelɔn tiŋki. Bi làá dāá jà Asidoodi yab kuwiŋkaŋu pu, ní kí kpìtī Eekrɔn tiŋki.

english_verse: To you people of Philistia who live along the coast, the Lord has this to say: “I am now your enemy, and I'll wipe you out!”
translation_verse: Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí nimbi Kafitoor yab bin kóò ditiŋkugbandee. Kaana, Fiiliistii yab tiŋki, ti-Dindaan bɔsooŋyi dàn̄ a-pu. M làá kúntí-si, di sá yii binib kaa ti kóò a-pu.

english_verse: Your seacoast will be changed into pastureland and sheep pens.
translation_verse: Tiŋku kpaanceetii dāa kpántí kunaakpaapɔɔu, laakin bipikpaaliibi kpàá tiwaŋkutee, nì laakin bi làá mā ipii naabakatee.

english_verse: The Lord God hasn't forgotten those survivors in Judah, and he will help them— his people will take your land to use for pasture. And when evening comes, they will rest in houses at Ashkelon. Judgment on Moab and Ammon *
translation_verse: Juuda yab bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee làá dāá jī ditinjandi gbanti. Niin ní bi làá dāá nīn kpàá bi-waŋkuti, ní kujoouee, bí cùú kɔ́ Asikeelɔn yab timmun kí dòon̄. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá sɔ̄ bi-saai, ní kí cúú tin poon bi bée kí kpántí. Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nibuliŋ pu

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I've heard Moab and Ammon insult my people and threaten their nation.
translation_verse: «M gbìl̄ Moowaab yab siibiliŋ nì Amɔn yab beelii pu. Bi sīī m-nibul ní ki fōō di-timmu ki kútì bi-yɔmu pu.

english_verse: And so, I swear by my very life that Moab and Ammon will end up like Sodom and Gomorrah— covered with thornbushes and salt pits forever. Then my people who survive will take their land.
translation_verse: An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu pūtì ki lī yii: <Moowaab tiŋki làá dāá kpántí kii Soodoom tiŋkee, ní Amɔn yab tiŋki mun ń kpántí kii Goomoora tiŋkee. Bi-tiŋki làá dāá kpántí ikuŋkum nì diyataŋkpal kí nīn cá jaanjaan. M-nibul yab bin làá dāá kíńee làá dāá fūkul̀-kì, m-timbundi yab bin kíǹee làá dāá fōō-kì.>»

english_verse: This is how Moab and Ammon will at last be repaid for their pride— and for sneering at the nation that belongs to me, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Bi-bayoondi puee, tipaal tin bi làá dāá fōōyee sèé. Di sá yii bi sīī ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nibul ní ki fōō di-timmu ki kútì bi-yɔmu pu.

english_verse: I will fiercely attack. Then every god on this earth will shrink to nothing, and everyone of every nation will bow down to me, right where they are. Judgment on Ethiopia
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan kaa làá dāá tàan̄-bi, u làá dāá kúntí awaa kɔkɔ kitiŋ pu. Atimbun ŋin bíń ndandatee làá dāá gbàan̄ u-nimbiin laakin ŋi bée. Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú nibuliŋ pu

english_verse: People of Ethiopia, the sword of the Lord will slaughter you! Judgment on Assyria
translation_verse: «Nimbi Eetiiyoopii yab mun, m làá dāá yàntī ní kpúń kujaaun ní.»

english_verse: The Lord will reach to the north to crush Assyria and overthrow Nineveh.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dāá já nì ŋgan pú tiŋki ní kí dāá nàan̄ Asuur tiŋki. Niiniifi tiŋki làá dāá kpántí ataŋkpakpuku, kitiŋkuliŋŋi kii kuteeuee.

english_verse: Herds of wild animals will live in its rubble; all kinds of desert owls will perch on its stones and hoot in the windows. Noisy ravens will be heard inside its buildings, stripped bare of cedar.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kansikin nì kansikin ní tiwaŋkuti dāa dɔ̀. Tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ nì ti-buluku, atulinjoo nì nlabinsamu dāa dɔ̀ jaantalkub yilpu ní. Bi dāa gbìl̀ adiin tɔkɔlab pu nnɔmbiyaamu siim pu. A tin pée lì yii a kóò kitiŋinee, tin a làá dāá kée di sá adigbun nì idɔ.

english_verse: This is the glorious city that felt secure and said, “I am the only one!” Now it's merely ruins, a home for wild animals. Every passerby simply sneers and makes vulgar signs.
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan kitiŋ kin nìn bí dipɔɔsɔŋkilin ki máká ki-ba pu ki lì yii: «Man di bí, m-boonee ubɔ gíti kpée.» Too, Niiniifi kpántì ataŋkpakpuku ŋma ní, tiwaŋkuti kɔŋkooŋŋu. Bin kɔkɔ jītí ki-caŋinee búǹ ifoon ki dɔ̀tī-kì dinyuncul.

english_verse: Too bad for that disgusting, corrupt, and lawless city!
translation_verse: Mbusu kɔ́ pɔɔgaati tiŋki, kitiŋ kin kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi ki wɔ́b́ binibee.

english_verse: Forever rebellious and rejecting correction, Jerusalem refuses to trust or obey the Lord God.
translation_verse: Kàa pílifì ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔ, kaa fōō u-saŋkii, kaa dū ki-mákal ki páaǹ ki-Dindaan pu, kaa sútì ki pìl̄ ki-Nimbɔtiu.

english_verse: Its officials are roaring lions, its judges are wolves; in the evening they attack, by morning nothing is left.
translation_verse: Ki-yidambi bí kii gbikintib bin sūǹee ní. Ki-bɔsoonliibi bí kii agbiŋgbil ŋin cá kukpɔŋu kujoou, ama ní kutaa nì ku-wuntilee, ŋaa ti cáá tiba kí ŋmɔ́ee ní.

english_verse: Jerusalem's prophets are proud and not to be trusted. The priests have disgraced the place of worship and abused God's Law.
translation_verse: Ki-bɔnaatiliibi kaa bí tiban, bi sá binib bin kíiĺ bi-jutiibee. Ki-saraaŋaliibi kɔ́ǹ tin bí circiree tijɔkɔndi, ní kaa fātìi tɔ́ mara.

english_verse: All who do evil are shameless, but the Lord does right and is always fair. With the dawn of each day, God brings about justice.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ti-Dindaan bí kitiŋin, waa ŋáań tin kaa bí deedeeyee. Kutaafaau kamaayee, u sòoǹ tibɔti, ntaafaabɔmbɔmee, u ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, binikpitib pée gbíntìi tūǹ atuŋkpiti kaa cáá icoo.

english_verse: The Lord wiped out nations and left fortresses crumbling in the dirt. Their streets and towns were reduced to ruins and emptied of people.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M kúntì atimbun ki wīī ŋi-guŋkpaaŋŋi ki yāntì ŋi-saŋyi kūń ubɔ kaa ti dì. M bíil̀ ŋi-tiŋki, uniseen kaa ti kóò ki-ni.

english_verse: God felt certain that Jerusalem would learn to respect and obey him. Then he would hold back from punishing the city and not wipe it out. But everyone there was eager to start sinning again. Nations Will Turn to the Lord
translation_verse: M lī m-ban yii: <Kɔŋkɔnnee kitiŋ nee nib làá nīn tɔ́-mi, bi làá fōō m-bɔkpaafikaati. Maa làá ti ŋá kii m nín bí yii m làá ŋá-kì puee, kaa làá ti kúntí-kì.> Ama ní ki-nib yáb́ ki túń atuŋkpiti.

english_verse: The Lord said: Just wait for the day when I accuse you nations. I have decided on a day, when I will bring together every nation and kingdom and punish them all in my fiery anger. I will become furious and destroy the earth.
translation_verse: An puee ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Ní cīitímaan-mi! Ní cīití ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāan̄ kí kɔ̄kɔl̀-nee. Di sá yii m lēē ki síiǹ yii m làá kóoǹ anibul nì abee kí kpāfì ní kí kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī ŋi-pu. M-ŋuul ŋmiŋuee làá wà kí céetí kitiŋ kɔkɔ.» Unimbɔti kpántì u-nibul bimbim

english_verse: I will purify each language and make those languages acceptable for praising me. Then, with hearts united, everyone will serve only me, the Lord.
