translation_verse: «Tiŋman, m làá ŋá m-nibul nyunculiŋ circir, ní bí ŋmā kí nīn yíì man bi-Dindaan yindi, ní kí kpāfì ubaanti kí nīn tūǹ m-tundi.

english_verse: From across the rivers of Ethiopia, my scattered people, my true worshipers, will bring offerings to me.
translation_verse: Bin jáaḿ-mi ki yàl̄ ki bíń Eetiiyoopii mɔɔgbandee làá dāá cáań-mi saraabi.» Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee

english_verse: When that time comes, you won't rebel against me and be put to shame. I'll do away with those who are proud and arrogant. Never will any of them strut around on my holy mountain.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin gbantee, m-nibul, icoo kaa làá ti cúú-si atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ a ŋá-mee pu. Di sá yii ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá nyāntí ni-kansikin timɔn dambi nì bin yòontí bi-ba yilpuee. Niinee, a làá dāá gbèen̄ kí taa ti yòon̄ a-ba yilpu m-circir jool pu.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, won't destroy any of your people who are truly humble and turn to me for safety.
translation_verse: M làá dāá kíń binib bin sīntiǹ bi-ba taapuee nì bisoodambi a-ni. Bi làá dāá nyàab̀ ḿ wúń bi-pu.

english_verse: The people of Israel who survive will live right and refuse to tell lies. They will eat and rest with nothing to fear. A Song of Celebration
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab bin làá dāá kíńee kaa ti làá dāá ŋá ikpiti, kaa ti làá dāá mɔ̄ntì inyimɔn, kaa ti làá dāá kīil̀ bi-jutiibi. Bi làá dāá kpàà bi-waŋkuti nì ŋgbansɔŋfi kí ŋùŋfì ní ubɔ dāa kpá kí fàaǹ-bi.» Bi làá fàtīí mā Jeerusaleem tiŋki

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem and Judah, celebrate and shout with all your heart!
translation_verse: Siiyɔn tiŋki, nín̄ kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi, Isirayeel yab, nín̄ fàal̀maan. Jeerusaleem, nín̄ fàal̀ nì a-pɔbil kɔkɔ!

english_verse: Zion, your punishment is over. The Lord has forced your enemies to turn and retreat. Your Lord is King of Israel and stands at your side; you don't have to worry about any more troubles.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan kākatì ditafadaaldi din bàà dàn̄ a-puee ki wāatì-si, u kākatì a-nannanliibi ki wāatì-si. Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel bɔtiu bí a-cee. Aa ti máaǹ kí fàŋkì mbusu ubɔ.

english_verse: Jerusalem, the time is coming, when it will be said to you: “Don't be discouraged or grow weak from fear!
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, bi làá dāá tùkù Jeerusaleem yii: «Siiyɔn tiŋki, taa fàŋkì, a-wunti ń taa yɔ̀tī.

english_verse: The Lord your God wins victory after victory and is always with you. He celebrates and sings because of you, and he will refresh your life with his love.” The Lord's Promise to His People
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu bí a-cee, úǹ di sá ubaatandaan un tìì-si dijajilee. A-pu ní u bí dipɔɔpindin, ní u-neendi tìì-si dimaŋfapɔndi, u fàal̀ ní ki bí dipɔɔpindin a-pu,

english_verse: The Lord has promised: Your sorrow has ended, and you can celebrate.
translation_verse: kii jiŋaal wiiŋŋuee.» Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Jeerusaleem, m làá dāá kàkatī nnaabu kí wàatī-si, án nín làá ŋá pu icoo ń taa ti cúú-see.

english_verse: I will punish those who mistreat you. I will bring together the lame and the outcasts, then they will be praised, instead of despised, in every country on earth.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá dáaĺ bin kɔkɔ sāaǹ-nee tafal. M làá dāá fīī apibil ŋin dúlifée, kí kóoǹ ŋin wáŋkèe kí kpāfì. M làá dāá tīī-ni tinyool ní ni-yindi ń gbìtī ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-ni icooyee.

english_verse: I will lead you home, and with your own eyes you will see me bless you with all you once owned. Then you will be famous everywhere on this earth. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá gíiǹní-ni. Án dāa sá ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfèe. M làá dāá tīī-ni tinyool ní ni-yindi ń dāá gbìtī ilaan kɔkɔ anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee kansikin. Di sá yii ni-nimbilaaliyin ní m làá dāá gíiǹní-ni diŋuŋfilin.» Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: On the first day of the sixth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak his message to the governor of Judah and to the high priest. So Haggai told Governor Zerubbabel and High Priest Joshua
translation_verse: Daariyusi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin ali iŋmal iluu wimpeepeekaaŋu dalee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Agaayi. U nìn bí ú tùkù Seeyaltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel un sá Juuda yab gɔminauee, nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa un sá usaraaŋakpilee yii:

english_verse: You harvest less than you plant, you never have enough to eat or drink, your clothes don't keep you warm, and your wages are stored in bags full of holes.
translation_verse: Ni búĺ tikpil ama ní ki cáń fiii, ni jīǹ ama ní kaa díkì, ni nyù ndaam ama ní an kaa nyàatī-ni, ni pèentí abɔkuti ama ní tiwool gbíntìi cáá-ni, ní utɔntɔnli ń fōō tipaal ní án kɔ́ kuloou kun cíl̀ee poon.

english_verse: But first, go to the hills and get wood for my temple, so I can take pride in it and be worshiped there.
translation_verse: Jɔ̄m̀maan dijool pu kí cáań idɔ kí fàtīí mā m-Diiku. Án làá mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-mi ní ḿ nyāntí m-nyooti kí dàkà, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: You expected much, but received only a little. And when you brought it home, I made that little disappear. Why have I done this? It's because you hurry off to build your own houses, while my temple is still in ruins.
translation_verse: Ni bàà cɔ́tí kí cā tikpil ní ki dūu cáń fiii. M tɔ́ tin ni yōoǹ ki cáań mmɔŋkee pu kubuŋu. Ba pu ní m ŋá míǹ? Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di bālifì míǹ. Di sá yii m-diiku lítì ki kpántì kudigbuŋu, ama ní báà ŋma nimbiliŋ máǹ u-diiku pu.

english_verse: That's also why the dew doesn't fall and your harvest fails.
translation_verse: An pu ní utaa kaa jōō, ní kitiŋ mun kaa lòon̄ báà tiba.

english_verse: And so, at my command everything will become barren—your farmland and pastures, your vineyards and olive trees, your animals and you yourselves. All your hard work will be for nothing.
translation_verse: An pu ní m cáań ŋweel ki tɔ́ kitiŋ nee nì ajoon nì fiinyi nì ɔliifi sufii sati pu, nì tin kɔkɔ kitiŋ pée lòoǹee pu. M cáań ki tɔ́ binib nì ipeel pu, nì tin kɔkɔ ni kùn̄ee pu.»

english_verse: Zerubbabel and Joshua, together with the others who had returned from exile in Babylonia, obeyed the Lord's message spoken by his prophet Haggai, and they started showing proper respect for the Lord.
translation_verse: Ní Seeyaltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa un sá usaraaŋakpilee, nì samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee pílifì tibɔti tin bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu dī u-bɔnaatiliu Agaayi pu ki sòon̄ nì bee. Min Agaayi túń ditundi din ti-Dindaan dūu ŋúbíǹ-uee dee, ní tifaandi kɔ́ samaa kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nimbiin.

english_verse: Haggai then told them that the Lord had promised to be with them.
translation_verse: Ní Agaayi, ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu dū tibɔti tin u fōōyee ki nāatì samaa yii: «M bí ni-cee, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: And the work began on the twenty-fourth day of that same month.
translation_verse: An nìn sá dibindi gbanti dibaantiil poon uŋmaluluuti, iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dal ní.

english_verse: On the twenty-first day of the next month, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak this message to Governor Zerubbabel, High Priest Joshua, and everyone else:
translation_verse: U nìn bí ú tùkù Seeyaltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel, Juuda yab gɔminau nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa usaraaŋakpil, nì samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee yii:

english_verse: Does anyone remember how glorious this temple used to be? Now it looks like nothing.
translation_verse: «Ubɔ bí ni-kansikin ki nìn ká kunimbɔtidii kukpikuuee nyaaŋkuɔɔɔ? Ni wāĺ kupɔŋu nee kúǹ mana? Naa ká yii kúǹ kaa bí tibanaaa?

english_verse: But cheer up! Because I, the Lord All-Powerful, will be here to help you with the work,
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee, Sooroobabeel, ká kunyannyaau! Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Yoosuwa usaraaŋakpil, ká kunyannyaau. Nimbi kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ nib, kámaan kunyannyaau. Kíĺmaan ditundi, man bí ni-cee. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: just as I promised your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt. Don't worry. My Spirit is right here with you.
translation_verse: M nín nìn nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee, m nìn lēē kí ŋá míǹ kí tīī-ni. M-Fam làá nīn bí ni-kansikin, ní taa fàŋkì tiba.

english_verse: Soon I will again shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Án kaa làá ti yúntí m làá cìŋkì yilpu nì taapu nì tiŋku nì kitiŋ.

english_verse: I will shake the nations, and their treasures will be brought here. Then the brightness of my glory will fill this temple.
translation_verse: M làá cìŋkì atimbun kɔkɔ ní ŋi-gaajati ń kpìntīí dāan̄ doo. M làá yàntī tinyool ń gbí kudii nee. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: All silver and gold belong to me,
translation_verse: Di sá yii, man di yì sindaariya, man di tí yì animbil.

english_verse: and I promise that this new temple will be more glorious than the first one. I will also bless this city with peace. The Past and the Future
translation_verse: Míǹ puee kunimbɔtidii kun ni fātìi máń nee nyooti làá nīn jítiǹ kukpikuu. Man ni-Dindaan di lī yii niinee, m làá tīī-ni ŋgbansɔŋfi. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.» Dinibul bí tijɔkɔndin

english_verse: to ask the priests for their opinion on the following matters:
translation_verse: U bí-u yii ú bàlifì bisaraaŋaliibi tibɔti nee taapu:

english_verse: Suppose meat ready to be sacrificed to God is being carried in the folds of someone's clothing, and the clothing rubs against some bread or stew or wine or olive oil or any other food. Would those foods that were touched then become acceptable for sacrifice? “Of course not,” the priests answered.
translation_verse: «Tí lì yii ubɔ dū saraa nanti ki ŋá dibɔkutil lookun. Boonee, dibɔkutilee gbēē kpɔnɔ àá tikuŋfaal àá ndamam àá ŋkpam àá tijin tin kamaa an yaa pée sée. Mimmee tijin gbanti làá kpántí circir jintaaa?» Ní bisaraaŋaliibi kíí-u yii: «Aayee».

english_verse: Then Haggai said, “Suppose someone has touched a dead body and is considered unacceptable to worship God. If that person touches these foods, would they become unclean?” “Of course they would,” the priests answered.
translation_verse: Ní Agaayi gíti bālifì yii: «Ubɔ yaa gbēē dinikpil ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ní ki gbēē tiwan gbanti kɔkɔee, tì làá kpántí tijɔkɔŋwanaaa?» Ní bisaraaŋaliibi kíí-u yii: «Iiin, tì làá kpántí tijɔkɔŋwan.»

english_verse: So the Lord told Haggai to say: That's how it is with this entire nation. Everything you do and every sacrifice you offer is unacceptable to me.
translation_verse: Ní Agaayi fātìi bí-bi yii: «Too, ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Míǹ ní kitiŋ nee nib nì atuun ŋin bi tūǹee bí. Míǹ ní tin kɔkɔ bi cāabìń ki ŋáań-mi saraayee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi>». Ŋyunti nee ní an sá tí dàkafì

english_verse: But from now on, things will get better. Before you started laying the foundation for the temple,
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti bí yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní dàkafì kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, tin làá jītée. Kí wàatī ní kíĺ kí dū ataŋkpee kí tɔ́kɔń tɔb pu kí mā man ni-Dindaan diikuee,

english_verse: That same day the Lord spoke to Haggai again and said:
translation_verse: Iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dal gbanti mbaantee, ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ nì Agaayi nliliitiim.

english_verse: I made all of your hard work useless by sending mildew, mold, and hail—but you still did not return to me, your Lord.
translation_verse: M kɔ́ǹ-ni agìń ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon. M yāntì ni-kpaajinti tiba kūń, tiba bùkū ní ataanyiŋkumbil lítì ki bíil̀ tiba, ama naa fātìi gítìń m-cee. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Today you have completed the foundation for my temple, so listen to what your future will be like.
translation_verse: Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, ní dáań tin làá jītée kí yóoń. Díǹ wiiŋŋu ŋun ni bíl̀ man ni-Dindaan diiku nyeel nee sá uŋmawawati iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa ní. Ní cúú kí yóoń!

english_verse: Although you have not yet harvested any grain, grapes, figs, pomegranates, or olives, I will richly bless you in the days ahead. God's Promise to Zerubbabel
translation_verse: Kéè tijimpin kaa kíǹ cakalaabinaa! Ki kpáaǹ isufi in bi yíì fiinyi nì fiigi nì greenaadi nì ɔliifee kaa lòon̄aa! Ama kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, m làá bìin̄ ni-pu.» Ti-Dindaan pōoǹ Sooroobabeel dipoondi

english_verse: Tell Governor Zerubbabel of Judah that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth
translation_verse: U nìn bí ú tùkù Sooroobabeel, Juuda yab gɔminau yii: «M làá cìŋkì kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ.

english_verse: and wipe out kings and their kingdoms. I will overturn war chariots, and then cavalry troops will start slaughtering each other.
translation_verse: M làá lábití bibɔtiibi beejaliŋ kí cìb̄, ní kí kúntí atimbun beeŋi pɔŋyi. M làá lábití janjatɔrɔkub nì bin kā bi-puee kí cìb̄. Bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ itaamu ní bitanjakaliibi ń kpɔ̀ tɔb.

english_verse: I am the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo. In the eighth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told me to say:
translation_verse: Daariyusi nín jíń dibeel dibinliliitiil ŋmaniniitiu poonee, ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Sakari, Baraaki jipɔɔn, Didoo naantiiu.

english_verse: Israel, I, the Lord All-Powerful, was very angry with your ancestors. But if you people will return to me, I will turn and help you.
translation_verse: Á tùkù Isirayeel yab yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé yii: «Fàtīí gítiḿmaan man cee, ní ma mun ń fàtīí gítiń ni-cee. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. They were warned by the earlier prophets to give up their evil and turn back to me, but they paid no attention.
translation_verse: Ní taa fōōmaan ni-baabi bimbim. Ŋyunti ŋun nìn jítèe, m-bɔnaatiliibi nìn dū m-nyɔɔbundi ki sòon̄ nì bi yii: <Fámaan ni-saŋkpitii nì ni-bimbikpitim>, ama baa nìn pílifiǹ-mi kaa fātìi tɔ́ mun. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Where are your ancestors now? Not even prophets live forever.
translation_verse: Ni-baabi gbanti bí la? M-bɔnaatiliibi gbíntìi báaa?

english_verse: But my warnings and my words spoken by the prophets caught up with your ancestors. So they turned back to me and said, “Lord All-Powerful, you have punished us for our sins, just as you had planned.” First Vision: Horses and Riders
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin m nìn dūu tùkū m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibee nìn gbēē ni-baabi pɔbiliŋ. An di nìn yāntì bi kpántì bi-bimbim ki lī yii: <Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín nìn lī yii ti-saŋkpitii nì ti-tuŋkpitiŋ pu u làá ŋá-ti miŋyee, míǹ ní u ŋá nee.>» Dileedakal dipeekaal: itaamu

english_verse: On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, which was the eleventh month of that same year, the Lord spoke to me in a vision during the night: In a valley among myrtle trees, I saw someone on a red horse, with riders on red, brown, and white horses behind him.
translation_verse: An lēē ki dàkā-mi kunyeeu gbanti. M ká utanjakal ubɔ kā utaamu un máǹ wèeeeyee pu. U nìn yú nsutantamu mun bi yíì miirtee taapu ditantakal diban. Itaamu in máń wèeeeyee nì in máǹ gàaayee nì itampiin iba mun yú u-boon.

english_verse: An angel was there to explain things to me, and I asked, “Sir, who are these riders?” “I'll tell you,” the angel answered.
translation_verse: Ní m bālifì-u yii: «M-Dindaan, itaamu nee taapu là kí lì yii ba dee?» Ní ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee bí-mi yii: «M làá tùkù-si i-taapu nín sá puee.»

english_verse: At once, the man standing among the myrtle trees said, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to find out what's happening on earth.”
translation_verse: Ní uninja un yú nsutantamu mun bi yíì miirtee kansikinee kíí yii: «An sá bin ti-Dindaan tú bí yìiǹ kí màntì kitiŋee.»

english_verse: Then the riders spoke to the Lord's angel, who was standing among the myrtle trees, and they said, “We have gone everywhere and have discovered that the whole world is at peace.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní binibee bí ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu ŋun yú nsutantamuee kansikinee yii: «Ti yìin̄ ki māntì kitiŋ ki kpēē, ti ká yii kitiŋ kɔkɔ bí ŋgbansɔŋfin, tiba kaa páb́ ki-nib.»

english_verse: So the angel told me to announce: I, the Lord All-Powerful, am very protective of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee bí-mi yii ḿ bāakì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bɔti nee yii: «M cáá dineeŋkpaandi Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì Siiyɔn gbantaŋki pu tikpil.

english_verse: For a while I was angry at the nations, but now I am furious, because they have made things worse for Jerusalem and are not the least bit concerned.
translation_verse: Ama m fōō atimbun ŋin máká ŋi-ba puee pu mbiim tikpil, di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun m nìn fōō m-nibul pu diŋuul fiiiyee, bíǹ dɔ́miń ki púntì ki nāaǹ-dì.

english_verse: And so, I will have pity on Jerusalem. The city will be completely rebuilt, and my temple will stand again.
translation_verse: An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, m lī yii m làá fàtīí gítiń Jeerusaleem kí dàkà m-laŋŋaŋfitiiku. Bi làá fàtīí mā m-diiku niin nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki.»

english_verse: I also promise that my towns will prosper—Jerusalem will once again be my chosen city, and I will comfort the people of Zion. Second Vision: Animal Horns
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní ntuunee bí-mi yii ḿ dū ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nyɔɔbundi nee kí nàatī: «M-timmu làá fàtīí tí kɔ́ digbíl poon. M làá fàtīí sɔ̀ŋkì Siiyɔn gbantaŋki pɔbil, ní kí fàtīí tí lēē Jeerusaleem tiŋki.»

english_verse: This time I saw someone holding a measuring line,
translation_verse: M wáaǹ ki kpēē kutaayee ní ki ká iyin inaa.

english_verse: and I asked, “Where are you going?” “To measure Jerusalem,” was the answer. “To find out how wide and long it is.”
translation_verse: Ní m bālifì ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee yii: «Iyin nee taapu là kí lì yii ba ní?» Ní ŋu kíí-mi yii: «Iyin nee sá atimbun ŋin jìn̄ Juuda nì Isirayeel nì Jeerusaleem yab ki yàl̄ee ní.»

english_verse: and said, “Hurry! Tell that man with the measuring line that Jerusalem won't have any boundaries. It will be too full of people and animals even to have a wall.
translation_verse: Ní m bālifì yii: «Bi dɔ́miń kí ŋá ba ní?» Ní ŋu kíí-mi yii: «Bi dɔ́miń kí kɔ́ǹ atimbun ŋin jìn̄ Juuda yab ki yàl̄ee dinyoondi kí nàan̄-ŋi ní. Bi jìn̄ Juuda yab bi yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu ní ubɔ kaa ŋúń ki yúl̀ bi-nimbiin.» Dileedakal ditataatiil: ŋŋmii ŋun bi cáa ŋmàntēe

english_verse: The Lord himself has promised to be a protective wall of fire surrounding Jerusalem, and he will be its shining glory in the heart of the city.” A Call to Action
translation_verse: M wáaǹ kutaayee ní an lēē ki dàkā-mi. M ká uninja ubɔ u ŋúb́ ŋŋmii ŋun bi cáa ŋmàntēe u-ŋaan.

english_verse: The Lord says to his people, “Run! Escape from the land in the north, where I scattered you to the four winds.
translation_verse: Ní m bālifì-u yii: «A cá la?» Ní u kíí-mi yii: «M cá kí ŋmàntī Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí béé ki-púuŋŋu nì ki-waaŋŋu nín sá puee.»

english_verse: Then the glorious Lord All-Powerful ordered me to say to the nations that had raided and robbed Zion: Zion is as precious to the Lord as are his eyes. Whatever you do to Zion, you do to him.
translation_verse: Ní ŋu bí ŋun túŋkí-ŋuee yii: «Sāǹ kí cùú tùkù unaacimpɔɔn un ŋúb́ ŋŋmii nee yii: <Jeerusaleem tiŋki kaa làá dāá nīn cáá digundi, binib nì tiwaŋkuti wíiŋŋu pu.

english_verse: And so, he will put you in the power of your slaves, and they will raid and rob you. Then you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Man m-ba làá nīn bí bi-cee kí nīn sá kii ŋŋmi gundee kí màntīí tù kitiŋ, ní kí lēē m-nyooti kí dàkà ki-kansikin.>» Bi yíiń bin bíń kunicaŋuee ń fàtīí gítiń

english_verse: City of Zion, sing and celebrate! The Lord has promised to come and live with you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan lī yii: Ēeyi! Nimbi bin m nìn jìn̄ ni yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu, ki bíń ŋgan nì ŋgiil púee, ŋwìiń nyalaŋki nì ŋu-jeetilaŋki púee, sām̀maan kɔŋkɔnnee, nyānnímaan ŋgan pú tiŋkin.

english_verse: Then Judah will be his part of the holy land, and Jerusalem will again be his chosen city.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un túnní-mi ki tīī-mi mpɔnee nín sòon̄ atimbun ŋin fúkúl̀-nee puee sèé: «Un kamaa yaa gbēē-nee gbēē man nimbibul dee.

english_verse: Everyone, be silent! The Lord is present and moving about in his holy place.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, m làá já nì atimbun gbanti yab. M làá yàntī bin bi nìn cúú kuyuŋuee ń fūkul̀-bi. Niinee, ni làá dāá béé yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di túnní-mi.

english_verse: I was given another vision. This time Joshua the high priest was standing in front of the Lord's angel. And there was Satan, standing at Joshua's right side, ready to accuse him.
translation_verse: Boonee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì m wál̀ Joosuwa usaraaŋakpil, u yú ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nimbiin. Sitaan nìn yú Joosuwa ŋaŋgiil pú ki kúŋfí u-boon.

english_verse: But the Lord said, “Satan, you are wrong. Jerusalem is my chosen city, and this man was rescued like a stick from a flaming fire.”
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu bí Sitaan yii: «Ti-Dindaan di làá kpìin̄-si, Sitaan. Tiŋman ti-Dindaan un di lēē Jeerusaleemee di làá kpìin̄-si. Joosuwa kaa sá kii kisanteei kin bi lēeńeeee?»

english_verse: So the angel told some of the people to remove Joshua's filthy clothes. Then he said to Joshua, “This means you are forgiven. Now I will dress you in priestly clothes.”
translation_verse: Ní ntuun bí bin yú ŋu-nimbiinee yii: «Pèetīmaan-u tiwan tin u pēē tì cáá tijɔkɔndee.» Boonee ní ŋu bí Joosuwa yii: «Kpèè, m cúú a-kpitii ki lēē a-pu, m làá dū jiŋaal bɔkutiŋ ní kí pèen̄-si.»

english_verse: I spoke up and said, “Also put a clean priestly turban on his head.” Then they dressed him in priestly clothes and put the turban on him, while the Lord's angel stood there watching.
translation_verse: Ní ŋu bí yii: «Bí dū ŋŋaabu ŋun ŋān̄ dándanee kí fìn̄ u-yil. Ní bi dū ŋŋaabu ŋun ŋān̄ dándanee ki fìn̄ u-yil, ní ki pēeǹ-u abɔkutimɔnti ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee nimbiin niin.»

english_verse: After this, the angel encouraged Joshua by telling him that the Lord All-Powerful had promised:
translation_verse: Boonee ntuunee nín sòon̄ nì Joosuwa puee sɔ̀.

english_verse: If you truly obey me, I will put you in charge of my temple, including the courtyard around it, and you will be allowed to speak at any time with the angels standing beside me.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «A yaa nóó m-saŋŋu, ki ŋúb́ m-marabee, sii di làá nīn kpòotī m-diiku poon tuuŋŋi, ní kí nīn cí m-cindi. M làá dū-si kí kūtì bin bí m-cee doo m-tundinee pu.» Unimbɔti làá fàtīí gíiǹ u-tɔntɔnliu

english_verse: Listen carefully, High Priest Joshua and all of you other priests. You are a sign of things to come, because I am going to bring my servant, the Chosen King.
translation_verse: «Pīlifì Joosuwa, sii un sá usaraaŋakpilee. Ni mun pīlifìmaan, nimbi bin sá u-tɔntɔnjutiibee. Di sá yii ni sá difiil din dòońee daaŋku ní. M làá yàntī m-tɔntɔnliu un bi yíì <Nnaantee> ń dāan̄.

english_verse: Joshua, I have placed in front of you a stone with seven sides. I will engrave something on that stone, and in a single day I will forgive this guilty country.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m dū ditaŋkpal diba ki bíl̀ Joosuwa nimbiin, ditaŋkpabaabil gbanti cáá animbil aluli ní. Man m-ba làá ŋmà di-pu tiŋmaŋmabiti. M làá dāá lēē kitiŋ gbanti kpitii ŋwimbaanti ní. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: Then each of you will live at peace and entertain your friends in your own vineyard and under your own fig trees.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbanti yaa láa bāańee, ni dāa yíì tɔb fiinyi nì fiigi subooŋyi taapu ní ki fàal̀ dibatɔl pu.»

english_verse: The angel who explained the visions woke me from what seemed like sleep.
translation_verse: Ntuun ŋun nìn bí ki sòoǹ nì mee fātìi gítìń ki fīntì-mi kii bi nín fìntī unil ŋgeem pu puee.

english_verse: Then he asked, “What do you see?” “A solid gold lampstand with an oil container above it,” I answered. “On the stand are seven lamps, each with seven flames.
translation_verse: Ní ŋu bālifì-mi yii: «Ba ní a wāĺ ní?» Ní m kíí-ŋu yii: «M wāĺ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati tin sá sindaariya ŋmee ní. Kusɔŋu kun poon bi ŋáań fitilab kpamee tɔ́kɔ́ ti-yilpu. Fitilab biluli tɔ́kɔ́ ti-pu ní fitila kamaa cáá iŋmii iluli.

english_verse: One olive tree is on the right side and another on the left of the oil container.
translation_verse: Ní ɔliifi sufii ili yú ki kɔ́ĺ kusɔŋuee, bubɔ yú ŋŋaŋgiil pú, bun kíǹee yú ŋŋaŋgan pú.»

english_verse: Then he asked, “Don't you know?” “No sir,” I replied.
translation_verse: Ní ŋu kíí-mi yii: «Aa nyí ti-taapuɔɔɔ?» Ní m kíí-ŋu yii «Aayee m-dindaan maa nyí.»

english_verse: Zerubbabel laid the foundation for the temple, and he will complete it. Then everyone will know that you were sent by me, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ní m fātìi bālifì-ŋu nliliitiim yii: «Ɔliifi pammu mun pu sindaariya nai ili túuń ɔliifi kpam dì i-pu ki còol̀ ki kóò fitilabinee taapu sá yii ba?»

english_verse: Then I asked the angel, “What about the olive trees on each side of the lampstand? What do they represent?
translation_verse: Niinee ní ŋu bí-mi yii: «An sá binib bili bin yil pu bi sītì ŋkpam ki dū-bi ki sú kitiŋ kɔkɔ Dindaan, bi bí u-nimbiin ki tūǹ u-tundee ní.» Dipoondi din ti-Dindaan pōoǹ Sooroobabeelee

english_verse: And what is the meaning of the two branches from which golden olive oil flows through the two gold pipes?”
translation_verse: Ntuunee tīī dinyɔɔbundi ḿ dūú nàatī Sooroobabeel yii: «An kaa sá nì mpɔn, kaa tí sá nì dikpabil, ama an sá nì man Fam ní.» Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: When I looked the next time, I saw a flying scroll,
translation_verse: M tí wáaǹ kutaayee ní ki ká kugbɔŋu kubɔ ŋàaǹ kutaa pu.

english_verse: and the angel asked, “What do you see?” “A flying scroll,” I answered. “About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide.”
translation_verse: Ní ntuun bālifì-mi yii: «Ba ní a wāĺ ní?» Ní m kíí yii: «M wāĺ kugbɔŋu kubɔ ŋàaǹ kutaa pu, ku-púuŋŋu sá meetab saalaa, ní ku-waaŋŋu sá meetab biŋmoo.»

english_verse: Then he told me: This scroll puts a curse on everyone in the land who steals or tells lies. The writing on one side tells about the destruction of those who steal, while the writing on the other side tells about the destruction of those who lie.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ŋu bí-mi yii: «An sá mbusu bɔti tin bi làá dūú tɔ̄ kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ puee ní. Bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti jandi diba pu yii bí jà binaayub kɔkɔ kitiŋ nee pu, ní ki ŋmàn̄ dijandi din kíǹee pu yii bí jà bin kɔkɔ pùtī fám fámee mun.»

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful has said, “I am sending this scroll into the house of everyone who is a robber or tells lies in my name, and it will remain there until every piece of wood and stone in that house crumbles.” Seventh Vision: A Woman in a Basket
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan lī yii: «Mama m-ba di tɔ́ń mbusu gbanti. U làá kɔ́ unaayuu kamaa diikun, unil un kamaa pùtī m-yindi fám fámee diikun. Mbusu gbanti làá gbíntí bi-diiŋŋin ní kí wà tikɔkɔ, kí kpáaǹ ŋi-dɔi nì ŋi-taŋkpeeŋi.» Dileedakal diluluútiil: unimpu un sá ikpiti daaŋkuee

english_verse: Now the angel who was there to explain the visions came over and said, “Look up and tell me what you see coming.”
translation_verse: Ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee sútìń ní ki bí-mi yii: «Yáatí kí kpèè kun còom̄ ki dòoń nee.»

english_verse: “I don't know what it is,” was my reply. “It's a big basket,” he said. “And it shows what everyone in the land has in mind.”
translation_verse: Ní m bālifì-ŋu yii: «Ba ní an sá ní?» Ní ŋu kíí yii: «An sá kukabiku kun poon ní kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ kpitii kēe.»

english_verse: The lead cover of the basket was opened, and in the basket was a woman.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, dibìil din sá tikúmanee cúu gántì yilpu ní m ká unimpu ubɔ kā kukabikuee poon.

english_verse: “This woman represents evil,” the angel explained. Then he threw her back into the basket and slammed the heavy cover down tight.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun bí-mi yii: «Unimpu nee sá tikpitil daaŋku ní.» Ní u téé-u ki gíiǹ ki tɔ́ kukabikun, ní ki dū ku-bìil kun sá tikúmanee ki púkuǹ.

english_verse: Right after this I saw two women coming through the sky with wings outstretched like a stork in the wind. Suddenly they lifted the basket into the air,
translation_verse: Míǹ boon m wáaǹ kutaayee ní ki ká binimpoobi bili páaǹní. Bi nìn cáá ifeen an náań nì naakpaapiin feeŋyi, ní kubuŋu téekí-bi bi ŋàaǹ ki cá. Ní bi yōoǹ kukabikuee ki cáa jɔ́ntì kutaa.

english_verse: and I asked the angel, “Where are they taking the basket?”
translation_verse: Ní m bālifì ntuun ŋun bí ki sòoǹ nì mee yii: «Bi cáǹ kukabikuee la?»

english_verse: “To Babylonia,” he answered, “where they will build a house for the basket and set it down inside.”
translation_verse: Ní ŋu kíí-mi yii: «Bi cáǹ-kù Sineeyaar tiŋkin kí tin mā-kù kuwaadii ní. Bi làá mā dikɔl ní kí dū-ku kí báań dikɔlee pu.»

english_verse: Finally, I looked up and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains.
translation_verse: M fātìi tí wáaǹ kutaa puee, ní ki wál̀ janjatɔrɔkub binaa nyánní tikúman jooŋŋi ali kansikin.

english_verse: The first chariot was pulled by red horses, and the second by black horses;
translation_verse: Itaamu in máǹ gàaayee di nìn dátí tɔrɔkupeepeekaa, ní itambɔn dátí tɔrɔkuliliiti,

english_verse: the third chariot was pulled by white horses, and the fourth by spotted gray horses.
translation_verse: ní itampiin dátí tɔrɔkutataati, ní itaamu in cáá atan atan ki ŋmàl̄ mmam gàaayee dátí tɔrɔkunanaati.

english_verse: Then he explained, “These are the four winds of heaven, and now they are going out, after presenting themselves to the Lord of all the earth.
translation_verse: Ní ntuunee kíí-mi yii: «Itaamu nì tɔrɔkub gbanti taapu dàkà kubuŋu kun nyēeń kitiŋ jannaatiliŋee ní. Ku nìn bí kitiŋ kɔkɔ Dindaan cee ní kɔŋkɔnnee ku yíkì u-cee.»

english_verse: The chariot with black horses goes toward the north, the chariot with white horses goes toward the west, and the one with spotted horses goes toward the south.”
translation_verse: Ní tɔrɔku un itambɔn dátée búntì ŋgan pú tiŋki watil, ní tɔrɔku un itampiin dátée búntì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ní tɔrɔku un itaamu in cáá atan atanee dátée búntì ŋgiil pú tiŋki watil.

english_verse: The horses came out eager to patrol the earth, and the angel told them, “Start patrolling the earth.” When they had gone on their way,
translation_verse: Itaamu in máǹ gàaayee nìn nyàab̀ malaa kí cùú yìiǹ kitiŋ pu. Ní ti-Dindaan bí-i yii: «Nín̄ cámaan kí yìiǹ kitiŋ pu.» Ní i búntì ki cūtìi yìin̄ kitiŋ pu.

english_verse: he shouted to me, “Those that have gone to the country in the north will do what the Lord's Spirit wants them to do there.” The Chosen Leader
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan yíiń-mi ki bí yii: «Kpèè, in búntì ŋgan pú tiŋki watilee làá sɔ̀ŋkì m-ŋuul kitiŋ gbanti pu.» Kibeefuulii kin sá kudaaŋŋu bi dūu cíkiǹ Joosuwayee

english_verse: The Lord said to me:
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii:

english_verse: Tell him that I, the Lord All-Powerful, say, “Someone will reach out from here like a branch and build a temple for me. I will name him ‘Branch,’ and he will rule with royal honors. A priest will stand beside his throne, and the two of them will be good friends.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, úǹ di làá dāá fàtīí mā ti-Dindaan diiku. U làá dāá nīn pēē abeebɔkuti. U làá dāá kàl̄ u-beejal pu kí kpòotī u-nibul. Usaraaŋal ubɔ làá dāá nīn yú u-ŋaŋgiil pú, ní bi-liitil ń dāá nīn gbìliǹ tɔb mmɔntiim.

english_verse: This crown will be kept in my temple as a reminder and will be taken care of by Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah.”
translation_verse: «<Kibeefuulii gbanti làá dāá nīn bí kunimbɔtidiin bí nīn cáa téetí Eeldayii nì Toobiya nì Yeedaya nì Seefaniya jipɔɔn ŋanti pu.>»

english_verse: When people from distant lands come and help build the temple of the Lord All-Powerful, you will know that the Lord is the one who sent me. And this will happen, if you truly obey the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Binib làá dāá nyānní ndandati kí fàtīí mā ti-Dindaan diiku. Niin ní ni dāa béetí yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di túnní-mi ni-cee. See ni yaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu mmɔntiimin baba ní án làá ŋá míǹ.

english_verse: On the fourth day of Chislev, the ninth month of the fourth year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord again spoke to me.
translation_verse: Daariyusi nín jíń dibeel dibinnanaatiil uŋmawawati, an dàkà yii uŋmal un bi yíì Kiisileefee iwiin inaa dal ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Sakari tibɔti nee.

english_verse: It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
translation_verse: Binib gbanti nìn máaǹ kí bàlifì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan saraaŋaliibi bin bí kunimbɔtidiinee nì u-bɔnaatiliibi yii: «Tí nīn gbíntìi sūǹ ki bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ uŋmaŋmooŋmooti poon kii ti nín pée kpààa ŋáań abin ŋin jítèe pueeyaaa, tí taa ti ŋá?»

english_verse: It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests: For
translation_verse: ḿ bàlifì kitiŋ nee pu yab kɔkɔ nì bisaraaŋaliibi yii: «Ni nín bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ ki sūǹ ki yáliŋkí uŋmaŋmooŋmooti nì uŋmaluluúti kamaa áli abin imuŋku ita nì saalaayee, ni ŋá míǹ án mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-mi níii?

english_verse: And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment?
translation_verse: Ni yaa nìn tí bíi jīǹ ki nyùee, kaa nìn sá nimbi ni-ba ní ni jīǹ ki tììii?»

english_verse: My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Jeerusaleem yab nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-kèe yab nìn dáá bí nsɔŋfinee, nì ŋyunti ŋun binib nìn dáá kóò Neegeeb teekun nì Seefeelaa paal puee, ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì u-bɔnaatiliibi dooooyee yab báakì ki kpáafì binib tibɔti gbanti.

english_verse: So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another!
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé yii: <Ní sòoǹ ni-juti bɔti nì mbaamɔn, ní báà ŋma ń dàkà u-juti dineendi nì disaasɔl.

english_verse: Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
translation_verse: Ní taa mùul̀ ukpiipu nì ditaŋkpiibil, nì unicaan nì bisoodambi. Ni-kansikin ubɔ ń taa dàkafì u-juti pu nlandɔkɔkpiti.»

english_verse: But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry
translation_verse: Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ kii ditaŋkpalee. Baa nìn là kí pīlifì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bɔti nì u-dakal din u-Fam nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliibi dooooyee yab pu ki tīī-bee. Niinee ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan gíí bi-pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu.

english_verse: and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
translation_verse: An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan lī yii: «Kii man nín yíiń-bi baa pílifiǹ-mee, míǹ mbaantiim ní bi yíiń-mi ní ma mun kaa pílifiǹ-bi.

english_verse: That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
translation_verse: M jìn̄-bi bi yàl̄ ki kɔ́ atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ baa nyée poon. Kitiŋ kin bi yíkìi yāntèe, bi nāaǹ-kì, ní ubɔ kaa ti cá ki-naaa, ubɔ kaa ti nyēē ki-ni. Kitiŋ kin nìn sá kimɔntii ki mɔ̄ ŋkaayee dūu kpántì kuteeu.»

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti nee yii:

english_verse: I love Zion so much that her enemies make me angry.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. M cáá Jeerusaleem pu dineeŋkpaandi, dì jákatí-mi.

english_verse: I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
translation_verse: An pu ní m lī yii, m làá fàtīí gítiń Siiyɔn jool pu, kí nīn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Bi làá dāá nīn yíì Jeerusaleem yii <Deedee tiŋki>, ní kí nīn yíì man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan jool yii <circir Jool>.

english_verse: while boys and girls play in the streets.
translation_verse: Nnaacimpɔmbiyaamu nì nsapɔmbiyaamu dāa gbéè kitiŋin kpacantib pu ní ki gbíiĺ.»

english_verse: This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan lī yii: «Isirayeel yab bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee yaa ká yii an kaa pée ŋūǹ kí bàń mimmee, ma mun máaǹ kí lì yii an pɔ̄ɔ̄ kí ŋá mimmaaa, man un sá ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaaneeee?»

english_verse: I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west,
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di bíi lì yii: «M làá fīī m-nibul kí nyāntí ntimu mun bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee nì mun bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee.

english_verse: and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
translation_verse: M làá gíiǹní-bi bí nīn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Bi làá dāá nīn sá man nibul, ní man ḿ dāá nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu ki ŋúb́-bi ibaamɔn nì deedee poon.»

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé: «Ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn bíl̀ m-diiku nyeelee, m-bɔnaatiliibi nìn pōoǹ-ni ipoon. Too, kámaan kunyannyaau, kun puee ŋyunti nee poonee, ni bíi gbìl̀ ipoon gbanti ibaanti.

english_verse: Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
translation_verse: Dooooyee, binib yaa nìn tūǹ ditundee, baa nìn cáá tipaal, ní tiwaŋkuti nìn tūǹ ditundi faalaa. Binannanliibi puee, binib kaa nìn tɔ́ bi-ba kí nyā kí cù laaba. Di sá yii m nìn yāntì binib nyáń tɔb pu.

english_verse: My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before.
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī yii, maa làá ti ŋá m-nibul din kíǹ kaa kpíìyee kii m nín nìn ŋá dooooyee yab puee.

english_verse: Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky.
translation_verse: Di sá yii bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí bɔ̄l̀ ŋgbansɔŋfin. Fiinyib làá dāá lòoǹ fiinyi biliŋ, ní kitiŋ ń dāá lòoǹ tikpaajin, ní kutagbɔŋu ń dāá tīī ntaanyim. M làá dāá dū tin bí nee kɔkɔ kí tīī m-nibul din kíǹ nee.

english_verse: People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
translation_verse: Nimbi Juuda nì Isirayeel naakɔtin yab, atimbun ŋin kíǹee ceeyee, ni nìn sá kii dinibul din bi tɔ́ mbusuee ní. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, m làá fīī-ni, ní ní kpántí kii dinibul din boon bi bīiǹee. An puee taa fàŋkìmaan! Kámaan kunyannyaau!»

english_verse: When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé: «Ŋyunti ŋun ni-baabi nìn kɔ́ǹ-mi diŋuulee, m nìn lēē yii m làá sàaǹ-ni, ní maa nìn kpántì m-landɔkɔŋu.

english_verse: Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness.
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, m kpántì m-landɔkɔŋu. M lēē kí ŋá Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu tiŋan. Ní taa fàŋkì.

english_verse: But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace.
translation_verse: Kpèèmaan tin ni máaǹ kí ŋée. Báà ŋma ń sòoǹ u-juti ibaamɔn. Ni-bɔsoondiiŋŋinee, ní dū ibaamɔn in làá cáań ŋgbansɔŋfee kí sòoǹ binib bɔti.

english_verse: Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things. A Time of Celebration
translation_verse: Ní taa nín̄ dàkafī tɔb pu tilandɔkɔkpiil, kí taa nín̄ pùtī fám. Di sá yii m ná atuun gbanti kɔkɔ, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.» Dinyɔɔboobil wiiŋyi làá kpántí jiŋaal wiiŋyi

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ nì mee sèé:

english_verse: People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
translation_verse: «Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di bí yii, ni nín bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ uŋmananaati nì uŋmaŋmooŋmooti nì uŋmaluluúti nì uŋmasaalaati poonee làá dāá kpántí nimbi Juuda yab cee dipɔɔpindi nì ifaal nì jiŋaal wiiŋyi ní. «Ama ní nīn néeń ibaamɔn nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.»

english_verse: I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé: «Anibul tikpil nì ntiŋkpaamu yab làá fàtīí tí dāan̄ Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
translation_verse: Kitiŋ kiba yab làá dāá tùkù kin kíǹee yab yii: <Tí cùmaan kí gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, kí nyàab̀-u.> Bíǹ làá dāá kíí-bi yii: <Ti mun làá cù.>

english_verse: Many people from strong nations will come to Jerusalem to worship me and to ask me to treat them with kindness.
translation_verse: Anibul tikpil nì atimbun ŋin cáá mpɔnee làá dāá dāan̄ Jeerusaleem kí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, kí gbàam̀-u.

english_verse: When this happens, ten people from nations with different languages will grab a Jew by his clothes and say, “Let us go with you. We've heard that God is on your side.” I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī puee sɔ̀. Ŋwiin gbantee binib saalaa bin sòoǹ isoon i-ba i-bee làá dāá nīn ŋúb́ ujuudaja bɔkutijuti kí bí-u yii: <Ti làá nóó-si kí cù, kun puee ti gbìl̄ yii Unimbɔti bí ni-cee.>»

english_verse: This is a message from the Lord: His eyes are on everyone, especially the tribes of Israel. So he pronounces judgment against the cities of Hadrach and Damascus.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. Ti-Dindaan bɔti bàn̄ Adiraaki tiŋki, ní ki gbēeǹ Damaasi tiŋkin. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nimbil kaa cɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋki ŋmaniŋma pu, ama ki kpáaǹ binib kɔkɔ pu ní.

english_verse: Judgment will also fall on the nearby city of Hamath, as well as on Tyre and Sidon, whose people are clever.
translation_verse: Dinyɔɔbundee sòoǹ nì Amati yab bin pìlīǹ Damaasee, nì Tiir nì Siidɔn timmu yab bin cáá iciinee.

english_verse: Tyre has built a fortress and piled up silver and gold, as though they were dust or mud from the streets.
translation_verse: Tiir yab máń digundi ki māntìi tú bi-tiŋki. Bi kóoǹ animbil an dɔ̄ ki kpúkú kii dibulee, ní ki kóoǹ sindaariya an dɔ̄ ki kpúkú kii didandi pu kpatee.

english_verse: Now the Lord will punish Tyre with poverty; he will sink its ships and send it up in flames.
translation_verse: Ama ti-Dindaan làá dāá já kí fōō-kì, ní kí téé ki-gundi ki lúkú tiŋkun, ní ŋŋmi ń dāá wà-kì.

english_verse: Both Ashkelon and Gaza will tremble with fear; Ekron will lose all hope. Gaza's king will be killed, and Ashkelon emptied of its people.
translation_verse: Asikeelɔn yab yaa láa ká mimmee, tifaandi làá dāá cúú-bi, ní Gaasaa yab ń dāá nīn jìkì tifaandi, ki kpáaǹ Eekrɔn yab, di sá yii baa ti làá ká un làá jòoń-bee. Gaasaa tiŋki kaa dāa gíti cáá ubɔti, ubɔ kaa dāa gíti kóò Asikeelɔn tiŋkin.

english_verse: A mob of half-breeds will settle in Ashdod, and the Lord himself will rob Philistia of pride.
translation_verse: Nyaaŋmaliŋku nib di làá dāá nìn kóò Asidoodi. Man ni-Dindaan di lī yii: «M làá dāá kúntí Fiiliistii yab lambil.

english_verse: No longer will the Philistines eat meat with blood in it or any unclean food. They will become part of the people of our God from the tribe of Judah. And God will accept the people of Ekron, as he did the Jebusites.
translation_verse: M làá dāá nyāntí tinan tin cáá fatikuee bi-nyɔmmun, kí lēē tiwaatootinan bi-nyiŋŋin. Bi-kansikin bin làá dāá kíń kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee làá dāá yíiń-mi bi-Nimbɔtiu kii Juuda maaliŋun yabee. Eekrɔn yab làá dāá kɔ́ m-nibul kansikin kii Jeebusi yab nín nìn ŋá puee.

english_verse: God says, “I will stand guard to protect my temple from those who come to attack. I know what's happening, and no one will mistreat my people ever again.” The Lord Tells about the Coming King
translation_verse: M làá dāá màntīí tū m-tiŋki kí nīn cí-kì, kí mɔ̄tì ki-pu binannanliibi bin cá ki gítiń ki là kí jáǹ-kèe cee. Upɔndaan ubɔ kaa làá ti dāan̄ kí wɔ́b́ m-nibul, kun puee man m-ba di cí-bi.» Ŋgbansɔŋfi bɔtiu

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem, celebrate and shout! Your king has won a victory, and he is coming to you. He is humble and rides on a donkey; he comes on the colt of a donkey.
translation_verse: Siiyɔn tiŋki, nín̄ fàal̀! Jeerusaleem, nín̄ kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi! Kpèè, a-bɔtiu dòoń a-cee. U sá deedeedaan ní ki sá ujajil. U sīntì u-ba taapu, ní ki kā kimaŋ pu, u kāń dimampɔmbil, kimansalii biki pu.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will take away war chariots and horses from Israel and Jerusalem. Bows that were made for battle will be broken. I will bring peace to nations, and your king will rule from sea to sea. His kingdom will reach from the Euphrates River across the earth. The Lord Promises To Rescue Captives
translation_verse: U làá dāá kúntí janjatɔrɔkub Eefiraayiim tiŋkin ní kí dāá kúntí kujaau taamui Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. U làá dāá kɔ̄fì kujaau tɔfii. U làá dāá cáań ŋgbansɔŋfi atimbun kansikin. U-beel làá dāá kíĺ Ŋyaam mɔɔl kí tin cáá sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu, ní kí yòon̄ Eefiraati mɔɔl kí tin cáá sāā kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ. Ti-Dindaan làá líí bisarkadambi

english_verse: When I made a sacred agreement with you, my people, we sealed it with blood. Now some of you are captives in waterless pits, but I will come to your rescue
translation_verse: Dipoondi din bí man nì ni kansikin ti dū saraabi fatikuu ki bóob́ee puee, m làá nyāntí ni-sarkadambi bin kā dilɔkɔgindi din kaa cáá nnyimee poon kí líí.

english_verse: and offer you hope. Return to your fortress, because today I will reward you with twice what you had.
translation_verse: Bisarkadambi bin cáá dimákalee, fàtīí gítímaan ni-tiŋki kin bi máń digundi ki māntìi túee. Díǹ gba, m tùkù-ni yii: M làá ŋá-ni tiŋan mili pu kí téeǹ falaa un ní ni jíńee pu.

english_verse: I will use Judah as my bow and Israel as my arrow. I will take the people of Zion as my sword and attack the Greeks. The Lord Will Protect His People
translation_verse: Juuda tiŋki ní m làá dūú píĺ kii butɔbuee ní Eefiraayiim tiŋki ń nīn sá ipiin. Siiyɔn, m làá tɔ̄ a-jipɔmbi bí cùú já nì Greesi yab. M làá dū-bi kí kpántí ubaatandaan tàataajiki.

english_verse: Like a cloud, the Lord God will appear over his people, and his arrows will flash like lightning. God will sound his trumpet and attack in a whirlwind from the south.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá nyā kí páanní u-nibul yilpu, ní kí tɔ̄ u-piiŋŋu kii utaa nín ŋmóò puee. Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti làá búń ŋyin, u làá nīn kāń kubuŋu kun nyánní ŋgiil púee kí dāan̄.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful will protect his people, and they will trample down the sharpshooters and their slingshots. They will drink and get rowdy; they will be as full as a bowl at the time of sacrifice.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá dāá wúń u-nib pu. Bi làá dāá wīī kí nà kujaataafuŋ taŋkpeeŋi. Bi làá dāá yàntī bi-nannanliibi fatikuu ń còol̀ kii ndamamee, kii saraabi fatikuu nín còol̀ kisambikin puee, àá kii fatiku un bi cáa yàantí nsaraafan yiŋyi puee.

english_verse: The Lord God will save them on that day, because they are his people, and they will shine on his land like jewels in a crown.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá fīī-bi ŋwiin gbanti dal kii upikpaal nín fìil̄ u-picaŋkpuŋku puee. Bi làá dāá nīn jìl̀ pàlpal bi-tiŋkin kii ataŋkpamɔnti ŋin jìl̀ ki náká kibeefuulii puee.

english_verse: How lovely they will be. Young people will grow there like grain in a field or grapes in a vineyard.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá nīn bí mmɔnneeee! Bi làá dāá nīn cáá kunyaaŋŋu! Bilee làá dāá yàntī binaacimpɔmbi ń yábití, ní ndapɔm ń dāá yàntī bisapɔmbi mun ń yábití.

english_verse: I, the Lord, am the one who sends storm clouds and showers of rain to make fields produce. So when the crops need rain, you should pray to me.
translation_verse: Mèèmaan ti-Dindaan ú yàntī ukpaasiitaa ń nì. Ti-Dindaan di yàntī utaa nì ki yàntī utaa ŋmóò ki tátí nì kubuŋu. U làá yàntī utaaja ń nì, ní báà ŋma saaku ń sɔ̀ŋkì timool ń nyā.

english_verse: You can't believe idols and fortunetellers, or depend on the hope you receive from witchcraft and interpreters of dreams. But you have tried all of these, and now you are like sheep without a shepherd.
translation_verse: Di sá yii awaa sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti ní, ní bibɔɔbi wāĺ tin kaa sá ibaamɔnee. Bi nín lèekī tidamintiil taapu puee sá inyimɔn ní, ní bi ŋmēentí binib fám. An pu ní dinibul nee yíkìi búntì nì falaa kii ipii in kaa cáá ukpaalee. Ti-Dindaan pōoǹ kí fīī u-nibul

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, am fiercely angry with you leaders, and I will punish you. I care for my people, the nation of Judah, and I will change this flock of sheep into charging war horses.
translation_verse: «Bipikpaaliibi pu ní m fōō diŋuul, iŋɔjaa tafal ní m làá dáaĺ. Tiŋman, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan làá dāan̄ kí kpàà m-picaŋkpuŋku, Juuda nibul. M làá dū-bi kí kpántí tinyool taamuu kí cáá-bi kí cùnnì dikɔ̀ndi.

english_verse: From this flock will come leaders who will be strong like cornerstones and tent pegs and weapons of war.
translation_verse: Juuda naakookun ní ditaŋkpal din tíkí kudiiyee, nì tanti kpakpaal nì bujanjatɔbu làá nyānní. Kunaakoou gbantin ní bibɔtiibi kɔkɔ làá nyānní.

english_verse: They will join in the fighting, and together they will trample their enemies like mud. They will fight, because I, the Lord, will be on their side. And they will crush the enemy cavalry.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá nīn bí kii bibaatandambee. Bi làá dāá nīn tà bi-nannanliibi ki múl̀ kii adan pu kpatee. Bi làá dāá nīn jáà míǹ, kun puee man bi-Dindaan bí bi-cee. Icoo làá cúú bi-nannanliibi bitanjakaliibi.

english_verse: I will strengthen the kingdoms of Judah and Israel. And I will show mercy because I am the Lord, their God. I will answer their prayers and bring them home. Then it will seem as though I had never rejected them.
translation_verse: M làá tīī Juuda yab mpɔn, m làá fīī Isirayeel yab. M làá fàtīí gíiǹ-bi bi-tiŋkin, kun puee bi kɔ́-mi falaa. Bi làá dāá nīn bí kii maa pée dū-bi ki fá ki kée. Di sá yii man di sá bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu, ní m làá fōō bi-wimmeem.

english_verse: Israel will be like a tribe of warriors celebrating with wine. When their children see this, they will also be happy because of me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Eefiraayiim yab làá dāá nīn cáá dipɔbil kii bibaatandambee. Bi làá dāá nīn bí dipɔɔpindin kii bi nyùn̄ ndaamee. Bi-jipɔmbi yaa láa ká mimmee, bi làá dāá nīn fàal̀, ní kí nīn bí mmɔŋkpaanni ti-Dindaan pu.

english_verse: I will give a signal for them to come together because I have rescued them. And there will be as many as ever before.
translation_verse: M làá búń ŋfoon kí yíiń m-nibul yab kí kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì, di sá yii m fōō-bi ki líì. Bi làá dāá bùtī kii njaminee.

english_verse: Although I scattered my people in distant countries, they won't forget me. Once their children are raised, they will return—
translation_verse: M yāaǹ-bi atimbun kansikin, kii bi nín yàantí iwambool puee. Ama ndandati timmu gbanti poonee, bi làá téetí m-pu. Bi làá dāá nīn bí niin dimaŋfalin nì bi-biyaamu ní kí fàtīí gítiń.

english_verse: I will bring them home from Egypt and Assyria, then let them settle as far as Gilead and Lebanon, until the land overflows with them.
translation_verse: M làá dāá nyāntiń-bi Eejipiti nì Asuur timmun, ní kí kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì. M làá dāá cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ Galaadi nì Leebanɔn timmun. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, an kaa làá dāá bà-bi.

english_verse: My people will go through an ocean of troubles, but I will overcome the waves and dry up the deepest part of the Nile. Assyria's great pride will be put down, and the power of Egypt will disappear.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá dùtī dinimbinaamandi mɔɔl. Man ni-Dindaan làá dāá fáá dimɔɔl nyiŋgbanti. Niil mɔɔl làá kpā kí tin sāā taapu. Asuur ulambidaan làá lítí, ní Eejipiti kaa ti làá nīn cáá mpɔn.

english_verse: I'll strengthen my people because of who I am, and they will follow me. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: M làá dāá tīī m-nibul yab mpɔn, ní bí nīn ŋáań min man lèe. Man bi-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: Lebanon, open your gates! Let the fire come in to destroy your cedar trees.
translation_verse: Leebanɔn tiŋki, pìitī a-punyɔmmu ŋŋmi ń wà a-seediri sufii.

english_verse: Cry, you cypress trees! The glorious cedars have fallen and are rotting. Cry, you oak trees of Bashan! The dense forest has been chopped down.
translation_verse: Siipreesi subu, nín̄ yáliŋkí, di sá yii seedir sufii lítì, bi nāaǹ isumɔnti gbanti. Baasan seeni sufii, nín̄ yáliŋkímaan, di sá yii bi gāā a-bambaŋku kun nìn múkú ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ee.

english_verse: Listen! Shepherds are crying. Their glorious pastures have been ruined. Listen! Lions are roaring. The forests of the Jordan Valley are no more to be found. Worthless Shepherds
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̀ bipikpaaliibi nín yáliŋkée, di sá yii bi-nyooti kúntì. Bi gbìl̀ gbikinti siim pu, di sá yii bi kpéelikì Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi mɔsɔŋku kɔkɔ. Bipikpaaliibi bili bɔti

english_verse: The Lord my God said to me: Tend those sheep doomed for slaughter!
translation_verse: M-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu tīī-mi mara nee yii: «Kpàà ipii in bi péetí ki cáǹ kí kpɔ̀ nee.

english_verse: The people who buy and butcher them go unpunished, while everyone who sells them says, “Praise the Lord! I'm rich.” Not even their shepherds have pity on them.
translation_verse: Bin dāā ipii gbantee kù-i an kaa ŋáań-bi nyàaa. Bin nyáfí-iee lì yii: <Ti jáam̀ ti-Dindaan, ti kpántì bigaajab!> I-bɔti kaa kpáàa cáá i-kpaaliibi falaa.

english_verse: Tend those sheep because I, the Lord, will no longer have pity on the people of this earth. I'll turn neighbor against neighbor and make them slaves of a king. They will bring disaster on the earth, and I'll do nothing to rescue any of them.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan di lī yii maa làá sɔ̄ kitiŋ nee pu nib saai. M làá gíiǹ unil kamaa kí ŋá u-juti nì u-bɔtiu ŋaan. Bibɔtiibi làá nùkù kitiŋ púb, ní maa làá fōō báà ubɔ bi-ŋaan.»

english_verse: So I became a shepherd of those sheep doomed to be slaughtered by the sheep dealers. And I gave names to the two sticks I used for tending the sheep: One of them was named “Mercy” and the other “Unity.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní m fōō ipii in binyampoobi bàà cáǹ kí kpɔ̀ee ki bíi kpàá. M yōoǹ atambɔn ali ki ŋúb́. M yíiń diba yii: <Disaasɔl>, ní ki yíiń din kíǹee yii <Mpèé>, ní m kíĺ ki bíi kpàá-i.

english_verse: In less than a month, I became impatient with three shepherds who didn't like me, and I got rid of them.
translation_verse: Ní m jìn̄ bipikpaaliibi bitee uŋmabaanti poon. Míǹ boonee ní maa ti cáá kimɔtii ipii pu, ní í mun núutiǹ-mi.

english_verse: Then I said, “I refuse to be your shepherd. Let the sheep that are going to die, go on and die, and those that are going to be destroyed, go on and be destroyed. Then let the others eat one another alive.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bí-i yii: «Maa làá ti kpàà-ni! In làá kpúee ń kpú, in làá wāŋkèe ń wāŋkì, ní in làá kíńee ń nīn tɔ̀ntī tɔb!»

english_verse: On that same day, I broke the stick named “Mercy” to show that the Lord had canceled his agreement with all people.
translation_verse: Ní m cúú m-tambɔndi din m yíì <Disaasɔlee> ki kóol̀ ki kpītì dipoondi din ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ anibul kɔkɔee.

english_verse: The sheep dealers who saw me knew at once that this was a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Yaadal ní dipoondi gbanti kpītì. Bibantiliibi bin dāā ipiiyee nín ká tin m ŋée, ní bi béè yii ti-Dindaan là kí dī tin m ŋée pu kí sòoǹ tiba ní.

english_verse: I told them, “Pay me my wages, if you think you should; otherwise, forget it.” So they handed me my wages, a measly
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Bi nín ká m-daaku nimbiŋmiiku sá puee dee! Yòon̄ animbikpaan gbanti kí cáá lúkú ukúduntil!» Ní m yōoǹ animbil jitɔmbi mmuŋku nì saalaayee ki cáa lúkú ukúduntil kunimbɔtidiin.

english_verse: Then I broke the stick named “Unity” and canceled the ties between Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní m cúú m-tambɔndi dililiitiil din m yíì <Mpèéyee> ki kóol̀ kí yàkatī kunabitiiu kun bí Juuda yab nì Isirayeel yab kansikinee.

english_verse: Next, the Lord said to me, “Act like a shepherd again—this time a worthless shepherd.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan gíti bí-mi yii: «Á gíiǹ a-ba upikpaagbaan yam.

english_verse: Once more I am going to let a worthless nobody rule the land—one who won't care for the strays or search for the young or heal the sick or feed the healthy. He will just dine on the fattest sheep, leaving nothing but a few bones.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii man làá yàntī upikpaal ubɔ mun ń dāan̄ kitiŋ nee ni. Waa dāa fātìi tɔ́ ipii in wáŋkèe bɔtaaa, kaa dāa nyàab̀ in wáŋkèeyaaa, kaa dāa cāantí in būǹeeyaaa, kaa làá dāá kpíiǹ in pɔ̄ɔ̄yee mun. Ama u dāa kù in gbìfì ki cáá ŋkpamee ki ŋmóò, ki dátí ki fúkutí i-tafuŋfukuti.»

english_verse: You worthless shepherd, deserting the sheep! I hope a sword will cripple your arm and blind your right eye.
translation_verse: An sá mbusu ní ki tīī upikpaagbaan un féeń u-picaŋkpuŋkuee! Bí gāā kí tùkutī u-ŋal kí lēē u-nimbil kujaaun! U-ŋal ń fáká ní u-ŋaŋgiinimbil ń kpú.

english_verse: This is a message from the Lord about Israel: I am the Lord! I stretched out the heavens; I put the earth on its foundations and gave breath to humans.
translation_verse: Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Isirayeel yab puee. Ti-Dindaan un kpátì kutagbɔŋu, ki báaǹ kitiŋ nyeel, ki náań kufoou ki ŋá unilinee nín lī puee sèé:

english_verse: I have decided that Jerusalem will become a bowl of wine that makes the neighboring nations drunk. And when Jerusalem is attacked, Judah will also be attacked.
translation_verse: «M làá dū Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí ŋá kii ndaam min gbéèyee ní kí tīī anibul ŋin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-kèe. Míǹ ní bi yaa láa māntìi tú Jeerusaleem kí já nì kèe, Juuda yab mun kɔkɔ làá dāá gbí.

english_verse: But I will turn Jerusalem into a heavy stone that crushes anyone who tries to lift it. When all nations on earth surround Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, m làá dū Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí ŋá kii ditaŋkpakpaandi din nyìm̀ ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí dúkutée. Un kamaa làá dāá màkan̄ kí dúkutí-dèe làá dāá fōō tiweendi. An pu ní kitiŋ pu timbuŋŋi kɔkɔ làá dāá kpāfì kí já nì kì.

english_verse: I will blind every horse and make them panic, and every rider will be confused. But at the same time, I will watch over Judah.
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan di lī yii, ŋwiin gbantee, m làá dāá kɔ́ǹ itaamu kɔkɔ dinyoondi, ní kí dāá tɔ̄ bitanjakaliibi kuwaatiiu, ní kí dāa tɔ̄ atimbun ŋin kíǹee taamui ijɔfi. Ama m-nimbiliŋ làá nīn cɔ́ Juuda naakooku pu.

english_verse: Then every clan in Judah will realize that I, the Lord All-Powerful, am their God, and that I am the source of their strength.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, Juuda yab kpilib dāa lì bi-pɔbiliŋin yii: <Isirayeel yab pɔŋŋu nyēeń ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bi-Nimbɔtiu cee ní.>

english_verse: At that time I will let the clans of Judah be like a ball of fire in a wood pile or a fiery torch in a hay stack. Then Judah will send the surrounding nations up in smoke. And once again the city of Jerusalem will be filled with people.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dū Juuda yab kpilib kí ŋá kii ŋŋmi ŋun fōō didɔkpukul taapuee, àá timool tin fōō ŋŋmi difeencundi taapuee. Bi làá wà anibul ŋin bí bi-ŋaŋgiil nì bi-ŋaŋgan pú ki māntìi tú-bee. Ama Jeerusaleem yab làá dāá nīn gbíntìi kā bi-tiŋkin.»

english_verse: But I will first give victory to Judah, so the kingdom of David and the city of Jerusalem in all of their glory won't be thought of more highly than Judah itself.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan làá dāá péé péé kí fīī Juuda yab dicaŋŋi ní, án nín làá ŋá pu Daafiidi naakookun yab nì Jeerusaleem yab ń taa dàkafì yii bíǹ jítiǹ Juuda yab bin kíǹee.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will protect Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there will be as strong as David, and David's kingdom will rule as though my very own angel were its leader.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá mɔ̄tì Jeerusaleem yab pu. Bi-kansikin bin sá biwɔfibee dāa kíǹ ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii Daafiidee, ní Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab dāa bí bi-cee kii Unimbɔtee, kii ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee. Kunimbaau jéetì kitiŋee kɔkɔ pu

english_verse: I am determined to wipe out every nation that attacks Jerusalem. Mourning for the One Pierced with a Spear
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbanti ní m làá bɔ́ntí kí kúntí anibul ŋin kɔkɔ dāa bíi jáà nì Jeerusaleemee.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will make the descendants of David and the people of Jerusalem feel deep sorrow and pray when they see the one they pierced with a spear. They will mourn and weep for him, as parents weep over the death of their only child or their first-born.
translation_verse: M làá dāá dū disaasɔl nì ŋwimmeem fam kí sìtīń Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab nì Jeerusaleem yab pu. Niinee ní bí dāá fàtī bi-nimbikpeeŋu kí túĺ-mi, un tikindi bi sāā ki cíl̀ee pu. Bi làá dāá sɔ̄ u-kpool, kii bi nín sūǹ dibibaabil kpool puee. Bi làá dāá sɔ̄ u-pu kii bi nín sūǹ ujipɔŋkpil kúm pu puee.

english_verse: On that day the people of Jerusalem will mourn as much as everyone did for Hadad Rimmon on the flatlands near Megiddo.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, bi làá dāá nīn sūǹ ki yáliŋkí nì kunimbaau Jeerusaleem tiŋkin kii bi nín sūǹ diwaal Adaadi-Riimɔn kpool Meegiidoo tantakalin puee.

english_verse: Everyone of each family in the land will mourn, and the men will mourn separately from the women. This includes those from the family of David, and the families of Nathan,
translation_verse: Kitiŋ nee kɔkɔnee, kudicaŋu kamaa làá dāá gàntì ku-ba kí sɔ̄ dikpool. Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab bininjab làá dāá gàntì bi-ba ní binimpoobi ń dāá gàntì bi-ba, ní Naatan dicaŋkun yab bininjab ń dāá gàntì bi-ba ní binimpoobi ń dāá gàntì bi-ba,

english_verse: In the future there will be a fountain, where David's descendants and the people of Jerusalem can wash away their sin and guilt.
translation_verse: «Ŋwiin gbantee, nnyim làá nyānní nnyimbul ŋubɔ poon kí fíntí Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab nì Jeerusaleem yab kpitii nì bi-jɔkɔnti.» Unimbɔti làá kúntí awaa nì inyimɔn bɔnaatiliibi

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful says: When that time comes, I will get rid of every idol in the country, and they will be forgotten forever. I will also do away with their prophets and those evil spirits that control them.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii: «M làá dāá kúntí awaa ŋin bí kitiŋ nee poonee, ní bí súntí ŋi-yiŋŋi pu. M làá dāá kúntí bin mɔ́ntí yii bi sá m-bɔnaatiliibee, ní kí lēē diwaatootil landɔkɔŋu bi-ni.

english_verse: If any such prophets ever appear again, their own parents must warn them that they will die for telling lies in my name—the name of the Lord. If those prophets don't stop speaking, their parents must then kill them with a sword.
translation_verse: Ubɔ yaa láa yíkì ki bí yii u sá m-bɔnaatiliuee, úǹ u-ba baa nì u-na di làá dāá tùkù-u yii: <A máaǹ ŋkúm, di sá yii tin a sòoǹ nee, a bíi mɔ́ntí ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔpu ní.> Ní ŋyunti ŋun u bíi sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti m-nyɔkɔpuee ní u-baa nì u-na ń dū kitàataajiki kí sāā kí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: Those prophets will be ashamed of their so-called visions, and they won't deceive anyone by dressing like a true prophet.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, icoo làá dāá cúú bibɔnaatiliibi bí nàatī tibɔti kí sòoǹ tin bi kée. Mimmee baa dāa gíti kíikí kí dū bibɔnaatiliibi bɔkutiŋ ŋin sá ŋgbanee kí pèen̄ kí mɔ̄ntì binib.

english_verse: Instead, they will say, “I'm no prophet. I've been a farmer all my life.”
translation_verse: Ama báà ŋma làá dāá lì yii: <Maa sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu, man sá ukpaal ní. Doooo m-biyatin ní m bōō ki kù.>

english_verse: And if any of them are asked why they are wounded, they will answer, “It happened at the house of some friends.” A Wounded Shepherd and Scattered Sheep
translation_verse: Ní bi yaa láa bālifì-u yii: <A ká la tiweendi tin kā a-bindi pu na?> U làá dāá kíí yii: <An sá m-bɔɔbi dumpu ní m ká tiweendi gbanti.>» Isirayeel nibul béè yii ti-Dindaan sá bi-Nimbɔtiu

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful said: My sword, wake up! Attack my shepherd and friend. Strike down the shepherd! Scatter the little sheep, and I will destroy them.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan lī yii: «Kitàataajiki, yīkì kí já nì m-pikpaaliu, kí já nì unil un bí ki pìl̄-mee. Fáá kí kpɔ̀ upikpaal ipii làá yàl̄, ní ḿ fàtīí nyā mpibiyaamu pu.»

english_verse: Nowhere in the land will more than a third of them be left alive.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan gíti lī yii: «Bi yaa cúú kitiŋ nee nib ki yākatì mitee, mili pu làá kpú ní diba pu ń ŋmátí.

english_verse: Then I will purify them and put them to the test, just as gold and silver are purified and tested. They will pray in my name, and I will answer them. I will say, “You are my people,” and they will reply, “You, Lord, are our God!”
translation_verse: M làá fíntí bin kíǹ kaa kpíì gbantee jɔkɔnti kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí kpèè kii bi nín dù tikúti nì sindaariya kí ŋá ŋŋmin kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí kpèè puee ní. Niinee bi làá dāá yíiń-mi ní man ḿ dāá kíí-bi. M làá dāá lì-bi yii bi sá <m-nibul> ní bi mun ń dāá lì-mi yii: <M-Nimbɔtiu di sá m-Dindaan.>»

english_verse: But first, he will bring many nations to attack Jerusalem—homes will be robbed, women raped, and half of the population dragged off, though the others will be allowed to remain.
translation_verse: Di sá yii ti-Dindaan làá dāá kóoǹ atimbun kɔkɔ nib kí kpāfì bí já nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Bi làá dāá já kí fōō kitiŋ, kí dāá fūkul̀ adiin, ní kí cúú binimpoobi kí dòon̄ nì bi mpɔn. Bí làá dāá cúú ki-nib dijandi kí cùnnì kuyuŋu, ama dijandi din kíǹee làá gbíntí kí nīn bí kitiŋin.

english_verse: The Lord will attack those nations like a warrior fighting in battle.
translation_verse: Niinee ti-Dindaan làá nyā kí já nì atimbun gbanti. U làá dāá já kii u nín pée kpààa jáà pu njanjawiinee.

english_verse: He will take his stand on the Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem, and the mountain will split in half, forming a wide valley that runs from east to west.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, u làá dāá dāan̄ kí yūĺ Ɔliifi sufii jool pu, Jeerusaleem caŋin ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú. Ɔliifi sufii jool làá dāá búkutí kansikin nì kansikin ní ditantakakpaandi diba ń dòon̄ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. Dijoolee dibukul diba làá búntí ŋgan pú, ní din kíǹee ń búntí ŋgiil pú.

english_verse: Then you people will escape from the Lord's mountain, through this valley, which reaches to Azal. You will run in all directions, just as everyone did when the earthquake struck in the time of King Uzziah of Judah. Afterwards, the Lord my God will appear with his holy angels.
translation_verse: Ni làá dāá sāǹ kí dī ditantakal din dɔ̄ ajoon kansikin nee, di sá yii dì dāa dɔ̄ kí tin sāā Asaal tiŋki. Ni làá dāá sāǹ kii Juuda bɔtiu Oosiyasi yuntiŋu, kitiŋ nín nìn cīŋkì ni-naanjab nìn sáǹ puee ní. Niinee ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu ń bàń, u nì u-circir tuuŋyi kɔkɔ.

english_verse: It will be a bright day that won't turn cloudy or cold.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee unil kaa dāa gíti nyàab̀ ŋwalifi. Tiwool dāa kpáaa, nsɔnsɔm mun dāa kpá.

english_verse: In both summer and winter, life-giving streams will flow from Jerusalem, half of them to the Dead Sea in the east and half to the Mediterranean Sea in the west.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee nnyim min tìì dimaŋfalee làá nyānní Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Nnyimee dijandi làá nīn pùub̀ ki cá Ŋyaam mɔɔlin, ní dijandi din kíǹee ń nīn pùub̀ ki cá Meediiteeranee tiŋkuun. Án làá nīn bí míǹ ní dipeel pu nì kuseeun kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Then there will be only one Lord who rules as King and whose name is worshiped everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan di dāa sá kitiŋ kɔkɔ bɔtiu. Ŋwiin gbantee ti-Dindaan baba di làá nīn sá Unimbɔti, ní u-yindi baba ní binib làá nīn nyí.

english_verse: Here is what the Lord will do to those who attack Jerusalem: While they are standing there, he will make their flesh rot and their eyes fall from their sockets and their tongues drop out.
translation_verse: Ditafadaaldi din ti-Dindaan làá dūú dáaĺ anibul ŋin kɔkɔ jáń nì Jeerusaleemee sɔ̀. Bi dáá kā ki wāĺ ní bi-wunnanti ń sūū, ní bi-nimbiliŋ ń sūū bi-nimbisɔntin, ní bi-limbiliŋ ń sūū bi-nyɔmmun.

english_verse: The Lord will make them go into a frenzy and start attacking each other,
translation_verse: Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan làá dāá dū dinyoondi kí tɔ̄ bi-pu. Bi làá dāá fàtīí nyā tɔb pu ní kí kíĺ ki bíi jáà.

english_verse: Afterwards, the survivors from those nations that attacked Jerusalem will go there each year to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
translation_verse: Niinee atimbun ŋin nìn jáń nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki, ki bí kaa kpíìyee, làá nīn jɔ́ḿ dibintil kamaa kí gbàan̄ ubɔti, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nimbiin kí jī tantib jiŋaaliu.

english_verse: No rain will fall on the land of anyone in any country who refuses to go to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ama kitiŋ pu nibul diba yaa kaa dāa cūtì Jeerusaleem kí gbàan̄ ubɔti ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nimbiinee, utaa kaa làá dāá nì di-tiŋki pu.

english_verse: This horrible disaster will strike the Egyptians and everyone else who refuses to go there for the celebration.
translation_verse: Eejipiti yab nì atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ yíì kaa cūtìi jíń tantib jiŋaaliuee tafadaaldi nín dāa sá puee dee.

english_verse: At that time the words “Dedicated to the Lord” will be engraved on the bells worn by horses. In fact, every ordinary cooking pot in Jerusalem will be just as sacred to the Lord All-Powerful as the bowls used at the altar. Any one of them will be acceptable for boiling the meat of sacrificed animals, and there will no longer be a need to sell special pots and bowls.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá dū akumboo ŋin kɔkɔ bí Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmunee kí sú ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan. Bin kɔkɔ dāa dòoń ki ŋáań saraabee dāa cáa tɔ̄kɔntí saraabi nanti. Ŋwiin gbanti yaa láa bāańee, baa dāa gíti kāntí ubantil ubɔ ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan diikun.

english_verse: I am Malachi. And this is the message that the Lord gave me for Israel. The Lord's Love for Israel
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan nín dī Malakii pu ki sòon̄ nì Isirayeel yab tibɔti tiŋyee sɔ̀. Isirayeel yab ní ti-Dindaan lēē

english_verse: Israel, I, the Lord, have loved you. And yet you ask in what way have I loved you. Don't forget that Esau was the brother of your ancestor Jacob, but I chose Jacob
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan bí u-nibul yii: «M néeń-ni.» Ní bi bí-u yii: «Ba di dàkà yii a néeń-ti?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-bi yii: «Eesayuu naal di kaa sá Jaakɔbaaa? Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m néeń Jaakɔb

english_verse: instead of Esau. And I turned Esau's hill country into a barren desert where jackals roam.
translation_verse: ama ní kaa là Eesayuu. M yāntì ajoon ŋin pu u kóòyee kpántì kuteeu, ní ki dū u-tiŋki ki tīī jiiŋkpaaibi bin bí kuteeunee.

english_verse: Esau's descendants may say, “Although our nation Edom is in ruins, we will rebuild it.” But I, the Lord All-Powerful, promise to tear down whatever they build. Then everyone will know that I will never stop being angry with them as long as they are so sinful.
translation_verse: Eedoom yab naantiibi yaa bí yii: <Bi nāaǹ ti-timmu, ama ti làá fātìi mā-mu.> Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé: <Bi ŋūǹ kí fàtīí mā-mu, ama man làá kpìtī-mu. Bi làá dāá páań-bi diyindi yii: <Ikpiti tiŋki> nì <Dinibul din pu ti-Dindaan gífí diŋuul an kaa kúntée.>

english_verse: Israel, when you see this, you will shout, “The Lord's great reputation reaches beyond our borders.” Judgment against Priests
translation_verse: Nimbi Isirayeel yab, ni làá dāá nīn kíǹ ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan sá ukpaan ní u-kpaanti lákatì Isirayeel tiŋki pu.>» Ti-Dindaan bíi wòoǹ bisaraaŋaliibi

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something to say to you priests. Children respect their fathers, and servants respect their masters. I am your father and your master, so why don't you respect me? You priests have insulted me, and now you ask, “How did we insult you?”
translation_verse: Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ nì bisaraaŋaliibi puee sèé: «Ujipɔnti tìì u-baa tinyool, ní utɔntɔnli tɔ́ u-kpiliu. M yaa sá ni-baa, ni tìì-mi tinyoolaaa? M yaa sá ni-kpiliu, ni tɔ́-maaa? Ni kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ m-yindi ní ki bàlifī-mi yii: <Mana ní ti kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ a-yindi?>

english_verse: You embarrass me by offering worthless food on my altar. Then you ask, “How have we embarrassed you?” You have done it by saying, “What's so great about the Lord's altar?”
translation_verse: Ni cāabìń tijin tin kaa bí circiree m-saraafaŋŋu pu ki ŋáań saraa, ní ki lì yii: <Nì mana ní ti kɔ̄ntí-si tijɔkɔndi?> An sá ni nín lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu kaa bí tibanee!

english_verse: But isn't it wrong to offer animals that are blind, lame, or sick? Just try giving those animals to your governor. That certainly wouldn't please him or make him want to help you.
translation_verse: Ni nín cāabìń kuwaŋkuluu kun jɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá-mi saraayee, an ŋān̄aaa? Ni nín cāabìń kuwaŋkuluu kun taal wɔ̀b̄ àá kun būǹee kí ŋá-mi saraayee, an ŋān̄aaa? Ní cáá-kù kí pɔ̄ ni-gɔminau kí kpèè ni-bɔti yaa làá mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u. U làá fōō-ni tiŋanaaa? Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di bàlifī-ni míǹ.

english_verse: I am the Lord God All-Powerful, and you had better try to please me. You have sinned. Now see if I will have mercy on any of you.
translation_verse: Ni yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ni dòoń ki gbàam̄ man Unimbɔti yii ḿ sɔ̄ ni-saai! Ni dàkafī yii m làá fōō-ni tiŋanaaa?> Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di bàlifī-ni míǹ.

english_verse: I wish someone would lock the doors of my temple, so you would stop wasting time building fires on my altar. I am not pleased with you priests, and I refuse to accept any more of your offerings.
translation_verse: An sɔ́ ni-kansikin ubɔ ń bàà cù kí pìin̄ m-diiku punyɔmmu ní taa ti kɔ́ kí tūū ŋŋmi m-saraafaŋŋu pu fám. Di sá yii ni-bɔti tiba kaa ti mɔ̄ǹ-mi ní ni-saraabi kaa ti fáatiǹ-mi. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: From dawn until dusk my name is praised by every nation on this earth, as they burn incense and offer the proper sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: Di sá yii kí yòon̄ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki kí cáá sāā ŋu-jeetilaŋkee, man yindi di sá diyiŋkpaandi atimbun kɔkɔ poon. Ijaan kɔkɔ poonee, bi tùutī talaalub ki ŋáań saraabi bin bí circiree ki tìì m-yindi. Di sá m-yindi sá diyiŋkpaandi atimbun kɔkɔ poon ní. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: But even you priests insult me by saying, “There's nothing special about the Lord's altar, and these sacrifices are worthless.”
translation_verse: Ama nimbi di kpèé diyindi gbanti fám ŋyunti ŋun ní ni lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, ní tijin tin bi pāantí ŋu-puee kaa náaǹ.>

english_verse: You get so disgusted that you even make vulgar signs at me. And for an offering, you bring stolen animals or those that are lame or sick. Should I accept these?
translation_verse: Ni lì gba yii: <An ŋman sá faalaa tundi ní!> Ni kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan. Ni cāabìń tiwaŋkuti tin ni yùn̄ee nì tin laaba wɔ̀b̄ee nì tin būǹee ki ŋáań-mi saraa. Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí fōō an saraabee?

english_verse: Instead of offering the acceptable animals you have promised, you bring me those that are unhealthy. I will punish you for this, because I am the great King, the Lord All-Powerful, and I am worshiped by nations everywhere.
translation_verse: An sá mbusu ní ki tīī umùuldi un di cáá upìjamɔnti u-picaŋkpuŋkun, ama ní ki dū upii un kaa bí tibanee ki ŋá-mi saraa kí pà ipoon in u pōoǹee puee. Di sá yii m sá ubɔtikpaan ní, man yindi ní atimbun kɔkɔ fàŋkí. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something else to say to you priests.
translation_verse: Kɔŋkɔnnee nimbi bisaraaŋaliibi ní m kpáafí tibɔti nee:

english_verse: You had better take seriously the need to honor my name. Otherwise, when you give a blessing, I will turn it into a curse. In fact, I have already done this, because you haven't taken to heart your duties as priests.
translation_verse: «Ni yaa kaa pílifì-tì, ki lēē ni-pɔbilin kí tīī m-yindi tinyoolee, m làá tɔ̄-ni mbusu, ní kí yàntī ni-biindi ń kpántí-ni mbusu. Tiŋman, m làá ŋá míǹ, di sá yii ni-kansikin ubɔ kaa bí ki yōoǹ tibɔti nee kii tì sá tiŋmanee. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I will punish your descendants and rub your faces in the manure from your animal sacrifices, and then be done with you.
translation_verse: M làá tāā kí bīikì ni-naantiibi pu. M làá dū tibin kí yàaǹ ni-nimbiin, an dàkà yii ni-jiŋaalib yuntiŋu tiwaŋkuti tin ni kù ki ŋáań-mi saraayee binti. M làá dāá ŋàtī tibin gbanti kí kpáaǹ-ni kí fá.

english_verse: I am telling you this, so I can continue to keep my agreement with your ancestor Levi.
translation_verse: Niin ní ni dāa béetí yii m nìn kpáafì-ni, án nín làá ŋá pu dipoondi din m pōoǹ Leefii yabee ń nīn bí ki cée. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: I blessed him with a full life, as I had promised, and he kept his part of the agreement by honoring me and respecting my name.
translation_verse: M-poondi gbanti puee, m nìn tīī-bi dimaŋfal nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. M nìn tīī-bi míǹ bí nīn fàŋkí-mi, ní bi nìn fàŋkí-mi ki jìkì m-nimbiin tɔ́kɔ́ tɔkɔ.

english_verse: He taught the truth and never told lies, and he led a lot of people to turn from sin, because he obeyed me and lived right.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dàkà mara un sá ibaamɔnee, baa nìn mɔ́ntí. Bi nìn nóó-mi deedee nì dipɔbil diba, ní ki yāntì binib tikpil fá ikpiti.

english_verse: You priests should be eager to spread knowledge, and everyone should come to you for instruction, because you speak for me, the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, usaraaŋal tundi di sá ú dàkà binib bí béé Unimbɔti. Úǹ cee ní binib tí cá kí béé marab. Di sá yii úǹ di sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan tuuŋŋu.

english_verse: But you have turned your backs on me. Your teachings have led others to do sinful things, and you have broken the agreement I made with your ancestor Levi.
translation_verse: Ama nimbee, ni dū nsan gbanti ki fá, ní ni-dàkatam yāntì binib tikpil gáatì. Ni bíil̀ dipoondi din bí man nì Leefii yab kansikinee. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.

english_verse: So I caused everyone to hate and despise you, because you disobeyed me and failed to treat all people alike. A Broken Agreement
translation_verse: Too, ma mun làá yàntī Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ ń kpèè-ni fám kí sìntīǹ-ni taapu taapu, di sá yii naa ŋúb́ m-marab ní ki pɔ̀ gandi.» Isan ili pu ní Juuda yab dī ki bíil̀ dipoondi

english_verse: Don't you know that we all have God as our Father? Didn't the one God create each of us? Then why do you cheat each other by breaking the agreement God made with your ancestors?
translation_verse: Ti-kɔkɔ baa kaa sá ubaantaaa? Unimbɔtibaanti di kaa náań-taaa? Kin ba pu ní ti nyēē tɔb booŋyi ki bíiĺ dipoondi din nìn bí Unimbɔti nì ti-naanjab kansikinee?
