translation_verse: Niinee, Ananiyasi búntì ki bàn̄ ki kɔ́ kudicaŋuee ni, ki dū u-ŋalii ki páaǹ Sɔɔl pu, ní ki bí yii: «M-nabiki Sɔɔl, ti-Dindaan di túnní-mi. Úǹ di sá Yeesu un a nìn ká nsanni a nín nìn dòoń puee. U là á wāl̀, kí gbí Circir Fam.»

english_verse: Then he ate and felt much better. Saul Preaches in Damascus For several days Saul stayed with the Lord's followers in Damascus.
translation_verse: Ní u jíń tijin ki fātìi ká mpɔn. Sɔɔl sòon̄ Unimbɔti bɔti Damaasi Ní Sɔɔl kāl̀ Damaasi iwiŋkaaŋkaa Yeesu boonnooliibi cee,

english_verse: Soon he went to the synagogues and started telling people that Jesus is the Son of God.
translation_verse: ní ki kpáàa kíĺ ki sòoǹ Yeesu pu akpafidiinni, yii u sá Unimbɔti Jipɔɔn.

english_verse: Everyone who heard Saul was amazed and said, “Isn't this the man who caused so much trouble for those people in Jerusalem who worship in the name of Jesus? Didn't he come here to arrest them and take them to the chief priests?”
translation_verse: An nìn ŋá bin kɔkɔwoooo nìn bíi pílifíǹ-uee bitii, ní bi lì yii: «Kaa sá un nìn bí Jeerusaleem ki páb̀ bin nóó Yeesuee deeee? Waa tí dɔ́miń doo kí cūtì-bi kí bóob́-bi kí cáá-bi bisaraaŋakpilib nimbiin deeee?»

english_verse: Later some of them made plans to kill Saul,
translation_verse: Iyunti tikpil jítèe, ní Juuda yab kpáfì kinyɔkɔ ki là kí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: but he found out about it. He learned that they were guarding the gates of the city day and night in order to kill him.
translation_verse: Ama Sɔɔl béè tin bi là kí ŋée. Bi nìn dòoń ki nākantí ki cīití-u Damaasi tiŋki gundi punyɔmmu nyɔkɔpui ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kí ŋmā kí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: Then one night his followers let him down over the city wall in a large basket. Saul in Jerusalem
translation_verse: Kunyeeuee, bin dī Sɔɔlee dū ŋŋmii ki kúĺ kukabiku ki dū Sɔɔl ki tākaǹ, ki dū-u ki nāatì digundi, ní u tin tīiǹ kitiŋ ki nyáń ki búntì. Sɔɔl bí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin

english_verse: Then Barnabas helped him by taking him to the apostles. He explained how Saul had seen the Lord and how the Lord had spoken to him. Barnabas also said when Saul was in Damascus, he had spoken bravely in the name of Jesus.
translation_verse: Ní Baarnaabaasi cáá-u ki cūnnì Yeesu kpambaliŋ cee ki máafì-bi Sɔɔl nín nìn ká ti-Dindaan nsanni, u sòon̄ nì u puee, nì min Sɔɔl nìn sòon̄ Damaasi ki cántì ki pɔ̀n̄ Yeesuee.

english_verse: Saul moved about freely with the followers in Jerusalem and told everyone about the Lord.
translation_verse: U nì bi nìn kíǹ ki yìiǹ Jeerusaleem, ní u sòoǹ ti-Dindaan pu, kaa fàŋkí.

english_verse: He was always arguing with the Jews who spoke Greek, and so they tried to kill him.
translation_verse: Ní u nì Juuda yab bin gbìl̀ Greeki sooŋyee sòoǹ ki kpākantí tɔb, ní bíǹ nìn kíǹ ki nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: But the followers found out about this and took Saul to Caesarea. From there they sent him to the city of Tarsus.
translation_verse: Nnabiyaamu mun kíǹee gbìl̄ mimmee, ní ki yōoǹ-u ki cūnnì Seesaaree, ní ki yāntì u búntì Taarsi.

english_verse: The church in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria now had a time of peace and kept on worshiping the Lord. The church became stronger, as the Holy Spirit encouraged it and helped it grow. Peter Heals Aeneas
translation_verse: Kriisitoo nikitil din nìn bí Juudee nì Galiilee nì Samaariiyee nìn kíǹ ki bí nsɔŋfin ki báaǹ inyaan ki fàŋkí ti-Dindaan, kaa là kí yìntīǹ-u. Ní bi-wíiŋŋu nìn gbēentí mun, kun puee Circir Fam nìn bí bi-cee. Eenee cáaǹtam

english_verse: While Peter was traveling from place to place, he visited the Lord's followers who lived in the town of Lydda.
translation_verse: Peetroo nìn yìiǹ niin timmu kɔkɔn ki màntī Kriisitoo yab pu, ní ki kpáàa sīntì bin nìn kóò Liida tiŋkinee cee,

english_verse: There he met a man named Aeneas, who for eight years had been sick in bed and could not move.
translation_verse: ní ki tin ká uninja ubɔ, bi yíì-u Eenee. U nìn sá ufaliŋfaan ki dɔ̄ u-lambaŋki pu abin anii.

english_verse: Peter said to Aeneas, “Jesus Christ has healed you! Get up and make up your bed.” At once he stood up.
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo bí-u yii: «Eenee, Yeesu Kriisitoo cáaǹ-si! Yīkìí kpáb́ a-lambaŋki.» Ní u yáatìi yúl̀ dicilpu niin.

english_verse: Many people in the towns of Lydda and Sharon saw Aeneas and became followers of the Lord. Peter Brings Dorcas Back to Life
translation_verse: Bin kɔkɔwoooo nìn kóò Liida nì Saarɔnee nìn ká-u, ní ki kpántì bi-ba ki kíǹ ki nóó ti-Dindaan. Tabiita fìkititam

english_verse: In Joppa there was a follower named Tabitha. Her Greek name was Dorcas, which means “deer.” She was always doing good things for people and had given much to the poor.
translation_verse: Unimpu ubɔ nìn bí Joopee ki nóó Yeesu, bi yíì-u Tabiita, - greeki sooŋyi poonee bi yíì-u Dɔɔrkaasi. - U nìn ŋáań binib tiŋan tikpil, ní ki pūǹ biwɔfib animbil mun.

english_verse: But she got sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upstairs room.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, u búŋkì ní ki kpíì. Bi fùl̄-u ki dóòyee, ki cáá-u ki jɔ́m̀ diditɔntɔkɔl pu ki bíl̀.

english_verse: Joppa wasn't far from Lydda, and the followers heard that Peter was there. They sent two men to say to him, “Please come with us as quickly as you can!”
translation_verse: Joopee nì Liida kaa nìn dátiǹ tɔb. Yeesu boonnooliibi gbìl̄ yii Peetroo bí Liida, ní bi tú bininjab bili u-cee bí cùú gbàamìń-u yii ú dāan̄ bi-cee malaa malaa.

english_verse: At once, Peter went with them. The men took Peter upstairs into the room. Many widows were there crying. They showed him the coats and clothes that Dorcas had made while she was still alive.
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo yíkì dicilpu, u nì bininjabee kɔkɔ búntì. Bi bàn̄ee, ní bi cáá-u ki jɔ́m̀ diditɔntɔkɔl pu. Bikpiipusoodambi kɔkɔ nìn dɔ́miń ki māntì ki gɔ́ń Peetroo ki sūǹ ki dàkà Peetroo Dɔɔrkaasi nín nìn dáá bí ki lù abɔkuti nì satab biŋyee.

english_verse: After Peter had sent everyone out of the room, he knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the body of Dorcas and said, “Tabitha, get up!” The woman opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo nyántì binib kɔkɔ ní ki gbāaǹ ki bíi mèé, ní ki fātì utaŋkpiil pu ki bí yii: «Tabiita, yīkìm̄!» Ní u ŋúbitì u-nimbiliŋ ki kpēē Peetroo, ní ki yáatìi kāl̀.

english_verse: He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet. Peter called in the widows and the other followers and showed them that Dorcas had been raised from death.
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo tāntì u-ŋal ki cúú-u ki yáatì-u ki yóoǹ, ní ki yíiń Kriisitoo yab nì bikpiipusoodambee, ki dū un fīkitèe ki dūu dàkā-bi.

english_verse: Everyone in Joppa heard what had happened, and many of them put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Joopee yab kɔkɔ gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ní binib tikpil fōō ti-Dindaan ki kíí.

english_verse: Peter stayed on for a while in Joppa in the house of a man named Simon, who made leather.
translation_verse: Peetroo nìn kāl̀ Joopee ki yúntì ugbanjɔb un bi nìn yíì Siimɔŋyee cee.

english_verse: In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, who was the captain of a group of soldiers called “The Italian Unit.”
translation_verse: Uninja ubɔ nìn bí Seesaaree, bi yíì-u Kɔɔrneeyi. U nìn sá usoojakpil disoojakitil din bi yíì Italii yalee kansikin.

english_verse: Cornelius was a very religious man. He worshiped God, and so did everyone else who lived in his house. He had given a lot of money to the poor and was always praying to God.
translation_verse: Uninja gbanti nìn nóó Unimbɔti ki sá unimɔnti, u nì u-dicaŋku kɔkɔ nìn fàŋkí Unimbɔti. U nìn pūǹ Juuda yab wɔfib tiwan ní ki mèé Unimbɔti baabadal.

english_verse: One afternoon at about three o'clock, Cornelius had a vision. He saw an angel from God coming to him and calling him by name.
translation_verse: Dalbee, an cá kii tikúti titee, u ká Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu kpìrrr, ŋu kóoń u-cee ní ki bí-u yii: «Kɔɔrneeyi!»

english_verse: Cornelius was surprised and stared at the angel. Then he asked, “What is this all about?” The angel answered, “God has heard your prayers and knows about your gifts to the poor.
translation_verse: Tifaandi nìn kɔ́-u, ní u kíǹ ki bíi kpèé Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu, ní ki bí yii: «Ba ŋá ní, m-Dindaan?» Ní ntuun bí-u yii: «A-wimmeem nì a nín pūǹ tiŋyee bàn̄ Unimbɔti, ní u téetì a-pu.

english_verse: Now send some men to Joppa for a man named Simon Peter.
translation_verse: Tɔ̄ bininjab kɔŋkɔnnee Joopee bí yíiń un bi yíì Siimɔn ki páaǹ-u diyindi yii Peetrooyee.

english_verse: He is staying with Simon the leather maker, who lives in a house near the sea.”
translation_verse: U bí ugbanjɔb un bi yíì Siimɔŋyee cee, un diiku bí tiŋku caŋinee.»

english_verse: After saying this, the angel left. Cornelius called in two of his servants and one of his soldiers who worshiped God.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun ntuun ŋun nìn dɔ́miń ki sòon̄ nì Kɔɔrneeyee búntèe, ní u yíiń u-tɔntɔnliibi bili nì sooja ubɔ un nìn bí u-cee ki fàŋkí Unimbɔtee.

english_verse: He explained everything to them and sent them off to Joppa.
translation_verse: U nìn máafì-bi tibɔtee ní ki dū-bi ki tú Joopee.

english_verse: The next day about noon these men were coming near Joppa. Peter went up on the roof of the house to pray
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe, bi bí nsanni ki tóob́ kitiŋ gbantee, Peetroo jɔ́m̀ kudii yilpu kuwiŋkuluu yuntiŋu kí mèè.

english_verse: and became very hungry. While the food was being prepared, he fell sound asleep and had a vision.
translation_verse: Ŋkùm nìn cúú-u, u bàà là kí jī. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi ŋáań-u tijinee, ní an ŋá-u kii ŋgeemee.

english_verse: He saw heaven open, and something came down like a huge sheet held up by its four corners.
translation_verse: Ní kutagbɔŋu pīitì, ní u ká tiwan tiba bí kii satakpaanee bi bóob́ ajannaatil pu ki sīntìń kitiŋ u-nimbiin.

english_verse: In it were all kinds of animals, reptiles, and birds.
translation_verse: Tiwan tin còom̄ ataa anaayee nì tin fùee nì nnɔmbiyaamu kɔkɔ nìn kā satee poon,

english_verse: A voice said to him, “Peter, get up! Kill these and eat them.”
translation_verse: ní nneen ŋubɔ bí-u yii: «Peetroo, yīkìm̄ kí kpɔ̀ kí ŋmɔ́!»

english_verse: But Peter said, “Lord, I can't do that! I've never eaten anything that is unclean and not fit to eat.”
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo bí yii: «Aayee, m-Dindaan! Maa láá pée jíń tijin tin kòóyee àá tin kaa bí circiree.»

english_verse: The voice spoke to him again, “When God says that something can be used for food, don't say it isn't fit to eat.”
translation_verse: Ní an gíti sòon̄ nì u nliliitiim yii: «Tin tin Unimbɔti ŋáŋkèe, sii ń taa lī yii taa ŋān̄!»

english_verse: This happened three times before the sheet was suddenly taken back to heaven.
translation_verse: An jítì míǹ diba dibee mita pu, ní tiwanee fātìi nín jɔ́ḿ yilpu.

english_verse: Peter was still wondering what all this meant, when the men sent by Cornelius came and stood at the gate. They had found their way to Simon's house
translation_verse: Peetroo bākatì ki kíǹ ki bíi dàkafī tin tin u bàà wál̀ee taapuee, niinee, bininjab bin Kɔɔrneeyi túnnée bālifì ki béè Siimɔn dumpu ki dɔ́miń ki yú kipunyɔkɔpu

english_verse: and were asking if Simon Peter was staying there.
translation_verse: ki yíiń ki bālifì yii: «Doo ní Siimɔn un bi yíì Peetrooyee kóòoo?»

english_verse: While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Holy Spirit said to him, “Three men are here looking for you.
translation_verse: Peetroo gbíntìi bíi dàkafī tin u bàà wál̀ee taapuee, ní Unimbɔti Fam bí-u yii: «Bininjab bita biba di nyàab̀-see.

english_verse: Hurry down and go with them. Don't worry, I sent them.”
translation_verse: Yīkìí kpákatí, taa gùgufì, si nì bi kɔkɔ ń nīn cá, kun puee man di túnní-bi.»

english_verse: Peter went down and said to the men, “I am the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Peetroo kpákatìń, ní ki bí bininjabee yii: «Man un ni nyàab̀ee sèé. Ba di ŋá ní ni dɔ́miń doo?»

english_verse: They answered, “Captain Cornelius sent us. He is a good man who worships God and is liked by the Jewish people. One of God's holy angels told Cornelius to send for you, so he could hear what you have to say.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Kɔɔrneeyi un sá usoojakpil ki bí deedee ki fàŋkí Unimbɔti, Juuda yab kɔkɔ sòoǹ u-pu yii u sá unimɔntee, Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ŋubɔ tùkū-u yii ú yíiń-si, á dāan̄ u-dumpu ú pīlifì tin tin a cáá kí tùkù-uee.»

english_verse: Peter invited them to spend the night. The next morning, Peter and some of the Lord's followers in Joppa left with the men who had come from Cornelius.
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo fōō-bi ki bíl̀. Kutaa wúntèe, u nì bi yíkìi búntì. Nnabiyaamu mun nìn bí Joopeeyee biba mun nìn céeǹ-u.

english_verse: The next day they arrived in Caesarea where Cornelius was waiting for them. He had also invited his relatives and close friends.
translation_verse: Ku wúntèe ní u dūu bàn̄ Seesaaree. Kɔɔrneeyi nìn yíiń u-yab nì u-bɔɔtimɔntiibi ki kíǹ ki kā ki cí-bi.

english_verse: When Peter arrived, Cornelius greeted him. Then he knelt at Peter's feet and started worshiping him.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Peetroo kóònée, ní Kɔɔrneeyi túŋkì-u ki gbāaǹ ki póofì-u kunɔpoou.

english_verse: But Peter took hold of him and said, “Stand up! I am nothing more than a human.”
translation_verse: Ama Peetroo yáatì-u, ní ki bí yii: «Yīkìm̄! Ma mun sá unil ní.»

english_verse: As Peter entered the house, he was still talking with Cornelius. Many people were there,
translation_verse: Bi bíi sòoǹee ní ki nín kóò, ní Peetroo bàn̄ ki ká kunipaau kpáfì ki kā.

english_verse: and Peter said to them, “You know that we Jews are not allowed to have anything to do with other people. But God has shown me that he doesn't think anyone is unclean or unfit.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-bi yii: «Kéè, ni nyí yii an sá timbi Juuda yab dikoobil ti nì binicambi ń kpāfì àá tí kɔ́ bi-dumpuyaa! Ama Unimbɔti dàkā-mi yii ḿ taa kpèè yii ubɔ sá ukpiti àá waa ŋān̄.

english_verse: I agreed to come here, but I want to know why you sent for me.”
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní ni tú ki yíiń-mi, m dɔ́miń kaa kpákáǹ. Too, ba pu ní ni yíiń-mi?»

english_verse: Cornelius answered: Four days ago at about three o'clock in the afternoon I was praying at home. Suddenly a man in bright clothes stood in front of me.
translation_verse: Ní Kɔɔrneeyi kíí-u yii: «Iwiin inaa sèé, tikúti tita, ŋyunti ŋun bí nee deedee, m bíi mèé m-dumpu. M kpēēyee, uninja ubɔ dee ki pēē dibɔkutil diba di jìl̀, ki yú m-nimbiin,

english_verse: He said, “Cornelius, God has heard your prayers, and he knows about your gifts to the poor.
translation_verse: ní ki bí yii: <Kɔɔrneeyi, Unimbɔti fōō a-wimmeem ki téetì a nín ŋáań biwɔfib tiŋan puee.

english_verse: Now send to Joppa for Simon Peter. He is visiting in the home of Simon the leather maker, who lives near the sea.”
translation_verse: Tɔ̄ Joopee bí yíiń Siimɔn un bi yíì Peetrooyee, u kóò Siimɔn ugbanjɔb un dumpu nákáǹ tiŋkuee.>

english_verse: I sent for you at once, and you have been good enough to come. All of us are here in the presence of the Lord God, so that we can hear what he has to say.
translation_verse: Dicilpu ní m tú binib a-cee, ní a ŋá tiniti ki dɔ́miń. Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-kɔkɔ bí Unimbɔti nimbiin kí pīlifì tin ti-Dindaan tīī-si á tùkù-tee.» Peetroo nyɔɔbundi

english_verse: Peter then said: Now I am certain that God treats all people alike.
translation_verse: Niinee, Peetroo kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì bi yii: «Ibaamɔn, m béè yii Unimbɔti kaa gàntī ubɔ.

english_verse: God is pleased with everyone who worships him and does right, no matter what nation they come from.
translation_verse: Ntimu kɔkɔn, un yaa fàŋkí-u ki ŋáań min kítèe ŋān̄ u-nimbiin.

english_verse: This is the same message that God gave to the people of Israel, when he sent Jesus Christ, the Lord of all, to offer peace to them.
translation_verse: «Ni nyí yii Unimbɔti túnní Tibɔmɔntiil Isirayeel yab cee, kí tùkù-bi yii nì Yeesu Kriisitoo puee bi làá ká nsɔŋfi: Yeesuee di sá ti-kɔkɔ Dindaan.

english_verse: You surely know what happened everywhere in Judea. It all began in Galilee after John had told everyone to be baptized.
translation_verse: Yoowaneesi nín sòon̄ Unimbɔti nyim difaldi bɔti ki dóò boonee, ni nyí tin jítì Juudee tiŋki kɔkɔn ki kíliń Galiileeyee.

english_verse: God gave the Holy Spirit and power to Jesus from Nazareth. He was with Jesus, as he went around doing good and healing everyone who was under the power of the devil.
translation_verse: Ni nyí yii Unimbɔti nìn tīiń Yeesu Naasaareeti yɔu u-Fam ki yāntì u cáá mpɔŋkpaan. U nìn cá ajan kɔkɔ ki ŋáań tiŋan ki cāantí bin kɔkɔ Sitaan pɔŋŋu nìn ŋúb́ee, kun puee Unimbɔti nìn bí u-cee.

english_verse: We all saw what Jesus did both in Israel and in the city of Jerusalem. Jesus was put to death on a cross.
translation_verse: Timbi kántì tin kɔkɔ u ŋáaǹ Juuda yab tiŋkin ki kpáaǹ Jeerusaleemee mun. Úǹ ní bi kpáá ndɔ pu, ki kūū-u.

english_verse: But three days later, God raised him to life and let him be seen.
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti fīkitì-u winta dal, ki yāntì bi ká-u.

english_verse: Not everyone saw him. He was seen only by us, who ate and drank with him after he was raised from death. We were the ones God chose to tell others about him.
translation_verse: An kaa sá samaa kɔkɔ di ká-u, asee Unimbɔti nín nìn pée lēē timbi bin bin ń ká-uee. Di sá u nín nìn fīkitì ditaŋkpiilinee, boonee, ti nì u di jíń ki nyùn̄.

english_verse: God told us to announce clearly to the people that Jesus is the one he has chosen to judge the living and the dead.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-ti yii tí nīn sòoǹ u-pu samaa cee, kí dàkà-bi yii úǹ Yeesu baba ní Unimbɔti lēē u-bɔsoonliu, ú sòoǹ bin wāĺee nì bin kpíìyee bɔti.

english_verse: Every one of the prophets has said that all who have faith in Jesus will have their sins forgiven in his name.
translation_verse: Úǹ pu ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ lēekì seera yii un sá kamaa yaa fōō-u ki kííyee kāntí u-kpitii pɔ̄tam u-yindi pu.» Bin kaa sá Juuda yabee mun fōō Circir Fam

english_verse: While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit took control of everyone who was listening.
translation_verse: Peetroo bíi sòoǹ mimmee, ní Circir Fam kpákatìń bin kɔkɔ nìn bíi pílifí u-nyɔɔbundee pu.

english_verse: Some Jewish followers of the Lord had come with Peter, and they were surprised that the Holy Spirit had been given to Gentiles.
translation_verse: Kriisitoo yab bin sá Juuda yab ki céeǹní Peetrooyee nìn bākatì. Di sá yii Unimbɔti nìn pú bin kaa sá Juuda yabee gba Circir Fam.

english_verse: Now they were hearing Gentiles speaking unknown languages and praising God. Peter said,
translation_verse: Bi nìn gbìl̄ binicambi bíi sòoǹ isooncaan ki nyɔ́ŋkí Unimbɔti. Niinee ní Peetroo bí yii:

english_verse: “These Gentiles have been given the Holy Spirit, just as we have! I am certain that no one would dare stop us from baptizing them.”
translation_verse: «Binib nee fōō Circir Fam kii timbee dee. Mimmee, ti ŋūǹ kí yíí yii taa làá fàl̀-bi Unimbɔti nyimaaa?»

english_verse: Peter ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and they asked him to stay on for a few days.
translation_verse: Ní u pú nsan yii bí fàl̀-bi Unimbɔti nyim Yeesu Kriisitoo yindi pu, ní bi gbāam̀-u yii ú kàl̄ bi-cee iwiŋkaaŋkaa.

english_verse: The apostles and the followers in Judea heard that Gentiles had accepted God's message.
translation_verse: Akpambal nì nnabiyaamu mun nìn bí Juudeeyee gbìl̄ yii bin kaa sá Juuda yabee mun fōō Unimbɔti nyɔɔbundi.

english_verse: So when Peter came to Jerusalem, some of the Jewish followers started arguing with him. They wanted Gentile followers to be circumcised, and
translation_verse: Peetroo nìn fātìi bāań Jeerusaleemee, bin nìn fōō ki kíí ki sá Juuda yabee nìn bíi wòoǹ-u,

english_verse: they said, “You stayed in the homes of Gentiles, and you even ate with them!”
translation_verse: yii u kɔ́ bin kaa gíí dikpancandee dumpu, u nì bi jíń tijin.

english_verse: Then Peter told them exactly what had happened:
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo bíi máafí-bi tin jítèe, an nín kíliń pu ki tin kúntì puee, yii:

english_verse: I was in the town of Joppa and was praying when I fell sound asleep and had a vision. I saw heaven open, and something like a huge sheet held by its four corners came down to me.
translation_verse: «M nìn bí Joopee tiŋki poon ki bíi mèé ní Unimbɔti ŋúbitì m-nimbiliŋ m wál̀ tiwan tiba, tì bí kii satakpaanee ki bóob́ ajannaatil pu ki nyánní yilpu ki sīntìń m-cee.

english_verse: When I looked in it, I saw animals, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds.
translation_verse: Ní m bíi kpèé sata poon dímmmee, ní ki ká tiwaŋkuti tin còom̄ ataa anaayee nì ipeel, nì tin fùee nì nnɔmbiyaamu,

english_verse: I heard a voice saying to me, “Peter, get up! Kill these and eat them.”
translation_verse: ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ bí-mi yii: <Peetroo, yīkìí kpɔ̀ kí ŋmɔ́!>

english_verse: But I said, “Lord, I can't do that! I've never taken a bite of anything that is unclean and not fit to eat.”
translation_verse: Ní m bí yii: <Aayee, m-Dindaan! Doooo nee tiwan tin ti kòó àá tin kaa bí circiree kaa láá pée kɔ́ m-nyɔkɔn.>

english_verse: The voice from heaven spoke to me again, “When God says that something can be used for food, don't say it isn't fit to eat.”
translation_verse: Nliliitiimin ní nneenee gíti lī yii: <Tin Unimbɔti ŋáŋkèe, sii taa lì yii taa ŋān̄!>

english_verse: This happened three times before it was all taken back into heaven.
translation_verse: Áli míǹ diba dibee mita, ní an wanti kɔkɔ fātìi nín jɔ́ḿ yilpu.

english_verse: Suddenly three men from Caesarea stood in front of the house where I was staying.
translation_verse: Dicilpu niinee, bininjab bita bin bi nìn túnní Seesaaree m-ceeyee bāań kudii kun ni m nìn kóòyee nyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: The Holy Spirit told me to go with them and not to worry. Then six of the Lord's followers went with me to the home of a man
translation_verse: Ní Circir Fam bí yii man nì bi ń nīn cá, ḿ taa gùgufì. Man nì nnabiyaamu muluu nee di nìn nóó ki cūtì Kɔɔrneeyi dumpu.

english_verse: who told us that an angel had appeared to him. The angel had ordered him to send to Joppa for someone named Simon Peter.
translation_verse: Ní u mun máafì-ti u nín nìn kā u-dumpu Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ŋubɔ bāań ki tùkū-u yii: <Tɔ̄ Joopee, bí yíiń-si Siimɔn un bi páaǹ diyindi yii Peetrooyee.

english_verse: Then Peter would tell him how he and everyone in his house could be saved.
translation_verse: U làá tùkù-si tibɔti tin pu sii nì a-samaau kɔkɔ làá dī kí ká difiilee.>

english_verse: After I started speaking, the Holy Spirit was given to them, just as the Spirit had been given to us at the beginning.
translation_verse: M kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì bee, ní Circir Fam kpákatìń bi-pu kii mì nín nìn kpákatìń ti mun pu mpeepeekaam puee.

english_verse: I remembered that the Lord had said, “John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: Niinee, m téetì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi nee pu yii: <Yoowaneesi nìn fùul̀ binib Unimbɔti nyim, ama Unimbɔti làá dāá fàl̀ nimbi nì Circir Fam ní.>

english_verse: God gave those Gentiles the same gift that he gave us when we put our faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. So how could I have gone against God?
translation_verse: Unimbɔti pú bi mun u-Fam mbaantiim kii u nín nìn pú ti mun puee ní, kun puee ti-kɔkɔ fōō ti-Dindaan Yeesu Kriisitoo ki kíí. Kin ma mun ŋma ní ḿ kpákáǹ Unimbɔti?»

english_verse: When they heard Peter say this, they stopped arguing and started praising God. They said, “God has now let Gentiles turn to him, and he has given life to them!” The Church in Antioch
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̄ mimmee, kaa ti bíi kpākantí-u, ki kíǹ ki bíi nyɔ́ŋkí Unimbɔti ki bí yii: «Mimmee, Unimbɔti yāntì bin kaa sá Juuda yabee mun fá bi-kpitii kí ŋmā kí ká dimaŋfal dee.» Kriisitoo nikitil din bí Antiyɔɔsee

english_verse: Some of the Lord's followers had been scattered because of the terrible trouble that started when Stephen was killed. They went as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, but they told the message only to the Jews.
translation_verse: Bin bin bi nìn páb́ bi yàl̄ Eetiyeen kúm boonee bàn̄ áli Feenisii nì Siipiri nì Antiyɔɔsi, ki sòoǹ Unimbɔti bɔti Juuda yab ŋmaniŋma cee.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch and started telling Gentiles the good news about the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Ama bi-kansikin biba bin nyánní Siipiri nì Siireenee bāań Antiyɔɔsi ki mun bíi tùkù bin kaa sá Juuda yabee Tibɔmɔntiil tin sòoǹ ti-Dindaan Yeesu puee.

english_verse: The Lord's power was with them, and many people turned to the Lord and put their faith in him.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu nìn bí bi-cee, ní kunipaau nìn fōō ki kíí ki nóó ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: News of what was happening reached the church in Jerusalem. Then they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
translation_verse: Kriisitoo nikitil din bí Jeerusaleemee nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee ní bi dū Baarnaabaasi ki tú Antiyɔɔsi.

english_verse: When Barnabas got there and saw how God had blessed them with undeserved grace, he was very glad. So he begged them to remain faithful to the Lord with all their hearts.
translation_verse: U bàn̄ee ní ki ká Unimbɔti nín bīiǹ bi-pu miŋyee ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u, ní u bíi tìì-bi kunyannyaau, yii bi-kɔkɔ ń nīn yú nì dipɔbil diba kí nīn nákáǹ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Barnabas was a good man of great faith, and he was filled with the Holy Spirit. Many more people turned to the Lord.
translation_verse: Di sá yii u nìn sá unimɔnti, ki gbí Circir Fam ki cáá fookii. An puee binib tikpil nìn dɔ́miń ki nóó ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee ní Baarnaabaasi búntì Taarsi kí nyàab̀ Sɔɔl.

english_verse: He found Saul and brought him to Antioch, where they met with the church for a whole year and taught many of its people. There in Antioch the Lord's followers were first called Christians.
translation_verse: U bàn̄ ki ká-uee, ní ki cáań-u Antiyɔɔsi. Dibimmɔndi kɔkɔee, bi nìn dūu kāl̀ Kriisitoo nikitil kansikin ki dàkà binib tikpil Unimbɔti bɔti. Antiyɔɔsi tiŋkin ní bi péé péé ki yíiń Yeesu boonnooliibi yii Kriisitoo yab.

english_verse: During this time some prophets from Jerusalem came to Antioch.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi biba nyánní Jeerusaleem ki sīntì Antiyɔɔsi.

english_verse: One of them was Agabus. Then with the help of the Spirit, he told that there would be a terrible famine everywhere in the world. And it happened when Claudius was Emperor.
translation_verse: Bi-kansikin ubɔ ní bi nìn yíì Agabusi. Unimbɔti Fam yāntì kijapaayee yíkìi lī yii, ŋkùm miba làá nyā kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu kí nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄. - Ní mì lafun bāań Kloodi beel yuntiŋu.

english_verse: The followers in Antioch decided to send whatever help they could to the followers in Judea.
translation_verse: Ní Yeesu boonnooliibi bíi màkà báà ŋma ń tīī u nín ŋūǹ puee bí dūú tūtuǹ bi-nabiyaamu mun kóò Juudeeyee.

english_verse: So they appointed Barnabas and Saul to take their gifts to the church leaders in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Bi tīīyee, ní ki yāntì Baarnaabaasi nì Sɔɔl yōoǹ ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem Kriisitoo nikitil kpilib cee.

english_verse: At that time King Herod caused terrible suffering for some members of the church.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, ubɔti Eeroodi kíĺ ki bíi sàantí Kriisitoo yab biba,

english_verse: He ordered soldiers to cut off the head of James, the brother of John.
translation_verse: ní ki yāntì bi dū kitàataajiki ki kūū Yakubu un sá Yoowaneesi maanee.

english_verse: When Herod saw that this pleased the Jewish people, he had Peter arrested during the Festival of Thin Bread.
translation_verse: U ká yii an ŋān̄ Juuda yab ceeyee, ní u yāntì bi cúú Peetroo mun. An nìn sá iwiin in poon bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee ní.

english_verse: He put Peter in jail and ordered four squads of soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to put him on trial in public after the festival.
translation_verse: Bi cúú-u ki tɔ́ sarkanee, ní ubɔti lēē asoojakiti anaa, dikitil kamaa cáá soojab binaa, bí nīn cīití-u ki kpántí. U là yii, bi yaa jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu ki dóòyee, ú cáań-u samaa nimbiin kí sòoǹ u-bɔti.

english_verse: While Peter was being kept in jail, the church never stopped praying to God for him. Peter Is Rescued
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Peetroo nìn bí kusarkadiinee, Kriisitoo nikitil nìn bí ki mèé Unimbɔti u-pu, kaa gbèentí. Ntuun nyántì Peetroo kusarkadiin

english_verse: The night before Peter was to be put on trial, he was asleep and bound by two chains. A soldier was guarding him on each side, and two other soldiers were guarding the entrance to the jail.
translation_verse: Kutaa ń wúntí Eeroodi ń cáá-u ibɔsoon samaa nimbiinee, kunyeeuee, Peetroo nìn sáká soojab bili kansikin ki dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ. Bi nìn bóob́-u ikusaka ili, ní soojab bili yú kipunyɔkɔpu ki cí kusarkadii.

english_verse: Suddenly an angel from the Lord appeared, and light flashed around in the cell. The angel poked Peter in the side and woke him up. Then he said, “Quick! Get up!” The chains fell off his hands,
translation_verse: Kpalaayee, Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ŋubɔ dɔ́miń, ní kusarkadiin wál̀ nyáka nyaka. Ní ntuun fáá Peetroo takakal ki fīntì-u, ní ki bí yii: «Yīkì malaa!» Ní ikusakee cúu fɔ́fì u-ŋaliiyin ki lítì.

english_verse: and the angel said, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” Peter did what he was told. Then the angel said, “Now put on your coat and follow me.”
translation_verse: Ní ntuun bí yii: «Gbìn̄ a-dambalau kí táká a-naatakaŋ.» Ní u ŋá míǹ. Ní ŋu gíti bí yii: «Dū a-satau kí pèen̄, kí nīn nóó-mi.»

english_verse: Peter left with the angel, but he thought everything was only a dream.
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo nóó-u ki nyánní kusarkadiin, kaa nyí min ntuun bíi ŋáańee sá tibɔŋman. Úǹ nìn dākafì yii an sá kudamintiiu ní.

english_verse: They went past the two groups of soldiers, and when they came to the iron gate to the city, it opened by itself. They went out and were going along the street, when all at once the angel disappeared.
translation_verse: Bi jítì soojapeekaabi pu ki tin jítì bililiitiibi mun pu, ní ki dūu bàn̄ tikúti punyɔkɔki kin túĺ kitiŋinee. Kipunyɔkɔee cúu pīitì ki-ba bi-nimbiin, ní bi nyáń ki tākaǹ didandi diba pu. Kpalaayee, ntuunee yíkì Peetroo cee.

english_verse: Peter now realized what had happened, and he said, “I am certain that the Lord sent his angel to rescue me from Herod and from everything the Jewish leaders planned to do to me.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Peetroo béè tin bāań-uee ní ki bí yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, tiŋman, m nyí yii ti-Dindaan di túnní u-tuuŋŋu ŋú dāá nyāntí-mi Eeroodi ŋaan nì tin kɔkɔwoooo Juuda yab bàà cí kí ŋá-mee.»

english_verse: Then Peter went to the house of Mary the mother of John whose other name was Mark. Many of the Lord's followers had come together there and were praying.
translation_verse: U yúl̀ ki dākafèe, ní ki nín dòoń Maarii, Yoowaneesi un bi páaǹ diyindi yii Maarkee na dumpu. Niin ní binib tikpil nìn kpáfì ki bíi mèé.

english_verse: Peter knocked on the gate, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer.
translation_verse: U bàn̄ ki fáá kunaakoou punyɔkɔ, ní utɔntɔnli ubɔ, u sá unimpu bi yíì Roodee sútìń kí pīlifì.

english_verse: When she heard Peter's voice, she was too excited to open the gate. She ran back into the house and said Peter was standing there.
translation_verse: U béè Peetroo neenee, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u. Ú bàà pìitī-uee, ní u sáǹ ki cūtìi lī yii Peetroo yú kipunyɔkɔpu.

english_verse: “You are crazy!” everyone told her. But she kept saying it was Peter. Then they said, “It must be his angel.”
translation_verse: Ní bi bí-u yii: «A wáatì níii?» Ní u bí yii: «An baasii sá ibaamɔn ní!» Niinee ní bi bí yii: «An làá nīn sá Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ŋun cí-uee ní!»

english_verse: But Peter kept on knocking, until finally they opened the gate. They saw him and were completely amazed.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee, Peetroo pée gbíntìi fátí. Bi cúu pīitì ki ká-uee, ní ki bākatì sèeee.

english_verse: Peter motioned for them to keep quiet. Then he told how the Lord had led him out of jail. He also said, “Tell James and the others what has happened.” After that, he left and went somewhere else.
translation_verse: Ní Peetroo dū u-ŋal ki téefì-bi yii bí ŋmīĺee, ní u máafì-bi Unimbɔti nín nyántì-u kusarkadiin puee. Ní u bí-bi yii: «Cùú tùkùmaan Yakubu nì nnabiyaamu mun kíǹee.» Ní u nyáń ki búntì laaba mun.

english_verse: The next morning the soldiers who had been on guard were terribly worried and wondered what had happened to Peter.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe, soojab pɔbiliŋ bíil̀ tikpil, ní bi bíi bàlifī tɔb yii: «Ba di nín ŋá Peetroo dee?»

english_verse: Herod ordered his own soldiers to search for him, but they could not find him. Then he questioned the guards and had them put to death. After this, Herod left Judea to stay in Caesarea for a while. Herod Dies
translation_verse: Eeroodi tú bí nyàab̀-u, ama ní baa ká-u. Ní u bí yii bí bàlifì soojab tibɔti, ní ki pú nsan bí kpɔ̀-bi. Míǹ boonee ní Eeroodi yíkì Juudee ki cūtìi kāl̀ Seesaaree ŋyunti ŋubɔ poon. Eeroodi kúm

english_verse: Herod and the people of Tyre and Sidon were very angry with each other. But their country got its food supply from the region that he ruled. So a group of them went to see Blastus, who was one of Herod's high officials. They convinced Blastus that they wanted to make peace between their cities and Herod,
translation_verse: Eeroodi nìn fōō Tiir nì Siidɔn yab pu diŋuul, ní bíǹ kpáfì dicilpu kí cùú ká-u. U-tiŋkin ní bi nìn tūntí tijin ki cāabìń bíǹ cee. Míǹ puee, bi píí ubɔti Eeroodi cindin kpiliu Blaastuusi kubɔɔtiiu ki wāatì, ní ki cūtìi gbāam̀ ubɔti Eeroodi.

english_verse: and a day was set for them to meet with him. Herod came dressed in his royal robes. He sat down on his throne and made a speech.
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun bi nìn síiǹee bāańee, Eeroodi pēeǹ u-beebɔkutil ki kā u-beejal pu ki bíi sòoǹ nì bi tibɔti.

english_verse: The people shouted, “You speak more like a god than a man!”
translation_verse: Ní samaa bíi kūuntí yii: «An sá unimbɔti ubɔ di sòoǹ, an kaa sá unil!»

english_verse: At once an angel from the Lord struck him down because he took the honor that belonged to God. Later, Herod was eaten by worms and died.
translation_verse: Dicilpu niin ní Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ŋubɔ cáań iween ki tɔ́ u-pu, kun puee waa tīī Unimbɔti tinyool. Ní akoosibil aba kɔ́ u-ni ki ŋmɔ́ ki kūū-u.

english_verse: And after Barnabas and Saul had done the work they were sent to do, they went back to Jerusalem with John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_verse: Baarnaabaasi nì Sɔɔl dóò bi-tuuŋŋi Jeerusaleemee, ní ki fātìi gítìń, ki kpáaǹní Yoowaneesi un bi páaǹ diyindi yii Maarkee.

english_verse: The church at Antioch had several prophets and teachers. They were Barnabas, Simeon, also called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen, who was Herod's close friend, and Saul.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì bidakaliibi biba nìn bí Kriisitoo nikitil din bí Antiyɔɔsee kansikin. Bíǹ di sá: Baarnaabaasi, Simeeyɔn un bi nìn páaǹ diyindi yii Niijeeree, nì Lusiyusi un sá Siireen tiŋkinee, nì Manayeen un nì Eeroodi, Galiilee gɔminau nìn jíń tibiyati mbaantiimee nì Sɔɔl.

english_verse: Everyone prayed and went without eating for a while longer. Next, they placed their hands on Barnabas and Saul to show that they had been appointed to do this work. Then everyone sent them on their way. Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus
translation_verse: Bi bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ki mēē ki dóòyee, ní bi dū bi-ŋalii ki páaǹ Baarnaabaasi nì Sɔɔl pu, ní ki yāntì bi búntì. Baarnaabaasi nì Sɔɔl bí Siipiri

english_verse: After Barnabas and Saul had been sent by the Holy Spirit, they went to Seleucia. From there they sailed to the island of Cyprus.
translation_verse: Baarnaabaasi nì Sɔɔl bin Unimbɔti Fam nìn túee nín sìntī Seelusii ki bàn̄ee, ki kɔ́ meela ki nín cá Siipiri.

english_verse: They arrived at Salamis and began to preach God's message in the synagogues. They also had John as a helper.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Salamiinee, ki bíi sòoǹ Unimbɔti bɔti Juuda yab kpafidiiŋŋin. Yoowaneesi-Maarki nìn bí bi-cee kí nīn tútúǹ-bi.

english_verse: Barnabas and Saul went all the way to the city of Paphos on the other end of the island, where they met a Jewish man named Bar-Jesus. He practiced witchcraft and was a false prophet.
translation_verse: Ní bi cōom̀ Siipiri timmu kɔkɔn, áli ki tin bàn̄ Pafɔsi. Niin ní bi tin ká ujuudaja ubɔ, u sá ukpaŋkpanti bi yíì-u Baar-Yeesu, u mɔ́ntí yii u sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu.

english_verse: He also worked for Sergius Paulus, who was very smart and was the governor of the island. Sergius Paulus wanted to hear God's message, and he sent for Barnabas and Saul.
translation_verse: Gɔmina Seegusi Poolusi uciŋfiti cee ní u nìn bí. Gɔminee là kí pīlifì Unimbɔti nyɔɔbundee ní ki yíiń Baarnaabaasi nì Sɔɔl.

english_verse: But Bar-Jesus, whose other name was Elymas, was against them. He even tried to keep the governor from having faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Ama Eelmaasi ukpaŋkpantee - u-yindi dee greeki sooŋyi poon - nìn mɔ́tí, ki là kí pìkiliǹ gɔmina ń taa fōō Unimbɔti bɔti kí kíí.

english_verse: Then Saul, better known as Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
translation_verse: Niinee, Unimbɔti Fam gbí Sɔɔl un bi gíti yíì Pɔɔlee, ní u kpēē-u soooo,

english_verse: and said, “You son of the devil! You are a liar, a crook, and an enemy of everything that is right. When will you stop speaking against the true ways of the Lord?
translation_verse: ní ki bí-u yii: «Sitaan biki, unyimɔndaan un bí nee! A kíiĺ binib ki jáà nì ibaamɔn kɔkɔ. Aa làá gbèen̄ ki gbíntìi bíiĺ Unimbɔti sàmbiyaamu mun tèen̄eeee?

english_verse: The Lord is going to punish you by making you completely blind for a while.” Suddenly the man's eyes were covered by a dark mist, and he went around trying to get someone to lead him by the hand.
translation_verse: Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, Unimbɔti làá yàntī á kpántí ujɔfu. Aa làá ti wāl̀ ŋwìiń iyunti iba poon.» Dicilpu niinee, u kpántì ujɔfu, ní u kíǹ ki bíi táfí ki nyàab̀ un làá dàtī-uee.

english_verse: When the governor saw what had happened, he was amazed at this teaching about the Lord. So he put his faith in the Lord. Paul and Barnabas in Antioch of Pisidia
translation_verse: Gɔminee nín ká tin jítèe ní u fōō ki kíí. Kun puee ti-Dindaan bɔti tin bi dàkèe kɔ́-u tiŋan. Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi bí Antiyɔɔsi tiŋkin, Piisidii watil

english_verse: Paul and the others left Paphos and sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl nì bin nìn cēentí-uee kɔ́ meela ki yíkì Pafɔsi ki bàn̄ Peeji, Paŋfilii watil. Ní Yoowaneesi-Maarki gbēeǹ niin ki nín gítiń Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: The rest of them went on from Perga to Antioch in Pisidia. Then on the Sabbath they went to the synagogue and sat down.
translation_verse: Bi yíkì Peeji, ki nín nìkì bi-saŋŋu ki tin bàn̄ Antiyɔɔsi tiŋki, Piisidii watil. Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee, bi kɔ́ Juuda yab kpafidiikun ki kāl̀.

english_verse: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the leaders sent someone over to tell Paul and Barnabas, “Friends, if you have anything to say that will help the people, please say it.”
translation_verse: Bi nín kàan̄ mara nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi gbɔnti poon ki dóòyee, ní kukpafidii kpilib túnní bi-cee yii: «Nnabiyaamu, ni yaa cáá isaŋki iba kí tīī samaa, ní sòoǹ.»

english_verse: Paul got up. He motioned with his hand and said: People of Israel, and everyone else who worships God, listen!
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl yíkì ki yōoǹ u-ŋal yilpu ki jáam̀-bi, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Nimbi Isirayeel yab, nì nimbi bin fàŋkí Unimbɔtee, pīlifìmaan!

english_verse: The God of Israel chose our ancestors, and he let our people prosper while they were living in Egypt. Then with his mighty power he led them out,
translation_verse: Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nìn lēē ti-naanjab ki yāntì bi būtì ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bí kunicaŋu Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Unimbɔti nìn dū u-pɔŋŋu ki nyántì-bi,

english_verse: Make sure what the prophets have said doesn't happen to you. They said,
translation_verse: Ní kpèèmaan tiŋan, tibɔti tin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nìn sòon̄ee ń taa bàń-ni, yii:

english_verse: He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave their land to our people.
translation_verse: U nìn jáń ki kúntì atimbun aluli Kanaan tiŋkin, ní ki dū Isirayeel yab ki kāaǹ bi kpántì bitindambi.

english_verse: Later, God removed Saul and let David rule in his place. God said about him, “David the son of Jesse is the kind of person who pleases me most! He does everything I want him to do.”
translation_verse: Boonee, Unimbɔti dū-u ki fá, ní ki dū Daafiidi ki kāaǹ. Úǹ pu ní u sòon̄ yii: <M ká Daafiidi Jeesee jipɔɔn. Úǹ di fáatì m-pɔbil. U làá dāá ŋá min kɔkɔ m lèe.>»

english_verse: God promised that someone from David's family would come to save the people of Israel, and this one is Jesus.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl nìkī ki lī yii: «U-maaliŋu poon ní Unimbɔti yāntì bi màl̄ Ufiil ubɔ ki tīī Isirayeel yab, kii u nín nìn pōoǹ puee: úǹ di sá Yeesu.

english_verse: But before Jesus came, John was telling everyone in Israel to turn back to God and be baptized.
translation_verse: Kí wàatī ú bàńee, Yoowaneesi nìn sòon̄ nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ bí fá bi-kpitii kí yàntī bí fàl̀-bi Unimbɔti nyim.

english_verse: Then, when John's work was almost done, he said, “Who do you people think I am? Do you think I am the Promised One? He will come later, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Yoowaneesi nìn làá dóó u-tundee, ní u bí-bi yii: <Ŋma ní ni dàkafī yii m sá ní? Maa sá un ní ni dàkafī yii m sée! Ama ubɔ dòoń man boon, maa kpántì kí bútí u-naataaŋmiii gba.>

english_verse: Now listen, you descendants of Abraham! Pay attention, all of you Gentiles who are here to worship God! Listen to this message about how to be saved, because it is for everyone.
translation_verse: «Nnabiyaamu, nimbi Abraam maaliŋun biyaamu, nì nimbi binicambi bin fàŋkí Unimbɔtee, timbi ní Unimbɔti dū dinyɔɔbundi nee ki tīiń, tí ká difiil.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem and their leaders didn't realize who Jesus was. And they didn't understand the words of the prophets they read each Sabbath. So they condemned Jesus just as the prophets had said.
translation_verse: Binib bin kóò Jeerusaleemee nì bi-bɔtiibi kaa nìn béè un ní Yeesu sée, kaa béè Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bɔti tin bi kàaǹ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa sá kamaa dalee taapu mun. Bi nín yāntì bi kūū Yeesu puee, bi ŋá min Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nìn sòon̄ ki yóoǹee dee.

english_verse: But God raised him from death!
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti fīkitì-u ditaŋkpiilin.

english_verse: Then for many days Jesus appeared to his followers who had gone with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are telling our people about him.
translation_verse: Boonee, bin nìn nyánní Galiilee ki céeǹní-u Jeerusaleemee nìn ká-u iwiin tikpil poon. Kɔŋkɔnnee, binibee di kíǹ ki sá seeradambi ki lèekī seera u-pu ki tìì samaa.

english_verse: God made a promise to our ancestors. And we are here to tell you the good news
translation_verse: «Míǹ pu ní timbi bíi tùkù-ni tibɔmɔntiil yii, dipoondi din Unimbɔti nìn pōoǹ ti-naanjabee,

english_verse: that he has kept this promise to us. It is just as the second Psalm says about Jesus, “You are my son because today I have become your Father.”
translation_verse: u nín fīkitì Yeesuee, u ŋá min u nìn pōoǹee ki tīī timbi bi-naantiibi dee. A lì kii an nín ŋmàn̄ Ilan gbɔŋku poon ayil

english_verse: God raised Jesus from death and will never let his body decay. It is just as God said, “I will make to you the same holy promises that I made to David.”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn sòon̄ ki síiǹ yii u làá fìkitī-u ditaŋkpiilin ní u-wunti ń taa sūū. U nín nìn sòon̄ puee di sá yii: M làá dāá tīī-ni tin m nìn pōoǹ Daafiidee, tin bí circir ki sá tiŋmanee.>

english_verse: And in another psalm it says, “God will never let the body of his Holy One decay.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ní Daafiidi lī u-gbɔŋku poon laaba Yeesu pu yii: <Aa làá yàntī a-circir tɔntɔnliu wunti ń sūū.>

english_verse: When David was alive, he obeyed God. Then after he died, he was buried in the family grave, and his body decayed.
translation_verse: Daafiidi yuntiŋuee u nìn sá Unimbɔti tɔntɔnliu ní ki ŋáań min ní Unimbɔti lēē ki síiǹee. U dāa kpíì, ní bi síb́-u ki kɔ́ĺ u-naanjab, ní u-wunti sūū.

english_verse: But God raised Jesus from death, and his body did not decay.
translation_verse: Ama Yeesu un Unimbɔti fīkitèe, úǹ wunti kaa sūū.

english_verse: My friends, the message is that Jesus can forgive your sins! The Law of Moses could not set you free from all your sins.
translation_verse: Nnabiyaamu, béémaan yii tin tin ní ti sòoǹ ki tùkù-ni nee di sá, úǹ pu ní ni kpántí deedeedambi Unimbɔti nimbiin. Ni nín nìn nóó Mooyiisi marabee, naa nìn ŋūǹ kí kpántí deedeedambi Unimbɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: But everyone who has faith in Jesus is set free.
translation_verse: Ama un yaa fōō Yeesu ki kííyee, Unimbɔti dù u-kpitii kɔkɔ ní kí pɔ̄-u.

english_verse: “Look, you people who make fun of God! Be amazed and disappear. I will do something today that you won't believe, even if someone tells you about it!”
translation_verse: Unimbɔti bí yii: <Kpeefandambi kpèèmaan, bàkatīmaan kí wāŋkìmaan! Di sá yii ni-yuntii nee poon m làá tɔ̄ ditundi diba din bi yaa láa bíi máafí-ni gba, naa làá fōō kí kííyee.>»

english_verse: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to say more about these same things on the next Sabbath.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi nyáń kukpafidiinee, ní bi mēē-bi yii ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun dòońee, bí dāá gíti sòoǹ tibɔti gbanti pu.

english_verse: After the service, many Jews and a lot of Gentiles who worshiped God went with them. Paul and Barnabas begged them all to remain faithful to God, who had treated them with undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Binib kɔkɔ yāaǹ ki nín kùǹee, Juuda yab nì binicambi bin fōō Juuda yab marabee tikpil nìn nóó Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi, ní bíǹ bíi sòoǹ ki tìì-bi kunyannyaau, yii bí nīn yú deedee ki ŋúb́ diyimɔɔl din Unimbɔti tīī-bee.

english_verse: The next Sabbath almost everyone in town came to hear the message about the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal fātìi bāańee, kitiŋ yab kɔkɔ ŋman nìn pée kóoǹní ní, kí dāá pīlifì Unimbɔti bɔti.

english_verse: When the Jewish people saw the crowds, they were very jealous. They insulted Paul and spoke against everything he said.
translation_verse: Juuda yab ká kunipaauee, ní ki kíǹ ki bíi ŋáań Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi ipoompoon, ki bí yii Pɔɔl nín sòon̄ tiŋyee kaa sá míǹ, ní ki sìí-u.

english_verse: But Paul and Barnabas bravely said: We had to tell God's message to you before we told it to anyone else. But you rejected the message! This proves that you don't deserve eternal life. Now we are going to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi tùkū-bi ibaamɔn, kaa fāŋkì, yii: «An sá nimbi cee ní ti máaǹ kí péé kí sòoǹ Unimbɔti bɔti. Ama, kii ni nín yíì tibɔti gbanti ki dàkafī yii naa máaǹ dimaŋfal din kaa cáá dikúntilee, an puee ti làá nīn kíǹ ki sòoǹ bin kaa sá Juuda yabee cee ní.

english_verse: The Lord has given us this command, “I have placed you here as a light for the Gentiles. You are to take the saving power of God to people everywhere on earth.”
translation_verse: Kun puee ti-Dindaan nín bí tí ŋá miŋyee dee. Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <M lēē-si á nīn sá ŋwalifi kí cùnnì difiil áli kitiŋgbeennyɔkɔ.>»

english_verse: This message made the Gentiles glad, and they praised what they had heard about the Lord. Everyone who had been chosen for eternal life then put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Bin kaa sá Juuda yabee gbìl̄ mimmee, ní ki bíi fàal̀ ki pàkà ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. Ní bin kɔkɔ nìn sá bin làá ká dimaŋfal din kaa cáá dikúntilee fōō ki kíí.

english_verse: The message about the Lord spread all over this region.
translation_verse: Ní ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi gbītì kitiŋ gbanti kɔkɔn.

english_verse: But the Jewish leaders went to some of the important men in the town and to some respected women who were religious. They turned them against Paul and Barnabas and started making trouble for them. They even chased them out of this part of the country.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab téé binimpukpaambi bin tɔ́ Unimbɔti marabee nì kitiŋ poon yidambi, ní bi yíkì ki páb́ Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi áli ki jìn̄-bi bi-tiŋki pu.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from that place off their feet and went on to the city of Iconium.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi gbáfì bi-taaŋi kpɔŋkpɔm, ní ki búntì Ikooniyum.

english_verse: But the Lord's followers in Antioch were very happy and were filled with the Holy Spirit.
translation_verse: Ama bin nìn fōō Yeesu ki kíí Antiyɔɔsi tiŋkinee nìn gbí dipɔɔpiŋkpaandi nì Circir Fam.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas spoke in the synagogue in Iconium, just as they had done at Antioch, and many Jews and Gentiles put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Ikooniyum tiŋkinee, Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi tí kɔ́ Juuda yab kpafidiikun mbaantiim, ki sòon̄ tiŋan, áli binib tikpil, Juuda yab nì Greeki yab, fōō ki kíí.

english_verse: But the Jews who did not have faith in him made the other Gentiles angry and turned them against the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab bin kaa fōō ki kííyee téé bin kaa sá Juuda yabee bí cùú ŋá Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi tin kaa ŋān̄ee.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas stayed there for a while, having faith in the Lord and bravely speaking his message. The Lord gave them the power to work miracles and wonders, and he showed that their message about his gift of undeserved grace was true.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi kāl̀ ki yúntì Ikooniyum ki sòon̄ ti-Dindaan bɔti, kaa fàŋkí, ní ti-Dindaan yāntì bi ŋáań tidaandi nì maamaacib kí dàkà yii bi nín sòoǹ u-ŋanti puee, an sá ibaamɔn.

english_verse: The people of Iconium did not know what to think. Some of them believed the Jewish group, and others believed the apostles.
translation_verse: Ní kitiŋin yab cúu yākatì mili: biba bí Juuda yab jandi pú, ní bin kíǹee mun bí Yeesu kpambaliŋ jandi pú.

english_verse: Finally, some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, decided to make trouble for Paul and Barnabas and to stone them to death.
translation_verse: Ní Juuda yab nì bin kaa sá Juuda yabee, ki kpáaǹ bi-bɔtiibi, kpáfì ki bíi bɔ́ntí ki là kí sàaǹ-bi, kí yāŋkì-bi ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀.

english_verse: In Lystra there was a man who had been born with paralyzed feet and had never been able to walk.
translation_verse: Ufaliŋfaan ubɔ nìn bí Liista. Bi pée màl̄-uee, u-taaŋi fáká ní waa cōom̀ ki ká.

english_verse: The man was listening to Paul speak, when Paul saw that he had faith in Jesus and could be healed. So he looked straight at the man
translation_verse: Dalba uninjee bíi pílifí Pɔɔl nyɔɔbundee, ní Pɔɔl dū u-nimbikpeeŋu ki báaǹ u-pu, ki béè yii u cáá fookii Unimbɔti pu ki ŋūǹ kí ká dicáaǹdee,

english_verse: and shouted, “Stand up!” The man jumped up and started walking around.
translation_verse: ní u téeń mpɔn yii: «Yīkìí yūĺ mɔ́lmɔl a-taaŋi pu!» Ní u nyīī ki yíkì kùrub ki bíi còom̄.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they yelled out in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have turned into humans and have come down to us!”
translation_verse: Samaa nìn ká min Pɔɔl ŋée, ní bi bíi tátí nì Liikayoonii sooŋyin yii: «Awaa aba kpántì binib ki kpákatìń ti-cee!»

english_verse: The people then gave Barnabas the name Zeus, and they gave Paul the name Hermes, because he did the talking.
translation_verse: Ní bi pú Baarnaabaasi diyindi yii Seeyusi, ní ki pú Pɔɔl mun yii Eermeesi, kun puee úǹ di nìn sòoǹ nì samaa.

english_verse: The temple of Zeus was near the entrance to the city. Its priest and the crowds wanted to offer a sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul. So the priest brought some bulls and flowers to the city gates.
translation_verse: Ní utandaan un nìn tòotī diwaal din bi yíì Seeyusi, di-diiku yú kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋuee, dūń nsupumpukum ki léeǹ inajaa ki cáań kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu, u nì samaa là kí dūú tòotī-bi.

english_verse: When the two apostles found out about this, they tore their clothes in horror and ran to the crowd, shouting:
translation_verse: Yeesu kpambaliŋ Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi gbìl̄ mimmee, an wùn̄-bi, ní bi cátì tiwan tin bi pēēyee ki sáǹ ki nín cá samaayee kansikin ki tátí yii:

english_verse: Why are you doing this? We are humans just like you. Please give up all this foolishness. Turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
translation_verse: «Ti-yab, ba ŋá ní ni ŋáań míǹ? Ti mun pée sá binib kii nimbee ní, tiwumbaantiil. Ti bíi tùkù-ni Tibɔmɔntiil yii ní fá ni-waaŋi gbanti ŋin sá fámee kí nóó Unimbɔti un bée. Úǹ di náań yilpu nì taapu nì tiŋku, nì tin kɔkɔwoooo pée bée.

english_verse: In times past, God let each nation go its own way.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun jítèe, u nìn yāntì ditimbundi kamaa nóó di-saŋŋu.

english_verse: But he showed he was there by the good things he did. God sends rain from heaven and makes your crops grow. He gives food to you and makes your hearts glad.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, u dàkā-ŋi u-laŋŋaŋfitiiku. Di sá yii u yàntī utaa nì, tiwan lòoǹ, tijikaal gbóotí ki tìì-ni dipɔɔpindi.»

english_verse: Even after Paul and Barnabas had said all this, they could hardly keep the people from offering a sacrifice to them.
translation_verse: Mpɔn nì mpɔn ní Yeesu kpambaliŋ dū tibɔti gbanti ki dūu pīiǹ samaa nsan bí taa ŋmā kí tòotī-bi.

english_verse: Some Jewish leaders from Antioch and Iconium came and turned the crowds against Paul. They hit him with stones and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead.
translation_verse: Boonee, Juuda yab biba nyánní Antiyɔɔsi nì Ikooniyum ki ŋúń ki ŋmātiǹ samaa. Bi nìn yáŋkì Pɔɔl ataŋkpee ki fùn̄-u ki cáa bíl̀ kitiŋ boon ŋkpaanceeti, ki dàkafī yii u kpíì.

english_verse: But when the Lord's followers gathered around Paul, he stood up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas went to Derbe. Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Ama Kriisitoo yab dāa dɔ́miń ki māntìi tú-u, ní Pɔɔl yíkì ki nín cá kitiŋin. Kutaa wúntèe, ní u nì Baarnaabaasi búntì Deerbi. Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi nín gítí Antiyɔɔsi Siirii tiŋkin

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas preached the good news in Derbe and won some people to the Lord. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch in Pisidia.
translation_verse: Bi sòon̄ Tibɔmɔntiil kitiŋ gbantin ki yāntì binib tikpil kpántì Kriisitoo yab. Boonee ní bi nín gítiń Liista, Ikooniyum nì Antiyɔɔsi.

english_verse: They encouraged the followers and begged them to remain faithful. They told them, “We have to suffer a lot before we can get into God's kingdom.”
translation_verse: Bi nìn tìì Kriisitoo yab kunyannyaau, ki sáŋkí-bi yii bí nīn pɔ̄ɔntí bi-ba fookii poon, ní ki bí-bi yii: «An sá nì falaakpaan ní tí nín ŋmā kí kɔ́ Unimbɔti Beelin.»

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas chose some leaders for each of the churches. Then they went without eating and prayed that the Lord would take good care of these leaders who had trusted in the Lord.
translation_verse: Bi nìn lēekì bikpilib Kriisitoo nikitil sá kamaa poon. Bi bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ki mēē ki dóòyee, ní ki dū-bi ki ŋá ti-Dindaan un bi fōō ki kííyee ŋaan.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas went on through Pisidia to Pamphylia,
translation_verse: Bi dīń Piisidii puee, ki bāań Paŋfilii.

english_verse: where they preached in the town of Perga. Then they went down to Attalia
translation_verse: Bi sòon̄ Unimbɔti bɔti Peeji ki dóòyee, ní ki nín sìntī Atalii.

english_verse: and sailed to Antioch in Syria. It was there that they had been placed in God's care for the work they had now completed.
translation_verse: Niin ní bi kɔ́ meela ki búntì Antiyɔɔsi, laakin Kriisitoo yab nìn mēē Unimbɔti ń tūtuǹ-bi atuun ŋin bi túńee puee.

english_verse: After arriving in Antioch, they called the church together. They told the people what God had helped them do and how he had made it possible for the Gentiles to believe.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ee ní ki kpáfì Kriisitoo nikitil ki máafì tin kɔkɔwoooo Unimbɔti ŋá ki tīī-bee, nì min ní u pīitì nsan bin kaa sá Juuda yabee kɔkɔ ń fōō kí kííyee.

english_verse: Then they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kāl̀ ki yúntì fiii Kriisitoo yab cee.

english_verse: Some people came from Judea and started teaching the Lord's followers that they could not be saved, unless they were circumcised as Moses had taught.
translation_verse: Bininjab biba nìn nyánní Juudee ki dɔ́miń Antiyɔɔsi, ki kíĺ ki bíi dàkà nnabiyaamu yii: «Ni yaa kaa gíí dikpancandi kii Mooyiisi marau nín lī puee, naa ŋūǹ kí ká difiil.»

english_verse: This caused trouble, and Paul and Barnabas argued with them about this teaching. So it was decided to send Paul and Barnabas and a few others to Jerusalem to discuss this problem with the apostles and the church leaders. The Church Leaders Meet in Jerusalem
translation_verse: Niinee, Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi kaa kíí, ní kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔkpaaŋŋu kɔ́ bi-kansikin. Ní bi bí yii Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi nì Kriisitoo yab biba mun ń jɔ̄m̀ Jeerusaleem Yeesu kpambaliŋ nì bikpilib cee, bí kpèè an bɔti.

english_verse: The men who were sent by the church went through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling how the Gentiles had turned to God. This news made the Lord's followers very happy.
translation_verse: Ní Kriisitoo nikitil nyántì-bi nsanni, ní bi dīń Feenisii nì Samaarii ki máafí bin kaa sá Juuda yabee nín kpántì bi-bimbim ki fōō Yeesu ki kíí puee. Niinee ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ Kriisitoo nikitil kɔkɔ.

english_verse: When the men arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, including the apostles and the leaders. They told them everything God had helped them do.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee, ní Yeesu kpambaliŋ nì bikpilib nì Kriisitoo nikitil kɔkɔ fōō-bi. Bi nìn máafì Unimbɔti nín dū-bi ki túń atuun puee.

english_verse: But some Pharisees had become followers of the Lord. They stood up and said, “Gentiles who have faith in the Lord must be circumcised and told to obey the Law of Moses.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Fariisab jandi din nìn fōō ki kííyee yíkì, kaa kíí, yii, bi máaǹ kí gīfì dikpancandi bin kaa sá Juuda yabee kí yàntī bí nīn ŋúb́ Mooyiisi marab kí wàatī ní bí nīn nín sá Kriisitoo yab.

english_verse: The apostles and church leaders met to discuss this problem about Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ní Yeesu kpambaliŋ nì bikpilib kpáfì kí kpèè an bɔti.

english_verse: They had talked it over for a long time, when Peter got up and said: My friends, you know that God decided long ago to let me be the one from your group to preach the good news to the Gentiles. God did this so they would hear and obey him.
translation_verse: Bi nìn kpáká ki yúntì, ní Peetroo dāa nín yíkì ki bí yii: «M-nabiyaamu, ni nyí yii, doooo ŋkilkaam ní Unimbɔti lēē-mi ni-kansikin ḿ sòoǹ tibɔmɔntiil kí tīī bin kaa sá Juuda yabee, bí gbìl̄ kí fōō kí kíí.

english_verse: He knows what is in everyone's heart. And he showed he had chosen the Gentiles, when he gave them the Holy Spirit, just as he had given his Spirit to us.
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti un nyí binib pɔbiliŋinee tīī-bi Circir Fam kii timbee, kí dàkà yii u fōō-bi.

english_verse: God treated them in the same way that he treated us. They put their faith in him, and he made their hearts pure.
translation_verse: Waa gāntì timbi nì bíǹ. Bi nín fōō-u ki kííyee ní u ŋá bi-pɔbiliŋ circir.

english_verse: Now why are you trying to make God angry by placing a heavy burden on these followers? This burden was too heavy for us or our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ba pu ní ni cɔ́ŋkí Unimbɔti ki cáá diwaŋgul din ti-naanjab nì timbi ti-ba kaa ŋúń ki túǹee, ki cáa tūntí Kriisitoo yab?

english_verse: But we believe that we will be saved by the gift of undeserved grace from our Lord Jesus Christ, just as the Gentiles are.
translation_verse: An sá nì ti-Dindaan Yeesu ŋanti pu ní ti máká yii ti ká difiil kii bi muee.»

english_verse: Everyone kept quiet and listened as Barnabas and Paul told how God had given them the power to work a lot of miracles and wonders for the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Niinee ní samaa kɔkɔ ŋmíl̀, ní ki kíǹ ki bíi pílifí Baarnaabaasi nì Pɔɔl nín bíi máafí Unimbɔti nín nìn dī bi-pu ki ŋáaǹ tidaandi nì maamaacib bin kaa sá Juuda yabee kansikinee.

english_verse: After they had finished speaking, James said: My friends, listen to me!
translation_verse: Bi sòon̄ ki dóòyee, ní Yakubu fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki bí yii: «M-nabiyaamu, pīlifìmaan-mi!

english_verse: Simon Peter has told how God first came to the Gentiles and made some of them his own people.
translation_verse: Siimɔn bàà máafì-ni min ní Unimbɔti nìn kpēē ki lútì doooo ŋkilkaamin bin kaa sá Juuda yabee kansikin bin ń nīn sá u-yabee.

english_verse: “I, the Lord, will return and rebuild David's fallen house. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again.
translation_verse: <Míǹ boonee, m làá dāá gítiń kí fàtīí mā Daafiidi diiku kun nìn lítèe. M làá dāá fàtīí mā u-guŋŋi mɔ́lmɔl,

english_verse: Then other nations will turn to me and be my chosen ones. I, the Lord, say this.
translation_verse: kí ŋmā kí yàntī binib bin kɔkɔ kíǹee ń nyàab̀ man bi-Dindaan, ki kpáaǹ atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ m yíiń ŋí nīn sá m-yabee.

english_verse: And so, my friends, I don't think we should place burdens on the Gentiles who are turning to God.
translation_verse: «Míǹ puee ní man Yakubu ká yii, an kaa máaǹ tí nīn páb́ bin kaa sá Juuda yab ki kpántì bi-ba ki nóó Unimbɔtee.

english_verse: We should simply write and tell them not to eat anything that has been offered to idols. They should be told not to eat the meat of any animal that has been strangled or that still has blood in it. They must also not commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Ama tí ŋmà kí tùkùmaan-bi bí yàntī kí taa ti nín̄ jīǹ tiwan tin bi dū ki tōotì awaayee, kí taa ŋá tilaakpaal, kí taa ŋmɔ́ fatiku, kí taa jī tiwan tin baa lāntì fatiku nyáńee.

english_verse: We must remember that the Law of Moses has been preached in city after city for many years, and every Sabbath it is read in our synagogues. A Letter to Gentiles Who Had Faith in the Lord
translation_verse: Di sá yii, doooo jaanjaan ki dāa dūu sāā díǹ, binib gbíntìi bí ki sòoǹ Mooyiisi marab pu ntimu sá kamaa poon, ki kàaǹ u-gbɔnti akpafidiinni ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa sá kamaa dal.» Kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋmàn̄ bin kaa sá Juuda yab ki fōō ki kííyee

english_verse: The apostles, the leaders, and all the church members decided to send some men to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Silas and Judas Barsabbas, who were two leaders of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Yeesu kpambaliŋ, nì bikpilib, nì Kriisitoo yab kɔkɔ bí yii bi làá lēē bi-kansikin biba kí tɔ̄ Antiyɔɔsi, bi nì Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi. Bin bi lēēyee di sá Juudi un bi nìn yíì Baarsabaasee, nì Siilasi. Bininjab bili gbanti ní nnabiyaamu kɔkɔ nìn tɔ́.

english_verse: They wrote a letter that said: We apostles and leaders send friendly greetings to all of you Gentiles who are followers of the Lord in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
translation_verse: Ní bi tīī-bi kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmàn̄ yii: «Timbi ni-nabiyaamu Yeesu kpambaliŋ nì bikpilib jáamiń nimbi nnabiyaamu mun kaa sá Juuda yab ki bí Antiyɔɔsi nì Siirii nì Siilisiiyee.

english_verse: We have heard that some people from here have terribly upset you by what they said. But we did not send them!
translation_verse: Ti gbìl̄ yii ti-yab biba dɔ́miń ni-cee ki sòon̄ nì ni tibɔti, ki yāntì ni bākatì nì ni-ba, ki bíil̀ ni-pɔbiliŋ. Ti mun kaa túnní-bi ni-cee.

english_verse: So we met together and decided to choose some men and to send them to you along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul.
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní ti mun sòon̄ ki kpáfì ki lēē binib biba ki dū-bi ki túnní ni-cee, bi nì Baarnaabaasi nì Pɔɔl, ti-nabineeŋkaamu,

english_verse: These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: binib bin dū bi-ba ki tīī ŋkúm ti-Dindaan Yeesu Kriisitoo yindi puee.

english_verse: We are also sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things that we are writing.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ní ti dū binib bili nee, Juudi nì Siilasi ki túnní ni-cee, bí sòoǹ ni-nimbiin tibɔbaantiil gbanti pu.

english_verse: The Holy Spirit has shown us that we should not place any extra burden on you.
translation_verse: Min ŋān̄ Circir Fam cee ki kpáaǹ ti mun ceeyee di sá tí taa ti dū awaŋgul aba kí túń-ni, an yaa kaa tin sá tin máaǹ ní ŋée.

english_verse: But you should not eat anything offered to idols. You should not eat any meat that still has the blood in it or any meat of any animal that has been strangled. You must also not commit any terrible sexual sins. If you follow these instructions, you will do well. We send our best wishes.
translation_verse: Tíǹ di sá yii ni máaǹ kí yíí kí taa ti ŋmɔ́ tiwaatootinan, kí taa ŋmɔ́ fatiku, kí taa ŋmɔ́ tiwan tin kpíì baa lāntì fatiku nyáńee, kí taa ŋá tilaakpaal. Min ŋān̄ ki tīī-nee di sá ní kòò tiwan gbanti. Ní nīn bí tiŋan!»

english_verse: The four men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Then they called the church members together and gave them the letter.
translation_verse: Niinee ní binib bin bi túee búntì Antiyɔɔsi. Bi bàn̄ee ki kpáfì Kriisitoo yab ki dū kugbɔŋu ki tīī-bi.

english_verse: When the letter was read, everyone was pleased and greatly encouraged.
translation_verse: Bi kàan̄ kugbɔŋuee ki dóòyee, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ báà ŋma, kun puee kugbɔŋuee cáań-bi dipɔɔsɔŋkil.

english_verse: Judas and Silas were prophets, and they spoke a long time, encouraging and helping the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Juudi nì Siilasi mun nìn sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi, ní ki sòon̄ tibɔti tikpil ki sɔ̄ŋkì nnabiyaamu pɔbiliŋ, ní an kútì-bi mpɔn.

english_verse: The men from Jerusalem stayed on in Antioch for a while. And when they left to return to the ones who had sent them, the followers wished them well.
translation_verse: An dāa ŋmāntì ŋyunti ŋubɔee, ní nnabiyaamu mun cee bi cūtèe kāaǹ-bi nì dipɔɔpindi, ki yāntì bi nín gítiń bin túnní-bee cee. [

english_verse: But Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached about the Lord. Paul and Barnabas Go Their Separate Ways
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi gbíntì Antiyɔɔsi bi nì binib tikpil bí ki sòoǹ ki dàkà ti-Dindaan bɔti. Pɔɔl nì Baarnaabaasi cúu yākatì tɔbin

english_verse: Sometime later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let's go back and visit the Lord's followers in the cities where we preached his message. Then we will know how they are doing.”
translation_verse: Iyunti iba jítì boonee, ní Pɔɔl bí Baarnaabaasi yii: «Yàntī tí gítí ntimu mun poon ti nìn sòon̄ ti-Dindaan bɔtee kí màntì ti-nabiyaamu pu kí kpèè yii bi bí mana.»

english_verse: Barnabas wanted to take along John, whose other name was Mark.
translation_verse: Ní Baarnaabaasi bàà là bí kpáaǹ Yoowaneesi un bi yíì Maarkee,

english_verse: But Paul did not want to, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had stopped working with them.
translation_verse: ní Pɔɔl kaa nìn kíí yii, baa ŋūǹ kí kpáaǹ unil un nìn dū-bi ki fá doooo Paŋfilii, bi nì u kaa ti nóó ki tūǹ ditundee.

english_verse: Paul and Barnabas argued, then each of them went his own way. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus,
translation_verse: Ní bi nìn kpáká áli an pɔ́ɔkì, ní ki dāa kpáàa dūu yāaǹ tɔbin. Ní Baarnaabaasi yōoǹ Maarki, bi kɔ́ meela ki nín cá Siipiri.

english_verse: but Paul took Silas and left after the followers had placed them in God's care.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl mun lēē Siilasi. Kí wàatī Pɔɔl ń nīn nín cée, nnabiyaamu mēē ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ u-boon.

english_verse: They traveled through Syria and Cilicia, encouraging the churches.
translation_verse: Ní u dī Siirii nì Siilisii timmu, ki mɔ̀tīi kútí Kriisitoo nikitiŋ mpɔn.

english_verse: Paul and Silas went back to Derbe and Lystra, where there was a follower named Timothy. His mother was also a follower. She was Jewish, and his father was Greek.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl bàn̄ Deebi nì Liistee, Kriisitoo yɔu ubɔ nìn bí niin, bi yíì-u Tiimootee. U-na nìn sá Ujuudanimpu ní ki fōō ki kíí, ní u-baa sá Ugreekija.

english_verse: The Lord's followers in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy,
translation_verse: Nnabiyaamu mun nìn bí Liista nì Ikooniyumee nìn sòoǹ kijapaayee pu yii u sá unimɔnti.

english_verse: and Paul wanted him to go with them. But Paul first had him circumcised, because all the Jewish people around there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nìn là Tiimootee ń nīn bí u-ceeyee, ní u kpáaǹ-u. Juuda yab bin nìn kóò niinee puee, u nìn gíí-u dikpancandi, kun puee bi kɔkɔ nìn nyí yii Tiimootee baa sá Ugreekija.

english_verse: As Paul and the others went from city to city, they told the followers what the apostles and leaders in Jerusalem had decided, and they urged them to follow these instructions.
translation_verse: Ntimu mun kɔkɔwoooo poon bi jītée, bi sòoǹ ki tùkù Kriisitoo yab yii Yeesu kpambaliŋ nì Jeerusaleem kpilib nín nìn kpáfì ki ká tiŋyee, bí nīn ŋúb́-tì tiŋan.

english_verse: The churches became stronger in their faith, and each day more people put their faith in the Lord. Paul's Vision in Troas
translation_verse: An nìn yāntì Kriisitoo nikitiŋ nìn mɔ̀tīi fòol̄ ki kíikí ní bi-wíiŋŋu gbēentí kutaa sá kamaa. Pɔɔl ká dileedakal Troowaasi tiŋkin

english_verse: Paul and his friends went through Phrygia and Galatia, but the Holy Spirit would not let them preach in Asia.
translation_verse: Circir Fam nìn yíì yii Pɔɔl ń taa sòoǹ Unimbɔti bɔti Asii tiŋkinee, ní bi dūu dī Friijii nì Galaati timmun watil.

english_verse: After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them.
translation_verse: Bi tóob́ Miisii tiŋkee ki bàà mākafì kí cù Bitinii, ama ní Yeesu Fam tí yíì, yii bí taa dī niin.

english_verse: So they went on through Mysia until they came to Troas.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi dūu dī Miisii ki nín sìntī Troowaasi.

english_verse: During the night, Paul had a vision of someone from Macedonia who was standing there and begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
translation_verse: Kunyeeuee ní Unimbɔti ŋúbitì Pɔɔl nimbiliŋ, u ká umaseeduwaanja ubɔ yú ki gbàam̄-u yii: «Dīń Maseeduwaan kí dāá jòoń-ti!»

english_verse: After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there. Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ká mimmee, ní ti béè yii Unimbɔti di yíì-ti tí cùú sòoǹ u-bɔmɔntiiti Maseeduwaan. Dicilpu niinee ní ti bɔ́ntì ki nín cá. Liidiya fōō Yeesu ki kíí Fiiliipi tiŋkin

english_verse: We sailed straight from Troas to Samothrace, and the next day we arrived in Neapolis.
translation_verse: Ti kɔ́ meela ki yíkì Troowaasi, ní ki túĺ dicancaal ki búntì Samootraasi. Kutaa wúntèe, ti nín cá Neeyapooliisi,

english_verse: From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia. We spent several days in Philippi.
translation_verse: ní ki dāa yíkì niin ki búntì Fiiliipi, kitiŋkpaaŋŋi kin bí Maseeduwaan tiŋkin, ki bí Room yab ŋaanee. Ti nìn kāl̀ kitiŋ gbantin iwiŋkaaŋkaa iba.

english_verse: Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came.
translation_verse: Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee, ti nyáń kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu ŋkpin ŋubɔ caŋin, ki nyàab̀ laakin bi kpáfí ki mèé Unimbɔtee. Ti kāl̀ee, ní ki sòon̄ nì binimpoobi bin nìn kpáfì niinee.

english_verse: One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying.
translation_verse: Unimpu ubɔ nìn bí bin nìn bíi pílifée kansikin, bi yíì-u Liidiya. U nìn nyánní Tiyatiir tiŋkin ki sá unyampu ki nyáfí bisatamambi. U nìn tɔ́ Unimbɔti marab, ní ti-Dindaan pīitì u-pɔbil ki yāntì u fōō Pɔɔl bɔti.

english_verse: Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation. Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
translation_verse: Unimpuee yāntì ti fùl̄ u nì u-samaau Unimbɔti nyim. Ní u mēē-ti yii: «Ni yaa lafun nyí yii tiŋman m fōō ti-Dindaan ki kíí, ní dāan̄ kí nīn kóò m-dumpu.» Ní u páb́-ti áli ti lafun cūtì u-dumpu. Bi cúú Pɔɔl nì Siilasi ki tɔ́ sarkan

english_verse: One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners.
translation_verse: Dalba ti nìn cá ŋwimmeem paaŋŋu puee, ti tú uyumbusapɔɔn ubɔ. U nìn cáá arasinii ubɔ u-ni ki wāĺ. An di nìn yì-tì u kāntí animbil tikpil ki cāabìń u-dindambi.

english_verse: The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
translation_verse: Ní usapɔɔnee kíǹ ki nóó ti nì Pɔɔl, ki tátí yii: «Bininjab nee sá yilpu Nimbɔtiu tɔntɔnliibi ní, bi bíi sòoǹ nì ni min ní ni làá dī kí ká difiilee ní!»

english_verse: This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
translation_verse: U dū iwiin tikpil ki nóó-ti ki sòoǹ an bɔti. Pɔɔl dāa gīīyee, ní ki fātìi bí arasiniiyee yii: «Nì Yeesu Kriisitoo yindi pu ní m bí yii á nyā usapɔɔn nee ni.» Ní arasiniiyee kpáàa nyáń niin dicilpu.

english_verse: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
translation_verse: Uyumbuee dindambi ká yii Pɔɔl bíil̀ nsan ŋun pu bi dì ki kāntí animbilee, ní bi cúú u nì Siilasi ki dáaĺ-bi ki cáa cūnnì bikpilib nimbiin laakin kunipaau nìn kpáfée,

english_verse: They are telling us to do things we Romans are not allowed to do.”
translation_verse: Marab bin bi dàkèe, timbi Room yab kaa ŋūǹ kí fōōyaaa, kaa ŋūǹ kí dī-bi mun.»

english_verse: The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip.
translation_verse: Niinee ní kunipaauee kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki kútì bi-pu, ní bi kpáfì Pɔɔl nì Siilasi pu, ní biyidambi dáaĺ Pɔɔl nì Siilasi bɔkutiŋ ki pēetì, ní ki bí yii bí gbá-bi anaalab.

english_verse: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
translation_verse: Bi yāntì bi tāfì-bi míǹ ki dóòyee, ní bi cáá-bi ki tɔ́ sarkan, ní ki bí yii sooja un cí bisarkadambee ń nīn kpèé-bi tiŋan.

english_verse: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
translation_verse: Bi kpáafì soojee míǹ ki dóòyee, ní u fōō-bi ki cáa tɔ́ kusarkadii poon ki bá-bi abaa.

english_verse: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened.
translation_verse: Kunyataasiiu nyɔkɔmee, Pɔɔl nì Siilasi bíi mèé ki gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí Unimbɔti, ní bisarkadambi bin kíǹee bíi pílifí.

english_verse: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
translation_verse: Kpalaa kpalaa niinee, kitiŋ cīŋkì ki kpáaǹ kusarkadii. Dicilpu niinee, mpunyɔmu kɔkɔ cúu pīitì, ní tin bi bóob́ bisarkadambee kɔkɔ cúu bútì.

english_verse: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
translation_verse: Sooja un cí bisarkadambee nín fīntì, mpunyɔmu wāāyee, u dàkafī yii bisarkadambi kɔkɔ sáǹ ki kátì dee, ní u dáaĺ ki fɔ́fì u-tàataajiki kí bàà kpɔ̀ u-ba.

english_verse: But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Pɔɔl téeń mpɔn yii: «Taa kpɔ̀ a-ba! Ti-kɔkɔ sèé doo.»

english_verse: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
translation_verse: Ní soojee bí yii bí pɔ̄ń-u ŋŋmi. Niinee ní u tóotì malaa ki cūtìi gbāaǹ Pɔɔl nì Siilasi nimbiin, tiwun jìkì.

english_verse: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
translation_verse: Ní u cáá-bi ki nyántì mmɔŋki, ní ki bālifì-bi yii: «M-dindambi, m làá ŋá mana ní kí nín ká difiil dee?»

english_verse: They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Fōō ti-Dindaan Yeesu kí kíí, a làá ká difiil, sii nì a-dicaŋku kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi bíi sòoǹ nì u nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí u-dumpuee ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi.

english_verse: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
translation_verse: Ní soojee yōoǹ-bi kunyeeu kukúluu gbanti poon ki fíntì bi-buuŋyi. Niin dicilpu ní bi fùl̄ u nì u-dicaŋku kɔkɔ Unimbɔti nyim.

english_verse: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
translation_verse: Boonee ní u yōoǹ-bi ki cáa jɔ́m̀ u-dumpu yilpu, ní ki ŋá-bi tijin. Ní u nì u-dicaŋku kíǹ ki bí dipɔɔpindin bi nín fōō Unimbɔti ki kííyee pu.

english_verse: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní biyidambee túnní pilisib ń dāá tùkù soojee ú líí binibee.

english_verse: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
translation_verse: Ní soojee cūtìi tùkū Pɔɔl yii: «Biyidambi túnní yii ḿ líí-ni. Míǹ puee, nyā kí nīn cámaan nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.»

english_verse: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl bí pilisibee yii: «Bi cúú timbi bin sá Room tindambiyaamuee, kaa sòon̄ ti-bɔti ki ká ti-bɔkpil ní ki gbáń-ti samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin ki cáań-ti ki pīiǹ kudii. Ní kɔŋkɔnnee, bi là kí báĺ soooo kí nyāntí-taaa? Ti yíì kpataaa, see biyidambi bi-ba ń dāan̄ kí nyāntí-ti!»

english_verse: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
translation_verse: Pilisib cáá dinyɔɔbundee ki fātìi bàn̄ biyidambee cee. Bi nín gbìl̄ yii njapaamu gbanti sá Room tindambiyaamuee, tifaandi kɔ́-bi.

english_verse: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
translation_verse: Ní bi dɔ́miń ki sɔ̄ŋkì bi-pɔbiliŋ ki nín nyántì-bi, ní ki gbāam̀-bi yii bí yīkì kitiŋ gbanti poon.

english_verse: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
translation_verse: Bi nyáń kusarkadiinee, ní ki cūtìi kɔ́ Liidiya cee ki ká nnabiyaamu ki kútì-bi tibɔti, ní ki nín yíkì niin.

english_verse: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nì Siilasi dī Aŋfiipooliisi pú ki cūtìi jítì Apooloonii, ní ki nín bàn̄ Teesalooniiki. Juuda yab nìn tí cáá niin kukpafidii.
