english_verse: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nìn kɔ́ ki bíi dàkà kii u nín pée ŋáań puee, ki ŋá nnyɔmu muta. Kinyɔŋ sá kamaa poonee, u nìn cá kukpafidiin ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal ki sòoǹ nì bi,

english_verse: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
translation_verse: ki kàaǹ ki dàkà-bi Unimbɔti gbɔŋku, laakin an nìn ŋmàn̄ yii Meesiya làá dāá kpú kí dāá fìkitī bitaŋkpiibi kansikinee. Ní u bí-bi yii: «Yeesu un bɔti m sòoǹ-ni nee, úǹ di sá Meesiya.»

english_verse: Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
translation_verse: Juuda yab kansikin biba béè mimmee, ki dū bi-ba ki nákáǹ Pɔɔl nì Siilasi. Míǹ mun ní ki kpáaǹ Greeki yab bin nìn tɔ́ Unimbɔti marabee tikpil, nì binimpugaakaabee tikpil mun nìn dū bi-ba ki nákáǹ-bi.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab ŋá ipoompoon ki cūtì kitiŋin ki nyàabìń anileen ŋin còom̄ adan puee ki kpáfì kunipaau, ki cáań fìkil fikil kitiŋ poon. Dinikitilee yíkìi cūtì Jasɔn dumpu kí nyàabìń Pɔɔl nì Siilasi kí cáań samaa nimbiin bí bàlifì-bi tibɔti.

english_verse: But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here,
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Jasɔn dumpu, kaa ká-bee, ní ki cúuń Jasɔn nì nnabiyaamu mubɔ ki cáań bikpilib nimbiin, ní ki tátí yii: «Bitiŋwiiliibi bin yìiǹ duulinya kɔkɔnee bāań ti-mun cee doo.

english_verse: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
translation_verse: Jasɔn fōō-bi bi kóò u-dumpu. Binib gbanti kaa fàŋkí gɔminakpaan Seesaar marab, kun puee bi cáá yii ubɔti ubɔ gíti bí, bi yíì-u Yeesu.»

english_verse: The officials and the people were upset when they heard this.
translation_verse: An bɔtee bíil̀ samaa kɔkɔ pɔbiliŋ ki kpáaǹ bikpilib,

english_verse: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
translation_verse: ní bikpilibee gíí Jasɔn nì bin kíǹee dipɔŋkpaandi bí pà kí wàatī bí nín líí-bi. Pɔɔl nì Siilasi bí Beeree

english_verse: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Kunyeeu mɔ́ kpalaayee, nnabiyaamu yāntì Pɔɔl nì Siilasi búntì Beeree. Bi bàn̄ niinee, ní ki nín cá Juuda yab kpafidiikun.

english_verse: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
translation_verse: Binib gbanti nìn cáá mbimbimɔntiim ki jítiǹ Teesalooniiki yab, kun puee bíǹ nìn fōō Unimbɔti bɔti mmɔntiimin. Bi nìn kpátí Unimbɔti gbɔŋku ŋwiin kamaa ki kpèé yii tin Pɔɔl sòoǹ nì bee yaa sá ibaamɔn.

english_verse: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
translation_verse: An pu ní bi-kansikin kunipaau, ki kpáaǹ Greeki pijab nì bininjab tikpil, nìn fōō ki kíí.

english_verse: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab bin bí Teesalooniikee nín béè yii Pɔɔl tí bíi sòoǹ Unimbɔti bɔti Beereeyee, ní bi dɔ́miń niin ki cáań fìkil fikil kitiŋin, ki yāntì samaa pɔbiliŋ bíil̀.

english_verse: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
translation_verse: Niinee ní nnabiyaamu yāntì Pɔɔl búntì tiŋku caŋin. Siilasi nì Tiimootee, bíǹ nìn gbíntìi bí Beeree niin.

english_verse: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
translation_verse: Bin nìn céeǹ Pɔɔlee nìn cáá-u ki cūnnì áli Ateeni ki fàtīi gítińee, ní Pɔɔl bí yii bi yaa bàn̄ee bí tùkù Siilasi nì Tiimootee yii bí kíntiń-u malaa. Pɔɔl bí Ateeni

english_verse: While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Pɔɔl nìn kā Ateeni ki cí-bee, an nìn páb́-u tikpil, kun puee kitiŋ gbanti sá awaa ŋmaniŋma ní.

english_verse: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
translation_verse: Ní u kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì Juuda yab nì bin nìn tɔ́ Unimbɔti marabee kukpafidiin, ní ki sòoǹ ŋwiin kamaa kinyɔŋin, laakin binib kpáfée.

english_verse: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
translation_verse: Anikiti ali aba nì Pɔɔl nìn bíi sòoǹ. Binib gbantee nìn nyí kugbɔŋu tiŋan. Dinikitil diba sá Eepiikuur yab, ní din kíǹee sá Stooyiiki yab. Ní biba bí yii: «Unifan nee kalin sòoǹ ba yati ní?» Ní bin kíǹee bí yii: «U máaǹ ki làá nīn sá un sòoǹ inimbɔticaan bɔtee ní.» Kun pu bi lì mimmee di sá yii Pɔɔl nìn bíi sòoǹ Yeesu nì difìkitil bɔti pu.

english_verse: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
translation_verse: Ní bi yōoǹ Pɔɔl ki cūnnì kitiŋ yidambi nimbiin, ní ki bí-u yii: «A-dàkatam nee sá tibɔcan, mimmee, a ŋūǹ kí tùkù-ti tibɔcan tin a dàkà nee taapuɔɔɔ?

english_verse: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
translation_verse: Kun puee tin ti pée gbìl̀ a sòoǹee, taa láá gbìl̄-tì ki ká dalba dalba. Míǹ puee, ti bàà là kí béé tibɔti gbanti nín sá puee.» -

english_verse: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Ateeni yab nì binicambi bin bí bi-kansikinee yati di nìn pée sá bí nīn kā ki pílifí tibɔcan ŋma. -

english_verse: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl yáatìi yúl̀ biyidambi nimbiin ki bí yii: «Ateeni yab, m ká yii, binib kansikinee, nimbi di sá bin nóó inimbɔti tiŋanee.

english_verse: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m nín jītí ni-tiŋki nee poonee, m ká tiwan tin ní ni jáaḿee. Áli gba, m kpáàa ká nsaraafan ŋun pu bi ŋmàn̄ yii: <Unimbɔti un baa nyée.> Un ni jáaḿ kaa nyée, úǹ pu ní m dɔ́miń kí sòoǹ nì ni.

english_verse: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
translation_verse: Úǹ di sá Unimbɔti un náań duulinya nì tin kɔkɔwoooo pée bée, ki sá yilpu nì taapu Dindaan. Waa kóò adiin ŋin binib cáá bi-ŋalii ki māāyee ni,

english_verse: He doesn't need help from anyone. He gives life, breath, and everything else to all people.
translation_verse: kaa nyàab̀ binib tūtuntam báà an yaa pée sá tintee. An kaa sá úǹ di tìì báà ŋma dimaŋfal nì ŋfam nì tikɔkɔɔɔ?

english_verse: From one person God made all nations who live on earth, and he decided when and where every nation would be.
translation_verse: Úǹ di dī unibaanti pu ki nyántì anibul ki gbéeǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu, ki síiǹ atimbun kɔkɔ nì ŋi-kɔŋkooŋyi nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
translation_verse: U ŋá míǹ ki là yii bin yaa táfí ki nyàab̀ úǹ Unimbɔtee yaa táá ŋmā kí ká-u. Ama Unimbɔti gbanti kaa dátiǹ-ti,

english_verse: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
translation_verse: di sá yii: <Úǹ pu ní ti fòotī ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní ki bí.> Kii ni-laŋgaaliibi biba nín gāā puee, yii: <Ti mun pée sá u-biyaamu ní.>

english_verse: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
translation_verse: Kii ti nín sá u-biyaamu puee, taa máaǹ kí dàkafì yii Unimbɔti sá kii awaa ŋin binib dākafì ki dū bi-ciiŋyi ki dū sindaariyab nì animbil ki mɔ́ɔ́yee, àá kii tiwaŋkpítikaalee.

english_verse: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti kaa dū ŋyunti ŋun binib kaa nìn nyí tibee ki dūu ŋá tibɔti. Míǹ puee ní kɔŋkɔnnee u bíi tùkù ajan kɔkɔ nib yii bi-kɔkɔ máaǹ kí fá bi-kpitii.

english_verse: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
translation_verse: Di sá yii u yóoǹ ŋwiin ŋubɔ ŋun ní u làá yàntī Yeesu ń sòoǹ duulinya kɔkɔ bɔti nì ibaamɔnee, kun puee uninja gbanti ní u fīkitì bitaŋkpiibi kansikin ki dàkā-ti kudaaŋŋu páaa yii úǹ ní u lēē.»

english_verse: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
translation_verse: Bi nín gbìl̄ u sòon̄ bitaŋkpiibi fìkititam puee, ní biba bíi bèel̄-u, ní bin kíǹee bí yii: «Dalba á dāá gíti sòoǹ tibɔti gbanti pu.»

english_verse: When Paul left the council meeting,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Pɔɔl yíkì bi-kansikin ki nyáń.

english_verse: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, binib biba nìn fōō ki kíí, ki dū bi-ba ki nákáǹ Pɔɔl. Uyidaan un bi yíì Deeniiyee nì unimpu ubɔ bi yíì-u Damariisi nìn bí bi-kansikin. Biba mun nìn kútì.

english_verse: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee, Pɔɔl dāa yíkì Ateeni ki búntì Kɔranti.

english_verse: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
translation_verse: Niin ní u ká uninja ubɔ, bi yíì-u Akiilasi, u sá Ujuudaja ní bi màl̄-u Pɔnti. U nìn nyánní Italii ki bāań kpalaa u nì u-nimpuu Priisiil, kun puee gɔminakpaan Kloodi nìn bí yii Juuda yab kɔkɔ ń nyā Room tiŋkin. Niinee bíǹ nì Pɔɔl dūu píí tɔb kubɔɔtiiu.

english_verse: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
translation_verse: Kii bi-kɔkɔ nín nìn tūǹ ditumbaantiil puee, ní u kɔ́ bi-cee, ní bi kpáfì ki tūǹ ditundi dicilpu. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn sá bitantiluliibi ní.

english_verse: Every Sabbath, Paul went to the synagogue. He spoke to Jews and Gentiles and tried to win them over.
translation_verse: Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal sá kamaayee, Pɔɔl nìn pɔ̄ɔntí ní ki sòoǹ kukpafidiin kí ŋmā Juuda yab nì Greeki yab.

english_verse: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Siilasi nì Tiimootee dāa nyánní Maseeduwaan ki bàn̄ee, ní Pɔɔl dū u-yuntiŋu kɔkɔ ki kíǹ ki cáa sòoǹ Unimbɔti bɔti, ki tùkù Juuda yab yii Yeesu di sá Meesiya.

english_verse: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab kaa nìn là min u sòoǹee, ní ki bíi sìí-u. Ní u gbáfì u-bɔkutiŋ, ki bí-bi yii: «Ni-busuu ń gítí ni-pu! Man nyáń ni-bɔtin. Kɔŋkɔnnee m làá nīn cá bin kaa sá Juuda yabee cee.»

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: U nìn yíkì niin, ki cūtìi kɔ́ uninja un nìn tɔ́ Unimbɔti marabee dumpu, bi yíì-u Titiyusi Justuusi. U-dumpu nìn nákáǹ kukpafidii.

english_verse: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
translation_verse: Ní Kriisipusi kukpafidii kpiliu nì u-dicaŋku kɔkɔ fōō ti-Dindaan ki kíí. Kɔranti yab bin nìn gbìl̄ Pɔɔl nyɔɔbundee tikpil nìn fòol̄ ki kíikí ki yàntī bi fùul̀-bi Unimbɔti nyim.

english_verse: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
translation_verse: Kunyeeu kubɔee ti-Dindaan nyántì u-ba ki dàkā Pɔɔl ní ki bí-u yii: «Á taa fàŋkì, ama nín̄ sòoǹ kí taa gbèen̄,

english_verse: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
translation_verse: di sá yii m bí a-cee. Ubɔ kaa làá sútiń kí pìlīń-si ní kaa nín ŋá-si tikpitil. Kun puee, m cáá binib tikpil kitiŋ nee poon.»

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nìn kāl̀ bi-kansikin dibindi diba nì dijandi, ki dàkà-bi Unimbɔti bɔti.

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Bi kāaǹ Galiyɔn gɔmina Akaayi tiŋkinee, ní Juuda yab kpáfì ki yíkìi cúú Pɔɔl, ki cáa cūnnì Galiyɔn nimbiin,

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: ní ki bí yii: «Unil nee yàntī bi nōotí Unimbɔti mbamin, min ní marab kaa lēe.»

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Pɔɔl bàà làá wàan̄ u-nyɔkɔ kí sòoǹee, ní gɔmina Galiyɔn bí Juuda yab yii: «Juuda yab, u yaa bàà ŋá tibɔkpitil tiba àá digaŋgam ubɔ, m bàà ŋūǹ kí pīlifiǹ-ni.

english_verse: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
translation_verse: Ama an yaa sá yii ni yaa bíi kpákà nimbi ni-ba marab pu tibɔti tiba nì ayin aba puee, m yíì, maa làá sòoǹ an bɔti. Nimbi ni-ba ń kpèè-tì!»

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Ní u jìn̄-bi ki nyántì.

english_verse: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Ní bi-kɔkɔ cúú Sɔsteen kukpafidii kpiliu, ki bíi gbáà gɔmina nimbiin. Ní gɔmina kaa kpáàa fātìi tɔ́. Pɔɔl gítìń Antiyɔɔsi

english_verse: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl gíti kāl̀ Kɔranti ki yúntì fiii. Boonee, u dāa yíkì nnabiyaamu cee ki kɔ́ meela ki búntì Siirii, u nì Priisiil nì Akiilasi. Kí wàatī ú nín yīkì Saŋkireeyee, Pɔɔl nìn kōol̀ diyibaakpandi kí dàkà yii u pōoǹ kí ŋá tiba kí tīī Unimbɔti.

english_verse: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Eefeesee, ní bin nì Pɔɔl nìn nóóyee gbíntì niin. Pɔɔl nìn kɔ́ kukpafidiin ki tí bíi sòoǹ nì Juuda yab.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Binib gbanti nìn bíi mèé-u yii ú gíti kàl̄ iwiŋkaaŋkaa bi-cee. Ní waa kíí.

english_verse: He told them goodbye and said, “If God lets me, I will come back.”
translation_verse: U làá yīkì bi-kansikinee, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Unimbɔti yaa là, m dāa gítiń ni-cee dalba.»

english_verse: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
translation_verse: U yíkì Eefeesee, ki kɔ́ meela ki kpákatì Seesaaree, ní ki jɔ́m̀ Jeerusaleem ki jáam̀ Kriisitoo yab, ní ki fātìi sīntìń Antiyɔɔsi.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: U kāl̀ ŋyunti ŋubɔee, ní ki yíkìi cūtì Galaati nì Friijii timmu kɔkɔn, ki tìì Kriisitoo yab kɔkɔ kunyannyaau. Apooloosi cūtì Eefeesi nì Kɔranti

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Ujuudaja ubɔ nìn bí, bi yíì-u Apooloosi. Bi nìn màl̄-u Aleekisandirii, ní u dɔ́miń Eefeesi. Uninja gbantee nìn sá un nyí ki sòoǹ tiŋanee, ki nyí Unimbɔti gbɔŋku mun tikpil.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Bi nìn dàkā-u ti-Dindaan bɔti, ní u mun cáa sòoǹ deedee ki dàkà Yeesu bɔti nì kunyannyaau. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Yoowaneesi nyiŋfàltam baba ní u nìn pée nyí.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: Ní u mɔ̄tìi bíi sòoǹ ki cántí-bi kukpafidiin. Priisiil nì Akiilasi gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki yōoǹ-u ki cáa cūnnì bi-cee, ki mɔ̄tìi dàkā-u Unimbɔti saŋŋu páaa.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Ní Apooloosi lēē yii u làá cù Akaayi. Niinee, nnabiyaamu tīī-u kunyannyaau ki ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī Kriisitoo yab bin bí lapuee, yii bí fōō-u tiŋan. U nín bàn̄ niinee, nì Unimbɔti pɔŋŋu puee, u tútúǹ bin fōō Yeesu ki kííyee tikpil.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: Di sá yii, u nì Juuda yab nìn kpákà samaa nimbiin, ní u nìn sòoǹ ki líikí-bi, ki dàkà-bi Unimbɔti gbɔŋku poon yii Yeesu di sá Meesiya.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Apooloosi nìn bí Kɔrantee, ní Pɔɔl dīń kitiŋ kin bí ajoon puee ki bāań Eefeesi. Niin ní u ká Kriisitoo yab biba,

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: ki bālifì-bi yii: «Ni nín fōō ki kííyee, ni fōō Circir Famaaa?» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Timbi kaa kpáàa gbìl̄ bi sòon̄ Unimbɔti Fam pu gba ní kaa nín fōō-mì.»

english_verse: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl bālifì-bi yii: «Mimmee, dinyiŋfaldi dilal ní bi fùl̄-ni ní?» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Yoowaneesi yal ní ti fùl̄.»

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Pɔɔl kíí-bi yii: «Yoowaneesi nyiŋfàltam sá ki tīī bin fá bi-kpitiiyee ní. U nìn tùkù samaa yii bí dāá fōō un làá dāá dāan̄ úǹ boonee kí kíí: an dàkà yii Yeesu.»

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ní ki yāntì bi fùl̄-bi nnyim ti-Dindaan Yeesu yindi pu.

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl dū u-ŋalii ki páaǹ bi-pu. Niinee, Circir Fam kpákatìń bi-pu, ní bi kíǹ ki bíi sòoǹ isooncaan ki nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Bininjab gbanti nìn bàn̄ binib saalaa nì bili nyɔkɔm.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Niinee ní Pɔɔl ŋá iŋmal ita ki kíǹ ki bí kukpafidiin ki mɔ̀tīi sòoǹ ki cántí-bi Unimbɔti Beel bɔti, án nín làá ŋá pu ní ú ŋmā-bee.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Ama biba nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ, kaa là kí fōō kí kíí, ní ki bí ki sòoǹ ki bíiĺ ti-Dindaan bɔti samaa nimbiin. Niinee ní Pɔɔl yíkì bi-cee, ki kpáaǹ Kriisitoo yab ki kākatì ní ki kíǹ ki dàkà-bi Unimbɔti bɔti ŋwiin kamaa Tranusi sukuliun.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: U nìn dàkā-bi míǹ áli abin ali. An di yāntì Juuda yab nì Greeki yab bin nìn kóò Asii tiŋkinee kɔkɔ ŋúń ki gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan bɔti. Sikeefa jipɔmbi bɔti

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn dì Pɔɔl pu ki ŋáań maamaacikpaambi.

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Pɔɔl ŋaabikaaa, u-wampeeŋkaati tiba ní bi yaa nìn cáań ki gbēē bibunliibee, iween nìn càntī-bi, ní arasiniibi mun nìn nyēē bi-pu.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Binyɔɔdambi biba nìn bí ki sá Juuda yab, ki yìiǹ ki cāantí bin cáá arasiniibee. Bi mun nìn mākaǹ kí yíiń ti-Dindaan Yeesu yindi kí jà arasiniibi. Bi nìn lī yii: «Nì Yeesu un pu Pɔɔl sòoǹee yindi pu ní m bí yii ní nyā.»

english_verse: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
translation_verse: Sikeefa, Juuda yab saraaŋakpiliu ubɔ jipɔmbi biluli di nìn ŋáań mimmee.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Ní arasiniiyee fātìi kíí-bi yii: «Man nyí Yeesu ki nyí Pɔɔl mun. Kin ni mun fáà, ni sá bilab?»

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Niinee, uninja un pu arasinii kēe ŋàan̄ ki cìb̄-bi, ní ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ bi-kɔkɔ, ki yāntì bi sáǹ mpɔn ki nyáń dicindi gbantin nì dicancaŋgbeel nì tiweendi.

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Juuda yab nì Greeki yab bin nìn kóò Eefeesee kɔkɔ nín gbìl̄ mimmee, ní tifaandi kɔ́-bi ní bi mɔ̀tīi tìì ti-Dindaan Yeesu yindi tinyool.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Bin nìn fōō ki kííyee tikpil nìn dòoń samaa nimbiin ki bìitī tin bi nìn ŋáaǹee pu.

english_verse: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan bɔti gbītì an kɔkɔ ki báaǹ inyaan mpɔn. Fìkil fikil kɔ́ Eefeesi tiŋkin

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Tíǹ jítèe, ní Pɔɔl bíi màkà yii u làá dī Maseeduwaan nì Akaayi pú kí cù Jeerusaleem. U lī mimmee, ní ki bí yii, u yaa bàn̄ niinee, see ú cù Room mun.

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: Ní u dū binib bili bin nìn bí u-cee ki tútúǹ-uee, Tiimootee nì Eeraasiti, ki dūu tú Maseeduwaan. Úǹ u-ba nìn gbíntìi kāl̀ Asii tiŋkin fiii.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti gbantee fìkil fikil ubɔ nìn kɔ́ní Eefeesi tiŋkin ti-Dindaan saŋŋu pu.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Di sá yii uninja ubɔ nìn bí, bi yíì-u Deemeetriyusi. Kijapaayee nìn cáá tikúti ki mɔ́ɔ̀ ŋwaadibiyaamu ki cáa nántíǹ diwaal Ariteemiisi diiku, ki nìn tìì u-tɔntɔnliibi bi mun ń nīn ŋáań ki kāntí ipaati tiŋan.

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: Ní u kpáfì u-tɔntɔnliibi nì bin kɔkɔ pée tūǹ an tundee, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ti-yab, kéè, ni-kɔkɔ nyí yii ti-tundi nee di yì ti-jimaa!

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Kéè, ni ká ki gbìl̄ Asii timmu kɔkɔn, an kaa sá Eefeesi ŋmaniŋma, Pɔɔl gbanti nín ŋúń ki dáaliń binib tikpil ki gíiǹní u-jandi pueeyaa! Pɔɔl ubaantee cáá yii inimbɔti in binib dū bi-ŋalii ki ŋée kaa sá inimbɔti.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: An sá mbusu ní, kun puee án làá yàntī baa làá nīn gíti tɔ́ ti-tundi nee. Áli gba, baa dāa gíti dù diwaakpaandi Ariteemiisi diiku kí yíiń tiba, ní diwaakpaandi gbanti din Eefeesi tiŋki nì duulinya timmu kɔkɔ nóóyee làá dāá ŋá fám!»

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ní ki fōō diŋuul, ní ki kíǹ ki bíi tátí yii: «Eefeesi yab waal Ariteemiisi di sá diwaakpaandi!»

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Niinee ní dipɔɔbiildi kɔ́ kitiŋ kɔkɔn. Ní bi cúú Maseeduwaan yab Gaayusi nì Ariistaarki bin nì Pɔɔl nìn nōotée, ki yōoǹ-bi ki cáa cūnnì laakin samaa nìn kpáfée.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl bàà nìn là kí cù niin samaa cee, ní Kriisitoo yab yíì.

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: Áli u-bɔɔbi biba bin nìn sá Eefeesi kpilibee nìn túnní u-cee, bí gbàam̀-u ú taa dāan̄ samaayee kansikin.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Dikpafil gbanti poonee, biba nìn tátí ki sòoǹ tiba, ní biba mun ŋúb́ tiba. An ŋá fìkil fikil, ní binib tikpil kaa kpáàa nyí kun pu ní bi baasii kpáfèe.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Kunipaauee kansikinee biba nìn cūtìi ká Aleekisandir, ní Juuda yab téé-u ki nyántìń ú sòoǹ. Ní Aleekisandir yōoǹ ŋŋal ki téefì-bi bí ŋmīĺ ú bàà sòoǹ nì samaa.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Ama bi nín dāa dūu béè yii u sá Ujuudajee, ní bi-kɔkɔ kpáfì ki tátí dicilpu áli tikúmɔn tili nyɔkɔm, ní ki cáá yii: «Eefeesi yab waal Ariteemiisi di sá diwaakpaandi!»

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Niinee ní ukpil ubɔ yāntì samaa ŋmíl̀, ní u bí yii: «Eefeesi yab, ŋma di kaa nyí yii Eefeesi tiŋki yab di kpèé diwaakpaandi Ariteemiisi din nyánní yilpu ki lítèe nì di-diiku?

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí kpákáǹ an bɔti. Míǹ puee, kàl̄maan soooo, taa jìkìmaan tibɔti nee pu.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Binib bin ni cáań nee, baa ŋá digaŋgam ubɔ kuwaadiin, kaa ti sīī ti-waal mun.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, Deemeetriyusi nì bitɔntɔnliibi bin bí u-ceeyee, ubɔ yaa ŋá-bi tibee, iwiin in bi sòoǹ tibɔtee bí, bibɔsoonliibi mun bí! Bí yíiń tɔb ibeeyiin kí sòoǹ.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: An yaa tí sá bikpilib bɔtaaa, ní bí kpāfì kí kpèè, kii bi nín pée ŋáań puee.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Ama tin bāań díǹ neeyee làá yàntī bí lì yii ti là kí bīil̀ gɔmina. Di sá yii taa ŋūǹ kí lì kí dàkà kun pu ní ti kpáfì dooyee taapu.»

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: U lī mimmee, ní ki bí yii báà ŋma ń nīn kùǹ.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Fìkil fikilee jítèe, ní Pɔɔl yíiń Kriisitoo yab, ki tīī-bi kunyannyaau, ní ki kāaǹ-bi, ní ki yíkì bi-kansikin ki búntì Maseeduwaan.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: U dī Maseeduwaan tiŋgbammun, ki sòon̄ nì Kriisitoo yab ki sáŋkí-bi tikpil ki wāatì ní ki nín bàn̄ Greeki tiŋkin.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: U nìn ŋá niin iŋmal ita ní. Ŋyunti ŋun u bɔ́ntì ki làá kɔ́ meela kí nīn cá Siiriiyee, ní u béè yii Juuda yab sòon̄ ki bɔ́ntì nsàmbiyaamu mun pu bi làá dī kí kpɔ̀-uee. Niinee ní u fātìi dūu dīń Maseeduwaan pú.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Bin nìn nóó-uee di sá: Sɔpateer, Piirusi jipɔɔn un nìn sá Beereeyee, nì Ariistaarki nì Seekundusi, bíǹ sá Teesalooniiki yab, Gaayusi un sá Deebee, nì Tiimootee nì Tiisiiki nì Troofiim, bíǹ nyánní Asii.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Bíǹ kɔkɔ nìn līntì ki cūtìi cíitì-ti Troowaasi.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Iwiin in poon Juuda yab ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee boonee, timbi kɔ́nní meela ki yíkìń Fiiliipi tiŋkin, ki ŋá iwiin iŋmoo ní ki nín bàn̄ bi-cee Troowaasi, ní ki ŋá iwiin iluli niin. Pɔɔl taaluŋkikaal Troowaasi tiŋkin

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Kinyɔŋ wimpeepeekaaŋu dalee, ti nìn kpáfì kí jī ti-Dindaan jikaati, ní Pɔɔl kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì bin kpáfì niinee. U nìn sòon̄ ki yúntì tikpil, áli kunyataasiiu tikúti saalaa nì tili, kun puee an nìn sá kutaa ń wúntí ú yīkì ní.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Fitilab nìn wīikí diditɔntɔkɔl din poon ti nìn kpáfèe ni tikpil.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Unaacimpɔɔn ubɔ nìn bí niin, bi yíì-u Eetiiki. U nìn kā diditɔntɔkɔl tɔkɔlau nyɔɔgbandi pu. Ŋyunti ŋun Pɔɔl gbíntìi bíi sòoǹ nì bi ki cée, ní ŋgeem cúú-u. U bíi gèeǹ tikpil tikpilee, ní ki dāa kpáàa nyánní diditɔntɔkɔl yilpu kuditataatiiu poon ki lítì kitiŋ. Bi pée yōoǹ-uee, u kpíì ní.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní Pɔɔl kpákatìń ki bōoǹ ki yōoǹ-u ní ki bí yii: «Ni-pɔbiliŋ ń taa máĺ, kun puee u fātìi jɔ́mìń!»

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Ní u fātìi nín jɔ́ḿ ki cūtìi yākatì kpɔnɔb bi ŋmɔ́, ní u fātìi tí kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì bi áli kutaa nì ku-wuntil, ní boonee u dāa nín yíkì.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Ní bi fātìi gíiǹ unaacimpɔɔnee u-dumpu nì alaafiya, ní an nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ báà ŋma tikpil. Pɔɔl yíkì Troowaasi ki búntì Miilee

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Ní timbi kɔ́ meela ki līntì kí cùú kíntí Pɔɔl Asoosi tiŋkin, kii u nín nìn pée sòon̄ puee, kun puee úǹ làá dāá còomìń ataa pu ní.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: U bāań ki ká-ti Asɔsee, ní ti yōoǹ-u ki nín cáa cá Miitileen.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti nín nìkì. Áli kutaa nì ku-wuntilee ní ti dūu bàn̄ Kiyoo. Ku tí wúntèe ní ti dūu bàn̄ Samɔsi, ní ku gíti tí wúntèe ní ti yúl̀ Troogiliyɔn ní ki nín bàn̄ Miilee.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nìn lēē yii u là kí gɔ́ntí Eefeesi kí taa bīil̀ ŋyunti kitiŋ gbantin. Míǹ pu ní u nìn túĺ dicancaal, án ŋá-u malaa u yaan ŋūǹ, ú bàà nín̄ bí Jeerusaleem Pantikooti wiiŋŋu dal. Pɔɔl kāaǹ Kriisitoo nikitil kpilib bin bí Eefeesee

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl bí Miileeyee, ní ki tú bí cù Eefeesi kí yíiń niin Kriisitoo nikitil kpilib.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Bi bāań u-ceeyee, ní u bí-bi yii: «Kéè, nimbi ni-ba nyí doooo ŋwimpeekaa ŋun m kóoń Asii tiŋkinee m nín bí nì ni baabadal miŋyeeyaa!

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní m nìn sīntiǹ m-ba ki túń ti-Dindaan tundi nì nnyinnyim, ki bí falaabi kansikin kun puee Juuda yab nìn nyàab̀ isan kí kpɔ̀-mi.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ni nyí yii maa nìn bál̀ tin ŋūǹ kí tūtuǹ-nee báà tiba, ki sòoǹ ki dàkà-ni Unimbɔti bɔti laakin binib kpáfée ki kpáaǹ ni-dumpui.

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: M nìn sáŋkí Juuda yab ki kpáaǹ Greeki yab tiŋan, yii bí fá ikpiti, kí fōō ti-Dindaan Yeesu kí kíí kí nóó Unimbɔti.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, m làá nīn cá Jeerusaleem dee kii Unimbɔti Fam nín bí ḿ ŋá puee, kaa nyí tin làá ŋá-mi niinee.

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ama ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon m jītée, Circir Fam tùkù-mi yii sarka nì dinimbinaamandi dɔ̄ ki cí-mi.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Ama, man maŋfal bɔti kaa páb́-mi, a lì kii an kaa sá-mi tiwammɔntiil tibee ní. Tin di páb́-mee di sá ḿ tɔ̄ ditundi din m fōō ti-Dindaan ceeyee: díǹ di sá ḿ sòoǹ Tibɔmɔntiil kí tùkù binib dineendi din Unimbɔti cáá ti-puee.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: «Míǹ puee, nimbi bin cee m jítì ki sòon̄ Unimbɔti Beel pu bɔtee, kɔŋkɔnnee m nyí yii naa làá ti ká-mi.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: An di yì-tì ní m tùkù-ni an bɔti díǹ kí síiń, boonee, ubɔ yaa láa gíti wáŋkèe, an kaa dāa gíti sá m-cee.

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m tùkū-ni kaa bál̀-ni Unimbɔti nín là kí dāá ŋá min miŋyee kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, ní kpèèmaan ni-ba tiŋan, kí kpèèmaan dinikitil din pu Circir Fam lēē-ni yii ní nīn sá bikpilibee, kí kpòotī Unimbɔti nikitil din u dū u-ba fatikuu ki dée tiŋan.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: M nyí yii, m-kpátam boonee, binib làá dāá kóoń ni-kansikin. Baa làá dāá tàan̄ dinikitil gbanti, a lì kii agbiŋgbil nín cáá ntoom, kaa tàantí dipikitil puee.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Míǹ ní ni-kansikin bininjab biba mun làá dāá yòon̄ tinyimɔmbɔti kí sòoǹ kí ŋmàtiǹ Kriisitoo yab biba ń nīn nóó-bi.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, ní nīn nyímaan nì ni-ba kí nīn téetí m nín nìn sáŋkí-ni pu nì nnyinnyim ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu áli abin atee.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, m dū-ni ki ŋá Unimbɔti ŋaan, ní nīn ŋúb́ u-bɔmɔntiitee. Tíǹ di cáá mpɔn kí yàntī ní béé Unimbɔti bɔti tikpil kí dāá fōō ipaati in u síiǹ kí tīī bin kɔkɔ sá u-yabee.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Ni nyí yii man kaa nìn là ubɔ nimbiliŋ, kaa nìn là ubɔ mun bɔkutil.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Nimbi ni-ba nìn nyí yii nì m-ŋalii in bí nee ní m nìn cáa tūǹ ditundi ní man nì bin nìn nóóyee jīǹ.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: M dàkā-ni ni-kɔkɔ ń béé yii ni máaǹ kí nīn tūǹ ditundi tikpil kí ŋmā kí tūtuǹ biwɔfib, kí nīn téetí ti-Dindaan Yeesu u-ba nín nìn lī dinyɔɔbundi diŋyee, yii: <Á pɔ̄ tiwanee mɔ̄ ki jítiǹ bí pɔ̄-si.>»

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl lī míǹ ki dóòyee, ní ki gbāaǹ, ní u nì bi kɔkɔ bíi mèé.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi-kɔkɔ bíi sūǹ, ní ki dū bi-ŋalii ki kpàl̄ Pɔɔl.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Tin nìn kɔ́ǹ-bi kunimbaauee di sá u nín lī yii dalba dalba baa làá ti ká-uee. Niinee ní bi céeǹ-u áli meela taapu.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Timbi nì bi dāa cúu yākatì tɔbinee, ní timbi kɔ́ meela ki túĺ dicancaal ki búntì Kɔɔsi, ní ku wúntèe ti dūu bàn̄ Roodi. Niinee ní ti cāatì Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Ní ki ká meela un cá Feenisiiyee, ní ti kɔ́ úǹ ki búntì.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Ti tin gbīitì Siipiri tiŋki kin nnyim māntì ki túee ní ki dū-kì ki fá ŋŋaŋgan pú, ní ki dūu dī Siirii watil pú, ní ki tin bàn̄ Tiir, laakin meela làá tàkatī u-wantee.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Ti nín kāl̀ iwiin gbanti dóò ti làá yīkìńee, bi nì bi-nimpoobi nì bi-biyaamu kɔkɔ céeǹní-ti áli ki nyántì kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu. Niinee ní ti gbāaǹ dimɔɔgbandi ki mēē.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Ti mēē ki dóòyee, ní ki kāaǹ tɔb, ní timbi búntì kí cùú kɔ́ meela, ní bi mun nín fàtī bi-dumpui.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Ní ti yíkì Tiir ki cūtì Tooleemayiisi, ki cūtìi jáam̀ nnabiyaamu, ki kāl̀ bi-cee ŋwiin ŋubɔ. Niin ní ti kúntì dimɔɔl pu saŋkindi.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní ti yíkì niin ki bàn̄ Seesaaree, ní ki kɔ́ Fiiliipi dumpu. U sá un sòoǹ Yeesu bɔmɔntiiti ki sá binib biluli bin bi nìn lēē bí nīn yàkatī tijinee kansikin ubɔee ní.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: U nìn cáá bisapɔmbi binaa bin kaa nyí uninjee, bi nìn sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Ti nìn kāl̀ u-cee ki yúntì fiii, ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ, bi yíì-u Agabusi, nyánní Juudee ki dɔ́miń ti-cee.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Kijapaayee yōoǹ Pɔɔl dambalau ní ki dūu bóob́ u-taaŋi nì u-ŋalii, ní ki bí yii: «Pīlifìmaan Circir Fam nín lī puee! Uninja un di yaa yì dambala neeyee, Juuda yab làá bóob́ udaan míǹ ní Jeerusaleem, ní kí dū-u kí tīī bin kaa sá Juuda yabee.»

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ti gbìl̄ mimmee, ní timbi nì laakin ti kóòyee yab bíi gbàam̄ Pɔɔl yii ú taa cù Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl bí-ti yii: «Ba ŋá ní ni sūǹ ki bíiĺ m-pɔbil míǹ? Báà bi yaa làá bóob́-mi kí kpɔ̀-mi gba Jeerusaleem niin ti-Dindaan Yeesu puɔɔɔ, maa mɔ́tí!»

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Ti lī-u tikɔkɔ kaa ŋúń-uee, ní ti cāntì-u, ní ki bí-u yii: «Too, ti-Dindaan yaa là miŋyee, án ŋá míǹ!»

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Iwiin gbanti boonee, ní ti bɔ́ntì ki nín jɔ́ḿ Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Kriisitoo yab bin bí Seesaareeyee biba céeǹní-ti ki cáa cūnnì kijapaai kin bi yíì Minaasɔnee dumpu. U nìn sá Siipiri, ki nìn fōō ki kíí dooooyee. Úǹ cee ní bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-ti. Pɔɔl cūtìi māntì Yakubu pu

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Ti bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee, ní nnabiyaamu fōō-ti nì dipɔɔpindi.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní ti nì Pɔɔl búntì Yakubu cee. Niin ní bikpilib kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: U jáam̀-bi ki dóòyee, ní ki bíi sòoǹ ki bɔ́bití-bi Unimbɔti nín dī u-pu ki túń ditundi din bin kaa sá Juuda yabee kansikinee.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Bi gbìl̄ mimmee, ní ki nyɔ́ŋkì Unimbɔti. Ní bi bí-u yii: «Ti-nabiki, a ká Juuda yab kansikin binib kutukub tikpil nín kpántì Kriisitoo yab, bi-kɔkɔ ŋúb́ Mooyiisi marab tiŋan pueeyaa!

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Di sá bi tùkū-bi yii a dàkà Juuda yab bin kóò binicambi kansikinee yii bí fá Mooyiisi marab kí taa ti nín̄ gífí bi-biyaamu akpancan, kí fá ti-naanjab koobiliŋ mun.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Báà an ŋá pu bi-kɔkɔ làá béé yii a dɔ́miń. Mimmee, ti làá ŋá mana kɔŋkɔnnee?

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, ti làá tùkù-si a nín làá ŋá puee. Bininjab binaa biba bí ti-kansikin doo ki pōoǹ ipoon.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Yòon̄-bi kí cù si nì bi kɔkɔ ń ŋá saraabi kí kòotī-bi, kí pà animbil bí kòol̀-bi. Niinee ní báà ŋma làá béé yii tin ní bi sòoǹ a-puee kaa sá ibaamɔn, ní kí ká yii sisi aba bí kii bin dī marabee nín bí puee.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: An yaa kíǹ bin kaa sá Juuda yab ki fōō Yeesu ki kííyee, ti nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tùkū-bi yii timbi kpēē yii an ŋān̄ bí taa ti ŋmɔ́ tiwaatootinan, kí taa ŋmɔ́ fatiku nì tiwan tin baa lāntì fatiku nyáńee, kí taa ŋá tilaakpaal mun.»

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní Pɔɔl yōoǹ bininjabee, ní u nì bi cūtì ki ŋá saraabi, ní ki kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin. Niin ní Pɔɔl yóoǹ ŋwiin ŋun bi làá kòotēe nì báà ŋma nín làá dāá cáań saraabi bin biŋyee. Bi cúú Pɔɔl kunimbɔtidiin

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Ŋwinluluútee cá dikúntilee, ní Juuda yab biba bin nyánní Asiiyee ká Pɔɔl kunimbɔtidiin. Niinee ní bi fíiǹ báà ŋma landɔkɔŋu ŋá mbaanti, ní bi cúú Pɔɔl.

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Bi cúú-uee, ní ki kíǹ ki bíi tátí yii: «Isirayeel yab, jòoḿmaan-ti! Kpèèmaan, uninjee dee un cá an kɔkɔ ki sòoǹ báà ŋma cee ki bíiĺ Isirayeel yab yindi nì Mooyiisi marab nì kunimbɔtidiiyee. Áli gba, u yāntì bin kaa sá Juuda yabee kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin, ki bíil̀ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu gbanti!»

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Kun yì-tèe di sá, bi nìn ká u nì Troofiim un sá Eefeesee kitiŋin, ní bi dākafì yii Pɔɔl nìn cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidiin.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Niin ní kitimmɔŋee fōō ki píĺ dàii, ní binib nyánní ajan kɔkɔ pu ki dɔ́miń ki cúú Pɔɔl ki dáaĺ-u ki nyántì kunimbɔtidiin, ní ki dū mpunyɔmu ki pīiǹ dicilpu niin.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Bi nín nìn pée nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-uee puee, an pūtì kpáàa pée bàn̄ Room yab soojakpikpaaŋwu, yii fìkil fikil ubɔ kóoń Jeerusaleem tiŋki kɔkɔn.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Dicilpu niinee, kijapaayee yōoǹ soojab ki kpáaǹ bi-kpilib biba ki sáń ki nín cá samaayee cee. Bi dāa ká usoojakpilee nì u-yab páaǹnée, ní bi gbēeǹ, kaa ti bíi gbáà Pɔɔl.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Room yab soojakpikpaaŋwu dāatìi cúú Pɔɔl, ní ki bí yii bí dū ikusaka ili kí bóob́-u, ní u bālifì-bi un Pɔɔl sée nì tin u ŋée.

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Kunipaau kansikinee, biba tátí ki lì tiba, ní bin kíǹee mun cáá tiba, an di nìn yì-tì waa nìn ŋúń ki béè mbaamɔn, ní u bí yii bí cáá-u kí cùnnì soojab dumpu.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi bāań akɔl puee, samaayee kɔkɔ nín páb́ Pɔɔl mpɔn puee ní soojab yōoǹ-u ki túǹ, kí mɔ̄tì u-pu.

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: Kun puee binib nìn wīikí tikpil ki pá u-boon ki tátí yii bí kpɔ̀-u. Pɔɔl bíi sòoǹ tin u cááyee samaa nimbiin

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Bi tóob́ kí kɔ́ soojab dumpuee, ní Pɔɔl bālifì usoojakpikpaan yii: «A kíikí ḿ sòoǹ nì si tibaaa?» Ní ukpilee fātìi bālifì-u yii: «A gbìl̀ Greeki yab sooŋyaaa?

english_verse: “Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led
translation_verse: Sii di kaa sá Ueejipitija un là kí bīil̀ kitiŋ yaadal nee, ki yíkìi yōoǹ digaŋgandambi kutukub binaa ki cūnnì kuteeuneeee?»

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl kíí-u yii: «Man sá Ujuudaja ní, ní bi màl̄-mi Taarsi, Siilisii tiŋkpaaŋkin. M baasii sá kitiŋkpaaŋŋi tindambiki ní. M gbāam̀-si, pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ sòoǹ nì samaa!»

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Niinee ní usoojakpikpaanee pú-u mpaan. Ní Pɔɔl yúl̀ akɔl pu ki yōoǹ u-ŋal ki téefì samaa. Niinee ní báà ŋma ŋmíl̀ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ. Ní u yōoǹ dinyɔɔbundi ki bíi sòoǹ nì samaa nì eebru sooŋyin, yii:

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Bi nín gbìl̄ u bíi sòoǹ nì bi Eebru sooŋyee, ní bi mɔ̄tìi ŋmíl̀ díkí diki. Ní Pɔɔl bí-bi yii:

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: «Man sá ujuudaja ní, bi màl̄-mi Taarsi Siilisii tiŋkin, ama kitiŋ nee poon ní m kāl̀ ki wíiǹ. Gamaliyeel cee ní m nìn bí ki bífì ti-naanjab marab kɔkɔ, ní ki nìn cáá dipɔ́ɔǹdi Unimbɔti bɔtin tiŋan, kii díǹ wiiŋŋu ni mun nín cáá dipɔ́ɔǹdi pu nan ní.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: M nìn páb́ bin nìn nóó ti-Dindaan saŋŋuee, áli ki kūū biba, ki cútì bininjab nì binimpoobi ki tɔ́ sarkan.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Usaraaŋakpil nì bibɔsooŋkpilib kɔkɔ nìn kántì m nín nìn ŋáaǹ puee. Bíǹ di ŋūǹ kí tùkù-ni mbaamɔn. Bíǹ gba di nìn tīī-mi tigbɔn ḿ cáá tīī Juuda yab kpilib bin kóò Damaasee kí ŋmā kí cúú Kriisitoo yab bin bí niinee, kí bóobiń-bi ikusaka kí cáań Jeerusaleem bí dáaĺ bi-tafal.» Pɔɔl bíi máafí u nín kpántì Kriisitoo yɔu puee (Kpèè Atuun

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: «Ki cá kuwiŋkuluuee, m nìn bí nsanni ki tóob́ Damaasi. Dicilpu niinee ní ŋwalifikpaŋkpaan ŋubɔ nyánní yilpu ki dɔ́miń ki māntìi tú-mi ki wāĺ nyáka nyaka,

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: ní m lítì kitiŋ. Niinee ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ bíi lì-mi yii: <Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, ba ŋá ní a páb́-mi míǹ?>

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Ní m fātìi bālifì-u yii: <An sá sii ŋma, m-Dindaan?> Ní u kíí-mi yii: <An sá man Yeesu Naasaareeti yɔu un a páb́ee.>

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Bin nìn bí m-ceeyee nìn ká ŋwalifi, ama ní kaa nìn nín gbìl̄ nneen ŋun sòon̄ nì mee pu.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bí yii: <Mimmee, m làá ŋá mana, m-Dindaan?> Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: <Yīkìí nīn cá Damaasi. Niin ní bi làá tin tùkù-si tin tin Unimbɔti bí yii á ŋée.>

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Ŋwalifee nín nìn jīliŋkì m-nimbiliŋ puee, maa nìn gíti wāĺ, ní man nì bin nìn nóóyee cúú m-ŋal ki dātì-mi ki cūnnì Damaasi.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: «Uninja ubɔ nìn bí niin, bi yíì-u Ananiyasi. U nìn nóó Unimbɔti deedee ki tɔ́ ti-marab, ní Juuda yab bin nìn kóò Damaasee kɔkɔ nìn pàkà-u.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Kijapaayee dɔ́miń ki yúl̀ m-cee, ní ki bí yii: <M-nabiki Sɔɔl, ŋúbití a-nimbiliŋ!> Kpalaa niinee, ní m cúu ŋúbitì, ní ki wál̀-u.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-mi yii: <Ti-naanjab Nimbɔtiuee di lēē-si dooooyee ki yóoǹ yii á béé u nín là puee kí ká Deedeedaan un u lēē ki túnnée kí gbìl̄ u-neen.

english_verse: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
translation_verse: Sii di làá nīn sá u-seeraleeliu, kí sòoǹ binib kɔkɔ nimbiin tin tin a kée nì tin a gbìl̄ee.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee ba di gíti ŋúb́-si kɔŋkɔnnee? Yīkìm̄ kí kúuǹ kí yíiń ti-Dindaan bí fàl̀-si Unimbɔti nyim á ká a-kpitii pɔ̄tam.>» Ti-Dindaan tú Pɔɔl bin kaa sá Juuda yabee cee

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nìkī ki lī yii: «M dāa fātìń Jeerusaleemee, ní ki kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin ki bíi mèé Unimbɔti, ní an fītì-mi ní m wál̀ ti-Dindaan.

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: Ní u tùkū-mi yii: <Nyā Jeerusaleem malaa, kun puee baa làá fōō tibɔti tin a bíi sòoǹ m-puee kí kíí.>

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Ní m fātìi kíí-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan, kéè, bíǹ bi-ba nyí-mi, m nín nìn yìiǹ Jeerusaleem akpafidiinni ki cútí bin nóó-see ki gbáà-bi ki cáa tòó sarkeeyaa!

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Kéè, bi nyí, daliŋkin bi bíi kù a-seeraleeliu Eetiyeenee, man di nìn bí niin ki bí yii u máaǹ ŋkúm, ní ki fōō bin bíi kù-uee bɔkutiŋ ki ŋúb́eeyaa!>

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ama ní u bí-mi yii: <Nín̄ cá. Bin bí ndan kaa sá Juuda yabee cee ní m tūǹ-si!>» Pɔɔl nì Room soojakpikpaaŋwu bíi sòoǹ

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Samaayee pílifiǹ Pɔɔl ki tin sāā laakin u bí yii ti-Dindaan tú-u bin kaa sá Juuda yabee cee. Niinee ní bi yíkì ki bíi tátí yii: «Bí kpɔ̀maan uninja nee! Bí taa tàan̄-u! Waa máaǹ kí nīn bí!»

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi bíi pùlifī ki pèetī bi-bɔkutiŋ ki fīintí, ní ki jáfí ntam ki tòó kutaa.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Ní usoojakpikpaanee bí yii bí cáá Pɔɔl kí kɔ́ǹ soojab dumpu kí gbá-u anaalab kí bàlifì-u kun di yì-tì ní samaa kɔkɔ tátí u-pu mimmee.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Bi bóob́-u ki dóò ki làá gbá-uee, ní Pɔɔl bí usoojakpil un nìn bí niinee yii: «An máaǹ ní gbá Room tindambiki un bɔti gba baa láá sòon̄eeee?»

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Ukpilee gbìl̄ an nyɔɔbundee, ní ki cūtìi tùkū usoojakpikpaanee yii: «Á nīn nyí nì a-ba! Kijapaayee sá Room tindambiki ní.»

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Niinee ní usoojakpikpaanee dɔ́miń ki bālifì Pɔɔl yii: «A sá Room tindambiki níii?» Ní Pɔɔl kíí-u yii: «Iiin.»

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní usoojakpikpaanee bí yii: «Man pàn̄ animbil tikpil ní ki nín kpántì Room tindambiki.» Ní Pɔɔl fātìi bí-u yii: «Bi pée màl̄-mee, m sá Room tindambiki ní.»

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Kpalaayee, bin bàà làá gbá-u kí yàntī ú sòoǹee kākatì ki wāatì-u. Usoojakpikpaanee nín dāa béè yii Pɔɔl sá Room tindambikee, ní tifaandi kɔ́ u mun u-ba, kun puee u nìn dū ikusaka ní ki bóob́-u. Pɔɔl yú bibɔsoonliibi kitil nimbiin

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Usoojakpikpaanee là kí béé kun di yì-tì ní Juuda yab ŋúb́ Pɔɔlee. An pu ní kutaa wúntèe u bútì-u ikusaka ní ki bí yii bisaraaŋakpilib nì bibɔsoonliibi kitil kɔkɔ ń kpāfì. Bi kpáfèe, ní u cáań Pɔɔl ki yóoǹ bi-nimbiin.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl dū u-nimbikpeeŋu ki báaǹ bikpilibee pu, ní ki bí-bi yii: «M-nabiyaamu, m nyí yii m ŋáaǹ tin kɔkɔwoooo m máaǹ kí ŋá kí tīī Unimbɔtee nì dipɔbil diba, ki dāa sāā díǹ wiiŋŋu nee.»

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Niinee ní usaraaŋakpil, un bi yíì Ananiyasee, bí bin yú ki pìl̄-uee yii bí cùú fáá u-nyɔkɔ.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl bí yii: «Unimbɔti làá dāá fáá si mun, upɔnyɔŋfiti! Sii kā ki cáá marab ki sòoǹ man bɔti, ki yìntī marab gbanti a-ba ní ki cáá yii bí gbá mama!»

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Ní bin nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ Pɔɔlee bí-u yii: «Mimmee, a bíi sìí Unimbɔti saraaŋakpiliu deeyaa!»

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl fātìi kíí-bi yii: «M-nabiyaamu, maa nyí yii an sá usaraaŋakpil. An yaa sá fam, maa bàà sòoǹ míǹ, kun puee Unimbɔti gbɔŋku poon tùkù-ti yii: <A taa sòoǹ ni-bɔtiu bɔfam.>»

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nìn nyí yii bibɔsoonliibee jandi diba sá Sadusab ní dijandi diba mun sá Fariisab. Míǹ pu ní u nìn téeń samaayee nimbiin yii: «M-nabiyaamu, ma mun sá Fariisa ní, Ufariisaja di màl̄-mi. Dimákal din m cáá bitaŋkpiibi fìkititam puee di yì-tì ní bi cáań-mi doo kí sòoǹ m-bɔti!»

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: U lī míǹ ki dóòyee, ní kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu kɔ́ Sadusab nì Fariisab kansikin, ní samaa gbanti cúu yākatì tɔbin.

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: Di sá yii Sadusab, bíǹ bí yii bitaŋkpiibi gíti kpá kí dāá fìkitī, Unimbɔti tuuŋyi kpá, kinaŋ mun kpá, ama Fariisab, bíǹ bí yii tíǹ kɔkɔ bí.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Niinee ní kujakpaaŋŋu jéetì bi-kansikin, ní bimaradakaliibi bin nìn sá Fariisab jandi púee biba yíkì, kaa kíí, ki bíi mɔ́tí yii: «Timbi kaa ká kijapaai nee ŋá tiba. An yaa yíì, Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu di làá nīn máaǹ ki sòon̄ nì u.»

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu mɔ̄tìi pɔ́ɔkèe, ní usoojakpikpaan fāŋkì yii bí taa ŋée kí cúú Pɔɔl kí tɔ̀ntī. Ní u yāntì soojab kpákatìi cúú Pɔɔl ki nyántì bi-kansikin, ki cáa cūnnì soojab dumpu.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: An nyeekuee, ti-Dindaan dɔ́miń Pɔɔl cee, ní ki bí-u yii: «Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba! Kii a nín sòon̄ m-pu Jeerusaleem doo puee, án máaǹ á cù Room mun kí tin sòoǹ m-pu niin mbaantiim míǹ.» Juuda yab bíi nyàab̀ isan kí kpɔ̀ Pɔɔl

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Ní bi cūtìi ká bisaraaŋakpilib nì bikpilib, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Timbi baasii pūtì ki tíntì yii, ti yaa kaa kūū Pɔɔl, taa làá dáká tiba.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, nimbi nì bibɔsoonliibi kitil kɔkɔ, ní mèè usoojakpikpaan ú cáań-ni Pɔɔl, yii nimbi là kí mɔ̀tīí bàlifì-u tin páaa ní u baasii ŋée. Mimmee, timbi ń bɔ́ntí, bi yaa cáá-u ki tóobińee, timbi ń kíntí kí kpɔ̀-u!»

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Niinee, Pɔɔl niisal biki gbìl̄ bi nín kpáfì ki sòon̄ tiŋyee, ní u búntì soojab dumpu ki kɔ́ ki tùkū Pɔɔl tin jítèe.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl yíiń bisoojakpilibee ubɔ ní ki bí-u yii: «Cáá kinaacimpɔmbiki nee kí cùnnì usoojakpikpaan cee, kun puee kì cáá tiba ki là kí tùkù-u.»

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Ukpilee yōoǹ-kì ki cáá-kì ki bàn̄ usoojakpikpaanee cee, ní ki bí yii: «Usarkadaan Pɔɔl di yíiń-mi ki gbāam̀ yii ḿ cáań-si kinaacimpɔmbiki nee, kì cáá tiba ki làá tùkù-si.»

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Niinee ní usoojakpikpaanee cúú kinaacimpɔmbikee ŋal ki kpáàa kākatì ŋkpaanceeti, ní ki bí-kì yii: «Tilati ní a cáań ní?»

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Ní kì kíí-u yii: «Juuda yab kpáfì kí mèè-si yii á cáań-bi Pɔɔl bibɔsoonliibi kitil nimbiin, bi là kí ŋá kii bi làá gíti mɔ̀tīí bàlifì-u tibɔti tiba yamee.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Niinee, usoojakpikpaanee bí kinaacimpɔmbikee yii: «Nín̄ kùǹ. Á taa sòoǹ ubɔ cee yii a tùkū-mi tibɔti gbanti!» Bi dū Pɔɔl ki tīī gɔmina Feeliikisi

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Bí nyàab̀ itaamu kí kàan̄ Pɔɔl, kí cáá-u kí bànnì gɔmina Feeliikisi cee nì alaafiya.

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Ní usoojakpikpaanee ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī gɔmina yii:

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: «Man Kloodi Liisiyasi di jáaḿ m-kpiliu gɔmina Feeliikisi.

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Di sá yii Juuda yab di cúú uninja nee ki là kí kpɔ̀-u. M nín gbìl̄ yii u sá Room tindambikee, ní man nì m-soojab cūtìi fōoń-u.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: M nìn là kí béé kun pu ní Juuda yab ŋúb́-u mimmee, ní m cáá-u ki cūnnì bi-bɔsoonliibi kitil cee.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m ká yii bi bí yii u yīntì bi-marab, ama an kaa sá tibɔti tin pu u máaǹ ŋkúmeeyaaa, kaa tí máaǹ sarka mun.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: M nín dāa béè yii Juuda yab kpáfì ki nyàab̀ isan kí kpɔ̀-uee puee, ní m dū-u ki tīiń-si malaa, ní ki bí u-nannanliibi yii bí dāan̄ kí yíiń-u a-cee ibeeyiin.»

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Soojabee lafun ŋá u nín lī puee, ki yōoǹ Pɔɔl ki cáá-u ki bānnì áli Antiipatriisi kunyeeu gbanti.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Ku wúntèe ní soojab bin nìn còom̄ ataa puee nín gítiń, ní itaamu dambee kpáaǹ Pɔɔl ki cáa nín cá.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Bi bàn̄ Seesaareeyee, ní ki dū kugbɔŋu ki tīī gɔmina, ní ki dū Pɔɔl ki dàkā-u.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Gɔmina kàan̄ kugbɔŋuee ki dóòyee, ní ki bālifì Pɔɔl yii u sá kitiŋ kilaka ní. Ní Pɔɔl bí-u yii u sá Siilisii. U béè mimmee,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: ní ki bí yii: «Si nì bin kpákèe yaa láa bāańee, á dāá sòoǹ tin a cááyee ḿ pīlifì.» U lī mimmee ní ki bí yii bí cáá-u kí cùnnì ubɔti Eeroodi dumpu.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Iwiin iŋmoo boonee ní usaraaŋakpil Ananiyasi bāań Seesaaree gɔmina cee, u nì bikpilib biba nì umɔtil ubɔ un bi yíì Teertuluusee, ki yíiń Pɔɔl ibeeyiin.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Bi yíiń Pɔɔl, ní Teertuluusi kíĺ ki bíi kàaǹ tibɔti yii: «Ukpimɔnti Feeliikisi, sii di yì ŋgbansɔŋfi ŋun poon ti bí, an kaa kúntí nee. A-ciiŋŋu pu ní a yāntì kitiŋ kpántì ní ki ŋáŋkì.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Ti kāntí a-ŋanti gbanti an kɔkɔ nì an kɔkɔ. Míǹ puee, ti jáaḿ-si tiŋan.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Maa là kí bīil̀ a-yuntiŋu tikpilee, an di yì-tì ní m mèé-si a-laŋŋaŋfitiiku puee, á pīlifiǹ-ti fiii.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: Di sá yii timbi ká yii kijapaai nee sá unil un sá asaluu daanee. Úǹ di yì-tì ní fìkil fikil kɔ́ Juuda yab bin bí duulinya nee nee kɔkɔ kansikin. Úǹ di sá Naasaareeti yab kitil kpiliu ubɔ.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: ní ki bí yii u nì bin kpákèe ń nīn dòoń sii cee.] Míǹ puee, sii a-ba yaa bālifì-u, a béetí kun pu ní ti ŋúb́-uee.»

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Ní Juuda yab bí yii Teertuluusi nín lī puee, míǹ ní an sá. Pɔɔl sòon̄ u-nyɔkɔpu yai Feeliikisi nimbiin

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Boonee ní gɔmina pú Pɔɔl nsan yii u mun ń sòoǹ. Ní Pɔɔl yōoǹ dinyɔɔbundi ki bí yii: «M nyí yii doooo abin kupaau sèé a nín sá kitiŋ nee poon ubɔsoonlee. An puee nì dimákal poon ní m làá sòoǹ tin m cááyee a-nimbiin.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Sii a-ba yaa bālifì gba, a làá béé yii an kaa láá bàn̄ iwiin saalaa nì ili m nín jɔ́m̀ Jeerusaleem kí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔtee.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Dalba dalba baa láá ká-mi kunimbɔtidiin man nì ubɔ bíi kpákà. Baa láá tí ká-mi m bí akpafidiinnaaa, kitiŋ poon laaba ki sòoǹ ki yòontí binib pɔbiliŋ.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Binib nee kaa ŋūǹ kí dàkà-si yii kun pu bi ŋúb́-mee baasii sèé.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Nì ibaamɔn poon ní m sòoǹ nì si nee, m nóó Yeesu saŋŋu ŋun bíǹ yíì yii ŋuaa ŋān̄ee, ní ki jáaḿ ti-naanjab Nimbɔtiu. Ama man nyí yii Mooyiisi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nín ŋmàn̄ tin tigbɔn poonee, an sá ibaamɔn.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: M cáá dimákal Unimbɔti pu, kii bi mun bi-ba nín cáá dimákal u-pu puee, yii binimɔntiibi nì binikpitib kɔkɔ bí kí dāá fìkitī ditaŋkpiilin.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní man bí ki pɔ̄ɔntí m-ba kí nīn sá unimɔnti Unimbɔti nimbiin nì binib mun cee.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: «Maa nìn gíti bí Jeerusaleem abiŋkaaŋkaa aba poon. Boonee ní m fātìi gítìń, ki cáań animbil kí tūtuǹ m-tiŋki nib, kí kpáàa ŋá saraabi.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: M ŋá akoobil ki dóò, boonee ní ki bíi ŋáań saraabi gbanti kunimbɔtidiin, ní bi bāań ki ká-mi. Biba kaa nìn kpáfì m-cee, fìkil fikil mun nìn kpá.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Juuda yab bin kóò Asii ki nìn ká-mee di yaa bàà bímaan bi-ba a-nimbiin doo kí bàà sòoǹ tin ní m ŋá-bee, an bàà ŋān̄.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Àá bin bí nee ń tùkù-si, bi nín nìn cáá-mi bibɔsoonliibi kitil nimbiinee, tikpitil tin bi ká m ŋá

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: an yaa kaa sá m nín nìn yú bi-kansikin ki téeń mpɔn dinyɔɔbumbaantiil yii: <M nín fōō ki kíí yii bitaŋkpiibi làá dāá fìkitēe puee ní m yú ni-nimbiin díǹ, ni bíi sòoǹ m-bɔtaa!>»

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl sòon̄ míǹ ki dóòyee, ní Feeliikisi, un di nìn nyí kun di sá Yeesu saŋŋu tiŋanee, dāa bí-bi yii bí nīn kùǹ. Ní ki bí yii: «Asee usoojakpikpaan Liisiyasi yaa láa dɔ́mińee, m dāa béetí ni-bɔti gbanti.»

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: U lī mimmee, ní ki bí yii usoojakpil ubɔ ń cáá Pɔɔl kí pìin̄, ama kí yàntī ú tɔ̄ u-ba ŋwaam pu, kí nīn pūǹ u-bɔɔbi nsan bí nīn dòoń u-cee ki cāabìń tin tin u yaa lèe. Pɔɔl yú Feeliikisi nì Drusii nimbiin

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Iwiin iba boonee ní Feeliikisi nì u-nimpuu Drusii un sá ujuudanimpuee dɔ́miń ní ki tú bi cūtìi yíiń Pɔɔl. Ní Pɔɔl sòon̄ u pílifì min di sá yii bí fōō Yeesu Kriisitoo kí kííyee.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun Pɔɔl kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ unil nín máaǹ kí nīn bí deedee kí fá u-wunti kɔdeeu puee nì ibɔsoon in bí ki dòońee puee, ní Feeliikisi fāŋkì, ní ki bí yii: «Nín̄ cá, daliŋkin m yaa ká mpaanee, m làá tí fàtīí yíiń-si.»

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
