translation_verse: U nìn dàkafī yii Pɔɔl làá tīī-u animbil ní, míǹ pu ní u nìn yíì-u múlmul bi sòoǹ.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Abin ali boonee ní Pɔɔsiyusi Feestuusi fōō Feeliikisi yil ki kíǹ ki sá gɔmina. Feeliikisi là an mɔ̄ɔkiǹ Juuda yabee, ní u yāntì Pɔɔl gbíntìi bí sarkan.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Feestuusi nìn bàn̄ Juudee watil. Iwiin ita boonee ní u yíkì Seesaaree ki nín jɔ́ḿ Jeerusaleem.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Ní bisaraaŋakpilib nì Juuda yab nikpaambi dɔ́miń ki kàan̄ Pɔɔl bɔti ki tùkū-u, ní ki gbāam̀ Feestuusi

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: yii ú jī kimɔtii kí yàntī Pɔɔl ń dāan̄ Jeerusaleem. Di sá yii bi bɔ́ntì ki cí kí kpɔ̀-u nsanni.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Ní Feestuusi kíí-bi yii: «Pɔɔl kā sarkan Seesaaree, man m-ba bíi bɔ́ntí kí fàtīí gítí niin ní nee.»

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Ní u gíti bí-bi yii: «Mimmee, ni-kpilib ń nóó-mi tí cù Seesaaree bí tin sòoǹ kí kpèè uninja gbanti yaa ŋá tikpitil tiba.»

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Feestuusi nìn ŋá iwiin inii kii saalaa pu bi-kansikin, ní ki fātìi gítìń Seesaaree. Kutaa wúntèe ní u kɔ́ ki kāl̀ kubɔsoondiin ní ki bí bí yíiń Pɔɔl.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl bāańee Juuda yab bin nyánní Jeerusaleemee yú ki kɔ́ĺ-u ki sòoǹ u-pu yii u ŋáaǹ tibɔkpaandi tikpil. Ama baa nìn ŋūǹ kí cáań tiba bí béé yii tin pu bi sòoǹee sá ibaamɔn.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl mun yōoǹní tin u cááyee ki lī yii: «Maa yīntì nì Juuda yab marab ubɔ, kaa tí yīntì nì kunimbɔtidii, kaa yīntì nì gɔminakpaan Seesaar mun.»

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Feestuusi nìn là án mɔ̄ɔkiǹ Juuda yabee, ní u bālifì Pɔɔl yii: «A là kí jɔ̄m̀ Jeerusaleem bí sòoǹ a-bɔti nee m-nimbiinaaa?»

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl kíí-u yii: «Gɔminakpaan Seesaar bɔsoondiikun ní man sí ki bí nee, niin ní an máaǹ bí sòoǹ m-bɔti! Kun puee maa ŋá Juuda yab tikpitil tiba, sii a-ba gba nyí míǹ tiŋan.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: M yaa sá unikpiti ní ki ŋá tin tin máaǹ ŋkúmee, mimmee maa mɔ́tí ŋkúm pu. Ama, an yaa tí sá yii tin bi sòoǹ m-puee yaa sá nnyimɔn, ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí dū-mi kí tīī-bi. See ḿ bà gɔminakpaan Seesaar nimbiin!»

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Niinee ní Feestuusi nì u-kpilib kāl̀ ki sòon̄ ki kpōotì tɔb, ní ki kíí-u yii: «Kéè, a bí yii a là kí cù gɔminakpaan nimbiinaa! Ti kíí á lafun cù u-nimbiin.» Pɔɔl yú Agriipa nì Beereeniisi nimbiin

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Iwiin ili boonee, ní ubɔti Agriipa nì Beereeniisi bāań Seesaaree kí jāam̀ Feestuusi.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Bi kāl̀ iwiŋkaaŋkaa iba poonee, ní Feestuusi dū Pɔɔl bɔti ki kàan̄ ki tùkū ubɔti yii: «Feeliikisi yāntì uninja ubɔ sarkan doo.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: M nín nìn cūtì Jeerusaleemee ní bisaraaŋakpilib nì Juuda yab kpilib tùkū-mi yii u nìn ŋá ikpiti ní, ní ki mēē-mi yii ḿ dáaĺ u-tafal.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Ní m kíí-bi yii Room yab bíǹ kaa dù unil kí tīī bí dáaĺ u-tafal, asee bí pɔ̄-u kinyɔkɔ u mun ń sòoǹ u-nannanliibi nimbiin kun pu ní bi bí ki jáàyee.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Bi dɔ́miń doo nee, kutaa wúntèe maa nìn gíti tāaǹ-bi, ní ki kɔ́ ki kāl̀ m-bɔsoondiikun ní ki bí bí cáań uninja gbanti.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Ní u-nannanliibi mun kàan̄. Ama maa ká tikpitil tin ní m bàà dàkafī yii u máaǹ ki ŋée.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: An nìn sá bíǹ bi-ba marab nì un bi yíì Yeesu u kpíì kin Pɔɔl bí yii u bée ŋmaniŋma pu ní bi bíi kpákà.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Maa nìn nyí m nín làá ŋá pu kí béé tibɔti gbanti yilee, an pu ní m bālifì Pɔɔl yii u yaa là kí cù Jeerusaleem ḿ sòoǹ u-bɔti gbanti niin.

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl yíì ki lī yii bí yàntī ú nīn bí sarkan kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní gɔminakpaan Seesaar làá dāá sòoǹ tibɔti gbantee. Ní m bí bí dū-u kí pìin̄ kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun m làá dāá dū-u kí tīī gɔminakpaanee.»

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ní Agriipa bí yii: «Man m-ba bàà là uninja gbanti ń sòoǹ ḿ pīlifì.» Ní Feestuusi kíí-u yii: «Tin u yaa cááyee, fool a fu gbìl̀.»

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní binib tikpil fōō Agriipa nì Beereeniisi, ní bi nì bisoojakpilib nì kitiŋ poon nikpaambi táá ki kɔ́ kubɔsoondiin. Ní Feestuusi yāntì bi cáań Pɔɔl,

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: ní ki bí yii: «Ubɔti Agriipa nì nimbi bin kɔkɔwoooo kpáfì doo nee, Juuda yab kɔkɔ dɔ́miń m-cee Jeerusaleem nì doo ki yíiń uninja un ni wāĺ nee ibeeyiin, ní ki tátí yii bi máaǹ kí kpɔ̀-u.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Ama man nyí yii waa ŋá tin máaǹ ŋkúmee, ní úǹ u-ba dāa bí yii gɔminakpaan ń sòoǹ u-bɔti. M kpēē yii an lafun máaǹ mimmee, ní m là kí dū-u kí tīī-u.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Maa láá nyí u-bɔti pu tiba kí ŋmà kí tīī ti-yidaaŋwu Seesaar kɔŋkɔnnee. Míǹ pu ní m cáań-u ni-cee, nì sii a-ba ubɔti Agriipa nimbiin, ní bi yaa bíi bàlifī-u anyɔɔbunee, ḿ ŋmā kí ká tiba poon kí ŋmà.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Di sá yii an kaa kítì ḿ dū usarkadaan kí tīī míǹ, kaa lī tin pu ní bi ŋúb́-uee.»

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: «Ubɔti Agriipa, an mɔ̄ǹ-mi díǹ wiiŋŋu tikpil ḿ yūĺ a-nimbiin kí sòoǹ kí nyāntí m-ba tibɔti tin kɔkɔ Juuda yab cáa tūntí m-puee ni.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: Di sá yii a nyí Juuda yab bimbim nì bi-nikpɔŋkpɔkɔku kɔkɔ pu. Míǹ puee m gbāam̀-si á jī kimɔtii kí pīlifiǹ-mi.»

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Ti-samaau tinaakɔti saalaa nì tilee máká yii bi làá dāá ká an poondi. An pu ní bi pɔ̄ɔntí ki nóó Unimbɔti ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Too, ubɔti, m nín máká tin pu Juuda yab ŋúb́-mee dee.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, ba pu ní nimbi nyí yii Unimbɔti kaa làá dāá fìkitī bitaŋkpiibi ní?

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: Min min m nìn ŋáań Jeerusaleemee dee. Bisaraaŋakpilib nìn tīī-mi mpɔn m cútí bin fōō Yeesu ki kííyee tikpil ki tòó sarkan, ní ŋyunti ŋun bi yaa là kí kpɔ̀-bee, man di nìn lì yii bi lafun máaǹ ŋkúm.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti sá kamaayee, m nìn dátí bi-tafal akpafidiinni, ki bàà là bí yíí Yeesu. M nìn fōō diŋuul bi-pu an tin lákatì, áli ki nìn cá ntimu mubɔn ki tin páb̀-bi.» Pɔɔl máafì u nín kpántì u-ba puee (Kpèè Atuun

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: «Míǹ pu ní bisaraaŋakpilib nìn tú-mi ki tīī-mi mpɔn, ní m búntì Damaasi.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: M bí nsanni kuwiŋkuluu ki cée, ní ki ká ŋwalifi ŋubɔ nyánní yilpu, ki wāĺ nyáka nyaka ki jítiǹ ŋwìiń, ki māntìi tú man nì bin nìn nóó ki cá nsanee.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Niinee ní ti-kɔkɔ lítì kitiŋ, ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ sòon̄ nì mi eebru sooŋyin yii: <Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, ba ŋá ní a páb́-mi míǹ? An làá nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki tīī-si á tɔ̄ ipiin pu ŋgbèen.>

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m bālifì yii: <An sá sii ŋma, m-Dindaan?> Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: <An sá man Yeesu un a páb̀ee!

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Ama yīkìí yūĺ a-taaŋi pu. M dɔ́miń kí dū-si kí ŋá m-tɔntɔnliu ní. Sii di làá tùkù bin kíǹee tin a ká m-cee díǹee, nì tin tin m làá dāá tí yàntī á kée.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: M làá dāá tɔ̄-si Juuda yab nì bin kaa sá Juuda yabee cee, ki làá dāá mɔ̄tì a-pu bí taa ŋá-si tiba.

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: A làá cù kí ŋúbití bi-nimbiliŋ, kí nyāntiń-bi dibɔmbɔndin kí cáań-bi ŋwalifin, kí fōō-bi Sitaan pɔŋŋun kí cáań Unimbɔti cee. Bi yaa fōō-mi ki kííyee ní bí ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam nì tipaal tin Unimbɔti làá dāá tīī bin u gāntì bi sá u-yabee.>» Pɔɔl sòon̄ u-tundi pu

english_verse: King Agrippa, I obeyed this vision from heaven.
translation_verse: «Míǹ pu ní, ubɔti Agriipa, maa kpēē tin nyánní yilpu m kée fám.

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: M nìn kíĺ ki tùkū Damaasi yab ki wāatì, ní boonee ní m tùkū Jeerusaleem yab, ní ki póotì Juudee tiŋki nib kɔkɔ, nì atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee yab, yii bí fá bi-kpitii kí gítiń Unimbɔti cee, kí nīn cáá mbimbim min dàkà yii bi lafun kpántì bi-bee.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Kun di yì-tì ní m nìn bí kunimbɔtidiin Juuda yab dɔ́miń ki cúú-mi ki bàà là kí kpɔ̀-mee dee.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti mɔ́tì m-pu áli ki dāa sāā díǹ. M gbíntìi bí ki lèekī m-seerau biwɔfib nì biyidambi nimbiin. Maa ti cáá tiba ki kútì tin tin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì Mooyiisi nìn lī ki yóoǹee pu,

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: yii Meesiya làá dāá jī falaa áli kí dāá kpú. Úǹ di dāa sá upeepeekaa un làá fìkitī bitaŋkpiibi kansikin, kí cáań Juuda yab nì bin kaa sá Juuda yabee ŋwalifee.» Pɔɔl gbāam̀ Agriipa ú fōō Yeesu kí kíí

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl bíi sòoǹ tin u cááyee, ní Feestuusi téeń mpɔn yii: «A wáatì ní, Pɔɔl! A nín bífì tigbɔn tikpil puee di bíil̀ a-yil.»

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl kíí-u yii: «Ukpil Feestuusi, maa wáatì. Tibɔti tin m sòoǹee sá ibaamɔn ní ki sá tibɔmɔntiil.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Ubɔti béè-tì, míǹ puee ní m ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ u-nimbiin kaa fàŋkí. M nyí yii u nyí tikɔkɔ, kun puee an kaa nìn sá dibalin ní tibɔtee nìn jítì.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Too, ubɔti Agriipa, a fōō ki kíí yii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nín nìn sòon̄ tiŋyee sá ibaamɔnaaa? Man nyí yii a fōō ki kíí yii an sá ibaamɔn.»

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Ní Agriipa bí Pɔɔl yii: «An kíǹ fiii, á bàà dū-mi kí kpántí Kriisitoo yɔu!»

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl kíí-u yii: «An yaa kíǹ fiiiyaaa, an yaa làá tí yúntáaa, m bàà là Unimbɔti ń ŋá míǹ. Án taa nín̄ sá gba sii baba, ama án nīn sá ki kpáaǹ bin kɔkɔ bíi pílifíǹ-mi díǹ nee, ama bí taa nín bóob́ nimbi nì ikusaka nee ní!»

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ubɔti nì gɔmina nì Beereeniisi nì bin kɔkɔ nìn kā bi-ceeyee

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: yíkì ki nyáń, ní ki bíi lì yii: «Kijapaai nee kaa yīntì tiba tin máaǹ bí kpɔ̀-ueeyaaa, kaa tí máaǹ bí cáá-u kí ŋá sarka mun.»

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Ní Agriipa bí Feestuusi yii: «Kijapaai nee yaa kaa nìn bí yii bí cáá-u gɔminakpaan cee, ti bàà ŋūǹ kí gíiǹ-u kí líí.»

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti ŋun bi bí yii tí dāá kɔ́ meela kí nīn cá Italiiyee, ní bi dū Pɔɔl nì bisarkadambi biba ki tīī kijapaai kin bi nìn yíì Juliyusee, u sá usoojakpil dikitil din bi nìn yíì «gɔminakpaan kitilee» poon.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Ní ti kɔ́ meela un nyánní Adramiiti ki làá nīn cá Asii timmu mun kɔkɔ bí tiŋku caŋinee, ní ti yíkì. Ariistaarki un sá Maseeduwaan Teesalooniiki tiŋkinee nìn bí ti-cee.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe ní ti bàn̄ Siidɔn. Kii Juliyusi nín nìn ŋúb́ Pɔɔl tiŋan puee, u pú-u kinyɔkɔ ú cù u-bɔɔbi cee kí nyàabìń tin u yaa lèe.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: Ti dāa yíkì niinee, ní ki dūu dī ki kpàkaǹ Siipiri tiŋki kin dimɔɔl māntì ki túee, kun puee kubuŋu nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní ki túŋkiń-ti.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Ní ti dūtì tiŋku un bí ki nákáǹ Siilisii nì Paŋfiliiyee, ní ki dūu bàn̄ Miira, Liisii tiŋkin.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Niin ní usoojakpilee nìn ká meela ubɔ nyánní Aleekisandirii ki cá Italii ní u yāntì ti kɔ́ úǹ.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Meelee nìn dū iwiin tikpil ki còom̄ soooo soooo nì falaa, ki wāatì ní ki nín bàn̄ ki ŋmāntì nì Kiniidi tiŋki. Kubuŋu nín nìn páb́-ti, taa ŋūǹ kí dī niin kí nīn cá ndanee puee, ní ti dūu dīń Salmoonee watil pú ki dūu bāań Kreeti caŋin.

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: Ti bíi kpàkaǹ ki cá nì falaayee, ní ki dūu bàn̄ kitiŋ kin bi yíì Laaseeyee caŋin laakin bi yíì Ditiŋkugbammɔntiilee.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Ti nìn cōom̀ ki yúntì tikpil áli disaŋkindee dāa dūu kpántì mbusu, kun puee Juuda yab nyɔɔboobil wiiŋŋu jítì ní kitiŋ gbanti seeku mun nìn tóobiń. Míǹ puee ní Pɔɔl nìn bí ki kpáafí-bi yii:

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: «Ti-yab, man wāĺ yii ti-saŋŋu nee làá cáań-ti dinimbinaamandi, kun puee meela nì tiwan tin u túee làá ká falaa tikpil, an yaa yíì gba, timbi ti-ba làá kpú.»

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Ama usoojakpilee kaa nìn fōō Pɔɔl nín sòon̄ puee ki kíí, ní ki nìn máká un nìn sá ukpil meelanee nì meeladaan pu.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Meela sililaŋki gbanti nín kaa ŋān̄ kuseeunee puee, ní binib tikpil nìn là kí yīkì niin, bi yaan ŋūǹ kí bà meela sililaŋki Feeniisi, Kreeti tiŋki kin nìn túliń ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, kí kàl̄ niin kuseeu ń jītí. Kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kun nìn jítì tiŋku puee bɔti

english_verse: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
translation_verse: Kubuŋu kubɔ nyánní ŋŋaŋgan pú ki kíĺ ki bíi jītí fiii fiii. Niinee ní bi dākafì yii bi làá ŋmā kí bà laakin bi bàà màkēe, ní ki dáaĺ dikújal din ŋúb́ meela nnyiminee ki cúu kútì, ní ki búntì ki kpākaǹ ki pìlīǹ Kreeti tiŋkugbandi.

english_verse: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
translation_verse: An kaa yúntì, kpalaayee ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kun bi yíì Urakilɔneeyee nyánní Kreeti jooŋŋin ki sīntìń,

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: ki dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ meela. Taa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiba kí pèefì meela, asee ti nín yāntì ku yōoǹ-ti ki kpáàa búntèe.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Ní ti cūtìi jítì kitimbilii kin bí tiŋku kansikinee bi yíì-kì yii Kooda. Nì falaakpaŋkpaan ní ti dāa nín ŋúń ki cúú buŋalimbu bun nìn nɔ̀b̄ meelee kitiŋ gbanti caŋin,

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: ki dáaliń-bu ki kɔ́ǹ meelan, ní ki dū iŋmii ki bóob́ ki māntìi tú meela taapu. Bi nín nìn fàŋkí yii tí taa cùú lítí Siirtii bul kpaanceetii puee, ní bi sīntì iŋaabu taapu, ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee cáá-ti ki cáa nín cá.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Ku nín gbíntìi mɔ̄tìi páb́-tee pu, ní kutaa wúntèe bi dū tinyɔmpuwan tiba ki tɔ́ tiŋkun.

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: Winta dalee, ní bíǹ bi-ba dū tin bi cáa kpòotī meelee ki tɔ́ nnyimin.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Iwiin tikpil poonee, taa ti ká ŋwìiń nì iŋmalbijaa, ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee gbíntìi jītí iwiin kɔkɔ ki pɔ̄ɔ̄. Niinee taa ti dàkafī gba yii ti làá ŋmátí.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Áli an yúntì bin nìn kā meelanee kaa jíń tiba. Niinee ní Pɔɔl yúl̀ bi-kansikin ki bí yii: «Ti-yab, ni yaa nìn pílifiǹ-mee, taa bàà yíkìń Kreeti. Taa bàà kāntí falaa nì asaluu un bí nee.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee m mèé-ni, ní pɔ́ɔǹ ni-ba, kun puee ni-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa làá wāŋkì, asee meela baba di làá bīil̀.

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Kun puee kunyeeu nee, Unimbɔti un yì-mi m nóó-uee túnní u-tuuŋŋu ŋubɔ m-cee,

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: ní ŋu bí-mi yii: <Pɔɔl, taa fàŋkì! Asee á bà gɔminakpaan nimbiin bí sòoǹ a-bɔti. Míǹ puee, Unimbɔti làá ŋá-si tiŋan kí yàntī bin kɔkɔwoooo kā meelanee ń ŋmátí!>

english_verse: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
translation_verse: An puee ti-yab, pɔ́ɔm̀maan ni-ba! Kun puee m cáá dimákal Unimbɔti pu yii u nín lī puee, míǹ ní án làá ŋá.

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Ama án làá cáá-ti kí kpàkan̄ kitimbilii kiba kin nnyim māntì ki túee kpaanceetiŋu laaba ní.»

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi cúú iŋmii ki cúu bútì, ní akújalee gbíntì nnyimin, ní bi cúú ŋŋmii ki cúu kútì tiwan tin kpòotī meelee, ní ki kpátì ŋŋaabu ŋun poon kubuŋu kóò ki téekí meelee. Kubuŋu bíi téekí meelee, ní bi dūu dī tiŋku gbandi watil pú.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Bimeelaŋaaliliibi nìn nyàab̀ kí nyā meelanee, ní bi gíiǹ buŋalimbu bun nìn nɔ̀b̄ meelee ki tɔ́ nnyimin, ní ki mɔ́ntí yii bíǹ bàà là kí cáá akújal aba kí kúĺ nyɔkɔpu mun ní.

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bi kíǹ ki fàŋkí yii ti-meelau nee ń taa ŋée kí cùú yā ataŋkpee. Míǹ puee ní bi dū akújal anaa ki tɔ́ boon án nīn ŋúb́ meela, ní ki kíǹ ki kā ki pòontí yii kutaa ń wúntí.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl bí usoojakpilee nì u-soojab yii: «Binib nee yaa kaa kāl̀ meelan soooo, naa làá ŋmátí!»

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Niinee ní soojab gíí iŋmii in nɔ̀b̄ buŋalimbuee ki tīl̀, ní bu gbíntì nnyimin.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, m gbàam̄-ni, ní jīmaan tijin, kun puee tijin bɔti páb́ ki tīī ni-maŋfal. Di sá yii ni-kansikin báà ubɔ yikpilku kaa làá wāŋkì.»

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: U lī míǹ ki dóòyee, ní ki yōoǹ kpɔnɔ ki jáam̀ Unimbɔti tijin gbanti pu bi-kɔkɔ nimbiin, ní ki gíí kpɔnɔ ki kíĺ ki bíi ŋmóò.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Niinee ní báà ŋma ká kunyannyaau, ki kíĺ ki bíi ŋmóò.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Bi jíń ki bál̀ee, ki là yii meela ń taa nín̄ gíti nyìm̀ kí nīn bí fúku fukuee, ní bi dū ŋkpɔnɔyim ki dūu tɔ́ nnyimin. Meela wīī

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Kutaa wúntèe, bimeelaŋaaliliibi kaa béè kitiŋ gbanti, ama ní ki ká dibunlɔkɔl diba, digbándi sá dibul ŋma, ní bi bí yii, bi yaan ŋūǹ kí bàà ŋàal̀ meela kí cùnnì niin.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Niinee ní meela cūtìi sàl̄ dibukpaandi diba kansikin ki gbíntì niin, ní u-nyɔkɔpu múĺ dibulin, kaa ti lèekī, ní tinyiŋgban dɔ́miń ki fáá ki wīī boon.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Niinee ní soojab bàà là kí kpɔ̀ bisarkadambi, yii bí taa ŋée kí wāŋkì nnyim kí nyā kí sāǹ kí kátí.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Ama usoojakpilee là kí fīī Pɔɔlee, ní ki yíì yii bí taa ŋá míǹ, ní ki bí yii bin ŋūǹ nnyimee ń péé kí yùkū kí tìin̄ kí wāŋkì kí nīn cá ditiŋkugbandi,

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: ní bin kíǹee ń nīn cáá idɔ àá ameelakati kí nīn wáŋkí ki pá bi-boon. Míǹ ní ti ŋá, ní ti-kɔkɔ nyáń dibuŋgbándi nì alaafiya.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: Ti ŋmátì ki dóòyee, ní ki nín béè yii bi yíì kitiŋ gbanti Maalti.

english_verse: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
translation_verse: Binib bin nìn kóò niinee baasii ŋúb́-ti mmɔntiimin. Utaa nìn kíĺ ki kíǹ ki nì, ní tiwool bí. Míǹ puee bi nìn kpāā ŋŋmi ní ki yíiń-ti ní ti-kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ ki māntìi tú ŋŋmee ki wùl̀.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Ní Pɔɔl cūtìi báań tikpaŋkpaal dibɔ́ndi diba, ukoowaati kā niin, ki cáań ki tɔ́ ŋŋmin. Niinee ní ŋŋmifaam píĺ ukoowaatee, ní u nyáń ki jú u-ŋal ki báaǹ.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Binibee nín ká yii ukoobu lúń Pɔɔl ŋal puee, ní bi bíi lì tɔb cee yii: «Uninja nee máaǹ ki làá nīn sá unikpɔl ní. Di sá yii, min kɔkɔwoooo u ŋmátì ki nyáń tiŋkunee, ti-waal deedeedaan kaa pú-u mpaan ú tɔ̄ u-ba.»

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Pɔɔl gbéeǹ ukoobuee ki fíiǹ ki tɔ́ ŋŋmin, kaa gbìl̄ tiba.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: Ní bi kíǹ ki kā ki kpèé yii an làá díkáaa, u làá lítí kí kpú niin niin. Ama bi kāl̀ ki cíitìi kpēē ki gīī, tiba kaa ŋá-uee, ní bi kpántì bi-landɔkɔi, ki kíǹ ki bíi cáá yii an sá diwaal diba ní.

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Niin caŋin ní kitiŋ gbanti bɔtiu un bi yíì Pubiliyusee saaku nìn bí. Kijapaayee nìn fōō-ti mmɔntiimin, ti dōoǹ u-dumpu iwiin ita.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Pubiliyusi baa nìn dɔ̄ u-wunti píĺ kpaŋkpam ki cɔ̀tī. Ní Pɔɔl cūtìi māntì u-pu, ní ki mēē ki tīī-u, ní ki dū u-ŋalii ki páaǹ u-pu, ní u pɔ́ɔkì.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Niinee ní bibunliibi bin bí niinee kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki ká dicáaǹdi.

english_verse: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
translation_verse: Binibee nìn ŋá-ti tiŋan tikpil, ní daliŋkin ti làá yīkèe, bi nìn tīī-ti tin kɔkɔ ti lèe. Pɔɔl bàn̄ Room

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Iŋmal ita boonee ní ti kɔ́ meela un nìn yúl̀ kitiŋ gbantin kuseeu jítèe. U nìn nyánní Aleekisandirii, bi kpítì awaa ali ki nántiǹ atab ki nákáǹ u-pu.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Ti bàn̄ Sirakuusi tiŋkinee, ní ki kāl̀ niin iwiin ita.

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: Niinee, ti yíkì ki kpàkaǹ ditiŋkugbandee, ní ki tin dūu bàn̄ Reejiyoo. Kutaa wúntèe, ní kubuŋu nyánní ti-boon pú ki kíĺ ki bíi jītí, ní ti dū iwiin ili ki dūu bàn̄ Pusɔl.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ gbantin ní ti nìn ká nnabiyaamu mubɔ, ní bi bí yii tí kàl̄ bi-cee kinyɔŋ kiba. Ti nín cōom̀ pu ki dāa bàn̄ Roomee dee.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Nnabiyaamu mun bí Roomee nín gbìl̄ ti-puee, ní bi yíkìi dɔ́miń áli Apiyusi nyɔŋkin nì kitimbilii kin bi yíì Inicaŋkɔŋkoon itee, ki túŋkì-ti. Pɔɔl nín pée ká-bee, ní u bíi nyɔ́ŋkí Unimbɔti ní ki ká kunyannyaau.

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: Ti nín bàn̄ Roomee, ní bi pú Pɔɔl nsan ú nīn kóò u-baba sooja ń nīn cí-u. Pɔɔl sòon̄ Unimbɔti bɔti Room tiŋkin

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Iwiin ita boonee, ní Pɔɔl yíiń Juuda yab kpilib bin nìn kóò Roomee bí kpāfì u-cee. Bi dɔ́miń ki kpáfèe, ní u bí-bi yii: «M-nabiyaamu, maa kpáàa ŋá ti-samaau tiba, kaa yīntiǹ ti-naanjab koobiliŋ mun. Ama bi cúú-mi Jeerusaleem, ki dū-mi ki tīī Room yab.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Ní bíǹ bālifì-mi anyɔɔbun, ní ki bàà là kí gíiǹ-mi kí líí, kun puee baa ká kun di yì-tì ní bi máaǹ kí kpɔ̀-mee.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
translation_verse: Ama Juuda yab kaa nìn kíí, yii bí taa líí-mi. An di yì-tì ní m nìn bí yii gɔminakpaan ń sòoǹ m-bɔti. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, maa làá bīil̀ m-yab.

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Kun pu ní m là kí ká-ni kí sòoǹ nì nee dee. Di sá yii dipoondi din pu Isirayeel yab kā ki mákée pu ní ikusaka kā m-ŋaan nee.»

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: Ní bi kíí Pɔɔl yii: «Juudee yab kaa ŋmàn̄ní-ti kugbɔŋu kubɔ ki sòon̄ a-bɔti pu tiba. Ti-nabiki kiba mun kaa tí nyánní niin ki dɔ́miń ki máafì-ti a-bɔti tiba. Ubɔ mun kaa tí tùkū-ti yii a ŋá tikpitil tiba.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, ti bàà là kí béé tin tin a cááyee, kun puee ti nyí yii báà laakiŋyee, binib tikpil kaa là nnimbɔtisan ŋun a nóó nee.»

english_verse: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
translation_verse: Ní bi fātìi yóoǹ-u ŋwiin, ní binib tikpil dāa dɔ́miń ŋwiin gbanti. Pɔɔl nìn kíĺ kutaafaau ki cáa sāā kujoou ki cáá Mooyiisi marab nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi gbɔnti ki sòoǹ nì bi Unimbɔti Beel bɔti taapu, ki nyàab̀ bí ŋmā kí fōō Yeesu kí kíí.

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: U nín nìn sòon̄ puee, biba nìn gbìl̄ ki fōō ki kíí, ama biba mun nìn yíì, kaa fōō ki kíí.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu nìn kɔ́ bi-kansikin. Bi làá nīn cée, ní Pɔɔl lī-bi dinyɔɔbundi nee yii: «Tiŋman, an sá ibaamɔn ní Unimbɔti Fam dī u-bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya pu dooooyee ki sòon̄ nì ni-naanjab, yii:

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: <Cù binib nee cee kí tùkù-bi yii: Ni làá dāá gbìl̄ nì ni-tafaliŋ ní kaa nyí taapu, ki làá dāá nīn kpèé nì ni-nimbiliŋ ní kaa wāĺ.

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: Di sá yii binib gbanti pɔbiliŋ gbìfì, bi kpáá bi-tafaliŋ ki ŋúb́ bi-nimbiliŋ. Baa là kí nīn wāĺ, kaa là kí nīn gbìl̀, kaa là bi-landɔkɔi mun ń béé taapu, bí bàà gítiń m-cee ḿ cáaǹ-bi!>»

english_verse: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl lī an nyɔɔbuŋŋee ki dóòyee ní Juuda yab búntì ki còom̄ ki kpákà bi-ŋmaniŋma tikpil.]

english_verse: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl nìn kāl̀ abin ali amɔn kudii kun u fōō ki pà ki kóòyee poon, ki nìn fòol̄ bin kɔkɔ dòoń u-ceeyee.

english_verse: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_verse: U nìn sòoǹ Unimbɔti Beel pu, ki dàkà ti-Dindaan Yeesu Kriisitoo bɔti nì tininjati, ubɔ kaa páb́-u.

english_verse: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
translation_verse: Man Pɔɔl un sá Yeesu Kriisitoo tɔntɔnliu, Unimbɔti yíiń-mi ki gāntì ḿ nīn sá Yeesu kpambal kí sòoǹ u-bɔmɔntiitee di jáaḿ-ni.

english_verse: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
translation_verse: Dooooyee ní Unimbɔti nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliibi pu ki pōoǹ-ti u-bɔmɔntiiti gbanti ki ŋá u-gbɔŋku poon ki síiǹ.

english_verse: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
translation_verse: Ti yaa làá tí kpèè u-Fam min sá circiree jandi púee, Unimbɔti nín fīkitì-u ditaŋkpiilinee, u dàkā nì mpɔn yii u sá u-Jipɔɔn.

english_verse: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
translation_verse: U-pu ní m ká diyimɔɔl kí nīn sá u-kpambal kí tīī Kriisitoo tinyool, án nín làá ŋá pu atimbun kɔkɔ nib ń fōō-u kí kíí kí nīn tɔ́-uee.

english_verse: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: Nimbi Room yab bin Unimbɔti yíiń ní nīn kíǹ ki sá Yeesu Kriisitoo yabee mun kútì poon.

english_verse: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
translation_verse: Nimbi ní m ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee, nimbi bin kɔkɔ Unimbɔti néeń ki yíiń ní nīn sá u-yabee. Ti-Baa Unimbɔti nì ti-Dindaan Yeesu Kriisitoo ń ŋá-ni tiŋan kí tīī-ni ŋgbansɔŋfi! Pɔɔl là kí cùú màntì Kriisitoo yab bin bí Roomee pu

english_verse: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
translation_verse: Mpeekaaminee, m dī Yeesu Kriisitoo pu ki jáaḿ m-Nimbɔtiu ni-kɔkɔ pu, kun puee bi sòoǹ ni nín fōō Unimbɔti bɔti ki kíí puee ilaan kɔkɔ.

english_verse: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
translation_verse: M téetí ni-pu múlmul m-wimmeem poon. Unimbɔti un m nóó nì m-pɔbil kɔkɔ ki sòoǹ u-Jipɔɔn bɔmɔntiitee nyí yii tin m lèe sá ibaamɔn.

english_verse: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
translation_verse: Baabadal m-wimmeem poonee, m bàlifī Unimbɔti yii an yaa sá u-lammi, ú pɔ̄-mi nsan ŋyunti nee ḿ dāan̄ kí màntì ni-pu.

english_verse: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
translation_verse: Di sá yii m-nimbiliŋ máǹ ḿ dāan̄ ni-cee kí cáań-ni Circir Fam pɔ̄kaati tiba tin ŋūǹ kí kūtì-ni mpɔnee.

english_verse: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
translation_verse: M nín làá lì puee di sá tí ŋmā kí dū ti-fookiiu un ti-kɔkɔ cáá Unimbɔti puee kí tīī tɔb kunyannyaau.

english_verse: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
translation_verse: Nnabiyaamu, m là ní béé yii m mākafì miŋa nì miŋa kí bàà dāan̄ ni-cee, ama nìn díǹ maa ká nsan. M bàà là yii m-tundi ń lòoǹ abil ni-cee kii dì nín lòon̄ atimbun ŋin kíǹee cee puee.

english_verse: It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome. The Power of the Good News
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní m-nimbiliŋ máǹ ḿ dāan̄ kí sòoǹ Tibɔmɔntiil gbanti kí tùkù nimbi bin bí Roomee mun. Mpɔn ŋun bí Unimbɔti Bɔmɔntiitinee

english_verse: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: An kaa cáá-mi icoo ḿ sòoǹ Tibɔmɔntiil gbanti, kun puee tì sá Unimbɔti pɔŋŋu ki fìil̄ bin fòol̄-tì ki kíikée. Mpeepeekaamee, Juuda yab, ní boonee ki dāa nín kpáaǹ bin kaa sá Juuda yabee mun.

english_verse: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
translation_verse: Tibɔtee dàkà-ti nsan ŋun Unimbɔti dì ki kpántí unil deedeedaan u-nimbiinee: an sá unil ń fōō kí kíí ní. An kífí nì fookii ní kí tin kúntí nì fookii, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ Unimbɔti gbɔŋku poon puee yii: «Deedeedaan kāntí dimaŋfal u-fookiiu pu ní.» Binib nín ŋáań ikpiti puee

english_verse: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
translation_verse: Di sá yii doooo yilpu ní Unimbɔti dàkà u-ŋuul nnibiyaamu bimbikpitim pu. Baa tɔ́ úǹ Unimbɔti ní ki ŋáań ikpiti. Bi-tuŋkpitiŋ kaa yàntī ibaamɔn ń tɔ̄ i-tundi bi-ni.

english_verse: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
translation_verse: Kun pu ní Unimbɔti làá dáaĺ bi-tafalee di sá bi wál̀ kun unil ŋūǹ kí ká kí béé Unimbɔtee. An sá Unimbɔti di nyántì ki dàkā-bi.

english_verse: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
translation_verse: Di sá yii doooo Unimbɔti nín náań yilpu nì taapuee, atuun ŋin u túńee ŋūǹ kí yàntī unil ń béé u-ban Unimbɔti bimbim min baa wāĺee, an dàkà yii u-pɔŋŋu ŋun kaa kúntée nì u-nimbɔtiiti. Mimmee unil kaa ŋūǹ kí ká nnaakpal yii waa nyí-u.

english_verse: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
translation_verse: Bi nyí Unimbɔti, ní kaa pàkà-u, kaa jáaḿ-u u-ŋanti pu min máaǹ bí jāam̀-uee. Bi fá-u, ki nóó bi-landɔkɔi in kaa bí deedeeyee, ki kpántì bigbaambi, ní bi-pɔbiliŋ kɔ́ dibɔmbɔndin.

english_verse: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
translation_verse: Bi bí ki gà bi-biŋŋi yii bi cáá iciin, kaa nyí yii bi wáatì ní.

english_verse: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
translation_verse: An nín bàà sá bí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔti tinyooldaan un kaa kúùyee puee, ní bi nyɔ́ŋkí tiwan tin bi kpítì ki nántiǹ unil un kúùyee nì inoon nì tiwaŋkuti nì tin fù kitiŋee mun.

english_verse: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
translation_verse: Kii bi-pɔbiliŋ poon bi nín lēē kí nīn ŋáań tijɔkɔndee puee, Unimbɔti dū-bi ki líiǹ tijɔkɔndi, bí nīn bíiĺ bi-ba.

english_verse: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
translation_verse: Bi dū Unimbɔti bɔti tin sá ibaamɔnee ki fá, ki yōoǹ inyimɔn, ní ki nóó ki tòotī tiwan tin Unimbɔti náańee, ní ki fá unáanli u-ba, úǹ un máaǹ bí nīn nyɔ́ŋkí-u baabadal kí nīn cée! Ameeni.

english_verse: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
translation_verse: Míǹ pu ní Unimbɔti dū-bi ki líiǹ kukpeeu kun kɔ̄ntí-bi icooyee. Di sá yii an nín bàà sá binimpoobi ń mɔ̄ǹ bininjabee, ní bi fàtīi cáa mɔ́ń bi-nimpujutiibi.

english_verse: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
translation_verse: Míǹ mbaantiim, bininjab kaa ti là binimpoobi, ní ki kíǹ ki là tɔb ŋmaniŋma tikpil ki dɔ̀ nì tɔb. Bi-tuuŋŋi gbanti cáań ditafadaaldi din sá bi-paati tin máaǹ-bee ki tɔ́ bi-pu.

english_verse: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
translation_verse: Kii bi-landɔkɔi nín sá yii Unimbɔti kaa máaǹ bí béé-uee puee, Unimbɔti dū-bi ki líì, ní bi-landɔkɔi gátì, ní bi kíǹ ki ŋáań min kaa máaǹ bí ŋée.

english_verse: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
translation_verse: Bi kpántì binikpitib mbaamɔm, ki ŋáań min kaa ŋān̄ee, ki cáá nnimbitaataam nì ntoom, ki cáá kináŋ nì nnikpaakoon tikpil, ki néeń kujaau, ki ŋmàtíǹ tɔb, ki kíiĺ tɔb, ki sòoǹ ki bíiĺ tɔb,

english_verse: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
translation_verse: ki sìí tɔb. Bi sá Unimbɔti nannanliibi, ki kpèé ki sɔ́kɔ̀ binib, ki yòontí bi-ba yilpu, ki dàkà bi-ba, ki nāantí isampɔɔn in pu bi dì ki ŋáań ikpitee, ní kaa tɔ́ bi-nab nì bi-baabi.

english_verse: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
translation_verse: Baa cáá iciin. Bi yaa pōoǹee, baa ŋáań tin bi pōoǹee. Baa cáá dineendi, kaa sūǹ bin kíǹee saai.

english_verse: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_verse: Nì min kamaa bi baasii nyí tiŋan yii Unimbɔti bí yii bin bin ŋáań ikpiti gbantee máaǹ ŋkúmee, bi gbíntì ki ŋáań ikpiti gbanti. Tin gíti lákatèe di sá bi bí yii bin ŋáań ikpiti gbantee di ŋáań min kítèe.

english_verse: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
translation_verse: Ŋma ní a sá, sii un sòoǹ bin béeyee bɔti yii bi nín ŋáań puee kaa ŋān̄ee. Aa cáá nnaakpal ŋubɔ kí dāá kpáĺ. Di sá yii sii un bíi sòoǹ bin béeyee bɔti yii bi nín ŋáań puee kaa ŋān̄, ní ki ŋáań míǹ a-bee, a bíi kù a-ba bɔti dee.

english_verse: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
translation_verse: Ti nyí yii Unimbɔti nín sòoǹ ki kù bin ŋáań an tuuŋŋee bɔtee, u cáá ibaamɔn.

english_verse: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
translation_verse: Mimmee, sii un kù bin béeyee bɔti ki mun ŋáań míǹ mbaantiimee, a dàkafī yii a làá nyā Unimbɔti bɔsooŋyinaaa?

english_verse: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
translation_verse: Unimbɔti ŋanti tin u cáá tikpilee, nì u-mɔtiiki nì u-niti ní a cáa kpèé fámaaa? Aa nyí yii Unimbɔti nín ŋáań-si tiŋan puee, u là kí tūtuǹ-si á kpántí a-bimbim níii?

english_verse: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
translation_verse: Di sá yii a nín pɔ́ɔkí a-pɔbil pu ki yíití, kaa là kí kpántí a-bimbimee, a mɔ̀tīi kútí a-ba ditafadaaldi din a làá fōō Unimbɔti ŋuul dalee, ŋwiin ŋun Unimbɔti làá dāá dū ibaamɔn kí sòoǹ binib bɔtee ní.

english_verse: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
translation_verse: Yaadal ní u làá pà báà ŋma u-tundi paati.

english_verse: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
translation_verse: U làá dū dimaŋfal din kaa cáá dikúntilee kí tīī bin pɔ̄ɔntí ki ŋáań tiŋan ki nyàab̀ tinyool nì ipampaka nì dimaŋfal din bí kaa kúntée.

english_verse: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
translation_verse: Bin yíì, kaa là kí nóó u-baamɔŋyi ki là kí nīn nóó tin kaa ŋān̄ee, u làá dāá fōō diŋuul bi-pu kí dáaĺ bi-tafal.

english_verse: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Falaa nì dinimbinaamandi dɔ̄ ki cí bin kɔkɔwoooo ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee. Juuda yab tafal ní Unimbɔti làá péé péé kí dáaĺ kí wàatī, ní kí dāá nín dáaĺ bin kaa sá Juuda yabee tafal.

english_verse: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ama, tinyool nì ipampaka nì ŋgbansɔŋfi dɔ̄ ki cí bin kɔkɔwoooo ŋáań tiŋanee. Juuda yab ní bi làá dāá péé kí tīī kí wàatī, ní kí nín tīī bin kaa sá Juuda yabee.

english_verse: God doesn't have any favorites!
translation_verse: Di sá yii Unimbɔti kaa gàntī binib.

english_verse: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
translation_verse: Bin kaa béè marab bin Unimbɔti tīī Mooyiisee yaa ŋá ikpitee, bi làá wāŋkì, ama marabee ní baa làá dūú sòoǹ bi-bɔti. Ní bin kɔkɔ nyí marab gbanti ní ki ŋáań ikpitee, marabee ní bi làá dūú sòoǹ bidambi bɔti.

english_verse: God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
translation_verse: Kaa sá bin pílifí marabee di sá deedeedambi Unimbɔti nimbiin. Ama bin bin ŋáań marabee nín lī puee, bíǹ ní bi dāa yíì deedeedambi.

english_verse: This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned,
translation_verse: An dàkà yii marab tuuŋŋi taapu ŋmàn̄ bi-pɔbiliŋ poon. Min máaǹee dòoń bi-neeŋyin, ní bi-landɔkɔi tùkù-bi ŋyunti ŋubɔee, tin bi yaa ŋá an ŋān̄ee, nì tin bi yaa ŋá an kaa ŋān̄ee.

english_verse: when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says. The Jews and the Law
translation_verse: Ŋwiin ŋun Unimbɔti làá yàntī Yeesu Kriisitoo ń bìitī nnibiyaamu tuuŋŋi ŋin bí dibalinee pu kí sòoǹee, tin tin báà ŋma làá dāá kée dee, kii Tibɔmɔntiil tin man Pɔɔl sòoǹee nín lì puee. Juuda yab nì mara

english_verse: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
translation_verse: Ama sii un bi yíì Juuda yɔu, a máká Mooyiisi marab pu, ki dàkà a-ba yii a nyí Unimbɔti,

english_verse: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
translation_verse: ki nyí u nín là puee, marab dàkà-si á lēē laakin ŋān̄ee.

english_verse: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
translation_verse: A nyí a-ba yii a ŋūǹ kí kpòotī bijɔfub kí nīn sá ŋwalifi kí tīī bin bí dibɔmbɔndinee,

english_verse: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
translation_verse: ki là kí nīn dàkà bin nimbiliŋ kaa ŋúbitèe nì bin kaa nyí tiba nnimbɔtisan poonee, kun puee a béè marab ní marabee dàkā-si iciin nì ibaamɔn kɔkɔ.

english_verse: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
translation_verse: Too, ba ŋá ní sii dàkà bin kíǹee, ní kaa dàkà a-ba ní? Ba ŋá ní sii un sòoǹ ki tùkù bin kíǹee yii bí taa yɔ̀ee, yù ní?

english_verse: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
translation_verse: Sii un lì yii an kaa máaǹ bí ŋá tilaakpaalee, ba ŋá ní sii ŋáań tilaakpaal ní? Sii un ná awaayee, ba ŋá ní a kóò awaadiinni ki yù tiwan ní?

english_verse: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
translation_verse: Sii un gà a-bindi yii a nyí marabee, ŋyunti ŋun a yìntīǹ marab gbantee, Unimbɔti yindi ní a bíi bíiĺ,

english_verse: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
translation_verse: kii Unimbɔti gbɔŋku poon nín lī puee yii: «Nimbi Juuda yab pu ní bin kaa sá Juuda yabee sòoǹ ki bíiĺ Unimbɔti yindi.»

english_verse: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
translation_verse: A yaa tɔ́ marabee, ní digiil din a gííyee ŋān̄ ki tīī-si, ama a yaa yìntī marabee, nì min kɔkɔ bi gíí-see, an sá fám ní.

english_verse: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
translation_verse: Unil un kaa gííyee yaa kpáafí marabee, nì min kɔkɔ baa gíí-uee, Unimbɔti kpèé-u kii u gííyee ní.

english_verse: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
translation_verse: Un baa gíí, u nóó marabee làá dāá jīǹ sii un gíí ki cáá marab gbɔŋku ki gíti yìntī marabee ibaamɔn.

english_verse: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
translation_verse: An kaa sá un bi wāĺ yii u sá Juuda yɔu, bi gíí-u, u cáá kudaaŋŋu u-wunti puee di sá Juuda yɔu ubaamɔn:

english_verse: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_verse: un sá Juuda yɔu ubaamɔnee di sá un sá Juuda yɔu u-pɔbil poonee. Bi gíí-u nì digiil din sá Unimbɔti Fam gíitamee, kaa sá marab gbɔŋku nín lī puee gíitam. Unimbɔti di pàkà an niliuee, an kaa sá binib di pàkà-u.

english_verse: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
translation_verse: A yaa sá Juuda yɔuee, a gíti cáá diyimɔɔl dibaaa? Àá digiil sá tiwammɔntiilaaa?

english_verse: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, bi-yimɔɔl jítiǹ bin béeyee yal kpataaa. Diyimɔɔpeepeekaal di sá Unimbɔti nín dū u-bɔti ki ŋúbiǹ Juuda yabee.

english_verse: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
translation_verse: Ama bi-kansikin biba kaa ŋúń ki yúl̀ deedee. Mimmee, bi nín kaa yúl̀ deedeeyee puee di làá yàntī Unimbɔti deedeeu ń ŋá fámaaa?

english_verse: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
translation_verse: Aayee, kpataaa! Unimbɔti di làá nīn pée sá deedeedaan, ní binib kɔkɔ ń nīn sá binyimɔndambi, kii Unimbɔti gbɔŋku nín lī puee yii: «Binib máaǹ kí ká a nín sá deedee puee tin a sòoǹee poon, ní bi yaa sòon̄ a-bɔtee, bí ká yii a cáá ibaamɔn.»

english_verse: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
translation_verse: Ti nín ŋáań ikpiti iŋyee yaa dàkà yii Unimbɔti sá umɔntee, mimmee u nín dátí ti-tafal ti-kpitii puee, waa bí deedee deeyaa! .

english_verse: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
translation_verse: Aayee kpataaa! Unimbɔti yaa kaa bàà bí deedee, waan ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ duulinya bɔti.

english_verse: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
translation_verse: Mimmee, m-nyimɔŋyi yaa ŋūǹ kí yàntī Unimbɔti baamɔŋyi ń nyā mpaampiin pu bí wāl̀ kí tīī-u tinyoolee, ba pu ní bi làá gíti sòoǹ kí kpɔ̀ m-bɔti yii m sá unikpiti?

english_verse: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
translation_verse: Míǹ puee, tí lì yii: «Tí nīn ŋáań ikpiti, án dāá kpántí tiŋanaa!» Míǹ ní bin mɔ́ntí nnyimɔn ki tūntí ti-puee lì. Bin sòoǹ ti-pu mimmee máaǹ ditafadaaldi. Ubɔ kaa bí ki bí deedee

english_verse: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
translation_verse: Mimmee, timbi Juuda yab jítiǹ binib bin kíǹeeee? Aayee, kpataaa! Kii m nín bàà pée lī puee, Juuda yab nì bin kaa sá Juuda yabee kɔkɔ bí ikpitin.

english_verse: The Scriptures tell us, “No one is acceptable to God!
translation_verse: Kii Unimbɔti gbɔŋku nín lī puee, yii: «Unil báà ubɔ kaa bí ki bí deedee, báà ubaanti, an kpá.

english_verse: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa bí ki cáá iciin. Ubɔ kaa bí ki nyàab̀ Unimbɔti.

english_verse: They have all turned away and are worthless. There isn't one person who does right.
translation_verse: Bi-kɔkɔ yīntiǹ-u ki wáŋkì, báà ubɔ kaa bí ki ŋáań tiŋan, báà uniseen, an kpá.

english_verse: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
translation_verse: Dikaakul din wāā ki núùyee nín bí puee, míǹ ní tibɔti tin bí bi-neeŋyinee bí. Bi cáá bi-limbiliŋ ki kíiĺ binib, bi-nyunculiŋ nín tábití ki sòoǹ tiŋyee sá tilool kii ukoowaati lootee ní.

english_verse: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
translation_verse: Bi-nyɔmmu poon gbí mbusu nì ntuntun.

english_verse: These people quickly become violent.
translation_verse: Bi yáb̀ nnikpaakoon pu.

english_verse: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
translation_verse: Laakin kamaa bi yaa cūtèe, see bí cáá bi-timbiilii nì falaa niin.

english_verse: They don't know how to live in peace.
translation_verse: Baa nyí ŋgbansɔŋfi saŋŋu.

english_verse: They don't even fear God.”
translation_verse: Baa fàŋkí Unimbɔti báà fiii.»

english_verse: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
translation_verse: Ti nyí yii marab nín sòoǹ tiŋyee kɔkɔee, bi sòoǹ ki tìì bin bin Unimbɔti nìn tīī u-marabee ní. Míǹ puee, ubɔ kaa dāa cáá kinyɔkɔ kí wàan̄ kí tīī nnaakpal. Kitiŋ pu yab kɔkɔ dāa béetí yii bi sá binikpitib Unimbɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
translation_verse: Di sá yii unil nín ŋúb̀ marab mmɔntiimin puee kaa ŋūǹ kí yàntī ú nīn bí deedee Unimbɔti nimbiin, kun puee marab tundi di pée sá bí dàkà binib kun di sá ikpitee. Min ní Unimbɔti dì kí fīī unilee

english_verse: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, Unimbɔti dàkā min ní unil ŋūǹ kí dī kí kpántí deedeedaan u-nimbiin kí taa dī marab puee: Mooyiisi gbɔnti nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi mun nìn sòon̄ an bɔti pu.

english_verse: God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ.
translation_verse: An sá ti nín fōō Yeesu Kriisitoo ki kííyee pu ní Unimbɔti kpántì-ti deedeedambi u-nimbiin. Unimbɔti kaa gàntī binib, an sá ki tīī bin kɔkɔ fōō Yeesu ki kííyee,

english_verse: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
translation_verse: kun puee báà ŋma ŋá ikpiti ki dátiǹ Unimbɔti nyooti.

english_verse: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti ŋáań-ti tiŋan ki yàntī ti kpántí deedee nib u-nimbiin faalaa, Yeesu Kriisitoo nín dū u-ba ki fīī-ti ki líìyee pu.

english_verse: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
translation_verse: Mimmee, unil cáá nsan kí dàkà u-baaa? Aayee, nsan kaa bí báà fiii. Ba pu ní a ká difiil? A nín nóó Mooyiisi marabee puɔɔɔ? Aayee, an sá a nín fōō ki kííyee pu.

english_verse: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
translation_verse: Ti nyí yii unil un fōō Yeesu ki kííyee di kpántí deedeedaan Unimbɔti nimbiin, an kaa sá marab bin u nóóyee pu.

english_verse: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
translation_verse: An yaan sá marab puee, mimmee, Unimbɔti bàà sá Juuda yab ŋmaniŋma Nimbɔtiu naa! Waa bàà sá bin kaa sá Juuda yabee mun Nimbɔtiu. Ama u sá báà ŋma Nimbɔtiu ní.

english_verse: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_verse: Mimmee, an dàkà yii ti yaa fōō Yeesu ki kííyee, taa ti dù marab kí yíiń tiba deeyaaa? Aayee, an kaa sá míǹ. Ŋyunti gbanti ní ti nín tìì marab mpɔn.

english_verse: Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham?
translation_verse: Mimmee, ti làá sòoǹ diyimɔɔl din timbi Juuda yab naanja Abraam nìn kée pu yii ba?

english_verse: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
translation_verse: An yaa sá Abraam tunnyaaŋŋi pu ní Unimbɔti yíiń-u deedeedaanee, u bàà ŋūǹ kí nīn dàkà u-ba. Ama waa ŋūǹ kí dàkà u-ba Unimbɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working.
translation_verse: Unil un túń ditundee, bi yaa pàn̄-uee, baa lì yii bi pú-u fám, ama u-tundi paati ní u fōō.

english_verse: But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him.
translation_verse: Un kaa ŋá diba, ama ní ki fōō Unimbɔti un di yàntī binikpitib kpántí deedeedambee ki kííyee, Unimbɔti yíì udaan deedeedaan u-fookiiu pu ní.

english_verse: In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
translation_verse: An di yāntì ní Daafiidi nìn lī yii un bí dipɔɔpindinee di sá unil un Unimbɔti yíiń deedeedaan an kaa sá u-tuuŋŋi puee.

english_verse: “What a blessing when God forgives our sins and our evil deeds. What a blessing when the Lord erases our sins from his book.”
translation_verse: Un ní ti-Dindaan kaa ti lì yii u ŋá ikpitee bí dipɔɔpindinaaa!»

english_verse: Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.
translation_verse: Mimmee, dipɔɔpindi gbanti sá ki tīī Juuda yab bin gífì dikpancandee ŋmaniŋma, kaa sá ki tīī bin kíǹeeee? Ti dáá ká yii: «Abraam nín fōō Unimbɔti ki kííyee pu ní Unimbɔti yíiń-u deedeedaan.»

english_verse: Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Boonee ní Unimbɔti bí Abraam ń gíí dikpancandi án nīn sá kudaaŋŋu yii u sá deedeedaan u-fookiiu pu. Míǹ puee, bin kɔkɔ fōō Unimbɔti ki kíí, kaa gífì ki sá deedeedambi Unimbɔti nimbiinee, bi-baa di sá Abraam,

english_verse: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
translation_verse: ní u sá bin gííyee mun baa. An kaa sá bi nín gííyee ŋmaniŋma pu, an sá bi nín fōō ki kííyee pu, kii ti-baa Abraam mun nín nìn fōō ki kíí pu, kaa láá gííyee. Abraam fōō Unimbɔti poondi nì fookii

english_verse: God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti nìn pōoǹ Abraam nì u-naantiibi yii u làá dāá dū duulinya kí tīī-bi. An kaa sá Abraam nín nìn nóó marabee pu ní u nìn pōoǹ-u míǹ, ama an sá u nín nìn fōō Unimbɔti ki kíí Unimbɔti yíì-u deedeedaanee pu.

english_verse: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
translation_verse: An yaa sá tí nīn tɔ́ marab ní kí fōō tin Unimbɔti pōoǹ-tee, mimmee fookii ŋá fám dee, ní Unimbɔti poondi kaa ti bí tiban.

english_verse: God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken.
translation_verse: Di sá yii marab cāabìń ditafadaaldi ní, ní laakin marab kpée, marab yìntitam mun kpá.

english_verse: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
translation_verse: Mimmee, ti ká yii ti nín fōō Unimbɔti ki kííyee pu ní ti fòol̄ tin u pòontí-tee. An sá Unimbɔti ŋanti pu ní an bí míǹ ki tīī Abraam maaliŋun yab kɔkɔ. An kaa sá ki tīī bin tɔ́ Mooyiisi marabee ŋmaniŋma, an sá ki kpáaǹ bin kɔkɔ fōō Unimbɔti ki kíí kii Abraam nín nìn fōō ki kíí puee. Timbi bin kɔkɔ fōō ki kííyee baa di sá Abraam.

english_verse: The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti lī u-gbɔŋku poon míǹ ní yii: «M dū-si ki kpántì atimbun tikpil baa.» Unimbɔti un fìkitī bitaŋkpiibi ki wāĺ tin kaa láá bée kii tì bée, Unimbɔti un pu Abraam nìn mákée yāntì u sá ti-baa.

english_verse: God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations.
translation_verse: Abraam nìn fōō ki kíí ní ki máká, nì min kɔkɔ dimákal diba nìn pée kpée, ní ki lafun dūu kpántì atimbun tikpil baa. Kii Unimbɔti nín nìn pée tùkū-u puee yii: «A-maaliŋun yab nín làá nīn wīikí min nyɔkɔmee dee.»

english_verse: But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
translation_verse: Waa fá u-mákal kí dàkafì yii Unimbɔti kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tin u pōoǹee, ama u-mákal tīī-u mpɔn ní u nyɔ́ŋkì Unimbɔti,

english_verse: Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised.
translation_verse: ki béè u-pɔbilin yii, ibaamɔn, Unimbɔti cáá mpɔn ki làá ŋá min u pōoǹee.

english_verse: So God accepted him,
translation_verse: An pu ní Unimbɔti yíiń-u deedeedaan.

english_verse: just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham.
translation_verse: An kaa sá úǹ baba pu ní an ŋmàn̄ yii Unimbɔti yíiń-u deedeedaan.

english_verse: They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life.
translation_verse: An sá ti mun pu, kun puee Unimbɔti kpèé-ti yii ti mun sá deedeedambi dimákal din ti cáá úǹ Unimbɔti un fīkitì ti-Dindaan Yeesu ditaŋkpiilinee pu.

english_verse: God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
translation_verse: Ti-kpitii pu ní Yeesu kpíì, ní ki fīkitì, ti mun ń ŋmā kí kpántí deedeedambi Unimbɔti nimbiin.

english_verse: By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God.
translation_verse: Mimmee, ti ká yii ti nín fōō-u ki kííyee pu ní ti kpántì deedeedambi Unimbɔti nimbiin, ní ti nì Unimbɔti kansikin ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan Yeesu Kriisitoo pu.

english_verse: Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God.
translation_verse: Yeesu Kriisitoo puee ní ti ŋúń ki jéetì diyimɔɔl din poon ti bí nee, ti nín fōō-u ki kííyee pu. Ní kun mɔ̄ǹ-tee di sá ti cɔ́tí yii ti làá kɔ́ Unimbɔti nyootin.

english_verse: But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure.
translation_verse: Áli gba, ti nín jīǹ falaa puee, an mɔ̄ǹ-ti, kun puee ti nyí yii falaa di yàntī unil ń pɔ́ɔǹ u-ba,

english_verse: that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
translation_verse: Taa cɔ́tí fám, kun puee Unimbɔti pú-ti Circir Fam min di gbēentí ti-pɔbiliŋ u-neendee.

english_verse: Christ died for us at a time when we were helpless and sinful.
translation_verse: Ti nín nìn dáá bí iwɔfineee, ní ŋyunti ŋun Unimbɔti yóoǹee bāań, ní Kriisitoo kpíì binikpitib pu.

english_verse: No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person.
translation_verse: An pɔ̄ɔ̄ unil ń kíí kí kpú deedeedaan pu. An yaa yíì ní ni kāntí ubɔ ń kíí kí kpú unimɔnti pu.

english_verse: But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
translation_verse: Ama Unimbɔti dàkà-ti u nín néeń-ti min bulifee di sá yii, ŋyunti ŋun ti dáá sá binikpitibee, Kriisitoo kpíì ti-pu.

english_verse: But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger.
translation_verse: U nín kpíìyee, ní u-fatikuu yāntì ti kpántì deedeedambi Unimbɔti nimbiin. Kin, an làá ŋá mana ní kɔŋkɔnnee waa làá ŋmā kí fīī-ti tí taa kɔ́ Unimbɔti ŋuulin?

english_verse: Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son.
translation_verse: Dooooyee, ti nìn dáá sá Unimbɔti nannanliibi ní. U-Jipɔɔn kúm di ŋáŋkì ti-kansikin, ní ti mɔ́ɔkì. Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-kansikin mɔ́ɔkì ki dóò, ní u-Jipɔɔn bí dimaŋfalin, kin, án làá gíti ŋá mana ní taa làá ká difiil?

english_verse: And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us. Adam and Christ
translation_verse: Tiba mun gíti sɔ̀: ti-Dindaan Yeesu Kriisitoo yāntì ti nì Unimbɔti kansikin ŋáŋkèe, ní ti bí ki fàal̀ Unimbɔti pu. Adam nì Yeesu bɔŋmantikaati

english_verse: Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die.
translation_verse: Unibaanti Adam pu ní ikpiti dī ki kɔ́nní duulinyan, ní ikpitee cáań ŋkúm, ní báà ŋma kúù, kun puee báà ŋma ŋá ikpiti.

english_verse: Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law.
translation_verse: Dooooyee, kí wàatī Unimbɔti ń nìn tīī Mooyiisi marabee, ikpiti nìn pée bí kitiŋ pu dee. Míǹ ní marab yaa kpá, baa ŋūǹ kí lì yii unil ŋá ikpiti.

english_verse: Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did. In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later.
translation_verse: Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, kí yòon̄ Adam yuntiŋu kí dāá sāā Mooyiisi yuntiŋuee, ŋkúm di nìn jíń báà ŋma, ki kpáaǹ binib bin kaa ŋá ikpiti kii Adam nín ŋá puee. Adam nìn sá Yeesu un dāa dɔ́miń boonee naŋku ní.

english_verse: But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
translation_verse: Ama Adam yìntitam nín cáań-ti tiŋyee kaa pēē nì tin Unimbɔti pūǹ-ti faalaayee. Tiŋman, binib kupaau kpíì unibaanti Adam yìntitam pu, ama Unimbɔti nín ŋáań binib tiŋan puee, ní u dū diyimɔɔl bulifi ki pú binib kupaau unibaanti Yeesu Kriisitoo pu.

english_verse: There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti pɔl nín tūǹ ditundi diŋyee nyáń di-ba nì unibaantee kpitii tundi. Unibaantee kpitii nín cáań-ti kun kuŋyee di sá ŋkúm. Unimbɔti ŋanti tin u pú-ti faalaayee nín cáań-ti kuŋyee di sá, a-kpitii yaa yāntì ki wīikí min kamaa, u làá dūú pɔ̄-si.

english_verse: Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
translation_verse: Tiŋman, unibaanti yìntitam pu ní ŋkúm jíń báà ŋma. Ama Yeesu Kriisitoo ubaanti pu ní binib fōō tiŋan tin bulifi Unimbɔti ŋée. U pú-bi bí nīn bí deedee u-nimbiin, bidambi ń nīn cáá dimaŋfal kí jī dibeel.

english_verse: Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life.
translation_verse: Kii Adam baba kpitii nín cáań nnibiyaamu kɔkɔ ŋkúm puee, Yeesu Kriisitoo tundi din u túń nì deedeeyee yāntì nnibiyaamu kɔkɔ ŋūǹ kí kpántí deedeedambi kí ká dimaŋfal.

english_verse: Adam disobeyed God and caused many others to be sinners. But Jesus obeyed him and will make many people acceptable to God.
translation_verse: Kii unibaanti yìntitam nín kɔ́ǹ binib tikpil ikpitin puee, míǹ ní unibaanti nín tɔ́ Unimbɔti puee di cāntì binib tikpil làá kpántí deedeedambi.

english_verse: The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful.
translation_verse: Mara úǹ dɔ́miń ikpiti ń wíiǹ ní. Ama ikpiti yaa yāntì ki wīikí min kamaa, Unimbɔti ŋanti wīikí ki jítiǹ-i.

english_verse: Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
translation_verse: An di yì-tì ní, kii ikpiti nín nìn jíń báà ŋma ki cáań ŋkúm puee, Unimbɔti ŋanti kíǹ ki jīǹ mpaan binib ń kpántí deedeedambi kí fōō dimaŋfal din kaa cáá dikúntilee ti-Dindaan Yeesu Kriisitoo pu.

english_verse: What should we say? Should we keep on sinning, so that God's gift of undeserved grace will show up even better?
translation_verse: Mimmee, tí lì yii ba? Tí nīn gbíntìi ŋáań ikpiti ní Unimbɔti ŋanti ń wíiǹaaa?

english_verse: No, we should not! If we are dead to sin, how can we go on sinning?
translation_verse: Aayee, kpataaa! Timbi bin kpíì ikpiti jandi púee, mana ní ti gíti ŋūǹ kí nīn bí ki ŋáań ikpiti?

english_verse: Don't you know that all who share in Christ Jesus by being baptized also share in his death?
translation_verse: Naa nyí yii, timbi bin kɔkɔ bi fùl̄ Unimbɔti nyim ti ŋá ubaanti nì Yeesu Kriisitooyee, ti kpáfì ki kpíì u-kúm min u kpíìyee níii?

english_verse: When we were baptized, we died and were buried with Christ. We were baptized, so we would live a new life, as Christ was raised to life by the glory of God the Father.
translation_verse: Kii bi nín fùl̄-ti Unimbɔti nyim puee, bi síb́-ti tí nīn bí ŋkúmin nì Yeesu dee, ní kii ti-Baa Unimbɔti nín dū u-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu ki fīkitì Yeesu Kriisitoo ditaŋkpiilin ki fātìi gíiǹní-u dimaŋfalin puee, mimmee, ti nì u kɔkɔ di kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfapɔndin.

english_verse: If we shared in Jesus' death by being baptized, we will be raised to life with him.
translation_verse: Di sá yii timbi nì u yaa kpáfì ki kpíì u-kúmee, míǹ mbaantiim ní ti nì u kpáfì ki fīkitì difìkitibaantiil.

english_verse: We know that the persons we used to be were nailed to the cross with Jesus. This was done, so our sinful bodies would no longer be the slaves of sin.
translation_verse: Tí béémaan yii, ti nín nìn bí min min dooooyee, ti-bimbim gbanti kpíì nì Yeesu ndɔpuntikaa pu. Mimmee ti-bimbikpitim kpíì dee. Tí taa ti nín̄ sá ikpiti yumbui.

english_verse: We know sin doesn't have power over dead people.
translation_verse: Di sá yii un yaa kpíìyee, úǹ nyáń ikpiti ŋaan dee.

english_verse: As surely as we died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him.
translation_verse: Ti nì Kriisitoo yaa kpáfì ki kpíì, ti nyí yii ti nì u làá kpāfì kí nīn tí bí dimaŋfalin.

english_verse: We know that death no longer has any power over Christ. He died and was raised to life, never again to die.
translation_verse: Ti nyí yii, Kriisitoo nín kpíì ki fātìi fīkitèe, waa ti bí kí kpú ŋwindal, ŋkúm kaa ti cáá u-pu mpɔn.

english_verse: When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God.
translation_verse: U nín kpíìyee, u kpíì diba pu ki kúntì ikpiti, ní kaa ti làá kpú jaanjaan. Kɔŋkɔnnee, u nín bí dimaŋfalinee, u bí ki tīī Unimbɔti ní.

english_verse: In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
translation_verse: Míǹ mbaantiim, ni nì Yeesu Kriisitoo nín ŋá ubaanti puee, ni mun ń nīn nyí yii ni kpíì ikpiti jandi pú, ki kíǹ ki bí ki tīī Unimbɔti.

english_verse: Don't let sin rule your body. After all, your body is bound to die, so don't obey its desires
translation_verse: Mimmee, ikpiti ń taa ti jī ni-wunti tin bí ki làá dāá kpúee ni mpaan, ní taa nín̄ nóó ni-landɔkɔkpitii nín là puee.
