translation_verse: Atimbun nìn gíí a-pu diŋuul, ama ŋyunti bāań á dàkà-ŋi a-ŋuul nín sá puee, kí sòoǹ bitaŋkpiibi bɔti. Ŋyunti bāań dee á pà a-tɔntɔnliibi bin sá a-bɔnaatiliibee paati, nì bin kɔkɔ sá a-yab ki fàŋkí-see, bikpaambi nì ŋwaamu. Ŋyunti bāań dee á kúntí bin bí ki nàantí duulinyee.»

english_verse: The door to God's temple in heaven was then opened, and the sacred chest could be seen inside the temple. I saw lightning and heard roars of thunder. The earth trembled and huge hailstones fell to the ground.
translation_verse: Ní bi cúú yilpu Nimbɔtidiiku ki pīitì ní dipoondi dakaau nyáń ki yú kunimbɔtidiin. Niinee ní an bíi ŋmóò ki tátí kii utaayee, ní m gbìl̄ dibintiŋkpaandi pu, ní kitiŋ cīŋkì ŋkpitim pu, ní ataanyiŋkumbil bíi lítí.

english_verse: She was about to give birth, and she was crying because of the great pain.
translation_verse: Unimpuee làá màal̀ ní ki yáliŋkí imatiŋween ki gbáà ibiil.

english_verse: Something else appeared in the sky. It was a huge red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and a crown on each of its seven heads.
translation_verse: Ní maamaaci ubɔ gíti nyáń ki páaǹ kutagbɔŋu pu: an sá kupeebiliŋŋu kubɔ, ku sá kumaŋu ki cáá ayil aluli nì iyin saalaa, ní kibeefuulii cíkí diyil sá kamaa pu.

english_verse: With its tail, it dragged a third of the stars from the sky and threw them down to the earth. Then the dragon turned toward the woman, because it wanted to eat her child as soon as it was born.
translation_verse: U-juul ní u dūu fùkū iŋmalbijaa yaa yākatì mitee diba pu ki lúkufìń kitiŋ pu, ní ki kíǹ ki yú ki kɔ́ĺ unimpu un làá màal̀ee, u yaa màl̄ee ú cúú kibikee kí ŋmɔ́.

english_verse: The woman gave birth to a son, who would rule all nations with an iron rod. The boy was snatched away. He was taken to God and placed on his throne.
translation_verse: Ní unimpuee dūu màl̄ kibininjabiki. Kíǹ di làá nīn cáá mpɔn kii tikútee kí dūú kpòotī atimbun kɔkɔ, ní bi yōoǹ u-bikee malaa ki jɔ́m̀ Unimbɔti cee, u-beejal laŋki.

english_verse: The woman ran into the desert to a place that God had prepared for her. There she would be taken care of for
translation_verse: Ní unaati sáǹ ki búntì kuteeun laakin binib kpée. Niin ní Unimbɔti bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ-u ú cùú kàl̄ bí nīn kpīintí-u kí tin sāā abin ata nì dijandi.

english_verse: A war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels were fighting against the dragon and its angels.
translation_verse: Niinee ní kujaau fōō ki píĺ kutagbɔŋu pu, Unimbɔti tuuŋyi kpiliu Mikayeel nì u-yab bí ki jáà nì kupeebiliŋŋuee nì u-yab,

english_verse: But the dragon lost the battle. It and its angels were forced out of their places in heaven
translation_verse: ní Mikayeel nì u yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ní ki jìn̄-bi bí taa ti kàl̄ kutagbɔŋun.

english_verse: and were thrown down to the earth. Yes, that old snake and his angels were thrown out of heaven! That snake, who fools everyone on earth, is known as the devil and Satan.
translation_verse: Ní bi téeń kupeebiliŋŋuee, ukookpiki un bi yíì Sitaan u kíil̀ duulinya kɔkɔee nì u-tuuŋyi ki tɔ́ń duulinyan.

english_verse: Then I heard a voice from heaven shout, “Our God has shown his saving power, and his kingdom has come! God's own Chosen One has shown his authority. Satan accused our people in the presence of God day and night. Now he has been thrown out!
translation_verse: Ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ téeń mpɔn yilpu yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee Unimbɔti fiil bāań dee! Min bí nee ní ti-Nimbɔtiu nyántì u-beel pɔŋŋu ki dàkā! Kɔŋkɔnnee u-Meesiyau dàkā mpɔn ŋun u cááyee, kun puee ukuŋfil un yú Unimbɔti nimbiin ki kúŋfí ti-nabiyaamu boon ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeuee, bi téé-u ki nyántì.

english_verse: “Our people defeated Satan because of the blood of the Lamb and the message of God. They were willing to give up their lives.
translation_verse: Dipibil fatikuu nì Unimbɔti bɔti tin ti-nabiyaamu sòon̄ee pu ní bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-u, kaa fāŋkì kí dū bi-ba kí tīī ŋkúm.

english_verse: “The heavens should rejoice, together with everyone who lives there. But pity the earth and the sea, because the devil was thrown down to the earth. He knows his time is short, and he is very angry.”
translation_verse: An puee án nīn mɔ̄ǹ yilpu yab. Án nīn mɔ̄ǹ nimbi bin kóò kutagbɔŋu puee, ama an sá mbusu ní ki tīī-ni tiŋku nì kitiŋ pu yab, kun puee nì diŋuukpaandi ní Sitaan dūu kpákatìń ni-cee, ki nyí mun yii ŋyunti fiii di kíǹ-u.»

english_verse: When the dragon realized it had been thrown down to the earth, it tried to make trouble for the woman who had given birth to a son.
translation_verse: Kupeebiliŋŋuee nín ká yii bi téeń-ku ki lúkuń taapuee, ní ku nín jì unimpu un nìn màl̄ kibininjabikee boon.

english_verse: But the woman was given two wings like those of a huge eagle, so she could fly into the desert. There she would escape from the snake and be taken care of for a time, two times, and half a time.
translation_verse: Ní bi tīī unimpuee ifeen ili kii ukaalun feeŋyee, ú ŋàaǹ kí nīn cá kuteeun laakin bi bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ-u ú cùú kàl̄ bí kpíiǹ-u abin ata nì dijandee, ukoobu ń taa ŋmā kí ká-u.

english_verse: The snake then spewed out water like a river to sweep the woman away.
translation_verse: Ukoobuee sáń ki jì-uee ní ki wūliŋkì nnyim ki tɔ́ unimpuee boon pú án kpántí dimɔɔl kí yòon̄-u.

english_verse: But the earth helped her and swallowed the water that had come from the dragon's mouth.
translation_verse: Ama ní kitiŋ fīī unimpuee. Kitiŋ wāaǹ ki dū nnyim min min kupeebiliŋŋuee bàà wūliŋkì ki tɔ́ń u-boon án bàà yòon̄-uee ki náĺ.

english_verse: This made the dragon terribly angry with the woman. So it started a war against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God and are faithful to what Jesus did and taught.
translation_verse: Niinee ní kupeebiliŋŋuee fōō unimpuee pu diŋuul ní ki cūtì ki bíi jáà nì unimpuee biyaamu mun kíǹee, bin kɔkɔ tɔ́ Unimbɔti marab ki ŋúb́ Yeesu bɔti deedeeyee.

english_verse: The dragon stood on the beach beside the sea.
translation_verse: Ní kupeebiliŋŋuee kíǹ ki yú tiŋku gbandi.

english_verse: I looked and saw a beast coming up from the sea. This one had ten horns and seven heads, and a crown was on each of its ten horns. On each of its heads were names that were an insult to God.
translation_verse: M kpēēyee, ní ki ká upeel ubɔ nyánní tiŋkun, ki cáá ayil aluli nì iyin saalaa ní ki cíkí u-yiŋŋu kamaa pu kibeefuulii, ní diyil sá kamaa puee disiibil náká ki sìí Unimbɔti.

english_verse: The beast I saw had the body of a leopard, the feet of a bear, and the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over its own power and throne and great authority to this beast.
translation_verse: Upeel un m kée náań nì ugbii ní, ní u-taaŋi náań nì digbiŋgbil, ní u-nyɔkɔ náań nì gbikinti nyɔkɔ, ní kupeebiliŋŋuee dū ku-pɔŋyi kɔkɔ nì ku-beel ki tīī-u.

english_verse: One of its heads seemed to have been fatally wounded, but now it was well. Everyone on earth marveled at this beast,
translation_verse: U-yiliŋee diba nìn fōō tiweendi ki cá ŋkúm, ama ní iweenee dāa dóò, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ duulinya yab kɔkɔ ní bi nóó upeelee.

english_verse: and they worshiped the dragon who had given its authority to the beast. They also worshiped the beast and said, “No one is like this beast! No one can fight against it.”
translation_verse: Ní binib kɔkɔ bí ki nyɔ́ŋkí kupeebiliŋŋuee ku nín dū ku-pɔŋyi kɔkɔ nì ku-beel ki dūu tīī upeel un nyánní tiŋkunee pu, ní bi bí ki nyɔ́ŋkí upeelee ki lì yii: «Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí dū u-ba kí ŋmàntīǹ upeel nee? Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí já nì u?»

english_verse: The beast cursed God, and it cursed the name of God. It even cursed the place where God lives, as well as everyone who lives in heaven with God.
translation_verse: U nìn lafun kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ tibɔfan ki bíiĺ Unimbɔti yindi, nì u-kɔŋkooŋŋu nì bin kɔkɔ kóò yilpuee.

english_verse: It was allowed to fight against God's people and defeat them. It was also given authority over the people of every tribe, nation, language, and race.
translation_verse: Bi nìn pú upeelee nsan ú já nì Unimbɔti yab kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi, ní ki tīī-u tinaakɔti kɔkɔ nì anibul kɔkɔ, nì isoon kɔkɔ nib nì atimbun kɔkɔ pu mpɔn.

english_verse: The beast was worshiped by everyone whose name wasn't written before the time of creation in the book of the Lamb who was killed.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ pu nib bin yiŋŋi kaa ŋmàn̄ doooo duulinya kíltam dimaŋfal gbɔŋku kun Dipibil din kpíìyee yèe poonee, an nibee kɔkɔ dāa jáaḿ upeelee ní.

english_verse: If you have ears, then listen!
translation_verse: «Un yaa cáá ditafalee ń pīlifì tiŋan.

english_verse: If you are doomed to be captured, you will be captured. If you are doomed to be killed by a sword, you will be killed by a sword. This means God's people must learn to endure and be faithful!
translation_verse: Un Unimbɔti lī yii bi làá cúú kuyuŋuee, see bí cúú-u kuyuŋu. Un Unimbɔti lī yii bi làá kpɔ̀-u nì kitàataajikee, see bí kpɔ̀ udaan nì kitàataajiki. An sá Unimbɔti yab ń dàkà bi-pɔ́ɔǹtam nì bi-fookiiu un bi cáá Unimbɔti puee ní.»

english_verse: I now saw another beast. This one came out of the ground. It had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon.
translation_verse: Boonee ní m ká upeel ubɔ mun púń ki nyáń kitiŋ ki cáá iyin ili an bí kii dipibil yiŋyee, ní ki sòoǹ kii kupeebiliŋŋuee.

english_verse: It worked for the beast whose fatal wound had been healed. And it used all its authority to force the earth and its people to worship that beast.
translation_verse: Upeel upeepeekaayee nimbiin ní u ŋáań maamaacib nì mpɔn ŋun u fōō u-ceeyee, ní ki yàntī binib bin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee jáaḿ upeel upeepeekaa un nìn fōō ŋkúm weeŋyi ki dāa pɔ́ɔkèe.

english_verse: It worked mighty miracles, and while people watched, it even made fire come down from the sky.
translation_verse: Upeel uliliitee nìn ŋáań maamaacikpaambi, ki yàntī ŋŋmi nyēeń yilpu ki lítí kitiŋ binib kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_verse: This second beast fooled people on earth by working miracles for the first one. Then it talked them into making an idol in the form of the beast that did not die after being wounded by a sword.
translation_verse: Mpɔn ŋun bi nìn tīī-u u cáa ŋáań maamaacib upeel upeepeekaa nimbiinee ní u nìn cáa kíiĺ binib ní ki páb́ binib bí náań upeel un bi nìn gāā kitàataajiki ki tīī tiweendi waa kpíìyee naŋku kí yóoń.

english_verse: It was allowed to put breath into the idol, so it could speak. Everyone who refused to worship the idol of the beast was put to death.
translation_verse: Ní u fōō mpɔn kí ŋmā kí tīī upeelee naŋku kun bi máńee kufoou, án nín làá ŋá pu kú ŋmā kí nīn sòoǹee, ní bin yaa kaa gbāaǹ ki jáam̀-kuee ú kpɔ̀ bidambee.

english_verse: All people were forced to put a mark on their right hand or forehead. Whether they were powerful or weak, rich or poor, free people or slaves,
translation_verse: Mbiyaamueeee, bikpaambeeee, bigaajabeeee, bisoodambeeee, bin tɔ́ bi-beeyeeee, iyumbueeee, u cāntì bi nákáǹ bi-kɔkɔ ŋaŋgiilii nì bi-yigbeeŋi pu tidaandi.

english_verse: they all had to have this mark, or else they could not buy or sell anything. This mark stood for the name of the beast and for the number of its name.
translation_verse: Ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí dā tiba, kaa tí ŋūǹ kí nyāfì tiba, upeelee yindi nì u-yindi nambau yaa kaa náká udaan pu.

english_verse: You need wisdom to understand the number of the beast! But if you are smart enough, you can figure this out. Its number is
translation_verse: An sá mpɔ́ɔn ní, un cáá iciinee ń tùkù taapu. Kun puee tita nì ita nì biluuyee (

english_verse: , and it stands for a person.
translation_verse: ) dàkà unil ubɔ yindi ní.

english_verse: Then I heard a sound from heaven that was like a roaring flood or loud thunder or even like the music of harps.
translation_verse: M gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ nyánní yilpu a lì kii mbuŋkpaan nyim nín sìtī puee, ní ki gíti bí kii utaa nín tátí pu mpɔn mpɔnee, ní nneen ŋun pu m gbìl̄ee bí kii bibeebɔɔliibi di bɔ̀ɔ́ bi-bati ki gà ilanee.

english_verse: And a new song was being sung in front of God's throne and in front of the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn that song, except the
translation_verse: Binib gbantee nìn yú dibeejal nì tiwan tinaa tin cáá kufoouee nì bikpilibee nimbiin ki gà nlampɔɔn, ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí bīfì-ŋu, asee binib kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku ili nì binaa bin bi dá ki nyántìń duulinyanee baba di ŋūǹ kí gāā an laŋŋu.

english_verse: All of these are pure virgins, and they follow the Lamb wherever he leads. They have been rescued to be presented to God and the Lamb as the most precious people on earth.
translation_verse: An nibee kaa dōoǹ nì binimpoobi ki kɔ́ǹ bi-ba tijɔkɔndi, bi ŋúb́ bi-ba circir ní. Bi dī Dipibil boon ki cá laakin dì yaa cée. Unimbɔti dá-bi ki nyántì binib kansikin bí nīn sá bin bi làá péé péé kí dūú sú Unimbɔti nì Dipibilee.

english_verse: They never tell lies, and they are innocent. The Messages of the Three Angels
translation_verse: Baa gbìl̄ an nibee mɔ́ntì nnyimɔn dalba ki ká, kaa ti kāntí ikpiti iba bi-pu kí lì. Ituun ita bɔti

english_verse: I saw another angel. This one was flying across the sky and had the eternal good news to announce to the people of every race, tribe, language, and nation on earth.
translation_verse: Boonee ní m ká ntuun ŋubɔ ŋàaǹ kutagbɔŋu pu yilpu yilpu ki cáá Tibɔmɔntiil tin kaa cáá dikúntilee ki tùkù binib bin kóò duulinyanee, ntimu kɔkɔ nib nì atimbun kɔkɔ nì isoon kɔkɔ nib nì anibul kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The angel shouted, “Worship and honor God! The time has come for him to judge everyone. Kneel down before the one who created heaven and earth, the oceans, and every stream.”
translation_verse: Ŋu nìn tátí mpɔn yii: «Fàŋkìmaan Unimbɔti kí tīī-u tinyool, kun puee ŋyunti bāań ú sòoǹ nnibiyaamu bɔti. Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan Unimbɔti un náań yilpu nì taapuee, nì tiŋku nì inyimbul kɔkɔee.»

english_verse: A second angel followed and said, “The great city of Babylon has fallen! This is the city that made all nations drunk and immoral. Now God is angry, and Babylon has fallen.”
translation_verse: Ní ntuun nliliiti páaǹní ní ki lī yii: «Babilooŋkpaan lítì! Kitiŋkpaaŋŋi lítì! U nyūntì atimbun kɔkɔ u-daam min sá u-laakpaati tin u ŋáań an lákatèe!»

english_verse: Finally, a third angel came and shouted: Here is what will happen if you worship the beast and the idol and have the mark of the beast on your hand or forehead.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun ntataati páaǹní ki lī mpɔn yii: «Un di yaa gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ upeelee nì u-naŋku, ní ki yāntì bi dáań u-yigbeel nì u-ŋalee,

english_verse: You will have to drink the wine that God gives to everyone who makes him angry. You will feel his mighty anger, and you will be tortured with fire and burning sulfur, while the holy angels and the Lamb look on.
translation_verse: Unimbɔti làá dāá nyùntī udaan ndaam min sá u-ŋuulee. U làá dāá fōō bidambi pu diŋuukpaandi din kaa cáá jutee kí dū-bi kí tɔ̄ farwata ŋmiŋun bí jī falaakpaan, u-tuuŋyi circirdambi nì Dipibil nimbiin.

english_verse: If you worship the beast and the idol and accept the mark of its name, you will be tortured day and night. The smoke from your torture will go up forever and ever, and you will never be able to rest.
translation_verse: Ŋŋmi ŋun poon bi làá nīn bí ki jīǹ falaayee làá nīn pée dùkù ní kaa cáá dikúntil. Baa dāa cáá diŋuŋfil ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu, bíǹ bin kɔkɔ gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ upeel nì u-naŋkuee, nì bin yāntì bi dū upeelee yindi ki dáań-bee.»

english_verse: God's people must learn to endure. They must also obey his commands and have faith in Jesus.
translation_verse: Ŋyunti nee di máaǹ Unimbɔti yab bin ŋúb́ u-marab tiŋan ki máká Yeesu puee ń pɔ́ɔǹ bi-ba, kí nīn cáá kimɔtii.

english_verse: Then I heard a voice from heaven say, “Put this in writing. From now on, the Lord will bless everyone who has faith in him when they die.” The Spirit answered, “Yes, they will rest from their hard work, and they will be rewarded for what they have done.” The Earth Is Harvested
translation_verse: Ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ sòon̄ní yilpu yii: «Ŋmà yii: <Bin nóó ti-Dindaan ki kúù kɔŋkɔnneeyee bí mmɔnneeee!> Unimbɔti Fam lī yii: <An sá mbaamɔn, bi làá cùú kàl̄ kí ŋùŋfì, kun puee atunnyaan ŋin bi túńee dī-bi!>» Tijin bīń bí cā

english_verse: I looked and saw a bright cloud, and someone who seemed to be the Son of Man was sitting on the cloud. He wore a gold crown on his head and held a sharp sickle in his hand.
translation_verse: M kpēēyee, ní ki ká ditagbampindi diba, ní ubɔ kā di-pu ki náań nì unil, ní ki cíkí sindaariya beefuuliiki ki ŋúb́ ugɔti un jītée u-ŋaan.

english_verse: An angel came out of the temple and shouted, “Start cutting with your sickle! Harvest season is here, and all crops on earth are ripe.”
translation_verse: Ní ntuun ŋubɔ nyánní kunimbɔtidiin ki téeń mpɔn ki tùkū un kā ditagbampindi puee yii: «Dū a-gɔtiuee kí cā tijikaal, kun puee kudiceeu ŋmāntì. Duulinya bīń ki ŋmāntì bí cā!»

english_verse: The one on the cloud swung his sickle and harvested the crops.
translation_verse: Niinee ní un kā ditagbandi puee dū u-gɔtiu ki bɔ́ duulinyan ní ki cáń duulinya.

english_verse: Another angel with a sharp sickle then came out of the temple in heaven.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun ŋubɔ mun gíti nyánní yilpu Nimbɔtidiikun ki mun ŋúb́ ugɔti un jītée.

english_verse: After this, an angel with power over fire came from the altar and shouted to the angel who had the sickle. He said, “All grapes on earth are ripe! Harvest them with your sharp sickle.”
translation_verse: Ní ntuun ŋubɔ gíti tí nyánní nsaraafanni, ŋúǹ di ŋúb́ ŋŋmi pɔŋŋu, ki téeń mpɔn ki tùkū ŋun ŋúb́ ugɔti an jītée yii: «Dū a-gɔtiu un jītée kí bɔ̄ fiinyi sufii in sí kitiŋ puee sakaŋi poon kí kìtī, kun puee abil bīń.»

english_verse: The angel swung his sickle on earth and cut off its grapes. He threw them into a pit where they were trampled on as a sign of God's anger.
translation_verse: Ní ntuunee dū ŋu-gɔtiu ki bɔ́ fiinyi sufiin ní ki kītì duulinya fiinyi biliŋ ki gbéeǹ mbookpaan ŋun ni bi ŋmāam̀ ki lèekī ndaamee, an dàkà yii bi cáa kɔ́ǹ Unimbɔti ŋuulin dee.

english_verse: The pit was outside the city, and when the grapes were mashed, blood flowed out. The blood turned into a river that was about
translation_verse: Ní bi ŋmáaḿ fiinyi biliŋee mbookpaanee ni kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu nnyim ń nyā. Kun nyáńee di sá fatiku, ki pùub̀ ki tin sāā ataŋkpee alaataa ata. Ní fatikuee nín dɔ̄ ki jɔ́m̀ puee tin sāā itaamu nyɔɔkpaaŋi.

english_verse: After this, I looked at the sky and saw something else that was strange and important. Seven angels were bringing the seven last terrible troubles. When these are ended, God will no longer be angry.
translation_verse: Ní m gíti ká kudaaŋŋu kubɔ yilpu, ku náaǹ ki cáá maamaaci. M ká ituun iluli ŋúb́ falaabi biluli. Bíǹ di sá bifalaajoolkaabi bin Unimbɔti làá dūú tɔ̄ binib pu ní u-ŋuul ń nín sɔ̀ŋkèe.

english_verse: Then I saw something that looked like a glass sea mixed with fire, and people were standing on it. They were the ones who had defeated the beast and the idol and the number that tells the name of the beast. God had given them harps,
translation_verse: Ní m ká tiba an náań nì tiŋku ní ki wāĺ kílkil kii digitilee ní ki ŋmàl̄ nì ŋŋmi, ní m ká bin jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ upeelee nì u-naŋku nì namba un sá u-yindee yú tiŋku un wāĺ kílkil kii digitilee cee ki ŋúb́ tibati tin Unimbɔti tīī-bee,

english_verse: and they were singing the song his servant Moses and the Lamb had sung. They were singing, “Lord God All-Powerful, you have done great and marvelous things. You are the ruler of all nations, and you do what is right and fair.
translation_verse: ní bi bí ki gà Mooyiisi Unimbɔti tɔntɔnliu nì Dipibil laŋyi yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, a-tuuŋŋi wīikí ki sá amɔnti, sii di sá atimbun bɔtiu. A nín lēē nsàmbiyaamu muŋyee bí deedee ní ki sá mbaamɔn.

english_verse: Lord, who doesn't honor and praise your name? You alone are holy, and all nations will come and worship you, because you have shown that you judge with fairness.”
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan, ŋma di kaa làá fàŋkì-si? Ŋma di làá yíí, kaa làá tīī-si tinyool? Kun puee sii baba di sá circirdaan, atimbun kɔkɔ làá dāan̄ ní kí gbàan̄ a-nimbiin kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si, kun puee báà ŋma ká a-tuuŋŋi, ŋi bí deedee.»

english_verse: After this, I noticed something else in heaven. The sacred tent used for a temple was open.
translation_verse: Míǹ boonee m ká kunimbɔtidii kun bí yilpuee cúu pīitì, ní Unimbɔti tantiu un dàkà u-bítamee yú poon,

english_verse: And the seven angels who were bringing the terrible troubles were coming out of it. They were dressed in robes of pure white linen and wore belts made of pure gold.
translation_verse: ní ituun iluli in ŋúb́ falaabi bilulee nyánní kunimbɔtidiiyee poon ki pēē tiwampin káŋkaŋ ki jìl̀, ní ki dū sindaariya dambalau ki cúú i-biŋŋi.

english_verse: One of the four living creatures gave each of the seven angels a bowl made of gold. These bowls were filled with the anger of God who lives forever and ever.
translation_verse: Tiwan tinaa tin cáá kufoouee kubɔ tīī ituun ilulee sindaariya sambiyaamu mululi, Unimbɔti un bí jaanjaanee ŋuul gbí poon.

english_verse: The temple quickly filled with smoke from the glory and power of God. No one could enter it until the seven angels had finished pouring out the seven last troubles.
translation_verse: Niinee ní Unimbɔti nyooti nì u-pɔŋŋu yāntì nnyiim yíkì ki gbí kunimbɔtidiin, ní ubɔ kaa ti ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ niin, see falaabi bin bi tīī ituun ilulee nín dāa jítèe.

english_verse: From the temple I heard a voice shout to the seven angels, “Go and empty the seven bowls of God's anger on the earth.”
translation_verse: Ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ nyánní kunimbɔtidiin ki sòoǹ mpɔn ki tùkù ituun ilulee yii: «Nín̄ cámaan kí kpáatí Unimbɔti ŋuul din kā nsambiyaamu mululinee kí sìtīmaan duulinyan.»

english_verse: The first angel emptied his bowl on the earth. At once ugly and painful sores broke out on everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun mpeepeekaa kpáatì diŋuul din gbí ŋu-sambikinee ki sītì duulinyan, ní ibunsoon dɔ́miń ki jéetì bin kɔkɔ cáá upeelee daaŋku ki jáaḿ u-naŋkuee pu.

english_verse: The second angel emptied his bowl on the sea. At once the sea turned into blood like that of a dead person, and every living thing in the sea died.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun nliliiti kpáatì diŋuul din gbí ŋu-sambikinee ki sītì tiŋkun, ní tiŋku nyim kpántì fatiku a lì kii unil un bi kūūyee fatikuuee, ní tin kɔkɔ bí tiŋkun ki cáá kufoouee kpíì.

english_verse: The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and streams. At once they turned to blood.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun ntataati kpáatì diŋuul din gbí ŋu-sambikinee ki sītì amɔɔ nì ikpin poon, ní inyiŋfi kpántì fatiku.

english_verse: Then I heard the angel, who has power over water, say, “You have always been, and you always will be the holy God. You had the right to judge in this way.
translation_verse: Niinee m gbìl̄ ntuun ŋun yì inyiŋfi pɔŋŋuee bí yii: «A sá deedeedaan ní a nín ŋá min nee pu, sii un bí ki nìn pée bí dooooyee, a sá circirdaan ní.

english_verse: They poured out the blood of your people and your prophets. So you gave them blood to drink as they deserve!”
translation_verse: Di sá bi nìn kūū a-nib nì a-bɔnaatiliibi bi-fatikuu nyáń ki fá, míǹ pu ní a yāntì inyiŋfi kpántì fatiku bí nyɔ̀, bi nín máaǹ puee ní a ŋá-bi nee!»

english_verse: After this, I heard the altar shout, “Yes, Lord God All-Powerful, your judgments are honest and fair.”
translation_verse: Ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ nyánní nsaraafanni ki lī yii: «Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, a nín sòon̄ binib bɔti miŋyee sá mbaamɔn ní ki sá deedee.»

english_verse: The fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, and it began to scorch people like fire.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun nnanaati kpáatì diŋuul din kā ŋu-sambikinee ki sītì ŋwìiń pu yii ŋwìiń ń píĺ binib tikpil.

english_verse: Everyone was scorched by its great heat, and all of them cursed the name of God who had power over these terrible troubles. But no one turned to God and praised him.
translation_verse: Ní kutuntuŋu píĺ binib tikpil ní bi bí ki bíiĺ Unimbɔti un cáá mpɔn falaabi gbanti puee yindi, ki yíì kaa fá bi-kpitii kí tīī Unimbɔti tinyool.

english_verse: The fifth angel emptied his bowl on the throne of the beast. At once darkness covered its kingdom, and its people began biting their tongues in pain.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun ŋŋmooŋmooti kpáatì diŋuul din gbí ŋu-sambikinee ki sītì upeelee beejal pu, ní u-beelin nib jéetì dibɔmbɔndin, ní tifaandi yāntì binib júntí bi-limbiliŋ, kun puee iween nìn gbìl̄-bi.

english_verse: And because of their painful sores, they cursed the God who rules in heaven. But still they did not stop doing evil things.
translation_verse: Bi-bunsooŋyi nì bi-falaau un bi bí ki jīǹee pu ní bi nìn bí ki bíiĺ Unimbɔti un yì yilpuee. Ama bi yíì, kaa fá bi-tuŋkpitiŋ.

english_verse: The sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great Euphrates River, and it completely dried up to make a road for the kings from the east.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun nluluuti kpáatì diŋuul din kā ŋu-sambikinee ki sītì Eefiraati mɔɔkpaandin, ní dimɔɔl fóotì ki kūń ní nsan dōoǹ ní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú bɔtiibi kíǹ ki dì.

english_verse: An evil spirit that looked like a frog came out of the mouth of the dragon. One also came out of the mouth of the beast, and another out of the mouth of the false prophet.
translation_verse: Ní m ká arasiniibi bita, bi náań nì kpaadalib ki nyánní kupeebiliŋŋuee nì upeel un kíǹee nì u-bɔnaatiliu unyimɔndaan nyɔmmun.

english_verse: These evil spirits had the power to work miracles. They went to every king on earth, to bring them together for a war against God All-Powerful. But that will be the day of God's great victory.
translation_verse: Arasiniibi bitee ŋáań maamaacib, ní ki cūtì ki ká duulinya kɔkɔ bɔtiibi ki kpáfì-bi bí dāá já nì Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan u-wiŋkpaaŋŋu dal.

english_verse: Remember Christ says, “When I come, it will surprise you like a thief! But God will bless you, if you are awake and ready. Then you won't have to walk around naked and be ashamed.”
translation_verse: «Ní pīlifì, m làá dāan̄ kii unaayuu yamee ní! Un kaa gèen̄ ki kā ki cí u-bɔkutil dɔ̄ ki kɔ́ĺ-uee bí mmɔnni. Udaan kaa dāa nyēē dicancaŋgbeel bí ká u-cooi.»

english_verse: Those armies came together in a place that in Hebrew is called Armagedon.
translation_verse: Ní arasiniibee kóoǹ bibɔtiibi ki cáa kpáfì laakin Eebru yab yíì yii Arimageedɔŋyee.

english_verse: As soon as the seventh angel emptied his bowl in the air, a loud voice from the throne in the temple shouted, “It's done!”
translation_verse: Ní ntuun nluluúti kpáatì diŋuul din kā ŋu-sambikinee ki yàl̄ kutaa pu, ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ nyánní kunimbɔtidiin dibeejal cee ki sòon̄ mpɔn yii: «An ŋá ki dóò!»

english_verse: The great city of Babylon split into three parts, and the cities of other nations fell. So God made Babylon drink from the wine cup filled with his anger.
translation_verse: Ní kitiŋkpaaŋŋi lítì ki nābitì agin ata, ní atimbun tiŋkpaammu kɔkɔ wīil̀. Niinee Unimbɔti téetì Babiloon kitiŋkpaaŋŋi pu, ní ki dū u-ŋuul din pɔ̄ɔ̄ kpaŋkpamee ki nyūntì-kì kii ndaamee.

english_verse: Every island ran away, and the mountains disappeared.
translation_verse: Ní ntimu mun bí amɔɔ kansikinee nì ajoon wáŋkì.

english_verse: One of the seven angels who had emptied the bowls came over and said to me, “Come on! I will show you how God will punish that shameless prostitute who sits on many oceans.
translation_verse: Boonee ní ituun iluli in kpáatì diŋuul ki sītì duulinya puee ŋubɔ sútìń m-cee ní ki bí-mi yii: «Dāan̄ tí cù ḿ dàkà-si bi nín làá dáaĺ ulaakpaadaan un pée sá ukpaan ki kā ikpin puee tafal miŋyee.

english_verse: Every king on earth has slept with her, and her shameless ways are like wine that has made everyone on earth drunk.”
translation_verse: Kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi dōoǹ nì u ní kitiŋ pu nib mɔ̄nnì-u ní u-laakpaati gbí-bi kii ndaamee.»

english_verse: With the help of the Spirit, the angel took me into a desert, where I saw a woman sitting on a red beast. The beast was covered with names that were an insult to God, and it had seven heads and ten horns.
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti Fam dɔ́miń m-ni ní ntuun yōoǹ-mi ti búntì kuteeun, ní m tin ká unimpu ubɔ kā upeel pu. Upeelee sá uman, ní u-wunti kɔkɔ náká asiibil ki sìí Unimbɔti, ki cáá ayil aluli nì iyin saalaa.

english_verse: The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet robes, and she wore jewelry made of gold, precious stones, and pearls. In her hand she held a gold cup filled with the filthy and nasty things she had done.
translation_verse: Unimpu gbanti pēē dibɔkutinyaandi diba dì máǹ, ní u-falfatib nì u-bɔmbiliŋ nì u-beedimbiliŋ sá sindaariya nì ataŋkpee ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaau ki jìl̀ee, ní ki ŋúb́ sindaariya sambiki ikpiti nì tilaakpaal tin u ŋáańee jɔkɔnti gbí poon.

english_verse: On her forehead a mysterious name was written: I AM THE GREAT CITY OF BABYLON, THE MOTHER OF EVERY IMMORAL AND FILTHY THING ON EARTH.
translation_verse: Ní dimaamaaciyindi diba ŋmàn̄ ki náká u-yigbeel pu yii: «Babiloon kitiŋkpaaŋŋi, tilaakpaal dambi nì bitiŋwiiliibi na.»

english_verse: I could tell that the woman was drunk on the blood of God's people who had given their lives for Jesus. This surprising sight amazed me,
translation_verse: Ní m ká yii unimpuee nyùn̄ Unimbɔti nib nì bin nóó Yeesu deedee bi kūū-bee fatikuu ki gbí. M nín ká mimmee ní m bākatì sèeee.

english_verse: and the angel said: Why are you so amazed? I will explain the mystery about this woman and about the beast she is sitting on, with its seven heads and ten horns.
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu bālifì-mi yii: «Ba ŋá ní a bākatì? M làá bìitī unimpuee nì upeel un pu u kā u cáá ayil aluli nì iyin saalaayee bɔɔŋŋi pu kí tùkù-si.

english_verse: The beast you saw is one that used to be and no longer is. It will come back from the deep pit, but only to be destroyed. Everyone on earth whose names were not written in the book of life before the time of creation will be amazed. They will see this beast that used to be and no longer is, but will be once more.
translation_verse: Upeel un a ká nee nìn bí dooooyee, ama kɔŋkɔnnee waa ti bí. U làá nyānní mbookpaan ŋun ni u nìn bée ní kí nīn cá laakin bi làá nàan̄-uee. An làá dāá ŋá bin doooo duulinya kíltam baa ŋmàn̄ bi-yiŋŋi dimaŋfal gbɔŋkunee maamaaci, bi yaa láa fātìi gíti ká upeel gbantee. Di sá upeelee nìn pée bí dooooyee ní ki dāa wáŋkì, ní ki dāa gíti fātìi nyánní.

english_verse: Anyone with wisdom can figure this out. The seven heads that the woman is sitting on stand for seven hills. These heads are also seven kings.
translation_verse: «Tibɔti nee pu ní unil máaǹ kí dàkà u-landɔkɔŋu nì u-ciiŋŋu. Upeelee yiliŋ alulee di sá ajoon aluli ŋin pu unimpuee kēe, ní ki sá bibɔtiibi biluli mun.

english_verse: Five of the kings are dead. One is ruling now, and the other one has not yet come. But when he does, he will rule for only a little while.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibi bilulee kansikin biŋmoo lítì, ubɔ kā dibeejal pu, ní un kíǹee kaa láá bāań, ama u mun yaa láa bāańee, waa làá dāá kàl̄ kí yúntí.

english_verse: You also saw a beast that used to be and no longer is. That beast is one of the seven kings who will return as the eighth king, but only to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Upeel un nìn bí ní kaa ti bée u-ba kútì ki sá ubɔtininiiti, u mun sá bibɔtiibi bilulee kansikin ubɔ ní. Úǹ ní bi làá nàan̄.

english_verse: The ten horns you saw are ten more kings, who have not yet come into power, and they will rule with the beast for only a short time.
translation_verse: «Iyin saalaa in a kée di sá bibɔtiibi saalaa bin kaa láá kāl̀ dibeel puee, ama bi làá tīī-bi mpɔn bi nì upeelee ń jī dibeel kukúluu kubɔ poon.

english_verse: They all think alike and will give their power and authority to the beast.
translation_verse: Bibɔtiibee kɔkɔ dāa pēē kinyɔkɔ ní kí dū bi-pɔŋyi kí kūtì upeelee.

english_verse: These kings will go to war against the Lamb. But he will defeat them, because he is Lord over all lords and King over all kings. His followers are chosen and special and faithful.
translation_verse: Ní bí jáǹ Dipibil, ní Dipibil ń dāá pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi, u nì bin kɔkɔ sá u-yab u lútì-bi bi yú deedeeyee, kun puee úǹ di sá bidindambi kɔkɔ Dindaan, nì bibɔtiibi kɔkɔ Bɔtiu.»

english_verse: The oceans you saw the prostitute sitting on are crowds of people from all races and languages.
translation_verse: Ní ntuunee gíti bí-mi yii: «Inyiŋfi in pu a ká kilaakpaayee kēe di sá atimbun nibiim nì isoon kamaa nib.

english_verse: The ten horns and the beast will start hating the shameless woman. They will strip off her clothes and leave her naked. Then they will eat her flesh and throw the rest of her body into a fire.
translation_verse: Iyin saalaa in a kée nì upeelee làá nīn ná kilaakpaayee ní. Bi làá dāá gbākal̀ tiwan tin kɔkɔ kā ki-wunti puee ní kí kíń dicancaŋgbeel, ní kí dāá ŋmɔ́ ki-nanti ní kí dū-kì kí wà ŋŋmi.

english_verse: God is the one who made these kings all think alike and decide to give their power to the beast. And they will do this until what God has said comes true.
translation_verse: Di sá Unimbɔti di dū min u lèe ki ŋá bi-pɔbiliŋin bí ŋá ubaanti kí dū bi-pɔŋyi kí kūtì upeelee pu, kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun Unimbɔti làá dāá ŋá min u nìn lī yii u làá ŋée.

english_verse: The woman you saw is the great city that rules over all kings on earth.
translation_verse: «Unimpu un a kée di sá kitiŋkpaaŋŋi kin tɔ́kɔ́ duulinya bɔtiibi puee.»

english_verse: I saw another angel come from heaven. This one had great power, and the earth was bright because of his glory.
translation_verse: Boonee ní m ká ntuun ŋubɔ nyánní yilpu ki cáá mpɔŋkpaan, ní ŋu nín jìl̀ puee ŋmíntì duulinya kɔkɔ.

english_verse: The angel shouted, “Fallen! Powerful Babylon has fallen and is now the home of demons. It is the den of every filthy spirit and of all unclean birds, and every dirty and hated animal.
translation_verse: Ní ntuunee téeń mpɔn yii: «Kì lítì, Babiloon tiŋkpaaŋkee lítì ki kpántì kɔŋkɔnnee arasiniibi kɔŋkooŋŋu, arasiniibi nín bí tɔbin puee balilaŋki, nì inoon in kɔkɔ kaa sàafì kpataaayee balilaŋki.

english_verse: Babylon's evil and immoral wine has made all nations drunk. Every king on earth has slept with her, and every merchant on earth is rich because of her evil desires.”
translation_verse: Di sá yii kì nyūntì atimbun kɔkɔ ki-daam min sá ki-jɔkɔmbiikuee. Duulinya bɔtiibi kɔkɔ dōoǹ nì kì ki kpántì bijɔkɔndambi, ní duulinya bantiliibi kūliŋkì ki-wannyaanti tikpil tikpil.»

english_verse: Then I heard another voice from heaven shout, “My people, you must escape from Babylon. Don't take part in her sins and share her punishment.
translation_verse: Ní m gíti gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ nyánní yilpu ki lī yii: «M-samaau, nyāmaan kitiŋ nee poon, án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa ŋá ki-kpitii, kí dāá fōō ki-tafadaaldi din bi bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ-kèe.

english_verse: Her sins are piled as high as heaven. God has remembered the evil she has done.
translation_verse: Kun puee kitiŋ gbanti yab kpitii kpúkú ní ki tin sāā kutagbɔŋu, Unimbɔti kaa súntì ki-tuŋkpitiŋ gbanti pu.

english_verse: Treat her as she has treated others. Make her pay double for what she has done. Make her drink twice as much of what she mixed for others.
translation_verse: Ŋámaan-kì kii kì nín ŋá-ni puee, téem̀maan-kì ikpiti in kì ŋá-nee mili pu. Kì nín dáaĺ ni-tafal miŋyee, nimbi ń dáaĺ-kì míǹ mili pu.

english_verse: That woman honored herself with a life of luxury. Reward her now with suffering and pain. “Deep in her heart Babylon said, ‘I am the queen! Never will I be a widow or know what it means to be sad.’
translation_verse: Kì nín cáá tiwannyaandi ki gà ki-bindi miŋyee, ní yàntī falaa nì dinimbinaamandi ń kɔ́-kì míǹ, kun puee kì sòoǹ ki pɔ̀ ki-ba yii kíǹ sá unimpubɔti ní, kaa sá ukpiipu, dinimbinaamandi kpá kí kɔ́ kíǹ dalba dalba.

english_verse: And so, in a single day she will suffer the pain of sorrow, hunger, and death. Fire will destroy her dead body, because her judge is the powerful Lord God.”
translation_verse: An pu ní ditafadaaldi din dɔ̄ ki cí-kèe kɔkɔ làá bàń ki-pu ŋwimbaanti, ŋkúm nì dinimbinaamandi nì ŋkùm, ní ŋŋmi ń dāá púntí-kì kí wà, kun puee ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti un dáaĺ ki-tafalee sá mpɔndaan ní.»

english_verse: Every king on earth who slept with her and shared in her luxury will mourn. They will weep, when they see the smoke from that fire.
translation_verse: Niin ní duulinya bɔtiibi bin nì u kpáfì ki ŋá tijɔkɔndi ki yākatì ki-wannyaantee làá sɔ̄ kí yāliŋkì bi yaa láa ká ŋŋmi ŋun bíi wù kitiŋ gbantee ŋminyiim yíkì jòoooyee.

english_verse: Her sufferings will frighten them, and they will stand at a distance and say, “Pity that great and powerful city! Pity Babylon! In a single hour her judgment has come.”
translation_verse: Dinimbinaamandi din poon kitiŋee làá dāá kɔ́ee làá cúú-bi tifaandi, ní bi dāa yú kudandaŋu ki lì yii: «Ba busuu di jéetì Babiloon kitiŋkpaaŋŋi kin cáá mpɔnee pu nan dee! Kukúbambaantiiu poon bi kpáàa pée dáaĺ sii tafal sɔkɔmiii?»

english_verse: Every merchant on earth will mourn, because there is no one to buy their goods.
translation_verse: Ní duulinya bantiliibi sūǹ ki yáliŋkí ki-pu, kun puee baa làá ti ká ubɔ ń dā bi-nyampuwanti,

english_verse: There won't be anyone to buy their gold, silver, jewels, pearls, fine linen, purple cloth, silk, scarlet cloth, sweet-smelling wood, fancy carvings of ivory and wood, as well as things made of bronze, iron, or marble.
translation_verse: bi-nyampuwanti tin sá sindaariyab nì animbil kúti, nì ataŋkpee ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee, nì abeedimbil nì iŋaamɔnti nì iŋaabɔn nì iman, nì in bí kii sirci ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee, nì idɔ in cáá kudapɔɔu tikpilee kɔkɔ, nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáá akuntinyin ki ŋáańee, nì bi nín cáá idɔ ki kpítí tiwammɔntiil tin an pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee, nì tasa kúti nì tikúti wanti nì ataŋkpee ŋin jìl̀ee,

english_verse: No one will buy their cinnamon, spices, incense, myrrh, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, slaves, and other humans.
translation_verse: nì talaalub nín bí tɔbin puee nì tifaal tin sɔ́fèe nì ŋkpaŋŋmitikaam, nì tikaliŋkpun tin bi tùutī an sɔ́fèe, nì idafi nì ikpafi nì ŋkpɔnɔyim, nì bilee biliŋ nì inaa nì ipii nì itaamu nì tɔrɔkub nì iyumbu, ki tin kpáaǹ binib nammu.

english_verse: Babylon, the things your heart desired have all escaped from you. Every luxury and all your glory will be lost forever. You will never get them back.
translation_verse: Ní binyampoobee kíǹ ki lì yii: «Tiwan tin pu a-nimbiliŋ máǹee kaa ti dàbiǹ-si, a-gaajati nì a-wannyaanti tin jìl̀ pàlpalee wáŋkì a-ŋaan, a pée gíti kpá kí ká-tì jaanjaan!»

english_verse: The merchants had become rich because of her. But when they saw her sufferings, they were terrified. They stood at a distance, crying and mourning.
translation_verse: Binyampoobi bin di bāntì kitiŋ gbanti poon ki ká animbilee, làá dāá fàŋkì falaa un kitiŋee bíi jīǹee, an pu ní bi dāa yú kudandaŋu ki sūǹ ki yáliŋkí,

english_verse: Then they shouted, “Pity the great city of Babylon! She dressed in fine linen and wore purple and scarlet cloth. She had jewelry made of gold and precious stones and pearls.
translation_verse: ki lì yii: «Mbusu, mbusu kɔ́ kitiŋkpaaŋŋi, kíǹ kin nìn pēē iŋaamɔnti, ibɔn nì iman bɔkutinyaaŋŋee. Kì nìn túuń sindaariya falfatib nì abeedimbil nì idiŋfi in pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaau ki jìl̀ee,

english_verse: Yet in a single hour her riches disappeared.” Every ship captain and passenger and sailor stood at a distance, together with everyone who does business by traveling on the sea.
translation_verse: kukúbambaantiiu ja poon ní bi dūu kúntì ki-gaajati kɔkɔ!» Bimeelaŋaalkpilib kɔkɔ nì bin kā meelabinee nì bimeelaŋaaliliibi nì bin kɔkɔ tūǹ ditundi tiŋkunee yúń kudandaŋu

english_verse: When they saw the smoke from her fire, they shouted, “This was the greatest city ever!”
translation_verse: ki wāĺ kitiŋee nín fōō ŋŋmi mi-nyiim yíkí jòoooyee, ní bi gbáà ibiil ki lì yii: «Kitiŋ kiba kpá bí dūú ŋmàntīǹ Babiloon tiŋki».

english_verse: They cried loudly, and in their sorrow they threw dust on their heads, as they said, “Pity the great city of Babylon! Everyone who sailed the seas became rich from her treasures. But in a single hour the city was destroyed.
translation_verse: Bi nìn jáfí ntam ki sìtī bi-yiliŋ pu ki sūǹ ki yáliŋkí ní ki lì yii: «Mbusu ulɔu di nín kɔ́ kitiŋkpaaŋŋi míǹ nan dee! Ki-gaajati pu ní meeladambi kpántì bigaajab. Ní kukúbambaantiiu ja poon ní bi kpáàa kúntì sii nì a-wanti kɔkɔɔɔ!»

english_verse: The heavens should be happy with God's people and apostles and prophets. God has punished her for them.”
translation_verse: Nimbi bin kóò yilpu ki sá Unimbɔti yab nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì Yeesu kpambaliŋee, nín̄ fàal̀maan tin bāań kitiŋkpaaŋŋi gbantee pu, kun puee ikpiti in kì ŋá-nee pu ní Unimbɔti dáaĺ ki-tafal kí pɔ̀-ni.

english_verse: A powerful angel then picked up a huge stone and threw it into the sea. The angel said, “This is how the great city of Babylon will be thrown down, never to rise again.
translation_verse: Niinee ní ntuun mpɔndaan ŋubɔ yōoǹ ditaŋkpal diba dì gbìfì kii kunaauee ki tɔ́ tiŋkun, ní ki bí yii: «Míǹ ní bi làá dāá téé Babiloon kitiŋkpaaŋŋi kìlkil kí tɔ̄ taapu, ubɔ kaa dāa gíti líkití ki-pu jaanjaan.

english_verse: The music of harps and singers and of flutes and trumpets will no longer be heard. No workers will ever set up shop in that city, and the sound of grinding grain will be silenced forever.
translation_verse: Baa làá ti gbìl̄ kitiŋ gbanti poon bi bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu, kaa làá ti gbìl̄ bi búǹ diwul àá dikantándi, kaa làá ti gbìl̄ bigbiŋgbiililiibi baa ubɔ pu, kaa làá ti wāl̀ utɔntɔnli báà uŋyee kitiŋ gbanti poon, kaa làá ti gbìl̄ bi nà kunaau.

english_verse: Lamps will no longer shine anywhere in Babylon, and couples will never again say wedding vows there. Her merchants ruled the earth, and by her witchcraft she fooled all nations.
translation_verse: Fitila walifiŋu kaa làá ti ŋmíntí kitiŋ gbanti pu. Baa làá ti gbìl̄ unimpucaan nì u-cal pu. Kun puee bibantiliibi sá bikpikpaambi ní kitiŋ gbanti poon, ní ki cáá bi-bɔti ki kíiĺ binib kɔkɔ.»

english_verse: On the streets of Babylon is found the blood of God's people and of his prophets, and everyone else.”
translation_verse: Kitiŋ gbanti fōō ditafadaaldi, kun puee bi kūū Unimbɔti yab nì u-bɔnaatiliibi nì bin kɔkɔ bi kūū kitiŋ puee.

english_verse: After this, I heard what sounded like a lot of voices in heaven, and they were shouting, “Praise the Lord! To our God belongs the glorious power to save,
translation_verse: Boonee ní m gbìl̄ yilpu an bí kii kunipaau neenee, ki lī mpɔn yii: «Aleeluya! Ti-Nimbɔtiu di yì difiil nì tinyool nì mpɔn.

english_verse: because his judgments are honest and fair. That filthy prostitute ruined the earth with shameful deeds. But God has judged her and made her pay the price for murdering his servants.”
translation_verse: U-bɔsòontam sá mbaamɔn ní ki bí deedee. Di sá yii u sòon̄ ki kūū kinimpulaakpaai bɔti kì nín dū ki-laakpaati ki tīntì kitiŋ pu kɔkɔ nib ki yāntì bi kpántì bikpitibee, ní ki dáaĺ ki-tafal ki tɔ̀n̄-kì ipɔntoon kì nín kūū u-tɔntɔnliibi puee.»

english_verse: Then the crowd shouted, “Praise the Lord! Smoke will never stop rising from her burning body.”
translation_verse: Ní ki gíti bí yii: «Aleeluya! Kun puee kitiŋ gbanti làá nīn pée wù ŋŋmi ní ki-ŋminyiim ń nīn yíkí míǹ kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_verse: From the throne a voice said, “If you worship and fear our God, give praise to him, no matter who you are.”
translation_verse: Ní nneen ŋubɔ nyánní dibeejal cee ki lī yii: «Nimbi bin kɔkɔ sá Unimbɔti tɔntɔnliibee, nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan-u! Bikpaambi nì mbiyaamu, bin kɔkɔ fàŋkí-uee, nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan-u!»

english_verse: Then I heard what seemed to be a large crowd that sounded like a roaring flood and loud thunder all mixed together. They were saying, “Praise the Lord! Our Lord God All-Powerful now rules as king.
translation_verse: Ní m gbìl̄ an bí kii binib kupaau di sòon̄ee, ní ki bí kii dimɔɔl nyim nín sìtī nsitimin puee, ní ki gíti bí kii utaa nín tátí mpɔn puee ki lì yii: «Aleeluya! Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan di sá ubɔti ki kā dibeel pu.

english_verse: So we will be glad and happy and give him praise. The wedding day of the Lamb is here, and his bride is ready.
translation_verse: Tí nīn fàal̀maan án nīn mɔ̄ǹ-ti tí nīn nyɔ́ŋkí Unimbɔti, kun puee Dipibil nimpucáatam bāań, u-bɔɔn bɔ́ntì ki dóò.

english_verse: Then the angel told me, “Put this in writing. God will bless everyone who is invited to the wedding feast of the Lamb.” The angel also said, “These things God has said are true.”
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu bí yii ḿ ŋmà yii: «Bin bi yíiń bí dāá jī Dipibil nimpucáatam jintee bí mmɔnneeee!» Ní ki gíti kútì yii: «Unimbɔti u-ba di lī míǹ.»

english_verse: I knelt at the feet of the angel and began to worship him. But the angel said, “Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you and everyone else who tells about Jesus. Don't worship anyone but God. Everyone who tells about Jesus does it by the power of the Spirit.” The Rider on the White Horse
translation_verse: U lī mimmee ní m gbāaǹ kí jāam̀-u, ní u bí-mi yii: «Taa ŋée! Ma mun pée sá utɔntɔnli kii si nì a-nabiyaamu mun bí ki sòoǹ Yeesu bɔti tin u nyántì ki dàkā-nee ní. Unimbɔti ní a máaǹ kí jāam̀.» Kun puee Unimbɔti Fam nín yāntì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi sòon̄ tiŋyee sòoǹ Yeesu pu ní. Utanjakal un kā utampiin puee

english_verse: I looked and saw heaven was open, and a white horse was there. Its rider was called Faithful and True, and he is always fair when he judges or goes to war.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m ká yilpu pīitì, ní utampiin ubɔ nyánní, ní unil ubɔ kā u-pu, bi yíì udaan yii Deedee nì Mbaamɔn, u sòoǹ tibɔti deedee ki jáà kujaau nì deedee.

english_verse: He had eyes like flames of fire, and he was wearing a lot of crowns. His name was written on him, but he was the only one who knew what the name meant.
translation_verse: U-nimbiliŋ ŋmóò làka laka kii ŋŋmee, ní u cíkí mbeefuulimu tikpil u-yil pu. Diyindi diba náká u-pu, báà ubɔ kaa nyí-dì, see úǹ baba.

english_verse: The rider wore a robe that was covered with blood, and he was known as “The Word of God.”
translation_verse: Ní u-bɔkutil din u pēēyee táká fatiku, ní bi yíì-u yii: «Unimbɔti nyɔɔbundi.»

english_verse: He was followed by armies from heaven that rode on white horses and were dressed in pure white linen.
translation_verse: Ní yilpu janjaliibi nóó-u ki kā itampiin pu ki pēē abɔkutimɔnti apiin káŋkaŋ.

english_verse: From his mouth a sharp sword went out to attack the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod and will show the fierce anger of God All-Powerful by trampling the grapes in the pit where wine is made.
translation_verse: U-nyɔkɔnee kitàataajiki kā ki jītí. An ní u làá dūú jáǹ atimbun. Mpɔn ŋun u làá dāá nīn cáa kpòotī-bee dāa pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii tikútee ní, ní Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín díkí bi-pu diŋuul diŋyee puee, u làá dāá nà-bi dúsi dusi kii bi nín nà asubil pu ki ŋáań ndaamee ní.

english_verse: On the part of the robe that covered his thigh was written, “KING OF KINGS AND Lord OF LordS.”
translation_verse: Bi ŋmàn̄ diyindi diba u-bɔkutil nì u-tapandi pu yii: «Bibɔtiibi kɔkɔ Bɔtiu, bidindambi kɔkɔ Dindaan.»

english_verse: I then saw an angel standing on the sun, and he shouted to all the birds flying in the sky, “Come and join in God's great feast!
translation_verse: Ní m ká Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ŋubɔ yú ŋwìiń poon, ní ŋu téeń mpɔn ki tùkū inoon in kɔkɔ ŋàaǹ kutaa puee yii: «Dāá kpāfìmaan kí jī Unimbɔti jiŋaakpaaŋwu!

english_verse: You can eat the flesh of kings, rulers, leaders, horses, riders, free people, slaves, important people, and everyone else.”
translation_verse: Ní dāan̄ kí jī bibɔtiibi nì bisoojakpilib nì bipɔndambi wunnanti nì itaamu nì bin kā-iee wunnanti, nì binib kɔkɔ wunnanti, bin yì bi-bee nì iyumbu, binikpaambi nì biwaabi.»

english_verse: I also saw the beast and all kings of the earth come together. They fought against the rider on the white horse and against his army.
translation_verse: Niinee ní m ká upeelee nì duulinya bɔtiibi nì bi-soojab kpáfì kí jáǹ un kā utaamu puee nì u-janjaliibi.

english_verse: But the beast was captured and so was the false prophet. This is the same prophet who had worked miracles for the beast, so he could fool everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol. The beast and the false prophet were thrown alive into a lake of burning sulfur.
translation_verse: Ní un kā utaamu puee nì u-janjaliibi cúú upeelee nì u-nyimɔmbɔnaatiliu un nìn ŋáań maamaacib upeelee nimbiin ki kíiĺ binib bin kɔkɔ bi nìn dáań upeelee daaŋku bi gbàantí ki jáaḿ upeelee naŋkuee. Ní bi dū bi-liitil nì bi-nimbiliŋ ki tɔ́ farwata ŋmibookun.

english_verse: But the rest of their army was killed by the sword that came from the mouth of the rider on the horse. Then birds stuffed themselves on the dead bodies.
translation_verse: Ní kitàataajiki kin nyēē un kā utampiinee nyɔkɔnee kūū bin kíǹee kɔkɔ, ní inoon dɔ́miń ki jíń bi-nanti ki bál̀.

english_verse: I saw thrones, and sitting on those thrones were the ones who had been given the right to judge. I also saw the souls of the people who had their heads cut off because they had told about Jesus and preached God's message. They were the same ones who had not worshiped the beast or the idol, and they had refused to let its mark be put on their foreheads or hands. They will come to life and rule with Christ for
translation_verse: Ní m ká abeejal aba, ní bi tīī bin kā ŋi-puee mpɔn bí nīn sá bibɔsoonliibi, ní m gíti ká bin nìn sòoǹ Unimbɔti bɔti ki lèekī Yeesu pu seera bi kūū-bee nammu, nì bin kaa nìn gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ upeelee nì u-naŋkuee, kaa yāntì bi dáań bi-yigbeeŋi nì bi-ŋaliiyee, bi-kɔkɔ fātìi fīkitì bi nì Kriisitoo kāl̀ dibeel abin kutuku.

english_verse: These people are the first to be raised to life, and they are especially blessed and holy. The second death has no power over them. They will be priests for God and Christ and will rule with them for
translation_verse: Bin yaa láa bí difìkitipeekaal poonee bí mmɔnni nì circir poon. Ŋkúnliliitiim kaa dāa gíti cáá bíǹ pu mpɔn. Bíǹ di dāa sá Unimbɔti nì Kriisitoo saraaŋaliibi, ní bi nì Kriisitoo ń kàl̄ u-beelin abin kutuku. Dijajikuntikaal

english_verse: He will fool the countries of Gog and Magog, which are at the far ends of the earth, and their people will follow him into battle. They will have as many followers as there are grains of sand along the beach,
translation_verse: U yaa nyáńee, u làá dāá nīn yìiǹ ki mɔ́ntí duulinya jannaatiliŋ timbuliŋ, an dàkà yii Gɔɔgi nì Maagoogi, kí kpāfì-bi bí bɔ́ntí kujaau. Bi làá dāá nīn wīikí tikpil kii tiŋku gbandi bulee ní.

english_verse: and they will march all the way across the earth. They will surround the camp of God's people and the city God loves. But fire will come down from heaven and destroy the whole army.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá kpátí kí gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ, ní kí dāá léeń Unimbɔti nibul nì kitiŋ kin u néeńee pu, ama ŋŋmi ŋubɔ làá nyānní yilpu kí dāá wà bi-kɔkɔ.

english_verse: Then the devil who fooled them will be thrown into the lake of fire and burning sulfur. He will be there with the beast and the false prophet, and they will be in pain day and night forever and ever. The Judgment at the Great White Throne
translation_verse: Ní bí dāá téé Sitaan un kíiĺ-bee kí tɔ̄ farwata nì ŋŋmi bookun, laakin upeelee nì u-nyimɔmbɔnaatiliu bée. Niin ní bi làá nīn bí falaa poon ki yáliŋkíǹ bi-ba ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Ibɔsoonjoolkaa

english_verse: I saw a great white throne with someone sitting on it. Earth and heaven tried to run away, but there was no place for them to go.
translation_verse: Boonee ní m ká dibeejapindi dikpaandi diba, ní kitiŋ nì kutagbɔŋu sáǹ un kā dibeejapindi gbanti puee nimbiin, baa ti ká-bi.

english_verse: I also saw all the dead people standing in front of that throne. Every one of them was there, no matter who they had once been. Several books were opened, and then the book of life was opened. The dead were judged by what those books said they had done.
translation_verse: Ní m ká bitaŋkpiibi, bikpaambi nì biwaabi yú dibeejalee nimbiin, ní bi cúú tigbɔn ki kpátì, ní ki gíti cúú kugbɔŋu kubɔ mun ki kpátì, kúǹ di sá dimaŋfal gbɔŋku. Ní bi sòon̄ bitaŋkpiibi bɔti ki táá nì bi nín túń atuun ŋin bi ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋu poonee.

english_verse: The sea gave up the dead people who were in it, and death and its kingdom also gave up their dead. Then everyone was judged by what they had done.
translation_verse: Ní tiŋku gíiǹní binib bin u nìn yōoǹee, ní ŋkúm nì ditaŋkpiil gíiǹní bitaŋkpiibi bin kɔkɔ bi ŋúb́ee, ní bi sòon̄ báà ŋma bɔti tin u ŋée.

english_verse: Afterwards, death and its kingdom were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
translation_verse: Ní bi téé ŋkúm nì ditaŋkpiil ki tɔ́ ŋŋmi bookun, ŋŋmi booku gbanti di sá ŋkúnliliitiimee.

english_verse: Anyone whose name wasn't written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
translation_verse: Un kamaa yindi ní baa ká dimaŋfal gbɔŋku poonee, bi dù-u kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmi bookun ní.

english_verse: I saw a new heaven and a new earth. The first heaven and the first earth had disappeared, and so had the sea.
translation_verse: Boonee ní m ká kutagbɔmpɔŋu nì kitimpɔŋ. Kutagbɔŋkpikuu nì kitiŋkpikii wáŋkì ní tiŋku kaa ti bí.

english_verse: I heard a loud voice shout from the throne: God's home is now with his people. He will live with them, and they will be his own. Yes, God will make his home among his people.
translation_verse: Ní m gbìl̄ nneen ŋubɔ nyánní dibeejal cee ki téeń mpɔn yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee Unimbɔti ŋá u-kɔŋkooŋŋu binib cee. U nì bi di làá nīn kíǹ ki kóò, ní bí nīn sá u-nibul, ní úǹ ń nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu un làá nīn bí bi-ceeyee.

english_verse: He will wipe all tears from their eyes, and there will be no more death, suffering, crying, or pain. These things of the past are gone forever.
translation_verse: Úǹ di làá dāá pítí bi-nyinnyim kɔkɔ, ŋkúm dāa gíti kpá, dinimbinaamandi nì ibiil nì iyaliŋki dāa gíti kpá, kun puee duulinyakpiki kpáaǹ tíǹ kɔkɔ ki jítì.»

english_verse: Then the one sitting on the throne said: I am making everything new. Write down what I have said. My words are true and can be trusted.
translation_verse: Ní un kā dibeejal puee bí yii: «Kpèèmaan, m fātìi ŋá tiwan kɔkɔ mpɔm,» ní ki bí-mi yii: «Á ŋmà-tì, kun puee tibɔti gbanti sá mbaamɔn ní ki máaǹ bí fōō-tì.»

english_verse: Everything is finished! I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will freely give water from the life-giving fountain to everyone who is thirsty.
translation_verse: Ní u gíti bí-mi yii: «An kɔkɔ bɔ́ntì ki dóò! Man di sá Alfa nì Oomeega, ukílkaa nì ukúntikaa. Un ní nnyinnyoo yaa cááyee ń dāan̄ m-cee, m làá tīī-u nnyim min nyēeń dimaŋfal nyimbuliŋunee faalaa.

english_verse: All who win the victory will be given these blessings. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
translation_verse: Un yaa jáń ki jíńee ní m làá tīī tiwammɔntiil gbanti, ní ki dāa sá u-Nimbɔtiu, ní úǹ dāa sá man biki.

english_verse: But I will tell you what will happen to cowards and to everyone who is unfaithful or dirty-minded or who murders or is sexually immoral or uses witchcraft or worships idols or tells lies. They will be thrown into that lake of fire and burning sulfur. This is the second death. The New Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ama an yaa kíǹ bifaantidambee nì bin kaa yú nì Unimbɔti deedeeyee, nì bijɔkɔndambee, nì binikpɔliibee, nì bin ŋáań tilaakpaalee, nì bikpaŋkpantiibee nì biwaatootiliibee nì binyimɔndambee kɔkɔee, bíǹ laŋki di sá farwata ŋmibookun, niin di sá ŋkúnliliitiimee.» Jeerusaleempɔɔn

english_verse: I saw one of the seven angels who had the bowls filled with the seven last terrible troubles. The angel came to me and said, “Come on! I will show you the one who will be the bride and wife of the Lamb.”
translation_verse: Ní ituun iluli ijoolkaa in bàà ŋúb́ nsambiyaamu falaabi gbí poonee kansikin ŋubɔ dɔ́miń ki bí-mi yii: «Dāan̄ ḿ dàkà-si unimpucaan, Dipibil nimpuu.»

english_verse: Then with the help of the Spirit, he took me to the top of a very high mountain. There he showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down from God in heaven.
translation_verse: Ní Unimbɔti Fam dɔ́miń m-ni, ní ntuun yōoǹ-mi ki jɔ́m̀ dijoofɔkɔl diba pu, ní ki dàkā-mi Jeerusaleem circir tiŋki kin nyánní Unimbɔti cee ki sìntīńee.

english_verse: The glory of God made the city bright. It was dazzling and crystal clear like a precious jasper stone.
translation_verse: Kì nìn jìlìń Unimbɔti nyaaŋku ní. Kitiŋee jìl̀ kii ataŋkpanyaanee, a lì kii ataŋkpee ŋin jɔ̀m̀ pɔ́lpɔl ki wāĺ kílkilee.

english_verse: The city had a high and thick wall with twelve gates, and each one of them was guarded by an angel. On each of the gates was written the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Ní digundi din bi máń ki māntì ki tú kitiŋee gbìfì ki fɔ̀kɔ̀ mun, ní ki cáá mpunyɔmu saalaa nì muli, ní ituun saalaa nì ili yú mpunyɔmu pu ki cí, ní bi ŋmàn̄ Isirayeel yab naakɔti saalaa nì tilee yiŋŋi ki nákáǹ mpunyɔmuee pu.

english_verse: Three of these gates were on the east, three were on the north, three more were on the south, and the other three were on the west.
translation_verse: Ní mpunyɔmu muta túĺ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, ní muta túĺ ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú, ní muta túĺ ŋgan pú, ní muta túĺ ŋgiil pú.

english_verse: The city was built on twelve foundation stones. On each of the stones was written the name of one of the Lamb's twelve apostles.
translation_verse: Ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali pu ní bi nìn máń kitiŋee gundi ki tɔ́kɔ́ǹ, ní ki ŋmàn̄ Dipibil kpambaliŋ saalaa nì alee yiŋŋi ataŋkpeeyee pu.

english_verse: The angel who spoke to me had a gold measuring stick to measure the city and its gates and its walls.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun ŋun yú ki sòoǹ nì mee ŋúb́ tiwaŋŋmantikaal, sindaariya kaluuku, kí ŋmàntī kitiŋee nì ki-punyɔmmu nì ki-guŋŋi.

english_verse: The city was shaped like a cube, because it was just as high as it was wide. When the angel measured the city, it was about
translation_verse: Kitiŋee púuŋŋu nì ki-waaŋŋu ŋmà ní. Ntuunee dū sindaariya kaluukuee ki ŋmāntì kitiŋee púuŋŋu, ní ki ká ataŋkpee kutukub bili nì kulaafaau, míǹ ní ki-waaŋŋu nì ki-fɔkɔŋŋu mun nìn sá.

english_verse: Then the angel measured the wall, and by our measurements it was about
translation_verse: Ní ŋu ŋmāntì digundi mun ní ki ká di-gbifiŋŋu meetab imuŋku ita nì biŋmoo, kii binib nín pée ŋmàntī puee ní ŋu ŋmāntì.

english_verse: The wall was built of jasper, and the city was made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
translation_verse: Ataŋkpee ŋin jɔ̀m̀ pɔ́lpɔlee ní bi dū ki máń digundi, ní kitiŋ ki-ba kɔkɔ sá sindaariyamɔnti ki wāĺ kílkil kii digitilee.

english_verse: the fifth was onyx, the sixth was carnelian, the seventh was chrysolite, the eighth was beryl, the ninth was topaz, the tenth was chrysoprase, the eleventh was jacinth, and the twelfth was amethyst.
translation_verse: ní ki yíì diŋmooŋmootiil yii saarduwaan, ní ki yíì diluluutiil yii kɔɔrnaliini, ní ki yíì diluluútiil yii kriistooliiti, ní ki yíì dininiitiil yii beeriil, ní ki yíì diwawaatiil yii toopaasi, ní ki yíì disaalaatiil yii kriisooprasi, ní ki yíì saalaa nì dipeepeekaal yii iyasinti, ní ki yíì dijoolkaalee yii ameetiisti.

english_verse: Each of the twelve gates was a solid pearl. The streets of the city were made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
translation_verse: Mpunyɔmu saalaa nì mulee sá ataŋkpanyaan ní. Kipunyɔkɔ kamaa nì ditaŋkpapiiŋkaal dimɔndi. Ní kitiŋ ki-ba daŋŋi sá sindaariyamɔnti ki wāĺ kílkil kii digitilee.

english_verse: I did not see a temple there. The Lord God All-Powerful and the Lamb were its temple.
translation_verse: Ama maa ká kunimbɔtidii kitiŋ gbanti poon, kun puee ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nì Dipibil di sá kunimbɔtidii.

english_verse: And the city did not need the sun or the moon. The glory of God was shining on it, and the Lamb was its light.
translation_verse: Kitiŋ gbanti kaa nyàab̀ ŋwìiń nì uŋmal ń ŋmíntí-kì i-walfiŋu, Unimbɔti nyooti di dāa sá-kì ŋwalifi, ní Dipibil dāa sá ki-fitilau.

english_verse: Nations will walk by the light of that city, and kings will bring their riches there.
translation_verse: Atimbun kɔkɔ dāa còom̄ ki-walifiŋun ní, ní duulinya bɔtiibi ń dāá cáań bi-gaajati niin.

english_verse: Its gates are always open during the day, and night never comes.
translation_verse: Mpunyɔmu dāa pée wāā ní ŋwiimpu, baa pìintí, kun puee kunyeeu dāa kpá niin.

english_verse: The glorious treasures of nations will be brought into the city.
translation_verse: Bi dāa cāabìń atimbun jilmau nì ŋi-nyooti niin.

english_verse: But nothing unworthy will be allowed to enter. No one who is dirty-minded or who tells lies will be there. Only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will be in the city.
translation_verse: Ikpiti iba kaa dāa kóò niin, nì bitiŋwiiliibi nì binyimɔndambi, see bin baba yiŋŋi bi ŋmàn̄ Dipibil gbɔŋku kun sá dimaŋfal gbɔŋkuee nee.

english_verse: The angel showed me a river that was crystal clear, and its waters gave life. The river came from the throne where God and the Lamb were seated.
translation_verse: Ní ntuun dàkā-mi mbun ŋun pùub̀ nnyim min tìì dimaŋfalee. Nnyim gbanti wāĺ ní kílkil ní ki jìl̀ pàlpal, ní ki nyēeń Unimbɔti nì Dipibil beejal laŋki.

english_verse: Then it flowed down the middle of the city's main street. On each side of the river are trees that grow a different kind of fruit each month of the year. The fruit gives life, and the leaves are used as medicine to heal the nations.
translation_verse: Mì pùub̀ kitiŋ kansikin didandi pu. Ní dimaŋfal subu yú abuŋgbán liitil pu ki lòoǹ dibindi poonee saalaa nì mili, an dàkà yii uŋmal kamaa poonee bu lòoǹ diba. Bu-faati di cāantí atimbun weeŋyi.

english_verse: God's curse will no longer be on the people of that city. He and the Lamb will be seated there on their thrones, and its people will worship God
translation_verse: Mbusu dāa gíti kpá. Unimbɔti nì Dipibil beejal làá dāá nīn bí kitiŋ poon ní, ní u-tɔntɔnliibi ń nīn nyɔ́ŋkí-u.

english_verse: and will see him face to face. God's name will be written on the foreheads of the people.
translation_verse: Bi làá dāá wāl̀ u-nimbiin, ní bi dāa ŋmà u-yindi bi-yigbeeŋi pu.

english_verse: Never again will night appear, and no one who lives there will ever need a lamp or the sun. The Lord God will be their light, and they will rule forever. The Coming of Christ
translation_verse: Kunyeeu kaa dāa gíti bí. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti nyàab̀ fitila kí tūū án nīn wāĺ-u, kaa dāa gíti nyàab̀ ŋwìiń ń nyā bí nīn wāĺ, kun puee ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di dāa sá-bi ŋwalifi, ní bí dāá nīn bí ki jīǹ dibeel kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Yeesu dāantam

english_verse: Then I was told: These words are true and can be trusted. The Lord God controls the spirits of his prophets, and he is the one who sent his angel to show his servants what must happen very soon.
translation_verse: Ní ntuunee bí-mi yii: «Tibɔti nee sá ibaamɔn ní, ki máaǹ bí fōō-tì. Ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti un tìì u-Fam u-bɔnaatiliibee túnní u-tuuŋŋu ń dāá dàkà u-tɔntɔnliibi tin làá bàń kɔŋkɔnneeyee.»

english_verse: Remember, I am coming soon! God will bless everyone who pays attention to the message of this book.
translation_verse: Ní Yeesu bí yii: «Pīlifì! M làá dāan̄ kɔŋkɔnnee. Un ŋúb́ tibɔti tin m sòon̄ bi ŋmàn̄ an kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee bí mmɔnni.»

english_verse: My name is John, and I am the one who heard and saw these things. Then after I had heard and seen all this, I knelt down and began to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown it to me.
translation_verse: Man Yoowaneesi di gbìl̄ an bɔtee kɔkɔ ki wál̀-tì mun. M nín gbìl̄ ki wál̀-tì mimmee ní m lítì dicincibil ntuun ŋun dàkā-mi tibɔti gbanti kɔkɔ taapuee nimbiin kí jāam̀-ŋu.

english_verse: But the angel said, Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you. I am the same as a follower or a prophet or anyone else who obeys what is written in this book. God is the one you should worship.
translation_verse: Ní ŋu bí-mi yii: «Taa ŋée, kun puee ma mun sá utɔntɔnli kii sisee ní, kii a-nabiyaamu mun nàatī Unimbɔti bɔtee, nì bin kɔkɔ tɔ́ tibɔti tin bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee poonee ní. Unimbɔti ní an sá á jāam̀.»

english_verse: Don't keep the prophecies in this book a secret. These things will happen soon.
translation_verse: Ní u bí-mi yii: «Á taa báĺ tibɔti tin bi nyántì ki dàkā-si tì kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee, kun puee ŋyunti ŋun an bɔtee kɔkɔ làá bàńee tóobiń.

english_verse: Evil people will keep on being evil, and everyone who is dirty-minded will still be dirty-minded. But good people will keep on doing right, and God's people will always be holy.
translation_verse: Unikpiti ń mɔ̀tīí nīn ŋáań u-kpitii, ujɔkɔndaan ń mɔ̀tīí nīn ŋáań u-jɔkɔnti, deedeedaan ń mɔ̀tīí nīn ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi, ní circirdaan ń mɔ̀tīí nīn bí circir.»

english_verse: Then I was told: I am coming soon! And when I come, I will reward everyone for what they have done.
translation_verse: Ní Yeesu bí-mi yii: «Pīlifì! M làá dāan̄ kɔŋkɔnnee kí nīn ŋúbiń tipaal, kí pà báà ŋma u-tundi nín sá puee.

english_verse: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
translation_verse: Man di sá Alfa nì Oomeega, an dàkà yii upeepeekaa nì ujoolkaa, ukílkaa nì ukúntikaa.»

english_verse: God will bless all who have washed their robes. They will each have the right to eat fruit from the tree that gives life, and they can enter the gates of the city.
translation_verse: Bin fíntí bi-bɔkutiŋ ŋaa cáá tijɔkɔndi, ki máaǹ kí ŋmɔ́ dimaŋfal subil, ki làá dī mpunyɔmu kí kɔ́ kitiŋinee bí mmɔnneeee!

english_verse: But outside the city will be dogs, witches, immoral people, murderers, idol worshipers, and everyone who loves to tell lies and do wrong.
translation_verse: Ní bijɔkɔndambi nì bikpaŋkpantiibi nì bin ŋáań tilaakpaalee nì binikpɔliibi nì biwaatootiliibi nì binyimɔndambee dāa yú kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu.

english_verse: I am Jesus! And I am the one who sent my angel to tell all of you these things for the churches. I am David's Great Descendant, and I am also the bright morning star.
translation_verse: «Man Yeesu di túnní m-tuuŋŋu ŋú sòoǹ an bɔti m-nikitiŋ kansikin kí tùkù-ni. M sá Daafiidi naakookun ní, ki sá utaafaaŋmalbija un jìl̀ee.»

english_verse: The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” Everyone who hears this should say, “Come!” If you are thirsty, come! If you want life-giving water, come and take it. It's free!
translation_verse: Unimbɔti Fam nì Unimpucaan bí yii: «Dāan̄!» Bin mun gbìl̄ an bɔtee ń lì yii: «Dāan̄!» Un nnyinnyoo yaa cááyee ń dāan̄ kí fōō nnyim min tìì dimaŋfalee faalaa. Tibɔjoolkaal

english_verse: Here is my warning for everyone who hears the prophecies in this book: If you add anything to them, God will make you suffer all the terrible troubles written in this book.
translation_verse: Man Yoowaneesi di kpáafí bin kɔkɔ gbìl̄ tibɔti tin Unimbɔti sòon̄ an kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee yii: Un yaa gbéeǹ tibɔti nee poon tibee, Unimbɔti làá dāá gbéeǹ udaan ditafadaaldi din u ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋu nee poonee.

english_verse: If you take anything away from these prophecies, God will not let you have part in the life-giving tree and in the holy city described in this book.
translation_verse: Un yaa tí bātì tibɔti gbanti poon tiba ki fée, Unimbɔti làá dāá fōō u-jandi din u cáá disubil din tìì dimaŋfalee poonee, ú taa kɔ́ circir tiŋki kin bɔti bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee poonee.

english_verse: The one who has spoken these things says, “I am coming soon!” So, Lord Jesus, please come soon!
translation_verse: Úǹ Yeesu un bí ki sòoǹ nì ti an bɔtee di lī yii: «Iiin! M làá dāan̄ kɔŋkɔnnee.» Án lafun ŋá míǹ! Dāan̄, ti-Dindaan Yeesu!

english_verse: I pray that the Lord Jesus will be kind to all of you.
translation_verse: Ti-Dindaan Yeesu ŋanti ń nīn bí ni-pu!
